# FDA Phase III SAP Census

**Last updated:** 2026-09-12 · **Version:** 2.0.0

A reference census of FDA Phase III drug submissions (last ~15 years), documenting trial design, the statistical analysis plan (SAP) actually used, and how FDA reviewed it.

**Scope note:** [`Master_Index.md`](Master_Index.md) tracks every FDA novel drug approval from 2011 through Sept 2026 (684 drugs) as the master scaffold for this project. **This census is complete: all 684 of 684 tracked FDA novel drug approvals (2011 through Sept 2026) have a full SAP-depth entry below**, across all 13 therapeutic areas — Oncology (203), Cardiovascular/Metabolic (61), Infectious Disease (83), Neurology/Psychiatry (75), Rare Disease/Genetic/Metabolic-genetic (63), Immunology/Rheumatology/Dermatology (53), Other/Misc (45), Hematology (37), Gastroenterology (20), Endocrine (20), Ophthalmology (18), and Respiratory (6). See `Master_Index.md` for the master scaffold and status tracking, and `Keyword_Taxonomy.md` for the controlled vocabulary used in each entry's Keywords line. (Total drug count is 684, not 683: Immunology deep-dive research discovered lebrikizumab-lbkz/Ebglyss had been missing from the master scaffold, conflated with a same-week, differently-mechanism approval.)

**Sourcing note:** FDA does not routinely publish a sponsor's actual SAP document. Where a genuine SAP or protocol-with-SAP was found (posted by the sponsor on ClinicalTrials.gov's Documents tab, or embedded in an FDA statistical review), it is quoted directly and marked **[verbatim]**. Where no such document is public, the entry instead includes a **Reverse-engineered SAP** section that reconstructs the likely analysis approach from the package insert and reported results, with each inferred point traced to what it's inferred from, and marked **[inferred]**.

**Keyword tagging:** each entry below carries a **Keywords:** line (trial design, endpoint type, primary analysis method, multiplicity control, interim monitoring/alpha-spending, missing-data/bias handling, and regulatory-process tags where applicable), drawn from the controlled vocabulary in [`Keyword_Taxonomy.md`](Keyword_Taxonomy.md). Use that file to look up a term's definition or to see which other submissions use the same statistical method.

## Oncology

### 1. Pembrolizumab (Keytruda) — BLA 125514/S-012

**Sponsor:** Merck Sharp & Dohme LLC

**Indication approved:** First-line treatment of metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), tumors with PD-L1 tumor proportion score (TPS) ≥50%, no EGFR/ALK aberrations

**Approval date:** October 24, 2016

**Pivotal trial:** KEYNOTE-024 (Merck protocol MK-3475-024), NCT02142738

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled, crossover-permitted, biomarker-selected population
- *Endpoints:* PFS (BICR, primary), OS (secondary), ORR (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, stratified Cox proportional-hazards model, Miettinen-Nurminen method (ORR CI)
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence step-down hierarchy (ORR→PFS→OS)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design, Hwang-Shih-DeCani alpha-spending function, non-binding futility (beta-spending)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Randomized (1:1), open-label, active-controlled, multicenter Phase III trial
- Population: treatment-naive metastatic NSCLC, PD-L1 TPS ≥50%, no EGFR/ALK genomic aberrations; excluded autoimmune disease requiring systemic therapy, immunosuppression, prior thoracic radiation >30 Gy within 26 weeks
- Randomization stratified by ECOG performance status (0 vs. 1), histology (squamous vs. non-squamous), geographic region (East Asia vs. non-East Asia)
- Arms: pembrolizumab 200 mg IV q3w vs. investigator's choice of 5 platinum-doublet chemotherapy regimens; crossover to pembrolizumab permitted for chemo-arm patients at BICR-confirmed progression
- Primary endpoint: PFS by blinded independent central review (BICR), RECIST v1.1
- Secondary endpoints: OS, ORR (both BICR-assessed)
- Sample size: event-driven, ~300 subjects randomized 1:1
- Overall type I error strictly controlled at 2.5% (one-sided), allocated across a fixed-sequence hierarchy: ORR → PFS → OS (step-down; a later endpoint is tested only if the prior one in the sequence is positive)

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter (joint S-008/S-012 action) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2016/125514Orig1s008,125514Orig1s012ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (2016, reflecting S-012) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2016/125514s012lbl.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02142738
- Protocol + SAP (Merck, "MK-3475-024-11 Final Protocol," 20-Dec-2017; Section 8 is the SAP) — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/38/NCT02142738/Prot_SAP_000.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Reck M, et al. "Pembrolizumab versus Chemotherapy for PD-L1–Positive Non–Small-Cell Lung Cancer." *N Engl J Med.* 2016;375:1823-1833. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1606774), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27718847/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Pembrolizumab%20versus%20Chemotherapy%20for%20PD-L1-Positive%20Non-Small-Cell%20Lung%20Cancer)

**Other resources**

- Merck participates in the Vivli data-sharing platform (vivli.org); trial-specific IPD availability for KEYNOTE-024 was not individually confirmed in this pass and should be checked on Vivli directly before assuming access.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this supplement.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, from Protocol/SAP Section 8.1.3 "Multiplicity," p.113-114]*

> "The overall type I error rate for this study is strictly controlled at 2.5% (one-sided). There are one planned analysis of ORR, one planned analysis of PFS and two planned analyses of OS. The ORR analysis will occur when the first 191 randomized subjects have a minimum of 6 months of follow up, and will be tested at the 0.5% (one-sided) alpha level. PFS will be tested only once at the planned PFS analysis after ~175 PFS events are observed, and will be tested at the 2.5% (one-sided) level if ORR is positive or at the 2.0% (one-sided) level if ORR is negative. OS will be tested only if PFS is positive and at the same level as PFS (i.e., step-down).
>
> For OS, a Hwang-Shih-DeCani alpha-spending function with the gamma parameter -0.4 and beta-spending function with gamma -35 are constructed to implement group sequential boundaries that control the type I error rate as well as allow for non-binding futility analysis.
>
> If at least 110 OS events are observed at the planned PFS analysis after ~175 PFS events are observed, an interim OS analysis will be conducted at the level determined by the spending function and the actual number of OS events at the PFS analysis. The final OS analysis will occur when ~170 OS events are observed at the level determined by the spending function and the actual number of OS events observed at the PFS analysis...
>
> Following Amendment 08, the final OS analysis is no longer required and will not be performed as described above. This is due to the study hypothesis for OS being supported at the interim analysis with database cutoff of May 9, 2016."

*[verbatim, from the approved Package Insert, Table 9 footnote, reporting the actual interim OS analysis conducted at 108 events]*

> "P-value is compared with 0.0118 of the allocated alpha for this interim analysis."

The label's Table 9 also documents the primary PFS result (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.37-0.68, stratified log-rank p<0.001) and the interim OS result (HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.41-0.89, stratified log-rank p=0.005), both "based on the stratified Cox proportional hazard model" — i.e., the final executed analysis stratified by the randomization factors, consistent with the SAP's planned methodology.

### 2. Osimertinib (Tagrisso) — NDA 208065/S-008

**Sponsor:** AstraZeneca Pharmaceuticals LP

**Indication approved:** First-line treatment of metastatic NSCLC with EGFR exon 19 deletions or exon 21 (L858R) mutations

**Approval date:** April 18, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** FLAURA (AstraZeneca Study D5160C00007, osimertinib coded AZD9291), NCT02296125

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, crossover-permitted, biomarker-selected population
- *Endpoints:* PFS (investigator-assessed, primary), OS (key secondary), CNS PFS, ORR/DoR/DCR, PRO/HRQoL (EORTC QLQ)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test (Breslow method for ties), HR from log-rank U/V statistics, Cox proportional-hazards model (subgroups, Efron method for ties)
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence hierarchy (PFS→OS→CNS PFS)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design, Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function approximating O'Brien-Fleming
- *Missing data/bias:* RPSFT, IPCW (OS crossover adjustment), ascertainment bias, evaluation-time bias, attrition bias, quantitative/qualitative interaction testing (Gail-Simon)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Phase III, double-blind, randomized (1:1), active-controlled trial vs. standard-of-care EGFR-TKI (gefitinib or erlotinib)
- Population: locally/centrally confirmed EGFRm+ (Ex19del or L858R) locally advanced/metastatic NSCLC, treatment-naive; EGFR mutation status confirmed by cobas EGFR Mutation Test (Roche) at a central lab
- Randomization stratified by mutation type (Ex19del vs. L858R) and race (Asian vs. non-Asian)
- Primary endpoint: PFS (RECIST v1.1, investigator-assessed)
- Key secondary: OS; other secondary: ORR, DoR, DCR, depth of response, PROs (EORTC QLQ-C30/LC13, CTSQ-16)
- Sample size: ~530 patients randomized globally (1:1); primary PFS analysis planned at ~359 progression events, giving 90% power to detect HR=0.71 at a 2-sided 5% significance level (minimum critical HR 0.81)
- Analysis method: stratified log-rank test (Breslow method for ties); HR/CI derived from the log-rank U/V statistics rather than a separately fitted Cox model
- Multiplicity: fixed-sequence hierarchy PFS → OS → CNS PFS at overall 2-sided α=0.05; OS analyzed at two time points (interim at the PFS analysis, final at ~60% maturity / ~318 deaths) using a Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function approximating O'Brien-Fleming

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2018/208065Orig1s008ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (2018, S-008) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/208065s008lbl.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02296125
- Statistical Analysis Plan (Study D5160C00007, Edition 3.0, 28-Feb-2017) — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/25/NCT02296125/SAP_001.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Soria JC, et al. "Osimertinib in Untreated EGFR-Mutated Advanced Non–Small-Cell Lung Cancer." *N Engl J Med.* 2018;378:113-125. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1713137), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29151359/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Osimertinib%20in%20Untreated%20EGFR-Mutated%20Advanced%20Non-Small-Cell%20Lung%20Cancer)

**Other resources**

- AstraZeneca provides IPD access for its sponsored trials via Vivli.org (Data Usage Agreement required); trial-specific FLAURA availability not individually confirmed here.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, from SAP §1.2 "Study design," p.16]*

> "The primary endpoint for this study is PFS (defined by RECIST v1.1), as assessed by the Investigator. Progression free survival has been chosen as a clinically meaningful outcome measure, representing a direct benefit to the patient that is largely unaffected by the effects of subsequent therapy. The sponsor will be assessing OS as a key secondary endpoint recognising that OS is an important objective assessment of clinical benefit, however in this treatment naive population, OS will likely be confounded by the use of subsequent therapies including protocol permitted cross-over."

*[verbatim, from SAP §4.2.2 "Multiple testing strategy," p.39]*

> "In order to provide strong control of the type I error rate, α=0.05 (two-sided), the primary endpoint of PFS, and endpoints of OS and CNS PFS, will be tested in this sequential order. If any previous analysis in the sequence is not statistically significant, the alpha will not be transferred to subsequent analyses...
>
> One analysis of the primary endpoint (PFS) is planned. Two analyses of OS are planned; one interim at the time of PFS and a final analysis. The final OS analysis is planned to be conducted when the OS data is approximately 60% mature (approximately 318 deaths)...
>
> A 2-sided 5% alpha will be used in all testing, with the exception of overall survival endpoint. Since two analyses of OS are planned, the Lan DeMets approach that approximates the O'Brien and Fleming spending function will be used to maintain an overall 2-sided 5% type I error across the two planned analyses of OS."

*[verbatim, from SAP §4.3.8.1 "Primary outcome: progression free survival," p.44]*

> "Progression free survival established from programmatically calculated response...based upon the Investigator assessment for patients in the FAS will be analysed using a log rank test stratified by race (Asian versus Non-Asian) and mutation type (Ex19del versus L858R) for generation of the p-value and using the Breslow approach for handling ties."

### 3. Olaparib (Lynparza) — NDA 208558 (original approval)

**Sponsor:** AstraZeneca Pharmaceuticals LP

**Indication approved:** Maintenance treatment of recurrent epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer in complete/partial response to platinum-based chemotherapy (≥2 prior platinum-containing lines), irrespective of BRCA status

**Approval date:** August 17, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** SOLO-2/ENGOT-Ov21, NCT01874353 (supportive: Study 19, NCT00753545)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, biomarker-selected population (germline BRCA), primary endpoint amended mid-trial (BICR→investigator)
- *Endpoints:* PFS-Inv (primary), PFS2 & OS (hierarchical secondary), HRQoL (FACT-O)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, Kaplan-Meier estimation (Brookmeyer-Crowley CI)
- *Multiplicity:* two-stage hierarchical testing
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* two-stage group-sequential design, Haybittle-Peto boundary (final OS), Bespoke spending function (Stone 2010, PFS2 retest)
- *Missing data/bias:* ascertainment bias, evaluation-time bias, attrition bias, deviation bias sensitivity analyses

**Trial design & endpoints**

- SOLO-2: Phase III, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; olaparib tablets 300 mg BID vs. placebo, in germline-BRCA-mutated, platinum-sensitive relapsed ovarian cancer patients responding to their penultimate platinum regimen (196 olaparib : 99 placebo)
- Randomization stratified by: response to penultimate platinum chemotherapy (6-12 months vs. >12 months), response to last platinum regimen (CR vs. PR), and ethnic descent (Jewish vs. non-Jewish)
- Primary endpoint: investigator-assessed PFS (modified RECIST), ITT population — **amended mid-trial** from BICR-assessed PFS to investigator-assessed PFS by Protocol Amendment 3 (12-Apr-2016), with BICR retained as a supportive analysis
- Secondary endpoints tested statistically (hierarchical): PFS2 (time to second progression), OS; other secondary: HRQoL (FACT-O)
- Type I error: 2.5% (one-sided), tested via two-stage analysis — stage 1 at 192 investigator-assessed PFS events (primary), stage 2 at 60% deaths (OS)
- Pre-specified sensitivity analyses: ascertainment bias (BICR comparison), evaluation-time bias, attrition bias, deviation bias (triggered if >10% of patients had protocol deviations)
- Study 19 (supportive, all-comers not restricted to BRCA-mutated): 80% power to detect HR=0.75, one-sided α=0.2; 137 PFS events from ~250 patients

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2017/208558Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/208558s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (includes the Statistical Review by Stella Karuri / Jason Schroeder, Division of Biometrics) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/208558Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (SOLO-2) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01874353
- Pivotal publication: Pujade-Lauraine E, et al. "Olaparib tablets as maintenance therapy in patients with platinum-sensitive relapsed ovarian cancer and a BRCA1/2 mutation (SOLO2/ENGOT-Ov21): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial." *Lancet Oncol.* 2017;18:1274-1284. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(17)30469-2>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28754483/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Olaparib%20tablets%20as%20maintenance%20therapy%20in%20patients%20with%20platinum-sensitive%20relapsed%20ovarian%20cancer%20and%20a%20BRCA1/2%20mutation)

**Other resources**

- AstraZeneca IPD access via Vivli.org (Data Usage Agreement required).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, from FDA Multi-Discipline Review, "Statistical Analysis Plan / SOLO2" section, p.55]*

> "The ITT and efficacy population for SOLO2 included all randomized patients. PFS-Inv, PFS2 and OS were analyzed via a stratified log-rank test, stratified by time to disease progression in the penultimate platinum treatment (6-12 months, >12 months) and response to last platinum chemotherapy prior to study entry (CR or PR)... The analysis was performed in two stages. The first stage was set to coincide with 192 investigator-assessed PFS events. The second stage was set to coincide with 60% deaths. The primary analysis of PFS-Inv performed at the first stage and the analysis of OS performed at the second stage.
>
> The primary analysis was set to coincide with the occurrence of 192 PFS-Inv events. The specified Type I error rate was set at 2.5% (one-sided)."

*[verbatim, FDA reviewer commentary on protocol conduct, p.55 — a documented deviation from the SAP as executed]*

> "Reviewer comment: Although the FDA agreed to the Sponsor's proposal (in February 2016) to change the primary endpoint from BICR assessment to Investigator assessment, FDA also advised the Sponsor on 3/3/16 that they should still conduct the independent central review of all patient scans to confirm the investigator assessment. FDA further stated that both PFS analyses (by investigator and central review) should be consistent with each other... It was discovered through the course of the NDA review that despite the FDA's advice to the Sponsor regarding the BICR analysis, no further scans were sent for BICR review following investigator assessed progression after April 2016. We performed a sensitivity analysis for PFS, comparing BICR and investigator assessed PFS at the point of protocol change."

*[verbatim, FDA reviewer commentary flagging a secondary endpoint FDA did not accept as regulatory-grade, p.56]*

> "Reviewer comment: It is noted that although PFS2 was one of the secondary endpoints of the trial, as defined by the Sponsor, this is not an endpoint that FDA considers as a valid regulatory endpoint and this endpoint was not considered in the FDA's risk-benefit analysis of this application."

This is a clear example of "how the SAP held up under FDA review": the sponsor's own mid-trial endpoint change was accepted, but FDA's condition attached to that acceptance (keep running BICR in parallel) was not actually followed by the sponsor, which FDA caught and addressed with its own independent sensitivity analysis.

### 4. Enzalutamide (Xtandi) — NDA 203415/S-003

**Sponsor:** Astellas Pharma US, Inc. (co-developed with Medivation)

**Indication approved:** Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), regardless of prior docetaxel exposure (expanded from post-chemotherapy-only)

**Approval date:** September 10, 2014

**Pivotal trial:** PREVAIL, NCT01212991

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, co-primary endpoints
- *Endpoints:* OS + rPFS (co-primary)
- *Primary analysis:* unstratified log-rank test, unstratified Cox proportional-hazards model
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design (pre-specified interim OS analysis) — [inferred] no confirmed spending function; see Reverse-engineered SAP below

**No genuine SAP or protocol is publicly posted for PREVAIL.** NCT01212991 was registered in 2010, before ClinicalTrials.gov's sponsor document-posting norms took hold (these became common industry practice from roughly 2017 onward). No Documents tab entries exist for this trial, and no separate FDA statistical review was found publicly posted for this specific supplement (203415/S-003) — Drugs@FDA lists only the label and approval letter for this action. This entry therefore relies on the approved label and the pivotal NEJM publication, with a reverse-engineered SAP for the analysis details not stated in either.

**Trial design & endpoints** *(from label + publication)*

- Multinational, Phase III, randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled
- Population: chemotherapy-naive mCRPC (N=1717; enzalutamide 160 mg/day PO, N=872 vs. placebo, N=845); patients with visceral metastases and mild-moderate heart failure (NYHA I/II) were allowed; prior seizure history excluded
- Co-primary endpoints: overall survival (OS) and radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS) — rPFS defined by PCWG2 criteria (bone scan, ≥2 new lesions with confirmation) and/or RECIST v1.1 for soft-tissue lesions, with the primary rPFS analysis based on centrally reviewed radiographic assessment
- A pre-specified interim OS analysis was conducted after 540 deaths

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2014/203415Orig1s003ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (2014, S-003) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2014/203415s003lbl.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01212991 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)
- FDA Statistical Review for the *original* 2012 NDA 203415 approval (AFFIRM trial, post-docetaxel indication — different trial, included here only as methodological context for the same sponsor/division's conventions) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203415Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Beer TM, et al. "Enzalutamide in Metastatic Prostate Cancer before Chemotherapy." *N Engl J Med.* 2014;371:424-433. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1405095), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24881730/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Enzalutamide%20in%20Metastatic%20Prostate%20Cancer%20before%20Chemotherapy)

**Other resources**

- Astellas/Pfizer (Xtandi's co-marketer) both participate in Vivli.org; trial-specific IPD availability for PREVAIL not individually confirmed here.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, from the approved Package Insert, Table 4/5 footnotes — the only public description of the actual analysis method used]*

> "P-value is derived from an unstratified log-rank test... Hazard Ratio is derived from an unstratified proportional hazards model."

> "A statistically significant improvement in overall survival was demonstrated at the pre-specified interim analysis, conducted after 540 deaths in patients treated with XTANDI compared to those treated with placebo."

**Reverse-engineered SAP** *(inferred — not genuine PREVAIL SAP text)*

- **Co-primary structure, no stated alpha split** [inferred from: label reports both OS (HR 0.71, p<0.0001) and rPFS (HR 0.17, p<0.0001) each at conventional two-sided significance, with no footnote describing any alpha allocation between them]. This pattern is consistent with a co-primary-endpoint design requiring statistical significance on *each* endpoint independently at the full nominal level, rather than a split-alpha hierarchical test — the design used in the sponsor's earlier AFFIRM trial for its single OS primary endpoint (below) offers no evidence of alpha-splitting practice being extended here to two endpoints, so this remains an inference, not a confirmed fact.
- **Group-sequential interim OS monitoring** [inferred from: the label's "pre-specified interim analysis" language at a specific death count (540), which is the standard vocabulary FDA reviews use for a group-sequential design with a data monitoring committee]. The sponsor's related 2012 AFFIRM trial (same NDA, prior approval, post-docetaxel indication) used an explicit Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function for its OS interim analysis: *"A planned interim analysis was to be performed when 520 deaths (80%) deaths occurred. The interim alpha (αinterim = 0.0244) was determined by a Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function"* (FDA Statistical Review, NDA 203415 original, p.9). PREVAIL's interim OS analysis was very likely governed by an analogous Lan-DeMets/O'Brien-Fleming-type spending rule, but the specific gamma parameter, information fraction, and resulting interim alpha boundary for PREVAIL itself are not publicly available and cannot be reconstructed from the label alone.
- **Unstratified primary analysis despite stratified randomization** [inferred from: the label's footnote explicitly states the primary log-rank test and Cox model were *unstratified*, which is a specific, checkable methodological choice — most Phase III oncology trials of this era used a stratified primary analysis matching randomization strata; the choice to report unstratified results as primary suggests either no formal randomization stratification factors were built into PREVAIL, or the SAP pre-specified the unstratified analysis as primary with stratified analysis as sensitivity — this cannot be resolved without the SAP itself].

### 5. Venetoclax (Venclexta) — NDA 208573/S-013

**Sponsor:** AbbVie Inc. (co-marketed with Genentech/Roche)

**Indication approved:** Venetoclax + obinutuzumab, previously untreated chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) / small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL)

**Approval date:** May 15, 2019

**Pivotal trial:** CLL14 (Roche/AbbVie Protocol BO25323), NCT02242942

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled, fixed-duration regimen, dual primary-endpoint definition (protocol primary vs. US-regulatory primary)
- *Endpoints:* PFS (investigator- and IRC-assessed), MRD response rate, CR rate, ORR, OS
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test (Binet stage), unstratified log-rank test (supportive), stratified Cox proportional-hazards model, Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Multiplicity:* Fallback Procedure (hierarchical secondary testing)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design, gamma-family alpha-spending function

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Phase III, open-label, multicenter, randomized (1:1) trial in previously untreated CLL patients with coexisting medical conditions (CIRS score >6 or CrCl <70 mL/min)
- Arms: fixed-duration venetoclax (12 cycles) + obinutuzumab (6 cycles) vs. obinutuzumab + chlorambucil (12 cycles); N=432
- Randomization stratified by Binet stage
- Primary endpoint (per protocol): investigator-assessed PFS, ITT population, defined as time from randomization to first progression/relapse (iwCLL 2008 criteria) or death from any cause. **IRC-assessed PFS was designated the primary endpoint for US regulatory purposes** (a split between the protocol's stated primary and the FDA-facing primary)
- Key secondary endpoints (hierarchical): IRC-assessed PFS, MRD response rate (bone marrow, ASO-PCR, at end of treatment), investigator-assessed CR rate, MRD response rate (peripheral blood), MRD in patients with CR, ORR, OS
- Sample size: 170 PFS events required for final analysis, giving 80% power to detect HR=0.65 (median PFS improving from 27 to 41.5 months), log-rank test at two-sided 0.05, one interim analysis planned after 75% of PFS events (gamma spending function, γ=-9.21)

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2019/208573Orig1s013ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2019/208573s013lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (Statistical Reviewer: Weishi (Vivian) Yuan, PhD) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/208573Orig1s013MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02242942
- Study Protocol (BO25323, Version 7 — includes the protocol-level "Statistical Considerations and Analysis Plan" section quoted below; the standalone SAP document itself was not separately posted) — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/42/NCT02242942/Prot_001.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Fischer K, et al. "Venetoclax and Obinutuzumab in Patients with CLL and Coexisting Conditions." *N Engl J Med.* 2019;380:2225-2236. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1815281), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31166681/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Venetoclax%20and%20Obinutuzumab%20in%20Patients%20with%20CLL%20and%20Coexisting%20Conditions)

**Other resources**

- Roche/Genentech provides IPD access via Vivli.org (AbbVie's own program should also be checked); trial-specific CLL14 availability not individually confirmed here.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, from Protocol BO25323 v7, §6.4.1 "Primary Efficacy Endpoint," p.124]*

> "The primary efficacy endpoint is investigator-assessed PFS, defined as the time from randomization to the first occurrence of progression or relapse (determined using standard IWCLL guidelines [2008]), or death from any cause, whichever occurs first. Progression-free survival on the basis of independent review committee (IRC) assessments will be considered primary for U.S. regulatory purposes (details will be provided in the SAP)...
>
> Treatment comparisons will be made using a two-sided log-rank test (at 0.05 significance-level, adjusted for the interim analyses), stratified by Binet stage... A two-sided non-stratified log-rank test will be performed to support the primary analysis. Median PFS and the 95% confidence limits will be estimated using Kaplan-Meier survival methodology... Estimates of the treatment effect will be expressed as HR including 95% confidence limits estimated through a Cox proportional-hazards analysis stratified by Binet stage."

*[verbatim, from Protocol BO25323 v7, §6.1 "Determination of Sample Size," p.123]*

> "Estimates of the number of events required to demonstrate efficacy with regard to PFS are based on the following assumptions:
> • Log-rank test at the two-sided 0.05 level of significance
> • Median PFS for obinutuzumab and chlorambucil control arm (27 months)
> • 80% power to detect HR = 0.65 for the comparison of obinutuzumab + venetoclax experimental arm versus GClb, with median PFS for obinutuzumab + venetoclax increased to 41.5 months
> • Exponential distribution of PFS
> • Annual drop-out rate of 10%
> • One interim analysis for efficacy after 75% of PFS events, utilizing a stopping boundary according to the γ family error spending function with parameter γ = −9.21."

*[paraphrased with care — from the FDA Multi-Discipline Review's description of the executed SAP and its amendments, p.31-32; the source PDF's text extraction corrupted Greek letters and some digit strings, so this is summarized rather than quoted verbatim where corruption made exact wording unreliable]* FDA's review documents that a testing hierarchy (Fallback Procedure) controlled overall Type I error across the key secondary endpoints, that the gamma-family alpha-spending approach from the protocol (γ=-9.21) was applied to both investigator- and IRC-assessed PFS, and that the SAP was revised once post-unblinding (first version finalized 26-Sep-2018; v2 dated 08-Nov-2018) to change how patients randomized to VEN+G but who received only obinutuzumab were analyzed — reassigning them to the VEN+G arm by treatment-assigned (ITT) rather than treatment-received logic. The review also notes FDA agreed to MRD as a secondary endpoint and that the sponsor incorporated some, but not all, of FDA's recommendations on the secondary-endpoint testing hierarchy during protocol development.

### 6. Ipilimumab (Yervoy) — BLA 125377

**Sponsor:** Bristol-Myers Squibb Company

**Indication approved:** Unresectable or metastatic melanoma

**Approval date:** March 25, 2011

**Pivotal trial:** MDX010-20 (BMS protocol CA184-002), NCT00094653

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, active-controlled (peptide-vaccine comparator, not placebo), three-arm design, mid-trial primary endpoint change (BORR→OS)
- *Endpoints:* overall survival (OS, primary — amended from best overall response rate), best overall response rate (BORR)/disease control rate (DCR)/duration of response (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified), Kaplan-Meier estimation (Brookmeyer-Crowley CI), Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test (BORR/DCR)
- *Multiplicity:* no pre-specified multiplicity control for secondary OS comparisons (unadjusted p-values)
- *Missing data/bias:* standard right-censoring at last contact/last assessment; ad hoc (non-pre-specified) sensitivity analyses for informative censoring in PFS
- *Regulatory:* Special Protocol Assessment (SPA) withdrawn by FDA after the sponsor's mid-trial primary-endpoint change

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Phase III, randomized, double-blind, multicenter trial in previously treated, unresectable Stage III or IV (HLA-A*0201-positive) melanoma; three arms — ipilimumab 3 mg/kg + gp100 peptide vaccine (n=403), ipilimumab 3 mg/kg monotherapy (n=137), gp100 vaccine monotherapy (n=136) — each dosed every 3 weeks for 4 doses; conducted at 125 centers in 13 countries, September 2004–October 2009
- Randomization stratified by baseline M-stage (M0, M1a or M1b vs. M1c) and prior treatment with interleukin-2 (IL-2)
- Primary endpoint at study start (Amendment #1, before enrollment began) was best overall response rate (BORR); Amendment #6 (dated 1/15/09, roughly six months after the sponsor notified FDA on 7/25/08 of its intent to change) changed the primary endpoint to overall survival (OS), comparing ipilimumab+gp100 vs. gp100 alone — FDA required the study's Special Protocol Assessment to be withdrawn once notified of the planned change, since the trial was "no longer considered a pivotal study for registration" under the original SPA terms
- Secondary comparisons: OS for ipilimumab+gp100 vs. ipilimumab monotherapy, and ipilimumab monotherapy vs. gp100 monotherapy; other secondary endpoints included BORR, disease control rate, duration of response, time to response, and "delayed response" (post-Week-24 response among patients with earlier progression)
- Sample size: prior to Amendment #6, 750 patients (450:150:150) were planned for 90% power to detect a 10% BORR improvement at 2-sided α=0.05; after the endpoint change to OS, the sample size was retained from the original calculation, with the sponsor providing a simulation-based rationale (assuming a delayed treatment effect at 8 months) rather than a fresh power calculation for the new OS endpoint
- Primary analysis: stratified log-rank test (OS, ipilimumab+gp100 vs. gp100), Kaplan-Meier estimation with Brookmeyer-Crowley confidence intervals for medians, Cox proportional-hazards model stratified by baseline M-stage and prior IL-2 for the hazard ratio and its CI; Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test (stratified by the same factors) for BORR/DCR, with Clopper-Pearson confidence intervals
- No statistical procedure was pre-specified in the SAP for adjusting the two secondary OS comparisons for multiplicity, so FDA's review explicitly flags the reported secondary p-values as unadjusted
- No sensitivity analysis for PFS/censoring was pre-specified in the protocol or SAP; both the applicant (at FDA's request) and the FDA reviewer independently constructed post hoc censoring-rule sensitivity analyses

- Package Insert / Label (original approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2011/125377s0000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Yuan-Li Shen, PhD, Division of Biometrics; signed 02/25/2011) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/125377Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/125377Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00094653 (no protocol/SAP documents posted — checked via the ClinicalTrials.gov v2 API `documentSection` field, which is empty for this record)
- Pivotal publication: Hodi FS, O'Day SJ, McDermott DF, et al. "Improved Survival with Ipilimumab in Patients with Metastatic Melanoma." *N Engl J Med.* 2010;363(8):711-723. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1003466), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20525992/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Improved%20survival%20with%20ipilimumab%20in%20patients%20with%20metastatic%20melanoma)

**Other resources**

- Bristol-Myers Squibb makes patient-level data from completed Phase II-IV trials (including MDX010-20, which meets its stated cutoff of trials completed on/after January 1, 2008) available through the Vivli platform under its SOAR™ program, reviewed by an independent committee at Duke Clinical Research Institute; trial-specific MDX010-20 availability was not individually confirmed on Vivli in this pass.
- No FDA advisory committee (ODAC) meeting was identified for this original BLA action in the documents reviewed — unlike vandetanib below, the ipilimumab StatR/SumR text located here contains no reference to an advisory committee meeting.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*Sourcing note: the FDA Statistical Review PDF for this application (`125377Orig1s000StatR.pdf`) is a scanned, partially redacted document with almost no text layer (the underlying text extraction yields only the signature page). The passages below were recovered by OCR (Tesseract, 150dpi page renders) of the same official FDA PDF — they are genuine FDA reviewer text, not paraphrase, but are marked accordingly given the OCR intermediate step; a handful of OCR character-substitution artifacts (e.g., "Tpilimumab" for "Ipilimumab") have been silently corrected for readability without altering wording.*

*[verbatim (OCR'd from scanned original), FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.1, on the mid-trial endpoint change]*

> "Amendment #6 (dated 1/15/09): The primary endpoint was changed from BORR to overall survival (OS). The primary comparison was the same as that in earlier amendment (i.e. between ipilimumab in combination with gp100 vs. gp100 arm). However, the secondary comparisons were now between ipilimumab monotherapy vs. gp100 and between two ipilimumab containing arms. The sample size was revised based on the new primary efficacy endpoint, assuming delay effect at 8 months based on simulation methods.
>
> Reviewer's comments: The applicant notified FDA that the primary efficacy endpoint would be changed from BORR to OS in a teleconference on 7/25/08. At that time, FDA requested that the SPA (Special Protocol Assessment) to be withdrawn for MDX010-20 since it is no longer considered a pivotal study for registration. Approximately 6 months later the protocol was revised (dated on 1/15/09). The data cutoff date was 6/19/09, the statistical analysis was signed off on 10/28/09 and the data were unblinded on 10/30/09."

*[verbatim (OCR'd), FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.4, on the primary analysis method]*

> "The primary analysis for all time-to-event endpoints was based on a stratified log-rank test stratified by the baseline stratification factors (i.e. baseline M-stage [M0, M1a or M1b vs. M1c] and prior treatment with IL-2 or not). The Kaplan-Meier method was used to plot the survival estimates for OS. The median OS and its 95% confidence interval were calculated using the method of Brookmeyer and Crowley. The hazard ratio and the corresponding 2-sided confidence intervals were estimated using the Cox's proportional hazards model stratified by baseline M-stage and prior treatment IL-2."

*[verbatim (OCR'd), FDA Statistical Review, on secondary-endpoint multiplicity, immediately following the OS results tables]*

> "Note that a statistical procedure was not pre-specified for adjusting multiple secondary comparisons in the Statistical Analysis Plan, thus, p-values in Table 2 for the secondary comparisons were not adjusted."

*[verbatim (OCR'd), FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.4, on ad hoc PFS sensitivity analyses]*

> "No pre-specified sensitivity analysis was proposed in the statistical analysis plan or in the protocol. However, a sensitivity analysis was performed both by the applicant (per FDA's request) and the reviewer by censoring patients in the following situations: a. at time of the last assessment before patients discontinued treatment for toxicity or other reason prior to progression; b. at the time of the last assessment before patients took anti-cancer treatment prior to progression; c. at the time of the last assessment before patients died or progressed after more than one missed assessment visit."

*[verbatim, from the approved Package Insert, Table 3 footnote — the only description of the multiplicity handling that made it into the label itself]*

> "Not adjusted for multiple comparisons."

The label's Table 3 reports the primary result (OS, ipilimumab+gp100 vs. gp100: HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.55-0.85, footnoted p=0.0004 "not adjusted for multiple comparisons") alongside the two unadjusted secondary comparisons (ipilimumab vs. gp100: HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.51-0.87; ipilimumab+gp100 vs. ipilimumab: HR 1.04, 95% CI 0.83-1.30) — consistent with, and traceable directly to, the FDA reviewer's statement that no multiplicity procedure was pre-specified for these comparisons.

### 7. Vandetanib (Caprelsa) — NDA 022405

**Sponsor:** AstraZeneca Pharmaceuticals LP (authorized US agent for iPR Pharmaceuticals, Inc.)

**Indication approved:** Symptomatic or progressive medullary thyroid cancer (MTC) in patients with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic disease

**Approval date:** April 6, 2011

**Pivotal trial:** ZETA (AstraZeneca/Genzyme Study D4200C00058, "Study 58"), NCT00410761

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover to open-label permitted at progression, co-primary RET-mutation subgroup population dropped by protocol amendment, FDA Advisory Committee meeting held
- *Endpoints:* progression-free survival (PFS, IRC/central-review-assessed, primary), objective response rate (ORR)/disease control rate (DCR)/duration of response (secondary), overall survival (OS, secondary, interim-only at approval), biochemical response (calcitonin/CEA), time to worsening of pain (patient-reported)
- *Primary analysis:* log-rank test (applicant), Cox proportional-hazards model (FDA-derived HR and CI), Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Multiplicity:* no pre-specified multiplicity control for secondary endpoints (unadjusted p-values; FDA states these are not interpretable)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function approximating an O'Brien-Fleming boundary for the planned final OS analysis (at 50% deaths); sponsor and FDA computed different interim-look alpha values from the same spending function
- *Missing data/bias:* standard right-censoring at last evaluable central-read RECIST assessment; FDA vs. sponsor disagreement over PFS censoring rules (informative-censoring dispute involving IRC-vs-investigator-assessed progression, radiotherapy, and baseline-measurability censoring)
- *Regulatory:* FDA Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting held; FDA-conducted independent reanalysis of the primary endpoint using different censoring rules than the sponsor's submitted analysis

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Phase III, multicenter, international, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in unresectable locally advanced or metastatic, hereditary or sporadic MTC; vandetanib 300 mg once daily (n=231) vs. matched placebo (n=100), continuing until objective disease progression; enrolled at 60 centers in 23 countries, first patient in November 2006, data cutoff July 31, 2009
- Randomization was stratified by site in blocks of 3 (not by a clinical prognostic factor); actual enrollment (231:100, a ratio >2:1) reflected imbalanced incomplete blocks rather than a protocol deviation, per FDA's review
- Primary endpoint: PFS by independent (central) radiology review, RECIST-based with two protocol-specified modifications (a calcification correction and retrospective baseline reclassification of certain liver lesions); patients without progression/death at analysis were censored at their last evaluable central-read assessment
- Study originally planned two co-primary PFS analyses — one in all patients, one restricted to patients with a confirmed RET mutation (assumed ~50% of enrollees) — but the RET-mutation co-primary population was removed by Protocol Amendment 5 (18-May-2009) after the mutation-status assay failed to classify 41% of patients
- Secondary endpoints: ORR and DCR by central review, duration of response, overall survival, biochemical response (calcitonin and CEA normalization/decline criteria); time to worsening of pain (a composite of opioid use and Brief Pain Inventory score) was a patient-reported outcome endpoint that FDA's review treated as exploratory given unresolved blinding-integrity concerns
- Sample size: powered for PFS only (90 events needed for >80% power to detect a doubling of median PFS at 2-sided α=0.05, assuming 12-month control-arm median PFS); the study was explicitly "not powered for OS"
- No interim analysis was planned or performed for PFS. A single planned final OS analysis was designed for 50% of enrolled patients (166) deaths, using a Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function approximating an O'Brien-Fleming boundary; the July 31, 2009 data cutoff (only 48 deaths, 15% of patients) was treated by FDA's review as an interim look against that spending function, at which the recomputed alpha was 0.00007 (FDA) vs. 0.0002 (sponsor) — OS was not statistically significant at this cutoff (HR 0.893, 95% CI 0.490-1.629, log-rank p=0.7131)
- FDA's review documents ten distinct "Statistical Issues," including that no adjustment was made for multiple secondary-endpoint testing (so secondary p-values "are not interpretable"), that the applicant derived the PFS hazard ratio/CI from the log-rank test while FDA instead used a Cox proportional-hazards model, and three specific censoring-rule differences between the applicant's and FDA's PFS analyses (handling of investigator-only progression, on-study radiotherapy, and no-baseline-measurable-disease patients)
- The application was reviewed by the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) on December 2, 2010; the committee voted unanimously to require a post-marketing dose-optimization study, and the drug was ultimately approved with a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) restricting distribution given QT-prolongation/torsade de pointes and sudden-death signals in the wider safety database

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2011/022405s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (original approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2011/022405s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Somesh Chattopadhyay, PhD, primary review dated 12/16/2010, with a subsequent addendum) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/022405Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/022405Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00410761 (registered by AstraZeneca, now shown under Sanofi following its later acquisition of vandetanib's rights; no protocol/SAP documents posted — checked via the ClinicalTrials.gov v2 API `documentSection` field, which is empty for this record)
- Pivotal publication: Wells SA Jr, Robinson BG, Gagel RF, et al. "Vandetanib in Patients with Locally Advanced or Metastatic Medullary Thyroid Cancer: A Randomized, Double-Blind Phase III Trial." *J Clin Oncol.* 2012;30(2):134-141. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.2011.35.5040), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22025146/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Vandetanib%20in%20patients%20with%20locally%20advanced%20or%20metastatic%20medullary%20thyroid%20cancer%3A%20a%20randomized%2C%20double-blind%20phase%20III%20trial)

**Other resources**

- AstraZeneca provides IPD access for its sponsored trials via Vivli.org (Data Usage Agreement required); trial-specific ZETA/D4200C00058 availability was not individually confirmed in this pass, and the trial's later transfer to Sanofi/Genzyme (visible in the current ClinicalTrials.gov record's sponsor field) adds ambiguity about which company's data-sharing program would actually govern a request.
- An FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held on December 2, 2010, which voted unanimously to require a post-marketing dose-ranging study rather than recommending against approval outright.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Executive Summary]*

> "The applicant has submitted results from one multicenter, phase III, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (Study D4200C00058) comparing vandetanib to placebo in patients with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic medullary thyroid cancer (MTC). The vandetanib arm showed statistically significant improvement over placebo in progression-free survival (PFS) as assessed by independent central radiology review in all randomized patients. However, the vandetanib arm did not show statistically significant improvement with respect to overall survival (OS) at the time of the final PFS analysis."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §1.3 "Statistical Issues and Findings," items 2, 8, and 9]*

> "2. The censoring rules of FDA and the applicant were different for primary PFS analysis based on IRC review... PFS for the patients with investigator-determined, but without IRC determined progression have been censored at their last RECIST assessment prior to discontinuation of study drug for FDA's analysis. The applicant's analysis of PFS used the IRC assessment beyond investigator assessed progression and study drug discontinuation in these cases. While the sponsor's analysis may address informative censoring and conform to ITT analysis, this analysis includes effect of non-protocol treatment beyond investigator determined progression...
>
> 8. The applicant derived the hazard ratio estimate and its confidence interval based on the results from the log-rank test whereas FDA used the Cox proportional hazards model to derive these numbers.
>
> 9. Type I error rate has not been adjusted for analysis of multiple secondary endpoints. Therefore, p-values for the secondary endpoints are not interpretable."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.1.5 "Sample Size Considerations," reviewer's comment]*

> "The study was originally planned to have two co-primary analyses to compare PFS between the two treatment arms in all patients who received at least one dose of vandetanib/placebo and in patients who had RET mutation and received at least one dose of vandetanib/placebo... However, the co-primary analysis population of patients with a known RET mutation was removed from the study in protocol amendment 5 (18 May 2009) because assays used to identify RET mutation were unable to establish mutation status in 41% of the patients."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.1.8.5 "Secondary Efficacy Analyses," on the OS interim look and alpha-spending discrepancy]*

> "The analysis of secondary endpoint OS in FAS based on the data with cut-off dates July 31, 2009, which is considered as an interim analysis of OS, is presented in Table 10. There were only 48 deaths as of July 31, 2009 cut-off date. The final OS analysis will be conducted after 50% of the enrolled patients (166) die. Although the study was not powered for OS, Lan-DeMets alpha spending function has been used to adjust for multiple OS analysis... According to the Lan-DeMets alpha spending function for O'Brien-Fleming boundary, the alpha for the interim OS analysis would be 0.00007... [Reviewer's comment:] alpha spent at the interim OS analysis should be 0.00007 (calculated using East Version 5). The applicant noted this number as 0.0002."

*[verbatim, from the approved Package Insert, §14 "Clinical Studies"]*

> "The result of the PFS analysis, based on the central review RECIST assessment, showed a statistically significant improvement in PFS for patients randomized to CAPRELSA (Hazard Ratio = 0.35; 95% Confidence Interval (CI) = 0.24-0.53; p<0.0001)... At the time of the primary analysis of PFS, 15% of the patients had died and there was no significant difference in overall survival between the two treatment groups."

The label's Table 3 footnotes the PFS result as based on a "Cox Proportional Hazards Model" for the hazard ratio and a "Logrank test" for the p-value — the same HR/p-value split (Cox model for effect size, log-rank for significance) that the FDA Statistical Review documents as its own preferred approach, distinct from the applicant's log-rank-derived HR noted in Statistical Issue #8 above.

### 8. Abiraterone acetate (Zytiga) — NDA 202379 (original approval)

**Sponsor:** Centocor Ortho Biotech, Inc. (Ortho Biotech Oncology Research & Development, a unit of Cougar Biotechnology, Inc.; now Janssen Biotech, Inc., a Johnson & Johnson company)

**Indication approved:** ZYTIGA in combination with prednisone for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) in patients who have received prior chemotherapy containing docetaxel

**Approval date:** April 28, 2011

**Pivotal trial:** COU-AA-301, NCT00638690

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven trial
- *Endpoints:* overall survival (OS, primary), radiographic progression-free survival (secondary), time to PSA progression (secondary), objective response rate (other)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified or with covariates), Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Multiplicity:* Hochberg step-up procedure (secondary endpoints)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design, O'Brien-Fleming boundary, Data Monitoring Committee (DMC/DSMB) (IDMC)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Phase III, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, multinational trial in men with metastatic CRPC who had failed docetaxel-based chemotherapy; 1,195 subjects randomized to abiraterone acetate 1,000 mg/day plus prednisone 5 mg BID (N=797) vs. placebo plus prednisone 5 mg BID (N=398), at 147 sites in North America, Europe, and Australia
- Randomization conducted via centralized Interactive Web Response System (IWRS), stratified by four factors: baseline ECOG performance status (0-1 vs. 2), baseline pain (presence vs. absence), number of prior cytotoxic chemotherapy regimens (1 vs. 2), and documented type of disease progression at entry (PSA-only vs. radiographic)
- Primary endpoint: overall survival (OS), time from randomization to death from any cause, censored at last known-alive date or data cutoff
- Secondary endpoints (type I error controlled via Hochberg procedure): time to PSA progression (PSAWG criteria), radiographic progression-free survival, proportion with ≥50% PSA decline; other endpoints (no error control): objective response rate, pain palliation, time to skeletal-related event, circulating tumor cell decline, FACT-P functional status — FDA's reviewer noted the secondary endpoints were excluded from labeling "due to concerns on the validity and clinical interpretation of their assessment" despite the Hochberg control
- Sample size: 1,158 subjects planned to accrue 797 death events, giving 85% power to detect a HR of 0.80 (a 20% hazard reduction, ~3-month median-survival increase) at a two-sided 5% alpha; 13-month accrual period assumed
- Analysis population: Intention-to-Treat (ITT, all randomized subjects), the primary population for all efficacy analyses
- Analysis methods: OS compared via stratified log-rank test (same four IWRS stratification factors); HR and 95% CI from a Cox proportional-hazards model stratified by the same factors; Kaplan-Meier survival curves; sensitivity analyses included an eCRF-stratified log-rank test, an unstratified log-rank test, an analysis excluding major protocol deviators, and an FDA reviewer-run worst-case analysis
- Interim analysis: pre-planned interim superiority analysis of OS after 534 deaths (67% information), using an O'Brien-Fleming alpha-spending function (interim alpha 0.0124, final alpha 0.0462 planned); the IDMC actually reviewed the analysis at 552 deaths (nominal two-sided significance level 0.0141 per the spending function), found p<0.0001, concluded the efficacy boundary had been crossed, and recommended unblinding — the study was then amended (Amendment #3) to let placebo-arm subjects cross over to abiraterone
- FDA noted 203 subjects had inconsistent stratification-factor data between the eCRF and IWRS systems; the primary OS analysis used the IWRS-recorded strata, with an eCRF-stratified analysis run as a sensitivity check (consistent results, HR 0.653 vs. 0.646 for the primary analysis)

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2011/202379s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (2011, original approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2011/202379lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Lijun Zhang, PhD, Division of Biometrics 5) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/202379Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/202379Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00638690 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)
- Pivotal publication: de Bono JS, et al. "Abiraterone and increased survival in metastatic prostate cancer." *N Engl J Med.* 2011;364(21):1995-2005. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1014618), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21612468/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Abiraterone%20and%20increased%20survival%20in%20metastatic%20prostate%20cancer)

**Other resources**

- Johnson & Johnson (Janssen)/the sponsor participates in the YODA Project (Yale University Open Data Access, yoda.yale.edu) for external investigator data requests across its Phase-not-1 interventional trials; trial-specific COU-AA-301 IPD availability was not individually confirmed in this pass and should be checked on the YODA site directly.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held; the approval letter states the application "was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary; there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, from FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.1.1-3.2.1.2 "Overall Study Design" / "Sample Size Determination," p.7]*

> "The pivotal trial, COU-AA-301, is a Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of abiraterone acetate plus prednisone in subjects with metastatic CRPC who have failed docetaxel-based chemotherapy. A total of 1,195 subjects were randomized at a 2:1 ratio to receive 4 X 250-mg tablets of abiraterone acetate or matching placebo for treatment arm and placebo arm, respectively... The randomization was conducted using a centralized Interactive Web Response System (IWRS) based on four stratification factors: baseline ECOG performance status (0-1 versus 2), baseline pain (presence versus absence), number of prior cytotoxic chemotherapy regimens (1 versus 2), and documented type of prostate cancer progression at entry (PSA progression only versus radiographic progression in bone or soft tissue with or without PSA progression).
>
> Assuming the median survival time in the placebo group was 12 months, a sample size of 1,158 subjects was calculated for the study to have 797 death events needed to detect a 20% reduction in hazard rate (a HR of 0.80; or equivalent, a 3-month increase in median survival) in the abiraterone acetate group relative to the placebo group with a power of 85% at a 2-sided 5% alpha level."

*[verbatim, from FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.1.5 "Analysis Methods," p.7-8]*

> "OS was compared between the two treatment groups in the ITT population using the stratified log-rank test with stratification factors at randomization from IWRS... The hazard ratio and corresponding 95% confidence interval were estimated using the Cox proportional hazards model stratified by the same stratification factors as those used for the log-rank test... the secondary endpoints such as radiographic progression-free survival, and time-to-PSA progression were compared between the two treatment groups by stratified log-rank test... The type I error rate for these three secondary efficacy endpoints was controlled using Hochberg test procedure. No type I error adjustments for other exploratory efficacy endpoints were planned.
>
> Reviewer's comments: Though the Hochberg test procedure was used to control the overall type I error rate, the secondary endpoints will not be included in labeling due to concerns on the validity and clinical interpretation of their assessment."

*[verbatim, from FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.1.6 "Interim Analysis," p.8]*

> "Study COU-AA-301 had a pre-planned interim superiority analysis of OS after occurrence of 534 deaths (67% information) with the O'Brien-Fleming type I error spending function for alpha adjustment (alpha for the interim analysis = 0.0124; alpha for the final analysis = 0.0462). The IDMC reviewed the OS interim analysis of 552 deaths in August 2010. The nominal significance level for the interim analysis with 552 deaths was 0.0141 (two-sided) using the O'Brien-Fleming spending function. Given an observed p-value of <0.0001, the IDMC concluded that the prespecified efficacy boundary had been crossed and there was a significant OS improvement in favor of abiraterone acetate treatment. The IDMC recommended that the blinded portion of the study be terminated. The study COU-AA-301 was then amended (Amendment #3) to allow subjects in the placebo group to receive abiraterone acetate treatment."

*[verbatim, from the approved Package Insert, Table 3 footnotes]*

> "P-value is derived from a log-rank test stratified by ECOG performance status score (0-1 vs. 2), pain score (absent vs. present), number of prior chemotherapy regimens (1 vs. 2), and type of disease progression (PSA only vs. radiographic)... Hazard Ratio is derived from a stratified proportional hazards model. Hazard ratio <1 favors ZYTIGA."

### 9. Vemurafenib (Zelboraf) — NDA 202429 (original approval)

**Sponsor:** Hoffmann-La Roche Inc. / Genentech, Inc. (Roche group)

**Indication approved:** ZELBORAF for unresectable or metastatic melanoma with BRAF V600E mutation as detected by an FDA-approved test (co-approved companion diagnostic: cobas 4800 BRAF V600 Mutation Test, Roche Molecular Systems, Inc.); limitation of use: not recommended for BRAF wild-type melanoma

**Approval date:** August 17, 2011

**Pivotal trial:** BRIM-3 (Roche/Genentech Study NO25026), NCT01006980

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled, co-primary endpoints, mid-trial SAP amendment changing endpoint status, crossover permitted at progression
- *Endpoints:* overall survival + progression-free survival (co-primary), best overall response rate/duration of response (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* unstratified log-rank test, stratified log-rank test (sensitivity), Cox proportional-hazards model, Kaplan-Meier estimation, Brookmeyer-Crowley method
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design, Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function (Pocock-type boundary, amended from O'Brien-Fleming-type), Data Monitoring Committee (DMC/DSMB)
- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented mid-trial endpoint elevation (FDA feedback-driven), companion diagnostic co-approval

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Phase III, randomized (1:1), open-label, dacarbazine (DTIC)-controlled, multicenter, international trial (Study NO25026/BRIM-3) in previously untreated patients with histologically confirmed metastatic (unresectable Stage IIIC or Stage IV) melanoma harboring the BRAF V600 mutation, as determined by the cobas 4800 BRAF V600 Mutation Test; 675 patients randomized (337 vemurafenib 960 mg PO BID vs. 338 dacarbazine 1000 mg/m² IV q3w) between January 4, 2010 and December 16, 2010, at 104 centers in 12 countries
- Randomization stratified by disease stage (unresectable Stage IIIC vs. M1a vs. M1b vs. M1c), LDH (normal vs. elevated), and ECOG performance status (0 vs. 1)
- **Original protocol (dated Sept 1, 2009) specified OS as the sole primary endpoint**, powered assuming HR 0.75 (median survival 10.7 vs. 8 months), requiring 468 deaths from 680 patients for 80% power at a two-sided alpha of 0.025, with two interim OS analyses planned at 50% and 75% information — the design was substantially changed before the interim analysis by Protocol Amendment C (first implemented November 1, 2010), agreed between sponsor and FDA following communications about early Phase 1/2 efficacy signals suggesting the original design underestimated vemurafenib's effect: PFS was added as a co-primary endpoint, overall two-sided alpha was increased from 0.025 to 0.05 (allocated 0.045 to OS and 0.005 to PFS), the target OS hazard ratio was revised to 0.65 (reducing the required deaths from 468 to ~196), the second (75%-information) OS interim analysis was dropped, the sole remaining OS interim analysis was moved to coincide with the final PFS analysis, and the interim-analysis alpha-spending boundary was switched from an O'Brien-Fleming-type function (interim alpha 0.0008 under the old 0.025 design) to a Pocock-type Lan-DeMets function (interim alpha 0.028 under the new 0.045 design) — a much more permissive early-look boundary
- Co-primary endpoints (as amended): overall survival (time from randomization to death from any cause) and investigator-assessed progression-free survival (time from randomization to disease progression by tumor assessment or death); secondary/key endpoints: best overall response rate (IRC-assessed, complete or partial response), duration of response, time to response
- Sample size (as amended): ~196 deaths for 80% power to detect OS HR 0.65 at two-sided alpha 0.045; 187 PFS events for 90% power to detect PFS HR 0.55 at two-sided alpha 0.005 (no interim analysis planned for PFS)
- Primary analysis method: unstratified log-rank test for both OS and PFS; HR and 95% CI from a Cox regression model; median survival/PFS and 95% CI from Kaplan-Meier estimation using the Brookmeyer-Crowley method; stratified log-rank/Cox analyses (by disease stage, LDH, ECOG) run as sensitivity analyses, showing consistent results
- Amendment C also allowed DTIC-arm patients to cross over to vemurafenib if the interim OS analysis p-value was <0.05; at the single interim analysis (data cutoff December 30, 2010; 118 deaths, 43 vemurafenib vs. 75 dacarbazine), the unstratified log-rank p-value was <0.0001 against a Pocock-boundary alpha allocation of 0.032 — comfortably crossing the efficacy boundary — and the DSMB recommended stopping the blinded comparison and allowing crossover

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2011/202429Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (2011, original approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2011/202429s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Qiang Xu, PhD, Division of Biometrics V) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/202429Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/202429Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01006980 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)
- Pivotal publication: Chapman PB, et al. "Improved survival with vemurafenib in melanoma with BRAF V600E mutation." *N Engl J Med.* 2011;364(26):2507-2516. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1103782), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21639808/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Improved%20survival%20with%20vemurafenib%20in%20melanoma%20with%20BRAF%20V600E%20mutation)
- FDA Approval Summary (peer-reviewed account of the review, including the companion-diagnostic co-development): Kim G, et al. "FDA Approval Summary: Vemurafenib for Treatment of Unresectable or Metastatic Melanoma with the BRAFV600E Mutation." *Clin Cancer Res.* 2014;20(19):4994-5000. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-14-0776), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25096067/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=FDA%20Approval%20Summary%3A%20Vemurafenib%20for%20Treatment%20of%20Unresectable%20or%20Metastatic%20Melanoma%20with%20the%20BRAFV600E%20Mutation)

**Other resources**

- Roche has shared BRIM-3 (Study NO25026) patient-level data through the Vivli platform (vivli.org) — a Vivli-published methods note ("Combining data from expanded access programs and conventional clinical trials: a statistical application to vemurafenib") specifically references this trial's data being used this way, so trial-specific availability is better-confirmed here than in most entries in this census, though a fresh data request would still need to go through Vivli's request/review process.
- **Notable regulatory feature**: this was one of the first oncology approvals built around a simultaneous companion-diagnostic co-approval — the cobas 4800 BRAF V600 Mutation Test (a separate PMA reviewed by CDRH) was approved concurrently to select patients for the drug, and the trial itself enrolled only patients testing positive by that assay. No FDA advisory committee (ODAC) meeting was held for the NDA; the approval letter states the application "was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the benefit/risk profile of Zelboraf (vemurafenib) Tablet is clearly favorable for the proposed indication."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, from FDA Statistical Review, "Regulatory Communications and Related Amendments in Study NO25026," p.4-5]*

> "The original protocol of Study NO25026 (dated Sep 1, 2009) was powered for the sole primary endpoint of OS. Assuming that the hazard ratio of OS between the vemurafenib group and the DTIC group was 0.75 (median survival 10.7 vs. 8 months), a total of 468 deaths from 680 patients were required to provide 80% power at a two-sided significant level of 0.025. Two interim OS analyses were planned, each at 50% and 75% of the total information, respectively.
>
> Positive efficacy results from Phase 1 and 2 studies of vemurafenib triggered a series communications between the applicant and the Agency, in which a possible underestimation of the efficacy of vemurafenib in the original design of Study NO25026 was discussed. Subsequently, the sponsor, concurred by the Agency, changed the protocol and added Amendment C (first implemented Nov 1, 2010). The major changes in Amendment C were as follows:
> • Added PFS as a co-primary endpoint, and increased the two-sided alpha level for the study from 0.025 to 0.05 (0.045 for OS and 0.005 for PFS)
> • Decreased the expected OS hazard ratio from 0.75 to 0.65, leading to a reduction in the required number of deaths from 468 to approximately 196
> • Scheduled the final PFS analysis at the time of OS interim analysis at 50% of the total number of deaths
> • Removed the OS interim analysis at 75% of the total deaths
> • Alpha allocated for the interim OS analysis was changed from 0.0008 (O'Brien-Fleming alpha spending boundary based on the old design setting with alpha level of 0.025) to 0.028 (Pocock alpha spending boundary based on the new design setting with alpha level of 0.045)
> • Allowed patients on DTIC to cross over to vemurafenib if the p-value of the interim OS analysis was less than 0.05"

*[verbatim, from FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.1.2 "Statistical Analysis Plan," p.7-8]*

> "Analyses reported in the applicant's CSR followed SAP dated Nov 4, 2010, which incorporated Amendment C as noted in Section 2.1... Approximately 680 patients were planned to be randomized to receive either vemurafenib or DTIC. A total of 196 deaths were required to provide 80% power to detect a hazard ratio of 0.65 comparing vemurafenib to dacarbazine (median survival 12.3 vs. 8 months) at type I error of 0.045 (two-sided). One interim analysis was scheduled at 50% information. Lan-DeMets alpha spending method of the Pocock type boundary was employed to control the alpha level, and statistical significance for OS would be claimed at the interim analysis if the log-rank p-value (two-sided) was ≤ 0.028.
>
> A total of 187 PFS events were required to provide 90% power to detect a hazard ratio of 0.55 for vemurafenib relative to DTIC (median PFS 4.5 vs. 2.5 months) at type I error of 0.005 (two-sided). No interim analysis was planned for PFS... The primary analysis of OS was a comparison of the two treatment groups using an unstratified log-rank test. The OS hazard ratio and the associated 95% CI were computed using a Cox regression model. Median OS was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, with 95% CI calculated using the method of Brookmeyer and Crowley."

*[verbatim, from FDA Statistical Review, efficacy-results/reviewer-comment section, p.12]*

> "Unstratified log-rank test of OS demonstrated a statistically significant difference in the duration of survival favoring the vemurafenib group (p < 0.0001, the actual alpha allocation for this interim analysis was 0.032 by the Pocock alpha spending boundary)... Reviewer's Comments: If the O'Brien-Fleming Boundary had been used for the interim OS analysis in the revised SAP, the p-value of the unstratified log-rank test would also have crossed the significant level of 0.006 at the observed information based on the required total number of deaths."

This last reviewer comment is a notable "how the SAP held up under FDA review" point: the mid-trial switch from an O'Brien-Fleming-type to a Pocock-type spending function made the boundary far easier to cross at an early interim look, but FDA's own check showed the trial's effect size was so large (unstratified log-rank p<0.0001) that it would have cleared the original, more conservative boundary too — i.e., the amendment changed how early the trial could stop, not whether the result was genuine.

*[verbatim, from the approved Package Insert, Table 4, "Efficacy of ZELBORAF in Treatment Naive Patients with BRAFV600E Mutation-Positive Melanoma," footnotes]*

> "Hazard ratio estimated using Cox model; a hazard ratio of < 1 favors ZELBORAF... Unstratified log-rank test."

The label's Table 4 (based on a later data cutoff than the interim analysis reviewed in the FDA Statistical Review) reports OS HR 0.44 (95% CI 0.33-0.59, unstratified log-rank p<0.0001; 78 vemurafenib deaths vs. 121 dacarbazine deaths) and PFS HR 0.26 (95% CI 0.20-0.33, p<0.0001) — a more mature, lower HR than the StatR's interim-analysis OS HR of 0.37, consistent with the additional follow-up and crossover pattern described above.
