### 10. Brentuximab vedotin (Adcetris) — BLA 125388

**Sponsor:** Seattle Genetics, Inc. (now Seagen, acquired by Pfizer in 2023)

**Indication approved:** (1) Hodgkin lymphoma after failure of autologous stem cell transplant (ASCT) or after failure of at least two prior multi-agent chemotherapy regimens in patients who are not ASCT candidates; and (2) systemic anaplastic large cell lymphoma (sALCL) after failure of at least one prior multi-agent chemotherapy regimen

**Approval date:** August 19, 2011 (accelerated approval)

**Pivotal trial:** SG035-0003 (Hodgkin lymphoma), NCT00848926; SG035-0004 (systemic ALCL), NCT00866047

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm trial, open-label, multicenter, two separate single-arm Phase 2 pivotal trials supporting two indications reviewed together (biomarker-defined population, CD30-positive lymphoma confirmed by central pathology review)
- *Endpoints:* ORR as sole primary endpoint (independent review facility-assessed), duration of response (secondary), complete remission (CR) rate (secondary), progression-free survival and overall survival (exploratory/descriptive)
- *Primary analysis:* Clopper-Pearson exact CI (two-sided 95% exact binomial CI), Kaplan-Meier estimation (duration of response, PFS, OS)
- *Missing data/bias:* IRF-investigator concordance analysis (kappa statistic) — an ORR-assessment analogue of this taxonomy's ascertainment-bias-assessment concept, comparing independent-review vs. investigator response calls rather than progression timing
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval based on ORR from two single-arm trials, FDA Advisory Committee meeting held (ODAC, 10-0 vote for both indications), two postmarketing confirmatory Phase 3 trials required as a condition of approval, two BLAs (125388 for Hodgkin lymphoma, 125399 for sALCL) approved together via a single joint action letter

**Trial design & endpoints**

- SG035-0003: open-label, multicenter, single-arm Phase 2 trial in 102 patients with CD30-positive (central pathology-confirmed) Hodgkin lymphoma that relapsed after auto-SCT; brentuximab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks for up to 16 cycles
- SG035-0004: open-label, multicenter, single-arm Phase 2 trial in 58 patients with relapsed/refractory systemic ALCL (72% ALK-negative), same dose/schedule
- Primary endpoint in both trials: objective response rate (ORR = complete remission [CR] + partial remission [PR]) assessed by an independent review facility (IRF), using the 2007 Revised Response Criteria for Malignant Lymphoma (modified)
- Secondary/supportive endpoints: duration of response, CR rate, progression-free survival, overall survival; investigator-assessed response was also collected as a protocol-defined exploratory analysis with IRF-investigator concordance measured via a kappa coefficient (SG035-0003)
- Sample size (SG035-0003, per the pivotal publication): 100 patients planned; with n=100, an observed ORR of 29% would allow exclusion of a ≤20% response-rate floor with 95% confidence — i.e., the trial was sized against a historical-control response-rate benchmark rather than powered for a formal hypothesis test against a comparator arm
- No interim analysis or group-sequential monitoring was used in either trial (single-stage, fixed-sample single-arm Phase 2 designs)
- Statistical method: ORR and its two-sided 95% exact confidence interval (Clopper-Pearson-type exact binomial CI); Kaplan-Meier method for duration of response, PFS, and OS

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter (joint BLA 125388/BLA 125399 action) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2011/125388s000,125399s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (2011, original approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2011/125388s000,125399s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/125388Orig1s000StatR.pdf (posted PDF is a "Best Available Copy" scan; the only legible content is a blank statistics filing checklist form — no reviewer analysis text is recoverable)
- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/125388Orig1s000SumR.pdf (posted PDF is almost entirely redacted as confidential commercial information, marked "(b)(4)" throughout)
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (SG035-0003) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00848926 (no protocol/SAP documents posted; trial predates ClinicalTrials.gov's routine document-posting era)
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (SG035-0004) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00866047 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)
- Pivotal publication (Hodgkin lymphoma): Younes A, et al. **Other resources**

- Seagen historically did not participate in Vivli or YODA in a way independently confirmed here; as part of Pfizer since 2023, legacy Adcetris trial data may fall under Pfizer's Vivli program, but trial-specific IPD availability for SG035-0003/SG035-0004 was not individually confirmed in this pass.
- This was an accelerated approval under 21 CFR 601.40-46 (biologics accelerated-approval regulations) based on ORR alone; the label states plainly: "These indications are based on response rate. There are no data available demonstrating improvement in patient reported outcomes or survival with ADCETRIS."
- An FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held July 14, 2011, considering the Hodgkin lymphoma indication (BLA 125388) in the morning session and the sALCL indication (BLA 125399) in the afternoon session; ODAC voted 10-0 to recommend accelerated approval for each.
- Two postmarketing confirmatory trials were required as a condition of accelerated approval (see verbatim excerpt below); both later matured into the well-known frontline trials ECHELON-1 (Hodgkin lymphoma, AVD vs. ABVD) and ECHELON-2 (CD30-positive mature T-/NK-cell lymphomas including sALCL, CH-P vs. CHOP).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, from the pivotal publication, Younes et al. 2012, "Statistical Analysis" section]*

> "The primary end point of this pivotal study was the ORR per IRF. Secondary end points included duration of response by IRF, complete remission (CR) rate by IRF, and progression-free survival (PFS) by IRF, as well as overall survival (OS) and the incidence and severity of adverse events... One hundred patients were planned to be enrolled onto this study. With a sample size of 100 patients, a 29% ORR enables exclusion of a rate of ≤ 20% with 95% confidence. The ORR per IRF and its two-sided 95% exact CI were calculated. The median and two-sided 95% CIs for duration of response, PFS, and OS were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. In addition to independent review, assessment of efficacy by the study investigators was collected as a protocol-defined exploratory analysis. A κ coefficient was calculated to characterize the agreement in objective response and best response assessments between IRF and investigator."

*[verbatim, from the approved Package Insert, §14 "Clinical Studies"]*

> "An independent review facility performed efficacy evaluations which included overall response rate (ORR = complete remission [CR] + partial remission [PR]) and duration of response as defined by clinical and radiographic measures including computed tomography (CT) and positron-emission tomography (PET) as defined in the 2007 Revised Response Criteria for Malignant Lymphoma (modified)."

The original-approval label (Table 2) reports, for the 102-patient Hodgkin lymphoma cohort: CR 32% (95% CI 23-42), PR 40% (95% CI 32-49), ORR 73% (95% CI 65-83), median duration of response 6.7 months (CR subgroup 20.5 months). For the 58-patient sALCL cohort (Table 3): CR 57% (95% CI 44-70), PR 29% (95% CI 18-41), ORR 86% (95% CI 77-95), median duration of response 12.6 months (CR subgroup not estimable). The Younes 2012 publication's slightly later data cutoff reports a matured ORR of 75% (CR 34%) for the Hodgkin cohort — the small difference from the label's 73% reflects the longer follow-up in the peer-reviewed report versus the BLA's original data-cutoff date.

*[verbatim, from the FDA Approval Letter, "Postmarketing Requirements" section — the confirmatory-trial condition attached to the accelerated approval]*

> "Granting of these approvals are contingent upon completion of clinical trials to verify the clinical benefit of brentuximab vedotin, as outlined in your letter of July 22, 2011... 1. CONFIRMATORY TRIAL - A randomized phase 3, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of SGN-35 (brentuximab vedotin) in combination with CH-P versus CHOP as frontline therapy in patients with CD30-positive mature T- and NK-cell lymphomas including systemic ALCL (sALCL). Enrollment of approximately 300 patients is expected with a primary endpoint of progression free survival as determined by an independent blinded review facility. Overall survival is a key secondary endpoint... 2. CONFIRMATORY TRIAL - A randomized phase 3 trial of SGN-35 (brentuximab vedotin) in combination with AVD versus ABVD as frontline therapy in patients with advanced Hodgkin Lymphoma. Enrollment of at least 880 patients is expected with a primary endpoint of progression free survival determined by an independent blinded review facility. Overall survival is a key secondary endpoint... Successful completion of either PMR 1 or PMR 2 could be considered to convert the accelerated approval to regular approval for both the Hodgkin lymphoma and sALCL indications."

**Reverse-engineered notes for the sALCL (SG035-0004) statistical methodology specifically** *(inferred — the Pro et al. 2012 JCO publication's own Statistical Analysis section could not be accessed; it is paywalled and has no PMC deposit)*

- **Same exact-CI/Kaplan-Meier framework as SG035-0003** [inferred from: the label's §14.2 describing SG035-0004 in near-identical language to §14.1 — "An independent review facility performed efficacy evaluations which included overall response rate... and duration of response" — combined with the fact both trials were run by the same sponsor, under contemporaneous protocols (SG035-0003 and -0004), submitted in the same BLA cycle, and reviewed by the same FDA division. It is highly likely SG035-0004 used the identical primary-endpoint definition (ORR by IRF), Clopper-Pearson-type exact 95% CI, and Kaplan-Meier estimation for duration of response as SG035-0003, but this is inferred by analogy rather than confirmed from the ALCL trial's own methods text.]
- **No stated multiplicity or interim-monitoring plan** [inferred from: neither the label nor the approval letter describes any interim analysis or alpha-spending for either trial, consistent with a fixed-sample, single-stage Phase 2 design with a single final analysis — the same conclusion drawn directly from SG035-0003's publication, extended here to SG035-0004 by the same reasoning.]

### 11. Crizotinib (Xalkori) — NDA 202570 (original approval)

**Sponsor:** Pfizer Inc.

**Indication approved:** Locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that is anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK)-positive, as detected by an FDA-approved test (the Vysis ALK Break-Apart FISH Probe Kit, approved concurrently as a companion diagnostic)

**Approval date:** August 26, 2011 (accelerated approval)

**Pivotal trial:** Study B / PROFILE 1005 (Protocol A8081005), NCT00932451 (pivotal, Phase 2); Study A / PROFILE 1001 Phase 1 expansion cohort (Protocol A8081001), NCT00585195 (supportive)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm trial, open-label, multicenter, two single-arm studies (one Phase 2, one a Phase 1 dose-expansion cohort), biomarker-selected population (ALK rearrangement by companion diagnostic), companion diagnostic co-approval
- *Endpoints:* ORR as sole primary endpoint (investigator-assessed, with independent radiology review as a supportive/retrospective analysis), duration of response (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* Clopper-Pearson exact CI ("exact method based on the F distribution"), Kaplan-Meier estimation (duration of response)
- *Missing data/bias:* Ascertainment bias assessment (EDR/LDR) — here applied to response-assessment (investigator- vs. independent-radiology-review ORR) rather than progression timing; FDA's review documents IRR-assessed ORR running roughly 10 percentage points below investigator-assessed ORR in both studies
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval based on ORR from two single-arm studies, no FDA advisory committee meeting held, two postmarketing confirmatory Phase 3 trials required (PROFILE 1007 and PROFILE 1014 — distinct from and not the basis for this original approval), companion diagnostic (Vysis ALK Break-Apart FISH Probe Kit) approved concurrently

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study B (PROFILE 1005 / Protocol A8081005): open-label, multicenter, single-arm Phase 2 trial of oral crizotinib 250 mg BID in previously treated (with the exception of 15 treatment-naive patients) locally advanced/metastatic ALK-positive NSCLC, identified by the Vysis ALK Break-Apart FISH Probe Kit; 136 treated patients analyzed at the original-NDA data cutoff (of 148 enrolled, including 13 who crossed over from the comparator arm of the then-ongoing randomized PROFILE 1007 trial)
- Study A (PROFILE 1001 Phase 1 expansion / Protocol A8081001): originally a Phase 1 dose-escalation/safety/PK study (3+3 design) that was amended in October 2007 to add an RP2D ALK-positive NSCLC expansion cohort after partial responses were observed in 7/14 previously treated ALK-positive NSCLC patients; 119 patients in the ALK-positive RP2D cohort at the original-NDA cutoff, with ALK status identified by a mix of local clinical-trial assays
- Primary endpoint in both studies: objective response rate (ORR = confirmed CR + PR) per RECIST (v1.1 in Study B, v1.0 in Study A), based on the response-evaluable population, using investigator tumor assessments as the primary analysis; response was also evaluated by an independent radiology review (IRR) panel as a supportive/retrospective analysis
- Secondary/supportive endpoints: duration of response (Kaplan-Meier), time to response, disease control rate at 6/12 (or 8/16) weeks, progression-free survival, survival probability at 6/12 months, overall survival
- Statistical method: "Exact 2-sided 95% confidence intervals based on the F distribution were calculated for all proportion estimates" (i.e., Clopper-Pearson exact binomial CI) — the identical method later documented in the ClinicalTrials.gov-posted Protocol A8081001 Statistical Analysis Plan (Final v10.0, dated August 22, 2019 — a much later, cumulative SAP version covering all of Study A8081001's subsequent cohorts and amendments through 2019, not the version in force at the time of the 2011 accelerated approval, but describing the same binary-endpoint methodology)
- No formal multiplicity control or interim/group-sequential monitoring: both were single-arm efficacy analyses with no comparator hypothesis test, per FDA's statistical review: "Both Study 1005 and Study 1001 are ongoing single-arm, open-label studies. No statistical inference on comparison was conducted within both studies."
- As supportive/exploratory context (not part of the primary efficacy claim), the applicant performed two retrospective analyses comparing Study 1001's ORR against covariate-matched and covariate-adjusted historical control-arm data from three randomized NSCLC trials, estimating historical ORRs of 10-24% (matched analysis) and 15-21% (modeling analysis) versus crizotinib's observed 61%

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2011/202570s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (2011, original approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2011/202570s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Lijun Zhang, PhD, dated August 5, 2011, with an August addendum) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/202570Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Summary Review (Division Director Review) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/202570Orig1s000SumR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (PROFILE 1001) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00585195 — **a genuine Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan are posted** (Final SAP v10.0, dated August 22, 2019; this is the study's final, cumulative SAP covering all cohorts/amendments through 2019, not a version contemporaneous with the 2011 approval) — Protocol: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/95/NCT00585195/Prot_002.pdf, SAP: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/95/NCT00585195/SAP_001.pdf
- Pivotal publication (PROFILE 1001, early cohort): Kwak EL, et al. "Anaplastic Lymphoma Kinase Inhibition in Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer." *N Engl J Med.* 2010;363:1693-1703. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1006448), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20979469/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Anaplastic%20Lymphoma%20Kinase%20Inhibition%20in%20Non-Small-Cell%20Lung%20Cancer)
- PROFILE 1005 final-results publication (later data cutoff than the 2011 approval dataset; no peer-reviewed PROFILE 1005 publication existed at the time of original approval): Kim DW, et al. "Final results of the large-scale multinational trial PROFILE 1005: efficacy and safety of crizotinib in previously treated patients with advanced/metastatic ALK-positive non-small-cell lung cancer." *ESMO Open.* 2017. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1136/esmoopen-2017-000219), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29209525/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Final%20results%20of%20the%20large-scale%20multinational%20trial%20PROFILE%201005%3A%20efficacy%20and%20safety%20of%20crizotinib%20in%20previously%20treated%20patients%20with%20advanced%2Fmetastatic%20ALK-positive%20non-small-cell%20lung%20cancer)

**Other resources**

- Pfizer participates in the Vivli data-sharing platform (vivli.org); trial-specific IPD availability for PROFILE 1001/1005 was not individually confirmed in this pass and should be checked on Vivli directly before assuming access.
- This was an accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.500-314.560 based on ORR from two single-arm studies; FDA's Division Director Review states plainly: "This accelerated approval is based on the results of two single-arm studies." Two randomized Phase 3 confirmatory trials were required as postmarketing commitments — PROFILE 1007 (crizotinib vs. pemetrexed/docetaxel, second-line) and PROFILE 1014 (crizotinib vs. pemetrexed/platinum, first-line) — which later independently supported regular approval in November 2013 and expansion to first-line use in 2014, respectively; **these later randomized trials are not the basis for this original 2011 accelerated approval** and are out of scope for this entry.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held: "The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues in the intended population. However, the application was discussed independently with two SGE's. Both recommended approval."
- The companion diagnostic, the Vysis ALK Break-Apart FISH Probe Kit (Abbott Molecular, Inc.), was approved concurrently with crizotinib.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, from FDA Statistical Review, Executive Summary, p.1]*

> "This is an original New Drug Application (NDA) submission seeking an accelerated approval of crizotinib for the treatment of anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) positive advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The applicant has submitted results from two single-arm studies: A8081005 (phase 2, second-line therapy) as a pivotal study and A8081001 (phase 1 expansion cohort) as a supportive study. The primary efficacy endpoint was the objective response rate (ORR) in both studies. Per FDA analyses, the ORR was 49.6% (95% CI: 40.9%, 58.4%) in Study A8081005 and 61.2% (95% CI: 51.7%, 70.1%) in Study A8081001, based on the investigator tumor assessments."

*[verbatim, from FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.1.5 "Efficacy Analysis Methods," p.10]*

> "The primary efficacy endpoint was the objective response rate (ORR = CR+ PR) and the primary efficacy analysis was based on the response-evaluable population. Exact 2-sided 95% confidence intervals based on the F distribution were calculated for all proportion estimates. Estimates of time-to-event endpoints were obtained using the Kaplan-Meier method."

*[verbatim, from FDA Statistical Review, Table 7 and surrounding text, p.14 — the primary analysis result as executed]*

> "In the response-evaluable population (n=116) [Study 1001], the ORR was 61.2% with a 95% CI of (51.7% -70.1%)... Table 7. Summary of Best Overall Response based on Investigator Assessments, Response-Evaluable Population... Objective Response Rate, n (%) (ORR = CR + PR): Study 1005 68 (51.1), Study 1001 71 (61.2). 95% Exact CI: Study 1005 (42.3, 59.9), Study 1001 (51.7, 70.1). [footnote] Using exact method based on F distribution."

*[verbatim, FDA reviewer commentary documenting the investigator-vs-independent-review discordance, p.15-16 — a reviewer-conducted sensitivity/ascertainment-bias check on the sponsor's primary analysis, the ORR analogue of the PFS ascertainment-bias checks seen elsewhere in this census]*

> "The IRR-assessed ORR in Study 1005 was 41.9% (95% CI: 32.3% -51.9%)... The IRR-assessed ORR was 52.4% (95% CI: 42.4% -62.2%) [Study 1001]... Reviewer's Comment: The ORRs per IRR appear 10% lower compared to the rates by investigator assessments in both studies."

*[verbatim, from ClinicalTrials.gov-posted Protocol A8081001 Statistical Analysis Plan (Final v10.0, 22-Aug-2019), §8.1.1 "Analyses of Binary Endpoint," p.30 — describing the same exact-CI method documented independently in the 2011 FDA review, though this SAP text postdates the original approval by 8 years]*

> "The point estimates of the rates of binary endpoints will be provided along with the corresponding exact 2-sided 95% confidence intervals using the exact method based on the F-distribution."

*[verbatim, from the approved Package Insert, §14 "Clinical Studies," and Table 5 footnote]*

> "The primary efficacy endpoint in both studies was Objective Response Rate (ORR) according to Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST). Response was evaluated by the investigator and by an independent radiology review panel."

> Table 5 footnote c: "Preliminary estimate using Kaplan-Meier method."

This is a clean example of a regulatory pattern seen elsewhere in this census (e.g., SOLO-2's BICR-vs-investigator sensitivity check): the sponsor's primary analysis used investigator assessment, and FDA independently verified it against blinded central/independent review, documenting a systematic ~10-point gap between the two — here disclosed transparently in both the FDA review and (implicitly, via the "evaluated by...an independent radiology review panel" language) the approved label, rather than concealed or contested.

### 12. Ruxolitinib (Jakafi) — NDA 202192

**Sponsor:** Incyte Corporation

**Indication approved:** Intermediate or high-risk myelofibrosis, including primary myelofibrosis, post-polycythemia vera myelofibrosis, and post-essential thrombocythemia myelofibrosis

**Approval date:** November 16, 2011

**Pivotal trial:** Study 351 / COMFORT-I, NCT00952289 (co-pivotal: Study 352 / COMFORT-II, NCT00934544)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (COMFORT-I); randomized, open-label, active-controlled (COMFORT-II vs. best available therapy); crossover permitted at progression
- *Endpoints:* proportion with >35% reduction in spleen volume by MRI/CT at Week 24 (COMFORT-I primary) or Week 48 (COMFORT-II primary), total symptom score response (key secondary, COMFORT-I), overall survival (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* Fisher's exact test (COMFORT-I), Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by prognostic risk category (COMFORT-II), Kaplan-Meier estimation (overall survival, duration of spleen response)
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing of secondary endpoints (COMFORT-I: total symptom score responder rate → change in total symptom score → overall survival, each only tested if the prior endpoint in the sequence was significant)
- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation (missing or discontinuation-associated spleen-volume/symptom-score assessments counted as non-response)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Two randomized, controlled Phase III trials supported approval: Study 351 (COMFORT-I: US/Canada/Australia, 89 centers, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 1:1 randomization, no stratification) and Study 352 (COMFORT-II: Europe, 57 centers, open-label, randomized 2:1 to ruxolitinib vs. investigator-selected best available therapy (BAT), stratified by IWG-MRT prognostic risk category [Intermediate-2 vs. High])
- Population: adults with primary myelofibrosis, post-polycythemia vera myelofibrosis, or post-essential thrombocythemia myelofibrosis, Intermediate-2 or High risk by IWG-MRT criteria, with palpable splenomegaly; starting dose (15 or 20 mg BID) determined by baseline platelet count
- COMFORT-I primary endpoint: proportion of subjects achieving >35% reduction in spleen volume from baseline to Week 24 by MRI (or CT); a missing Week 24 assessment, early dropout for lack of efficacy/adverse events, or early crossover (placebo arm) was counted as a non-responder
- COMFORT-I secondary endpoints, tested only if the primary endpoint was positive, in a pre-specified fixed sequence each at the 0.05 two-sided level: (1) proportion with ≥50% reduction in Total Symptom Score (TSS) at Week 24, (2) change from baseline to Week 24 in TSS (Wilcoxon rank-sum test), (3) overall survival (Kaplan-Meier)
- COMFORT-I sample size: 240 subjects (120/arm) planned for 97% power to detect a treatment difference (30% vs. 10% response) at two-sided alpha 0.05 using the chi-square test; 309 subjects were actually randomized (155 ruxolitinib : 154 placebo); after roughly half the remaining subjects completed Week 36 and all completed Week 24 or discontinued, the database was frozen for the primary analysis and the study unblinded, after which placebo subjects could cross over
- COMFORT-II primary endpoint: proportion achieving ≥35% spleen-volume reduction from baseline at Week 48 by MRI/CT, analyzed via CMH test stratified by risk category; key secondary endpoint was the identical proportion measured at Week 24 (no formal multiplicity adjustment was applied per FDA's reviewer checklist, since only a single secondary endpoint was tested and not included as a distinct labeling claim); other secondary endpoints (duration of maintained spleen response, time to first ≥35% reduction, progression-free/leukemia-free/overall survival, transfusion status, bone marrow histomorphology) were descriptive
- COMFORT-II sample size: 150 subjects (100:50) planned for ≥90% power to detect a treatment difference (35% vs. 10% response) at two-sided alpha 0.05 using the chi-square test; 219 subjects were actually randomized (146 ruxolitinib : 73 BAT)
- Per FDA's reviewer checklist, neither trial had a formal interim analysis, and no sensitivity analyses beyond the pre-specified non-responder imputation rule were performed by the sponsor

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2011/202192s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (original, 2011) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2011/202192lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Division of Biometrics) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/202192Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (COMFORT-I) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00952289 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (COMFORT-II) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00934544 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)
- Pivotal publication (COMFORT-I): Verstovsek S, et al. "A Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial of Ruxolitinib for Myelofibrosis." *N Engl J Med.* 2012;366(9):799-807. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1110557), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22375971/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=A%20Double-Blind%2C%20Placebo-Controlled%20Trial%20of%20Ruxolitinib%20for%20Myelofibrosis)
- Pivotal publication (COMFORT-II): Harrison C, et al. "JAK Inhibition with Ruxolitinib versus Best Available Therapy for Myelofibrosis." *N Engl J Med.* 2012;366(9):787-798. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1110556), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22375970/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=JAK%20Inhibition%20with%20Ruxolitinib%20versus%20Best%20Available%20Therapy%20for%20Myelofibrosis)

**Other resources**

- Incyte operates its own qualified-researcher data-sharing program (via incyteclinicaltrials.com) rather than participating in Vivli/YODA; trial-specific IPD availability for COMFORT-I/II was not individually confirmed in this pass.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was identified for this original approval.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §2.1 "Overview," p.4]*

> "Study 351 is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study comparing the efficacy and safety of ruxolitinib to placebo in subjects with Primary Myelofibrosis (PMF), Post Polycythemia-myelofibrosis (PPV-MF) or Post Essential Thrombocythemia myelofibrosis (PET-MF). Subjects were randomized with a 1:1 ratio to receive ruxolitinib or matching placebo tablets. The primary endpoint of Study 351 was the proportion of subjects achieving >35% reduction in spleen volume from baseline to Week 24 as measured by MRI (or by CT for applicable)... The trial was originally planned with a sample size of 240 subjects, which provided a 97% power to detect a treatment difference in the primary endpoint at two-sided alpha level of 0.05 using the chi-square test."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.1.1 "Study Design and Endpoints," p.5-6]*

> "The primary efficacy endpoint is the proportion of subjects achieving >35% reduction in spleen volume from baseline to Week 24 as measured by MRI (or by CT for applicable). The treatment difference in the proportion was tested by Fisher's exact test. A subject must have a baseline spleen volume in order to be included in the primary efficacy analysis. A subject with a missing Week 24 spleen volume was considered as having not achieved the >35% reduction... The secondary efficacy endpoints was analyzed only when the study had reached the efficacy objective in the primary endpoint and was tested in a fixed sequence-testing procedure with each at the 0.05 alpha level in the order below: 1. The proportion of subjects who have a 50% reduction from baseline to Week 24 in the total symptom score[;] 2. Change from baseline to Week 24 in the total symptom score; and 3. Overall Survival."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.2.1 "Study Design and Endpoints" (Study 352/COMFORT-II), p.9-10]*

> "The primary efficacy endpoint of this study was the proportion of subjects achieving ≥ 35% reduction in spleen volume from baseline at Week 48 as measured by MRI or CT (for subjects unable to undergo MRI)... The two proportions were compared using the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by prognostic category (Intermediate-2 or High risk). The definition and analysis of the key secondary endpoint was identical to the definition and main analysis of the primary endpoint, the only difference being the timing of evaluation, at 24 weeks. This key secondary endpoint will be tested at 2-sided alpha level of 0.05 if the primary endpoint is statistically significant at two-sided alpha level of 0.05."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, "Trial Specification" summary tables, p.18-20]*

> Study 351 — "Interim Analysis: No... Was there a Multiplicity involved? Yes. Multiple Secondary Endpoints: Are they being included in the label? Yes. Gate keeper method is used to adjust for multiplicity... Were there any Discrepancies between the protocol/statistical analysis plan vs. the study report? No. Overall, was the study positive? Yes."
>
> Study 352 — "Interim Analysis: No... Was there a Multiplicity involved? No. Multiple Secondary Endpoints: Are they being included in the label? No... Were there any Discrepancies between the protocol/statistical analysis plan vs. the study report? No. Overall, was the study positive? Yes."

The FDA reviewer's use of "Gate keeper method" for Study 351 refers to the same fixed-sequence hierarchical procedure quoted above; both studies were reported by FDA as executed without discrepancy from their pre-specified statistical analysis plans, an unusually clean regulatory record compared to some other entries in this census.

### 13. Asparaginase Erwinia chrysanthemi (Erwinaze) — BLA 125359

**Sponsor:** EUSA Pharma, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Component of a multi-agent chemotherapeutic regimen for acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) in patients who have developed hypersensitivity to E. coli-derived asparaginase

**Approval date:** November 18, 2011

**Pivotal trial:** Study 1 (Children's Oncology Group protocol AALL07P2), NCT00537030

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial (no randomized comparator); multicenter, cooperative-group-run (Children's Oncology Group/NCI)
- *Endpoints:* pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic activity-threshold endpoint (serum trough asparaginase activity ≥0.1 IU/mL as a surrogate for asparagine depletion and clinical efficacy)
- *Primary analysis:* exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval (proportion of patients achieving the pre-specified activity threshold)
- *Regulatory:* orphan drug designation, priority review

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 1 (AALL07P2) was a single-arm, open-label, multicenter safety/clinical-pharmacology trial — not a randomized controlled trial — run through the Children's Oncology Group (NCI cooperative group network), reflecting both the rarity of E. coli-asparaginase hypersensitivity in ALL and the ethical/practical difficulty of randomizing patients who need an urgent asparaginase substitute
- Population: 58 patients (48 evaluable for the primary outcome based on pharmacokinetic sample availability) with ALL, treated on NCI-sponsored cooperative-group ALL protocols, who were unable to continue pegaspargase because of hypersensitivity reactions; median age 10 years (range 2-18)
- Intervention: ERWINAZE 25,000 IU/m² administered intramuscularly three times weekly (Monday/Wednesday/Friday) for six doses, substituting for each remaining scheduled pegaspargase dose in the patient's original treatment protocol
- Primary (main) outcome measure: proportion of patients achieving serum trough asparaginase activity ≥0.1 IU/mL at 48 or 72 hours after the third dose of course 1 — a level chosen because it had been shown to correlate with asparagine depletion (asparagine <0.4 mcg/mL) and, in turn, with clinical efficacy; this is a pharmacodynamic surrogate endpoint, not a direct clinical response or survival endpoint
- Exploratory secondary analysis used a higher activity cut-off (≥0.4 IU/mL) at the same timepoints
- Success criterion: the trial "met its main outcome measure" by demonstrating that more than 50% of evaluable patients achieved the pre-specified ≥0.1 IU/mL threshold; results were reported with 95% confidence intervals around the observed proportions (100% [35/35] at 48 hours; 100% [13/13] at 72 hours, main outcome)
- No formal hypothesis test, alpha-spending plan, or multiplicity adjustment is described in the label — consistent with a single-arm pharmacometric-bridging design rather than a comparative Phase III trial; the label's "Clinical Studies" section (§14) presents point estimates and exact-type binomial CIs by timepoint rather than a p-value against a null hypothesis

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2011/125359s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (original, 2011) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2011/125359lbl.pdf
- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/125359Orig1s000SumR.pdf (26-page scanned document; text layer did not extract cleanly via `pdftotext`, so it is cited here as a document link but not quoted verbatim)
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (Study 1 / AALL07P2) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00537030 (no protocol/SAP documents posted; record confirms lead sponsor Children's Oncology Group, single-group interventional design, enrollment 59, and a primary outcome measure — "Percentage of Participants With Trough Serum Asparaginase Activity ≥ 0.1 IU/mL" — matching the label's Study 1 description)
- Pivotal publication: Salzer WL, Asselin B, Supko JG, et al. "Erwinia asparaginase achieves therapeutic activity after pegaspargase allergy: a report from the Children's Oncology Group." *Blood.* 2013;122(4):507-514. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1182/blood-2013-01-480822), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23741010/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Erwinia%20asparaginase%20achieves%20therapeutic%20activity%20after%20pegaspargase%20allergy%20a%20report%20from%20the%20Children%27s%20Oncology%20Group)

**Other resources**

- Erwinaze carries orphan drug designation for this rare-hypersensitivity indication; EUSA Pharma (a small specialty biopharmaceutical company, later acquired by Jazz Pharmaceuticals in 2012) is not known to participate in Vivli, YODA, or Project Data Sphere, and no trial-specific IPD access program was identified for Study 1.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was identified for this application.
- The pivotal publication postdates approval by roughly 18 months (submitted as a BLA using unpublished cooperative-group trial data, then published afterward in Blood) — an example of the trial-registration-to-publication lag common for cooperative-group-run trials rather than industry-sponsored ones.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, approved Package Insert, §14 "Clinical Studies"]*

> "The safety and efficacy of ERWINAZE was established in Study 1, a single-arm, multi-center, open-label, safety and clinical pharmacology trial... Study 1 enrolled patients treated on National Cancer Institute (NCI)-sponsored cooperative group ALL protocols who were unable to continue to receive pegaspargase due to hypersensitivity reactions. The main outcome measure was determination of the proportion of patients who achieved a serum trough asparaginase level greater than or equal to 0.1 International Units/mL. Serum trough asparaginase activity ≥ 0.1 International Units/mL has been demonstrated to correlate with asparagine depletion (asparagine < 0.4 mcg/mL or 3 µM) and to serum levels that predict clinical efficacy. Patients received ERWINAZE 25,000 International Units/m2 intramuscularly for two weeks (total 6 doses) as a replacement for each scheduled dose of pegaspargase remaining on their original treatment protocol.
>
> Fifty-eight patients were enrolled in Study 1, of these 48 were evaluable for the main outcome measure based on availability of pharmacokinetic samples in course 1... Study 1 met its main outcome measure of demonstrating that greater than 50% of the patients achieved the pre-specified trough asparaginase activity level of ≥ 0.1 International Units/mL at 48 or 72 hours following the third dose."

*[verbatim, approved Package Insert, Table 3, "Proportion of Patients in Study 1 with Sustained Asparaginase Activity"]*

> "Main Outcome... 48-hour: Proportion (n/N) and 95% CI with asparaginase activity ≥ 0.1 IU/mL: 100% (35/35), 95% CI: 90%, 100%. 72-hour: 100% (13/13), 95% CI: 77%, 100%."

**Reverse-engineered SAP** *(inferred — the exact statistical methodology/CI method beyond what the label states is not public)*

- **Binomial exact/Clopper-Pearson-type confidence interval methodology** [inferred from: the label reports asymmetric-looking 95% CIs around small-sample proportions (e.g., 100% [35/35] → 95% CI 90%-100%) that are consistent with an exact (Clopper-Pearson) binomial CI rather than a normal-approximation Wald interval, which would be undefined/degenerate at an observed proportion of 100%; the label itself does not name the specific CI method, so this is inferred from the shape of the reported interval, not a confirmed citation].
- **No formal hypothesis test against a pre-specified null response rate** [inferred from: the label's "met its main outcome measure of demonstrating that greater than 50% of the patients achieved..." language describes a threshold-crossing success criterion rather than a p-value or test statistic — consistent with a single-arm pharmacometric bridging study design where the regulatory question is "does activity exceed a clinically-validated threshold in most patients," not a comparative superiority test].

### 14. Axitinib (Inlyta) — NDA 202324

**Sponsor:** Pfizer Inc.

**Indication approved:** Advanced renal cell carcinoma (RCC) after failure of one prior systemic therapy

**Approval date:** January 27, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** AXIS (Study A4061032), NCT00678392

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled
- *Endpoints:* PFS (IRC-assessed, primary), PFS (investigator-assessed, secondary), overall survival (secondary), objective response rate/duration of response (IRC-assessed, secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified or with covariates)
- *Multiplicity:* unadjusted secondary/supportive testing (single formal primary endpoint)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design, Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function, O'Brien-Fleming boundary (efficacy), Pampallona-Tsiatis power-family futility boundary, sample-size re-estimation (Cui-Hung-Wang method), Data Monitoring Committee (DMC/DSMB)
- *Regulatory:* FDA Advisory Committee meeting held, reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Multicenter, international, randomized (1:1), open-label, active-controlled Phase III trial of axitinib vs. sorafenib in metastatic RCC patients who had failed one prior first-line systemic regimen (sunitinib, bevacizumab+IFN-α, temsirolimus, or cytokine therapy); enrolled at 175 centers in 22 countries
- Randomization stratified by ECOG performance status (0 vs. 1) and prior therapy type (sunitinib-, bevacizumab-, temsirolimus-, or cytokine-containing regimens)
- Primary endpoint: progression-free survival (PFS) by independent radiology committee (IRC) review, RECIST v1.0; secondary endpoints: investigator-assessed PFS, overall survival (OS), objective response rate (ORR) and duration of response (both IRC-assessed)
- Sample size originally planned for 409 PFS events, giving 90% power to detect a median PFS improvement from 5 to 7 months at one-sided alpha 0.025, with a non-binding futility analysis planned at ~50% of events (204 events); target enrollment was later increased mid-trial (Protocol Amendment 4 / SAP v1.2, Nov-Dec 2009) from 540 to 650 patients, though actual enrollment reached 723 — a discrepancy FDA's statistical reviewer flagged as unjustified by the stated rationale (dropout-rate underestimation) since observed censoring rates did not support it
- Statistical methods: PFS compared via a one-sided stratified log-rank test at alpha=0.025 (stratified by ECOG PS and prior therapy); hazard ratio and 95% CI from a stratified Cox model; an unstratified log-rank test and Cox model were run as a supportive/sensitivity analysis
- Interim/final analysis used an asymmetric Lan-DeMets spending-function design: an O'Brien-Fleming-type efficacy boundary for PFS/OS paired with a non-binding Pampallona-Tsiatis power-family futility boundary (shape parameter 0.3); an independent DMC reviewed the interim analysis (June 11, 2010) and recommended continuing the study unchanged
- FDA's reviewer separately recalculated the required PFS event count after the interim analysis occurred later than planned (289 vs. the planned 204 events) and found the applicant's claimed need to increase the event target to 423 was not correct (reviewer's own calculation, using East v5, put the ceiling at 414 events); the DMC nonetheless found no safety signal, no futility-boundary crossing, and recommended no design change
- Result: PFS statistically significant favoring axitinib (HR 0.667, 95% CI 0.546-0.814, one-sided stratified log-rank p<0.0001; median PFS 6.7 vs. 4.7 months); OS was not statistically different between arms (HR 0.969, 95% CI 0.800-1.174, one-sided p=0.3744) — secondary/supportive endpoints were tested without any formal multiplicity adjustment, consistent with the single formal primary-endpoint design

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2012/202324s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (original, 2012) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2012/202324lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/202324Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00678392 (no protocol/SAP documents posted; trial registered 2008, before ClinicalTrials.gov's sponsor SAP-posting norms took hold)
- Pivotal publication: Rini BI, Escudier B, Tomczak P, et al. "Comparative effectiveness of axitinib versus sorafenib in advanced renal cell carcinoma (AXIS): a randomised phase 3 trial." *Lancet.* 2011;378(9807):1931-1939. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(11)61613-9>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22056247/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Comparative%20effectiveness%20of%20axitinib%20versus%20sorafenib%20in%20advanced%20renal%20cell%20carcinoma)

**Other resources**

- Pfizer participates in clinicalstudydatarequest-successor data-sharing arrangements for its sponsored trials; trial-specific IPD availability for AXIS was not individually confirmed in this pass.
- An FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held on December 7, 2011; the committee voted unanimously that axitinib's benefit-risk ratio was favorable for the proposed indication.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, "Executive Summary"]*

> "The applicant has submitted results from one multicenter, phase III, randomized, open-label, clinical trial (Study A4061032) comparing axitinib, a new molecular entity (NME), to sorafenib in patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma (RCC)... The axitinib arm showed statistically significant improvement over sorafenib in progression-free survival (PFS) as assessed by independent radiology committee in all randomized patients. However, the axitinib arm did not show statistically significant improvement with respect to overall survival (OS). The application was discussed at the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee meeting on December 7, 2011. The committee voted unanimously in favor of axitinib to the question whether the benefit-risk ratio of axitinib is favorable."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.5 "Sample Size Considerations"]*

> "The sample size for this study was calculated based on PFS. In order to detect a median PFS of 7 months in the axitinib arm versus a median PFS of 5 months in the sorafenib arm at a one-sided significance level of 0.025 with 90% power, 1:1 randomization and a futility analysis at 50% PFS events, a total of 409 PFS events were required... Other secondary and supportive analyses were tested at a significance level of 0.025 (1-sided test). No adjustments were planned for multiple testing/comparisons in those secondary and supportive hypothesis tests."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, reviewer's comments following §3.2.5 — a documented discrepancy between the sponsor's stated rationale and the reviewer's own analysis]*

> "The initial target enrollment was 540 patients. The applicant (then sponsor) increased the sample size to 650 in the Protocol Amendment 4 dated November 16, 2009 and the corresponding Statistical Analysis Plan (version 1.2) dated December 7, 2009. The applicant claims that this change was made due to an underestimation of the dropout rate in the original protocol. However, Table 1 shows that only 21 patients in the axitinib arm (5.8% of the all axitinib patients) and 37 patients in the sorafenib arm (10.2% of the all sorafenib patients) were censored prior to data cut-off. However, changing the sample size alone without any change in the number of events does not affect the error rates... The actual sample size for the study was 723, which is even much higher than 650... There was no justification provided for such a big difference between the planned and actual sample size... The applicant claims that because the interim analysis occurring later than planned, the required number of PFS events would need to be increased to 423 in order to maintain 90% power with the same design parameters... Applicant's claim about the need to increase the number of events was not correct. Based on the reviewer's calculation using East version 5, the number of events should not be more than 414... The independent DMC met on June 11, 2010 to analyze the interim results; the DMC concluded that there were no safety concerns, the PFS results did not cross the futility boundary, no adjustment of sample size was necessary, and that the study should continue as planned."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.6 "Interim Analyses"]*

> "A formal efficacy boundary for rejecting the null hypothesis and futility boundary (nonbinding) for rejecting the alternative hypothesis were constructed by using the spending function methodology of Lan and DeMets in an asymmetric fashion. An O'Brien-Fleming stopping boundary was used for the efficacy and a Pampallona-Tsiatis Power boundary (with parameter 0.3) was used for the futility... The sample size of the study could be adjusted using the method outlined by Cui, Hung and Wang (1999)."

This is a clear "how the SAP held up under FDA review" case: the sponsor's sample-size increase to 650, and its post-hoc claim that the delayed interim analysis required raising the event target to 423, were both directly disputed by FDA's own independent recalculation — yet the trial's primary result was positive regardless, and the discrepancy did not block approval, only prompting the reviewer's documented skepticism.

### 15. Vismodegib (Erivedge) — NDA 203388

**Sponsor:** Genentech, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adults with metastatic basal cell carcinoma (BCC), or with locally advanced BCC that has recurred following surgery or who are not candidates for surgery or radiation

**Approval date:** January 30, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** ERIVANCE BCC (Study SHH4476g), NCT00833417

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial (no randomized comparator), two-cohort design (metastatic BCC and locally advanced BCC cohorts)
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR) as assessed by an independent review facility (IRF), sole primary endpoint per cohort; duration of response (secondary, Kaplan-Meier)
- *Primary analysis:* one-sided exact binomial test (single-arm ORR hypothesis test), Blyth-Still-Casella exact confidence interval, Kaplan-Meier estimation (duration of response)
- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation for patients without a post-baseline tumor assessment; sensitivity analyses varying central-pathology-confirmation and response-criteria assumptions

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study SHH4476g was a Phase II, multicenter, single-arm, two-cohort trial (not a randomized controlled trial) — patients with locally advanced BCC not amenable to surgery/radiation (cohort 1, n=71) or metastatic BCC (cohort 2, n=33) each received open-label vismodegib 150 mg/day; there was no control arm
- Primary endpoint: objective response rate (ORR) as assessed by an independent review facility (IRF), analyzed separately for each cohort (not pooled, because the response criteria differed: RECIST for metastatic BCC; a composite radiographic/photographic/pathologic criterion for locally advanced BCC, given the difficulty of applying RECIST to externally visible/ulcerating skin lesions)
- Response required confirmation on two consecutive assessments at least 4 weeks apart; patients without any post-baseline tumor assessment were counted as non-responders in the primary analysis
- Per the sponsor's SAP, the primary ORR hypothesis was formally tested with a one-sided exact binomial test at alpha=0.025 in each cohort against a pre-specified null response rate: H0: ORR ≤0.10 vs. H1: ORR >0.10 in the metastatic cohort, and H0: ORR ≤0.20 vs. H1: ORR >0.20 in the locally advanced cohort; 95% Blyth-Still-Casella exact confidence intervals were calculated for each cohort's ORR
- With ~100 patients total, the SAP-specified design had ≥80% power to detect a true response rate of ≥37% (metastatic cohort, ~20 evaluable patients) or ≥34% (locally advanced cohort, ~80 evaluable patients)
- Results (96 efficacy-evaluable patients after central pathology confirmation excluded some enrollees): ORR 30.3% (95% CI 15.6-48.2) in the metastatic BCC cohort and 42.9% (95% CI 30.5-56.0) in the locally advanced BCC cohort, both IRF-assessed; median duration of response 7.6 months in each cohort (95% CI 5.62-not evaluable [metastatic]; 5.65-9.66 [locally advanced])
- Because the trial was single-arm and non-comparative, FDA's statistical reviewer explicitly stated that "no statistical inferential conclusion can be drawn from the study" in the between-treatment sense — the exact binomial test only supports rejecting a pre-specified low null response rate, not a claim of superiority over any comparator
- FDA's Division Director Summary Review concluded that regular approval (not accelerated approval) was appropriate based on the durability of the observed responses in a serious, life-threatening disease with no FDA-approved systemic therapy, drawing an explicit analogy to FDA's prior acceptance of durable ORR as sufficient for regular approval in cutaneous T-cell lymphoma; no advisory committee meeting was held, and the approval letter's postmarketing requirements were safety-focused (505(o), e.g., a pregnancy/embryo-fetal risk pharmacovigilance program) rather than an efficacy-confirmation requirement of the kind attached to accelerated approvals

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2012/203388s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (original, 2012) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2012/203388lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203388Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Summary Review (Division Director) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203388Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00833417 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)
- Pivotal publication: Sekulic A, Migden MR, Oro AE, et al. "Efficacy and safety of vismodegib in advanced basal-cell carcinoma." *N Engl J Med.* 2012;366(23):2171-2179. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1113713), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22670903/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Efficacy%20and%20safety%20of%20vismodegib%20in%20advanced%20basal-cell%20carcinoma)

**Other resources**

- Genentech/Roche provides IPD access via Vivli.org (Data Usage Agreement required); trial-specific SHH4476g availability was not individually confirmed in this pass.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this original approval.
- Notably, this approval was granted as a *regular* (not accelerated/Subpart H) approval — a point worth flagging because a single-arm, ORR-based design is often assumed to imply accelerated approval; here FDA instead treated durable tumor response in a serious disease with no approved alternative as sufficient for regular approval outright, with only routine 505(o) safety-related postmarketing requirements attached (not an efficacy-confirmation trial requirement).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, "Executive Summary"]*

> "In the new drug application (NDA), the applicant submitted the efficacy data collected from a single arm two cohort study to seek an approval of Vismodegib for the treatment of adult patients with advanced basal cell carcinoma (BCC) for whom surgery is inappropriate. The pivotal study SHH4476g was a phase II, multicenter, single-arm, two-cohort trial... Because Study SHH4476g was a single arm non-comparative study, no statistical inferential conclusion can be drawn from the study."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, "Statistical Methodologies"]*

> "Per the statistical analysis plan (SAP), the primary endpoint ORR would be formally tested using one-sided exact binomial tests in the metastatic and locally advanced BCC cohorts. Specifically, the following hypothesis would be tested at the one-sided α = 0.025 level in the mBCC cohort: H0: ORR ≤ 0.10 versus H1: ORR > 0.10; And the following hypothesis would be tested at the one-sided α = 0.025 level in the locally advanced BCC cohort: H0: ORR ≤ 0.20 versus H1: ORR > 0.20; Ninety-five percent Blyth–Still–Casella exact confidence intervals for the ORR would be calculated for each patient cohort... For handling missing data, the SAP specified that patients who had received at least one dose of vismodegib and who discontinued for any reason prior to undergoing one post-baseline response evaluation would be considered non-responders in the primary analysis... Per the SAP, with 100 patients, this study would have at least 80% probability of detecting an RR of 37% or higher in the mBCC cohort (with 20 treated patients) and 34% or higher in the locally advanced BCC cohort (with 80 treated patients)."

*[verbatim, FDA Division Director Summary Review, §1 "Introduction"]*

> "Regular approval should be granted for this application based on the long duration of responses, which provide both cosmetic improvement as well as the potential for symptomatic relief, in a population with a serious and potentially life-threatening disease. FDA has previously considered durable objective tumor responses as sufficient to support regular approval in cutaneous T-cell lymphoma."

### 16. Pertuzumab (Perjeta) — BLA 125409

**Sponsor:** Genentech, Inc.

**Indication approved:** In combination with trastuzumab and docetaxel, first-line treatment of patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer who have not received prior anti-HER2 therapy or chemotherapy for metastatic disease

**Approval date:** June 8, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** CLEOPATRA (Genentech/Roche Study WO20698/TOC4129g), NCT00567190

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
- *Endpoints:* PFS (IRF-assessed, primary), OS (secondary), ORR/duration of response (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified), Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence hierarchical testing (OS→ORR, both after the primary PFS analysis)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function, O'Brien-Fleming boundary (interim OS analysis), Data Monitoring Committee (DMC/DSMB)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Phase III, multicenter, randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; pertuzumab + trastuzumab + docetaxel vs. placebo + trastuzumab + docetaxel in HER2-positive locally recurrent, unresectable, or metastatic breast cancer, no prior anti-cancer treatment for metastatic disease (at most one prior hormonal therapy for MBC allowed)
- Randomization stratified by prior treatment status (de novo vs. prior adjuvant/neoadjuvant therapy) and region (Europe vs. North America vs. South America vs. Asia); 808 patients randomized (402 pertuzumab, 406 placebo) at 204 centers in 25 countries
- Primary endpoint: PFS by independent radiology facility (IRF) assessment (RECIST 1.0), time from randomization to first documented progression or death within 18 weeks of last tumor assessment, whichever occurred first
- Secondary endpoints: OS, investigator-assessed PFS, ORR (IRF), duration of response — OS and ORR tested via a fixed hierarchical sequence after the primary PFS analysis (OS first, then ORR only interpreted if OS was significant)
- Sample size: powered to detect a 33% improvement in median PFS (10.5 vs. 14 months, HR 0.75) at two-sided α=0.05, 80% power, requiring 381 IRF-assessed PFS events (~800 patients enrolled); also powered for a 33% OS improvement (36 vs. 48 months, HR 0.75), requiring 385 deaths with one interim OS analysis planned at ~50% of events
- No efficacy interim analysis of PFS was planned or conducted (only a safety interim analysis after the first 100 patients had 4 months of follow-up, reviewed by a DMC); one interim efficacy analysis of OS was planned, controlled via a Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function approximating an O'Brien-Fleming boundary
- Analysis methods: stratified log-rank test (prior treatment status, region) for PFS/OS; Kaplan-Meier for median PFS/OS; stratified Cox proportional-hazards model for hazard ratios and 95% CIs; Mantel-Haenszel/Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test (stratified) for ORR

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2012/125409Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (2012) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2012/125409lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID: 3129137) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/125409Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Medical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/125409Orig1s000MedR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00567190
- Pivotal publication: Baselga J, Cortés J, Kim SB, et al. "Pertuzumab plus Trastuzumab plus Docetaxel for Metastatic Breast Cancer." *N Engl J Med.* 2012;366(2):109-119. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1113216), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22149875/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Pertuzumab%20plus%20Trastuzumab%20plus%20Docetaxel%20for%20Metastatic%20Breast%20Cancer)

**Other resources**

- No genuine sponsor SAP/protocol document was found posted on ClinicalTrials.gov's Documents tab for NCT00567190 (no `documentSection` entry as of this review) — the excerpts below are drawn entirely from the FDA Statistical Review, which reproduces substantial verbatim analysis-plan content.
- Genentech/Roche provides IPD access via Vivli.org (Data Usage Agreement required); trial-specific CLEOPATRA availability was not individually confirmed in this pass.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this original 2012 approval (an ODAC meeting did occur in September 2013, but for a separate neoadjuvant-indication supplement, not this original BLA).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §1 "Executive Summary," p.4-5]*

> "The applicant has submitted results from one multicenter, phase III, randomized, double-blind clinical trial (Study WO20698/TOC4129g or CLEOPATRA) comparing pertuzumab, a new molecular entity (NME) in combination with trastuzumab and docetaxel, to placebo in combination with trastuzumab and docetaxel in patients with HER2-positive locally recurrent, unresectable or metastatic breast cancer (MBC)... The randomization was stratified by prior treatment status (de novo vs. adjuvant or neoadjuvant) and region (Europe vs. North America vs. South America vs. Asia)... The primary efficacy endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS) as assessed by an independent radiology facility (IRF). The secondary efficacy endpoints included overall survival (OS), investigator-assessed PFS, overall response rate (ORR) as assessed by the IRF and duration of response."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §3.2.5 "Sample Size Considerations," p.12]*

> "The sample size for this study was calculated based on PFS and OS. In order to detect a 33% improvement in median PFS (10.5 months in the control arm vs. 14 months in the experimental arm) or a hazard ratio of 0.75 at a two-sided significance level of 0.05 with 80% power and 1:1 randomization, a total of 381 IRF-assessed PFS events (corresponding to approximately 448 investigator assessed PFS events) were required... The study was also adequately powered for detecting a 33% improvement in median OS (36 months in the control arm vs. 48 months in the experimental arm) or a hazard ratio of 0.75 with a 0.05 two sided level of significance and 80% power. This would require 385 deaths with one interim analysis at 50% events."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §3.2.6 "Interim Analyses," p.13]*

> "No efficacy interim analysis of PFS was planned or conducted... An interim efficacy analysis of OS was planned and conducted at the time of the final PFS analysis. It was estimated that there would be 50% OS events at the time of the interim analysis. A Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function with an O'Brien-Fleming stopping boundary was used for the interim analysis of OS. According to the Lan-DeMets alpha spending function for O'Brien-Fleming boundary and the actual number of events, the alpha for the interim OS analysis with cut-off date May 13, 2011 was 0.0012. At the interim OS analysis, there were 165 deaths (42.8% of the OS events needed for the final analysis). The observed p-value (0.0050) did not cross the stopping boundary (p≤0.0012)."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §3.2.7.2 "Analysis of Primary Endpoint," p.14]*

> "The primary endpoint was IRF-assessed PFS. A log-rank test, stratified by prior treatment status (de novo vs. prior adjuvant or neoadjuvant therapy) and region (Europe vs. North America vs. South America vs. Asia), was used to compare PFS between the two treatment arms. The Kaplan-Meier approach was used to estimate median PFS for each treatment arm and the Cox proportional hazard model, stratified by prior treatment status and region was used to estimate the hazard ratio between the two treatment arms and its 95% confidence interval (CI)."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review's statistical-reviewer checklist, p.35 — documenting the multiplicity method and the actual outcome of the hierarchy as executed]*

> "Was there a Multiplicity involved? Yes. If yes, Multiple Arms (Yes/No)? No. Multiple Endpoints (Yes/No)? Yes. Which method was used to control for type I error? Hierarchical testing for multiple secondary endpoints... Multiple Secondary Endpoints: Are they being included in the label? If yes, method to control for type 1 error. Yes. Hierarchical testing. The first secondary endpoint OS is not significant; the next secondary endpoint included descriptively."

Because OS (first in the secondary hierarchy) was not statistically significant at the interim analysis (HR 0.642, 95% CI 0.470-0.877, stratified log-rank two-sided p=0.0053, versus the O'Brien-Fleming boundary of p≤0.0012), the label and review both treat the reported ORR difference (80.2% vs. 69.3%) as descriptive only, per the pre-specified hierarchy — a clean example of a fixed-sequence testing plan being followed exactly as designed even though it meant a nominally low OS p-value could not be formally claimed at this interim look.

### 17. Carfilzomib (Kyprolis) — NDA 202714

**Sponsor:** Onyx Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma in patients who have received at least two prior therapies, including bortezomib and an immunomodulatory agent, and have demonstrated disease progression on or within 60 days of completion of the last therapy

**Approval date:** July 20, 2012 (accelerated approval)

**Pivotal trial:** PX-171-003, Part 2 ("PX-171-003-A1"), no registered NCT number found for the Part 2 cohort specifically (parent study NCT00511238)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm accelerated-approval design (open-label, single-arm, multicenter Phase II study)
- *Endpoints:* overall response rate (ORR, IRC-assessed, primary), duration of response (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* one-sample binomial proportion estimate with exact/Clopper-Pearson-style two-sided 95% CI (lower bound pre-specified to exceed 10% for study success)
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval (surrogate endpoint, ORR); post-marketing requirement for a confirmatory randomized trial

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 3 (PX-171-003, Part 2/"A1"): open-label, single-arm, multicenter Phase II study; carfilzomib IV bolus over 2-10 minutes, 20 mg/m² on Days 1, 2, 8, 9, 15, 16 of the 28-day Cycle 1, then 27 mg/m² in Cycle 2 onward for up to 12 cycles, with dexamethasone premedication to reduce infusion reactions
- Population: relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma, heavily pretreated (266 patients enrolled in the ITT population; the proposed label population — patients unresponsive/intolerant to 5 of 6 classes of approved MM agents excluding carmustine — comprised 69 of the 266)
- Primary endpoint: best overall response rate (ORR) as determined by an Independent Response Review Committee (IRC), in the Response Evaluable Population; study pre-specified to be declared successful if the lower bound of the two-sided 95% CI for ORR exceeded 10%
- Result: ORR 22.9% (FDA-confirmed the same figure independently of the Applicant's analysis); ORR 23.2% in the smaller heavily-pretreated subset that matched the proposed indication; median duration of response 7.8 months
- No comparator arm, no randomization, no formal multiplicity or interim-analysis structure — this was a single pre-specified hypothesis test of one binomial proportion against a fixed lower-bound threshold, not a comparative superiority/non-inferiority trial
- Supporting evidence: Study PX-171-004 (open-label, single-arm, bortezomib-naive and bortezomib-treated cohorts, ORR by IRC in Response Evaluable Subset) and Study PX-171-005 (renal-impairment PK study; ORR/DOR/PFS/OS as secondary analyses in the Response Evaluable Population) — both similarly single-arm
- At the time of this approval, the sponsor's randomized Phase III confirmatory trial (PX-171-009, later ASPIRE — carfilzomib+lenalidomide+dexamethasone vs. lenalidomide+dexamethasone, PFS primary endpoint, ~700 patients planned) was ongoing but not yet reported; accelerated approval was explicitly conditioned on ORR as a surrogate reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit, pending that confirmatory trial

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2012/202714Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (2012) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2012/202714lbl.pdf
- FDA Clinical Review (Thomas M. Herndon, MD) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/202714Orig1s000MedR.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Youngsook Jeon, PhD; concurring: Yi Tsong, PhD) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/202714Orig1s000StatR.pdf (largely scanned/non-text-extractable in the publicly posted copy; the Clinical Review reproduces the same efficacy-analysis description in extractable text and is quoted below)
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (parent study, PX-171-003) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00511238
- Pivotal publication: Siegel DS, Martin T, Wang M, et al. "A phase 2 study of single-agent carfilzomib (PX-171-003-A1) in patients with relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma." *Blood.* 2012;120(14):2817-2825. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1182/blood-2012-05-425934), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22833546/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=A%20phase%202%20study%20of%20single-agent%20carfilzomib%20%28PX-171-003-A1%29%20in%20patients%20with%20relapsed%20and%20refractory%20multiple%20myeloma)

**Other resources**

- Onyx/Amgen's IPD-sharing program was not individually confirmed for this trial; no Vivli/YODA listing was checked directly in this pass.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was identified for this 2012 accelerated approval.
- Regulatory follow-through: the accelerated approval's post-marketing requirement was satisfied years later — FDA converted the monotherapy indication to full/regular approval alongside a January 2016 combination approval, citing the completed randomized Phase III confirmatory trials ASPIRE (carfilzomib+lenalidomide+dexamethasone vs. lenalidomide+dexamethasone; PFS HR reduction of 31%) and ENDEAVOR (carfilzomib+dexamethasone vs. bortezomib+dexamethasone; median PFS 18.7 vs. 9.4 months). Those later randomized trials are out of scope for this entry, which documents only the original 2012 single-arm approval basis.

**Reverse-engineered SAP**

This submission was not a randomized hypothesis-testing trial, so the usual SAP/testing-hierarchy framework used elsewhere in this census does not apply. The following points reconstruct the single-arm statistical approach from the FDA Clinical Review (which reproduces the sponsor's design and analysis in extractable text; the Statistical Review's own text was not extractable from the posted PDF, which appears to be a scanned document):

- *[inferred, from FDA Clinical Review p.29: "The study was pre-specified to be successful if the lower boundary of the 2-sided 95% CI of the ORR was > 10%"]* — the primary analysis was a single one-sample proportion test: compute the observed ORR and its two-sided 95% CI (standard practice for single-arm oncology trials of this era is Clopper-Pearson exact CI, though the review does not name the CI method explicitly), and declare success if the CI's lower bound exceeded a fixed 10% floor — i.e., a pre-specified performance-goal design rather than a comparative test against a concurrent or historical control arm.
- *[inferred, from FDA Clinical Review p.29, stating the ORR of 22.9% "whether analyzed by the Applicant or by the FDA"]* — FDA independently re-derived the ORR from IRC-assessed response data rather than relying solely on the sponsor's tabulation, standard verification practice for accelerated-approval single-arm submissions where no independent control group exists to cross-check the treatment effect.
- *[inferred, from the label's description of the accelerated-approval basis and FDA's routine post-marketing-requirement language for ORR-based approvals]* — because ORR is a surrogate endpoint under accelerated approval (21 CFR 314.510), the approval was necessarily contingent on a subsequent randomized trial (PX-171-009/ASPIRE, already underway) to verify clinical benefit (PFS/OS), rather than a data-analysis method internal to this submission.
