### 18. Ziv-aflibercept (Zaltrap) — BLA 125418

**Sponsor:** Sanofi-Aventis U.S. LLC (co-developed with Regeneron Pharmaceuticals)

**Indication approved:** In combination with FOLFIRI (5-fluorouracil, leucovorin, irinotecan), treatment of metastatic colorectal cancer resistant to or progressed following an oxaliplatin-containing regimen

**Approval date:** August 3, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** VELOUR (Study EFC10262), NCT00561470

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
- *Endpoints:* overall survival (OS, primary), PFS (IRC-assessed, key secondary), ORR (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, stratified Cox proportional-hazards model, stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test (ORR)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design (two planned interim OS efficacy analyses plus one futility analysis)
- *Missing data/bias:* standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment, sensitivity analyses for PFS assessment-schedule/site-level protocol-deviation issues

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study EFC10262 (VELOUR): single, randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter Phase III trial in 1,226 patients with metastatic colorectal cancer previously treated with one oxaliplatin-based regimen (including patients relapsing within 6 months of adjuvant oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy); prior bevacizumab was permitted, prior irinotecan was not
- Arms: aflibercept 4 mg/kg IV over 1 hour on Day 1 vs. matching placebo, both followed immediately by FOLFIRI, every 2 weeks until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or discontinuation
- Randomization via IVRS, permuted-block, stratified by prior bevacizumab therapy (yes/no) and ECOG performance status (0 vs. 1 vs. 2)
- Primary endpoint: overall survival (OS), time from randomization to death from any cause
- Secondary endpoints: PFS by independent review committee (IRC), RECIST v1.0 (an IRC was only established after Amendment 2 in April 2008; investigator assessment was used for PFS in patients who died before that amendment or who declined IRC review consent); ORR by IRC, evaluated only in the Evaluable Patient population (randomized patients with measurable disease and ≥1 valid post-baseline tumor evaluation, per IRC, and consenting to IRC review)
- Sample size: assuming median OS 11 months (control) vs. 13.75 months (aflibercept), HR 0.80, a total of 863 deaths were required to detect a 20% risk reduction with 90% power, two-sided log-rank test at significance level 0.0499; design incorporated two planned interim OS efficacy analyses (at 36.5% and 65% information) plus one futility analysis at the first interim look
- Primary analysis: log-rank test stratified by the randomization factors (prior bevacizumab, ECOG PS), ITT population; HR and CI from a stratified Cox proportional-hazards model; PFS analyzed similarly at significance level 0.0001, with two pre-specified sensitivity analyses (IRC-assessed PFS censoring events/progression >9 weeks after last valid tumor assessment; investigator-assessed PFS counting symptomatic deterioration as an event); ORR difference compared via stratified CMH test
- Results: median OS 13.5 vs. 12.1 months, stratified HR 0.816 (95% CI 0.713-0.934), stratified log-rank p=0.0032; median PFS 6.9 vs. 4.7 months, stratified HR 0.756 (95% CI 0.660-0.876), p=0.00007; ORR 19.8% vs. 11.1%, stratified CMH p=0.0001
- FDA-identified issues resolved via sensitivity analysis rather than affecting the primary conclusion: a discrepancy between IVRS-recorded and case-report-form-recorded stratification factors (sensitivity analysis using CRF stratification gave similar results), and a GCP-inspection finding of protocol non-compliance at one Australian site (sensitivity OS analysis excluding those 23 patients gave similar results)

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2012/125418Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (2012) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2012/125418s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Jing J. Zhang, Kun He; Division Director sign-off: Rajeshwari Sridhara) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/125418Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Medical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/125418Orig1s000MedR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00561470
- Pivotal publication: Van Cutsem E, Tabernero J, Lakomy R, et al. "Addition of aflibercept to fluorouracil, leucovorin, and irinotecan improves survival in a phase III randomized trial in patients with metastatic colorectal cancer previously treated with an oxaliplatin-based regimen." *J Clin Oncol.* 2012;30(28):3499-3506. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.2012.42.8201), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22949147/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Addition%20of%20aflibercept%20to%20fluorouracil%2C%20leucovorin%2C%20and%20irinotecan%20improves%20survival%20in%20a%20phase%20III%20randomized%20trial)

**Other resources**

- No genuine sponsor SAP/protocol was found posted on ClinicalTrials.gov's Documents tab for NCT00561470 (no `documentSection` entry as of this review); the excerpts below are drawn from the FDA Statistical Review, which reproduces substantial verbatim design/analysis detail.
- Sanofi participates in data-sharing generally; trial-specific VELOUR IPD availability (Vivli or Sanofi's own portal) was not individually confirmed in this pass.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was identified for this original approval.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §1 "Executive Summary," p.5]*

> "The primary support for efficacy comes from a single randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multi-center phase III study (Study EFC10262 [VELOUR]) in 1226 patients with colorectal cancer treated with FOLFIRI as second line treatment for metastatic disease. The primary efficacy endpoint was overall survival (OS). The primary analysis was a log-rank test stratified by prior therapy with bevacizumab (yes vs. no) and ECOG performance status (0 vs. 1 vs. 2). Secondary endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS) and overall response rate (ORR)."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §3.2 "Evaluation of Efficacy," Sample Size Determination, p.7]*

> "For the primary endpoint of OS, the expected median survival time was 11 months in the control arm and 13.75 months in the treatment arm, corresponding to a hazard ratio (HR) of 0.80. Assuming exponential survival times, a total of 863 deaths were required to detect a 20% risk reduction in the aflibercept arm relative to the placebo arm with 90% power, using a two-sided log-rank test at a significance level of 0.0499. This calculation took into account two interim efficacy analyses for OS at 36.5% and 65% information and one futility analysis at the time of the first interim efficacy analysis."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §3.2 "Statistical Methodologies," p.7]*

> "The intent-to-treat (ITT) population was the primary analysis population and consists of all randomized patients with treatment as assigned at randomization. The primary analysis comparing OS between the two treatment arms was performed in the ITT population using the log-rank test stratified by the stratification factors specified at randomization (i.e., prior therapy with bevacizumab and ECOG PS). The hazard ratio (HR) and corresponding (1-α)% confidence interval (CI) were obtained from a stratified Cox proportional hazards model. Similar analyses were performed for PFS at a significance level of 0.0001... Two sensitivity analyses of PFS were performed: Sensitivity analysis #1: PFS endpoint as assessed by the IRC, censoring for progression or death occurring more than 9 weeks (i.e., >1.5 times the assessment interval length) after the last valid tumor assessment and for other anti-tumor therapies in patients who did not have PD documented before such therapies. Sensitivity analysis #2: PFS endpoint determined and analyzed using the investigator's assessment, and considering clinical disease progression (symptomatic deterioration) as an event... ORR based on IRC evaluation was summarized using descriptive statistics and 95% CIs. The difference in ORR between treatment arms was compared using a stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §5.1 "Statistical Issues and Collective Evidence," p.19]*

> "There were no major statistical issues with this application. The following is a list of statistical concerns that were evaluated and resolved by the reviewer: There were some discrepancies in stratification by IVRS (interactive voice response system) versus CRF (case report form). Thus, a sensitivity analysis using the CRF stratification was conducted. The results were similar to the primary analysis using IVRS stratification. Some evidence of non-compliance at the Australian site (036007) was found during the Sanofi New Jersey inspection. There were issues with protocol compliance, dosing, etc. A sensitivity OS analysis excluding the 23 patients from site 036007 was performed. The results were similar to the primary analysis."

### 19. Tbo-filgrastim (Granix) — BLA 125294

**Sponsor:** Sicor Biotech UAB (a Teva Pharmaceuticals subsidiary; U.S. applicant: Teva Pharmaceuticals USA, Inc.)

**Indication approved:** To reduce the duration of severe neutropenia in patients with non-myeloid malignancies receiving myelosuppressive anti-cancer drugs associated with a clinically significant incidence of febrile neutropenia

**Approval date:** August 29, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** Study XM02-02 (international, multicenter, randomized, placebo- and active-controlled Phase III trial in breast cancer), no NCT registration number found (trial predates/falls outside routine ClinicalTrials.gov registration for this sponsor at the time)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, active-controlled (three-arm: tbo-filgrastim vs. placebo vs. non-US-approved filgrastim product)
- *Endpoints:* duration of severe neutropenia (DSN, Cycle 1, primary), incidence of febrile neutropenia (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* analysis of covariance/stratified chi-square-type test adjusting for treatment, country, adjuvant-vs.-metastatic therapy, and baseline ANC
- *Regulatory:* 351(a) standalone BLA (not a 351(k) biosimilar application — that pathway did not yet exist), FDA rejected the sponsor's proposed equivalence/non-inferiority framing against a non-US comparator as not relevant for U.S. regulatory purposes

**Trial design & endpoints**

- This is a supportive-care biologic BLA, and the "usual SAP/hypothesis-testing framework" used elsewhere in this census (superiority RCT against placebo or an FDA-agreed active comparator, with a pre-specified multiplicity/alpha-spending plan) is a poor fit here: the sponsor's own framing was an equivalence claim against a non-US-licensed filgrastim product, which FDA explicitly declined to accept as the basis for approval.
- Study XM02-02: international, multicenter, randomized, controlled Phase III trial in 350 chemotherapy-naive patients with high-risk Stage II-IV breast cancer receiving doxorubicin 60 mg/m² + docetaxel 75 mg/m²; three arms — tbo-filgrastim (XM02), placebo, and a non-US-approved filgrastim product — each dosed at 5 mcg/kg subcutaneously once daily starting one day post-chemotherapy for at least 5 days (up to 14) or until post-nadir ANC ≥10,000×10⁶/L
- Primary efficacy endpoint: duration of severe neutropenia (DSN) in Cycle 1 (severe neutropenia defined by ANC threshold per standard G-CSF trial convention)
- The trial had two pre-planned comparisons: tbo-filgrastim vs. placebo, and tbo-filgrastim vs. the non-US-approved filgrastim product; placebo was only ethically permissible/used in Cycle 1
- Two supporting Phase III trials (lung cancer, N=240; non-Hodgkin lymphoma, N=92) contributed primarily to the safety database rather than to the efficacy claim; ~680 patients were enrolled across the three Phase III trials, of whom 541 received tbo-filgrastim
- Result: mean DSN 1.1 days (tbo-filgrastim) vs. 3.8 days (placebo), a statistically significant difference (p<0.0001) after adjustment for treatment, country, adjuvant-vs.-metastatic chemotherapy setting, and baseline ANC
- **Critical regulatory point, stated plainly by FDA in the Summary Review:** the sponsor's proposed equivalence/non-inferiority comparison to the non-US-approved filgrastim product had not been discussed and agreed with FDA in advance, no data were submitted comparing that non-US product to U.S.-licensed Neupogen (they are legally two separate products), and no justification was given for the proposed 1-day equivalence margin. FDA therefore held that "the comparison to the non-US-approved filgrastim product is not considered relevant for regulatory purposes," and that **the demonstration of effectiveness rested solely on the tbo-filgrastim-vs.-placebo comparison** — i.e., approval was granted on ordinary superiority-to-placebo grounds, not on a biosimilar-style equivalence claim, despite the trial having been designed with an equivalence comparison in mind and despite the pivotal trial's own 2008 publication being titled around equivalence to Neupogen.
- Statistical/regulatory pathway: BLA under PHS Act §351(a) (a standalone, fully independent biologics application containing complete nonclinical/clinical pharmacology/clinical data) — the abbreviated 351(k) biosimilar pathway did not yet exist in the U.S. in 2012 (it was not used for an approval until Zarxio in 2015), even though Teva had already obtained EU marketing authorization for the same product via EMA's biosimilar pathway in 2008. This submission followed a 2010 FDA Complete Response Letter citing deficiencies including database-integrity concerns, device (pre-filled syringe) issues, missing reproductive-toxicity data, nomenclature, anti-drug-antibody characterization, pediatric-use information, and QT-prolongation potential; the August 2012 approval resolved those items without new clinical efficacy data being submitted in the resubmission cycle.

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2012/125294Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (2012) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2012/125294s0000lbl.pdf
- FDA Summary Review (Signatory Authority Review) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/125294Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (resubmission cycle; Qing Xu, PhD, concurring Mark Rothmann PhD and Rajeshwari Sridhara PhD — this document notes no new clinical study was submitted in the resubmission and refers to "Dr. Lu's statistical report" for the original submission's efficacy statistics, which was not separately located as a standalone posted PDF) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/125294Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- Pivotal publication: del Giglio A, Eniu A, Ganea-Motan D, Topuzov E, Lubenau H. "XM02 is superior to placebo and equivalent to Neupogen in reducing the duration of severe neutropenia and the incidence of febrile neutropenia in cycle 1 in breast cancer patients receiving docetaxel/doxorubicin chemotherapy." *BMC Cancer.* 2008;8:332. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2407-8-332), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19014494/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=XM02%20is%20superior%20to%20placebo%20and%20equivalent%20to%20Neupogen%20in%20reducing%20the%20duration%20of%20severe%20neutropenia)
- Supporting safety meta-analysis: Engert A, del Giglio A, Bias P, Lubenau H, Gatzemeier U, Heigener D. "Incidence of febrile neutropenia and myelotoxicity of chemotherapy: a meta-analysis of biosimilar G-CSF studies in breast cancer, lung cancer, and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma." *Onkologie.* 2009;32(10):599-604. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1159/000232580), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19816079/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Incidence%20of%20febrile%20neutropenia%20and%20myelotoxicity%20of%20chemotherapy%20biosimilar%20G-CSF%20studies)

**Other resources**

- No IPD-sharing platform participation was confirmed for this trial in this pass.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was identified for this approval.
- Regulatory context worth noting for readers of this census: this is one of the earliest FDA approvals in the "biosimilar-adjacent" supportive-care space, predating the U.S. 351(k) biosimilar approval pathway by roughly three years; the entry is retained here as a documented case where a sponsor's international equivalence-trial design did not translate directly into the U.S. regulatory argument FDA ultimately accepted.

**Reverse-engineered SAP**

Given that no standalone efficacy-statistics SAP document was located as extractable text (the Statistical Review posted for the approved supplement addresses only the resubmission cycle, which added no new clinical data), the following points reconstruct FDA's accepted analysis approach from the Summary Review and label:

- *[inferred, from FDA Summary Review p.10: "The results after adjustment for 'treatment', 'country' and 'adjuvant vs. metastatic therapy' and baseline absolute neutrophil count revealed a statistically significant difference (P< 0.0001, Χ2) in mean duration of severe neutropenia"]* — the primary analysis was a covariate-adjusted comparison of mean DSN between the tbo-filgrastim and placebo arms (chi-square-type test statistic reported), not a simple unadjusted t-test, with treatment center/country, disease setting, and baseline ANC as pre-specified adjustment covariates.
- *[inferred, from FDA Summary Review p.10: "The statistical review team performed several sensitivity analyses due to applicant's method of data imputation for missing data to ensure the robustness of the applicant's result for the primary comparison"]* — DSN in Cycle 1 relied on some imputed values for missing neutrophil-count observations, and FDA's own reanalysis under alternative imputation assumptions was needed to confirm the primary result was not an artifact of the imputation method chosen by the sponsor — i.e., a missing-data sensitivity check functionally analogous to (though not named as) the sensitivity analyses seen in this census's oncology RCTs.
- *[inferred, from FDA Summary Review p.10, "the comparison to the non-US-approved filgrastim product is not considered relevant for regulatory purposes"]* — no multiplicity adjustment for the placebo/active-comparator dual-comparison structure was needed or reported, because in the reviewer's own words the entire regulatory determination rested on the single placebo comparison; the active-comparator arm's role was effectively demoted to descriptive/supportive after review, not part of a formally tested hierarchy.

### 20. Bosutinib (Bosulif) — NDA 203341

**Sponsor:** Wyeth Pharmaceuticals Inc. (a subsidiary of Pfizer Inc.)

**Indication approved:** Chronic, accelerated, or blast phase Philadelphia chromosome-positive (Ph+) chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) in adult patients with resistance or intolerance to prior therapy

**Approval date:** September 4, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** Study 3160A4-200-WW ("Study 200"), no NCT registration identified in the FDA review materials examined for the CP CML resistant/intolerant cohort specifically

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm accelerated-approval design *(note: despite the single-arm data, FDA granted regular, not accelerated, approval — see below)*, multi-cohort Phase 1/2 study
- *Endpoints:* major cytogenetic response (MCyR) rate at week 24 (primary, CP CML cohorts), complete hematologic response (CHR) by week 48 (advanced-phase cohorts)
- *Primary analysis:* one-sample binomial hypothesis test against a fixed uninteresting-rate threshold, 4-stage group-sequential design (primary cohort), Simon 2-stage design (secondary/smaller cohorts)
- *Regulatory:* regular approval granted despite single-arm pivotal evidence; reviewer-documented methodological criticism (Simon 2-stage design used for an efficacy claim rather than its intended go/no-go screening purpose); supportive randomized trial (Study 3000/BELA) failed its primary endpoint

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 200 (3160A4-200-WW): open-label, 2-part, multi-cohort Phase 1/2 study of once-daily oral bosutinib in Philadelphia-chromosome-positive (Ph+) leukemia. Part 1 was a dose-escalation study in imatinib-resistant chronic-phase (CP) CML (18 subjects; doses 400/500/600 mg) that selected 500 mg/day for Part 2. Part 2 enrolled 571 patients total across cohorts: 288 CP CML previously treated with imatinib only (second-line), 118 CP CML previously treated with imatinib plus ≥1 other TKI (third-line-plus), 76 accelerated-phase CML, 64 blast-phase CML, plus a small Ph+ ALL cohort; 503 CML patients were in the evaluable/analysis population (received ≥1 dose, adequate baseline efficacy assessment)
- Primary objective/endpoint (label-supporting cohort): major cytogenetic response (MCyR) rate at week 24 in the imatinib-resistant, no-other-TKI-exposure CP CML cohort (second-line, 200 of the 288 patients were imatinib-resistant specifically; 88 were imatinib-intolerant)
- Secondary/exploratory endpoints: MCyR at week 24 in the imatinib-intolerant CP CML cohort (formally a secondary objective, not met per pre-specified criteria); CHR by week 48 in accelerated- and blast-phase cohorts; various smaller TKI-sequencing cohorts (e.g., dasatinib-resistant, nilotinib-resistant) treated as exploratory
- Design/statistics: the primary (imatinib-resistant CP CML) cohort was tested as H0: MCyR rate p ≤ 0.23 vs. one-sided H1: p > 0.23, one-sided α=0.05, 80% power at p=0.33, via a 4-stage group-sequential design with interim analyses at 25%/50%/75% information and a maximum planned sample size of 167 evaluable subjects. The imatinib-intolerant CP CML cohort (secondary objective) was sized via a Simon 2-stage design (H0: p≤0.56 vs. H1: p>0.73, α=0.05, β=0.2, maximum 55 patients, 16 in the first stage); several smaller cohorts (dasatinib-resistant/intolerant, nilotinib-resistant, advanced-disease subgroups) each had their own separate Simon 1- or 2-stage designs with cohort-specific "interesting"/"uninteresting" response-rate assumptions
- Results as reported by the sponsor: primary objective met — 35.5% MCyR at week 24 (95% CI 29.7-41.7) in imatinib-resistant second-line CP CML; secondary objective not met — 30% MCyR at week 24 (90% CI 21.6-39.5) in imatinib-intolerant CP CML (cumulative MCyR including maintained/achieved responders reached 61.3% in that cohort); responses were durable (e.g., 43.6% of imatinib-intolerant MCyR responders maintained response at 2 years per the FDA reviewer's own analysis)
- A separate, supportive randomized Phase III trial (Study 3160A4-3000-WW / BELA) compared bosutinib vs. imatinib in newly diagnosed CP CML, primary endpoint complete cytogenetic response (CCyR) rate at 1 year — this trial **failed to demonstrate superiority** of bosutinib over imatinib and did not support a first-line indication
- FDA's statistical reviewer explicitly flagged a design/inference problem: a Simon 2-stage design (traditionally a screening "go/no-go" tool, not intended to support a definitive efficacy conclusion) had been used for the imatinib-intolerant secondary cohort's hypothesis test, and cautioned that the pre-specified "uninteresting" response rates used across the smaller cohort designs were arbitrary
- Despite the single-arm design across all cohorts, the primary clinical reviewer recommended, and FDA granted, **regular (not accelerated) approval**, reasoning from the size and durability of the observed MCyR/CHR response rates in a resistant/intolerant, later-line population where no comparator arm was ethically feasible

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2012/203341Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (2012) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2012/203341lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Kallappa Koti, PhD reviewer cited within) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203341Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Summary Review (Signatory Authority Review, reproducing the primary Clinical Reviewer's Executive Summary) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203341Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- FDA Medical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203341Orig1s000MedR.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Cortes JE, Kantarjian HM, Brümmendorf TH, et al. "Safety and efficacy of bosutinib (SKI-606) in chronic phase Philadelphia chromosome-positive chronic myeloid leukemia patients with resistance or intolerance to imatinib." *Blood.* 2011;118(17):4567-4576. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1182/blood-2011-05-355594), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21865346/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Safety%20and%20efficacy%20of%20bosutinib%20%28SKI-606%29%20in%20chronic%20phase%20Philadelphia%20chromosome-positive%20chronic%20myeloid%20leukemia%20patients%20with%20resistance%20or%20intolerance%20to%20imatinib)

**Other resources**

- No IPD-sharing platform participation was confirmed for Study 200 in this pass.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was identified for this approval.
- This is a useful contrast case within the census: contemporaneous CML TKIs (dasatinib, nilotinib) received *accelerated* approval in the newly-diagnosed setting on single-arm/surrogate grounds per the FDA reviewer's own comparison table, whereas bosutinib's later-line resistant/intolerant indication was granted *regular* approval on single-arm response-rate data, illustrating that "single-arm" and "accelerated" are not synonymous in FDA's own approval mechanism choices.

**Reverse-engineered SAP**

No standalone sponsor SAP document was located as a separate posted PDF; the points below are traceable directly to genuine verbatim FDA Statistical Review and Summary Review text (quoted above and below), so this section blends verbatim reviewer commentary with light inference about the overall inferential logic:

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review p.4]* — "The primary objective was the determination of efficacy in patients with CP CML resistant to imatinib who have had no prior exposure to other tyrosine kinase inhibitors. The determination of efficacy was based on MCyR rate at 24 weeks. The hypotheses on the MCyR rate at 24 weeks (p) were H0: p ≤ 0.23 against the 1-sided alternative H1: p > 0.23. Testing was based on a one-sided type 1 error rate of 0.05 and 80% power at p = 0.33. The design of the primary cohort incorporated a 4-stage group sequential design, with interim analyses at 25%, 50%, and 75% information fraction based on a maximum sample size of 167 evaluable subjects for the imatinib-resistant cohort."
- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review p.3, reviewer's own methodological criticism]* — "Additionally, a Simon 2-stage design appears to have been used in the evaluation of MCyR at week 24 in patients with imatinib-intolerant disease. A Simon 2-stage design is traditionally a design to address a 'go no-go' question, not for drawing conclusion on efficacy."
- *[verbatim, FDA Summary Review p.5, primary Clinical Reviewer's Executive Summary]* — "This reviewer recommends regular approval of Bosulif (bosutinib) for the treatment of chronic, accelerated, or blast phase Philadelphia chromosome positive (Ph+) chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) in adult patients with resistance to, or intolerance of prior therapy... The pivotal trial was a Phase 2, single arm trial which required all subjects to have previously been treated with imatinib."
- *[inferred, from the absence of any comparator/randomization language throughout both reviews and the explicit "single arm trial" characterization above]* — because there was no concurrent control group, FDA's benefit-risk judgment rested on the observed MCyR/CHR magnitude and durability (e.g., the FDA reviewer's own follow-up calculation that 43.6% of imatinib-intolerant MCyR responders maintained response at 2 years) compared against literature/historical expectations for this heavily pretreated population, rather than any within-study comparative test — the standard inferential logic FDA applies to later-line single-arm oncology submissions where randomization is not considered ethical or feasible.

### 21. Choline C 11 Injection (unbranded) — NDA 203155

**Sponsor:** Mayo Clinic (Department of Radiology / PET Radiochemistry Facility, Rochester, MN)

**Indication approved:** PET imaging agent to identify sites of recurrent prostate cancer in patients with rising serum PSA (biochemical recurrence) after prior treatment, when standard imaging is negative or non-informative

**Approval date:** September 12, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** No single pivotal trial — approval basis was (1) a systematic review of the published literature and (2) an unpublished retrospective chart review of the Mayo Clinic's own clinical experience (September 2007-November 2010); no ClinicalTrials.gov registration was identified for either evidence source

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* diagnostic performance study (retrospective, single-institution chart review; not a therapeutic-efficacy RCT)
- *Endpoints:* imaging sensitivity and specificity against a composite reference/"truth" standard (histopathology, conventional imaging, or ≥50% PSA decline after targeted salvage radiotherapy of choline-avid lesions)
- *Primary analysis:* descriptive diagnostic-accuracy statistics (sensitivity, specificity) computed against the composite truth standard, stratified by primary-treatment subgroup (radical prostatectomy vs. other)
- *Regulatory:* NDA required under the FDA Modernization Act of 1997's PET-drug cGMP transition provisions (21 CFR Part 212), rather than a conventional new-molecular-entity efficacy-supplement pathway; approval basis modeled on FDA's earlier literature-based reviews for other clinically-used PET drugs (FDG, ammonia N-13)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- This is a diagnostic radiopharmaceutical NDA, not a therapeutic drug submission, and the usual SAP/hypothesis-testing/multiplicity framework used elsewhere in this census does not really apply: there was no randomization, no control arm, no formal primary/secondary endpoint hierarchy, and no alpha-controlled significance testing. The relevant statistical questions were about diagnostic accuracy (sensitivity/specificity) against a reference standard, evaluated descriptively.
- Regulatory mechanism: Choline C 11 had been used clinically at Mayo Clinic for years under provisions of the FDA Modernization Act of 1997, which permitted continued use of PET drugs already in clinical practice until FDA finalized PET-specific cGMP regulations (December 2009), which then triggered a requirement that sponsors submit NDAs/ANDAs by June 12, 2012 for all such PET drugs still in use — this NDA exists because of that regulatory deadline, not because of a conventional drug-development program.
- At a pre-NDA meeting (February 8, 2011), FDA agreed the sponsor could rely on a systematic literature review plus its own institutional experience rather than a prospective sponsor-run clinical trial, consistent with precedent set by FDA's earlier literature-based approvals of other PET drugs (fludeoxyglucose F18 for oncology, reviewed by Dr. Florence Houn; FDG for cardiac use, Dr. Victor Raczkowski; ammonia N-13 for cardiac use, Drs. Houn and Castillo)
- Evidence source 1 — systematic literature review: sponsor searched PubMed (searched May 8, 2011, terms "C11 choline + prostate cancer"), applying inclusion/exclusion criteria that excluded reports focused on tracer radiochemistry/biodistribution, technology-update pieces, non-choline-C11 tracers, and likely-duplicate reports; of 20 initially identified publications, 11 were judged pertinent to the restaging-after-therapy indication (2 of those 11 actually used choline F18 rather than C11); reviewers classified included studies as 3 prospective-design and 6 retrospective-design reports and gave priority weight to prospective designs with imaging results compared against histopathology/another reference standard
- Evidence source 2 (basis for the label's actual Clinical Studies section) — Mayo Clinic retrospective chart review: not based on a written clinical protocol but on a data-collection format/table applied to existing medical records; examined 231 patients imaged with Choline C11 PET between September 2007 and November 2010, of whom 176 met the biochemical-recurrence (BCR) case definition (2 PSA measurements 3 months apart, post-prostatectomy; nadir+2 ng/mL post-radiation/cryoablation; or a steady PSA rise on primary ADT)
- "Truth standard" (reference standard) for a scan read as positive: >50% PSA decline after selective irradiation of choline-avid lesions, histologic confirmation, or confirmation by conventional imaging; "true negative" was defined by negative histopathology or negative conventional imaging; a truth standard was unavailable for 17 of the 176 patients
- Results: among the 159 patients with an assignable truth standard, 44 read negative and 114 (with the remaining split across true/false status) read positive; overall sensitivity 93%, specificity 76%; in the subgroup of 126 patients who had undergone primary radical prostatectomy (where the truth standard was confined to pathology or imaging alone), sensitivity rose to 95% and specificity to 86%; PET positivity was more common at higher serum PSA values
- FDA noted material limitations of this evidence base: the retrospective review was not conducted under a written protocol until after FDA requested one; the sponsor's April 2012 submission acknowledged there was no follow-up data on 35 patients and no information on what specifically prompted biopsy or biopsy-site selection; images were interpreted with knowledge of clinical findings (i.e., not blinded to clinical context) — a limitation FDA's review explicitly notes without rejecting the overall submission
- The proposed labeling's Clinical Studies section is based entirely on this Mayo Clinic experience (not on the literature review), and cites the experience via abstracts published in *The Journal of Urology*

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2012/203155Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (2012) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2012/203155s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Summary Review (Signatory Authority Review; signed by Rafel D. Rieves, MD) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203155Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- FDA Medical Review (primary reviewer William Dickerson, MD; contributing reviewers Lan Huang, MD and colleagues) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203155Orig1s000MedR.pdf
- FDA prior literature-based PET drug reviews referenced as precedent (FDG oncology/cardiac, ammonia N-13, reviewed by Drs. Houn, Raczkowski, and Castillo per the Summary Review) are cited in the FDA Summary Review above; no separately working standalone URL for those older PET-drug reviews was confirmed in this pass (FDA's website restructuring since 2012 has broken the original ucm-prefixed link).
- No single pivotal-trial publication exists for this NDA (evidence was a literature synthesis plus an unpublished institutional chart review); the Mayo Clinic's own choline C11 experience was summarized only in conference abstracts in *The Journal of Urology*, as cited in the label, which were not independently verified via PubMed/DOI lookup in this pass since they are abstracts rather than indexed full articles.

**Other resources**

- Not applicable in the usual IPD/data-sharing sense — there is no randomized trial or industry sponsor data-sharing program relevant to this NDA.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was identified for this approval.
- This entry is a deliberate departure from this census's usual RCT-centric format: it is included specifically to document a case where "the SAP" is properly understood as a retrospective chart-review analysis plan for a diagnostic-accuracy study, not a therapeutic hypothesis test, and where FDA's own approval mechanism (literature-based review under the PET drug transition provisions) differs structurally from a standard NDA efficacy supplement.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, quoting the sponsor's retrospective-review "statistical analytical plan" dated February 2, 2011, p.8]*

> "This was a retrospective review of data extracted and statistically analyzed from hospital charts of patients who developed biochemical recurrence (BCR) after primary treatment failure of prostate cancer. Patients' charts were consecutively selected if they underwent a Choline C 11 PET scan at Mayo Clinic within the time interval September 2007 through November 2010 so as not to exclude or select cases. This time frame was selected because the Mayo Clinic clinical program in Choline C 11 PET began in September, 2007."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, quoting the sponsor's April 17, 2012 submission clarifying the retrospective study's limitations, p.8]*

> "Follow-up of the patients was not part of this retrospective study. Any reference to recurrence was to the status of disease at the time of the Choline scan and/or immediate medical status as determined by the summation of all of the testing at that time. Therefore there is no follow-up data on the 35 patients. We likewise have no information on what prompted biopsy as the data was not collected prospectively as to what information was used to make this decision or how a decision was made on selecting a location for biopsy."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, reviewer's own description of the truth standard and reported diagnostic-accuracy results, p.8]*

> "The sponsor's major findings are described in Dr. Wilkerson's reports (e.g., sensitivity/specificity, etc). The 'positive' truth standard definition includes 'a decrease in PSA> 50% after selective irradiation of choline-avid lesions' or histologic confirmation or confirmation by conventional imaging. A 'true negative' was denoted by negative histopathology or 'negative conventional imaging.' Images were interpreted with knowledge of clinical findings. Among the 176 reported patients, 44 were reported as 'negative' and 114 were reported as 'positive.' A truth standard was missing for 17 of the 176 subjects; among the remaining 159 subjects the sensitivity was reported as 93% and the specificity as 76%. The report notes that the sensitivity (95%) and specificity results (86%) are numerically higher in the subset of men who had undergone primary RP (n = 126) in whom the truth standard was confined to pathology or imaging."

### 22. Regorafenib (Stivarga) — NDA 203085 (original approval)

**Sponsor:** Bayer HealthCare Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) previously treated with fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-based chemotherapy, an anti-VEGF therapy, and (if KRAS wild-type) an anti-EGFR therapy

**Approval date:** September 27, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** CORRECT (Study 14387), NCT01103323

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven trial
- *Endpoints:* overall survival (OS) (primary); progression-free survival (PFS) and objective response rate (ORR) / disease control rate (DCR) (key secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, Kaplan-Meier estimation, stratified Cox proportional-hazards model, Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test
- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (PFS→ORR)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design, Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function, O'Brien-Fleming boundary, Data Monitoring Committee (DMC/DSMB)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 14387 (CORRECT): international, multicenter, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trial of regorafenib 160 mg/day (3 weeks on/1 week off) plus best supportive care (BSC) vs. placebo plus BSC, in mCRC patients previously treated with (or intolerant of) fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-based chemotherapy, bevacizumab, and (if KRAS wild-type) cetuximab/panitumumab; 760 patients randomized (505 regorafenib : 255 placebo) at 114 centers in 16 countries
- Randomization centrally stratified by: prior anti-VEGF therapy (yes/no — turned out degenerate since all enrolled patients had received bevacizumab), time from diagnosis of metastatic disease (≥18 vs. <18 months), and geographic region (Region 1: North America/W. Europe/Israel/Australia vs. Region 2: Asia vs. Region 3: South America/Turkey/E. Europe); Asia enrollment capped at ≤250 patients per protocol
- Primary endpoint: overall survival (OS), ITT population, time from randomization to death from any cause; patients lost to follow-up with no post-randomization contact were censored at day 1
- Key secondary endpoints tested in a pre-specified hierarchical order (PFS, then ORR): PFS was investigator-assessed per RECIST v1.1; FDA's primary PFS analysis excluded investigator-called "clinical progression" events as insufficiently objective, retaining only radiologically/pathologically documented progression. Disease control rate (DCR) was a protocol secondary objective, but the sponsor told FDA in April 2012 it would not be used for a labeling claim, so FDA's review did not evaluate it
- Sample size: 582 OS events (~690 patients) for 90% power to detect HR=0.75 at two-sided α=0.05, assuming 4.5- vs. 6.0-month median OS
- Two planned OS interim analyses (futility look at ~174 deaths/30%; combined efficacy/futility look at ~408 deaths/70%) using a Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function with an O'Brien-Fleming-type boundary; the DMC recommended stopping after the second interim look (432 deaths observed, 74% information, allocated nominal two-sided α=0.018) crossed the efficacy boundary, with an actual stratified log-rank p=0.0102
- ORR was analyzed via a stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test and showed no benefit (1% vs. 0.4%, p=0.38) — FDA's statistical reviewer recommended the label reflect that regorafenib "does not work on the ORR at all"

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2012/203085Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2012/203085lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Huanyu (Jade) Chen, PhD, Division of Biometrics V; concurred Kun He, Rajeshwari Sridhara) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203085Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (CORRECT) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01103323 (no protocol/SAP documents posted; trial registered 2010, before sponsor document-posting norms took hold)
- Pivotal publication: Grothey A, et al. "Regorafenib monotherapy for previously treated metastatic colorectal cancer (CORRECT): an international, multicentre, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial." *Lancet.* 2013;381(9863):303-312. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(12)61900-X>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23177514/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Regorafenib%20monotherapy%20for%20previously%20treated%20metastatic%20colorectal%20cancer%20%28CORRECT%29%3A%20an%20international%2C%20multicentre%2C%20randomised%2C%20placebo-controlled%2C%20phase%203%20trial)

**Other resources**

- Bayer participates in Vivli.org for patient-level data sharing, but its stated commitment covers medicines/indications approved on or after January 1, 2014 — regorafenib's 2012 mCRC approval predates that cutoff, so trial-specific IPD availability for CORRECT was not confirmed here.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was identified for this application.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.5 "Interim Analysis," p.10]*

> "According to SAP, two interim analyses were planned. The first interim OS analysis for futility was planned at approximately 174 deaths (30%) at 15.5 months. The second OS interim analysis for efficacy and futility was planned at approximately 408 deaths (70%) at 23.5 months. The Lan-DeMets alpha spending function with an O'Brien-Fleming type of boundary was used to adjust alpha for the 2nd efficacy interim and final analyses."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.6 "Statistical Methodologies," p.11]*

> "The analysis for OS was performed using a stratified log-rank test, stratified by the same stratification factors as used for randomization... The hazard ratio (HR) and 95% confidence interval (CI) of REG/BSC over the PBO/BSC were estimated by a stratified Cox regression procedure... The analysis for ORR was performed using a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test adjusting for the same stratification factors at randomization... A hierarchical procedure of testing secondary endpoints in the order of PFS and ORR was proposed."

*[verbatim, FDA reviewer commentary on a degenerate stratification factor, p.11]*

> "Because all patients received prior VEGF therapy, this reviewer excluded prior VEGF therapy from the stratification log-rank test and stratified CMH test."

*[verbatim, FDA reviewer commentary on the PFS endpoint definition, p.9]*

> "Due to potential subjectivity in clinical assessment, the investigator defined clinical PD event is not included as PD event for purposes of determining PFS. Progression is defined by the objective pathologic or radiological findings. This reviewer considered PFS results excluding all of the clinical PD events as FDA's primary analysis on PFS."

This is a case where the SAP held up almost exactly as pre-specified — the stratified log-rank/Cox primary analysis, group-sequential OS monitoring, and PFS→ORR testing hierarchy were all executed as planned — with FDA's only substantive changes being a data-driven stratification-factor exclusion (VEGF pretreatment was non-informative because it applied to 100% of patients) and a stricter PFS censoring rule that excluded subjective "clinical progression" calls from the primary analysis.

### 23. Omacetaxine Mepesuccinate (Synribo) — NDA 203585 (original, accelerated approval)

**Sponsor:** IVAX International GmbH / Teva Branded Pharmaceutical Products R&D, Inc. (applicant of record on the approval letter; the NDA itself was submitted by Cephalon, Inc., a Teva subsidiary); originally developed by ChemGenex Pharmaceuticals

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with chronic phase or accelerated phase chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) with resistance and/or intolerance to two or more approved tyrosine kinase inhibitors (imatinib, dasatinib, nilotinib)

**Approval date:** October 26, 2012 (accelerated approval; converted to regular approval in February 2014 on the basis of 24-month follow-up data from the same two trials)

**Pivotal trial:** No randomized pivotal trial exists. The basis for approval was Analysis CML-300, a regulatory-agreed, post-hoc pooled subset analysis of patients drawn from two single-arm Phase II studies — CML-202, NCT00375219, and CML-203, NCT00462943

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label Phase II study, post-hoc pooled subset analysis across trials, regulatory-agreed
- *Endpoints:* major cytogenetic response (MCyR) rate — chronic phase; major hematologic response (MaHR) rate — accelerated phase
- *Primary analysis:* descriptive response-rate analysis with exact one-sided 95% confidence limit; no formal hypothesis test (single-arm, no concurrent control)
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.500 / Subpart H; postmarketing requirement (PMR) to confirm/convert accelerated approval; FDA Advisory Committee meeting held for an earlier, withdrawn NDA using the same two trials (not this application)

**No genuine sponsor SAP or protocol is publicly posted, and — more fundamentally — no prospective, hypothesis-testing SAP of the kind the rest of this census documents was ever executed.** This was a single-arm, response-rate-based accelerated approval, not a randomized controlled trial with a pre-specified primary hypothesis test. FDA's own statistical reviewer stated this plainly: "Efficacy data for this application came from single-arm studies without any pre-specified statistical considerations. Therefore, there is no formal statistical conclusions can be made" (FDA Statistical Review, Executive Summary, p.6). The section below is a **Reverse-engineered SAP**, reconstructed from FDA's Statistical Review, Cross-Discipline Team Leader Review, and the approved label, rather than a verbatim sponsor SAP quote.

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Regulatory history: omacetaxine was first submitted (NDA 22-374, ChemGenex) for CML patients with the Bcr-Abl T315I mutation, based on Studies CML-202 and CML-203. FDA's Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) voted 7-1 on March 22, 2010 that a well-characterized companion diagnostic for T315I would be required before approval; NDA 22-374 received a Complete Response letter (April 2010) and was withdrawn (February 2011)
- At a June 30, 2010 Type A meeting, FDA and the sponsor agreed a combined dataset from a "homogeneous patient population" across CML-202 and CML-203 — patients who failed imatinib (CML-202) or failed/were intolerant of ≥2 TKIs (CML-203) — could support a third-line NDA; this became Analysis CML-300 (a subset of 122 patients from the two trials who had received ≥2 approved TKIs with documented resistance/intolerance to dasatinib and/or nilotinib)
- Cephalon (by then a Teva subsidiary, having acquired ChemGenex in 2011) submitted NDA 203585 on March 30, 2012 using Analysis CML-300 as the sole efficacy basis; no new trial was conducted for this application
- CML-202 and CML-203 were both open-label, single-arm Phase II trials: omacetaxine 1.25 mg/m² SC BID for 14 days per 28-day cycle (induction, up to 6 cycles), then 7 days per 28-day cycle (maintenance, up to 24 months)
- Primary efficacy endpoint for chronic-phase (CP) patients: major cytogenetic response (MCyR = complete + partial cytogenetic response); for accelerated-phase (AP) patients: major hematologic response (MaHR = complete hematologic response or no evidence of leukemia), and/or MCyR — all responses adjudicated by an independent Data Monitoring Committee (DMC), not investigator assessment alone
- No sample size was calculated for Analysis CML-300 ("the study size was not driven by any statistical considerations" — FDA Statistical Review); FDA's efficacy analysis population excluded 3 CP patients from two sites (22, 30) found by FDA's Division of Scientific Investigations to have regulatory deviations, leaving 119 evaluable patients (78 CP, 41 AP)
- Two pre-specified subgroup analyses were run (by number of prior approved TKIs; by resistance vs. intolerance category), with no formal between-subgroup statistical testing
- Response rate was reported with an exact confidence interval only; FDA additionally recalculated response rates excluding patients who already met the response definition at study entry ("best response at study entry"), producing lower, more conservative rates (18.4% CP, 14.3% AP vs. the sponsor's 19.8%/26.8%) that were adopted in the approved label in place of the sponsor's original figures
- PMR #1 (required under Subpart H to convert accelerated to regular approval) required 24-month median follow-up data from the same two trials; this was satisfied, and FDA converted the approval to regular approval in February 2014

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter (accelerated approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2012/203585Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2012/203585lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Chia-Wen Ko, PhD, Division of Biometrics 5; concurred Mark Rothmann, Rajeshwari Sridhara) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203585Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Cross-Discipline Team Leader Review (Virginia Kwitkowski, MD) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203585Orig1s000CrossR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov records: CML-202 — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00375219 ; CML-203 — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00462943 (neither has posted protocol/SAP documents)
- Pivotal publications: Cortes J, et al. "Phase 2 study of subcutaneous omacetaxine mepesuccinate for chronic-phase chronic myeloid leukemia patients resistant to or intolerant of tyrosine kinase inhibitors." *Am J Hematol.* 2013;88(5):350-354. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1002/ajh.23408), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23468307/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Phase%202%20study%20of%20subcutaneous%20omacetaxine%20mepesuccinate%20for%20chronic-phase%20chronic%20myeloid%20leukemia%20patients%20resistant%20to%20or%20intolerant%20of%20tyrosine%20kinase%20inhibitors) — and — Cortes JE, et al. "Final analysis of the efficacy and safety of omacetaxine mepesuccinate in patients with chronic- or accelerated-phase chronic myeloid leukemia: Results with 24 months of follow-up." *Cancer.* 2015;121(10):1637-1644 (the confirmatory 24-month follow-up analysis submitted for PMR #1/conversion to regular approval). [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1002/cncr.29240), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25586015/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Final%20analysis%20of%20the%20efficacy%20and%20safety%20of%20omacetaxine%20mepesuccinate%20in%20patients%20with%20chronic-%20or%20accelerated-phase%20chronic%20myeloid%20leukemia%3A%20Results%20with%2024%20months%20of%20follow-up)

**Other resources**

- No Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere availability was identified for CML-202/CML-203; Teva's general data-sharing commitments were not confirmed as covering this program specifically.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for NDA 203585 itself. An ODAC meeting was held March 22, 2010 for the earlier, withdrawn NDA 22-374 (T315I indication, same two underlying trials), documented above.

**Reverse-engineered SAP** *(each point traced to FDA review/label text; there is no genuine sponsor SAP for a prospective hypothesis-testing trial because none was run)*

- **No formal statistical hypothesis test underlies the approval** *[inferred from: FDA Statistical Review Executive Summary — "Statistical issues with this application include: 1) The application is not supported by randomized studies; 2) Analysis CML-300 sample size is not driven by any statistical considerations... Efficacy data for this application came from single-arm studies without any pre-specified statistical considerations. Therefore, there is no formal statistical conclusions can be made" (p.5-6)]*. Response rates are reported descriptively with an exact one-sided 95% lower confidence limit, not compared against a concurrent control or a pre-specified null response rate.
- **Response-rate thresholds function as an implicit historical-control comparison** *[inferred from: FDA's Cross-Discipline Team Leader Review's background section, which frames the applicable regulatory standard by reciting how dasatinib and nilotinib were each granted accelerated approval on single-arm Phase II response rates in the same post-imatinib setting — "MCyR has been accepted as the efficacy endpoint for patients with Chronic Phase CML. Either MaHR or CHR have been accepted as efficacy endpoints for Accelerated Phase and Blast Phase CML in previous approvals" (CrossR, p.4)]*. No formal statistical comparison against those prior drugs' response rates was conducted in the omacetaxine review; the analogy functioned as regulatory precedent, not a pre-specified statistical test.
- **DMC adjudication substituted for randomization/blinding as the main safeguard against assessment bias** *[inferred from: the label's statement that "Responses were adjudicated by an independent Data Monitoring Committee (DMC)" (Label §14) and the Statistical Review's use of "DMC adjudicated treatment response" as the analysis-population endpoint (Table 1)]*. Because there was no concurrent control arm, independent DMC adjudication — rather than randomization — was the design's primary defense against biased response assessment.
- **FDA-driven, not sponsor-driven, sensitivity re-analysis set the labeled response rate** *[inferred from: the Statistical Review's Table 11 recalculation excluding patients who "presented with best response at study entry," lowering reported rates from the sponsor's 19.8%/26.8% to FDA's 18.4%/14.3%, and the reviewer's explicit labeling recommendation to "Replace the applicant's results on response rate and duration of response with the FDA results, which did not include patients who were characterized by DMC as responders at study entry" (p.19)]* — the approved label's Table 4/Table 5 (76 CP / 35 AP patients, 18.4%/14.3%) confirms FDA's numbers, not the sponsor's, were adopted.
- **Accelerated-approval structure implies an unstated confirmatory-trial condition, made explicit in the label and CrossR** *[inferred from/confirmed by: the label's boxed statement "This indication is based upon response rate. There are no trials verifying an improvement in disease-related symptoms or increased survival with SYNRIBO" (Label, Indications and Usage) and the Cross-Discipline Team Leader Review's PMR #1, requiring 24-month follow-up data from the same two trials "to convert the accelerated approval to regular approval" under Subpart H (CrossR, p.26)]*.

### 24. Cabozantinib (Cometriq) — NDA 203756 (original approval)

**Sponsor:** Exelixis, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Progressive, unresectable locally advanced or metastatic medullary thyroid cancer (MTC)

**Approval date:** November 29, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** EXAM (Study XL184-301), NCT00704730

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven trial, Special Protocol Assessment (SPA) agreement
- *Endpoints:* progression-free survival (PFS) (primary); overall survival (OS) and objective response rate (ORR) (key secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, Kaplan-Meier estimation, stratified Cox proportional-hazards model, Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test
- *Multiplicity:* parallel split-alpha testing of secondary endpoints — ORR at two-sided α=0.01 and OS at two-sided α=0.04, both contingent on a significant primary PFS result
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design (one planned OS interim analysis), Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function, O'Brien-Fleming boundary

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study XL184-301 (EXAM): international, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trial of cabozantinib 140 mg/day vs. placebo in patients ≥18 years with unresectable, locally advanced, or metastatic MTC and documented disease progression within 14 months of screening; 330 patients randomized (219 cabozantinib : 111 placebo) at 90 sites in 23 countries
- Received a Special Protocol Assessment (SPA) agreement from FDA in June 2008; randomization used a permuted-block design stratified by age (≤65 vs. >65) and prior TKI receipt (yes/no)
- Primary endpoint: progression-free survival (PFS), IRC-assessed per mRECIST for the large majority of patients (Protocol Amendment 2, implemented after 89% of patients had enrolled, switched the on-study PD determination used for treatment-discontinuation decisions to investigator assessment, but IRC assessment remained the basis for the primary PFS analysis); PFS defined as time from randomization to the earlier of IRC-determined progression or death from any cause, with detailed pre-specified censoring rules (right-censoring for long gaps since last tumor assessment, for post-baseline anti-cancer therapy start, etc.)
- Key secondary endpoints, tested only if PFS was significant: objective response rate (ORR, tested at two-sided α=0.01) and overall survival (OS, tested at two-sided α=0.04) — a parallel, split-alpha (not sequential) testing structure for the two secondaries once the primary endpoint gated the family
- Sample size: 138 PFS events for 90% power to detect HR=0.571 (log-rank test, two-sided α=0.05); separately, 217 deaths were planned to give 80% power to detect HR=0.667 for OS (two-sided α=0.04, per the alpha-spending allocation)
- One planned OS interim analysis at ~31% information fraction (~67 deaths, coincident with the primary PFS analysis), with an expected interim significance level of 0.00006 under a Lan-DeMets O'Brien-Fleming-type alpha-spending function; the final OS analysis was planned at 217 deaths at an expected 0.04 level
- Results: the primary PFS analysis was strongly positive (median PFS 11.2 vs. 4.0 months; stratified HR 0.28, 95% CI 0.19-0.40; stratified log-rank p<0.0001), ORR was also positive (27% vs. 0%, stratified CMH p<0.0001), but OS did not reach significance at either the 44%-information first interim look (HR 0.997) or a later 120-day-update/75%-information analysis (HR 0.825, p=0.24) — FDA's statistical reviewer attributed this to the trial's OS assumptions having been "too optimistic" for the treatment arm (33 assumed vs. ~26 observed median months), and recommended the label include the PFS/ORR results but not present the immature OS analysis as a treatment-benefit claim

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2012/203756Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2012/203756lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Yuan Li Shen, PhD, reviewing statistician; concurred Kun He, Rajeshwari Sridhara) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203756Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203756Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (EXAM) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00704730 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)
- Pivotal publication: Elisei R, et al. "Cabozantinib in progressive medullary thyroid cancer." *J Clin Oncol.* 2013;31(29):3639-3646. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.2012.48.4659), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24002501/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Cabozantinib%20in%20progressive%20medullary%20thyroid%20cancer)

**Other resources**

- No confirmed Exelixis participation in Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere was identified; trial-specific IPD availability for EXAM was not confirmed.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this application (FDA Medical Review, §9.3: "This application was not brought to the Oncology Drug Advisor Committee (ODAC)").

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3 "Statistical Evaluation," p.3]*

> "The final draft statistical analysis plan (SAP) for Special Protocol Assessment (SPA) was dated 4/21/2008... 2/7/2011: Clarified the method used to address missing or inadequate tumor assessments for PFS and ORR per FDA's feedback; Clarified details of planned supportive analyses and added additional sensitivity analysis of PFS based on investigator assessment of radiographic progression."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, "Sample Size Calculation" and "Interim Analysis," p.6]*

> "Assuming exponential distribution of PFS time and proportional hazards, 138 PFS events were required for this study to have a 90% power to detect a hazard ratio (HR) of 0.571 based on a log-rank test and a 2-sided 5% significance level... One interim analysis was planned at 31% information level (approximately 67 deaths) when the primary efficacy analysis on PFS was performed. If the result of the primary endpoint (PFS) was significant, the two key secondary endpoints would be tested in parallel. The ORR and OS would be tested at 2-sided 0.01 and 0.04 levels, respectively. An interim analysis of OS was expected to be performed at the 0.00006 level per a Lan-DeMets O'Brien-Fleming alpha spending function based on an expected 31% information level."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.3 "Statistical Methodologies," p.14]*

> "The statistical analysis method for PFS was based on the stratified log rank test at a 2-sided 0.05 α level using the stratification factors documented based on the IVRS... The HR would be estimated based on the stratified Cox's proportional hazards model."

*[verbatim, FDA reviewer's concluding assessment of the OS shortfall, p.30-31]*

> "The main issue from this study is that the OS analysis was not nominally statistically significant. In the protocol, the assumed median OS time in the placebo arm (i.e. 21 months) appears to be close to the actual result observed based on the updated OS analysis (20.3 months). However, the assumed median OS time in the Cabozantinib arm of the study design was too optimistic (i.e. 33 months for the assumed median OS time vs. 26 months for the actual result observed from the study). The reason of lacking survival benefit is unclear."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §5.3 "Labeling Recommendations," p.32]*

> "This statistical review supported the inclusion of results from the progression free survival and objective response rate, but not the overall survival results, based on the pre-specified statistical analysis plan. The overall survival data is not mature at this time, the current OS data is not reliable."

This is a case of an SPA-agreed design holding up almost entirely as pre-specified (primary PFS analysis, stratification, alpha-spending, censoring rules) — the one notable gap being a key secondary endpoint (OS) that the SAP anticipated testing but that had not, per FDA's own diagnosis, reached significance because the underlying survival assumption for the experimental arm was over-optimistic at the design stage, not because of any deviation in trial conduct.

### 25. Ponatinib (Iclusig) — NDA 203469 (original, accelerated approval)

**Sponsor:** ARIAD Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with chronic phase, accelerated phase, or blast phase chronic myeloid leukemia (CML), or Philadelphia chromosome-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia (Ph+ ALL), resistant or intolerant to prior tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy, including patients with the T315I mutation

**Approval date:** December 14, 2012 (accelerated approval)

**Pivotal trial:** PACE (Ponatinib Ph+ ALL and CML Evaluation), Study AP24534-10-201, NCT01207440

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label Phase 2 study, multi-cohort design (six pre-specified disease/mutation-status cohorts)
- *Endpoints:* major cytogenetic response (MCyR, primary, CP-CML cohorts); major hematologic response (MaHR, primary, AP-CML and BP-CML/Ph+ ALL cohorts)
- *Primary analysis:* one-sample binomial hypothesis test per cohort against pre-specified null/alternative response-rate pairs, exact 95% confidence intervals
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval (surrogate response-rate endpoints); FDA-conducted independent re-adjudication of response endpoints; 2013 post-marketing partial clinical hold/voluntary marketing suspension for arterial occlusive events (context, not part of the original approval basis)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study AP24534-10-201 (PACE): multicenter, international, single-arm, open-label Phase 2 trial of oral ponatinib 45 mg once daily until progression, in North America, Europe/Australia, and Asia, in patients with CML (any phase) or Ph+ ALL who were resistant or intolerant to dasatinib or nilotinib ("R/I"), or who carried the T315I mutation regardless of prior TKI ("T315I") — T315I status was determined by centralized mutation testing to standardize cohort assignment
- Patients were assigned to one of six pre-specified cohorts by disease phase and mutation status: Cohort A (CP-CML R/I, n=203), Cohort B (CP-CML T315I, n=64), Cohort C (AP-CML R/I, n=65), Cohort D (AP-CML T315I, n=18), Cohort E (BP-CML/Ph+ ALL R/I, n=48), Cohort F (BP-CML/Ph+ALL T315I, n=46) — 444 patients total (267 CP-CML, 83 AP-CML, 94 BP-CML/Ph+ALL)
- Primary endpoints, tested separately per cohort as one-sample proportion tests against pre-specified null (uninteresting) vs. alternative (interesting) response rates: MCyR at any time by week 12, in the CP-CML cohorts (R/I: H0 rate 20% vs. H1 35%; T315I: H0 10% vs. H1 35%); MaHR by week 12, in the AP-CML and BP-CML/Ph+ALL cohorts (H0 10% vs. H1 30% in each)
- Every cohort met its pre-specified objective of ruling out the null response rate: observed MCyR was 48.8% (R/I CP-CML) and 70.3% (T315I CP-CML); observed MaHR was 60.0% (R/I AP-CML), 50.0% (T315I AP-CML), 35.4% (R/I BP-CML/Ph+ALL), and 32.6% (T315I BP-CML/Ph+ALL) — all far exceeding the pre-specified alternative rates, and all 95% CIs cleared the null threshold with margin
- A notable design/enrollment issue documented by FDA: the AP-CML T315I cohort was planned for 40 patients (89% power at α=0.05 to rule out a 10% MaHR rate against a 30% alternative) but only 18 were actually analyzed; FDA's reviewer explicitly checked whether under-enrollment invalidated the conclusion, finding the observed 95% CI (26%, 74%) still ruled out 10% even under a hypothetical fully-enrolled-but-no-additional-responders scenario (which would have given (11%, 38%))
- A second design nuance: because T315I-cohort enrollment was still open when the R/I CP-CML cohort's planned enrollment of 100 was reached, the sponsor continued enrolling into R/I CP-CML beyond the original target; FDA's reviewer performed a supportive sensitivity analysis restricted to the first 100 R/I CP-CML patients enrolled (who had more follow-up time by the data cutoff) and obtained a similar MCyR rate (48.0%) to the full-cohort primary analysis, addressing a potential "longer follow-up window inflates response" concern
- FDA independently re-adjudicated response endpoints rather than relying solely on the sponsor's assessments (e.g., FDA's own analysis of MaHR/CHR/NEL components in the AP-CML and BP-CML/Ph+ALL cohorts produced response and duration-of-response figures that differed somewhat from the sponsor's, e.g., median duration of MaHR in BP-CML/Ph+ALL was 4.7 months per the sponsor vs. 3.5 months per FDA's own analysis)
- No randomization, no concurrent control arm, and no formal multiplicity adjustment across the six cohorts — each cohort's hypothesis test stood on its own, consistent with the accelerated-approval, response-rate-as-surrogate framework used for other later-line CML/Ph+ ALL TKIs

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter (accelerated approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2012/203469Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (2012) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2012/203469lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203469Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Summary Review (Signatory Authority Review) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203469Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- FDA Medical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203469Orig1s000MedR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (PACE) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01207440 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)
- Pivotal publication: Cortes JE, Kim DW, Pinilla-Ibarz J, et al. "A phase 2 trial of ponatinib in Philadelphia chromosome-positive leukemias." *N Engl J Med.* 2013;369(19):1783-1796. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1306494), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24180494/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=A%20phase%202%20trial%20of%20ponatinib%20in%20Philadelphia%20chromosome-positive%20leukemias)

**Other resources**

- No IPD-sharing platform participation was confirmed for PACE in this pass.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was identified for this original December 2012 approval.
- **Post-approval safety history (context, not part of the 2012 approval basis):** in October 2013, following an FDA partial clinical hold triggered by an increased rate of arterial occlusive events (cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, and peripheral vascular) observed in PACE and the ongoing randomized front-line trial (EPIC, which was halted), Ariad voluntarily suspended marketing and new-patient enrollment; the drug returned to market in December 2013 with a substantially revised label (new boxed warning on arterial occlusion, vascular occlusion, and heart failure risks) and a narrower recommended population. The original accelerated approval was later converted to regular/full approval (2016) following additional long-term PACE follow-up data. These events postdate and are unrelated to the statistical design of the original 2012 single-arm submission documented above.

**Reverse-engineered SAP**

No standalone sponsor SAP/protocol document was located as posted text; the points below are directly traceable to genuine verbatim FDA Statistical Review language (quoted below), so — as with the other single-arm accelerated approvals in this batch — this section is a hybrid of direct quotation and light inference about the overall inferential logic, rather than a quotation of a sponsor-authored SAP document:

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Executive Summary, p.5-6]*

> "The primary objective was to examine the efficacy of ponatinib for patients with resistant or intolerant to dasatinib or nilotinib (R/I) or those with the T315I mutation (T315I). The primary endpoints were the major cytogenetic response (MCyR) rates based on the null and alternative rates of 20% and 35%, respectively in the R/I CP-CML cohort and 10% and 35%, respectively in the T315I CP-CML cohort and major hematologic response rates based on the null and alternative rates of 10% and 30%, respectively in the AP-CML and BP-CML/Ph + ALL cohorts. For R/I CP-CML, the study met its objective in ruling out MCyR rates of 20% and 10%, respectively for the R/I and T315I cohorts. For R/I AP-CML disease, the study met its objective in ruling out MaHR rates of 10% for all cohorts."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, p.7, on the under-enrolled AP-CML T315I cohort]*

> "The planned sample size of the AP-CML T315I cohort was 40 patients based on 10% of null MaHR rate and 30% of alternative MaHR rate with the power of 89% at an alpha of 0.05, but only 18 patients were used for analyses... The 95% confidence interval for the MaHR rate in the AP-CML T315I cohort was (26%, 74%) easily ruling out a MaHR rate of 10%. Additionally, it should be noted that had the T315I cohort been fully enrolled to 40 patients without having any additional patients achieving a MaHR, the 95% confidence interval for MaHR rate would have been (11%, 38%) and thus, a 10% MaHR rate would have still been ruled out."

- *[inferred, from the cohort-by-cohort independent null/alternative-rate structure quoted above and the absence of any cross-cohort multiplicity language in the review]* — each of the six cohorts functioned as its own self-contained one-sample hypothesis test (a "rule out a fixed uninteresting response rate" design, structurally similar to a single-stage Simon-type design applied six times in parallel), with no formal alpha-adjustment across cohorts; this is consistent with accelerated-approval practice for other single-arm, later-line oncology submissions in this batch (bosutinib, omacetaxine) where response-rate thresholds are set per population rather than shared across a family-wise error rate framework.
- *[inferred, from the review's repeated practice of recomputing response/duration figures "based on FDA analysis" distinct from the sponsor's]* — FDA's standard verification practice for single-arm submissions without a concurrent control (independently re-deriving response and duration-of-response endpoints from the underlying assessment data, rather than accepting sponsor tabulations at face value) was applied here as thoroughly as in the carfilzomib and omacetaxine entries in this batch, reflecting a consistent agency practice across single-arm CML/leukemia accelerated approvals in this era.
