### 26. Pomalidomide (Pomalyst) — NDA 204026

**Sponsor:** Celgene Corporation (now Bristol Myers Squibb)

**Indication approved:** Multiple myeloma in patients who have received at least two prior therapies including lenalidomide and bortezomib and have demonstrated disease progression on or within 60 days of completion of the last therapy

**Approval date:** 2013-02-08 (accelerated approval, 21 CFR 314.510)

**Pivotal trial:** The Feb 2013 accelerated approval itself rested on CC-4047-MM-002 ("Trial 1"), NCT00833833, a Phase 1/2 randomized open-label trial — NOT on MM-003 as might be assumed. The randomized Phase 3 confirmatory trial MM-003 ("NIMBUS"), NCT01311687, was already complete (data cutoff 7 Sept 2012) at the time of approval and was required as postmarketing requirement PMR 2006-8; it later supported conversion to regular approval.

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Accelerated approval based on response-rate data from a randomized Phase 2 trial whose arms were not formally compared for efficacy (CC-4047-MM-002); confirmatory trial MM-003 was Randomized open-label active-controlled with Crossover permitted at progression (2:1 randomization, 302 pomalidomide+low-dose dex vs. 153 high-dose dexamethasone)
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR)/duration of response (DoR), assessed per treatment arm (CC-4047-MM-002, the actual accelerated-approval basis); Progression-free survival (PFS) primary with Overall survival (OS) as key secondary (MM-003)
- *Primary analysis:* One-sided one-sample binomial test for ORR within each arm (α=1.25%, H0: p≤0.12 vs. H1: p>0.12), Kaplan-Meier estimation for duration of response (CC-4047-MM-002); Stratified log-rank test and Cox proportional-hazards model for PFS, stratified by age, disease population, and number of prior treatments (MM-003, inferred from published/registry data)
- *Multiplicity:* No between-arm efficacy comparison was performed in CC-4047-MM-002 (reviewer-confirmed); "no formal statistical comparisons were performed between two treatment arms"
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* CC-4047-MM-002's original PFS endpoint (later abandoned in favor of ORR) had a planned group-sequential design using a Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function of the O'Brien-Fleming type (one interim analysis at 50% information, critical two-sided p=0.003; final at p=0.0245); IFM 2009-02 used a two-stage binomial (Simon-type) design for ORR
- *Missing data/bias:* Standard right-censoring at last evaluable disease assessment; treatment effect of pomalidomide "could not be isolated" in either supporting Phase 2 study because both arms received pomalidomide
- *Regulatory:* Reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan (PFS was the original primary endpoint in CC-4047-MM-002's protocol but was replaced by ORR because the study, though randomized, was not controlled for efficacy); Endpoint not accepted as a valid regulatory endpoint for between-arm comparison (PFS results/p-values were explicitly excluded from labeling by the statistical reviewer)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- CC-4047-MM-002 (basis for the actual Feb 2013 approval): a Phase I/II, multicenter, randomized (1:1), open-label, dose-escalation study of pomalidomide alone versus pomalidomide plus low-dose dexamethasone (40 mg weekly, or 20 mg for patients >75) in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma patients who had received ≥2 prior regimens including lenalidomide and bortezomib with progression on the last therapy; randomization (via IVRS) was stratified by age (≤75 vs. >75), prior number of treatments (2 vs. >2), and prior thalidomide exposure; 221 subjects were randomized (113 to Pom+Dex, 108 to Pom alone) at 18 US/Canada sites between 1 Dec 2009 and 22 Sept 2010, data cutoff 1 April 2011 (updated OS analysis 16 Sept 2011)
- The original primary efficacy endpoint per protocol was IRC-assessed PFS, planned for a log-rank test at two-sided α=0.05, with ~192 patients (85% power to detect HR 0.6, i.e., median PFS 10 vs. 6 months) and one interim analysis at 50% information (~70 events) using an O'Brien-Fleming alpha-spending boundary (critical two-sided p=0.003 at interim, p=0.0245 at final analysis of 139 events). Because the study, though randomized, did not isolate the treatment effect of pomalidomide (patients on the monotherapy arm could add dexamethasone at progression), FDA's statistical reviewer determined PFS was not a valid between-arm comparison, and the applicant instead reported ORR per IRC (EBMT criteria) descriptively within each arm, tested against a historical/uninteresting response rate of 12% (one-sided binomial, α=1.25% per arm). Secondary endpoints were DOR, time to response (TTR), and OS. Results: ORR 29.2% (Pom+Dex) vs. 7.4% (Pom alone); median DOR 7.4 months (Pom+Dex)
- IFM 2009-02 (secondary supporting evidence): an open-label, multicenter, randomized (1:1), non-comparative Phase 2 study of two pomalidomide dosing schedules (21/28 vs. 28/28 days) plus low-dose dexamethasone in 84 relapsed/refractory patients from 22 French sites (16 Oct 2009–28 July 2010), data cutoff 1 March 2011. Primary endpoint was ORR per IRC (IMWG criteria); design used a Simon-type two-stage binomial rule (H0: p≤0.25 vs. H1: p≥0.45, two-sided α=0.05, 80% power) with an initial safety look at 6 patients/arm and a stage-1 futility look at ~34 patients (≥5 responses required to proceed). Secondary endpoints: DOR, TTR, TTP, OS
- MM-003/NIMBUS (confirmatory Phase 3, PMR 2006-8): a multicenter, randomized (2:1), open-label trial in 455 patients with refractory or relapsed-and-refractory MM after failure of bortezomib and lenalidomide, conducted in Australia, Canada, Europe, Russia, and the US; stratification factors were age (≤75 vs. >75), disease population (refractory vs. relapsed-and-refractory vs. bortezomib-intolerant), and number of prior treatments (2 vs. >2). Arms: pomalidomide 4 mg/day (days 1–21 of 28-day cycle) + low-dose dexamethasone (302 patients) vs. high-dose dexamethasone (153 patients) until progression or unacceptable toxicity; crossover to pomalidomide was permitted for high-dose-dexamethasone patients after progression (29% ultimately crossed over). Primary endpoint was IRC-assessed PFS (IMWG criteria); OS was a key secondary endpoint. At the prespecified data cutoff for the final PFS/interim OS analysis (7 Sept 2012), 267 PFS events had occurred. Reported results (published 2013): median PFS 4.0 vs. 1.9 months, HR 0.48 (95% CI 0.39–0.60), p<0.0001; this trial was already complete before the Feb 2013 approval decision but its full study report was not due to FDA until June 2013, and it later underpinned conversion to regular approval

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter (accelerated approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2013/204026Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (2013, original) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2013/204026lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Yun Wang, PhD; Division of Biometrics V) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/204026Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Clinical/Medical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/204026Orig1s000MedR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (MM-003/NIMBUS) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01311687
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (CC-4047-MM-002) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00833833
- Pivotal publication (accelerated-approval basis, CC-4047-MM-002): Richardson PG, Siegel DS, Vij R, et al. "Pomalidomide alone or in combination with low-dose dexamethasone in relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma: a randomized phase 2 study." *Blood.* 2014;123(12):1826-1832. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1182/blood-2013-11-538835), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24421329/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Pomalidomide%20alone%20or%20in%20combination%20with%20low-dose%20dexamethasone%20in%20relapsed%20and%20refractory%20multiple%20myeloma%3A%20a%20randomized%20phase%202%20study)
- Confirmatory-trial publication (MM-003): San Miguel J, Weisel K, Moreau P, et al. "Pomalidomide plus low-dose dexamethasone versus high-dose dexamethasone alone for patients with relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma (MM-003): a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial." *Lancet Oncol.* 2013;14(11):1055-1066. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(13)70380-2>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24007748/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Pomalidomide%20plus%20low-dose%20dexamethasone%20versus%20high-dose%20dexamethasone%20alone%20for%20patients%20with%20relapsed%20and%20refractory%20multiple%20myeloma%20%28MM-003%29%3A%20a%20randomised%2C%20open-label%2C%20phase%203%20trial)

**Other resources**

- IPD/dataset access: Bristol Myers Squibb (which acquired Celgene) is a Vivli member and states a general commitment to sharing individual anonymized participant data upon qualified researcher request; trial-specific availability of CC-4047-MM-002 or MM-003 datasets on Vivli was not individually confirmed.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held. Verbatim from the approval letter: "Your application for Pomalyst (pomalidomide) capsules was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because this drug is not the first in its class and the safety profile is similar to that of other drugs or biologics approved for this indication."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review NDA 204026, §2.1, p.5–6]*

> "The original primary efficacy endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS) based on independent review committee (IRC) assessments. However, since this study was randomized but uncontrolled, which did not isolate the treatment effect of pomalidomide, PFS was not comparable between two treatment arms, the applicant proposed ORR, based on IRC assessments using European Group for Blood and Marrow Transplantation (EBMT) criteria, was more appropriate and used primarily to evaluating efficacy in this study."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review NDA 204026, §3.2.1.1.1, p.8–9]*

> "One interim analysis was planned with 50% information (~70 PFS events). The superiority boundaries were calculated using alpha-spending function of the O'Brien-Fleming type with overall two-sided Type I error of 0.05... The sample size was calculated based on log-rank test of PFS at a significance level of 5% (two-sided). With a 12-month accrual period and 12-month follow-up after the study closes to accrual, assuming a 10% drop-out rate, a sample size of 192 will have 85% power to detect a PFS HR ratio of 0.6."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review NDA 204026, §3.2.2.1.1, p.10]*

> "According to the statistical analysis plan, PFS will be compared between Pom(21/28) + Dex arm and Pom arm using log-rank test... One-sided one-sample binomial test for ORR in each arm will be performed with α=1.25%... However, the comparisons of PFS or ORR across two arms were not performed and HR for PFS with corresponding 95% CI was not calculated in this statistical review since CC-4047-MM-002 was a randomized but uncontrolled study."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review NDA 204026, §5.1–5.4, p.27–28]*

> "The treatment effect of pomalidomide can not be isolated and the contribution of pomalidomide to the treatment benefit of pomalidomide plus low-dose dexamethasone can not be evaluated in both studies CC-4047-MM-002 and IFM 2009-02... Since there is no controlled comparison that isolated the effect of pomalidomide, PFS results, p values or any comparative statements between treatment arms should not be included in the labeling."

*[verbatim, FDA Approval Letter, NDA 204026, PMR 2006-8]*

> "Conduct a randomized controlled trial (MM-003) of the combination of pomalidomide and dexamethasone in patients with previously treated multiple myeloma, to determine the safety profile of pomalidomide and dexamethasone combination as compared to a treatment arm without pomalidomide." Timetable submitted: "Final Protocol Submission: 3/2011 (completed); Trial Completion: 9/2012 (completed); Final Report Submission: 6/2013."

*[verbatim, approved Label, 2013, Indications and Usage]*

> "This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate. Clinical benefit, such as improvement in survival or symptoms, has not been verified."

**Reverse-engineered SAP (MM-003/NIMBUS)** *[inferred]* — genuine FDA statistical review text for this confirmatory trial specifically was not located in the public original-approval package (it postdates the 2013 accelerated approval and was reviewed later, at conversion to regular approval); the following are inferred from the Lancet Oncology publication and the ClinicalTrials.gov registry record.

- *[inferred, from CT.gov outcome-measure definitions and 2:1 enrollment of 302:153]* Randomization was almost certainly stratified with a fixed 2:1 allocation ratio favoring the pomalidomide arm, consistent with a design intended to maximize exposure/safety data on the investigational arm while retaining adequate power for a large treatment effect.
- *[inferred, from "267 PFS events had occurred" at the prespecified 7 Sept 2012 cutoff and the resulting HR 0.48, p<0.0001]* The protocol likely specified a fixed information-based trigger (a target PFS event count, ~267) for the final PFS analysis rather than a calendar date, typical of an event-driven survival design with a single primary PFS look.
- *[inferred, from the 29% crossover rate reported for the high-dose-dexamethasone arm]* The protocol pre-specified permitted crossover to pomalidomide at documented progression, which — combined with OS being only a secondary/key-secondary endpoint rather than co-primary — suggests the SAP anticipated attenuated OS treatment effects and did not rely on OS for the primary claim.
- *[inferred, from IRC-based PFS per IMWG criteria and the standard censoring language used across Celgene's MM program]* Censoring at last adequate disease assessment for patients without a documented progression event, consistent with standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment.

### 27. Ado-trastuzumab emtansine (Kadcyla, T-DM1) — BLA 125427

**Sponsor:** Genentech, Inc. (Roche)

**Indication approved:** HER2-positive, unresectable locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer in patients who previously received trastuzumab and a taxane, separately or in combination (with disease recurrence during or within six months of completing adjuvant therapy, or progression on prior therapy for metastatic disease)

**Approval date:** 2013-02-22 (regular/standard BLA approval)

**Pivotal trial:** EMILIA (TDM4370g/BO21977), NCT00829166 — randomized, multicenter, open-label Phase 3 trial with co-primary endpoints of IRC-assessed PFS and OS (PFS was the original single primary endpoint per the initial SAP, elevated to co-primary with OS following FDA feedback at the End-of-Phase-2 meeting)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized open-label active-controlled, co-primary endpoints, mid-trial SAP amendment changing endpoint status, crossover permitted at progression (control-arm patients could receive T-DM1 after the second OS interim analysis crossed the efficacy boundary)
- *Endpoints:* progression-free survival (PFS) (IRC-assessed, co-primary), overall survival (OS) (co-primary), objective response rate (ORR)/duration of response (DoR) (key secondary), investigator-assessed PFS (key secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test (region, number of prior chemotherapy regimens, visceral vs. non-visceral disease), unstratified log-rank test as support, Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified) for hazard ratio estimation, Kaplan-Meier estimation for medians
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing — PFS tested first, OS hypothesis test conducted only if PFS was statistically significant, both at two-sided α=0.05; secondary endpoints (investigator PFS, ORR, time to treatment failure, time to symptom progression) tested in pre-specified order only if both co-primary endpoints were significant
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design, Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function with O'Brien-Fleming boundary for OS monitoring, two OS interim analyses (1st at final-PFS-analysis timepoint, 2nd added via SAP Amendment 2 at ≥50% of planned deaths), Data Monitoring Committee (DMC/DSMB)
- *Missing data/bias:* standard right-censoring at last evaluable tumor assessment or date of randomization+1 day if no post-baseline assessment; ascertainment bias assessment — FDA reviewer flagged that the sponsor supplied IRC oncologists with drug-specific toxicity information, potentially unblinding/biasing IRC tumor-progression calls; two retrospective sensitivity analyses (radiologist-only assessment; earliest of radiology/oncology/death) were conducted and were consistent with the primary analysis
- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented mid-trial endpoint elevation (FDA feedback-driven) — OS was added as a co-primary endpoint after FDA's End-of-Phase-2 comment that PFS alone was inadequate in an open-label trial; reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan concern regarding a second, data-trend-driven OS interim analysis, which FDA judged did not materially inflate Type I error (per Lan-DeMets O'Brien-Fleming spending, citing Proschan et al. 1992)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- EMILIA (TDM4370g/BO21977) was a Phase III, randomized (1:1), multicenter, open-label trial comparing T-DM1 monotherapy (3.6 mg/kg IV every 21 days) with lapatinib (1250 mg/day orally) plus capecitabine (1000 mg/m² orally twice daily, days 1-14 of each 21-day cycle) in patients with HER2-positive (centrally confirmed) locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer previously treated with a taxane and trastuzumab. 991 patients were randomized (495 T-DM1, 496 control) between 23 Feb 2009 and 13 Oct 2011, stratified by world region (US, Western Europe, other), number of prior chemotherapy regimens for advanced/metastatic disease (≤1 vs. >1), and visceral vs. non-visceral disease. CNS-only disease was excluded; cardiac ejection fraction ≥50% was required
- Primary endpoints (co-primary, per amended SAP): PFS by IRC, defined as time from randomization to first IRC-documented progression (modified RECIST 1.0) or death from any cause, with patients censored at last evaluable tumor assessment (or randomization+1 day if no post-baseline assessment; patients receiving non-protocol anti-cancer therapy were not censored at that initiation, i.e., analyzed under ITT follow-up); and OS, defined as time from randomization to death from any cause
- Key secondary endpoints: investigator-assessed PFS, IRC-assessed ORR (with duration of response), time to treatment failure, and time to symptom progression (FACT-B TOI-PFB, ≥5-point decrease from baseline). Patients were followed with tumor assessments every 6 weeks; after progression, survival follow-up occurred every 3 months. An independent DMC reviewed safety data at least every 6 months (SAEs every 3 months) until the primary PFS analysis; the IRC was blinded to treatment assignment for tumor-response adjudication, though FDA's review flagged that IRC oncologists were also given drug-specific toxicity information
- Sample size/power: originally 580 patients for PFS alone; SAP Amendment 1 (11 May 2011) added OS as co-primary and increased the sample size to 980 to power OS adequately — targeting detection of a 4.3-month median OS improvement (17.2 to 21.5 months, HR 0.8), requiring 632 deaths for 80% power at two-sided α=0.05; PFS was separately powered to detect a 2.1-month median improvement (6.2 to 8.3 months, HR 0.75), requiring 508 PFS events for 90% power at two-sided α=0.05
- Multiplicity/interim analysis: a fixed-sequence gatekeeping procedure tested PFS first; OS was tested only if PFS was significant, using the same stratification factors, supported by an unstratified log-rank test. One interim OS analysis (at the time of final PFS analysis) was specified in SAP Amendment 1. SAP Amendment 2 (22 June 2012) — proposed by the sponsor at a pre-BLA meeting after the first interim OS analysis showed a positive trend, and accepted by FDA "with appropriate alpha adjustment" — added a second interim OS analysis at ≥50% of the planned 632 deaths, using a Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function with an O'Brien-Fleming boundary to control Type I error across looks
- Results: IRC PFS — 569 events (265 T-DM1, 304 control); stratified HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.55–0.77), stratified log-rank p<0.0001; median PFS 9.6 vs. 6.4 months. Investigator PFS — HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.56–0.77), p<0.0001. 1st OS interim (223 deaths, 35% of planned) — HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.48–0.81), p=0.0005, but did not cross the efficacy boundary (α=0.0003 at that look). 2nd OS interim (data cutoff 31 July 2012; 331 deaths, 52% of planned; 149 T-DM1, 182 control) — stratified HR 0.68 (95% CI 0.55–0.85), p=0.0006, crossing the pre-specified efficacy stopping boundary of α=0.0037, and thus statistically significant; median OS 30.9 vs. 25.1 months. ORR (IRC-confirmed): 43.6% vs. 30.8%

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter (regular approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2013/125427Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (2013, original) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2013/125427lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Qiang "Casey" Xu, PhD, with Team Leader's Memo; Division of Biometrics V) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/125427Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Clinical/Medical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/125427Orig1s000MedR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (EMILIA) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00829166
- Pivotal publication: Verma S, Miles D, Gianni L, et al. (EMILIA Study Group). "Trastuzumab emtansine for HER2-positive advanced breast cancer." *N Engl J Med.* 2012;367(19):1783-1791. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1209124), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23020162/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Trastuzumab%20emtansine%20for%20HER2-positive%20advanced%20breast%20cancer)

**Other resources**

- IPD/dataset access: Roche (Genentech's parent) is a Vivli member and participates in patient-level data sharing per the EFPIA-PhRMA principles; trial-specific availability of the EMILIA (TDM4370g/BO21977) dataset on Vivli was not individually confirmed.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held. Verbatim from the approval letter: "Your application for Kadcyla (ado-trastuzumab emtansine) was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary; there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review BLA 125427, §2.1 "Regulatory Communications and Related Amendments," p.8]*

> "One of the major issues was the choice of the primary endpoint. In the original statistical analysis plan (SAP), PFS was the primary endpoint with OS as a key secondary endpoint. During the end-of-phase 2 (EOP2) meeting on August 8, 2008, FDA emphasized that 'We encourage the use of Overall Survival as the primary efficacy endpoint, instead of PFS. You should be aware that PFS is subject to ascertainment bias, especially in an open label trial.' In response to the FDA's advice, the SAP Amendment 1 (May 11, 2011) incorporated overall survival (OS) as a co-primary endpoint with PFS and increased sample size from 580 to 980 to ensure an adequate study power for OS."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review BLA 125427, §2.1, p.8]*

> "In light of the strong evidence of clinical improvement demonstrated at the time of the primary PFS analysis, the sponsor during the pre-BLA meeting on May 30, 2012 proposed adding an additional interim analysis for OS when at least 50% of the planned number of deaths had occurred, allowing the patients in the control arm the opportunity to receive T-DM1 earlier if the statistical significance was established at the second OS interim analysis. The Agency stated that 'it is acceptable to add an additional interim OS analysis with appropriate alpha adjustment in the sequential testing plan.' The SAP Amendment 2 (June 22, 2012) subsequently reflected this change."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review BLA 125427, §3.2.2 "Statistical Analysis Plan," p.10–12]*

> "Two primary comparisons were planned for the co-primary endpoints of IRC-assessed PFS and OS in a fixed-sequence procedure in which PFS would be tested first followed by the hypothesis testing on OS if the result of PFS was statistically significant. Both tests would be conducted at a two-sided type I error of 0.05... One interim OS analysis at the time of the final PFS analysis was scheduled initially in SAP Amendment 1... in SAP Amendment 2, a second interim OS analysis was added at the time when at least 50% of the planned number of deaths had occurred... Lan-DeMets alpha spending function with an O'Brien-Fleming boundary was used to determine the significance level for OS analyses based on the realized events in the analysis datasets."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review BLA 125427, §5.1, p.27]*

> "The 2nd OS interim analysis was driven by the positive trend in OS improvement observed in the 1st interim analysis, and thus overall type I error was inflated. However, the use of Lan-DeMets alpha spending function O'B-F boundary for study monitoring greatly alleviated the alpha inflation caused by data-driven interim analyses, leading to an inflation no more than 10% (Proschan et al., 1992). Given the efficacy stopping boundary of 0.0037 for the 2nd interim analysis, this reviewer considered that the p-value observed in the 2nd OS interim analysis (0.0006) was adequate to reject the null hypothesis and to show statistical significance."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review BLA 125427, §2.1/§5.1 "Major Issues," p.8, 27]*

> "Information on drug-specific toxicities was provided by the sponsor to the IRC oncologist, potentially biasing the IRC tumor assessments. Two sensitivity analyses were retrospectively conducted in which PFS was derived based on (1) IRC radiologist-assessed progression or death and (2) the earliest progression of either radiology or oncology review or death. The hazard ratios were 0.65 (95%CI: 0.54, 0.77) and 0.66 (95%CI: 0.56, 0.78), respectively, showing consistent results with the primary analyses."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review BLA 125427, Team Leader's Memo, p.2]*

> "This team leader concurs with the recommendations and conclusions of the statistical reviewer (Dr. Qiang (Casey) Xu) of this application. The statistical results provide adequate evidence to support the PFS and OS claims proposed in the BLA."

### 28. Technetium Tc 99m tilmanocept (Lymphoseek) — NDA 202207

**Sponsor:** Navidea Biopharmaceuticals, Inc. (trials conducted under the company's former name, Neoprobe Corporation)

**Indication approved:** Radioactive diagnostic agent for lymphatic mapping using a handheld gamma counter to assist in the localization of lymph nodes draining a primary tumor in patients with breast cancer or melanoma

**Approval date:** March 13, 2013

**Pivotal trials:** NEO3-05, NCT00671918, and NEO3-09, NCT01106040 (two near-identical Phase 3 trials, each enrolling both breast cancer and melanoma patients)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* diagnostic-accuracy study (see below), open-label, non-randomized, single-arm, within-patient paired comparison against an active comparator (vital blue dye)
- *Endpoints:* nodal concordance rate vs. reference standard, reverse concordance rate (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* exact binomial test against a pre-specified performance goal / lower confidence bound

**This entry is a genuine outlier in this census: Lymphoseek is a diagnostic radiopharmaceutical, not a therapeutic drug, and it was not approved on a randomized efficacy trial.** There is no control arm, no survival or response endpoint, no multiplicity/alpha-spending procedure, and no interim monitoring — the entire "SAP" apparatus this census otherwise documents (log-rank tests, Cox models, alpha-spending, censoring rules) genuinely does not apply here. What FDA reviewed instead was a paired, within-patient diagnostic-agreement (concordance) study against a pre-specified performance goal. The two normal keyword categories that do carry over (Design, Endpoints, Primary analysis) needed new taxonomy terms because nothing in the existing oncology-efficacy-trial vocabulary describes a single-arm diagnostic mapping-agent accuracy study; proposed additions are listed at the end of this file.

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Two prospective, multicenter, open-label, single-arm, within-patient comparison Phase 3 trials (NEO3-05 and NEO3-09), "almost identical in study design," per FDA's review, each titled "A Phase 3, Prospective, Open-Label, Multicenter Comparison Study of Lymphoseek® and Vital Blue Dye as Lymphoid Tissue Targeting Agents in Patients With Known Melanoma or Breast Cancer Who Are Undergoing Lymph Node Mapping"
- Population: patients ≥18 years old with known melanoma or breast cancer who were surgical candidates for lymphatic mapping; every patient received both a single 50 mcg dose of Tc 99m tilmanocept and the active comparator, vital blue dye (VBD/Lymphazurin), before intraoperative lymphatic mapping (ILM); excised nodes (radioactive and/or blue-stained) were examined by histopathology
- Primary endpoint: node-level "concordance" — the proportion of VBD-identified (blue-stained) nodes also detected by Tc 99m tilmanocept, using VBD as the de facto standard of truth — i.e., a paired detection-agreement (sensitivity-like) measure rather than a clinical-outcome endpoint; pre-specified performance goal: lower bound of the two-sided 95% CI >90%
- NEO3-05: planned sample size 238 (to yield an expected 203 VBD-stained nodes); enrolled 195 patients (179-patient safety population: 85 melanoma, 94 breast cancer); 475 lymph nodes harvested from 176 patients across 380 surgical specimens
- NEO3-09: planned sample size up to 155 (to yield an expected 196 VBD-stained nodes); enrolled 163 patients (153-patient safety population: 76 melanoma, 77 breast cancer)
- Secondary endpoint added partly at FDA's request: "reverse concordance" — the proportion of Tc 99m tilmanocept-identified nodes that were also detected by VBD — to check whether the new agent identified nodes VBD missed, rather than only whether it matched VBD's detections
- Statistical method (sponsor's primary analysis): one-sided exact binomial test of H0: concordance rate R≤0.90 vs. Ha: R>0.90, with a two-sided 95% CI via large-sample normal approximation; no randomization, no comparator arm receiving a different treatment, and no formal multiplicity or alpha-spending procedure, because this is a single-arm diagnostic-agreement study rather than a therapeutic RCT
- NEO3-05's result came in at a lower 95% CI bound of 0.8958 — just under the pre-specified 0.90 performance goal — which FDA's own review characterized as the study having "only marginally won" against its own pre-specified criterion
- FDA additionally ran its own independent node-level analysis using histopathology (lymphoid vs. non-lymphoid tissue) as the reference standard, rather than accepting VBD-concordance as the sole efficacy measure, because the review team considered "concordance with blue dye" an imperfect proxy for the actual diagnostic question (how well Lymphoseek identifies lymph nodes as such)

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2013/202207Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2013/202207s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Medical/Clinical Review (Division of Medical Imaging Products; for this diagnostic radiopharmaceutical, clinical and statistical analysis are combined in one review memorandum rather than a separate Statistical Review) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/202207Orig1s000MedR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record, NEO3-05 — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00671918 (no protocol/SAP posted)
- ClinicalTrials.gov record, NEO3-09 — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01106040 (no protocol/SAP posted)
- Pivotal publication (breast cancer cohort): Wallace AM, Han LK, Povoski SP, et al. "Comparative Evaluation of [99mTc]Tilmanocept for Sentinel Lymph Node Mapping in Breast Cancer Patients: Results of Two Phase 3 Trials." *Ann Surg Oncol.* 2013;20(8):2590-2599. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1245/s10434-013-2887-8), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23504141/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Comparative%20Evaluation%20of%20Tilmanocept%20for%20Sentinel%20Lymph%20Node%20Mapping%20in%20Breast%20Cancer%20Patients%20Results%20of%20Two%20Phase%203%20Trials)
- Pivotal publication (melanoma cohort): Sondak VK, King DW, Zager JS, et al. "Combined Analysis of Phase III Trials Evaluating [99mTc]Tilmanocept and Vital Blue Dye for Identification of Sentinel Lymph Nodes in Clinically Node-Negative Cutaneous Melanoma." *Ann Surg Oncol.* 2013;20(2):680-688. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1245/s10434-012-2612-z), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23054107/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Combined%20Analysis%20of%20Phase%20III%20Trials%20Evaluating%20Tilmanocept%20and%20Vital%20Blue%20Dye%20for%20Identification%20of%20Sentinel%20Lymph%20Nodes%20in%20Clinically%20Node-Negative%20Cutaneous%20Melanoma)

**Other resources**

- No IPD/dataset-sharing program (Vivli, YODA, Project Data Sphere) was identified for Navidea Biopharmaceuticals; as a small specialty radiopharmaceutical company, trial-specific IPD access should not be assumed absent explicit confirmation.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held. Per FDA's review: "Since there are already two other products on the market for similar indications, the Division decided not to hold an advisory committee meeting for the application."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Medical/Clinical Review Memorandum, NDA 202207, §6.2, describing both pivotal trials]*

> "The two phase 3 clinical studies submitted in the NDA, NEO-05 and NEO-09, are almost identical in study design. Both studies are titled 'A Phase 3, Prospective, Open-Label, Multicenter Comparison Studies of Lymphoseek® and Vital Blue Dye as Lymphoid Tissue Targeting Agents in Patients With Known Melanoma or Breast Cancer Who Are Undergoing Lymph Node Mapping'. Both studies were prospective, multicenter, open-label, single arm, within-patient comparative studies conducted in patients 18 years of age or older with known melanoma or breast cancer who were candidates for surgical intervention and who met the study entry criteria. All patients received a single dose of 50 μg Tc 99m Lymphoseek and VBD prior to ILM. The primary objective of both studies was to determine the concordance between Tc 99m Lymphoseek and VBD in the in vivo detection of the excised lymph node(s) as confirmed by histopathology."

*[verbatim, same review, §6.3.1/6.4, on the primary endpoint definition and FDA's disagreement with it]*

> "In the sponsor's primary efficacy analysis, concordance is based on the comparator blue dye and is essentially the sensitivity of Lymphoseek using blue dye as the standard of truth... Throughout the milestone meetings, the FDA review team expressed concerns on using this so called 'concordance' as the primary efficacy endpoint. One situation the FDA review team asked the sponsor to consider was that Lymphoseek could potentially identify more lymph nodes that the comparator blue dye. Therefore in secondary efficacy analyses, Navidea also conducted analysis on the 'reverse concordance', which is taking all the Lymphoseek identified lymph nodes, and look to see how many of them were also identified by the blue dye... The FDA review team conducted its own analysis during the NDA review. The FDA review was conducted on a node level, using each surgical specimen's histopathology (lymphoid tissue vs. non-lymphoid tissue) as the standard of truth."

*[verbatim, same review, §6.4, on the marginal result in NEO3-05]*

> "Note that the lower bound of the 95% confidence interval in study NEO3-05 was 0.8958, slightly lower than the prespecified threshold level of 0.90. Therefore study NEO3-05 only marginally won."

*[verbatim, same review, §9.1]*

> "Since there are already two other products on the market for similar indications, the Division decided not to hold an advisory committee meeting for the application."

Unlike every other entry in this census, Lymphoseek's approval basis is a single-arm diagnostic-accuracy criterion (a one-sided test of a pre-specified performance goal on a paired concordance rate), not a randomized comparison of clinical outcomes. This is documented honestly here rather than forced into the RCT/SAP template used for therapeutic drugs.

### 29. Radium Ra 223 dichloride (Xofigo) — NDA 203971

**Sponsor:** Bayer HealthCare Pharmaceuticals Inc.

**Indication approved:** Castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) with symptomatic bone metastases and no known visceral metastatic disease

**Approval date:** May 15, 2013

**Pivotal trial:** ALSYMPCA (Study BC1-06, "ALpharadin in SYMptomatic Prostate CAncer"), NCT00699751

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven trial, early-stopped for efficacy
- *Endpoints:* overall survival (OS, primary), time to first symptomatic skeletal event (SSE), time to total-ALP progression/response/normalization, time to PSA progression (hierarchical key secondary endpoints)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified), Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (gatekeeping procedure across 5 ordered secondary endpoints)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design, Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function (O'Brien-Fleming), Data Monitoring Committee (DMC/DSMB)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Phase 3, randomized (2:1, radium-223:placebo), double-blind, placebo-controlled, multinational trial (921 patients enrolled, 128 centers) in symptomatic CRPC with bone metastases and no visceral metastases, in patients who had received, were ineligible for, or declined docetaxel
- Randomization stratified by three binary factors: total alkaline phosphatase (ALP) (<220 vs. ≥220 U/L), current bisphosphonate use (yes/no), and prior docetaxel use (yes/no) — the docetaxel-use stratifier was added mid-study by protocol amendment
- Arms: radium-223 dichloride 50 kBq/kg IV every 4 weeks for 6 administrations plus best standard of care (BSoC), vs. matching placebo plus BSoC
- Primary endpoint: overall survival, time from randomization to death from any cause; patients alive or lost to follow-up censored at the last known-alive date or the data cutoff, whichever came first
- Key secondary endpoints, tested sequentially only if OS was significant (a gatekeeping/step-down hierarchy, each tested at a 0.05 significance level): (1) time to total-ALP progression, (2) total-ALP response at week 12, (3) time to first symptomatic skeletal event (SSE — EBRT for skeletal symptoms, new symptomatic pathological fracture, spinal cord compression, or tumor-related orthopedic surgery), (4) total-ALP normalization, (5) time to PSA progression
- Sample size and design evolved across four protocol amendments: sample size increased from 450 to 750 to (ultimately) 900 patients; power increased from 80% to 90%; a planned unblinded interim OS analysis was added; the docetaxel-use stratification factor was added; a blinded sample-size re-estimation was conducted at ~500-600 enrolled patients (per Bolland et al.'s method, requiring no Type I error adjustment)
- Final analysis planned at 640 death events; one planned interim analysis at 320 deaths (50% of target), with the nominal two-sided significance level for that interim set at 0.0031 via a Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function approximating an O'Brien-Fleming boundary
- Trial stopped early for efficacy: the pre-specified interim OS analysis (314 events, cutoff October 14, 2010, 809 patients enrolled) crossed the efficacy boundary; the Independent Data Monitoring Committee (IDMC) recommended unblinding and that placebo patients be offered radium-223, June 3, 2011
- Primary analysis method: OS compared via a stratified log-rank test (using the three randomization stratification factors); hazard ratio and 95% CI from a Cox proportional-hazards model stratified by the same factors; Kaplan-Meier method for median survival times and curves
- Sensitivity analyses (sponsor and FDA reviewer): a stratified log-rank test using IVRS (Interactive Voice Response System)-recorded stratification factors, an unstratified log-rank test, and analyses adjusted for baseline PSA, Gleason score, TNM staging, and time from hormone-therapy initiation to castration resistance
- A data-quality issue FDA's review flags explicitly: 83 of 809 ITT patients (10.3%) had discrepancies between the stratification-factor values recorded by the IVRS at randomization and the patients' actual (source-verified) stratification-factor values; the primary analysis used the actual values, and FDA confirmed via a sensitivity analysis using the IVRS-recorded values that results were consistent

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2013/203971Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2013/203971lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Division of Biometrics) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/203971Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/203971Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00699751 (no protocol/SAP posted)
- Pivotal publication: Parker C, Nilsson S, Heinrich D, et al. "Alpha Emitter Radium-223 and Survival in Metastatic Prostate Cancer." *N Engl J Med.* 2013;369:213-223. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1213755), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23863050/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Alpha%20Emitter%20Radium-223%20and%20Survival%20in%20Metastatic%20Prostate%20Cancer)

**Other resources**

- Bayer participates in the Vivli data-sharing platform; trial-specific IPD availability for ALSYMPCA was not individually confirmed in this pass.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held. Per FDA's Summary Review: "The application for Xofigo® (radium Ra 223 dichloride) Injection was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the application showed improvement in overall survival and did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 203971, §3.2.1, p.15]*

> "Study BC1-06 was a phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of Radium-223 in the treatment of patients with symptomatic CRPC with bone metastases and no evidence of visceral metastatic disease. The primary endpoint was OS, supported by key secondary endpoints including: (1) time to total-ALP progression, (2) total-ALP response at Week 12, (3) time to occurrence of first SSE, (4) total-ALP normalization, and (5) time to PSA progression."

*[verbatim, same review, §3.2.1.1, p.11, on sample size and the interim alpha boundary]*

> "Final analysis would be performed when 640 death events occurred. The sample size estimation was performed using simulations in R. A planned interim analysis would be conducted when 320 deaths (50% of required deaths for final analysis) were observed. The nominal significance level for the interim analysis with 320 deaths was 0.0031 (two-sided) using the Lan-DeMets alpha-spending approach with O-Brien-Fleming spending function."

*[verbatim, same review, §3.2.1.3.2, on the secondary-endpoint gatekeeping procedure]*

> "A gatekeeping procedure was used to control the overall type I error rate. These five secondary endpoints were ordered hierarchically. Each endpoint was tested at a 0.05 significance level. No claims could be based on a secondary endpoint which had a rank lower than the secondary endpoint which was the first in the hierarchical sequence that did not reach a significant result."

*[verbatim, same review, §3.2.2, on the primary analysis method]*

> "Overall survival was compared between the two treatment groups in the ITT population using a stratified log-rank test with three binary stratification factors at randomization: total ALP (< 220 U/L versus ≥ 220 U/L), current use of bisphosphonates (yes versus no), and any prior use of docetaxel (yes versus no). The hazard ratio and corresponding 95% confidence interval were estimated using the Cox proportional hazards model stratified by the same stratification factors."

*[verbatim, same review, on the IVRS stratification-factor discrepancy and FDA's response, p.21]*

> "Stratification assignment was performed using an integrated voice response system (IVRS). It is noted that there were 83 subjects (10.3%) with inconsistent stratification factor data between IVRS and actual stratification factors (Table 8). No significant imbalance was seen between the two treatment groups... The primary analysis of OS used actual randomization stratification factors. Given the discrepancies between IVRS randomization stratification factors and actual randomization stratification factors, a sensitivity analysis of OS was performed using IVRS randomization stratification factors. The sensitivity analyses results were consistent with the primary analysis results, supporting that the primary OS analysis is robust."

### 30. Dabrafenib (Tafinlar) — NDA 202806

**Sponsor:** GlaxoSmithKline, LLC

**Indication approved:** Unresectable or metastatic melanoma with BRAF V600E mutation as detected by an FDA-approved test (label specifies Tafinlar is not indicated for wild-type BRAF melanoma)

**Approval date:** May 29, 2013

**Pivotal trial:** BREAK-3 (protocol BRF113683), NCT01227889

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled, crossover permitted at progression, biomarker-selected/enriched population
- *Endpoints:* progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS) — key secondary, not accepted for a confirmatory labeling claim at time of approval, objective response rate (ORR)/duration of response (DoR)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, HR derived from log-rank U/V statistics (Pike estimator), Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Multiplicity:* no multiplicity adjustment proposed in the SAP for secondary endpoints; FDA treated OS, ORR and DoR as exploratory/supportive only
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* no interim efficacy analysis planned (design used a single, highly over-powered 1-sided 0.02-alpha test); independent data monitoring committee (IDMC) conducted safety-only reviews
- *Missing data/bias:* standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment; no crossover-adjustment method (RPSFT/IPCW) applied to the confounded OS analysis despite 33% of DTIC patients crossing over
- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan (FDA re-derived the primary stratification variable and re-built PFS from raw lesion data rather than the applicant's derived datasets)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Phase III, randomized (3:1), open-label, multicenter, dacarbazine (DTIC)-controlled trial in previously untreated adults with BRAF V600E mutation-positive unresectable (Stage III) or metastatic (Stage IV) melanoma, measurable disease per RECIST 1.1, ECOG 0–1, no active CNS disease and no prior BRAF/MEK inhibitor or systemic therapy for advanced disease (IL-2 permitted); randomization was stratified by disease stage at study entry (unresectable III + IVM1a/IVM1b vs. IVM1c); patients received oral dabrafenib 150 mg twice daily or intravenous DTIC 1000 mg/m2 every 3 weeks until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or death, and DTIC patients could cross over to open-label dabrafenib at documented progression
- Primary endpoint: investigator-assessed PFS, defined as time from randomization to the first date of objective disease progression (RECIST 1.1) or death from any cause, with an independent radiology/oncology review committee (IRC) providing a sensitivity assessment
- Secondary endpoints: overall survival (time from randomization to death from any cause, including deaths after crossover, censored at last known alive; survival follow-up planned to continue until 70% of randomized patients had died), objective response rate (confirmed/unconfirmed CR+PR by RECIST 1.1, investigator and IRC), and duration of response (from first CR/PR to progression or death, responders only)
- Sample size: 200 patients planned to accrue 102 PFS events, giving ~99.7% power at a 1-sided alpha of 0.02 assuming HR 0.33 (median PFS 2 vs. 6 months); no interim efficacy analysis was planned; 250 patients were actually randomized (187 dabrafenib : 63 DTIC), exceeding the target by 50 patients
- Statistical methods: PFS and OS summarized by Kaplan-Meier, treatment difference tested with a stratified log-rank test (stratified on disease stage at screening), HR estimated by the Pike estimator; ORR compared via Fisher's exact test with exact 95% CIs; the SAP proposed no multiplicity adjustment across secondary endpoints, so FDA's statistical reviewer treated OS/ORR/DoR as exploratory; FDA's reviewer additionally disagreed with the applicant's operational definition of the randomization stratum (data captured on the case report form) and instead used the stratum recorded at randomization as the primary analysis, and rebuilt the efficacy datasets from raw per-lesion data rather than the applicant's derived response datasets

### 31. Trametinib (Mekinist) — NDA 204114

**Sponsor:** GlaxoSmithKline, LLC

**Indication approved:** Unresectable or metastatic melanoma with BRAF V600E or V600K mutations as detected by an FDA-approved test (label specifies Mekinist is not indicated for patients who have received prior BRAF inhibitor therapy)

**Approval date:** May 29, 2013

**Pivotal trial:** METRIC (protocol MEK114267), NCT01245062

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled, crossover permitted at progression, biomarker-selected/enriched population, mid-trial SAP amendment changing endpoint status, dual primary-endpoint definition (protocol vs. regulatory)
- *Endpoints:* progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS) — key secondary, nominally significant despite substantial crossover, objective response rate (ORR)/duration of response (DoR)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test (as specified in SAP) vs. unstratified log-rank test (as actually used by the FDA reviewer), Cox proportional-hazards model, HR derived from log-rank U/V statistics (Pike estimator), Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Multiplicity:* no multiplicity adjustment proposed for secondary/subgroup endpoints; FDA treated OS, ORR, DoR and all subgroup analyses as exploratory/supportive
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* no interim efficacy analysis; trial designed for a single final PFS analysis at ~145 events (2-sided alpha 0.05)
- *Missing data/bias:* standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment; stratification-factor (baseline LDH) misclassification between IVRS and eCRF (11% discordance) led FDA to reject the SAP's stratified analysis as primary; no RPSFT/IPCW crossover adjustment applied to OS despite 47% of chemotherapy patients crossing over to trametinib
- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan (FDA used the ITT population and an unstratified log-rank test as primary, rejecting the SAP's "Primary Efficacy" [BRAF V600E, no brain metastases] population and stratified analysis); reviewer-documented mid-trial endpoint elevation (FDA feedback-driven) (FDA rejected the sponsor's proposed PFS/OS co-primary design pre-trial and recommended PFS alone, or OS alone, as primary)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Phase III, randomized (2:1), open-label, multinational trial (MEK114267) comparing trametinib 2 mg once daily to investigator's choice of chemotherapy (dacarbazine 1000 mg/m2 or paclitaxel 175 mg/m2, every 3 weeks) in adults with histologically confirmed Stage IIIC unresectable or Stage IV cutaneous melanoma, centrally confirmed BRAF V600E/K mutation-positive, measurable disease per RECIST 1.1, ECOG 0–1, no prior BRAF/MEK inhibitor exposure, and no more than one prior chemotherapy regimen for advanced disease; randomization was centralized and stratified by baseline LDH (>ULN vs. ≤ULN) and prior chemotherapy for advanced/metastatic disease (yes/no); chemotherapy patients could cross over to trametinib after independently confirmed progression
- Primary endpoint: investigator-assessed PFS (time from randomization to earliest RECIST 1.1 progression or death); at a July 2010 Type B meeting FDA rejected the sponsor's originally proposed PFS/OS co-primary design and recommended OS alone as the sole primary endpoint, while agreeing to discuss a PFS-only design; the sponsor amended the protocol on October 18, 2010 to make PFS the sole primary endpoint, then further amended the primary analysis population on October 21, 2011 (five days before the primary data cut-off) from the intent-to-treat (ITT) population to a "Primary Efficacy" (PE) population restricted to BRAF V600E patients without prior brain metastases; FDA's statistical reviewer used the full ITT population as primary instead
- Secondary endpoints: OS (time from randomization to death from any cause, including post-crossover deaths, censored at last known alive; survival follow-up planned to ~80% of randomized patients dead/lost to follow-up), ORR (confirmed/unconfirmed CR+PR by RECIST 1.1) and DoR, each also assessed by blinded independent radiology/oncology review (IRC)
- Sample size: ~297 patients (198 trametinib : 99 chemotherapy planned; 322 patients actually randomized, 214:108) to accrue 145 PFS events, giving 99% power to detect HR 0.4286 at 2-sided alpha 0.05 (median PFS assumption 3 vs. 7 months); pre-specified subgroup analyses (BRAF V600E without brain metastases, with/without prior chemotherapy) were powered at 87%; no interim efficacy analysis was planned
- Statistical methods: the SAP specified PFS/OS analyzed by stratified log-rank test (stratified on the randomization factors LDH and prior chemotherapy) with Kaplan-Meier estimation and Pike-estimator HRs, and ORR by stratified Fisher's exact test; FDA's reviewer found that the applicant's baseline LDH stratum used post-randomization lab values and/or IVRS-imputed values in 11% of patients (invalidating the randomization strata), and — after the applicant agreed in a face-to-face meeting to accept either an unstratified analysis or a stratified analysis excluding LDH — FDA adopted the unstratified log-rank test/Cox model on the ITT population as its primary analysis; the SAP proposed no multiplicity adjustment, so OS, ORR, DoR and all subgroup analyses were treated as exploratory; notably, FDA's own statistical review states the applicant's final SAP (submitted December 16, 2011) was never reviewed by FDA because the trial had not undergone Special Protocol Assessment

The approval letter and FDA Summary Review both state the trametinib application "was not referred to an FDA advisory committee" because the review "did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues that would benefit from the Advisory Committee's expertise."
- Trametinib was later approved (2014) in combination with dabrafenib for the same biomarker-defined population, based on trial COMBI-d, via efficacy supplements to both NDAs 204114 and 202806 — that combination approval is outside the scope of this single-agent entry.

The final statistical analysis plan (SAP) was submitted on December 16, 2011. As stated by the applicant's email on Sep. 21, 2012, 'Study MEK114267 was never submitted for a Special Protocol Assessment and therefore FDA comments on the statistical analysis plan (SAP) were never requested.'"

Secondary endpoints and subgroup analyses were considered as supportive and were to be tested if the primary analysis of PFS in the ITT population was statistically significant. **Reverse-engineered SAP** *[inferred]* — points not found verbatim, inferred from reported results.

- *[inferred, from the OS results section reporting only unstratified/stratified Cox and Pike HRs, while 51 of 108 chemotherapy patients (47%) are reported to have entered the crossover population]* No RPSFT/IPCW crossover-adjustment method was pre-specified or applied to the OS analysis — a proportion large enough that the nominally significant OS result (p=0.0136) is likely conservative with respect to the true single-agent effect, but no sensitivity analysis addressing this is described.
- *[inferred, from the reviewer's paraphrase of the applicant's analysis plan rather than a directly quoted SAP passage]* The IRC (independent radiology/oncology review) censoring rule — censoring PFS at the last "adequate" (CR/PR/SD) assessment prior to IRC-determined progression, death, new anticancer therapy, or two consecutive missing assessments — is reconstructed rather than directly quoted.

### 32. Afatinib (Gilotrif) — NDA 201292

**Sponsor:** Boehringer Ingelheim Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** First-line treatment of patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) whose tumors have EGFR exon 19 deletions or exon 21 (L858R) substitution mutations, as detected by an FDA-approved test

**Approval date:** July 12, 2013

**Pivotal trial:** LUX-Lung 3 (Study 1200.32), NCT00949650

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled, biomarker-selected/enriched population (central EGFR-mutation testing required for eligibility)
- *Endpoints:* progression-free survival (PFS), key secondary endpoint (objective response rate (ORR)/duration of response (DoR)/disease control rate (DCR), tested in fixed sequence), overall survival (OS), patient-reported outcomes/HRQoL
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing across secondary endpoints (objective response → disease control → OS); no control for multiplicity across the pre-specified EGFR-subgroup (Del19/L858R/Other) or race analyses
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Haybittle-Peto boundary for a single interim OS analysis (nominal p<0.0001) conducted at the time of the primary PFS analysis; final OS analysis planned after 209 deaths
- *Missing data/bias:* standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment, evaluation-time bias (assessed via imaging-schedule concordance), ascertainment bias assessment (investigator vs. blinded central review, plus "extreme worst case" and "symmetric worst case" censoring-rule sensitivity analyses)
- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan (sponsor's SAS code computed a linear rank test rather than the specified stratified log-rank test); endpoint not accepted as a valid regulatory endpoint for OS-based subgroup exclusion (reviewer declined to restrict the indication based on an unadjusted subgroup finding)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Randomized (2:1), open-label, parallel-arm, multinational Phase 3 trial in patients with Stage IIIB (with pleural/pericardial effusion) or Stage IV lung adenocarcinoma harboring a centrally-confirmed activating EGFR mutation, EGFR-TKI-naive, ECOG 0–1; randomization stratified by EGFR mutation type (Del19 vs. L858R vs. Other) and race (Asian vs. non-Asian) via central IVRS/IWRS; arms were afatinib 40 mg orally once daily (dose-adjustable 20–50 mg, continued to progression) vs. IV pemetrexed 500 mg/m² + cisplatin 75 mg/m² every 21 days for up to 6 cycles; trial was open-label because of differing routes of administration between arms
- Primary endpoint: PFS per RECIST 1.1 by blinded, independent central review (two radiologists plus an adjudicating third radiologist, with final progression date confirmed by an oncologist), defined as time from randomization to progression or death from any cause
- Key secondary endpoints, tested in a pre-specified fixed sequence: objective response (complete or partial response), disease control (response or stable disease), then overall survival; logistic regression (adjusted for stratification factors) was used for the response-rate endpoints, and OS was analyzed with the same stratified log-rank approach as PFS. Additional secondary endpoints included tumor shrinkage and time-to-deterioration in cough, dyspnea, and pain via EORTC QLQ-C30/LC13 (reported separately in a companion publication)
- Sample size/power: the primary PFS analysis was planned after approximately 217 PFS events, powered at 90% assuming a hazard ratio of 0.64 favoring afatinib; the planned final OS analysis required 209 deaths, with one interim OS look at the time of the primary PFS analysis using a pre-specified conservative stopping boundary (p<0.0001)
- Statistical methods: the primary PFS analysis had an unstratified-vs-stratified log-rank test issue flagged by FDA — the sponsor's SAS 9.2 code (`test trt; strata ... /test=none;`) computed a stratified linear rank test rather than the true stratified log-rank test; the FDA reviewer re-ran the correct syntax and obtained similar but non-identical results. Four protocol-defined sensitivity analyses recomputed PFS/censoring dates using investigator assessment, "extreme worst case" (earliest progression date if central/investigator disagree, chosen asymmetrically favoring chemotherapy), "symmetric worst case" (always choosing the earlier date), and treating unconfirmed investigator-detected progression as occurring at the next scheduled assessment. EGFR-subgroup (and 13 other exploratory factor) analyses were explicitly unadjusted for multiplicity per the SAP, which the FDA reviewer flagged as material to interpreting a nominally significant OS-harm signal (p=0.03) in the small "Other" EGFR mutation subgroup (37 patients, 23 deaths) — a finding that lost significance under even a simple post-hoc Bonferroni correction

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2013/201292s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Jonathan D. Norton, Division of Biometrics) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/201292Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/201292Orig1s000SumR.pdf

"Phase III study of afatinib or cisplatin plus pemetrexed in patients with metastatic lung adenocarcinoma with EGFR mutations." *J Clin Oncol.* 2013;31(27):3327-3334. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.2012.44.2806), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23816960/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Phase%20III%20study%20of%20afatinib%20or%20cisplatin%20plus%20pemetrexed%20in%20patients%20with%20metastatic%20lung%20adenocarcinoma%20with%20EGFR%20mutations)

**Other resources**

- Boehringer Ingelheim participates in the Vivli data-sharing platform generally (anonymized patient-level data, CRFs, and specifications for Phase 2–4 studies supporting a regulatory approval); individual confirmation that LUX-Lung 3 (Study 1200.32) specifically is listed as an available dataset on Vivli was not separately confirmed.
- No FDA Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held; per the Summary Review, FDA stated the NDA "was not referred for review to the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee because outside expertise was not necessary as there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion." The application received priority review, and afatinib held orphan drug designation for this NSCLC subpopulation.
- Companion HRQoL/symptom-control publication: Yang JC, Hirsh V, Schuler M, et al. "Symptom control and quality of life in LUX-Lung 3." *J Clin Oncol.* 2013;31(27):3342-3350. DOI 10.1200/JCO.2012.46.1764, PMID 23816967.

> "Study 1200.32 was a randomized, open-label, parallel-arm Phase 3 trial comparing afatinib with pemetrexed/cisplatin. Eligible patients had Stage IIIB or IV adenocarcinoma, were EGFR-TKI (tyrosine-kinase inhibitor) naïve, and had an EGFR mutation. Screening was done using a laboratory developed test. Patients were randomized in a 2:1 ratio to afatinib or chemotherapy."
>
> "The primary endpoint of the study was progression-free survival (PFS) as determined by central assessment. Afatinib was statistically superior to chemotherapy by stratified log-rank test with p = 0.0003. The median PFS was 11.14 months (95% confidence interval (CI) = [9.63, 13.63]) in the afatinib arm compared to 6.90 months (95% CI = [5.39, 8.25]) in the chemotherapy arm."

The results were similar but not identical."

>

An interim OS analysis was to occur at the time of the primary analysis, using a stopping boundary of p < 0.0001. The final OS analysis was to occur after 209 deaths."
>
> "Despite the interest in the EGFR subgroups, there was no plan for controlling multiplicity across the three subgroups. The SAP stated that the efficacy would be 'explored' in these subgroups along with numerous other factors."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §5.1 "Statistical Issues," p.22]*

> "If one uses a post-hoc Bonferroni correction for the three subgroups, then the OS result is no longer significant. ### 33. Obinutuzumab (Gazyva) — BLA 125486

**Sponsor:** Genentech, Inc. (U.S. applicant; global sponsor F. Hoffmann-La Roche)

**Indication approved:** In combination with chlorambucil, for the treatment of patients with previously untreated chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL)

**Approval date:** November 1, 2013

**Pivotal trial:** CLL11 / Study BO21004, Stage 1a, NCT01010061

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled, 3-arm parallel design (GClb vs. RClb vs. Clb) with 2:2:1 overall randomization, fixed-duration regimen (six 28-day cycles in all arms), crossover permitted at progression (Clb-alone arm patients could cross to GClb), dual primary-endpoint definition (protocol vs. regulatory) — investigator-assessed PFS was the protocol-defined primary endpoint, but IRC-assessed PFS was pre-specified as the basis for U.S. regulatory decisions
- *Endpoints:* progression-free survival (PFS), minimal residual disease (MRD) response rate, objective response rate (ORR)/duration of response (DoR), overall survival (OS, immature/secondary), event-free survival
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test (stratified by Binet stage), Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Multiplicity:* closed testing procedure (global closed test for any difference among the 3 arms in PFS before proceeding to pairwise Stage 1 comparisons); no adjustment for multiplicity on secondary endpoints, because Type I error not spent in Stage 1 was reserved for Stage 2
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design, Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function (overall alpha of 0.05 allocated across a Stage 2 interim analysis and Stage 2 final analysis)
- *Missing data/bias:* standard right-censoring at last evaluable tumor assessment (or at randomization if no post-baseline assessment), attrition bias (reviewer-conducted sensitivity analyses treating missed assessments/loss-to-follow-up as PFS events under worst-case assumptions)
- *Regulatory:* Breakthrough Therapy Designation (granted May 9, 2013, alongside priority review and orphan drug designation for CLL); regulatory approval based solely on the Stage 1a (GClb vs. Clb) comparison, with Stage 1b (RClb vs. Clb) and Stage 2 (GClb vs. RClb) reported later as separate ClinicalTrials.gov records

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Open-label, 3-arm, randomized, parallel-group Phase 3 trial (BO21004) in previously untreated CD20+ CLL patients with comorbidities (Cumulative Illness Rating Scale >6 and/or creatinine clearance <70 mL/min); randomized 2:2:1 to obinutuzumab + chlorambucil (GClb), rituximab + chlorambucil (RClb), or chlorambucil alone (Clb), stratified by Binet stage and region (analyses ultimately stratified by Binet stage only, given small regional cell sizes). The trial was structured in stages for separate primary analyses: Stage 1a = GClb vs. Clb (this BLA's basis, reported as NCT01010061), Stage 1b = RClb vs. Clb (NCT01998880), Stage 2 = GClb vs. RClb head-to-head (NCT02053610). Each arm received a fixed 6 cycles of 28-day chlorambucil (0.5 mg/kg orally, days 1 and 15); GClb patients received obinutuzumab 1000 mg IV on days 1 (split 100 mg/900 mg by amendment), 8, and 15 of cycle 1 and day 1 of cycles 2–6; RClb patients received rituximab 375 mg/m² (cycle 1) then 500 mg/m² (cycles 2–6). Clb-arm patients with progression could cross over to GClb
- Primary endpoint: PFS, defined as time from randomization to first progression, relapse, or death from any cause per IWCLL criteria; the protocol-defined primary analysis used investigator assessment, but IRC-assessed PFS was the endpoint FDA relied on for the U.S. approval decision
- Secondary endpoints: end-of-treatment response rate, best overall response rate (CR/CRi/nPR/PR per IWCLL), duration of response, molecular remission (MRD-negative) rate, event-free survival, disease-free survival, time to new anti-leukemic therapy, and overall survival; percentage outcomes were compared using a chi-square test with continuity correction
- Sample size/power and interim analysis plan: FDA's public statistical review does not disclose the sponsor's protocol-specified sample-size/power calculations (redacted portions of the review), but confirms four protocol-specified primary-PFS analysis triggers: the Stage 1a analysis (triggered once 118 patients were randomized to Clb and 175 total PFS events had occurred across the 3 arms), a Stage 1b analysis, a Stage 2 interim analysis, and a Stage 2 final analysis — with Stage 2's overall alpha allocated between the interim and final looks via a Lan-DeMets spending function. This BLA submission (356 Stage 1a patients: 238 GClb, 118 Clb) supported approval on the strength of the Stage 1a result alone
- Statistical methods: primary time-to-event comparisons used a two-sided, Binet-stage-stratified log-rank test with Kaplan-Meier median estimation; to control overall Type I error at 0.05, the design first required a global closed test for any difference in PFS among all 3 arms before unlocking pairwise Stage 1 comparisons. Six protocol-defined PFS sensitivity analyses (missing assessments as events, censoring for new anti-leukemic treatment, early-withdrawal-as-event, censoring for late deaths, protocol-defined event counts, per-protocol population) all showed hazard ratios in the 0.12–0.26 range, consistent with the primary result (HR 0.16); the FDA reviewer additionally ran two independent worst-case sensitivity analyses for missed assessments/loss-to-follow-up, yielding HRs of 0.15 and 0.30

### 34. Ibrutinib (Imbruvica) — NDA 205552

**Sponsor:** Pharmacyclics, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) in patients who have received at least one prior therapy

**Approval date:** 2013-11-13 (original accelerated approval)

**Pivotal trial:** PCYC-1104-CA, NCT01236391 — a single-arm Phase 2 trial, NOT a randomized Phase III trial (this original approval was granted under FDA's accelerated-approval pathway)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial (no internal comparator)
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR)/duration of response (DoR)/disease control rate (DCR)
- *Primary analysis:* descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (point estimate + confidence interval; no formal hypothesis test)
- *Missing data/bias:* investigator-assessed ORR as the primary read, with Independent Review Committee (IRC) central read as a corroborating sensitivity analysis
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval based on a surrogate endpoint, subject to confirmatory-trial requirement (21 CFR 314.510)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- PCYC-1104-CA was a multicenter, open-label, single-arm Phase 2 study (not a randomized Phase III trial) in 111 evaluable patients with relapsed or refractory MCL who had received at least one prior therapy (ClinicalTrials.gov lists 115 total enrolled); FDA's Summary Review states "Study PCYC-1104-CA was designed as a nonrandomized study. Therefore, all statistical analyses were descriptive and no formal statistical comparisons were performed"
- Patients received oral ibrutinib 560 mg once daily until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity, with no comparator arm
- Primary endpoint: investigator-assessed overall response rate (ORR = CR + PR), assessed per the revised (2007) International Working Group (IWG) response criteria for non-Hodgkin lymphoma — the first regulatory MCL application to use the 2007 criteria rather than the 1999 criteria used for the earlier Velcade/Revlimid MCL accelerated approvals; a key feature of the 2007 criteria is mandatory integration of FDG-PET scans for documentation of complete response, and 100% of patients had baseline FDG-PET scans (versus 25% exploratory use in the Revlimid trial and none in the Velcade trial)
- Key secondary/supportive measures: duration of response (DoR), an Independent Review Committee (IRC) central read of ORR as a corroborating analysis, and safety; there was no formal PFS/OS comparison because there was no comparator arm, and FDA explicitly noted that long-term correlation of FDG-PET-based response with outcomes was unresolved ("Patients were not followed long enough to correlate FDG-PET scan determination of response with long-term outcomes")
- No sample-size/power calculation, interim analysis plan, or alpha-spending plan applied, because the trial was a single-arm descriptive study — FDA's statistical review contains no formal Type-I-error control section, consistent with a non-comparative accelerated-approval design
- Statistical methods were limited to descriptive point estimates and two-sided 95% confidence intervals for ORR and Kaplan-Meier-type estimation of median duration of response (95% CI lower bound only, upper bound "not reached/not evaluable"); no censoring rule beyond standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment is described in the public FDA materials, and no CI method (e.g., Clopper-Pearson) is specified in the public review

- FDA Summary Review (combined statistical/clinical/CDTL review; no separate StatR/MedR was filed for this NDA) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/205552Orig1s000SumR.pdf

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1306220), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23782157/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Targeting%20BTK%20with%20Ibrutinib%20in%20Relapsed%20or%20Refractory%20Mantle-Cell%20Lymphoma)

- No FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held. Per FDA's Summary Review: "This application was not taken to an Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee meeting because there were no issues with the trial design, conduct, endpoint or data analysis." The approval letter states similarly: "Your application for Imbruvica (ibrutinib) Capsules, 140 mg was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues in the intended population."
