### 35. Ramucirumab (Cyramza) — BLA 125477

**Sponsor:** Eli Lilly and Company (originally developed by ImClone Systems, acquired by Lilly)

**Indication approved:** Advanced or metastatic gastric or gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) adenocarcinoma, as a single agent, in patients with disease progression on or after prior fluoropyrimidine- or platinum-containing chemotherapy

**Approval date:** 2014-04-21

**Pivotal trial:** REGARD (I4T-IE-JVBD / IMCL CP12-0715), NCT00917384

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven trial
- *Endpoints:* overall survival (OS, primary), progression-free survival (PFS), objective response rate (ORR)/duration of response (DoR), patient-reported outcomes/HRQoL (EORTC QLQ-C30)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified), Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (OS tested first; PFS tested only if OS was statistically significant; ORR/DoR/PRO treated as exploratory, unadjusted)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design, non-binding futility boundary (beta-spending, Gamma(-1) spending function) at a single interim futility look (35% of expected OS events), gamma-family alpha-spending function (nuisance Gamma(-30), used only for sample-size planning), Data Monitoring Committee (DMC/DSMB)
- *Missing data/bias:* standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment; reviewer-identified stratification-factor discrepancies between IVRS/IWRS and eCRF data (affecting 7.6% of patients), resolved via a reviewer-conducted sensitivity analysis
- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan (sample size/event target amended three times by the sponsor without FDA statistical review)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- REGARD was a multinational, multicenter, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial in 355 patients with metastatic gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma who had progressed during or within 4 months after first-line platinum- or fluoropyrimidine-containing combination therapy (or within 6 months after adjuvant therapy), ECOG PS 0-1, and adequate organ function
- Patients were randomized via IVRS/IWRS to ramucirumab 8 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks plus best supportive care (BSC, n=238) or placebo plus BSC (n=117), stratified by weight loss (≥10% vs. <10% over the prior 3 months), geographic region (three groupings), and location of primary tumor (gastric vs. GEJ)
- Primary endpoint: overall survival (OS), time from randomization to death from any cause; patients alive at data cutoff or lost to follow-up censored at the last date known to be alive
- Secondary endpoints: progression-free survival (PFS; time from randomization to RECIST v1.0-defined progression or death), a 12-week PFS rate, objective response rate (ORR; CR+PR per RECIST v1.0, non-responders imputed for missing assessments), duration of response, and change from baseline in EORTC QLQ-C30 quality-of-life scores; safety and pharmacokinetic/immunogenicity endpoints also collected
- Sample size/design evolution: originally powered for 615 patients/459 OS events (90% power); amended (Protocol Version 6.0, November 23, 2010) to 315 patients/256 events (80% power, revised assumed HR 0.69, assumed median OS 5 vs. 7.25 months); then amended again to 348 patients/268 events (Version 7.0, October 31, 2011), which also converted the futility boundary from binding to non-binding — FDA's statistical reviewer explicitly noted "the sample size was amended 3 times without statistical review by the Agency"
- One non-binding interim futility analysis of OS was planned at 94 deaths (35% of target events), using a Gamma(-1) beta-spending function for the futility boundary; there was no interim efficacy analysis, and a nuisance Gamma(-30) alpha-spending function was used only for sample-size planning purposes
- Primary analysis method: stratified log-rank test (using the same three stratification factors as randomization, per IVRS/IWRS-recorded values), stratified Cox proportional-hazards model for the hazard ratio, Kaplan-Meier estimation of median survival times; a gatekeeping/hierarchical testing strategy controlled overall two-sided Type I error at 0.05 by testing PFS only if the primary OS analysis was statistically significant, with other secondary endpoints treated as exploratory (unadjusted) per the FDA reviewer's comments
- Results: stratified log-rank p=0.0473 for OS; median OS 5.2 months (95% CI 4.4-5.7) vs. 3.8 months (95% CI 2.8-4.7); stratified Cox HR 0.776 (95% CI 0.603-0.998)

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2014/125477lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID 3440485) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/125477Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Medical Review (contains §9.3 Advisory Committee discussion) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/125477Orig1s000MedR.pdf

"Ramucirumab monotherapy for previously treated advanced gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (REGARD): an international, randomised, multicentre, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial." *Lancet.* 2014;383(9911):31-39. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(13)61719-5>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24094768/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Ramucirumab%20monotherapy%20for%20previously%20treated%20advanced%20gastric%20or%20gastro-oesophageal%20junction%20adenocarcinoma)

**Other resources**

- No FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held, despite the Medical Review noting FDA had initially anticipated one. Per FDA's Medical Review §9.3: "This application was not referred to ODAC because outside expertise was not necessary as there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion."

### 36. siltuximab (Sylvant) — BLA 125496

**Sponsor:** Janssen Biotech, Inc. (Janssen Research & Development)

**Approval date:** April 23, 2014

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover permitted at progression
- *Endpoints:* durable tumor and symptomatic response (composite, primary), tumor response, time to treatment failure, hemoglobin response, PRO-based symptom endpoints (MCD-SS, FACIT-F)
- *Primary analysis:* exact Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test (stratified), Kaplan-Meier estimation, stratified log-rank test (time-to-event secondaries)
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (6 ordered secondary endpoints)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Data Monitoring Committee (DMC), no formal alpha-spending boundary — [inferred] see entry below
- *Regulatory:* FDA guidance against single-arm design for registration (documented in Statistical Review)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Phase 2, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial (38 centers, 19 countries) in patients with symptomatic MCD, measurable disease confirmed by central pathology review, HIV-negative and HHV-8-negative
- Arms: siltuximab 11 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks + best supportive care (BSC), n=53, vs. placebo + BSC, n=26; randomization stratified by concomitant corticosteroid use at study entry; placebo patients with treatment failure could cross over to open-label siltuximab
- Primary endpoint: durable tumor and symptomatic response — a composite of (a) tumor response (complete or partial response by modified Cheson criteria, assessed by independent review) and (b) resolution/stabilization of MCD-related symptoms (per investigator-graded NCI-CTCAE severity of 34 MCD-related signs/symptoms), both sustained for at least 18 weeks during the Blinded Treatment Period
- Six protocol-specified secondary endpoints tested sequentially at 2-sided alpha=0.05 after the primary endpoint: (1) tumor response by central review, (2) time to treatment failure, (3) hemoglobin response (≥15 g/L increase at Week 13, in patients with baseline anemia), (4) time to improvement in the Multicentric Castleman's Disease Symptom Scale (MCD-SS) total score, (5) time to improvement in FACIT-Fatigue score, (6) discontinuation of corticosteroids (≥9 consecutive weeks corticosteroid-free)
- Sample size: sized (2:1 randomization) to detect a 30% response rate with siltuximab vs. 5% with placebo at 2-sided alpha=0.05 and 80% power
- Analysis method: primary and categorical secondary endpoints compared via an exact Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by baseline corticosteroid use; time-to-event secondary endpoints compared via a log-rank test stratified by the same factor; Kaplan-Meier estimation used for time-to-event medians
- Two DMC meetings were held (after the first 41 evaluable-equivalent enrollees, and a final review at end of enrollment); no protocol changes resulted from either meeting
- Result: durable tumor and symptomatic response rate 34% (siltuximab) vs. 0% (placebo), p=0.0012; tumor response, time to treatment failure, and hemoglobin response secondaries were also statistically significant in the pre-specified sequence, while the MCD-SS, FACIT-F, and corticosteroid-discontinuation secondaries were not

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2014/125496s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (2014, original approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2014/125496s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Reviewer: Chia-Wen Ko, PhD, Division of Biometrics 5) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/125496Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01024036 (no protocol/SAP documents posted in the Documents tab)
- Pivotal publication: van Rhee F, Wong RS, Munshi N, et al. "Siltuximab for multicentric Castleman's disease: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial." *Lancet Oncol.* 2014;15(9):966-974. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(14)70319-5>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25042199/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Siltuximab%20for%20multicentric%20Castleman%27s%20disease%3A%20a%20randomised%2C%20double-blind%2C%20placebo-controlled%20trial)

**Other resources**

- Johnson & Johnson/Janssen participates in the Yale Open Data Access (YODA) Project for data-sharing requests; trial-specific MCD2001 IPD availability was not individually confirmed in this pass.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this original approval.
- FDA's Statistical Review explicitly documents pre-submission regulatory advice to the sponsor that "a single-arm trial would not be acceptable for registration" for this indication, given MCD's heterogeneous natural history — a notable design-level regulatory interaction worth flagging distinctly from the post-hoc review commentary seen in other entries in this census.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Executive Summary, p.5]*

> "The main study MCD2001 supporting this application is a phase 2, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study in 79 patients with MCD to assess the efficacy and safety of Siltuximab plus best supportive care (n=53) compared with placebo plus best supportive care (n=26). Patient randomization was stratified by concomitant corticosteroid use at study entry. The major efficacy outcome of the study was durable tumor and symptomatic response, defined as tumor response (complete or partial response based on modified Cheson criteria) assessed by independent review and complete resolution or stabilization of MCD symptoms, sustained for at least 18 weeks."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §2.1 "Regulatory Interactions," p.6]*

> "A single-arm trial would not be acceptable for registration, because a single-arm trial is unlikely to provide meaningful data to assess clinical benefit to treatment for such a disease with several patterns of disease progression. All study patients should be required to be symptomatic and have measurable disease. Centralized pathology reviews should be used for eligibility. The definition for response as the primary study endpoint should also include stabilization or improvement in disease-related symptoms for a partial response and absence of symptoms for a complete response."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.2 "Statistical Methodologies," p.8-9]*

> "The primary efficacy endpoint was durable tumor and symptomatic response during the blinded Treatment Period, based on independently reviewed tumor assessments and investigator determined severity grades for disease related signs and symptoms. The primary analysis of the primary endpoint occurred after all study patients had completed the Week 48 assessment. The durable tumor and symptomatic response rates for the 2 treatment groups were compared using an exact Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test, adjusted for the stratification factor, baseline corticosteroid use... The study was sized, with a 2:1 randomization, to detect a 30% response rate in the siltuximab group versus 5% response rate in the placebo group with a 2-sided 5% significance level and 80% power. Secondary response endpoints were also compared between the treatment groups based on an exact Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test with adjustment for baseline corticosteroid use. Time-to-event endpoints were compared between the treatment groups using the log-rank test stratified by baseline corticosteroid use."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.4.2 "The Secondary Endpoints," p.12]*

> "Study MCD2001 has 6 protocol-specified major secondary endpoints for sequential testing after the primary endpoint. Table 5 shows the results for the 6 multiplicity-controlled secondary endpoints in the pre-specified testing sequence. Statistical significance was found for the difference between siltuximab and placebo in tumor response and median time to treatment failure in the ITT population. Statistical significance was also reported for the endpoint of hemoglobin response in the subgroup of anemic patients."

No genuine sponsor SAP document itself was found publicly posted (ClinicalTrials.gov's Documents tab has no entries for NCT01024036, consistent with this being a pre-2017 registration); the passages above are FDA's Statistical Review description of the SAP's content as executed, not the SAP document itself. The FDA review's characterization of the interim DMC process (two meetings, no protocol changes) suggests routine safety monitoring rather than a formal group-sequential efficacy stopping rule — no alpha-spending function or interim efficacy boundary is described anywhere in the review, so this is treated as **[inferred]** absence of formal interim efficacy monitoring rather than a confirmed design feature.

### 37. ceritinib (Zykadia) — NDA 205755

**Sponsor:** Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation

**Indication approved:** ALK-positive metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with disease progression on or intolerance to crizotinib — accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314 Subpart H, based on tumor response rate and duration of response, with continued approval contingent on a confirmatory trial

**Approval date:** April 29, 2014

**Pivotal trial:** Study CLDK378X2101 / ASCEND-1, NCT01283516

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label — [note: not currently in Keyword_Taxonomy.md's Design table; flagged as a candidate new term, "Single-arm, open-label, dose-escalation/expansion (accelerated approval)," seen here and in the belinostat/blinatumomab entries in this same batch]
- *Endpoints:* overall response rate (ORR, BIRC-assessed, primary for regulatory purposes), duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival
- *Primary analysis:* exact binomial confidence interval for ORR, Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval (21 CFR 314 Subpart H), Breakthrough Therapy Designation, End-of-Phase-1/pre-Phase-3 meeting agreement on regulatory ORR threshold, reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan (primary assessor switched from investigator to BIRC)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study X2101 was a Phase I, multicenter, open-label, dose-escalation/dose-expansion trial of ceritinib (LDK378) in patients with tumors harboring ALK genetic abnormalities; the dose-escalation stage used an adaptive Bayesian logistic regression model (2-parameter, escalation-with-overdose-control) to identify the maximum tolerated dose, followed by disease-specific expansion cohorts (Arms A1/A2: ALK+ NSCLC progressed on/after a prior ALK inhibitor; Arm B: ALK+ NSCLC previously treated with an ALK inhibitor but not refractory; Arm C: ALK+ NSCLC ALK-inhibitor-naive; Arm D: non-NSCLC ALK+ malignancies)
- The regulatory (accelerated-approval) efficacy population was 163 NSCLC patients in Arms A1+A2 (all previously treated with crizotinib), treated at the 750 mg/day recommended Phase 2 dose
- Original protocol specified investigator-assessed RECIST v1.0 response as primary, with a purely descriptive analysis plan (ORR and 95% CI by treatment subgroup, no formal hypothesis test); FDA later required the protocol be amended to add Blinded Independent [Central] Review Committee (BIRC) assessment, which became the primary analysis for regulatory purposes once BIRC review was feasible for nearly all patients
- At an End-of-Phase-1/pre-Phase-3 meeting (Nov 20, 2012), FDA and Novartis agreed the NDA would need to demonstrate an ORR >52% in at least 80 patients (exact binomial 95% CI lower bound >40%) meeting specific eligibility criteria (prior crizotinib, dose ≥750 mg/day, ≥12 weeks follow-up) to support accelerated approval — the actual submitted efficacy population (n=163) and observed ORR far exceeded this pre-agreed bar
- Result: BIRC-assessed ORR 44% (95% CI 36-52%) in the efficacy population (N=163), investigator-assessed ORR 55% (95% CI 47-62%); median duration of response 7.1 months (BIRC, 95% CI 5.6-NE) vs. 7.4 months (investigator)
- No formal multiplicity control or interim/alpha-spending plan — consistent with a single-arm, descriptive-statistics accelerated-approval design; not referred to ODAC (FDA determined the application raised no controversial public-health questions warranting a public advisory committee meeting, per the Division Director Review)
- A confirmatory Phase III trial (Study A2303, later reported as ASCEND-4/-5 family trials) was required as a post-marketing requirement under Subpart H to verify clinical benefit

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2014/205755Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (2014, original approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2014/205755s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Division Director (Summary) Review, which contains the substantive statistical/regulatory-history detail for this application (the separately filed Statistical Review PDF is only a 1-page filing checklist) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/205755Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (ASCEND-1) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01283516 (no protocol/SAP documents posted in the Documents tab)
- Pivotal publication: Shaw AT, Kim DW, Mehra R, et al. "Ceritinib in ALK-Rearranged Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer." *N Engl J Med.* 2014;370(13):1189-1197. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1311107), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24670165/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Ceritinib%20in%20ALK-Rearranged%20Non-Small-Cell%20Lung%20Cancer)

**Other resources**

- Novartis participates in Vivli.org for IPD sharing requests; trial-specific ASCEND-1/X2101 availability was not individually confirmed in this pass.
- No FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held; two Special Government Employees (a physician and a patient representative) were consulted individually instead, per the Division Director Review.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Division Director Review, "Regulatory History," p.3-4]*

> "November 20, 2012: End of Phase 1/Pre-Phase 3 with Novartis. The purpose of the meeting was to seek advice on the ongoing trial (CLKD378X2101) to support a request for accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.510 (Subpart H)... FDA agreed that ALK-rearranged NSCLC patients who have received prior chemotherapy and prior crizotinib represent a population with an unmet medical need and that demonstration of durable objective tumor shrinkage (ORR) may be used to support market authorization under 21 CFR 314 Subpart H regulations if both the magnitude of the response rate and duration of responses appear likely to predict clinical benefit and the risk-benefit analysis appears favorable at the time of review. An NDA submission would be based on demonstration of an ORR of more than 52% observed in at least 80 patients (corresponding to an exact binomial 95% CI with a lower bound greater than 40%)... For regulatory purposes, the determination of overall response rate and response duration would be based upon independent review."

*[verbatim, FDA Division Director Review, describing the sponsor's original protocol-specified analysis plan, p.13-14]*

> "The analysis plan was limited to descriptive statistics, with calculation of the objective response rate and respective 95% confidence intervals around the observed response rate in each treatment subgroup (Arms A1, A2, B, or C). Descriptive statistics would also be applied to the assessment of duration of response, progression-free survival, and overall survival, including assessment of time-to-event endpoints at 3, 6, 12, 18, and 24 months."

*[verbatim, FDA Division Director Review, documenting the FDA-driven amendment switching the primary assessor from investigator to BIRC, p.5]*

> "Novartis stated that the protocol was amended to require BIRC review in response to FDA's advice during the November 20, 2012 [meeting], however Novartis anticipates that images will not be obtainable for all patients. In light of this, FDA agreed that the BIRC-assessment would be supportive, with investigator-assessed responses as primary... [later, Nov 20, 2013 Pre-NDA meeting] As previously stated, FDA considers the BIRC-assessed analyses to be the primary analyses for efficacy, conducted in all patients receiving at least one dose of LDK378, with analyses in the 'evaluable analysis set' to be supportive."

*[verbatim, FDA Division Director Review, results, p.15-16 — the actual executed primary analysis]*

> "Since only 2 of the 163 patients refused to give consent for BIRC review, as originally requested by FDA in November 2012, the primary efficacy analysis for overall response rate and response duration should be based on the BIRC-assessment and the investigator-assessment is considered secondary... Overall Response Rate (BIRC Assessment, N=163): 44% (95% CI 36, 52). Overall Response Rate (Investigator Assessment, N=163): 55% (95% CI 47, 62). Median duration of response: 7.1 months (BIRC, 95% CI 5.6, NE) vs. 7.4 months (Investigator, 95% CI 5.4, 10.1)."

This is a clean documented example of the primary-analysis assessor itself moving during the course of a single-arm trial — first investigator-assessed by protocol, then FDA-requested BIRC review made supportive-only per an early sponsor amendment, then re-elevated to primary once BIRC coverage proved to be nearly complete (161/163 patients) — with FDA's own review recording each step of that back-and-forth rather than treating it as a fixed a priori plan.

### 38. belinostat (Beleodaq) — NDA 206256

**Sponsor:** Spectrum Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Relapsed or refractory peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL) — accelerated approval based on tumor response rate; continued approval contingent on verification of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial

**Approval date:** July 3, 2014

**Pivotal trial:** BELIEF (Study PXD101-CLN-19), NCT00865969

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label — [note: not in current taxonomy as a distinct "Design" term; existing entries with a single-arm accelerated-approval design (e.g. PREVAIL-adjacent context) do not supply one either, so this is flagged as a candidate new term, "Single-arm, open-label (accelerated approval)"]
- *Endpoints:* overall response rate (ORR, by independent review, primary), duration of response (DoR), time to response, time to progression, PFS, overall survival
- *Primary analysis:* exact (Clopper-Pearson-type) confidence interval for ORR, Kaplan-Meier estimation (duration of response)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Simon two-stage optimal design (built-in futility analysis), Data Monitoring Committee
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval (single-arm ORR basis), FDA Statistical Review documents no formal hypothesis test (descriptive analysis only)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study CLN-19 (BELIEF) was a single-arm, open-label, multicenter, nonrandomized Phase 2 trial of belinostat monotherapy (1,000 mg/m²/day, days 1-5 of a 21-day cycle) in patients with relapsed/refractory PTCL after at least 1 prior systemic therapy; conducted under a Special Protocol Agreement (SPA) obtained September 2008
- 129 patients enrolled (May 2009-August 2011) at 62 sites (US, Canada, Europe, Israel, Africa); 120 of the 129 had PTCL diagnosis confirmed by central/independent review committee (IRC) and made up the primary efficacy analysis population
- Primary endpoint: ORR by IRC (complete + partial response); secondary endpoints: duration of response (DoR), time to response, time to progression, progression-free survival, 1-year PFS rate, overall survival, 1-year survival rate
- Design used Simon's two-stage optimal design: hypothesized ORR of 20% (target) vs. 9% (uninteresting/null); a built-in futility rule required at least 5 objective responses among the first 41 evaluable patients (by IRC) to continue; final target of ~100 evaluable patients (120 enrolled assuming 15% attrition) sized to detect ORR=20% with 90% power at one-sided alpha=0.05 (95% CI half-width ≈7.8%)
- As a nonrandomized single-arm study, all statistical analyses were descriptive; no formal hypothesis tests were performed against a comparator — FDA's Statistical Review states this explicitly
- Duration of response was calculated two ways: per International Working Group (IWG) criteria (censoring at last evaluable assessment) and per SAP-defined criteria that additionally counted death as an event (used for labeling)
- Result: ORR 25.8% (95% CI 18.3%-34.6%) by IRC in the efficacy analysis population (n=120); median duration of response 8.4 months (95% CI 4.5-29.4) among 31 responders; investigator-assessed ORR was concordant at 22.5%

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2014/206256Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (2014, original approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2014/206256lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Reviewer: Erik Bloomquist, PhD, Division of Biometrics V) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/206256Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00865969 (no protocol/SAP documents posted in the Documents tab; this trial predates ClinicalTrials.gov's sponsor document-posting norms)
- Pivotal publication: O'Connor OA, Horwitz S, Masszi T, et al. "Belinostat in Patients With Relapsed or Refractory Peripheral T-Cell Lymphoma: Results of the Pivotal Phase II BELIEF (CLN-19) Study." *J Clin Oncol.* 2015;33(23):2492-2499. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.2014.59.2782), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26101246/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Belinostat%20in%20Patients%20With%20Relapsed%20or%20Refractory%20Peripheral%20T-Cell%20Lymphoma%3A%20Results%20of%20the%20Pivotal%20Phase%20II%20BELIEF%20%28CLN-19%29%20Study)

**Other resources**

- Acrotech Biopharma (which acquired belinostat rights from Spectrum) has not been confirmed to participate in Vivli/YODA-style IPD sharing; trial-specific CLN-19 dataset availability was not identified in this pass.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this original approval.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Executive Summary, p.4]*

> "The sponsor relied on a single-arm, phase 2, pivotal study to support their NDA submission (Study PXD101-CLN-19). Study CLN-19 examined belinostat monotherapy at a dose of 1,000 mg/m2/day in the treatment of patients with relapsed or refractory PTCL after failure of at least 1 line of prior systemic therapy. The study used the optimal 2-stage Simon design. The planned enrollment was approximately 120 patients to ensure a minimum of 100 evaluable patients at the conclusion of accrual... Study CLN-19 was designed as a nonrandomized study. Therefore, all statistical analyses were descriptive and no formal statistical comparisons were performed."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3 "Statistical Evaluation," p.6]*

> "There were five versions of protocol with the first version dated 4/25/08 and the last version (V. 5) dated 1/4/2010. No patients were enrolled under protocol versions 1, 2 and 4. The first patient was enrolled under protocol version 3.0. The original SAP was dated 4/11/2008 and the final SAP was signed off on 1/30/2013. The SAP was amended twice during the course of the study, on 7/16/2008 and 2/11/2011, in order to align with amendments to the protocol. The only change in the SAP that may affect the efficacy evaluation is the addition of the duration of response calculated per IWG criteria."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.1.1 "Study Design," p.6-7 — sample size and interim monitoring]*

> "The sponsor hypothesized an ORR of p1=20% for belinostat and a minimal or 'uninteresting' ORR of p0=9%. Based upon these numbers, if there were fewer than 5 objective responses in the first 41 evaluable patients (based on IRC), the trial would have been discontinued for futility... This sample size was calculated assuming that at least 14 objective responses in 100 evaluable patients were required to confirm the 20% target response rate with an alpha of 0.05 assuming a power of 90%... DMC (Data Monitoring Committee) meetings were conducted twice in the study, one after the first cohort of 41 evaluable patients enrolled and a final review at the end of enrollment. There was no change to the protocol at either of the 2 DMC meetings."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.1.2 "Efficacy Endpoints," p.7]*

> "As defined by the international working group (IWG), the duration of response was measured from the date that measurement criteria were first met for CR or PR (whichever status was recorded first) until the first subsequent date that relapse or progression was documented. The duration of response was also measured by the SAP-defined criteria that expanded the IWG criteria by including death in addition to relapse or progression (i.e. based on the International Harmonization Project [IHP] revision of IWG criteria). The SAP-defined criteria were used in the labelling."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.4.1 "Results of Overall response," p.12]*

> "Based on FDA analysis, study CLN-19 had an overall response rate (ORR) of 25.8% (95% CI [18.3%, 34.6%]). The median duration of response, based on 31 responding patients, was 8.4 months (95% CI, 4.5-29.4)."

### 39. idelalisib (Zydelig) — NDA 206545

**Sponsor:** Gilead Sciences, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Two indications approved the same day under companion NDAs with different evidentiary bases and different review pathways: (1) NDA 206545 (this entry), standard approval — relapsed chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), in combination with rituximab, in patients for whom rituximab alone would be considered appropriate therapy due to other co-morbidities; and (2) NDA 205858 (cross-referenced in the same approval letters), accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.510 — relapsed follicular B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (FL) and relapsed small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL), each as monotherapy in patients who had received at least two prior systemic therapies, based on objective response rate (ORR) as a surrogate endpoint

**Approval date:** July 23, 2014 (both NDA 206545 and NDA 205858 approved on this date; the FL/SLL accelerated-approval indications under NDA 205858 were later voluntarily withdrawn by Gilead effective May 26, 2022, per 87 FR 32031)

**Pivotal trial:** For the CLL indication (the true SAP-bearing pivotal trial for this entry): Study 116 (Gilead protocol GS-US-312-0116), NCT01539512 — Phase III, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of idelalisib + rituximab vs. placebo + rituximab, stopped early for efficacy. For the FL/SLL accelerated-approval indications (documented here for completeness, not the SAP-depth focus of this entry): Study 101-09 (GS-1101-09), NCT01282424 — single-arm, open-label Phase II study using a Simon optimal two-stage design, ORR as primary endpoint

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (Study 116); early-stopped for efficacy (Study 116, halted after the first interim on DMC recommendation); event-driven trial (PFS-event-driven, Study 116); single-arm, open-label trial (Study 101-09, the accelerated-approval basis for the separate FL/SLL indications) — note: Study 101-09's Simon optimal two-stage design (null ORR ≤20% vs. alternative ORR ≥39%, one-sided α=0.005) is not yet its own row in `Keyword_Taxonomy.md` §1; flagging as a candidate addition rather than forcing it under "single-arm, open-label trial"
- *Endpoints:* progression-free survival (PFS) — primary, Study 116; objective response rate (ORR)/duration of response (DoR) — key secondary in Study 116, primary endpoint in Study 101-09; overall survival (OS) — secondary in Study 116, not powered; lymph node response (LNR) — key secondary in Study 116, not currently in `Keyword_Taxonomy.md` §2, flagging as a candidate addition
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test (PFS and OS, Study 116); unstratified log-rank test (supportive, Study 116); Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified, Study 116); Kaplan-Meier estimation; Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test (ORR and LNR, stratified by randomization factors, Study 116); Exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval (ORR, Study 101-09) — plus, not yet in the taxonomy: an exact one-sided binomial test of the Simon two-stage design's final-stage response-count boundary (≥31/100 responders) used for Study 101-09, flagged as a candidate addition
- *Multiplicity:* fixed order of secondary-endpoint testing in Study 116 (ORR→lymph-node response→OS→CR rate, reordered by Protocol Amendment 4/SAP revision of September 2013 "to control Type I error rate for secondary endpoints") — FDA's statistical review does not name a specific step-down or gatekeeping procedure, so this is tagged loosely to *Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing* rather than asserted as a fully specified alpha-controlled hierarchy
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design (Study 116, two pre-planned interim PFS analyses at ~50% and ~75% of expected events); Data Monitoring Committee (DMC/DSMB) — note: the boundary was a set of fixed nominal significance levels (0.001 at interim 1, 0.005 at interim 2, 0.044 at final) rather than a named alpha-spending function (no Lan-DeMets/O'Brien-Fleming/Hwang-Shih-DeCani/gamma-family functional form appears in the FDA statistical review), so "fixed nominal-alpha group-sequential boundary (no named spending function)" is flagged as a candidate taxonomy addition
- *Missing data/bias:* standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment (Study 116); per-protocol-set and single-site-exclusion sensitivity analyses (Study 116); a conservative "worst-case" sensitivity rule censoring/eventing lost-to-follow-up non-progressors asymmetrically by arm (Study 116) — this asymmetric worst-case censoring rule is not currently in `Keyword_Taxonomy.md` §6, flagged as a candidate addition
- *Regulatory:* FDA's statistical reviewer explicitly declined to accept the sponsor's post-hoc alpha adjustment for OS (significance level of 0.034) "due to lack of a pre-specified alpha spending plan for OS" — closest existing analog is *Reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan*, but this is a rejected post-hoc justification rather than a documented protocol deviation, so a new tag ("FDA rejected sponsor's post-hoc alpha adjustment — no pre-specified spending plan") is flagged as a candidate addition; also notable and not yet a taxonomy row: simultaneous same-day approval of two indications for one molecule under separate NDAs with different evidentiary standards (randomized Phase III vs. single-arm accelerated approval), and accelerated approval (21 CFR 314.510) with postmarketing confirmatory-trial requirements, later resulting in the sponsor's voluntary 2022 withdrawal of the FL/SLL indications

**Trial design & endpoints**

- **CLL indication, Study 116 (GS-US-312-0116) — the pivotal RCT:** Phase III, multicenter (58 sites, US/France/UK/Italy/Germany), randomized 1:1, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in adults with relapsed CLL who required treatment but were considered unable to tolerate cytotoxic chemoimmunotherapy (reduced renal function, myelosuppression from prior cytotoxic therapy, or major coexisting illness); 220 subjects (110/110) received rituximab (8 infusions) plus either idelalisib 150 mg BID or placebo BID until progression/intolerable toxicity
- Randomization stratified by 17p deletion and/or TP53 mutation status (either vs. neither/indeterminate) and IGHV mutation status (unmutated/IGHV3-21 vs. mutated/indeterminate)
- Primary endpoint: IRC-assessed progression-free survival (PFS) per IWCLL criteria, ITT population; secondary endpoints in pre-specified testing order (reordered once, see below): objective response rate (ORR), lymph node response (LNR), overall survival (OS), complete response (CR) rate — CR was never formally analyzed because no CR events occurred
- Sample size: 220 patients (110/arm) planned to detect an improvement in median PFS from 6 to 10.5 months; 119 PFS events required to detect HR=0.57 with >85% power, stratified log-rank test, two-sided α=0.05; 12-month accrual, minimum 12-month follow-up, 10% assumed loss to follow-up
- Interim analysis plan (per Amendment 3, 21 June 2013, and the SAP finalized 7 November 2013): two formal interim efficacy analyses at ~50% (~60th event) and ~75% (~90th event) of the expected 119 PFS events, with pre-specified nominal significance levels of 0.001 (interim 1) and 0.005 (interim 2), and 0.044 reserved for the final analysis if the trial continued to completion
- Statistical methods: PFS and OS analyzed by stratified log-rank test (with Cox proportional-hazards HR/CI) adjusted for the two randomization strata, plus an unstratified log-rank test as a supportive sensitivity analysis; ORR and LNR compared via CMH chi-square tests adjusted for stratification factors; Kaplan-Meier estimation throughout; censoring at last evaluable tumor assessment, with a pre-specified worst-case sensitivity rule for lost-to-follow-up non-progressors (counted as an event if randomized to idelalisib, censored if randomized to placebo)
- FDA's statistical reviewer additionally restricted the OS analysis to Study 116 data alone (excluding the companion extension study GS-US-312-0117), rejecting the sponsor's combined-study OS analysis "due to the concern of confounding effect (i.e., control arm crossing over to take Idela)"
- **FL/SLL indications, Study 101-09 (GS-1101-09) — single-arm accelerated-approval basis, documented for completeness:** Phase II, single-arm, open-label, multicenter (US/Europe) study of idelalisib 150 mg BID monotherapy until progression/intolerable toxicity in 125 patients with indolent B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (72 FL, 26 SLL [FDA-analyzed count; 28 SLL as sponsor-labeled before 2 exclusions], 15 LPL/WM, 10 MZL) refractory to both rituximab and an alkylating agent
- Primary endpoint: IRC-assessed ORR (Cheson 2007 criteria); planned sample size of 100 (ultimately 125 enrolled) using Simon's optimal two-stage design, testing null ORR ≤20% against alternative ORR ≥39% (~40%), >90% power at one-sided α=0.005, with an exact binomial test used at final analysis; stage 1 required a minimum response count among the first patients to justify proceeding to stage 2 (69 additional patients) toward the total planned 100
- The sponsor explicitly designed this as a single-arm, non-inferential (descriptive-only) study: "GS-1101-09 was designed as a nonrandomized study. Therefore, all statistical analyses were descriptive and no formal statistical comparisons were performed" *(FDA Statistical Review, NDA 205858, Executive Summary, p.6)*
- FL/SLL subgroup ORRs (54.2%/57.7% by FDA's tabulation) were consistent with the overall study ORR (54.4% IRC-assessed) but were explicitly flagged by FDA as post-hoc, unpowered subgroup analyses: "There were no pre-planned sample size calculations in order to rule out certain lower percentage of responses in the subgroup disease categories" *(FDA Statistical Review, NDA 205858, Executive Summary, p.5)*

**Other resources**

- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held at the time of original approval: the approval letters state "Your application for Zydelig (idelalisib) was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant public health questions" *(FDA Approval Letter, NDA 205858, "Advisory Committee" section)* — notably, FDA's Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee did later (2022) vote unanimously that future PI3K-inhibitor approvals in hematologic malignancies should be supported by randomized data, a stance informed in part by idelalisib's history.
- Gilead maintains its own clinical-trial data-request process; trial-specific individual patient data availability for Study 116 or Study 101-09 via Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere was not individually confirmed here — state this plainly rather than asserting access.
- Accelerated-approval postmarketing requirements for NDA 205858 included PMR 2180-2 (Phase III confirmatory trial GS-US-313-0124, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, idelalisib + rituximab in previously untreated iNHL) and PMR 2180-1 (dose-optimization trial); the FL/SLL indications were ultimately withdrawn voluntarily by Gilead in 2022 rather than confirmed by these trials — see Federal Register notice above.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 206545 (Study GS-US-312-0116), Executive Summary, p.4]*

> "The applicant submitted Study GS-US-312-0116 results to seek a first-line indication for the treatment of patients who were previously treated for chronic lymphocytic leukemia. The study is designed with progression free survival as the primary endpoint and the secondary endpoints in the order of objective response rate, lymph node response rate and overall survival. Two formal interim analyses were conducted with data cutoff date on 30 August 2013 and 9 October 2013.
>
> Based on study GS-US-312-0116, the results demonstrated statistically significant improvement based on the progression free survival in favor of the Idelalisib + rituximab treatment compared to placebo + rituximab. The p-value for the primary endpoint, progression free survival, based on the first interim analysis results crossed the pre-specified alpha boundary of 0.001 and hence a decision was made to stop the blinded-phase of the study after the first interim."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 206545, §"Interim Analyses," p.11]*

> "Two formal interim analyses of efficacy were planned to assess the evidence of clinical benefit. These interim analyses are conducted after ~50% and ~75% of the expected total number of PFS events (PD or deaths) had occurred. Stopping the study for substantial evidence of Idela benefit will be considered if the PFS is significantly better in the treatment arm (Idela + rituximab) compared to the control arm (placebo + rituximab). The significance level for the first interim analysis will be 0.001 and for the second interim analysis will be 0.005. If a decision is made to stop the trial based on an interim analysis, the database will be cleaned and locked for the subsequent final analysis and the significance level of 0.044 will be used."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 206545, §"Sample Size Calculation," p.11]*

> "A total of 220 patients were planned to be randomized to either of the treatment arms (110 patients to each treatment arm) to achieve an improvement in median PFS from 6 months to 10.5 months due to the addition of Idela to rituximab in the treatment arm. 119 events (definitive CLL progressions) are required to detect a hazard ratio of 0.57 along with achieving a power of >0.85 based on a stratified log-rank test with a 2-sided significance level of 0.05."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 206545, §"Summary of Protocol amendments" and Table 2 "Summary of SAP amendments," pp.6-8]*

> "Amendment 4 (10 September 2013) ... Changed the order of the secondary endpoints, placing overall survival (OS) prior to complete response (CR). Based on the results of other studies in relapsed CLL with IDELA, it was expected that CR would be infrequent in this population and testing for a statistically significant difference might be less informative than OS. ... The final version statistical analysis plan was signed off on 7 November 2013 ... 5 September 2013 [SAP §3.5 and 6.4]: Change the order of secondary endpoint CR rate and OS."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 206545, reviewer's timeline reconstruction of the endpoint-order amendment relative to unblinding, p.8]*

> "From the above dates, it was noted that applicant changed the order of secondary endpoint testing (from ORR, LNR, CR rate and OS to OR, LNR, OS and CR rate) on 9/10/2013 at the amendment #4 of the protocol and on 9/5/2013 for the SAP, after the database cutoff date for the first interim analysis (8/30/2013) but before the potential unblinding date on 9/23/2013 (unblinding the executive team including 1 statistician and 1 medical writer). ... Because the data was unblinded on 9/23/2013 ... any revision of the analysis plan after these days will not be considered as a basis for this statistical review."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 206545, §3.2.3 "Statistical Methodologies," pp.15-17]*

> "PFS between the 2 treatment arms was compared, based on the ITT analysis set using a stratified log-rank test, adjusted for the stratification factors (17p deletion and/or TP53 mutation status and IGHV mutation status) used for randomization. ... ORR: Differences in number and percentage of subjects between the treatment arms in ORR were compared using CMH Chi-square tests after adjusting for stratification factors. ... OS: The OS analysis (i.e., under alpha-protection) was performed using the ITT analysis set ... Differences between treatment arms in OS were assessed in the ITT analysis set using a stratified log-rank test, adjusted for stratification factors."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 206545, reviewer's rejection of the sponsor's OS analysis and post-hoc alpha adjustment, pp.17, 26-27]*

> "FDA does not agree with the inclusion of the Study GS-US-312-117 data for the analysis of OS due to the concern of confounding effect (i.e. control arm crossing over to take Idela) from the combined analysis. So the FDA's OS analysis will be based on Study GS-US-312-116 data alone. ... It is noted that the study was not powered based on the overall survival analysis. ... The applicant submitted a simulation study on 06 April 2014 to justify that the Type I error is adequately controlled for the OS analysis at a significance level of 0.034 ... However, they demonstrated through simulation results that the type-I error rate is not adequately controlled at the pre-specified significance level of 0.05 ... The applicant claims that Type I error may be controlled if the significance level of 0.034 had been used. This statistical reviewer concludes that an adjusted P-value cannot be calculated due to lack of a pre-specified alpha spending plan for OS. Also, in clinical perspective, the agency considers that the results may not be reliable or reproducible due to the small number of deaths."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 206545, §5.3 "Conclusions and Recommendations," p.33]*

> "In summary, based on study GS-US-312-0116, the results demonstrated statistically significant improvement on progression free survival, objective response rate and lymph node response for the Idela treatment arm. The results appear to be robust based on sensitivity analyses including the analyses using different database cutoff dates. ... However, whether or not the overall survival result is significant based on the first or second interim analysis is not clear because the significance level for interim analysis of OS was not pre-specified. In conclusion, this statistical reviewer confirms the applicant's results submitted. Whether the results demonstrate an overall favorable benefit to risk ratio in supporting an indication of the Idela + rituximab treatment in patients with previously treated chronic lymphocytic leukemia will defer to the clinical review team."

*[verbatim, sensitivity-analysis specification, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 206545, §"Sensitivity Analysis for primary endpoint," p.16]*

> "PFS will be further analyzed by censoring data from surviving, non-progressing subjects only at the last time that lack of definitive CLL progression was objectively documented. An additional worst-case sensitivity analysis will be performed in which surviving, non-progressing subjects who are lost to follow-up are categorized as having an event at the time of the last known CLL tumor status assessment if they were in the treatment arm and are categorized as censored at the time of the last known CLL tumor status assessment if they were in the control arm."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 205858 (Study GS-1101-09), Executive Summary, p.6]*

> "GS-1101-09 is an ongoing Phase 2, single-arm, study of Idelalisib in subjects with previously treated Indolent B-Cell Non-Hodgkin Lymphomas (iNHL), refractory to both rituximab and alkylating agent containing therapy. ... GS-1101-09 was designed as a nonrandomized study. Therefore, all statistical analyses were descriptive and no formal statistical comparisons were performed."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 205858, §"Sample Size Determination," p.9]*

> "The planned sample size of 100 patients was calculated assuming null hypothesis, IRC-reviewed ORR of ≤20% and alternative hypothesis of ≥39% (~ 40%). Simon's optimal 2-stage design was [used]... A planned sample size of 100 provides more than 90% power with a 1-sided significance level of < 0.005."

*[verbatim, Protocol 101-09 (Version 9.0, Final, 05 September 2017, as posted on ClinicalTrials.gov), §10.1 "Statistical Basis for Proposed Sample Size," p.99]*

> "The study will test the null hypothesis that the IRC-reviewed ORR is ≤20% against the alternative hypothesis that it is ≥39% (ie, ~40%). Using Simon's optimum 2-stage design {Simon 1989}, a sample size of 100 subjects provides a power of >0.90 to achieve a 1-sided significance level of 0.005 and will provide an ample safety database. Under the Simon's 2-stage design, an ORR of 31% (ie, 31 subjects responding of 100 subjects evaluated) will achieve this significance level. The exact binomial test will be used in the final analyses because of the practical consideration that accrual cannot be limited to exactly 100 subjects and because subjects included in the interim analysis ... as nonresponding may be included in the final analysis as responding if they experience a late response."

**Reverse-engineered SAP** *[inferred]*

- *[inferred]* The precise formal name of the multiplicity-control procedure applied to Study 116's re-ordered secondary endpoints (ORR→LNR→OS→CR) is not stated in the FDA statistical review beyond "updated statistical plan to control Type I error rate for secondary endpoints" — the fixed testing order itself is documented (Table 2, SAP amendment log), but whether it operated as a strict step-down gatekeeping procedure (later endpoints tested only if earlier ones were significant) versus a less formal ordering convention is inferred from the review's silence on any other multiplicity-adjustment method, combined with the review's own uncertainty about whether the OS result was "significant" at all given the missing pre-specified alpha-spending plan.
- *[inferred]* The label's statement that idelalisib + rituximab improved OS is not directly supported by a claim of statistical significance in the label itself — Table 6 of the package insert reports only the PFS hazard ratio and p-value, omitting OS entirely from the formal efficacy table, which is consistent with (and traceable to) FDA's statistical review conclusion that the OS result's significance could not be determined due to the absent pre-specified interim alpha for that endpoint.
- *[inferred]* The Simon two-stage design's stage-1 stopping rule (minimum responders required among the first ~31 patients to justify proceeding toward the full 100, per the standard Simon 1989 optimal design construction) is described generically in Protocol 101-09 §10.4.1, but the exact stage-1 sample size and critical response count are redacted/not reproduced verbatim here because the extracted protocol text did not resolve a specific integer stage-1 boundary value in the pages reviewed; the final analysis boundary of ≥31/100 responders (ORR≥31%) is, however, directly stated in the FDA statistical review and is treated as confirmed rather than inferred.

### 40. netupitant/palonosetron (Akynzeo) — NDA 205718

**Sponsor:** Helsinn Healthcare SA

**Indication approved:** Prevention of acute and delayed nausea and vomiting associated with initial and repeat courses of highly emetogenic cancer chemotherapy (HEC), including but not limited to high-dose cisplatin, and of moderately emetogenic cancer chemotherapy (MEC) — a supportive-care (antiemetic) indication, not a disease-modifying oncology claim

**Approval date:** October 10, 2014

**Pivotal trial:** Two pivotal efficacy trials supported the two chemotherapy-emetogenicity settings: Study NETU-07-07 (HEC, a Phase 2 dose-ranging trial retroactively accepted by FDA as the sole pivotal HEC trial — not registered on ClinicalTrials.gov; conducted 2008 in Russia/Ukraine, before ClinicalTrials.gov registration was standard for non-US-only trials of this type) and Study NETU-08-18 (MEC pivotal Phase III trial), NCT01339260

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (Study NETU-07-07: dose-ranging, palonosetron-alone control, with an exploratory non-blinded aprepitant reference arm; Study NETU-08-18: two-arm, active-controlled against palonosetron alone); Study NETU-07-07 was originally a Phase 2 dose-ranging design later accepted post hoc as pivotal — not currently captured by any single Design term in `Keyword_Taxonomy.md`; flagged as a candidate new term, "Phase 2 trial retroactively accepted as pivotal (post hoc FDA determination)"
- *Endpoints:* complete response (CR) — defined as no emetic episodes and no rescue medication, assessed separately in the acute (0-24h), delayed (25-120h), and overall (0-120h) phases; this specific CR definition is not yet a row in `Keyword_Taxonomy.md` §2 and is flagged as a candidate addition ("Complete response (CR): no emesis + no rescue medication, by CINV phase")
- *Primary analysis:* logistic regression adjusted for a covariate (protocol-specified primary method, Study NETU-07-07), Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by gender/region (FDA-required re-analysis method, both studies)
- *Multiplicity:* Holm-Bonferroni sequentially rejective procedure (three netupitant dose-vs-control pairwise comparisons, Study NETU-07-07)
- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation for missing CR data; site-level exclusion and per-protocol sensitivity analyses following a Good Clinical Practice audit finding at one high-enrolling site
- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan (primary endpoint and analysis method both changed post hoc, sponsor initially resisted the switch), FDA post hoc acceptance of a Phase 2 trial as the sole pivotal trial for an indication, ITT sensitivity analysis reversing statistical significance under multiplicity control

**Trial design & endpoints**

- **Study NETU-07-07 (HEC pivotal):** randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, dose-ranging, multicenter Phase 2 trial (Russia, 29 sites; Ukraine, 15 sites; conducted Feb-Nov 2008) in chemotherapy-naive patients receiving their first cycle of cisplatin-based HEC (cisplatin ≥50 mg/m²); 5 arms (1:1:1:1:1): oral palonosetron 0.5 mg alone, or combined with oral netupitant 100/200/300 mg, plus an exploratory (non-comparative) aprepitant+ondansetron reference arm; randomization used a dynamic gender-adaptive allocation scheme, not simple randomization
- Protocol-specified primary endpoint was CR (no emesis, no rescue medication) in the overall phase (0-120h), analyzed by a gender-covariate-adjusted logistic regression, with the 3 netupitant-dose-vs-palonosetron-alone comparisons controlled by the Holm-Bonferroni procedure at one-sided alpha=0.05; sample size (680 planned, 694 randomized) was powered at 85% for these pairwise comparisons assuming 70% vs. 50% responder rates
- **FDA post hoc reclassification**: after data collection, FDA determined this Phase 2 trial could serve as the sole pivotal trial for the HEC indication, but only after several changes to the pre-specified analysis: (1) primary endpoint changed from CR in the overall phase to CR in the delayed phase (25-120h), (2) primary analysis method changed from logistic regression to a CMH test stratified by gender, (3) analysis population changed from the modified full analysis set (MFAS, treated patients) to intent-to-treat (all randomized patients) as a sensitivity analysis, and (4) a formal hierarchical multiplicity procedure was retroactively imposed across delayed→acute→overall phase CR
- A Good Clinical Practice audit (triggered because FDA required confirmation of the trial's data integrity before it could be used as pivotal) found major protocol violations at one Russian site (site #120, 39 patients), prompting FDA-requested sensitivity analyses excluding or reclassifying that site's patients as treatment failures — in one such sensitivity scenario, the 300 mg netupitant dose's significance versus palonosetron alone reversed on the strength of a single reclassified patient
- Under ITT (all randomized patients, not just treated patients) with the Holm-Bonferroni procedure applied, results for CR in the delayed phase were statistically significant only for netupitant 100 mg (p=0.017); the 200 mg and 300 mg doses were not statistically significant in the ITT sensitivity population — a materially different conclusion from the originally reported (treated-population) results
- **Study NETU-08-18 (MEC pivotal), NCT01339260:** randomized, double-blind, Phase III trial (N=1455) of a single oral dose of netupitant 300 mg/palonosetron 0.5 mg fixed-dose combination vs. oral palonosetron 0.5 mg alone, both with oral dexamethasone, across repeated cycles of moderately emetogenic chemotherapy; primary endpoint CR in the delayed phase (Cycle 1), analyzed by CMH test; result (Cycle 1, ITT): 74.3% (NEPA) vs. 66.6% (palonosetron alone) responders, difference 7.7% (95% CI 3.0-12.3), odds ratio 1.47 (1.17-1.85), p=0.001; consistent results in the per-protocol set and in key secondary endpoints (CR in acute and overall phases)
- **Study PALO-10-01** (non-inferiority bridging study, not itself a netupitant efficacy trial): established that oral palonosetron 0.5 mg is non-inferior to IV palonosetron 0.25 mg for CR in the acute phase following HEC (non-inferiority margin -15%, CMH-adjusted 99% CI), which was necessary to justify using oral palonosetron alone as an acceptable active comparator in Study NETU-07-07
- **Study NETU-10-29** (safety-only, multi-cycle, MEC/HEC; NCT01376297): 3:1 randomization of netupitant/palonosetron vs. aprepitant/palonosetron, powered only to characterize adverse-event rates (no formal efficacy hypothesis test), used as supportive multi-cycle safety data

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Statistical Team Leader Memorandum, p.1]*

> "The four important clinical trials conducted in the clinical program are listed below. The three efficacy studies were evaluated in the primary review... • Study NETU-07-07: Superiority; HEC; single cycle • Study NETU-08-18: Superiority; MEC; single and multiple cycles • Study NETU-10-29: Safety; MEC and HEC; multiple cycles • Study PALO-10-01: Non-inferiority; HEC; single cycle. The primary endpoint in all three efficacy studies was complete response (CR) defined as no emetic episodes and no rescue medication."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, regulatory history, p.2-3]*

> "Another Type A meeting following the no-agreement letters was held on July 15, 2010... During the meeting, more discussion occurred regarding the phase 2 trial (NETU-07-07). The FDA stated that CR in the delayed phase was the primary analysis of interest although overall phase CR was the pre-specified primary endpoint; and a CMH test instead of the pre-specified logistic regression model should be the primary analysis. Moreover, the FDA noted that a multiplicity adjustment plan was only pre-specified for the primary endpoint of overall phase CR, but not for the secondary endpoints of delayed and acute phase CR. Helsinn stated that re-analyses of Study NETU-07-07 data according to the recommendations would be conducted... the FDA pointed out that the full analysis set (FAS)...was used as the primary analysis population, and stated that the intent-to-treat (ITT) population...should be used instead. The preliminary results showed statistical insignificance in treatment comparisons using the ITT population... Helsinn expressed concerns that Study NETU-07-07 might not be considered an adequate study to support the netupitant-palonosetron FDC for HEC."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.1.1 "Study Objective and Study Design," p.7]*

> "Regarding the sample size planning, with a total of 680 subjects – 136 subjects per treatment group, the power of the study was estimated to be 85% for the three pairwise comparisons of netupitant plus palonosetron versus palonosetron alone based on a one-sided test at α=0.05 adjusted for three multiple comparisons using the Holm-Bonferroni method."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.1.2 "Efficacy Endpoints & Analyses," p.8-9]*

> "For each hypothesis test, the three comparisons were made using one-sided p-values according to the Holm-Bonferroni method. That is, in order to claim a significant difference, the smallest of the three p-values must not exceed 0.05/3. If this is achieved, the second smallest p-value must not exceed 0.05/2 in order to be significant, and if this is also achieved, the significance threshold for the third p-value is 0.05. This sequential procedure stops, if the respective threshold is exceeded."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.4 "Statistical Reviewer's Findings and Comments," Item 1, p.23]*

> "On March 8th of 2010, the FDA Division of Gastroenterology Products, after discussion with the Office of Medical Policy, commented in their advice/information letter that this study would be acceptable to support the NDA for the proposed fixed dose combination capsule for the prevention of acute and delayed CINV in the HEC setting provided that 'FDA would be able, after review of the trial data, to confirm the positive study outcome.' For this reason, besides the routine quality assurance (QA) auditing process conducted during the study at 8 sites, an additional in-depth QA audit plan was implemented after the study had been completed... One site in Russia (site #120) presented multiple major audit findings, ranging from failure to meet eligibility criteria and administration of prohibited medications to inconsistencies between source data and Case Report Forms (CRFs)."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.4, Item 2 "ITT Results for Study NETU-07-07," p.24]*

> "As noted...for the purpose of considering Study NETU-07-07 as the sole pivotal trial for CINV-HEC indication, the FDA requested the sponsor to perform some additional analyses, including the sensitivity analysis on the Intent to Treat (ITT) population, which was defined as all randomized patients. The sponsor's ITT analysis results are presented in Table 15. There was only 17 patients excluded from the FAS population; however, it would alter the final conclusions. The ITT results were all insignificant for all doses and all phases when the Holm-Bonferroni multiplicity method was implemented."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.3.2 (Study PALO-10-01), reviewer's note, p.18]*

> "The sponsor proposed non-inferiority margin -15% was agreed upon by the FDA prior to the trial initiation. Note that this margin was derived based on the available history information and has also been used in the pivotal CINV studies for other 5-HT3 antagonists. In particular, Sancuso granisetron transdermal patch sole pivotal efficacy study used a non-inferiority margin of -15% to support approval."

This is an unusually well-documented example of a trial's pivotal status itself being negotiated after the fact: NETU-07-07 was designed and executed as an ordinary Phase 2 dose-ranging study with a different primary endpoint, a different primary analysis method, and no multiplicity control on what later became its key secondary endpoints — FDA agreed to accept it as the sole pivotal HEC trial only conditionally, then required an endpoint switch, an analysis-method switch, a population switch (to ITT, which reversed significance for two of the three doses), and a for-cause GCP audit before finalizing that acceptance — with the sponsor's own contemporaneous statements on record expressing doubt that the trial would hold up as pivotal evidence.

### 41. blinatumomab (Blincyto) — BLA 125557

**Sponsor:** Amgen, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adults with Philadelphia chromosome-negative relapsed or refractory B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL); approved under accelerated approval (21 CFR 601 Subpart E), with continued approval contingent on verification of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial

**Approval date:** December 3, 2014

**Pivotal trial:** Study MT103-211 ("Study '211"), NCT01466179

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label, multicenter Phase II trial; Simon's 2-stage design with a third extension/expansion stage for final estimation (three-stage go/no-go structure: stages 1-2 for interim futility decisions, stage 3 to reach the target N for the final point estimate)
- *Endpoints:* CR/CRh* rate within the first 2 cycles of treatment (complete remission or complete remission with partial hematological recovery, bone-marrow-blast-based composite response endpoint used as an accelerated-approval surrogate); minimal residual disease (MRD) response rate (secondary); duration of response/relapse-free survival, event-free survival, overall survival, allogeneic HSCT rate (secondary, descriptive, non-confirmatory)
- *Primary analysis:* exact two-sided 95% binomial confidence interval (analogous to the Clopper-Pearson/exact-CI approach used elsewhere in this census); weighted historical-control benchmarking — sponsor-conducted retrospective pooled cohort (Study 20120310) re-weighted by age x prior-therapy-line strata to Study '211's own stratum distribution, used to justify the pre-specified 30% efficacy threshold
- *Multiplicity:* unadjusted secondary/supportive testing (single formal primary endpoint) — only the CR/CRh* rate was formally powered/tested; all other endpoints, including CRh* itself as a distinct construct, were treated as descriptive/supportive by FDA
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* two-stage (plus extension) go/no-go interim design with a pre-specified futility threshold (continuation past stage 2 required rejecting a 20% CR/CRh* futility rate); Data Monitoring Committee (DMC/DSMB) reviewed interim data, per FDA's filing checklist
- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation for missing binary efficacy data (patients with no response assessment in the first 2 cycles, 9.7% of the analysis set, counted as non-responders for the primary endpoint); reviewer-documented redefinition of a protocol-specified endpoint — FDA's Statistical Review states the protocol defined "duration of response" as time-to-hematological-relapse (implicitly censoring death), but the Agency instead analyzed it as relapse-free survival, counting death from any cause as an event
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval based on a single-arm surrogate response-rate endpoint (no prior taxonomy entry for the accelerated-approval/single-arm-response-rate regulatory pathway itself, as distinct from the single-arm design keyword already in the Design category); Breakthrough Therapy designation (granted June 30, 2014); confirmatory trial required post-approval (Phase 3 randomized, open-label, active-controlled Study 00103311 vs. standard of care, overall survival primary endpoint)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study MT103-211 was an open-label, single-arm, multicenter Phase 2 trial of blinatumomab monotherapy in adults with Philadelphia chromosome-negative relapsed/refractory B-precursor ALL, run as a "core study" (efficacy/safety) plus a separate cohort evaluating CNS symptoms
- Eligibility: age ≥18 years, Ph-negative B-precursor ALL relapsed/refractory per specific criteria (first relapse ≤12 months, relapsed/refractory after first salvage, or relapsed within 12 months of allogeneic HSCT), ≥10% bone marrow blasts, ECOG ≤2; excluded Ph-positive ALL, Burkitt leukemia, active/history of clinically relevant CNS pathology, recent autologous/allogeneic HSCT, active GvHD, and prior blinatumomab exposure
- Dosing: continuous IV infusion, step-dose regimen of 9 mcg/day (week 1) then 28 mcg/day (weeks 2-4) of cycle 1 and 28 mcg/day for subsequent cycles, 4 weeks on/2 weeks off per 42-day cycle; per FDA's Medical Review, this step-dose schedule (rather than a flat starting dose) was itself chosen for safety reasons, based on cytokine-release-syndrome dose-limiting toxicities observed at higher flat/BSA-based starting doses in the earlier dose-finding studies (Protocols 205/206) and supporting PK/PD analyses
- Primary endpoint: proportion of patients achieving CR or CRh* within the first 2 treatment cycles (12 weeks), assessed by central-laboratory bone marrow review — CR = ≤5% blasts, no disease evidence, full peripheral count recovery (platelets >100,000/uL, ANC >1,000/uL); CRh* = same blast/disease criteria with only partial count recovery (platelets >50,000/uL, ANC >500/uL)
- Secondary endpoints: CR rate alone, CRh* rate alone, partial remission rate, time to hematological relapse/duration of response, relapse-free survival, event-free survival, overall survival, proportion undergoing allogeneic HSCT during remission, 100-day post-HSCT mortality, overall adverse-event incidence/severity
- Sample size: minimum 140 patients for >90% power to reject the null hypothesis (first-2-cycle CR/CRh* rate = 30%) at 1-sided 2.5% type I error; enrollment extended up to 190 patients to ensure at least 50 patients treated with the to-be-marketed Commercial Material (CTM5) for a CTM4-vs-CTM5 comparability check; 189 patients enrolled in the core study for the primary efficacy assessment, with 4 later excluded by FDA as not meeting the intended relapsed/refractory population definition, leaving an FDA primary analysis set of 185
- Interim design: 3-stage structure — stages 1 and 2 supported a go/no-go continuation decision (the trial continued past stage 2 after confirming at least 19/61 responders, exceeding a pre-specified 20% futility threshold), and stage 3 was an extension to reach the target sample size for the final CR/CRh* rate estimate
- Primary analysis: exact two-sided 95% confidence intervals were calculated for the combined CR/CRh* rate and separately for CR and CRh* rates; patients with no response assessment in the first 2 cycles were counted as non-responders; no formal multiplicity adjustment across secondary endpoints, since the trial was sized only for the single primary endpoint and FDA's review explicitly states secondary endpoints "should not be considered as confirmatory for treatment efficacy"
- Supportive analyses submitted to justify the pre-specified 30% threshold: a sponsor-conducted retrospective pooled historical-control study (Study 20120310, approximately 1,139 patients from EU/US sites, 1990-2014) yielding a stratum-weighted historical CR rate of 24% (95% CI 20%-27%), reweighted across six age x prior-therapy-line strata to match Study '211's own stratum distribution; and a separate model-based meta-analysis (Studies 118427/119834, mixed-effects models from 24 published studies, approximately 4,058 patients) projecting a comparative CR rate of 12-13% for existing salvage therapies vs. 32-33% for blinatumomab

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2014/125557Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (original, 2014) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2014/125557lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/125557Orig1s000StatR.pdf
