- FDA Summary Review (Signatory Authority Review) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/125557Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01466179 (checked via the v2 API `studies/NCT01466179` endpoint: no documentSection field is present, i.e. no sponsor protocol/SAP PDF is posted for this trial)
- Pivotal publication: Topp MS, Gokbuget N, Stein AS, et al. "Safety and activity of blinatumomab for adult patients with relapsed or refractory B-precursor acute lymphoblastic leukaemia: a multicentre, single-arm, phase 2 study." *Lancet Oncol.* 2015;16(1):57-66. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(14)71170-2>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25524800/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Safety%20and%20activity%20of%20blinatumomab%20for%20adult%20patients%20with%20relapsed%20or%20refractory%20B-precursor%20acute%20lymphoblastic%20leukaemia%3A%20a%20multicentre%2C%20single-arm%2C%20phase%202%20study)

**Other resources**

- Amgen participates generally in the Vivli data-sharing platform (vivli.org); trial-specific IPD availability for Study MT103-211 was not individually confirmed in this pass and should be checked on Vivli directly before assuming access.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held; FDA's Summary Review states the application "did not require discussion at an ODAC meeting due to the fact that trial results were superior to other products for a similar disease indication and the risk/benefit was thought to be favorable."
- Post-marketing requirement: complete and submit the final study report from Study 00103311, a Phase 3 randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial of blinatumomab vs. standard of care in the same population, with overall survival as the primary endpoint, to verify clinical benefit under the accelerated-approval/Subpart H requirement (this trial later became publicly known as TOWER, NCT02013167).
- A REMS with a communication plan was required at approval given the boxed-warning risks of cytokine release syndrome and neurological toxicities/medication errors, per the OSE/DRISK review summarized in the Summary Review.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, cover-page "Keywords" field, p.1]*

> "Keywords: ALL, CR/CRh* rate, historical controls, Simon's 2-stage design with extension"

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Section 1 "Executive Summary," p.5]*

> "The main study MT103-211 supporting this application is a Phase 2, fixed-dose, open-label, single-arm trial that included a core study to assess the treatment efficacy and safety, and an additional evaluation cohort to evaluate central nervous system symptoms. A total of 185 eligible patients were treated in the core study of trial MT103-211... The primary endpoint for Study MT103-211 was the proportion of patients who achieved CR or CRh* within the first 2 cycles of treatment with blinatumomab. Study MT103-211 met its primary objective to demonstrate that the CR/CRh* rate within 2 cycles of treatment with blinatumomab exceeded the pre-specified efficacy threshold of 30%."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Section 3.2.2 "Statistical Methodologies," p.11]*

> "The primary efficacy endpoint was the CR and CRh* rate within the first 2 cycles of treatment with blinatumomab. The study continued to stage 3 for its full enrollment after rejecting the 20% futility threshold with at least 19 responders out of 61 patients at the end of stage 2. The primary analysis of the primary endpoint was planned at the end of stage 3, testing against 30% as the threshold for the demonstration of treatment efficacy. Exact two-sided 95% confidence intervals were calculate for the CR+CRh* rate and separately for CR and CR* rates. Patients with missing information for response assessment within the first two cycles of treatment were included in the analysis of the primary efficacy endpoint as non-responders. The study planned to enroll between 140 and 190 patients for treatment efficacy evaluation. A minimum of 140 patients was required to provide >90% power to reject the null hypothesis: (first 2-cycle CR/CRh* rate) = 30% at 1-sided 2.5% type I error."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, "Reviewer Comments" following Section 3.2.2, p.11-12 — documents FDA's own redefinition of a protocol-specified secondary endpoint]*

> "The protocol defined duration of response to be the same as time to hematological relapse. However, the Agency considers progression of disease (relapse) or death due to any cause as events for the calculation of response duration. Duration of response, as considered by the Agency, is consistent with relapse-free survival instead. Study MT103-211 was a single-arm study sized only based on the primary endpoint. Secondary endpoints should not be considered as confirmatory for treatment efficacy."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Section 3.2.5 "Evaluation of Review Issues," Question 2, p.20-21 — the historical-control benchmarking used to support the 30% threshold]*

> "Table 9 below shows the strata-specific and combined weighted estimate of CRsg from Study 20120310... The stratum-specific estimates were pooled into a combined estimate with each stratum weighted to the percentage of patients observed in that stratum from Study MT103-211... The estimated overall CR rate as reported is 24% (95% confidence interval: 20% to 27%)."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Section 3.2.5, Reviewer comments, p.23-24 — FDA's regulatory reasoning on CRh* as a surrogate]*

> "This question arises because the accelerated approval regulations require that the approval be based on a surrogate reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit. The Agency has accepted durable CR as such a surrogate, but has not formally adopted a position on the use of CRh* as a surrogate reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit... However, no definite conclusion could be made from this comparison, because it was not a randomized comparison, and neither the number of responders nor the number of events in responders was sufficient to demonstrate meaningful differences between CR and CRh* responders."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistics Filing Checklist (appended to the Statistical Review), p.2 — documents the pre-specified 30% threshold's own lack of formal justification]*

> "As a single-arm trial, the pivotal study is sized to rule out a complete remission rate of 30%. An external DSMB reviewed the interim analyses. DSMB meeting minutes are included in an appendix of the study report. The threshold of 30% was not formally justified. Study 20120310 provided a weighted estimate of 24% based on a historical database."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, Section 7 "Clinical/Statistical-Efficacy," p.2, clinical reviewer's recommendation]*

> "This reviewer recommends approval of blinatumomab under 21 CFR 601 Subpart E for the treatment of patients with Philadelphia chromosome negative relapsed or refractory precursor B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia. Approval is supported by the results of Protocol 211 in which 32% (95% CI, 26% - 40%) of patients in the intended population achieved complete remission (CR) with 2 cycles of treatment with single-agent blinatumomab, and the response was durable (median 6.7 months; range, <0.1 - 16.5 months)... The efficacy of blinatumomab in comparison to available therapy remains to be confirmed in a postmarketing study."

*[verbatim, FDA Medical Review (redacted), p.6 — on the safety rationale for the step-dose regimen used in the pivotal trial]*

> "The flat dose-schedule used in the pivotal trial, the 9→28 ug/day step-dose by continuous infusion for 28 days of a 42-day cycle, was based on safety in the BSA-based protocols and results of pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) analyses."

No sponsor-authored protocol or SAP document for Study MT103-211 is publicly posted (ClinicalTrials.gov's documentSection is absent for NCT01466179 as of this check), so the passages above — drawn entirely from FDA's own Statistical Review, Summary Review, and Medical Review — are the fullest public account of the analysis actually executed; no further "Reverse-engineered SAP" subsection is needed given how much of the sponsor's original design (Simon's 2-stage-with-extension structure, the 30% null threshold, the exact-CI methodology, and the historical-control weighting scheme) is already documented verbatim by the reviewer.

### 42. nivolumab (Opdivo) — BLA 125554

**Sponsor:** Bristol-Myers Squibb Company

**Indication approved:** Unresectable or metastatic melanoma and disease progression following ipilimumab and, if BRAF V600 mutation positive, a BRAF inhibitor; per the approval letter and label, "This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and durability of response. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in confirmatory trials."

**Approval date:** December 22, 2014 (initial accelerated approval; original BLA submitted July 30, 2014)

**Pivotal trial:** CheckMate 037 (BMS protocol CA209-037/CA209037), NCT01721746 — an ongoing randomized Phase 3 trial whose co-primary comparative endpoints (ORR, OS) had not matured; the accelerated approval itself rested on a non-comparative interim analysis of the nivolumab arm only

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled (existing taxonomy term; CheckMate 037/CA209037, 2:1 randomization, dacarbazine or carboplatin/paclitaxel per investigator's choice); flagged new term — "non-comparative interim subset analysis within an ongoing randomized Phase 3 trial," i.e., a protocol amendment converted one co-primary endpoint (ORR) from a planned comparative test into a single-arm, descriptive interim analysis restricted to the experimental arm specifically to support an accelerated-approval filing while the trial's true comparative endpoints (OS, PFS) continued to accrue under the original randomized design — not captured by the existing "single-arm, open-label trial" term, which describes a trial designed as single-arm from the outset rather than a randomized trial's arm analyzed non-comparatively at an interim look
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR) — confirmed, IRRC-assessed per RECIST v1.1, co-primary endpoint of the RCT but the sole, non-comparative basis for accelerated approval; overall survival (OS) — co-primary, only described descriptively at this submission, comparative analysis deferred; progression-free survival (PFS) — key secondary, IRRC-assessed, gated behind a positive final OS result; objective response rate (ORR) / duration of response (DoR) / disease control rate (DCR) (existing taxonomy term covers DOR and time-to-response here as well)
- *Primary analysis:* exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval (existing term; used for the ORR point estimate), Kaplan-Meier estimation (DOR, TTR, and descriptive OS/PFS), Cox proportional-hazards model (descriptive HR for OS/PFS, single covariate = treatment arm); flagged new term — Newcomb method (used for unweighted between-arm ORR-difference confidence intervals in subgroup/forest-plot analyses, not currently in the taxonomy alongside Miettinen-Nurminen)
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (existing term) governs the trial's full, still-pending comparative hierarchy (ORR→OS→PFS with OS as gatekeeper for PFS); notably, no formal hypothesis test of ORR was conducted at all for this accelerated-approval interim submission — the FDA statistical reviewer states explicitly "There was no formal hypothesis test of ORR planned for this interim report"
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design, Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function, O'Brien-Fleming boundary (existing terms; apply to the RCT's still-pending interim/final OS analyses, not to the ORR-based accelerated-approval submission itself)
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval under 21 CFR 601 Subpart E (biologics equivalent of NDA Subpart H); postmarketing requirement (PMR 2838-1) for a randomized superiority trial to verify clinical benefit; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held; flagged new candidate regulatory term — "accelerated approval based on a non-comparative subset analysis embedded in an ongoing pivotal RCT" (distinct from the existing "single-arm, open-label trial" tag, which applies to trials single-arm by design)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- CheckMate 037/CA209037: randomized (2:1), open-label, active-controlled, multicenter (90 sites), multinational (14 countries) Phase 3 trial in patients ≥18 years with histologically confirmed unresectable (Stage III) or metastatic (Stage IV) melanoma with objective evidence of progression during or after ≥1 (BRAF wild-type) or ≥2 (BRAF V600 mutation-positive) prior anti-CTLA-4-containing regimens; key exclusions were active/suspected autoimmune disease, need for systemic immunosuppression or corticosteroids >10 mg/day prednisone-equivalent, ocular melanoma, active brain/leptomeningeal metastasis, unknown BRAF status, and any prior anti-PD-1/PD-L1/PD-L2 therapy
- Randomization stratified by PD-L1 expression status, BRAF V600 mutation status (wild-type vs. mutation-positive), and best response to prior ipilimumab (complete/partial response or stable disease vs. progressive disease)
- Arms: nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV over 60 minutes every 2 weeks vs. investigator's choice of dacarbazine 1000 mg/m2 IV every 3 weeks or carboplatin AUC 6 + paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 IV every 3 weeks, each continued until progression or unacceptable toxicity; 405 of 631 enrolled patients were randomized (272 nivolumab : 133 investigator's choice)
- Co-primary endpoints (full RCT, as originally designed): ORR (IRRC-assessed, RECIST v1.1) in the nivolumab vs. investigator's-choice arms, and OS (time from randomization to death from any cause); key secondary endpoint: PFS (IRRC-assessed, RECIST v1.1, or death); ORR further characterized by duration of response (DOR) and time to response (TTR)
- Original sample size: approximately 390 randomized (2:1) for adequately powered co-primary comparative analyses of ORR and OS at overall two-sided alpha 0.05, split 0.001 (ORR) / 0.049 (OS); OS final analysis powered (90%) to detect HR 0.65 (median OS 8 vs. 12.3 months) at 260 deaths, with one planned interim OS analysis at 169 deaths (65% of target events), boundaries per a Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function approximating O'Brien-Fleming (significance level 0.0105 at interim, 0.0457 at final, two-sided); PFS to be analyzed only at the time of final OS analysis, gated behind a positive OS result (OS as formal gatekeeper for PFS)
- Protocol Amendment 9 (24-Oct-2013) restructured the timing of analyses to allow an earlier, still-comparative ORR analysis while preserving power for the OS comparison; Protocol Amendment 10 (28-Mar-2014) converted the ORR analysis from a between-arm comparative test into a single-arm, non-comparative, descriptive estimation restricted to nivolumab-treated patients only — specifically to support an accelerated-approval submission — and the FDA Summary Review documents that the OS comparison's allocated significance level was reported as increasing from 2.5% to 4.9% under this amendment (the Statistical Review separately reports the finalized two-sided alpha split as 0.1%/4.9% for ORR/OS; both figures come directly from FDA review text and are presented here as documented rather than fully reconciled)
- Accelerated-approval interim analysis population ("Treated Subjects among ORR population"): the first 120 nivolumab-treated, randomized patients (of 272 total randomized to nivolumab) with at least 6 months of follow-up (or earlier progression/death), out of a broader 182-patient "ORR population" (122 nivolumab, 60 investigator's choice) with at least 6 months' follow-up across both arms; database lock for this interim analysis was April 30, 2014, with the last patient's last ORR-analysis visit on March 10, 2014
- Primary analysis method executed: point estimate of confirmed IRRC-assessed ORR plus a two-sided 95% exact Clopper-Pearson confidence interval; the planned sample size of 120 nivolumab-treated patients was chosen so that, assuming a true ORR of 25-30%, the lower bound of the exact 95% CI would exclude an ORR of 15% or less; DOR and TTR estimated by the Kaplan-Meier method; sensitivity analyses included investigator-assessed ORR (same population) and an IRRC/investigator concordance check; subgroup ORR differences (BRAF status, PD-L1 status, prior ipilimumab benefit, M-stage, age, sex, race, region, ECOG PS, brain metastasis history, smoking status, baseline LDH, AJCC stage) used unweighted differences with 95% CIs by the Newcomb method
- OS and PFS were reported only descriptively at this interim submission (Kaplan-Meier medians/CIs, Cox proportional-hazards HR with treatment arm as sole covariate) — no formal hypothesis test of either endpoint was performed; the FDA statistical reviewer states plainly that "the formal analysis of OS will be included in a separate CSR to be submitted later"
- FDA's March 27, 2013 Advice/Information Request letter shaped the SAP as executed, directing BMS to: require that the primary ORR analysis be IRRC-based with confirmation of response durability at ≥4 weeks; require investigator (not sponsor) selection of the comparator chemotherapy regimen; systematically collect BRAF V600 mutation testing method/result, preferably via central laboratory; and ensure the SAP specified censoring rules and sensitivity analyses for patients with symptomatic deterioration in the absence of objectively documented radiographic progression
- FDA's January 16, 2014 Advice/Information Request letter, responding to BMS's proposal to "decouple" the co-primary ORR/OS analysis timing, accepted an earlier ORR analysis but rejected BMS's proposed change to the ORR/OS alpha-allocation ratio (retained at two-sided 0.001/0.049 as in the original SAP), affirmed that IRRC-determined ORR would be the primary efficacy endpoint for regulatory purposes, and rejected a proposal to count unconfirmed tumor responses toward ORR

**Other resources**

- Bristol-Myers Squibb participates in the Vivli data-sharing platform (vivli.org); trial-specific IPD availability for CheckMate 037 (NCT01721746) was not individually confirmed in this pass and should be checked directly on Vivli before assuming access.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held; the Summary Review states this BLA "was not referred to the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee because this biologic is not the first in its class, the clinical study design was acceptable, and the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues" — notably, pembrolizumab (Keytruda, BLA 125514) had already received accelerated approval for the same melanoma indication on September 4, 2014, about 3.5 months before nivolumab's approval, so nivolumab was the second (not first) PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor to reach the US market, despite being developed on a similar timeline.
- Postmarketing requirement PMR 2838-1 (per the approval letter, subject to 21 CFR 601.70 reporting): "Conduct and submit the results of a multicenter, randomized trial or trials establishing the superiority of nivolumab over standard therapy in adult patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma who are refractory to ipilimumab or who have not been previously treated with ipilimumab," original final report submission date December 31, 2016 — substantially addressed by the mature comparative OS/PFS analysis of this same CheckMate 037 trial (and by the independent CheckMate 066 trial in ipilimumab-naive patients).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Executive Summary, p.3]*

> "The study CA 209037 was a randomized, open-label, Phase 3, multicenter, global study designed to evaluate nivolumab monotherapy (3 mg/kg every two weeks [Q2W]) vs. investigator's choice (dacarbazine or carboplatin and paclitaxel) with overall response rate (ORR) and overall survival (OS) as the co-primary endpoints. The key secondary endpoint was progression free survival. Although the study was a randomized study with two treatment arms, in this submission of interim results, a non-comparative analysis of only one of the co-primary endpoints of the study, overall response rate, was performed. The efficacy analysis population for the primary endpoint of response rate was restricted to a total of 120 subjects who were randomized and received at least one dose of the study drug, nivolumab, and had at least 6 months of follow-up... The primary analysis was to provide the point estimates of ORR and the corresponding two-sided 95% exact confidence interval using Clopper-Pearson method."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.2 "Statistical Methodologies," p.14]*

> "There was no formal hypothesis test of ORR planned for this interim report of Study CA209037 and the formal analysis of OS will be included in a separate CSR to be submitted later... The planned analysis of ORR was originally designed to compare the nivolumab treatment to the investigator's choice arm; however, due to protocol amendment-10, the study design was modified to allow non-comparative estimation of ORR on nivolumab arm."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Table 5 "Protocol Amendments," p.13, row for Amendment 10]*

> "Revised Protocol 4 (Amendment-10), 28-Mar-2014: Study design is modified to allow non comparative estimation of ORR on nivolumab arm. OS co-primary endpoint comparison significance level increased from 2.5% to 4.9%."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, "Sample Size Calculations," p.11]*

> "A total of approximately 390 subjects were planned to be randomized to the two treatment arms in a 2:1 ratio to account for the co-primary efficacy endpoints of ORR and OS with an alpha allocation of 0.1% and 4.9%, respectively... A sample size of 120 patients was chosen such that the lower-limit of the exact 95% confidence interval excludes a response rate of 15% or less."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, "Multiplicity adjustment," p.14]*

> "The efficacy analysis for the key secondary endpoint of PFS will conducted only at the time of final OS analysis. The co-primary endpoint OS analysis will serve as the gatekeeper for the PFS analyses, i.e., the primary efficacy hypothesis of OS must be rejected at the 2-sided 0.049 significance level before the efficacy hypotheses for the secondary efficacy endpoints of PFS can be evaluated."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, "Key Amendments to Protocol CA209037," pp.10-11]*

> "In a February 13, 2014, submission, BMS proposed to modify the design of Study CA209037 to incorporate a new analysis of ORR; in this new analysis, you propose to calculate the IRRC-assessed ORR in the first 120 patients treated with nivolumab to seek accelerated approval. The timing of this analysis will be based on a minimum of 6 months follow-up for all patients and the supporting assumptions are that a minimum of 22 responses out of 120 treated subjects (≥ 18% ORR) would need to be observed for the 99% confidence interval to rule out an ORR <10% based on the lower bound of the 99% confidence interval."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, regulatory history, pp.5-6, quoting FDA's March 27, 2013 and January 16, 2014 Advice/Information Request letters to BMS]*

> "March 27, 2013: FDA issued an Advice/Information Request letter, advising BMS to: Revise protocol to require that primary analysis of ORR be based on independent review and require confirmation of durability for ≥ 4 weeks; Revise the protocol to require that the investigator select the choice of chemotherapy that will be administered if patient is randomized to the chemotherapy arm; Systematically collect information on BRAF V600 mutation test method and result: if possible, determine BRAF mutation status at a central laboratory; Ensure that the statistical analytical plan includes censoring rules and sensitivity analyses for patients who experience symptomatic deterioration in the absence of objective radiographic evidence of disease progression... January 16, 2014: FDA issued an Advice/Information Request letter regarding the proposed modification to the trial to 'decouple' the analysis of the co-primary endpoints. FDA stated that the proposal to perform an earlier analysis of ORR was acceptable, however FDA disagreed with the proposed change in alpha allocation to the co-primary endpoints and recommended that the two-sided, alpha allocation ratio remains 0.01 for ORR and 0.04 for OS, respectively, as in the original statistical analysis plan; ORR based on IRC-determined responses will be considered the primary efficacy endpoint to support a regulatory action; and the proposal to include unconfirmed tumor responses as objective responses in the determination of ORR was not acceptable."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, Division Director's Regulatory Action, p.15]*

> "Regulatory Action: I recommend accelerated approval under the provisions of 21 CFR 601 Subpart E... Based on the results of Study 209037, nivolumab demonstrated an overall response rate of 32% which is durable for more than 6 months in approximately one-third of responding patients. This is approximately two-fold higher than the reported response rates for approved or off-label chemotherapeutic agents and the duration of responses are substantially longer with nivolumab... The observed response rate of 32%, combined with the durability of the responses, is reasonably likely to predicted prolongation in progression-free survival of a clinically important magnitude and potentially an improvement in overall survival."

*[verbatim, FDA Approval Letter, "Accelerated Approval Requirements" / postmarketing requirement 2838-1, p.3-4]*

> "Products approved under the accelerated approval regulations, 21 CFR 601.41, require further adequate and well-controlled studies/clinical trials to verify and describe clinical benefit... 2838-1: Conduct and submit the results of a multicenter, randomized trial or trials establishing the superiority of nivolumab over standard therapy in adult patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma who are refractory to ipilimumab or who have not been previously treated with ipilimumab. Final Report Submission: December 31, 2016."

*[verbatim, approved Package Insert, §1 Indications and Usage]*

> "OPDIVO is a human programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1) blocking antibody indicated for the treatment of patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma and disease progression following ipilimumab and, if BRAF V600 mutation positive, a BRAF inhibitor. This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and durability of response. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in the confirmatory trials."

*[verbatim, approved Package Insert, §14 Clinical Studies]*

> "Efficacy was evaluated in a single-arm, non-comparative, planned interim analysis of the first 120 patients who received OPDIVO in Trial 1 and in whom the minimum duration of follow up was 6 months. The major efficacy outcome measures in this population were confirmed objective response rate (ORR) as measured by blinded independent central review using Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST 1.1) and duration of response... The ORR was 32% (95% confidence interval: 23, 41), consisting of 4 complete responses and 34 partial responses in OPDIVO-treated patients. Of 38 patients with responses, 33 patients (87%) had ongoing responses with durations ranging from 2.6+ to 10+ months, which included 13 patients with ongoing responses of 6 months or longer."

This is a clean documented case of "how the SAP held up under FDA review": the sponsor twice sought to relax the pre-specified statistical plan under regulatory time pressure (proposing to reallocate co-primary alpha, and to count unconfirmed responses as objective responses), and FDA's January 16, 2014 letter rejected both changes while accepting the underlying idea of an earlier, non-comparative ORR look — meaning the accelerated approval was granted on a purely descriptive point estimate and exact confidence interval (no hypothesis test at all), with the trial's actual pre-specified comparative hypothesis tests (ORR vs. chemotherapy, OS, PFS) left completely unexecuted at the time of approval and deferred to the mature analysis mandated by PMR 2838-1.

### 43. palbociclib (Ibrance) — NDA 207103

**Sponsor:** Pfizer Inc.

**Indication approved:** In combination with letrozole, for the treatment of postmenopausal women with estrogen receptor (ER)-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative advanced breast cancer as initial endocrine-based therapy for their metastatic disease — approved under accelerated approval based on progression-free survival (PFS); continued approval contingent on verification of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial

**Approval date:** February 3, 2015

**Pivotal trial:** PALOMA-1/TRIO-18 (Study A5481003), NCT00721409

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled, Phase II trial used as the sole pivotal basis for accelerated approval (not Phase III) — a status this census has not previously tagged; sequential two-cohort design in which Part 1 (an all-comers population, n=66) was followed by Part 2 (a biomarker-enriched population selected for CCND1 amplification and/or CDKN2A/p16 loss, n=99), with the two parts later pooled into a single primary analysis population by a mid-conduct SAP amendment (no existing Keyword_Taxonomy.md row captures this sequential-cohort-then-pool structure; the closest term, "Biomarker-selected/enriched population," describes an upfront-restricted enrollment, not a two-part sequential design recombined post hoc — new term recommended, e.g. "Sequential two-cohort design (all-comers cohort + later biomarker-enriched cohort, pooled by SAP amendment)")
- *Endpoints:* investigator-assessed PFS (primary), overall survival and objective response rate (labeled "key secondary" by the sponsor, though FDA noted no alpha was formally allocated to OS), BICR-assessed PFS (FDA-mandated 100% re-review, supportive)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test (strata: disease site, time to recurrence, study part), Kaplan-Meier estimation, Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test (ORR)
- *Multiplicity:* no formal Type I error control was ultimately applied to the primary PFS analysis — FDA's Statistical Review explicitly designates all reported p-values "nominal" and states "from a statistical point of view, inference cannot be drawn," because of repeated data-driven (not merely pre-specified) changes to the SAP during the trial (existing Multiplicity-category terms describe formal hierarchical/adjustment procedures; a reviewer's explicit statement that no p-value in the trial is inferential due to data-driven design changes is a distinct concept — new term recommended)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* originally a single futility-only interim look; Protocol/SAP Amendment 5 removed the futility look and added "two, and possibly three" efficacy interim looks; Amendment 7 then moved the final analysis trigger from 114 to 95 PFS events — FDA's review states that, given these changes, "it makes little sense to discuss the interim analyses for the primary analysis" (no alpha-spending function is identified anywhere in the review)
- *Missing data/bias:* ascertainment bias assessment (EDR/LDR) comparing investigator- vs. BICR-assessed PFS, including an FDA-run randomization-test analysis of the discordance rates; standard right-censoring
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval granted on PFS from a randomized, controlled Phase II trial rather than a Phase III trial or a single-arm surrogate-response trial (the pattern the census's existing "Single-arm, open-label trial" tag describes) (no existing Regulatory-category term captures an accelerated approval anchored to a randomized, non-Phase-III pivotal trial — new term recommended); FDA-mandated 100% BICR re-review of an open-label trial's primary endpoint; PMR requiring PALOMA-2 (Phase III, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled confirmatory trial, NCT01740427) PFS/OS data; PMC specifically requiring further study of the p16/CCND1 biomarker's prognostic/predictive significance in PALOMA-2

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study A5481003 (PALOMA-1/TRIO-18): open-label, multicenter, randomized (1:1) Phase I/II trial; FDA's review (and this entry) concerns only the Phase II portion — palbociclib 125 mg/day (3 weeks on/1 week off) plus letrozole 2.5 mg/day continuous (P+L, n=84) vs. letrozole 2.5 mg/day alone (L, n=81), in postmenopausal women with inoperable/metastatic, ER-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer with no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease
- Randomization stratified by disease site (visceral vs. bone-only vs. other) and time to recurrence (disease-free interval >12 vs. ≤12 months); at study end FDA found substantial stratification-factor misclassification at randomization (29 disease-site and 22 time-to-recurrence errors), assessed in sensitivity analyses and found not to materially affect results
- Design history (per FDA's Statistical Review, Table 2, "SAP Amendments"): the trial was originally a single, all-comers, 150-patient 1:1 randomized study; Amendment 3 (July 1, 2010) split it into Part 1 (all-comers, enrollment halted at 66, made exploratory) and Part 2 (biomarker-selected for CCND1 amplification [CCND1 >1.5] and/or CDKN2A/p16 loss [p16 <0.8], planned n=150, made primary); Amendment 5 (June 21, 2012) — prompted by an interim look at Part 1 efficacy data — recombined Part 1 and Part 2 into a single primary analysis population; Amendment 6 (Nov 8, 2012) added a 100% BICR re-review for all enrolled patients; Amendment 7 (July 11, 2013) moved the final PFS analysis trigger from 114 to 95 events due to a slower-than-expected event rate
- Primary endpoint: investigator-assessed PFS (RECIST), Part 1 + Part 2 combined ITT population; key secondary endpoints per protocol: overall survival and objective response rate
- Sample size: originally powered for HR=0.67 (13.5 vs. 9 month median PFS), 114 events for 80% power at 1-sided alpha=0.10 — a design alpha FDA noted was set this way "because this study was not originally designed to be a registration study"; later re-triggered at 95 events (Amendment 7)
- Statistical methods: stratified log-rank test (disease site, time-to-recurrence, and study part as strata) for investigator-assessed PFS in the pooled ITT population; log-rank tests for OS and time-to-progression; Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test for ORR; BICR-assessed PFS analysis used only "study part" as a stratification factor (sponsor pre-specified this reduced stratification set for the BICR analysis)
- Because of the data-driven SAP amendments, FDA's review reports investigator-assessed PFS results (HR 0.488, 95% CI 0.319-0.748; median 20.2 vs. 10.2 months) with p-values capped and labeled only "<0.01, nominal," and states no formal inference is possible
- FDA required a 100% BICR re-review of all randomized patients given open-label conduct; BICR PFS (HR 0.621, 95% CI 0.378-1.017 per the review's Part1+Part2 combined row; median 25.7 vs. 14.8 months) was directionally consistent but attenuated, and FDA's own discordance analysis (early/late discordance rate, EDR/LDR, per Amit et al. 2011) found evidence of investigator bias favoring the P+L arm (LDR difference of 22.5 percentage points between arms, at the 98th percentile of a 10,000-iteration randomization-test null distribution), only partially explained by differential handling of bone-only-disease progression
- FDA's clinical review team additionally re-adjudicated case report forms/narratives for the 96 patients where investigator and BICR disagreed on PFS timing/censoring, producing an FDA "sensitivity analysis" PFS estimate (HR 0.574, 95% CI 0.378-0.870) that fell closer to the investigator-assessed result than to BICR

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter (accelerated approval, signed by Richard Pazdur, 02/03/2015) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2015/207103Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (original approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2015/207103s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Erik W. Bloomquist / Shenghui Tang / Rajeshwari Sridhara, Division of Biometrics) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/207103Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Clinical/Medical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/207103Orig1s000MedR.pdf
- FDA Summary Review (Division Director Review, incl. accelerated-approval risk-benefit rationale and PMR/PMC list) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/207103Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (PALOMA-1/TRIO-18) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00721409 (no protocol/SAP posted in the record's documentSection as of this review)
- Pivotal publication: Finn RS, Crown JP, Lang I, et al. "The cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 inhibitor palbociclib in combination with letrozole versus letrozole alone as first-line treatment of oestrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative, advanced breast cancer (PALOMA-1/TRIO-18): a randomised phase 2 study." *Lancet Oncol.* 2015;16(1):25-35. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(14)71159-3>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25524798/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=The%20cyclin-dependent%20kinase%204/6%20inhibitor%20palbociclib%20in%20combination%20with%20letrozole%20versus%20letrozole%20alone%20as%20first-line%20treatment%20of%20oestrogen%20receptor-positive%2C%20HER2-negative%2C%20advanced%20breast%20cancer)

**Other resources**

- Pfizer IPD access via Vivli.org; trial-specific PALOMA-1 availability not individually confirmed here.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held — the Summary Review states outside expertise was not necessary and there were no controversial issues warranting discussion.
- Confirmatory trial: PALOMA-2 (Study A5481008), a randomized, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trial (palbociclib + letrozole vs. placebo + letrozole), required as PMR #1; a PMC additionally required analysis from PALOMA-2 of the prognostic/predictive significance of the p16/CCND1 biomarker.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Executive Summary, p.4]*

> "At the outset, PALOMA-1 was not designed to be a registrational trial, and had several flaws of execution. The study also had several data-driven amendments to the statistical analysis plan. These included splitting the study into two parts, one an all-comers population and the other a biomarker selected population, and then recombining the two study parts back into one analysis population."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §2.2 "Study Design and Changes," Table 2 "SAP Amendments," p.6-7]*

> "SAP Amend#1 / Protocol Amend#3 (July 1, 2010): Phase 2 portion of study split into two parts: Part 1 (all-comers) and Part 2 (biomarker selected) based upon preclinical models. The biomarker selected population included patients with CCND1 amplification (CCND1 > 1.5) and/or CDKN2A loss (P16 < 0.8). Part 1 population enrollment halted at 66 and considered exploratory analysis population. Part 2 population set to be 150 patients and considered primary analysis population.
> SAP Amend#2 / Protocol Amend#5 (June 21, 2012): Primary analysis population becomes Part 1 combined with Part 2. Change due to interim look at Part 1 efficacy data.
> SAP Amend#3a / Protocol Amend#6 (Nov 8, 2012): Added BICR analysis for all patients enrolled in study.
> SAP Amend#3a / Protocol Amend#7 (July 11, 2013): Changed the final analysis time of PFS from 114 PFS events to 95 PFS events based upon slower than expected event rate."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.3 "Sample Size," p.9]*

> "The sample size for this study was originally determined using a HR=0.67, with the P+L arm having a 13.5 month median PFS time and the L arm having a 9 month PFS time. A total of 114 events were needed to achieve 80% power to detect an HR=0.67 with a 1-sided alpha = 0.10... Reviewer Comments: This study was not originally designed to be a registration study and thus the reason for setting alpha = 20% for a two-sided test. The sample size is too small for a confirmatory study."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.4 "Primary Endpoint," Reviewer Comment, p.11]*

> "The results of the primary analysis suggest longer a PFS with Palbociclib + letrozole compared to letrozole treatment. Because the goal of this trial was to explore, a number of data-driven changes were made to the protocol. Therefore, from a statistical point of view, inference cannot be drawn. Due to the number of data-driven changes to the SAP, p-values are only reported as approximate and nominal. The results clearly suggest an impact of SAP amendments on the outcome. Therefore, pooling Part 1 and Part is problematic."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.4.4 "Early and Late Discrepancy Rate," p.16, on FDA's own ascertainment-bias sensitivity analysis]*

> "For the LDR, however, there does appear to be investigator bias towards the treatment group. The difference in the LDR between the two arms was 22.5% and in a randomization test, this difference falls in the 98% percentile of the distribution... There still appears to be an unquantifiable investigator bias towards the P+L arm over the L arm."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §4.3 "Biomarker Selection," p.22, on the exploratory p16/CCND1 subgroup findings]*

> "But for the p16 biomarker, there appeared to be a strong difference between those above 0.8 and those below 0.8. For those with p16 levels above 0.8 (n=112), the HR = 0.315 95% CI = (0.189, 0.523) with a 17.4 month increase in median PFS. But for those with p16 levels below 0.8 (n=33), the HR equaled 0.731 95% CI = (0.320, 1.667) with only a 1.5 month increase in PFS... All the results for P16 are only exploratory results. But due to the large differences in magnitude between the two groups, FDA has requested a PMC to assess P16 and its relationship to Palbociclib in the confirmatory study."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review (Division Director Review), Risk Benefit Assessment, p.13]*

> "A single study with two cohorts have been submitted to support the NDA for postmenopausal women with estrogen receptor (ER)-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative advanced breast cancer who have not received previous systemic treatment for their advanced disease. The magnitude of improvement in PFS is relatively large. ORR and OS results are supportive, as are the BICR results. Multiple sensitivity analyses were performed and these remained in favor of palbociclib. However, multiple issues arose, and while the p value is uninterpretable, and the magnitude of improvement of PFS may decrease relatively, it is likely that palbociclib will confer an improvement of several months of PFS... Given the observed risk-benefit profile, ongoing confirmatory trial PALOMA-2, the seriousness of the disease, I recommend an accelerated approval of palbociclib."

This is an unusually clean example of "how the SAP held up under FDA review" for an accelerated approval: FDA accepted a randomized Phase II trial whose SAP was reshaped three separate times by the sponsor in response to its own emerging data (splitting into an all-comers cohort and a biomarker-selected cohort, then pooling them, then adding a mandatory BICR re-review, then moving the event-count trigger) — and rather than treating any resulting p-value as confirmatory, FDA's own Statistical Review explicitly declassified every p-value in the trial as "nominal," ran its own independent bias-detection analysis (EDR/LDR) and case-report-form re-adjudication, and based the accelerated approval on the estimated magnitude of the PFS effect and risk-benefit judgment rather than on formal hypothesis-test inference — deferring formal confirmation to the pre-specified, fully powered Phase III PALOMA-2 trial required as a postmarketing commitment.

### 44. lenvatinib (Lenvima) — NDA 206947

**Sponsor:** Eisai Inc.

**Indication approved:** Radioactive iodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC)

**Approval date:** February 13, 2015

**Pivotal trial:** SELECT (Study E7080-G000-303), NCT01321554

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover permitted at progression
- *Endpoints:* progression-free survival (PFS, primary, blinded independent imaging review), overall survival (OS, secondary), objective response rate (ORR, secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified), Kaplan-Meier estimation, Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test (ORR)
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (ORR→OS, each at 2-sided alpha=0.05)
- *Missing data/bias:* Rank-Preserving Structural Failure Time (RPSFT) model (OS crossover adjustment)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- SELECT was a randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter Phase III trial in patients with radioiodine-refractory DTC and documented disease progression (RECIST 1.1, centrally confirmed) within the prior 12 months; 392 patients randomized to lenvatinib 24 mg/day continuous oral dosing (n=261) or matching placebo (n=131)
- Randomization stratified by geographic region (Europe, North America, Other), age group (≤65 vs. >65 years), and prior VEGF/VEGFR-targeted therapy (0 vs. 1 prior regimen)
- Primary endpoint: PFS by blinded independent imaging review (IIR) per RECIST 1.1, defined as time from randomization to first documentation of disease progression or death; tumor assessments every 8 weeks during the randomized phase
- Secondary endpoints: overall survival (OS) and objective response rate (ORR), both IIR-assessed; placebo patients with IIR-confirmed progression could enter an optional open-label (OOL) lenvatinib period, and lenvatinib patients without progression could later continue open-label lenvatinib after the primary analysis
- Sample size: 214 PFS events needed to detect HR=0.57 (median PFS 8 vs. 14 months) with 90% power at 2-sided alpha=0.01; ~360 patients planned (20/month accrual, 10% dropout), with 214 events expected at ~29 months
- Primary analysis: stratified log-rank test (region, age group, prior VEGF/VEGFR therapy) at 2-sided alpha=0.01 (tighter than the conventional 0.05, reflecting the primary-endpoint significance threshold used for this application); HR/CI from a Cox model stratified by the same three factors; Kaplan-Meier estimation for medians
- Secondary-endpoint multiplicity: ORR (CMH test, stratified) and OS (stratified log-rank test) were both tested at 2-sided alpha=0.05 using a fixed-sequence hierarchy — ORR tested first, and OS tested only if ORR was statistically significant
- OS analysis was pre-specified to include not only a stratified log-rank test but also a Rank-Preserving Structural Failure Time (RPSFT) model (Robins and Tsiatis, 1991) to correct for bias introduced by the substantial placebo-to-lenvatinib crossover after progression
- Result: median PFS 18.3 months (lenvatinib) vs. 3.6 months (placebo), stratified log-rank p<0.0001, HR 0.21 (95% CI 0.16-0.28); ORR 64.8% vs. 1.5% (CMH p<0.0001); OS not statistically significant at the interim analysis reported (118 deaths, log-rank p=0.1032, HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.50-1.07), with 79% of placebo-arm deaths having occurred among patients who had crossed over to lenvatinib — consistent with the OS hierarchy correctly not being "unlocked" for a superiority claim, since ORR was significant but OS was not

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2015/206947Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (2015, original approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2015/206947s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Reviewer: Xiaoping (Janet) Jiang, PhD, Division of Biometrics V) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/206947Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01321554 (no protocol/SAP documents posted in the Documents tab)
- Pivotal publication: Schlumberger M, Tahara M, Wirth LJ, et al. "Lenvatinib versus placebo in radioiodine-refractory thyroid cancer." *N Engl J Med.* 2015;372(7):621-630. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1406470), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25671254/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Lenvatinib%20versus%20placebo%20in%20radioiodine-refractory%20thyroid%20cancer)

**Other resources**

- Eisai's IPD data-sharing policy/participation in Vivli or a comparable platform was not individually confirmed for SELECT in this pass.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this original approval.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Executive Summary, p.3]*

> "In SELECT, a total of 392 eligible patients were randomized in a 2:1 ratio to receive either lenvatinib 24 mg by continuous once daily oral administration or matching placebo administered as blinded study drug. The randomization was stratified by geographic region (Europe, North America, and Other), age group (≤65 or >65 years), and prior VEGF/VEGFR-targeted therapy (0 or 1). The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS), determined by blinded independent imaging review (IIR) conducted by the imaging core laboratory using Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST 1.1) criteria. The primary analysis was a stratified log-rank test."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2 "Statistical Methodologies," p.6]*

> "Per the protocol and statistical analysis plan (SAP), the primary analysis of PFS was a log-rank test stratified by region (Europe, North America, Other), age group (≤65, >65years), and prior VEGF/VEGFR therapy (0, 1) at two-sided significance level of 0.01. The primary analysis was based on intent-to-treat (ITT) population, defined as all randomized patients... Assuming that the true PFS hazard ratio was 0.57 corresponding to median PFS of 8 months in the placebo arm and 14 months in the lenvatinib arm, a total of 214 events were needed to detect a hazard ratio of 0.57 with 90% power at a 2-sided alpha level of 0.01."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2 "Statistical Methodologies," p.6 — secondary-endpoint hierarchy]*

> "According to the protocol and SAP, the secondary endpoints ORR and OS would be compared between the treatment groups by controlling the overall family-wise error rate at level α = 0.05, using sequential testing procedure as the followings: the ORR would be tested first at the 0.05 level. Only if it was significant, OS would then be tested at the 0.05 level."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Reviewer's Comments, p.6 — on the RPSFT crossover-adjustment plan]*

> "The applicant pre-specified in the protocol that overall survival curves compared between treatment groups using the stratified log rank test. However, the applicant stated in the SAP that not only overall survival curves compared between treatment groups using the stratified log rank test, but also the rank preserving structural failure time (RPSFT) model (Robin and Tsiatis, 1991) would be used in OS analysis to correct the bias introduced by cross-over and estimate the true treatment effect on OS."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, results, p.3]*

> "Based on 220 PFS events determined by IIR, the PFS result demonstrated that patients treated with lenvatinib had statistically significant improvement in PFS compared to patients treated with placebo (stratified log-rank p-value<0.0001)... With 118 death events occurred, the overall survival (OS) analysis result showed that there was no statistical difference between the two treatment arms (log-rank p-value= 0.1032) with hazards ratio of 0.73 (95% CI: 0.50, 1.07)... Among 47 deaths from placebo arm in OS analysis, 37 (79%) were crossed-over to receive lenvatinib after confirmed disease progression."

### 45. panobinostat (Farydak) — NDA 205353

**Sponsor:** Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation

**Indication approved:** Multiple myeloma, in combination with bortezomib and dexamethasone, in patients who have received at least 2 prior regimens including bortezomib and an immunomodulatory agent (a narrower population than the pivotal trial's overall enrollment — see below)

**Approval date:** February 23, 2015

**Pivotal trial:** PANORAMA-1 (Study D2308), NCT01023308

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
- *Endpoints:* progression-free survival (PFS, investigator-assessed per mEBMT criteria, primary; IRC-assessed, sensitivity), overall survival (OS, key secondary), overall response rate (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified), Kaplan-Meier estimation, Clopper-Pearson exact confidence interval (response rate)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design (2 planned PFS interim analyses at 33%/80% of target events — first for futility, second for efficacy), O'Brien-Fleming alpha-spending function (PFS and, separately, OS)
- *Missing data/bias:* heavy differential censoring documented as a major statistical issue (FDA-identified), IRC re-assessment triggered by protocol non-adherence at multiple sites, sensitivity analyses re censoring rules and missing M-protein assessments
- *Regulatory:* FDA Advisory Committee meeting held (ODAC, 2-5-0 vote against a favorable benefit-risk balance), reviewer-documented major statistical issue undermining confidence in the primary analysis, approved indication narrower than full trial population

**Trial design & endpoints**

- PANORAMA-1 (Study D2308) was a randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter Phase III trial of panobinostat 20 mg + bortezomib + dexamethasone vs. placebo + bortezomib + dexamethasone in 768 patients with previously treated multiple myeloma (1-3 prior lines); randomization stratified by number of prior anti-myeloma regimens (1 vs. 2-3) and prior bortezomib use (yes/no)
- Treatment given in two phases (Phase 1: 8 cycles/24 weeks; Phase 2: additional 24 weeks for patients with clinical benefit by modified European Bone Marrow Transplant [mEBMT] criteria); no treatment crossover permitted
- Primary endpoint: PFS by investigator assessment per mEBMT response criteria (based on serial monoclonal M-protein measurement); secondary endpoints included OS (the only secondary endpoint with formal pre-specified hypothesis testing) and overall response rate
- Sample size: 762 patients planned to detect a 2.7-month median PFS improvement (7.5 vs. 10.2 months, HR=0.74) at 2-sided alpha=0.05, 90% power, with ~460 PFS events targeted at final analysis, accounting for group-sequential interim testing
- Interim analysis plan: two pre-planned PFS interim analyses at 33% and 80% of the 460 targeted events — the first for futility, the second for efficacy — with Type I error controlled via an O'Brien-Fleming alpha-spending function; OS was to be tested (with its own, separately pre-specified O'Brien-Fleming spending function keyed to the anticipated OS event counts at each planned PFS analysis and a final target of 415 OS events) only if PFS was statistically significant, implementing a hierarchical group-sequential testing procedure (per Glimm/Maurer/Bretz 2009 and Tamhane/Mehta/Liu 2010) that avoided inflating overall Type I error
- Major statistical issue identified by FDA: a substantial subset of study sites (193 patients, 25.1%) did not correctly follow the mEBMT M-protein measurement criteria, prompting the sponsor to convene an Independent Review Committee (IRC) and run an IRC-based sensitivity re-analysis of PFS; the primary investigator-assessed result showed a 3.9-month median PFS improvement (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.52-0.76), but heavy and differential censoring (46.5% of panobinostat-arm patients censored vs. 31.8% placebo) substantially reduced FDA's confidence in this result, and the IRC-based sensitivity analysis cut the estimated improvement to 2.2 months (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.58-0.83)
- The application was referred to FDA's Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) on November 6, 2014; the committee voted 2 (yes) to 5 (no) against a favorable benefit-risk balance for the full trial population, citing the marginal/uncertain PFS benefit (which did not translate into an OS or quality-of-life benefit) and substantial toxicity (on-treatment death 7.8% vs. 4.8%; Grade 3-4 AEs 95.1% vs. 82.5%; treatment discontinuation for AEs 36.0% vs. 20.4%)
- FDA ultimately approved a narrower indication than the full D2308 population — restricted to patients who had received at least 2 prior regimens including both bortezomib and an immunomodulatory agent — reflecting a subgroup-specific risk-benefit judgment rather than the trial's full enrolled population

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2015/205353Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (2015, original approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2015/205353s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (original, dated August 26, 2014; Reviewer: Chia-Wen Ko, PhD, with Lei Nie, PhD and Rajeshwari Sridhara, PhD, Division of Biometrics) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/205353Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- The same StatR PDF also contains a Statistical Review Addendum (dated November-December 2014) documenting the additional analyses prepared for and discussed at the ODAC meeting, including an updated OS interim analysis and a revised IRC-PFS sensitivity analysis
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01023308 (no protocol/SAP documents posted in the Documents tab)
- Pivotal publication: San-Miguel JF, Hungria VT, Yoon SS, et al. "Panobinostat plus bortezomib and dexamethasone versus placebo plus bortezomib and dexamethasone in patients with relapsed or relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma: a multicentre, randomised, double-blind phase 3 trial." *Lancet Oncol.* 2014;15(11):1195-1206. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(14)70440-1>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25242045/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Panobinostat%20plus%20bortezomib%20and%20dexamethasone%20versus%20placebo%20plus%20bortezomib%20and%20dexamethasone%20in%20patients%20with%20relapsed%20or%20relapsed%20and%20refractory%20multiple%20myeloma)

**Other resources**

- Novartis participates in Vivli.org for IPD-sharing requests; trial-specific PANORAMA-1 availability was not individually confirmed in this pass.
- An FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee meeting was held on November 6, 2014 (voted 2-5-0 against a favorable benefit-risk determination for the studied population); FDA nonetheless approved a narrower indication than the one discussed at the ODAC vote.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.1 "Study Design and Endpoints," p.7]*

> "Study D2308 was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, Phase 3 study to assess the efficacy and safety of panobinostat (PAN) + bortezomib (BTZ) + dexamethasone (DEX) compared with placebo (PBO) + bortezomib (BTZ) + dexamethasone (DEX) in patients with previously treated MM. The study enrolled a total of 768 patients, randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive panobinostat at 20 mg (n=387) or placebo (n=381) plus bortezomib and dexamethasone. The randomization was stratified by number of prior lines of anti-myeloma therapy (1 vs. 2 or 3) and prior use of bortezomib (yes vs. no)."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.2 "Statistical Methodologies of the Pivotal Study," p.9]*

> "The study was sized at 762, with a 1:1 randomization, to detect an increase of 2.7 months in median PFS from 7.5 months in the placebo-control arm to 10.2 months in panobinostat arm (corresponding hazard ratio [HR] = 0.74) with a 2-sided 5% significance level and 90% power... The primary comparison in PFS between treatment arms was based on a 2-sided stratified (by randomization factors) log-rank test... Two interim analyses for PFS were planned after observing 33% and 80% of the 460 events targeted for the final analysis. The first interim analysis was for testing futility, while the second interim analysis was intended to test for treatment efficacy. OS would be tested if the primary endpoint PFS was statistically significant for efficacy. The Type I error control for multiple testing in PFS was done through the O'Brien-Fleming alpha spending function approach. For the key secondary endpoint OS, a separate pre-planned O'Brien-Fleming function was utilized for alpha spending based on anticipated number of OS events at the planned PFS analyses and the final targeted 415 OS events for the final OS analysis. This strategy, as shown in Glimm et al (2009, Statistics in Medicine) and Tamhane et al (2010, Biometrics), utilized a hierarchical testing procedure allowing for the testing of OS after PFS was statistically significant without inflating the study Type I error."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §5.1-5.2 "Statistical Issues" / "Collective Evidence," p.21]*

> "The major statistical issue with the efficacy evaluation was that some study sites did not follow the mEMBT criteria and used non-PEP M-protein measuring methods for the determination of responses and disease/relapse. This protocol violation concerned a total of 193 patients (25.1% of the study participants). As a result, the Applicant established an IRC to perform response assessments and specified additional sensitivity analyses for PFS by IRC assessment... The primary analysis of PFS based on investigator assessment showed an improvement of 3.9 months in median PFS by panobinostat (HR [95% CI]: 0.63 [0.52, 0.76]), but the sensitivity analysis of PFS by IRC assessment had the estimated improvement reduced to 2.2 months (HR [95% CI]: 0.69 [0.58, 0.83])."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §5.3 "Conclusions and Recommendations," p.21]*

> "Efficacy and safety results included in this application are not sufficient for this reviewer to derive a definite conclusion and recommendation."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review Addendum, §1 "Introduction," p.1-2 — prepared for the ODAC meeting]*

> "Trial D2308 showed an improvement in median progression-free survival (PFS) of 3.9 months as assessed by investigators as the primary endpoint analysis. However, large amounts of censored data limited the Agency's confidence in the primary analysis results. Sensitivity analyses for PFS submitted in the NDA application by Applicant showed much shorter improvement in median PFS by panobinostat. In addition, the patients on Trial D2308 panobinostat treatment group had twice the incidence of on-treatment deaths not due to disease progression – 7 percent vs. 3.5 percent – and a high incidence of myelosuppression, hemorrhage, infection, and cardiac toxicity. The high amount of observed toxicity combined with unreliable efficacy results make the benefit/risk assessment of panobinostat in combination with bortezomib and dexamethasone challenging."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review Addendum, §4 "ODAC Vote and Discussion," p.8]*

> "The ODAC was asked to vote: 'Given this benefit:risk profile of the addition of panobinostat to bortezomib and dexamethasone, does the benefit outweigh the risks for patients with relapsed multiple myeloma?' The results of the vote were: 2 Yes, 5 No, and 0 Abstain. The major concerns with panobinostat of the ODAC were: (1) treatment in-tolerability and subsequent therapy options, particularly the issue of potential treatment withdrawals and on-treatment deaths due to adverse events; (2) uncertainty about treatment benefit: the observed improvement in PFS was marginal and did not transfer into a survival or quality of life benefit in the study patients."

This is one of the clearest documented cases in this census of a negative-leaning ODAC vote followed by approval anyway, on a substantially narrowed population — the statistical review's own primary-analysis censoring concerns (differential censoring, non-adherent sites, a shrinking effect size under IRC re-analysis) were not resolved by the ODAC discussion, and FDA's final action addressed the risk-benefit concern not by requiring new data but by restricting the label to a heavily pretreated subgroup (≥2 prior regimens including both bortezomib and an IMiD) believed to have the most favorable benefit-risk balance.

### 46. Dinutuximab (Unituxin) — BLA 125516

**Sponsor:** United Therapeutics Corporation

**Indication approved:** In combination with GM-CSF, IL-2, and 13-cis-retinoic acid (RA), for the treatment of pediatric patients with high-risk neuroblastoma who achieve at least a partial response to prior first-line multiagent, multimodality therapy

**Approval date:** March 10, 2015

**Pivotal trial:** ANBL0032 (Children's Oncology Group), NCT00026312

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled, 24-stratum randomization (pre-ASCT response status x pre-ANBL0032 treatment protocol), non-randomized "Stratum 07" cohort with residual disease added alongside the randomized comparison
- *Endpoints:* event-free survival (EFS, primary — time from enrollment to relapse, progressive disease, secondary malignancy, or death), overall survival (OS, key secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test (protocol-specified), unstratified log-rank test (as actually reported, because of sparse/empty strata among the 24 randomization strata), Cox proportional-hazards model (FDA-added HR/CI), Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Multiplicity:* none — no adjustment was made for testing EFS and OS (single primary + one key secondary)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design with 7 planned interim looks every 6 months starting at 20% of expected events; boundaries calculated first via the Fleming-Harrington-O'Brien method (alpha 0.05, then 0.025) and, at the final (7th) look, via a Lan-DeMets Rho-family spending function; Data Monitoring Committee (DSMC)
- *Missing data/bias:* standard right-censoring at last contact; post-halt crossover of 4 RA-alone patients to the immunotherapy regimen after randomization was stopped

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ANBL0032: Phase III, randomized (1:1), open-label, multicenter, active-controlled trial of ch14.18 (dinutuximab) immunotherapy (dinutuximab + RA in cycles 1,3,5 with GM-CSF in cycles 2,4 and IL-2 in cycles 1,3,5; RA alone in cycle 6) versus RA alone (6 cycles), in pediatric patients with high-risk neuroblastoma who had achieved at least a partial response to first-line multiagent induction, myeloablative consolidation with autologous stem cell transplant, and radiotherapy
- Randomization was stratified by pre-ASCT response status (CR, VGPR, PR) crossed with the specific prior first-line treatment protocol (COG/POG/CCG predecessor studies), yielding 24 strata; a separate non-randomized cohort of 25 patients with biopsy-proven residual disease ("Stratum 07") received the experimental regimen but was excluded from the primary ITT efficacy analysis
- Primary endpoint: event-free survival (EFS), defined as time from study enrollment to first relapse, progressive disease, secondary malignancy, death, or last contact (INSS/INRC response criteria); key secondary endpoint: overall survival (OS), time from randomization to death from any cause
- Planned sample size: 386 randomized patients (1:1) to detect a 15-point improvement in 3-year EFS rate (65% vs. 50%) with 137 EFS events, 80% power, one-sided alpha=0.025 stratified log-rank test (increased from an original 322-patient/one-sided-0.05 design by Protocol Amendment 4, 12-Mar-2004)
- Randomization to the RA-alone control arm was halted early by the DSMC after the 7th interim analysis (data cutoff Jan 13, 2009): unstratified log-rank EFS p=0.0115 was inside the pre-specified Lan-DeMets boundary of 0.0108 (nominal alpha at that look)
- FDA's statistical reviewer confirmed the applicant's efficacy results but recommended that the OS p-value from the interim analysis be excluded from labeling because no alpha had been formally allocated to the OS interim test

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2015/125516Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2015/125516s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Sirisha Mushti, Division of Biometrics V; Reference ID 3627251) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/125516Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (ANBL0032) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00026312
- Protocol / SAP: not posted publicly (COG cooperative-group protocol; SAP finalized 24-Feb-2014 per FDA review, not independently available)
- Pivotal publication: Yu AL, Gilman AL, Ozkaynak MF, et al. "Anti-GD2 antibody with GM-CSF, interleukin-2, and isotretinoin for neuroblastoma." *N Engl J Med.* 2010;363:1324-1334. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa0911123), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20879881/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Anti-GD2%20antibody%20with%20GM-CSF%2C%20interleukin-2%2C%20and%20isotretinoin%20for%20neuroblastoma); long-term follow-up: Yu AL, Gilman AL, Ozkaynak MF, et al. "Long-Term Follow-up of a Phase III Study of ch14.18 (Dinutuximab) + Cytokine Immunotherapy in Children with High-Risk Neuroblastoma: COG Study ANBL0032." *Clin Cancer Res.* 2021;27:2179-2189. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-20-3909), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33504555/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Long-Term%20Follow-up%20of%20a%20Phase%20III%20Study%20of%20ch14.18%20%28Dinutuximab%29%20%2B%20Cytokine%20Immunotherapy%20in%20Children%20with%20High-Risk%20Neuroblastoma)

**Other resources**

- No confirmed IPD/dataset-sharing program for United Therapeutics was identified; the underlying trial was run by the NCI-funded Children's Oncology Group rather than industry, so patient-level data governance follows COG/NCI policy rather than a sponsor Vivli/YODA program.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this application.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, BLA 125516, Reference ID 3627251, §3.2.2-3.2.3]* — "Eligible patients after screening were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to either the treatment arm (Immunotherapy + RA) or the control arm (RA alone) and randomization was stratified using the pre-ASCT response status (CR, VGPR, or PR) and by pre-ANBL0032 treatment... Hence, a combination of the pre-ASCT response status and the pre-ANBL0032 treatment categories described above resulted in 24 strata for randomization... For the randomized portion of the study, a total of 386 patients were planned to be randomized to either of the treatment arms in a 1:1 ratio to detect a difference of 15% (Immunotherapy + RA: 65% vs. RA alone: 50%), in the 3-year EFS rate. 137 EFS events were required to detect a hazard ratio of 0.25 along with achieving an 80% power based on a stratified log-rank test with a 1-sided significance level of 0.025."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.2.4 Statistical Methodologies]* — "The primary endpoint for the study was EFS defined as time from study enrollment to the occurrence of an event which was defined as relapse, PD, secondary malignancy, or death, and the key secondary endpoint was OS. The primary analysis of EFS was a stratified log-rank test in the ITT population... An unstratified log-rank test was used to perform the analysis since there were a large number of strata (24 strata) and there were no subjects associated to some of these strata... No multiplicity adjustment was made in the primary and secondary analyses."

*[verbatim, same source, interim monitoring history]* — "The interim monitoring boundaries were calculated using different methods for different interim looks... For the Nov 2008, the Lan-DeMets (LD) upper boundary calculated using a Rho family spending function αt2 for a cumulative alpha level of 0.025 was applied... Based on the 7th interim analysis with a data cutoff date on Jan. 13, 2009, results of the primary endpoint (EFS), p-value = 0.0115, was close to the pre-specified alpha boundary of 0.0108 and hence a decision was made by the DMC to stop the randomized-phase of the study after this interim analysis."

*[verbatim, same source, §5.3 Labeling Recommendations — a reviewer-imposed limit on the label]* — "This statistical review supported the inclusion of results based on the primary analysis (Jan. 13, 2009 cutoff) for the event free survival and overall survival for the indication of high-risk neuroblastoma... However, due to the issue of no suitable allocated alpha for the interim analysis of OS, p-value for OS analysis should not be included in the label."

This is a case where the sponsor's actual conduct (an FDA-run cooperative-group trial with no formal alpha spent on the OS interim test) directly shaped what FDA would allow into the approved label — OS results could be described descriptively but the OS p-value itself was withheld from labeling.

### 47. Sonidegib (Odomzo) — NDA 205266

**Sponsor:** Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adults with locally advanced basal cell carcinoma (laBCC) that has recurred following surgery or radiation therapy, or who are not candidates for surgery or radiation therapy

**Approval date:** July 24, 2015

**Pivotal trial:** BOLT (Study CLDE225A2201), NCT01327053

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blinded, non-comparative, dose-ranging, biomarker-selected population by disease subtype (laBCC/mBCC cohorts), single trial with no formal treatment-arm comparison
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR, primary, per central/independent review using protocol-specified mRECIST for laBCC and RECIST 1.1 for mBCC), duration of response (DoR), patient-reported outcomes (EORTC QLQ-C30/H&N35, SF-36)
- *Primary analysis:* single-arm-style descriptive analysis of ORR per treatment group (no formal hypothesis test comparing arms), exact (Clopper-Pearson) 95% CI around ORR
- *Multiplicity:* not applicable — no comparative hypothesis test was planned between the 200 mg and 800 mg arms
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* single planned futility interim analysis (predictive-probability rule) on investigator-assessed ORR after the first 48 patients reached 16 weeks
- *Regulatory:* FDA reviewer classified the randomized, double-blind design as analytically equivalent to two single-arm studies because no comparative hypothesis was pre-specified

**Trial design & endpoints**

- BOLT: Phase II (publication) / pivotal registration trial for NDA purposes, randomized (2:1), double-blind, multicenter trial of sonidegib 800 mg vs. 200 mg once daily until progression or intolerable toxicity, in patients with laBCC (n=194) or metastatic BCC (mBCC, n=36); centralized randomization stratified by disease stage
- Primary endpoint: ORR (confirmed CR or PR on repeat assessment ≥4 weeks apart) per central/independent review — mRECIST (integrated radiographic/photographic/histologic composite) for laBCC, RECIST 1.1 for mBCC
- Analysis populations: Full Analysis Set (FAS/ITT, all randomized patients) and a later-introduced Primary Efficacy Analysis Subset (pEAS, laBCC patients evaluable by mRECIST); FDA required the primary analysis be reported in the FAS rather than the sponsor's preferred pEAS
- Sample size: designed for 80% power to detect an ORR ≥30% on either arm (assuming a true ORR ≤20%) at a two-sided alpha of 0.003 (800 mg arm) and 0.024 (200 mg arm) in a 2:1 randomization, ~150 patients needed in the pEAS
- No statistical test of hypothesis compared the two dose arms; sonidegib would be considered sufficiently efficacious if observed ORR on either arm was ≥30%, with clinical relevance further supported if the ORR's 95% CI lower bound exceeded 20%
- Primary analysis result: ORR 36% (200 mg) and 34% (800 mg) in laBCC per central review; the FDA statistical reviewer explicitly flagged that, absent a comparative arm, any time-to-event analysis (PFS, DoR) in this design is "uninterpretable and considered descriptive"

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2015/205266Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (original) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2015/205266Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID 3768106) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/205266Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (BOLT) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01327053 (no protocol/SAP posted in the Documents tab)
- Pivotal publication: Migden MR, Guminski A, Gutzmer R, et al. "Treatment with two different doses of sonidegib in patients with locally advanced or metastatic basal cell carcinoma (BOLT): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind phase 2 trial." *Lancet Oncol.* 2015;16:716-728. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(15)70100-2>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25981810/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Treatment%20with%20two%20different%20doses%20of%20sonidegib%20in%20patients%20with%20locally%20advanced%20or%20metastatic%20basal%20cell%20carcinoma%20BOLT)

**Other resources**

- Novartis participates in the Vivli data-sharing platform generally; trial-specific IPD availability for BOLT was not individually confirmed.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this application.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 205266, Reference ID 3768106, §3.2.3, Reviewer's Comments]* — "Without a comparative arm, this randomized two arms study's hypothesis and analysis should be evaluated as a single arm study. Any time-to-event analysis in the single arm study is uninterpretable and considered descriptive."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.2.7 Statistical Methodologies]* — "No statistical test of hypothesis comparing the two treatment arms was planned and was not required to observe a statistically significant difference in ORR between the two treatment arms. Treatment with sonidegib would be considered sufficiently efficacious if the observed ORR on any treatment arm at the end of the study was 30% or higher. The point estimate of ORR of each arm and its 95% exact CI would be provided as well as the difference in ORR between the two treatment arms. If the lower bounds of the associated 95% CIs of ORR in either treatment arm exceeded 20%, then it would be considered clinical relevance."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.2.4, Reviewer's Comment #4]* — "In response to the applicant briefing package (submitted on April 3, 2013), FDA stated that the primary analysis of ORR should be performed in the FAS."

This entry illustrates a submission where the FDA statistical reviewer treated the trial's own randomized/blinded design as a formality: because no hypothesis test was pre-specified between the two dose arms, the review explicitly downgraded the analysis to single-arm, descriptive logic — a useful contrast case against the census's other, genuinely comparative randomized trials.
