### 48. Rolapitant (Varubi) — NDA 206500

**Sponsor:** Tesaro, Inc.

**Indication approved:** In combination with other antiemetic agents, for prevention of delayed nausea and vomiting associated with initial and repeat courses of emetogenic cancer chemotherapy, including but not limited to highly emetogenic chemotherapy (HEC)

**Approval date:** September 1, 2015

**Pivotal trial:** Study TS-P04832 (HEC1, NCT01499849) and TS-P04833 (HEC2, NCT01500213); supportive: TS-P04834 (MEC, NCT01500226)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, active-controlled (granisetron + dexamethasone backbone in both arms), stratified by gender, two identical HEC trials plus one MEC trial supporting the same indication
- *Endpoints:* complete response (CR, primary — no emesis and no rescue medication) in the delayed phase (>24-120h post-chemotherapy), key secondary CR in the acute (0-24h) and overall (0-120h) phases
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by gender (primary confirmatory analysis), logistic regression model with treatment/sex/concomitant-emetogenic-chemotherapy covariate (earlier phase 2 dose-ranging study)
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (primary CR → key secondary CR delayed → key secondary CR acute), Bonferroni-Holm sequentially rejective procedure for the remaining 5 secondary endpoints
- *Missing data/bias:* missing diary data imputed as treatment failure for all binary efficacy endpoints (non-responder imputation)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Two identical global Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled trials (HEC1/TS-P04832, HEC2/TS-P04833) in patients receiving cisplatin-based highly emetogenic chemotherapy, plus a third Phase 3 trial (MEC/TS-P04834, ~1369 patients) in moderately emetogenic chemotherapy and AC (anthracycline/cyclophosphamide) regimens; all arms received background granisetron + dexamethasone, with rolapitant 180 mg (single oral dose) or placebo added
- Randomization stratified by gender only, 1:1 within each study
- Primary endpoint (all three trials): complete response (no emesis, no rescue antiemetic medication) in the delayed phase, >24 through 120 hours post-chemotherapy-initiation; key secondary endpoints: CR in the acute (0-24h) and overall (0-120h) phases
- Primary confirmatory analysis used a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel chi-square test stratified by gender; a hierarchical multiplicity procedure required the primary and both key secondary endpoints to reach significance before the remaining 5 secondary endpoints (no-emesis rates, no-significant-nausea, time to first emesis) could be formally tested, controlled within that secondary family by the Bonferroni-Holm procedure
- FDA's statistical reviewer noted the CMH-based primary result for at least one HEC study was not fully robust to analysis method (CMH p=0.056 vs. the sponsor's protocol-specified logistic regression, which fell below 0.05 only with a pre-specified covariate included) and separately evaluated efficacy consistency across investigator sites and geographic region given the trials' predominantly non-U.S. enrollment (no U.S. sites in the earlier phase 2 dose-finding study, TS-P04351)

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2015/206500Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2015/206500Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID 3764824) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/206500Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov records — HEC1: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01499849, HEC2: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01500213, MEC: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01500226 (no protocol/SAP posted in any Documents tab)
- Pivotal publications: Rapoport BL, Chasen MR, Gridelli C, et al. Complete response was defined as no emesis and no use of rescue medication... In addition, statistical significance of the other 5 secondary efficacy variables... could be established only if the primary and the two key secondary variables were deemed to be statistically significant. To control for multiplicity within the secondary endpoints, the Bonferroni-Holm procedure was used."

*[verbatim, same source, primary analysis method]* — "the between group comparison in the response rate was carried out using the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel χ2 test stratified by gender (SAS CMH test)."

*[verbatim, same source, reviewer robustness check]* — "the delayed phase was not robust to analysis method as the CMH had a p-value of 0.056... using the protocol specified logistic regression model, the p-value would be greater than 0.05 when the pre-specified CEC covariate was removed from the logistic regression model."

### 49. Trifluridine/tipiracil (Lonsurf) — NDA 207981

**Sponsor:** Taiho Oncology, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer previously treated with fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-based chemotherapy, an anti-VEGF biological therapy, and, if RAS wild-type, an anti-EGFR therapy

**Approval date:** September 22, 2015

**Pivotal trial:** RECOURSE (Study TPU-TAS-102-301), NCT01607957

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven trial, international (US/EU/Japan) enrollment stratified by region
- *Endpoints:* overall survival (OS, primary), progression-free survival (PFS, secondary), objective response rate (ORR, secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified), Kaplan-Meier estimation, Fisher's exact test (ORR)
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing — PFS tested only if OS reached significance at the one-sided 0.025 level
- *Missing data/bias:* standard right-censoring at last follow-up/data cutoff; sensitivity analyses using unstratified log-rank test, as-treated population, and CRF-based (rather than IVRS-based) stratification factors, all consistent with the primary analysis

**Trial design & endpoints**

- RECOURSE: Phase III, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, multinational trial of trifluridine/tipiracil (TAS-102) plus best supportive care (BSC) vs. placebo plus BSC, in patients with previously treated (≥2 lines) metastatic colorectal cancer (n=800: 534 TAS-102, 266 placebo)
- Randomization via IWRS, stratified by KRAS status (wild-type/mutant), time since diagnosis of first metastasis (<18 vs. ≥18 months), and geographic region (Japan vs. US/Europe/Australia)
- Primary endpoint: OS, time from randomization to death (censored at last follow-up or cutoff); secondary endpoints: investigator-assessed PFS and ORR
- Sample size: 800 patients planned for 571 OS events, 90% power, one-sided alpha=0.025, assuming HR=0.75 and 5-month median OS in the placebo arm; no interim efficacy analysis was planned, only periodic DMC safety review
- Testing procedure: if OS reached significance at the one-sided 0.025 level, PFS could subsequently be tested at the same level (fixed-sequence hierarchy); ORR was analyzed via Fisher's exact test without multiplicity adjustment
- Primary result: OS HR 0.68 (median 7.1 vs. 5.3 months, p<0.0001, stratified log-rank); PFS HR 0.48 (median 2.0 vs. 1.7 months, p<0.0001)

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2015/207981Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2015/207981Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID 3802437) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/207981Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (RECOURSE) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01607957 (no protocol/SAP posted in the Documents tab)
- Pivotal publication: Mayer RJ, Van Cutsem E, Falcone A, et al. "Randomized trial of TAS-102 for refractory metastatic colorectal cancer." *N Engl J Med.* 2015;372:1909-1919. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1414325), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25970050/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Randomized%20trial%20of%20TAS-102%20for%20refractory%20metastatic%20colorectal%20cancer)

**Other resources**

- No confirmed sponsor IPD-sharing program (Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere) was identified for Taiho Oncology; trial-specific data availability was not individually confirmed.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this application.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 207981, Reference ID 3802437, §3.2.1]* — "A total of 800 patients were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to TAS-102 plus BSC or placebo plus BSC. Randomization were conducted via an Interactive Voice/Web Response System (IWRS) and stratified by: KRAS gene status (wild-type, mutant); Time since diagnosis of first metastasis (<18 months, ≥18 months); Geographical region (Region 1: Asia [Japan]; Region 2: Western [US, Europe and Australia])."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.2.3-3.2.4]* — "The planned sample size was 800 patients with 571 OS events for the final analysis... One-sided type I error rate of 0.025 and 90% power... No interim efficacy analysis was planned for this study... OS and PFS were summarized using the Kaplan-Meier estimates and the difference between the two treatment arms was tested using a stratified log-rank test, stratifying for stratification factors at randomization. If OS demonstrated significance at the 1-sided 0.025 level, PFS could subsequently be tested at the 1-sided 0.025 level."

### 50. Trabectedin (Yondelis) — NDA 207953

**Sponsor:** Janssen Products, LP

**Indication approved:** Treatment of patients with unresectable or metastatic liposarcoma or leiomyosarcoma who received a prior anthracycline-containing regimen

**Approval date:** October 23, 2015

**Pivotal trial:** Study ET743-SAR-3007 ("Study 3007"), NCT01343277

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled (dacarbazine comparator), mid-trial primary-endpoint change (OS→PFS) driven by external ODAC precedent rather than trial-internal data, biomarker-free enrollment restricted by histology (liposarcoma/leiomyosarcoma) and prior therapy line
- *Endpoints:* progression-free survival (PFS, investigator-assessed, primary as amended), overall survival (OS, originally-planned primary, retained as key secondary), objective response rate (ORR)
- *Primary analysis:* unstratified log-rank test (as executed, despite protocol-specified randomization stratification), Cox proportional-hazards model, Kaplan-Meier estimation, blinded independent radiologist audit of a subset of scans supporting the PFS result
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* one planned interim OS analysis at 188 deaths (50% information), O'Brien-Fleming Lan-DeMets alpha-spending method (alpha 0.003 interim / 0.047 final)
- *Missing data/bias:* no formal control of overall two-sided type I error (0.05) across the primary PFS analysis and the secondary endpoint family — explicitly noted as absent by the FDA statistical reviewer
- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented deviation from the originally agreed analysis plan — FDA initially rejected PFS as the primary endpoint at trial design, and the sponsor's later switch to PFS was justified by referencing a March 2012 ODAC discussion of a *different* drug (pazopanib), not new data from this trial

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 3007: Phase III, randomized (2:1), open-label, active-controlled, multicenter trial of trabectedin (1.5 mg/m² IV over 24h, q3wk) vs. dacarbazine (1 g/m² IV, q3wk) in patients ≥15 years with unresectable, locally advanced, or metastatic liposarcoma/leiomyosarcoma previously treated with an anthracycline (n=518: 345 trabectedin, 173 dacarbazine), conducted Dec 2010-Jan 2015 at 84 centers (Australia, Brazil, New Zealand, US)
- Randomization was centralized (IVRS/IWRS, permuted-block) and stratified by number of prior chemotherapy lines (1 vs. ≥2), ECOG PS (0 vs. 1), and sarcoma subtype (liposarcoma vs. leiomyosarcoma)
- The trial was originally designed with OS as the primary endpoint; FDA did not agree at the design stage with the sponsor's proposal to use PFS as primary. Following a March 20, 2012 ODAC meeting that discussed pazopanib and endorsed a ~2.6-month PFS improvement as clinically meaningful, the sponsor amended the protocol to make PFS the primary endpoint supporting approval, ahead of the first planned OS interim analysis
- Efficacy measures: OS, investigator-assessed PFS, and ORR; a blinded independent-radiologist audit of a subset of scans (307 patients, 59% of ITT) supported the PFS result at the time of the OS interim analysis
- Result: PFS HR 0.55 (95% CI 0.44-0.70, unstratified log-rank p<0.0001; median 4.2 vs. 1.5 months); OS was not statistically significant at either the interim or final (Jan 5, 2015 cutoff) analysis (unstratified log-rank p=0.49, HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.75-1.15); no ORR improvement (9.9% vs. 6.9%)
- FDA's statistical reviewer explicitly flagged that the major protocol/SAP changes were submitted after enrollment completed and the final SAP was finalized after the clinical data cutoff, and that no method was proposed to control the overall two-sided type I error rate across the primary and secondary endpoint analyses

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2015/207953Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2015/207953s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID 3796653) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/207953Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (Study 3007) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01343277 (no protocol/SAP posted in the Documents tab)
- Pivotal publication: Demetri GD, von Mehren M, Jones RL, et al. "Efficacy and Safety of Trabectedin or Dacarbazine for Metastatic Liposarcoma or Leiomyosarcoma After Failure of Conventional Chemotherapy: Results of a Phase III Randomized Multicenter Clinical Trial." *J Clin Oncol.* 2016;34:786-793. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.2015.62.4734), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26371143/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Efficacy%20and%20Safety%20of%20Trabectedin%20or%20Dacarbazine%20for%20Metastatic%20Liposarcoma%20or%20Leiomyosarcoma)

**Other resources**

- IPD access for NCT01343277 is available through the YODA Project (Yale University, on behalf of Janssen) — https://yoda.yale.edu/clinical-trial/nct01343277-a-study-of-trabectedin-or-dacarbazine-for-the-treatment-of-patients-with-advanced-liposarcoma-or-leiomyosarcoma/.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held specifically for trabectedin; the March 2012 ODAC discussion cited as regulatory precedent concerned pazopanib, a separate application.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 207953, Reference ID 3796653, §2.1.3]* — "The trial was originally designed using OS as the primary endpoint. At the study design phase, FDA did not agree with the proposal of using PFS as the primary endpoint. On March 20, 2012, the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee (ODAC) discussed pazopanib and agreed with the magnitude of a 2.6 months improvement in median PFS to be clinically meaningful. After this ODAC meeting, the applicant submitted a protocol amendment to use PFS for supporting an approval before the first interim analysis of OS was performed as originally designed in the trial since the regulatory standard for approval of this indication changed."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "The issue is that the major protocol/statistical analysis plan (SAP) changes were submitted after the completion of patient enrollment, and the final SAP was finalized after the clinical cut-off date. Whether the data and analyses from trabectedin demonstrated an overall favorable benefit vs. risk profile is deferred to the clinical team reviewing this application."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.2.2 Study Design]* — "Approximately 570 patients (age ≥ 15 years) were planned to be randomized based on a permuted-block randomization method using a 2:1 allocation. The randomization was centralized and stratified by three baseline factors: the number of lines of prior chemotherapy (1 vs. ≥ 2), Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status (PS) score (0 vs.1), and L-sarcoma subtype (liposarcoma vs. leiomyosarcoma)."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.2.4]* — "A statistical method was not proposed to control the overall type I error rate at 0.05 (2-sided) for [the primary endpoint and secondary endpoints]... An interim efficacy analysis at 188 deaths (50%) was planned. The O'Brien-Fleming Lan-Demets alpha spending method was utilized with alpha allocation of 0.003 and 0.047 for interim [and final analyses]."

This is a genuine example of a sponsor's primary endpoint being changed for regulatory reasons unconnected to this trial's own accumulating data — the precedent came from a different drug's advisory committee meeting — and of FDA's statistical review flagging the timing of the SAP finalization (after database lock) as a reviewable concern in its own right.

### 51. Cobimetinib (Cotellic) — NDA 206192

**Sponsor:** Genentech, Inc.

**Indication approved:** In combination with vemurafenib, for treatment of patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma with a BRAF V600E or V600K mutation

**Approval date:** November 10, 2015

**Pivotal trial:** coBRIM (Study GO28141), NCT01689519

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, biomarker-selected population (BRAF V600E/K mutation-positive), stratified by region and disease stage
- *Endpoints:* progression-free survival (PFS, primary, investigator-assessed with IRF as supportive), objective response rate (ORR, key secondary), overall survival (OS, key secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified), Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing at overall two-sided alpha=0.05 — ORR tested first after PFS reached significance, then OS tested only if ORR was significant
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* two planned interim OS analyses (first coincident with final PFS analysis, second at 256/67% of targeted OS events), Lan-DeMets implementation of the O'Brien-Fleming spending function
- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented deviation from an unresolved protocol/SAP ambiguity — the applicant had not pre-specified whether stratification factors from the interactive randomization system (IxRS) or the case report form (CRF) governed the primary stratified analysis; FDA designated the IxRS-based analysis as primary on ITT-principle grounds and the CRF-based analysis as merely supportive

**Trial design & endpoints**

- coBRIM (GO28141): Phase III, randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial of cobimetinib 60 mg QD (days 1-21 of each 28-day cycle) + vemurafenib 960 mg BID vs. placebo + vemurafenib, in previously untreated BRAF V600 mutation-positive unresectable locally advanced or metastatic melanoma (n=495: 247 cobimetinib arm, 248 placebo arm)
- Randomization stratified by geographic region (North America, Europe, Australia/New Zealand, Other) and AJCC metastatic classification (M-stage)
- Primary endpoint: PFS per investigator assessment (log-rank test stratified by the two randomization factors, two-sided alpha=0.05), ITT population; an Independent Review Facility (IRF) assessment of PFS was a supportive analysis
- Multiplicity: hierarchical family-wise testing at overall alpha=0.05 — ORR (chi-square test) tested first at 0.05 after PFS showed significance; only if ORR was significant would OS (stratified log-rank) then be tested at 0.05
- Interim monitoring: two planned OS interim analyses (first at the time of final PFS analysis with data cutoff May 9, 2014; second at 256 events/~67% information), Lan-DeMets O'Brien-Fleming spending function to control overall two-sided alpha=0.05 across all OS looks
- Primary result: PFS HR 0.51 (unstratified, per IxRS-based stratified log-rank p<0.0001; stratified analysis by IRF assessment p=0.0003); first OS interim analysis showed a trend favoring cobimetinib (stratified log-rank p=0.0463/0.0273 depending on stratification source) that did not cross the pre-specified O'Brien-Fleming boundary

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2015/206192Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2015/206192Orig1s000lbl.pdf

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1408868), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25265494/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Combined%20vemurafenib%20and%20cobimetinib%20in%20BRAF-mutated%20melanoma)

**Other resources**

- Genentech/Roche participates in the Vivli data-sharing platform; trial-specific IPD availability for coBRIM was not individually confirmed.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this application.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 206192, Reference ID 3748873, §3.2.2]* — "Per the protocol and the SAP, the primary analysis of PFS was a log-rank test stratified by two randomized stratified factors: geographic region (North America, Europe, Australia/New Zealand...) [and metastatic classification]... at a two-sided significance level of 0.05. The primary analysis was based on the intent-to-treat (ITT) population."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "A hierarchical order to control the overall family-wise error rate at level α = 0.05 for the secondary endpoints ORR and OS was pre-specified in the protocol and SAP: the ORR would be tested first at the 0.05 level after the primary analysis of PFS showing statistical significance. Only if it was significant, OS would then be tested at the 0.05 level."

*[verbatim, same source, Reviewer's Comment #1]* — "The applicant did not pre-specify whether strata derived from case report form (CRF) or from randomization system IxRS would be used in the primary PFS and OS analyses. FDA considers the stratified analysis using strata recorded from IxRS as the primary analysis because it is consistent with the intend-to-treat (ITT) principle. FDA considers the stratified analysis using strata recorded from CRFs as a supportive analysis."

### 52. Daratumumab (Darzalex) — BLA 761036

**Sponsor:** Janssen Biotech, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of patients with multiple myeloma who have received at least three prior lines of therapy including a proteasome inhibitor (PI) and an immunomodulatory agent, or who are double-refractory to a PI and an immunomodulatory agent (accelerated approval, Subpart H)

**Approval date:** November 16, 2015

**Pivotal trial:** SIRIUS (Study MMY2002), NCT01985126; supportive: GEN501, NCT00574288

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H/21 CFR 314.510, Simon's two-stage design used for dose selection in Part 1 of GEN501, pooled analysis across two independently conducted single-arm studies
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR, primary, per independent review committee [IRC] using IMWG 2011 criteria), duration of response (DOR), clinical benefit rate, time to progression, progression-free survival, overall survival (all secondary/descriptive — not formally testable in a single-arm design)
- *Primary analysis:* exact (Clopper-Pearson) binomial confidence interval around ORR; one-sided hypothesis test of a single proportion (H0: ORR≤15% vs. Ha: ORR≥40%, one-sided alpha=2.5%, 85% power) used only for Part 1 dose-selection in GEN501, not for the pivotal ORR claim itself
- *Multiplicity:* not applicable — no comparative or multi-endpoint hypothesis test was pre-specified
- *Missing data/bias:* not applicable in the conventional sense (no censoring/crossover issue); FDA reviewer explicitly noted that time-to-event endpoints (PFS, DOR, OS, TTP) "cannot be evaluated based on a single arm trial" and were treated as descriptive only
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval (Subpart H) based on ORR as a surrogate reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit; two randomized Phase III confirmatory trials (MMY3003/POLLUX and MMY3004/CASTOR) required as post-marketing requirements to support conversion to regular approval

**Trial design & endpoints**

- SIRIUS (MMY2002): open-label, single-arm, multicenter Phase II trial of daratumumab monotherapy (16 mg/kg) in patients with multiple myeloma who had received ≥3 prior lines (including a PI and an IMiD) or were double-refractory; 124 patients enrolled, 106 treated at the approved dose and included in the primary efficacy analysis
- Primary endpoint: ORR (PR or better — PR/VGPR/CR/sCR per International Myeloma Working Group [IMWG] 2011 criteria) assessed by an independent review committee (IRC), based on central-laboratory results; investigator and a sponsor computerized algorithm also generated response assessments for comparison
- Supportive study GEN501: two-part Phase I/II trial — Part 1 was a randomized (for dose-selection purposes only, not efficacy comparison) Simon's two-stage design comparing 8 mg/kg vs. 16 mg/kg dosing to allow early termination of an ineffective dose for futility; Part 2 was a descriptive single-arm extension characterizing the Phase 3 drug product at the selected 16 mg/kg dose
- Sample-size logic for GEN501 Part 1: null hypothesis ORR≤15%, alternative ORR≥40%, one-sided alpha=2.5%, 85% power, requiring 36 response-evaluable subjects per dose arm (reject H0 if ≥11 of 36 respond)
- Results: SIRIUS ORR 29% (95% CI 21-39%), median DOR 7.4 months; GEN501 (16 mg/kg cohort) ORR 36% (95% CI 22-52%), median DOR 6.9 months
- FDA's clinical/statistical reviewer stated plainly that "time to event endpoints cannot be evaluated based on a single arm trial" — PFS, OS, TTP, and DOR were reported descriptively rather than as formally tested claims, and the accelerated-approval benefit-risk determination rested on the ORR/DOR results alone

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2015/761036Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2015/761036Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Clinical & Statistical Review (B.W. Miller, Y. Wang; Reference ID 3839530) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/761036Orig1s000MedR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov records — SIRIUS: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01985126, GEN501: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00574288 (no protocol/SAP posted in either Documents tab)
- Pivotal publication: Lonial S, Weiss BM, Usmani SZ, et al. "Daratumumab monotherapy in patients with treatment-refractory multiple myeloma (SIRIUS): an open-label, randomised, phase 2 trial." *Lancet.* 2016;387:1551-1560. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(15)01120-4>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26778538/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Daratumumab%20monotherapy%20in%20patients%20with%20treatment-refractory%20multiple%20myeloma%20SIRIUS)

**Other resources**

- Janssen participates in the YODA Project for IPD sharing; trial-specific availability for SIRIUS/GEN501 was not individually confirmed.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this initial application.
- Postmarketing requirements: completion of confirmatory randomized Phase III trials MMY3003 (daratumumab + lenalidomide/dexamethasone vs. Rd, "POLLUX") and/or MMY3004 (daratumumab + bortezomib/dexamethasone vs. Vd, "CASTOR") could support conversion from accelerated to regular approval.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Clinical & Statistical Review, BLA 761036, Reference ID 3839530]* — "The benefit-risk assessment supports accelerated approval under Subpart H (21 CFR 314.510) for the proposed indication... Of the 124 patients enrolled, 106 received the proposed dose and were the focus of the efficacy analysis. Patients had received a median of 5 prior treatments. Results showed that ORR was achieved by 31 (29%) patients (95% CI: 21-39%) with a median DOR of 7.4 months."

*[verbatim, same source, Sample Size Considerations, GEN501 Part 1]* — "The null hypothesis is that the ORR is at most 15%, and the alternative hypothesis is that the ORR is at least 40%. With a one-sided α of 2.5%, and a power of 85%, the total sample size within each randomized treatment group in Part 1 is 36 response-evaluable subjects... the null hypothesis will be rejected if 11 or more responses were observed."

*[verbatim, same source, Efficacy Analysis Method]* — "Reviewer comment: Time to event endpoints cannot be evaluated based on a single arm trial."

*[verbatim, same source, §12 Post-marketing Requirements]* — "Successful completion of either PMR 1 or 2 may be adequate, after review, for regular approval. PMR 1: Submit the complete final report and data showing clinical efficacy and safety from trial MMY3003, a Phase 3, 2-arm, randomized, parallel-group trial of lenalidomide and dexamethasone with or without daratumumab... PMR 2: Submit the complete final report and data showing clinical efficacy and safety from trial MMY3004, a Phase 3, 2-arm, randomized, parallel-group trial of bortezomib and dexamethasone with or without daratumumab."

Cross-reference note: unlike the two other multiple myeloma drugs in this batch (ixazomib/TOURMALINE-MM1, elotuzumab/ELOQUENT-2), daratumumab's initial 2015 approval rests on single-arm ORR data with no randomized comparator and no formal hypothesis test of a time-to-event endpoint — the statistical "SAP" here is essentially a proportion-estimation exercise (Simon's two-stage dose selection, then a fixed-sample ORR/CI), a materially different regulatory pathway (accelerated approval) from the superiority-hypothesis designs used by the other two.

### 53. Ixazomib (Ninlaro) — NDA 208462

**Sponsor:** Millennium Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (a wholly owned subsidiary of Takeda)

**Indication approved:** In combination with lenalidomide and dexamethasone, for treatment of patients with multiple myeloma who have received at least one prior therapy

**Approval date:** November 20, 2015

**Pivotal trial:** TOURMALINE-MM1 (Study C16010), NCT01564537

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, add-on design (novel agent + Rd backbone vs. placebo + Rd — same convention as elotuzumab/ELOQUENT-2 from the same approval cycle), stratified by prior therapy count, PI exposure, and ISS stage
- *Endpoints:* progression-free survival (PFS, primary, per independent review committee [IRC] using IMWG criteria), overall survival (OS, key secondary), OS in high-risk del(17) patients (key secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, stratified Cox proportional-hazards model, Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Multiplicity:* closed sequential testing procedure — OS (and OS in del(17) patients) tested only if PFS reached significance at a given analysis
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design, Lan-DeMets O'Brien-Fleming alpha-spending function for both PFS (interim ~262 events, final ~365 events) and OS (interim analyses at ~154/222/322 deaths, final at ~486 deaths)
- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented discordance between interim and final PFS results — the pre-specified first interim PFS analysis crossed the superiority boundary and supported approval, but the subsequent final PFS analysis (per protocol, intended to be non-inferential once interim superiority was declared) no longer reached significance, and investigator-assessed PFS was not significant at either analysis

**Trial design & endpoints**

- TOURMALINE-MM1 (C16010): Phase III, randomized (1:1), double-blind, multicenter trial of oral ixazomib (or placebo) added to lenalidomide + dexamethasone (Rd) in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma patients who had received ≥1 prior therapy; ~722 patients randomized via IVRS
- Randomization stratified by number of prior therapies (1 vs. 2-3), prior PI exposure (yes/no), and ISS stage (1/2 vs. 3)
- Primary endpoint: PFS by IRC assessment (IMWG criteria); with Protocol Amendment 3 (8-Jul-2014), the original single planned PFS analysis (at 234 events) was revised to add an interim PFS analysis (~262 events) ahead of a final analysis (~365 events), using a Lan-DeMets O'Brien-Fleming boundary
- Per the SAP, a closed sequential testing procedure controlled the overall two-sided alpha at 0.05 across the primary (PFS) and 2 key secondary endpoints (OS; OS in del(17) high-risk patients) — OS testing was gated on PFS reaching significance
- Result: at the first interim PFS analysis, HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.59-0.94, p=0.01; median 20.6 vs. 14.7 months) crossed the pre-specified superiority boundary (0.023, two-sided) and supported approval; at the subsequent (per-protocol non-inferential) final analysis, HR was 0.82 (95% CI 0.67-1.0, p=0.0548) and no longer significant; investigator-assessed PFS was not significant at either analysis, and the FDA statistical reviewer flagged discrepancies in event counts/censoring between the interim and final PFS datasets, concluding a "reliable estimate of the magnitude of treatment effect based on PFS could not be ascertained" despite recommending approval on the totality of evidence

### 54. Necitumumab (Portrazza) — BLA 125547

**Sponsor:** Eli Lilly and Company

**Indication approved:** In combination with gemcitabine and cisplatin, for first-line treatment of patients with metastatic squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC)

**Approval date:** November 24, 2015

**Pivotal trial:** SQUIRE (Study I4X-IE-JFCC), NCT00981058

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled, event-driven trial, stratified by ECOG PS and geographic region
- *Endpoints:* overall survival (OS, primary), progression-free survival (PFS, secondary, investigator-assessed), objective response rate (ORR, secondary), time to treatment failure (TTF, secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, stratified Cox proportional-hazards model, Kaplan-Meier estimation, Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test (ORR)
- *Multiplicity:* Hochberg's step-up procedure to adjust for multiplicity across the two secondary endpoints (PFS, ORR) tested after a significant primary OS result
- *Missing data/bias:* discordance identified between stratification data captured on the IVRS system vs. the case report form (eCRF); sensitivity analyses using each data source were consistent with the primary analysis
- *Regulatory:* FDA Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting held July 9, 2015, discussing whether SQUIRE's squamous-NSCLC efficacy/safety findings (and the premature closure of the related non-squamous INSPIRE safety trial) supported approval

**Trial design & endpoints**

- SQUIRE: Phase III, randomized (1:1), open-label, multicenter, multinational trial of necitumumab + gemcitabine/cisplatin (GC+N) vs. gemcitabine/cisplatin (GC) as first-line treatment for Stage IV squamous NSCLC (n=1093: 545 GC+N, 548 GC)
- Randomization via IVRS/IWRS, stratified permuted-block, stratified by ECOG PS (0-1 vs. 2) and geographic region (North America/Europe/Australia vs. South America/South Africa/India vs. Eastern Asia)
- Primary endpoint: OS (no interim efficacy analysis planned, only IDMC-monitored safety); secondary endpoints: investigator-assessed PFS, ORR (RECIST), and TTF
- Sample size: ≥844 OS events needed to detect HR=0.80 (11 to 13.75-month median OS increase) with 90% power, two-sided alpha=0.05, log-rank test; 1080 patients planned assuming 5% dropout
- Primary analysis: OS compared via log-rank test stratified by ECOG PS and region (IVRS-recorded), HR from a correspondingly stratified Cox model; secondary endpoints PFS/ORR tested for labeling consideration only if OS reached significance, with Hochberg's method controlling multiplicity between PFS and ORR
- Result: OS HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.74-0.96, two-sided log-rank p=0.012; median 11.5 vs. 9.9 months); PFS HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.74-0.98, p=0.02; median 5.7 vs. 5.5 months)
- A related trial (INSPIRE), evaluating necitumumab in non-squamous NSCLC (safety-focused submission data), was closed prematurely at the request of its DMC due to an imbalance in thromboembolic-event deaths in the necitumumab arm; this safety finding was specifically discussed at the July 9, 2015 ODAC meeting alongside the SQUIRE efficacy data

### 55. Elotuzumab (Empliciti) — BLA 761035

**Sponsor:** Bristol-Myers Squibb Company

**Indication approved:** In combination with lenalidomide and dexamethasone, for treatment of patients with multiple myeloma who have received one to three prior therapies

**Approval date:** November 30, 2015

**Pivotal trial:** ELOQUENT-2 (Study CA204004), NCT01239797

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled, add-on design (novel agent + Rd backbone vs. placebo + Rd — same convention as ixazomib/TOURMALINE-MM1 from the same approval cycle), mid-trial SAP amendment changing endpoint status (ORR added as a co-primary endpoint via Amendment 10, alongside the original PFS primary), stratified by β2-microglobulin, prior lines of therapy, and prior IMiD exposure
- *Endpoints:* co-primary endpoints — progression-free survival (PFS, per IRC using modified EBMT criteria) and objective response rate (ORR, per IRC); overall survival (OS, key secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test (PFS) with Cox proportional-hazards model for the HR, Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test (ORR), both stratified by the randomization factors
- *Multiplicity:* co-primary endpoints with split alpha (two-sided 0.5% for ORR, two-sided 4.5% for PFS, preserving overall two-sided 5%) plus hierarchical testing of the key secondary OS only after both co-primary endpoints were addressed
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* one planned interim PFS analysis at ≥70% of targeted PFS events (Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function, efficacy boundary 2-sided 0.0239 at 82.4% information); one planned interim OS analysis timed to follow the interim PFS analysis by ≥1 year
- *Regulatory:* mid-trial SAP amendment changing endpoint status — ORR was added as a co-primary endpoint via Protocol Amendment 10 following discussion between BMS and FDA, after the trial was already underway

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ELOQUENT-2 (CA204004): Phase III, randomized (1:1), open-label, multicenter trial of elotuzumab + lenalidomide/dexamethasone (E+Ld) vs. lenalidomide/dexamethasone alone (Ld) in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma patients with 1-3 prior therapies; 646 patients randomized (planned 640)
- Randomization stratified by β2-microglobulin (<3.5 vs. ≥3.5 mg/L), number of prior lines (1 vs. 2-3), and prior immunomodulatory drug exposure (none/thalidomide-only/other)
- Co-primary endpoints (both IRC-assessed, EBMT criteria): PFS and ORR — if either analysis reached its pre-specified significance level, the study would be declared positive; alpha was split unevenly (2-sided 0.5% for ORR, 2-sided 4.5% for PFS) so the trial was unlikely to be declared positive on the ORR result alone, and a minimum 16-month follow-up was additionally required for the ORR analysis to allow adequate assessment of duration of response
- The key secondary endpoint, OS, was tested only hierarchically after the co-primary endpoints, with a single planned interim analysis timed ≥1 year after the interim PFS analysis (or at the time of final PFS analysis if PFS was not significant at interim)
- Sample size: 640 patients gave 88.5% power to detect a 15-point ORR difference (75% vs. 60%) at 2-sided alpha=0.005, and 88.7% power to detect PFS HR=0.74 (466 targeted events) at 2-sided alpha=0.045; OS was powered at 80% for HR=0.76 (427 targeted events, 2-sided alpha=0.05)
- FDA's statistical reviewer noted that ORR was added as a co-primary endpoint via Protocol Amendment 10, following discussion between the sponsor and the Agency, after the trial had already begun — a change the reviewer characterized as unlikely to independently drive a positive study result given the small alpha allocation, but one that nonetheless altered the trial's formal primary-endpoint structure mid-conduct

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1505654), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26035255/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Elotuzumab%20Therapy%20for%20Relapsed%20or%20Refractory%20Multiple%20Myeloma)

- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this application.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Clinical & Statistical Review, BLA 761035, Reference ID 3847429]* — "ORR and PFS, both as assessed by the IRC, were the co-primary endpoints of the trial. If either of these two analyses achieved the pre-specified level of significance, the study would be declared positive. The pre-specified level of significance for ORR was 2-sided 0.5% and was 2-sided 4.5% for PFS to preserve the overall type-I error for comparing the primary endpoints at the 5% level."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "ORR was introduced into the protocol as a co-primary endpoint in 2014 following a discussion between the Applicant and the Agency. The alpha allocation for ORR was much less than the alpha allocation for PFS, so that the study was not likely to stop based solely on the ORR result... The overall study Type I error was controlled at 2-sided 0.05, by splitting the alpha between the 2 co-primary endpoints and by hierarchically testing the secondary endpoint OS after the primary endpoints."

*[verbatim, same source, Protocol Amendments]* — "Notable changes include a revision of the primary endpoint in Amendment 10. In that amendment, ORR was added to PFS as the primary endpoint. This change allowed for a positive result in either ORR or PFS to be sufficient [to declare the study positive]."

*[verbatim, same source, Statistical Analysis Plan]* — "The primary analysis of ORR compared the two treatment arms using the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by the treatment randomization factors. The primary analysis of PFS compared the two treatment arms via the log-rank test stratified by the treatment randomization factors."

Cross-reference note: elotuzumab (ELOQUENT-2) and ixazomib (TOURMALINE-MM1), approved 10 days apart in November 2015, share the same basic trial architecture — a novel agent added to a lenalidomide/dexamethasone backbone versus placebo + Rd, with IRC-assessed PFS as (co-)primary and OS hierarchically gated behind it — but differ in exactly how each handled multiplicity: ELOQUENT-2 split alpha across two co-primary endpoints (PFS and ORR) declared via an OR-rule, while TOURMALINE-MM1 used a single primary endpoint (PFS) with OS/OS-in-del(17) gated in a closed sequential procedure. Daratumumab's contemporaneous single-arm accelerated approval (BLA 761036, above) used neither convention.

### 56. Alectinib (Alecensa) — NDA 208434

**Sponsor:** Hoffmann-La Roche (Genentech)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of patients with anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK)-positive, metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who have progressed on or are intolerant to crizotinib

**Approval date:** December 11, 2015

**Pivotal trial:** Pooled analysis of NP28761, NCT01871805, and NP28673, NCT01801111 (two single-arm Phase I/II trials)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial, pooled analysis of two independently-conducted single-arm Phase I/II trials for accelerated-approval review; biomarker-selected/enriched population (ALK-positive NSCLC, post-crizotinib)

- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR) per independent review committee (IRC) using RECIST v1.1 as primary endpoint in both trials; duration of response (DoR), CNS ORR (CORR) and CNS DoR (CDoR) as secondary endpoints; in NP28673, ORR in patients with prior chemotherapy (ORR-PC) as an additional co-primary endpoint

- *Primary analysis:* exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval

- *Interim/alpha-spending:* non-binding interim futility analysis on the first 30 patients based on an 80% CI around the observed investigator-assessed ORR (ad hoc rule replacing an earlier Simon's two-stage design specified in Protocol V1-V4)

- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval based on pooled ORR/DoR from single-arm trials, confirmatory trial required; FDA and sponsor agreed by protocol amendment to lower the pre-specified null-hypothesis ORR threshold from 50% to 35% before the primary analysis

**Trial design & endpoints**

- NP28761 (two-part, dose-finding + activity-estimating, open-label, multicenter) and NP28673 (three-part: dose-finding, activity-estimating, access) both enrolled ALK-positive NSCLC patients who had progressed on or were intolerant to crizotinib; activity-estimating cohorts were N=87 (NP28761) and N=138 (NP28673), both dosed at alectinib 600 mg BID

- Primary endpoint in both trials was ORR per IRC assessment using RECIST v1.1; secondary endpoints included DoR, CORR, and CDoR (assessed using both RECIST and RANO criteria for CNS lesions per FDA's November 2013 request)

- Sample size for NP28761 (N=85) was chosen so that, under an assumed 46% observed ORR, the two-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson CI lower bound would exceed the pre-specified null threshold of 35% (originally 50% in Protocol V1, revised in Protocol V5, March 8, 2013); FDA agreed to this ORR=35% null hypothesis in a September 30, 2014 Type B meeting

- Results: NP28673 ORR 44.2% (95% CI: 35.8%, 52.9%) per IRC in the activity-estimating cohort (N=138), ORR-PC 39% (95% CI: 30%, 49%); NP28761 ORR 38% (95% CI: 28%, 49%) (N=87); pooled measurable-CNS-lesion ORR 61% (95% CI: 46%, 74%) across both trials — all lower CI bounds exceeded the pre-specified 35% threshold

- A postmarketing requirement (confirmatory trial, final report due June 2018) required at least one multicenter, randomized clinical trial establishing superiority of alectinib over available therapy in metastatic ALK-positive NSCLC; this became the Phase III ALEX trial (NCT02075840), which supported alectinib's subsequent full approval for first-line ALK-positive NSCLC in November 2017

### 57. Atezolizumab (Tecentriq) — BLA 761034

**Sponsor:** Genentech, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of patients with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma who have disease progression during or following platinum-containing chemotherapy, or within 12 months of neoadjuvant or adjuvant platinum-containing chemotherapy

**Approval date:** May 18, 2016

**Pivotal trial:** IMvigor210 (Study GO29293), Cohort 2, NCT02108652

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial (Cohort 2 of a two-cohort Phase II study); PD-L1 tumor-infiltrating-immune-cell (IC) subgroup enrichment analysis, with the PD-L1 (SP142) IHC assay used as a complementary (not mandatory) diagnostic

- *Endpoints:* confirmed ORR as assessed by an Independent Review Facility (IRF) per RECIST v1.1 (primary) and by investigator per modified immune-related RECIST (co-primary); DOR and PFS (IRF-assessed, key secondary), OS (secondary)

- *Primary analysis:* exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval; descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (point estimate + CI, no formal hypothesis test) — FDA's reviewers explicitly declined to report inferential p-values against the assumed historical control given its uncertainty

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing of ORR against an assumed 10% historical response rate across three pre-specified populations (PD-L1 IC2/3, then IC1/2/3, then the intent-to-treat population), each tested at a two-sided alpha of 0.05

- *Interim/alpha-spending:* non-binding futility interim analysis in the PD-L1 IC0/1 subgroup after the first 100 patients (stopping boundary: unconfirmed investigator-assessed ORR ≤5%), monitored by an IDMC

- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval based on ORR/DoR in a single-arm trial, confirmatory trial required; this accelerated-approval indication was voluntarily withdrawn by Genentech in April 2021 (BLA 761034/S-041) after the confirmatory Phase III trial (GO29294/IMvigor211, a postmarketing requirement) did not verify an overall-survival benefit — voluntary post-approval withdrawal of an accelerated-approval indication after a negative confirmatory trial

**Trial design & endpoints**

- IMvigor210 Cohort 2: international, multicenter, single-arm, open-label Phase II trial of atezolizumab 1200 mg IV every 3 weeks in locally advanced/metastatic urothelial carcinoma patients who progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy; 310 treated patients out of 315 enrolled

- Co-primary endpoints: confirmed ORR by IRF per RECIST v1.1 and confirmed ORR by investigator per modified (immune-related) RECIST, both analyzed by intent-to-treat; PD-L1 expression on tumor-infiltrating immune cells (IC0 <1%, IC1 ≥1%-<5%, IC2/3 ≥5%) was assessed prospectively at a central laboratory

- Design assumed a historical control ORR of 10% in second-line advanced urothelial carcinoma (based on published literature) and enrolled ~300 patients (~100 expected IC2/3) to test observed ORR against that threshold hierarchically across the IC2/3, IC1/2/3, and all-patient populations

- Results: confirmed ORR (IRF, RECIST v1.1) was 14.8% (95% CI: 11.1%, 19.3%) in all 310 patients; 26.0% (95% CI: 17.7%, 35.7%) in the 100 IC2/3 patients; 9.5% (95% CI: 5.9%, 14.3%) in the 210 IC0/1 patients; median DOR was not reached (range 2.1+ to 13.8+ months), with 80% (37/46) of responders having ongoing responses ≥6 months

- FDA's statistical/clinical reviewers stated explicitly: "In general, a clinically meaningful effect on response rate with a reasonable duration of response and an acceptable safety profile can be considered for regulatory evaluation and approval," while separately noting that, "for a single-arm, open-label study, a detected statistical significance, as compared to the debatable historical control, may not represent a true clinical improvement. Therefore, no statistical tests and P-values will be reported in this review."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Clinical & Statistical Review, BLA 761034, Reference ID 3924918]* — "This single-arm study was designed to characterize ORR in all study patients and to examine whether there was a statistically difference between the observed ORR and an assumed historical response rate of 10% in patients with advanced urothelial carcinoma. Cohort 2 planned to enroll approximately 300 patients, assuming a 30% prevalence rate of IC2/3 patients (n~100) in the overall locally advanced or metastatic UBC population. Comparison of ORR between atezolizumab treatment and the assumed historical response rate was to be tested for three patient populations using a hierarchical fixed-sequence procedure."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "The exact 95% CIs using the Clopper-Pearson method for ORR were calculated... DOR was calculated as the time from the initial occurrence of documented CR or PR (whichever occurred first) until documented disease progression or death due to any cause... the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the median DOR was to be presented; along with the 95% CIs computed using the Brookmeyer and Crowley method."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "A futility interim analysis on the IC0/1 patients was planned after the first 100 patients had at least 18 weeks of follow-up. The futility interim analysis was based on the unconfirmed ORR as assessed by the investigator per RECIST 1.1. The stopping boundary was set as 5%. If the stopping boundary for futility was crossed (i.e., ORR ≤5%) at the interim analysis, the IDMC could recommend stopping recruitment of IC0/1 patients."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "The review team considered the ITT population as the primary efficacy analysis population for ORR analyses. The presumed historical ORR control of 10% for the statistical test is debatable in patients with advanced urothelial carcinoma... For a single-arm, open-label study, a detected statistical significance, as compared to the debatable historical control, may not represent a true clinical improvement. Therefore, no statistical tests and P-values will be reported in this review."

*[verbatim, same source, §4.6 Devices and Companion Diagnostic Issues]* — "Based on the clinical evidence presented in this BLA, the CDRH review team is in agreement with the clinical review team that the PD-L1 (SP142) assay should be used as a complementary [diagnostic]... Due to the design of Study GO 29293 (all patients received atezolizumab without a control), it is not possible to assess whether the associations between PD-L1 IC status and ORR are prognostic and/or predictive of responses in advanced urothelial carcinoma."

*[verbatim, FDA Clinical & Statistical Review, §12 Postmarketing Requirements and Commitments]* — "Conduct 'GO29294: A Phase III, Open-label, Multicenter, Randomized Study to Investigate the Efficacy and Safety of Atezolizumab Compared with Chemotherapy in Patients with Locally Advanced or Metastatic Urothelial Bladder Cancer After Failure with Platinum-containing Chemotherapy' and provide a study report, datasets, and, if appropriate, revised labeling." GO29294 is publicly known as IMvigor211; its confirmatory result did not verify the overall-survival benefit, and Genentech subsequently requested removal of this indication (BLA 761034/S-041, approved April 14, 2021 per the supplement approval letter's PDF metadata).

### 58. Fluciclovine F 18 (Axumin) — NDA 208054

**Sponsor:** Blue Earth Diagnostics, Ltd.

**Indication approved:** PET imaging agent indicated for men with suspected prostate cancer recurrence based on elevated prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels following prior treatment

**Approval date:** May 27, 2016

**Pivotal trial:** Retrospective re-analyses (Blue Earth Diagnostics studies BED-001 and BED-002) of an investigator-initiated Emory University study, "Study R01," NCT00562315, with a comparator series from the University of Bologna

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison); retrospective sponsor re-analysis of data from independently-conducted, investigator-initiated academic studies not originally designed as registration trials — the sponsor acquired rights to re-analyze data from a published Emory University study (Schuster et al. 2014) and a published University of Bologna comparator series (Nanni et al. 2015), rather than conducting a prospective company-sponsored pivotal trial

- *Endpoints:* positive predictive value (PPV) at the subject level (sponsor's primary endpoint); "modified sensitivity," a non-standard, post hoc-constructed measure defined as the proportion of subjects with a standard-of-truth (SOT)-positive lesion who were also fluciclovine-positive

- *Primary analysis:* no taxonomy term precisely fits; FDA's statistical reviewer computed one-sided 97.5% confidence interval lower limits for PPV and for "modified sensitivity" at the subject level, but explicitly noted the absence of a reference standard independent of the test itself (verification bias) as a fundamental limitation on any performance-measure calculation

- *Missing data/bias:* verification bias explicitly flagged by the FDA reviewer — "Sensitivity" and "Specificity," as defined in this study, could not be interpreted as standard diagnostic-performance measures because the standard of truth (biopsy-directed histology) was itself directed by the imaging results being evaluated

**Trial design & endpoints**

- This NDA was "primarily a retrospective evaluation" (FDA Statistical Review) of two existing academic data sets rather than a prospective, sponsor-run pivotal trial: the Emory Study (R01, published as Schuster et al., *J Urol* 2014, comparing fluciclovine F 18 PET-CT to ¹¹¹In-capromab pendetide SPECT-CT), and a comparator series from the University of Bologna (published as Nanni et al., *Clin Nucl Med* 2015, comparing fluciclovine to ¹¹C-choline PET/CT)

- Patients had rising PSA after primary prostate cancer therapy, suggestive of recurrence; per FDA's review, "there is no SOT that evaluates the subject's status independently of histology evaluations of lesions detected by test, control, and other images or methods that direct biopsies," meaning true sensitivity/specificity could not be calculated in the standard sense

- The sponsor's chosen primary endpoint was PPV at the subject level; because PPV alone is affected by disease prevalence (70% in this cohort) and does not penalize under-detection, FDA's reviewer added "modified sensitivity" as a companion statistic, and — at FDA's recommendation — the sponsor conducted a blinded re-read of the Emory images by three independent readers (naive to clinical information and to the original SOT) to mitigate reader bias, since the on-site reads had been performed with full access to biopsy/clinical data

- Results (Emory data, on-site read vs. three blinded re-reads): PPV ranged from roughly 79% (on-site, lower 97.5% CI limit 71%) to slightly lower with blinded reads; modified sensitivity was approximately 99% (lower 97.5% CI limit 97%) on-site, generally high but variable across blinded readers; FDA's reviewer noted that PPV and sensitivity/PPV estimates "markedly decreased when the reader were unaware of patient clinical information," underscoring the dependence of the observed performance on non-blinded interpretation

- This was a standard (regular) NDA approval, not an accelerated approval; the FDA approval letter contains no accelerated-approval or subpart-H language, despite the unusually thin, retrospective, investigator-initiated evidentiary base — a notable departure from the randomized/prospective evidence typical of the other entries in this batch

- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this application.

**Reverse-engineered SAP** *[inferred]*

- *[inferred, from FDA Statistical Review §1.2 and §3]* Because this was a retrospective re-analysis of pre-existing, already-unblinded academic data (the sponsor "already knew the results including the histological standard of truth"), no prospective sponsor SAP predating outcome-knowledge exists for the primary Emory dataset; the closest analogue — the blinded three-reader re-analysis (BED-002) — was itself an FDA-recommended post hoc addition to reduce (not eliminate) the read-bias inherent in the original on-site interpretation.

- *[inferred, from the label's Clinical Studies section describing "Study A/B/C"]* The final approved label organizes the evidence as three studies (A = the Emory/VUMC-analogous BED-001 reanalysis, n=97/78 evaluable; B and C = the published Bologna-type comparator series, n=104 and n=63), each using a different, study-specific reference standard (histopathology and/or clinical follow-up), implying the SAP-level analysis was necessarily conducted separately per data source rather than under a single harmonized prospective protocol.

### 59. Gallium Ga 68 dotatate (Netspot) — NDA 208547

**Sponsor:** Advanced Accelerator Applications

**Indication approved:** PET imaging agent for localization of somatostatin receptor-positive neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) in adult and pediatric patients

**Approval date:** June 1, 2016

**Pivotal trial:** Vanderbilt University Medical Center (VUMC) prospective single-center study, NCT01396382 (labeled "Study A"), plus two previously-published single-center studies ("Study B" and "Study C")

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison); primary evidentiary basis was a single-center prospective diagnostic-accuracy study (VUMC) plus two published single-center studies, rather than a single multi-site pivotal trial; sponsor also submitted a literature meta-analysis that the FDA statistical reviewer explicitly rejected as an inadequate basis for a regulatory performance estimate

- *Endpoints:* patient-level sensitivity and specificity of Ga 68 dotatate PET versus a reference standard/standard of truth (histopathology and/or ¹¹¹In-pentetreotide SPECT plus CT/MRI and clinical follow-up, varying by study)

- *Primary analysis:* no taxonomy term precisely fits; performance-measure analysis without an independent reference standard, subject to verification bias — the VUMC study's inclusion criterion required a pre-existing NET diagnosis, which FDA's reviewer noted made "the existence of true negatives within the study difficult to interpret"

- *Missing data/bias:* FDA's statistical reviewer found most of the sponsor's meta-analysis component studies contained no true-negative patients, writing that "a study of diagnostic performance should include both truly positive and truly negative patients in order to provide performance estimates that can be evaluated in context," and that the meta-analysis "should not be considered in the evaluation of 68 Ga-DODATATE for regulatory purposes because the component studies are inadequate for the purpose"

**Trial design & endpoints**

- "Study A" (VUMC 2015): sponsor-described prospective, single-center, open-label Phase I/II study; 97 patients with known/suspected neuroendocrine tumors enrolled, 78 included in the primary analysis set after excluding 19 patients without a viable comparator (¹¹¹In-pentetreotide) scan; images read by consensus with third-reader adjudication

- Sponsor-reported estimates (VUMC): Ga 68 dotatate sensitivity 96.0% (95% CI: 86.3%, 99.5%), specificity 92.9% (95% CI: 76.5%, 99.1%); comparator ¹¹¹In-pentetreotide sensitivity 72.0% (95% CI: 57.5%, 83.8%), specificity 89.3% (95% CI: 71.8%, 97.7%) — FDA's reviewer flagged that the reference standard was "not well defined... because the inclusion criterion... requires a patient to be known to have NET to enter the study making the existence of true negatives within the study difficult to interpret"

- "Study B" (published, likely corresponding to Haug AR et al., *J Nucl Med* 2012, cited by FDA's reviewer as supporting "the presence of NET" indication) and "Study C" (published, corresponding to Haug AR et al., *Radiology* 2014, cited as supporting the NET-recurrence indication) each used consensus or independent-reader interpretation against a histopathology/clinical-follow-up reference standard; per the approved label, Study B enrolled 104 patients (36 reference-standard-positive; 29 true positives, 7 false negatives; of 68 reference-standard-negative, 61 true negatives, 7 false positives) and Study C enrolled 63 patients (two independent blinded readers correctly localizing NETs in 23/29 and 22/29 reference-standard-positive patients, respectively)

- Of an 8-study sponsor meta-analysis, FDA's reviewer found 4 studies (Haug 2009, Alonso 2014, Kayani 2008, Wild 2013) included no true-negative patients at all, and rejected the meta-analysis's pooled sensitivity (90%, 95% CI 86-100%) and pooled specificity (90%, 95% CI 84%-?) as an invalid regulatory basis, stating plainly that "whether the evaluable studies are adequate to support the indication is a clinical determination" resting instead on the individual VUMC/Haug studies

- This was a standard (regular) NDA approval, not an accelerated approval; there is no subpart-H or accelerated-approval language in the FDA approval letter, despite FDA's own statistical reviewer disqualifying the sponsor's primary proposed analysis (the meta-analysis) as inadequate — an unusually candid instance of a reviewer rejecting the sponsor's stated primary analysis outright while still recommending approval on narrower grounds

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.2967/jnumed.111.101675), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22984220/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=The%20role%20of%2068Ga-DOTATATE%20PET%2FCT%20in%20suspected%20neuroendocrine%20tumors)

### 60. Olaratumab (Lartruvo) — BLA 761038

**Sponsor:** Eli Lilly and Company

**Indication approved:** In combination with doxorubicin, for the treatment of adult patients with soft tissue sarcoma (STS) with a histologic subtype for which an anthracycline-containing regimen is appropriate and which is not amenable to curative treatment with radiotherapy or surgery

**Approval date:** October 19, 2016

**Pivotal trial:** Trial JGDG (Study I5B-IE-JGDG), NCT01185964; confirmatory trial ANNOUNCE (Study I5B-MC-JGDJ), NCT02451943

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized (1:1), open-label, active-controlled Phase Ib/II "activity-estimating" trial (JGDG), randomization via dynamic minimization stratified by PDGFR-α expression, prior lines of treatment, histologic subtype, and ECOG status; confirmatory ANNOUNCE trial was randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled with a dual-primary-population design (total STS population + leiomyosarcoma [LMS] subpopulation), using a graphical alpha-propagation multiple-testing procedure (Maurer and Bretz 2013)

- *Endpoints:* PFS by investigator per RECIST v1.1 (JGDG primary endpoint); OS (JGDG secondary endpoint, tested with no pre-specified multiplicity control; ANNOUNCE dual-primary endpoint in both the total-STS and LMS populations)

- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test and stratified Cox proportional-hazards model for JGDG PFS; unstratified Cox model/log-rank test for JGDG OS; stratified log-rank test for ANNOUNCE OS in each primary population, with an unstratified log-rank test as a sensitivity analysis

- *Multiplicity:* JGDG PFS was tested at a pre-specified, non-standard adjusted two-sided alpha of 0.1999 (reflecting the trial's small, "activity-estimating" Phase II intent); JGDG's OS analysis had "no pre-specified plan for controlling type I error"; ANNOUNCE used a weighted, recycling graphical testing procedure initially splitting one-sided alpha 0.025 as 0.005 (LMS OS) / 0.02 (ITT OS), with the weight of edges set via an ε=0.001 parameter so that rejecting either primary hypothesis passed essentially all remaining alpha to the other, followed by fixed-sequence testing of PFS then ORR

- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval based on a small, open-label, randomized Phase Ib/II "activity-estimating" trial that was not designed as a registration study; FDA required a confirmatory Phase III trial (ANNOUNCE) as a condition of accelerated approval; ANNOUNCE failed to verify an OS benefit (total STS: HR 1.05 [95% CI 0.84-1.30], p=0.69; LMS: HR 0.95 [95% CI 0.69-1.31], p=0.76), and Eli Lilly requested withdrawal (revocation) of the BLA under 21 CFR 601.5(a) on September 27, 2019; FDA published the Federal Register notice revoking the license on July 17, 2020

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Trial JGDG: multicenter, open-label, randomized (1:1) Phase Ib/II trial of doxorubicin plus olaratumab (15 mg/kg IV Days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle) versus doxorubicin alone (75 mg/m² Day 1) in advanced STS patients naive to anthracyclines, with crossover to single-agent olaratumab offered to control-arm patients at progression; randomization stratified via dynamic minimization by PDGFR-α expression, prior lines of treatment, histologic subtype (leiomyosarcoma vs. synovial sarcoma vs. all others), and ECOG status

- JGDG primary endpoint was investigator-assessed PFS per RECIST v1.1, sized for 130 patients/110 events assuming HR 0.67 (2- vs. 3-month median PFS) to provide 80% power at a two-sided alpha of 0.20 (reflecting its Phase II "activity-estimating" design); OS was a secondary endpoint tested at a nominal two-sided alpha of 0.05 with, per FDA's reviewer, "no pre-specified plan for controlling type I error in testing of the secondary efficacy endpoints"

- JGDG results: median PFS 6.6 vs. 4.1 months (stratified HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.44-1.02, two-sided p=0.06) — meeting its pre-specified 0.1999 significance threshold; median OS 26.5 vs. 14.7 months (unstratified HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.34-0.79, p<0.05); confirmed ORR by BICR 18.2% vs. 7.5%

- ANNOUNCE (confirmatory trial, required as a condition of accelerated approval): randomized 1:1, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trial (n=509: 258 olaratumab, 251 placebo) of doxorubicin plus olaratumab/placebo, with dual-primary objectives of OS in (1) the total advanced/metastatic STS population and (2) the LMS subpopulation, using a graphical multiple-testing procedure (initial one-sided alpha split 0.005 LMS/0.02 ITT, ε=0.001) that, after rejection of either primary hypothesis, passed nearly all remaining alpha to the other and then gated PFS and ORR in fixed sequence

- ANNOUNCE results (published 2020): no statistically significant OS difference in either population — total STS HR 1.05 (95% CI 0.84-1.30), p=0.69, median OS 20.4 vs. 19.7 months; LMS HR 0.95 (95% CI 0.69-1.31), p=0.76, median OS 21.6 vs. 21.9 months — "did not confirm the overall survival benefit observed in the phase 2 trial"

For the Phase 2 portion, assuming a hazard ratio of 0.67 with a median PFS of 2 months in the control arm and 3 months in the experimental arm, a total of 130 patients with 110 events for the final analysis were needed to provide 80% power at a two-sided alpha level of 20%. Overall survival (OS), a secondary endpoint, was to be tested at a two-sided alpha level of 5%. There was no pre-specified plan for controlling type I error in testing of the secondary efficacy endpoints."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "Trial JGDG met its primary endpoint based on the pre-specified, adjusted significance level of 0.1999 (two-sided)... a stratified HR of 0.67 (95% CI: 0.44, 1.02; two-sided p-value of 0.06)... Patients randomized to receive olaratumab plus doxorubicin demonstrated significantly improved OS... an unstratified HR of 0.52 (95% CI: 0.34, 0.79; p-value <0.05)."

*[verbatim, same source, §Regulatory Background]* — "FDA stated if interim results were to be provided, adequate information to assess the robustness of the preliminary clinical data with regard to the treatment effects of olaratumab on PFS and OS should be provided including the statistical analysis plan for the trial to provide details of the pre-specified analyses of the primary endpoint, including censoring rules for PFS as well as the plan for Type I error adjustment for interim analyses, sensitivity analyses for PFS based on histological subtype of sarcoma, and analyses to assess for investigator bias in an open-label trial with a primary endpoint of investigator-assessed PFS."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "As a condition of the accelerated approval, the applicant must verify and describe the clinical benefit of olaratumab. A multicenter, double-blind, randomized controlled trial has completely enrolled and is ongoing to confirm the clinical benefit of olaratumab in combination with doxorubicin in patients with metastatic STS that is not amenable to curative treatment with surgery or radiation."

*[verbatim, ANNOUNCE Statistical Analysis Plan (I5B-MC-JGDJ, Version 3), posted on ClinicalTrials.gov, §4.1/§5.11]* — "The primary objective is to compare doxorubicin plus olaratumab versus doxorubicin plus placebo with respect to overall survival (OS) in 2 populations: (1) Patients with advanced or metastatic soft tissue sarcoma (STS)... (2) Patients with advanced or metastatic leiomyosarcoma (LMS)..." — "For the primary comparison of OS, the primary endpoint, between the assigned study treatment arms, a stratified log-rank test will be performed... An unstratified log-rank test will also be performed as sensitivity analysis."

*[verbatim, same source, Table JGDJ.5.5]* — "Initially, the overall one-sided alpha of 0.025 is split between the primary objectives of OS in the LMS population (H11) and OS in the ITT population (H12), with H11 tested at a one-sided α1=0.005 and H12 tested at a one-sided α2=0.02... the weight of the line from H11 to H12 is 1, indicating that H12 receives all of the alpha allotted to H11 if H11 is rejected, and similarly, the weight of the line from H12 to H11 is 1-ε, where ε is set equal to 0.001... After rejecting H11 and/or H12, further testing essentially becomes a gatekeeping strategy to assess PFS and ORR in fixed sequence."

*[verbatim, JAMA 2020, PMID 32259228, Results/Conclusions]* — "No statistically significant difference in overall survival was observed between the doxorubicin plus olaratumab group vs the doxorubicin plus placebo group in either population (total STS: hazard ratio, 1.05 [95% CI, 0.84-1.30], P=.69... LMS: hazard ratio, 0.95 [95% CI, 0.69-1.31], P=.76)... The findings did not confirm the overall survival benefit observed in the phase 2 trial."

*[verbatim, Federal Register notice 2020-15516]* — "On September 27, 2019, Eli Lilly requested withdrawal (revocation), in writing, of the BLA for LARTRUVO (olaratumab) injection (BLA 761038) under § 601.5(a) (21 CFR 601.5(a)) because the ANNOUNCE trial failed to demonstrate improvement in overall survival for olaratumab in combination with [doxorubicin]."

### 61. Rucaparib (Rubraca) — NDA 209115

**Sponsor:** Clovis Oncology, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Monotherapy treatment of patients with deleterious BRCA mutation (germline and/or somatic)-associated advanced ovarian cancer who have been treated with two or more chemotherapies

**Approval date:** December 19, 2016

**Pivotal trial:** Pooled analysis of Study 10 (CO-338-010), NCT01482715, and ARIEL2 (CO-338-017), NCT01891344 (both single-arm trials)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial; pooled analysis of patient subsets from two independently-conducted single-arm trials for accelerated-approval review; companion diagnostic co-approval (FoundationFocus CDx BRCA, a next-generation-sequencing tissue assay)

- *Endpoints:* investigator-assessed confirmed ORR per RECIST v1.1 (primary), with independent radiology review (IRR) as a supportive analysis; duration of response (DoR, key secondary, investigator-assessed with IRR support)

- *Primary analysis:* descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (point estimate + CI, no formal hypothesis test)

- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval based on ORR/DoR in single-arm trials, confirmatory trial required; two confirmatory Phase III trials required as postmarketing requirements — ARIEL4 (CO-338-043, randomized rucaparib-vs-chemotherapy treatment trial) and ARIEL3 (CO-338-014, randomized maintenance trial) — reflecting that the confirmatory-evidence requirement was satisfied across both a treatment-setting and a maintenance-setting trial rather than a single like-for-like confirmatory study

**Trial design & endpoints**

- The primary rucaparib efficacy population (N=106) was pooled from patients across five trial sections of two ongoing, international, multicenter, single-arm, open-label Phase I/II trials: Study 10 Part 2A (N=42, all gBRCA-mutated by local lab testing) and ARIEL2 Part 1 (N=24) and Part 2 (N=40, both tBRCA-mutated by central assay or local lab), all having received ≥2 prior chemotherapy regimens including ≥2 platinum-based regimens

- Primary efficacy endpoint was confirmed ORR (CR or PR per RECIST v1.1, confirmed at a subsequent tumor assessment ≥28 days later) as assessed by investigator, with IRR as a supportive analysis to mitigate potential open-label investigator bias; DoR (investigator-assessed, IRR-supported) was a key secondary measure

- FDA's reviewer noted: "This NDA is based on data from two different trials, and the analyses for the combined studies were agreed upon in a pre-NDA meeting. Standard SAS procedures were used for performing analyses," and that "the data provided by the applicant allowed replication of the primary efficacy and key secondary results"

- Results: confirmed ORR 54% (95% CI: 44%, 64%) in the pooled 106-patient efficacy population (9% CR, 45% PR); median DoR 9.2 months (95% CI: 6.6, 11.6); investigator-assessed ORR was 66% (52/79) in the platinum-sensitive subgroup; ORR was similar across BRCA1 vs. BRCA2 mutation carriers

- Reviewer's comment on potential bias: "The potential for the introduction of bias into objective response and PFS determination as per investigator (INV) in this single-arm trial was mitigated by incorporation of independent radiologic review (IRR) of trial imaging studies, which generally supported the investigator analysis... there were some discrepancies between INV and IRR that underwent further scrutiny during the FDA analysis, but which did not reveal overt systematic bias on the part of the investigator"
