### 62. Telotristat ethyl (Xermelo) — NDA 208794

**Sponsor:** Lexicon Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** In combination with somatostatin analog (SSA) therapy, for treatment of adults with carcinoid syndrome diarrhea inadequately controlled by SSA therapy alone

**Approval date:** February 28, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** TELESTAR (LX1606.1-301-CS / LX301), NCT01677910, and TELECAST (LX1606.1-303-CS / LX303), NCT02063659

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, add-on trials (background SSA therapy continued in all arms); two companion Phase III trials with different enrollment criteria and different primary objectives (TELESTAR enrolled patients with ≥4 bowel movements/day on stable-dose SSA; TELECAST enrolled patients with less-frequent symptoms, with or without SSA)

- *Endpoints:* change from baseline in bowel-movement (BM) frequency/day averaged over the 12-week double-blind period (TELESTAR primary endpoint; TELECAST secondary, not included in its multiple-testing procedure); percent change from baseline in 24-hour urinary 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (u5-HIAA) at Week 12 (TELECAST primary endpoint; TELESTAR secondary endpoint, included in its multiple-testing procedure)

- *Primary analysis:* stratified Wilcoxon rank-sum test (block, two-sample), stratified by baseline u5-HIAA level, with the Hodges-Lehmann estimator of location shift and associated confidence limits

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing within each dose-vs-placebo contrast in TELESTAR (two comparisons, 250 mg and 500 mg vs. placebo, each at a two-sided 0.025 significance level); in TELECAST, sequential (hierarchical) testing of the 500 mg-vs-placebo comparison before the 250 mg-vs-placebo comparison on the primary u5-HIAA endpoint, with no multiplicity adjustment for its other secondary endpoints (unadjusted secondary/supportive testing)

- *Missing data/bias:* in TELESTAR's primary analysis, change from baseline in BM frequency was imputed as zero for a diary-week if the patient had ≥6 weeks of missing diary data (a "missing week" defined as ≥4 missing diary days); otherwise the mean response was computed only from valid non-missing days

**Trial design & endpoints**

- TELESTAR (LX301): Phase III, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, three-arm (telotristat 250 mg, 500 mg, placebo) trial in patients with carcinoid syndrome experiencing >4 BMs/day on stable-dose SSA therapy; primary objective was to confirm reduction in BM frequency/day versus placebo, with change in u5-HIAA at Week 12 as a secondary endpoint included in the multiplicity procedure

- TELECAST (LX303), the companion study, enrolled patients either on SSA with <4 BMs/day and ≥1 CS symptom, or off SSA with ≥1 CS symptom; its primary objectives were safety/tolerability and the u5-HIAA endpoint, with BM frequency as one of six secondary endpoints not included in its multiple-testing procedure

- Both trials used the intent-to-treat population for efficacy analyses; the pre-specified primary analysis in each was the blocked two-sample Wilcoxon rank-sum statistic stratified by baseline u5-HIAA level (≤ULN, >ULN, unknown), with the Hodges-Lehmann estimator and CLs reported, and the same method applied to secondary endpoints

- Results: in TELESTAR, both doses were statistically significantly different from placebo on both BM frequency and u5-HIAA (nominal p<0.01, no multiplicity adjustment mentioned needed since results were significant at both doses); in TELECAST, both doses were statistically significantly different from placebo on the primary u5-HIAA endpoint; FDA's reviewer noted that baseline u5-HIAA levels were imbalanced across the three TELESTAR arms (stratified Wilcoxon overall p=0.04), complicating interpretation of the u5-HIAA treatment effect despite confirming the sponsor's primary BM-frequency result

### 63. Ribociclib (Kisqali) — NDA 209092

**Sponsor:** Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation

**Indication approved:** In combination with an aromatase inhibitor, for the treatment of postmenopausal women with hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer, as initial endocrine-based therapy

**Approval date:** March 13, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** MONALEESA-2 (Study CLEE011A2301), NCT01958021

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven trial, stratified by presence of liver and/or lung metastases

- *Endpoints:* investigator-assessed PFS per RECIST v1.1 (primary endpoint); OS (key secondary endpoint)

- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, stratified Cox proportional-hazards model, Kaplan-Meier estimation

- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design with a single planned interim PFS efficacy analysis (changed by protocol amendment from two planned interim analyses using an O'Brien-Fleming boundary to a single interim analysis at 70% information using a Haybittle-Peto boundary with a minimum hazard-ratio stopping threshold of 0.56); planned interim/final OS analyses at 100, 300, and 400 events

- *Regulatory:* FDA suggested the Haybittle-Peto stopping-boundary/HR-threshold change specifically "to provide consistent advice across the CDK 4/6 drug class" — FDA-directed cross-class harmonization of an interim stopping-boundary choice

**Trial design & endpoints**

- MONALEESA-2 (Study CLEE011A2301): international, multicenter, randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trial of ribociclib plus letrozole versus placebo plus letrozole as first-line therapy in postmenopausal women with HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer; 334 patients per arm (668 total), randomization stratified by presence of liver and/or lung metastases; conducted at 223 sites in 29 countries

- Originally designed to enroll 500 patients (88.5% power for HR 0.67, 9.0 vs. 13.4-month median PFS); amended (Amendment 2, November 24, 2014) to 650 patients to increase power for the secondary OS endpoint, raising primary-endpoint power to 93.5%; primary PFS analysis planned at 302 events

- Interim analysis plan was originally two looks (152 and 243 events) under an O'Brien-Fleming boundary; Amendment 3 (April 9, 2015) changed this to a single interim analysis at 211 events (70% information) under a Haybittle-Peto boundary with a minimum HR stopping threshold of 0.56, which FDA's reviewer stated was "suggested by the agency in order to provide consistent advice across the CDK 4/6 drug class"

- Primary and secondary endpoints were tested via stratified log-rank test at a one-sided alpha of 2.5%; the trial was stopped early for superior efficacy at the single interim PFS analysis (data cutoff January 29, 2016); a second interim OS analysis occurred at 100 events (per Amendment 5, December 21, 2016) to provide updated data to regulators, with a planned third interim analysis at 300 events and final analysis at 400 events

### 64. Avelumab (Bavencio) — BLA 761049

**Sponsor:** EMD Serono, Inc. (Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adults and pediatric patients 12 years and older with metastatic Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC)

**Approval date:** March 23, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** JAVELIN Merkel 200 (Study EMR 100070-003 / "Study 003"), NCT02155647

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial, two-stage group-sequential design (futility interim + efficacy interim)

- *Endpoints:* confirmed best overall response (BOR) by Independent Endpoint Review Committee (IERC) per RECIST v1.1 (primary endpoint, ORR = proportion with confirmed CR/PR); DOR, PFS (IERC-assessed), and OS (secondary)

- *Primary analysis:* exact binomial test against a pre-specified performance goal (null ORR ≤20%, alternative ORR >20%, one-sided alpha 0.025); Clopper-Pearson confidence interval, repeated-CI method for the two-stage group-sequential design (Jennison and Turnbull)

- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design with a non-binding futility interim analysis after 20 patients (≥3 months' follow-up; enrollment paused for SMC review if there were no unconfirmed responses) and an efficacy interim analysis after 56 patients (6 months later; nominal one-sided p-value threshold 0.0045, with the primary analysis at 6 months post-last-patient-enrolled allocated the remaining alpha of 0.0205)

- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval based on ORR/DoR in a single-arm trial, confirmatory trial required; the confirmatory evidence requirement was ultimately satisfied via an expanded, continued enrollment cohort of the same pivotal trial ("Part B of Study 003") rather than an independently-designed confirmatory trial

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 003 (JAVELIN Merkel 200): international, multicenter, single-arm, open-label Phase II trial of avelumab 10 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks in metastatic MCC patients who had received ≥1 prior line of chemotherapy

- Primary endpoint was confirmed BOR (CR or PR per RECIST v1.1) as determined by IERC; sample size of 84 patients assumed a true ORR of 35% versus a null of ≤20%, providing 87% power at a one-sided alpha of 0.025

- A non-binding futility interim analysis occurred after the first 20 patients had ≥3 months' follow-up (based on unconfirmed investigator-assessed RECIST responses); an efficacy interim analysis occurred 6 months after the 56th patient was enrolled, allocated a nominal one-sided p-value threshold of 0.0045, with the remaining alpha (0.0205) reserved for the primary analysis conducted 6 months after the last patient was enrolled

- FDA's statistical reviewer stated explicitly: "In a single arm trial, FDA will not use inferential procedures to evaluate the trial results. Instead the efficacy decision will be based on whether the lower limit of 95% confidence interval of the response rate exceeds a clinically irrelevant response rate and whether the duration of response is adequate"

- FDA required a confirmatory study "to verify the clinical benefit of avelumab for the treatment of patients with metastatic Merkel Cell Carcinoma"; this was ultimately satisfied via Part B of the same Study 003 trial (an expanded, chemotherapy-naive cohort added under a protocol amendment) rather than a separately-designed Phase III confirmatory trial

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

The posted ClinicalTrials.gov SAP PDF's text layer uses a non-standard font encoding that strips normal spacing and substitutes a constant character-code shift; the passages below were reconstructed by decoding that shift (verified against the plainly-legible portions of the same document and cross-checked against the FDA Multi-Discipline Review's paraphrase of the same content), and are presented as reconstructed-from-source rather than a direct copy-paste, per this project's convention for non-standard PDF text layers.

*[reconstructed from source, Avelumab Statistical Analysis Plan (EMR 100070-003), ClinicalTrials.gov SAP_000.pdf, §on primary endpoint]* — "The primary endpoint of the trial is the confirmed best overall response (BOR) according to RECIST 1.1, based on independent review of tumor assessments. The objective response rate (ORR) will be determined as the proportion of subjects with a confirmed BOR of PR or CR. The trial aims at demonstrating an ORR greater than [20]% by means of an exact binomial test."

*[reconstructed from source, same document]* — "The Clopper-Pearson method will be used to calculate the two-sided CI for the ORR at both the interim and the primary analysis... In order to account for the two-stage group sequential design as applied in this study, the repeated CI method according to Jennison and Turnbull... will be used to construct the two-sided CI."

*[reconstructed from source, same document]* — "Therefore the overall Type I error rate is controlled at a level of [0.025] (one-sided). As some subjects included in the interim analysis will be followed up until the time of the primary analysis, some subjects' BOR might change from nonresponse at the interim analysis to response at the primary analysis. As the parameter of interest is the response at the time of the primary analysis, the actual type I error rate of this study might be slightly smaller than designed."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761049, Reference ID 4073902]* — "There was one interim analysis for futility after 20 patients were enrolled and observed for at least 3 months and one interim analysis for efficacy 6 months after 56 patients were enrolled... A sample size of 84 patients was planned for the study assuming an overall response rate (ORR) of 35%, and overall alpha of 0.025, and 87% power for rejecting the null hypothesis... the overall type I error rate was controlled at 0.025 (1-sided)."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "In a single arm trial, FDA will not use inferential procedures to evaluate the trial results. Instead the efficacy decision will be based on whether the lower limit of 95% confidence interval of the response rate exceeds a clinically irrelevant response rate and whether the duration of response is adequate."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "On September 2, 2016, a Type B meeting (teleconference) was held to discuss the proposed confirmatory study (Part B of Study 003) to verify the clinical benefit of avelumab for the treatment of patients with metastatic Merkel Cell Carcinoma."

### 65. Niraparib (Zejula) — NDA 208447

**Sponsor:** Tesaro, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Maintenance treatment of adult patients with recurrent epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer who are in a complete or partial response to platinum-based chemotherapy

**Approval date:** March 27, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** NOVA (ENGOT-OV16/NOVA, PR-30-5011-C), NCT01847274

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven trial, stratified by time to progression after penultimate platinum therapy, bevacizumab use, and best response to last platinum regimen; two independently-powered, independently-tested biomarker-defined cohorts (gBRCAmut and non-gBRCAmut), each allocated its own separate one-sided alpha of 0.025; within the non-gBRCAmut cohort, fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (HRD-positive subset tested first, then the entire non-gBRCAmut cohort)

- *Endpoints:* PFS per blinded independent central review (IRC), using RECIST v1.1 (primary endpoint, evaluated independently in the gBRCAmut and non-gBRCAmut cohorts)

- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, stratified Cox proportional-hazards model, Kaplan-Meier estimation

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing within the non-gBRCAmut cohort (HRD-positive subset first, full cohort second), each cohort's family-wise Type I error controlled at one-sided 0.025

- *Regulatory:* FDA raised a concern, during trial conduct, that the gBRCAmut cohort was overpowered to detect a PFS difference that "may not be clinically relevant," leading the sponsor to reduce planned power from >95% to 90% for that cohort; homologous-recombination-deficiency (HRD) testing via Myriad's myChoice HRD assay was used to define the biomarker subgroup within the non-gBRCAmut cohort but was recommended as a "complementary" (not mandatory companion) diagnostic

**Trial design & endpoints**

- NOVA: international, multicenter, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III maintenance trial of niraparib versus placebo in patients with platinum-sensitive, recurrent ovarian cancer in response to their last platinum regimen; patients were first stratified by germline BRCA mutation (gBRCAm) status into a gBRCAmut cohort (n=203) and a non-gBRCAmut cohort (n=350), with each cohort randomized and analyzed as an independent study (each allocated its own one-sided alpha of 0.025)

- Within the non-gBRCAmut cohort, tumors were tested post hoc for homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) using Myriad's myChoice HRD assay (HRD score ≥42 or a deleterious/suspected-deleterious somatic/germline BRCA mutation); PFS was evaluated in a pre-specified hierarchical manner — first in the HRD-positive subset (n=162), and only if that result was statistically significant, then in the overall non-gBRCAmut cohort (n=350)

- Sample-size assumptions (per the posted SAP): the gBRCAmut cohort was originally sized for >95% power (140 PFS events, true HR=0.50) but was reduced, at FDA's request during a Type C meeting, to 90% power (~100 PFS events) "to maintain 90% power," given FDA's concern that the original design was "overpowered to detect a small PFS difference that may not be clinically relevant"; the non-gBRCAmut cohort's HRD-positive subgroup was sized for 90% power (98 events) and the overall cohort for >95% power (140 events), both at one-sided alpha=0.025

- Results: median PFS 21.0 vs. 5.5 months in the gBRCAmut cohort (HR 0.27, 95% CI: 0.173, 0.410, p<0.0001); 12.9 vs. 3.8 months in the non-gBRCAmut HRD-positive subgroup (HR 0.38, 95% CI: 0.243, 0.586, p<0.0001); 9.3 vs. 3.9 months in the overall non-gBRCAmut cohort (HR 0.45, 95% CI: 0.338, 0.607, p<0.0001) — niraparib met the primary PFS endpoint in all three pre-specified populations, and FDA approved the indication irrespective of biomarker status given the consistent benefit across all groups

- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 4068706/4074987) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/208447Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (NOVA) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01847274 (protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan posted in the Documents tab)

- Pivotal publication: Mirza MR, Monk BJ, Herrstedt J, et al. "Niraparib Maintenance Therapy in Platinum-Sensitive, Recurrent Ovarian Cancer." *N Engl J Med.* 2016;375:2154-2164. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1611310), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27717299/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Niraparib%20Maintenance%20Therapy%20Platinum-Sensitive%20Recurrent%20Ovarian%20Cancer)

**Other resources**

- Tesaro was acquired by GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) in 2019; GSK participates in the Vivli data-sharing platform, but trial-specific IPD availability for NOVA was not individually confirmed.

- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this application.

Each cohort will have a separate randomization and the primary PFS analysis will be performed separately for each cohort."

### 66. Midostaurin (Rydapt) — NDA 207997

**Sponsor:** Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation

**Indication approved:** In combination with standard cytarabine and daunorubicin induction and high-dose cytarabine consolidation chemotherapy, for newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia (AML) that is FLT3 mutation-positive (as detected by an FDA-approved companion diagnostic)

**Approval date:** April 28, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** CALGB 10603 / RATIFY (Study A2301, Alliance for Clinical Trials in Oncology), NCT00651261

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven trial, biomarker-selected/enriched population (FLT3-mutated AML, stratified by FLT3-ITD allelic ratio <0.7 vs. ≥0.7 vs. FLT3-TKD), fixed-duration regimen (induction/consolidation) followed by continuation-phase monotherapy without re-randomization, cooperative-group-sponsored trial with industry co-sponsorship (Alliance for Clinical Trials in Oncology / Novartis)
- *Endpoints:* overall survival (OS, primary — time from randomization to death from any cause, not censored at stem cell transplant), event-free survival (EFS, key secondary — failure to achieve CR within 60 days, relapse, or death), disease-free survival (DFS) and complete remission (CR) by Day 60 and stem cell transplantation (SCT) rate as other secondary endpoints
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test and Cox proportional-hazards model (both stratified by FLT3 mutation status at randomization) for OS and EFS; Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (exact) test stratified by FLT3 mutation status for CR and SCT rate comparisons
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing — EFS was the only multiplicity-adjusted key secondary endpoint and was tested for statistical significance only after OS reached significance
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* one planned interim analysis of OS at 50% of expected events (187 deaths, occurred June 2012) with an alpha spend of 0.005 (one-sided) and a non-binding futility rule (conditional power to reject the null <0.10); Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) reviewed the interim look and recommended continuing without changes; because of slow event accrual, the trial was closed for a fixed-date final analysis (data cutoff April 1, 2015, 357 OS events) before reaching the originally planned 509-event target, with the final critical 2-sided p-value recalculated to 0.047 to preserve overall 2-sided alpha of 0.05 given the alpha already spent at interim
- *Missing data/bias:* standard right-censoring at last contact for OS (patients alive/lost to follow-up censored at last contact before the April 1, 2015 data cutoff; missing last-contact dates imputed as the end of the corresponding reporting period — FDA's clinical reviewer flagged this as an imputation rule that could artificially inflate OS estimates on both arms); primary OS analysis was not censored at stem cell transplant, with a sponsor-proposed sensitivity analysis censoring at SCT presented separately
- *Regulatory:* companion diagnostic co-approval (LeukoStrat CDx FLT3 Mutation Assay)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study A2301 (RATIFY): Phase III, randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, international trial of midostaurin (50 mg twice daily) vs. placebo added to standard 7+3 induction (cytarabine 200 mg/m²/day days 1-7, daunorubicin 60 mg/m²/day days 1-3) and high-dose cytarabine consolidation (3 g/m² every 12 hours, days 1/3/5), in adults 18-60 years with newly diagnosed FLT3-mutated AML; patients continuing in remission after consolidation received up to 12 cycles of midostaurin/placebo monotherapy continuation without re-randomization
- Randomization stratified by FLT3 mutation subtype: FLT3-ITD allelic ratio <0.7, FLT3-ITD allelic ratio ≥0.7, or FLT3-TKD
- Primary endpoint: overall survival (OS), time from randomization to death from any cause, not censored for stem cell transplant
- Key secondary endpoint (only formally multiplicity-adjusted secondary): event-free survival (EFS), defined as failure to achieve CR within 60 days of starting protocol therapy, relapse, or death from any cause
- Other secondary endpoints: CR rate by Day 60, disease-free survival (DFS), stem cell transplantation rate
- Sample size: original plan of ≥714 patients to observe 509 OS events, ~85% power to detect HR=0.78 (median OS 16.3 vs. 20.9 months) at overall 2-sided alpha=0.05, accounting for one planned interim OS analysis at 50% of events; the trial ultimately enrolled 717 patients (360 midostaurin, 357 placebo) and was closed for final analysis with 357 observed OS events (below the original 509-event target) because of markedly slowed event accrual (only one death observed in the six months before the March 2015 look)
- Result: OS HR 0.77 (95% CI 0.63-0.95), 2-sided p=0.016 (interim analysis at 255 events was not significant, p=0.0252); EFS HR 0.78 (95% CI 0.66-0.93), p=0.004; DFS HR 0.71 (95% CI 0.55-0.92), p=0.010; CR by Day 60 58.9% vs. 53.5% (p=0.146, not significant, but not part of the multiplicity-controlled hierarchy); FDA's statistical reviewer noted the OS Kaplan-Meier curves plateaued before reaching their medians, making the reported median OS values (74.4 vs. 25.6 months) unreliable as summary statistics despite the HR being the basis for the efficacy claim

Cooperative-group trial data of this kind sometimes become available via the NCI's data archives; trial-specific IPD availability for A2301 was not individually confirmed here.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this application.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 207997, Reference ID 4049883]* — "Study A2301 primary efficacy endpoint was overall survival (OS), defined as the time from randomization to death from any cause. Event-free survival (EFS) was the only multiplicity adjusted key secondary endpoint... Other secondary endpoints included complete remission rate within 60 days of start of treatment, disease-free survival, and stem cell transplantation rate."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "The primary comparison between treatment arms in OS was based on log-rank test and Cox regression model stratified for FLT3 mutation status used in the randomization. OS was not censored at the time of SCT in the primary analysis. The primary analysis of EFS was conducted using the same methodology as the primary analysis of OS. For the control of Type I error, comparison in EFS was tested for statistical significance after comparison in OS was significant."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "Study A2301 planned to enroll at least 714 patients, in order to have 509 OS events at the final analysis to demonstrate a hazard ratio of 0.78 for midostaurin versus placebo... with approximately 85% power at an overall 2-sided alpha level of 0.05. The sample size calculation also accounted for one planned interim analysis of OS at 50% of events... Due to slow occurrence of death events, Study A2301 protocol was amended to perform the final OS analysis with a data cut off of 01-April-2015. The critical 2-sided p-value to declare statistical significance was calculated to be 0.047 for the maintenance of overall 2-sided alpha at 0.05, based on total of 357 events occurred up to April 2015 and the alpha already spent (fixed at 2-sided 0.01) at the interim analysis."

*[verbatim, same source, reviewer comment]* — "The planned interim analysis for OS was conducted with 255 death events. The result was not significant with a 2-sided p-value of 0.0252. The study continued, but the event occurrence became very slow. In March 2015, 350 events had been observed with only one death in the prior 6 months."

*[verbatim, FDA Clinical Review, NDA 207997, Reference ID 4051527]* — "One interim analysis for the overall survival endpoint was planned, after 50% of expected events (187), with an alpha spend of 0.005. A conditional probability of rejecting the null hypothesis of < 0.10 was planned to be grounds for stopping for early futility. This interim analysis occurred in June 2012 and the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) concluded that the study should proceed without changes."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "The original statistical analysis plan was finalized in June of 2011 based on protocol amendment 4, which increased the sample size to 714 patients and number of required OS events to 509 due to revised assumptions about the frequency of HSCT and FLT3-TKD on the study... A revised statistical analysis plan was generated in 2015 due to slow accrual of OS events... and was finalized prior to the primary analysis of the primary endpoint in July of 2015."

*[verbatim, same source, reviewer comment]* — "Imputation of the date of last contact as the end date of the corresponding reporting period may artificially increase estimates of OS on both arms."

Note the two FDA-reported alpha-spend figures for the single planned interim OS analysis differ slightly across the Clinical Review (0.005, one-sided, tied to a non-binding futility rule) and the Statistical Review (a fixed 2-sided 0.01 "already spent" at interim, used to back into the final critical value of 0.047) — both are quoted verbatim above rather than reconciled, since each is drawn from a different FDA reviewer's own account of the same design element.

### 67. Brigatinib (Alunbrig) — NDA 208772

**Sponsor:** Ariad Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** ALK-positive metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in patients who have progressed on or are intolerant to crizotinib (accelerated approval, 21 CFR 314.510)

**Approval date:** April 28, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** ALTA (Study AP26113-13-201), NCT02094573

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized (1:1, stratified permuted block, stratified by baseline brain metastases and best response to prior crizotinib), open-label, multicenter, two-dose-regimen trial in which each arm was analyzed independently as its own cohort against a fixed performance goal rather than compared to the other arm — randomization was used only to allocate/balance patients across the two brigatinib dosing regimens (90 mg QD continuously [Arm A] vs. 90 mg QD x7 days then 180 mg QD [Arm B]), with no formal between-arm statistical hypothesis; single-arm-by-cohort trial supporting accelerated approval; biomarker-selected population (ALK-positive NSCLC, post-crizotinib progression)
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR, primary, investigator-assessed per RECIST v1.1, with IRC-assessed ORR as a secondary/confirmatory analysis); duration of response (DoR), intracranial CNS ORR (IRC-assessed), intracranial CNS PFS, disease control rate, time to response, overall survival (all secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (point estimate + 95% Clopper-Pearson exact binomial confidence interval, calculated separately for each dosing-regimen arm, with no between-arm comparative test); the SAP itself pre-specified an exact one-sided/two-sided binomial test of each arm's ORR against a fixed 20% "uninteresting" performance-goal threshold at 97.5% confidence, but FDA's statistical reviewer noted "there were no formal statistical hypotheses specified" for the trial and that the Agency's own primary analysis approach was simply the ORR point estimate and 95% CI per arm, using IRC assessment as FDA's preferred (not the sponsor's investigator-assessed) primary analysis
- *Missing data/bias:* standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment for time-to-event secondary endpoints (DoR, intracranial PFS); patients with no measurable disease at baseline or no adequate post-baseline assessment counted as non-responders for the ORR numerator
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.510 Subpart H on the surrogate endpoint of ORR, with a randomized confirmatory trial (ALTA-1L, first-line vs. crizotinib) required post-marketing to verify clinical benefit; FDA's Office of Scientific Investigations (OSI) verified the primary ORR endpoint at four inspected clinical sites; lack of a non-brigatinib comparator arm was explicitly identified by FDA as a limitation of the safety database

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study AP26113-13-201 (ALTA): Phase II, randomized (1:1), open-label, multicenter, international trial of brigatinib in 222 patients with ALK-positive, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC who had progressed on crizotinib; patients were randomized to one of two dosing regimens — Arm A: 90 mg orally once daily continuously (n=112 enrolled/109 in the labeled-dose efficacy analysis per FDA's count); Arm B: 90 mg once daily for 7 days, then escalated to 180 mg once daily continuously (n=110), the regimen ultimately adopted in product labeling
- Randomization was stratified by presence of brain metastases at baseline (yes/no) and best prior response to crizotinib (CR/PR vs. any other response/unknown), using a stratified permuted block design — but the trial was not designed or analyzed as a comparative RCT between the two arms; each dosing regimen was evaluated as an independent cohort against a fixed external performance goal
- Primary endpoint: objective response rate (ORR), investigator-assessed per RECIST v1.1, defined as the proportion of patients confirmed to achieve CR or PR (confirmation required on repeat imaging ≥4 weeks after initial response)
- Secondary endpoints: IRC-assessed ORR, duration of response, intracranial CNS ORR/PFS (IRC-assessed, for patients with baseline brain metastases), disease control rate, time to response, time on treatment, overall survival
- Sample size: the SAP specified ≥218 eligible patients (109/regimen) to provide ~88-90% power (reviewer's and sponsor's stated power estimates differ slightly, 88% vs. 90%) to rule out an "uninteresting" ORR of 20% when the true rate was 35% or higher, at two-sided alpha=0.025 using an exact binomial test per regimen — but FDA's statistical reviewer explicitly stated the study had "no formal statistical hypotheses" driving the approval decision, and instead reviewed ORR as a descriptive point estimate with a 95% (not the sponsor's 97.5%) Clopper-Pearson exact CI, preferring IRC assessment over the sponsor's investigator-assessed primary analysis
- Result (labeled dose, Arm B, IRC-assessed, the basis cited in FDA's efficacy conclusion): ORR 53% (95% CI 43-62%) in the pivotal ALTA cohort; investigator-assessed ORR was similar (54%, 95% CI 44-63%); Arm A (90 mg) showed IRC-assessed ORR 45% (95% CI 35-54%) and investigator-assessed 48% (95% CI 39-58%); median duration of response was approximately 14 months in the labeled-dose arm; intracranial responses were also observed in patients with baseline brain metastases

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/208772Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (Statistical Reviewer: Thomas Ly, PhD; Reference ID 4090771) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/208772Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf

- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this application.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, ALTA Statistical Analysis Plan, AP26113-13-201, Version 1.0, 25 February 2016]* — "This is a phase 2, open-label, randomized, multicenter, international study... Patient will be randomized 1:1 to receive AP26113 in one of two different dosing regimens. In Arm A, AP26113 will be administered at a dose of 90 mg orally QD, continuously... In Arm B, AP26113 will be administered at a dose of 90 mg orally QD for 7 days, then 180 mg orally QD, continuously."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "Patients will be allocated in a 1:1 ratio to each dosing regimen using a randomized block design stratified by the following factors: 1. Presence of brain metastases at baseline (Yes vs. No) 2. Best prior response to crizotinib therapy as assessed by the investigator (CR/PR vs. Any other response or status unknown)."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "The primary endpoint, ORR assessed by the investigator, is defined as the proportion of the [randomized patients who are confirmed to have achieved CR or PR after the initiation of study treatment]... A sample size of at least 218 eligible patients (109 per treatment regimen) will provide approximate 90% power to rule out an uninteresting rate of 20% when the true rate is 35% or higher at two-sided alpha level of 0.025 using exact binomial test. The treatment regimen will be considered to have achieved the primary objective when ORR assessed by the investigator is shown to be significantly higher than 20% at a two-sided alpha level of 0.025 at final analysis for that regimen."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "97.5% confidence intervals for the ORR will be calculated based on the binomial distribution. The primary analysis will be performed on ORR assessed by the investigator among all the randomized patients."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 208772, Statistical Review section, Reference ID 4090771]* — "There were no formal statistical hypotheses specified for Study AP26113-13-201... The primary analysis of ORR, in the intention-to-treat (ITT) population was computation of exact 2-sided 97.5% binomial confidence intervals for each treatment arm... FDA usually considers a 95% CI in the evaluation of ORR for single arm trials without adjusting the level of confidence. Thus, the 95% CI will be reported in this review."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "The primary analysis of ORR is based on estimated response rate and its corresponding confidence interval. FDA traditionally uses ORR assessed by IRC as the primary analysis and assessment by the investigators as secondary. In this review, both assessment methods will be evaluated."

*[verbatim, same source, Executive Summary]* — "The recommendation for accelerated approval according to 21 CFR 314.510 Subpart H is primarily based on the results of a single trial (ALTA) that demonstrated a durable 53% Independent Review Committee-assessed response rate in 110 patients in the study arm where patients received the brigatinib dose proposed in product labeling... A limitation of the database was lack of a non-brigatinib comparator arm. ARIAD will obtain additional data regarding risk in an ongoing randomized study comparing brigatinib to crizotinib in the first-line setting" — this ongoing study became ALTA-1L, the confirmatory trial that later supported brigatinib's full approval in the first-line setting in 2020 (not covered by this entry, which documents only the 2017 accelerated approval).

### 68. Durvalumab (Imfinzi) — BLA 761069

**Sponsor:** AstraZeneca AB (MedImmune, LLC, as applicant of record)

**Indication approved:** Locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma in patients who have disease progression during or following platinum-containing chemotherapy, or disease progression within 12 months of neoadjuvant or adjuvant treatment with platinum-containing chemotherapy — approved under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and duration of response, with continued approval contingent on verification of clinical benefit in confirmatory trials.

**Approval date:** May 1, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** Study 1108 (urothelial carcinoma expansion cohort), NCT01693562

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label trial (Phase 1/2 dose-expansion cohort within a larger multi-tumor first-in-human study, not a standalone registration trial); post-hoc recombination of differently-enrolled cohorts into one primary analysis population (early PD-L1-high-enriched enrollment under Amendment 8 combined with later all-comer enrollment into a single pooled primary efficacy population)
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR) / duration of response (DoR) / disease control rate (DCR), assessed as the primary endpoint (not secondary, as in most oncology entries in this census) by Blinded Independent Central Review (BICR) per RECIST v1.1, with investigator assessment as a concordant secondary analysis; PFS and OS collected as key secondary endpoints but explicitly noted by the FDA reviewer as uninterpretable absent a control arm
- *Primary analysis:* Exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval for ORR, with the primary endpoint declared met if the lower bound of the exact 2-sided 95% CI excluded a pre-specified historical control response rate of 10% — a CI-exclusion decision rule rather than a formal hypothesis test with a reported p-value (FDA's reviewers explicitly declined to report significance tests, judging the historical-control comparison too uncertain to support one)
- *Missing data/bias:* Standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment for time-to-event secondary endpoints; DoR analyses restricted to confirmed responders, with duration of response for non-progressors reported as censored ("+") values
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval (21 CFR 314.500) based on single-arm ORR/DoR in a non-randomized expansion cohort, with a randomized Phase 3 confirmatory trial (DANUBE) already underway at the time of approval; the confirmatory trial (DANUBE, NCT02516241) subsequently failed to meet its overall-survival endpoints in both co-primary comparisons — durvalumab monotherapy vs. chemotherapy in the PD-L1-high population (median OS 14.4 vs. 12.1 months) and durvalumab plus tremelimumab vs. chemotherapy in the intention-to-treat population (median OS 15.1 vs. 12.1 months), neither statistically significant (Powles et al. 2020) — and FDA's withdrawn-cancer-accelerated-approvals list records the urothelial carcinoma indication as withdrawn February 19, 2021, as part of an industry-wide FDA reassessment of unconfirmed oncology accelerated approvals

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 1108 was an open-label, multicenter, multi-part, Phase 1/2 study of durvalumab (MEDI4736) monotherapy in advanced solid tumors, first proposed in April 2012 and amended four major times with FDA feedback; the urothelial carcinoma (UC) cohort analyzed for this approval was a dose-expansion cohort, not a separately randomized trial
- 191 patients with metastatic or locally advanced UC enrolled in the UC cohort; the FDA-designated primary efficacy/safety population was 182 patients who had received first dose of durvalumab 10 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks at least 13 weeks before the October 24, 2016 data cutoff, with at least 2 RECIST follow-up scans
- Enrollment initially targeted PD-L1-high patients specifically (per Amendment 8) to validate an investigational PD-L1 diagnostic (VENTANA PD-L1 [SP263] assay, TC/IC ≥25% cutoff derived from an interim look at the first 20 UC patients), then continued as all-comers once ~132 PD-L1-high subjects had accrued; both enrollment waves were pooled into a single primary efficacy analysis population
- Primary endpoint: confirmed ORR by RECIST v1.1 per BICR in 2nd-line-and-later PD-L1-high UC patients in the Full Analysis Set, considered met if the lower bound of the exact 2-sided 95% CI for ORR excluded a historical control response rate of 10%; if met, ORR was also reported (not separately tested) for all 2nd-line-and-later UC patients regardless of PD-L1 status
- Sample size: with ~70 PD-L1-high subjects, an 85% chance existed of observing ≥13 responses (18.6% ORR) with the CI lower bound excluding 10% if the true ORR was 23%; with ~100 PD-L1-high subjects, that chance rose to 94% (for ≥17 responses, 17% ORR)
- Key secondary endpoints: disease-control rate, duration of response, PFS, and OS, all assessed by both BICR and investigator; FDA's reviewers explicitly stated that PFS/OS from this single-arm study were not interpretable given the absence of a control arm
- Reported result: BICR-assessed ORR 17.0% overall (31/182; 95% CI 11.9-23.3%), 26.3% in PD-L1-high patients (25/95; 95% CI 17.8-36.4%), 4.1% in PD-L1-low/negative patients (3/73), and 21.4% in PD-L1-not-evaluable patients (3/14); median DoR not reached overall (range 0.9+ to 19.9+ months), with 45% of responders ongoing at ≥6 months and 16% at ≥12 months
- An interim efficacy analysis was planned after ~103 UC subjects had ≥13 weeks of follow-up, with a second updated analysis ~90 days later; no formal stopping rule or alpha adjustment was associated with either look, since the trial's endpoint structure was a single CI-exclusion criterion, not a group-sequential test

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (DANUBE, confirmatory trial) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02516241
- Pivotal publication (Study 1108 UC cohort, updated results, a later data cut than the 182-patient FDA-reviewed approval basis): Powles T, Durán I, van der Heijden MS, et al. "Efficacy and Safety of Durvalumab in Locally Advanced or Metastatic Urothelial Carcinoma: Updated Results From a Phase 1/2 Open-label Study." *JAMA Oncol.* 2017;3(9):e172411. **Other resources**

- AstraZeneca participates in the Vivli data-sharing platform; trial-specific IPD availability for Study 1108 was not individually confirmed.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for the original 2017 accelerated approval; the urothelial indication was later discussed, alongside several other unconfirmed checkpoint-inhibitor accelerated approvals, at a 2021 ODAC meeting on accelerated-approval indications lacking confirmed benefit, culminating in AstraZeneca's voluntary withdrawal of this indication.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Clinical and Statistical Review, BLA 761069, Reference ID 4068251]* — "The sample size justification for the total of 192 patients planned for the UC cohort was based on the expected ORR in the PD-L1-high status group with a goal of excluding the historical ORR of 10%. With approximately 100 patients with a PD-L1-high status would provide an expected ORR in the range of 17%-33%. With a total of 70 PD-L1-high UC subjects, there is an 85% chance of observing at least 13 responses (an ORR of 18.6% with the lower-limit of the exact 95% CI excluding a historical response rate of 10%) if the true ORR is 23%."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "The primary analysis of ORR based on RECIST v1.1 by BICR will be performed for all 2L+ PD-L1 high UC subjects in the FAS enrolled in the entire study. The primary endpoint for UC cohort in PD-L1-high subgroup is considered to be met if the lower-limit of the exact 2-sided 95% CI for ORR excludes a historical response rate of 10%.... If the primary endpoint for the PD-L1-high subgroup of the UC cohort is met, the ORR based on RECIST v1.1 by BICR along with its 95% CI will be also provided for all 2L+ UC subjects in the FAS (regardless of PD-L1 status) enrolled in the entire study."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "Review Comments: The review team considered the 2L+ UC subjects in Study 1108 (regardless of PD-L1 status) as the primary efficacy analysis population for ORR analyses. The presumed historical ORR control of 10% for the statistical test is debatable in patients with advanced urothelial carcinoma.... For a single-arm, open-label study, a detected statistical significance, as compared to the debatable historical control, may not represent a true clinical improvement. Therefore, no statistical tests and P-values will be reported in this review."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "Review comments: PFS/OS results from a single-arm study are not interpretable because of the absence of a control."

Cross-reference note: this is the second single-arm accelerated-approval oncology entry in this census whose confirmatory trial is documented as having failed post-approval (compare the FDA reviewer's contemporaneous skepticism about the historical-control comparison, which proved warranted when DANUBE's randomized comparison did not confirm benefit).

### 69. Neratinib (Nerlynx) — NDA 208051

**Sponsor:** Puma Biotechnology, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Extended adjuvant treatment of adult patients with early-stage HER2-overexpressed/amplified breast cancer, to follow adjuvant trastuzumab-based therapy

**Approval date:** July 17, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** ExteNET (Study 3004), NCT00878709

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; randomization stratified by ER/PgR status (positive vs. negative), nodal status, and prior trastuzumab administration (sequential vs. concurrent with chemotherapy); trial conducted across three successive sponsors (Wyeth, Pfizer, Puma) with repeated protocol amendments changing the eligibility population, primary analysis population (amended ITT vs. reverted-to-ITT), and follow-up duration (5 years shortened to 2 years, then extended again via patient reconsent)
- *Endpoints:* Invasive disease-free survival (iDFS), defined as time from randomization to first invasive ipsilateral or contralateral breast recurrence, local/regional invasive recurrence, distant recurrence, or death from any cause (a modified, non-STEEP-criteria definition); secondary endpoints DFS-including-DCIS, distant disease-free survival, time to distant recurrence, cumulative incidence of CNS recurrence, and overall survival (OS, key secondary, gated behind a significant primary iDFS result)
- *Primary analysis:* Stratified log-rank test (one-sided alpha 0.025) with stratified Cox proportional-hazards model for the hazard ratio and 95% CI, Kaplan-Meier estimation for iDFS curves; stratified one-sided Gray's test for the CNS-recurrence cumulative-incidence secondary endpoint; repeated-measures ANCOVA (with a mixed-model sensitivity analysis) for quality-of-life endpoints
- *Multiplicity:* No formal multiplicity adjustment across secondary endpoints other than OS, which was gated hierarchically behind a significant primary iDFS result (fixed-sequence hierarchical testing, iDFS→OS)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Original Wyeth-era protocol specified two interim analyses (futility-only at ~135 events; futility and efficacy at ~236 events, efficacy boundary p<0.0005); interim analyses were removed entirely in a later amendment when the primary analysis was converted to a fixed 2-year, time-driven follow-up window rather than an event-driven design; a single planned interim OS analysis at 50% information was added post-database-lock (per FDA request) using a Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function approximating an O'Brien-Fleming boundary
- *Missing data/bias:* Tipping-point analysis (multiple imputation), conducted by FDA (not the sponsor) to address concerns about differential early dropout/attrition between arms (attrition bias) — an FDA-run simulation reassigning censored patients to events under progressively adverse assumptions until the hazard ratio crossed 0.9 or the log-rank p-value exceeded 0.05, which it did not under either tipping-point scenario at the observed early-dropout rates
- *Regulatory:* FDA Advisory Committee meeting held (Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee, May 24, 2017; voted 12-4 that ExteNET's efficacy/safety results support a positive benefit-risk assessment); reviewer-documented mid-trial changes to censoring rules and addition of the interim OS analysis, both made per FDA request after the sponsor's SAP was already in place; the label extrapolates the indication to "adult patients" (including males) despite no male patients being enrolled in ExteNET, based on sponsor-provided mechanistic rationale rather than trial data (extrapolation of efficacy across a related population)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ExteNET (Study 3004): Phase 3, multicenter, randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of one year of neratinib versus placebo in women with early-stage (originally stage 1-3c, later restricted to stage 2-3) HER2-positive breast cancer who had completed adjuvant trastuzumab-based therapy; 2,840 patients randomized (1,420 per arm)
- Randomization stratified by hormone-receptor status (ER and/or PgR positive vs. both negative), nodal status (dichotomized to 1-3 vs. ≥4 positive nodes after Amendment 3), and whether prior trastuzumab was given concurrently or sequentially with chemotherapy
- Primary endpoint: invasive disease-free survival (iDFS), time from randomization to first ipsilateral invasive breast tumor recurrence, invasive contralateral breast cancer, local/regional invasive recurrence, distant recurrence, or death from any cause — a definition FDA's reviewer noted departs somewhat from the field-standard STEEP criteria (Hudis et al. 2007)
- The trial changed sponsors twice (Wyeth to Pfizer in 2010, Pfizer to Puma in 2012) and underwent at least four major protocol amendments: Amendment 3 (2010) enriched the population to higher-risk patients and reduced planned sample size to 3,300 (aITT analysis population); Amendment 9 (2011) stopped enrollment at 2,840 patients and shortened planned follow-up from 5 to 2 years, removing the two originally planned interim analyses; Amendment 13 (2014, under Puma) reverted the primary analysis population back to full ITT (reintroducing node-negative patients) and introduced a patient-reconsent process to collect extended 5-year follow-up data
- Final SAP (dated April 6, 2016): primary analysis of iDFS on the ITT population, with iDFS events counted up to a cutoff of 2 years + 28 days from randomization (with specific censoring rules for patients with ≥2 missing physical exams), analyzed via a stratified log-rank test at one-sided alpha 0.025 with a stratified Cox model for the hazard ratio; no adjustment for multiplicity across secondary endpoints except OS, which was gated behind a significant iDFS result
- Reported primary result: stratified HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.49-0.90), unstratified HR 0.67; 2-year iDFS rate 94.2% (neratinib) vs. 91.9% (placebo), an absolute difference of 2.3%
- OS: planned final analysis at 248 events (80% power to detect HR 0.7); one planned interim OS analysis at 50% information added post-database-lock using a Lan-DeMets/O'Brien-Fleming spending function, per FDA request
- FDA-conducted sensitivity analyses (not sponsor-planned) addressed concern over an early-dropout imbalance between arms (372 neratinib patients [26%] vs. 72 placebo patients [5%] discontinued treatment due to adverse events) that could differentially bias ascertainment of iDFS events: an FDA simulation reassigning censored patients to events, and a formal tipping-point analysis testing whether the primary result would reverse (p>0.05, or HR≥0.9) under increasingly adverse assumptions about undetected neratinib-arm events — the primary conclusion did not tip under the scenarios FDA tested
- Applicant's own exploratory analyses using extended (2-year and 5-year) reconsent follow-up data showed a similar treatment effect persisting over time (updated 2-year stratified HR 0.68 [95% CI 0.51-0.91]; 5-year stratified HR 0.73 [95% CI 0.57-0.92], iDFS rates 90.2% vs. 87.7%), though these were explicitly labeled sensitivity/exploratory analyses rather than a re-run of the confirmatory primary analysis

[DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(17)30717-9>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29146401/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Neratinib%20after%20trastuzumab-based%20adjuvant%20therapy%20HER2-positive%20breast%20cancer%20ExteNET%205-year%20analysis)

**Other resources**

- Puma Biotechnology's data-sharing/IPD-access practices for ExteNET were not individually confirmed against Vivli, YODA, or Project Data Sphere.
- FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting held May 24, 2017; voted 12-4 that ExteNET's efficacy and safety results support a positive benefit-risk assessment for the proposed extended-adjuvant population.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 208051, Reference ID 4125095]* — "Under the final version of the SAP (dated April 6, 2016), the primary analysis of iDFS was performed on the ITT population. The primary analysis included iDFS events up to a cutoff date of 2 years + 28 days from randomization unless the events occurred after 2 or more missing physical exams.... A stratified log-rank test with type-1 error controlled at a one-sided significance level of 0.025 was conducted. The stratified Cox proportional hazards model was used to estimate the treatment hazard ratio and corresponding 95% confidence interval, and a Kaplan-Meier plot was created."

*[verbatim, same source, Table 11 narrative]* — "Study 3004 was held by three different sponsors, leading to several major protocol amendments. Under Wyeth's original protocol (April 2009), the study was designed to enroll 3850 patients in order to observe the 337 DFS events necessary to detect a hazard ratio of 0.70 with 90% power and a one-sided significance level of 0.025. There were two planned interim analyses at approximately 135 (for futility only) and 236 (for futility and efficacy; efficacy boundary: p-value<0.0005) DFS events."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "Reviewer's Comments: 1. Changes to the SAP made post-database lock mainly had to do with changes to censoring rules and the addition of an interim analysis for OS (with an O'Brien-Fleming efficacy boundary for alpha adjustment), both per FDA request."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "To address concerns regarding the missing data, the FDA conducted a tipping point analysis... increased the number of events on the neratinib arm among the 419 missing observations until two tipping points were reached: 1. Tipping Point #1: The p-value exceeds 0.05 (two-sided) 2. Tipping Point #2: The hazard ratio equals or exceeds 0.9.... Results for the tipping points are shown in Table 20. In both cases, the results did not tip unless the rate of new neratinib events was higher than the expected 5.1%."

*[verbatim, same source, Summary Review]* — "Given these uncertainties, the Division convened an Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting on May 24, 2017, to advise and offer insight on the overall benefit-risk of neratinib in the proposed population. The committee voted 12-4 that the efficacy and safety results of ExteNET supports a positive benefit-risk assessment of neratinib for the proposed population."

Cross-reference note: unlike this census's other extended-adjuvant HER2 entry conventions, ExteNET's own sponsor-run SAP contained no formal missing-data sensitivity method for the early-dropout imbalance — the tipping-point analysis here was FDA-initiated, not sponsor-planned, a notable contrast to SELECT's sponsor-run tipping-point analysis in the cardiovascular section of this census.

### 70. Enasidenib (Idhifa) — NDA 209606

**Sponsor:** Celgene Corporation

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with an IDH2 mutation as detected by an FDA-approved test

**Approval date:** August 1, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** Study AG221-C-001, NCT01915498

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label, multicenter, two-part (Phase 1 dose-escalation/expansion plus Phase 2) trial in relapsed/refractory AML with a centrally confirmed IDH2 mutation; no randomized comparator and no planned interim analysis; FDA required the primary efficacy analysis to combine the Phase 1 and Phase 2 cohorts rather than rely on the sponsor's originally-submitted Phase-1-only interim dataset
- *Endpoints:* protocol-specified primary endpoint was investigator-assessed overall response rate (ORR: CR+CRp+CRi+PR+MLFS); the endpoints FDA ultimately relied on for the efficacy claim were the composite CR/CRh rate, duration of CR/CRh, and rate of conversion from red-cell/platelet transfusion-dependence to transfusion-independence; overall survival was tracked descriptively only (not interpretable without a comparator)
- *Primary analysis:* Descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (point estimate + 2-sided exact binomial 95% CI, no formal hypothesis test) for ORR and CR/CRh; Kaplan-Meier estimation for duration of response and OS
- *Regulatory:* Endpoint not accepted as a valid regulatory endpoint (FDA rejected investigator-assessed ORR as the basis for an AML efficacy claim and required CR/CRh plus transfusion-independence instead); reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan (sponsor submitted an interim Phase-1-only analysis as the pivotal dataset, contrary to the protocol's designation of Phase 2 as pivotal, prompting FDA to require a combined Phase 1 + Phase 2 re-analysis)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study AG221-C-001 was an open-label, single-arm, multicenter, two-part (Phase 1 dose-escalation/expansion; Phase 2) study of oral enasidenib in adults with IDH2-mutated advanced hematologic malignancies (AML and MDS); the 100 mg once-daily dose used in the pivotal analysis was selected from Phase 1 based on near-maximal 2-hydroxyglutarate suppression, comparable response rates above 100 mg, and the lowest rate of dose reductions for toxicity at 100 mg among doses greater than 100 mg
- The efficacy population for the R/R AML indication comprised 199 adults with centrally confirmed IDH2-mutated relapsed/refractory AML who received enasidenib 100 mg daily (101 from Phase 1, 98 from Phase 2); relapsed/refractory was protocol-defined (post-transplant relapse, second-or-later relapse, relapse within 1 year without favorable-risk cytogenetics, or refractory to induction/re-induction or at least 2 cycles of first-line therapy)
- The protocol's primary endpoint was ORR by investigator assessment (CR, CRp, CRi, PR, or MLFS), with no interim analysis planned; the protocol treated a 2-sided exact binomial 95% CI lower bound greater than 25% as the pre-specified threshold for "clinically meaningful," but no formal hypothesis test was specified
- Before submission, FDA advised that ORR was not an acceptable regulatory endpoint for R/R AML — because an enasidenib-induced CR, given its differentiating (non-cytotoxic) mechanism, could occur alongside persistent minimal residual disease and thus might not carry the same prognostic value as a chemotherapy-induced CR — and required CR, CR/CRh, and transfusion-independence conversion to be added/emphasized as secondary endpoints supporting the efficacy claim; FDA also required at least 6 months of Phase 2 follow-up because Phase 1 showed responses occurring as late as cycle 6
- Sample size was originally sized only against the ORR "clinically meaningful" threshold (125 planned Phase 2 subjects gave a CI lower bound greater than 25% if the true ORR was at least 33%), with no separate power calculation for CR/CRh
- The sponsor initially submitted the NDA using only the Phase 1 interim dataset (April 15, 2016 cutoff) — contrary to the protocol's designation of Phase 2 as the pivotal portion — citing high unmet need; FDA required the sponsor to instead analyze combined, fully accrued Phase 1 plus Phase 2 data
- In the 199-subject R/R AML efficacy population, the CR/CRh rate was 23% (95% CI 18-30%), consistent between Phase 1 (23.8%) and Phase 2 (22.5%); median duration of response was 8.2 months; 34% of baseline transfusion-dependent patients (53/157) converted to transfusion independence for at least 56 days; FDA's independent analysis of the Phase 2 cohort alone gave an ORR of 34.6% (95% CI 25.3-44.2%), meeting the sponsor's pre-specified threshold
- FDA granted regular (not accelerated) approval, concluding that the consistent CR/CRh rate with associated transfusion-independence across both phases constituted substantial evidence of effectiveness for a fatal disease with no other approved options for this genotype

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2017/209606Orig1s000.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/209606s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (Statistical Reviewer Qing Xu, PhD; Statistical Team Leader Yuan-Li Shen, Dr.PH; Reference ID 4131433) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209606Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (AG221-C-001) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01915498 (no protocol/SAP posted in the Documents tab)
- Pivotal publication: Stein EM, DiNardo CD, Pollyea DA, et al. "Enasidenib in mutant IDH2 relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia." *Blood.* 2017;130(6):722-731. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1182/blood-2017-04-779405), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28588020/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Enasidenib%20in%20mutant%20IDH2%20relapsed%20or%20refractory%20acute%20myeloid%20leukemia)

**Other resources**

- Celgene (acquired by Bristol-Myers Squibb in 2019) participates in the Vivli data-sharing platform; trial-specific IPD availability for AG221-C-001 was not individually confirmed.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this application (Multi-Discipline Review, Section 8: "This Application was not presented to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee or any other advisory committee.").

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 209606, Reference ID 4131433]* — "The primary endpoint of Study AG221-C-001 was overall response rate (ORR, defined as CR, CRp, CRi, morphologic leukemia-free state and PR) as determined by investigator. There was no planned interim analysis in the protocol, and the final analysis was to be performed on 125 subjects in the Phase 2 portion. There was no hypothesis testing planned, but the protocol indicated that a binomial 95% CI lower bound >25% was considered clinically meaningful."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "ORR was not considered an appropriate endpoint for regulatory decision-making for R/R AML. CR is usually used as a surrogate reasonably likely to predict survival. However, the applicant reported that subjects tested at best response still had minimal residual disease (MRD) including in cells other than blasts, so it was not clear that a CR induced by enasidenib, a differentiating agent, had the same prognostic value as a CR induced by cytotoxic chemotherapy. Therefore, FDA recommended that the applicant assess CR and CRh along with measures of transfusion independence to assess clinical benefit, and these were added as secondary endpoints in the protocol."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "Although the applicant originally intended Phase 2 to be the pivotal portion of the study, their analysis of data from Phase 1, with a data cut date of April 15, 2016, was submitted as the basis for the NDA to support the proposed indication due to the high unmet need in this patient population. During the course of the review, the FDA asked the applicant to analyze updated data from Phase 1 and Phase 2 together, and the applicant submitted additional information to comply with this request."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "An observed ORR in R/R AML subjects in the combined Phase 1 with the lower bound of the exact binomial 95% CI greater than 25% was deemed as clinically meaningful in this setting and exceeded the ORR expected with available therapies. This was considered to be evidence of clinically significant activity from AG-221."

*[verbatim, same source, Statistical Issues]* — "The major issue in this application is a single arm study and only treatment effect may be estimated and no inference can be draw. The investigator assessed CR rate and sponsor assessed CR rate are different."

*[verbatim, same source, Conclusions and Recommendations]* — "It is concluded that the consistent CR/CRh rates with associated transfusion-independence across Phase 1 and Phase 2 constitutes substantial evidence of effectiveness."

### 71. Inotuzumab ozogamicin (Besponsa) — BLA 761040

**Sponsor:** Pfizer Inc. (submitted by Wyeth Pharmaceuticals, Inc., a Pfizer subsidiary)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adults with relapsed or refractory B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL)

**Approval date:** August 17, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** Study B1931022 (INO-VATE ALL), NCT01564784

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized (1:1), open-label, active-controlled, multicenter, global phase 3 trial of inotuzumab ozogamicin vs. a defined investigator's-choice chemotherapy regimen (FLAG, mitoxantrone/cytarabine, or high-dose cytarabine) in adults with relapsed/refractory CD22-positive B-cell precursor ALL due to receive salvage 1 or 2 therapy; stratified by duration of first remission (<12 vs. ≥12 months), salvage line (1 vs. 2), and age (<55 vs. ≥55 years); co-primary endpoints; mid-trial SAP amendment changing endpoint status (OS reclassified from key secondary to co-primary endpoint in SAP v3.0, before unblinding)
- *Endpoints:* co-primary — hematologic remission (CR/CRi, EAC-adjudicated, with investigator assessment as a secondary check) and overall survival (OS); secondary — progression-free survival, duration of remission, and minimal residual disease (MRD) response rate
- *Primary analysis:* Chi-square test or Fisher's exact test (for cell counts under 5) for the CR/CRi comparison at 1-sided alpha=0.0125, with exact-CI methodology (F-distribution method for arm-level rates, normal approximation for the between-arm difference); Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified and unstratified) for the OS hazard ratio; Kaplan-Meier estimation for OS/PFS/duration of remission
- *Multiplicity:* alpha for the two co-primary endpoints (CR/CRi and OS) split evenly, each tested at 1-sided alpha=0.0125, from an overall 1-sided alpha=0.025
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design for OS with 2 planned interim analyses (~25% and at least 60% of 248 target OS events) permitting non-binding futility stopping at the first look and futility-or-efficacy stopping at the second (efficacy boundary 1-sided p<0.003 if exactly 149 events, futility if p>0.17), monitored by an external Data Monitoring Committee (eDMC); the final OS analysis (248 events) had not been reported at the time of this submission
- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation for missing binary/diary efficacy data (patients without a post-baseline disease assessment, including those never treated, counted as non-responders for CR/CRi), with a bias-direction sensitivity analysis assuming all untreated patients were responders; standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment for OS/PFS
- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented statistical concerns about the missed OS co-primary result — non-proportional hazards, an unexplained censoring-distribution imbalance between arms, and confounding of the OS comparison by a large imbalance in subsequent allogeneic HSCT use (43% inotuzumab vs. 11% control) — did not preclude standard approval, which instead rested on the significant CR/CRi result, MRD-negativity rate, and duration of response, alongside a boxed warning for hepatotoxicity/veno-occlusive disease tied to post-treatment HSCT

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study B1931022 (INO-VATE ALL): open-label, randomized (1:1), multicenter, global phase 3 trial comparing inotuzumab ozogamicin (divided-dose IV regimen, up to 6 cycles) to a defined investigator's-choice chemotherapy (FLAG, MXN/Ara-C, or HIDAC) in adults with relapsed/refractory CD22-positive B-cell precursor ALL eligible for salvage 1 or 2 therapy; conducted at approximately 190 sites over approximately 4 years
- Randomization stratified by duration of first remission (<12 vs. ≥12 months), salvage treatment line (1 vs. 2), and age at randomization (<55 vs. ≥55 years)
- Co-primary endpoints: hematologic remission (CR/CRi) adjudicated by an independent Endpoint Adjudication Committee (EAC), and overall survival (OS) from randomization to death from any cause; per FDA's reviewer comment, the protocol initially referred to CR/CRi as "the" primary endpoint and OS as a key secondary endpoint, and SAP version 3.0 later clarified that OS was in fact one of two co-primary endpoints
- Secondary endpoints: progression-free survival (with a defined censoring rule for assessment-interval gaps greater than 28 weeks with a prior post-baseline assessment, or greater than 12 weeks with none), duration of remission, and MRD-negativity rate
- Sample size/power: 218 patients (the "first-218" population) gave 88.5% power to detect a CR/CRi difference of 61% (inotuzumab) vs. 37% (control) at 1-sided alpha=0.0125; separately, 325 total patients (248 planned OS events) gave 80% power to detect an OS hazard ratio of 0.67 (median OS improvement from 4.3 to 6.45 months) at 1-sided alpha=0.0125; sample size was increased via Protocol Amendment 3 (March 28, 2014) after higher-than-expected early discontinuation and loss to survival follow-up in the control arm
- OS interim monitoring used a group-sequential design with 2 planned interim analyses (~25% and at least 60% of target OS events) for futility (first) and futility-or-efficacy (second), overseen by an external Data Monitoring Committee (eDMC)
- Results as reviewed by FDA: CR/CRi in the first 218 randomized patients was 81% (95% CI 72-88%) with inotuzumab vs. 29% (95% CI 21-39%) with chemotherapy; CR alone was 36% vs. 17%; MRD-negativity among responders was markedly higher with inotuzumab (78% vs. 38% in the ITT population). OS in the full ITT population (n=326) did not meet the pre-specified 1-sided p-value boundary of 0.0104 — stratified HR 0.77 (97.5% CI 0.578-1.026), median OS 7.7 vs. 6.7 months
- FDA's statistical reviewer flagged several issues with the OS result: non-proportional hazards (limiting interpretability of the log-rank/median-based estimate), an unexplained censoring-distribution imbalance between arms, imbalanced subsequent anti-cancer therapy and drug exposure, and — most notably — a large imbalance in subsequent allogeneic HSCT (43% inotuzumab vs. 11% control) that appeared to confound the OS comparison (nominally significant HSCT-by-treatment interaction; no OS difference in patients who did not proceed to HSCT, but a later survival advantage for inotuzumab among those who did, alongside more non-relapse mortality overall in the inotuzumab arm, chiefly hepatic veno-occlusive disease)
- Standard (not accelerated) approval was granted on the CR/CRi co-primary result plus supportive secondary endpoints (CR, duration of response, MRD-negativity), notwithstanding the missed OS co-primary endpoint; the increased risk of hepatotoxicity/VOD, especially with subsequent HSCT, was addressed with a boxed warning

Patient age at randomization (<55 or ≥55 years)."

At the second interim analysis, the study could have been stopped for futility or efficacy. However, the OS results show that the hazards in the two treatment arms were not proportional... The OS result was confounded by HSCT. The interaction between HSCT and treatment in the Cox model is nominally significant (nominal p<0.05)."

### 72. Copanlisib (Aliqopa) — NDA 209936

**Sponsor:** Bayer HealthCare Pharmaceuticals Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with relapsed follicular lymphoma (FL) who have received at least two prior systemic therapies — accelerated approval under 21 CFR Subpart H, based on tumor response rate and durability of response

**Approval date:** September 14, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** Study 16349 ("CHRONOS-1"), Part B, NCT01660451

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial, biomarker-agnostic relapsed/refractory indolent-NHL population (Part B restricted to FL, MZL, SLL, LPL/WM), fixed dosing regimen (60 mg IV weekly, 3 weeks on/1 week off)
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR: CR + PR by IRC per Revised Response Criteria for Malignant Lymphoma/Cheson 2007), duration of response (DoR, key secondary), progression-free survival and overall survival (secondary, not formally analyzed given single-arm design), FACT-Lym patient-reported outcome (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* sponsor's SAP pre-specified a one-sided exact binomial test against a performance goal (Exact binomial test against a pre-specified performance goal: H0: ORR ≤ 40%, Ha: ORR > 40%, alpha = 0.025 one-sided) with exact 95% Clopper-Pearson confidence interval; FDA's statistical reviewer instead treated all efficacy endpoints as Descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (point estimate + CI, no formal hypothesis test) given the single-arm design
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval based on a single-arm trial's surrogate response-rate endpoint (21 CFR 314.500-series/Subpart H analog for oncology); no FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee meeting was held; reviewer-documented departure from the sponsor's proposed inferential framework — FDA's statistical review states time-to-event endpoints "are not interpretable in single arm studies" and analyzed ORR/DoR/PFS/OS descriptively rather than via the sponsor's pre-specified hypothesis test

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 16349 Part B (CHRONOS-1): open-label, single-arm, multicenter Phase II trial of copanlisib monotherapy (60 mg IV on days 1, 8, and 15 of a 28-day cycle) in patients with relapsed or refractory indolent B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (follicular lymphoma, marginal zone lymphoma, small lymphocytic lymphoma, or lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma/Waldenström macroglobulinemia) who had received at least 2 prior lines of therapy including rituximab and an alkylating agent
- Primary efficacy endpoint: objective response rate (best response of CR or PR per IRC/central blinded review, using the Cheson 2007 lymphoma response criteria), assessed up to 16 weeks after the last FAS-eligible patient started treatment
- Secondary endpoints: progression-free survival, duration of response, overall survival, and FACT-Lym quality-of-life questionnaire (symptom subscale and total score) at week 16
- Analysis population: full analysis set (FAS) = all patients assigned to study treatment (primary efficacy population); a per-protocol set was also defined, excluding major-deviation patients
- Sponsor's SAP specified ORR would be analyzed via a one-sample exact one-sided binomial test (H0: true ORR ≤ 40% vs. Ha: ORR > 40%) at alpha = 0.025, with an exact Clopper-Pearson 95% CI; DoR was to be assessed against a null median of ≤8.5 months, testing whether the lower bound of the 2-sided 95% Kaplan-Meier CI exceeded 8.5 months; FACT-Lym change-from-baseline was planned for a two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test with Hodges-Lehmann CIs
- In the FL efficacy population (n=104 in the FAS), 61 patients achieved an objective response (ORR 58.7%), with a complete response rate of 14.4% and partial response rate of 44.2%; the 95% CI around the ORR excluded the 40% performance-goal threshold; median duration of response was 12.2 months
- FDA's statistical reviewer, while noting the sponsor's pre-specified inferential test, concluded that "due to the single arm study design, in FDA reviewer analysis, all the efficacy endpoints were analyzed with descriptive statistics without formal hypothesis testing," and separately stated that time-to-event endpoints (PFS, OS, DoR) "are not interpretable in single arm studies" — the accelerated approval rested on the magnitude and durability of the observed ORR rather than on rejection of the sponsor's formal null hypothesis
