- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2017/209936Orig1s000Ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/209936s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (Statistical Reviewer Xin (Cindy) Gao, PhD; combined Clinical/Statistical/Clin Pharm review package, NDA 209936) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209936Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (Study 16349/CHRONOS-1) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01660451 (no protocol/SAP posted in the Documents tab as of this review)
- Pivotal publication: Dreyling M, Morschhauser F, Bouabdallah K, et al. "Phase II study of copanlisib, a PI3K inhibitor, in relapsed or refractory, indolent or aggressive lymphoma." *Ann Oncol.* 2017;28(9):2169-2178. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1093/annonc/mdx289), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28633365/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Phase%20II%20study%20of%20copanlisib%2C%20a%20PI3K%20inhibitor%2C%20in%20relapsed%20or%20refractory%2C%20indolent%20or%20aggressive%20lymphoma)

**Other resources**

- Bayer's general data-sharing policy covers requests through the Vivli platform; trial-specific IPD availability for Study 16349/CHRONOS-1 was not individually confirmed.
- No FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee meeting was held for this application.
- Confirmatory trial requirement: continued approval was contingent on verification of clinical benefit in confirmatory trials (including the Phase III CHRONOS-3 and CHRONOS-4 studies in combination regimens); copanlisib was voluntarily withdrawn from the US market by Bayer in 2023 after a required confirmatory trial did not confirm clinical benefit — a fact outside the scope of the original 2017 approval package but relevant to how this accelerated approval concluded.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 209936, Statistical Analysis Plan section]* — "The Applicant analyzed the primary endpoint, ORR, by one-sample exact binomial test for hypothesis testing, with Null hypothesis H0: p ≤ p0, where p0 = 0.4 and Alternative hypothesis H1: p > p0. The null hypothesis was tested by exact one sided binomial test with type one error rate of alpha = 0.025. Point estimate along with its exact 95% Clopper Pearson confidence interval were calculated."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "Duration of response was evaluated for patients with at least one tumor response of complete response or partial response. The median and its 95% CI of duration of response were calculated based on Kaplan-Meier methodology and Kaplan-Meier plots were produced. The Applicant planned to compare the lower bound of the 2-sided 95% CI of the Kaplan-Meier estimator for the median DOR with 8.5 months, and null hypothesis of having a median ≤ 8.5 months would be rejected."

*[verbatim, same source, Reviewer Comment]* — "Due to the single arm study design, in FDA reviewer analysis, all the efficacy endpoints were analyzed with descriptive statistics without formal hypothesis testing." and, elsewhere in the same review, "Time-to-event endpoints are not interpretable in single arm studies."

*[verbatim, same source, benefit-risk summary]* — "The efficacy of copanlisib is primarily based on the results of a single-arm, open-label study evaluating copanlisib monotherapy in patients with relapsed follicular lymphoma... The complete response rate was 14.4% and partial response rate was 44.2%."

### 73. Abemaciclib (Verzenio) — NDA 208716

**Sponsor:** Eli Lilly and Company

**Indication approved:** In combination with fulvestrant, for women with hormone receptor (HR)-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer with disease progression following endocrine therapy (a companion monotherapy indication for prior chemotherapy-treated patients was approved concurrently, supported by the single-arm MONARCH 1 trial)

**Approval date:** September 28, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** MONARCH 2 (Study I3Y-MC-JPBL), NCT02107703

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, add-on design (novel agent + fulvestrant backbone vs. placebo + fulvestrant), event-driven trial, stratified by nature of disease (visceral metastases vs. bone-only vs. other) and sensitivity to endocrine therapy (primary vs. secondary resistance), mid-trial protocol/SAP amendments removing an endocrine-therapy-naive stratum and altering the interim-analysis plan
- *Endpoints:* progression-free survival (PFS, primary, investigator-assessed per RECIST 1.1; BICR-assessed PFS as a supportive/concordance analysis), overall survival (OS, gated key secondary), objective response rate/duration of response/clinical benefit rate/disease control rate (secondary), patient-reported outcomes (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test (1-sided), stratified by the randomization factors, with a stratified Cox proportional-hazards model for the hazard ratio and Wald CI; restricted-mean-difference-in-PFS supportive analysis (Irwin/Karrison/Meier method, KM-curve-area approach)
- *Multiplicity:* Gated Secondary Endpoint/gatekeeping strategy — OS tested only if PFS was significant, at a cumulative 1-sided alpha of 0.025, per Glimm et al. (2010) hierarchical group-sequential testing of multiple endpoints
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* 2-look group-sequential design for PFS (1 interim + 1 final analysis), interim planned at ~70% of information (265 of 378 planned events), nominal alpha of 0.00001 spent at interim (Slud-Wei boundary-calculation method) with the remainder spent at the final analysis (final boundary p=.02499996 assuming exact planned event counts); OS given up to 4 sequential hierarchical looks (at PFS interim, PFS final, 331 OS events, and 441 OS events) using a Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function with an O'Brien-Fleming-type boundary shape
- *Missing data/bias:* Ascertainment bias assessment (EDR/LDR) comparing investigator- vs. BICR-assessed PFS to check for investigator-favoring bias
- *Regulatory:* mid-trial SAP amendment changing endpoint status is not present here (PFS was primary throughout), but four sequential protocol/SAP amendments changed dose (200mg→150mg BID), excluded a previously-enrolled endocrine-naive stratum from the primary ITT population (with an FDA-requested sensitivity analysis including them), and removed a second planned interim analysis in response to a competitor CDK4/6-inhibitor's Phase 3 fulvestrant-combination results

**Trial design & endpoints**

- MONARCH 2 (I3Y-MC-JPBL): multicenter, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trial of abemaciclib + fulvestrant vs. placebo + fulvestrant in women with HR+/HER2- locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer previously treated with endocrine therapy; 669 patients randomized, with the primary efficacy population restricted to 630 "endocrine therapy pretreated" (EP) patients (446 abemaciclib, 223 placebo, after a protocol amendment excluded a smaller endocrine-therapy-naive cohort from the primary analysis)
- Randomization stratified by nature of disease (visceral metastases vs. bone-only metastatic disease vs. other) and sensitivity to endocrine therapy (primary vs. secondary resistance)
- Primary endpoint: investigator-assessed PFS (RECIST 1.1), tested via a 1-sided stratified log-rank test at cumulative alpha 0.025, with BICR-assessed PFS as a supportive/concordance analysis
- Key gated secondary endpoint: overall survival, tested only if PFS reached significance, using the same stratified log-rank framework, with up to four sequential analysis timepoints and a Lan-DeMets/O'Brien-Fleming-type alpha-spending function to preserve the overall 1-sided 0.025 error rate
- Other secondary endpoints: ORR, DoR, clinical benefit rate, disease control rate (all CR+PR or CR+PR+SD-based per RECIST), and patient-reported pain/quality-of-life instruments (BPI, EORTC QLQ-C30/BR23, EQ-5D-5L)
- Sample size: 378 PFS events (~630 EP patients, ~40% censoring) gave ~90% power to detect HR=0.703 (assumed median PFS improvement from 6.5 to ~9.25 months) at 1-sided alpha 0.025; the SAP underwent four versions, with amendments removing the endocrine-naive stratum from the primary ITT population, tightening the interim-analysis efficacy stopping boundary (to HR<0.56), and — following Phase III results from a competitor CDK4/6 inhibitor + fulvestrant combination — eliminating a second planned interim analysis and moving the (now single) interim/final PFS analysis earlier
- At the interim analysis (265 events), the pre-specified efficacy boundary was not crossed, so the trial continued to the final PFS analysis; the final analysis occurred at 379 events (1 more than the 378 planned), with investigator-assessed HR 0.553 (95% CI 0.449-0.681, p<0.0001; median PFS 16.4 vs. 9.3 months) and a concordant BICR-assessed HR of 0.460; OS was immature at the primary analysis data cutoff (133/441 planned events, HR 0.854, 95% CI 0.598-1.221, p=0.38) and was not formally significant, consistent with the gatekeeping rule requiring no OS claim at that time

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, ClinicalTrials.gov, SAP version 4, Section 4.1]* — "The primary objective of Study I3Y-MC-JPBL (JPBL) is to compare abemaciclib plus fulvestrant versus placebo plus fulvestrant with respect to progression-free survival (PFS) for women with hormone receptor (HR)+, human epidermal growth factor receptor (HER)2- locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer."

The interim analysis is planned to take place after approximately 265 (70% of the 378 planned) investigator-assessed PFS events have occurred. The final PFS analysis will be performed after 378 PFS events have occurred... Assuming a hazard ratio (HR) of 0.703, 378 events yields approximately 90% statistical power to detect superiority of the abemaciclib plus fulvestrant arm over the placebo plus fulvestrant arm with the use of a 1-sided log-rank test and a type I error of 0.025."

*[verbatim, same source, Section 6.7.2.2]* — "There is 1 planned interim analysis and 1 final analysis to test these hypotheses. At each analysis, the hypotheses above will be tested using a 1-sided stratified log rank test, stratified by nature of disease and prior sensitivity to endocrine therapy... At the interim analysis, the nominal alpha level will be.00001. The remaining alpha will be spent at the final analysis... If the analyses are performed at exactly 265 and 378 events then the boundary p-value at the final analysis will be.02499996."

*[verbatim, same source, Section 6.7.3.1 and 6.7.3.3]* — "Overall survival (OS) is an important secondary endpoint for this study. A gate-keeping strategy will be utilized to control the overall type I error at 0.025 (one-sided) for the secondary endpoint OS. That is, OS will be tested only if PFS is significant... To maintain the experiment-wise type I error rate, OS will be hierarchically tested in the following way: only if the test of PFS is significant will OS also be tested inferentially for significance (Glimm et al. 2010)... The cumulative 1-sided type I error rate of.025 will be maintained using the Lan-Demets method... an α-spending function corresponding to [an] O'Brien-Fleming type stopping boundary will be used for this interim efficacy analysis."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 208716]* — "The initial statistical analysis plan (SAP) provided for a 2-look group-sequential design of the primary endpoint of investigator assessed PFS... The SAP for MONARCH 2 had four versions. Versions 2 through 4 were approved after the first patient was enrolled." The review further documents that Amendment JPBL(b) "removed the inclusion of endocrine therapy naïve patients, increased the sample size for endocrine therapy pretreated patients, and updated the statistical analysis plan to include interim analyses... Note that the agency conducted a sensitivity analysis that included all randomized patients, and this exclusion has only a negligible difference when compared to the full ITT population," and that Amendment JPBL(d) "removed the second planned interim analysis of efficacy and changed the primary efficacy analysis to occur earlier given Phase 3 study results of fulvestrant in combination with another CDK 4/6 inhibitor."

*[verbatim, same source, Efficacy Results]* — "As described in the Statistical Analysis Plan section, the Applicant also conducted an interim analysis of PFS when 265 progression events had occurred. Based upon the results of the interim analysis, however, the study did not cross the pre-determined efficacy boundary, and the study continued until the final PFS analysis."

### 74. Acalabrutinib (Calquence) — NDA 210259

**Sponsor:** Acerta Pharma B.V.

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) who have received at least one prior therapy (accelerated approval)

**Approval date:** October 31, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** ACE-LY-004, NCT02213926

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label trial (approximately 70 global centers), Simon's two-stage design (original protocol enrolled two parallel cohorts — bortezomib-naive and bortezomib-exposed — each on a Simon's two-stage structure with a response-rate futility rule, later merged into one cohort by Protocol Amendment 4 after both cohorts cleared their stage-1 thresholds)
- *Endpoints:* Overall response rate (ORR, PR+CR per Lugano 2014 classification, investigator-assessed per protocol/SAP); dual primary-endpoint definition (protocol vs. regulatory) — investigator-assessed ORR remained the SAP's formal primary endpoint, while FDA (via a Type C meeting) required IRC-assessed ORR per Lugano classification for labeling purposes, so both were analyzed identically; key secondary endpoints: duration of response (DOR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), all also IRC-assessed
- *Primary analysis:* Descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (point estimate + CI, no formal hypothesis test) — "No formal statistical hypotheses will be tested" per SAP Section 5; exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval for the ORR point estimate; Kaplan-Meier estimation for DOR/PFS/OS
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Pre-merger interim futility analysis based on a response-rate stopping rule under the original Simon's two-stage cohort design (≥8/28 responders in the bortezomib-naive cohort, ≥3/12 in the bortezomib-exposed cohort, both thresholds exceeded in September 2015); no formal group-sequential alpha-spending function was used for the merged single-arm final analysis
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval (21 CFR 314.500) based on a single-arm ORR endpoint with a required confirmatory trial; final analysis timing amended (Protocol Amendment 6) to occur ~14 months after last-subject-enrolled, at FDA's request, to obtain ≥12 months of DOR follow-up in responders

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ACE-LY-004: Phase 2, single-arm, open-label, multicenter (~70 sites globally) trial of acalabrutinib 100 mg orally twice daily until progression or unacceptable toxicity, in 124 patients with histologically confirmed MCL who had relapsed after or were refractory to 1-5 prior treatment regimens
- Originally designed (Protocol Amendment 1) as two parallel cohorts — bortezomib-naive and bortezomib-exposed — each following a Simon's two-stage design; merged into a single cohort by Amendment 4 (November 2015) after an interim futility look (September 2015) showed both cohorts had exceeded their stage-1 continuation thresholds and after emerging acalabrutinib data (and published ibrutinib MCL data) suggested prior bortezomib exposure did not meaningfully affect response
- Primary endpoint: investigator-assessed ORR (PR or CR per Lugano 2014 classification for NHL) on the All-treated Population (all enrolled subjects receiving ≥1 dose); IRC-assessed ORR per Lugano classification was analyzed identically to meet FDA's labeling requirement, established via a Type C meeting, that the label reflect IRC assessment
- Secondary endpoints: DOR and PFS (investigator- and IRC-assessed per Lugano classification), OS, plus safety, PK, and PD endpoints
- Sample size: ~117 (117 planned; 124 actually enrolled) subjects, based on a one-sample chi-square test (0.025 one-sided significance level) giving >99% power to reject a null ORR ≤20% in favor of an alternative ORR ≥40% — used only for sample-size justification, not as a final formal hypothesis test (Section 5 of the SAP: "No formal statistical hypotheses will be tested")
- Results: investigator-assessed ORR 80.6% (FDA's MDR reports 80-81% depending on section), complete response rate 39.5% (95% CI: 30.9-48.7); FDA's Office of Hematology and Oncology Products recommended accelerated approval, noting uncertainty about the relationship of ORR/DOR to eventual OS and that 37.1% of patients had discontinued for disease progression as of the data cutoff (28 February 2017)
- Statistical methods: ORR and its 95% two-sided CI calculated using the exact binomial distribution; DOR, PFS, and OS estimated via Kaplan-Meier method with censoring-reason summaries; prespecified subgroup analyses of ORR/CR across 16 baseline covariates (age, sex, race, Ann Arbor stage, simplified MIPI risk group, ECOG status, bone marrow/extranodal/GI involvement, tumor bulk, refractory status, prior regimen count, prior proteasome inhibitor/stem-cell transplant/hyper-CVAD/lenalidomide exposure, region)

### 75. Lutetium Lu 177 dotatate (Lutathera) — NDA 208700

**Sponsor:** Advanced Accelerator Applications USA, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Somatostatin receptor-positive gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (GEP-NETs), including foregut, midgut, and hindgut neuroendocrine tumors in adults

**Approval date:** January 26, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** NETTER-1 (Study AAA-III-01), NCT01578239

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, open-label, active-controlled (vs. high-dose 60 mg octreotide LAR), biomarker-selected/enriched population (somatostatin receptor-positive tumors confirmed by OctreoScan imaging), event-driven trial (74 centrally confirmed PFS events for the primary analysis; 158 death events or 5 years post-last-randomization for the OS end-of-study), stratified by centrally-assessed somatostatin receptor scintigraphy tumor-uptake grade and duration on the most recent constant octreotide dose (≤6 vs. >6 months); randomization method changed mid-trial (July 2013, at FDA's advice) from a biased-coin method to a stratified permuted-block method after the first 28 patients
- *Endpoints:* Progression-free survival (PFS, IRC-assessed per RECIST 1.1, primary); key secondary endpoints objective response rate (ORR, best overall response of PR or CR, all randomized patients) and overall survival (OS); patient-reported outcomes/HRQoL (EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-G.I.NET21)
- *Primary analysis:* Unstratified log-rank test (specified as the primary PFS analysis method despite stratified randomization, per Protocol Amendment dated 25 March 2014), Kaplan-Meier estimation (median PFS/OS with 95% CIs), Fisher's exact test (ORR between-arm comparison) with exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval for each arm's ORR; stratified log-rank test and stratified Cox proportional-hazards model conducted as sensitivity analyses only
- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing of the two key secondary endpoints in the pre-specified order ORR then OS, to control the family-wise type I error rate for the secondary endpoints
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Group-sequential design for OS with an O'Brien-Fleming boundary (via EAST 6.6.1) across three looks — a pre-planned interim analysis (48/158 deaths, 2-sided alpha 0.00008), an FDA-requested updated analysis with no incremental alpha penalty (70/158 deaths, cumulative alpha 0.002), and a final analysis (158 deaths, alpha 0.049)
- *Missing data/bias:* Standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment (detailed, situation-by-situation censoring rules specified for PFS, including a 210-day missed-assessment threshold that FDA's statistical reviewer flagged as should have been 175 days per its own PFS-endpoint guidance); evaluation-time bias — FDA's reviewer found tumor-assessment timing from randomization was nominally different between arms at the first eight visits, traced to a delay in treatment initiation on the Lutathera arm rather than to differential on-study assessment scheduling once measured from treatment start
- *Regulatory:* Reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan — the applicant conducted neither of the two unplanned interim PFS/OS analyses envisioned by the original SAP, and FDA's statistical reviewer independently recalculated the OS alpha-spending allocation via EAST because the originally proposed 0.000085 interim alpha value was, in the reviewer's words, of "unclear" meaning given the actual projected event counts; SAP revised to Version 3 following FDA's Complete Response Letter on the original NDA submission

**Trial design & endpoints**

- NETTER-1 (AAA-III-01): international, open-label, randomized (1:1) Phase 3 trial at 41 sites in 8 countries, enrolling 229 patients with histologically confirmed, locally advanced/inoperable or metastatic, somatostatin receptor-positive midgut carcinoid tumors that had progressed on a fixed dose of octreotide LAR (20 or 30 mg, ≥12 weeks); an additional 22 non-randomized patients were enrolled in a parallel dosimetry/PK/ECG sub-study and excluded from the efficacy analysis
- Randomized to Lutathera (7.4 GBq every 8 weeks x4 doses, max cumulative 29.6 GBq, plus 30 mg octreotide LAR for symptom control; N=112) or high-dose octreotide LAR (60 mg every 4 weeks; N=111), stratified by centrally-assessed SSTR scintigraphy uptake grade (2, 3, or 4) and duration on the most recent constant octreotide dose (≤6 vs. >6 months); randomization method switched from a coin-toss method to a stratified permuted-block method partway through enrollment, at FDA's advice
- Primary endpoint: PFS (IRC-assessed per RECIST 1.1, time from randomization to progression or death), analyzed on the intent-to-treat population (termed the Full Analysis Set in the SAP/protocol) via an unstratified log-rank test, with Kaplan-Meier median PFS and 95% CIs
- Key secondary endpoints, tested hierarchically (ORR then OS) to control the family-wise error rate: ORR (Fisher's exact test, all randomized patients with measurable baseline disease per protocol, though FDA required the ITT-population analysis as primary) and OS (identical analysis methodology to PFS)
- Sample size: 74 centrally-confirmed PFS events (assuming 14- vs. 30-month median PFS) for 90% power at 2-sided alpha 0.05 to detect HR=0.47; 158 death events (assuming 32- vs. 50-month median OS) for 80% power at 1-sided alpha 2.5% to detect HR=0.64, with a planned interim OS analysis at the time of the PFS analysis
- Results: 91 IRC-confirmed PFS events; unstratified log-rank p<0.0001, HR 0.18 (95% CI: 0.11-0.29), median PFS not reached (Lutathera) vs. 8.5 months (95% CI: 5.8-9.1) (octreotide); ORR 12.9% (95% CI: 7-19%) vs. 3.5% (95% CI: 0.1-7%), Fisher's exact p=0.0148; OS immature at both the pre-planned interim (48 deaths) and FDA-requested updated (70 deaths, updated cutoff June 30, 2016) analyses, neither crossing its O'Brien-Fleming boundary, with median OS not reached in either arm at the time of review
- FDA's statistical reviewer devoted substantial attention to potential evaluation-time/assessment-timing bias given the trial's open-label design and asymmetric tumor-assessment timing from randomization between arms, tracing the asymmetry to a delay in treatment initiation on the Lutathera arm (an artifact of following FDA's ITT-analysis principle) rather than to differential assessment scheduling once timed from actual treatment start

PFS was defined as the time from the date of randomization to the date of tumor progression using RECIST 1.1 criteria as assessed by the IRC or death from any cause."

### 76. Apalutamide (Erleada) — NDA 210951

**Sponsor:** Janssen Biotech, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of patients with non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (nmCRPC)

**Approval date:** February 14, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** SPARTAN (Study ARN-509-003), NCT01946204

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven trial, 2:1 randomization ratio, stratified by PSA doubling time (≤6 vs. >6 months), bone-sparing agent use (yes/no), and presence of locoregional disease (N0 vs. N1)
- *Endpoints:* metastasis-free survival (MFS, primary, per blinded independent central review [BICR] using RECIST v1.1 — time to first BICR-confirmed bone/soft-tissue distant metastasis or death from any cause) — secondary endpoints time to metastasis (TTM), progression-free survival (PFS), time to symptomatic progression (a novel composite of skeletal-related events, pain-driven new anti-cancer therapy, or locoregional progression requiring surgery/radiation), overall survival (OS), time to initiation of cytotoxic chemotherapy
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, stratified Cox proportional-hazards model for the hazard ratio, Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing of secondary endpoints in a pre-specified order (TTM→PFS→time to symptomatic progression→OS→time to cytotoxic chemotherapy), each endpoint tested at 2-sided alpha=0.05 only if every endpoint above it in the hierarchy was statistically significant
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* no interim analysis planned for the primary endpoint (MFS) or for TTM/PFS; group-sequential design for time to symptomatic progression, OS, and time to cytotoxic chemotherapy using an O'Brien-Fleming-type alpha-spending function, with event-count re-estimation targeting 90% conditional power and an inverse normal p-value combination method to combine interim- and final-stage test statistics under the resulting adaptive design
- *Missing data/bias:* sensitivity analysis of MFS excluding 47 patients at sites where shipping/labeling documents created a potential unblinding risk; missing supplemental-treatment data for 8 of 127 patients in the symptomatic-progression composite were reviewed individually and censored rather than imputed, with results consistent with the original analysis
- *Regulatory:* Special Protocol Assessment (SPA) agreement (November 2012) later rescinded by FDA (May 2017) after a March 2017 SAP amendment changed the secondary-endpoint multiplicity procedure to a hierarchical adaptive group-sequential design while the trial was already fully enrolled — FDA required OS to be tested at the time of the primary MFS analysis at a small allocated alpha rather than deferred; Fast Track designation granted August 2017 based on SPARTAN topline results; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- SPARTAN (ARN-509-003): multicenter, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trial of apalutamide (240 mg/day) + ADT vs. placebo + ADT in men with high-risk non-metastatic (M0) castration-resistant prostate cancer, defined by PSA doubling time (PSADT) ≤10 months during continuous ADT; 1207 patients randomized (806 apalutamide, 401 placebo), enrolled October 2013-December 2016
- Randomization centrally via IVRS, stratified by PSADT (≤6 vs. >6 months), bone-sparing agent use (yes/no), and presence of locoregional disease (N0 vs. N1)
- Primary endpoint: metastasis-free survival (MFS) — time from randomization to first BICR-confirmed radiographically detectable bone or soft-tissue distant metastasis, or death from any cause, whichever occurred first; radiographic scans (bone scan, CT/MRI) performed throughout the study, with new bone lesions requiring second-modality confirmation; separate US- and ex-US-regulatory censoring rules were pre-specified for patients lost to follow-up or who started new anti-cancer therapy before documented progression
- Secondary endpoints, tested hierarchically only if MFS and every preceding secondary endpoint reached significance: time to metastasis (TTM), progression-free survival (PFS, includes locoregional progression), time to symptomatic progression (composite of skeletal-related events, pain/symptom-driven new anti-cancer therapy, or locoregional progression requiring surgery/radiation), overall survival (OS), and time to initiation of cytotoxic chemotherapy
- Sample size: 90% power to detect HR=0.70 for MFS (30% risk reduction) at 2-sided alpha=0.05, requiring ~372 MFS events and ~1200 randomized patients (assumed placebo-arm median MFS 25 months); separately powered at 85% to detect HR=0.75 for OS (427 death events) assuming placebo-arm median OS of 49 months
- Interim analysis: none planned for MFS, TTM, or PFS; one interim analysis for time to symptomatic progression and up to two interim analyses for OS and time to cytotoxic chemotherapy, using an O'Brien-Fleming-type alpha-spending function with event-count re-estimation (90% conditional power) and an inverse normal p-value combination method to preserve strong control of the familywise type I error rate under the adaptive design
- Primary analysis: MFS compared via a two-sided stratified log-rank test (stratified by the three randomization factors) at the 0.05 significance level, with the hazard ratio and 95% CI from a correspondingly stratified Cox proportional-hazards model; non-stratified log-rank test provided as a sensitivity analysis
- Results: MFS HR 0.28 (95% CI 0.23-0.35, p<0.0001; median 40.51 vs. 16.20 months); TTM HR 0.27 (95% CI 0.22-0.34, p<0.0001); PFS HR 0.29 (95% CI 0.24-0.36, p<0.0001); time to symptomatic progression (interim, 28% of planned events) HR 0.45 (95% CI 0.31-0.64, p<0.0001, crossed the O'Brien-Fleming efficacy boundary of p=0.00008); OS (interim, 24% of planned events) HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.47-1.04, p=0.07), which did not cross the pre-specified efficacy boundary (p=0.000012), so no alpha was allocated to time to cytotoxic chemotherapy and OS was reported descriptively in labeling

### 77. Fosnetupitant/palonosetron (Akynzeo) — NDA 210493

**Sponsor:** Helsinn Healthcare SA

**Indication approved:** Prevention, in combination with dexamethasone, of acute and delayed nausea and vomiting associated with initial and repeat courses of highly emetogenic cancer chemotherapy (HEC) — an intravenous formulation of the same netupitant/palonosetron (NEPA) combination approved as oral Akynzeo capsules (NDA 205718, entry above); labeling explicitly states the drug "has not been studied for the prevention of nausea and vomiting associated with anthracycline plus cyclophosphamide chemotherapy" (AC), so the IV indication is narrower than the oral capsule's AC-inclusive HEC/MEC indication

**Approval date:** April 19, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** No single dedicated efficacy trial of the IV fosnetupitant/palonosetron fixed-dose combination against placebo was conducted. FDA instead accepted a three-study bridging program, agreed with the sponsor in a Type B teleconference on February 4, 2015: Study PALO-15-17 (non-inferiority trial isolating the palonosetron component, IV 30-minute infusion vs. the already-approved IV 30-second bolus), NCT02557035; Study PNET-12-23 (Phase 1 relative-bioavailability/bioequivalence bridging study, IV fosnetupitant vs. oral netupitant, healthy subjects; no ClinicalTrials.gov record found — appears unregistered, a Phase 1 European single-center study); and Study NEPA-15-18 (Phase 3 safety trial, IV NEPA FDC vs. oral Akynzeo capsules, efficacy assessed only descriptively), NCT02517021

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* PALO-15-17 — randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled, parallel-group, non-inferiority trial isolating a single component (palonosetron infusion duration) rather than the fixed-dose combination itself; NEPA-15-18 — randomized, double-blind, active-controlled trial (oral NEPA capsules as comparator) powered only for safety, with efficacy as a descriptive secondary objective; PNET-12-23 — Phase 1 relative-bioavailability/bioequivalence bridging study. The overall pattern — a component-level non-inferiority trial plus a PK bioequivalence bridge plus a safety-only comparative trial, substituted for any dedicated efficacy trial of the new formulation/combination — is not currently captured by a single Design term in `Keyword_Taxonomy.md`; flagged as a candidate new term, "PK/bioequivalence-bridged formulation approval (in lieu of a dedicated efficacy trial for the new formulation)"
- *Endpoints:* Complete Response (CR) — no emesis + no rescue medication, by CINV phase (acute 0-24h, delayed >24-120h, overall 0-120h) — primary endpoint of PALO-15-17 (acute phase only) and a descriptive secondary endpoint of NEPA-15-18; NEPA-15-18's actual primary endpoint was percentage of patients with adverse events (a safety, not efficacy, endpoint)
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by sex and country, for the non-inferiority comparison of CR proportions (PALO-15-17); descriptive statistics only, no formal hypothesis test, for the CR comparison in NEPA-15-18
- *Multiplicity:* Unadjusted secondary/supportive testing (single formal primary endpoint) — PALO-15-17 had one primary endpoint (CR, acute phase) with no multiplicity adjustment; delayed- and overall-phase CR were explicitly analyzed with no pre-specified non-inferiority margin and no alpha control, "for descriptive purposes" only
- *Missing data/bias:* Non-responder imputation for missing binary/diary efficacy data — patients missing diary data on emetic episodes or rescue-medication use were counted as treatment failures (PALO-15-17)
- *Regulatory:* FDA-negotiated multi-study bridging program substituting PK bioequivalence + single-component non-inferiority + safety-only comparison for a dedicated efficacy trial of the new IV combination (505(b) full NDA referencing the sponsor's own prior oral NDA's efficacy data by extrapolation); an interdisciplinary split verdict in which FDA's statistical reviewer limited her formal efficacy conclusion to the acute phase only (delayed-phase CR rate 9-12 percentage points lower than oral NEPA in two separate comparisons) and explicitly deferred the delayed-phase efficacy question to the clinical pharmacology reviewer, whose netupitant-exposure bioequivalence argument is what ultimately supported the delayed-phase label claim — not currently captured by a Regulatory term in `Keyword_Taxonomy.md`; flagged as a candidate new term, "Interdisciplinary resolution of an efficacy question via PK bridging after biostatistics review limited its conclusion to a subset of the labeled indication"; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- **Study PALO-15-17** (NCT02557035): Phase 3, multicenter (88 sites, mostly Eastern Europe/former Soviet states, no US sites), randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, parallel-group, non-inferiority trial in chemotherapy-naive HEC patients (cisplatin ≥70 mg/m², cyclophosphamide ≥1500 mg/m², carmustine >250 mg/m², dacarbazine, or mechlorethamine — AC-based HEC excluded); patients randomized 1:1 (stratified by sex and country) to a single dose of palonosetron 0.25 mg as either a 30-minute IV infusion (the proposed Akynzeo IV posology) or the already-approved 30-second IV bolus (Aloxi IV), each with oral dexamethasone, using a double-dummy design so every patient received one infusion and one bolus (one active, one placebo); planned N=440 (220/arm), 441 randomized
- Primary endpoint: proportion of patients with Complete Response (CR — no emetic episode and no rescue medication) in the acute phase (0-24h) after a single HEC cycle; non-inferiority margin fixed at -15% on the two-sided 99% CI for the CMH stratum-adjusted risk difference (infusion minus bolus), a margin carried over from the oral Akynzeo program's PALO-10-01 bridging trial and ultimately traced to a literature-based "modeled historical placebo" meta-analysis (PALO-01-23) since placebo-controlled CINV trials are no longer considered ethical
- Result (FAS): CR acute phase 82.7% (186/225) infusion vs. 86.5% (186/215) bolus; CMH risk difference -3.8% (99% CI: -12.2%, 4.7%) — since the lower bound was well above -15%, non-inferiority of the 30-minute infusion was demonstrated; FDA's statistical reviewer independently confirmed this result
- Secondary/delayed- and overall-phase CR endpoints were explicitly not governed by any pre-specified non-inferiority margin or multiplicity control and were reported "only for descriptive purposes" — FDA's clinical reviewer noted IV palonosetron alone has never carried a delayed-phase HEC indication, so these secondary analyses had no bearing on labeling
- **Study PNET-12-23**: Phase 1, single ascending-dose, relative-bioavailability/bioequivalence study in 158 healthy subjects, comparing 260 mg IV fosnetupitant (a phosphate prodrug of netupitant) to the already-approved 300 mg oral netupitant dose; bioequivalence criteria were met for AUC0-120h and AUC0-∞, but Cmax for IV fosnetupitant was ~1.5x the oral Cmax and fell outside BE bounds — a difference that, per the Type B meeting record, triggered FDA's requirement for the dedicated HEC safety trial (NEPA-15-18) rather than allowing the AUC-based PK bridge to stand alone
- **Study NEPA-15-18** (NCT02517021): Phase 3, multicenter (80 sites, including US), randomized, double-blind, active-controlled trial in HEC patients (AC-based HEC excluded) receiving up to 4 repeated chemotherapy cycles; randomized 1:1 to IV NEPA FDC (260 mg fosnetupitant/0.25 mg palonosetron, 30-minute infusion) or oral NEPA FDC (300 mg netupitant/0.5 mg palonosetron capsule), both with dexamethasone; N=405 enrolled. Primary endpoint was safety (percentage of patients with adverse events over 4 cycles) — explicitly a safety, not efficacy, study, sized so that if a given AE were not observed in the ~100 patients treated at Cycle 4 with the IV product, an AE incidence ≥3% could be excluded with 95% confidence; CR by phase was a descriptive secondary endpoint only, with the study report stating results "cannot be claimed in the labeling"
- Result (FAS, Cycle 1, delayed phase): CR 78.3% (159/203) IV NEPA vs. 87.6% (176/201) oral NEPA, CMH risk difference -9.0% (95% CI: -15.8%, 2.2%) — a 9-percentage-point numerically lower response rate for the IV product that FDA's statistical reviewer flagged (compounded by a separately observed 12-point gap versus the oral program's original HEC pivotal trial, NETU-07-07) as unresolved by a formal non-inferiority test, since none was pre-specified for this comparison
- FDA's statistical review concluded efficacy was formally demonstrated only for the acute phase (via PALO-15-17); whether the delayed-phase claim was supportable was explicitly "deferred to the clinical pharmacology reviewer's evaluation" — which concluded, based on the PNET-12-23 AUC bioequivalence of fosnetupitant/netupitant metabolites (assuming netupitant's efficacy is exposure-driven), that comparable delayed-phase efficacy could be expected despite the numerically lower observed CR rates in NEPA-15-18 and NETU-07-07
- Supportive Phase 1 studies not reviewed for efficacy: PNET-13-63 (drug-drug interaction with oral dexamethasone, healthy volunteers) and NEPA-15-19 (single-cycle PK/safety study of the IV FDC in cancer patients)

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, embedded Statistical Review (Ref ID 4197201), §1 Executive Summary, p.3]*

> "The applicant submitted one phase 3 efficacy study with IV palonosetron in cancer patients (PALO-15-17) and one phase 3 safety study with fosnetupitant-palonosetron FDC (NEPA-15-18) to support the use of IV fosnetupitant-palonosetron FDC in preventing acute and delayed nausea and vomiting associated with initial and repeat courses of highly emetogenic cancer chemotherapy... Based on the FDA's advice after negotiation, the ultimate requirements for the IV NEPA FDC clinical development program should include a bioequivalence trial (PNET-12-23), a non-inferiority (NI) efficacy trial on the palonosetron component (PALO-15-17), a clinical safety trial (NEPA-15-18) and two clinical pharmacology trials."

*[verbatim, same source, §2.1.1 Regulatory History, Type B teleconference 2/4/2015, p.6-7]*

> "The favorable PK, safety and efficacy data from PNET-12-23, NEPA-15-18 and PALO-15-17 studies collectively comprise the IV NEPA FDC NDA clinical development program as agreed with FDA and are considered adequate to support the proposed indication cited above... 'Yes, we agree the planned clinical development program appears adequate for NDA submission, as proposed. The adequacy of the submission for the indication proposed will be a review issue.'"

*[verbatim, same source, §2.1.1, FDA Biostatistics Written Replies, 6/06/2016, p.8]*

> "Please submit your revised phase 3 protocols and SAP for review prior to starting your studies. Note that key features of your statistical plan, including primary and secondary endpoints and analyses, type I error control, missing data handling strategy, etc., should be pre-specified in your protocol and not introduced in the SAP after start of study."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.2.2 Statistical Reviewer's Findings and Comments, p.17-18]*

> "1. (Efficacy Findings for Study PALO-15-17) The statistical reviewer confirmed the applicant's analysis results for the primary endpoint. We concluded that the study data support non-inferiority of palonosetron 0.25 mg administered as a 30-min IV infusion compared with administration as a 30-sec IV bolus, in terms of the proportion of patients reporting CR... in the acute phase. 2. (Efficacy Results for Study NEPA-15-18) The rate of complete response (CR) in the delayed phase for IV NEPA FDC arm was observed to be 9% more lower than that for the concurrent oral Akynzeo arm in the safety Study NEPA-15-18. In addition, the observed CR rate in the delayed phase was 12% more lower than that for oral Akynzeo in Study NETU-07-07. Whether the data supported the efficacy of delayed phase for IV fosnetupitant-palonosetron is deferred to the clinical pharmacology reviewer's evaluation."

*[verbatim, same source, §5.2 Conclusions and Recommendations, p.21]*

> "Study PALO-15-17 is positive and support the indication of preventing acute nausea and vomiting associated with initial and repeat courses of highly emetogenic cancer chemotherapy (HEC)... In conclusion, data of Study PALO-15-17 indeed supported the efficacy of IV Akynzeo in preventing the nausea and vomiting associated with initial and repeat courses of highly emetogenic cancer chemotherapy (HEC) only for the acute phase."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, §6.1.1 Study Design (PALO-15-17), Primary Efficacy Analysis and NI Margin, p.51]*

> "To test the null hypothesis, the lower limit of the two-sided 99% CI for the difference in proportion of patients with CR in the acute phase between palonosetron IV 30-minute infusion and palonosetron IV 30-second bolus will be compared to the pre-set noninferiority margin set at -15%. The null hypothesis can be written as: H0: πT – πC ≤ –Δ. H0 will be tested against the alternative hypothesis: H1: πT – πC > –Δ... Δ is the non-inferiority margin which is fixed at 15%."

*[verbatim, same source, §6.1.1, Adjustment for Multiplicity, p.51]*

> "No adjustment for multiplicity was made in the study. All secondary efficacy endpoints were intended to provide supportive evidence related to the primary objective or additional clinical characterization of treatment effect, the results on these were interpreted in only a descriptive manner."

*[verbatim, same source, §6.1.1, Missing Data, p.51]*

> "With respect to missing data, any patients who did not provide data about the occurrence of emetic episodes and rescue medication intake or that did not provide a full set of these data throughout the 24 hours after HEC administration were considered as treatment failures (i.e., non-responders) for the primary efficacy analysis."

*[verbatim, same source, §6.1.2 Study Results (PALO-15-17), Efficacy Results, p.62]*

> "The analysis of FAS revealed that 186 (82.7%) patients in the infusion group reported CR in the acute phase, as did 186 (86.5%) patients in the bolus group. The stratum-adjusted CMH method for difference in proportions, stratified by sex and country, with associated two sided 99% CI was used for non-inferiority testing. The difference in proportion between the 30-minute infusion and 30-second bolus treatment groups was -3.8% (99% CI: -12.2%, 4.7%). Since the lower limit of the two-sided 99% CI for the difference in proportions was greater (i.e., closer to zero) than the pre-defined non-inferiority margin of -15%, non-inferiority of palonosetron 30-min infusion vs. 30-sec bolus was demonstrated."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, §4.5.3 Pharmacokinetics, Clinical Pharmacology Review excerpt, p.30-31]*

> "Because Akynzeo IV is administered over 30 minutes while Aloxi is administered via IV push over 30 seconds, the Cmax of Aloxi will be higher than that from Akynzeo IV while AUC will be comparable because the dose is the same. Therefore, safety of the 30-minute infusion of palonosetron is at least comparable if not better than Aloxi administered by IV push. On the other hand, the sponsor conducted a pivotal phase 3 study to evaluate the potential difference in efficacy due to the lower Cmax and demonstrated that the efficacy of palonosetron IV administered over 30 minutes is not inferior to Aloxi injectable... Assuming the efficacy of netupitant is based solely on netupitant levels..., these BE study results indicate that the efficacy of the oral netupitant and the intravenous fosnetupitant component of the two products can be expected to be comparable. However, the safety of the higher netupitant Cmax associated with the intravenous product must be addressed. The safety was evaluated in Study NEPA 15-18."

This is a genuine, unusually explicit example of a follow-on IV formulation approved almost entirely by evidentiary bridging rather than a dedicated efficacy trial: the sponsor's own biostatistics reviewer confirmed non-inferiority for only one endpoint, in one phase, in one component (palonosetron infusion duration) of a two-drug combination, then formally handed off the harder question — whether the new IV combination's numerically lower delayed-phase response rates (9 and 12 percentage points below two different oral-NEPA comparators) still supported a delayed-phase efficacy claim — to a different discipline's PK bioequivalence argument. The approved label's delayed-phase claim for Akynzeo IV therefore rests on an assumption (netupitant efficacy is exposure-driven, and fosnetupitant/netupitant AUC is bioequivalent) rather than on a statistical test of clinical response in the delayed phase.

### 78. Encorafenib (Braftovi) — NDA 210496

**Sponsor:** Array BioPharma Inc.

**Indication approved:** In combination with binimetinib, for the treatment of patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma with a BRAF V600E or V600K mutation, as detected by an FDA-approved test

**Approval date:** June 27, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** COLUMBUS (Study CMEK162B2301), NCT01909453

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled, two-part trial (Part 1: 1:1:1 encorafenib+binimetinib "Combo 450" vs. vemurafenib vs. encorafenib monotherapy 300 mg; Part 2: 3:1 encorafenib+binimetinib "Combo 300" vs. encorafenib monotherapy, added mid-trial via protocol amendment at FDA's request to address a contribution-of-components concern), event-driven trial, biomarker-selected/enriched population (BRAF V600E/K mutation-positive), companion diagnostic co-approval (bioMerieux THxID BRAF assay), mid-trial SAP amendment adding a second trial part after FDA raised a design objection
- *Endpoints:* progression-free survival (PFS, primary, per blinded independent central review [BIRC] using RECIST v1.1), overall survival (OS, other secondary — not tested for statistical significance at time of approval), objective response rate (ORR)/duration of response (DoR) (secondary), patient-reported outcomes/HRQoL (FACT-M melanoma subscale, EQ-5D-5L, EORTC QLQ-C30 — exploratory, no alpha allocated)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, stratified Cox proportional-hazards model, Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing across four pre-specified tests (Test 1: PFS Combo 450 vs. vemurafenib; Test 2: PFS Combo 450 vs. encorafenib; Test 3: PFS Combo 300 vs. pooled encorafenib; Test 4: OS Combo 450 vs. vemurafenib), overall two-sided alpha of 0.05
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design for OS only (one planned interim analysis at 75% of target deaths), Gamma-family alpha-spending function (parameter 1; 0.042 spent at interim, 0.008 at final)
- *Missing data/bias:* pre-specified "backdated" censoring sensitivity analysis for PFS (events after ≥2 missed tumor assessments backdated to the visit following the last adequate assessment) to address potential bias from differential missed-assessment patterns; separate sensitivity analysis restricting Test 3 to only concurrently-randomized Part 2 patients, because Part 1 and Part 2 used separate randomizations
- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented mid-trial design change driven by FDA feedback (Part 2 added after FDA told the sponsor that comparing a higher-dose combination arm to a lower-dose monotherapy arm could not isolate binimetinib's contribution); FDA statistical reviewer explicitly flagged that Test 3's cross-part comparison "may be biased"; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- COLUMBUS (CMEK162B2301, Protocol Version 4): Phase III, randomized, open-label, multicenter, two-part trial in adults with unresectable or metastatic BRAF V600E/K-mutant melanoma; Part 1 randomized 577 patients 1:1:1 to encorafenib 450 mg once daily + binimetinib 45 mg twice daily ("Combo 450"), encorafenib 300 mg once daily alone, or vemurafenib 960 mg twice daily; Part 2 (added by Protocol Amendment 3, 04-Nov-2014) randomized 344 additional patients 3:1 to encorafenib 300 mg + binimetinib 45 mg ("Combo 300") or encorafenib 300 mg alone
- Randomization stratified by AJCC stage (IIIB/IIIC/IVM1a/IVM1b vs. IVM1c), ECOG performance status (0 vs. 1), and (in Part 1 only, per an interim protocol version later reverted) prior first-line immunotherapy; BRAF mutation subtype (V600E vs. V600K) was originally a planned stratification factor but was dropped before enrollment given its expected low prevalence, per the protocol
- Primary endpoint: PFS (BIRC-assessed, RECIST v1.1) for Combo 450 vs. vemurafenib (Test 1); key secondary endpoints were PFS for Combo 450 vs. encorafenib monotherapy (Test 2, intended to assess binimetinib's contribution) and PFS for Combo 300 vs. pooled encorafenib monotherapy patients from both parts (Test 3); other secondary endpoints included OS (Combo 450 vs. vemurafenib, and vs. encorafenib), ORR, and DoR
- Sample size: Part 1's 577 patients gave 80% power to detect HR=0.667 (median PFS 8→12 months) at overall two-sided alpha=0.05, and 90% power for HR=0.58 (Combo 450 vs. vemurafenib); Part 2's 344 patients (pooled with 194 Part-1 encorafenib patients, 538 total for Test 3) gave 80% power to detect HR=0.667 (median PFS 8→11 months); OS was separately powered assuming 17- vs. 22-month medians, with one interim analysis planned after 75% of target deaths, using a Gamma(1) alpha-spending function allocating 0.042 to the interim and 0.008 to the final analysis — the FDA statistical reviewer noted this gave OS analyses "low" power relative to the PFS analyses
- Statistical methods: stratified log-rank test for all PFS/OS comparisons (stratified by AJCC stage and ECOG PS; the immunotherapy stratum was dropped from the analysis-level stratification once the two levels were combined to avoid empty strata), Cox proportional-hazards model (same stratification factors) for hazard ratios, Kaplan-Meier estimation for survival curves; overall type I error across the four hierarchical tests was controlled by testing in the fixed order Test 1 → Test 2 → Test 3 → Test 4 (OS), each at the nominal two-sided 0.05 level, conditional on the preceding test(s) reaching significance
- Result: Test 1 (Combo 450 vs. vemurafenib) was positive — median PFS 14.9 vs. 7.3 months, stratified HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.41-0.71), stratified log-rank p<0.0001 — and supported approval; Test 2 (Combo 450 vs. encorafenib) was not significant (median 14.9 vs. 9.6 months, HR 0.75 [0.56-1.00], two-sided p=0.0513); because Test 2 failed, Test 3 (Combo 300 vs. pooled encorafenib) had no formal hypothesis test performed under the hierarchical rule, though it showed a numerical improvement (median 12.9 vs. 9.2 months, HR 0.77 [0.61-0.97]); OS data were immature at the time of the primary analysis and were not formally tested
- FDA's reviewer explicitly stated that COLUMBUS "was not adequately designed to demonstrate that the efficacy of Combo 450 is superior to Combo 300 for any endpoint" because the two parts were randomized at different times, and separately flagged that Test 3's pooling of Part 1 and Part 2 encorafenib patients "may be biased" since the two parts had independent randomizations

**Other resources**

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held for this NDA — the Multi-Disciplinary Review states plainly, "No advisory committee meeting was held for this NDA."
- Array BioPharma was acquired by Pfizer in 2019, after this 2018 approval; sponsor of record at approval was Array BioPharma Inc. Pfizer participates in clinical-trial data-sharing arrangements generally, but trial-specific IPD availability for COLUMBUS was not individually confirmed; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing for this trial was located during this review.
- Postmarketing commitments (per the approval letter) were pharmacokinetic drug-interaction studies (moderate CYP3A4 inducer effect on encorafenib exposure; encorafenib's effect on sensitive CYP substrates), plus submission of the final COLUMBUS clinical study report to update the label with mature OS data — none were efficacy-confirmatory trials, since this was a regular (not accelerated) approval.
- Cross-reference: binimetinib (Mektovi, NDA 210498) was approved the same day, in combination with encorafenib, based on the same COLUMBUS trial; see that entry for details specific to binimetinib's own review record. The two NDAs share one Multi-Disciplinary Review package and one statistical analysis.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review and Evaluation, NDA 210496, Reference ID 4282494, §8.1.1 Statistical Analysis Plan]* — "The stratified log-rank test was used for PFS and OS endpoints in all analyses, with an overall significance level of 5% (two-sided). The Kaplan-Meier method was used to estimate the PFS and OS curves for each treatment arm, and the Cox proportional hazards model was used for the estimation of hazard ratios for comparisons between arms. Overall type I error was controlled among these endpoints by a hierarchical testing procedure, where the order of testing was Test 1: PFS (Combo 450 vs. vemurafenib) Test 2: PFS (Combo 450 vs. encorafenib) Test 3: PFS (Combo 300 vs. encorafenib) Test 4: OS (Combo 450 vs. vemurafenib)."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.1.1]* — "The sample size for Part 1 of this study was estimated using the assumption that the median PFS was 7 months for the vemurafenib arm and 8 months for the encorafenib arm. A total of 577 patients (using a 1:1:1 randomization) were randomized. The study was designed to detect an improvement in median PFS from 8 months in the encorafenib arm to 12 months in the Combo 450 arm. This improvement corresponds to a hazard ratio of 0.667 with 80% power while maintaining an overall significance level of 5% (two-sided)."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.1.1, citing COLUMBUS SAP v4 Table 3-1, dated 28-Mar-2017]* — "The trial was also designed to test OS, using the assumption that the median OS would be 17 months in the vemurafenib arm and 22 months in the Combo 450 arm. One interim analysis was planned for OS after 75% of deaths had occurred... Overall type I error was controlled for the interim analysis with the α-spending function using a Gamma function with parameter 1. This spending function had an alpha allocation of 0.042 to the interim analysis and 0.008 to the final analysis. Reviewer's comment: The power for the OS analysis is low relative to the power for the PFS analyses."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.1.1 Protocol Amendments, quoting FDA correspondence to the applicant dated April 28, 2014]* — "...comparing encorafenib plus binimetinib to encorafenib alone will also not allow FDA to determine the contribution of binimetinib to the combination because the combination arm uses a higher dose of encorafenib (450 mg) than the encorafenib alone arm (300 mg)…the encorafenib alone arm should use the same or higher dose than the dose of encorafenib as used in the combination arm. Otherwise, the contribution of binimetinib to the effect of the combination therapy may not [be] interpretable."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.1.1, quoting protocol v3]* — "Due to the relatively low expected prevalence of patients with prior immunotherapy (around 15%), the two prior immunotherapy strata (yes and no) will be combined at the time of the analysis to avoid small or empty strata. The log-rank test will therefore be stratified by the two randomization strata variables cancer stage and ECOG PS."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.1.3, Sensitivity Analysis for Test 3, quoting SAP v.4]* — "Stratified analyses for PFS (i.e. log-rank-test, Kaplan-Meier estimates and plots and Cox regression) will be repeated with data only for patients enrolled during Part 2 of the study. This will be performed separately for data assessed by BIRC and locally."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.1.3, Sensitivity Analyses for Test 2]* — "Array pre-specified a sensitivity analysis for PFS that would repeat the primary analysis with a censoring rule that backdates events occurring after one or more missing tumor assessments. Events were to be backdated to the assessment following the last adequate assessment: 8 weeks (or 12 weeks if the patient had been on treatment long enough) after the last adequate tumor assessment... If missed assessments are related to progression, the primary analysis may be biased, as patients who miss two or more assessments are censored at the last adequate assessment, even if they progress after the second missed assessment."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.3 Statistical Issues]* — "COLUMBUS was not adequately designed to demonstrate that the efficacy of Combo 450 is superior to Combo 300 for any endpoint. Because Part 1 and Part 2 were randomized at different times, comparisons of Combo 450 to Combo 300 may not be meaningful... The test pre-specified to assess this comparison, Test 3, utilized patients from both Parts 1 and 2, and consequently may be biased."

*[verbatim, same source, §9 Advisory Committee Meeting and Other External Consultations]* — "No advisory committee meeting was held for this NDA."

### 79. Binimetinib (Mektovi) — NDA 210498

**Sponsor:** Array BioPharma Inc.

**Indication approved:** In combination with encorafenib, for treatment of patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma with a BRAF V600E or V600K mutation, as detected by an FDA-approved test — binimetinib carries no monotherapy indication; the approved label's Indications and Usage statement is written only "in combination with encorafenib."

**Approval date:** June 27, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** COLUMBUS (Study CMEK162B2301), NCT01909453

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled, event-driven trial, biomarker-selected/enriched population (BRAF V600E/V600K mutation, centrally confirmed), 2-part design in which Part 2 (Combo 300 vs. encorafenib monotherapy, 3:1 randomization) was added mid-conduct via a protocol amendment at FDA's request, after FDA stated Part 1's design (which used a higher encorafenib dose in the combination arm than the monotherapy arm) could not adequately assess binimetinib's individual contribution to the combination — an application of the combination-rule "contribution of each component" requirement to two simultaneously-developed, previously-unapproved drugs
- *Endpoints:* progression-free survival (PFS, primary for the binimetinib registrational claim, BIRC-assessed per RECIST v1.1, Combo 450 vs. vemurafenib), PFS Combo 450 vs. encorafenib monotherapy (key secondary, intended to demonstrate binimetinib's contribution), overall survival (OS, other secondary), objective response rate (ORR)/duration of response (DoR)/disease control rate (DCR)/time to response (secondary), patient-reported outcomes (FACT-M, EORTC QLQ-C30)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified), Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence hierarchical testing across 4 pre-specified tests (Test 1: PFS Combo 450 vs. vemurafenib; Test 2: PFS Combo 450 vs. encorafenib; Test 3: PFS Combo 300 vs. pooled encorafenib population; Test 4: OS Combo 450 vs. vemurafenib), overall two-sided alpha of 0.05 controlled across the family
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design for OS, one planned interim OS analysis after 75% of target deaths, Gamma-family alpha-spending function (γ=1), interim alpha allocation 0.042 / final 0.008
- *Regulatory:* combined FDA Multi-Discipline Review package jointly covering NDA 210496 (encorafenib) and NDA 210498 (binimetinib), reviewer-documented mid-trial redesign in response to FDA feedback (Part 2 added because Part 1 could not isolate binimetinib's contribution — FDA cited its guidance "Codevelopment of Two or More Unmarketed Investigational Drugs for Use in Combination"), companion diagnostic (bioMérieux THxID BRAF Assay Kit, cross-referenced PMA supplement P120014/S008) not yet finally determined by CDRH at time of NDA action, no FDA advisory committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- COLUMBUS (CMEK162B2301): Phase III, 2-part, randomized, open-label, multicenter trial in adults with locally advanced unresectable or metastatic cutaneous melanoma (AJCC Stage IIIB/IIIC/IV) with a centrally-confirmed BRAF V600E or V600K mutation, naive or previously treated with at most one line of immunotherapy, ECOG PS 0-1, and no untreated CNS lesions
- Part 1 (first patient randomized 30-Dec-2013): 577 patients randomized 1:1:1 to encorafenib 450 mg QD + binimetinib 45 mg BID ("Combo 450"), encorafenib 300 mg QD monotherapy, or vemurafenib 960 mg BID; randomization stratified by AJCC stage (IIIB+IIIC+M1a+M1b vs. M1c), ECOG PS (0 vs. 1), and prior first-line immunotherapy (yes/no)
- Part 2 (first patient randomized 19-Mar-2015, added via Protocol Amendment/Version 3, submitted 20-Nov-2014): 344 patients randomized 3:1 to encorafenib 300 mg QD + binimetinib 45 mg BID ("Combo 300") or encorafenib 300 mg QD monotherapy — added specifically because FDA, in an End-of-Phase-2 meeting (29-Apr-2013) and subsequent Type C interactions (Apr/Jul 2014), stated that Part 1's asymmetric encorafenib dosing (450 mg in the combination arm vs. 300 mg in the monotherapy arm) confounded assessment of binimetinib's individual contribution to the combination's effect, and that the sponsor's proposed Bayesian contribution analysis was not acceptable
- Primary endpoint for the binimetinib regulatory claim: PFS by blinded independent central review (BIRC) per RECIST v1.1 (Combo 450 vs. vemurafenib, "Test 1") — all tumor response endpoints were BIRC-assessed
- Key secondary endpoint intended to demonstrate binimetinib's contribution: PFS, Combo 450 vs. encorafenib monotherapy ("Test 2"); in Part 2, PFS Combo 300 vs. encorafenib monotherapy ("Test 3", using a pooled encorafenib-monotherapy population combining Part 1's 194 encorafenib-arm patients with Part 2's encorafenib-arm patients, 538 total)
- Other secondary endpoints: OS (Combo 450 vs. vemurafenib, "Test 4"; Combo 450 vs. encorafenib), ORR, time to response, disease control rate, duration of response, and patient-reported outcomes (FACT-M melanoma subscale, EORTC QLQ-C30, EQ-5D-5L, time to ECOG PS deterioration)
- Sample size, Part 1: assuming median PFS of 7 months (vemurafenib) and 8 months (encorafenib), 577 patients (1:1:1) gave 80% power to detect HR=0.667 for Combo 450 vs. encorafenib and 90% power to detect HR=0.58 for Combo 450 vs. vemurafenib, at an overall two-sided alpha of 0.05
- Sample size, Part 2: assuming median PFS of 8 months (encorafenib), 344 patients (3:1) combined with Part 1's encorafenib arm gave 80% power to detect HR=0.667 for Combo 300 vs. pooled encorafenib, two-sided alpha 0.05
- OS was additionally powered assuming median OS of 17 months (vemurafenib) vs. 22 months (Combo 450), with one interim analysis planned after 75% of target deaths had occurred, using a Gamma(1) alpha-spending function (interim alpha allocation 0.042, final 0.008); FDA's statistical reviewer noted the power for the OS analysis was low relative to the PFS analyses
- Statistical methods: stratified log-rank test used for all PFS and OS comparisons (overall two-sided significance level 0.05), Kaplan-Meier estimation of PFS/OS curves, Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified) for hazard ratios; overall type I error across the four pre-specified tests was controlled by fixed-sequence hierarchical testing in the order Test 1 (PFS, Combo 450 vs. vemurafenib) → Test 2 (PFS, Combo 450 vs. encorafenib) → Test 3 (PFS, Combo 300 vs. pooled encorafenib) → Test 4 (OS, Combo 450 vs. vemurafenib)
- Results: Test 1 (binimetinib's pivotal claim) — median PFS 14.9 months (Combo 450) vs. 7.3 months (vemurafenib), stratified HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.41-0.71), stratified log-rank p<0.0001; Test 2 (contribution of binimetinib) — median PFS 14.9 vs. 9.6 months, stratified HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.56-1.00), two-sided stratified log-rank p=0.0513 (not significant); because Test 2 did not reach significance, Test 3 (Combo 300 vs. pooled encorafenib: median PFS 12.9 vs. 9.2 months, HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.61-0.97) was reported only descriptively per the hierarchical testing rule, with no formal hypothesis test performed; OS (Test 4) was not formally tested at the time of the original approval because survival data were immature (interim OS event threshold not yet reached) — FDA's review states a "trend toward improved overall survival" for Combo 450 vs. vemurafenib was observed but "statistical testing will not be performed on this endpoint" at that data cut
- FDA's benefit-risk conclusion: despite the trial design limiting a statistically robust demonstration of each individual drug's contribution, "based on the totality of the data generated by COLUMBUS, both encorafenib and binimetinib are required to yield the observed efficacy," supporting regular approval of both NDAs on the Combo 450 vs. vemurafenib PFS result

The Kaplan-Meier method was used to estimate the PFS and OS curves for each treatment arm, and the Cox proportional hazards model was used for the estimation of hazard ratios for comparisons between arms. Overall type I error was controlled among these endpoints by a hierarchical testing procedure, where the order of testing was Test 1: PFS (Combo 450 vs. vemurafenib) Test 2: PFS (Combo 450 vs. encorafenib) Test 3: PFS (Combo 300 vs. encorafenib) Test 4: OS (Combo 450 vs. vemurafenib)."

*[verbatim, same source, same section]* — "Tests that included the Combo 450 arm were performed on the ITT population from Part 1. In the comparison of the Combo 300 arm and the encorafenib arm (Test 3), the log-rank test was performed using a pooled population for the encorafenib arm, in which all patients randomized to encorafenib monotherapy in either Part 1 or Part 2 were combined, and the ITT population from Part 2 for the Combo 300 arm."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "The sample size for Part 1 of this study was estimated using the assumption that the median PFS was 7 months for the vemurafenib arm and 8 months for the encorafenib arm. A total of 577 patients (using a 1:1:1 randomization) were randomized. The study was designed to detect an improvement in median PFS from 8 months in the encorafenib arm to 12 months in the Combo 450 arm. This improvement corresponds to a hazard ratio of 0.667 with 80% power while maintaining an overall significance level of 5% (two-sided). This sample size also provided 90% power to detect a hazard ratio 0.58 for the Combo 450 vs. vemurafenib comparison while maintaining the overall significance level."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "The trial was also designed to test OS, using the assumption that the median OS would be 17 months in the vemurafenib arm and 22 months in the Combo 450 arm. One interim analysis was planned for OS after 75% of deaths had occurred.... Overall type I error was controlled for the interim analysis with the α-spending function using a Gamma function with parameter 1. This spending function had an alpha allocation of 0.042 to the interim analysis and 0.008 to the final analysis." Table source cited in the review: "COLUMBUS SAP v4 Table 3-1, dated 28-Mar-2017." *Reviewer's comment:* "The power for the OS analysis is low relative to the power for the PFS analyses."

*[verbatim, same source, describing FDA's End-of-Phase-2 meeting of 29-Apr-2013 and subsequent correspondence]* — "FDA did not object to the proposed statistical analysis methods for independent comparisons of both the LGX818/MEK162 combination versus vemurafenib and LGX818 versus vemurafenib. FDA noted that the Bayesian analysis for estimating the contribution of MEK162 to the combination of LGX818 plus MEK162 would be considered exploratory. FDA recommended that the primary analyses of PFS and OS be conducted at a prespecified number of events, that the O'Brien-Fleming method be used for alpha adjustment for interim analysis of overall survival (OS), and that given the proposal to ignore or group strata, the primary analysis should be unstratified." (Note: the final SAP as executed used a stratified, not unstratified, primary analysis and a Gamma(1) spending function rather than O'Brien-Fleming for the OS interim look — the review does not further reconcile this divergence from FDA's initial 2013 recommendation.)

*[verbatim, same source, Advice/Information Request letter dated 22-Oct-2013]* — "Please be advised that you will need to demonstrate the relative contribution of each investigational product to the effect of the combination in an NDA submission seeking initial approval of two previously unapproved investigational products for use in combination. Data that is limited to clinical outcomes evaluating only LGX818 and MEK162 as single agents would not be sufficient to demonstrate the contribution of each component of the combination. Please refer to the FDA Guidance for Industry 'Codevelopment of Two or More Unmarketed Investigational Drugs for Use in Combination.'"

*[verbatim, same source, efficacy results summary]* — "The Combo 450 arm had significantly longer PFS compared to the vemurafenib arm, with a stratified log-rank test p-value of <0.0001. The estimated median PFS times were 14.9 months (95% CI: [11.0, 18.5]) for the Combo 450 arm and 7.3 (95% CI: [5.6, 8.2]) for the vemurafenib arm. The stratified hazard ratio of PFS for the Combo 450 arm compared to the vemurafenib arm was 0.54 (95% CI: [0.41, 0.71])."... "The Combo 450 arm did not demonstrate a significant improvement in PFS when compared to the encorafenib arm, with a two-sided stratified log-rank test p-value of 0.0513."... "The Combo 300 arm exhibited a numerical improvement in progression-free survival when compared to encorafenib monotherapy, though no formal test was performed due to hierarchical testing rules."

*[verbatim, same source, Benefit-Risk Assessment]* — "Patients treated with encorafenib in combination with binimetinib also had a trend toward improved overall survival compared to patients treated with vemurafenib, but survival data is not yet mature, and statistical testing will not be performed on this endpoint. While limitations in study design prevented a statistically robust demonstration of the contribution of each individual drug to the overall treatment effect, the totality of the data generated on COLUMBUS, which incorporated an encorafenib monotherapy arm, supported the FDA's conclusion that both drugs are required to maximize clinical benefit."

Submissions related to encorafenib as a single agent were submitted to NDA 210496, and submissions related to binimetinib as a single agent were submitted to NDA 210498." — this confirms the review package is a single combined document (Reference ID 4282505) authored to support both applications simultaneously, rather than two independently written statistical reviews.
