### 80. Ivosidenib (Tibsovo) — NDA 211192

**Sponsor:** Agios Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with a susceptible isocitrate dehydrogenase-1 (IDH1) mutation as detected by an FDA-approved test

**Approval date:** July 20, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** Study AG120-C-001, NCT02074839 (single-arm, open-label, multicenter Phase 1 dose-escalation/expansion trial; the R/R AML expansion cohorts, Arms 1 and 4, provided the pivotal efficacy population)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial (Phase 1 dose-escalation and multi-arm expansion, not a dedicated registration-intent Phase 3), companion diagnostic co-approval (Abbott RealTime IDH1 Assay), FDA-conducted independent expansion of the efficacy analysis population beyond the sponsor's pre-specified primary analysis set, using a later data cut and revised inclusion criteria
- *Endpoints:* complete remission (CR) + CR with partial hematologic recovery (CRh) rate — a composite response endpoint specific to R/R AML (primary), overall response rate (ORR, secondary, includes CRi/CRp/PR/MLFS), duration of CR+CRh/CR/CRh, time to response, event-free survival (EFS), overall survival (OS, all descriptive/exploratory given the absence of a control arm), RBC/platelet transfusion independence
- *Primary analysis:* exact binomial test against a pre-specified performance goal (null CR+CRh rate of 10% vs. a target of 20%, one/two-sided alpha=0.05 as reported, 89% power for 125 evaluable subjects); exact (Clopper-Pearson-type) 2-sided 95% binomial confidence interval around the observed CR+CRh rate, with a lower-bound-excludes-10% decision rule serving as the effective significance threshold
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* single interim safety/futility look after the first 25 Arm 1 expansion subjects were treated and followed 2 cycles (or discontinued earlier) — enrollment of an additional 100 subjects proceeded only because the observed ORR exceeded the pre-specified 15% futility threshold
- *Missing data/bias:* multiple named censoring-rule variations for duration-of-response/EFS sensitivity analyses (censor at last adequate assessment before HSCT; treat discontinuation for undocumented progression as an event at last dose; treat ≥2 consecutive missing assessments before a later event as an event on that event date; treat start of subsequent anticancer therapy as an event), reverse Kaplan-Meier method for follow-up duration, OS sensitivity analysis censoring at start of subsequent anticancer therapy
- *Regulatory:* regular approval (21 CFR 314.105), not accelerated approval — FDA's own wording frames CR/CRh plus transfusion-independence conversion as sufficient evidence of effectiveness in this setting rather than as a surrogate pending confirmation; orphan drug designation (exempting the program from PREA pediatric-study requirements); priority review; companion diagnostic co-approval (Abbott RealTime IDH1 Assay, cross-referencing PMA P170041); reviewer-documented widening of the efficacy analysis population by FDA itself (see Design); no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held; three postmarketing requirements (long-term safety follow-up from the same ongoing trial; hepatic-impairment PK studies) rather than a randomized confirmatory efficacy trial, consistent with the non-accelerated approval basis

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study AG120-C-001: open-label, nonrandomized, multicenter, two-part Phase 1 trial of oral ivosidenib (AG-120) in adults with IDH1 R132-mutated advanced hematologic malignancies — Part 1 was a 3+3 dose-escalation across 7 dose levels/schedules (~36 subjects), Part 2 was a multi-arm expansion (Arm 1: R/R AML n≈125 planned, later enrolled to ~179; Arm 2: untreated AML in patients ≥75 or ineligible for intensive chemotherapy; Arm 3: maintenance post-HSCT; Arm 4: R/R AML at doses other than 500 mg); enrollment reached 258 treated patients by the May 12, 2017 data cutoff, with the trial still ongoing at the time of the FDA review (later data cuts in the ClinicalTrials.gov record show continued recruitment for other malignancy cohorts as of 2026)
- The dose used in the pivotal analysis, 500 mg once daily, was selected from Phase 1 based on overlapping exposure, maximal 2-HG suppression, comparable response rates, dose-limiting toxicities, and QT-prolongation risk all favoring 500 mg over higher doses tested
- Primary efficacy endpoint: proportion of R/R AML patients (Arm 1+ population — Arm 1 expansion subjects plus Arm-1-eligible dose-escalation subjects who started at 500 mg qday) achieving CR or CRh, based on investigator-assessed CR and a CRh category derived by the sponsor from investigator-collected bone marrow/hematology data (no independent review committee was used for expansion-phase efficacy — Protocol Amendment 5 explicitly removed the IRC)
- Analysis-set structure: Full Analysis Set (FAS, all treated patients), Full Analysis Set 1 (FAS1, the subset of FAS with ≥6 months since first dose at the analysis cutoff — the sponsor's primary efficacy analysis set for Arm 1+), Safety Analysis Set, Dose Determining Set, Pharmacokinetic Analysis Set; the sponsor's primary analysis (Arm1+, FAS1) comprised 125 patients, reported CR/CRh in 38 (30.4%, 95% CI 22.5-39.3%), meeting the pre-specified success criterion
- Sample-size logic: an observed CR+CRh rate ≥16% in 125 treated subjects (≥20/125 responses) would yield an exact binomial 95% CI whose lower bound excludes 10%, equivalent to 89% power to distinguish a 20% target rate from a 10% null rate at 2-sided alpha=0.05 — framed by FDA's reviewer as a deliberately low evidentiary bar ("the investigators set a low bar regarding 'clinically significant activity'")
- FDA conducted its own independent efficacy analysis rather than simply accepting the sponsor's FAS1 cut: it excluded 6 subjects whose IDH1 mutation was not confirmed by the Abbott RealTime IDH1 companion diagnostic assay and used an updated November 10, 2017 data cut (agreed with the sponsor's 90-day safety update), which added 34 subjects and more mature response data — yielding an FDA "Original Efficacy Set" of 153 patients and a broader "R/R AML Efficacy Set" of 173 patients that FDA, not the sponsor, ultimately designated as the basis for labeling
- Labeled efficacy result (R/R AML Efficacy Set, N=173, FDA analysis): CR+CRh rate 32.9% (57/173, 95% CI 26.0-40.5%), median duration of CR+CRh 8.2 months (95% CI 5.6-12.0), median time to CR+CRh 2.0 months; CR alone 24.9% (43/173), CRh alone 8.1% (14/173); median overall survival 9.1 months (95% CI 7.4-10.2), with the FDA reviewer noting the survival curve implies a "palliative, as opposed to curative" benefit despite the response rate; a sensitivity analysis on the smaller "Original Efficacy Set" (N=153) gave concordant results (CR+CRh 30.7%)
- Secondary/supportive endpoints (all descriptive, no formal multiplicity control since there was no comparator arm): CR rate, ORR (CR+CRi/CRp+PR+MLFS), duration of CR/CRh/response, time to CR/CRh/response, EFS, OS, and RBC/platelet transfusion independence (evaluated pre- vs. post-baseline by best response category)
- FDA's statistical reviewer flagged that time-to-event endpoints, including OS and EFS, are difficult to interpret without a control arm, and separately noted that EFS's definition (counting only confirmed relapse/progression or death as events, not stable disease) limited its interpretability relative to duration of CR+CRh/DOCR

- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (Reference ID 4293723; separate StatR/MedR PDFs were not posted for this NDA — statistical review content is embedded in this combined review) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/211192Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (Study AG120-C-001) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02074839 (no protocol/SAP posted in the Documents tab; verified via the ClinicalTrials.gov v2 API, `documentSection` absent)
- Pivotal publication: DiNardo CD, Stein EM, de Botton S, et al. "Durable Remissions with Ivosidenib in IDH1-Mutated Relapsed or Refractory AML." *N Engl J Med.* 2018;378(25):2386-2398. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1716984), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29860938/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Durable%20Remissions%20with%20Ivosidenib%20in%20IDH1-Mutated%20Relapsed%20or%20Refractory%20AML)

**Other resources**

- Agios' data-sharing/IPD participation was not individually confirmed for this trial; Agios' oncology franchise (including ivosidenib) was later acquired by Servier in 2021, which is now the ClinicalTrials.gov record's listed sponsor of record.
- No FDA Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held for this application.
- Postmarketing requirements: PMR-1, long-term safety follow-up (~3 additional years) from the same ongoing Study AG120-C-001, including subgroup analyses by cytogenetics/mutation status; PMR-2, completion of Study AG120-C-012 (hepatic-impairment PK); PMR-3, a dedicated hepatic-impairment dosing PK study (potentially a sub-study of AG120-C-001) — none of these are a randomized confirmatory efficacy trial, consistent with this being regular rather than accelerated approval.
- Ivosidenib carries a boxed warning for differentiation syndrome, identified by FDA's reviewers (alongside QT prolongation) as one of the two major safety issues driving labeling.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 211192, Reference ID 4293723, §1.2 "Conclusions on the Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness"]* — "The review team recommends regular approval of ivosidenib under 21 CFR 314.105 for the indication 'treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with a susceptible isocitrate dehydrogenase-1 (IDH1) mutation as detected by an FDA-approved test' using a dose of 500 mg daily. The recommendation is based on the finding of durable complete remission with complete or partial hematopoietic recovery (CR/CRh) and conversion to transfusion independence in Study AG120-C-001 (NCT02074839)."

*[verbatim, same source, Statistical Analysis Plan section]* — "The statistical analysis plan for Study AG120-C-001 was submitted while the trial was ongoing, and called for a primary analysis of efficacy and safety when at least 125 expansion Arm 1 eligible subjects (including Arm 1 eligible subjects from dose escalation whose starting dose was 500 mg qday) had received at least 6 months of ivosidenib or had discontinued study therapy earlier... an observed CR+CRh rate of at least 16% in 125 treated subjects (at least 20 responses in 125 subjects) would result in an exact binomial 95% CI with a lower bound that excludes 10%. This is equivalent to testing a null CR+CRh rate of 10% compared to a target rate of 20% with 89% power and 2 sided alpha of 0.05. This was considered evidence of clinically significant activity of ivosidenib in R/R AML."

*[verbatim, same source, reviewer comment immediately following]* — "It is furthermore noted that the investigators set a low bar regarding 'clinically significant activity of ivosidenib,' requiring a CR+CRh rate of only 16%. The ultimate benefit will need to be weighed carefully against the observed safety profile."

*[verbatim, same source, "Analysis of Primary Efficacy Endpoint"]* — "The primary efficacy endpoint of CR+CRh was defined as the rate of responses including CR and CRh, where CR was based on investigator assessment of response and CRh was derived by the Applicant from relevant data, including investigator-collected BM and hematology data. The CR+CRh rate was summarized by the percentage of responses primarily in the FAS1 for Arm 1+ subjects with 2-sided exact binomial 95% confidence interval (CI). An observed CR+CRh rate in R/R AML subjects in the FAS1 Arm1+ with the lower bound of the exact binomial 95% CI greater than 10% was deemed as clinically meaningful in this setting."

*[verbatim, same source, on FDA's independent reanalysis]* — "FDA's analysis differed from the analysis provided by the Applicant in the original NDA submission in the following ways: The FDA excluded 6 subjects from the analysis who did not have an IDH1 mutation identified by the Abbott RealTime IDH1TM mutation assay. The FDA used updated data sets, with a data cut date of November 10, 2017; this resulted in the addition of 34 subjects to the analysis as well as more matured response data. Thus, FDA had 153 patients in their Original Efficacy Set (compared to n=125 in Arm 1+ FAS1 per the Sponsor) and 173 patients in their R/R AML Efficacy Set (compared to n=179 per the Sponsor's All R/R AML at 500 mg QD set). Reviewer comments: For the purposes of labeling, FDA agrees with presenting the R/R AML Efficacy set."

*[verbatim, same source, Efficacy Results / Table 33]* — "The primary efficacy endpoint is the proportion of patients in the primary analysis cohort who achieved complete remission (CR) or complete remission with partial hematological response (CRh). Fifty-seven out of one hundred and seventy-three patients (33%) experienced either a CR or CRh. The lower bound of 95% CI was 26%, which is higher than the pre-specified boundary of 10%. This met the applicant's pre-defined criteria for evidence of clinically significant activity... The median overall survival was 9.1 months with 95% CI [7.4, 10.2]... Reviewer comments: Despite the demonstrated response rate, the overall survival curve indicates that very few patients will survive long-term. Thus, this therapy appears to be more palliative, as opposed to curative, in nature."

*[verbatim, same source, §9 "Advisory Committee Meeting and Other External Consultations"]* — "This Application was not presented to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee or any other external consultants."

Cross-reference note: like daratumumab (BLA 761036, above), ivosidenib's pivotal evidence is a single-arm trial with a binomial-proportion primary analysis rather than a comparative hypothesis test — but unlike daratumumab's accelerated approval, ivosidenib received regular approval, and unlike the sponsor-defined analysis population typically taken at face value in single-arm submissions, here FDA itself expanded the efficacy analysis population beyond what the sponsor's own SAP had pre-specified (153/173 patients vs. the sponsor's 125/179), using its own data-cut and mutation-confirmation criteria, before designating that FDA-defined population as the one to appear in labeling.

### 81. Mogamulizumab-kpkc (Poteligeo) — BLA 761051

**Sponsor:** Kyowa Kirin, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory mycosis fungoides (MF) or Sézary syndrome (SS) after at least one prior systemic therapy

**Approval date:** August 8, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** MAVORIC (Study 0761-010), NCT01728805

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled, event-driven trial, stratified by disease type (MF vs. SS) and stage (IB/II vs. III/IV) and (at analysis) region, crossover permitted at progression, biomarker-agnostic enrollment (irrespective of CCR4 expression status)
- *Endpoints:* progression-free survival (PFS-INV, primary, per Olsen 2011 global composite response criteria combining skin/lymph node/blood/viscera compartments), objective response rate (ORR-INV, key secondary, confirmed CR/PR per Global Composite Response Score), patient-reported outcomes/quality of life (key secondary: Skindex-29, FACT-G, EQ-5D-3L index; other secondary: Pruritus/Itchy QoL), PFS-IRC and ORR-IRC (other secondary), overall survival (exploratory, data immature at cutoff)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified), Kaplan-Meier estimation, Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test (ORR, adjusted for disease type/stage/region), repeated-measures ANCOVA / mixed-effects model with REML (Skindex-29, FACT-G, EQ-5D-3L, unstructured covariance)
- *Multiplicity:* Šidák-adjusted p-value method (1-(1-p)^4) applied jointly across the four key secondary endpoints (ORR, Skindex-29, FACT-G, EQ-5D-3L) to control overall study-wise Type I error at 0.05
- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation for missing ORR data (ITT denominator); scoring-guideline-based missing-data rules for Skindex-29/FACT-G/EQ-5D-3L (item-response-rate thresholds); FDA identified imbalanced/informative censoring between arms (41% of mogamulizumab-arm patients censored for PFS-INV vs. lower rate for vorinostat, driven largely by AE/intolerance discontinuation being more common on vorinostat) and required four additional sponsor-defined sensitivity analyses plus FDA-requested censoring-reason tabulation by information request
- *Regulatory:* Priority Review, Orphan Drug Designation (CTCL, 2010), Breakthrough Therapy Designation (2017, based on top-line MAVORIC results); no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held ("application did not raise significant efficacy or safety issues")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- MAVORIC (Study 0761-010): multicenter, open-label, randomized (1:1) Phase 3 trial of mogamulizumab (1 mg/kg IV, days 1/8/15/22 of cycle 1, then days 1/15 of subsequent 28-day cycles) vs. vorinostat (400 mg orally daily) in 372 adults with Stage IB-IV MF or SS after failure of ≥1 prior systemic therapy, irrespective of CCR4 expression status; randomization stratified by disease type (MF vs. SS) and stage (IB/II vs. III/IV)
- One-way crossover from vorinostat to mogamulizumab was permitted upon disease progression (generally after a minimum of 2 cycles) or intolerable toxicity
- Primary endpoint: PFS-INV — time from randomization to investigator-assessed documented progression (per Olsen et al. 2011 consensus global composite response criteria, requiring assessment across the skin, lymph node, blood, and visceral compartments — e.g., skin: ≥25% increase in disease burden from baseline or new T3 tumors; blood: >50% increase from baseline/nadir with ≥5,000 neoplastic cells/µL; lymph node: ≥50% increase in SPD or new pathologically-confirmed N3 node; viscera: >50% increase in SPD or new organ involvement) or death from any cause; not a solid-tumor RECIST endpoint
- Key secondary endpoints (in stated order): ORR-INV (confirmed CR/PR per Global Composite Response Score, confirmation required ≥4 weeks later); change from baseline in Skindex-29, FACT-G total, and EQ-5D-3L index scores through the 6-month assessment
- Other secondary endpoints: PFS-IRC, ORR-IRC, best overall response, duration of response, time to response, ORR after crossover, QoL/pruritus measures at other timepoints; exploratory endpoints included overall survival, time to treatment failure, and PFS after crossover
- Sample size: targeted a 50% improvement in median PFS (169 to 254 days), with 255 PFS events, 24-month accrual and 12-month minimum follow-up giving 90% power at a one-sided alpha of 0.025 (two-sided 0.05); no formal interim analysis was planned; the sponsor implemented an earlier-than-specified 31 Dec 2016 efficacy cutoff (241 of the planned 255 events observed) based on blinded review showing >85% power was retained
- Primary analysis: ITT population, PFS compared via a log-rank test stratified by disease type, disease stage, and region (US/Japan/rest of world), with censoring at initiation of new anti-lymphoma therapy (including crossover) absent documented progression, and at last tumor assessment for clinical (non-formal) progression; four sponsor-defined sensitivity analyses varied event/censoring definitions around clinical progression and post-treatment deaths
- Secondary analyses: ORR compared via CMH test stratified by disease type/stage/region with exact 95% CIs; QoL scores analyzed via a repeated-measures mixed-effects (REML) model with treatment, region, disease type, disease stage, time, and time-by-treatment interaction, baseline score as covariate, unstructured covariance, with a pre-specified fallback to Wilcoxon rank-sum if residuals were non-normal
- Result (FDA-recalculated, using 30.4375 days/month rather than the sponsor's 30-day convention): PFS-INV HR 0.53 (95% CI 0.41-0.69), 2-sided log-rank p<0.0001; median PFS 7.6 months (mogamulizumab) vs. 3.1 months (vorinostat); FDA flagged that 41% of mogamulizumab-arm patients were censored (vs. a lower vorinostat-arm rate) and, after an information request on censoring reasons, ran additional sensitivity analyses (HRs ranging 0.53-0.74) to address the imbalance before concluding the primary result was robust
- ORR-INV also reached statistical significance (a key secondary endpoint); FDA concluded no reliable conclusion could be drawn on the PRO/QoL endpoints due to a large amount of missing data (especially at early timepoints), inconsistent results, and instrument limitations
- Eight protocol amendments were filed; major changes included adding a DSMB, raising primary-analysis power to 90%, converting the design to event-driven with a maximum-time provision, and reordering secondary/exploratory objectives to prioritize QoL comparisons (Amendment 2, Feb 2013)

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2018/761051Orig1s000Ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/761051s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (includes Statistical Review, Reference ID 4303536) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/761051Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (MAVORIC) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01728805 (no protocol/SAP posted in the Documents tab; API `documentSection` field absent)
- Protocol / SAP: not publicly posted — see Statistical Analysis Plan excerpts below, drawn from FDA's Multi-Discipline Review, which reproduces the sponsor's SAP content in narrative form
- Pivotal publication: Kim YH, Bagot M, Pinter-Brown L, et al., for the MAVORIC Investigators. "Mogamulizumab versus vorinostat in previously treated cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (MAVORIC): an international, open-label, randomised, controlled phase 3 trial." *Lancet Oncol.* 2018;19(9):1192-1204. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(18)30379-6>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30100375/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Mogamulizumab%20versus%20vorinostat%20in%20previously%20treated%20cutaneous%20T-cell%20lymphoma%20MAVORIC%20an%20international%20open-label%20randomised%20controlled%20phase%203%20trial)

**Other resources**

- Kyowa Kirin's participation in third-party IPD-sharing platforms (Vivli, YODA Project, Project Data Sphere) was not confirmed; trial-specific IPD availability for MAVORIC was not individually confirmed.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held for this application (see verbatim quote below).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761051, Reference ID 4303536, §8 Statistical and Clinical Evaluation, "Trial Design"]* — "Study 0761-010 is a multicenter, open-label, randomized phase 3 study comparing mogamulizumab at the recommended dose-schedule vs. vorinostat 400 mg daily in 372 adults with MF/SS after at least one prior systemic therapy. The randomization ratio was 1:1, and randomization was stratified by disease type (MF vs. SS) and stage (IB/II vs. III/IV). One-way crossover from vorinostat to mogamulizumab was permitted in the case of disease progression (generally after a minimum of 2 cycles) or intolerable toxicity. Disease assessment was based on global composite response criteria which combine measures from each disease compartment (Olsen et al 2011)."

*[verbatim, same source, "Statistical Analysis Plan"]* — "Primary analysis: The primary comparison of PFS with mogamulizumab vs. vorinostat was performed by intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis using a log-rank test stratified by disease type (MF or SS), disease stage (IB/II or III/ IV), and region (U.S., Japan, and rest of world). PFS measurements were censored at time of initiation of new anti-lymphoma therapy (including crossover) in the absence of progression of disease (PD). In addition, patients with clinical progression that did not meet formal PD criteria were censored at the time of clinical progression."

*[verbatim, same source, "Assumptions and sample size determination"]* — "The study targeted a 50% improvement in median PFS from an assumed 169 days with vorinostat to 254 days. With an expected 24 month accrual and 12 month minimum follow-up time, with a total of 255 PFS events and a one sided type I error rate of 0.025, the expected power is 90%."

*[verbatim, same source, "Timing of analyses"]* — "There was no formal interim analysis. The final primary analysis was to require 255 PFS events or a maximum of 24 month after the last randomized patient's first dose (1/29/2016). Based on ongoing blinded review of data, the Applicant reported that a total 241 PFS events had occurred as of 31 Dec 2016. With 90% of patients having discontinued randomized treatment and the remaining 10% having been followed for at least approximately 1 year, the Applicant chose to implement 31 Dec 2016 as an earlier than specified cut-off date, with the analysis having >85% power."

*[verbatim, same source, "Multiplicity control"]* — "Comparisons of these four key secondary endpoints between the two treatment arms will be conducted using p-values that are adjusted to control the overall study-wise Type 1 error rate of 0.05. The four statistical tests that will be conducted are: ORR as assessed by the Investigator, Change in Skindex-29 score at through the 6-month assessment, Change in FACT-G total score at through the 6-month assessment, and Change in EQ-5D-3L index score at through the 6-month assessment. Since these tests are not independent, the four key secondary tests will be conducted using the Sidak adjusted p-value method defined as 1-(1-p)4, where p is the original p-value of the individual test. These adjusted p-values will then be compared to.05 for each test."

*[verbatim, same source, Statistical review comment on censoring]* — "Notably 76 (41%) patients in the mogamulizumab arm were censored in the analysis of PFS-INV, among which 36 (47% of 76) patients were censored before 6 months since randomization. Because of the large amount of early censoring, the estimation of survival distribution including PFS rates at 6, 12, 18 months and median PFS may not be reliable."... "Since Table 10 shows imbalanced censoring between two treatment arms, which raised the concern of potential premature censoring and informative censoring, FDA conducted additional sensitivity analyses (see Table 13). These additional sensitivity analyses support the efficacy of mogamulizumab and show that mogamulizumab is associated with prolonged PFS compared to vorinostat with HRs ranging from 0.53 to 0.74."

*[verbatim, same source, §9 Advisory Committee Meeting and Other External Consultations]* — "Mogamulizumab was not presented to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee or other external consultants because the application did not raise significant efficacy or safety issues for the proposed indication."

*[verbatim, same source, Summary and Conclusions, "Statistical Issues"]* — "The submitted clinical data from Study 0761-010 show that there was a statistically significant improvement in PFS and ORR with mogamulizumab compared to vorinostat. The PRO data, which the Applicant views as showing a meaningful benefit with mogamulizumab compared to vorinostat, have multiple limitations. From a statistical point of view, the study achieved the primary objective and one of the key secondary objectives (ORR)."

### 82. Moxetumomab pasudotox-tdfk (Lumoxiti) — BLA 761104

**Sponsor:** AstraZeneca AB (BLA applicant, via AstraZeneca Pharmaceuticals LP/MedImmune LLC); Study 1053 was originated by the NCI Center for Cancer Research (protocol 13-C-0106) and transitioned to MedImmune LLC as industry sponsor at Protocol Amendment 4 (12-Aug-2014)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory hairy cell leukemia (HCL) who have received at least two prior systemic therapies, including treatment with a purine nucleoside analog (PNA)

**Approval date:** September 13, 2018 — regular approval (not accelerated approval/Subpart H); neither the approval letter nor the FDA review package contains any accelerated-approval, Subpart H, or 21 CFR 314.510/601.41 language, and the postmarketing requirement described below is a safety-characterization study, not an efficacy-confirmatory trial

**Pivotal trial:** Study 1053 / CD-ON-CAT-8015-1053, "A Pivotal Multicenter Trial of Moxetumomab Pasudotox in Relapsed/Refractory Hairy Cell Leukemia," NCT01829711

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label trial — here supporting *regular* approval rather than the accelerated-approval use this taxonomy term more typically describes; mid-study sponsor transition from an NCI-originated protocol to industry sponsorship
- *Endpoints:* Durable complete response (CR) rate — CR (blood/bone marrow/imaging criteria) confirmed by blinded independent central review (BICR), followed by hematologic remission (HR) maintained >180 days — a novel composite responder endpoint not previously used to support an HCL approval; secondary/descriptive endpoints: objective response rate (ORR), CR rate, MRD-negative CR rate, duration of CR/HR/objective response, progression-free survival (PFS), time to treatment failure (TTF) — all treated as descriptive, not formally tested, per FDA's single-arm caveat
- *Primary analysis:* Exact (Clopper-Pearson) binomial confidence interval around the durable CR rate in the ITT population; protocol-specified decision rule (lower 95% CI bound above a 13% historical-control durable-CR-rate benchmark derived from rituximab data) that FDA's statistical reviewer characterized as "no hypothesis testing planned" yet numerically equivalent to a one-sided exact binomial test at p<0.025 — closest existing taxonomy terms are "Exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval" and "One-sided exact binomial test (single-arm ORR hypothesis test)," applied here to durable CR rather than ORR
- *Multiplicity:* Not applicable — single formal primary endpoint, no comparator arm, no multiplicity adjustment
- *Missing data/bias:* Standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment for HR duration, with two pre-specified sensitivity analyses varying the censoring rule for missed/non-evaluable hematologic assessments (both reproduced the 30% primary-analysis result); FDA reviewer documented substantial BICR-vs-investigator discordance in durable CR (30.0% vs. 47.5%) and explicitly stated "Time-to-event endpoints are difficult to interpret in a single-arm trial"
- *Regulatory:* Regular approval based on a single-arm trial (FDA cited its own precedent of granting regular approval to cladribine and pentostatin in HCL on CR/duration-of-response grounds); no FDA Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held; boxed warning for capillary leak syndrome (CLS) and hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS); postmarketing requirement is a safety-only study in patients ≥65 years and those with moderate renal impairment, not a confirmatory efficacy trial

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 1053: open-label, single-arm, multicenter Phase 3 trial of moxetumomab pasudotox 40 µg/kg IV on Days 1, 3, 5 of each 28-day cycle (up to 6 cycles) in adults with histologically confirmed relapsed/refractory HCL or HCL variant who had received ≥2 prior systemic therapies including ≥1 purine nucleoside analog; 80 patients enrolled and treated (77 classic HCL, 3 HCL variant), median age 60 (range 34-84), median 3 prior therapies (range 2-11), all with prior PNA, 75% with prior rituximab
- Primary endpoint: durable CR rate — overall response meeting blood/bone-marrow/imaging CR criteria by BICR, followed by hematologic remission (neutrophils ≥1.5×10⁹/L, platelets ≥100×10⁹/L, hemoglobin ≥11.0 g/dL, without transfusion/growth-factor support for ≥4 weeks) maintained for >180 days
- Secondary endpoints: CR rate, MRD-negative CR rate (central IHC on bone marrow biopsy), time to CR, duration of CR, duration of HR, ORR (CR+PR), time to objective response, duration of objective response, PFS, time to treatment failure (TTF); immunogenicity and PK as additional/exploratory endpoints
- Sample size: per the FDA Statistical Review, historical durable CR rate in this population was assumed ≤13% (based on rituximab data), target rate for moxetumomab pasudotox assumed ≥28%; using an exact binomial test, 77 subjects gave 90% power to detect a 28% vs. 13% difference at a 2-sided alpha of 0.05, with a 77-subject sample yielding a two-sided 95% CI of roughly ±10 percentage points around an observed 28% rate — 80 subjects were ultimately enrolled and treated
- Analysis populations: ITT (all subjects entered and treated) as primary efficacy population; efficacy-evaluable population as supportive; safety population; PK population
- Statistical method: durable CR rate, CR rate, ORR, and HR rate (all binary) summarized as proportions with Clopper-Pearson exact 95% CIs in the ITT population, primarily by BICR with investigator assessment as supportive; time-to-event endpoints (time to CR/HR/response, PFS, TTF) summarized descriptively by Kaplan-Meier, explicitly not treated as formally tested claims because the trial has no comparator arm
- Results: durable CR rate 30.0% (24/80; 95% CI 20.3-41.3%) per BICR (label rounds to 30%, 95% CI 20-41%); CR rate 41.3% (95% CI 30.4-52.8%); ORR 75% (95% CI 64-84%); median duration of CR/response not reached at a median follow-up of 16.7 months; investigator-assessed durable CR rate was higher (47.5%, 38/80), with FDA attributing most of the 14-patient discordance to earlier CR calls by investigators and non-evaluable bone-marrow assessments driving BICR non-CR calls

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2018/761104Orig1s000Ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (original, 2018) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/761104s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (combined Clinical/Statistical/Cross-Discipline Team Leader review package; Statistical Reviewer Jiaxi Zhou, MS; Reference ID 4319411) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/761104Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01829711 — genuine sponsor Statistical Analysis Plan and Study Protocol posted in the Documents tab
- Protocol / SAP (posted) — SAP (dated 25-Jul-2017, Final): https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/11/NCT01829711/SAP_000.pdf; Study Protocol (dated 29-Mar-2017): https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/11/NCT01829711/Prot_001.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Kreitman RJ, Dearden C, Zinzani PL, Delgado J, Karlin L, Robak T, et al. "Moxetumomab pasudotox in relapsed/refractory hairy cell leukemia." *Leukemia.* 2018;32(8):1768-1777. Note: the task brief for this entry assumed this was published in *J Clin Oncol*; NCBI E-utilities confirms the actual journal is *Leukemia*, not JCO — corrected here rather than left as assumed. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41375-018-0210-1), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30030507/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Moxetumomab%20pasudotox%20in%20relapsed%2Frefractory%20hairy%20cell%20leukemia)

**Other resources**

- AstraZeneca (BLA holder) participates in general clinical-trial-data-sharing arrangements (e.g., Vivli); trial-specific IPD availability for Study 1053 was not individually confirmed.
- No FDA Advisory Committee (ODAC or other) meeting was held for this application, per the FDA Multi-Discipline Review's Advisory Committee section — contrary to an initial assumption that the CLS/HUS boxed-warning safety signal would have triggered one.
- Postmarketing requirement PMR 3477-1: a safety-characterization study (not a confirmatory efficacy trial, since this was regular rather than accelerated approval) in patients ≥65 years old and patients with moderate renal impairment, with draft protocol due 10/2018, final protocol 01/2019, interim analysis 03/2021, and final report 03/2024.
- FDA/Safety Surveillance concluded a REMS was not needed.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

A genuine sponsor Statistical Analysis Plan (MedImmune, dated 25-Jul-2017, Final, for Protocol CD-ON-CAT-8015-1053) and Study Protocol are posted on ClinicalTrials.gov. The SAP PDF's text layer is not plain text: nearly all body-text paragraphs are rendered through a font whose character codes are consistently offset from standard encoding (decodable — a fixed-offset substitution recovers correct letters — but inter-word spacing is not preserved in the extracted text and had to be manually re-inserted), a redaction/protection artifact functionally similar to, but mechanically distinct from, the space-stripping issue previously documented for a Novo Nordisk SAP in this census. Section numbers/headings, by contrast, extract cleanly in plain text. Per the sourcing playbook, passages recovered this way are labeled as reconstructed rather than plain verbatim; specific numeric thresholds that failed to extract at all from the SAP text layer (rendered as blank in a different, uncaptured numeral font) are corroborated below from the FDA review's direct quotation of the same protocol language.

- *[reconstructed from ClinicalTrials.gov SAP_000.pdf §2.1.2 Primary Study Objective; word-spacing manually restored from a character-substitution-encoded PDF text layer]* — "The primary objective of this study is to determine the rate of durable complete response (CR) in multiply relapsed HCL with moxetumomab pasudotox. To meet the primary endpoint, subjects will need to meet standard criteria for CR by analysis of blood, bone marrow and imaging, and maintain a hematologic remission (HR), namely the blood counts needed for CR, for >180 days."
- *[reconstructed from ClinicalTrials.gov SAP_000.pdf §3.5.2.1 Analyses of Primary Efficacy Endpoint; word-spacing manually restored, numeric thresholds unrecoverable from this PDF's text layer and shown in brackets from the corroborating FDA-review quote below]* — "Durable CR rate is defined as the proportion of subjects with durable CR. Durable CR rate based on the BICR and its CI will be constructed using the exact probability method (Clopper-Pearson exact interval) in the ITT population. If the lower bound of the CI is above [13%] (or equivalently, the binomial exact test one-sided p-value [<0.025]), it will be concluded that the durable CR rate in this subject population is significantly higher than the historical control value of [13%]."
- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761104, Reference ID 4319411, p.13, "Conclusions on the Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness"]* — "No statistical hypothesis tests were performed but the 95% confidence interval (CI) for the durable CR rate was constructed using the Clopper-Pearson exact method. The protocol indicated that a lower bound of the 95% CI above 13% was considered clinically meaningful (the estimated durable CR rate to best alternative therapy rituximab). FDA's analysis of the primary endpoint includes 80 subjects with relapsed HCL; the durable CR rate for Study 1053 was 30.3% (95% CI: 20.3%, 41.3%)."
- *[verbatim, same source, p.61, "Statistical Analysis Plan" / "Sample Size Considerations"]* — "The sample size estimation in this study assumed that the historical durable CR rate in this population is ≤ 13%. This is based on previous studies of rituximab. The target durable CR for moxetumomab pasudotox was assumed to be at least 28%. Using the exact binomial test, a total of 77 subjects was expected to provide 90% power to detect a difference between 28% and 13% durable CR rates at a 2-sided significance level of 0.05."
- *[verbatim, same source, p.78, Statistical Review, "Efficacy Endpoints"]* — "There was no hypothesis testing planned, but the protocol indicated that if the lower bound of the 95% CI is above 13% (or equivalently, the binomial exact test one-sided p-value <0.025), it will be concluded that the durable CR rate in the subject population is significantly higher than the historical control value of 13% and considered clinically meaningful. FDA's analysis of the primary endpoint included 80 subjects with R/R HCL; the durable CR rate for the Phase 3 trial was 30.0% (95% CI: 20.3%, 41.3%) as determined by BICR, which met the Applicant's prespecified definition for clinical meaningfulness. Hence, this was a positive trial."
- *[verbatim, same source, p.69, "Efficacy Results – Primary Endpoint"]* — "The durable CR rate assessed by BICR in the ITT Population was 30.0% (24/80 subjects; 95% CI: 20.3%, 41.3%)... The durable CR rate assessed by investigator in the ITT Population was 47.5% (38/80 subjects; 95% CI: 36.2%, 59%)."
- *[verbatim, same source, p.69-70, Statistical/Clinical Reviewer comment on BICR-investigator discordance]* — "The main reasons for the discordances: the investigator determined CR earlier than the BICR, and there was not enough time to reach the durable CR criterion by the data cutoff date per BICR; some patients did not achieve a CR per BICR due to non-evaluable bone marrow."
- *[verbatim, same source, Statistical Reviewer comment, "Dose/Dose Response" section]* — "Time-to-event endpoints are difficult to interpret in a single-arm trial."
- *[verbatim, same source, p.121, "Advisory Committee Meeting and Other External Consultations"]* — "This Application was not presented to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee nor any other external consultants."
- *[verbatim, same source, p.125, "Postmarketing Requirements and Commitment"]* — "PMR 3477-1 Conduct a study to provide evidence characterizing 1) the safety of moxetumomab pasudotox in patient who are 65 years of age and older and 2) the safety of moxetumomab pasudotox in patients who have moderate renal impairment."
- *[verbatim, FDA Package Insert, LUMOXITI label, 2018, §14 "Clinical Studies"]* — "Efficacy of LUMOXITI in HCL was evaluated by the IRC-assessed rate of durable CR, as confirmed by maintenance of hematologic remission (hemoglobin ≥ 11 g/dL, neutrophils ≥ 1500/mm3, and platelets ≥ 100,000/mm3 without transfusions or growth factor for at least 4 weeks) more than 180 days after IRC-assessed CR. The IRC-assessed durable CR rate was 30% (24/80 patients; 95% CI: 20, 41)."

### 83. Duvelisib (Copiktra) — NDA 211155

**Sponsor:** Verastem, Inc. (original NDA holder at approval; U.S. marketing rights and the NDA were subsequently transferred to Secura Bio, Inc., which is the applicant of record on the 2021-2024 supplements cited below)

**Indication approved:** Two indications were approved the same day under one NDA, administratively designated as separate "Original" applications with different evidentiary bases: NDA 211155/Original 2 (this entry's focus, standard approval) — treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) or small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL) after at least two prior therapies; and NDA 211155/Original 1, accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.500 — treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma (FL) after at least two prior systemic therapies, based on ORR in the single-arm Study IPI-145-06 (DYNAMO). The FL indication was voluntarily withdrawn by Secura Bio effective the December 17, 2021 supplement approval (NDA 211155/S-005) rather than confirmed by a completed randomized trial.

**Approval date:** September 24, 2018 (both Original 1 and Original 2 approved on this date)

**Pivotal trial:** DUO (Study IPI-145-07), NCT02004522, randomized duvelisib vs. ofatumumab in relapsed/refractory CLL/SLL. For the FL accelerated-approval indication (documented here for completeness, not the SAP-depth focus of this entry): Study IPI-145-06 (DYNAMO), NCT01882803 — single-arm, open-label Phase 2 study, ORR as primary endpoint.

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled (DUO/Study IPI-145-07, duvelisib vs. ofatumumab, stratified by del(17p) status, purine-analog refractory/early-relapse status, and Grade 4 cytopenias); event-driven trial (both PFS- and OS-event-driven); single-arm, open-label trial (DYNAMO/Study IPI-145-06, the accelerated-approval basis for the separate FL indication, later voluntarily withdrawn)
- *Endpoints:* progression-free survival (PFS) — primary, IRC-assessed per IWCLL/IWG criteria, DUO; objective response rate (ORR) — key secondary, DUO; overall survival (OS) — key secondary, DUO; lymph node response rate and hematologic improvement rate — secondary, DUO (lymph node response rate is not yet its own row in `Keyword_Taxonomy.md` §2, flagging as a candidate addition, as also flagged in the idelalisib entry); duration of response (DoR) — secondary
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test (PFS, OS); stratified Cox proportional-hazards model (HR/CI for PFS and OS); Kaplan-Meier estimation; Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test (ORR, stratified by randomization factors)
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical/gatekeeping testing (PFS→ORR→OS, each at one-sided α=0.025; because OS did not reach its stopping boundary, formal sequential testing stopped there and no further secondary endpoint could claim statistical significance)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design (PFS: one interim at ~50% information fraction/93 events; OS: two interims at 24 and 58 events plus a final analysis at 161 events); Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function for an O'Brien-Fleming efficacy boundary; Hwang-Shih-DeCani gamma(-4) spending function as a non-binding futility (beta-spending) boundary
- *Missing data/bias:* standard right-censoring at last evaluable disease assessment; a pre-specified worst-case sensitivity rule censoring/eventing lost-to-follow-up non-progressors asymmetrically by arm (same construct flagged as a candidate addition in the idelalisib entry); event-free survival (EFS) as a PFS-robustness sensitivity endpoint; an FDA-conducted competing-risk analysis of death-without-progression vs. death-with-progression, and an FDA exploratory sensitivity analysis censoring OS at start of subsequent anticancer therapy
- *Regulatory:* FDA narrowed the approved indication to a more heavily pretreated subgroup (patients with ≥2 prior therapies, versus the trial's ≥1-prior-therapy eligibility) based on benefit-risk, despite the full ITT population meeting its primary PFS endpoint — not yet a `Keyword_Taxonomy.md` §7 term, flagged as a candidate addition ("FDA restricted an approved indication to a subgroup narrower than the pivotal trial's enrolled population, based on a toxicity signal"); no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held; boxed warning plus a communication REMS imposed at original approval; a "Treatment-Related Mortality" boxed-warning addition and Limitations-of-Use restriction against earlier-line use, added in a July 2024 label update upon fulfillment of the 5-year OS follow-up postmarketing requirement, after mature data showed a numeric OS hazard ratio favoring the comparator

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study IPI-145-07 (DUO): Phase III, multicenter, randomized 1:1, open-label trial of duvelisib 25 mg orally twice daily (until progression/unacceptable toxicity) vs. ofatumumab (an initial 300 mg IV dose followed by 7 weekly 2000 mg doses, then 2000 mg every 4 weeks for 4 cycles) in adults with CLL (n=312) or SLL (n=7) who had received at least one prior therapy; 319 patients randomized (160 duvelisib, 159 ofatumumab)
- Randomization stratified by: (1) high-risk cytogenetics (presence/absence of del(17p)), (2) refractory or early relapse to purine-analog-based therapy (progression <12 months after fludarabine/pentostatin), and (3) Grade 4 cytopenias (neutropenia or thrombocytopenia) at baseline
- Primary endpoint: PFS per IRC assessment (IWCLL/revised IWG criteria, with modification for treatment-related lymphocytosis), ITT population; key secondary endpoints ORR and OS, gatekept behind PFS; other secondary endpoints: lymph node response rate, hematologic improvement rate, duration of response
- Sample size: 185 PFS events planned to give ~93% power to detect HR=0.6 using a one-sided log-rank test at a 2.5% overall significance level, with one interim analysis at ~50% information (93 events); OS was assessed at two interims (planned at 24 and 58 OS events, timed to coincide with the PFS interim and final analyses) plus a final analysis (161 OS events), with nominal one-sided p-value boundaries of 0.0001, 0.0249, and 0.0003 if the analyses occurred exactly at the planned event counts
- Statistical methods: primary PFS analysis via stratified log-rank test (one-sided α=0.025) with HR/CI from a stratified Cox proportional-hazards model; ORR via stratified CMH test; OS via stratified log-rank test/Cox model, tested only if both PFS and ORR were declared significant (fixed-sequence gatekeeping); sensitivity analyses included investigator-assessed PFS, a pre-specified worst-case censoring/eventing rule applied asymmetrically by arm, event-free survival, per-protocol and all-treated population analyses, unstratified analyses, and a stepwise covariate-adjusted Cox model
- Results (data cutoff May 19, 2017): PFS HR 0.52 (95% CI 0.39-0.69), median 13.3 vs. 9.9 months, one-sided p<0.0001; ORR 73% vs. 45%, odds ratio 3.4 (95% CI 2.09-5.43), one-sided p<0.0001; OS showed no significant difference, HR 0.99 (95% CI 0.65-1.50), one-sided p=0.4807, with median OS not estimable in either arm — the multiplicity sequence therefore stopped after OS and no further secondary endpoint could claim formal significance
- A higher proportion of duvelisib-arm patients died before disease progression (12% vs. 6% on ofatumumab), and FDA's exploratory competing-risk analysis found a numerically higher cumulative incidence of non-relapse (non-progression) death with duvelisib (16%) than ofatumumab (9%); because the trial enrolled patients after only one prior therapy but the observed toxicity was judged too severe to support use that early, FDA restricted the approved indication (and the label's efficacy table) to the subset with ≥2 prior therapies (95/160 duvelisib, 101/159 ofatumumab), in whom the PFS benefit was larger (HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.27-0.59; median 16.4 vs. 9.1 months) and the toxicity/benefit balance was judged more favorable
- A final, 5-year-follow-up OS analysis (median follow-up 63 months, submitted to fulfill PMR 3494-3) showed a numeric OS hazard ratio favoring ofatumumab in both the overall trial population (HR 1.09, 95% CI 0.79-1.51; median OS 52 vs. 63 months) and the approved ≥2-prior-therapy population (HR 1.06, 95% CI 0.71-1.58; median OS 44 vs. 47 months); treatment-related mortality occurred in 15% (23/158) of duvelisib-treated patients overall and 14% (13/93) in the approved population, mostly from infection — FDA added a "Treatment-Related Mortality" boxed warning and a Limitations-of-Use statement against initial/second-line use in the July 2024 label update (NDA 211155/S-007)
- FL indication (Study IPI-145-06/DYNAMO, documented for completeness): single-arm, open-label Phase 2 trial (group-sequential design with one non-binding futility interim at ~4 months/30 patients), testing null ORR ≤30% against alternative ORR ≥45%, one-sided α=0.025, >90% power with a planned 120 patients (~80 with FL); approved via accelerated approval on ORR, with PMR 3494-1 requiring a randomized Phase 3 confirmatory trial that was not completed; the FL indication was instead voluntarily withdrawn in December 2021

- FDA Approval Letter (FL indication, NDA 211155/Original 1, accelerated approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2018/211155Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (combined Statistical/Clinical/Safety review covering both Original 1 and Original 2), Reference ID 4324739 — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/211155Orig1Orig2s000MultidisciplineR.pdf

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1182/blood-2018-05-850461), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30287523/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=The%20phase%203%20DUO%20trial%3A%20duvelisib%20vs%20ofatumumab%20in%20relapsed%20and%20refractory%20CLL%2FSLL)

**Other resources**

- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held: the approval letter states "Your application for duvelisib was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because this drug is not the first in its class" *(FDA Approval Letter, NDA 211155/Original 2, "Advisory Committee" section)*, and FDA's Multi-Discipline Review similarly states the application "was not presented to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee or other external consultants because duvelisib is not first-in-class, and the application did not raise new efficacy or safety issues for the recommended indications" *(FDA Multi-Discipline Review, §9)*. This benefit-risk judgment was made before the DUO trial's mature 5-year OS data (showing a numeric OS trend against duvelisib) became available; no subsequent advisory committee review specific to duvelisib was identified in the documents checked.
- Verastem, Inc. (the original sponsor) / Secura Bio, Inc. (the current NDA holder) data-sharing/IPD availability for Study IPI-145-07 via Vivli, YODA Project, or Project Data Sphere was not individually confirmed — state this plainly rather than asserting access.
- Postmarketing requirements: PMR 3494-1 (randomized Phase 3 confirmatory trial for the FL indication — not completed; the FL indication was instead voluntarily withdrawn in 2021), PMR 3494-2 (long-term safety characterization across four duvelisib trials), and PMR 3494-3 (overall survival from Study IPI-145-07 with 5 years of follow-up — fulfilled in 2024, prompting the Treatment-Related Mortality boxed warning and Limitations-of-Use restriction).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 211155, Reference ID 4324739, §8.1.1 "Study Design," p.76]*

> "Study IPI-145-07 was a randomized, open-label, actively controlled phase 3 study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of duvelisib compared to ofatumumab in patients with relapsed or refractory CLL or SLL. Patients were randomized 1:1 and were stratified by: 1. High-risk cytogenetics (presence or absence of deletion 17p) 2. Refractory or early relapse to purine analog based therapy (defined as progression <12 months after fludarabine/pentostatin) 3. Grade 4 cytopenias (presence or absence of neutropenia or thrombocytopenia at baseline)"

*[verbatim, same source, §"Sample Size," p.79]*

> "A total of 185 PFS events were determined to provide approximately 93% power to detect a hazard ratio (HR) of 0.6 using a one-sided log-rank test at a 2.5% overall significance level with one interim analysis planned at 50% information time for both efficacy and futility. The study design employed the Lan-DeMets spending function for O'Brien-Fleming boundary as the alpha spending function and the Hwang-Shih-DeCani gamma (-4) spending function as the beta spending function. The futility boundary of this study was non-binding."

*[verbatim, same source, §"Analysis Methods for Primary Endpoint of PFS," pp.79-80]*

> "The primary analysis of PFS will use a stratified log-rank test to compare PFS of the duvelisib arm against PFS of the ofatumumab arm based on IRC assessment with a one-sided overall significance level of 0.025 in the ITT population. The strata for the test will be those used for stratified randomization per interactive response technology (IRT), with potential pooling of strata. If the interim analysis and final analysis occur exactly at 93 and 185 PFS events, the p-value boundaries for efficacy at the two analyses are 0.0015 and 0.0245."

*[verbatim, same source, §"Overall Survival," pp.82-83]*

> "Two interim analyses and one final analysis are planned for OS. The first OS interim analysis will be performed at the time of the planned PFS interim analysis after 93 PFS events have occurred. The second interim analysis of OS will be performed at the planned PFS final analysis after 185 PFS events have occurred.... The estimated number of OS events at the three analyses are 24, 58 and 161.... If the OS analyses occur at 24, 58, and 161 OS events, the p-value stopping boundaries for the three analyses will be 0.0001, 0.0249 and 0.0003, respectively."

*[verbatim, same source, §"Multiplicity Adjustment," pp.82-83]*

> "The primary endpoint PFS and key secondary endpoints ORR and OS will be tested at a one-sided overall significance level of 0.025 based on a gatekeeping approach. ORR will be tested at the one-sided 0.025 level only if PFS is declared statistically significant. OS will be tested according to the planned p-value boundaries only if PFS and ORR are declared statistically significant. If any null hypothesis is not rejected in this sequence of tests, formal sequential testing will be stopped. The analyses of other secondary efficacy endpoints will claim no statistical significance."

*[verbatim, same source, sensitivity-analysis specification, §"Analysis Methods for Primary Endpoint of PFS," p.80]*

> "Worst-case sensitivity analysis: Patients who are alive and have not had documented progression by data cutoff and who are lost to follow-up (missing at least one disease assessment right before data cut-off) will be treated as censored at their last adequate disease assessment if they are on ofatumumab and treated as having a PFS event at the time of the next scheduled assessment following the last adequate disease assessment if they are on duvelisib."

*[verbatim, same source, PFS results and reviewer comment, pp.89-90]*

> "The results of Study IPI-145-07 demonstrate that treatment with duvelisib was associated with a statistically significant improvement in PFS per IRC compared to ofatumumab with a HR of 0.52 (95% CI: 0.39, 0.69) with a one-sided p-value less than 0.0001 (stratified log-rank test).... In the PFS per IRC analysis, it's noted that a higher proportion of patients on the duvelisib arm died before progression (12%) compared to the ofatumumab arm (6%), raising a concern for increased death due to toxicity with duvelisib."

*[verbatim, same source, OS results and reviewer comment, pp.100-101]*

> "The analysis of OS fails to demonstrate a significant difference in OS between patients treated with duvelisib compared to ofatumumab with a hazard ratio of 0.99 (95% CI: 0.65, 1.50) with a one-sided p-value 0.4807 (stratified log-rank test).... The median OS was not estimable in either treatment arm, which indicates that the data may be premature to make reliable conclusion.... Since the benefit demonstrated in PFS did not translate into an OS benefit, the FDA statistical reviewer issued an IR for the Applicant to explain possible reasons an OS benefit was not seen."

*[verbatim, same source, §"Benefit-Risk Assessment," p.16]*

> "Although Study IPI-145-07 required failure of at least one prior regimen, the review team felt that the severity of risks associated with duvelisib warrants restricting the CLL/SLL indication to a more pretreated patient population. Because patients who require third-line therapy or beyond have few or no available therapies, it is reasonable to assume more risk for the potential of clinical benefit. In the phase 3 trial in CLL/SLL, 60% of patients had 2 or more prior therapies. In this subset of patients, as in the overall efficacy population, PFS and ORR were clinically meaningful in favor of duvelisib. The benefit/risk assessment of duvelisib is favorable for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory CLL or SLL after at least two prior therapies."

*[verbatim, same source, class-level safety context, §"Benefit-Risk Assessment," p.16]*

> "The benefit/risk determination considered the totality of safety data on duvelisib, as well as information on same-in-class agents, including the 2016 termination of six idelalisib trials due to excess toxicity (largely infection-driven) and death."

> "This application was not presented to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee or other external consultants because duvelisib is not first-in-class, and the application did not raise new efficacy or safety issues for the recommended indications."

> "This Prior Approval sNDA provides for the following updates to the US Prescribing Information (USPI) based on the results from the DUO study... We have reviewed your submission and conclude that the above requirement was fulfilled" — referring to PMR 3494-3, "Submit reports and datasets for overall survival from trial IPI-145-07 with 5 years of follow-up."

### 84. Dacomitinib (Vizimpro) — NDA 211288

**Sponsor:** Pfizer Inc.

**Indication approved:** First-line treatment of metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with EGFR exon 19 deletion or exon 21 L858R substitution mutations, as detected by an FDA-approved test

**Approval date:** September 27, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** ARCHER 1050 (Pfizer/SFJ Pharmaceuticals Study A7471050), NCT01774721

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled, event-driven trial, biomarker-selected/enriched population (EGFR exon 19del/L858R), no crossover permitted (contrast with FLAURA, which permitted crossover)
- *Endpoints:* PFS (IRC-assessed per RECIST v1.1, primary), ORR (key secondary), OS (key secondary), duration of response (DoR), PRO/HRQoL (EORTC QLQ-C30/LC13, exploratory, no formal multiplicity adjustment)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified), Kaplan-Meier estimation, Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test (ORR), Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval (ORR)
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (PFS → ORR → OS); OS was never formally tested because the ORR step failed, so no alpha remained for OS despite a nominally significant OS p-value
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* no interim analysis for the PFS primary endpoint (a previously planned PFS interim was removed by protocol amendment); one interim OS analysis, added at FDA's request, conducted for futility only at the time of the final PFS analysis with no alpha spent

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ARCHER 1050: Phase III, randomized (1:1), open-label, multinational, active-controlled trial of dacomitinib 45 mg orally once daily vs. gefitinib 250 mg orally once daily, continuous 28-day cycles until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity, in treatment-naive patients with locally advanced/metastatic NSCLC harboring a centrally/locally confirmed EGFR exon 19 deletion or exon 21 L858R mutation (ECOG PS 0-1, no brain metastases)
- Randomization stratified by two factors: race/region (Japanese vs. mainland Chinese vs. other East Asian vs. non-Asian) and EGFR mutation type (exon 19 deletion vs. exon 21 L858R)
- Primary endpoint: PFS per blinded Independent Radiologic Central (IRC) review, RECIST v1.1, in the intent-to-treat (ITT) population
- Secondary endpoints tested under the hierarchy: ORR (per IRC), then OS (time from randomization to death from any cause); other secondary/exploratory endpoints: duration of response, PRO/HRQoL (EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-LC13, assessed descriptively with no pre-specified multiplicity adjustment)
- Sample size: ~440 patients planned (452 actually randomized, 227 dacomitinib/225 gefitinib), assuming median PFS 9.5 months (gefitinib) vs. 14.3 months (dacomitinib), HR 0.67, powered at ~90% for a two-sided alpha of 0.05; ~256 PFS events (ITT) required for the primary analysis
- Statistical methods: time-to-event endpoints summarized by Kaplan-Meier estimation, treatment difference tested by a stratified log-rank test (stratified by the randomization factors), HR/95% CI from a stratified Cox proportional-hazards model; ORR compared via a stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test with Clopper-Pearson exact 95% CIs
- Multiplicity: a fixed-sequence gatekeeping procedure tested PFS, then ORR, then OS, at an overall two-sided alpha of 0.05; because the ORR comparison was not statistically significant (two-sided p=0.39), no alpha remained to formally test OS — the label states plainly, "No formal testing of OS was conducted since the formal comparison of ORR was not statistically significant"
- Protocol amendment 6 removed a previously planned PFS interim analysis (at ~50% information) and, per FDA's request, added a single interim OS analysis for futility only, timed to coincide with the final PFS analysis, with no alpha spent on that interim look
- **Crossover:** ARCHER 1050 had no crossover provision — patients randomized to gefitinib could not switch to dacomitinib on progression, unlike FLAURA (osimertinib vs. gefitinib/erlotinib), which explicitly permitted crossover and required RPSFT/IPCW adjustment for its OS analysis. Neither the ClinicalTrials.gov record, the FDA Multi-Discipline Review, nor the approved label mentions any crossover mechanism, and no RPSFT/IPCW-type crossover-adjustment methodology appears anywhere in the review or label — consistent with a trial design in which the OS hazard ratio is interpretable as a direct (unconfounded-by-crossover) comparison, though FDA's reviewer separately flagged that the OS Kaplan-Meier curves crossed at approximately 12 months, violating the proportional-hazards assumption used to compute the HR, and cautioned that "hazard ratio may not be appropriate to summarize the results and the KM-estimated medians are not appropriate summary statistics to characterize OS" for that reason (a proportional-hazards violation, not a crossover-confounding issue)
- Because no alpha remained for OS under the pre-specified hierarchy, the reported OS result (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.58-0.99; nominal two-sided p=0.044 in the JCO 2018 publication) is descriptive/non-confirmatory from a regulatory-multiplicity standpoint, even though it was nominally below 0.05 — a clean illustration of gatekeeping procedures overriding a nominally "significant" p-value

- Package Insert / Label (original approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/211288s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (Statistical Reviewer Weishi (Vivian) Yuan, PhD; Statistical Team Leader Kun He, PhD; Reference ID 4326788) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/211288Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01774721 (checked via `clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT01774721`; no `documentSection`/protocol/SAP posted)

"Improvement in Overall Survival in a Randomized Study That Compared Dacomitinib With Gefitinib in Patients With Advanced Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer and EGFR-Activating Mutations." *J Clin Oncol.* 2018;36(22):2244-2250. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.2018.78.7994), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29864379/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Improvement%20in%20Overall%20Survival%20in%20a%20Randomized%20Study%20That%20Compared%20Dacomitinib%20With%20Gefitinib%20in%20Patients%20With%20Advanced%20Non-Small-Cell%20Lung%20Cancer%20and%20EGFR-Activating%20Mutations) (erratum: *J Clin Oncol.* 2020;38(31):3725, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.20.02783))

**Other resources**

- Pfizer participates in the Vivli.org data-sharing platform (Data Usage Agreement required); trial-specific ARCHER 1050 IPD availability was not individually confirmed here.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this NDA — the Multi-Discipline Review states plainly, in its Advisory Committee section, that "no advisory committee meeting was requested for this application and no external consultations were required because the safety profile is acceptable for the treatment of patients with metastatic EGFR mutation-positive NSCLC, the application did not raise significant public health questions on the role of dacomitinib for this indication and outside expertise was not necessary since there were no controversial issues that would benefit from an advisory committee discussion."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

No genuine sponsor SAP or protocol document was found publicly posted for ARCHER 1050 (ClinicalTrials.gov's `documentSection` is empty for NCT01774721), but the FDA Multi-Discipline Review's "Statistical Analysis Plan" subsection (§8.1.1) describes the sponsor's plan in enough second-hand detail to quote directly, and the label independently corroborates the key multiplicity result, so this is treated as genuine (if second-hand) verbatim FDA-review text rather than a reverse-engineered SAP.

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, §8.1.1 "ARCHER 1050," "Statistical Analysis Plan" subsection, p.90, Reference ID 4326788]*

> "The ITT population was used for the efficacy analysis. The ITT population comprises all randomized patients regardless of whether treatment was administered. Time-to-event endpoints were summarized using Kaplan-Meier estimates and the difference between treatment arms was tested using a stratified log-rank test, stratifying for the pre-specified stratification factors used for randomization. The hazard ratio and corresponding 95% CI were calculated using the Cox proportional hazards model. The ORR and corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using the Clopper-Pearson method. The difference in the response rates for each treatment comparison is also presented along with its 95% exact confidence intervals. Comparisons of ORRs were conducted based on the Cochran-Mantel Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by the pre-specified stratification factors. DOR was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier estimates. There is no interim analysis for PFS. An interim analysis of OS, to assess for futility only, was performed at the time of the final analysis of PFS; no alpha was spent for this OS analysis. At the time of final analysis of the primary endpoint of PFS, a gate-keeping procedure was used for hypothesis testing in a hierarchical approach in the order of PFS, ORR per BIRC, and OS."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.1.1 "Protocol Amendments," p.90]*

> "Protocol amendment 6 removed a previously planned interim analysis of PFS at approximately 50% of information. The number of events for PFS final analysis was changed from 275 to 256. Per FDA's request, an interim analysis of OS was added, to be conducted at the time of the final PFS analysis."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.1.2 "Efficacy Results – Secondary and other relevant endpoints," p.96]*

> "The secondary endpoints were ORR and OS. According to the protocol, if PFS was statistically significant, then the testing order would be ORR followed by OS.... The CMH test failed to show a statistically significant difference for the dacomitinib arm compared with the gefitinib arm.... Since the test for ORR was not statistically significant there is no alpha left to test for OS."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.1.2, Reviewer's Comment on the OS Kaplan-Meier curves, p.98]*

> "Reviewer's Comment: Note that the OS curves cross at approximately 12 months. The assumption of proportional hazards is violated. Therefore, hazard ratio may not be appropriate to summarize the results and the KM-estimated medians are not appropriate summary statistics to characterize OS. Kaplan-Meier Curves are provided for information only to summarize OS results."

*[verbatim, approved label, §14 "Clinical Studies," p.14]*

> "The hierarchical statistical testing order was PFS followed by ORR and then OS. No formal testing of OS was conducted since the formal comparison of ORR was not statistically significant."

*[verbatim, same source, §11 "Advisory Committee Meeting and Other External Consultations," p.153]*

> "No advisory committee meeting was requested for this application and no external consultations were required because the safety profile is acceptable for the treatment of patients with metastatic EGFR mutation-positive NSCLC, the application did not raise significant public health questions on the role of dacomitinib for this indication and outside expertise was not necessary since there were no controversial issues that would benefit from an advisory committee discussion."
