### 85. Cemiplimab-rwlc (Libtayo) — BLA 761097

**Sponsor:** Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of patients with metastatic cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) or locally advanced CSCC who are not candidates for curative surgery or curative radiation

**Approval date:** September 28, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** EMPOWER-CSCC-1 / Study R2810-ONC-1540 ("Study 1540"), NCT02760498; supportive: Study R2810-ONC-1423 ("Study 1423," first-in-human Phase 1 dose-escalation/expansion trial), NCT02383212

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label, multicenter, non-randomized, multicohort Phase 1/2 program (Study 1423 dose-escalation + expansion Cohorts 7 [metastatic CSCC] and 8 [locally advanced CSCC]; Study 1540 Groups 1 [metastatic CSCC, 3 mg/kg Q2W] and 2 [locally advanced CSCC, 3 mg/kg Q2W], with a not-yet-mature Group 3 [350 mg Q3W] excluded from the efficacy analysis population); pre-specified pooled efficacy analysis combining the Phase 1 expansion cohorts and the Phase 2 multicohort trial into a single primary analysis population per disease-stage group; dose-bridging of the to-be-marketed flat dose (350 mg Q3W, Group 3) to the trial dose (3 mg/kg Q2W, Groups 1–2) via population PK modeling rather than inclusion in the pooled efficacy population
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR, primary endpoint, by independent/central review — RECIST v1.1 for metastatic CSCC; a composite of RECIST v1.1 plus WHO bidimensional clinical/photographic response criteria, adjudicated by an independent composite response committee, for locally advanced CSCC), duration of response (DOR, secondary), safety (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* exact (Clopper-Pearson) binomial confidence interval around ORR, computed separately for the metastatic and locally advanced pooled populations and for the combined population; sample sizes (53 metastatic, 76 locally advanced) were set so that a pre-specified null ORR (15% metastatic, 25% locally advanced) would be excluded by the lower bound of the two-sided 95% CI — a CI-exclusion sample-size design rather than a formally stated one-sided hypothesis test with a pre-declared alpha
- *Multiplicity:* not applicable — single formal primary endpoint (ORR) per disease-stage group, no comparator arm and no formal multiple-testing hierarchy; DOR and other endpoints reported descriptively
- *Missing data/bias:* patients classified as not evaluable (NE) were not counted as achieving PR or CR and were treated as non-responders for ORR in the intent-to-treat population (Non-responder imputation for missing binary/diary efficacy data, extended here to non-evaluable tumor-response classification rather than diary data)
- *Regulatory:* regular approval (21 CFR part 601, not accelerated approval/Subpart H) based on durable ORR, with FDA's review explicitly treating durable objective response plus visible shrinkage of disfiguring CSCC lesions as direct clinical benefit rather than merely a surrogate reasonably likely to predict benefit — precedent cited from prior approvals for malignancies with primary skin involvement; postmarketing commitment (PMC), not postmarketing requirement (PMR), to submit the final Study 1540 clinical trial report with ≥150 patients total (≥75 locally advanced) and ≥1.5 years of post-treatment follow-up — consistent with regular- rather than accelerated-approval status; no FDA advisory committee (ODAC) meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Two open-label, multicenter, non-randomized trials supported the BLA: Study 1423 (first-in-human Phase 1 dose-escalation/expansion trial in advanced solid tumors, with disease-specific expansion Cohort 7 [metastatic CSCC] and Cohort 8 [locally advanced CSCC], cemiplimab 3 mg/kg IV Q2W or 1 mg/kg Q2W) and Study 1540/EMPOWER-CSCC-1 (Phase 2, non-randomized, multicohort: Group 1 metastatic CSCC and Group 2 locally advanced CSCC, both 3 mg/kg IV Q2W; Group 3, 350 mg IV Q3W flat-dose regimen across both disease groups, not yet mature at the BLA data cutoff and excluded from the efficacy analysis)
- Primary efficacy population for the accelerated- vs. regular-approval determination: pooled data from Study 1423 (Cohorts 7 and 8) and Study 1540 (Groups 1 and 2) — 75 patients with metastatic CSCC (16 from Study 1423 + 59 from Study 1540 Group 1) and 33 patients with locally advanced CSCC (10 from Study 1423 + 23 from Study 1540 Group 2, the latter restricted to patients with ≥9 months' follow-up from enrollment at the BLA cutoff), for a combined analysis population of 108 patients
- Primary endpoint: ORR (best overall response of CR or PR) by independent/central review — RECIST v1.1 for metastatic CSCC; a composite response assessment (RECIST v1.1 plus WHO bidimensional clinical/photographic criteria for externally visible lesions, requiring biopsy confirmation of complete response) for locally advanced CSCC, reflecting that many locally advanced lesions were externally visible and disfiguring rather than only radiographically measurable
- Secondary endpoint: duration of response (DOR), reported descriptively (median not reached in either group at the BLA data cutoff)
- Data cutoffs: October 16, 2017 (Study 1423 ORR analysis) and October 27, 2017 (Study 1540 ORR analysis)
- Results at BLA cutoff: metastatic CSCC ORR 46.7% (95% CI 35.1–58.6%; 35/75, including 4 CR/31 PR), locally advanced CSCC ORR 48.5% (95% CI 30.8–66.5%; 16/33), combined ORR 47.2% (95% CI 37.5–57.1%; 51/108); 80% (28/35) of metastatic responders and 81% (13/16) of locally advanced responders had ongoing responses at data cutoff
- The pivotal NEJM publication (Migden et al. 2018) reports an earlier, smaller data cut restricted to the Study 1423 expansion cohorts (26 patients, metastatic + locally advanced pooled, ORR 50%) and the Study 1540 metastatic-disease cohort alone (Group 1, n=59, ORR 47%) — it predates and does not include the locally advanced Group 2 cohort that the FDA's later, more mature review incorporated into the approved label
- No formal hypothesis test of ORR against a null rate was pre-specified; instead, sample size (53 metastatic, 76 locally advanced patients) was chosen so that, if the true ORR met design assumptions, the lower bound of the two-sided 95% exact binomial CI would exclude a pre-specified floor (15% metastatic, 25% locally advanced) — the two disease-group cohorts in Study 1540 did not reach their full planned enrollment targets before the BLA was filed, given the FDA/Regeneron agreement to file on the mature Group 1 data plus Group 2 data with adequate follow-up
- No stratification, randomization, blinding, DMC/interim alpha-spending boundary, or multiplicity adjustment across efficacy endpoints — consistent with a single-arm response-rate trial

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2018/761097Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (original, 2018) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/761097s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (combined Summary/Clinical/Statistical Review; primary statistical reviewer Mallorie Fiero; Reference ID 4324348) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/761097Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov records — Study 1540/EMPOWER-CSCC-1: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02760498, Study 1423: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02383212 (no protocol/SAP posted in either Documents tab; the ClinicalTrials.gov v2 API's `documentSection` field is empty for both records, confirmed via direct API query)
- Pivotal publication: Migden MR, Rischin D, Schmults CD, et al. "PD-1 Blockade with Cemiplimab in Advanced Cutaneous Squamous-Cell Carcinoma." *N Engl J Med.* 2018;379(4):341-351. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1805131), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29863979/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=PD-1%20Blockade%20with%20Cemiplimab%20in%20Advanced%20Cutaneous%20Squamous-Cell%20Carcinoma)

**Other resources**

- Regeneron's clinical-trial data-sharing policy/portal was not independently confirmed in this pass, and Regeneron does not appear to be a listed Vivli or YODA Project member; trial-specific IPD availability for Study 1540/Study 1423 should be checked directly with Regeneron before assuming access.
- No FDA advisory committee (ODAC) meeting was held; the approval letter states this was because the biologic "is not a first in class approval" (nivolumab and pembrolizumab were already approved PD-1 inhibitors in other indications; cemiplimab was the first PD-1 inhibitor specifically approved for CSCC) and the safety profile was considered acceptable for the indicated population.
- Postmarketing commitment 3489-1: submit the final Study 1540 (Groups 1, 2, and 3) clinical trial report with the final ORR/DOR analysis, requiring enrollment of at least 150 patients (including at least 75 with locally advanced CSCC) and at least 1.5 years of post-treatment follow-up, to further characterize durability of response — a PMC (not a PMR), reflecting that this was a regular- rather than accelerated-approval action with no confirmatory-trial requirement in the accelerated-approval sense.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761097, Reference ID 4324348, §8.1.1]* — "The primary efficacy endpoint of both Study 1423 and Study 1540 was ORR as assessed by central review. ORR was defined as the proportion of patients with best overall response of complete response (CR) or partial response (PR) in the intent-to-treat (ITT) population. Patients who were not evaluable (NE) were not considered to have achieved PR or CR for ORR."

*[verbatim, same source, Statistical Analysis Plan / ORR]* — "The sample size calculation in Study 1540 was based on the primary endpoint of ORR. For the metastatic CSCC group, a total of 53 patients were needed for an ORR of 15% to be excluded using the lower limit of a two-sided 95% CI. For the locally advanced CSCC group, a total of 76 patients were needed for an ORR of 25% to be excluded using the lower limit of a two-sided 95% CI. The primary analysis of ORR was analyzed using the exact binomial CI using the Clopper-Pearson method... The primary analysis was summarized together and by group using pooled data from Study 1423 and Study 1540."

*[verbatim, same source, §7.2 Review Strategy]* — "The efficacy review focused on the pooled results of patients enrolled in Study 1423 (Expansion cohorts 7 and 8) and patients enrolled in Study 1540 Groups 1 and 2. The efficacy results from Group 3 of Study 1540 were not mature at the time of data cutoff and were not reviewed to support the indication."

*[verbatim, same source, §1.2 Conclusions on the Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness]* — "Durable objective response rate of sufficient magnitude is an acceptable surrogate endpoint considered reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit (i.e., improved survival) in patients with advanced cancers. There is also regulatory precedent for durable tumor shrinkage as a primary endpoint to support regular approval for drugs treating malignancies with primary skin involvement... In summary, review of the efficacy and safety data in the BLA determined that cemiplimab should receive regular approval for both types of advanced CSCC: patients with metastatic CSCC and patients with locally advanced CSCC who are not candidates for surgery or curative radiation."

*[verbatim, same source, §9 Advisory Committee Meeting and Other External Consultations]* — "The Division did not obtain the advice of the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee (ODAC) or Special Government Employees (SGEs) for this application as there were no public health issues raised that would benefit from a public discussion or that required the expert opinions of the Committee."

*[verbatim, same source, §13 Postmarketing Requirements and Commitment]* — "To submit the (b)(4) trial report for trial R2810-ONC-1540 that includes the final analysis of objective response rate and duration of response in patients with advanced cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) including patients with metastatic disease and patients with locally advanced CSCC who are not candidates for surgery or radiation. Trial R2810-ONC-1540 will enroll at least 150 patients including at least 75 patients with locally advanced CSCC. All patients will have at least 1.5 years of follow-up following completion of cemiplimab treatment to further characterize the durability of responses in both subgroups."

Cross-reference note: unlike daratumumab/SIRIUS (BLA 761036, elsewhere in this census), where single-arm ORR supported accelerated approval under Subpart H with randomized Phase III confirmatory PMRs (POLLUX, CASTOR) required for conversion to regular approval, cemiplimab's single-arm, non-randomized, multicohort ORR data were judged by FDA to support regular approval outright — the review reasons that durable objective response, together with directly observed shrinkage of visible disfiguring CSCC lesions (documented via required baseline and on-treatment photography adjudicated by an independent composite response committee), itself constitutes direct clinical benefit in this disease, rather than treating ORR only as a surrogate for a separately required survival/PFS confirmation. This is a materially different regulatory reasoning from other single-arm oncology approvals in this census and is why the postmarketing obligation here is a PMC (further characterizing durability) rather than a PMR tied to accelerated-approval verification.

### 86. talazoparib (Talzenna) — NDA 211651

**Sponsor:** Pfizer Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adult patients with deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA-mutated (gBRCAm), HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer, selected for therapy based on an FDA-approved companion diagnostic for talazoparib (BRACAnalysis CDx)

**Approval date:** October 16, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** EMBRACA (Study C3441009), NCT01945775

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled (physician's-choice single-agent chemotherapy: capecitabine, eribulin, gemcitabine, or vinorelbine), biomarker-selected population (germline BRCA1/2 mutation via BRACAnalysis CDx or another applicant-approved lab), companion diagnostic co-approval, event-driven trial, multiple SAP amendments (4 versions) prior to database lock
- *Endpoints:* progression-free survival (PFS, primary, IRF/BICR-assessed), overall survival (OS, key secondary), objective response rate (ORR, investigator-assessed, exploratory as finalized), duration of response (DOR)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified), Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing — OS tested only if PFS reached significance; final SAP version (v4, Sept 2017) removed the planned multiplicity adjustment for ORR, leaving ORR analyzed descriptively/exploratorily with no type I error control
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* one planned interim OS analysis (at the time of the PFS analysis, ~160 deaths) using a Haybittle-Peto boundary at a 0.0001 two-sided significance level; final OS analysis planned at ~321 deaths at a 2-sided 0.0499 level
- *Missing data/bias:* standard right-censoring at last evaluable tumor assessment per a pre-specified censoring-rule table; FDA-conducted sensitivity analyses addressing discordance between IVRS/IWRS- and CRF-recorded stratification factors, an imbalance in censoring from earlier antineoplastic-therapy initiation on the talazoparib arm, and IRF-derived vs. raw-tumor-measurement progression status — all supportive of the primary PFS result
- *Regulatory:* companion diagnostic co-approval (Myriad Genetics BRACAnalysis CDx, PMA supplement reviewed concurrently by CDRH); no FDA advisory committee meeting was convened

**Trial design & endpoints**

- EMBRACA (C3441009): Phase 3, randomized (2:1), open-label, multicenter (145 centers, 16 countries) trial of talazoparib 1 mg orally QD vs. physician's choice of single-agent chemotherapy (capecitabine, eribulin, gemcitabine, or vinorelbine, selected per-patient before randomization) in patients with gBRCAm HER2-negative locally advanced/metastatic breast cancer who had received ≤3 prior cytotoxic regimens (n=431: 287 talazoparib, 144 PCT); the phase 3 control-arm agents were discussed and agreed with FDA at an End-of-Phase-2 meeting (April 12, 2013)
- Randomization was centralized (IVRS/IWRS) and stratified by number of prior cytotoxic chemotherapy regimens for locally advanced/metastatic disease (0 vs. 1, 2, or 3), triple-negative vs. non-triple-negative receptor status (most recent biopsy), and history of CNS metastasis (yes/no)
- Primary endpoint: PFS by Independent Radiology Facility (IRF/BICR) assessment (RECIST v1.1), ITT population, stratified log-rank test (two-sided alpha=0.05), with the stratified Cox model HR reported alongside; sample size was 429 patients (288 PFS events) to detect HR=0.67 with 90% power
- Key secondary endpoint: OS, formally tested via stratified log-rank test only if PFS reached significance; the trial was additionally powered for OS (~321 deaths, 80% power to detect HR=0.72)
- Other secondary/exploratory endpoints: investigator-assessed ORR (with pre-specified multiplicity control dropped in the final SAP version), duration of response, and PRO instruments (EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-BR23, exploratory, no formal statistical testing/no type I error control)
- The SAP went through 4 versions (initial: Feb 28, 2013; final: Sept 1, 2017) — key changes tracked target PFS events (256→288), added/then removed a stratified CMH test and multiplicity adjustment for ORR, and clarified the OS interim/final alpha allocation; FDA's reviewer concluded there were "no major changes to the primary efficacy endpoints and analysis prior to data cut-off that would compromise the integrity of the trial"
- Primary result: PFS HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.41-0.71, stratified log-rank p<0.0001; median PFS 8.6 vs. 5.6 months). OS at data cutoff (163 deaths, ~51% of the target for final analysis) was immature and not statistically significant (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.55-1.06, p=0.1053) and did not cross the pre-specified Haybittle-Peto interim boundary; investigator-assessed ORR was 50.2% vs. 18.4% (exploratory, no formal test)

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2018/211651Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/211651s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review and Evaluation (includes Statistical Review; Reference ID 4334555; Statistical Reviewer Stella Karuri, Statistical Team Leader Lijun Zhang) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/211651Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (EMBRACA) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01945775 (no protocol/SAP posted in the Documents tab as of this writing)
- Pivotal publication: Litton JK, Rugo HS, Ettl J, et al. "Talazoparib in Patients with Advanced Breast Cancer and a Germline BRCA Mutation." *N Engl J Med.* 2018;379:753-763. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1802905), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30110579/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Talazoparib%20in%20Patients%20with%20Advanced%20Breast%20Cancer%20and%20a%20Germline%20BRCA%20Mutation)

**Other resources**

- Pfizer participates in data-sharing arrangements (Vivli); trial-specific IPD availability for EMBRACA was not individually confirmed.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this application (per the MDR: "No ODAC was convened for this application").
- Companion diagnostic: BRACAnalysis CDx (Myriad Genetics), originally approved December 19, 2014, updated concurrently via PMA supplement using EMBRACA PFS data from the 354 BRACAnalysis-CDx-confirmed patients (comparable to the full 431-patient ITT results).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review and Evaluation, NDA 211651, Reference ID 4334555, §8 Statistical Analysis Plan]* — "The study was sized to detect a PFS hazard ratio (HR) of 0.67 with 90% power using a log-rank test with alpha (two-sided) equal to 0.05... Up to 429 patients were to be randomized at a ratio of 2:1 to the talazoparib and PCT arms and a total of 288 PFS events were needed for the PFS analysis."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "The primary analysis was event driven and was timed to occur with 288 PFS events (by IRF) in the ITT population. The primary method of analysis was a stratified log-rank test, with stratification factors equal to the IVRS/IWRS stratification factors: Number of prior cytotoxic chemotherapy regimens for locally advanced and/or metastatic disease (0 vs 1, 2, or 3); Triple-negative...vs non triple-negative receptor status...; History of central nervous system (CNS) metastasis vs no CNS metastasis... If PFS results reached statistical significance, formal hypothesis tests for OS would be performed via a stratified log-rank test with stratification factors equal to the randomization stratification factors."

*[verbatim, same source, Interim Analyses]* — "No interim analysis was planned for PFS. One interim analysis of OS was to be performed at the time of the PFS analysis at a 0.0001 significance level using Haybittle-Peto boundary if PFS is statistically significant, with approximately 160 deaths... The final analysis of OS would be conducted with the occurrence of approximately 321 death events at a 2-sided 0.0499 significance level. Reviewer's comments: No other multiplicity adjustments were planned for other secondary endpoints apart from OS. The Haybittle-Peto boundaries are more conservative than the O'Brien Fleming type boundaries."

*[verbatim, same source, SAP Amendments]* — "There were four versions of the SAP; the initial version of the SAP is dated February 28, 2013. The agency provided feedback to this SAP in a meeting on December 4th, 2013 (IND108708)... Version 4 dated September 1, 2017: This is the final analysis plan. Multiplicity adjustments for ORR were removed to allow for an alpha of 0.0499 for the final OS analysis. Reviewer's comments: There were no major changes to the primary efficacy endpoints and analysis prior to data cut-off that would compromise the integrity of the trial."

*[verbatim, same source, OS Analysis]* — "The results from the stratified log-rank test were not statistically significant (HR: 0.76 (95% CI: 0.55, 1.06), p-value=0.1053)... Reviewer's comments: Results from the interim OS analysis did not cross the pre-specified boundary corresponding to the statistical significance level of 0.0001. The final analysis is timed to occur with 321 deaths."

*[verbatim, same source, Investigator Assessed ORR]* — "Reviewer's comments: Per SAP, no multiplicity adjustments were planned for other secondary endpoints apart from OS, therefore, ORR analysis is considered exploratory."

This is a case where FDA's own review narrates the SAP's evolution across four dated versions (2013-2017), including the sponsor dropping a previously-planned ORR multiplicity adjustment in the final version specifically to free up alpha for the final OS analysis — documented by the reviewer as not compromising trial integrity, but a clear instance of late-stage SAP flexibility disclosed rather than concealed.

### 87. lorlatinib (Lorbrena) — NDA 210868

**Sponsor:** Pfizer, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of patients with anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK)-positive metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) whose disease has progressed on crizotinib and at least one other ALK inhibitor, or on alectinib or ceritinib as the first ALK inhibitor for metastatic disease

**Approval date:** November 2, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** Study B7461001, NCT01970865

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial, non-randomized multi-cohort dose-finding and dose-expansion (Phase 1/2) design, biomarker-selected population (ALK-positive NSCLC, ROS1-positive cohort also enrolled but not part of this indication), continual reassessment model (CRM) for dose-finding, post-hoc recombination of differently-enrolled cohorts into one primary analysis population (FDA-defined "primary efficacy population" spanning Part 1, Part 2, and the Japanese lead-in cohort, broader than any single sponsor-reported cohort)
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR, primary for Part 2, per independent review committee [IRC]/RECIST v1.1), intracranial objective response rate (IC-ORR, primary for Part 2, per modified RECIST for CNS lesions), duration of response (DOR, secondary), progression-free survival and overall survival (secondary, explicitly non-interpretable in a single-arm design), Cycle 1 dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs, primary endpoint of Part 1 and the Japanese lead-in cohort)
- *Primary analysis:* descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (point estimate + exact/Clopper-Pearson 95% CI, no formal hypothesis test), Kaplan-Meier estimation (DOR, PFS, OS, descriptive only)
- *Missing data/bias:* investigator-vs-IRC discordance analysis of intracranial response (reviewer-conducted, not a pre-specified sensitivity analysis)
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval (21 CFR 314.510) based on ORR and durability of response in a single-arm trial; reviewer-documented deviation from the sponsor's planned analysis structure — FDA rejected Pfizer's cohort-by-cohort/subgroup-pooled reporting and instead defined its own broader "primary efficacy population" pooling all ALK-positive patients across Part 1, Part 2, and the Japanese lead-in cohort who received the 100 mg recommended Phase 2 dose; postmarketing requirement for a randomized confirmatory trial (later fulfilled by CROWN, NCT03052608) in treatment-naive ALK-positive NSCLC

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study B7461001: a global, two-part, multi-cohort, open-label, non-randomized, multicenter Phase 1/2 trial of lorlatinib in 334 patients with advanced ALK-positive or ROS1-positive NSCLC (accelerated approval supported only by the ALK-positive population); Part 1 was a dose-finding study (continual reassessment model, 10-200 mg cumulative daily dose range, 12-36 patients planned; 54 enrolled, 15 ALK-positive and treated at the 100 mg recommended Phase 2 dose [RP2D]); Part 2 was a dose-expansion study enrolling into cohorts EXP-1 through EXP-6 defined by line of therapy and prior ALK-TKI/chemotherapy exposure, plus a separate Japanese-patient-only lead-in cohort (3 patients)
- Primary endpoint of Part 1 and the Japanese lead-in cohort: Cycle 1 DLTs, used to establish the RP2D (100 mg once daily); primary endpoints of Part 2: ORR and IC-ORR per independent central radiology (ICR/IRC) assessment using RECIST v1.1 (extracranial) and a modified RECIST for intracranial lesions (up to 5 CNS target lesions ≥5 mm by gadolinium-contrast MRI, confirmation required ≥4 weeks after initial response); investigator (INV)-assessed ORR/IC-ORR, PFS, OS, and DOR were secondary
- Sample size logic was not a formal hypothesis test: the sponsor's SAP specified separate ORR analyses by cohort (EXP-1 through EXP-6) and by several pooled subgroups (EXP-2:EXP-5, EXP-2:EXP-3, EXP-4:EXP-5, and sub-splits of EXP-3 into EXP-3A/EXP-3B), sized to produce informative 95% CIs around the observed response rate at different assumed true rates rather than to power a Neyman-Pearson test; no formal statistical hypothesis was pre-specified or tested for either Part
- The protocol was amended seven times (June 2013-March 2018); Amendment 3 (Oct 2014) added a rule that "if the total number of responding patients is equal to or greater than 20 for each subpopulation, then the null hypothesis will be rejected," and progressively increased/reallocated cohort sample sizes as the RP2D and post-crizotinib treatment landscape were refined
- FDA's statistical reviewer did not accept Pfizer's cohort/subgroup reporting structure as the basis for the efficacy claim: Pfizer reported the pooled subgroup EXP-2:EXP-3A (not the SAP-specified EXP-2:EXP-3) and reported efficacy by trial Part rather than pooling across Parts; FDA instead defined its own "primary efficacy population" as all patients across Study B7461001 purported to have ALK-positive NSCLC who received the 100 mg RP2D (n=215), spanning Part 1, Part 2, and the Japanese lead-in cohort together
- Key result in the FDA-defined primary efficacy population (data cutoff Sept 15, 2017): ORR per IRC 48% (95% CI 42-55%), IC-ORR per IRC 54% (95% CI 45-62%) among 149 patients with baseline intracranial disease, median DOR 12.5 months (95% CI 8.4-23.7) overall and 19.6 months (95% CI 14.5-NE) intracranially; ORR per investigator was lower (44%, 95% CI 37-51%) and IC-ORR per investigator markedly lower (31%, 95% CI 23-39%) than per IRC, prompting a dedicated FDA discordance analysis (26-31% discordance rate between IRC and INV intracranial response calls, attributed mainly to IRC calling responses that investigators did not)
- FDA's statistical reviewer explicitly stated: "Time-to-event endpoints are not interpretable in a single-arm trial" — PFS and OS were reported only descriptively and played no role in the accelerated-approval determination

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/210868s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (combined clinical/statistical, Reference ID 4344794) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/210868Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf

"Lorlatinib in patients with ALK-positive non-small-cell lung cancer: results from a global phase 2 study." *Lancet Oncol.* 2018;19(12):1654-1667. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(18)30649-1>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30413378/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Lorlatinib%20in%20patients%20with%20ALK-positive%20non-small-cell%20lung%20cancer%20results%20from%20a%20global%20phase%202%20study)

**Other resources**

- Pfizer participates in the Vivli data-sharing platform; trial-specific IPD availability for Study B7461001 was not individually confirmed.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held; the approval letter states this was because "this drug is not the first in its class, outside expertise was not necessary and there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion."
- Postmarketing requirement: conduct and submit results of at least one multicenter, randomized clinical trial verifying clinical benefit of lorlatinib in treatment-naive, advanced/metastatic ALK-positive NSCLC — subsequently fulfilled by the CROWN trial (NCT03052608), which supported later conversion/expansion of lorlatinib's approval to the first-line setting.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 210868, Reference ID 4344794, Review Strategy]* — "The NDA submission contained data from one non-randomized, multi-cohort, dose-finding and activity-estimating trial, Study B7461001... The review of efficacy is based on Study B7461001, including the Clinical Study Report (CSR), case report forms (CRFs), statistical analysis plan (SAP), datasets, and Statistical Analysis System (SAS) program."

*[verbatim, same source, Statistical Analysis Plan section]* — "The ITT analysis set as defined in the protocol included all enrolled patients with documented ALK or ROS1 rearrangement who received at least one dose of lorlatinib (including Day-7 Lead-in dose). The primary analysis of ORR was the point estimate of ORR accompanied by the corresponding exact 95% confidence interval (CI). Time-to-event endpoints (PFS and OS) were described using Kaplan-Meier methods."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "The statistical analysis plan (SAP) specified that the primary ORR analysis was to be performed separately for each cohort EXP-1 through EXP-6. In addition, the SAP stated that the primary analysis would be performed on the following pooled subgroups: EXP-2:EXP-5..., EXP-2:EXP-3, and EXP-4:EXP-5... Part 1 employed a continual reassessment model (CRM) to estimate the MTD... No formal statistical hypothesis was tested... In Part 2, the sample size was based on the 95% CI which would result for different levels of response in the pooled subgroups and cohorts... No formal statistical hypotheses were tested."

*[verbatim, same source, Reviewer's Comment]* — "Pfizer reported the pooled subgroup EXP-2:EXP-3A rather than EXP-2:EXP-3. As described below, FDA requested Pfizer to report efficacy data for all patients across the study who were purported to have ALK-positive NSCLC and received 100 mg of lorlatinib. Pfizer did not report this, but rather reported efficacy by part for patients in this group. This review defines the primary efficacy population as any patient in Study B761001 who was purported to have ALK-positive NSCLC and received 100 mg of lorlatinib."

*[verbatim, same source, Efficacy Results]* — "Reviewer's Comment: The intracranial response rate per INV (31%) was lower than the intracranial response rate per IRC (53%). Refer to Section 19.5 for evaluation of discordance."... "Reviewer's Comment: Time-to-event endpoints are not interpretable in a single-arm trial."

*[verbatim, same source, §19.5 Discordance analysis]* — "The discordance rate between IRC and INV in assessing intracranial response among those patients with CNS disease was 26%... Although the discordance rates between INV and IRC are similar for ORR and IC-ORR, the source of discordance is different. For ORR, discrepancies in response assessment are similar between IRC reporting a non-responder as a responder and vice versa. For IC-ORR, all but two of the cases of discordance are caused by the IRC reporting a non-responder per INV as a responder."

*[verbatim, FDA Approval Letter, NDA 210868, Reference ID 4344940]* — "This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and durability of response. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in the confirmatory trials."... "3500-1: Conduct and submit the results of at least one multicenter, randomized clinical trial that verifies and describes the clinical benefit of lorlatinib in patients with locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer without a history of prior systemic therapy for advanced disease and whose tumors harbor anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) gene arrangement."

This is a genuine example of FDA statistical review substantively overriding a sponsor's own analysis-population definition in a single-arm accelerated-approval submission — rather than simply accepting Pfizer's cohort/subgroup reporting, the reviewer constructed an independent, more inclusive "primary efficacy population" pooling patients across the trial's dose-finding, dose-expansion, and Japanese lead-in components, and then further audited the reliability of the resulting intracranial response claim through a dedicated IRC-vs-investigator discordance analysis.

### 88. glasdegib (Daurismo) — NDA 210656

**Sponsor:** Pfizer, Inc.

**Indication approved:** In combination with low-dose cytarabine, for treatment of newly-diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia (AML) in adult patients who are >75 years old or who have comorbidities that preclude use of intensive induction chemotherapy

**Approval date:** November 21, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** BRIGHT AML 1003 (Study B1371003), randomized Phase 2 "P2Unfit" sub-study, NCT01546038

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized (2:1), open-label, active-controlled (low-dose cytarabine [LDAC] alone comparator), event-driven trial (target 92 OS events), stratified by cytogenetic risk (poor vs. good/intermediate), randomized sub-study nested within a larger multi-cohort Phase 1b/2 trial that also included non-randomized intensive-chemotherapy and decitabine cohorts
- *Endpoints:* overall survival (OS, primary), complete response (CR) rate and other response categories (CRi, MLFS, PR, PRi, MR, SD, CRc, CRm — secondary, exploratory, no formal multiplicity plan)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test (one-sided alpha=0.10, Full Analysis Set = all randomized patients), Kaplan-Meier estimation, unstratified log-rank test and Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified, run with two alternative stratification-factor sources — IVRS vs. CRF — as secondary/supportive analyses of the primary endpoint)
- *Multiplicity:* unadjusted secondary/supportive testing (single formal primary endpoint) — FDA's reviewer explicitly noted no formal plan to control multiplicity across the many secondary/response endpoints, so these are properly viewed as exploratory
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design with one planned non-binding futility analysis at 46 OS events (50% information), Fleming-Harrington rho(1) beta-spending function for the futility boundary
- *Missing data/bias:* standard right-censoring at last known-alive date (with partial-date imputation rules for missing day/month only); post-hoc covariate-adjusted sensitivity analyses (Cox models adjusting individually and jointly for gender, serum creatinine, ECOG status, cardiac-disease severity, and age) conducted by FDA to probe an observed baseline imbalance between arms
- *Regulatory:* liberal one-sided alpha threshold (0.10, versus the more conventional one-sided 0.025) used by the sponsor for the primary OS analysis, with FDA explicitly confirming the efficacy conclusion also held under a stricter one-sided 0.025 criterion; full/regular approval (not accelerated approval/Subpart H) granted on the basis of OS from a randomized Phase 2 trial rather than a dedicated Phase 3; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- BRIGHT AML 1003 (Study B1371003) was an open-label, multicenter Phase 1b/2 trial of glasdegib (an oral Hedgehog-pathway inhibitor) evaluated across three chemotherapy-combination settings; the pivotal evidence for this approval comes specifically from "P2Unfit," a randomized (2:1) Phase 2 sub-study comparing glasdegib + low-dose cytarabine (G+LDAC) to LDAC alone in patients with previously untreated AML or high-risk MDS considered unfit for intensive induction chemotherapy (age ≥75, ECOG PS 2, serum creatinine >1.3 mg/dL, or severe cardiac disease at screening)
- Randomization was stratified by cytogenetic risk (poor — inv(3), t(6;9), 11q23, -5, del(5q), -7, abnl(17p), or complex karyotype [≥3 clonal abnormalities] — vs. good/intermediate); 132 patients were randomized (88 G+LDAC, 44 LDAC alone)
- Primary endpoint: overall survival (OS), defined as time from randomization to death from any cause, with survivors censored at last known-alive date; OS assessed monthly for 2 months post-discontinuation, then every 2 months, followed for up to 4 years from first dose
- Secondary endpoints: complete response (CR) and a family of related response categories (CRi, MLFS, PR, PRi, MR, SD, CRc, CRm), adverse events, pharmacodynamic/pharmacokinetic parameters, and QTc interval — analyzed on a Full Analysis Set (all randomized patients) using derived-response data as primary and investigator-assessed data as secondary, with no formal multiplicity control across this secondary-endpoint family
- Sample size: assuming a historical median OS of ~5 months for LDAC vs. an expected 8 months for G+LDAC (HR≈0.625), a 2:1 randomization, ~13-month accrual, ~6-month follow-up, one-sided alpha=0.10 log-rank test, and one non-binding futility analysis at 46 OS events (50% information, Fleming-Harrington rho(1) beta-spending function), a total of 92 OS events was calculated to provide 80% power to detect HR=0.625
- Primary analysis (per SAP, reproduced in the FDA statistical review's Table 2): OS in the FAS via a stratified (by cytogenetic risk) one-sided log-rank test (alpha=0.10) with Kaplan-Meier estimation; secondary/supportive analyses included an unstratified log-rank test and Cox models using two alternative sources of stratification data (IVRS-recorded vs. CRF-recorded cytogenetic risk), and a sensitivity analysis censoring at transplant
- FDA's statistical reviewer restricted its primary efficacy conclusion to the AML-only subset of randomized patients (excluding ~12% MDS patients and one patient with indeterminate AML status), reporting OS HR 0.46 (95% CI 0.30-0.71), one-sided log-rank p=0.0002, median OS 8.3 vs. 4.3 months, and CR 18.2% (14/77) vs. 2.6% (1/38) — consistent with, but a more conservative population than, the sponsor's all-randomized-patients (AML+MDS) result of HR 0.51 (95% CI 0.34-0.77), p=0.0004
- The approved label's efficacy population (Section 14) matches FDA's AML-restricted analysis: 115 AML patients aged ≥55 (77 G+LDAC, 38 LDAC alone), OS HR 0.46 (95% CI 0.30-0.71), one-sided log-rank p=0.0002 (Cox model stratified by cytogenetic risk), median OS 8.3 vs. 4.3 months
- FDA noted a baseline imbalance between arms (gender, ECOG status, cardiac-disease severity) despite randomization and, rather than treating this as invalidating, ran its own multivariable Cox sensitivity analyses adjusting for each imbalanced covariate individually and jointly; the adjusted HRs (0.44-0.46 across six models) were consistent with the primary result

- Glasdegib carries orphan drug designation for this indication (noted in the FDA approval letter's postmarketing-reporting-exemption discussion).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 210656, Reference ID 4354085, §3.1.2]* — "P2Unfit initiates after Phase 1b identifies the RP2D. It is a Phase 2, randomized (2:1 ratio), open-label study that directly compares the efficacy and safety of G+LDAC to LDAC alone. Randomization is stratified by cytogenetic risk (poor vs good/intermediate)."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.1.2.2 Sample Size Determination]* — "The historical median OS for LDAC was estimated at 5 months and the expected median OS for G+LDAC is 8 months, which induces an expected HR=0.625. Based on the following design parameters: 2:1 randomization, a planned accrual period of approximately 13 months, a follow-up period of approximately 6 months, a 1-sided log-rank test with one-sided α = 0.1 (type I error) and one futility analysis when 46 OS events are observed (50% information, rho(1) beta spending function), a total of 92 OS events provide 80% power to detect a hazard ratio of 0.625. A total of 132 subjects (88 in the G+LDAC arm and 44 in the LDAC arm) were randomized."

*[verbatim, same source, Table 2, "Excerpted from Table 2 in the statistical analysis plan"]* — primary analysis of OS: "Stratified log-rank test (1-sided, α = 0.10) Kaplan-Meier estimate" on the Full Analysis Set, with censoring rules applied for missing data, objective "Primary analysis"; secondary analyses specified a matching unstratified log-rank test and "Cox model to be run with two different set of stratification factors: as per IVRS (main Cox model analysis) and as per CRF (secondary Cox model analysis)"; a further stratified log-rank/Kaplan-Meier sensitivity analysis was specified "Sensitivity Analysis of primary endpoint" censoring upon receiving transplant.

*[verbatim, same source, §5.1.2 Multiple Endpoints]* — "As noted in Section 3.1.3, the primary endpoint is OS and there are multiple secondary endpoints with no formal plan to address multiple testing. Without such a plan, complete remission and other endpoints can reasonably be viewed as exploratory endpoints."

*[verbatim, same source, §5.1.1 Overview]* — "There are no major statistical issues that have the potential to invalidate the overall efficacy conclusion that glasdegib, in combination with low-dose cytarabine, is superior to low-dose cytarabine alone as characterized by overall survival and complete remission. Although the sponsor presented results based on one-sided α = 0.10 in the CSR, the conclusion remains intact under the more stringent one-sided α = 0.025 criterion."

*[verbatim, same source, §5.1.3 Baseline Imbalance]* — "An examination of baseline characteristics in Section 3.1.5 identified notable differences in the baseline distributions of various attributes between the two arms; for example, Gender, ECOG status, and Cardiac disease severity. It is not clear as to the reasons for the observed imbalance as the study was randomized... The Agency conducted additional sensitivity analyses to examine the behavior of the hazard ratio under various models... the superiority of G+LDAC over LDAC alone continues to hold after adjusting for potentially imbalanced covariates."

Cross-reference note: this is a rare case in the census of a drug receiving full/regular (not accelerated) approval on the strength of a randomized Phase 2 trial rather than a purpose-built Phase 3 — FDA's statistical review is explicit that it independently re-derived the efficacy conclusion on a narrower (AML-only, one patient excluded) population than the sponsor's all-randomized-patients analysis, and that it re-checked the result against a stricter alpha threshold than the sponsor's own one-sided 0.10 design choice.

### 89. larotrectinib (Vitrakvi) — NDA 210861

**Sponsor:** Loxo Oncology, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adult and pediatric patients with solid tumors that have a neurotrophic receptor tyrosine kinase (NTRK) gene fusion without a known acquired resistance mutation, are metastatic or where surgical resection is likely to result in severe morbidity, and have no satisfactory alternative treatments or that have progressed following treatment

**Approval date:** November 26, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** pooled analysis across three single-arm trials — LOXO-TRK-14001 (adult Phase 1), NCT02122913; SCOUT (LOXO-TRK-15003, pediatric Phase 1/2), NCT02637687; NAVIGATE (LOXO-TRK-15002, adult/adolescent Phase 2 basket), NCT02576431

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* tumor-agnostic basket trial, pooled/integrated analysis across three independently conducted single-arm trials of different phase and population (adult Phase 1, pediatric Phase 1/2, adult/adolescent Phase 2 basket), formally agreed sponsor-FDA Statistical Analysis Plan for an Integrated Summary of Efficacy (ISE) defining a fixed-size "Primary Analysis Set" (first 55 evaluable NTRK-fusion patients across all three trials) rather than a single trial's enrollment, biomarker-defined population (NTRK1/2/3 gene fusion, tumor histology-agnostic), rare-disease/ultra-rare-biomarker population (estimated US incidence 1,500-5,000 cases/year across all tumor types)
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR, primary, per independent review committee [IRC] using RECIST v1.1 confirmed CR/PR), duration of response (DOR, secondary, Kaplan-Meier with Greenwood's-formula CI)
- *Primary analysis:* exact (Clopper-Pearson) binomial confidence interval around ORR, descriptive Kaplan-Meier estimation for DOR, exploratory subgroup analyses of ORR/DOR by tumor type and by NTRK fusion subtype (NTRK1/2/3), FDA-conducted concurrence analysis between IRC and investigator response assessments
- *Multiplicity:* not applicable — single primary endpoint, no comparative or multi-endpoint hypothesis test
- *Missing data/bias:* not applicable in the conventional censoring sense (no comparator arm); FDA explicitly noted the pooled population's small size and tumor-type heterogeneity as a residual uncertainty rather than a bias-correction issue
- *Regulatory:* second-ever tumor-agnostic accelerated approval (21 CFR 314, Subpart H), after pembrolizumab/MSI-H — approval based on a sponsor-FDA-agreed pooled analysis of the first 55 enrolled NTRK-fusion patients across three trials rather than a single pivotal study; postmarketing requirement for further confirmatory data (including a minimum patient threshold in colorectal cancer, NSCLC, CNS tumors, and melanoma) to verify clinical benefit; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held, but three special government employees (SGEs) consulted via teleconference in lieu of a public ODAC

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Efficacy for the tumor-agnostic indication rests on a pooled analysis of the first 55 evaluable adult and pediatric patients with NTRK-fusion-positive solid tumors enrolled and treated with larotrectinib across three independently conducted, multicenter, open-label, single-arm trials: LOXO-TRK-14001 (adult Phase 1 dose-escalation/expansion), NAVIGATE/LOXO-TRK-15002 (adult/adolescent Phase 2 basket trial across 9 tumor-type cohorts), and SCOUT/LOXO-TRK-15003 (pediatric Phase 1/2); the broader safety database spanned 176 patients (both NTRK-fusion-positive and NTRK-fusion-negative "all comers" enrolled in the same protocols)
- Sponsor-FDA agreements incorporated into a dedicated Statistical Analysis Plan for the Integrated Summary of Efficacy (ISE) fixed the primary efficacy analysis to a "Primary Analysis Set" (PAS) of the first 55 patients meeting three criteria: documented NTRK fusion by local testing, non-CNS primary tumor with ≥1 measurable lesion by RECIST 1.1, and receipt of ≥1 dose of larotrectinib — a population defined across trials and by enrollment order rather than within any single protocol
- Primary endpoint: ORR by independent review committee (IRC) assessment (confirmed CR or PR per RECIST 1.1), analyzed as a point estimate with a 2-sided 95% exact (Clopper-Pearson) binomial CI on the PAS; secondary endpoint DOR (time from first CR/PR to progression or death), summarized descriptively by Kaplan-Meier with Greenwood's-formula CI
- Sample-size logic: assuming an observed ORR of at least 50%, a sample of 55 patients provided 80% power to exclude 30% from the lower bound of the 2-sided 95% CI for ORR — a threshold negotiated with FDA (at the Breakthrough Therapy meeting and pre-NDA meeting) specifically because the extreme rarity of NTRK-fusion solid tumors precluded a randomized controlled trial or a larger single-tumor-type study
- Result (data cutoff Feb 19, 2018): ORR 75% (95% CI 61-85%) in the PAS (22% CR, 53% PR); median DOR not reached, with 73% of the 41 responders having DOR ≥6 months and 39% having DOR ≥12 months (range 1.6-33.2 months); FDA additionally conducted its own IRC-vs-investigator concurrence analysis and exploratory subgroup analyses of ORR/DOR by tumor histology and by NTRK1/2/3 fusion subtype, both described in the review as exploratory given small subgroup sample sizes
- FDA's benefit-risk review explicitly framed the pooling decision as resting on a specific evidentiary chain — strong biologic rationale for TRK inhibition, consistent nonclinical antitumor activity across NTRK-fusion partners, and clinically consistent durable tumor shrinkage across histologically diverse tumors — concluding that "pooling of results from patients with NTRK fusion-solid tumors was warranted and supported a tissue agnostic indication"
- As a condition of accelerated approval, Loxo Oncology was required to conduct postmarketing studies providing additional ORR/DOR data (via independent central review, ≥12 months follow-up for responders) in tumor types underrepresented in the approval population — specifically colorectal cancer, NSCLC, CNS tumors, and melanoma — plus a minimum of 40 patients across other rarer histologies

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2018/210861Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/210861s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (joint review of NDA 210861 capsules and NDA 211710 oral solution; Reference ID 4354090; Statistical Reviewer Xiaoping (Janet) Jiang, PhD) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/210861Orig1s000_211710Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov records — LOXO-TRK-14001: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02122913, SCOUT: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02637687, NAVIGATE: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02576431 (no protocol/SAP posted in any of the three Documents tabs; confirmed via the CT.gov API v2 study records, none of which return a `documentSection` field)
- Pivotal publication: Drilon A, Laetsch TW, Kummar S, DuBois SG, Lassen UN, Demetri GD, Nathenson M, Doebele RC, Farago AF, Pappo AS, Turpin B, Dowlati A, Brose MS, Mascarenhas L, Federman N, Berlin J, El-Deiry WS, Baik C, Deeken J, Boni V, Nagasubramanian R, Taylor M, Rudzinski ER, Meric-Bernstam F, Sohal DPS, Ma PC, Raez LE, Hechtman JF, Benayed R, Ladanyi M, Tuch BB, Ebata K, Cruickshank S, Ku NC, Cox MC, Hawkins DS, Hong DS, Hyman DM. "Efficacy of Larotrectinib in TRK Fusion-Positive Cancers in Adults and Children." *N Engl J Med.* 2018;378(8):731-739. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1714448), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29466156/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Efficacy%20of%20Larotrectinib%20in%20TRK%20Fusion-Positive%20Cancers%20in%20Adults%20and%20Children)

**Other resources**

- No IPD-sharing platform participation (Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere) was identified for Loxo Oncology (acquired by Eli Lilly in 2019, after this approval); trial-specific data availability was not confirmed.
- No public FDA Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held. FDA instead cleared three special government employees (an adult oncologist, a pediatric oncologist, and a patient representative with rare-cancer expertise) through the Advisory Committee Oversight and Management Staff for a private divisional consultation, each indicating via teleconference that the risk-benefit assessment was favorable.
- FDA's review explicitly compared this approval's evidentiary challenges to the only prior tumor-agnostic approval, pembrolizumab (MSI-H/dMMR, 2017), noting larotrectinib's efficacy population (N=55) was smaller than pembrolizumab's (N=149) but that larotrectinib's safety database (N=176) was comparatively small due to the rarity of NTRK-fusion tumors and its status as a new molecular entity.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation, NDA 210861/211710, Reference ID 4354090, Statistical Analysis Plan for Integrated Summary of Efficacy]* — "Agreements between Loxo Oncology and FDA on issues that affect the statistical analysis were incorporated into the statistical analysis plan for the ISE. The most notable agreements include the following: The primary analysis of effectiveness would be based on results from the first 55 evaluable patients with NTRK fusion cancers enrolled and treated with larotrectinib across Studies 14001, 15002, and 15003. Overall response rate (ORR) determined by an independent review committee (IRC) would serve as the primary endpoint for efficacy."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "The analyses described in the SAP were primarily based on the Primary Analysis Set (PAS). The PAS was defined as the first 55 patients (pediatrics and adults) enrolled across clinical studies LOXO-TRK-14001, -15002, and -15003 who met the following criteria: 1) documented NTRK fusion as determined by local testing[,] 2) non-CNS primary tumor with 1 or more measurable lesions at baseline as assessed by RECIST 1.1[,] 3) received 1 or more doses of larotrectinib... The prespecified primary analysis of the ORR was a point estimate based on the proportion of patients in the PAS with best overall response of confirmed CR or confirmed PR with a 2-sided 95% exact binomial CI using the Clopper-Pearson method. The SAP considered that the effectiveness of larotrectinib would be demonstrated if the lower limit of the 2-sided 95% CI for the point estimate of ORR exceeded 30%."

*[verbatim, same source, Clinical Reviewer comment]* — "During the initial breakthrough therapy meeting and the pre-NDA meeting, FDA requested that Loxo Oncology provide a justification for the proposed size of the efficacy population (N=55) supporting this application. FDA concluded that the rarity of solid tumors harboring the activating NTRK rearrangements precluded the conduct of randomized controlled trials and that the size of the efficacy population was adequate to characterize the overall response rate in patients with NTRK-positive solid tumors."

*[verbatim, same source, Benefit-Risk Assessment]* — "In light of these factors, the FDA review teams concluded that pooling of results from patients with NTRK fusion-solid tumors was warranted and supported a tissue agnostic indication."... "FDA determined that additional data are needed to verify and describe the clinical benefit of larotrectinib given numerous histologic subtypes of cancer included in this indication and the relatively small efficacy database supporting these applications. Granting accelerated approval allows for residual uncertainty to be addressed regarding the biomarker-driven indication, regardless of histology."

*[verbatim, same source, §13 Postmarketing Requirements and Commitment]* — "Submit the final report, including datasets, from ongoing and proposed trials conducted to verify and describe the clinical benefit of larotrectinib, through more precise estimation of the overall response rate and mature response duration per independent review assessment... A sufficient number of patients will be evaluated to characterize response and durability of response for each of the following tumor types: colorectal cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, central nervous system tumors, and melanoma."

*[verbatim, same source, §9 Advisory Committee Meeting and Other External Consultations]* — "FDA did not hold an advisory committee meeting for these applications because no review issues were identified that raised significant public health questions regarding the risk:benefit assessment of larotrectinib for the proposed indication."

This is one of the census's clearest examples of a "SAP" being constructed at the cross-trial level rather than within a single protocol — the operative statistical document is the sponsor-FDA-agreed ISE plan defining a fixed enrollment-order-based pooled population (the first 55 qualifying patients across three separately-designed trials of different phase and age population), not any one trial's own SAP.

### 90. gilteritinib (Xospata) — NDA 211349

**Sponsor:** Astellas Pharma US, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adult patients who have relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with a FMS-like tyrosine kinase 3 (FLT3) mutation as detected by an FDA-approved test

**Approval date:** November 28, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** ADMIRAL (Study 2215-CL-0301), NCT02421939

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized (2:1), open-label, active-controlled (salvage chemotherapy: LDAC, azacitidine, MEC, or FLAG-IDA per investigator preselection), event-driven trial, stratified by response to first-line AML therapy and preselected salvage chemotherapy, companion diagnostic co-approval (LeukoStrat CDx FLT3 Mutation Assay), interim single-arm response-rate analysis nested within an ongoing randomized trial while the sponsor remained blinded to the randomized comparison
- *Endpoints:* co-primary endpoints of complete remission/complete remission with partial hematologic recovery rate (CR/CRh, evaluated only at the first interim analysis, gilteritinib arm only) and overall survival (OS, evaluated only at the second interim and final analyses, full randomized comparison); key secondary event-free survival (EFS) and CR rate (gated behind OS); other secondary endpoints included duration of CR/CRh, transfusion-independence conversion rate, and CRc (CR+CRi+CRp)
- *Primary analysis:* exact (two-sided 95%) binomial confidence interval around CR/CRh rate compared against a pre-specified 12% benchmark (first interim analysis only), stratified log-rank test and stratified Cox proportional-hazards model for OS (planned for later analyses), Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing for OS→EFS→CR, each tested only if the preceding endpoint's null hypothesis was rejected, to preserve the overall one-sided alpha=0.025; the CR/CRh interim analysis used a separate, non-recycled nominal alpha (0.0005 one-sided) that was explicitly walled off from the OS/EFS/CR family
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design for the co-primary OS endpoint, O'Brien-Fleming boundaries (non-binding) implemented via the Lan-DeMets alpha/beta-spending method, Independent Data Monitoring Committee (IDMC) oversight, two planned interim analyses (CR/CRh at ~141 gilteritinib-arm subjects/112 days follow-up; OS at ~129 of 258 planned deaths) plus a final OS analysis (258 deaths)
- *Missing data/bias:* not applicable in the conventional censoring sense at this data cutoff; FDA statistical reviewer flagged that the sponsor's sample-size justification for the CR/CRh interim analysis lacked a documented basis ("major deficiency of the design") despite the pre-specified 12% exclusion threshold being met
- *Regulatory:* sponsor requested accelerated approval (21 CFR 314.510) based on CR/CRh, DOR, and transfusion-independence conversion as a claimed advantage over available therapy; FDA instead granted regular approval under 21 CFR 314.105, treating durable CR/CRh with transfusion independence as substantial evidence of effectiveness in its own right rather than as an accelerated-approval surrogate — an FDA-defined Efficacy Analysis Population (restricted to confirmed relapsed/refractory FLT3-mutation-positive patients receiving the recommended dose) narrower than the sponsor's RAS/ITT populations; no FDA advisory committee meeting was held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ADMIRAL (2215-CL-0301): Phase 3, randomized (2:1), open-label, multicenter, multinational trial of gilteritinib 120 mg orally once daily vs. investigator-preselected salvage chemotherapy (high-intensity: FLAG-IDA or MEC; low-intensity: LDAC or azacitidine) in adults with relapsed/refractory FLT3-mutated AML after first-line therapy; 429 screened, 255 randomized at the time of the first interim analysis (169 gilteritinib, 86 chemotherapy), out of a total planned enrollment of ~369 (246 gilteritinib, 123 chemotherapy, assuming 10% dropout)
- Randomization (via IRT) was stratified by response to first-line AML therapy (relapse within/after 6 months of allogeneic HSCT, primary refractory without HSCT, relapse within/after 6 months of CRc without HSCT) and by preselected salvage chemotherapy intensity (high vs. low)
- The trial used analysis-set definitions specific to each planned look: the Response Analysis Set (RAS — patients ≥112 days past first dose/randomization, used only for the first interim CR/CRh analysis), the Intention-to-Treat Set (ITT, for OS/EFS), the Full Analysis Set (FAS, all randomized patients with centrally-confirmed FLT3 mutation), and the Safety Analysis Set (as-treated)
- This NDA's approval was based entirely on the pre-specified first interim analysis: a two-sided 95% exact confidence interval around the CR/CRh rate in the 142-patient RAS gilteritinib arm, with the lower bound required to exceed a 12% historical-control benchmark; the sponsor remained blinded to the randomized chemotherapy-arm data throughout, so the interim look assessed the gilteritinib arm's single-arm response rate only, not a between-arm comparison
- Sample size: 141 gilteritinib-arm subjects were calculated (by the FDA reviewer, who noted the sponsor provided no documented sample-size justification) to give 80% power to exclude a CR/CRh rate below 12% via the exact 95% CI, assuming a true rate of 21%; separately, the trial's overall design was powered on the co-primary OS endpoint — 258 total deaths for 90% power to detect HR=0.65 (median OS 7.7 vs. 5.0 months) at one-sided alpha=0.0245 — with OS and the key secondary EFS/CR endpoints to be assessed only at the not-yet-reached second interim and final analyses
- Results supporting this approval (data cutoff Aug 4, 2017): sponsor's RAS analysis showed CR/CRh 21.8% (95% CI 15.3-29.5%) in 142 gilteritinib-arm patients, exceeding the 12% benchmark; FDA's independently adjudicated, dose/diagnostic-restricted Efficacy Analysis Population (n=138) showed CR/CRh 21.0% (95% CI 14.5-28.8%), median duration of response 4.6 months, and transfusion-independence conversion in 31.1% of previously transfusion-dependent patients; supportive single-arm Study 2215-CL-0101 (n=49, FDA-adjudicated) showed CR/CRh 18.4% (95% CI 8.8-32.0%), median DOR 12.3 months
- OS, EFS, and CR (the trial's actual co-primary/key-secondary comparative endpoints) had not yet been formally tested at the time of this approval — those results were reported later (final OS analysis: HR 0.64, median OS 9.3 vs. 5.6 months) and supported a 2019 labeling supplement, not this original approval
- FDA's statistical review explicitly recommended regular, not accelerated, approval: "It is concluded that the durable CR or CRh associated with transfusion-independence induced by gilteritinib constitutes substantial evidence of effectiveness" — despite the sponsor having filed under an accelerated-approval framework — with postmarketing studies required to characterize long-term safety, differentiation syndrome, and the FLT3-TKD-mutation subgroup

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/211349s000lbl.pdf

- FDA combined review package for the 2019 efficacy supplement (adds final OS/EFS data) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/211349Orig1s001.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (ADMIRAL) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02421939 (genuine sponsor Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan posted in the Documents tab)
- Protocol / SAP (sponsor-posted, genuine): SAP Final Version 4.0, dated 31-May-2022 — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/39/NCT02421939/SAP_003.pdf; Protocol — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/39/NCT02421939/Prot_002.pdf

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1902688), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31665578/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Gilteritinib%20or%20Chemotherapy%20for%20Relapsed%20or%20Refractory%20FLT3-Mutated%20AML)

**Other resources**

- Astellas has not been individually confirmed to participate in a major third-party IPD-sharing platform (Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere) for this trial; trial-specific data availability was not confirmed.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held; the approval letter states the application "was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the safety profile is acceptable for treatment of patients with relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia with a FLT3 mutation."
- Companion diagnostic: LeukoStrat CDx FLT3 Mutation Assay (Invivoscribe), cross-referenced to PMA P160040, used to select patients for ADMIRAL and required for the approved indication.
- The posted sponsor SAP is the final version (v4.0, dated 31-May-2022, reflecting the completed trial including the later OS analyses); the interim-analysis design language quoted below was carried through from the original SAP into this final version, as confirmed against the contemporaneous 2018 FDA review's description of the same interim-analysis plan.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, sponsor Statistical Analysis Plan, Study 2215-CL-0301, SAP Final Version 4.0, 31-May-2022, §3.2]* — "Two interim analyses by an Independent Data Monitoring Committee (IDMC) will be conducted. The first interim analysis is planned when approximately 141 subjects are randomized into ASP2215 arm and at least 112 days (4 treatment cycles) post first dose or randomization (for subjects who received no study drug). The first interim analysis will be performed to evaluate the efficacy endpoint of CR/CRh rate and the study conduct will not be impacted by the result of the CR/CRh rate."

*[verbatim, same source, §4]* — "The overall 0.025 one-sided type I error rate is allocated by 0.0005 and 0.0245 (corresponding to 0.001 and 0.049 for two-sided type I error rates) for the two co-primary efficacy endpoints of CR/CRh and OS, respectively. The type I error (alpha) in the first interim analysis is a nominal alpha which is arbitrarily selected for acknowledgement of the CR/CRh rate evaluation at the first interim and will not be recycled in the second interim analysis and final analysis... A sample size of 141 subjects provides 80% power to exclude a CR/CRh rate of 12% using the two-sided 95% exact CI when the CR/CRh rate of ASP2215 is assumed to be 21%."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review and Evaluation, NDA 211349, Reference ID 4353716, §1.2]* — "The review team recommends regular approval of gilteritinib under 21 CFR 314.105 for the indication 'Treatment of adult patients who have relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with a FMS-like tyrosine kinase 3 (FLT3) mutation as detected by an FDA-approved test' using a dose of 120 mg daily. The recommendation is based on the finding of durable complete remission with complete or partial hematopoietic recovery (CR/CRh) and conversion to transfusion independence in Study 2215-CL-0301 (NCT02421939)."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "The design included an interim single-arm analysis of CR/CRh to be performed when approximately 141 patients on the gilteritinib arm had completed at least 112 days (4 cycles) or discontinued (RAS population). There was no basis provided for the sample size, which is a major deficiency of the design, but the Applicant prespecified that the lower limit of the confidence interval was required to exclude 12%."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "It is concluded that the durable CR or CRh associated with transfusion-independence induced by gilteritinib constitutes substantial evidence of effectiveness."

*[verbatim, same source, §18 Division Director review]* — "Priority review was requested. Accelerated approval was also requested as the Sponsor claimed that gilteritinib demonstrates an advantage over the available therapies, as measured by complete remission (CR)/complete remission with incomplete hematopoietic recovery (CRh), the duration of CR/CRh (DOR), and the rate of conversion from transfusion dependence to transfusion independence. The request for accelerated approval relied upon one phase 3 trial (the Admiral trial-NCT02421939)..."

This is a distinctive regulatory pattern in the census: a sponsor requested accelerated approval (Subpart H) for an interim single-arm response-rate result nested inside an ongoing randomized Phase 3 trial, and FDA instead granted regular/full approval on that same CR/CRh evidence — treating durable remission plus transfusion-independence conversion as direct substantial evidence of effectiveness rather than as a surrogate needing post-marketing confirmation. The trial's actual comparative co-primary endpoint (OS) and hierarchically-gated secondaries (EFS, CR) were not tested until later data cuts that supported a subsequent labeling supplement, not this original November 2018 approval.

### 91. calaspargase pegol-mknl (Asparlas) — BLA 761102

**Sponsor:** Servier Pharmaceuticals LLC (BLA developed by Baxalta, Inc./Shire; Shire's oncology portfolio, including calaspargase pegol, was acquired by Servier in October 2018, shortly before approval)

**Indication approved:** Component of a multi-agent chemotherapeutic regimen for the treatment of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) in pediatric and young adult patients age 1 month to 21 years

**Approval date:** December 20, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** DFCI Protocol 11-001 (also referred to in FDA review as DFCI 11-011), NCT01574274; supportive: COG AALL07P4

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled (pegaspargase comparator), stratified by disease type/age/initial risk group, historical-control comparison against a prior institutional protocol (DFCI 05-001) for safety/MRD monitoring, dose-comparison arm within the supportive trial (AALL07P4 tested calaspargase pegol 2100 IU/m2 vs. 2500 IU/m2 vs. pegaspargase 2500 IU/m2)
- *Endpoints:* pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic activity-threshold endpoint (serum asparaginase activity [SAA] ≥0.10 IU/mL post-induction-dose; nadir serum asparaginase activity [NSAA] ≥0.10 IU/mL at steady state during post-induction therapy — same construct as Erwinaze's PK/PD threshold endpoint), safety/toxicity rate vs. historical control, end-induction minimal residual disease (MRD) and complete remission (CR) rate, event-free survival (EFS)/disease-free survival (DFS)/overall survival (OS) (all descriptive/secondary, not powered)
- *Primary analysis:* one-sided Fisher's exact test (NSAA responder-proportion comparability, powered analysis), population pharmacokinetic (PPK) modeling with empirical Bayes estimation used to impute NSAA for the majority of subjects whose observed PK data were later ruled unusable, exact (Clopper-Pearson-type) binomial confidence intervals for toxicity/MRD monitoring rates, generalized estimating equations (GEE) and random-effects mixed models (longitudinal asparaginase-activity comparison, exploratory)
- *Missing data/bias:* study drug's own primary PK dataset was declared unreliable by FDA's bioanalytical inspection team (>90% of observed asparaginase-activity measurements from Study DFCI 11-001 could not be used), forcing near-total reliance on PPK-model-imputed NSAA values pooled across the pivotal and supportive trials to support the effectiveness determination
- *Regulatory:* explicit statistical-reviewer statement that the pivotal trial "was not designed to assess efficacy with respect to clinical endpoints...either in the sense of superiority or in the sense of non-inferiority to pegasparagase," and that "there is no agreed upon margin from which to formally conclude similarity" for MRD/CR; approval rested on the Office of Clinical Pharmacology's assessment of NSAA as an established surrogate for efficacy rather than on a formal comparative efficacy hypothesis test; no FDA advisory committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- DFCI 11-001: Phase 2, randomized (1:1), open-label, multicenter trial (Dana-Farber Cancer Institute ALL Consortium, US and Canada) comparing IV calaspargase pegol 2,500 IU/m2 (single induction dose, then every 3 weeks for 30 weeks post-induction) against IV pegaspargase (Oncaspar) 2,500 IU/m2 (single induction dose, then every 2 weeks for 30 weeks post-induction), layered onto the DFCI Consortium's standard multi-agent chemotherapy backbone, in newly-diagnosed pediatric/young-adult patients (age 1-22 years) with ALL or lymphoblastic lymphoma; planned enrollment 240 (actual 239: 119 calaspargase pegol, 120 pegaspargase), enrolled 2012-2016
- Randomization was stratified by disease type, age, and initial NCI risk-group classification (standard-risk <10 years, high-risk <10 years, high-risk ≥10 years [by definition], lymphoblastic lymphoma)
- The trial was explicitly designed and powered as a safety/feasibility and PK-comparability study, not a clinical-efficacy trial: the sponsor's own SAP states the study was designed to determine whether calaspargase pegol's every-3-week regimen provides NSAA comparable to pegaspargase's every-2-week regimen, with comparable safety and "no erosion" in EFS/OS — explicitly not to demonstrate superiority or non-inferiority on those clinical endpoints
- Primary feasibility/PK endpoint: proportion of patients with at least one NSAA measurement ≥0.10 IU/mL (the asparaginase activity level considered to produce complete asparagine depletion) during post-induction therapy, compared between arms by a one-sided Fisher's exact test (alpha=0.025); powered (89% power, assuming a 99% pegaspargase-arm response rate) to detect a 10-percentage-point reduction with calaspargase pegol, using 112 evaluable patients per arm
- Safety and MRD "endpoints" were not compared between randomized arms directly but were each monitored against a fixed historical-control rate drawn from a prior DFCI Consortium protocol (05-001): overall asparaginase-related toxicity rate 27% and end-induction high-MRD rate 12.5%; a Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) reviewed rates at each of three planned interim looks (roughly every 6 months) plus a final analysis, using pre-specified exact-binomial stopping boundaries (e.g., stop and refer to the DMC if ≥38/112, 34%, of patients on either arm experienced asparaginase-related toxicity)
- Efficacy endpoints (Day-32 MRD status, CR rate, EFS, DFS, OS) were collected and reported descriptively on the full analysis set but were never intended as formally powered comparisons
- Supportive trial COG AALL07P4 (also randomized, multi-agent chemotherapy backbone) tested calaspargase pegol at two dose levels (2,100 and 2,500 IU/m2) against pegaspargase 2,500 IU/m2 during the induction phase only; it was suspended in Dec 2010 after the 2,100 IU/m2 calaspargase pegol arm showed a statistically significant excess of Day-29 MRD-positivity, crossing a pre-specified safety-monitoring boundary — informing DFCI 11-001's decision to test only the 2,500 IU/m2 dose
- Critical review complication: during BLA review, FDA's bioanalytical-method inspection found that the assay validation used to measure asparaginase activity in Study DFCI 11-001 was unreliable, invalidating over 90% of the trial's own observed PK data (leaving only 11 evaluable calaspargase pegol and 16 evaluable pegaspargase patients for induction-phase PK analysis, and 5 and 3 evaluable patients respectively for post-induction NSAA at 30 weeks)
- To salvage the effectiveness assessment, FDA's clinical pharmacology review team re-fit a population PK (PPK) model using the 124 subjects (pooled across DFCI 11-001 and AALL07P4) with at least one valid PK observation, then used empirical Bayes estimation to impute each subject's expected NSAA at steady state under the proposed 2,500 IU/m2 Q3W regimen; the imputed data indicated more than 99% (123/124) of subjects would maintain NSAA ≥0.10 IU/mL from Week 6 to Week 30 — this imputed-NSAA comparability, not the trial's own (largely invalidated) observed PK dataset, became the primary basis for the effectiveness finding
- Result: combined observed-plus-imputed data supported comparable steady-state NSAA between calaspargase pegol Q3W and pegaspargase Q2W at the same 2,500 IU/m2 dose; safety profiles were reported as comparable and acceptable between arms; MRD-negativity and CR rates appeared similar between arms but with "no agreed upon margin from which to formally conclude similarity," per the FDA statistical reviewer

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/761102s000lbl.pdf

**Other resources**
