Place, MD) with Shire and the National Cancer Institute as collaborators, rather than a conventional industry-run registration trial — a materially different sponsorship structure from most entries in this census.
- No trial-specific IPD/dataset access (Vivli, YODA Project, Project Data Sphere) was identified for DFCI 11-001; general participation in these platforms was not individually confirmed for Servier/Shire for this trial.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this application.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, sponsor Protocol/SAP, DFCI Protocol 11-001, Version Date 02/24/2016, §16.1]* — "A total of 240 patients will be enrolled on this trial to evaluate the primary endpoint. We plan to enroll 120 patients on each arm to have 112 patients on each arm evaluable for the monitoring of asparaginase toxicity in Consolidation I, CNS and Consolidation II phases of treatment and the pharmacokinetic secondary endpoint. The randomization will be stratified into four groups based on disease type, age and risk group classification."

*[verbatim, same source, §16.1.1.1]* — "The safety analysis will not be a comparison of randomized arms, but each arm will be monitored by comparing toxicity rates to the historical control arm of IV Oncaspar on 05-001. We will monitor the proportion of patients experiencing asparaginase-related toxicity to ensure that this rate does not significantly differ from the 27%, observed on 05-001 in either arm. Assuming we have approximately 30 patients enrolled on each arm (60 total)...at the time of the first interim analysis, if 12 or more of the 30 (40%; exact two-sided 80% CI: 28%-53%) patients experience asparaginase-related toxicity, we would consider this unacceptable, as the expected rate of 27% is excluded from the lower bound of the exact one-sided binomial 90% confidence interval."

*[verbatim, same source, §16.1.2.1]* — "The feasibility of administering IV SC-PEG at a dose of 2500 IU/m2 every 3-weeks will be assessed by calculating the proportion patients who achieve a nadir serum asparaginase activity (NSAA) level ≥0.10 IU/mL (considered therapeutic) at any post-induction time point in each arm...we will have 89% power to detect a 10% reduction in the proportion of patients who have at least 1 NSAA level ≥ 0.10 IU/mL during the post-induction asparaginase consolidation, using a one-sided Fisher exact test at the 0.025 significance level. If there is no difference...we will consider the administration of every 3-week IV SC-PEG feasible."

*[verbatim, same source, §16.1.1.2]* — "COG Protocol AALL07P4 tested SC-PEG asparaginase during the induction phase...The study was suspended on December 22, 2010 based on a higher rate of Day 29 end-induction MRD-positivity (MRD+) for patients treated with SC-PEG 2100 IU/m²/dose compared with SC-PEG 2500 IU/m²/dose or Oncaspar 2500 IU/m²/dose. The difference in frequency of MRD-positivity was statistically significant and crossed pre-defined safety monitoring boundaries."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761102, Reference ID 4365594, §8.1.1]* — "DFCI 11-001 was not originally designed as a study to support a regulatory submission. The original protocol objectives were modified for this BLA application. The following study objectives are derived from the statistical analysis plan (SAP) submitted by Baxalta 6/21/16, amended 7/23/17."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.1.1 Statistical Analysis Plan]* — "As noted below, DFCI 11-001 was designed to assess the safety and feasibility of IV administration of calaspargase pegol 2500 IU/m2. It was not designed to assess efficacy with respect to clinical endpoints such as: Minimal residual disease; Complete remission; Overall survival; Disease free survival; Event free survival."

*[verbatim, same source, Statistical Reviewer Comment]* — "While the statistical analysis plan discusses how these endpoints are to be analyzed, there are no prespecified criteria from which a determination of efficacy is to be made. For example, there were no agreed-up[on] margins on which non-inferiority between IV calaspargase pegol 2500 IU/m2 and pegasparagase can be determined. Furthermore, the amount of statistical information for time-to-event endpoints is insufficient for making statements about OS, DFS, and EFS."

*[verbatim, same source, §7 Sources of Clinical Data]* — "During the review process, the PK bioanalysis inspection team reported that the bioanalytical validation method used in Study DFCI 11-001 to determine the asparaginase activity is not reliable, which leads to >90% observed PK data can not be used for PK analysis...Because the low evaluable observed PK data is lack of power for any decision making, the review team utilized an imputation method based on the population PK modeling and simulation, and combined it with the limited observed PK data to support an approval of the proposed dosing regimen of CalPEG Q3W."

*[verbatim, same source, §6.1.1]* — "The evidence of effectiveness comes from the combination of observed valid PK data in the pivotal Study DFCI 11-001 and the estimated NSAA data based on a population PK model validated for both Study DFCI11-001 and Study AALL 07P4...PPK estimated data indicated comparable level of NSAA at steady state between CalPEG Q3W and Oncaspar Q2W at the same dose of 2500 U/m2."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.4-8.5 Statistical Issues / Conclusions]* — "It was not designed to assess efficacy with respect to clinical endpoints (MRD, CR, EFS, DFS, OS) either in the sense of superiority or in the sense of non-inferiority to pegasparagase...there is no agreed upon margin from which to formally conclude similarity...This review team defers to the Clinical Pharmacology reviewers' assessment of NSAA as an established surrogate for efficacy. There are no clinical data that signal erosion of efficacy, and there is no unexpected or unacceptable safety issue. Approval is recommended." — signed Kunthel By, PhD (Primary Statistical Reviewer) and Yuan-Li Shen, DrPH (Statistical Team Leader).

This is a genuine example of an approval built almost entirely on a PK/PD activity-threshold comparability argument rather than a powered clinical-efficacy hypothesis test — and, unusually among this census, one where the trial's own primary PK dataset failed bioanalytical validation mid-review and had to be substituted with a population-PK-model imputation pooling data across the pivotal and a separate supportive trial, a rescue strategy FDA's statistical reviewer both relied on and explicitly flagged as leaving the underlying clinical endpoints (MRD, CR, EFS, OS) without any pre-specified basis for a similarity conclusion.

---

### 92. tagraxofusp-erzs (Elzonris) — BLA 761116

**Sponsor:** Stemline Therapeutics, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm (BPDCN) in adults and in pediatric patients 2 years and older

**Approval date:** December 21, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** STML-401-0114 ("Study 0114"), NCT02113982

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial, multi-stage (4-stage) design with a data-driven carve-out of a later-enrolled cohort (Stage 3) formally designated as the pivotal cohort by FDA agreement mid-trial, rare-disease population (no biomarker enrichment — BPDCN itself is the defining diagnosis), dose-focused analysis restricting the efficacy population to patients treated at the intended 12 µg/kg/day dose
- *Endpoints:* complete response rate (CR+CRc, primary, investigator-assessed with FDA clinical-reviewer adjudication), duration of CR+CRc (key secondary), objective response rate (ORR, secondary), bone marrow complete response (BMCR) rate and duration (secondary), overall survival and progression-free survival reported descriptively only (explicitly not treated as interpretable given the single-arm design)
- *Primary analysis:* exact (Clopper-Pearson) binomial confidence interval around CR+CRc rate compared descriptively against a 10% reference/historical-control benchmark, Kaplan-Meier estimation for duration-of-response and OS
- *Multiplicity:* not applicable — no comparative or multi-endpoint hypothesis test was pre-specified
- *Missing data/bias:* not applicable in the conventional censoring sense; FDA reviewer explicitly stated PFS and OS "is not interpretable" in a single-arm study and reported them for context only; efficacy results reported are FDA's clinical-reviewer-adjudicated response determinations (sponsor concurred), not the sponsor's own unadjudicated assessment
- *Regulatory:* regular approval (not accelerated) granted on a single-arm CR+CRc rate in a rare, previously-untreatable, uniformly fatal malignancy, following a Type B meeting (Dec 20, 2016) at which FDA and the sponsor agreed to define a specific later-enrolled patient cohort (Stage 3, first-line BPDCN patients enrolled on/after Oct 26, 2016) as the pivotal analysis population for the primary efficacy claim

**Trial design & endpoints**

- STML-401-0114 (Study 0114): multi-stage, nonrandomized, open-label, multicenter trial of tagraxofusp (SL-401) in BPDCN and AML patients, divided into 4 stages — Stage 1 (dose-finding, MTD determination, first-line or R/R BPDCN/AML), Stage 2 (efficacy/safety characterization at MTD in BPDCN and AML), Stage 3 (first-line BPDCN only, defined as the pivotal cohort), Stage 4 (first-line or R/R BPDCN); initiated June 2014, ongoing at time of submission
- Following a Type B meeting with FDA on December 20, 2016, first-line BPDCN patients enrolled on or after October 26, 2016 were designated a separate, pivotal patient cohort (Stage 3) for the primary statistical analysis; data cutoff for the primary efficacy analysis was September 25, 2017, with all surviving Stage 3 patients having at least 6 months of follow-up
- Primary efficacy population: modified intent-to-treat (mITT) — all patients eligible per screening criteria who received at least one dose of tagraxofusp; the efficacy analysis was further restricted to patients dosed at 12 µg/kg/day (the sponsor's intended commercial dose), and analyzed separately for first-line vs. relapsed/refractory patients despite concurrent enrollment
- Primary endpoint: complete response rate (CR + CR with residual skin abnormality not indicative of active disease [CRc]) by investigator assessment, in first-line BPDCN patients in Stage 3, with duration of CR+CRc as a key secondary endpoint in this cohort; secondary endpoints included CR+CRc rate/duration in Stages 1-2 and pooled across Stages 1-3, ORR (CR+CRc+CRi+PR) and duration, bone marrow complete response (BMCR) rate/duration, proportion proceeding to stem cell transplant, and pooled PFS/OS (descriptive only)
- Sample-size logic: for Stage 3, the sample size was based on the lower bound of a two-sided 95% CI for the CR rate ruling out a 10% reference/historical-control rate; assuming a true CR rate of at least 60%, a minimum of 10 first-line BPDCN patients provided ≥90% power for the primary efficacy assessment (13 were ultimately enrolled in Stage 3)
- Results (FDA clinical-reviewer-adjudicated, sponsor-concurred): first-line BPDCN — Stage 3 CR+CRc rate 53.8% (95% CI 25.1-80.8%, n=7/13), all-stages-pooled CR+CRc rate 72.4% (95% CI 52.8-87.3%, n=21/29 at 12 µg/kg/day), median duration of CR+CRc not estimable in either Stage 3 or all-stages; relapsed/refractory BPDCN — CR+CRc rate 13.3% (95% CI 1.7-40.5%, n=2/15), durations of the two responses 3.7 and 13.9 months; PFS/OS were reported descriptively (e.g., R/R median OS 7.1 months, 95% CI 4.1-11.9) but the statistical reviewer stated these "is not interpretable" given the single-arm design
- FDA's statistical review concluded "No major statistical issue was identified in the review," deferring the ultimate risk-benefit judgment to the clinical review team; the product carries a boxed warning for Capillary Leak Syndrome

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2018/761116Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/761116s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Cindy Gao, Ph.D.; Reference ID 4351575) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/761116Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (Study 0114) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02113982 (no protocol/SAP posted in the Documents tab)
- Pivotal publication: Pemmaraju N, Lane AA, Sweet KL, et al. "Tagraxofusp in Blastic Plasmacytoid Dendritic-Cell Neoplasm." *N Engl J Med.* 2019;380(17):1628-1637. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1815105), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31018069/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Tagraxofusp%20in%20Blastic%20Plasmacytoid%20Dendritic-Cell%20Neoplasm)

**Other resources**

- No IPD-sharing platform participation (Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere) was identified for Stemline Therapeutics; trial-specific data availability was not confirmed.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this application; BPDCN's rarity (no approved therapy existed at the time) and the trial's design were instead worked out directly with FDA via a Type B meeting (Dec 20, 2016) that defined the pivotal Stage 3 cohort.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, BLA 761116, Reference ID 4351575, Background]* — "The pivotal study STML-401-0114 (i.e., Study 0114) is a multi-stage, nonrandomized, open-label, multicenter study of SL-401 in BPDCN and AML patients divided into 4 stages... The primary efficacy endpoint is CR rate (CR + CRc) using the Investigator's response determinations, in first-line BPDCN patients in Stage 3, accompanied by an evaluation of the durability of response, as a key secondary endpoint in this cohort."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "The sample size for the pivotal cohort Stage 3 was determined based on the lower bound of a 2-sided 95% confidence interval of the CR rate to rule out the reference rate of 10%. Assuming a CR rate of at least 60%, a minimal sample size of 10 first-line BPDCN patients provided at least 90% power for the primary efficacy assessment. For the timing of the analysis, in accordance with agreement with FDA in the Type B meeting on 20 Dec 2016, first-line BPDCN patients enrolled on or after 26 Oct 2016 were considered as a separate, pivotal patient cohort for statistical analysis (i.e, Stage 3)."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "The primary analysis population for analysis of efficacy is modified intent-to-treatment (mITT) population, defined as all patients who were eligible based on the screening criteria and who received at least 1 dose of SL-401. For analysis methods, response rate with 95% CI based on Clopper-Pearson Exact method would be presented with 10% as the benchmark for comparison. Time-to-event endpoints would be analyzed with Kaplan–Meier method."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "Note that the result of PFS and OS is not reported here because the study is a single arm study and therefore PFS and OS is not interpretable... During the review, the FDA clinical reviewer Dr. Jen adjudicated the response and the sponsor agreed with Dr. Jen's adjudication results. Therefore, the efficacy results in the following are based on Dr. Jen's adjudication results."

*[verbatim, same source, Summary]* — "No major statistical issue was identified in the review. The judgment of whether a favorable result of SL-401 treatment is demonstrated will be based on the risk-benefit assessment for patients with BPDCN and is deferred to clinical decision."

### 93. erdafitinib (Balversa) — NDA 212018

**Sponsor:** Janssen Biotech, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma with susceptible FGFR3 or FGFR2 genetic alterations that has progressed during or following at least one line of prior platinum-containing chemotherapy, including within 12 months of neoadjuvant or adjuvant platinum-containing chemotherapy, selected for therapy based on an FDA-approved companion diagnostic

**Approval date:** April 12, 2019

**Pivotal trial:** BLC2001 (Study 42756493BLC2001), NCT02365597

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial (final/pivotal Regimen 3 cohort), preceded by an internal randomized dose-comparison stage (Regimen 1 vs. Regimen 2) resolved via a Data Review Committee interim analysis before a third, pharmacodynamically-guided dose regimen was selected for further single-arm enrollment — an adaptive seamless dose-selection-into-expansion design, biomarker-selected population (susceptible FGFR3/FGFR2 genetic alterations by clinical trial assay), companion diagnostic co-approval (therascreen FGFR RGQ RT-PCR Kit, PMA P180043 reviewed concurrently by CDRH)
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR, primary, confirmed CR+PR per RECIST v1.1, Blinded Independent Review Committee [BIRC] assessment for the primary/final analyses per a pre-specified rule), duration of response (DOR, secondary), progression-free survival and overall survival (secondary, explicitly described by FDA as uninterpretable without a comparator arm)
- *Primary analysis:* response-rate confidence-interval exclusion rule against a pre-specified 25% threshold, using a normal-approximation (Wald) 95% two-sided CI for a single proportion rather than an exact/Clopper-Pearson interval, Kaplan-Meier estimation (DOR, PFS, OS, descriptive only)
- *Missing data/bias:* investigator-vs-BIRC assessment-source switching rule specified prospectively (BIRC used as primary/final analysis only if the investigator-assessed ORR's 95% CI lower bound exceeded 25%, else investigator assessment stands as primary with BIRC supportive)
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval (21 CFR 314.510) based on ORR and duration of response in a single-arm trial; reviewer-documented narrowing of the sponsor's proposed analysis population — FDA restricted the primary efficacy population to the 87 chemo-relapsed/refractory patients (excluding 12 cisplatin-ineligible patients from the sponsor's n=99 Regimen 3 population) as the basis for the labeled indication; companion diagnostic co-approval; postmarketing requirement for a randomized Phase 3 confirmatory trial (BLC3001, vs. vinflunine/docetaxel/pembrolizumab); no FDA advisory committee meeting was held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- BLC2001 (42756493BLC2001): Phase 2, multicenter, open-label, non-randomized (after an initial randomized dose-comparison stage) trial of erdafitinib (JNJ-42756493) in patients with metastatic or surgically unresectable urothelial carcinoma harboring specified FGFR3/FGFR2 genetic alterations; patients were initially randomized to Regimen 1 (10 mg intermittent, 7 days on/7 off) or Regimen 2 (6 mg continuous daily), stratified by ECOG PS, hemoglobin, FGFR alteration type, pretreatment status, and disease distribution
- At Interim Analysis 1 (IA1), the Data Review Committee (DRC) selected the continuous schedule (Regimen 2) for continued development, then — based on additional safety/efficacy analyses and PK/PD modeling — recommended Regimen 3 (8 mg once daily with a pharmacodynamically-guided increase to 9 mg based on Cycle 1 Day 14-17 serum phosphate and tolerance), implemented via Protocol Amendment 3 (August 9, 2016); all subsequent enrollment used Regimen 3, with a planned ~100 patients (≥80 chemo-relapsed/refractory)
- Primary endpoint: confirmed best objective response (BOR = CR or PR per RECIST v1.1); response was assessed by investigators for all patients and by a Blinded Independent Review Committee (BIRC) for Regimen 3 patients; per the SAP, if the lower bound of the investigator-assessed ORR's 95% two-sided CI exceeded 25%, the BIRC assessment would be used for the primary/final analyses (investigator assessment then supportive) — otherwise investigator assessment stood as primary
- Primary analysis population: the Applicant defined it as all Regimen 3 patients treated with ≥1 dose (n=99). FDA and the Applicant agreed the primary efficacy population supporting the labeled indication would be the chemo-relapsed/refractory subset (n=87), excluding 12 cisplatin-ineligible patients
- Sample size: assuming a true ORR of 42%, 88 chemo-relapsed/refractory patients gave ≥85% (SAP: "at least 80%") power for the lower bound of the 95% two-sided CI (normal approximation to the binomial) to exceed the pre-specified 25% threshold; secondary endpoints (DOR, PFS, OS) analyzed via Kaplan-Meier, DOR assessed only in responders
- Result (data cutoff March 15, 2018, n=87 primary efficacy population): confirmed ORR (BIRC) 32.2% (95% CI 22.4-42.0%; CR 2.3%, PR 29.9%), median DOR 5.4 months (95% CI 4.2-6.9); by alteration subtype, ORR was 40.6% (FGFR3 point mutation, n=64), 11.1% (FGFR3 fusion, n=18), and 0% (FGFR2 fusion, n=6) — FDA noted the FGFR2 companion-diagnostic test kit was not itself analytically/clinically validated by FDA at the time
- FDA's statistical reviewer stated plainly that "In single arm trials, FDA does not use inferential procedures to evaluate trial results. Instead, the efficacy evaluation is based on the magnitude of response rate and adequate duration of response," and separately that time-to-event endpoints (PFS, OS) are "uninterpretable without a comparator arm"

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2019/212018Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2019/212018s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (combined Summary/Clinical/Statistical Review; Statistical Reviewer Wei Zhang, Statistical Team Leader Lijun Zhang; Reference ID 4418085) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/212018Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (BLC2001) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02365597
- Protocol / SAP (sponsor-posted, genuine): SAP Amendment 1, dated September 29, 2016 — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/97/NCT02365597/SAP_001.pdf; Protocol — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/97/NCT02365597/Prot_000.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Loriot Y, Necchi A, Park SH, et al. "Erdafitinib in Locally Advanced or Metastatic Urothelial Carcinoma." *N Engl J Med.* 2019;381:338-348. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1817323), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31340094/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Erdafitinib%20in%20Locally%20Advanced%20or%20Metastatic%20Urothelial%20Carcinoma)

**Other resources**

- Janssen (Johnson & Johnson) participates in the Yale Open Data Access (YODA) Project for IPD sharing; trial-specific availability for BLC2001 was not individually confirmed.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held; the Multi-Discipline Review states this NDA "was not presented to an advisory committee because the benefit-risk profile demonstrated for erdafitinib is clearly favorable for its proposed use. No controversial issues were identified that would necessitate an advisory committee meeting."
- Companion diagnostic: therascreen FGFR RGQ RT-PCR Kit (QIAGEN), PMA P180043, reviewed concurrently by CDRH; tumor samples from 69 of the 87 primary-efficacy-population patients were retrospectively tested with this assay.
- Postmarketing requirement: Submit the final report/analysis demonstrating clinical benefit from clinical trial BLC3001, "A Phase 3 Study of Erdafitinib Compared With Vinflunine or Docetaxel or Pembrolizumab in Subjects with Advanced Urothelial Cancer and Selected FGFR Gene Aberrations" (final protocol submission 10/2017; trial completion 04/2022; final report submission 10/2022).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, sponsor Statistical Analysis Plan – Amendment 1, Study 42756493BLC2001, dated 29 September 2016, §1.1.1]* — "The primary objective of the study is to evaluate the objective response (complete response [CR]+ partial response [PR]) rate of the selected dose regimen in subjects with metastatic or surgically unresectable urothelial cancers that harbor specific FGFR genomic alterations."

*[verbatim, same source, §1.2 Trial Design]* — "Based on analysis of data up to Interim Analysis 1 (IA1), the Data Review Committee (DRC) decided to terminate further enrollment to the intermittent schedule and select the continuous schedule with a starting dose of 8 mg and possible up-titration to 9 mg (Regimen 3) for further enrollment... When approximately 88 subjects have been treated in Regimen 3, if less than 80 subjects are chemo-refractory, then enrollment of chemo-naïve subjects in Regimen 3 will be stopped but enrollment of chemo-refractory subjects will continue until at least 80 chemo-refractory subjects are treated in Regimen 3."

*[verbatim, same source, §1.4 Sample Size Justification]* — "Enrollment of at least 80 chemo-refractory subjects will provide at least 80% power to reject the null hypothesis within the chemo-refractory subgroup under the above assumptions."

*[verbatim, same source, §5.1.1 Level of Significance]* — "Statistical inference on the primary endpoint will be tested at 0.025 one-sided level. Efficacy for the secondary endpoint will be tested at one-sided 0.025 level for the chemo-refractory subgroup, after the primary endpoint has been declared significant."

*[verbatim, same source, §5.2.2 Analysis Method]* — "The objective response rate is defined as the proportion of responders over the PE population. The response rate and its 95% 2-sided confidence interval will be calculated using normal approximation to the binomial distribution. The null hypothesis will be rejected if the low bound of 95% 2-sided confidence interval of the response rate is above 25%."

*[verbatim, same source, §5.1.3]* — "If response is assessed by an IRRC, the IRRC assessment of response will be used for the primary and final analyses, and the response assessed by the investigators will be used for supportive analyses."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 212018, Reference ID 4418085, Statistical Review §Statistical Analysis Plan]* — "The primary hypothesis was that the selected dose regimen had an objective response rate > 25% in patients with metastatic or surgically unresectable urothelial cancer harboring select FGFR alterations... If the true response rate is 42%, 88 patients would provide at least 85% power to obtain the lower bound of 95% 2-sided confidence interval above 25%."

*[verbatim, same source, Analysis Population]* — "The Applicant defined the primary analysis population as all patients who were treated with at least 1 dose of study drug in Regimen 3 (n=99). Reviewer Comments: The Applicant and FDA agreed that the patients with chemo-relapsed/refractory disease would be the primary efficacy population in Regimen 3 (n=87) and would form the basis for the labeled indication population. Patients ineligible for cisplatin-based therapy (n=12) were excluded from the FDA primary efficacy analysis."

*[verbatim, same source, Study Endpoints]* — "Reviewer Comments: In single arm trials, FDA does not use inferential procedures to evaluate trial results. Instead, the efficacy evaluation is based on the magnitude of response rate and adequate duration of response. Additionally, we note that time-to-event endpoints are uninterpretable without a comparator arm."

*[verbatim, FDA Approval Letter, NDA 212018, Reference ID 4418725]* — "This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification of clinical benefit in confirmatory trials."... "3561-1 Submit the analysis, and datasets with the final report demonstrating clinical benefit of erdafitinib in patients with locally advanced and metastatic urothelial carcinoma with susceptible FGFR 3 or FGFR 2 genetic alterations from clinical trial BLC3001..."

This is a genuine example where the sponsor's own SAP specifies a decision rule blending an inferential framing (a "null hypothesis" tied to a 25% response-rate threshold, tested via a normal-approximation rather than exact binomial CI) with FDA's stated policy of not treating single-arm response-rate results as formal hypothesis tests at all — and where FDA's review narrowed the sponsor's own proposed 99-patient analysis population by 12 patients before accepting it as the basis for labeling, a smaller-scale analogue to the population-redefinition dynamic seen in lorlatinib's review.

### 94. alpelisib (Piqray) — NDA 212526

**Sponsor:** Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation

**Indication approved:** In combination with fulvestrant, for the treatment of postmenopausal women, and men, with hormone receptor (HR)-positive, HER2-negative, PIK3CA-mutated, advanced or metastatic breast cancer as detected by an FDA-approved test, following progression on or after an endocrine-based regimen

**Approval date:** May 24, 2019

**Pivotal trial:** SOLAR-1 (Study CBYL719C2301/BYL719C2301), NCT02437318

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, international multicenter Phase III trial, biomarker-selected primary cohort (PIK3CA-mutant tumor tissue, confirmed by a Novartis-designated central laboratory) with a parallel PIK3CA non-mutant cohort analyzed as an independent proof-of-concept objective, stratified by presence of lung/liver metastases and prior CDK4/6-inhibitor use
- *Endpoints:* progression-free survival (PFS, primary, local-radiology assessment per RECIST v1.1, with BICR/central-review PFS as a supportive sensitivity analysis) in the PIK3CA-mutant cohort, overall survival (OS, key secondary, PIK3CA-mutant cohort), objective response rate (ORR)/clinical benefit rate (CBR, other secondary/exploratory), patient-reported outcomes/HRQoL (EORTC QLQ-C30, EQ-5D-5L, BPI-SF — exploratory, not multiplicity-controlled)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, stratified Cox proportional-hazards model, Kaplan-Meier estimation, Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test (ORR/CBR), Bayesian posterior-probability decision rule combined with a hazard-ratio threshold (HR≤0.60 and posterior probability of HR<1 ≥90%) used as a proof-of-concept gate for testing PFS in the PIK3CA non-mutant cohort
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (PFS→OS) within the PIK3CA-mutant cohort at a one-sided 2.0% level; a Bonferroni-style split of the overall one-sided 2.5% type I error between the PIK3CA-mutant cohort (2.0%) and the independently-analyzed PIK3CA non-mutant cohort (0.5%); no multiplicity adjustment for ORR/CBR or PRO endpoints (reported as nominal p-values only)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design, Haybittle-Peto boundary for the 3-look PFS analysis (futility look at ~97 events/40% information, interim efficacy look at ~185 events/76% information, final at ~243 events), separate Lan-DeMets O'Brien-Fleming alpha-spending function (independent of the PFS Haybittle-Peto boundary) for the 3-look OS analysis, Data Monitoring Committee
- *Missing data/bias:* standard right-censoring at last evaluable tumor assessment per a pre-specified event/censoring-rule table; primary PFS analysis used an ITT approach that ignores new antineoplastic therapy for censoring purposes (ongoing tumor assessments still counted), with a pre-specified sensitivity analysis instead censoring at last adequate assessment before new antineoplastic therapy start; ~50%-sample audit of local-radiology PFS by BIRC as a supportive robustness check
- *Regulatory:* companion diagnostic co-approval (therascreen PIK3CA RGQ PCR Kit, Qiagen Manchester Ltd., reviewed concurrently by CDRH); no FDA advisory committee meeting was held; reviewer-documented disagreement with sponsor's promotional characterization of secondary/exploratory ORR, CBR, and subgroup results as showing "marked" or "substantial" improvement, given the absence of any surviving alpha for those endpoints after the immature first OS interim analysis; OS final analysis deferred to a postmarketing commitment

**Trial design & endpoints**

- SOLAR-1 (CBYL719C2301): Phase III, randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, international, multicenter trial of alpelisib 300 mg orally QD (or placebo) plus fulvestrant 500 mg IM (days 1 and 15 of cycle 1, then day 1 of each subsequent 28-day cycle) in men and postmenopausal women with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer that had relapsed/progressed on or after an aromatase inhibitor; 275 sites, 33 countries; 572 subjects enrolled and centrally assigned via IRT to a PIK3CA-mutant cohort (n=341) or PIK3CA non-mutant cohort (n=231) based on central tumor-tissue testing, then randomized 1:1 within each cohort
- Randomization within each cohort was stratified by presence of lung and/or liver metastases (yes/no) and previous treatment with any CDK4/6 inhibitor (yes/no); patients and investigators were blinded to both treatment assignment and cohort/mutation status; crossover from placebo to alpelisib was not permitted
- Primary endpoint: PFS by local (investigator) radiological assessment (RECIST v1.1) in the PIK3CA-mutant cohort, tested via a stratified log-rank test at a one-sided 2.0% significance level (of an overall one-sided 2.5% type I error, split Bonferroni-style with 0.5% reserved for the non-mutant cohort's PFS proof-of-concept test); sample size targeted ~84% power to detect HR=0.60 (median PFS 11.7 vs. 7.0 months) with 243 PFS events
- Key secondary endpoint: OS in the PIK3CA-mutant cohort, tested only if PFS was statistically significant (hierarchical/fixed-sequence gate), via stratified log-rank test at a one-sided 2.0% level with a separate 3-look Lan-DeMets O'Brien-Fleming alpha-spending function (independent of the PFS Haybittle-Peto boundary); OS was powered at 72% for HR=0.67 with 178 target deaths, first interim analysis co-timed with the final PFS analysis, second interim planned at 151 deaths (85% information)
- PFS in the PIK3CA non-mutant cohort was a secondary/proof-of-concept objective (downgraded from a co-primary objective by Protocol/SAP Amendment 1, 09-Mar-2016) gated by a Bayesian decision rule (estimated stratified HR≤0.60 and posterior probability of true HR<1 ≥90%); only if both criteria were met would a formal one-sided 0.5%-level stratified log-rank test of PFS (and, contingent on that, OS) be performed in that cohort
- Other secondary/exploratory endpoints: ORR and clinical benefit rate (CBR) compared via Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by randomization factors (nominal p-values only, no alpha allocated); time to definitive ECOG PS deterioration and time to 10% deterioration in global health status/QoL (Kaplan-Meier); PRO subscale changes from baseline analyzed via linear mixed-effects models — none of these had multiplicity control
- The SAP was amended 4 times during the trial (per FDA's review); Amendment 1 (09-Mar-2016) downgraded the non-mutant cohort's PFS analysis from primary to secondary/proof-of-concept and reallocated the resulting alpha (2.0% mutant / 0.5% non-mutant) to preserve the overall one-sided 2.5% type I error; FDA's reviewer stated none of the four amendments "impacted the integrity of the trial or the interpretation of the results"
- Result: PFS HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.50-0.85; one-sided stratified log-rank p=0.00065, crossing the final-analysis Haybittle-Peto boundary; median PFS 11.0 vs. 5.7 months) in the PIK3CA-mutant cohort — the basis for regular approval. At the first (and, at approval, only completed) OS interim analysis (92 deaths, 51.7% information fraction), HR was 0.73 (95% CI 0.48-1.10, one-sided p=0.06), not crossing the pre-specified O'Brien-Fleming stopping boundary (one-sided p≤0.00121) — OS was immature and not statistically significant, so no alpha remained for any further secondary-endpoint testing. In the PIK3CA non-mutant cohort, the proof-of-concept criteria were not met (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.58-1.25, 79.4% posterior probability of HR<1), so no formal hypothesis test of that cohort's PFS was performed
- FDA's review explicitly reports p-values at the conventional two-sided level throughout (noting the applicant's submitted Assessment Aid materials use one-sided values, requiring a ×2 conversion for direct comparison) and separately pushed back on sponsor labeling/promotional language describing the (statistically unsupported) ORR/CBR and subgroup findings as "marked" or "substantial" improvements

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2019/212526Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2019/212526s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (includes Statistical Review; Statistical Reviewer Laura L. Fernandes, PhD; Reference ID 4437533) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/212526Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (SOLAR-1) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02437318 (genuine sponsor Protocol and SAP posted in the Documents tab)
- Protocol / SAP (sponsor-posted, genuine): Protocol — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/18/NCT02437318/Prot_002.pdf; SAP, Amendment 6, dated 08-May-2023 — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/18/NCT02437318/SAP_003.pdf (note: this posted SAP version postdates the May 2019 approval — it reflects a later amendment, e.g. covering final-OS/COVID-19 sensitivity-analysis language — but its core primary-PFS hypothesis/testing-hierarchy text is consistent with, and elaborates on, what FDA's 2019 statistical review describes for the approval)
- Pivotal publication: André F, Ciruelos E, Rubovszky G, et al., for the SOLAR-1 Study Group. "Alpelisib for PIK3CA-Mutated, Hormone Receptor-Positive Advanced Breast Cancer." *N Engl J Med.* 2019;380:1929-1940. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1813904), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31091374/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Alpelisib%20for%20PIK3CA-Mutated%2C%20Hormone%20Receptor-Positive%20Advanced%20Breast%20Cancer)

**Other resources**

- Novartis participates in data-sharing arrangements (including the Vivli platform and a direct Novartis clinical-trial-data-request process); trial-specific IPD availability for SOLAR-1 was not individually confirmed beyond the genuine protocol/SAP already posted to ClinicalTrials.gov.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this application (FDA's review states plainly: "No advisory committee discussion or consultations external to the FDA were deemed necessary").
- Companion diagnostic: therascreen PIK3CA RGQ PCR Kit (Qiagen Manchester Ltd.), approved via a concurrently reviewed PMA to identify PIK3CA-mutant tumor tissue for patient selection.
- Final OS analysis for SOLAR-1 was deferred to Postmarketing Commitment #1, with a final report expected per FDA's review in 08/2022.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, sponsor Statistical Analysis Plan, Study CBYL719C2301/BYL719C2301 (SOLAR-1), Amendment 6, 08-May-2023, §3.8.1.2]* — "The overall Type I error for the trial is one-sided 2.5%. The primary efficacy analysis of PFS based on the population of patients with PIK3CA mutant status will be performed at a one-sided 2.0% level of significance. A secondary efficacy analysis of PFS based on the population of patients with PIK3CA non-mutant status will be performed at a one-sided 0.5% level of significance... This approach guarantees the protection of the overall type I error at 2.5% (based on a Bonferroni adjustment). The primary efficacy analysis will be the comparison of PFS between the two treatment arms using a stratified log-rank test at a one-sided 2.0% level of significance for the PIK3CA mutant cohort."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.8.2.2]* — "PFS treatment effect in this cohort will be considered to be clinically relevant via a Bayesian decision rule if: The estimated HR (stratified according to presence of lung and/or liver metastasis and previous treatment with CDK4/6 inhibitor) ≤ 0.60 and The posterior probability (HR < 1) ≥ 90%... If both these criteria are met then the comparison of PFS between the two treatment arms in this cohort using a stratified log-rank test at a one-sided 0.5% level of significance, will be made."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.8.2.1 (OS, mutant cohort)]* — "The final OS analysis will not be performed at the time point of the final PFS analysis in the PIK3CA mutant cohort, but after additional follow-up. Therefore, a three-look group sequential design is considered for OS... The type I error probability will be controlled by using a separate Lan-DeMets (O'Brien-Fleming) alpha spending function independent of the Haybittle-Peto boundary used for the primary efficacy analysis of PFS at a 2.0% level of significance. This guarantees the protection of the overall type I error (α = 2.5%) across all hypotheses."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 212526, Reference ID 4437533, §8 Statistical Review]* — "The primary efficacy analysis was the comparison of the distribution of PFS between the two treatment groups using a stratified log-rank test at a one-sided 2.0% level of significance in the PIK3CA mutant cohort. A group sequential design using a Haybittle-Peto boundary was used to address multiplicity and control the overall type-I error rate. A maximum of three analyses was planned; a futility interim analysis after observing approximately 97 PFS events (corresponding to a 40% information fraction), an interim efficacy analysis after approximately 185 PFS events (76% information fraction), and a final PFS analysis after approximately 243 events."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "The statistical plan was amended four times during the study to reflect changes in protocol design... Amendment 1 (09-Mar-2016) changed the efficacy analysis for the PIK3CA non-mutant cohort from a primary objective to a secondary, proof-of-concept objective. Consequently, the primary and key secondary objectives of the study focused on the comparison of PFS and OS between treatment groups for subjects in the PIK3CA mutant cohort... an alpha of 0.5% was assigned to the non-mutant cohort comparison, while an alpha of 2% was assigned to the mutant cohort comparison to control the overall type I error... None of the implemented changes impacted the integrity of the trial or the interpretation of the results."

*[verbatim, same source, Integrated Review of Effectiveness]* — "Given that the null hypothesis was rejected for the PFS endpoint (i.e. the primary endpoint was met), all alpha allocation remained to test OS at the first interim analysis of OS. The first interim OS analysis was not statistically significant, and hence there is no alpha allocation remaining for testing additional secondary endpoint hypotheses... As a result, p-values reported for all other secondary efficacy endpoints, such as ORR, are nominal p-values, and no efficacy claims should be made based upon other endpoints."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "The FDA disagrees with the promotional language regarding 'marked improvements' in ORR and CBR. While the ORR in patients with measurable disease was approximately doubled in the alpelisib plus fulvestrant arm relative to the control arm, the ORR was modest in both arms, and complete responses were rare and did not differ between arms... No alpha has been allocated to these subgroup analyses, and therefore all results should be considered exploratory."

*[verbatim, same source, §9]* — "No advisory committee discussion or consultations external to the FDA were deemed necessary."

SOLAR-1 is a case where the genuine sponsor SAP (posted to ClinicalTrials.gov, though in a 2023-dated later amendment) and FDA's contemporaneous 2019 statistical review independently corroborate the same core design: a Bonferroni-style alpha split between two biomarker-defined cohorts analyzed as functionally separate trials, a Bayesian posterior-probability gate (rather than a conventional hypothesis test) deciding whether the non-mutant cohort's PFS was even formally tested, and an explicit FDA rebuke of sponsor promotional language for secondary endpoints left without any surviving alpha once the first OS interim analysis fell short.

### 95. polatuzumab vedotin-piiq (Polivy) — BLA 761121

**Sponsor:** Genentech, Inc.

**Indication approved:** In combination with bendamustine and a rituximab product, for treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), not otherwise specified, after at least two prior therapies (accelerated approval)

**Approval date:** June 10, 2019

**Pivotal trial:** Study GO29365 (randomized Phase Ib/II cohort, Arms C/D), NCT02257567

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled, small-sample Phase Ib/II trial used as the pivotal registration study (not a dedicated Phase 3), multi-histology/multi-regimen master protocol (also enrolling R/R follicular lymphoma and obinutuzumab-containing arms not part of this indication), stratified permuted-block randomization, single-arm supportive cohort (Arm G, lyophilized formulation) analyzed separately without a concurrent comparator
- *Endpoints:* complete response (CR) rate at primary response assessment (6-8 weeks after Cycle 6 Day 1 or last dose) by PET-CT per modified Lugano 2014 criteria, assessed by an independent review committee (IRC) — primary; objective response rate (ORR) and best overall response (BOR) — additional; duration of response (DOR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS) — additional, explicitly not usable for a definitive treatment-effect conclusion at this data maturity
- *Primary analysis:* exact (Clopper-Pearson) binomial confidence interval per arm, difference in CR rates estimated via normal-approximation CI with the Miettinen-Nurminen method applied by the FDA reviewer (no method pre-specified by the sponsor for the rate-difference CI), Bayesian analysis with uniform priors conducted by the FDA reviewer to further characterize the treatment effect and its posterior probability of exceeding several effect-size thresholds, Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified by duration of response to prior therapy) for descriptive PFS/OS hazard ratios, Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Multiplicity:* not applicable — no statistical hypothesis test was pre-specified for the CR-rate difference between arms, and no multiplicity adjustment was pre-specified for additional (secondary) outcomes; the sponsor's protocol/SAP separately specified an exploratory Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test adjusted for randomization stratification factors, which the FDA statistical reviewer's account of the analysis does not describe using as the basis for any efficacy claim
- *Missing data/bias:* FDA reviewer explicitly characterized PFS and OS estimation as "unreliable due to high uncertainty" given the limited number of events (24/32 PFS events, 23/28 OS events in the P+BR/BR arms) and stated "no definitive conclusions can be drawn based on these data"
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval (21 CFR 601.41) based on CR rate as a surrogate reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit, from a randomized but non-registrational-scale Phase Ib/II trial (n=40 per arm) rather than a dedicated confirmatory Phase 3; two alternative randomized confirmatory postmarketing requirements (PMR 3630-1, PMR 3630-2), either of which could satisfy the accelerated-approval requirement; no FDA advisory committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study GO29365: "A Phase Ib/II study evaluating the safety, tolerability, and anti-tumor activity of polatuzumab vedotin in combination with rituximab (R) or obinutuzumab (G) plus bendamustine (B) in relapsed or refractory follicular or diffuse large B-cell lymphoma" — a multi-cohort master protocol; the pivotal evidence for this approval is the randomized DLBCL cohort (Arms C/D): polatuzumab vedotin + bendamustine + rituximab (P+BR, n=40) vs. bendamustine + rituximab alone (BR, n=40), 1:1 randomization via stratified permuted blocks, in adults with R/R DLBCL who had received ≥1 prior therapy and were not candidates for hematopoietic stem cell transplant; enrollment ran Oct 2014-Sept 2016 (Arm G/lyophilized-formulation cohort added later, data cutoff Nov 15, 2018), primary analysis data cutoff April 30, 2018
- Randomization was stratified by duration of response (DOR) to prior anti-lymphoma therapy (<12 vs. ≥12 months), the same factor later used as the covariate in the descriptive Cox model for PFS/OS
- Primary endpoint: CR rate at primary response assessment (6-8 weeks after Cycle 6 Day 1 or last dose) by PET-CT scan per modified Lugano 2014 criteria, assessed by an independent review committee; sample size (n=40/arm) was explicitly not based on a pre-specified hypothesis test but on the width of the 95% exact Clopper-Pearson CI achievable for the CR-rate estimate at various assumed true rates
- Additional (non-hypothesis-tested) endpoints: ORR, BOR, DOR, PFS, OS — all per IRC; a separate single-arm cohort of 32 patients (part of "Arm G," lyophilized formulation) was analyzed descriptively for CR rate against a one-sided exact binomial test (H0: CR≤15% vs. Ha: CR>15%, alpha=2.5%, 92% power for a true rate of 40%), a materially different statistical structure from the randomized comparison supporting the DLBCL indication itself
- Result: CR rate 40% (95% CI 25-57%) in P+BR vs. 18% (95% CI 7-33%) in BR alone; estimated CR-rate difference 22% (95% CI 3-41%, Miettinen-Nurminen); FDA's Bayesian analysis (uniform priors) estimated the treatment-effect magnitude at 21% (95% credible interval 2-40%), with a 99% posterior probability the true effect exceeds 0, 88% probability it exceeds 10%, and 56% probability it exceeds 20%; ORR 45% vs. 18%, BOR (CR+PR) 62% vs. 25%; PFS HR 0.29 (95% CI 0.16-0.52, median 7.6 vs. 2.4 months) and OS HR 0.42 (95% CI 0.24-0.75, median 12.4 vs. 4.7 months) were reported but explicitly flagged by FDA as unreliable given event counts, with no claim on either endpoint permitted in labeling
- FDA's statistical review concluded benefit was demonstrated on the pre-specified major efficacy outcome (CR rate) with internal consistency from BOR/DOR, but noted "residual uncertainty about the treatment effect exists, given the small number of patients randomized," recommending confirmation via a PFS or OS outcome in "an adequately designed randomized trial" — realized as the two accelerated-approval postmarketing requirements (GO39942/POLARIX, a randomized front-line R-CHP vs. R-CHOP trial with PFS as primary endpoint; and MO40598, a randomized R-GemOx ± polatuzumab trial with OS as primary endpoint)

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter (BLA Accelerated Approval, Reference ID 4446006) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2019/761121Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2019/761121s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID 4440120; Statistical Reviewer Alexei C. Ionan, Team Leader Jingjing Ye) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/761121Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Clinical/Medical Review and Summary Review also on file at the same Drugs@FDA docket (761121Orig1s000MedR.pdf, 761121Orig1s000SumR.pdf)
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (Study GO29365) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02257567
- Protocol / SAP (sponsor-posted, genuine, combined document, Protocol GO29365 Version 8, dated 2020-03-23 — a later protocol version than the one supporting the 2018 BLA submission, but describing the same randomized DLBCL design/analysis) — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/67/NCT02257567/Prot_SAP_000.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Sehn LH, Herrera AF, Flowers CR, et al. "Polatuzumab Vedotin in Relapsed or Refractory Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma." *J Clin Oncol.* 2020;38(2):155-165. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.19.00172), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31693429/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Polatuzumab%20Vedotin%20in%20Relapsed%20or%20Refractory%20Diffuse%20Large%20B-Cell%20Lymphoma)

**Other resources**

- Genentech/Roche participates in the Vivli data-sharing platform; trial-specific IPD availability for Study GO29365 was not individually confirmed.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held; the approval letter states this was "because evaluation of the data did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues in the intended population."
- Postmarketing requirements: PMR 3630-1 (Study GO39942/POLARIX, randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial of polatuzumab vedotin + R-CHP vs. R-CHOP in previously untreated DLBCL, PFS primary) and PMR 3630-2 (Study MO40598, randomized trial of polatuzumab vedotin + R-GemOx vs. R-GemOx alone in R/R large B-cell lymphoma, OS primary) — either could satisfy the accelerated-approval verification requirement.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, BLA 761121, Reference ID 4440120, §3.2.1]* — "This review focuses on efficacy in patients randomized to polatuzumab vedotin in combination with rituximab and bendamustine (P+BR; N=40) or rituximab and bendamustine (BR; N=40) in relapsed or refractory (R/R) diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL)... To evaluate the efficacy of the combination of polatuzumab vedotin plus BR compared with BR alone in patients with R/R DLBCL as measured by positron emission tomography (PET)-defined complete response (CR) rate using Modified Lugano 2014 Response Criteria... at the time of primary response assessment (6-8 weeks after Cycle 6 Day 1 or last dose of study medication) per Independent Review Committee (IRC)."

*[verbatim, same source, Sample Size Determination]* — "Eighty patients were planned to be enrolled and randomized 1:1 to BR and P+BR groups. The sample size was not calculated based on a pre-specified hypothesis. With 40 patients per group, 95% exact Clopper-Pearson confidence intervals (CI) for estimation of the true CR rate were calculated, given various assumptions on response rates."

*[verbatim, same source, Analysis of Major Outcome]* — "The response rates were estimated with the percentage of patients with response per study group, along with the corresponding Clopper-Pearson exact 95% confidence intervals. The 95% confidence interval for the CR rate difference between P+BR and BR groups was estimated based on a normal approximation. A specific method for estimating rate difference was not specified in the protocol – Miettinen-Nurminen method is used in this review... No statistical hypothesis was pre-specified for testing CR rate difference between study groups. Bayesian analyses with uniform priors were conducted by the Reviewer to further characterize the treatment effect."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.2.4.1]* — "Bayesian analyses have been conducted to characterize the magnitude and uncertainty of the treatment effect. The estimated magnitude of the treatment effect, as measured by the difference in complete response rates between patients treated with P+BR and BR, is 21% (95% Credible Interval: 2, 40)... The probability that the treatment effect (measured as difference in effect) exceeds 0 is 99%. The probability that the treatment effect exceeds 10% is 88%. The probability that the treatment effect exceeds 20% is 56%."

*[verbatim, same source, PFS/OS]* — "Progression-free survival estimation based on the data in Study GO29365 is unreliable due to high uncertainty with 24 and 32 events in P+BR and BR groups, respectively... No definitive conclusions can be drawn based on these data."... "Overall survival estimation based on the data in Study GO29365 is unreliable due to high uncertainty with 23 and 28 events in P+BR and BR groups, respectively... No definitive conclusions can be drawn based on these data."

*[verbatim, same source, §5.3-5.4 Conclusions and Labeling Recommendations]* — "Benefit of polatuzumab vedotin in combination with rituximab and bendamustine for the treatment of patients with R/R DLBCL has been demonstrated based on the randomized pivotal Study GO29365. However, some residual uncertainty about the treatment effect exists, given the small number of patients randomized and limited number of events in the PFS and OS... Treatment effect observed in the pivotal Study GO29365 should be confirmed with a progression-free or overall survival outcome in an adequately designed randomized trial."... "Efficacy labeling should be primarily based on pre-specified major outcome... labeling should not allow for any claims on time-to-event secondary endpoints due to no multiple testing plan and limited number of events."

*[verbatim, sponsor Protocol/SAP, Study GO29365, Version 8 (dated 2020-03-23), Primary Efficacy Endpoint section]* — "CR at Primary Response Assessment (6-8 weeks after Cycle 6, Day 1 or last dose of study drug) as measured by PET-CT scan and as determined by an IRC will be used as the primary efficacy endpoint... The CR rate, defined as the percentage of patients with CR, will be estimated and the corresponding Clopper-Pearson exact 95% CI will be constructed for each treatment arm. The difference in CR rates between the combination of polatuzumab vedotin+BR and BR randomized arms will be estimated along with the corresponding 95% CI on the basis of normal approximation to the binomial distribution. An exploratory comparison of CR rates for the BR-containing regimens will be conducted using the Cochran Mantel Haenszel χ2 test adjusted for randomization stratification factors."

*[verbatim, FDA Approval Letter, BLA 761121, Reference ID 4446006]* — "Products approved under the accelerated approval regulations, 21 CFR 601.41, require further adequate and well-controlled clinical trials to verify and describe clinical benefit... Verification of clinical benefit through either PMR 3630-1 or PMR 3630-2 would be adequate to fulfill the accelerated approval requirement."... "PMR 3630-1 Complete Study GO39942, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial that evaluates polatuzumab vedotin-piiq in combination with R-CHP... versus R-CHOP... The primary endpoint would be progression-free survival."... "PMR 3630-2 Complete Study MO40598, a randomized clinical trial that evaluates polatuzumab vedotin-piiq in combination with rituximab, gemcitabine, and oxaliplatin (R-GemOx) versus R-GemOx alone... The primary endpoint would be overall survival."

Note on multiplicity discrepancy: the sponsor's protocol/SAP (as posted, a later version) specifies an exploratory CMH-test comparison of CR rates adjusted for randomization stratification factors, but FDA's statistical review states plainly that "no statistical hypothesis was pre-specified for testing CR rate difference between study groups" and that the reviewer's own Clopper-Pearson/Miettinen-Nurminen/Bayesian analyses — not a sponsor-executed hypothesis test — formed the actual basis of the efficacy characterization; this is a case where the review's stated analytic basis differs from what the currently-posted protocol document specifies, most plausibly because the posted SAP version postdates the original BLA submission's operative analysis plan. This is also a rare example of an FDA statistical reviewer conducting and reporting an original Bayesian analysis (uniform priors, posterior probability of exceeding several effect thresholds) as a formal part of the review, rather than the sponsor's frequentist analysis alone.

### 96. selinexor (Xpovio) — NDA 212306

**Sponsor:** Karyopharm Therapeutics Inc.

**Indication approved:** In combination with dexamethasone, for adult patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM) who have received at least four prior therapies and whose disease is refractory to at least two proteasome inhibitors, at least two immunomodulatory agents, and an anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody — approved under accelerated approval based on response rate

**Approval date:** July 3, 2019

**Pivotal trial:** STORM Part 2 (Study KCP-330-012), NCT02336815

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H/21 CFR 314.510, dose/schedule carried forward from a non-randomized Phase 1 trial (KCP-330-001) with no dedicated dose-ranging study at the to-be-marketed dose/schedule, indication narrowed mid-review from a broader triple-class-refractory population to a narrower quad-refractory subpopulation via a post-ODAC major amendment
- *Endpoints:* overall response rate (ORR, primary, IRC-assessed per IMWG 2016 criteria — sCR/CR/VGPR/PR), duration of response (DOR, key secondary), progression-free survival, overall survival, time-to-progression, clinical benefit rate, disease control rate, quality of life (FACT-MM) (all secondary/descriptive — not formally testable in a single-arm design)
- *Primary analysis:* two-sided exact (Clopper-Pearson-type) 95% confidence interval around ORR in the mITT population, compared descriptively to a pre-specified minimal threshold of 10% (design-stage one-sided exact binomial test of H0: ORR≤10% vs. H1: ORR≥20%, one-sided α=0.025, 90% power, n=122)
- *Multiplicity:* not applicable — single formal primary endpoint, no comparative or multi-endpoint hypothesis test
- *Missing data/bias:* not applicable in the conventional sense (no censoring/crossover comparator issue); FDA reviewer explicitly noted the modest magnitude (ORR 25.4%) and limited durability (median DOR 4.4 months) of the response, and could not exclude that the substantial background activity of high-dose dexamethasone alone (historically 10-27% ORR in RRMM) confounds attribution of effect to selinexor, since selinexor monotherapy in the Phase 1 trial (KCP-330-001) produced only 1 response in 56 patients
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval (Subpart H) based on ORR as a surrogate reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit; FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) met February 26, 2019 and voted 8-5 in favor of delaying approval until results of the randomized confirmatory Phase 3 trial (KCP-330-023/BOSTON) were available; following a post-ODAC meeting with FDA (March 11, 2019), the Applicant submitted a major amendment narrowing the indication and extending the user-fee goal date, after which the narrower indication was approved; a randomized Phase 3 trial with a survival signal in a different population (KCP-330-008, selinexor vs. physician's choice in AML) was cited by FDA as a toxicity concern at the ODAC meeting

**Trial design & endpoints**

- STORM Part 2 (KCP-330-012): open-label, single-arm, multicenter Phase 2b trial of oral selinexor 80 mg plus low-dose dexamethasone 20 mg, both dosed twice weekly (four-week cycles), in patients with "penta-refractory" multiple myeloma previously treated with lenalidomide, pomalidomide, bortezomib, carfilzomib, and daratumumab, and refractory to glucocorticoids, an immunomodulatory agent (IMiD), a proteasome inhibitor (PI), and the anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody daratumumab; 122 patients enrolled and treated in Part 2 (first patient enrolled May 26, 2015; last patient March 23, 2018; data cutoff April 24, 2018)
- Primary endpoint: ORR (proportion achieving confirmed PR or better — PR/VGPR/CR/sCR per IMWG 2016 criteria, two consecutive confirmatory readings required) assessed by a blinded Independent Review Committee (IRC), in the modified intent-to-treat (mITT) population (patients meeting all eligibility criteria, or granted a Sponsor waiver, who received ≥1 dose)
- Design-stage sample-size logic: n=122 for Part 2 was estimated to yield 90% power to detect an ORR of ≥20% against a minimal threshold of 10%, using a one-sided exact test at α=0.025; the executed primary analysis reported to FDA instead used a two-sided exact 95% CI for the ORR rate compared descriptively to the 10% threshold (no interim analysis was planned)
- Key secondary endpoints: DOR, clinical benefit rate (CBR), disease control rate (DCR), PFS, OS, time-to-progression (TTP), and quality of life via the FACT-MM instrument — all summarized descriptively, consistent with the single-arm design
- Results: ORR 25.4% (95% CI 18.0-34.1%; 31/122 responders: 2 sCR, 6 VGPR, 23 PR), median DOR 4.4 months (range 0.8-9.0). FDA's reviewer commented: "An ORR of 25.4% is a modest response rate for this population and the duration of response was limited at only 4.4 months. It is unclear whether this represents a substantially meaningful clinical benefit in this population considering the degree of toxicity associated with treatment with selinexor."
- The indication approved is narrower than the trial's full Part 2 population: following the post-ODAC meeting, the Applicant amended the proposed indication from all 122 patients (triple-class refractory, ≥3 prior therapies) to a subpopulation of 83 patients with ≥4 prior therapies who were refractory to ≥2 PIs, ≥2 IMiDs, and an anti-CD38 mAb
- Safety: essentially all patients (100%) had a treatment-emergent adverse event; 60.2% had a serious adverse event; 91.1% required dose modification; 26.8% discontinued due to a TEAE — cited at ODAC as a significant toxicity signal, compounded by the fact that the phase 1 dose-finding trial (KCP-330-001) did not test doses of selinexor below 45 mg/m² in combination with the proposed dexamethasone regimen

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2019/212306Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2019/212306s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 4457008, NDA 212306) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/212306Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (STORM) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02336815 (Study Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan Version 2.0 both posted in the Documents tab)
- Protocol / SAP — Study Protocol: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/15/NCT02336815/Prot_000.pdf; Statistical Analysis Plan v2.0: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/15/NCT02336815/SAP_001.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Chari A, Vogl DT, Gavriatopoulou M, et al. "Oral Selinexor-Dexamethasone for Triple-Class Refractory Multiple Myeloma." *N Engl J Med.* 2019;381:727-738. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1903455), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31433920/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Oral%20Selinexor-Dexamethasone%20for%20Triple-Class%20Refractory%20Multiple%20Myeloma)

**Other resources**

- Karyopharm's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for STORM; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for this trial.
- FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting held February 26, 2019; voting question was whether approval should be delayed until results of the randomized confirmatory Phase 3 trial (BOSTON, KCP-330-023) were available — vote was 8 Yes (delay), 5 No.
- Postmarketing requirement: verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial (the label states continued approval for this indication may be contingent on this); the ongoing randomized BOSTON trial (selinexor + bortezomib + dexamethasone vs. bortezomib + dexamethasone) served this role for a related indication approved in 2020.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, STORM Statistical Analysis Plan v2.0, §1.2.1 Primary Objectives]* — "Evaluate the efficacy (overall response rate [ORR] based on IRC assessment) for treatment with selinexor 80 mg plus low-dose dexamethasone (20 mg) (Sd) twice weekly (four-week cycles) in patients with penta-refractory MM previously treated with lenalidomide, pomalidomide, bortezomib, carfilzomib, and daratumumab; and refractory to prior treatment with glucocorticoids, an IMiD, a PI, and the anti-CD38 mAb daratumumab. ORR will include patients who experience PR, very good partial response (VGPR), CR, or sCR, based on IMWG response criteria (Kumar 2016). The ORR for patients with penta-refractory MM in Part 2 will be compared to a minimal threshold level of 10%."

*[verbatim, same source, §1.5 Interim Analysis]* — "No interim analysis is planned for this study."

*[verbatim, same source, §1.6 Database Lock]* — "The primary analysis will be performed after all patients have completed the Cycle 2 MM Assessments, and will include a formal snapshot of database and analyses of efficacy, safety, and PK data. A clinical study report (CSR) will be prepared after the primary analysis... The final analysis will be performed at the end of the study after all patients have completed the 12-month follow-up period."

*[verbatim, same source, §2.1 General Analysis Methods]* — "This is a single-arm, open-label study. All summary statistics will be computed and displayed among the corresponding analysis population, and by each scheduled assessment time point whenever applicable... For time-to-event variables, the Kaplan-Meier method will be used for descriptive summaries."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 212306, Reference ID 4457008, Statistical Analysis Plan section]* — "It was estimated that a sample size of 122 patients for Part 2 would yield 90% power to detect an ORR of ≥20% against a minimal threshold of 10%, using a one-sided test with α=0.025. The mITT population was defined as patients in Part 2 who met all eligibility criteria (or received a waiver to participate) and received at least one dose of selinexor."

*[verbatim, same source, Efficacy Results — Primary Endpoint]* — "The ORR was assessed by an IRC and results were compared to a minimal threshold of 10%. The analysis used a 2-sided, exact 95% confidence interval (CI), calculated for the rate of ORR among the mITT population... The ORR was 25.4% (95% CI: 18%, 34.1%), and the median DOR was 4.4 months (range 0.8 to 9.0 months)."

*[verbatim, same source, Reviewer Comment]* — "An ORR of 25.4% is a modest response rate for this population and the duration of response was limited at only 4.4 months. It is unclear whether this represents a substantially meaningful clinical benefit in this population considering the degree of toxicity associated with treatment with selinexor."

*[verbatim, same source, §8 Advisory Committee Meeting]* — "Single Arm Trial of a Combination: STORM was a single arm trial evaluating the combination of selinexor and dexamethasone. Given that historical studies have shown response rates of 10-27% to high-dose dexamethasone for RRMM and selinexor did not demonstrate single agent activity in RRMM in the phase 1 trial KCP-330-001, it is difficult to isolate the treatment effect of selinexor... The voting question was 'Should the approval of selinexor be delayed until results of the randomized phase 3 trial, KCP-330-023 (BOSTON), are available?' The final vote was 8 votes Yes, 5 votes No."

Note: the SAP's own primary-analysis text (§4.1.2, "Primary Analysis of ORR") could not be reliably extracted verbatim — that page range of the posted SAP PDF has a corrupted/non-standard font encoding in its text layer (unlike the STORM protocol and most of the SAP, which extract cleanly) — but the identical analysis method and 10% threshold are independently confirmed verbatim in the FDA Multi-Discipline Review quoted above, so no inference was needed for that content. This is a clear-cut case of an accelerated approval granted over an ODAC committee's majority vote to delay: FDA approved a narrower version of the requested indication rather than following the committee's recommendation to wait for randomized confirmatory data, and the reviewer's own commentary flags the modest, non-durable nature of the response-rate benefit supporting the surrogate endpoint.
