### 97. darolutamide (Nubeqa) — NDA 212099

**Sponsor:** Bayer HealthCare Pharmaceuticals Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of patients with non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (nmCRPC)

**Approval date:** July 30, 2019

**Pivotal trial:** ARAMIS (Study 17712, protocol BAY 1841788/17712), NCT02200614

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven trial, group-sequential design (interim OS analysis coincident with the final primary MFS analysis), Special Protocol Assessment (SPA)-agreed design that was formally amended twice before database lock to revise the target hazard ratio and event target in light of external trials' published results
- *Endpoints:* metastasis-free survival (MFS, primary, BICR-adjudicated; defined as time from randomization to confirmed metastasis or death from any cause within 32(+1) weeks of the last evaluable scan)" — distinct from PFS/rPFS already in the taxonomy), overall survival (OS, key secondary), time to pain progression, time to first symptomatic skeletal event (SSE), time to initiation of first cytotoxic chemotherapy (key secondaries)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified), Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing of key secondaries (OS → time to pain progression → time to cytotoxic chemotherapy → time to first SSE), each tested only if the prior endpoint in the sequence was significant
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design for OS and the gated secondary endpoints, rho-family alpha-spending function (parameter rho=10) implemented via the EAST software package"), Data Monitoring Committee (DMC/DSMB)
- *Missing data/bias:* standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment, two-tier blinded independent central review (BICR) structure separating a baseline-eligibility read (reader pool 1) from the on-study efficacy read that determined the primary analysis (reader pool 2), with discordance-adjudication flags between site radiologist, investigator, and central readers
- *Regulatory:* Special Protocol Assessment (SPA) agreed February 2014 and amended twice (2017, 2018) pre-database-lock to revise the target hazard ratio (0.75→0.70→0.65) and MFS event target (572→370→385) based on published results from other companies' nmCRPC trials (SPARTAN, PROSPER), not from ARAMIS's own accumulating data; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ARAMIS (Study 17712/BAY 1841788): Phase III, multinational, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of darolutamide 600 mg orally twice daily plus androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) vs. placebo plus ADT in 1,509 men with high-risk nmCRPC (PSA doubling time ≤10 months, PSA >2 ng/mL, castrate serum testosterone, no detectable metastases at baseline by independent central review)
- Randomization was centralized (IRT/IVRS, permuted blocks by center) and stratified by PSA doubling time (≤6 vs. >6 months) and use of osteoclast-targeted therapy at randomization (yes vs. no)
- Primary endpoint: metastasis-free survival (MFS) per blinded independent central review (BICR), defined as time from randomization to confirmed evidence of metastasis (new lesion on bone scan, with anatomic-imaging confirmation required for a single-region bone finding, or RECIST 1.1 soft-tissue progression excluding asymptomatic pelvic-node progression) or death from any cause occurring within 32(+1) weeks of the last evaluable scan, whichever occurred first
- Key secondary endpoints, tested hierarchically only if MFS was significant: overall survival (OS); time to pain progression (≥2-point increase from baseline on BPI-SF item 3, or initiation of opioids for pain); time to first symptomatic skeletal event (SSE: external beam radiation for skeletal symptoms, new symptomatic pathologic fracture, spinal cord compression, or tumor-related orthopedic surgery); time to initiation of first cytotoxic chemotherapy for prostate cancer
- Sample size/power: original SPA-agreed design targeted 572 MFS events (assumed HR 0.75) in ~1,500 patients; amended twice pre-database-lock — first to 370 events (target HR 0.70, Amendment 3, Nov 2017), then to the final design of 385 events (target HR 0.65, diluted to 0.71 accounting for baseline-metastasis patients, June 2018) — each time maintaining an overall two-sided alpha of 0.05 and giving ~91% power at the final analysis; 40-month accrual and a 40% dropout assumption drove the final target enrollment of ~1,500 patients (1,000 darolutamide : 500 placebo)
- No formal interim analysis was performed for the primary MFS endpoint; a single interim analysis of OS (and the gated secondary endpoints) was planned to coincide with the final MFS analysis, using a rho-family (Kim-DeMets, rho=10) alpha-spending function computed in EAST, chosen because it is slightly more conservative than an O'Brien-Fleming boundary at the first (interim) look
- Primary analysis population was the Full Analysis Set (FAS, all randomized patients per ITT, equivalent to the protocol's "ITT" population); statistical methods were a two-sided stratified log-rank test (stratified by the two randomization factors, using IRT/IVRS-recorded strata) and a stratified Cox proportional-hazards model for the hazard ratio and 95% CI, with Kaplan-Meier estimation (Greenwood's formula for CIs) for medians and landmark rates
- Result at the March-2018-cutoff (data cutoff 3 Sept 2018, 437 MFS events): stratified HR 0.413 (95% CI 0.341-0.500; two-sided stratified log-rank p<0.0001); median MFS 40.4 months (darolutamide) vs. 18.4 months (placebo); the coincident interim OS analysis (136 of 240 planned events, 56.7% information) showed HR 0.706 (95% CI 0.501-0.994, p=0.045), which did not cross the pre-specified interim efficacy boundary (alpha 0.0005), so the remaining gated secondary endpoints (pain progression, SSE, chemotherapy initiation) were reported descriptively only, per the pre-specified hierarchical gate

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2019/212099Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2019/212099Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (combined Clinical/Statistical Review, Reference ID 4469844) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/212099Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (ARAMIS) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02200614 (both protocol and SAP posted in the Documents tab)
- Protocol (v4.0/Amendment 3, includes integrated SAP framework) — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/14/NCT02200614/Prot_002.pdf
- Statistical Analysis Plan (v4.2, dated 12 Mar 2021, describing the final primary/OS analyses) — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/14/NCT02200614/SAP_003.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Fizazi K, Shore N, Tammela TL, et al., for the ARAMIS Investigators. "Darolutamide in Nonmetastatic, Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer." *N Engl J Med.* 2019;380:1235-1246. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1815671), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30763142/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Darolutamide%20in%20Nonmetastatic%2C%20Castration-Resistant%20Prostate%20Cancer)

**Other resources**

- Bayer participates in the Vivli data-sharing platform for clinical trial data requests; trial-specific individual patient data (IPD) availability for ARAMIS/NCT02200614 was not individually confirmed.
- No FDA Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held for this application — the Multi-Discipline Review states the Division did not refer it to ODAC "because darolutamide is not the first drug in this class, the safety profile is acceptable in this indication, and the clinical trial design is similar to that used previously in this class."
- The Agency separately engaged the prostate-cancer research community on MFS as an endpoint construct through two ODAC meetings on the broader nmCRPC drug-development question (not a review of this specific application), and published a 2018 draft guidance, "Nonmetastatic, Castration Resistant Prostate Cancer: Considerations for Metastasis-Free Survival Endpoint in Clinical Trials."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, ClinicalTrials.gov-posted Statistical Analysis Plan, NCT02200614, SAP v4.2, §1 Introduction]* — "Study 17712 (ARAMIS) is a multinational, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase III efficacy and safety study of darolutamide in men with high-risk non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (nmCRPC). This statistical analysis plan (SAP) describes the analyses and data presentations for final primary efficacy endpoint (metastasis-free survival) and the final overall survival analysis at the end of double-blind part when targeted number of primary endpoint events is collected."

*[verbatim, same source, §3 Study Design]* — "Approximately 1500 patients will be randomized to receive darolutamide or placebo in a 2:1 ratio in a double-blind manner. Randomization will be stratified by prostate-specific antigen doubling time (PSADT) (≤ 6 vs. > 6 months) and use of osteoclast-targeted therapy (yes vs. no)."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.1 Determination of Sample Size]* — "The assumptions used in determining the sample size for this study are as follows: Overall 2-sided type I error rate: 0.05, Assumed hazard ratio of 0.65, Accounting for 5% of the patients with baseline metastasis, diluted hazard ratio of 0.71, Randomization ratio: 2:1, Statistical power at the final analysis: 91%, Median MFS for placebo: 25 months, 385 MFS events will provide approximately 91% power to detect a statistically significant difference in MFS times, with a two-sided log-rank test with a 0.05 level of significance."

*[verbatim, same source, §6.2]* — "MFS will be compared between the treatment arms using a two-sided stratified log-rank test, stratified by PSADT (≤6 vs. >6 months) and use of osteoclast-targeted therapy (yes vs. no) at randomization. A two-sided overall alpha of 0.05 will be used for the efficacy analysis of MFS... The hazard ratio as well as its 95% confidence interval (CI) will be presented based on fitting a Cox regression model with treatment as factor and stratified by PSA doubling time (≤6 vs. >6 months) and use of osteoclast-targeted therapy (yes vs. no) at randomization."

*[verbatim, same source, §6.2.2 Analysis of secondary efficacy endpoints]* — "Secondary endpoints will be tested with the hierarchical gatekeeping procedure. The order of secondary endpoints is (1) Overall survival (OS), (2) Time to pain progression (PP), (3) Time to cytotoxic chemotherapy (CYTOC), (4) Time to first symptomatic skeletal event (SSE). Secondary endpoints are tested only if the primary endpoint MFS is significant... A rho-family spending function with parameter rho=10 will be used for OS, time to pain progression, time to cytotoxic chemotherapy and time to first SSE to determine the two stopping boundaries for efficacy at the interim and final analyses... This choice is motivated by the low likelihood to achieve a significant result for the hierarchically first secondary endpoint OS at the first test for both spending functions."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 212099, Reference ID 4469844, §3.2.2 Key regulatory history of darolutamide under IND 114769]* — "February 21, 2014: The FDA agreed to a Special Protocol Assessment (SPA) for the design of the ARAMIS trial. MFS would be the primary efficacy endpoint, and 1500 enrolled patients would be expected to provide 572 MFS events... November 9, 2017: A Type A meeting was held to discuss the revised statistical analysis plan submitted in Protocol Amendment 3. This revised plan would change the target HR from 0.75 to 0.70, require 370 MFS events instead of 572 MFS events to reach the primary endpoint, while maintaining the type 1 error rate of 0.05 (2-sided) and 90% power; and reduce the number of patients enrolled from approximately 1500 to 1300. June 28, 2018: FDA agreed to a proposed Special Protocol Assessment amendment changing the target hazard ratio for MFS from 0.75 to 0.65 and thus the targeted number of MFS events from 572 to 385 due to recently published results from SPARTAN and PROSPER that suggested that a target hazard ratio of 0.75 was too conservative."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.3 Statistical Issues]* — "There were no major statistical issues with this application... Results showed a statistically significant improvement in MFS for patients on darolutamide compared to placebo with a stratified hazard ratio of 0.413 (95% CI: 0.341, 0.500; two-sided stratified log-rank p-value <0.0001)... The stratified HR for the interim OS analysis was 0.706 (95% CI: [0.501, 0.994]; p = 0.045), and medians were not reached in either treatment arm. These results were not considered statistically significant as the p-value was greater than the pre-specified interim alpha boundary of 0.0005. Since OS was not statistically significant at its interim analysis, the remaining key secondary endpoints of time to pain progression, time to first symptomatic skeletal event, and time to initiation of cytotoxic chemotherapy could only be summarized descriptively."

This is a genuine example of a sponsor's SAP assumptions (target hazard ratio and event target) being revised twice through the SPA amendment process, in each case formally agreed with FDA before database lock and driven by externally published results from other companies' trials in the same disease setting (apalutamide/SPARTAN, enzalutamide/PROSPER) rather than by ARAMIS's own accumulating data — a softer, agency-blessed analogue to the trabectedin case elsewhere in this census, where a similar externally-motivated design change was instead flagged by FDA as a reviewable deviation.

### 98. pexidartinib (Turalio) — NDA 211810

**Sponsor:** Daiichi Sankyo, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with symptomatic tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TGCT) associated with severe morbidity or functional limitations and not amenable to improvement with surgery

**Approval date:** August 2, 2019

**Pivotal trial:** ENLIVEN (Study PLX108-10), NCT02371369

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, two-part study (Part 1 randomized/controlled, Part 2 open-label extension with placebo crossover), randomization stratified by US vs. non-US sites and by upper vs. lower extremity tumor location, REMS-restricted distribution due to hepatotoxicity risk
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR, primary — proportion achieving CR or PR at Week 25 by centrally-read MRI/RECIST 1.1), duration of response (key secondary, descriptive), range of motion (ROM), tumor volume score (TVS) response, PROMIS Physical Function Scale, Worst Stiffness NRS, BPI Worst Pain NRS/analgesic use (BPI-30) (all key secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* Fisher's exact test (two-sided, α=0.05) on the ITT population; two-sided 95% CI for the ORR difference using the Wilson method
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical ("gatekeeping") testing of key secondary endpoints, each tested only if the prior endpoint in the sequence was significant at α=0.05
- *Missing data/bias:* reviewer-documented mid-trial SAP amendment reordering the secondary-endpoint testing hierarchy (Protocol Version 8, September 11, 2017) made after a blinded review of the database — prior to unblinding — revealed substantial missingness in Week-25 patient-reported outcomes (BPI-30, PROMIS Physical Function, Worst Stiffness NRS); FDA explicitly flagged this as discouraged practice that limits interpretability of the secondary results, even though it accepted the sponsor's stated rationale
- *Regulatory:* boxed warning for hepatotoxicity and REMS-restricted distribution program (including a patient registry) recommended and implemented based on 2 cases of irreversible liver injury among 768 patients across the development program; trial was placed on partial clinical hold in October 2016 after the DMC identified two cases of potential cholestatic liver injury, after which placebo-to-pexidartinib crossover was discontinued and hepatic monitoring intensified

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ENLIVEN (PLX108-10): Phase 3, two-part, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial of pexidartinib (starting dose 400 mg/day, later reduced) vs. placebo in adults with symptomatic advanced TGCT (pigmented villonodular synovitis [PVNS] or giant cell tumor of the tendon sheath [GCT-TS]) not amenable to surgical improvement; Part 1 was the randomized 24-week placebo-controlled period (n=120, 1:1), Part 2 an open-label extension in which placebo patients could cross over to pexidartinib
- Randomization was centralized and stratified by US vs. non-US site and by upper- vs. lower-extremity tumor location
- Primary endpoint: proportion of subjects achieving a complete response (CR) or partial response (PR) at the Week 25 visit, based on centrally-read MRI scans per RECIST 1.1, analyzed in the ITT population by two-sided Fisher's exact test at α=0.05, with a Wilson-method 95% CI for the between-group difference
- Sample size: 126 ITT subjects (63 per arm) was planned to provide 90% power to detect a difference between an assumed 10% placebo ORR and 35% pexidartinib ORR at two-sided α=0.05; no interim analyses were pre-specified
- Key secondary endpoints (fixed-sequence hierarchical/gatekeeping testing, each gated on the prior endpoint reaching p<0.05): as originally specified in Protocol Version 1 (Sep 2014) the order was BPI-30 responder proportion → ORR per tumor volume score (TVS) → mean change in ROM → PROMIS Physical Function → Worst Stiffness NRS; this was revised in Protocol Version 8 (Sep 11, 2017, before database unblinding) to ROM → TVS ORR → PROMIS Physical Function → Worst Stiffness NRS → BPI-30, because a substantial fraction of Week-25 patient-reported-outcome data (BPI-30, PROMIS, Worst Stiffness) were missing
- Results: ORR at Week 25 was 38% (95% CI 26-50%) with pexidartinib vs. 0% (95% CI 0-6%) with placebo (p<0.0001); among responders, duration of response ranged from 6.9+ to 24.9+ months, with 22 of 23 responders followed ≥6 months maintaining response
- Safety: hepatotoxicity was the central safety finding — abnormal liver tests and hepatotoxicity each occurred in 3.3% of patients as reasons for permanent discontinuation; 2 of 768 patients across the full development program experienced irreversible liver injury with evidence of bile duct injury/ductopenia on biopsy; the trial was placed on a partial clinical hold in October 2016 after a DMC review of unblinded safety data identified two cases of potential cholestatic liver injury

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2019/211810Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2019/211810s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 4470487, NDA 211810) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/211810Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (ENLIVEN) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02371369 (combined Study Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan posted in the Documents tab, dated January 22, 2020)
- Protocol / SAP — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/69/NCT02371369/Prot_SAP_001.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Tap WD, Gelderblom H, Palmerini E, et al. "Pexidartinib versus placebo for advanced tenosynovial giant cell tumour (ENLIVEN): a randomised phase 3 trial." *Lancet.* 2019;394(10197):478-487. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(19)30764-0>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31229240/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Pexidartinib%20versus%20placebo%20for%20advanced%20tenosynovial%20giant%20cell%20tumour%20ENLIVEN)

**Other resources**

- Daiichi Sankyo's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for ENLIVEN; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for this trial.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this application.
- Pexidartinib is distributed only through the TURALIO REMS Program (restricted distribution, prescriber/pharmacy certification, patient registry) due to the risk of serious and potentially fatal hepatotoxicity; FDA also recommended a postmarketing study to evaluate the long-term risk of pexidartinib in patients who experience severe liver injury.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, ENLIVEN Protocol/SAP, Protocol Amendment PLX108-10 v10.0, Statistical Analyses]* — "The primary endpoint is the proportion of subjects who achieve a CR or PR at the Week 25 Visit based on centrally read MRI scans and RECIST 1.1. The proportions in the two treatment groups will be compared using Fisher's exact test (two-sided) at the alpha = 0.05 level of significance. In addition, the two-sided 95% confidence interval (CI) for the difference between the responder proportions in the two treatment groups will be provided using the Wilson method."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "These above-listed endpoints will be analyzed using a hierarchical ('gatekeeping') testing procedure. Thus, if the primary analysis is statistically significant (p<0.05), then secondary endpoint #1 will be analyzed, also based on the use of a two-sided test at the alpha=0.05 level of significance. If secondary endpoint #1 is statistically significant (p<0.05), then the testing procedure will proceed to secondary endpoint #2, and so on. If the test for a particular endpoint is not statistically significant, the inference for all subsequent endpoints in the hierarchy will not be performed."

*[verbatim, same source, Sample Size Evaluation]* — "The assumed responder rates for the primary endpoint are 10% (placebo) and 35% (pexidartinib). Based on the use of a two-sided, two-sample comparison of proportions at the alpha=0.05 level of significance by Fisher's exact test, a sample size of 126 ITT subjects (63 per arm) provides 90% power to detect this magnitude of difference."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 211810, Reference ID 4470487, §8 Statistical Analysis Plan]* — "The trial was designed to accrue 126 patients to provide 90% power to detect a significant difference in ORR at a two-sided alpha level of 0.05, assuming an ORR of 10% in the placebo arm and of 35% in the pexidartinib arm. There were no pre-specified interim analyses. The primary analysis was a Fisher's exact test performed on the intent-to-treat (ITT) population, and the Wilson method was used to estimate the two-sided 95% confidence interval (CI) for ORR."

*[verbatim, same source, Table 57/Protocol Amendments]* — "6 Oct 10, 2016 Response to clinical hold, protocol was placed on clinical hold when the data monitoring committee reviewed unblinded safety data and identified two cases of potential cholestatic liver injury. Updated safety information. Enrollment was stopped. Patients randomized to placebo no longer allowed to crossover to pexidartinib therapy."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "In Protocol Version 8 (September 11, 2017), Daiichi Sankyo revised the hierarchical testing order for the secondary endpoints based on blinded assessments of the database prior to the lock and unblinding of the data, which revealed a substantial amount of missing Week 25 patient-reported outcome (PRO) assessments, specifically for BPI-30, PROMIS® Physical Function items, and Worst Stiffness NRS. The proportion of responders based on BPI-30 was moved from position #1 to position #5 and ROM was moved from position #3 to position #1 in the hierarchy of secondary endpoints analyses."

*[verbatim, same source, Reviewer Comment]* — "Changing the statistical analysis plan after completion of the trial is strongly discouraged due to introduction of potential bias. However, FDA acknowledged the concern regarding the statistical validity of the originally proposed hierarchical analysis given the substantial amount of missing data. The revision in hierarchy of secondary endpoints limits the interpretability of the ENLIVEN results."

*[verbatim, same source, §8 Conclusions]* — "The review team recommends a boxed warning for hepatotoxicity and distribution through a restricted program under a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) program, which will include a patient registry to provide additional information to further characterize the risk of hepatotoxicity in the indicated population outside of the clinical trial setting and to elucidate the potential long-term risk of liver injury associated with pexidartinib treatment. The review team also recommends that the applicant conduct a study to evaluate the long-term risk of pexidartinib in patients who experience severe liver injury, as a postmarketing requirement."

This is a genuine example — unlike most of this batch — of a randomized, adequately-powered, blinded Phase 3 superiority trial with a clean statistically significant primary result (38% vs. 0% ORR, p<0.0001), yet FDA's own review still documents a reviewer-flagged mid-trial (pre-unblinding) SAP deviation on the secondary-endpoint hierarchy, driven by a safety-related clinical hold that also reshaped the trial's conduct (crossover halted, monitoring intensified) — illustrating that "real" randomized designs are not immune from the same kind of SAP-timing scrutiny seen in this project's single-arm accelerated approvals.

### 99. entrectinib (Rozlytrek) — NDA 212725

**Sponsor:** Genentech, Inc. (a member of the Roche Group; entrectinib was originally developed by Ignyta, Inc., acquired by Roche/Genentech in 2018, and traces to an earlier compound code NMS-1191372/RXDX-101)

**Indication approved:** (1) Adult patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) whose tumors are ROS1-positive (NDA 212725, regular approval); (2) adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older with solid tumors that have a neurotrophic tyrosine receptor kinase (NTRK) gene fusion without a known acquired resistance mutation, are metastatic or where surgical resection is likely to result in severe morbidity, and have progressed following treatment or have no satisfactory alternative therapy (NDA 212726, tissue-agnostic accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.510/Subpart H)

**Approval date:** August 15, 2019 (both indications approved the same day, reviewed together as a combined Multi-Discipline Review package)

**Pivotal trial:** Pooled cross-trial analysis of three independently conducted, single-arm, open-label trials — ALKA-372-001 ("ALKA", Study GO40783, EudraCT 2012-000148-88, not registered on ClinicalTrials.gov), STARTRK-1 (NCT02097810), and STARTRK-2 (NCT02568267, "Basket Study of Entrectinib... for Solid Tumors Harboring NTRK 1/2/3, ROS1, or ALK Gene Rearrangements")

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial, first-in-human dose-escalation design with 3+3 scheme (ALKA-372-001), Phase 1 multicenter dose-expansion (STARTRK-1), basket trial — histology-agnostic enrollment by shared molecular alteration (STARTRK-2, an explicitly named "Global Phase 2 Basket Study"), cross-trial pooled integrated analysis across independently conducted single-arm trials — distinct from the taxonomy's existing "Post-hoc recombination of differently-enrolled cohorts into one primary analysis population" (PALOMA-1), which pools cohorts *within* one trial rather than pooling patients across three separately sponsored/protocoled trials run years apart
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR, primary, per blinded independent central review [BICR] using RECIST v1.1), duration of response (DOR, key secondary/co-primary in practice), intracranial ORR (IC-ORR) and intracranial DOR (IC-DOR, pre-specified descriptive secondary endpoints in patients with CNS disease), progression-free survival/overall survival/clinical benefit rate (reported descriptively only — FDA reviewer stated these "cannot be evaluated based on a single arm trial" and excluded them from the efficacy determination)
- *Primary analysis:* descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (point estimate + CI, no formal hypothesis test) — no formal statistical test was pre-specified in the SAP for either the ROS1-NSCLC or NTRK-fusion pooled populations; exact (Clopper-Pearson) binomial confidence interval for ORR; Kaplan-Meier estimation and Brookmeyer-Crowley method for median DOR
- *Multiplicity:* not applicable — no comparative or multi-endpoint hypothesis test was pre-specified for either pooled population
- *Missing data/bias:* BICR review of tumor scans was prospective for STARTRK-2 patients but retrospective (by the same BICR team, using "equivalent Imaging Review Charters") for the ALKA and STARTRK-1 patients folded into the pooled analysis; major protocol deviations affected 23.3% of STARTRK-2 patients (informed consent, eligibility, and investigational-product compliance deviations), with an internal reviewer memo (IR-33, dated 10 May 2018) used to reclassify "major" protocol violations across the pooled dataset after the fact
- *Regulatory:* tissue-agnostic (tumor-agnostic) indication based on a shared molecular alteration across histologies — FDA's review explicitly frames this as only the third such approval after pembrolizumab (MSI-H/dMMR) and larotrectinib (NTRK fusion); accelerated approval (Subpart H, 21 CFR 314.510) granted on pooled single-arm ORR/DOR data across three independently conducted trials rather than a single registrational trial; regular (non-accelerated) approval also granted on pooled single-arm ORR/DOR data alone for the ROS1-NSCLC indication, reasoning explicitly by analogy to the single-arm precedent set by crizotinib's ROS1 approval; no FDA Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held for either indication

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ALKA-372-001 (GO40783, EudraCT 2012-000148-88): first-in-human, open-label, single-arm, nonrandomized, multicenter Phase 1 dose-escalation study of entrectinib (as RXDX-101) in adult patients with advanced/metastatic solid tumors harboring NTRK1/2/3, ROS1, or ALK molecular alterations; standard 3+3 dose-escalation scheme across three dosing schedules (100-1600 mg/m2 or 600 mg fixed dose), not registered on ClinicalTrials.gov
- STARTRK-1 (NCT02097810): Phase 1, multicenter, open-label study of oral entrectinib in adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic cancer confirmed positive for NTRK1/2/3, ROS1, or ALK molecular alterations, sponsored by Hoffmann-La Roche
- STARTRK-2 (NCT02568267): open-label, multicenter, global Phase 2 "basket" study — prospective enrollment of patients by molecular alteration (NTRK1/2/3, ROS1, or ALK gene rearrangement) regardless of tumor histology, with tumor scans read prospectively by the same BICR team used retrospectively for the two earlier trials
- Two independent, non-overlapping response-evaluable ("efficacy-evaluable") populations were carved from the pooled dataset per an Integrated Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP version-5): (1) the ROS1-NSCLC "primary efficacy set" — the first 51 consecutively enrolled, ROS1-TKI-naive patients with ROS1-positive metastatic NSCLC and measurable disease per RECIST v1.1, each with ≥12 months of follow-up from first post-treatment tumor assessment; and (2) the NTRK efficacy-evaluable population — the first 54 sequentially enrolled, TRK-inhibitor-naive adult patients with NTRK fusion-positive solid tumors and measurable disease, each with ≥6 months of follow-up
- Endpoint definitions were standardized across the three trials for the pooled analysis: ORR = proportion with confirmed CR or PR by BICR per RECIST v1.1 (repeat imaging ≥4 weeks after initial documentation required to confirm); DOR = time from first confirmed response to progression or death, censored at last tumor assessment if neither occurred; IC-ORR/IC-DOR defined analogously but restricted to CNS target/non-target lesions
- Sample-size logic was a precision (not power) calculation for each population separately: for ROS1-NSCLC, assuming a true BICR ORR of 70%, ≥50 patients gave 82% power to exclude a 50% lower confidence bound; for NTRK fusion tumors, assuming a true BICR ORR of 60%, 56 patients (evaluated at the first 54) were estimated to yield a 95% two-sided CI excluding a 30% lower bound — neither calculation was a formal null-hypothesis test
- Results: ROS1-NSCLC pooled ORR by BICR was 78% (95% CI 65-89%), median DOR 15.7 months (95% CI 11.4-34.8, not included in labeling because only 30% of responders had observed DOR ≥18 months); NTRK-fusion pooled ORR by BICR was 57.4% (95% CI 43.2-70.8%), median DOR not reached at the primary data cutoff (31 May 2018), with 68% of responders having DOR ≥6 months and 45% ≥12 months at an updated cutoff (31 October 2018)
- FDA's statistical reviewer stated plainly that time-to-event endpoints (OS, PFS) and clinical benefit rate "cannot be evaluated based on a single arm trial" and excluded them from the substantial-evidence-of-effectiveness determination for both indications; the reviewer's summary noted "no major statistical issues that impacted the overall efficacy conclusions" but cautioned that pooled cross-study assessments generally require caution given "underlying heterogeneity in the design of each of the studies included in pooled assessment"
- As a condition of the NTRK indication's accelerated approval, Genentech must submit final study reports/datasets from the pooled 54-patient efficacy population (with ≥2 years' follow-up from response) and additional prospective single-arm data (≥40 patients in specified tumor types not already well-characterized, e.g., colorectal cancer, CNS tumors, gynecological cancers, melanoma) to verify clinical benefit through more precise ORR/DOR estimation — FDA explicitly stated that, given the observed effect size, "equipoise no longer exists and verification of clinical benefit in randomized trials would no longer be feasible even in any tumor type at this time"

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter, NDA 212725 (ROS1-positive NSCLC, regular approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2019/212725Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- FDA Approval Letter, NDA 212726 (NTRK fusion-positive solid tumors, accelerated approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2019/212726Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2019/212725s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (combined package covering both NDA 212725 and NDA 212726) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/212725Orig1s000%2C%20212726Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record, STARTRK-2 — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02568267 (no documentSection/protocol/SAP posted, confirmed via the ClinicalTrials.gov API)
- ClinicalTrials.gov record, STARTRK-1 — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02097810 (no documentSection/protocol/SAP posted, confirmed via the ClinicalTrials.gov API)
- ALKA-372-001: no ClinicalTrials.gov record identified; registered only under EudraCT 2012-000148-88 (EU trial predating Ignyta/Genentech's involvement)
- Pivotal publication (NTRK fusion-positive solid tumors): Doebele RC, Drilon A, Paz-Ares L, et al. "Entrectinib in patients with advanced or metastatic NTRK fusion-positive solid tumours: integrated analysis of three phase 1-2 trials." *Lancet Oncol.* 2020;21:271-282. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(19)30691-6>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31838007/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Entrectinib%20in%20patients%20with%20advanced%20or%20metastatic%20NTRK%20fusion-positive%20solid%20tumours)
- Pivotal publication (ROS1 fusion-positive NSCLC): Drilon A, Siena S, Dziadziuszko R, et al. "Entrectinib in ROS1 fusion-positive non-small-cell lung cancer: integrated analysis of three phase 1-2 trials." *Lancet Oncol.* 2020;21:261-270. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(19)30690-4>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31838015/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Entrectinib%20in%20ROS1%20fusion-positive%20non-small-cell%20lung%20cancer)

**Other resources**

- Genentech/Roche participates in the Vivli data-sharing platform; trial-specific IPD availability for ALKA-372-001, STARTRK-1, or STARTRK-2 was not individually confirmed.
- No FDA Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held for either the ROS1-NSCLC or NTRK-fusion indication; the Multi-Discipline Review states the Division "did not refer this NDA to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee (ODAC) because the safety profile is acceptable for the treatment of the indicated population and the application did not raise significant public health questions."
- Postmarketing requirements beyond the NTRK-indication efficacy-verification studies described above include a hepatic-impairment clinical pharmacology PMR, a nonclinical off-target receptor/transporter characterization PMR, cardiac-risk-characterization clinical PMRs (505(o)) for both indications, and a pediatric long-term growth/neurodevelopmental-outcomes PMR tied to the accelerated approval.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 212725, Reference ID 4477648, §8 "Statistical Analysis Plan for Integrated Summary of Efficacy (ISE)", p.109]* — "The statistical analysis plan (SAP) describes an integrated efficacy analysis pooled across the three clinical trials in adult patients (STARTRK-2, ALKA, STARTRK-1) to support the approval of entrectinib for the treatment of patients with ROS1-positive NSCLC. Per the SAP, the definitions of efficacy endpoints for this integrated analysis have been standardized across studies. No formal statistical test was planned in the SAP."

*[verbatim, same source, p.109]* — "The primary analysis of the primary endpoint ORR was to provide the point estimator of ORR (the proportion of patients with confirmed CR or PR with its two-sided 95% CI) using the Clopper-Pearson exact method. Kaplan-Meier method would be used to summarize DOR including estimating the median DOR and its 95% CI using the method of Brookmeyer and Crowly (1982) and Klein and Moeschberger (1997). Per the SAP, final analysis would be performed for marketing application submission after approximately 50 patients with ROS1-positive NSCLC had been enrolled across the three studies."

*[verbatim, same source, p.109]* — "Per the SAP, efficacy analyses would be presented only for the ROS1 NSCLC efficacy-evaluable population, which is called the 'primary analysis set' throughout this review. The primary analysis set was defined as ROS1 inhibitor-naïve patients with ROS1-positive NSCLC with measurable disease at baseline as determined per RECIST v1.1 by investigator."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 212726, Reference ID 4476394, §8 "Statistical Analysis Plan for Integrated Summary of Efficacy (ISE)", p.145]* — "The efficacy endpoints for the integrated analysis of effectiveness are provided in Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) version-5 and are summarized below: Primary Endpoints: Overall response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DOR) as assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR) using RECIST v1.1."

*[verbatim, same source, p.166, "Assessment of Efficacy Across Trials"]* — "There were no meaningful secondary endpoints specified in the SAP of each study aside from DOR... No subpopulations were identified a priori or in the SAP."

*[verbatim, same source, p.148]* — "Clinical Reviewer Comment: During the initial breakthrough therapy meeting and the pre-NDA meeting, FDA requested that Genentech (formerly Ignyta) provide a justification for the proposed size of the efficacy population (N=54) supporting this application. FDA concluded that the rarity of solid tumors harboring the activating NTRK rearrangements precluded the conduct of randomized controlled trials and that the size of the efficacy population was adequate to characterize the overall response rate in patients with NTRK-positive solid tumors."

*[verbatim, NDA 212725 Multi-Discipline Review, Reference ID 4477648, §8, "Statistical Reviewer's Comments"]* — "Clinical Benefit Rate (CBR), which includes stable disease, is not an acceptable endpoint in a single arm study; this endpoint was not evaluated in this review. Time-to-event endpoints such as OS or PFS are not interpretable in a single-arm study; the results of PFS, OS and other time-to-event endpoints, with the exception of DOR and IC-DOR, were not evaluated in this review."

*[verbatim, NDA 212726 Multi-Discipline Review, Reference ID 4476394, "Summary and Conclusions — Statistical Issues", p.222]* — "There were no major statistical issues that impacted the overall efficacy conclusions. However, the single arm nature of the study does not allow for statistical inferences to be made. In general, when considering integrated assessment strategy using data pooled across multiple studies, the findings need to be assessed with caution due to the underlying heterogeneity in the design of each of the studies included in pooled assessment... Time-to-event endpoints were included as the secondary endpoints supporting efficacy in the integrated assessments, but due to the non-randomized nature of the study these endpoints are not interpretable and cannot be used to support the efficacy of the study drug."

*[verbatim, same source, "Conclusions and Recommendations", p.222-223]* — "Drug approval based on the presence of a common genetic defect, regardless of primary tumor site of origin and histology (i.e., tissue-agnostic) is a new paradigm; the only previous drugs to be approved under this paradigm is pembrolizumab for the treatment of microsatellite instability high (MSI-H)/mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) metastatic solid tumors that has progressed on or for which there is no available therapy, and larotrectinib for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients with solid tumors that have an NTRK gene fusion without a known [acquired resistance mutation]."

*[verbatim, NDA 212725 Multi-Discipline Review, Reference ID 4477648, §9 "Advisory Committee Meeting and Other External Consultations"]* — "The Division did not refer this NDA to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee (ODAC) because the safety profile is acceptable for the treatment of the indicated population and the application did not raise significant public health questions regarding role of entrectinib for this indication. Outside expertise was not necessary as there were no controversial issues that could benefit from an ODAC discussion."

This entry documents a genuinely cross-trial, single-arm, response-rate-based approval basis for both of entrectinib's indications — not a randomized trial with a pooled sensitivity analysis, but two independently-defined, non-overlapping response-evaluable populations (n=51 and n=54) each assembled from the first sequentially-enrolled qualifying patients across three separately sponsored/protocoled Phase 1-2 trials (one of which, ALKA-372-001, predates Genentech's and even Ignyta's involvement and has no ClinicalTrials.gov record at all). FDA's own review text repeatedly and explicitly disclaims any comparative/inferential statistical conclusion from this design, and separately treats the ROS1-NSCLC indication (regular approval, reasoning by analogy to crizotinib's precedent) and the NTRK-fusion indication (accelerated approval, explicitly framed by FDA as only the third-ever tissue-agnostic approval) as two distinct regulatory determinations resting on the same three-trial pooling strategy.

### 100. Ga 68 DOTATOC (unbranded) — NDA 210828

**Sponsor:** University of Iowa Health Care (UIHC PET Imaging Center)

**Indication approved:** Ga 68 DOTATOC Injection, a radioactive diagnostic agent for use with positron emission tomography (PET) for localization of somatostatin receptor-positive neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) in adult and pediatric patients

**Approval date:** August 21, 2019

**Pivotal trial:** RET-NET-01, a retrospective pooled analysis of three prospective single-center studies conducted at the University of Iowa Hospitals and Clinics — Study 1 (NCT01619865), Study 2 (NCT01869725), and Study 3 (NCT02441062)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison against a composite reference standard), retrospective pooled/cross-trial analysis of three independently conducted prospective single-center studies, academic (non-industry) 505(b)(2) NDA sponsor
- *Endpoints:* concordance rate (diagnostic/mapping agent vs. reference standard) — termed "positive percent agreement" and "negative percent agreement" by FDA rather than sensitivity/specificity, because the composite reference standard was not uniformly pathology-based
- *Primary analysis:* one-sided exact binomial test against a pre-specified performance goal (positive percent agreement >80%; negative percent agreement >70%), exact 95% confidence intervals around each agreement rate
- *Missing data/bias:* patients with insufficient data to establish NET status per the composite reference were classified as indeterminate and excluded from the efficacy analysis population (a substantial exclusion — e.g., only 44.2% of Study 3's full population qualified for the efficacy population); FDA noted the applicant could not verify whether all available Ga-68-DOTATOC images (versus a selective subset) were re-reviewed for enrolled patients, since data traceable to the original per-study case report forms was not submitted
- *Regulatory:* retrospective cross-study pooling protocol (RET-NET-01) was never submitted to FDA prior to being conducted, so the Agency had no opportunity to discuss the pooling design in advance; FDA's review team ultimately relied on only 2 of the 3 pooled studies (Study 1 and Study 2) as sufficiently reliable for the labeled efficacy claim, treating Study 3 as unreliable due to incomplete enrollment relative to its original design; no FDA advisory committee meeting was held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- RET-NET-01 was a prospectively-planned retrospective clinical study assembled from three independently ongoing, open-label, single-center (University of Iowa) prospective trials of Ga-68-DOTATOC PET/CT in patients with known or suspected somatostatin receptor (SSTR)-positive NETs: Study 1 (n=220, "known or suspected SSTR2 positive tumors," comparing Ga-68-DOTATOC to conventional imaging in the same subjects), Study 2 (n=62, "histologically proven NET or other SSTR2 positive tumors," comparing Ga-68-DOTATOC to Octreoscan plus contrast-CT), and Study 3 (n=52 planned, later only 68 of a planned 200 enrolled, designed to assess change in patient management)
- All patients received a single IV dose of Ga-68-DOTATOC (~3.7-4.0 mCi; mass dose <50 micrograms) followed by PET/CT imaging 55-90 minutes later
- Endpoint definition: images from all three studies were re-read by two independent nuclear-medicine physicians ("readers"), blinded to clinical data and other imaging, as positive or negative for NET in each patient; disagreements were resolved by consensus, with a third blinded reader adjudicating remaining disagreements (residual disagreement classified as indeterminate). Per-patient PET status was compared against a composite reference standard combining histopathology, other imaging (MRI/CT/In-111 pentetreotide or Octreoscan), and biochemical markers (chromogranin A, pancreastatin) obtained within 1 year of the Ga-68-DOTATOC scan
- Because some patients were classified NET-positive by the composite reference without pathologic confirmation, FDA's reviewers explicitly declined to call the Applicant's endpoints "sensitivity" and "specificity," relabeling them positive percent agreement (PPA) and negative percent agreement (NPA) with the composite reference
- Design-stage hypothesis tests (as planned by the Applicant): one-sided exact binomial test of H0: PPA=0.80 vs. H1: PPA>0.80, and H0: NPA=0.70 vs. H1: NPA>0.70, each with a two-sided exact CI reported for context
- Results (pooled RET-NET-01 efficacy population, n=259 of 334 enrolled across all three studies): consensus-read PPA 92.1% (95% exact CI 87.5-95.4%), NPA 92.3% (95% exact CI 81.5-97.9%); individual-study results were consistent with the pooled estimate (Study 1/"Study A" reader agreement ~90-91% positive, ~86-89% negative per label Table 6; Study 2/"Study B" PPA/NPA ~90-92%/75%)
- FDA's statistical reviewers reviewed the three constituent study protocols individually and concluded only Studies 1 and 2 were sufficiently reliable to support the labeled efficacy claim — both were prospectively designed for performance evaluation with reasonable alignment between planned and actual enrollment — while Study 3 (designed to evaluate management-decision impact, and only 68 of 200 planned patients enrolled) was excluded from reliance for efficacy
- A supportive systematic review/meta-analysis of 17 published studies (Graham et al. 2017, "GRAHAM-2017") was submitted by the Applicant, but FDA's review team did not rely on it for its findings because the underlying publications were not associated with new Applicant claims, pre-specified protocols, or submitted patient-level data — it was treated as supportive context only

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2019/210828Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2019/210828s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review and Evaluation, NDA 210828 505(b)(2) (Reference ID 4478031) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/210828Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov records — Study 1: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01619865; Study 2: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01869725; Study 3: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02441062 (no protocol/SAP posted in any of the three Documents tabs; the pooling protocol for RET-NET-01 itself was never separately registered)
- Supportive meta-analysis (not the pivotal evidentiary basis, but the Applicant's submitted supportive literature review): Graham MM, Gu X, Ginader T, Breheny P, Sunderland JJ. "⁶⁸Ga-DOTATOC Imaging of Neuroendocrine Tumors: A Systematic Review and Metaanalysis." *J Nucl Med.* 2017;58(9):1452-1458. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.2967/jnumed.117.191197), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28280220/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=68Ga-DOTATOC%20Imaging%20of%20Neuroendocrine%20Tumors%20Systematic%20Review%20and%20Metaanalysis)

**Other resources**

- No IPD-sharing program (Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere) applies to this academic single-institution sponsor; not applicable.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this NDA.
- This is one of a small family of academic-sponsor Ga-68 somatostatin-analog PET NDAs approved in this era (alongside gallium Ga 68 dotatate/Netspot, NDA 208547, Advanced Accelerator Applications, approved 2016) — University of Iowa's submission is distinctive for being sponsored and run entirely by a single academic PET imaging center rather than an industry sponsor.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review and Evaluation, NDA 210828, Reference ID 4478031, §7.1]* — "The Applicant submitted two clinical datasets to support the safety and efficacy of Ga-68-DOTATOC: 1. RET-NET-01, a retrospective analysis of data from three prospectively conducted clinical studies and patient-level data... 2. GRAHAM-2017, from 17 clinical publications on Ga-68-DOTATOC, selected by the Applicant and group-level data extracted from the publications (Graham et al. 2017)."

*[verbatim, same source, §7.2 Review Strategy]* — "The review team identified Studies 1 and 2 in the RET-NET-01 protocol as sufficiently reliable for inclusion in labeling to support efficacy. Both studies were prospectively designed for performance evaluation and featured reasonable alignment between planned and actual enrollment at the time of analysis. In contrast, Study 3 was designed for evaluation of management decisions and enrollment was insufficiently complete (only 68 patients enrolled of 200 planned) to permit focus on management endpoints or reliance on this study for efficacy... the publications identified in GRAHAM-2017 were not associated with new Applicant claims, prespecified protocols, or submission of patient-level data. Therefore, the review team did not rely on these publications for its findings."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.1.1 Study RET-NET-01, Trial Design]* — "While the Applicant acknowledged that the three studies varied in overall design, the Applicant claimed in the protocol of Study RET-NET-01 that the patient populations are sufficiently consistent to allow for prospectively planned analysis. The Applicant did not clarify the rationale of combining Study 1, Study 2, and Study 3 instead of analyzing these studies separately."

*[verbatim, same source, Comment]* — "The protocol of Study RET-NET-01 had not been submitted to the Agency through pre-IND 125673 prior to its conduct; the Agency did not have the opportunity to discuss the study design and analysis with the Applicant. The Applicant did not submit data traceable to the pre-specified CRFs for individual Studies 1 to 3, so it cannot be verified whether all available or selective Ga-68-DOTATOC PET/CT images were re-reviewed for enrolled patients."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.1.2 Study Endpoints / Statistical Analysis Plan]* — "The protocol pre-specified co-primary sensitivity and specificity endpoints were not agreed upon by FDA and were based on consensus reads... Comment: Using the Applicant's composite reference, some patients' disease statuses were identified as positive without pathology; therefore, to avoid misuse of terminology, the Applicant's so-defined 'sensitivity' and 'specificity' are referred to as the positive percent agreement and negative percent agreement, respectively... The one-sided exact binomial test was planned by the Applicant to test: H0: positive percent agreement based on consensus reads =0.80 versus H1: positive percent agreement based on consensus reads >0.80 and H0: negative percent agreement based on consensus reads =0.70 versus H1: negative percent agreement based on consensus reads >0.70."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.1.2 Study Results]* — "For Study RET-NET-01, the positive percent agreement based on consensus reads was 92.1 (95% exact CI: 87.5%, 95.4%); the negative percent agreement based on consensus reads was 92.3 (95% exact CI: 81.5%, 97.9%)."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.3 Statistical Issues]* — "There were no apparent statistical issues in this application that affect the performance characteristics of Ga-68-DOTATOC for use with positron emission tomography for localization of somatostatin receptor positive NETs... The observed patient level positive and negative agreements demonstrated between NET status and Ga-68-DOTATOC PET imaging appear to suggest Ga-68-DOTATOC efficacy when used as indicated for localizing SSR+ NETs in adult and pediatric patients."

This entry is a genuinely different animal from the oncology therapeutics in this batch: it is a diagnostic PET tracer, not a treatment, with no OS/PFS/ORR and no randomized comparator — the "SAP" question resolves to a paired detection-agreement design, and FDA's own review is notably candid that the sponsor's cross-study pooling protocol was assembled and executed without prior Agency input, that one of the three pooled studies had to be excluded from the efficacy claim for under-enrollment, and that the sponsor could not document complete/non-selective image re-review — genuine reviewable concerns despite the ultimately favorable approval decision, none of which required inference to describe.

### 101. zanubrutinib (Brukinsa) — NDA 213217

**Sponsor:** BeiGene USA, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) who have received at least one prior therapy (accelerated approval, based on overall response rate)

**Approval date:** November 14, 2019

**Pivotal trial:** BGB-3111-206 ("Study 206"), NCT03206970; supportive: BGB-3111-AU-003, NCT02343120

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial supporting accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.510 Subpart H, pooled/supportive analysis across two independently conducted single-arm studies (206 as primary, AU-003 as supportive)
- *Endpoints:* overall response rate (ORR, primary, per Independent Review Committee [IRC] using the 2014 Lugano Classification/IWG-NHL criteria), duration of response (DOR), complete response (CR) rate, progression-free survival (PFS) and time to response (TTR) (secondary/descriptive, not formally testable in a single-arm design), ORR by investigator (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* one-sided binomial exact test of a single proportion against a pre-specified null (H0: ORR=40% vs. Ha: ORR≥40%), two-sided Clopper-Pearson exact 95% confidence interval around ORR
- *Multiplicity:* not applicable — SAP states "Multiplicity Adjustment: Not applicable" (single formal primary endpoint, no comparator arm)
- *Missing data/bias:* subjects with no post-baseline response assessment (for any reason) counted as non-responders for ORR (non-responder imputation); FDA independently re-adjudicated best overall response and found several sponsor-assessed complete responses downgraded to partial response for inadequate confirmation of bone marrow/GI disease response
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval (Subpart H) based on ORR as a surrogate reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit; randomized Phase 3 confirmatory trial (BGB-3111-306) required as a postmarketing requirement to verify clinical benefit; no Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- BGB-3111-206: single-arm, open-label, multicenter Phase 2 study conducted in China, enrolling patients with histologically documented, centrally confirmed relapsed/refractory MCL who had received ≥1 but <5 prior treatment regimens; 86 patients enrolled and treated with zanubrutinib 160 mg orally twice daily until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or withdrawal
- Primary endpoint (per SAP §4.1/Protocol §10.1.1): "the rate of objective response, defined as the achievement of either a partial response (PR) or complete response (CR) as determined by the Independent Review Committee (IRC) according to the [2014] modification of the International Working Group on Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (NHL) Criteria (Cheson) at any time on study drug"
- Secondary endpoints: PFS (IRC-assessed, investigator-assessed as sensitivity), duration of response (DOR), time to response (TTR), ORR by investigator, and standard safety endpoints (TEAE incidence/severity per CTCAE)
- Analysis populations: Safety Population (all subjects who received any dose of study drug); Revised Safety Population (subjects in the Safety Population with pathologically confirmed MCL — also the primary efficacy-evaluable population, per SAP §6.1); Per-Protocol Population (Revised Safety population subjects without major protocol deviations, used only as a supplementary analysis)
- Sample size (per FDA Statistical Review, based on SAP logic): approximately 80 subjects were planned, sized on precision of the ORR estimate rather than a formal comparative power calculation — "for a sample size of 80 patients, for an observed ORR of 70% (60/86), the 95% exact confidence interval (CI) is (59%, 79%)"; the SAP's own text (with digits unrecoverable from the posted PDF's text layer due to a font-encoding artifact on that page) frames the design as demonstrating statistical significance against a historical-control ORR assumption using a one-sided binomial exact test at alpha=0.025
- Statistical methods: primary analysis was a point estimate and two-sided Clopper-Pearson exact 95% CI for ORR, plus a one-sided binomial exact test of H0: ORR=0.40 vs. Ha: ORR≥0.40 at a one-sided significance level of 0.025; Kaplan-Meier estimation (with Brookmeyer-Crowley-type CIs) used descriptively for PFS/DOR; no formal multiplicity adjustment (single primary endpoint, no comparator arm)
- Results: ORR by IRC 84% (95% CI: 74, 91), CR rate 59% (95% CI: 48, 70), median DOR 19.5 months (95% CI: 16.6, NE) in Study 206; supportive Study AU-003 MCL cohort (N=32) showed ORR 84% (95% CI: 67, 95), CR 22% (95% CI: 9, 40), median DOR 18.5 months (95% CI: 12.6, NE)
- FDA independently re-adjudicated best overall response in Study 206 and identified discordances (Table 19) — e.g., subjects the Applicant scored as complete response were reclassified by FDA to partial response for inadequate confirmation of bone marrow or gastrointestinal disease involvement — but the FDA-adjudicated ORR still rejected the null hypothesis (84%, 95% CI: 74, 91)

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2019/213217s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (Statistical Reviewer Alexei C. Ionan, PhD; Statistical Team Leader Jingjing Ye, PhD; Reference ID 4519846) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/213217Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03206970
- Protocol (posted, Version 4.0, 6 September 2018) — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/70/NCT03206970/Prot_001.pdf
- Statistical Analysis Plan (posted, Version 2.0, 2 April 2018) — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/70/NCT03206970/SAP_000.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Song Y, Zhou K, Zou D, et al. "Treatment of Patients with Relapsed or Refractory Mantle-Cell Lymphoma with Zanubrutinib, a Selective Inhibitor of Bruton's Tyrosine Kinase." *Clin Cancer Res.* 2020;26(16):4216-4224. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-19-3703), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32461234/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Treatment%20of%20Patients%20with%20Relapsed%20or%20Refractory%20Mantle-Cell%20Lymphoma%20with%20Zanubrutinib%20a%20Selective%20Inhibitor%20of%20Bruton%27s%20Tyrosine%20Kinase)

**Other resources**

- BeiGene's individual participation in a specific IPD-sharing program (Vivli, YODA Project, Project Data Sphere) was not confirmed — the company's clinical-data-sharing policy page could not be verified during this research (its former beigene.com data-sharing URL now redirects to a rebranded beonemedicines.com domain that returned a 404), so trial-specific IPD availability should be treated as unconfirmed rather than assumed unavailable.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held: per the Multi-Discipline Review, "This application was not presented to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee or other external consultants because zanubrutinib is not first-in-class, and the application did not raise new efficacy or safety issues for the recommended indications."
- Postmarketing requirement: BGB-3111-306, an ongoing randomized Phase 3 trial of zanubrutinib + rituximab vs. bendamustine + rituximab in previously untreated MCL (~500 patients planned, primary endpoint IRC-assessed PFS, OS a key secondary endpoint, with a pre-specified superiority evaluation plan), required to verify clinical benefit and support conversion to regular approval.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, posted Statistical Analysis Plan, BGB-3111-206, Version 2.0 (2-Apr-2018), §6.4.1 Primary Efficacy Endpoint]* — "The primary analysis of ORR will be based on the PET-based assessments by the Independent Review Committee (IRC) following the 2014 modification of the International Working Group in NHL criteria. ORR is defined as the proportion of subjects achieving a best overall response of CR or PR. A point estimate and a 2-sided Clopper-Pearson 95% confident interval (CI) of ORR will be provided. A binomial exact test will be performed to test against the null hypothesis H0: ORR=0.40 using the significant level of 0.025 (1-sided). Best overall response (BOR) is defined as the best response recorded from the start of BGB-3111 until data cut or start of new anti-cancer treatment. Subjects with no post-baseline response assessment (due to any reason) will be considered non-responders for ORR."

*[verbatim, same source, §6.4 Efficacy Analysis]* — "All efficacy analyses will be based on the Revised Safety population. The primary endpoint of ORR will also be analyzed using the safety population and the per-protocol population (if necessary) as supplementary to the primary analysis."

*[verbatim, same source, §6.2.5 Multiplicity Adjustment]* — "Not applicable."

*[verbatim, posted Protocol, Version 4.0 (6 September 2018), §10.1.1 Primary Endpoint]* — "The primary endpoint of the study is the rate of objective response, defined as the achievement of either a partial response (PR) or CR as assessed by the IRC according to the 2014 modification of the International Working Group on NHL Criteria (Cheson, 2014) (Appendix 3) at any time on study drug."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 213217, Reference ID 4519846, §Statistical Analysis Plan/Sample Size Determination]* — "Approximately 80 subjects were planned to be enrolled. The sample size calculation was mainly based on the level of precision of the estimated ORR. With a sample size of 80 patients, for an observed ORR of 70% (60/86), the 95% exact confidence interval (CI) is (59%, 79%). A binomial exact test will be performed for hypothesis testing H0: ORR=40% vs. Ha: ORR ≥ 40%. Two-sided Clopper-Pearson 95% confidence interval (CI) of ORR will be constructed to assess the precision of the point estimate of ORR."

*[verbatim, same source, §Efficacy Results – Primary Endpoint]* — "Overall response rate is 84% (95% CI: 74, 91) – the null hypothesis is rejected."

*[verbatim, same source, §Conclusions on the Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness]* — "The rationale for the recommendation of accelerated approval for zanubrutinib is founded upon the following considerations: Uncertainty as to the relationship of ORR and DOR to the ultimate outcome of overall survival. Although the ORR was 84% per independent review committee assessment, 22% of patients discontinued treatment due to progressive disease."

*[verbatim, same source, §9 Advisory Committee Meeting and Other External Consultations]* — "This application was not presented to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee or other external consultants because zanubrutinib is not first-in-class, and the application did not raise new efficacy or safety issues for the recommended indications."

*[verbatim, same source, §13 Postmarketing Requirements and Commitment]* — "To verify the clinical benefit of zanubrutinib, complete and submit the final results of Trial BGB-3111-306 - the ongoing randomized, Phase 3 clinical trial of BRUKINSA in combination with rituximab versus bendamustine and rituximab in patients with previously untreated mantle cell lymphoma. The primary endpoint is progression free survival as assessed by Independent Review Committee (IRC). Overall survival is a key secondary endpoint. The statistical plan should include a plan for a superiority evaluation of the primary endpoint. Enrollment of approximately 500 patients is expected."

*[verbatim, approved Package Insert, §1 Indications and Usage]* — "This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate [see Clinical Studies (14.1)]. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial."

Note on source quality: unlike some other entries in this census where the sponsor's true SAP had to be reverse-engineered, BeiGene's actual protocol and SAP for Study 206 are posted on ClinicalTrials.gov and were read directly — no reverse-engineered section is needed here. One caveat: two pages of both the posted Protocol PDF and posted SAP PDF (covering Study Objectives, Study Endpoints, and the Sample Size Considerations/Statistical Methods sections) have a text layer where digit characters do not extract correctly (a font-encoding artifact, not a redaction), so the sponsor's own stated numeric sample-size assumptions (e.g., the assumed historical-control ORR) could not be pulled verbatim from those specific pages; the equivalent numeric detail was instead sourced from FDA's Statistical Review, which quotes the same Sample Size Determination section without the encoding defect.

### 102. enfortumab vedotin-ejfv (Padcev) — BLA 761137

**Sponsor:** Astellas Pharma US, Inc. (co-developed with Seattle Genetics, Inc.)

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer who have previously received a PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitor, and platinum-containing chemotherapy in the neoadjuvant/adjuvant, locally advanced, or metastatic setting (or are platinum-ineligible) — approved under accelerated approval based on response rate

**Approval date:** December 18, 2019

**Pivotal trial:** EV-201 (Study SGN22E-001) Cohort 1, NCT03219333

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H/21 CFR 314.510, confirmed ORR primary endpoint agreed with FDA prospectively at a pre-protocol End-of-Phase-1 Type B meeting, two-cohort structure (Cohort 1 platinum-treated, Cohort 2 platinum-naive/cisplatin-ineligible, only Cohort 1 supporting the initial approval), exposure-response analysis pooled across two trials (EV-101 Part C and EV-201 Cohort 1) used as supportive evidence
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR, primary — confirmed CR or PR per RECIST 1.1 by blinded independent central review [BICR]), duration of response (DOR, key secondary), disease control rate at 16 weeks (DCR16), progression-free survival, overall survival, ORR/DOR/DCR16/PFS per investigator assessment (supportive), patient-reported outcomes (EORTC QLQ-C30, EQ-5D)
- *Primary analysis:* two-sided 95% exact confidence interval (Clopper-Pearson method) for the response rate, calculated on the full analysis set; design-stage one-sided exact test (EAST software, Cytel) of H0: ORR≤10% vs. Ha: ORR>10% against a historical 10% response-rate benchmark for later-line chemotherapy
- *Multiplicity:* not applicable — single formal primary endpoint, no comparative or multi-endpoint hypothesis test in a single-arm design
- *Missing data/bias:* not applicable in the randomized-trial sense (no crossover/censoring comparator issue); an independent data monitoring committee (IDMC) reviewed safety periodically, including a pre-specified stopping-rule analysis of ocular (corneal) adverse events in the first 60 enrolled subjects
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval (Subpart H) based on ORR as a surrogate reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit; the confirmed-ORR primary endpoint and its acceptability for accelerated approval was discussed with, and agreed to by, FDA at a Type B End-of-Phase-1 meeting (April 21, 2017) before protocol finalization; FDA determined no advisory committee meeting was needed because the benefit-risk profile was "clearly favorable" and no controversial issues were identified

**Trial design & endpoints**

- EV-201 (SGN22E-001): single-arm, open-label, multicenter Phase 2 trial of enfortumab vedotin 1.25 mg/kg IV on Days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle, in adults with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer previously treated with a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor; Cohort 1 (n=125 efficacy-evaluable of 128 treated) enrolled patients who had also received platinum-containing chemotherapy, Cohort 2 enrolled platinum-naive, cisplatin-ineligible patients (not part of the initial approval basis)
- Primary endpoint: confirmed ORR (CR or PR per RECIST 1.1, confirmed by repeat scan ≥4 weeks after initial documentation of response) as determined by an independent review facility/BICR, in the full analysis set; two-sided 95% exact (Clopper-Pearson) CI reported for the rate
- Sample-size/power logic: ~200 subjects total (~100+ in Cohort 1, ~100 in Cohort 2) were planned; with ~100 Cohort 1 subjects the study had 98% power to detect an ORR increase from a 10% historical benchmark to 25%, and 81% power to detect an increase to 20%, at one-sided α=0.025 using exact methods (EAST v6.0, Cytel)
- Secondary endpoints: DOR, DCR16, PFS, and OS (all per BICR, with investigator-assessed versions as supportive), safety/tolerability, PK, and anti-therapeutic antibody incidence; exploratory endpoints included Nectin-4 biomarker expression and patient-reported quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30, EQ-5D)
- No randomization or blinding of treatment assignment was used (single-arm design); an IDMC reviewed unblinded safety data periodically, and a pre-specified surveillance rule monitored corneal/ocular adverse events (slit-lamp exams) in the first 60 enrolled subjects, with a stopping threshold if events occurred in ≥15% of that cohort
- Results: confirmed ORR (Cohort 1, BICR) was 44% (55/125; 95% CI 35.1-53.2%), median DOR 7.6 months (95% CI 6.34-not reached), median time to response 1.84 months; 84% of response-evaluable subjects (92/110) had target-lesion size reduction
- FDA's review states the confirmed-ORR primary endpoint was discussed with and agreed to by FDA at an April 21, 2017 Type B End-of-Phase-1 meeting, before protocol finalization, as an endpoint that "may predict clinical benefit and be an acceptable endpoint for accelerated approval pending review of the data" — an unusually explicit, prospectively documented instance of FDA sign-off on the accelerated-approval endpoint ahead of the pivotal data

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2019/761137Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2019/761137Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 4536389, BLA 761137) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/761137Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (EV-201) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03219333 (Statistical Analysis Plan Version 4, 17-SEP-2020, posted in the Documents tab)
- Protocol / SAP — Statistical Analysis Plan: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/33/NCT03219333/SAP_001.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Rosenberg JE, O'Donnell PH, Balar AV, et al. "Pivotal Trial of Enfortumab Vedotin in Urothelial Carcinoma After Platinum and Anti-Programmed Death 1/Programmed Death Ligand 1 Therapy." *J Clin Oncol.* 2019;37(29):2592-2600. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.19.01140), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31356140/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Pivotal%20Trial%20of%20Enfortumab%20Vedotin%20in%20Urothelial%20Carcinoma)

**Other resources**

- Astellas/Seattle Genetics' general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for EV-201; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for this trial.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held; FDA's review states the BLA "was not presented to an advisory committee because the benefit-risk profile demonstrated for enfortumab is clearly favorable for its proposed use. No controversial issues were identified that would necessitate an advisory committee meeting."
- Postmarketing requirement: verification of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial was required to support conversion from accelerated to regular approval; the randomized EV-301 trial (enfortumab vedotin vs. chemotherapy) subsequently served this role and supported full approval in 2021.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, EV-201 (SGN22E-001) Statistical Analysis Plan v4, 17-SEP-2020, §2.1 Primary Objectives]* — "To determine the antitumor activity of single-agent enfortumab vedotin as measured by confirmed objective response rate (ORR) in patients with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer who have previously received systemic therapy with a CPI and either received platinum-containing chemotherapy or are platinum-naïve and cisplatin-ineligible."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.1 Primary Endpoint]* — "The primary efficacy endpoint of this study is ORR (confirmed complete response [CR] or partial response [PR] per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors [RECIST] Version 1.1) as determined by an independent review facility (IRF)."

*[verbatim, same source, §6.2 Determination of Sample Size]* — "The study is designed to estimate the confirmed ORR in the full analysis set and to detect an improvement in the ORR compared with a historical 10% response rate. The primary efficacy hypothesis is H0: ORR ≤10% vs. Ha: ORR >10%... Using the estimate of approximately 100 subjects in Cohort 1, the study will have 98% power to detect a 15% increase in ORR from 10% to 25%, and 81% power to detect a 10% increase in ORR from 10% to 20%, at one-sided significance level of 0.025, based on exact methods using EAST®, Version 6.0, by Cytel Inc."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "The two-sided 95% exact CI using the Clopper-Pearson method will be calculated for the response rates where applicable (e.g., ORR) (Clopper 1934)."

*[verbatim, same source, §6.3 Randomization and Blinding]* — "This is a single-arm, open-label study. No randomization or blinding will be used."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761137, Reference ID 4536389, Study Endpoints]* — "The primary endpoint for this study was confirmed ORR, defined as the proportion of subjects who achieved a confirmed CR or PR as assessed by a BICR using RECIST Version 1.1. This endpoint was chosen because this is a single arm study and confirmed ORR is a direct measure of anti-tumor activity... Prior to protocol finalization, the confirmed ORR primary endpoint was discussed with FDA on 21 April 2017 (Face-to-Face Type B EOP1 Meeting), and there was agreement that the confirmed ORR may predict clinical benefit and be an acceptable endpoint for accelerated approval pending review of the data."

*[verbatim, same source, Evidence of Effectiveness]* — "Evidence of effectiveness was obtained from pivotal Study EV-201, Cohort 1 which included 125 subjects with locally advanced or metastatic UC who received prior treatment with a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor and a platinum-based chemotherapy. Efficacy was established based upon confirmed ORR by blinded independent central review (BICR). The ORR was 44% (55/125 subjects; 95% CI: 35.1, 53.2)."

*[verbatim, same source, §9 Advisory Committee Meeting]* — "This BLA was not presented to an advisory committee because the benefit-risk profile demonstrated for enfortumab is clearly favorable for its proposed use. No controversial issues were identified that would necessitate an advisory committee meeting."

Notably, this is one of the cleaner accelerated-approval SAPs in this batch: the sponsor's posted SAP is genuinely detailed and internally consistent with the FDA review's description, and — unlike selinexor in this same batch — the confirmed-ORR endpoint's regulatory acceptability was explicitly negotiated and agreed with FDA in a pre-specified End-of-Phase-1 meeting well before the pivotal data were generated, rather than being contested after the fact at an advisory committee.
