### 103. fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki (Enhertu) — BLA 761139

**Sponsor:** Daiichi Sankyo, Inc. (co-developed with AstraZeneca)

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer who have received two or more prior anti-HER2-based regimens in the metastatic setting — approved under accelerated approval based on response rate

**Approval date:** December 20, 2019

**Pivotal trial:** DESTINY-Breast01 (Study DS8201-A-U201), NCT03248492

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label, multi-part trial (Part 1 dose-finding, Part 2a/2b dose-expansion at the recommended Phase 2 dose) supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H/21 CFR 314.510, independent adjudication committee established specifically for a drug-class safety signal (interstitial lung disease) rather than for the efficacy endpoint
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR, primary — confirmed CR or PR per RECIST 1.1 by independent central imaging review), duration of response, disease control rate, clinical benefit rate, progression-free survival, overall survival (all secondary/descriptive), investigator-assessed ORR (supportive)
- *Primary analysis:* two-sided 95% exact confidence interval around ORR, calculated in the Response Evaluable Set (all subjects who received the recommended Phase 2 dose in Part 1 and Part 2a); design-stage sample-size justification based on the binomial distribution (not a formal hypothesis test against a fixed null, but a precision/CI-width target)
- *Multiplicity:* not applicable — single formal primary endpoint, no comparative or multi-endpoint hypothesis test in a single-arm design
- *Missing data/bias:* not applicable in the randomized-trial sense (no censoring/crossover comparator issue); a dedicated, independent Interstitial Lung Disease (ILD) Adjudication Committee was established to centrally and blindly adjudicate all suspected ILD/pneumonitis cases across the development program, given the emerging severity of this safety signal (adjudicated ILD occurred in 9.4% of patients, with fatal outcomes in 2.6%)
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval (Subpart H) based on ORR as a surrogate reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit; boxed warning added for interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis and for embryo-fetal toxicity; no REMS was required; FDA determined no advisory committee meeting was necessary for this BLA

**Trial design & endpoints**

- DESTINY-Breast01 (DS8201-A-U201): single-arm, open-label, multicenter, multi-part Phase 1/2 trial of trastuzumab deruxtecan (DS-8201a) in patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer previously treated with T-DM1 (ado-trastuzumab emtansine); Part 1 was a dose-finding phase across multiple dose levels, Part 2a/2b expanded enrollment at the selected recommended Phase 2 dose (5.4 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks)
- Primary endpoint: ORR (proportion of subjects achieving a best overall response of CR or PR, confirmed) as assessed by an independent central imaging facility per RECIST 1.1, analyzed in the Response Evaluable Set (all subjects who initially received the recommended Phase 2 dose in Part 1 and Part 2a)
- Planned sample size was approximately 230 subjects overall; a subset of 150 subjects (50 from the optimal Part 1 dose level plus 100 from Part 2a) was calculated to yield an ORR estimate with a 95% CI within ±10 percentage points, with a 98.2% probability that the CI's lower bound would exceed 20% and a 91.6% probability that the observed ORR would be ≥30%, assuming a true ORR of 35% (probabilities derived from the binomial distribution, not a randomized power calculation)
- Secondary endpoints: duration of response, best percent change in sum of longest diameters, disease control rate (CR+PR+SD), clinical benefit rate (CR+PR+SD≥6 months), PFS, OS, and investigator-assessed ORR, each summarized descriptively (Kaplan-Meier/Brookmeyer-Crowley methods for time-to-event medians); extensive exploratory subgroup analyses were pre-specified (hormone-receptor status, prior pertuzumab, renal/hepatic impairment, brain metastases, age, race, region, ECOG PS, etc.), explicitly flagged in the protocol as exploratory due to small subgroup sample sizes
- Results: confirmed ORR was 60.3% (95% CI 52.9-67.4%; 4.3% complete response, 56.0% partial response), median duration of response 14.8 months
- Interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis emerged as the central safety issue: an independent ILD Adjudication Committee reviewed all suspected cases across the program; adjudicated drug-related ILD occurred in 9.4% of patients, with fatal ILD/pneumonitis outcomes in 6 patients (2.6%) — leading FDA to require a boxed warning for ILD (and separately for embryo-fetal toxicity) rather than a REMS

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2019/761139Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2019/761139Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (BLA 761139) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/761139Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (DESTINY-Breast01) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03248492 (combined Study Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan, Version 5.0, 26-APR-2019, posted in the Documents tab)
- Protocol / SAP — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/92/NCT03248492/Prot_SAP_000.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Modi S, Saura C, Yamashita T, et al. "Trastuzumab Deruxtecan in Previously Treated HER2-Positive Breast Cancer." *N Engl J Med.* 2020;382(7):610-621. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1914510), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31825192/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Trastuzumab%20Deruxtecan%20in%20Previously%20Treated%20HER2-Positive%20Breast%20Cancer)

**Other resources**

- Daiichi Sankyo/AstraZeneca's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for DESTINY-Breast01; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for this trial.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held; the review states plainly, "No advisory committee discussion or consultations external to the FDA were deemed necessary for this BLA application."
- Postmarketing requirement: verification of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial was required for conversion from accelerated to regular approval; the randomized DESTINY-Breast03 trial (trastuzumab deruxtecan vs. T-DM1) subsequently served this role and supported full approval in 2022.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, DESTINY-Breast01 (DS8201-A-U201) Protocol/SAP v5.0, 26-APR-2019, Synopsis]* — "To determine the objective response rate (ORR) of DS-8201a in [subjects with HER2-positive, unresectable and/or metastatic breast cancer previously treated with T-DM1]."

*[verbatim, same source, §11.4.1.1 Primary Efficacy Analysis]* — "The primary endpoint is ORR (the proportion of subjects who achieved a best overall response of CR or partial response [PR]). Tumor responses will be assessed by an independent central imaging facility based on RECIST version 1.1. The primary efficacy analysis will be performed for all subjects who initially received the RP2D of DS-8201a in Part 1 and Part 2a of the Response Evaluable Set. Confirmation of CR/PR is required for this study. The estimate of ORR and its two-sided 95% exact confidence intervals (CI) will be provided."

*[verbatim, same source, §11.6 Sample Size Determination]* — "The sample size of approximately 230 subjects was chosen to further confirm the safety profile and secure adequate accuracy to determine ORR of DS-8201a. A sample size of 150 subjects (50 subjects from Part 1 who receive the optimal dose level and 100 subjects from Part 2a) provides ORR with 95% CI within plus or minus 10% of the ORR. The probabilities of observing the lower bound of the 95% CI > 20% and ORR ≥ 30% are 98.2% and 91.6% under the expected ORR 35%, respectively. The probability values for the sample size are derived based on binomial distribution using SAS® version 9.3 or higher."

*[verbatim, same source, §11.7 Statistical Analysis Process]* — "To preserve the integrity of the statistical analysis and clinical study conclusions, the SAP will be finalized prior to database lock."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761139, Recommendation on Regulatory Action]* — "The ORR was 60.3% (95% CI: 52.9, 67.4), with a 4.3% complete response rate and a 56% partial response rate. Median DOR was 14.8 [months]... Therefore, the FDA review team recommends granting accelerated approval to ENHERTU (fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan)."

*[verbatim, same source, ILD safety discussion]* — "ILD/pneumonitis is an important safety signal related to fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan. Of the [patients treated with] fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan, ILD (adjudicated by the independent ILD committee) occurred in 9.4% of patients. Fatal outcomes due to ILD and/or pneumonitis occurred in 6 (2.6%) patients treated with fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan. The prescribing information includes a Boxed Warning to advise health professionals of the risk of interstitial lung disease (ILD)."

*[verbatim, same source, §9 Advisory Committee Meeting]* — "No advisory committee discussion or consultations external to the FDA were deemed necessary for this BLA application."

Like enfortumab vedotin in this same batch, this is a comparatively clean single-arm accelerated approval with a genuinely posted sponsor protocol/SAP and a large, clearly favorable ORR (60.3%) — the principal reviewable tension here is not endpoint validity but drug safety: FDA's review devotes substantial attention to a dedicated independent adjudication process for a serious, sometimes-fatal class safety signal (ILD) that emerged during the program and directly shaped the boxed-warning labeling decision.

### 104. avapritinib (Ayvakit) — NDA 212608

**Sponsor:** Blueprint Medicines Corporation

**Indication approved:** Adults with unresectable or metastatic gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) harboring a platelet-derived growth factor receptor alpha (PDGFRA) exon 18 mutation, including PDGFRA D842V mutations — approved under accelerated approval based on response rate

**Approval date:** January 9, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** NAVIGATOR (Study BLU-285-1101), NCT02508532

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label, multi-part, multi-cohort (Part 1 dose-escalation, Part 2 dose-expansion with molecularly-defined groups) trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H/21 CFR 314.510, biomarker-selected/enriched population (PDGFRA exon 18-mutant GIST, predominantly D842V), sample-size logic based on three separately powered Part 2 expansion groups defined by mutation status and prior therapy line
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR, primary — confirmed CR or PR by central radiology per modified RECIST 1.1 [mRECIST 1.1]), duration of response (key secondary), investigator-assessed ORR and Choi-criteria response (supportive/sensitivity analyses)
- *Primary analysis:* two-sided 95% exact (Clopper-Pearson) confidence interval around ORR in the Safety Population; per-group design-stage one-sided exact binomial tests (e.g., D842V group: H0 ORR≤10% vs. Ha ORR≥35%, 90% power, 2-sided type I error 0.05)
- *Multiplicity:* not applicable — no formal multi-endpoint hypothesis test; each Part 2 expansion group (D842V, non-D842V 3rd-line+, non-D842V 2nd-line) was analyzed and reported separately rather than combined into one family-wise-controlled test
- *Missing data/bias:* not applicable in the randomized-trial sense (no censoring/crossover comparator issue); duration-of-response censoring rules were pre-specified per both FDA (2007 Guidance for Cancer Trial Endpoints) and EMA conventions, with the FDA rule set as primary and EMA rules as a sensitivity analysis
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval (Subpart H) based on ORR as a surrogate reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit; extrapolation of efficacy across a related molecular subgroup — the approved indication (any PDGFRA exon 18 mutation) is broader than the trial's primary evidentiary population (predominantly D842V-mutant patients), extrapolated by FDA to the small number of non-D842V exon 18 patients based on disease-biology rationale and a supportive 40% ORR in just 5 non-D842V patients; no FDA advisory committee meeting was held; a boxed warning for intracranial hemorrhage was required, and cognitive impairment was flagged as a frequent CNS-related adverse effect

**Trial design & endpoints**

- NAVIGATOR (BLU-285-1101): single-arm, open-label, multicenter, multi-part Phase 1 trial of avapritinib in patients with unresectable or metastatic GIST and other advanced solid tumors; Part 1 was dose-escalation to determine the MTD/RP2D, Part 2 was dose-expansion across three pre-specified groups — Group 1: non-D842V GIST patients who had progressed on ≥3 prior lines including imatinib (planned n=100), Group 2: GIST patients with a PDGFRA D842V mutation regardless of prior line (planned n=31, targeting up to 35), Group 3: non-D842V GIST patients progressing after imatinib as the sole prior line (planned n=50)
- Primary endpoint: ORR, defined as the proportion of patients with a confirmed (CR/PR at ≥2 consecutive assessments with no intervening progression) best overall response of CR or PR, assessed primarily by central radiology per mRECIST 1.1 (investigator assessment and central Choi-criteria assessment were supportive only)
- Sample-size/power logic (Group 2/D842V, the approval-relevant cohort): a sample size of 31 D842V patients was designed to test H0: ORR≤10% vs. Ha: ORR≥35% using an exact binomial test with 90% power at 2-sided type I error 0.05; an observed ORR ≥26% in 31 patients would yield an exact 95% CI with a lower bound exceeding 10% — analogous logic (differing null/alternative rates) applied to Groups 1 and 3
- Secondary endpoint (duration of response): time from first documented CR/PR to first documented progression or death, censored per FDA (2007) Guidance for Cancer Trial Endpoints as the primary censoring convention, with EMA 2017 guideline-based censoring as a sensitivity analysis; summarized via Kaplan-Meier median and 25th/75th percentiles, with Greenwood's-formula standard errors for landmark timepoint estimates
- Efficacy results supporting approval: among 43 evaluable patients with a PDGFRA exon 18 mutation (38 with D842V), ORR was 84% (95% CI 69-93%) overall and 89% (95% CI 75-97%) in the D842V subset, with median duration of response not reached and 61% of exon-18 responders maintaining response ≥6 months; in the 5 patients with non-D842V exon 18 mutations, ORR was 40%
- Safety: cognitive impairment occurred in 41% of patients overall (Grade ≥3 in 3.6%); avapritinib also carried a risk of intracranial hemorrhage, leading to a boxed warning

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2020/212608Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2020/212608s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 4543562, NDA 212608) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/212608Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (NAVIGATOR) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02508532 (Study Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan both posted in the Documents tab)
- Protocol / SAP — Study Protocol: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/32/NCT02508532/Prot_000.pdf; Statistical Analysis Plan: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/32/NCT02508532/SAP_001.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Heinrich MC, Jones RL, von Mehren M, et al. "Avapritinib in advanced PDGFRA D842V-mutant gastrointestinal stromal tumour (NAVIGATOR): a multicentre, open-label, phase 1 trial." *Lancet Oncol.* 2020;21(7):935-946. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(20)30269-2>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32615108/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Avapritinib%20in%20advanced%20PDGFRA%20D842V-mutant%20gastrointestinal%20stromal%20tumour%20NAVIGATOR)

**Other resources**

- Blueprint Medicines' general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for NAVIGATOR; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for this trial.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held; the review states, "This Application was not presented to the oncologic Drug Advisory Committee or any other external consultants."
- Postmarketing requirement: verification of clinical benefit was required for conversion from accelerated to regular approval; avapritinib was subsequently converted to regular approval for PDGFRA exon 18-mutant GIST based on continued follow-up data.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, NAVIGATOR (BLU-285-1101) Statistical Analysis Plan, §1.3 Sample Size Justification]* — "In Part 2 Group 2, a sample size of 31 D842V patients will allow testing the null hypothesis of ORR ≤10% versus the alternative hypothesis of ORR ≥35% using exact binomial test with 90% power assuming a 2-sided type I error rate of 0.05. An observed ORR of ≥26% in 31 patients will result in an exact binomial 95% CI with a lower bound greater than 10% (Table 1), which is clinically meaningful, and exceeds the ORR expected with available therapies (Cassier, 2012; Yoo, 2016). We target to enroll up to 35 D842V patients."

*[verbatim, same source, §4.6 Efficacy Analyses — Analysis of Primary Efficacy Endpoint]* — "The primary efficacy endpoint of ORR is defined as the proportion of patients with a confirmed (CR/PR for at least two assessments with no progression in between) best response of complete response (CR) or partial response (PR). The primary analysis of ORR will be assessed by central radiology per mRECIST 1.1. ORR will be estimated using frequency, percentage, and two-sided 95% CI based on the exact binomial distribution (Clopper-Pearson) for the Safety Population."

*[verbatim, same source, Analysis of Secondary Efficacy Endpoints — Duration of Response]* — "Complete censoring rules (both European Medicines Agency [EMA] and United States [US] Food and Drug Administration [FDA]) are specified in Table 4. The analysis will be primarily based on FDA Guidance for Cancer Trial Endpoints (FDA, 2007). The censoring rules based on the EMA Guideline on the evaluation of anticancer medicinal products in man will be used as sensitivity analysis (EMA, 2017)."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 212608, Reference ID 4543562]* — "Patients with unresectable or metastatic GIST harboring a PDGFRα exon 18 mutation were identified by local or central assessment using a PCR- or NGS-based assay. The assessment of efficacy was based on a total of 43 patients, including 38 patients with PDGFRα D842V mutations. The median duration of follow up for patients with PDGFRα exon 18 mutations was 10.6 months (range: 0.3 to 24.9 months). The ORR was 84% (95% CI: 69, 93) in patients with PDGFRα exon 18 mutations, and 89% (95% CI: 75, 97) in the subset with PDGFRα D842V mutations."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "In the 5 patients with non-D842V exon 18 mutations treated on the study, avapritinib yielded an ORR of 40%. After analyzing all available clinical and nonclinical data regarding the activity of avapritinib and of available therapies in patients with non-D842V exon 18 mutations, and considering disease biology, the review team has recommended that the indication be granted to patients with any PDGFRα exon 18 mutation, in line with [the D842V evidence]."

*[verbatim, same source, safety discussion]* — "The most frequent CNS effects were related to cognitive impairment, which occurred in 41% of patients, although only 3.6% of patients experienced Grade ≥ 3 cognitive impairment. Avapritinib also appears to carry a risk of intracranial hemorrhage."

*[verbatim, same source, §9 Advisory Committee Meeting]* — "This Application was not presented to the oncologic Drug Advisory Committee or any other external consultants."

This entry is a clear instance of the "extrapolation of efficacy across a related trial setting" regulatory pattern already catalogued in this taxonomy (previously seen with Rolapitant's MEC indication) — here applied at the molecular-subgroup level: FDA extended the labeled indication from the well-populated D842V evidentiary base (38 patients, 89% ORR) to the much thinner non-D842V exon-18 evidence (5 patients, 40% ORR) based on biological plausibility rather than a separately powered, statistically conclusive cohort for that subgroup.

### 105. tazemetostat (Tazverik) — NDA 211723

**Sponsor:** Epizyme, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adults and pediatric patients aged 16 years and older with metastatic or locally advanced epithelioid sarcoma not eligible for complete resection — approved under accelerated approval based on response rate

**Approval date:** January 23, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** Study EZH-202, Cohort 5 (epithelioid sarcoma), NCT02601950

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label, multi-cohort basket trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H/21 CFR 314.500, Green-Dahlberg two-stage design (a named variant of Simon's two-stage design) used for Cohort 5, with an unplanned mid-trial primary-endpoint reversal
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR, primary — confirmed CR or PR per RECIST 1.1), disease control rate (DCR, briefly the primary endpoint before being reverted to a secondary/supportive role), duration of response (elevated to most important secondary endpoint)
- *Primary analysis:* exact 95% binomial confidence interval for ORR/DCR point estimates in the Cohort 5 (and pooled Cohort 5+6) analysis populations
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Green-Dahlberg two-stage design with a futility stopping rule at the end of Stage 1 (15 subjects); Cohort 5's futility criterion was surpassed, and an Independent Data Monitoring Committee (IDMC) endorsed continuation into Stage 2 and a subsequent Cohort 5 Expansion
- *Missing data/bias:* not applicable in the randomized-trial sense (no censoring/crossover comparator issue); FDA explicitly noted the Applicant did not collect data on patients' pre-tazemetostat treatment-free/stable-disease intervals, which would have been needed to contextualize observed periods of stable disease against each patient's individual disease history
- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented mid-trial SAP amendment changing endpoint status not once but twice — Cohort 5's primary endpoint was ORR at trial start, was changed to DCR mid-trial (IDMC-endorsed, October 2016) after the Stage 1 futility criterion was surpassed, and was then changed back to ORR (with DOR elevated to key secondary) following a May 2017 meeting at FDA's specific request, because FDA had not agreed with DCR as the primary endpoint at a prior End-of-Phase-2 meeting; FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) met December 18, 2019 and voted 11-0 that benefits outweighed risks, but the clinical reviewer and Division Director's written conclusion explicitly disagreed with the committee, finding the Applicant had NOT presented substantial evidence of effectiveness — approval was granted regardless via the Office Director's override of that internal recommendation; boxed warning for secondary malignancies (a mechanistically-plausible, EZH2-inhibition-related class risk)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study EZH-202: open-label, multicenter, multi-cohort Phase 2 basket trial of tazemetostat monotherapy (starting at 800 mg BID) across several INI1-negative/EZH2-altered tumor types; relevant to this approval is Cohort 5 (epithelioid sarcoma, INI1-negative, relapsed/refractory or treatment-naive, metastatic or locally advanced, not eligible for complete resection), which enrolled 62 patients as the primary basis for approval, with supportive data from Cohort 6 (epithelioid sarcoma with mandatory tumor biopsy, added later to further explore immune-priming effects) and pooled Cohort 5+6 analyses
- Cohort 5 used a Green-Dahlberg two-stage design: Stage 1 enrolled the first 15 subjects with a pre-specified futility stopping rule (enrollment to continue only if evidence of activity was sufficient); the futility criterion was surpassed on October 4, 2016, and the IDMC endorsed continuation to Stage 2 (15 more subjects), after which a further Cohort 5 Expansion (30 more subjects) opened once the Stage 2 criterion was also surpassed
- Endpoint history for Cohort 5 is the central statistical story of this submission: the endpoint began as ORR, was changed mid-trial to DCR (CR+PR or SD maintained ≥32 weeks) on IDMC endorsement in October 2016, and was then changed back to ORR — with duration of response elevated to the most important secondary endpoint — following a May 2017 sponsor-FDA meeting, at FDA's specific request; FDA's review states this reflected FDA's position (from an earlier End-of-Phase-2 meeting) that it "did not agree with the proposed primary endpoint of disease control rate," while agreeing "that ORR may be an acceptable primary endpoint for accelerated approval if supported by an adequate characterization of durability of response," determined by blinded independent central review with ≥6 months follow-up from response onset
- Results: ORR in Cohort 5 was 15% (95% CI 7-26%); ORR in Cohort 6 was 11% (95% CI 4-25%); pooled Cohort 5+6 ORR was 13% (95% CI 7-21%) — FDA's review explicitly notes "the lower bound of the associated confidence interval implies that the true ORR may be as low as the single digits." Of 14 responders across Cohorts 5-6, 9 had responses >6 months and 4 had responses >12 months; median DOR was not estimable
- FDA's Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) met December 18, 2019 and voted 11-0 that the benefits of tazemetostat outweighed the risks in the proposed population — but the clinical reviewer's and Division Director's own written conclusions in the FDA review explicitly state they held "a minority view" opposing the committee, concluding the Applicant had "presented insufficient evidence of the effectiveness of tazemetostat to meet the regulatory standard for accelerated or regular approval"; the application was nonetheless approved at a higher sign-off level (Office Director), with a post-marketing requirement for additional ORR/DOR data collection in a shorter timeframe than the planned 8-10-year randomized confirmatory trial (a first-line randomized trial vs. doxorubicin-based chemotherapy, primary endpoint PFS) would take to read out
- Safety: secondary malignancies (including a case of an EZH2-related lymphoma seen in the broader tazemetostat development program) were treated as a mechanistically plausible, on-target risk of EZH2 inhibition and became a labeled boxed warning

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2020/211723Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2020/211723s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 4550626, NDA 211723) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/211723Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (EZH-202) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02601950 (Statistical Analysis Plan V3.0, 30-NOV-2022, posted in the Documents tab — a later/updated version of the SAP than the one used for the 2020 approval, since the trial continued with additional cohorts after approval)
- Protocol / SAP — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/50/NCT02601950/SAP_001.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Gounder M, Schöffski P, Jones RL, et al. "Tazemetostat in advanced epithelioid sarcoma with loss of INI1/SMARCB1: an international, open-label, phase 2 basket study." *Lancet Oncol.* 2020;21(11):1423-1432. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(20)30451-4>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33035459/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Tazemetostat%20in%20advanced%20epithelioid%20sarcoma%20with%20loss%20of%20INI1%2FSMARCB1)

**Other resources**

- Epizyme's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for EZH-202; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for this trial.
- FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting held December 18, 2019; voted 11-0 that the benefits of tazemetostat outweighed the risks for the proposed epithelioid sarcoma indication — notably, over the explicit written objection of FDA's own clinical reviewer and Division Director.
- Postmarketing requirement: a randomized, first-line confirmatory trial of tazemetostat (primary endpoint PFS) was required to verify clinical benefit, expected to read out over 8-10 years; in the interim, an additional 25 subjects were added to Cohort 6 (per the approval conditions) to further characterize ORR.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, EZH-202 Statistical Analysis Plan V3.0, Note: Changes to Cohorts]* — "For Cohort 5, the futility criterion was surpassed on 04-Oct. 2016. The IDMC endorsed continuing enrollment to Stage 2 completion. On 21-Oct. 2016, the IDMC endorsed a change in the primary endpoint for Cohort 5 from ORR to DCR (which includes subjects who achieve a confirmed response [CR+PR] or who maintain SD for at least 32 weeks). In Dec. 2016, after the Stage 2 DCR criterion was surpassed, enrollment was opened in the extension stage. In May 2017, Epizyme met with the FDA regarding future development plans for tazemetostat. Based on a specific request by FDA, with Amendment 5 the primary endpoint for Cohort 5 has been changed to ORR and duration of response in responding subjects has been elevated to the most important secondary endpoint."

*[verbatim, same source, Interim Analyses]* — "For each cohort (except Cohorts 6 and 8), a two-stage, Green-Dahlberg design was utilized with a stopping rule to allow for early termination at the end of Stage 1 if there was strong evidence of lack of efficacy... Cohort 1 (rhabdoid tumors), Cohort 3 (INI1-negative/EZH2 GOF mutation), and Cohort 5 (ES) continued into Stage 2, to enroll an additional 15 subjects each."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 211723, Reference ID 4550626, Summary of Presubmission Regulatory Activity]* — "On May 12, 2017, an End-of-Phase 2 (EOP2) meeting was held to obtain feedback on the acceptability of Trial EZH-301 to support an NDA submission and discuss the preliminary results of study EZH-202. Key FDA comments included: FDA did not agree with the proposed primary endpoint of disease control rate. FDA agreed that ORR may be an acceptable primary endpoint for accelerated approval if supported by an adequate characterization of durability of response. FDA stated that ORR should be determined by blinded independent review and that an application based on this endpoint should have a minimum follow up time of 6 months from the onset of response for responding patients."

*[verbatim, same source, Conclusions on the Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness]* — "This conclusion is based on the results of a single, open-label, single-arm cohort (Cohort 5) of a multi-center study (EZH-202) in patients INI1-negative, metastatic, relapsed or refractory epithelioid sarcoma that demonstrated an overall response rate (ORR) of 15% (95% CI: 7, 26). Supportive data from Cohort 6 and pooled efficacy data from Cohort 5 and 6 demonstrated similar results, with ORRs of 11% (95% CI: 4, 25) and 13% (95% CI: 7, 21), respectively. The lower bound of the associated confidence interval implies that the true ORR may be as low as the single digits."

*[verbatim, same source, Summary]* — "It is my conclusion, and that of the clinical reviewer, that the Applicant has presented insufficient evidence of the effectiveness of tazemetostat to meet the regulatory standard for accelerated or regular approval. As the ODAC voted 11-0 in favor of the opposite conclusion, I recognize that the clinical reviewer and I hold a minority view. If, after consideration of this by the Office of Oncologic Diseases, the application receives accelerated approval, we recommend that the Applicant be required to collect ORR and DOR data from additional patients to confirm and further describe the findings of Study EZH-202 in a shorter period of time than the 8-10 years expected for the randomized confirmatory trial to read out."

*[verbatim, same source, Office Director Comments]* — "After consideration of the FDA Review documents, selected documents submitted to the NDA, ODAC materials, discussions with the review team, and discussion at the December 18, 2019 ODAC, I conclude that the application for tazemetostat meets the statutory standards for marketing approval under 21 CFR 314, subpart H... for the following indication: treatment of adults and pediatric patients aged 16 years and older with metastatic or locally advanced epithelioid sarcoma not eligible for complete resection."

This is the most striking internal-disagreement case in this batch: the trial's primary endpoint was changed twice (ORR→DCR→ORR, the second change made at FDA's explicit request), and even after that resolution, FDA's own clinical reviewer and Division Director recorded in writing that they did not believe the data met the legal standard for either accelerated or regular approval — a conclusion at odds with the ODAC's unanimous 11-0 vote — yet the application was approved anyway at the Office Director level. Unlike selinexor (also in this batch, where FDA approved after ODAC voted to delay), here the internal FDA disagreement ran the opposite direction from the committee, and the drug was still approved.

### 106. Isatuximab-irfc (Sarclisa) — BLA 761113

**Sponsor:** Sanofi-Aventis U.S., LLC

**Indication approved:** In combination with pomalidomide and dexamethasone, for the treatment of adult patients with multiple myeloma who have received at least two prior therapies including lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor

**Approval date:** March 2, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** ICARIA-MM (Study EFC14335), NCT02990338

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial (1:1, isatuximab + pomalidomide + dexamethasone [IPd] vs. pomalidomide + dexamethasone [Pd]), event-driven trial (enrollment capped at ~300 patients or upon reaching the PFS analysis event target, whichever came first), randomization stratified by age (<75 vs. ≥75 years) and number of prior lines of therapy (2-3 vs. >3) via interactive response technology

- *Endpoints:* Progression-free survival (PFS) by IRC assessment per IMWG criteria — primary; objective response rate (ORR) — key secondary; overall survival (OS) — key secondary; duration of response (DoR), time to progression, clinical benefit rate, VGPR-or-better rate, minimal residual disease (MRD) rate, PFS in high-risk cytogenetic subgroup, patient-reported outcomes (EORTC QLQ-C30/QLQ-MY20, EQ-5D-5L) — additional secondary/exploratory, descriptive only

- *Primary analysis:* Stratified log-rank test (one-sided alpha 0.025) for PFS, Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified) for hazard ratio and 95% CI, Kaplan-Meier estimation with Brookmeyer-Crowley method (log-log transformation) for percentile CIs, Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test (stratified) for the ORR comparison, Exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval for response-rate estimates per arm

- *Multiplicity:* Closed testing procedure implemented as fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing at the one-sided 2.5% significance level (PFS → ORR → OS), with no multiplicity adjustment for other secondary or exploratory endpoints

- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Group-sequential design for OS, with a single planned interim OS analysis timed to coincide with the primary PFS analysis (at ~36% of the targeted 220 OS events) plus a final OS analysis, using an O'Brien-Fleming alpha-spending function; a protocol amendment (Amendment 6) made after the primary PFS/interim-OS analysis and reflected in SAP Version 3 (20-Oct-2020) added a second interim OS analysis at ~90% of events and updated the final-analysis boundary — this amendment post-dates the March 2020 approval

- *Missing data/bias:* Standard right-censoring at last valid disease assessment for PFS/TTP/DOR (censored before initiation of further anti-myeloma treatment or at data cut-off, whichever came first), Inverse Probability of Censoring Weighting (IPCW) sensitivity analysis adjusting OS for patient crossover/subsequent treatment with daratumumab, five pre-specified PFS sensitivity analyses varying censoring/event rules, FDA-flagged unadjusted (exploratory-only) subgroup interaction p-values

- *Regulatory:* Standard (non-accelerated) BLA approval under section 351(a) of the PHS Act based on a statistically significant, clinically meaningful PFS improvement (supported by ORR) in a randomized Phase 3 trial — not an accelerated-approval/surrogate-endpoint pathway; no FDA advisory committee (ODAC) meeting held ("Not Applicable" per the Multi-Discipline Review); OS was immature and not statistically significant at approval (interim HR 0.69, did not cross the pre-specified O'Brien-Fleming boundary), with final OS analysis required as a routine postmarketing commitment (PMC, not an accelerated-approval PMR) rather than a condition of approval

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ICARIA-MM (Study EFC14335): a prospective, multicenter, multinational, randomized, open-label, parallel-group, 2-arm Phase 3 trial in adults with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma who had received ≥2 prior lines of therapy including ≥2 consecutive cycles of lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor (bortezomib, carfilzomib, or ixazomib), and were refractory to (or intolerant of) that prior therapy, progressing on or within 60 days of its completion; 387 patients screened, 307 randomized 1:1 (154 IPd, 153 Pd) at 102 sites in 24 countries between January 10, 2017 and February 1, 2018, stratified by age (<75 vs. ≥75) and number of prior lines (2-3 vs. >3) via IRT; data cut-off for the primary analysis was October 11, 2018

- Primary endpoint: PFS (time from randomization to first IRC-determined disease progression per IMWG criteria or death from any cause), assessed by an Independent Response Committee; the primary analysis population was the intent-to-treat (ITT) population

- Key secondary endpoints (formally elevated for hierarchical alpha-controlled testing after PFS): ORR (IRC-assessed, IMWG criteria, sCR/CR/VGPR/PR) and OS; other secondary/exploratory endpoints (DOR, TTP, time to first/best response, VGPR-or-better rate, clinical benefit rate, PFS in the high-risk cytogenetic subgroup [del(17p), t(4;14), t(14;16)], MRD rate, safety, PK, immunogenicity, and health-related quality of life via EORTC QLQ-C30/QLQ-MY20 and EQ-5D-5L) were analyzed descriptively only, with any testing considered exploratory

- Sample size/power: 162 PFS events targeted for 90% power to detect a HR of 0.60 (median PFS improving from 4.0 to 6.67 months) using a one-sided log-rank test at alpha=0.025; 220 OS deaths targeted for 80% power to detect a HR of 0.685 (median OS 13.0 months in Pd, a 6-month improvement), with one planned interim OS analysis timed to the PFS analysis (~36% information) using an O'Brien-Fleming alpha-spending function; at the time of the final PFS analysis the critical value for the Wald test on the PFS hazard ratio was 0.734, and the final-analysis nominal one-sided significance level for OS (220 events) was calculated as approximately 0.02-0.024 (reported as 0.0200 in the sponsor's SAP v3 and as 0.0244 in the FDA review's restatement of the design, corresponding to a boundary HR of roughly 0.76)

- Statistical methods: primary PFS analysis via a stratified one-sided log-rank test (alpha=0.025) with Cox proportional-hazards HR/CI (stratified by the same IRT factors) and Kaplan-Meier estimation (Brookmeyer-Crowley CIs for percentiles); five pre-specified PFS sensitivity analyses (ignoring censoring for further anti-myeloma treatment; investigator-assessed response with and without symptomatic deterioration as an event; further-treatment-initiation as an event; assessment-schedule-adjusted censoring); a stratified CMH test for the ORR comparison with Clopper-Pearson exact CIs per arm; OS via a stratified one-sided log-rank test with an O'Brien-Fleming interim boundary, plus an IPCW sensitivity analysis adjusting OS for crossover to daratumumab-containing regimens; prespecified forest-plot subgroup analyses (Cox model with factor-by-treatment interaction tested at a 10% alpha, explicitly not multiplicity-adjusted); a stepwise multivariate Cox model (15% significance level for removal) used to screen for confounding prognostic-factor imbalances

- Results: median PFS 11.53 months (IPd) vs. 6.47 months (Pd), stratified HR 0.596 (95% CI 0.436-0.814), a 40.4% risk reduction, one-sided stratified log-rank p=0.0010 (FDA-computed two-sided p=0.001); ORR 60.4% (IPd) vs. 35.3% (Pd), one-sided stratified CMH p<0.0001; at the interim OS analysis (99 deaths observed, ~45% of the 220-event target), HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.46-1.02), stratified log-rank p=0.06 — not crossing the pre-specified O'Brien-Fleming boundary of 0.0016 at that information fraction, so OS was reported as immature/not statistically significant at approval, with the final OS analysis required as a postmarketing commitment

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter (BLA, Reference ID 4568826) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2020/761113Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2020/761113s000lbl.pdf

- FDA combined Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 4568595; no separate stand-alone Statistical Review, Clinical Review, or Summary Review is posted for this original BLA — Drugs@FDA lists only the combined Multi-Discipline Review) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/761113Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (Study EFC14335/ICARIA-MM) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02990338

- Protocol / SAP (sponsor-posted, genuine, but both as-posted versions post-date the March 2020 approval): Study Protocol (version dated 2020-11-26) — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/38/NCT02990338/Prot_002.pdf; Statistical Analysis Plan Version 3 (dated 20-Oct-2020) — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/38/NCT02990338/SAP_003.pdf

- Pivotal publication: Attal M, Richardson PG, Rajkumar SV, et al, for the ICARIA-MM study group. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(19)32556-5>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31735560/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Isatuximab%20plus%20pomalidomide%20and%20low-dose%20dexamethasone%20versus%20pomalidomide%20and%20low-dose%20dexamethasone%20in%20patients%20with%20relapsed%20and%20refractory%20multiple%20myeloma%20ICARIA-MM)

**Other resources**

- Sanofi participates in the Vivli data-sharing platform as a general sponsor policy; trial-specific IPD availability for Study EFC14335/ICARIA-MM was not individually confirmed.

- No FDA advisory committee (ODAC) meeting was held; the Multi-Discipline Review's dedicated section on advisory committee consultation states plainly "Not Applicable."

- Postmarketing requirements/commitments (per the approval letter): Required trial 3782-2 (505(o), submit a final interim report assessing infusion-related reactions in patients weighing ≥100 kg vs. <100 kg, using pooled data from several studies); Postmarketing Commitment 3782-3 (506B, submit the overall survival analysis and datasets with the final report of the ICARIA/EFC14335 trial "to provide additional long term efficacy data that may inform product labeling," originally scheduled for trial completion 06/2021 and final report 12/2021); Postmarketing Commitment 3782-4 (develop and validate an assay to detect isatuximab interference with M-protein assessment, to facilitate determination of complete response).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, sponsor Statistical Analysis Plan, SAR650984-EFC14335, Version 3, dated 20-Oct-2020, §1.1 Study Design and Randomization, p.7 — text recovered via OCR from a scanned/image-only PDF; no native text layer was present in the posted document, so this passage, while genuinely reproduced from the posted SAP, was not extracted directly from a text layer]* — "This is a prospective, multicenter, multinational, randomized, open-label, parallel group and 2-arm study evaluating the clinical benefit of isatuximab in combination with pomalidomide and low-dose dexamethasone as compared to pomalidomide and low-dose dexamethasone for the treatment of patients with refractory or relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma who have received at least two lines of therapy including lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor (bortezomib, carfilzomib or ixazomib) alone or in combination and have demonstrated disease progression on or within 60 days of completion of the last therapy."

- *[verbatim, same source (OCR), §1.2.1 Primary objectives, p.7]* — "The primary objective of this study is to demonstrate the benefit of IPd arm in the prolongation of PFS as compared to Pd arm in patients with refractory or relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma."

- *[verbatim, same source (OCR), §1.3 Determination of Sample Size, p.8]* — "The sample size calculation is based on the primary efficacy endpoint (ie, PFS)... Pd arm has a median PFS of 4.0 months. IPd arm will have 40% risk reduction in hazard rate in comparison to Pd arm. The targeted hazard ratio is 0.60... A log-rank test at a one-sided 2.5% significance level. Based on the above assumptions, a total of 162 PFS events are needed to achieve a 90% power for the study."

- *[verbatim, same source (OCR), §2.4.4.1 Analysis of primary efficacy endpoint(s), p.40]* — "Primary analysis will consist of PFS comparison between IPd group versus Pd group through a log-rank test procedure stratified by stratification factors as entered in the IRT (ie, age and number of previous lines of therapy) and using a 1-sided 0.025 alpha level. The cut-off date for the analysis of PFS is the actual date when the 162 events... have been observed... At the time of final PFS analysis, the critical value for the Wald test on PFS hazard ratio would be 0.734."

- *[verbatim, same source (OCR), §2.4.4.4 Multiplicity issues, p.46]* — "Hypothesis testing of the key secondary efficacy endpoints will be carried out. A closed test procedure will be used to control the type I error rate meaning that not further testing will be performed unless the significance level had been reached on PFS. The hierarchical procedure will be then carried out at the one-sided 2.5% significance level in the following order: ORR at the time of the primary analysis on PFS (first cut-off date). OS tested both at the time of the primary analysis on PFS (at about 36% information), and at the end of the study (final analysis on OS). No update of PFS or ORR as per IRC will be provided at the time of final OS analysis."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761113, Reference ID 4568595, "Statistical Analysis Plan and Amendments," p.92]* — "The primary analysis was a comparison of PFS based on IRC assessment in the IPd group versus the Pd group using a log rank test procedure stratified by stratification factors as entered in the IRT (ie, age and number of previous lines of therapy) and using a 1-sided 0.025 alpha level. The cut-off date for the analysis of PFS was the actual date when 162 events... were observed. At the time of final PFS analysis, the critical value for the Wald test on PFS HR would be 0.734."

- *[verbatim, same source, "Multiplicity," p.95]* — "In the Phase 3 study EFC14335, hypothesis testing of the key secondary efficacy endpoints was carried out. A closed testing procedure was used to control the Type I error rate meaning that no further testing was to be performed unless the significance level had been reached for PFS. The hierarchical procedure was then carried out at the 1-sided 2.5% significance level in the following order: ORR at the time of the primary analysis on PFS (first cut-off date). OS tested both at the time of the primary analysis on PFS (at about 36% information), and at the end of the study (final analysis on OS)."

- *[verbatim, same source, FDA's statistical assessment, pp.102-103]* — "The portions of the Assessment Aid completed by the Applicant are ambiguous in reporting the one-sided level of significance and p-values. The FDA reports all p-values at the two-sided level of significance. In general, to get the equivalent two-sided value, the estimate should be multiplied by two. Study EFC14335 was designed to have approximately 90% power to detect a hazard ratio of 0.60 (median PFS 6.67 months versus 4 months) with a two-sided type I error of 5%... There was one planned interim analysis for OS timed to coincide with the analysis of PFS and using the O'Brien Fleming boundary condition for controlling of the type I error. A hierarchical testing strategy was employed in which PFS was tested first followed by the key secondary endpoint of ORR and then OS. No multiplicity adjustments were made for other secondary or exploratory endpoints."

- *[verbatim, same source, p.115]* — "The FDA agrees with the applicant's results presented in Table 15 and notes that the PFS comparison at the two through 16-month time points is arbitrary and was not pre-specified. No conclusions should be drawn, nor any efficacy claims made, based upon differences in PFS at these two-month time-point intervals. Also, the FDA notes that the corresponding two-sided p-value is 0.001."

- *[verbatim, same source, p.119]* — "The FDA agrees with the applicant's subgroup analyses presented in Table 16 and notes that the p-values have not been adjusted for multiplicity. No alpha has been allocated to the subgroup analyses, therefore, all results should be considered exploratory. There were insufficient African American patients for any comparative analyses."

- *[verbatim, same source, pp.126-127]* — "The FDA agrees that the OS data at the first interim analysis of OS are immature. There was a total of 99 deaths, 43 (28%) on IPd and 56 (37%) on the Pd arm. No detriment in OS with isatuximab is apparent at this time... The estimated HR at the interim OS analysis is 0.69 (95% CI: 0.46,1.02, stratified log-rank p-value=0.06). The result was not statistically significant when compared to the 0.0016 significance level (calculated from the O'Brien-Fleming alpha spending function at 45% of the targeted 220 events). The final report of OS is expected in 2021 per Post marketing Commitment (PMC) #1."

- *[verbatim, same source, "9 Advisory Committee Meeting and Other External Consultations," p.200]* — "The FDA's Assessment: Not Applicable."

- *[verbatim, FDA Approval Letter, BLA 761113, Reference ID 4568826]* — "SARCLISA is indicated in combination with pomalidomide and dexamethasone, for the treatment of adult patients with multiple myeloma who have received at least two prior therapies including lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor."... "3782-3 Submit the overall survival analysis and datasets with the final report for clinical trial (ICARIA)... to provide additional long term efficacy data that may inform product labeling."

Note on sourcing: the SAP and Protocol documents posted on ClinicalTrials.gov are scanned/image-only PDFs (no extractable text layer); the SAP excerpts above were recovered via OCR (Tesseract) rather than direct text extraction, and cross-checked against the FDA Multi-Discipline Review's independent restatement of the same design elements (sample size, critical value, hierarchical order) wherever both sources cover the same content — the two match verbatim on every checked figure (162 events, HR 0.734 critical value, one-sided 2.5% alpha, hierarchical PFS→ORR→OS order), so no inference was needed. Both posted documents are later versions (Protocol dated 2020-11-26, SAP Version 3 dated 2020-10-20) than the version operative at the March 2020 approval; SAP Version 3 itself documents that it added a second OS interim analysis via a post-primary-analysis protocol amendment, a change that post-dates approval and does not affect the primary PFS analysis or the interim OS analysis described in the FDA review. This is a case, like polatuzumab vedotin/BLA 761121 in this census, where the only publicly posted protocol/SAP text is a later amended version, but the portions relevant to the approved analysis remain consistent with the FDA review's independent account.

### 107. Selumetinib (Koselugo) — NDA 213756

**Sponsor:** AstraZeneca Pharmaceuticals LP (NDA applicant); the pivotal trial itself (SPRINT) was designed, sponsored, and conducted by the National Cancer Institute (NCI) Pediatric Oncology Branch (POB) under the NCI Cancer Therapy Evaluation Program (CTEP) — AstraZeneca was not the trial sponsor and submitted the NDA based on NCI's trial data, per FDA's Multi-Discipline Review

**Indication approved:** Treatment of pediatric patients 2 years of age and older with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) who have symptomatic, inoperable plexiform neurofibromas (PN)

**Approval date:** April 10, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** SPRINT Phase II Stratum 1 (Study 11-C-0161 / CTEP #8799), NCT01362803

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial — an NCI-designed and NCI-run academic Phase II study (not an industry-designed registration trial) later used by AstraZeneca as the sole pivotal basis for its NDA; external natural-history/historical-control comparison used descriptively only, not for formal statistical testing
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR)/duration of response (DoR) — ORR (major efficacy outcome measure: complete response [disappearance of target PN] or confirmed partial response [≥20% PN volume reduction, confirmed within 3-6 months], per REiNS volumetric-MRI criteria), DoR (additional efficacy outcome measure); progression-free survival, time to progression, and time to response were collected but treated by FDA as exploratory/uninterpretable without a comparator arm
- *Primary analysis:* descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (point estimate + CI, no formal hypothesis test) — no pre-specified null response-rate threshold or formal power calculation; exact (Clopper-Pearson) binomial confidence interval for ORR; Kaplan-Meier estimation for DoR; a dual-reader structure atypical for single-arm oncology trials — the primary ORR rested on a single NCI central reviewer (also a SPRINT investigator), with a separately contracted blinded independent central review (ICR) conducted only as a pre-specified sensitivity analysis, not the primary assessment
- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation for missing binary/diary efficacy data, adapted here — full analysis set (FAS) patients with no imaging assessments were counted as non-responders; FDA documented a large (66% vs. 44%) divergence between the NCI central reviewer's ORR and the independent central review's ORR, attributing it in part to 6 patients whose observed PN shrinkage (-19.2% to -19.9%) narrowly missed the pre-specified 20% partial-response threshold
- *Regulatory:* regular approval grounded in durable-ORR-as-direct-clinical-benefit (single-arm trial) — regular approval under 21 CFR 314.126(a)(b)/FDCA §505(b)(1), not accelerated approval/Subpart H, with no post-marketing efficacy-confirmatory-trial requirement (postmarketing requirements are safety-only: long-term growth/development and MEK-class-toxicity follow-up, plus a food-effect PK study); Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher awarded; no FDA Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- SPRINT Phase II Stratum 1 was an open-label, single-arm, multicenter trial conducted at 4 US sites, coordinated by the NCI POB under CTEP sponsorship; it enrolled 50 pediatric patients (ages 2-18, later described in the label as median age 10.2 years, range 3.5-17.4) with NF1 and inoperable, PN-related-morbid plexiform neurofibromas, who received selumetinib 25 mg/m2 orally twice daily continuously until progression or intolerable toxicity; enrollment of 50 patients for Stratum 1 (plus 25 for a separate, less-mature Stratum 2 not included in this NDA) was set as a feasibility-driven target for this ultra-rare pediatric population rather than derived from a formal statistical power calculation
- Primary/major efficacy outcome measure: ORR (complete response, defined as disappearance of the target PN, or confirmed partial response, defined as ≥20% reduction in target PN volume confirmed at a subsequent assessment within 3-6 months), assessed via centrally read volumetric MRI per REiNS criteria, on the full analysis set (FAS, all patients who received ≥1 dose); additional efficacy outcome measure: DoR (Kaplan-Meier, median and ≥12-month landmark)
- A companion prospective NCI POB NF1 Natural History Study (real-world PN growth rates in an age-matched population) and the placebo arm of a separate NCI-sponsored crossover trial of tipifarnib (Study 01-C-0222, N=29 in the relevant phase) were submitted as external control data for PN growth rate and PFS; FDA explicitly declined to treat these as formal comparative analyses, calling them "exploratory" and "supportive but inadequate for any comparative analyses" given unmeasured cross-study heterogeneity, while accepting that the natural history data showed spontaneous PN regression is uncommon (supporting causal attribution of observed SPRINT responses to the drug)
- Results at the primary-analysis data cutoff (June 29, 2018; 50 patients treated for a median 802 days): confirmed ORR per NCI central review 66% (33/50; 95% CI 51-79%), all confirmed partial responses (no complete responses); among the 33 NCI-assessed responders, median DoR not reached and 82% (27/33) had DoR ≥12 months; a separately contracted blinded independent central review (ICR) of the same volumetric MRI data returned a materially lower ORR of 44% (22/50; 95% CI 30-59%), with 59% (13/22) of ICR-assessed responders reaching DoR ≥12 months — FDA attributed part of the gap to 6 patients whose best response (-19.2% to -19.9% PN shrinkage) fell just short of the 20% threshold under one reader's measurements; the approved label reports the higher NCI-review ORR (66%) as the headline Table 8 result, with the ICR's 44% disclosed in accompanying label text
- Supportive (non-pivotal) response data came from SPRINT Phase I (24 patients, NCI-review ORR 67%, 95% CI 45-84%) and SPRINT Phase II Stratum 2 (25 patients, ORR 68%, 95% CI 47-85%); FDA agreed with the Applicant's decision not to pool these cohorts with the Stratum 1 primary analysis population, given differences in trial design and patient characteristics, but required them to be presented as supportive efficacy data in the Summary of Clinical Efficacy
- Clinical outcome assessments (COAs: pain [NRS-11/PII], motor function, airway function [AHI, spirometry], bladder/bowel function, visual function, disfigurement photography, Global Impression of Change, PedsQL, 6-minute walk test) were analyzed descriptively and via mixed-model repeated measures (MMRM), correlated with PN volume change via Spearman rank correlation, and individual patient reviews (IPRs) were submitted narratively; FDA considered the COA endpoints exploratory given the open-label design (risk of assessment-favoring bias from unblinded patients/caregivers/investigators), small subgroup sample sizes, and instrument limitations, but treated a general association between tumor shrinkage and durable clinical-outcome improvement as supportive of direct clinical benefit
- The sponsor's Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) went through 5 editions (Edition 1.0, March 1, 2017, through Edition 5.0, January 21, 2019), with amendments adding formal ICR analysis (at FDA's request), an inter-reader variability/measurement-error analysis, and expanded COA summaries; FDA's review states the SAP "was agreed upon and finalized prior to the conduct of any efficacy analysis and locking of the database," and separately states it "agrees with the definition of the primary endpoint, primary analysis population, and statistical method used for the analysis of the primary endpoint"
- Postmarketing requirements are safety-focused, not an efficacy-confirmatory trial: (1) long-term growth-and-development follow-up (≥7 years, including height/weight/Tanner staging) in SPRINT and other selumetinib studies; (2) long-term (≥7-year) follow-up characterizing specific MEK-class toxicities (ocular, cardiac, muscle, GI, dermatologic); (3) a dedicated pediatric PK trial to characterize the food effect on selumetinib exposure with the marketed capsule

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2020/213756Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2020/213756s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 4589744; Statistical Reviewer Arup Sinha, PhD; Statistical Team Leader Pallavi Mishra-Kalyani, PhD; Clinical Reviewer Denise Casey, MD; Clinical Team Leader Suzanne Demko, PA-C) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/213756Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01362803 (lead sponsor National Cancer Institute (NCI); no protocol/SAP posted — confirmed via the CT.gov API v2 study record, which returns no `documentSection` field)
- Protocol / SAP (posted): none found on ClinicalTrials.gov; the genuine sponsor/NCI SAP text is instead reproduced within the FDA Multi-Discipline Review's "Applicant's Description" of the Statistical Analysis Plan and Amendments (see excerpts below)
- Pivotal publication: Gross AM, Wolters PL, Dombi E, Baldwin A, Whitcomb P, Fisher MJ, Weiss B, Kim A, Bornhorst M, Shah AC, Martin S, Roderick MC, Pichard DC, Carbonell A, Paul SM, Therrien J, Kapustina O, Heisey K, Clapp DW, Zhang C, Peer CJ, Figg WD, Smith M, Glod J, Blakeley JO, Steinberg SM, Venzon DJ, Doyle LA, Widemann BC. "Selumetinib in Children with Inoperable Plexiform Neurofibromas." *N Engl J Med.* 2020;382(15):1430-1442. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1912735), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32187457/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Selumetinib%20in%20Children%20with%20Inoperable%20Plexiform%20Neurofibromas)

**Other resources**

- AstraZeneca participates generally in the Vivli data-sharing platform for its own sponsored trials, but SPRINT was an NCI-sponsored, not an AstraZeneca-sponsored, trial; trial-specific individual patient data (IPD) availability for SPRINT via Vivli, YODA, or another platform was not individually confirmed, and NCI/NIH-run trials of this kind typically follow NIH data-sharing policy rather than a commercial sponsor's IPD-sharing program.
- No FDA Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held. Per the FDA Multi-Discipline Review, §9: "The Division did not obtain the advice of the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee (ODAC) or Special Government Employees (SGEs) for this NDA. There were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion."
- Selumetinib was granted Orphan Drug Designation for NF1 (February 14, 2018) and Breakthrough Therapy Designation (March 29, 2019); the approval also carried a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher (PRV), per the FDA approval letter, awarded under FDCA §529.
- FDA's review documents an unusually long, cooperative pre-NDA regulatory history between FDA, the NCI, and AstraZeneca dating to a September 8, 2014 pre-IND meeting, in which FDA laid out in advance the evidentiary bar a single-arm trial would need to clear (unequivocal, durable treatment effect on PN-related morbidity, corroborated by an adequately characterized natural history of the disease) before the Phase II expansion cohort that became SPRINT Stratum 1 was even added to the protocol.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation, NDA 213756, Reference ID 4589744, Executive Summary, p.19-20]* — "The recommendation to approve selumetinib is based on results from a single trial, entitled, 'A Phase I/II Study of the Mitogen Activated Protein Kinase Kinase (MEK) 1 Inhibitor Selumetinib (AZD6244; HYD Sulfate) in Children with Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1) and Inoperable Plexiform Neurofibromas (PN)' (SPRINT), specifically from Phase II, Stratum 1 of the trial. SPRINT was an open-label, single arm, multi-center trial conducted by the National Cancer Institute (NCI) Pediatric Oncology Branch (POB)."

*[verbatim, same source, Table 1 Major Regulatory Milestones, p.33, re: Type C meeting of November 2, 2017]* — "Agreement that data from SPRINT Phase II Stratum 1, with supportive data from SPRINT Phase I and the NCI POB NF1 Natural History study, may support regular approval of selumetinib. Agreement to perform independent review of the volumetric MRIs as a sensitivity analysis."

*[verbatim, same source, re: Type B Pre-IND meeting, September 8, 2014, p.35]* — "FDA stated that given the rarity of NF1 PN, lack of treatment alternatives, and the debilitating complications arising from progressive PN, and provided that the natural history of disease has been adequately established through the NCI natural history study, a single-arm trial could support an application seeking marketing approval if the study demonstrates unequivocal evidence of an important treatment effect that results in an improvement in PN-related functional impairment or other well-characterized signs or symptoms of progressive PN disease. The FDA emphasized that the results of the trial must also demonstrate that treatment responses are sufficiently durable, considering the long-term survival of patients with NF1 PN."

*[verbatim, same source, Statistical Analysis Plan and Amendments — Applicant's Description, p.125-127]* — "The SAP was agreed upon and finalized prior to the conduct of any efficacy analysis and locking of the database. Ad hoc analyses were added following the database lock to support the clinical interpretation."... "The primary efficacy endpoint of the study was ORR based on the NCI POB central analysis of volumetric MRI of target PN."... "FAS patients with no imaging assessments were counted as non-responders. ORR was presented with corresponding 2-sided exact 95% CIs based on the Clopper-Pearson method (Clopper and Pearson 1934)."... "A sensitivity analysis of the ORR based on the ICR of the imaging data was also performed. Supplementary analyses were performed to derive ORR based on all available volumetric MRI scans."

*[verbatim, same source, FDA's Assessment, p.125]* — "The FDA agreed with plan to assess ORR by both the NCI POB central analysis and by an external independent central review committee. In general, the FDA requests confirmation of investigator assessed ORR and DOR with independent central review for regulatory assessment in the context of a single-arm trial."... "The FDA considers time-to-event endpoints, such as PFS, TTP, TTR, to be uninterpretable in a single-arm trial. The analyses of these endpoints were considered exploratory and were not verified by the FDA."

*[verbatim, same source, FDA's Assessment, p.130]* — "The FDA agrees with the definition of the primary endpoint, primary analysis population, and statistical method used for the analysis of the primary endpoint for Study SPRINT Phase II Stratum 1."

*[verbatim, same source, FDA's Assessment, p.199]* — "SPRINT Phase II Stratum 1 enrolled 50 pediatric patients with NF1 and an inoperable PN that resulted in significant clinical morbidity. The ORR per NCI central review using REiNS criteria was 66% (33/50; 95% CI: 51, 79). All responses were confirmed PRs. Among the 33 responders, the median DOR was not reached, and the proportion of patients who experienced DOR >12 months was 82% (27/33). The ORR per ICR was 44% (22/50; 95% CI: 30, 59); the proportion of patients who experienced DOR >12 months per ICR was 59% (13/22). The FDA notes that the difference in ORR observed between the NCI central review and the ICR is in part due to tumor volume measurements for 6 patients that showed PN shrinkage between -19.2% and -19.9% as best objective response (i.e., not meeting the 20% threshold for PR)."

*[verbatim, same source, Statistical Issues, p.285]* — "While there were no major statistical issues with this application, there are some limitations to deriving inference from a small, non-randomized study. The response rate of patients treated with selumetinib varied by assessor (NCI central review vs. independent central review); however, regardless of assessor, the estimated response rate was considered clinically and statistically meaningful."... "FDA considered the comparisons of efficacy endpoints in SPRINT Phase II Stratum 1 to the placebo arm of Study 01-C-0222 or the Natural History study to be exploratory, due to potential between-study differences including patient eligibility criteria, assessment frequencies of endpoint, and endpoint definition."

*[verbatim, same source, Conclusions and Recommendations, p.286-287]* — "In conclusion, the benefit:risk assessment for selumetinib is favorable, and the FDA review team recommends regular approval for selumetinib for the treatment of pediatric patients 2 years of age and older with NF1 who have symptomatic, inoperable PN at a dose of 25 mg/m2 administered twice daily on a continuous basis. Selumetinib has demonstrated statistically significant and clinically meaningful efficacy, including confirmed ORR that is durable and correlates with improvements in PN-related clinical morbidities. These results represent direct clinical benefit for pediatric patients with NF1 PN."

*[verbatim, same source, §9 Advisory Committee Meeting and Other External Consultations, p.288]* — "The Division did not obtain the advice of the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee (ODAC) or Special Government Employees (SGEs) for this NDA. There were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion."

*[verbatim, FDA approved Package Insert, NDA 213756, §14.1, p.17]* — "An independent centralized review of tumor response per REiNS criteria resulted in an ORR of 44% (95% CI: 30, 59)."... footnote to Table 8: "The ORR assessment was conducted by a single National Cancer Institute reviewer who was a SPRINT investigator and who evaluated all PN imaging from patients enrolled at all trial sites."

This is a genuine example of a "corporate-sponsored NDA built on an academic/government pivotal trial": the operative SAP governing the pivotal efficacy analysis was NCI's (not AstraZeneca's) trial statistical plan, reproduced in the FDA review as the Applicant's Description once AstraZeneca adopted SPRINT as its registration-supporting study; it is also a rare instance in this census of a labeled primary efficacy result (66% ORR) resting on a single non-blinded central reviewer rather than a multi-reader blinded independent review committee, with the blinded independent review (44% ORR) relegated to a pre-specified sensitivity analysis rather than the primary regulatory endpoint — a considerably larger primary-vs-sensitivity gap than is typical for oncology single-arm approvals, which FDA nonetheless found did not undermine the "clinically and statistically meaningful" conclusion, given both estimates' lower confidence bounds remained well above zero and DoR was durable under either assessment.
