### 108. Pemigatinib (Pemazyre) — NDA 213736

**Sponsor:** Incyte Corporation

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adults with previously treated, unresectable locally advanced or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma with a fibroblast growth factor receptor 2 (FGFR2) fusion or other rearrangement as detected by an FDA-approved test — approved under accelerated approval based on durable tumor response rate

**Approval date:** April 17, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** FIGHT-202 (Study INCB 54828-202), NCT02924376

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label, non-randomized, multicenter, multi-cohort Phase 2 trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H/21 CFR 314.510; biomarker-selected/enriched population (Cohort A restricted to central-genomics-laboratory-confirmed FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement, the only cohort supporting the approved indication; Cohorts B [other FGF/FGFR alterations] and C [FGF/FGFR-negative, US only] were exploratory and not part of the approved claim); concurrent companion-diagnostic co-approval (FoundationOne CDx, via supplemental PMA) restricting the indication to FDA-approved-test-confirmed patients
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR, primary — CR or PR per RECIST v1.1, IRC-assessed, confirmation required), duration of response (DOR, key secondary), disease control rate (DCR), progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) (both secondary, descriptive only), patient-reported outcomes (EORTC QLQ-C30, QLQ-BIL21, exploratory)
- *Primary analysis:* descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (point estimate + two-sided 95% exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval around ORR in the efficacy-evaluable population, "exact method for binomial distribution" per SAP §7.2.1) with no formal hypothesis test against the design-stage 15% threshold; Kaplan-Meier estimation with Brookmeyer-Crowley 95% CIs for the secondary time-to-event summaries (DOR, PFS, OS)
- *Multiplicity:* not applicable — SAP §7.1 states "Efficacy Hypotheses: Not applicable"; a single descriptive primary endpoint (ORR) with no comparator arm and no pre-specified alpha, consistent with the "Descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis" pattern used elsewhere in this census (Carfilzomib, Ponatinib/PACE)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* non-binding, single-look futility rule based on responder count in a single-arm trial
- *Missing data/bias:* not a conventional censoring/crossover issue; per SAP §7.2.1, subjects without sufficient baseline or on-study response-assessment information were retained in the ORR denominator as non-responders rather than excluded; separately, FDA's statistical reviewer explicitly declined to interpret the secondary time-to-event endpoints, stating that "in a single arm trial, FDA considers time-to-event endpoints to be uninterpretable" given the absence of a comparator or natural-history benchmark (FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Statistical Review section)
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval based on single-arm ORR/DoR, confirmatory trial required (21 CFR 314.500/314.510); no FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting held — the approval letter states the application "was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the clinical trial design is similar to that previously used to support accelerated approval, the evaluation of the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues..., and there were no controversial issues"; two individually consulted special government employees (an oncologist and a patient representative) gave informal favorable input in lieu of a public ODAC meeting; postmarketing requirement (PMR 3801-1) for a randomized trial demonstrating PFS or OS improvement — subsequently identified (independently, via ClinicalTrials.gov) as FIGHT-302 (NCT03656536, pemigatinib vs. gemcitabine+cisplatin in the first-line setting), which was terminated early for lack of enrollment (a first-line standard-of-care shift, not a safety or futility signal) but whose posted results nonetheless showed a directionally favorable stratified-log-rank PFS result (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.39-0.87, p=0.0078) at the time of termination

**Trial design & endpoints**

- FIGHT-202 (Study INCB 54828-202): open-label, non-randomized, multicenter, multi-cohort Phase 2 trial of oral pemigatinib 13.5 mg once daily (2 weeks on / 1 week off, 21-day cycles) in adults with advanced/metastatic or surgically unresectable cholangiocarcinoma who had progressed on or after ≥1 prior systemic therapy; genomic testing (local, confirmed centrally) assigned subjects to Cohort A (FGFR2 fusion/other rearrangement, the population supporting the approved indication), Cohort B (other FGF/FGFR alterations), or Cohort C (FGF/FGFR-negative, US only)
- Primary endpoint (Cohort A only): ORR, defined as the proportion of subjects with a best overall response of CR or PR per RECIST v1.1, assessed by an independent radiological review committee (IRC), with confirmation of CR/PR required; analyzed in the efficacy-evaluable population (all Cohort A subjects with a confirmed FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement who received ≥1 dose)
- Secondary endpoints: ORR in Cohort B and in Cohorts A+B combined and in Cohort C; DOR, PFS, DCR, and OS (all cohorts, all descriptive, per SAP); safety/tolerability; population pharmacokinetics
- Sample-size logic (SAP §3.2, as amended by Protocol Amendment 5): assuming a true ORR of 33% and 10% dropout, ~100 Cohort A subjects would give >95% probability that the lower bound of the 95% CI around the observed ORR would exceed 15% (Amendment 5 increased the Cohort A target from 60 to 100, raising this probability from an originally planned 80%); a single non-binding interim futility look was planned at ~25 Cohort A subjects (stop if ≤2 responders); no interim analysis of any kind was planned for Cohorts B/C beyond an analogous nonbinding rule
- Statistical methods: ORR (and DCR) summarized as a point estimate with a two-sided exact (Clopper-Pearson-type) binomial 95% CI, per SAP §7.2.1 — no formal single-arm hypothesis test was specified (SAP §7.1: "Efficacy Hypotheses: Not applicable"); DOR/PFS/OS summarized by Kaplan-Meier with Brookmeyer-Crowley 95% CIs for medians; PFS/DOR censoring followed the FDA 2015/2018 cancer-endpoints guidance algorithm reproduced in SAP Table 1; the Per Protocol population served as a sensitivity population for the primary ORR analysis
- Results (Cohort A, N=107, data cutoff March 22, 2019): ORR 36% (95% CI 27-45%; 3 CR, 35 PR); median DOR 9.1 months (95% CI 6.0-14.5); 24/38 responders (63%) had DOR ≥6 months and 7/38 (18%) had DOR ≥12 months; FDA's statistical reviewer characterized this as "sufficiently large in magnitude...and durability...to be clinically meaningful," given a reference life expectancy of 5-6 months in this setting and no other FDA-approved second-line options
- An interim look at 47 Cohort A patients (data cutoff November 27, 2017) had shown an ORR of only 17% (95% CI 7.6-31%; 8/47 responders) — above the nonbinding ≤2-responder futility threshold, so accrual continued; the final analysis's much higher 36% reflects substantially longer follow-up and a near-doubled sample rather than a changed population or method

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2020/213736Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2020/213736s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 4594191, NDA 213736) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/213736Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (FIGHT-202) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02924376 (Study Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan both posted in the Documents tab)
- Protocol / SAP — Study Protocol (Amendment 7, dated 2 Apr 2020): https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/76/NCT02924376/Prot_000.pdf; Statistical Analysis Plan (Amendment 1, dated 15 Apr 2019): https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/76/NCT02924376/SAP_001.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Abou-Alfa GK, Sahai V, Hollebecque A, et al. "Pemigatinib for previously treated, locally advanced or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma: a multicentre, open-label, phase 2 study." *Lancet Oncol.* 2020;21(5):671-684. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(20)30109-1>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32203698/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Pemigatinib%20for%20previously%20treated%2C%20locally%20advanced%20or%20metastatic%20cholangiocarcinoma%3A%20a%20multicentre%2C%20open-label%2C%20phase%202%20study)

**Other resources**

- Incyte's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for FIGHT-202; no Vivli/YODA Project/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for this trial.
- No FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held; per the approval letter, FDA instead consulted two special government employees (an oncologist with cholangiocarcinoma expertise and a patient representative) individually by teleconference, both of whom found the risk-benefit assessment favorable.
- Postmarketing requirement (PMR 3801-1): a randomized trial demonstrating PFS or OS improvement, to confirm clinical benefit; this appears to be satisfied by FIGHT-302 (NCT03656536), a Phase 3 trial of first-line pemigatinib vs. gemcitabine+cisplatin in FGFR2-rearranged cholangiocarcinoma, which was terminated in 2025 for enrollment failure attributed to a shift in first-line standard of care (not a safety concern), after already reaching results (median PFS 8.34 vs. 6.80 months; stratified-log-rank p=0.0078; stratified Cox HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.39-0.87, favoring pemigatinib) per its ClinicalTrials.gov results posting — a genuinely mixed outcome for the accelerated-approval confirmatory requirement: the trial did not run to its originally planned completion, but the data in hand at termination were directionally positive rather than a confirmatory failure.
- Two additional PMRs (3801-2, 3801-3) required dedicated hepatic- and renal-impairment PK/safety studies, unrelated to the efficacy confirmation requirement.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, Statistical Analysis Plan, INCB 54828-202, Amendment 1 (15 Apr 2019), §2.2.1 Primary Objective]* — "To evaluate the efficacy of INCB054828 in subjects with advanced/metastatic or surgically unresectable cholangiocarcinoma with FGFR2 translocation who have failed at least 1 previous treatment."

*[verbatim, same source, §2.3.1 Primary Endpoint]* — "To determine the ORR in subjects with FGFR2 translocations based on the central genomics laboratory results. Objective response rate is defined as the proportion of subjects who achieved a CR (disappearance of all target lesions) or a PR (≥ 30% decrease in the sum of the longest diameters of target lesions) based on RECIST v1.1. Clinical response will be determined by an independent radiological review committee."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.2 Sample Size Considerations]* — "Approximately 100 subjects with documentation of FGFR2 translocation from the central genomics laboratory are planned for the final analysis of the primary endpoint of ORR. With the assumed rate of 33% for the intervention, a sample size of approximately 100 subjects would provide > 95% probability to have a 95% CI with lower limit of > 15%, assuming 10% lost to follow-up."

*[verbatim, same source, §7.1 Efficacy Hypotheses]* — "Not applicable."

*[verbatim, same source, §7.2.1 Primary Efficacy Analysis]* — "The primary endpoint of the study is ORR in subjects with FGFR2 translocations based on the central genomics laboratory results, defined as the proportion of subjects with best response of CR or PR based on review of scans by an independent centralized radiological review committee per RECIST v1.1 (Eisenhauer et al 2009) results. Confirmation of CR and PR is required and documented in the Independent Central Review Charter. This analysis will be based on efficacy evaluable population for subjects with FGFR2 translocations. Subjects who do not have sufficient baseline or on-study response assessment information to be adequately assessed for response status will be included in the denominators in the calculation of ORR. The 95% CI for ORR will be calculated using exact method for binomial distribution."

*[verbatim, same source, §9 Interim Analyses]* — "For Cohort A (FGFR2 translocation), a futility analysis will be performed when approximately 25 subjects are enrolled into the cohort and have at least 1 tumor assessment or have permanently discontinued study treatment. Cohort A can be stopped for futility if 2 or fewer responders are observed, for which there is less than a 10% probability of claiming ORR > 15% at final analysis based on a 60-subject cohort, as initially planned before Amendment 5. This rule is just a guidance and is nonbinding."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 213736, Reference ID 4594191, Statistical Review, Statistical Analysis Plan subsection]* — "In Cohort A, assuming a response rate of 33% and a drop-out rate of 10%, 100 patients were needed to obtain a probability of more than 95% to rule out a response rate of 15% by the lower limit of the 95% confidence interval (CI). One non-binding interim analysis for futility was planned for Cohort A after 25 patients were enrolled and had at least one tumor assessment (or had permanently discontinued from the study). If there were less than three responders, accrual to Cohort A could be stopped. An interim analysis was conducted after 47 patients were enrolled in Cohort A based on the data cutoff date of November 27, 2017. Eight patients had confirmed partial responses resulting in an ORR of 17% with a 95% CI of (7.6%, 31%)."

*[verbatim, same source, same subsection]* — "Reviewer Comment: The timing of the final analysis was not pre-specified in the protocol. However, during the pre-NDA meeting dated August 8, 2019 FDA acknowledged that the proposed data cut-off of March 22, 2019 would provide a minimum of 7 months of follow-up for all patients and a minimum of 6 months of follow-up from time of initial response for 92% of responders."

*[verbatim, same source, same subsection]* — "Reviewer Comment: In a single arm trial, FDA considers time-to-event endpoints to be uninterpretable, and the results will not be described in this review."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.3 Statistical Issues]* — "There were no major statistical issues in the review of this NDA. However, the single-arm design of the main trial supporting efficacy limits the interpretation of time-to-event endpoints, such as PFS and OS, given the absence of an active control or comparison to the natural history of disease."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.4 Conclusions and Recommendations]* — "The response rate is sufficiently large in magnitude (36% with a lower bound of the 95% confidence interval of 27%) and durability (DoR ≥ 6 months in 63% of responders and ≥ 12 months in 18% of responders) to be clinically meaningful to patients with cholangiocarcinoma who have received prior treatment, given that the life expectancy in this setting is 5-6 months."

*[verbatim, same source, §9 Advisory Committee Meeting and Other External Consultations]* — "The Division did not obtain the advice of the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee (ODAC) for this NDA because no review issues were identified that raised significant public health questions regarding the risk:benefit assessment of pemigatinib for the proposed indication."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "3801-1 Submit the results of a randomized trial demonstrating improvement of progression-free survival or overall survival in patients with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma with a fibroblast growth receptor 2 (FGFR2) gene fusion or rearrangement, to confirm clinical benefit of pemigatinib."

Note on genuineness and completeness: this entry is unusual in this census for having both a genuine sponsor Protocol and a genuine sponsor SAP posted on ClinicalTrials.gov that extracted cleanly with `pdftotext -layout` (no redaction-pipeline spacing corruption of the kind seen elsewhere in this project), so essentially none of the SAP content above required inference — it is drawn directly from primary sponsor and FDA-review text. The one substantive design element without an exact match in `Keyword_Taxonomy.md` is the single, non-binding, responder-count futility rule in SAP §9, marked ".

### 109. Tucatinib (Tukysa) — NDA 213411

**Sponsor:** Seattle Genetics, Inc. (rebranded Seagen Inc. in 2020; acquired by Pfizer in December 2023)

**Indication approved:** In combination with trastuzumab and capecitabine, for treatment of adult patients with advanced unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer, including patients with brain metastases, who have received one or more prior anti-HER2-based regimens in the metastatic setting

**Approval date:** April 17, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** HER2CLIMB (Study ONT-380-206), NCT02614794 — confirmed via ClinicalTrials.gov and the FDA review to be a randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled **Phase 2** trial (official CT.gov title: "Phase 2 Randomized, Double-Blinded, Controlled Study of Tucatinib vs Placebo in Combination With Capecitabine and Trastuzumab in Patients With Pretreated Unresectable Locally Advanced or Metastatic HER2+ Breast Carcinoma"), not a dedicated Phase 3 trial, despite supporting regular (not accelerated) approval.

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled (add-on design: both arms received the same trastuzumab + capecitabine background therapy, with the control arm substituting placebo for tucatinib), biomarker-selected/enriched population (centrally confirmed HER2-positive by IHC/ISH), dynamic hierarchical (biased-coin/minimization-type) randomization scheme balancing on 3 stratification factors with re-randomization-based inference, primary-endpoint analysis timed to a fixed subset of the first 480 randomized patients rather than to a target event count or calendar date
- *Endpoints:* progression-free survival (PFS) per BICR using RECIST v1.1 (primary), overall survival (OS, alpha-controlled key secondary), objective response rate (ORR) per BICR (alpha-controlled key secondary), subgroup-specific PFS in patients with brain metastases present/history at baseline (PFSBrainMets), elevated to a fourth alpha-controlled key secondary endpoint
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified), Kaplan-Meier estimation, re-randomization test (Rosenberger and Lachin, 2002) used in place of the ordinary log-rank/Cox asymptotic p-value to account for the dynamic biased-coin randomization scheme, Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test (stratified, for ORR), exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval (for ORR)
- *Multiplicity:* group sequential Holm variable (GSHν) procedure (Ye 2013) governing the 3 alpha-controlled key secondary endpoints, alpha recycling between PFSBrainMets and OS (each endpoint's allocated alpha passed to the other upon rejection)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design for the key secondary endpoints only (not the primary endpoint), Lan-DeMets O'Brien-Fleming alpha-spending function, Data Monitoring Committee (independent Data Monitoring Committee, IDMC)
- *Missing data/bias:* standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment, four pre-specified sensitivity analyses varying the censoring rule for PFS (ignoring vs. imputing missing disease-assessment visits; treating initiation of new anti-cancer therapy or new radiotherapy before progression/death as a censoring event rather than ignoring it), partial-date imputation rule for incomplete AE/event dates (15th of the month if only day missing; July 1 if day and month both missing)
- *Regulatory:* regular approval based on statistically significant PFS (primary) plus OS, PFSBrainMets, and ORR (all alpha-controlled key secondaries) demonstrated in a single randomized Phase 2 trial rather than a dedicated Phase 3 trial," seen in Glasdegib/BRIGHT AML 1003, but here the primary basis was PFS, not OS), FDA-directed removal of two successively planned formal interim analyses of the primary PFS endpoint across Protocol Amendments 2 and 7, Project Orbis international collaborative review (with Australia TGA, Singapore HSA, Health Canada, Swissmedic) and Real-Time Oncology Review (RTOR) pilot participation, Breakthrough Therapy Designation, Fast Track Designation, Orphan Drug Designation (BC with brain metastases), no FDA Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- HER2CLIMB (ONT-380-206): global, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2 trial of tucatinib 300 mg PO BID + trastuzumab + capecitabine vs. placebo + trastuzumab + capecitabine in 612 patients with locally advanced unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer (including patients with brain metastases) who had received prior trastuzumab, pertuzumab, and T-DM1; conducted at 155 sites in 15 countries
- Randomization used a dynamic hierarchical (biased-coin) allocation scheme via Interactive Response Technology, stratified by presence/history of brain metastases (yes/no), ECOG performance status (0/1), and region of world (US, Canada, rest of world); because of the dynamic randomization, p-values were computed with a re-randomization test (Rosenberger and Lachin, 2002) rather than the ordinary asymptotic log-rank/Cox test
- Primary endpoint: PFS per blinded independent central review (BICR) using RECIST v1.1, analyzed in the ITT-PFS population defined as the first 480 randomized subjects (320 tucatinib : 160 placebo), not the full enrolled population of 612 — a deliberate SAP choice, accepted by FDA, to avoid bias from short follow-up in later-enrolled patients
- Alpha-controlled key secondary endpoints, tested in the full ITT-OS population (N=612) via the group sequential Holm variable (GSHν) procedure (Ye 2013): overall survival (OS); PFS per BICR in the subgroup with brain metastases at baseline (PFSBrainMets, analyzed in the ITT-PFSBrainMets population, N=291); confirmed ORR per BICR (in patients with measurable disease at baseline, N=511). Other secondary endpoints (investigator-assessed PFS/ORR, duration of response, clinical benefit rate) were not subject to formal Type I error control
- Sample size grew across 3 protocol amendments — 180 → 480 (Amendment 6, Nov 2016, "to provide greater statistical power to the primary and key secondary endpoints") → 600 (Amendment 8, Nov 2018, "to increase the sample size to provide greater power for the endpoints PFSBrainMets and OS") — with Amendment 8 also switching the key-secondary testing structure from hierarchical (sequential) to parallel (independent-alpha) for PFSBrainMets and OS, and Amendment 10 (Mar 2019) clarifying that the primary PFS analysis would still use only the first 480 randomized patients
- No formal interim analysis was ever conducted for the primary PFS endpoint: a planned interim PFS analysis in the original protocol was removed in Amendment 2 (Sept 2015) at FDA's recommendation ("interim analysis may not provide an accurate or reproducible estimate of the treatment effect size to support demonstration of efficacy"), and a second planned interim PFS analysis (added when the sample size was raised to 480) was likewise removed in Amendment 7 (Aug 2017) for the same FDA-stated reason
- One formal interim analysis was planned (and reached) for PFSBrainMets and up to two for OS, contingent on the primary PFS analysis being significant, using an initial alpha split of 0.03 (PFSBrainMets) and 0.02 (OS) with alpha recycling between the two if one crossed its boundary first; boundaries were computed with the Lan-DeMets O'Brien-Fleming spending function — at the actual interim look, the 2-sided alpha threshold was 0.0080 for PFSBrainMets (71% information fraction) and 0.0074 for OS (60% information fraction); both were statistically significant at this single interim look, so no further formal testing of either endpoint was planned
- Primary result (10.4-month median PFS follow-up): median PFS 7.8 months (tucatinib) vs. 5.6 months (placebo), stratified HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.42-0.71), 2-sided re-randomization p<0.00001. Key secondary OS (14-month median follow-up): median OS 21.9 vs. 17.4 months, HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.50-0.87), p=0.00480 (vs. an alpha boundary of 0.0074). Key secondary PFSBrainMets: median 7.6 vs. 5.4 months, HR 0.48 (95% CI 0.34-0.69), p<0.00001 (vs. a boundary of 0.0080). Key secondary confirmed ORR: 40.6% vs. 22.8%, stratified CMH p=0.00008
- Four pre-specified sensitivity analyses of PFS censoring rules (ignoring vs. imputing missing disease assessments; treating new anti-cancer therapy or new radiotherapy before progression/death as a censoring event) were all consistent with the primary result; a further sensitivity analysis without the re-randomization procedure (ordinary stratified log-rank/Cox on final randomized assignment) gave a nominal p<0.00001, confirming the dynamic-randomization adjustment did not drive the result

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2020/213411Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2020/213411s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (combined Clinical/Statistical Review, Reference ID 4593552) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/213411Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02614794 (no protocol or SAP posted in the Documents tab as of this writing; the CT.gov API's `documentSection` field is empty for this study)
- Protocol / SAP: not publicly posted by the sponsor; all SAP methodology detail in this entry is drawn from the FDA Multi-Discipline Review's paraphrase/quotation of the sponsor's SAP (see below)
- Pivotal publication: Murthy RK, Loi S, Okines A, et al. "Tucatinib, Trastuzumab, and Capecitabine for HER2-Positive Metastatic Breast Cancer." *N Engl J Med.* 2020;382(7):597-609. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1914609), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31825569/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Tucatinib%2C%20Trastuzumab%2C%20and%20Capecitabine%20for%20HER2-Positive%20Metastatic%20Breast%20Cancer)

**Other resources**

- Seagen (the current NDA holder's predecessor name) is not itself listed as a Vivli enrolled member organization; its acquirer, Pfizer, is a Vivli member, but trial-specific individual patient data (IPD) availability for HER2CLIMB/NCT02614794 was not individually confirmed.
- No FDA Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held for this application — the Multi-Discipline Review states: "FDA did not refer this new drug application to an advisory committee as no significant efficacy or safety issues were identified during the review that required external input for the proposed indication."
- This was one of the first applications reviewed under FDA's Project Orbis (simultaneous collaborative review with the Australian Therapeutic Goods Administration, Singapore Health Sciences Authority, Health Canada, and Swissmedic) and the Real-Time Oncology Review (RTOR) pilot program, both agreed to on October 21, 2019; tucatinib also received Fast Track (June 2016), Orphan Drug (June 2017, for BC with brain metastases), and Breakthrough Therapy (December 2019) designations.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 213411, Reference ID 4593552, §8, "Statistical Analysis Plan and Amendments" — Applicant's Description]* — "The Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP), version 1, was finalized on 07 Aug 2019, prior to analysis of the primary endpoint. There were no amendments... The primary analysis of PFS per BICR used the ITT-PFS population. The two treatment groups were compared using a stratified log-rank test controlling for the randomization stratification factors. The p-value for this test was calculated using a re-randomization procedure to reflect the dynamic hierarchical allocation scheme used in the study randomization. A Cox proportional-hazards model taking into account the stratification factors was used to estimate the treatment arm hazard ratio (HR) and its 95% CI... To maintain strong control of the family-wise type I error rate at 0.05, PFS per BICR was tested at the 0.05 level first in the ITT-PFS population, and then the key secondary endpoints of OS and PFSBrainMets were tested using the group sequential Holm variable (GSHv) procedure, followed by the test of confirmed ORR."

*[verbatim, same source, "Interim Analyses" / "Control of Multiplicity"]* — "No interim analyses for efficacy were planned for the primary endpoint. One formal interim analysis for superiority was planned for the key secondary endpoint of PFSBrainMets and 2 formal interim analyses for superiority were planned for the key secondary endpoint of OS if the primary analysis for PFS was statistically significant... The initial α split between PFSBrainMets and OS was α=0.03 and α=0.02, respectively. If one was statistically significant, the α would be passed to the other endpoint... Based on the observed information fraction of 71% and total alpha of 0.03, according to the Lan-DeMets O'Brien-Fleming spending function, the 2-sided alpha level at this interim analysis for PFSBrainMets was 0.0080. Similarly, based on the observed information fraction of 60% and total alpha of 0.05, the 2-sided alpha level at this interim analysis for OS was 0.0074. If both PFSBrainMets and OS are statistically significant, ORR will be formally compared with the 2 arms using a 2-sided α of 0.05."

*[verbatim, same source, "Regulatory Authorities Assessment" of the SAP]* — "FDA reviewed the SAP prior to submission of this NDA and found it to be acceptable, but note the following: 1. The sample size increased from 480 to 600 under protocol version 8 to enroll more patients with brain metastases, but the primary analysis of PFS by BICR is conducted in the first 480 patients. The applicant notes that this was to avoid potential bias from early progression events in the overall population as many patients may have short follow-up. FDA found this approach acceptable. 2. The stratified log-rank p-value for the primary and secondary analyses were calculated using a re-randomization procedure to account for the dynamic randomization scheme used. This was consistent with FDA recommendations... 5. Both the secondary endpoints (OS and PFSBrainMets) were statistically significant at their first interim analyses, so no further formal testing for OS or PFSBrainMets is planned."

*[verbatim, same source, Table 14, "Summary of Key Changes in Protocol Amendments, HER2CLIMB"]* — Amendment 2 (25-Sep-2015): "A planned interim analysis of PFS as the primary endpoint was removed," rationale: "FDA Recommendation that interim analysis may not provide an accurate or reproducible estimate of the treatment effect size to support demonstration of efficacy if using this trial to support drug approval." Amendment 7 (30-Aug-2017) repeats the identical change and rationale for a second planned interim PFS analysis. Amendment 8 (12-Nov-2018): "Amended the statistical testing from a hierarchical to parallel structure for key secondary endpoints of PFSBrainMets and OS," rationale: "Given the importance of OS as a clinical endpoint, this allowed for testing of OS in a parallel structure with the other key secondary endpoint, PFSBrainMets."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.3 "Statistical Issues"]* — "There were no major statistical issues with this application. HER2CLIMB showed a statistically significant improvement in favor of the tucatinib arm with respect to the primary endpoint PFS by BICR and secondary endpoints OS, PFSBrainMets, and ORR by BICR."

*[verbatim, same source, Executive Summary, "Conclusions on the Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness"]* — "The use of a single randomized trial to support approval is acceptable due to the disease setting, consistent demonstration of superiority across multiple efficacy endpoints, and robust efficacy results on statistical evaluation. Therefore, the FDA review team recommends granting regular approval to TUKYSA (tucatinib)."

*[verbatim, Package Insert, Table 9 footnotes, Reference ID 4593756]* — "3. Two-sided p-value based on re-randomization procedure (Rosenberger and Lachin 2002) controlling for stratification factors, compared with the allocated alpha of 0.05... 4. Two-sided p-value based on re-randomization procedure (Rosenberger and Lachin 2002) controlling for stratification factors, compared with the allocated alpha of 0.0074 for this interim analysis (with 60% of the planned number of events for final analysis)... 6. Two-sided p-value based on re-randomization procedure (Rosenberger and Lachin 2002) controlling for stratification factors, compared with the allocated alpha of 0.0080 for this interim analysis (with 71% of the planned number of events for final analysis)... 7. Two-sided 95% exact confidence interval, computed using the Clopper-Pearson method (1934)."

This is a genuine example of FDA repeatedly steering a sponsor away from formal interim analysis of a primary efficacy endpoint (twice, across Amendments 2 and 7) on reliability grounds, while simultaneously accepting a fixed-N (first-480-patients) rather than event-driven timing rule for that same primary analysis, and accepting a re-randomization-based (rather than ordinary asymptotic) hypothesis test to account for a non-standard dynamic/biased-coin randomization scheme — a cluster of methodological accommodations that let a single randomized Phase 2 trial (not a dedicated Phase 3) support regular approval.

### 110. Sacituzumab govitecan-hziy (Trodelvy) — BLA 761115

**Sponsor:** Immunomedics, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (mTNBC) who have received at least two prior therapies for metastatic disease (accelerated approval)

**Approval date:** April 22, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** Study IMMU-132-01 (Phase I/II, open-label, multi-cohort basket trial; mTNBC expansion cohort), NCT01631552

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial supporting accelerated approval, conducted as one disease-specific expansion cohort (mTNBC, n=108, treated at the to-be-marketed 10 mg/kg dose with ≥2 prior therapies for metastatic disease) within a larger Phase I/II basket protocol that separately enrolled and analyzed non-TNBC breast, urothelial, NSCLC, SCLC, and other epithelial-cancer cohorts (efficacy not pooled across histologies), no formal sample size calculation or statistical hypothesis pre-specified for the trial
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR, CR+PR by RECIST 1.1, investigator-assessed) — primary/major efficacy outcome measure; duration of response (DOR) — key secondary; time to response (TTR), clinical benefit rate (CBR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS) — secondary/descriptive; independent central review (ICR) of a triggered subgroup — supportive
- *Primary analysis:* descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (point estimate + exact/Clopper-Pearson-type 2-sided 95% binomial confidence interval, no formal hypothesis test against a pre-specified performance goal), Kaplan-Meier estimation for DOR/PFS/OS with 95% CIs via the Brookmeyer-Crowley method (log-log transformation)
- *Multiplicity:* not applicable — single-arm design with one major efficacy outcome measure (ORR) and no comparator arm or formal multi-endpoint testing hierarchy
- *Missing data/bias:* FDA required the applicant to recalculate duration of response using the standard regulatory event definition (progression or death, whichever occurs first) after the sponsor's SAP-specified DOR definition omitted death as an event; FDA excluded the sponsor's double-read independent central review (ICR) results from labeling consideration because ICR was performed only on a triggered subgroup (patients whose local scans showed CR, PR, or ≥20% shrinkage, n=55/108), which the reviewer judged an inadequate, bias-prone partial assessment rather than a full-population reanalysis; on-site inspection (OSI) found that two patients at one clinical site had undocumented brain-metastasis progression not properly recorded as disease progression in the submitted datasets, prompting FDA to revise their progression dates
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval (21 CFR 601.41) based on ORR and DOR, benchmarked against historical single-arm ORR/DOR data for the two prior late-line mTNBC approvals (eribulin, ixabepilone) to support a claim of "improvement over available therapy"; original BLA received a Complete Response (CR) action January 17, 2019, solely for chemistry-manufacturing-controls (CMC) deficiencies (unrelated to the clinical/statistical package, which OSI found reliable), including a pre-license inspection finding of "data falsification to obtain favorable results" at the drug-substance manufacturing facility; a planned FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was cancelled in late 2018 amid the CMC/data-integrity investigation and was not rescheduled; BLA resubmitted December 2, 2019 and approved without an advisory committee meeting; postmarketing requirement (PMR 3504-1) was the randomized confirmatory trial IMMU-132-05 (ASCENT), which later supported conversion to regular approval in 2021 (outside the scope of this entry)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study IMMU-132-01: "A Phase I/II Study of IMMU-132 (hRS7-SN38 Antibody Drug Conjugate) in Patients with Epithelial Cancer" — a non-randomized, open-label, single-arm basket-design study of sacituzumab govitecan (then IMMU-132) in adults with Trop-2-expressing advanced/metastatic epithelial cancers refractory to or relapsed after ≥1 prior standard regimen; Phase I used a standard 3+3 dose-escalation design (starting dose 8 mg/kg) to select a Phase II dose; Phase II enrolled disease-specific expansion cohorts including mTNBC, non-TNBC HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer, metastatic urothelial cancer, NSCLC, SCLC, and other tumor types, with 10 mg/kg IV on Days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle selected for further development; total trial enrollment was 515 patients across all phases/cohorts (per the sponsor's SAP), with 420 patients having received sacituzumab govitecan at some dose across all indications combined (per FDA's review); this BLA's efficacy population is limited to the "Target mTNBC Population": 108 patients with relapsed/refractory mTNBC who had received ≥2 prior therapies for metastatic disease and who received the 10 mg/kg dose; enrollment of this target population was stopped February 14, 2017 once the enrollment goal was met; per label, patients with bulky disease (mass >7 cm) were excluded, and patients with treated, non-progressing brain metastases not requiring high-dose steroids were eligible
- Primary/major efficacy outcome measures: investigator-assessed objective response rate (ORR = CR+PR) by RECIST 1.1, with responses requiring confirmation no sooner than 4 weeks after criteria for response were first met, and duration of response (DOR) among responders; there was no formal, pre-specified statistical hypothesis test of ORR against a null/performance-goal threshold — the FDA statistical reviewer explicitly noted "there was no formal statistical justification for the sample size"
- Independent central review (ICR) was specified in the SAP (not in the protocol) and performed only on the subset of patients (n=55/108) whose tumor scans showed CR, PR, or ≥20% shrinkage by local read; the ICR charter was amended from a single-read to a double-read-with-adjudication design in October 2017, at FDA's recommendation given at an October 2017 pre-BLA meeting, after FDA raised concerns about a single unadjudicated reviewer; the single-read ICR results were not used in the final review
- Secondary/supportive endpoints: time to response (TTR, descriptive), clinical benefit rate (CBR = CR+PR+SD≥6 months, exact binomial 95% CI), progression-free survival and overall survival (Kaplan-Meier, Brookmeyer-Crowley 95% CIs); planned sensitivity analyses used the Per-Protocol population (n=102, patients who completed ≥1 cycle with ≥1 response assessment) and a subgroup of 94 patients who had received ≥2 lines of prior standard chemotherapy specifically (as opposed to hormonal/investigational therapy); planned exploratory subgroup analyses covered age, race, ECOG status, Trop-2 expression status, visceral/liver disease, and number of prior chemotherapies
- Results (data cutoff June 30, 2017, primary; December 1, 2017, updated DOR maturity, both as reported in FDA's review): confirmed investigator-assessed ORR 33.3% (36/108; 95% CI 24.6-43.1%; 3 CR [2.8%], 33 PR [30.6%]); median time to response 2.0 months; median DOR 7.7 months (95% CI 4.9-10.8) at the more mature December 2017 cutoff (8.4 months, 95% CI 4.9-11.6, at the original June 2017 cutoff); FDA requested the more mature DOR cutoff because 15 of 36 responses were censored due to data cutoff, including 7 censored under 3 months; double-read ICR in the triggered n=55 subgroup gave a supportive but not identical ORR of 32.4% (95% CI 23.7-42.1%; investigator-vs-ICR concordance 76% by exact response category, 92% for responder-vs-non-responder); FDA declined to include the ICR results in labeling given the non-representative, bias-prone subgroup on which ICR was conducted
- FDA's benefit-risk framing for accelerated approval compared this ORR/DOR result against the only two prior approvals in a similar late-line mTNBC-eligible population: ixabepilone (investigator ORR 18.3%, DOR 6.0 months by central assessment) and eribulin (ORR 11%, DOR 4.2 months), concluding sacituzumab govitecan's 33.3% ORR / 7.7-month DOR was "reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit and to be better than the available therapies"

**Other resources**

- Immunomedics (acquired by Gilead Sciences in October 2020, after this approval) does not have a confirmed trial-specific IPD listing for IMMU-132-01 on Vivli, YODA, or Project Data Sphere; general sponsor-level participation was not individually confirmed.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for the 2020 approval; the approval letter states this was because the application "did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues that were unexpected for a biologic of this class or in the intended population." Notably, an ODAC meeting had originally been anticipated/planned in mid-late 2018 but was cancelled amid the manufacturing data-integrity investigation described below, and no ODAC meeting occurred at any point in the approval history of this BLA.
- Postmarketing requirement (PMR 3504-1): submit the final study report and datasets for progression-free survival and overall survival from Trial IMMU-132-05 ("Phase III Study of Sacituzumab Govitecan (IMMU-132) in Refractory/Relapsed Triple-Negative Breast Cancer," i.e., ASCENT, NCT02574455), to confirm clinical benefit; this randomized confirmatory trial later supported conversion of this indication to regular approval in April 2021 — a separate, later regulatory action not covered by this entry.
- Regulatory history is unusually contentious for reasons unrelated to the statistical/clinical package: the original BLA (submitted May 18, 2018) received a Complete Response action on January 17, 2019 solely for CMC deficiencies, including an FDA finding of data falsification during a pre-license inspection of the hRS7 antibody-intermediate manufacturing facility (Morris Plains, NJ) and a subsequent third-party investigation into a data-integrity breach; FDA's Office of Scientific Investigations separately audited clinical trial conduct/data (6-9 sites) based on high enrollment and confidential-informant allegations of GCP violations, and — apart from the site-level progression-date discrepancies noted above — concluded the clinical data submitted in support of BLA 761115 "appear reliable."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, sponsor Statistical Analysis Plan, Protocol IMMU-132-01, Version 3.0, 27 February 2019, §2.1 Primary Objective]* — "The primary objective in Phase I is to identify the maximum acceptable dose and evaluate the safety and tolerability of IMMU-132 as a single agent administered in 3-week treatment cycles, in previously treated patients with advanced epithelial cancers. The primary objective in Phase II is the evaluation of the safety and efficacy of IMMU-132 administered in 3-week treatment cycles, at a dose selected in Phase I."

*[verbatim, same source, §4, Analysis Populations]* — "Target mTNBC Population: Patients with relapsed/refractory mTNBC who have received at least 2 prior therapies for metastatic disease and who received IMMU-132 at a dose of 10 mg/kg. Per-Protocol (PP) Population (specific to the Target mTNBC Population): This will include patients of the Target mTNBC Population who received at least 1 complete cycle of IMMU-132 and had data available from at least 1 response assessment."

*[verbatim, same source, §6.2, Objective Response Rate]* — "The ORR is defined as the rate of the overall best response as CR or PR. All patients in the applicable analysis population will be included in the denominator in the calculation of the percentage for each response category and ORR. ORR will be summarized by the percentage of responses with 2-sided exact binomial 95% CI."

*[verbatim, same source, §6, introductory efficacy-analysis text]* — "The primary endpoint will be the objective response rate (ORR) [PR+CR], with responders requiring a confirmatory response assessment no sooner than 4 weeks after the criteria for response are first met... Secondary efficacy endpoints will include time to response (TTR), duration of response (DOR), clinical benefit rate (CR+PR+SD [stable disease] ≥6 months), progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS). DOR, PFS, and OS data will be analyzed via Kaplan-Meier method and 95% CI from Brookmeyer and Crowley method with log-log transformation."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761115, Clinical Review, "Statistical Analysis Plan" section]* — "There was no formal sample size determination for Trial IMMU-132-01. The Phase II trial planned to enroll up to 150 patients in each of 5 expansion cohorts (TNBC, non-TNBC, NSCLC, SCLC, UC)... Reviewer comment: The CSR submitted for this BLA was based on the mTNBC Target Population consisting of n=108 patients and a database cutoff of June 30, 2017. There was no formal statistical justification for the sample size."

*[verbatim, same source, continuing]* — "For the primary analysis of the primary efficacy endpoint of ORR per RECIST 1.1 as assessed by investigator, the ORR was summarized by the percentage of responses (CR or PR) with a two-sided exact binomial 95% CI. The secondary endpoints of DOR, PFS, and OS were analyzed with Kaplan-Meier methods with 95% confidence intervals calculated from the Brookmeyer and Crowley method with log-log transformation."

*[verbatim, same source, Reviewer Comment on ICR]* — "ICR was prespecified in the SAP but not in protocol. Initially ICR was based on single-read (imaging charter dated August 15, 2016) and double-read was added in the charter amendment (October 30, 2017) after pre-BLA meeting (October 12, 2017) per FDA's recommendation. The applicant initially performed a single-read ICR. In the October 2017 pre-BLA meeting, FDA notified the applicant of concerns regarding using a single blinded reviewer without adjudication for the BICR. Taking FDA's recommendation, the applicant amended their charter to include a double-read ICR with adjudication. The single-read ICR results are not reported in this review."

*[verbatim, same source, Reviewer Comment on DOR definition]* — "On July 3, 2018, the FDA sent an IR to the applicant asking them to recalculate duration of response with death included. The standard regulatory definition of DOR is defined from the onset of response until PD or death, whichever occurs first. Death after 2+ missing scheduled assessments should be censored at the last assessment prior to the missing ones. The DOR results presented in this review follow the standard regulatory definition."

*[verbatim, same source, Efficacy Results — Primary Endpoint]* — "The analysis of the primary efficacy endpoint of ORR per RECIST 1.1 as assessed by investigator was based upon the efficacy population (n=108) and a trial cutoff data of June 30, 2017; the results are shown in Table 15. The confirmed ORR was 33.3% (n=36; 95% CI: 24.6%, 43.1%) consisting of 3 complete responses (CRs, 2.8%) and 33 partial responses (PRs, 30.6%)."

*[verbatim, same source, Reviewer Comment on ICR labeling recommendation]* — "The double-read ICR assessment was based on a subgroup of patients with tumor scans showing CR, PR, or at least 20% shrinkage by local site evaluation rather than the entire efficacy population. Given the inherent bias in evaluating response only among patients whom have been identified by investigators as responders or as having 20% tumor shrinkage [i.e. SD], FDA considers the partial review inadequate to determine whether there is consistency in the ORR results across both assessment methods. As such, this reviewer recommends not including this information in product labeling... In the applicant's response to the CR, they noted that a blinded independent central review will not be done for the entire efficacy population and agreed to limit the efficacy data presentation in the product label to the investigator-assessed results."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Office of Scientific Investigations findings]* — "The data from Study IMMU-132-01 submitted to the Agency in support of BLA 761115, appear reliable."... "Inspection of Site 255 (Principal Investigator: Dr. Bardia) revealed that source documentation associated with efficacy assessments for 2 patients was not consistent with datasets submitted to the Agency. Specifically, [two] Patient[s] were identified as responders in the BLA submission. However, they were noted to have undergone brain imaging (MRI) between scheduled study visits, which revealed that both patients had brain metastases. The findings of brain metastases were not appropriately recorded as an event of disease progression in either patient in the datasets and clinical reports submitted in the BLA."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Product Quality / Regulatory Background section, on the original Complete Response action]* — "Several objectionable conditions were identified during the pre-license inspection of the manufacturing facility for hRS7 antibody intermediate, including data falsification to obtain favorable results. Additionally, the data submitted in the application are not sufficient to support a conclusion that the manufacture of sacituzumab govitecan is well-controlled and will lead to a product that is pure and potent for the duration of the shelf-life."

*[verbatim, FDA Approval Letter, BLA 761115, Reference ID 4596074]* — "This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and duration of response. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in confirmatory trials."... "3504-1 Submit the final study report and datasets for progression-free survival and overall survival from trial IMMU-132-05 titled 'Phase III Study of Sacituzumab Govitecan (IMMU-132) in Refractory/Relapsed Triple-Negative Breast Cancer', to confirm clinical benefit of sacituzumab that may inform product labeling."... "Your application for sacituzumab govitecan-hziy was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues that were unexpected for a biologic of this class or in the intended population."

Note on the SAP/analysis relationship: unlike several other single-arm accelerated approvals in this census (e.g., selinexor/STORM, vismodegib/ERIVANCE BCC), the IMMU-132-01 SAP and FDA's statistical review did not specify a one-sided hypothesis test of ORR against a pre-specified performance-goal threshold — both the sponsor's SAP and the FDA reviewer describe only a descriptive exact-binomial CI around the observed ORR, consistent with the "no formal sample size determination" and "no formal statistical justification for the sample size" reviewer comments. This is also a rare case where FDA's principal reviewer-documented "deviations from the agreed analysis plan" concern methodology used to characterize the primary endpoint's central-review supportive analysis and the definition of a secondary time-to-event endpoint (DOR), rather than multiplicity or interim-analysis conduct as seen elsewhere in this census — and where the approval's central regulatory drama (a Complete Response Letter, a cancelled advisory committee meeting, and a manufacturing-facility data-falsification finding) was driven entirely by CMC/manufacturing-integrity concerns that FDA's own reviewers state were separate from, and did not undermine, the reliability of the clinical efficacy data.

### 111. Capmatinib (Tabrecta) — NDA 213591

**Sponsor:** Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) whose tumors have a mutation that leads to mesenchymal-epithelial transition (MET) exon 14 skipping, as detected by an FDA-approved test — approved under accelerated approval based on response rate and duration of response in two separately analyzed cohorts (treatment-naïve and previously treated)

**Approval date:** May 6, 2020 (accelerated approval, 21 CFR 314.500); converted to full/regular approval effective August 10, 2022 (NDA 213591/S-004, Prior Approval supplement fulfilling the postmarketing requirement)

**Pivotal trial:** GEOMETRY mono-1 (Study CINC280A2201/A2201), NCT02414139

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial supporting accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.500, multi-cohort trial with cohorts stratified by molecular-alteration subtype (MET exon 14 skipping mutation vs. MET amplification by gene copy number [GCN]) and line of therapy — of the trial's 7 cohorts, only the two MET exon-14-skipping-mutation cohorts (Cohort 4, previously treated, N=69; Cohort 5b, treatment-naïve, N=28) supported this NDA's approved indication, while the MET-amplification cohorts (1a, 1b, 2, 3, 5a, 6) did not, companion diagnostic co-approval (FoundationOne CDx)
- *Endpoints:* overall response rate (ORR, primary, BIRC-assessed per RECIST 1.1 — confirmed CR+PR), duration of response (DOR, key secondary, BIRC), disease control rate, time to response, progression-free survival, overall survival (all secondary/descriptive, not formally testable in a single-arm design)
- *Primary analysis:* exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval around ORR by cohort in the full analysis set (FAS); one-sided exact binomial test (single-arm ORR hypothesis test) at α=0.025 per cohort, operationalized as rejecting H0 if the lower bound of the two-sided 95% exact CI exceeds a cohort-specific null threshold (25% for previously-treated cohorts including Cohort 4; 35% for treatment-naïve cohorts including Cohort 5b), against a "clinically relevant efficacy" point-estimate target of ~35% (pretreated cohorts) or ~55% (treatment-naïve cohorts)
- *Multiplicity:* not applicable in the conventional sense — each cohort tested independently against its own pre-specified null, no formal adjustment across cohorts because each cohort supports a logically distinct (and, for the amplification cohorts, ultimately unapproved) claim
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* per-cohort futility interim analysis based on a Bayesian predictive probability-of-success (POS) rule with a minimally informative Beta(0.3333,1) prior (Neuenschwander 2008 method), computed at a fixed number of evaluable patients per cohort (28 for Cohorts 1a/1b/2/4; 20 for Cohort 3), stopping for futility if POS<10%
- *Missing data/bias:* patients with a best overall response (BOR) of "Unknown" per RECIST 1.1, or with no BIRC data, were counted as non-responders in the ORR calculation (i.e., missing/indeterminate response imputed as treatment failure); FDA explicitly flagged the general limitation of single-arm trials — "potential for known and unknown patient selection bias" — and grounded approval in the magnitude/durability of response rather than the pre-specified thresholds themselves
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval (Subpart H/21 CFR 314.500) based on ORR/DOR as a surrogate reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit; confirmatory evidence via continuation/expansion of the same pivotal single-arm trial (not an independent trial) — the postmarketing requirement was fulfilled using additional follow-up data from Study A2201/GEOMETRY mono-1 itself, not a new trial; accelerated-to-regular approval conversion following confirmatory PMR fulfillment, effective August 10, 2022; no FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held — FDA's Multi-Discipline Review states the division did not refer the application to an advisory committee because it "did not raise significant public health questions on the role of capmatinib in the proposed indication" nor "significant safety or efficacy issues"

**Trial design & endpoints**

- GEOMETRY mono-1 (Study CINC280A2201, sponsor internal code INC280/capmatinib): multicenter, non-randomized, open-label, multi-cohort Phase 2 trial of oral capmatinib 400 mg twice daily in patients with advanced/metastatic NSCLC, enrolling 7 cohorts defined by MET alteration type (MET amplification, stratified further by gene copy number [GCN] thresholds ≥4, ≥6, ≥10; or MET exon 14 skipping mutation) and by line of therapy (treatment-naïve vs. one-to-two prior lines); the approval basis was limited to the two MET-exon-14-mutation cohorts, Cohort 4 (previously treated, N=69) and Cohort 5b (treatment-naïve, N=28), for a combined primary efficacy analysis population of 97 patients
- Primary endpoint: overall response rate (ORR) — proportion of patients with a best overall confirmed complete response (CR) or partial response (PR) per RECIST 1.1, assessed by a Blinded Independent Review Committee (BIRC) — analyzed separately by cohort, not pooled across cohorts, on the Full Analysis Set (FAS: all patients who received ≥1 dose)
- Key secondary endpoint: duration of response (DOR) by BIRC, calculated only among confirmed responders, from first documented response to first documented progression or death, censored at last adequate tumor assessment if no event, summarized by Kaplan-Meier methodology; DOR analysis by BIRC was gated on the primary ORR analysis being "considered positive"
- Other secondary/descriptive endpoints: ORR and DOR by investigator assessment (supportive), disease control rate, time to response, progression-free survival, and overall survival — all analyzed descriptively (Kaplan-Meier for time-to-event measures), explicitly not treated as formally testable given the absence of a comparator arm
- Sample-size/power logic and interim monitoring: the protocol's Section 10.8 sample-size tables show that, at N=69 (Cohorts 1a/1b/2/4) and N=27-28 (Cohorts 5a/5b/7), if the true ORR were 35% the probability of a "positive conclusion" at final analysis was ≥44%, rising to >90% at a true ORR of 45%+; a single per-cohort futility interim analysis (no formal alpha-spending function; not a fixed information-fraction group-sequential design) was planned once a fixed number of evaluable patients per cohort was reached (28 for Cohorts 1a/1b/2/4, 20 for Cohort 3), using a Bayesian predictive probability-of-success (POS) rule — POS = Prob[final observed ORR ≥ 35% | interim data], computed under a minimally informative Beta(0.3333,1) prior (mean 25%) — with the cohort stopped for futility if POS<10% (e.g., ≤7 of 28 evaluable responders in Cohorts 1a/1b/2/4); no interim analysis was planned for Cohorts 5a, 5b, or 6
- Missing data/censoring: BOR of "Unknown" and missing BIRC assessments were both counted as non-responders (i.e., treated as treatment failures, not excluded) when estimating ORR; patients who progressed and continued study drug were counted as PD at the time of progression rather than censored
- Results (as reported in the approved label, Table 5, BIRC assessment): treatment-naïve Cohort 5b — ORR 68% (95% CI 48-84%), including 4% CR; median DOR 12.6 months (95% CI 5.5-25.3), 47% with DOR ≥12 months; previously-treated Cohort 4 — ORR 41% (95% CI 29-53%); median DOR 9.7 months (95% CI 5.5-13.0), 32% with DOR ≥12 months. FDA's Multi-Discipline Review (using a later data cut for a subset of tables) reports near-identical figures: Cohort 5b ORR 67.9% (95% CI 47.6-84.1%), median DOR 11.14 months; Cohort 4 ORR 40.6% (95% CI 28.9-53.1%), median DOR 9.72 months
- Both cohort-specific thresholds for "clinically relevant efficacy" were met: Cohort 4's observed ORR (~41%) exceeded the ~35% target with a lower 95% CI bound (29%) above the pre-specified 25% null; Cohort 5b's observed ORR (~68%) exceeded the ~55% target with a lower 95% CI bound (48%) above the pre-specified 35% null
- A companion diagnostic, FoundationOne CDx, was reviewed and approved contemporaneously (supplemental premarket application from Foundation Medicine Inc.); 78 of the 97 primary-efficacy-population samples (originally confirmed via an RNA-based clinical trial assay) were retested with FoundationOne CDx, showing 99% (72/73 evaluable) positive percentage agreement

**Other resources**

- Novartis's general clinical-trial data-sharing commitments (e.g., via the former clinicalstudydatarequest.com consortium) were not individually confirmed for GEOMETRY mono-1; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for this trial specifically.
- No FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held for this NDA; FDA's Multi-Discipline Review states the division "did not refer this efficacy supplement to an advisory committee because the application did not raise significant public health questions on the role of capmatinib in the proposed indication," nor significant safety or efficacy issues.
- Postmarketing requirement (clinical PMR): submit final reports/datasets to confirm and further characterize clinical benefit, providing a more precise BIRC-assessed ORR/DOR estimate from ≥60 additional treatment-naïve patients (12-month minimum responder follow-up) and ≥85 additional previously-treated (platinum-pretreated) patients (6-month minimum responder follow-up); final report submission target was February 2022. This PMR was fulfilled via continued enrollment/follow-up of the same trial (Study A2201/GEOMETRY mono-1, expansion Cohorts 6 and 7), and the accelerated-approval indication was converted to full/regular approval via NDA 213591/S-004, effective August 10, 2022.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, GEOMETRY mono-1 Statistical Analysis Plan v1.0 (Final CSR), §2.7.2 "Statistical hypothesis, model, and method of analysis"]* — "The primary analysis will be performed on the FAS. The primary efficacy endpoint ORR will be estimated and the exact 95% confidence interval (CI) (Clopper and Pearson 1934) provided by cohort. Treatment with INC280 will be considered to have clinically relevant efficacy in cohort (1-4) if an ORR of ~35% is observed in that cohort with lower bound of exact 95% CI greater than 25%. Whereas, in cohorts (5a and 5b and 7), treatment with INC280 will be considered to have clinically relevant efficacy if an ORR of ~55% is observed in that cohort with lower bound of exact 95% CI greater than 35%. No hypothesis testing is planned for cohort 6."

*[verbatim, same source, §2.7.3 "Handling of missing values/censoring/discontinuations"]* — "Patients with a BOR of 'Unknown' per RECIST 1.1 will be considered as non-responders when estimating ORR. Patients with no BIRC data will be considered as non-responders when estimating ORR. Patients who have disease progression and continue to receive study drug after progression will qualify for PD at the time of progression and will be counted as PD in the derivation of ORR and any other efficacy endpoints."

*[verbatim, same source, §2.11 "Interim analysis for futility"]* — "The decision to stop for futility for the respective cohort at interim will be based on the probability of success (POS). POS is the probability of a positive conclusion of the study if the study continued beyond interim, (i.e., till the final analysis), given the interim observed data (x) and success among n patients. Thus, POS = Prob[ Final observed ORR ≥ 35% | x,n]. Minimally informative Beta distribution prior (Neuenschwander 2008) with prior mean equal to 25% will be used, i.e., the prior distribution will be Beta (0.3333, 1) for the POS calculations at the interim analysis. The respective cohort will be stopped for futility at the interim analysis if the respective POS < 10%."

*[verbatim, Amended Protocol Version 06 (Clean), Protocol No. CINC280A2201, §10.4.2 "Statistical hypothesis, model, and method of analysis"]* — "In addition, 5 hypotheses will be tested as following for the cohorts/sub-cohorts respectively (Hi0 and Hi1 correspond to cohort/sub-cohort i where i=1a, 1b, 2, 3 or 4) Hi0: ORR ≤ 25% In favor of the alternative Hi1: ORR > 25%... In addition, 3 hypotheses will be tested as following for the cohorts/sub-cohorts (Hi0 and Hi1 correspond to Sub-cohort i where i=5a, 5b or 7): Hi0: ORR ≤ 35% In favor of the alternative Hi1: ORR > 35% The tests will be performed based on the exact CI for ORR in each cohort/sub-cohort using a one-sided α= 0.025 level... The null hypothesis will be rejected if the lower bound of the two-sided 95% exact CI is >25% in Cohorts/Sub-cohorts 1a, 1b, 2, 3 and 4. And the null hypothesis will be rejected in Sub-cohorts 5a and 5b if the lower bound of the two-sided 95% exact CI is >35%."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 213591, Reference ID 4603952, Benefit-Risk Summary and Assessment]* — "In the opinion of the reviewers, the submitted evidence meets the statutory evidentiary standard for accelerated approval. Capmatinib has a favorable benefit-risk profile in the indicated population based on the high response rate and durable responses observed in a patient population with a life-threatening disease and an unmet medical need. Given the relatively limited duration of follow-up for both cohorts and the small number of treatment-naïve patients in the primary efficacy analysis population for this application, the current data are considered adequate to support accelerated approval rather than regular approval. Due to the relatively low incidence of MET mutations leading to exon 14 skipping in NSCLC, a randomized trial in this patient population is not feasible. To verify the clinical benefit of capmatinib in patients with NSCLC whose tumors have a mutation that leads to MET exon 14 skipping, additional data will be obtained from the clinical trial which supported this approval, Study A2201."

*[verbatim, same source, Benefit-Risk table, "Evidence and Uncertainties" column]* — "A limitation of single arm trials is the potential for known and unknown patient selection bias."

*[verbatim, same source, §9 "Advisory Committee Meeting and Other External Consultations"]* — "The division did not refer this efficacy supplement to an advisory committee because the application did not raise significant public health questions on the role of capmatinib in the proposed indication. The application also did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues."

*[verbatim, same source, §13 "Postmarketing Requirements and Commitment"]* — "Novartis has agreed to the following postmarketing requirement (PMR): Submit the final reports including datasets from clinical studies to confirm and further characterize the clinical benefit of capmatinib for the treatment of patients with Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) whose tumors have a mutation that leads to MET exon 14 skipping who are treatment-naïve and who have previously received platinum-based chemotherapy, by providing a more precise estimation of the blinded independent central review-assessed overall response rate and duration of response."

*[verbatim, FDA Supplement Approval Letter, NDA 213591/S-004, dated August 10, 2022]* — "This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for conversion from accelerated to full approval of Tabrecta tablets for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) whose tumors have a mutation that leads to mesenchymal-epithelial transition (MET) exon 14 skipping as detected by an FDA-approved test."

Note: this is a case where genuine, verbatim sponsor SAP and protocol text (both posted on ClinicalTrials.gov) independently corroborate the FDA review's account of the statistical design — an unusually well-documented single-arm accelerated approval. The posted SAP (v1.0, dated March 2023) is explicitly labeled "for Final CSR (End of Study)," i.e., it postdates the original 2020 accelerated-approval submission and reflects the trial's full, closed-out design (including the later PMR-fulfilling cohorts 6/7); its primary-objective, hypothesis-testing, and futility-rule language is nonetheless textually identical to the corresponding sections of the original Amended Protocol Version 06 (dated February 2019, the version in force at NDA submission) and to the FDA reviewer's own description of "the Applicant's Description" of the SAP, so no inference was needed to reconstruct the analysis actually used to support the 2020 approval.

### 112. Selpercatinib (Retevmo) — NDA 213246

**Sponsor:** Loxo Oncology, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Eli Lilly and Company

**Indication approved:** (1) Adult patients with metastatic RET fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); (2) adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older with advanced or metastatic RET-mutant medullary thyroid cancer (MTC) who require systemic therapy; (3) adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older with advanced or metastatic RET fusion-positive thyroid cancer who require systemic therapy and who are radioactive iodine-refractory (if radioactive iodine is appropriate) — all three indications approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DOR)

**Approval date:** May 8, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** LIBRETTO-001 (Study LOXO-RET-17001), a single multicenter, single-arm, open-label, first-in-human Phase 1/2 dose-escalation and dose-expansion trial, NCT03157128 — the sole trial supporting all three indications, with tumor-type- and treatment-history-defined analysis populations (not separate registration trials) carved out of one continuously enrolling study

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial (first-in-human dose-escalation and dose-expansion design) supporting accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.500/314.510; multi-cohort trial with independently analyzed, tumor-type- and treatment-history-defined primary analysis sets carved from one continuously enrolling study
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR) / duration of response (DoR) — ORR (primary, BICR-assessed per RECIST v1.1, confirmed CR+PR) analyzed separately per tumor-type/treatment-history population; DOR (secondary, Kaplan-Meier); intracranial ORR and intracranial DOR (IC-ORR/IC-DOR, pre-specified descriptive secondary endpoints in the NSCLC population with baseline measurable CNS metastases); progression-free survival, overall survival, clinical benefit rate — reported descriptively only, explicitly not interpretable in a single-arm design per FDA
- *Primary analysis:* exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval for ORR (2-sided 95%) by population; one-sided exact binomial test (single-arm ORR hypothesis test) operationalized as a pre-specified lower-CI-bound threshold rather than a formal p-value — effectiveness considered demonstrated for RET fusion-positive NSCLC if the ORR's 95% CI lower bound exceeded 30%, and for RET-mutant MTC if the lower bound exceeded 20% (no formal pre-specified threshold identified in the review for the smaller RET fusion-positive thyroid cancer population); Kaplan-Meier estimation for DOR
- *Multiplicity:* not applicable — each of the five tumor-type/treatment-history populations was analyzed independently against its own pre-specified threshold, with no formal alpha-splitting or joint multiplicity procedure across populations (distinct from the "Cohort-level Bonferroni alpha allocation" pattern used elsewhere in this census for a small number of jointly-tested biomarker cohorts; here, each population supports a logically separate, independently-approvable indication)
- *Missing data/bias:* not a conventional censoring/crossover issue for a single-arm accelerated approval; FDA explicitly declined to characterize DOR's median in the treatment-naive NSCLC population in labeling because only 3% of the 33 responders had an observed DOR ≥18 months at a short follow-up, judging the estimate potentially unreliable; FDA separately noted that CNS response data (IC-ORR 90.9% in 11 patients with baseline measurable CNS metastases) required cautious interpretation given the very small subgroup
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval (21 CFR 314.500/314.510) based on ORR/DOR as a surrogate reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit, granted simultaneously across three histologically distinct indications (NSCLC, MTC, thyroid cancer) from one ongoing single-arm trial; no FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting held; three separate postmarketing requirements (PMR 3829-1: a randomized trial of selpercatinib vs. physician's choice in kinase-inhibitor-naive MTC, with PFS as a key BICR-assessed secondary endpoint, to confirm clinical benefit for the MTC treatment-naive population; PMR 3829-2: continued single-arm follow-up in LIBRETTO-001 to more precisely estimate BICR ORR/DOR in NSCLC, both treatment-naive and platinum-pretreated; PMR 3829-3: continued single-arm follow-up to more precisely estimate BICR ORR/DOR in ≥50 additional RET fusion-positive thyroid cancer patients) — a notable case where the confirmatory-evidence requirement differs by indication (randomized trial required only for the MTC treatment-naive population; expanded single-arm follow-up sufficient for the others)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- LIBRETTO-001 (LOXO-RET-17001): open-label, multicenter, first-in-human Phase 1 (dose-escalation, 3+3-informed) and Phase 2 (dose-expansion) trial of oral selpercatinib (LOXO-292) in patients with advanced solid tumors harboring RET alterations, including RET fusion-positive NSCLC, RET-mutant MTC, RET fusion-positive thyroid cancer, and other RET-altered tumors, confirmed by a CLIA-certified (or equivalent ex-US) molecular pathology report; the recommended Phase 2 dose (160 mg twice daily) was selected during Phase 1 and used for all expansion-cohort enrollment
- Per FDA-agreed analysis-plan conventions incorporated into the SAP, the primary analysis of effectiveness for each indication was based on a fixed, sequentially-enrolled primary analysis set (PAS) rather than the full accruing population: the first 105 RET fusion-positive NSCLC patients who had progressed on/after platinum-based chemotherapy (with a separate, non-overlapping supplemental analysis set of 39 treatment-naive RET fusion-positive NSCLC patients), and the first 55 RET-mutant MTC patients previously treated with cabozantinib and/or vandetanib (with a separate supplemental analysis set of 88 treatment-naive MTC patients); RET fusion-positive thyroid cancer patients (n=27, RAI-refractory if appropriate to histology, including a previously-treated subset of 19 and an RAI-only subset of 8) formed an additional, smaller primary efficacy population
- Primary endpoint for each population: confirmed ORR (CR or PR per RECIST v1.1) assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR); the SAP pre-specified that effectiveness would be considered demonstrated for RET fusion-positive NSCLC if the lower bound of the ORR's 2-sided 95% exact (Clopper-Pearson) CI exceeded 30%, and for RET-mutant MTC if the lower bound exceeded 20%; DOR was summarized descriptively via Kaplan-Meier
- Results (Original NDA data cutoff June 17, 2019, updated in a 60-Day Safety Update dated December 16, 2019): RET fusion-positive NSCLC, platinum-pretreated (PAS, n=105) — confirmed ORR 63.8% (95% CI 53.9-73.0%), excluding the ORR range of approved second-line NSCLC therapy (ramucirumab+docetaxel, ORR 23%); treatment-naive (n=39) — ORR 84.6% (95% CI 69.5-94.1%), excluding the ORR range of approved first-line chemo-immunotherapy regimens (48-58%); median DOR not included in labeling for the treatment-naive population because only 3% of responders had observed DOR ≥18 months at the available follow-up
- RET-mutant MTC: previously treated with cabozantinib and/or vandetanib (PAS, n=55) — ORR 69.1% (95% CI 55.2-80.9%); treatment-naive (n=88) — ORR 72.7% (95% CI 62.2-81.7%), excluding the ORR of the only approved biomarker-unselected therapy (vandetanib, ORR 45%)
- RET fusion-positive thyroid cancer (n=27): previously-treated subset (n=19) — ORR 78.9% (95% CI 54.4-93.9%); RAI-only, no subsequent systemic therapy subset (n=8) — ORR 100% (95% CI 63-100%); responses were observed across histologic subtypes (papillary, poorly differentiated, anaplastic), a response rate FDA judged to compare favorably with lenvatinib (65%) and sorafenib (12%) in the broader RAI-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer population regardless of RET status
- Intracranial activity in NSCLC was a pre-specified descriptive secondary analysis: among 11 patients in the NSCLC PAS with baseline measurable CNS metastases (BICR-assessed, no brain radiation within 2 months of first dose), confirmed intracranial ORR was 90.9%, though FDA cautioned this point estimate warranted caution given the very small subgroup
- FDA's review states, for each indication, that a randomized trial was not considered feasible given the rarity of the genetically-defined populations, and that the ORR magnitude plus observed durability were sufficient to establish clinical benefit in each population without a concurrent comparator; time-to-event endpoints (PFS, OS) and clinical benefit rate were treated as non-interpretable in this single-arm design and excluded from the substantial-evidence-of-effectiveness determination
