**Other resources**

- Eli Lilly participates in general clinical-trial data-sharing platforms; trial-specific individual patient data (IPD) availability for LIBRETTO-001/NCT03157128 via Vivli, YODA, or another platform was not individually confirmed, and no such listing was identified during this review.
- No FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held. Per the FDA Multi-Discipline Review, §9: "FDA did not hold an advisory committee meeting for these applications because no review issues were identified that raised significant public health questions regarding the risk:benefit assessment of selpercatinib for the proposed indications."
- Postmarketing requirements (per the Multi-Discipline Review §13 and the approval letter): PMR 3829-1 (a randomized, multicenter trial comparing selpercatinib to physician's choice of approved therapy in kinase-inhibitor-naive, progressive, advanced/metastatic RET-mutant MTC, with BICR-assessed PFS as a key secondary endpoint, to confirm clinical benefit for the MTC treatment-naive indication); PMR 3829-2 (continued follow-up within the same ongoing trial to more precisely estimate BICR-assessed ORR/DOR in both treatment-naive and platinum-pretreated RET fusion-positive NSCLC, requiring minimum responder follow-up of 12 and 6 months respectively, in expanded populations of at least 65 and 180 patients); PMR 3829-3 (continued follow-up within the same trial in at least 50 total RET fusion-positive thyroid cancer patients, 12 months minimum responder follow-up, to more precisely estimate BICR ORR/DOR); PMR 3829-4 (integrated long-term safety analysis characterizing growth-and-development effects, including growth-plate abnormalities, in adolescent patients with MTC and thyroid cancer).
- A separate pediatric trial (LOXO-RET-18036, Phase 1/2, ages 6 months-21 years, RET-altered solid or primary CNS tumors) had enrolled 2 patients as of November 2019 and was ongoing at the time of this approval, unrelated to the adult/adolescent indications approved here.

*[verbatim, same source, §13, PMR 3829-2]* — "Submit a final report including datasets from an ongoing clinical trial to verify and further characterize the clinical benefit of selpercatinib for the treatment of patients with 1) treatment-naïve RET fusion-positive NSCLC and with 2) RET fusion-positive NSCLC who have previously received platinum chemotherapy that will provide a more precise estimation of the BICR-assessed overall response rate and duration of response after all responders in the population of at least 65 patients have been followed for at least 12 months from the date of initial response... and after all responders have been followed for at least 6 months in the population of patients (at least 180 patients) with NSCLC previously treated with platinum therapy."

Continued approval for these indications may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in confirmatory trial(s)."

Note on sourcing: no genuine sponsor SAP or protocol document reflecting the version operative at this May 2020 approval is publicly posted — the Protocol and SAP now posted on ClinicalTrials.gov (SAP Version 3, dated December 2022; Protocol dated August 2023) are materially later versions reflecting the trial's continued maturation and use "proposed indication"-based analysis groupings rather than the original protocol-defined cohort structure described in the approval-era SAP (dated 08 August 2019, referenced but not separately posted). All SAP-specific content quoted above is instead drawn directly from the FDA Multi-Discipline Review's verbatim reproduction of the Applicant's SAP description, which is treated here as the most reliable public source for the original approval-era analysis plan; no inference/reverse-engineering was needed since the review quotes the SAP's threshold language and sample-size logic directly. This is also a rare example in this census of a single ongoing early-phase trial supporting three histologically distinct indications simultaneously, each accelerated-approval indication carrying a differently-scoped confirmatory-evidence requirement (a randomized trial for treatment-naive MTC; expanded single-arm follow-up within the same trial for the other four populations).

### 113. Ripretinib (Qinlock) — NDA 213973

**Sponsor:** Deciphera Pharmaceuticals, LLC

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adult patients with advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) who have received prior treatment with 3 or more kinase inhibitors, including imatinib (i.e., 4th-line-or-later disease)

**Approval date:** May 15, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** INVICTUS (Study DCC-2618-03-001), NCT03353753

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven trial (primary analysis triggered by accrual of a target number of PFS events), crossover permitted at progression (placebo patients unblinded and offered ripretinib after BICR-confirmed progression; 66% of placebo patients switched)
- *Endpoints:* progression-free survival (PFS, primary, BICR-assessed per modified RECIST 1.1 for GIST), objective response rate (ORR, key secondary, BICR-assessed), overall survival (OS, secondary, gated), patient-reported outcomes / HRQoL (EORTC QLQ-C30 role- and physical-functioning subscales and EQ-5D-5L/EQ-VAS, gated secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified), Kaplan-Meier estimation, Fisher's exact test (unstratified, for ORR)
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (PFS → ORR → OS → QOL, each tested only if the prior endpoint was significant at the 2-sided 0.05 level; testing stopped at ORR, so OS and QOL were reported descriptively only)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* O'Brien-Fleming boundary (applied post hoc to a single primary analysis conducted with 88 of the 90 planned PFS events, adjusting the significance threshold to 0.047, rather than as part of a genuine multi-look group-sequential design), Data Monitoring Committee (independent Data Monitoring Committee, IDMC)
- *Missing data/bias:* standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment, FDA-conducted post hoc covariate-adjusted sensitivity analysis (baseline imbalance) (FDA independently examined PFS/ORR/OS by pre-specified age subgroup after noting more older patients were enrolled on the placebo arm), sponsor-conducted BICR-vs-investigator discordance analysis for disease progression (20.2% overall discordance)
- *Regulatory:* Regular approval (not accelerated) based on a randomized, controlled Phase 3 trial with PFS as the primary endpoint; no FDA Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- INVICTUS (DCC-2618-03-001): Phase 3, international, multicenter, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of ripretinib 150 mg orally once daily plus best supportive care vs. placebo plus best supportive care in patients with advanced GIST who had progressed on or were intolerant to imatinib, sunitinib, and regorafenib; 129 patients (85 ripretinib, 44 placebo) were randomized at 29 sites in 12 countries between Feb 27, 2018 and Nov 16, 2018 (of 154 patients screened)
- Randomization was via interactive response technology (IRT), using randomly permuted blocks of six, and stratified by number of prior therapies (3 vs. ≥4) and ECOG performance status (0 vs. 1 or 2); enrollment of patients with ≥4 prior therapies was capped at <40% of the study population
- Primary endpoint: progression-free survival (PFS), defined as the interval from randomization to the earliest documented disease progression by blinded independent central review (BICR, per modified RECIST v1.1 for GIST, in which lymph nodes and bone lesions are not target lesions) or death from any cause on initially assigned treatment, whichever occurred first, analyzed only for the double-blind period
- Key secondary endpoint: objective response rate (ORR) by BICR (confirmed CR or PR, confirmation required ≥4 weeks after criteria first met); other secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS, time from randomization to death from any cause), quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30 role- and physical-functioning subscales, EQ-5D-5L, EQ-VAS, change from baseline to Cycle 2 Day 1), time to tumor progression (TTP), and duration of response (DOR); disease control rate and PK/PD analyses were planned but not part of the double-blind efficacy report
- Crossover design element: patients were unblinded at BICR-confirmed progression; placebo patients could then cross over to open-label ripretinib 150 mg QD (66% of placebo-arm patients ultimately did so), while ripretinib patients at progression could dose-escalate to 150 mg BID, continue at the same dose, or discontinue — this crossover was built into the protocol from the start (not an amendment), and OS was analyzed on the original randomized assignment (ITT) without any crossover-adjustment method (e.g., RPSFT/IPCW) applied
- Sample size/power: a sample of 120 patients (80 ripretinib : 40 placebo, later refined to the actual 129/85/44) was calculated assuming 15% dropout and a two-sided 0.05 significance level, giving >90% power to detect a PFS difference (assumed median PFS 4.5 months ripretinib vs. 1.0 month placebo) and ~80% power for a 20% ORR difference (22% vs. 2%); the primary analysis was planned to occur at 90 accrued PFS events but was actually conducted with 88 events at the May 31, 2019 data cutoff
- Statistical methods: PFS and OS were compared using a two-sided stratified log-rank test (stratified by the two randomization factors) at the 0.05 level, with hazard ratios and 95% CIs from a stratified Cox proportional-hazards model (Wald-method CIs); ORR was compared using an unstratified two-sided Fisher's exact test, with the ORR difference's 95% CI from the Newcombe method; time-to-event endpoints were summarized by Kaplan-Meier methodology; multiplicity across PFS→ORR→OS→QOL was controlled by fixed-sequence gatekeeping, each endpoint tested only if the prior one was significant
- The SAP was amended once (Final 1.0, 28 Nov 2018 → Final 2.0, 08 Aug 2019); the protocol itself was amended five times, including Amendment 1 (07 Nov 2017, before enrollment began) which replaced time-to-tumor-progression with ORR as the key secondary objective and specified an unstratified log-rank/Cox primary analysis, and Amendment 5 (30 Oct 2018, mid-trial but pre-database-lock/pre-unblinding) which changed the primary population label from "mITT" to "ITT," clarified missing-data handling and multiplicity adjustments (dropping low-power/low-importance endpoints from the testing hierarchy and clarifying which QOL measures were gated), and — to comply with ICH guidance — switched the primary PFS and OS models from unstratified to stratified
- Results (31 May 2019 cutoff): PFS — 51/85 (60%) ripretinib patients and 37/44 (84%) placebo patients had events; median PFS 6.3 months (95% CI 4.6–6.9) vs. 1.0 month (0.9–1.7); stratified HR 0.15 (95% CI 0.09–0.25), 2-sided stratified log-rank p<0.0001 (remained significant even after an O'Brien-Fleming adjustment to alpha=0.047, applied because the actual 88 events fell slightly short of the planned 90). ORR: 9.4% (8/85) vs. 0% (0/44), Fisher's exact p=0.0504 — not statistically significant, closing the multiplicity gate. OS: median 15.1 months (12.3–15.1) vs. 6.6 months (4.1–11.6), HR 0.36 (95% CI 0.21–0.62), nominal log-rank p=0.0004 — not formally tested per the pre-specified hierarchy (no alpha remained), and the label explicitly states OS was "[n]ot evaluated for statistical significance as a result of the sequential testing procedure." FDA disagreed with the Applicant's characterization of a "37 weeks added survival benefit," calling OS inferences exploratory given no alpha was allocated to test it
- FDA noted an enrollment imbalance in older patients on the placebo arm and independently re-ran PFS/ORR/OS by pre-specified age subgroup (18–64, 65–74, ≥75 years); results were consistent with the overall analysis and did not change FDA's conclusions
- No major statistical issues were identified overall; FDA concluded the trial supported regular (not accelerated) approval based on a statistically significant and clinically meaningful PFS improvement

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2020/213973Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2020/213973s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (combined Clinical/Statistical/Non-Clinical/Clinical Pharmacology Review, Reference ID 4609309/4609640) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/213973Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (INVICTUS) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03353753 (no protocol or SAP document posted in the Documents tab as of this writing; confirmed via the ClinicalTrials.gov API `documentSection` field, which is empty for this study)
- Protocol / SAP: not publicly posted on ClinicalTrials.gov; the pivotal publication's data-sharing statement indicates Deciphera intended to post a redacted protocol and make individual patient data available on request (see "Other resources" below)
- Pivotal publication: Blay J-Y, Serrano C, Heinrich MC, Zalcberg J, Bauer S, Gelderblom H, Schöffski P, Jones RL, Attia S, D'Amato G, Chi P, Reichardt P, Meade J, Shi K, Ruiz-Soto R, George S, von Mehren M, for the INVICTUS investigators. "Ripretinib in patients with advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumours (INVICTUS): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial." *Lancet Oncol.* 2020;21(7):923-934. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(20)30168-6>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32511981/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Ripretinib%20in%20patients%20with%20advanced%20gastrointestinal%20stromal%20tumours%20%28INVICTUS%29%3A%20a%20double-blind%2C%20randomised%2C%20placebo-controlled%2C%20phase%203%20trial)

**Other resources**

- Deciphera's data-sharing statement in the pivotal publication states the company will share a redacted INVICTUS protocol online and will consider qualified researcher requests for de-identified individual patient data submitted to the company directly; trial-specific participation in Vivli, the YODA Project, or Project Data Sphere was not identified and is not confirmed.
- No FDA Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held for this application. The Multi-Discipline Review states: "No major review issues were identified during the review of this application and thus, the review team did not seek input from external consultants or refer the application to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, Blay et al. 2020, Lancet Oncology, Methods — "Statistical analysis"]* — "A sample size of 120 patients (ripretinib, n=80; placebo, n=40) was calculated to provide both power for efficacy and size for the safety database with an assumed 15% patient dropout, and a two-sided 0·05 significance level in testing the hypothesis of no difference between ripretinib and placebo was expected to provide over 90% power to detect a difference in progression-free survival between ripretinib and placebo. This power assumed a median progression-free survival of 4·5 months for ripretinib and 1·0 month for placebo and approximately 80% power to detect a 20% difference in objective response, with the assumption of an objective response for ripretinib of 22% and 2% for placebo. To control family-wise type I error, the hypothesis tests for treatment differences were done at a two-sided 0·05 level of significance sequentially in the following order: progression-free survival, objective response rate, overall survival, and QOL as determined by changes from baseline to cycle two on day 1 in physical and role functioning scale subsets of the EORTC-QLQ-C30 (each at 0·025 level of significance). Other endpoints (eg, time to progression, time to best response, and investigator-assessed progression-free survival) were not included in the hierarchy because we deemed that there would be insufficient power to test these. Once a hypothesis test was non-significant at α=0·05 level, the remaining analyses were reported as descriptive."

*[verbatim, same source, Methods — "Randomisation and masking" / "Procedures"]* — "Randomisation was done via an interactive response technology system by use of randomly permuted block sizes of six and stratified according to number of previous therapies (three vs four or more) and ECOG performance status (0 vs 1 or 2)... Patients, investigators, research staff, and the sponsor study team were masked to a patient's treatment allocation until the blinded independent central review (BICR) confirmed progressive disease for the patient. At the time of progressive disease by BICR (as defined by mRECIST version 1.1), patients were unblinded and offered the option to continue or crossover to ripretinib open-label therapy."

*[verbatim, same source, Methods]* — "We used a two-sided stratified log-rank test (0·05 significance level) to evaluate treatment difference. Hazard ratios (HRs) were obtained from a Cox regression model, and the 95% CIs were obtained using the Wald method... Objective response was analysed by an unstratified two-sided Fisher's exact test (using a 0·05 significance level) to evaluate treatment difference, and the 95% CI of the treatment difference was calculated with the Newcombe method."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 213973, Reference ID 4609309/4609640, §8.1.1, "Statistical Analysis Plan and Amendments," The Applicant's Description]* — "The SAP was finalized prior to the conduct of any efficacy analysis and unblinding of the database... One amendment was made to the SAP for this study. SAP version history for this study is below: Statistical Analysis Plan – Final 1.0 (28 Nov 2018); Statistical Analysis Plan – Final 2.0 (08 Aug 2019)."

*[verbatim, same source, Table 4: DCC-2618-03-001 Protocol Amendments, "Amendment 5, 30 October 2018"]* — "Clarified the statistical analysis methodology, including: Clarified the analysis population definitions, including a global change of 'mITT' to 'ITT'; Clarified the procedures for handling missing data; Clarified adjustments for multiplicity comparisons, including removing endpoints with low power and importance in the multiplicity testing procedure and clarified the QOL endpoints to be included in the testing procedure; Clarified the conditions under which study unblinding may take place; Clarified that the primary analysis would take place when 90 PFS events have occurred; For the primary endpoint analysis (PFS) and the analysis of overall survival, changed the unstratified model to stratified model with stratification factors to comply to the ICH guidance."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.1.2, "Efficacy Results – Primary Endpoint"]* — "Patients in the ripretinib arm had an 85% reduced risk of disease progression or death which was statistically significant (hazard ratio = 0.15; stratified log-rank test p < 0.0001) compared to placebo. Since the number of PFS events included in the primary analysis (88 events) was less than the planned 90 events, an O'Brien-Fleming method was considered to assess the robustness of the result. Using the O'Brien-Fleming method, the alpha level was adjusted to be 0.047 and the hypothesis test of PFS (p<0.0001) still remained highly statistically significant at the adjusted alpha level."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.1.2, "Efficacy Results – Secondary and other relevant endpoints"]* — "Ripretinib demonstrated an ORR of 9.4% compared with 0% for placebo (p-value = 0.0504), which was not statistically significant... ripretinib in this study also showed a clinically meaningful improvement over placebo in terms of the secondary endpoint OS (median OS 65.6 weeks vs. 28.6 weeks, HR = 0.36, nominal p-value = 0.0004). Because of the prespecified hierarchical alpha spending plan for secondary endpoints and since statistical significance was not achieved for ORR, the hypothesis testing of OS was not formally performed."

*[verbatim, same source, Regulatory Authorities' Assessment, following the primary-endpoint results]* — "The FDA does not agree with the Applicant statement that there is 37 weeks added survival benefit in patients who were randomized to the ripretinib arm compared to those who were randomized to the placebo arm; inferences based on observed survival results should be interpreted with caution and are considered by FDA to be exploratory due to lack of allocation of alpha to test OS."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.3, "Statistical Issues"]* — "No major statistical issues were identified while reviewing the data and results submitted in this application; however, FDA noted an imbalance between the treatment groups with respect to older patients. Additional analyses were performed to assess the impact of this imbalance on the primary and key secondary endpoints considered in the study. In general, the results appear to be robust and there was no impact on the conclusions."

*[verbatim, same source, §9, "Advisory Committee Meeting and Other External Consultations"]* — "No major review issues were identified during the review of this application and thus, the review team did not seek input from external consultants or refer the application to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee."

*[verbatim, Package Insert, Table 6 footnote "e"]* — "Not evaluated for statistical significance as a result of the sequential testing procedure for the secondary endpoints of ORR and OS."

This is a genuine example of a fixed-sequence multiplicity gate (PFS → ORR → OS → QOL) closing at the second step: because ORR narrowly missed significance (p=0.0504 vs. the 0.05 threshold), the numerically large and clinically striking OS effect (HR 0.36) could not be formally claimed, and both FDA and the approved label explicitly flag the resulting OS point estimate as non-confirmatory — a clean illustration of how a hierarchical testing procedure, not the underlying effect size, determines what a sponsor is permitted to claim.

### 114. Fluoroestradiol F18 (Cerianna) — NDA 212155

**Sponsor:** Zionexa-US Corporation (NDA holder of record at approval; the compound and its predecessor French-market product, Estrotep, were developed academically over three decades at institutions including the University of Washington before Zionexa's 505(b)(2) submission; per the 2024-revised label, Cerianna is now "Distributed by GE Healthcare Inc., Marlborough, MA," reflecting GE Healthcare's subsequent acquisition of the product)

**Indication approved:** A radioactive diagnostic agent indicated for use with positron emission tomography (PET) imaging to detect estrogen receptor (ER)-positive lesions as an adjunct to biopsy in patients with recurrent or metastatic breast cancer; labeling explicitly states tissue biopsy should be used to confirm recurrence and verify ER status by pathology, and that Cerianna does not image HER2 or the progesterone receptor

**Approval date:** May 20, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** No sponsor-conducted pivotal trial exists. Zionexa's 505(b)(2) submission relied on published reports of three independently designed, independently sponsored academic studies, none run by the Applicant: Study 1, Chae et al. 2019 (Asan Medical Center, South Korea), NCT01986569; Study 2, Peterson et al. 2014 (University of Washington/Fred Hutchinson, sponsored by the U.S. National Cancer Institute), NCT00602043; and Study 3, Venema et al. 2017 (University Medical Center Groningen, Netherlands), NCT01988324. A fourth study, Estrotepredic (NCT01627704, Assistance Publique-Hôpitaux de Paris), an exploratory trial of FES to predict hormone-therapy response, was also submitted but was not relied upon for the approved detection indication.

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* retrospective/non-prospective diagnostic evidentiary basis (academic or literature-derived, not a company-sponsored pivotal trial); diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient comparison of FES PET against a histopathology/IHC reference standard, rather than an active-comparator drug); 505(b)(2) NDA relying on three independently conducted, non-pooled academic studies rather than a single integrated dataset (contrast with the cross-study pooling protocol used for Ga 68 DOTATOC/NDA 210828)
- *Endpoints:* positive percent agreement (PPA) and negative percent agreement (NPA) of qualitative FES-PET reads vs. immunohistochemical (IHC) Allred-score ER status on the largest biopsied lesion (concordance rate (diagnostic/mapping agent vs. reference standard), FDA/study-author terminology in place of "sensitivity/specificity"); performance-measure analysis without full index-test/reference-standard independence (verification bias) — FDA explicitly attributes the PPA/NPA (rather than sensitivity/specificity) terminology to image readers being unblinded to the location of the largest biopsied ("reference") lesion, even though fully blinded to the biopsy's pathology result
- *Primary analysis:* descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (point estimate + CI, no formal hypothesis test) — applied here to PPA/NPA rather than oncology response rate; no pre-specified performance-goal hypothesis test was used, unlike other diagnostic-agent precedents in this census (Lymphoseek, Ga 68 DOTATOC); point estimates reported with an approximate 95% confidence interval (exact CI-construction method not specified in the FDA review)
- *Missing data/bias:* FDA review flags ER-status heterogeneity across lesions and over time (documented via external literature, Yang et al. 2018 and Meng et al. 2016) as a limitation on interpreting any single-lesion, single-timepoint reference standard; the review separately flags that reader unblinding to reference-lesion location "restricts generalizability of the primary endpoint," and that the Applicant could not obtain per-reader/per-lesion line-item data from Study 1's authors when FDA requested it
- *Regulatory:* 505(b)(2) approval built on the Applicant's literature review, undertaken at FDA's own request (Pre-IND meeting, September 19, 2017: "FDA requested a protocol for literature review"); no Office of Scientific Investigations (OSI)/bioresearch-monitoring inspection was conducted because "the approvability of this NDA does not rely on sponsor-conducted studies"; no FDA advisory committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- This is a diagnostic PET imaging agent, not a therapeutic drug, and there is no OS/PFS/ORR primary endpoint, no randomization, no control arm, and no multiplicity/alpha-spending/interim-monitoring apparatus — the entire RCT-SAP framework this census otherwise documents does not apply
- FDA's Division of Imaging and Radiation Medicine (DIRM) review states plainly that "efficacy evaluation for this 505(b)(2) submission primarily relied on a published study report from an uninspected investigational site and without review of submitted patient- and reader-level data"
- Study 1 (Chae et al. 2019), the study the review "mainly relied on," was itself a prospective, non-randomized, single-center (Asan Medical Center, Seoul) Phase 3 cohort study of 90 women with recurrent/metastatic breast cancer; 85 of 90 completed both an FES-PET scan and had a biopsy with IHC ER assessment (efficacy-evaluable population)
- Endpoint definition: each patient's largest biopsied ("reference") lesion was scored by three blinded nuclear-medicine readers as FES-positive/negative (majority read used); ER status by the reference lesion's Allred score (positive if ≥3 of 0-8); PPA/NPA computed by comparing the two
- Results (Study 1, N=85): 47 patients were ER-positive by IHC; FES-PET was positive in 36 (PPA 76.6%, i.e., 23.4% false-negative rate, 95% CI approx. 12.3-38%); all 38 ER-negative patients had a negative FES scan (NPA 100%); recast as predictive values, positive predictive agreement was 100% and negative predictive agreement 77.6%; inter-reader kappa was 0.90
- FDA identified a "recurring issue in the design of studies for new diagnostic imaging drugs": image readers, while blinded to pathology results, were told the location of the largest biopsied lesion before scoring — a partial breakdown of index-test/reference-standard independence that the review explicitly ties to the study authors' and FDA's shared preference for "PPA/NPA" over "sensitivity/specificity" terminology
- Study 2 (Peterson et al. 2014, University of Washington, NCI-sponsored) and Study 3 (Venema et al. 2017, Groningen) were smaller (13-15 efficacy-evaluable patients each), used largely quantitative SUV-threshold (>1.5) FES-positivity criteria rather than Study 1's qualitative reads, and were treated by FDA as supportive/confirmatory rather than primary evidence; FDA's own conclusion states it relied "primarily on Study 1 plus confirmatory evidence from Study 2"
- No statistical hypothesis test against a pre-specified performance goal was used (contrast with the one-sided exact-binomial-against-a-performance-goal approach used for Technetium Tc 99m tilmanocept/Lymphoseek and Ga 68 DOTATOC); FDA's Statistical Issues section instead reasons qualitatively that "PPA and NPA exceed clinically meaningful thresholds for detecting ER-positive lesions"
- FDA required labeling changes (added "as an adjunct to biopsy" language and a new "Risk of Misdiagnosis"/"False Negative CERIANNA Scan" warning) specifically to address the observed 23.4% false-negative rate and the single-lesion/single-timepoint limitations of the reference standard, rather than requiring additional clinical data
- No Statistical Analysis Plan exists for this application in the conventional sense; FDA's own review states plainly, for Study 1: "Statistical Analysis Plan: Not applicable for this literature-based review"

- Package Insert / Label (original, 2020) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2020/212155s000lbl.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (revised, 2024, post-acquisition by GE HealthCare) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/212155s021lbl.pdf

**Other resources**

- No IPD/dataset-sharing program (Vivli, YODA, Project Data Sphere) was identified for Zionexa or GE Healthcare in connection with Cerianna; as with other literature-based diagnostic-agent NDAs in this census, trial-specific IPD access should not be assumed absent explicit confirmation, and in any case the underlying data belong to three independent academic sponsors (Asan Medical Center, NCI, University Medical Center Groningen), not the Applicant.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held. Per FDA's review, §9: "There was no advisory committee meeting or other external consultations for this NDA review."
- Cerianna is one of a small family of academic-origin PET tracers reviewed by FDA's Division of Imaging and Radiation Medicine on a literature-based 505(b)(2) evidentiary basis in this era, alongside Ga 68 DOTATOC (NDA 210828, University of Iowa) and, earlier, Fluciclovine F 18/Axumin and Gallium Ga 68 dotatate/Netspot — though unlike Ga 68 DOTATOC's RET-NET-01, no formal cross-study pooling protocol was submitted here; the three studies were reviewed and reported individually.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

This is a genuine outlier in this census, structurally similar to Technetium Tc 99m tilmanocept/Lymphoseek (NDA 202207) and Ga 68 DOTATOC (NDA 210828): Cerianna is a diagnostic radiopharmaceutical with no sponsor-run pivotal trial, no SAP, and no randomized comparison. What follows is verbatim FDA review text (the closest available substitute for a genuine SAP), not an inferred reconstruction, because FDA's own combined review directly documents its statistical reasoning about the published literature it relied on.

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 212155, Reference ID 4610895, §7 "Sources of Clinical Data and Review Strategy," p.29]* — "The Applicant has submitted an original NDA for FES. The Applicant is seeking approval through the 505(b)(2) regulatory pathway and is relying on findings of safety and effectiveness from published literature... Since then, there have been more than 35 clinical studies of FES reporting on more than 1000 subjects. However, a search for investigations aimed at the MBC population yielded three relevant papers submitted by the Applicant."

*[verbatim, same source, §8, Study 1 (Chae et al. 2019), "Statistical Analysis Plan," p.34]* — "Not applicable for this literature-based review."

*[verbatim, same source, §8, Study 1 "Imaging Interpretation," Comment, p.33-34]* — "Mismatch between the scope of ascertainment between image reading (here from skull base to upper thighs) and the standard used for image performance quantification (here pathology from largest biopsied lesion, with typically only one lesion biopsied per patient) is a recurring issue in the design of studies for new diagnostic imaging drugs... a key disadvantage of this design is that while pathologists were fully independent of image readers, the converse was only partially true: image readers selected one lesion per subject for study interpretation with prior knowledge of the location of the largest biopsied lesion ('reference lesion'). This key methodological limitation constrains generalizability of the primary endpoints... It also explains the study authors' and review team's preference for descriptive terminology 'positive/negative percent agreement' (PPA/NPA) and 'positive/negative predictive agreement' over the identically calculated 'sensitivity/specificity' and 'positive/negative predictive value.' The latter more familiar terms are most meaningfully reserved for study designs that provide for greater independence between image reading and the standard used for performance quantification."

*[verbatim, same source, §8, Study 1 "Efficacy Results — Primary Endpoint," p.36-37]* — "FES scan was positive in 36 of 47 ER-positive patients, yielding a PPA of 76.6%. All 38 ER-negative patients had negative FES PET, yielding an NPA of 100%. With the same 2x2 tabulation data analyzed based on proportion of positive and negative FES scans, positive predictive agreement was 100% and negative predictive agreement was 77.6%... The review team requested that the Applicant obtain and submit reader-level performance data (per reader and per lesion line-item data) supporting this conclusion. Based on the response, although the Applicant was able to contact study authors, they were unable to obtain and submit the requested information."

*[verbatim, same source, §8 "Assessment of Efficacy Across Trials," p.41]* — "Such convergence mitigates against added uncertainty shared by all members of the review team, given that Applicant proposes to rely primarily on published reports, as authorized under 505(b)(2) of the FD&C, and review flexibility, as discussed in recent FDA draft guidance for industry Demonstrating Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness for Human Drug and Biological Products (December 2019)... In summary, relying primarily on Study 1 plus confirmatory evidence from Study 2, the review team finds substantial evidence that PPA and NPA exceed clinically meaningful thresholds for detecting ER-positive lesions in patients with recurrent or metastatic breast cancer."

*[verbatim, same source, §8 "Statistical Issues," p.46-47]* — "This application is 505(b)(2) with three relevant papers from the clinical literature... Sensitivity and specificity computations require that 'independently determined complete (lesion level) truth standard' be available. Therefore, the authors use, fittingly, the terminology of positive and negative percent agreements, which are pre-specified coprimary endpoints of the study. This study provides the statistical evidence in support of a FES indication for detection of ER positive metastatic/recurrent lesions via high PPrV and high NPA (both 100% with (approx.) 95% CI (90%, 100%))... High false negative results in this study (23.4%, 95% CI (12.3%, 38%)) raise concerns about the need to not rely on a discordant Cerianna scan."

*[verbatim, same source, §4 "Office of Scientific Investigations (OSI)," p.16]* — "The approvability of this NDA does not rely on sponsor-conducted studies, therefore no OSI review was conducted."

*[verbatim, same source, §3 "U.S. Regulatory Actions and Marketing History," p.15]* — "September 19, 2017: Pre-investigational new drug (Pre-IND) 135755 meeting for new drug application (NDA) submission with 505(b)(2) pathway; FDA requested a protocol for literature review."

*[verbatim, same source, §9 "Advisory Committee Meeting and Other External Consultations," p.49]* — "There was no advisory committee meeting or other external consultations for this NDA review."

*[verbatim, same source, §8 "Conclusions and Recommendations," p.48]* — "The review team finds that the benefit-risk of Cerianna is favorable for detection of estrogen receptor (ER)-positive lesions as an adjunct to biopsy in patients with recurrent or metastatic breast cancer. Applicant has agreed to major recommended labeling revisions, and the review team therefore recommends approval of this NDA."

Unlike every therapeutic-drug entry in this census, Cerianna's approval basis is a literature-based 505(b)(2) evaluation of three independently conducted, non-industry-sponsored diagnostic-accuracy studies (Korea, US/NCI, Netherlands) rather than a sponsor-run trial with a SAP. There is no randomization, no control arm, no survival/response endpoint, no formal multiplicity or alpha-spending procedure, and — distinct even from this census's other diagnostic-agent entries (Lymphoseek, Ga 68 DOTATOC) — no pre-specified statistical hypothesis test against a performance goal at all; FDA's conclusion rests on a qualitative judgment that descriptive PPA/NPA point estimates "exceed clinically meaningful thresholds," paired with labeling changes (an explicit false-negative-rate warning and "adjunct to biopsy" language) to manage the residual uncertainty. This is documented honestly here rather than forced into the RCT/SAP template used for therapeutic drugs.

### 115. Lurbinectedin (Zepzelca) — NDA 213702

**Sponsor:** NDA held by Pharma Mar USA, Inc. (the FDA approval letter is addressed to Pharma Mar USA, Inc.); the molecule was discovered and is globally developed by PharmaMar, S.A. (Madrid, Spain). Jazz Pharmaceuticals holds an exclusive license/collaboration agreement for commercialization of lurbinectedin in the United States and jointly announced the 2020 approval with PharmaMar — the precise date and full terms of the Jazz–PharmaMar agreement were not independently verifiable in this session (web search was unavailable; PharmaMar/Jazz press-release URLs attempted via direct fetch returned 403/404), so this should be treated as a plainly-stated but not primary-source-confirmed detail.

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with metastatic small cell lung cancer (SCLC) with disease progression on or after platinum-based chemotherapy — approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DoR)

**Approval date:** June 15, 2020 (FDA Approval Letter, NDA 213702; the letter PDF's own creation timestamp is June 16, 2020 EDT)

**Pivotal trial:** PM1183-B-005-14 ("Study B-005"), the SCLC cohort of a multicenter, open-label, single-arm, multi-cohort Phase 2 basket trial ("A Multicenter Phase II Clinical Trial of Lurbinectedin (PM01183) in Selected Advanced Solid Tumors"), NCT02454972 — confirmed via the ClinicalTrials.gov registry record (sponsor PharmaMar, official title as above) and independently confirmed as the sole pivotal evidentiary trial in FDA's Multi-Discipline Review

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H/21 CFR 314.510; FDA's own review explicitly labels Study B-005 "a single-arm, multi-cohort, basket trial" (nine tumor-type-specific cohorts — SCLC, head and neck carcinoma, neuroendocrine tumors, biliary tract, endometrial, BRCA1/2 breast, carcinoma of unknown primary, germ cell tumors, Ewing's-family tumors — each analyzed independently by tumor type rather than pooled across histologies, unlike a tissue-agnostic basket trial)
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR) / duration of response (DoR) — here ORR by investigator assessment (IA) per RECIST v1.1 was the primary endpoint (not secondary, as in most randomized entries in this census), with IRC-assessed ORR as a secondary/supportive endpoint; progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were pre-specified secondary endpoints but summarized purely descriptively, with FDA explicitly stating single-arm data cannot adequately characterize time-to-event endpoints
- *Primary analysis:* sponsor's SAP pre-specified a one-sided exact binomial test (single-arm ORR hypothesis test) of H0: ORR≤15% vs. H1: ORR≥30% (fixed historical control rate of 15%, n=100 for 95% power); the sponsor's executed/reported primary analysis instead used an exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval (95% two-sided) around the observed ORR; FDA's reviewer explicitly declined to base the approval decision on the sponsor's hypothesis test at all, instead using a descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (point estimate + CI, no formal hypothesis test) — judging the ORR magnitude and 95% CI as excluding "clinically irrelevant" response rates, alongside a "clinically meaningful" duration of response
- *Multiplicity:* not applicable — one formal primary endpoint (ORR), no comparator arm, no multi-endpoint testing hierarchy
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* not a formal group-sequential/alpha-spending design; instead a multi-stage accrual-continuation rule based on interim response counts (see Design), added and revised across Protocol Amendments 02 and 05, with FDA review noting these amendments were made "to provide further details on the control of type I and II error probability" for two planned interim looks at 15 and 25 patients
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval (Subpart H, 21 CFR 314.510) based on ORR/DoR, confirmatory trial required (existing taxonomy term); no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held — FDA's review states plainly "the application did not raise significant public health questions regarding the role of lurbinectedin for the proposed indication"; the required confirmatory trial (ATLANTIS, PM1183-C-003-14, NCT02566993, a randomized Phase 3 trial of lurbinectedin+doxorubicin vs. investigator's-choice CAV/topotecan, OS primary endpoint) subsequently reported a negative result — HR 0.967 (95% CI 0.815–1.148), stratified log-rank p=0.9029, median OS 8.6 vs. 7.6 months — per ClinicalTrials.gov's posted results record; despite this, the SCLC monotherapy accelerated-approval indication is unchanged and still marked as accelerated approval, pending confirmatory verification, in the most recent label on file (213702s012, dated 2026) — a case, alongside olaratumab/ANNOUNCE and the Durvalumab urothelial withdrawal already in this census, worth comparing for how FDA handles a failed single confirmatory trial differently across sponsors/indications (here the accelerated approval has neither converted to regular approval nor been withdrawn as of this review)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study B-005 ("A Multicenter Phase II Clinical Trial of Lurbinectedin (PM01183) in Selected Advanced Solid Tumors") is an open-label, exploratory, single-arm, multi-cohort Phase 2 trial dosing lurbinectedin 3.2 mg/m² (capped at 6.4 mg) as a 60-minute IV infusion on Day 1 of each 21-day cycle, across nine tumor-type-defined cohorts; only the SCLC cohort (n=105) supports this NDA
- SCLC-cohort eligibility: pathologically confirmed SCLC, ECOG PS ≤2, exactly one prior chemotherapy-containing line (immunotherapy could have been given as part of that one line), measurable disease and documented progression per RECIST v1.1, adequate organ function; patients with known CNS involvement were excluded
- Primary efficacy endpoint: confirmed ORR (CR or PR as best overall response, per RECIST v1.1) by investigator assessment (IA) in the All Treated Patients population; secondary endpoints: ORR by independent review committee (IRC), duration of response (DoR, IA and IRC), progression-free survival (PFS, IA and IRC), and overall survival (OS)
- Design-stage sample size: 100 evaluable patients gave 95% power to test H0: ORR≤15% vs. H1: ORR≥30% (one-sided); ≥23 confirmed responses among 100 patients would reject H0. The design was originally staged (continue to 25 if ≥1 response in the first 15; continue up to 100 if ≥2 confirmed responses in the first 25), then further amended (Protocol Amendment 05, March 2017) to allow up to 100 SCLC patients and to add IRC review of tumor assessments
- Six substantial protocol amendments were made to the SCLC cohort between the original protocol (October 7, 2014) and July 2018, progressively expanding sample size, adding IRC assessment as a secondary endpoint, adding MRI as an option for brain-metastasis/tumor assessment, and extending survival follow-up
- Results (105 patients, data cutoff January 15, 2019 per the Statistical section table headers): investigator-assessed ORR 35% (95% CI 26–45%), median DoR 5.3 months (95% CI 4.1–6.4); IRC-assessed ORR 30% (95% CI 22–40%), median DoR 5.1 months (95% CI 4.9–6.4). By platinum sensitivity: platinum-resistant patients (43% of cohort, defined as progression <90 days after completing platinum-based chemotherapy) had IA ORR 22% (95% CI 11–37) vs. IRC ORR 13% (95% CI 5–27); platinum-sensitive patients (57%) had IA ORR 45% (95% CI 32–58) vs. IRC ORR 43% (95% CI 31–57)
- FDA's benefit-risk framing explicitly contrasts these results against topotecan (the only other FDA-approved second-line SCLC therapy), which historically showed ORR 24% (95% CI 16–32) and median DoR 3.3 months — a historical, non-randomized comparison, not a head-to-head trial
- Safety pool for the SCLC indication drew on the broader 554-patient safety database (335 from Study B-005 across all cohorts, 219 from a separate ovarian-cancer trial, CORAIL/PM1183-C-004-14, using the same dose/regimen); grade 3–4 adverse reactions ≥5% in the SCLC cohort were myelosuppression, fatigue, pneumonia, hyponatremia, elevated liver enzymes, and hyperglycemia
- Pre-submission regulatory history: the intended confirmatory trial (ATLANTIS, IND 127944) was placed under FDA full clinical hold in November 2015 because the original combination design (lurbinectedin+doxorubicin vs. topotecan) could not isolate lurbinectedin's individual contribution; the sponsor added a CAV (cyclophosphamide/doxorubicin/vincristine) control-arm option and a contribution-of-lurbinectedin secondary comparison, and the hold was lifted in March 2016. Orphan drug designation for SCLC was granted August 1, 2018. A Type B End-of-Phase-2 meeting (December 11, 2018) discussed the SCLC cohort of Study B-005 as the basis for an accelerated-approval application, with ATLANTIS intended to serve as confirmatory

[DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(20)30068-1>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32224306/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Lurbinectedin%20as%20second-line%20treatment%20for%20patients%20with%20small-cell%20lung%20cancer%3A%20a%20single-arm%2C%20open-label%2C%20phase%202%20basket%20trial)

**Other resources**

- No Vivli, YODA Project, or Project Data Sphere listing for Study B-005 (PM1183-B-005-14) was identified; PharmaMar's/Jazz's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed in this session.
- No FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held for this NDA; FDA's review states the application "did not raise significant public health questions regarding the role of lurbinectedin for the proposed indication."
- Confirmatory trial ATLANTIS (NCT02566993, PM1183-C-003-14): randomized Phase 3 trial of lurbinectedin+doxorubicin vs. investigator's-choice CAV or topotecan, primary endpoint OS. Per ClinicalTrials.gov's posted results, median OS was 8.6 months (95% CI 7.1–9.4) for lurbinectedin+doxorubicin vs. 7.6 months (95% CI 6.6–8.2) for control, HR 0.967 (95% CI 0.815–1.148), stratified log-rank p=0.9029 — a negative confirmatory trial. As of the most recent label on file (213702s012), the original 2020 accelerated-approval SCLC monotherapy indication remains in place, unconverted to regular approval and not withdrawn, alongside a newer (later-supplement) regular-approval indication for ES-SCLC maintenance therapy in combination with atezolizumab, added based on a different trial (not reviewed in depth here, as it falls outside this entry's 2020 approval scope).
- Postmarketing requirements (NDA 213702, per the Multi-Discipline Review's Section 13): PMR #3831-1 required submission of the final report/datasets for OS and IRC-assessed PFS from a confirmatory trial (explicitly naming ATLANTIS as the anticipated source), with the review's stated rationale that "[t]ime-to-event endpoints such as overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) cannot be adequately interpreted in single-arm clinical trials due to confounding effects of heterogeneity of the patient population."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 213702, Reference ID 4624183, §7 Sources of Clinical Data and Review Strategy]* — "The primary evidence establishing the efficacy of lurbinectedin in patients with SCLC whose disease progressed on or after prior platinum-containing therapy is derived from PM1183-B-005-14 (Study B-005), a single-arm, multi-cohort, basket trial investigating lurbinectedin in patients with a variety of advanced solid tumors, including a cohort of patients with SCLC that progressed on or after first-line treatment."

*[verbatim, same source, §8 Statistical and Clinical Evaluation, Statistical Analysis Plan]* — "The sponsor based their primary evaluation of efficacy on the comparison of ORR for lurbinectedin to a fixed historical control rate of 15%. The ORR was estimated using an exact binomial distribution and its 95% 2-sided exact confidence interval using the Clopper-Pearson method."

*[verbatim, same source, Reviewer Comment immediately following]* — "Although the sponsor proposed a hypothesis test for evaluation of efficacy, the FDA is basing its efficacy evaluation on what it considers to be an adequate ORR magnitude with corresponding 95% confidence interval excluding clinically irrelevant response rates and a clinically meaningful duration of response. Additionally, while the statistical analysis plan included summary statistics of PFS and OS as secondary efficacy endpoints, FDA notes that single arm trials do not adequately characterize time-to-event endpoints, making these results uninterpretable without a comparator."

*[verbatim, same source, Sample Size Considerations]* — "The sample size was updated in two protocol amendments. The first stage allowed for continuation of accrual to 25 evaluable patients if there was 1 response among the first 15 evaluable patients. The second stage allowed for continuation of accrual up to 100 evaluable patients if there were ≥2 confirmed responses in the first 25 evaluable patients. With 100 patients there was 95% power to test the null hypothesis that 15% or less patients achieve a response (p ≤ 0.15) versus the alternative hypothesis that 30% or more patients achieve a response (p ≥ 0.30). If the number of patients who achieved a confirmed response was ≥ 23, then this would allow the rejection of the null hypothesis."

*[verbatim, same source, Analysis Populations]* — "All Treated Patients, defined as all included patients who have received any partial or complete infusion of PM01183, will be used for the primary endpoint analysis of ORR and for the secondary endpoints of clinical benefit (ORR or stable disease ≥ 4 months), PFS (including PFS4/PFS6 months), and OS6/OS12 months. All Responding Patients, defined as all evaluable patients who have had a confirmed CR or PR as overall best response according to RECIST v1.1, will be used for the secondary endpoint analysis of DoR."

*[verbatim, same source, Protocol Amendment 05 (08-March-2017) summary]* — "Allow up to 100 patients in the small cell lung cancer (SCLC) cohort of the study[;] The statistical methods section has been amended to update the sequential test methodology and to provide further details on the control of type I and II error probability (alpha and beta), taking into account the two planned interim analysis performed at 15 and 25 patients per group for the expanded cohorts[.]"

*[verbatim, same source, Conclusions on the Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness]* — "The recommendation for accelerated approval, according to 21 CFR 314.510 Subpart H, is based on the results from a single trial, PM1183-B-005-14 (Study B-005), an ongoing, multicenter, open-label, non-randomized, multi-cohort trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of lurbinectedin as a single-agent in adult patients with advanced solid tumors. The efficacy is primarily based on results from a cohort of 105 patients with metastatic SCLC who had disease progression on or after first-line treatment with platinum-based chemotherapy... the confirmed investigator-assessed overall response rate (ORR), as per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version 1.1 (RECIST v.1.1), was 35% (95% CI: 26, 45). The median duration of response (DOR) was 5.3 months (95% CI: 4.1, 6.4)."

*[verbatim, same source, §9 Advisory Committee Meeting and Other External Consultations]* — "The Division did not refer this NDA to an advisory committee because the application did not raise significant public health questions regarding the role of lurbinectedin for the proposed indication. The demonstrated benefit-risk profile for lurbinectedin is favorable in patients with metastatic SCLC who have progressed after first-line therapy."

*[verbatim, same source, §13 Postmarketing Requirements and Commitment, PMR #3831-1 Rationale]* — "The proposed indication for lurbinectedin is treatment of adult patients with metastatic small cell lung cancer who have progressed on or after prior platinum-containing chemotherapy. Efficacy is based on data from a single, uncontrolled phase 2 study (PM1183-B-005-14), in which a cohort of 105 patients with SCLC, who had progressed following prior platinum-containing therapy, were treated with lurbinectedin as a single-agent... Time-to-event endpoints such as overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) cannot be adequately interpreted in single-arm clinical trials due to confounding effects of heterogeneity of the patient population. Long term efficacy outcomes including OS from a randomized controlled clinical trial are needed to confirm clinical benefit of lurbinectedin."

*[verbatim, FDA Approval Letter, NDA 213702, Reference ID 4624945]* — "This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate and duration of response. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial(s)."

Note: no sponsor-authored protocol or SAP document for Study B-005 is posted on ClinicalTrials.gov (confirmed by inspecting the record's `documentSection` via the CT.gov API — it is absent), so unlike some other entries in this census, every SAP-related passage above is genuine verbatim text from FDA's own Multi-Discipline Review (which itself quotes/paraphrases the sponsor's SAP content in describing it) rather than the sponsor's original SAP document — no inference/reverse-engineering was needed, since the FDA review's "Statistical Analysis Plan" and "Sample Size Considerations" subsections describe the sponsor's actual pre-specified analysis in detail, including the point where FDA explicitly departed from the sponsor's proposed hypothesis-testing framework in favor of a purely descriptive ORR/CI-based approval rationale.

### 116. Decitabine and cedazuridine (Inqovi) — NDA 212576

**Sponsor:** Astex Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (the NDA applicant of record; both Astex and its US commercial affiliate Taiho Oncology, Inc., which is the label's medical-inquiries/adverse-event contact, are subsidiaries of Otsuka Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.)

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS), including previously treated and untreated, de novo and secondary MDS with the following French-American-British subtypes (refractory anemia, refractory anemia with ringed sideroblasts, refractory anemia with excess blasts, and chronic myelomonocytic leukemia [CMML]) and intermediate-1, intermediate-2, and high-risk International Prognostic Scoring System groups

**Approval date:** July 7, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** ASTX727-02 ("ASCERTAIN"), NCT03306264, supported by the earlier phase 1/2 study ASTX727-01 (dose-confirmation/FDC stages, referred to as ASTX727-01-B in the FDA review) — **this was not a randomized efficacy trial; it was a PK/exposure-equivalence (bioequivalence-style) bridging study** comparing oral decitabine-cedazuridine to IV decitabine, leveraging IV decitabine's pre-existing 2006 efficacy approval

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two-period, two-sequence, randomized (1:1), open-label crossover trial with no stratification factors, used to bridge effectiveness from a previously approved reference product via demonstrated pharmacokinetic exposure-equivalence rather than a new randomized efficacy comparison; after the two crossover cycles, all subjects rolled over to open-label oral therapy only (single-arm from Cycle 3 onward)
- *Endpoints:* total 5-day AUC0-24 of decitabine (primary; PK exposure-equivalence endpoint, not a clinical/response endpoint), with maximum %LINE-1 DNA-demethylation (pharmacodynamic surrogate for decitabine's mechanism of action), IWG 2006 MDS response criteria (CR/mCR/PR/HI, externally adjudicated by 3 independent expert medical reviewers), RBC/platelet transfusion independence, leukemia-free survival, and overall survival as secondary/descriptive endpoints only
- *Primary analysis:* two one-sided tests (TOST) procedure for average bioequivalence — 90% CI of the geometric mean ratio (ASTX727 5-day AUC0-24 / IV decitabine 5-day AUC0-24) required to fall within pre-specified equivalence limits of 0.80-1.25
- *Multiplicity:* not applicable — a single formal PK equivalence hypothesis was tested; all clinical/efficacy secondary endpoints (response rate, transfusion independence, LFS, OS) were summarized descriptively only, with explicit no-comparison-between-sequences language in the SAP
- *Missing data/bias:* complete-case handling for the Primary Endpoint PK Analysis Population (required a full 5-day dosing course in both cycles, no dose delays >3 hours for oral dosing, no vomiting within 6 hours of oral dosing); two supplementary "Evaluable unpaired" and "Paired sensitivity" PK populations were pre-specified to test robustness to missing/excluded PK samples; no crossover-adjustment method was needed because the trial's PK/PD endpoints were assessed within each cycle rather than across a survival timeline
- *Regulatory:* FDA agreed to the PK-bridging regulatory strategy — establishing effectiveness via demonstrated exposure-equivalence to the previously approved IV decitabine rather than requiring a new randomized efficacy trial — at a Type B End-of-Phase 2 meeting held March 20, 2017, before the pivotal trial began; Orphan Drug Designation (granted August 21, 2019); Priority Review; no FDA Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ASTX727-02: Phase 3, multicenter (37 sites in the US and Canada), randomized (1:1), open-label, 2-period, 2-sequence crossover study in adults with MDS or CMML who were candidates to receive IV decitabine (ECOG 0-1, adequate hepatic/renal function, life expectancy ≥3 months); subjects were randomized to receive either the ASTX727 fixed-dose combination tablet (35 mg decitabine + 100 mg cedazuridine) once daily on Days 1-5 of Cycle 1 followed by IV decitabine 20 mg/m² once daily on Days 1-5 of Cycle 2, or the converse sequence; from Cycle 3 onward all subjects received open-label oral ASTX727 in 28-day cycles until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or withdrawal
- Randomization used a computer-generated schedule accessed via an interactive voice response system; there were no stratification factors and no blinding (open-label)
- Primary endpoint: total 5-day cumulative AUC0-24 of decitabine after ASTX727 vs. after IV decitabine, calculated from serial PK sampling on Days 1, 2, and 5 (ASTX727) and Days 1 and 5 (IV decitabine) of each cycle; adequate PK assessments from both Cycles 1 and 2 were required for a subject to be evaluable for the primary endpoint
- Secondary endpoints: safety (AEs, labs, ECOG, ECG); maximum %LINE-1 demethylation (pharmacodynamic surrogate for global DNA methylation, the biological readout of decitabine's mechanism); additional PK parameters (Cmax, Tmax, t1/2, CL/F, Vz/F for decitabine, cedazuridine, and cedazuridine-epimer); clinical response (CR/mCR/PR/HI per IWG 2006 MDS criteria, adjudicated by 3 independent expert medical reviewers blinded to treatment sequence, based on peripheral blood, bone marrow, and transfusion data); RBC/platelet transfusion independence (no transfusion for ≥56 consecutive days); leukemia-free survival and overall survival (from randomization) — all reported descriptively, with the SAP explicitly stating there would be "no comparison analyses between treatment sequences" for efficacy variables
- Sample size: based on an intra-subject CV of 0.55 (conservative estimate from the preceding ASTX727-01 study), 118 subjects in the Primary Endpoint PK Analysis Set were calculated to give 90% power for the two one-sided equivalence tests of the geometric mean AUC ratio at a 5% significance level, assuming a true ratio of 1.0 and 90% CI equivalence bounds of 0.80-1.25; allowing for ~10% non-evaluability, ~132 subjects were planned for randomization — 138 were ultimately randomized and 133 treated (of 173 screened, February 2018-June 2021)
- Result: primary-endpoint geometric mean ratio of total 5-day AUC0-24 (ASTX727 vs. IV decitabine) was 98.93% (90% CI 92.66-105.60) in the pivotal publication's paired-cycle analysis (FDA's own reviewer-run analysis in the Multi-Discipline Review reported a closely consistent 0.98, 90% CI 0.92-1.05, N=109) — within the pre-specified 80-125% equivalence bounds; maximum %LINE-1 demethylation was comparable between arms; CR rate was 21% (95% CI 15-29) in ASTX727-02 (133 pts) and 18% (95% CI 10-28) in the earlier ASTX727-01-B phase 2 study (80 pts), each consistent with the 16-17% ORR (9-15% CR) reported in IV decitabine's own approval-supporting studies
- Because this was designed and analyzed as PK-bridging (not an efficacy-comparative) trial, FDA's Statistical Review explicitly states both studies "are considered as single arm trial[s] in terms of efficacy assessment, therefore results of time to event endpoints are not interpretable" — i.e., the OS/LFS Kaplan-Meier curves generated from the crossover design carry no comparative efficacy weight and were not part of the effectiveness basis

- Astex Pharmaceuticals' general participation in IPD-sharing platforms (Vivli, YODA Project, Project Data Sphere) was not identified; trial-specific individual patient data availability for ASTX727-02/NCT03306264 was not confirmed.
- No FDA Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held for this application.
- FDA's Summary of Presubmission/Submission Regulatory Activity documents that the PK-bridging strategy itself — using demonstrated AUC exposure-equivalence to IV decitabine as the basis for effectiveness, rather than a new randomized efficacy trial — was proposed by the sponsor and agreed to by FDA at a Type B End-of-Phase 2 meeting on March 20, 2017, well before the pivotal Phase 3 study began enrollment (February 2018); the same overall development plan was also discussed with EMA's CHMP (Scientific Advice, July 2018) and Health Canada (November 2018, a joint meeting attended by Otsuka Pharmaceutical Co., Astex Pharmaceuticals, and Taiho Pharma Canada).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, ClinicalTrials.gov-posted Statistical Analysis Plan for ASTX727-02 (MDS/CMML cohort), dated 27 February 2019, introductory paragraph]* — "The main purpose of the current study is to demonstrate decitabine AUC equivalence after administration of ASTX727 and IV decitabine."

*[verbatim, same source, §2.1 Primary Objective]* — "To establish decitabine AUC equivalence of 5-day dosing between ASTX727 and IV decitabine."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.1 Overall Study Design]* — "This is a Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, open-label, 2-period, 2-sequence crossover study comparing decitabine AUC equivalence of ASTX727 and IV decitabine. Adult subjects with MDS or CMML who are candidates to receive decitabine will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive the ASTX727 fixed-dose combination (FDC) tablet Daily×5 in Cycle 1, followed by IV decitabine 20 mg/m2 Daily×5 in Cycle 2, or the converse order... Adequate PK assessments from Cycles 1 and 2 will be required for subjects to be evaluable for analysis of the primary endpoint."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.2.1 Primary Endpoint]* — "Comparison between ASTX727 and IV decitabine: total 5-day AUC0-24 exposures of decitabine after treatment with ASTX727 versus IV decitabine."

*[verbatim, same source, §4.0 Sample Size]* — "The sample size calculation for this study was based on preliminary analysis of 5-day AUC in study ASTX727-01, which showed an estimate of intra-subject CV of 0.5. A conservative CV value of 0.55 was chosen to calculate the sample size. A total of 118 subjects in the Primary Endpoint PK Analysis Set (Section 5.5) included in the 2 one-sided equivalence tests for the geometric mean ratio of ASTX727 5-day AUC relative to IV decitabine 5-day AUC will provide 90% power at the statistical significance level of 0.05, when the true ratio of geometric means is 1.0, the CV under an unlogged scale is 0.55, and the 90% CI equivalence limits for the ratio of geometric means are 0.8 and 1.25. Assuming 10% of subjects may not be evaluable in the study, approximately 132 subjects will need to be randomized."

*[verbatim, same source, §7.5 Efficacy Variables and Analyses]* — "Efficacy analyses will be based on the Efficacy Analysis Set (Section 5.3). Efficacy variables will be summarized using descriptive statistics and there will be no comparison analyses between treatment sequences."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 212576, Reference ID 4636063, Summary of Presubmission/Submission Regulatory Activity]* — "The design of the Phase 3 study was discussed and agreed to with FDA at the End-of-Phase 2 (EOP2) Meeting held on 20 March 2017. The pharmacokinetic (PK) bridging approach to establish the effectiveness of ASTX727 FDC tablets (100 mg cedazuridine and 35 mg decitabine) compared to the 5-day regimen of IV decitabine (20 mg/m2 Daily×5) was agreed to with the FDA at the ASTX727 EOP2 meeting on 20 March 2017."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.2.2 Study Endpoints (Phase 3)]* — "The primary endpoint for the study was based on agreement with FDA at EOP2 meeting on using a PK bridging approach to primarily establish efficacy. The 5-day total cycle AUC0-24 was agreed upon during the pharmacometric analysis plan assessment by FDA... efficacy endpoints were secondary in the trial to assess consistency with efficacy previously reported with IV decitabine."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.3 Analysis of Effectiveness discussion]* — "FDA agrees with the Applicant's position on the effectiveness of ASTX727 tablet (35 mg of decitabine and 100 mg of cedazuridine)... The Phase 3 study demonstrated comparable 5-day cumulative decitabine exposure (primary PK endpoint) between ASTX727 and IV decitabine as shown in Table 6, and that the 90% confidence intervals of the geometric mean ratio were within bioequivalence limits of 80% and 125%."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.4 Statistical Issues]* — "The submitted clinical data from studies ASTX727-01-B (phase 2) and ASTX727-02 (phase 3) demonstrated: 1) a CR rate of 18-21% with median duration of CR responses of 7.5-8.7 months. These results are similar to the ORRs (CR+PR) reported in the USPI for IV decitabine, which were 17% for the randomized trial and 16% for the single arm trial... Of note, 1) both studies ASTX727-01-B (phase 2) and ASTX727-02 (phase 3) are considered as single arm trial in terms of efficacy assessment, therefore results of time to event endpoints are not interpretable."

*[verbatim, same source, §9 Advisory Committee Meeting and Other External Consultations]* — "No Oncology Drug Advisory Committee (ODAC) Meeting or other external consultations are required for the current application."

This entry documents a distinct approval pattern not yet otherwise represented in this census: FDA accepted a demonstrated pharmacokinetic exposure-equivalence bridge to an already-approved reference product (IV decitabine, approved 2006) as the basis for effectiveness of a new oral formulation, in lieu of requiring a new randomized efficacy trial — with the sponsor's own SAP explicitly disclaiming any comparative efficacy interpretation of the crossover study's secondary clinical endpoints, and FDA's Statistical Review independently reaffirming that the time-to-event endpoints from both supporting trials are not interpretable as efficacy evidence because both trials are, for efficacy purposes, single-arm.
