### 117. Tafasitamab-cxix (Monjuvi) — BLA 761163

**Sponsor:** MorphoSys US Inc. (in collaboration with Incyte Corporation)

**Indication approved:** In combination with lenalidomide, for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) not otherwise specified, including DLBCL arising from low grade lymphoma, and who are not eligible for autologous stem cell transplant (ASCT) — approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate

**Approval date:** July 31, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** L-MIND (Study MOR208C203), NCT02399085

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial supporting accelerated approval under 21 CFR 601.41 (BLA accelerated approval regulations), no randomized comparator; supportive single-arm monotherapy trial for contribution-of-tafasitamab evidence (MOR208C201); propensity-score-matched retrospective real-world comparator cohort used only for supportive, non-primary context, explicitly not accepted by FDA as demonstrating statistical significance
- *Endpoints:* overall response rate (ORR, primary, IRC-assessed per IWG 2007/Cheson criteria — CR+PR), duration of response (DoR, key secondary, Kaplan-Meier), disease control rate (DCR = CR+PR+SD), progression-free survival, overall survival, time-to-progression, time-to-next-treatment (all secondary/descriptive — not formally tested in the single-arm design)
- *Primary analysis:* two-sided exact (Clopper-Pearson) 95% confidence interval around ORR in the sponsor's Full Analysis Set (FAS, N=80/81), with no formal hypothesis test against a pre-specified threshold and no comparator arm; FDA independently reconstructed the efficacy-evaluable population as the 71 patients with DLBCL confirmed by retrospective central pathology review (versus the sponsor's local-pathology-based enrolled population of 81), yielding a different headline ORR (55% vs. the sponsor's reported 60%) that became the number carried into the approved label
- *Multiplicity:* not applicable — single formal primary endpoint (ORR), no comparative or multi-endpoint hypothesis test
- *Missing data/bias:* patients with no post-baseline response assessment counted as non-responders in the primary ORR denominator; sensitivity analyses on the Per-Protocol Set (PPS, excluding major protocol deviations) and by investigator vs. IRC assessment (88.2% IRC/investigator concordance for best ORR); FDA reviewer explicitly declined to treat the single-arm time-to-event endpoints (PFS, OS) as supportive evidence, noting they are "prone to bias" versus historical controls, and separately declined to accept the sponsor's RE-MIND propensity-matched comparison as statistically valid confirmation of tafasitamab's contribution to the combination
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval (21 CFR 601.41) based on ORR as a surrogate reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit; no FDA advisory committee meeting held ("the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues in the intended population" per the approval letter); postmarketing requirement (PMR 3904-1) for a randomized Phase 3 confirmatory trial with PFS as primary endpoint, due 2025 per the original letter (satisfied by frontMIND, NCT04824092); FDA reviewer independently corrected one patient's best response from CR to SD during review, altering the reported response counts in the approved label relative to the sponsor's original submission

**Trial design & endpoints**

- L-MIND (MOR208C203): open-label, single-arm, multicenter Phase 2 trial of tafasitamab (MOR208/MOR00208) 12 mg/kg IV in combination with lenalidomide 25 mg orally on Days 1-21 of each 28-day cycle for up to 12 cycles, followed by tafasitamab monotherapy until progression or unacceptable toxicity, in adults with relapsed/refractory DLBCL after 1-3 prior systemic therapies (including a CD20-directed antibody) who were not candidates for high-dose chemotherapy/ASCT; 81 patients enrolled and treated based on local pathology (first patient enrolled 2016-03-29); retrospective central pathology review found 71 of 81 had confirmed DLBCL, 9 had a different lymphoma subtype, and 2 were unknown
- Primary endpoint: best objective response rate (ORR = CR + PR per IWG 2007/Cheson criteria), assessed by a blinded Independent Review Committee (IRC), in the sponsor's Full Analysis Set (FAS — patients dosed with at least one dose each of tafasitamab and lenalidomide, N=80 of 81 enrolled); no formal hypothesis test was pre-specified — the SAP states "no formal statistical hypothesis testing will be performed," with the study instead designed (per an earlier design-stage calculation) around detecting an ORR improvement from a 20% lenalidomide-monotherapy historical benchmark to 35% under combination therapy (73 patients for 85% power at two-sided alpha=0.05 by exact binomial test, ~80 with a 10% drop-out allowance)
- Key secondary endpoints: duration of response (DoR, Kaplan-Meier, median and 25th/75th percentiles, landmark rates at 1/3/6/12/18/24/30 months with Greenwood-formula CIs), disease control rate (DCR), progression-free survival, overall survival, time-to-progression, time-to-next-treatment — all descriptive, no formal testing, consistent with the single-arm design
- Analysis populations per the SAP: Full Analysis Set (FAS, ≥1 dose each of tafasitamab and lenalidomide), Per-Protocol Set (PPS, FAS minus major protocol deviations and patients with no post-baseline response assessment), Safety Analysis Set (SAF, ≥1 dose of either drug)
- Sponsor-reported primary result (FAS, N=80): ORR 60% (95% CI 48.4-70.8%), CR rate 42.5% (95% CI 31.5-54.1%), PR rate 17.5% (95% CI 9.9-27.6%); PPS sensitivity analysis (N=70) ORR 65.7% (95% CI 53.4-76.7%)
- FDA's independent primary efficacy analysis, on the 71 patients with centrally-confirmed DLBCL (excluding the 9 patients with an alternative central-pathology diagnosis, using all 71 eligible/enrolled patients rather than the 70 who received both study drugs, "as excluding patients who met eligibility criteria but were not treated is susceptible to outcome-dependent sampling"): ORR 55% (95% CI 43-67%), CR 37% (95% CI 25-49%), PR 18% (95% CI 10-29%), median DoR 21.7 months (range 0-24) — this 71-patient/55% analysis, not the sponsor's 80-patient/60% analysis, is what appears in the approved USPI Table 5
- Supportive contribution-of-effect evidence: single-arm tafasitamab-monotherapy trial MOR208C201 (ORR 26%, 95% CI 13-43%, in 35 DLBCL patients) and RE-MIND (MOR208C206), a retrospective, propensity-score-matched (nearest-neighbor 1:1, exact/expanded propensity-score matching, ~500 real-world lenalidomide-monotherapy patients screened to match against the L-MIND cohort) observational comparator estimating a lenalidomide-monotherapy ORR of 32% (95% CI 21-43%); FDA explicitly disagreed with the sponsor's characterization of RE-MIND as demonstrating a statistically significant improvement, noting "several limitations with the RE-MIND study," and treated it as context only
- SAP amendment history: original SAP dated September 9, 2019 (contemporaneous with database lock the same day); amended once on October 29, 2019 to address FDA comments (clarifications and programming detail, no change to primary analysis concept); subsequent addenda (through Version 2.0-Addendum 8.0, February 10, 2023) extended the SAP to cover long-term follow-up analyses well after the July 2020 accelerated approval

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter (BLA Accelerated Approval, Reference ID 4650017) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2020/761163Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2020/761163s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 4650005; Statistical Reviewer Kunthel By, PhD; Statistical Team Leader Yu-te Wu, PhD) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/761163Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (L-MIND) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02399085 (Study Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan both posted in the Documents tab)
- Protocol / SAP — Study Protocol (Amendment 5, Final Version 8.0, dated February 24, 2021): https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/85/NCT02399085/Prot_001.pdf; Statistical Analysis Plan (Final Version 2.0 - Addendum Version 8.0, dated February 10, 2023, incorporating the original September 2019 primary-analysis SAP language plus later long-term-follow-up addenda): https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/85/NCT02399085/SAP_002.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Salles G, Duell J, González Barca E, et al. "Tafasitamab plus lenalidomide in relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (L-MIND): a multicentre, prospective, single-arm, phase 2 study." *Lancet Oncol.* 2020;21(7):978-988. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(20)30225-4>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32511983/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Tafasitamab%20plus%20lenalidomide%20in%20relapsed%20or%20refractory%20diffuse%20large%20B-cell%20lymphoma%20L-MIND)

**Other resources**

- MorphoSys/Incyte's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for L-MIND; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for this trial.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held; the approval letter states the application "did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues in the intended population."
- Postmarketing requirement (PMR 3904-1, per the approval letter): a randomized Phase 3 trial to verify clinical benefit of tafasitamab plus lenalidomide, with PFS as the primary endpoint and OS/ORR as secondary endpoints, including sufficient racial/ethnic minority representation — trial completion was targeted for June 2025 in the original letter; this requirement is understood in the field to be addressed by frontMIND (NCT04824092, tafasitamab + lenalidomide + R-CHOP vs. R-CHOP in previously untreated high-intermediate/high-risk DLBCL), though the approval letter itself does not name a specific confirmatory trial. A postmarketing commitment (PMC 3904-2) also required further characterization of safety/efficacy in underrepresented racial and ethnic minority patients.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, L-MIND Statistical Analysis Plan, MorphoSys AG, §9 Primary Objective]* — "The primary objective is to determine the activity of a combination of LEN with MOR00208 in terms of best objective response rate (ORR = rate of patients with complete response [CR] or partial response [PR]) in adult patients with R-R DLBCL."

*[verbatim, same source, §9.2 Main analysis]* — "The number and percentage of patients classified as having best overall response of CR or PR as well as 95% confidence limits (using the Clopper-Pearson exact method) will be presented... Patients with no post-baseline assessment of response will be included as non-responders... No formal hypothesis testing will be conducted. The main analysis will be performed using the FAS."

*[verbatim, same source, §5.3 Determination of sample size]* — "As the primary purpose of this study is to evaluate the clinical efficacy of 25 mg daily oral LEN combined with 12 mg/kg MOR00208 administered by IV infusion in patients with R-R DLBCL, no formal statistical hypothesis testing will be performed... For the determination of a suitable sample size, it is assumed that the combination treatment could improve the ORR of LEN from a value of 20% (under monotherapy) to 35% (under combination therapy). Applying an exact binomial test with a two-sided significance level of 5% and a power of 85% the estimated sample size is 73 patients (calculation performed by nQuery Advisor® 7.0)... Assuming a drop-out rate of 10%, a total sample size of about 80 patients is estimated."

*[verbatim, same source, §10.3.2-10.3.4 Duration of response]* — "DoR is defined as the elapsed time between the date of first documented response (CR or PR) and the following date of event defined as the first documented progression or death... The distribution of DoR will be estimated using the Kaplan-Meier (K-M) method. The median DoR along with 95% confidence interval will be presented... No formal hypothesis testing will be conducted. The main analysis will be conducted on the FAS based on the IRC response assessment."

*[verbatim, L-MIND Protocol MOR208C203, Amendment 5 Final Version 8.0, §10.1 Populations for Analysis]* — "Full analysis set (FAS): The FAS includes all patients who received at least one dose of MOR00208 and one dose of LEN... Per protocol set (PPS): The PPS is the subset of all subjects in the FAS without any major protocol non-compliances... Safety analysis set (SAF): All patients who received at least one dose of MOR00208 or LEN study drug... The primary analysis of the primary efficacy endpoint will be based on the FAS, whereas the analysis using the PPS has a supportive function."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation, BLA 761163, Reference ID 4650005, Conclusions on the Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness]* — "Trial MOR208C203 (L-MIND) enrolled 81 patients with relapsed or refractory DLBCL based on local pathology... The primary efficacy population was a total of 71 patients who had confirmed DLBCL based on central pathology."

*[verbatim, same source, Efficacy Results — Primary Endpoint]* — "Not all patients in the L-MIND study had confirmed DLBCL at baseline. Out of the 81 patients in the enrolled set, 71 had confirmed DLBCL, hereafter referred to as the confirmed enrolled set. During the review, further information was requested from the Applicant regarding the adjudication of the response determination. As a result of this review by the FDA and the Applicant, it was determined an error was made as one patient who was previously considered to be a CR should have been a best response of SD... Per the SAP, the primary analysis set was FAS which was defined as consisting of patients who were dosed with both drugs at least once. This suggests that FDA's analyses should include only 70 patients in the denominator. However, as stated earlier, excluding patients who met eligibility criteria but were not treated is susceptible to outcome-dependent sampling in the sense that patients not dosed has the potential to be less likely to respond than those who were dosed. Therefore, FDA's analysis uses all 71 eligible patients in the denominator."

*[verbatim, same source, Review of Effectiveness — FDA's Assessment]* — "The time-to-event endpoints (PFS and OS) are difficult to interpret in single-arm studies. The time-to-event endpoints are not likely to constitute supportive evidence because their measurements in isolation are out of context and comparing them to historical controls is prone to bias... FDA disagrees with the Applicant's assertions regarding the statistical significance of the results from the RE-MIND study. FDA notes several limitations with the RE-MIND study and does not agree that the data can be used to confirm statistically significant improvement of response of tafa+LEN compared to lenalidomide."

*[verbatim, same source, §13 Postmarketing Requirements and Commitment]* — "A PMR to confirm the benefit of tafasitamab in a randomized controlled trial will be issued. A PMC will be issued to further characterize the safety and efficacy of tafasitamab in combination with lenalidomide in the underrepresented racial and ethnic minority patients with DLBCL."

*[verbatim, FDA Approval Letter, BLA 761163, Reference ID 4650017]* — "Your application for tafasitamab-cxix was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues in the intended population."... "3904-1 Submit the final report and datasets from a randomized, Phase 3 clinical trial to verify the clinical benefit of tafasitamab in patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. The trial should include sufficient numbers of racial and ethnic minority patients to better reflect the U.S. patient population and allow for the interpretation of the results in these patient populations. Patients should be randomized to receive immunotherapy and/or chemotherapy with or without tafasitamab and lenalidomide. The primary endpoint should be progression-free survival, with secondary endpoints that include overall survival and objective response rate."

This is a case where the genuine sponsor SAP and protocol are both posted verbatim on ClinicalTrials.gov, and the resulting picture is unusually candid about a divergence between sponsor and regulator: the SAP's own pre-specified primary analysis population (FAS, dosed patients from the local-pathology-based enrolled set, N=80, ORR 60%) is not the population or the response rate that ended up in the approved label. FDA instead built its own primary efficacy population from the 71 patients whose DLBCL diagnosis was confirmed on retrospective central pathology review, corrected an individual patient's response classification from CR to SD, and explicitly reasoned through (and rejected, on outcome-dependent-sampling grounds) narrowing the denominator further to the 70 who received both study drugs — arriving at a lower ORR (55%) and a longer median DoR (21.7 months) that both differ from the sponsor's own SAP-driven numbers. The sponsor's RE-MIND propensity-matched real-world comparator, offered to support that tafasitamab (not lenalidomide alone) was driving the effect, was explicitly rejected by FDA as statistically inconclusive and used only as background context — leaving the accelerated approval resting on the single-arm ORR/DoR data alone, with a randomized Phase 3 confirmatory trial required.

### 118. Belantamab mafodotin-blmf (Blenrep) — BLA 761158 (original 2020 accelerated approval, revoked 2023); BLA 761440 (2025 re-approval, new application)

**Sponsor:** GlaxoSmithKline Intellectual Property Development Ltd. England (original 2020 BLA 761158 holder); GlaxoSmithKline LLC (2025 BLA 761440 holder)

**Indication approved:** Original (2020, BLA 761158, later revoked): monotherapy treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma who have received at least 4 prior therapies, including an anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody, a proteasome inhibitor, and an immunomodulatory agent — accelerated approval under 21 CFR part 601, subpart E, based on overall response rate and duration of response. Current (since October 2025, BLA 761440, a different regimen and population): in combination with bortezomib and dexamethasone, for adult patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma who have received at least 2 prior lines of therapy including a proteasome inhibitor and an immunomodulatory agent — regular (non-accelerated) approval

**Approval date:** August 5, 2020 (original accelerated approval, BLA 761158); biologics license revoked effective February 6, 2023 (per FDA's revocation letter to GSK; Federal Register notice announcing the revocation published March 30, 2023), after GSK requested revocation in writing on November 18, 2022; BLA 761440 approved as a new, separately-numbered original biologics license application on October 23, 2025, for a different combination regimen, following a July 17, 2025 ODAC meeting

**Pivotal trial:** DREAMM-2 (Study 205678), NCT03525678 — basis of the original 2020 accelerated approval (BLA 761158); DREAMM-3 (Study 207495), NCT04162210 — the required confirmatory trial, failed; DREAMM-7 (Study 207503), NCT04246047 — basis of the October 2025 re-approval under new BLA 761440 (with bortezomib + dexamethasone); DREAMM-8 (NCT04484623) — a related trial (with pomalidomide + dexamethasone) reviewed at the same 2025 advisory committee meeting but not approved

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* DREAMM-2 — two-arm, randomized (1:1), open-label Phase II trial in which each dose arm (2.5 mg/kg vs. 3.4 mg/kg) was analyzed independently against a fixed ORR performance goal rather than compared to the other arm — a randomized non-comparative dose-regimen cohort design (cf. brigatinib/ALTA); group-sequential design with a single non-binding futility interim analysis plus an additional Bayesian cross-arm comparative-futility rule; protocol amended mid-conduct to shift the primary analysis population from a planned first-130-patient subset to all ~200 randomized patients after substantial over-enrollment. DREAMM-3 (confirmatory) — randomized (2:1), open-label, active-controlled Phase III trial of belantamab monotherapy vs. pomalidomide plus low-dose dexamethasone. DREAMM-7 (basis of 2025 re-approval) — randomized (1:1), open-label, active-controlled, event-driven Phase III trial of belantamab mafodotin + bortezomib + dexamethasone (BVd) vs. daratumumab + bortezomib + dexamethasone (DVd)
- *Endpoints:* DREAMM-2 — overall response rate (ORR) by IRC per 2016 IMWG criteria, primary (evaluated per arm, "supported by the duration of response" per FDA's effectiveness conclusion); clinical benefit rate, duration of response, time to response, PFS, OS — secondary/descriptive only. DREAMM-3 — PFS, primary (failed). DREAMM-7 — PFS, primary; overall survival, duration of response, and MRD-negativity rate, key secondary endpoints under a two-family hierarchical/graphical alpha-propagation testing structure
- *Primary analysis:* DREAMM-2 — per-arm framework testing H0: ORR≤15% (historical control) vs. H1: ORR≥33%, with a two-sided 97.5% exact (Clopper-Pearson) confidence interval reported for each arm's ORR in the Intent-to-Treat population; no formal between-arm hypothesis test; participants with unknown/missing response treated as non-responders (included in the denominator). DREAMM-7 — stratified log-rank test and stratified Cox proportional-hazards model for PFS/OS, Kaplan-Meier estimation, Brookmeyer-Crowley method for Kaplan-Meier median confidence intervals
- *Multiplicity:* DREAMM-2 — none across the two dose arms ("No hypothesis testing for comparing ORR between the two arms will be performed"). DREAMM-7 — two-family graphical/step-down testing structure (Bretz 2009; Li 2017): family 1 = PFS (tested at one-sided 2.5% alpha); upon rejection, alpha propagates in full to family 2 (OS, DoR, MRD-negativity) via a weighted Bonferroni split (4/5 to OS, 1/5 to DoR) with step-down/recycling rules
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* DREAMM-2 — single futility interim analysis (~25 patients/arm, ~38% information fraction) using a Hwang-Shih-DeCani-family gamma spending function (γ=1.1, later γ=5.4 after over-enrollment) as a non-binding beta-spending (futility) boundary, computed in East 6.4; an additional Bayesian comparative-futility rule (non-informative Beta(0.025, 0.1) priors, ≥97.5% posterior probability of one arm's superiority) could drop an inferior arm; an Independent Data Monitoring Committee (IDMC) oversaw the interim look. DREAMM-7 — group-sequential design with 2 planned PFS analyses and 4 planned OS analyses, each using a Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function approximating an O'Brien-Fleming boundary
- *Missing data/bias:* DREAMM-2 — non-responder imputation for missing/not-evaluable disease-assessment data; a pre-specified confirmed-response algorithm requiring two consecutive assessments. DREAMM-7's SAP specifies a primary PFS estimand plus four pre-specified supplementary estimands (S1-S4) and a distinct COVID-19 supplementary estimand, each defined by a different intercurrent-event handling/censoring rule — an ICH E9(R1)-style multi-estimand sensitivity framework
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval (21 CFR part 601, subpart E) granted August 5, 2020 (BLA 761158) on ORR/DoR from DREAMM-2 in a heavily pretreated (median 7 prior lines) population, following a July 14, 2020 ODAC meeting that voted 12-0 that belantamab mafodotin's benefit outweighed its risks in the proposed population; REMS with Elements to Assure Safe Use (ETASU) required for ocular toxicity, plus a Boxed Warning; **voluntary withdrawal of an accelerated-approval indication after confirmatory-trial failure** — the required confirmatory trial (DREAMM-3) did not meet its primary PFS endpoint; GSK requested revocation of BLA 761158 in writing on November 18, 2022, and FDA revoked the license effective February 6, 2023; GSK subsequently obtained approval of a new, separately-numbered BLA (761440, submitted by GlaxoSmithKline LLC) on October 23, 2025, for belantamab mafodotin + bortezomib + dexamethasone, a regular (non-accelerated) approval based on the DREAMM-7 randomized trial, granted despite a negative July 17, 2025 ODAC vote (5 Noes/3 Yeses that the BVd regimen's benefit-risk was "not favorable at the proposed dosage in the proposed patient population"); a companion regimen from DREAMM-8 (belantamab + pomalidomide + dexamethasone) was voted down more decisively (7 Noes/1 Yes) and was not approved

**Trial design & endpoints**

- DREAMM-2 (Study 205678, BLA 761158's pivotal trial): open-label, two-arm, randomized (1:1) Phase II trial; adults with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma who had received ≥3 prior lines of therapy that included a proteasome inhibitor (PI), an immunomodulatory agent (IMiD), and an anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody, randomized to belantamab mafodotin 2.5 mg/kg or 3.4 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks (21-day cycles); 196 participants randomized to the two frozen-liquid dose cohorts (97 at 2.5 mg/kg, 99 at 3.4 mg/kg), plus a separate ~25-patient exploratory lyophilized-formulation cohort not powered for efficacy; the approval population (95 patients dosed at the to-be-marketed 2.5 mg/kg) had a median age of 65 years (range 39-85) and had received a median of 7 prior lines of therapy (95% had received ≥4 prior lines)
- Primary endpoint: ORR by IRC per 2016 IMWG response criteria (confirmed PR or better: PR, VGPR, CR, sCR), analyzed within each dose arm against a fixed performance goal (H0: ORR≤15% vs. H1: ORR≥33%), not compared between arms; secondary/descriptive endpoints included investigator-assessed ORR, clinical benefit rate, duration of response, PFS, and OS
- The protocol was amended mid-study to address substantial over-enrollment: FDA's review states the primary analysis was "based on all randomized participants (approximately 200) enrolled into the Intent-to-Treat (ITT) Population," with "a sensitivity analysis based on the first 130 randomized participants... performed to account for the original study design"
- Result (2.5 mg/kg cohort, the to-be-marketed dose): ORR 31% (97.5% CI 20.8-42.6); median DoR not reached at a median follow-up of 6.3 months, with 73% of responders having a DoR ≥6 months — FDA's effectiveness conclusion states this recommendation "is based on the observed response rate and duration of response"
- Ocular toxicity was the dominant safety signal and the central focus of the July 14, 2020 ODAC meeting: 71% of patients in the 2.5 mg/kg cohort had keratopathy of any grade, 44% had severe (Grade 3-4) keratopathy; 53% had any decrease in visual acuity, 26% a >3-line decrease, 17% worsened to a level inconsistent with legal driving, and 1 patient's vision worsened to a level consistent with legal blindness; only 43% of patients with keratopathy on exam reported ocular symptoms, raising a detection concern absent close monitoring; the ODAC's voting question was "Does the demonstrated benefit of belantamab mafodotin outweigh the risks in the proposed patient population with multiple myeloma?" — the final, confirmed vote (per FDA's own Multi-Discipline Review) was 12 Yes, 0 No
- As a condition of accelerated approval, FDA required a postmarketing requirement for "the final study report and datasets from a randomized phase 3 clinical trial that verifies and describes the clinical benefit of belantamab mafodotin in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma," with PFS as the primary endpoint and OS/ORR/patient-reported outcomes as secondary endpoints, specifically requiring adequate representation of older patients (ages 65-74 and ≥75) and patients with extramedullary disease — this became DREAMM-3
- DREAMM-3 (Study 207495, NCT04162210) — the confirmatory trial: open-label, randomized (2:1) Phase III trial at 108 sites in 18 countries; adults with ≥2 prior lines including ≥2 consecutive cycles each of lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor, randomized to belantamab mafodotin 2.5 mg/kg IV every 21 days (n=218) or pomalidomide 4 mg/day (days 1-21) plus dexamethasone 40 mg weekly in 28-day cycles (n=107), stratified by prior anti-CD38 therapy, ISS stage, and number of prior therapies; primary endpoint PFS; enrolled April 2020-April 2022, data cutoff September 12, 2022
- DREAMM-3 result: median PFS 11.2 months (95% CI 6.4-14.5) with belantamab mafodotin vs. 7.0 months (4.6-10.6) with pomalidomide-dexamethasone; hazard ratio 1.03 (95% CI 0.72-1.47), p=0.56 — numerically longer median but a hazard ratio on the wrong side of 1.0, and nowhere near statistical significance; the published interpretation states plainly: "Belantamab mafodotin was not associated with statistically improved progression-free survival compared with standard-of-care"
- Per the Federal Register: on November 2, 2022, FDA and GSK met to discuss the DREAMM-3 results and "considerations regarding withdrawal (revocation) of the biologics license for BLENREP because the confirmatory DREAMM-3 trial did not meet its primary endpoint"; GSK requested revocation in writing on November 18, 2022, under 21 CFR 601.5(a) and waived its opportunity for a hearing; "On February 6, 2023, the Agency issued a letter to GSK revoking the biologics license for BLENREP" (BLA 761158) — the Federal Register notice formally announcing this was itself published March 30, 2023, but the legal revocation date is the earlier February 6, 2023 letter date; this removed Blenrep from the US market for roughly two years and eight months
- DREAMM-7 (Study 207503, NCT04246047) — the trial supporting the October 2025 re-approval under new BLA 761440: open-label, randomized (1:1) Phase III trial in adults with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma who progressed after ≥1 prior line of therapy (excluding those refractory/intolerant to daratumumab or bortezomib, or with prior anti-BCMA exposure); randomized to belantamab mafodotin 2.5 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks + bortezomib/dexamethasone for cycles 1-8 then belantamab alone (BVd, n=243) vs. daratumumab + bortezomib/dexamethasone for cycles 1-8 then daratumumab alone (DVd, n=251); primary endpoint PFS by IRC; key secondary endpoints OS, duration of response, and MRD-negativity rate
- DREAMM-7 full-trial (ITT) result (NEJM, median follow-up 28.2 months): median PFS 36.6 months (BVd) vs. 13.4 months (DVd), HR 0.41 (95% CI 0.31-0.53), p<0.001; 18-month OS 84% vs. 73%; ocular adverse events in 79% (BVd) vs. 29% (DVd); the FDA-approved label restricts the indication to patients with ≥2 prior lines including a PI and an IMiD — a narrower efficacy-evaluable subgroup (108 BVd / 109 DVd patients out of 494 randomized) for which the label reports PFS HR 0.31 (95% CI 0.21-0.47) and OS HR 0.49 (95% CI 0.32-0.76), more favorable than the full-ITT NEJM estimates
- DREAMM-8 (NCT04484623), reviewed at the same July 2025 ODAC meeting but not approved: randomized Phase III trial of belantamab mafodotin + pomalidomide + dexamethasone (BPd, n=155) vs. a pomalidomide/bortezomib/dexamethasone-class comparator PVd (n=147) in lenalidomide-exposed patients with ≥1 prior line; 12-month PFS 71% vs. 51%, HR 0.52 (95% CI 0.37-0.73), p<0.001, but ocular events occurred in 89% of BPd patients (43% grade ≥3) — a more severe ocular-toxicity signal that the committee voted 7 Noes/1 Yes as an unfavorable benefit-risk at the proposed dosage/population

**Other resources**

- GSK's general participation in third-party clinical-data-sharing platforms (historically ClinicalStudyDataRequest.com, now largely folded into Vivli) was not individually confirmed for DREAMM-2/DREAMM-3/DREAMM-7/DREAMM-8 IPD availability.
- FDA ODAC met July 14, 2020, on BLA 761158; voting question "Does the demonstrated benefit of belantamab mafodotin outweigh the risks in the proposed patient population with multiple myeloma?"; final vote 12 Yes, 0 No (confirmed directly from FDA's Multi-Discipline Review, not merely secondary press reporting).
- FDA ODAC met July 17, 2025 (Docket No. FDA-2025-N-1534), on BLA 761440 for two proposed combination regimens (BVd from DREAMM-7, BPd from DREAMM-8); voted 5 Noes/3 Yeses that BVd's benefit-risk was "not favorable at the proposed dosage in the proposed patient population," and 7 Noes/1 Yes likewise for BPd. FDA subsequently approved only the BVd regimen (October 23, 2025), for a narrower population (≥2 prior lines) than the ≥1-prior-line population discussed at the meeting; the BPd/DREAMM-8 regimen was not approved.
- Postmarketing requirements attached to the original 2020 accelerated approval (BLA 761158) included the DREAMM-3 confirmatory trial (PFS primary, OS/ORR/PROs secondary, with required representation of older patients and extramedullary disease), an integrated pooled ocular-toxicity analysis for the lyophilized presentation, a superficial-keratectomy mechanistic study of corneal deposits, and several clinical-pharmacology PMRs (a randomized Phase 2 lower-dose/alternative-regimen trial for the lyophilized presentation, hepatic- and renal-impairment PK trials, and a bioanalytical stability assessment).
- Postmarketing requirements attached to the October 2025 approval (BLA 761440) are safety-focused (consistent with regular, not accelerated, approval): a randomized trial of alternative belantamab mafodotin dosage regimens with bortezomib/dexamethasone to further characterize ocular toxicity, and a PK trial in patients with moderate hepatic impairment.
- BLENREP is subject to a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) with Elements to Assure Safe Use for ocular toxicity under both the original and current approvals, including mandatory ophthalmic exams, prescriber/pharmacy certification, and periodic REMS assessment reporting.
- This is one of relatively few oncology accelerated approvals to be fully revoked (license actually pulled, not merely relabeled) after a confirmatory-trial failure, and one of even fewer to subsequently be re-approved for a related but distinct combination-regimen use — notably, under an entirely new, separately-numbered BLA (761440) rather than a reinstatement of the original, revoked BLA (761158) — following new randomized confirmatory evidence. Contrast with olaratumab and the durvalumab urothelial indication elsewhere in this census, neither of which returned to market.

*[verbatim, sponsor Statistical Analysis Plan, Study 205678, dated 06 Apr 2022, §2.2 Study Objective(s) and Endpoint(s)]* — "To evaluate the clinical efficacy of 2 doses of GSK2857916 in participants with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma.... ORR, defined as the percentage of participants with a confirmed partial response (PR) or better (i.e., PR, very good partial response [VGPR], complete response [CR] and stringent complete response [sCR]), according to the 2016 International Myeloma Working Group (IMWG) Response Criteria by Independent Review Committee (IRC)."

*[verbatim, same source, §2.4 Statistical Hypotheses / Statistical Analyses]* — "Study 205678 is designed to provide evidence with respect to ORR to either support the null hypothesis, H0: ORR ≤15%, or reject H0 in favor of the alternative hypothesis, H1: ORR≥33%. The hypothesis testing will be performed within each arm separately. No hypothesis testing for comparing ORR between the two arms will be performed."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.1.1 Futility Stopping Rule Based on Group Sequential Design]* — "For each arm (2.5 mg/kg or 3.4 mg/kg), a single futility IA is planned for the primary endpoint ORR after approximately 25 participants (~38% information fraction) per arm are evaluable. A user-defined gamma spending function (γ=1.1) [Hwang, 1990] was used as a beta-spending function to determine the non-binding futility boundary (as implemented in East 6.4).... the stopping boundary in IA is identified as 0.16 on the proportion scale (4 responders out of 25 participants)... Due to over enrolment, it is estimated that approximately 200 participants (~100 per arm) will be randomized to the frozen liquid solution. At the primary analysis, the null hypothesis will be rejected if the lower bound of 2-sided 97.5% exact C.I. exceeds the historical control rate of 15%."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.1.2 Additional Comparative Futility Stopping Rule Based on Bayesian Approach]* — "If both arms pass the futility boundaries based on group sequential design described above, posterior probability of observing a better RR in one arm relative to the other will be calculated. If such a probability is at least 97.5%, then the treatment arm with lower RR will be dropped due to lack of efficacy.... To calculate the posterior probability, a non-informative Beta prior (0.025, 0.1) will be used for each arm."

*[verbatim, same source, §7.1.1 Overall Response Rate (ORR) based on IRC assessment]* — "Subjects with only assessments of Not Evaluable or missing response will be treated as non-responders; i.e. they will be included in the denominator when calculating the percentage."... The ORR in the 2.5 mg/kg treatment group was 31% (97.5% CI: 20.8, 42.6). At the time of data cut-off with a median follow-up of 6.3 months, the median DoR was not reached. Seventy-three percent of responders had a DoR ≥6 months."

Note on this entry's correction history: an earlier draft of this entry, produced during this project's multi-pass drafting process, mistakenly asserted the original 2020 approval was filed under BLA 761440 — the number the live Drugs@FDA overview page currently displays, since that page no longer surfaces the revoked 2020 application at all and instead shows only the October 2025 "ORIG-1" action. This was corrected by directly fetching and reading the actual 2020-dated FDA documents from `accessdata.fda.gov` — the original approval letter, label, and a 23.8 MB Multi-Discipline Review (Reference ID 4651784, Statistical Reviewer Qing Xu PhD), all explicitly headed "BLA761158" and addressed to GSK regarding Blenrep — and independently corroborating both the BLA number and the February 6, 2023 revocation date verbatim from the Federal Register's official revocation notice. This is retained here as a documented example of how a live regulatory database's user-facing search/overview page can silently drop a revoked application's history, making primary-document verification (rather than reliance on a current database front-end alone) essential.

### 119. Copper Cu 64 dotatate (Detectnet) — NDA 213227

**Sponsor:** RadioMedix, Inc. (developer and clinical-trial sponsor of record on the NDA and on ClinicalTrials.gov); Curium US LLC is listed as the applicant/marketer on Drugs@FDA and manufactures/distributes the approved product

**Indication approved:** Positron emission tomography (PET) for localization of somatostatin receptor-positive neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) in adult patients

**Approval date:** September 3, 2020 (matching the PDUFA goal date of 9/3/2020 recorded in the Multi-Discipline Review)

**Pivotal trial:** Study RMX-18-22 ("NETMedix"), NCT03673943, plus a sponsor re-analysis of previously published data (the "NETMedix Denmark Study," re-analyzing patients from Pfeifer et al. 2015) and two additional published studies (Pfeifer et al. 2012; Johnbeck et al. 2017) reviewed as supportive-only evidence

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison) — Study RMX-18-22 was a prospective, single-center (Excel Diagnostics and Nuclear Oncology Center, Houston), single-dose, single-arm, non-comparative Phase 3 trial conducted under a Special Protocol Assessment (SPA) agreement (request 4/6/2018, agreement letter 5/17/2018); retrospective/non-prospective diagnostic evidentiary basis (academic or literature-derived, not a company-sponsored pivotal trial) for the two supportive studies (Pfeifer et al. 2015/NETMedix Denmark re-analysis, Johnbeck et al. 2017); 505(b)(2) NDA for a designated new molecular entity, the first NDA submitted for an imaging drug labeled with a copper radionuclide

- *Endpoints:* co-primary endpoints were subject-level sensitivity and specificity (per-reader) of Cu-64 dotatate PET against a standard of truth (SOT)/composite reference standard, evaluated by three independent blinded readers; secondary endpoints were majority-read sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, and accuracy, plus localized-vs-metastatic disease classification; tertiary endpoints were inter-reader (Fleiss'/generalized Kappa) and intra-reader (Cohen's Kappa) agreement

- *Primary analysis:* no taxonomy term precisely fits; performance-measure analysis without an independent reference standard, subject to verification bias — FDA's statistical reviewer explicitly renamed the sponsor's "sensitivity"/"specificity" as positive percent agreement (PPA) and negative percent agreement (NPA) throughout the review because the SOT was a composite reference standard (a single blinded oncologist's synthesis of histopathology where available, plus conventional/other SSTR imaging and clinical data) rather than an independent histopathology truth standard; success criteria were pre-specified exact-binomial hypothesis tests (one-sided α=0.025) that the lower bound of the 95% CI (Wilson's score method with continuity correction) exceed 70% for sensitivity and 60% for specificity, in the same two of three independent readers

- *Missing data/bias:* FDA's review team documented and explicitly disregarded a post-hoc sponsor request to reclassify three false-negative subjects (subjects 42, 43, 51) as true negatives via an "Oncologist Note to File" submitted after database lock, on the grounds that this converted study failures into successes after the fact; FDA also flagged that one of the NETMedix Denmark Study's own SOT-determination rules used a positive Cu-64 dotatate PET read as part of establishing the reference standard against which Cu-64 dotatate PET was then judged, a form of incorporation bias/circularity the statistics team noted "may tend to favor the imaging performance evaluation of Cu-64 dotatate PET"

- *Regulatory:* Special Protocol Assessment (SPA) agreement honored for a diagnostic single-arm imaging trial, standard (not accelerated) approval, granted priority review by FDA's Division of Imaging and Radiation Medicine, with no advisory committee meeting held ("No advisory committee meeting or external consultation was needed for this NDA")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study RMX-18-22: prospective, open-label, single-center, single-dose, single-arm Phase 3 trial at Excel Diagnostics and Nuclear Oncology Center (Houston, TX). 66 subjects enrolled (including 4 subjects carried over from the Phase 1 dose-ranging study RMX-17-22 at the same 4.0 mCi dose); 3 withdrew consent before dosing; the Efficacy Evaluable (EE)/safety population was 63 subjects: 42 adult patients with known/suspected NET (37 with a prior confirmed NET history, 5 with suspicion but no prior history) plus 21 healthy adult volunteers recruited to help estimate specificity/NPA. Median age 54 years (range 25-82); 56% female; 86% white.

- Standard of truth (SOT): all 21 healthy volunteers were categorized "No Disease" based on a negative contrast-CT read by an independent, PET-blinded radiologist. For the 42 patients, a single oncologist blinded to the Cu-64 dotatate PET results assigned "Disease"/"No Disease" status using a pre-specified hierarchy of evidence (histopathology first if available; otherwise anatomic/functional imaging — MRI, contrast CT, F-18 FDG PET/CT, F-18 NaF PET/CT, bone scintigraphy, In-111 pentetreotide SPECT, Ga-68 dotatate PET/CT — collected within 8 weeks of Cu-64 dotatate PET, supported by clinical/laboratory data). FDA's reviewer characterized this SOT as "more appropriately described as a composite reference standard" rather than a true independent standard, since not all subjects had histopathology.

- Co-primary efficacy endpoints: subject-level sensitivity and specificity (per FDA's terminology, PPA and NPA) of Cu-64 dotatate PET against the SOT, read independently by three nuclear-medicine readers blinded to clinical information, other imaging, and SOT results, using the liver as a reference region for abnormal-uptake calls. Secondary endpoints: majority-read sensitivity/specificity/PPV/NPV/accuracy, and localized-vs-metastatic classification accuracy. Tertiary endpoints: inter-reader agreement (generalized Fleiss' Kappa across all three readers) and intra-reader agreement (Cohen's Kappa on 7 randomly re-read scans per reader, re-read ≥4 weeks after the primary read).

- Sample size/power: the protocol/CSR states the trial was powered for ≥80% overall power (each of the two co-primary hypotheses individually powered at 90%) to detect sensitivity >70% and specificity >60%, assuming true sensitivity and specificity of 0.90 each and inter-reader read correlation r=0.70, determined via Monte Carlo simulation (5,000 replications); this required n=63 (42 SOT-positive, 21 SOT-negative, a 2:1 allocation), tested with one-sided exact binomial tests at α=0.025 per hypothesis.

- Results: all three readers met the pre-specified success criteria — PPA was 91% (95% CI lower bound >70%) for all three readers, and NPA ranged 80-97% across readers (all lower bounds >60%). Majority-read analysis: sensitivity 90.9% (p=0.0042), specificity 96.6% (p<0.0001), PPV 96.8%, NPV 90.3%, accuracy 93.6%. Inter-reader agreement was Kappa=0.76 (95% CI 0.62-0.91); intra-reader agreement showed readers 1 and 3 with perfect agreement (Kappa=1.00) and reader 2 agreeing on 5/7 re-reads.

- Post-hoc issue disregarded by FDA: an "Oncologist Note to File" retrospectively requested reclassifying three false-negative subjects (all previously had NET resected with no imaging/clinical evidence of recurrence) from SOT-positive to SOT-negative after database lock — which would have converted three failures on the primary endpoint into agreements. FDA's review team stated it "disregarded this post-hoc analysis" and based its Table 10/primary results on the original SOT determination.

- Supportive studies reviewed: (1) the "NETMedix Denmark Study," the Applicant's retrospective re-analysis (no re-reading of images) of source data from the Pfeifer et al. 2015 publication (112 patients with pathologically confirmed NET, prospectively scanned head-to-head with Cu-64 dotatate PET and In-111 pentetreotide SPECT in Denmark), testing the same pre-specified one-sided-α=0.025 hypotheses (sensitivity >80%, specificity >60%) against a composite reference standard built from agreement between reference scans plus follow-up; FDA noted this SOT construction incorporated the investigational Cu-64 dotatate PET read itself into truth-standard determination in some cases, a circularity concern, but found the underlying case narratives "reasonable" on review; (2) Johnbeck et al. 2017, a head-to-head Cu-64 dotatate vs. Ga-68 dotatoc comparison in 59 NET patients (Copenhagen), reviewed as supportive-only given unequal CT quality between arms, unspecified blinding, and no submitted source data for verification.

- Safety: 197 total unique subjects exposed to Cu-64 dotatate across four studies/sources contributing to the safety database; in Study RMX-18-22, 9 adverse events (all mild-to-moderate, none serious, none related to study drug) occurred in 5 of 63 subjects, with no clinically significant changes in labs, vital signs, or ECG parameters.

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2020/213227Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label (original approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2020/213227s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 4665064; includes Summary Review, Cross-Discipline Team Leader Review, Clinical Review, Non-Clinical Review, Statistical Review, and Clinical Pharmacology Review as a single combined package) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/213227Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf

**Other resources**

- Neither RadioMedix, Inc. nor Curium US LLC participation in Vivli, the YODA Project, or Project Data Sphere was identified; trial-specific IPD availability was not confirmed.

- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this application ("No advisory committee meeting or external consultation was needed for this NDA" — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Section 9).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, RMX-18-22 Clinical Study Report, as posted on ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03673943 Documents tab ("Statistical Analysis Plan"/SAP_001.pdf and "Study Protocol"/Prot_000.pdf — both contain this identical Synopsis/Section 9.7 text), §9.7.1.2.6.1 Analysis of Primary Efficacy Endpoints]* — "The following two hypotheses were tested at the end of the study relative to the co-primary endpoints: Ha0: Sensitivity ≤ 70% vs Ha1: Sensitivity > 70% and Hb0: Specificity ≤ 60% vs Hb1: Specificity > 60%. Each hypothesis test was conducted at the one-sided α = 0.025 level of significance. Point estimates of sensitivity and specificity were calculated along with two-sided 95% confidence intervals using the score method. The sensitivity and specificity were calculated on a by-reader basis. Success upon the primary endpoints was declared if two of the three independent readers achieved sensitivity and specificity results in excess of the thresholds designated above."

*[verbatim, same source, §9.7.2 Determination of Sample Size]* — "The study was powered with respect to the co-primary endpoints of sensitivity and specificity. In order to have at least a 90% chance of showing that the sensitivity was at least 0.70 and the specificity was at least 0.60 a sample of 63 subjects was needed, divided among n1 = 42 SOT positive subjects and n2 = 21 SOT negative subjects. This sample size was derived under the assumptions that the readers were viewing the same images and that their reads were correlated at r = 0.70 and that the true Sensitivity and Specificity are each 0.90... This sample size was determined by Monte Carlo simulation with the parameter values given above. The simulation used 5000 replications: the standard error of the estimated power was no more than 0.6%."

*[verbatim, same source, §9.8 Changes in the Conduct of the Study or Planned Analyses]* — "There was a discrepancy between the SAP and the protocol regarding the following items: injection of radioactivity, waiting time allowed for tracer distribution, and PET scan acquisition time. The SAP required an injection of 185-227 MBq (5.0-6.0 mCi) of 64Cu-DOTATATE followed by a 20 minute PET scan beginning 50 minutes post-injection. The protocol required an injection of 148 ± 10% MBq (4.0 ± 10% mCi) of 64Cu-DOTATATE followed by a 5 minute per bed position PET scan beginning 60 ± 15 minutes post-injection. The protocol was followed during the clinical study." (This passage indicates a genuinely separate SAP document existed and differed from the protocol on dosing/imaging-window parameters; that stand-alone SAP itself does not appear to be the document posted under the "SAP" label on ClinicalTrials.gov, which instead reproduces this CSR text.)

*[verbatim, same source, §13.1 Discussion]* — "It is important to note that failures in detecting disease were retrospectively reviewed by the investigators after the database was locked. Upon review of these failures it was noted that three SOT image reads determined to be positive for disease by the oncologist were in fact negative for disease. Included in these miscalls were subjects 42, 43, and 51... The oncologists have included a note-to-file... describing this error. Taking this into account Readers 1 & 3 and the Majority Read would have a sensitivity of 1.000, a specificity of 0.9688..."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 213227, Reference ID 4665064, §8.1.1 Study RMX-18-22, Standard of Truth]* — "Reviewer's Comments: Given that not all subjects have histopathology data, the review team considers this SOT to be more appropriately described as a composite reference standard."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.1.1 Statistical Analysis Plan]* — "Reviewer's Comments: Using the Applicant's composite reference standard, some SOT results were assigned as positive without histopathology data. However, sensitivity and specificity are generally defined based on a histopathology truth standard. Therefore, the review team refers to 'sensitivity' as positive percent agreement (PPA) and to 'specificity' as negative percent agreement (NPA), although 'sensitivity' and 'specificity' will be displayed in the Applicant's analyses."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.1.1 Efficacy Results, Table 10 commentary]* — "Reviewer's comments: The majority read data displayed in Table 10 above include three false negative subjects. The NDA contains an 'Oncologist Note to File' in which the Applicant retrospectively requested the oncologist making the SOT determination to change the initial SOT assessment of positive for NET disease to negative for NET disease for these three subjects, essentially converting the three false negatives to 'true negatives'. The review team disregarded this post-hoc analysis. The above Table 10 as well as primary analysis results in this section and Section 8.3 reflect the original SOT determined by the study oncologist."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.3 Statistical Evaluation, NETMedix Denmark Study]* — "The statistics team identified the same concern as the clinical team regarding the SOT determination of NET status. For example, one of the SOT rules, states that if both Cu-64 dotatate and In-111-pentetreotide were positive, the patient was considered true positive and no further follow-up was needed, and thus includes the use of the investigational Cu-64 dotatate PET imaging for SOT determination. This SOT rule may tend to favor the imaging performance evaluation of Cu-64 dotatate PET."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.3 Statistical Summary]* — "A major statistical concern for this confirmatory clinical study is the lack of an objective method of establishing the SOT for NET status. Since there was no follow-up biopsy or longitudinal imaging in patients who had no available histopathology, the NET status in some patients enrolled in study RMX-18-22 relied only on other imaging performed near the time of Cu-64 dotatate PET... Therefore, defining imaging performance of Cu-64 dotatate with PPA and NPA is more appropriate than defining its imaging performance with sensitivity and specificity."

### 120. Pralsetinib (Gavreto) — NDA 213721

**Sponsor:** Blueprint Medicines Corporation (sponsor of record at approval). Global rights subsequently moved more than once: by the time of the November 2021 EU approval and the August 2023 accelerated-to-regular-approval conversion, correspondence to FDA was submitted by Genentech, Inc./F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd (the posted ClinicalTrials.gov protocol and SAP versions from this period are headed "Pralsetinib—{Genentech, Inc./F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd}"); by September 2023 (NDA supplement removing a related thyroid-cancer indication) and September 2024 (a further supplement), correspondence reverted to Blueprint Medicines Corporation; by March 2025 (NDA supplement adding a boxed warning), the sNDA sponsor of record was Rigel Pharmaceuticals, Inc., which remains the manufacturer named on the current (December 2025) label

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with metastatic RET (rearranged during transfection) fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), as detected by an FDA-approved test — granted under accelerated approval (21 CFR 314.500) based on overall response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DOR)

**Approval date:** September 4, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** ARROW (Study BLU-667-1101/BO42863), NCT03037385

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial supporting accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.510 Subpart H; a disease-and-treatment-history-defined efficacy cohort (RET fusion-positive NSCLC, split into platinum-pretreated and treatment-naïve subgroups) analyzed within one arm of a much larger multi-cohort, multi-tumor-type Phase 1/2 basket trial (ARROW also enrolled RET-altered medullary thyroid cancer, RET-fusion thyroid cancer, and other RET-altered solid tumors, each as a separately powered/analyzed cohort) — not a tumor-agnostic pooled analysis, since each disease cohort was analyzed and reported separately; Phase 1 dose-escalation (BOIN design) feeding into a Phase 2 dose-expansion at the RP2D (400 mg QD)
- *Endpoints:* confirmed overall response rate (ORR, primary, per blinded independent central review [BICR] of local imaging using RECIST v1.1), duration of response (DOR, secondary), clinical benefit rate (CBR), disease control rate (DCR), progression-free survival and overall survival (secondary/descriptive only — FDA considered PFS/OS "not interpretable in a single arm study"), intracranial ORR/DOR in patients with CNS metastases (added as a secondary endpoint via SAP amendment before database lock), quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30, exploratory)
- *Primary analysis:* two-sided exact (Clopper-Pearson) 95% confidence interval around ORR in the efficacy population, reported descriptively — no formal single-arm hypothesis test of ORR against a null threshold was used for the primary analysis actually submitted (design-stage sample-size assumptions for each Phase 2 cohort were instead framed as two-sided power calculations against a null-vs-alternative ORR pair, e.g., Group 1/platinum-pretreated NSCLC: n≈80 for >95% power at two-sided α=0.05 to detect ORR=0.5 vs. a null of ORR=0.23)
- *Multiplicity:* not applicable — SAP states "No multiplicity adjustment is planned in this study"; each disease/treatment-history cohort analyzed independently with its own descriptive ORR/DOR estimate
- *Missing data/bias:* patients with no post-baseline disease assessment imputed as "not evaluable" for best overall response; no pre-specified rule existed for handling missing response assessments in the ORR analysis (FDA reviewer noted this gap); FDA re-derived its own primary analysis population and ORR table from a later data cutoff (February 13, 2020) than the one the Applicant highlighted (November 18, 2019), designating the FDA-recut table as "the primary analysis for this application"
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval (Subpart H) based on ORR/DOR as a surrogate reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit, contingent on a postmarketing requirement (PMR 3916-1) to verify clinical benefit; no FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting held; companion diagnostic (Oncomine Dx Target Test) co-reviewed for contemporaneous approval; NSCLC indication later converted from accelerated to regular approval (NDA 213721/S-009, August 9, 2023) after PMR 3916-1 was fulfilled with longer follow-up data, including from the randomized confirmatory trial AcceleRET-Lung (NCT04222972)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ARROW (BLU-667-1101, protocol number BO42863) is a multicenter, non-randomized, open-label Phase 1/2 study of pralsetinib in patients with RET-altered thyroid cancer, NSCLC, and other advanced solid tumors, sponsored globally by F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd with Genentech, Inc. as the US affiliate (originating sponsor for the NDA was Blueprint Medicines Corporation). Phase 1 used a Bayesian optimal interval (BOIN) dose-escalation design (target toxicity rate 30%) to identify the maximum tolerated dose/recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D: 400 mg orally once daily); Phase 2 then enrolled disease- and treatment-history-defined expansion cohorts at the RP2D (Groups 1-9, covering RET-fusion NSCLC by platinum-pretreatment status, RET-mutant/RET-fusion thyroid cancer by prior TKI status, and other RET-altered solid tumors)
- This NDA's efficacy claim rests on two of those cohorts: RET fusion-positive NSCLC patients previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy, and treatment-naïve RET fusion-positive NSCLC patients, both dosed at 400 mg QD, enrolled on or before July 11, 2019
- Primary efficacy endpoint (per both the Applicant's SAP and FDA's review): confirmed ORR (proportion with a best overall response of complete response [CR] or partial response [PR], confirmed on two assessments ≥28 days apart with no progression in between), assessed by BICR of local imaging per RECIST v1.1, in the efficacy population subset of RET-fusion NSCLC patients dosed at 400 mg QD
- Secondary endpoints: DOR, CBR, DCR, PFS, OS, correlation of RET gene status (plasma/tissue) with response measures; intracranial ORR/DOR were added as a secondary endpoint via a SAP version issued before database lock, per FDA's clarification memo, after having originally been mislabeled exploratory
- Sample size/power: per the final (October 30, 2019) version of the SAP used to support this NDA, the platinum-pretreated cohort (Group 1) was sized at ~80 patients to give >95% power (two-sided α=0.05) to detect ORR=0.5 against a null of ORR=0.23; the treatment-naïve cohort (Group 2) was sized at ~170 patients for >90% power (two-sided α=0.05) to detect ORR=0.61 against a null of ORR=0.48. There was no interim analysis or formal stopping rule tied to these calculations, and no pre-defined plan for handling missing ORR response assessments
- Statistical methods: two-sided exact (Clopper-Pearson) binomial 95% CI around ORR, reported by cohort, by prior-therapy subgroup, and by RET fusion partner (KIF5B, CCDC6, other); Kaplan-Meier estimation used descriptively for DOR/PFS/OS; no formal multiplicity adjustment (SAP: "No multiplicity adjustment is planned in this study")
- FDA's own primary analysis (constructed from a later, February 13, 2020 data cutoff, in a subpopulation of patients with measurable metastatic disease) reported: platinum-pretreated NSCLC (N=87), ORR 57% (95% CI 46, 68); treatment-naïve NSCLC (N=27), ORR 70% (95% CI 50, 86), median DOR 9.0 months (95% CI 6.3, NE), with 58% of responders having DOR ≥6 months. The Applicant's own submitted analysis (November 18, 2019 cutoff, all patients including non-measurable disease, N=132 total) reported an overall ORR of 56.8% (95% CI 47.9, 65.4)
- FDA's Statistical/Clinical review explicitly flags that PFS and OS "are considered not interpretable in a single arm study," and that "any corresponding analyses were considered descriptive and were not confirmed by FDA review" — the entire regulatory basis rests on ORR magnitude and DOR durability, evaluated against FDA's Guidance for Industry on NSCLC clinical trial endpoints

- FDA Accelerated Approval Letter (September 4, 2020) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2020/213721Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- FDA Supplement Approval Letter converting NSCLC indication from accelerated to regular approval (NDA 213721/S-009, August 9, 2023) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2023/213721Orig1s009ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label, original (2020) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2020/213721s000lbl.pdf; current (December 2025, S-016) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/213721s016lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (NDA 213721, Reference ID 4667100), including the Statistical and Clinical Evaluation section (§8) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/213721Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (ARROW) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03037385 (Study Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan posted in the Documents tab, both later versions — Protocol Amendment 15/dated December 1, 2022, and SAP Version 6/dated November 2, 2022 — reflecting the trial's post-approval continuation, not the version in effect at the September 2020 approval)
- Protocol / SAP (posted, later versions) — Protocol Amendment 15: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/85/NCT03037385/Prot_000.pdf; Statistical Analysis Plan Version 6: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/85/NCT03037385/SAP_001.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Gainor JF, Curigliano G, Kim DW, et al. "Pralsetinib for RET fusion-positive non-small-cell lung cancer (ARROW): a multi-cohort, open-label, phase 1/2 study." *Lancet Oncol.* 2021;22(7):959-969. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(21)00247-3>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34118197/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Pralsetinib%20for%20RET%20fusion-positive%20non-small-cell%20lung%20cancer%20ARROW%20a%20multi-cohort%20open-label%20phase%201%2F2%20study)

**Other resources**

- Companion diagnostic: Life Technologies Corporation (Thermo Fisher Scientific)'s Oncomine Dx Target Test (ODxTT), a next-generation-sequencing-based qualitative in vitro diagnostic, was reviewed by CDRH (sPMA P160045/S019) to add RET fusion detection in NSCLC for patient selection, timed for contemporaneous approval alongside pralsetinib.
- No FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held; per the Multi-Discipline Review, "An advisory committee meeting was not deemed necessary for this application because no review issues were identified that raised significant public health questions regarding the risk:benefit assessment of pralsetinib for the proposed indication."
- Confirmatory evidence: postmarketing requirement PMR 3916-1 (verify/further characterize clinical benefit with longer follow-up of ORR/DOR in both NSCLC subgroups) was fulfilled and released as of the August 2023 accelerated-to-regular-approval conversion; the label's current Adverse Reactions and Clinical Studies sections also cite a separate randomized, open-label confirmatory trial, AcceleRET-Lung (NCT04222972, single-agent pralsetinib, n=108, vs. investigator's choice of chemotherapy/immunotherapy, n=104, in treatment-naïve RET fusion-positive NSCLC).
- A related indication for this drug (advanced/metastatic RET-mutant medullary thyroid cancer, approved under a separate original application, NDA 214701, accelerated approval December 1, 2020) was voluntarily withdrawn from the Gavreto label in 2023 (NDA 213721/S-014, approved July 20, 2023) after the sponsor and FDA discussed "challenges associated with fulfilling the confirmatory study" for that indication — a withdrawal for feasibility/business reasons rather than a failed or negative confirmatory trial result. The RET fusion-positive thyroid cancer indication (distinct from RET-mutant MTC) remains on the label under accelerated approval as of the December 2025 label revision.
- Gavreto's EU marketing authorization (originally granted under conditional approval, November 18, 2021) was withdrawn by the European Commission effective October 24, 2024, at the marketing authorization holder's request, "for commercial reasons" — explicitly not a safety or efficacy concern, per EMA's public procedural documentation.
- IPD/dataset access: no Vivli, YODA Project, or Project Data Sphere listing was individually confirmed for ARROW under any of its successive sponsors (Blueprint Medicines, Genentech/Roche, or Rigel Pharmaceuticals); trial-specific IPD availability should be treated as unconfirmed rather than assumed unavailable given Roche's general participation in data-sharing arrangements during its period of sponsorship.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 213721, Reference ID 4667100, §8 Conclusions on the Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness]* — "The recommendation for accelerated approval according to 21 CFR 314.510 Subpart H is based on results from two cohorts of patients with RET fusion-positive NSCLC who received pralsetinib 400 mg once daily in a multicenter, non-randomized, multi-cohort clinical trial in patients with thyroid cancer, NSCLC, and other advanced solid tumors (Study BLU-667-1101; ARROW)."

*[verbatim, same source, §8, Study Endpoints/Primary Efficacy Endpoint]* — "The primary efficacy endpoint was the confirmed ORR based on RECIST v1.1 as assessed by BICR of local imaging. For BICR of local imaging, CT and magnetic resonance imaging scans were sent to a central radiology laboratory for assessment of response and progression by 2 board certified radiologists (if necessary, adjudication was performed by a third board certified radiologist) blinded to patient identification and starting dose."

*[verbatim, same source, §8, Statistical Analysis Plan and Amendments]* — "The final version of the statistical analysis plan, dated October 30, 2019, included assumptions for sample size calculation in the expansion phase for prior platinum therapy and the treatment-naïve cohorts. In cohort 1, which includes patients with RET-fusion positive NSCLC who were previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy, assuming a null hypothesis that ORR=0.23 against an alternative hypothesis of ORR=0.5 with two-sided type I error rate of 0.05, a sample size of 80 will provide more than 95% power. Similarly, in cohort 2, which includes treatment-naïve patients with RET-fusion positive NSCLC, assuming a null hypothesis that ORR = 0.48 against an alternative hypothesis of ORR=0.61 at two-sided type I error rate of 0.05, a sample size of 170 will provide more than 90% power. There was no pre-defined plan for handling missing response assessments for ORR analysis."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "For a single arm study, FDA's efficacy analysis is based on ORR of adequate magnitude and a clinically meaningful duration of response. A statistically significant ORR compared to a historical rate may not necessarily be clinically meaningful."

*[verbatim, same source, Study Endpoints, FDA's Assessment]* — "FDA considers the endpoints of CBR, DCR and 'correlation of RET gene status in plasma and/or tumor tissue with ORR, CBR, DOR, PFS, OS, and DCR' to be exploratory in nature. Additionally, FDA considers the time to event endpoints of PFS and OS to be not interpretable in a single arm study, and any corresponding analyses were considered descriptive and were not confirmed by FDA review."

*[verbatim, same source, Efficacy Results, FDA's Assessment]* — "The efficacy results for the primary endpoint of ORR as assessed by BICR provided by the Applicant is based on the data cutoff of November 18, 2019. The following table provides the ORR analysis based on data cutoff of February 13, 2020. This analysis is considered the primary analysis for this application."

*[verbatim, same source, §9 Advisory Committee Meeting and Other External Consultations]* — "An advisory committee meeting was not deemed necessary for this application because no review issues were identified that raised significant public health questions regarding the risk:benefit assessment of pralsetinib for the proposed indication."

*[verbatim, posted Statistical Analysis Plan, ARROW/BO42863, Version 6 (2-Nov-2022), §1.4.2 Phase 2 (Dose-expansion at the MTD/RP2D)]* — "Group 1: The sample size of approximately 80 RET-fusion NSCLC patients who previously received treatment with a platinum-based chemotherapy will provide > 95% power at the 2-sided significance level of 0.05 for testing the assumption of the null hypothesis ORR=0.23 versus the alternative ORR=0.5. Group 2: The sample size of approximately 170 treatment naïve (1st line) RET-fusion NSCLC patients will provide >90% power at the 2-sided significance level of 0.05 for testing the assumption of the null hypothesis ORR=0.48 versus the alternative ORR=0.61."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.1 Randomization, Stratification, and Blinding]* — "This is an open label, single arm study with no randomization or stratification."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.2 Multiplicity Adjustment]* — "No multiplicity adjustment is planned in this study."

*[verbatim, same source, §4.6.1 Primary Efficacy Endpoint]* — "The primary efficacy endpoint of ORR is defined as the proportion of patients with a confirmed response (complete response [CR] or partial response [PR] for at least two assessments with at least 28 days apart and no disease progression [PD] in between) before PD and/or other anticancer therapy. ORR and its two-sided 95% CI, which is based on the exact binomial distribution (Clopper-Pearson), will be presented."

*[verbatim, FDA Supplement Approval Letter, NDA 213721/S-009, August 9, 2023]* — "This Prior Approval sNDA provides for the conversion from accelerated to regular approval of GAVRETO for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic rearranged during transfection (RET) fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), as detected by an FDA-approved test... SUBPART H FULFILLED. We approved this NDA under the regulations at 21 CFR 314 Subpart H for accelerated approval of new drugs for serious or life-threatening illnesses. Approval of this supplement fulfills your commitments made under 21 CFR 314.510 with respect to the indication for the treatment of patients with metastatic RET fusion-positive NSCLC."

*[verbatim, FDA Supplement Approval Letter, NDA 213721/S-014, July 20, 2023]* — "This Prior Approval sNDA provides for removal of the Advanced and Metastatic RET-mutant Medullary Thyroid Cancer (MTC) Indication, approved under accelerated approval, from GAVRETO United States Prescribing Information (USPI). Following a meeting with FDA wherein the challenges associated with fulfilling the confirmatory study for the MTC indication were discussed, you requested withdrawal of approval of this indication and waived the expedited withdrawal procedures set forth in section 506(c)(3) of the Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act."

Note on source quality: this entry draws on genuine verbatim SAP text, but the posted ClinicalTrials.gov SAP (Version 6, dated November 2, 2022) and Protocol (Amendment 15, dated December 1, 2022) are later versions than the one in effect at the September 2020 approval (which FDA's review identifies as "the final version of the statistical analysis plan, dated October 30, 2019"). The primary-endpoint definition, Clopper-Pearson CI methodology, "no multiplicity adjustment" statement, and no-randomization/no-stratification statement are structural features very unlikely to have changed between versions and are corroborated independently by FDA's Multi-Discipline Review's description of the same methods, so they are presented here as verbatim and reliable; the October 2019 sample-size assumptions themselves are quoted directly from FDA's review (which cites that specific SAP version) rather than reverse-engineered.
