### 121. Naxitamab-gqgk (Danyelza) — BLA 761171

**Sponsor:** Y-mAbs Therapeutics, Inc.

**Indication approved:** In combination with granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF), for the treatment of pediatric patients 1 year of age and older and adult patients with relapsed or refractory high-risk neuroblastoma in the bone or bone marrow who have demonstrated a partial response, minor response, or stable disease to prior therapy — approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DoR)

**Approval date:** November 25, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** two independently conducted single-arm trials pooled to support approval — Study 12-230 (Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center protocol), NCT01757626, and Study 201, NCT03363373

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial (x2, cross-trial pooled/integrated analysis of independently conducted, separately protocoled trials — Study 12-230 is a single-institution MSK trial, Study 201 is a separate multicenter trial), pediatric rare-disease context (rare pediatric disease priority review voucher granted per FDCA §529)
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR, primary — confirmed CR or PR per the 2017-revised International Neuroblastoma Response Criteria [INRC], by blinded independent central review), duration of response (DoR, key secondary, Kaplan-Meier estimated)
- *Primary analysis:* exact/Clopper-Pearson binomial confidence interval around ORR, evaluated per-trial against a pre-specified performance goal (effectiveness concluded if the lower bound of the 2-sided exact 95% CI exceeded 20%, as agreed with FDA at a pre-IND meeting) rather than a pooled formal test
- *Missing data/bias:* not applicable in the randomized-trial sense (no comparator arm); DoR was censored at last disease assessment for non-progressors, with a conservative sensitivity analysis treating non-progressors as having progressed at last assessment; patients whose only evaluable disease site received radiation were excluded from the efficacy analysis (both trials), and patients with progressive disease as best response to prior therapy were excluded from the efficacy population entirely
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval based on single-arm ORR/DoR, confirmatory trial required (here, under the biologics-specific accelerated-approval regulation, 21 CFR 601.41, rather than Subpart H); no FDA advisory committee meeting was held (FDA's review states ODAC referral was unnecessary given the boxed warning adequately addressed safety and there were "no controversial issues"); rare pediatric disease priority review voucher granted concurrently with approval

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 12-230 (MSK, single institution): originally a Phase 1 dose-escalation (3+3) trial of naxitamab (as the murine/humanized 3F8 antibody lineage) plus GM-CSF, later expanded into a single-arm Phase 2 portion; efficacy population at the time of the BLA (Primary Analysis Set, PAS) comprised 38 patients with primary refractory disease or incomplete response to salvage treatment in bone and/or bone marrow, of whom 22 had prior anti-GD2 antibody exposure; the trial protocol was amended 22 times over its long life (institution-run trial spanning 2013-2020 amendments)
- Study 201 (multicenter, 3 sites — US and Spain): a separate single-arm, open-label trial designed as the planned confirmatory/expansion vehicle; at the interim analysis submitted in the BLA, the primary efficacy population comprised 22 patients
- Both trials enrolled patients ≥1 year old with relapsed/refractory high-risk neuroblastoma in bone or bone marrow who had achieved at least stable disease to prior therapy, excluding those with progressive disease as best response and those whose only evaluable disease had received radiation
- Dosing in both trials: naxitamab 3 mg/kg/day IV on Days 1, 3, and 5 of each 4-week cycle (9 mg/kg/cycle total), with GM-CSF 250 μg/m²/day subcutaneously Days -4 to 0 and 500 μg/m²/day Days 1-5; cycles continued until CR/PR followed by 5 additional cycles
- Primary endpoint (both trials): ORR (CR+PR) per blinded independent central review using the revised (2017) INRC, with a 2-sided 95% exact (Clopper-Pearson) binomial CI; per the pre-IND agreement with FDA, effectiveness in each trial was to be concluded if the lower bound of that CI exceeded 20%
- Secondary endpoint: DoR, Kaplan-Meier estimated, censored at last disease assessment for patients without documented progression, with a conservative descriptive sensitivity analysis assuming progression at last assessment for censored patients
- Efficacy results supporting the 2020 approval: in Study 201 (n=22 efficacy population), confirmed ORR was 45% (95% CI: 24-68%), with 30% of the 10 responders having DoR ≥6 months; in Study 12-230 (n=38 efficacy population), confirmed ORR was 34% (95% CI: 20-51%), with 23% of the 13 responders having DoR ≥6 months — both lower CI bounds cleared the pre-specified 20% threshold. FDA's review attributed the numerically lower ORR in Study 12-230 to a higher proportion of heavily pretreated relapsed patients (55% vs. 36% in Study 201)
- FDA's Benefit-Risk conclusion (Multi-Discipline Review) explicitly noted the rarity of the disease as a rationale for accepting single-arm evidence: "Given the rarity of relapsed or refractory high-risk neuroblastoma and the lack of an approved or standard treatment, a randomized trial is not likely to be feasible in this population."
- Safety pooled across both trials (Study 201 n=25, Study 12-230 n=72, safety populations): serious infusion-related reactions (including one cardiac arrest), severe neuropathic pain, and neurotoxicity (including reversible posterior leukoencephalopathy syndrome) drove a boxed warning; no on-study deaths attributable to adverse events were reported

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2020/761171Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2020/761171lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 4707829, BLA 761171; primary statistical reviewer Xiaoxue Li, statistical team leader Pallavi Mishra-Kalyani) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/761171Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (Study 12-230) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01757626
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (Study 201) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03363373
- Protocol / SAP: not posted publicly for either trial (checked via the ClinicalTrials.gov API `documentSection` field for both NCT01757626 and NCT03363373 — neither returns a documents listing); the FDA Multi-Discipline Review directly describes and quotes SAP content (see below) but the sponsor's standalone SAP document itself is not independently available
- Pivotal publications (both published years after the 2020 accelerated approval, reporting more mature/differently-defined cohorts than the interim datasets submitted in the BLA — see note below): Mora J, Chan GCF, Morgenstern DA, et al. "The anti-GD2 monoclonal antibody naxitamab plus GM-CSF for relapsed or refractory high-risk neuroblastoma: a phase 2 clinical trial." *Nat Commun.* 2025;16(1):1636 (Study 201/NCT03363373, final N=74 enrolled, ORR 50% [95% CI 36-64%] in the 52-patient efficacy population). [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-56619-x), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39952926/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=The%20anti-GD2%20monoclonal%20antibody%20naxitamab%20plus%20GM-CSF%20for%20relapsed%20or%20refractory%20high-risk%20neuroblastoma); Kushner BH, Modak S, Mauguen A, et al. "Naxitamab plus stepped-up dosing of granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor for primary refractory high-risk neuroblastoma: results of a phase I/II trial." *J Hematol Oncol.* 2025;18(1):114 (Study 12-230/NCT01757626, a 32-patient primary-refractory subgroup reported with CR-rate/survival endpoints rather than the BLA's ORR framing). [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13045-025-01770-7), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41299684/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Naxitamab%20plus%20stepped-up%20dosing%20of%20granulocyte-macrophage%20colony-stimulating%20factor%20for%20primary%20refractory%20high-risk%20neuroblastoma)

**Other resources**

- No Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for either trial; Study 12-230 was an investigator-initiated MSK protocol (data governance via MSK/NCI norms rather than an industry IPD-sharing program), and Y-mAbs' general IPD-sharing practices for Study 201 were not individually confirmed.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held; per the FDA Multi-Discipline Review, §9: "The Division did not refer this BLA to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee (ODAC) because, in the setting of the boxed warning and other advice in the product labeling, the safety profile is acceptable for the treatment of the indicated population and the application did not raise significant public health questions."
- A rare pediatric disease priority review voucher (FDCA §529) was granted concurrently with approval, per the FDA approval letter.
- Postmarketing requirement (PMR #3950-1): submit the final report and datasets from the ongoing multicenter Study 201, enrolling a minimum of 80 patients with evaluable disease across at least 6 sites (≥5 patients per site in ≥5 sites), with responders followed ≥12 months from response onset, to verify and further characterize clinical benefit and provide a more precise ORR/DoR estimate. A second PMR (#3950-2) required a comprehensive multicenter characterization of infusion-related-reaction risk, given that most premarket safety data came from the single-institution Study 12-230.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761171, Reference ID 4707829, §7 Statistical Analysis Plan and Amendments]* — "The statistical analyses for the interim analysis were defined in the protocol. A standalone statistical analysis plan (SAP) was made. There is only one version of the SAP. The SAP was signed after the statistical analyses of efficacy had started. The principal features in the SAP followed the ones in the protocol. The SAP deviated from the protocol in the following key features: Additional data (e.g., demographics, baseline characteristics, safety, efficacy subgroups) and corresponding analyses, to provide and facilitate an overall interpretation of the results, were specified in the SAP. The per protocol set analyses were not included in the SAP. The analyses performed followed the SAP."

*[verbatim, same source, §7 Efficacy Analysis — Primary efficacy endpoint]* — "The primary efficacy endpoint for the interim analysis of the pivotal Trial 12-230 was the ORR calculated along with a 95% confidence interval using the Clopper-Pearson exact methodology. As agreed at the pre-IND meeting with FDA, effectiveness was concluded if the lower limit of the exact 95% confidence interval was above 20%."

*[verbatim, same source, §7 Efficacy Analysis — Secondary efficacy endpoint]* — "The duration of response (DoR) was estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods and presented in a Kaplan-Meier plot. DoR was censored at the date of last disease assessment in subjects who did not experience PD. As a conservative sensitivity analysis, DoR was also analyzed with descriptive summary statistics in which the subjects were considered to have progressed at last disease assessment."

*[verbatim, same source, §7 Efficacy Analysis — Lack of evaluable disease at baseline]* — "In line with International Council for Harmonisation E9 guidance (Section 5.2.1), subjects who lacked evaluable disease at baseline, as determined by the independent reviewers, were excluded from the efficacy analysis sets. All subjects in the Trial 12-230 Primary Analysis Set [PAS] had a completed baseline response assessment."

*[verbatim, same source, Benefit-Risk Assessment]* — "In Trial 201 (n=22), the confirmed ORR in patients with metastatic, relapsed or refractory high-risk neuroblastoma in the bone or bone marrow who demonstrated a response of stable disease, partial response, or minor response to prior therapy per blinded, independent review was 45% (95% CI: 24%, 68%), with 30% of the 10 responders having observed duration of response (DOR) of at least 6 months... In Trial 12-230 (n=38), the confirmed ORR per blinded, independent review according to the revised INRC was 34% (95% CI: 20%, 51%), with 23% of the 13 responders having an observed DOR of 6 months... The difference in the point estimates of ORR between the two trials may be explained by the higher percentage of relapsed patients, who are more heavily pre-treated, in Trial 12-230 (55% vs. 36% in Trial 201)."

*[verbatim, same source, Benefit-Risk Assessment — rationale for accepting single-arm evidence]* — "Given the rarity of relapsed or refractory high-risk neuroblastoma and the lack of an approved or standard treatment, a randomized trial is not likely to be feasible in this population. The review team considers that the observed ORR in the two trials, along with the DOR, in patients treated with naxitamab in combination with GM-CSF sufficient to provide substantial evidence of the effectiveness of naxitamab in the rare population of patients with relapsed or refractory neuroblastoma who have disease in the bone or bone marrow."

*[verbatim, same source, Benefit-Risk Assessment — accelerated-approval recommendation]* — "The reviewers recommend accelerated approval under Subpart E (21 CFR 601.41) for naxitamab, in combination with GM-CSF, for the treatment of patients with relapsed or refractory high-risk neuroblastoma in the bone or bone marrow who have demonstrated a response of stable disease, partial response or minor response to prior therapy. Accelerated approval is recommended given the small sample size and need for additional multicenter data to confirm the efficacy and safety of naxitamab. Clinical benefit will be verified and further characterized by submission of data on response rate and durability of response from additional patients who will enroll across multiple sites in the ongoing clinical trial, Study 201."

*[verbatim, same source, §13 Postmarketing Requirements, PMR #3950-1 rationale]* — "Naxitamab is being considered under accelerated approval for the treatment of patients with relapsed or refractory neuroblastoma in bone or bone marrow who have demonstrated a response of stable disease or better following initial or subsequent therapy. Approval is based upon the results of a single center study and an interim analysis for an ongoing multicenter study. Continued approval may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit through submission of additional efficacy data from additional patients in the ongoing multicenter clinical trial (Study 201)."

This is a genuinely small-numbers, single-arm accelerated-approval case documented honestly: the entire evidentiary base for the 2020 approval was 60 patients across two uncontrolled trials (22 from a 3-site multicenter trial, 38 from a single MSK institution), with FDA's own review acknowledging a randomized trial was infeasible given disease rarity and basing the ORR performance-goal threshold (lower 95% CI bound >20%) on a pre-IND agreement rather than a formal comparative hypothesis test. Both pivotal trials were subsequently published only in 2024-2025 (years after approval, reflecting the natural lag of small pediatric rare-disease trials plus the confirmatory-trial follow-up period) and, notably, report somewhat different patient subsets and endpoint framings (Study 201's final 74-patient enrollment vs. the 22-patient interim population at approval; Study 12-230's 2025 publication restricted to a 32-patient primary-refractory subgroup using CR-rate and survival endpoints rather than the pooled ORR/DoR framing used in the BLA) — a reminder that a trial's eventual publication does not always map cleanly back onto the specific interim dataset an accelerated approval was actually granted on.

### 122. Gallium Ga 68 PSMA-11 (unbranded) — NDA 212642/212643

**Sponsor:** University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA Biomedical Cyclotron), NDA 212642; and University of California, San Francisco (UCSF Radiopharmaceutical Facility), NDA 212643 — two academic (non-industry) sponsors, each holding a separate, simultaneously-approved New Drug Application for the same unbranded radiopharmaceutical

**Indication approved:** A PET imaging agent indicated for positron emission tomography (PET) of prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) positive lesions in men with prostate cancer: (1) with suspected metastasis who are candidates for initial definitive therapy, and (2) with suspected recurrence based on elevated serum prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level

**Approval date:** December 1, 2020 (both NDAs approved the same day)

**Pivotal trial:** PSMA-PreRP (initial-staging population), run in parallel at UCLA (NCT03368547) and UCSF (NCT02919111); and PSMA-BCR (biochemical-recurrence population), run in parallel at UCLA (NCT02940262) and UCSF (NCT02918357) — each a prospective, single-arm, open-label, two-center (UCLA + UCSF) diagnostic-accuracy trial, with supportive literature meta-analyses (PSMA-PreRP-Meta, PSMA-BCR-Meta) submitted but treated as high-risk-of-bias secondary evidence, not primary evidence

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison) — patients underwent both 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET and a reference standard (surgical histopathology in PSMA-PreRP; a composite clinical reference standard in PSMA-BCR), prospective single-arm open-label two-center trial run jointly across two academic sponsors under a rare "dual-NDA" filing structure, unplanned interim analysis conducted by the Applicants without any statistical adjustment
- *Endpoints:* per-patient sensitivity and specificity of 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET for pelvic nodal metastases against a histopathology reference standard (PSMA-PreRP, co-primary), per-patient and per-region positive predictive value (PPV) against a composite reference standard (PSMA-BCR, primary), positive/negative predictive value for pelvic nodal metastases (PSMA-PreRP, key secondary) — a diagnostic-accuracy endpoint framework, not a clinical-outcome or survival endpoint
- *Primary analysis:* Applicant used the Wilson score method for 95% confidence intervals around sensitivity/specificity/PPV/NPV, and the same method to evaluate whether observed PPV exceeded the pre-specified performance threshold; FDA's own default method for proportion CIs was the Wald method without continuity correction, with Clopper-Pearson exact confidence intervals substituted whenever cell counts were small (np<5 or n(1-p)<5), plus Fisher's exact test for between-group proportion comparisons and t-test for continuous variables (both two-sided); FDA's statistical/clinical team independently re-derived essentially all reported results directly from the submitted patient-level datasets rather than relying on Applicant-computed tables
- *Missing data/bias:* performance-measure analysis without a fully independent reference standard for a subset of the biochemical-recurrence (PSMA-BCR) population, where the composite reference standard incorporated clinical follow-up rather than uniform histopathology — a verification-bias concern FDA explicitly weighed in its benefit-risk assessment; retrospective/non-prospective diagnostic evidentiary basis (two sponsor-submitted literature meta-analyses, PSMA-PreRP-Meta and PSMA-BCR-Meta) downgraded by FDA to supportive-only status because of high assessed risk of bias in the underlying retrospective literature; an unplanned 2018 interim analysis (325 enrolled, 127 with completed prostatectomy, short of the 203-patient efficacy target) triggered no statistical correction because all submitted data had already been collected by that point
- *Regulatory:* regular approval (not accelerated; standard NDA pathway for a New Molecular Entity, Type 1) granted in parallel to two academic-institution NDAs for the identical unbranded product, an FDA-negotiated "dual NDA" arrangement (agreed by email in December 2017) under which the second-filed application had to be submitted before the first's action date and each institution waived exclusivity/patent rights against the other, avoiding the need for either to file an ANDA referencing the other's approval; no FDA advisory committee meeting identified

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Both pivotal trials were prospective, single-arm, open-label, two-center studies conducted jointly at UCLA and UCSF, using identical protocols/case report forms across sites (Module 5 clinical data were reported as identical in both NDAs) but registered as separate ClinicalTrials.gov records per institution: PSMA-PreRP enrolled 325 patients with biopsy-proven intermediate- or high-risk prostate cancer who were candidates for initial definitive therapy (prostatectomy with pelvic lymph-node dissection) — the "Full Data Analysis Set" (patients who received 68Ga-PSMA-11 and subsequently underwent prostatectomy plus pelvic lymph-node dissection) intersected with an "Efficacy Analysis Set" (patients whose scans were independently, blindly interpreted on a per-region basis) formed the primary analysis population, with a separate "Inter-Reader Set" (three independent readers) used for reproducibility analyses
- PSMA-BCR enrolled 635 patients with biochemical recurrence of prostate cancer after definitive local therapy (prostatectomy or radiotherapy), with a composite (not uniformly histopathologic) reference standard used to adjudicate true detection status per patient/region
- PSMA-PreRP primary endpoint: per-patient sensitivity and specificity of 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET for pelvic lymph-node metastases against a histopathology reference standard from prostatectomy/pelvic lymph-node dissection specimens, with pre-specified performance goals of 65% sensitivity and 90% specificity; a key secondary endpoint was per-patient PPV/NPV for the same detection task
- PSMA-BCR primary endpoint: per-patient and per-region PPV of 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET for tumor detection against the composite reference standard, in patients with rising PSA after definitive therapy
- Sample size/power: the Applicants' power analysis for PSMA-PreRP compared 68Ga-PSMA-11's anticipated 65% per-patient nodal-metastasis detection sensitivity against conventional imaging's assumed 45% sensitivity; at 80% power and a 0.01 significance level, 61 patients with nodal metastases were required, which (assuming a 30% true nodal-metastasis prevalence among intermediate/high-risk patients undergoing prostatectomy, and that 25% of enrolled patients would not proceed to prostatectomy) translated to a planned efficacy-evaluable target of 203 prostatectomy patients out of ~271 total planned enrollees
- FDA's statistical/clinical review team re-derived nearly all reported diagnostic-accuracy results directly from patient-level SAS datasets submitted by the Applicants (an amended dataset received January 24, 2020, plus original per-trial datasets), rather than accepting Applicant-computed summary tables at face value, and explicitly notes that "a detailed statistical analysis plan was not submitted with the protocol" — the statistical methodology used in the review was reconstructed largely from the clinical study report and a biostatistics information request response dated October 7, 2019
- Key results: in PSMA-PreRP, using histopathology as the reference standard, 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET had a per-patient sensitivity of 47% (95% CI 29-65%) and specificity of 90% (95% CI 84-96%) for pelvic nodal metastases, with a PPV of 61% (95% CI 41-81%) — notably, the observed sensitivity (47%) fell short of the pre-specified 65% performance goal, while specificity (90%) met its 90% goal exactly; in PSMA-BCR, patient-level PPV against the composite reference standard was 83% (95% CI 75-91%)
- Two supportive literature meta-analyses (PSMA-PreRP-Meta, pooling 5 studies/266 patients from Germany, Australia, and China; PSMA-BCR-Meta, pooling 15 studies/256 patients from 10 countries) and one externally published prospective trial (van Kalmthout et al. 2019, a 104-patient Dutch study with a similar design to PSMA-PreRP) were submitted as supportive evidence but were assessed by FDA as carrying high risk of bias given their retrospective, literature-derived nature (or, for the external trial, lack of FDA access to source data), and were treated as secondary/supportive rather than primary evidence of effectiveness

- FDA Approval Letter (UCSF, NDA 212643) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2020/212643Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (UCLA) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2020/212642s000lbl.pdf

- Drugs@FDA overview / Table of Contents pages: NDA 212642 (UCLA) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/212642Orig1s000TOC.html; NDA 212643 (UCSF) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/212643Orig1s000TOC.html
- ClinicalTrials.gov records: PSMA-PreRP at UCLA — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03368547; PSMA-PreRP at UCSF — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02919111; PSMA-BCR at UCLA — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02940262; PSMA-BCR at UCSF — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02918357

- Pivotal publication (PSMA-BCR): Fendler WP, Calais J, Eiber M, et al. "Assessment of 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET Accuracy in Localizing Recurrent Prostate Cancer: A Prospective Single-Arm Clinical Trial." *JAMA Oncol.* 2019;5(6):856-863. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1001/jamaoncol.2019.0096), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30920593/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Assessment%20of%2068Ga-PSMA-11%20PET%20Accuracy%20in%20Localizing%20Recurrent%20Prostate%20Cancer)
- Pivotal publication (PSMA-PreRP): Hope TA, Eiber M, Armstrong WR, et al. "Diagnostic Accuracy of 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET for Pelvic Nodal Metastasis Detection Prior to Radical Prostatectomy and Pelvic Lymph Node Dissection: A Multicenter Prospective Phase 3 Imaging Trial." *JAMA Oncol.* 2021;7(11):1635-1642. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1001/jamaoncol.2021.3771), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34529005/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Diagnostic%20Accuracy%20of%2068Ga-PSMA-11%20PET%20for%20Pelvic%20Nodal%20Metastasis%20Detection)

**Other resources**

- No FDA advisory committee meeting was identified for either application.
- This is one of the few entries in the census where the "sponsor" is not a pharmaceutical company but two public universities acting as co-developing academic institutions, each separately regulated as an NDA holder — UCLA's IND (130649) was received in 2016, UCSF's earlier IND (127621) in 2015, and the two institutions cross-referenced each other's INDs for most regulatory milestones.
- IPD/dataset access: no Vivli, YODA Project, or Project Data Sphere listing was identified for either trial; as academic-sponsor INDs/NDAs rather than industry submissions, these trials are outside the typical scope of industry data-sharing platforms.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review, NDA 212643, Reference ID 4705530, Regulatory History]* — "Two new drug applications for 68Ga-PSMA-11 injection were received by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on September 6, 2019, NDA 212642 from the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA), and NDA 212643 from the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF). The two Applicants collaborated to conduct the two prospective trials to support both NDAs. They do not wish to file a single NDA due to separate manufacturing processes, and neither wishes to file an ANDA after approval of an NDA submitted by the other. FDA concurrence with the dual NDA approach was sent to the Applicants by email on December 17, 2017, with the conditions that the second NDA be filed before the action date of the first and that the first NDA Applicant waives all exclusivity and patent rights."

*[verbatim, same source, Review Strategy]* — "Primary evidence of effectiveness and safety for 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET for imaging of prostate cancer was provided in two prospective trials, PSMA-PreRP and PSMA-BCR. These trials were conducted in two distinct populations, patients with new diagnoses of prostate cancer who were candidates for initial definitive therapy and patients with biochemical recurrence of disease. The Applicants for NDA 212642 and NDA 212643 collaborated to perform these studies and the Module 5 data presented in each application were identical."

*[verbatim, same source, statistical methods]* — "The 95% confidence intervals for proportions used the method of Wald without continuity correction, unless the sample size was small (defined as np <5 or n(1-p)<5), in which case Clopper-Pearson confidence intervals were reported. Evaluations for difference used t-test for continuous variables and Fisher's exact test for proportions. All tests were two-sided."

*[verbatim, same source, treatment of supportive literature evidence]* — "Because 68Ga-PSMA-11 has been widely used experimentally for several years, the Applicant included two meta-analyses from the scientific literature in similar populations as those of the prospective trials, PSMA-PreRP-Meta and PSMA-BCR-Meta, as evidence of effectiveness. The statistical and clinical teams have reviewed these sources, but due to the retrospective nature of most of the literature, the potential for bias was assessed as high. As such, the meta-analyses were considered as secondary supportive evidence."

*[verbatim, same source, PSMA-PreRP Statistical Analysis Plan section]* — "A detailed statistical analysis plan was not submitted with the protocol. Much of the following is taken from the clinical study report (CSR) and the response to the biostatistics information request received on October 7, 2019."... "The primary endpoints were analyzed using the patients from the intersection of the Full Data Analysis Set and the Efficacy Analysis Set. Goals for sensitivity and specificity were predefined at 65% and 90%, respectively. The 95% confidence intervals for sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV were calculated by the Applicant using the Wilson score method."

*[verbatim, same source, sample size/power]* — "The Applicant's power analysis was based on the comparison of sensitivity between conventional imaging and 68Ga-PSMA-11. With a power of 80% and a significance level of 0.01, a sample size of 61 patients with nodal metastases would be required. The study planned to enroll a total of 271 patients, although only those undergoing prostatectomy were to be included for efficacy analysis (203 patients)."

*[verbatim, same source, unplanned interim analysis]* — "An unplanned interim analysis performed by the Applicant in early 2018, prior to implementation of UCLA protocol version 5 and UCSF protocol version 4... determined that they had not yet met their goal sample size of 203 patients who had undergone prostatectomy. At that time, 325 patients had been enrolled, of whom 127 had subsequently undergone prostatectomy. The study remained open to enrollment after that point, but all data submitted to this application were already collected at the time of the interim analysis. Accordingly, no statistical corrections were applied by the Applicants."

*[verbatim, same source, key results]* — "Using histopathology as the reference standard in patient-level analysis, 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET had a sensitivity of 47% (95% confidence interval 29-65%), specificity of 90% (84-96%), and positive predictive value (PPV) of 61% (41-81%)."... "68Ga-PSMA-11 had a patient-level PPV of 83% (75-91%) using a histopathology reference standard" [PSMA-BCR].

Note on the unusual dual-NDA structure: this is the only entry in the census (so far) where the same clinical data package supports two independently filed and independently approved NDAs from two different (academic, non-industry) sponsors on the same day, a regulatory arrangement FDA agreed to in advance specifically because the two universities used separate manufacturing/synthesis processes for their own cyclotron-produced radiopharmaceutical and neither wished to depend on the other's exclusivity; the substantive clinical/statistical review is a single shared document (issued under the UCSF application number but stated to apply identically to UCLA's).

### 123. Margetuximab-cmkb (Margenza) — BLA 761150

**Sponsor:** MacroGenics, Inc.

**Indication approved:** In combination with chemotherapy, for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer who have received two or more prior anti-HER2 regimens, at least one of which was for metastatic disease

**Approval date:** December 16, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** Study CP-MGAH22-04 ("SOPHIA"), NCT02492711

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized (1:1), open-label, active-controlled Phase 3 trial, stratified permuted randomization, non-randomized infusion-duration sub-study nested within the same protocol (Stages A1/A2/B, evaluating a reduced 30-minute infusion), event-driven trial
- *Endpoints:* progression-free survival (PFS) by blinded independent central review (BICR) — first primary; overall survival (OS) — second primary, tested only if PFS was significant; objective response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DOR) — secondary; investigator-assessed PFS — secondary; patient-reported outcomes (NFBSI-16, EQ-5D-5L) — tertiary
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified by backbone chemotherapy, number of metastatic sites, and number of prior lines of metastatic therapy), Kaplan-Meier estimation, Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test for ORR
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing — PFS tested first at two-sided α=0.05; OS tested only if the PFS null hypothesis was rejected; Hochberg step-up procedure specified in the SAP for two named secondary endpoints
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design for OS (up to three planned analyses: at the time of the primary PFS analysis, at ~70% of target OS events, and at the final analysis of ~385 OS events), Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function with an O'Brien-Fleming stopping boundary, non-binding futility analysis for PFS via conditional power (DSMC could consider stopping if conditional power <20%) at ~100 PFS events, Data Safety Monitoring Committee (DSMC)
- *Missing data/bias:* standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment, four pre-specified PFS sensitivity analyses (uncensoring events regardless of timing; counting unconfirmed clinical progressions; censoring at last assessment before discontinuation for non-progression reasons; excluding patients with major protocol deviations), post-hoc interval-censored PFS analysis conducted specifically to address a review concern that the median PFS difference (0.9 months) was smaller than the 6-week scheduled imaging interval, post-hoc covariate-adjusted analyses exploring a CD16A (FCGR3A) genotype-by-treatment interaction that showed no apparent margetuximab benefit in CD16A-158 V/V homozygotes
- *Regulatory:* regular (traditional) approval based on PFS by BICR in a randomized, active-controlled trial — not accelerated approval; three postmarketing commitments (PMCs), no postmarketing requirements (PMRs), including submission of the final OS analysis from the same trial and a genotype-outcome correlation study for CD16A F158V; no FDA advisory committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study CP-MGAH22-04 (Study 04, SOPHIA): multicenter, randomized (1:1), open-label, active-controlled Phase 3 trial of margetuximab (15 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks) plus chemotherapy vs. trastuzumab (8 mg/kg loading, then 6 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks) plus chemotherapy (investigator's choice of capecitabine, eribulin, gemcitabine, or vinorelbine) in adults with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer who had received ≥2 prior anti-HER2 regimens, ≥1 for metastatic disease; randomization stratified by chemotherapy choice, number of prior lines of metastatic therapy (≤2 vs. >2), and number of metastatic sites (≤2 vs. >2); 536 patients randomized (margetuximab arm n=266, trastuzumab arm n=270)
- Sequential co-primary/dual-primary endpoints, tested in a pre-specified fixed order: PFS by BICR (per RECIST 1.1) tested first; OS tested only if PFS was statistically significant. Per the sponsor's Statistical Analysis Plan (Version 4.0), "Rejecting either the PFS null hypothesis or both the PFS and OS null hypotheses will be considered sufficient for achieving the study's primary objective" and "If the PFS null is not rejected, based on the hierarchical approach, OS cannot be tested"
- Sample size: 257 PFS events were calculated to give 90% power (2-sided α=0.05) to detect a hazard ratio of 0.67 (median PFS improvement from 4 to 6 months); the same overall enrollment (~530 patients accruing ~385 OS events) was separately sized to give 80% power for OS (HR=0.75, median OS improvement from 12 to 16 months) via a group-sequential design with 2 planned interim OS analyses
- Non-randomized infusion sub-study (~78 additional patients, Stages A1/A2/B) evaluated reducing the margetuximab infusion duration from 120 minutes (Cycle 1) to 60 or 30 minutes (Cycle 2+), supporting the to-be-marketed 30-minute maintenance infusion
- Results (data cutoff 10-Oct-2018 for primary PFS analysis): median PFS 5.8 months (95% CI 5.52–6.97) with margetuximab plus chemotherapy vs. 4.9 months (95% CI 4.17–5.59) with trastuzumab plus chemotherapy; stratified HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.593–0.979), stratified log-rank p=0.0334. ORR 22% (95% CI 17–27%) vs. 16% (95% CI 12–20%); median DOR 6.1 vs. 6.0 months. At the second interim OS analysis (data cutoff 10-Sep-2019, 270/385 target OS events, 70% information fraction): median OS 21.6 months (95% CI 18.86–24.05) vs. 19.8 months (95% CI 17.54–22.28); stratified HR 0.885 (95% CI 0.693–1.130), stratified log-rank p=0.3264 — the pre-specified stopping boundary was not crossed, and FDA's review states "No formal conclusions can be drawn from available data. OS data continue to mature"
- Two review issues documented in the FDA Multi-Discipline Review: (1) the median PFS improvement (0.9 months) was smaller than the trial's 6-week scheduled imaging interval — addressed by a post-hoc interval-censored sensitivity analysis (median PFS 5.6 vs. 4.4 months) that FDA accepted as supportive, alongside the reviewers' framing that regular approval does not require superiority over the active comparator, only reasonable assurance of at least comparable benefit; (2) an unexpected CD16A (FCGR3A) genotype-by-treatment interaction (interaction p=0.0121 for PFS) in which margetuximab showed no benefit, or a trend favoring trastuzumab, in CD16A-158 V/V homozygotes (n=69) — mechanistically unexpected given margetuximab's Fc-engineering for higher affinity to both CD16A allotypes, which FDA required be further characterized via a postmarketing commitment rather than treated as disqualifying
- Approval was granted as regular (not accelerated) approval on the BICR-assessed PFS result from this single randomized, active-controlled Phase 3 trial, with three postmarketing commitments (PMCs) and no postmarketing requirements (PMRs): submission of the final OS analysis (completed 2022, published 2023), the CD16A F158V genotype-outcome correlation report, and a validated neutralizing-antibody assay study

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, sponsor Statistical Analysis Plan, Protocol CP-MGAH22-04, Version 4.0, 13 March 2018, §3.2 Statistical Hypotheses]* — "The primary endpoints of centrally-assessed PFS and OS will be compared between groups and tested in sequential order. PFS will be tested first. If PFS is statistically significant, only then will OS be tested. Both hypotheses will be evaluated at α = 0.05... Rejecting either the PFS null hypothesis or both the PFS and OS null hypotheses will be considered sufficient for achieving the study's primary objective. If the PFS null is not rejected, based on the hierarchical approach, OS cannot be tested."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.3.2 Sample Size Justification]* — "To detect a 2 month improvement in median PFS from 4 months to 6 months (HR=0.67) in patients treated with margetuximab plus chemotherapy, assuming that PFS is exponentially distributed, a total of 257 PFS events are required to provide 90% power at a 2-sided α=0.05... assuming that OS is exponentially distributed with median OS time of 12 months for trastuzumab plus chemotherapy arm and 16 months for margetuximab plus chemotherapy arm, 2 interim analyses are performed as described in Section 6.1.1, and a Lan-DeMets alpha spending function using an O'Brien-Fleming stopping boundary is used, approximately 385 deaths will be required to provide 80% power to achieve statistical significance at overall type I error of 2-sided alpha=0.05."

*[verbatim, same source, §6.1.1 Interim Analyses]* — "When approximately 100 of the planned PFS events have occurred, a futility analysis will be performed. Futility will be assessed using conditional power conducted both under the initial study design and under the current trend of the data... The DSMC may consider recommending termination of the study if conditional power is low, such as <20%... The DSMC will also perform a maximum of three efficacy evaluations for the OS endpoint. The first evaluation will be at the time of the PFS assessment endpoint, the second will occur when approximately 70% of the OS events have occurred if the OS endpoint has not been reached at the time of the PFS assessment and lastly if not reached at the second interim, at the time of study completion when approximately 385 OS events have occurred."

*[verbatim, same source, §6.3.1.1]* — "[PFS] compared using a stratified log-rank test, stratified by backbone chemotherapy, number of metastatic sites, and number of lines of prior therapy in the metastatic setting... If the procedure for removing stratification factors in the case of small strata results in the removal of all 3 stratification factors, then the unstratified log-rank test [will be used]."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761150, Reference ID 4717868, Clinical Pharmacology Executive Summary]* — "The sequential primary endpoints of Study 04 were PFS, followed by OS. Study 04 met one of its primary objectives with a PFS prolongation of 0.9 months in the margetuximab + chemotherapy arm (median PFS = 5.8 months) compared to the trastuzumab +chemotherapy arm (median PFS = 4.9 months) and a hazard ratio of 0.76 (95% CI: 0.593, 0.979) favoring margetuximab."

*[verbatim, same source, Efficacy Results — Primary Endpoint, Overall Survival]* — "A second interim analysis of OS after 270 deaths occurred had data cutoff 10-Sep-2019... Median OS was 21.6 months on margetuximab and 19.8 months on trastuzumab (stratified Cox model HR: 0.885; 95% CI: 0.693, 1.130; stratified log-rank p = 0.3264). The stopping threshold was not reached, and the study is powered for final analysis at 385 events. No formal conclusions can be drawn from available data. OS data continue to mature and support clinically meaningful benefit of margetuximab plus chemotherapy in this population."

*[verbatim, same source, Executive Summary]* — "A major review issue with this application was that the magnitude of improvement in median PFS per BIRC was shorter than the imaging interval of 6 weeks. However, as trastuzumab plus chemotherapy is an active control, there is a reasonable assurance that margetuximab plus chemotherapy confers, at the minimum, the same amount of benefit, if not more, as trastuzumab plus chemotherapy in this disease setting. There is not a requirement that a therapy for regular approval be better than that of available therapies... the Applicant conducted a post-hoc interval censored analysis of PFS to assess sensitivity of primary analysis results with respect to imaging interval. The median PFS estimated with this approach in the margetuximab plus chemotherapy arm was 5.6 months... and in trastuzumab plus chemotherapy arm was 4.4 months... These results provide further assurance of robustness of primary analysis results."

*[verbatim, same source, Executive Summary, CD16A subgroup]* — "An additional review issue was that the subgroup of patients with Fc-receptor CD16A-158 V/V homozygote appeared to have different outcomes in a direction unfavorable to margetuximab plus chemotherapy compared to overall study population and other subgroups. This is a mechanistically unexpected finding because margetuximab is specifically Fc-engineered to provide higher affinity, compared to trastuzumab, to both F-carriers and V/V alleles. Further post-hoc analysis accounting for moderate imbalance in prognostics factors did not yield a satisfactory explanation for this observed anomaly... More studies will be required to explain and better understand this apparent incongruity."

*[verbatim, same source, §13 Postmarketing Requirements and Commitment]* — "Postmarketing Requirements (PMRs): None. Postmarketing Commitments (PMCs): 1. Submit the final overall survival analysis and datasets with the final report from clinical Study CP-MGAH22-04... to further confirm the clinical benefit of margetuximab... 2. Provide the final report and dataset containing information pertinent to CD16A (FCGR3A) F158V genotype and patient outcome from clinical trials that correlate CD16A (FCGR3A) F158V genotype with trial efficacy endpoints to further characterize the clinical benefit of margetuximab..."

Note: this is a rare example in the census of a two-endpoint, fixed-sequence PFS→OS design executed as regular (not accelerated) approval, where the second (OS) hypothesis remained formally untested/unresolved at approval (interim analysis only, stopping boundary not crossed) yet approval proceeded on the first (PFS) endpoint alone per the pre-specified hierarchy — with the unresolved OS question and an unexplained pharmacogenomic subgroup anomaly (CD16A V/V) both deferred to postmarketing commitments rather than blocking approval. The genuine sponsor SAP text (Version 4.0) and the FDA Multi-Discipline Review's own framing of the two "major review issues" (imaging-interval-sized PFS effect; CD16A V/V anomaly) are independently consistent, so no inference was needed for the core methodology.

### 124. Relugolix (Orgovyx) — NDA 214621

**Sponsor:** Myovant Sciences GmbH (parent: Myovant Sciences, Inc.) at approval; Myovant was acquired by Sumitomo Pharma in 2023, and the U.S. business now operates as Sumitomo Pharma America, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adult patients with advanced prostate cancer (an oral gonadotropin-releasing hormone [GnRH] receptor antagonist used for androgen deprivation therapy)

**Approval date:** December 18, 2020 (PDUFA goal date December 20, 2020; Priority Review)

**Pivotal trial:** HERO (Study MVT-601-3201), NCT03085095

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized (2:1), open-label, parallel-group, active-controlled (leuprolide acetate depot) phase 3 trial; dual primary-endpoint definition (protocol vs. regulatory) — Evaluation Criterion 1 (a single-arm ≥90% lower-CI-bound threshold in the relugolix group only) was the FDA-designated primary success criterion, while Evaluation Criterion 2 (non-inferiority of relugolix vs. leuprolide) was designated primary for EMA/PMDA; no formal interim efficacy analysis was performed; an external independent Data and Safety Monitoring Board reviewed only periodic safety data, under a separate safety SAP
- *Endpoints:* sustained castration (testosterone-suppression) responder rate — the cumulative probability, estimated by the Kaplan-Meier method, of maintaining serum testosterone <50 ng/dL from Week 5 Day 1 through Week 49 Day 1 (48 weeks), a time-to-event/interval-censored responder construct rather than a single-timepoint proportion; non-inferiority comparison of the same sustained-castration-rate construct between relugolix and leuprolide (secondary for FDA, primary for EMA/PMDA); castration rate at Day 4 and at Week 3 Day 1, confirmed PSA response rate, profound castration rate (<20 ng/dL), FSH suppression at Week 25, castration-resistance-free survival (added for the metastatic subgroup via Protocol Amendment 3), and testosterone recovery rate after treatment discontinuation, all as alpha-protected key secondary endpoints; MACE composite (nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, death from any cause) as a pre-specified but explicitly descriptive/exploratory, unadjudicated safety endpoint
- *Primary analysis:* Kaplan-Meier estimation (Greenwood's formula for variance) with 95% CIs via log-log (complementary log-log) transformation of the survival function, applied both to the single-arm relugolix threshold (Evaluation Criterion 1) and to the between-arm treatment difference (Evaluation Criterion 2)
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing of a deep chain of key secondary endpoints (non-inferiority → Day 4 castration rate → Week 3 castration rate → confirmed PSA response → profound castration rate → FSH level → castration-resistance-free survival → testosterone recovery), each tested only if all prior endpoints in the chain were significant, with separate pre-specified testing orders for the FDA vs. EMA/PMDA given the swapped primary/secondary status of Evaluation Criteria 1 and 2
- *Missing data/bias:* rule-based imputation/censoring for missed testosterone-assessment visits within the interval-censored Kaplan-Meier responder analysis (a patient with a non-castrate reading immediately after a >42-day visit gap is imputed as having escaped castration at the earliest missed-visit date; a single missed visit flanked by castrate readings is imputed as castrate; ≥2 consecutive missed visits [>70-day gap] flanked by castrate readings are censored at the last available assessment); four pre-specified sensitivity analyses (per-protocol population; excluding patients on testosterone-affecting concomitant medications/herbal supplements; treating missed-visit patients as events rather than censored; censoring patients not yet castrate at Week 5 rather than counting them as an immediate event)
- *Regulatory:* FDA-agreed SAP reached via Type C meeting (July 2019, not a Special Protocol Assessment), with FDA-requested additions (extra sensitivity analyses, an Ischemic Heart Disease SMQ) incorporated into Protocol Amendment 3; endpoint not accepted as a valid regulatory endpoint — FDA explicitly declined to accept the non-inferiority secondary comparison (citing undisclosed [b][4]-redacted concerns and differing censoring rules vs. historical trials) and separately declined to credit the numerically lower MACE rate as evidence of "improved cardiac safety," since MACE analysis was pre-specified only as descriptive/unadjudicated; regular approval (not accelerated); no FDA Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- HERO (MVT-601-3201): phase 3, multinational, randomized (2:1), open-label, parallel-group trial of oral relugolix (360 mg loading dose Day 1, then 120 mg once daily) vs. leuprolide acetate depot (22.5 mg, or 11.25 mg in Japan/Taiwan/China, every 12 weeks by injection) in men with androgen-sensitive advanced prostate cancer requiring ≥1 year of continuous androgen deprivation therapy; randomization was stratified by geographic region, presence of metastatic disease, and baseline age (≤75 vs. >75 years)
- Approximately 915 patients were planned for the primary efficacy population under Protocol Amendment 2; after that target was reached, Amendment 3 restricted further enrollment (except in China/Taiwan) to metastatic patients specifically to power the castration-resistance-free-survival secondary endpoint in that high-risk subgroup, driving a total planned enrollment of ~1,100 (actual completed enrollment 1,134 per ClinicalTrials.gov; the primary modified intent-to-treat [mITT] analysis population was 930 patients, 622 relugolix : 308 leuprolide)
- Primary endpoint: sustained castration rate, the cumulative probability (Kaplan-Meier) of testosterone suppression to <50 ng/dL while on treatment from Week 5 Day 1 (Day 29) through Week 49 Day 1 (Day 337); the study specified two separate evaluation criteria to satisfy different regulators — Evaluation Criterion 1 (FDA's primary criterion): the lower bound of the 95% CI for the relugolix-arm sustained castration rate must be ≥90%; Evaluation Criterion 2 (EMA/PMDA's primary criterion): the lower bound of the 95% CI for the relugolix-minus-leuprolide difference must be ≥ −10% (non-inferiority)
- Sample size was based on assumed true sustained-suppression probabilities of 94% (relugolix) and 96% (leuprolide), a 2:1 randomization ratio, and a 15% dropout rate: 610 relugolix patients gave ~90% power to rule out a <90% threshold (Criterion 1), and ~915 total patients gave ≥99% power for the 10%-margin non-inferiority comparison (Criterion 2); no interim efficacy analysis was planned
- Key secondary endpoints, tested in a pre-specified fixed-sequence order only if all preceding endpoints were significant: sustained-castration-rate non-inferiority (Criterion 2, first in the FDA order after Criterion 1 passed); castration rate at Day 4 and Week 3 Day 1; confirmed PSA response rate (>50% reduction, confirmed) at Week 3; profound castration rate (<20 ng/dL) at Week 3; FSH level at Week 25; castration-resistance-free survival in metastatic patients (and in the combined metastatic/non-metastatic population), tested only at the final analysis; time to testosterone recovery to >280 ng/dL at 90-day follow-up
- Statistical methods: Kaplan-Meier estimation with Greenwood's-formula variance and log-log-transformed 95% CIs for both the single-arm proportion and the between-arm difference; detailed rule-based censoring conventions handled missed visits (treating certain missed-visit patterns as an escape event, others as imputed-castrate, others as censored, depending on the surrounding assessments); four pre-specified sensitivity analyses (per-protocol population; excluding patients on testosterone-affecting concomitant medications; conservative missed-visit-as-event; delayed-suppression censoring) all supported the primary result
- Result: sustained castration rate at Day 337 was 96.7% (95% CI 94.9%-97.9%) for relugolix vs. 88.8% (95% CI 84.6%-91.8%) for leuprolide in the mITT population — the primary endpoint (Evaluation Criterion 1, lower bound ≥90%) was met (94.9% > 90%); FDA, however, did not accept the non-inferiority secondary comparison (Evaluation Criterion 2) as valid supporting evidence, citing an undisclosed reason plus differing censoring conventions between HERO and the historical trials used for cross-trial comparison, and therefore also declined any superiority claim (which was not pre-specified in the SAP in any case)
- Safety/MACE: a pre-specified but explicitly descriptive, unadjudicated MACE composite (nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, death from any cause) occurred in 2.9% of relugolix patients vs. 6.2% of leuprolide patients over 48 weeks (a numerical/exploratory HR of 0.46, 95% CI 0.24-0.88, per the Applicant); FDA's Multi-Discipline Review explicitly states it "does not agree that the HERO study demonstrated an improved cardiac safety profile compared to leuprolide," because "analysis of MACE was pre-specified only as a descriptive endpoint without alpha control and no adjudication was performed," and FDA "considers these results exploratory only" — a genuine sponsor-vs.-FDA disagreement over how much weight an unadjudicated, non-alpha-protected safety signal can bear

**Other resources**

- Myovant/Sumitomo Pharma's general IPD-sharing program participation (e.g., Vivli, YODA Project) was not individually confirmed for HERO/NCT03085095; state plainly as unconfirmed rather than assumed.
- No FDA Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held for this application; the Multi-Discipline Review states simply, "This application was not presented to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee."
- Regulatory history in the Multi-Discipline Review documents an unusually FDA-collaborative SAP development process: agreement on the primary endpoint definition and KM analytic method at an October 2015 End-of-Phase-2 meeting (under the original sponsor, Takeda/Millennium), a July 2019 Type C meeting to finalize the SAP (with FDA-requested sensitivity analyses and an added Ischemic Heart Disease SMQ folded into Protocol Amendment 3), and a February 2020 pre-NDA meeting agreeing the integrated efficacy/safety analysis plans — none of these were a formal Special Protocol Assessment.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, ClinicalTrials.gov-posted Statistical Analysis Plan, NCT03085095, SAP dated 7 Nov 2019, §2.1 Summary]* — "The MVT-601-3201 (HERO) study is a phase 3, multinational, randomized, open-label, parallel-group study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of relugolix in patients with androgen-sensitive advanced prostate cancer who require at least 1 year of continuous androgen deprivation therapy... The primary endpoint is sustained castration rate, defined as the cumulative probability of testosterone suppression to < 50 ng/dL (1.7 nmol/L) while on study treatment from Week 5 Day 1 (Study Day 29) through Week 49 Day 1 (Study Day 337)."

*[verbatim, same source, §2.2 Sample Size Justification]* — "For Evaluation Criterion 1, 610 patients in the relugolix group will provide approximately 90% power to rule out a fixed probability of sustained testosterone suppression of < 90% at a two-sided type I error rate of 0.05. For Evaluation Criterion 2, with a noninferiority margin of -10% and an overall two-sided type I error rate of 0.05, a total of approximately 915 patients (610 receiving relugolix, 305 receiving leuprolide acetate) will yield at least 99% power to declare the noninferiority of relugolix to leuprolide acetate. The 10% noninferiority margin for the comparison of relugolix versus leuprorelin is based on regulatory precedence of pivotal assessment of gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) antagonist degarelix versus leuprorelin as well as studies of branded GnRH agonist generics."

*[verbatim, same source, §7.2 Multiplicity Adjustment]* — "The primary and the key secondary efficacy analyses will be performed at an overall two-sided type I error of 0.05... If the result of the primary endpoint analysis meets the respective evaluation criterion of the primary endpoint, the key secondary endpoints will then be tested with a fixed-sequence testing procedure... to maintain the overall familywise error rate of 0.05 for the testing of primary and key secondary endpoints."

*[verbatim, same source, §7.3 Primary Efficacy Endpoint]* — "Evaluation Criterion 1: to determine whether the sustained castration rate for relugolix is ≥ 90%. The lower bound of the 95% CI for the cumulative probability of sustained testosterone suppression in the relugolix treatment group will be calculated and must be at least 90% for this criterion to be met... Evaluation Criterion 2: to establish the noninferiority of relugolix to leuprolide acetate 3-M depot injection... Evaluation Criterion 1 is a regulatory requirement from the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA). Evaluation Criterion 2 is required by European Medicines Agency (EMA) and Japanese Pharmaceutical and Medical Device Agency (PMDA)."

*[verbatim, same source, §7.3.1.2 Kaplan-Meier Analysis and Censoring Rules]* — "Patients who had one or more consecutive missed visits (ie, a visit gap of > 42 days) and had a non-castrate assessment immediately after the missed visit(s) will be considered as having an escape at the target day of the earliest missed visit prior to the non-castrate assessment; Patients with one missed visit who has a castrate assessment immediately before and after the missed visit will be assumed to be castrated at the missed visit; Patients with two or more consecutive missed visits (ie, a visit gap of > 70 days) and who had a castrate assessment immediately before and after the missed visits will be censored at the last available testosterone assessment prior to the missed visits."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 214621, Reference ID 4719259, §3.2 Summary of Presubmission/Submission Regulatory Activity]* — "In July 2019, a Type C meeting was held with the FDA to discuss and agree to the original SAP for the pivotal study MVT-601-3201. Myovant incorporated feedback from the FDA including the additions for sensitivity analyses and an analysis using the Ischemic Heart Disease Standardised MedDRA query (SMQ) that includes all ischemic cardiovascular disease in addition to myocardial infarction. The updated SAP was based on protocol Amendment 3 and included modifications to the censoring rules and testing procedures for the primary and alpha-protected secondary endpoints."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.3 Statistical Issues]* — "Study HERO met its primary objective of achieving and maintaining castration (testosterone suppression to < 50 ng/dL) while on study treatment (from Week 5 Day 1 through 48 weeks) by demonstrating that the lower bound of the 95% CI around the cumulative probability of castration rate at the end of 48 weeks was greater than 90%. The results were supported by sensitivity analyses and subgroup analyses. FDA does not accept the first key secondary endpoint of sustained castration rate (non-inferiority test between relugolix and leuprolide) [redacted, b(4)]... Another issue for conducting the non-inferiority comparison is that different censoring rules were used in historical trials and study HERO. As the proposed non-inferiority comparison was not acceptable, no further claims could be made on this comparison including a superiority claim that was not pre-specified in the study statistical analysis plan."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.2 (safety narrative)]* — "The FDA does not agree that the HERO study demonstrated an improved cardiac safety profile compared to leuprolide. While the incidence of MACE as defined by the SMQs of myocardial infarction, central nervous system hemorrhages, and cerebrovascular conditions, and death due to any cause was numerically lower on the relugolix arm compared to the leuprolide arm, analysis of MACE was pre-specified only as a descriptive endpoint without alpha control and no adjudication was performed. The FDA considers these results exploratory only."

This is a genuine example of an FDA-collaborative but ultimately partly-rejected SAP: FDA agreed the primary endpoint definition, the Kaplan-Meier method, and even added its own requested sensitivity analyses and an SMQ during a 2019 Type C meeting — yet at review, FDA still declined to accept the sponsor's non-inferiority secondary claim (over a redacted concern plus a cross-trial censoring-rule mismatch) and separately refused to credit the numerically favorable, unadjudicated MACE signal as evidence of a genuine cardiac-safety advantage, despite that signal later becoming a prominent part of relugolix's clinical narrative and labeling discussion. It illustrates that pre-submission FDA collaboration on a SAP does not guarantee FDA will accept every analysis the collaboratively-built SAP subsequently produces.

### 125. Tepotinib (Tepmetko) — NDA 214096

**Sponsor:** EMD Serono, Inc. (Billerica, MA) — the US commercial name for the healthcare business of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, in the United States and Canada; not affiliated with Merck & Co., Inc. (Kenilworth, NJ/Rahway, NJ), an entirely separate company that has held the "Merck" name in the US/Canada since the two firms split in 1917. Tepotinib was discovered and is manufactured by Merck KGaA (the VISION trial's clinical-trial-registry sponsor is listed as Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany).

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring mesenchymal-epithelial transition (MET) exon 14 (METex14) skipping alterations

**Approval date:** February 3, 2021 (accelerated approval, 21 CFR 314.500/Subpart H); converted to traditional/regular approval February 15, 2024 (NDA 214096/S-003), upon fulfillment of the postmarketing requirement

**Pivotal trial:** VISION (Study MS200095-0022), NCT02864992

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial; multi-cohort Phase II design in which Cohort A (METex14 skipping, first enrolled) and Cohort C (METex14 skipping, opened later via Protocol Amendment 6 as an explicitly-labeled "confirmatory part" enrolling under identical eligibility criteria and procedures) together supplied the confirmatory evidence for the same molecularly-defined indication, while a third, ineligible-for-this-indication cohort (Cohort B, MET amplification/METex14-negative) was enrolled in parallel under the same protocol; biomarker-selected/enriched population (METex14 skipping alterations confirmed centrally by tissue [TBx] and/or plasma circulating-tumor-DNA liquid biopsy [LBx] assay); interim futility analysis with a pre-specified minimum-responder stopping rule (enrollment of TBx-only-positive patients into Cohort A would have stopped had ≤3 of the first 12 TBx-analysis-set subjects responded; analogous ≤2-of-12 rule for Cohort B)
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR, primary; confirmed complete response [CR] or partial response [PR] per RECIST 1.1, assessed by a blinded Independent Review Committee [IRC/BICR]), duration of response (DOR, key secondary), progression-free survival and overall survival (secondary, descriptive/exploratory — FDA and the sponsor agreed these are not interpretable without a randomized control), patient-reported outcomes (EQ-5D-5L, EORTC QLQ-C30, EORTC QLQ-LC13, secondary/exploratory)
- *Primary analysis:* exact/Clopper-Pearson-type two-sided 95% binomial confidence interval around ORR; descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (point estimate + CI, no formal hypothesis test — the sponsor's original design-stage sample-size target of an ORR of 40-50% with the CI lower bound exceeding 20% was used by FDA only "as a guide to facilitate sample size calculation," not as a pre-specified pass/fail hypothesis test; the executed primary analysis reported the ORR and Clopper-Pearson CI with no formal statistical test); Kaplan-Meier estimation used descriptively for DOR/PFS/OS
- *Missing data/bias:* standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment; FDA separately performed a descriptive comparison of tepotinib's ORR/DOR/PFS/OS against literature-derived and within-study "prior-therapy" historical-control response rates for context, but flagged this as limited by selection bias of the VISION-enrolled population and differences in study design/population versus the literature-derived comparators; FDA also noted small subgroup sample sizes (e.g., smoking-status subgroup) yielded wide, overlapping confidence intervals from which "no definitive conclusions can be drawn"
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval based on single-arm ORR/DoR, confirmatory trial required; confirmatory evidence via continuation/expansion of the same pivotal single-arm trial (not an independent trial) — the Clinical PMR required a more precise BICR-assessed ORR/DOR estimate from ≥130 treatment-naïve and ≥143 previously-treated patients (drawing on the Cohort A + Cohort C expansion of VISION), and the requirement was reviewed and deemed fulfilled in the February 15, 2024 NDA 214096/S-003 supplement, converting the indication to traditional approval; no FDA Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting held ("the application did not raise significant public health questions...or significant safety or efficacy issues"); post-marketing commitment (PMC) for analytical/clinical validation of a companion diagnostic test, since no FDA-approved test for METex14 skipping existed at approval

**Trial design & endpoints**

- VISION (MS200095-0022): ongoing, multicenter (128 sites; Belgium, France, Germany, Israel, Italy, Japan, Poland, South Korea, Spain, Taiwan, the Netherlands, US), Phase II, single-arm, open-label trial of tepotinib 500 mg orally once daily (equivalent to 450 mg free-base tepotinib) in adults with advanced/metastatic NSCLC harboring METex14 skipping alterations (Cohorts A and C) or MET amplification without METex14 skipping (Cohort B, outside the approved indication), treatment-naïve or with ≤2 prior lines of systemic therapy, measurable disease by RECIST 1.1, ECOG 0-1
- Primary endpoint: ORR (confirmed CR or PR) per RECIST 1.1 as assessed by a blinded IRC; secondary endpoints: ORR by investigator assessment, DOR and PFS (IRC and investigator), overall survival, and patient-reported outcomes
- No formal statistical hypothesis was tested; per the FDA Statistical/Clinical Review, "data were analyzed in a descriptive manner." Design-stage sample-size logic (protocol §8.1) aimed to show an ORR of 40-50% with the lower bound of the exact two-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson CI exceeding 20%, based on n=60-per-analysis-set operating characteristics (e.g., a 60% ORR with n=60 yields a 95% CI of 46.5-72.4%) — but FDA's review explicitly states it "does not abide by the target ORR selected by the applicant for efficacy assessment but allows it only as a guide to facilitate sample size calculation"
- At the efficacy data cutoff supporting the original approval (January 1, 2020), the efficacy-evaluable population comprised 152 Cohort A patients with METex14 skipping alterations — 69 treatment-naïve and 83 previously treated (1-2 prior lines) — with Cohort C still enrolling; by the July 1, 2020 safety-update cutoff, Cohorts A + C together totaled 255 METex14-positive patients used to inform labeling's safety sections
- Results at approval: BICR-assessed ORR 43% (95% CI 32-56%), median DOR 10.8 months (95% CI 6.9-NE), 67% of 31 responders with DOR ≥6 months in the treatment-naïve population; BICR ORR 43% (95% CI 33-55%), median DOR 11.1 months (95% CI 9.5-18.5), 50% of 37 responders with DOR ≥6 months in the previously-treated population
- Analysis-population structure was unusually granular for a single-arm trial: three parallel primary analysis sets per cohort (TBx-and/or-LBx combined, LBx-only, TBx-only), reflecting that METex14 status could be established by either a tissue or a liquid-biopsy central assay, with subjects positive by both assigned to both sets
- FDA's Statistical/Clinical Review states the current data were "considered adequate to support accelerated approval rather than regular approval" because of the "relatively limited duration of follow-up and the number of patients in the primary efficacy analysis population," and that "due to the relatively low incidence of MET exon 14 skipping alterations in NSCLC, a randomized trial in this patient population is not feasible" — additional confirmatory data were instead to come from continued follow-up/enrollment of the same VISION trial (i.e., Cohort C's continuing enrollment and longer follow-up of Cohort A), rather than a separate, independently designed confirmatory trial

- FDA Approval Letter (original accelerated approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2021/214096Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- FDA Supplement Approval Letter (S-003, Subpart H fulfilled / traditional approval, Feb 15, 2024) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2024/214096Orig1s003ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (original) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2021/214096s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (combined Clinical/Statistical/Clinical Pharmacology review, Reference ID 4737966, NDA 214096 original approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/214096Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (VISION) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02864992 (Study Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan [titled "Integrated Analysis Plan"] both posted in the Documents tab)
