- Pivotal publication: Paik PK, Felip E, Veillon R, et al. "Tepotinib in Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer with MET Exon 14 Skipping Mutations." *N Engl J Med.* 2020;383(10):931-943. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2004407), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32469185/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Tepotinib%20in%20Non-Small-Cell%20Lung%20Cancer%20with%20MET%20Exon%2014%20Skipping%20Mutations)

**Other resources**

- The ClinicalTrials.gov record's IPD-sharing statement indicates Merck KGaA/EMD Serono commits to sharing study protocols, anonymized patient data, study-level data, and redacted clinical study reports with qualified researchers within six months of approval of a new product/indication in both the US and EU (portal: bit.ly/IPD21); trial-specific fulfillment for VISION was not individually confirmed beyond the posted protocol/SAP documents.
- No FDA Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held for this application.
- A companion-diagnostic PMC (analytical/clinical validation of a METex14-skipping test) was outstanding as of the 2024 S-003 letter, which noted a related postmarketing commitment "is still open."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, ClinicalTrials.gov-posted Integrated Analysis Plan (IAP)/SAP, NCT02864992, MS200095-0022, §14.1.1 Primary analyses of objective response (based on independent review)]* — "The primary endpoint is objective response (confirmed complete response [CR] or partial response [PR]) determined according to RECIST Version 1.1, based on independent review (IRC)... For all cohorts the primary analysis of the primary endpoint will be based on the SAF analysis set... No formal statistical hypotheses will be tested. The number of subjects achieving objective response and the ORR (based on independent review) and the corresponding 2-sided exact Clopper-Pearson 95% CI will be presented." *(Note: this document's text layer has individually kerned/spaced characters — a redaction-pipeline artifact seen previously in this census on other sponsors' posted PDFs — recovered here by collapsing single intra-word spaces and treating double-spaces as word boundaries; the quoted passage above is a faithful reconstruction of unambiguous plain text, not a paraphrase.)*

*[verbatim, same source, §6 Overview of Planned Analyses, Part 1: Cohort A]* — "Interim Futility Analysis: When 12 subjects in the TBx analysis set have completed 4 cycles (84 days +/- 3 days) or have prematurely discontinued trial treatment for any reason, whichever comes first... If 3 or less confirmed responders are observed at the futility interim analysis on 12 subjects in the TBx analysis set, the enrolment of subjects into Cohort A, tested positive for METex14 skipping alterations TBx, but not in plasma ctDNA will be discontinued... 9-month follow-up analysis:...It will be used as the primary analysis for United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA)... 15-month follow-up analysis:...This analysis has been introduced in accordance with feedback from the FDA."

*[verbatim, ClinicalTrials.gov-posted Protocol, NCT02864992, MS200095-0022, §8.1 Sample Size]* — "In each of the 3 primary analysis sets, the trial aims to show an ORR based on independent review (performed by an IRC) in the range of 40% to 50% and to demonstrate that the lower limit of the corresponding exact 2-sided 95% confidence interval (CI; according to Clopper-Pearson) for ORR exceeds 20% across lines of therapy... With a sample size of n = 60 per analysis set, a maximum width for the 95% CI of 26.4% will be achieved."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.5.2 Analysis of Primary Endpoint]* — "Objective response rate (confirmed CR or PR) and the corresponding 2-sided exact Clopper-Pearson 95% CI will be presented. Part 1: Cohort A (METex14 skipping alterations) and Part 2: Cohort C (confirmatory part for METex14 skipping alterations)... The primary endpoint analysis will be based on the 3 primary analysis sets: ITT TBx or LBx analysis set... ITT LBx analysis set... ITT TBx analysis set."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation, NDA 214096, Reference ID 4737966, §8 Statistical and Clinical Evaluation — Statistical Analysis Plan and Amendments]* — "No formal statistical hypothesis was tested; data were analyzed in a descriptive manner... The primary endpoint of OR was assessed by the ORR, which was defined as the proportion of patients with a best overall response (BOR) of confirmed CR or PR, as assessed per RECIST 1.1 by IRC. The study aims for an ORR (based on an IRC primary endpoint measure) in the range of 40% to 50%, with a lower limit of the corresponding exact 2-sided 95% CI (according to Clopper-Pearson) to be above 20%... The FDA's Assessment: FDA generally agrees with the Applicant's description of primary and secondary endpoints and statistical analysis plan. FDA does not abide by the target ORR selected by the applicant for efficacy assessment but allows it only as a guide to facilitate sample size calculation. Time-to-event endpoints such PFS and OS are not interpretable in non-randomized open-label trials without a control arm."

*[verbatim, same source, Conclusions on the Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness]* — "The submitted evidence meets the statutory evidentiary standard for accelerated approval. The recommendation for accelerated approval according to 21 CFR 314.510 Subpart H is based on results from patients with metastatic NSCLC harboring mesenchymal-epithelial transition (MET) exon 14 skipping alterations who received tepotinib 450 mg once daily in a multicenter, non-randomized, multi-cohort study (VISION). The demonstrated overall response rates (ORR) per Blinded Independent Review Committee (BIRC) of 43% (95% CI 32, 56) with a median duration of response (DOR) of 10.8 months in 69 treatment-naïve patients and 43% (95% CI 33, 55) with a median DOR of 11.1 months in 83 patients who had disease progression after one or two prior therapies are considered clinically meaningful."

*[verbatim, same source, Benefit-Risk Assessment]* — "Given the relatively limited duration of follow-up and the number of patients in the primary efficacy analysis population for this application, the current data are considered adequate to support accelerated approval rather than regular approval. Due to the relatively low incidence of MET exon 14 skipping alterations in NSCLC, a randomized trial in this patient population is not feasible. To verify the clinical benefit of tepotinib in patients with NSCLC whose tumors harbor MET exon 14 skipping alterations, additional data will be obtained from the clinical trial which supported this approval, the VISION Study."

*[verbatim, same source, §8, Statistical Issues]* — "Regarding the smoking status subgroup results, though it seems like a significant difference, FDA believes it is hard to make inference regarding a subgroup from a small trial. The smoking status subgroup confidence intervals are wide and overlap, so given the relatively small sample sizes no definitive conclusions can be drawn... As described in FDA's Assessment of Study Endpoints, PFS and OS results are difficult to interpret in a non-randomized, open-label trial without a control, and therefore are considered exploratory in the VISION study. FDA did not independently confirm the results of these endpoints."

*[verbatim, same source, §9 Advisory Committee Meeting and Other External Consultations]* — "The division did not refer this application to an advisory committee because the application did not raise significant public health questions on the role of tepotinib in the proposed indication. The application also did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues."

*[verbatim, FDA Supplement Approval Letter, NDA 214096/S-003, Feb 15, 2024]* — "We approved this NDA under the regulations at 21 CFR 314 Subpart H for accelerated approval of new drugs for serious or life-threatening illnesses. Approval of this supplement fulfills your commitments made under 21 CFR 314.510... We have received your submission dated April 25, 2023, containing the final report for the following postmarketing requirement listed in the February 3, 2021 approval letter... We have reviewed your submission and conclude that the above requirement was fulfilled."

Both the sponsor's Integrated Analysis Plan/SAP and its underlying protocol were located as genuine posted documents on ClinicalTrials.gov, and the FDA Multi-Discipline Review independently confirms (and in places directly quotes) the same primary-analysis language, so no reverse-engineering was required for this entry. Tepotinib is a clean example of a Subpart H accelerated approval whose confirmatory-evidence requirement was satisfied entirely by continued follow-up/enrollment of the same pivotal single-arm trial (VISION's Cohort A extended follow-up plus Cohort C, an explicitly protocol-labeled "confirmatory part" for the identical molecular population) rather than an independently designed randomized confirmatory trial — and, unlike several other single-arm accelerated approvals in this census, the confirmatory requirement was reviewed and confirmed fulfilled, converting to traditional approval within three years.

### 126. umbralisib (Ukoniq) — NDA 213176

**Sponsor:** TG Therapeutics, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with relapsed or refractory marginal zone lymphoma (MZL) who have received at least one prior anti-CD20-based regimen, and adult patients with relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma (FL) who have received at least three prior lines of systemic therapy — both indications approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate (the NDA carried two "Original" submission numbers, Orig1 for MZL and Orig2 for FL, reviewed and approved together)

**Approval date:** February 5, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** UNITY-NHL (Study UTX-TGR-205), NCT02793583 — MZL and FL cohorts (single-arm, Simon's two-stage design per cohort), within a larger multi-cohort Phase 2b trial that separately also contained a randomized combination-therapy comparison unrelated to these two accelerated-approval cohorts

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial (Simon's two-stage design per cohort, embedded within a larger multi-cohort trial whose overall registration record on ClinicalTrials.gov is titled as a Phase 2b randomized study, though the MZL/FL accelerated-approval cohorts themselves were single-arm), biomarker/histology-selected cohorts (MZL cohort required ≥1 prior anti-CD20 regimen; FL cohort required ≥3 prior lines, a threshold FDA raised from the sponsor's proposed ≥2)
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR)/duration of response (DoR) (primary, assessed by an independent central radiology group [ICRG] using IWG 2007 criteria modified so index lesions could be nodal or extranodal per the Lugano 2014 approach); PFS and OS were reported but explicitly flagged as not usable for a definitive conclusion given the single-arm design
- *Primary analysis:* exact (Clopper-Pearson) binomial confidence interval around ORR in each cohort; per-cohort design-stage one-sided hypothesis test (MZL: H0 ORR≤25% vs. Ha ORR≥45%; FL: H0 ORR≤35% vs. Ha ORR≥51.5%, each at one-sided α=2.5%), though FDA's review states plainly it "does not use inferential procedures... to evaluate single arm trial results" and instead bases its conclusion on the estimated ORR magnitude and durability
- *Multiplicity:* not applicable — no formal multi-endpoint hypothesis test; the MZL and FL cohorts were analyzed and reported entirely separately
- *Missing data/bias:* not applicable in the randomized-trial sense; FDA's review states that in "the absence of a control arm and due to the open-label single-arm design of the trial, it is difficult to interpret and is unlikely to provide evidence to support the time-to-event endpoints, PFS and OS... comparing them to historical controls is prone to bias"
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval (21 CFR 314.500) based on ORR in two separately-evidenced single-arm cohorts; FDA narrowed the sponsor's proposed FL line-of-therapy threshold (≥2 prior lines → ≥3) citing "residual uncertainty regarding the benefit" relative to other 3rd-line-plus options with reported ORRs of 57-80%; voluntary withdrawal of the entire marketing authorization (both indications) in 2022 after a confirmatory trial in a *different* indication/population (UNITY-CLL, chronic lymphocytic leukemia) revealed a possible overall-survival/mortality signal — a materially different and more severe pattern than the standard "confirmatory trial simply failed to verify benefit" withdrawal already catalogued in this taxonomy under "Voluntary withdrawal of an accelerated-approval indication after confirmatory-trial failure" — a cross-indication safety-driven withdrawal.

**Trial design & endpoints**

- UNITY-NHL / UTX-TGR-205: an open-label, multi-cohort trial (NCT02793583) sponsored by TG Therapeutics; the MZL cohort enrolled 69 patients and the FL cohort enrolled 131 (117 evaluable), each analyzed as a single-arm Simon's two-stage design with a futility stopping rule; response and progression were determined by an independent central radiology group (ICRG) applying IWG 2007 criteria as modified by the Lugano 2014 classification (index lesions could be nodal or extranodal rather than tracked separately)
- Primary endpoint (both cohorts): ORR by ICRG, with duration of response as a key secondary measure; Protocol Amendment 6 (20 Aug 2018) formally made ORR the primary endpoint for all cohorts and demoted CR rate/PFS to secondary status
- Sample size/power: MZL planned n=60 (enrolled 69), designed so an ORR of 38% (23/60 responders) would achieve a one-sided 97.5% lower confidence bound above the 25% null; FL planned n=100 (117 enrolled, 117 evaluable minus exclusions), designed so an ORR of 45% (45/100) would achieve a one-sided 97.5% lower bound above the 35% null
- Efficacy results: MZL — ORR by IRC 49% (95% CI 37.0-61.6%), 16% CR, median follow-up 20.3 months; FL — ORR by IRC 42.7% (95% CI 33.6-52.2%), 3.4% CR, median duration of response 11.1 months (95% CI 8.3-16.4), median follow-up 20.1 months
- FDA's Office of Scientific Investigations inspected the two top-enrolling sites (MD Anderson, Levine Cancer Institute) plus the sponsor and found the data "reliable... in compliance with Good Clinical Practice"
- No formal SAP-driven confirmatory Phase 3 trial for MZL/FL was completed before the entire authorization was withdrawn; the required postmarketing confirmatory trial (PMR 3999-1, a randomized Phase 3 immunotherapy ± umbralisib design) had a final-report target of June 2027 and was overtaken by events in the unrelated UNITY-CLL trial

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2021/213176s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Drug Safety Communication, initial signal (Feb 3, 2022) — https://www.fda.gov/drugs/development-approval-process-drugs/fda-investigating-possible-increased-risk-death-lymphoma-medicine-ukoniq-umbralisib

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 213176, MZL cohort sample-size section]* — "According to the SAP, the planned sample size was 60 patients. When using a test having one-sided 2.5% false positive error rate to assess the null hypothesis that the IRC-reviewed ORR is 25%, the trial would have 90% power (respectively, 97.5% power) against the alternative hypothesis that ORR is 45% (respectively, 49%). Using a confidence interval of the ORR derived using the Clopper-Pearson exact method, an estimated ORR of 38% (i.e., 23 subjects responding of 60 MZL subjects evaluated) would achieve a 1-sided 97.5% lower bound of 25.0%."

*[verbatim, same source, FL cohort sample-size section]* — "According to the sample size calculation provided in the SAP, 100 patients in the FL cohort would provide a 90% power at the 5% level of significance to rule out 35% ORR under the null against the alternative hypothesis that ORR is 51.5%. Using a confidence interval of the ORR derived using the Clopper-Pearson exact method, an estimated ORR of 45% (i.e., 45 subjects responding of 100 FL subjects evaluated) would achieve a 1-sided 97.5% lower bound of 35.0%."

*[verbatim, same source, response-criteria section]* — "The determination of response and progression was based on the International Working Group (IWG) Revised Response Criteria for Malignant Lymphoma (Cheson et al., 2007) modified so that the six index lesions included both nodal and extranodal lesions as described in the Lugano classification (Cheson et al. 2014) rather than considering nodal and extranodal lesions separately. The best clinical response and disease progression were determined by the independent central radiology group (ICRG)."

*[verbatim, same source, time-to-event caveat]* — "In the absence of a control arm and due to the open-label single-arm design of the trial, it is difficult to interpret and is unlikely to provide evidence to support the time-to-event endpoints, PFS and OS... comparing them to historical controls is prone to bias."

*[verbatim, FDA efficacy summary, MZL]* — "median follow-up was 20.3 months (range 15.0 to 28.7 months). The ORR per IRC was 49% (95% CI: 37.0, 61.6], with 16% achieving a complete response."

*[verbatim, FDA efficacy summary, FL]* — "The median follow-up time was 20.1 months (range: 13.5 to 29.6 months). The overall response rate per IRC was 42.7% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 33.6, 52.2), with 3.4% achieving a complete response. The median duration of response was 11.1 months (95% CI: 8.3, 16.4)."

*[verbatim, FDA Drug Safety Communication, February 3, 2022]* — "We conducted an initial review of data from UNITY, a phase 3, randomized, controlled clinical trial in patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL)... The results showed a possible increased risk of death in patients receiving the combination of Ukoniq and the monoclonal antibody compared to the control arm. Those receiving the combination... also experienced more serious adverse events than those in the control arm... clinical trials of other medicines in the same PI3 kinase inhibitor class as Ukoniq have shown similar safety concerns."

*[verbatim, TG Therapeutics press release, April 15, 2022]* — "The decision to withdraw was based on recently updated overall survival (OS) data from the UNITY-CLL Phase 3 trial that showed an increasing imbalance in OS... In a first analysis of OS using a cut-off date of September 2021, there was an imbalance in favor of the control arm (HR: 1.23). However, based on the ad hoc nature of the analysis, approximately 15% of patients had missing or outdated survival data. Further, when excluding deaths related to COVID-19, the two arms were approximately balanced (HR: 1.04)... Pursuant to a recent information request made by the FDA, updated OS data were collected that showed an increasing imbalance in favor of the control arm... OS was designated as a secondary efficacy endpoint in the UNITY-CLL protocol but was not part of the primary analysis in accordance with the study's statistical analysis plan agreed upon via a SPA [Special Protocol Assessment]... the study was not powered for overall survival. The trial met its primary endpoint, with U2 significantly prolonging independent review committee (IRC) assessed progression-free survival (PFS) vs. the control arm."

*[verbatim, Federal Register, 87 FR 32425]* — "TG Therapeutics, Inc. (TGT) has voluntarily requested that FDA withdraw approval of this application and has waived its opportunity for a hearing... approval of NDA 213176 for UKONIQ (umbralisib tosylate) Tablets, EQ 200 mg base, and all amendments and supplements thereto, is withdrawn under §314.150(d)."

*[verbatim, FDA Drug Safety Communication, June 1, 2022]* — "Due to safety concerns, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has withdrawn its approval for the cancer medicine Ukoniq (umbralisib)... Updated findings from the UNITY-CLL clinical trial continued to show a possible increased risk of death in patients receiving Ukoniq. As a result, we determined the risks of treatment with Ukoniq outweigh its benefits... In limited circumstances in which a patient may be receiving benefit from Ukoniq, TG Therapeutics plans to make it available under expanded access."

This is the most severe outcome documented anywhere in this census to date: unlike the standard accelerated-approval-withdrawal pattern (a required confirmatory trial in the *same* indication fails to show benefit), here the withdrawal was triggered by a safety signal from a confirmatory trial (UNITY-CLL) run in an entirely *different* indication and population (CLL, not MZL/FL) — the MZL/FL accelerated approvals themselves were never directly contradicted by a failed confirmatory trial in lymphoma; the entire US marketing authorization was pulled anyway, given the class-wide PI3K-inhibitor mortality-signal pattern FDA cited and the absence of any completed confirmatory efficacy data for the approved indications themselves.

### 127. trilaciclib (Cosela) — NDA 214200

**Sponsor:** G1 Therapeutics, Inc.

**Indication approved:** To decrease the incidence of chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression in adult patients when administered prior to a platinum/etoposide-containing regimen or topotecan-containing regimen for extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) — full/traditional approval, not accelerated approval

**Approval date:** February 12, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** G1T28-05, NCT03041311 (confirmatory/primary evidentiary trial), with two additional randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled supportive trials, G1T28-02 (NCT02499770) and G1T28-03 (NCT02514447)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials (three: G1T28-05 the pivotal trial, G1T28-02 and G1T28-03 explicitly supportive/exploratory only per FDA — "due to the limitations of the study design for Study G1T28-02-Part 2 and Study G1T28-03-Part 2, these 2 studies will be considered as supportive. No inference should be made by analysis results from these 2 studies"); mid-trial SAP amendment changing endpoint status — G1T28-05 was originally powered for overall survival, then amended prior to unblinding to two co-primary myelosuppression endpoints once early OS data from G1T28-02 showed no signal; co-primary endpoints (duration of severe Grade 4 neutropenia in Cycle 1, and occurrence of severe Grade 4 neutropenia)
- *Endpoints:* duration of severe (Grade 4) neutropenia (DSN) in Cycle 1 and occurrence of severe (Grade 4) neutropenia — co-primary; all-cause dose reductions, RBC transfusion ≥Week 5, G-CSF administration — key secondary; OS and PFS retained only as secondary/exploratory, explicitly flagged by FDA as statistically unreliable given small sample size
- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA for DSN (continuous), modified Poisson regression for occurrence of severe neutropenia (binary); Brookmeyer-Crowley-type censoring conventions were not needed since myelosuppression endpoints are within-cycle laboratory measures rather than time-to-event
- *Multiplicity:* Hochberg-based gatekeeping procedure controlling the familywise error rate across 5 hypotheses grouped into 3 families (F1 = DSN Cycle 1; F2 = occurrence of severe neutropenia; F3 = dose reductions, RBC transfusion, G-CSF administration) at a 1-sided α=0.025, "satisfies the positive dependence condition at the 1-sided setting"
- *Missing data/bias:* FDA's statistical reviewer explicitly flagged that "given the small sample size for the studies supporting the trilaciclib indication for SCLC, the 95% CI of hazard ratio for OS and PFS were wide and the estimates may be unreliable," and in the topotecan-regimen trial (G1T28-03) "an increased risk of death was observed... with a hazard ratio of 1.38 (95% CI: 0.78, 2.45) in favor of the placebo group" — a signal that directly motivated a postmarketing survival-monitoring requirement rather than a labeling claim
- *Regulatory:* full/traditional approval (not accelerated) on a surrogate/supportive-care endpoint (myelosuppression reduction) rather than a tumor-response or survival endpoint; no FDA advisory committee meeting held; postmarketing requirement imposed specifically to rule out a survival detriment given the wide, inconclusive OS confidence intervals and the numerically unfavorable topotecan-trial signal

**Trial design & endpoints**

- G1T28-05 (pivotal): randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter Phase 2 trial of trilaciclib vs. placebo administered prior to each cycle of etoposide/carboplatin plus atezolizumab (E/P/A) in patients with newly diagnosed ES-SCLC, n=107 treated, stratified by ECOG status and brain metastases; originally designed with OS as the primary endpoint (n=100, 80% power to detect HR 0.6 at 1-sided α=0.1), then amended before unblinding — after G1T28-02's early OS data showed no efficacy signal — to two co-primary myelosuppression endpoints (retaining OS as a secondary endpoint), with the type I error rebalanced via a Bonferroni-style split (1-sided α=0.0125 per co-primary endpoint) and the sample size recalculated to 106 patients for 90% power to detect a ≥2-day difference in DSN
- G1T28-02 and G1T28-03 (supportive only, per FDA's explicit instruction not to draw inference from either): G1T28-02 (n=75 treated, 1:1) tested trilaciclib with an E/P backbone at a looser 2-sided 20% significance threshold "determined by clinical rather than statistical considerations"; G1T28-03 (n=60 treated, 2:1) tested trilaciclib prior to topotecan
- Primary results (G1T28-05): mean DSN in Cycle 1 was 0 days (SD 1.0) with trilaciclib vs. 4 days (SD 4.7) with placebo, treatment effect −3.6 days (95% CI −4.9, −2.3), 1-sided adjusted p<0.0001 (Hochberg gatekeeping); severe neutropenia occurrence 1.9% vs. 49.1%, adjusted relative risk 0.038 (95% CI 0.008, 0.195), p<0.0001
- Supportive results: G1T28-02 DSN 0 days (SD 0.5) vs. 3 days (SD 3.9), severe-neutropenia occurrence 5.1% vs. 42.1%; G1T28-03 DSN 2 days (SD 3.9) vs. 7 days (SD 6.2), severe-neutropenia occurrence 40.6% vs. 75.9%
- Postmarketing requirement (PMR 4018-1): a dedicated survival-focused postmarketing study with ≥2 years of follow-up, because FDA stated "an analysis of spontaneous postmarketing adverse events... will not be sufficient to assess a signal of a serious risk of worse overall survival"

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2021/214200Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2021/214200s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/214200Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/214200Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (G1T28-05) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03041311 (Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan both posted in the Documents tab)
- Protocol / SAP (G1T28-05) — Protocol: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/11/NCT03041311/Prot_000.pdf; SAP: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/11/NCT03041311/SAP_001.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov records for supportive trials — G1T28-02: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02499770 (Protocol/SAP posted); G1T28-03: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02514447 (Protocol and two regional SAPs posted)
- Pivotal publication: Daniel D, Kuchava V, Bondarenko I, Ivashchuk O, Reddy S, Jaal J, et al. "Trilaciclib prior to chemotherapy and atezolizumab in patients with newly diagnosed extensive-stage small cell lung cancer: A multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase II trial." *Int J Cancer.* 2021;148(10):2557-2570. **Other resources**

- G1 Therapeutics' participation in Vivli, YODA, or Project Data Sphere was not confirmed with available access.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held; both the approval letter and Summary Review state the application "did not raise significant or controversial safety or efficacy issues that could benefit from a public discussion." No REMS was required.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 214200, trial-identification section]* — "Trilaciclib efficacy was investigated in Study G1T28-05, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, Phase 2 study of the efficacy and safety of trilaciclib versus placebo therapy for patients with newly diagnosed extensive-stage SCLC, and 2 additional randomized double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trials (Study G1T28-02 and Study G1T28-03), where the efficacy examination is not the primary objective but only exploratory... Due to the limitations of the study design for Study G1T28-02-Part 2 and Study G1T28-03-Part 2, these 2 studies will be considered as supportive. No inference should be made by analysis results from these 2 studies."

*[verbatim, same source, design-amendment history]* — "Study G1T28-05 was originally designed to evaluate Overall Survival (OS) as the primary efficacy endpoint... based on the myelopreservation efficacy insignificant results of OS from Study G1T28-02, the protocol for Study G1T28-05 was amended prior to unblinding to update 2 co-primary and key secondary endpoints... while retaining OS as a secondary endpoint. There were 2 co-primary myelosuppression efficacy endpoints: Duration of severe (Grade 4) neutropenia in Cycle 1 and occurrence of severe (Grade 4) neutropenia."

*[verbatim, same source, sample-size/multiplicity]* — "The initial sample size calculations were based on a primary endpoint of OS where a sample size of 100... provided 80% power to detect a hazard ratio of 0.6 using an overall type 1 error probability of 0.1 (1-sided). With the change in endpoints... the overall type I error rate was now 0.025 (1-sided)... To maintain the overall type I error rate, by using Bonferroni procedure for the 2 primary endpoints, a 1-sided individualized type I error rate 0.025/2 = 0.0125 is assigned... a true difference in the duration of severe (Grade 4) neutropenia in Cycle 1 of at least 2 days... requires 82 evaluable patients (41 per treatment arm)... the final adjusted sample size was 106." "A Hochberg-based gatekeeping procedure was utilized to control the global familywise error rate across the 5 null hypotheses at a 1-sided alpha=0.025 level, and it satisfies the positive dependence condition at the 1-sided setting."

*[verbatim, same source, safety caveat]* — "Given the small sample size for the studies supporting the trilaciclib indication for SCLC, the 95% CI of hazard ratio for OS and PFS were wide and the estimates may be unreliable." In Study 3 (G1T28-03/topotecan), "An increased risk of death was observed... with a hazard ratio of 1.38 (95% CI: 0.78, 2.45) in favor of the placebo group."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review]* — "The trilaciclib application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because evaluation of the data did not raise significant or controversial safety or efficacy issues that could benefit from a public discussion." "A Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) program is not necessary for this application."

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP, Study G1T28-05, primary-endpoint definitions]* — "5.1.1.1. Occurrence of Severe (Grade 4) Neutropenia — For the induction treatment period, the total number of SVN events is the number of induction cycles where at least one ANC value is < 0.5 x 10⁹/L..." "5.1.1.2. Duration of Severe (Grade 4) Neutropenia (DSN) — There will be three different strategies for assessing DSN in each cycle... strategy 1 considered as the primary, and strategy 2 and strategy 3 being supportive sensitivity analyses."

Unlike every other drug in this batch, trilaciclib is a genuine full (not accelerated) approval on a supportive-care surrogate endpoint (myelosuppression reduction) rather than a tumor-response or survival endpoint — and its SAP history illustrates a mid-trial primary-endpoint amendment driven by another trial's early null OS signal, executed *before* unblinding, followed by a formal Bonferroni-then-Hochberg multiplicity structure across the resulting co-primary/secondary family — while an inconclusive but unfavorable OS point estimate in one of the two purely supportive trials became the direct basis for a dedicated postmarketing survival-monitoring requirement.

### 128. melphalan flufenamide (Pepaxto) — NDA 214383

**Sponsor:** Oncopeptides AB

**Indication approved:** In combination with dexamethasone, for adult patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma who have received at least four prior lines of therapy and whose disease is refractory to at least one proteasome inhibitor, one immunomodulatory agent, and one CD38-directed monoclonal antibody — single-arm accelerated approval based on response rate

**Approval date:** February 26, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** HORIZON (Study OP-106), NCT02963493 (single-arm accelerated-approval basis); confirmatory trial OCEAN (Study OP-103), NCT03151811 (randomized, active-controlled vs. pomalidomide/dexamethasone)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial (HORIZON) supporting accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.500, with the accelerated-approval indication restricted to a triple-class-refractory subpopulation (97 of 157 enrolled patients) rather than the full enrolled cohort; randomized, open-label (assessor-blinded), active-controlled confirmatory trial (OCEAN) using a non-inferiority-margin framework repurposed as a superiority test (superiority declared only if the hazard ratio's 95% CI upper bound fell below 1.0)
- *Endpoints:* overall response rate (ORR, primary, investigator-assessed per IMWG criteria) in HORIZON; progression-free survival (PFS, primary, IRC-assessed) with overall response rate and overall survival as secondary endpoints in OCEAN
- *Primary analysis:* exact (Clopper-Pearson) binomial confidence interval for ORR (HORIZON); stratified log-rank test with Cox proportional-hazards model (Efron method for ties) for PFS, Kaplan-Meier estimation with Brookmeyer-Crowley-type CI for medians (OCEAN)
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing in OCEAN — PFS → ORR → OS, gated at 2-sided α=0.05, with any endpoint after a non-significant step reported as "nominal, descriptive and exploratory" only
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* OCEAN's SAP specified no interim analyses for the primary PFS analysis ("No interim analyses are planned")
- *Missing data/bias:* reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan — Oncopeptides' post hoc reanalysis of OCEAN reclassified 29 patients with unconfirmed progression in the control (pomalidomide/dexamethasone) arm as PFS events rather than censoring them, a change FDA stated was made "outside of the prespecified statistical analysis plan agreed upon with CDER," producing "the paradoxical finding of an improved PFS but inferior OS"
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval based on ORR from a single-arm trial, with the required randomized confirmatory trial (OCEAN) both failing to achieve statistical significance on its primary PFS analysis under FDA's own re-adjudication and additionally showing a directionally unfavorable overall-survival signal; FDA Advisory Committee (ODAC) voted 14-2 that the benefit-risk profile was not favorable (Sept 22, 2022); this is the first drug for which FDA used the amended accelerated-approval withdrawal procedures enacted by the 2022 Food and Drug Omnibus Report Act (FDORA), issuing a formal contested withdrawal decision (Feb 23, 2024) after Oncopeptides briefly rescinded an earlier voluntary-withdrawal request

**Trial design & endpoints**

- HORIZON (OP-106): single-arm, open-label, multicenter Phase 2 trial of melflufen 40 mg IV Day 1 plus dexamethasone in 157 patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (≥2 prior lines including an IMiD and a PI); the accelerated-approval indication was restricted to a 97-patient subgroup refractory to a PI, an IMiD, and a CD38-directed antibody, with ≥4 prior lines
- Primary endpoint (HORIZON): ORR per IMWG criteria (investigator-assessed); sample-size framework targeted an ORR lower confidence bound above 15% in the triple-class-refractory subgroup; result in the 97-patient approval population — ORR 23.7% (95% CI 15.7-33.4%), no complete or stringent complete responses, median duration of response 4.2 months (95% CI 3.2-7.6)
- OCEAN (OP-103): randomized (1:1), open-label, active-controlled Phase 3 trial, n=495 (246 melflufen+dexamethasone vs. 249 pomalidomide+dexamethasone), in patients refractory to lenalidomide within 18 months and with 2-4 prior lines including an IMiD and a PI; randomization not stratified reported here but primary analysis pre-specified as stratified; sample size targeted 339 PFS events for 90% power to detect HR=0.70 at 2-sided α=0.05, with a "non-inferiority margin of 1.2" reframed into a superiority decision rule (upper 95% CI bound of the HR <1.0)
- OCEAN's pre-specified (FDA-endorsed) primary PFS analysis: median PFS 6.9 months (95% CI 5.1-8.5) melflufen vs. 4.9 months (95% CI 4.2-5.9) pomalidomide; HR 0.817 (95% CI 0.659-1.012), p=0.0644 — not statistically significant; secondary OS analysis: median OS 19.7 months (95% CI 15.1-25.6) vs. 25.0 months (95% CI 18.1-31.9), HR 1.104 (95% CI 0.846-1.441); a later data cutoff (Feb 3, 2022) showed HR 1.14 (95% CI 0.91-1.42), "associated with a decrease in median OS of 3.8 months with MelDex"
- Grade 3-4 hematologic toxicity in OCEAN: neutropenia 56% vs. 41%, anemia 42% vs. 18%, thrombocytopenia 63% vs. 10% (melflufen vs. pomalidomide arms)
- FDA's own decisional analysis tabulated five different PFS analyses of the same OCEAN data (applicant's original ITT p=0.0644; FDA's original ITT p=0.1122; applicant's post hoc reassessment p=0.0322; FDA re-adjudicated post hoc under the applicant's censoring rules p=0.0359; FDA re-adjudicated post hoc under FDA's own censoring rules p=0.0837), illustrating how sensitive the nominally "positive" post hoc reanalysis was to censoring-rule choices that departed from the pre-specified SAP

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2021/214383Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (original, Feb 2021) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2021/214383s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/214383Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (HORIZON/OP-106) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02963493 (Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan posted in the Documents tab)
- Protocol / SAP (HORIZON) — Protocol: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/93/NCT02963493/Prot_000.pdf; SAP: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/93/NCT02963493/SAP_002.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (OCEAN/OP-103) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03151811 (status: terminated; Protocol and SAP posted, results posted)
- Protocol / SAP (OCEAN) — Protocol: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/11/NCT03151811/Prot_002.pdf; SAP: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/11/NCT03151811/SAP_003.pdf

"Melflufen and Dexamethasone in Heavily Pretreated Relapsed and Refractory Multiple Myeloma." *J Clin Oncol.* 2021;39(7):757-767. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S2352-3026(21)00381-1>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35032434/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Melflufen%20pomalidomide%20dexamethasone%20multiple%20myeloma%20refractory%20lenalidomide%20OCEAN)

**Other resources**

- No Vivli, YODA, or Project Data Sphere listing was found for Oncopeptides.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held at original approval (2021). An ODAC meeting was held September 22-23, 2022 specifically to review OCEAN's results; the committee voted 14-2 that "given the potential detriment in [OS], failure to demonstrate a [PFS] benefit, and lack of an appropriate dose, [the] benefit-risk profile of [Pepaxto was] favorable for the currently indicated patient population" — i.e., 14-2 against a favorable benefit-risk finding.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP, HORIZON/OP-106, sample-size section]* — "A total number of approximately 150 patients are planned to be enrolled in the study, to achieve 130 patients evaluable for efficacy... The protocol hypothesizes an observed ORR of 30%, and an exact 95% confidence interval from 22.3% to 38.7%, given a sample size of 130 patients... The primary endpoint will be considered met if the lower bound of the 95% confidence interval for actual ORR among triple-class refractory patients is higher than 15%."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, HORIZON efficacy summary]* — "Efficacy of melphalan flufenamide in combination with dexamethasone was evaluated in Trial OP-106 a single arm, open label, Phase 2 multicenter trial that enrolled 157 patients... The recommendation for approval is based on a subpopulation of 97 patients... treated with 4 or more lines of therapy... refractory to at least 1 proteasome inhibitor, 1 immunomodulatory drug and 1 CD38 directed monoclonal antibody... The overall response rate in the 97 patients was 23.7% (95% confidence interval: 15.7, 33.4)... median duration of response was 4.2 months (95% CI: 3.2, 7.6)... There were no complete or stringent complete responses."

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP, OCEAN/OP-103, primary analysis method]* — "The primary analysis of PFS will be performed using a log rank test stratified by the randomization stratification factors... K-M estimates... The 95% CI for median PFS will be constructed using the method of Brookmeyer [Brookmeyer and Crawley, 1982]... The hazard ratio and 95% CI will be determined based on a semi parametric Cox proportional hazards regression model stratified by randomization strata... Ties will be handled using the Efron methodology." Superiority criterion: "the superiority of Melflufen + Dexamethasone versus Pomalidomide + Dexamethasone will be demonstrated if the upper limit of the 95% confidence interval for the hazard ratio is < 1.0."

*[verbatim, same source, FDA-driven amendment]* — "Per FDA feedback received 27APR2021, the following updates were made: Primary endpoint analysis based on stratified log-rank test; DOR moved from key secondary objective/endpoint to other secondary objective/endpoint, removing it from multiplicity adjustment."

*[verbatim, same source, multiplicity]* — fixed-sequence gatekeeping across PFS → ORR → OS, each endpoint tested only if the prior step reached 2-sided significance of 0.05, otherwise treated as "nominal, descriptive and exploratory."

*[verbatim, same source, interim analysis]* — "No interim analyses are planned."

*[verbatim, FDA Final Decision memorandum, Feb 23, 2024]* — "The agency determined the following grounds for withdrawal were met: (1) the confirmatory study conducted as a condition of accelerated approval did not confirm Pepaxto's clinical benefit, and (2) the available evidence demonstrates that Pepaxto is not shown to be safe or effective under its conditions of use." The same memorandum documents that Oncopeptides' post hoc PFS reanalysis "included 29 individuals who had unconfirmed progression in the PomDex arm" reclassified as events rather than censored, "outside of the prespecified statistical analysis plan agreed upon with CDER," producing "the paradoxical finding of an improved PFS but inferior OS."

*[verbatim, FDA Drug Safety Communication, July 28, 2021]* — "FDA is alerting patients and health care professionals that a clinical trial (OCEAN, Study OP-103) evaluating Pepaxto (melphalan flufenamide) with dexamethasone to treat patients with multiple myeloma showed an increased risk of death."

This entry is one of two market-withdrawal stories in this batch, and the most procedurally elaborate: Oncopeptides first voluntarily withdrew (October 2021, after an ODAC meeting had already been scheduled and was cancelled), then rescinded that withdrawal request (January 2022) and continued (unsuccessfully, given the drug was not marketed in the interim) to contest the science, leading to a full ODAC re-review (Sept 2022, voting 14-2 against a favorable benefit-risk profile) and ultimately the first-ever contested withdrawal decision issued under FDORA's 2022 amended accelerated-approval-withdrawal authority (Feb 2024) — ~2 years after the confirmatory trial's initial safety signal was first disclosed.

### 129. tivozanib (Fotivda) — NDA 212904

**Sponsor:** Aveo Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with relapsed or refractory advanced renal cell carcinoma (RCC) following two or more prior systemic therapies — full/traditional approval, not accelerated approval

**Approval date:** March 10, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** TIVO-3, NCT02627963 (randomized, open-label, active-controlled vs. sorafenib)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial (comparator sorafenib, itself an approved active RCC therapy), stratified by IMDC risk category (favorable/intermediate/poor) and prior-therapy category (two prior VEGFR TKIs vs. checkpoint inhibitor+VEGFR TKI vs. VEGFR TKI+other systemic agent); non-proportional-hazards concern flagged by FDA on the primary PFS analysis (Schoenfeld residual test p=0.01)
- *Endpoints:* progression-free survival (PFS, primary, by blinded independent radiological review [BIRC] per RECIST 1.1); overall survival (OS), objective response rate (ORR), and duration of response (DOR) as secondary endpoints, all considered exploratory since no multiplicity adjustment was pre-specified for them
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test (one-sided) with hazard ratio and CI from a Cox proportional-hazards model stratified by the same randomization factors; supplemented, once FDA flagged a non-proportional-hazards signal, by 6- and 12-month landmark PFS-rate estimates
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function with an O'Brien-Fleming boundary for the OS interim/final analyses (two-sided 0.8% significance level via East software), plus a separate non-binding futility interim analysis for PFS after 128 events (Lan-DeMets spending-type function, O'Brien-Fleming stopping boundary, 1.2% two-sided beta spent)
- *Missing data/bias:* FDA conducted a post hoc restricted mean survival time (RMST) sensitivity analysis on OS after noting an early, non-statistically-significant numerical OS signal favoring sorafenib at the first interim look (HR 1.12); the RMST analysis found "a difference of RMST estimate between tivozanib and sorafenib is -0.4 months (95% CI: -3.7, 2.9)," leading FDA to conclude "tivozanib does not have an apparent detrimental effect on OS"
- *Regulatory:* full/traditional approval (not accelerated) based on a statistically significant PFS benefit in a randomized, active-controlled trial, despite a numerically unfavorable early OS signal that FDA ultimately concluded was not a true detriment; no FDA advisory committee meeting held for this (2021) approval — note this is tivozanib's *second* US regulatory cycle: an earlier NDA based on the first-line TIVO-1 trial was reviewed by ODAC in 2013, which voted against approval (13-1, per secondary reporting not independently re-verified against a primary FDA source in this research pass), followed by a Complete Response Letter, before Aveo returned with the TIVO-3-based application in the third-line-plus refractory setting

**Trial design & endpoints**

- TIVO-3: randomized (1:1), open-label, active-controlled, multicenter Phase 3 trial of tivozanib vs. sorafenib in 350 patients (175/arm) with metastatic clear-cell RCC who had received 2-3 prior systemic regimens, at least one a VEGFR TKI other than sorafenib/tivozanib; randomization stratified by IMDC risk category and prior-therapy category
- Primary endpoint: PFS by BIRC per RECIST 1.1; sample size targeted 322 patients (161/arm) and 255 events for 90% power to detect a difference between an assumed 4-month (sorafenib) and 6-month (tivozanib) median PFS at one-sided α=0.025; SAP specified no multiplicity adjustment across secondary endpoints, stating "PFS with one treatment contrast (tivozanib vs. sorafenib) is the only primary analysis defined for this study"
- Primary result (data cutoff Oct 4, 2018, 246 PFS events): median PFS 5.59 months (95% CI 4.83-7.33) tivozanib vs. 3.88 months (95% CI 3.71-5.55) sorafenib; HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.56-0.95), p=0.016 (stratified log-rank); 6-/12-month PFS rates 45%/28% vs. 37%/11%
- Secondary/supportive results: final OS analysis (data cutoff May 1, 2020, 251 deaths) — median OS 16.39 months (95% CI 13.44-21.95) vs. 19.15 months (95% CI 14.92-24.21), HR 0.97 (95% CI 0.75-1.24); ORR 31/175 (17.7%) vs. 14/175 (8.0%); DOR not reached (lower 95% CI bound 12.91 months) vs. 5.65 months, with too few events in either arm to calculate an upper bound
- FDA's reviewer flagged a Schoenfeld-residual departure from the proportional-hazards assumption (p=0.01) on the primary PFS Cox model and supplemented the hazard-ratio-based analysis with landmark PFS-rate comparisons as a robustness check; an early OS interim analysis had shown a point estimate numerically favoring sorafenib (HR 1.12, 95% CI 0.40-1.51 per one cutoff cited in the review), which FDA's RMST sensitivity analysis and the subsequent final OS analysis (HR 0.97) resolved as not indicating a true survival detriment

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2021/212904Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2021/212904s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/212904Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (TIVO-3) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02627963 (Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan both posted in the Documents tab; results posted)
- Protocol / SAP (TIVO-3) — Protocol: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/63/NCT02627963/Prot_000.pdf; SAP: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/63/NCT02627963/SAP_001.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Rini BI, Pal SK, Escudier BJ, Atkins MB, Hutson TE, Porta C, et al. "Tivozanib versus sorafenib in patients with advanced renal cell carcinoma (TIVO-3): a phase 3, multicentre, randomised, controlled, open-label study." *Lancet Oncol.* 2020;21(1):95-104. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(19)30735-1>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31810797/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Tivozanib%20versus%20sorafenib%20advanced%20renal%20cell%20carcinoma%20TIVO-3%20phase%203)

**Other resources**

- No Vivli, YODA, or Project Data Sphere listing was found for Aveo Pharmaceuticals or its ex-US commercialization partner EUSA Pharma; the EUSA partnership itself does not appear in any FDA document reviewed (approval letter, label, or Multi-Discipline Review all reference only Aveo Pharmaceuticals, Boston, MA) and should be treated as background commercial context rather than an FDA-record fact.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for the 2021, TIVO-3-based approval, per both the approval letter and the Multi-Discipline Review. A wholly separate, earlier NDA cycle for tivozanib (based on the first-line TIVO-1 trial) went to ODAC in May 2013 and was not recommended for approval, followed by a Complete Response Letter — a different regulatory action from the one documented in this entry.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP, TIVO-3, sample-size section]* — "A sample size of 322 subjects (161 subjects per treatment arm) with a total number of 255 events will provide 90% power to detect a statistically significant difference between treatment arms with respect to PFS as assessed by the IRR... a log-rank test with one-sided 2.5% significance level... median PFS for subjects receiving sorafenib and tivozanib is 4 months and 6 months, respectively... The estimate was obtained by using East® statistical package Version 6.3 by Cytel Inc."

*[verbatim, same source, primary hypothesis]* — "H0: mPFStivozanib ≤ mPFSsorafenib; Ha: mPFStivozanib > mPFSsorafenib. A one-sided, log-rank test stratified for IMDC risk category (favorable vs. intermediate vs. poor) and prior therapy... at a significance level of α = 0.025 will be used."

*[verbatim, same source, multiplicity]* — "There will be no adjustment for multiplicity. PFS with one treatment contrast (tivozanib vs. sorafenib) is the only primary analysis defined for this study."

*[verbatim, same source, interim/alpha-spending]* — "An interim analysis will be performed after 128 PFS events have been observed. The interim analysis will look into the study's futility... utilizes a Lan-DeMets spending-type function with an O'Brian-Fleming stopping boundary and estimated two-sided beta (Type II error) of 1.2% spent during this interim look. A planned futility analysis will also be performed." For the OS secondary endpoint: "two-sided 0.8% significance level (utilizing a Lan-DeMets alpha spending function with an O'Brien Fleming boundary)... 245 OS events at the time of final OS analysis and 149 OS events at the time of final PFS analysis will yield approximately 61% power... given 2.5% type I error (one-sided)."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, primary PFS result]* — "HR was from a Cox proportional hazards model stratified by IMDC risk categories and prior therapy collected from IWRS." "A Schoenfeld residual test for non-proportional hazards had a p-value of 0.01 which suggested a departure from the proportional hazards assumption."

*[verbatim, same source, OS sensitivity analysis]* — "difference of RMST estimate between tivozanib and sorafenib is -0.4 months (95% CI: -3.7, 2.9)... it appears that tivozanib does not have an apparent detrimental effect on OS."

*[verbatim, same source, multiplicity note]* — "The study statistical analysis plan did not pre-specify any multiplicity adjustment method for analyses of secondary endpoints... Therefore, analyses of all secondary endpoints are considered exploratory."

*[verbatim, FDA Approval Letter]* — "Your application for Fotivda was not referred to a FDA advisory committee because (1) this drug is not the first in its class (2) the safety profile is acceptable for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory advanced renal cell carcinoma (RCC) following two or more prior systemic therapies (3) the clinical trial design is acceptable."

Tivozanib is the one entry in this batch approved on a full (not accelerated) basis from a randomized, active-controlled trial with a clean, statistically significant primary PFS result — its most notable statistical feature is the early, transient OS signal favoring the control arm that FDA resolved via a restricted-mean-survival-time sensitivity analysis rather than treating it as a genuine detriment, alongside an explicit non-proportional-hazards flag on the primary Cox model that the review addressed with supplementary landmark PFS-rate comparisons.

### 130. dostarlimab-gxly (Jemperli) — BLA 761174

**Sponsor:** GlaxoSmithKline (originally developed by Tesaro, Inc., acquired by GSK)

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) recurrent or advanced endometrial cancer, as determined by an FDA-approved test, that has progressed on or following prior treatment with a platinum-containing regimen — single-arm accelerated approval based on ORR/DOR

**Approval date:** April 22, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** GARNET, NCT02715284 (dMMR endometrial cancer Cohort A1, within a larger multicohort Phase 1 trial)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label, multicohort, non-randomized, sequential dose-escalation/cohort-expansion Phase 1 trial, with the dMMR endometrial cancer cohort (A1) serving as the accelerated-approval evidentiary basis and other cohorts (A2/MMR-proficient EC, E/NSCLC, F/other dMMR tumors) run in parallel; biomarker-selected population (dMMR/MSI-H status by central IHC, VENTANA MMR RxDx Panel)
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DOR), both primary and assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR) per RECIST 1.1
- *Primary analysis:* two-sided 95% exact binomial confidence interval for ORR; Kaplan-Meier estimation for DOR
- *Multiplicity:* not applicable — no formal multi-endpoint hypothesis test; "no adjustments for multiplicity were made. Separate inferences were drawn for each tumor cohort"; sample size (H0 ORR≤20% vs. Ha ORR≥40%, one-sided α=2.5%) was a design-stage power calculation, not treated by FDA as an inferential hypothesis test of the single-arm result
- *Missing data/bias:* reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan — FDA overrode the Applicant's proposed primary efficacy analysis set (n=70, which excluded one responder-eligible patient via a 24-week-minimum-follow-up gating rule) because "the Agency did not agree with the Applicant's use of the condition that a minimum of 24 weeks of tumor assessment prior to the data cutoff date was required, as this could introduce a selection bias," instead defining its own n=71 population used in the approved label
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval (21 CFR 601 Subpart E) based on ORR/DOR as a surrogate reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit; no FDA advisory committee meeting held; this indication was subsequently converted to full/regular approval in February 2023 (~22 months post-approval), among the faster accelerated-to-full conversions documented in this census, while GSK's GARNET trial continued enrolling and a newer, separate tumor-agnostic dMMR solid-tumor indication was later added under its own, still-active accelerated-approval status

**Trial design & endpoints**

- GARNET: Phase 1, multicenter, multicohort, open-label, non-randomized, sequential trial of dostarlimab (TSR-042) across several tumor cohorts; Cohort A1 (dMMR/MSI-H recurrent or advanced endometrial cancer, progressed on/after a platinum doublet, ≤2 prior lines) is the approval-relevant cohort
- Primary endpoint: ORR and DOR by BICR per RECIST 1.1; design-stage sample-size justification (per Protocol Section 8.9) assumed H0: ORR≤20% vs. Ha: ORR≥40%, yielding 92% power with 65 treated subjects at a one-sided 2.5% type I error rate
- FDA's revised primary efficacy analysis set (n=71, data cutoff July 8, 2019): confirmed ORR 42.3% (95% CI 30.6-54.6%), CR 12.7%, PR 29.6%, disease control rate 57.7% (95% CI 45.4-69.4%); of 30 responders, median DOR not reached, with Kaplan-Meier probability of maintained response 96.4% (95% CI 77.2-99.5) at 6 months, 76.8% (95% CI 48.0-90.9) at 12 months, and 61.4% (95% CI 24.6-84.4) at 18 months
- FDA's conclusion: "an ORR of 42.3% with a median DoR not reached at the time of data cutoff and the majority of responses durable for at least six months, is of sufficient magnitude to serve as evidence that is reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit over available therapies in support of accelerated approval"
- Postmarketing requirement (PMR 3909-1): a randomized Phase 3 trial (chemotherapy ± dostarlimab, PFS primary) or, alternatively, a final GARNET report with updated ORR/DOR data, to verify clinical benefit — ultimately fulfilled via the GARNET final CSR (submitted May 2022), leading to conversion to regular approval for this indication in February 2023

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2021/761174Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (original) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2021/761174s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/761174Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- FDA Approval Letter, full-approval conversion (S-003/S-004, Feb 9, 2023) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2023/761174Orig1s003,s004ltr.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (GARNET) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02715284 (no Protocol/SAP PDF posted in the Documents tab; IPD sharing statement present, see below)
- Pivotal publication: Oaknin A, Tinker AV, Gilbert L, et al. "Clinical Activity and Safety of the Anti-Programmed Death 1 Monoclonal Antibody Dostarlimab for Patients With Recurrent or Advanced Mismatch Repair-Deficient Endometrial Cancer: A Nonrandomized Phase 1 Clinical Trial." *JAMA Oncol.* 2020;6(11):1766-1772. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1001/jamaoncol.2020.4515), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33001143/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Clinical%20Activity%20Safety%20Anti-Programmed%20Death%201%20Monoclonal%20Antibody%20Dostarlimab%20Endometrial%20Cancer)

**Other resources**

- ClinicalTrials.gov's IPD sharing statement for GARNET confirms `ipdSharing: YES`, description "IPD for this study will be made available via the Clinical Study Data Request site," info types Study Protocol/SAP/ICF/CSR, timeframe "within 6 months of publishing the results of the primary endpoints, key secondary endpoints and safety data," accessed via GSK's legacy Clinical Study Data Request (CSDR) portal at clinicalstudydatarequest.com, subject to independent review panel approval and a data sharing agreement.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held; GARNET itself remains an active, ongoing trial per ClinicalTrials.gov (still enrolling additional cohorts as of the most recent status check).
- Regulatory-status note: this original endometrial-cancer monotherapy indication converted to full/regular approval in February 2023; the drug's *current* label separately carries an accelerated-approval footnote only for a newer, distinct tumor-agnostic "dMMR recurrent or advanced solid tumors" indication added later — the two indications should not be conflated.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761174, sample-size/hypothesis section]* — "The determination of the sample size is described in Protocol 4010-01-001, Section 8.9. For Cohort A1 in Part 2B, the null hypothesis that the true response rate was ≤20% (H0: p≤0.2) had been planned to be tested against a one-sided alternative of ≥40% (Ha: p≥0.4). With 65 subjects treated, there was 92% power to rule out a ≤20% ORR (null hypothesis) when the true ORR was 40% at the 2.5% type I error rate (one-sided)."

*[verbatim, same source, analysis-set definition]* — "Primary efficacy analysis set (RECIST v1.1 per BICR): All subjects in the safety analysis set with measurable disease at baseline (defined as the existence of at least 1 target lesion at baseline tumor assessment by BICR) who had the opportunity for at least 24 weeks of tumor assessment at the time of data cutoff (July 8, 2019)."

*[verbatim, same source, FDA's population override]* — "the Agency did not agree with the Applicant's use of the condition that a minimum of 24 weeks of tumor assessment prior to the data cutoff date was required, as this could introduce a selection bias."

*[verbatim, same source, multiplicity]* — "No adjustments for multiplicity were made. Separate inferences were drawn for each tumor cohort." "The FDA does not use inferential procedures (testing procedures, performance goals, type I error control, etc.) to evaluate single-arm trial results. Therefore, FDA efficacy evaluation is based on the estimated magnitude of ORR and adequate duration of response."

*[verbatim, same source, efficacy conclusion]* — "an ORR of 42.3% with a median DoR not reached at the time of data cutoff and the majority of responses durable for at least six months, is of sufficient magnitude to serve as evidence that is reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit over available therapies in support of accelerated approval... The clinical and statistical reviewers agree that dostarlimab-gxly has a favorable risk-benefit profile in the indicated population and agree with accelerated approval."

*[verbatim, FDA Approval Letter, postmarketing requirement 3909-1]* — "Submit the final report and datasets from a clinical trial evaluating overall response rate, and duration of response, to verify and describe the clinical benefit of dostarlimab in patients with mismatch repair deficient (dMMR), recurrent or advanced endometrial cancer (EC)... Alternatively, submit the final report and datasets from a randomized, phase 3 clinical trial that verifies and describes the clinical benefit of dostarlimab."

*[verbatim, FDA Approval Letter, S-003/S-004, Feb 9, 2023]* — "Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application S-003 provides for regular approval of Jemperli as monotherapy for the treatment of adult patients with recurrent or advanced mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) endometrial cancer... SUBPART E FULFILLED: We approved this BLA under the regulations at 21 CFR 601 Subpart E for Accelerated Approval of Biological Products for Serious or Life-Threatening Illnesses. Approval of this supplement fulfills your commitments made under 21 CFR 601.41."

Dostarlimab's endometrial-cancer indication is a clean, comparatively fast-converting accelerated approval, notable statistically for FDA's explicit rejection of the sponsor's proposed primary-analysis-set gating rule (a 24-week minimum follow-up requirement FDA judged could introduce selection bias) in favor of its own broader, one-patient-larger population — the population and ORR figure that ultimately appear in the approved label.

### 131. loncastuximab tesirine-lpyl (Zynlonta) — BLA 761196

**Sponsor:** ADC Therapeutics SA

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma after two or more lines of systemic therapy, including diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) not otherwise specified, DLBCL arising from low-grade lymphoma, and high-grade B-cell lymphoma — single-arm accelerated approval based on ORR

**Approval date:** April 23, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** LOTIS-2 (Study ADCT-402-201), NCT03589469

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label, single-group Phase 2 trial supporting accelerated approval under 21 CFR 601 Subpart E; Simon's two-stage design (futility interim analysis on the first 52 patients, requiring ≥10 responders to continue to full enrollment)
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR, primary — CR+PR as best overall response, by independent central review per Lugano 2014 criteria); duration of response (DOR, secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* one-sided exact binomial test of a single proportion against a pre-specified null (H0: ORR≤20% vs. Ha: ORR>20%, using 40% for sample-size calculation), tested at a 2-sided significance level of 0.05 (>99% power with the planned 140-patient enrollment)
- *Missing data/bias:* reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan — FDA's review states "the FDA does not agree with the Applicant's statement that 'the final analysis was based on 145 patients using a single stage approach.' According to the SAP, Simon's 2-stage design was employed"; separately, FDA flagged that DOR interpretation was limited by "a large number of censored events (28 censored events, 40%)... The most common reason for censoring is the new anticancer treatment started, excluding SCT (17 patients, 24%)"
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval based on ORR from a single-arm trial; postmarketing requirement for a randomized Phase 3 confirmatory trial (loncastuximab tesirine + immunotherapy/immunochemotherapy vs. immunochemotherapy alone, PFS primary) — the confirmatory trial (LOTIS-5) has materially missed its original target completion timeline, and as of the most recent label reviewed the indication remains under accelerated approval more than five years post-approval, without conversion to full approval

**Trial design & endpoints**

- LOTIS-2 (ADCT-402-201): Phase 2, multicenter, open-label, single-arm, non-randomized trial of loncastuximab tesirine monotherapy in 145 adult patients with relapsed/refractory DLBCL (including transformed low-grade and high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC/BCL2/BCL6 rearrangements) after ≥2 multi-agent systemic regimens, excluding bulky disease and active CNS lymphoma
- Primary endpoint: ORR (CR+PR best overall response) by independent central review per Lugano 2014 criteria; a Simon's two-stage design targeted ~140 patients, with a futility interim analysis at 52 patients requiring ≥10 responders (CR+PR) to proceed to full enrollment; sample size gave >99% power to reject H0: ORR≤20% at a 2-sided α=0.05 given an assumed true ORR of 40%
- Efficacy result (All-Treated population, N=145): ORR by IRC 48.3% (95% CI 39.9-56.7%), with 24.1% CR and 24.1% PR; per-protocol population (n=121) ORR 53.7% (95% CI 44.4-62.8%); FDA independently reproduced the primary result and confirmed "the study met its primary objective" since the ORR's lower 95% CI bound (39.9%) exceeded the pre-specified 20% null
- DOR: median 10.25 months (FDA MDR)/10.3 months (label) (95% CI ~6.9-not estimable); FDA flagged that 40% of responses were censored, primarily due to initiation of new anticancer therapy, limiting confidence in the durability estimate; probability of maintained response 68.1% at 6 months, 63.8% at 9 months, 38.3% at 12 months per the Applicant's analysis
- FDA also flagged that subgroup analyses on ORR were "considered exploratory" given small subgroup sizes, explicitly disagreeing with any subgroup-level inferential claim by the Applicant

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2021/761196Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (original) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2021/761196s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/761196Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (LOTIS-2) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03589469 (Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan both posted in the Documents tab)
- Protocol / SAP (LOTIS-2) — Protocol: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/69/NCT03589469/Prot_000.pdf; SAP (v2.0): https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/69/NCT03589469/SAP_002.pdf
- Confirmatory trial LOTIS-5, NCT04384484 (randomized Phase 3, loncastuximab tesirine + rituximab vs. immunochemotherapy) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04384484
- Pivotal publication: Caimi PF, Ai W, Alderuccio JP, et al. "Loncastuximab tesirine in relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (LOTIS-2): a multicentre, open-label, single-arm, phase 2 trial." *Lancet Oncol.* 2021;22(6):790-800. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(21)00139-X>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33989558/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Loncastuximab%20tesirine%20relapsed%20refractory%20diffuse%20large%20B-cell%20lymphoma%20LOTIS-2)

**Other resources**

- ClinicalTrials.gov's IPD sharing statement for LOTIS-2 records `ipdSharing: NO` — ADC Therapeutics does not commit to individual patient data sharing for this trial; no Vivli, YODA, or Project Data Sphere listing was found.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held; the approval letter states the application "did not raise significant public health questions on the role of the biologic in the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment, or prevention of a disease."
- Confirmatory trial LOTIS-5 (NCT04384484) is active but not yet complete; its enrollment/completion timeline has materially lagged the original postmarketing-requirement schedule (originally targeting trial completion mid-2025), and as of the most recent label reviewed the accelerated-approval status for this indication has not been converted to full approval.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP, LOTIS-2 (ADCT-402-201), design/sample-size section]* — "This is a Phase 2, multi-center, open-label, single-arm study. The study will enroll approximately 140 patients. A 2-stage design will be used, with an interim analysis for futility on the first 52 patients. If ≥10 patients respond (complete response [CR]+partial response [PR]), the study will proceed to complete full enrollment... The primary hypothesis is that the overall response rate (ORR) based on central review for patients treated with loncastuximab tesirine is significantly greater than 20% (i.e., H0: p ≤0.2 vs. Ha: p >0.2). This hypothesis will be tested at type I error of 0.05 (2-sided). Using nQuery exact test for single proportion, a sample size of 140 patients has >99% power to achieve a 1-sided significance level of 0.025 (2-sided significance level of 0.05)."

*[verbatim, same source, primary-endpoint definition]* — "Overall response rate is defined as the proportion of patients who achieve either CR or PR as best overall response (BOR) as determined by central review according to the 2014 Lugano Classification criteria before the start of subsequent anticancer therapy or procedure. For the primary ORR analysis in the all-treated population, patients with a CR or PR will be counted as successes and all other patients (including those with missing response information) will be counted as failures."

*[verbatim, same source, DOR definition/censoring]* — "Duration of response will be defined for patients with CR or PR only as the interval between the date of initial documentation of a response and the date of the first documented evidence of progressive disease based on independent radiographic assessment or death, whichever occurs first... Patients who have the event after the start of subsequent anticancer therapy/procedure, or are progression-free and alive at the time of clinical cut-off, or have unknown status, will be censored at the last valid tumor assessment."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, deviation-from-plan note]* — "The FDA does not agree with the Applicant's statement that 'The final analysis was based on 145 patients using a single stage approach.' According to the SAP, Simon's 2-stage design was employed with a futility interim analysis on the first 52 patients enrolled."

*[verbatim, same source, efficacy result]* — "the ORR was 48.3% (70/145 patients; 95% CI: 39.9% to 56.7%). BORs included 35 patients (24.1%) with CR and 35 patients (24.1%) with PR." "The ORR by IRC estimate is 48.3% with the lower bound of its 95% confidence interval of 39.9% which is greater than the pre-specified null hypothesis rate of 20%. Therefore, the study met its primary objective."

*[verbatim, same source, DOR concern]* — "The FDA has concerns with the Applicant's statement about the duration of response (DOR)... the FDA identified a large number of censored events (28 censored events, 40%) reported during the study which may substantially affect the interpretation of durability of response... The most common reason for censoring is the new anticancer treatment started, excluding SCT (17 patients, 24%)."

*[verbatim, same source, subgroup caveat]* — "The FDA does not agree with the Applicant's statement about the subgroup analyses on ORR. Since the number of patients in subgroups are relatively small, all subgroup analysis results on ORR are considered exploratory."

Loncastuximab tesirine's SAP history illustrates a reviewer-documented factual dispute over trial design characterization itself — FDA's review directly contradicts the Applicant's own description of a "single stage" analysis, pointing to the SAP's actual Simon's two-stage futility structure — layered on top of a genuine durability-of-response concern (40% censoring) that the review flagged without disqualifying the ORR-based accelerated approval; more than five years on, this remains one of the longer-unconverted accelerated approvals documented in this census, its confirmatory trial (LOTIS-5) still active and behind its original schedule.
