### 132. amivantamab-vmjw (Rybrevant) — BLA 761210

**Sponsor:** Janssen Biotech, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations, as detected by an FDA-approved test, whose disease has progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy — single-arm accelerated approval based on ORR

**Approval date:** May 21, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** CHRYSALIS, NCT02609776 (Cohort D of a Phase 1 dose-escalation/expansion trial)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label, multi-part Phase 1 trial (dose escalation plus multiple dose-expansion cohorts) supporting accelerated approval under 21 CFR 601 Subpart E; biomarker-selected population (EGFR exon 20 insertion mutation, post-platinum); non-binding futility interim analysis built into the cohort-expansion design
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR, primary, by blinded independent central review [BICR] per RECIST 1.1, using a 2-reader-plus-adjudication paradigm with a third radiologist for discordant cases, followed by an independent oncologist's overall clinical assessment); duration of response (DOR, key secondary); clinical benefit rate (exploratory, not verified by FDA)
- *Primary analysis:* two-sided 95% exact confidence interval for ORR; Kaplan-Meier estimation for DOR/PFS/OS
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* non-binding futility interim analysis planned at ~30 response-evaluable patients in Cohort D, with a futility criterion of 5 or fewer responses among those 30
- *Missing data/bias:* reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan — FDA's review states "although not mentioned in the Applicant's description above, the SAP for Study EDI1001 describes formal hypothesis tests for each cohort. FDA does not consider inferential procedures in the evaluation of single arm study results"; FDA also independently defined the BLA-specific primary efficacy population following a July 2020 Format & Content meeting, distinct from the original Phase 1 protocol's SAP
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval based on ORR/DOR as a surrogate reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit; postmarketing requirement for a randomized confirmatory trial (PAPILLON, amivantamab+carboplatin/pemetrexed vs. carboplatin/pemetrexed) plus companion-diagnostic validation requirements; this single-agent, post-platinum indication was converted to full/traditional approval in March 2024 concurrently with a new first-line combination indication supported by PAPILLON — one of the faster accelerated-to-full conversions in this census (~34 months)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- CHRYSALIS: Phase 1, first-in-human, open-label, multicenter, dose-escalation and multi-cohort dose-expansion trial of amivantamab (a bispecific EGFR/cMet antibody) in advanced NSCLC; Cohort D enrolled patients with EGFR exon 20 insertion-mutated NSCLC not previously treated with an exon-20ins-active TKI, who had progressed after, been ineligible for, or refused platinum-based chemotherapy, at the recommended Phase 2 dose (1050 mg <80 kg / 1400 mg ≥80 kg, weekly ×4 then every 2 weeks)
- Primary endpoint: confirmed ORR by BICR (RECIST 1.1), agreed with FDA at a May 2020 Type B meeting; a non-binding futility interim analysis was planned after ~30 response-evaluable patients (futility if ≤5 responses); the primary ORR analysis was planned at 12 weeks after the start of treatment for the last enrolled patient or study end, whichever occurred first
- Primary efficacy result (N=81, data cutoff Oct 8, 2020): BICR-confirmed ORR 39.5% (95% CI 28.8-51.0%) — rounded to 40% (95% CI 29-51%) in the approved label — with 3.7% CR and 35.8% PR; clinical benefit rate 74.1% (95% CI 63.1-83.2%); investigator-assessed ORR 35.8% (95% CI 25.4-47.2%)
- DOR (BICR): median 11.14 months (95% CI 6.90-not estimable; rounded to 11.1 months in the label), with 62.5% (20/32) of responders maintaining response ≥6 months; median PFS (BICR) 8.28 months (95% CI 6.51-10.87); median OS 22.77 months (95% CI 14.59-not estimable), 71.6% censored
- Postmarketing requirements: PMR 4070-1 required final PFS/ORR/DOR/OS data from a randomized confirmatory trial (satisfied by PAPILLON, NCT04538664, amivantamab+carboplatin/pemetrexed vs. carboplatin/pemetrexed alone in the first-line setting); PMR 4070-2 required a final CHRYSALIS ORR/DOR update after ~128 responders had ≥6 months follow-up; PMC 4070-4 required analytical/clinical validation of a tissue-based companion diagnostic for EGFR exon20ins

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2021/761210Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (original) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2021/761210s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/761210Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- FDA Approval Letter, full-approval conversion + new first-line indication (S-003, March 1, 2024) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2024/761210Orig1s003ltr.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (CHRYSALIS) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02609776 (no Protocol/SAP PDF posted in the Documents tab)
- Confirmatory trial PAPILLON, NCT04538664 (randomized Phase 3, first-line combination) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04538664
- Pivotal publication: Park K, Haura EB, Leighl NB, Mitchell P, Shu CA, et al. "Amivantamab in EGFR Exon 20 Insertion-Mutated Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer Progressing on Platinum Chemotherapy: Initial Results From the CHRYSALIS Phase I Study." *J Clin Oncol.* 2021;39(30):3391-3402. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.21.00662), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34339292/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Amivantamab%20EGFR%20Exon%2020%20Insertion-Mutated%20Non-Small-Cell%20Lung%20Cancer%20CHRYSALIS)

**Other resources**

- Janssen/Johnson & Johnson participates in both the YODA Project (Yale) and Vivli as a general data-sharing partner; trial-specific IPD availability for CHRYSALIS was not individually confirmed.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held; the approval letter states the application "did not raise significant public health questions on the role of amivantamab-vmjw in the proposed indication. The application also did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues."
- The March 2024 supplement converted the original single-agent, post-platinum accelerated approval to full/traditional approval while simultaneously adding a new first-line combination indication based on PAPILLON — a notable case of a single label revision resolving both the accelerated-approval verification requirement and expanding the indication.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761210, population/design section]* — "Key inclusion criteria: Subjects 18 years of age or older with histologically or cytogically confirmed diagnosis of advanced NSCLC, with evaluable disease (Part 1) or measurable disease according to RECIST v1.1 (Part 2)... Specifically for Cohort D of Part 2, inclusion criteria required the presence of previously-diagnosed activating EGFR Exon 20ins not previously treated with a TKI having known activity in Exon 20ins disease... Subjects in this cohort must have progressed after, been ineligible for, or have refused standard-of-care platinum-based chemotherapy."

*[verbatim, same source, reader methodology]* — "a 2-reader with adjudication paradigm... Cases for which the best response (adjudication variable #1) or date for first response (adjudication variable #2) were discordant between the 2 independent readers were adjudicated to a third independent radiologist. Following the radiographic review (and adjudication, if necessary), an independent oncologist incorporated applicable clinical data to determine an overall response assessment."

*[verbatim, same source, sample-size/futility]* — "The study design assumed an ORR in Cohort D greater than 25%. A non-binding interim futility analysis was planned based on approximately 30 response evaluable patients, with a futility criterion of observing 5 or less responses among those 30 patients. The primary analysis of ORR was planned at 12 weeks after the start of treatment for the last enrolled patient or at end of the study, whichever occurred first."

*[verbatim, same source, deviation-from-plan note]* — "Although not mentioned in the Applicant's description above, the SAP for Study EDI1001 describes formal hypothesis tests for each cohort. FDA does not consider inferential procedures in the evaluation of single arm study results."

*[verbatim, same source, efficacy result, Table 15]* — BICR: ORR 32/81 = 39.5% (95% CI 28.8%, 51.0%); CR 3.7% (n=3), PR 35.8% (n=29); CBR 74.1% (95% CI 63.1%, 83.2%). DOR (Table 17): median 11.14 months (95% CI 6.90, NE); ≥6 months in 62.5% (20/32) of responders.

*[verbatim, FDA Approval Letter, PMR 4070-1]* — "Submit the final report, including datasets for progression free survival, overall response rate, duration of response, and overall survival from a randomized clinical trial to verify and confirm the clinical benefit... This could be from the ongoing clinical trial entitled, 'A Randomized, Open-label Phase 3 Study of Combination Amivantamab and Carboplatin-Pemetrexed Therapy, Compared With Carboplatin-Pemetrexed, in Patients With EGFR Exon 20ins Mutated Locally Advanced or Metastatic Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.'"

*[verbatim, FDA Approval Letter, S-003, March 2024]* — "This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application provides for: A new indication of amivantamab in combination with carboplatin and pemetrexed for the first-line treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations... Revisions to US Prescribing Information (USPI) to support the fulfillment of the subpart E postmarketing requirement and traditional approval of amivantamab as a single agent."

Note on rounding: the FDA Multi-Discipline Review's precise ORR figure (39.5%, 95% CI 28.8-51.0%) and the approved label's rounded figure (40%, 95% CI 29-51%) both derive from the identical N=81, October 2020-cutoff dataset — a benign rounding-convention difference between the underlying review and the label, not a discrepant analysis, worth noting for anyone cross-referencing the two source documents.

### 133. piflufolastat F 18 (Pylarify) — NDA 214793

**Sponsor:** Progenics Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (a Lantheus company)

**Indication approved:** Positron emission tomography (PET) imaging agent for prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-positive lesions in men with prostate cancer, with suspected metastasis who are candidates for initial definitive therapy, or with suspected recurrence based on elevated serum PSA — a diagnostic imaging agent, not a therapeutic; standard (not accelerated) approval

**Approval date:** May 26, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** OSPREY, NCT02981368 (Cohort A, pre-prostatectomy/pelvic-nodal-staging setting) and CONDOR, NCT03739684 (biochemical-recurrence setting) — two independent diagnostic-accuracy trials

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison) — OSPREY Cohort A compared PET findings against surgical histopathology in the same patients undergoing planned radical prostatectomy with pelvic lymph node dissection; CONDOR compared PET localization findings against a composite reference/truth standard (histopathology, or informative conventional imaging, or confirmed PSA response) in patients with biochemically recurrent disease; both trials used multiple independent, blinded central readers rather than a single reader
- *Endpoints:* co-primary sensitivity and specificity of PSMA PET/CT for detecting pelvic nodal metastasis relative to histopathology (OSPREY Cohort A); correct localization rate (CLR), which FDA's review reclassified as functionally a patient-level positive predictive value (PPV) metric due to protocol-definition ambiguity, against the composite truth standard (CONDOR)
- *Primary analysis:* per-reader hypothesis tests of sensitivity/specificity against pre-specified performance goals (OSPREY: H0 specificity=0.80 vs. H1 specificity≠0.80, tested first; if rejected, H0 sensitivity=0.40 vs. H1 sensitivity≠0.40 tested next, same readers), with a multiplicity rule requiring ≥2 of 3 readers to independently reject each null for the endpoint to be deemed a success (CONDOR: patient-level PPV threshold of 0.20 against the lower bound of each reader's 95% CI, again requiring ≥2 of 3 readers to exceed)
- *Missing data/bias:* performance-measure analysis complicated by an imperfect/non-independent reference standard — CONDOR's composite truth standard incorporated conventional imaging (including 18F-fluciclovine PET in 50-54% of the composite-truth-derived subset) rather than histopathology alone in the majority of cases, and OSPREY excluded PET-non-evaluable regions from consideration; FDA explicitly reframed CONDOR's named primary endpoint (CLR) as a de facto PPV metric because of definitional ambiguity in how the sponsor operationalized it
- *Regulatory:* standard (non-accelerated) NDA approval for a diagnostic imaging agent, evaluated on diagnostic-accuracy criteria (sensitivity/specificity/PPV against pre-specified performance goals) rather than a tumor-response or survival endpoint; no FDA advisory committee meeting held, "because this drug is not the first in its class"

**Trial design & endpoints**

- OSPREY: prospective, open-label, non-randomized, multicenter Phase 2/3 diagnostic-accuracy trial; Cohort A enrolled patients with high-risk prostate cancer planned for radical prostatectomy with pelvic lymph node dissection, all of whom received piflufolastat F 18 PET/CT before surgery, with pelvic-lymph-node histopathology as the reference standard; images were centrally read by three independent, blinded radiologists/nuclear medicine physicians, blinded to local reads, clinical information, and baseline conventional imaging
- OSPREY sample size: 262 planned Cohort A subjects, targeting ≥80% power to reject a sensitivity null of 40% if true sensitivity was ≥60%, and ≥80% power to reject a specificity null of 80% if true specificity was ≥87.8%
- OSPREY result (N=252 evaluable, per-reader, no region-matching): all three readers exceeded the pre-defined specificity goal of 80% (reader range 96-99%), but none met or exceeded the pre-defined sensitivity goal of 40% (reader range 31-42%); PPV ranged 78-90%, NPV 81-84% across readers; with region-matching applied, the label reports sensitivity 28-39%, specificity 95-98%, PPV 72-81%
- CONDOR: prospective, open-label, multicenter Phase 3 diagnostic trial in men with biochemically recurrent prostate cancer (rising PSA after primary therapy) and negative or equivocal conventional imaging; every PET-positive finding was evaluated against a composite reference/truth standard — histopathology where available, otherwise informative conventional imaging, otherwise confirmed PSA response (≥50% decline) — by a two-member central "truth panel" distinct from and blinded to the PET readers
- CONDOR sample size: assumed a true CLR/PPV of 30%, requiring 81 PET-positive scans (134 evaluable subjects, ~192 enrolled after accounting for a 30% non-evaluable rate); "no interim analyses planned"
- CONDOR result (N=208, per-reader): patient-level PPV/CLR ranged 85-87% across the three readers (95% CIs approximately 78-94%); correct detection rate 40-43%; an exploratory "imputed CLR" accounting for PET-positive patients lacking reference-standard information ranged 78-81%
- FDA's terminology clarification (CONDOR): "the Applicant's understanding of CLR functionally represents a patient-level positive predictive value (PPV) metric" due to ambiguity in the protocol's definition, so the review refers to the endpoint as PPV throughout its efficacy section rather than as CLR

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2021/214793Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2021/214793s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/214793Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (OSPREY) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02981368 (Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan both posted in the Documents tab)
- Protocol / SAP (OSPREY) — Protocol: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/68/NCT02981368/Prot_000.pdf; SAP: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/68/NCT02981368/SAP_001.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (CONDOR) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03739684 (Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan both posted in the Documents tab)
- Protocol / SAP (CONDOR) — Protocol: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/84/NCT03739684/Prot_000.pdf; SAP: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/84/NCT03739684/SAP_001.pdf

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-20-4573), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33622706/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Diagnostic%20Performance%2018F-DCFPyL-PET%2FCT%20Biochemically%20Recurrent%20Prostate%20Cancer%20CONDOR)

**Other resources**

- No Vivli, YODA, or Project Data Sphere listing was found for Progenics Pharmaceuticals or Lantheus.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held; the approval letter states this was "because this drug is not the first in its class."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP, OSPREY, endpoint definitions]* — "This is an open-label, non-randomized, Phase 2/3, multi-center study designed to evaluate the safety and diagnostic performance of 18F-DCFPyL PET/CT imaging to determine the presence or absence of metastatic prostate cancer in subjects with high risk prostate cancer who were planned for radical prostatectomy with pelvic lymph node dissection (cohort A)." "1. Specificity of 18F-DCFPyL PET/CT imaging to determine the absence of metastatic prostate cancer within the pelvic lymph nodes relative to histopathology in Cohort A. 2. Sensitivity of 18F-DCFPyL PET/CT imaging..."

*[verbatim, same source, sample size/multiplicity]* — "H0: πSp = 0.80 versus H1: πSp ≠ 0.80" (specificity, tested first); if rejected, "H01: πSe = 0.40 versus H11: πSe ≠ 0.40" (sensitivity, same readers). "A total of 262 subjects from Cohort A will provide 80% power to reject the null hypothesis about sensitivity at the 5% significance level if the true sensitivity is at least 60% and at least 80% power to reject the null hypothesis about specificity... if the true specificity is at least 87.8%." "At least two of the three readers must reject the null hypothesis for specificity to be deemed a success. If specificity is a success, then the same two readers need to reject the null hypothesis for sensitivity leading to overall success."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, OSPREY reader methodology]* — "The PET/CT images were centrally evaluated by three independent, blinded radiologists or nuclear medicine physicians. Blinding specifically included local radiology assessments, clinical information, and baseline conventional imaging... Positive was defined as 'uptake greater than background activity and judged by the reader to be consistent with disease.'"

*[verbatim, same source, OSPREY result]* — "All three readers exceeded the predefined specificity goal of 80%, however, none of them met or exceeded the sensitivity goal of 40%."

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP, CONDOR, primary endpoint definition]* — "The primary endpoint of the CLR is evaluated in a subset of Full Analysis Set (FAS) subjects with at least one positive lesion identified by 18F-DCPyL PET/CT imaging by the local reader and then evaluated against the composite truth standard by three independent, blinded central imaging readers. The CLR at the subject level is defined as the percentage of subjects for whom there is a one-to-one correspondence between localization of at least one lesion identified on 18F-DCFPyL PET/CT imaging (by central review) and the composite truth standard, which is defined either as: 1) evaluable local histopathology... 2) if evaluable histopathology is not available, informative conventional imaging... 3) if neither of the above is available or informative, confirmed PSA response (PSA decline by ≥50% from baseline...)."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, CONDOR terminology clarification]* — "there was some ambiguity in this endpoint... the Applicant clarified that CLR would be assessed in patients with positive piflufolastat F 18 PET scans and evaluable reference standard information. Thus, the Applicant's understanding of CLR functionally represents a patient-level positive predictive value (PPV) metric. Because of the ambiguity of the CLR definition, this primary endpoint will be referred to as PPV throughout Section 8.1.4."

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP, CONDOR, sample size]* — "The assumed CLR of 18F-DCFPyL PET/CT imaging is 30%... This will thus require a total of 81 positive PyL scans, which translates to a total of 134 PyL PET/CT scans or evaluable subjects needed. Accounting for a 30% non-evaluable (including loss to follow-up) rate, approximately 192 subjects will need to undergo PyL PET/CT." "No interim analyses planned."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, CONDOR truth-panel methodology]* — "If follow up correlative imaging or image-guided biopsy was performed, those images were evaluated by a two member central 'truth panel' and consensus results were reported. Truth panel readers were distinct from the investigational PET readers and were blinded to piflufolastat F 18 PET reads."

Piflufolastat F 18 is the one entry in this batch built entirely on diagnostic-accuracy statistics rather than a therapeutic-outcome endpoint — its most notable methodological feature is FDA's explicit reclassification of CONDOR's named primary endpoint (correct localization rate) as functionally equivalent to a patient-level positive predictive value, an example of a primary-endpoint-definition ambiguity being resolved during FDA review rather than left as originally labeled by the sponsor; both OSPREY and CONDOR are unusual in this census for having genuine sponsor-posted SAPs available for both trials.

### 134. sotorasib (Lumakras) — NDA 214665

**Sponsor:** Amgen Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with KRAS G12C-mutated locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), as determined by an FDA-approved test, who have received at least one prior systemic therapy — single-arm accelerated approval based on ORR/DOR

**Approval date:** May 28, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** CodeBreaK 100 (Study 20170543), NCT03600883; confirmatory trial CodeBreaK 200, NCT04303780 (randomized vs. docetaxel)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label, multicohort trial supporting accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.500 (dose-expansion phase of a Phase 1/2 trial); confirmatory trial (CodeBreaK 200) is a randomized, open-label, active-controlled Phase 3 trial with crossover permitted from docetaxel to sotorasib at confirmed progression
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR, primary, by BICR per RECIST 1.1, confirmed at ≥4 weeks) and duration of response (DOR, key secondary) in CodeBreaK 100; progression-free survival (PFS, primary, by BICR per RECIST 1.1) and overall survival (OS, secondary) in CodeBreaK 200
- *Primary analysis:* descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis with exact (Clopper-Pearson) 95% CI (CodeBreaK 100); stratified log-rank test with Cox proportional-hazards model for PFS (CodeBreaK 200), stratified by prior lines of therapy, race (Asian vs. non-Asian), and CNS involvement
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* CodeBreaK 200 used an O'Brien-Fleming-type alpha-spending function for the PFS interim analysis (planned at ~70%/160 of 230 target PFS events, 0.007 one-sided alpha spent at the interim), plus a planned OS interim/primary analysis at ~198 events (~60% maturity)
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval based on ORR from a single-arm dose-expansion cohort; postmarketing requirement (PMR 4071-1) for the randomized confirmatory trial CodeBreaK 200, which met its primary PFS endpoint (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.51-0.86, p=0.0017) but whose adequacy to support full-approval conversion became contentious — FDA convened an ODAC on October 5, 2023 specifically to discuss converting the accelerated approval to full approval based on CodeBreaK 200, and as of the most recent label reviewed the NSCLC indication remains under accelerated approval, i.e., conversion had not occurred; published post-hoc critique (Ranganathan, Prasad, Olivier, *Lancet Oncol* 2024) characterized the regulatory outcome as unresolved, with an Amgen-affiliated rebuttal published in response

**Trial design & endpoints**

- CodeBreaK 100: open-label, multicenter, multicohort, single-arm study; the NSCLC dose-expansion cohort (primary efficacy population, n=124) enrolled patients with KRAS G12C-mutated locally advanced/metastatic NSCLC at the RP2D of 960 mg daily, the majority (n=100) having received both prior platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy
- Primary endpoint: ORR by BICR per RECIST 1.1 (confirmed complete or partial response at ≥2 consecutive assessments); design-stage sample size (~105 NSCLC patients) targeted ~90% probability that the ORR 95% CI lower bound would exceed a pre-specified tumor-specific benchmark ORR of 23%, with a minimal observed ORR of 32% needed to exclude the benchmark from the CI
- Efficacy result (N=124, cutoff Sept 1, 2020): ORR 36.3% (95% CI 27.9-45.4%; rounded to 36% in some FDA summary text), 1.6% CR and 34.7% PR; DOR (cutoff Dec 1, 2020, n=45 responders) median 10.0 months (95% CI 6.9-11.1), Kaplan-Meier DOR rate 70.2% at 6 months and 54.7% at 9 months, 57.8% (26/45) censored
- CodeBreaK 200 (confirmatory): randomized (1:1) Phase 3 trial of sotorasib vs. docetaxel in ~345 previously-treated KRAS G12C-mutated NSCLC patients; primary PFS analysis planned at ~230 events for ~90% power to detect HR=0.65 at one-sided α=0.025; result — median PFS 5.6 months (95% CI 4.3-7.8) sotorasib vs. 4.5 months (95% CI 3.0-5.7) docetaxel, HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.51-0.86), p=0.0017; fewer grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events with sotorasib (33% vs. 40%)
- No ODAC was held for the original 2021 accelerated approval; an ODAC was later convened October 5, 2023 specifically to discuss the sNDA (214665/S-005) proposing conversion to full approval based on CodeBreaK 200's results and to weigh the drug's benefit-risk profile — the meeting outcome/vote tally was not located in this research pass, but the practical outcome (accelerated-approval status retained in the current label) indicates conversion had not occurred as of the most recent label reviewed

"Sotorasib versus docetaxel: evidence supporting CodeBreaK 200." *Lancet Oncol.* 2024;25(8):e334. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(24)00388-7), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39089308/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Sotorasib%20versus%20docetaxel%20evidence%20supporting%20CodeBreaK%20200)

**Other resources**

- Amgen is not listed among Vivli's data-contributor members; no YODA or Project Data Sphere listing was confirmed for CodeBreaK 100/200.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held at original approval ("this drug is not the first in its class"); an ODAC was later convened October 5, 2023 to review CodeBreaK 200 results and discuss full-approval conversion.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 214665, sample-size section]* — "Per the final SAP, the primary efficacy endpoint is ORR as assessed by BICR per RECIST 1.1, to be summarized descriptively with a Clopper-Pearson exact 95% CI. The phase II part of the study planned to enroll approximately 105 patients with NSCLC. A sample size of 105 subjects for NSCLC would provide approximately a 90% probability that the lower limit of the ORR 95% CI exceeds the pre-specified tumor-specific benchmark ORR of 23%. The minimal observed ORR that would exclude the benchmark ORR from the 95% CI with this sample size is 32%."

*[verbatim, same source, endpoint definition]* — "Tumor response assessments were conducted by an independent, external radiologic central laboratory (blinded independent central review [BICR]) using RECIST 1.1 criteria... Complete and partial response required confirmatory CT or MRI repeat assessment at least 4 weeks after the first detection of response."

*[verbatim, same source, efficacy result]* — "The full analysis set comprised 124 evaluable subjects... Forty-five subjects in the full analysis set of the phase 2 NSCLC group achieved a confirmed partial response or confirmed complete response... for an ORR of 36.3% (95% CI: 27.9, 45.4)... Of the 45 responders..., 2 subjects (1.6%) achieved complete response and 43 subjects (34.7%) achieved partial response."

*[verbatim, same source, DOR definition/result]* — "The DOR (calculated only for those subjects with a confirmed complete response or partial response per RECIST 1.1 as of the 01 September 2020 data cutoff) was defined as the time from first objective response to disease progression as assessed by BICR per RECIST 1.1 or death due to any cause, whichever was earlier. Responses were censored at the last assessment not confirming disease progression." "median (95% CI) DOR for the 45 objective responders was 10.0 months (6.9, 11.1) months... Kaplan-Meier estimates for DOR at 6 and 9 months are 70.2% and 54.7%, respectively."

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP, CodeBreaK 200, design/statistics]* — "Approximately 330 previously treated subjects... will be enrolled and randomized 1:1 to receive either AMG 510 or docetaxel." "The PA of PFS will occur when approximately 230 PFS events have been observed. With 230 PFS events, the study will have ~90% power to show a statistically significant PFS at the 2.5% 1-sided significance level if the true treatment effect hazard ratio (HR) is assumed 0.65... An IA is planned when approximately 70% (160) of the target PFS events have been observed... O'Brien-Fleming type alpha spending function for multiplicity adjustment with 0.007 one-sided alpha spent at the PFS IA."

*[verbatim, published CodeBreaK 200 result]* — "the study met its primary endpoint of a statistically significant increase in the progression-free survival for sotorasib, compared with docetaxel (median progression-free survival 5.6 months [95% CI 4.3-7.8] vs 4.5 months [3.0-5.7]; hazard ratio 0.66 [0.51-0.86]; p=0.0017)."

*[verbatim, ODAC meeting announcement, Oct 5, 2023]* — "The Committee will discuss supplemental new drug application (sNDA) 214665/S-005, for LUMAKRAS (sotorasib) tablets, submitted by Amgen Inc.,... This supplement proposes to convert the NDA to full approval based on the confirmatory study, CodeBreaK 200. The Committee will consider the results of the CodeBreaK 200 study and discuss the benefit-risk profile of LUMAKRAS."

Sotorasib is a useful contrast case within this batch: its confirmatory trial (CodeBreaK 200) met its primary PFS endpoint with a statistically significant result, unlike the withdrawal cases elsewhere in this batch, yet full-approval conversion remained unresolved as of the most recent label reviewed, and the sufficiency of a PFS-only randomized confirmatory result (without a clear OS benefit) became the subject of public post-hoc scientific dispute — illustrating that a "positive" confirmatory trial does not automatically resolve an accelerated approval's regulatory status.

### 135. infigratinib (Truseltiq) — NDA 214622

**Sponsor:** BridgeBio Pharma, Inc. (QED Therapeutics); later commercialized in the US by Helsinn Healthcare SA

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with previously treated, unresectable locally advanced or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma with a fibroblast growth factor receptor 2 (FGFR2) gene fusion or other rearrangement, as detected by an FDA-approved test — single-arm accelerated approval based on ORR/DOR

**Approval date:** May 28, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** Study CBGJ398X2204 (Study 2204), NCT02150967, Cohort 1; intended confirmatory trial PROOF-301 (also referred to as "PROOF 301"), NCT03773302

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label, multicohort trial supporting accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.500 (Cohort 1, FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement); intended confirmatory trial (PROOF-301) was a randomized (2:1), open-label, active-controlled (gemcitabine+cisplatin) first-line Phase 3 trial that was terminated early for a reason unrelated to safety or efficacy (see Regulatory below)
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR, primary, by BICR per RECIST 1.1) and duration of response (DOR, key secondary), both assessed by central imaging review with disease control rate treated as exploratory; FDA explicitly states "time-to-event endpoints of OS and PFS are not interpretable in a single arm study"
- *Primary analysis:* exact (Clopper-Pearson) binomial confidence interval for ORR; Brookmeyer-Crowley method for constructing 95% CIs for time to response and duration of response
- *Missing data/bias:* not applicable in the randomized-trial sense (single-arm design); BICR-vs-investigator concordance for responders was 80% (18/25), with the investigator-assessed ORR (30.6%) numerically higher than the BICR-assessed ORR (23.1%) used for the regulatory decision
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval based on ORR/DOR from a single-arm trial; postmarketing requirement for a randomized confirmatory trial (PROOF-301, first-line vs. gemcitabine/cisplatin); PROOF-301 was terminated early (48 of a much larger planned enrollment) and its own ClinicalTrials.gov record states plainly "the discontinuation of the study was not due to safety issues" — instead "due to the discontinuation of infigratinib development in oncology within the sponsor's territory"; the drug was withdrawn from the US market via a formal FDA Federal Register notice effective May 16, 2024, following a company request (May 30, 2023) explicitly and solely citing "difficulties in recruiting and enrolling study subjects for the required confirmatory clinical trial" and a determination that "continued distribution of TRUSELTIQ in second line cholangiocarcinoma... is not commercially reasonable" — an explicitly commercial/enrollment-driven withdrawal, not a safety- or efficacy-failure withdrawal, a materially different pattern from umbralisib and melphalan flufenamide elsewhere in this batch

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study CBGJ398X2204 (Study 2204): open-label, non-randomized, multicohort Phase 2 trial; Cohort 1 (FGFR2 gene fusion/rearrangement, ≥1 prior therapy) enrolled 108 patients who received infigratinib 125 mg orally once daily, 21 days on/7 days off, in 28-day cycles; the trial's other cohorts (2 and 3, exploratory, non-FGFR2-fusion alterations) were separately terminated early for limited efficacy — a termination the ClinicalTrials.gov record states explicitly "had no impact on the primary efficacy analysis (i.e., results reported for Cohort 1)"
- Primary endpoint: ORR by central/BICR review per RECIST 1.1, analyzed via the SAP's final version (dated May 13, 2020, matching the FDA review's citation) with a Clopper-Pearson exact 95% CI; FDA noted "this sample size justification appeared adequate from the FDA perspective as FDA does not consider inferential procedures in the evaluation of single arm study results"
- Efficacy result (Interim Analysis Set 2, Cohort 1, N=108, cutoff March 31, 2020): BICR-assessed ORR 23.1% (95% CI 15.6-32.2%), 1 CR + 24 PR; median DOR 5.03 months (95% CI 3.71-9.26), with 32% (8/25) of responders maintaining response ≥6 months and 4% (1/25) ≥12 months; investigator-assessed ORR was numerically higher at 30.6% (95% CI 22.1-40.2%), with 80% (18/25) reader concordance among BICR responders
- PROOF-301 (intended confirmatory trial): randomized 2:1 (infigratinib vs. gemcitabine+cisplatin), first-line, open-label Phase 3 trial; enrolled only 48 of its planned target before the sponsor closed the study; ClinicalTrials.gov's stated reason for termination: "The sponsor has decided to close the study due to the discontinuation of infigratinib development in oncology within the sponsor's territory. The discontinuation of the study was not due to safety issues"

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2021/214622Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2021/214622s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/214622Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (Study 2204/CBGJ398X2204) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02150967 (status: terminated for Cohorts 2/3 only; Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan both posted in the Documents tab)
- Protocol / SAP (Study 2204) — Protocol: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/67/NCT02150967/Prot_000.pdf; SAP v3.0: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/67/NCT02150967/SAP_001.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (PROOF-301) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03773302 (status: terminated at 48/planned enrollment; Protocol and SAP posted, limited results posted)
- Protocol / SAP (PROOF-301) — Protocol: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/02/NCT03773302/Prot_000.pdf; SAP: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/02/NCT03773302/SAP_001.pdf
- Federal Register withdrawal notice (89 FR 42887-42888, effective May 16, 2024) — https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/05/16/2024-10714/helsinn-healthcare-sa-withdrawal-of-approval-of-new-drug-application-for-truseltiq-infigratinib

[DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S2468-1253(21)00196-5>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34358484/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Infigratinib%20BGJ398%20previously%20treated%20advanced%20metastatic%20cholangiocarcinoma%20FGFR2%20fusions%20mature%20results)

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.2217/fon-2020-0299), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32580579/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Infigratinib%20advanced%20cholangiocarcinoma%20FGFR2%20gene%20fusions%20translocations%20PROOF%20301%20trial)

**Other resources**

- No Vivli, YODA, or Project Data Sphere listing was found for BridgeBio Pharma or QED Therapeutics.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held; the approval letter states this was "because this drug is not the first in its class and no review issues were identified that raised significant public health questions regarding the risk:benefit assessment of infigratinib for the proposed indication."
- BridgeBio has continued developing infigratinib for non-oncology indications (achondroplasia/hypochondroplasia), later licensing ex-US rights to Kyowa Kirin (Feb 2024) — underscoring that the oncology withdrawal reflected a business-prioritization decision about the oncology program specifically, not a finding against the molecule.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 214622, trial-identification/efficacy summary]* — "This approval recommendation is primarily based on safety and efficacy results of a single trial, Study CBGJ398X2204 (also referred to as Study 2204; NCT02150967). Study 2204 is an open label, non-randomized, multi-cohort trial that evaluated the efficacy of infigratinib in 108 patients with locally advanced unresectable or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma harboring an FGFR2 gene fusion or rearrangement, whose disease had progressed on or after at least 1 prior therapy (Cohort 1)."

*[verbatim, same source, endpoint/analysis method]* — "FDA's efficacy evaluation is based on the primary endpoint of overall response rate (ORR) by BICR according to RECIST v1.1, accompanied with the durability of response (DOR) by BICR. FDA considers disease control rate (DCR) to be an exploratory endpoint... time-to-event endpoints of OS and PFS are not interpretable in a single arm study." "The estimated overall response rate (ORR) is presented with corresponding 95% confidence interval (CI) based on the binomial distribution (Clopper-Pearson exact method) accompanied by duration of response (DOR)."

*[verbatim, same source, sample size]* — "The final version of the statistical analysis plan dated 13 May 2020 included justification for sample size based on estimation precision. This sample size justification appeared adequate from the FDA perspective as FDA does not consider inferential procedures in the evaluation of single arm study results."

*[verbatim, same source, efficacy result, Table 30]* — BICR: ORR 23.1% (95% CI 15.6, 32.2%), 1 CR + 24 PR, median DOR 5.03 months (95% CI 3.71, 9.26), DOR≥6mo in 8 (32%), DOR≥12mo in 1 (4%). Investigator: ORR 30.6% (95% CI 22.1, 40.2%), 0 CR + 33 PR, median DOR 5.95 months (95% CI 5.16, 9.00). Concordance between BICR and investigator = 80% (18/25 BICR responders also called responders by investigator).

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP, Study 2204, primary endpoint/analysis]* — "For Cohort 1, the primary objective of the study is to assess anti-tumor activity of infigratinib using overall response rate assessed by central imaging review... Overall response rate (ORR) is defined as the proportion of patients with a best overall response of confirmed Complete Response (CR) or Partial Response (PR), as per RECIST version 1.1... ORR (central imaging assessment) is the primary efficacy endpoint, and its analysis consists of a Clopper-Pearson 95% CI accompanied by a characterization of time to response (TTR) and duration of response (DOR)... The Brookmeyer-Crowley method will be used to construct the 95% CI for each of TTR and DOR."

*[verbatim, ClinicalTrials.gov, Study 2204 termination reason]* — "The study was terminated early due to limited efficacy in Cohorts 2 and 3 (exploratory endpoints). Termination was not due to concerns about safety and had no impact on the primary efficacy analysis (ie, results reported for Cohort 1)."

*[verbatim, ClinicalTrials.gov, PROOF-301 termination reason]* — "The sponsor has decided to close the study due to the discontinuation of infigratinib development in oncology within the sponsor's territory. The discontinuation of the study was not due to safety issues."

*[verbatim, Federal Register, 89 FR 42887-42888, withdrawal notice]* — "On October 5, 2022, Helsinn voluntarily requested withdrawal of approval of TRUSELTIQ... On May 30, 2023, Helsinn submitted a letter asking FDA to withdraw approval of NDA 214622... In its letter requesting withdrawal of approval, Helsinn stated that it is voluntarily requesting withdrawal due to difficulties in recruiting and enrolling study subjects for the required confirmatory clinical trial in first line cholangiocarcinoma (a new indication under investigation for TRUSELTIQ), and the determination that, as a result, continued distribution of TRUSELTIQ in second line cholangiocarcinoma (the accelerated approval indication) is not commercially reasonable. Helsinn stated that it agreed to withdrawal of the application for this reason only." "Approval is withdrawn as of May 16, 2024."

*[verbatim, BridgeBio Pharma FY2023 10-K]* — "Helsinn permanently discontinued the distribution of TRUSELTIQ™ and requested a withdrawal of the NDA in May 2023, additionally, all clinical investigations under the associated IND are discontinued." "While a request to withdraw the New Drug Application... for TRUSELTIQ™ was submitted in May 2023, all clinical investigations under the associated Investigational New Drug application... were discontinued as of March 2023 due to difficulty enrolling study patients for the required confirmation trial."

Infigratinib is the third market-withdrawal story in this batch, but a categorically different one from umbralisib and melphalan flufenamide: every source reviewed — the Federal Register withdrawal notice, PROOF-301's own ClinicalTrials.gov termination record, and BridgeBio's SEC filings — independently and consistently attributes the withdrawal to commercial/enrollment infeasibility of the required first-line confirmatory trial, not to any safety signal or failed efficacy readout; the company's own withdrawal request (May 2023) and FDA's formal Federal Register action giving it effect (May 2024) fall a year apart, worth noting explicitly since both dates appear in different secondary sources.

### 136. asparaginase erwinia chrysanthemi (recombinant)-rywn (Rylaze) — BLA 761179

**Sponsor:** Jazz Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (drug developed as JZP-458 / recombinant crisantaspase produced in *Pseudomonas fluorescens*)

**Indication approved:** As a component of a multi-agent chemotherapeutic regimen for the treatment of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and lymphoblastic lymphoma (LBL) in adult and pediatric patients 1 month or older who have developed hypersensitivity to *E. coli*-derived asparaginase

**Approval date:** June 30, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** Study JZP458-201 (also reported as the pediatric-oncology-cooperative-group study AALL1931), NCT04145531

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial; sequential-cohort, multi-part dose-confirmation design with a Study Data Review Committee (SDRC) reviewing accruing NSAA data at pre-specified patient counts and issuing stop/continue/expand decisions per cohort
- *Endpoints:* pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic activity-threshold endpoint (nadir serum asparaginase activity, NSAA, ≥0.1 IU/mL at the last 72-hour and 48-hour timepoints of Course 1) — same construct as the original Erwinaze approval
- *Primary analysis:* single-proportion responder-rate analysis using a Wald 95% confidence interval, with a pre-specified decision rule (CI lower bound must exceed 90%) rather than a p-value hypothesis test
- *Regulatory:* accelerated/standard approval of a bridging biologic supported in part by FDA-conducted population-PK modeling and simulation after the observed primary endpoint was not met in any of the three directly studied dosing cohorts

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Open-label, multicenter, sequential-cohort study in ALL/LBL patients hypersensitive (or with "silent inactivation") to long-acting *E. coli*-derived asparaginase; Part A (intramuscular, IM) enrolled three MWF dosing cohorts (25 mg/m² x6, Cohort 1A; 37.5 mg/m² x6, Cohort 1B; 25-25-50 mg/m² x6, Cohort 1C) followed by an expansion cohort at the selected dose, and Part B evaluated intravenous administration
- Primary endpoint: proportion of patients with the last 72-hour NSAA level ≥0.1 IU/mL during the first course of IM administration (key secondary: same threshold at 48 hours)
- Planned sample size of 98 patients was calculated to give 83% probability that the lower bound of the 95% Wald CI would exceed 90%, assuming a true response rate of 96% and 5% dropout; one interim analysis was planned at 51 patients (70% probability of the same criterion)
- As of the data cutoff supporting approval, 102 patients had been accrued (33 in Cohort 1A, 53 in 1B, 16 in 1C); FDA's review states plainly that "the objective of a 72-hour NSAA ≥0.1 U/mL in at least 90% of patients was not met in any of the three dosage cohorts" — point estimates were <90% in Cohorts 1A/1B, and in Cohort 1C the point estimate exceeded 90% but the CI lower bound did not, "due to the small sample size"
- FDA then built its own population-PK (PopPK) model from the observed SAA data and simulated two alternative dosing regimens in 2,000 virtual NHANES-derived subjects; the simulations (not the directly observed trial data) projected that ≥90% of patients would achieve and maintain NSAA ≥0.1 IU/mL with 25 mg/m² IM every 48 hours (93.6%, 95% CI 92.6–94.6%) or with a 25-25-50 mg/m² MWF schedule (91.4%, 95% CI 90.2%–unreported upper bound in the excerpt reviewed) — these FDA-simulation-supported regimens, not the as-studied cohort doses, underpin the approved dosing
- The sponsor's SAP was amended four times (18-Dec-2019 through 16-Dec-2020); amendments clarified the efficacy/PK/PD analysis sets and interim/primary-analysis sample sizes and added a COVID-19 sensitivity analysis — FDA's review states it "agrees that these were the submitted SAP amendments" but separately notes "there was not a clear plan for adaptive modifications based on prespecified interim analyses of PK and PD"

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2021/761179Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2021/761179s000lbledt.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (BLA 761179) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/761179Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04145531
- Study Protocol (posted on ClinicalTrials.gov) — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/31/NCT04145531/Prot_000.pdf
- Statistical Analysis Plan, Version 3.0/final, dated 16-Dec-2020 (posted on ClinicalTrials.gov) — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/31/NCT04145531/SAP_002.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Maese L, Loh ML, Choi MR, et al. "Recombinant Erwinia asparaginase (JZP458) in acute lymphoblastic leukemia: results from the phase 2/3 AALL1931 study." *Blood.* 2023;141(7):704-712. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1182/blood.2022016923), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36108304/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Recombinant%20Erwinia%20asparaginase%20JZP458%20in%20acute%20lymphoblastic%20leukemia%20results%20from%20the%20phase%202%2F3%20AALL1931%20study)

**Other resources**

- Jazz Pharmaceuticals does not have a broad, publicly documented IPD-sharing commitment comparable to Vivli/YODA participation for this trial; trial-specific IPD availability was not individually confirmed here.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this approval.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761179, "Conclusions on the Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness," p.17]* "The planned sample size of 98 patients was calculated to provide 83% probability that the lower bound of the 95% Wald CI exceeds 90%, assuming a true response rate of 96% for the primary efficacy endpoint and a 5% drop out rate. There was one planned interim analysis with 51 patients... On the basis of the observed data, the objective of a 72-hour NSAA ≥ 0.1 U/mL in at least 90% of patients was not met in any of the three dosage cohorts. In Cohorts 1A and 1B, the point estimate for NSAA response was < 90%. In Cohort 1C, the point estimate for NSAA response was > 90%, but the lower bound of the 95% confidence interval did not meet the objective due to the small sample size."
- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761179, "Statistical Analysis Plan and Amendments," p.92]* "The SAP was amended four times... SAP Version 1.4 was approved prior to the database freeze for the initial interim analysis... The FDA agrees that these were the submitted SAP amendments for JZP458-201. FDA also notes that there was not a clear plan for adaptive modifications based on prespecified interim analyses of PK and PD."
- *[reconstructed — see caveat below, sponsor SAP v3.0, §"Analysis of the Primary Efficacy Endpoint"]* "The primary efficacy endpoint will be estimated using the Efficacy Analysis Set for patients administered the final IM RCP dose level... Missing data will not be imputed. The response rate along with the Wald CI will be provided. The primary efficacy endpoint will be met if the lower bound of the CI of the response rate exceeds [90%]."
- *[reconstructed — see caveat below, sponsor SAP v3.0, §"Hypotheses Testing, Level of Significance and Multiplicity Adjustment"]* "No formal statistical testing is planned for this study and thus no multiplicity adjustment is applicable."
- **Extraction caveat:** the posted SAP PDF's text layer is corrupted in two compounding ways: (1) nearly all inter-word spaces are missing (individually positioned glyphs with no space characters, the same failure mode documented for the SELECT/semaglutide entry in this census), and (2) every character's code point is additionally offset by a fixed +29/-29 shift (a font-encoding artifact), which was reversed programmatically; digits in particular did not survive this reversal (they map to non-printable control characters and are dropped by the text extractor), so numeric values in the reconstructed SAP passages above are not reliable and have been redacted/bracketed rather than guessed — the equivalent numeric detail is instead sourced from the cleanly-extracted FDA Multi-Discipline Review quotes above.

### 137. belzutifan (Welireg) — NDA 215383

**Sponsor:** Merck Sharp & Dohme LLC (drug developed by Peloton Therapeutics, a subsidiary of Merck; internal code MK-6482/PT2977)

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) disease who require therapy for associated renal cell carcinoma (RCC), central nervous system (CNS) hemangioblastomas, or pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (pNET), not requiring immediate surgery

**Approval date:** August 13, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** Study MK-6482-004, NCT03401788

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial; biomarker/genetically-defined rare-disease population (germline VHL alteration) with multiple VHL-associated tumor types (RCC, CNS hemangioblastoma, pNET) each analyzed as a separate efficacy cohort within one single-arm trial rather than pooled across unrelated histologies
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DoR), assessed separately for RCC and non-RCC (CNS hemangioblastoma, pNET) lesions per RECIST v1.1 by independent review committee (IRC); progression-free survival (PFS) and time to surgery (TTS) reported descriptively only — FDA's review states these are "uninterpretable in a single arm study without a comparator arm"
- *Primary analysis:* descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (point estimate + exact Clopper-Pearson 95% CI, no formal hypothesis test)
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval based on single-arm ORR/DoR, confirmatory trial required; post-hoc addition of IRC-adjudicated response analyses into the statistical analysis plan after enrollment had already completed

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Open-label, single-arm, multicenter Phase 2 trial enrolling adult VHL-disease patients with at least one measurable, non-surgery-indicated RCC lesion (plus, for the broader label, non-RCC VHL-associated lesions present at screening); all patients received belzutifan 120 mg orally once daily; radiologic tumor assessments occurred every 12 weeks (Q12W)
- Primary efficacy population/analysis set: All Patients as Treated (APaT), all allocated participants who received ≥1 dose
- Primary endpoint: confirmed ORR (CR or PR per RECIST v1.1, IRC-assessed) in VHL-associated RCC lesions; parallel ORR analyses were conducted for CNS hemangioblastoma and pNET lesions
- Sample size was driven by feasibility in this ultra-rare, genetically-defined population (61 RCC-evaluable patients at the data cutoff supporting approval) rather than a powered comparative calculation
- The original protocol (finalized 10-Nov-2017) was amended 13 times (7 major versions); FDA's review documents that the sponsor decided, after enrollment had already completed, to add IRC review of CNS hemangioblastoma, retinal hemangioblastoma, and pancreatic lesions — this was first incorporated into a revised SAP (v2.0, 12-Jul-2020) and then consolidated into a global protocol amendment (v8.0, 2-Mar-2021)
- Statistical methods: ORR and disease control rate (DCR) reported with two-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson exact confidence intervals; no formal multiplicity control, since there is a single primary efficacy population per tumor type and no between-arm comparison

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2021/215383Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2021/215383s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (NDA 215383) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/215383Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03401788
- Protocol / SAP: not posted on ClinicalTrials.gov as of this writing (no `documentSection` present in the record)

The APaT population was used for all analyses of efficacy and safety... All changes to the statistical analysis plan were made via protocol amendments." FDA's assessment on the same page: "FDA agrees with the Applicant's description of the statistical analysis plan... the Sponsor decided to pursue IRC review of CNS hemangioblastoma, retinal hemangioblastoma, and pancreatic tumors including pNET after enrollment in the study was completed. The IRC review and analyses were initially incorporated into the revised Statistical Analysis Plan (version 2.0, dated 12-JUL-2020)."
- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 215383, Table 8, "Summary of Best Overall Tumor Response for RCC Tumors (RECIST 1.1) – IRC (Efficacy Analysis Set)," data cutoff 01-Jun-2020]* Objective response rate (CR+PR): 22/61 (36.1%), 95% CI (24.2, 49.4); Disease Control Rate (CR+PR+SD): 60/61 (98.4%), 95% CI (91.2, 100.0). Footnote: "95% confidence intervals are constructed using 2-sided Clopper-Pearson method."
- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 215383, p.5089]* "Progression-free survival (PFS) is a time-to-event endpoint and results are uninterpretable in a single arm study without a comparator arm. Time to surgery (TTS) results are also difficult to interpret in this setting because although in theory it would be helpful to know about surgical decisions, there were no objective criteria in the protocol that dictated when the decision for a patient to undergo nephrectomy or other RCC-directed procedures was made and this subjectivity limits interpretability."

### 138. mobocertinib (Exkivity) — NDA 215310

**Sponsor:** Takeda Pharmaceuticals U.S.A., Inc. (drug developed as TAK-788 / AP32788)

**Indication approved (2021, accelerated approval; voluntarily withdrawn 2023 — see Post-approval outcome):** Locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations, as detected by an FDA-approved test, whose disease has progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy

**Approval date:** September 15, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** Study 101 / AP32788-15-101, Part 3 extension cohort ("EXCLAIM"), NCT02716116; confirmatory trial EXCLAIM-2, NCT04129502

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial (accelerated-approval basis, Part 3 of a Phase 1/2 dose-escalation/expansion/extension study); confirmatory trial was randomized, open-label, active-controlled (mobocertinib vs. platinum-based chemotherapy, 1:1)
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR) / duration of response (DoR) (accelerated-approval basis, IRC-assessed confirmed ORR, cORR); progression-free survival (PFS) by blinded independent central review (BICR) as the confirmatory trial's primary endpoint
- *Primary analysis:* exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval (two-sided exact 95% CI for cORR, accelerated-approval basis); stratified log-rank test and Cox proportional-hazards model (confirmatory trial)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* single planned interim/futility analysis in the confirmatory trial at ~70% of 227 expected PFS events, with a pre-specified futility boundary (HR > 1)
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval based on single-arm ORR/DoR, confirmatory trial required; voluntary withdrawal of an accelerated-approval indication after confirmatory-trial failure

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Accelerated-approval basis: Study 101 was an open-label Phase 1/2 dose-escalation (Part 1), expansion-cohort (Part 2), and extension-cohort (Part 3) trial of oral mobocertinib in NSCLC with EGFR or HER2 alterations; the extension cohort ("EXCLAIM," n=91 planned, 96 enrolled) specifically evaluated 160 mg QD in patients with locally advanced/metastatic NSCLC harboring EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations who had received ≥1 prior line of therapy including platinum-based chemotherapy
- Primary endpoint (Part 3): confirmed ORR (cORR) per RECIST v1.1, IRC-assessed; sample size (91 patients, ~73 with centrally-confirmed mutation) was set to provide >91% power to rule out an "uninteresting" ORR of 20%, assuming a true rate of 36%, at a 1-sided alpha of 0.025; the SAP for Study 101 was finalized 24-Aug-2020, specifying the "Pooled Prior Platinum Analysis Set" (RP2D-dosed, platinum-pretreated patients from Parts 1/2/3) as the primary efficacy population
- A Bayesian futility analysis was planned for Part 3 after ~20 patients completed their Cycle 4 assessment (stop if posterior probability that ORR<25% exceeded 90%); the actual interim result met the pre-specified criterion to continue
- cORR (per the FDA review, Pooled Prior Platinum Analysis Set) was tested using exact methods with two-sided exact 95% binomial CIs; no censoring rules applied to cORR (PFS/DoR, secondary endpoints, used censoring rules aligned with FDA's 2015 NSCLC endpoints guidance)
- Confirmatory trial (EXCLAIM-2): randomized 1:1, open-label Phase 3 trial of first-line mobocertinib vs. platinum-doublet chemotherapy (pemetrexed + cisplatin/carboplatin) in treatment-naive EGFR exon-20-insertion-positive advanced/metastatic NSCLC; primary endpoint PFS by BICR, planned interim analysis at ~70% of 227 expected events; 354 patients randomized (179 mobocertinib, 175 chemotherapy)

"Treatment Outcomes and Safety of Mobocertinib in Platinum-Pretreated Patients With EGFR Exon 20 Insertion-Positive Metastatic Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Phase 1/2 Open-label Nonrandomized Clinical Trial." *JAMA Oncol.* 2021;7(12):e214761. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1001/jamaoncol.2021.4761), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34647988/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Treatment%20Outcomes%20and%20Safety%20of%20Mobocertinib%20in%20Platinum-Pretreated%20Patients%20With%20EGFR%20Exon%2020%20Insertion-Positive%20Metastatic%20Non-Small%20Cell%20Lung%20Cancer)
- Confirmatory-trial publication: Jänne PA, Wang BC, Cho BC, et al. "First-Line Mobocertinib Versus Platinum-Based Chemotherapy in Patients With EGFR Exon 20 Insertion-Positive Metastatic Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer in the Phase III EXCLAIM-2 Trial." *J Clin Oncol.* 2025;43(13):1553-1563. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO-24-01269), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39879577/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=First-Line%20Mobocertinib%20Versus%20Platinum-Based%20Chemotherapy%20EXCLAIM-2)
- FDA Drugs@FDA overview page confirming "Discontinued" marketing status — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cder/daf/index.cfm?event=overview.process&ApplNo=215310

**Other resources**

- Takeda's general clinical-data-sharing policy allows qualified-researcher access via a formal request process; trial-specific IPD availability was not individually confirmed here.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for the original 2021 accelerated approval.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 215310, "Statistical Analysis Plan and Amendments," p.123]* "A Statistical Analysis Plan for Study 101 was finalized on 24 Aug 2020. The SAP specified that the primary endpoint was IRC cORR for patients from Parts 1, 2, and 3 treated with 160 mg who a previously received a platinum-based therapy for the NSCLC that harbored exon 20 insertion mutations."
- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 215310, "Interim Analyses," p.123]* "A futility analysis was planned for the primary endpoint for Part 3 when approximately 20 patients had completed their Cycle 4 disease assessment. The study would have been stopped for futility if there was >90% posterior probability that the ORR was less than 25%. The futility analysis was conducted on the first 20 patients in the Part 3 full analysis set with a data cutoff of 08 November 2019; the results met the prespecified criteria to continue the study."
- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 215310, "Primary Efficacy Analyses," p.124]* "Two-sided exact 95% binomial CIs were computed for all binary efficacy endpoints... The primary endpoint of cORR, as assessed by the IRC, was tested using exact methods in the full analysis set. Exact 2-sided 95% CIs for the cORR were calculated based on the binomial distribution... No censoring rules were applied to the analysis of cORR."
- *[verbatim, Jänne et al., JCO 2025, EXCLAIM-2 abstract]* "The primary end point was progression-free survival (PFS) by blinded independent central review (BICR), with planned interim analysis (IA) after approximately 70% of 227 expected PFS events... At IA (cutoff: April 4, 2023), the median PFS per BICR was 9.6 months in each treatment arm (hazard ratio [HR], 1.04 [95% CI, 0.77 to 1.39]; P =.803). The primary end point crossed the prespecified futility boundary (HR > 1)... The EXCLAIM-2 trial did not meet its primary end point."

**Post-approval outcome**

Mobocertinib's 2021 approval was granted under accelerated approval (Subpart H), contingent on the randomized confirmatory trial EXCLAIM-2 verifying clinical benefit. EXCLAIM-2 compared first-line mobocertinib against platinum-based chemotherapy in treatment-naive EGFR exon-20-insertion-positive NSCLC; at its planned interim analysis (data cutoff April 4, 2023), median PFS by BICR was identical in both arms (9.6 months each; HR 1.04, 95% CI 0.77-1.39, P=.803), crossing the pre-specified futility boundary and formally failing the primary endpoint. Takeda subsequently discontinued marketing of Exkivity in the United States; FDA's own Drugs@FDA database lists the product's marketing status as "Discontinued" as of this writing. This is a directly analogous outcome to the "Voluntary withdrawal of an accelerated-approval indication after confirmatory-trial failure" pattern already documented in this census for olaratumab and the durvalumab urothelial indication.

### 139. tisotumab vedotin-tftv (Tivdak) — BLA 761208

**Sponsor:** Seagen Inc. (co-developed with Genmab A/S)

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer with disease progression on or after chemotherapy

**Approval date:** September 20, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** innovaTV 204 / GOG-3023 / ENGOT-cx6, NCT03438396

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial
- *Endpoints:* objective response rate (ORR) / duration of response (DoR), confirmed response (PR or better, confirmed ≥4 weeks later) per RECIST v1.1, IRC-assessed
- *Primary analysis:* one-sided exact binomial test (single-arm ORR hypothesis test); exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval
- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation for missing binary efficacy data (subjects with missing/unconfirmed response counted as non-responders)
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval based on single-arm ORR/DoR, confirmatory trial required; FDA-documented concern about confirmatory-trial enrollment pace

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Single-arm, open-label, multicenter, international Phase 2 trial in patients with recurrent/metastatic cervical cancer previously treated with doublet chemotherapy (with or without bevacizumab); 102 patients enrolled, 101 treated, tisotumab vedotin 2.0 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks
- Primary endpoint: confirmed ORR (CR or PR per RECIST v1.1, IRC-assessed); the sample size of 100 subjects was based on GEN701 first-in-human data (9/34, 26% confirmed responders) and was calculated to provide ≥80% power to reject an ORR of 11% (the combined ORR of available second-line therapies) for true ORRs in the range 21%-25%
- Formal statistical hypothesis: H0: θ≤11% vs. Ha: θ>11%, tested as a one-sided exact binomial test at the 2.5% alpha level, with a two-sided exact 95% Clopper-Pearson CI reported alongside; analysis performed on the Full Analysis Set under an ITT approach, with any subject with missing/unconfirmed response counted as a non-responder
- Result: confirmed ORR 24% (95% CI 16-33%; 7 CR + 17 PR), which excluded the pre-specified 11% null and supported the accelerated-approval decision
- FDA's review recommended accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and duration of response, "with the requirement for verification and description of clinical benefit in confirmatory trials," and separately documented ongoing FDA concern about enrollment pace in the randomized confirmatory trial, innovaTV 301, meeting with the sponsor in 2021 to discuss its accrual status

[DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(21)00056-5>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33845034/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Efficacy%20and%20safety%20of%20tisotumab%20vedotin%20in%20previously%20treated%20recurrent%20or%20metastatic%20cervical%20cancer)

Applying a one-sided exact binomial test at the 0.025 significance level, the planned sample size of 100 subjects provides ≥ 80% power to reject an ORR of 11%, the combined ORR for available second-line therapies... or less for true ORRs in the range 21% - 25%, representing clinically relevant improvements over available second-line treatments."
- *[verbatim, SAP §13.1 "Primary Objective," p.15]* "The following statistical hypotheses will be tested to address the primary efficacy objective: H0: θ ≤ 11% vs. HA: θ > 11%, where θ is the ORR. The test will be performed as an exact test at a one-sided 2.5% alpha level. In addition an exact 95% two-sided confidence interval for the ORR will be provided using the Clopper-Pearson method. The analysis will be performed on the FAS with an ITT approach so that any subjects with missing information regarding response to treatment will be counted as non-responders."
- *[verbatim, SAP §4.8.1 "Primary Endpoint," p.11]* "Any subjects with missing information regarding response to treatment will be counted as non-responders. This also includes subjects with response that cannot be confirmed according to RECIST v1.1 criteria."

### 140. asciminib (Scemblix) — NDA 215358

**Sponsor:** Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation

**Indication approved:** (1) Philadelphia chromosome-positive chronic myeloid leukemia in chronic phase (Ph+ CML-CP) previously treated with two or more tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs); and (2) Ph+ CML-CP with the T315I mutation

**Approval date:** October 29, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** ASCEMBL (Study CABL001A2301), NCT03106779 (indication 1); single-arm Phase 1 dose-expansion cohort of Study CABL001X2101, NCT02081378 (indication 2, T315I, per label — not independently verified against a posted SAP for this entry)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled Phase 3 trial (indication 1); single-arm, open-label trial (indication 2, T315I)
- *Endpoints:* Major Molecular Response (MMR) rate at 24 weeks — a molecular surrogate endpoint defined as BCR-ABL1 ≤0.1% on the International Scale
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test, stratified by baseline major cytogenetic response status; Mantel-Haenszel estimate of the common risk difference with a Wald confidence interval; response rates presented with Pearson-Clopper (exact) 95% CIs
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing — key secondary endpoint (MMR at 96 weeks) tested only if the primary endpoint (MMR at 24 weeks) was statistically significant, via a formal gatekeeping procedure

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ASCEMBL: randomized (2:1), open-label, multicenter Phase 3 trial of asciminib 40 mg BID vs. bosutinib 500 mg QD in Ph+ CML-CP patients previously treated with ≥2 TKIs, stratified by major cytogenetic response (MCyR) status at screening; 233 patients randomized (157 asciminib, 76 bosutinib)
- Primary endpoint: MMR rate at 24 weeks (BCR-ABL1 ≤0.1% by IS), analyzed on the Full Analysis Set (FAS) under an ITT principle; a patient who achieved MMR earlier but lost it by 24 weeks was counted as a non-responder, and patients discontinuing before 24 weeks for any reason were counted as non-responders (with one pre-specified imputation exception when 16- and 36-week PCR both indicated MMR)
- Formal hypothesis: null of no difference in MMR rate at 24 weeks between arms, tested via the CMH chi-square test stratified by the randomization factor (MCyR status), two-sided alpha 0.05; MMR rate and its Pearson-Clopper 95% CI were presented by arm, and the between-arm difference (with 95% Wald CI) via the Mantel-Haenszel estimator
- Key secondary endpoint (MMR at 96 weeks) formally tested at two-sided alpha 0.05 only if the primary endpoint was significant, via a gatekeeping procedure; all other secondary efficacy endpoints (cytogenetic response, time-to-MMR, duration of MMR, time-to-treatment-failure, PFS, OS) were analyzed without formal multiplicity control ("a nominal p-value will be presented for exploratory purposes")
- Result: MMR at 24 weeks was 25.5% with asciminib vs. 13.2% with bosutinib; MCyR-adjusted difference 12.2% (95% CI 2.19-22.30), two-sided P=.029
- Indication 2 (T315I mutation): per the approved label, based on a single-arm cohort of patients with the T315I mutation treated with asciminib 200 mg BID, evaluated for MMR rate with a descriptive point estimate and exact CI (no comparator); this entry did not independently locate and extract a posted SAP for this specific cohort, so its statistical detail here is sourced to the label rather than a primary SAP/protocol document

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2021/215358s000Orig1lbl.pdf

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1182/blood.2020009984), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34407542/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=A%20phase%203%20open-label%20randomized%20study%20of%20asciminib%20a%20STAMP%20inhibitor%20vs%20bosutinib%20in%20CML)

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, combined Protocol/SAP CABL001A2301, §10.4 "Primary objective," p.97]* "The primary objective of the study is to evaluate the efficacy of ABL001 at the recommended dose in CML patients in chronic phase, previously treated with 2 or more tyrosine kinase inhibitors and to compare this efficacy profile in this population with that achieved by patients receiving bosutinib."
- *[verbatim, combined Protocol/SAP CABL001A2301, §10.4.2 "Statistical hypothesis, model, and method of analysis"]* "The MMR rate at 24 weeks will be calculated based on the FAS and according to the Intent To Treat (ITT) principle. MMR rate and its 95% confidence interval based on the Pearson-Clopper method will be presented by treatment group. The confidence interval for the difference in MMR rate between treatment groups will be provided using the Wald method. The null hypothesis is that there is no difference between the treatment groups with respect to MMR rate at 24 weeks. The Cochrane-Mantel-Haenszel chi-square test, stratified by the randomization stratification factor, i.e. major cytogenetic response status (PCyR or CCyR vs others) at screening, will be used to compare MMR rate between the two treatment groups, at the two-sided 5% level of significance. The Mantel-Haenszel estimate of the common risk difference and the corresponding 95% confidence interval will also be provided."
- *[verbatim, combined Protocol/SAP CABL001A2301, §10.5.1.1 "Analysis for key secondary objectives"]* "The null hypothesis is that there is no difference between the treatment groups with respect to MMR rate at 96 weeks. Formal statistical testing of the key secondary endpoint will be performed with α = 0.05 (two-sided) only if the primary endpoint is significant by means of a gatekeeping procedure to control the overall alpha level."
- *[verbatim, combined Protocol/SAP CABL001A2301, §10.5.2 "Other secondary efficacy objectives"]* "No statistical testing of non-key secondary efficacy endpoints will be performed, however a nominal p-value will be presented for exploratory purposes."

### 141. pafolacianine (Cytalux) — NDA 214907

**Sponsor:** On Target Laboratories, LLC

**Indication approved:** Adjunct for intraoperative identification of malignant lesions in patients with ovarian cancer, used with fluorescence imaging under real-time visualization during surgery

**Approval date:** November 29, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** Study OTL-2016-OTL38-006 ("Study 006"), NCT03180307

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* within-patient paired-comparison diagnostic-imaging study — every enrolled patient underwent both standard visualization (normal light/palpation) and fluorescence-guided imaging with the same investigational agent, with detection compared per-lesion within-patient rather than between randomized treatment arms (randomization in this trial governed the imaging system/workflow used, not drug vs. no-drug) — reuses and extends the existing "Diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison)" concept to an intraoperative fluorescence-imaging agent
- *Endpoints:* incremental lesion-detection rate — proportion of patients with at least one evaluable, histologically-confirmed folate-receptor-positive lesion detected by fluorescence imaging but missed by normal light/palpation; patient-level false positive rate (FPRp) as a major secondary endpoint; lesion-level sensitivity and false-positive rate as further secondary/exploratory endpoints
- *Primary analysis:* exact binomial test against a pre-specified performance goal (one-sample test for a proportion, two-tailed alpha 0.05)
- *Regulatory:* regular (not accelerated) approval of an intraoperative diagnostic imaging agent, based on a randomized-workflow, within-patient-comparison Phase 3 trial rather than a treatment-outcome trial

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Phase 3, randomized, single-dose, open-label, multicenter trial; all enrolled patients with known/suspected folate-receptor-positive (FR+) ovarian cancer scheduled for primary cytoreduction, interval debulking, or recurrent-disease surgery received a single IV dose of OTL38 (pafolacianine) prior to surgery, and lesions were assessed intraoperatively first under normal light/palpation and then under fluorescence imaging
- Primary efficacy population: Full Analysis Set (FAS)/modified-ITT — patients exposed to OTL38 who were evaluated under both normal light and fluorescent light and had central pathology confirmation of ≥1 FR+ lesion; analysis was conducted at the evaluable-lesion level within this patient set
- Primary endpoint: proportion of patients with ≥1 additional FR+ ovarian cancer lesion, confirmed by central pathology, detected under the combination of OTL38 and fluorescent light but not detected by palpation/normal-light visualization
- Primary analysis: a one-sample test for a proportion via an exact binomial test, two-tailed alpha 0.05 (against a pre-specified performance goal); no formal comparator arm
- Secondary endpoints included the patient-level false positive rate (FPRp — proportion of FR+ patients in whom all fluorescence-only-detected lesions were histologically negative), reported descriptively with a two-sided 95% Wilson (score) CI, and lesion-level sensitivity/false-positive rate
- Result (per FDA review): estimated sensitivity 97.97% (one-sided lower 95% CI 87.75%); lesion-level false positive rate 32.7%; no major safety concerns identified beyond rare hypersensitivity reactions, attributed by FDA to Cytalux aggregate formation

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

Continuing: "For each subgroup, the point estimate and the exact 95% CI for the primary efficacy endpoint will be provided."
