### 142. tebentafusp-tebn (Kimmtrak) — BLA 761228

**Sponsor:** Immunocore Ltd.

**Indication approved:** HLA-A*02:01-positive adult patients with unresectable or metastatic uveal melanoma

**Approval date:** January 25, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** IMCgp100-202, NCT03070392

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled Phase 2 trial (2:1 randomization vs. investigator's choice); dual-analysis-population design with independent alpha allocation to an Intent-to-Treat (ITT) set and a "Randomized-and-Started" (RAS) set to address immortal-time bias in the experimental arm
- *Endpoints:* overall survival (OS, primary); progression-free survival (PFS) and best overall response (BOR) as key secondary endpoints tested in a fixed sequence
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test (by baseline LDH status); Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified by LDH) with the Efron approach for ties; Kaplan-Meier estimation; Brookmeyer-Crowley method (applied to median follow-up time via the reverse-Kaplan-Meier method)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design with two formal interim analyses (at ~60% and ~80% of planned OS events) using O'Brien-Fleming-type boundaries implemented via the Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function; overall alpha of 0.05 split as α=0.045 (ITT) / α=0.005 (RAS), with provision to recycle the RAS alpha into the ITT analysis if the RAS boundary was crossed
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (OS → PFS → BOR for the ITT analyses)
- *Regulatory:* regular approval based on OS from a randomized Phase 2 trial (not a dedicated Phase 3) — first FDA-approved T-cell receptor (TCR) bispecific therapy

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Randomized (2:1), open-label, multicenter Phase 2 trial of tebentafusp vs. investigator's choice (pembrolizumab, ipilimumab, or dacarbazine) in HLA-A*02:01-positive, previously untreated metastatic uveal melanoma patients, stratified by baseline LDH (≤ vs. > ULN, 250 U/L); 378 patients randomized (252 tebentafusp, 126 control)
- Primary endpoint: overall survival, powered assuming a design HR of 0.645 (89% power, 250 deaths required, two-sided alpha 0.045 for the ITT analysis after allocation)
- A parallel, independently-alpha-allocated RAS ("Randomized-and-Started") analysis set and boundary (α=0.005) were pre-specified specifically to guard against immortal-time bias arising because tebentafusp-arm patients had to survive an initial dose-titration period to be eligible for the RAS population; a rule allowed the ITT alpha to absorb the full RAS alpha if the RAS boundary was crossed first
- Interim monitoring: two formal interim OS analyses at ~60% (150 events) and ~80% (200 events) of the 250 total planned events, using O'Brien-Fleming boundaries approximated via the Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function; stopping boundaries were pre-tabulated by information fraction for both the RAS and ITT analysis sets
- Multiple-testing control: OS, then key secondary endpoints PFS and BOR, tested in a fixed sequence for the ITT analyses; PFS and BOR were not tested at interim looks and were each tested at the overall alpha (0.045, or 0.05 if RAS alpha was recycled) only after OS was significant
- Primary analysis: two-sided stratified log-rank test (by LDH) for the p-value; HR estimated via a stratified Cox proportional-hazards model using the Efron method for tied event times, with profile-likelihood 95% CIs; median follow-up time (and its CI) estimated via the reverse Kaplan-Meier method with the Brookmeyer-Crowley/log-log-transformation approach
- Result (primary analysis): 1-year OS 73% (tebentafusp) vs. 59% (control), HR 0.51 (95% CI 0.37-0.71), P<0.001; PFS at 6 months 31% vs. 19%, HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.58-0.94), P=0.01
- FDA's review concludes the OS result "supports regular approval for this indication," notwithstanding the trial's Phase 2 label — the first regular approval in this census's oncology set to rest on OS from a randomized Phase 2 (rather than a dedicated Phase 3) trial, matching the pattern already documented for glasdegib

Assuming a 2:1 randomization ratio of tebentafusp vs. Investigator Choice, 250 events (deaths) are needed in the randomized trial to provide 89% power to detect a difference of survival distribution that can be characterized by a 0.645 hazard ratio (HR) for OS with a 2-sided significance level of 0.045... The Lan-DeMets approach... that approximates the O'Brien-Fleming spending function will be used... α=0.045 will be devoted to the ITT analyses and α=0.005 will be devoted to analyses in the RAS, thereby controlling the overall experiment-wise error rate at 0.05."

### 143. pacritinib (Vonjo) — NDA 208712

**Sponsor:** CTI BioPharma Corp. (subsequently acquired by Sobi)

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with intermediate- or high-risk primary or secondary (post-polycythemia vera or post-essential thrombocythemia) myelofibrosis with a platelet count below 50 x 10⁹/L

**Approval date:** February 28, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** PERSIST-2, NCT02055781

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled Phase 3 trial (pacritinib vs. best available therapy, including ruxolitinib); post-clinical-hold, safety-restricted approval narrowing the indication to a severe-thrombocytopenia subgroup
- *Endpoints:* co-primary spleen-volume-reduction (SVR35, ≥35% reduction by imaging) and symptom-score-reduction (TSS50, ≥50% reduction in Total Symptom Score) responder-rate endpoints, standard in myelofibrosis trials of this era
- *Primary analysis:* responder-proportion comparison between arms, most likely via a chi-square or Fisher's exact-type test (method inferred from the label/publication — no posted SAP was located; see Reverse-engineered SAP below)
- *Regulatory:* accelerated/restricted approval following a prior full clinical hold; label restricted to platelet count <50 x 10⁹/L, a narrower population than the original PERSIST-2 all-comer thrombocytopenic enrollment criterion

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Randomized, open-label Phase 3 trial in patients with myelofibrosis (any subtype) and thrombocytopenia (platelet count <100 x 10⁹/L), randomizing pacritinib 200 mg BID vs. best available therapy (BAT, which could include ruxolitinib) in a 1:1 ratio; 311 patients randomized
- Co-primary endpoints (per label/publication): proportion of patients achieving ≥35% spleen volume reduction (SVR35) at Week 24 by MRI/CT, and proportion achieving ≥50% reduction in Total Symptom Score (TSS50) at Week 24 by patient-reported symptom diary
- FDA had previously placed a full clinical hold on all pacritinib trials in February 2016 after safety signals (increased rates of cardiac events, bleeding, and death) emerged in this era of JAK-inhibitor development for myelofibrosis; the hold was lifted in 2019, and the eventual approval restricted the label to patients with platelet counts below 50 x 10⁹/L (a severe-thrombocytopenia subgroup of the broader PERSIST-2 enrollment population, in which ruxolitinib and other JAK inhibitors are often not usable or tolerated), rather than the full PERSIST-2 population
- No FDA combined statistical/clinical review package or sponsor SAP/protocol was located publicly posted for this NDA (Drugs@FDA's overview page lists only the approval letter and label; the ClinicalTrials.gov record for PERSIST-2 has no posted `documentSection`) — this entry's methodological detail is therefore reconstructed from the label and the pivotal publication rather than sourced to a primary SAP or FDA review document

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2022/208712Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2022/208712s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical/Clinical Review or combined Multi-Discipline Review: not found publicly posted for this NDA
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02055781
- Protocol / SAP: not posted on ClinicalTrials.gov (no `documentSection` present in the record)
- Pivotal publication: Mascarenhas J, Hoffman R, Talpaz M, et al. "Pacritinib vs Best Available Therapy, Including Ruxolitinib, in Patients With Myelofibrosis: A Randomized Clinical Trial." *JAMA Oncol.* 2018;4(5):652-659. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1001/jamaoncol.2017.5818), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29522138/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Pacritinib%20vs%20Best%20Available%20Therapy%20Including%20Ruxolitinib%20in%20Patients%20With%20Myelofibrosis)

**Other resources**

- CTI BioPharma/Sobi's participation in a formal IPD-sharing program (Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere) was not identified for this trial.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was identified for this approval, though the drug's clinical-hold history was the subject of extensive FDA safety review during the hold period (2016-2019).

**Reverse-engineered SAP**

- *[inferred, from the approved label's efficacy tables and the JAMA Oncology publication]* The primary analysis population was most likely the intent-to-treat population (all randomized patients), with SVR35 and TSS50 response status at Week 24 treated as binary responder endpoints and missing/non-evaluable assessments counted as non-responders — this is the near-universal convention for spleen-volume/symptom-score responder endpoints in myelofibrosis trials of this era (e.g., ruxolitinib's COMFORT trials, both already documented in this census, used Fisher's exact and CMH tests for exactly this endpoint type), and PERSIST-2 is described in the label as reporting SVR35/TSS50 responder proportions by arm with no indication of a time-to-event or continuous-change primary analysis.
- *[inferred, from the co-primary-endpoint structure]* A split-alpha or Bonferroni-type allocation across the two co-primary endpoints (SVR35 and TSS50) was likely pre-specified, consistent with regulatory convention for dual spleen/symptom co-primary endpoints in this drug class, though the exact allocation (e.g., 0.025/0.025 vs. some other split) could not be confirmed without a posted SAP.
- *[inferred, from the restricted final label population]* The approved label's restriction to platelet count <50 x 10⁹/L (narrower than PERSIST-2's <100 x 10⁹/L enrollment criterion) implies FDA's review concluded that the efficacy/safety balance was favorable only in the more severely thrombocytopenic subgroup — consistent with a subgroup analysis by baseline platelet count being a key part of FDA's actual (but non-public) statistical review, analogous to subgroup-driven label narrowing documented elsewhere in this census, but the specific subgroup statistical methodology is not independently confirmed here.

### 144. nivolumab and relatlimab-rmbw (Opdualag) — BLA 761234

**Sponsor:** Bristol-Myers Squibb Company

**Indication approved:** Adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age or older with unresectable or metastatic melanoma

**Approval date:** March 18, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** RELATIVITY-047 (Study CA224-047), NCT03470922

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, active-controlled Phase 2/3 trial; adaptive seamless Phase 2-to-3 design with a blinded, DMC-reviewed interim go/no-go decision on whether to continue enrollment into Phase 3
- *Endpoints:* progression-free survival (PFS, primary, BICR-assessed per RECIST v1.1); objective response rate (ORR) and overall survival (OS) as secondary endpoints subject to the same testing hierarchy
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test; Cox proportional-hazards model with treatment, PD-L1, and other baseline covariates
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design (Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function approximating an O'Brien-Fleming boundary for the OS analyses); a separate, non-alpha-spending interim PFS analysis (at ~400 randomized patients / ≥150 BICR PFS events) used solely to decide whether to expand enrollment from the planned Phase 2 N=400 to the full Phase 3 N=700
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (PFS, then OS interim/final analyses contingent on PFS significance, per a pre-specified hierarchical procedure with group-sequential testing)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Randomized (1:1), double-blind, multicenter Phase 2/3 trial of a fixed-dose combination of relatlimab (anti-LAG-3) and nivolumab (anti-PD-1) vs. nivolumab monotherapy in previously untreated, unresectable Stage III/IV melanoma; stratified by PD-L1 expression (≥1% vs. <1%), LAG-3 expression (≥1% vs. <1%), BRAF mutation status, and AJCC M-stage; 714 patients ultimately randomized
- Adaptive design: the trial began as a Phase 2 study (planned N=400) with a single blinded interim PFS analysis (conducted by an external analysis team to preserve sponsor blinding) triggered at ~400 randomized patients with 12 weeks' minimum follow-up or ≥150 BICR PFS events; a positive result per the DMC charter's pre-specified criteria triggered continuation into the Phase 3 portion (an additional 300 patients, for ~700 total) rather than unblinding or stopping
- Primary endpoint: PFS by BICR per RECIST v1.1; final Phase 2 PFS analysis (if the study had stopped at Phase 2) was planned at 183 events, and the final (Phase 3) PFS analysis at 365 BICR PFS events
- Primary analysis: two-sided, stratified log-rank test among all randomized subjects for the primary PFS comparison, with the HR estimated via a stratified Cox proportional-hazards model (exact method for ties); a pre-specified fixed-sequence hierarchy tested PFS first, then (contingent on PFS significance) OS via group-sequential interim/final analyses using an O'Brien-Fleming-type boundary implemented with the Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function
- Result: median PFS 10.1 months (relatlimab-nivolumab) vs. 4.6 months (nivolumab), HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.62-0.92), P=0.006 by stratified log-rank test; 12-month PFS 47.7% vs. 36.0%

### 145. lutetium Lu 177 vipivotide tetraxetan (Pluvicto) — NDA 215833

**Sponsor:** Advanced Accelerator Applications USA, Inc., a Novartis company (drug developed by Endocyte, Inc., subsequently acquired by Novartis)

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with PSMA-positive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) who have been treated with androgen receptor pathway inhibition and taxane-based chemotherapy

**Approval date:** March 23, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** VISION (Study PSMA-617-01), NCT03511664

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled Phase 3 trial; co-primary endpoints (radiographic progression-free survival, rPFS, and overall survival, OS)
- *Endpoints:* radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS, per PCWG3-modified RECIST criteria) and overall survival (OS), co-primary
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test; Cox proportional-hazards model with covariates
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design with an interim OS analysis conducted contemporaneously with the primary rPFS analysis, plus a final OS analysis; alpha recycling — the final-analysis alpha for OS was raised or held depending on whether the rPFS and interim-OS results individually crossed their own pre-specified boundaries
- *Missing data/bias:* attrition bias — a high, differential early dropout/withdrawal-of-consent rate in the best-supportive-care-only control arm, addressed by a mid-trial redefinition of the primary rPFS analysis population to patients randomized on or after a specified date, following remedial site-level measures

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Randomized (2:1), open-label, international, multicenter Phase 3 trial of ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 plus best standard of care (BSoC) vs. BSoC alone in PSMA-PET-positive mCRPC patients previously treated with ≥1 androgen-receptor-pathway inhibitor and 1-2 taxane regimens; 831 of 1,179 screened patients randomized (originally planned N=750, later increased to N=814 as part of the remedial redesign described below)
- Co-primary endpoints: rPFS (by blinded independent central review, PCWG3-modified RECIST v1.1) and OS
- Sample-size/design assumptions: under the null, median rPFS 4 months / median OS 10 months on BSoC alone; under the alternative, median rPFS 6 months (HR 0.67) / median OS 13.7 months (HR 0.7306); the design targeted 364 rPFS events (84% power at 1-sided alpha 0.004) and 508 deaths (≥90% power at 1-sided alpha ≥0.020) for OS
- Mid-trial design amendment: shortly after the trial began, FDA's review and the sponsor's SAP both document "a high, early dropout rate amongst those randomized to BSC/BSoC only," with "the majority of these dropouts withdrawing consent to follow-up," which "consequently could result in bias in the analysis of rPFS." Remedial measures took effect 5-Mar-2019, and — rather than simply continuing — the primary analysis of rPFS was redefined to include only patients prospectively randomized on or after that date (~557 of the eventual 814 randomized patients), while the OS analysis (interim and final) remained ITT and included all randomized patients regardless of randomization date; total planned enrollment was increased from 750 to 814 to preserve the originally-powered treatment-effect assumptions
- Alpha allocation across the co-primary/interim structure: rPFS tested at 1-sided alpha 0.004 (364 events); a contemporaneous interim OS analysis tested at 1-sided alpha 0.001 (341 expected deaths); the alpha available for the final OS analysis (508 deaths) then depended combinatorially on whether the rPFS and interim-OS results individually crossed their respective boundaries, ranging from 0.020 (if neither crossed) up to 0.025 (1-sided, if both crossed) — a within-trial alpha-recycling scheme conceptually similar to, but structurally more elaborate than, the alpha-recycling rule already documented in this census for dapagliflozin/DECLARE-TIMI58
- Result: rPFS 8.7 vs. 3.4 months (HR 0.40, 99.2% CI 0.29-0.57, P<0.001); OS 15.3 vs. 11.3 months (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.52-0.74, P<0.001)
- FDA's review explicitly flags the open-label design and differential dropout as limitations: "Open-label trial designs can lead to bias... A high rate of dropout was noted on VISION during the trial, and the Applicant met with the FDA to discuss considerable withdrawal of consent and disproportionate dropout in the BSoC only (control) [arm]"

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2107322), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34161051/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Lutetium-177-PSMA-617%20for%20Metastatic%20Castration-Resistant%20Prostate%20Cancer)

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, SAP §"Study design update," p.9]* "The trial was originally designed to randomize 750 patients, targeting the primary analysis of rPFS with 457 events, an interim analysis of Overall Survival (OS), to be conducted contemporaneously with the primary analysis of rPFS, and a final analysis of OS with 489 deaths. However, shortly after commencement of the trial, a high, early dropout rate amongst those randomized to BSC/BSoC only became evident with the majority of these dropouts withdrawing consent to follow-up. This meant that rPFS data could not be collected for these patients which consequently could result in bias in the analysis of rPFS. Remedial measures to curtail this phenomenon were implemented and made effective on 5-Mar-2019. As part of the plan to address the early withdrawal of consent in the BSC/BSoC-only arm, the primary analysis of rPFS was altered to focus on patients prospectively randomized on or after 5-Mar-2019... To achieve these analyses, the total number of subjects randomized into the trial was increased from N=750 to N=814."
- *[verbatim, SAP §3.4 "Sample Size Justification," p.11]* "The alpha level applicable to OS in the final analysis will depend upon the earlier rPFS and interim OS results: if p<0.004 1-sided is achieved for rPFS and p<0.001 1-sided is achieved for interim OS, then the alpha level for the final analysis of OS will be raised to 0.025 1-sided. If p<0.004 1-sided is achieved for rPFS but p<0.001 1-sided is not achieved for interim OS, then the alpha level for the final analysis of OS will be 0.024 1-sided. If p<0.004 1-sided is not achieved for rPFS but p<0.001 1-sided is achieved for interim OS, then the alpha level for the final analysis of OS will be raised to 0.021 1-sided. If p<0.004 1-sided is not achieved for rPFS and p<0.001 1-sided is not achieved for interim OS, then the alpha level for the final analysis of OS will remain at 0.020 1-sided."

A high rate of dropout was noted on VISION during the trial, and the Applicant met with the FDA to discuss considerable withdrawal of consent and disproportionate dropout in the BSoC only (control) [arm]... Open-label trial designs can lead to bias."

### 146. eflapegrastim (Rolvedon) — BLA 761148

**Sponsor:** Spectrum Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** To decrease the incidence of infection, as manifested by febrile neutropenia, in adult patients with non-myeloid malignancies receiving myelosuppressive anti-cancer drugs associated with a clinically significant incidence of febrile neutropenia

**Approval date:** September 9, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** Two co-pivotal Phase 3 trials — Study SPI-GCF-301 / "ADVANCE" (NCT02643420) and Study SPI-GCF-302 / "RECOVER" (NCT02953340)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, open-label, active-controlled (pegfilgrastim as the active comparator rather than placebo); two co-pivotal replicate non-inferiority trials required because FDA told the sponsor a single pivotal trial "may not be sufficient evidence for approval of a marketing application of a supportive care drug"
- *Endpoints:* Duration of severe neutropenia (DSN) in Cycle 1 — primary in both trials, defined as number of days with ANC <0.5×10^9/L after study-drug administration, with patients who never developed severe neutropenia assigned DSN=0, a continuous hematologic-toxicity surrogate endpoint); key secondaries were time to ANC recovery, depth of ANC nadir, and incidence of febrile neutropenia in Cycle 1, all descriptive only per FDA's regulatory history ("the planned analyses of Time to ANC Recovery and Depth of ANC Nadir would not support a labeling claim for these two outcomes")
- *Primary analysis:* Bootstrap resampling method (10,000 samples, treatment as sole stratification factor) used to construct the 2-sided 95% CI around the between-arm difference in mean DSN, because DSN's distribution (small non-negative integers, heavily zero-inflated) is skewed; non-inferiority declared if the upper bound of that 95% CI was <0.62 days; Poisson and negative-binomial regression used as sensitivity analyses
- *Missing data/bias:* Asymmetric worst-case-scenario imputation — missing ANC values between Day 5 and ANC recovery were imputed as ANC<0.5×10^9/L (severe neutropenia) for the eflapegrastim arm but as ANC≥0.5×10^9/L (recovered) for the pegfilgrastim arm
- *Regulatory:* Special Protocol Assessment (SPA), formally amended pre-unblinding (FDA's December 15, 2015 SPA letter for SPI-GCF-301/ADVANCE was later modified by a March 16, 2017 written agreement that cut the per-arm sample size from 290 to 200 and changed the significance level from 0.5% to 2.5%, without rescinding the SPA); Complete Response Letter issued August 3, 2021 after the first review cycle, approved on resubmission, scaled down "in order to maintain the results of the randomized trials comparing DSN of pegfilgrastim (Neulasta) to Neupogen which led to the approval of Neulasta"

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Two separately protocoled, near-identical Phase 3 trials in early-stage breast cancer patients receiving docetaxel 75 mg/m2 + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m2 (TC) every 21 days for up to 4 cycles: ADVANCE (SPI-GCF-301, NCT02643420, n=406, randomized 1:1, stratified only by site) and RECOVER (SPI-GCF-302, NCT02953340, n=237, randomized 1:1 via IWRS permuted-block design, block size 4 per country); both open-label, active-controlled (pegfilgrastim 6 mg vs. eflapegrastim 13.2 mg, both given SC on Day 2 of each cycle, roughly 24-26 hours after chemotherapy)
- Primary endpoint (both trials): duration of severe neutropenia (DSN) in Cycle 1, i.e., number of days with ANC<0.5×10^9/L after study-drug dosing; patients who never developed severe neutropenia were assigned DSN=0; if multiple same-day ANC values existed, the last value of the day was used
- Key secondary endpoints (Cycle 1): time to ANC recovery (to ≥1.5×10^9/L after nadir), depth of ANC nadir, incidence of febrile neutropenia (oral temp >38.3°C, or two readings ≥38.0°C two hours apart, with ANC<1.0×10^9/L); additional secondaries included DSN in Cycles 2-4, neutropenic complications, febrile neutropenia in Cycles 2-4, and relative dose intensity of TC chemotherapy
- Sample size: ADVANCE was designed assuming pooled SD of DSN = 2.0 days (referencing the two original pegfilgrastim registrational trials, which used SDs of 2.17 and 1.5 days) with true mean difference assumed 0; 200 patients/arm gave 87% power for a one-sided, two-sample t-test at 2.5% one-sided alpha against a 0.62-day non-inferiority margin; this margin was set by FDA (not the sponsor's originally proposed 1.0-day margin) specifically to preserve the statistical logic of the original pegfilgrastim-vs-filgrastim non-inferiority showing; RECOVER used pooled SD=1.5 days (monitored from the concurrently running ADVANCE trial) for a planned n=218 (109/arm, 86% power); FDA required the two-trial design because a single trial "may not be sufficient evidence for approval of a marketing application of a supportive care drug"
- Statistical method: primary analysis used bootstrap resampling (10,000 samples per the SAP) to build a 2-sided 95% CI on the ITT-population mean DSN difference (eflapegrastim minus pegfilgrastim), because DSN's distribution is discrete, right-skewed, and zero-inflated; Poisson/negative-binomial regression and a per-protocol analysis served as sensitivity analyses; a pre-specified worst-case-scenario sensitivity analysis imputed missing post-Day-5 ANC values asymmetrically against the investigational arm only
- Results: both trials independently met the non-inferiority criterion — ADVANCE: DSN difference -0.148 days, 95% CI (-0.265, -0.033); RECOVER: DSN difference -0.073 days, 95% CI (-0.292, 0.129) — both upper bounds below the 0.62-day margin; secondary endpoints (ANC recovery time, nadir depth, febrile neutropenia incidence) showed no significant between-arm differences in either trial

### 147. futibatinib (Lytgobi) — NDA 214801

**Sponsor:** Taiho Oncology, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adults with previously treated, unresectable locally advanced or metastatic intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma harboring a fibroblast growth factor receptor 2 (FGFR2) gene fusion or other rearrangement — approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate and duration of response

**Approval date:** September 30, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** TAS-120-101 / FOENIX-CCA2, NCT02052778 (Phase 1/2, cholangiocarcinoma expansion cohort)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label, multi-cohort Phase 1/2 basket trial (dose-escalation followed by Phase 1 expansion across 8 disease groups) supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H/21 CFR 314.500; biomarker-selected/enriched population (FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement, 78% fusions/22% other rearrangements); sample-size logic based on ruling out a historical control response rate
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR, primary — confirmed CR or PR per RECIST 1.1, blinded independent central review); duration of response (DOR, key secondary); disease control rate (DCR, FDA classified as exploratory and "not supportive of registration"); progression-free survival and overall survival (secondary, explicitly noted by FDA as "not interpretable in a single arm study")
- *Primary analysis:* Exact 95% binomial confidence interval (Clopper-Pearson) around ORR in the Efficacy Population; design-stage exact-binomial power calculation (81% power to rule out a 10% historical control ORR by the lower bound of the 95% CI, assuming a 20% target response rate, approximately 100 patients planned)
- *Missing data/bias:* Not applicable in the randomized-trial sense (no comparator/crossover); DOR and PFS censored per FDA 2007 Guidance for Cancer Trial Endpoints conventions; non-responder imputation for patients without a confirmed response by data cutoff
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval (Subpart H) based on ORR/DOR as a surrogate reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit; postmarketing requirement for a randomized confirmatory trial comparing futibatinib 20 mg vs. 16 mg daily to verify clinical benefit and characterize dose-response; postmarketing commitment to develop a companion diagnostic (none was FDA-approved and linked to futibatinib at time of approval); no FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting held, as FDA identified no review issues raising significant public-health risk-benefit questions

**Trial design & endpoints**

- TAS-120-101 (FOENIX-CCA2): open-label, multicenter, multi-part Phase 1/2 trial of futibatinib (TAS-120) in patients with advanced solid tumors harboring FGF/FGFR aberrations; the Phase 1 Expansion enrolled patients across 8 disease groups at 20 mg QD, with the cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) cohort (combining disease groups 1-4) as "Cohort 1" and the approval-relevant population being 103 patients with previously treated, FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement-positive intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma who received at least one dose
- Primary endpoint: ORR, defined as the proportion of patients with a confirmed (per RECIST 1.1 confirmation rules requiring a minimum 4-week interval between assessments) best overall response of CR or PR; per protocol, ORR for CCA and CNS-tumor cohorts was based on independent central (Core Imaging Laboratory/IRC) review, while other tumor-type cohorts used investigator assessment
- Sample-size/power logic: the study was designed to have 81% power to rule out a historical control response rate of 10% (based on published second-line iCCA chemotherapy response rates) by the lower limit of the 95% CI, assuming a target futibatinib response rate of 20%; approximately 100 patients were planned for the iCCA/FGFR2 fusion-positive cohort
- Secondary endpoints: duration of response (time from first confirmed response to progression or death, Kaplan-Meier estimation, FDA 2007 Guidance censoring rules), disease control rate (CR+PR+SD without confirmation requirement, Clopper-Pearson 95% CI), progression-free survival and overall survival (Kaplan-Meier estimation); results were also broken out by FGFR2 fusion vs. other rearrangement, and by prior FGFR inhibitor exposure
- Efficacy results supporting approval: among 103 patients, the centrally reviewed (IRC) ORR was 42% (95% CI 32-52%), all responses were partial responses, exceeding the pre-specified 20% target and clearing the 10% historical-control margin; median DOR was 9.07 months (95% CI 7.6, 17.7), with 72% of responders maintaining response ≥6 months
- Safety: near-universal hyperphosphatemia (97% of the 103-patient iCCA cohort, an on-target FGFR-inhibitor class effect managed with dietary phosphate binders), plus ocular toxicity — notably retinal pigment epithelial detachment (9% across 318 futibatinib-treated patients, with FDA noting the true incidence is likely underestimated because OCT was not performed systematically in all patients) — leading to a recommended ophthalmologic/OCT monitoring schedule

- FDA Approval Letter (corrected) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2022/214801Orig1s000Correctedltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/214801Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 5053333, NDA 214801, Statistical Reviewer Sirisha Mushti) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/214801Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (TAS-120-101) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02052778 (Study Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan both posted in the Documents tab)
- Protocol / SAP — Study Protocol: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/78/NCT02052778/Prot_000.pdf; Statistical Analysis Plan (Phase I Expansion, v2.0, protocol version 25 OCT 2019, finalized 15 Oct 2020): https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/78/NCT02052778/SAP_001.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Goyal L, Meric-Bernstam F, Hollebecque A, et al. "Futibatinib for FGFR2-Rearranged Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma." *N Engl J Med.* 2023;388(3):228-239. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2206834), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36652354/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Futibatinib%20for%20FGFR2-Rearranged%20Intrahepatic%20Cholangiocarcinoma)

**Other resources**

- Taiho Oncology's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for TAS-120-101; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for this trial.
- No FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held; FDA's review states no issues were identified "that raised significant public health questions regarding the risk:benefit assessment of futibatinib for the proposed indication," noting futibatinib was the fourth in-class FGFR inhibitor reviewed and the third specifically for FGFR2-altered iCCA.
- Postmarketing requirements: a randomized trial comparing futibatinib 20 mg vs. 16 mg daily to verify clinical benefit and characterize the dose-response relationship; further characterization of ocular toxicity; a pediatric-population study; and a postmarketing commitment to develop a companion diagnostic test.

The blinding/unblinding is not applicable in this study. Primary endpoints for CCA and CNS patients, ORR will be based on the independent review of images by the Core Imaging Laboratory according to the RECIST 1.1. For the other tumor types, ORR will be based on investigators assessment."

The 95% confidence interval (binomial proportion confidence interval) for ORR will be constructed with Clopper-Pearson 95% CI. The ORR summary based on Independent Review will be presented for iCCA patients by the 4 categories of: with FGFR2 rearrangement, without FGFR2 rearrangement, with FGFR2 rearrangement with GEM/CIS and without FGFRi Prior Treatment, with FGFR2 rearrangement with FGFRi prior treatment."

### 148. tremelimumab (Imjudo) — BLA 761289

**Sponsor:** AstraZeneca

**Indication approved:** In combination with durvalumab, for the treatment of adults with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC)

**Approval date:** October 21, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** HIMALAYA (Study D419CC00002), NCT03298451

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, open-label, active-controlled (sorafenib as the active comparator); event-driven trial; originally a four-arm design (tremelimumab 75 mg + durvalumab [T75+D], tremelimumab 300 mg single priming dose + durvalumab [T300+D, the "STRIDE" regimen], durvalumab monotherapy [D], sorafenib [S]) that dropped the T75+D arm mid-trial and restructured to a dual-primary/hierarchical design after an interim analysis from a separate companion trial (Study 22) suggested inferior tolerability/activity for the lower tremelimumab dose
- *Endpoints:* Overall survival (OS, primary for T300+D vs. sorafenib; key secondary for durvalumab-monotherapy non-inferiority, then superiority, vs. sorafenib); OS at 36 months (further key secondary, alpha-gated); objective response rate, progression-free survival, duration of response, disease control rate (secondary/supportive; investigator-assessed per RECIST 1.1)
- *Primary analysis:* Stratified log-rank test and stratified Cox proportional-hazards model for OS (stratified by macrovascular invasion/extrahepatic spread, ECOG status, and region); Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence hierarchical testing (H1 T300+D superiority → H2 durvalumab non-inferiority → H3 durvalumab superiority → OS36), with alpha recycling contingent on each prior hypothesis's success; non-inferiority margin of HR 1.08 derived via a 95%-95% fixed-margin approach from two historical randomized sorafenib trials (pooled HR 0.686); an earlier protocol version had specified a Dunnett and Tamhane step-up procedure for the two original key secondary OS comparisons before the design was restructured around the T75+D arm closure
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Group-sequential design with two interim analyses (IA1 for ORR, IA2 and FA for OS) and Lan-DeMets alpha-spending approximating O'Brien-Fleming; 0.1% (2-sided) alpha spent on an interim ORR/DoR look, remaining 4.9% spent across the OS analyses
- *Regulatory:* FDA did not refer the application to ODAC, stating "no significant review issues were identified during the review of this application"; FDA's efficacy conclusion rested on the T300+D-vs-sorafenib comparison, treating the durvalumab-vs-sorafenib comparison and single-agent tremelimumab data (from the companion Study 22) as supportive only

**Trial design & endpoints**

- HIMALAYA (D419CC00002): randomized, open-label, global Phase III trial in patients with unresectable HCC, no prior systemic therapy, and not eligible for locoregional therapy; the original four-arm design (T75+D, T300+D, D, S) discontinued the T75+D arm via Amendment 4 after an interim analysis of a separate, ongoing companion study (Study 22, D419CC00022) indicated inferior tolerability/activity relative to T300+D, at which point the primary efficacy endpoints were restructured into the dual-primary design retained at approval (OS of T300+D vs. S; OS of D vs. S as key secondary)
- Primary efficacy objective: whether OS with T300+D (a one-time 300 mg tremelimumab dose plus durvalumab 1500 mg in cycle 1, then durvalumab 1500 mg Q4W) differs from OS with sorafenib in the full analysis set (FAS); key secondary objectives, tested only if the primary succeeds, are non-inferiority (margin HR 1.08) of durvalumab monotherapy vs. sorafenib, then (if non-inferiority holds) superiority of durvalumab vs. sorafenib, then (if both succeed) a further comparison of 36-month OS rates between T300+D and sorafenib
- Sample size/power: assumed an average HR of 0.70 for T300+D vs. sorafenib (median OS 11.5 to 16.5 months, 18-month OS rate 33.8% to 46.8%); approximately 404 OS events (~52% maturity) at the second interim analysis gave at least 85% power at a 2-sided 2.22% significance level, and approximately 515 events (~67% maturity) at final analysis gave at least 97% power at 4.25%; the durvalumab-vs-sorafenib non-inferiority comparison (margin HR 1.08, derived via a 95%-95% fixed-margin approach from the SHARP and Asian-Pacific sorafenib trials) was powered at approximately 84% assuming HR 0.84 with about 560 events
- Statistical methods: stratified log-rank test and stratified Cox model for OS; Lan-DeMets alpha-spending (approximating O'Brien-Fleming) across the two OS analyses; fixed-sequence hierarchical/gated testing with alpha recycling — the full 4.9% (2-sided) alpha assigned to H1 is recycled to H2, then to H3, then to OS36, only if each prior hypothesis in the chain succeeds
- Results: T300+D reduced risk of death vs. sorafenib (stratified HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.66-0.92, stratified log-rank 2-sided p=0.0035); investigator-assessed ORR was 20.1% with T300+D vs. 17.0% with durvalumab monotherapy, with median DoR 22.34 months (T300+D) vs. 16.82 months (D); single-agent tremelimumab (from the supportive Study 22) had only 7.2% ORR but a median OS of 17.05 months similar to T300+D, which FDA's review states means "the limited ORR in patients receiving tremelimumab does not preclude an OS benefit"

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2022/761289s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 5064925, BLA 761289 and sBLA 761069, Statistical Reviewer Jiaxin Fan) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/761289Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (HIMALAYA) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03298451 (Study Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan both posted in the Documents tab)
- Protocol / SAP — Study Protocol (v16.0): https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/51/NCT03298451/Prot_016.pdf; Statistical Analysis Plan (Edition 4.0, 30 Jul 2021): https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/51/NCT03298451/SAP_018.pdf

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/EVIDoa2100070), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38319892/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Tremelimumab%20plus%20Durvalumab%20in%20Unresectable%20Hepatocellular%20Carcinoma)

**Other resources**

- AstraZeneca's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for HIMALAYA; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for this specific trial.
- No FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held; FDA's review states "no significant review issues were identified during the review of this application."
- HIMALAYA's discontinued T75+D arm is reported only descriptively, separate from the formal hypothesis tests, since no interim efficacy analysis was conducted specifically within HIMALAYA when that arm was dropped (the decision was driven by results from the separate Study 22).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, HIMALAYA (D419CC00002) Statistical Analysis Plan, Edition 4.0, 30 Jul 2021, §1.1 Study objectives]* — "The primary objective is to test Hypothesis 1 (H1); i.e., whether subject's OS when randomized to receive durvalumab plus tremelimumab (Arm C) is significantly different than the OS of subjects randomized to receive sorafenib (Arm D) in the full analysis set (FAS). The key secondary objectives are to first test H2; i.e., whether subject's OS when randomized to receive durvalumab monotherapy (Arm A) is not inferior to the OS of subjects randomized to receive sorafenib (Arm D) with NI margin of 1.08 in the FAS, and then test H3."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "No formal efficacy analysis will be conducted for Arm B, durvalumab plus tremelimumab combination therapy arm, which was closed for enrolment with Amendment 4. Instead, results for Arm B will be summarized descriptively and separately from other study arms."

*[verbatim, same source, §3 Sample Size, Arm C vs Arm D]* — "At the time of IA2, the analysis of OS will be performed when approximately 404 OS events in Arm C and Arm D combined (~52% maturity) have occurred... This number of OS events will provide at least 85% power to demonstrate a statistically significant difference in OS at a 2 sided 2.22% significance level. At the time of FA, the analysis of OS will be performed when approximately 515 events in Arm C and Arm D combined (~67% maturity) have occurred... This number of OS events will provide at least 97% power to demonstrate a statistically significant difference in OS at a 2 sided 4.25% significance level."

*[verbatim, same source, non-inferiority margin justification]* — "The statistical margin of 1.21 (M1) and clinical noninferiority margin (M2) of HR 1.08 are determined using 95%-95% fixed margin approach (FDA Guidance 2016; EMEA Guideline 2005) based on two phase 3 trials of sorafenib (Llovet 2008a and Cheng 2009) in first-line HCC and assuming conservative 60% retention."

*[verbatim, same source, §4.2.1 Multiplicity]* — "To strongly control the familywise error rate (FWER) at the 5% level (2-sided), an alpha level of 0.1% will be spent on the interim ORR analysis (IA1) while the remaining 4.9% alpha level will be spent on all OS analyses... If the primary comparison (H1: Arm C vs. Arm D) is statistically significant in the OS analyses at IA2 or FA, then the 4.9% alpha will be recycled to H2 across IA2 and FA. Otherwise neither H2 nor H3 will be tested... If all the OS analyses (H1, H2, and H3) are considered successful..., the 4.9% alpha level will be passed to test the difference in the three year survival rates (OS36) between Arm C and Arm D; Otherwise the test will not be conducted."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761289, Reference ID 5064925, primary efficacy result]* — "HIMALAYA demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in OS in patients randomized to the T300+D arm compared to those who were randomized to the sorafenib arm (stratified hazard ratio [HR] of 0.78 [95% CI: 0.66, 0.92], stratified log-rank 2-sided p-value = 0.0035)."

*[verbatim, same source, on the original CSP's key-secondary testing procedure]* — "In the original CSP, the primary efficacy endpoint is to compare OS of T75+D vs. S at 2-sided alpha of 4.9%. An alpha level of 0.1% was spent on the interim ORR and DoR analysis to strongly control the type-1 error rate. The two key secondary endpoints, comparing OS of T300+D vs. S and OS of D vs. S, were tested at 2-sided alpha of 4.9% with Dunnett and Tamhane's step-up procedure to control the overall type-1 error rate. Following Amendment 4, enrollment into T75+D arm was discontinued based on interim analysis results regarding tolerability and clinical activity obtained from another ongoing study, Study 22 (D419CC00022)."

*[verbatim, same source, on the limited-ORR/OS-benefit tension for tremelimumab monotherapy]* — "While the response rate for tremelimumab monotherapy was 7.2%, responses were durable (23.95 months). The median OS of 17.05 months for T was similar to that observed with T300+D... Thus, the limited ORR in patients receiving tremelimumab does not preclude an OS benefit."

*[verbatim, same source, §9 Advisory Committee Meeting and Other External Consultations]* — "The Division did not refer the application to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee (ODAC) or seek input from Special Government Employees (SGEs) for this BLA as no significant review issues were identified during the review of this application."

### 149. teclistamab-cqyv (Tecvayli) — BLA 761291

**Sponsor:** Janssen Biotech, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adults with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma who have received at least four prior lines of therapy, including a proteasome inhibitor, an immunomodulatory agent, and an anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody — approved under accelerated approval based on response rate

**Approval date:** October 25, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** MajesTEC-1, NCT03145181 (Phase 1) and NCT04557098 (Phase 2)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H/21 CFR 601.41; step-up ("priming") dosing regimen prior to the therapeutic dose, specifically to mitigate cytokine release syndrome (CRS) risk from a T-cell-engaging bispecific antibody
- *Endpoints:* Overall response rate (ORR: sCR+CR+VGPR+PR, primary, by Independent Review Committee per IMWG 2016 criteria); duration of response (key secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* Response-rate point estimate with 95% confidence interval in the efficacy population (label does not specify the CI construction method; Clopper-Pearson exact binomial CI is inferred by analogy to essentially universal FDA practice for single-arm ORR endpoints in this era — see Reverse-engineered SAP below)
- *Missing data/bias:* Not applicable in the randomized-trial sense (no comparator/crossover); standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment for duration of response
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval (Subpart H) based on ORR as a surrogate reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit; postmarketing requirement to complete MajesTEC-1 with longer follow-up to further characterize ORR and DOR, and a separate postmarketing requirement for a randomized confirmatory trial (teclistamab-based regimen vs. standard therapy, primary endpoint PFS) to verify clinical benefit; a mandatory Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) was required for CRS and neurologic toxicity including ICANS, requiring inpatient monitoring for the step-up doses and prescriber/pharmacy certification

**Trial design & endpoints**

- MajesTEC-1: single-arm, open-label, multicenter study of teclistamab (a BCMA×CD3 bispecific antibody) spanning a Phase 1 dose-escalation portion (NCT03145181) and a Phase 2 dose-expansion portion (NCT04557098) at the recommended dose; patients received step-up doses of 0.06 mg/kg and 0.3 mg/kg followed by the therapeutic dose of 1.5 mg/kg subcutaneously once weekly until progression or unacceptable toxicity
- Efficacy population: 110 patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma who had received at least 3 prior therapies including a proteasome inhibitor, an immunomodulatory agent, and an anti-CD38 antibody (median 5 prior lines, 78% with ≥4 prior lines, 76% triple-class refractory); patients with prior BCMA-targeted therapy were excluded from the efficacy population
- Primary endpoint: ORR (sCR+CR+VGPR+PR) by Independent Review Committee assessment using IMWG 2016 criteria; secondary/supportive: duration of response, time to response
- Results: ORR was 61.8% (95% CI 52.1-70.9), including a complete response or better in 28.2% of patients; median time to first response was 1.2 months; with a median follow-up of 7.4 months among responders, the estimated DOR rate was 90.6% at 6 months and 66.5% at 9 months (median DOR not estimable, 95% CI 9.0 months-not estimable)
- Safety: CRS occurred in a majority of patients (managed via the mandatory step-up dosing schedule and REMS-mandated inpatient monitoring); neurologic toxicity including ICANS was also observed, driving the boxed warning and REMS requirement

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2022/761291Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2022/761291s000lbl.pdf
- No FDA Statistical Review, Clinical Review, or combined Multi-Discipline Review package was found publicly posted for this original approval on Drugs@FDA (only the approval letter and label are linked from the ApplNo 761291 overview page; direct-pattern URL guesses at `accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/{nda,bla}/2022/761291Orig1s000{StatR,MedR,MultidisciplineR}.pdf` all returned 404)
- ClinicalTrials.gov records — Phase 1: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03145181 (no protocol/SAP posted in Documents tab); Phase 2: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04557098 (no protocol/SAP posted in Documents tab)
- Pivotal publication: Moreau P, Garfall AL, van de Donk NWCJ, et al. "Teclistamab in Relapsed or Refractory Multiple Myeloma." *N Engl J Med.* 2022;387(6):495-505. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2203478), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35661166/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Teclistamab%20in%20Relapsed%20or%20Refractory%20Multiple%20Myeloma)

**Other resources**

- Janssen's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for MajesTEC-1; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for this trial.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was identified for this submission.
- Postmarketing requirements per the approval letter: complete the MajesTEC-1 trial (Study 64007957MMY1001) with longer follow-up "to obtain the overall response rate and duration of response" in the labeled population; and conduct a randomized trial of a teclistamab-based regimen vs. standard therapy for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma, primary endpoint PFS, with secondary endpoints including OS, ORR, and DOR, and a requirement to enroll a study population reflecting U.S. racial/ethnic and age diversity.
- A REMS program (communication plan, elements to assure safe use, implementation system) was required specifically to mitigate CRS and neurologic toxicity risk.

**Reverse-engineered SAP**

- *[inferred, from the label's Table 13 and REMS requirements]* The primary analysis was almost certainly a simple response-rate estimate (count of IRC-confirmed responders / efficacy population) with a two-sided 95% confidence interval, most likely constructed via the Clopper-Pearson exact binomial method — this is the near-universal convention for single-arm ORR primary endpoints across this era's oncology accelerated approvals (confirmed explicitly in this same census for avapritinib, tazemetostat, futibatinib, olutasidenib, mirvetuximab, and adagrasib), but the label itself does not state the CI method and no public FDA statistical review or sponsor SAP was located to confirm it for teclistamab specifically.
- *[inferred, from the efficacy population definition]* The efficacy-evaluable population (n=110) almost certainly reflects a pre-specified analysis set restricted to patients meeting the ≥3-prior-lines/triple-class-exposure eligibility criteria and excluding prior BCMA-therapy recipients, consistent with how the label describes the population, though the underlying protocol-level analysis-set definitions were not publicly available to confirm directly.
- *[inferred, from DOR reporting with "not estimable" bounds]* Duration of response was almost certainly analyzed via Kaplan-Meier estimation with standard right-censoring of patients without a documented progression/death event at last evaluable assessment, consistent with the reported "median DOR: NE (9.0, NE)" — a pattern only produced by KM estimation with heavy administrative censoring, not a completed-events analysis.

### 150. mirvetuximab soravtansine-gynx (Elahere) — BLA 761310

**Sponsor:** ImmunoGen, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adults with folate receptor alpha (FRα)-positive, platinum-resistant epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer, previously treated with 1-3 prior systemic treatment regimens — approved under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and durability of response

**Approval date:** November 14, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** SORAYA (Study IMGN853-0417), NCT04296890

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H/21 CFR 601.41; biomarker-selected/enriched population (FRα-positive by the VENTANA FOLR1 [FOLR1-2.1] RxDx companion diagnostic assay); companion diagnostic co-approval
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR, primary — investigator-assessed, confirmed CR/PR per RECIST 1.1, with independent radiology review reported as consistent/supportive); duration of response (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* One-sided exact binomial test against a pre-specified performance goal (H0: ORR≤12% vs. Ha: ORR=24%, one-sided alpha 0.025, actual achieved significance level 0.0242); non-inferiority/superiority declared if the lower bound of the 2-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson exact confidence interval for ORR exceeded 12% (exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval); confidence-interval approach used in lieu of a reported p-value, as is standard for single-arm ORR primary endpoints (descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis, adapted here to a formal one-sided test framing rather than a purely descriptive CI)
- *Missing data/bias:* Not applicable in the randomized-trial sense (no comparator/crossover); standard right-censoring for duration of response
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval (Subpart H) based on tumor response rate and durability of response; companion diagnostic (VENTANA FOLR1 [FOLR1-2.1] RxDx Assay) co-approved to select the FRα-positive population; postmarketing requirement for a confirmatory trial to verify clinical benefit; no FDA advisory committee meeting held ("outside expertise was not necessary")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- SORAYA (IMGN853-0417): single-arm, open-label, multicenter Phase 3 trial of mirvetuximab soravtansine (an FRα-directed antibody-drug conjugate) in patients with platinum-resistant, high-grade epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer with high FRα expression (VENTANA FOLR1 [FOLR1-2.1] RxDx Assay-positive), who had received 1-3 prior systemic regimens including at least one line containing bevacizumab
- Primary endpoint: investigator-assessed ORR (confirmed CR or PR per RECIST 1.1) in the Efficacy Evaluable population; the study tested the null hypothesis that ORR is 12% (drawn from historical platinum-resistant ovarian cancer chemotherapy response rates) against an alternative of 24%
- Sample size/power: approximately 110 patients planned for enrollment so that 105 would be efficacy-evaluable, giving 90% power to detect the 12%-vs-24% ORR difference using a one-sided binomial test at a target one-sided alpha of 0.025 (actual achieved significance level 0.0242); the study would reject the null hypothesis if the lower bound of the 95% (2-sided) Clopper-Pearson CI for ORR exceeded 12%
- Secondary endpoints: duration of response, GCIG CA-125 response rate, progression-free survival, overall survival — evaluated descriptively to further characterize efficacy, with no formal hypothesis testing (the SAP states "no formal hypothesis testing will be performed" on these secondary endpoints)
- Results: among 104 efficacy-evaluable patients with platinum-resistant disease and measurable disease, the confirmed ORR was 31.7% (95% CI 22.9-41.6%; 4.8% CR, 26.9% PR), clearing the 12% performance goal; median duration of response was 6.9 months (95% CI 5.6-9.7) among the 33 responders; independent radiology review was consistent with investigator assessment

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2022/761310s000lbl.pdf
- No FDA Statistical Review, Clinical Review, or combined Multi-Discipline Review package was found publicly posted for this original approval on Drugs@FDA (only the approval letter and label are linked from the ApplNo 761310 overview page; direct-pattern URL guesses at `accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/bla/2022/761310Orig1s000{StatR,MedR,MultidisciplineR}.pdf` all returned 404)

- Pivotal publication: Matulonis UA, Lorusso D, Oaknin A, et al. "Efficacy and Safety of Mirvetuximab Soravtansine in Patients With Platinum-Resistant Ovarian Cancer With High Folate Receptor Alpha Expression: Results From the SORAYA Study." *J Clin Oncol.* 2023;41(13):2436-2445. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.22.01900), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36716407/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Efficacy%20and%20Safety%20of%20Mirvetuximab%20Soravtansine%20in%20Patients%20With%20Platinum-Resistant%20Ovarian%20Cancer%20With%20High%20Folate%20Receptor%20Alpha%20Expression%20SORAYA)

**Other resources**

- ImmunoGen's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for SORAYA; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for this trial.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held; the approval letter states the application "was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary; there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion."
- Postmarketing requirement (per the approval letter, referencing the sponsor's October 18, 2022 submission): conduct confirmatory trial(s) to verify and describe clinical benefit — the confirmatory evidence program subsequently included the randomized MIRASOL trial (NCT04209855), reported after this approval.
- Companion diagnostic: the VENTANA FOLR1 (FOLR1-2.1) RxDx Assay was approved concurrently to identify FRα-positive patients eligible for treatment.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

The study is designed to test the null hypothesis that the ORR is 12% (Eisenhauer 2009, Pujade-Lauraine 2014)... Approximately 110 patients will be enrolled so that a total of 105 patients will be efficacy evaluable. A sample size of 105 efficacy evaluable patients achieves 90% power to detect a difference in ORR of 12% (24% vs 12%) using a one-sided binomial test. The target significance level (one-sided α level) is 0.025. The actual significance level achieved by this test is 0.0242."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.11.2 Secondary Endpoints]* — "The secondary endpoints of DOR, GCIG CA-125 response rate, PFS, and OS will be evaluated to further characterize the efficacy of MIRV. No formal hypothesis testing will be performed on [these secondary endpoints]."

### 151. olutasidenib (Rezlidhia) — NDA 215814

**Sponsor:** Rigel Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adults with relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with a susceptible IDH1 mutation, as detected by an FDA-approved test — approved under accelerated approval based on complete remission rate and complete remission with partial hematologic recovery rate, and the duration of complete remission plus complete remission with partial hematologic recovery

**Approval date:** December 1, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** Study 2102-HV / 2102-HEM-101, NCT02719574 (Phase 2 Cohort 1)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label, multi-cohort Phase 1/2 trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H; group-sequential design with two interim analyses for the pivotal Phase 2 Cohort 1; biomarker-selected/enriched population (IDH1-R132 mutation confirmed by companion diagnostic); other Phase 2 cohorts used Simon optimal two-stage designs not relevant to the approval-supporting cohort
- *Endpoints:* Composite CR/CRh (complete remission + complete remission with partial hematologic recovery) rate (primary — investigator-assessed, at 6 months); duration of CR/CRh, conversion to transfusion independence (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* One-sided exact binomial test against a pre-specified performance goal (H0: CR+CRh rate ≤15% vs. Ha: true rate 25%, one-sided alpha 0.025, 90% power); exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval for the primary estimate, with Atkinson-Brown confidence intervals used as a sensitivity analysis correcting for the two-stage/group-sequential design
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* O'Brien-Fleming boundary for both the efficacy-stopping (alpha) and futility-stopping (beta) bounds at two interim analyses (~33% and ~67% of information); Data/Independent Monitoring oversight of the interim looks
- *Missing data/bias:* Not applicable in the randomized-trial sense (no comparator/crossover); standard right-censoring for duration of response
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval (Subpart H) based on CR/CRh rate as a surrogate reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit; FDA independently re-derived the efficacy population from the sponsor's reported 123-patient interim-analysis set to a larger, updated 147-patient set using a later data cutoff and excluding subjects not centrally confirmed IDH1 R132-positive (FDA-conducted independent expansion of the efficacy analysis population, though here FDA both expanded via later follow-up and narrowed via biomarker confirmation); no FDA advisory committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 2102-HEM-101 (also referred to as Study 2102-HV): open-label, multicenter Phase 1/2 trial of olutasidenib (FT-2102) as a single agent and in combination with azacitidine in patients with AML or myelodysplastic syndrome harboring an IDH1 mutation; Phase 2 Cohort 1 (relapsed/refractory AML with IDH1-R132 mutation, olutasidenib 150 mg BID monotherapy) is the approval-supporting cohort, using a group-sequential design with a futility interim analysis at approximately 33% of information and an efficacy interim analysis at approximately 67%
- Primary endpoint: investigator-assessed CR+CRh rate in Cohort 1, tested against the null hypothesis that the true CR+CRh rate is 15% or less, versus the alternative that it exceeds 15%, assuming a true rate of 25%, at a one-sided 2.5% significance level (equivalently 2-sided alpha 0.05)
- Sample-size/power logic: 173 evaluable patients (of ~190 enrolled, to allow for central-lab discordance on IDH1-R132 status) gave 90% power to identify a 25% CR+CRh rate while excluding a 15% rate; interim analysis 1 (58 patients) used an O'Brien-Fleming futility bound (≤6/58 responses, spending 0 alpha/0.004 beta) with no possibility of stopping for efficacy; interim analysis 2 (115 patients) allowed stopping for efficacy (≥28/115 responses, spending 0.006 alpha/0.044 beta) or futility (≤20/115 responses)
- Secondary endpoints: duration of CR/CRh (Kaplan-Meier, Brookmeyer-Crowley-type median CI), overall response rate, transfusion independence conversion (proportion of baseline RBC/platelet-transfusion-dependent patients who became independent during any 56-day post-baseline window); all proportional endpoints reported with Clopper-Pearson 95% CIs
- Results: at interim analysis 2, CR or CRh was achieved by 41 of 123 efficacy-evaluable patients (33%, 95% CI 25.1-42.4%) by investigator assessment, meeting the primary objective; using an updated data cutoff (June 18, 2021) and an FDA-narrowed/expanded population of 147 centrally-confirmed patients, the CR/CRh rate as adjudicated by FDA's clinical and statistical reviewers was 35% (95% CI 27-43%); median time to response was 1.9 months; median duration of CR/CRh was 25.9 months (95% CI 13.5-not reached); 34% of baseline transfusion-dependent patients converted to transfusion independence

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2022/215814Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2022/215814s000lbl.pdf

- Pivotal publication: Watts JM, Baer MR, Yang J, et al. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S2352-3026(22)00292-7>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36370742/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Olutasidenib%20alone%20or%20with%20azacitidine%20in%20IDH1-mutated%20acute%20myeloid%20leukaemia%20and%20myelodysplastic%20syndrome)

**Other resources**

- Rigel Pharmaceuticals' general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for Study 2102-HEM-101; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for this trial.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held; the review states "this application was not presented to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee or any other external consultants."
- FDA's review documents a data-cutoff and analysis-population update between the sponsor's initial 90-day-safety-update submission (123 evaluable patients) and FDA's own final assessment (147 confirmed patients using a June 18, 2021 cutoff), after excluding subjects not centrally confirmed positive for the IDH1 R132 mutation.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, Study 2102-HEM-101 Statistical Analysis Plan, §IV.C Sample Size, Phase 2 Cohort 1]* — "One hundred seventy-three (173) patients provide 90% power to test the null hypothesis that the true complete response rate (CR + CRh) is 15% or less versus the one-sided alternative hypothesis that the true complete response rate is greater than 15%, assuming a true response rate of 25%, with a 2.5% significance level using a one-sided exact test for a binomial proportion."

*[verbatim, same source, interim analysis rules]* — "Two interim analyses are planned, at approximately 33% and 67% of the information, respectively. O'Brien-Fleming stopping boundaries will be used for both alpha and beta adjustments. At the first interim, if ≤6/58 responses are observed..., the trial may be stopped early for futility... Interim analysis 1 spends 0 alpha and 0.004 beta... At the second interim analysis, if ≥28/115 responses are observed..., the trial may stop enrollment for efficacy and if there are 20 or fewer responses..., the trial will be stopped for futility. Interim analysis 2 spends 0.006 alpha and 0.044 beta."

*[verbatim, same source, primary efficacy analysis]* — "The number and proportion of patients achieving CR/CRh response will be reported by cohort from the binomial proportion, along with Clopper-Pearson 95% confidence interval for AML and MDS patients respectively... For Phase 2 Cohort 1, a sensitivity analysis will be performed on the CR/CRh rate in which Atkinson and Brown confidence intervals will be calculated."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 215814, Reference ID 5086659, primary endpoint description]* — "The primary efficacy endpoint of Study of 2102-HEM-101 was investigator-assessed CR + CRh in all patients in Cohort 1 treated with olutasidenib 150 mg BID... The sample size of 173 evaluable patients had 90% power to identify a 25% CR + CRh rate while excluding a 15% CR + CRh rate with a 2-sided alpha of 0.05. In Cohort 1, the Applicant reported that a CR or CRh was achieved by 41 out of 123 efficacy evaluable subjects at the time of interim analysis 2 (33%; 95% CI 25.1%-42.4%), so the primary objective of the study was met."

*[verbatim, same source, on FDA's re-derivation of the efficacy population]* — "FDA sought to assess efficacy in the broadest population available... FDA excluded enrolled subjects who were not confirmed positive for IDH1 R132 mutation using the proposed companion diagnostic assay and evaluated patients for documentation of relapse at study entry. Using the updated data set with a cut-off date of June 18, 2021, FDA confirmed 147 patients for analysis... The CR/CRh rate as adjudicated by the clinical and statistical reviewers was 35% (95% CI: 27% - 43%)."

*[verbatim, same source, sensitivity analysis discussion]* — "The lower bound of the more conservative Atkinson-Brown 95% CI (22.7%, 33.6%), which corrects for a two-stage design, also exceeds 15%, demonstrating the robustness of the estimate."

*[verbatim, same source, §10.0 Advisory Committee Meeting and Other External Consultations]* — "This application was not presented to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee or any other external consultants."

### 152. adagrasib (Krazati) — NDA 216340

**Sponsor:** Mirati Therapeutics, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adults with KRAS G12C-mutated locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), as determined by an FDA-approved test, who have received at least one prior systemic therapy — approved under accelerated approval based on objective response rate and duration of response

**Approval date:** December 12, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** KRYSTAL-1 (Study 849-001), Cohort A, NCT03785249

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label, multi-cohort Phase 1/2 basket trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H/21 CFR 314.500; biomarker-selected/enriched population (KRAS G12C mutation by the ctDx FIRST companion diagnostic assay); noncomparative design using a confidence-interval-to-exclude-a-benchmark approach against a literature-derived standard-of-care ORR (descriptive/exact-binomial single-arm response-rate analysis against a pre-specified performance goal)
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR, primary — blinded independent central review [BICR] per RECIST 1.1); duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* Exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval used to exclude a pre-specified benchmark ORR of 23% (docetaxel + ramucirumab historical control), assuming a target adagrasib ORR of at least 35%; FAS-BICR (primary) and FAS-Investigator (sensitivity) analysis populations both pre-specified
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Non-binding futility boundary derived from a Rho-family (parameter 2.0) beta-spending function via East software, controlling Type II error at 0.2 (Fleming-Harrington/rho-family spending function, here used for futility rather than efficacy); futility analysis at approximately 32 evaluable patients (~30% of target), stopping bound of 6 or fewer responses
- *Missing data/bias:* Missing data were not imputed for the primary ORR analysis; time-to-event endpoints used standard right-censoring per the SAP
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval (Subpart H) based on ORR/DOR as a surrogate reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit; the choice of ORR as primary endpoint was raised and discussed with FDA at a Type B meeting before Cohort A began enrolling, though FDA's review explicitly notes it does not characterize this as an "agreement" but as FDA "provid[ing] recommendations"; no FDA advisory committee meeting held, as "no significant efficacy or safety issues were identified during the review that required external input"

**Trial design & endpoints**

- KRYSTAL-1 (Study 849-001): open-label, multiple-expansion-cohort Phase 1/2 trial of adagrasib (MRTX849) in patients with KRAS G12C-mutated advanced solid tumors; Cohort A (adagrasib 600 mg orally BID monotherapy in previously treated NSCLC) is the registration-enabling cohort, with a noncomparative design and pre-specified subgroup analyses (gender, age, number of prior regimens, concurrent vs. sequential prior therapy, smoking history, ECOG PS, organ sites of disease)
- Primary endpoint: ORR based on BICR assessment per RECIST 1.1 in the FAS-BICR population (patients with measurable disease at baseline per BICR who received at least one dose); FAS-Investigator served as a sensitivity-analysis population
- Sample-size/power logic: the sample-size calculation used a confidence-interval approach to exclude the benchmark ORR associated with standard-of-care docetaxel + ramucirumab (23%, from Garon et al. 2014), assuming adagrasib would achieve at least 35% ORR; approximately 105 evaluable patients was estimated to be sufficient for the lower bound of a 2-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson CI to exclude 23%; a non-binding futility stopping rule (Rho-family, parameter 2.0, via East software v6.5, Type II error 0.2) triggered a futility look at approximately 32 patients (bound: 6 or fewer responses among the first 32)
- Secondary endpoints: duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival — all summarized descriptively; FDA's review explicitly states these time-to-event endpoints are supportive only, not independently interpretable without a randomized comparator
- Results: as of the June 15, 2021 data cutoff, 112 patients in Cohort A had measurable disease at baseline per BICR; ORR was 42.9% (48 of 112 patients, 95% CI 33.5-52.6%), and the lower limit of the 95% CI excluded the prespecified 23% benchmark; responses included 1 complete response and 47 partial responses
- Sample-size and protocol amendment history: the statistical design and sample size for Cohort A were revised multiple times via protocol amendments (Amendment 4 and Amendment 9, dated August 31, 2022) that increased the sample size, reflecting the evolving competitive landscape (sotorasib's approval occurred during KRYSTAL-1's conduct) and FDA feedback on adequate characterization of ORR/DOR magnitude

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2022/216340Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2022/216340Orig1s000Corrected_lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 5092534, NDA 216340, Statistical Reviewer Chuck Song) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/216340Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (KRYSTAL-1) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03785249 (no protocol/SAP posted in the Documents tab)
- Pivotal publication: Jänne PA, Riely GJ, Gadgeel SM, et al. "Adagrasib in Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer Harboring a KRAS(G12C) Mutation." *N Engl J Med.* 2022;387(2):120-131. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2204619), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35658005/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Adagrasib%20in%20Non-Small-Cell%20Lung%20Cancer%20Harboring%20a%20KRAS%20G12C%20Mutation)

**Other resources**

- Mirati Therapeutics' general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for KRYSTAL-1; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for this trial.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held; FDA's review states it "did not refer this application to an advisory committee as no significant efficacy or safety issues were identified during the review that required external input for the proposed indication."
- Postmarketing requirements per the approval letter: a randomized comparative confirmatory trial ("A Randomized Phase 3 Study of MRTX849 versus Docetaxel," i.e., KRYSTAL-12) to verify clinical benefit, plus a further postmarketing requirement to characterize dosing/exposure-response.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 216340, Reference ID 5092534, Statistical Analysis Plan (the Applicant's Description, quoted by FDA)]* — "The design for Cohort A was noncomparative and used ORR as the primary endpoint. The sample size calculation for the pivotal study, Study 849-001 Cohort A, is based on the confidence interval (CI) approach to exclude the benchmark ORR associated with the standard of care of docetaxel with ramucirumab, where the associated ORR is 23% (Garon et al. 2014). Based on the assumption that treatment with adagrasib would result in an ORR of at least 35% in this treatment setting, a sample size of approximately 105 evaluable patients would be sufficient for the lower bound of a 2 sided 95% CI (Clopper-Pearson method) to exclude an ORR of 23%."

*[verbatim, same source, futility rule]* — "The design for Cohort A included a non-binding stopping rule for futility derived using East® software v6.5 to control the Type 2 error rate of 0.2. The Type 2 error spending function was based on the Rho family with parameter 2.0. The futility analysis was to be conducted when approximately 32 evaluable patients (approximately 30% of the total number of patients) were available for the response assessment. The futility bound was 6 or fewer observed responses among the first 32 patients."

*[verbatim, same source, FDA's assessment of endpoint choice]* — "FDA agrees with the Applicant's description of the trial endpoints with the exception that FDA does not reach 'agreements' with Sponsors or Applicants. FDA provides recommendations and provides the current thinking on matters regarding the study endpoints in single arm trials."

*[verbatim, same source, primary result]* — "The ORR in Cohort A was 42.9% (48 patients with response among 112 patients; 95% CI: 33.5% to 52.6%). The lower limit of the 95% CI excluded the prespecified benchmark ORR of 23%. Disease responses included 1 complete response (CR) and 47 partial responses (PRs)."

*[verbatim, same source, §9 Advisory Committee Meeting and Other External Consultations]* — "FDA did not refer this application to an advisory committee as no significant efficacy or safety issues were identified during the review that required external input for the proposed indication."
