### 153. mosunetuzumab-axgb (Lunsumio) — BLA 761263

**Sponsor:** Genentech, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adults with relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma who have received at least two prior lines of systemic therapy — approved under accelerated approval based on response rate and durability of response

**Approval date:** December 22, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** GO29781, NCT02500407

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label, multicenter, multi-cohort trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H/21 CFR 601.41; step-up ("priming") dosing regimen across the first two cycles specifically to mitigate CRS risk from a T-cell-engaging bispecific antibody (reused proposed term introduced at teclistamab in this same batch); fixed-duration regimen for complete responders (treatment limited to 8 cycles, with continuation to a maximum of 17 cycles only for patients with a partial response or stable disease)
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR, primary — independent-review-facility-assessed per Cheson 2007 NHL response criteria); complete response rate and duration of response (secondary/key supportive)
- *Primary analysis:* Response-rate point estimate with 95% confidence interval in the efficacy population (label does not specify the CI construction method; Clopper-Pearson exact binomial CI is inferred by analogy to essentially universal FDA practice for single-arm ORR endpoints in this era — see Reverse-engineered SAP below)
- *Missing data/bias:* Not applicable in the randomized-trial sense (no comparator/crossover); standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment for duration of response
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval (Subpart H) based on ORR/durability of response as a surrogate reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit; postmarketing requirement for a randomized confirmatory trial (mosunetuzumab + lenalidomide vs. rituximab + lenalidomide, primary endpoint PFS) to verify clinical benefit; mandatory boxed warning/monitoring for CRS given the bispecific-antibody mechanism, though (unlike teclistamab) without a formal REMS program

**Trial design & endpoints**

- GO29781: open-label, multicenter, multi-cohort Phase I/II trial of mosunetuzumab (a CD20×CD3 T-cell-engaging bispecific antibody) as a single agent and in combination with atezolizumab, across non-Hodgkin lymphoma and CLL cohorts; the relapsed/refractory follicular lymphoma expansion cohort (single-agent mosunetuzumab, ≥2 prior lines including an anti-CD20 antibody and an alkylating agent) is the approval-supporting population
- Dosing: step-up doses of 1 mg (Cycle 1 Day 1) and 2 mg (Cycle 1 Day 8), then 60 mg (Cycle 1 Day 15 and Cycle 2 Day 1), then 30 mg every 3 weeks; treatment given for 8 cycles, with complete responders discontinuing therapy and partial responders/stable disease continuing up to 17 cycles total
- Primary endpoint: ORR and duration of response as assessed by an independent review facility using Cheson 2007 NHL response criteria, in an efficacy population of 90 patients (median 3 prior therapies, 79% refractory to prior anti-CD20 therapy, 53% double-refractory to anti-CD20 and alkylator therapy, 21% with prior autologous stem cell transplant, 3% with prior CAR-T therapy)
- Results: ORR was 80% (72 of 90 patients, 95% CI 70-88%), including a 60% complete response rate (95% CI 49-70%) and 20% partial response rate; median follow-up for duration of response was 14.9 months, with median DOR 22.8 months (95% CI 10-not reached) and continued-response rates of 62% at 12 months and 57% at 18 months
- Safety: CRS was an expected on-mechanism toxicity managed via the step-up dosing schedule and monitoring recommendations in the label, alongside a boxed warning

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2023/761263Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2022/761263s000lbl.pdf
- No FDA Statistical Review, Clinical Review, or combined Multi-Discipline Review package was found publicly posted for this original approval on Drugs@FDA (only the approval letter and label are linked from the ApplNo 761263 overview page; direct-pattern URL guesses at `accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/bla/{2022,2023}/761263Orig1s000{StatR,MedR,MultidisciplineR}.pdf` all returned 404)
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (GO29781) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02500407 (no protocol/SAP posted in the Documents tab)
- Pivotal publication: Budde LE, Sehn LH, Matasar M, et al. "Safety and efficacy of mosunetuzumab, a bispecific antibody, in patients with relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma: a single-arm, multicentre, phase 2 study." *Lancet Oncol.* 2022;23(8):1055-1065. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(22)00335-7>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35803286/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Safety%20and%20efficacy%20of%20mosunetuzumab%20bispecific%20antibody%20relapsed%20or%20refractory%20follicular%20lymphoma%20single-arm%20multicentre%20phase%202)

**Other resources**

- Genentech's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for GO29781; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for this trial.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was identified for this submission.
- Postmarketing requirement per the approval letter: "Conduct a randomized clinical trial in patients with relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma, with patients randomized to receive mosunetuzumab in combination with lenalidomide or rituximab in combination with lenalidomide. The primary endpoint should be progression-free survival, with secondary endpoints that include response rate and overall survival," enrolling a population reflecting U.S. racial/ethnic diversity.

**Reverse-engineered SAP**

- *[inferred, from the label's Table 11 and the "independent review facility" language]* The primary analysis was almost certainly a simple response-rate estimate (count of independent-review-facility-confirmed responders / efficacy population, n=90) with a two-sided 95% confidence interval, most likely Clopper-Pearson exact binomial — the same convention confirmed explicitly elsewhere in this census (avapritinib, tazemetostat, futibatinib, olutasidenib, mirvetuximab, adagrasib) — but no public FDA statistical review or sponsor SAP was located to confirm the exact method for mosunetuzumab specifically.
- *[inferred, from the fixed 8-cycle-then-response-adaptive regimen]* The complete-response-triggered treatment discontinuation rule (stop after 8 cycles for CR, continue to 17 cycles for PR/SD) implies the efficacy analysis population and safety-exposure population are not identical — patients accrue materially different treatment durations depending on response category — though the label does not spell out how this was handled analytically (e.g., whether DOR clock start/stop conventions accounted for the response-adaptive stopping rule).
- *[inferred, from "median follow-up for DOR was 14.9 months" and "not reached" upper CI bound]* Duration of response was almost certainly analyzed via Kaplan-Meier estimation with standard right-censoring for patients without a documented progression/death event at last evaluable assessment, consistent with the reported not-reached upper confidence bound.

### 154. pirtobrutinib (Jaypirca) — NDA 216059

**Sponsor:** Loxo Oncology, Inc. (a subsidiary of Eli Lilly and Company)

**Indication approved:** Adults with relapsed or refractory mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) after at least two prior lines of therapy, including a Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitor — approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate and duration of response

**Approval date:** January 27, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** BRUIN (Study LOXO-BTK-18001), NCT03740529

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label, international, multicenter trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H; pirtobrutinib is a noncovalent (reversible) BTK inhibitor, mechanistically distinct from the covalent BTK inhibitors (ibrutinib, acalabrutinib, zanubrutinib) that all enrolled patients had previously progressed on or discontinued
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR, primary — Independent Review Committee assessment per 2014 Lugano criteria); duration of response (secondary); PFS and OS regarded by FDA as exploratory only
- *Primary analysis:* Exact binomial test against a pre-specified performance goal (hypothesized ORR ≥40%, sample size of 65 patients estimated for ~95% power to achieve a lower 2-sided 95% exact-binomial CI bound exceeding a 20% performance goal, later increased to N=90 following FDA feedback)
- *Missing data/bias:* FDA-conducted independent expansion (here, pooling/redefinition) of the efficacy analysis population — FDA disagreed with the sponsor's proposed Primary Analysis Set (PAS, restricted by starting dose) and instead pooled the PAS with a supplemental analysis set (SAS1) of similarly-eligible patients treated at variable doses, yielding an FDA primary efficacy population of 120 patients rather than the sponsor's 74-90 (FDA-conducted independent expansion of the efficacy analysis population)
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval (Subpart H) based on ORR/DOR as a surrogate reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit; FDA explicitly recommended delaying NDA submission until sample size and follow-up duration were increased; postmarketing requirement for a randomized confirmatory trial (pirtobrutinib vs. investigator's choice of BTK inhibitor in BTK-inhibitor-naive MCL, i.e., BRUIN MCL-321) to verify clinical benefit; no FDA advisory committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- BRUIN (LOXO-BTK-18001): open-label, international, multicenter Phase 1/2 study of oral pirtobrutinib monotherapy in patients with previously treated CLL/SLL or non-Hodgkin lymphoma, including an MCL cohort that supports this approval; regulatory history shows FDA recommended in an October 2021 pre-NDA meeting that "the proposed submission of data from 65 patients with MCL would be insufficient and that responders should have at least 9 months of follow-up for duration of response," and recommended delaying submission — the sponsor subsequently increased the primary analysis set (PAS) to 90 patients with at least 9 months' follow-up from response onset in ≥90% of patients
- Primary endpoint: ORR by IRC assessment (Lugano 2014 criteria) based on best overall response of PR or better; sample size originally estimated at 65 patients for ~95% power to achieve a lower 2-sided 95% exact binomial CI bound exceeding a 20% performance goal (assuming a hypothesized ORR of at least 40%), later increased to N=90 following FDA's pre-NDA feedback, with a data cutoff chosen so that most PAS responders had ≥9 months of follow-up from response onset
- Analysis-population dispute: the sponsor's PAS (n=74-90) restricted eligibility to patients meeting specific dosing criteria across the trial's Phase 1/2 conduct; FDA's review states "The FDA disagrees with the proposed analysis population and the description of the duration of follow-up for the responders within the analysis population," and instead defined its own primary efficacy population of 120 patients by pooling the PAS with a Supplemental Analysis Set (SAS1) of patients with consistent eligibility criteria, while excluding SAS2 (patients without radiographically assessable disease, deemed uninformative) and SAS3 (BTK-inhibitor-naive patients, not representative of the intended pretreated population)
- Results: in FDA's pooled 120-patient primary efficacy population, the IRC-assessed ORR was 50% (95% CI 41-59%) with a 13% CR rate and median time to response of 1.8 months; Kaplan-Meier median DOR was 8.3 months (95% CI 5.68-not estimable), with a 6-month DOR rate of 65.3%; in the sponsor's own narrower PAS (n=74), ORR was numerically higher at 57% (95% CI 45-68%) — the labeled, FDA-adjudicated ORR (50%, n=120) is materially lower than the sponsor's originally proposed analysis
- Safety: notable rates of hematologic toxicity (given heavy pretreatment — median 3 prior lines including a BTK inhibitor in 100% of patients) and infections were characterized in the safety database of 583 patients across all BRUIN cohorts

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter (corrected) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2023/216059Orig1s000Corrected_ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2023/216059Orig1s000Corrected_lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 5116352, NDA 216059, Statistical Reviewer Kun Wang, PhD) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/216059Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (BRUIN) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03740529 (no protocol/SAP posted in the Documents tab)
- Pivotal publications: Mato AR, Woyach JA, Brown JR, et al. "Pirtobrutinib in relapsed or refractory B-cell malignancies (BRUIN): a phase 1/2 study." *Lancet.* 2021;397(10277):892-901 (first-in-human BRUIN report, precedes the MCL-specific efficacy population supporting this approval). [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(21)00224-5), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33676628/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Pirtobrutinib%20in%20relapsed%20or%20refractory%20B-cell%20malignancies%20BRUIN); Wang ML, Jurczak W, Jerkeman M, et al. - Loxo Oncology/Lilly's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for BRUIN; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for this trial.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held; the review states "the application was not presented to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee or other external consultants."
- FDA also published a separate FDA Approval Summary journal article covering this decision: Purohit VS, Adhav CV, Amiri-Kordestani L, et al. "FDA Approval Summary: Pirtobrutinib for Relapsed or Refractory Mantle Cell Lymphoma." *Clin Cancer Res.* 2024;30(1):17-22. PMID 37624619.
- Postmarketing requirement: a randomized confirmatory trial (BRUIN MCL-321) comparing pirtobrutinib to investigator's choice of BTK inhibitor in BTK-inhibitor-naive MCL patients, to verify clinical benefit.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 216059, Reference ID 5116352, October 18, 2021 pre-NDA meeting, FDA's Assessment]* — "The FDA stated that the proposed submission of data from 65 patients with MCL would be insufficient and that responders should have at least 9 months of follow-up for duration of response. The FDA recommended delaying NDA submission until increased sample size and adequate follow-up in the PAS population was achieved."

*[verbatim, same source, sample size description, the Applicant's Description]* — "An ORR of ≥ 40% was hypothesized when pirtobrutinib is administered to patients in the proposed indication. A sample size of 65 patients was estimated to provide approximately 95% power to achieve a lower boundary of a 2-sided 95% exact binomial CI about the estimated ORR that exceeds 20%. The sample size in the PAS was increased to N = 90 following FDA feedback received during the pre-NDA FDA meeting."

*[verbatim, same source, FDA's disagreement with the proposed analysis population]* — "The FDA agrees with the Applicant's description of the eligibility criteria for the PAS and the description of the planned sample size. The FDA disagrees with the proposed analysis population and the description of the duration of follow-up for the responders within the analysis population."

*[verbatim, same source, FDA's own primary efficacy population definition]* — "The FDA primary efficacy analysis set (n=120) includes patients who were pooled between the PAS and SAS1, as these sets had consistent eligibility criteria and contained only BTK inhibitor-pretreated patients. The FDA did not adjudicate the responses of patients in the SAS2 and SAS3 analysis sets... FDA does not consider evaluation of efficacy in the SAS3 set to be informative..., given that the patients in SAS3 were BTK inhibitor-naive."

*[verbatim, same source, Integrated Review of Effectiveness, primary result]* — "In the PAS + SAS1 population (n=120), the IRC-assessed ORR was 50% (95% CI: 41, 59) and CR rate was 13%, with median time to response of 1.8 months. The Kaplan-Meier estimate of median DOR per IRC was 8.3 months (95% CI: 5.68, NE) and the Kaplan-Meier estimate of 6-month DOR was 65.3% (95% CI: 49.8, 77.1)."

*[verbatim, same source, §9.0 Advisory Committee Meeting and Other External Consultations]* — "The application was not presented to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee or other external consultants."

### 155. elacestrant (Orserdu) — NDA 217639

**Sponsor:** Stemline Therapeutics, Inc. (a Menarini Group company)

**Indication approved:** Postmenopausal women and adult men with estrogen receptor (ER)-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative, ESR1-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer, with disease progression following at least one line of endocrine therapy — regular approval (not accelerated approval)

**Approval date:** January 27, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** EMERALD (Study RAD1901-308), NCT03778931

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, open-label, active-controlled Phase III trial (standard-of-care fulvestrant or an aromatase inhibitor as the comparator); stratified randomization by ESR1 mutational status (ESR1-mut vs. ESR1-mut-not-detected) determined by a central ctDNA (Guardant360 CDx) assay; two pre-specified co-primary populations sharing the same endpoint construct — PFS tested as primary in both the ESR1-mut subpopulation and the full ITT population
- *Endpoints:* Progression-free survival (PFS, primary — IRC-assessed per RECIST 1.1, in ESR1-mut subjects and in all subjects); overall survival (OS, key secondary, in ESR1-mut subjects and in all subjects); objective response rate, clinical benefit rate, duration of response (further secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* Stratified log-rank test/Cox model for PFS, Kaplan-Meier estimation; restricted mean survival time (RMST) analysis as a supportive sensitivity analysis
- *Multiplicity:* Truncated Hochberg parallel gatekeeping procedure; Haybittle-Peto boundary used to further adjust alpha for the two planned OS analysis timepoints, contingent on the PFS gatekeeping outcome
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* OS analyzed at two pre-specified timepoints (at the primary PFS analysis, and at final analysis when ~50% of subjects had died), with alpha passed from PFS to OS only through the truncated-Hochberg/Haybittle-Peto gatekeeping structure described above
- *Missing data/bias:* Attrition bias sensitivity analysis for OS (reversed-censoring-indicator Kaplan-Meier plot to examine premature-censoring patterns by treatment group); a pre-specified COVID-19 death-censoring sensitivity analysis for OS
- *Regulatory:* Regular approval (21 CFR 314.126), not accelerated approval — unusual for this batch; FDA restricted the approved indication to the ESR1-mut subpopulation despite the trial meeting its co-primary PFS endpoint in both the ESR1-mut subgroup and the full ITT population, because FDA concluded the ITT-population PFS result was "primarily driven by" the ESR1-mut subgroup and that patients without a detectable ESR1 mutation did not show a clinically meaningful benefit once weighed against GI toxicity and dyslipidemia risks

**Trial design & endpoints**

- EMERALD (RAD1901-308): randomized, open-label, active-controlled, multicenter Phase III trial of elacestrant (an oral selective estrogen receptor degrader) vs. investigator's choice of standard-of-care endocrine therapy (fulvestrant or an aromatase inhibitor) in 478 patients with ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced/metastatic breast cancer who had progressed on 1-2 prior lines of endocrine therapy, including one line containing a CDK4/6 inhibitor; randomization (1:1) was stratified by ESR1 mutation status (detected via the Guardant360 CDx ctDNA assay), prior fulvestrant exposure, and presence of visceral metastases
- Co-primary endpoints: IRC-assessed PFS in the ESR1-mut subjects, and IRC-assessed PFS in all subjects (ESR1-mut and ESR1-mut-not-detected combined); key secondary endpoints were OS in the ESR1-mut subpopulation and OS in all subjects
- Sample size/power: approximately 220 ESR1-mut subjects (110/arm) were required for 80% power to detect HR 0.610 at a 2-sided alpha of 2.5%, and approximately 466 total subjects (233/arm, 340 PFS events) for 92% power to detect HR 0.667 among all subjects at the same 2-sided alpha of 2.5%; the 2.5% per-population alpha was chosen specifically so that at least one of the two co-primary PFS populations could pass a Hochberg-type procedure while controlling overall alpha at 5%
- Multiplicity structure: a truncated Hochberg procedure (truncation fraction 0.9) governed testing of the two co-primary PFS populations, with the resulting endpoint-specific alpha levels (r1=0.0475, r2=0.025) combining conventional-Hochberg and equally-weighted-Bonferroni allocations; if the PFS analyses succeeded, alpha was passed via a parallel gatekeeping strategy to the OS analyses, further adjusted by a Haybittle-Peto rule across the two planned OS looks (at the PFS analysis and at final analysis, ~50% of subjects deceased)
- Results: in the ESR1-mut subpopulation, median PFS was 3.8 months with elacestrant vs. 1.9 months with SOC (HR 0.55, 95% CI 0.39-0.77, p=0.0005), robust to multiple sensitivity analyses; OS in the ESR1-mut subpopulation was not statistically significant (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.63-1.30) but showed no trend toward detriment; in the full ITT population, PFS also met its endpoint (median 2.8 vs. 1.9 months, HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.55-0.88, p=0.0018), but FDA's review concluded this ITT result was "primarily driven by" the ESR1-mut subgroup (48% of ITT), with the ESR1-mut-not-detected subgroup (52% of ITT) showing no clinically meaningful PFS benefit, a numerically lower ORR on elacestrant than SOC, and increased GI toxicity/dyslipidemia — leading FDA to restrict the approved indication to ESR1-mut patients only

"Elacestrant (oral selective estrogen receptor degrader) Versus Standard Endocrine Therapy for Estrogen Receptor-Positive, Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2-Negative Advanced Breast Cancer: Results From the Randomized Phase III EMERALD Trial." *J Clin Oncol.* 2022;40(28):3246-3256. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.22.00338), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35584336/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Elacestrant%20oral%20selective%20estrogen%20receptor%20degrader%20Versus%20Standard%20Endocrine%20Therapy%20EMERALD%20Trial)

**Other resources**

- Stemline/Menarini's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for EMERALD; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for this trial.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held; FDA's review states the application "did not raise significant efficacy or safety issues... which required external input for the proposed indication."
- Companion diagnostic: the Guardant360 CDx ctDNA assay was used to identify ESR1 mutations for stratified randomization and for the FDA-restricted indication.
- This is the only entry in this batch approved via regular approval rather than accelerated approval, and the only randomized (rather than single-arm) pivotal trial among the batch aside from tremelimumab/HIMALAYA.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, EMERALD (RAD1901-308) Statistical Analysis Plan, Version 1.1, 10-MAY-2021, §1033-1041 Primary/Key Secondary Objectives]* — "The primary endpoints of this study are as follows: IRC-assessed PFS in the ESR1-mut subjects; IRC-assessed PFS in all subjects (ESR1-mut and ESR1-mut-nd)... [Key secondary endpoints:] OS in ESR1-mut subjects; OS in all subjects (ESR1-mut and ESR1-mut-nd)."

*[verbatim, same source, §4.1 Sample Size Justification]* — "Among the ESR1-mut subjects, the study requires approximately 160 PFS events to have a power of 80% to detect a hazard ratio of 0.610 at the 2-sided alpha level of 2.5%... Among all subjects (ESR1-mut and ESR1-mut-nd), a total of approximately 340 PFS events will have 92% power to detect a hazard ratio of 0.667 at the 2-sided alpha level of 2.5%. The 2-sided alpha level of 2.5% for the sample size calculation is selected to ensure that at least 1 of the 2 primary efficacy endpoints will pass the Hochberg procedure (Hochberg, 1988) to control the overall alpha level at 5.0%."

*[verbatim, same source, §4.2.6 Multiple Comparisons/Multiplicity]* — "Although the sample size estimates were based on the conventional Hochberg procedure, a parallel gatekeeping strategy based on the truncated Hochberg procedure (Dmitrienko et al. 2011) will be used to control the family-wise type I error rate at 5% (2-sided) and to allow alpha to pass along from the analyses of the primary endpoint of PFS to the analyses of the key secondary endpoint of OS... The analyses will use a truncation fraction of 0.9: r1 = 0.05*0.9 + 0.05/2*(1-0.9) = 0.0475; r2 = 0.05/2*0.9 + 0.05/2*(1-0.9) = 0.025."

*[verbatim, same source, OS analysis timing and alpha adjustment]* — "OS is planned to be analyzed at the following 2 time points: At the time of the primary PFS analysis..., and At the time of the final OS analysis (when approximately 50% of the subjects have died)... A Haybittle-Peto rule will be used to adjust the alpha for the analyses of OS at 2 time points."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 217639, Reference ID 5116375, Conclusions on the Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness]* — "Study RAD1901-308 also statistically met its PFS endpoint in the ITT population with a median PFS of 2.8 months (95% CI: 1.9, 3.8) in the elacestrant arm compared to 1.9 months (95% CI: 1.9, 2.1) in the SOC arm (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.55-0.88; p= 0.0018), however the FDA considered these results to be primarily driven by the 48% of patients in the ESR1-mut subpopulation. The FDA concluded that a clinically meaningful improvement in PFS had not been demonstrated for patients in the ESR1-mut-not detected (nd) subpopulation (52% of ITT)."

*[verbatim, same source, benefit-risk conclusion]* — "The review team concluded that elacestrant did not demonstrate a favorable benefit-risk profile for patients in the ESR1-mut-nd subpopulation... In contrast, the review team concluded that elacestrant demonstrated a favorable benefit-risk profile for patients in the ESR1-mut subpopulation... Therefore, the review team recommends granting regular approval to elacestrant in the ESR1-mut subpopulation... [this] will be the first FDA-approved therapy specifically for patients with ESR1 mutation(s)."

*[verbatim, same source, §9 Advisory Committee Meeting and Other External Consultations]* — "The FDA did not refer this application to an advisory committee as there were no efficacy or safety issues identified during the review which required external input for the proposed indication."

### 156. retifanlimab-dlwr (Zynyz) — BLA 761334

**Sponsor:** Incyte Corporation

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adult patients with metastatic or recurrent locally advanced Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC); per the label, "This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and duration of response. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in confirmatory trials."

**Approval date:** March 22, 2023 (original action letter; a corrected letter was issued March 24, 2023 solely to add FDORA accelerated-approval language, with the effective action date remaining March 22, 2023)

**Pivotal trial:** POD1UM-201 / INCMGA 0012-201 (NCT03599713) — an open-label, multiregional, single-arm Phase 2 study of retifanlimab 500 mg IV every 4 weeks in patients with metastatic or recurrent locally advanced MCC who had not received prior systemic therapy for advanced disease; primary efficacy population N=65 chemotherapy-naive patients (FDA's primary analysis population), with a broader safety population of 105 patients

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label trial
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR) / duration of response (DoR) / disease control rate (DCR), assessed by independent central/radiographic review (ICR/IRC) per RECIST v1.1
- *Primary analysis:* Descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (point estimate + CI, no formal hypothesis test), using an Exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval for ORR/DCR ("CI calculated based on the exact method for binomial distributions") and Brookmeyer-Crowley / Klein-Moeschberger log-log-transformed CIs for median DOR (Kaplan-Meier)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* A single formal futility interim analysis was pre-specified (after ~20 chemotherapy-naive patients assessable for response), reviewed by an independent DMC, with a stop-for-futility rule (conditional power <20%, equivalent to <6 responders); no alpha-spending for efficacy claims since the confirmatory analysis was descriptive, not a formal hypothesis test
- *Missing data/bias:* No formal imputation for missing response assessments — patients with missing/insufficient data to ascertain response are counted as non-responders/included in the ORR denominator ("no data imputation will be applied")
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval based on single-arm ORR/DoR, confirmatory trial required (postmarketing requirement 4412-1: a confirmatory multicenter trial enrolling ≥100 patients followed ≥12 months for ORR/DOR durability, plus overall survival analysis at 70% deaths or 3 years' follow-up); no FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this BLA

**Trial design & endpoints**

- POD1UM-201 was a non-randomized, open-label, single-arm, multicenter/multiregional Phase 2 trial (allocation: non-randomized per ClinicalTrials.gov) enrolling 107 total participants (chemotherapy-naive and chemotherapy-refractory cohorts, though only the 65 chemotherapy-naive patients constituted the FDA primary efficacy/registrational population), with the chemotherapy-refractory cohort restricted to enrollment only up to Protocol Amendment 4 per sponsor decision after FDA feedback limited the primary endpoint to the chemotherapy-naive subset (SAP Amendment 1, 27 JUN 2018).
- The primary endpoint was ORR, defined per the SAP as "the percentage of participants with CR or PR at any postbaseline visit before first PD or new anticancer therapy, according to RECIST v1.1 (Eisenhauer et al 2009) as determined by an ICR," with investigator-assessed ORR reported as a pre-specified sensitivity analysis and an efficacy-evaluable-population analysis as a supportive analysis.
- Sample size was justified against two historical single-arm benchmarks (avelumab ORR 39.7%, lower 95% CI 30.7%, D'Angelo et al 2019; pembrolizumab ORR 56%, lower 95% CI 35%, Nghiem et al 2016/2019), targeting an assumed ORR of ~48% in ~60 chemotherapy-naive patients, which the SAP states gives "over 80% power to exclude the lower 95% confidence limit of 30% with α = 0.025 (1-sided)" — i.e., an implicit performance-goal framing used only for sample-size planning, while the reported primary analysis itself remained descriptive (2-sided 95% CI, no formal test).
- A pre-planned futility interim analysis occurred after ~20 chemotherapy-naive patients were response-evaluable; the SAP records that the independent Data Monitoring Committee reviewed this interim look, found ORR by ICR exceeded the futility threshold, and recommended the study continue as planned.
- FDA's Multi-Discipline Review states plainly that "No inferential procedures were used to evaluate the single-arm study results. The efficacy evaluation was based on the magnitude of objective response rate and adequate duration of response" — confirming FDA reviewed the primary analysis as a descriptive point-estimate-plus-CI exercise, not a formal hypothesis test, consistent with the single-arm accelerated-approval pathway.
- Confirmed ORR by ICR in the 65-patient primary efficacy population was 52.3% (95% CI: 39.5, 65.0) [FDA MDR Table 17] / reported in the label as 52% (95% CI: 40, 65), with 18% complete responses; of 34 responders, DOR was ≥6 months in 76.5% and ≥12 months in 61.8%, with median DOR not reached (95% CI: 14.0, NE) at a median follow-up of 13.9 months.
- FDA required a postmarketing confirmatory trial (PMR 4412-1) enrolling at least 100 additional patients followed a minimum of 12 months to verify ORR/DOR durability, plus an overall-survival analysis once 70% of patients have died or all have been followed ≥3 years; no ODAC/advisory committee meeting was convened for BLA 761334, as FDA noted it had already approved two other single-arm anti-PD-1/PD-L1 agents (avelumab, pembrolizumab) for MCC and identified no new safety/efficacy issues warranting external discussion (a separate ODAC on 24 June 2021 concerned a different retifanlimab BLA, 761209, for anal canal carcinoma, and is unrelated to this MCC approval).

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2023/761334Orig1s000correctedlbl.pdf

- *[verbatim, SAP §3.4 "Sample Size Considerations"]* "Based on a target ORR of 48% and a sample size of approximately 60, this study has over 80% power to exclude the lower 95% confidence limit of 30% with α = 0.025 (1-sided) in the chemotherapy-naive population."
- *[verbatim, SAP §3.4]* "Approximately 100 chemotherapy-naive participants will be enrolled for the final analysis. This sample size ensures that half of the 95% CI will be approximately 10% for an ORR ranging from 40% to 60%. This sample size also ensures 99% power to detect any AE with an underlying event rate as low as 0.5%."

Objective response rate and its exact 95% CI will be presented. In addition, ORR by investigator assessment will be provided as sensitivity analysis for the primary endpoint. The analysis will be repeated using the efficacy evaluable population as supportive analysis."

- *[verbatim, SAP §11 "Interim Analyses"]* "An analysis is planned after approximately 20 chemotherapy-naive participants are assessable for response according to RECIST v1.1. The primary intent of this analysis is to minimize unnecessary exposure of participants to INCMGA00012 in the event of futility... At the time of this amendment, the DMC has reviewed the data for the interim analysis. The preliminary efficacy based on the ORR assessed by ICR exceeded the futility threshold, and the DMC recommended the study to proceed as planned."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, "Statistical Issues"]* "No major statistical issues were identified that impacted the results or interpretation of the efficacy results from PODIUM-201. No inferential procedures were used to evaluate the single-arm study results. The efficacy evaluation was based on the magnitude of objective response rate and adequate duration of response."

The trial will enroll at least 100 patients to be followed for a minimum of 12 months to establish the objective response rate and characterize the durability of response. Include an analysis of overall survival, when 70% of patients have died, or all patients have been followed for at least three years."

### 157. epcoritamab-bysp (Epkinly) — BLA 761324

**Sponsor:** Genmab US, Inc. (Genmab); AbbVie is a collaborator/co-commercialization partner per the ClinicalTrials.gov record for the pivotal trial.

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), not otherwise specified, including DLBCL arising from indolent lymphoma, and high-grade B-cell lymphoma, after two or more lines of systemic therapy — approved under accelerated approval based on response rate and durability of response, with continued approval contingent on verification and description of clinical benefit in confirmatory trial(s).

**Approval date:** May 19, 2023.

**Pivotal trial:** EPCORE NHL-1 (Study GCT3013-01; NCT03625037), an open-label, multi-cohort, multicenter, single-arm Phase 1/2 trial; efficacy in the accelerated-approval decision was based on 157 patients with relapsed/refractory large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL) in the aggressive-NHL expansion cohort (label's Table 10 reports on a 148-patient subset restricted to DLBCL-NOS/high-grade B-cell lymphoma, excluding other LBCL subtypes such as PMBCL and FL grade 3B).

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label trial
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR) / duration of response (DoR) / disease control rate (DCR)
- *Primary analysis:* Exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval; sample size informed by an exact binomial test against a pre-specified performance goal (35% ORR null vs. 50% ORR alternative), though FDA notes no formal hypothesis test was actually performed on the reported result
- *Missing data/bias:* FDA statistical review explicitly flagged the historical-control comparator (35% ORR benchmark) as subject to cross-trial confounding (design, conduct, response-assessment intervals, population differences) and stated the null hypothesis was used only to size the trial, not to test efficacy
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval based on single-arm ORR/DoR, confirmatory trial required

**Trial design & endpoints**

- EPCORE NHL-1 (GCT3013-01) enrolled patients with R/R LBCL after ≥2 prior lines of systemic therapy including an anti-CD20 antibody; it excluded patients with CNS lymphoma involvement, prior allogeneic HSCT/solid organ transplant, active infection, or impaired T-cell immunity, and used step-up dosing in Cycle 1 (0.16 mg Day 1, 0.8 mg Day 8, 48 mg Days 15 and 22) followed by 48 mg on a weekly/every-2-week/every-4-week schedule that tapers by cycle.
- The primary efficacy endpoint was ORR (CR+PR) assessed by an Independent Review Committee (IRC) per Lugano 2014 criteria, with duration of response (DoR) as a co-primary/key secondary efficacy measure; in the 157-patient LBCL expansion cohort ORR by IRC was 63% (95% CI 55–71%) with 39% CR (95% CI 31–47%), and median DoR was 15.5 months at a median DoR follow-up of 9.8 months (label's narrower 148-patient DLBCL/HGBCL efficacy population reported ORR 61% [95% CI 52.5–68.7], CR 38%, median DoR 15.6 months [95% CI 9.7, NR], 9-month DoR estimate 63%).
- No formal statistical hypothesis testing was performed on the expansion cohort; a sample size of 128 DLBCL subjects (assuming 10% non-evaluable rate) was estimated to give ~90% power to detect an alternative ORR of ≥50% at 2-sided alpha 0.05 using a one-sample exact binomial test under a null hypothesis of ORR ≤35%, with futility probability at end of Stage 1 of ~30% under the null and 2.1% under the alternative.
- The 35% ORR performance-goal benchmark was derived from response rates of available third-line-and-later therapies (chemoimmunotherapy regimens 25–38% ORR, polatuzumab vedotin + BR ~63% ORR, CAR T-cell therapies 50–73% ORR with DoR 9.2–16.7 months); FDA's statistical reviewer explicitly cautioned that using this historical control to judge treatment effect is "challenging" given cross-trial differences, and stated "the null hypothesis of 35% was only used to inform the sample size" rather than to formally test efficacy.
- A supportive Japanese single-arm cohort (Study GCT3013-04, n=36) reported ORR by IRC of 56% (95% CI 38–72%) with 44% CR, which FDA considered consistent with and supportive of the GCT3013-01 pivotal results, while noting the same single-arm limitations (time-to-event endpoints deemed exploratory/not interpretable without a comparator arm).
- Sensitivity analyses compared IRC-assessed ORR to investigator-assessed ORR (58.6% in LBCL subjects, 95% CI 50.5–66.4%) with 88.9% concordance between IRC and investigator assessments, plus subgroup ORR analyses (per-protocol, response-evaluable, and modified response-evaluable populations) that FDA found consistent with the primary analysis.
- Safety was characterized by a Grade ≥2 cytokine release syndrome (CRS) rate that the step-up/priming dosing regimen (0.16 mg/0.8 mg/48 mg) was specifically designed to mitigate; FDA's clinical pharmacology review found the proposed priming and intermediate doses produced numerically lower peak IL-6 concentrations and lower incidence of ≥Grade 2 CRS versus other regimens tested in dose escalation, supporting the dosing regimen as "strong evidence" of CRS attenuation; in the safety pool (n=167) 50.3% of subjects experienced any-grade CRS (mostly Grade 1–2, no Grade 4/5), with median time to CRS onset of 16.0 days generally following the first full 48 mg dose on Cycle 1 Day 15.
- FDA did not convene the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) or hold any external advisory committee meeting for this application, stating the application "did not raise significant efficacy or safety issues for the recommended indication."
- FDA imposed three postmarketing requirements (PMRs) and one postmarketing commitment (PMC): PMR #1 is the accelerated-approval confirmatory trial — a randomized trial of epcoritamab monotherapy versus investigator's choice of standard therapy in R/R LBCL with overall survival as the primary endpoint (secondary endpoints PFS and response rate; trial completion 12/2024, final report 12/2025); PMR #2 is a pediatric dose-confirmation/safety/PK/preliminary-efficacy trial; PMR #3 is an integrated long-term safety analysis of ICANS, neurologic toxicity, hematologic AEs, and infections; the PMC addresses safety/efficacy/PK/PD characterization in U.S. racial and ethnic minority patients.
- The approved label carries a boxed warning for cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS), mandates the step-up dosing schedule specifically to reduce CRS incidence/severity, and requires 24-hour post-dose hospitalization after the Cycle 1 Day 15 (first full 48 mg) dose.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review BLA 761324, Statistical Review section, "Sample Size," p.102]* "Assuming a non-evaluable rate of 10%, a sample size of 128 subjects in DLBCL group was estimated to provide approximately 90% power to detect the alternative hypothesis of at least 50% ORR while ensuring a 2-sided significance level of 0.05 using one-sample exact binomial test under the null hypothesis of at most 35% ORR. The probability of futility at the end of Stage 1 was approximately 30% under the null and 2.1% under the alternative hypothesis."
- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review BLA 761324, Statistical Review, pp.102–103]* "No formal hypothesis testing was performed on the aNHL expansion cohort... The FDA agrees with Applicant's description of the Statistical Analysis Plan; no formal hypothesis testing was performed on the aNHL expansion cohort. The 35% ORR rate was considered as a benchmark based on therapies with regular approval or standard of care regimens to inform the proposed sample size. The FDA agrees with Applicant's calculation of sample size."
- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review BLA 761324, Table 34, p.119]* "Overall response rate (ORR)... 99 (63.1%)... (95% CI) (55.0, 70.6)... Based on the Clopper and Pearson method."
- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review BLA 761324, Statistical Review, Conclusions section]* "A 35% ORR rate was chosen to compare with ORR rates obtained in GCT3013-01 and GCT3013-04 studies. The use of this 35% control rate from historical trials to assess whether the observed treatment effect represents an improvement over available therapy is challenging. There can be differences across trials (e.g., in design, conduct, response assessment intervals, study population, etc.) which may or may not be easily discernible and which could lead to erroneous conclusions... Thus, the null hypothesis of 35% was only used to inform the sample size for the two studies respectively."
- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review BLA 761324, Statistical Review, Conclusions section]* "Analyses for time-to-event endpoints are not interpretable in a single arm study due to lack of comparator arm. FDA considers such endpoints exploratory and not adequate to be used as measures of efficacy in single-arm trials intended to support approval."
- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review BLA 761324, Clinical Pharmacology section 6.3.2.2, pp.86–87]* "The proposed 0.16 mg priming dose and 0.8 mg intermediate dose of epcoritamab produced similar or numerically lower peak IL-6 concentrations compared with the other priming and intermediate doses tested in the Dose Escalation Part of the GCT3013-01 trial... A diminishing relationship between IL-6 peak concentration and CRS incidence over time was observed, which provides strong evidence that the proposed step-up dosing regimen (ie, 0.16 mg priming/0.8 mg intermediate doses) attenuated the incidence of CRS."
- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review BLA 761324, Section 9, p.237]* "This application was not presented to the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee or other external consultations because the application did not raise significant efficacy or safety issues for the recommended indication."
- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review BLA 761324, Section 13, p.243]* "Complete a randomized clinical trial in patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma. The trial should compare epcoritamab monotherapy to an investigator's choice of standard therapies for patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma. The primary endpoint should be overall survival with secondary endpoints that include progression-free survival and response rate." (PMR #1; Trial Completion 12/2024, Final Report Submission 12/2025)
- *[verbatim, Epkinly USPI, original approval label, Highlights of Prescribing Information]* "This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on response rate and durability of response. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial(s)."

### 158. flotufolastat F 18 (Posluma) — NDA 216023

**Sponsor:** Blue Earth Diagnostics Ltd.

**Indication approved:** POSLUMA is a radioactive diagnostic agent indicated for positron emission tomography (PET) of prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-positive lesions in men with prostate cancer (1) with suspected metastasis who are candidates for initial definitive therapy, or (2) with suspected recurrence based on elevated serum prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level.

**Approval date:** May 25, 2023 (standard review, 505(b)(1); NDA submitted/received May 25, 2022).

**Pivotal trial:** LIGHTHOUSE / BED-PSMA-301 (NCT04186819) — newly diagnosed, unfavorable intermediate-, high-, or very-high-risk prostate cancer, pre-prostatectomy nodal staging — and SPOTLIGHT / BED-PSMA-302 (NCT04186845) — suspected biochemical recurrence after prior therapy.

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison) — both LIGHTHOUSE and SPOTLIGHT were prospective, multicenter, single-arm, open-label, within-patient Phase 3 imaging trials (no control arm; every enrolled patient served as their own comparison against a reference standard), with flotufolastat F 18 PET/CT interpreted by both a local (site) reader and, for the primary endpoint, by three blinded independent central readers (BIE), with a pre-specified majority (2-of-3) read as the primary analysis.
- *Endpoints:* LIGHTHOUSE co-primary endpoints were patient-level sensitivity and specificity of flotufolastat F 18 PET for detecting pelvic lymph node (N1) metastasis against histopathology from radical prostatectomy plus pelvic lymph node dissection (PLND); SPOTLIGHT co-primary endpoints were patient-level Correct Detection Rate (CDR, percentage of patients with at least one true-positive lesion regardless of coexisting false positives) and region-level positive predictive value (PPV), both against a composite Standard of Truth (SoT) of histopathology or confirmatory imaging.
- *Primary analysis:* Each co-primary endpoint was tested against a pre-specified minimum performance goal using one-sided exact (Clopper-Pearson) binomial confidence intervals — LIGHTHOUSE: H0: Sensitivity ≤22.5% or Specificity ≤82.5% vs H1: Sensitivity >22.5% and Specificity >82.5%; SPOTLIGHT: H0: CDR ≤36.5% or PPV ≤62.5% vs H1: CDR >36.5% and PPV >62.5%; a trial was declared successful only if the lower bound of the 95% CI exceeded the performance goal for both co-primary endpoints in the same two of the three blinded independent readers.
- *Multiplicity:* Both SAPs specify one-sided 0.025 exact binomial tests for each co-primary endpoint per reader, and reader-level multiplicity across the three independent BIE readers was handled by a pre-specified "success" rule requiring both co-primary endpoints to reach significance in the same at least two of the three readers, per the FDA's 2007 diagnostic-test guidance explicitly cited in both SAPs.
- *Missing data/bias:* Performance-measure analysis without an independent reference standard (verification bias) applied materially to SPOTLIGHT — FDA's review found only 69/366 EAP patients (18.9%) had histopathology SoT, the remainder relying on a composite imaging-based SoT read centrally but "directed by" the PET-positive lesion location, which FDA flagged as a "major weakness" potentially lowering PPV; for LIGHTHOUSE, 60/356 imaged patients (16.9%) were excluded from the primary Efficacy Analysis Population (chiefly because PET-detected M1 disease diverted them from RP/PLND, so no histopathology was ever available), and FDA ran its own tipping-point missing-data sensitivity analysis (a 20% disease-positive imputation rate among the excluded patients) to argue the sensitivity goal would in fact have been met in two of three readers.
- *Regulatory:* No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this NDA; notably, both pivotal trials formally missed one of their two co-primary endpoints (LIGHTHOUSE missed the sensitivity goal in all three readers; SPOTLIGHT missed the region-level PPV goal in all three readers) yet FDA concluded substantial evidence of effectiveness was nonetheless established from the totality of the two mutually supportive trials.

**Trial design & endpoints**

- LIGHTHOUSE (BED-PSMA-301, NCT04186819) enrolled 356 adult men with newly diagnosed, untreated, biopsy-proven unfavorable intermediate-, high-, or very-high-risk prostate cancer (NCCN v1.2020 criteria) who were candidates for radical prostatectomy with pelvic lymph node dissection; each patient received a single 8 mCi (296 MBq, ±20%) IV dose of flotufolastat F 18 with PET/CT acquired 50-70 minutes post-injection, was read locally to guide management and, for the primary endpoint, by three blinded independent central readers (majority/2-of-3 read as the pre-specified primary analysis), and then proceeded to standard-of-care RP and PLND within 60 days, with resected pelvic lymph node tissue analyzed histopathologically as the Standard of Truth for N1 disease; co-primary endpoints were patient-level sensitivity and specificity for N1 detection, and results ranged 22.9-30.0% sensitivity (all three readers' 95% CI lower bounds below the 22.5% goal, i.e., the goal was not formally met) and 92.9-96.9% specificity (all readers comfortably exceeding the 82.5% goal, p<0.001).
- SPOTLIGHT (BED-PSMA-302, NCT04186845) enrolled 391 men with suspected biochemical recurrence being considered for curative-intent salvage treatment, with the same single-dose flotufolastat F 18 PET/CT and three-blinded-central-reader (majority-read) design; because most recurrent lesions could not ethically or feasibly be biopsied, the reference standard was a composite Standard of Truth combining histopathology (available in only a minority of patients) with centrally adjudicated confirmatory conventional imaging obtained within a defined post-scan window; co-primary endpoints were patient-level CDR and region-level PPV (up to three regions per patient, with variance adjusted for within-patient clustering of regions), and results were 48.3-50.9% CDR (all three readers' 95% CI lower bounds above the 36.5% goal — endpoint formally met) and 46.2-60.3% PPV (all three readers' 95% CI lower bounds below the 62.5% goal — endpoint formally not met).
- Both trials pre-specified subgroup analyses (by PCa risk category, most recent PSA level, race, and age) using confidence intervals only, without formal hypothesis testing, and both used kappa statistics to assess inter- and intra-reader agreement among the three blinded independent PET readers as a secondary/exploratory endpoint.
- FDA's Multi-Discipline Review concluded that, despite each trial formally missing one co-primary endpoint, "the effectiveness and clinical utility of flotufolastat F 18 PET were still evident in the investigated patient populations of these two mutually supportive trials," citing added diagnostic value from the PPV exceeding background nodal-metastasis prevalence in LIGHTHOUSE and the ability of flotufolastat F 18 to upstage patients (N0→N1 in 3.7-5.1%; M0→M1 in 8-12.2%) and to detect recurrent lesions with reasonable reliability (PPV) in SPOTLIGHT.

**Other resources**

- ClinicalTrials.gov API confirms both records include posted large documents: LIGHTHOUSE (NCT04186819) has both a Study Protocol and a Statistical Analysis Plan (dated 2021-10-01), and SPOTLIGHT (NCT04186845) has both a Study Protocol and a Statistical Analysis Plan (dated 2021-10-07) — both retrieved directly for this entry via the CT.gov large-docs CDN rather than reverse-engineered.
- IPD/dataset access: LIGHTHOUSE's ClinicalTrials.gov IPD Sharing Statement is explicitly "NO"; SPOTLIGHT's record carries no IPD Sharing Statement module at all. No genuine individual patient-level data sharing plan by Blue Earth Diagnostics is confirmed for either trial.
- Post hoc/secondary analyses of pooled LIGHTHOUSE + SPOTLIGHT data have since been published on normal-organ biodistribution (Penny et al., *Am J Nucl Med Mol Imaging* 2024;14(5):337-344, PMID 39583908) and urinary activity (Kuo et al., *Mol Imaging Biol* 2024;26(1):53-60, PMID 37932609).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, LIGHTHOUSE SAP v3.0, Section 2.1 "Primary Objective(s)", p.10]* "The primary objective of the study is to assess the sensitivity and specificity of rhPSMA-7.3 (18F) positron emission tomography (PET) in detecting N1 disease (as determined by the central BIE) on a patient level compared to the histopathology of pelvic lymphatic tissue removed during RP and PLND. At least one positive pelvic LN on PET (N1) and one positive LN as determined by histopathology (pN1) on the same side of the pelvis (left or right) will be deemed a True Positive (TP) at the patient level."
- *[verbatim, LIGHTHOUSE SAP v3.0, Section 4.14.1 "Analysis and Data Conventions", p.24]* "The primary hypothesis involves a joint assessment of sensitivity and specificity against individual performance goals: H0: Sensitivity ≤ Se0 or Specificity ≤ Sp0 versus H1: Sensitivity > Se0 and Specificity > Sp0... Performance goals of 22.5% (Se0) for sensitivity and 82.5% (Sp0) were selected based on the low sensitivity but high specificity of other PSMA ligands used for lymph node staging."
- *[verbatim, LIGHTHOUSE SAP v3.0, Section 4.14.1.2 "Handling of Dropouts or Missing Data", p.24]* "Missing evaluation results in the biopsy/surgery will be assigned the worst value. Hence, a side with a positive rhPSMA-7.3 (18F) PET will be considered as false positive (i.e. SoT will be set to negative), while a side with negative rhPSMA-7.3 (18F) PET will be a false negative (i.e. SoT set to positive)."
- *[verbatim, LIGHTHOUSE SAP v3.0, Section 4.2, p.14 — identical language appears in the SPOTLIGHT SAP]* "CIs of proportions will be presented to three decimal places (e.g. 1/3 will be a proportion of 0.333) and exact intervals (Clopper-Pearson) will be employed unless specified otherwise."
- *[verbatim, LIGHTHOUSE SAP v3.0, Section 4.16 "Determination of Sample Size", p.34]* "A total sample size of approximately 375 patients is planned in order to obtain 300 evaluable patients for analysis of the primary endpoint. Assuming a sensitivity of 40% of PSMA ligands for detecting N1 disease (based on the previous OSPREY [NCT02981368]), a sample size of 75 positive cases provides 90% power to reject the performance goal of 22.5%."
- *[verbatim, LIGHTHOUSE SAP v3.0, Section 4.12 "Standard of Truth", pp.21-22]* "Histology or confirmatory imaging will be used as the Standard of Truth (SoT)... Reads of the confirmatory imaging as SoT will be directed by rhPSMA-7.3 (18F) PET findings (for confirmation of lesion location only)."
- *[verbatim, SPOTLIGHT SAP v3.0, Section 2.1 "Primary Objective(s)", p.12]* "The primary objective of the study is to assess the patient level CDR and region level PPV of rhPSMA-7.3 (18F) PET for BCR of PCa using histopathology or imaging as a SoT. The CDR is defined as the percentage of all patients scanned who have at least one TP lesion (localized correspondence between rhPSMA-7.3 (18F) PET imaging and the reference standard) regardless of any coexisting FP findings."
- *[verbatim, SPOTLIGHT SAP v3.0, Section 4.16 "Efficacy Evaluation", pp.32-33]* "H0: CDR ≤36.5% or PPV ≤62.5% versus H1: CDR >36.5% and PPV >62.5%... For the study to be considered a success, the p-values for both endpoints must be statistically significant (P<0.025) for at least two out of the three blinded image evaluation readers (same readers for both CDR and PPV)."
- *[verbatim, SPOTLIGHT SAP v3.0, Section 4.18 "Determination of Sample Size", p.41]* "Approximately 316 patients will be enrolled in this study. For the PPV endpoint, based on a one-sided 0.025 exact binomial test and assuming a true PPV of 73.5%, a sample size of 190 positive cases provides >88% power for the evaluation of region level PPV (H0: PPV ≤62.5%)."
- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, "Conclusions on the Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness", pp.15-16]* "Both BED-PSMA-301 and BED-PSMA-302 failed to meet one of two pre-specified co-primary diagnostic performance endpoints. However, as discussed elsewhere in this review, the effectiveness and clinical utility of flotufolastat F 18 PET were still evident in the investigated patient populations of these two mutually supportive trials."
- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Clinical Review discussion of BED-PSMA-302 results]* "A major weakness of the BED-PSMA-302 trial was the use of a composite reference standard, which may have contributed to lowering PPV values... The overreliance on imaging for SoT determination in BED-PSMA-302, with only 69 out of the 366 patients in the EAP (18.9%) having histopathology, was a further weakness of the trial."

### 159. glofitamab-gxbm (Columvi) — BLA 761309

**Sponsor:** Genentech, Inc. (a member of the Roche Group)

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), not otherwise specified, or large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL) arising from follicular lymphoma, after two or more lines of systemic therapy — approved under accelerated approval based on response rate and durability of response.

**Approval date:** June 15, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** NP30179 (NCT03075696), an open-label, multicenter, multicohort Phase I/II trial sponsored by Hoffmann-La Roche; the pivotal efficacy cohort was expansion Cohort D3 (fixed-dose obinutuzumab-pretreatment cohort), analyzed in 132 patients

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label trial; fixed-duration regimen (glofitamab given for a maximum of 12 cycles regardless of continuing response, after a single fixed 1000 mg obinutuzumab pretreatment dose)
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR) / duration of response (DoR); complete response (CR) rate was the SAP-designated primary endpoint, supported by ORR/DoR — FDA's own efficacy determination was based on ORR and DoR (assessed by IRC per Lugano 2014 criteria) supported by CR-rate durability, a subtle divergence between the Applicant's and FDA's framing of which measure was "primary"
- *Primary analysis:* Exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval for response-rate point estimates; Brookmeyer-Crowley method for the 95% CI around median duration of response (Kaplan-Meier); reverse Kaplan-Meier method used to estimate median follow-up for DOR
- *Missing data/bias:* FDA required the SAP be amended (Version 3, per FDA feedback from a Type C meeting) specifically to revise "censoring rules for response assessment prior to the [clinical cutoff date] for the primary analysis" and to add a COVID-19 sensitivity analysis on the primary endpoint (IRC-assessed CR); FDA's own efficacy-population definition also diverged from the Applicant's, including all patients who received ≥1 glofitamab dose and were assessed (or unevaluable) for response, versus the Applicant's population which included a patient treated with obinutuzumab but not glofitamab
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval based on single-arm ORR/DoR, confirmatory trial required — confirmatory trial is the randomized Phase III STARGLO study (Study GO41944, glofitamab + GemOx vs. rituximab + GemOx, primary endpoint OS); no FDA advisory committee meeting was held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- NP30179 (initial protocol dated 21 July 2016, amended 11 times through the 27 May 2021 data cutoff) enrolled adult patients with R/R DLBCL, NOS, or transformed follicular lymphoma (trFL) after ≥2 prior systemic therapies including an alkylating agent and an anti-CD20 antibody; the pivotal efficacy population (n=132) had a median of 3 prior lines of therapy (range 2-7), 83% refractory to most recent therapy, and 30% with prior CAR-T therapy.
- Dosing: a single fixed 1000 mg IV dose of obinutuzumab 7 days before glofitamab initiation (Gpt, to mitigate cytokine release syndrome), then glofitamab step-up dosing of 2.5 mg (Cycle 1 Day 8), 10 mg (Cycle 1 Day 15), then 30 mg on Day 1 of Cycles 2-12 (21-day cycles), for a fixed maximum of 12 cycles.
- The Applicant's SAP-designated primary endpoint was CR rate assessed by IRC per 2014 Lugano Classification criteria; secondary endpoints included investigator-assessed CR rate, ORR, duration of complete response (DOCR), duration of response (DOR), progression-free survival (PFS), and time to first (complete) response — FDA agreed with the CR-rate primary endpoint as prespecified but based its own efficacy determination on IRC-assessed ORR supported by CR-rate durability, and stated it "considers the time-to-event endpoints, including progression-free survival, to have limited interpretability in single-arm trials" and treats them as exploratory.
- Sample size/historical control: the original sample size was set to rule out a CR rate of 20%, derived from a random-effects meta-analysis of 19 published studies (1,373 patients, 2007-2019) of chemoimmunotherapy, CAR-T, lenalidomide, polatuzumab vedotin, and other R/R LBCL regimens, which calculated a historical control CR rate of 20% (95% CI: 14%-28%).
- The SAP was revised across five versions: V1 (approved June 2020, primary analysis for R/R DLBCL cohorts including pivotal Cohort D3); V2 (June 2021, specifically named Cohort D3 as pivotal); V3 (post-Type-C-meeting, August 17 2021, revised censoring rules for response assessment prior to the clinical cutoff date and added a COVID-19 sensitivity analysis on IRC-assessed CR); V4 (updated analyses of monotherapy cohorts); V5 (expanded analysis across Cohorts D2/D3/D5) — FDA states there were no changes to the planned primary-endpoint analysis for pivotal Cohort D3 itself, and that the revisions were "primarily based on the Agency's feedback that all patients with R/R LBCL who had received 2 prior systemic therapies and received the recommended glofitamab dosage should be included in the primary efficacy analysis... and that all responders should have at least 6 months of follow up for DOR."
- Results: ORR by IRC was 56% (95% CI: 47, 65) with a CR rate of 43% (95% CI: 35, 52) and median time to response of 42 days; at an estimated median follow-up of 11.6 months, estimated median DOR was 18.4 months (95% CI: 11.4, NE) with an estimated 9-month DOR rate of 68.5% (95% CI: 56.7, 80.3); in patients achieving CR, median DOR was not estimable (95% CI: 16.8 months, NE).
- FDA's postmarketing requirements: (1) an accelerated-approval PMR to "complete a randomized clinical trial that evaluates the clinical benefit of glofitamab in patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma," comparing glofitamab + GemOx to rituximab + GemOx with OS as the primary endpoint and PFS/response rate as secondary endpoints (this became STARGLO); (2) a PREA pediatric PMR; plus two postmarketing commitments (persistence of treatment effect after 12-cycle completion; safety/efficacy characterization in racial/ethnic minorities).

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2023/761309Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (original, 2023) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2023/761309s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 5192035) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/761309Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf

- Pivotal publication: Dickinson MJ, Carlo-Stella C, Morschhauser F, et al. Glofitamab for Relapsed or Refractory Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma. *N Engl J Med.* 2022;387(24):2220-2231. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2206913), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36507690/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Glofitamab+for+Relapsed+or+Refractory+Diffuse+Large+B-Cell+Lymphoma+Dickinson+NEJM+2022)

**Other resources**

- IPD/dataset access: Roche/Genentech participates in clinical-trial data-sharing generally (Roche is a Vivli member), but trial-specific IPD availability for NP30179 was not individually confirmed in this research and should be treated as unconfirmed rather than absent.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for BLA 761309.
- Confirmatory trial STARGLO (GO41944) was, per the FDA review, "well underway and fully enrolled" at the time of the accelerated approval decision, supporting FDA's favorable benefit-risk determination.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761309, "Study Endpoints," p.116]* "The primary efficacy endpoint of this study was CR rate assessed by an Independent Review Committee (IRC) according to the 2014 Lugano Classification Criteria (Cheson et al. 2014). Additional efficacy endpoints included CR rate (Investigator [INV]-assessed), and ORR, duration of complete response (DOCR), duration of response (DOR), progression-free survival (PFS), time to first overall response (TFOR)... and time to first complete response (TFCR)."
- *[verbatim, same source]* "FDA agrees with the Applicant's description of the primary endpoint of complete response rate per Lugano 2014 criteria as prespecified in the study... For regulatory purposes, response rate is considered an intermediate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit. FDA's assessment of efficacy is based on IRC-assessed objective response rate and supported by duration of response. FDA considers the time-to-event endpoints, including progression-free survival, to have limited interpretability in single-arm trials and therefore considers them exploratory."
- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, "Statistical Analysis Plan and Amendments," pp.116-117]* "The SAP was discussed with the FDA as part of the Type C Content and Format meeting, 17 August 2021, and was subsequently amended (V3) to incorporate FDA feedback on censoring rules for response assessment prior to the CCOD for the primary analysis and to add coronavirus-19 (COVID-19) sensitivity analysis on the primary endpoint IRC-assessed CR... The revisions were primarily based on the Agency's feedback that all patients with R/R LBCL who had received 2 prior systemic therapies and received the recommended glofitamab dosage should be included in the primary efficacy analysis, including the dexamethasone (D5) cohort, and that all responders should have at least 6 months of follow up for DOR measured from the date of initial response."
- *[verbatim, same source]* "The sample size calculation was based on CR rate, using 20% as the historical reference CR rate based on a systematic literature review of regimens including CAR-T therapies, chemoimmunotherapy, lenalidomide, polatuzumab vedotin, and other regimens. This review identified 19 studies that together included 1373 patients... A random-effects model meta-analysis was performed, which calculated a historical control rate of 20% (95% CI: 14% to 28%)."
- *[verbatim, same source]* "The FDA's efficacy population includes all patients who received at least one dose of glofitamab and were assessed for response or who were not evaluable for response for any reason. This contrasts with the Applicant's efficacy population which included a patient treated with obinutuzumab but not glofitamab. For response rates, frequency counts and percentages were summarized, and exact 95% CIs for the rates were calculated using the Clopper-Pearson method. For Kaplan-Meier analyses, the Brookmeyer-Crowley method was used to construct the 95% CI for the median DOR. Median follow-up for DOR was estimated using the reverse Kaplan-Meier method."
- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, "1.2 Conclusions on the Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness," p.21]* "The ORR per IRC was 56% (95% CI: 47, 65), with a CR rate of 43% (95% CI: 35, 52) and median time to response of 42 days. With an estimated median follow-up of 11.6 months, the estimated median DOR was 18.4 months (95% CI: 11.4, NE)... The accelerated approval and favorable benefit-risk determination are supported by the confirmatory trial being well underway and fully enrolled."
- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, "12 Postmarketing Requirements and Commitment"]* "1. Complete a randomized clinical trial that evaluates the clinical benefit of glofitamab in patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. The trial should compare glofitamab in combination with gemcitabine and oxaliplatin (GemOx) to rituximab in combination with GemOx for patients with relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. The primary endpoint should be overall survival with secondary endpoints that include progression-free survival and response rate."
- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, "8 Advisory Committee Meeting and Other External Consultations"]* "This application was not presented to the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee or other external consultations."

### 160. quizartinib (Vanflyta) — NDA 216993

**Sponsor:** Daiichi Sankyo, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia (AML) that is FLT3-ITD positive (as detected by an FDA-approved test), in combination with standard cytarabine and anthracycline induction and standard cytarabine consolidation chemotherapy, and as continuation monotherapy following consolidation chemotherapy

**Approval date:** July 20, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** QuANTUM-First (Protocol AC220-A-U302), NCT02668653

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; event-driven trial; randomization 1:1 stratified by age, region, and WBC count at diagnosis
- *Endpoints:* Overall survival (OS, primary — time from randomization to death from any cause); event-free survival (EFS, key secondary, IRC-assessed per Cheson 2003/ELN Guidance criteria, with investigator assessment as sensitivity analysis); CR rate, CR rate with FLT3-ITD MRD negativity, composite CR (CRc) rate, and CRc-with-MRD-negativity rate (further secondary, tested in that hierarchical order); relapse-free survival, duration of CR (exploratory)
- *Primary analysis:* Stratified log-rank test with the 3 randomization stratification factors, 2-sided alpha 0.05; Kaplan-Meier estimation with Brookmeyer-Crowley method for median OS/EFS 95% CIs; stratified Cox proportional-hazards model for HR estimation (SAS PROC PHREG); Clopper-Pearson's method (reused "Exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval" term) for CR/CRc rate CIs; Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by the 3 randomization factors for between-arm CR/CRc rate comparisons
- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing — serial hierarchically ordered gatekeeping: OS (primary) tested first; if significant at 2-sided alpha 0.05, EFS tested next; then CR rate, CR-rate-with-MRD-negativity, CRc rate, and CRc-rate-with-MRD-negativity in that fixed order; testing stops at the first non-significant result in the sequence
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* No formal group-sequential interim efficacy analysis; a single primary OS analysis was performed when the target 287 OS events were observed and a minimum of 24 months had elapsed since the last subject was randomized (or, failing that, at a maximum of 30 months); sample size/timing was derived from simulations using a piecewise-exponential model to account for an observed post-30-month survival "plateau effect" in the historical RATIFY trial control arm; Data Monitoring Committee (DMC/DSMB) reviewed accumulating safety/efficacy data
- *Regulatory:* Prior related NDA (212166, QuANTUM-R, relapsed/refractory monotherapy) was the subject of a May 2019 ODAC and received a Complete Response Letter in June 2019; QuANTUM-First's own review involved two separate February/March 2023 Special Government Employee (SGE) consultations (not a full public ODAC) specifically on benefit-risk given non-significant secondary endpoints (EFS, CR rate) and QTc-prolongation/Torsade de Pointes/cardiac-arrest risk requiring a boxed warning and a REMS with Elements to Assure Safe Use (ETASU)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- QuANTUM-First (AC220-A-U302): randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multiregional Phase III trial of quizartinib (an oral FLT3 inhibitor) versus placebo, each added to standard "7+3" cytarabine/anthracycline induction and cytarabine consolidation chemotherapy, followed by up to 36 cycles of continuation monotherapy (quizartinib or placebo), in adults 18-75 years old with newly diagnosed FLT3-ITD-positive AML; ~536 planned subjects randomized 1:1, stratified by age, region (North America, Europe, Asia excluding Japan, and Japan), and WBC count at diagnosis
- Primary endpoint: OS, defined as time from randomization to death from any cause, analyzed in the ITT population via stratified log-rank test; key secondary endpoint: EFS (IRC-assessed per applicable AML response-criteria guidance), defined as time from randomization to induction treatment failure, relapse from CR/CRc, or death, whichever occurs first
- Sample size/power: simulations (accounting for the RATIFY-trial-observed survival plateau after 30 months) targeted 287 OS events among ~536 subjects for 84% power at 2-sided alpha 0.05, with OS analyzed either at 287 events (minimum 24 months post-last-randomization) or at a maximum of 30 months if that event count was not reached; simulations run in EAST v6.3, analyses in SAS v9.2+
- Multiplicity: family-wise type-I error controlled via a serial hierarchically ordered gatekeeping strategy — OS tested first; if significant, EFS (IRC) tested next; then CR rate, CR-with-FLT3-ITD-MRD-negativity rate, CRc rate, and CRc-with-MRD-negativity rate, each via CMH test stratified by the 3 randomization factors; testing stops once any one test in the sequence is non-significant
- Results: median OS 31.9 months (quizartinib) vs. 15.1 months (placebo), HR 0.78 (95% CI 0.62-0.98), p=0.0324, satisfying the primary endpoint; per FDA's SGE-meeting framing, the secondary efficacy endpoints of EFS and CR rate were not statistically significant, and there was no observed OS benefit specifically attributable to the continuation/maintenance monotherapy phase post-HSCT — FDA's benefit-risk review explicitly weighed the significant primary OS result against these non-significant secondaries and the drug's unique QTc-prolongation/Torsade de Pointes/cardiac-arrest risk

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2023/216993Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2023/216993s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 5211984, NDA 216993) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/216993Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf

- Pivotal publication: Erba HP, Montesinos P, Kim HJ, et al.
