[DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(23)00464-6>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37116523/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Quizartinib%20plus%20chemotherapy%20in%20newly%20diagnosed%20FLT3-ITD-positive%20AML%20QuANTUM-First)

**Other resources**

- Daiichi Sankyo's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for QuANTUM-First; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for this trial specifically.
- No public ODAC meeting was held for NDA 216993 itself; instead, FDA convened two separate Special Government Employee (SGE) consultations (February 27 and March 6, 2023) specifically to discuss benefit-risk given the non-significant secondary endpoints and QTc-prolongation risk. A prior, unrelated quizartinib NDA (212166, relapsed/refractory monotherapy, QuANTUM-R) was reviewed by a full public ODAC in May 2019 and received a Complete Response Letter the following month; quizartinib was separately approved in Japan (MHLW, June 2019) for relapsed/refractory FLT3-ITD-positive AML under the same brand name Vanflyta.
- A REMS with Elements to Assure Safe Use (ETASU) is required, addressing quizartinib's boxed warning for QT interval prolongation, Torsade de Pointes, and cardiac arrest; FDA's Office of Surveillance and Epidemiology concluded a communication-plan-based REMS (rather than a more restrictive ETASU-only program) was necessary given the seriousness of the arrhythmia risk.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, QuANTUM-First (AC220-A-U302) Protocol/SAP, Version 7.0, 26-May-2021, §2.1.1 Primary Objective]* — "The primary objective is to compare the effect of quizartinib versus placebo (administered with standard induction and consolidation chemotherapy, and as maintenance monotherapy for up to 36 cycles) on the primary endpoint of overall survival (OS) in subjects with newly diagnosed FLT3-ITD (+) AML."
- *[verbatim, same source, §11.4.1.1 Primary Efficacy Analyses]* — "The primary analysis for OS will be based on the ITT Analysis Set. Comparison of distribution of OS between treatment groups will be made using a stratified log-rank test with the 3 stratification factors used at randomization at a 2-sided 5% significance level. The median OS will be calculated based on Kaplan-Meier estimates and the corresponding 95% CI will be calculated using the method provided by Brookmeyer and Crowley... In addition, the stratified Cox proportional hazards regression model will be performed to estimate hazard ratio (HR) along with the 2-sided 95% CI, and SAS PROC LIFETEST and PROC PHREG will be used in the analysis."
- *[verbatim, same source, §11.4.1.2 Secondary Efficacy Analyses]* — "The CR rate, rate of subjects achieving CR with FLT3-ITD MRD negativity, CRc rate, and rate of subjects achieving CRc with FLT3-ITD MRD negativity will be summarized along with 95% CI using Clopper-Pearson's method. Comparisons... between treatment groups will be made using a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test with the 3 stratification factors used in randomization. To control for the family-wise type I error rate for the primary and secondary efficacy endpoints, a serial hierarchically ordered gatekeeping strategy will be employed. The primary assessment of OS in the ITT Analysis Set will be evaluated first, and if significant at a 2-sided alpha of 0.05, a statistical evaluation of EFS by IRC... will be performed... After EFS evaluation, the order of other secondary endpoints to be tested will be CR rate, rate of subjects achieving CR with FLT3-ITD MRD negativity, CRc rate, and rate of subjects achieving CRc with FLT3-ITD MRD negativity. Testing will stop once 1 test in the sequence fails to be statistically significant."
- *[verbatim, same source, §11.5 Sample Size Determination]* — "For OS, a plateau effect was observed after 30 months of treatment in the control arm of the Midostaurin RATIFY study. Therefore, a piecewise exponential model was considered to account for the plateau effect. Simulations indicate that about 84% power and 287 events will be obtained to achieve a statistically significant difference in OS distribution with approximately 536 subjects by a 2-sided log-rank test at the 0.05 significance level when OS is analyzed at 24 months after the last subject is randomized."
- *[verbatim, same source, §5.1.2 Method of Treatment Allocation]* — "Subjects will be randomized into 1 of the 2 treatment groups (quizartinib or placebo) in a 1:1 ratio. The randomization will be stratified by age, region, and WBC count at the time of diagnosis of AML."
- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 216993, Reference ID 5211984, Conclusions]* — "In conclusion, the primary endpoint used to assess efficacy in the pivotal QuANTUM-First trial was OS. The median OS was 31.9 months (95% CI [...]) [...] with HR 0.78 (95% CI 0.62, 0.98); p = 0.0324."
- *[verbatim, same source, §9 Advisory Committee Meeting and Other External Consultations]* — "Meetings with two separate Special Government Employees (SGEs) were conducted on February 27, 2023 and March 6, 2023. Noting the lack of statistical significance of the secondary efficacy endpoints of EFS and CR rate on QuANTUM-First, the lack of an OS benefit in patients treated with quizartinib maintenance post-HSCT, and the unique risk of QTc prolongation, FDA requested a discussion of benefit-risk for the proposed indication, as well as the need for additional education and risk mitigation measures to prevent serious and potentially fatal arrhythmias."
- *[verbatim, same source, on the earlier related application]* — "In September 2018, a new drug application (NDA 212166) for quizartinib was submitted for the treatment of patients with relapsed/refractory (R/R) FLT3-ITD (+) AML based on Study AC220-007 (QuANTUM-R). The application was the subject of an Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting in May 2019, and the FDA subsequently issued a Complete Response Letter in June 2019."

### 161. talquetamab-tgvs (Talvey) — BLA 761342

**Sponsor:** Janssen Biotech, Inc. (Janssen Research & Development, LLC is the ClinicalTrials.gov study sponsor)

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma who have received at least four prior lines of therapy, including a proteasome inhibitor, an immunomodulatory agent, and an anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody; approved under accelerated approval based on response rate and durability of response.

**Approval date:** August 9, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** MonumenTAL-1 (Study 64407564MMY1001 / MMY1001), a single-arm, open-label, multicenter Phase 1/2 study combining a Phase 1 dose-escalation/expansion study (NCT03399799) and a Phase 2 dose-expansion study (NCT04634552) under one protocol; the two registered subcutaneous regimens (0.4 mg/kg weekly and 0.8 mg/kg every 2 weeks) were the RP2Ds identified in Phase 1 Part 2 and each was independently enrolled and analyzed as a separate, non-randomized Phase 2 Part 3 cohort (Cohort A = 0.4 mg/kg weekly, Cohort C = 0.8 mg/kg biweekly; supportive Cohort B enrolled patients with prior T-cell redirection exposure)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label trial — non-randomized, parallel dose-regimen expansion cohorts (Phase 2 Part 3 Cohort A and Cohort C), each independently analyzed for efficacy rather than compared to one another; FDA's statistical review states plainly "Assignment to treatment: Randomization was not applicable," so patients were assigned to a cohort based on RP2D selection and enrollment period, not individually randomized between the 0.4 mg/kg weekly and 0.8 mg/kg biweekly regimens — "non-randomized parallel dose-regimen expansion cohorts, each analyzed independently"
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR) / duration of response (DoR) — ORR per Independent Review Committee (IRC) using IMWG 2016 criteria was the primary endpoint for the pivotal Phase 2 analysis; DOR, VGPR-or-better, CR-or-better, sCR, MRD-negativity, TTR, PFS and OS were key secondary/exploratory endpoints, with FDA specifically excluding PFS/OS/TTR from its efficacy determination because "time-to-event endpoints... cannot be accurately interpreted in single-arm studies"
- *Primary analysis:* Exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval — the SAP specified that the ORR and its 2-sided 95% exact CI for each cohort was presented, calculated separately for each dose-regimen cohort with no formal hypothesis test against a pre-specified performance goal; no cross-cohort statistical comparison was performed since the two regimens were not intended to be compared to each other
- *Missing data/bias:* Participants with no post-baseline response assessment were counted as non-responders in the ORR analysis; response after start of subsequent anticancer therapy was not counted; sensitivity analyses using investigator and computerized-algorithm assessment (with kappa statistics vs. IRC) supported the primary IRC-based result
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval based on single-arm ORR/DoR, confirmatory trial required — postmarketing requirement (PMR 4473-1) mandates a randomized confirmatory trial (talquetamab-based regimen vs. standard therapy, primary endpoint PFS) now running as MonumenTAL-3 (NCT05455320); FDA's approval letter states talquetamab "was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant public health questions"; boxed warning for CRS and neurologic toxicity/ICANS with a shared TECVAYLI-TALVEY REMS with ETASU; additional PMR (4473-2) to characterize oral toxicity (stomatitis/dysgeusia-related weight loss) from on-target, off-tumor GPRC5D effects

**Trial design & endpoints**

- MonumenTAL-1 was conducted in three parts: Part 1 (Phase 1 dose escalation, IV and SC dosing from 0.0005 mg/kg up through 1.6 mg/kg monthly) and Part 2 (Phase 1 dose expansion at putative RP2Ds) were considered Phase 1 with safety as the primary endpoint, while Part 3 (Phase 2) enrolled patients at the two confirmed RP2Ds — 0.4 mg/kg SC weekly (Cohort A) and 0.8 mg/kg SC every 2 weeks (Cohort C), both in T-cell-redirection-naive patients, plus Cohort B for patients previously exposed to T-cell redirection therapy — with ORR as the Part 3 primary endpoint.
- FDA's primary efficacy population (187 patients: 100 on 0.4 mg/kg weekly, 87 on 0.8 mg/kg biweekly) was restricted to patients who had received ≥4 prior lines of therapy including a PI, an IMiD, and an anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody, matching the approved indication.
- At the September 12, 2022 data cutoff, ORR by IRC was 73% (95% CI: 63.2%–81.4%) for the 0.4 mg/kg weekly cohort with median DOR 9.5 months (95% CI: 6.5, not estimable), and 73.6% (95% CI: 63.0%–82.4%) for the 0.8 mg/kg biweekly cohort with median DOR not estimable at a median follow-up of 5.9 months, with an estimated 85% of responders maintaining response for at least 9 months.
- FDA repeatedly flagged during End-of-Phase-1, Type C, and pre-BLA meetings that it had concerns about basing accelerated approval on a single-arm trial and had recommended the sponsor consider a randomized registration trial; FDA also declined to pool Phase 1 and Phase 2 patients for the primary efficacy analysis (Phase 1 pooling was accepted only as "supportive"), and flagged that median follow-up for the 0.8 mg/kg biweekly cohort (5.8 months in the indicated ≥4-prior-line population) was shorter than the 9-12 months FDA generally recommends for a robust durability assessment.
- A supportive subset of 32 patients from Cohort B (previously exposed to T-cell redirection therapy, treated at 0.4 mg/kg weekly, ≥4 prior lines) showed an ORR by IRC of 72% (95% CI: 53%-86%), which FDA noted was based on a small sample without a pre-planned sample size calculation and was included in the USPI as supportive but not primary evidence.
- Because MonumenTAL-1 was single-arm, FDA compared the observed ORR/DOR narratively (not via formal statistical test) against the closest available therapy, selinexor + dexamethasone (ORR 25.3%, DOR 3.8 months), noting teclistamab (a BCMA-directed bispecific) was excluded as "available therapy" because it remained under accelerated approval itself, and that CAR-T products were excluded due to patient-specific manufacturing and toxicity considerations.
- Substantial evidence of effectiveness was established from this single trial alone; FDA's MDR states MonumenTAL-1 was "considered to be the scientific equivalent of two clinical investigations," consistent with FDA's "one adequate and well-controlled study plus confirmatory evidence" pathway for accelerated approval in a serious, unmet-need setting.

- No FDA advisory committee (ODAC or otherwise) meeting was held for talquetamab; the approval letter states the application "was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant public health questions on the role of the biologic."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, "Statistical Analysis Plan and Amendments," p.115]* "Analysis of efficacy and safety was based on All Treated Analysis Set. For analysis of ORR, participants with no postbaseline data were considered as non-responders. Response after the start of subsequent therapy was not considered. The ORR and its 2-sided 95% exact CI for each cohort was presented. A forest plot of subgroup analysis on ORR was generated. Sensitivity analyses of ORR was performed using disease response based on computerized algorithm and investigator assessment according to IMWG response criteria."

It should be noted that time-to-event endpoints such as TTR, PFS, and OS cannot be accurately interpreted in single-arm studies."
- *[verbatim, FDA MDR, "Summary and Conclusions — Statistical Issues," p.216-217]* "There were no major statistical issues identified in this submission... The clinical benefit of talquetamab will need to be verified in a randomized confirmatory clinical trial."

### 162. elranatamab-bcmm (Elrexfio) — BLA 761345

**Sponsor:** Pfizer Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma who have received at least four prior lines of therapy, including a proteasome inhibitor, an immunomodulatory agent, and an anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody — approved under accelerated approval based on response rate and durability of response.

**Approval date:** August 14, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** MagnetisMM-3 (Study C1071003, NCT04649359), an open-label, multicenter, non-randomized Phase 2 study; the approved indication is supported by the 97-patient primary efficacy population within Cohort A (BCMA-directed-therapy-naive patients who met the ≥4-prior-line criterion and were treated at the recommended dose)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label trial; two-cohort structure with independent primary endpoints for each cohort — Cohort A (BCMA-directed-therapy-naive) and Cohort B (prior exposure to a BCMA-directed therapy), each with its own null-hypothesis performance goal and its own two-stage exact-binomial design — "two independently-tested, non-comparative prior-therapy-defined cohorts within a single-arm trial, each with a distinct null-hypothesis ORR threshold"
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR) / duration of response (DoR), assessed by Blinded Independent Central Review (BICR) per IMWG criteria
- *Primary analysis:* Exact binomial test against a pre-specified performance goal — Cohort A tested H0: ORR ≤30% vs. H1: ORR >30% (1-sided alpha 0.025); Cohort B tested H0: ORR ≤15% vs. H1: ORR >15% (1-sided alpha 0.025); response-rate point estimates reported with Exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence intervals; Brookmeyer-Crowley method used for the 95% CI around median DOR (Kaplan-Meier)
- *Multiplicity:* Within Cohort A, a hierarchical gatekeeping procedure tested a key secondary endpoint (ORR in the EMD-negative subgroup, H0: ORR ≤38%) only if the Cohort A primary ORR null was rejected, followed by ORR in the EMD-positive subgroup (H0: ORR ≤12%) only if the EMD-negative test also rejected, each at 1-sided alpha 0.025
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* A non-binding futility/efficacy interim analysis was pre-specified for each cohort (Cohort A at 90 patients enrolled/treated with sufficient follow-up, Cohort B at 30 patients), with stopping boundaries "equivalent to what would be induced if using the rho family beta-spending boundary with parameter = 3 and the rho family alpha-spending boundary with parameter = 5" when implemented via an exact binomial test at each look — reusing the taxonomy's rho-family alpha/beta-spending framework in a single-arm exact-binomial context rather than a group-sequential survival-endpoint context; no interim analysis was ultimately performed for Cohort B due to insufficient follow-up
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval based on single-arm ORR/DoR, confirmatory trial required — confirmatory trial is the ongoing randomized Phase 3 study MagnetisMM-5 (C1071005: elranatamab monotherapy and elranatamab + daratumumab vs. daratumumab + pomalidomide + dexamethasone, primary endpoint PFS by BICR), 554 of a planned 750 patients enrolled as of the review; no FDA advisory committee meeting was held; boxed warning for CRS and neurotoxicity/ICANS with a shared REMS

**Trial design & endpoints**

- MagnetisMM-3 (C1071003) is an open-label, multicenter, non-randomized Phase 2 study of elranatamab monotherapy in patients with multiple myeloma refractory to at least one proteasome inhibitor (PI), one immunomodulatory drug (IMiD), and one anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody, using step-up priming doses (12 mg Day 1, 32 mg Day 4) before the full 76 mg weekly dose from Day 8, with a switch to biweekly dosing available for responders from week 25.
- Two cohorts were defined by prior BCMA-directed therapy exposure: Cohort A (BCMA-naive) and Cohort B (previously exposed to a BCMA-directed therapy, e.g., an antibody-drug conjugate, CAR-T, or another bispecific); the sponsor's SAP specified independent sample sizes/hypotheses for each: 120 Cohort A patients for ~98% power to detect a true ORR of 48% (vs. H0 ORR ≤30%) and 60 Cohort B patients for ~91% power to detect a true ORR of 34% (vs. H0 ORR ≤15%), both at 1-sided alpha 0.025 using a two-stage exact-binomial design.
- FDA's primary efficacy population was 97 Cohort A patients meeting the ≥4-prior-line (PI + IMiD + anti-CD38 mAb) criterion and treated at the proposed dosing regimen (median age 69; 96.9% triple-class refractory; 94.8% refractory to last line); the ORR in this population was 57.7% (95% CI: 47.3%, 67.7%), with median DOR not reached at a median follow-up of 11.1 months among responders (DOR rate 90.4% at 6 months, 82.3% at 9 months).
- Among 64 Cohort B patients (all with prior PI/IMiD/anti-CD38 mAb exposure) the ORR was 33.3% (95% CI: 22.0%, 46.3%), with median DOR not reached at a median follow-up of 10.2 months (DOR rate 84.3% at 9 months) — supportive but not part of the accelerated-approval efficacy claim, which was restricted to BCMA-naive patients.
- FDA's benefit-risk narrative compared elranatamab's Cohort A ORR/DOR against the only relevant approved comparator, selinexor + dexamethasone (ORR 25.3%, 95% CI 16.4-36.0; DOR 3.8 months), explicitly excluding teclistamab (a BCMA-directed bispecific approved in 2023 for the same population but "not considered available therapy because this remains under accelerated approval") and the two approved BCMA CAR-T products (excluded due to patient-specific manufacturing requirements and toxicity profile).
- Confirmatory evidence for the accelerated-approval benefit-risk determination was the ongoing randomized Phase 3 confirmatory trial MagnetisMM-5 (C1071005), described by FDA as "well underway" with 554 of a planned 750 patients enrolled as of July 12, 2023, testing elranatamab monotherapy and elranatamab + daratumumab against daratumumab + pomalidomide + dexamethasone with PFS by BICR as the primary endpoint.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, MagnetisMM-3 Statistical Analysis Plan, 26 OCT 2022, §5.1.1 "Hypotheses and Sample Size"]* "This study has two cohorts: Cohort A will enroll participants who are naïve to BCMA-directed therapies, and Cohort B will enroll participants who have prior exposure to BCMA-directed therapies. The primary objective of this study is to determine the efficacy in Cohort A and Cohort B with respect to ORR by BICR, as defined by IMWG. In Cohort A, the study will test the null hypothesis that the ORR by BICR as defined by IMWG is ≤30% versus the alternative hypothesis that the ORR by BICR as defined by IMWG is >30%. In Cohort B, the study will test the null hypothesis that the ORR by BICR as defined by IMWG is ≤15% versus the alternative hypothesis that the ORR by BICR as defined by IMWG is >15%."
- *[verbatim, same source]* "A total of 120 participants enrolled and treated in Cohort A provides approximately 98% power to detect a true ORR by BICR of 48% to reject the null hypothesis, with a 1-sided significance level of 0.025. Similarly, a total of 60 participants enrolled and treated in Cohort B provides approximately 91% power to detect a true ORR by BICR of 34% to reject the null hypothesis, with a 1-sided significance level of 0.025."
- *[verbatim, same source, §5.1.2 "Decision Rules"]* "An interim analysis for both futility (non-binding) and efficacy will be conducted for the primary endpoint for Cohort A and Cohort B. At the time of the interim analysis, the testing rule based on an exact binomial test will depend on the actual number of participants included in the analysis for each cohort with sufficient follow-up... It can be noted that the futility and efficacy stopping boundaries for both cohorts at the interim analysis are equivalent to what would be induced if using the rho family beta-spending boundary with parameter = 3 and the rho family alpha-spending boundary with parameter = 5, respectively, when testing the results with an exact binomial test."
- *[verbatim, same source, §6.1.1 "Main Analysis"]* "The primary endpoint is ORR by BICR, defined as the proportion of participants with an objective response by BICR per IMWG criteria... Point estimates of ORR will be calculated along with corresponding 2-sided exact 95% CIs using the Clopper-Pearson method. The null hypotheses will be tested at 1-sided alpha of 0.025 using an exact binomial test independently in each cohort."
- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761345, "Conclusions on the Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness"]* "The primary efficacy population included 97 patients in Cohort A with RRMM who had received at least 4 prior lines of therapy, including a PI, an IMiD, and an anti-CD38 mAb and who were treated at the proposed dosing regimen... The ORR in the efficacy population was 57.7% (95% CI: 47.3%, 67.7%)... Among the 64 patients enrolled in Cohort B who previously received a PI, IMiD, and an anti-CD38 mAb, the ORR was 33.3% (95% CI: 22.0%, 46.3%)."
- *[verbatim, same source]* "Selinexor has regular approval for the treatment of adult patients with RRMM who have received 4 prior therapies... Teclistamab, a bispecific BCMA directed CD3 T-cell engager was approved in 2023 for the same population requested by the Applicant but is not considered available therapy because this remains under accelerated approval. The two CAR T-cell products... are not included in the Division's consideration of available therapy due to the requirement for patient-specific manufacturing and the toxicity profile of these products."
- *[verbatim, same source]* "The accelerated approval and favorable benefit-risk determination are supported by the confirmatory trial being well underway. The proposed confirmatory trial is the ongoing randomized controlled study MagnetisMM-5 (C1071005)... The primary endpoint of Study C1071005 is progression-free survival by blinded independent central review (BICR). The study is well underway with 554 of a planned 750 patients as of July 12, 2023."

### 163. toripalimab-tpzi (Loqtorzi) — BLA 761240

**Sponsor:** Shanghai Junshi Biosciences Co., Ltd. (originator/trial sponsor); Coherus BioSciences, Inc. (U.S. license holder/co-applicant)

**Indication approved:** Two indications for nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), both granted traditional (regular) approval: (1) in combination with cisplatin and gemcitabine, for the first-line treatment of adults with metastatic or with recurrent, locally advanced NPC; (2) as a single agent, for the treatment of adults with recurrent unresectable or metastatic NPC with disease progression on or after platinum-containing chemotherapy

**Approval date:** October 27, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** JUPITER-02 (Study JS001-015-III-NPC, NCT03581786) for indication (1), and POLARIS-02 (Study JS001-Ib-CRP-1.0, NCT02915432) for indication (2)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trial for JUPITER-02 (toripalimab + cisplatin/gemcitabine vs. placebo + cisplatin/gemcitabine, 1:1); single-arm, open-label trial for POLARIS-02 (Cohort 3, previously treated patients); both trials were conducted exclusively at sites in China (POLARIS-02) or China/Taiwan/Singapore (JUPITER-02) — regular approval based on entirely foreign (Asia-only) trial data under 21 CFR 314.106(b)
- *Endpoints:* Progression-free survival (PFS) by IRC per RECIST v1.1 (JUPITER-02 primary endpoint), with overall survival (OS) as a key secondary endpoint tested hierarchically; objective response rate (ORR) by BICR per RECIST v1.1 with duration of response (DoR) (POLARIS-02 primary/key endpoints, single-arm)
- *Primary analysis:* Stratified log-rank test and stratified Cox proportional-hazards model (JUPITER-02 PFS/OS, stratified by ECOG performance status and other randomization factors); Kaplan-Meier estimation throughout; for POLARIS-02, a descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (point estimate + CI, no formal hypothesis test against a pre-specified null) — the ORR of 21% (95% CI: 15, 28) with median DOR of 14.9 months was evaluated by FDA as "clinically meaningful" narratively rather than via a formal binomial test against a performance goal
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function used to approximate an O'Brien-Fleming boundary for JUPITER-02's PFS interim/final analysis (one interim analysis at ~130 PFS events [65% information fraction], final analysis at ~200 PFS events, two-sided stopping boundary p-values of 0.011 and 0.047 respectively); an independent Data Monitoring Committee (iDMC) reviewed safety on an ongoing basis and the single planned efficacy interim analysis
- *Regulatory:* Regular approval grounded in durable-ORR-as-direct-clinical-benefit (single-arm trial) — reused for the POLARIS-02-supported monotherapy indication, which FDA granted as traditional/regular approval (not accelerated approval, and with no confirmatory-trial PMR of the accelerated-approval type) based on POLARIS-02's durable ORR considered clinically meaningful in the intended second-line population, further supported by JUPITER-02's results; both indications relied on trial data collected entirely outside the U.S. (China/Taiwan/Singapore), evaluated by FDA under the 21 CFR 314.106(b) foreign-data framework (applicability to U.S. population/practice, investigator competence, and on-site inspection feasibility); FDA conducted on-site clinical investigator/site inspections in China (delayed by COVID-19 pandemic travel restrictions) to validate both trials' data before approval; no FDA advisory committee meeting was held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- JUPITER-02 randomized 289 patients with recurrent or metastatic NPC without prior systemic chemotherapy for recurrent/metastatic disease (prior curative-intent chemoradiation was allowed) 1:1 to toripalimab 240 mg or placebo, each combined with cisplatin + gemcitabine for up to 6 cycles, followed by toripalimab or placebo monotherapy maintenance until progression or unacceptable toxicity, in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled design; sample size (280 patients, 200 PFS events) was calculated for 80% power to detect a PFS hazard ratio of 0.67 at a 2-sided alpha of 0.05, assuming a 7-month median PFS in the chemotherapy-alone arm.
- The primary endpoint was PFS (IRC-assessed per RECIST v1.1), analyzed via a 1-sided stratified log-rank test (stratified by randomization factors) with the hazard ratio and 95% CI from a stratified Cox proportional-hazards model; secondary endpoints included ORR, DOR, disease control rate (DCR) by RECIST v1.1 and irRECIST, and OS.
- JUPITER-02 crossed its pre-specified O'Brien-Fleming/Lan-DeMets interim stopping boundary for PFS at the planned interim analysis (data cutoff 30 May 2020), reaching statistical significance; FDA's review states the demonstration of "a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in PFS... supported by a statistically significant improvement in ORR, a longer median DOR... and no evidence of a detrimental effect on OS" provided substantial evidence of effectiveness for the first-line combination indication, further supported at the final OS analysis by a statistically significant OS improvement (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.45-0.89, p=0.0083).
- POLARIS-02 was an open-label, multicenter, multicohort Phase Ib/II trial conducted exclusively in China, evaluating toripalimab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks as monotherapy across multiple advanced tumor types; the NPC efficacy population supporting the second-line monotherapy indication was 172 patients with unresectable/metastatic NPC previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy (a median of 2 prior lines), with ORR (BICR, RECIST v1.1) as the primary efficacy measure — 21% (95% CI: 15, 28) — and median DOR of 14.9 months (95% CI: 10.3, NE), with 83% of the 36 responders having DOR ≥6 months and 39% ≥12 months.
- FDA explicitly reasoned that the POLARIS-02 monotherapy indication did not require accelerated approval/a confirmatory trial: "the ORR of 21% with a median DOR of 14.9 months demonstrated in POLARIS-02 is considered clinically meaningful when considering the intended patient population, and the results of the JUPITER-02 study provide further confidence in the benefit of toripalimab for the treatment of advanced NPC," reflecting an expectation that most U.S. NPC patients would receive first-line toripalimab + chemotherapy and only a minority would need second-line monotherapy.
- Because both pivotal trials were conducted entirely in Asia, FDA applied the 21 CFR 314.106(b) foreign-data framework, concluding a "flexible regulatory approach is warranted given the high unmet need and lack of FDA approved immunotherapies for US patients with NPC," that the cisplatin/gemcitabine comparator matched U.S. standard of care, and that on-site clinical investigator/site inspections (delayed by COVID-19 China travel restrictions) validated the submitted data; FDA also required a postmarketing commitment to collect additional U.S.-population-representative clinical data for the combination indication.

**Other resources**

The interim and final analyses of PFS use the Lan DeMets alpha spending function to approximate the O'Brien Fleming boundary."

- *[verbatim, same source, results update section]* "The study has crossed the O'Brien-Fleming boundary for the planned interim analysis of primary endpoint PFS. Substantial evidence of effectiveness is now further supported by the results of the final analysis of OS, which demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in OS with a HR of 0.63 (95% CI: 0.45, 0.89, p-value 0.0083)."

### 164. fruquintinib (Fruzaqla) — NDA 217564

**Sponsor:** Takeda Pharmaceuticals U.S.A., Inc. (originally developed by Hutchmed/Hutchison MediPharma Limited, which sponsored the pivotal trial and holds the ClinicalTrials.gov registration)

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) who have been previously treated with fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-based chemotherapy, an anti-VEGF therapy, and, if RAS wild-type, an anti-EGFR therapy — regular approval

**Approval date:** November 8, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** FRESCO-2 (Study 2019-013-GLOB1, NCT04322539), a global, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trial, with the earlier China-only FRESCO trial as supportive evidence

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (quadruple masking: participant, care provider, investigator, outcomes assessor); event-driven trial; fruquintinib plus best supportive care (BSC) vs. placebo plus BSC, 2:1 randomization
- *Endpoints:* Overall survival (OS, primary endpoint); progression-free survival (PFS, key secondary endpoint)
- *Primary analysis:* Stratified log-rank test (1-sided, per SAP) for the primary OS comparison, accounting for randomization stratification factors; hazard ratio and 95% CI from a stratified Cox proportional-hazards model with treatment group as the only covariate; Kaplan-Meier estimation with Brookmeyer-Crowley log-log-transformed CIs for medians and landmark survival probabilities
- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing — a two-hypothesis family (H1: OS, H2: PFS) tested in strict order, with PFS superiority tested at the 2-sided 0.05 level only if the primary OS analysis reached 2-sided p≤0.05
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* One non-binding futility-only interim analysis of OS planned at approximately 1/3 of total required OS events (160 of ~480 events, per the amended/final SAP), using a Lan-DeMets spending-function approach; the independent Data Monitoring Committee (IDMC) was instructed to recommend stopping for futility only if the 1-sided stratified log-rank p-value at the interim was ≥0.772 (corresponding to an observed HR of 1.133), with no plan to stop early for efficacy
- *Missing data/bias:* Standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment for OS/PFS; a reversed-censoring-indicator Kaplan-Meier plot (attrition-bias-style sensitivity analysis) was pre-specified for PFS; sensitivity analyses re-ran the primary Cox/log-rank models using both stratified and unstratified approaches and both ITT and per-protocol populations
- *Regulatory:* Regular approval (not accelerated); no FDA advisory committee meeting was held; Takeda participates in Vivli's clinical-trial-data-sharing platform generally (trial-specific listing for FRESCO-2 not individually confirmed)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- FRESCO-2 was a global (Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific ex-China, Australia, Japan), multicenter, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trial enrolling 691 patients with refractory mCRC previously treated with fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-based chemotherapy, an anti-VEGF therapy, and (if RAS wild-type) an anti-EGFR therapy, plus either trifluridine-tipiracil or regorafenib (or both); patients received oral fruquintinib 5 mg once daily (3 weeks on/1 week off per 28-day cycle) plus BSC, or matching placebo plus BSC.
- The primary endpoint was OS, defined per the SAP as "the time (months) from date of randomization to death," analyzed via a 1-sided stratified log-rank test (2-sided-equivalent framing reported at the 0.05 level) accounting for randomization-schedule stratification factors, with the treatment-effect hazard ratio and 95% CI estimated from a stratified Cox proportional-hazards model; the key secondary endpoint was PFS, defined analogously and tested only if the primary OS analysis was statistically significant, per a fixed-sequence hierarchical testing procedure controlling overall type I error at 0.05.
- Sample size was based on detecting an OS hazard ratio of 0.73 (fruquintinib vs. placebo), yielding approximately 90% statistical power (per the final SAP version; an earlier version targeted 80% power before recruitment was expanded from an earlier planned total to 687-691 patients).
- One non-binding futility-only interim OS analysis was planned once approximately 1/3 of total OS events (160 events, per the amended text; an earlier SAP version cited 121 events) had occurred; the independent Data Monitoring Committee (IDMC) was to recommend stopping for futility only if the 1-sided stratified log-rank p-value was at least 0.772 (HR ≥1.133), with no efficacy stopping rule at the interim; the SAP's operating-characteristics text states there was "a 22.8% chance of terminating the study for futility at the interim analysis if the true median OS in fruquintinib arm is 5 months" (i.e., fruquintinib ineffective) versus only a 0.4% chance of stopping if the true median OS was 6.8 months (i.e., fruquintinib effective).
- Reported results (per FDA review and the pivotal publication): fruquintinib improved OS with an HR of 0.65 (95% CI: 0.51-0.83, 2-sided p<0.001) and also improved PFS (HR 0.32, 95% CI 0.27-0.39, i.e. HR 0.279-0.425 range cited across data cuts), statistically significant per the fixed-sequence hierarchy since the primary OS analysis was positive.
- No FDA advisory committee was convened; FDA's review states plainly that "no advisory committee was convened for this... application as the application did not raise any issues that warranted the committee's input."

- *[verbatim, same source, §9.2.5.1.1 "Primary Endpoint - Overall Survival"]* "A 1-sided stratified log-rank test will be used for the comparison of OS of the fruquintinib... The hazard ratio (HR) between the 2 treatment groups (fruquintinib vs placebo), together with its 95% CI, will be calculated from a stratified Cox proportional hazard model... in which the treatment group is the only covariate in the model."

Assuming an OS hazard ratio (HR) of 0.73 (fruquintinib arm/placebo arm), this sample size yields approximately 90% statistical power to detect superiority of the fruquintinib arm over placebo arm."
- *[verbatim, same source, "Interim Analyses"]* "One interim non-binding futility analysis is to be performed once 1/3 of the total number of overall survival (OS) events (i.e., 160 OS events) have occurred. There is a 22.8% chance of terminating the study for futility at the interim analysis if the true median OS in fruquintinib arm is 5 months... There is a 0.4% chance of stopping for futility... if the true median OS in fruquintinib arm is 6.8 months."
- *[verbatim, same source, "Multiplicity Adjustments"]* "The multiplicity problem includes 2 hypotheses of no effect: Hypothesis H1. Comparison of fruquintinib + BSC versus placebo + BSC for OS. Hypothesis H2. Comparison of fruquintinib + BSC versus placebo + BSC for PFS... A fixed-sequence (hierarchical) testing procedure is used to control the overall type I error rate at 0.05. If the resulting 2-sided p-value from the analysis of primary endpoint OS is ≤ 0.05, then, a superiority test for PFS will be conducted at the two-sided significance level of 0.05."
- *[verbatim, same source, "Key Secondary Efficacy Endpoint and Analysis"]* "A Kaplan-Meier plot of the time to censoring, where the censoring indicator of the primary PFS analysis is reversed, will be presented."
- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, "Executive Summary"]* "Fruquintinib is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) who have been previously treated with fluoropyrimidine‑, oxaliplatin‑, and irinotecan‑based chemotherapy, an anti‑VEGF therapy, and, if RAS wild‑type, an anti-EGFR therapy."
- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Section 9]* "No advisory committee was convened for this supplemental application as the application did not raise any issues that warranted the committee's input."

### 165. repotrectinib (Augtyro) — NDA 218213

**Sponsor:** Bristol Myers Squibb Company (originally developed by Turning Point Therapeutics, Inc., acquired by BMS in 2022; Turning Point remains the ClinicalTrials.gov study sponsor of record)

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) — covering both ROS1 tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI)-naive patients and patients previously treated with one ROS1 TKI (and no prior chemotherapy in that setting) — granted traditional (regular) approval for the full indication, not accelerated approval

**Approval date:** November 15, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** TRIDENT-1 (Study CA127-1024 / TPX-0005-01, NCT03093116), an international, single-arm, open-label, first-in-human Phase 1/2 dose-escalation-and-expansion study; the primary efficacy evidence comes from pooled expansion cohorts EXP-1 (ROS1 TKI-naive) and EXP-4 (1 prior ROS1 TKI, no prior chemotherapy)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label trial; multi-cohort expansion structure defined by prior ROS1-TKI/chemotherapy exposure (EXP-1 through EXP-6), with EXP-1 and EXP-4 pooled as the primary efficacy analysis populations — this is a ROS1-specific (not tissue/tumor-agnostic) multi-cohort design, so the taxonomy's "Tumor-agnostic (tissue-agnostic) basket trial" term does not apply; described here as "pooled prior-therapy-defined expansion cohorts within a single-arm, single-gene-target trial"
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR) / duration of response (DoR), confirmed ORR by blinded independent central review (BICR) per RECIST v1.1 as the primary endpoint; secondary endpoints included time to response (TTR), clinical benefit rate (CBR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), intracranial ORR (IC-ORR) and CNS-PFS per modified RECIST v1.1
- *Primary analysis:* Exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval — ORR point estimates with 2-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson exact CIs; duration of response summarized via Kaplan-Meier with landmark DOR-rate proportions (6, 9, 12, 18, 24 months) also using Clopper-Pearson exact CIs; no formal hypothesis test against a pre-specified performance goal was identified in the reviewed FDA sections — the analysis was descriptive (point estimate plus CI), consistent with a single-arm trial
- *Regulatory:* Regular approval based on single-arm ORR/DoR, supported by same-pharmacologic-class approved-drug precedent as confirmatory evidence rather than an independent randomized confirmatory trial — FDA concluded the statutory "substantial evidence of effectiveness" standard was met from TRIDENT-1 alone (a single adequate and well-controlled trial) plus confirmatory evidence consisting of the established effectiveness of entrectinib and crizotinib, two other ROS1 TKIs approved in the same indication on similarly durable ORR; no FDA advisory committee meeting was held; postmarketing requirements addressed PREA pediatric study obligations and hepatic-impairment/mass-balance pharmacokinetics, not an accelerated-approval clinical-benefit verification trial

**Trial design & endpoints**

- TRIDENT-1 enrolled patients with advanced solid tumors harboring ALK, ROS1, or NTRK1-3 rearrangements across Phase 1 (dose escalation) and Phase 2 (dose expansion) portions; the ROS1-positive NSCLC primary efficacy populations were pooled across the two study phases: pooled EXP-1 (TKI-naive, n=71: 8 from Phase 1, 63 from Phase 2) and pooled EXP-4 (1 prior ROS1 TKI and no prior chemotherapy, n=56), with patients dosed at the recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D) or, for some Phase 1 patients, at the dose administered during Phase 1; patients had to have received at least one dose of repotrectinib on or before October 15, 2021, and be followed for at least 8 months to be included in the primary efficacy analysis (19-Dec-2022 data cutoff).
- The primary endpoint was confirmed ORR by BICR per RECIST v1.1, defined as the proportion of patients with a confirmed complete response (CR) or partial response (PR); secondary endpoints included DOR, TTR, CBR, PFS, OS, and CNS-specific measures (IC-ORR, CNS-PFS) by modified RECIST v1.1.
- Results in the TKI-naive pooled EXP-1 cohort (n=71): ORR 79% (95% CI: 68, 88); median DOR 34.1 months (95% CI: 26, NE), with 70% of responders having DOR ≥12 months; intracranial responses were observed in 7 of 8 patients with measurable baseline CNS metastases. In the TKI-pretreated pooled EXP-4 cohort (n=56): ORR 38% (95% CI: 25, 52); median DOR 14.8 months (95% CI: 7.6, NE), with 48% of responders having DOR ≥12 months; intracranial responses were observed in 5 of 12 patients with measurable baseline CNS metastases, and responses were seen in 6 of 8 patients with documented ROS1 resistance mutations (including solvent-front G2032R and gatekeeper L2026M) following prior TKI therapy.
- FDA's Multi-Discipline Review states the "statutory requirement for demonstration of substantial evidence of effectiveness is met based on the efficacy results from a single adequate and well-controlled trial (TRIDENT-1) with confirmatory evidence consisting of evidence of effectiveness of other drugs (i.e., entrectinib and crizotinib) in the same pharmacologic class for the same indication," and that "an indication that includes patients who are ROS1 TKI naïve and who have received one prior ROS1 TKI is warranted based on the evidence of effectiveness demonstrated in both populations" — i.e., FDA granted a single, undifferentiated regular-approval indication spanning both prior-therapy subgroups, rather than splitting the indication by approval type.
- No formal statistical hypothesis test against a pre-specified null ORR was described in FDA's efficacy conclusion section; instead, FDA judged "the ORR, which is large in magnitude, along with the observed duration of responses... sufficient to establish clinical benefit in the genetically defined (ROS1-positive), rare subgroup of patients," a qualitative/narrative benefit-risk judgment characteristic of regular approval grounded in durable single-arm ORR for a rare, genetically-defined, high-unmet-need population.
- FDA's postmarketing requirements (5 PMRs, 4 PMCs per FDA's summary) addressed PREA pediatric study obligations and drug-drug-interaction/hepatic-impairment pharmacokinetics (a mass-balance study showed 89% of total repotrectinib-related radioactivity was recovered), not an accelerated-approval-style clinical-benefit-verification trial, consistent with this being a regular (not accelerated) approval.

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2023/218213Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (original, 2023) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2023/218213s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (Reference ID 5277412) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/218213Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2302299), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38197815/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Repotrectinib+ROS1+Fusion-Positive+Non-Small-Cell+Lung+Cancer+Drilon+NEJM+2024)

**Other resources**

- IPD/dataset access: Bristol Myers Squibb participates in clinical-trial data-sharing generally (BMS is a Vivli member), but trial-specific IPD availability for TRIDENT-1 was not individually confirmed in this research and should be treated as unconfirmed rather than absent.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for NDA 218213.
- Breakthrough Therapy Designations were granted separately for the TKI-naive ROS1+ NSCLC population (EXP-1) and, later, in additional settings, reflecting FDA's early recognition of the drug's potential across multiple ROS1-defined subgroups.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 218213, "Conclusions on the Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness"]* "The data submitted by the Applicant provides substantial evidence of effectiveness to support the traditional approval of repotrectinib for the treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive NSCLC. The recommendation for traditional approval is based on the results from TRIDENT-1... The statutory requirement for demonstration of substantial evidence of effectiveness is met based on the efficacy results from a single adequate and well-controlled trial (TRIDENT-1) with confirmatory evidence consisting of evidence of effectiveness of other drugs (i.e., entrectinib and crizotinib) in the same pharmacologic class for the same indication."
- *[verbatim, same source]* "The primary objective was to determine the confirmed objective response rate (ORR) as assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR) using Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version 1.1; ORR is defined as the proportion of patients with a confirmed complete response (CR) or partial response (PR)."
- *[verbatim, same source]* "Among the 71 ROS1 TKI-naïve patients, the ORR was 79% (95% CI 68, 88). The median duration of response was 34.1 months (95% CI 26, NE); 70% of responders had a DOR ≥ 12 months... Among the 56 patients who had received 1 prior ROS1 TKI, the ORR was 38% (95% CI 25, 52). The median duration of response was 14.8 months (95% CI 7.6, NE); 48% of responders had a DOR ≥ 12 months."
- *[verbatim, same source]* "Confirmatory evidence necessary to support an approval based on a single adequate and well-controlled trial derives from data from other products in the same class which are approved in the same indication as well as strong mechanistic evidence of ROS1 alterations being molecular drivers of NSCLC. Both entrectinib and crizotinib were approved for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic NSCLC whose tumors are ROS1-positive based on robust and durable tumor response rates and repotrectinib has a similar mechanism of action as these approved therapies."
- *[verbatim, same source]* "The submitted evidence meets the statutory evidentiary standard for traditional approval. Treatment with repotrectinib demonstrated a clinically meaningful and durable ORR among adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive NSCLC who were ROS1 TKI-naïve and ROS1 TKI-pretreated... An indication that includes patients who are ROS1 TKI naïve and who have received one prior ROS1 TKI is warranted based on the evidence of effectiveness demonstrated in both populations."
- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, statistical methodology section, p.~93]* "The primary endpoint of ORR is based on the radiologic assessments evaluated by the BICR for Phase 1 and Phase 2 of the TRIDENT-1 protocol using RECIST v1.1 and used the Efficacy Analysis Set, reported as the proportion of responders by RECIST v1.1 along with the corresponding 2-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson exact confidence interval. DOR... was calculated only for the subgroup of subjects with a confirmed objective tumor response (PR or CR) and analyzed and presented graphically using the Kaplan-Meier method... Landmark analyses are presented for the proportion of subjects with observed DOR and 95% CI, using the Clopper-Pearson method, of at least 6, 9, 12, 18, and 24 months."
- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Table 64, Section 1 Indications and Usage]* "Indicated for the treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC)... FDA reviewed and accepted the proposed indication."
- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Section 9]* "FDA did not refer this application to an advisory committee as no significant efficacy or safety [issues were identified]."

### 166. capivasertib (Truqap) — NDA 218197

**Sponsor:** AstraZeneca

**Indication approved:** In combination with fulvestrant, for adults with hormone receptor (HR)-positive, HER2-negative, locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer with one or more biomarker alterations (PIK3CA, AKT1, or PTEN) as detected by an FDA-approved test, following progression on or after an endocrine-based regimen

**Approval date:** November 16, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** CAPItello-291 (D3615C00001), NCT04305496

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; dual primary-population design testing PFS in both the all-comers overall population and a pre-specified PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered subgroup, both populations pre-specified from trial start rather than post-hoc; randomization stratified by liver metastases, prior CDK4/6 inhibitor use, and geographic region; dedicated China-cohort enrollment target (~134 patients) run in parallel to satisfy NMPA requirements
- *Endpoints:* Progression-free survival (PFS, dual primary — investigator-assessed per RECIST v1.1, in the overall population and in the altered subgroup; BICR-assessed PFS as sensitivity analysis); overall survival (OS, key secondary, in both populations); objective response rate (ORR, further secondary, tested only if OS positive)
- *Primary analysis:* Stratified log-rank test, stratified Cox proportional-hazards model, Kaplan-Meier estimation (all s)
- *Multiplicity:* Alpha recycling via a predefined multiple-testing procedure with alpha-exhaustive recycling (Burman et al 2009) that accounts for correlation between test statistics (Spiessens and Debois 2010); two families (PFS, then OS), each split across the overall and altered populations; ORR tested last only if OS significant in both populations
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* O'Brien-Fleming boundary via Lan-DeMets alpha-spending for the OS interim analysis (~394 events, 80% information fraction) and final analysis (~70% maturity); a small bespoke alpha spend (0.0001) was added at the PFS primary analysis data cutoff specifically to monitor for OS non-detriment, added "following FDA advice"
- *Regulatory:* Companion diagnostic co-approval — FoundationOne CDx (F1CDx) approved contemporaneously to identify PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN alterations; no FDA advisory committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- CAPItello-291: randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trial of capivasertib (400 mg BID, 4 days on/3 days off) plus fulvestrant vs. placebo plus fulvestrant in patients with HR+/HER2- locally advanced (inoperable) or metastatic breast cancer recurring or progressing on/after an aromatase inhibitor, with or without a prior CDK4/6 inhibitor; ~700 patients randomized (350/arm), stratified by liver metastases (yes/no), prior CDK4/6 inhibitor use (yes/no), and geographic region (3 regions); crossover from placebo to capivasertib was not permitted
- Dual primary endpoint: investigator-assessed PFS (RECIST v1.1) tested separately in the overall population and in the PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered subgroup (expected ~40-45% prevalence, with a list of eligible variants finalized before the primary analysis); key secondary endpoint OS in both populations; BICR-assessed PFS was a pre-specified sensitivity analysis
- Sample size/power: PFS primary analysis planned at ~77% maturity (542 events overall; 217 events in the altered subgroup assuming a 0.4 events ratio to overall); overall-population PFS tested at alpha 0.035, with the altered-subgroup alpha (0.021 or up to 0.05) depending on whether the overall-population test rejected, per the alpha-recycling MTP
- Results: in the overall population, PFS HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.51-0.71; p<0.001), median PFS 7.2 vs. 3.6 months; in the PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered population, PFS HR 0.50 (95% CI 0.38-0.65; p<0.001), median PFS 7.3 vs. 3.1 months; in the non-altered subgroup (exploratory), investigator-assessed median PFS was 5.3 vs. 3.7 months (~6-week difference, not considered clinically meaningful); OS HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.56-0.88) overall and HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.61-1.02) in the altered population at the interim look

- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this application.
- FoundationOne CDx (Foundation Medicine) received a contemporaneous supplemental PMA approval as the companion diagnostic device for capivasertib.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, CAPItello-291 Statistical Analysis Plan, Version 5.0, 22-Nov-2022, §1.2 Study design]* — "The study is powered to show a statistically significant difference between capivasertib + fulvestrant and placebo + fulvestrant in PFS in the overall population and the PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered populations (dual primary endpoint)) and OS (key secondary endpoint) in the overall population and in the PIK3CA/AKT/PTEN-altered sub-population will be assessed."

*[verbatim, same source, §1.3 Number of subjects]* — "It is expected that an estimated 930 patients will be screened so that approximately 700 patients can be randomised 1:1, with approximately 350 included in each arm. Of these 700 randomised patients, based on a prevalence of 40% to 45% for PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN alterations... and a test failure rate of 20%, it is expected that a minimum of 224 patients will test positive for tumours with these alterations."

*[verbatim, same source, §4.2.1 Multiplicity]* — "To control the family-wise error rate in the strong sense at 5% for the treatment comparisons in OS and PFS, a predefined MTP with an alpha-exhaustive recycling strategy (Burman et al 2009) taking into account intrinsic correlation between test statistics (Spiessens and Debois 2010), will be applied... Tests will be grouped into 2 main families: one for the comparisons in PFS, the other for the comparisons in OS... The PFS family will be tested first, the OS family will be tested later."

*[verbatim, same source, §4.2.1, OS alpha-spending]* — "The OS Interim Analysis is expected to occur when approximately 394 OS events have been observed in the overall population (56% maturity, 80% information fraction)... The exact significance level will be determined according to the O'Brien & Fleming method (Lan and DeMets 1983) based on the actual number of events observed at the OS Interim Analysis. Following FDA advice, a small alpha spend will be applied to the analysis of no OS detriment assessed at the time of the PFS primary analysis. This will use a bespoke alpha spending function with 0.0001 alpha assigned to DCO1 in each of the overall and PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered populations."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 218197, Integrated Review of Effectiveness]* — "CAPItello-291 met its dual primary endpoints in both the overall population (median PFS 7.2 months [95% CI: 5.5, 7.4] vs 3.6 months...) and the PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered population... In the exploratory subgroup analysis, the median PFS by investigator assessment in the known non-altered population was 5.3 months (95% CI: 3.6, 7.3) in the capivasertib arm and 3.7 months (95% CI: 3.5, 5.1) in the placebo arm which is a median PFS difference of [approximately 6 weeks]."

### 167. nirogacestat (Ogsiveo) — NDA 217677

**Sponsor:** SpringWorks Therapeutics, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adults with progressing desmoid tumors who require systemic treatment

**Approval date:** November 27, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** DeFi (Protocol NIR-DT-301), NCT03785964

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; double-blind phase followed by an open-label extension permitting placebo patients to cross to active treatment
- *Endpoints:* Progression-free survival (PFS, primary — BICR-assessed per RECIST v1.1); objective response rate (ORR, secondary); patient-reported outcomes
- *Primary analysis:* Stratified log-rank test, stratified Cox proportional-hazards model, 1-sided testing at alpha 0.025
- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing — PFS, then a pre-specified order of secondary/PRO endpoints
- *Regulatory:* Mid-trial SAP amendment changing endpoint status — per FDA comment, an MRI tumor-volume endpoint and a duplicative PROMIS-PF measure were moved from secondary to exploratory, and duration-of-response/duration-of-stable-disease and a BPI-SF responder measure were removed from the hierarchical secondary-testing family; no FDA advisory committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- DeFi (NIR-DT-301): randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trial of nirogacestat (a gamma-secretase inhibitor) in adults with progressing desmoid tumor/aggressive fibromatosis; 118 patients randomized, with an open-label extension phase for placebo patients after unblinding/progression
- Primary endpoint: PFS assessed by BICR per RECIST v1.1, tested at a 1-sided alpha of 0.025; secondary objectives included safety/tolerability, ORR (CR+PR), and PRO measures (GODDESS, BPI short form, EORTC QLQ-C30)
- Sample size/power: 51 PFS events were planned to provide 90% power (1-sided alpha 0.025) to detect a hazard ratio of 0.4, assuming median PFS of 20 months (nirogacestat) vs. 8 months (placebo); 118 participants were randomized 1:1 assuming a 10% dropout rate and a 20% spontaneous-regression rate in the placebo arm; no interim analysis was ultimately conducted (the SAP's "Changes to Planned Analyses" section notes an interim analysis originally planned in the protocol was dropped)
- Results: PFS HR 0.29 (95% CI 0.15-0.55; p<0.001) by BICR; a supportive investigator-assessed analysis gave HR 0.31 (95% CI 0.16-0.62); median PFS was not reached in either arm at the primary analysis given event immaturity

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, DeFi Statistical Analysis Plan, Protocol NIR-DT-301, 12 May 2022, Final Version 2.0, Primary Objective]* — "The primary objective of this study is: To determine the efficacy (as defined by progression-free survival [PFS]) of nirogacestat in adult participants with progressing DT/AF."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.1 Sample Size Justification]* — "A total of 51 events will provide 90% power and a 1-sided type 1 error rate of 0.025 (1-side hypothesis) to detect a difference between nirogacestat and placebo, assuming the median PFS in the nirogacestat group is 20 months and 8 months in the placebo group (corresponding to a hazard ratio of 0.4 relative to placebo). Assuming a 10% dropout rate and a 20% spontaneous regression rate, 118 participants will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to observe the required number of events."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.7 Multiple Comparisons/Multiplicity]* — "Multiplicity will be controlled via hierarchical testing method for the primary and secondary endpoints in the order as listed in Section 4.3."

*[verbatim, same source, §5 Changes to Planned Analyses]* — "I. An interim analysis is no longer planned. II. 'Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System Physical Function (PROMIS PF) short form 10a plus 3 additional items from PROMIS item banks' has been moved from secondary to exploratory endpoint... due to duplications to other PROs. IV. Duration of Response and Duration of Stable disease have been removed from the hierarchical testing of secondary endpoints as they are considered supportive of ORR. V. Proportion of participants with improvement in BPI-SF API score at Cycle 10 has been removed from the hierarchical testing of secondary endpoints."

### 168. tislelizumab-jsgr (Tevimbra) — BLA 761232

**Sponsor:** BeiGene, Ltd. / BeiGene USA, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adults with unresectable or metastatic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) after prior systemic chemotherapy that did not include a PD-(L)1-targeted therapy

**Approval date:** March 13, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** RATIONALE-302 (BGB-A317-302), NCT03430843

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, open-label, active-controlled — tislelizumab vs. investigator's choice of chemotherapy (ICC: paclitaxel, docetaxel, or irinotecan) as second-line treatment; randomization stratified by ECOG performance status, ICC choice, and geographic region (region not adjusted in the primary model)
- *Endpoints:* Overall survival (OS, primary — ITT population;); OS in the PD-L1-positive population (vCPS ≥10% by VENTANA PD-L1 [SP263] CDx assay, key secondary;); ORR, PFS, duration of response (further secondary, no alpha allocated)
- *Primary analysis:* Stratified log-rank test, stratified Cox proportional-hazards model
- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing — OS (ITT) tested once at 1-sided alpha 0.025; only if rejected is OS (PD-L1-positive) tested at the same level
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* No planned interim analysis (explicit in the SAP) — event-driven single final analysis after ~400 deaths
- *Regulatory:* No advisory committee meeting identified in the FDA review materials for this application

**Trial design & endpoints**

- RATIONALE-302: randomized (1:1), open-label, active-controlled, international Phase III trial of tislelizumab vs. investigator-chosen chemotherapy (paclitaxel, docetaxel, or irinotecan) as second-line treatment for advanced/metastatic unresectable ESCC; ~500 patients planned, stratified by ECOG PS (0 vs. 1) and ICC option
- Primary endpoint: OS in the ITT population; key secondary endpoint: OS in the PD-L1-positive analysis set (vCPS ≥10% via the VENTANA PD-L1 [SP263] CDx assay); other secondary endpoints (ORR, PFS, DOR, HRQoL via EORTC QLQ-C30/QLQ-OES18/EQ-5D-5L) carried no formal alpha allocation
- Sample size/power: ~500 patients (1:1) over a 26-month accrual period to accumulate ~400 deaths, assuming an OS HR of 0.75 (median OS 8 vs. 6 months), for 82% power at a 1-sided alpha of 0.025; no interim analysis was planned
- Results: OS HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.57-0.85; 1-sided p=0.0001), median OS 8.6 months (tislelizumab) vs. 6.3 months (ICC); ORR and DOR also favored tislelizumab (DOR 7.1 vs. 4.0 months)

Assuming an OS-HR (Arm tislelizumab/Arm ICC) is 0.75 and a dropout rate of 5% per year, approximately 500 patients will be enrolled and randomized in a 1:1 ratio... over 26-month period in order to accumulate approximately 400 deaths when median OS in the tislelizumab and ICC arms are 8 months and 6 months, respectively."

### 169. pegulicianine (Lumisight) — NDA 214511

**Sponsor:** Lumicell, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Optical imaging agent indicated with the LUM Imaging System for intraoperative, real-time detection of residual cancer in the tumor bed of adult patients with breast cancer during breast-conserving surgery

**Approval date:** April 17, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** Study CL0007 ("Investigation of Novel Surgical Imaging for Tumor Excision"), NCT03686215 (supportive study: CL0006)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison) — every enrolled patient in the device arm received standard-of-care lumpectomy first, then LUM-guided re-excision ("T-shaves") of any additional imaged tissue, with pathology as the reference standard; three co-primary endpoints assessed on the same population
- *Endpoints:* Removal of residual cancer (co-primary — proportion of device-arm patients with residual cancer found in ≥1 LUM-guided therapeutic shave); tissue-level sensitivity and tissue-level specificity (co-primary — using a hierarchical truth-standard algorithm: shave pathology, then re-excision pathology, then margin assessment, in descending priority); patient-level sensitivity/specificity (secondary, added per FDA feedback)
- *Primary analysis:* Exact binomial test against a pre-specified performance goal for the residual-cancer-removal endpoint (performance goal 3%, one-sided alpha 2.5%); for tissue-level sensitivity/specificity, a GEE-based estimator with an exchangeable working-correlation structure (accounting for multiple tissue samples per patient) plus bootstrap resampling for the confidence interval, tested one-sided at alpha 2.5% against performance goals of 40% (sensitivity) and 60% (specificity)
- *Regulatory:* FDA Advisory Committee meeting held — Medical Imaging Drugs Advisory Committee, March 5, 2024, to discuss persuasiveness of the effectiveness evidence and risk mitigation for hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study CL0007: a controlled, multicenter, single-arm (within-patient paired) pivotal trial of the LUM Imaging System (pegulicianine fluorescence imaging agent plus the LUM Imaging Device) in 357 patients undergoing breast-conserving surgery, with a smaller supportive/confirmatory study (CL0006) providing additional evidence; every device-arm patient's cavity was imaged intraoperatively after standard-of-care lumpectomy, and any positive-signal region was excised as an additional "LUM-guided shave" and sent for pathology
- Three co-primary endpoints: (1) removal of residual cancer — proportion of patients with residual cancer found in at least one LUM-guided shave after SOC surgery was completed (performance goal 3%, one-sided exact binomial test at alpha 2.5%); (2) tissue-level sensitivity and (3) tissue-level specificity of the device for detecting residual cancer, using a hierarchical truth-standard (shave pathology > re-excision pathology > margin assessment), with performance goals of 40% (sensitivity, lower 95% CI bound) and 60% (specificity, lower 95% CI bound)
- Results: residual-cancer removal rate 8% (27/357; 95% CI 5%-11%), passing the 3% performance goal; tissue-level specificity 87% (95% CI 85%-88%), passing the 60% goal; tissue-level sensitivity 49% (95% CI 36%-62%) — the lower CI bound (36%) fell short of the pre-specified 40% performance goal, so this co-primary endpoint was not formally met, though the point estimate exceeded the goal
- The Medical Imaging Drugs Advisory Committee (March 5, 2024) discussed this mixed result; members generally agreed the device showed a "modest" but real incremental benefit (meeting 2 of 3 co-primary endpoints, including patient-level detection) despite the missed tissue-level sensitivity goal, and that hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis risk was manageable with labeling/risk mitigation

"Clinical Impact of Intraoperative Margin Assessment in Breast-Conserving Surgery With a Novel Pegulicianine Fluorescence-Guided System: A Nonrandomized Controlled Trial." *JAMA Surg.* 2022;157(7):e220254. - This is a diagnostic imaging agent/device combination product rather than a systemic anticancer therapy; there is no accelerated-approval/confirmatory-trial framework analogous to the other entries in this batch.

Residual cancer is defined as tumor found by pathology in a therapeutic shave after the SOC surgical procedure is completed; that is, tumor that current SOC surgery failed to remove."

*[verbatim, same source, §4.2 Residual cancer removal (co-primary endpoint)]* — "The hypothesis will be tested using an exact Binomial test at a one-sided significance level of [2.5%]... removal of residual cancer sensitivity is larger than the performance goal of 3%."

*[verbatim, same source, §4.3.2 Performance goals]* — "The verification of the sensitivity and specificity co-primary endpoints will be a refutation of the [null hypotheses]... These hypotheses will be tested using a one-sided significance level of 2.5%. To account for [clustering, a GEE method with] working correlation structure, will be used to estimate sensitivity and specificity along with [a] bound of the confidence interval for sensitivity is larger than the performance goal of 40%... specificity is larger than the performance goal of 60%."

The Committee members were in general agreement that there was a modest overall benefit observed with use of pegulicianine, as it met its prespecified endpoints for patient-level detection of residual cancer and tissue-level specificity, but did not meet its tissue-level sensitivity goal."

### 170. nogapendekin alfa inbakicept-pmln (Anktiva) — BLA 761336

**Sponsor:** ImmunityBio, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adults with BCG-unresponsive non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) with carcinoma in situ (CIS), with or without papillary tumors, in combination with intravesical Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG)

**Approval date:** April 22, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** QUILT-3.032, NCT03022825

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label trial, three independent cohorts (Cohort A: N-803 + BCG in CIS ± papillary; Cohort B: N-803 + BCG, papillary-only; Cohort C: N-803 alone); Simon's two-stage design used for Cohort C to decide whether to continue enrollment based on an interim look at antitumor activity
- *Endpoints:* Complete response (CR) rate at any time (primary, Cohort A — local pathology, per FDA's BCG-unresponsive NMIBC guidance definition) with a retrospective cytology-based imputation rule for indeterminate/positive interim cytology results; duration of CR (supportive of durability); central-pathology-reviewed CR rate (supportive/sensitivity analysis)
- *Primary analysis:* Exact binomial test against a pre-specified performance goal — for the primary endpoint to succeed in Cohort A, the lower bound of the 95% CI for CR rate had to exceed a 20% performance goal
- *Regulatory:* Regular approval grounded in durable single-arm CR rate as direct clinical benefit — the review team found interpretation of a single-arm CR-rate endpoint appropriate for CIS per prior December 2019 ODAC precedent (established for a different single-arm PD-1 inhibitor trial in the same disease setting), and recommended regular (not accelerated) approval; postmarketing commitment for better characterization of duration/durability

**Trial design & endpoints**

- QUILT-3.032: an open-label, single-arm, three-cohort, multicenter Phase 2/3 study of intravesical N-803 (nogapendekin alfa inbakicept, an IL-15 superagonist) combined with BCG (Cohorts A and B) or N-803 alone (Cohort C, using a Simon's two-stage design to gate continued enrollment based on an IDMC review of antitumor activity after the first stage); this entry covers Cohort A (BCG-unresponsive CIS ± papillary tumors), the basis for approval, enrolling 88 patients
- Primary endpoint (Cohort A): complete response (CR) rate at any time by local pathology, defined per FDA's BCG-unresponsive NMIBC guidance (negative cystoscopy + negative/atypical cytology; or biopsy-proven benign/low-grade Ta with negative cytology; or negative cystoscopy with malignant cytology only if an alternative non-bladder source is identified), plus a sponsor-added retrospective imputation rule treating an indeterminate/positive cytology result as a CR if the next visit's cytology was negative
- FDA identified and required correction of two definitional issues during review: the sponsor's training materials had implied a visit could be scored CR based on malignant cytology alone (without requiring identification of a non-bladder source), which FDA clarified was inconsistent with its own guidance; and the imputation rule (not discussed in prior regulatory meetings) was found "generally reasonable" by the review team once clarified and made retrospective-only
- Results: complete response rate (local pathology, at any time) 62.3% (n=48/77 efficacy-evaluable in the analysis reviewed) with durable responses (median duration of response reported as not reached at the data cutoff in the label); a supportive central-pathology-reviewed CR rate was 51.7% (30/58); statistical rule for primary-endpoint success required the lower 95% CI bound to exceed the 20% performance goal, which the observed result cleared

The definition of the primary endpoint of CR in the protocol generally followed the FDA Guidance verbatim, with two important caveats."

### 171. tovorafenib (Ojemda) — NDA 218033

**Sponsor:** Day One Biopharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Patients 6 months of age and older with relapsed or refractory pediatric low-grade glioma (LGG) harboring a BRAF fusion/rearrangement or BRAF V600 mutation — approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate and duration of response

**Approval date:** April 23, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** FIREFLY-1 (DAY101-001), Arm 1, NCT04775485

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label trial, multi-arm study (Arm 1: pivotal dose-expansion cohort; Arm 2: expanded-access safety cohort; Arm 3: modified Simon's two-stage design in a separate population); supports accelerated approval under Subpart H
- *Endpoints:* Overall response rate (ORR, primary — independent-review-assessed; the pivotal analysis used RAPNO-LGG criteria [CR/PR/minor response] for the approved label, with RANO-HGG-based ORR also specified as an endpoint in the SAP); duration of response, time to response, progression-free survival (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* Exact binomial test against a pre-specified performance goal — Arm 1 sample size of 60 evaluable patients assumed a true ORR of 40% vs. a null of 21% (2-sided alpha 0.05, 88% power; ≥20/60 responses significant); Arm 3 used a modified Simon's two-stage design (stage 1: stop if ≤1/12 responses; total N=20; null ORR 5%, assumed true ORR 25%, 1-sided alpha 0.1, 90% power; ≥3/20 responses significant)
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval based on single-arm ORR/DoR, confirmatory trial required — confirmatory trial is the randomized FIREFLY-2/LOGGIC study (NCT05566795, tovorafenib vs. standard-of-care chemotherapy in first-line systemic therapy); no FDA statistical/clinical review package was found publicly posted for this NDA (checked standard Drugs@FDA URL patterns; not linked from the overview page and not found at the direct-path pattern used elsewhere in this census)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- FIREFLY-1 (DAY101-001): multicenter, open-label, multi-arm study of tovorafenib (a type II pan-RAF inhibitor) in pediatric and young adult patients with relapsed/refractory low-grade glioma harboring a BRAF alteration; Arm 1 (the pivotal cohort supporting accelerated approval) enrolled patients aged 6 months-25 years with ≥1 prior systemic therapy and RANO-defined measurable disease; Arm 3 used a modified Simon's two-stage design in a separate population
- Primary endpoint (Arm 1, per SAP): ORR by independent radiology review committee (IRC); the approved label's efficacy table instead reports ORR by RAPNO-LGG criteria (CR+PR+minor response) as the major efficacy outcome measure, reflecting a criteria refinement over the course of the program; secondary endpoints included ORR by RANO-HGG and by RANO-LGG, PFS, duration of response, time to response, and safety/PK/ECG measures
- Sample size (Arm 1): 60 evaluable patients provided 88% power to reject a null ORR of 21% assuming a true ORR of 40% (2-sided alpha 0.05); a result of ≥20/60 (33%) responses would be statistically significant; total study enrollment across arms was ~140 patients
- Results (efficacy population, N=76, RAPNO-LGG by IRC): ORR 51% (95% CI 40%-63%), including 0% CR, 37% PR, 14% minor response; median duration of response 13.8 months (95% CI 11.3-NE) among 39 responders
