### 172. tarlatamab-dlle (Imdelltra) — BLA 761344

**Sponsor:** Amgen Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adults with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) with disease progression on or after platinum-based chemotherapy — approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate and duration of response

**Approval date:** May 16, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** DeLLphi-301 (Study 20200491), NCT05060016

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label trial — a Phase 2 dose-expansion study (10 mg and 100 mg dose groups) nested within a larger first-in-human multi-part study of the DLL3xCD3 bispecific T-cell engager tarlatamab; supports accelerated approval under Subpart H
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR, primary — BICR-assessed, with investigator assessment secondary); disease control rate (DCR), duration of disease control (DoDC), duration of response (DOR), PFS, OS (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* Exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval — ORR analyzed with a Clopper-Pearson exact CI (the sponsor's SAP originally specified 97.5%, later revised); DOR/DoDC/PFS/OS via Kaplan-Meier with Brookmeyer-Crowley CIs and Greenwood-formula variance for landmark rates
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval based on single-arm ORR/DoR, confirmatory trial required — confirmatory Phase 3 trial (Study 20210004, randomized vs. standard of care) was already under FDA discussion/submitted before the BLA was filed; FDA-directed change to the primary analysis population and CI method during pre-BLA review — at a September 8, 2023 pre-BLA meeting, FDA requested a 95% (not 97.5%) Clopper-Pearson CI for ORR and specified the as-treated population (all patients receiving ≥1 dose) as the primary efficacy analysis population; no FDA advisory committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- DeLLphi-301 (Study 20200491): open-label, multi-part, multicenter Phase 1/2 study of tarlatamab (a DLL3xCD3 bispecific T-cell engager) in patients with relapsed/refractory extensive-stage SCLC who had progressed after platinum-based chemotherapy; the registration-supporting cohort evaluated tarlatamab 10 mg (the to-be-marketed dose) and 100 mg administered IV every 2 weeks after step-up dosing
- Primary endpoint: ORR by BICR per RECIST 1.1 (subjects without a post-baseline tumor assessment counted as non-responders); secondary endpoints included DCR, duration of disease control, DOR, PFS (BICR and investigator), and OS (investigator-assessed)
- SAP amendment history: five amendments between the original SAP and BLA submission, including updates to the analysis-set definitions, addition of a DLL3-expression subgroup analysis, and (per FDA's pre-BLA feedback) a switch from a 97.5% to a 95% Clopper-Pearson CI for ORR and adoption of the as-treated population as primary
- Results (10 mg dose group, BICR): ORR 41.4% (41/99 or as reported in the review's dose-group table), DCR 52.5% (95% CI 45.7%-59.2%); an unconfirmed partial response awaiting a confirmatory scan was noted in the interim data; DOR and OS data were still maturing at the time of approval

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

No sponsor SAP or protocol is posted on ClinicalTrials.gov for DeLLphi-301; the following are verbatim excerpts from the FDA Multi-Discipline Review, which reproduces the Applicant's statistical-methods table and FDA's own commentary on it directly.

DCR: Clopper Pearson exact 95% CI... DoDC, DOR, PFS, OS: Kaplan-Meier estimates for median and selected quantiles with 95% CI calculated using the Brookmeyer and Crowley method (Brookmeyer and Crowley, 1982)."

*[verbatim, same source, FDA's Assessment]* — "FDA agrees with the Applicant's descriptions of the statistical analysis plan. In addition, during the pre-BLA meeting dated September 8, 2023, FDA requested that the Applicant provide a 95% CI of ORR using the Clopper-Pearson exact method, and FDA also commented that the as-treated population, which includes all patients who received at least one dose of tarlatamab, should be the primary efficacy analysis population."

*[verbatim, same source, regulatory history table]* — "05 December 2022 Type B (pre-phase 3) meeting to discuss proposed Study 20210004 to support regular approval of tarlatamab for a second-line SCLC indication and will serve as the confirmatory study to support full approval for the proposed indication. 22 December 2022 New phase 3 confirmatory Study 20210004 (IND 134859) submitted."

### 173. vorasidenib (Voranigo) — NDA 218784

**Sponsor:** Servier Pharmaceuticals LLC (originally developed by Agios Pharmaceuticals)

**Indication approved:** Adults and pediatric patients ≥12 years with grade 2 astrocytoma or oligodendroglioma with a susceptible IDH1 or IDH2 mutation, following surgery (biopsy, sub-total resection, or gross total resection)

**Approval date:** August 6, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** INDIGO (AG881-C-004), NCT04164901

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; crossover permitted at progression — placebo patients could cross to vorasidenib after BIRC-confirmed radiographic progression, with crossover-arm treatment counted as an event for the key secondary endpoint (TTNI); randomization stratified by 1p19q codeletion status and baseline tumor size
- *Endpoints:* Progression-free survival (PFS, primary — BIRC-assessed per modified RANO-LGG;); time to next intervention (TTNI, key secondary); tumor growth rate, objective response, OS, HRQoL (FACT-Br), neurocognitive function, seizure activity (further secondary/exploratory)
- *Primary analysis:* Stratified log-rank test, Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing — TTNI tested only if PFS reached statistical significance at the corresponding interim or final analysis
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Group-sequential design, Gamma-family alpha-spending function, non-binding futility boundary (all s) — 3-look design for PFS with a Gamma(-24) alpha-spending function and a Gamma(-5) beta-spending function (non-binding futility), and a 2-look design for TTNI with a Gamma(-22) alpha-spending function
- *Regulatory:* No FDA advisory committee meeting held ("no significant efficacy or safety issues... required external input")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- INDIGO (AG881-C-004): randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trial of vorasidenib (a dual IDH1/IDH2 inhibitor) in patients with residual or recurrent grade 2 oligodendroglioma or astrocytoma with an IDH1 or IDH2 mutation who had undergone surgery as their only treatment and were ≥1 year post-surgery; ~340 patients randomized, stratified by chromosome 1p19q codeletion status and baseline tumor size (≥2 cm vs. <2 cm); placebo patients could cross to open-label vorasidenib after BIRC-confirmed radiographic progression
- Primary endpoint: PFS by BIRC per modified RANO-LGG (time to first documented radiographic progression or death); key secondary endpoint: TTNI (time from randomization to initiation of first subsequent anticancer therapy, including vorasidenib for crossover patients, or death) — a construct designed to capture clinical benefit even though crossover limits interpretability of a conventional OS analysis
- Sample size/power: 164 PFS events for ≥90% power to detect HR 0.6 (1-sided log-rank test, stratified, alpha 0.025), using a 3-look group-sequential design (Gamma(-24) alpha-spending, Gamma(-5) beta-spending for non-binding futility); 152 TTNI events for ~80% power to detect HR 0.636 (1-sided alpha 0.025, 2-look Gamma(-22) alpha-spending), tested only if PFS was significant, per a fixed-sequence procedure (Westfall and Krishen 2001)
- Results: PFS 27.7 months (vorasidenib) vs. 11.1 months (placebo), HR 0.26 (95% CI 0.15-0.43; p<0.0001); TTNI was also significantly improved (consistent with the PFS result, given the fixed-sequence gate)

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2024/218784Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/218784s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (NDA 218784) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/218784Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (INDIGO) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04164901 (Study Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan both posted in the Documents tab)
- Protocol / SAP — Study Protocol (Amendment 3, Version 4.0, 20-Jul-2021): https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/01/NCT04164901/Prot_000.pdf; Statistical Analysis Plan (Version 2.0): https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/01/NCT04164901/SAP_001.pdf — **note:** the posted SAP PDF's text layer is corrupted (per-glyph character spacing defeats reliable automated extraction, the same known failure mode documented elsewhere in this census for redaction-pipeline PDFs); the protocol PDF's text layer is intact and clean, so verbatim quotes below are drawn from the protocol (which contains the same statistical-hypotheses/sample-size language) rather than the SAP
- Pivotal publication: Mellinghoff IK, Penas-Prado M, Peters KB, et al. "Vorasidenib in IDH1- or IDH2-Mutant Low-Grade Glioma." *N Engl J Med.* 2023;389(7):589-601. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2304194), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37272516/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Vorasidenib%20in%20IDH1-%20or%20IDH2-Mutant%20Low-Grade%20Glioma)

**Other resources**

- Servier's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for INDIGO; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for this trial.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held; the review states FDA "did not refer this application to an advisory committee as no significant efficacy or safety [issues required external input]."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, INDIGO Study Protocol, AG881-C-004, Amendment 3, Version 4.0, 20-Jul-2021, §2.1 Primary Objective]* — "The primary objective of the study is to demonstrate the efficacy of vorasidenib based on radiographic PFS per BIRC compared with placebo in subjects with residual or recurrent Grade 2 oligodendroglioma and astrocytoma with an IDH1 or IDH2 mutation who have undergone surgery as their only treatment."

*[verbatim, same source, §2.5.1-2.5.2 Primary and Key Secondary Endpoints]* — "The primary endpoint is PFS, defined as the time from date of randomization to date of first documented radiographic PD (as assessed by the BIRC per modified Response Assessment for Neuro-oncology for Low-Grade Gliomas [RANO-LGG])... The key secondary endpoint is TTNI, defined as the time from randomization to the initiation of the first subsequent anticancer therapy (including vorasidenib, for subjects randomized to placebo who subsequently cross over) or death due to any cause."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.2 Statistical Hypotheses and Sample Size Estimation]* — "For the primary endpoint, a total of 164 PFS events will be required to have at least 90% power to detect a hazard ratio of 0.6 using a 1-sided log-rank test stratified by the randomization stratification factors at a significance level of 0.025, and a 3-look group sequential design with a Gamma family (-24) α-spending function to determine the efficacy boundaries and a Gamma family (-5) β-spending function to determine the nonbinding futility boundary."

*[verbatim, same source, continued]* — "For TTNI, a total of 152 TTNI events will be required to have approximately 80% power to detect a hazard ratio of 0.636 using a 1-sided log-rank test stratified by the randomization stratification factors at a significance level of 0.025, and a 2-look group sequential design with a Gamma family (-22) α-spending function to determine the efficacy boundaries. To preserve the overall type I error in the study, the fixed sequence testing procedure (Westfall and Krishen, 2001) will be followed; TTNI will be tested only if PFS has reached statistical significance."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 218784, Integrated Review of Effectiveness]* — "PFS of 27.7 months (95% CI: 17, NE) compared to 11.1 months (95% CI: 11, 13.7) on the placebo arm. The hazard ratio (HR) for PFS for patients in the vorasidenib arm vs placebo arm with a HR of 0.26 (95% CI: 0.15, 0.43; p-value of < 0.0001)."

### 174. inavolisib (Itovebi) — NDA 219249

**Sponsor:** Genentech, Inc. (a member of the Roche Group)

**Indication approved:** In combination with palbociclib and fulvestrant, for adults with endocrine-resistant, PIK3CA-mutated, HR-positive, HER2-negative, locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer, with disease recurrence on or within 12 months of completing adjuvant endocrine therapy

**Approval date:** October 10, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** INAVO120 (WO41554), NCT04191499

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; randomization stratified by presence of visceral disease, primary vs. secondary endocrine resistance, and geographic region; ICH E9(R1) estimand framework — a treatment-policy strategy specified for intercurrent events (start of non-protocol anticancer therapy, early treatment discontinuation)
- *Endpoints:* Progression-free survival (PFS, primary — investigator-assessed per RECIST v1.1); overall survival (OS, key secondary); ORR, best overall response rate, clinical benefit rate (further secondary); time to confirmed deterioration (TTCD) in pain, physical functioning, role functioning, and Global Health Status/QoL (PRO secondary endpoints)
- *Primary analysis:* Stratified log-rank test, stratified Cox proportional-hazards model, Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing — an 8-endpoint pre-specified order (OS, ORR, BOR, CBR, then 4 TTCD domains), each tested at 2-sided alpha 0.05, gated behind the primary PFS result
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function, O'Brien-Fleming boundary, non-binding futility boundary (all s) — an iDMC-conducted non-binding futility analysis for PFS occurred at 75 events (33% information), with a futility rule (point-estimate HR >1.1) chosen to keep the chance of stopping a truly positive trial below 3%; OS used a Lan-DeMets (O'Brien-Fleming) group-sequential design with an interim analysis at the time of the primary PFS analysis
- *Regulatory:* No FDA advisory committee meeting identified in the review materials

**Trial design & endpoints**

- INAVO120 (WO41554): randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trial of inavolisib (a PI3Kα inhibitor/degrader) plus palbociclib and fulvestrant vs. placebo plus palbociclib and fulvestrant, as first-line therapy for PIK3CA-mutated, HR+/HER2- locally advanced/metastatic breast cancer in patients with disease recurrence during or within 12 months of completing adjuvant endocrine therapy; 325 patients randomized, stratified by visceral disease, endocrine-resistance type, and region
- Estimand framework (ICH E9(R1)): population defined per protocol eligibility (PIK3CA-mutant, endocrine-resistant per the trial's specific definitions); variable PFS by investigator RECIST v1.1; treatment-policy strategy specified for intercurrent events (non-protocol anticancer therapy, early discontinuation) so that post-ICE tumor assessments remained in the primary analysis
- Sample size/power: 194 PFS events for 85% power to detect HR 0.65 (2-sided log-rank test, alpha 0.05), assuming median PFS improvement from 11 to 16.9 months; secondary-endpoint hierarchy (OS→ORR→BOR→CBR→4 TTCD domains) tested only if the immediately preceding hypothesis was significant; OS assumed HR 0.7 (35 vs. 50 months median), with 105 events expected at the PFS analysis and 153 at OS final analysis
- Results: PFS HR 0.43 (95% CI 0.32-0.59; p<0.0001), median PFS 15.0 vs. 7.3 months; interim OS HR 0.64 (95% CI 0.43-0.97; p=0.0338, not crossing the pre-specified interim efficacy boundary of alpha 0.0098) — no detriment signal, with final OS analysis expected in a subsequent quarter under a postmarketing commitment; ORR difference 33.4 percentage points (58.4% vs. 25.0%)

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2024/219249Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/219249s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (NDA 219249) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/219249Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (INAVO120) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04191499 (Study Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan both posted in the Documents tab)
- Protocol / SAP — Statistical Analysis Plan (WO41554): https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/99/NCT04191499/SAP_001.pdf; Study Protocol: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/99/NCT04191499/Prot_000.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Turner NC, Im SA, Saura C, et al. "Inavolisib-Based Therapy in PIK3CA-Mutated Advanced Breast Cancer." *N Engl J Med.* 2024;391(17):1584-1596. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2404625), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39476340/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Inavolisib-Based%20Therapy%20in%20PIK3CA-Mutated%20Advanced%20Breast%20Cancer)

**Other resources**

- Genentech/Roche's general clinical-trial data-sharing policy participates in the Vivli platform; trial-specific IPD availability for INAVO120 was not individually confirmed.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was identified in the review materials for this application.
- Postmarketing commitment for the final OS analysis, expected after further follow-up beyond the interim look reported at approval.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, INAVO120 Statistical Analysis Plan, WO41554, §2.1 Statistical Hypotheses]* — "The primary analysis will be a comparison of the Investigator-assessed PFS between the two treatment arms using a stratified log-rank test at an overall 0.05 significance level (two-sided)."

*[verbatim, same source, §2.2 Sample Size Determination]* — "Eighty-five percent power to detect a hazard ratio for inavolisib plus palbociclib and fulvestrant versus placebo plus palbociclib and fulvestrant of 0.65, corresponding to an improvement of 5.9 months (from 11 to 16.9 months) in median PFS for the treatment arm over the control arm... With these assumptions, 194 PFS events are required to achieve 85% power for the primary analysis."

*[verbatim, same source, §4.3 Secondary Endpoint(s) Analysis]* — "The type I error-controlled secondary endpoints of this study will be tested hierarchically according to the following pre-specified and fixed order of endpoints only if the primary endpoint, PFS, is statistically significant at the primary PFS analysis: 1. Overall survival (OS) 2. Objective response rate (ORR) 3. Best overall objective response rate (BOR) 4. Clinical benefit rate (CBR) 5. Time to confirmed deterioration (TTCD) in pain 6. TTCD in physical functioning (PF) 7. TTCD in role functioning (RF) 8. TTCD in Global Health Status/Quality of Life (GHS/QoL)."

*[verbatim, same source, §4.7.1 Planned Interim Analyses]* — "One interim analysis for futility of the primary endpoint has been conducted by iDMC after 75 PFS events (33% of information) were observed. The futility boundary was non-binding. The futility boundary (point estimate of PFS HR >1.1) has been chosen so that the probability of stopping for futility when the study would be positive at primary analysis was small (<3%)."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 219249, Integrated Review of Effectiveness]* — "INAVO120 demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in the primary endpoint of PFS based on investigator assessment. The median PFS was 15 months (95% CI 11.3, 20.5) vs. 7.3 months (95% CI: 5.6, 9.3) favoring inavolisib + palbociclib + fulvestrant (HR 0.43, 95% CI: 0.32, 0.59; p-value <0.0001)."

### 175. zolbetuximab-clzb (Vyloy) — BLA 761365

**Sponsor:** Astellas Pharma Global Development, Inc.

**Indication approved:** In combination with fluoropyrimidine- and platinum-containing chemotherapy, for adults with locally advanced unresectable or metastatic, CLDN18.2-positive, HER2-negative gastric or gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) adenocarcinoma

**Approval date:** October 18, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** SPOTLIGHT (8951-CL-0301), NCT03504397 (co-pivotal trial: GLOW, NCT03653507, evaluating zolbetuximab plus CAPOX)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled — zolbetuximab plus mFOLFOX6 vs. placebo plus mFOLFOX6 as first-line treatment; randomization stratified by region (Asia vs. non-Asia), number of organs with metastatic sites (0-2 vs. ≥3), and prior gastrectomy
- *Endpoints:* Progression-free survival (PFS, primary — IRC-assessed); overall survival (OS, key secondary); time to confirmed deterioration (TTCD) in physical functioning, abdominal pain (OG25-Pain), and Global Health Status/QoL, each tested non-inferiority-then-superiority (key secondary PRO family); ORR, DOR (further secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* Log-rank test stratified, stratified Cox proportional-hazards model, 1-sided alpha 0.025
- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing — OS tested only if PFS significant; TTCD family tested only if OS significant, using a gatekeeping procedure that runs non-inferiority-then-superiority — PF, then OG25-Pain, then GHS/QoL, non-inferiority first across all three, then superiority across all three, each at 0.025
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* O'Brien-Fleming-type alpha-spending function via Lan-DeMets, implemented in East software — a single OS interim analysis (concurrent with the final PFS analysis) with early-stopping possible for a highly favorable result, followed by a final OS analysis
- *Regulatory:* No advisory committee meeting identified in the review materials; approval supported by two co-pivotal randomized trials (SPOTLIGHT with mFOLFOX6, GLOW with CAPOX) — not itself a distinct taxonomy keyword but noted for context

**Trial design & endpoints**

- SPOTLIGHT (8951-CL-0301): randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter Phase III trial of zolbetuximab (an anti-Claudin 18.2 monoclonal antibody) plus mFOLFOX6 vs. placebo plus mFOLFOX6, as first-line treatment in 565 patients with CLDN18.2-positive, HER2-negative, locally advanced unresectable or metastatic gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma; stratified by region, number of organs with metastatic sites, and prior gastrectomy; zolbetuximab/placebo given on Days 1 and 22 of each 42-day cycle alongside 12 cycles of mFOLFOX6 (then optional 5-FU/folinic acid maintenance)
- Primary endpoint: PFS by IRC (RECIST-based radiological progression or death), tested at 1-sided alpha 0.025; key secondary endpoint OS, tested only if PFS was significant; a further key-secondary PRO family (TTCD in physical functioning, OG25-Pain, and GHS/QoL) tested only if OS was significant, via a gatekeeping procedure running non-inferiority tests first across all three domains, then superiority tests across all three, each at 0.025
- Sample size/power: 300 PFS events for 93.4% power to detect HR 0.67 (median PFS 9 vs. 6 months, 1-sided alpha 0.025); 396 OS events for 81% power to detect HR 0.75 (median OS 14.7 vs. 11 months, 1-sided alpha 0.025); a single OS interim analysis (at the time of final PFS analysis) used an O'Brien-Fleming-type Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function, with the possibility of early termination for a highly favorable result
- Results: PFS HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.598-0.942; 1-sided p=0.0066), median PFS 10.6 vs. 8.7 months; OS HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.601-0.936; 1-sided p=0.0053), median OS 18.2 vs. 15.5 months — both co-primary/key-secondary endpoints met, supporting regular approval; the co-pivotal GLOW trial (zolbetuximab + CAPOX) independently showed PFS HR 0.687 (95% CI 0.544-0.866; 1-sided p=0.0007), median PFS 8.2 months in the zolbetuximab arm

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/761365s000lbl.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (SPOTLIGHT) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03504397 (Study Protocol and a Patient-Reported-Outcomes-focused SAP posted in the Documents tab)
- Protocol / SAP — Study Protocol (Version 8.0, 14-Nov-2024, incorporating Substantial Amendment 7): https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/97/NCT03504397/Prot_002.pdf; PRO Statistical Analysis Plan (Version 2.0, 02-May-2023): https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/97/NCT03504397/SAP_003.pdf — **note:** only a PRO-focused SAP is posted under the generic "Statistical Analysis Plan" document slot; it references a separate main clinical efficacy SAP (dated 18-Nov-2021) that is not independently posted, so this entry's primary-endpoint statistical detail is drawn from the (clean, fully extractable) protocol rather than the main SAP
- Pivotal publication: Shitara K, Lordick F, Bang YJ, et al. "Zolbetuximab plus mFOLFOX6 in patients with CLDN18.2-positive, HER2-negative, untreated, locally advanced unresectable or metastatic gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (SPOTLIGHT): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, phase 3 trial." *Lancet.* 2023;401(10389):1655-1668. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(23)00620-7), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37068504/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Zolbetuximab%20plus%20mFOLFOX6%20SPOTLIGHT%20phase%203%20trial)

**Other resources**

- Astellas' general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for SPOTLIGHT; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for this trial.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was identified in the review materials for this application.

*[verbatim, SPOTLIGHT Study Protocol, ISN/Protocol 8951-CL-0301, Version 8.0, 14-Nov-2024, §7.1 Sample Size]* — "The planned 300 PFS events during the study will provide 93.4% power to detect a difference in PFS between Arm A (zolbetuximab + mFOLFOX6) with the assumption of 9 months median PFS time and Arm B (placebo + mFOLFOX6) with the assumption of 6 months median PFS time (hazard ratio = 0.67) at the overall 1-sided 0.025 significance level. Similarly, the planned 396 OS events during the study will provide 81% power to detect a difference in OS... (hazard ratio = 0.75) at the overall 1-sided 0.025 significance level."

*[verbatim, same source, §7.4.1.1 Primary Analysis]* — "The primary endpoint is PFS assessed by the blinded IRC... The hypothesis testing on the primary analysis will be performed at an overall 1-sided 0.025 significance level to test the null hypothesis that PFS is not prolonged in Arm A compared to Arm B versus the alternative hypothesis that PFS is prolonged in Arm A compared to Arm B."

Non-inferiority testing for TTCD in OG25-Pain... 3. Non-inferiority testing for TTCD in GHS/QoL... 4. Superiority testing for TTCD in PF... 5. Superiority testing for TTCD in OG25-PA... 6. Superiority testing for TTCD in GHS/QoL."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761365, Integrated Review of Effectiveness]* — "The PFS hazard ratio (HR) was 0.75 (95% CI: 0.598, 0.942; 1-sided p=0.0066) with a median PFS of 10.6 months (95% CI 8.9, 12.5) in the zolbetuximab.clzb and chemotherapy arm vs. 8.7 months (95% CI 8.2, 10.3) in the placebo and chemotherapy arm... The OS HR was 0.75 (95% CI: 0.601, 0.936; 1-sided p=0.0053) with a median OS of 18.2 months (95% CI: 16.4, 22.9) in the zolbetuximab.clzb and chemotherapy arm and 15.5 months (95% CI: 13.5, 16.5) for the placebo and chemotherapy arm."

### 176. revumenib (Revuforj) — NDA 218944

**Sponsor:** Syndax Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adult and pediatric patients 1 year and older with relapsed or refractory acute leukemia with a KMT2A translocation — approved under accelerated approval based on complete remission (CR) plus CR with partial hematologic recovery (CRh) rate and duration of CR/CRh

**Approval date:** November 15, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** AUGMENT-101 (Study SNDX-5613-0700), NCT04065399

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label, multi-cohort Phase 1/2 trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H/21 CFR 314.500; biomarker-selected/enriched population; post-hoc recombination of differently-enrolled cohorts into one primary analysis population; Simon's two-stage design
- *Endpoints:* Composite CR/CRh (complete remission + complete remission with partial hematologic recovery) rate; duration of CR/CRh, transfusion independence conversion (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* Efficacy boundary derived from the exact binomial distribution of a group-sequential trial
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Group-sequential design, with a single efficacy interim analysis added via protocol/SAP amendment, timed to completion of Cohort 2B's Simon two-stage Stage 1, controlling overall one-sided alpha under 0.025
- *Missing data/bias:* Not applicable in the randomized-trial sense (no comparator); standard right-censoring for duration of response
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval (Subpart H) based on CR/CRh rate; reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan"); central companion-diagnostic assay ruled analytically invalid by CDRH mid-review, prompting a switch to a local-testing-based labeling population; no FDA advisory committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- AUGMENT-101 (SNDX-5613-0700): open-label, multicenter Phase 1/2 trial of revumenib monotherapy in patients ≥30 days old with relapsed/refractory acute leukemia; Phase 2 pivotal cohorts (2A: ALL/MPAL, 2B: AML) enrolled patients with KMT2A rearrangement (KMT2Ar) confirmed centrally by a clinical trial assay (CTA), ≥5% marrow blasts, treated at the recommended dose (163 mg q12h with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, capsule formulation)
- Primary endpoint: CR+CRh rate (investigator-assessed), tested against a null hypothesis of ≤10% drawn from historical KMT2Ar salvage-therapy response rates
- Design evolved substantially by amendment: pediatric/adult and ALL-MPAL/AML cohorts were pooled by protocol v15 (Sept 2022), then a formal efficacy interim analysis on the pooled population was added by protocol v17/SAP v5 (Nov 2023) in response to FDA feedback, timed to completion of the first 38 adult efficacy-evaluable patients in Cohort 2B's Simon two-stage design; the efficacy boundary (≥12/57 responders) was derived from the exact binomial distribution of a group-sequential trial, controlling overall one-sided alpha under 0.025
- Secondary endpoints: duration of CR/CRh; transfusion independence (any ≥56-day transfusion-free interval)
- Results and FDA's departure from the sponsor's plan: in the prespecified Pivotal Cohort (N=57, centrally CTA-confirmed), CR/CRh was 21% (95% CI 11-34%), crossing the prespecified 10% lower bound; CDRH then determined the central CTA was not analytically valid, so FDA substituted an independently defined "Efficacy Cohort" (N=104, KMT2A translocation confirmed by local assay) for labeling — CR/CRh was again 21% (95% CI 13.8-30.3%), but analyses of this substitute population were descriptive only, with no formal hypothesis test
- FDA separately noted that the estimand it had recommended in October 2022 correspondence was never incorporated into the protocol/SAP, though FDA applied its own estimand logic in the remission-adjudication process regardless

A superiority/efficacy IA for primary endpoint (CR+CRh rate) in the pooled KMT2Ar population (Cohort 2A +2B adults and pediatrics) was conducted at the time of the pre-planned IA timepoint defined by the Simon's 2-stage design for Cohort 2B... The efficacy boundary of ≥ 12 CR+CRh responders was determined based on the actual number of efficacy evaluable patients available for the IA (N=57) using fixed alpha spend at the IA by controlling the overall alpha under 0.025."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "As the prespecified efficacy analysis population required the central confirmation of mutation status, whose data was determined as invalid by FDA (see Section 4.3), FDA concluded that a cohort identified by conventional testing locally may be a better representation of patients with KMT2A translocations."

*[verbatim, same source, FDA Table 65]* — "CR/CRh 22/104 (21.2%; 95% CI 13.8, 30.3)."

*[verbatim, same source, "Summary and Conclusions — Statistical Issues"]* — "FDA used an additional analysis set of Efficacy Cohort whose mutation was locally confirmed in the USPI, and all the analysis based on this analysis set were descriptive only with no formal testing."

### 177. zanidatamab-hrii (Ziihera) — BLA 761416

**Sponsor:** Jazz Pharmaceuticals

**Indication approved:** Adults with previously treated, unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive (IHC 3+) biliary tract cancer (BTC), as detected by an FDA-approved test — approved under accelerated approval based on objective response rate and duration of response

**Approval date:** November 20, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** HERIZON-BTC-01 (Study ZWI-ZW25-203), NCT04466891

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label, multicenter Phase 2b trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H; biomarker-selected/enriched population; companion diagnostic co-approval
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (cORR, primary, by independent central review [ICR] per RECIST 1.1); duration of response, clinical benefit rate, disease control rate, PFS, OS (secondary/exploratory — FDA classified all time-to-event endpoints and CBR/DCR as exploratory because "time-to-event endpoints are not interpretable in single-arm studies")
- *Primary analysis:* Descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (point estimate + CI, no formal hypothesis test) — "no statistical hypotheses were tested"; exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval for cORR, CBR, DCR; Brookmeyer-Crowley-type Kaplan-Meier median CIs with log-log transformation for DOR/PFS/OS
- *Missing data/bias:* Standard right-censoring per prespecified rules — PFS/OS censored at last evaluable CR/PR/SD/non-CR-non-PD assessment
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval (Subpart H) based on ORR and DOR; FDA narrowing of a sponsor-proposed eligibility/line-of-therapy threshold — FDA restricted the approved population to IHC3+ patients (cORR 51.6%) after finding IHC2+ patients responded far less (cORR 5.6%), despite the sponsor's broader HER2-amplified (ISH+) eligibility criterion; no FDA advisory committee meeting located in the reviewed sections

**Trial design & endpoints**

- HERIZON-BTC-01 (ZWI-ZW25-203) Cohort 1: single-arm, open-label, multicenter Phase 2b trial of zanidatamab monotherapy (20 mg/kg IV Q2W) in patients with centrally HER2-amplified (ISH+), previously gemcitabine-treated, unresectable/metastatic BTC; central HER2 IHC (2+ or 3+) was assessed but was not itself a prespecified eligibility criterion
- Primary endpoint: confirmed ORR (cORR) by RECIST 1.1 per ICR; no formal null hypothesis was tested — "This was a single-arm, open-label study. No statistical hypotheses were tested."
- Secondary/exploratory endpoints: DOR, clinical benefit rate, disease control rate, PFS, OS by ICR and investigator; FDA classified time-to-event endpoints and CBR/DCR as exploratory only, as they are "not interpretable in single-arm studies"
- Results (data cutoff 28 July 2023; efficacy analysis set N=80): cORR 41.3% (95% CI 30.4-52.8%; 2.5% CR, 38.8% PR); clinical benefit rate 47.5% (95% CI 36.2-59.0%); disease control rate 68.8% (95% CI 57.4-78.7%). Subgroup analysis by IHC status showed cORR 51.6% (95% CI 38.6-64.5%) in IHC3+ patients (n=62) versus 5.6% (95% CI 0.1-27.3%) in IHC2+ patients (n=18) — FDA restricted the approved indication to the IHC3+ subgroup on this basis, requiring an FDA-approved companion diagnostic

[DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(23)00242-5>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37276871/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Zanidatamab+for+HER2-amplified+unresectable+locally+advanced+or+metastatic+biliary+tract+cancer+HERIZON-BTC-01)

### 178. zenocutuzumab-zbco (Bizengri) — BLA 761352

**Sponsor:** Merus N.V.

**Indication approved:** Adults with unresectable or metastatic NRG1 fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) or pancreatic adenocarcinoma who have progressed on or after prior systemic therapy — approved under accelerated approval based on objective response rate and duration of response, labeled separately by tumor type

**Approval date:** December 4, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** eNRGy (Study MCLA-128-CL01), NCT02912949

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label, multicohort Phase 1/2 trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H; biomarker-selected/enriched population; tumor-agnostic (tissue-agnostic) basket trial
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR, primary, per RECIST 1.1 by investigator, supported by BICR); duration of response (key secondary); clinical benefit rate at 24 weeks (secondary, not considered by FDA to itself reflect antitumor activity)
- *Primary analysis:* Descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis — no formal hypothesis test, ORR reported as a point estimate with 95% CI separately for each tumor type
- *Missing data/bias:* Not applicable in the randomized sense; time-to-event endpoints (PFS/OS) considered exploratory only, "not interpretable in a single arm study due to lack of comparator"
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval (Subpart H) based on ORR/DOR in two separately labeled tumor types from one shared single-arm trial; confirmatory evidence via continuation/expansion of the same pivotal single-arm trial; no FDA advisory committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- eNRGy (MCLA-128-CL01): open-label, multicenter, multicohort Phase 1/2 trial of zenocutuzumab (750 mg IV Q2W) in patients with advanced solid tumors harboring an NRG1 gene fusion (by local or central NGS testing) across histologies; NSCLC and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cohorts were each analyzed and labeled as separate primary efficacy populations rather than pooled
- Primary endpoint: ORR by RECIST 1.1 (investigator-assessed, with BICR-assessed ORR as a supportive secondary); key secondary endpoint DOR
- FDA/sponsor agreement on endpoint acceptability was documented explicitly for the rare PDAC cohort: "ORR may be considered acceptable in this rare population depending on the magnitude of response and depending on the characterization of duration of response with a sufficient number of responding patients being followed for at least six months from onset of response"
- Analysis populations per SAP v4.0 (20 Sep 2023): Safety Analysis Set; Primary Efficacy Set (PES, requiring ≥24 weeks follow-up opportunity); Supportive Efficacy Set; disease-specific PES subsets for NSCLC (previously-treated, platinum-pretreated, platinum/immunotherapy-pretreated, treatment-naive) and PDAC
- Results (data cutoff 31 Jul 2023): in previously-treated NRG1+ NSCLC (N=64), ORR by BICR was 33% (95% CI 22-46%); in NRG1+ PDAC (N=30), ORR by BICR was 40% (95% CI 23-59%); a substantial majority of responders in both cohorts had DOR ≥6 months
- FDA required the efficacy population to also include patients screened but initially deemed ineligible, once an independent reviewer retrospectively confirmed NRG1-fusion functionality — broader than the sponsor's SAP-defined criteria alone

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/761352s000lbl.pdf

*[verbatim, same source, FDA's Assessment on endpoints]* — "FDA considers ORR per RECIST 1.1. by BICR an appropriate efficacy endpoint to support accelerated approval where ORR is of sufficient magnitude and duration... time to event endpoints such as 'time from start of treatment until progression or death, whichever occurs first' and 'time from start of treatment until death' are not interpretable in a single arm study due to lack of comparator, and will be considered exploratory only."

### 179. cosibelimab-ipdl (Unloxcyt) — BLA 761297

**Sponsor:** Checkpoint Therapeutics, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adults with metastatic cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (mCSCC) or locally advanced cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (laCSCC) who are not candidates for curative surgery or curative radiation — regular (traditional) approval based on objective response rate and duration of response, supported by correlative shrinkage of disfiguring cutaneous lesions

**Approval date:** December 13, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** Study CK-301-101, NCT03212404

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label, multiregional, dose-escalation and multicohort-expansion Phase 1 trial
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR, primary, by independent central review [ICR] per RECIST 1.1, with digital-photography/WHO-criteria assessment for laCSCC lesions not assessable by imaging); duration of response (key secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* Descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (point estimate + CI, no formal hypothesis test) with exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval
- *Missing data/bias:* Standard right-censoring per prespecified rules, refined via 2022 FDA information requests specifically on censoring conventions for time-to-event endpoints
- *Regulatory:* Regular approval grounded in durable-ORR-as-direct-clinical-benefit (single-arm trial); original BLA received a Complete Response Letter (December 15, 2023) solely for CMC/manufacturing-facility inspection deficiencies at a third-party manufacturer, not for clinical efficacy — FDA had already concluded "the evidentiary requirement for traditional approval has been met" before the CRL and reaffirmed it after CMC remediation; no FDA advisory committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study CK-301-101: open-label, multicenter, multiregional, dose-escalation and multicohort-expansion Phase 1 trial of cosibelimab (an anti-PD-L1 antibody) in patients with unresectable laCSCC or mCSCC not amenable to local therapy; the pivotal efficacy population comprised 109 patients treated with cosibelimab 800 mg IV Q2W, bridged via flat exposure-response relationships to a proposed 1200 mg Q3W commercial dosage
- Primary endpoint: ORR by ICR per RECIST 1.1, with digital-photography/WHO-criteria assessment for laCSCC lesions with externally visible target lesions not assessable radiologically; key secondary endpoint duration of response
- FDA and the sponsor negotiated trial conduct extensively across multiple Type B/Type C meetings (2019-2022): FDA agreed pre-IND that single-arm ORR/DOR data could support a BLA, required responders to generally have ≥6 months of follow-up, rejected the sponsor's initial Integrated Summary of Safety pooling proposal, and set stricter inclusion criteria than proposed for a laCSCC (Group 2) interim analysis
- Results: confirmed ORR 47% (95% CI 36-59%; n=37) in mCSCC, with median DOR not reached (range 1.4+ to 34.1+ months); confirmed ORR 48% (95% CI 30-67%; n=15) in laCSCC with median DOR 17.7 months
- Regulatory history: the original BLA (submitted January 3, 2023) was assessed by FDA's clinical review team as meeting the evidentiary bar for traditional approval, but received a Complete Response Letter (December 15, 2023) solely due to premarket-inspection deficiencies at the Samsung Biologics (Incheon, Korea) manufacturing facility; after CMC remediation, the resubmitted BLA was approved December 13, 2024 with no new efficacy/safety data required

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2024/761297Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/761297s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation, combining the original review (Reference ID 5294759) and post-CRL resubmission review (Reference ID 5495364), BLA 761297 — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/761297Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (Study CK-301-101) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03212404 (no protocol or SAP posted in the Documents tab as of this writing)

### 180. ensartinib (Ensacove) — NDA 218171

**Sponsor:** Xcovery Holdings, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adults with locally advanced or metastatic ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), as detected by an FDA-approved test — regular approval based on progression-free survival in a randomized, active-controlled trial

**Approval date:** December 18, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** eXalt3, NCT02767804

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial in TKI-naive ALK-positive NSCLC; biomarker-selected/enriched population; randomization stratified by prior chemotherapy, ECOG PS, CNS metastases, and geographic region
- *Endpoints:* Progression-free survival (PFS, primary, by BICR per RECIST 1.1); overall survival (key secondary); CNS response rate, time to CNS progression, ORR (other secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* [inferred] Cox proportional-hazards model / log-rank test — the label reports an unstratified log-rank p-value (0.0007) alongside an HR of 0.56 (95% CI 0.40-0.79); [inferred] given the four-factor stratified randomization design, the SAP plausibly prespecified a stratified analysis as primary, with the unstratified log-rank result being what the label happens to footnote — this cannot be confirmed without the SAP or an FDA statistical review, neither of which is publicly posted
- *Missing data/bias:* [inferred] standard right-censoring at last evaluable tumor assessment
- *Regulatory:* No accelerated-approval language in the label; approved on PFS in a randomized, active-controlled trial, with mature final OS reported as not statistically significant (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.63-1.23, p=0.4570) — [inferred] regular approval

**Trial design & endpoints**

- eXalt3: open-label, randomized (1:1), active-controlled, multicenter Phase 3 trial of ensartinib (225 mg PO once daily) versus crizotinib (250 mg PO BID) in TKI-naive, ALK-positive, locally advanced (Stage IIIB) or metastatic NSCLC; up to one prior chemotherapy regimen permitted, no prior ALK-targeted therapy
- Randomization stratified by prior chemotherapy (0 vs. 1), ECOG PS (0/1 vs. 2), CNS metastases (yes/no), and geographic region (Asia vs. rest of world)
- Primary endpoint: PFS by BICR per RECIST 1.1; key secondary: OS; other secondary: CNS response rate, time to CNS progression, ORR
- Results (label Table 6): 290 patients randomized (ensartinib n=143, crizotinib n=147); median PFS 25.8 months vs. 12.7 months, HR 0.56 (95% CI 0.40-0.79), p=0.0007 (unstratified log-rank per label footnote); ORR 74% vs. 67%; median DOR not estimable vs. 27.3 months; final OS showed no statistically significant difference (p=0.4570), median OS 63.2 vs. 55.7 months, HR 0.88 (95% CI 0.63-1.23); CNS ORR in patients with baseline measurable CNS disease was 59% vs. 21%
- No FDA Statistical Review, Clinical Review, or combined Multi-Discipline Review package is publicly posted for NDA 218171 as of this writing — the SAP below is therefore reverse-engineered from the label and the pivotal publication rather than quoted from a genuine SAP or FDA review

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2024/218171Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/218171s000lbl.pdf

- *[inferred, from the "key secondary" designation of OS in the label]* a hierarchical or alpha-preserving testing procedure linking PFS and OS was likely prespecified, though whether it was fixed-sequence, alpha-spending, or a simple hierarchical gate cannot be confirmed without the SAP; OS was reported as non-significant at final, mature analysis (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.63-1.23, p=0.4570), consistent with a secondary readout that did not undermine the PFS-based approval.
- *[inferred, from the label's dedicated CNS-subgroup table]* CNS response rate and time to CNS progression were likely prespecified secondary endpoints given their systematic reporting for the measurable-CNS-disease subgroup (N=17 vs. 24), standard oncology-SAP practice for ALK inhibitors given the drug class's known CNS activity.

### 181. datopotamab deruxtecan-dlnk (Datroway) — BLA 761394

**Sponsor:** Daiichi Sankyo, Inc. (co-developed with AstraZeneca)

**Indication approved:** Adults with unresectable or metastatic, hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative (IHC 0, IHC 1+, or IHC 2+/ISH-) breast cancer who have received prior endocrine-based therapy and chemotherapy for metastatic disease — regular approval based on progression-free survival

**Approval date:** January 17, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** TROPION-Breast01 (Study D9268C00001), NCT05104866

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial; randomization stratified by number of previous chemotherapy lines, geographic region, and prior CDK4/6 inhibitor use; co-primary/dual endpoint structure spanning PFS and OS with formal alpha reallocation between them
- *Endpoints:* Progression-free survival (PFS, primary, by BICR per RECIST 1.1); overall survival (dual/co-primary-tested secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* Stratified log-rank test with hazard ratio and CI from a stratified Cox proportional-hazards model (ties = Efron, profile-likelihood CI)
- *Multiplicity:* Alpha recycling — the 1.0% two-sided alpha allocated to PFS was reallocated in full to OS (bringing OS's total alpha to 5.0%) once the PFS analysis crossed its efficacy threshold
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function approximating an O'Brien-Fleming boundary governing two OS interim analyses (~40% and ~80% information fraction) plus a final OS analysis
- *Missing data/bias:* Inverse Probability of Censoring Weighting (IPCW) — a post hoc sponsor sensitivity analysis adjusting final OS for imbalanced subsequent anti-cancer-drug-conjugate (ADC) therapy use, which FDA judged unreliable due to untestable no-unmeasured-confounders assumptions; tipping-point analysis (multiple imputation) addressing informative censoring from withdrawal of consent/loss to follow-up
- *Regulatory:* Regular approval based on PFS despite a numerically unfavorable final OS hazard ratio (1.01, 95% CI 0.83-1.22) — FDA and the sponsor both ran extensive OS sensitivity analyses (HR range 0.86-1.09) without reversing this conclusion; no FDA advisory committee meeting held ("FDA did not refer this application to an advisory committee as there were no efficacy or safety issues that were unexpected")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- TROPION-Breast01 (D9268C00001): open-label, randomized (1:1), multicenter Phase 3 trial of datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd, 6 mg/kg IV Q3W) versus ICC in 732 patients with inoperable/metastatic HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer previously treated with 1-2 lines of chemotherapy for metastatic disease and endocrine-based therapy; randomization stratified by number of previous lines of chemotherapy, geographic region, and prior CDK4/6 inhibitor use
- Primary endpoint: PFS by BICR per RECIST 1.1, analyzed by stratified log-rank test with HR/CI from a stratified Cox model (Efron ties, profile-likelihood CI); design assumed a true PFS HR of 0.55 (median PFS 4.7 vs. 8.5 months), with 419 events (60% maturity) giving >99% power at a 2-sided 1.0% alpha
- OS design: primary OS analysis planned at ~444 events (63% maturity), assuming a true HR of 0.75 and 19.0-month median OS in ICC, for 85% power at a 2-sided 5.0% alpha if PFS crossed its efficacy threshold (which it did, so the full 5.0% alpha applied to OS); two OS interim analyses were planned at ~40% and ~80% information fraction using a Lan-DeMets/O'Brien-Fleming-type spending function
- Results: PFS HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.52-0.76, 99% CI 0.49-0.80; p<0.0001), median PFS 6.9 months (Dato-DXd) vs. 4.9 months (ICC); at the first OS interim analysis, HR was 0.84 (95% CI 0.62-1.14); at the final OS analysis (data cutoff July 24, 2024), the observed HR was 1.01 (95% CI 0.83-1.22) — i.e., no OS benefit and a numerically unfavorable point estimate
- FDA and the sponsor conducted multiple OS sensitivity analyses to probe this result: an unstratified Cox model (HR 1.01), a tipping-point analysis imputing informative censoring for ICC-arm dropouts (HR 1.09), censoring those same patients at cutoff (HR 1.09), and a post hoc IPCW analysis adjusting for imbalanced subsequent ADC-class therapy use (Dato-DXd 12% vs. ICC 24%; HR 0.86) — FDA judged the IPCW analysis's interpretability limited by untestable confounding assumptions and it "did not meaningfully contribute to the FDA's assessment of OS"
- The review team ultimately recommended regular approval for the PFS result, alongside supportive DOR/ORR/quality-of-life secondary findings, despite the unfavorable final OS point estimate

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.24.00920), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39265124/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Datopotamab+Deruxtecan+Versus+Chemotherapy+in+Previously+Treated+Inoperable+Metastatic+Hormone+Receptor-Positive+HER2-Negative+Breast+Cancer+TROPION-Breast01)

- Two postmarketing OS interim analyses beyond the first (submitted with the initial BLA) were reviewed by FDA during the review cycle as they matured, ultimately reaching the numerically unfavorable final HR of 1.01 described above.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation, BLA 761394, Reference ID 5513740, "Statistical Analysis Plan and Amendments"]* — "Progression-free survival was analyzed using a log-rank test stratified by number of previous lines of chemotherapy, geographic region, and prior use of CDK4/6i. The hazard ratio together with its 95% CI and p-value was presented... The hazard ratio and CI were estimated from a stratified Cox Proportional Hazards model (with ties = Efron), and the CI calculated using a profile likelihood approach."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "For the primary analysis of PFS, assuming the true PFS treatment effect under the alternative hypothesis was a hazard ratio of 0.55 for Dato-DXd versus ICC... 419 PFS events from the FAS population (60% maturity) would provide greater than 99% power to demonstrate statistical significance at the 2-sided alpha level of 1.0%."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "The Lan DeMets approach (Lan and DeMets 1983) that approximates the O'Brien and Fleming spending function will be used to maintain an overall 2-sided type I error across the 3 planned analyses of OS. If the PFS dual primary analysis crosses the efficacy threshold, the 1.0% type I error allocated to the PFS endpoint will be reallocated to the OS endpoint for a total 2-sided type I error of 5.0%."

*[verbatim, same source, FDA's Assessment]* — "Since no alpha was allocated to endpoints other than PFS per BICR assessment and OS, all other endpoints are considered exploratory, and no statistical inference can be drawn from them. Since the final PFS analysis was statistically significant, the OS analyses were conducted with a 2-sided type I error of 5%."

*[verbatim, same source, final OS sensitivity discussion]* — "At the final OS analysis, the observed hazard ratio was 1.01 (95% CI: 0.83, 1.22). Both FDA and the Applicant conducted multiple sensitivity analyses to further explore the final OS results... Hazard ratio point estimates ranged from 0.86 to 1.09 across sensitivity analyses."

*[verbatim, same source, on the IPCW sensitivity analysis]* — "The FDA review team notes that the interpretation of this analysis is limited by uncertainties in model specification and assumptions, since the model relies on the key assumption of no unmeasured confounders and this assumption could not be tested in practice... This particular analysis did not meaningfully contribute to the FDA's assessment of OS."

*[verbatim, same source, Advisory Committee]* — "FDA did not refer this application to an advisory committee as there were no efficacy or safety issues that were unexpected for a drug of this class."

### 182. mirdametinib (Gomekli) — NDA 219379

**Sponsor:** SpringWorks Therapeutics, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adults and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) who have symptomatic plexiform neurofibromas (PN) not amenable to complete resection — regular approval based on objective response rate and duration of response, treating durable tumor-volume regression as direct clinical benefit

**Approval date:** February 11, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** ReNeu, NCT03962543

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label, multicenter Phase 2b trial, enrolling separate adult and pediatric cohorts within one trial rather than pooling them; biomarker-selected/enriched population not applicable (genetically-defined disease, NF1, rather than a molecularly-selected subgroup within a broader cancer)
- *Endpoints:* Confirmed overall response rate (ORR, primary, by BICR per REiNS-modified criteria, requiring confirmation at a subsequent assessment 2-6 months later); duration of response (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* [inferred] Descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis with exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval — no formal null-hypothesis test is described in the label
- *Missing data/bias:* [inferred] Non-responder imputation for missing binary/diary efficacy data — the label states "patients who had no post-baseline MRI assessment or no confirmed overall response were treated as non-responders"
- *Regulatory:* Regular approval grounded in durable-ORR-as-direct-clinical-benefit (single-arm trial) — no accelerated-approval language in the label; no FDA statistical/clinical/multi-discipline review is publicly posted

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ReNeu: multicenter, single-arm, open-label Phase 2b trial of mirdametinib (2 mg/m² PO BID for 21 of every 28 days) in 114 patients ≥2 years old with symptomatic, inoperable NF1-associated plexiform neurofibromas causing significant morbidity (defined by encasement/proximity to vital structures, invasiveness, or high vascularity precluding complete surgical removal), enrolled as separate adult (N=58) and pediatric (N=56) cohorts
- Primary endpoint: confirmed ORR — complete response (disappearance of the target PN) or partial response (≥20% volume reduction) by BICR volumetric MRI per REiNS criteria, modified to require confirmation at a subsequent assessment within 2-6 months during the 24-cycle treatment phase
- Secondary endpoint: duration of response for confirmed responders
- Results: confirmed ORR was 41% (95% CI 29-55%) in adults and 52% (95% CI 38-65%) in the pediatric cohort; among responders, 88% (adults) and 90% (pediatric) had DOR ≥12 months, and 50% (adults) and 48% (pediatric) had DOR ≥24 months; median time to onset of response was 7.8 months (adults) and 7.9 months (pediatric)
- No FDA Statistical Review, Clinical Review, or combined Multi-Discipline Review package is publicly posted for NDA 219379 as of this writing (direct-pattern URL guesses under both the 219379 and a related 219389 application-number prefix all returned 404) — the SAP below is therefore reverse-engineered from the label and the pivotal publication

**Reverse-engineered SAP** *[inferred]*

- *[inferred, from the label's explicit Clopper-Pearson footnote in Table 7]* the primary ORR analysis almost certainly used an exact (Clopper-Pearson) binomial confidence interval, consistent with the standard convention for single-arm oncology response-rate endpoints and directly confirmed by the label's own methods footnote ("Obtained using the Clopper-Pearson approach"), even though no formal null-hypothesis performance goal is stated in the label.
- *[inferred, from separate adult/pediatric cohort reporting in Table 7]* the SAP likely prespecified adult and pediatric cohorts as co-primary or separately powered analysis populations rather than a single pooled population, since the label reports fully separate ORR/DOR estimates and confidence intervals for each age group rather than a combined estimate.
- *[inferred, from the label's non-responder imputation language]* missing or unconfirmed response data were almost certainly handled by a prespecified non-responder-imputation rule, given the label's explicit statement that "patients who had no post-baseline MRI assessment or no confirmed overall response were treated as non-responders" — a conservative missing-data convention typical of single-arm ORR SAPs.
- *[inferred, from the requirement for confirmation "within 2-6 months"]* the SAP likely specified an explicit confirmatory-assessment window (2-6 months) as an endpoint-definition rule to guard against transient or measurement-noise responses being counted as confirmed, consistent with REiNS-based volumetric MRI practice in NF1-PN trials generally.
- *[inferred, from the trial's single-arm design and lack of an accelerated-approval statement in the label]* FDA likely treated durable, BICR-confirmed volumetric tumor regression in this visibly consequential, disfiguring/functionally-morbid disease as direct evidence of clinical benefit (rather than a surrogate requiring confirmatory-trial verification), paralleling the regulatory logic previously applied to selumetinib in the same indication and to cemiplimab in cutaneous SCC.

### 183. vimseltinib (Romvimza) — NDA 219304

**Sponsor:** Deciphera Pharmaceuticals, LLC

**Indication approved:** Adults with symptomatic tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TGCT) associated with severe morbidity or functional limitations and not amenable to improvement with surgery — regular approval based on objective response rate in a randomized, placebo-controlled trial

**Approval date:** February 14, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** MOTION (Study DCC-3014-03-001), NCT05059262

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial — a design choice explicitly following the pexidartinib/ENLIVEN precedent in the same disease; randomization stratified by region (US vs. non-US) and tumor location
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR, primary, per RECIST 1.1 and per tumor volume score [TVS], both by BICR at Week 25); active range of motion (ROM), PROMIS Physical Function, Worst Stiffness NRS, EQ-5D-5L VAS, BPI-30 worst-pain response (key secondary endpoints, tested hierarchically)
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test, stratified by the randomization factors, for ORR by RECIST and by TVS; mixed model for repeated measurements (MMRM) with a sandwich variance estimator for continuous patient-reported-outcome key secondaries; Fisher's exact test for the BPI-30 binary responder analysis
- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing across seven ordered primary/key-secondary endpoints (ORR-RECIST → ORR-TVS → active ROM → PROMIS-PF → Worst Stiffness NRS → EQ-VAS → BPI-30 responder), each tested at a two-sided 0.05 alpha level only if all prior endpoints in the sequence were significant
- *Missing data/bias:* Multiple imputation (missing-at-random, by randomized treatment) and a Pattern Mixture Model (missing-not-at-random, imputing vimseltinib-arm AE-driven discontinuations as if on placebo) for key secondary endpoints with >10% missingness at Week 25
- *Regulatory:* Regular approval based on ORR from a randomized, placebo-controlled trial (not accelerated) — an evidentiary approach the review explicitly analogizes to pexidartinib's prior ENLIVEN-based approval in the same indication; no FDA advisory committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- MOTION (DCC-3014-03-001): double-blind, multicenter, randomized (2:1), placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial of vimseltinib (30 mg PO twice weekly) versus placebo in 123 adult patients with TGCT not amenable to surgical improvement; crossover to open-label vimseltinib was permitted for placebo patients after the Week-25 double-blind primary analysis
- Sample size: 120 patients (2:1 randomization) planned for 98% power to detect a difference between assumed true ORRs of 35% (vimseltinib) and 5% (placebo), using a two-sided Fisher's exact test at a 5% alpha level
- Primary endpoint: ORR at Week 25 per RECIST 1.1 by BICR; ORR per tumor volume score (TVS) by BICR was co-primary/parallel; both analyzed with a stratified CMH test
- Key secondary endpoints (hierarchically tested, each at two-sided 0.05 alpha, in order): active ROM (affected joint), PROMIS Physical Function, Worst Stiffness NRS, EQ-5D-5L VAS (all via MMRM with treatment, timepoint, treatment-by-timepoint, stratification factors, and baseline value as covariates), then BPI-30 worst-pain responder rate (Fisher's exact test)
- Results: ORR at Week 25 by RECIST/BICR was 40% (95% CI 29-51%) for vimseltinib vs. 0% for placebo (stratified CMH p=0.0025 per one reported comparison in the review); statistically significant improvements were also demonstrated on several — though not all — of the hierarchically-ordered key secondary endpoints (stratified CMH p-values 0.0025-0.1621 were reported across the tested measures, with the final endpoint(s) in the sequence not reaching significance, per FDA Table); a separate open-label Phase 1/2 safety cohort (Cohorts A, B, and 5) and the placebo-crossover patients contributed pooled long-term safety data
- Protocol Amendment 3 (May 31, 2023, after enrollment completed) reclassified secondary endpoints into hierarchical ("key-secondary") versus non-hierarchical groups and moved RECIST-based ORR to secondary status in the protocol text — though FDA's review confirms RECIST-ORR was analyzed as (co-)primary for the regulatory submission

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/219304s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 5532076, NDA 219304) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219304Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf

[DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(24)00885-7>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38843860/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Vimseltinib+versus+placebo+for+tenosynovial+giant+cell+tumour+MOTION+phase+3+trial)

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation, NDA 219304, Reference ID 5532076, "Statistical Analysis Plan and Amendments"]* — "In this study, a total of 120 patients were planned to be randomized in a 2:1 ratio to vimseltinib and placebo arms. This sample size would provide 98% power to detect a statistically significant difference between treatment groups, assuming true ORRs of 35% and 5% in the vimseltinib arm and the placebo arm, respectively, using a two-sided Fisher's exact test at 5% type I error rate level."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "To control overall type I error, a hierarchical testing procedure was used. Statistical testing was performed for the analysis of primary and key secondary endpoints in the following order at a two-sided 0.05 alpha level for each: ORR per RECIST v1.1 at Week 25; ORR per TVS at Week 25; Mean change from baseline in active ROM at Week 25; Mean change from baseline in the PROMIS-PF score at Week 25; Mean change from baseline in the Worst Stiffness NRS score at Week 25; Mean change from baseline in EQ-VAS at Week 25; Proportion of responders based on BPI-30 Worst Pain NRS score and narcotic analgesic use at Week 25."

*[verbatim, same source, FDA Table 23]* — "ORR (RECIST 1.1 and TVS): Stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test... ROM/PROMIS-PF/Worst Stiffness NRS/EQ-5D-5L VAS: MMRM... BPI-30 Worst Pain NRS: Fisher's Exact test."

*[verbatim, same source, missing-data handling]* — "If there was more than 10% of missing data at Week 25 in any of the endpoints, then the impact of the missing data was explored for that endpoint... Multiple imputation based on randomized treatment to mimic missing at random; A Pattern Mixture Model approach where participants who discontinued treatment due to an AE on vimseltinib were imputed based on the missing not at random assumption and imputed as if they received placebo."

### 184. penpulimab-kcqx (unbranded) — BLA 761258

**Sponsor:** Akeso Biopharma, Inc. (Akeso, Inc.)

**Indication approved:** (1) In combination with cisplatin or carboplatin and gemcitabine, for first-line treatment of adults with recurrent or metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), based on progression-free survival in a randomized trial; and (2) as a single agent, for adults with metastatic non-keratinizing NPC with disease progression on or after platinum-based chemotherapy and at least one other prior line of therapy — approved under accelerated approval based on objective response rate and duration of response

**Approval date:** April 23, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** AK105-202 (single-agent indication), NCT03866967; AK105-304 (first-line combination indication), NCT04974398

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label, single-country trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H for the single-agent indication; randomized, double-blind, multicenter trial for the separately/regularly-approved first-line combination indication; retrospective/non-prospective regulatory sequence in which a first BLA cycle relying solely on the single-arm trial was rejected, and a second cycle adding randomized data succeeded
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR, primary, AK105-202, by independent radiology review committee [IRRC] per RECIST 1.1); progression-free survival (PFS, primary, AK105-304, by BICR) with overall survival as key secondary
- *Primary analysis:* Descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis with exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval implied by the SAP's sample-size framework; stratified log-rank test / Cox proportional-hazards model
- *Missing data/bias:* Not applicable in the randomized sense for AK105-304; for AK105-202, an interim analysis was conducted once ~110 patients had ≥8 months follow-up opportunity (to allow ≥6 months follow-up past response onset), a durability-driven analysis-timing rule rather than a formal alpha-spending interim
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval (Subpart H) based on ORR/DOR for the single-agent indication; FDA issued a Complete Response Letter on the original 2021 single-arm-only submission (January 19, 2024) on grounds that penpulimab "did not demonstrate a clear advantage over currently available therapeutic options" given an intervening approval of a competing anti-PD-1 (toripalimab) in the same setting, plus CGMP manufacturing-facility deficiencies; approval was ultimately achieved via a Class 2 resubmission adding the randomized AK105-304 first-line data; extrapolation of foreign trial data under 21 CFR 314.106(b), as both pivotal trials were conducted essentially exclusively in China; no FDA advisory committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- AK105-202 (single-agent indication): open-label, multicenter, single-arm, single-country (China) trial of penpulimab 200 mg IV Q2W in 125 patients with metastatic non-keratinizing NPC and disease progression after platinum-based chemotherapy plus at least one other prior line; major efficacy outcome measures were ORR and DOR by IRRC per RECIST 1.1
- AK105-202 sample-size logic: 110 patients needed for a lower 95% CI bound to exclude a 15% historical ORR benchmark, assuming a true penpulimab ORR of 26% (82% chance of observing ≥25 responses); an efficacy interim analysis was conducted once ~110 patients had an opportunity for ≥8 months of follow-up (to permit ≥6 months follow-up past response onset for durability assessment), with no formal stopping rule or alpha adjustment — "no formal statistical adjustments were planned"
- AK105-202 results: IRRC-assessed ORR was 28% (95% CI 20-37%); median DOR not reached (95% CI 9.2-not evaluable); 46% of the 35 responders had DOR ≥12 months
- AK105-304 (first-line combination indication): randomized (1:1), double-blind, multicenter trial of penpulimab (or placebo) plus cisplatin/carboplatin and gemcitabine for up to 6 cycles, followed by penpulimab (or placebo) monotherapy, in 291 patients with treatment-naive recurrent/metastatic NPC; primary endpoint PFS by BICR, key secondary OS
- AK105-304 results: at an interim PFS analysis (189 events, 85% information fraction), PFS HR was 0.45 (95% CI 0.33-0.62, p<0.0001), median PFS 9.6 vs. 7.0 months; at an OS interim analysis (70% information fraction), OS HR was 0.91 (95% CI 0.64-1.31), not yet significant, with 80% of placebo patients crossing over to anti-PD-(L)1 therapy at progression, complicating OS interpretability
- Regulatory sequence: the original BLA (July 2021), based solely on AK105-202, received a Complete Response Letter (January 19, 2024) because penpulimab "did not demonstrate a clear advantage over currently available therapeutic options" (the treatment landscape had shifted with toripalimab's 2023 approval in the same setting) and because of CGMP manufacturing deficiencies; the sponsor added the completed randomized AK105-304 trial in a Class 2 resubmission, which succeeded in April 2025, approving both a first-line combination indication (on AK105-304) and the original single-agent salvage indication (on AK105-202, whose data FDA still considered "clinically meaningful" once presented alongside the randomized confirmatory-style evidence)

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2025/761258Orig1s000correctedltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/761258Orig1s000correctedlbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 5577575, current cycle, with embedded content from the original 2021 review cycle at Reference ID 5313694), BLA 761258 — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/761258Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (AK105-202) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03866967; ClinicalTrials.gov record (AK105-304) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04974398 (no protocol or SAP posted in the Documents tab for either trial as of this writing)
- Pivotal publications: no dedicated peer-reviewed primary publication for AK105-202 or AK105-304 was identified via PubMed as of this writing (both trials are Chinese-sponsored studies whose primary results appear to be reported to date only via the FDA review and label); readers should treat the FDA review (cited above) and the label's §14 Clinical Studies as the primary public efficacy sources pending journal publication

**Other resources**

- Akeso's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for AK105-202 or AK105-304; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing identified.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for either indication.
- Both pivotal trials were conducted essentially exclusively in China (AK105-202: 100% enrolled in China per the label; AK105-304: 96% of randomized patients); FDA's review specifically discusses the 21 CFR 314.106(b) foreign-data-acceptability criteria as a "major limitation of this application."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation, BLA 761258, Reference ID 5577575, Executive Summary]* — "An initial Biologics Licensing Application (BLA) was submitted for penpulimab as a single-agent for patients with previously treated nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) on July 16, 2021, based on the results of the single-arm trial, Study AK105-202. FDA issued a Complete Response on January 19, 2024, as penpulimab did not demonstrate a clear advantage over currently available therapeutic options due to changes in the treatment landscape for NPC, to grant accelerated approval. Additionally, deficiencies were identified in CGMP operations in the penpulimab drug substance and drug product manufacturing facility."

*[verbatim, same source, Conclusions on Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness]* — "At an interim analysis of PFS based on 189 events (85% information fraction [IF]), the trial demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in BICR-assessed PFS favoring the penpulimab arm, with a hazard ratio (HR) of 0.45 (95% CI 0.33, 0.62, p-value <0.0001)... Notably, 80% of patients receiving placebo either crossed over to open-label treatment with penpulimab or received another anti-PD-(L)1 antibody as the next subsequent therapy upon confirmed disease progression, which may impact interpretability of the OS results."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "Study AK105-202 provides the primary efficacy data in support of the indication for the treatment of patients with non-keratinizing NPC... The IRRC-assessed ORR was 28% (95% CI: 20, 37) and the median duration of response (DOR) was not reached (95% CI: 9.2, not evaluable)."

*[verbatim, embedded original-cycle review, Reference ID 5313694, §7.1.1.3 "Statistical Analysis Plan and Amendments"]* — "A total of 110 patients were needed for an ORR of 15% to be excluded using the lower limit of a two-sided 95% CI. If an ORR of 26% is assumed for penpulimab, there is 82% chance of observing at least 25 responses (an ORR of 22.7%)... There were no plans to stop the trial based on either of these analyses and no formal statistical adjustments were planned."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "An interim analysis of efficacy was conducted after approximately 110 patients treated with penpulimab had an opportunity to be followed for at least 8 months prior to data cutoff date (to allow at least 6 months follow-up past onset of response assuming the response occurs at the first follow-up scan)."

*[verbatim, Reference ID 5577575, foreign-data limitation]* — "A major limitation of this application was that Study AK105-304 was conducted mostly in China (96% of randomized patients) and Study AK105-202 was conducted exclusively in China. Section 21 CFR 314.106(b) outlines three requirements to establish the acceptability of foreign data..."
