### 185. avutometinib/defactinib (Avmapki/Fakzynja) — NDA 219616

**Sponsor:** Verastem, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adults with KRAS-mutated recurrent low-grade serous ovarian cancer (LGSOC) who have received prior systemic therapy — approved under accelerated approval based on objective response rate and duration of response

**Approval date:** May 8, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** RAMP-201 (Study VS-6766-201), NCT04625270

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Adaptive seamless dose-selection-into-expansion design — an internal randomized dose/regimen-comparison stage (Parts A/B, avutometinib monotherapy vs. combination) resolved via interim analysis to select a go-forward (GF) regimen, followed by a single-arm expansion cohort (Part C) and a further low-dose exploratory arm (Part D) added by later amendment; single-arm, open-label trial for the pooled GF-regimen efficacy analysis (Parts A+B+C) supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H; biomarker-selected/enriched population
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR, primary, by BICR per RECIST 1.1, evaluated simultaneously in the overall GF-regimen population and in the KRAS-mutant subgroup); duration of response (secondary, responders only)
- *Primary analysis:* Exact binomial test against a pre-specified performance goal explicitly used only "to inform decision making and sample size planning" rather than as formal inference; FDA's own assessment applied descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis instead, stating that "statistical inferential procedures... will not be used to evaluate single-arm oncology trial results"
- *Missing data/bias:* Concordance/agreement analysis (positive/negative percent agreement), run as a sensitivity analysis on the biomarker-subgroup classification underlying the approved indication
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval (Subpart H) based on ORR/DOR restricted to the KRAS-mutant subgroup, despite the trial also enrolling and reporting results in KRAS-wild-type patients; contribution-of-components-adjacent dose/regimen comparison used to select and justify the combination regimen and its lower-dose alternative (Part D) prior to full-scale single-arm expansion; postmarketing requirement to complete RAMP-301, an ongoing randomized Phase 3 confirmatory trial; no FDA advisory committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- RAMP-201 (VS-6766-201): open-label, multicenter, multi-part adaptive trial of avutometinib (a RAF/MEK clamp) plus defactinib (a FAK inhibitor) in recurrent LGSOC; Part A/B randomized dose-regimen comparison (avutometinib monotherapy vs. combination, and among combination dose levels) resolved via interim analysis to select the go-forward (GF) regimen — avutometinib 3.2 mg PO BIW + defactinib 200 mg PO BID for 3 of every 4 weeks; Part C added a 40-patient single-arm expansion cohort at the GF regimen; Part D (added by a 2023 amendment) explored a lower starting dose (avutometinib 1.6 mg BIW + defactinib) against a disease-progression-rate comparator to rule out under-dosing
- Primary endpoint: confirmed ORR by BICR per RECIST 1.1 in the pooled GF-regimen population (Parts A+B+C), evaluated both overall and in the KRAS-mutant subgroup by local testing, at ~12 months' follow-up opportunity for all GF-regimen patients
- Sample-size/design logic: the GF-regimen ORR analysis was framed (for planning purposes only) as an exact binomial test of H0: ORR≤15% vs. Ha: ORR=40% at a nominal two-sided 2.5% level, with ≥36 patients giving ≥88% power — explicitly not intended as formal statistical inference, "a standard approach for single arm studies in oncology"
- Results: in patients with KRAS-mutated recurrent LGSOC (N=57), confirmed ORR by BICR was 43.9% (95% CI 30.7-57.6%); in the combination-arm KRAS-mutant subgroup within the randomized Part A/B comparison, ORR was 43.9% (95% CI 30.7-57.6%) vs. 23.3% (95% CI 9.9-42.3%) for avutometinib monotherapy; across the full combination-arm population (KRAS-mutant + wild-type, N=109), ORR by BICR was 31.2% (95% CI 22.7-40.8%) — the approved indication was ultimately restricted to the KRAS-mutant subgroup, where both magnitude and consistency of benefit were considered adequate
- Postmarketing requirement: the ongoing randomized RAMP-301 trial (avutometinib + defactinib vs. investigator's choice) was made a condition of accelerated approval, alongside routine echocardiographic monitoring added to its protocol in response to cardiomyopathy signals seen with the RAMP-201 combination

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2025/219616Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/219616s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 5586960, NDA 219616) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219616Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (RAMP-201) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04625270 (no protocol or SAP posted in the Documents tab as of this writing)
- Pivotal publication: Banerjee SN, Ghatage P, Monk BJ, et al. "Efficacy and Safety of Avutometinib ± Defactinib in Recurrent Low-Grade Serous Ovarian Cancer: Primary Analysis of ENGOT-OV60/GOG-3052/RAMP 201." *J Clin Oncol.* 2025;43(25):2782-2792. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO-25-00112), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40644648/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Efficacy+and+Safety+of+Avutometinib+Defactinib+in+Recurrent+Low-Grade+Serous+Ovarian+Cancer+RAMP+201)

**Other resources**

- Verastem's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for RAMP-201; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing identified.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this application.
- Postmarketing requirement: completion of RAMP-301 (NCT06072781 or related registration, an ongoing randomized Phase 3 trial comparing avutometinib+defactinib to investigator's choice) to verify clinical benefit, per accelerated-approval conditions; routine echocardiography was added to the RAMP-301 protocol specifically to characterize a cardiomyopathy risk signal observed in RAMP-201.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation, NDA 219616, Reference ID 5586960, §8.1.1.5 "Statistical Analysis Plan and Amendments"]* — "The overall objective of this adaptive study was to estimate the confirmed ORR for patients treated at the recommended dose... Confirmed BIRC ORR in the efficacy evaluable population for the GF regimen was assessed using an exact binomial test with a nominal 2.5% two-sided significance level using a null hypothesis ORR of 15% and alternative hypothesis ORR of 40%. The sample size of at least 36 patients was planned for at least 88% power to detect the difference between these hypotheses. The pre-specified criteria were to inform decision making and sample size planning and do not represent formal statistical inference. This is a standard approach for single arm studies in oncology."

*[verbatim, same source, FDA's Assessment]* — "The FDA notes that statistical inferential procedures (testing procedures, performance goals, type I error control, etc.) will not be used to evaluate single-arm oncology trial results. The FDA's efficacy evaluation was based on the descriptive assessment of magnitude of response rate as the primary endpoint and the duration of response as an additional endpoint."

*[verbatim, same source, dose-selection rule]* — "To support dose-optimization, rate of disease progression in the low-dose group (Part D) was compared with the go-forward regimen (Parts A, B, and C). If the rate of disease progression by 4 months was > 50% higher than that observed with avutometinib 3.2 mg PO BIW + defactinib, then the starting dose combination of avutometinib 1.6 mg PO BIW + defactinib was determined to be suboptimal."

*[verbatim, same source, KRAS assay sensitivity analysis]* — "Concordance/agreement (PPA, Positive Percent Agreement and, NPA, Negative Percent Agreement) between the local clinical trial assays used for determination of KRAS status and the central KRAS assay (Tempus xT) was analyzed as a sensitivity analysis to assess the robustness of the data."

*[verbatim, label §14, confirmed via FDA review results tables]* — "The confirmed ORR was 43.9% (n= 25/57; 95% CI: 30.7, 57.6) in the 57 patients with KRAS-mutated, recurrent LGSOC... comparing avutometinib monotherapy [23.3% (95% CI 9.9, 42.3)] with the combination [43.9% (95% CI 30.7, 57.6)] in the KRAS-mutated subgroup of the randomized cohort (Part A and B)."

*[verbatim, same source, postmarketing commitment]* — "Applicant agreed to a post-marketing requirement to submit results from RAMP-301, the ongoing randomized trial comparing [avutometinib plus defactinib to investigator's choice of treatment]... added routine echocardiography to the protocol of the ongoing phase 3 trial, RAMP-301, and a PMR was issued to conduct a clinical trial (i.e., RAMP-301) to characterize the risk of cardiomyopathy."

### 186. Telisotuzumab vedotin-tllv (Emrelis) — BLA 761384

**Sponsor:** AbbVie Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adults with locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), EGFR wildtype, whose tumors have high c-Met protein overexpression, as determined by an FDA-approved test, and who have received a prior systemic therapy — approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate and duration of response

**Approval date:** May 14, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** LUMINOSITY (Study M14-239), NCT03539536

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label, multi-cohort Phase 2 trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H/21 CFR 314.500; biomarker-selected/enriched population (c-Met protein overexpression, high-expression cohort, EGFR wildtype)
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR, primary — blinded independent central review [BICR] per RECIST v1.1); duration of response (DoR, secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* Descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (point estimate + CI, no formal hypothesis test) — ORR and DoR reported as point estimates with 95% CIs; the label does not name a specific CI-construction method (e.g., Clopper-Pearson) or a pre-specified null/performance-goal threshold
- *Missing data/bias:* Not applicable in the randomized-trial sense (no comparator/crossover); standard right-censoring for duration of response
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval (Subpart H) based on ORR/DoR, confirmatory trial required; companion diagnostic (VENTANA MET [SP44] RxDx Assay) used as a retrospective bridging assay to the trial's prospective clinical-trial assay; no FDA advisory committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- LUMINOSITY (M14-239): multicenter, open-label, single-arm, multi-cohort Phase 2 trial of telisotuzumab vedotin (a c-Met-directed antibody-drug conjugate) in adults with locally advanced/metastatic, non-squamous, EGFR-wildtype NSCLC with c-Met protein overexpression and no more than one prior line of systemic therapy in the locally advanced/metastatic setting
- c-Met overexpression (high: ≥50% of tumor cells with strong [3+] membrane staining by IHC) was determined prospectively before enrollment using the MET (SP44) clinical trial assay; the efficacy-supporting population (N=84) is the high-expression, EGFR-wildtype, non-squamous cohort
- A retrospective bridging analysis compared the trial's clinical-trial assay against the VENTANA MET (SP44) RxDx companion diagnostic assay in 38/84 (45%) of samples: of 37 evaluable, 32 (87%) were also classified as high-expression by the RxDx assay
- Primary (major) efficacy outcome measure: confirmed ORR by BICR per RECIST v1.1; additional efficacy measure: DOR by BICR
- Dosing: telisotuzumab vedotin 1.9 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity
- Results: confirmed ORR 35% (95% CI 24-46%; 0% CR, 35% PR) among 84 efficacy-evaluable patients; median DOR 7.2 months (95% CI 4.2-12) among 29 responders, with 59% of responses lasting ≥6 months and 21% lasting ≥12 months
- No sample-size/power justification, statistical testing procedure, or CI-construction method is stated in the publicly available label text — consistent with a purely descriptive single-arm response-rate presentation

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2025/761384Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/761384s000lbl.pdf
- No FDA Statistical Review, Clinical Review, or combined Multi-Discipline Review package was found publicly posted for this application as of this writing (direct-pattern URL checks at `accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/bla/2025/761384Orig1s000{StatR,MedR,MultidisciplineR,SumR,ClinPharmR}.pdf` all returned 404); consistent with this being a very recent (May 2025) approval
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (LUMINOSITY) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03539536 (no protocol/SAP posted in the Documents tab as of this writing; the API record has no `documentSection`)
- Pivotal publication: Camidge DR, Bar J, Horinouchi H, Goldman J, Moiseenko F, Filippova E, Cicin I, Ciuleanu T, Daaboul N, Liu C, Bradbury P, Moskovitz M, Katgi N, Tomasini P, Zer A, Girard N, Cuppens K, Han JY, Wu SY, Baijal S, Mansfield AS, Kuo CH, Nishino K, Lee SH, Planchard D, Baik C, Li M, Ansell P, Xia S, Bolotin E, Looman J, Ratajczak C, Lu S. "Telisotuzumab Vedotin Monotherapy in Patients With Previously Treated c-Met Protein-Overexpressing Advanced Nonsquamous EGFR-Wildtype Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer in the Phase II LUMINOSITY Trial." *J Clin Oncol.* 2024;42(25):3000-3011. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.24.00720), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38843488/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Telisotuzumab%20Vedotin%20Monotherapy%20in%20Patients%20With%20Previously%20Treated%20c-Met%20Protein-Overexpressing%20Advanced%20Nonsquamous%20EGFR-Wildtype%20Non-Small%20Cell%20Lung%20Cancer%20LUMINOSITY)

**Other resources**

- AbbVie's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for LUMINOSITY; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for this trial.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held; the approval letter states the application "was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant public health questions on the role of the biologic in the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment, or prevention of a disease."
- Postmarketing requirement (PMR 4844-1, per the approval letter): complete the ongoing randomized trial, Study M18-868, to verify and describe clinical benefit in previously treated c-Met-overexpressing, EGFR-wildtype, locally advanced/metastatic non-squamous NSCLC; per the sponsor's May 8, 2025 submission, estimated trial completion December 2028 and final report submission June 2029.

**Reverse-engineered SAP** *[inferred]*

- *[inferred, from label §14/Table 8 and the JCO publication's Methods]* — Efficacy analysis was almost certainly conducted on a pre-specified "efficacy-evaluable" analysis set restricted to EGFR-wildtype, non-squamous, high c-Met-overexpression patients (N=84), given that the label reports results only for this subgroup rather than for all LUMINOSITY enrollees (the trial's broader multi-cohort design included squamous histology and lower c-Met-expression cohorts not carried into the approved indication).
- *[inferred, from the absence of any named CI method or performance-goal threshold in the label]* — The primary ORR analysis is most likely a simple descriptive estimate with a two-sided 95% confidence interval (plausibly Clopper-Pearson, the field's near-universal default for single-proportion CIs in oncology single-arm trials, per its use in comparable accelerated-approval ADC/TKI submissions in this census such as mirvetuximab soravtansine/Elahere and olutasidenib/Rezlidhia), rather than a formal one-sided hypothesis test against a pre-specified null ORR, since no null/performance-goal value is stated anywhere in the public label.
- *[inferred, from the trial's "Phase 2, Open-Label Safety and Efficacy" title and its 2016-era registration as a multi-cohort dose-expansion study]* — DOR was almost certainly analyzed via Kaplan-Meier methodology among confirmed responders only, censored at last evaluable tumor assessment for patients without a documented progression/death event, consistent with standard practice for this endpoint type across the census.
- *[inferred, from the retrospective assay-bridging description in label §14]* — The VENTANA MET (SP44) RxDx companion diagnostic assay was evaluated for concordance against the trial's prospective clinical-trial assay using a simple positive-percent-agreement calculation (32/37 = 87%) rather than a pre-specified formal bridging-study hypothesis test, consistent with how retrospective companion-diagnostic bridging analyses are typically reported when the CDx assay is developed after trial enrollment is underway.

### 187. Taletrectinib (Ibtrozi) — NDA 219713

**Sponsor:** Nuvation Bio Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adults with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) — approved under traditional/regular approval, not accelerated approval, based on durable objective response rate treated as direct clinical benefit (FDA's Multi-Discipline Review states plainly: "the submitted evidence meets the statutory evidentiary standard for traditional approval")

**Approval date:** June 11, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** Pooled analysis of TRUST-I (Study AB-106-C203), NCT04395677, and TRUST-II (Study AB-106-G208), NCT04919811

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Cross-trial pooled/integrated analysis (independently conducted, separately sponsored/protocoled trials) (TRUST-I, a China-only trial, pooled with TRUST-II, a global trial, into one Response-Evaluable Population); single-arm, open-label trial; biomarker-selected/enriched population (ROS1 gene fusion-positive), with separate TKI-naive and TKI-pretreated cohorts analyzed independently
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR, primary — confirmed response by independent review committee [IRC] per RECIST v1.1); duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival, intracranial ORR/DOR/PFS, time to intracranial progression (all secondary, IRC/RECIST v1.1 or mRECIST v1.1 for CNS)
- *Primary analysis:* Descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (point estimate + CI, no formal hypothesis test), using an exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval for the two-sided 95% CI around confirmed ORR; FDA explicitly declined to apply inferential hypothesis testing, stating time-to-event secondary endpoints (PFS, OS, TTiP) are "difficult to interpret in a single arm trial without the context of a comparator arm and are considered exploratory"
- *Missing data/bias:* Not applicable in the randomized-trial sense (no comparator/crossover); standard right-censoring for duration of response, PFS, and OS; FDA required a post-hoc SAP modification excluding 3 participants who started below the intended 600 mg QD dose from all efficacy analyses
- *Regulatory:* Regular approval grounded in durable-ORR-as-direct-clinical-benefit (single-arm trial) (FDA's rationale cites "the rarity of ROS1-positive NSCLC" as rendering "the conduct of a randomized trial challenging," paralleling the cemiplimab precedent in this census); no FDA advisory committee meeting held; FDA declined to present pooled TRUST-I/TRUST-II results in the product label itself, citing differing baseline demographics and follow-up durations between the two trials, even though the pooled analysis was the basis for approval

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Two independently conducted, separately protocoled single-arm, open-label, multicenter Phase 2 trials of taletrectinib (a ROS1 TKI) in ROS1-positive, locally advanced/metastatic NSCLC: TRUST-I (China only, N=173 enrolled) and TRUST-II (global, N=217 enrolled)
- Integrated efficacy was analyzed in a pooled Response-Evaluable Population (REP) split into two cohorts analyzed separately: ROS1 TKI-naive (N=157: 103 from TRUST-I + 54 from TRUST-II) and ROS1 TKI-pretreated (N=113: 66 from TRUST-I + 47 from TRUST-II)
- Primary endpoint: confirmed ORR (confirmed CR or PR) by IRC per RECIST v1.1 in the REP, with a two-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson CI; the SAP for this integrated summary of efficacy was finalized June 26, 2024, and — per FDA request after NDA submission — was amended to exclude 3 participants in TRUST-I who started below the intended 600 mg QD dose from all efficacy analyses
- Secondary endpoints: DOR, PFS, OS (all IRC/RECIST v1.1), and, in patients with baseline CNS metastases, intracranial ORR/DOR/PFS and time to intracranial progression (IRC/mRECIST v1.1); investigator-assessed ORR and a ≥14-month-follow-up sensitivity population served as supportive analyses
- Results (data cutoffs June 7, 2024 for ORR/DCR and October 28, 2024 for DOR/PFS/OS): TKI-naive cohort cORR 88.5% (95% CI 82.5-93.1), median DOR 43.3 months (95% CI 30.4-not reached); TKI-pretreated cohort cORR 55.8% (95% CI 46.1-65.1), median DOR 14.7 months (95% CI 10.6-24.9)
- FDA explicitly declined to present a single pooled-across-trials efficacy table in the approved label, instead presenting TRUST-I and TRUST-II results separately, because of differing baseline demographics and follow-up duration between the two trials — even though the integrated/pooled analysis was the evidentiary basis FDA's own review relied on for the approval decision
- A postmarketing requirement was issued for a dose/exposure-response optimization study (400 mg QD with standard meals vs. the approved 600 mg QD fasted regimen), following an exposure-response analysis showing flat efficacy but a positive exposure-toxicity trend for Grade ≥3 adverse events at 600 mg

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2025/219713Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/219713s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 5606238; Statistical Reviewer Shabnam Ford, Statistical Team Leader Flora Mulkey, Clinical Reviewer Ha Nguyen) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219713Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov records — TRUST-I: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04395677; TRUST-II: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04919811 (neither has a protocol/SAP posted in the Documents tab; confirmed via the API's absence of a `documentSection` for both records)
- Pivotal publication (pooled/integrated analysis matching the approval-supporting data): Pérol M, Li W, Pennell NA, et al. "Taletrectinib in ROS1+ Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: TRUST." *J Clin Oncol.* 2025;43(16):1920-1929. - Companion single-trial publication (TRUST-I only): Li W, Xiong A, Yang N, et al. "Efficacy and Safety of Taletrectinib in Chinese Patients With ROS1+ Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: The Phase II TRUST-I Study." *J Clin Oncol.* 2024;42(22):2660-2670. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.24.00731), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38822758/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Efficacy%20and%20Safety%20of%20Taletrectinib%20in%20Chinese%20Patients%20With%20ROS1%2B%20Non-Small%20Cell%20Lung%20Cancer%20TRUST-I)

**Other resources**

- Nuvation Bio's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for TRUST-I/TRUST-II; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held; FDA's review states no significant efficacy or safety issues were identified that required external input.
- Postmarketing requirement: a dosage-optimization trial comparing 400 mg QD (with standard meals) against the approved 600 mg QD (fasted) regimen, based on flat exposure-efficacy but a positive exposure-toxicity relationship for Grade ≥3 adverse events; a separate pediatric PMR was also agreed per PREA/iPSP (May 3, 2024).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 219713, Reference ID 5606238, §8.1.1]* — "The primary endpoint for the integrated efficacy analysis was ORR as assessed by IRC per RECIST v1.1 for the REP. The confirmed ORR (cORR) was determined as the proportion of participants with confirmed objective response (confirmed complete response [cCR] or confirmed partial response [cPR]) along with the two-sided 95% CI using the Clopper-Pearson method."

*[verbatim, same source, on inferential procedures]* — "FDA did not use inferential procedures to evaluate the results of these single arm trials. Instead, FDA relied on overall benefit-risk assessment... Analyses of time-to-event endpoints such as PFS, OS, TTiP are difficult to interpret in a single arm trial without the context of a comparator arm and are considered exploratory."

*[verbatim, same source, on the post-submission SAP amendment]* — "the integrated summary of efficacy (ISE) statistical analysis plan (SAP), finalized on 26 Jun 2024... Per FDA request, the analysis was modified after NDA submission to exclude 3 participants in Study C203 with a starting dose lower than 600 mg QD from all efficacy analyses."

*[verbatim, same source, on why results were not pooled in the label]* — "given the differences in baseline demographics and follow-up durations between Study C203 and Study G208... it is not considered appropriate to present pooled efficacy results in the product label."

*[verbatim, same source, approval rationale]* — "The magnitude and duration of responses observed with taletrectinib are considered to reflect clinically meaningful benefit... coupled with the rarity of ROS1-positive NSCLC, render the conduct of a randomized trial challenging."

*[verbatim, same source, regulatory action]* — "The submitted evidence meets the statutory evidentiary standard for traditional approval... Therefore, traditional approval is recommended for taletrectinib."

### 188. Linvoseltamab-gcpt (Lynozyfic) — BLA 761400

**Sponsor:** Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adults with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma who have received at least four prior lines of therapy, including a proteasome inhibitor, an immunomodulatory agent, and an anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody — approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate and duration of response

**Approval date:** July 2, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** LINKER-MM1 (Study R5458-ONC-1826), NCT03761108

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label, multi-cohort Phase 1/2 dose-escalation-into-expansion trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H; step-up priming-dose regimen prior to the full treatment dose, to mitigate cytokine release syndrome risk; FDA narrowing of a sponsor-proposed eligibility/line-of-therapy threshold (FDA restricted the approval-supporting efficacy population from the sponsor's pooled Phase 1+2, ≥3-prior-line population (n=117) down to a Phase-2-only, ≥4-prior-line population (n=80))
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR, primary — per IMWG criteria, adjudicated by an independent review committee [IRC]); duration of response, complete-response-or-better rate, time to response (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* Exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval for ORR; sponsor's SAP framed ORR as a formal one-sided hypothesis test (H0: ORR≤31% vs. Ha: 45%, one-sided alpha 0.025, 80% power, planned n=104/cohort) against a historical-reference benchmark, but FDA's review states this inferential framework was "not used to evaluate results," with the approval decision instead based on whether the 95% CI lower bound exceeded a clinically relevant response rate — i.e., descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (point estimate + CI, no formal hypothesis test) in practice, despite a formally-specified test in the SAP
- *Missing data/bias:* Not applicable in the randomized-trial sense (no comparator/crossover); standard right-censoring for duration of response
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval based on single-arm ORR/DoR, confirmatory trial required; FDA narrowing of a sponsor-proposed eligibility/line-of-therapy threshold; prior Complete Response Letter on manufacturing/CMC grounds only (original PDUFA date August 22, 2024), not efficacy or safety, ahead of a January 2025 resubmission and this July 2025 approval; no FDA advisory committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- LINKER-MM1 (R5458-ONC-1826): open-label, multicenter, multi-cohort Phase 1/2 trial of linvoseltamab, a BCMAxCD3 T-cell-engaging bispecific antibody, in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma; dosing used weekly step-up priming doses (5 mg Day 1, 25 mg Day 8) before the 200 mg full dose beginning Day 15, given weekly through Week 13, then every 2 weeks through Week 24, then every 4 weeks in patients maintaining a response of VGPR or better
- The sponsor's primary efficacy/safety analysis population pooled Phase 1 and Phase 2 patients treated at 200 mg with at least 3 prior lines of therapy (n=117); FDA instead restricted the approval-supporting efficacy population to the Phase 2 cohort only, with at least 4 prior lines of therapy (n=80) — narrower on line-of-therapy than the sponsor proposed
- Primary endpoint: ORR (partial response or better) per IMWG 2016 criteria, assessed by an independent review committee, in the FDA-defined efficacy population; the SAP's stated hypothesis-testing framework (H0: ORR≤31% vs. Ha: true ORR 45%, one-sided alpha 0.025, ~80% power, target n=104/cohort) was not what FDA ultimately relied on to reach its efficacy conclusion
- Secondary endpoints: duration of response (Kaplan-Meier), complete-response-or-better rate, time to response; all proportions reported with Clopper-Pearson exact 95% CIs
- Results (label, primary data cutoff): confirmed ORR 70% (95% CI 59-80) in the n=80 population, complete-response-or-better rate 45%, median time to response 0.95 months; response-duration rate 89% (95% CI 77-95) at 9 months and 72% (95% CI 54-84) at 12 months; at an updated data cutoff (July 23, 2024, 21.7 months median follow-up, submitted during the resubmission cycle) median DOR was 21.0 months (95% CI 19.0-not evaluable)
- SAP amendment history documented by FDA spans an original version (January 2021) through a 4th version (March 2023) across 9 protocol amendments, reflecting substantial mid-trial evolution of the dosing regimen and analysis populations over the trial's conduct

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2025/761400Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/761400s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (posted under the `nda/2025/` path despite this being a BLA; Reference ID 5432800 for the original review cycle, plus a Reference ID 5617927 resubmission addendum) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/761400Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (LINKER-MM1) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03761108 (no protocol/SAP posted in the Documents tab; confirmed via the API's empty `documentSection`)
- Pivotal publication: Bumma N, Richter J, Jagannath S, et al. "Linvoseltamab for Treatment of Relapsed/Refractory Multiple Myeloma." *J Clin Oncol.* 2024;42(22):2702-2712. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.24.01008), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38879802/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Linvoseltamab%20for%20Treatment%20of%20Relapsed%2FRefractory%20Multiple%20Myeloma)

**Other resources**

- Regeneron's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for LINKER-MM1; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for this trial.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this approval.
- Regulatory history: the original BLA had a PDUFA goal date of August 22, 2024, and FDA's recommended action at that cycle was a Complete Response, explicitly for manufacturing/CMC reasons rather than efficacy or safety; the sponsor resubmitted in January 2025, leading to this July 2, 2025 approval.
- Postmarketing requirement (PMR 4848-1): a randomized confirmatory trial, LINKER-MM3 (Study R5458-ONC-2245), NCT05730036, comparing linvoseltamab to elotuzumab + pomalidomide + dexamethasone in CD38-exposed multiple myeloma patients, with PFS as the primary endpoint and ORR/OS as key secondary endpoints; per FDA's review the trial was fully enrolled as of April 1, 2025, with a PFS readout projected for approximately Q2 2026 and trial completion/final report due December 2026/June 2027.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761400, original review cycle, Reference ID 5432800, on the Complete Response decision]* — "linvoseltamab has a favorable benefit-risk balance... Given the manufacturing issues, described further in the OPQ Executive Summary, which must be resolved prior to approval... the Agency's recommended regulatory action... is a Complete Response."

*[verbatim, FDA Approval Letter, BLA 761400, Advisory Committee]* — "was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant public health questions..."

No sponsor SAP or protocol document is posted on ClinicalTrials.gov for NCT03761108; the statistical detail above (efficacy-population narrowing, the SAP's originally-specified hypothesis-testing framework, and FDA's explicit statement that this framework was not what it used to reach its efficacy conclusion) is drawn from FDA's own description of the sponsor's SAP within the Multi-Discipline Review, not from a directly quoted sponsor SAP passage — treat these as FDA-review-sourced facts rather than first-party verbatim SAP text.

### 189. Sunvozertinib (Zegfrovy) — NDA 219839

**Sponsor:** Dizal Pharmaceutical (Jiangsu) Co., Ltd.

**Indication approved:** Adults with locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations, as detected by an FDA-approved test, whose disease has progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy — approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate and duration of response, at a 200 mg once-daily dose

**Approval date:** July 2, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** WU-KONG1B (Part B of the WU-KONG1 Phase 1/2 trial), NCT03974022

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label, multi-cohort Phase 1/2 trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H; randomized non-comparative dose-regimen cohort design (WU-KONG1B Part B randomized patients 1:1 to 200 mg QD vs. 300 mg QD, a within-trial dose-optimization comparison under FDA's Project Optimus initiative, not a between-arm efficacy comparison); biomarker-selected/enriched population (EGFR exon 20 insertion mutation-positive)
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR, primary — confirmed response by independent review committee [IRC] per RECIST v1.1); duration of response (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* Sponsor's primary analysis used a one-sided exact test against a pre-specified performance goal (H0: ORR≤25%, referencing a Simon's-two-stage-style historical benchmark) with a 97.5% CI computed via Jung's method, and approved the lower 200 mg dose on that basis
- *Missing data/bias:* Not applicable in the randomized-trial sense (no comparator/crossover); standard right-censoring for duration of response
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval based on single-arm ORR/DoR, confirmatory trial required; FDA-directed dose down-selection under Project Optimus, approving a lower dose (200 mg) than the sponsor's proposed to-be-marketed dose (300 mg) "due to comparable efficacy results and reduced toxicity"; companion diagnostic (Oncomine Dx Express Test, PMA P240040) co-approved; no FDA advisory committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- WU-KONG1B: the Phase 2 dose-optimization/expansion part (Part B) of the open-label, multicenter, multi-cohort WU-KONG1 Phase 1/2 trial of sunvozertinib (an EGFR/HER2 exon 20 insertion-selective TKI) in previously treated, platinum-pretreated, EGFR exon 20 insertion-positive locally advanced/metastatic NSCLC; patients were randomized 1:1 between 200 mg QD and 300 mg QD, reflecting FDA's Project Optimus dose-selection guidance rather than a comparative efficacy design
- Primary endpoint: confirmed ORR by IRC per RECIST v1.1; the sponsor's primary efficacy analysis pooled all patients treated at 300 mg (N=107, including patients from outside the randomized comparison), reporting cORR 45.8% (97.5% CI 34.8-56.1, Jung's method) with a one-sided p<0.0001 against a 25% historical-benchmark null
- Following a May 2, 2025 FDA Information Request, the sponsor produced a 200 mg-only analysis (N=85): cORR 45.9% (95% CI 35.0-57.0, Clopper-Pearson) — essentially identical efficacy to the 300 mg pooled result — and FDA approved sunvozertinib at 200 mg QD, the lower of the two randomized doses, citing comparable efficacy and a better toxicity profile
- Approved label (Table 6, N=85, 200 mg QD): ORR 46% (95% CI 35-57, Clopper-Pearson); median DOR 11.1 months (95% CI 8.2-not evaluable, Kaplan-Meier)
- Secondary endpoints included DOR, PFS, and intracranial response in patients with baseline CNS metastases, reported descriptively
- A companion diagnostic, the Oncomine Dx Express Test (PMA P240040), was approved contemporaneously to identify EGFR exon 20 insertion-positive patients

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO-25-00788), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40923280/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Phase%20II%20Dose-Randomized%20Study%20of%20Sunvozertinib%20in%20Platinum-Pretreated%20Non-Small%20Cell%20Lung%20Cancer%20With%20Epidermal%20Growth%20Factor%20Receptor%20Exon%2020%20Insertion%20Mutations)

The sponsor's "300 mg-all" primary-analysis figures (cORR 45.8%, 97.5% CI 34.8-56.1 via Jung's method, one-sided p<0.0001 against a 25% null) and the FDA-requested 200 mg-only figures (cORR 45.9%, 95% CI 35.0-57.0, Clopper-Pearson) are drawn from FDA's Multi-Discipline Review's description/tabulation of the sponsor's analysis (§8.1.1.1, Reference ID 5618719) rather than from a directly quoted sponsor SAP passage — no sponsor SAP or protocol document is posted on ClinicalTrials.gov for NCT03974022, so these figures should be treated as FDA-review-sourced facts, not first-party verbatim SAP text.

### 190. Dordaviprone (Modeyso) — NDA 219876

**Sponsor:** Chimerix, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adults and pediatric patients 1 year of age and older with H3 K27M-mutant diffuse midline glioma, progressive disease following prior therapy — approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate and duration of response

**Approval date:** August 6, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** Pooled integrated efficacy population across 5 single-arm studies — ONC006 (NCT02525692), ONC013 (NCT03295396), ONC014 (NCT03416530), ONC016 (NCT05392374), and ONC018 (NCT03134131)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Cross-trial pooled/integrated analysis (independently conducted, separately sponsored/protocoled trials) (5 separately conducted, open-label, non-randomized studies of dordaviprone/ONC201 pooled into one integrated efficacy population); single-arm, open-label trial; biomarker-selected/enriched population (H3 K27M mutation, progressive disease post-radiation)
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR, primary — BICR-assessed per RANO-HGG, including complete response, partial response, and minor response categories); duration of response (secondary); overall survival tracked as an exploratory landmark analysis, not a formal endpoint
- *Primary analysis:* Exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval for ORR on the integrated efficacy population (N=50); sponsor's sample-size justification was framed around excluding a lower 95% CI bound below 10% given an assumed observed ORR of 20%, which FDA's review states it "did not agree" was an adequate justification
- *Missing data/bias:* Not applicable in the randomized-trial sense (no comparator/crossover); standard right-censoring for duration of response and overall survival; exploratory landmark ORR-vs-OS analyses (log-rank test, Cox model) were characterized by FDA as "difficult to interpret in the absence of randomization"
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval based on single-arm ORR/DoR, confirmatory trial required; no FDA advisory committee meeting held; this was the first NDA ever submitted for dordaviprone, reviewed in a single cycle with no Complete Response Letter

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Efficacy was evaluated across 5 completed, open-label, non-randomized, single-arm studies of dordaviprone (ONC201/TIC10, a small-molecule imipridone) in H3 K27M-mutant diffuse midline glioma: ONC006, ONC013, ONC014, ONC016, and ONC018; FDA pooled patients across these studies who met pre-specified eligibility criteria (progressive, measurable disease per RANO-HGG; at least 90 days post-radiation; adequate radiation washout; KPS/LPS ≥60; stable or decreasing corticosteroid dose) into a single integrated efficacy population of N=50
- Primary endpoint: BICR-assessed ORR per RANO-HGG/RANO 2.0 criteria in the integrated efficacy population, including complete response, partial response, and a "minor response" category (a lesser degree of tumor shrinkage not meeting standard partial-response criteria, atypical relative to conventional RECIST-based solid-tumor response criteria used elsewhere in this census)
- Sponsor's planned sample size (50 patients) was justified as sufficient to exclude a lower 95% CI bound below 10%, assuming a 20% observed ORR; FDA's review explicitly states it did not agree this justification was adequate, and that at a May 12, 2020 meeting FDA "would not commit to a specific response rate or lower bound" in advance
- Secondary endpoint: duration of response, by Kaplan-Meier estimation with censoring at the earlier of last disease assessment or initiation of other anticancer therapy (per the ONC006/ONC013 SAPs); overall survival was analyzed only as an exploratory landmark analysis (log-rank test, Cox model) relating early response status to later survival, which FDA characterized as difficult to interpret without a randomized comparator
- Results: BICR-assessed ORR 22% (95% CI 12-36; 16% partial response, 6% minor response) in the N=50 integrated efficacy population; median duration of response 10.3 months (95% CI 7.3-15.2), with 73% of responses lasting ≥6 months and 27% lasting ≥12 months
- Broader, supportive (non-primary) analyses were also reported: an investigator-assessed population of 93 patients (of 220 total enrolled across the pooled studies) and a separate newly-diagnosed-population analysis (N=75, investigator-assessed RANO-HGG), both descriptive only and not part of the primary accelerated-approval claim

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2025/219876Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/219876s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 5638121) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219876Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov records — ONC006: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02525692; ONC013: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03295396 (both have a genuine Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan posted in the Documents tab; ONC014/ONC016/ONC018 do not)
- Protocol / SAP — ONC006 SAP: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/92/NCT02525692/SAP_001.pdf; ONC013 SAP: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/96/NCT03295396/SAP_001.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Arrillaga-Romany I, Gardner SL, Odia Y, et al. "ONC201 (Dordaviprone) in Recurrent H3 K27M-Mutant Diffuse Midline Glioma." *J Clin Oncol.* 2024;42(13):1542-1552. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.23.01134), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38335473/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=ONC201%20Dordaviprone%20in%20Recurrent%20H3%20K27M-Mutant%20Diffuse%20Midline%20Glioma)

**Other resources**

- Chimerix's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for the ONC006/ONC013/ONC014/ONC016/ONC018 studies; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held; FDA's review states no significant efficacy or safety issues were identified requiring external input. This was the first NDA submitted for dordaviprone (submitted December 18, 2024; Late-Cycle Meeting July 8, 2025), reviewed and approved in a single cycle with no Complete Response Letter.
- Postmarketing requirements: PMR 4861-1 is the ACTION trial (Study ONC201-108), NCT05580562, a randomized, multiregional Phase 3 trial in newly diagnosed H3 K27M-mutant diffuse glioma with overall survival as the primary endpoint; as of FDA's review it was ongoing, actively recruiting, with only early blinded safety data available and no efficacy readout yet — 292 patients enrolled (including 46 pediatric) as of the July 8, 2025 Late-Cycle Meeting, with an estimated completion date of January 2031 and final report due July 2031. PMR 4861-2 is a separate pediatric confirmatory trial (a draft protocol was due to FDA by March 2026). Note for the record: as of this research pass, ACTION has not yet reported efficacy results (it has neither succeeded nor failed); any characterization of ACTION as a completed or failed trial would be inaccurate as of the approval date.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, ONC006 (NCT02525692) Statistical Analysis Plan, posted on ClinicalTrials.gov]* — defines the All Treated Analysis Set and specifies RANO-based investigator-assessed efficacy analyses (ORR, best overall response, disease control rate, duration of response, PFS, OS); the censoring rule for time-to-event analyses is "censored at the earlier of: (1) last disease assessment or (2) initiation of other anticancer therapy," with no imputation for missing data other than for partial dates.

*[verbatim, ONC013 (NCT03295396) Statistical Analysis Plan, posted on ClinicalTrials.gov]* — follows the same sponsor SAP template and analysis-population/censoring conventions as the ONC006 SAP above (both signed by the same Chimerix VP of Biostatistics).

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 219876, Reference ID 5638121, on the sponsor's sample-size justification]* — the sponsor's "planned sample size for the primary efficacy analysis was 50, which would exclude a lower 95% CI boundary of <10% with an observed 20% response rate by RANO"; FDA "did not agree that a sample size justification based on 50 patients and a target ORR of 20%... would be sufficient," and at a May 12, 2020 meeting "would not commit to a specific response rate or lower bound."

*[verbatim, same source, on the exploratory OS analysis]* — landmark ORR-vs-OS analyses (log-rank test, Cox model) were "difficult to interpret in the absence of randomization."

*[verbatim, same source, Advisory Committee]* — "FDA did not refer this application to an advisory committee as no significant efficacy or safety issues were identified."

*[verbatim, same source, on trial history]* — "This is the first time a New Drug Application... has been submitted for dordaviprone."

### 191. Zongertinib (Hernexeos) — NDA 219042

**Sponsor:** Boehringer Ingelheim Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adults with unresectable or metastatic non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) whose tumors have activating HER2 (ERBB2) tyrosine kinase domain mutations, as detected by an FDA-approved test, and who have received a prior systemic therapy — approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate and duration of response, at a 120 mg once-daily dose

**Approval date:** August 8, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** Beamion LUNG-1 (Study 1479-0001), NCT04886804

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label, multicenter Phase Ia/Ib trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H; adaptive seamless dose-selection-into-expansion design (Cohort 1 underwent an internal randomized 1:1 dose comparison, 120 mg QD vs. 240 mg QD, stratified by mutation status, before 120 mg QD was selected as the recommended dose for the single-arm expansion); biomarker-selected/enriched population (activating HER2 tyrosine kinase domain mutations); FDA-conducted independent regrouping/reclassification of the efficacy analysis population
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR, primary — confirmed response by blinded independent central review [BICR] per RECIST v1.1); duration of response (DOR) and CNS response per RANO-BM (secondary); PFS and OS were tracked but FDA states these "are not interpretable for efficacy evaluation in a single arm study due to a lack of comparator and are considered exploratory only"; FDA explicitly rejected disease control rate (DCR) as an acceptable regulatory efficacy endpoint
- *Primary analysis:* One-sample z-test against a pre-specified performance goal, tested separately by dose (120 mg and 240 mg QD each against a 30% ORR benchmark, one-sided alpha 0.0125 per dose) within a fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing; the trial's later follow-up analysis of Cohort 1 was purely descriptive, reporting a point estimate with a Wilson-method confidence interval rather than re-testing; FDA's review states plainly that "in a single arm trial, no inferential procedures would be used to evaluate the trial results," basing its efficacy decision instead on whether the 95% CI lower bound excluded a clinically relevant response rate, combined with duration of response and overall benefit-risk
- *Missing data/bias:* Not applicable in the randomized-trial sense (no comparator/crossover); standard right-censoring for duration of response
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval based on single-arm ORR/DoR, confirmatory trial required; FDA-conducted independent regrouping/reclassification of the efficacy analysis population; no FDA advisory committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Beamion LUNG-1 (Study 1479-0001): open-label, multicenter, multiple-expansion-cohort Phase Ia (dose escalation) / Ib (dose expansion) trial of zongertinib, an HER2-selective, irreversible oral TKI, in HER2-altered advanced solid tumors, with Cohort 1 (HER2 tyrosine kinase domain mutation-positive, non-squamous NSCLC, ≥1 prior platinum-based chemotherapy line) as the approval-supporting cohort
- Cohort 1 underwent an internal randomized 1:1 dose-optimization comparison (120 mg QD vs. 240 mg QD, stratified by mutation status) before 120 mg QD was selected as the recommended dose carried into further single-arm expansion; the protocol underwent 4 global amendments, with Amendment 2 (August 2022) adding Cohorts 2-3, raising the planned Phase Ib sample size to 200 (266 overall), broadening eligibility beyond exon 20 to all activating HER2 mutations, and introducing the randomized dose-optimization design
- FDA "regrouped" the Applicant's Cohort 1 and Cohort 5 populations into its own "FDA Cohort 1"/"FDA Cohort 5," citing heterogeneity in the sponsor's original groupings by prior lines of therapy/eligibility criteria
- Primary endpoint: confirmed ORR per RECIST v1.1 by BICR; the pre-specified statistical analysis plan tested each dose separately against a 30% ORR benchmark (one-sample z-test, one-sided alpha 0.0125 per dose) within a 2-step hierarchical framework (all treated Cohort 1 patients, then the HER2 exon 20 mutation subset); a supportive Cohort 5 (patients previously treated with an HER2-directed antibody-drug conjugate) used the same 2-step framework at 120 mg QD only, against a 25% benchmark, one-sided alpha 0.025
- Sample size/timing: the primary analysis of Cohort 1 was timed at approximately 70 patients treated at 120 mg QD who had either completed 2 post-baseline tumor assessments or reached an earlier competing event, "to ensure that the majority of the responders in Cohort 1 had a chance to reach the 6 months follow-up after the onset of response"
- Secondary endpoints: DOR (BICR), CNS response per RANO-BM in patients with baseline brain metastases; PFS/OS collected but explicitly deemed exploratory-only by FDA given the absence of a comparator arm; FDA also explicitly declined to accept DCR as a valid regulatory efficacy endpoint
- Results (FDA's re-derived "FDA Cohort 1," N=71, BICR-assessed): ORR 75% (95% CI 63-83, Wilson method), 6% CR, 69% PR; among 53 responders, DOR ranged from 1.3+ to 15+ months, with 58% of responses lasting ≥6 months (median DOR reported elsewhere as 14.1 months, 95% CI 6.9-not evaluable); in the prior-HER2-ADC-treated "FDA Cohort 5," ORR was 44% (95% CI 29-61)

### 192. Pembrolizumab and berahyaluronidase alfa-pmph (Keytruda Qlex) — BLA 761467

**Sponsor:** Merck Sharp & Dohme LLC

**Indication approved:** A subcutaneous co-formulation of pembrolizumab (with the hyaluronidase berahyaluronidase alfa to enable subcutaneous delivery) approved across a broad subset of pembrolizumab's existing intravenous solid-tumor indications (not confirmed exhaustive against the full current IV Keytruda label) — approved on the basis of a pharmacokinetic non-inferiority bridge to intravenous pembrolizumab, with efficacy across tumor types extrapolated from IV pembrolizumab's already-established efficacy rather than demonstrated fresh in this trial

**Approval date:** September 19, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** Study MK-3475A-D77 (3475A-D77), NCT05722015

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized (2:1), open-label, active-controlled, parallel-group PK-noninferiority bridging trial, and geographic region; co-primary endpoints (dual PK non-inferiority endpoints, each independently required)
- *Endpoints:* Cycle 1 AUC0-6wks and steady-state (Cycle 3) Ctrough (co-primary pharmacokinetic exposure endpoints, non-inferiority framing); objective response rate, progression-free survival, and overall survival tracked as additional descriptive efficacy outcome measures, not formally tested for non-inferiority
- *Primary analysis:* PK/exposure-equivalence bridging study (crossover, not a fresh efficacy RCT) — geometric mean ratio (GMR) of MK-3475A SC vs. pembrolizumab IV for each PK parameter, tested against a pre-specified non-inferiority margin of 0.8, using Welch's t-test-based confidence intervals on the log-transformed PK parameters; ORR was assessed only descriptively/supportively via the FDA 2016 synthesis method for non-inferiority (not a formal co-primary or key-secondary test)
- *Multiplicity:* Graphical alpha-propagation (Maurer-Bretz method), with alpha reallocated to the other hypothesis if either is rejected
- *Missing data/bias:* Not applicable in the crossover-adjustment sense; standard right-censoring for PFS/OS; no crossover between study arms was permitted
- *Regulatory:* PK/exposure-equivalence bridging study (crossover, not a fresh efficacy RCT) used as the regulatory basis; efficacy across pembrolizumab's numerous approved tumor types was extrapolated from IV pembrolizumab's own separately-established pivotal trials rather than demonstrated fresh in this bridging trial; no FDA advisory committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- MK-3475A-D77 (3475A-D77): Phase 3, randomized 2:1, open-label, active-controlled trial in treatment-naive metastatic NSCLC (excluding EGFR/ALK/ROS1-altered tumors), comparing MK-3475A (pembrolizumab coformulated with berahyaluronidase alfa, given subcutaneously) against intravenous pembrolizumab, both in combination with platinum-doublet chemotherapy, dosed Q6W for up to 18 cycles; 377 participants randomized (SC arm n=251, IV arm n=126); randomization stratified by ECOG performance status (0 vs. 1), histology (squamous vs. non-squamous), PD-L1 TPS (<50% vs. ≥50%), and region (East Asia vs. North America/Western Europe/Australia/New Zealand vs. rest of world); no crossover between arms was permitted
- Dual primary objectives: compare Cycle 1 AUC0-6wks and steady-state (Cycle 3) Ctrough between MK-3475A SC and pembrolizumab IV, each evaluated for non-inferiority against a pre-specified GMR margin of 0.8; the protocol's rationale states Cycle 1 AUC0-6wks is "the most conservative PK value to ensure noninferiority of SC exposure relative to IV," while Cycle 3 Ctrough reflects steady-state target (PD-1) saturation, such that demonstrating non-inferiority on both supports the inference that "efficacy similar to pembrolizumab IV dosing will be maintained"
- Multiplicity: an overall one-sided alpha of 0.05 was split via the graphical Maurer-Bretz method into 0.02 (Cycle 1 AUC0-6wks) and 0.03 (Cycle 3 Ctrough), with alpha reallocated to the untested hypothesis if the other's null (GMR≤0.8) was rejected; each hypothesis was tested only once
- ORR was designated a secondary endpoint and was not formally tested for non-inferiority; the protocol nonetheless pre-specified a supportive power calculation (~89% power to reject a synthesis-method non-inferiority null, at an overall one-sided alpha of 0.025, assuming a true ORR of 51.1% in both arms) referencing the FDA's 2016 synthesis-method guidance for non-inferiority trials, anchored to historical KEYNOTE-189/KEYNOTE-407 pembrolizumab-plus-chemotherapy data
- Results: GMR for Cycle 1 AUC0-6wks was 1.14 (96% CI 1.06-1.22) and GMR for Cycle 3 Ctrough was 1.67 (94% CI 1.52-1.84), both clearing the pre-specified 0.8 non-inferiority margin (i.e., SC exposure was non-inferior to, and numerically higher than, IV exposure); confirmed ORR by BICR was 45% (SC) vs. 42% (IV), with no notable differences observed in PFS or OS between arms
- Efficacy across pembrolizumab's many approved solid-tumor indications was not independently re-established in this trial; the label extrapolates efficacy from IV pembrolizumab's own extensive pivotal-trial program, supported by this trial's PK/safety/limited-efficacy bridging data in first-line metastatic NSCLC

- Indication scope: the approved Qlex label carries a broad subset of pembrolizumab IV's approved solid-tumor indications; whether it is a fully exhaustive match to the current IV Keytruda label (which continues to accumulate new indications) was not independently confirmed in this research pass.

Noninferiority will be evaluated with the noninferiority margin of 0.8."

If the hypothesis for Cycle 1 AUC0-6 wks is rejected, the corresponding alpha can be reallocated to Cycle 3 Ctrough. *[verbatim, same source, §4.2]* — "Participants are not permitted to crossover to the other study intervention arm."

*[verbatim, Package Insert, §14 Clinical Studies]* — Cycle 1 AUC0-6wks GMR 1.14 (96% CI: 1.06, 1.22); Cycle 3 Ctrough GMR 1.67 (94% CI: 1.52, 1.84); confirmed ORR by BICR 45% (SC) vs. 42% (IV); no notable differences in PFS or OS between arms.

### 193. Imlunestrant (Inluriyo) — NDA 218881

**Sponsor:** Eli Lilly and Company

**Indication approved:** Adults with estrogen receptor (ER)-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer with an ESR1 mutation, as detected by an FDA-approved test, with disease progression on or after an aromatase inhibitor, with or without a prior CDK4/6 inhibitor — approved under regular approval based on a statistically significant improvement in progression-free survival

**Approval date:** September 25, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** EMBER-3 (Study J2J-OX-JZLC), NCT04975308

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized (1:1:1), open-label, active-controlled, 3-arm Phase 3 trial — Arm A (imlunestrant monotherapy), Arm B (investigator's choice endocrine therapy: fulvestrant or exemestane), and Arm C (imlunestrant plus abemaciclib, added by protocol amendment and explicitly out of scope for this NDA's review); co-primary endpoints (investigator-assessed PFS tested as co-primary in both the ITT population and the ESR1-mutation-detected subgroup); biomarker-selected key subgroup defined by the Guardant360 CDx blood ctDNA assay, limited to specific ESR1 ligand-binding-domain mutations; mid-trial SAP amendment changing endpoint status/SAP Version 5, approved before unblinding, reallocated the initial alpha split between the ITT and ESR1m co-primary populations in response to newly available external competitor oral-SERD trial data)
- *Endpoints:* Progression-free survival (PFS, primary — investigator-assessed per RECIST v1.1, in both the ITT and ESR1m populations, with BIRC-assessed PFS as a consistent supportive analysis); overall survival (OS, key secondary, in ITT, ESR1m, and Arm C-vs-A populations, each gated behind its corresponding PFS hypothesis); objective response rate (secondary, measurable-disease subset)
- *Primary analysis:* Stratified log-rank test for PFS, stratified by prior CDK4/6 inhibitor use, visceral metastasis, and region for the ITT comparison (region excluded from the ESR1m-subset analysis to reduce strata from 12 to 4); Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified) for the hazard ratio and CI; graphical alpha-propagation (Maurer-Bretz method) (per Bretz et al. 2009 and Maurer & Bretz 2013) used to test 3 PFS primary hypotheses and 3 OS key-secondary hypotheses within a single overall 1-sided family-wise alpha of 0.025
- *Multiplicity:* The graphical approach initially allocated alpha 0.005 (1-sided) to H1 (PFS, Arm A vs. B, ITT) and 0.02 (1-sided) to H2 (PFS, Arm A vs. B, ESR1m), with H3 (PFS, Arm C vs. A, ITT) and the three OS key-secondary hypotheses (H4-H6) initially assigned zero alpha; local significance levels were re-allocated to not-yet-rejected hypotheses via a pre-specified algorithm each time a hypothesis was rejected (e.g., H1 could be re-tested at up to alpha 0.019-0.0249989 depending on which other hypotheses were rejected first); cohort-level Bonferroni alpha allocation across independently tested biomarker cohorts
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Group-sequential design with a futility-only interim PFS analysis for the ITT comparison at ~192 events (40% information fraction); no interim analysis was planned for the ESR1m PFS comparison (final analysis only, at ~192 events), though FDA's review flags a discrepancy between its own and the sponsor's characterization of this specific interim-analysis description; Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function (O'Brien-Fleming type) governed a multi-look, event-driven OS interim/final analysis schedule (looks anchored to ITT PFS analysis timing, then further OS-event counts) for both the ITT and ESR1m OS comparisons
- *Missing data/bias:* Standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment; OS at the time of the primary PFS analysis was immature in the ESR1m population (31% of events observed), limiting interpretability of the key secondary endpoint at this data cut
- *Regulatory:* Regular approval (not accelerated) grounded in a statistically significant, clinically meaningful PFS improvement in the ESR1m population; the ITT PFS comparison "did not cross the prespecified significance alpha level" and was therefore not statistically significant, which in turn meant OS could not be formally tested in the ITT population under the graphical gating scheme; companion diagnostic (Guardant360 CDx) co-approved to identify ESR1m-positive patients; no FDA advisory committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- EMBER-3: Phase 3, randomized, open-label, active-controlled, multicenter trial of imlunestrant (an oral selective estrogen receptor degrader) enrolling 874 patients with ER-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer previously treated with an aromatase inhibitor (with or without a CDK4/6 inhibitor); patients were randomized 1:1:1 to imlunestrant monotherapy (Arm A), investigator's choice of endocrine therapy — fulvestrant or exemestane (Arm B, "TPC"), or imlunestrant plus abemaciclib (Arm C, added mid-trial by protocol amendment and not part of this NDA's efficacy review); randomization was stratified by prior CDK4/6 inhibitor use (yes/no), visceral metastasis (yes/no), and region
- ESR1-mutation status (limited to specific mutations in the estrogen receptor ligand-binding domain) was determined from blood circulating tumor DNA using the Guardant360 CDx assay; of the 874 randomized patients, 323 were ESR1-mutation-detected, with 256 on the imlunestrant or TPC arms (138 imlunestrant, 118 TPC) forming the efficacy-evaluable ESR1m analysis population reported in the label
- Primary endpoint: investigator-assessed PFS per RECIST v1.1, formally tested in 3 pre-specified comparisons under one graphical multiplicity-control framework — (H1) Arm A vs. Arm B in the ITT population, (H2) Arm A vs. Arm B in the ESR1m-detected population, and (H3) Arm C vs. Arm A in the concurrent ITT population (not reviewed under this NDA); H3 could only be tested if at least one of H1/H2 was rejected
- Sample-size/power logic: for the ITT comparison, assuming a TPC-arm median PFS of 4.3 months (from an unpublished meta-analysis of historical controls) and a target hazard ratio of 0.74, 480 events gave at least 76% power at the (eventually allocated) 1-sided alpha of 0.005; for the ESR1m comparison, assuming a TPC-arm median PFS of 3.6 months and a target hazard ratio of 0.57, 192 events gave approximately 97% power at 1-sided alpha 0.02
- Key secondary endpoint: OS, tested in the same 3 populations (H4-H6), each gated to be tested only if its corresponding PFS hypothesis was rejected; OS was analyzed by Kaplan-Meier estimation and compared via a log-rank test stratified the same way as PFS, with the hazard ratio from a stratified Cox model
- Protocol/SAP history: the SAP underwent 5 versions between initial approval (July 26, 2021, before first patient visit) and Version 5 (approved August 24, 2023, filed to the IND before database lock/unblinding); Amendment (d)/SAP Version 5 changed the initial alpha allocation between the ITT and ESR1m PFS comparisons, giving relatively more alpha to the ESR1m comparison, explicitly based on newly available external data from other oral SERDs in breast cancer (i.e., competitor-trial results that became available during EMBER-3's conduct)
- Results: in the ESR1m population, median PFS was 5.5 months (imlunestrant) vs. 3.8 months (TPC), HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.46-0.82), 2-sided p=0.0008 (compared against a 2-sided significance threshold of 0.04, i.e., the allocated 1-sided alpha of 0.02 doubled); BIRC-assessed PFS was consistent with the investigator assessment; ORR among patients with measurable disease was 14.3% (95% CI 7.8-20.8) vs. 7.7% (95% CI 2.2-13.2); the ITT PFS comparison did not cross its prespecified significance threshold and was therefore not statistically significant, so OS could not be formally tested in the ITT population; OS in the ESR1m population was immature (31% of events) and not statistically significant at this analysis (HR 0.55, 95% CI 0.35-0.86, favoring imlunestrant with no detriment observed)

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/218881s000lbl.pdf (Reference ID 5665612)
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 5665313) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/218881Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf

**Other resources**

- Eli Lilly's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for EMBER-3; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for this trial.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held; the approval letter states the application "was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary; there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion."
- Postmarketing commitment (PMC 4902-1, per the approval letter and MDR): complete the pre-specified, event-driven OS analyses comparing the imlunestrant monotherapy and standard-of-care endocrine therapy arms from the ongoing EMBER-3 trial, to further characterize the clinical benefit of imlunestrant in the ESR1-mutated population; per the sponsor's schedule, interim report submission February 2026, trial completion (monotherapy in the ESR1m population) November 2026, final report submission May 2027. As a postmarketing commitment rather than a requirement, this reflects the regular-approval (not accelerated-approval) basis of this indication.
- Companion diagnostic: the Guardant360 CDx blood-based ctDNA assay was used to identify ESR1-mutation-positive patients eligible for this indication.
- This is the one randomized (not single-arm) pivotal trial among the ten submissions documented in this batch.

Initially, the overall 1-sided significance level of α = 0.025 will be split between H1 and H2, with H1 tested at the 1-sided significance level of α = 0.005, and H2 tested at the 1-sided significance level of α = 0.02. No significance level (α = 0) is initially assigned to H3, H4, H5 and H6."

*[verbatim, same source, on interim PFS monitoring]* — "For the primary objective of PFS for Arm A versus Arm B in the ITT population, one interim PFS analysis will be conducted when approximately 192 (40% information fraction) investigator-assessed events have been observed... *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 218881, Reference ID 5665313, §8.1.1, on the SAP amendment history]* — "The initial alpha allocation for the PFS primary endpoint analysis between Arms A and B for ITT and the ESR1 subgroup was changed with greater alpha assigned to the latter. This was based on new external data of oral SERDs in breast cancer" (Amendment (d), 31-Jul-2023, implemented in SAP Version 5, approved 24-Aug-2023, before database lock/unblinding).

*[verbatim, same source, on FDA's efficacy conclusion]* — "EMBER-3 demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in PFS by investigator assessment in the ESR1m population. Median PFS was 5.5 months versus 3.8 months (HR 0.62, 95% CI: 0.46-0.82; p-value 0.0008). The PFS endpoint in the ITT population did not cross the prespecified significance alpha level and therefore was not statistically significant... OS could not be tested in the ITT population since PFS in the overall population failed to meet the prespecified threshold."

### 194. Ziftomenib (Komzifti) — NDA 220305

**Sponsor:** Kura Oncology, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adults with relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with an NPM1 mutation who have no satisfactory alternative treatment options — approved under regular/traditional approval (not accelerated approval), grounded in substantial evidence of effectiveness from one adequate and well-controlled clinical investigation plus confirmatory evidence, at a 600 mg once-daily dose

**Approval date:** November 13, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** KOMET-001 (Study KO-MEN-001), NCT04067336

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label, multicenter, multi-cohort Phase 1/2 trial; biomarker-selected/enriched population (NPM1-mutated AML); regular approval based on one adequate/well-controlled trial plus confirmatory evidence (FDA's 2023 "Demonstrating Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness Based on One Adequate and Well-Controlled Clinical Investigation and Confirmatory Evidence" framework)
- *Endpoints:* Composite CR/CRh (complete remission + complete remission with partial hematologic recovery) rate; duration of CR/CRh, transfusion independence conversion rate (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* One-sided exact binomial test (single-arm ORR hypothesis test) — H0: CR/CRh rate ≤12% (drawn from historical relapsed/refractory NPM1-mutant AML control-arm data) vs. Ha: true rate higher, one-sided alpha 0.025, with a planned Phase 2 sample size of ≥85 patients estimated to give 89% power to exclude the null; exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval for the reported CR/CRh rate
- *Missing data/bias:* Standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment for duration of CR/CRh (Kaplan-Meier)
- *Regulatory:* Regular approval based on one adequate/well-controlled trial plus confirmatory evidence — explicitly not an accelerated approval, so no Subpart H confirmatory-trial requirement applies; reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan (FDA's independent re-adjudication of Phase 2 responses, using a marrow-sampling/CBC timing window the SAP had not pre-specified, caused the Phase 2-only CR/CRh rate to fall from the Applicant's reported 21.7% to an adjudicated 18.5%, whose 95% CI lower bound no longer excluded the 12% null — FDA then relied on an SAP-deviating pooled Phase 1b+Phase 2 population to sustain the efficacy claim); no FDA advisory committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- KOMET-001 (KO-MEN-001): open-label, multicenter, multi-cohort Phase 1/2 first-in-human trial of ziftomenib (a menin-KMT2A inhibitor, development code KO-539) in relapsed/refractory AML; the Phase 2 portion (single cohort, 600 mg QD continuous 28-day cycles, in NPM1-mutant relapsed/refractory AML) served as FDA's single adequate and well-controlled clinical investigation, with a Phase 1b dose-expansion cohort at the same dose (n=20) serving as confirmatory evidence, per FDA's 2023 "one adequate and well-controlled investigation plus confirmatory evidence" guidance rather than the accelerated-approval/Subpart H pathway used elsewhere in this batch
- Primary endpoint: composite CR/CRh rate, in the modified intent-to-treat (mITT) Phase 2 population as the primary analysis population, with an Efficacy Analysis Set (locally confirmed NPM1-mutant, 600 mg QD) and a Pooled Population (Phase 1b Efficacy Analysis Set plus Phase 2 mITT) as supportive analyses, and a Per-Protocol Set excluding major protocol deviations as an additional supportive population
- Sample-size/power logic: the Phase 2 sample size of at least 85 patients was chosen to provide adequate power to determine whether ziftomenib's CR/CRh rate exceeded a null hypothesis of 12% (derived from historical relapsed/refractory NPM1-mutant AML control-arm data judged by FDA to itself be an overestimate); at a one-sided alpha of 0.025, 85 patients gave 89% power to exclude that null; the primary analysis was timed to 168 days after the 85th patient was dosed (or each patient's earlier end-of-study), so that at least 85 patients would have approximately 6 treatment cycles (168 days) of follow-up
- Secondary endpoints: duration of CR/CRh (Kaplan-Meier), transfusion independence conversion rate
- Results (label, N=112 treated at 600 mg QD): CR/CRh rate 21.4% (95% CI 14.2-30.2; CR alone 17.0%, 95% CI 10.5-25.2; CRh alone 4.5%, 95% CI 1.5-10.1); median duration of CR/CRh 5.0 months (95% CI 1.9-8.1); median time to first response 2.7 months (range 0.9-15); FDA's Pooled Efficacy Cohort analysis reported a consistent CR/CRh rate of 21.4% (95% CI 14.2-30.2), with the Phase 2 subset alone at 18.5% (95% CI 11.1-27.9) and a transfusion-independence conversion rate of 21.2% (95% CI 12.1-33.0)
- Notable review nuance: in the Applicant's own Phase 2 analysis (n=92), CR/CRh was 21.7% (95% CI 13.8-31.6, p=0.0058), which excluded the 12% null; when FDA independently re-adjudicated the same Phase 2 responses — using a (-7, +14)-day marrow-sampling-to-CBC window the protocol/SAP had not pre-specified — the adjudicated Phase 2-only CR/CRh rate fell to 18.5% (95% CI 11.1-27.9), whose lower bound no longer excluded the 12% null; FDA's review states this "raises questions about the robustness of the results," and the ultimately approved label population instead relies on the FDA-pooled Phase 1b + Phase 2 cohort (21.4%, 95% CI 14.2-30.2), a pooling FDA itself notes "differed from what was specified in the SAP"

- Kura Oncology's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for KOMET-001; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for this trial.
- No FDA advisory committee (ODAC) meeting was held (verbatim quote below); this differs from revumenib, a comparator menin inhibitor that did receive ODAC scrutiny in the same drug class.
- Because this was a regular approval (not accelerated), no Subpart H post-marketing efficacy-confirmatory-trial requirement applies; the postmarketing requirements/commitments issued are PK/CMC/companion-diagnostic-focused: PMR 4929-5 (itraconazole drug-drug interaction study), PMR 4929-6 (BCRP inhibitor drug-drug interaction study), PMR 4929-7 (midazolam drug-drug interaction study), PMC 4929-8 (companion diagnostic development for NPM1 mutation detection), and PMC 4929-9 (in vitro activity study for non-A/B/D NPM1 mutation subtypes).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 220305, Reference ID 5694243, on the regulatory pathway]* — Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness (SEE) was established via "One adequate and well-controlled clinical investigation and confirmatory evidence," citing FDA's 2023 guidance "Demonstrating Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness Based on One Adequate and Well-Controlled Clinical Investigation and Confirmatory Evidence."

*[verbatim, same source, on sample-size justification]* — "The Phase 2 sample size of at least 85 patients was chosen to evaluate the safety profile further and secure adequate power to determine whether the CR/CRh rate of ziftomenib was greater than the null hypothesis of 0.12... With a 1-sided alpha of 0.025, a total of 85 NPM1-m patients provided 89% power to exclude the null hypothesis."

*[verbatim, same source, review team recommendation]* — "the review team recommend approval for ziftomenib for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory AML with an NPM1 mutation who have no satisfactory alternative treatment options."

*[verbatim, same source, on the post hoc re-adjudication crossing the null boundary]* — "The protocol and SAP did not specify a window between the marrow sampling and the CBC for remission assessment. This complicated the independent response adjudication based on the raw data. For the adjudication process, the FDA used a window of (-7, +14) days in addition to with clinical judgement. While the results submitted by the Applicant for the Phase 2 cohort excluded the benchmark rate of 12%, the adjudicated results of the Phase 2 cohort did not. This raises questions about the robustness of the results... Although the CR + CRh rate in the Phase 2 patients excluded the null hypothesis of 12% based on the Applicant's assessments, it did not based on the FDA's adjudication. The FDA also evaluated this in the Pooled Efficacy Cohort by pooling the Phase 1 patients given two phases had the same eligibility criteria and two phases of patients had similar baseline characteristic. This differed from what was specified in the SAP but provided a more comprehensive experience."

*[verbatim, same source, Advisory Committee]* — "This application was not discussed at an Advisory Committee meeting. The review of this drug did not raise significant safety issues that were unexpected for the class of drug or for the treatment of patients with R/R AML. In addition, the efficacy appears to be consistent among other drugs in this class."

No protocol/SAP document is posted on ClinicalTrials.gov for NCT04067336; the sample-size/estimand detail (referenced by FDA as living in the sponsor's "SAP Section 7.5.1") is drawn from FDA's Multi-Discipline Review's description of the sponsor's SAP, not from a directly quoted sponsor SAP passage.
