### 195. Sevabertinib (Hyrnuo) — NDA 219972

**Sponsor:** Bayer HealthCare Pharmaceuticals Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adults with locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) whose tumors have HER2 (ERBB2) tyrosine kinase domain (TKD) activating mutations, as detected by an FDA-approved test, who have received prior systemic therapy — approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate and duration of response, at a 20 mg twice-daily dose

**Approval date:** November 19, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** SOHO-01 (Study 21607), NCT05099172

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label, multicenter, multi-cohort Phase 1/2 trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H (21 CFR 315.510); biomarker-selected/enriched population (HER2 TKD activating mutations); two-group split by prior anti-HER2 exposure (Group D, primary — anti-HER2-therapy-naive; Group E, supportive — previously treated with an HER2-directed antibody-drug conjugate)
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR, primary — confirmed response by blinded independent central review [BICR] per RECIST v1.1); duration of response (secondary); PFS, OS, and time to response tracked by both BICR and investigator assessment as additional endpoints
- *Primary analysis:* Exact binomial test against a pre-specified performance goal — for Group D, a true ORR ≥50% was hypothesized, with ~70 patients (minimum 30 responders) estimated to give 90.6% power for the lower bound of a 2-sided 95% exact binomial CI to exceed 30%; for Group E, a true ORR ≥40% was hypothesized, with ~51 patients (minimum 17 responders) estimated to give 86.8% power for the lower bound to exceed 20%; exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval used for the reported ORR CIs
- *Missing data/bias:* Standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment for DOR/PFS/OS (Kaplan-Meier); partial missing dates for adverse events and time-to-event censoring/event dates were imputed per rules specified in the SAP
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval based on single-arm ORR/DoR, confirmatory trial required; the confirmatory trial (SOHO-02) was already underway and partially enrolled at the time of approval, which FDA's review explicitly ties to the Consolidated Appropriations Act (2023) authority requiring confirmatory studies to be underway prior to accelerated approval; no FDA advisory committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- SOHO-01 (Study 21607): open-label, single-arm, multicenter, multi-cohort trial of sevabertinib (an HER2-selective TKI, development code BAY 2927088) in previously treated, locally advanced/metastatic, non-squamous NSCLC with HER2 (ERBB2) activating mutations, determined by local laboratory testing prior to enrollment; patients received 20 mg orally twice daily until progression or unacceptable toxicity
- Primary efficacy endpoint: confirmed ORR by BICR per RECIST v1.1 (major efficacy outcome measure); duration of response was the additional major efficacy outcome measure; the FDA-defined primary efficacy population comprised 122 patients across Group D (n=70, naive to anti-HER2-directed therapy) and Group E (n=52, previously treated with an HER2-directed antibody-drug conjugate) — narrower than the sponsor's originally submitted analysis populations for these groups (81 and 55 treated participants, respectively, per an earlier data cut), reflecting FDA's use of an updated data cutoff and analysis-population definition
- Sample-size/power logic: for Group D, a hypothesized true ORR of ≥50% and an approximate sample size of 70 (minimum 30 responders) were estimated to give 90.6% power for the lower bound of a 2-sided 95% exact binomial CI to exceed a 30% performance-goal threshold; for Group E, a hypothesized true ORR of ≥40% and a sample size of 51 (minimum 17 responders) were estimated to give 86.8% power to exceed a 20% threshold; exact 2-sided 95% CIs for ORR were computed from the binomial distribution (Clopper-Pearson per the label footnote)
- No formal interim analyses were planned; futility was instead assessed independently within each expansion cohort once approximately 14-17 efficacy-evaluable participants had been observed, and Groups D and E were prioritized for the trial's Extension part based on those futility assessments; 2 primary analyses were planned, timed to each group's completion of the Extension part
- Secondary/other endpoints: DOR, PFS, OS, and time to response, all assessed by both BICR and investigator, using Kaplan-Meier methodology for time-to-event summaries; pre-specified exploratory subgroup analyses of ORR spanned demographics, ECOG PS, region, smoking status, histology, prior therapy exposures, brain metastases, and HER2 TKD mutation subtype
- Results: Group D (n=70) ORR 71% (95% CI 59-82; 2.9% CR, 69% PR), median DOR 9.2 months (95% CI 6.3-15.0), DOR ≥6 months in 54% and ≥12 months in 18% of responders; Group E (n=52) ORR 38% (95% CI 25-53; 6% CR, 33% PR), median DOR 7.0 months (95% CI 5.6-not evaluable), DOR ≥6 months in 60% and ≥12 months in 10% of responders
- A retrospective bridging analysis compared prospective local HER2 TKD testing against the Oncomine Dx Target Test (Life Technologies) in 82 of 122 (67.2%) samples across Groups D and E, finding 92.7% (76/82) concordant positivity, with the remainder unevaluable rather than discordant-negative

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/219972s000lblCorrected.pdf

**Other resources**

- Bayer's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for SOHO-01; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for this trial.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held (verbatim quote below).
- Postmarketing requirements: PMR 4933-1 is the confirmatory trial, Study SOHO-02, an open-label, randomized, controlled global trial of sevabertinib versus pembrolizumab plus platinum-doublet chemotherapy in previously untreated, HER2 TKD-mutant, non-squamous NSCLC, with PFS by BICR as the primary endpoint and ORR/OS as key secondary endpoints; per FDA's review, SOHO-02 was 60% enrolled as of October 2025, with topline PFS data expected Q1 2027, and the review division "considers the confirmatory trial for this accelerated approval to be underway" (citing the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 authority to require confirmatory studies underway prior to accelerated approval). PMR 4933-2 is a hepatic-impairment PK trial; PMR 4933-3 is a clinical drug-interaction study.
- For cross-reference within this census: sevabertinib is now one of two single-arm-accelerated-approval HER2-mutant-NSCLC TKIs approved in 2025 alongside zongertinib (Hernexeos, approved August 8, 2025); FDA's SOHO-01 review explicitly benchmarks sevabertinib's Group D ORR against the HER2-directed ADC fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki's reported 58% ORR "in a population similar to the Group D efficacy analysis population," rather than against zongertinib specifically.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 219972, Reference ID 5697816, §8.1.1, on Group D/E sample size]* — "For Group D, a true ORR of ≥ 50% was hypothesized. An approximate sample size of 70 participants including participants from Dose Expansion and Dose Extension, with a minimum of 30 responders, was estimated to provide 90.6% power to achieve a lower bound of a 2-sided 95% exact binomial CI for the estimated ORR that exceeds 30%. For Group E, a true ORR of ≥ 40% was hypothesized. An approximate sample size of 51 participants... was estimated to provide 86.8% power to achieve a lower bound of a 2-sided 95% exact binomial CI for the estimated ORR that exceeds 20%."

*[verbatim, same source, on the primary analysis method]* — "The ORR was assessed by both BICR (primary efficacy endpoint) and by the investigator (secondary efficacy endpoint). The exact 2-sided 95% CIs for the ORR were calculated based on binomial distribution... The secondary efficacy endpoints, DOR and PFS by investigator assessment and BICR, and OS were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier methods."

*[verbatim, same source, on interim futility monitoring]* — "During the Dose Expansion and Dose Extension parts, no formal interim analyses of the data were planned, and futility was to be assessed independently for each Expansion cohort when approximately 14-17 participants evaluable for efficacy were observed. Based on futility assessments in the Expansion part, Groups D and E were prioritized in the Extension part."

*[verbatim, same source, on the confirmatory trial timing requirement]* — "The Consolidated Appropriations Act (2023) provides FDA with the authority to require that confirmatory studies to verify clinical benefit be underway prior to accelerated approval. SOHO-02 is 60% enrolled as of October 2025, and topline data from the primary PFS analysis are expected Q1 2027. As such, the review division considers the confirmatory trial for this accelerated approval to be underway."

*[verbatim, FDA Approval Letter, NDA 219972, Advisory Committee]* — "Your application for Hyrnuo (sevabertinib) was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because no significant efficacy or safety issues were identified during the review that required external input and the application did not raise significant public health questions regarding the role of sevabertinib for the proposed indication."

No protocol/SAP document is posted on ClinicalTrials.gov for NCT05099172; all statistical detail above is sourced to the FDA Multi-Discipline Review (Reference ID 5697816) and the approved label, not to a directly posted sponsor SAP.

### 196. vepdegestrant (Veppanu) — NDA 219835

**Sponsor:** Arvinas, Inc. / Pfizer Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adults with estrogen receptor (ER)-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative, ESR1-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer, as detected by an FDA-authorized test, with disease progression following at least one line of endocrine therapy

**Approval date:** May 1, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** VERITAC-2 (Study C4891001), NCT05654623

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, open-label, active-controlled Phase III trial; stratified randomization by ESR1 mutation status (detected vs. not detected, by central/local ctDNA testing) and visceral metastasis; dual co-primary populations sharing one endpoint construct (PFS tested as primary in both the ESR1m subpopulation and the ITT population), directly analogous to elacestrant/EMERALD's co-primary-population structure
- *Endpoints:* Progression-free survival (PFS, primary — BICR-assessed per RECIST 1.1, in the ESR1m population and the ITT population); overall survival (OS, key secondary, same two populations); objective response rate (ORR), clinical benefit rate (CBR), duration of response (DOR) and patient-reported outcomes (further secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* Stratified log-rank test and stratified Cox proportional-hazards model for PFS/OS, Kaplan-Meier estimation; Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio with Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test for ORR/CBR
- *Multiplicity:* Graphical multiple testing strategy (Bretz/Maurer-type graphical approach) controlling family-wise type I error at 1-sided 0.025, splitting alpha 3/4 (0.01875) to the PFS family and 1/4 (0.00625) to the OS family
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function approximating an O'Brien-Fleming boundary for two planned OS looks (first at the PFS analysis, second at 130 ESR1m deaths/66.7% information fraction)
- *Missing data/bias:* Ascertainment bias assessment via early/late discordance rates (EDR/LDR) between BICR- and investigator-assessed PFS; a distinct, trial-specific unblinding issue in which an interim BICR data-capture system explicitly labeled the first 33 ESR1m patients' expedited-review requests as "confirmation of progression," potentially unblinding BICR to investigator assessment — addressed via a sensitivity analysis excluding these patients
- *Regulatory:* Regular approval (21 CFR 314.126), not accelerated approval; FDA restricted the approved indication to the ESR1m population (narrower than the Applicant's proposed indication, which did not specify a test-detected ESR1m restriction as precisely) because the ITT-population PFS result did not achieve statistical significance under the graphical procedure; companion diagnostic co-approval — a supplemental PMA for the Guardant360 CDx ctDNA assay received contemporaneous approval; postmarketing commitment (PMC) to submit updated OS data given the immature/exploratory nature of the unplanned interim OS look submitted with the NDA

**Trial design & endpoints**

- VERITAC-2 (Study C4891001): randomized (1:1), open-label, active-controlled, multicenter Phase III trial of vepdegestrant (an oral PROTAC ER degrader) 200 mg once daily vs. fulvestrant 500 mg IM in 624 patients with ER-positive/HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer who had progressed on 1-2 prior lines of endocrine therapy including one CDK4/6 inhibitor; randomization stratified by ESR1 mutation status (detected vs. not detected, central/local ctDNA) and visceral metastasis (yes/no); 270 of 624 patients had ESR1-mutated tumors
- Co-primary endpoints: BICR-assessed PFS (RECIST 1.1) in the ESR1m population and in the ITT population (ESR1m + ESR1-mut-not-detected); key secondary endpoint was OS in the same two populations
- Sample size/power: for PFS in the ITT population, 310 events gave 92.5% power for a one-sided log-rank test at 0.01875 to detect HR<0.67; for PFS in the ESR1m population, 165 events gave 88% power at 0.01875 to detect HR<0.60; for OS in the ITT population, 396 events gave 80% power at 0.025 to detect HR<0.75; for OS in the ESR1m population, 194 events gave 80% power at 0.025 to detect HR<0.667
- Multiplicity: a graphical multiple-testing strategy controlled family-wise type I error at 1-sided 0.025 total, split 3/4 (0.01875) to the PFS family and 1/4 (0.00625) to the OS family; the SAP was amended (version 2, 05 Nov 2024, before database lock) at FDA's recommendation to reorder the hypothesis-testing strategy based on emerging evidence of differential SERD efficacy by ESR1 status
- Results: in the ESR1m population, PFS met its endpoint — median PFS 5.0 vs. 2.1 months (HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.42-0.77; one-sided p=0.0001); PFS in the ITT population did not cross its pre-specified alpha boundary and was not statistically significant; OS in the ESR1m population was not significant at the first interim analysis (HR 1.04, 95% CI 0.57-1.90 per FDA's exec-summary framing; HR 1.32, 95% CI 0.846-2.050 per the Applicant's stratified analysis table) and OS in the ITT population could not be formally tested because the ESR1m OS gate was not passed; a later, unplanned interim OS look (added after database unblinding, ~50.5% information fraction) showed HR 0.92 (95% CI 0.62-1.36) but was excluded from labeling given its unplanned/premature nature, with a PMC requiring the next prespecified OS analyses

- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 5789627, Statistical Reviewer Yifan (Katie) Wang, Statistical Team Leader Xin (Cindy) Gao) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/219835Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (VERITAC-2) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05654623 (no protocol/SAP posted in the Documents tab as of this writing)
- Protocol / SAP — not publicly posted; the FDA review references SAP Version 2 (finalized 05 Nov 2024) and a further OS-related SAP amendment (Version 3, Nov 2025), but the documents themselves are not available on ClinicalTrials.gov or Drugs@FDA

**Other resources**

- Arvinas/Pfizer's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for VERITAC-2; Pfizer participates in the Vivli data-sharing platform generally, but trial-specific availability was not confirmed.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this application; the only committee-concurrence reference found in the review package is an internal Executive Carcinogenicity Assessment Committee (eCAC) sign-off on the nonclinical rasH2-mouse carcinogenicity study (eCAC meeting 13-Jan-2026), not a public advisory committee.
- Companion diagnostic: Guardant360 CDx (ctDNA-based) received contemporaneous supplemental PMA approval as the FDA-authorized test for ESR1 mutation detection.
- Vepdegestrant carries a QTc-prolongation Warning and Precaution (mean ΔQTcF 10.9 msec [90% CI 8.2-13.6]); 11% of vepdegestrant-arm patients had AEs in the Torsades-de-Pointes/QT-prolongation SMQ vs. 1% on fulvestrant, though no ventricular arrhythmias occurred in either arm.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation, NDA 219835, Reference ID 5789627, §8.1.1.4 Statistical Analysis Plan and Amendments]* — "Amended statistical hypothesis testing strategy per FDA recommendation based on emerging evidence of differential efficacy of SERDs in ESR1 mutation positive vs ESR1 mutation negative patients. The new hypothesis testing strategy incorporates a testing order based on clinical importance and logical relevance per FDA comments."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "Adjustment for Multiplicity: Multiplicity adjustments are needed to control the family-wise error rate for the overall study. A graphical multiple testing strategy was used to strongly control the family-wise error rate of the whole study at the 1-sided 0.025 level... A Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function that approximates O'Brien-Flemming stopping boundaries will be used to control the overall type I error rate [for the two OS interim analyses]."

*[verbatim, same source, Sample Size Determination]* — "For PFS in the ITT population, a total of 310 PFS events will provide 92.5% power for a one-sided log-rank test at a 0.01875 significance level to detect a HR < 0.67. For PFS in ESR1m population, 165 PFS events will provide 88% power for a one-sided log-rank test at a 0.01875 significance level to detect a HR < 0.60."

*[verbatim, same source, FDA's Assessment of the primary endpoint]* — "The FDA identified that the first 33 (12% of ESR1m population) BICR confirmation of progression (COP) reads in the ESR1m population... may have been influenced by investigator bias due to the BICR reviewers having knowledge of the investigator's assessment of progression. However, a sensitivity analysis excluding these 33 patients from the analysis population demonstrated a PFS HR of 0.58 (95% CI: 0.41, 0.81), consistent with the primary analysis HR of 0.57 (95% CI: 0.42, 0.77)."

*[verbatim, same source, Conclusions on the Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness]* — "VERITAC-2 demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in PFS by BICR in the ESR1m population. Median PFS was 5.0 months versus 2.1 months (HR 0.57, 95% CI: 0.42-0.77; one-sided p-value 0.0001)... The PFS endpoint in the ITT population did not cross the prespecified significance alpha level and therefore was not statistically significant... Given the unplanned nature of the updated OS analysis with premature OS data, the results were not included in labeling. A postmarketing commitment (PMC) was agreed to by the Applicant to provide the next prespecified interim and final OS results for the ESR1m population."

### 197. sonrotoclax (Beqalzi) — NDA 220711

**Sponsor:** BeOne Medicines (BeiGene)

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with relapsed or refractory (R/R) mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) after at least two lines of systemic therapy, including a Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitor (BTKi) — accelerated approval based on response rate and durability of response

**Approval date:** May 13, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** Study BGB-11417-201, NCT05471843

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label trial — a Phase 1/2 multicenter study with a dose-ramp-up phase followed by a dose-expansion cohort; the Applicant's protocol amendment simplified the ramp-up regimen mid-study (from a Daily to a BIW schedule) based on Part 1 safety data, and the efficacy/safety analysis population pooled patients who received either ramp-up regimen at the same target dose
- *Endpoints:* Overall response rate (ORR, primary — IRC-assessed per 2018 iwCLL criteria adapted for MCL response categories, concept), duration of response (DOR, key secondary,)
- *Primary analysis:* Exact binomial test against a pre-specified performance goal — H0: ORR≤30% vs. H1: ORR>30%, one-sided alpha 0.025; Clopper-Pearson exact 95% CI
- *Multiplicity:* Unadjusted secondary/supportive testing (single formal primary endpoint)
- *Missing data/bias:* Non-responder imputation — patients without any post-baseline response assessment were counted as non-responders regardless of reason (conceptually reused from the "Non-responder imputation" family of terms, though here applied to a single-arm ORR rather than a diary-based composite); DOR censoring at the last disease assessment before new anticancer therapy or after ≥2 consecutive missed assessments
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval based on single-arm ORR/DoR, confirmatory trial required — the intended confirmatory trial (CELESTIAL-RRMCL, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 study of sonrotoclax+zanubrutinib vs. placebo+zanubrutinib in R/R MCL, NCT06742996) was underway at submission (76 of a planned 300 patients enrolled at NDA submission, 208 by April 2026)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- **Note on indication:** the task brief describing this submission as a chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) approval does not match the genuine FDA record for NDA 220711 — the FDA review package and the approved Beqalzi label both confirm the approved indication is relapsed/refractory **mantle cell lymphoma (MCL)**, not CLL. BeOne Medicines is separately developing sonrotoclax in CLL/SLL (e.g., a single-arm Phase 2 study, NCT05479994, and randomized Phase 3 trials CELESTIAL-RRCLL/NCT06943872 and a first-line CLL trial, NCT06073821), but none of these had led to an FDA approval as of this writing. This entry documents the genuine, FDA-confirmed MCL approval.
- Study BGB-11417-201: multicenter, single-arm, open-label Phase 1/2 trial of sonrotoclax (an oral BCL-2 inhibitor) monotherapy in adults with R/R MCL after anti-CD20-based therapy and a BTKi; after a 4-week dose ramp-up, patients received the RP2D of 320 mg once daily until progression or unacceptable toxicity; the efficacy analysis (Part 2) included 103 dose-expansion patients treated at the target dose (median 3 prior lines, range 1-8; 89% with ≥2 prior lines)
- Primary endpoint (estimand-framed, per the SAP): a binary IRC-assessed overall-response variable, with new anticancer therapy started before response counted as non-response (composite strategy) and post-discontinuation assessments still counted (treatment-policy strategy for early discontinuation)
- Sample size: ~100 patients in Part 2 gave >90% power to distinguish an assumed 50% ORR from a 30% historical-control null rate at one-sided alpha 0.025; a futility analysis was conducted on the first 14 Cohort-1 patients
- Results: ORR per IRC was 52% (95% CI 42-62%) with 16% complete response; estimated median DOR was 15.8 months (95% CI 7.4-NE) after median follow-up of 11.9 months — exceeding the historical-control benchmarks of bortezomib/lenalidomide (ORR ~20-30%) cited by FDA as confirmatory context

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter (Accelerated Approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2026/220711Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (BEQALZI) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/220711Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 5796969, Statistical Reviewer Shu Wang, PhD) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/220711Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (BGB-11417-201) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05471843 (no protocol/SAP posted in the Documents tab)
- Protocol / SAP — not publicly posted
- Pivotal publication: Eyre TA, Song Y, Hermine O, et al. "Phase I/II Study of Sonrotoclax (BGB-11417) Monotherapy in Patients With Mantle Cell Lymphoma Previously Treated With Anti-CD20 Therapy and a Bruton Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor." *J Clin Oncol.* 2026;44(23):2233-2243. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO-26-00550), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42385124/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Phase%20I%2FII%20Study%20of%20Sonrotoclax%20BGB-11417%20Monotherapy%20Mantle%20Cell%20Lymphoma)

**Other resources**

- BeOne Medicines' general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed for this trial; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held.
- Sonrotoclax carries a Boxed-Warning-adjacent tumor lysis syndrome (TLS) risk requiring dose ramp-up and prophylaxis; laboratory or clinical TLS occurred in 7% of patients, and fatal adverse reactions occurred in 4.3%.
- Breakthrough Therapy Designation was granted for the R/R MCL indication (per the FDA review's regulatory-history table), supporting the accelerated-approval pathway.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation, NDA 220711, Reference ID 5796969, §1.2 Conclusions on the Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness]* — "Efficacy is based on overall response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DOR), as determined by an independent review committee (IRC) in 103 patients (dose expansion) who received sonrotoclax at the target dose of 320 mg once daily... The ORR per IRC was 52% (95% CI: 42, 62) with complete response in 16%. The estimated median DOR was 15.8 months (95% CI: 7.4, NE) after an estimated median follow-up of 11.9 months."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.1.1.4 Statistical Analysis Plan and Amendments]* — "Primary analysis (Part 2): null hypothesis: H0: ORR ≤ 30%; alternative hypothesis: H1: ORR > 30%. A binomial exact test was used to evaluate ORR. The test against the H0 was performed at a 1-sided significance level of 0.025... The associated 2-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson CI of ORR was calculated."

*[verbatim, same source, Sample Size]* — "With a planned sample size of 100 in Part 2, there would be more than 90% power to detect an ORR difference between 50% and assumed 30% in historical control given a one-sided significance level of 0.025."

*[verbatim, same source, Pooling Patients that Received Different Dose Ramp-up Regimens]* — "In the Type C meeting 5/2025 and pre-NDA meeting 7/2025, FDA stated that the Applicant should include justification for pooling in the efficacy analysis population based on variable ramp-up regimens... the review team agrees with pooling patients received Daily and BIW ramp-up regimens for efficacy and safety analysis... The SAP was not amended to reflect the supplementary efficacy analysis by ramp-up regimen."

*[verbatim, same source, Benefit-Risk Summary]* — "The confirmatory, randomized phase 3 trial (Study BGB-11417-302) in patients with R/R MCL is underway, with 76 of a planned 300 enrolled at the time of NDA submission, and 208 enrolled as of April 9, 2026."

### 198. pivekimab sunirine-pvzy (Decnupaz) — BLA 761460

**Sponsor:** AbbVie Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm (BPDCN) — regular approval (not accelerated)

**Approval date:** May 27, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** CADENZA (IMGN632-0801), NCT03386513

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label trial — a multicohort Phase 1/2 study (dose escalation plus five dose-expansion cohorts) in which two disease-status cohorts (frontline/treatment-naive BPDCN in Cohort 6, and relapsed/refractory BPDCN pooled from Cohorts 1 and dose-escalation) were analyzed as separate efficacy populations within the same trial
- *Endpoints:* Composite CR/CRc rate (complete remission + clinical complete remission, primary in the frontline/de novo primary analysis population [PAP]; secondary in the all-frontline and R/R populations); duration of CR/CRc (DoCR, key secondary, Kaplan-Meier-based, concept)
- *Primary analysis:* Exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval for CR/CRc rate; descriptive Kaplan-Meier estimation of DoCR (25th/median/75th percentile and 3/6/9/12/18-month CR/CRc-maintenance probabilities, "Kaplan-Meier estimation")
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* A single interim futility analysis on the first 14 Cohort-1 patients, without a formal alpha-spending function
- *Missing data/bias:* Non-responder imputation for subjects without any post-baseline response assessment; DoCR censored at last disease assessment before new anticancer therapy
- *Regulatory:* Regular approval (not accelerated approval) based on one single-arm trial plus confirmatory evidence consisting of nonclinical in vitro/in vivo mechanistic proof-of-concept studies, rather than a second clinical trial or a post-marketing confirmatory-trial contingency

**Trial design & endpoints**

- CADENZA (IMGN632-0801): multicenter, single-arm, open-label Phase 1/2 trial of pivekimab sunirine (a CD123-directed antibody-drug conjugate) monotherapy at the RP2D of 0.045 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks, enrolling patients with CD123-positive AML, ALL, or BPDCN; the BPDCN efficacy analysis drew on 179 mITT-population subjects overall, with three defined BPDCN sub-populations: the primary analysis population (PAP, 20 de novo frontline patients enrolled in Cohort 6 with no prior systemic therapy and no prior/concurrent hematologic malignancy [PCHM]), an "all frontline" population (33 patients, PAP plus 2 additional de novo patients and 11 PCHM patients from Cohorts 1/6), and an R/R population (51 patients with 1-3 prior lines, from Cohort 1 plus dose-escalation)
- Primary endpoint: CR/CRc rate in the PAP (de novo frontline BPDCN), with CR/CRc rate in the all-frontline and R/R populations as secondary endpoints; a futility analysis was conducted after the first 14 Cohort-1 (R/R) patients
- Sample size: Cohort 1 (n=50 R/R) was powered at 91% to distinguish a 20% CR/CRc rate from a 5% null via a one-sided binomial test (alpha 0.025); Cohort 6 (n=20 frontline) was powered at 90% to distinguish 41.5% from a 10% null under the same test
- Results: in the PAP (n=20), CR/CRc was 75% (95% CI 51-91%, per FDA adjudication), exceeding the pre-specified lower bound of 10%; median DoR 10.6 months, median time to response 1.5 months; in the all-frontline population (n=33, the population reported in the label), CR/CRc was 69.7% with median DoR 9.7 months; in the R/R population (n=51), CR/CRc was 15.7% (95% CI 7.0-28.6%), exceeding the pre-specified 5% benchmark, with median DoR 9.2 months

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2026/761460Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (DECNUPAZ) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/761460Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 5805215, Statistical Reviewer Xin Wang) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761460Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (CADENZA) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03386513 (no protocol/SAP posted in the Documents tab)
- Protocol / SAP — not publicly posted; the FDA review notes the SAP "was agreed upon with FDA (Reference ID: 5455833) before it was finalized," but that reference itself is an internal FDA record, not a publicly posted document
- Pivotal publication: Pemmaraju N, Marconi G, Montesinos P, et al. "Pivekimab Sunirine in Blastic Plasmacytoid Dendritic Cell Neoplasm." *J Clin Oncol.* 2026;44(10):861-873. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO-25-02083), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41671533/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Pivekimab%20Sunirine%20in%20Blastic%20Plasmacytoid%20Dendritic%20Cell%20Neoplasm)

**Other resources**

- AbbVie participates in clinical-trial data-sharing generally, but trial-specific IPD availability for CADENZA was not confirmed; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held.
- BPDCN is a rare, aggressive malignancy (expected untreated survival 7-12 months); the only other approved therapy is tagraxofusp-erzs (~54% CR/CRc in frontline disease per the FDA review's benefit-risk narrative), which the review cites as context for pivekimab's benefit-risk assessment.
- Additional post-marketing studies were required to confirm long-term safety, characterize pediatric use, and further characterize veno-occlusive disease/capillary leak syndrome risks (both subjects of a Boxed Warning).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation, BLA 761460, Reference ID 5805215, §1.2 Conclusions on the Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness]* — "The primary analysis population (PAP) included a total of 20 patients with de novo newly diagnosed BPDCN who were enrolled prospectively to Cohort 6. Of these, 15 (75%; 95% CI 51, 91%) achieved a CR/CRc (per FDA adjudication). Because the 95% CI exceeded the prespecified lower bound of 10%, the trial was considered positive."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "A total of 51 patients with relapsed or refractory BPDCN (R/R Cohort) were enrolled on the study. CR/CRc rate was 15.7% (95% CI 7.0, 28.6) in patients with R/R BPDCN. Response rates exceeded the pre-specified benchmark of 5% for R/R disease... Confirmatory evidence was provided by strong mechanistic support based on nonclinical in vitro and in vivo proof-of-concept studies."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.1.1.4 Statistical Analysis Plan and Amendments]* — "The SAP was agreed upon with FDA (Reference ID: 5455833) before it was finalized. The SAP was finalized prior to the Cutoff date (02 October 2024) and before results were known... Three frontline subjects (2 with de novo and 1 with PCHM) enrolled before protocol version 6.0 were excluded from the PAP."

*[verbatim, same source, Sample Size]* — "Cohort 1: A sample size of 50 R/R BPDCN patients provides 91% power to distinguish a CR+CRc rate of 20% from a null rate of 5% using a 1-sided binomial test with a significance level is 0.025. Cohort 6: A sample size of 20 frontline BPDCN patients provides 90% power to distinguish a CR+CRc rate of 41.5% from a null rate of 10% using a 1-sided binomial test with a significance level is 0.025."

*[verbatim, same source, Handling Missing Data]* — "For the binary variables of response rate, if a subject did not have any response assessments, this subject was treated as a non-responder... No imputation methods were used for the OS endpoint."

### 199. gedatolisib (Revtorpyk) — NDA 219908

**Sponsor:** Celcuity Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adults with hormone receptor (HR)-positive, HER2-negative, locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer without a PIK3CA mutation detected, in combination with fulvestrant with or without palbociclib, following progression on or after at least one line of endocrine therapy in the metastatic setting — regular approval

**Approval date:** July 14, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** VIKTORIA-1, Study 1 (CELC-G-301), NCT05501886

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, open-label, active-controlled, three-arm Phase III trial — Arm A (gedatolisib + palbociclib + fulvestrant, "triplet"), Arm B (gedatolisib + fulvestrant, "doublet"), Arm C (fulvestrant, control); randomization stratified by visceral metastases, duration on immediate prior therapy, and geographic region; crossover permitted at progression — Arm C patients could cross over to Arm A or B at progression
- *Endpoints:* Progression-free survival (PFS, primary — BICR-assessed per RECIST 1.1, for Arm A vs. Arm C and Arm B vs. Arm C,); overall survival (OS, key secondary,); objective response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DOR) (additional secondary, exploratory-only per FDA)
- *Primary analysis:* Stratified log-rank test for PFS/OS treatment comparisons; stratified Cox proportional-hazards model with confidence intervals from the score test"); Kaplan-Meier estimation with Brookmeyer-Crowley CIs
- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing across five ordered hypotheses at one-sided alpha 0.025 each: (1) PFS Arm A vs. C, (2) PFS Arm B vs. C, (3) OS Arm A vs. C, (4) OS Arm B vs. C, (5) OS Arm A vs. B — testing stopped at the first failure to reject, with all subsequent comparisons treated as descriptive/exploratory
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* One interim OS analysis planned at the time of the primary PFS analysis (63 OS events expected, ~45% information fraction); a pre-specified rule removed a stratification factor from the stratified test if it produced <5 events in a stratum, with that factor instead used as an independent covariate for HR estimation
- *Missing data/bias:* Extensive PFS sensitivity analyses (excluding patients without tissue PIK3CA testing but with wild-type liquid-biopsy results only, excluding concurrent bone-metastasis therapy, adjusting for off-schedule imaging, and both including and censoring new anticancer therapy) — all HRs remained <0.4, supporting robustness
- *Regulatory:* Regular/traditional approval based on one adequate and well-controlled trial (VIKTORIA-1 Study 1) plus confirmatory evidence from an earlier single-arm Phase 1b study (B2151009, ORR 56% and median PFS 12.9 months for the same triplet regimen); postmarketing commitment (PMC) issued both for final OS data and for a companion diagnostic device to reliably identify PIK3CA-non-mutated patients, since no CDx was co-approved at the time of drug approval

**Trial design & endpoints**

- VIKTORIA-1 Study 1 (CELC-G-301): randomized, open-label, multicenter, multinational (23 countries) Phase III trial of gedatolisib (a pan-PI3K/mTOR inhibitor) plus fulvestrant with or without palbociclib vs. fulvestrant (± palbociclib per investigator choice for the control arm's own comparator structure) in 351 patients with HR-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer without a detectable PIK3CA mutation, previously treated with a CDK4/6 inhibitor plus endocrine therapy; randomization (1:1:1) stratified by visceral metastases, duration of immediate prior therapy (≤6 vs. >6 months), and region (US vs. rest-of-world); Arm C patients could cross over to Arm A/B at progression
- Primary endpoint: BICR-assessed PFS for Arm A vs. Arm C and Arm B vs. Arm C (co-primary comparisons); key secondary endpoint OS across all three pairwise comparisons
- Sample size/power: for Arm A vs. C, 145 PFS events gave ~98% power to detect HR 0.5 at one-sided alpha 0.025; for Arm B vs. C, 155 PFS events gave ~75% power to detect HR 0.652; for OS Arm A vs. C, 140 events gave ~85% power to detect HR 0.6; for OS Arm B vs. C, 149 events gave ~42% power to detect HR 0.75; for OS Arm A vs. B, 129 events gave ~24% power to detect HR 0.8 — reflecting that the OS comparisons were markedly underpowered relative to PFS, consistent with OS being immature at the primary analysis
- Multiplicity/testing order: type I error was controlled across PFS and OS in the fixed sequence (1) PFS A vs. C, (2) PFS B vs. C, (3) OS A vs. C, (4) OS B vs. C, (5) OS A vs. B; a protocol amendment (Version 7.0, 17 May 2024) demoted the PFS Arm A vs. Arm B comparison from key secondary to additional/exploratory and removed its dedicated sample-size determination
- Results: Arm A (triplet) vs. Arm C — median PFS 9.3 vs. 2.0 months (HR 0.24, 95% CI 0.17-0.35, p<0.0001); interim OS (48% information fraction) HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.43-1.12, p=0.133, not significant); Arm B (doublet) vs. Arm C — median PFS 7.4 vs. 2.0 months (HR 0.33, 95% CI 0.24-0.48, p<0.0001); interim OS (46% information fraction) not formally testable under the hierarchical procedure (observed HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.46-1.19)

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2026/219908Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (REVTORPYK) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/219908Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (Reference ID 5832496, Statistical Reviewer Haley Gittleman) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/219908Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (VIKTORIA-1) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05501886 (no protocol/SAP posted in the Documents tab)
- Protocol / SAP — not publicly posted
- Pivotal publication: Hurvitz SA, Layman RM, Curigliano G, et al., for the VIKTORIA-1 Study Group. "VIKTORIA-1 Trial of Gedatolisib Plus Fulvestrant With or Without Palbociclib in Hormone Receptor-Positive/HER2-/PIK3CA Wild-Type Advanced Breast Cancer." *J Clin Oncol.* 2026;44(12):1108-1119 (erratum: *J Clin Oncol.* 2026 Jul). [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO-25-02643), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41802242/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=VIKTORIA-1%20Trial%20of%20Gedatolisib%20Plus%20Fulvestrant%20With%20or%20Without%20Palbociclib)

**Other resources**

- Celcuity's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for VIKTORIA-1.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held.
- A first-line companion trial, VIKTORIA-2 (NCT06757634), is separately ongoing in the same PIK3CA-wild-type population.
- Major protocol deviations were notably imbalanced across arms (42% Arm A, 30% Arm B, 28% Arm C), driven partly by Arm-C-to-Arm-A/B crossover-related deviations; FDA's review characterized the overall deviation profile as not affecting interpretation.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation, NDA 219908, Reference ID 5832496, Executive Summary]* — "In Study 1 of VIKTORIA-1, gedatolisib in combination with palbociclib and fulvestrant demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in BICR-assessed PFS with a hazard ratio (HR) of 0.24 (95% CI: 0.17, 0.35; p<0.0001)... In an interim analysis of OS at the time of PFS analysis based on 48% information fraction, OS was not statistically significant with a HR of 0.69 (95% CI: 0.43, 1.12; p=0.133)."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.1.1.4 Statistical Analysis Plan and Amendments]* — "A statistical test of the treatment effects between the randomized treatment arms was carried out with a one-sided alpha of 0.025 per endpoint in Study 1 in hierarchical order, as listed below, until an endpoint failed to reject the null hypothesis... Any endpoints immediately after the one failing to reject the null hypothesis became descriptive and the p-value was displayed for descriptive purposes."

*[verbatim, same source, FDA's Assessment of sample size]* — "For the comparison of Arm A vs. Arm C, 145 PFS events would provide a power of approximately 98% to detect a HR of 0.5 with a 1-sided type I error of 2.5%... For OS, for the comparison of Arm A vs. Arm C, a total of 140 OS events would provide a power of approximately 85% to detect a HR of 0.6... For the comparison of Arm A vs. Arm B, a total of 129 OS events would provide a power of approximately 24% to detect a HR of 0.8."

*[verbatim, same source, stratification-sparsity rule]* — "It was pre-specified that a stratification factor that caused sparsity (defined as <5 events in one or more strata) would be removed from the stratified test... A removed stratification factor would be utilized as an independent factor for estimating the hazard ratio for the treatment effect."

*[verbatim, same source, benefit-risk conclusion]* — "As Study 1 of VIKTORIA-1 is an ongoing trial, the FDA issued a postmarketing commitment (PMC) for results of the final OS to further characterize the benefit-risk for gedatolisib... A clinical PMC was also issued for a companion diagnostic device to accurately and reliably identify patients who do not harbor a PIK3CA mutation."

### 200. zidesamtinib (Jideytro) — NDA 220185

**Sponsor:** Nuvalent, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who received a prior ROS1 tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) — traditional/regular approval

**Approval date:** July 22, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** ARROS-1 (NVL-520-01), NCT05118789

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label trial — a non-randomized, sequential Phase 1/2 study; the primary efficacy analysis pooled data across the Phase 1 dose-escalation portion and four Phase 2 expansion sub-cohorts (2b/2c/2d/2e) into one integrated Primary Analysis Set
- *Endpoints:* Objective response rate (ORR, primary — BICR-assessed per RECIST 1.1,); duration of response (DOR, secondary,); intracranial objective response rate (IC-ORR, secondary, modified RECIST v1.1)
- *Primary analysis:* Exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval for ORR; time-to-event secondary endpoints (PFS, OS, CNS progression) treated as exploratory-only, per FDA, "due to the lack of a randomized control arm"
- *Missing data/bias:* Primary Analysis Set (PAS) required patients to have started treatment ≥8 months before data cutoff specifically to ensure ≥6 months' potential follow-up for DOR maturity in responders — a data-cutoff/analysis-population design choice to manage immature-follow-up bias in a single-arm trial (conceptually related to the taxonomy's "reviewer-documented... follow-up" concerns seen in other single-arm accelerated-approval reviews, though here it is Applicant-designed rather than FDA-imposed)
- *Regulatory:* Traditional/regular approval (not accelerated) based on a single adequate and well-controlled trial, with confirmatory evidence drawn from other approved drugs in the same pharmacologic class (crizotinib, entrectinib, repotrectinib, taletrectinib) rather than a second trial, because "the rarity of ROS1-positive NSCLC render[s] the conduct of a randomized trial infeasible"

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ARROS-1 (NVL-520-01): non-randomized, sequential, open-label Phase 1/2 trial of zidesamtinib (a selective, brain-penetrant ROS1 TKI designed to retain activity against ROS1 resistance mutations, including the solvent-front G2032R mutation) 100 mg once daily, enrolling adults with ROS1-positive advanced NSCLC and other solid tumors; the ROS1-TKI-pretreated efficacy population (Primary Analysis Set, PAS) pooled 117 patients (26 from Phase 1, 91 from Phase 2 sub-cohorts 2b/2c/2d/2e) who had received ≥1 prior ROS1 TKI, had measurable disease per BICR, received the RP2D, and started treatment ≥8 months before the 21-Mar-2025 data cutoff; a Response Analysis Set (RAS, 227 patients) served as supportive evidence
- Primary endpoint: confirmed ORR per RECIST 1.1 by BICR in the PAS; secondary endpoints included DOR, IC-ORR/IC-DOR (in patients with baseline measurable CNS metastases, no recent brain radiation), time to response, clinical benefit rate, PFS, CNS progression, OS, and PROs (the latter group considered exploratory by FDA given the single-arm design)
- Analysis-population construction: of 349 ROS1-TKI-pretreated patients enrolled overall, 232 were excluded from the PAS by BICR (189 for starting treatment after the 31-May-2024 cutoff needed for follow-up maturity, 43 for lacking BICR-measurable baseline lesions)
- Results: ORR was 44% (95% CI 34-53%) including one complete response; with 6 additional months of follow-up (22-Sep-2025 DOR cutoff), 82% of the 51 responders had DOR ≥6 months and 69% had DOR ≥12 months; intracranial ORR was 48% (95% CI 34-63%) among 50 patients with baseline measurable CNS metastases, including 11 complete responses; among 42 patients with ROS1 resistance mutations, ORR was 50% (95% CI 34-66%), including 54% (95% CI 33-73%) among the 26 with the G2032R solvent-front mutation specifically

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2026/220185Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (JIDEYTRO) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/220185s000lbl.pdf

Available secondary literature: "Zidesamtinib (Jideytro): a new selective, brain-penetrant ROS1 inhibitor approved for the treatment of ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer." *Med Chem Res.* 2026;35(9):1543-1547. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00044-026-03606-6), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42611059/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Zidesamtinib%20Jideytro%20a%20new%20selective%20brain-penetrant%20ROS1%20inhibitor)

**Other resources**

- Nuvalent's general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for ARROS-1.
- FDA's review states no advisory committee meeting was held: "FDA did not refer this application to an advisory committee or seek input from other external..." (source text truncated in extraction but unambiguous in context).
- Zidesamtinib is the fourth ROS1 TKI to reach approval in this indication area (after crizotinib, entrectinib, and repotrectinib) and the second developed with an explicit brain-penetrance/resistance-mutation design rationale (alongside taletrectinib); FDA's SEE conclusion leans on this established drug-class precedent as confirmatory evidence for a single pivotal trial.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation, NDA 220185, Reference ID 5838569, §1.2 Conclusions on the Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness]* — "The statutory requirement for demonstration of substantial evidence of effectiveness is met based on the efficacy results from one adequate and well-controlled trial with confirmatory evidence consisting of evidence of effectiveness of other drugs (i.e., crizotinib, entrectnib, repotrectinib, and taletrectinib) in the same pharmacologic class in patients with ROS1-positive NSCLC."

*[verbatim, same source]* — "The magnitude and duration of responses observed with zidesamtinib reflect clinically meaningful benefit in the indicated patient population; these results, coupled with the rarity of ROS1-positive NSCLC, render the conduct of a randomized trial infeasible."

*[verbatim, same source, §8.1.1.4 Statistical Analysis Plan and Amendments]* — "The primary evidence of the efficacy of zidesamtinib is based on the analyses of pooled efficacy and safety data from the Phase 1 and Phase 2 portions of the ARROS-1 study (NVL-520-01)... started study treatment at least 8 months prior to data cutoff date to ensure that responders had at least 6 months follow-up post onset of response to adequately characterize DOR."

*[verbatim, same source, FDA's Assessment of endpoints]* — "FDA considers ORR per RECIST 1.1 by blinded independent central review (BICR) along with adequate DOR as potentially acceptable to support approval of a marketing application... FDA considers time to response, time to IC-response, CBR, PFS, CNS progression, and OS exploratory only, as time-to-event endpoints are challenging to interpret for efficacy evaluation in single arm studies due to the lack of a randomized control arm."

### 201. iberdomide (Zenbexus) — NDA 221075

**Sponsor:** Bristol Myers Squibb

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with multiple myeloma who have received at least 1 prior line of therapy including a proteasome inhibitor and an immunomodulatory agent, in combination with daratumumab and hyaluronidase-fihj and dexamethasone (IberDd) — accelerated approval based on MRD-negative complete response rate

**Approval date:** August 13, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** EXCALIBER-RRMM, NCT04975997

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial — a two-stage, Phase 3, multicenter study comparing IberDd against daratumumab+bortezomib+dexamethasone (DVd); patients were randomized across 3 iberdomide dose levels plus DVd in Stage 1 (n=279), then to the selected iberdomide 1 mg dose (IberDd) or DVd in Stage 2 (n=660), with the primary MRD-negativity efficacy population combining the first 420 patients (207 IberDd/213 DVd) randomized to the 1 mg dose across both stages
- *Endpoints:* Minimal residual disease (MRD)-negative complete response (≥CR) at any time (primary/major efficacy outcome — concept "Minimal residual disease (MRD) response rate," here specifically gating on CR rather than a standalone MRD-negativity rate); progression-free survival (PFS, co-primary per the trial design, not yet reported at accelerated approval) and overall survival (OS, secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* Miettinen-Nurminen method combined with Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) weighting across two enrollment stages, stratified by number of prior lines (1 vs. 2), age (≤70 vs. >70), and ISS stage (I/II vs. III)
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval based on MRD-negative CR rate (multiple myeloma surrogate endpoint); Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) required given embryo-fetal toxicity and thromboembolism boxed warnings (a cereblon-modulator/IMiD-class risk shared with lenalidomide/pomalidomide-class REMS programs)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- EXCALIBER-RRMM: two-stage, Phase 3, randomized, multicenter, open-label trial of iberdomide (an oral cereblon-modulating protein degrader) plus daratumumab/hyaluronidase-fihj and dexamethasone (IberDd) vs. daratumumab/hyaluronidase-fihj plus bortezomib and dexamethasone (DVd) in adults with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM) after 1-2 prior lines of therapy; patients refractory to a prior anti-CD38 antibody or to prior bortezomib were excluded; a total of 939 patients were randomized across the two stages (3 iberdomide dose levels tested in Stage 1)
- Primary/major efficacy outcome measure: MRD-negative CR (≥CR, threshold 10⁻⁵ by a Hematogenix next-generation flow cytometry assay) at any time, assessed in the primary efficacy population of 420 patients (207 IberDd 1 mg / 213 DVd) pooled across both stages; response was assessed by an Independent Review Committee per IMWG 2016 criteria
- Baseline characteristics of the primary efficacy population: median age 68 years; median 1 prior line (67% with 1, 33% with 2); 95% prior proteasome inhibitor, 90% prior immunomodulatory agent (70% prior lenalidomide), only 4% prior anti-CD38 antibody; 22% high-risk cytogenetics
- Results: MRD-negative CR (≥CR) at any time was 41% (85/207, 95% CI 34-48%) with IberDd vs. 21% (44/213, 95% CI 15-27%) with DVd (2-stage combined one-sided p<0.0001); among patients achieving CR, 89% (85/95) were MRD-negative in the IberDd arm vs. 83% (44/53) in the DVd arm; PFS and OS were not yet mature/reported at the time of this accelerated approval

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter (Accelerated Approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2026/221075Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (ZENBEXUS) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/221075Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical/Clinical Review — not yet posted to Drugs@FDA as of this writing (checked at the standard `Orig1s000StatR.pdf`/`MultidisciplineR.pdf` paths; both return 404, consistent with the very recent approval date)
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (EXCALIBER-RRMM) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04975997 (no protocol/SAP posted in the Documents tab)
- Protocol / SAP — not publicly posted
- Pivotal publication: no primary efficacy-results publication was identified as of this writing; the only EXCALIBER-RRMM-specific PubMed entry found is a trial-design paper published before results were available: "EXCALIBER-RRMM: a phase III trial of iberdomide, daratumumab, and dexamethasone in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma." *Future Oncol.* 2025;21(14):1761-1769. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1080/14796694.2025.2501920), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40346992/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=EXCALIBER-RRMM%20phase%20III%20trial%20iberdomide%20daratumumab%20dexamethasone)

**Other resources**

- Bristol Myers Squibb participates in the Vivli data-sharing platform generally, but trial-specific IPD availability for EXCALIBER-RRMM was not confirmed.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was identified for this application (no MDR/StatR is posted yet to confirm this directly; inferred from the absence of any public AC docket reference found).
- A related BMS trial, EXCALIBER-Maintenance (NCT05827016, iberdomide vs. lenalidomide maintenance post-transplant in newly diagnosed myeloma), is separately ongoing and not part of this approval's evidentiary basis.
- Iberdomide carries a Boxed Warning for embryo-fetal toxicity and serious venous/arterial thromboembolism, and is distributed only through a REMS program.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, ZENBEXUS Package Insert, §14 Clinical Studies]* — "The efficacy of ZENBEXUS in combination with daratumumab and hyaluronidase-fihj and dexamethasone (IberDd) compared with daratumumab and hyaluronidase-fihj, bortezomib and dexamethasone (DVd) was evaluated in adult patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM) in a phase 3, two-stage, randomized, multicenter open-label study (EXCALIBER-RRMM) (NCT04975997)... The major efficacy outcome measure was minimal residual disease (MRD) negative complete response (CR) at any time."

*[verbatim, same source, Table 4 footnotes]* — "Response was based on Independent Review Committee (IRC) assessment per International Myeloma Working Group (IMWG) 2016 criteria... Based on a threshold of 10-5 using a Hematogenix Next Generation Flow Cytometry assay... The 2-stage combined one-sided p-value based on Miettinen-Nurminen with CMH weights, stratified by number of prior lines (1 vs 2), Age (≤70 vs >70) and ISS staging (I and II vs III)."

*[verbatim, same source, Table 4]* — "Minimal Residual Disease (MRD) negative complete response (≥ CR) at any time, n(%): ZENBEXUS + Daratumumab and Hyaluronidase-fihj + Dexamethasone (IberDd) (N=207): 85 (41), (95% CI 34, 48); Daratumumab and hyaluronidase-fihj + Bortezomib + Dexamethasone (DVd) (N=213): 44 (21), (95% CI 15, 27); p-value < 0.0001."

**Reverse-engineered SAP** *[inferred]*

- *[inferred, from the label's description of a "two-stage" design and a "primary efficacy population" restricted to the first 420 of 939 randomized patients]* — the trial likely used an adaptive/group-sequential dose-selection element in Stage 1 (three iberdomide dose levels tested against DVd) before consolidating on the 1 mg dose for Stage 2, analogous to other seamless dose-selection-into-expansion oncology designs in this census (e.g., erdafitinib/BLC2001), though the label does not disclose the Stage 1 dose-selection decision rule itself.
- *[inferred, from the label's silence on PFS/OS results and the standard accelerated-approval PMC structure used elsewhere in this batch]* — PFS (a co-primary endpoint per the registered CT.gov record) and OS were almost certainly not yet mature at this data cutoff, and a postmarketing commitment to report mature PFS/OS as confirmatory evidence for the accelerated approval is expected, consistent with the standard accelerated-approval contingency language on the label ("Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in confirmatory trial(s)"), though the specific PMC milestone timing was not available in any document reviewed.

### 202. daraxonrasib (Rasonque) — NDA 220910

**Sponsor:** Revolution Medicines, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adult patients with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma with disease progression after one prior line of systemic therapy — regular approval (traditional NDA approval, not accelerated)

**Approval date:** August 26, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** RASolute 302, NCT06625320

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, open-label, active-controlled Phase III trial; enrichment by local RAS-mutation testing at baseline with the pre-specified primary analysis restricted to the RAS G12-mutant subpopulation while a secondary analysis covered the full ITT population, structurally similar to the taxonomy's biomarker-enriched-population pattern combined with a co-primary-population design
- *Endpoints:* Co-primary endpoints — overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS, BICR-assessed per RECIST 1.1) in the RAS G12-mutant population; OS/PFS in the overall population and objective response rate (ORR) were secondary; patient-reported time-to-deterioration (EORTC QLQ-PAN26) was an additional secondary endpoint
- *Primary analysis:* Stratified Cox proportional-hazards model for OS/PFS hazard ratios; stratified log-rank test for the OS/PFS p-values; stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel chi-square test for the ORR comparison, restricted to patients with BICR-measurable disease at baseline
- *Regulatory:* Regular approval (21 CFR 314.126) based on a randomized, active-controlled Phase III trial demonstrating a statistically significant OS benefit — not accelerated approval, unusual for this batch alongside vepdegestrant, pivekimab, gedatolisib, and zidesamtinib

**Trial design & endpoints**

- RASolute 302: global, randomized (1:1), open-label, multicenter Phase III trial of daraxonrasib (an oral RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor) 300 mg once daily vs. physician's-choice standard-of-care chemotherapy (mFOLFIRINOX, gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel, FOLFOX, or nal-IRI+5-FU/LV) in 500 patients with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma progressing after one prior line of fluoropyrimidine- or gemcitabine-based systemic therapy; documentation of locally tested RAS mutation status (mutant or wild-type) was required for enrollment; 92% of randomized patients had KRAS G12 mutations specifically (RAS G12 population, n=459), with 5% harboring other RAS mutations (G13/Q61) and 3% RAS-wild-type by local testing
- Co-primary endpoints: OS and BICR-assessed PFS in the RAS G12-mutant population; OS/PFS in the overall population and ORR (RAS G12 and overall) were additional/secondary efficacy outcomes
- Results (RAS G12 population): median OS 13.2 vs. 6.6 months (HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.30-0.54, p<0.0001); median PFS 7.3 vs. 3.5 months (HR 0.45, 95% CI 0.34-0.59, p<0.0001); ORR 32% vs. 11% (p<0.0001). Results (overall population, per the label's Table 6): median OS 13.2 vs. 6.7 months (HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.30-0.53, p<0.0001); median PFS 7.2 vs. 3.6 months (HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.38-0.64, p<0.0001); ORR 30% vs. 11% (p<0.0001)
- Regulatory context: this is a regular (traditional), not accelerated, approval — the only fully randomized OS-driven Phase III trial among the three RAS(ON)-class submissions in Revolution Medicines' broader daraxonrasib program at the time of approval, with additional Phase 3 studies (RASolute 303 in the first-line setting, RASolute 304 in the adjuvant setting) ongoing

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2026/220910Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (RASONQUE) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/220910Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical/Clinical Review — not yet posted to Drugs@FDA as of this writing (`Orig1s000StatR.pdf`/`MultidisciplineR.pdf` both return 404, consistent with the very recent approval date)
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (RASolute 302) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06625320 (no protocol/SAP posted in the Documents tab)
- Protocol / SAP — not publicly posted
- Pivotal publication: O'Reilly EM, Wainberg ZA, Hendifar AE, et al., for the RASolute 302 Trial Investigators. "Daraxonrasib or Chemotherapy in Previously Treated Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer." *N Engl J Med.* 2026;395(4):325-337. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2605555), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42223072/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Daraxonrasib%20or%20Chemotherapy%20in%20Previously%20Treated%20Metastatic%20Pancreatic%20Cancer)

**Other resources**

- Revolution Medicines' general IPD-sharing practices were not individually confirmed; no Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere listing was identified for RASolute 302.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was identified for this application (no posted MDR/StatR yet to confirm directly).
- An expanded-access program for daraxonrasib in previously treated metastatic PDAC (NCT07573215) was operating in parallel with the pivotal trial, indicating substantial pre-approval access demand.
- Daraxonrasib's label carries Warnings and Precautions for rash/dermatologic toxicity, stomatitis, diarrhea, gastrointestinal perforation, and interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis, each with graded dose-modification algorithms.

**Reverse-engineered SAP** *[inferred]*

- *[inferred, from the label's Table 6 footnotes and the co-primary RAS-G12/overall-population structure]* — because OS and PFS were each tested in both the RAS G12 population and the overall population, the SAP almost certainly used a multiplicity-control structure (e.g., a graphical or fixed-sequence hierarchical procedure, or a Bonferroni-type split) to allocate alpha across the two populations and two endpoints, similar in spirit to elacestrant/EMERALD's co-primary-population gatekeeping strategy elsewhere in this census — but the label does not disclose the specific procedure or the per-comparison alpha levels, and no FDA statistical review is yet posted to confirm this.
- *[inferred, from the trial's four-regimen "physician's choice" SOC comparator arm]* — the SAP likely pre-specified a stratification factor for chemotherapy-regimen choice (or region/prior-therapy-type) to account for the heterogeneous comparator arm when computing the stratified Cox model and log-rank test, following standard practice for multi-regimen-comparator oncology trials, though the specific stratification factors used are not stated in the label.

### 203. camizestrant (Etcamah) — NDA 220359

**Sponsor:** AstraZeneca Pharmaceuticals LP

**Indication approved:** Adults with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative, locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer, in combination with a CDK4/6 inhibitor (abemaciclib, palbociclib, or ribociclib), upon detection of an ESR1 mutation during aromatase-inhibitor + CDK4/6-inhibitor therapy, based on an FDA-authorized test — accelerated approval based on progression-free survival measured from the time of ESR1-mutation detection

**Approval date:** September 4, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** SERENA-6, NCT04964934

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trial; ctDNA-guided early-switch design in which randomization was triggered by on-treatment detection of an emergent ESR1 mutation (via serial ctDNA testing every 2-3 months) during ongoing first-line AI+CDK4/6-inhibitor therapy, rather than by a baseline biomarker-defined enrollment criterion; stratified randomization by visceral disease, order of ESR1-mutation detection (first vs. subsequent ctDNA test), time on prior AI+CDK4/6i therapy (<18 vs. ≥18 months), and CDK4/6 inhibitor identity (abemaciclib/palbociclib/ribociclib)
- *Endpoints:* Progression-free survival (PFS, primary — investigator-assessed per RECIST 1.1, notably not BICR-assessed, concept); overall survival (OS, additional efficacy outcome, immature at approval — 12% maturity)
- *Primary analysis:* Stratified Cox proportional-hazards model for the PFS hazard ratio; stratified log-rank test for the PFS p-value; Kaplan-Meier estimation for median PFS
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval based on PFS from a ctDNA-triggered randomized Phase 3 trial; companion diagnostic — Guardant360 CDx ctDNA assay used both for serial on-treatment monitoring and as the FDA-authorized test defining the approved population

**Trial design & endpoints**

- SERENA-6: randomized (1:1), double-blind, double-dummy, placebo-controlled, multicenter, ctDNA-guided trial of camizestrant (an oral next-generation SERD) vs. continued aromatase inhibitor (anastrozole or letrozole), each in combination with the patient's ongoing CDK4/6 inhibitor (abemaciclib, palbociclib, or ribociclib); eligible patients were on first-line AI+CDK4/6i therapy for ≥6 months with no investigator-assessed progression, and were serially tested for emergent ESR1 mutations via the Guardant360 CDx ctDNA assay every 2-3 months (3,256 patients had ≥1 ctDNA test); randomization occurred only once an ESR1 mutation was detected, at which point patients were assigned (1:1, stratified) to switch to camizestrant or continue the AI, both combined with the unchanged CDK4/6 inhibitor; 315 patients were ultimately randomized (157 camizestrant, 158 AI)
- Primary endpoint: investigator-assessed PFS per RECIST v1.1 (notably investigator- rather than BICR-assessed, unusual among the double-blind Phase III designs in this census); additional efficacy outcome: OS
- Results: median PFS 16.0 vs. 9.2 months (HR 0.44, 95% CI 0.31-0.60, p<0.00001); at the time of the PFS analysis, OS data were immature (39 deaths, 12% maturity)
- Regulatory basis: accelerated approval rests on the PFS result "as measured from detection of ESR1 mutation" (i.e., from the ctDNA-triggered randomization point, not from initial diagnosis or first-line-therapy start), with confirmatory evidence (presumably mature OS and/or later-line outcomes) required post-marketing per standard accelerated-approval contingency language on the label

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter (Accelerated Approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2026/220359Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (ETCAMAH) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/220359Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical/Clinical Review — not yet posted to Drugs@FDA as of this writing (`Orig1s000StatR.pdf`/`MultidisciplineR.pdf` both return 404, consistent with the very recent — one-week-old at time of writing — approval date)
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (SERENA-6) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04964934 (no protocol/SAP posted in the Documents tab)
- Protocol / SAP — not publicly posted
- Pivotal publication: Bidard FC, Mayer EL, Park YH, et al., for the SERENA-6 Study Group. "First-Line Camizestrant for Emerging ESR1-Mutated Advanced Breast Cancer." *N Engl J Med.* 2025;393(6):569-580. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2502929), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40454637/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=First-Line%20Camizestrant%20for%20Emerging%20ESR1-Mutated%20Advanced%20Breast%20Cancer); a companion patient-reported-outcomes paper is also available: "Patient-reported outcomes in the SERENA-6 trial..." *Ann Oncol.* 2026;37(2):180-193. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.annonc.2025.10.006), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41125211/)

**Other resources**

- AstraZeneca participates in the Vivli data-sharing platform generally, but trial-specific IPD availability for SERENA-6 was not confirmed.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was identified for this application (no posted MDR/StatR yet to confirm directly, but AstraZeneca's press materials and the NEJM publication do not reference one).
- Camizestrant's label carries Warnings and Precautions for QTc-interval prolongation (notably compounded when combined with ribociclib, itself a QTc-prolonging CDK4/6 inhibitor) and bradycardia (8% incidence), both monitored by on-treatment ECG.
- SERENA-6's design is notable within this census as the first ctDNA-triggered "pre-progression early switch" trial architecture — randomization is contingent on an on-treatment molecular event rather than either baseline enrollment criteria or radiographic progression, a structurally distinct paradigm from every other biomarker-selected design catalogued so far (e.g., KEYNOTE-024, FLAURA, SOLO-2, elacestrant/EMERALD), all of which select patients by a baseline biomarker before randomization.

**Reverse-engineered SAP** *[inferred]*

- *[inferred, from the label's stratification-factor list and the double-blind/double-dummy design]* — the SAP almost certainly pre-specified the same four stratification factors (visceral disease, order of ESR1 detection, time-on-prior-therapy, CDK4/6i identity) for the primary Cox model and log-rank test as were used for randomization, following standard practice reflected elsewhere in this census (e.g., VERITAC-2, VIKTORIA-1) — but the label does not itself confirm the stratified analysis used all four randomization factors versus a subset.
- *[inferred, from the "accelerated approval based on progression-free survival" label language and the 12%-maturity OS figure]* — a postmarketing requirement for mature OS data (and/or a confirmatory trial in a similar ctDNA-triggered switch design) is a near-certain contingency of this accelerated approval, consistent with the standard boilerplate ("Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial(s)"), though no FDA statistical review is yet posted to state the specific PMC/PMR terms.

## Cardiovascular / Metabolic

### 1. Empagliflozin (Jardiance) — NDA 204629/S-008

**Sponsor:** Boehringer Ingelheim / Eli Lilly

**Indication approved:** Reduce the risk of cardiovascular death in adults with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease

**Approval date:** December 2, 2016

**Pivotal trial:** EMPA-REG OUTCOME, NCT01131676

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-arm pooling, non-inferiority-then-superiority
- *Endpoints:* 3-point MACE (primary), 4-point MACE (key secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* Cox proportional-hazards model with covariates
- *Multiplicity:* fixed four-step hierarchy (NI 3-pt→NI 4-pt→Superiority 3-pt→Superiority 4-pt)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Haybittle-Peto adjustment for a single interim analysis
- *Regulatory:* FDA Advisory Committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Phase III, multicenter, international, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled cardiovascular safety trial; empagliflozin 10 mg, empagliflozin 25 mg, and placebo, each added to standard of care
- Population: type 2 diabetes with established cardiovascular disease (~7065 randomized at 607 sites, 42 countries); the two empagliflozin dose arms were pre-specified to be pooled for the primary analysis
- Primary endpoint: time to first occurrence of adjudicated 3-point MACE (CV death including fatal stroke/MI, non-fatal MI excluding silent MI, non-fatal stroke)
- Key secondary endpoint: time to first occurrence of 4-point MACE (3-point MACE plus hospitalization for unstable angina)
- Pre-specified testing hierarchy (four sequential hypotheses, each gating the next): (1) non-inferiority, 3-point MACE; (2) non-inferiority, 4-point MACE; (3) superiority, 3-point MACE; (4) superiority, 4-point MACE
- Analysis method: Cox proportional hazards model with covariates for treatment, age, sex, geographic region, baseline BMI category, baseline HbA1c category, and baseline eGFR category
- Non-inferiority margin: HR upper bound of 1.3 (ruling out ≥30% excess risk vs. placebo); tested at one-sided α=0.0249 (95.02% CI), reflecting a Haybittle-Peto adjustment of 0.0001 from the nominal 0.025 to account for one pre-specified interim analysis
- One interim analysis was conducted (to support the original glycemic-control NDA, filed before the CV indication); the same trial data later supported this separate CV-indication supplement

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2016/204629Orig1s008ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (2016, S-008) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2016/204629s008lbl.pdf
- FDA combined review package (includes Division Director Review with full testing-hierarchy detail) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/204629Orig1s008.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01131676 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)
- Pivotal publication: Zinman B, et al. "Empagliflozin, Cardiovascular Outcomes, and Mortality in Type 2 Diabetes." *N Engl J Med.* 2015;373:2117-2128. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1504720), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26378978/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Empagliflozin%2C%20Cardiovascular%20Outcomes%2C%20and%20Mortality%20in%20Type%202%20Diabetes)

**Other resources**

- Boehringer Ingelheim/Lilly IPD access via Vivli.org; trial-specific EMPA-REG availability not individually confirmed here.
- An FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held for this supplement (recommended approval 12-11).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, from FDA combined review, "Division Director Review," p.6]*

> "Type-1 error was controlled across the four pre-specified hypotheses to be tested using a hierarchical testing strategy (see below). Non-inferiority refers to the non-inferiority hypothesis to rule out a 30% or greater risk relative to placebo. Superiority refers to the superiority hypotheses to test whether empagliflozin conferred a benefit on MACE or MACE+ over placebo.
>
> Pre-specified Testing Hierarchy
> 1. Non-inferiority: 3-Point MACE
> 2. Non-inferiority: 4-Point MACE
> 3. Superiority: 3-Point MACE
> 4. Superiority: 4-Point MACE
>
> For the analyses, the applicant had pre-specified that the 10 mg and 25 mg empagliflozin treatment arms would be combined into a single group. A cox proportional hazards model with factors for treatment (pooled empagliflozin vs. placebo), age, sex, geographical region..., baseline values for BMI..., HbA1c..., and eGFR... was used to test for non-inferiority of the primary and secondary endpoints against a margin of 1.3 using a 1 sided alpha of 0.0249 (corresponding to 95.02% confidence intervals). The alpha had been adjusted by 0.0001 based on a Haybittle-Peto method to account for a single interim analysis to preserve the overall alpha-level level at 0.025. If non-inferiority was established for both 3-Point and 4-Point MACE, then testing for superiority was to occur in sequence for 3 and 4-Point MACE respectively."

Note the review's own remark elsewhere that "testing was based on a 95.02% confidence interval as an interim analysis was previously conducted to support the original NDA" — i.e., the alpha spent for the interim analysis of the *glycemic* NDA persists as a debit against the type-I error budget used for this later CV-indication analysis of the same trial data, which is a subtle and easy-to-miss point about reusing one trial's data across two separate regulatory submissions.
