### 10. Lorcaserin hydrochloride (Belviq) — NDA 22529

**Sponsor:** Arena Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Chronic weight management (weight loss and maintenance) as an adjunct to a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity, in obese adults (BMI ≥30 kg/m²) or overweight adults (BMI ≥27 kg/m²) with at least one weight-related comorbidity

**Approval date:** June 27, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** BLOOM (Study APD356-009), NCT00395135; BLOSSOM (Study APD356-011), NCT00603902; BLOOM-DM (Study APD356-010), NCT00603291 — the trial FDA's statistical review designates as the "pivotal study" of the 2012 complete-response resubmission, evaluated alongside the original BLOOM/BLOSSOM data

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
- *Endpoints:* percent weight loss from baseline, continuous; weight-loss responder rate, ≥5%/≥10% categorical
- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA (continuous weight-loss endpoint, covariates treatment/baseline weight/baseline HbA1c stratum/baseline medication stratum in BLOOM-DM); logistic regression (categorical responder-rate endpoints, adjusted for treatment/gender/baseline weight)
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical/gate-keeping testing across three primary efficacy endpoints (5% responder → mean weight change → 10% responder) and, within that sequence, a conditional test of the lower (QD) dose arm gated on both the higher-priority endpoint's and the BID arm's significance
- *Missing data/bias:* last observation carried forward (LOCF) imputation for continuous and categorical efficacy endpoints, applied to the Modified Intent-to-Treat (MITT) population; FDA reviewer explicitly criticized LOCF's inferential properties, citing the FDA-commissioned 2010 National Academy of Sciences report on missing data in clinical trials, and required a non-responder-imputation sensitivity analysis as a supportive analysis alongside the primary MITT/LOCF result
- *Regulatory:* Complete Response Letter (CRL) followed by resubmission and approval (Oct. 2010 CRL citing marginal efficacy and requesting the BLOOM-DM final study report; approved June 2012); postmarketing-required cardiovascular outcomes trial with pre-specified cancer surveillance, imposed as a condition of approval following FDA's rat-carcinogenicity findings; voluntary market withdrawal after a required postmarketing safety trial met its primary safety objective but revealed an unrelated cancer signal — see Withdrawal subsection below

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Original 2009 NDA (22-529) rested on two Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials: BLOOM (Study APD356-009, 104-week/2-year, N=3,182: ~1,538 lorcaserin 10 mg BID / 1,499 placebo) and BLOSSOM (Study APD356-011, 52-week, N=4,008: 1,561 BID / 771 QD / 1,541 placebo)
- FDA issued a Complete Response Letter on October 22, 2010, citing "marginal" weight-loss efficacy of lorcaserin 10 mg BID relative to placebo and requesting the final study report for BLOOM-DM (a third trial already underway in patients with type 2 diabetes)
- The 2012 resubmission added BLOOM-DM (Study APD356-010): 52-week, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial in overweight/obese subjects with type 2 diabetes, N=604 (253 placebo, 95 lorcaserin QD, 256 lorcaserin BID); the QD arm was discontinued mid-enrollment via Protocol Amendment 03 due to slow accrual, splitting the trial into pre- and post-amendment enrollment subgroups
- Three primary efficacy endpoints across all three trials: (1) percent change in body weight from baseline to week 52 (continuous), (2) proportion of subjects losing ≥5% of baseline body weight, (3) proportion of subjects losing ≥10% of baseline body weight — evaluated in a pre-specified ordered gate-keeping sequence (5% responder → mean weight change → 10% responder), each tested two-sided at α=0.05, for the lorcaserin BID vs. placebo comparison; the lorcaserin QD vs. placebo comparison (BLOSSOM only) was tested conditionally, only where the BID comparison and the higher-priority QD endpoint(s) were already significant
- Secondary endpoints grouped into five gate-keeping families (glycemic: HbA1c/fasting glucose/fasting insulin/HOMA-IR; lipid: TG/HDL/LDL/TC; blood pressure: systolic/diastolic; body composition: total body fat; quality of life), each tested at α=0.05 in sequence within its family, conditional on the 5% responder primary endpoint's significance
- Analysis population: Modified Intent-to-Treat (MITT, all randomized subjects with a baseline and ≥1 post-baseline weight measurement; ≥98% of randomized subjects), with the last observation on or before discontinuation carried forward (LOCF); FDA's statistical reviewer flagged that a substantial proportion of subjects (34%-55% depending on study/arm) withdrew before week 52, that early withdrawal correlated with less weight lost at the time of withdrawal, and that both the completer and MITT/LOCF populations were therefore likely to overestimate weight loss in the intended population — requiring, as a supportive analysis, a non-responder-imputation sensitivity analysis for the categorical endpoints
- Primary analysis method: ANCOVA (continuous weight-change endpoint; covariates varied by study — e.g., BLOOM-DM used treatment, baseline body weight, baseline HbA1c stratum, and baseline medication stratum); logistic regression, adjusted for treatment, gender, and baseline body weight (categorical 5%/10% responder endpoints)
- Reported primary results (MITT/LOCF): BLOOM — placebo-adjusted weight loss -3.7% (95% CI -4.1, -3.3, p<0.0001), 47.5% vs. 20.3% achieved ≥5% loss (OR 3.6, p<0.001); BLOSSOM — placebo-adjusted weight loss -3.0% (95% CI -3.4, -2.6, p<0.0001) for BID, 47.2% vs. 25.0% achieved ≥5% loss (OR 2.7, p<0.0001); BLOOM-DM — placebo-adjusted weight loss -3.1% (95% CI 2.2, 3.9, p reported significant), 27.3-percentage-point absolute increase in 5% responders vs. placebo. FDA's own conclusion noted the placebo-adjusted effect was "relatively low, compared to the benchmark of 5%" in FDA's February 2007 draft weight-management guidance, though the categorical responder-rate criterion was met.

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter (2012) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2012/022529Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (original, 2012) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/022529Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (combined document spanning the original 2010 NDA review of BLOOM/BLOSSOM and the 2012 complete-response review of BLOOM-DM) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/022529Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Clinical/Medical Review (Reviewer: J. Golden) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/022529Orig1s000MedR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov records — BLOOM: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00395135; BLOSSOM: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00603902; BLOOM-DM: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00603291 (no protocol/SAP documents posted for any of the three)
- Pivotal publication (BLOOM): Smith SR, Weissman NJ, Anderson CM, et al. "Multicenter, placebo-controlled trial of lorcaserin for weight management." *N Engl J Med.* 2010;363(3):245-256. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa0909809), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20647200/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Multicenter%2C%20placebo-controlled%20trial%20of%20lorcaserin%20for%20weight%20management)
- Pivotal publication (BLOSSOM): Fidler MC, Sanchez M, Raether B, et al. "A one-year randomized trial of lorcaserin for weight loss in obese and overweight adults: the BLOSSOM trial." *J Clin Endocrinol Metab.* 2011;96(10):3067-3077. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1210/jc.2011-1256), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21795446/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=A%20one-year%20randomized%20trial%20of%20lorcaserin%20for%20weight%20loss%20in%20obese%20and%20overweight%20adults%20the%20BLOSSOM%20trial)
- Postmarketing safety trial — CAMELLIA-TIMI 61, NCT02019264: ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02019264; Statistical Analysis Plan (sponsor-posted, Version 3.0, 18 May 2018) — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/64/NCT02019264/SAP_001.pdf; Protocol — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/64/NCT02019264/Prot_000.pdf; publication and FDA Safety Communication cited in the Withdrawal subsection below

**Other resources**

- Arena/Eisai IPD/dataset access via Vivli.org or YODA Project not individually confirmed here; no trial-specific access program identified.
- Two FDA Advisory Committee meetings were held on lorcaserin — one for the original 2009 NDA and a second tied to the carcinogenicity findings — per the Medical Review's reference to "the two lorcaserin advisory committee meetings"; specific vote counts were not re-confirmed in this research pass.
- Postmarketing requirement, imposed at approval (per FDA Clinical Review, "Recommendations for Postmarket Requirements and Commitments"): "A cardiovascular outcomes trial in a high-risk patient population that additionally includes echocardiograms, cancer surveillance including breast cancer screening, and monitoring for adverse events of special interest" — this requirement produced CAMELLIA-TIMI 61, documented below.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 022529, original-NDA review section, "Executive Summary," p.6/73]*

> "Confirmation of efficacy: The results of two Phase 3 studies are consistent and confirm the efficacy of lorcaserin 10 mg bid and 10 mg qd compared to placebo after 52 weeks of treatment, in the co-primary weight loss endpoints of average weight loss compared to baseline, the percentage of subjects who lost at least 5% of baseline body weight, and the percentage of subjects who lost at least 10% of baseline body weight... However, the placebo-adjusted weight loss was relatively low, compared to the benchmark of 5% described in the February 2007 draft Guidance for Industry: Developing Products for Weight Management."

*[verbatim, same source, complete-response review section by Janice Derr, Ph.D., "2.1.3 Major Statistical Issues," p.10/60]*

> "A substantial percentage of randomized subjects, 34%, withdrew from Study 010 prior to week 52... The average weight loss of the full analysis set with last observation carried forward (LOCF) imputation is also likely to overestimate the average weight loss in the intended population. Moreover, the use of LOCF as an imputation method has recently been criticized for its poor inferential properties. [footnote:] See the 2010 report from the National Academy of Sciences (NAS), *The Prevention and Treatment of Missing Data in Clinical Trials*. This report was commissioned by the FDA. The report states 'The panel believes that in nearly all cases, there are better alternatives to [LOCF]…which are based on more reasonable assumptions and hence result in more reliable inferences about treatment effects'."

*[verbatim, same source, "Statistical analysis methods for the primary efficacy endpoint"]*

> "Continuous endpoint: Change in weight was analyzed with analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) models with treatment, baseline body weight, baseline HbA1c measurement (≤ 9.0, and > 9.0), and baseline medication stratum (Metformin only, or Sulfonylurea with or without metformin)... Categorical endpoints: The yes/no occurrence of 5% responders was analyzed with a logistic regression model with effects for treatment, gender and baseline body weight."

*[verbatim, same source, "Approach to multiplicity," p.31/60]*

> "The applicant described an ordered gate-keeping sequence of comparisons for the three primary efficacy endpoints. The endpoints were evaluated in the following sequence for the lorcaserin 10 mg bid versus placebo comparison: 1) the proportion of 5% responders; 2) the change from baseline in body weight; and 3) the proportion of 10% responders. Each endpoint was evaluated at the two-tailed α of 0.05. The lorcaserin 10 mg qd vs placebo comparisons: The comparisons of lorcaserin 10 mg qd were carried out conditionally, if: (1) the lorcaserin 10 mg bid versus placebo was statistically significant for a given endpoint, and if: (2) the lorcaserin 10 mg qd versus placebo comparisons of the endpoint(s) with higher testing priority were also statistically significant."

*[verbatim, FDA Clinical Review (Golden, J.), NDA 022529, "Belviq (lorcaserin hydrochloride)," pp.14-15 — the carcinogenicity finding that foreshadows the 2020 withdrawal]*

> "Breast neoplasms and other malignancies: A large part of the review of the original NDA submission and discussion at the two lorcaserin advisory committee meetings was related to the rat carcinogenicity study findings. In the original submission, lorcaserin caused mammary gland tumors in both sexes at clinically relevant exposures, with no safety margin identified for female rats... Despite these reassuring findings, I think cancer surveillance should be considered as part of the CV outcomes trial. Lorcaserin has been characterized as a carcinogen in rats, and I am not convinced that we fully understand its effects with respect to tumor promotion in humans."

> "Recommendations for Postmarket Requirements and Commitments: The company should be required to conduct the following studies post-marketing: A cardiovascular outcomes trial in a high-risk patient population that additionally includes echocardiograms, cancer surveillance including breast cancer screening, and monitoring for adverse events of special interest..."

Notably, at the time of the 2012 approval, pooled Phase 3 human cancer surveillance data actually showed a numerically *lower* malignancy incidence in the lorcaserin arm than placebo — making the later reversal of that direction in CAMELLIA-TIMI 61 a genuine finding rather than a foregone conclusion foreshadowed only by the animal data.

**2020 postmarketing withdrawal — CAMELLIA-TIMI 61 and the FDA-requested market withdrawal**

The cardiovascular-outcomes/cancer-surveillance trial required as a condition of the 2012 approval was **CAMELLIA-TIMI 61** (Eisai protocol APD356-G000-401, "A Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled, Parallel-group Study to Evaluate the Effect of Long-term Treatment with BELVIQ (lorcaserin HCl) on the Incidence of Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events and Conversion to Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus in Obese and Overweight Subjects with Cardiovascular Disease or Multiple Cardiovascular Risk Factors"), NCT02019264, N=12,000, enrolled 2014-2018, sponsored by Eisai Inc. (which had taken over US marketing from Arena).

A genuine, sponsor-posted Statistical Analysis Plan is publicly available on ClinicalTrials.gov (Version 3.0, dated May 18, 2018) at https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/64/NCT02019264/SAP_001.pdf:

*[verbatim, CAMELLIA-TIMI 61 SAP (Eisai Protocol APD356-G000-401), Section 3.1 "Primary Objectives"]*

> "Safety: To demonstrate that, in obese and overweight subjects with CV disease and/or multiple CV risk factors, lorcaserin HCl 10 mg administered BID does not increase the incidence of MACE (myocardial infarction [MI], or stroke, or CV death) compared to placebo, with a non-inferiority margin for the hazard ratio of 1.4.
>
> Efficacy (revised per Amendment 02): To demonstrate that, in obese and overweight subjects with CV disease and/or multiple CV risk factors, lorcaserin HCl 10 mg BID reduces the incidence of MACE+ (MACE or hospitalization for unstable angina or heart failure (HF), or any coronary revascularization) compared to placebo."

> "When 460 adjudicated MACE (composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction or stroke) events have accrued, an interim analysis will be conducted to establish whether the primary safety objective (MACE non-inferiority) has been achieved... This analysis will be performed by an independent statistician and governed by the independent Data Monitoring Committee (DMC)... If the primary safety objective has been achieved, the trial will continue until 1401 MACE+ events, and 2.5 years median treatment duration."

The trial's primary safety objective (MACE non-inferiority, margin 1.4) **was met** — lorcaserin did not increase cardiovascular risk. The trial's cancer-surveillance requirement, however, surfaced the signal that triggered withdrawal. Per the pivotal publication:

Bohula EA, Wiviott SD, McGuire DK, et al. "Cardiovascular Safety of Lorcaserin in Overweight or Obese Patients." *N Engl J Med.* 2018;379(12):1107-1117. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1808721), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30145941/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Cardiovascular%20Safety%20of%20Lorcaserin%20in%20Overweight%20or%20Obese%20Patients)

FDA's Drug Safety Communication, issued February 13, 2020, requesting the withdrawal and summarizing the cancer data — https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-communications/fda-requests-withdrawal-weight-loss-drug-belviq-belviq-xr-lorcaserin-market — states:

> "The primary safety analysis showed no meaningful difference between lorcaserin and placebo in the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events, demonstrating noninferiority... There was a numerical imbalance in the number of patients with malignancies, with one additional cancer observed per 470 patients treated for one year. During the course of the trial, 462 (7.7 percent) patients treated with lorcaserin were diagnosed with 520 primary cancers compared to the placebo group, in which 423 (7.1 percent) patients were diagnosed with 470 cancers. Imbalances in specific cancers including pancreatic, colorectal, and lung contributed to the observed overall imbalance in cancer cases."

> "The drug manufacturer, Eisai Inc., has submitted a request to voluntarily withdraw the drug."

Eisai voluntarily withdrew Belviq and Belviq XR (lorcaserin) from the US market in February 2020, at FDA's request, following this communication — making lorcaserin a case where the *required* postmarketing safety trial actually satisfied its own primary (cardiovascular) safety objective, yet a secondary/exploratory surveillance finding (cancer incidence) specifically mandated by FDA at the time of the original approval — motivated by the pre-existing rat-carcinogenicity signal documented in the original Medical Review, quoted above — is what ultimately ended the drug's marketing life. This is a materially different regulatory pattern from a failed confirmatory-efficacy trial (e.g., olaratumab, melphalan flufenamide) or a cross-indication mortality signal (umbralisib): here, the trial's own primary hypothesis was confirmed, and withdrawal instead followed the specific, pre-specified ancillary safety surveillance that FDA had required precisely because of a concern flagged nearly a decade earlier in the approval package.

---

### 11. Lomitapide (Juxtapid) — NDA 203858

**Sponsor:** Aegerion Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adjunct to a low-fat diet and other lipid-lowering treatments (including LDL apheresis, where available) to reduce LDL-C, total cholesterol, apolipoprotein B, and non-HDL-C in patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH)

**Approval date:** December 21, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** Phase 3 HoFH Lomitapide Study, Protocol UP1002/AEGR-733-005, NCT00730236

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial
- *Endpoints:* LDL-C percent change from baseline (lipid-lowering surrogate endpoint)
- *Primary analysis:* paired t-test / Wilcoxon signed-rank test for a single-arm pre-post continuous endpoint
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (TC → Apo B → TRIG, each gated on the prior endpoint's significance)
- *Missing data/bias:* last observation carried forward (LOCF) imputation for a continuous efficacy endpoint
- *Regulatory:* FDA Advisory Committee meeting held; REMS (Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy) required as a condition of approval

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Phase 3, open-label, single-arm (non-randomized, no concurrent control group), multicenter, multinational, dose-escalation trial (doses of 5, 10, 20, 40, and up to 80 mg/day, individually titrated to a maximum tolerated dose), conducted at 11 sites in the US (2), Canada (2), South Africa (3), and Italy (4); 78 weeks total (26-week efficacy phase followed by a 52-week safety phase at the dose established at Week 26)
- Population: 29 patients ≥18 years old with clinically or genetically confirmed HoFH, on stable concomitant lipid-lowering therapy (including apheresis where applicable) for ≥6 weeks before baseline, maintained stable through Week 26; a 6-week run-in required a low-fat diet (<20% energy from fat) plus vitamin E/fatty-acid supplementation
- Primary endpoint: percent change from baseline in LDL-C at Week 26, at each patient's individually titrated maximum tolerated dose
- Key secondary endpoints, tested sequentially to preserve the overall Type I error rate at α=0.05: total cholesterol (TC), apolipoprotein B (Apo B), and triglycerides (TRIG), each analyzed only if the endpoint before it in the sequence was statistically significant; other lipid parameters (non-HDL-C, VLDL-C, Lp(a), HDL-C) were analyzed without multiplicity adjustment
- Sample size: 29 subjects enrolled based on an assumed 25% mean LDL-C reduction with a 30% SD and a 15% dropout rate, giving at least 90% power for the primary endpoint (a supportive Phase 2 dose-escalation study, UP1001, enrolled 6 additional patients but was not powered or pre-specified with a formal SAP)
- Baseline defined as the average of Week -2 and Week 0 values; the ITT population (all treated patients with a baseline and ≥1 post-baseline LDL-C value, N=29) was the primary efficacy population, with missing Week 26 data imputed via LOCF; a completer-only analysis (N=23 at Week 56) was run in parallel to assess the impact of dropouts
- Primary analysis: sponsor used a paired t-test (single-arm, within-patient pre-post comparison — there was no concurrent control arm to compare against); the FDA statistical reviewer independently re-ran the analysis using a Wilcoxon signed-rank test, better suited to the small sample size and potential non-normality
- Reported result: mean LDL-C reduction from baseline to Week 26 was approximately -40% in the ITT/LOCF population (N=29) and -50% in completers (N=23); 20/29 (69%) had a >15% LDL-C reduction

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2012/203858Orig1s000ltr_replace.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (original, 2012) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2012/203858s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review and Evaluation of Clinical Trials — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203858Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Summary Review (includes Advisory Committee vote) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203858Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00730236 (no protocol/SAP documents posted; record confirms non-randomized, single-group allocation, no masking, actual enrollment 29)
- REMS program record — http://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cder/rems/index.cfm?event=IndvRemsDetails.page&REMS=25
- Pivotal publication: Cuchel M, Meagher EA, du Toit Theron H, et al (Phase 3 HoFH Lomitapide Study investigators). "Efficacy and safety of a microsomal triglyceride transfer protein inhibitor in patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia: a single-arm, open-label, phase 3 study." *Lancet.* 2013;381(9860):40-46. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(12)61731-0>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23122768/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Efficacy%20and%20safety%20of%20a%20microsomal%20triglyceride%20transfer%20protein%20inhibitor%20in%20patients%20with%20homozygous%20familial%20hypercholesterolaemia)

**Other resources**

- Aegerion IPD/dataset access via Vivli.org or YODA Project not individually confirmed here; no trial-specific access program identified.
- An FDA Advisory Committee (Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee) meeting was held October 17, 2012; the committee voted 13-2 in favor of approval.
- Approved with a REMS program (Elements to Assure Safe Use) restricting prescribing/dispensing to certified prescribers/pharmacies, given the boxed warning for hepatotoxicity; a postmarketing long-term observational registry (LOWER, NCT02135705) was also required.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review and Evaluation of Clinical Trials, NDA 203-858/N-000, Section 3.1.1 "Study Design and Endpoints," p.6]*

> "Protocol UP1002/AEGR-733-005 was a Phase 3, 78-week, open-label, single-arm, dose-escalation (5, 10, 20, 40, 60 mg/day), multicenter, multinational trial, conducted at 11 sites located in US (2 sites), Canada (2 sites), South Africa (3 sites), and Italy (4 sites)... The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the efficacy of lomitapide as defined by percent change from baseline in LDL-C at an individually-identified maximum tolerated dose after 26 weeks of treatment in patients with HoFH. Based on the assumptions of 25% change in LDL-C after 26 weeks of treatment with a 30% SD and 15% dropout rate, 29 subjects were enrolled to obtain at least 90% power for the study."

*[verbatim, same source, Section 3.1.2 "Statistical Methods," p.7]*

> "For Study UP1002/AEGR-733-005, the primary efficacy endpoint was percent change from baseline in LDL-C at Week 26 and was analyzed using paired t-test by the sponsor. This reviewer also analyzed the data using Wilcoxon signed-rank test which can accommodate small sample sizes and non-normality... There were 3 key secondary efficacy variables: total cholesterol (TC), Apo B, and triglycerides (TRIG). They were prioritized sequentially by the sponsor and analyzed using the same test to preserve the Type 1 error rate at α = 0.05... The ITT population consisting of subjects who had received at least one dose of lomitapide, and had a baseline and a post-baseline LDL-value was the primary population for efficacy analyses. Missing data at Week 26 were imputed using the LOCF method."

*[verbatim, same source, Section 5.1 "Statistical Issues and Collective Evidence," p.15]*

> "As shown in Table 6, for the pivotal Phase 3 trial (Study UP1002/AEGR-733-005), the mean % decrease in LDL-C from baseline to Week 26 was about 40% for the ITT/LOCF population (N = 29) and 50% for the completers (N = 23). In addition, a total of 20 patients had a > 15% decrease in LDL-C at Week 26."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, Section 6 "Advisory Committee Meeting"]*

> "This application was discussed at the Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drug Advisory Committee on October 17, 2012... Regarding whether there is sufficient evidence of efficacy and safety to support the marketing approval of lomitapide, the vote was 13 versus 2 in favor of approval."

Note the FDA reviewer's own methodological caveat about the sponsor's dose-response claim (Section 5.1, p.15): the sponsor's CSR reported an apparent LDL-C dose-response relationship across patients whose maximum tolerated doses were 20/40/60 mg, but the reviewer flagged this as "misleading because the patient who dropped out at 40 mg had a +17% change from baseline" — illustrating how, in a single-arm study this small, one patient's outcome and the choice of imputation rule (LOCF vs. completers) materially changes the interpretation of a dose-response signal. This is the kind of small-N regulatory nuance worth capturing verbatim rather than summarizing away.

### 12. Apixaban (Eliquis) — NDA 202155

**Sponsor:** Bristol-Myers Squibb (co-developed with Pfizer)

**Indication approved:** Reduce the risk of stroke and systemic embolism in patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation

**Approval date:** December 28, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** ARISTOTLE (Study CV185030), NCT00412984

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, non-inferiority-then-superiority, event-driven trial
- *Endpoints:* stroke/systemic-embolism composite (ischemic, hemorrhagic, or unspecified stroke, or non-CNS systemic embolism; primary); ISTH major bleeding, all-cause death (secondary, sequentially tested)
- *Primary analysis:* Cox proportional-hazards model, stratified by prior warfarin/VKA-use status and geographic region (site pooled to region for sparsity)
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (NI → superiority stroke/SE → superiority major bleeding → superiority all-cause death)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Haybittle-Peto-type boundary (single interim analysis at 50% of target events; fixed 1-sided p<0.0001 stopping threshold)
- *Missing data/bias:* simulation-based sensitivity analysis of undetected treatment-dispensing errors; reviewer-conducted missing-vital-status fragility analysis
- *Regulatory:* Complete Response Letter (CRL) followed by resubmission and approval; GCP site-misconduct data-integrity investigation (OSI)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Phase III, multicenter, international, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled (vs. dose-adjusted warfarin, target INR 2.0-3.0), non-inferiority-then-superiority trial; 18,201 of 20,998 enrolled subjects randomized 1:1, at 1,053 sites in 40 countries (424 Europe, 316 North America, 176 Asia/Pacific, 137 Latin America); population had nonvalvular AF plus ≥1 additional CHADS2 stroke-risk factor
- Apixaban dosed 5 mg twice daily, reduced to 2.5 mg twice daily in patients with ≥2 of: age ≥80 years, body weight ≤60 kg, or serum creatinine ≥1.5 mg/dL
- Primary efficacy endpoint: time from randomization to first confirmed stroke (ischemic, hemorrhagic, or unspecified type) or systemic embolism
- Two major secondary endpoints tested hierarchically after the primary result: ISTH major bleeding, then all-cause death
- Sample size: event-driven, target of 448 primary efficacy events (477 were ultimately analyzed); one planned interim analysis at 224 events (50% of target) for superiority, with the DMC empowered to recommend stopping if the 1-sided superiority p-value was <0.0001 (this negligible-impact boundary left the final NI test at 1-sided α=0.025 and final superiority tests at 1-sided α=0.02499)
- Primary analysis method: Cox proportional-hazards model stratified by prior warfarin/VKA-use status and geographic region (individual site could not be used as a stratification factor because >1,000 sites across 40 countries would have produced excessively sparse strata against a target of only 448 events, so sites were pooled to the region level); SAP finalized May 11, 2010
- Non-inferiority margin of 1.38 (per FDA's recommendation; the sponsor's originally proposed margin is redacted as confidential/commercial information in the public FDA review) tested at 1-sided α=0.025; hierarchical testing then proceeded to superiority for the primary endpoint, then major bleeding, then all-cause death, each gated on the prior step's significance
- **Two distinct data-integrity controversies surfaced during review**: (1) a large, arm-imbalanced rate of medication-dispensing errors (bottles of the wrong blinded study drug dispensed) discovered late in the review cycle, which triggered a June 22, 2012 Complete Response Letter; and (2) an FDA Office of Scientific Investigations (OSI) inspection finding of Good Clinical Practice (GCP) misconduct — falsified subject records — by a Bristol-Myers Squibb employee at a Shanghai, China site, which led FDA to extend the original PDUFA date by three months and to require exclusion of Chinese-site data from certain analyses

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2012/202155Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2012/202155s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Steve Bai, PhD) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/202155Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Medical Review (includes the original Clinical Review, a September 2012 Complete-Response review, a December 2012 Clinical Review Addendum by Martin Rose, MD, JD, and B. Nhi Beasley, PharmD, and Thomas Marciniak, MD's "Completeness of follow-up and bleeding and cancer" special review) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/202155Orig1s000MedR.pdf
- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/202155Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00412984 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)
- Pivotal publication: Granger CB, Alexander JH, McMurray JJV, et al. "Apixaban versus Warfarin in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation." *N Engl J Med.* 2011;365(11):981-992. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1107039), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21870978/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Apixaban%20versus%20Warfarin%20in%20Patients%20with%20Atrial%20Fibrillation)

**Other resources**

- Bristol-Myers Squibb/Pfizer IPD access via Vivli.org; trial-specific ARISTOTLE availability not individually confirmed here.
- **No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held** for apixaban — a deliberate contrast worth noting alongside ticagrelor's contentious AC meeting above; per the Medical Review, this was because two other oral anticoagulants (dabigatran, rivaroxaban) had already been approved for the same indication, and by the time trial-conduct issues surfaced late in the review cycle, FDA concluded an AC "could not be usefully addressed... with the information currently available."
- FDA's Office of Scientific Investigations (OSI) inspected both BMS and its CRO (PPD) specifically regarding trial oversight/monitoring, and separately investigated the Shanghai GCP-misconduct incident; the OSI Clinical Inspection Summary (May 11, 2012) also documented two instances of investigators unblinding subjects without notifying the sponsor, and one investigator in India who knowingly kept subjects' INR below the protocol-specified range.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Steve Bai, PhD, §3.1.1 "CV185030 (ARISTOTLE)," pp.9-10]*

> "The study included 1 planned interim analysis for efficacy. The planned interim analysis for efficacy was to be performed after 50% (224) of the primary event have been confirmed... The DMC could recommend stopping the study if the one-sided p-values associated with the superiority test for the primary efficacy endpoint is < 0.0001... Negligible effect on the type I error for the final assessment of NI (<5x10-10); therefore the final assessment of NI will be performed at one-sided 0.025 when using NI margin of 1.38. The final tests of superiority for the efficacy endpoints will be performed at one-sided 0.02499... The statistical analysis plan (SAP) was finalized on May 11, 2010... Site and prior Warfarin/VKA status will be included in the model as stratification factors... With a target 448 primary efficacy events, the large number of strata... produces very sparse data... For this reason, when using a Cox proportional hazards model stratified by prior warfarin/VKA status and investigative site, site will be pooled to the Geographic Region level. Testing Strategy: A hierarchical testing strategy will be followed: If NI for the primary efficacy endpoint (using a NI margin of 1.38) is demonstrated, then superiority for primary efficacy endpoint will be tested at the one-sided α=0.025. If superiority for the primary efficacy endpoint is demonstrated then superiority for major bleeding will be tested at the one-sided α=0.025. If superiority for major bleeding is demonstrated then superiority for all-cause death will be tested at the one-sided α=0.025."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, "1.4 Medication Errors in CV185030," pp.4-7]*

> "The CV185030 study report indicated that 664 (7.3%) and 109 patients (1.2%) in the Apixaban and warfarin arms, respectively, had medication errors... After counted erroneous dispensing of active or placebo, increased but balanced number, 8.6% and 7.9%, of patients in the Apixaban and warfarin arms, respectively, that had medication errors... The sponsor performed a series of assumption-based modeling analyses of key endpoint results to explore how many medication errors would likely be needed to nullify the significant results... The sponsor argues that the mean p-values for the primary efficacy endpoint and ISTH major bleeding did not exceed 0.05 even when overall error in treatment dispensations was simulated to be 5%, which is more than 13 times the 0.38% reported error rate... it may still be problematic to conclude the robustness of the study based on this modeling approach."

*[verbatim, FDA Division memo (justifying the June 22, 2012 Complete Response Letter), Stephen M. Grant, MD, June 22, 2012]*

> "The reviewers also found that monitoring of the trial at least with respect to dispensing of study drug was clearly inadequate. Although site monitoring did detect some instances of subjects receiving bottles of study drugs different from those assigned, errors in dispensing study drug continued during the conduct of the trial with no action taken to lessen their frequency... OSI concludes that the study appears to have been conducted and monitored adequately. They did recommend that data from sites in China be excluded because the employee who committed the GCP violation in China was involved in the conduct of the trial at all Chinese sites. Two observations in the OSI Clinical Inspection Summary dated 11 May 2012 are of note: Two instances were found of investigators unblinding subjects for reasons other than medical emergency... One investigator in India knowingly maintained subjects' INRs in a range below that specified in the protocol."

*[verbatim, FDA Clinical Review (Updated), Thomas A. Marciniak, MD, "Completeness of Follow-up and Fragility of Results in ARISTOTLE," December 17, 2012, pp.2-5]*

> "I document below that completeness of follow-up and reporting of dates were poor in ARISTOTLE. Our confidence in the fragile alleged death benefit (with one additional death in the apixaban arm eliminating statistical significance) is destroyed by the missing vital status... The clinical study report (CSR) for the ARISTOTLE trial... states that vital status could not be determined for 2.0% in the apixaban group and 2.2% in the warfarin group... The p-value is close to 0.05 and the upper confidence limit for the hazard ratio is 1.00 so we know that this result is very fragile. How fragile? A change in only one death... could make this result nominally statistically insignificant. This critical number 1 is dwarfed by 317, the estimated — but still likely optimistic — number of patients with missing vital status in the apixaban arm."

*[verbatim, FDA Clinical Review Addendum, Martin Rose, MD, JD, and B. Nhi Beasley, PharmD, responding to Dr. Marciniak, December 17, 2012, p.3]*

> "In addition, the missing data rate in ARISTOTLE cited by Dr. Marciniak (3.2% to 3.6% for vital status) is not especially large and more importantly, it is unclear whether the missingness was biased in favor of apixaban... A p-value of 0.0465 already implies that the results are close... it is not appropriate to require both the 'cushion' of fewer deaths needed to achieve statistical significance at the 0.05 level plus an additional cushion to take care of post hoc 'what ifs.'"

Note the same statistical resolution as the FDA package-insert text confirms: the label (§14.2, ARISTOTLE results) does state the ARISTOTLE all-cause-death finding (p=0.046) in narrative form, but — consistent with the Rose/Beasley rebuttal above winning out over Marciniak's recommendation — it does **not** include Marciniak's proposed fragility caveat or the dispensing-error/missing-follow-up disclosure language he wanted added to the Clinical Studies section.

### 13. Alogliptin (Nesina) — NDA 022271

**Sponsor:** Takeda Pharmaceuticals

**Indication approved:** Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (dipeptidyl peptidase-4 [DPP-4] inhibitor)

**Approval date:** January 25, 2013

**Pivotal trial:** Study 010 ("SYR-322-PLC-010"), NCT00286455 — 26-week monotherapy trial supporting the glycemic-control claim; concurrent/required cardiovascular-safety trial: EXAMINE ("SYR-322_402"), NCT00968708

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (Study 010, monotherapy); randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven trial (EXAMINE, in a recent acute-coronary-syndrome population)
- *Endpoints:* HbA1c change from baseline (primary, glycemic-control program); 3-point MACE (primary, EXAMINE)
- *Primary analysis:* analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) with LS-means adjusted for treatment, baseline value, geographic region, and duration of diabetes (glycemic trials, per label footnote); Cox proportional-hazards model / one-sided hazard-ratio exclusion test (EXAMINE interim and final CV analyses)
- *Missing data/bias:* last observation carried forward (LOCF) for the primary HbA1c analysis (Study 010, per label)
- *Regulatory:* Complete Response Letter (CRL) followed by resubmission and approval (two separate review-cycle CRLs: an original-cycle CRL citing insufficient cardiovascular risk exclusion, and a second CRL in April 2012 citing a hepatotoxicity signal); premarket/postmarket cardiovascular risk-margin exclusion under the FDA's December 2008 Diabetes Mellitus CV-risk guidance, with a dedicated CVOT (EXAMINE) required as a Section 505(o) postmarketing requirement to complete exclusion of a 1.3 hazard-ratio margin **

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 010: Phase III, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial in patients with T2DM inadequately controlled on diet/exercise; a total of 329 patients randomized to alogliptin 12.5 mg, alogliptin 25 mg, or placebo once daily for 26 weeks after a 4-week single-blind placebo run-in
- Primary endpoint: change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 26; patients failing pre-specified hyperglycemic goals received glycemic rescue therapy and were counted per the ITT/LOCF convention
- Analysis method (per label Table 3 footnote): intent-to-treat population using last observation on study (LOCF), with LS-means adjusted for treatment, baseline HbA1c, geographic region, and duration of diabetes — i.e., an ANCOVA model; alogliptin 25 mg produced a placebo-adjusted mean HbA1c reduction of −0.6% (95% CI −0.8, −0.3; p<0.01)
- The approved glycemic-control indication ultimately rested on a program of 10 double-blind trials (~8,673 randomized patients) spanning monotherapy, active-comparator (glyburide, glipizide), and add-on combination designs (metformin, pioglitazone, insulin) — Study 010 was the dedicated placebo-controlled monotherapy pivotal trial; no single trial name/NCT is cited in the label itself (pre-2015-era label convention describes each trial generically, e.g. "In a 26-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled study...", without naming it)
- EXAMINE (regulatory/CV-safety trial, run in parallel with the efficacy program): Phase III, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven trial of alogliptin added to standard of care vs. placebo in 5,380 patients with T2DM and a recent (15-90 day) acute coronary syndrome; primary endpoint was time to first adjudicated 3-point MACE (CV death, non-fatal MI, non-fatal stroke)
- EXAMINE's role was purely regulatory/safety, not to support the efficacy claim: FDA's December 2008 guidance, *Diabetes Mellitus — Evaluating Cardiovascular Risk in New Antidiabetic Therapies to Treat Type 2 Diabetes*, required new antidiabetic drugs to exclude a pre-specified upper-bound risk margin (an 1.8 hazard ratio premarket, tightening to 1.3 if excluded pre-market or otherwise required post-market) via a meta-analysis of trial-level CV events, with a dedicated CVOT if the original efficacy program's CV event data could not do so alone
- Regulatory history reconstructed from FDA's Summary Review and approval letter: original NDA submitted 27-Dec-2007; FDA's review of the original efficacy data could not exclude the CV risk margin required by the December 2008 guidance, and Takeda initiated EXAMINE in response; a resubmission received 25-Jul-2011 included EXAMINE's interim CV meta-analysis results, which FDA judged sufficient to exclude an ≥80% excess CV risk (the premarket 1.8-margin standard), concluding "this application has met the pre-marketing requirements for demonstration of CV safety" while noting "more definitive conclusions on CV safety will have to await the completion of EXAMINE"; that same review cycle identified an unexpected hepatotoxicity signal (including a serious DILI case later reclassified after Takeda discovered a treatment-code error, per Section 8 of the Summary Review), leading to a second Complete Response Letter dated 25-Apr-2012; a final resubmission (26-Jul-2012) addressing the hepatic-safety findings led to approval on 25-Jan-2013
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held for the final (2013) review cycle — the approval letter states explicitly that "Your application for Nesina was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because this drug is a member of a class of drugs (DPP-4 inhibitors) for which we have already received extensive advice..." (the original 2007-09 review cycle is widely reported to have involved advisory-committee-level scrutiny of DPP-4-inhibitor cardiovascular risk data more broadly, but a specific alogliptin-dedicated meeting date was not independently confirmed in the documents retrieved for this entry)

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter (2013) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2013/022271Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (2013, original approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2013/022271s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Summary Review (Division Director Review, Mary H. Parks, M.D.) — the only individual-discipline review publicly posted for the original NDA (no separate Statistical Review or Medical Review is linked from Drugs@FDA for NDA 022271 Orig-1) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/022271Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record, Study 010 — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00286455 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)
- ClinicalTrials.gov record, EXAMINE — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00968708 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)
- Pivotal publication (Study 010): DeFronzo RA, Fleck PR, Wilson CA, Mekki Q; Alogliptin Study 010 Group. "Efficacy and safety of the dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor alogliptin in patients with type 2 diabetes and inadequate glycemic control: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study." *Diabetes Care.* 2008;31(12):2315-2317. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.2337/dc08-1035), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18809631/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Efficacy%20and%20safety%20of%20the%20dipeptidyl%20peptidase-4%20inhibitor%20alogliptin%20in%20patients%20with%20type%202%20diabetes%20and%20inadequate%20glycemic%20control)
- EXAMINE publication: White WB, Cannon CP, Heller SR, et al.; EXAMINE Investigators. "Alogliptin after acute coronary syndrome in patients with type 2 diabetes." *N Engl J Med.* 2013;369(14):1327-1335. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1305889), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23992602/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Alogliptin%20after%20acute%20coronary%20syndrome%20in%20patients%20with%20type%202%20diabetes)

**Other resources**

- Takeda's general clinical-data-sharing policy may cover Study 010 and/or EXAMINE; trial-specific IPD availability was not individually confirmed here.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held for this (2013) review cycle, per the approval letter (see above).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, from FDA Summary Review (Division Director Review), §2.1-2.2, pp.1-2]*

> "After the initial submission of this NDA, FDA issued a Guidance to Industry in December 2008 titled Diabetes Mellitus – Evaluating CV Risk in New Anti-diabetic Therapies to Treat Type 2 Diabetes. FDA's review of the original alogliptin NDA supported a conclusion that the drug was effective at lowering HbA1c in different clinical settings; however, it could not conclusively exclude a CV risk margin of 1.8 as discussed in the guidance. Consequently, the applicant, with feedback from the FDA, initiated a cardiovascular outcomes trial (CVOT) titled, EXAMINE (also referred to as Study 402) which is a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study evaluating alogliptin with standard of care in patients with T2DM who had a recent acute coronary syndrome (ACS)... The interim results of EXAMINE were submitted and reviewed in the first resubmission. The trial is continuing as a required trial under FDAAA in order to obtain important longer-term CV safety data and to address the FDA requirements to exclude a lower CV risk margin of 1.3. Takeda has provided sufficient evidence from the interim analysis that alogliptin is not associated with an 80% or higher excess CV risk over standard-of-care therapies for T2DM. Consequently, it has been concluded that this application has met the pre-marketing requirements for demonstration of CV safety. More definitive conclusions on CV safety will have to await the completion of EXAMINE."

*[verbatim, from FDA Summary Review, §13 "Decision/Action/Risk Benefit Assessment," p.11]*

> "The applicant has provided sufficient and consistent evidence for effectiveness as an anti-diabetic for all three products that is comparable to other drug products approved in this class. Previous deficiencies surrounding inadequate CV risk assessment and potential liver toxicity have been adequately addressed with resubmitted data... The ongoing CVOT, EXAMINE, is a postmarketing required trial for the alogliptin NDA. The event rates for this trial have been higher than anticipated and the second interim analysis to determine if the 1.3 margin is excluded may occur within this year."

*[verbatim, from approved Package Insert, Table 3 footnotes, p.16]*

> "Intent-to-treat population using last observation on study... Least squares means adjusted for treatment, baseline value, geographic region, and duration of diabetes."

*[verbatim, from FDA Approval Letter, §"POSTMARKETING REQUIREMENTS UNDER 505(o)," p.4-5]*

> "2007-5: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating the effect of Nesina (alogliptin) on the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. The primary objective of the trial is to establish that the upper bound of the 2-sided 95% confidence interval for the estimated risk ratio comparing the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events observed with Nesina (alogliptin) to that observed in the control group is less than 1.3... Trial Completion: December 31, 2013."

This PMR is, in substance, the requirement to complete EXAMINE itself (already fully enrolled at approval) rather than a newly initiated trial — the trial's completion (and White et al.'s NEJM publication) followed within months of approval, confirming a final HR of 0.96 (upper 1-sided 99.98% CI of 1.16), excluding the 1.3 margin.

### 14. Mipomersen sodium (Kynamro) — NDA 203568

**Sponsor:** Genzyme Corporation (a Sanofi company; developed by Isis Pharmaceuticals, Inc., now Ionis Pharmaceuticals)

**Indication approved:** Adjunct to lipid-lowering medications and diet to reduce LDL-C, apolipoprotein B, total cholesterol, and non-HDL-C in patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH)

**Approval date:** January 29, 2013

**Pivotal trial:** Study ISIS 301012-CS5, NCT00607373

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
- *Endpoints:* LDL-C percent change from baseline (lipid-lowering surrogate endpoint)
- *Primary analysis:* conditional two-sample t-test / Wilcoxon rank-sum test, selected by a pre-specified Kolmogorov-Smirnov normality pre-test
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (Apo B → TC → non-HDL-C, each gated on the primary endpoint and the prior secondary's significance)
- *Missing data/bias:* last observation carried forward (LOCF) imputation for a continuous efficacy endpoint
- *Regulatory:* FDA Advisory Committee meeting held; REMS (Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy) required as a condition of approval

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Randomized (2:1 mipomersen:placebo), double-blind (quadruple-masked: participant, care provider, investigator, outcomes assessor), placebo-controlled, parallel-group Phase 3 trial (Study ISIS 301012-CS5); ≤4-week screening, 26-week weekly subcutaneous treatment period, 24-week post-treatment follow-up (except patients entering the open-label extension, ISIS 301012-CS6)
- Population: 51 randomized patients (34 mipomersen, 17 placebo) at 9 study centers with HoFH, age ≥12 years, Tanner stage >2, fasting LDL-C ≥130 mg/dL, TG <350 mg/dL; stratified by body weight (≥50 kg received 200 mg mipomersen or matching placebo; <50 kg received 160 mg or matching placebo); patients on stable (≥12-week) concomitant lipid-lowering therapy were required to remain on the same regimen throughout
- Primary endpoint: percent change from baseline in LDL-C to the primary efficacy timepoint (PET), defined as the post-baseline visit closest to 14 days after the last dose of study drug
- Secondary endpoints (percent change from baseline to PET), tested in a fixed pre-specified sequence to control Type I error, each contingent on the prior endpoint's significance: apolipoprotein B, then total cholesterol, then non-HDL-C; tertiary/exploratory endpoints (TG, Lp(a), VLDL-C, LDL/HDL ratio, Apo A-I, HDL-C — the last tracked specifically to monitor for an adverse HDL-lowering trend) were not multiplicity-adjusted
- Sample size: designed with 15 patients in the control arm and 30 in the mipomersen arm to give ≥80% power to detect a 20% between-group difference in percent LDL-C change, assuming an SD of ~22%
- Analysis population: the Full Analysis Set (FAS, "the practically-feasible ITT population" per ICH E9) — patients from the Safety Set with a valid baseline and ≥1 post-baseline LDL-C value; primary analysis compared percent change from baseline to PET between arms
- Primary analysis method: both a two-sample t-test and a Wilcoxon rank-sum test were pre-specified; a Kolmogorov-Smirnov normality test determined which result would be used as the primary inferential result (Wilcoxon if K-S test significant at p<0.05, otherwise the t-test); within-arm changes were assessed with the Wilcoxon signed-rank test
- Missing data handling: LOCF was used for the primary comparison; the FDA reviewer specifically required sensitivity analyses comparing observed-cases (OC) vs. LOCF results, given a differential dropout pattern (6/34, or 17.6%, of the mipomersen arm discontinued treatment vs. 0/17 in placebo, mostly for hepatic-enzyme-related adverse events)
- Reported result: mean LDL-C change from baseline to PET was -24.7% (mipomersen) vs. -3.3% (placebo), treatment difference statistically significant at p<0.001

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2013/203568Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (original, 2013) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2013/203568s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review and Evaluation of Clinical Trials — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/203568Orig1s000StatR.pdf (this review reproduces extensive verbatim excerpts of the sponsor's "Mipomersen Core Statistical Analysis Plan," MCSAP)
- FDA Summary Review (includes Advisory Committee vote) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/203568Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00607373 (no protocol/SAP documents posted; record confirms randomized, quadruple-masked, parallel design, actual enrollment 51)
- REMS program record — http://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cder/rems/index.cfm?event=IndvRemsDetails.page&REMS=27
- Pivotal publication: Raal FJ, Santos RD, Blom DJ, et al. "Mipomersen, an apolipoprotein B synthesis inhibitor, for lowering of LDL cholesterol concentrations in patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial." *Lancet.* 2010;375(9719):998-1006. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(10)60284-X>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20227758/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Mipomersen%2C%20an%20apolipoprotein%20B%20synthesis%20inhibitor%2C%20for%20lowering%20of%20LDL%20cholesterol%20concentrations%20in%20patients%20with%20homozygous%20familial%20hypercholesterolaemia)

**Other resources**

- Genzyme/Sanofi and Isis/Ionis IPD/dataset access via Vivli.org not individually confirmed here; no trial-specific access program identified.
- An FDA Advisory Committee (Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee) meeting was held October 18, 2012; the committee voted 9 "yes" to 6 "no" on whether the efficacy/safety data supported approval — members voting against cited the modest mean LDL-C lowering as insufficient to offset hepatotoxicity concerns.
- Approved with a REMS program (prescriber/pharmacy certification, patient enrollment) given the boxed warning for hepatotoxicity (elevated transaminases, hepatic steatosis).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review and Evaluation of Clinical Trials, NDA 203568, "Study Design and Endpoints"]*

> "This was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study, which consisted of a <= 4-week screening period, 26-week treatment period, and a 24-week post-treatment follow-up period... Eligible patients were randomized in a 2:1 ratio to receive mipomersen or placebo as a subcutaneous (SC) injection, once a week for 26 weeks. Patients were stratified by weight... The primary endpoint assessment was at Week 28."

*[verbatim, same source, reproducing the sponsor's Mipomersen Core Statistical Analysis Plan (MCSAP), Section 4.2.2 "Statistical Methods for Evaluation of Efficacy Parameters"]*

> "The primary analysis of efficacy parameters will be assessment of the percent change from baseline to PET compared between treatment groups. Both the two-sample t-test and the Wilcoxon rank sum test will be assessed for the comparison between treatment groups. If the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test of normality is statistically significant (p<0.05) then the Wilcoxon rank sum test results will be utilized. Otherwise, the two-sample t-test will be used. Changes within treatment groups will be assessed using the Wilcoxon signed rank test... Inflation of type I error due to multiple secondary endpoints will be controlled by, first, the specification of a small number of secondary parameters and, second, use of sequential inferential approach in which statistical significance of the primary parameter is required before drawing inferential conclusions about the first secondary parameter... Inferential conclusions about each successive parameter require statistical significance of the prior one. No further adjustments will be made for tertiary parameters."

*[verbatim, same source, Section 6 "Sample Size, Power and Randomization" of the MCSAP]*

> "Based upon prior clinical trial experience with mipomersen, it is estimated that the standard deviation of the percent change in LDL-C is approximately 22%. With 15 subjects in the control group and 30 subjects in the mipomersen-treated group, this study would have at least 80% power to detect a 20% difference between the two groups."

*[verbatim, same source, efficacy results]*

> "The mean percent change in LDL-C was -24.7% for patients in the mipomersen group and -3.3% for patients in the placebo group. The treatment difference was statistically significant."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, Section 8 "Advisory Committee Meeting"]*

> "The Division's advisory committee met on 18 October 2012 to discuss the efficacy and safety of mipomersen when used as a therapeutic option for patients with HoFH. When asked if the efficacy and safety data for mipomersen supported marketing for the treatment of HoFH, the committee voted 9 'yes' and 6 'no'. Among the committee members who voted against approval, the modest mean lowering of LDL-C was insufficient to offset the potential safety concerns, in particular, liver toxicity."

The FDA reviewer's note on the sponsor's Kolmogorov-Smirnov normality-test reporting is also worth preserving as a genuine methodological critique: *[verbatim, same source]* "By this reviewer's understanding, for test of normality, there should be two p-values – one for placebo responses and another for mipomersen responses. From the only one p-value (0.120), provided by the sponsor for the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test in the efficacy results Table, it appears that this p-value is for the test of equality of the two distributions... Also, it is not a protocol mentioned or generally used test for testing the equality of means or medians." This documents FDA statistical review pushing back on ambiguity in how the sponsor executed its own pre-specified test-selection rule — a useful, concrete example of reviewer scrutiny of a small-trial SAP's operational details.

### 15. Canagliflozin (Invokana) — NDA 204042

**Sponsor:** Janssen Research & Development, LLC

**Indication approved:** Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (SGLT2 inhibitor)

**Approval date:** March 29, 2013

**Pivotal trial:** DIA3005 ("CANTATA-M"), NCT01081834 — 26/52-week monotherapy registration trial; concurrent/required cardiovascular-safety trial: DIA3008/CANVAS, NCT01032629

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (DIA3005 and 6 of the other 8 Phase III trials); randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, non-inferiority (DIA3009 vs. glimepiride, DIA3015 vs. sitagliptin); randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven trial (CANVAS, ongoing at time of approval); cross-trial pooled/integrated analysis (9-trial premarket CV-safety meta-analysis, stratified by CANVAS vs. non-CANVAS)
- *Endpoints:* HbA1c change from baseline (primary, all 9 Phase III efficacy trials); MACE-plus composite (CV death, non-fatal MI, non-fatal stroke, hospitalized unstable angina) (primary, premarket CV-safety meta-analysis)
- *Primary analysis:* analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) with LS-means (treatment, stratification factor(s), baseline HbA1c as covariate); mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) as supportive analysis; Cox proportional-hazards model with two strata (CANVAS vs. non-CANVAS) for the CV-safety meta-analysis
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence hierarchical testing per trial (primary → major secondary endpoints), with a Hochberg step-up procedure for a second family of endpoints (SBP, HDL-C, TG, HOMA2-%B) in some trials
- *Missing data/bias:* last observation carried forward (LOCF) as the primary method for the ANCOVA analysis, with MMRM (observed-data, unstructured covariance) as a supportive sensitivity analysis
- *Regulatory:* premarket/postmarket cardiovascular risk-margin exclusion under the FDA's December 2008 Diabetes Mellitus CV-risk guidance, supported by an interim pooled meta-analysis (including an ongoing, not-yet-complete CVOT) that excluded the premarket 1.8 margin but left the lower 1.3 margin to be excluded by a Section 505(o) postmarketing requirement **; FDA Advisory Committee meeting held (Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee, January 10, 2013)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- DIA3005/CANTATA-M: Phase III, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial ("A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Parallel-Group, Multicenter Study to Evaluate the Efficacy, Safety, and Tolerability of Canagliflozin as Monotherapy..."); 678 subjects total, comprising a 52-week Main Study (587 randomized 1:1:1 to placebo, canagliflozin 100 mg, canagliflozin 300 mg — 26-week placebo-controlled core followed by a 26-week active-controlled extension) and a 26-week High Glycemic Substudy (91 subjects, HbA1c >10-12%, randomized 1:1 to the two canagliflozin doses only, no placebo arm)
- Primary endpoint across the entire Phase III program (9 trials: DIA3002, DIA3004, DIA3005, DIA3006, DIA3008 [SU and insulin substudies], DIA3009, DIA3010, DIA3012, DIA3015): change from baseline in HbA1c to end of study; major secondary endpoints included FPG, 2-hour postprandial glucose, proportion reaching HbA1c <7%, and percent change in body weight, HDL-C, fasting triglycerides, and SBP
- Analysis sets: modified intent-to-treat (mITT, all randomized subjects who took ≥1 dose of double-blind drug — the primary analysis set), per-protocol, and completers
- Primary analysis method (FDA Statistical Review, Wei Liu, Ph.D.): ANCOVA with LOCF for missing data, model terms of treatment and randomization stratification factor(s) as fixed effects plus baseline HbA1c as covariate (baseline eGFR added as an additional covariate in DIA3004); MMRM (observed data, treatment/stratification/visit/treatment-by-visit interaction, unstructured covariance) used as a supportive analysis, consistent with the LOCF-based primary result in every trial
- Non-inferiority margin of 0.3% HbA1c was pre-specified for the two active-comparator trials (DIA3009 vs. glimepiride at 52 weeks; DIA3015 vs. sitagliptin at 52 weeks); canagliflozin 300 mg was additionally shown superior to glimepiride in DIA3009 (p=0.016, small effect size of −0.12%)
- Each trial used a pre-specified fixed-sequence testing hierarchy across the primary and major secondary endpoints to control family-wise error at 5%, with some trials proceeding to a second family of endpoints (SBP, HDL-C, TG, and HOMA2-%B in DIA3012) tested via a Hochberg step-up procedure conditional on the prior family's significance
- CANVAS (DIA3008, "CANagliflozin cardioVascular Assessment Study"): a dedicated, event-driven Phase III CVOT (N=4,330) begun in December 2009 that was **still ongoing (not completed)** at the time of the March 2013 approval; two of CANVAS's internal treatment sub-populations (background sulfonylurea and background insulin users) were also used, unusually, as two of the nine glycemic-efficacy trials (the "DIA3008 SU substudy" and "DIA3008 Insulin substudy" in the efficacy analysis above)
- Premarket CV-safety basis for approval: a pre-specified meta-analysis (agreed with FDA under a July 2010 SAP submitted to IND 76479) pooling all 9 Phase 2/3 trials (including CANVAS's accrued interim data), using a Cox proportional-hazards model stratified by CANVAS vs. non-CANVAS trials, to test whether canagliflozin's MACE-plus hazard ratio excluded the FDA's premarket 1.8 upper-bound margin
- A co-specified, more stringent test (two-sided α=0.001) was intended to exclude a lower 1.3 margin at the same premarket analysis, but the 99.9% CI (0.56, 1.48) did not exclude 1.3 — per the pre-agreed SAP, that lower-margin exclusion was deferred to future analyses planned after 500 and 700 MACE-plus events accrue in the ongoing canagliflozin CVOT program, and was ultimately made a Section 505(o) postmarketing requirement
- FDA's statistical reviewer flagged a non-proportional-hazards concern: an early (first-30-day) imbalance of MACE-plus events within CANVAS specifically (13/2,886 canagliflozin vs. 1/1,441 placebo; HR 6.49, 95% CI 0.85-49.64), attributable to the trial's higher-baseline-CV-risk population, while the hazard ratio after the first 30 days (0.89, 0.64-1.25) and in the 8 non-CANVAS trials (0.64, 0.34-1.19) showed no comparable signal

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter (2013) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2013/204042Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (2013, original approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2013/204042s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review(s) — a bundled PDF containing three separate reviews: a carcinogenicity statistical review (Min Min, Ph.D.), the **efficacy Statistical Review of Clinical Studies** (Wei Liu, Ph.D., dated May 31, 2012 — source of the DIA3005/9-trial SAP detail above), and the **premarket cardiovascular-safety Statistical Review** (Eugenio Andraca-Carrera, Ph.D. — source of the CANVAS meta-analysis detail above) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/204042Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Medical (Clinical) Review (Hyon J. Kwon, PharmD, MPH), including the January 10, 2013 Advisory Committee discussion summary — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/204042Orig1s000MedR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record, DIA3005/CANTATA-M — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01081834 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)
- ClinicalTrials.gov record, CANVAS — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01032629 (no protocol/SAP documents posted; trial continued to final completion in February 2017, well after this NDA approval)
- Pivotal publication (DIA3005/CANTATA-M, 26-week primary analysis): Stenlöf K, Cefalu WT, Kim KA, et al. "Efficacy and safety of canagliflozin monotherapy in subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus inadequately controlled with diet and exercise." *Diabetes Obes Metab.* 2013;15(4):372-382. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1111/dom.12054), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23279307/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Efficacy%20and%20safety%20of%20canagliflozin%20monotherapy%20in%20subjects%20with%20type%202%20diabetes%20mellitus%20inadequately%20controlled%20with%20diet%20and%20exercise)
- 52-week extension publication (same trial): Stenlöf K, Cefalu WT, Kim KA, et al. "Long-term efficacy and safety of canagliflozin monotherapy in patients with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled with diet and exercise: findings from the 52-week CANTATA-M study." *Curr Med Res Opin.* 2014;30(2):163-175. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1185/03007995.2013.850066), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24073995/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Long-term%20efficacy%20and%20safety%20of%20canagliflozin%20monotherapy%20in%20patients%20with%20type%202%20diabetes%20inadequately%20controlled%20with%20diet%20and%20exercise)

**Other resources**

- Janssen (Johnson & Johnson) IPD access via the Yale Open Data Access (YODA) Project; trial-specific DIA3005/CANVAS availability not individually confirmed here.
- An FDA Advisory Committee meeting (Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee) was held January 10, 2013, focused primarily on benefit-risk in moderate renal impairment and on a fracture-risk imbalance signal, rather than on the CV-safety meta-analysis itself.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, from FDA Statistical Review, CV-safety section (Eugenio Andraca-Carrera, Ph.D.), §1.1 "Conclusions and Recommendations," p.2-3]*

> "The Sponsor evaluated the CV safety of canagliflozin through a meta-analysis of 9 randomized, controlled Phase 2 and Phase 3 trials, including a dedicated cardiovascular outcomes trial, Study 3008, also known as CANVAS... The pre-specified Cox proportional hazards model with two strata (CANVAS and non-CANVAS trials) including all 9 trials yielded an estimated hazard ratio of canagliflozin vs. all comparators of 0.91 with 95% confidence interval (0.68, 1.21). The upper bound of this 95% confidence interval is below the risk margin of 1.8 necessary to show adequate cardiovascular safety of new antidiabetic products in accordance to the FDA Diabetes Guidance for assessing cardiovascular safety (2008). However, the data showed some evidence to suggest that the assumption of proportional hazards necessary to interpret the pre-specified Cox proportional hazards model may not have been met... An imbalance of MACE-plus was observed during the first 30 days in CANVAS."

*[verbatim, from FDA Statistical Review, §1.3 "Statistical Issues and Findings," p.4]*

> "In the Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) to assess Cardiovascular Safety submitted to IND 76479 on 13 July 2010 and agreed upon by the FDA, it was determined that the CV safety of canagliflozin would be evaluated through a meta-analysis of Phase 2 and Phase 3 clinical trials for canagliflozin, including the dedicated cardiovascular trial CANVAS... A test to rule out a hazard ratio of MACE-plus larger than 1.3 with a two-sided α=0.001 was planned to be conducted at the same time as the pre-specified meta-analysis assessment of the HR risk margin of 1.8. The estimated 99.9% confidence interval for the hazard ratio of MACE-plus based on the primary Cox model was (0.56, 1.48), and therefore the upper bound of the 99.9% confidence interval did not rule out a hazard ratio of 1.3 at this time as pre-specified. Based on the agreed-upon SAP, the Sponsor plans to conduct future analyses to rule out a hazard ratio risk margin of 1.3 after 500 and 700 MACE-plus have been observed in the canagliflozin development program."

*[verbatim, from FDA Statistical Review, efficacy section (Wei Liu, Ph.D.), §3.2, pp.11-12]*

> "The sponsor's pre-specified primary analysis of HbA1c used an analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) model using the last observation carried forward method (LOCF) for missing observations. In general, the ANCOVA model included terms for treatment and randomization stratification factor(s) (if applicable) as fixed effects and the corresponding baseline HbA1c value as a covariate... As an additional supportive analysis, change from baseline in HbA1c was analyzed using mixed model repeated measures (MMRM)... For each Phase 3 study, a pre-specified sequential testing procedure by the sponsor was applied to testing the treatment differences of the primary and major secondary efficacy endpoints, to control the family-wise error rate at 5%... in some studies, the testing proceeded to testing 2 families of tests using the Hochberg procedure for endpoints of SBP, HDL-C, TG, and HOMA2-%B (DIA3012 only), conditional upon the statistical significance of the prior test(s)."

*[verbatim, from FDA Approval Letter, §"POSTMARKETING REQUIREMENTS UNDER 505(o)," p.4]*

> "2027-5: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating the effect of canagliflozin on the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. The primary objective of the trial should be to demonstrate that the upper bound of the 2-sided 95% confidence interval for the estimated risk ratio comparing the incidence of MACE... observed with canagliflozin to that observed in the placebo group is less than 1.3."

Unlike alogliptin's PMR 2007-5 (which was essentially "finish the already-enrolled EXAMINE"), canagliflozin's approval letter schedule for PMR 2027-5 shows "Trial Completion: June 2017" — CANVAS itself would not complete for another four years, meaning approval was granted while the *entire* CVOT was still mid-conduct, not merely awaiting a final readout — a materially earlier-stage version of the same 2008-guidance CV-safety pattern seen in alogliptin/EXAMINE.

### 16. Riociguat (Adempas) — NDA 204819

**Sponsor:** Bayer HealthCare Pharmaceuticals

**Indication approved:** Two indications approved together: (1) persistent/recurrent chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) after surgical treatment, or inoperable CTEPH, to improve exercise capacity and WHO functional class; (2) pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH, WHO Group I) to improve exercise capacity, WHO functional class, and delay clinical worsening

**Approval date:** October 8, 2013

**Pivotal trial:** CHEST-1 (CTEPH), NCT00855465; PATENT-1 (PAH), NCT00810693

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; two separately-indicated pivotal trials in a single NDA
- *Endpoints:* continuous functional-capacity endpoint (6-minute walk distance)
- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA (contingent primary test), stratified Wilcoxon rank-sum test with Hodges-Lehmann estimator (actual primary test triggered by a failed Shapiro-Wilk normality check)
- *Multiplicity:* unadjusted secondary/supportive testing (single formal primary endpoint)
- *Regulatory:* FDA Advisory Committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- CHEST-1: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 261 adults with inoperable CTEPH (PVR>300 dyn·sec·cm⁻⁵, mPAP>25 mmHg, ≥90 days post full anticoagulation) or persistent/recurrent CTEPH ≥180 days after pulmonary endarterectomy; randomized to riociguat titrated to 2.5 mg tid (n=173) or placebo (n=88)
- PATENT-1: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 443 adults with symptomatic PAH (PVR>300, mPAP>25); randomized to riociguat titrated to 2.5 mg tid (n=254), an exploratory capped-titration 1.5 mg tid arm (n=63), or placebo (n=126)
- Primary endpoint in both trials: change from baseline in 6-minute walk distance (6MWD) at week 16 (CHEST-1) or week 12 (PATENT-1), using the ITT population, with the last observed value carried forward and worst-value/zero imputation applied for subjects who died or had clinical worsening before their final scheduled visit
- Pre-specified primary analysis: ANCOVA comparing pooled active-dose riociguat vs. placebo; the SAP specified that if the Shapiro-Wilk test found the ANCOVA residuals non-normal, the stratified Wilcoxon rank-sum test would instead be the formal test of statistical significance, with the Hodges-Lehmann estimator used for the treatment-effect point estimate/CI
- Secondary endpoints (both trials): change in WHO Functional Class, time to clinical worsening, Borg dyspnea score, quality-of-life measures; no formal multiplicity adjustment across secondary endpoints (single primary endpoint design)
- No interim analysis or alpha-spending plan (fixed-duration 12/16-week trials, not event-driven)
- CHEST-1 result: placebo-adjusted mean 6MWD increase of 46 m (95% CI 25-67; p<0.0001); Hodges-Lehmann median difference 39 m (95% CI 25-54)
- PATENT-1 result (2.5 mg arm): placebo-adjusted mean 6MWD increase of 36 m (95% CI 20-52; p<0.0001); Hodges-Lehmann median difference 29 m (95% CI 17-40)

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2013/204819Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2013/204819s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/204819Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Summary Review (Cross-Discipline Team Leader Review) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/204819Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- FDA Medical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/204819Orig1s000MedR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (CHEST-1) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00855465 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (PATENT-1) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00810693 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)
