### 32. Betrixaban (Bevyxxa) — NDA 208383

**Sponsor:** Portola Pharmaceuticals

**Indication approved:** Prophylaxis of venous thromboembolism (VTE) in adults hospitalized for an acute medical illness who are at risk for thromboembolic complications due to moderate or severe restricted mobility and other risk factors for VTE

**Approval date:** June 23, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** APEX, NCT01583218

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled, event-driven, mid-trial SAP amendment (population-enrichment protocol amendment mid-enrollment, splitting the primary analysis into progressively broader cohorts) (closest existing entry, "Mid-trial SAP amendment changing endpoint status," describes an endpoint-status change, not a population/cohort restructuring of this kind)
- *Endpoints:* composite VTE efficacy endpoint (asymptomatic proximal DVT, symptomatic DVT/PE, VTE-related death), major bleeding (safety)
- *Primary analysis:* relative risk on the primary efficacy outcome population (PEOP), by cohort
- *Multiplicity:* closed testing procedure across three progressively broader analysis cohorts (Cohort 1 elevated D-dimer only → Cohort 2 elevated D-dimer + age≥75 → full PEOP), each stage's result formally exploratory unless the prior stage was statistically significant
- *Regulatory:* Complete Response Letter not issued here, but a notable case of an FDA-approved efficacy claim resting on formally "exploratory" (not confirmatory) statistical results because the pre-specified first-stage cohort analysis narrowly missed significance

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Phase III, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-comparator trial; N=7,513 randomized 1:1 to extended-duration betrixaban (160 mg oral loading dose then 80 mg once daily for 35-42 days, plus subcutaneous placebo enoxaparin for 6-14 days) or standard-duration enoxaparin (40 mg subcutaneous once daily for 6-14 days, plus oral placebo betrixaban for 35-42 days); dose reductions (betrixaban 40 mg / enoxaparin 20 mg) were applied for severe renal insufficiency or concomitant strong P-gp inhibitor use
- Population: adults hospitalized for an acute medical illness (e.g., heart failure, respiratory failure, infection, rheumatic disease, ischemic stroke) with restricted mobility and elevated VTE risk
- Primary efficacy endpoint: a composite of asymptomatic proximal DVT (assessed day 32-47), symptomatic proximal or distal DVT, symptomatic non-fatal PE, or VTE-related death (day 1-42), analyzed in the pre-specified primary efficacy outcome population (PEOP: randomized patients who received ≥1 dose and were evaluable for every component of the primary endpoint; N=6,286, 3,112 betrixaban / 3,174 enoxaparin)
- **Mid-trial cascading-cohort restructuring**: after 35% enrollment, the protocol was amended to restrict further enrollment to higher-risk patients (elevated D-dimer ≥2× ULN or age ≥75), and the SAP was modified to define a closed hypothesis-testing procedure across three progressively broader analysis populations: Cohort 1 (elevated D-dimer only) as the first, formally primary, analysis; Cohort 2 (Cohort 1 plus age ≥75) as the second; and the full/overall PEOP as a final analysis — with the SAP specifying explicitly that Cohort 2 and the overall-population analyses would count as formal (confirmatory) results *only if* Cohort 1 reached one-sided significance at α=0.025, and would otherwise be exploratory only
- **Result: Cohort 1 narrowly missed significance.** The primary efficacy outcome occurred in 132/1,914 (6.9%) betrixaban patients vs. 166/1,956 (8.5%) enoxaparin patients in Cohort 1 (RR 80.6%, 95% CI 0.647-1.004, p=0.054) — because this crossed 1 (i.e., was not statistically significant under the pre-specified one-sided 0.025 threshold), the closed testing procedure formally rendered the Cohort 2 result (RR 80%, 95% CI 65.5%-97.7%) and the full-PEOP result (RR 76%, 95% CI 62.5%-92.3%) exploratory rather than confirmatory, even though both were numerically favorable and of a similar magnitude to Cohort 1
- FDA's benefit-risk conclusion rested on this exploratory (not formally confirmatory) efficacy result, supported by consistency across supportive analyses (the modified intent-to-treat population, D-dimer measured by a central laboratory instead of local labs, and an alternate ultrasound assessment window) and a documented but unadjusted caveat that the apparent dose-response pattern (80 mg outperforming a 40 mg reduced dose) was confounded, since dose level was assigned by baseline renal function/P-gp-inhibitor status rather than by randomization
- Primary safety endpoint (major bleeding): 25/3,716 (0.67%) betrixaban vs. 21/3,716 (0.57%) enoxaparin — similar overall rates, with a numerical increase in major GI bleeding (19 vs. 9) and a numerical decrease in major intracranial bleeding (2 vs. 7) on betrixaban; one fatal bleed occurred in each arm

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2017/208383Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/208383s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Summary Review ("Signatory Authority Review," the primary source for the cascading-cohort detail below) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/208383Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- FDA Medical Review (exists at the same URL pattern with `MedR.pdf`; not separately mined for this entry beyond confirming its existence)
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01583218 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)
- Pivotal publication: Cohen AT, et al. (APEX Investigators). "Extended Thromboprophylaxis with Betrixaban in Acutely Ill Medical Patients." *N Engl J Med.* 2016;375(6):534-544. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1601747), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27232649/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Extended%20Thromboprophylaxis%20with%20Betrixaban%20in%20Acutely%20Ill%20Medical%20Patients)

**Other resources**

- Portola Pharmaceuticals was acquired by Alexion Pharmaceuticals in 2020, which itself merged into AstraZeneca in 2021; no trial-specific IPD/Vivli availability confirmed here.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held for this NDA (see verbatim quote below).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, from FDA Summary Review, "Signatory Authority Review," Ref ID 4115764, p.3-4]*

> "While the study was ongoing (after 35% enrollment), the protocol was amended to enrich the study with high risk patients by restricting further enrollment to patients with elevated D-dimer ≥ 2 x ULN or age of 75 years or older. The statistical analysis plan was modified to establish two cohorts. Cohort 1 included patients who had an elevated baseline D-dimer level (i.e., at least two times the upper limit of the normal range). Cohort 2 included the patients in Cohort 1 plus those who were 75 years of age or older. In addition, a closed hypothesis testing procedure for the efficacy endpoints was established and the subgroup of patients in Cohort 1 was designated as the first primary efficacy analysis cohort. A second analysis population to be tested was Cohort 2, and a final analysis was defined as all evaluable patients (completed evaluation for every component of the primary endpoint) enrolled in the trial, formally if the initial hypothesis was tested statistically significant at 1-sided 0.025, and exploratory if not."

*[verbatim, from FDA Summary Review, Ref ID 4115764, p.11]*

> "The primary efficacy outcome in Cohort 1 of the PEOP occurred in 132/1914 (6.9%) patients of the betrixaban group and 166/1956 (8.5%) patients of the enoxaparin group, an absolute difference in event rate of 1.6%... The relative risk (RR) was 80.6% (95% CI [0.647, 1.004]). Since the analysis for the primary endpoint in cohort 1 failed to reach statistical significance (p=0.054) and based on the statistical analysis plan, the subsequent analyses are considered exploratory."

*[verbatim, from FDA Summary Review, Ref ID 4115764, p.4]*

> "Even though the pre-specified analysis did not meet the pre-specified testing criteria based on Cohort 1 of PEOP, the beneficial effect of betrixaban for Cohort 1 appeared to be supported by the results based on analyses using the modified Intent-to-Treat (mITT) population, D-dimer assessment per central laboratory measurement as well as different assessment window for the ultrasound evaluation... Based on these assessments, the benefit risk analysis appears favorable based on the reduction of VTE events during 35±7 day treatment period."

*[verbatim, from FDA Summary Review, Ref ID 4115764, p.~15, "Advisory Committee Meeting" section — quoted as written, including an apparent template/copy-paste artifact]*

> "9. Advisory Committee Meeting: This product was not taken to an Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee because there were no issues requiring discussion."

That reference to an *Oncologic* Drugs Advisory Committee (for a VTE-prophylaxis anticoagulant) is evidently a boilerplate template artifact carried over uncorrected from another review — worth flagging rather than silently correcting, since it is exactly what the FDA document says — but the substantive point stands regardless: no Advisory Committee meeting of any kind was held for this NDA, despite the closed-testing-procedure result being no less numerically borderline than many submissions that do go to committee.

### 33. Semaglutide (Ozempic) — NDA 209637 (original approval)

**Sponsor:** Novo Nordisk A/S

**Indication approved:** Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus

**Approval date:** December 5, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** SUSTAIN program (SUSTAIN 1-6; SUSTAIN 6, NCT01720446, is the dedicated cardiovascular outcomes trial)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (SUSTAIN 1, 5, 6) or open-label, active-controlled (SUSTAIN 2, 3, 4), non-inferiority-then-superiority (active-controlled trials), event-driven (SUSTAIN 6), dose-arm pooling considerations across two semaglutide doses
- *Endpoints:* change in HbA1c from baseline (primary, key efficacy trials), change in body weight (key secondary, key efficacy trials), 3-point MACE (primary, SUSTAIN 6), diabetic retinopathy complications (secondary safety signal, SUSTAIN 6)
- *Primary analysis:* mixed model for repeated measurements (MMRM) using on-treatment data (pre-specified), multiple imputation based on retrieved dropouts followed by ANCOVA (FDA-preferred, per pre-NDA meeting agreement), stratified Cox proportional-hazards model (SUSTAIN 6)
- *Multiplicity:* pre-specified hierarchical testing scheme controlling study-wise type I error across primary and confirmatory secondary endpoints in each trial, with semaglutide 1.0 mg tested before 0.5 mg within each endpoint
- *Missing data/bias:* retrieved-dropout multiple imputation (added at FDA's request at a 2016 pre-NDA meeting, after an earlier 2010 end-of-phase-2 agreement had permitted excluding post-discontinuation/rescue data from the primary analysis)
- *Regulatory:* FDA Advisory Committee meeting held October 18, 2017 (focused on the diabetic retinopathy safety signal)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Five key efficacy Phase 3 trials plus the cardiovascular outcomes trial supported NDA 209637: SUSTAIN 1 (monotherapy, placebo-controlled, double-blind, N=259, 30 weeks), SUSTAIN 2 (add-on to metformin/TZD, double-blind double-dummy vs. sitagliptin, N=1,231, 56 weeks), SUSTAIN 3 (add-on to 1-2 OADs, open-label vs. exenatide extended-release, N=813, 56 weeks), SUSTAIN 4 (add-on to metformin ± sulfonylurea in insulin-naive patients, open-label vs. insulin glargine, N=1,089, 30 weeks), SUSTAIN 5 (add-on to basal insulin ± metformin, double-blind, placebo-controlled, N=397, 30 weeks), and SUSTAIN 6 (the cardiovascular outcomes trial, double-blind, placebo-controlled, N=3,297, 104 weeks); all were randomized, parallel-group, multinational trials in adults with type 2 diabetes at two semaglutide doses (0.5 mg and 1.0 mg once weekly)
- Primary endpoint in the five key efficacy trials: change in HbA1c from baseline to end of the planned treatment period; key secondary endpoint: change in body weight from baseline; pre-specified primary analysis was an MMRM using on-treatment data (treatment, country, and stratification factors as fixed effects, baseline value as covariate, nested within visit, unstructured covariance) — at a June 2010 end-of-phase-2 meeting FDA had agreed that data collected after treatment discontinuation or rescue-medication initiation could be excluded from the primary analysis, but by the August 2016 pre-NDA meeting, in light of FDA's evolving missing-data guidance, the sponsor agreed to also perform a retrieved-dropout multiple-imputation analysis (multiple imputation within each arm using data from patients who returned for assessment after discontinuation, followed by an ANCOVA on the completed datasets); FDA's statistical reviewer considered this retrieved-dropout/ANCOVA analysis "more appropriate for labeling" than the sponsor's on-treatment MMRM
- Multiplicity: study-wise type I error was controlled via a pre-specified hierarchical testing scheme in each trial — placebo-controlled trials tested superiority for HbA1c directly, while active-controlled trials tested non-inferiority (margin 0.3%) before superiority, and where both semaglutide doses were studied, the 1.0 mg dose was tested before the 0.5 mg dose within each endpoint (with the exact ordering varying slightly by trial)
- Both doses of semaglutide demonstrated superiority to placebo (SUSTAIN 1, 5) and to active comparators sitagliptin and insulin glargine (SUSTAIN 2, 4) on the HbA1c primary endpoint, and semaglutide 1.0 mg also demonstrated superiority to exenatide ER (SUSTAIN 3); both doses demonstrated superiority to comparators on body-weight change across all five trials
- SUSTAIN 6 (NCT01720446) was designed and powered as a non-inferiority safety trial: randomized 1:1 (1,648 semaglutide, 1,649 placebo, both added to standard of care), event-driven, primary endpoint time to first 3-point MACE (CV death including unknown-cause death, non-fatal MI, non-fatal stroke), analyzed via a pre-specified stratified Cox proportional-hazards model, tested against the 2008 FDA Diabetes Guidance's 1.8 risk margin; pre-specified confirmatory secondary efficacy endpoints embedded in SUSTAIN 6 were change in body weight at week 104 and change in HbA1c at week 30 in two background-therapy subgroups (sulfonylurea monotherapy, premix insulin)
- SUSTAIN 6's result was unusual for a pre-approval CVOT of this class: 108 semaglutide vs. 146 placebo MACE events, HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.58-0.95) — not only ruling out the 1.8 margin but reaching nominal statistical significance in the beneficial direction, a signal the FDA statistical review treated as supportive safety evidence rather than a formal superiority claim, since the trial was designed and powered as a non-inferiority study; SUSTAIN 6 also identified a statistically significant increase in diabetic retinopathy complications (HR 1.76, 95% CI 1.11-2.78), which the sponsor argued post hoc was mediated by the magnitude of early HbA1c reduction — a finding FDA's reviewer treated with caution given the post hoc, covariate-adjusted nature of that explanatory analysis

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2017/209637Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (2017 original) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/209637lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (combined document covering both the SUSTAIN 6 cardiovascular/retinopathy safety evaluation and the five-trial glycemic-efficacy evaluation) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209637Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Summary Review (documents the Advisory Committee meeting) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209637Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record for SUSTAIN 6 — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01720446 (no protocol/SAP documents posted; note Novo Nordisk has posted SAP/protocol documents through a redaction pipeline that strips inter-word spacing for at least one other trial in this census, semaglutide/Wegovy's SELECT — no equivalent posting was found for SUSTAIN 6)
- Pivotal publications: Marso SP, Bain SC, Consoli A, et al. (SUSTAIN-6 Investigators). "Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes." *N Engl J Med.* 2016;375(19):1834-1844. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1607141), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27633186/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Semaglutide%20and%20Cardiovascular%20Outcomes%20in%20Patients%20with%20Type%202%20Diabetes); Ahren B, Masmiquel L, Kumar H, et al. "Efficacy and safety of once-weekly semaglutide versus once-daily sitagliptin as an add-on to metformin, thiazolidinediones, or both, in patients with type 2 diabetes (SUSTAIN 2)." *Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol.* 2017;5(5):341-354. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S2213-8587(17)30092-X>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28385659/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Efficacy%20and%20safety%20of%20once-weekly%20semaglutide%20versus%20once-daily%20sitagliptin%20SUSTAIN%202)

**Other resources**

- Novo Nordisk IPD access via Novo Nordisk's own clinical trial data-sharing portal and/or Vivli.org; trial-specific SUSTAIN availability not individually confirmed here.
- An FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held October 18, 2017, focused on the diabetic retinopathy safety signal from SUSTAIN 6 alongside the overall benefit-risk assessment.
- This is a distinct, separate NDA/submission from the semaglutide/Wegovy SELECT cardiovascular-outcomes entry already in this census (NDA 215256/S-011, approved 2024) — same active ingredient, different product/dose/indication and an entirely different pivotal trial and review record.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, from FDA Statistical Review, Reference ID 4145686, Executive Summary (SUSTAIN 6 section)]*

> "SUSTAIN 6 was an event-driven trial designed and powered to demonstrate the non-inferiority of semaglutide relative to placebo, both added on to standard-of-care, for the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE)... SUSTAIN 6 was designed to test whether the upper bound of the 95% confidence interval for the hazard ratio of MACE associated with semaglutide met the 1.8 risk margin specified by the 2008 FDA Diabetes Guidance... The pre-specified stratified Cox proportional hazards model for the primary MACE analysis estimated a hazard ratio of 0.74 with an associated 95% confidence interval of (0.58, 0.95) associated with semaglutide. The upper bound of 0.95 ruled out the risk margin of 1.8... The results of SUSTAIN 6 suggest that semaglutide is not associated with increased cardiovascular risk relative to placebo."

*[verbatim, from FDA Statistical Review, Reference ID 4145686, retinopathy section]*

> "The pre-specified Cox proportional hazards model for the secondary endpoint of diabetic retinopathy complications obtained a hazard ratio of 1.76 with 95% confidence interval of (1.11, 2.78) associated with semaglutide... The Sponsor conducted a post hoc analysis to further assess the effect of semaglutide on retinopathy risk. This post hoc analysis resulted in an estimated hazard ratio of semaglutide relative to placebo of 1.22 with 95% confidence interval of (0.71, 2.09)... We caution that the results of this post hoc analysis may have limitations and should be interpreted with caution."

*[verbatim, from FDA Statistical Review, Reference ID 4138507, Executive Summary (glycemic-efficacy section)]*

> "The pre-specified primary analysis was a mixed model for repeated measurements (MMRM) analysis using on-treatment data. MMRM rarely estimates a relevant causal effect in the presence of missing data. The applicant also performed multiple imputation based on data from retrieved dropouts followed by an analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) model... The statistical reviewer thinks results from this analysis are more appropriate for labeling."

*[verbatim, from FDA Statistical Review, Reference ID 4138507, §3.2.2 "Statistical Methodologies"]*

> "Following FDA's advice at the pre-NDA meeting, the applicant performed retrieved dropout analysis for the HbA1c and body weight endpoints... The study-wise type I error was controlled for the primary and confirmatory secondary endpoints using a pre-specified hierarchical testing scheme. For the placebo-controlled key efficacy trials, superiority testing for change in HbA1c was performed. For the active-controlled key efficacy trials, testing of non-inferiority for change in HbA1c was performed before testing for superiority. The pre-specified non-inferiority margin was 0.3%. For the key efficacy trials with two semaglutide doses, semaglutide 1.0 mg was tested before semaglutide 0.5 mg within each endpoint."

This original Ozempic approval is a useful counterpart to the SELECT/Wegovy entry already in the census: it shows FDA's missing-data preferences evolving over the course of a single development program — an MMRM-with-exclusion approach agreed at a 2010 end-of-phase-2 meeting was superseded, by the time of the 2016 pre-NDA meeting, by a request for retrieved-dropout multiple imputation, which the reviewer then treated as the more labeling-appropriate estimate — and it documents an unusual case (SUSTAIN 6) where a trial designed only to rule out cardiovascular harm nonetheless produced a nominally significant benefit signal that FDA's review treated as supportive rather than confirmatory, alongside a genuine safety signal (retinopathy) that reached the opposite, unfavorable conclusion.

### 34. Ertugliflozin (Steglatro) — NDA 209803

**Sponsor:** Merck Sharp & Dohme Corp. (developed jointly with Pfizer)

**Indication approved:** Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus

**Approval date:** December 19, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** VERTIS program (7 confirmatory trials; representative trial VERTIS MONO, Study P003), plus VERTIS CV, NCT01986881, as the required (then-ongoing) cardiovascular outcomes trial

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (5 of 7 studies) or active-controlled (2 of 7, vs. glimepiride), non-inferiority-then-superiority (active-controlled study), full factorial design (one study), simultaneous submission of a monotherapy NDA and two fixed-dose-combination NDAs sharing pooled trial evidence
- *Endpoints:* change in HbA1c from baseline (primary, all 7 studies), change in fasting plasma glucose and systolic blood pressure (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* constrained longitudinal data analysis (cLDA)/MMRM-type model for the continuous HbA1c endpoint
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence hierarchical testing at family-wise one-sided α<0.025 in all seven studies, Hochberg step-up procedure nested within the hierarchy for two blood-pressure sub-endpoints in the active-controlled non-inferiority study
- *Missing data/bias:* extensive pre-submission FDA correspondence (2014-2015) on missing-data prevention and analysis method, given that none of the sponsor's trials followed patients for efficacy after treatment discontinuation
- *Regulatory:* approval granted while the dedicated cardiovascular outcomes trial (VERTIS CV) was still ongoing, consistent with the 2008 FDA Diabetes Guidance's framework for approving glycemic-control claims on an interim cardiovascular risk-margin basis pending a postmarketing-committed CVOT

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Seven confirmatory Phase III trials (Merck/Pfizer internal codes P001-P003, P005-P007, P017) supported this NDA, all randomized, double-blind (with double-dummy blinding where an active comparator was used), evaluating ertugliflozin 5 mg and 15 mg once daily; some of the same trials also supported simultaneously-submitted fixed-dose-combination NDAs for ertugliflozin/sitagliptin (Steglujan, NDA 209805) and ertugliflozin/metformin (Segluromet, NDA 209806)
- Study P002 was a 52-week non-inferiority trial of ertugliflozin 15 mg and 5 mg vs. glimepiride (active comparator), with change in HbA1c at 52 weeks as the primary endpoint (non-inferiority margin 0.3%, the same margin FDA had previously accepted for empagliflozin/Jardiance, NDA 204629); Study P005 was a five-arm full-factorial trial of ertugliflozin + sitagliptin combinations vs. each component alone; the remaining studies (P001, P003, P006, P007, P017) were 26-week placebo-controlled trials in monotherapy or add-on settings, including one dedicated stage-3 chronic kidney disease safety/efficacy trial (P001)
- Primary endpoint in all seven studies: change in HbA1c (%) from baseline; FDA's statistical review documents a multi-year missing-data dialogue with the sponsor beginning under the original IND (106447): in January 2014 FDA advised that "the number of subjects not measured for the primary endpoint should be kept to a minimum," in October 2014 FDA specified detailed protocol expectations for preventing and documenting missing data, and in June 2015 FDA's reviewer noted that none of the sponsor's eight Phase 3 trials followed the intention-to-treat principle in the strict sense, since subjects were not followed for efficacy after stopping study drug
- Multiplicity: all seven studies used a fixed-sequence hierarchical testing strategy to control the one-sided type I error rate at α<0.025; within Study P002's hierarchy specifically, a Hochberg step-up procedure governed two systolic blood pressure sub-endpoints (ertugliflozin 15 mg and 5 mg each vs. glimepiride), with hierarchical testing of subsequent endpoints proceeding only if both, one (via the Hochberg rule), or neither SBP comparison reached significance according to a defined decision rule
- Primary-endpoint analyses across all seven studies except the renal-impairment trial (P001, a safety/tolerability-focused study) demonstrated statistically significant superiority (placebo-controlled studies) or non-inferiority-then-superiority (active-controlled Study P002) of ertugliflozin for HbA1c reduction
- A dedicated cardiovascular outcomes trial, VERTIS CV (NCT01986881, "Cardiovascular Outcomes Following Ertugliflozin Treatment in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Participants With Vascular Disease"), randomizing ertugliflozin 5 mg, 15 mg, and placebo (approximately 1,340 per arm) in patients with established vascular disease, was described in the 2017 FDA statistical review as still ongoing (estimated completion October 2019) at the time of this approval — meaning cardiovascular safety was established at approval only via the pre-specified interim risk-margin framework under the 2008 FDA Diabetes Guidance, not via a completed dedicated outcomes trial; VERTIS CV's results were reported several years after this approval

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2017/209803Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/209803s000lbl.pdf
- FDA combined Statistical Review (covers NDA 209803 ertugliflozin monotherapy plus the related NDA 209805/209806 fixed-dose-combination submissions filed the same day) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209803,209805,209806Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA combined Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209803,209805,209806Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record for VERTIS CV — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01986881 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)
- Pivotal publication: Terra SG, Focht K, Davies M, et al. "Phase III, efficacy and safety study of ertugliflozin monotherapy in people with type 2 diabetes mellitus inadequately controlled with diet and exercise alone." *Diabetes Obes Metab.* 2017;19(5):721-728. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1111/dom.12888), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28116776/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Phase%20III%2C%20efficacy%20and%20safety%20study%20of%20ertugliflozin%20monotherapy%20in%20people%20with%20type%202%20diabetes%20mellitus)

**Other resources**

- Merck and Pfizer generally participate in clinical-trial data-sharing (Merck via the Merck Data Sharing portal and/or Vivli.org); trial-specific availability not individually confirmed here.
- No evidence of an FDA Advisory Committee meeting for this NDA was found in the sources reviewed.
- Same pharmacologic class (SGLT2 inhibitor) as empagliflozin/EMPA-REG OUTCOME and dapagliflozin/DECLARE-TIMI 58, both already in this census; unlike those two entries (both CV-outcome-indication supplements built on completed CVOTs), this is the original glycemic-control NDA, approved before ertugliflozin's own CVOT had read out.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, from FDA Statistical Review, Reference ID 4144831, §2.1.2 "Select Submission History and Communication to Sponsor," FDA comments to sponsor under IND 106447, October 2014]*

> "Considerable efforts should be made in order to avoid any missing data. Measurements on HbA1c at key time-points should be taken for all study subjects regardless of adherence to therapy or study protocol. A sizable amount of missing data will impact our confidence in study findings... It is therefore critical that extensive efforts are made to prevent missing data... The protocol should (1) describe the procedures that will be in place to prevent missing data which should include training the site investigator, (2) collect the reason for missing data, when it does occur, and (3) describe the assumptions that went into the choice of the primary analysis method."

*[verbatim, from FDA Statistical Review, Reference ID 4144831, June 2015 FDA comment under IND 106447]*

> "None of the sponsor's eight phase 3 trials were designed to support an analysis that follows the ITT principle since subjects were not followed for efficacy after stopping treatment."

*[verbatim, from FDA Statistical Review, Reference ID 4144831, "Multiple Testing Procedure"]*

> "All seven studies use a hierarchical testing strategy to control Type 1 Error rate at α < 0.025, one-sided. The order of the hierarchical testing for each study is shown in Table 2. Within the hierarchical testing for Study P002, the Hochberg procedure is used for the SBP endpoints: E15 vs. glimepiride and E5 vs. glimepiride. If previous endpoints in the hierarchical testing order are all significant at p < 0.025 one-sided, then testing for the two SBP endpoints proceeds as follows: 1) The two p-values for the SBP tests are ordered from largest to smallest. 2) If the highest of the two p-values is < α1=0.025 (one-sided), then SBP for both E5 and E15 vs. glimepiride are declared significant, and hierarchical testing proceeds to the next test (superiority for HbA1c). 3) If the highest p-value is >0.025 one-sided, but the other p-value is < α2=0.0125 one-sided, then only the endpoint with p-value < 0.0125 is declared statistically significant. The hierarchical testing stops, and no further endpoints are tested."

*[verbatim, from FDA Statistical Review, Reference ID 4139753, on VERTIS CV's status at the time of this NDA's review]*

> "P004/B1521021 is a Phase 3 trial titled: 'Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-Controlled, Parallel-Group Study to Assess Cardiovascular Outcomes Following Treatment with Ertugliflozin (MK-8835/PF-04971729) in Subjects with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Established Vascular Disease, The VERTIS CV Study'... This trial is ongoing. According to clinicaltrials.gov, the start date is 04 November 2013 and estimated completion date for this trial is October 31, 2019."

The FDA reviewer's multi-year, quoted-verbatim correspondence with the sponsor on missing-data prevention (2014-2015, under the pre-NDA IND) is unusually well-documented for this census and reflects the same post-2009 FDA missing-data-guidance shift visible in the lixisenatide/Adlyxin entry above — by this point in the SGLT2/GLP-1 development era, FDA's statistical reviewers were routinely pushing sponsors toward stronger missing-data prevention and more defensible imputation assumptions well before NDA submission, rather than only raising the issue during review.

### 35. Angiotensin II (Giapreza) — NDA 209360

**Sponsor:** La Jolla Pharmaceutical Company

**Indication approved:** To increase blood pressure in adults with septic or other distributive shock

**Approval date:** December 21, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** ATHOS-3 (LJ501-CRH01), NCT02338843

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel 2-arm
- *Endpoints:* targeted MAP responder rate at hour 3 (primary), change in cardiovascular and total SOFA scores at hour 48 (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* logistic regression with baseline covariates (chi-square test)
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence hierarchical testing (primary endpoint → CV SOFA → total SOFA)
- *Missing data/bias:* worst-case (treatment failure) imputation for death, last-observation-carried-forward for other missing values, multiple imputation as a sensitivity analysis
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* single unblinded interim analysis at 150 evaluable patients, reviewed by an independent DSMB
- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held ("outside expertise was not necessary")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ATHOS-3 was a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel two-arm Phase III trial in adult patients with catecholamine-resistant hypotension (CRH) — distributive/vasodilatory shock (predominantly septic shock, 80.7% of patients) remaining hypotensive despite fluid resuscitation and standard vasopressor therapy, hospitalized in an ICU setting; 344 patients were enrolled and 321 comprised the modified intent-to-treat (mITT) population (all patients who received study drug: 158 placebo, 163 angiotensin II)
- Primary efficacy endpoint: "targeted MAP" response at hour 3, defined as achieving a mean arterial pressure ≥75 mmHg or an increase of ≥10 mmHg from baseline, without an increase in the dose of background (non-study) vasopressors (total norepinephrine-equivalent dose); analyzed via a logistic regression model adjusted for baseline MAP (<65 vs. ≥65 mmHg), APACHE II score, vasopressin use in the 6 hours before randomization, and average norepinephrine-equivalent dose in the 6 hours before randomization, on the mITT population
- Secondary endpoints: change in cardiovascular (CV) SOFA score and change in total SOFA score, both from screening to hour 48; CV SOFA analyzed via a stratified van Elteren (stratified Wilcoxon) rank test adjusting for baseline MAP, screening APACHE II score, and screening SOFA score; total SOFA analyzed via an adjusted general linear model including all randomization strata
- Sample size: 315 patients planned, based on a hypothesized responder rate of 40% (placebo) vs. 60% (angiotensin II), a two-by-two chi-square test at two-sided α=0.05, giving 90% power to demonstrate superiority
- Multiplicity: a fixed hierarchical testing strategy preserved the overall type I error across the primary and two secondary endpoints, tested in the order: primary endpoint (targeted MAP responder rate) → change in CV SOFA at hour 48 → change in total SOFA at hour 48
- Missing-data handling: for the primary and secondary endpoints, a patient's death before assessment was treated as a treatment failure for the primary responder endpoint, and assigned the worst possible score (CV SOFA = 4, total SOFA = 24) for the SOFA secondary endpoints; missing values for reasons other than death used last-observation-carried-forward as the primary imputation method for the primary endpoint, with multiple imputation performed as a sensitivity analysis
- An interim analysis was conducted after 150 evaluable patients had data through day 28, with blinded pooled data reviewed in open session (including sponsor representatives) and unblinded analyses reviewed only by an independent statistician and the DSMB per its charter
- Result: the primary responder rate was 69.9% (114/163) with angiotensin II vs. 23.4% (37/158) with placebo (adjusted odds ratio 7.95, 95% CI 4.76-13.3, p=2.54×10⁻¹⁵); the CV SOFA secondary endpoint reached significance (mean change -1.75 vs. -1.28, p=0.0129) but the total SOFA secondary endpoint did not (p=0.4901 by the general linear model), so under the pre-specified hierarchy no further endpoints beyond total SOFA were formally tested

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/209360s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209360Orig1s000StatR.pdf

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1704154), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28528561/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Angiotensin%20II%20for%20the%20Treatment%20of%20Vasodilatory%20Shock)

**Other resources**

- La Jolla Pharmaceutical Company was acquired by Innoviva in 2020; no trial-specific IPD/Vivli availability confirmed here.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held for this NDA: the approval letter states plainly, "Your application for Angiotensin II was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary; there were no controversial issues that would benefit from an advisory committee discussion."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, from FDA Statistical Review, Reference ID 4185106, §1.2 "Brief Overview of Clinical Studies"]*

> "This NDA is intended to obtain approval of an indication for the treatment of CRH based on a phase 3, placebo-controlled, randomized, double-blind, multicenter study of LJPC-501 in patients with CRH. The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the effect of LJPC-501 infusion on mean arterial pressure (MAP). The primary efficacy endpoint was clinical response at 3 hours as defined by achieving a MAP of at least 75 mmHg or 10 mmHg above baseline without increasing other vasopressor doses."

*[verbatim, from FDA Statistical Review, Reference ID 4185106, §3.2.3 "Efficacy Measures and Analyses"]*

> "Primary efficacy endpoint (targeted MAP at Hour 3): A logistic regression was used for the primary endpoint analysis adjusted by fixed covariates of baseline MAP (<65 mmHg vs ≥65 mmHg), Acute Physiologic Assessment and Chronic Health Evaluation (APACHE) II score, vasopressin use over the 6 hours prior to randomization (yes vs no), and average norepinephrine equivalent dose over the 6 hours prior to randomization using modified intent-to-treat (mITT, all patients who received study drug) population... Multiplicity: Hierarchical testing strategy was applied to preserve Type 1 error across the primary and secondary efficacy endpoints in the following order: significant treatment effect for the primary efficacy hypothesis; change in CV SOFA at Hour 48; and change in Total SOFA scores at Hour 48... Handling missing data: Missing primary and secondary endpoints due to death: A failure was assigned to missing primary endpoint. A CV SOFA score of 4 and a Total SOFA scores of 24, the highest scores for the respective endpoints were assigned to missing SOFA scores. Missing primary and secondary endpoints for reasons other than death: In the mITT population, the last observed MAP value was carried forward as a primary imputation method. Multiple imputation was used as a sensitivity analysis for the primary endpoint in the mITT analysis population... Interim analysis: An interim analysis was conducted after data for 150 evaluable patients through Day 28 were collected. Blinded data using data pooled across the 2 treatment arms were reviewed by the open-session participants including La Jolla representatives. Unblinded data analyses including tables, figures, and listings were provided by an independent statistician to the DSMB for review of efficacy and safety according to the DSMB Charter."

*[verbatim, from FDA Statistical Review, Reference ID 4185106, §3.2.7-3.2.8]*

> "This reviewer was able to confirm the sponsor's primary and secondary endpoints analyses and concurred with the results. There seems no statistical issue that may have impact on the interpretation of the study results... The study seems to support the superiority of LJPC-501 in increasing MAP."

ATHOS-3/Giapreza is one of the more straightforward single-trial submissions in this census statistically (a single Phase III RCT with a short, mechanistically direct physiological primary endpoint rather than a long-term clinical-outcome composite), but it is also one of the only entries where the FDA statistical reviewer raised no substantive issues at all with the sponsor's design or conduct — a useful contrast with the multiplicity, missing-data, and interim-analysis controversies documented elsewhere in this batch (e.g., betrixaban/APEX, lixisenatide/GetGoal, ertugliflozin/VERTIS).

### 36. Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate (Lokelma) — NDA 207078

**Sponsor:** AstraZeneca Pharmaceuticals LP (originally developed by ZS Pharma, Inc., acquired by AstraZeneca in 2015)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of hyperkalemia in adults, with a labeled Limitation of Use that it should not be used as an emergency treatment for life-threatening hyperkalemia because of its delayed onset of action.

**Approval date:** May 18, 2018 (this NDA had a prior review cycle: original submission May 26, 2015; Complete Response Letter issued March 16, 2017; resolved by a complete-response amendment submitted November 22, 2017)

**Pivotal trial:** HARMONIZE (ZS-004), NCT02088073, supported by ZS-003 (NCT01737697) and open-label ZS-005 (NCT02163499)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; randomized-withdrawal design (open-label or single-arm acute-correction phase followed by re-randomization of responders to active-drug-continuation doses vs. placebo for a maintenance phase) **; cross-study pooling of efficacy evidence across a dose-finding trial (ZS-002), a randomized-withdrawal trial (ZS-003), and the pivotal randomized-withdrawal trial (ZS-004/HARMONIZE)
- *Endpoints:* serum-biomarker exponential-rate-of-change endpoint (acute phase) and longitudinal LS-mean serum-potassium endpoint (maintenance phase) **
- *Primary analysis:* longitudinal random-slopes mixed model (SAS PROC MIXED) fit to log-transformed serum potassium, with least-squares means for treatment comparison **
- *Multiplicity:* closed testing procedure (dose order high-to-low within each study)
- *Missing data/bias:* not addressed in detail in the public FDA review
- *Regulatory:* Complete Response Letter (CRL) followed by resubmission and approval; reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ZS-004/HARMONIZE: Phase III, randomized, quadruple-masked (participant/care provider/investigator/outcomes assessor), placebo-controlled trial with an open-label acute correction phase followed by a double-blind, placebo-controlled 28-day randomized-withdrawal maintenance phase; 258 patients enrolled, requiring two consecutive point-of-care potassium readings ≥5.1 mmol/L within 1 day of first dose; excluded dialysis, cardiac arrhythmia requiring immediate treatment, life expectancy <3 months, and recent use of other potassium-binding resins
- ZS-003: Phase III, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with an analogous two-part acute (48-hour) plus subacute randomized-withdrawal structure across four sodium zirconium cyclosilicate doses (1.25/2.5/5/10 g)
- Primary endpoint, acute phase (ZS-002/ZS-003): the difference in the exponential rate of change in serum potassium during the initial 48 hours of treatment, placebo vs. drug
- Primary endpoint, maintenance phase (ZS-004/HARMONIZE, exact label wording): "the mean serum potassium value over the period from Day 8 to Day 29, comparing LOKELMA treated and placebo treated patients," estimated as the model-based least-squares mean of all available serum-potassium values during Study Days 8-29
- Secondary endpoints (HARMONIZE): total number of normokalemic days during Days 8-29; proportion of subjects normokalemic at Day 29/exit; standard deviation of serum potassium during maintenance
- Statistical methods: longitudinal mixed models (SAS PROC MIXED) with unstructured covariance, subject as a random effect, and fixed effects for treatment, baseline potassium, age category, and RAAS-inhibitor/CKD/heart-failure/diabetes indicators; each of the three studies used a closed testing procedure ordering doses from highest to lowest for the primary endpoint, but FDA's review found no pre-specified multiple-comparison procedure had actually been defined for ZS-003's secondary endpoints despite the sponsor's SAP asserting a closed testing procedure "as previously detailed"
- No formal efficacy interim analysis is described for these trials in the public FDA review; a DSMB in the early dose-finding study (ZS-002) reviewed safety only between escalating-dose cohorts

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/207078s000lbl.pdf

- Pivotal publication (HARMONIZE): Kosiborod M, Rasmussen HS, Lavin P, et al. "Effect of Sodium Zirconium Cyclosilicate on Potassium Lowering for 28 Days Among Outpatients With Hyperkalemia: The HARMONIZE Randomized Clinical Trial." *JAMA.* 2014;312(21):2223-2233. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2014.15688), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25402495/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Effect%20of%20Sodium%20Zirconium%20Cyclosilicate%20on%20Potassium%20Lowering%20for%2028%20Days%20Among%20Outpatients%20With%20Hyperkalemia)
- Supporting publication (ZS-003): Packham DK, Rasmussen HS, Lavin PT, et al. "Sodium Zirconium Cyclosilicate in Hyperkalemia." *N Engl J Med.* 2015;372(3):222-231. - No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held for this application.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review (207078Orig1s000StatR.pdf), quoting the ZS-003 SAP, p.36-37]*

> "Secondary efficacy endpoints will include S-K at all time points, time to normalization of S-K [...], time to first decrease in S-K of 0.5 mmol/l, and proportion of subjects who achieve normalization in S-K levels at the end of 24 and 48 hours" (Acute Phase). "[...] maintaining normokalemic control [...], time to a 0.5 mmol/l increase, and time to relapse [...], which will serve as the lead secondary efficacy endpoints" (Subacute Phase).

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §5.1 "Statistical Issues"]*

> "No multiple comparison procedure was pre-specified for the secondary endpoints in Study ZS-003. The overall type I error was not controlled and analysis for the secondary endpoints in Study ZS-003 can only be viewed as exploratory."

This is a clean example of a reviewer-documented gap between what the sponsor's SAP asserted (a closed testing procedure "as previously detailed") and what the SAP actually pre-specified (only the primary endpoint's testing order), leaving the secondary endpoints of one of the three supporting trials without type-I-error control.

### 37. Tafamidis meglumine (Vyndaqel) — NDA 211996

**Sponsor:** Pfizer Inc. (via FoldRx Pharmaceuticals, a wholly owned Pfizer subsidiary); reviewed jointly with the companion NDA 212161 (Vyndamax, tafamidis free acid), both approved the same day from one combined FDA review package

**Indication approved:** Treatment of the cardiomyopathy of wild-type or hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis (ATTR-CM) in adults, to reduce cardiovascular mortality and cardiovascular-related hospitalization.

**Approval date:** May 3, 2019

**Pivotal trial:** ATTR-ACT, NCT01994889 (protocol B3461028)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven trial; dose-arm pooling (20 mg and 80 mg tafamidis pooled into a single comparison vs. placebo, 1:2:2 randomization)
- *Endpoints:* patient-reported outcomes / HRQoL (KCCQ-Overall Summary); key secondary endpoint (6-Minute Walk Test, KCCQ-OS)
- *Primary analysis:* Finkelstein-Schoenfeld hierarchical composite (rank-based) method, prioritizing all-cause mortality then frequency of cardiovascular-related hospitalization within randomization strata **; Cox proportional-hazards model (mortality component); mixed model for repeated measurements (6MWT, KCCQ-OS); Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test (TTR stabilization)
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (primary → 6MWT → KCCQ-OS)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* none — no formal efficacy interim analysis was planned; Data Monitoring Committee (DMC/DSMB) for safety only
- *Missing data/bias:* multiple imputation sensitivity analysis (primary endpoint); pattern-mixture model sensitivity analysis (key secondary endpoints)
- *Regulatory:* regular approval grounded in a single adequate and well-controlled trial, per FDA's single-study evidence guidance **

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Phase III, multicenter, international, randomized, quadruple-masked, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial; 441 subjects randomized 1:2:2 to placebo (n=177), tafamidis 20 mg (n=88), or tafamidis 80 mg (n=176) once daily for 30 months plus standard of care; stratified by variant vs. wild-type TTR genotype and baseline NYHA class (I/II combined vs. III); heart/liver transplant or cardiac mechanical assist device implantation during the trial was treated as equivalent to death for the primary analysis
- Primary endpoint (exact SAP wording): "a hierarchical combination applying the method of Finkelstein-Schoenfeld... to: (1) All-cause mortality, and (2) Frequency of cardiovascular-related hospitalizations over the duration of the trial"
- Key secondary endpoints: change from baseline to Month 30 in 6-Minute Walk Test distance; change from baseline to Month 30 in KCCQ-Overall Summary score, tested only if the primary analysis was significant
- Other secondary endpoints: CV-related mortality, frequency of CV-related hospitalization, all-cause mortality, TTR stabilization at Month 1
- Sample size/power: no closed-form solution existed for the Finkelstein-Schoenfeld primary analysis, so sample size was determined by simulation assuming a 12.5% vs. 25.0% all-cause mortality rate (tafamidis vs. placebo) and 1.5 vs. 2.5 mean CV-related hospitalizations over 30 months; 400 subjects were targeted for approximately 90% power at two-sided alpha=0.05 (a more conservative 30%-mortality-reduction assumption still yielded ~80% power at 300 subjects)
- No formal efficacy interim analysis was planned; an external DMC monitored unblinded safety data (mortality, hospitalizations, adverse events, labs) only, with no efficacy stopping boundary
- Finkelstein-Schoenfeld mechanics: every pair of subjects within the same randomization stratum is compared — if both died, the longer survivor "wins"; if one died and the other survived, the survivor wins; if both survived, the subject with fewer CV-related hospitalizations wins; transplant/mechanical-assist-device subjects were handled the same as deaths, and a subject censored before Month 30 with unknown vital status was compared using hospitalization frequency up to the shorter of the two subjects' follow-up times
- Multiplicity: statistical significance of the two key secondary endpoints depended on first achieving significance on the primary endpoint, then the 6MWT result had to be significant (p≤0.05) before KCCQ-OS could be formally tested — a strict fixed-sequence gatekeeping structure with no separate adjustment across doses because the two tafamidis doses were pooled by design for the primary comparison
- Missing data: no imputation was used for the primary Finkelstein-Schoenfeld analysis itself, but a multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis (Rubin's method) was pre-specified; the key secondary endpoints (MMRM-based, which handles missingness implicitly) were also checked via a pattern-mixture-model sensitivity analysis grouping subjects by their missing-data pattern

- Pivotal publication: Maurer MS, Schwartz JH, Gundapaneni B, et al; ATTR-ACT Study Investigators. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1805689), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30145929/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Tafamidis%20Treatment%20for%20Patients%20with%20Transthyretin%20Amyloid%20Cardiomyopathy)

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held; the Summary Review states the applications "did not raise significant public health questions... outside expertise was not deemed necessary."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP §6.1.1, Version 5, January 30, 2018]*

> "The primary analysis uses a hierarchical combination applying the method of Finkelstein-Schoenfeld (Finkelstein 1999) to: (1) All-cause mortality, and (2) Frequency of cardiovascular-related hospitalizations over the duration of the trial, which is defined as the number of times a subject is hospitalized (ie, admitted to a hospital) for cardiovascular-related morbidity."

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP §8.1.1]*

> "If both subjects are dead, then the subject with a longer survival time is assigned +1... If one subject is alive and the other is not, the live subject receives a +1... If both subjects are alive, the comparison uses cardiovascular-related hospitalization... The subject with the fewer cardiovascular related hospitalization (frequency) receives a +1."

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP §8.2.2]*

> "Statistical significance of the key-secondary analyses is dependent on first achieving statistically significant results in the primary analysis. In this hierarchical approach... the change from Baseline to Month 30 in distance walked during the 6MWT is first tested at the 0.05 level. If the p-value for the test of 6MWT is ≤0.05, the 2nd variable... KCCQ Overall Summary score will be tested at the 0.05 level."

With these assumptions, 300 subjects... yields a power of over 90%... increasing the number of subjects to 400... yields a power of approximately 90%."

> "ATTR-ACT, as a single adequate and well controlled study, is sufficient to provide evidence of effectiveness without supporting information from a second study."

### 38. Bempedoic acid (Nexletol) — NDA 211616

**Sponsor:** Esperion Therapeutics, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adjunct to diet and maximally tolerated statin therapy for the treatment of adults with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH) or established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) who require additional lowering of LDL-C; label carries a Limitations of Use statement that the effect of bempedoic acid on cardiovascular morbidity and mortality had not been determined at the time of this approval.

**Approval date:** February 21, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** CLEAR Harmony, NCT02666664 (co-pivotal with CLEAR Wisdom, NCT02991118; FDA's Integrated Review analyzed the two together as a "High CV Risk Pool")

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; dual-pivotal-trial submission reviewed as a pooled high-CV-risk population without a formal statistical pooling of the primary test **
- *Endpoints:* percent-change-from-baseline continuous lipid-biomarker endpoint (LDL-C) **
- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA with a heterogeneous-variance mixed-model implementation and Kenward-Roger denominator degrees of freedom **
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing
- *Missing data/bias:* FDA-conducted washout (non-MAR) imputation disputing the sponsor's pattern-mixture missing-at-random assumption **
- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan

**Trial design & endpoints**

- CLEAR Harmony: Phase III, multicenter, randomized 2:1, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial billed by its own SAP as evaluating "the long-term safety and tolerability of ETC-1002 in high cardiovascular (CV) risk patients with hyperlipidemia (patients with underlying HeFH and/or ASCVD)"; randomization stratified by HeFH status and baseline statin intensity via IWRS; 2230 patients randomized (1488 bempedoic acid / 742 placebo), 52 weeks
- CLEAR Wisdom: same design family, same stratification factors, 779 patients randomized (522/257), 52 weeks; FDA's Integrated Review treated both trials together as the pivotal "High CV Risk" pool, distinct from two smaller/shorter supportive trials (CLEAR Serenity, CLEAR Tranquility) in statin-intolerant populations that were not part of the pivotal evidence
- Primary efficacy endpoint: percent change from baseline to Week 12 in LDL-C
- Key secondary endpoints, tested in a pre-specified step-down order: percent change from baseline to Week 24 in LDL-C; percent change to Week 12 in non-HDL-C, total cholesterol, apolipoprotein B, and high-sensitivity CRP
- Sample size was driven primarily by safety power (≥95% power to detect adverse-event rates observed in a reference PCSK9-inhibitor safety study) rather than by an efficacy power calculation, consistent with the trial's title as a long-term safety/tolerability study; no interim analysis was planned, though an external DMC monitored safety only
- Primary analysis method: ANCOVA with treatment group and randomization stratum as fixed effects and baseline LDL-C as a covariate, implemented as a mixed model with a treatment-arm-heterogeneous residual variance structure and Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom; missing data handled by a sponsor pattern-mixture imputation (early discontinuers assumed to revert toward placebo-like LDL-C levels), with treatment effects from multiply imputed datasets combined via Rubin's method
- CLEAR Outcomes, a dedicated cardiovascular outcomes trial, was ongoing at the time of this NDA and not part of the approval basis; FDA's review explicitly notes no CVOT data were submitted with this application

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, CLEAR Harmony SAP §3.3.1/§4.4/§4.5/§5.3]*

> "This is a Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group study evaluating the long-term safety and tolerability of ETC-1002 in high cardiovascular (CV) risk patients with hyperlipidemia (patients with underlying HeFH and/or ASCVD)... Percent change from baseline to Week 12 in LDL-C [is the primary efficacy endpoint]... No interim analysis is planned for this study... The primary and key secondary efficacy endpoints will be included in a step-down testing procedure to control overall type I error. Below endpoints will be tested sequentially at alpha level of 0.05. Each endpoint will be tested only if the previous endpoint achieved statistical significance."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review §6.2.3 "Analyses of Primary Endpoint," p.37-38]*

> "The Applicant analyzed the percent change in LDL-C using an analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) model with treatment, randomization strata, and baseline value as covariates. Missing data were imputed using a pattern mixture model, where subjects who discontinued treatment were considered to have similar post-discontinuation LDL-C levels as subjects on placebo, i.e., assuming that the data for subjects on treatment was missing at random. The review team does not agree with the assumption that subjects who discontinued treatment early will have similar post-discontinuation biomarker levels as placebo. Therefore, for subjects in the treatment group, we conducted washout imputations without missing at random assumption... Results from an ANCOVA model fit to the imputed datasets were analyzed and combined using Rubin's method."

This is a clean example of an FDA statistical reviewer independently re-deriving a sensitivity analysis specifically to test a missing-data assumption it disagreed with, rather than simply accepting the sponsor's pattern-mixture model — and reaching the same qualitative conclusion under a stricter (non-MAR) assumption.

### 39. Vericiguat (Verquvo) — NDA 214377

**Sponsor:** Merck Sharp & Dohme Corp.

**Indication approved:** To reduce the risk of cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization following a hospitalization for heart failure or need for outpatient IV diuretics, in adults with symptomatic chronic heart failure and ejection fraction less than 45%; carries a boxed warning for embryo-fetal toxicity.

**Approval date:** January 19, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** VICTORIA, NCT02861534

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven trial
- *Endpoints:* CV death / HF-hospitalization composite
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified or with covariates), Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (two secondary-endpoint families)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Hwang-Shih-DeCani alpha-spending function, Data Monitoring Committee (DMC/DSMB)
- *Missing data/bias:* standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment; sponsor-cancelled pre-specified interim analysis (event-rate-driven), reviewed by FDA for type-I-error impact **
- *Regulatory:* cross-trial safety-signal review using a pre-specified subgroup analysis, corroborated by a related-population trial **

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Randomized 1:1, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, double-blind, event-driven, multicenter trial ("A Randomized Parallel-Group, Placebo-Controlled, Double-Blind, Event-Driven, Multi-Center Pivotal Phase III Clinical Outcome Trial"), stratified by geographic region and race (6 strata) via IWRS; 5050 patients randomized (2526 vericiguat / 2524 placebo) at 694 sites in 42 countries (8% US), conducted September 2016 to September 2019
- Population: adults ≥18 with chronic HF, NYHA class II-IV, LVEF <45%, elevated natriuretic peptides, and a recent HF decompensation (HF hospitalization within 6 months, or outpatient IV diuretics within 3 months without hospitalization)
- Primary efficacy endpoint: time to first occurrence of the composite of CV death or HF hospitalization, with all events adjudicated by a blinded Clinical Events Committee; subjects without an event censored at last available information, date of non-CV death, or the primary-analysis database cutoff (June 18, 2019), whichever occurred first
- Secondary endpoints tested in two fixed-sequence families: Family 1 = components of the primary endpoint (time to CV death; time to first HF hospitalization); Family 2 = time to total (recurrent) HF hospitalizations via an Andersen-Gill model, time to composite of all-cause mortality or HF hospitalization, and time to all-cause mortality
- Sample size driven by the CV-death component: assuming an 11% comparator 12-month CV-death rate and a 20% relative risk reduction (HR 0.8), the design targeted 4872 subjects and 782 CEC-confirmed CV deaths for 80% power on that component, with ~98% power projected for the composite primary endpoint (23% assumed comparator event rate); one-sided significance level 0.025, stratified log-rank test with matching stratified Cox model for the HR/CI
- One efficacy interim analysis was planned at ~75% of the target CV deaths (587 events) using a Hwang-Shih-DeCani (γ=-6.5) alpha-spending boundary requiring significance on both the composite endpoint and the CV-death component (nominal one-sided p<0.0049 at interim, p<0.0242 at final); a co-timed futility rule used a simple HR threshold (HR>0.95 primary AND HR>1.0 CV death simultaneously)
- The sponsor cancelled both the efficacy and futility interim analyses before unblinding, because a higher-than-expected CV-death event rate meant the interim look would have occurred too close to the planned final analysis; FDA, the DSMB, and site investigators were informed of the decision, and the interim-related multiplicity adjustments were removed from the final analysis

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §5.2.9]*

> "However, the interim analyses were cancelled by the applicant prior to the unblinded interim analysis due to a higher than expected CV death event rate that would cause the efficacy interim analysis to be too close to the final analysis... The decision to cancel the interim analyses was made by the applicant and Executive Committee (EC)... The Agency, Data & Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB), and the trial site investigators were informed of the applicant's decision. Statistical analysis procedures and the multiplicity adjustments for the secondary endpoints related to the interim analysis were removed."
>
> "Reviewer's Comment: Given that the applicant's decision to cancel the interim analyses was based on the total number of CV death events that occurred before unblinding the interim analysis data, this decision did not seem to affect the efficacy results and therefore the type I error rate."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, Executive Summary]*

> "The major clinical review issue for this NDA was related to information suggesting that CV death and sudden cardiac death (SCD) occurred more frequently in some vericiguat-treated subjects... we observed and were concerned that in VICTORIA, a higher incidence of CV death occurred in vericiguat-treated patients compared to the placebo-treated patients in the subset of those in the highest baseline NT-proBNP quartile (>5300 pg/mL, N=1201, 208 deaths [34%] vs.169 deaths [29%])... Of note, the subgroup analysis of the primary efficacy outcome by NT-proBNP quartile was pre-specified in the VICTORIA statistical analysis plan. In a post hoc analysis, it was further concerning that a strong/significant interaction was seen for the outcome of CV death by the presence versus absence of an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) at baseline (HR: 0.69 [0.55,0.88] vs. HR: 1.06 [0.90,1.25], interaction p=0.004)."

The NT-proBNP-quartile subgroup finding is notable precisely because the reviewer traces it back to a pre-specified SAP subgroup analysis rather than a post hoc finding, while explicitly flagging the ICD interaction as post hoc — a clear example of an FDA review distinguishing pre-specified from exploratory subgroup evidence within the same safety concern.

### 40. Evinacumab-dgnb (Evkeeza) — BLA 761181

**Sponsor:** Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adjunct to other LDL-C-lowering therapies for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH); the label states the safety and effectiveness of evinacumab have not been established outside this population.

**Approval date:** February 11, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** R1500-CL-1629 ("ELIPSE HoFH"), NCT03399786

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group; small ultra-rare-disease trial population (65 randomized)
- *Endpoints:* percent-change-from-baseline continuous lipid-biomarker endpoint (LDL-C) **
- *Primary analysis:* mixed-effect model with repeated measures (MMRM), with population-weighted least-squares means to handle stratification-factor imbalance
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (key secondary lipid endpoints)
- *Missing data/bias:* multiple imputation (Markov Chain Monte Carlo, 100 datasets) combined via Rubin's rules, under a missing-not-at-random assumption that treatment discontinuers revert toward their own baseline
- *Regulatory:* none notable beyond standard BLA review

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study; patients received evinacumab 15 mg/kg IV every 4 weeks or matching placebo for a 24-week double-blind treatment period, stratified by apheresis treatment status (yes/no) and region (Japan vs. rest of world), followed by a 24-week open-label extension in which all patients received evinacumab
- Only 65 patients were randomized (43 evinacumab, 22 placebo) — reflecting the ultra-rare nature of homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia — with just two adolescent patients enrolled in the double-blind period; FDA's statistical reviewer flagged this small adolescent subset as a specific limitation and deferred to the clinical team on adequacy of evidence for that age group
- Primary efficacy endpoint: percent change in calculated LDL-C from baseline to Week 24 (ITT estimand — analyzed regardless of adherence to treatment or use of subsequent lipid-lowering therapies)
- Key secondary endpoints, tested via a fixed hierarchical sequence: percent change in Apolipoprotein B, non-HDL-C, and total cholesterol at Week 24; proportion of patients achieving ≥30% and ≥50% reductions in calculated LDL-C; absolute change in calculated LDL-C
- Sample size: 57 patients (38 evinacumab, 19 placebo) were calculated to give 90% power (two-sample t-test, two-sided alpha=0.05) to detect a 38-percentage-point treatment difference in mean percent LDL-C change, assuming a common SD of 35%, inflated for a 5% non-evaluable rate and 15% dropout
- Primary analysis: MMRM using all post-baseline data from Weeks 2 through 24, with fixed effects for treatment, randomization strata, time point, treatment-by-time and strata-by-time interactions, and baseline LDL-C (plus its interaction with time) as a continuous covariate; unstructured within-patient covariance, REML/Newton-Raphson estimation, Satterthwaite degrees of freedom; within-group least-squares means were weighted by the population's observed stratum proportions rather than equally, to handle imbalance across the small stratification cells
- Missing-data sensitivity analysis used a pattern-mixture-style multiple imputation: patients who stopped treatment were assumed to see LDL-C return toward their own baseline value (not toward the observed on-treatment trajectory), 100 completed datasets generated via SAS PROC MI (MCMC), combined via PROC MIANALYZE / Rubin's formulae — a stricter, non-missing-at-random assumption than a naive MAR imputation
- The one-step, two-step analysis structure meant the double-blind primary/key-secondary testing was fully concluded (alpha remained at the full 0.05) before any open-label-period data were used, and open-label results were summarized descriptively only, with no further formal hypothesis testing

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP §4.7.1, Version 1.0]*

> "The primary endpoint is the percent change in calculated LDL-C from baseline to week 24. The primary endpoint is defined as: 100x (calculated LDL-C value at week 24 - calculated LDL-C value at baseline)/calculated LDL-C value at baseline... The calculated LDL-C at week 24 will be the LDL-C value obtained within the week 24 efficacy analysis window, regardless of adherence to treatment and subsequent therapies (intent-to-treat [ITT] estimand)."

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP §5.7.1, "Analysis of Primary Efficacy Variable"]*

> "The model will include the fixed categorical effects of treatment group (evinacumab versus placebo), randomization strata (apheresis [Yes/No] and region [Japan, Rest of World]), time point (weeks 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, and 24), treatment-by-time point interaction, and strata-by-time point interaction, as well as the continuous fixed covariates of baseline calculated LDL-C value and baseline value-by-time point interaction... Within treatment group least-square means and standard errors will be adjusted using weights equal to the observed proportion of patients in strata variable levels across the study population (i.e. 'population weight'), rather than equal weights."

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP §5.8, "Adjustment for Multiple Comparison"]*

> "In order to handle multiple key secondary endpoints during the DBTP for the comparison of the evinacumab group and the placebo group, the overall type-I error will be controlled by the use of a hierarchical inferential approach. Statistical significance of the primary parameter at the 0.05 alpha level is required before drawing inferential conclusions about first key secondary parameter."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, "Summary and Conclusions"]*

> "There were no major statistical issues that would impact or change the overall conclusions. The amount of missing data was small throughout the study and the sensitivity analyses using the pre-specified [pattern-mixture-model] approach supported the robustness of the primary efficacy results... The study population primarily consisted of adults ≥18 years and included only two adolescent patients for the double-blind treatment period. Because of the small number of adolescent patients in the study population, we have concerns whether this provides sufficient data to support approval for adolescent patients. We defer to the clinical team to determine the adequacy of indication for adolescent patients."

### 41. Dasiglucagon (Zegalogue) — NDA 214231

**Sponsor:** Zealand Pharma A/S

**Indication approved:** Treatment of severe hypoglycemia in pediatric and adult patients with diabetes aged 6 years and above.

**Approval date:** March 22, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** ZP4207-16137, NCT03378635 (adults), with supporting pivotal trials ZP4207-17145, NCT03688711 (adults, autoinjector device) and ZP4207-17086, NCT03667053 (pediatric, ages 6-17)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group; three co-pivotal trials (two adult, one pediatric) sharing an identical primary endpoint and analysis method
- *Endpoints:* time-to-recovery endpoint (time to plasma glucose recovery, a beneficial rather than hazardous time-to-event outcome)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, Kaplan-Meier estimation, Cox proportional-hazards model (descriptive, used only when the proportional-hazards assumption held)
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (primary endpoint then eight key secondary endpoints in a pre-specified order)
- *Missing data/bias:* standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment (subjects requiring rescue IV glucose censored as "not recovered" at 45 minutes), with sensitivity analyses varying the censoring rule
- *Regulatory:* none notable beyond standard NDA review

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ZP4207-16137: Phase III, randomized, double-blind, parallel trial in adults with type 1 diabetes, comparing a single subcutaneous 0.6 mg dose of dasiglucagon to placebo (with a GlucaGen active-comparator arm included for assay sensitivity, but not part of the inferential testing hierarchy) during a hypoglycemic clamp procedure; 170 subjects randomized
- ZP4207-17145: analogous adult trial evaluating dasiglucagon delivered via an autoinjector device
- ZP4207-17086: analogous pediatric trial (ages 6-17) with the same primary/key-secondary structure
- Primary endpoint (identical across all three pivotal trials, exact wording): "Time to plasma glucose recovery. Plasma glucose recovery is defined as first increase in plasma glucose of ≥20 mg/dL (1.1 mmol/L) from baseline during the hypoglycemic clamp procedure without administration of rescue IV glucose"
- Key secondary endpoints 1-4: plasma glucose recovery within 30, 20, 15, and 10 minutes after study drug injection without rescue IV glucose; key secondaries 5-8: plasma glucose change from baseline within those same four windows
- Primary analysis: Kaplan-Meier estimates stratified by treatment group and injection site; treatment difference evaluated via a two-sided log-rank test stratified by injection site; subjects requiring rescue IV glucose were censored as "not recovered" at 45 minutes after dosing, with sensitivity analyses both omitting this censoring rule and censoring at the actual time of rescue administration; a Cox proportional-hazards model was fit descriptively only when a graphical proportional-hazards check passed and no more than two-thirds of recovery times were censored in either arm
- Multiplicity: a strict fixed-sequence hierarchical procedure tested the primary endpoint first, then key secondaries 1-4, then key secondaries 5-8, each at the two-sided 0.05 level, proceeding only as long as each prior test in the sequence was significant; the GlucaGen-vs-placebo comparisons were explicitly excluded from this inferential hierarchy, serving only to support assay sensitivity for the dasiglucagon-vs-placebo comparisons
- FDA's statistical review, covering all three pivotal trials plus a supportive trial (17084), found the median time to recovery with dasiglucagon was approximately 10 minutes versus over 35 minutes with placebo, and concluded there was no major statistical issue with the efficacy evaluation across the pooled pediatric and adult evidence

> "Primary: To demonstrate superiority of dasiglucagon compared to placebo following a single subcutaneous 0.6 mg dose administered to subjects with type I diabetes mellitus with insulin-induced hypoglycemia... Plasma glucose recovery is defined as first increase in plasma glucose of ≥20 mg/dL (1.1 mmol/L) from baseline during the hypoglycemic clamp procedure without administration of rescue IV glucose."

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP §4.7.1, "Hierarchical testing procedure"]*

> "For the confirmatory analyses, the following a priori defined hierarchical inferential test order will be applied for the control of the type 1 error rate across the planned multiple comparisons... inference will proceed at the two sided 0.05 criterion significance level until the first failure to reject the null hypothesis for a dasiglucagon versus placebo comparison: Primary: Time to plasma glucose recovery. Key secondaries 1-4: Plasma glucose recovery within 30 minutes, within 20 minutes, within 15 minutes, and within 10 minutes... Key secondaries 5-8: Plasma glucose changes from baseline within 30 minutes, within 20 minutes, within 15 minutes, and within 10 minutes... The GlucaGen versus placebo comparisons will not be included in the inferential testing hierarchy, since the efficacy of GlucaGen is previously established, and these comparisons are intended to support the validity of the study for the dasiglucagon versus placebo comparisons."

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP §4.7.2.1, "Primary analysis"]*

> "The primary endpoint will be summarized using Kaplan-Meier (KM) estimates stratified by treatment group and injection site. The treatment group difference between dasiglucagon and placebo will be evaluated inferentially using a two-sided log-rank test stratified by injection site... Those subjects who receive IV glucose will be censored (and set to 'not recovered') at 45 minutes after dosing."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, "Summary and Conclusions"]*

> "All three pivotal efficacy trials (Trials 16137, 17145 and 17086) demonstrated the superiority of dasiglucagon compared to placebo in time to plasma glucose recovery from insulin-induced hypoglycemia... The median time to recovery in the dasiglucagon was significantly shorter than one in the placebo group (10 minutes versus over 35 minutes)."
