### 42. Finerenone (Kerendia) — NDA 215341

**Sponsor:** Bayer HealthCare Pharmaceuticals Inc.

**Indication approved:** To reduce the risk of sustained eGFR decline, end-stage kidney disease, cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, and hospitalization for heart failure in adult patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) associated with type 2 diabetes (T2D).

**Approval date:** July 9, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** FIDELIO-DKD, NCT02540993

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, event-driven trial
- *Endpoints:* renal composite endpoint (primary); CV death / HF-hospitalization-type composite (key secondary); all-cause mortality (as a distinct secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test, Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified), Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Multiplicity:* Bonferroni-Holm sequentially rejective procedure (weighted variant, applied to the primary renal composite and a family of ordered secondary endpoints)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design with a single interim analysis at 2/3 information fraction, non-binding early-stopping-for-success rule
- *Missing data/bias:* standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment, with a defined time-window rule for events occurring near a missed clinic visit
- *Regulatory:* none notable beyond standard NDA review; no FDA statistical/clinical review package found publicly posted for this NDA

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter, event-driven trial in patients with type 2 diabetes and CKD at high risk of progressing to end-stage renal disease, stratified by region, eGFR category, and albuminuria category
- Primary efficacy endpoint: time to first occurrence of a composite of onset of kidney failure, a sustained decrease in eGFR of ≥40% from baseline over at least 4 weeks, or renal death, with all events adjudicated by an independent committee
- Secondary objectives, tested in a pre-specified hierarchy after the primary and a key secondary CV composite: time to first occurrence of a CV mortality/morbidity composite endpoint (key secondary); time to all-cause mortality; time to all-cause hospitalization; change in urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) from baseline to Month 4; time to first occurrence of a second renal composite using a more stringent ≥57% eGFR-decline threshold (rather than ≥40%) plus kidney failure or renal death
- Sample size/power: the trial was designed to accrue 1068 primary-endpoint events for at least 90% power (two-sided logrank test at a nominal significance level reflecting the interim-analysis adjustment), assuming a 20% relative risk reduction (true HR 0.80) and an annual placebo event rate of 12%; with an assumed 44-month total study duration (33-month recruitment, 11-month minimum treatment for the last-recruited patient), approximately 4690 subjects were planned for randomization
- One interim analysis was planned at 2/3 of the target information (event count), with a non-binding stopping rule for early success: if the trial stopped early, both the primary and key secondary CV endpoints would be tested at a two-sided 0.270% significance level, after which the remaining secondary endpoints (in the fixed order above) would also be tested at 0.270%; if the trial continued to its planned final analysis, a weighted Bonferroni-Holm procedure allocated adjusted alpha levels between the primary renal composite (0.03282695 or 0.04967388, depending on which endpoint reached significance first) and the key secondary CV composite (0.01576184 or 0.04967388) to preserve the overall two-sided 5% significance level, with the remaining secondary endpoints tested only if both the primary and key secondary CV endpoints achieved formal significance
- Primary analysis: stratified log-rank test (region, albuminuria type, and eGFR category as strata) against the null hypothesis of equal hazard functions between finerenone and placebo within every stratum; hazard ratio and 95% CI estimated via a stratified Cox proportional-hazards model (SAS PROC PHREG, Efron method for ties); Kaplan-Meier curves for cumulative incidence by treatment group
- Censoring: subjects without a primary-endpoint event were censored at the date of their last visit with complete information on all components of the composite, with a defined rule extending the censoring window up to one day before the next planned clinic visit (maximum ~5 months) to capture kidney-failure/renal-death events occurring between visits

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP §2, Protocol No. BAY 94-8862/16244]*

> "The primary objective of this study is to: Demonstrate whether, in addition to standard of care (SoC), finerenone is superior to placebo in delaying the progression of kidney disease, as measured by the composite endpoint of time to first occurrence of kidney failure, a sustained decrease in eGFR of ≥40% from baseline over at least 4 weeks, or renal death."

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP §4.7, "Testing procedure and multiplicity adjustment"]*

> "If the decision will be not to stop the study early for success, the final primary analyses will be performed as follows: A group sequential design with a single interim analysis when 2/3 of the information is available with a stopping rule of two-sided p<0.00270 requires a small adjustment to the final analysis... The weighted Bonferroni-Holm procedure will be used for the hierarchical testing of the primary and secondary efficacy endpoints with the following adjusted alpha levels, which apply for an information fraction of 2/3: If the primary renal composite endpoint achieves statistical significance at a two-sided p value ≤ 0.03282695, the secondary CV endpoint will be tested at the two sided 0.04967388 level. Alternatively, if the secondary CV endpoint achieves statistical significance at a two sided p value ≤ 0.01576184, the primary renal composite endpoint will be tested at the two-sided 0.04967388 level. Only if both the renal and CV endpoints achieve formal statistical significance, the remaining secondary endpoints will be tested at a two-sided level of 0.04967388 according to the hierarchy above."

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP §6.2.1.1, "Primary efficacy variable: primary analysis"]*

> "The primary efficacy variable is the time to first occurrence of the composite endpoint of onset of kidney failure, a sustained decrease of eGFR ≥ 40% from baseline over at least 4 weeks, or renal death. All events classifying for the primary endpoint have to be adjudicated positively by an independent adjudication committee... The test statistic of the stratified logrank test compares the observed number of events with the number of events expected under the null hypothesis H0 in each treatment group per stratum."

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP §2, sample size]*

> "A total of 1068 primary efficacy endpoint events will have a minimum 90% power to demonstrate superiority of finerenone to placebo using a logrank test at a two sided significance level of 3.3333%, assuming a 20% relative risk reduction, i.e. a true hazard ratio of 0.80... the planned total number of subjects to be randomized is estimated to be 4690 subjects."

### 43. Inclisiran (Leqvio) — NDA 214012

**Sponsor:** Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation (trials originally conducted by The Medicines Company, acquired by Novartis in January 2020)

**Indication approved:** Adjunct to diet and maximally tolerated statin therapy for the treatment of adults with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH) or clinical atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) who require additional lowering of LDL-C; label states the effect of inclisiran on cardiovascular morbidity and mortality had not been determined at approval.

**Approval date:** December 22, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** ORION-10 (NCT03399370) and ORION-11 (NCT03400800), with ORION-9 (NCT03397121) as a third co-pivotal trial in a different population

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group; cross-trial pooled/integrated analysis of three independently conducted, identically designed trials in different but related populations (HeFH vs. ASCVD vs. ASCVD-risk-equivalent)
- *Endpoints:* co-primary endpoints (percent change in LDL-C to Day 510, and time-averaged percent change in LDL-C from Day 90 to Day 540)
- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA on multiply imputed datasets, combined via Rubin's method
- *Multiplicity:* nested (fixed-sequence) testing procedure between the two co-primary endpoints
- *Missing data/bias:* multiple imputation washout model (missing-not-at-random) for the Day-510 co-primary endpoint; control-based pattern-mixture model for the time-averaged co-primary endpoint
- *Regulatory:* none notable beyond standard NDA review

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ORION-9, -10, and -11 were three separately conducted, similarly designed Phase III, randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, each stratified by current use of statins/other lipid-modifying therapy (ORION-9 and -11 also stratified by country; ORION-10 was US-only); ORION-9 enrolled patients with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia, ORION-10 enrolled US patients with ASCVD and elevated LDL-C, and ORION-11 enrolled patients with ASCVD or ASCVD-risk equivalents (including type 2 diabetes and familial hypercholesterolemia) despite maximally tolerated lipid-lowering therapy
- Co-primary endpoints (identical across all three trials): (1) percentage change in LDL-C from baseline to Day 510; (2) time-adjusted percentage change in LDL-C from baseline after Day 90 and up to Day 540 (a measure of steady-state effect once the drug's twice-yearly maintenance dosing regimen begins at Day 90)
- Statistical hypotheses were tested using a nested (fixed-sequence) procedure: the family-wise two-sided type-I error rate of 0.05 was preserved by testing the Day-510 co-primary endpoint first, and only if that null hypothesis was rejected (superiority claimed) was the time-adjusted co-primary endpoint tested, also at a two-sided 0.05 level; secondary endpoints were not tested at all if either co-primary endpoint's null hypothesis failed to be rejected
- Key secondary endpoints: absolute change in LDL-C from baseline to Day 510; time-adjusted absolute change from Day 90 to Day 540; percentage change to Day 510 in PCSK9, total cholesterol, ApoB, and other lipid parameters
- LDL-C was measured using a "reflexive" approach: calculated LDL-C (Friedewald formula) was used unless it was below 40 mg/dL, triglycerides exceeded 400 mg/dL, or the calculated value was missing, in which case directly measured (ultracentrifugation) LDL-C was substituted
- Primary analysis for the Day-510 co-primary endpoint: ANCOVA (treatment group and baseline LDL-C as fixed effects) fit to 100 multiply imputed datasets, with missing values imputed via a multiple-imputation "washout model," and treatment effects combined across the 100 analyses using Rubin's method (SAS PROC MIANALYZE)
- Primary analysis for the time-adjusted co-primary endpoint: a control-based pattern-mixture model (following Ratitch and O'Kelly, 2011) assumed that subjects who discontinued the study without further follow-up would have outcomes similar to placebo-arm subjects with similar baseline characteristics (a missing-not-at-random assumption), while subjects with only intermittent missing data were imputed under a missing-at-random assumption
- Sample size: approximately 1425 evaluable subjects (across placebo and inclisiran 300 mg arms, ~5% assumed dropout) were calculated to provide more than 90% power to detect a 30% reduction in LDL-C at a two-sided alpha of 0.025 (per trial)
- FDA's statistical review analyzed all three trials together, noting each trial's independent primary result was consistent (percent LDL-C reduction at Day 510: -47.89% [ORION-9], -52.34% [ORION-10], -49.80% [ORION-11], all with non-overlapping 95% CIs vs. zero) and that its own re-analysis, with minor imputation-related differences (within 1% of the applicant's results), corroborated the sponsor's findings across all three trials

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2021/214012Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (original, December 2021) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2021/214012lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (posted under the 2022 year folder despite the December 2021 approval date) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/214012Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov records — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03399370 (ORION-10), https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03400800 (ORION-11), https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03397121 (ORION-9); all three have genuine Protocol and SAP documents posted
- Protocol / SAP (ORION-10, dated September 13, 2019) — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/70/NCT03399370/SAP_001.pdf
- Pivotal publication (ORION-10/ORION-11): Ray KK, Wright RS, Kallend D, et al. "Two Phase 3 Trials of Inclisiran in Patients with Elevated LDL Cholesterol." *N Engl J Med.* 2020;382(16):1507-1519. > "The co-primary endpoints for this study are: Percentage change in LDL-C from baseline to Day 510. Time adjusted percentage change in LDL-C from baseline after Day 90 and up to Day 540. This is the average percentage change in LDL-C from baseline over the period after Day 90 and up to Day 540... There were no major statistical issues found in the review of this submission... Based on these findings, we recommend approval for the requested indication."

### 44. Mavacamten (Camzyos) — NDA 214998

**Sponsor:** MyoKardia, Inc. (acquired by Bristol Myers Squibb in 2020, prior to approval)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adults with symptomatic New York Heart Association (NYHA) class II-III obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM), to improve functional capacity and symptoms.

**Approval date:** April 28, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** EXPLORER-HCM (MYK-461-005), NCT03470545

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group
- *Endpoints:* composite functional responder endpoint (pVO2 improvement paired with NYHA class improvement, or a larger pVO2 improvement alone); patient-reported outcomes / HRQoL (KCCQ clinical summary score, HCMSQ shortness-of-breath subscore)
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (five ordered secondary endpoints, gated behind the primary responder endpoint)
- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation for the composite responder endpoint (early discontinuers/unassessable patients counted as non-responders); no imputation for MMRM-based continuous secondary endpoints
- *Regulatory:* no FDA statistical review found publicly posted for this NDA (only a Clinical Pharmacology Review was located)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial in adults with symptomatic obstructive HCM; 251 patients randomized, stratified by NYHA class (II or III), current beta-blocker use, exercise-testing ergometer type, and consent to a cardiac MRI substudy
- Primary efficacy endpoint: a composite clinical-response responder endpoint at Week 30, defined as achieving either (1) an improvement of at least 1.5 mL/kg/min in peak oxygen consumption (pVO2) by cardiopulmonary exercise testing together with a reduction of at least one NYHA class, or (2) an improvement of at least 3.0 mL/kg/min in pVO2 with no worsening of NYHA class
- Secondary endpoints, tested via a strict fixed sequential order gated behind the primary endpoint (each tested only if the prior one in the sequence was significant): (1) change from baseline to Week 30 in post-exercise LVOT peak gradient; (2) change from baseline to Week 30 in pVO2; (3) proportion of patients with at least one NYHA class improvement; (4) change from baseline to Week 30 in KCCQ clinical summary score; (5) change from baseline to Week 30 in HCMSQ shortness-of-breath subscore
- Sample size/power: 220 participants (110 per arm) were planned assuming a 25-percentage-point difference in the clinical-responder rate between mavacamten and placebo (50% responder rate observed for mavacamten in the Phase II PIONEER-HCM study vs. an assumed 25% placebo rate), giving 96% power at a two-sided 5% significance level; participants who terminated early or could not be assessed for clinical response at Week 30 were counted as non-responders in the primary analysis
- Multiplicity control (exact wording): if the primary endpoint was not statistically significant, none of the secondary endpoint tests were considered statistically significant regardless of their nominal p-values; conditional on primary-endpoint significance, the five secondary endpoints above were tested sequentially at a two-sided alpha of 0.05
- FDA's only publicly posted review document for this NDA is a Clinical Pharmacology Review (no separate Statistical Review, Medical Review, Summary Review, or combined Multi-Discipline/Integrated Review was found under the standard Drugs@FDA URL patterns for any year folder from 2022 through 2025)

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2022/214998s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Clinical Pharmacology Review (the only individual review document publicly posted for this NDA) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/214998Orig1s000ClinPharmR.pdf

- Protocol / SAP (Version 2.0) — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/45/NCT03470545/SAP_001.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Olivotto I, Oreziak A, Barriales-Villa R, et al; EXPLORER-HCM study investigators. "Mavacamten for treatment of symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (EXPLORER-HCM): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial." *Lancet.* 2020;396(10253):759-769. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(20)31792-X>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32871100/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Mavacamten%20for%20treatment%20of%20symptomatic%20obstructive%20hypertrophic%20cardiomyopathy%20EXPLORER-HCM)

> "Primary Efficacy Endpoints: The primary efficacy endpoint was a clinical response at Week 30 defined as achieving: 1. An improvement of at least 1.5 mL/kg/min in pVO2 as determined by cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) and a reduction of one or more class in NYHA class OR 2. An improvement of 3.0 mL/kg/min or more in pVO2 with no worsening in NYHA class."

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP §5]*

> "Approximately 220 participants will be randomized, with 110 participants in each of the 2 groups... If the primary endpoint is not statistically significantly different between treatment groups, none of the tests for secondary endpoints will be considered statistically significant despite the nominal p-values. Change from baseline to Week 30 in post-exercise LVOT peak gradient. 2. Change from baseline to Week 30 in pVO2 as determined by CPET. 3. Proportion of subjects who had at least 1 class of NYHA improvement from baseline at Week 30. 4. Change from baseline to Week 30 in patient-reported health-related QoL as assessed by the KCCQ-23 CSS. 5. Change from baseline to Week 30 in patient-reported severity of HCM symptoms as assessed by the HCMSQ SoB subscore."

### 45. Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) — NDA 215866

**Sponsor:** Eli Lilly and Company

**Indication approved:** Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide [GIP] / glucagon-like peptide-1 [GLP-1] receptor agonist).

**Approval date:** May 13, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** SURPASS program — SURPASS-1 (NCT03954834), SURPASS-2 (NCT03987919), SURPASS-3 (NCT03882970), SURPASS-4 (NCT03730662), and SURPASS-5 (NCT04039503)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind (tirzepatide doses blinded; some trials open-label as to active comparator), placebo-controlled and active-controlled variants across five co-pivotal trials; dose-arm program (5/10/15 mg tirzepatide tested in parallel across all five trials)
- *Endpoints:* HbA1c change from baseline (primary, all five trials); key secondary endpoints included incidence of HbA1c<7% and <5.7%, change in body weight, and change in fasting serum glucose
- *Primary analysis:* MMRM-type mixed models with ANCOVA-style fixed effects (country, baseline HbA1c category, and trial-specific covariates)
- *Multiplicity:* graphical alpha-propagation method (Bretz/Maurer sequentially rejective graphical testing procedure), applied per trial across multiple tirzepatide doses and multiple endpoints
- *Missing data/bias:* return-to-baseline / retrieved-dropout imputation for missing primary-endpoint measures, informed by data from patients who discontinued treatment but remained in follow-up
- *Regulatory:* FDA-conducted CV meta-analysis across the Phase II/III program as part of the original review

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Five Phase III, multicenter, multinational, randomized, parallel-arm trials, each comparing three once-weekly tirzepatide doses (5, 10, 15 mg, following an identical dose-escalation scheme) against a different comparator: SURPASS-1 (double-blind, placebo-controlled, monotherapy, 1:1:1:1, N=478); SURPASS-2 (open-label as to comparator but double-blind across tirzepatide doses, active-controlled vs. semaglutide 1 mg, both as add-on to metformin, 1:1:1:1, N=1879); SURPASS-3 (active-controlled vs. insulin degludec, add-on to metformin +/- SGLT2i); SURPASS-4 (active-controlled vs. insulin glargine, add-on therapy, in patients with increased cardiovascular risk, randomized 1:1:1:3); SURPASS-5 (double-blind, placebo-controlled, add-on to insulin glargine +/- metformin)
- Primary endpoint (identical across all five trials): change from baseline in HbA1c (%) at Week 40 (SURPASS-1, -2, -5) or Week 52 (SURPASS-3, -4)
- Key secondary endpoints (SURPASS-1, exact list): incidence of HbA1c<7%; incidence of HbA1c<5.7%; change from baseline in fasting serum glucose; change from baseline in body weight
- SURPASS-1 sample size/power: 472 patients (1:1:1:1) were calculated to give at least 90% power to establish superiority of any tirzepatide dose over placebo, assuming each dose tested in parallel at a two-sided significance level of 0.0017 (alpha/3), a minimum 0.65-percentage-point HbA1c difference vs. placebo, and a common SD of 1.3%
- SURPASS-2 primary objective was non-inferiority of tirzepatide 10 mg and/or 15 mg to semaglutide on HbA1c change (non-inferiority margin 0.3%, tested at two-sided alpha 0.025 per dose, i.e., alpha/2), with 1872 patients calculated for at least 90% power; the graphical testing scheme specified 14 pre-specified hypotheses spanning non-inferiority and superiority tests on HbA1c and body weight for the 10 mg and 15 mg doses, then analogous tests for the 5 mg dose, then HbA1c<7% incidence for all three doses
- Multiplicity: each trial used a sequentially rejective graphical testing procedure (Bretz, Maurer, Brannath & Posch's graphical approach) to control the family-wise two-sided type-I error rate at 5% across the multiple tirzepatide doses and multiple efficacy objectives (HbA1c superiority/non-inferiority, body weight, HbA1c<7%, HbA1c<5.7%) within each trial, propagating alpha from rejected hypotheses to remaining ones per a pre-specified transition-weight graph
- Missing primary-endpoint data (ranging from 4.2% to 9.6% across the five trials) were imputed using a return-to-baseline approach informed by "retrieved dropouts" (patients who discontinued study drug but continued in follow-up), falling back to placebo-arm data where insufficient retrieved-dropout data existed
- A separate FDA-conducted cardiovascular meta-analysis (as part of this original review, not a later supplement) pooled 7 trials (1 Phase II, 6 Phase III, including 3 open-label trials) to assess CV safety via a pre-specified 4-component MACE composite (CV death, MI, stroke, hospitalization for unstable angina); the pre-specified interim analysis (116 MACE-4 events) produced a hazard ratio of 0.81 (97.85% CI 0.52-1.26), meeting the pre-specified upper-bound margin of 1.8

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §5.3, "Conclusions and Recommendations"]*

> "The statistical findings have shown robust and superior effectiveness of tirzepatide 5mg, 10mg and 15mg in treating adults with T2DM... These results were able to provide adequate statistical evidence to support the proposed indication for T2DM. The statistical reviewer recommends an approval of the proposed indication."

The upper bound of this interval is less than 1.8 and thus meets the pre-specified margin in the meta-analysis statistical analysis plan."

### 46. Bexagliflozin (Brenzavvy) — NDA 214373

**Sponsor:** TheracosBio, LLC

**Indication approved:** Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus

**Approval date:** January 20, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** Protocol THR-1442-C-419 (placebo-controlled), NCT03259789; supported by an active-controlled program including NCT03115112 (vs. sitagliptin) and NCT02769481 (vs. glimepiride)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; companion active-controlled non-inferiority trials in the same NDA program (vs. sitagliptin, vs. glimepiride)
- *Endpoints:* change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 24 (primary)
- *Primary analysis:* mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM; unstructured covariance, falling back to AR(1) if non-convergent; Kenward-Roger denominator degrees of freedom)
- *Missing data/bias:* three-step sequential multiple imputation (non-monotone MCMC imputation followed by monotone regression imputation, combined via Rubin's rules), pattern-mixture model and tipping-point analysis as sensitivity checks

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; approximately 300 patients with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled by metformin alone, randomized 1:1 to bexagliflozin 20 mg or placebo added to metformin over a 24-week double-blind period
- Primary endpoint: change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 24 (superiority hypothesis: H0 μ(bexagliflozin) − μ(placebo) ≥ 0 vs. Ha < 0)
- Secondary endpoints (change in FPG, change in SBP, proportion achieving HbA1c ≤7%, change in body weight in patients with baseline BMI ≥25 kg/m², HbA1c change in baseline-HbA1c subgroups) were tested descriptively only — "no formal hypothesis testing will be performed for secondary efficacy endpoints. All nominal p-values will be presented for exploratory purpose"
- Sample size: ~300 randomized 1:1 gives ~90% power to detect a 0.4% HbA1c difference (assumed SD 1%, 12% dropout)
- Primary analysis: MMRM with treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction, baseline HbA1c, and country as fixed effects; missing Week-24 values multiply imputed via a three-step procedure (non-monotone MCMC imputation, then monotone regression imputation), combined via Rubin's combination rule (PROC MIANALYZE); pattern-mixture model and tipping-point analysis used to probe robustness to missing-data assumptions

### 47. Sotagliflozin (Inpefa) — NDA 216203

**Sponsor:** Lexicon Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** To reduce the risk of cardiovascular death, hospitalization for heart failure, and urgent visit for heart failure in adults with (a) heart failure, or (b) type 2 diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, and other cardiovascular risk factors

**Approval date:** May 26, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** SOLOIST-WHF, NCT03521934, and SCORED, NCT03315143 (both trials jointly support the approved indication)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; dual-trial evidentiary basis (worsening-heart-failure population in SOLOIST-WHF, T2D+CKD population in SCORED); early terminated for external/non-efficacy reasons — COVID-19 pandemic disruption (SOLOIST-WHF) and sponsor loss of funding (SCORED) — with the statistical analysis plan finalized in a blinded fashion after trial closure and before unblinding **
- *Endpoints:* total (recurrent) cardiovascular event-count composite — total occurrences of CV death, hospitalization for heart failure (HHF), and urgent HF visit, counting first *and subsequent* events per patient rather than time-to-first-event **
- *Primary analysis:* marginal Cox proportional-hazards model for total (recurrent) events with non-cardiovascular death treated as a competing/terminal event, robust sandwich covariance to allow multiple events per patient, tested via a stratified Wald test **
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing of secondary time-to-event endpoints (same total-events methodology as primary), each requiring significance of the prior endpoint at 2-sided α=0.05
- *Regulatory:* approval combined evidence from two independently conducted, differently enrolled trials of the same drug rather than resting on a single pivotal trial

**Trial design & endpoints**

- SOLOIST-WHF: Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, stratified (by baseline LVEF <50%/≥50% and region) trial in 1,222 patients (608 sotagliflozin, 614 placebo) hospitalized for worsening heart failure with type 2 diabetes, randomized 1:1 to sotagliflozin (200 mg up-titrated to 400 mg) or placebo, initiated in-hospital or shortly after discharge; originally planned for ~4,000 patients but closed early in March 2020 due to COVID-19-related sponsor/funding disruption
- SCORED: Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in patients with type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease (eGFR 25-60 mL/min/1.73m²), and cardiovascular risk factors; also closed early in March 2020 for non-efficacy (sponsor/funding) reasons before the originally planned enrollment was reached
- Primary endpoint (both trials): total number of adjudicated/investigator-reported CV deaths, hospitalizations for heart failure, and urgent HF visits — "the key efficacy focus is on total (first and potentially subsequent) investigator-reported events... a standard assessment of time to a first event may not capture the totality of the effects of treatment"
- Primary analysis: comparison via a stratified Wald test at 2-sided α=0.05; hazard ratio and 95% CI from a marginal Cox proportional-hazards model stratified by region and LVEF category, with a robust sandwich covariance matrix to accommodate multiple events per patient (event times on the same day jittered by 0.1 day to break ties) and non-CV death treated as a competing event
- Because early termination occurred before either protocol could be formally amended, "changes to the intended analysis plan are reflected in this document [the SAP], rather than the protocol, and this plan takes precedence where there are differences between the two documents" — both statistical plans were finalized by an independent academic statistician, verified by the Lexicon statistical team, "in a blinded fashion without the use of any unblinded interim analysis"
- Secondary endpoints (total HHF+urgent HF visits; CV death alone; all-cause mortality; a 5-component composite adding MI and stroke; change in KCCQ-12; change in eGFR) tested via the same total-events framework, in a fixed hierarchical sequence controlling overall 2-sided type-I error at 0.05

### 48. Aprocitentan (Tryvio) — NDA 217686

**Sponsor:** Idorsia Pharmaceuticals US Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of hypertension, in combination with other antihypertensive drugs, to lower blood pressure in adult patients not adequately controlled on other drugs

**Approval date:** March 19, 2024 (corrected approval letter)

**Pivotal trial:** PRECISION, NCT03541174

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; three-part sequential design within one randomized treatment period (4-week double-blind parallel-group part, 32-week single-blind active part, 12-week double-blind randomized-withdrawal part with re-randomization at Week 36); ICH E9(R1) estimand framework — treatment-policy strategy for intercurrent events **
- *Endpoints:* change from baseline to Week 4 in mean trough sitting systolic BP (AOBPM) (primary, Part 1); change from Week-36 (DB-WD baseline) to Week 40 in mean trough sitting SBP (key secondary, Part 3 randomized-withdrawal)
- *Primary analysis:* mixed model (MMRM-type) with treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction, baseline SBP and baseline-by-visit interaction as covariates; unstructured covariance
- *Multiplicity:* graphical alpha-propagation method (Maurer-Bretz/Bretz 2009) — parallel Bonferroni testing of H10 (25 mg) and H20 (12.5 mg) each at 2-sided α=0.025, with any rejected endpoint's alpha propagated to gate the Part-3 withdrawal hypothesis H30 (tested at 0.05 if both rejected, 0.025 if only one rejected)
- *Missing data/bias:* primary analysis handles missing data via the mixed model under missing-at-random (MAR), without imputation; sensitivity analyses probe departures from MAR and an alternative (hypothetical) estimand

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Phase 3, multicenter, blinded, randomized, parallel-group trial in patients with resistant hypertension on a standardized fixed-dose background regimen (amlodipine/valsartan/hydrochlorothiazide); randomized treatment period had three sequential parts: (1) 4-week double-blind part, patients randomized 1:1:1 to aprocitentan 25 mg, 12.5 mg, or placebo; (2) 32-week single-blind part, all patients receive aprocitentan 25 mg; (3) 12-week double-blind withdrawal (DB-WD) part, patients re-randomized 1:1 at Week 36 to aprocitentan 25 mg or placebo
- Ultimately 730 subjects were randomized (versus a planned ≥600), with over-enrollment attributed to added sites/countries and a late screening surge compensating for COVID-19-related recruitment disruption; ≥380 patients were targeted for re-randomization in the DB-WD part (85% power), achieved with lower-than-expected dropout
- Primary endpoint: change from baseline to Week 4 in mean trough sitting SBP by automated office BP monitoring (AOBPM), each dose vs. placebo, tested at 2-sided α=0.025 per comparison
- Key secondary (Part 3): change from DB-WD baseline (Week 36) to Week 40 in mean trough SiSBP, aprocitentan 25 mg vs. placebo, tested only if either H10 or H20 was rejected in Part 1
- Primary analysis population: FAS (full analysis set); primary estimand is a treatment-policy estimand — "all AOBPM measurements, irrespective of any intercurrent event(s), will be included in the main analysis" — handled via a mixed model assuming missing-at-random rather than imputation
- Overall type-I error strongly controlled at 0.05 via a graphical (Bretz 2009) testing strategy: H10 and H20 tested in parallel via Bonferroni at 0.025 each; if either is rejected, its allocated alpha propagates to H30

> "Three null hypotheses will be tested in this study. The first two null hypotheses (H10 and H20) will be tested in parallel using the Bonferroni correction. The third null hypothesis (H30) will only be tested if H10 or H20 is rejected... H10: μ1 = μ0 vs H1a: μ1 ≠ μ0 [aprocitentan 25 mg vs. placebo]... This hypothesis will be tested at a two-sided significance level of 0.025. ### 49. Sotatercept-csrk (Winrevair) — BLA 761363

**Sponsor:** Merck Sharp & Dohme LLC (drug originally developed by Acceleron Pharma Inc., acquired by Merck in 2021)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adults with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH, WHO Group 1) to increase exercise capacity, improve WHO functional class, and reduce the risk of clinical worsening events

**Approval date:** March 26, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** STELLAR, NCT04576988

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, add-on to stable background PAH therapy
- *Endpoints:* change from baseline in 6-minute walk distance (6MWD) at Week 24 (primary); 9-item ranked secondary hierarchy including a multicomponent responder endpoint, PVR, NT-proBNP, WHO functional class, time-to-clinical-worsening (TTCW), a risk-score responder endpoint, and three PAH-SYMPACT domain scores
- *Primary analysis:* stratified Wilcoxon rank-sum test with Hodges-Lehmann estimator (randomization factors as strata)
- *Multiplicity:* gatekeeping/fixed-sequence step-down procedure across the 9 ranked secondary endpoints, each tested at 2-sided α=0.05 only if all preceding endpoints in the sequence were significant
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* no interim efficacy analyses planned; unblinded safety-only DMC review at fixed intervals
- *Missing data/bias:* worst-rank composite imputation for participants who die or have a clinical-worsening event before Week 24 (tied and untied variants), standard multiple imputation for other missingness, ANCOVA and MMRM sensitivity analyses, tipping-point analysis **

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial adding sotatercept or placebo to stable background PAH therapy (mono-, double-, or triple-combination therapy, with or without prostacyclin infusion)
- Primary endpoint: change from baseline in 6MWD at Week 24, analyzed via the stratified Wilcoxon rank-sum test (randomization factors as strata) with the Hodges-Lehmann estimate of the location shift and its 95% CI
- Missing-data handling for the primary endpoint: participants who miss the Week-24 6MWT for reasons other than death or a clinical-worsening event are multiply imputed under MAR; participants who die receive the worst-rank score; participants with a non-fatal clinical-worsening event receive the next-worst-rank score — several alternative tie-breaking/imputation-magnitude variants (untied worst-rank using −2000 m for death, −1000 m for clinical worsening, etc.) were pre-specified as sensitivity analyses, along with an ANCOVA model and a tipping-point analysis
- 9 pre-specified secondary endpoints ranked in a fixed testing sequence (multicomponent improvement responder rate → PVR → NT-proBNP → WHO FC improvement → time-to-clinical-worsening-or-death → French risk-score responder rate → 3 PAH-SYMPACT domain scores), each analyzed by CMH test, ANCOVA, or log-rank test as appropriate to the endpoint type, and "a gatekeeping method will be used to control the Type I error rate in secondary endpoints by testing in the order of the secondary endpoints listed above, after successful testing for the primary endpoint"
- No interim efficacy analyses were planned; an external independent DMC reviewed unblinded *safety* data only, beginning after ≥15 participants completed Visit 2 and approximately every 3 months thereafter

### 50. Flurpiridaz F 18 (Flyrcado) — NDA 215168

**Sponsor:** GE Healthcare (compound originally developed as BMS747158 by Bristol-Myers Squibb, then Lantheus Medical Imaging, before GE Healthcare)

**Indication approved:** Radioactive diagnostic drug for PET myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI), under rest or stress (pharmacologic or exercise), in adults with known or suspected coronary artery disease (CAD), to evaluate for myocardial ischemia and infarction

**Approval date:** September 27, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** GE-265-303, NCT03354273 (co-primary efficacy trial anchoring this approval), with the earlier BMS747158-301, NCT01347710, serving as a supportive/secondary trial in the same review

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison), each subject undergoing flurpiridaz PET MPI, SPECT MPI, and invasive coronary angiography (ICA) as reference standard
- *Endpoints:* co-primary sensitivity and specificity of flurpiridaz PET MPI vs. ICA (≥50% stenosis by QCA) for detection of significant CAD, assessed per-reader by 3 independent blinded readers **; key secondary sensitivity/specificity superiority (sensitivity) and non-inferiority (specificity, 10% margin) of PET MPI vs. SPECT MPI using the same reference standard
- *Primary analysis:* one-sample z-test (normal approximation to the binomial) against a pre-specified performance goal (lower bound of 2-sided 95% CI must exceed 60% for both sensitivity and specificity), with a replication-across-readers success criterion requiring the same 2-of-3 (or all 3) independent readers to reject each null hypothesis **
- *Missing data/bias:* Modified Intent-to-Treat (MITT: completed both PET and reference-standard assessment) as primary analysis population for co-primary endpoints; Secondary MITT (SMITT: also completed SPECT) for key secondary endpoints; FDA reviewer noted the diagnostic-accuracy design's reliance on ICA as an imperfect but independent reference standard
- *Regulatory:* regular approval of a diagnostic imaging agent based on two company-sponsored diagnostic-accuracy trials rather than a randomized clinical-outcome trial; no dedicated peer-reviewed publication identified for the confirmatory GE-265-303 trial as of this writing — its results are documented only in the FDA review and the approved label

**Trial design & endpoints**

- GE-265-303: Phase 3, open-label, multicenter, international trial; 604 patients with known or suspected CAD each underwent flurpiridaz PET MPI (rest and stress) and ICA; co-primary endpoints were the sensitivity and specificity of flurpiridaz PET MPI for detecting significant CAD (≥50% stenosis of a major coronary artery/branch by QCA), read independently by 3 blinded readers, in the MITT population
- Success criterion (pre-specified in the SAP): "the criteria for primary efficacy will be proving the statistical superiority of both the true specificity and sensitivity to a threshold of 60%... the lower bound of the 2-sided 95% confidence interval (CI) for both sensitivity and specificity must exceed 60%," tested via a 1-sided 1-sample z-test at α=0.025 per hypothesis, required to be met "for each reader and for all readers... or by the same 2 out of 3 readers" for the study to be a statistical success
- Key secondary endpoints: sensitivity/specificity of flurpiridaz PET MPI compared to SPECT MPI (same patients, same ICA reference standard) in the SMITT population — superiority (1-sided α=0.025) for sensitivity and non-inferiority (10% margin) for specificity, again requiring the same 2-of-3 (or all 3) readers
- BMS747158-301 (the earlier, Bristol-Myers-Squibb/Lantheus-era trial, N=795): a similarly designed diagnostic-accuracy trial that established sensitivity of PET MPI over SPECT but did not demonstrate non-inferior specificity; described in the FDA review as supportive/historical context alongside GE-265-303 rather than as the anchor for the 2024 approval
- No formal interim analyses were planned for GE-265-303

**Documents**

*[verbatim, GE-265-303 Statistical Analysis Plan, Version 2.0, §6.4.3, p.24]*

> "The criteria for primary efficacy will be proving the statistical superiority of both the true specificity and sensitivity to a threshold of 60% in Flurpiridaz (18F) Injection PET MPI. To meet the criteria for success in this study, both the sensitivity and the specificity of Flurpiridaz (18F) Injection PET MPI must exceed 60%. Thus, the lower bound of the 2-sided 95% confidence interval (CI) for both sensitivity and specificity must exceed 60%... H01: s1 ≤ 0.60; H02: p1 ≤ 0.60... each of the above endpoint comparisons will be performed by using a 1-sided 1-sample test with type 1 error (α)= 0.025. The test will be based on the 1-sample z-test for proportions, using the normal approximation to the binomial distribution. The analysis will be done for each reader and for all readers. If each null hypothesis is rejected in the analysis of all readers or by the same 2 out of 3 readers, the study will be considered a statistical success. There will be no formal interim efficacy analysis for this study."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review and Evaluation, "Study Endpoints," p.112]*

> "The co-primary efficacy endpoints of GE-265-303 were the sensitivity and specificity of flurpiridaz F 18 PET MPI in the detection of significant CAD as defined by ICA... The selected co-primary endpoints are reasonable and have been successfully used to support marketing applications for other diagnostic imaging drugs. The success thresholds ensure better than chance performance and are acceptable accounting for expected performance of other imaging drugs used for the indication... We also note that while false positive and false negative results of MPI can have significant adverse consequences, in the setting of suspected CAD, false negative results are of greater concern as they could result in delay of clinically indicated revascularization."

### 51. Acoramidis (Attruby) — NDA 216540

**Sponsor:** BridgeBio Pharma, Inc. (developed by Eidos Therapeutics, a BridgeBio affiliate)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of the cardiomyopathy of wild-type or variant transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis (ATTR-CM) in adults, to reduce cardiovascular death and cardiovascular-related hospitalization

**Approval date:** November 22, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** ATTRibute-CM, Study AG10-301, Part B, NCT03860935

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; two-part trial with a pre-specified alpha split across parts (Part A, short-term dose-confirmation, 2-sided α=0.01; Part B, 30-month pivotal, 2-sided α=0.04) **; ICH E9(R1) estimand framework — treatment-policy strategy for intercurrent events including tafamidis initiation **
- *Endpoints:* four-component hierarchical composite of all-cause mortality, cumulative frequency of adjudicated CV-related hospitalization, change from baseline in NT-proBNP, and change from baseline in 6-minute walk distance (6MWT), evaluated pairwise within randomization strata over 30 months **
- *Primary analysis:* Finkelstein-Schoenfeld hierarchical composite test (a generalized Gehan-Wilcoxon procedure), with the win ratio (Pocock 2012) and its CI reported as a companion effect-size measure **
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing of key secondary endpoints (6MWT → KCCQ-OS → serum TTR → all-cause mortality via stratified Cox model), each tested only if the prior endpoint was significant at the α(B)=0.04 level
- *Missing data/bias:* treatment-policy estimand — component measurements used regardless of treatment discontinuation or open-label tafamidis initiation; heart transplant/cardiac mechanical assist device counted as death for efficacy analysis

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study AG10-301 (ATTRibute-CM) Part B: Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in adults with symptomatic ATTR-CM (wild-type or variant) and baseline eGFR ≥30 mL/min/1.73m², randomized 2:1 to acoramidis 800 mg twice daily or placebo for 30 months, stratified by ATTR genotype (ATTRm vs. ATTRwt, ≥20% targeted variant), baseline NT-proBNP, and baseline disease severity (8 strata, collapsed if any stratum had <5 patients)
- Power was originally estimated for a two-component hierarchical endpoint (mortality + CV-related hospitalization; simulations based on ATTR-ACT data gave >90% power at 2-sided α=0.04 with N≈460) but the final primary endpoint expanded to four components (mortality, CV-hospitalization frequency, NT-proBNP change, 6MWT change) once tafamidis became an available concomitant/rescue therapy; simulated power across scenarios accounting for tafamidis use remained above 80%
- Primary endpoint pairwise comparison structure: patients compared within stratum on all-cause mortality first (transplant/CMAD counted as death); if tied, then on cumulative CV-related hospitalizations; if tied, then on the difference in NT-proBNP change from baseline (only a difference ≥500 pg/mL breaks the tie); if still tied, on 6MWT change from baseline — ranked scores summed by treatment group per the Finkelstein-Schoenfeld method, with the win ratio and its 95% CI (from the CI of log win-ratio, using the F-S test's Z-score to derive the standard error) reported alongside the F-S p-value
- Key secondary endpoints (6MWT, KCCQ-Overall Summary, serum TTR level, all-cause mortality via a stratified Cox proportional-hazards model) tested in a fixed sequence at α(B)=0.04, each gated on significance of the prior endpoint; "multiplicity adjustment will apply to primary efficacy endpoint and key secondary endpoints only" and is applied only to the modified-ITT (mITT) analysis set

Receiving a heart transplant or a cardiac mechanical assist device (CMAD) will be treated as death... The stratified non-matched Win-Ratio method will allocate all treated and placebo pairs within each stratum in the same hierarchical structure from F-S test. The win ratio (RW) will be calculated by adding all wins from treatment group and dividing it by all wins from placebo group."

> "To control [the family-wise type I error at α(B)], the following efficacy endpoints will be formally tested sequentially in the order specified below: The primary efficacy endpoint; Change from baseline to Month 30 in 6MWT; Change from baseline to Month 30 in KCCQ-OS; Change from baseline to Month 30 in serum TTR level; All-Cause Mortality by Month 30 (stratified cox proportional hazard model)... Multiplicity adjustment will apply to primary efficacy endpoint and key secondary endpoints only. The multiplicity procedure will be applied to the mITT analysis set only."

### 52. Landiolol (Rapiblyk) — NDA 217202

**Sponsor:** AOP Health (AOP Orphan Pharmaceuticals AG)

**Indication approved:** Short-term reduction of ventricular rate in adults with supraventricular tachycardia (SVT), including atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter

**Approval date:** November 22, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** None — this NDA relied entirely on a cross-trial, literature-based evidentiary basis integrating 8 previously published, independently conducted (not FDA-registered, mostly Japanese) randomized controlled trials, rather than a company-sponsored pivotal trial; the two most substantively discussed component trials are the J-Land Study (landiolol vs. digoxin, Nagai et al. 2013) and the JL-KNIGHT study (landiolol vs. diltiazem, Sakamoto et al. 2012 — ultimately excluded by FDA as uninterpretable)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* literature-based approval integrating a post-hoc composite endpoint across multiple independently conducted, non-company-sponsored published RCTs, with no dedicated pivotal trial or posted protocol/SAP **
- *Endpoints:* post-hoc composite endpoint (≥20% reduction from baseline in heart rate, OR decrease in HR to <100 bpm, OR conversion to sinus rhythm), applied retrospectively across trials whose own original primary efficacy endpoints were heterogeneous and different from this composite **
- *Primary analysis:* descriptive, trial-by-trial comparison of the proportion of patients meeting the post-hoc composite endpoint on landiolol vs. placebo or active comparator; no pooled formal cross-trial hypothesis test was performed
- *Regulatory:* FDA invoked a decades-old approved-class endpoint precedent (the identical HR-reduction/conversion-to-sinus-rhythm endpoint underlying esmolol's 1986 approval, endorsed at a 1986 Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee meeting) to justify accepting a post-hoc composite endpoint for landiolol **; FDA explicitly reasoned that a consistent direction of effect across 7 of the 8 submitted RCTs "mitigates concerns for type 1 error that can arise with post-hoc efficacy endpoints"

**Trial design & endpoints**

- No dedicated landiolol pivotal trial was conducted for this NDA. FDA's clinical review states the Applicant "relied on 8 publications, without patient-level data. Six publications described randomized placebo-controlled trials and 2 publications described randomized active-controlled trials with diltiazem and digoxin, respectively," of which the diltiazem trial (Sakamoto et al. 2012, the JL-KNIGHT study, N=71) was excluded from the effectiveness argument as "uninterpretable"
- Individual component trials had heterogeneous original primary endpoints, intention-to-treat populations, dosing, treatment duration, and safety-data collection, precluding a formal meta-analysis; instead, the Applicant proposed — and FDA accepted — a single post-hoc composite efficacy endpoint applied consistently across all trials: ≥20% reduction from baseline in heart rate for patients with SVT, a decrease in HR to <100 bpm, or conversion to sinus rhythm
- The digoxin-comparator trial (Nagai et al. 2013, the J-Land Study, N=214, patients with AF/AFL and left ventricular dysfunction) showed 43% of landiolol-treated heart-failure patients achieved the post-hoc endpoint vs. 12% on digoxin; across the placebo-controlled trials, 42%-89% achieved the endpoint on landiolol vs. 0%-11% on placebo
- FDA's Cross-Discipline Team Leader Review grounds acceptance of this post-hoc, literature-derived approach explicitly in the historical precedent that "this was precisely the treatment effect for which esmolol was approved in 1986 following a Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee (AC) meeting on September 29, 1986," reasoning that a consistent finding of effectiveness across the 7 usable RCTs mitigated the elevated type-I-error risk normally associated with a post-hoc endpoint

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/217202s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Clinical Review and CDER Cross-Discipline Team Leader Review (combined Medical Review document) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/217202Orig1s000MedR.pdf
- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/217202Orig1s000SumR.pdf

"Urgent management of rapid heart rate in patients with atrial fibrillation/flutter and left ventricular dysfunction: comparison of the ultra-short-acting β1-selective blocker landiolol with digoxin (J-Land Study)." *Circ J.* 2013;77(4):908-916. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1253/circj.cj-12-1618), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23502991/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Urgent%20management%20of%20rapid%20heart%20rate%20in%20patients%20with%20atrial%20fibrillation%20flutter%20and%20left%20ventricular%20dysfunction%20J-Land%20Study)
- Key component publication (active-comparator, diltiazem — excluded by FDA as uninterpretable): Sakamoto A, et al. "Landiolol, an ultra-short-acting β1-blocker, more effectively terminates atrial fibrillation than diltiazem after open heart surgery: prospective, multicenter, randomized, open-label study (JL-KNIGHT study)." *Circ J.* 2012;76(5):1097-1101. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1253/circj.cj-11-1332), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22361918/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Landiolol%20an%20ultra-short-acting%20beta1-blocker%20more%20effectively%20terminates%20atrial%20fibrillation%20than%20diltiazem%20JL-KNIGHT)

**Other resources**

- Landiolol has been marketed in Japan (as Onoact) since 2002 by Ono Pharmaceutical; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held for this NDA despite the unusual literature-only evidentiary basis. No IPD access program applicable (no company-sponsored trial).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA CDER Cross Discipline Team Leader Review by Fred Senatore MD, PhD, FACC, "Clinical Review," p.6]*

> "There was inconsistency amongst the published papers that served as the basis of the landiolol NDA with respect to the intention-to-treat populations, posology, duration of treatment, primary efficacy endpoints, and how safety data were collected. Given the heterogeneity of the publications supporting this NDA, the Applicant proposed a post-hoc primary efficacy endpoint of a ≥20% reduction from baseline in HR for patients with SVT, a decrease in HR to <100 bpm, or conversion to sinus rhythm. This was precisely the treatment effect for which esmolol was approved in 1986 following a Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee (AC) meeting on September 29, 1986... Despite the disparate primary endpoints utilized in each of the randomized controlled trials submitted to support the NDA, each trial included as a primary or secondary endpoint the effect of landiolol on HR in the short-term setting thus facilitating an integrated review of the trial HR data. However, each trial was judged on its own merit regarding their respective primary efficacy endpoints. Of note, there is a consistent finding of effectiveness of landiolol across 7 randomized, controlled clinical trials, which mitigates concerns for type 1 error that can arise with post-hoc efficacy endpoints."

*[verbatim, FDA Clinical Review, "Conclusions on the Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness," p.12]*

> "Based on the data in the published literature from 6 randomized placebo-controlled trials and 2 randomized active-controlled trials, landiolol hydrochloride was effective at decreasing heart rate (HR) for patients with supraventricular tachycardia (SVT), including atrial fibrillation (AF) and atrial flutter (AFL), and including for patients with a diagnosis of heart failure... Therefore, the applicant has provided substantial evidence of effectiveness and safety of landiolol for the short-term reduction in ventricular rate in the intended population of patients with SVT including AF and AFL."

### 53. Olezarsen (Tryngolza) — NDA 218614

**Sponsor:** Ionis Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adjunct to diet to reduce triglycerides in adults with familial chylomicronemia syndrome (FCS)

**Approval date:** December 19, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** Balance, Protocol ISIS 678354-CS3, NCT04568434

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, two-dose-cohort trial (each cohort separately randomized drug:placebo); ICH E9(R1) estimand framework — treatment-policy strategy for intercurrent events **
- *Endpoints:* percent change from baseline in fasting triglycerides (TG) at the primary analysis time point, Month 6 (primary)
- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA (treatment, randomization stratification factors, and log-transformed baseline TG) with a heteroskedasticity-robust variance estimator (Bell and McCaffrey method, per Imbens and Kolesár 2016) for the treatment-difference confidence interval **
- *Multiplicity:* gatekeeping/fixed-sequence hierarchical testing — the 80 mg dose vs. pooled placebo comparison gates testing of the 50 mg dose vs. pooled placebo; secondary endpoint family (fasting TG at Month 12, fasting apoC-III at the primary time point and Month 12, ≥40% TG-responder rate, apoB-48, non-HDL-C) tested in a fixed sequence only if both doses were significant on the primary endpoint
- *Missing data/bias:* multiple imputation of missing TG values from "retrieved dropouts" (patients with late off-treatment TG measurements) where sufficient data exist; otherwise a Jump-to-Reference (J2R) "wash-out" multiple-imputation approach for the active arms (imputing to the placebo-group trajectory) and MAR-based multiple imputation for the placebo arm **

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in patients with genetically or clinically confirmed FCS; approximately 60 patients randomized 1:1 to Cohort A (50 mg) or Cohort B (80 mg), each cohort further randomized 2:1 to olezarsen or matching placebo, dosed subcutaneously every 4 weeks for a 53-week treatment period, stratified by prior history of pancreatitis and previous volanesorsen treatment
- Primary endpoint: percent change from baseline to the primary analysis time point (Month 6) in fasting TG, evaluated after the last patient completed the Week 53/early-termination visit
- Primary analysis: ANCOVA model (treatment, 2 stratification factors, log-transformed baseline TG) per dose group vs. pooled placebo in the Full Analysis Set (FAS), with the 95% CI of the treatment difference calculated using the Bell-McCaffrey robust variance estimator to account for potential heteroscedasticity; a "treatment policy" estimand is used — post-intercurrent-event assessments remain in the analysis
- Missing-data handling: multiple imputation using "retrieved dropout" data (patients who discontinued before Week 23 but still have TG values at Weeks 23/25/27) when sufficient such patients exist; otherwise a Jump-to-Reference approach is used — olezarsen-arm dropouts are imputed assuming the treatment effect has "washed out" (using the patient's baseline TG plus the placebo group's imputation model), while placebo-arm dropouts are imputed under MAR using placebo-arm data only
- Multiplicity: "the gatekeeping testing strategy will be applied to the primary endpoint family and secondary endpoint family" — the 80 mg-vs-placebo comparison is tested first at α=0.05; only if significant is the 50 mg-vs-placebo comparison tested at α=0.05; the ranked secondary-endpoint family is tested only if *both* dose comparisons were significant on the primary endpoint

> "Primary Objective: To evaluate the efficacy of ISIS 678354 as compared to placebo on the percent change in fasting triglycerides (TG) from Baseline... Following qualification, approximately 60 eligible patients will be randomized 1:1 to Cohort A (50 mg) or Cohort B (80 mg) and each cohort further randomized 2:1 to receive ISIS 678354 or placebo in a 53-week Treatment Period... The primary endpoint for the study will be evaluated after the last patient has completed the Week 53/ET Visit and will be based on the percent change in fasting TG from Baseline at the primary analysis time point (Month 6)."

*[verbatim, Protocol, §10.5 "Interim Analysis and Multiplicity," p.69]*

> "To control the overall Type I error rate at 0.05 across the primary endpoints and secondary endpoints for the final analysis, the gatekeeping testing strategy will be applied to the primary endpoint family and secondary endpoint family. The hierarchical testing procedure will be utilized within the primary endpoint family and secondary endpoint family. For the primary endpoint family, the 2 treatment arms will be compared against pooled placebo using the hierarchical testing procedure, in which the ISIS 678354 80 mg treatment group will be compared to the pooled placebo at the alpha level of 0.05, if the comparison is statistically significant (p < 0.05), then the ISIS 678354 50-mg treatment group is compared against the pooled placebo at the alpha level of 0.05."

*[verbatim, Statistical Analysis Plan §10.6.3.1 "Analysis of Primary Endpoint," p.72]*

> "The primary analysis of the primary endpoint is to compare the percent change from Baseline to the primary analysis time point in fasting TG between each ISIS 678354 treatment group vs. pooled placebo using an ANCOVA model in the FAS... To account for potential heterogeneity in variance, the 95% CI of the treatment differences will be calculated using the robust variance estimator based on the Bell and McCaffrey method (Imbens and Kolesár 2016)... Patients with a missing TG value after discontinuation will have TG value multiply imputed at Primary analysis time point based on the known assessments from the retrieved dropouts... If there is not a sufficient number of retrieved dropouts, missing TG value at the primary time point will be imputed using a 'wash-out' (Jump to Reference, J2R) multiple imputation approach. With the approach, patients treated with ISIS 678354 who discontinue study will have missing post-discontinuation TG values multiply imputed based on the fasting TG at Baseline, 2 randomization stratification factors, and the imputation model for the placebo group."

### 54. Plozasiran (Redemplo) — NDA 219947

**Sponsor:** Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adjunct to diet to reduce triglycerides in adults with familial chylomicronemia syndrome (FCS)

**Approval date:** November 18, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** PALISADE, Protocol AROAPOC3-3001, NCT05089084

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, two-dose-cohort trial (72 subjects randomized 2:1:2:1 across two independently placebo-controlled dose cohorts, 25 mg and 50 mg)
- *Endpoints:* percent change from baseline in fasting triglycerides (TG) at Month 10 (primary)
- *Primary analysis:* Wilcoxon rank-sum test with Hodges-Lehmann estimator (median difference and 95% CI), chosen because "the known distribution of TG and percent change from baseline in TG" makes a normality assumption difficult to satisfy
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing across a 4-step endpoint sequence (TG at Month 10 → averaged TG at Months 10/12 → apoC-III at Month 10 → apoC-III at Month 12), each dose tested only after the prior endpoint reached significance for both doses
- *Missing data/bias:* pattern-mixture multiple imputation with a treatment-arm-specific washout assumption — plozasiran-arm dropouts imputed as if the treatment effect had washed out (using baseline TG plus placebo-arm data), placebo-arm dropouts imputed under MAR **; sensitivity analyses include analysis of heterogeneous covariance (ANHECOVA, per Ye et al. 2022), MMRM, and a tipping-point analysis *(ANHECOVA is a)*

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in adults with FCS; 72 subjects randomized 2:1:2:1 to plozasiran 25 mg, its matched placebo, plozasiran 50 mg, or its matched placebo, dosed subcutaneously once every 3 months
- Primary endpoint: percent change from baseline in fasting TG at Month 10, with the primary estimand defined as "the difference in median percent change from baseline in fasting TG at Month 10 in FCS population, regardless of treatment compliance or other intercurrent events post-baseline" (a treatment-policy-type estimand)
- Primary analysis: nonparametric Hodges-Lehmann estimate of the median treatment difference (extension of the Wilcoxon rank-sum test), implemented via SAS `PROC NPAR1WAY... / HL`; missing Month-10 TG values handled by a pattern-mixture multiple-imputation model incorporating demographics, disease status, baseline TG, and adherence — non-adherent patients with missing data are imputed from non-adherent patients with observed data in the same arm where possible, and where too few such patients exist, plozasiran-arm patients are imputed as washed-out to placebo-like values while placebo-arm patients are imputed under MAR from placebo-arm data
- Multiplicity: "in order to control the family-wise Type I error at a 0.05 level, a fixed sequential testing procedure will be implemented in a hierarchical step-down manner" — secondary endpoints (averaged TG at Months 10/12, apoC-III at Month 10, apoC-III at Month 12) tested only if the endpoint before it in the sequence was significant for both dose levels; within each endpoint, the two doses are tested sequentially (higher dose gates the lower)
- Sensitivity analyses for the primary endpoint include an ANCOVA model, an "analysis of heterogenous covariance (ANHECOVA) as proposed in Ye et al (2022)," an MMRM model under MAR, and a tipping-point analysis of departures from the MAR assumption

*[verbatim, SAP §3.5.1 "Primary Efficacy Endpoint," p.33]*

> "Due to the known distribution of TG and percent change from baseline in TG, normality assumption is usually difficult to satisfy. A nonparametric approach will be used as the primary analysis for the primary efficacy endpoint. As an extension to the Wilcoxon rank-sum test, the Hodges-Lehmann method will be used to estimate the median difference and its corresponding 95% CI for percent changes between ARO-APOC3 doses and placebo."

*[verbatim, SAP, "Multiplicity" section, p.28]*

> "In order to control the family-wise Type I error at a 0.05 level, a fixed sequential testing procedure will be implemented in a hierarchical step-down manner. The hypothesis testing procedure from primary efficacy endpoint to key secondary endpoints will use a fixed-sequence stepping-down procedure. That is, only if the primary efficacy analysis of primary endpoint proves significantly in favor of active treatment groups will the secondary endpoints [be] tested."

*[verbatim, SAP §3.5.1 "Sensitivity Analyses," p.33]*

> "For change from baseline at Month 10 in fasting TG, an analysis of heterogenous covariance (ANHECOVA) as proposed in Ye et al (2022) will be performed using FAS if data permit."

### 55. Lerodalcibep-liga (Lerochol) — BLA 761427

**Sponsor:** LIB Therapeutics, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adjunct to diet and exercise to reduce low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) in adults with hypercholesterolemia, including heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH)

**Approval date:** December 12, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** Trial 1 = LIBerate-HR, NCT04797247; Trial 2, NCT04806893; both are 52-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials in patients with ASCVD or increased ASCVD risk requiring further LDL-C reduction, jointly supporting the approved indication (a third trial, LIBerate-HeFH, NCT04797104, provides supportive evidence in the specifically HeFH-labeled population)

**No FDA statistical review or genuine sponsor SAP/protocol was found publicly posted for this BLA.** Drugs@FDA lists only the approval letter and label for BLA 761427; no Multi-Disciplinary Review, Statistical Review, or Clinical Review document was found under the standard `accessdata.fda.gov` naming patterns (checked both `nda/` and `bla/` directory conventions across the 2025-2026 year folders). NCT04797247, NCT04806893, and NCT04797104 have no protocol or SAP posted in ClinicalTrials.gov's Documents tab. This entry relies on the approved label's Section 14 (Clinical Studies) tables and footnotes, and the peer-reviewed publications, with a reverse-engineered SAP for analysis details not stated in either.

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* [inferred] randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 52-week trials — see Reverse-engineered SAP below
- *Endpoints:* [inferred] placebo-adjusted percent change from baseline in LDL-C at Week 52 (primary) — see Reverse-engineered SAP below
- *Primary analysis:* [inferred] ANCOVA with a heteroskedasticity-robust ("unequal variances") variance assumption, multiple imputation for missing Week-52 values — see Reverse-engineered SAP below

**Trial design & endpoints** *(from label + publications)*

- Trial 1 (NCT04797247) and Trial 2 (NCT04806893): multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled 52-week trials; 1,844 adults with ASCVD or increased ASCVD risk, stable on maximally tolerated statin (with or without other oral lipid-modifying therapy), randomized 2:1 to lerodalcibep 300 mg (n=1,229) or placebo (n=615) by subcutaneous injection every 4 weeks
- Primary efficacy outcome measure in both trials: placebo-adjusted ITT analysis of percent change in LDL-C from baseline to Week 52 — Trial 1: −55% (95% CI −59.2%, −50.8%; p<0.0001); Trial 2: −50% (95% CI −54.2%, −45.2%; p<0.0001)
- LDL-C, total cholesterol, non-HDL-C, and ApoB were missing at Week 52 for 7.5% (placebo) and 10.4% (lerodalcibep) of patients; the label states "a multiple imputation washout model was implemented for imputing missing values at Week 52"
- Least-squares means came from "an Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) model including treatment as a factor and baseline value as a covariate, assuming unequal variances between groups"; the label footnotes that the LDL-C comparison was "controlled for Type I error rate" while total cholesterol, non-HDL-C, and ApoB were "not controlled for Type I error rate" — implying LDL-C was the sole formally tested (alpha-protected) endpoint in the family, with the lipid panel otherwise reported descriptively
- LIBerate-HeFH (NCT04797104, Trial 3 per label numbering) is a separate 52-week placebo-controlled trial in HeFH patients on oral lipid therapy, supporting the HeFH-specific portion of the label; its published Phase 3 report (Raal F, et al., *Eur Heart J* 2023) also used an ANCOVA-based percent-change-in-LDL-C primary analysis

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (Trial 2) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04806893 (no protocol/SAP posted)
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (LIBerate-HeFH) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04797104 (no protocol/SAP posted)
- Pivotal publication (Trial 1 / LIBerate-HR): Klug EQ, Llerena S, Burgess LJ, et al. - Supportive publication (LIBerate-HeFH): Raal F, Fourie N, Scott R, et al. **Other resources**

- FDA required a deferred pediatric postmarketing study (ages 6 to <18 with HeFH) as a condition of approval. No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was identified. No IPD access program confirmed for LIB Therapeutics.

**Reverse-engineered SAP** *(inferred — not genuine LIBerate/Lerochol SAP text)*

- **ANCOVA with a robust ("unequal variances") variance assumption for the primary LDL-C endpoint** [inferred from: the label's Table 3/4 footnote "Least-squares mean from an Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) model including treatment as a factor and baseline value as a covariate, assuming unequal variances between groups"]. This closely parallels the heteroskedasticity-robust ANCOVA approaches (e.g., Bell-McCaffrey) seen in this same batch's olezarsen/Balance SAP, suggesting a similar design-era statistical convention across recent lipid-lowering FCS/hypercholesterolemia trials, but the exact estimator (Bell-McCaffrey vs. a simple Satterthwaite/Welch-type unequal-variance ANCOVA) cannot be confirmed without the SAP.
- **Multiple imputation "washout model" for missing Week-52 values** [inferred from: the label's footnote "a multiple imputation washout model was implemented for imputing missing values at Week 52" applied to 7.5%-10.4% of patients]. The word "washout" strongly suggests a Jump-to-Reference-style approach (treated-arm dropouts imputed toward a placebo-like trajectory) analogous to the explicit J2R method documented in this batch's genuine olezarsen and plozasiran SAPs, but the precise imputation model, reference group, and sensitivity analyses are not stated in the label and cannot be confirmed without the SAP.
- **Single formally alpha-controlled primary endpoint (LDL-C), other lipid parameters descriptive only** [inferred from: the label's Table 3/4 footnotes marking the LDL-C treatment difference "p-value <0.001 for superiority, controlled for Type I error rate" while marking total cholesterol, non-HDL-C, and ApoB differences "Not controlled for Type I error rate"]. This implies no formal multiplicity procedure was needed beyond the single primary LDL-C hypothesis (per trial, per dose-vs-placebo comparison), but whether any hierarchy existed across Trial 1 and Trial 2 themselves (e.g., co-primary vs. independently powered trials) is not stated in the label and cannot be confirmed without the SAP or FDA statistical review.

### 56. Etripamil (Cardamyst) — NDA 218571

**Sponsor:** Milestone Pharmaceuticals Inc. (Milestone Pharmaceuticals USA, Inc.)

**Indication approved:** Termination of paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (PSVT) in adults, self-administered as a nasal spray in a medically unsupervised (at-home) setting after training by a healthcare provider

**Approval date:** December 12, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** RAPID (NODE-301 Part 2), NCT03464019; supportive real-world safety trial NODE-303, NCT04072835

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, self-administered at-home dosing regimen with an optional repeat dose, large single-arm open-label safety trial as a distinct supportive study (NODE-303) rather than a continuation of the pivotal trial
- *Endpoints:* time to adjudicated conversion of PSVT to sinus rhythm within a fixed observation window
- *Primary analysis:* Peto-Peto/Wilcoxon-type test for censored time-to-event data via SAS LIFETEST, Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified or with covariates) for the hazard ratio, Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (primary endpoint plus 12 ordered secondary endpoints, two-sided α=0.05 at each step)
- *Missing data/bias:* Standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment, with pre-specified alternative-censoring sensitivity analyses for external medical intervention
- *Regulatory:* Complete Response Letter (CRL) followed by resubmission and approval (first-cycle CRL was CMC/nitrosamine-impurity related, not clinical)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- RAPID is Part 2 of the NODE-301 study (NCT03464019, one shared registration record covering NODE-301 Parts 1-3): a multi-center, multi-national, randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of self-administered intranasal etripamil (2×70 mg, second dose optional at 10 minutes if symptoms persisted) vs. placebo for spontaneous PSVT episodes in a medically unsupervised setting, in adults ≥18 with a documented history of sustained PSVT episodes
- NODE-301 Part 1 (in-clinic/physician-witnessed dosing, 300-minute observation window) failed to demonstrate superiority (HR 1.1, p=0.12, Peto-Peto test) despite a numerically faster conversion in the etripamil arm; after consultation with FDA, the Applicant amended the protocol (Amendment 5, July 16, 2020) to add Parts 2 (RAPID) and 3 (RAPID Extension), moving to self-administration in an unsupervised setting with a shorter 30-minute primary observation window
- Primary endpoint: time to an adjudicated termination of a confirmed episode of PSVT (confirmed by an Independent Adjudication Committee reading ambulatory ECG/cardiac-monitoring-system data) and conversion to sinus rhythm for at least 30 seconds, within 30 minutes of study drug administration
- Analysis populations: Efficacy Population = mITT subjects who took study drug for an IAC-confirmed PSVT episode (184 of 255 mITT subjects: 99 etripamil, 85 placebo); Safety Population = mITT Population (all randomized subjects who took study drug for a perceived episode)
- 12 secondary endpoints tested in a pre-specified hierarchical gatekeeping order (time to conversion within 10/45/60 minutes; treatment satisfaction; symptom-improvement items; rate of seeking additional medical intervention) — each tested only if all prior endpoints in the sequence were significant
- Sample size: powered from Part 1 data (54% vs. 30% conversion at 30 minutes) for ≥90% power at two-sided α=0.05 with 180 confirmed PSVT episodes needed; enrollment continued to the 180th adjudicated episode, yielding a final analyzable 184 confirmed episodes
- Primary analysis method: SAS LIFETEST procedure using a Wilcoxon (Peto-Peto-type) test for the time-to-event primary endpoint; HR and 95% CI from a Cox proportional-hazards model; Kaplan-Meier estimation of time to conversion; secondary time-to-event endpoints analyzed the same way, other secondary endpoints via ANOVA
- Censoring rules: subjects whose ECG recording was interrupted before Minute 30 were censored at the interruption time; subjects receiving rescue medical intervention without conversion by end of window, or converting after the window, were censored at 31 minutes (analogous rule at 46 minutes for the 45-minute analysis)
- Result: primary endpoint met — conversion in 64% of etripamil-arm vs. 31% of placebo-arm Efficacy Population subjects, HR 2.59-2.6 (95% CI 1.66, 4.15), p<0.001
- NODE-303 (NCT04072835) is a separate, non-randomized, open-label, single-arm Phase 3 safety trial of self-administered etripamil for PSVT (enrolled 1,116 per ClinicalTrials.gov, with an open-label extension in NCT04952610); it does not carry an efficacy endpoint and is not the source of the approved efficacy claim, but its large real-world self-administration safety database (503 subjects who took ≥1 dose, per the FDA Integrated Review's safety tables) was central to addressing FDA's device-use/self-administration safety concerns
