- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/218571s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Integrated Review (combined clinical/statistical/nonclinical review) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/218571Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (NODE-301/RAPID) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03464019 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (NODE-303) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04072835

[DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(23)00776-6>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37331368/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Self-administered%20intranasal%20etripamil%20using%20a%20symptom-prompted%2C%20repeat-dose%20regimen%20for%20atrioventricular-nodal-dependent%20supraventricular%20tachycardia)

**Other resources**

- First-cycle regulatory history: NDA 218571 received a Complete Response on March 27, 2025, driven by unresolved Office of Pharmaceutical Quality issues (control of a nitrosamine impurity) and a pharmacology/toxicology recommendation against approval on the same impurity's acceptable-intake data, plus a required preapproval manufacturing-facility inspection; the June 13, 2025 resubmission added no new clinical, clinical-pharmacology, or device data and was approved on the current (December 12, 2025) cycle once OPQ and pharm/tox reviews cleared.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.2.3 "Statistical Analysis Plan," p.28-30]*

> "The statistical analysis plan for NODE-301 Part 2 or RAPID trial was signed on June 6, 2022, before the database was locked and treatment codes were unblinded... The primary objective of this study was to determine whether etripamil NS self-administered by patients is superior to placebo at terminating episodes of PSVT in an at-home setting... The primary endpoint is time to an adjudicated termination of a confirmed episode of PSVT and conversion to SR for at least 30 seconds within 30 minutes of start of study drug... The primary endpoint was analyzed via Statistical Analysis System Lifetest procedure using Wilcoxon test. The hazard ratio and 95% confidence interval were calculated using the Cox proportional hazards model... The primary endpoint and 12 secondary endpoints were included in the multiplicity adjustment using a hierarchical gatekeeping approach to control the type I error. For each hypothesis testing, a two-sided 0.05 significant level was used. Once the primary endpoint achieved statistical significance, the secondary efficacy endpoints would be tested in the prespecified order listed above. That is, an endpoint can only be tested if all endpoints before it achieved statistical significance."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, censoring rules, p.29]*

> "In the primary analysis, subjects whose recordings were interrupted before Minute 30 were censored at the time when the interruptions occurred (e.g., at the time of loss of ECG signal). Subjects who received an additional medical intervention after failing to achieve conversion following study drug administration by the end of the relevant observation window of 30 minutes, or who achieved conversion after the observation window of 30 minutes, were censored after the end of the observation period (at 31 minutes)."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, RAPID Part 1 background and results, p.24-26]*

> "The study of NODE-301 Part 1 failed to demonstrate superiority in conversion of PSVT... in PSVT conversion between the etripamil 70 mg and placebo groups, with a hazard ratio of 1.1 (p=0.12, Peto-Peto test). However, subjects in the etripamil group converted more rapidly... After consultation with the FDA, the Applicant amended the NODE-301 protocol to Version 6 (Protocol Amendment 5), dated July 16, 2020. That is the rationale that the Part 2 and Part 3 are conducted. In this report we focus on the pivotal trial – Part 2, i.e., RAPID."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, regulatory history, p.1]*

> "NDA 218571 received a CR on March 27, 2025, for the first review cycle... On June 13, 2025, the Applicant resubmitted NDA 218571... The resubmission did not include any new clinical-pharmacology, clinical, or device-related data. OPQ review dated October 23, 2025, recommended approval."

### 57. Aficamten (Myqorzo) — NDA 219083

**Sponsor:** Cytokinetics, Incorporated

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adults with symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM)

**Approval date:** December 19, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** SEQUOIA-HCM (CY 6031), NCT05186818

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-count/sample-size increase rule based on blinded pooled nuisance-parameter monitoring
- *Endpoints:* peak oxygen uptake (pVO2) by cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET), patient-reported outcomes / HRQoL (KCCQ-CSS), NYHA functional class improvement, Valsalva LVOT-G change and threshold response
- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA (single time-point, distinct from the taxonomy's existing repeated-measures ANCOVA), Mixed model for repeated measurements (MMRM), Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test
- *Multiplicity:* Closed testing procedure (11-step fixed sequence across primary + 10 secondary endpoints)
- *Missing data/bias:* Multiple imputation under a missing-at-random (MAR) assumption; reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan (FDA biometrics disagreed with the MAR assumption in writing before database lock and continued to disagree in the review)
- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan; reviewer-conducted reanalysis after finding the Applicant's stepwise covariate-selection approach unacceptable

**Trial design & endpoints**

- SEQUOIA-HCM (Trial CY 6031) is a Phase 3, multi-center, randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of aficamten (starting 5 mg, titrated up to 15 mg based on echocardiographic response) vs. placebo, added to background oHCM therapy, in adults with symptomatic oHCM and LVOT gradient ≥30 mmHg at rest or post-Valsalva
- Primary endpoint: change in peak oxygen uptake (pVO2) by CPET from baseline to Week 24
- Key secondary endpoints (closed testing procedure, tested in this pre-specified order after the primary): KCCQ Clinical Summary Score (CSS) change at Week 24; proportion with ≥1 NYHA class improvement at Week 24; Valsalva LVOT-gradient (LVOT-G) change at Week 24; proportion with Valsalva LVOT-G <30 mmHg at Week 24; duration of septal-reduction-therapy (SRT) eligibility over 24 weeks (in patients SRT-eligible at baseline); then the same KCCQ-CSS/NYHA/LVOT-G triad again at Week 12; then change in total CPET workload at Week 24
- Analysis population: Full Analysis Set (FAS) = all randomized subjects (redefined by Protocol Amendment 04, December 8, 2023, to include all randomized subjects rather than a narrower completer-type set)
- Sample size: 270 subjects (1:1) for >90% power to detect a 1.5 mL/kg/min between-arm difference in pVO2 change (SD 3.5), with a pre-specified option — exercised once, based on blinded pooled missing-data-rate and pooled-SD monitoring — to increase enrollment to maintain power; final N=282
- Primary analysis method: ANCOVA with treatment, randomization strata (beta-blocker use, CPET modality), baseline pVO2, and baseline body weight as covariates in the FAS; missing Week-24 pVO2 imputed via multiple imputation (100 datasets) under a MAR assumption, combined via Rubin's rule
- FDA's statistical reviewer disagreed in writing with the Applicant's MAR imputation approach — advice documented as given to the sponsor on the SAP itself, dated August 11, 2023, before database lock — and separately disagreed with the Applicant's stepwise covariate-selection method for one secondary analysis, which FDA found led to no covariates ultimately being retained in that model
- Result: primary endpoint met — LS-mean treatment difference in pVO2 change of 1.74 mL/kg/min (95% CI 1.04, 2.44; p<0.0001); Applicant's own pre-specified analysis reported an LS-mean difference of 1.76 (95% CI not shown in this excerpt) with baseline pVO2 ≈18.4-18.6 mL/kg/min in both arms
- Protocol Amendment 04 (December 8, 2023) also simplified the multiplicity structure from a parallel-gatekeeping method to a single closed testing procedure

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/219083s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Integrated Review (combined clinical/statistical/nonclinical review) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/219083Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05186818

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2401424), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38739079/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Aficamten%20for%20Symptomatic%20Obstructive%20Hypertrophic%20Cardiomyopathy)

**Other resources**

- Cytokinetics trial-specific IPD access via Vivli/YODA was not individually confirmed here.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting is recorded for this application in the reviewed documents.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, sponsor's posted SAP, "Statistical Analysis Plan - Protocol CY 6031," Version 2 Final, October 2, 2023, §7.6]*

> "The null hypothesis for the primary and secondary efficacy variables in the FAS will be tested in the pre-specified order using a closed testing procedure. For preservation of the overall type I error rate at two-sided 0.05 for the primary and secondary endpoints, the closed testing procedure will be used to address multiplicity. The primary endpoint is tested first at two-sided 0.05. If the primary endpoint achieves statistical significance at two-sided alpha level of 0.05, then the secondary endpoints will be tested at two-sided 0.05, with their testing being in the sequential order of KCCQ-CSS change from baseline, proportion of patients with ≥1 NYHA functional class improvement, post-Valsalva LVOT-G change from baseline, and proportion of patients with post-Valsalva LVOT-G < 30 mmHg in FAS at Week 24; duration of SRT eligibility up to 24 weeks of treatment for those who were SRT eligible at baseline; KCCQ-CSS change from baseline, proportion of patients with ≥1 NYHA functional class improvement, post-Valsalva LVOT-G change from baseline, and proportion of patients with post-Valsalva LVOT-G < 30 mmHg in FAS at Week 12; and change from baseline to Week 24 in total workload."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.1.3 "Statistical Analysis Plan, CY 6031," p.34-36]*

> "The review division provided comments on the Trial CY 6031 protocol (preliminary meeting minutes dated June 1, 2021, End-of-Phase 2 meeting minutes dated August 3, 2021) and the statistical analysis plan (SAP) (dated August 11, 2023, and November 1, 2023)... During the trial, the Applicant pre-specified periodic assessments of the blinded aggregate pooled missing data rate and overall pooled SD for the change from baseline in pVO2 at Week 24. Based on these assessments, the Applicant could increase the sample size once to maintain the intended power. Thus, there were 282 subjects, rather than 270, enrolled and randomized in the trial."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, reviewer disagreement on missing-data handling, p.36]*

> "It should be noted that the review team did not agree with the Applicant's approach for missing data. For the primary analyses, the Applicant imputed the missing data under the missing-at-random assumption despite the advice provided by the biometrics division, dated August 11, 2023, on the CY 6031 statistical analysis plan (SAP): 'We continue to disagree that an MAR assumption is appropriate given that patients with missing data are likely to be different from those who remain in the trial on treatment... those who die should not be imputed with similar outcomes to those who are able to remain in the study... For those who die before the primary endpoint can be assessed, we generally accept a worst-case type of imputation where the worst 10% of observed outcomes can be used for a multiple imputation of missing data due to death.' Additionally, the review team did not agree with the use of stepwise model selection approach due to well-known issues with overestimation of model fit and increase in type I error. In this case, no adjusting covariates were ultimately included in the model."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, primary result, p.41]*

> "There was a statistically significant treatment effect of 1.74 mL/kg/min (95% CI: 1.04, 2.44; p<0.0001) when comparing change from baseline to Week 24 in pVO2 in the aficamten group to the placebo group."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, Table 130 "Summary of Changes to the Protocol for SEQUOIA-HCM," Amendment 04, December 8, 2023]*

> "Added the safety endpoint of incidence of LVEF <50% with signs and symptoms of heart failure... Updated the definition of the FAS to include all randomized subjects. Simplified the testing hierarchy from a parallel gatekeeping method to a closed testing procedure."

### 58. Insulin icodec-abae (Awiqli) — BLA 761326 (Original-2, resubmission)

**Sponsor:** Novo Nordisk

**Indication approved:** To improve glycemic control in adults with diabetes mellitus (once-weekly basal insulin; efficacy for labeling drawn from the type 2 diabetes trials ONWARDS 1-4 and the type 1 diabetes trial ONWARDS 6)

**Approval date:** March 26, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** ONWARDS 1, NCT04460885 (lead trial of the six-trial ONWARDS 1-6 phase 3a program; ONWARDS 5, NCT04760626, was excluded from labeling because its digital-titration-app design confounded the treatment comparison)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled (double-blind in ONWARDS 3), non-inferiority-then-superiority hierarchy, cross-trial pooled/integrated analysis (six independently randomized trials reviewed as one program for a common HbA1c non-inferiority claim, not pooled into one dataset)
- *Endpoints:* HbA1c change from baseline (glycemic control primary endpoint), continuous-glucose-monitoring (CGM)-derived Time in Range (TIR), hypoglycemic-episode incidence rate
- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA with treatment-policy estimand and retrieved-dropout/return-to-baseline multiple imputation
- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (non-inferiority in HbA1c gating a superiority test in HbA1c, and in ONWARDS 1, a further TIR superiority test)
- *Missing data/bias:* Tipping-point analysis (multiple imputation); retrieved-dropout and return-to-baseline multiple imputation for missing continuous endpoint data; reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan (a sensitivity re-imputation overturned the sponsor's ONWARDS 5 superiority conclusion from superior to not-superior)
- *Regulatory:* Complete Response Letter (CRL) followed by resubmission and approval (first-cycle CRL was CMC-only, addressing manufacturing-site and specification deficiencies, not clinical data)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Six Phase 3a trials (ONWARDS 1-6), each an independent randomized, multi-center, active-controlled, 2-arm, parallel-group, treat-to-target trial of once-weekly insulin icodec vs. a once-daily basal insulin comparator; ONWARDS 1, 3, 5 enrolled insulin-naive type 2 diabetes patients, ONWARDS 2 and 4 enrolled T2D patients already on basal (or basal-bolus, ONWARDS 4) insulin, and ONWARDS 6 enrolled type 1 diabetes patients; only ONWARDS 3 was double-blind, the rest open-label; treatment duration was 26 weeks (ONWARDS 2/3/4/6) or 52 weeks (ONWARDS 1/5), with extension periods for ONWARDS 1 and 6
- Primary endpoint (each trial): non-inferiority of insulin icodec vs. the daily-basal-insulin comparator, measured as change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 26 or 52, with a non-inferiority margin of 0.3%
- Key secondary/superiority objective: HbA1c superiority tested only if non-inferiority was met; in ONWARDS 1, CGM-derived Time in Range (70-180 mg/dL) was a further key secondary endpoint gated behind HbA1c non-inferiority and superiority, itself pursued as a superiority claim
- Primary estimand: treatment-policy estimand (all randomized subjects, intercurrent events of discontinuation/rescue-bolus-initiation handled via a "treatment policy" approach rather than censoring at the intercurrent event)
- Missing-data method: for ONWARDS 1, 2, 3, missing endpoint HbA1c was imputed from subjects who discontinued treatment or initiated ≥2 weeks of bolus insulin and had an endpoint measurement ("retrieved dropouts", denoted LAOT-WOB — last available on-treatment-without-bolus measurement); for ONWARDS 5, retrieved dropouts based on treatment discontinuation only (LAOT); for ONWARDS 4, an insufficient number of retrieved dropouts forced a return-to-baseline (RTB) imputation as the primary analysis instead; 1,000 multiply-imputed datasets were generated per trial and analyzed via ANCOVA (treatment + pre-specified fixed effects + baseline HbA1c as covariate), combined via Rubin's rule
- Sensitivity analyses: two-way tipping-point analysis for the treatment-policy estimand in every trial; RTB and a conservative "null imputation" (adding a 0.3 penalty to RTB-imputed values for icodec-arm missing data only) as further sensitivity checks
- Result pattern: non-inferiority (upper 95% CI bound <0.3%) was met in all five T2D trials and in ONWARDS 6 (T1D); superiority in HbA1c was also met in ONWARDS 1, 2, 3, and 5, but not in ONWARDS 4 (LS-mean difference +0.02%, not tested for superiority per the pre-specified hierarchy, since the point estimate favored the comparator)
- FDA's null-imputation sensitivity analysis overturned the ONWARDS 5 HbA1c superiority conclusion from "superior" to "not superior" — but ONWARDS 5 was not proposed for labeling regardless, because its insulin-icodec arm alone received a digital dose-titration app (DoseGuide) not given to the comparator arm, confounding the treatment comparison
- The application was originally a single BLA cycle (761326-Original 1) that received a Complete Response Letter on July 10, 2024, for CMC deficiencies only; the September 26, 2025 Class 2 resubmission (761326-Original 2) added an updated safety-data cut (through June 1, 2025) but no new efficacy analyses, and was approved March 26, 2026

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review Memorandum, §1.1 "Brief Overview of Clinical Studies," p.6]*

> "The application included six phase III studies: ONWARDS 1 (4477), ONWARDS 2 (4478), ONWARDS 3 (4479), ONWARDS 4 (4480), ONWARDS 5 (4481), and ONWARDS 6 (4625). Each study was a randomized, multi-center, active-controlled, 2-arm, parallel-group trial. The primary objective for each study was to demonstrate non-inferiority of insulin icodec against daily basal insulin (comparator), as measured by change from baseline in HbA1c, using a non-inferiority margin of 0.3%... Regarding ONWARDS 5, subjects on insulin icodec were given a digital titration application (DoseGuide), whereas subjects on the comparator were not, so efficacy results may be questionable. Efficacy results for ONWARDS 5 are not being proposed for the label."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review Memorandum, §1.2 "Statistical Issues," p.6]*

> "For each study, the sponsor targeted the treatment policy estimand. Missing data was addressed using subjects who discontinued treatment or initiated bolus treatment and had their endpoint HbA1c measurement for ONWARDS 1, 2, and 3... For ONWARDS 5, missing data was addressed using subjects who discontinued treatment and had their endpoint HbA1c measurement (retrieved dropouts)... For ONWARDS 4, there was an insufficient number of retrieved dropouts to build the imputation model, so a return-to-baseline approach was taken for the primary analysis."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review Memorandum, §3.2.2 "Statistical Methodologies," p.17-19]*

> "Primary estimand: Treatment policy estimand... Statistical model for the primary analysis: The method of imputing missing data based on subjects who discontinued randomized treatment or initiated bolus insulin treatment for more than 2 weeks prior to the endpoint visit and have their endpoint measurement (ONWARDS 1, 2, 3)... is described as follows... Each dataset will be analyzed using ANCOVA with treatment, and pre-specified fixed effects, and baseline HbA1c as a covariate. Rubin's rule will be applied for inference."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review Memorandum, sensitivity-analysis overturn, p.20-21]*

> "Since the primary objective for each of the ONWARDS studies were to demonstrate non-inferiority, and as missing data may attenuate differences making it easier to conclude non-inferiority when non-inferiority does not exist (i.e., commit a type 1 error), a null imputation was performed... As expected, the LS Mean change from baseline for insulin icodec reduced slightly compared to the RTB analysis and the treatment differences move slightly in favor of the comparator. For ONWARDS 5, there is an overturn in the conclusion from superior to not superior."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review Memorandum, Table 7, primary result for ONWARDS 1]*

> "ONWARDS 1 — Difference in LS Means (95% CI): -0.19 (-0.36, -0.03); P value Non-inferiority: <0.001; Superiority: 0.021."

### 59. Orforglipron (Foundayo) — NDA 220934

**Sponsor:** Eli Lilly and Company

**Indication approved:** To reduce excess body weight and maintain weight reduction long term in adults with obesity, or adults with overweight in the presence of at least one weight-related comorbid condition (oral GLP-1 receptor agonist; note — this NDA's approved indication is weight management, not a type 2 diabetes glycemic-control claim; see note below)

**Approval date:** April 1, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** ATTAIN-1, NCT05869903 (adults with obesity/overweight without diabetes); ATTAIN-2, NCT05872620 (adults with obesity/overweight and type 2 diabetes)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, treatment-regimen estimand as primary with a supportive efficacy estimand
- *Endpoints:* percent change in body weight from baseline, waist circumference, cardiometabolic secondary parameters
- *Primary analysis:* analysis of heterogeneous covariance (ANHECOVA); logistic regression with robust variance for binary endpoints
- *Multiplicity:* Graphical alpha-propagation method (Maurer-Bretz) (family-wise two-sided α=0.05 across primary and key secondary objectives, per estimand, per study)
- *Missing data/bias:* reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan (FDA required a different missing-data imputation model — retrieved-dropout multiple imputation, "RDMI" — for a specific intercurrent-event category than the Applicant used, and re-ran all primary/key-secondary analyses on that basis); two-way tipping-point sensitivity analysis
- *Regulatory:* reviewed under a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher (CNPV)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- **Important note on this NDA's actual scope:** the FDA Multi-Discipline Review for NDA 220934 (Foundayo) states the applicant-proposed and FDA-recommended indication is body-weight reduction/maintenance in adults with obesity or overweight-with-comorbidity — reviewed by the Division of Diabetes, Lipid Disorders, and Obesity under Commissioner's National Priority Voucher priority — supported by ATTAIN-1 (excludes diabetes) and ATTAIN-2 (includes type 2 diabetes as a comorbid population within the weight-management indication). The FDA document does not use the name "ACHIEVE" anywhere and does not describe this NDA as carrying a standalone type 2 diabetes glycemic-control indication; Lilly's separately named ACHIEVE program (glycemic-control trials in T2D) appears to be a distinct clinical program not covered by this specific NDA/approval date as documented in the primary source reviewed here
- ATTAIN-1 and ATTAIN-2 are each Phase 3, multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of oral orforglipron (6 mg, 12 mg, and/or 36 mg once daily, dose-escalated) vs. placebo over 72 weeks, with dietitian-delivered lifestyle counseling in both arms and a blinded independent clinical endpoint committee adjudicating MACE and pancreatic AEs (no DMC)
- ATTAIN-1 population: adults with obesity (BMI ≥30) or overweight (BMI 27-<30) plus ≥1 weight-related comorbidity, without diabetes (N=3,127 randomized: placebo 949, 6 mg 723, 12 mg 725, 36 mg 730)
- ATTAIN-2 population: adults with obesity/overweight and type 2 diabetes (design otherwise parallel to ATTAIN-1)
- Primary objective/endpoint (both trials): superiority of each orforglipron dose vs. placebo in mean percent change in body weight from baseline to Week 72
- Key secondary objectives (multiplicity-controlled via a graphical multiple-testing procedure at family-wise two-sided α=0.05): additional body-weight thresholds, waist circumference, and cardiometabolic parameters
- Primary analysis: the treatment-regimen estimand (average treatment effect regardless of adherence or initiation of prohibited weight-management therapies) was designated primary for labeling, with an efficacy (per-protocol-like) estimand as supportive only; analyzed via ANCOVA (continuous endpoints) or logistic regression with robust variance (binary endpoints), model terms = treatment, region, strata, baseline covariate, plus strata-by-treatment and baseline-by-treatment interactions; pooled-dose vs. placebo contrasts used a linear-contrast average of individual dose estimates
- FDA's disagreement: the Agency rejected the Applicant's prespecified missing-data imputation scheme for one specific intercurrent-event category (study/treatment discontinuation coded as "administrative," SAP category 5B) — absent a pandemic/epidemic-related reason, FDA's preferred approach was retrieved-dropout multiple imputation (RDMI) rather than the Applicant's alternative; FDA additionally required imputing missing baseline values via MAR-by-treatment-group using only observed baseline data (not post-baseline data), and required all randomized subjects (not just those with observed baseline data) be analyzed; FDA re-ran every key secondary endpoint under its preferred imputation approach because the Applicant's approach was judged incompatible with FDA's preferred handling of category 5B, but agreed with the Applicant's ANHECOVA model choice (adopted to accommodate the unequal randomization ratio and obtain robust variance estimates) and with the graphical multiplicity procedure itself
- Result (ATTAIN-1, FDA's preferred re-analysis, Table 23): percentage-change-in-body-weight treatment effect vs. placebo of -5.3% (6 mg), -6.2% (12 mg), and -9.0% (36 mg), all p<0.001; missingness at Week 72 was higher in placebo (23.9%) than in any active-dose arm (13.8-15.8%)
- A data-integrity issue arose from Good Clinical Practice violations at a single ATTAIN-1 site (46 subjects, 1.5% of the trial); the Applicant's own sensitivity analysis excluding that site did not change conclusions, and FDA's primary analyses retained all randomly assigned subjects from that site regardless

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/220934Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (combined summary/clinical/nonclinical/statistical/clinical-pharmacology review) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/220934Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf

[DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(25)02165-8>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41275875/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Orforglipron%2C%20an%20oral%20small-molecule%20GLP-1%20receptor%20agonist%2C%20for%20the%20treatment%20of%20obesity%20in%20people%20with%20type%202%20diabetes)

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, §8, "Statistical analysis plan and amendments," p.97-99]*

> "In ATTAIN-1, treatment-regimen and efficacy estimands were used to evaluate efficacy endpoints. Results of analyses for the treatment-regimen estimand were used for proposed labeling and therefore only treatment-regimen is further discussed here. The treatment-regimen estimand assessed the average treatment effect regardless of participants' adherence or the initiation of prohibited weight management therapies... All data were subsequently analyzed using ANCOVA for continuous endpoints and logistic regression for binary endpoints with robust variance estimations... The primary and key secondary objectives were analyzed using a graphical multiple testing procedure, maintaining a family-wise type I error rate at a two-sided alpha of 0.05 within each estimand for each study."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, FDA's disagreement with the imputation approach, p.98]*

> "FDA disagrees with the Applicant's imputation approaches for the primary analysis... Unless missing was due to the pandemic or epidemic reason, missing values should be imputed using the RDMI. As there were no missing data due to pandemic/epidemic reasons under 5B category in ATTAIN-1 and ATTAIN-2, FDA's preferred primary imputation approach would be the RDMI for category 5B. To account for unequal randomization ratio, and to obtain robust variance estimates, the analysis of heterogeneous covariance (ANHECOVA) was implemented as primary analysis model with covariates as prespecified... FDA agrees with the Applicant's multiplicity control strategy using graphical approach and conduct across all primary and key secondary endpoints, as prespecified in the SAP."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, primary result, Table 8.4/FDA Table 23, p.111-112]*

> "All three orforglipron dose groups resulted in statistically significant greater percentage reduction in body weight compared to placebo. The treatment effect on percentage change in body weight was -5.3%, -6.2%, and -9.0% in the orforglipron 6 mg, 12 mg, and 36 mg, respectively."

### 60. Baxdrostat (Baxfendy) — NDA 219878

**Sponsor:** AstraZeneca AB / AstraZeneca Pharmaceuticals LP

**Indication approved:** In combination with other antihypertensive drugs, for the treatment of hypertension, to lower blood pressure in adults who are not adequately controlled on other agents (trial population spanned uncontrolled hypertension (uHTN) and resistant hypertension (rHTN) cohorts)

**Approval date:** May 15, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** BaxHTN, NCT06034743

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, two-cohort design combining a 12-week fixed double-blind period with a randomized withdrawal design in cohort 2 for maintenance-of-effect assessment
- *Endpoints:* change from baseline in seated systolic blood pressure (SBP), change from baseline in seated diastolic blood pressure (DBP), proportion achieving SBP <130 mmHg
- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA, logistic regression for binary BP-threshold endpoint, Bayesian shrinkage estimation for subgroup treatment effects
- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (each dose tested at one-sided α=0.025, unused alpha carried forward through the secondary-endpoint sequence, 2 mg dose then 1 mg dose)
- *Missing data/bias:* retrieved-dropout (MNAR) and washout (MAR) multiple imputation for missing continuous endpoint data; reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan (FDA found the Applicant's description of its own estimand strategy internally inconsistent with what was actually implemented)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- BaxHTN is a Phase 3, multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of baxdrostat 1 mg or 2 mg once daily vs. placebo in adults with uncontrolled hypertension (seated SBP ≥140 and <170 mmHg on ≥2 antihypertensive agents, cohort 1) or treatment-resistant hypertension (cohort 2, on ≥3 agents including a diuretic); 796 of 2,591 screened subjects were randomized; extensive cardiac/metabolic exclusion criteria (severe LVOT obstruction including obstructive HCM, arrhythmia history, uncontrolled diabetes, severe hepatic/renal impairment, prior MRA use, among others)
- Primary endpoints (co-primary by dose): change from baseline in seated SBP at Week 12 for baxdrostat 2 mg vs. placebo, and separately for 1 mg vs. placebo, with cohort-1/cohort-2 data combined and analyzed without regard to cohort of origin
- Secondary endpoints, in testing-hierarchy order: change in seated SBP between Week 24 and Week 32 during a randomized-withdrawal period (cohort 2 only, 2 mg dose only); change in seated SBP at Week 12 in the resistant-hypertension (rHTN) subpopulation only; change in seated DBP at Week 12; proportion achieving SBP <130 mmHg at Week 12
- Analysis population: Full Analysis Set (FAS) = all randomized 12-week double-blind participants who received ≥1 dose
- Primary analysis method: ANCOVA with treatment and baseline hypertension category (uHTN/rHTN) as factors and baseline SBP as covariate (logistic regression, with baseline SBP as covariate, for the binary <130 mmHg threshold endpoint)
- Missing-data handling: the Applicant described using a "treatment policy" strategy for all analyses, but FDA determined this description was inaccurate — missing data in the baxdrostat arm following rescue-therapy initiation were actually imputed via a hypothetical-MAR "washout" method (MI-WO, imputing a return to a placebo-like trajectory) rather than treatment-policy handling; missing data from other causes (e.g., death) used a straightforward MAR imputation; non-monotone missingness was imputed first, then monotone missingness following treatment discontinuation was imputed under an MNAR assumption using retrieved dropouts (MI-RD) from same-arm subjects who discontinued; 100 multiply-imputed datasets combined via Rubin's rule
- Multiplicity: type I error controlled across doses and the secondary-endpoint hierarchy by testing each primary-endpoint dose comparison at one-sided α=0.025, with the summed significant alpha carried through the secondary sequence, 2 mg first then 1 mg
- Sample size: powered (≈98%) for a 720-subject sample assuming a 6 mmHg true SBP-change difference (SD 15) at a two-sided α=0.025, two-sample t-test
- Protocol was amended April 10, 2024 — after a July 7, 2023 End-of-Phase-2 meeting where the Division raised concerns — to formally specify the treatment-policy strategy (which the Applicant then did not, in FDA's assessment, correctly implement for the rescue-therapy intercurrent event)
- Result: primary endpoint met for both doses — placebo-adjusted seated-SBP reduction of -8.7 mmHg (95% CI -11.5, -5.8) for 1 mg and -9.8 mmHg (95% CI -12.6, -7.0) for 2 mg, both p<0.0001

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2026/219878Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/219878Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Clinical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/219878Orig1s000MedR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06034743 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2507109), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40888730/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Efficacy%20and%20Safety%20of%20Baxdrostat%20in%20Uncontrolled%20and%20Resistant%20Hypertension)
- Trial-design publication: "Baxdrostat for uncontrolled and resistant hypertension: rationale and design of the Phase 3 clinical trials BaxHTN, BaxAsia, and Bax24." *Hypertens Res.* 2025;48:2911-2923. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41440-025-02297-7), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40850955/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Baxdrostat%20for%20uncontrolled%20and%20resistant%20hypertension%20rationale%20and%20design%20BaxHTN%20BaxAsia%20Bax24)

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting is recorded for this application in the reviewed documents.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Clinical Review, §7.1.1.3 "Study Endpoints, BaxHTN," p.37]*

> "The primary endpoints in BaxHTN were change from baseline in seated systolic blood pressure at Week 12 for baxdrostat 2 mg once daily compared to placebo and for baxdrostat 1 mg once daily compared to placebo. In the analysis of these endpoints, the data from the two cohorts were combined and analyzed without regard to the cohort of origin."

*[verbatim, FDA Clinical Review, §7.1.1.4 "Statistical Analysis Plan, BaxHTN," p.37-38]*

> "BaxHTN week-12 seated systolic and diastolic blood pressures were analyzed using an analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) model with treatment and HTN category at baseline (uHTN, rHTN) as factors, and with baseline value as a covariate... For all analyses, the Applicant incorrectly stated that a treatment policy strategy was used, with analyzed data including all available measurements regardless of treatment discontinuation or initiation of rescue therapy. In alignment with the treatment policy strategy, participants who permanently discontinued treatment were asked to attend the remainder of the study visits and perform the study assessments indicated in the protocol. However, in contrast to a treatment policy strategy, missing data in the baxdrostat arm following initiation of rescue therapy were imputed with a washout method (MI-WO), a hypothetical MAR (missing at random) strategy based on return to placebo... To control type 1 error over multiple endpoints and doses, analyses were conducted in a hierarchy sequence... For the primary endpoint, each dose was tested at the 0.025 level of significance, with the sum of significant tested levels carried through the secondary endpoints, first for the 2 mg dose, then for the 1 mg dose."

*[verbatim, FDA Clinical Review, protocol amendment note, p.38]*

> "The protocol was amended on April 10, 2024 to indicate that a treatment policy strategy would be used to handle the intercurrent event of rescue therapy. This change was made following the July 7, 2023, end-of-phase 2 meeting, at which the Division expressed concern about the Applicant's proposed strategy."

*[verbatim, FDA Clinical Review, Table 19, primary endpoint result, p.48]*

> "Δ seated SBP W12 — Placebo -5.8 (N=263); Baxdrostat 1 mg -14.5 (N=264), Diff -8.7 (95% CI -11.5,-5.8), p<0.0001; Baxdrostat 2 mg -15.7 (N=266), Diff -9.8 (95% CI -12.6,-7.0), p<0.0001."

### 61. Enlicitide decanoate (Lipfendra) — NDA 220848

**Sponsor:** Merck Sharp & Dohme LLC

**Indication approved:** Indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to reduce low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) in adults with hypercholesterolemia, including heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH) (oral PCSK9 inhibitor)

**Approval date:** July 15, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** CORALreef Lipids (protocol P013/MK-0616-013), NCT05952856; supportive trials CORALreef HeFH (P017), NCT05952869, and CORALreef AddOn (P018), NCT06450366

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (CORALreef Lipids, CORALreef HeFH); randomized, double-blind, active- and placebo-controlled 4-arm design vs. ezetimibe and/or bempedoic acid (CORALreef AddOn)
- *Endpoints:* percent change in LDL-C from baseline, percent change in non-HDL-C/ApoB, percent change in Lp(a)
- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA with nested bootstrap-within-multiple-imputation; Stratified Wilcoxon rank-sum test (aligned rank-stratified variant, for the Lp(a) secondary endpoint)
- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (H1 primary, then ordered secondary hypotheses H2-H5, testing stopped at the first one-sided p≥0.025; overall one-sided α=0.025)
- *Missing data/bias:* reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan (FDA disputed the analysis population definition, intercurrent-event handling, and — most notably — a post-hoc revision to the LDL-C data-handling rule made by the Applicant after database unblinding)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- CORALreef Lipids (P013) is a Phase 3, multi-center, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of oral enlicitide 20 mg once daily vs. placebo, added to background statin therapy (or documented statin intolerance), in adults with hypercholesterolemia including HeFH, with or without prior major ASCVD (N=2,912 enrolled across 167 sites/14 countries; FAS N=2,904 per Applicant, N=2,907 per FDA's preferred population)
- CORALreef HeFH (P017) mirrors P013's design and SAP in a dedicated heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia population (N=303); CORALreef AddOn (P018) is a randomized, active-controlled, 4-arm trial of enlicitide vs. bempedoic acid vs. ezetimibe vs. their combination over a shorter (56-day) primary endpoint window (N=301)
- Primary endpoint (P013/P017): mean percent change from baseline in LDL-C at Week 24; key secondary endpoints: mean percent change in LDL-C at Week 52, mean percent change in non-HDL-C and ApoB at Week 24, percent change in Lp(a) at Week 24
- Analysis population: Full Analysis Set (FAS) per the sponsor's SAP = all randomized subjects who received ≥1 dose of double-blind study intervention and had baseline endpoint data, excluding subjects discovered to be enrolled at more than one enlicitide study/site; FDA disagreed with excluding such subjects, preferring all randomized-and-treated subjects
- Primary analysis method: ANCOVA with treatment and stratification factors (renal function, geographic region) as fixed effects and baseline LDL-C as covariate; missing data imputed via a washout-imputation (WI) method as primary, with return-to-baseline as sensitivity, using a nested procedure of 100 multiple imputations within each of 1,000 bootstrap samples, then combining across the 1,000 bootstrap estimates; Lp(a) analyzed via an aligned rank-stratified Wilcoxon test with multiple-imputation-based missing-data handling
- Multiplicity: sequential (fixed-sequence) testing of H1 (primary) through H5 (ordered secondary endpoints), stopping at the first hypothesis with a one-sided p-value ≥0.025, strongly controlling one-sided type I error at 0.025
- LDL-C data-handling controversy: the SAP prespecified that unreportable/≤0 beta-quantification (BQ) LDL-C values be converted to 1 mg/dL; after database unblinding, the Applicant instead implemented a revised rule treating those values as missing and substituting Martin-Hopkins (MH) values where available — motivated by extreme outlier percent-changes produced by the original rule, but changed only after seeing unblinded data
- FDA's assessment explicitly flagged this as a post-hoc, post-unblinding change and stated it "raises concerns about the integrity of study results," even though both the prespecified and revised rules produced statistically significant, broadly consistent treatment effects; FDA also required death be treated as an intercurrent event with the worst-observed-value imputed (rather than the Applicant's washout imputation for deaths) and requested/received a supplementary analysis on that basis
- Result (P013, Applicant's revised-rule analysis): LDL-C difference from placebo of -59.7% (95% CI -62.3, -57.1), p<0.001; FDA's own preferred-method analysis (all randomized/treated subjects, SAP-prespecified data handling) estimated a difference of -55.8% (95% CI -60.9, -50.7) — FDA agreed the primary endpoint was met under either approach

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Table 3 "Applicant - Key Elements of the Statistical Plan (P013)," p.59]*

> "The primary efficacy analysis compared the mean percent change from baseline in LDL-C at Week 24 using an ANCOVA model with treatment and stratification factors (renal function and geographic region) as fixed effects and baseline LDL-C as a covariate... Missing data were imputed using the WI imputation method as the primary analysis method and return to baseline imputation method as the sensitivity analysis method... Testing was performed in order of the primary and ordered secondary efficacy endpoints with hypotheses and was stopped with the first comparison that had a one-sided p-value ≥0.025... The multiplicity strategy strongly controls the Type I error at 0.025 (one-sided)."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, LDL-C data-handling revision and FDA's integrity concern, p.60-61]*

> "After database lock and study unblinding, the Applicant implemented a revised LDL-C data handling rule. This revision modified one aspect of the prespecified procedure: BQ results of 'calculated LDL unreportable' remained as missing rather than being converted to 1 mg/dL... This change was motivated by seeing extreme outliers of percentage change values due to baseline values being set to 1... Prespecification of analytical methods helps ensure that the analysis plan is developed based on scientific and statistical considerations rather than observed results. Changing data-handling rules posthoc, particularly after unblinding, raises concerns about the integrity of study results... this issue was foreseeable and ideally should have been addressed earlier during the blinded data review and in the original statistical analysis plan."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, primary endpoint result and FDA's own analysis, p.74-75]*

> "The FDA agrees that the trial met the primary endpoint using the SAP prespecified method. The observed mean percentage change from baseline in LDL-C at Week 24 was -57.1% (SD 101.0) in the enlicitide group and 3.0% (SD 32.5) in the placebo group. The difference in model estimated mean percentage change from baseline in LDL-C at Week 24 between the enlicitide group and the placebo group was -55.8% (95% confidence intervals [CI]: -60.9%, -50.7%)... Using this posthoc revised LDL-C data handling in Applicant Table 8, which yielded a treatment difference of -59.7% (95% CI: -62.3%, -57.1%)... But changing data-handling rules posthoc, particularly after unblinding, should be generally discouraged. Thus, this analysis will only be considered as a supplementary analysis."

## Infectious Disease

### 1. Boceprevir (Victrelis) — NDA 202258

**Sponsor:** Schering Corporation (Schering-Plough; acquired by Merck & Co. in 2009)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of chronic hepatitis C (CHC) genotype 1 infection, in combination with peginterferon alfa and ribavirin, in adult patients 18 years of age and older, with compensated liver disease including cirrhosis, who are previously untreated or who have failed previous interferon and ribavirin therapy

**Approval date:** May 13, 2011

**Pivotal trial:** SPRINT-2 (Schering protocol P05216), NCT00705432

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, three-arm trial (fixed-sequence step-down comparisons of two boceprevir regimens vs. one control), race-stratified independent cohorts (non-Black cohort and Black cohort randomized and analyzed separately within one protocol), event-triggered futility stopping rule
- *Endpoints:* sustained virologic response (SVR), defined as undetectable HCV RNA at follow-up week 24 (primary)
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by baseline factors
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (boceprevir fixed-duration arm vs. control tested first, then response-guided-therapy arm vs. control only if the first comparison was significant)
- *Missing data/bias:* earlier-timepoint carry-forward imputation for the primary responder endpoint (missing follow-up-week-24 result counted as SVR if follow-up-week-12 was undetectable)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter Phase III trial in treatment-naive genotype 1 chronic hepatitis C; a non-Black cohort (~938 subjects) and a separate Black cohort (≥159 subjects) were enrolled and randomized independently under one protocol, reflecting the known lower response rate to interferon-based therapy in Black patients
- Three arms: Arm 1 (control) — peginterferon alfa-2b/ribavirin (PR) for 48 weeks plus placebo; Arm 2 — boceprevir response-guided therapy (RGT): 4-week PR lead-in, then triple therapy with duration determined by on-treatment virologic response; Arm 3 — fixed-duration boceprevir: 4-week PR lead-in plus 44 weeks of triple therapy
- Randomization stratified by screening HCV RNA viral load (≤400,000 vs. >400,000 IU/mL) and HCV genotype 1 subtype (1a vs. 1b)
- Primary endpoint: SVR, defined as undetectable plasma HCV RNA at follow-up week 24 in the Full Analysis Set (FAS); a subject missing the follow-up-week-24 value but undetectable at follow-up week 12 was counted as an SVR
- Key secondary endpoint (mITT population — subjects who received ≥1 dose of boceprevir/placebo, i.e., completed the PR lead-in): undetectable HCV RNA at follow-up week 24
- Futility rule: detectable HCV RNA at treatment week 24 triggered discontinuation of all study treatment
- Sample size: ~930 non-Black subjects (310/arm) planned for 90% power to detect a 13-percentage-point absolute improvement in SVR (58% vs. an assumed 45% control rate) using a two-sided chi-square test at alpha=0.05; the Black cohort (≥150 subjects) was not powered for a formal comparison, sized instead to estimate the treatment difference within roughly ±14% via a two-sided 95% CI
- Primary analysis: two-sided CMH chi-square test adjusted for the baseline stratification factors; type-I error across the two boceprevir-vs-control comparisons was controlled by a step-down procedure — Arm 3 vs. Arm 1 tested first, and only if that comparison was significant at 0.05 was Arm 2 vs. Arm 1 tested at the same level using the same CMH test

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2011/202258lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/202258Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Medical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/202258Orig1s000MedR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00705432 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)
- Pivotal publication: Poordad F, McCone J Jr, Bacon BR, et al.; SPRINT-2 Investigators. "Boceprevir for untreated chronic HCV genotype 1 infection." *N Engl J Med.* 2011;364(13):1195-1206. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1010494), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21449783/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Boceprevir%20for%20untreated%20chronic%20HCV%20genotype%201%20infection)

**Other resources**

- Merck (successor sponsor) participates in general cross-industry IPD-sharing platforms (e.g., Vivli); trial-specific SPRINT-2 availability was not individually confirmed here.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was referenced in the Statistical Review text for this NDA; not independently confirmed beyond that document.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 202258, p.18-19]* — "This is a randomized, multicenter study, double-blinded for boceprevir or placebo in combination with open-label PegIntron (PEG) and ribavirin (RBV)... There are three arms: Arm 1 [control, PR48], Arm 2 [response-guided therapy, RGT], Arm 3 [fixed 44-week boceprevir, BOC/PR48]."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, p.19]* — "The primary efficacy endpoint is the achievement of SVR, defined as undetectable plasma HCV-RNA at Follow-up Week (FW) 24 based on the Full Analysis Set (FAS). If a subject is missing FW24 data and has undetectable HCV-RNA level at FW12, the subject would be considered an SVR."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, p.20]* — "All primary and secondary efficacy analyses will be carried out using the two-sided Cochran-Mantel Haenszel (CMH) chi-square test (adjusted for the baseline stratification factors)... In order to control the type 1 error for the two comparisons (Arm 3 vs. Control, and Arm 2 vs. Control)... [a] step-down approach was used to control multiplicity. First, Arm 3 will be compared against the control arm (Arm 1)... If this p-value is less than 0.05, ... the next comparison will be carried out, i.e., ... Arm 2 will be compared against the control arm using the same CMH test."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, p.20]* — sample-size justification: "90% power to detect a combined 13% improvement in the SVR rate, assuming a control SVR rate of 45% (i.e., 58% vs. 45%) using a 2-sided chi-square test at alpha = 0.05."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, p.52]* — results: "SVR rates in subjects who received boceprevir treatment were 63% and 66% in RGT and BOC/PR48 arms, respectively, vs. 38% in the control arm (P<.0001)."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, p.119-120]* — conclusions: "These two key phase 3 studies have demonstrated that boceprevir plus PR is efficacious for HCV-1a or HCV-1b infected subjects in both treatment-naïve (SVR rates of 63-66% in BOC contained arms vs. 38% in control arm)..." with an explicit caveat about lower SVR rates in the Black cohort (42-53%) and an underpowered late-responder duration question the review flags as statistically unresolved.

### 2. Rilpivirine (Edurant) — NDA 202022

**Sponsor:** Tibotec, Inc. (Janssen)

**Indication approved:** EDURANT (rilpivirine) tablets in combination with other antiretroviral agents for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in treatment-naive adult patients

**Approval date:** May 20, 2011

**Pivotal trial:** ECHO (TMC278-C209, NCT00540449) and THRIVE (TMC278-C215, NCT00543725) — two identically-designed Phase III trials analyzed separately by FDA (not pooled)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, two identically-designed trials analyzed independently rather than pooled
- *Endpoints:* virologic response, HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL at week 48 (primary; sponsor's protocol-specified TLOVR algorithm for secondary/supportive analyses, FDA's preferred Snapshot algorithm for the primary regulatory analysis) (FDA Snapshot algorithm)
- *Primary analysis:* non-inferiority analysis of stratified difference in response proportions (12% margin), intention-to-treat population
- *Missing data/bias:* FDA Snapshot algorithm (premature discontinuation/missing data counted as failure at all subsequent visits)
- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented FDA-directed pre-submission change in primary analysis algorithm, DMC partial-unblinding review of a safety signal without a protocol change

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Two Phase III, multinational, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled trials (rilpivirine 25 mg once daily vs. efavirenz 600 mg once daily, each plus 2 background NRTIs) in treatment-naive HIV-1-infected adults; ~680 subjects randomized 1:1 per trial
- Randomization stratified by screening plasma HIV-1 RNA (≤100,000; >100,000-≤500,000; >500,000 copies/mL)
- Primary endpoint (protocol-specified): proportion of subjects with plasma HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL at week 48 by TLOVR (time to loss of virologic response) algorithm, intention-to-treat population, non-inferiority margin 12%
- FDA's own primary regulatory analysis instead used the Snapshot algorithm (simple proportion responding at week 48, missing/discontinuation = failure); per the review, FDA had communicated this preference to the sponsor before submission, so the sponsor provided the primary analysis using Snapshot while all other analyses (secondary endpoints, subgroups) remained TLOVR-based
- Key finding driving the label and later development: virologic response was statistically inferior to efavirenz in the subgroup with baseline viral load >100,000 copies/mL, while rilpivirine showed statistically significantly fewer adverse-event-related discontinuations than efavirenz across both high- and low-viral-load subgroups — FDA's review explicitly frames the overall non-inferiority conclusion as resting on what is "effectively a composite endpoint of efficacy and safety" because TLOVR/Snapshot both classify AE-driven discontinuation as failure
- A pre-specified interim DSMB review found an increased rate of virologic failure in the high-baseline-viral-load rilpivirine stratum and recommended partial unblinding to a sponsor review committee; after review, the DSMB could not draw a definitive safety conclusion and recommended the trials continue unchanged to week 48
- Analysis populations: intention-to-treat (ITT — all randomized subjects who took ≥1 dose, regardless of protocol adherence/eligibility) for the primary analysis; per-protocol as a supportive analysis
- Missing/censored viral-load handling: left-censored (below quantification limit) values scored as 49 copies/mL, right-censored (above upper limit) scored as 750,001 copies/mL for continuous summaries; subjects who discontinued were counted as failures (non-responders) at all subsequent scheduled visits

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 202022, p.7]* — "Both are Phase III, multi-national, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled trials to compare the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of TMC278 25 mg q.d. vs. EFV 600 mg q.d. in treatment-naïve HIV-1 infected subjects... approximately 680 subjects [per trial] to TMC278... and EFV... in a 1:1 ratio. Randomization... stratified by screening plasma viral load (strata were ≤100,000; >100,000 to ≤500,000; and >500,000 copies/ml)."

*[verbatim, p.7]* — "the primary efficacy parameter was planned to be the proportion of subjects with plasma viral load <50 copies/ml at Week 48 (TLOVR), based on an ITT population... with a maximum allowable difference of 12%."

*[verbatim, p.3]* — "while TMC278 demonstrates its statistically significant superiority over EFV in terms of reduction in adverse events (AE), it also demonstrates its statistically significant inferiority relative to EFV in terms of virologic suppression... TMC278's inferior virologic suppression is primarily driven by subjects with high baseline viral loads [>100,000 copies/mL]... its superior ability of reduction in AE... is demonstrated in subjects with either high or low baseline viral loads." And: "We conclude that TMC278 is noninferior to EFV. The conclusion is based on the analysis of the pre-specified and commonly used primary endpoint, which is a composite endpoint of efficacy and safety (AEs)."

*[verbatim, p.19]* — "FDA reviewers now prefer a simpler endpoint, the proportion of subjects responding at Week 48, referred [to] as [the] Snapshot approach... Since FDA communicated with the sponsor about the current preference of [the] snapshot algorithm prior to the submission, the sponsor has provided the primary analysis based on the snapshot results. On the other hand, all other analyses, including analyses for secondary endpoints, subgroups analyses, are based on the TLOVR algorithms."

*[verbatim, p.19]* — "Subjects who prematurely discontinued the trial were considered non-responders at all subsequent visits after discontinuation... All the missing data were treated as failures. This is a traditional treatment of the missing in the HIV trials and was considered appropriate."

*[verbatim, p.7-8]* — on the DSMB review: the committee identified "an ongoing increased risk of virologic failure in the subjects receiving TMC278 with high baseline viral load (>100k)" at a planned interim look, and recommended partial unblinding of that stratum to the Sponsor Review Committee; "After detailed review and discussion of the available data, the DSMB agreed that they were unable to draw definitive conclusions regarding the presence of a safety concern related to virologic failure and thus recommended the study continue unchanged through week 48."

### 3. Telaprevir (Incivek) — NDA 201917

**Sponsor:** Vertex Pharmaceuticals

**Indication approved:** Treatment of genotype 1 chronic hepatitis C, in combination with peginterferon alfa and ribavirin, in adult patients with compensated liver disease including cirrhosis, who are treatment-naive or who have failed previous interferon-based therapy

**Approval date:** May 23, 2011

**Pivotal trial:** ADVANCE (Trial 108), NCT00627926 — companion trials ILLUMINATE (Trial 111, response-guided duration in treatment-naive eRVR responders) and REALIZE (Trial 216, NCT01023035-type retreatment trial in prior treatment failures) supported labeling for those respective populations

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, three-arm trial (two telaprevir durations vs. control)
- *Endpoints:* sustained virologic response (SVR24 — undetectable HCV RNA at end of treatment and 24 weeks later)
- *Primary analysis:* logistic regression (treatment, genotype 1 subtype, baseline HCV RNA category)
- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation for missing follow-up HCV RNA (missing = failure), FDA cross-check against week-72-from-start regardless of actual treatment duration
- *Regulatory:* FDA Antiviral Drugs Advisory Committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ADVANCE: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter Phase III trial in treatment-naive genotype 1 chronic hepatitis C; N=1095 (365/365/365) randomized to T8PR (telaprevir 8 weeks + PR), T12PR (telaprevir 12 weeks + PR), or PR48 (control, PR alone 48 weeks); a superiority design
- Primary endpoint: SVR, defined as HCV RNA below the limit of quantitation (BLQ) both at planned end of treatment and 24 weeks later (SVR24); FDA reviewers additionally cross-checked the undetectable-virus endpoint at week 72 from treatment start regardless of whether treatment ended at week 24 or 48
- Primary analysis: logistic regression predicting SVR from treatment arm, HCV genotype 1 subtype (1a vs. non-1a), and baseline HCV RNA category (<800,000 vs. ≥800,000 IU/mL)
- ILLUMINATE (Trial 111): open-label, randomized, response-guided-duration trial in treatment-naive patients achieving extended rapid virologic response (eRVR) at week 12 on telaprevir+PR, comparing 24 vs. 48 total weeks of PR; a non-inferiority design, margin 10.5% (24-week regimen declared non-inferior if the 95% lower confidence bound for the difference exceeded −10.5%); primary analysis used a normal-approximation interval, with logistic regression (treatment, subtype, race) and a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel interval as supportive analyses
- REALIZE (Trial 216): double-blind, placebo-controlled, three-arm retreatment trial (telaprevir 12 weeks, telaprevir 12 weeks with a delayed start, or placebo, all plus PR48) in patients who failed prior interferon-based therapy (relapsers, partial responders, null responders); logistic regression included treatment, prior-response type, baseline HCV RNA, and a treatment-by-prior-response interaction term; missing week-72 data was imputed as failure
- Missing-data handling across all three trials: last-observation-carried-forward-style imputation of undetectable status was noted by the reviewer to be conservative given the low relapse rates observed among subjects who achieved suppression at end of treatment (5-7% in treatment-naive patients, 9-11% in prior treatment failures)

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2011/201917lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/201917Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Medical Review (confirms ADVANCE/ILLUMINATE/REALIZE trial-name-to-number mapping and the April 28, 2011 Antiviral Products Advisory Committee meeting) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/201917Orig1s000MedR.pdf

"Telaprevir for previously untreated chronic hepatitis C virus infection." *N Engl J Med.* 2011;364(25):2405-2416. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1012912), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21696307/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Telaprevir%20for%20previously%20untreated%20chronic%20hepatitis%20C%20virus%20infection)

**Other resources**

- Vertex participates in general cross-industry IPD-sharing platforms; trial-specific ADVANCE availability was not individually confirmed here.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 201917, §2.2.4.2, p.12]* — "In all three trials, the primary efficacy variable was the percent of subjects with sustained viral response (SVR), defined as HCV RNA below limit of quantitation (BLQ) both at planned end of therapy and 24 weeks later. The FDA reviewers also expect the endpoint of undetectable virus to be met at week 72 from start of therapy, regardless of whether treatment ended at week 24 or 48."

*[verbatim, §2.2.5, p.12]* — "Trials 108 and 216 were superiority trials; trial 111 was a non-inferiority trial with the rule for declaring 24 weeks of RBV+PI as non-inferior to 48 weeks of RBV+PI... [being] that a 95% lower confidence bound for the difference was greater than -10.5%."

*[verbatim, §5, Statistical Reviewer's Conclusions, p.67]* — "The applicant has demonstrated in three trials that telaprevir is an effective treatment of genotype 1 chronic Hepatitis C when used for 12 weeks at the indicated dose in combination with 48 weeks of peg-interferon and ribavirin... The benefit manifests itself as a 25-30% increase in percentage SVR24 in naive subjects and as a ~50% increase in percentage SVR24 in prior failures."

*[verbatim, §5, p.68]* — "The relapse rate for subjects achieving suppression at EOT is only 5-7% for naïve subjects and 9-11% for previous failures on PI+RBV... suggesting that in future submissions with direct acting anti-virals using LOCF to impute missing data will be conservative."

### 4. Fidaxomicin (Dificid) — NDA 201699

**Sponsor:** Optimer Pharmaceuticals

**Indication approved:** Treatment of Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea (CDAD) in adults

**Approval date:** May 27, 2011

**Pivotal trial:** Study 003 (protocol 101-1-C-003, NCT00314951) and Study 004 (protocol 101-1-C-004, NCT00468728) — two identically-designed Phase III non-inferiority trials vs. oral vancomycin

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, non-inferiority-then-superiority hierarchy, two identically-designed trials
- *Endpoints:* clinical cure at end of treatment (primary), global/sustained cure — clinical cure with no recurrence through the end of follow-up (key secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified difference in proportions (non-inferiority CI), superiority CI for global cure
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence hierarchical testing (non-inferiority on clinical cure gating the superiority test on global cure), described in the review's own header as a "gate-keeping multiple testing strategy"
- *Missing data/bias:* multiple pre-specified sensitivity definitions of failure (deaths, early assessment, concomitant CDAD medication counted as failure under FDA's preferred sensitivity analysis)
- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented mid-trial endpoint elevation (FDA feedback-driven) — global cure changed from exploratory to secondary at sponsor's request during Study 004, FDA Advisory Committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Two identically-designed, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled (oral vancomycin 125 mg four times daily x10 days) Phase III trials of fidaxomicin 200 mg twice daily x10 days for CDAD; Study 003 (US/Canada), Study 004 (US/Canada/Western Europe); randomization stratified by CDAD history (no prior episode vs. one prior episode within the last 3 months)
- Primary endpoint: clinical cure at end of treatment — a clinician's assessment of no need for additional CDAD therapy within 2 days of the end of treatment (day 10) — analyzed as a non-inferiority comparison, margin 10%, proposed by the applicant and agreed at a Type B pre-NDA meeting (July 1, 2010) based on historical vancomycin-vs-tolevamer superiority-trial data
- Key secondary endpoint: global cure (clinical cure at end of treatment with no recurrence through the end of the follow-up period, ≥36 days from study start) — analyzed as a superiority comparison, supporting the drug's differentiating claim of a lower recurrence rate rather than a higher cure rate
- A second Phase III trial (Study 004) was required by FDA at a July 13, 2005 meeting because a single non-inferiority trial was not considered sufficient; global cure was changed from an exploratory to a secondary endpoint for the ongoing Study 004 at the sponsor's request at a September 18, 2009 Type C meeting — after Study 003 results were already known
- Results (mITT): clinical cure 88% fidaxomicin vs. 86% vancomycin (Study 003), 88% vs. 87% (Study 004) — non-inferiority margin met in both; global cure 74% vs. 64% (Study 003), 77% vs. 63% (Study 004) — superiority shown, with FDA's preferred sensitivity analysis (treating deaths, early assessment, and concomitant CDAD medication as failures) giving somewhat lower but still superior rates (71% vs. 57%, and 72% vs. 59%)
- A pre-specified subgroup concern: the global-cure treatment effect was attenuated and not statistically significant among subjects with the virulent (e.g., NAP1/BI/027) C. difficile strain in Study 003 (interaction p=0.009), a pattern not replicated in Study 004 (interaction p=0.29)
- Analysis populations: modified intention-to-treat (mITT — randomized subjects who received ≥1 dose of study drug and had confirmed CDAD)

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2011/201699s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (plus a May 18, 2011 addendum re-analyzing global cure at study day 36 vs. the original day-31 cutoff) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/201699Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Medical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/201699Orig1s000MedR.pdf

And: "The primary endpoint of clinical cure at end of treatment is a clinician's assessment of the need for no additional CDAD therapy within two days of the end of treatment (day 10)... The key secondary endpoint of global cure at the end of treatment is a composite of clinical cure at the end of treatment with no recurrence until the end of the follow up period."

Global Cure changed from exploratory to secondary endpoint (at the request of the applicant) for the ongoing Phase 3 study 004." And: "July 1, 2010 — Type B Meeting... Adequacy of 10% non-inferiority margin based on the proposed justification was agreed to."

*[verbatim, p.5]* — on the virulent-strain subgroup finding: "There are concerns for global cure that the treatment effect of fidaxomicin relative to vancomycin was significantly decreased for subjects with the C. Difficile virulent strain in comparison to those with the non-virulent strain."

### 5. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (Stribild) — NDA 203100

**Sponsor:** Gilead Sciences

**Indication approved:** A complete regimen for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in adults 18 years of age and over who are antiretroviral (ARV)-naive or who have no known substitutions associated with resistance to the individual components

**Approval date:** August 27, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** Study 102 (GS-US-236-0102, NCT01095796, vs. efavirenz/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF) and Study 103 (GS-US-236-0103, NCT01106586, vs. ritonavir-boosted atazanavir + emtricitabine/tenofovir DF)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, two identically-structured trials against two different active regimens
- *Endpoints:* virologic success, HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL at week 48 by FDA-defined Snapshot algorithm (primary)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) chi-square test, non-inferiority difference-in-proportions (12% margin)
- *Missing data/bias:* FDA Snapshot algorithm; TLOVR analysis conducted as a concordant supportive analysis
- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented investigation of a randomization-file/IVRS date-generation discrepancy, concluded to have no material effect on randomization integrity

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Two Phase III, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, multicenter trials in treatment-naive HIV-1-infected adults comparing the elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF (E/C/F/TDF) single-tablet regimen against efavirenz/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF (Study 102) or ritonavir-boosted atazanavir plus emtricitabine/tenofovir DF (Study 103)
- Randomization stratified by screening HIV-1 RNA level (≤100,000 vs. >100,000 copies/mL), and by region in Study 103
- Primary endpoint: percentage of subjects with virologic success (HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL) at week 48 by the FDA-defined Snapshot algorithm; non-inferiority margin of −12% (a "clinical," M2-type margin, not the smaller statistical M1 margin) using a two-sided 95% CI
- Primary analysis: two-sided stratum-adjusted Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) chi-square test adjusted for the baseline stratification factors, used to estimate the odds ratio, corresponding 95% CI, and p-values
- Three pre-specified sensitivity analyses probed robustness of the primary result to non-efficacy discontinuers with a last viral load <50 copies/mL (excluded from both numerator and denominator; counted as success) and to potential confounding by region/baseline viral load (comparing region-only-stratified and unstratified CMH analyses against the primary baseline-viral-load-stratified analysis)
- Secondary endpoint: time-to-loss-of-virologic-response, analyzed via Kaplan-Meier estimates and a log-rank test stratified by baseline HIV-1 RNA category
- Results: virologic success 87.6% (305/348) E/C/F/TDF vs. 84.1% (296/352) efavirenz-based regimen (Study 102); 89.5% (316/353) E/C/F/TDF vs. 86.8% (308/355) atazanavir/ritonavir-based regimen (Study 103); lower bound of the 95% CI for the difference was −1.6% and −1.9% respectively, both well within the −12% margin, with TLOVR analyses giving concordant results
- FDA's review documents an investigation into a randomization-file discrepancy in Study 103 (an incorrect IVRS-vendor-generated date, traced to a vendor typographic/programming error) and concluded randomization stratification integrity was not materially affected

- FDA Statistical Review (posted as an "Addendum to the Statistical Review and Evaluation, Clinical Studies," containing the full primary-analysis methodology) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203100Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203100Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (Study 102) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01095796 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (Study 103) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01106586 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)

[DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(12)60917-9>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22748591/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Co-formulated%20elvitegravir%20cobicistat%20emtricitabine%20tenofovir%20versus%20efavirenz%20emtricitabine%20tenofovir)

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review (Addendum), NDA 203100]* — "The primary objective of both phase 3 studies is to evaluate the efficacy of E/C/F/T versus a regimen containing ATR or ATV/r + TVD in HIV-1 infected ARV treatment-naive adult subjects. The non-inferiority margin used in both studies was -12%, which is a clinical margin. The primary efficacy endpoint is the percentage of subjects with virologic success (ie, HIV-1 RNA < 50 copies/mL) at Week 48 using the FDA-defined snapshot analysis."

*[verbatim]* — "These two key phase 3 studies have demonstrated that the E/C/F/T STR was noninferior to ATR or ATV/r + TVD. The lower bound of the 2-sided 95% CI of the difference in virologic success rate was −1.6% for (E/C/F/T – ATR) and −1.9% for (E/C/F/T – (ATV/r + TVD)), which were greater than the pre-specified −12% noninferiority margin. The results are robust because the TLOVR analysis provided very similar results."

*[verbatim]* — "The NI margins used in these two pivotal studies... were 12% in the treatment naïve population... This NI margin is a clinical margin, so-called M2, not the M1 margin... Clinically the response that we would be willing to give up in terms of undetectable rate of 48 weeks of treatment in treatment-naïve population is about 12% (i.e., M2, the clinical margin)."

*[verbatim]* — "The percentage of subjects with virologic success at Week 48 was used to assess treatment noninferiority of the E/C/F/T STR compared with the ATR STR using a conventional 95% CI approach, with a noninferiority margin of 12%. All primary and secondary efficacy analyses will be carried out using the two-sided stratum-adjusted Mantel Haenszel (MH) chi-square test (adjusted for the baseline stratification factors)."

*[verbatim]* — randomization: "Randomization was stratified by HIV-1 RNA level (≤ 100,000 copies/mL or > 100,000 copies/mL)."

*[verbatim]* — on TLOVR/secondary analysis: "The time-to-loss-of-virologic-response will be analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier estimates and the log rank test stratified by the baseline HIV-1 RNA level (≤100,000 copies/mL versus >100,000 copies/mL)."
