### 6. Raxibacumab (unbranded) — BLA 125349

**Sponsor:** Human Genome Sciences

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adult and pediatric patients with inhalational anthrax due to Bacillus anthracis in combination with appropriate antibacterial drugs, and for prophylaxis of inhalational anthrax when alternative therapies are not available or are not appropriate. Limitations of use: "The effectiveness of raxibacumab is based solely on efficacy studies in animal models of inhalational anthrax."

**Approval date:** December 14, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** No human efficacy trial — approved under 21 CFR 601, Subpart H ("Approval of Biological Products When Human Efficacy Studies Are Not Ethical or Feasible," the BLA/biologic-side counterpart of the Animal Rule) based on two animal efficacy studies: rabbit Study 682-G005758 and cynomolgus monkey Study 724-G005829 (plus a resubmission "added-benefit" rabbit study, 1141-CG920871, and a histopathology/CNS study, 1103-G923704), bridged to humans via PK/PD and human safety/PK data. None of the animal studies is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov — expected, since they are preclinical studies rather than human trials

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Animal Rule efficacy basis (no human efficacy trial; regular approval grounded in randomized, placebo-controlled animal-model survival studies plus human PK bridging)
- *Endpoints:* survival at a pre-specified day (day 14 in rabbits, day 28 in monkeys)
- *Primary analysis:* two-sided Fisher's exact test (survival-rate comparison), unconditional exact confidence interval for the risk difference
- *Missing data/bias:* logistic-regression check for a spore-dose (LD50) confounding effect on survival
- *Regulatory:* Complete Response Letter followed by resubmission and approval (FDA required a new "added-benefit" animal study post-CRL), population-PK-based dose extrapolation to pediatric patients absent any human pediatric efficacy or PK data

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Pivotal efficacy basis: two randomized, blinded, placebo-controlled animal monotherapy studies of raxibacumab in lethal aerosolized Bacillus anthracis spore-challenge models — New Zealand White rabbits (Study 682-G005758, survival assessed at day 14) and cynomolgus monkeys (Study 724-G005829, survival assessed at day 28) — each comparing a single IV dose of raxibacumab to placebo with no concurrent antibiotic
- Results: rabbit study, 0/13 (0%) placebo vs. 6/17 (35.3%) raxibacumab survived, risk difference 35.3% (95% CI 7.3, 59.6), two-sided Fisher's exact p=0.0237; monkey study, 0/10 (0%) placebo vs. 9/13 (69.2%) raxibacumab, risk difference 69.2% (95% CI 31.1, 88.9), p=0.0016
- FDA issued a Complete Response Letter (November 14, 2009) on the original 2009 BLA, requiring a new "added-benefit" animal study to demonstrate raxibacumab's benefit on top of background antibiotic therapy, because the antibiotic-alone survival rate in the original studies (85-100%, given immediately at symptom onset) was considered too high to represent a realistic worst-case human treatment scenario (historical human survival in the 2001 anthrax attacks was ~55% with antibiotics)
- At a Type A meeting (January 29, 2010), FDA directed the sponsor to redesign the confirmatory study so background-antibiotic-alone survival approximated the ~55% historical rate, using a human-equivalent antibiotic dose with treatment initiated only once animals were symptomatic
- Resubmission added-benefit rabbit study (1141-CG920871, raxibacumab + levofloxacin vs. levofloxacin alone) did not reach statistical significance: a 17-percentage-point absolute survival improvement, p=0.0874, a result the reviewer noted was underpowered (a study with 80% power to detect that same 17-point difference would require 116 animals per arm, 232 total, which "may not be ethical or feasible"); a replication study (1103-G923704) of the original monotherapy design did reach significance (0/24 placebo vs. 11/24 raxibacumab, difference 45.83%, 95% CI 25.27-67.18, p=0.0002)
- Approval rested on the "collective evidence" (FDA's own term) of the two original positive monotherapy pivotal studies plus the replication study, notwithstanding the non-significant standalone result of the added-benefit combination-therapy study
- Statistical methods throughout: two-sided Fisher's exact test for survival-rate comparisons (small-N binomial data), unconditional exact 95% CIs for risk differences, exploratory log-rank test for survival time, and logistic regression to rule out spore-dose (LD50) as a confounder of the added-benefit result (adjusted OR for treatment 3.12; LD50 effect itself not significant, p=0.1557)
- Human dose selection (40 mg/kg IV) was based on PK/PD modeling bridging the animal efficacy studies to human PK and safety data, per 21 CFR 601.90-601.95; pediatric dosing (no pediatric efficacy or PK data existed) was derived by population-PK simulation under three allometric-scaling scenarios (fixed exponent of 1; exponents fit from adult data; literature-derived exponents), concluding the same 40 mg/kg dose was appropriate across all pediatric age groups, with a second 40 mg/kg dose at day 14 recommended for children <12 years if signs of anthrax toxemia persist

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2012/125349Orig1s000ltr%28r%29.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2012/125349s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (animal efficacy studies) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/125349Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Clinical Pharmacology Review (human/pediatric PK bridging and dose selection) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/125349Orig1s000ClinPharmR.pdf
- FDA Pharmacology/Toxicology Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/125349Orig1s000PharmR.pdf
- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/125349Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- Pivotal publication (describes the original rabbit/monkey monotherapy efficacy studies and early human PK/safety data underlying the 2012 approval; no separate publication was located describing the 2012 resubmission's added-benefit study): Migone TS, Subramanian GM, Zhong J, et al. "Raxibacumab for the treatment of inhalational anthrax." *N Engl J Med.* 2009;361(2):135-144. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa0810603), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19587338/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Raxibacumab%20for%20the%20treatment%20of%20inhalational%20anthrax)

**Other resources**

- No NCT numbers exist for the pivotal studies because they are preclinical animal challenge studies with internal Human Genome Sciences study numbers, not registered human trials — this is expected and appropriate for an Animal Rule approval, not a sourcing gap.
- IPD/dataset access notes not applicable to the pivotal animal studies; not checked for the human PK/safety studies.
- Whether an FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held for this BLA was not confirmed in this research pass and should be verified before treating its absence/presence as settled.

**Reverse-engineered SAP notes and genuine SAP excerpts**

*[verbatim, package insert, Limitations of Use]* — "The effectiveness of raxibacumab is based solely on efficacy studies in animal models of inhalational anthrax. There have been no studies of raxibacumab in the pediatric population. Dosing in pediatric patients was derived using a population PK approach. Raxibacumab does not cross the blood-brain barrier and does not prevent or treat meningitis."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, added-benefit study 1141 conclusion]* — "A single IV dose of 40 mg/kg raxibacumab given in combination with levofloxacin resulted in 17% (P-value=0.0874) improvement in survival over levofloxacin monotherapy. This study was not powered to produce a statistically significant (p < 0.05) result with an absolute difference in survival rate of 17%. A trial with 80% power to detect a statistically significant result with the 17% difference seen in the current study would require 116 animals per group to be treated (232 animals)... A study of this size may not be ethical or feasible."

*[verbatim, FDA Clinical Pharmacology Review]* — "FDA has made provision for approval of drugs or biologics when it is unethical to assess the efficacy in controlled human clinical trials as outlined in 21CFR601.90 through 21CFR601.95... Based on rabbit and monkey PK/PD and efficacy studies and human PK and safety studies, sponsor concluded that the 40 mg/kg raxibacumab IV dose can provide adults with the desired level of protection against lethality."

*[inferred]* The choice of Fisher's exact test (rather than a large-sample chi-square or CMH test) for the primary survival-rate comparisons follows directly from the very small per-arm animal sample sizes (10-24 animals) reported in the Statistical Review's results tables, where exact small-sample methods are the standard, appropriate choice.

### 7. Bedaquiline (Sirturo) — NDA 204384

**Sponsor:** Janssen Research & Development

**Indication approved:** Pulmonary multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) as part of combination antibacterial therapy in adults, when an effective treatment regimen cannot otherwise be provided — approved under accelerated approval (21 CFR 314, Subpart H) on the surrogate endpoint of time to sputum culture conversion, with continued approval contingent on verification of clinical benefit in confirmatory trials

**Approval date:** December 28, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** Trial C208 (TMC207-TiDP13-C208, Stage 1 and Stage 2), NCT00449644

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, stratified (site, lung-cavitation extent), two-stage trial (exploratory Stage 1, pivotal Stage 2)
- *Endpoints:* time to sputum culture conversion (primary, surrogate endpoint), sputum culture conversion rate at week 24 (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* Cox proportional-hazards model (covariates: lung-cavitation extent, trial center)
- *Missing data/bias:* multiple concordant sensitivity analyses for discontinuation/censoring (missing treated as censored; missing treated as failure with end-censoring; no-overruling of investigator-assessed conversion)
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval based on a surrogate endpoint (culture conversion), Boxed Warning added after a reviewer-documented mortality imbalance, FDA Advisory Committee meeting held with a split safety vote

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Phase II, multicenter, stratified, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial with two consecutive, separately-analyzed stages: Stage 1 (exploratory, 8-week treatment) and Stage 2 (proof-of-efficacy/pivotal, 24-week treatment); N=160 randomized 1:1 in Stage 2 to bedaquiline or placebo, each added to a background MDR-TB regimen; randomization via IVRS with minimization, stratified by trial site and extent of lung cavitation
- Primary endpoint: time to sputum culture conversion, defined as two consecutive negative MGIT liquid cultures collected ≥25 days apart; analyzed via a Cox proportional-hazards model adjusted for cavitation extent and trial center — FDA's modified-intention-to-treat analysis found a relative risk (hazard ratio) of 2.15 (95% CI 1.39, 3.31), p=0.0005
- Secondary endpoint: culture conversion rate at week 24 — 78% bedaquiline vs. 58% placebo, difference 20% (95% CI 4.5, 35.6), p=0.014
- Multiple pre-specified sensitivity analyses for missing/discontinued data (missing=censored; missing=failure with end-censoring; no-overruling of investigator-assessed conversion) were concordant with the primary result
- Central regulatory story: a 4-month post-database-lock safety update revealed a mortality imbalance in Stage 2 — 10/79 (12.6%) deaths on bedaquiline vs. 2/81 (2.5%) on placebo, difference 10.2% (95% CI 2.1, 19.7), p=0.0167; across the full development program (including Stage 1, an earlier trial C202, and the open-label trial C209) 36 deaths were reported in total. Detailed case-by-case review by FDA's medical review team, the applicant, two independent expert panels convened by the applicant, and the Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee found no consistent relationship between death and culture conversion status, relapse, HIV status, or baseline disease severity
- Given the mortality imbalance, FDA required a Boxed Warning (mortality and QT prolongation) and restricted the indication to use "when an effective treatment regimen cannot otherwise be provided," with continued approval contingent on a required Phase III confirmatory trial (C210) verifying clinical benefit
- Surrogate-endpoint status of sputum culture conversion had itself been recommended by the Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee in June 2009, prior to this approval

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2012/204384s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/204384Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Summary Review (contains the extensive mortality-imbalance and accelerated-approval-rationale narrative) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/204384Orig1s000SumR.pdf

**Other resources**

- Janssen participates in general cross-industry IPD-sharing platforms; trial-specific C208 availability was not individually confirmed here.
- FDA Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee meeting held November 28, 2012: efficacy question (culture conversion acceptable as a surrogate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit, but not adequate for traditional/full approval) passed 18-0; safety question passed 11-7 (no abstentions), reflecting substantial committee concern about the mortality imbalance.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 204384]* — C208 is "a Phase II, multicenter, stratified, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial with two consecutive but completely separate stages."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review]* — mITT primary analysis result: relative risk (hazard ratio) "2.15, 95% CI [1.39, 3.31], p=0.0005" for time to culture conversion (n=67 vs. 66); secondary week-24 conversion-rate difference "20% (4.5%, 35.6%), p=0.014."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review]* — on the mortality imbalance: "10/79 (12.6%)" deaths bedaquiline vs. "2/81 (2.5%)" placebo in C208 Stage 2, difference "10.2% (95% CI [2.1%, 19.7%])," p=0.0167; no clear relationship between death and sputum-culture-conversion status, relapse, HIV status, or disease severity was found "by either the medical review team, the applicant, the two expert panels convened by the applicant..., or by members of the Anti-infective Drugs Advisory Committee."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review]* — regulatory basis: approval granted under 21 CFR 314.500 (accelerated approval, Subpart H) on the surrogate endpoint of sputum culture conversion, with the indication restricted to use "when an effective treatment regimen cannot otherwise be provided" pending the required Phase III confirmatory trial.

### 8. Crofelemer (Fulyzaq) — NDA 202292

**Sponsor:** Salix Pharmaceuticals (originally developed by Napo Pharmaceuticals/Glenmark)

**Indication approved:** Symptomatic relief of non-infectious diarrhea in adult patients with HIV/AIDS on antiretroviral therapy

**Approval date:** December 31, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** ADVENT, NCT00547898

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two-stage adaptive design (interim dose-selection analysis pooled into a final combined-stage inference), randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
- *Endpoints:* responder rate (≤2 watery bowel movements per week during at least 2 of 4 efficacy-assessment weeks)
- *Primary analysis:* combined-stage adaptive-design inference per Posch et al. methodology (as specified in the sponsor's SAP; FDA's own re-analysis found the sponsor's applied method was actually an unadjusted asymptotic test rather than the specified combination method)
- *Missing data/bias:* diary-based non-responder classification (excess rescue-medication use or missing diary days classified as non-response), reviewer-documented operational interim-analysis error affecting the observed treatment effect
- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan (FDA statistical reviewer disputed the sponsor's own explanation for inconsistent efficacy across trial stages)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ADVENT: a two-stage adaptive-design, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in HIV-seropositive adults with chronic non-infectious diarrhea on stable antiretroviral therapy; each stage comprised a 10-day single-blind placebo screening period, randomization, a 31-day double-blind treatment phase (3-day run-in plus a 4-week efficacy-assessment period), a 20-week placebo-free extension, and a 14-day post-treatment safety follow-up call
- Stage 1: randomized approximately 50 subjects per arm to crofelemer 125 mg, 250 mg, 500 mg, or placebo; an interim analysis selected the 125 mg dose to advance to Stage 2
- Stage 2: randomized additional subjects to crofelemer 125 mg (final N=92) or placebo (final N=88); the sponsor's SAP specified combining Stage 1 and Stage 2 data for final inference using the adaptive-design methods of Posch et al. (2005)
- Primary endpoint: responder = reported ≤2 watery bowel movements per week during at least 2 of the 4 weeks of the efficacy-assessment period; non-responder = >3 days of antidiarrheal/opiate rescue-medication use during the 4-week window, or discontinuation before the relevant study visit; weeks with <5 of 7 diary days completed were not counted toward responder classification
- Results: crofelemer 125 mg 17.6% responders vs. placebo 8.0%, difference 9.6% (one-sided 97.5% CI: 1.2% to infinity), one-sided p=0.01 at alpha=0.025
- FDA statistical review flagged substantial concerns: the overall treatment effect was driven almost entirely by Stage 1 (p=0.002) with Stage 2 alone not reaching significance (p=0.169) despite a larger sample size; the reviewer explicitly disagreed with the sponsor's proposed explanation (a baseline diarrhea-severity imbalance between stages) for this inconsistency
- FDA's review also documented an operational error in the interim analysis — the sponsor's statistician mistakenly included run-in-period data and used a narrower non-responder data source than the final analysis, which "changed the response rates in a way that increased the treatment effect seen for Stage I" and might have led to the trial being stopped for futility had a formal stopping rule existed
- FDA's review further found the sponsor's clinical study report mischaracterized its own statistical method — citing the Posch & Bauer combined-stage adaptive method while the analysis actually performed was an unadjusted asymptotic Pearson chi-square test with Yule-type confidence intervals
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was found referenced for this NDA in the documents reviewed

- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/202292Orig1s000StatR.pdf

"Efficacy and safety of crofelemer for noninfectious diarrhea in HIV-seropositive individuals (ADVENT trial): a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, two-stage study." *HIV Clin Trials.* 2013;14(6):261-273. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1310/hct1406-261), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24334179/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Efficacy%20and%20safety%20of%20crofelemer%20for%20noninfectious%20diarrhea%20in%20HIV-seropositive%20individuals%20ADVENT)

**Other resources**

- Salix/successor sponsors' IPD-sharing participation not individually confirmed here.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was identified for this NDA.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 202292]* — trial design: ADVENT was "a two-stage adaptive design study"; each stage was double-blind and placebo-controlled (not an open-label lead-in, contrary to an initial assumption based on the drug's later marketed profile).

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review]* — primary endpoint definition: responder = subjects who "reported two or less watery bowel movements per week during at least two of the four weeks of the efficacy assessment period."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §5.2 conclusions]* — "The statistical evidence to support the desired indication for crofelemer... is modest... the 10% treatment effect size is not consistent across important study design attributes, including stage of study and study sites. Further, the within group clinical response rate of 18% for crofelemer 125 mg is relatively low."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review]* — on the interim-analysis error: the operational mistake (including run-in-period data and using a narrower non-responder data source) "changed the response rates in a way that increased the treatment effect seen for Stage I."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review]* — on the sponsor's mischaracterized method and the Stage 1/Stage 2 discrepancy: the reviewer states "I do not agree with the Applicant's conclusions" regarding the sponsor's baseline-imbalance explanation for the inconsistent stage-level results.

### 9. Dolutegravir (Tivicay) — NDA 204790

**Sponsor:** GlaxoSmithKline / ViiV Healthcare

**Indication approved:** Dolutegravir in combination with other antiretroviral agents for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in adults and pediatric patients

**Approval date:** August 12, 2013

**Pivotal trial:** SPRING-2 (trial 3086, NCT01227824, vs. raltegravir) and SINGLE (trial 4467, NCT01263015, vs. efavirenz/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF, with dolutegravir given as dolutegravir/abacavir/lamivudine)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, two identically-structured trials against two different active regimens
- *Endpoints:* HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL at week 48 by Snapshot algorithm (primary)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test, non-inferiority difference-in-proportions (10% margin), superiority conclusion reached in SINGLE
- *Missing data/bias:* FDA Snapshot algorithm, reviewer-documented sensitivity analysis excluding a GCP-non-compliant trial site
- *Regulatory:* Good Clinical Practice (GCP) misconduct finding at a trial site (one Russian SPRING-2 site found in violation, sensitivity analysis excluding it did not change conclusions)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Two Phase III, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, multicenter trials in treatment-naive HIV-1-infected adults: SPRING-2 (dolutegravir 50 mg once daily vs. raltegravir 400 mg twice daily, each on an investigator-selected NRTI backbone) and SINGLE (dolutegravir/abacavir/lamivudine fixed-dose once daily vs. efavirenz/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF fixed-dose once daily)
- Randomization stratified by screening HIV-1 RNA (≤ or >100,000 copies/mL) and, in SPRING-2, NRTI background regimen, or in SINGLE, baseline CD4 count
- Primary endpoint (both trials): HIV-1 RNA below the limit of quantification (BLQ, <50 copies/mL) at week 48 by the FDA Snapshot algorithm
- Primary analysis: dolutegravir vs. control compared via the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) method, stratified by the randomization factors; non-inferiority to raltegravir or efavirenz was declared if the lower bound of the 95% CI for the treatment difference exceeded −10%; a secondary CMH comparison was conducted at week 96 in both trials, with no multiple-comparison adjustment applied since the week-48 analysis was the sole formal primary comparison
- SPRING-2 result: dolutegravir 88% (361/411) vs. raltegravir 85% (351/411), adjusted difference 2.5% (95% CI −2.2, 7.1) at week 48 — non-inferiority declared
- SINGLE result: dolutegravir/abacavir/lamivudine 88% (364/414) vs. efavirenz/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF 81% (338/419), adjusted difference 7.4% (95% CI 2.5, 12.3) — the protocol-specified non-inferiority comparison was not only met but was statistically significantly superior; discontinuation for adverse events was markedly lower with dolutegravir (2%) than efavirenz (10%), consistent with tolerability being a key driver of the superiority result
- One SPRING-2 trial site (Russia, site 083505) was found in violation of Good Clinical Practice; a sensitivity analysis excluding that site (8 dolutegravir, 6 raltegravir subjects) left the primary conclusion unchanged
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was found referenced for this NDA in the review documents

*[verbatim]* — "The primary endpoint in both phase 3 trials with treatment naïve subjects, Spring 2 and Single, was HIV-1 RNA observed BLQ at week 48 (regardless of subsequent confirmation or prior rebound, i.e. snapshot)."

*[verbatim]* — "the DTG and control arms (RAL in Spring 2, EFV in Single) were compared by the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) method, stratifying by the randomization factors... Non-inferiority to RAL or EFV was declared if the lower confidence bound for the week 48 differences was >-10%. In both trials, a secondary CMH comparison was done at week 96. Since the week 48 analysis was primary, no multiple comparison adjustment was done at week 96."

*[verbatim]* — on the GCP finding: "One Russian site in the Spring 2 trial, site 083505, was found in violation of GCP... sensitivity analyses excluding this site were also conducted" (8 DTG, 6 RAL subjects), with results unchanged.

*[verbatim]* — on the SINGLE superiority result: "The protocol specified primary comparison of non-inferiority of the DTG regimen to the EFV regimen was established. In fact, the DTG regimen was statistically significantly superior."

### 10. Luliconazole (Luzu) — NDA 204153

**Sponsor:** Medicis Pharmaceutical

**Indication approved:** Topical treatment of interdigital tinea pedis, tinea cruris, and tinea corporis caused by Trichophyton rubrum, Trichophyton mentagrophytes, or Epidermophyton floccosum, in patients 18 years of age and older

**Approval date:** November 14, 2013

**Pivotal trial:** Three Special-Protocol-Assessment-agreed Phase III trials — MP-1000-01 (tinea cruris, NCT01342315), MP-1000-02 (tinea pedis, NCT01396785), MP-1000-03 (tinea pedis, NCT01396811)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled, superiority design, Special Protocol Assessment (SPA)-agreed
- *Endpoints:* complete clearance (mycological cure + clinical cure) at day 42 (tinea pedis) or day 28 (tinea cruris)
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by analysis center, Breslow-Day test for treatment-by-center interaction
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing of secondary endpoints ("a sequential testing approach was used for multiplicity adjustment for the secondary endpoints")
- *Missing data/bias:* last-observation-carried-forward (LOCF) primary imputation, with all-missing-as-failure, multiple imputation, and repeated-measures logistic regression (GEE) sensitivity analyses

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Three randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled, multicenter Phase III trials of luliconazole cream 1% once daily, each individually agreed with FDA via a Special Protocol Assessment: MP-1000-01 (tinea cruris, 7-day treatment, 2:1 randomization, block size 6, enrolled 483, modified-intention-to-treat [MITT] N=256); MP-1000-02 and MP-1000-03 (tinea pedis, 14-day treatment, 1:1 randomization, enrolled 321 and 322, MITT N=209 and 214 respectively)
- Regulatory history: an End-of-Phase-2 meeting for tinea pedis was held December 16, 2009; a Special Protocol Assessment for the tinea pedis Phase III protocol was submitted May 24, 2010 and agreed July 7, 2010, with agreement that two tinea pedis trials plus one tinea cruris trial would be adequate to support the expanded indication; the tinea cruris SPA was agreed February 17, 2011; protocols were subsequently amended (April 8, 2011; July 14, 2011) to add multiple-imputation and GEE sensitivity-analysis detail
- Primary endpoint: "complete clearance" at day 42 (tinea pedis) or day 28 (tinea cruris), defined as both mycological cure (negative KOH microscopy and negative fungal culture) and clinical cure (a score of 0 on each of erythema, scaling, and pruritus)
- Primary analysis: Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by analysis center (centers with fewer than 4 subjects per arm pooled with other centers); treatment-by-center interaction assessed via the Breslow-Day test at alpha=0.1; multiplicity across secondary endpoints controlled via a sequential (step-down) testing approach
- Missing-data handling: last observation carried forward (LOCF) as the primary imputation method for the binary complete-clearance endpoint, with three pre-specified sensitivity analyses — all missing counted as failure, multiple imputation, and a repeated-measures logistic regression/GEE model
- Results (MITT, all p<0.001 vs. vehicle): tinea cruris (Study 01) 21.2% (35/165) vs. 4.4% (4/91), difference 15.8% (95% CI 7.8, 24.6); tinea pedis (Study 02) 26.4% (28/106) vs. 1.9% (2/103), difference 24.5% (95% CI 15.5, 34.0); tinea pedis (Study 03) 14.0% (15/107) vs. 2.8% (3/107), difference 11.2% (95% CI 3.7, 19.5)
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held; the FDA Medical Review states plainly that one was not needed for this topical product

### 11. Simeprevir (Olysio) — NDA 205123

**Sponsor:** Janssen Research & Development, LLC

**Indication approved:** In combination with peginterferon alfa and ribavirin for the treatment of chronic hepatitis C (HCV) genotype 1 infection, including in patients with compensated liver disease (including cirrhosis)

**Approval date:** November 22, 2013

**Pivotal trial:** QUEST-1 (Study TMC435-C208), NCT01289782; QUEST-2 (Study TMC435-C216), NCT01290679; supportive trial PROMISE (Study HPC3007, prior relapsers), NCT01281839

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (background peginterferon alfa-2a/RBV given to both arms; QUEST-1/QUEST-2 in treatment-naive genotype 1 patients, PROMISE in prior relapsers); response-guided treatment duration (therapy stopped at Week 24 for patients meeting protocol-defined HCV RNA thresholds at Weeks 4 and 12)
- *Endpoints:* sustained virologic response 12 weeks after planned end of therapy (SVR12)
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by HCV genotype 1 subtype and IL28B genotype (QUEST-1/QUEST-2) or subtype and prior response type (PROMISE)
- *Missing data/bias:* missing SVR12 substituted by SVR24 if available, otherwise imputed as treatment failure ("HCV SVR12/SVR24 substitution-then-failure imputation rule") — FDA reviewer independently re-derived SVR12 using a slightly modified visit-window algorithm as a sensitivity check and obtained materially consistent results

**Trial design & endpoints**

- QUEST-1 and QUEST-2 were phase 3, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trials in treatment-naive, genotype 1 chronic HCV-infected subjects (screening HCV RNA >10,000 IU/mL); subjects received 12 weeks of simeprevir (TMC435) 150 mg once daily or placebo, both combined with peginterferon alfa-2a/ribavirin (QUEST-1) or alfa-2a or alfa-2b/ribavirin (QUEST-2, up to 30% of subjects on the alfa-2b regimen), followed by peginterferon/ribavirin alone; randomization was stratified by HCV genotype 1 subtype and IL28B genotype
- Response-guided therapy: subjects in the simeprevir arm who achieved HCV RNA <25 IU/mL (detectable or undetectable) at Week 4 and undetectable at Week 12 stopped all therapy at Week 24; all others (and all control-arm subjects) continued peginterferon/ribavirin to Week 48
- PROMISE enrolled genotype 1 patients who had relapsed after a prior course of interferon-based therapy, using the same 2:1 randomization, response-guided design, and stratification factors
- Primary efficacy endpoint (all three trials): proportion of subjects achieving SVR12, defined as HCV RNA below the lower limit of quantification 12 weeks after the actual (or planned, if discontinued) end of therapy
- Primary analysis method: difference in SVR12 rates between simeprevir and control arms calculated via the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel method, controlling for the randomization stratification factors; the null hypothesis was that there was no statistically significant difference between arms in SVR12
- A supportive phase 2b, 7-arm, dose-ranging trial (Study TMC435-C206/ASPIRE, NCT00980330, N=463) in prior null/partial responders and relapsers informed the 150 mg/12-week regimen and contributed supportive SVR24 data for the harder-to-treat prior-null-responder subgroup, which the FDA reviewer flagged as having a lower estimated response rate than the treatment-naive population

### 12. Sofosbuvir (Sovaldi) — NDA 204671

**Sponsor:** Gilead Sciences, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection, genotypes 1-4, as a component of a combination antiviral treatment regimen (with ribavirin, or with peginterferon alfa and ribavirin)

**Approval date:** December 6, 2013

**Pivotal trial:** NEUTRINO (Study GS-US-334-0110), NCT01641640; FISSION (Study GS-US-334-1231/P7977-1231), NCT01497366; POSITRON (Study GS-US-334-0107), NCT01542788; FUSION (Study GS-US-334-0108), NCT01604850

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial tested against a historical performance goal (NEUTRINO, genotypes 1/4/5/6, treatment-naive); randomized, open-label, active-controlled, non-inferiority trial (FISSION, genotypes 2/3 treatment-naive, SOF+RBV 12 weeks vs. peginterferon+RBV 24 weeks); randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (POSITRON, interferon-ineligible/intolerant genotype 2/3); randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with two treatment durations (FUSION, treatment-experienced genotype 2/3, 12 vs. 16 weeks SOF+RBV)
- *Endpoints:* sustained virologic response 12 weeks after end of therapy (SVR12)
- *Primary analysis:* one-sample two-sided exact test against a pre-specified historical performance goal of 60% (NEUTRINO); Mantel-Haenszel stratum-adjusted proportions and Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by genotype, baseline HCV RNA, and cirrhosis status (FISSION); Clopper-Pearson exact confidence intervals for within-arm SVR12 rates (all four studies)
- *Multiplicity:* closed testing procedure for FISSION's primary endpoint (non-inferiority tested first; if non-inferiority null hypothesis rejected, the 2-sided superiority p-value was then calculated)
- *Missing data/bias:* missing SVR12 substituted by SVR24 if available, otherwise imputed as treatment failure (same HCV-specific SVR12/SVR24 imputation rule applied across HCV entries in this census); FDA reviewer conducted an independent bridging analysis (relative-risk and risk-difference extrapolation methods) to estimate the SVR12 rate for a 16-week SOF+RBV regimen in treatment-naive genotype 3 patients that was not directly studied at that duration in NEUTRINO

**Trial design & endpoints**

- NEUTRINO (Study 110) was a phase 3, open-label, single-arm trial of 12 weeks of sofosbuvir 400 mg once daily plus peginterferon alfa-2a/ribavirin in 327 treatment-naive subjects with chronic genotype 1, 4, 5, or 6 HCV infection; the primary hypothesis was that the SVR12 rate exceeded a 60% historical control rate (based on clinical judgment, not a formal meta-analysis)
- FISSION (Study 1231) was a phase 3, randomized (1:1), open-label, active-controlled, non-inferiority trial of 12 weeks of sofosbuvir+ribavirin vs. 24 weeks of peginterferon+ribavirin (standard of care) in 499 treatment-naive genotype 2/3 subjects, randomization stratified by genotype, screening HCV RNA level, and baseline cirrhosis; the pre-specified non-inferiority margin was 15%, justified by an assumed ~70% SVR rate for the standard-of-care control and a small assumed monotherapy ribavirin effect
- POSITRON (Study 107) and FUSION (Study 108) were phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of sofosbuvir+ribavirin in genotype 2/3 subjects who were interferon-ineligible/intolerant/unwilling (POSITRON, 12 weeks) or treatment-experienced (FUSION, randomized 12 vs. 16 weeks); no placebo subjects in Study 107 achieved SVR12
- Primary efficacy endpoint across all four trials: SVR12, defined as HCV RNA below the lower limit of quantification (LLOQ) 12 weeks after the last dose of study drug
- FISSION primary analysis: 2-sided 95% CI on the stratum-adjusted Mantel-Haenszel treatment difference in SVR12 (SOF+RBV minus PEG+RBV); if the lower CI bound exceeded -15%, non-inferiority was concluded, and the 2-sided p-value for superiority was then calculated (superiority declared if p<0.05) — a closed testing procedure
- A large, consistent genotype 2-vs-3 efficacy gap was observed across all four studies (e.g., FISSION: 97% vs. 56% SVR12 in the 12-week SOF+RBV arm, genotypes 2 vs. 3 respectively, p=0.0002), which the FDA reviewer treated as clinically important and pre-specifiable given genotype was already a randomization stratification factor in two of the four trials

> "This was a Phase 3, open-label, single arm trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of SOF in combination of with PEG and RBV in the treatment of treatment-naive subjects with chronic genotype 1, 4, 5 or 6 HCV infection... The primary hypothesis was that the SVR12 rate was greater than the 60% historical rate. The historical rate was based on clinical judgment... Two-sided one-sample exact test was performed to determine whether the SVR12 rate was higher than 60%. Also, the Clopper Pearson exact approach was used to construct the 95% CI on the SVR12 rate."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, FISSION non-inferiority margin and closed testing procedure, p.11-12]*

> "The primary hypothesis was that the 12-week SOF+RBV treatment was non-inferior to the 24-week PEG+RBV regimen in the primary efficacy endpoint of SVR12 rate by 15%. Of note, the 15% non-inferiority margin was pre-specified in the protocol... In the analysis of the primary efficacy endpoint of the SVR12 rate, a closed testing procedure was used. The non-inferiority of SOV+RBV to PEG+RBV was tested first. If the lower limit of the 2-sided 95% CI on the treatment difference (SOF+RBV group minus PEG+RBV group) in the SVR12 rates was > -15%, then it was concluded that SOF+RBV was non-inferior to PEG+RBV. If the non-inferiority null hypothesis was rejected, then the p-value associated with the test of superiority was calculated. Superiority would have been demonstrated if the 2-sided p-value was < 0.05."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, data quality assessment, p.11]*

> "Prior to the NDA submission, the applicant provided the SAP for each study, and each was reviewed. In addition, the reviewers requested sample datasets before the NDA submission and identified data issues which were clarified with the applicant before the submission. In general, the data in this NDA was of high quality, which made it possible for the statistical reviewer to reproduce the applicant's efficacy results easily."

### 13. Miltefosine (Impavido) — NDA 204684

**Sponsor:** Paladin Therapeutics Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of visceral leishmaniasis due to *Leishmania donovani*, cutaneous leishmaniasis due to *L. braziliensis*, *L. guyanensis*, or *L. panamensis*, and mucosal leishmaniasis due to *L. braziliensis* in patients 12 years of age and older

**Approval date:** March 19, 2014

**Pivotal trial:** Study 3154 (visceral leishmaniasis, India) — no registered NCT number identified (predates ClinicalTrials.gov mandatory-registration era); supportive/co-pivotal studies Study 3168 (cutaneous, Colombia/Guatemala), Study Soto (cutaneous, Bolivia), Study Z020 (cutaneous, Brazil), Study Z025 (visceral, Ethiopia), and Study Z022 (mucosal, Bolivia) — none of these older international investigator/NIH/military-sponsored trials appear to carry NCT numbers either

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled, non-inferiority trial (Study 3154, VL, miltefosine vs. intravenous amphotericin B; Study Z025, VL, miltefosine vs. sodium stibogluconate); randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (Study 3168, CL); randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial (Study Soto and Study Z020, CL, vs. meglumine antimoniate/Glucantime); single-arm, open-label trial (Study Z022, ML)
- *Endpoints:* definite/final cure rate at 6 months post-treatment (VL); definite cure rate at 6 months post-treatment (CL); apparent cure at 2 weeks and cure at 6-12 months post-treatment (ML)
- *Primary analysis:* stratum-adjusted (center-adjusted) confidence bound on the absolute difference in cure rates for non-inferiority testing (Study 3154); descriptive intent-to-treat response-rate analysis with treatment-arm comparison (Study 3168, superiority vs. placebo)
- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation for patients lost to follow-up before final-cure assessment, applied identically in both arms (Study 3154); FDA and sponsor disagreed on the statistically/clinically justified non-inferiority margin
- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan (sponsor's 15% non-inferiority margin for Study 3154 was rejected by FDA in favor of a stricter 10% margin, communicated to the sponsor in writing before database lock); most supportive studies lacked a prospective SAP or a justified non-inferiority margin at the time of conduct

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 3154 (the primary VL evidence) was a randomized (3:1), open-label, active-controlled, multicenter phase 3 trial conducted in Bihar, India, comparing 28 days of oral miltefosine (2.5 mg/kg/day target dose) to intravenous amphotericin B (15 mg/kg total dose, every other day over 30 days); 400 patients aged ≥12 were randomized (398 exposed: 299 miltefosine, 99 amphotericin B)
- Primary endpoint: final cure rate at 6 months after end of treatment, defined as initial cure (clinical cure with no relapse) maintained through 6-month follow-up; primary analysis population was intent-to-treat, with dropouts before final-cure assessment counted as non-responders in both arms
- Study Z025 (Ethiopia, supportive VL) compared miltefosine to intramuscular sodium stibogluconate in 580 male patients (including many HIV-coinfected subjects); reviewed only via sponsor study report and the Ritmeijer et al. (2006) publication due to lack of available patient-level data
- Study 3168 (primary CL evidence) was a randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in Colombia and Guatemala; 133 patients ≥12 years received oral miltefosine 50 mg or placebo for 28 days; primary endpoint was definite cure at 6 months post-treatment, analyzed via intent-to-treat comparison of cure proportions between arms, with reviewer concern that blinding/randomization-list compliance may have been imperfect at one site
- Studies Soto (Bolivia) and Z020 (Brazil, two sub-populations by predominant *Leishmania* species) were open-label, active-comparator (Glucantime) supportive CL trials; Study Z022 (Bolivia) was a single-arm, uncontrolled, single-center phase 2 trial supporting extension of the CL indication to mucosal leishmaniasis
- Sample size for Study 3154 was based on a restricted-maximum-likelihood calculation assuming final cure rates of 88-92% (miltefosine) vs. 94-98% (amphotericin B), 1-sided alpha of 0.025, 80% power, and a 15% non-inferiority margin, yielding a planned enrollment of 400 (300 miltefosine, 100 amphotericin B) at a 3:1 allocation chosen to maximize miltefosine clinical experience

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1086/383321), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15127339/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Miltefosine%20for%20New%20World%20cutaneous%20leishmaniasis)

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting is recorded for this NDA in the reviewed documents.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Reference ID 3380815, FDA-sponsor non-inferiority margin dispute for Study 3154, p.12]*

> "According to the sponsor, the confirmatory analysis calculated a center adjusted 97.5%-upper confidence bound for the absolute difference of response rate (AMB – MLT). Non-inferiority was concluded if this upper confidence limit was ≤15%... The FDA considered a 10% margin statistically justified and more clinically acceptable... The Agency defined an acceptable non-inferiority margin of 10% in a communication with the sponsor dated March 20, 2012: 'For Study 3154, our analysis estimates the pseudo-placebo response rate at 47.1% (38.14%, 56.03%), and the response rate to amphotericin B at 97.8% (96.14%, 99.52%). M1 is therefore conservatively estimated at 40.11%. Although a margin of 15% could be supported, a margin of 10% is more appropriate for this potentially fatal disease.'"

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Study 3154 sample size, p.12]*

> "According to the protocol, the sample size calculation was based on the final cure rates using the restricted maximum likelihood method. An allocation ratio of 3:1 in favor of miltefosine was chosen in order to gain more experience with miltefosine. The significance level for the 1-sided non-inferiority test was 0.025, the required power was 80%, and the non-inferiority margin used by the sponsor was 15%."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Study 3168 (CL) result, p.4]*

> "In total 133 patients aged ≥12 years entered the study; all received at least one dose of study medication (89 on miltefosine and 44 on placebo). At 6 months after treatment completion, 59 (66.3%) miltefosine-treated patients and 13 (29.6%) placebo-treated patients achieved definite cure. There was a significant improvement of 36.8% in definite cure in the miltefosine group over the placebo group (p < 0.0001)... However, it is of concern that this pivotal trial may not have been completely blinded and that the pre-generated randomization list might not have been fully complied with at one study site."

### 14. Dalbavancin (Dalvance) — NDA 021883

**Sponsor:** Durata Therapeutics, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI) caused by susceptible gram-positive organisms

**Approval date:** May 23, 2014

**Pivotal trial:** DISCOVER 1 (Trial DUR001-301), NCT01339091; DISCOVER 2 (Trial DUR001-302), NCT01431339

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled, non-inferiority trial (dalbavancin single IV loading + Day-8 dose vs. 10-14 days of vancomycin with optional oral linezolid switch); Special Protocol Assessment (SPA), formally amended pre-unblinding is not applicable here — SPA was agreed and unchanged, but the agreed primary endpoint was superseded by later FDA guidance ("SPA-agreed primary endpoint retained for approval despite being superseded by revised disease-specific FDA guidance")
- *Endpoints:* early clinical response (responder rate) at 48-72 hours post first infusion, composite of cessation of spread of erythema and afebrile status (2010 ABSSSI guidance-era endpoint); clinical status (success/failure) at end of therapy (EOT) and short-term follow-up (SFU) as secondary/supportive endpoints
- *Primary analysis:* stratum-adjusted (baseline fever status) Miettinen-Nurminen method for the non-inferiority confidence interval on the treatment difference in early clinical response rates
- *Missing data/bias:* FDA reviewer explicitly flagged that the EOT/SFU "clinical status" secondary endpoint's success criteria (any-magnitude decrease in lesion size) were inconsistent with, and less stringent than, the ≥20% reduction required at the earlier 48-72-hour primary timepoint, limiting interpretability of later-timepoint concordance/sensitivity analyses
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* sample-size re-estimation (SSR) at ~60% enrollment (334 patients), based on blinded overall response rate, reviewed by an independent DMC-supported blinded statistician

**Trial design & endpoints**

- DISCOVER 1 and DISCOVER 2 were identically designed phase 3, multicenter, randomized (1:1), double-blind, double-dummy trials comparing a single 1000 mg IV dose of dalbavancin on Day 1 plus a second 500 mg IV dose on Day 8, against a 10-14 day regimen of IV vancomycin (1000 mg or 15 mg/kg q12h) with an optional switch to oral linezolid after ≥3 days, in adults with ABSSSI
- Both trials were conducted under a Special Protocol Assessment following the 2010 FDA ABSSSI guidance, with primary efficacy defined as early clinical response (responder) at 48-72 hours: cessation of spread of erythema/edema/induration from baseline plus resolution of fever, analyzed in the intent-to-treat population
- Non-inferiority margin: 10%, justified by the applicant using historical sulfonamide-vs-UV-light erysipelas data (Snodgrass et al. 1937) estimating a control effect of ~12% at the 48-72 hour timepoint (M1), such that the 10% margin preserved ~80% of the estimated control effect; the margin was accepted by FDA under the SPA
- Primary result: responder rate 83.3% (dalbavancin) vs. 81.8% (comparator) in DISCOVER 1 (difference 1.5%, 95% CI -4.6% to 7.9%), and 76.8% vs. 78.3% in DISCOVER 2 (difference -1.5%, 95% CI -7.4% to 4.6%); both trials met non-inferiority since the lower 95% CI bound exceeded -10%
- Because the trials were designed and largely conducted under the 2010 guidance's fever/cessation-of-spread definition, the FDA reviewer also computed a secondary responder definition matching the subsequently issued 2013 ABSSSI guidance (≥20% reduction in lesion area at 48-72 hours, no fever component), finding consistent non-inferiority (89.9% vs. 90.9% in DISCOVER 1; 87.6% vs. 85.9% in DISCOVER 2)
- The FDA reviewer conducted additional sensitivity/concordance analyses at EOT and SFU using more clinically stringent success criteria than the sponsor's pre-specified ones, finding larger, less-favorable treatment differences in DISCOVER 1 but not DISCOVER 2 — a reviewer-driven robustness check rather than a change to the primary conclusion

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2014/021883s000lbl.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (DISCOVER 2) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01431339
- Pivotal publication: Boucher HW, et al. "Once-weekly dalbavancin versus daily conventional therapy for skin infection." *N Engl J Med.* 2014;370(23):2169-79. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1310480), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24897082/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Once-weekly%20dalbavancin%20versus%20daily%20conventional%20therapy%20for%20skin%20infection)

**Other resources**

- Durata (subsequently acquired by Allergan/Actavis) trial-specific IPD access via Vivli.org/YODA Project was not individually confirmed here.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting is recorded for this NDA in the reviewed documents.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Reference ID 3505302, primary endpoint definition and NI margin, p.4]*

> "Both trials also evaluated the primary endpoint of early clinical response (i.e. responder rates) in the intent-to-treat (ITT) population where responders had to achieve cessation of spread of erythema at the lesion site along with absence of fever at 48-72 hours from baseline. This endpoint was evaluated under a non-inferiority (NI) design with a pre-specified margin of 10%. A 10% NI margin is supported by findings from two historical studies (Snodgrass et. al, 1937) comparing sulfonamides to UV light in patients diagnosed with erysipelas at the 48-72 hour time points."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, primary result and reviewer concern about later-timepoint endpoints, p.5]*

> "The responder rate was 83.3% in the dalbavancin arm compared to 81.8% in the comparator arm resulting in a treatment difference of 1.5% (95% confidence interval (CI): (-4.6%, 7.9%) in Trial 301. In Trial 302, the responder rate was 76.8% in the dalbavancin arm compared to 78.3% in the comparator arm... However, interpretability of these findings may be limited by the success criteria used in the clinical status endpoints since these criteria may fail to address the appropriate degree of improvement in local signs that would be expected at later assessments. For example, the success criteria used for lesion area/erythema at EOT and SFU only required a decrease (i.e. any magnitude of decrease) in lesion size which is inconsistent with the requirement of at least a 20% reduction in lesion area at an earlier time point (i.e. at 48-72 hours) under the current ABSSSI guidance."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, sample-size re-estimation, p.18]*

> "Interim Analyses: In order to ensure that the point estimate of early clinical response used in the estimation of sample size was valid for this Study, an interim analysis for sample size re-estimation (SSR) was performed when early clinical response data at 48 to 72 hours were available for approximately 60% of the patients (334 patients)... The sample size re-estimation was based on the blinded overall (not by treatment group) clinical response rate and was conducted by an independent, blinded statistician. A Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) was provided with the [results]."

### 15. Efinaconazole (Jublia) — NDA 203567

**Sponsor:** Dow Pharmaceutical Sciences, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Onychomycosis of the toenail(s) due to *Trichophyton rubrum* and *Trichophyton mentagrophytes*

**Approval date:** June 6, 2014

**Pivotal trial:** Study P3-01 (DPSI-IDP-108-P3-01), NCT01008033; Study P3-02 (DPSI-IDP-108-P3-02), NCT01007708

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized (3:1), double-blind, vehicle-controlled trial, once-daily topical application for 48 weeks with follow-up to Week 52; mid-trial SAP amendment changing endpoint status (a second SAP version, signed ~5 weeks after the first, redefined the set and order of secondary/supportive endpoints without changing the primary endpoint)
- *Endpoints:* complete cure at Week 52 (0% clinical involvement of target toenail plus negative KOH and negative culture); clinical efficacy rate (≤10% affected nail), mycologic cure rate, and unaffected new nail growth as secondary endpoints
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by (pooled) analysis center for response-rate endpoints; ANOVA with treatment and analysis-center factors for continuous new-nail-growth endpoint; Breslow-Day test for consistency of treatment effect across analysis centers
- *Missing data/bias:* last observation carried forward (LOCF) as primary missing-data method for the primary efficacy analysis, with sensitivity analyses imputing missing Week-52 assessments as failures and, separately, as successes

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Studies P3-01 and P3-02 were identically designed phase 3, randomized (3:1 efinaconazole:vehicle), double-blind, vehicle-controlled trials in subjects aged 18-70 with 20-50% target-toenail involvement (excluding dermatophytoma/lunula involvement), uninfected nail length ≥3mm, thickness ≤3mm, positive KOH, and positive dermatophyte (or mixed dermatophyte/*Candida*) culture; efinaconazole 10% solution or vehicle was applied once daily at bedtime for 48 weeks, with evaluation continuing to Week 52
- P3-01 randomized 870 subjects (656 efinaconazole/214 vehicle); P3-02 randomized 785 (581 efinaconazole/204 vehicle, four randomized-in-error subjects excluded from the ITT population)
- Primary efficacy endpoint: complete cure at Week 52 (0% clinical involvement of the target toenail, negative KOH, and negative fungal culture)
- Small analysis centers were pooled (centers with fewer than 9 efinaconazole or 3 vehicle subjects combined, smallest with largest, iteratively) before the CMH/ANOVA analyses; consistency of the treatment effect across centers was assessed via the Breslow-Day test, with sensitivity analyses planned if significant at the 0.10 level
- Notably, the applicant issued two versions of the SAP: the first signed off about a week after the last P3-01 subject completed, consistent with the protocol-specified endpoints; a second version signed 5 weeks later redefined the list and testing order of secondary/supportive endpoints (adding "clear nail," "almost clear nail," and refining the "clinical efficacy" cutoff from <10% to ≤10% affected nail) — the primary endpoint and its result were unchanged by this revision, and the FDA reviewer's analysis focused on the protocol/first-SAP-specified endpoints
- Primary result: complete cure 17.8% (efinaconazole) vs. 3.3% (vehicle) in P3-01, and 15.2% vs. 5.5% in P3-02 (both p<0.001)

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Reference ID 3271427/3500837, primary endpoint and SAP-versioning note, p.2]*

> "The primary efficacy endpoint was complete cure at Week 52 (0% clinical involvement of target toenail plus negative KOH and negative culture)... The applicant created two versions of the Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP). The first version of the SAP was signed off about a week after the last subject completed Study P3-01 and the proposed analyses were consistent with the endpoints and analyses specified in the protocol. However, the applicant then revised the SAP about 5 weeks later. The second version of the SAP redefined the sets of secondary and supportive endpoints, and the order in which they were to be analyzed. The primary endpoint remained the same in both versions of the SAP, and thus the primary conclusions of the study are not affected by the changes to the SAP."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, missing-data handling and per-protocol definition, p.8]*

> "The primary method of handling missing data for the primary efficacy analysis was last observation carried forward (LOCF). As a sensitivity analysis, subjects with missing Week 52 complete cure assessments were imputed as failures. A second sensitivity analysis imputes subjects with missing values as successes."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, analysis-center pooling rule, p.8]*

> "Small centers were combined into analysis centers for the CMH and ANOVA analyses. Centers with fewer than 9 efinaconazole and 3 vehicle subjects were pooled into analysis centers. Among the centers with fewer than 9 efinaconazole or 3 vehicle subjects, the smallest center was pooled with the largest, etc. until all analysis centers met the minimum size. Consistency of treatment response across analysis centers for the primary endpoint was assessed with the Breslow-Day test."

### 16. Tedizolid phosphate (Sivextro) — NDA 205435

**Sponsor:** Cubist Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI) caused by susceptible gram-positive organisms

**Approval date:** June 20, 2014

**Pivotal trial:** ESTABLISH-1 (Study TR701-112), NCT01170221; ESTABLISH-2 (Study TR701-113), NCT01421511

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, non-inferiority trial (oral tedizolid 6 days vs. oral linezolid 10 days, ESTABLISH-1; IV-to-oral tedizolid 6 days vs. IV-to-oral linezolid 10 days, ESTABLISH-2); Special Protocol Assessment (SPA), formally amended pre-unblinding (ESTABLISH-2's primary responder definition was changed via Protocol Amendment 6, acknowledged by FDA on December 7, 2012, before the trial's results were known)
- *Endpoints:* early clinical response (responder) at the 48-72 hour visit — defined initially (ESTABLISH-1, per the original 2010 SPA) as cessation of lesion spread plus resolution of fever, later redefined (ESTABLISH-2, per the amended SPA and evolving FDA guidance) as ≥20% reduction in lesion area from baseline, without a fever component
- *Primary analysis:* stratified proportion-difference test with adjusted 95% confidence interval for the non-inferiority comparison of early clinical response rates
- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented mid-trial endpoint elevation/redefinition (FDA feedback-driven) — the responder definition for ESTABLISH-2 (and, as a post hoc consistency check, recalculated for ESTABLISH-1) was changed from a fever/cessation-of-spread composite to a pure ≥20% lesion-area-reduction criterion, driven by the August 2010 FDA ABSSSI draft guidance, a 2011 Type C meeting, sponsor-reported practical difficulty obtaining reliable temperature measurements, and a June 2012 Biomarkers Consortium recommendation against including fever in the primary outcome

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ESTABLISH-1 and ESTABLISH-2 were phase 3, randomized (1:1), double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled, non-inferiority trials of tedizolid phosphate 200 mg once daily for 6 days vs. linezolid 600 mg twice daily for 10 days in adults with ABSSSI; ESTABLISH-1 used oral dosing throughout, ESTABLISH-2 allowed an initial IV phase with optional switch to oral
- On June 9, 2010, FDA issued a Special Protocol Agreement for ESTABLISH-1 defining the primary endpoint as cessation of spread of the primary lesion plus afebrile status (≤37.6°C, oral) at 48-72 hours, following the pattern of the era's ABSSSI trials; this SPA predated FDA's August 2010 draft ABSSSI guidance
- A January 2011 Type C meeting removed the SPA's minimum-febrile-patient enrollment quota for both trials but left ESTABLISH-1's primary endpoint definition otherwise intact; an August 2, 2011 SPA for ESTABLISH-2 initially retained a similar fever-inclusive composite responder definition
- Following sponsor-reported challenges collecting reliable serial temperature measurements (February 2012) and a June 2012 Biomarkers Consortium (Foundation for the NIH) recommendation that fever be excluded from the ABSSSI primary outcome, FDA acknowledged a November 9, 2012 protocol amendment (Amendment 6) to ESTABLISH-2 redefining the responder criterion as a pure ≥20% reduction in lesion area from baseline at 48-72 hours, without a temperature component — an amendment to (not a rescission of) the SPA
- Primary results: early clinical response 79.3% (tedizolid) vs. 79.1% (linezolid) in ESTABLISH-1 (treatment difference 0.1%, adjusted 95% CI -6.2% to 6.3%, using the original fever-inclusive definition), and 85.2% vs. 82.6% in ESTABLISH-2 (difference 2.6%, unadjusted 95% CI -3.0% to 8.2%, using the ≥20%-reduction definition); both trials met the pre-specified non-inferiority margin of -10% on the lower CI bound
- As a consistency check, the FDA reviewer recalculated ESTABLISH-1 using ESTABLISH-2's ≥20%-lesion-reduction definition (78.0% vs. 75.5%, difference 2.6%) and found non-inferiority would still have been demonstrated under that alternative definition

> "On 09 June 2010, the FDA issued a Special Protocol-Agreement letter for Study TR 701-112. The primary efficacy endpoint was agreed to be: cessation of spread of the primary ABSSSI lesion, compared with baseline...; and, temperature measurement (assessed by the Investigator) is ≤37.6°C (oral) and the next measurement (taken within 24 hours of the 48-72 Hour Visit) is also ≤37.6°C (oral)... The SPA was issued prior to the issuance of the FDA draft guidance 'Acute Bacterial Skin and Skin Structure Infections: Developing Drugs for Treatment' in August 2010."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, ESTABLISH-2 endpoint amendment, p.14]*

> "On June 2012, the Biomarkers Consortium of the Foundation for the National Institutes of Health recommended defining the early response in clinical trials for ABSSSI as a decrease from baseline of ≥20% in lesion area... at 48 to 72 hours after randomization and added that absence of elevated body temperature (fever) should not be a component of the primary outcome measure... On 07 December 2012, the FDA acknowledged the 09 November 2012 amendment to Study TR701-113 protocol (Protocol Amendment 6), amending the special protocol agreement. The amendment made the following modifications: Change the definition of a responder to the primary efficacy endpoint of a ≥20% reduction in lesion area from baseline."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, primary results, p.9]*

> "The early clinical response at the 48-72 Hour Visit in Study TR 701-112 was observed in 256/323(79.3%) of patients in the tedizolid phosphate group and 258/326(79.1%) of patients in the linezolid group in the ITT* Population, with a treatment difference 0.1% [adjusted 95% CI: -6.2%, 6.3%]. In Study TR 701-113, the early clinical response based on ≥ 20% decrease from baseline at 48-72 hour visit in lesion area was observed in 283/332(85.2%) of patients in the tedizolid phosphate group and 276/334(82.6%) of patients in the linezolid group, with a treatment difference of 2.6% [unadjusted 95% CI: -3.0%, 8.2%]. The lower limits of the 95% confidence intervals meet the pre-specified NI margin which required for it to be greater than -10%."

### 17. Tavaborole (Kerydin) — NDA 204427

**Sponsor:** Anacor Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Onychomycosis of the toenails due to *Trichophyton rubrum* or *Trichophyton mentagrophytes*

**Approval date:** July 7, 2014

**Pivotal trial:** Study 301, NCT01270971; Study 302, NCT01302119

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled trial, once-daily topical application for 48 weeks with follow-up to Week 52, submitted under Special Protocol Assessments
- *Endpoints:* complete cure at Week 52 (completely clear target nail, negative KOH, negative culture)
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by (pooled) analysis center
- *Missing data/bias:* last observation carried forward (LOCF) as primary missing-data method, with pre-specified sensitivity analyses imputing missing data as failures, as successes, and via multiple imputation

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 301 and Study 302 were identically designed phase 3, randomized (roughly 2:1 tavaborole:vehicle), double-blind, vehicle-controlled trials in subjects aged 18 and older with 20-60% target-toenail involvement and a clinical/mycological diagnosis of distal subungual onychomycosis; tavaborole topical solution 5% or vehicle was applied once daily to affected toenails for 48 weeks, with assessment through Week 52
- Study 301 randomized 400 tavaborole and 194 vehicle subjects (594 total); Study 302 randomized 399 tavaborole and 205 vehicle subjects (604 total, three randomized-in-error tavaborole subjects excluded)
- Primary efficacy endpoint: complete cure at Week 52 (completely clear target nail, negative KOH, and negative fungal culture), analyzed via a CMH test stratified by (pooled) analysis center; small centers were pooled using the same minimum-size rule later reused for efinaconazole's P3-01/P3-02 review (same FDA review division/statistical team era)
- Primary result: complete cure 6.5% (tavaborole) vs. 0.5% (vehicle), p=0.001, in Study 301, and 9.1% vs. 1.5%, p<0.001, in Study 302
- The protocols pre-specified three sensitivity analyses for missing Week-52 data: imputing missing as failure, imputing missing as success, and multiple imputation; the FDA reviewer found the "missing as failure" and LOCF analyses nearly identical (few subjects had post-baseline data supporting a success classification under LOCF), and per-protocol results consistent with the ITT/LOCF primary analysis

### 18. Oritavancin diphosphate (Orbactiv) — NDA 206334

**Sponsor:** The Medicines Company

**Indication approved:** Acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI) caused by susceptible gram-positive organisms

**Approval date:** August 6, 2014

**Pivotal trial:** SOLO I, NCT01252719; SOLO II, NCT01252732

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, non-inferiority trial (single 1200 mg IV oritavancin dose vs. 7-10 days of IV vancomycin), designed per the 2010 FDA ABSSSI guidance and agreed under a Special Protocol Agreement
- *Endpoints:* early clinical evaluation (ECE) composite responder rate at 48-72 hours (cessation of spread/reduction in lesion size, afebrile status, no rescue antibiotics); investigator-assessed clinical cure at post-therapy evaluation (PTE, 7-14 days after end of therapy) as a non-inferential secondary endpoint
- *Primary analysis:* stratified proportion-difference method for the non-inferiority comparison of ECE responder rates in the modified intent-to-treat (mITT) population
- *Regulatory:* SPA-agreed primary endpoint later superseded by revised disease-specific FDA guidance (same phenomenon flagged for dalbavancin and tedizolid in this batch) — the reviewer explicitly noted the ECE composite endpoint (fever-inclusive) "is no longer recommended for non-inferiority trials in ABSSSI" under the 2013 FDA guidance, which instead recommends a pure ≥20%-lesion-reduction endpoint; FDA also declined to treat the PTE clinical-cure secondary as formally testable for non-inferiority, citing a lack of a scientifically justifiable margin for that endpoint

**Trial design & endpoints**

- SOLO I and SOLO II were phase 3, global, multicenter, randomized (1:1), double-blind, active-controlled, parallel-group, non-inferiority trials of a single 1200 mg IV dose of oritavancin vs. 7-10 days of IV vancomycin (1 g or 15 mg/kg twice daily) in adults with ABSSSI suspected or confirmed to involve a gram-positive pathogen
- Primary efficacy endpoint: a composite responder definition at the Early Clinical Evaluation (ECE) timepoint (48-72 hours after infusion) requiring cessation of spread or reduction in size of the baseline lesion, absence of fever, and no rescue antibiotic medication, analyzed in the modified intent-to-treat (mITT) population; missing outcomes were treated as failures (responder-rate-based analyses), with a sensitivity analysis re-run treating missing data as successes
- Non-inferiority margin: 10%, with sample size (~960 patients, 480/arm) based on an assumed 75% responder rate in both arms providing ≥90% power at 1-sided alpha=0.025 to reject a null hypothesis that vancomycin's ECE responder rate exceeded oritavancin's by ≥10%; enrollment continued until approximately 175 MRSA-positive-at-baseline patients were confirmed
- Primary results: ECE responder rate 82.3% (391/475, oritavancin) vs. 78.9% (378/479, comparator) in SOLO I (difference 3.4%, 95% CI -1.6% to 8.4%), and 80.1% (403/503) vs. 82.9% (416/502) in SOLO II (difference -2.7%, 95% CI -7.5% to 2.0%); both met the pre-specified 10% non-inferiority margin
- The FDA reviewer explicitly noted that although the ECE endpoint was pre-specified and SPA-agreed, "this endpoint is no longer recommended for non-inferiority trials in ABSSSI" under the interim 2013 FDA guidance, and separately calculated a ≥20%-lesion-size-reduction responder rate at 48-72 hours (86.9% vs. 82.9% in SOLO I; 85.9% vs. 85.3% in SOLO II) as a bridge to the newer standard, finding consistent non-inferiority
- Investigator-assessed clinical cure at PTE (a secondary endpoint) was reported descriptively (79.6% vs. 80.0% in SOLO I; 82.7% vs. comparator in SOLO II) without a formal non-inferiority test, because FDA and the applicant agreed no scientifically justified margin existed for that later timepoint

H0: PVancomycin -POritavancin ≥ 0.10... However, patient enrollment was not to stop until approximately 175 patients were confirmed with MRSA as a baseline pathogen."

### 19. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir (Harvoni) — NDA 205834

**Sponsor:** Gilead Sciences, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) genotype 1 infection, as a fixed-dose combination tablet

**Approval date:** October 10, 2014

**Pivotal trial:** ION-1 (Study GS-US-337-0102), NCT01701401; ION-2 (Study GS-US-337-0109), NCT01768286; ION-3 (Study GS-US-337-0108), NCT01851330

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized non-comparative dose-regimen cohort design (each study randomized subjects across ledipasvir/sofosbuvir ± ribavirin regimens of differing duration, with each arm tested independently against a fixed historical performance goal rather than against each other); adaptive seamless enrollment with a Part A/Part B conditional-power gate (ION-1 halted enrollment after ~25% of planned subjects per arm, with an external DMC reviewing conditional power on SVR4 before authorizing full Part B enrollment (conditional-power-gated two-part enrollment design))
- *Endpoints:* sustained virologic response 12 weeks after end of therapy (SVR12)
- *Primary analysis:* one-sample binomial test against a pre-specified historical control SVR rate (60% for treatment-naive subjects in ION-1/ION-3; 25% for treatment-experienced subjects in ION-2)
- *Multiplicity:* Hochberg step-up procedure applied across the family of simultaneous one-sample tests (one per treatment arm/duration) to control the family-wise type I error rate
- *Missing data/bias:* missing SVR12 substituted by SVR24 if available, otherwise imputed as treatment failure (same HCV-specific SVR12/SVR24 imputation rule applied across HCV entries in this census)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ION-1 (treatment-naive, cirrhotic and non-cirrhotic, US and European sites) and ION-3 (treatment-naive, non-cirrhotic only, US sites) were phase 3, multicenter, randomized, open-label trials of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir fixed-dose combination (FDC) with or without ribavirin for varying durations; ION-1 had four arms (12- and 24-week FDC ± RBV) while ION-3 had three arms (8-week FDC ± RBV, 12-week FDC); the pre-NDA meeting agreement was that ION-1's 24-week arms would not be needed for the submission if the 12-week arms achieved SVR12 ≥90% in both cirrhotic and non-cirrhotic subjects
- ION-1 used a two-part adaptive design: Part A enrolled ~25% of the planned sample (~50/arm); after all Part A subjects in the two 12-week arms reached post-treatment Week 4, an external Data Monitoring Committee computed conditional power on SVR4 rates and authorized full Part B enrollment (~600 more subjects across all four arms) only if conditional power was ≥5%
- ION-2 enrolled treatment-experienced (including cirrhotic) subjects, all from US sites, in the same four-arm 12-/24-week ± RBV structure as ION-1
- Primary efficacy endpoint (all three trials): SVR12, with the primary hypothesis that each treatment arm's SVR12 rate exceeded a historical-control performance goal; historical rates were set at 60% for treatment-naive subjects (ION-1/ION-3) and 25% for treatment-experienced subjects (ION-2), the latter derived by the applicant from a weighted average of telaprevir/boceprevir retreatment SVR rates (~65% for PegIFN/RBV-experienced, 5% for prior protease-inhibitor-regimen failures) discounted 10 percentage points for the shorter/safer regimen
- A Hochberg step-up multiple-comparison procedure controlled the family-wise type I error rate across the simultaneous one-sample tests for each arm within a study
- FDA's Division agreed with the applicant's 25% historical rate for ION-2 based on historical data and clinical factors (citing Poynard et al., Gastroenterology 2009)

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2014/205834Orig1s000ltr.pdf

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Reference ID 3539966, ION-1 adaptive two-part design, p.8]*

> "There were two parts in subject enrollment in the ION-1 study. Part A planned to randomize approximately 50 subjects in each arm (i.e., 25% of the planned sample size). Enrollment was halted once Part A was fully enrolled. After all subjects in the two 12-week arms completed post-treatment Week 4, an interim analysis was planned to be conducted by the external data monitoring committee to determine whether to terminate or continue the two 12-week regimens. The interim analysis calculated the conditional power based on the SVR4 rates for the two 12-week arms. If the conditional power was less than 5%, the two 12-week arms would be discontinued. If the conditional power was equal to or greater than 5%, Part B would start to enroll and randomize approximately 600 additional subjects into all four treatment groups."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, ION-1/ION-3 primary hypothesis, p.8]*

> "The primary efficacy endpoint in both studies was the proportion of subjects achieving SVR12. Also, the two studies had the same primary hypothesis which was that the SVR12 rate in each treatment arm was superior to the historical control rate of 60%."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, ION-2 historical-rate justification, p.18]*

> "The one-sample binomial test was performed to evaluate whether the SVR12 rate in each treatment group was superior to the 25% historical rate. A Hochberg procedure was applied to control the family-wise type I error rate... A 35% null SVR rate was obtained after averaging a 65% retreatment SVR control rate for treatment-experienced subjects... and a 5% SVR control rate for subjects who failed prior treatment with a PI+Peg-IFN+RBV regimen... In addition, a discount of 10 percentage points in efficacy was allowed due to the expected improved safety profile and significantly shorter duration associated with the treatment, which resulted in a null SVR rate for this study of 25%. The Division agreed with the historical rate of 25% based on considering historical data and clinical factors (Poynard et al, Gastroenterology 2009)."
