### 20. Finafloxacin (Xtoro) — NDA 206307

**Sponsor:** Alcon Research, Ltd.

**Indication approved:** Acute otitis externa (AOE) caused by susceptible isolates of *Pseudomonas aeruginosa* and *Staphylococcus aureus*

**Approval date:** December 17, 2014

**Pivotal trial:** Study C-10-018, NCT01535599; Study C-10-019, NCT01535560 (registered under sponsor code AL-60371)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-masked, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group trial (topical otic suspension)
- *Endpoints:* clinical cure in the study ear at test-of-cure (TOC, Day 11 +2), defined as a sum score of zero across tenderness, erythema, and edema; microbiological success and time to cessation of ear pain (patient/caregiver telephone diary, twice-daily) as secondary endpoints
- *Primary analysis:* stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test, adjusted for baseline otowick use, on clinical cure rates; Kaplan-Meier estimation with log-rank test for the time-to-cessation-of-ear-pain secondary endpoint
- *Missing data/bias:* missing data imputed as treatment failures for the primary analysis (patients not completing the study, or missing one or more of the three component clinical signs), with LOCF and observed-cases-only sensitivity analyses; the applicant's pre-specified primary analysis population was the pathogen-positive subset of the ITT population (only ~41-51% of enrolled subjects at each site had a positive baseline culture for the two named target organisms), with the FDA reviewer additionally reporting results in the broader ITT and culture-positive-subset populations

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Studies C-10-018 and C-10-019 were two identically designed phase 3, multicenter (US, Canada, Puerto Rico), randomized (1:1), double-masked, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group trials of finafloxacin otic suspension 0.3% vs. vehicle in patients aged 6 months and older with a clinical diagnosis of acute otitis externa; C-10-018 randomized/treated 686 subjects (67 centers), C-10-019 randomized/treated 548 subjects (46 centers)
- Primary efficacy endpoint: clinical cure in the study ear at the test-of-cure (TOC) visit (Day 11 +2), defined as a sum score of zero across the three clinical signs of AOE (ear tenderness, erythema, edema), each assessed by the investigator via otoscope
- The applicant pre-specified the primary analysis population as the "ITT pathogen positive subset" — ITT subjects with a baseline microbiological specimen containing *Pseudomonas aeruginosa* and/or *Staphylococcus aureus* — capturing only 41.2% (C-10-018) and 50.5% (C-10-019) of the full ITT population; the FDA clinical review team additionally required reporting in a broader "ITT culture positive subset" (any positive baseline culture, not restricted to the two named pathogens)
- Sample size (500 subjects, 250/arm, across both trials) was based on Fisher's exact test at 2-sided alpha=0.05, an assumed 74% finafloxacin cure rate, a 20-percentage-point treatment difference, 90% power, and an assumed 56% baseline pathogen-positivity rate
- Primary analysis: stratified CMH test (adjusting for baseline otowick use) comparing clinical cure rates between arms in the ITT pathogen-positive subset; the same CMH approach was applied to the microbiological-success secondary endpoint; time to cessation of ear pain used Kaplan-Meier estimation with a log-rank test, right-censoring non-resolvers at their last diary timepoint (or Day 11 for early discontinuers)
- Primary results (ITT pathogen-positive subset, TOC visit): clinical cure 71.7% (104/145) in C-10-018 and 68.7% (101/147) in C-10-019 for finafloxacin, each superior to vehicle (exact comparator rates not extracted here)
- Notably, the pivotal journal publication reporting these two studies did not appear until 2026 — roughly 11 years after FDA approval — illustrating that publication timing for older ABSSSI/otic-indication trials can lag approval substantially

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2014/206307s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/206307Orig1s000StatR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (Study C-10-019) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01535560
- Pivotal publication: Edmunds A, et al. "Efficacy and Safety of Finafloxacin Otic Suspension, 0.3% for the Treatment of Acute Otitis Externa: Results from two Phase III Randomized Clinical Studies." *Ann Otol Rhinol Laryngol.* 2026 May 28 (online ahead of print). [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1177/00034894261453726), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42210509/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Efficacy%20and%20Safety%20of%20Finafloxacin%20Otic%20Suspension%20Acute%20Otitis%20Externa)

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting is recorded for this NDA in the reviewed documents.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Reference ID 3633338, primary endpoint and pivotal studies, p.3]*

> "In order to support the approval of Finafloxacin otic suspension for AOE, the applicant submitted two pivotal studies: Study C-10-018, and Study C-10-019. Studies C-10-018 and C-10-019 were two identically designed phase 3 studies. Both were multicenter, randomized, double-masked, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group studies... The primary efficacy endpoint was the percentage of patients with clinical cures at the test-of-cure (TOC) visit (Day 11 + 2); a subject was considered as clinical cure if the subject's sum score of ear tenderness, erythema, and edema was zero (i.e., none)."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, primary analysis population definition, p.3]*

> "The protocol-defined primary analysis set for the evaluation of the primary, secondary efficacy endpoints was the pathogen positive subset of intent-to-treat (ITT) population (referred as ITT pathogen positive subset throughout this review), which included all subjects who received study treatment and had a microbiological specimen in the study ear that contained at least one of the following two organisms (considered by the applicant as etiological agents of AOE) at baseline: Pseudomonas aeruginosa and/or Staphylococcus aureus."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, sample size and missing-data handling, p.11-12]*

> "The sample size estimation of 500 subjects (250 per arm) for both studies was based on the following assumptions proposed by the applicant to support the primary efficacy endpoint: Fisher's exact test at the 0.05 two-sided level of significance; Clinical cure rate of 74% for the finafloxacin treatment group; A treatment difference of 20% between the finafloxacin group and the vehicle group; 90% power... For the primary efficacy analysis, missing data were imputed as 'failures' for patients who did not complete the study or who had missing scores for 1 or more of the components of clinical cure."

### 21. Ceftolozane/tazobactam (Zerbaxa) — NDA 206829

**Sponsor:** Cubist Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Complicated intra-abdominal infections (cIAI, in combination with metronidazole) and complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI), including pyelonephritis

**Approval date:** December 19, 2014

**Pivotal trial:** ASPECT-cIAI (Trial cIAI-10-08&09), NCT01445678; ASPECT-cUTI (Trial cUTI-10-04&05), NCT01345929

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled; post-hoc recombination of differently-enrolled cohorts into one primary analysis population (two identical cIAI Phase 3 protocols pooled into one trial per FDA draft guidance)
- *Endpoints:* clinical cure rate at Test-of-Cure (cIAI); composite of clinical cure AND microbiological eradication at Test-of-Cure (cUTI)
- *Primary analysis:* non-inferiority via two-sided 95% CI on treatment difference in clinical cure rates (Miettinen-Nurminen-type large-sample CI)
- *Missing data/bias:* treatment-failure imputation for missing/indeterminate response (MITT population)
- *Regulatory:* FDA Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee input on composite-endpoint adequacy; reviewer-documented concern about a well-defined-endpoint criterion (21 CFR adequate-and-well-controlled standard) for the cUTI composite

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ASPECT-cIAI: randomized, double-blind, double-dummy trial of IV ceftolozane/tazobactam 1.5 g q8h + metronidazole vs. IV meropenem 1 g q8h in adults with cIAI; originally two identical 906-subject Phase 3 protocols, pooled into a single 993-subject trial after FDA's draft cIAI guidance and Division discussions; primary analysis population was the Microbiological Intent-to-Treat (MITT) population (all randomized patients with ≥1 baseline intra-abdominal pathogen, N=806)
- ASPECT-cIAI primary endpoint: clinical cure rate at the Test-of-Cure (TOC) visit, Day 24-32, in the MITT population; 10% non-inferiority margin agreed with the Agency in advance; sample size ~988 (494/arm) planned assuming 75% clinical cure and 40% of ITT patients contributing to MITT
- ASPECT-cUTI: randomized, double-blind trial of IV ceftolozane/tazobactam vs. IV levofloxacin in 1083 subjects (modified MITT, mMITT, N=800) with cUTI including pyelonephritis; primary endpoint was a composite requiring both investigator-judged clinical cure AND microbiological eradication at TOC (7±2 days post-therapy); 10% non-inferiority margin, no provision for oral step-down
- No formal interim analyses in either trial; missing/indeterminate clinical response in the MITT population was counted as treatment failure (as-observed approach used for the ME/CE/Expanded-ME populations)

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, cIAI Executive Summary, p.5]*

> "This submission provided adequate evidence of efficacy and safety for ZerbaxaTM (ceftolozane/tazobactam)... However, overall evidence was not considered to be highly robust since it relied on a single Phase 3 pivotal trial (Trial cIAI-10-08&09)... which only narrowly met its primary objective of demonstrating the non-inferiority of ceftolozane/tazobactam + metronidazole to comparator therapy (i.v. meropenem) using a pre-specified margin of 10%... The primary analysis showed lower rates in the ceftolozane/tazobactam + metronidazole arm than in the meropenem arm at 323/389 (83.0%) vs. 364/417 (87.3%), a treatment difference of -4.3% (95% CI: -9.2%, 0.7%)... This finding satisfied the pre-specified non-inferiority hypothesis based on a 10% NI margin with a lower confidence limit of -9.2% which fell slightly above the minimum requirement for non-inferiority at -10%."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, cIAI section, p.6]*

> "Originally, Cubist initiated 2 identical Phase 3 trials, each with a planned sample size of 906 subjects (453 subjects per arm). However, based on the release of the FDA Draft Guidance for cIAI and subsequent discussions with the Division, Cubist switched to a single study strategy for the cIAI indication. Such a strategy was achieved by pooling subjects from the two ongoing Phase 3 trial protocols into a single Phase 3 trial (Trial -08&09)."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, cUTI Executive Summary, Reference ID 3632844]*

> "The primary analysis population was the modified microbiological intention-to-treat population (mMITT)... The primary efficacy endpoint was a composite requiring both investigator judgment that signs and symptoms had resolved and microbiological eradication of the causative pathogen by the test of cure (TOC) visit 7 ± 2 days following the end of therapy... Although designed to evaluate non-inferiority... ceftolozane/tazobactam met statistical criteria for demonstrating superiority relative to the levofloxacin control with respect to the primary efficacy analysis. The likely reason for the superiority demonstration was that 212 subjects (27%) in the primary mMITT population had baseline pathogens resistant to levofloxacin."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, cUTI section 3.2.1.9, Reference ID 3632844]*

> "The thinking of this reviewer is that treatment effects on the clinical and microbiological components of the composite can potentially leave several questions unanswered. First, a treatment effect on the microbiological endpoint may not reflect patient benefit in terms of feeling, function, or survival, which is the ultimate measure of efficacy... Second, this reviewer's view is that the clinical cure endpoint is not sufficiently well-defined, and the meaningfulness of the endpoint cannot be assured if it is unclear what the endpoint measures."

### 22. Peramivir (Rapivab) — NDA 206426

**Sponsor:** BioCryst Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of acute uncomplicated influenza in patients 18 years and older

**Approval date:** December 19, 2014

**Pivotal trial:** Trial 0722T0621 ("Study 621"), Japan, no confirmed NCT registration (Shionogi-conducted, JAPIC-era trial); supportive active-controlled Trial 0815T0631, no confirmed NCT registration

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (Study 621); randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled vs. oral oseltamivir (Study 815, non-pivotal due to a Tamiflu-resistant epidemic season); cross-trial pooled/integrated analysis (five BioCryst/Shionogi trials pooled for dose-response and subgroup conclusions)
- *Endpoints:* time to alleviation of symptoms ("time to healing" — all 7 influenza symptoms mild/absent for ≥21.5 hours), ITTI (intent-to-treat infected) population
- *Primary analysis:* Cox proportional-hazards regression (stratified by smoking status and baseline composite symptom score), hazard ratio and Kaplan-Meier median time-to-healing; Wilcoxon-Gehan test (Study 212, alternate design)
- *Multiplicity:* Bonferroni adjustment across multiple peramivir dose arms within a trial; primary comparison in Study 621 was pooled 300 mg + 600 mg arms vs. placebo to sidestep the two-active-arm multiplicity problem
- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented deviation from proper multiplicity handling — the non-inferiority margin for Study 815 used a 97.5% CI with no adjustment for two dose arms tested against Tamiflu, when reviewer calculates 98.75% would have been the multiplicity-correct bound

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 621: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in Japan (2007-08 flu season), 300 subjects at 75 centers randomized 1:1:1 to peramivir 300 mg IV, 600 mg IV, or placebo, single dose; randomization stratified by smoking status and baseline composite symptom score (≤14 vs. >14, summed 0-3 across 7 symptoms); considered the pivotal trial
- Study 815: randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, three-arm active-controlled trial (1099 subjects, 146 centers, 2008-09 season) of peramivir 300 mg or 600 mg IV vs. oral oseltamivir 75 mg BID x5 days; an unforeseen, widespread oseltamivir-resistant (H275Y) strain circulated that season, meaning most "active-control" subjects were not on a provably effective comparator — FDA's reviewer concluded this prevented Study 815 from serving as a pivotal non-inferiority trial
- Primary endpoint (all trials): time to alleviation of symptoms, defined as hours from study-drug initiation to the first of two consecutive diary entries ≥21.5 hours apart with no moderate/severe/missing symptom score across all seven symptoms (cough, sore throat, nasal congestion, headache, feverishness, myalgia, fatigue)
- Three supportive US trials (211, 311, 212) used intramuscular dosing (150/300/600 mg) with a bioequivalence bridge to the IV formulation; Study 815's non-inferiority margin (upper 97.5% CI bound on HR of 1.17) was derived by pooling historical Tamiflu-NDA data
- Results: Study 621 showed peramivir 600 mg reduced median time to healing by ~20-30 hours vs. placebo; none of the smaller supportive trials reached formal one-sided 0.025 significance alone, though FDA's reviewer found the pooled dose-response pattern and consistent effect direction supportive

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2014/206426lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (combined carcinogenicity + clinical statistical review; clinical review by Thomas Hammerstrom, PhD) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/206426Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov: no NCT record confirmed for Study 621/Study 815 via search (likely JAPIC-registered, Japan-conducted trials predating routine ClinicalTrials.gov registration for non-US trials)

"Efficacy and safety of intravenous peramivir for treatment of seasonal influenza virus infection." *Antimicrob Agents Chemother.* 2010;54(11):4568-74. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1128/AAC.00474-10), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20713668/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Efficacy%20and%20safety%20of%20intravenous%20peramivir%20for%20treatment%20of%20seasonal%20influenza%20virus%20infection)
- Supportive publication (Study 815): Kohno S, et al. "Phase III randomized, double-blind study comparing single-dose intravenous peramivir with oral oseltamivir in patients with seasonal influenza virus infection." *Antimicrob Agents Chemother.* 2011;55(11):5267-76. [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21825298/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Phase%20III%20randomized%20double-blind%20study%20comparing%20single-dose%20intravenous%20peramivir%20with%20oral%20oseltamivir)

**Other resources**

- No sponsor IPD-sharing program participation confirmed.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting identified for this NDA.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Executive Summary, Reference ID 3615270]*

> "Two of these trials, 0722T0621 and 0815T0631 (henceforth, trials 722 and 815), used the 600 mg IV dose proposed in the application... Trial 722 was placebo controlled and 815 was active controlled with Tamiflu. Trial 722 will be considered the pivotal trial. A flu season with an unforeseen and widespread Tamiflu resistant influenza strain means that the majority of the control subjects in trial 815 were not treated with a provably effective active drug. Thus, establishment of non-inferiority in trial 815 cannot be interpreted as non-inferiority to an active drug. This prevents trial 815 from being a pivotal trial."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §2.2.5, Reference ID 3615270]*

> "The primary endpoint was the time until all seven symptoms were mild or none for two consecutive diary entries at least 21.5 hours apart... The multiplicity problem created by the presence of two peramivir arms was dealt with by making the primary comparison placebo to the pooled 300mg and 600mg arms."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §2.2.5, Reference ID 3615270]*

> "Trial 815 also based its primary analysis on a Cox regression. Because this trial had an active control, Tamiflu, a non-inferiority comparison was proposed. A conclusion of efficacy for either the 300 mg or the 600 mg arm would be made if the 97.5% upper bound for the hazard ratio of that arm to Tamiflu was <1.17... One may briefly note that using 97.5% upper bound makes no adjustment for multiplicity. The appropriate confidence limit would have been 98.75%."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Executive Summary conclusion, Reference ID 3615270]*

> "In short summary, peramivir at 600mg is convincingly effective against Tamiflu susceptible strains of influenza A with about a 30 hour reduction is symptom duration... it is unlikely that peramivir is very effective against influenza B or against strains of influenza A that are Tamiflu resistant."

### 23. Ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir + dasabuvir (Viekira Pak) — NDA 206619

**Sponsor:** AbbVie Inc.

**Indication approved:** Chronic genotype 1 hepatitis C virus infection, including patients with compensated cirrhosis

**Approval date:** December 19, 2014

**Pivotal trial:** SAPPHIRE-I (M11-646), SAPPHIRE-II (M13-098), PEARL-II (M13-389), PEARL-III (M13-961), PEARL-IV (M14-002), TURQUOISE-II (M13-099); NCTs not individually re-confirmed via ClinicalTrials.gov search for this entry (all pre-date routine SAP/protocol posting)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (SAPPHIRE-I/II, with an embedded delayed-treatment placebo arm for safety characterization); randomized, double-blind, active-component-comparison design (PEARL trials, 3DAA vs. 3DAA+RBV); randomized, open-label, dose-duration comparison in cirrhotics (TURQUOISE-II); historical-control non-inferiority/superiority threshold analysis (no concurrent active comparator arm) **
- *Endpoints:* sustained virologic response at post-treatment week 12 (SVR12)
- *Primary analysis:* two-sided 95%/97.5% CI on SVR12 proportion compared against a pre-specified historical-control threshold derived from telaprevir + pegIFN/RBV trials (REALIZE, ADVANCE, ILLUMINATE); non-inferiority tested first, then superiority, per population-specific margins
- *Missing data/bias:* SVR12 treatment-failure imputation for missing/discontinued patients
- *Regulatory:* FDA-agreed pre-specified historical-control thresholds set at the IND stage; reviewer-documented limitation that historical-control comparisons are potentially confounded relative to a concurrent randomized control

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Six Phase 3 double-blind, randomized, multicenter trials plus one 14-arm Phase 2 study supported the NDA; primary efficacy comparison in all six Phase 3 trials was not a concurrent active-control comparison but a comparison of the observed SVR12 rate's 95% CI lower bound against pre-specified non-inferiority/superiority thresholds computed from historical telaprevir+pegIFN/RBV trial data (REALIZE, ADVANCE, ILLUMINATE), weighted by expected sub-genotype/treatment-history population balance
- SAPPHIRE-I (M11-646, N=631, genotype 1 treatment-naive non-cirrhotic) and SAPPHIRE-II (M13-098, N=394, treatment-experienced non-cirrhotic): randomized 3:1 to 3DAA+RBV for 12 weeks or blinded placebo for 12 weeks (placebo patients then received open-label 3DAA+RBV); primary purpose of the placebo arm was double-blind characterization of adverse events in an untreated HCV population, not an efficacy comparator
- PEARL-II/III/IV (M13-389/M13-961/M14-002): randomized, double-blind trials in non-cirrhotic patients comparing 3DAA+RBV vs. 3DAA alone for 12 weeks, to assess whether ribavirin could be omitted by genotype 1 subtype
- TURQUOISE-II (M13-099, N=380): randomized, open-label trial in genotype 1 patients with compensated cirrhosis comparing 12 vs. 24 weeks of 3DAA+RBV; randomized 3:5 then 3:1 (12-week:24-week arms) as enrollment progressed; primary objective (12-week regimen vs. historical control) was easily met, so FDA's review focused on the secondary 12-vs-24-week comparison
- Thresholds (examples): genotype 1 treatment-naive non-cirrhotic NI margin 70%/superiority 80%; genotype 1 treatment-experienced non-cirrhotic NI 60%/superiority 70%; cirrhotic genotype 1 treatment-naive NI 56%/superiority 67% — all derived by subtracting a 10.5% non-inferiority margin from the historical-control superiority threshold

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §2.3, Reference ID 3630096]*

> "Primary efficacy is demonstrated in the Phase 3 trials of this submission based on comparisons of the test regimen (3DAA+RBV or 3DAA alone) to an historical control of telaprevir plus pegIFN and RBV. Based on historical data, thresholds for demonstrating non-inferiority (NI) and superiority (SUP) were named in the Phase 3 protocols. To demonstrate efficacy, a 95% confidence interval was constructed for the primary endpoint results (SVR12 rate) and the lower bound was compared against the appropriate threshold... At the IND stage, the thresholds presented here were agreed upon by both the clinical and statistical FDA staff."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §2.3, Reference ID 3630096]*

> "Clearly, the use of historical controls suffers from potential confounding associated with lack of patient comparability at baseline with respect to both measured and unmeasured variables that could bias the outcomes."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §3.1.3.2, Reference ID 3630096]*

> "These studies were unique in that they included a placebo arm. Patients were randomized to 3DAA+RBV or placebo... The applicant stated that the inclusion of a blinded placebo arm allows for 'characterization of adverse events in an untreated, chronically HCV infected population.' A primary purpose of the trial then appears to be to compare safety outcomes during the initial 12 weeks."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §3.1.3.3, Reference ID 3630096]*

> "The primary objective of the study was to compare the 12-week regimen SVR12 rate to the historical SVR12 rate of telaprevir plus pegIFN and RBV using a 2-sided 97.5% confidence interval and a non-inferiority margin of 43% and a superiority margin of 54%... The primary objective was easily achieved with SVR12 rates over 90% seen in each arm. Therefore the primary question addressed in this review is whether 24 weeks of treatment is better than 12 weeks of treatment for all cirrhotic patients."

### 24. Ceftazidime/avibactam (Avycaz) — NDA 206494

**Sponsor:** Forest Laboratories, Inc. / Cerexa, Inc. (AstraZeneca-Forest-Cerexa; later Allergan)

**Indication approved:** Complicated intra-abdominal infections (cIAI, with metronidazole) and complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI), in patients with limited or no alternative treatment options

**Approval date:** February 25, 2015

**Pivotal trial:** No single pivotal Phase 3 trial reviewed at approval — Phase 2 trials NXL104/2001 (cUTI), NCT00690378, and NXL104/2002 (cIAI), NCT00752219, plus preliminary/topline data from the ongoing Phase 3 RECLAIM cIAI trials (D4280C00001/D4280C00005), NCT01499290 and NCT01726023

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, investigator-blind or double-blind, active-controlled Phase 2 trials (no formal hypothesis testing); accelerated approval based on limited/descriptive efficacy data given unmet medical need 
- *Endpoints:* clinical and microbiological response/cure at Test-of-Cure (descriptive, not a formally tested primary endpoint in the reviewed Phase 2 data)
- *Primary analysis:* descriptive point estimates and 95% CIs for response-rate differences, no pre-specified "win" criteria (exploratory analyses only)
- *Missing data/bias:* none — reviewer explicitly notes the trials had no pre-specified inferential hypotheses to test
- *Regulatory:* 505(b)(2) approval relying on prior FDA findings of ceftazidime efficacy/safety plus published literature; QIDP designation (March 2013); Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee (AIDAC) meeting December 5, 2014 recommended approval with labeling restrictions despite incomplete confirmatory data; reviewer-documented mortality imbalance in a renally-impaired subgroup used to justify a boxed-warning-adjacent labeling restriction

**Trial design & endpoints**

- NXL104/2001 (cUTI): Phase 2, multicenter, randomized, investigator-blind, active-controlled trial vs. imipenem-cilastatin, with an oral ciprofloxacin step-down option; mMITT population N=95; "these trials were not designed with any formal statistical hypotheses for inferential testing, and therefore, statistical analysis on efficacy was limited to descriptive data summaries with no objectively defined 'win' criteria" (FDA reviewer)
- NXL104/2002 (cIAI): Phase 2, multicenter, randomized, double-blind trial of CAZ-AVI + metronidazole vs. meropenem; mMITT N=174; sponsor-verified clinical cure at TOC was numerically lower for CAZ-AVI+MTZ (82.4%) than meropenem (88.8%)
- Study D4280C00006: ongoing open-label Phase 3 trial in ceftazidime-non-susceptible (CAZ-NS) pathogens, comparing CAZ-AVI to best-available-therapy (carbapenems); only 4 cIAI and 44 cUTI mMITT subjects available at the interim cutoff reviewed
- RECLAIM (D4280C00001/D4280C00005): randomized, multicenter, double-blind, non-inferiority Phase 3 trial of CAZ-AVI + metronidazole vs. meropenem in cIAI, 10% non-inferiority margin, primary endpoint clinical cure at TOC (Day 28-35) in the mMITT population, N=1066 — "the data from this trial has not been submitted to the Agency for review" at the time of the statistical review; only sponsor-submitted topline tables (including a renal-impairment subgroup analysis and a mortality imbalance) were available
- FDA's reviewer found lower clinical cure rates in CAZ-AVI patients with baseline creatinine clearance 30-50 mL/min (85%→45%) versus meropenem (86%→74%) in RECLAIM topline data, alongside a numerically higher mortality rate in that renally-impaired CAZ-AVI subgroup (25.8% vs. 8.6%)

### 25. Isavuconazonium sulfate (Cresemba) — NDA 207500 (capsules) / NDA 207501 (injection)

**Sponsor:** Astellas Pharma US, Inc. (developed by Basilea Pharmaceutica)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of invasive aspergillosis and invasive mucormycosis in patients 18 years of age and older

**Approval date:** March 6, 2015

**Pivotal trial:** SECURE (Study 9766-CL-0104), NCT00412893 (aspergillosis, non-inferiority vs. voriconazole); VITAL (Study 9766-CL-0103), NCT00634049 (mucormycosis and renally-impaired aspergillosis, single-arm)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, non-inferiority, active-controlled comparative-group trial (SECURE); single-arm, open-label trial (VITAL)
- *Endpoints:* all-cause mortality through Day 42 (SECURE primary); all-cause mortality through Day 42 among a Data Review Committee-adjudicated proven/probable subgroup (VITAL)
- *Primary analysis:* two-sided 95% CI on the treatment difference in all-cause mortality, compared against a pre-specified 10% non-inferiority margin (SECURE); exact (Clopper-Pearson-type) binomial confidence interval on all-cause mortality rate, descriptive (VITAL, no comparator)
- *Missing data/bias:* unknown-survival-status patients through Day 42/84 counted as deaths (worst-case imputation)
- *Regulatory:* mucormycosis indication approved on a single open-label trial's proven/probable subgroup, supported by a treatment-effect analogy to other approved antifungals in a comparably difficult-to-treat infection — an FDA reviewer explicitly deferred the ultimate weighing of this evidence to the review team

**Trial design & endpoints**

- SECURE (Study 9766-CL-0104): randomized, double-blind, multicenter, non-inferiority, comparative-group trial of isavuconazole vs. voriconazole in patients with invasive mold disease, primarily invasive aspergillosis; primary objective was to assess non-inferiority of isavuconazole vs. voriconazole in all-cause mortality through Day 42; primary analysis population included patients with proven/probable/possible invasive fungal disease and mycological confirmation (mycological ITT, myITT)
- SECURE primary analysis: two-sided 95% CI for the difference in all-cause-mortality rates (isavuconazole minus voriconazole) compared to a pre-specified 10% non-inferiority margin; all-cause mortality through Day 42 was 18.6% (isavuconazole) vs. 20.2% (voriconazole) in the ITT population, treatment difference 95% CI (-8.0%, 5.9%); non-inferiority demonstrated in ITT and proven/probable subpopulations (upper CI bounds 7.3-8.2%, below the 10% margin)
- VITAL (Study 9766-CL-0103): single-arm, open-label trial in patients with invasive mucormycosis, invasive aspergillosis with renal impairment, or other invasive fungal disease; 46 patients enrolled with mucormycosis, 37 DRC-adjudicated as proven/probable mucormycosis-only; all-cause mortality through Day 42 reported descriptively with an exact 95% CI, no comparator arm or pre-specified hypothesis test
- Supportive aspergillosis-with-renal-impairment data: 24 patients from VITAL assessed by the Data Review Committee as having aspergillosis only (20 renally impaired); all-cause mortality through Day 42 was 12.5%
- FDA's reviewer concluded adequate evidence of efficacy for invasive aspergillosis (SECURE plus the VITAL renal-impairment subset) but treated the mucormycosis indication as resting on a single uncontrolled trial subset, recommending the review team weigh it "similar to" other single-arm evidentiary bases used for difficult-to-treat fungal infections

The primary efficacy endpoint was the crude rate of all-cause mortality through Day 42."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review Executive Summary]*

If the upper bound was less than 10%, isavuconazole was considered non-inferior to voriconazole with respect to all-cause mortality through Day 42."

This study enrolled 46 patients with mucormycosis, 37 were assessed by the DRC as having proven or probable invasive mucormycosis infection only."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review Executive Summary]*

In conjunction with the successful outcome of the larger randomized, comparative Study 9766-CL-0104 in invasive aspergillosis, another difficult to treat fungal infection, it is recommended that the results of Study 9766-CL-0103 be considered adequate evidence of efficacy to support the indication of treatment of invasive mucormycosis for isavuconazole. The final decision, however, is left to the Medical Division."

### 26. Daclatasvir (Daklinza) — NDA 206843

**Sponsor:** Bristol-Myers Squibb Company

**Indication approved:** Chronic hepatitis C virus genotype 3 infection, in combination with sofosbuvir

**Approval date:** July 24, 2015

**Pivotal trial:** ALLY-3 (Study AI444218), NCT02032901

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial (no concurrent comparator arm); Complete Response Letter followed by resubmission and approval (original NDA 206,843 for daclatasvir+asunaprevir genotype 1/4 data received a CRL, Nov 2014; genotype 3 resubmission based on a single new trial)
- *Endpoints:* sustained virologic response at post-treatment week 12 (SVR12)
- *Primary analysis:* descriptive proportion with 95% CI (no protocol-defined "win" criterion); FDA post-hoc derivation of an implicit non-inferiority margin for a single-arm trial from historical placebo/standard-of-care SVR12 data **
- *Missing data/bias:* SVR12 treatment-failure imputation for missing values
- *Regulatory:* reviewer-identified statistical issue — protocol did not pre-specify a non-inferiority margin or win criterion, so the statistical reviewer independently computed a range of plausible NI margins (as low as -17%) from historical data to contextualize the single-arm result

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Original NDA 206,843 (daclatasvir) and companion NDA 206,844 (asunaprevir) were submitted together in March 2014 for genotype 1/4 HCV, supported by three Phase 3 trials (AI447026, AI447028, AI447029); NDA 206,844 was withdrawn by the sponsor mid-cycle and FDA issued a Complete Response Letter for NDA 206,843 on November 25, 2014
- The resubmission reviewed here provided only one new Phase 3 study, AI444218 (ALLY-3), to support daclatasvir + sofosbuvir (no ritonavir/asunaprevir) for genotype 3 HCV
- ALLY-3: single-arm, open-label trial, 152 subjects (101 treatment-naive, 51 pegIFN/RBV-treatment-experienced) with genotype 3 HCV, treated with daclatasvir 60 mg + sofosbuvir 400 mg once daily for 12 weeks; primary endpoint SVR12 (HCV RNA below LLOQ at post-treatment week 12); no comparator arm and no protocol-defined non-inferiority margin or hypothesis test
- Overall SVR12 89% (135/152, 95% CI 83-93%); SVR12 was markedly lower in patients with baseline cirrhosis (63%, 20/32) and in patients with the NS5A Y93H baseline resistance polymorphism (54%, 7/13), non-overlapping CIs vs. the respective complementary subgroups
- Because the protocol specified no win criterion, FDA's statistical reviewer independently derived a range of non-inferiority margins (as low as -17%, without clinical input) by comparing to historical sofosbuvir+ribavirin 24-week standard-of-care data; the observed ~2% SVR12 difference (95% CI -4%, 9%) exceeded even this ad hoc bound

### 27. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide (Genvoya) — NDA 207561

**Sponsor:** Gilead Sciences, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Complete regimen for treatment of HIV-1 infection in adults and pediatric patients weighing ≥25 kg, without prior antiretroviral treatment failure

**Approval date:** November 5, 2015

**Pivotal trial:** GS-US-292-0104, NCT01780506; GS-US-292-0111, NCT01797445 (both treatment-naive, active-controlled vs. Stribild); GS-US-292-0109 (switch trial), NCT01815736

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, active-controlled, double-blind, double-dummy trials against the sponsor's own prior fixed-dose combination (Stribild) as the sole comparator; randomized, open-label switch trial in virologically suppressed patients (0109); PK/exposure-equivalence bridging rationale for the single new component (TAF vs. TDF) rather than a de novo efficacy trial for the whole regimen *(proposed extension of existing bridging-study keyword to a within-regimen single-component substitution)*
- *Endpoints:* FDA Snapshot-algorithm proportion with HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL at Week 48 (treatment-naive trials); proportion maintaining virologic suppression at Week 48 post-switch (0109)
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel-adjusted (stratified) confidence interval on treatment difference, non-inferiority margin 12%
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design, two interim analyses per Phase 3 trial with an extremely conservative nominal boundary (99.999% two-sided CI at interim vs. 95.002% at final analysis)
- *Missing data/bias:* FDA Snapshot algorithm classifies discontinuations/switches as failures (non-completer-equals-failure handling)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- The entire efficacy case for the new component, tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) 10 mg, rests on non-inferiority to tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) 300 mg within an otherwise identical fixed-dose combination (elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine), with Stribild (E/C/F/TDF) as the active comparator in every trial — not an independent, de novo efficacy demonstration for the full four-drug regimen
- GS-US-292-0104 and -0111: identically designed randomized, active-controlled, double-blind, double-dummy, multicenter trials in treatment-naive adults; each intended to randomize 840 subjects 1:1 to E/C/F/TAF vs. Stribild, stratified by screening viral load, CD4 count, and region; actual N=872 each; primary endpoint FDA Snapshot-algorithm HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL at Week 48
- GS-US-292-0109: open-label switch trial in virologically suppressed adults on Stribild, Atripla, or ritonavir/cobicistat-boosted atazanavir + Truvada, randomized 2:1 to switch to E/C/F/TAF or remain on current regimen (planned N=1500, actual randomized 1443)
- Non-inferiority margin 12% in both Phase 3 treatment-naive trials, assessed via Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel-adjusted 95%/99.999% CIs stratified by the randomization factors; two group-sequential interim analyses per trial (after 420 subjects reached Week 12, and after all subjects reached Week 24) using an extremely conservative nominal alpha at each interim look
- Results: non-inferiority of E/C/F/TAF to Stribild established in both treatment-naive Phase 3 trials (treatment difference 95% CI between roughly -5% and +10%) and in the switch trial (95% CI between -4% and +2%); CD4 count changes were comparable across regimens in all trials

### 28. Elbasvir/grazoprevir (Zepatier) — NDA 208261

**Sponsor:** Merck Sharp & Dohme Corp.

**Indication approved:** Chronic hepatitis C virus genotype 1 or genotype 4 infection

**Approval date:** January 28, 2016

**Pivotal trial:** C-EDGE TN (Trial 060), NCT02105467; C-EDGE TE (Trial 068), NCT02105701; C-EDGE CO-INFECTION (Trial 061), NCT02105662; C-SURFER (Trial 052), C-WORTHY (Trial 035)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized (C-EDGE TN, placebo-deferred-treatment design) and non-randomized/open-label (C-EDGE TE, CO-INFECTION) Phase 2/3 trials; historical-control non-inferiority/superiority threshold analysis (no concurrent active comparator, same general approach as the Viekira Pak review) **
- *Endpoints:* sustained virologic response at post-treatment week 12 (SVR12)
- *Primary analysis:* exact (Clopper-Pearson) binomial confidence interval on SVR12 proportion, compared to a pre-specified historical-control threshold; superiority to historical control was the design objective, not superiority/non-inferiority to a concurrent comparator
- *Missing data/bias:* SVR12 treatment-failure imputation for missing values
- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented key limitation — "none of the clinical trials were designed to assess compare SVR12 against a concurrent active control consisting of an approved HCV treatment," reflecting the absence of any approved IFN-sparing comparator at the time these trials were designed; reviewer also flagged the lack of post-treatment follow-up beyond week 12 in most trials as limiting long-term relapse/durability assessment

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Seven trials supported the NDA (Phase 2 Trial 048, Phase 2/3 C-SURFER Trial 052, Phase 3 C-EDGE TN Trial 060, C-EDGE CO-INFECTION Trial 061, C-EDGE TE Trial 068, plus earlier Phase 2 dose-finding studies 035 and 047); "the Phase 2/3 and 3 trials were designed to demonstrate that the SVR12 proportion in the GZR/EBR arm is superior to a pre-specified historical rate, which varies according to CHC sub-population and genotype"
- C-EDGE TN (Trial 060): Phase 3, randomized (drug now vs. placebo-then-drug deferred-treatment design), genotype 1/4/6 treatment-naive patients (with/without cirrhosis), GZR 100 mg/EBR 50 mg x 12 weeks, N=316 in the immediate-treatment group
- C-EDGE TE (Trial 068): Phase 3, non-randomized, genotype 1/4/6 patients who failed prior pegIFN/RBV, GZR/EBR ± ribavirin for 12 or 16 weeks
- C-EDGE CO-INFECTION (Trial 061): Phase 3, non-randomized, HIV/HCV genotype 1/4/6 co-infected patients, GZR/EBR x 12 weeks
- C-SURFER (Trial 052): Phase 2/3, randomized, chronic kidney disease (stage 4-5) patients with genotype 1 HCV; overall SVR12 94% (115/122)
- Across trials, SVR12 point estimates ranged 86-97% for the 12-week regimen; the historical-control superiority thresholds were pre-specified per genotype/treatment-history subpopulation (Appendix A of the statistical review) using the same general historical-borrowing logic as other DAA programs reviewed in the same period; exact (Clopper-Pearson) binomial CIs were used throughout given the absence of a concurrent randomized comparator in most trials

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §1, Reference ID 3839672]*

> "There are few key limitations in the reviewed NDA data with the first being that none of the clinical trials were designed to assess compare SVR12 against a concurrent active control consisting of an approved HCV treatment as a control. *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §1, Reference ID 3839672]*

> "The other key limitation to these data is the lack of post-treatment follow up after week 12 in all but two of the seven reviewed clinical trials. While it was agreed upon in advance that these data did not have to be submitted with the NDA (but would be required at a later time) there are limitations in being able to fully assess the sustainability of virologic response at week 24 and longer."

### 29. Obiltoxaximab (Anthim) — BLA 125509

**Sponsor:** Elusys Therapeutics, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of inhalational anthrax due to *Bacillus anthracis*, in combination with appropriate antibacterial drugs, and for prophylaxis of inhalational anthrax when alternative therapies are not available or are not appropriate

**Approval date:** March 18, 2016

**Pivotal trial:** No human efficacy trial — efficacy shown entirely in 22 randomized animal-efficacy studies in cynomolgus monkeys and New Zealand White rabbits under the FDA Animal Rule (21 CFR 314.600s); human data limited to 3 healthy-volunteer PK/safety studies (320 subjects total), no confirmed NCT numbers identified

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Animal Rule approval basis — efficacy demonstrated only in validated animal models, human trials limited to safety/PK **; randomized (and, in some studies, blinded) monkey/rabbit challenge studies across monotherapy treatment, post-exposure prophylaxis, and pre-exposure prophylaxis designs
- *Endpoints:* survival at Day 28 (or Day 56, in one pre-exposure study) after *B. anthracis* spore challenge
- *Primary analysis:* per-study comparison of survival proportions (Fisher's exact / logistic regression with covariates); cross-species meta-analysis of survival endpoint at the proposed human-equivalent dose (fixed-effect and random-effects risk-difference models) **
- *Multiplicity:* Bonferroni adjustment applied by the FDA reviewer to studies with multiple dose-arm comparisons, even where the sponsor's own analysis plan did not pre-specify a comparable adjustment
- *Missing data/bias:* GEE regression modeling to account for pre-treatment bacteremia/protective-antigen (PA) level as a prognostic covariate across studies of varying design
- *Regulatory:* Animal Rule (21 CFR 314.600 series) approval basis, analogous to raxibacumab; reviewer-documented failed monkey treatment study (AP203) with the to-be-marketed (Lonza) product, prompting a sponsor hypothesis (severity of illness at treatment) and an additional confirmatory monkey study (AP202) under a Special Protocol Assessment

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Because human efficacy trials in inhalational anthrax are neither ethical nor feasible, the entire efficacy case rests on 22 of 26 submitted animal-efficacy studies (the other 4 combined obiltoxaximab with antibacterial therapy or used mice), each a randomized challenge study in cynomolgus monkeys ("AP" studies) or New Zealand White rabbits ("AR" studies), some conducted by NIAID; primary endpoint in all studies was survival, typically at Day 28 post-challenge
- Study types: 5 monkey + 4 rabbit IV monotherapy treatment studies (treatment initiated after onset of clinical signs/symptoms); 3 monkey + 6 rabbit post-exposure prophylaxis studies (IV or IM, at varying times after challenge); 4 supportive pre-exposure prophylaxis and re-challenge studies
- The proposed to-be-marketed dose, 16 mg/kg IV, was shown effective in 2 monkey and 2 rabbit monotherapy treatment studies; a 16 mg/kg IM dose was effective in post-exposure prophylaxis studies when given within 24 hours, and in pre-exposure prophylaxis studies when given 30 minutes to 3 days before challenge — the IV route's prophylactic effectiveness was extrapolated from the IM prophylaxis data rather than separately demonstrated
- One monkey treatment study (AP203), using product from the sponsor's to-be-marketed (Lonza) manufacturing process, failed to show a significant treatment effect; the applicant hypothesized this reflected greater illness severity (bacteremia/PA levels) at the time of treatment rather than a product problem, and an additional confirmatory study (AP202) was conducted under a Special Protocol Assessment
- FDA's reviewer conducted exploratory fixed-effect and random-effects meta-analyses of survival risk differences at the 16 mg/kg IV dose across the monkey studies (risk difference 0.36-0.38, 95% CI excluding 0) and rabbit studies (risk difference 0.74-0.75), describing these as "merely exploratory" given small per-study sample sizes; safety and PK were characterized in 320 healthy human volunteers across 3 clinical studies (including a placebo-controlled single-dose study), with no efficacy claim derived from human data

**Documents**

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2016/125509lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (animal-efficacy studies, monotherapy) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/125509Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/125509Orig1s000SumR.pdf

- Pivotal publication (animal efficacy): Yamamoto BJ, Shadiack AM, Carpenter S, et al. "Obiltoxaximab Prevents Disseminated Bacillus anthracis Infection and Improves Survival during Pre- and Postexposure Prophylaxis in Animal Models of Inhalational Anthrax." *Antimicrob Agents Chemother.* 2016;60(10):5796-805. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1128/AAC.01102-16), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27431219/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Obiltoxaximab%20Prevents%20Disseminated%20Bacillus%20anthracis%20Infection%20Animal%20Models)

**Other resources**

- Not applicable — no human efficacy dataset exists to share via IPD platforms; animal-study data reside with FDA/sponsor per Animal Rule submission requirements.
- No public FDA Advisory Committee meeting identified for this BLA (consistent with other single-sponsor Animal Rule biodefense products).

> "The applicant submitted this BLA to seek the approval of a monoclonal antibody ETI-204 (Obiltoxaximab) for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients with inhalational anthrax due to Bacillus anthracis in combination with appropriate antibacterial drugs and for prophylaxis of inhalational anthrax when alternative therapies are not available or are not appropriate. Due to ethical reasons, the Animal Rule was used for the development of this product."

A 16 mg/kg IM dose given to monkeys and rabbits by 24 hours was effective... We can extrapolate that the IV dose would also be effective in the prophylaxis setting."

### 30. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir (Epclusa) — NDA 208341

**Sponsor:** Gilead Sciences, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Chronic hepatitis C virus infection, genotypes 1-6, including patients with compensated cirrhosis or (with ribavirin) decompensated cirrhosis — the first pangenotypic HCV regimen

**Approval date:** June 28, 2016

**Pivotal trial:** ASTRAL-1, NCT02201940; ASTRAL-2, NCT02220998; ASTRAL-3, NCT02201953; ASTRAL-4, NCT02201901

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (ASTRAL-1, placebo arm for comparative safety only); randomized, open-label, active-controlled vs. approved standard of care (ASTRAL-2, ASTRAL-3); randomized, open-label, three-arm regimen-comparison trial in decompensated cirrhosis, no active-controlled arm feasible (ASTRAL-4)
- *Endpoints:* sustained virologic response at post-treatment week 12 (SVR12)
- *Primary analysis:* stratum-adjusted Mantel-Haenszel proportion difference and Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test for superiority (ASTRAL-2/3, closed testing procedure: non-inferiority first, then superiority); comparison of SVR12 CI lower bound against a pre-specified performance threshold (ASTRAL-1, vs. 85%; ASTRAL-4, vs. an assumed 1% spontaneous-clearance rate)
- *Multiplicity:* closed testing procedure (non-inferiority null tested first; superiority p-value only calculated if non-inferiority null rejected) in ASTRAL-2 and ASTRAL-3
- *Missing data/bias:* SVR12 treatment-failure imputation for missing values
- *Regulatory:* Bayesian approach used by the sponsor (accepted by the reviewer) to justify the ASTRAL-2 non-inferiority margin, borrowing information across genotypes/regimens given limited direct historical data for 12-week sofosbuvir monotherapy in genotype 2 patients

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Four Phase 3 randomized, multicenter trials (ASTRAL-1 to 4) all used the same primary endpoint, SVR12, defined as HCV RNA below the lower limit of quantitation 12 weeks after end of treatment
- ASTRAL-1: randomized double-blind trial in genotype 1/2/4/6 patients (with/without compensated cirrhosis) to 12 weeks of SOF/VEL or placebo (placebo purely for comparative safety, since no placebo subject was expected to achieve SVR12); genotype 5 patients were assigned open-label SOF/VEL; SVR12 99% vs. a pre-specified 85% performance threshold
- ASTRAL-2: randomized, active-controlled trial in genotype 2 patients comparing 12 weeks of SOF/VEL to 12 weeks of sofosbuvir + ribavirin (standard of care); a closed testing procedure first assessed non-inferiority (stratum-adjusted Mantel-Haenszel CI, 10% margin, using a sponsor Bayesian justification for the margin that borrowed information across genotypes/regimens given sparse direct historical data), then superiority via Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test (SVR12 99% vs. 94%, p<0.05)
- ASTRAL-3: randomized, active-controlled trial in genotype 3 patients comparing 12 weeks of SOF/VEL to 24 weeks of sofosbuvir + ribavirin (approved standard of care); SVR12 95% vs. 80%, with pre-specified subgroup analyses (cirrhosis, treatment history) showing the largest relative benefit in cirrhotic and treatment-experienced genotype 3 patients (roughly 25-27 percentage points higher SVR12)
- ASTRAL-4: randomized, open-label trial in genotypes 1-6 with decompensated (Child-Pugh-Turcotte B/C) cirrhosis, comparing three regimens (12-week SOF/VEL, 12-week SOF/VEL+RBV, 24-week SOF/VEL) with no active-controlled arm feasible since no IFN-free DAA regimen was approved for this population; SVR12 94% (SOF/VEL+RBV), 83% (SOF/VEL 12 wk), 86% (SOF/VEL 24 wk) — all superior to an assumed spontaneous-clearance rate of 1%; pairwise regimen comparisons were not pre-specified, and the reviewer noted the apparent superiority of the 12-week SOF/VEL+RBV arm was driven largely by genotype 1/3 and CPT-class-B subjects given limited genotype 2/4/5/6 and CPT-class-A/C representation

### 31. Bezlotoxumab (Zinplava) — BLA 761046

**Sponsor:** Merck Sharp & Dohme Corp.

**Indication approved:** To reduce recurrence of Clostridium difficile infection (CDI) in patients 18 years of age or older who are receiving antibacterial drug treatment for CDI and are at high risk for CDI recurrence

**Approval date:** October 21, 2016

**Pivotal trial:** MODIFY I, NCT01241552, and MODIFY II, NCT01513239

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; 4-arm factorial design in MODIFY I with an interim-analysis-driven arm drop ("DMC-recommended dropping of a randomized monoclonal-antibody arm at interim analysis for low efficacy and safety") ; two co-sponsored Phase 3 trials run with intentionally divergent primary endpoints between trials after a documented sponsor-FDA disagreement
- *Endpoints:* CDI recurrence rate at 12 weeks post-clinical-cure ("CDI recurrence rate, conditional on initial clinical cure of the index episode"); global cure rate ("global cure rate (composite: clinical cure of index episode + no CDI recurrence)"); clinical cure of the initial CDI episode
- *Primary analysis:* Miettinen-Nurminen method (stratified by SOC therapy and hospitalization status)
- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (combined monoclonal antibody vs. placebo tested before individual monoclonal antibody vs. placebo comparisons); additional alpha adjustment in MODIFY I to account for the interim analysis and the second family of comparisons (individual vs. combined monoclonal antibody)
- *Missing data/bias:* sensitivity analyses imputing failure for subjects with missing CDI-recurrence status
- *Regulatory:* FDA Advisory Committee meeting held (Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee, June 9, 2016, 10-5-1 vote); "SPA-agreed primary endpoint retained by sponsor across a companion trial despite FDA's documented concern that the endpoint's underlying assumption (no drug effect on initial clinical cure) was contradicted by accruing results"

**Trial design & endpoints**

- MODIFY I (P001) and MODIFY II (P002) were Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trials of a single IV infusion of monoclonal antibodies to C. difficile toxin A (actoxumab, MK-3415) and/or toxin B (bezlotoxumab, MK-6072) added to standard-of-care (SOC) antibiotic therapy (oral metronidazole, vancomycin, or fidaxomicin) in adults with confirmed CDI
- P001 randomized 1:1:1:1 to actoxumab, bezlotoxumab, actoxumab+bezlotoxumab (MK-3415A), or placebo (1,452 randomized; FAS n=1,396); enrollment in the actoxumab arm was halted after an interim analysis when the Data Monitoring Committee found low efficacy and more deaths/serious adverse events versus placebo in that arm; P002 randomized 1:1:1 to bezlotoxumab, MK-3415A, or placebo (no actoxumab arm)
- Both trials stratified randomization by oral SOC therapy and hospitalization status (inpatient/outpatient)
- Primary efficacy endpoint (both trials, Full Analysis Set): proportion of subjects with CDI recurrence — a new episode of diarrhea with a positive toxigenic-C.-difficile stool test — during the 12-week (Day 85 ± 5) follow-up after clinical cure of the baseline episode; because only initial clinical cures are at risk of "recurrence," patients who never achieved clinical cure of the baseline episode are counted as recurrence non-events (i.e., successes) under the protocol definition
- Key secondary endpoint: global cure (clinical cure of the baseline episode AND no CDI recurrence), which FDA's review argued was the more clinically interpretable endpoint precisely because it does not treat initial-treatment failures as recurrence successes
- Sample size: P001 planned ~1,600 subjects (400/arm) for ~95% power to detect an ~9-10 percentage-point difference in CDI recurrence at one-sided α=0.0125; P002 planned ~1,200 subjects (400/arm) with the same power/alpha assumptions
- Type I error was controlled across two analysis time points (one interim, one final) and two comparison families (each monoclonal antibody vs. placebo; each individual monoclonal antibody vs. the combination) via a pre-specified sequential/graphical testing strategy, with final-analysis one-sided significance cutoffs of 0.0125 for MK-3415A vs. placebo and bezlotoxumab vs. placebo, and 0.0066 for MK-3415A vs. bezlotoxumab
- FDA's SPA process history: the Division wanted CDI recurrence in P001 assessed among all randomized subjects rather than just clinical cures, and in August 2012 asked the sponsor to change the P002 primary endpoint from CDI recurrence to global cure over concern about imbalances in initial clinical cure; the sponsor proposed (November 2012) to keep CDI recurrence in P002 with added sensitivity analyses, and by August 2013 FDA acknowledged the sponsor's intent to preserve the original endpoint despite the Division's repeated recommendation to switch

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2016/761046Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2016/761046s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/761046Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/761046Orig1s000SumR.pdf

- Pivotal publication: Wilcox MH, Gerding DN, Poxton IR, et al. "Bezlotoxumab for Prevention of Recurrent Clostridium difficile Infection." *N Engl J Med.* 2017;376(4):305-317. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1602615), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28121498/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Bezlotoxumab%20for%20Prevention%20of%20Recurrent%20Clostridium%20difficile%20Infection)

**Other resources**

- Merck's trial-specific IPD access via its clinical trial data-sharing portal was not individually confirmed here.
- FDA Advisory Committee meeting: Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee, June 9, 2016; the committee voted 10 (yes) - 5 (no) - 1 (abstain) that substantial evidence of safety and effectiveness had been shown, with several members expressing concern about bezlotoxumab's possible negative effect on initial clinical cure.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, BLA 761046, p.3-4]* > "The primary efficacy objective of both trials was to determine if treatment with a single infusion of actoxumab + bezlotoxumab with SOC therapy and the individual monoclonal antibody therapies (actoxumab and/or bezlotoxumab) decreases the proportion of subjects with CDI recurrence over a period of 12 weeks as compared to treatment with a single infusion of placebo with SOC therapy... The primary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of subjects in the Full Analysis Set (FAS) population with CDI recurrence during the 12-week (Day 85 ± 5 days) follow-up period after a clinical cure of the baseline CDI episode... It should be noted that clinical cure is a requirement for the assessment of CDI recurrence. Since the proportion of subjects with CDI recurrence is based on the FAS population by default subjects who were not initial clinical cures are treated as not having a recurrence i.e. successes."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, BLA 761046, p.8-9, SAP/SPA history]* > "Following review of the protocol for P002 in August 2012, the Division requested that the Applicant revise the primary efficacy endpoint in P002 to be global cure... rather than CDI recurrence... In November 2012, the Applicant proposed to retain CDI recurrence as the primary endpoint in P002 since this was the agreed upon endpoint for P001 but to conduct additional sensitivity analyses to assess the impact of clinical cure on the recurrence endpoint... Finally in August 2013, the Division acknowledged the Applicant's intent to preserve the efficacy endpoint definition and primary efficacy analysis in P002 despite its recommendations."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, BLA 761046, p.12-13, multiplicity]* > "Overall Type I error was controlled for multiple treatment comparisons at two analysis time points (one interim analysis and the final analysis)... For the comparisons of interest in the final analysis, the p-value cut-offs for declaring statistical significance are as follows: MK-3415A vs bezlotoxumab: 0.0066 (1-sided); MK-3415A vs placebo: 0.0125 (1-sided); bezlotoxumab vs placebo: 0.0125 (1-sided)."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, BLA 761046, p.51, Conclusions and Recommendations]* > "Based on the results of the Phase 3 trials, there is concern as to whether the efficacy of bezlotoxumab for the prevention of CDI recurrence has been adequately shown. While there appears to be a decrease in CDI recurrence with the use of bezlotoxumab, a negative effect of bezlotoxumab on clinical cure of the initial CDI episode cannot be ruled out. Therefore, the efficacy of bezlotoxumab is better assessed by global cure... Although CDI recurrence was the agreed upon primary endpoint in an SPA for P001, it was under the assumption that the monoclonal antibody would not have an effect on the initial clinical cure. However, the results for all three arms that contained a monoclonal antibody in P001 and the combined monoclonal antibody arm in P002 indicate that there may be a negative effect of the monoclonal antibody on clinical cure."

### 32. Delafloxacin (Baxdela) — NDA 208610/208611

**Sponsor:** Melinta Therapeutics, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI) in adults caused by susceptible Gram-positive and Gram-negative organisms

**Approval date:** June 19, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** Study 302 (RX-3341-302), NCT01811732, and Study 303 (RX-3341-303), NCT01984684

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled; non-inferiority design; Study 302 evaluated IV-only delafloxacin, Study 303 evaluated an IV-to-oral switch regimen; both trials reviewed under Special Protocol Agreements
- *Endpoints:* "Objective clinical response (≥20% reduction in lesion erythema area at 48-72 hours)" — the FDA-guidance-recommended early ABSSSI endpoint; investigator-assessed response (cure or success) at follow-up/late-follow-up visits as a key secondary endpoint
- *Primary analysis:* Miettinen-Nurminen method (unstratified, for the ITT population difference in response rates)
- *Multiplicity:* not applicable — single primary endpoint per study, no formal multiplicity adjustment needed for the non-inferiority conclusion
- *Missing data/bias:* non-completer/missing = failure imputation at the primary 48-72-hour assessment ("missing-outcome-at-primary-timepoint = failure imputation"); FDA reviewer flagged the clinically evaluable (CE) population as subject to post-randomization selection bias, noting CE-population response rates were "substantially higher" and "not overly informative" versus the ITT population
- *Regulatory:* two Special Protocol Agreements (SPA) governing trial design (February 2013 for Study 302, July 2015 for Study 303); no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 302 and Study 303 were prospective, 1:1 randomized, double-blind, multicenter, active-controlled (vancomycin plus aztreonam) trials of delafloxacin in adults with ABSSSI meeting the FDA ABSSSI Guidance's minimum lesion-size threshold (≥75 cm²); Study 302 tested delafloxacin 300 mg IV only (n=660 ITT: 331 delafloxacin, 329 control); Study 303 tested an IV-to-oral switch regimen (delafloxacin 300 mg IV for 6 doses then 450 mg oral) (n=850 ITT: 423 delafloxacin, 427 control)
- Primary objective (both trials, per the FDA ABSSSI Guidance and the SPA agreements): demonstrate non-inferiority of delafloxacin to vancomycin+aztreonam using a 10% margin on the primary endpoint of objective clinical response (≥20% reduction in lesion erythema area) at 48-72 hours; non-inferiority concluded if the lower bound of the 2-sided 95% CI for the response-rate difference (delafloxacin − control) exceeds −10%
- Enrollment limits per FDA guidance: no more than 30% of ITT patients could have major cutaneous abscess, and no more than 25% could have received prior antibacterial therapy for the ABSSSI episode
- Both studies met the primary non-inferiority objective: Study 302 treatment difference −2.6% (95% CI −8.8%, 3.6%); Study 303 treatment difference +3.1% (95% CI −2.0%, 8.3%)
- Missing primary-outcome data (patients without an evaluation in the 48-72-hour window) were counted as failures and were notably higher than typical (~7% in Study 302, ~5% in Study 303); sensitivity analyses of the missing-data handling were consistent with the primary analysis
- Key secondary endpoint (investigator-assessed cure/success at Day 14 follow-up and Day 21-28 late follow-up) was analyzed in both the ITT and clinically evaluable (CE) populations; FDA's reviewer specifically cautioned that CE-population analyses exclude patients based on post-randomization factors that could be treatment-related, inflating apparent response rates
- Supportive Phase 2 studies (RX-3341-201, RX-3341-202) were exploratory, without formal hypothesis testing, and were not relied upon for the efficacy conclusion

- Pivotal publication (Study 302): "Efficacy and safety of delafloxacin compared with vancomycin plus aztreonam for acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections: a Phase 3, double-blind, randomized study." *J Antimicrob Chemother.* 2017;72(12):3471-3480. **SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 208610/208611, p.4]* > "The primary objective of these studies is to demonstrate that delafloxacin is non-inferior to control using a margin of 10% and based on a primary endpoint of objective clinical response, i.e., reduction in lesion size of at least 20%, at 48 to 72 hours. This endpoint is consistent with FDA ABSSSI Guidance. For the primary analysis, a conclusion of noninferiority is made if the lower bound of the 2-sided 95% confidence interval (CI) for the difference in the objective clinical response rates (delafloxacin – control) exceeds -10%."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 208610/208611, p.5, missing data]* > "As shown in this table, the percentage of patients with missing primary outcome data, i.e. patients who did not have an efficacy evaluation within the first 3 days of study, appears somewhat high in both studies (approximately 7% in Study 302 and 5% in Study 303). Sensitivity analyses to assess the impact of missing data yields consistent findings with the primary analysis."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 208610/208611, p.5, on the CE population]* > "It should be noted that interpretation of findings from the clinically evaluable population is problematic because patients have been excluded based on post-randomization factors, which might be influenced by treatment... the resulting response rates from such analyses are substantially higher (at least 95% for each treatment arm) in this population than observed in the ITT population... Therefore, the response rates in the CE population could be artificially high and not overly informative."

### 33. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir/voxilaprevir (Vosevi) — NDA 209195

**Sponsor:** Gilead Sciences, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) genotype 1-6 infection in adults without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis who previously received an NS5A inhibitor-containing regimen, or genotype 1a or 3 infection who previously received sofosbuvir without an NS5A inhibitor

**Approval date:** July 18, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** POLARIS-1, NCT02607735, and POLARIS-4, NCT02639247

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (POLARIS-1); randomized, open-label, active-controlled (POLARIS-4, vs. sofosbuvir/velpatasvir); both enrolled DAA-treatment-experienced subjects, stratified by HCV genotype/cirrhosis status
- *Endpoints:* "Sustained virologic response at 12 weeks post-treatment (SVR12, HCV RNA < LLOQ)" — the standard chronic-HCV registration endpoint; secondary SVR4/SVR24, on-treatment virologic failure/relapse
- *Primary analysis:* One-sample z-test against a pre-specified performance goal (per-dose) (POLARIS-1: SVR12 vs. an 85% performance goal, two-sided exact one-sample binomial test with Clopper-Pearson 95% CI; POLARIS-4: two co-primary tests, SOF/VEL/VOX and SOF/VEL each vs. the same 85% goal)
- *Multiplicity:* Bonferroni adjustment (POLARIS-4's two primary efficacy tests each conducted at a 0.025 significance level)
- *Missing data/bias:* non-completer/missing = failure imputation (subjects without HCV RNA < LLOQ data at the Week-12-post-treatment visit counted as SVR12 non-responders); SVR12 responders with no further RNA data imputed as SVR24 successes given the high correlation between the two endpoints
- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held (NDA received Breakthrough Therapy designation; review team's preliminary benefit/risk assessment was not considered controversial)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- POLARIS-1 was a Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial in NS5A-inhibitor-experienced subjects (mostly HCV genotype 1, n=263 total in the SOF/VEL/VOX 12-week arm across GT1 and other genotypes, n=150 placebo comparator for the GT1 cohort); POLARIS-4 was a Phase 3, randomized, open-label, multicenter trial in non-NS5A-inhibitor DAA-experienced subjects (GT1, 2, or 3), randomizing 1:1 to SOF/VEL/VOX 12 weeks (n=163) or SOF/VEL 12 weeks (n=151), stratified by genotype and cirrhosis status
- Primary efficacy endpoint (both trials): proportion of subjects achieving SVR12 (HCV RNA below the lower limit of quantification 12 weeks after treatment cessation)
- POLARIS-1's primary hypothesis compared the SOF/VEL/VOX SVR12 rate to an 85% historical performance-goal threshold (not a concurrent-placebo hypothesis test, since placebo subjects were not expected to achieve any meaningful SVR12); POLARIS-4 had two co-primary tests (SOF/VEL/VOX and SOF/VEL, each vs. 85%), each tested at a Bonferroni-adjusted 0.025 two-sided significance level using the same exact-test/Clopper-Pearson-CI methodology
- Secondary endpoints: SVR4 and SVR24; on-treatment HCV RNA suppression by visit; log10 HCV RNA change from baseline; virologic failure/relapse classifications; baseline and treatment-emergent resistance-associated substitutions
- Results: POLARIS-1 SOF/VEL/VOX SVR12 = 97.8% (vs. 85% goal); POLARIS-4 SOF/VEL/VOX SVR12 = 97.4% and SOF/VEL SVR12 = 90.1% (both significantly above the 85% goal); reviewer noted the additional contribution of voxilaprevir was not obvious in some subgroups (NS5A-inhibitor-naive, NS5B-inhibitor-experienced GT1b/2/4/5/6), which the review team raised with the applicant during mid-cycle communication
- Missing-data handling: any subject without HCV RNA < LLOQ 12 weeks post-treatment was counted as a treatment failure (non-completer/missing = failure); visit windows were pre-specified as half the interval between consecutive scheduled visits

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/209195s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209195Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209195Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02607735 (POLARIS-1), https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02639247 (POLARIS-4) — no protocol/SAP documents posted for either trial
- Pivotal publication: Bourlière M, Gordon SC, Flamm SL, et al. "Sofosbuvir, Velpatasvir, and Voxilaprevir for Previously Treated HCV Infection." *N Engl J Med.* 2017;376(22):2134-2146. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1613512), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28564569/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Sofosbuvir%2C%20Velpatasvir%2C%20and%20Voxilaprevir%20for%20Previously%20Treated%20HCV%20Infection)

**Other resources**

- Gilead's trial-specific IPD access was not individually confirmed here.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held; the Summary Review states the NDA "was not presented at the Antimicrobial Drug Advisory Committee because SOF/VEL/VOX received breakthrough designation and the benefit/risk assessment did not appear controversial."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 209195, Table 2 and §3.2.1.1]* > "For POLARIS-1 and POLARIS-4, the primary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of subjects that achieved SVR12 defined as HCV RNA < LLOQ 12 weeks after cessation of study treatment."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 209195, §3.2.1.2, Efficacy Analysis]* > "In POLARIS-1, the SVR12 rate for the 12-week SOF/VEL/VOX regimen was compared to the 85% benchmark using a two-sided exact one-sample binomial test. The two-sided 95% exact confidence interval (CI) based on the Clopper-Pearson method was used to calculate the SVR12 rate. POLARIS-4 had two primary efficacy tests: the SVR12 rates for the 12-week SOF/VEL/VOX and 12-week SOF/VEL regimens were compared to the performance goal of 85% separately. To control the overall Type I error, each primary efficacy test was tested at the significance level of 0.025 using a Bonferroni adjustment."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 209195, §3.2.1.2, Handling Missing Data]* > "In the analysis of the primary efficacy endpoint, all subjects who did not have HCV RNA below LLOQ 12 weeks after the end of treatment were considered as not achieving SVR12... subjects categorized as successes for SVR12 who had no further HCV RNA measurements collected were counted as successes for SVR24 due to the potential high correlation between these 2 endpoints."

### 34. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir (Mavyret) — NDA 209394

**Sponsor:** AbbVie Inc.

**Indication approved:** Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) genotype 1-6 infection in adults without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis, including patients with severe renal impairment or on dialysis

**Approval date:** August 3, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** ENDURANCE-1, NCT02604017; ENDURANCE-3, NCT02640157; EXPEDITION-4, NCT02651194 (plus ENDURANCE-2 and supportive Phase 2 trials SURVEYOR-1/2, EXPEDITION-1, MAGELLAN-1, ENDURANCE-4)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (ENDURANCE-1, -2); randomized, open-label, active-controlled (ENDURANCE-3, vs. sofosbuvir/daclatasvir); single-arm, open-label trial (EXPEDITION-4, EXPEDITION-1, ENDURANCE-4); pangenotypic dose/duration-finding program feeding into a multi-trial pooled registration package
- *Endpoints:* "Sustained virologic response at 12 weeks post-treatment (SVR12)" — pangenotypic HCV registration endpoint
- *Primary analysis:* One-sample z-test against a pre-specified performance goal (per-dose) (ENDURANCE-1 vs. a 97% clinical threshold using a 6% "non-inferiority" margin that FDA's reviewer reinterpreted as a superiority test against a 91% threshold, absent a concurrent active control); descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (EXPEDITION-4, no testable hypothesis)
- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (ENDURANCE-1's three ranked endpoints: 12-week SVR12 vs. 91% threshold, then 8-week vs. 12-week non-inferiority in two populations)
- *Missing data/bias:* "Wilson score method substituted for normal-approximation CI at a 100% observed response rate"; FDA reviewer disputed the sponsor's exclusion of DAA/HCV-co-infected subjects from the primary ENDURANCE-1 analysis population and the sponsor's per-protocol-population-first testing order for the 8-week-vs-12-week comparison
- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held (Breakthrough Therapy designation; benefit/risk not considered controversial); reviewer-documented disagreement over whether ENDURANCE-3's non-randomized 8-week arm met its efficacy threshold ("reviewer reclassification of a trial's non-inferiority framing as a de facto single-arm superiority test due to absence of a concurrent comparator for that arm")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Registration rested on 4 Phase 3 trials (ENDURANCE-1, -2, -3, EXPEDITION-4; 974 HCV-infected adults, 759 on GLE/PIB 300 mg/120 mg) plus 5 supportive Phase 2 trials (SURVEYOR-1/2, EXPEDITION-1, MAGELLAN-1, ENDURANCE-4; 1,273 adults, 970 on the to-be-marketed dose); all nine trials shared the same primary efficacy endpoint of SVR12
- ENDURANCE-1 (GT1, non-cirrhotic, treatment-naive or PegIFN/ribavirin/sofosbuvir-experienced): 1:1 randomized 8-week vs. 12-week GLE/PIB, designed to demonstrate superiority against a pre-specified 91%/97% SVR12 clinical threshold; ENDURANCE-2 (GT2): double-blind, placebo-controlled 12-week GLE/PIB vs. threshold; ENDURANCE-3 (GT3, treatment-naive, non-cirrhotic): open-label 8- or 12-week GLE/PIB vs. sofosbuvir+daclatasvir active control, designed for non-inferiority; EXPEDITION-4: single-arm 12-week GLE/PIB in 104 GT1-6 subjects with severe renal impairment/ESRD (85 on dialysis), with no testable hypothesis
- Primary analysis population for ENDURANCE-1 was the sponsor-defined "ITT-Primary Subset" (mono-infected, DAA-naive, randomized, ≥1 dose); FDA's reviewer stated it was "unclear" why HIV/HCV-co-infected subjects were excluded and included them in its own reviewer-defined ITT-PS analysis
- ENDURANCE-1's 3 ranked primary/key-secondary endpoints (fixed-sequence): (1) 12-week SVR12 vs. 91% threshold (superiority, per FDA's reframing) in the ITT-PS, tested via a normal-approximation 95% CI (Wilson score method if SVR12=100%); (2) 8-week vs. 12-week non-inferiority (5% margin) in the per-protocol population; (3) 8-week vs. 12-week non-inferiority (5% margin) in the ITT-PS — FDA's reviewer specifically criticized testing the per-protocol comparison before the ITT-PS comparison as bias-prone given the per-protocol population's exclusionary criteria
- ENDURANCE-3's 12-week arm met non-inferiority to sofosbuvir+daclatasvir; its 8-week arm was non-randomized (a separate, later-enrolled cohort), so FDA's reviewer judged formal non-inferiority statistically inappropriate for that arm and instead compared it descriptively to the 92% clinical threshold — a comparison the review concluded the 8-week arm failed to clearly exceed
- Results: ENDURANCE-1 8-week SVR12 (95% CI) 99% (97,100) vs. 91% threshold; ENDURANCE-3 8-week and 12-week SVR12 95% (90,97) and 95% (92,97) respectively; EXPEDITION-4 SVR12 98.1% (93,99)
