- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2017/209394Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/209394s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209394Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209394Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02604017 (ENDURANCE-1), https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02640157 (ENDURANCE-3), https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02651194 (EXPEDITION-4) — no protocol/SAP documents posted
- Pivotal publication: Zeuzem S, Foster GR, Wang S, et al. "Glecaprevir-Pibrentasvir for 8 or 12 Weeks in HCV Genotype 1 or 3 Infection." *N Engl J Med.* 2018;378(4):354-369. *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 209394, §3.2.2, Statistical Methods, ENDURANCE-1]* > "ENDURANCE-1 was designed to compare the 12-week GLE/PIB regimen to a pre-specified SVR12 of 97% using a 6% margin, i.e. achieve a lower bound of the 95% CI around the 12-week GLE/PIB SVR12 of 91% of greater... Reviewer's Comment: The trial objective was to show NI of the 12-week regimen to a clinical threshold SVR12, however, in the absence of a concurrent active-control, findings based on non-inferiority hypothesis is not appropriate or interpretable. Therefore, the reviewer views the primary objective as one of superiority versus a clinical threshold SVR12 of 91%."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 209394, §3.2.2, on the primary analysis population]* > "ITT-Primary Subset (ITT-PS) includes the subset of mono-infected, HCV DAA-naïve, randomized subjects who received at least one dose of study drug. This is the primary efficacy analysis population. Reviewer's Comment: It is unclear as to why co-infected subjects were omitted from the primary analysis population. The reviewer's analysis will consider these subjects among the ITT-PS."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 209394, §3.2.2, on testing order]* > "The primary efficacy analyses included three ranked endpoints (tested using a fixed sequential approach): SVR12 of the 12 week regimen vs. a reference rate of 91%... 8 week versus 12 week SVR12 assessed via evaluating of the lower bound around the difference (test of NI, 5% margin) in the per-protocol ITT-PS and NI of the 8 week regimen to the 12-week regimen (5% margin) in the ITT-PS primary population. Reviewer's Comment: The applicant's testing strategy included testing for NI of the 8 week to 12 week regimens in the per-protocol population prior to testing NI in the primary efficacy ITT-PS population. The ITT-PP-PS population is subject to bias given the exclusionary nature of the population."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 209394, Executive Summary, on ENDURANCE-3's 8-week arm]* > "The 8-week arm was non-randomized and therefore comparisons of NI are statistically inappropriate. Instead, the regimen was compared against the pre-specified 92% clinical threshold and findings suggest that the arm failed to achieve superiority against this rate."

### 35. Meropenem/vaborbactam (Vabomere) — NDA 209776

**Sponsor:** The Medicines Company

**Indication approved:** Complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI), including pyelonephritis, in patients 18 years of age and older caused by susceptible microorganisms

**Approval date:** August 29, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** TANGO-1 (Study 505), NCT02166476

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled (vs. piperacillin-tazobactam); non-inferiority design with a pre-specified sequential test for superiority
- *Endpoints:* "Overall Response (composite: clinical cure/improvement + microbiological eradication) at end of IV therapy" — the FDA-cUTI-guidance primary endpoint
- *Primary analysis:* Miettinen-Nurminen method (two-sided 95% CI for the treatment-arm risk difference)
- *Multiplicity:* not applicable — single primary comparison, with a pre-specified non-inferiority-then-superiority sequential test (statistically valid without alpha adjustment)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Data Monitoring Committee (DMC/DSMB) — safety-only reviews (no interim efficacy looks) shared with the companion TANGO-2 (Study 506) trial
- *Missing data/bias:* non-completer/missing = failure imputation (dropouts and missing-outcome subjects counted as failures; an earlier-timepoint Clinical Outcome of failure carried forward to later visits)
- *Regulatory:* non-inferiority margin widened from 10% to 15% via a blinded SAP amendment during the trial ("in-study, still-blinded widening of a pre-specified non-inferiority margin"); no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- TANGO-1 (Study 505) was a Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, multicenter, active-controlled trial of meropenem/vaborbactam vs. piperacillin/tazobactam in adults with cUTI or acute pyelonephritis (AP), planned for 500 subjects (final N=550, sponsor over-enrolled ~10% "to be on the conservative side")
- Primary efficacy endpoint (End of IV therapy visit): "Overall Response," a composite requiring both clinical cure/improvement and microbiological eradication (or presumed eradication), analyzed in the microbiologically-modified-intent-to-treat (m-MITT) population, which FDA's reviewer noted was "protected from confounding by randomization" because m-MITT membership was defined by pre-randomization baseline cultures
- Non-inferiority margin was 15% on the risk-difference scale for the primary FDA analysis (widened from an original 10% margin via a single SAP amendment made while the study remained blinded); a companion set of EMA co-primary endpoints (microbiological eradication at test-of-cure) also used a 15% margin
- If non-inferiority was demonstrated, the pre-specified plan allowed a subsequent test for superiority using the same confidence interval — a form of sequential testing FDA's reviewer explicitly noted "is statistically appropriate and does not lead to Type I error rate inflation"; superiority was in fact demonstrated in the primary analysis
- FDA's guidance recommended co-primary analyses at both end-of-IV-therapy and ~7 days after all therapy for IV-only drugs; the sponsor instead used only the end-of-IV-therapy timepoint, reasoning that later timepoints would be complicated by oral step-down therapy and introduce a post-randomization-dependent assessment window
- Sample size: 500 subjects planned for 90% power under a 60% m-MITT-membership assumption and an assumed 80% overall success rate in both arms
- Secondary endpoints (not powered for non-inferiority): Overall Response at both end-of-IV-therapy and test-of-cure by infection type; microbiological eradication at test-of-cure using both FDA (<10^4 CFU/mL) and EMA (<10^3 CFU/mL) urine thresholds; clinical cure at multiple visits
- A shared DMC reviewed only safety data for TANGO-1 and its companion open-label CRE trial TANGO-2 (Study 506) at pre-specified combined-enrollment milestones (~25%, ~50%); no interim efficacy analyses were planned or conducted

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2018.0438), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29486041/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Effect%20of%20Meropenem-Vaborbactam%20vs%20Piperacillin-Tazobactam%20Complicated%20Urinary%20Tract%20Infection%20TANGO%20I)

The confidence interval was to be based on the Miettinen and Nurminen method... This was a noninferiority trial with a pre-specified margin of 15% on the risk difference scale... The statistical analysis plan stated that if noninferiority was demonstrated, superiority was to be examined using the confidence interval approach. This form of sequential testing is statistically appropriate and does not lead to Type I error rate inflation."

A Clinical Outcome of failure at an earlier time point was also carried forward to subsequent visits."

### 36. Benznidazole (unbranded) — NDA 209570

**Sponsor:** Chemo Research, S.L.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of Chagas disease (American trypanosomiasis) caused by Trypanosoma cruzi in pediatric patients 2 to 12 years of age

**Approval date:** August 29, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** De Andrade et al. (1996) and Sosa-Estani et al. (1998) pediatric trials — both predate ClinicalTrials.gov and have no NCT registration; supported by an adult long-term cardiac-outcomes study (Viotti et al. 2006) and two adult Phase 2 comparator trials (Molina and DNDi-CH-E1224-001)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Literature-based approval (no dedicated pivotal trial) — randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pediatric trials conducted independently of the applicant, decades before the NDA, plus a non-randomized adult long-term cardiac-outcomes cohort comparison
- *Endpoints:* "Seronegative conversion rate (proportion of subjects with negative anti-T. cruzi serology at extended follow-up)" — measured via multiple assay platforms (EIA/conventional ELISA, IHA, IFA, F29 chemiluminescent immunoassay) with materially different results by assay
- *Primary analysis:* Analysis of covariance (continuous log-titer change from baseline, adjusted for baseline); exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval-style two-sided exact CIs for between-arm differences in seronegative-conversion proportions
- *Multiplicity:* not applicable — FDA reviewer explicitly noted no control for Type I error was applied across the many serologic-assay/timepoint comparisons
- *Missing data/bias:* "Missing binary serology imputed as positive (non-responder) / missing continuous titer data excluded (complete-case)" — asymmetric imputation across the endpoint types
- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held; approval grounded in academic/literature evidence rather than a company-sponsored pivotal trial, per FDA's own statistical review of decades-old published trials

**Trial design & endpoints**

- The NDA's efficacy basis rested on five controlled clinical studies not conducted by the applicant: two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pediatric trials (de Andrade et al., 129 symptom-free children aged 7-12 with T. cruzi antibodies, benznidazole 7.5 mg/kg vs. placebo for 60 days; Sosa-Estani et al., 106 children aged 6-12, benznidazole 5 mg/kg vs. placebo) plus three adult studies (a long-term cardiac-outcomes comparison by Viotti et al., and two Phase 2 comparator trials, Molina and DNDi-CH-E1224-001, in which benznidazole served as the control arm for experimental antifungal-repurposed compounds)
- Primary endpoint in both pediatric trials (per FDA's statistical review, quoting the studies' stated statistical analysis plans): proportion of subjects with negative seroconversion against T. cruzi at extended follow-up (3 years in de Andrade, 4 years in Sosa-Estani) using conventional EIA/ELISA; both published papers instead emphasized results from the non-conventional F29 chemiluminescent assay, which showed larger, statistically significant treatment effects than the pre-specified conventional-assay endpoint
- Results: de Andrade — F29 seronegative-conversion 55% (benznidazole) vs. 5% (placebo), statistically significant; no significant difference by conventional ELISA. Sosa-Estani — F29 seronegative-conversion 60% (benznidazole) vs. 14% (placebo), statistically significant; no significant difference by conventional ELISA
- FDA's statistical reviewer explicitly noted that neither the protocol nor the publication for at least one trial reported a sample-size/power justification, and that no adjustment for multiple testing was applied across the several serologic assays and follow-up timepoints examined
- The supportive adult study (Viotti et al.) reported statistically significantly fewer benznidazole-treated patients with cardiac disease progression (4% vs. 14% untreated) or new ECG abnormalities (5% vs. 16%) over long-term follow-up, providing indirect clinical-benefit context for the surrogate serologic endpoint used in the pediatric trials
- Missing binary serology data were imputed as "positive" (i.e., treatment failure) for the efficacy analysis; missing continuous titer values were excluded from analysis (complete-case) rather than imputed
- FDA deferred to its microbiology review team on the acceptability of the serologic-assay cutoffs used across the pooled literature analysis

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/209570lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209570Orig1s000StatR.pdf

[DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/s0140-6736(96)04128-1>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8937280/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Randomised%20trial%20of%20efficacy%20of%20benznidazole%20in%20treatment%20of%20early%20Trypanosoma%20cruzi%20infection)

### 37. Secnidazole (Solosec) — NDA 209363

**Sponsor:** Symbiomix Therapeutics, LLC

**Indication approved:** Bacterial vaginosis (BV) in women and postmenarchal adolescent girls, as a single 2-gram oral dose

**Approval date:** September 15, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** SYM-1219-301, NCT02418845

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; 2:1 randomization to a single 2 g oral dose vs. placebo; stratified by BV-episode history and race
- *Endpoints:* "Clinical outcome responder (normal vaginal discharge + negative whiff test + clue cells <20%) at test-of-cure"; secondary Nugent-score normalization and "therapeutic outcome" (clinical response + normal Nugent score)
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test (stratified by BV-episode history and race), with the treatment-arm difference and 95% CI estimated via normal approximation to the binomial for the FDA reviewer's supplementary analysis
- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation for missing binary/diary efficacy data (missing clinical/therapeutic-outcome data imputed as non-responder; missing Nugent-score data imputed as abnormal; per protocol, no imputation applied to the Investigator's Clinical Assessment)
- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- SYM-1219-301 was a Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of a single oral 2 g dose of secnidazole (SYM-1219) vs. placebo in adult women and postmenarchal adolescent girls (≥12 years) with a clinical (Amsel-criteria) diagnosis of BV and a Gram-stain Nugent score ≥4 (confirmed post-randomization)
- Randomization (2:1, secnidazole:placebo) was stratified by number of BV episodes in the prior 12 months (≤3 vs. ≥4) and by race (Black vs. all others); treatment was self-administered on Day 1, with an interim visit Day 7-14 and a test-of-cure (TOC) visit Day 21-30
- Primary efficacy endpoint: clinical outcome responder at TOC, defined as normal vaginal discharge, negative 10% KOH whiff test, and clue cells <20%
- Secondary endpoints: clinical outcome at the interim visit; Nugent score (normal = 0-3) at interim and TOC; therapeutic outcome responder (clinical outcome responder AND normal Nugent score) at interim and TOC; investigator's clinical assessment of need for additional BV treatment at TOC
- Primary analysis: CMH chi-square test comparing responder rates between arms, adjusted for the randomization strata (BV-episode history, race); FDA's reviewer additionally computed the risk difference and a normal-approximation 95% CI
- Analysis populations: ITT (all randomized); modified ITT (mITT, Nugent score ≥4 at baseline and negative for other STIs) as the primary efficacy population; per-protocol (PP) as a supportive population; safety population (all randomized who received study drug)
- Sample size: 132 subjects planned assuming a 50% clinical-outcome-responder rate for secnidazole vs. 25% for placebo, 2-sided α=0.05, 80% power, 2:1 randomization
- Missing-data handling: missing clinical/therapeutic-outcome data were imputed as non-responder; missing Nugent-score data were imputed as abnormal; no imputation was applied to the Investigator's Clinical Assessment per protocol

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1097/AOG.0000000000002135), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28697102/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Secnidazole%20Treatment%20of%20Bacterial%20Vaginosis%20A%20Randomized%20Controlled%20Trial)

The primary efficacy endpoint was clinical outcome at TOC. A clinical outcome responder was defined as a patient with a normal vaginal discharge, a negative whiff test, and clue cells < 20%."

Thus, a total sample size of 132 subjects was [planned]."

### 38. Letermovir (Prevymis) — NDA 209939/209940

**Sponsor:** Merck Sharp & Dohme Corp.

**Indication approved:** Prophylaxis of cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection and disease in adult CMV-seropositive recipients [R+] of an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant

**Approval date:** November 8, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** P001 (MK-8228-001), NCT02137772

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; stratified by trial center and CMV-reactivation risk (high/low)
- *Endpoints:* "Clinically significant CMV infection (composite: CMV end-organ disease OR initiation of anti-CMV pre-emptive therapy based on documented viremia)" through Week 24 post-transplant; all-cause mortality through Week 24/48 as a secondary/exploratory time-to-event endpoint
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test (stratum-adjusted, with continuity correction, stratified by CMV-reactivation risk); stratified log-rank test and Kaplan-Meier estimation for the time-to-event presentation of the same endpoint and for mortality
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* periodic safety reviews and one interim futility analysis, with a small alpha penalty (0.0001) deducted from the final analysis "for statistical rigor" despite the sponsor's position that futility/safety looks do not inflate Type I error, yielding a final one-sided significance level of 0.0249 (vs. nominal 0.025)
- *Missing data/bias:* non-completer/missing = failure imputation ("Non-Completer = Failure primary missing-data approach") — subjects with clinically significant CMV infection, premature discontinuation, or missing Week-24 outcome all counted as failures
- *Regulatory:* "sponsor data-quality/programming-error correction changing a statistically significant secondary result to non-significant" — a SAS `proc lifetest` treatment-group/stratification-variable mislabeling inflated the apparent mortality p-values (reported as significant at 0.019/0.018 for interim/final Week 48 analyses when the corrected values were non-significant at 0.10/0.12); reviewer-documented incomplete post-study mortality ascertainment for discontinued subjects

**Trial design & endpoints**

- P001 was a Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (2:1 randomization, 360 letermovir : 180 placebo) in adult, CMV-seropositive [R+] allogeneic HSCT recipients with no detectable CMV DNA on Day 1 (when study medication started); randomization was stratified by trial center and by CMV-reactivation risk (high risk defined by HLA-mismatch/haploidentical/cord-blood donor source, ex vivo T-cell depletion, or Grade ≥2 GVHD requiring systemic corticosteroids)
- Primary efficacy endpoint: proportion of subjects with "clinically significant CMV infection" through Week 24 post-transplant, a composite of CMV end-organ disease OR initiation of anti-CMV pre-emptive therapy (PET) based on documented viremia and clinical judgment
- Primary analysis: stratum-adjusted Mantel-Haenszel test with continuity correction (risk stratum as the adjustment factor); non-completer = failure was the primary missing-data approach (any subject with clinically significant CMV infection, premature study-drug discontinuation, or a missing Week-24 outcome was counted as a failure)
- Sample size: ~540 subjects (2:1 randomization) for ≥90% power to detect a treatment difference at 1-sided p≤0.0249, assuming a 35% placebo incidence inflated to 55% and a 17%-reduced letermovir incidence inflated to 37% to account for an anticipated 20% non-completion rate under the Non-Completer=Failure approach
- Alpha accounting: two IDMC interim looks (Week 12, Week 24) each "spent" 0.0001 of alpha, reducing the two-sided final-analysis significance level from 0.05 to 0.04998 (a one-sided cutoff of 0.0249 rather than 0.025) — the sponsor stated no formal alpha-spending function was applied because futility/safety monitoring alone does not inflate Type I error, but a small allocation was nonetheless deducted "for statistical rigor"
- Kaplan-Meier curves and a stratified log-rank test were used for the time-to-event presentation of clinically significant CMV infection; although the protocol pre-specified no formal statistical test for the exploratory all-cause-mortality analyses, the sponsor also applied a log-rank test to those data
- Data-integrity issues surfaced during review: (1) a SAS `proc lifetest` programming error swapped the treatment-group and risk-stratification variables, producing statistically significant mortality p-values (0.019 interim, 0.018 final Week 48) that FDA determined should have been non-significant (0.10, 0.12) once corrected; (2) the sponsor initially counted only deaths occurring while a patient remained enrolled, leaving 76 of 87 discontinued patients with unknown post-study vital status at the time the Week 24 CSR was finalized — vital-status follow-up for 58 of those 76 was not completed and submitted until several months later, following repeated FDA information requests

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2017/209939Orig1s000,209940Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/209939Orig1s000,209940Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209939Orig1s000,209940Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02137772 — no protocol/SAP documents posted
- Pivotal publication: Marty FM, Ljungman P, Chemaly RF, et al. "Letermovir Prophylaxis for Cytomegalovirus in Hematopoietic-Cell Transplantation." *N Engl J Med.* 2017;377(25):2433-2444. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1706640), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29211658/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Letermovir%20Prophylaxis%20for%20Cytomegalovirus%20in%20Hematopoietic-Cell%20Transplantation)

**Other resources**

- Merck's trial-specific IPD access via its clinical trial data-sharing portal was not individually confirmed here.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was identified in the reviewed documents for this application.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 209939/209940, §3.2.2, Statistical Methodologies]* > "To test the primary hypothesis that letermovir was superior to placebo in the prevention of clinically significant CMV infection, the stratum-adjusted Mantel-Haenszel method (with continuity correction) was used to compare the two treatment groups with respect to the proportion of subjects with clinically significant CMV infection through Week 24 (~6 months) post-transplant... Letermovir was to be considered superior to placebo if the one-sided p-value was less than or equal to 0.0249."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 209939/209940, §3.2.2, on alpha spending]* > "The applicant stated that since stopping for futility and periodic safety checks do not inflate type I error rate, no alpha spending was planned for these analyses and that there was no intention for stopping for overwhelming efficacy at the time of the interim. However Merck stated that they allocated a small amount of alpha (0.0001) for statistical rigor and consequently used a one-sided statistical significance level of 0.0249 at the end of the trial instead of 0.025 for declaring statistical significance for the primary endpoint."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 209939/209940, §3.1, on the programming error]* > "Merck resubmitted the mortality analyses due to a SAS programming error discovered with proc lifetest where the treatment group and high vs. low risk stratification variables were switched. The error resulted in p-values being reported for a comparison between high vs. low risk randomization strata rather than for the comparison between letermovir vs. placebo treatment groups. Instead of a statistically significant two-sided p-value of 0.019 they should have obtained a non-significant p-value of 0.10 for the interim Week 48 analysis at the time of database lock."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 209939/209940, §3.1, on mortality ascertainment]* > "Merck stated that they did not proactively follow up patients who discontinued from the trial in order to determine their mortality status. Instead, Merck stated that they only counted deaths while patients were still enrolled in the trial... The applicant stated on page 9 of the Week 48 Mortality Statistical Report that 'post-study deaths are not included in the mortality analysis, as the reporting of information after a subject had completed the clinical trial was not required.'"

### 39. Ozenoxacin (Xepi) — NDA 208945

**Sponsor:** Ferrer Internacional, S.A.

**Indication approved:** Topical treatment of impetigo (due to Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes) in patients 2 months of age and older

**Approval date:** December 11, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** Trial 880, NCT01397461, and Trial 881, NCT02090764

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; Trial 880 additionally included a retapamulin arm as an internal-validity comparator ("active-comparator arm included solely for internal assay sensitivity, not for a formal ozenoxacin-vs-active-comparator hypothesis test")
- *Endpoints:* "Clinical response (success/cure via a Skin Infection Rating Scale [SIRS] composite) at end of therapy" — a multi-component sign/symptom severity-score-based responder definition, modified slightly between the two trials
- *Primary analysis:* chi-square test (without continuity correction), Wald (asymptotic normal-approximation) 95% CI for the ozenoxacin-vs-placebo difference in success rates
- *Missing data/bias:* non-completer/missing = failure imputation (FDA reviewer's primary analysis counted all ITTC/ITTB patients with missing/indeterminate outcomes as failures, departing from the sponsor's primary analysis, which excluded such patients — a completers-only approach the reviewer found "slightly more conservative" only because placebo had more missingness); reviewer sensitivity analyses also included an observed-cases-only replication of the sponsor approach and a worst-case scenario (failure for ozenoxacin, success for placebo)
- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Trial 880 and Trial 881 were randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter Phase 3 trials of ozenoxacin 1% cream (applied twice daily) in pediatric, adolescent, and adult patients with impetigo; Trial 880 additionally randomized a retapamulin 1% ointment arm to assess internal trial validity (not for a formal comparative claim); Trial 881's modified SIRS scoring (dropping tissue warmth/edema, adding blistering, combining itching/pain into one item) was implemented to align with a June 2010 FDA draft guidance update on evaluating topical antibiotics for impetigo using a modified SIRS
- Primary efficacy endpoint (both trials): clinical response (success/cure) at the end-of-therapy visit (Day 6-7) in the intent-to-treat-clinical (ITTC) population, with success requiring a composite SIRS score of 0 across the evaluated signs/symptoms (exudate/pus, crusting, erythema, etc., per trial-specific SIRS version)
- Secondary endpoints: clinical response at earlier/later visits in ITTC, per-protocol-clinical (PPC), intent-to-treat-bacteriological (ITTB), and per-protocol-bacteriological (PPB) populations; SIRS-score change from baseline; affected-area size ratio to baseline; microbiological response and combined clinical+microbiological ("therapeutic") response in ITTB/PPB; time to clinical response; time to bacterial eradication
- Sponsor's primary analysis: chi-square test (without continuity correction) with an asymptotic Wald 95% CI for the ozenoxacin-vs-placebo difference in success rates at end-of-therapy, in the ITTC population, excluding patients with missing outcome data
- FDA's reviewer disagreed with excluding missing-data patients from the primary analysis (noting the placebo arm tended to have more missingness, making the sponsor's approach "slightly more conservative" only incidentally) and instead ran its own primary analysis treating all ITTC/ITTB patients with missing or indeterminate outcomes as failures, consistent with the intent-to-treat principle, alongside observed-cases-only and worst-case sensitivity analyses
- Sample size: Trial 880 planned 465 patients (155/arm, ozenoxacin/placebo) for 90% power to detect a 20-percentage-point difference at a 5% 2-sided significance level, with age-based enrollment quotas (≥258 patients aged 2 to <12, ≥24 aged 12 to <18); Trial 881 planned 412 patients (206/arm) for 90% power to detect a 15-percentage-point difference, with quotas (≥226 aged 2 months to <12 years, ≥20 aged 12 to <18)
- Results (reviewer's primary analysis, Trial 880): success rates 34.8% (ozenoxacin) vs. 19.2% (placebo) at end-of-therapy, a statistically significant difference

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2017/208945Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/208945lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/208945Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/208945Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01397461 (Trial 880), https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02090764 (Trial 881) — no protocol/SAP documents posted
- Pivotal publication (Trial 880): Gropper S, Albareda N, Chelius K, et al. "Ozenoxacin 1% cream in the treatment of impetigo: a multicenter, randomized, placebo- and retapamulin-controlled clinical trial." *Future Microbiol.* 2014;9(9):1013-1023. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.2217/fmb.14.78), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25340832/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Ozenoxacin%201%25%20cream%20in%20the%20treatment%20of%20impetigo%20multicenter%20randomized%20placebo%20retapamulin%20controlled)

**Other resources**

- Ferrer's trial-specific IPD access was not individually confirmed here; Trial 881's individual results are documented primarily in the FDA review and label rather than in a dedicated peer-reviewed publication identified here.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held; the Summary Review states the NDA "was not discussed at an advisory committee meeting as there were no specific questions/issues that needed input from the committee."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 208945, Endpoints]* > "Primary efficacy endpoint: Clinical response (success (cure) or failure) at end of therapy (Visit 3, Day 6-7) in the ITTC population."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 208945, §3.2.3.1, Statistical Methodologies (Applicant)]* > "In Trials 880 and 881, the primary analysis involved testing the superiority of ozenoxacin versus placebo with respect to clinical response (clinical success or clinical failure) at the end of therapy visit (Visit 3) in the ITTC population... the Applicant used a chi-square test (without continuity correction) with corresponding 95% asymptotic (Wald) confidence interval (CI) to evaluate the difference in success rates."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 208945, §3.2.3.1, reviewer comment on missing data]* > "Reviewer Comments: The Applicant's primary and secondary analyses conducted in the ITTC (and ITTB) populations excluded patients with missing data in the ITTC population. This resulted in slightly more conservative findings since the placebo arm tended to have more missing data. However, Reviewer analyses, as noted below, included all ITTC (and ITTB) patients in the analysis and considered patients with missing data as failures."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 208945, §3.2.3.2, Statistical Methodologies (Reviewer)]* > "The Reviewer used statistical methodologies which were similar to those proposed by the Applicant. However, the Reviewer primary analyses considered all patients with missing/indeterminate outcomes as failures. The Reviewer considers this to be a preferable approach since it adheres it the intent-to-treat principle."

### 40. Bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide (Biktarvy) — NDA 210251

**Sponsor:** Gilead Sciences, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Complete regimen for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in adults with no prior antiretroviral treatment history or to replace the current antiretroviral regimen in virologically-suppressed adults

**Approval date:** February 7, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** Study 1489 (GS-US-380-1489), NCT02607930, and Study 1490 (GS-US-380-1490), NCT02607956

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled; non-inferiority design; Study 1489 vs. abacavir/dolutegravir/lamivudine (double-blind, double-dummy), Study 1490 vs. dolutegravir + emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide, in antiretroviral-treatment-naive adults
- *Endpoints:* "US FDA-defined snapshot algorithm responder (HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL at Week 48)" — the standard modern HIV-1 registration endpoint
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test (stratum-adjusted Mantel-Haenszel proportion difference and CI, stratified by baseline HIV-1 RNA level and region; Breslow-Day test for homogeneity of odds ratios across regions)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Data Monitoring Committee (DMC/DSMB) — Independent Data Monitoring Committee (IDMC) reviews at Weeks 12 and 24, each formally "charged" a small alpha penalty (0.00001 per look) against the final analysis despite no pre-specified intent to stop early for efficacy, producing a final two-sided significance level of 0.04998 (95.002% CI) rather than the nominal 0.05
- *Missing data/bias:* non-completer/missing = failure imputation (US FDA snapshot algorithm's default handling of missing on-treatment RNA data and non-efficacy discontinuations)
- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held ("there are previously approved drugs in this ARV class, available safety data did not reveal issues that were unexpected for the class")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 1489 and Study 1490 were near-identically designed Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, non-inferiority trials (each 1:1, 300 subjects/arm) in HIV-1-infected, antiretroviral-treatment-naive adults; Study 1489 compared bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide (B/F/TAF) to abacavir/dolutegravir/lamivudine (ABC/DTG/3TC) using a double-blind, double-dummy design; Study 1490 compared B/F/TAF to dolutegravir + emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide (DTG+F/TAF)
- Randomization in both trials was stratified by baseline HIV-1 RNA (≤100,000; >100,000-≤400,000; >400,000 copies/mL), baseline CD4+ count (<50; 50-199; ≥200 cells/µL), and region (US vs. ex-US)
- Primary efficacy endpoint (both trials): proportion of subjects with HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL at Week 48, per the US FDA-defined snapshot algorithm; pre-specified null hypothesis: the B/F/TAF response rate is at least 12 percentage points lower than the active-control response rate (a 12% non-inferiority margin, considered clinically acceptable per FDA guidance for treatment-naive HIV-1 trials)
- Sample size: ~600 subjects total (300/arm) per trial for ≥95% power to rule out a 12% margin, assuming a 91% response rate in both arms (based on Gilead's Genvoya development program) at a one-sided 0.025 significance level
- Alpha accounting: two Independent Data Monitoring Committee (IDMC) interim looks (Weeks 12 and 24) each "spent" an alpha of 0.00001, even though the sponsor's SAP states it "does not have a prior intent to ask the IDMC to review Week 48 results or to consider early termination... even if there is early evidence of favorable efficacy" — reducing the two-sided final significance level from 0.05 to 0.04998 (a 95.002% CI, the source of the unusual CI width seen throughout the FDA review's result tables)
- Primary analysis: stratum-adjusted Mantel-Haenszel (MH) proportion difference (harmonic-mean-weighted across the 4 baseline-HIV-RNA-by-region strata) and 95.002% CI on the Full Analysis Set (FAS); non-inferiority concluded if the lower bound of the CI for (B/F/TAF − active control) exceeds −12%; the CMH-derived odds ratio and a Breslow-Day homogeneity test across regions were reported as supportive analyses
- Results: Study 1489 FAS response 92.4% (B/F/TAF) vs. 93.0% (ABC/DTG/3TC), difference −0.6% (95.002% CI −4.8%, 3.6%), non-inferiority met; Study 1490 FAS response 89.4% (B/F/TAF) vs. 92.9% (DTG+F/TAF), difference −3.5% (95.002% CI −7.9%, 1.0%), non-inferiority met
- FDA's review also drew on two supportive switch/co-infection trials (Study 1844, vs. ABC/DTG/3TC in virologically-suppressed switch patients; Study 1878, vs. boosted-PI-based regimens), each using a similar snapshot-algorithm design with a modified primary endpoint of virologic failure (HIV-1 RNA ≥50 copies/mL) tested against a 4% non-inferiority margin

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2018/210251Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/210251s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/210251Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02607930 (Study 1489), https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02607956 (Study 1490)
- Protocol / SAP (posted, Study 1489) — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/30/NCT02607930/SAP_007.pdf (Statistical Analysis Plan, Week 48 Interim Analysis, Version 1.0, dated May 10, 2017)
- Pivotal publication (Study 1489): Gallant J, Lazzarin A, Mills A, et al. "Bictegravir, emtricitabine, and tenofovir alafenamide versus dolutegravir, abacavir, and lamivudine for initial treatment of HIV-1 infection (GS-US-380-1489): a double-blind, multicentre, phase 3, randomised controlled non-inferiority trial." *Lancet.* 2017;390(10107):2063-2072. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(17)32299-7>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28867497/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Bictegravir%20emtricitabine%20and%20tenofovir%20alafenamide%20versus%20dolutegravir%20abacavir%20and%20lamivudine%20GS-US-380-1489)
- Pivotal publication (Study 1490): Sax PE, Pozniak A, Montes ML, et al. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(17)32340-1>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28867499/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Coformulated%20bictegravir%20emtricitabine%20and%20tenofovir%20alafenamide%20versus%20dolutegravir%20GS-US-380-1490)

**Other resources**

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held; the Multi-Discipline Review states one "was not held for this NDA because there are previously approved drugs in this ARV class, available safety data did not reveal issues that were unexpected for the class, and efficacy results from phase 3 trials did not pose specific concerns."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, Study 1489 Statistical Analysis Plan (Week 48 Interim Analysis, Version 1.0, 10 May 2017), §6.1.1]* > "The primary efficacy endpoint is the proportion of subjects with HIV-1 RNA < 50 copies/mL at Week 48 as determined by the US FDA-defined snapshot algorithm."

*[verbatim, Study 1489 SAP, §6.1.3, Statistical Hypothesis for the Primary Efficacy Endpoint]* > "Null hypothesis: The B/F/TAF group (Treatment Group 1) is at least 12% lower than the ABC/DTG/3TC group (Treatment Group 2) with respect to the proportion of subjects with HIV-1 RNA < 50 copies/mL ('response rate', as determined by the US FDA-defined snapshot algorithm) at Week 48. Alternative hypothesis: The B/F/TAF group (Treatment Group 1) is less than 12% lower than the ABC/DTG/3TC group (Treatment Group 2)..."

*[verbatim, Study 1489 SAP, §6.1.4, Primary Analysis of the Primary Efficacy Endpoint]* > "For each interim analyses performed for the IDMC at Weeks 12 and 24, an alpha of 0.00001 has been spent. Therefore, the significance level for the 2-sided test in the primary analysis at Week 48 will be 0.04998 (corresponding to 95.002% CI). It will be concluded that B/F/TAF is noninferior to ABC/DTG/3TC if the lower bound of the 2-sided 95.002% CI of the difference (B/F/TAF group − ABC/DTG/3TC group) in the response rate is greater than -12%. The primary analysis will use the FAS."

*[verbatim, Study 1489 SAP, §2.1, Data Monitoring Committee Analyses]* > "The Week 12 Independent Data Monitoring Committee (IDMC) analysis was conducted after approximately the first 50% of subjects enrolled completed their Week 12 visit or prematurely discontinued the study drug. The Week 24 IDMC analysis was conducted after all subjects enrolled completed their Week 24 visit or prematurely discontinued the study drug... Gilead does not have a prior intent to ask the IDMC to review Week 48 results or to consider early termination of the study even if there is early evidence of favorable efficacy for B/F/TAF."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 210251, §Results for the Primary Endpoint]* > "The percentages of subjects in the FAS with HIV-1 RNA < 50 copies/mL at Week 48 were 92.4% in the B/F/TAF group and 93.0% in the ABC/DTG/3TC with a difference in percentages of −0.6%, 95.002% CI: (−4.8% to 3.6%). The non-inferiority of B/F/TAF to ABC/DTG/3TC was demonstrated since the lower bound of the 95.002% CI of the difference between treatment groups was greater than the prespecified −12% margin."

### 41. Ibalizumab-uiyk (Trogarzo) — BLA 761065

**Sponsor:** TaiMed Biologics Inc. (marketed in the US by Theratechnologies Inc.)

**Indication approved:** In combination with other antiretroviral(s), for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in heavily treatment-experienced adults with multidrug-resistant HIV-1 infection failing their current antiretroviral regimen.

**Approval date:** 2018-03-06

**Pivotal trial:** TMB-301, NCT02475629

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label trial
- *Endpoints:* Virologic response (proportion achieving a ≥0.5 log10 decrease in HIV-1 RNA)
- *Primary analysis:* McNemar's test (paired within-subject comparison of control-period vs. monotherapy-period response)
- *Missing data/bias:* Non-responder imputation for missing binary/diary efficacy data (applicant's "missing equals failure," MEF, approach)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- TMB-301 was a single-arm, multicenter, 24-week trial in 40 heavily treatment-experienced adults with multidrug-resistant HIV-1 who had documented resistance to (or intolerance of) drugs from at least 3 of the 4 main antiretroviral classes and had ≤2 fully active agents remaining — a population for whom a randomized comparator arm was not considered feasible or ethical
- Three-phase design: (1) a 7-day "control period" (Days 0-6) on the patient's existing (failing) background regimen with no ibalizumab, used to characterize the natural trajectory of each patient's own viral load; (2) a 2000 mg loading dose of ibalizumab added on Day 7 to the still-failing background regimen (an effectively "monotherapy" period, since the background regimen was not yet optimized), with viral load reassessed on Day 14; (3) background regimen then optimized to include ≥1 antiretroviral the patient's virus was still susceptible to, plus ibalizumab 800 mg IV every 2 weeks through Week 25
- Primary efficacy endpoint: proportion of subjects achieving a ≥0.5 log10 decrease in HIV-1 RNA from Day 7 (post-loading-dose) to Day 14, compared against the proportion achieving the same decrease from Day 0 to Day 7 (i.e., the within-patient comparison of the ibalizumab-attributable change against each patient's own untreated control-period trajectory) — analyzed as a paired binary outcome via McNemar's test
- Secondary endpoints: proportion with HIV-1 RNA <50 and <400 copies/mL at Week 25, proportion with ≥0.5 and ≥1 log10 decreases in HIV-1 RNA from Day 7 baseline at Week 25, and change in CD4+ T-cell count
- Missing virologic data at Day 14 or Week 25 were classified as failures for all dichotomous efficacy endpoints (MEF); missing CD4 counts were imputed by last-observation-carried-forward (LOCF) as the primary approach, with the FDA statistical reviewer independently re-running a multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis
- Given n=40 and a single arm, pre-specified subgroup analyses (age, sex, race, region) were explicitly flagged by the FDA reviewer as underpowered and not meaningfully interpretable

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2018/761065Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/761065lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/761065Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (TMB-301) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02475629
- No sponsor SAP/protocol is posted on ClinicalTrials.gov for TMB-301 (no documentSection entries as of this review)
- Pivotal publication: Emu B, Fessel J, Schrader S, et al. "Phase 3 Study of Ibalizumab for Multidrug-Resistant HIV-1." *N Engl J Med.* 2018;379(7):645-654. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1711460), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30110589/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Phase%203%20Study%20of%20Ibalizumab%20for%20Multidrug-Resistant%20HIV-1)

**Other resources**

- No trial-specific IPD/dataset access (Vivli, YODA) was individually confirmed for TMB-301.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting is recorded for this application; ibalizumab received Breakthrough Therapy and Priority Review designations reflecting the small, hard-to-treat, high-unmet-need population.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Reference ID 4162418, §3.2.1.4]*

> "Table 7 summarizes the applicant's results for the primary efficacy endpoint. Thirty-three subjects (82.5% with 95% CI of [67.2%, 92.7%]) achieved a ≥ 0.5 log10 decrease from Day 7 to Day 14. By contrast, only one subject (2.5% with 95% CI of [0.06%, 13.2%]) achieved a ≥ 0.5 log10 decrease from Day 0 to Day 7. However, this subject violated the protocol by taking an OBR at the end of the control period on Day 6. The percentage of subjects achieving a ≥ 0.5 log10 decrease from Day 7 to Day 14 was significantly higher than the percentage of subject achieving a ≥ 0.5 log10 decrease from Day 0 to Day 7 (p<0.0001 based on McNemar's test). The reviewer agrees with the applicant's results."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.1.3/D, missing-data handling]*

> "The applicant applied the 'missing equals failure' (MEF) approach as the primary method in the... Patients with missing efficacy data at Day 14 or Week 25 (EOS) had this result set to failure for all dichotomous efficacy variables. If a viral load measurement was missing at any visit, the value was replaced with the measurements of <0.5 log10 decline from the baseline viral load beginning at Day 14."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §4.1, subgroup-analysis limitation]*

> "The pre-specified subgroup analyses for primary efficacy endpoint included age (< 50 vs. ≥ 50 years), gender (female vs. male), race (white, Asian, vs other) and region (Taiwan vs. US)... In the reviewer's opinion, a small sample size in the study and high percentage of subjects achieving a ≥ 0.5 log10 decrease in HIV RNA from Day 7 to Day 14 precluded meaningful interpretation of the results of the subgroup analyses."

The review's front-matter keywords line lists the methods actually used: *"single-arm, McNemar's test, Fisher's exact test, Wald Chi-Square test..."* — confirming this submission's statistical toolkit was built around small-sample, within-subject and exact methods rather than a between-arm comparative framework, consistent with a 40-patient single-arm trial in a population with essentially no viable randomized comparator.

### 42. Moxidectin (unbranded) — NDA 210867

**Sponsor:** Medicines Development for Global Health (MDGH)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of onchocerciasis (river blindness) due to *Onchocerca volvulus* in patients aged 12 years and older.

**Approval date:** 2018-06-13

**Pivotal trial:** Protocol ONCBL60801, NCT00790998

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled
- *Endpoints:* Parasite density reduction (skin microfilariae density)
- *Primary analysis:* Hierarchical/multilevel linear model with site-level random intercepts on log-transformed density ratio
- *Missing data/bias:* Arm-differentiated missing-data imputation (baseline value carried forward for moxidectin non-responders vs. most-recent-observation carried forward for ivermectin)
- *Regulatory:* FDA statistical reviewer critique of the applicant's primary model specification as inappropriate for a 4-site trial

**Trial design & endpoints**

- A Phase 3, multisite (4 sites), randomized, double-blind trial in the Democratic Republic of Congo, Liberia, and Ghana; 1,472 participants randomized 2:1 to a single 8 mg oral dose of moxidectin or a single body-weight-based oral dose of ivermectin (the WHO-standard comparator), following a positive Phase 2 dose-ranging trial (2 mg/4 mg/8 mg vs. ivermectin, 172 participants) that had already shown 8 mg and 4 mg moxidectin superior to ivermectin
- Primary analysis population: as-randomized modified intention-to-treat (AR-mITT), n=1,472 (977 moxidectin, 495 ivermectin); analyzed by arm as randomized regardless of the drug actually received
- Primary efficacy endpoint: density of *O. volvulus* skin microfilariae at 12 months (natural-log[1+density] scale), modeled via a two-level hierarchical linear model (participants nested within 4 sites) with treatment, log-transformed baseline density, and sex as covariates, estimated by REML; the exponentiated treatment coefficient is interpreted as the ratio of geometric mean (1+density) between arms
- Secondary endpoints: skin microfilariae density at 1, 6, and 18 months; proportion with undetectable skin microfilariae at 1, 6, 12, and 18 months (via an analogous logistic multilevel model); percent reduction in ocular microfilariae by 12 months in a 236-participant subset with high baseline ocular counts
- Missing endpoint data (6.6% moxidectin, 4.9% ivermectin at 18 months) were handled asymmetrically by treatment arm in the applicant's primary approach (see SAP excerpt below), with reviewer-conducted "worst case" sensitivity analyses assessing robustness
- Result: moxidectin was significantly superior to ivermectin on the primary skin-microfilariae-density endpoint and on undetectability at all timepoints in both applicant and FDA-reviewer analyses (e.g., undetectable-microfilariae rates at 12 months of ~91% moxidectin vs. ~12% ivermectin); moxidectin and ivermectin were comparably effective at reducing ocular microfilariae by 12 months

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2018/210867Orig1s000Ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/210867lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID 4238817) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/210867Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00790998
- No sponsor SAP/protocol is posted on ClinicalTrials.gov for this trial
- Pivotal publication: Opoku NO, Bakajika DK, Kanza EM, et al. "Single dose moxidectin versus ivermectin for Onchocerca volvulus infection in Ghana, Liberia, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo: a randomised, controlled, double-blind phase 3 trial." *Lancet.* 2018;392(10154):1207-1216. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(17)32844-1>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29361335/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Single%20dose%20moxidectin%20versus%20ivermectin%20for%20Onchocerca%20volvulus%20infection)

**Other resources**

- Moxidectin was developed through a public-private partnership (originally Wyeth, transferred to WHO/TDR, then to Medicines Development for Global Health); no commercial IPD-sharing platform (Vivli/YODA) participation was confirmed, but the trial's global-health sponsorship model makes broader data sharing with WHO/academic partners plausible, though not individually confirmed here.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting is recorded for this application.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Reference ID 4238817, Executive Summary]*

> "This review evaluates the strength of the evidence for the efficacy and safety of moxidectin for the treatment of onchocerciasis, based on analyses of data from a Phase 3 multisite double-blinded randomized controlled trial involving 1472 participants in Democratic Republic of Congo, Liberia, and Ghana. The review concludes that there is very strong evidence for the efficacy of moxidectin relative to standard treatment (ivermectin)."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, primary-endpoint model specification]*

> "The applicant specified random intercept models to analyze the primary and secondary efficacy endpoints... Let j index sites (j = 1,…,4) and i index participants within sites... The hierarchical linear model used to perform the applicant's analysis of the primary endpoint is [Level 1] Y12ij = βj + β1Tij + β2Ybaseij + β3sexij + εij [Level 2] βj = β0 + ej... β1 gives the average treatment effect... exp(β1) can be interpreted as the ratio of the population geometric mean of 1+mean mf density under the moxidectin condition to the population geometric mean of 1+mean mf density under the ivermectin condition. REML was used to estimate the model's parameters."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, missing-data handling]*

> "...missing endpoint values in the [moxidectin] arm are replaced with the participant's baseline value, and missing endpoint values in the ivermectin arm are replaced with the participant's most recent endpoint observation."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, "Reviewer Comments" — a genuine, unusually detailed methodological critique]*

> "There are several grounds for questioning the adequacy of the statistical analyses: First, multilevel models with site-level random intercepts were used to analyze primary and secondary efficacy endpoints, but these models are inappropriate given the small number of sites in the study... 'A random-effects approach should be used only if there is a sufficient number of clusters [i.e., sites] in the sample, typically more than 10 or 20... Poor estimation of ψ translates to poor estimation of the standard error of β' (Rabe-Hesketh and Skrondal, 2012)... Because the study only used four sites, it would be better to perform the efficacy analyses using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) models (or their analogue for logistic regression) with site fixed effects and computing robust or nonparametric bootstrap standard errors."

Despite this documented methodological disagreement about model choice, the reviewer's own re-analyses (using the ANCOVA/fixed-effects approach it preferred) still found moxidectin significantly superior to ivermectin, and the review recommended approval on efficacy grounds independent of which model specification was used.

### 43. Plazomicin (Zemdri) — NDA 210303

**Sponsor:** Achaogen, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI), including pyelonephritis, caused by susceptible Enterobacteriaceae, in patients with limited or no alternative treatment options.

**Approval date:** 2018-06-25

**Pivotal trial:** EPIC (Study ACHN-490-009), NCT02486627

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled
- *Endpoints:* Composite of microbiological eradication and clinical cure rate (cUTI)
- *Multiplicity:* Co-primary timepoints for a single composite endpoint, non-inferiority required at both (Day 5 and Test-of-Cure)
- *Primary analysis:* Miettinen-Nurminen method
- *Missing data/bias:* Indeterminate-outcome sensitivity analyses for a composite responder endpoint
- *Regulatory:* Bloodstream-infection (BSI) indication submitted but not granted; FDA statistical review "only focuses on the cUTI indication"

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, multicenter, active-controlled trial (plazomicin 15 mg/kg/day IV vs. meropenem 1.0 g IV every 8 hours) in adults with cUTI, including acute pyelonephritis (AP), with an optional switch to open-label oral levofloxacin after a minimum of 4 days of blinded IV therapy (maximum IV duration 7 days)
- Co-primary composite endpoints: composite of microbiological eradication and clinical cure, assessed separately at Day 5 and at Test-of-Cure (TOC, Day 17±2), in the microbiological modified intent-to-treat (mMITT) population (all randomized patients treated with study drug who had ≥1 qualifying baseline uropathogen susceptible to both study drugs); non-inferiority required to be shown at *both* visits for the trial to be declared successful, with a non-inferiority margin of -15% on the risk-difference scale — since both timepoints had to succeed independently for the overall claim, no formal alpha-splitting/multiplicity adjustment across the two timepoints was applied
- A total of 609 patients were randomized; the mMITT population comprised 388 patients (191 plazomicin, 197 meropenem); roughly 25% had aminoglycoside-resistant pathogens and ~28% had ESBL-producing pathogens
- Result: composite cure rates at Day 5 were 88.0% (168/191) plazomicin vs. 91.4% (180/197) meropenem, and at TOC were 81.7% (156/191) plazomicin vs. 70.1% (138/197) meropenem — the lower bound of the 95% CI for the risk difference exceeded the pre-specified -15% margin at both visits, establishing non-inferiority
- Missing/indeterminate clinical or microbiological outcomes were classified as "indeterminate," and the FDA reviewer explicitly checked the robustness of the primary conclusion to how indeterminate outcomes and cures attributable to the optional oral-switch therapy were handled
- A separate, small, non-comparative supportive study (Study 002, plazomicin vs. levofloxacin, not designed for hypothesis testing) was reviewed only as supportive context; the FDA reviewer stated no conclusion could be drawn from it alone given its small sample size

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2018/210303Orig1s000Ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/210303Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID 4263656) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/210303Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (EPIC) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02486627
- No sponsor SAP/protocol is posted on ClinicalTrials.gov for this trial
- Pivotal publication: Wagenlehner FME, Cloutier DJ, Komirenko AS, et al. "Once-Daily Plazomicin for Complicated Urinary Tract Infections." *N Engl J Med.* 2019;380(8):729-740. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1801467), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30786187/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Once-Daily%20Plazomicin%20for%20Complicated%20Urinary%20Tract%20Infections)

**Other resources**

- Achaogen filed for bankruptcy in 2019, less than a year after plazomicin's approval, for commercial (not efficacy/safety) reasons; the drug's marketing rights subsequently changed hands. No trial-specific IPD access (Vivli/YODA) was confirmed.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting is recorded for this application.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Reference ID 4263656, trial summary]*

> "The co-primary endpoints were composite microbiological eradication and clinical cure rate in the microbiological modified intent-to-treat (mMITT) population at the Day 5 and TOC visits... To claim this study successful, noninferiority would need to be shown for the primary endpoints at both Day 5 and TOC. The noninferiority margin for this trial was -15% on the risk difference scale."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, primary result]*

> "The composite cure rates at Day 5 in the mMITT population were 168/191 (88%) for plazomicin and 180/197 (91.4%) for meropenem, and 156/191 (81.7%) for plazomicin and 138/197 (70.1%) for meropenem at TOC visit. Lower limits of the 95% CIs for the rate differences for both visits were above the pre-specified -15% NI margin. The efficacy findings were robust to the handling of indeterminate data, and to the handling of the data for the cures that were likely due to oral therapy."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, scope note on indication]*

> "The applicant, Achaogen Inc., submitted a New Drug Application seeking authorization to market plazomicin for the treatment of complicated urinary tract infections (cUTIs) and bloodstream infections (BSIs). This review only focuses on cUTI indication."

### 44. Tecovirimat (Tpoxx) — NDA 208627

**Sponsor:** SIGA Technologies, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of human smallpox disease caused by variola virus.

**Approval date:** 2018-07-13

**Pivotal trial:** No human efficacy trial — approved under the FDA Animal Rule on the basis of NHP/monkeypox-virus and rabbit/rabbitpox-virus lethal-challenge efficacy studies, bridged to humans via the Phase 3 human PK/safety trial, Study 246-008 (NCT02474589)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Animal Rule pivotal efficacy trials (non-variola surrogate-orthopoxvirus lethal-challenge models, bridged to human PK/safety data)
- *Endpoints:* Survival (mortality) endpoint in an animal lethal-challenge model
- *Primary analysis:* between-arm survival-proportion comparison in randomized, placebo-controlled animal efficacy studies (statistical review by Dr. Wen Zeng; exact test not extracted from the reviewed document)
- *Regulatory:* Approval under the FDA Animal Rule (21 CFR Part 314, Subpart I)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Because natural human smallpox infection has not occurred since global eradication (last natural case 1977) and deliberate human challenge with variola virus is unethical, and because a consistently reproducible, human-disease-mimicking variola/NHP model does not exist, tecovirimat's efficacy could not be shown in a conventional human RCT
- Following a 2009 FDA public workshop and a 2011 FDA Antiviral Drugs Advisory Committee meeting, FDA and its advisors agreed that a combination of lethal animal models using surrogate (non-variola) orthopoxviruses — provided the drug's molecular target is conserved across orthopoxviruses — could support approval under the Animal Rule (21 CFR 314, Subpart I / equivalent 601, Subpart H for biologics)
- SIGA's two pivotal animal efficacy programs: (1) cynomolgus macaques challenged intravenously with 5×10^7 PFU of monkeypox virus (MPXV) Zaire '79, with treatment triggered by skin-lesion onset (Day 4 post-challenge) — four randomized, placebo-controlled studies (three double-blinded) showed a statistically significant survival benefit at tecovirimat 3, 10, or 20 mg/kg/day for 14 days, with 10 mg/kg/day selected as the "fully effective" dose; (2) New Zealand white rabbits challenged intradermally with 1,000 PFU of rabbitpox virus (RPXV) Utrecht (LD50 <4.66 PFU), with treatment triggered by fever onset (Day 4) — two randomized studies (one placebo-controlled pivotal efficacy study, one non-blinded PK study) showed a significant survival benefit at 20, 40, 80, or 120 mg/kg/day for 14 days, with 40 mg/kg/day selected as "fully effective"
- Primary efficacy endpoint in both animal models: mortality (survival to a prospectively defined humane-euthanasia endpoint)
- Human dosing (600 mg BID × 14 days) was selected not from a human efficacy endpoint but by comparing human PK exposures (from the Phase 3 human safety trial, Study 246-008, healthy volunteers) against the PK/PD exposures associated with the "fully effective" doses in the NHP/MPXV and rabbit/RPXV models, ensuring human exposures exceeded the animal fully-effective-dose exposures — the Animal Rule's core evidentiary logic (animal efficacy + human PK bridging + human safety, rather than human efficacy)
- No formal statistical hypothesis test details for the animal-model comparisons were extracted from the reviewed FDA summary document (it references a separate Statistical Review by Dr. Wen Zeng and a Virology Review, not independently retrieved here)

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2018/208627Orig1s000ltr.PDF
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/208627s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Cross-Discipline Team Leader and Division Director (Summary) Review (Reference ID 4278529) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/208627Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (human PK/safety trial, Study 246-008) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02474589
- Pivotal publication (human PK/safety + supportive animal survival data): Grosenbach DW, Honeychurch K, Rose EA, et al. "Oral Tecovirimat for the Treatment of Smallpox." *N Engl J Med.* 2018;379(1):44-53. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1705688), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29972742/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Oral%20Tecovirimat%20for%20the%20Treatment%20of%20Smallpox)

**Other resources**

- Because there is no human efficacy trial, there is no human efficacy IPD to share via Vivli/YODA; SIGA's animal-study data underlying the Animal Rule approval are documented in the FDA review package rather than a public repository.
- The 2011 FDA Antiviral Drugs Advisory Committee meeting (cited above) addressed the general Animal Rule approach for smallpox antivirals rather than this specific NDA at a formal vote.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Cross Discipline Team Leader and Division Director Review, Reference ID 4278529, Animal Rule background]*

> "Because natural variola virus infection and smallpox disease are specific to humans... efficacy trials are not feasible, and human challenge studies in healthy subjects are unethical. Therefore, tecovirimat was developed under the Animal Rule (21 CFR part 314, subpart I), which supports a regulatory approval pathway in which studies using suitable animal models contribute directly to drug approval."

*[verbatim, same source, animal model selection]*

> "During the 2011 Antiviral Drugs Advisory Committee meeting, the advisory committee agreed with the FDA's assessment of the scientific and practical limitations of the available variola virus/NHP model. Furthermore, the FDA and advisory committee concluded that a combination of other lethal animal models using surrogate orthopoxviruses could be used to evaluate the efficacy of antiviral drugs for smallpox, provided the drug target is conserved across different orthopoxviruses... Mortality, based on prospectively defined criteria for euthanasia, was the primary efficacy endpoint in these studies."

*[verbatim, same source, human dose-selection bridging logic]*

> "Human PK data of the investigational agent, combined with PK and PD data obtained in the same animal models that were used to demonstrate animal efficacy, were used to identify an efficacious dose in humans under the Animal Rule. The dosing regimen for humans was selected to provide exposures that exceeded those associated with the fully effective dose in animals, as recommended under FDA's Animal Rule Guidance... Based on these PK results, the favorable safety profile of tecovirimat as demonstrated in Study 246-008..., and the limitations on human exposure based on the toxicology findings..., a human dosing regimen of 600 mg BID x 14 days was selected."

### 45. Tafenoquine (Krintafel) — NDA 210795

**Sponsor:** GlaxoSmithKline (developed in partnership with Medicines for Malaria Venture)

**Indication approved:** Radical cure (prevention of relapse) of *Plasmodium vivax* malaria in patients aged 16 years and older receiving appropriate antimalarial therapy for the acute infection.

**Approval date:** 2018-07-20

**Pivotal trial:** DETECTIVE (Phase 2b/3), NCT01376167; GATHER1 (Phase 3), NCT02216123

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled (three-arm: tafenoquine, primaquine, placebo, all with concomitant chloroquine)
- *Endpoints:* Recurrence-free efficacy (radical cure / relapse-free status at 6 months)
- *Primary analysis:* Logistic regression for binary recurrence-free response, covariate-adjusted by treatment and region
- *Missing data/bias:* Non-responder imputation for missing binary/diary efficacy data (patients with missing Day-180 assessment, or who took disallowed antimalarial medication, or failed initial parasite clearance, were counted as recurrences)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- **DETECTIVE** (NCT01376167) was a two-part, randomized, double-blind trial: Part 1 was a dose-ranging study to select an efficacious, well-tolerated tafenoquine dose to co-administer with chloroquine; Part 2 (the label's "Trial 1," 522 adults across Asia, Africa, and Latin America) randomized patients 2:1:1 to a single tafenoquine dose (two 150 mg tablets) plus chloroquine, an active-control regimen (primaquine) plus chloroquine, or placebo plus chloroquine, all patients receiving chloroquine (600 mg free base Days 1-2, 300 mg Day 3) for the acute infection
- **GATHER1** (NCT02216123) was a separate, larger, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy Phase 3 trial comparing single-dose tafenoquine plus chloroquine against 14-day primaquine plus chloroquine (no placebo arm), designed principally to characterize the comparative incidence of tafenoquine-associated hemolysis in patients with normal G6PD activity, while also assessing relapse-free efficacy
- Primary endpoint (both trials): recurrence-free status at 6 months, defined per the label as demonstrating initial parasite clearance, taking no disallowed antimalarial medication, and being confirmed parasite-free at the Day-180 final assessment; patients not meeting these conditions (including those with a missing Day-180 assessment) were conservatively counted as recurrences
- G6PD-deficient patients (<70% of the site median G6PD activity) were excluded from both trials given tafenoquine's hemolysis risk as an 8-aminoquinoline
- Result in DETECTIVE (Lacerda et al.): recurrence-free at 6 months in 62.4% tafenoquine vs. 27.7% placebo vs. 69.6% primaquine (ITT); hazard ratio for recurrence 0.30 (95% CI 0.22-0.40) tafenoquine vs. placebo (p<0.001) — a clear, statistically decisive win over placebo
- Result in GATHER1 (Llanos-Cuentas et al.): recurrence-free at 6 months in 67.0% tafenoquine vs. 72.8% primaquine, odds ratio for recurrence 1.81 (95% CI 0.82-3.96) — **tafenoquine was not shown to be non-inferior to primaquine** in this trial, an important complication of the approval basis; approval nonetheless rested on tafenoquine's clear, consistent superiority to placebo (from DETECTIVE) and the totality of evidence, rather than on demonstrated non-inferiority to the existing standard-of-care 14-day primaquine regimen
- Label's "Trial 2" (dose-ranging, 57 tafenoquine 300 mg + 54 placebo, both plus chloroquine) showed 84% vs. 39% recurrence-free efficacy at 6 months (difference 45%, 95% CI 29-61%) and appears to correspond to the DETECTIVE Part 1 dose-selection sub-study (same registered NCT as Part 2 per the label)

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2018/210795Orig1s000Ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/210795s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical/Clinical Review: attempted direct-pattern URLs (StatR, MedR, ClinPharmR, SumR) for NDA 210795 all returned 404 as of this review; the FDA review-package TOC page (JavaScript-rendered, not retrievable via automated fetch) is at https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/210795Orig1s000TOC.html
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (DETECTIVE) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01376167
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (GATHER1) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02216123
- No sponsor SAP/protocol is posted on ClinicalTrials.gov for either trial
- Pivotal publication (DETECTIVE): Lacerda MVG, Llanos-Cuentas A, Krudsood S, et al. "Single-Dose Tafenoquine to Prevent Relapse of Plasmodium vivax Malaria." *N Engl J Med.* 2019;380(3):215-228. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1710775), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30650322/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Single-Dose%20Tafenoquine%20to%20Prevent%20Relapse%20of%20Plasmodium%20vivax%20Malaria)
- Pivotal publication (GATHER1): Llanos-Cuentas A, Casapia M, Chuquiyauri R, et al. "Tafenoquine versus Primaquine to Prevent Relapse of Plasmodium vivax Malaria." *N Engl J Med.* 2019;380(3):229-241. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1802537), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30650326/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Tafenoquine%20versus%20Primaquine%20to%20Prevent%20Relapse%20of%20Plasmodium%20vivax%20Malaria)

**Other resources**

- No trial-specific IPD access (Vivli/YODA) was confirmed; GSK has a general clinical-data-sharing policy but trial-specific availability was not individually verified here.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting is recorded for this application; tafenoquine received orphan drug designation and priority review.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, approved Package Insert, Section 14 Clinical Studies, Trial 1/DETECTIVE]*

> "Patients were considered recurrence-free at 6 months if they demonstrated initial parasite clearance, took no anti-malarial medications, and were confirmed parasite-free at the 6-month final assessment (i.e., absence of relapse or new infection)... The risk of recurrence for KRINTAFEL plus chloroquine was reduced by 76% compared with placebo plus chloroquine."

*[verbatim, approved Package Insert, Table 2 footnote — the actual primary-analysis statistical method]*

> "Odds ratio of the risk of recurrence of tafenoquine plus chloroquine versus placebo plus chloroquine using logistic regression model with treatment and region as covariates. Subjects who did not demonstrate initial clearance, took a concomitant medication with anti-malarial activity, or who had a missing Day 180 assessment were considered 'missing/indeterminate' and were counted as recurrences in the analysis."

**Reverse-engineered SAP** *[inferred]*

- *[inferred, from the GATHER1 abstract's reported point estimate and 95% CI]* — the GATHER1 primary analysis almost certainly pre-specified a formal non-inferiority margin for the tafenoquine-vs-primaquine odds ratio or risk difference; because the reported 95% CI (OR 0.82-3.96) straddles both 1 and any plausible pre-specified NI margin, the trial's own primary hypothesis test would have failed to reject the null of inferiority — consistent with the publication's explicit statement that "tafenoquine was not shown to be noninferior to that of primaquine."

### 46. Eravacycline (Xerava) — NDA 211109

**Sponsor:** Tetraphase Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Complicated intra-abdominal infections (cIAI) in patients 18 years of age and older.

**Approval date:** 2018-08-27

**Pivotal trial:** IGNITE1, NCT01844856; IGNITE4, NCT02784704

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled
- *Endpoints:* Clinical response (cure/failure) at Test-of-Cure visit (cIAI)
- *Primary analysis:* Miettinen-Nurminen method (unstratified)
- *Multiplicity:* dual regulator-specific co-primary populations (FDA primary endpoint in micro-ITT population; EMA primary endpoint in a separate population), each independently required to meet non-inferiority, so no formal alpha-splitting was applied across them
- *Missing data/bias:* Non-responder imputation for missing binary/diary efficacy data (missing/indeterminate clinical response classified conservatively)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- **IGNITE1** (NCT01844856): Phase 3, randomized, double-blind trial of eravacycline vs. ertapenem in cIAI (541 randomized, 270 eravacycline/271 ertapenem); non-inferiority declared in the microbiological intent-to-treat population (clinical cure at TOC: 86.8% eravacycline vs. 87.6% ertapenem, difference -0.80%, 95% CI -7.1 to 5.5)
- **IGNITE4** (NCT02784704, Protocol TP-434-025): Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy trial of eravacycline (1.0 mg/kg q12h) vs. meropenem (1.0 g q8h) in cIAI, designed to satisfy both FDA and EMA regulatory requirements simultaneously
- Primary efficacy population for IGNITE4: microbiological intent-to-treat (micro-ITT) — all randomized subjects with ≥1 qualifying baseline pathogen against which both study drugs had activity; primary endpoint was clinical response (cure/failure/indeterminate) at the Test-of-Cure (TOC) visit
- Non-inferiority margin: 12.5% on the risk-difference scale (one-sided alpha 0.025, 80% power), based on historical antibiotic treatment-effect data and results from the prior eravacycline Phase 3 cIAI study (IGNITE1); the primary analysis also had to satisfy the EMA's co-primary efficacy outcome (a secondary outcome for FDA) in a separately defined clinically-evaluable-type population — the trial's sample size (~466) was driven by ensuring adequate power for both regulators' distinct primary populations simultaneously
- Sample size was reassessed mid-trial: "Based upon the results of the pre-specified blinded assessment of the actual number of subjects in the micro-ITT population following completion of the 250th subject, the evaluability rate is assumed to be 68.75%," triggering an increase in target enrollment to ~466
- Result (IGNITE4): eravacycline non-inferior to meropenem in the primary endpoint (177/195, 90.8% vs. 187/205, 91.2%; difference -0.5%, 95% CI -6.3 to 5.3), exceeding the pre-specified margin; consistent results in secondary populations (modified ITT and clinically evaluable) and in the ESBL-producing-Enterobacteriaceae subgroup

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/211109lbl.pdf
- FDA Review package (TOC) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/211109Orig1s000TOC.html (direct-pattern StatR/MedR URL guesses were not resolved for this NDA)

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (IGNITE4) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02784704
