**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, IGNITE4 Clinical Protocol TP-434-025, Version 2.0 (20 March 2017), §14.2.1 Efficacy Analyses]*

> "The primary efficacy outcome measure is clinical response at the TOC Visit (incorporating the SAC assessment) in the micro-ITT population... A 2-sided 95% CI for the observed difference in clinical cure rates (eravacycline treatment group minus meropenem treatment group) will be calculated using the method without stratification of Miettinen and Nurminen. If the lower limit of the 95% CI for the difference in clinical cure rates in the micro-ITT population exceeds -12.5%, then non-inferiority of eravacycline to meropenem will be declared."

*[verbatim, same source, §14.2.3 Sample Size Considerations]*

> "This study is designed to demonstrate non-inferiority of 1.0 mg/kg q12h eravacycline to meropenem in the primary outcome measure of clinical response at the TOC Visit in the micro-ITT Population. An NI margin of 12.5% will be used, which is based on historical data regarding the treatment effect of antibiotics and the results of the previously completed eravacycline phase 3 cIAI study... The sample size calculation is based on ensuring sufficient power for the primary efficacy outcome for the FDA as well as the primary efficacy outcome for the EMA (which are secondary efficacy outcomes for the FDA)."

*[verbatim, same source, mid-trial sample-size re-estimation]*

> "Based upon the results of the pre-specified blinded assessment of the actual number of subjects in the micro-ITT population following completion of the 250th subject, the evaluability rate is assumed to be 68.75%."

### 47. Doravirine (Pifeltro) — NDA 210806

**Sponsor:** Merck Sharp & Dohme LLC

**Indication approved:** In combination with other antiretroviral agents, for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in adults with no prior antiretroviral treatment history.

**Approval date:** 2018-08-30

**Pivotal trial:** DRIVE-FORWARD, NCT02275780; DRIVE-AHEAD, NCT02403674

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled; Non-inferiority-then-superiority hierarchy
- *Endpoints:* Virologic suppression rate (HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL, FDA Snapshot algorithm)
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test (stratum-adjusted Mantel-Haenszel weighted difference in proportions)
- *Multiplicity:* Closed testing procedure (superiority tested only if non-inferiority is first established; no multiplicity penalty required)
- *Missing data/bias:* FDA Snapshot algorithm / Non-Completer=Failure (NC=F) approach for HIV virologic-response missing data

**Trial design & endpoints**

- **DRIVE-FORWARD** (NCT02275780, Protocol MK-1439-018): randomized, double-blind, active-controlled non-inferiority trial in treatment-naive adults, comparing doravirine 100 mg once daily vs. ritonavir-boosted darunavir 800/100 mg once daily, each with 2 investigator-selected NRTIs (tenofovir/emtricitabine or abacavir/lamivudine), for up to 96 weeks; randomization stratified by screening HIV-1 RNA (≤ vs. >100,000 copies/mL) and NRTI pair
- **DRIVE-AHEAD** (NCT02403674, Protocol MK-1439A-021): randomized, double-blind trial of a once-daily fixed-dose combination of doravirine/lamivudine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (DOR/3TC/TDF) vs. efavirenz/emtricitabine/TDF (EFV/FTC/TDF, i.e., ATRIPLA) in treatment-naive adults, over 96 weeks
- Primary endpoint (both trials): proportion of participants with HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL at Week 48, using the FDA "snapshot" algorithm — the Non-Completer=Failure (NC=F) approach in which "all missing data will be treated as failures regardless of the reason," applied in the Full Analysis Set (all randomized subjects who received ≥1 dose and had baseline data)
- Primary analysis: stratum-adjusted Mantel-Haenszel method, with the treatment-group difference in proportions weighted by the harmonic mean of the per-stratum sample sizes; non-inferiority margin of 10 percentage points on the response-rate difference
- Multiplicity/hierarchy: "Due to the principles of closed testing, no adjustment for multiplicity is required for the superiority test since non-inferiority can always be concluded whenever the data also support superiority" — superiority tested only after non-inferiority was established, at the same alpha
- Sensitivity analysis: an Observed-Failure (OF) approach in which non-intermittent missing data due to lack of efficacy were treated as failures thereafter but other missingness was excluded, contrasted against the NC=F primary approach
- Results: DRIVE-FORWARD — 84% (321/383) doravirine vs. 80% (306/383) darunavir/ritonavir achieved HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL at Week 48 (difference 3.9%, 95% CI -1.6 to 9.4), establishing non-inferiority; DRIVE-AHEAD — 84.3% (307/364) DOR/3TC/TDF vs. 80.8% (294/364) EFV/FTC/TDF (difference 3.5%, 95% CI -2.0 to 9.0), also non-inferior, with markedly fewer neuropsychiatric adverse events and more favorable lipid changes than efavirenz

### 48. Omadacycline (Nuzyra) — NDA 209816

**Sponsor:** Paratek Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (via Paratek Pharma, LLC)

**Indication approved:** Community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (CABP) in adults.

**Approval date:** 2018-10-02

**Pivotal trial:** OPTIC (Protocol PTK-CABP-002), NCT02531438

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, non-inferiority
- *Endpoints:* Early Clinical Response (ECR) — FDA primary endpoint for CABP registration trials
- *Primary analysis:* Miettinen-Nurminen method (unstratified for the FDA primary endpoint/ITT population; stratified, by randomization stratification factors, for the EMA primary endpoint/CE population)
- *Multiplicity:* dual regulator-specific co-primary endpoints (FDA: Early Clinical Response in ITT; EMA: Investigator's Assessment of Clinical Response at Post-Treatment Evaluation in ITT and CE populations restricted to PORT Risk Class III+), each independently required to show non-inferiority, so no alpha adjustment across them

**Trial design & endpoints**

- OPTIC was a Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, multicenter trial comparing omadacycline (IV, with optional switch to oral) vs. moxifloxacin (IV, with optional switch to oral) in adult CABP patients, stratified by PORT Risk Class, receipt of allowed antibacterial therapy in the hours before study treatment, and geographic region
- FDA primary endpoint: Early Clinical Response (ECR), a composite based on the patient's respiratory/vital-sign status at a defined early timepoint, analyzed in the ITT population; EMA primary endpoint: Investigator's Assessment of Clinical Response at Post-Treatment Evaluation (PTE), analyzed in both the ITT and clinically evaluable (CE) populations restricted to PORT Risk Class III or higher
- Non-inferiority declared if the lower bound of the two-sided confidence interval for the omadacycline-minus-moxifloxacin difference in response rate exceeded the pre-specified margin, using the unstratified Miettinen-Nurminen method for the FDA (ECR) endpoint and the stratified Miettinen-Nurminen method (stratified by randomization factors) for the EMA (PTE) endpoint
- Because the FDA and EMA co-primary endpoints/populations were each independently required to show non-inferiority to conclude overall non-inferiority, the protocol states no formal multiplicity adjustment was applied across them; if the null hypothesis of inferiority was rejected for ECR and the observed omadacycline response rate exceeded moxifloxacin's, a formal superiority test was also conducted
- Results (published trial report): ITT population 386 omadacycline / 388 moxifloxacin; omadacycline non-inferior to moxifloxacin for early clinical response (81.1% vs. 82.7%, difference -1.6 points, 95% CI -7.1 to 3.8) and for investigator-assessed clinical response at PTE (87.6% vs. 85.1%, difference 2.5 points, 95% CI -2.4 to 7.4)

### 49. Baloxavir marboxil (Xofluza) — NDA 210854

**Sponsor:** Shionogi Inc.

**Indication approved:** Acute uncomplicated influenza in patients 12 years of age and older who have been symptomatic for no more than 48 hours.

**Approval date:** 2018-10-24

**Pivotal trial:** CAPSTONE-1, NCT02954354

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled
- *Endpoints:* Time to alleviation of symptoms (TTAS, patient-reported influenza symptom diary)
- *Primary analysis:* Peto-Prentice generalized Wilcoxon test (stratified); FDA reviewer's independent re-analysis instead used the Gehan generalized Wilcoxon test
- *Multiplicity:* Hochberg step-up procedure (Phase 2b dose-selection stage, per applicant); FDA reviewer instead applied the Hochberg procedure directly comparing each dose to placebo
- *Missing data/bias:* Conservative failure-imputation for missing patient-diary symptom assessments in a time-to-event analysis
- *Regulatory:* FDA statistical reviewer conducted an independent re-analysis using an alternative primary-test variant from the applicant's

**Trial design & endpoints**

- CAPSTONE-1 was a randomized, double-blind, placebo- and oseltamivir-controlled Phase 3 trial in otherwise-healthy outpatients 12-64 years old with acute uncomplicated influenza, following a positive Phase 2 dose-ranging placebo-controlled trial; patients received a single weight-based dose of baloxavir (40 or 80 mg), placebo, or oseltamivir 75 mg twice daily for 5 days
- Primary efficacy endpoint: time to alleviation of symptoms (TTAS), defined as the time from treatment initiation until all 7 influenza symptoms (cough, sore throat, headache, nasal congestion, feverishness/chills, muscle/joint pain, fatigue) were patient-rated as "None" or "Mild" for a sustained duration of at least 21.5 hours, in the intention-to-treat-infected (ITTI) population
- Primary analysis: stratified Peto-Prentice's generalized Wilcoxon test, stratified by baseline composite symptom score (≤11 vs. ≥12) and region (Japan/Asia vs. rest of world); patients not experiencing alleviation were censored at their last observation; missing symptom assessments were conservatively treated as continuing moderate/severe symptoms (i.e., as ongoing "failures") rather than excluded
- Sample size: the trial was powered assuming a 65% RT-PCR-confirmed influenza positivity rate, targeting 1,494 randomized patients (144 aged 12-19, 1,350 aged 20-64) to yield 618 patients in the ITTI population, giving ≥90% power at two-sided alpha=0.05 for the stratified generalized Wilcoxon test under an assumed 36-hour treatment difference
- FDA statistical reviewer disagreement: the applicant used the Peto-Prentice version of the generalized Wilcoxon test as primary (having used the Gehan version as a secondary analysis in the earlier Phase 2b trial, per a Hommel-adjusted, dose-vs-placebo Phase 2b primary analysis based on a Cox model); the FDA reviewer instead used the more common Gehan generalized Wilcoxon test as its own primary comparison method — both because the applicant's own Phase 2b trial had used the Gehan version and because it is more widely used — and ran log-rank, Peto, and modified-Peto sensitivity analyses; median-difference estimates used the Hodges-Lehmann estimator with censored values set to the 14-day maximum follow-up
- Result (ITTI population, n=1,064; 84.8-88.1% influenza A(H3N2)): median TTAS 53.7 hours (95% CI 49.5-58.5) with baloxavir vs. 80.2 hours (95% CI 72.6-87.1) with placebo (p<0.001); TTAS was similar between baloxavir and oseltamivir

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2018/210854Orig1s000ltr_ReplacementLtr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/210854s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID 4324624) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/210854Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (CAPSTONE-1) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02954354
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (CAPSTONE-2, high-risk-of-complications population, supportive) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02949011
- Protocol (Clinical Study Protocol 1601T0831, 6 July 2017) — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/54/NCT02954354/Prot_000.pdf
- Statistical Analysis Plan (6 July 2017) — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/54/NCT02954354/SAP_001.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Hayden FG, Sugaya N, Hirotsu N, et al. "Baloxavir Marboxil for Uncomplicated Influenza in Adults and Adolescents." *N Engl J Med.* 2018;379(10):913-923. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1716197), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30184455/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Baloxavir%20Marboxil%20for%20Uncomplicated%20Influenza%20in%20Adults%20and%20Adolescents)

**Other resources**

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting is recorded for this application.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, CAPSTONE-1 Statistical Analysis Plan, §9.1.1.1 Primary Analysis]*

> "Time to alleviation of symptoms will be compared between the S-033188 group and the placebo group using the stratified Peto-Prentice's generalized Wilcoxon test with composite symptoms score at baseline (≤ 11 or ≥ 12) and region (Japan/Asia or Rest of the world) as stratification factors. Patients who do not experience alleviation of symptoms will be censored at the last observation time point. If at least one of the 7 influenza symptom scores is missing at date and time of assessment that patients have, missing assessments of influenza symptoms conservatively will be treated as having moderate or severe symptoms (as failures) at the corresponding date and time of assessment."

```
proc lifetest data = analysisdata;
 where TRTP in ("S-033188", "Placebo");
 time TIME * CENSOR (0);
 strata SCOREC REGION / group = TRTP test = PETO ;
run;quit;
```

*[verbatim, CAPSTONE-1 Protocol, §6.4 Handling of Missing Data]*

> "Missing data will not be imputed... If all symptoms were missing after baseline, time to alleviation of symptoms... will be handled as missing. For the sensitive analysis for primary endpoint, the patients who do not [experience alleviation]... time to alleviation of symptoms will be censored as 14 days."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Reference ID 4324624, reviewer's divergent test choice]*

> "In the phase 2b trial, the applicant used the Cox proportional hazards model for the primary analysis... The applicant used the Hommel method in the phase 2b trial to adjust for multiplicity... Because the proportional hazards assumption is violated, the Wilcoxon tests were more powerful than the Cox proportional hazards or logrank tests. Therefore, the applicant decided to use the Peto-Prentice version of the generalized Wilcoxon test as the primary analysis for the phase 3 trial while the reviewer used the Gehan generalized Wilcoxon test. The Peto and modified Peto approaches are variations of the Wilcoxon test and typically produce similar results. The reviewer chose to use the more common Gehan version of the Wilcoxon test in part because the applicant used this version in their phase 2b trial and because it has been more commonly used than the other versions."

### 50. Triclabendazole (Egaten) — NDA 208711

**Sponsor:** Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation

**Indication approved:** Fascioliasis in patients 6 years of age and older.

**Approval date:** 2019-02-13

**Pivotal trial:** No single dedicated Phase 3 pivotal trial with an NCT registration — approval rested on one small randomized open-label trial (Hien et al., 2008, Vietnam) plus a pooled literature/clinical-development-program dataset of 6 non-randomized open-label studies

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Literature-based approval (no dedicated pivotal trial) — closest existing taxonomy fit, though here the evidentiary basis includes one small dedicated randomized trial alongside pooled non-randomized literature, rather than published literature alone (proposed refinement noted)
- *Endpoints:* Parasitological cure rate (absence of *Fasciola* eggs in stool by Kato-Katz method at Day 60)
- *Primary analysis:* Descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (point estimate + CI, no formal hypothesis test) (reused for the pooled open-label studies); simple two-sided CI for the risk difference (unstratified) for the one randomized comparator trial

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Triclabendazole (Egaten) had been used for decades outside the US (including via a WHO donation program) before this 2019 US approval; the NDA's clinical evidence package assembled prior international trials and clinical experience rather than a newly conducted, FDA-registered pivotal Phase 3 trial
- **Randomized comparator evidence:** an open-label, randomized trial conducted in Vietnam (100 patients, ages 9-74, with acute symptomatic fascioliasis, 50 per arm) compared triclabendazole (two 10 mg/kg doses 12 hours apart, with food) against oral artesunate (4 mg/kg once daily for 10 days); at 3 months, 92% (triclabendazole) vs. 76% (artesunate) of patients reported no clinical symptoms (difference 16 percentage points, 95% CI 1.7-30.8, p=0.035) — this trial (Hien et al., *Am J Trop Med Hyg* 2008) predates ClinicalTrials.gov-era registration and has no NCT number
- **Pooled non-randomized literature basis:** 6 non-randomized, open-label studies conducted in Cuba, Bolivia, Peru, Chile, and Iran, totaling 245 adult and pediatric patients with stool-confirmed fascioliasis, of similar design across studies; triclabendazole doses ranging 5-20 mg/kg given over Days 1-3; cure defined as absence of *Fasciola* eggs in stool (Kato-Katz method) at Day 60 in patients positive at baseline
- Result (pooled studies): a clear dose-response was observed — Day-60 cure rate 95.5% (95% CI 77-100%) at the approved 20 mg/kg (2 divided doses) regimen, vs. 88% (64-99%), 80% (73-86%), and 50% (27-73%) at 15, 10, and 5 mg/kg respectively (the lower doses are not approved); these rates were compared descriptively against a 22% (95% CI 9.8-38.2) cure rate estimated from patients receiving inadequate, non-triclabendazole treatment in a separate study
- No formal multiplicity control, alpha-spending, or missing-data-imputation methodology is described in the label for either the randomized trial or the pooled open-label program — consistent with a literature-synthesis regulatory basis rather than a single pre-specified confirmatory trial

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2019/208711Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2019/208711s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Review package (TOC) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/208711Orig1s000TOC.html (direct-pattern MedR/StatR URL guesses were not resolved for this NDA)
- No ClinicalTrials.gov record exists for the Vietnam randomized trial (it predates registration-era requirements); a post-approval Phase 4 confirmatory/registry-type study is recorded at https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04230148 (not part of the original approval basis)
- Pivotal publication (randomized comparator trial): Hien TT, Truong NT, Minh HN, et al. "A Randomized Controlled Pilot Study of Artesunate versus Triclabendazole for Human Fascioliasis in Central Vietnam." *Am J Trop Med Hyg.* 2008;78(3):388-392. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.4269/ajtmh.2008.78.388), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18337331/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=A%20Randomized%20Controlled%20Pilot%20Study%20of%20Artesunate%20versus%20Triclabendazole%20for%20Human%20Fascioliasis)

**Other resources**

- No trial-specific IPD access (Vivli/YODA) applies, given the literature-synthesis basis of this approval; the individual pooled-study reports/authors were not identified individually in the label and were not traced further here.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting is recorded for this application.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, approved Package Insert, Section 14 Clinical Studies]*

> "An open label, randomized trial, conducted in Vietnam compared the efficacy of triclabendazole (two 10 mg/kg doses given 12 hours apart with food) to oral artesunate (4 mg/kg, given once daily for 10 days). One hundred patients (age range: 9-74 years) with acute symptomatic fascioliasis were randomized, 50 in each treatment group. At 3 months after treatment, 92% and 76% (difference 16%; 95% CI [1.7, 30.8], p = 0.035) of patients in the triclabendazole and artesunate arms respectively, reported no clinical symptoms."

*[verbatim, same source, pooled literature basis and dose-response]*

> "The clinical development program of triclabendazole for the treatment of fascioliasis included 6 non-randomized, open label studies performed in Cuba, Bolivia, Peru, Chile, and Iran in a total of 245 adult and pediatric patients with stool-confirmed fascioliasis. All studies were similar in design. The studied triclabendazole doses ranged from 5 mg/kg to 20 mg/kg administered on Days 1-3. Cure was defined as absence of Fasciola eggs in the stool based on the Kato-Katz method at Day 60 in patients who were positive at baseline. Across these studies, there was a finding of a dose response. Specifically, the Day 60 cure rate was highest (95.5%; 95% CI [77%, 100%]) for the 20 mg/kg dose, which was given in 2 divided doses, followed by cure rates of 88% (95% CI [64%, 99%]), 80% (95% CI [73%, 86%]), and 50% (95% CI [27%, 73%]) in the 15 mg/kg, 10 mg/kg, and 5 mg/kg dose groups, respectively... These rates were significantly higher than that estimated from patients receiving an inadequate, non-triclabendazole treatment in a separate study (22%; 95% CI [9.8, 38.2])."

### 51. Imipenem/cilastatin/relebactam (Recarbrio) — NDA 212819

**Sponsor:** Merck Sharp & Dohme Corp.

**Indication approved:** Complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI), including pyelonephritis, and complicated intra-abdominal infections (cIAI) caused by designated susceptible Gram-negative microorganisms in patients with limited or no alternative treatment options

**Approval date:** July 16, 2019

**Pivotal trial:** RESTORE-IMI 1 (Protocol MK-7655A-013), NCT02452047

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, non-randomized open-label supplementary treatment group, small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (imipenem-resistant infections are a rare enrollment population; only 31 randomized subjects total)
- *Endpoints:* proportion of subjects with a favorable overall response (composite of clinical and/or microbiological response by infection type), favorable clinical response at Day 28, all-cause mortality at Day 28
- *Primary analysis:* descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (point estimate + CI, no formal hypothesis test) — 95% CI (Agresti & Coull method) for a single-group proportion in each treatment arm, reported without a formal between-arm hypothesis test; Miettinen & Nurminen method (post hoc, stratified difference)
- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation for missing binary/diary efficacy data (protocol-specified "missing = failure" rule for the primary and key secondary endpoints)
- *Regulatory:* accelerated/limited-population antibacterial approval based on a single small estimation trial with no formal statistical testing, supported by PK/PD and in vitro microbiology data (Limited Population Pathway for Antibacterial and Antifungal Drugs, LPAD)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- RESTORE-IMI 1 randomized approximately 54 subjects 2:1 to imipenem/cilastatin/relebactam (IMI/REL) or colistimethate sodium plus imipenem/cilastatin (CMS+IMI), stratified by infection type (HABP/VABP, cIAI, cUTI), all with imipenem-resistant/imipenem-nonsusceptible Gram-negative bacterial infections; an additional 5-10 subjects with imipenem- and colistin-resistant infection were enrolled non-randomly, open-label, into a third IMI/REL-only group
- Primary efficacy endpoint: proportion of subjects with a favorable overall response at Day 28 (a composite defined per infection type: survival through Day 28 for HABP/VABP; clinical response at Day 28 for cIAI; clinical and microbiological response at early follow-up for cUTI), assessed in the microbiological modified intent-to-treat (mMITT) population
- Key secondary endpoints: favorable clinical response at Day 28 following initiation of IV therapy, and all-cause mortality within 28 days after initiation of study therapy
- Sample size: the protocol explicitly states this was "an estimation study; no formal statistical testing will be performed for the efficacy endpoints. The sample sizes planned for the study arise from logistic feasibility and are not driven by statistical considerations" — the target was a minimum of 45 mMITT subjects (15 per infection type)
- Statistical method: 95% CIs for single-group proportions (Agresti & Coull method) reported separately for each treatment arm and infection type, with missing data imputed as treatment failure; a key secondary safety objective (treatment-emergent nephrotoxicity) compared IMI/REL vs. CMS+IMI using a 95% CI for the between-group difference and Fisher's exact test
- Result: favorable overall response in the mMITT population was 71.4% (15/21) for IMI/REL and 70.0% (7/10) for CMS+IMI; favorable clinical response at Day 28 was numerically higher with IMI/REL (71.4% vs. 40.0%) and all-cause mortality through Day 28 was numerically lower (9.5% vs. 30.0%), but the FDA statistical reviewer emphasized that "given the small sample size, the results are highly variable"

An additional 5 to 10 subjects with imipenem-resistant and colistin-resistant bacterial infection will be enrolled into a third non-randomized, open-label treatment group (Group 3: IMI/REL). This is an estimation study; no formal statistical testing will be performed for the efficacy endpoints. The sample sizes planned for the study arise from logistic feasibility and are not driven by statistical considerations."

Proportion of subjects with all-cause mortality at Day 28 post randomization — 95% confidence interval (Agresti & Coull) for single group proportion — mMITT — Missing = Failure."

As the following table shows, favorable overall response proportions were about 70% in both randomized treatment groups. Results are also given by infection type. Favorable clinical response at Day 28 in the IMI/REL group was higher than the CMS+IMI group and all-cause mortality through Day 28 was lower. However, given the small sample size, the results are highly variable."

### 52. Pretomanid (unbranded) — NDA 212862

**Sponsor:** Global Alliance for TB Drug Development (TB Alliance)

**Indication approved:** As part of the BPaL regimen (bedaquiline, pretomanid, linezolid) for treatment of a limited and specific population of adult patients with pulmonary extensively drug-resistant (XDR-TB) or treatment-intolerant or nonresponsive multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB)

**Approval date:** August 14, 2019

**Pivotal trial:** Nix-TB, NCT02333799

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial (Phase 3, uncontrolled, in an ultra-rare/life-threatening disease population), small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population
- *Endpoints:* incidence of bacteriologic failure, relapse, or clinical failure ("unfavourable status") at 6 months after end of treatment
- *Primary analysis:* descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (point estimate + CI, no formal hypothesis test) compared against a prespecified historical-control threshold, plus a separate matched historical-control cohort comparison
- *Missing data/bias:* three parallel analysis populations (ITT, MITT, per-protocol) constructed with progressively stricter exclusion rules; sensitivity analyses re-classifying reinfections and deaths as unfavourable outcomes
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval of a novel drug supported almost entirely by a single small single-arm trial plus a matched historical-control comparison, on the basis of an unmet medical need in a fatal, treatment-resistant disease population; Limited Population Pathway (LPAD)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Nix-TB is a Phase 3, open-label, single-arm trial enrolling up to 200 adults with pulmonary XDR-TB or treatment-intolerant/non-responsive MDR-TB, treated with bedaquiline plus pretomanid (200 mg once daily) plus linezolid for 6 months (extendable to 9 months if still culture-positive at month 4)
- Primary efficacy endpoint: incidence of bacteriologic failure, bacteriologic relapse, or clinical failure through 6 months after the end of treatment ("unfavourable status"); the SAP designated the modified intent-to-treat (MITT) analysis as primary "for publication purposes," while explicitly noting FDA and other regulators would treat the ITT analysis as primary for registration purposes
- The NDA submission was based on the first 45 patients to reach the primary endpoint per an interim data cutoff plan, with the SAP stating interim analyses would be conducted cumulatively on every 15 patients who completed treatment
- No formal hypothesis test against a null value was pre-specified in the classical sense; instead, "for success, the lower bound of the 95% confidence interval for a favorable outcome should be above 50%" (SAP-specified success criterion), and separately, an FDA-agreed historical-control threshold of 50% unfavorable-outcome-free rate (later described in FDA's review as needing to clear a 50% historical control bar) was used
- FDA review additionally compared the trial's 89% favorable-outcome rate to a matched historical control cohort (11% favorable outcome), Relative Risk 64.5 (95% CI 9-472), p<0.0001
- Result: as of the January 18, 2019 interim efficacy data cutoff, the rate of favorable outcomes for the agreed 45-patient population was 40/45 (89%, 95% CI 76%-96%) in the ITT population, substantially exceeding the prespecified historical-control threshold

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, Nix-TB Efficacy Statistical Analysis Plan, v1.0, 11 July 2017, §2 "Primary Efficacy Endpoint," p.4]*

> "The primary efficacy endpoint will be the incidence of bacteriologic failure or relapse or clinical failure at 6 months after the end of therapy... There will be three main analyses of the primary efficacy endpoint: An intent to treat (ITT) analysis; a modified intent to treat (MITT) analysis and a per protocol (PP) analysis. The 'unfavourable' rates in any defined 'ITT' population will likely be increased by factors other than bacteriologic or clinical treatment failure and relapse. The MITT analysis will therefore be considered primary for publication purposes. However, we recognize that FDA and other regulatory agencies will consider the ITT analysis primary for the purpose of the NDA filing."

*[verbatim, Nix-TB SAP, §7 "Primary endpoint analysis," p.10]*

> "The MITT analyses will be considered primary. The proportion of assessable patients with a favourable and unfavourable outcome, with 95% confidence intervals, will be presented. For success, the lower bound of the 95% confidence interval for a favourable outcome should be above 50%. This MITT analysis is consistent with the TB literature over the past 50 years. However, we recognize that for the purposes of the NDA, FDA and other regulatory agencies will consider the ITT analysis primary, where all patients who are not proven to have a favourable outcome will be classified as having an unfavourable outcome."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Statistical Review section]*

> "As of the January 18, 2019 interim efficacy data cutoff, the rate of favorable outcomes was 40/45 [89%, 95% CI, 76% - 96%] in the ITT population... The success rate for BPaL was substantially larger than the 50% rate prespecified as the historical control rate threshold. In addition, a comparison was made to the outcomes in a matched historical control cohort and outcomes for XDR-TB reported in the literature. Matched historical control favorable outcome was 11% compared to 89%, in the Nix-TB trial, Relative Risk 64.5, 95% CI [9 to 472], p <0.0001... While there are uncertainties with use of historical controls, treatment effect seen with the BPaL regimen significantly exceeded the published historical control rates seen in patients treated for XDR-TB without pretomanid, bedaquiline, or linezolid, or in a matched historically controlled comparison."

### 53. Lefamulin (Xenleta) — NDA 211672

**Sponsor:** Nabriva Therapeutics AG

**Indication approved:** Community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (CABP) in adults

**Approval date:** August 19, 2019

**Pivotal trial:** LEAP 1 (Protocol NAB-BC-3781-3101), NCT02559310, and LEAP 2 (Protocol NAB-BC-3781-3102), NCT02813694

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled, non-inferiority-then-superiority hierarchy (NI only; no superiority claim sought)
- *Endpoints:* early clinical response (ECR) at 96 ± 24 hours after first dose (primary, FDA-preferred endpoint); investigator assessment of clinical response (IACR) at test-of-cure (secondary for FDA, primary for EMA)
- *Primary analysis:* continuity-corrected Z-test for a difference of two proportions (unadjusted), one-sided non-inferiority test at the 2.5% significance level
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* sample-size re-estimation (Cui-Hung-Wang-style blinded reassessment) at ~60% of ECR data collected, reviewed by an independent, blinded Interim Analysis Committee separate from the safety-monitoring DMC
- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation for missing binary/diary efficacy data (indeterminate/missing ECR outcomes counted as non-responders in the denominator)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- LEAP 1 (Trial 3101) randomized 1:1 (551 subjects) to IV-to-oral lefamulin or IV-to-oral moxifloxacin (with optional adjunctive linezolid for suspected MRSA), stratified by geographic region, prior short-acting antibiotic use, and PORT risk class; LEAP 2 (Trial 3102) randomized 1:1 (738 subjects) to entirely oral 5-day lefamulin vs. oral 7-day moxifloxacin in a lower-severity outpatient-eligible population
- Primary efficacy endpoint (both trials, FDA's preferred assessment): percentage of subjects with an early clinical response (ECR) — improvement in at least 2 of 4 cardinal CABP symptoms without worsening of any, no receipt of rescue antibacterial therapy, and survival — at 96 ± 24 hours after the first dose, in the ITT Analysis Set
- Secondary endpoint used as the primary endpoint for EMA: Investigator Assessment of Clinical Response (IACR) success at the test-of-cure (TOC) visit, in the modified-ITT and clinically-evaluable analysis sets
- Non-inferiority margin: originally 10% (LEAP 1 protocol), amended in March 2016 — before enrollment was underway — to 12.5% for the ECR endpoint (matching the FDA CABP guidance's suggested margin), which allowed the planned sample size to decrease from 738 to 550 in LEAP 1
- Statistical method: null hypothesis H0: P(lefamulin) − P(moxifloxacin) ≤ −Δ, tested one-sided at the 2.5% level using an unadjusted continuity-corrected Z-test; non-inferiority declared if the lower bound of the 95% CI for the ECR rate difference exceeded −12.5% (LEAP 1) or the IACR rate difference exceeded −10% (secondary, both trials)
- Interim analysis: a blinded sample-size re-estimation was performed once ECR data were available for ~60% of randomized subjects, per FDA's 2016 non-inferiority guidance, with a separate Interim Analysis Committee (blinded to treatment assignment) making the sample-size recommendation, distinct from the safety-focused Data Monitoring Committee
- Results: LEAP 1 ECR rate was 87.3% (lefamulin) vs. 90.2% (moxifloxacin), difference −2.9% (95% CI −8.5, 2.8); LEAP 2 ECR rate was 90.8% for both arms, difference 0.0% (95% CI −4.4, 4.5) — non-inferiority was demonstrated in both trials

### 54. Cefiderocol (Fetroja) — NDA 209445

**Sponsor:** Shionogi Inc.

**Indication approved:** Complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI), including pyelonephritis, caused by designated susceptible Gram-negative microorganisms in patients ≥18 years with limited or no alternative treatment options

**Approval date:** November 14, 2019

**Pivotal trial:** APEKS-cUTI, NCT02321800; supportive safety trial CREDIBLE-CR, NCT02714595

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, active-controlled non-inferiority-then-superiority hierarchy (APEKS-cUTI); randomized, open-label, active-controlled descriptive study with no pre-specified hypothesis testing (CREDIBLE-CR)
- *Endpoints:* composite of clinical response (cure) and microbiological eradication at test-of-cure (TOC) in the micro-ITT population (APEKS-cUTI primary); all-cause mortality at Day 14, Day 28, and overall (CREDIBLE-CR)
- *Primary analysis:* 95% CI for the difference in composite response rates (APEKS-cUTI, NI margin 15%); descriptive rate reporting with 95% CIs and Kaplan-Meier survival curves, no formal hypothesis test (CREDIBLE-CR)
- *Missing data/bias:* conservative worst-case imputation sensitivity analysis (impute failure for cefiderocol/success for control among indeterminate outcomes) confirmed the primary conclusion in APEKS-cUTI
- *Regulatory:* approval based on a single adequate and well-controlled trial with supportive in vitro/animal-model evidence (Limited Population Pathway, LPAD); post-approval safety signal from a separate randomized trial (CREDIBLE-CR) prompting a labeled Warning and Precaution rather than a Boxed Warning after Advisory Committee discussion

**Trial design & endpoints**

- APEKS-cUTI randomized 448 adults with cUTI (including pyelonephritis) 2:1 to cefiderocol 2 g IV q8h (1-hour infusion) or imipenem-cilastatin (IMP) 1 g/1 g IV q8h for 7 days; primary endpoint was the composite of clinical response (cure) and microbiological eradication at the TOC visit (7±2 days post-therapy) in the micro-ITT population, using a 15% non-inferiority margin — "considered acceptable to support a limited use indication" per FDA
- Result: composite response rates were 183/252 (72.6%) for cefiderocol vs. 65/119 (54.6%) for IMP, difference 18.6% (95% CI 8.2 to 28.9); because the lower CI bound exceeded zero, cefiderocol met criteria for statistical superiority even though the trial was designed as non-inferiority — FDA noted this was "primarily based on the microbiologic endpoint," with clinical response rates similar between arms
- CREDIBLE-CR (submitted with the same NDA as supportive safety data) randomized ~150 patients 2:1 to cefiderocol or best available therapy (BAT) across a heterogeneous population with cUTI, HABP/VABP/HCABP, or bloodstream infection/sepsis due to carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative organisms; per protocol, "this is a descriptive study; no formal hypothesis testing is planned"
- CREDIBLE-CR safety signal: FDA's review states "a mortality imbalance disfavoring cefiderocol was noted in the study, particularly in the subgroup of patients with HABP/VABP/HCABP, BSI and sepsis. In the small subgroup of patients with cUTI, no difference in mortality was observed. While the cause of the imbalance in mortality has not been established, some of the deaths were due to worsening of the underlying infection particularly in those with infections due to organisms such as A. baumannii"
- FDA's review documents that a subsequently completed but not-yet-submitted active-controlled non-inferiority trial in HABP/VABP (APEKS-NP) showed cefiderocol non-inferior to meropenem for 14-day all-cause mortality — topline results only, "no definitive conclusions can be drawn as these data have not yet been submitted to the Agency for review" at the time of the cUTI approval
- Labeling resolution: "Communicating to health care providers in labeling regarding the mortality imbalance disfavoring cefiderocol in the CREDIBLE-CR study was discussed by the Advisory Committee and was a significant review issue. While the Agency review team considered a Boxed Warning, it was decided that a Warning and Precaution in section 5.1 in the Prescribing Information was more appropriate for this drug indicated for patients who have limited or no available treatment options"

The CREDIBLE-CR study was a descriptive study with no pre-specified hypothesis testing. A mortality imbalance disfavoring cefiderocol was noted in the study, particularly in the subgroup of patients with HABP/VABP/HCABP, BSI and sepsis... While the cause of the imbalance in mortality has not been established, some of the deaths were due to worsening of the underlying infection particularly in those with infections due to organisms such as A. baumannii."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Statistical Review, APEKS-cUTI primary analysis]*

> "As displayed in the table below, response rates for the primary endpoint were 183/252 (72.6%) for the cefiderocol group and 65/119 (54.6%) in the IMP group, leading to a point estimate for the difference in success rates of 18.6%, and a 95% confidence interval for the difference from 8.2% to 28.9%. Because the lower bound of this confidence interval exceeded zero, cefiderocol met statistical criteria for declaring superiority to IMP, even though this study was designed as a noninferiority trial. The difference in overall response was driven primarily by the microbiologic success component of the composite endpoint."

### 55. Artesunate (unbranded) — NDA 213036

**Sponsor:** Amivas LLC

**Indication approved:** Initial treatment of severe malaria in adult and pediatric patients

**Approval date:** May 26, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** SEAQUAMAT (South East Asian Quinine Artesunate Malaria Trial), a Wellcome Trust-funded academic trial predating routine trial registration; no NCT number is associated with SEAQUAMAT. Supportive evidence from AQUAMAT (African Quinine Artesunate Malaria Trial), also unregistered on ClinicalTrials.gov.

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial; literature-based approval (no dedicated pivotal trial) — approval rests on FDA's own review of a published, investigator-led, academically-sponsored randomized trial rather than a trial run by the NDA applicant
- *Endpoints:* in-hospital mortality (primary, both SEAQUAMAT and AQUAMAT)
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test, stratified by site (per the trial's own SAP), Cox proportional-hazards model and Kaplan-Meier estimation (protocol-specified), Pearson's Chi-squared test for unstratified mortality comparisons
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* unplanned unblinded interim looks prompting an ad hoc multiplicity correction — the trial's DSMC conducted two unplanned interim analyses with no prespecified alpha-spending or stopping boundary, and FDA's statistical reviewer retrospectively checked whether the result would have crossed an O'Brien-Fleming or Haybittle-Peto boundary had one been pre-specified
- *Regulatory:* approval by an applicant (Amivas) that did not conduct the pivotal trial itself, based on FDA's independent statistical re-review of a decade-old academic trial's protocol, SAP, and case report forms obtained after the fact

**Trial design & endpoints**

- SEAQUAMAT was a randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial conducted 2003-2005 at 10 hospital sites in Southeast Asia (Bangladesh, India, Indonesia, Myanmar), comparing IV artesunate to IV quinine in 1,461 patients ≥2 years old with severe or suspected severe falciparum malaria; it was designed, run, and published independently of Amivas, which later cross-referenced the trial (along with AQUAMAT and its own PK/safety data) to support the NDA
- Primary efficacy endpoint (per the original trial protocol/SAP): in-hospital mortality, analyzed in the intent-to-treat population using a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by site, with relative risk and odds ratios and 95% CIs; sample size was calculated as 2,000 patients to detect a 33% relative reduction in mortality (from 12% to 8%) at 80% power and two-sided α=0.05
- Result: in-hospital mortality was 13% with artesunate vs. 21% with quinine (OR 0.59, 95% CI 0.44-0.79, p=0.0002); the supportive African pediatric trial AQUAMAT showed 8.5% vs. 10.9% mortality (OR 0.75, 95% CI 0.63-0.90, p=0.0022)
- Interim-monitoring issue flagged by FDA: the trial's DSMC (chaired by Prof. T. Peto) conducted an unplanned first interim analysis after 659 patients and a second after 1,294 patients (two-thirds of the planned 2,000), at which point the trial was stopped early (p=0.0007) — but "the protocol did not provide a formal pre-specified plan to control the Type 1 error and there were no formal stopping rules pre-specified." FDA's statistical reviewer independently checked whether the observed result would have crossed a standard O'Brien-Fleming or Haybittle-Peto boundary (it would have) before accepting the trial's early-stopped result as reliable
- FDA's benefit-risk conclusion rested on the trial's post-hoc application of a modified severe-malaria case definition (Hien et al. 1996) to the randomized ITT population, given that not all randomized patients ultimately met strict severe-malaria criteria on blood-smear review

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2020/213036Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2020/213036s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/213036Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — none; SEAQUAMAT predates routine trial registration and has no NCT number
- Protocol / SAP — not separately posted; FDA's Multi-Discipline Review quotes the SEAQUAMAT protocol/SAP and Clinical Study Report directly (see excerpts below)
- Pivotal publication: Dondorp A, Nosten F, Stepniewska K, Day N, White N (South East Asian Quinine Artesunate Malaria Trial group). "Artesunate versus quinine for treatment of severe falciparum malaria: a randomised trial." *Lancet.* 2005;366(9487):717-725. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(05)67176-0>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16125588/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Artesunate%20versus%20quinine%20treatment%20severe%20falciparum%20malaria%20randomised%20trial)

**Other resources**

- IV artesunate had been available in the US for years before this approval only via a CDC-run expanded-access IND (protocol CDC-060); FDA also reviewed CDC-060's uncontrolled, retrospective safety data as part of this NDA.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting is recorded for this application in the reviewed documents.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Statistical Review, describing the SEAQUAMAT protocol/SAP, p.100-101]*

> "In the protocol, Kaplan-Meier plots and Cox's regression analysis were specified for the primary and secondary outcome variables. In the SAP, Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) method was specified for the primary efficacy analysis in the ITT population, stratified by site (hospital). The relative risk and odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) would be calculated... A sample size of 2000 was calculated for a detection of a 33% reduction in mortality from 12% to 8% with a statistical power of 80% and a two-sided Type I error of 5%, allowing a drop-out rate of 5%."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Statistical Review, interim-monitoring critique, p.101]*

> "According to the CSR, the protocol specified an interim analysis by an external Data Safety Monitoring Committee (DSMC) after inclusion of 500 patients and subsequently at time points chosen by the committee. The protocol did not provide a formal pre-specified plan to control the Type 1 error and there were no formal stopping rules pre-specified... The primary endpoint was planned to be analyzed with a two-tailed test with a Type I error =0.05 at the final analysis with the planned sample size. There was no consideration for Type I error control due to the interim analyses. The method used to control the Type I error should have been prespecified in the analysis plan of the study. The Applicant considered this for the interim analyses and claimed that the test statistic would have crossed the stopping boundary had either of two commonly used stopping criteria been proposed, the O'Brien-Fleming or the Haybittle-Peto procedure with 3 to 5 interim analyses planned."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Executive Summary]*

> "IV artesunate was superior to IV quinine, the standard of care when the study was conducted, for the treatment of severe malaria in a single, randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial in adults and pediatric patients in Southeast Asia (SEAQUAMAT)... In SEAQUAMAT, which enrolled patients two years of age and older with severe malaria, in-hospital mortality was 13% in artesunate recipients compared to 21% in quinine recipients [OR 0.59, 95% CI (0.44, 0.79), p=0.0002]."

### 56. Fostemsavir (Rukobia) — NDA 212950

**Sponsor:** ViiV Healthcare

**Indication approved:** In combination with other antiretrovirals, for adults with HIV-1 infection who are heavily treatment-experienced with multidrug-resistant HIV-1 failing their current antiretroviral regimen due to resistance, intolerance, or safety considerations

**Approval date:** July 2, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** BRIGHTE, NCT02362503

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized non-comparative dose-regimen cohort design ("randomized functional-monotherapy lead-in with non-randomized expansion cohort" — a randomized, placebo-controlled cohort assessing a brief blinded functional-monotherapy period, paired with a separate non-randomized open-label cohort for patients with no remaining fully active background options), randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (Randomized Cohort only)
- *Endpoints:* log10 change in plasma HIV-1 RNA from Day 1 to Day 8 (primary, Randomized Cohort); proportion with HIV-1 RNA decline >0.5 log10 and >1.0 log10 at Day 8 (key secondary); durability of virologic response (HIV-1 RNA <40 copies/mL) at Weeks 24, 48, 96 via FDA Snapshot algorithm
- *Primary analysis:* one-way analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) with baseline log10 HIV-1 RNA as covariate
- *Missing data/bias:* Day 1 observation carried forward for subjects without an on-treatment Day 8 value; last observation carried forward for subjects with an early value before the Day 8 window; FDA Snapshot algorithm (per FDA antiretroviral guidance) counting missed visits, discontinuations, and efficacy-driven regimen changes as failures for the durability analyses
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval-style reliance on a short (8-day) blinded functional-monotherapy period layered onto an open-label extension, in a heavily treatment-experienced population with few remaining active agents

**Trial design & endpoints**

- BRIGHTE enrolled heavily treatment-experienced adults with multidrug-resistant HIV-1 into two cohorts: a Randomized Cohort (patients with 1-2 remaining fully active antiretroviral classes, N≈272, randomized 3:1 to blinded fostemsavir (FTR) 600 mg BID or placebo, each added to a failing regimen for 8 days) and a Non-randomized Cohort (patients with no remaining fully active options, open-label FTR plus optimized background therapy from Day 1)
- Primary efficacy endpoint (Randomized Cohort only): log10 change in plasma HIV-1 RNA from Day 1 to Day 8 of blinded functional monotherapy, using the HIV-1 RNA value within a window of Day 6-10
- After Day 8, both randomized-cohort arms transitioned to open-label FTR plus optimized background therapy (OBT); key secondary/durability endpoints (viral suppression <40 copies/mL by FDA Snapshot algorithm) were then assessed at Weeks 24, 48, and 96 across both cohorts, pooled, since "the brief 8-day randomized period is not anticipated to change the [later durability] outcome"
- Sample size: at least 140 subjects were planned to be randomized 3:1 to FTR or placebo for the Day 8 primary analysis; all statistical tests were performed at the two-sided 0.05 alpha level
- Primary analysis method: one-way ANCOVA with log10 HIV-1 RNA change from Day 1 to Day 8 as the dependent variable, treatment as the independent variable, and log10 Day 1 HIV-1 RNA as a continuous covariate; missing Day 8 values imputed via Day 1 observation carried forward (if no on-treatment value) or last observation carried forward (if an earlier on-treatment value existed)
- Result: FTR was superior to placebo in reducing HIV-1 RNA during the 8-day blinded period; durability results at Week 96 (all subjects on open-label FTR + OBT by then) showed viral suppression maintained in a majority of subjects despite most having had a suboptimal Day-8 monotherapy response, which FDA's review called "a testament" to the value of adding FTR to a fully reconstructed background regimen rather than evidence from the brief comparative period alone

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2020/212950Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2020/212950s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Integrated Review (combined clinical/statistical review template) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/212950Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02362503 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)
- Pivotal publication: Kozal M, Aberg J, Pialoux G, et al. "Fostemsavir in Adults with Multidrug-Resistant HIV-1 Infection." *N Engl J Med.* 2020;382(13):1232-1243. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1902493), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32212519/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Fostemsavir%20Adults%20Multidrug-Resistant%20HIV-1%20Infection%20Kozal)

**Other resources**

- ViiV/GSK's general participation in trial-specific IPD-sharing programs (e.g., ClinicalStudyDataRequest.com) was not individually confirmed for this trial.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting is recorded for this application in the reviewed documents.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, Statistical Review section, primary analysis description]*

> "The primary efficacy endpoint was assessed in the Randomized Cohort. The study was designed to show superior antiviral activity of FTR compared to placebo when combined with a failing regimen over a period of 8 days. At least 140 subjects were planned to be randomized 3:1 to FTR or placebo. Log10 HIV-1 RNA change from Day 1 to Day 8 was calculated using the HIV-1 RNA value closest to Day 8, and within an analysis visit window inclusive of Day 6 through Day 10 of blinded treatment. All tests were performed at the two-sided 0.05 alpha level... The primary efficacy analysis of the primary endpoint fit a one-way analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) with log10 HIV-1 RNA change from Day 1 at Day 8 as the dependent variable, treatment (FTR or placebo) as an independent variable, and log10 Day 1 HIV-1 RNA as a continuous covariate. Missing HIV-1 RNA values at Day 8 were imputed using (a) Day 1 Observation Carried Forward for subjects without a value during blinded treatment (i.e., imputing a zero change from Day 1), and (b) last observation carried forward (LOCF) for subjects with an early value during blinded treatment before the Day 8 analysis visit window."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, durability-analysis methodology]*

> "The durability of virologic response (HIV-1 RNA <40, <200, and <400 copies/mL) at Week 24, 48, and 96 was assessed using the FDA Snapshot algorithm... During the course of the trial, changes in OBT were permitted. Subjects without an HIV-1 RNA value at a relevant time point due to missed visits or discontinuation or subjects who changed OBT due to lack of efficacy were counted as treatment failures."

### 57. Abametapir (Xeglyze) — NDA 206966

**Sponsor:** Hatchtech Pty Ltd (originator, IND holder, and sponsor of the pivotal Phase 3 program); ownership of the application was transferred to Dr. Reddy's Laboratories, S.A. before the September 2015 NDA submission, and the approved NDA is currently held by LNHC (successor sponsor)

**Indication approved:** Topical treatment of head lice infestation (Pediculosis capitis) in patients 6 months of age and older

**Approval date:** July 24, 2020 (original NDA submitted September 14, 2015; Complete Response Letter issued for a manufacturing-facility inspection deficiency; approved on resubmission)

**Pivotal trial:** Trials Ha03-001 and Ha03-002 ("Trial 001" and "Trial 002"), two identical Phase 3 studies; no NCT numbers with posted protocol/SAP documents (NCT02062060 and NCT02060903)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, multicenter, vehicle-controlled, two identical confirmatory Phase 3 trials conducted under a Special Protocol Assessment (SPA)
- *Endpoints:* proportion of index subjects lice-free at all follow-up visits through Day 14 (Days 1, 7, and 14)
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by pooled site
- *Missing data/bias:* protocol-specified imputation of missing Day-14 assessments as treatment failures
- *Regulatory:* Special Protocol Assessment (SPA)-agreed primary endpoint; Complete Response Letter followed by resubmission and approval (CRL driven by a manufacturing-site inspection finding at the sponsor's facility, not by clinical/statistical deficiencies)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Trials 001 and 002 were identical randomized, double-blind, multicenter, vehicle-controlled Phase 3 trials in subjects ≥6 months old with active head lice infestation (≥3 live lice for the index/youngest household subject, ≥1 live louse for other household members), N=108 (Trial 001) and N=108 (Trial 002)
- Primary endpoint (SPA-agreed): proportion of index subjects who were lice-free at all follow-up visits through Day 14 (Days 1, 7, 14); the SAP specified that any live lice detected at any post-treatment clinic visit (including unscheduled visits) classified a subject as a treatment failure
- Statistical method: CMH test stratified by pooled study site, comparing abametapir vs. vehicle lotion; the protocol-specified imputation rule treated missing Day-14 assessments as treatment failures
- A supportive in vitro ovicidal study (Study 008) assessed egg viability after ex vivo exposure, but FDA had previously cautioned (Pre-NDA meeting, January 2015) that "the ovicidal activity observed ex-vivo may not predict the ovicidal activity observed in-vivo," limiting its regulatory weight
- Results: primary endpoint success was 43/53 (81%) with abametapir vs. 28/55 (51%) with vehicle in Trial 001 (p=0.001), and 45/55 (82%) vs. 25/53 (47%) in Trial 002 (p<0.001)
- FDA's statistical reviewer concluded "there were no major statistical issues affecting the overall conclusions" for the two pivotal trials
- Regulatory history: the original NDA (submitted by Dr. Reddy's Laboratories, S.A., which had received a "Transfer of Ownership of an Application" from Hatchtech Pty Ltd) received a Complete Response Letter after an FDA facility inspection found deficiencies at a Dr. Reddy's manufacturing unit; the clinical/statistical package itself was not the basis for the CRL. The applicant resubmitted in November 2019 with no new clinical data, and the application was approved in 2020 once manufacturing-facility issues were resolved

### 58. Nifurtimox (Lampit) — NDA 213464

**Sponsor:** Bayer HealthCare LLC

**Indication approved:** Treatment of Chagas disease (American trypanosomiasis) caused by *Trypanosoma cruzi* in pediatric patients (originally birth to <18 years and <40 kg body weight)

**Approval date:** August 6, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** CHICO (Study 16027 / BAY A2502), NCT02625974

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial (historically-controlled; prospective, historically controlled study rather than a randomized comparison), randomized non-comparative dose-regimen cohort design (60-day vs. 30-day nifurtimox regimens compared to each other and, separately, to historical placebo)
- *Endpoints:* sero-reduction (≥20% decrease in optical density) or sero-conversion (negative IgG) at 12 months post-treatment by conventional ELISA serology, treated as a binary cure/no-cure primary variable
- *Primary analysis:* one-sample asymptotic 2-sided 95% CI with continuity correction (1/2n) for a single proportion, compared against a historical-control threshold derived from two published placebo-controlled trials
- *Multiplicity:* none formally applied; a secondary dose-comparison (60-day vs. 30-day) used its own separate CI for the difference of two proportions
- *Missing data/bias:* sensitivity analyses re-classifying indeterminate/missing serology as treatment failure vs. exclusion; FDA reviewer disagreement on whether pooling two distinct "conventional" ELISA tests (TPA lysate and recombinant) into a single averaged primary endpoint was appropriate, given the two tests' imperfect correlation (r=0.697)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- CHICO (Part 1) was a prospective, single-arm, historically-controlled trial in patients 0-17 years old with chronic Chagas disease, randomized only between two nifurtimox dosing durations (30-day, N=111, and 60-day, N=219 in the Full Analysis Set), with no concurrent placebo arm; historical placebo cure rates were derived from two published pediatric trials (de Andrade et al. 1996: 5% [1-13%]; Sosa et al. 1998: 5% [1-16%])
- Primary efficacy variable: sero-reduction (≥20% average decrease in optical density across two conventional ELISA tests) or sero-conversion (both tests negative), assessed at 12 months post-treatment as a binary cure/no-cure outcome
- Primary analysis: an asymptotic 2-sided 95% CI (with a 1/(2n) continuity correction) for the proportion of 60-day-regimen subjects achieving cure; superiority over the historical placebo rate was to be confirmed if the lower CI bound exceeded 16% (the higher of the two published trials' upper 95% CI bounds)
- Sample size: 260 subjects in the 60-day regimen (assuming a 55% true cure rate per Guhl et al.) gave 99% power for the lower 95% CI bound to exceed 16%; 130 additional subjects were enrolled in a 30-day regimen for a secondary dose-comparison
- Result: cure rate was 32.9% (72/219, FAS) in the 60-day regimen, 95% CI (26.4%, 39.3%) — well above the 16% historical-control threshold — and 18.9% (21/111) in the 30-day regimen, 95% CI (11.2%, 26.7%); the 60-day vs. 30-day dose-response difference was statistically significant (FAS p=0.0043)
- FDA statistical reviewer's methodological critique: the Applicant's primary analysis averaged optical-density reduction across two separate "conventional" ELISA assays (TPA lysate and recombinant), but FDA's own analysis found the two assays' reduction rates correlated only 0.697 with each other and "detect different kinds of antibodies," concluding "we did not consider it appropriate to pool results from two different 'conventional' ELISA tests as was done for the Applicant's primary efficacy endpoint," and presented each test's results separately as a sensitivity analysis

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2020/213464s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/213464Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf

- Pivotal publication: Altcheh J, Bisio M, Lattner J, et al. "Prospective, historically controlled study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of a new paediatric formulation of nifurtimox in children aged 0 to 17 years with Chagas disease one year after treatment (CHICO)." *PLoS Negl Trop Dis.* 2021;15(1):e0008912. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pntd.0008912), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33412557/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Prospective%20historically%20controlled%20study%20nifurtimox%20children%20Chagas%20disease%20CHICO)

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, CHICO Statistical Analysis Plan, BAY No. A2502/IMPACT No. 16027, §6.2.1.1 "Primary efficacy variable and analysis," p.17-18]*

> "The primary efficacy variable will be sero-reduction (defined as a ≥ 20% reduction in optical density [OD]) or sero-conversion (defined as negative Immunoglobulin G [IgG] concentration) in the 60-day regimen group at 12 months post-treatment using two conventional ELISA serology tests... Both publications show a 5% cure rate for the placebo group. For the primary objective in our study, superiority over placebo will be confirmed if the lower limit of the 95% CI for the nifurtimox (60-day regimen) cure rate is greater than 16%, the larger of the upper limits of the 95% CIs from the two publications."

*[verbatim, CHICO SAP, §6.5 "Determination of sample size," p.20]*

> "According to Guhl et al., nifurtimox 12 months post-treatment cure rate is about 55%, with a sample size of 260 for the 60-day regimen, the power is 99% for the lower limit of the 95% CI to be greater than 16%. The number of subjects in the 30-day treatment regimen is based on the width of a 95% CI for the difference of two proportions."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Statistical Reviewer's comment on the primary endpoint's ELISA-pooling method]*

> "The relationship between recombinant ELISA values and antibody titers is not linear... For this reason, comparison to a historical control rate on change in optical density for the ELISA serologic tests is difficult to interpret... The correlation of the two separate reduction rates is 0.697. Also note that the two 'conventional' ELISA tests detect different kinds of antibodies. Based on this information, we did not consider it appropriate to pool results from two different 'conventional' ELISA tests as was done for the Applicant's primary efficacy endpoint. We present the results for each of the individual ELISA tests."

### 59. Atoltivimab/maftivimab/odesivimab-ebgn (Inmazeb) — BLA 761169

**Sponsor:** Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of infection caused by Zaire ebolavirus in adult and pediatric patients, including neonates born to a mother positive for Zaire ebolavirus infection

**Approval date:** October 14, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** PALM (Pamoja Tulinde Maisha), NCT03719586

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, controlled trial with response-adaptive elements conducted during an active outbreak (multi-outbreak, open-label, 4-arm then interim-narrowed randomized controlled trial); real-world/outbreak-embedded pragmatic RCT design
- *Endpoints:* 28-day all-cause mortality (primary); mortality through Day 58, time-to-death, time-to-viral-clearance, time-to-discharge-eligibility (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* Boschloo's exact two-tailed test at α=0.05 for each pairwise comparison to control, with no multiple-comparison adjustment across the multiple experimental arms
- *Multiplicity:* unadjusted secondary/supportive testing (single formal primary endpoint) — the trial's SAP explicitly rejected multiplicity adjustment across arms as inappropriate given the outbreak setting and distinct manufacturers per arm
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Data and Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) review with a non-standard, less-conservative type-I-error approach (α=0.05 two-tailed per comparison, explicitly chosen over stricter conventions given outbreak urgency); trial stopped early for two arms after an interim analysis showed superior survival with mAb114 and REGN-EB3 vs. ZMapp
- *Regulatory:* approval based on a randomized controlled trial conducted collaboratively by NIH/NIAID, WHO, and DRC health authorities during a live Ebola outbreak, rather than a conventional sponsor-run registration trial

**Trial design & endpoints**

- PALM was a multicenter, multi-outbreak, randomized, controlled, open-label trial conducted during the 2018-2020 Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo; the trial began as a 3-arm design (November 2018) and was amended to a 4-arm design in December 2018, randomizing patients with confirmed Ebola virus disease 1:1:1:1 to ZMapp (control), remdesivir, mAb114 (ansuvimab), or REGN-EB3 (atoltivimab/maftivimab/odesivimab, i.e., Inmazeb)
- Primary hypothesis: the 28-day mortality rate of each investigational arm would be lower than that of the ZMapp control arm; the SAP explicitly used Boschloo's exact test rather than Fisher's exact test "due to less conservative small-sample performance," anticipating early interim looks with limited patient numbers
- Multiplicity approach (unusual for a registration trial): the SAP states there would be "no multiple comparison adjustment for the fact that multiple experimental arms are compared with the control," reasoning that "the products in this trial are made by different manufacturers, so one could view the comparisons almost like separate trials," and citing PREVAIL II's precedent of allowing a higher-than-usual type-I error rate in this disease setting
- Planned sample size: up to 725 randomized subjects across outbreaks; the trial was stopped for the ZMapp and remdesivir arms in August 2019 on a DSMB recommendation after an interim analysis showed both mAb114 and REGN-EB3 had superior mortality outcomes compared to ZMapp, and remaining patients were randomized only between mAb114 and REGN-EB3
- Result (final concurrent ITT analysis, REGN-EB3 vs. ZMapp): 28-day mortality was 52/159 (32.7%) with REGN-EB3 vs. 84/169 (49.7%) with ZMapp, a difference of -17.0 percentage points (95% CI -27.5, -4.6), p=0.0020; roughly two-thirds of deaths in both arms occurred within the first 3 days of treatment

**Other resources**

- Trial governance involved NIAID/NIH, WHO, DRC's INRB, and multiple NGOs (MSF, ALIMA, IMC); no conventional commercial IPD-sharing program applies given the trial's public-health-emergency, multi-institutional sponsorship.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, 2018 Ebola MCM RCT Protocol, v7.0, "Less strict error rate control," p.39]*

> "Most clinical trials that intend to provide definitive evidence opt for strict control of the two-tailed type 1 error rate at level 0.05, with adjustments for multiple comparisons of arms. This necessitates larger sample sizes to ensure high power. The current circumstances of high mortality, intermittent outbreaks, and the need to find effective treatments as quickly as possible argue for less austere statistical penalties. As a result, the current trial will use Boschloo's exact two-tailed tests at alpha=0.05 for each pairwise comparison. There will be no multiple comparison adjustment for the fact that multiple experimental arms are compared with the control... The products in this trial are made by different manufacturers, so one could view the comparisons almost like separate trials."

*[verbatim, 2018 Ebola MCM RCT Protocol, "Study hypotheses and statistical analysis," p.39]*

> "The primary hypothesis is that the 28-day mortality rate of the investigational arms will be lower than that of the control arm. Boschloo's test will be used to evaluate the primary hypothesis. For comparison of a given arm to control, two-tailed tests will be used. Note that an exact procedure was chosen in anticipation of early looks with limited numbers. Boschloo's test was chosen over Fisher's exact test due to less conservative small-sample performance."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Efficacy Results]*

> "[28-day mortality, ITT Overall population]: 52/159 (32.7%) REGN-EB3 vs. 84/169 (49.7%) ZMapp, difference -17.0 (95% CI: -27.5, -4.6), p=0.0020."
