### 60. Remdesivir (Veklury) — NDA 214787

**Sponsor:** Gilead Sciences, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of COVID-19 in adults and pediatric patients requiring hospitalization

**Approval date:** October 22, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** ACTT-1 (Adaptive COVID-19 Treatment Trial), NIH/NIAID-sponsored (DMID Protocol 20-0006), NCT04280705

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven trial; NIH/NIAID-sponsored government trial (not industry-run) supporting a commercial NDA
- *Endpoints:* time to recovery through Day 29 (primary; recovery = clinical status 8-point ordinal scale score of 1, 2, or 3); clinical status on the 8-point ordinal scale at Day 15 (originally the primary endpoint, later changed to key secondary); 14- and 28-day all-cause mortality
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test (stratified by baseline disease-severity category), stratified Cox proportional-hazards model for the "recovery rate ratio" (a hazard ratio for a favorable rather than unfavorable event), Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Mid-trial SAP amendment changing endpoint status:* the original primary endpoint (Day 15 ordinal-scale score, analyzed via proportional-odds model) was changed to time-to-recovery while the trial was ongoing but still blinded, a change FDA's statistical reviewer found not to raise "problematic statistical properties because the modification was made independently of comparative data from the trial"
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function, O'Brien-Fleming boundary (two one-sided boundaries at level 0.025 each), event-driven interim efficacy review planned at ~50% information fraction (computed as recoveries observed / 400 target recoveries)
- *Regulatory:* interim results were disclosed publicly by NIAID (April 29, 2020 news release) before the trial's planned final analysis, "due to the urgent public health imperative presented by the COVID-19 pandemic"; per the SAP amendment, "the timing of the final analyses was modified from the original plan" following discussions with FDA

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ACTT-1 randomized 1,062 hospitalized adults with COVID-19 1:1 to remdesivir or placebo, stratified by baseline disease severity (mild-moderate vs. severe); this was an event-driven trial with sample size based on the number of "recovery" events observed rather than a fixed enrollment target
- Primary efficacy endpoint: time to recovery through Day 29, where recovery was defined as a clinical status 8-point ordinal scale score of 1 ("not hospitalized, no limitations"), 2, or 3; analyzed via a stratified log-rank test, with the "recovery rate ratio" (functionally a hazard ratio) and its CI estimated from a stratified Cox proportional-hazards model
- Sample size: ~400 recovery events were targeted for 85% power to detect a recovery rate ratio of 1.35, using a two-sided log-rank test at α=0.05; per the sample-size formula in the SAP, E ≈ 4(1.96+z_β)²/[ln(θ)]²
- Interim monitoring: a single interim efficacy analysis was planned at ~50% information fraction (t = r/400 recoveries), using the Lan-DeMets spending-function analog of the O'Brien-Fleming boundary with an overall two-sided type-I error of 0.05 (two one-sided 0.025 boundaries); interim results were presented to the DSMB on April 27, 2020, and — per DSMB recommendation — disclosed to blinded NIAID leadership and then publicly announced April 29, 2020, before the trial's originally planned final analysis, given the pandemic's urgency; the SAP's version 3.0 amendment, written after this disclosure, states "the timing of the final analyses was modified from the original plan" following discussion with FDA
- Endpoint history: the trial's original primary endpoint was the Day 15 8-point ordinal scale (proportional-odds model); this was changed to time-to-recovery while the study remained blinded, which FDA's statistical reviewer concluded "did not lead to problematic statistical properties because the modification was made independently of comparative data from the trial" — the Day 15 ordinal-scale analysis was retained as a key secondary endpoint
- Result: median time to recovery was 10 days with remdesivir vs. 15 days with placebo, recovery rate ratio 1.29 (95% CI 1.12-1.49, p<0.001); a key secondary ordinal-scale endpoint and Kaplan-Meier mortality trends also favored remdesivir, though FDA's review noted "remaining uncertainty regarding the treatment effect on all-cause mortality"
- FDA's review separately flagged two open-label, Gilead-sponsored supportive trials (comparing 5-day vs. 10-day remdesivir regimens) as limited by "receipt of the statistical analysis plan after release of results" and, for one of the two, "receipt of the statistical analysis plan and corresponding method multiplicity control after release of topline results" — a data-integrity caveat that did not apply to ACTT-1 itself

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2020/214787Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2020/214787Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/214787Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04280705
- Study Protocol (posted) — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/05/NCT04280705/Prot_001.pdf
- Statistical Analysis Plan v3.0, 29-May-2020 (posted) — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/05/NCT04280705/SAP_002.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Beigel JH, Tomashek KM, Dodd LE, et al. (ACTT-1 Study Group Members). "Remdesivir for the Treatment of Covid-19 — Final Report." *N Engl J Med.* 2020;383(19):1813-1826 (originally published as a preliminary report May 22, 2020). [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2007764), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32445440/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Remdesivir%20Treatment%20Covid-19%20Final%20Report%20ACTT-1)

**Other resources**

- ACTT-1 was designed and run by NIH/NIAID as a public-sector platform trial; individual-participant data are accessible through NIAID/BARDA-affiliated data-sharing mechanisms rather than a commercial-sponsor IPD portal.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting is recorded for this application in the reviewed documents; review proceeded on an expedited basis given the COVID-19 public health emergency.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, ACTT-1 Statistical Analysis Plan v3.0, DMID Protocol 20-0006, 29-May-2020, introductory note, p.9-10]*

> "The version 3.0 amendment to this SAP was written after the interim analysis results were presented to the DSMB on April 27, 2020. Per DSMB recommendation, the results were then provided to blinded NIAID study leadership. Due to the urgent public health imperative presented by the COVID-19 pandemic, the interim efficacy results were disclosed publicly (NIAID April 29, 2020 News Release). Per discussions with the FDA, the timing of the final analyses was modified from the original plan (see Section 6.2)."

*[verbatim, ACTT-1 SAP v3.0, §6.6.2 "Interim Efficacy Review," p.33]*

> "Interim efficacy analyses will be conducted after at approximately 50% of total information. The information fraction at an interim analysis will be computed as t = r/400, where r is the number of recoveries by the time of the data freeze date for the interim analysis. The Lan-DeMets spending function analog of the O'Brien-Fleming boundary will be used to monitor the primary endpoint using an overall two-sided type-I error rate of 0.05."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, describing the endpoint change]*

> "For the key secondary endpoint of the Day 15 ordinal scale, the analysis was to be conducted using a proportional odds model that included terms for treatment and baseline disease severity (mild-to-moderate versus severe). As noted above, this was the original primary endpoint. The endpoint was changed while the study was ongoing but remained blinded, and this did not lead to problematic statistical properties because the modification was made independently of comparative data from the trial."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, ACTT-1 primary result]*

> "Time to recovery was significantly faster in the remdesivir group than the placebo group (recovery rate ratio 1.29; 95% CI: 1.12 to 1.49; p<0.001). There were several complexities to the time to recovery primary analysis related to the handling of deaths in the analysis, the handling of relapses or readmissions following discharge, and a change in the primary endpoint during the trial. However, results also strongly favored remdesivir for a key secondary efficacy endpoint based on analysis of an ordinal scale at Day 15, which was less affected by these issues and had been the originally specified primary endpoint."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, on the two supportive Gilead-sponsored open-label trials]*

> "This trial was limited by potential open-label effects, a high degree of imputed data for the primary endpoint, and receipt of the statistical analysis plan after release of results."

### 61. Ansuvimab-zykl (Ebanga) — BLA 761172

**Sponsor:** Ridgeback Biotherapeutics

**Indication approved:** Treatment of infection caused by Zaire ebolavirus in adults and pediatric patients, including neonates born to a mother who is RT-PCR positive for Zaire ebolavirus infection

**Approval date:** December 21, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** PALM (PAmoja TuLinde Maisha), NCT03719586 — a four-arm randomized platform trial in the Democratic Republic of the Congo conducted jointly with NIAID; the same trial (and the same shared ZMapp control arm) also supported atoltivimab/maftivimab/odesivimab-ebgn (Inmazeb), approved a few months earlier in October 2020, via the REGN-EB3 arm

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* multi-arm adaptive platform trial with response-adaptive arm dropping via DSMB, randomized, open-label, active-controlled, event-driven trial
- *Endpoints:* 28-day all-cause mortality (binary primary responder-type endpoint)
- *Primary analysis:* Boschloo's exact test (unconditional exact test for two binomial proportions)
- *Multiplicity:* no multiplicity adjustment across multiple experimental arms vs. shared control, each pairwise comparison treated as a separate trial
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Data Monitoring Committee (DMC/DSMB), early-stopped for efficacy (two of four arms, at the fourth interim analysis)
- *Regulatory:* cross-referenced pivotal trial shared with a separately approved BLA (Inmazeb/atoltivimab-maftivimab-odesivimab)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- PALM was a randomized, controlled, open-label platform trial run in Ebola Treatment Units in the Democratic Republic of the Congo during the 2018-2020 Kivu outbreak, comparing four investigational arms — ZMapp (shared control, chosen because it was the most-studied prior candidate from PREVAIL II), remdesivir, ansuvimab-zykl (mAb114/Ebanga), and atoltivimab/maftivimab/odesivimab (REGN-EB3/Inmazeb) — in patients with RT-PCR-confirmed Zaire ebolavirus disease
- Randomization was 1:1:1:1 across arms with equal allocation continuing to the retained arms after two arms (ZMapp, remdesivir) were dropped at the fourth interim DSMB look; the concurrent intent-to-treat (cITT) population (all randomized subjects excluding a small number re-randomized due to drug unavailability/quarantine) was the primary efficacy population, comprising 174 ansuvimab-zykl and 168 ZMapp patients
- Primary endpoint: 28-day all-cause mortality; a 10-day mortality rate was used operationally at the interim analysis because it was shown to closely track the 28-day rate (most deaths occurred by Day 11)
- Key secondary endpoint: mortality distributed by study day; safety and viral clearance were also assessed
- Sample size/power: no fixed target size was pre-specified in the traditional sense — the trial used an open-ended, event-driven group-sequential design with repeated Boschloo's-test interim looks; by the time of DSMB-directed early stopping of two arms, 499 participants had been enrolled with ≥10 days of follow-up
- Statistical methods: the protocol explicitly rejected the conventional two-sided alpha=0.05 with multiplicity adjustment in favor of an unadjusted two-sided Boschloo's exact test at alpha=0.05 for each experimental-arm-vs.-control pairwise comparison, reasoning that with multiple manufacturers involved the comparisons were "almost like separate trials"; the final analysis (fifth interim look) used the interim monitoring boundary, requiring a two-sided p<0.028 for significance

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2020/761172s000lbl.pdf

- Pivotal publication: Mulangu S, et al. "A Randomized, Controlled Trial of Ebola Virus Disease Therapeutics." *N Engl J Med.* 2019;381:2293-2303. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1910993), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31774950/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=A%20Randomized%20Controlled%20Trial%20of%20Ebola%20Virus%20Disease%20Therapeutics)

**Other resources**

- No IPD/dataset access program (Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere) was individually confirmed for PALM; the trial was run as a multi-partner public health response (NIAID, INRB, WHO, and industry partners) rather than a conventional sponsor-run registration trial.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting is recorded for this application.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, PALM Protocol §6 "Statistical Considerations," version 7.0, 4 October 2019, p.39]*

> "Most clinical trials that intend to provide definitive evidence opt for strict control of the two-tailed type 1 error rate at level 0.05, with adjustments for multiple comparisons of arms. This necessitates larger sample sizes to ensure high power. The current circumstances of high mortality, intermittent outbreaks, and the need to find effective treatments as quickly as possible argue for less austere statistical penalties. As a result, the current trial will use Boschloo's exact two-tailed tests at alpha=0.05 for each pairwise comparison. There will be no multiple comparison adjustment for the fact that multiple experimental arms are compared with the control... The products in this trial are made by different manufacturers, so one could view the comparisons almost like separate trials."

*[verbatim, PALM Protocol §6, "Study hypotheses and statistical analysis," p.39]*

> "The primary hypothesis is that the 28-day mortality rate of the investigational arms will be lower than that of the control arm. Boschloo's test will be used to evaluate the primary hypothesis... Note that an exact procedure was chosen in anticipation of early looks with limited numbers. Boschloo's test was chosen over Fisher's exact test due to less conservative small-sample performance."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.3 "Statistical Analysis Plan," p.25]*

> "An independent DSMB actively monitored interim data to make recommendations about early study closure or changes to study arms. During the fourth interim analysis, the trial results crossed the prespecified efficacy boundary and the DSMB decided to stop dosing with ZMapp and another treatment (remdesivir), but to continue ansuvimab-zykl and the other treatment arm (REGN-EB3)... The final analysis occurred at the fifth interim analysis, and the corresponding interim monitoring boundary was used to assess significance. Thus, a p-value of <0.028 (two-sided) for the comparison of ansuvimab-zykl to ZMapp was required to claim statistical significance for the primary endpoint."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, Table 12, p.28]*

> "Concurrent ITT — Ansuvimab-zykl 61/174 (35.1%) deaths, ZMapp 83/168 (49.4%) deaths, Rate Difference -14.4% (95% CI: -24.8, -2.4), Boschloo's two-sided P-value 0.0075... The Applicant's results were used in the label."

### 62. Cabotegravir/rilpivirine (Cabenuva) — NDA 212888 (cabotegravir extended-release injectable suspension) / NDA 212887 (rilpivirine extended-release injectable suspension)

**Sponsor:** ViiV Healthcare (cabotegravir); Janssen Pharmaceuticals (rilpivirine), co-reviewed and co-approved as a combined regimen

**Indication approved:** Complete long-acting injectable regimen (administered monthly) for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in adults, to replace a current antiretroviral regimen in those who are virologically suppressed (HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL) on a stable regimen, with no history of treatment failure and no known/suspected resistance to either cabotegravir or rilpivirine — the first complete long-acting injectable regimen approved for HIV-1

**Approval date:** January 21, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** FLAIR, NCT02938520 (oral-induction-then-switch design), and ATLAS, NCT02951052 (direct switch from a stable oral regimen)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled, cross-trial pooled/integrated analysis (FLAIR + ATLAS pooled for the 4% margin, stratified across 10 combined strata)
- *Endpoints:* virologic non-response by FDA Snapshot algorithm (HIV-1 RNA ≥50 copies/mL at Week 48)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Bayesian posterior predictive probability futility monitoring at ~50% of subjects reaching Week 24, with no alpha spent because no hypothesis test was conducted and the Applicant remained blinded

**Trial design & endpoints**

- FLAIR (treatment-naive population) and ATLAS (treatment-experienced, virologically suppressed population) were near-identically designed randomized (1:1), open-label, active-controlled, multicenter, non-inferiority Phase III trials; FLAIR first induced subjects to virologic suppression on oral ABC/DTG/3TC before randomizing to switch to monthly IM cabotegravir + rilpivirine (CAB+RPV) vs. continuing oral ART, while ATLAS randomized already-suppressed subjects directly
- Randomization stratification: baseline HIV-1 RNA (<100,000 vs. ≥100,000 copies/mL) and sex at birth (FLAIR); baseline third-agent class (INSTI/NNRTI/PI) and sex at birth (ATLAS)
- Primary endpoint: proportion of subjects with HIV-1 RNA ≥50 copies/mL at Week 48 (FDA Snapshot algorithm), ITT-exposed population, individually for each trial and pooled
- Key secondary endpoint: virologic success (HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL) at Week 48, tested against a -10% non-inferiority margin
- Sample size/power: 285 subjects/arm per individual trial gave 97% power for a 6% non-inferiority margin; a pooled 570 subjects/arm gave 90% power for a 4% margin, all at one-sided alpha=0.025
- Interim monitoring: an unblinded IDMC reviewed accumulating efficacy data at ~50% of subjects reaching Week 24 using a Bayesian posterior-predictive-probability futility rule; because no formal hypothesis test was conducted, no alpha was spent, and the Applicant itself remained blinded throughout
- Homogeneity of the pooled treatment effect across the ten combined randomization strata was checked with a Breslow-Day test (p=0.2, consistent effect)

- Pivotal publication (ATLAS): Swindells S, et al. "Long-Acting Cabotegravir and Rilpivirine for Maintenance of HIV-1 Suppression." *N Engl J Med.* 2020;382:1112-1123. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1904398), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32130809/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Long-Acting%20Cabotegravir%20and%20Rilpivirine%20for%20Maintenance%20of%20HIV-1%20Suppression)

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting is recorded for this application.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §6.3.3 "Statistical Analysis Plan," p.68]*

> "The Applicant and the review division agreed on the FLAIR and ATLAS statistical analysis plan (SAP) prior to the trial completion. The target sample size of 285 subjects per arm for both FLAIR and ATLAS trials was estimated to have 97% power to demonstrate noninferiority using a margin of 6% for the primary efficacy endpoint for individual trials, and a combined sample size of 570 per arm (using weighted pooling of the data from FLAIR and ATLAS) would achieve 90% power for concluding noninferiority using a margin of 4%, all using one-sided α level 0.025."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §6.3.3, p.68]*

> "The primary efficacy analysis compared the proportion of subjects with a week 48 HIV-1 RNA ≥50 copies/mL between the two arms (CAB+RPV – CAR) using FDA snapshot algorithm. This was performed using stratified Cochran-Mantel Haenszel (CMH) method, adjusting induction baseline HIV-1 RNA (<100,000 or ≥100,000 copies/mL) and sex at birth for FLAIR, and baseline third agent class (INSTI, NNRTI, or PI) and sex at birth for ATLAS... A conclusion of noninferiority of CAB+RPV compared to CAR can be determined if the upper bound of the 95% CI is less than the noninferiority margin."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §6.3.3, p.68-69]*

> "An interim analysis that evaluated accumulative efficacy results was conducted for the two individual trials when approximately 50% of the subjects reached week 24. A futility rule based on Bayesian posterior predictive probability was applied to assess the probability that CAB+RPV is noninferior to CAR. An independent data monitoring committee (IDMC) was unblinded and evaluated the efficacy results, while the Applicant remained blinded. No alpha (α) was spent on the interim analysis because there was no hypothesis test conducted, and the Applicant remained blinded to the randomization and the interim results."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §6.4.2, p.71-72]*

> "The Applicant's primary efficacy results were confirmed by the statistical review team, and the results demonstrate noninferiority in both FLAIR and ATLAS. The upper bound of the 95% CI for the adjusted difference in the proportion of subjects with HIV-1 RNA >50 copies/mL at week 48 (CAB+RPV – CAR) was lower than the prespecified 6% margin for each trial. Specifically, those upper bounds were 2.1% in FLAIR and 2.5% in ATLAS... Homogeneity of the results across the ten randomization strata was evaluated using Breslow-Day test for the pooled analyses. The result showed that the treatment effect was consistent across strata (p-value=0.2)."

### 63. Ibrexafungerp (Brexafemme) — NDA 214900

**Sponsor:** Scynexis, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC) in non-pregnant females ≥12 years of age (including postmenopausal women) — first FDA-approved oral non-azole antifungal for acute VVC

**Approval date:** June 1, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** VANISH-303 (SCY-078-303), NCT03734991, and VANISH-306 (SCY-078-306), NCT03987620

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
- *Endpoints:* clinical cure rate (complete resolution of vulvovaginal signs and symptoms at test-of-cure)
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test, Miettinen-Nurminen method
- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation for missing binary/diary efficacy data
- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan (FDA required the Applicant to revert the modified intent-to-treat (mITT) population definition to the SAP-stated definition and rerun the primary analysis)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Two identically designed, randomized (2:1 ibrexafungerp:placebo), double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trials of a single oral dose of ibrexafungerp (two 300 mg doses 12 hours apart) in non-pregnant, post-menarchal females with acute VVC and a positive baseline Candida culture; VANISH-303 was conducted only in the U.S., VANISH-306 in the U.S. and Bulgaria
- Analysis populations: ITT (all randomized, consented, dosed), modified ITT (mITT — all randomized subjects with a positive baseline Candida culture who received ≥1 dose, the pre-specified primary efficacy population), and per-protocol (PP, supportive)
- Primary endpoint: clinical cure (total vaginal symptom score = 0) at the test-of-cure (TOC) visit, Day 11±3
- Secondary endpoints: mycological eradication and overall (clinical + mycologic) success at TOC, using the same analysis methods as the primary endpoint
- Primary analysis method: Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test adjusted for site and diabetes-mellitus diagnosis for the treatment-difference significance test, with the risk difference (ibrexafungerp − placebo) and 95% CI computed via the Miettinen-Nurminen method; missing categorical responses were imputed as non-responders (failures)
- FDA-identified deviation: the Study 306 clinical study report used a revised mITT definition that diverged from the SAP-stated definition, and the same substitution was found to have been silently applied in Study 303's underlying data-definition file; FDA's Division did not agree with the change and issued a Request for Information requiring the Applicant to rerun the primary analyses using the SAP-defined mITT population — all discussion and results in the final review use the SAP-based definition
- Result (VANISH-303, SAP-defined mITT): clinical cure 95/190 (50.0%) ibrexafungerp vs. 28/100 (28.0%) placebo, difference 22.0% (95% CI 10.2, 32.8), p=0.001

Additionally, the difference in proportions (ibrexafungerp – placebo) and corresponding 95% confidence interval based on the Miettinen and Nurminen method were calculated... For the categorical endpoints (primary and secondary), missing responses were imputed as non-responders (failures, mycological persistence) in the analyses."

### 64. Fexinidazole (unbranded) — NDA 214429

**Sponsor:** Sanofi, developed in partnership with the Drugs for Neglected Diseases initiative (DNDi)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of human African trypanosomiasis (HAT, sleeping sickness) due to *Trypanosoma brucei gambiense* in patients 6 years of age and older weighing at least 20 kg, for both stage 1 (hemolymphatic) and early stage 2 (meningoencephalitic, CSF white blood cell count ≤100 cells/µL) disease

**Approval date:** July 16, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** DNDiFEX004, NCT01685827 ("Pivotal Study of Fexinidazole for Human African Trypanosomiasis in Stage 2")

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled
- *Endpoints:* clinical success at 18 months (composite lumbar-puncture/CSF-white-blood-cell-based cure definition)
- *Primary analysis:* Pocock-type adjusted confidence interval for a group-sequential noninferiority comparison of two proportions
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design (single planned interim analysis added mid-trial by protocol amendment, at the recommendation of an Expert Committee, to allow an early registration submission)
- *Missing data/bias:* multi-method sensitivity imputation cascade for missing lumbar-puncture/relapse outcome data — a protocol-defined primary imputation rule plus three alternative methods, including expert-panel adjudication and a logistic-regression-based probability-of-relapse imputation
- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan (post-database-lock addition of independent expert adjudication to the primary missing-data imputation method)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Randomized (2:1 fexinidazole:NECT), open-label, active-controlled, multicenter, non-inferiority trial in patients ≥15 years old with confirmed late-stage-1 or early-stage-2 (CSF WBC ≤100 cells/µL) *T.b. gambiense* HAT, conducted at sites in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Central African Republic
- Comparator: NECT (nifurtimox-eflornithine combination therapy), the WHO-recommended standard of care for stage 2 disease at the time, chosen as an active comparator because placebo would have been unethical in a fatal disease
- Analysis populations: intent-to-treat (ITT, all randomized who received ≥1 dose, used for sensitivity analysis and safety) and modified ITT (mITT, all ITT patients except those excluded due to inability to obtain post-treatment data because they fled areas of armed conflict — the primary efficacy population)
- Primary endpoint: treatment success at 18 months, a composite outcome derived from lumbar puncture/CSF assessment, symptom status, and relapse status, using a pre-specified classification algorithm
- Sample size: initially 510 subjects (2:1 ratio, 94%/89% assumed success rates, one-sided alpha=0.025, 87.8% power, -13% non-inferiority margin); reduced mid-trial to 390 (80% power, same margin) on the recommendation of an Expert Committee after slower-than-expected enrollment — FDA's review specifically assessed whether this change (made while unblinded efficacy data were limited to early timepoints only) threatened trial integrity and concluded it did not
- Interim analysis: added via Protocol Amendment 3 (February 2015) at Expert Committee recommendation — if fexinidazole was non-inferior to NECT at 12 months in 195 patients, an early registration submission would be pursued; because of this planned interim look, the two-sided critical Z-value for both interim and final analyses was 2.178 (equivalent two-sided alpha=0.0294), and the treatment-difference CI was a Pocock-type adjusted CI
- Primary analysis method: two-sided Pocock-adjusted CI for the difference in success proportions (fexinidazole minus NECT); non-inferiority concluded if the CI lower bound was ≥-13%; an exact test was used when either arm had fewer than 5 failures; a secondary stratified-by-site analysis used the Breslow-Day test for treatment-by-site interaction, and cumulative failure curves were compared via log-rank test
- Missing-data handling: the protocol pre-specified a primary imputation rule (subjects who refused a lumbar puncture but had no HAT signs/symptoms and no later relapse were counted as successes; all other missing/lost-to-follow-up subjects were failures) plus three alternative sensitivity methods (failure-if-no-lumbar-puncture; no imputation/censoring for the Kaplan-Meier analysis; and a logistic-regression-based predicted-probability-of-relapse imputation using external MSF cohort data); after database lock, the Applicant added independent 3-expert-panel adjudication on top of the primary imputation method, changing the classification of 5 patients — FDA's review explicitly flagged this post-database-lock change as potentially problematic and assessed its impact using the originally-planned ITT-population imputation as a check

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2021/214429s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/214429Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf

"Oral fexinidazole for late-stage African Trypanosoma brucei gambiense trypanosomiasis: a pivotal multicentre, randomised, non-inferiority trial." *Lancet.* 2018;391:144-154. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(17)32758-7>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29113731/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Oral%20fexinidazole%20for%20late-stage%20African%20Trypanosoma%20brucei%20gambiense%20trypanosomiasis)

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting is recorded for this application.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, §7, "Statistical Analysis Plan," "Sample Size Calculation," p.106]*

> "The initially planned sample size was 510 with a 2:1 randomization ratio (fexinidazole:NECT), with an assumed success rate of 94% for NECT and 89% for fexinidazole, a one-sided Type I error rate of 0.025, a noninferiority margin of -13%, and a statistical power of 87.8%. In 2013, after a few months of enrollment, the Applicant determined that the planned sample size would be difficult to reach, due to slower enrollment than expected. An Expert Committee meeting was held on June 24, 2013 to discuss this issue. The Expert Committee recommended a sample size reduction to 390, using a lower statistical power of 80%, other things being unchanged... Therefore, the effect of change in sample size on the integrity of the trial was not a concern."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, §7, "Primary Efficacy Analysis," p.106]*

> "Statistical analysis of the primary efficacy endpoint, to assess the difference in response rates between the two treatment groups (fexinidazole minus NECT), was performed by calculating the 2-sided Pocock adjusted CI for the difference. Because of the planned interim analysis..., the calculated critical Z-value for the primary endpoint of the interim analysis and final analysis was 2.178; therefore, the two-sided significance level (alpha) was equal to 0.0294 for both analyses... The noninferiority margin for the difference in success proportions between the two treatment groups was -13%."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, §7, "Methods for handling missing data," p.107]*

> "After database lock, changes were made to the primary imputation method to consider experts' adjudication. In the study report, the primary analysis used the primary imputation method with the adjudication by 3 independent experts. This impacted the results of five patients. This change of the primary analysis method after database lock could be problematic. We will assess the impact of this change by also considering the primary imputation in the ITT population as initially planned."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, primary efficacy result, p.197-198]*

> "Trial DNDiFEX004 adequately supported noninferiority of fexinidazole to NECT in late second stage g-HAT. The clinical success rates in the mITT population at 18 months were 239/262 (91.2%) in the fexinidazole group and 124/127 (97.6%) in the NECT group."

### 65. Maribavir (Livtencity) — NDA 215596

**Sponsor:** Takeda Pharmaceuticals (development originated at Shire, acquired by Takeda in 2019)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of post-transplant cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection/disease that is refractory to treatment (with or without genotypic resistance) with ganciclovir, valganciclovir, cidofovir, or foscarnet, in adult and pediatric patients ≥12 years old weighing ≥35 kg

**Approval date:** November 23, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** SOLSTICE (Shire protocol SHP620-303), NCT02931539

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, active-controlled
- *Endpoints:* confirmed viral load clearance (2 consecutive undetectable plasma CMV DNA assessments ≥5 days apart)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test; minimum risk weight method (Mehrotra-Railkar) as a pre-specified fallback when stratum heterogeneity was detected
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (primary endpoint, then key secondary, each at α=0.05 two-sided)
- *Missing data/bias:* reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan (FDA and the Applicant disputed how to classify subjects with missing Week 7/8 data who discontinued early, given open-label-design selection-bias concerns)
- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Randomized (2:1 maribavir:investigator-assigned therapy [IAT]), open-label, active-controlled, multicenter Phase III trial in solid organ transplant (SOT) and hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) recipients with CMV infection refractory (with or without genotypic resistance) to ganciclovir, valganciclovir, foscarnet, or cidofovir; IAT could be any single/combination of these four agents at the investigator's discretion, reflecting the lack of any approved alternative at the time
- Randomization stratified by transplant type (SOT vs. HSCT) and baseline plasma CMV DNA level (with high/intermediate levels collapsed into one stratum when subgroup counts were too small)
- Primary endpoint: confirmed CMV viremia clearance at end of Study Week 8 (2 consecutive plasma CMV DNA concentrations <137 IU/mL by central-lab COBAS assay, ≥5 days apart), regardless of whether study treatment was discontinued before Week 8, as long as the subject had not switched to a prohibited anti-CMV agent or maribavir rescue therapy
- Key secondary endpoint: CMV viremia clearance and symptom control (resolution/improvement of tissue-invasive disease or CMV syndrome) at Week 8, maintained through Follow-up Week 16 (8 weeks off treatment)
- Primary analysis method: stratified CMH-weighted risk difference (maribavir − IAT) with 95% CI via normal approximation; a Breslow-Day test checked homogeneity across strata, with a pre-specified fallback to the Mehrotra-Railkar minimum-risk-weight method if heterogeneity was significant at alpha=0.05
- Multiplicity: fixed-sequence testing — the primary endpoint was tested first at two-sided alpha=0.05; only if significant was the key secondary endpoint then tested, also at alpha=0.05
- FDA-Applicant dispute: subjects with missing Week 7/8 data who had achieved confirmed clearance at the time of early discontinuation were classified as non-responders by the Applicant's SAP; FDA requested (via information request) that such subjects be classified as responders regardless of discontinuation timing or switch to maribavir rescue, citing selection-bias risk inherent to the open-label design; the Applicant declined, citing a prior Type C meeting agreement fixing the assessment timepoint at 8 weeks on therapy
- Result: primary endpoint achieved by 131/235 (56%) maribavir subjects vs. 28/117 (24%) IAT subjects; 57% of IAT-arm subjects were never given the chance to try alternative anti-CMV agents before being classified as treatment failures, per FDA's review, because they switched to maribavir rescue or discontinued the study first

*[verbatim, sponsor Statistical Analysis Plan, SHP620-303, Amendment 3, 28 Sep 2020, §2.6 "Multiplicity Adjustments for Type I Error Control," p.23]*

> "The hypothesis-testing of the primary and key secondary endpoint will be adjusted for multiple comparisons using a fixed-sequence testing procedure to control the family-wise Type 1 error rate at 2-sided 5% level. The statistical test will be performed sequentially in the order of primary efficacy endpoint, and the key secondary endpoint. First, the primary endpoint analysis will be assessed at α=0.05 (2-sided). If and only after the primary efficacy endpoint is statistically significant, the key secondary endpoint will be assessed at α=0.05 (2-sided)."

*[verbatim, sponsor Statistical Analysis Plan, §10.1.2 "Analysis of Primary Efficacy Endpoint," p.46]*

> "The difference in proportion of responders between treatment groups will be obtained using Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) weighted average across all strata..., and tested using CMH method, with transplant type and baseline plasma CMV DNA concentration as two stratification factors... Homogeneity across strata will be tested using Breslow-Day test. If the test is significant at the alpha=0.05 level, stratum-specific differences in proportions will be reported and the adjusted difference and 95% CI in proportion of responders between treatment groups will be obtained and tested using minimum risk weight method of Mehrotra and Railkar (2000) instead of the CMH method."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.1.3 "Statistical Analysis Plan, Trial 303," p.23]*

> "The Applicant's primary efficacy analysis considered subjects with missing data at Week 7 and 8 who achieved confirmed viremia clearance at the time of early discontinuation to be non-responders and as responders in sensitivity analyses. Due to concerns about the open-label design and potential selection biases, the FDA requested that these subjects be classified as responders in the primary efficacy analysis... The Applicant disagreed and stated that this would conflict with the previous agreement that the timing of assessment of the primary endpoint for clearance of CMV viremia should occur at a fixed timepoint, specifically 8 weeks while on therapy, citing Type C Meeting Minutes on December 7, 2015."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, Table 12, p.28]*

> "Subjects who achieved primary endpoint: Maribavir 131 (56%) (N=235), IAT 28 (24%) (N=117)... Only 24 (21%) of the 117 subjects randomized to IAT were switched to at least one prohibited anti-CMV treatment, while 22 (19%) of the 117 subjects randomized to IAT were switched to maribavir rescue therapy... Therefore, it appears that 57% of the subjects in the IAT treatment arm were not given the opportunity to try other anti-CMV treatments before they were classified as treatment failures as pre-specified for the primary efficacy analysis in the protocol."

### 66. Oteseconazole (Vivjoa) — NDA 215888

**Sponsor:** Mycovia Pharmaceuticals

**Indication approved:** Reduce the incidence of recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis (RVVC) in females with a history of RVVC who are not of reproductive potential — the labeled restriction to non-reproductive-potential patients reflects nonclinical embryo-fetal toxicity findings for this long-half-life azole

**Approval date:** April 26, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** ultraVIOLET-1 (Trial CL-011), NCT03562156, and ultraVIOLET-2 (Trial CL-012), NCT03561701; supportive induction/comparator Trial CL-017, NCT03840616

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (CL-011/CL-012 maintenance-phase trials); randomized, double-blind, active-controlled (CL-017, fluconazole-controlled induction-phase comparator study)
- *Endpoints:* recurrence rate (culture-verified acute VVC episode during an extended maintenance phase through Week 48)
- *Primary analysis:* multiple imputation (SAS PROC MI, 10 datasets) combined via Wilson-Hilferty-transformed chi-square statistics under Rubin's rule (SAS PROC MIANALYZE)
- *Missing data/bias:* embedded within the primary analysis (auxiliary-variable multiple imputation for all missing scheduled-visit sign/symptom and culture data)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- CL-011 and CL-012 were identically designed, randomized (2:1 oteseconazole:placebo), double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trials in females with a history of recurrent VVC (≥3 episodes in the past year); subjects first received open-label induction therapy (fluconazole, per Trial CL-017's comparator design in a subset) to clear an acute episode, then entered a 48-week randomized, blinded maintenance phase
- Primary endpoint: proportion of subjects with ≥1 culture-verified acute VVC episode during the Maintenance Phase (post-randomization through Week 48), ITT population
- Analysis populations: ITT (all randomized subjects); a per-protocol population was supportive
- Missing-data handling (SAP-specified, Trial CL-011, §3.4.4): scheduled-visit sign/symptom or culture results missing at a scheduled visit — including all visits after early discontinuation — were imputed via multiple imputation (SAS PROC MI, 10 imputed datasets), using region, treatment, baseline BMI, baseline age, ethnicity, and visit as auxiliary variables; unscheduled-visit data were substituted for a missing scheduled visit first, where available, before imputation
- Primary analysis method: the primary endpoint was derived independently in each of the 10 imputed datasets and analyzed via a chi-square test; the Wilson-Hilferty transformation was applied to the chi-square statistics before combining the 10 results using SAS PROC MIANALYZE (Rubin's rule) to obtain a single inferential result
- Visit-window rule: unscheduled visits were used only if the scheduled visit was unavailable, except that an unscheduled visit with a culture-verified acute VVC episode and signs/symptoms score >3 always counted the subject as a treatment failure for the primary and key secondary endpoints
- Result (CL-011, ITT population): 14/oteseconazole vs. 45/placebo subjects had ≥1 culture-verified acute VVC episode through Week 48; 53 of 235 randomized subjects (42 oteseconazole, 11 placebo) did not have complete follow-up

### 67. Lenacapavir (Sunlenca) — NDA 215973 (subcutaneous injection) / NDA 215974 (oral tablets)

**Sponsor:** Gilead Sciences

**Indication approved:** In combination with other antiretroviral(s), for treatment of HIV-1 infection in heavily treatment-experienced (HTE) adults with multidrug-resistant HIV-1 infection failing their current antiretroviral regimen due to resistance, intolerance, or safety considerations — the original treatment-indication approval for this first-in-class capsid inhibitor; lenacapavir was later also approved (2025, PURPOSE-1/PURPOSE-2 trials) for HIV-1 pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), a separate and much larger indication not covered by this entry

**Approval date:** December 22, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** CAPELLA (Study GS-US-200-4625), NCT04150068

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* multi-arm trial mixing a randomized comparison with a modified single-arm dose-confirmation cohort (Cohort 1 randomized placebo-controlled functional-monotherapy period; Cohort 2 non-randomized, all-lenacapavir)
- *Endpoints:* antiviral activity threshold endpoint (≥0.5 log10 HIV-1 RNA reduction from baseline during a 14-day functional monotherapy period)
- *Primary analysis:* Chan and Zhang unconditional exact method (two inverted one-sided tests) for a difference in proportions
- *Missing data/bias:* last observation carried forward (LOCF) imputation for missing end-of-functional-monotherapy HIV-1 RNA values

**Trial design & endpoints**

- CAPELLA enrolled heavily treatment-experienced adults with multidrug-resistant HIV-1 (resistant to ≥2 agents in each of ≥3 of the 4 main antiretroviral classes, with ≤2 remaining fully active agents) who were failing their current regimen with HIV-1 RNA ≥400 copies/mL
- Cohort 1 (randomized, 2:1 lenacapavir:placebo, double-blind, placebo-controlled): subjects received 14 days of oral lenacapavir or placebo added to their existing failing regimen (functional monotherapy period, FMP), then all transitioned to open-label subcutaneous lenacapavir plus an optimized background regimen (OBR)
- Cohort 2 (non-randomized, open-label): subjects who did not qualify for Cohort 1 (e.g., insufficient residual viremia decline) received oral lenacapavir plus OBR directly, with no functional-monotherapy comparison; Cohort 1 and Cohort 2 are explicitly not intended to be compared to one another
- Primary endpoint (Cohort 1 only): proportion of subjects achieving ≥0.5 log10 copies/mL reduction from baseline in HIV-1 RNA at the end of the FMP (Day 15 or Day 1 SC, whichever earlier); Full Analysis Set (FAS) = all randomized subjects in the FMP who received ≥1 dose of blinded study drug
- Secondary endpoints: proportion with HIV-1 RNA <50 and <200 copies/mL at Weeks 26 and 52 (FDA Snapshot algorithm), "All LEN" population
- Primary analysis method: two-sided unconditional exact method using two inverted one-sided tests (Chan and Zhang, 1999) at alpha=0.05 to test superiority of lenacapavir vs. placebo for the FMP responder proportion, implemented via SAS PROC FREQ with the RISKDIFF/EXACT BARNARD option; for subjects with a missing end-of-FMP HIV-1 RNA value, the value was imputed using last observation carried forward; a supportive per-protocol-set analysis assessed robustness
- Result: 21/24 (87.5%) lenacapavir subjects vs. 2/12 (16.7%) placebo subjects met the primary endpoint, difference 70.8% (95% CI 34.9, 90.0), p<0.0001 — notably, this primary comparison rested on only 36 randomized Cohort 1 subjects, reflecting the very narrow eligible population of HTE patients with multidrug-resistant virus

### 68. Rezafungin (Rezzayo) — NDA 217417

**Sponsor:** Cidara Therapeutics (development/US registration sponsor), partnered with Mundipharma for ex-U.S. commercialization

**Indication approved:** Treatment of candidemia and invasive candidiasis in patients ≥18 years of age who have limited or no alternative treatment options — the "limited or no alternative treatment options" qualifier was a direct consequence of the wide (20%) non-inferiority margin used, per FDA's review

**Approval date:** March 22, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** ReSTORE (Study CD101.IV.3.05), NCT03667690

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled, non-inferiority-then-superiority hierarchy
- *Endpoints:* all-cause mortality at a fixed post-treatment day (Day 30 (-2 days), binary primary noninferiority endpoint)
- *Primary analysis:* Miettinen-Nurminen method
- *Regulatory:* noninferiority margin width tied to a labeled "limited population" restriction — FDA agreed the wider 20% margin (vs. a stricter 10%) was acceptable only in exchange for a narrower approved population

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Randomized (1:1), double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled, multicenter, non-inferiority Phase III trial of once-weekly IV rezafungin (400 mg loading dose, then 200 mg weekly) vs. daily IV caspofungin (70 mg loading, then 50 mg daily) in adults with candidemia and/or invasive candidiasis
- Dual FDA/EMA primary endpoints, reflecting divergent regulatory requirements: for the FDA, all-cause mortality (ACM) at Day 30 (-2 days); for the EMA, Day 14 global response (a composite of investigator-assessed clinical cure, radiological cure for IC, and DRC-adjudicated mycological eradication)
- Analysis population: modified ITT (mITT, subjects with a qualifying baseline Candida culture); for the FDA primary endpoint, subjects with unknown Day-30 survival status were counted as deceased
- Primary analysis method (FDA endpoint): one-sided hypothesis test at the 2.5% significance level, based on the upper limit of the two-sided 95% CI for the treatment difference in Day 30 ACM (rezafungin minus caspofungin), calculated using the unadjusted Miettinen and Nurminen method; non-inferiority concluded if the upper CI bound was <20% (the pre-specified non-inferiority margin); superiority testing (upper bound <0) was pre-specified to follow only if non-inferiority was met AND observed rezafungin mortality was numerically lower than caspofungin's — which did not occur, since rezafungin's observed mortality was numerically higher
- Non-inferiority margin: 20%, wider than typically seen in this class; FDA's review states this reflected the difficulty of a stricter margin design in this population, and explicitly that FDA agreed a 20% margin was usable only in exchange for a narrower, "limited or no alternative treatment options" approved population, rather than a full unrestricted indication
- Result: Day 30 ACM 22/93 (23.7%) rezafungin vs. 20/94 (21.3%) caspofungin, difference 2.4% (95% CI -9.7, 14.4) — non-inferiority declared at the 20% margin, but the trial did not meet a stricter 10% margin, which FDA noted would have been required for a full/unrestricted approval

This non-inferiority test will be based on the upper limit of the two-sided 95% confidence interval (CI). The primary efficacy outcome is the percentage of subjects that died at Day 30... where p1 is the all-cause mortality rate at Day 30 (-2 days) in the Rezafungin for Injection treatment group, p2 is the primary ACM at Day 30 (-2 days) rate in the caspofungin treatment group, and Δ is the non-inferiority margin of 20%... To test the null hypothesis, a two-sided 95% CI for the observed difference in primary outcome rates... will be calculated for the mITT population using the unadjusted methodology of Miettinen and Nurminen (Miettinen and Nurminen, 1985). If the upper limit of the 95% CI for the difference in the mITT population is lower than 20%, then the null hypothesis will be rejected and non-inferiority... will be declared."

If the upper bound of the 95% CI is less than 0, superiority of rezafungin will be concluded."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.2.3 "Statistical Analysis Plan, Phase 3 Study," p.31]*

> "To control the overall alpha level, superiority of rezafungin for injection for ACM at Day 30 was planned to test if noninferiority was established and the observed mortality was lower in the rezafungin arm. Analysis for superiority was not conducted, as the observed mortality was higher in the rezafungin arm."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, Table 19 and surrounding text, p.36]*

> "The Applicant's primary efficacy results for all-cause mortality at Day 30 were confirmed by the statistical review team, and the results demonstrated noninferiority using a 20% noninferiority margin... Mortality rates were 23.7% (22/93) in the rezafungin arm and 21.3% (20/94) in the caspofungin arm, which lead to an estimated difference in mortality rates of 2.4% [95% CI: -9.7% to 14.4%]. It is noted that the study did not meet a 10% noninferiority margin, as indicated by the upper limit of the 95% CI. At the protocol development stage, FDA agreed that 20% could be used but would result in a limited use indication. A 10% margin would be needed for a full approval."

### 69. Sulbactam/durlobactam (Xacduro) — NDA 216974

**Sponsor:** Entasis Therapeutics

**Indication approved:** Treatment of Hospital-Acquired Bacterial Pneumonia and Ventilator-Associated Bacterial Pneumonia (HABP/VABP) caused by susceptible isolates of *Acinetobacter baumannii*-calcoaceticus complex, in patients ≥18 years of age

**Approval date:** May 23, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** ATTACK (Study CS2514-2017-0004), NCT03894046

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, assessor-blinded, active-controlled (outcome assessors were blinded to treatment while treating clinicians were not, distinct from a fully double-blind design); two-part trial mixing a randomized comparative portion (Part A) with a single-group supportive portion (Part B, for colistin-resistant/-ineligible patients, analyzed descriptively)
- *Endpoints:* all-cause mortality at a fixed post-treatment day (28-day all-cause mortality, binary primary noninferiority endpoint)
- *Primary analysis:* continuity-corrected Z-statistic for a difference in proportions
- *Missing data/bias:* patients with missing survival status were treated as deaths for the primary analysis; patients who withdrew consent from survival follow-up were excluded (with a sensitivity analysis including them)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ATTACK Part A was the pivotal, randomized (1:1), assessor-blinded (outcomes adjudicated by a blinded assessor, while treating clinicians and patients were not blinded to treatment assignment), active-controlled trial of IV sulbactam-durlobactam + imipenem/cilastatin vs. colistin + imipenem/cilastatin, in patients with HABP, VABP, or bacteremia due to *Acinetobacter baumannii*-calcoaceticus complex (ABC); imipenem/cilastatin was included as background therapy in both arms specifically to provide Gram-negative coverage against non-ABC pathogens while durlobactam's activity was isolated to the ABC target
- Part B was a single-group, open-label, supportive portion enrolling patients with colistin-resistant or otherwise colistin-ineligible ABC infections who could not be randomized in Part A
- Primary analysis population: CRABC (carbapenem-resistant ABC) modified-MITT population in Part A — 63 sulbactam-durlobactam and 62 colistin patients, out of 181 total Part A randomizations (only ~35% of randomized/screened patients had confirmed carbapenem-resistant ABC infection meeting the modified-MITT definition)
- Primary endpoint: 28-day all-cause mortality; patients who discontinued study drug prematurely for any reason remained in the mortality analysis (unless consent for survival follow-up was withdrawn); patients with missing survival status were counted as deaths
- Primary analysis method: two-sided 95% CI via a continuity-corrected Z-statistic for the difference in 28-day mortality rates (sulbactam-durlobactam minus colistin, both plus background imipenem/cilastatin); non-inferiority concluded if the CI upper bound was <20% (pre-specified margin, chosen partly based on literature-derived HABP/VABP adequate-vs-inadequate-therapy mortality differences per FDA's HABP/VABP guidance, and partly to reduce sample size given COVID-19 pandemic enrollment constraints); superiority (upper bound <0) would be tested only after non-inferiority was established
- Sensitivity analyses were pre-specified across multiple axes: culture timing relative to first dose (>48h vs. ≤48h before treatment), baseline susceptibility status, inclusion of Part-A-to-Part-B transfers, and exclusion of missing-survival-status patients
- Result: 28-day all-cause mortality 12/63 (19.0%) sulbactam-durlobactam vs. 20/62 (32.3%) colistin, difference -13.2% (95% CI -30.0, 3.5) — non-inferiority (and numerically favorable point estimate) with a much narrower margin than the pre-specified 20%, which FDA's review specifically highlighted as stronger evidence than the design required

### 70. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir (Paxlovid) — NDA 217188

**Sponsor:** Pfizer Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of mild-to-moderate COVID-19 in adults at high risk for progression to severe COVID-19, including hospitalization or death — this entry documents the full NDA approval (May 25, 2023); nirmatrelvir/ritonavir first reached the U.S. market via Emergency Use Authorization on December 22, 2021, based on the same EPIC-HR interim analysis described below, roughly 17 months before full approval

**Approval date:** May 25, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** EPIC-HR (Protocol C4671005), NCT04960202

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven trial, group-sequential design
- *Endpoints:* COVID-19-related hospitalization or death through Day 28 (composite binary endpoint)
- *Primary analysis:* Kaplan-Meier estimation; complementary log-log (Greenwood's-formula) confidence interval for a Kaplan-Meier proportion difference
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (primary endpoint → 2 ordered key secondary endpoints → remaining secondaries under Hochberg step-up procedure)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function, O'Brien-Fleming boundary, sample-size re-estimation (Cui-Hung-Wang method)
- *Regulatory:* Emergency Use Authorization preceding full approval, based on the same trial's interim analysis; full approval later granted on the completed trial

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter Phase II/III trial of oral nirmatrelvir/ritonavir vs. placebo, twice daily for 5 days, in symptomatic, non-hospitalized adults at high risk for progression to severe COVID-19, unvaccinated and without prior SARS-CoV-2 infection, enrolled within 5 days of symptom onset
- Analysis populations: Full Analysis Set (FAS, all randomized regardless of dosing); pre-specified primary population modified ITT (mITT, treated ≤3 days of symptom onset, no baseline/anticipated monoclonal antibody use); mITT1 (≤5 days of symptom onset, same mAb restriction) and mITT2 (≤5 days, no mAb restriction) for key/additional secondary analyses; per-protocol (PP) as supportive
- Primary endpoint: proportion of subjects with COVID-19-related hospitalization or death from any cause through Day 28 in the mITT population, estimated via the Kaplan-Meier method (to account for variable follow-up/censoring) with the between-group difference and 95% CI computed via a complementary log-log transformation of the KM survival estimate with Greenwood's-formula variance
- Key secondary endpoints, tested in fixed sequence after a positive primary result: (1) the same hospitalization/death endpoint in the broader mITT1 population, then (2) time to sustained alleviation of all targeted COVID-19 signs/symptoms through Day 28; remaining secondary endpoints (time to sustained symptom resolution; proportion with resting SpO2 ≥95% at Days 1 and 5; number of COVID-19-related medical visits) were then tested via the Hochberg step-up procedure
- Interim monitoring: a planned formal interim analysis for efficacy and futility, with a possible sample-size re-estimation (Cui-Hung-Wang method, based on conditional power) at the first interim look; the significance boundary at both the interim and final analyses was determined using the Lan-DeMets implementation of an O'Brien-Fleming-type spending function, with the overall two-sided significance level fixed at 5%
- Result at the pre-specified interim analysis (data cutoff October 26, 2021, which supported the EUA): mITT population — 3/389 (0.8%) nirmatrelvir/ritonavir vs. 27/385 (7.0%) placebo with the primary composite event, an 89.1% relative risk reduction, absolute difference -6.3% (95% CI -9.0, -3.6), significant at the interim's pre-specified alpha=0.002; at the completed trial (supporting full approval), mITT population — 5/671 (0.7%) vs. 44/647 (6.8%), difference -6.1% (95% CI -8.2, -4.1), nominal p<0.0001

### 71. Nirsevimab-alip (Beyfortus) — BLA 761328

**Sponsor:** AstraZeneca AB (manufacturer); distributed by Sanofi Pasteur, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Prevention of Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) lower respiratory tract disease in neonates and infants born during or entering their first RSV season, and in children up to 24 months of age who remain vulnerable to severe RSV disease through their second RSV season — a long-acting monoclonal antibody, not a vaccine

**Approval date:** July 17, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** MELODY (Trial 04 / D5290C00004), NCT03979313; supportive trial MEDLEY (Trial 05 / D5290C00005), NCT03959488

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (MELODY); Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled (MEDLEY, vs. palivizumab); Extrapolation of efficacy across a related trial setting (regulatory precedent) (MEDLEY was not independently powered for efficacy — efficacy in the palivizumab-eligible high-risk population was extrapolated from MELODY/Trial 03 data)
- *Endpoints:* medically attended RSV lower respiratory tract infection (MA RSV LRTI, inpatient + outpatient), incidence through Day 150 postdose; RSV-associated hospitalization (key secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* Poisson regression with robust variance (Zou 2004 method) for relative risk reduction **
- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (primary MA RSV LRTI incidence tested before the secondary hospitalization endpoint, both at 2-sided alpha 0.05)
- *Regulatory:* FDA Advisory Committee meeting held (Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee, June 8, 2023); Reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan (the Applicant proposed pooling MELODY with an earlier Phase 2b trial for secondary-endpoint analysis; FDA had already flagged this issue at a July 2022 pre-BLA meeting and excluded the pooled analyses from its formal review, treating them as exploratory only)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- MELODY (NCT03979313) is a Phase 3, multicenter, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of a single intramuscular dose of nirsevimab vs. placebo in healthy late-preterm and term infants (≥29 weeks gestational age) entering their first RSV season; initial planned sample size was 3,000 subjects, but COVID-19 disrupted enrollment and, after a December 2020 Type B meeting with FDA, the trial was amended so the Primary Cohort (and primary analysis) was based on the 1,490 subjects randomized prior to the enrollment pause
- Primary endpoint: incidence of MA RSV LRTI (RT-PCR-confirmed) through Day 150 postdose; key secondary endpoint: RSV-associated hospitalization through Day 150
- MEDLEY (NCT03959488) is a Phase 2/3, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled (palivizumab) trial in palivizumab-eligible preterm and congenital heart/chronic lung disease infants; primary endpoint was safety/tolerability (treatment-emergent adverse events, adverse events of special interest), not efficacy — enrollment was similarly reduced by COVID-19 (from a planned ~1,500 to ~600 subjects, agreed with FDA)
- Primary analysis method (MELODY): a Poisson regression model with robust variance, with treatment group, age group at randomization, and hemisphere as covariates, estimating relative risk reduction (RRR = 1 − RR) and its 2-sided 95% CI; a protocol deviation was made during blinded data review when zero Southern Hemisphere MA RSV LRTI events in the primary cohort caused a model convergence issue, leading to hemisphere being dropped as a covariate from the final model
- Sample size/power: the reduced ~1,490-subject Primary Cohort retained ≥99% power to detect a 70% RRR assuming an 8% placebo-arm MA RSV LRTI incidence, 2-sided alpha 0.05
- Multiplicity: secondary hypotheses (including RSV-associated hospitalization) were tested only if the primary endpoint's treatment effect was significant at 2-sided alpha 0.05, in a prespecified hierarchical order
- Result: nirsevimab reduced MA RSV LRTI incidence with an RRR of 74.5% (95% CI 49.6, 87.1) vs. placebo in the Primary Cohort (per the pivotal NEJM publication)

> "The primary endpoint is the incidence of medically attended RSV LRTI (inpatient and outpatient) through 150 days post dose. For subjects with multiple medically attended RSV LRTI events (inpatient or outpatient), only the first occurrence will be used in the primary analysis."

*[verbatim, MELODY SAP, p.17]*

> "The primary efficacy analysis of the primary endpoint will be performed on ITT1. A Poisson regression model with robust variance (Zou, 2004) will be used as the primary efficacy analysis model to estimate the relative risk (RR) on the incidence of medically attended RSV LRTI between the MEDI8897 and the placebo groups... Statistical significance will be achieved if the 2-sided p-value is ≤ 0.05." And, on the mid-study covariate deviation: "During blinded data review prior to the DBL for Primary Analysis, it was revealed that there was no incidence of medically attended RSV LRTI events through 150 days post dose for [Southern Hemisphere] in primary cohort, which would cause known convergence or estimation issue. Therefore it was decided to drop the stratification factor hemisphere from the full model..."

*[verbatim, MELODY SAP, p.9, sample size/power]*

> "the sample size of approximately 1,500 subjects in the primary cohort has at least 99% power to detect 70% relative risk reduction (RRR), assuming a placebo group medically attended RSV LRTI incidence of 8%. Power calculations are based on a Poisson regression model with robust variance (Zou, 2004) comparing MEDI8897 versus placebo, with 2-sided, α = 0.05."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, 761328Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf, p.52, on the pooling deviation]*

> "For the secondary endpoints, the Applicant proposed to pool Trial 03 and Trial 04 together to ascertain efficacy of nirsevimab on hospitalization... The Agency alerted the Applicant about this issue during the pre-BLA meeting on July 26, 2022. Therefore, no analysis based on pooled data from Trials 03 and 04 will be included or discussed in this review... All analyses based on the Primary and Safety Cohorts together were not planned to be adjusted for multiplicity and therefore will only be considered as exploratory analyses."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, p.150-151, Advisory Committee]*

> "An Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee Meeting (AMDAC) was held on June 8, 2023... The committee unanimously voted that the overall benefit-risk assessment favors the use of nirsevimab for the prevention of RSV lower respiratory disease in neonates and infants born during or entering their first RSV season... the majority (19/21) of the committee members agreed that the overall assessment was favorable for... children up to 24 months of age who remain vulnerable to severe RSV disease through their second RSV season."

### 72. Taurolidine/heparin (Defencath) — NDA 214520

**Sponsor:** CorMedix Inc.

**Indication approved:** Reduction of the incidence of catheter-related bloodstream infections (CRBSI) in adult patients with kidney failure receiving chronic hemodialysis through a central venous catheter — approved under the Limited Population Pathway for Antibacterial and Antifungal Drugs (LPAD, section 506(h) FDCA)

**Approval date:** November 15, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** LOCK-IT-100, NCT02651428

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled (taurolidine/heparin catheter lock solution vs. heparin-alone lock solution); Event-driven trial (continued until a target CRBSI event count accrued); Limited Population Pathway for Antibacterial and Antifungal Drugs (LPAD) approval, 506(h) **
- *Endpoints:* time to first CAC (Clinical Adjudication Committee)-adjudicated catheter-related bloodstream infection (CRBSI)
- *Primary analysis:* Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified or with covariates); Kaplan-Meier estimation
- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (secondary endpoint of catheter loss for any reason tested only if the primary CRBSI endpoint was significant)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Pocock group-sequential boundary ** — 2-sided nominal significance level of 0.0294 at both the interim (28 events) and final (56 events) analyses
- *Missing data/bias:* Standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment (catheter removal for reasons other than CRBSI, death, dialysis termination, and study completion were all handled as censoring events; FDA's statistical reviewer flagged the assumption of noninformative censoring as potentially invalid and ran sensitivity analyses treating death and other non-CRBSI dispositions as events)
- *Regulatory:* Complete Response Letter (CRL) followed by resubmission and approval (a manufacturing-related CRL was issued February 26, 2021; the application was approved on resubmission after a May 2023 amendment)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- LOCK-IT-100 (NCT02651428) is a Phase 3, multicenter, randomized (1:1), double-blind, active-controlled trial of taurolidine/heparin (originally named "Neutrolin") vs. heparin-alone catheter lock solution in adult hemodialysis patients using a chronic central venous catheter; 806 subjects were randomized (397 Defencath, 398 heparin, per the label's efficacy population)
- Primary endpoint: time to first CAC-adjudicated CRBSI, defined by the same organism growing from a peripheral-site/bloodline sample and either the arterial or venous catheter hub (or dialysis-circuit lines)
- Secondary endpoint: catheter loss for any reason, gated behind a significant primary result
- Original sample size was 632 subjects; after early conduct issues, the protocol was amended (while blinded) to introduce a Clinical Adjudication Committee, revise the primary endpoint definition to CAC-adjudicated CRBSI, increase the sample size to 900, and add an interim analysis at 28 CRBSI events, targeting a total of 56 events for 80% power
- Primary analysis method: a log-rank test for the treatment difference, with a Cox proportional-hazards model used to estimate the hazard ratio and its 95% CI; SAS PROC LIFETEST and PROC PHREG were the specified software procedures
- Interim monitoring: the method of Pocock was used to derive the interim efficacy boundary, giving a 2-sided nominal significance level of 0.0294 at both the interim and final analyses
- Result: CAC-adjudicated CRBSI occurred in 9/397 (2.3%) Defencath subjects vs. 32/398 (8.0%) heparin subjects; event rate per 1,000 catheter-days 0.13 (95% CI 0.07, 0.26) vs. 0.46 (95% CI 0.33, 0.66)
- An FDA Advisory Committee meeting was originally scheduled for January 14, 2021 but was cancelled (decision communicated November 16, 2020) after FDA concluded the benefit-risk assessment was clear and did not need Committee input

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.2215/CJN.0000000000000278), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37678222/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Taurolidine+Heparin+Lock+Solution+and+Catheter-Related+Bloodstream+Infection+in+Hemodialysis)

- CorMedix trial-specific IPD access via Vivli.org was not individually confirmed here.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was ultimately held (see above — one was scheduled, then cancelled by FDA before it occurred).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, ClinicalTrials.gov-posted SAP, SAP_001.pdf, p.4, sample size/power]*

> "This trial has been designed to achieve 80% power for the comparison between treatment arms subject to the following specifications: testing will be conducted at a 2-sided overall 5% alpha level using the log-rank test, Neutrolin is associated with a 55% reduction in the risk of CRBSI relative to the control arm... one interim analysis will be performed at the midpoint of the trial with adjustment of the alpha level using the method of Pocock. Fifty-six CRBSI events in total will be needed to achieve the desired power. The interim analysis will be conducted based on the first 28 CRBSIs."

*[verbatim, SAP, p.5, primary endpoint analysis]*

> "The primary analysis will be conducted using a log-rank test for the time to CRBSI at an overall 2-sided 5% alpha level... Subjects without a CRBSI will be treated as censored in this analysis if the catheter is removed for reasons other than CRBSI... or follow-up is completed in the absence of CRBSI. Because an interim analysis for efficacy will be performed, the method of Pocock will be used to control the overall alpha level. Therefore, the nominal significance level at the interim and final statistical analyses for the primary efficacy endpoint will be 0.0294."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, p.24, on the mid-conduct protocol amendment]*

> "Due to these issues, the Applicant implemented changes in the protocol while maintaining the study blind. These changes included: (1) introduction of a CAC for ascertaining CRBSIs, (2) revision of the definition of the primary endpoint to incidence of CAC-adjudicated CRBSIs, (3) increase in sample size from 632 to 900, and (4) introduction of an interim analysis to be performed after 28 events of CRBSI."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, p.41, reviewer's censoring concern]*

> "The Applicant assumed all censored data was noninformative, which implied that censoring was unrelated to the study treatment. This assumption may not be valid. The statistical reviewer conducted sensitivity analyses to evaluate the robustness of the study results by including death as an event in addition to CRBSI and also by considering nonpositive disposition events as events."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, p.101, Advisory Committee]*

> "An advisory committee meeting was originally scheduled for this NDA on January 14, 2021... The review team concluded that the overall benefit/risk was clear and there were no issues that would benefit from Advisory Committee discussion. The decision to cancel the advisory committee meeting was communicated to the Applicant on November 16, 2020."

### 73. Cefepime/enmetazobactam (Exblifep) — NDA 216165

**Sponsor:** Allecra Therapeutics SAS (original NDA applicant; the product has since changed hands, with Drugs@FDA's current record listing Orchid Pharma as company of record)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adults with complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI) including pyelonephritis caused by susceptible isolates of *Escherichia coli*, *Klebsiella pneumoniae*, *Pseudomonas aeruginosa*, *Proteus mirabilis*, and *Enterobacter cloacae* complex

**Approval date:** February 22, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** AT-301 (referred to in some secondary sources as "ALLIUM," though neither FDA's review, ClinicalTrials.gov, nor the pivotal JAMA publication uses that acronym), NCT03687255

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled (vs. piperacillin/tazobactam); Non-inferiority-then-superiority hierarchy (superiority assessed as a secondary objective, without a type-I-error correction, only if non-inferiority was met)
- *Endpoints:* overall treatment success (composite of clinical cure and microbiological eradication, <10³ CFU/mL) at the test-of-cure visit
- *Primary analysis:* stratified Newcombe method for the confidence interval on a treatment difference in proportions (stratified by infection type, prior therapy category, and region) *(the taxonomy's existing "Miettinen-Nurminen method" and "Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel" entries are related but not identical to the Newcombe-CI construction used here)*
- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held (FDA stated outside expertise was not necessary)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Trial AT-301 (NCT03687255) is a Phase 3, randomized (1:1), double-blind, active-controlled, multicenter (90 sites across Europe, the Americas, and South Africa) non-inferiority trial of cefepime/enmetazobactam vs. piperacillin/tazobactam in adults with cUTI or acute pyelonephritis; FDA's Integrated Review at points also describes the trial as "assessor-blinded," an internal inconsistency in FDA's own document
- Primary analysis population: microbiological modified intent-to-treat (m-MITT), 345 cefepime/enmetazobactam vs. 333 piperacillin/tazobactam subjects
- Primary endpoint: overall treatment success (clinical cure + microbiological eradication) in the m-MITT population at test-of-cure
- Non-inferiority margin: −10%, assessed via the stratified Newcombe 2-sided 95% CI for the treatment difference (cefepime/enmetazobactam minus piperacillin/tazobactam), stratified by infection type, prior antibacterial therapy, and region; if non-inferiority was met, superiority was assessed as a secondary objective without a type-I-error correction
- Sample size/power (per the JAMA publication; not separately detailed in FDA's Integrated Review): ~1,040 subjects randomized, anticipating ~811 in the primary analysis population, for 90% power to demonstrate non-inferiority at a 10% margin assuming a 74% overall success rate in both arms
- Result: overall success 79.1% (cefepime/enmetazobactam) vs. 58.9% (piperacillin/tazobactam) in the m-MITT population; treatment difference 21.2% (95% CI 14.3%, 27.9%) — non-inferiority and superiority both demonstrated
- Secondary endpoints were tested for superiority (significant if the lower 95% CI bound exceeded zero) but the publication notes findings should be interpreted as exploratory given the potential for multiplicity-driven type I error

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/216165s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Integrated Review (no separate Statistical, Clinical, or Multi-Discipline Review was posted; combined into this single review) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/216165Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf
