"Effect of Cefepime/Enmetazobactam vs Piperacillin/Tazobactam on Clinical Cure and Microbiological Eradication in Patients With Complicated Urinary Tract Infection or Acute Pyelonephritis: A Randomized Clinical Trial." *JAMA.* 2022;328(13):1304-1314. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2022.17034), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36194218/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Effect+of+Cefepime+Enmetazobactam+vs+Piperacillin+Tazobactam+on+Clinical+Cure+and+Microbiological+Eradication)

**Other resources**

- Allecra/Orchid Pharma trial-specific IPD access via Vivli.org was not individually confirmed here.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held: FDA's Integrated Review states "outside expertise was not necessary as there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, 216165Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf, p.19]*

> "The microbiological modified intent-to-treat (m-MITT) population was the primary efficacy analysis population... Overall treatment success was defined as the composite of clinical outcome of cure and the microbiological outcome of eradication (<10³ CFU/mL in urine culture)."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, p.19]*

> "The noninferiority assessment was based on the stratified Newcombe 2-sided 95% confidence interval (CI) for the difference in the proportions of subjects with overall treatment successes in the m-MITT population, calculated as the rate in the cefepime-AAI101 group minus that of the piperacillin/tazobactam group. Stratification was applied for type of infection, prior therapy category, and region. Noninferiority was concluded if the lower limit of the 2-sided 95% CI was >-10%, the noninferiority margin. If noninferiority was demonstrated, an assessment for superiority on the primary endpoint was performed as a secondary objective without the need for type I error correction."

*[verbatim, JAMA publication (PMC9533186), sample size/power]*

> "Investigators planned to randomize approximately 1040 patients, anticipating that approximately 811 would meet criteria for the primary analysis set, providing 90% power to demonstrate noninferiority of cefepime/enmetazobactam relative to piperacillin/tazobactam using a margin of 10% if an overall success rate of 74% was achieved in both groups."

*[verbatim, JAMA publication, secondary-endpoint multiplicity caveat]*

> "Secondary end points were tested for superiority with statistical significance indicated if the lower bound of the 2-sided 95% CI was greater than zero. Because of the potential for type I error due to multiple comparisons, findings for analyses of secondary end points should be interpreted as exploratory."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, p.61, Advisory Committee]*

> "Outside expertise was not necessary as there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion."

### 74. Ceftobiprole medocaril (Zevtera) — NDA 218275

**Sponsor:** Basilea Pharmaceutica International, Ltd., Allschwil

**Indication approved:** (1) *Staphylococcus aureus* bloodstream infections (bacteremia), including in patients with right-sided infective endocarditis, in adults; (2) acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI) in adults; (3) community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (CABP) in adults and pediatric patients 3 months to <18 years — all caused by susceptible isolates

**Approval date:** April 3, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** ERADICATE (BPR-CS-009), NCT03138733 (bacteremia); TARGET (BPR-CS-008), NCT03137173 (ABSSSI); a legacy trial, CAP-3001, NCT00326287 (CABP)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled (ERADICATE vs. daptomycin; TARGET vs. vancomycin plus aztreonam; CAP-3001 vs. ceftriaxone ± linezolid); Non-inferiority-then-superiority hierarchy (TARGET tested for superiority only if non-inferiority was met, without further alpha correction)
- *Endpoints:* overall success at the Post-Therapy Evaluation visit, Day 70 (ERADICATE); early clinical response at 48-72h (TARGET, primary) and clinical cure at test-of-cure (TARGET, main secondary); clinical cure rate at test-of-cure in co-primary Clinically Evaluable and Intent-to-Treat populations (CAP-3001)
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test (region- and infection-type-adjusted weighted treatment difference, all three trials)
- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (CAP-3001 secondary endpoints — microbiological eradication, clinical cure in high-severity subjects, 30-day mortality — used a step-down sequence with a 15% non-inferiority margin that FDA's review notes "has not been scientifically justified," so treated as descriptive only)
- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held; Good Clinical Practice inspection cleared prior data-integrity concerns (an FDA Office of Scientific Investigations inspection of the legacy CAP-3001 trial, prompted by the drug's history, found "no evidence of unblinding or biased data collection")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ERADICATE (NCT03138733) is a Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled (daptomycin) non-inferiority trial in adults with *S. aureus* bacteremia including right-sided endocarditis; designed for ~80% power at a one-sided alpha of 0.025, a 15% non-inferiority margin, and 195 subjects per arm (390 total), assuming a 40% overall-success rate in each arm; primary endpoint was overall success at the Day-70 (±5) Post-Therapy Evaluation visit in the modified intent-to-treat population, analyzed via a CMH-weighted 95% CI; result: adjusted treatment difference 2.0% (95% CI −7.1, 11.1), non-inferiority met
- TARGET (NCT03137173) is a Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled (vancomycin plus aztreonam) non-inferiority trial in ABSSSI, 674 subjects (337/arm), ≥90% power, one-sided alpha 0.025, 10-percentage-point non-inferiority margin on early clinical response (primary) and clinical cure at test-of-cure (main secondary); CMH-weighted treatment difference in the intent-to-treat population, adjusted for region and infection type; non-inferiority declared if the lower 95% CI bound exceeded −10%, with a pre-specified superiority test (lower bound >0) performed if non-inferiority was met; result: early clinical response 91.3% vs. 88.1%, difference 3.3% (95% CI −1.2, 7.8), non-inferiority met
- CAP-3001 (NCT00326287) is a legacy Phase 3 trial (conducted 2006-2007, reused as pivotal CABP evidence in this 2024 NDA), randomized, double-blind, active-controlled (ceftriaxone ± linezolid), 670 subjects (335/arm), 80% power, two-sided alpha 5%, 10% non-inferiority margin, with co-primary Clinically Evaluable and Intent-to-Treat analysis populations; result: CE 86.6% vs. 87.4% (difference −0.8%, 95% CI −6.9, 5.3), ITT 76.4% vs. 79.3% (difference −2.9%, 95% CI −9.3, 3.6), non-inferiority met in both; a post-hoc re-analysis applying the FDA's 2020 CABP Guidance primary endpoint (Day-3 clinical success, 12.5% margin) also met non-inferiority
- No cross-trial multiplicity adjustment was applied — each trial independently supports a distinct approved indication
- Regulatory history: ceftobiprole was first submitted to FDA in 2007 (NDA 022132, by a different sponsor, Johnson & Johnson) for complicated skin/skin-structure infections and received an Approvable Letter (2008) then two Complete Response Letters (2008, 2009) citing data-integrity/clinical deficiencies in two trials not included in the current NDA; ownership reverted to Basilea in 2011, and this 2024 NDA is built on entirely new trials (ERADICATE, TARGET) plus the older CAP-3001 CABP trial, subjected to a fresh FDA site-integrity inspection that found no issues

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/218275s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Integrated Review (no separate Statistical, Clinical, or Multi-Discipline Review was posted; combined into this single 561-page review) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/218275Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (ERADICATE) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03138733; Protocol/SAP: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/33/NCT03138733/Prot_000.pdf, https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/33/NCT03138733/SAP_001.pdf (SAP PDF's font encoding is not machine-readable; no verbatim SAP text could be extracted from it)

### 75. Sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid (Orlynvah) — NDA 213972

**Sponsor:** Iterum Therapeutics US Limited (NDA applicant); trials were run by the affiliated entity Iterum Therapeutics International Limited

**Indication approved:** Treatment of uncomplicated urinary tract infections (uUTI) caused by *Escherichia coli*, *Klebsiella pneumoniae*, or *Proteus mirabilis* in adult women who have limited or no alternative oral antibacterial treatment options — the "limited or no alternative" restriction was added following a September 2024 FDA Advisory Committee recommendation

**Approval date:** October 25, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** Trial 301 ("SURE-1"), NCT03354598 (vs. ciprofloxacin); Trial 310 ("REASSURE"), NCT05584657 (vs. amoxicillin/clavulanate) — REASSURE, not a second "SURE" trial, is the trial that actually supported this approval; a distinct trial sometimes informally grouped under "SURE" naming, Trial 302 (NCT03357614), was in fact a *complicated* UTI trial that failed its primary endpoint and is unrelated to this uUTI indication

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled (Trial 301 vs. ciprofloxacin; Trial 310/REASSURE vs. amoxicillin/clavulanate); Non-inferiority-then-superiority hierarchy (REASSURE); Dual mutually-exclusive-subgroup co-primary regulatory strategy (Trial 301 tested susceptible and comparator-resistant subpopulations as separate primary populations, with either analysis being positive sufficient to establish efficacy) **
- *Endpoints:* overall response (combined clinical + microbiologic success) at test-of-cure (Day 12±1)
- *Primary analysis:* Miettinen-Nurminen method (unstratified, Trial 301); stratified/CMH-weighted proportion difference (Trial 310)
- *Missing data/bias:* Reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan (Applicant excluded a trial site from the Trial 301 efficacy analysis after an unblinded interim look; FDA did not find sufficient reason to exclude it)
- *Regulatory:* Complete Response Letter (CRL) followed by resubmission and approval (July 2021 CRL citing lack of substantial evidence of effectiveness; approved on resubmission in 2024); Special Protocol Assessment (SPA) obtained for the post-CRL confirmatory trial *(SPA issued July 2022 specifically for Trial 310/REASSURE, the trial that ultimately supported approval)*; FDA Advisory Committee meeting held (Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee, September 9, 2024); FDA narrowing of a sponsor-proposed eligibility/line-of-therapy threshold (label restricted, per the Committee's recommendation, to women with limited or no alternative oral options)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Trial 301/"SURE-1" (NCT03354598) is a Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled trial of oral sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid vs. oral ciprofloxacin in uUTI, with a co-primary regulatory strategy testing the ciprofloxacin-susceptible (micro-MITTS) and ciprofloxacin-resistant (micro-MITTR) populations as mutually exclusive primary analyses — efficacy would be established if either population's test was positive
- In the micro-MITTS population (the one relevant to a general uUTI claim), sulopenem was **not** non-inferior to ciprofloxacin: treatment difference −11.4% (95% CI −17.9, −4.8) per the final label; sulopenem was superior to ciprofloxacin only in the resistant (micro-MITTR) subgroup, difference 15.3% (95% CI 4.4, 26.1) in FDA's primary analysis (26.6%, 95% CI 15.1, 37.4, in the Applicant's post-hoc site-exclusion analysis, which FDA declined to accept)
- A second trial in the same original submission, Trial 302 (NCT03357614), was actually a *complicated* UTI trial (IV-to-oral sulopenem vs. ertapenem-to-ciprofloxacin) and failed its primary endpoint; a third trial, Trial 303 (complicated intra-abdominal infection, NCT03358576), also failed to show non-inferiority — together with Trial 301's susceptible-population failure, these results led to a July 23, 2021 Complete Response Letter for lack of substantial evidence of effectiveness
- Following the CRL, Iterum obtained a Special Protocol Assessment (July 2022) for a new trial, Trial 310/"REASSURE" (NCT05584657): a Phase 3, multicenter, double-blind, double-dummy, randomized, controlled trial of oral sulopenem vs. oral amoxicillin/clavulanate in uUTI, with a target micro-MITTS enrollment (DMC-recommended range 1,966-2,428 subjects; 2,222 ultimately randomized)
- REASSURE's primary endpoint was overall success at Day 12 (±1)/test-of-cure in the micro-MITT, micro-MITTS, and micro-MITTR populations, with non-inferiority declared if the lower 95% CI bound exceeded −10% and superiority declared if it exceeded 0; result in micro-MITTS: 61.7% (sulopenem) vs. 55.0% (amoxicillin/clavulanate), difference 6.7% (95% CI 0.3, 13.0) — both non-inferiority and superiority met
- This 2024 NDA resubmission was discussed at a September 9, 2024 FDA Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee meeting, whose recommendations led FDA to narrow the approved indication to women with "limited or no alternative oral antibacterial treatment options"

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/213972s000lbl.pdf

### 76. Gepotidacin (Blujepa) — NDA 218230

**Sponsor:** GlaxoSmithKline, LLC

**Indication approved:** Treatment of female adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older weighing at least 40 kg with uncomplicated urinary tract infections (uUTI) caused by susceptible isolates of *Escherichia coli*, *Klebsiella pneumoniae*, *Citrobacter freundii* complex, *Staphylococcus saprophyticus*, and *Enterococcus faecalis* — the first new oral antibiotic class approved for UTI in decades (a triazaacenaphthylene bacterial type II topoisomerase inhibitor)

**Approval date:** March 25, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** EAGLE-2, NCT04020341; EAGLE-3, NCT04187144

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled (vs. nitrofurantoin); Non-inferiority-then-superiority hierarchy
- *Endpoints:* composite therapeutic response (clinical + microbiological success) at test-of-cure
- *Primary analysis:* Farrington and Manning test, stratified (by age category and acute-cystitis-recurrence status) **
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function (Pocock-type stopping boundary), one pre-planned interim analysis at ~60% of subjects reaching test-of-cure
- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- EAGLE-2 (NCT04020341) and EAGLE-3 (NCT04187144) are two identically designed Phase 3, randomized, multicenter, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled non-inferiority trials of oral gepotidacin 1,500 mg twice daily for 5 days vs. oral nitrofurantoin 100 mg twice daily for 5 days in female adult/pediatric uUTI patients, each with 4 visits over 28 days (Screening/Randomization, On-Therapy, Test-of-Cure Days 10-13, Follow-up Day 28±3)
- Primary analysis population: micro-ITT nitrofurantoin-susceptible (micro-ITT NTF-S) population in both trials
- Primary endpoint: composite response (clinical + microbiological success) at test-of-cure
- Non-inferiority margin: −10%, tested via the Farrington and Manning method stratified by age category (≤50 years, >50 years) and acute cystitis recurrence status (4 strata); if non-inferiority was declared, a superiority test was conducted for the same endpoint
- Interim monitoring: one pre-planned interim analysis when ~60% of the micro-ITT NTF-S population reached the test-of-cure visit, with nominal significance levels at the interim and final analyses determined by the Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function using a Pocock-type stopping boundary
- Result: EAGLE-2 met non-inferiority (treatment difference 4.3%, 95% CI −3.6, 12.1) but not superiority; EAGLE-3 met both non-inferiority and superiority (treatment difference 14.6%, 95% CI 6.4, 22.8)

### 77. Clesrovimab-cfor (Enflonsia) — BLA 761432

**Sponsor:** Merck Sharp & Dohme LLC

**Indication approved:** Prevention of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) lower respiratory tract disease in neonates and infants born during or entering their first RSV season — a long-acting monoclonal antibody, placebo-controlled (not compared head-to-head against nirsevimab)

**Approval date:** June 9, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** CLEVER (Trial 004 / MK-1654-004), NCT04767373

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (single intramuscular dose)
- *Endpoints:* RSV-associated medically attended lower respiratory infection (MALRI), incidence Days 1-150 postdose; RSV-associated hospitalization (key secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* CI-based success-threshold decision rule (lower bound of the 95% CI for relative risk reduction required to exceed a prespecified 25% threshold, rather than a conventional p-value hypothesis test) **
- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (primary MALRI endpoint tested before the key secondary hospitalization endpoint, both at one-sided alpha 0.025)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Group-sequential design (two pre-planned interim analyses, futility-only, no alpha adjustment required)
- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- CLEVER (NCT04767373) is a Phase 2b/3, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, multi-country (22 countries, both hemispheres) trial of a single 105 mg intramuscular dose of clesrovimab vs. saline placebo in healthy preterm (≥29 to <35 weeks gestational age) and full-term (≥35 weeks) infants entering their first RSV season; 2,411 clesrovimab and 1,203 placebo subjects in the Full Analysis Set
- Primary endpoint: incidence of RSV-associated MALRI (outpatient + inpatient), Days 1-150 postdose, defined by qualifying respiratory signs/symptoms plus an RT-PCR-confirmed RSV-positive nasopharyngeal sample; key secondary endpoint: RSV-associated hospitalization over the same window
- Statistical criterion for success (not a conventional null-hypothesis test): the lower bound of the 95% CI for the relative risk reduction had to exceed a prespecified 25% threshold for the primary endpoint (and exceed 0% for the hospitalization key secondary), tested in hierarchical order at one-sided alpha 0.025; two pre-planned interim analyses were for futility only and required no alpha-spending adjustment
- Result (FDA's independent analysis): relative risk reduction of 60.4% (95% CI 44.1, 71.9; p<0.001) for MALRI — the label's applicant-reported figure of 60.5% (95% CI 44.2, 72.0) differs trivially; both exceeded the 25% success threshold. Hospitalization key secondary: 84.3% efficacy (95% CI 66.7, 92.6) per the label

- Package Insert / Label (corrected) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/761432s000lbledt.pdf

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2502984), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40961446/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Clesrovimab+for+Prevention+of+RSV+Disease+in+Healthy+Infants)

### 78. Zoliflodacin (Nuzolvence) — NDA 219491

**Sponsor:** Entasis Therapeutics, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of uncomplicated urogenital gonorrhea due to *Neisseria gonorrhoeae* in adults and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older weighing at least 35 kg — a first-in-class spiropyrimidinetrione antibacterial, developed with support from the Global Antibiotic Research and Development Partnership (GARDP)

**Approval date:** December 12, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** STI_Zoli001, NCT03959527 (also registered as EudraCT 2019-000990-22)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, open-label, active-controlled (single-dose oral zoliflodacin vs. single-dose intramuscular ceftriaxone plus single-dose oral azithromycin)
- *Endpoints:* microbiological cure (culture-confirmed eradication of *N. gonorrhoeae* at urethral/cervical sites) at test-of-cure (Day 6±2)
- *Primary analysis:* Newcombe method for the confidence interval on a treatment difference in proportions (same Newcombe-method construction used in the cefepime/enmetazobactam entry)
- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held; FDA-negotiated widening of a pre-specified non-inferiority margin, from 10% to 12%, via an October 2022 Type C meeting **; FDA narrowing of a sponsor-proposed eligibility/line-of-therapy threshold (approved indication restricted to urogenital gonorrhea specifically, per the Integrated Review's account of the Division modifying the Applicant's proposed indication)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- STI_Zoli001 (NCT03959527) is an international, multicenter, randomized (2:1), open-label, active-controlled non-inferiority trial comparing a single 3 g oral dose of zoliflodacin to combination therapy (single 500 mg intramuscular ceftriaxone plus single 1 g oral azithromycin) in patients ≥12 years old weighing ≥35 kg with uncomplicated gonorrhea; enrolled November 2019-March 2023 at 16-17 sites in Belgium, the Netherlands, South Africa, Thailand, and the USA
- Primary analysis population: micro-ITT (urogenital) population
- Primary endpoint: microbiological cure by culture at urethral or cervical sites at test-of-cure (Day 6±2)
- Non-inferiority margin: originally specified as 10% in the protocol, widened to 12% after FDA indicated (per a Type C meeting, October 2022) that a wider margin could be acceptable; assessed via a two-sided 95% Newcombe score CI
- Sample size: target micro-ITT population of 696 (up to ~928 randomized to reach that target)
- Result: zoliflodacin cure 460/506 (90.9%) vs. ceftriaxone-azithromycin cure 229/238 (96.2%); difference −5.3% (95% CI −8.6, −1.4) — within the 12% non-inferiority margin (and also within a more conservative 10% margin), though FDA noted the confidence interval for the treatment difference was "completely below zero," i.e., zoliflodacin was statistically inferior to the combination even while meeting the pre-specified non-inferiority criterion
- FDA modified the Applicant's originally proposed (not site-restricted) indication to specifically "uncomplicated urogenital gonorrhea," per the Integrated Review, citing confirmatory evidence from a separate Phase 2 open-label trial (DMID 14-0014) for that narrower claim

### 79. Doravirine/islatravir (Idvynso) — NDA 216964

**Sponsor:** Merck Sharp & Dohme LLC

**Indication approved:** As a complete two-drug regimen (100 mg doravirine / 0.25 mg islatravir once daily) to replace the current antiretroviral regimen in adults with HIV-1 infection who are virologically suppressed (HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL) on a stable regimen, with no history of virologic failure and no known doravirine-resistance substitutions — a **switch-only** indication; a treatment-naive Phase 3 trial (NCT05705349) exists but is not part of this approval

**Approval date:** April 20, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** Trial 051, NCT05631093 (switch from any oral ART); Trial 052, NCT05630755 (switch from bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, open-label, active-controlled (Trial 051, 2:1 randomization vs. continuing baseline ART); Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled (Trial 052, 2:1 vs. bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide)
- *Endpoints:* proportion with HIV-1 RNA ≥50 copies/mL at Week 48 (virologic non-response)
- *Primary analysis:* Miettinen-Nurminen method (stratified by baseline ART regimen in Trial 051; unstratified in Trial 052)
- *Missing data/bias:* FDA Snapshot algorithm for handling missing virologic-response data **
- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held ("this drug is not the first in its class")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Trial 051 (NCT05631093) is a Phase 3, randomized (2:1), open-label, active-controlled non-inferiority trial switching virologically suppressed adults from any oral antiretroviral regimen to doravirine/islatravir (100 mg/0.25 mg) vs. continuing baseline ART (N=366 vs. N=185)
- Trial 052 (NCT05630755) is a Phase 3, randomized (2:1), double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled non-inferiority trial switching virologically suppressed adults from bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide to doravirine/islatravir vs. continuing bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide (N=342 vs. N=171)
- Primary endpoint (both trials): proportion of participants with HIV-1 RNA ≥50 copies/mL at Week 48, using the FDA Snapshot algorithm to classify missing/discontinued participants as non-responders
- Non-inferiority margin: 4 percentage points (not the 10% margin more commonly used in earlier-generation HIV switch trials), assessed via the Miettinen-Nurminen method — stratified by baseline ART regimen in Trial 051, unstratified in Trial 052 (only one baseline regimen, bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide, was eligible)
- One-sided type I error of 0.0249 per the SAP
- Results at Week 48: Trial 051 — doravirine/islatravir 1% vs. baseline ART 5% (difference −3.6%, 95% CI −7.8, −0.8); Trial 052 — doravirine/islatravir 1% vs. bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide 1% (difference 0.9%, 95% CI −1.9, 2.9) — non-inferiority met in both
- Development history: an earlier, higher-dose islatravir formulation (up to 2.25 mg) program was placed under a partial FDA clinical hold in December 2021 after exposure-response modeling linked higher islatravir exposures to lymphocyte and CD4+ T-cell declines; the label states no clinically meaningful reduction in lymphocytes/CD4+ T-cells was observed at exposures associated with the approved 0.25 mg dose

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/216964Orig1s000lbl.pdf

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(25)01948-8), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41654375/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Switch+to+fixed-dose+doravirine+and+islatravir+once+daily+bictegravir+emtricitabine+tenofovir+alafenamide)

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(25)01945-2), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41654374/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Switch+to+fixed-dose+doravirine+and+islatravir+once+daily+oral+antiretroviral+therapy)

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held: the approval letter cites "(1) this drug is not the first in its class (2) the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues that were unexpected for a drug of this class."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*No FDA Statistical or Clinical Review has been posted for this NDA as of this research (direct URL probes for Statistical Review, Clinical/Medical Review, Summary Review, and Integrated Review all returned HTTP 404), so the excerpts below come from the genuine sponsor protocol/SAP posted on ClinicalTrials.gov rather than from an FDA review.*

*[verbatim, ClinicalTrials.gov-posted Trial 052 Protocol/SAP (NCT05630755, "MK-8591A-052-02 FINAL PROTOCOL"), internal p.121]*

> "For the primary hypothesis (H1), DOR/ISL will be considered non-inferior to BIC/FTC/TAF if the upper bound of the 2-sided multiplicity-adjusted 95% CI for the between-treatment difference in the percentage of participants with HIV-1 RNA ≥50 copies/mL at Week 48 (DOR/ISL minus BIC/FTC/TAF) is less than 4 percentage points (non-inferiority margin). The CI will be based on the unstratified Miettinen and Nurminen method... The FDA snapshot algorithm [Food and Drug Administration (CDER) 2015] will be used to handle missing data for the analysis of the primary efficacy hypothesis."

*[verbatim, Trial 052 Protocol/SAP, internal p.143]*

> "The non-inferiority margin is 4 percentage points. To establish non-inferiority, the upper bound of the 2-sided 95% CI for the difference between groups (Group 1 minus Group 2) in the percentage of participants with HIV-1 RNA ≥50 copies/mL must be <4 percentage points... The 1-sided Type 1 error is 0.0249."

- *[inferred from the 4-percentage-point margin, narrower than the classic 10% HIV treatment-initiation NI margin, and from the label's exposure-response language]*: the tighter margin and the CD4/lymphocyte exposure-response caveat in label Section 12.2 together suggest FDA required both a stricter efficacy standard and close safety scrutiny for a switch population already on suppressive therapy, consistent with — but not independently confirmed by — the drug's 2021 partial-clinical-hold history at higher islatravir doses.

### 80. Bulevirtide-gmod (Hepcludex) — BLA 761468

**Sponsor:** Gilead Sciences, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of chronic hepatitis delta virus (HDV) infection in adults without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis — approved under accelerated approval based on a decrease in HDV RNA and ALT normalization; an improvement in disease-related clinical outcomes has not been established. Bulevirtide was previously approved in the EU (conditional marketing authorization, 2020; converted to full authorization, 2023) under the same brand name; this is its first US approval

**Approval date:** May 22, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** MYR301, NCT03852719

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, open-label, delayed-treatment-controlled design (no placebo arm, given the absence of any approved HDV therapy at the time; delayed-treatment subjects crossed over to active drug after the Week-48 primary assessment) **
- *Endpoints:* combined response at Week 48 (virologic response — undetectable HDV RNA or ≥2 log10 IU/mL decrease from baseline — plus ALT normalization)
- *Primary analysis:* Fisher's exact test
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* alpha split across two analysis timepoints — 0.01 (2-sided) for a Week-24 interim look, 0.04 for the Week-48 final analysis, from an overall 0.05 **
- *Regulatory:* Accelerated approval based on a non-oncology surrogate endpoint (combined virologic + biochemical response), postmarketing confirmatory study required *(the taxonomy's existing accelerated-approval entries are oncology-specific)*; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- MYR301 (NCT03852719) is a Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, open-label trial in adults with chronic HDV infection and compensated liver disease, comparing bulevirtide 2 mg/day and bulevirtide 10 mg/day (nominal; delivered dose later determined to be 8.5 mg, the approved dose) subcutaneously once daily, each vs. a delayed-treatment (48-week observation, then bulevirtide 10 mg/day) control arm; 150 subjects randomized (FDA's primary efficacy comparison used 101 subjects, bulevirtide 10 mg [n=50] vs. delayed treatment [n=51], per the Multi-Discipline Review; the approved label separately reports N=50 vs. N=51 for the 8.5 mg dose)
- Primary endpoint: combined response at Week 48, defined as achieving both (1) undetectable HDV RNA (<LLOQ/target not detected) or a ≥2 log10 IU/mL decrease from baseline, and (2) ALT normalization
- Primary analysis method: proportions of subjects with combined response for each bulevirtide dose group compared with the delayed-treatment group via Fisher's exact test, with the overall 0.05 two-sided significance level split as 0.01 for a Week-24 interim analysis and 0.04 for the Week-48 final analysis
- Sample size/power: 47 patients per arm gave 97.8% power at a 0.04 two-sided significance level, assuming ≥45% response in the bulevirtide arms and ≤8% in the delayed-treatment arm; increased to 50 per arm (150 total) to allow for early withdrawals
- Result: combined response — delayed treatment 1/51 (2.0%); bulevirtide 2 mg 22/49 (44.9%); bulevirtide 10 mg 24/50 (48.0%); difference (10 mg minus delayed treatment) 46.0% (96% CI 30.5, 61.4), p<0.0001; difference (2 mg minus delayed treatment) 42.9% (96% CI 27.0, 58.5), p<0.0001. Label reports (8.5 mg approved dose): combined response 48% vs. 2%, difference 46% (96% CI 31, 61)
- No validated clinical-outcome (as opposed to surrogate) endpoint exists for chronic HDV, which FDA's review cites as the basis for using accelerated approval; the postmarketing requirement (PMR 4982-1) is an observational study of bulevirtide-treated vs. historical/untreated control patients, up to 5 years' follow-up, due 2034

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/761468Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (no separate Statistical or Clinical Review was posted; combined into this single 287-page review) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761468Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2213429), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37345876/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=A+Phase+3+Randomized+Trial+of+Bulevirtide+in+Chronic+Hepatitis+D)

- EMA granted Hepcludex conditional marketing authorization in the EU on July 31, 2020, converted to a standard marketing authorization on July 18, 2023 — well before this first US approval.
- A requested Tropical Disease Priority Review Voucher was denied, as HDV is not a designated tropical disease.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held: the approval letter states "outside expertise was not necessary as there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, 761468Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf, p.12]*

> "The efficacy of bulevirtide 8.5 mg (nominal 10 mg) administered subcutaneously once daily was evaluated in one pivotal Phase 3 trial (MYR301), with supportive data from three Phase 2 trials (MYR202, MYR203, MYR204). Trial MYR301 was a randomized, open-label, multicenter trial in 150 adults with chronic HDV infection and compensated liver disease. The trial compared BLV 10 mg and BLV 2 mg, both administered subcutaneously once daily, to a delayed treatment arm for 48 weeks."

*[verbatim, ClinicalTrials.gov-posted SAP ("MYR301 Statistical Analysis Plan Final 3.0," 2021-08-20), p.11, sample size]*

With a sample size of 47 patients per treatment group a Fisher's exact test with a 0.04 two-sided significance level will have 97.8% power... This sample size will be slightly increased to 50 patients per treatment group to account for a few potential early withdrawals before exposure. Hence 150 patients will be randomized."

ALT normalization... The proportions of subjects with combined response at Week 48 for each of bulevirtide 2 mg and bulevirtide 10 mg will be compared with the control group of delayed treatment. Fisher's exact test will be used... The overall significance level will be 0.05... the nominal two-sided significance level will be split among the time points with 0.01 for Week 24 and 0.04 for Week 48."

### 81. Cefepime/zidebactam (Zaynich) — NDA 220787

**Sponsor:** Wockhardt Bio AG (c/o VRT Pharma Consulting LLC)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adult patients with complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI), including pyelonephritis, caused by designated susceptible microorganisms (cefepime, an FDA-approved cephalosporin, combined with zidebactam, a novel beta-lactamase inhibitor/non-beta-lactam antibacterial)

**Approval date:** May 29, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** Study W-5222-301, NCT04979806

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, active-controlled; non-inferiority-then-superiority hierarchy (prespecified superiority testing conditional on demonstrated non-inferiority); dose-arm/regimen 2:1 randomization
- *Endpoints:* composite overall response/success (clinical cure + microbiologic eradication) at test-of-cure
- *Primary analysis:* Miettinen-Nurminen method; Farrington-Manning sample-size approach
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (non-inferiority tested first, superiority conditional on non-inferiority)
- *Missing data/bias:* worst-case sensitivity imputation of missing/indeterminate binary responder outcomes, imputed as success in the control arm and failure in the treatment arm
- *Regulatory:* Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) designation; FDA declines a superiority labeling claim from a single trial pending replication

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study W-5222-301: a single, randomized (2:1), double-blind, multicenter, multinational, active-comparator, non-inferiority phase 3 trial of cefepime-zidebactam (FEP-ZID, 3 g total: 2 g cefepime + 1 g zidebactam, IV) vs. meropenem in adults with cUTI (including acute pyelonephritis, with or without concurrent bacteremia); 7-10 days of therapy with no oral step-down; randomization stratified by entry diagnosis (cUTI vs. AP) and geographic region
- Primary efficacy population: mMITT-STIC (microbiological modified intent-to-treat, defined using susceptibility testing interpretive criteria — excludes subjects whose infection was caused solely/partly by a carbapenem-resistant pathogen); other prespecified populations included ITT, MITT, e-mMITT, clinically evaluable (CE), and microbiologically evaluable (ME)
- Primary efficacy endpoint: overall outcome (composite of clinical cure and microbiological eradication) at test-of-cure (TOC, 17±3 days after randomization) in the mMITT-STIC population
- Secondary endpoints: overall outcome at TOC in CE/ME populations; overall outcome at end-of-therapy (EOT); clinical and microbiological outcomes individually at EOT/TOC across populations; by-pathogen outcomes; clinical outcome at late follow-up (LFU)
- Sample size: assumed 70% overall success rate, 75% evaluability, 85% power, 2:1 randomization, one-sided alpha=0.025, and a 15% non-inferiority (NI) margin (wider than the 10% margin generally recommended by FDA's 2018 cUTI guidance, justified by FEP-ZID's target population of multidrug-resistant/extensively-drug-resistant gram-negative pathogens including metallo-beta-lactamase producers); required 396 mMITT subjects via a Farrington-Manning sample-size approach for the Miettinen-Nurminen method, implying 528 ITT subjects
- Primary analysis: unstratified Miettinen-Nurminen method for the 95% CI of the risk difference (overall success rate, FEP-ZID minus meropenem); NI declared if the CI lower bound exceeded -15%; superiority (a secondary, prespecified analysis in the e-mMITT population) declared if the CI lower bound exceeded 0
- Result: overall success in 89.0% (250/281) of FEP-ZID subjects vs. 68.4% (93/136) of meropenem subjects in the mMITT-STIC population, treatment difference 20.6% (95% CI 12.3, 29.5) — non-inferiority met; in the preplanned e-mMITT superiority analysis, treatment difference 16.5% (95% CI 8.5, 25.0) — superiority also met, but FDA declined to grant a superiority labeling claim because the finding came from only a single trial (evidence of superiority is generally expected to be replicated in two adequate and well-controlled studies) and because the effect was found to be driven mainly by the microbiological component of the composite, with a much smaller clinical-component treatment difference (1.9%)
- Sensitivity analyses: a stratified (by entry diagnosis and region) Miettinen-Nurminen CI narrowed the lower bound slightly (11.8% vs. 12.3% unstratified); worst-case imputation of missing/indeterminate TOC outcomes as success for meropenem and failure for FEP-ZID still yielded a positive lower bound (9.6%), all well above the -15% NI margin, leading FDA to characterize the NI finding as "highly robust"

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2026/220787Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/220787Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Integrated Review (combined summary/clinical/statistical/nonclinical review) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/220787Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (Study W-5222-301) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04979806 (completed; no protocol/SAP documents posted in the Documents tab as of this writing)
- No peer-reviewed pivotal-trial publication for Study W-5222-301 was found as of this writing; the only indexed publication specific to this approval is an Adis "New Drug" profile: Shirley M. "Cefepime/Zidebactam: First Approval." *Drugs.* 2026 Aug 19. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40265-026-02374-2), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42616342/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Cefepime%20Zidebactam%20First%20Approval)

**Other resources**

- Wockhardt-specific IPD/dataset access via Vivli or YODA was not individually confirmed here.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held; the Integrated Review states one "was not necessary for this drug, as there were no controversial issues" warranting it.
- Development history: zidebactam (WCK 5107) was first submitted under IND 116002 in 2015; QIDP and Fast Track designations were granted December 4, 2015, for cUTI, complicated intra-abdominal infection, and hospital-/ventilator-associated bacterial pneumonia indications, though only the cUTI indication was ultimately approved in this NDA.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, Section 6.2.1.3 "Statistical Analysis Plan, Study W-5222-301," p.28]*

> "Based on these findings, the study assumed a 70% overall success rate at TOC, 75% evaluability rate, 85% power, 2:1 randomization, and a one-sided alpha of 0.025. Using a Farrington-Manning sample size approach for the Miettinen and Nurminen method, a total of 396 subjects were required in the mMITT population... An NI margin of 10% is usually recommended for the cUTI indication based on the FDA guidance for industry Complicated Urinary Tract Infections: Developing Drugs for Treatment (June 2018)... However, an NI margin of 15% has been considered acceptable in this development program as FEP-ZID targets a wide range of multidrug-resistant/extensively drug-resistant gram-negative bacteria, including metallo-β-lactamase (MBL)-producers."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, Section 6.2.1.4 "Results of Analyses," efficacy results, p.36-37]*

> "Overall success rates were observed in 250 (89.0%) subjects in the FEP-ZID arm versus 93 (68.4%) subjects in the meropenem arm, with a treatment difference of 20.6% (95% CI: 12.3, 29.5). Since the lower limit of the 95% CI for the treatment difference was greater than or equal to the noninferiority margin of −15.0%, FEP-ZID demonstrated noninferiority to meropenem. In the preplanned superiority analysis conducted in the e-mMITT population, the overall success rate was observed in 259 (87.2%) subjects in the FEP-ZID arm versus 104 (70.7%) subjects in the meropenem arm, with a treatment difference of 16.5% (95% CI: 8.5, 25.0). Since the lower limit of the 95% CI for the treatment difference was greater than 0, FEP-ZID demonstrated superiority to meropenem. FEP-ZID demonstrated superiority to meropenem in Study W-5222-301; however, the Division recommended against a superiority claim... since the evidence of superiority was obtained from only a single study. For [redacted] superiority, we generally recommend that the evidence of superiority be replicated in two adequate and well-controlled studies."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, Section 6.3.2 "Limited Interpretation of Superiority Findings Based on Overall Success," p.48]*

> "Findings for the two components of overall success ('clinical success' and 'microbiological success') were observed to be very different, with respect to both the overall rates and the magnitude of the treatment effect... This relatively strong influence of the microbiological component and relatively weak influence of the clinical component in the overall success definition clearly benefited the FEP-ZID arm, which showed a large treatment benefit for the microbiological component (20.5%) and a much smaller benefit for the clinical component (1.9%)."

### 82. Ensitrelvir (Xocova) — NDA 220442

**Sponsor:** Shionogi Inc.

**Indication approved:** Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) in adults and adolescents 12 years of age and older following contact with an individual who has COVID-19 (oral SARS-CoV-2 main protease [Mpro/3CLpro] inhibitor) — note this initial U.S. approval is for prophylaxis, not treatment; ensitrelvir was not submitted for a U.S. COVID-19 treatment indication with this NDA

**Approval date:** May 29, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** SCORPIO-PEP (Study 2206T1331), NCT05897541

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; household-contact post-exposure prophylaxis design
- *Endpoints:* symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection incidence (risk ratio), post-exposure prophylaxis
- *Primary analysis:* Poisson regression with generalized estimating equations (GEE) and robust (sandwich) variance for risk-ratio estimation
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (primary endpoint then key secondary endpoint, both two-sided alpha=0.05)
- *Missing data/bias:* ICH E9(R1) estimand framework with treatment-policy and composite intercurrent-event strategies
- *Regulatory:* FDA-documented subgroup efficacy heterogeneity (region, timing-to-enrollment) accepted as a non-disqualifying limitation; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held; prior emergency/full regulatory approval in Japan preceding this U.S. approval

**Trial design & endpoints**

- SCORPIO-PEP: a Phase 3, randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial (178 sites, 5 countries: primarily U.S., Japan, plus Argentina, South Africa, Vietnam pooled as "rest of world") of oral ensitrelvir (375 mg Day 1, then 125 mg Days 2-5) vs. placebo in household contacts of an individual with symptomatic COVID-19, enrolled within 72 hours of the index patient's symptom onset; randomization stratified by time-to-enrollment (<48h vs. 48-72h) and geographic region
- Primary efficacy endpoint: risk ratio (ensitrelvir vs. placebo) of the proportion of participants with central-laboratory-confirmed positive SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR and onset of COVID-19 symptoms through Day 10 (mITT population, N=2,041)
- Key secondary endpoint: the same risk-ratio definition analyzed in the ITT population (N=2,387)
- Sample size: assumed a 7.0% placebo-arm incidence and a target risk ratio of 0.5, requiring ~92 events from ~2,200 participants (1:1) for 90% power at two-sided alpha=0.05; the SAP prespecified that enrollment could be expanded (to ~2,600) if the event rate ran lower than assumed; no interim analysis was planned or performed
- Primary analysis method: Poisson regression with a GEE approach (exchangeable working correlation within household, sandwich/robust variance estimator), covariates = treatment group, time from index-patient symptom onset to enrollment (<48h/≥48h), and geographic region (North America/Japan/rest of world); statistical success criterion = upper bound of the 95% CI for the risk ratio <1
- Intercurrent events handled per a prespecified estimand: withdrawal due to rescue/prohibited medication used a treatment-policy strategy (continued follow-up, data used in the primary analysis); death, hospitalization, or study withdrawal before the primary-endpoint event used a composite strategy (counted as infected-with-symptoms from that time)
- Result (mITT, primary): risk ratio 0.33 (95% CI 0.22, 0.49), p<0.0001 — a 67% relative risk reduction (2.9% ensitrelvir vs. 9.0% placebo); key secondary (ITT) result: risk ratio 0.43 (95% CI 0.32, 0.59), p<0.0001; five sensitivity-analysis settings (including reversing an Applicant exclusion for two subjects flagged for site misconduct) all produced closely aligned risk ratios (0.33-0.41)
- FDA-identified limitation: a substantial regional inconsistency in the primary endpoint's risk ratio — Japan 0.18 (95% CI 0.10, 0.33) vs. North America 0.60 (95% CI 0.32, 1.12) vs. rest-of-world 0.84 (95% CI 0.27, 2.61), driven by a much higher placebo-arm event rate in Japan (22.96%) than North America (3.66%); a post hoc Japan-vs-North-America interaction test gave p=0.014. A second, similar inconsistency was seen by enrollment timing (risk ratio 0.26 for <48h vs. 0.69 for 48-72h, post hoc interaction p=0.04). Neither FDA nor the Applicant could identify a single explanatory factor (candidates included differing baseline antibody titers, index-patient viral RNA levels, and circulating SARS-CoV-2 variants); FDA concluded the trial was not designed to demonstrate region-specific efficacy and that the totality of data still supported effectiveness across regions, while flagging the inconsistency as a labeled limitation of the review
- Confirmatory evidence: the Applicant did not submit efficacy data from two COVID-19 treatment trials (ACTIV-2d and the Phase 3 portion of SCORPIO-SR) with this NDA, per Agency advice that the data would likely be inadequate to support a treatment indication; virologic data from those trials (0.7-1.5 log10 viral RNA reduction vs. placebo at Day 4) were submitted and accepted by FDA as confirmatory (not primary) evidence supporting the PEP indication

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2026/220442Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/220442Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Combined Summary, Clinical and Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/220442Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- FDA Clinical Pharmacology Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/220442Orig1s000ClinPharmR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (SCORPIO-PEP) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05897541 (completed; no protocol/SAP documents posted in the Documents tab as of this writing)
- Pivotal publication: Hayden FG, Shinkai M, Clark TW, et al., for the SCORPIO-PEP Study Team. "Ensitrelvir for Covid-19 Postexposure Prophylaxis in Household Contacts." *N Engl J Med.* 2026;394(19):1905-1915. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2509306), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42127390/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Ensitrelvir%20for%20Covid-19%20Postexposure%20Prophylaxis%20in%20Household%20Contacts)

**Other resources**

- Shionogi-specific IPD/dataset access via Vivli or YODA was not individually confirmed here.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held for this application.
- Regulatory/international context: ensitrelvir received emergency regulatory approval in Japan in November 2022 (under Japan's expedited pathway) and full approval there in March 2024; it was also approved in Singapore (November 2023). FDA granted Fast Track designation for COVID-19 treatment in March 2023, later extended; this NDA is ensitrelvir's first U.S. approval, and it is for post-exposure prophylaxis specifically, a narrower indication than Xocova's approved use in Japan.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Combined Summary, Clinical and Statistical Review, Section 6.2.4 "Statistical Analysis Plan, SCORPIO-PEP," p.48]*

> "For the primary endpoint analysis, a Poisson regression model with a generalized estimating equations (GEE) approach and robust variance was used to estimate the risk ratio of the incidence of infection with SARS-CoV-2 (central laboratory-confirmed positive RT-PCR test) and having COVID-19 symptoms onset through Day 10 between the two treatment groups. In the GEE approach, an exchangeable structure was applied to model the correlation between any pair of participants within the same household and the sandwich estimator for the structure was used for the robust inference... The statistical criterion for success requires the upper bound of 95% CI of the risk ratio to be < 1. The significance level is 0.05 (two-sided)."

*[verbatim, FDA Combined Summary, Clinical and Statistical Review, Table 10 and surrounding text, p.54]*

> "Ensitrelvir shows a statistically significant reduction in the risk of symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection through Day 10 in household contacts of an individual with symptomatic COVID-19; risk ratio (0.33 [95% CI: 0.22 - 0.49]; p-value <0.0001). The upper bound of 95% CI for the risk ratio was less than 1, thereby the trial met the statistical criterion for success."

*[verbatim, FDA Combined Summary, Clinical and Statistical Review, Section 6.3.1 "Potential inconsistencies in efficacy across geographic regions," p.60]*

> "Although the primary efficacy endpoint of risk ratio of COVID-19 through Day 10 was met in SCORPIO-PEP, the review team noted potential inconsistencies in efficacy across geographic regions; specifically, the risk ratio was substantially lower in Japan (0.18, 95% CI: 0.10, 0.33) than North America (0.60, 95% CI: 0.32, 1.12) and the rest of the world (0.84, 95% CI: 0.27, 2.61)... Neither the Applicant nor the FDA were able to identify a single factor responsible for the potential difference in efficacy observed across geographic regions... SCORPIO-PEP was not designed to detect differences in efficacy across geographic regions or to demonstrate efficacy in each individual geographic region. Overall, the totality of the clinical data indicates that ensitrelvir is effective across the regions despite regional variations in the rate of symptomatic COVID-19 events among placebo recipients."

### 83. Tebipenem pivoxil (Utebzi) — NDA 215960

**Sponsor:** GlaxoSmithKline LLC (GSK), under an exclusive license from Spero Therapeutics, Inc., which conducted the pivotal trial and the original NDA submission

**Indication approved:** Treatment of complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI), including pyelonephritis, in adult patients — an oral penem (carbapenem-class) antibacterial, notable as potentially the first oral carbapenem approved in the United States

**Approval date:** June 17, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** SPR994-305 / PIVOT-PO, NCT06059846

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled non-inferiority trial (oral tebipenem plus IV placebo vs. IV imipenem-cilastatin plus oral placebo); group-sequential design; Special Protocol Assessment (SPA) agreement for a second confirmatory Phase 3 trial following a Complete Response Letter
- *Endpoints:* composite overall response/success (clinical cure + microbiologic eradication) at test-of-cure
- *Primary analysis:* stratified Miettinen-Nurminen method
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* rho-family error-spending boundary (Jennison-Turnbull 2000) for both the efficacy boundary (rho=2) and a non-binding futility boundary (rho=3); Independent Data Monitoring Committee (IDMC)
- *Missing data/bias:* ICH E9(R1) estimand framework with treatment-policy and composite intercurrent-event strategies
- *Regulatory:* Complete Response Letter (CRL) followed by resubmission and approval, using an entirely new confirmatory Phase 3 trial rather than added data to the original trial; reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan (Applicant used an ad hoc confidence-interval construction rather than the SAP-prespecified stratified Miettinen-Nurminen method); Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) designation; FDA Advisory Committee meeting planned then cancelled once statistical issues with the original pivotal trial were identified

**Trial design & endpoints**

- SPR994-305 (PIVOT-PO): a Phase 3, randomized (1:1), double-blind, double-dummy, multicenter, multinational, active-controlled non-inferiority trial of oral tebipenem pivoxil hydrobromide (TBP-PI-HBr, 600 mg q6h plus dummy IV infusion) vs. IV imipenem-cilastatin (500 mg q6h plus dummy oral tablets) for 7-10 days in adults hospitalized with cUTI or acute pyelonephritis; conducted December 2023-February 2025, predominantly in Central/Eastern Europe (90% of the micro-ITT population: Romania, Bulgaria, Serbia, Georgia, Poland); randomization stratified by age (<65 vs. ≥65), baseline diagnosis (cUTI vs. AP), and urinary-tract-instrumentation status
- Primary analysis population: micro-ITT (all randomized subjects with a baseline Enterobacterales uropathogen, or specified other pathogens, against which imipenem has activity, and no more than two baseline organisms); N=929 of 1,690 enrolled (55%)
- Primary efficacy endpoint: overall response at test-of-cure (TOC) in the micro-ITT population — a binary composite, TRUE only if the subject achieved both clinical cure (resolution/significant improvement of cUTI/AP signs and symptoms, no further antimicrobial therapy warranted) and per-subject microbiological eradication (baseline uropathogens reduced to <10^3 CFU/mL, negative repeat blood culture if applicable) at TOC
- Secondary endpoints: overall response at EOT/LFU; clinical response and microbiological response individually at EOT/TOC/LFU across micro-ITT/CE/ME populations; outcomes restricted to subjects with drug-resistant Enterobacterales
- Sample size/design: planned to enroll ~2,648 subjects for ~1,588 evaluable (60% assumed evaluability); a single interim analysis (IA) was planned at 60% information fraction (954 micro-ITT subjects) for possible early stopping for efficacy or futility, using Jennison-Turnbull (2000) rho-family error-spending functions (rho=2 for the efficacy/alpha boundary, rho=3 for a non-binding futility/beta boundary); overall one-sided alpha=0.025, NI margin Delta=10%, 89% power assuming 60%/58% overall response rates
- Statistical method: one-sided testing of H0: (p_trt - p_ctrl) <= -10% via a stratified (by randomization strata) Miettinen-Nurminen confidence interval for the risk difference, using Miettinen-Nurminen (1985) Equation 16 weights; NI declared if the CI lower bound exceeded -10%
- Interim result: at the IA (929 micro-ITT subjects, 58.5% information fraction), the adjusted one-sided alpha was 0.009 (98.2% CI), and the study stopped for efficacy — the IA dataset became the final dataset (enrollment had been paused pending the IA)
- Primary result (FDA's direct stratified Miettinen-Nurminen CI): overall response 58.5% (261/446) tebipenem vs. 60.2% (291/483) imipenem-cilastatin, risk difference -1.15% (98.2% CI -8.64, 6.32) — non-inferiority declared, as the lower bound exceeded the -10% margin
- Regulatory history: Spero's original NDA 215960 (submitted October 27, 2021) relied on trial SPR994-301 (ADAPT-PO: tebipenem 600 mg q8h vs. IV ertapenem); FDA issued a Complete Response Letter on June 24, 2022, citing failure to demonstrate substantial evidence of effectiveness in the ertapenem-susceptible population against a 12.5% NI margin, plus deficiencies in the bioanalytical assay supporting PK/PD target-attainment analyses. Spero (with GSK, following an exclusive license) then conducted SPR994-305 with three key design changes: increased dosing frequency (q6h vs. q8h), a switched comparator (imipenem-cilastatin instead of ertapenem, to permit enterococcal co-infections), and a prospectively narrowed micro-ITT definition restricted to imipenem-susceptible Enterobacterales; FDA granted Special Protocol Assessment agreement for this redesigned trial on July 25, 2023
- FDA statistical review issue (Section 6.3.1): the Applicant computed its one-sided NI p-value (0.003) and 95% CI (-7.5, 4.8) via an ad hoc multi-step procedure (constructing per-stratum 95% Miettinen-Nurminen CIs, then combining via inverse-variance weights derived from those CI widths) rather than directly constructing the SAP-prespecified 98.2% stratified Miettinen-Nurminen CI; FDA's direct-approach 98.2% CI (-8.64, 6.32) and the Applicant's ad hoc-derived 98.2% CI (-8.73, 6.03) both excluded the -10% margin, so FDA's review used its own direct-approach result as authoritative while noting both methods reached the same NI conclusion
- FDA also rejected the Applicant's proposed "extended micro-ITT" population (which would have included baseline pathogens regardless of susceptibility to the control drug) for identifying target pathogens/breakpoints, on the grounds that hypothesis testing of efficacy is not valid without a susceptible comparator — the micro-ITT population (the prespecified primary-analysis population) was used instead

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2026/215960Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/215960Origs000lbl.pdf
- FDA Integrated Review (combined summary/clinical/statistical/nonclinical review, second-cycle resubmission) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/215960Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (SPR994-305/PIVOT-PO) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06059846 (completed; sponsor Spero Therapeutics; no protocol/SAP documents posted in the Documents tab as of this writing)
- No peer-reviewed publication for SPR994-305 (PIVOT-PO) — the trial that is the primary evidence of effectiveness for this 2026 approval — was found as of this writing
- Background publication (earlier trial, SPR994-301/ADAPT-PO, which supported the original 2021 NDA and was the subject of the 2022 Complete Response Letter, not the primary evidence for this approval): Eckburg PB, Muir L, Critchley IA, et al. "Oral Tebipenem Pivoxil Hydrobromide in Complicated Urinary Tract Infection." *N Engl J Med.* 2022;386(14):1327-1338. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2105462), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35388666/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Oral%20Tebipenem%20Pivoxil%20Hydrobromide%20in%20Complicated%20Urinary%20Tract%20Infection)

**Other resources**

- GSK's general participation in clinical-trial data-sharing programs (e.g., ClinicalStudyDataRequest.com) was not individually confirmed for this trial/application.
- An FDA Advisory Committee meeting was originally planned during the first review cycle (to discuss substantial evidence of effectiveness for a limited-use cUTI indication and stewardship measures for an oral carbapenem) but was cancelled once the review team identified the statistical issues with the primary endpoint in trial SPR994-301, since an AC meeting was no longer judged necessary to inform the (negative) decision at that time; no AC meeting was held during the resubmission cycle reviewed here.
- Tebipenem pivoxil (as ORAPENEM, a different salt/dosage form) has been marketed in Japan since 2009 for pediatric bacterial pneumonia, otitis media, and sinusitis; the U.S. formulation (hydrobromide salt, tablet) is a distinct product.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, Section 6.2.2.3 "Statistical Analysis Plan, Study SPR994-305," p.34]*

> "For the primary endpoint, the null and alternative hypotheses are, respectively, that TBP-PI-HBr is and is not inferior to imipenem-cilastatin with respect to a NI margin Δ = 10%... One-sided hypothesis testing for the risk difference at the significance level α involves computing a (1 − 2α) confidence interval for this risk difference, using the stratified (using the randomization strata) Miettinen and Nurminen method with the weights in Equation 16 of Miettinen and Nurminen (1985). If the lower bound of the confidence interval is greater than −Δ, then the noninferiority of TBP-PI-HBr will be declared... An interim analysis (IA) was planned to assess both efficacy and futility by the Independent Data Monitoring Committee (IDMC)... The significance level at the IA was adjusted to control the overall type-1 error rate using rho family error spending boundaries given by f(t) = αt^ρ... The stopping boundary for assessing efficacy at interim used ρ = 2 and a (nonbinding) stopping rule for futility at interim used ρ = 3."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, Section 6.3.1 "Confidence Interval Method," p.59-60]*

> "The Applicant used an ad hoc procedure to construct the confidence interval for the primary analysis. The statistical analysis plan specified that the primary endpoint would be evaluated using a stratified Miettinen-Nurminen (MN) procedure. At the interim analysis, the adjusted one-sided significance level was 0.009. Instead of constructing a 1−2×0.009=98.2% stratified MN confidence interval (CI) for the risk difference (RD), the Applicant computed a one-sided p-value using [a multi-step, per-stratum-CI-derived] procedure... This direct approach is preferable to the ad hoc approach followed by the Applicant... Under the direct approach, the 98.2% stratified MN CI for the RD is (−8.64%, 6.32%), which does not include the −10% NI margin. Under the approach used by the Applicant, the stratified 98.2% CI for the RD is (−8.73%, 6.03%)... Both approaches reject the −10% NI margin, indicating that the treatment was noninferior to the active control."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, regulatory history and CR letter deficiency, p.42-43]*

> "Spero Therapeutics, Inc. submitted NDA 215960 on October 27, 2021, based on the phase 3 trial SPR994-301 (ADAPT-PO), which compared oral TBP-PI-HBr 600 mg every eight hours to intravenous ertapenem. On June 24, 2022, FDA issued a CR letter stating that the application could not be approved in its present form. The CR letter cited failure to provide substantial evidence of effectiveness as the primary deficiency precluding approval: in the ertapenem-susceptible population... the overall response at test of cure did not meet the predetermined noninferiority margin of 12.5%... To address the clinical efficacy deficiency, Spero conducted a new phase 3 trial, SPR994-305 (PIVOT-PO), with key design modifications: (1) increased dosing frequency... (2) changed comparator from ertapenem to imipenem-cilastatin... and (3) prospectively defined the primary analysis population (micro-ITT) to include only subjects with imipenem-susceptible Enterobacterales species. FDA granted Special Protocol Assessment agreement for the trial design on July 25, 2023."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, Section 11 "Advisory Committee Summary" (first review cycle), p.84]*

> "An Advisory Committee (AC) meeting was initially planned to discuss whether substantial evidence of effectiveness has been provided to support approval of tebipenem pivoxil for a limited use indication for treatment of cUTIs and to discuss the measures that could be employed to mitigate the risk of increased carbapenem-class resistance with the availability of an oral carbapenem drug in the United States. However, the AC meeting was cancelled once the review issues regarding the analysis of the primary endpoint in the single phase 3 trial were identified and it was determined that an AC meeting was no longer needed to inform decision-making."

## Neurology / Psychiatry

### 1. Ioflupane I 123 (DaTscan) — NDA 22454

**Sponsor:** GE Healthcare

**Indication approved:** SPECT imaging of striatal dopamine transporters to assist in the evaluation of adult patients with suspected Parkinsonian syndromes (PS), to help differentiate essential tremor (ET) from tremor due to PS (idiopathic Parkinson's disease, multiple system atrophy, and progressive supranuclear palsy); an adjunct to other diagnostic evaluations

**Approval date:** January 14, 2011

**Pivotal trial:** No single pivotal efficacy trial in the usual sense — approval rested on three sponsor-run "confirmatory clinical studies" (internally PD008-003 / "Study 003", PDT3004 / "Study 304", and PDT301 / "Study 301"), a supportive unpublished autopsy-correlation series (the "Walker Study," n=22), and preclinical (autoradiography) binding data; none of these studies were registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (conducted in Europe between 1997 and 2006, predating routine U.S. trial registration)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison) — though unlike the paired-imaging-comparator entries elsewhere in this census, the "comparator" here is a clinical diagnosis established by a blinded panel of movement-disorder/dementia specialists at long-term follow-up (36 months in Study 304, 12 months in Study 301), not a second imaging modality or histopathology; multiple independently-conducted, differently-designed single-arm studies pooled qualitatively (not statistically) as a "totality of data" package rather than a single confirmatory trial

- *Endpoints:* positive/negative percent agreement (sensitivity/specificity) of blinded-reader DaTscan image classification (normal/abnormal) against a clinical-diagnosis reference standard for PS-vs-ET (Studies 003, 304) or probable dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB)-vs-non-DLB (Study 301) (clinical-diagnosis, non-histopathological reference-standard sensitivity/specificity)

- *Primary analysis:* exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval — FDA's statistical reviewer recomputed sensitivity/specificity for each blinded central reader as a two-sided 95% exact binomial CI; only Study 301 had a pre-specified statistical hypothesis (one-sided exact binomial test, α=0.025, against thresholds of 65% sensitivity/73% specificity); Studies 003 and 304 had prespecified analysis plans but no prespecified statistical thresholds or tests

- *Regulatory:* FDA Advisory Committee meeting held (August 11, 2009; voted 11-2 in favor of a favorable risk-benefit determination); two Complete Response Letters issued in earlier review cycles, both solely for labeling deficiencies (package-insert text; then Schedule II controlled-substance labeling), not efficacy; statistical reviewer recommended against approval on efficacy grounds, overruled by the Division Director based on the totality of preclinical/clinical evidence and the Advisory Committee vote (statistical reviewer's non-approval recommendation overruled by division leadership on totality-of-evidence/AdComm grounds)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Regulatory framework: as a diagnostic radiopharmaceutical, DaTscan was evaluated under 21 CFR 315, which assesses effectiveness by the drug's ability to provide useful clinical information via comparison against "a diagnostic standard," "standards of demonstrated accuracy," or information "established in another manner, e.g., patient follow-up" — DaTscan's program relied on the third of these (clinical follow-up), not a histopathological or alternative-imaging gold standard

- Study 003 (PD008-003): 6 European sites, 1997-1998; enrolled subjects with a clinical diagnosis of Parkinson's disease, multiple system atrophy, or essential tremor (i.e., already-established diagnoses); institutional read plus 5 independent-but-site-affiliated blinded reader reads; standard of truth was the baseline clinical diagnosis; primary analysis population was the per-protocol set; primary statistical summary was the lower limit of a one-sided 95% CI, with no pre-specified test or threshold; 4 protocol amendments (none addressing design/statistics)

- Study 304 (PDT3004): 10 European sites, 1999-2005; enrolled patients with early, diagnostically uncertain features of Parkinsonism (excluding those with clear MSA/PSP features or long-established diagnoses) plus healthy volunteers; 3-year study with clinical/imaging assessments at 0, 18, and 36 months; standard of truth was the diagnosis (probable/possible PD, ET, or other) assigned by two blinded, independent central movement-disorder specialists using video assessments through 36 months, with disagreements resolved by consensus; DaTscan reads came from an institutional reader plus three independent blinded central readers; 10 protocol amendments, the most consequential (Amendment 4, August 15, 2000) extending follow-up from 3 to 36 months and increasing sample size from 60 to 180 subjects to meet a European post-authorization commitment

- Study 301 (PDT301): 40 European sites, 2003-2006; enrolled subjects with probable/possible dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) or non-DLB dementia (Alzheimer's disease, vascular dementia); standard of truth was diagnosis by a panel of three central dementia experts at baseline (with a 12-month follow-up diagnosis as a secondary analysis) using International Consensus Criteria; DaTscan reads came from an institutional reader plus three independent blinded central readers; primary statistical analysis was a one-sided exact binomial test (α=0.025) against pre-specified sensitivity (0.65) and specificity (0.73) thresholds — the only one of the three studies with pre-specified statistical hypotheses; 4 protocol amendments, none raising major statistical issues beyond sample-size revisions

- Walker Study (supportive, unpublished, n=22): compared antemortem DaTscan images to autopsy-confirmed dementia diagnoses; clinical diagnosis was incorrect in 9/22 patients and DaTscan reads were incorrect in 4/22 patients — the only study in the program with a true histopathological reference standard, but regarded by FDA as limited by small sample size and imperfect histopathological diagnostic criteria

- Results (FDA Statistical Review, exact two-sided 95% CIs, blinded central readers): Study 003 sensitivity 92.4%-96.8% (CI lower limits 87.1%-92.8%), specificity 74.1%-96.3% (CI lower limits 53.7%-81.0%); Study 304 sensitivity 77.5%-78.6% (CI lower limits 66.0%-67.1%), specificity all readers 96.8% (CI lower limit 83.3%); Study 301 sensitivity 75.3%-80.3% (CI lower limits 64.2%-69.9%), specificity 88.5%-91.2% (CI lower limits 82.0%-85.2%) — Study 301 met its pre-specified specificity threshold for all 3 readers but its sensitivity threshold for only 2 of 3 readers

- FDA's statistical reviewer concluded the confirmatory program did not meet the usual two-adequate-and-well-controlled-trials standard (only Study 301 had a prespecified hypothesis, and its clinical-diagnosis standard of truth was itself questioned by the Walker Study's discordance rate), while the medical/clinical review team and the Division Director concluded the totality of preclinical (autoradiography, animal binding/displacement) and clinical data supported approval for the narrowed PS-vs-ET indication ultimately reflected in the label

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2011/022454s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2011/022454Orig1s000Lbl.pdf

- FDA Summary Review (Reference ID 2887072; Dwaine Rieves, MD, Division Director) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/022454sOrig1s000SumR.pdf

- FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID from original review cycle; statistical reviewers Mark Levenson, PhD and Jyoti Zalkikar, PhD) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/022454sOrig1s000StatR.pdf

- FDA Medical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/022454sOrig1s000MedR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov: no record was identified for Studies 003, 304, 301, or the Walker Study — all were conducted in Europe in 1997-2006, before routine U.S. trial registration; none of the three confirmatory studies nor the Walker Study appear to have a dedicated peer-reviewed publication independently verified via PubMed in this pass (the FDA Summary/Statistical Reviews are the primary public source of the underlying study data)

**Other resources**

- No Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere participation was identified for GE Healthcare specific to this program; not independently confirmed.

- FDA Advisory Committee meeting held August 11, 2009 (Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee), voting 11-2 in favor of a favorable risk-benefit determination for DaTscan.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3, p.13-14]* — "This section presents a detailed review of the studies DP008-003, PDT3004, PDT301, and a discussion of the Walker study... The primary efficacy analysis was the sensitivity and specificity of distinguishing PS from ET. This analysis did not include HVs. The primary image read was the institutional read. The standard of truth was the baseline clinical determination. The primary analysis set was the per-protocol set. The primary statistical summary was the lower limit of a one-sided 95% confidence interval. There were no pre-specified statistical tests or thresholds." (Study PD008-003)

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.3, p.16-17, on Study PDT301]* — "The primary statistical analysis was exact binomial test of the sensitivity and specificity with a one-sided α=0.025. The threshold for sensitivity was 0.65 and the threshold for specificity was 0.73."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §5.1 Conclusions and Recommendations, p.29-30]* — "The statistical rigor of the Phase III program was not strong... generally at least two adequate and well-controlled studies are needed [to] establish effectiveness... All three studies had prespecified analysis plans. However, only one study PDT301 had prespecified statistical hypothesis... Overall, the Phase III program does not support for the approval of Datscan. The Phase III program did not meet the standard of providing two adequate and well controlled trials."

The statistical reviewer did not regard the phase 3 study data as statistically persuasive to support approval of the drug... I agreed with the advisory committee and the clinical team that the totality of the nonclinical and clinical data were sufficient to support approval of DaTscan to assist in the evaluation of certain patients (as described in the final indication)."
