### 2. Vilazodone hydrochloride (Viibryd) — NDA 22567

**Sponsor:** Trovis Pharmaceuticals LLC (a subsidiary of Clinical Data, Inc.; the statistical review lists the applicant of record at time of submission as "PGxHealth," Clinical Data's specialty-pharma division, restructured to Trovis Pharmaceuticals LLC by the time of approval; Clinical Data, Inc. was acquired by Forest Laboratories in January 2011, shortly after this approval)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD) in adults

**Approval date:** January 21, 2011

**Pivotal trial:** Two identically-designed 8-week trials — GNSC-04-DP-02, NCT00285376, and CLDA-07-DP-02, NCT00683592

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter, U.S. 8-week trials; five earlier phase II studies (two negative, three "failed") and a one-year open-label extension (Study CLDA-07-DP-04, NCT00644358) were also submitted but not part of the primary efficacy basis

- *Endpoints:* change from baseline to Week 8 in the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) total score (continuous psychiatric rating-scale change-from-baseline endpoint); secondary/supportive endpoints included CGI-Severity, CGI-Improvement, and HAM-D17 total score change, none designated as multiplicity-controlled key secondaries

- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA on the LOCF-imputed endpoint (ANCOVA on last-observation-carried-forward-imputed continuous endpoint), with treatment, pooled center, and baseline MADRS score as model terms; sensitivity analysis via mixed model for repeated measurements (MMRM) with an unstructured covariance matrix (distinct from the sandwich-variance-estimator MMRM already catalogued elsewhere in this taxonomy)

- *Missing data/bias:* last observation carried forward (LOCF) imputation for the primary continuous endpoint (LOCF imputation for a continuous endpoint); two pairs of duplicate-enrollment subjects (same individual enrolled at two sites) identified post hoc via DNA/genotype analysis and excluded from the primary analysis in Study CLDA-07-DP-02

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Both trials were U.S., randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter studies with a washout period, a screening period, and an 8-week double-blind treatment period; patients were titrated to the 40 mg/day target dose by Day 15

- Eligibility: adults 18-70 with MDD (single or recurrent episode, DSM-IV-TR), HAM-D-17 (first 17 items of the 21-item scale) score ≥22 at screening and baseline, and a HAM-D item 1 (depressed mood) score ≥2

- Primary efficacy measure: change from baseline to Week 8 in MADRS total score, assessed at baseline, weeks 1, 2, 4, 6, and 8 (or early termination); missing values imputed by LOCF

- Study CLDA-07-DP-02 (NCT00683592) was planned for 235 patients/arm to provide 90% power to detect an effect size of 0.3; 481 subjects were randomized (231 placebo, 232 vilazodone after exclusion of duplicate-enrollment subjects)

- Study GNSC-04-DP-02 (NCT00285376) was planned for 408 patients (266 randomized in the primary genetic-substudy analysis); 410 patients were randomized total (205 vilazodone, 205 placebo)

- Primary analysis: ANCOVA with terms for treatment and (pooled) center, and baseline MADRS total score as covariate; pre-specified sensitivity analyses included an ANCOVA with treatment-by-center interaction and an MMRM (fixed categorical terms for treatment, center, visit, and treatment-by-visit interaction; continuous fixed covariates for baseline MADRS and baseline-by-visit interaction; unstructured covariance matrix)

- Results, Study CLDA-07-DP-02 (FDA reviewer-confirmed): LS-mean change -13.3 (vilazodone) vs. -10.8 (placebo), difference -2.5 (95% CI -4.4, -0.6), p=0.009; reviewer's MMRM sensitivity analysis showed a similar but not identical week-8 treatment difference (-2.9, p=0.006, unadjusted for multiplicity); CGI-S and CGI-I and HAM-D17 secondary results were directionally supportive (unadjusted p=0.004, 0.004, 0.0256 respectively)

- Results, Study GNSC-04-DP-02: primary MADRS change from baseline analyzed identically (ANCOVA, LOCF); the FDA reviewer's statistical review presents Sponsor and reviewer tables of the same primary/secondary structure as CLDA-07-DP-02 (see Documents)

- FDA's statistical review concluded: "Vilazodone at a 40 mg/day was positive in the acute treatment of major depressive disorder... based on two pivotal studies," while flagging that none of the secondary efficacy measures had been designated as multiplicity-controlled key secondaries and that long-term efficacy was supported only by a one-year open-label, uncontrolled extension study subject to bias

### 3. Gabapentin enacarbil (Horizant) — NDA 22399

**Sponsor:** Glaxo Group Limited, d/b/a GlaxoSmithKline (originated and co-developed by XenoPort, Inc., which held the individual trial registrations on ClinicalTrials.gov as sponsor)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of moderate-to-severe primary Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS) in adults

**Approval date:** April 6, 2011

**Pivotal trial:** Trial 52 (XP052), NCT00298623; Trial 53 (XP053), NCT00365352; supported by Trial 60 (XP060, randomized-withdrawal long-term trial), NCT00311363; and an exploratory dose-ranging Trial 81, NCT01332305

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter, 12-week trials (Trials 52/53); randomized-withdrawal design for long-term-effectiveness Trial 60 (single-blind run-in on active drug, then double-blind randomization of responders to continued drug or placebo)

- *Endpoints:* co-primary endpoints of International Restless Legs Scale (IRLS) score change from baseline and Clinical Global Impression of Improvement (CGI-I) responder proportion (IRLS-score-change / CGI-I-responder co-primary endpoint pair — the same pair used in the registrational trials for ropinirole and pramipexole per FDA's review)

- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA (IRLS change from baseline, with pooled site and baseline value as covariates) and logistic regression (CGI-I responder proportion, with pooled site); modified intent-to-treat (MITT) population, defined as all randomized patients who completed a baseline IRLS assessment and had ≥1 on-treatment IRLS assessment

- *Multiplicity:* both co-primary endpoints required statistical significance (each tested at the two-sided 0.05 level) for a trial to be considered to have demonstrated efficacy — a conjunctive (both-must-win) co-primary decision rule, distinct from the alpha-splitting or hierarchical co-primary structures already catalogued in this taxonomy (conjunctive dual-co-primary decision rule, no alpha adjustment)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Trials 52 (n=222) and 53 (n=325) were multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 12-week trials in adults with moderate-to-severe primary RLS; Trial 52 compared gabapentin enacarbil 1200 mg/day to placebo; Trial 53 was identically designed but added a 600 mg/day arm via an early protocol amendment made in response to FDA's recommendation

- Co-primary endpoints: (1) IRLS total score (0-40, patient-rated 10-item scale) change from baseline to end of treatment, analyzed by ANCOVA with pooled site, treatment, and baseline value as covariates; (2) proportion of CGI-I responders ("much improved"/"very much improved" at the investigator-rated 7-category scale), analyzed by logistic regression with treatment and pooled site as factors; both endpoints had to reach significance (0.05, two-sided) for the trial to provide evidence of efficacy

- Trial 52 results: 222 randomized (114 gabapentin enacarbil, 108 placebo); ~86% completion in both arms; mean IRLS change -13.2 (drug) vs. -8.8 (placebo), p=0.0003; CGI-I responders 76.1% vs. 38.9%, p<0.0001

- Trial 53 results: 325 randomized (113 at 1200 mg, 115 at 600 mg, 97 placebo); mean IRLS change -13.0 (1200 mg) / -13.8 (600 mg) vs. -9.8 (placebo) (1200 mg vs. placebo p<0.002; 600 mg vs. placebo p<0.0001); CGI-I responders 77.5%/72.8% vs. 44.8% (both doses p<0.0001); a sex-based subgroup analysis found no apparent treatment effect on the IRLS endpoint among male subjects (41% of the sample), though the CGI-I responder analysis was robust in both sexes

- Trial 60 (randomized withdrawal, long-term effectiveness): 327 subjects entered a 24-week single-blind run-in on gabapentin enacarbil 1200 mg/day; 194 (59%) met pre-specified "responder" criteria (≥6-point IRLS reduction to ≤15, "much/very much improved" on CGI-I, stable dose ≥1 month) and were randomized double-blind to continue gabapentin enacarbil (n=96) or switch to placebo (n=98) for 12 weeks; primary outcome was relapse proportion (≥6-point IRLS increase from Week 24 to ≥15, plus "much/very much worse" CGI-I, on ≥2 consecutive visits ≥1 week apart, or withdrawal for lack of efficacy); relapse occurred in 9.4% (drug) vs. 22.7% (placebo), p<0.02

- Trial 81 (exploratory, 5-arm dose-ranging, not powered for pairwise dose comparisons): 217 randomized across placebo and 600/1200/1800/2400 mg/day; IRLS change from baseline ranged -12.9 to -14.0 across active doses vs. -9.3 (placebo) (nominal p=0.04-0.09 depending on dose); responder rates 64%-82% (active) vs. 45% (placebo), with no clear dose-response trend above 600 mg/day

- FDA's Summary Review concluded the trials were "appropriate in design, reasonable in duration, utilized standard endpoint measures ... and enrolled subjects that seem relevant to the 'real world,'" and that "the statistical analyses were performed as prospectively planned"

### 4. Ezogabine (Potiga) — NDA 22345

**Sponsor:** Valeant Pharmaceuticals North America (co-developed with GlaxoSmithKline, which retained ex-U.S. rights)

**Indication approved:** Adjunctive treatment of partial-onset seizures in adults with epilepsy

**Approval date:** June 10, 2011

**Pivotal trial:** Study 301 (VRX-RET-E22-301, "RESTORE 1"), NCT00232596; Study 302 (VRX-RET-E22-302, "RESTORE 2"), NCT00235755; supported by phase IIb Study 205 (dose-ranging)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, parallel-group, fixed-dose trials, each independently powered and analyzed (no cross-trial pooling for the primary claim); Study 301 tested a single dose (1200 mg/day) vs. placebo; Study 302 tested two doses (600 mg/900 mg/day) vs. placebo; Study 205 (phase IIb) tested 900/1200 mg/day vs. placebo

- *Endpoints:* percent change in 28-day total partial-seizure frequency from baseline to the double-blind phase (titration plus maintenance) (partial-seizure-frequency percent-change endpoint); secondary endpoints included responder rate (≥50% seizure reduction), seizure-free proportion, and time without seizures

- *Primary analysis:* non-parametric stratified rank ANCOVA (Studies 301/302), stratified by geographic region and baseline seizure-frequency category, using standardized within-stratum ranks of percent change as the response and standardized ranks of baseline seizure rate as a nested covariate; Study 205 used a rank ANCOVA with dose-response contrasts under a closed testing procedure; responder-rate secondary analyses used logistic regression/Fisher's exact test

- *Missing data/bias:* patients with no post-baseline seizure data were excluded from the primary analysis; for patients who discontinued prematurely, seizures reported up to discontinuation (before the taper phase) were used to compute the 28-day rate — an as-observed approach with no formal imputation for early discontinuation

- *Regulatory:* an initial Complete Response Letter was issued in this application's history (per the approval letter's reference to a prior action letter and amendments responding to it) before final approval

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 301 (n=306) and Study 302 (n=538/539) were randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trials in adults with drug-resistant partial-onset seizures (with or without secondary generalization) on 1-3 concomitant antiepileptic drugs; each had a prospective baseline phase, a forced titration period (up to 6 weeks in Study 301, up to 4 weeks in Study 302), and a 12-week double-blind maintenance phase; Study 301 tested ezogabine 1200 mg/day vs. placebo; Study 302 tested 600 mg/day and 900 mg/day vs. placebo

- Primary endpoint (all three studies): percent change in 28-day total partial-seizure frequency, baseline vs. double-blind phase (titration + maintenance combined); primary efficacy analysis population was patients dosed with ≥1 baseline and ≥1 on-treatment seizure assessment

- Primary analysis (Studies 301/302): "a non-parametric stratified rank analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) to compare the percent change in total partial seizure frequency of the retigabine and placebo treatment groups... stratified by geographic region [Canada/United States versus Mexico/South America in study 301, and Central/Eastern Europe versus rest of the world in study 302] and baseline seizure frequency category" (FDA Statistical Review); responder-rate secondary endpoints compared by logistic regression / Fisher's exact test

- Results: Study 301 (1200 mg/day vs. placebo) — statistically significant seizure-frequency reduction, p<0.001; Study 302 — 600 mg/day p=0.007, 900 mg/day p<0.001, both vs. placebo; Study 205 (phase IIb) — 1200 mg/day p<0.001 vs. placebo, with a numerical dose-response trend across 600-1200 mg/day but no formal dose-response test reaching significance at every dose

- Patient disposition showed a clear dose-related discontinuation gradient: overall withdrawal ranged from 15%-22% (placebo) to 37%-43% (1200 mg/day arms), driven mainly by adverse events (8%-13% placebo vs. 27%-31% at 1200 mg/day), while discontinuation for lack of efficacy was uncommon (≤4%) and showed no clear dose relationship

- FDA's statistical reviewer did not identify a formal cross-trial multiplicity-control mechanism, consistent with each of the three studies being independently powered and analyzed against its own single primary endpoint at its own nominal alpha

### 5. Clobazam (Onfi) — NDA 202067

**Sponsor:** Lundbeck Inc. (clobazam's U.S. development for this indication was originated by Ovation Pharmaceuticals, acquired by Lundbeck in 2009; Lundbeck Inc. is the NDA applicant of record on the approval letter)

**Indication approved:** Adjunctive treatment of seizures associated with Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (LGS) in patients 2 years of age or older

**Approval date:** October 21, 2011

**Pivotal trial:** OV-1012, NCT00518713, supported by phase II Study OV-1002

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter, weight-based fixed-dose-tier trial (three active dose levels vs. placebo) with a 4-week baseline, 3-week titration, and 12-week maintenance period (OV-1012); phase II supportive study OV-1002 was a 2-arm (low-dose vs. high-dose, no placebo arm) trial with a shorter 4-week maintenance period

- *Endpoints:* percent reduction in average weekly rate of drop seizures (atonic, tonic, or tonic-clonic), baseline vs. maintenance period (drop-seizure-frequency percent-reduction endpoint); secondary endpoints included percent reduction in total (drop plus non-drop) seizures, responder rates at ≥25%/≥50%/≥75%/100% thresholds, and physician/caregiver global evaluations

- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA (percent reduction in drop seizures as dependent variable; treatment, pooled center, and baseline drop-seizure rate as covariates), with a step-down procedure across three dose levels (fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing, starting with the high-dose-vs-placebo comparison); OV-1002 used a one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test comparing high-dose to low-dose directly

- *Missing data/bias:* weekly seizure rate computed over non-missing days within the maintenance period (an implicit average-rate imputation for missing/post-discontinuation days, rather than an explicit imputation method); extensive pre-specified sensitivity analyses (12 lettered variants, A-L) probing alternative country/center adjustments, alternative seizure-count boundary conventions, log-transformation, demographic covariate adjustment, and exclusion of subjects affected by a blinding-integrity incident; blinding-integrity sensitivity analysis excluding 7 subjects at one site where the blind was administratively broken due to a warehouse documentation error

**Trial design & endpoints**

- OV-1012: multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in subjects aged 2-54 with LGS-associated drop seizures, conducted at sites in the U.S. (69.3% of subjects) and India (23.1%); 238 subjects randomized to placebo (n=59), low-dose (target 0.25 mg/kg/day, up to 10 mg/day, n=58), medium-dose (n=62), or high-dose (target 1.0 mg/kg/day, up to 40 mg/day, n=59) clobazam; 4-week baseline, 3-week titration, 12-week maintenance

- OV-1002 (phase II, supportive, U.S.-only): 68 subjects randomized to low-dose (n=32) or high-dose (n=36) clobazam, no placebo arm; 4-week maintenance period

- Primary efficacy variable (both studies): percent reduction in average weekly rate of drop seizures from the 4-week baseline period to the maintenance period; primary analysis population was the modified intent-to-treat (MITT) population (randomized subjects with study drug exposure, baseline and post-baseline measurement, and ≥1 maintenance-period measurement)

- Primary analysis (OV-1012): ANCOVA with treatment, pooled center, and baseline drop-seizure rate as effects; "superiority of clobazam to placebo (p ≤ 0.01) was to be considered a statistical evidence in a single multicenter study, consistent with FDA guidance"; statistical comparisons used a step-down procedure starting with the high-dose group vs. placebo

- Results (OV-1012, MITT population): median percent reduction in average weekly drop-seizure rate was 23.2% (placebo), 46.7% (low dose), 57.9% (medium dose), and 86.5% (high dose); all three active doses were statistically significantly superior to placebo (p=0.012 low dose, p=0.0015 medium dose, p<0.0001 high dose, two-sided pairwise ANCOVA comparisons); results from OV-1002 (p<0.0001 for the high-vs-low dose Wilcoxon comparison) were supportive

- Twelve lettered sensitivity analyses (A-L) were pre-specified/conducted, spanning alternative covariate sets (country, center-pooling conventions), alternative handling of ambiguous case-report-form seizure-count entries ("10-20" or ">20" boxes), log-transformed responses, rank-based (rank ANCOVA) analysis, demographic covariate adjustment (weight, age, gender), imputation of baseline rate after AE-related discontinuation, and exclusion of subjects following a blind-break incident

- Blinding-integrity issue: "The sponsor instructed Site 700 to record the blind as broken for all 7 subjects [OV-1012] when documentation with study drug identification was inadvertently sent to the site by the warehouse" — a pre-specified sensitivity analysis (Analysis J) excluded these 7 subjects and found results consistent with the primary analysis

### 6. Florbetapir F 18 (Amyvid) — NDA 202008

**Sponsor:** Avid Radiopharmaceuticals, Inc. (an Eli Lilly and Company subsidiary)

**Indication approved:** PET imaging of the brain to estimate β-amyloid neuritic plaque density in adult patients with cognitive impairment being evaluated for Alzheimer's disease and other causes of cognitive decline; a negative scan indicates sparse to no plaques

**Approval date:** April 6, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** Study 18F-AV-45-A07, NCT00857415 (autopsy-correlation study), with a continuation/expansion autopsy cohort under Study 18F-AV-45-A16, NCT01447719, plus reader-training/reliability studies A08 (NCT01565369) and PT01 (NCT01550549) submitted in a 2011 resubmission

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison) — here uniquely paired against a true histopathological reference standard (postmortem quantitative immunohistochemistry [IHC] amyloid burden), unlike several other imaging-agent entries in this census that lacked an independent reference standard; open-label, single-arm design with an Autopsy Cohort (correlation/sensitivity-specificity analysis) and a separate Specificity Cohort of young, cognitively normal, non-ApoE-ε4-carrier volunteers

- *Endpoints:* Spearman correlation between semi-quantitative visual PET read and quantitative IHC cortical amyloid burden (original pivotal hypothesis); sensitivity/specificity of binary (positive/negative) PET read vs. histopathological reference standard; Fleiss' kappa inter-reader/intra-reader reliability of the binary read

- *Primary analysis:* Spearman's rho correlation test (original submission's primary hypothesis #1); one-sided/two-sided exact binomial tests of sensitivity/specificity against fixed thresholds (≥80% in the resubmission's Study A16; ≥90% specificity threshold for the original Specificity Cohort); Fleiss' kappa with 95% CI for inter-reader agreement (resubmission's primary outcome)

- *Regulatory:* original NDA statistical review explicitly concluded the data "does not support the proposed indication" due to inter-reader variability and inadequate sample size, leading to a Complete Response Letter (March 17, 2011); resubmission (October 7, 2011) developed and validated a new standardized binary-read training methodology (in-person and web-based) across four studies with 19 readers, which the Division and Advisory Committee input had recommended — FDA-mandated post-CRL development of a standardized diagnostic reader-training/interpretation methodology as the basis for resubmission and approval

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Original pivotal trial (Study A07): open-label, single-arm study at 34 U.S. centers enrolling 226 subjects — 152 in an "Autopsy Cohort" (end-of-life/late-life populations expected to yield autopsies) and 74 young, cognitively/neurologically healthy, non-ApoE-ε4-carrier volunteers in a "Specificity Cohort"; three independent blinded imaging physicians (readers 1-3) rated florbetapir retention in the Autopsy Cohort on a 0-4 semi-quantitative scale, with the median of the three reads as the primary efficacy endpoint, correlated against quantitative IHC at autopsy

- Two primary hypotheses (original submission): (1) statistically significant correlation (Spearman's ρ>0) between semi-quantitative visual PET rating and quantitative IHC cortical amyloid burden; (2) florbetapir-PET specificity ≥90% in the young healthy Specificity Cohort

- Original results: 35 of the 152 Autopsy Cohort subjects came to autopsy within 1 year of imaging; a predefined "front-runner" group of 6 plus 29 additional subjects formed the primary efficacy population (n=29 emphasized in FDA's review as the true primary analysis set); primary correlation was Spearman's rho=0.78 (p<0.0001, 95% CI 0.58-0.89); for the Specificity Cohort, 100% (47/47) of young healthy volunteers were read amyloid-negative by the median of three additional blinded readers (readers 4-6), with two of three readers negative on all 47 and the third negative on 46/47

- FDA's original statistical review found the correlation result statistically significant but concluded performance-characteristic (sensitivity/specificity) data were inadequate to support the indication: "the data do not produce evidence of clinical usefulness of the Amyloid detection by Amyvid since its performance characteristics (sensitivity and specificity) show considerable inconsistency among the readers," compounded by a small (n=29) primary efficacy population, use of the same images for both training-set development and performance evaluation, and only 14 patients with a pathological standard of truth available for the proposed binary (qualitative) read — leading to a Complete Response Letter

- Resubmission program (4 new reader-training/reliability studies, 19 readers total, no new PET scans — all reads were new interpretations of existing A05/A07 images): Study A08 (35 A07 autopsy cases, 9 readers, in-person core-lab training); Study A09 (40 cases from Study A05, 7 readers, reliability only, no reference standard); Study A16 (all 59 available autopsy cases by then, 5 readers, in-person training, sensitivity/specificity of majority read plus individual-reader sensitivity/specificity and inter-reader Fleiss' kappa); Study PT01 (the pivotal resubmission study — 151 subjects [59 autopsy + 92 non-autopsy MCI/AD/healthy-control cases], 5 readers trained via a web-based self-study program in their own clinical practice setting, no in-person contact)

- PT01 primary analysis: overall inter-reader Fleiss' kappa among 5 readers across 119 cases (powered at 90% to detect an observed kappa ≥0.64 against an expected 0.70, with a lower 95% CI bound requirement of ≥0.58); secondary analysis: sensitivity/specificity of each reader vs. CERAD-derived histopathological positive/negative status, with a hypothesis that ≥3 of 5 readers would show a lower 95% CI bound ≥0.50 for both measures

- Study A16 primary analyses: (1) sensitivity/specificity of the majority (binary) read vs. autopsy status among all subjects autopsied within 24 months, tested against Hypothesis A (sensitivity ≥80%) and Hypothesis B (specificity ≥80%); (2) re-test of the correlation hypothesis from A07 using the expanded autopsy set

- Resubmission results: inter-reader Fleiss' kappa = 0.83 (95% CI 0.78, 0.88) across 151 PT01 subjects (no repeated reads), with >75% pairwise reader agreement across all subgroups; PT01 reader-level sensitivity/specificity for the 59 autopsy subjects ranged 69%-92% / 90%-95% across the five web-trained readers; Study A16 in-person-trained readers showed sensitivity 87%-95% and specificity 95%(-100%) across readers; across all three reliability studies with an autopsy reference standard (A08, A16, PT01), 16/19 readers exceeded 80% sensitivity (median 92%) and 18/19 exceeded 80% specificity (median 94%)

- FDA's resubmission statistical review concluded the binary-read methodology, whether taught via in-person or web-based self-study training, produced acceptable inter-reader reliability and reader-level sensitivity/specificity, while noting the MCI subgroup's autopsy sample (n=5) was too small for a formal sensitivity/specificity conclusion in the population expected to benefit most from the test

### 7. Teriflunomide (Aubagio) — NDA 202992

**Sponsor:** Sanofi-aventis U.S. Inc. (Genzyme)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of patients with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (RMS)

**Approval date:** September 12, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** TEMSO (EFC5049), NCT00134563; supported by interim data from TOWER (EFC10531), NCT00751881, ongoing at the time of NDA submission

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, multicenter, multinational, placebo-controlled, double-blind, parallel-group, 3-arm (placebo/7 mg/14 mg), approximately 2-year trials; TOWER contributed only interim (ARR-only) data at NDA submission since it had not completed

- *Endpoints:* annualized relapse rate (ARR), defined as confirmed relapses per patient-year; key secondary endpoint time to disability progression (≥1-point EDSS increase if baseline <5.5, or ≥0.5-point if baseline >5.5, sustained ≥12 weeks); other secondary endpoints included Fatigue Impact Scale (FIS), MRI burden of disease (BOD, cubic-root-transformed T2+T1-hypointense lesion volume), and Gd-enhancing T1 lesion count

- *Primary analysis:* Poisson regression with robust (sandwich/GEE) error variance for ARR (treatment group, EDSS strata, and region as covariates; log-transformed standardized study duration as an offset; implemented via SAS PROC GENMOD with repeated-statement robust variance, equivalent to a GEE model); stratified log-rank test (region and EDSS strata) for time to disability progression, with Kaplan-Meier estimation; MMRM with unstructured covariance and Satterthwaite denominator degrees of freedom (REML/Newton-Raphson) for MRI burden of disease

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing across a 5-endpoint, 2-dose family — first H1 (14 mg vs. placebo, ARR), then H2 (7 mg vs. placebo, ARR), then S1/S2 (disability progression, 14 mg/7 mg vs. placebo) at 5%, then (only if all four were significant) a further step-down at 2.5% within each dose across FIS, Gd-enhancing-lesion count, and MRI burden of disease, in that order

- *Regulatory:* both 7 mg and 14 mg doses met the primary ARR endpoint in TEMSO, but only the 14 mg dose reached significance on the disability-progression key secondary endpoint (7 mg "failed to reach statistical significance"), and TOWER's disability-progression data were not yet available (interim ARR-only) at submission — FDA's statistical reviewer explicitly stated disability-progression evidence was "not strong enough to allow a definitive conclusion" pending TOWER's completion

**Trial design & endpoints**

- TEMSO: 1088 randomized (1:1:1 to placebo/7 mg/14 mg), 126 sites in 21 countries (4 U.S. sites), adults 18-55 meeting McDonald criteria for MS with a relapsing course (RRMS, SPMS, or progressive-relapsing), ≥1 relapse in the preceding year or ≥2 in the preceding 2 years, EDSS ≤5.5; randomization stratified by center and baseline EDSS (<3.5 vs. >3.5); ~2-year treatment duration

- TOWER: 1096 randomized as of the interim data cutoff (February 28, 2011) for the NDA submission (out of 1418 screened); identical design to TEMSO; disability-progression analysis was not conducted since only ARR data were available at the time of the interim cut

- Primary endpoint (both trials): annualized relapse rate (ARR), confirmed relapses per patient-year, with relapses confirmed by the treating (unblinded) neurologist based on objective assessment by an independent blinded examining neurologist

- TEMSO results: adjusted ARR 0.539 (placebo), 0.370 (7 mg, 31.2% relative risk reduction, p=0.0002), 0.369 (14 mg, 31.5% relative risk reduction, p=0.0005); of 1086 treated patients, 290 (26.7% overall) discontinued treatment, most commonly for adverse events, patient preference, or lack of efficacy

- TEMSO key secondary (time to 12-week-confirmed disability progression): 14 mg was statistically superior to placebo; 7 mg was not — "The effect of treatment in delaying disability progression is only shown in Teriflunomide 14 mg in the TEMSO study, as Teriflunomide 7 mg failed to reach statistical significance as compared to placebo" (FDA Statistical Review)

- TOWER interim results: consistent ARR reduction at both doses (reviewer noted the interim TOWER data were "sufficient evidence that Teriflunomide is efficacious in reducing the relapse rate," consistent in direction/magnitude with TEMSO); TOWER discontinuation was also substantial (~20-22% by the interim cutoff, with average ongoing-patient follow-up of only ~1 year), leading the reviewer to flag "concern of the quality of in study conduct" given the large number of patient-requested discontinuations

- FDA's overall statistical conclusion: "the effect of Teriflunomide in reducing the relapse rate is clearly established based on data from TEMSO and TOWER. The evidence of effect of Teriflunomide in delaying the physical disability is not strong enough to allow a definitive conclusion, and should be determined when the TOWER study completes."

### 8. Perampanel (Fycompa) — NDA 202834

**Sponsor:** Eisai, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adjunctive treatment of partial-onset seizures, with or without secondarily generalized seizures, in patients with epilepsy aged 12 and older

**Approval date:** October 22, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** Study 304 (E2007-G000-304), NCT00699972; Study 305 (E2007-G000-305), NCT00699582; Study 306 (E2007-G000-306), NCT00700310

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* three randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase III trials, each with a 6-week titration and 13-week maintenance period; Studies 304/305 tested 8 mg and 12 mg vs. placebo; Study 306 tested 2 mg, 4 mg, and 8 mg vs. placebo

- *Endpoints:* percent change in seizure frequency per 28 days during the maintenance period relative to the pre-randomization baseline (full ITT population, LOCF); key secondary endpoint of responder rate (≥50% seizure-frequency reduction) for non-EU markets; percent change in complex-partial-plus-secondarily-generalized seizure frequency as a supportive endpoint

- *Primary analysis:* rank ANCOVA — both baseline and on-treatment percent-change seizure frequencies were separately rank-transformed, then analyzed by ANCOVA with treatment and pooled country as factors and ranked baseline frequency as covariate, with a log-transformation-based ANCOVA run as a robustness check; Hodges-Lehmann estimator and 95% CI for the treatment-difference point estimate; Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test (adjusting for pooled country) for the responder-rate secondary endpoint

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical dose testing via a closed testing procedure — Studies 304/305 tested from the lower dose upward (8 mg vs. placebo first, then 12 mg only if 8 mg was significant); Study 306 tested from the highest dose downward (8 mg, then 4 mg only if 8 mg was significant, then 2 mg only if both 8 mg and 4 mg were significant)

- *Regulatory:* post-completion analysis-population-set amendment — the primary analysis set for Studies 304 and 306 was changed from the originally-planned ITT set to the "Full ITT" set after both studies had completed (Study 305's change was made pre-unblinding), which the FDA reviewer noted flipped Study 304's primary-endpoint conclusion from a fail (original ITT set) to a win (Full ITT set) (post-hoc analysis-population-set amendment made after study completion/unblinding that reverses a trial's primary-endpoint result)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 304 (n=390: placebo 122, 8 mg 133, 12 mg 135) and Study 305 (n=389: placebo 138, 8 mg 130, 12 mg 121) were identically designed randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trials in patients aged 12+ with refractory partial-onset seizures; Study 306 (n=712: placebo 187, 2 mg 180, 4 mg 174, 8 mg 171) added a lower-dose 2 mg/4 mg arm structure; all three used a 6-week titration and 13-week maintenance period with a 4-week follow-up

- Primary efficacy measure: percent change in seizure frequency per 28 days in the Maintenance Period relative to the Pre-randomization Phase, in the (Full) ITT analysis set using LOCF imputation; missing-data handling used a tiered rule based on the proportion of randomized subjects with <2 weeks of double-blind seizure data (if >10% of subjects were affected, endpoint frequency for those subjects was computed from their last 2 weeks of available data, including pre-randomization days; if ≤10%, those subjects' endpoint frequency was set to missing)

- Analysis-population controversy: "In reviewing the sponsor's protocol and SAP, the agency recommended that the full ITT analysis set should be used for the primary analysis, but the sponsor did not take the agency's recommendation into consideration until later time in the trial prior to data un-blinded for Study 305, and when Study 304 and Study 306 have completed... The results were consistent from both analysis sets in Study 305 and Study 306, but were inconsistent in Study 304. Study 304 would fail on the primary analysis when the originally planned ITT analysis set was used, but would win only when the full ITT analysis set was used" (FDA Statistical Review) — leading FDA to characterize Study 304 as supportive rather than fully confirmatory evidence

- Multiplicity/dose-ordering: Studies 304/305 tested the 8 mg dose vs. placebo first (two-sided α=0.05); only if significant was the 12 mg dose then tested vs. placebo at α=0.05. Study 306 tested 8 mg first, then 4 mg (only if 8 mg was significant), then 2 mg (only if both 8 mg and 4 mg were significant)

- Results: perampanel 4, 8, and 12 mg were each shown effective in reducing seizure frequency across the three studies (specific dose-by-study significance patterns documented in reviewer's Tables 5-7); responder-rate analyses (CMH test) were consistently supportive across studies and doses

- FDA's Executive Summary: "The three clinical studies 304, 305 and 306 support that perampanel 4, 8 and 12 mg are effective in reducing seizure frequencies in subjects with refractory partial seizures. However, the results of the efficacy in Study 304 are not consistent because the statistical significance in the test of efficacy varies, depending on the patient population included in the analysis, and the change of patient population was made after the study completed. Therefore Study 304 may be used as supportive for efficacy."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.1.4, p.8]* — "For primary efficacy endpoint, a closed testing procedure will be employed to control family wise type-I error rate. For Study 304 & 305, the test starts from the lower dose, first the 8 mg treatment group will be compared with the placebo... For Study 306, the test starts from the higher dose. First, the 8 mg treatment group was compared with placebo..."

### 9. Dimethyl fumarate (Tecfidera) — NDA 204063

**Sponsor:** Biogen Idec, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of patients with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (RMS)

**Approval date:** March 27, 2013

**Pivotal trial:** DEFINE (Study 301/109MS301), NCT00420212; CONFIRM (Study 302/109MS302, with glatiramer acetate active reference arm), NCT00451451

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind (oral treatments)/single-blind (glatiramer acetate reference)/rater-blinded, parallel-group, 96-week phase III trials, each testing two dose regimens (BG00012/dimethyl fumarate 240 mg BID and 240 mg TID) vs. placebo; CONFIRM additionally included an open-label-to-site but rater-blinded glatiramer acetate (GA) 20 mg SC QD reference arm; a Special Protocol Assessment (SPA) was sought for both trials' designs but Agency agreement was not reached, though FDA's pre-trial advice (240 mg BID dose group; primary-endpoint choice; 1-year minimum before rescue-treatment eligibility) was incorporated into the protocols anyway

- *Endpoints:* Study 302/CONFIRM primary — annualized relapse rate (ARR) at 2 years; Study 301/DEFINE primary — proportion of subjects relapsed at 2 years (Kaplan-Meier-estimated probability); secondary endpoints in both included disability progression (12-week-confirmed EDSS increase), new/newly-enlarging T2 lesions, and new T1 hypointense lesions (negative binomial models)

- *Primary analysis:* DEFINE — Cox proportional-hazards model (baseline EDSS category, baseline age category, region as covariates) for time to first relapse/proportion relapsed; CONFIRM — negative binomial regression (with a pre-specified fallback to Poisson regression if the data were underdispersed or the negative binomial model failed to converge) for ARR, adjusted for baseline EDSS category, baseline age category, region, and number of relapses in the year prior to entry, with log(time-on-study) as an offset

- *Missing data/bias:* INEC (blinded Independent Neurology Evaluation Committee)-confirmed relapses only were used in the primary analyses, with data censored at the time a subject switched to an alternative MS medication; FDA's reviewer independently conducted "worst case scenario" sensitivity analyses (a form of tipping-point/bias analysis) counting all relapses, including post-alternative-medication relapses, for the dimethyl fumarate arms while restricting the placebo arm to pre-switch INEC-confirmed relapses only, to test robustness against possible unblinding bias from the drug's flushing side effect (worst-case-scenario asymmetric relapse-counting sensitivity analysis for suspected unblinding bias); MRI lesion-count missing data imputed under a constant-rate-of-new-lesion-development assumption, truncated at the largest observed value

- *Regulatory:* FDA reviewer identified and adjudicated a discrepancy between the final protocols (which specified baseline EDSS ≤3.5 vs. >3.5 as the primary-analysis covariate categorization) and the later-dated SAPs (which specified ≤2.0 vs. >2.0); reviewer accepted the SAP's categorization as controlling because the SAP postdated the protocol, and separately confirmed robustness using the protocol's ≤3.5/>3.5 categorization (FDA reviewer resolves a protocol-vs.-SAP covariate-definition discrepancy by deferring to the later-dated document, with an independent robustness check)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- DEFINE (Study 301): 1237 RRMS subjects randomized equally across placebo/BID/TID; enrollment began under Protocol Version 1 (September 21, 2006), amended 5 times (final amendment May 26, 2010); first subject treated March 14, 2007, last subject completed February 23, 2011; SAP finalized March 10, 2011, prior to database lock; subjects could have prior GA exposure if discontinued ≥3 months before randomization

- CONFIRM (Study 302): 1430 RRMS subjects randomized equally across placebo/BID/TID/GA; enrollment began under Protocol Version 1 (October 16, 2006), amended 3 times (final version January 9, 2008); first subject treated July 28, 2007, last subject completed August 24, 2011; SAP finalized October 3, 2011, prior to database lock; no prior GA exposure permitted

- Eligibility (both trials): EDSS 0-5 at randomization, ≥1 relapse in the year prior to randomization or a Gd-enhancing MRI lesion within 6 weeks prior; ~40-45% of randomized subjects at qualifying sites participated in a dedicated MRI cohort, with randomization stratified by site to balance MRI-cohort representation across arms

- DEFINE results (proportion relapsed at 2 years): 0.46 (placebo, 171/408 relapsed) vs. 0.27 (BID, hazard ratio 0.51, 95% CI 0.40-0.66, 48.5% risk reduction, p<0.0001) vs. 0.26 (TID, HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.39-0.65, 49.5% risk reduction, p<0.0001); FDA's independent worst-case-scenario Cox-model sensitivity analysis (counting all relapses for drug arms vs. only pre-switch INEC-confirmed relapses for placebo) still reached significance for both doses (p<0.0001 and p=0.0001)

- CONFIRM results (adjusted ARR at 2 years): 0.401 (placebo) vs. 0.224 (BID, rate ratio 0.560, 44.0% reduction, p<0.0001) vs. 0.198 (TID, rate ratio 0.495, 50.5% reduction, p<0.0001) vs. 0.286 (GA reference arm, rate ratio 0.714, 28.6% reduction, p=0.0128); worst-case-scenario sensitivity analysis again supported the primary result (BID p=0.0023, TID p=0.0001, GA p=0.0115)

- FDA's reviewer concluded treatment discontinuation (elevated in both studies partly because subjects were permitted to cross over to alternative MS treatments) "did not appear to have a significant effect on the efficacy results or conclusions," based on the series of worst-case and per-protocol sensitivity analyses; efficacy was "generally consistent across a variety of subgroups defined by demographic and baseline disease characteristics"

### 10. Vortioxetine (Brintellix) — NDA 204447

**Sponsor:** Takeda Pharmaceuticals U.S.A., Inc. (co-developed and co-marketed with H. Lundbeck A/S; Takeda is the NDA applicant of record on the approval letter)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD) in adults

**Approval date:** September 30, 2013

**Pivotal trial:** Ten short-term placebo-controlled trials were submitted (studies 11492A/NCT00839423, 11984A/NCT00635219, 303/NCT00672958, 304/NCT00672620, 305/NCT00735709, 13267A/NCT01140906, 315/NCT01153009, 316/NCT01163266, 317/NCT01179516, and the elderly-population study 12541A/NCT00811252), of which FDA's statistical reviewer identified only 6 as positive for at least one dose (11492A, 305, 13267A, 315, 316, 12541A); a long-term relapse-prevention trial (11985A) was also submitted

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, fixed-dose, 6-to-8-week short-term trials (several duloxetine- or venlafaxine- or agomelatine-referenced, i.e., three-arm designs with an active non-placebo comparator alongside vortioxetine and placebo, without the active arm itself powering a formal non-inferiority/superiority claim), across 5-20 mg doses, plus one flexible-dose (5/10 mg) long-term relapse-prevention trial (11985A); 4 of 10 short-term trials were negative/failed (11984A, 303, 304, 317) — a substantial failed/negative-trial rate documented in a dedicated FDA review appendix

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint was change from baseline in MADRS or HAM-D24 total score (varying by study) at Week 6 or Week 8; sponsor-proposed key secondary endpoints varied by study (Sheehan Disability Scale [SDS], CGI-Improvement, HAM-D24 response rate, MADRS remission rate [MADRS ≤10], change in HAM-D24 among patients with baseline HAM-A ≥20) — FDA restricted the acceptable key-secondary-endpoint set to CGI-I or SDS only, per a September 14, 2010 Advice Letter, rejecting the sponsor's broader proposed secondary-endpoint list as exploratory/non-labeling-eligible (FDA-restricted acceptable key-secondary-endpoint set, narrower than sponsor's proposed list)

- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA on LOCF-imputed MADRS/HAM-D24 change (treatment and center as fixed factors, baseline score as covariate) as the primary method in most trials, with MMRM as a co-primary or sensitivity method in others (varying by study, both approaches used across the program); logistic regression (adjusting for baseline score and treatment) for MADRS-remission and HAM-D24-response secondary endpoints, analyzed under both LOCF and observed-cases (OC)

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing per study/dose — a pre-specified sequential family (e.g., MADRS/HAM-D24 change, then CGI-I, then HAM-D24 response rate, then a HAM-A≥20 subgroup analysis, then MADRS remission rate) tested in order at the 5% level, continuing only while each preceding comparison remained significant

- *Regulatory:* FDA statistical reviewer's Executive Summary explicitly frames the efficacy conclusion around only the positive-trial subset (6 of 10 short-term studies), with a dedicated Appendix summarizing the 4 negative/failed studies separately; only the 20 mg dose (not 5, 10, or 15 mg) was statistically superior to placebo across the U.S.-only trial subset, per the reviewer's note that "the doses lower than 20 mg were not statistically significantly better than placebo in US studies" (regular approval granted across a program with a substantial proportion of negative/failed pivotal trials)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Program overview: 10 short-term (6- or 8-week) placebo-controlled fixed-dose trials (9 in adults, 1 in elderly subjects) spanning doses of 1-20 mg, run across the U.S. (5 trials exclusively U.S.), Canada, and non-North-American sites, plus one long-term (24-week stabilization then double-blind relapse-prevention) trial (11985A, flexible 5/10 mg dosing)

- Of the 10 short-term trials, FDA's reviewer determined 6 had positive efficacy results for at least one investigated dose (11492A [venlafaxine-referenced], 305, 13267A [duloxetine-referenced], 315 [duloxetine-referenced], 316, and 12541A [elderly, duloxetine-referenced]); the reviewer evaluated efficacy results "only for positive short-term studies and for the maintenance study," with the 4 negative/failed studies (11984A [duloxetine-referenced], 303, 304, 317) summarized separately in an appendix

- Analysis/imputation approach (representative, Study 305/CONFIRM-analogous design): primary analysis was ANCOVA on change from baseline in MADRS total score (FAS, LOCF) with treatment and center as fixed factors and baseline MADRS as covariate; multiplicity for the family of key secondary endpoints was controlled via "a closed testing procedure that ranked hypotheses hierarchically and continued testing at the 5% level of significance as long as the previous [comparison was significant]"

- Long-term relapse-prevention trial (11985A): responders (MADRS <10 at both Weeks 10 and 12 of open-label stabilization on 5 or 10 mg) were randomized to continue vortioxetine or switch to placebo; relapse was defined as MADRS >22 or unsatisfactory clinical response requiring intervention; both 5 mg and 10 mg were statistically superior to placebo for relapse prevention, though FDA noted the required pre-randomization stabilization period (2 weeks minimum per protocol) was shorter than the Division had recommended at the End-of-Phase-II meeting (February 5, 2008), with only ~60% of subjects actually stable ≥4 weeks and few stable ≥10 weeks — a limitation the reviewer noted could not be corrected because "the protocol was submitted to the Division after this non-US study was initiated"

- Elderly study (12541A): a duloxetine-referenced, placebo-controlled, fixed-dose (5 mg) trial in elderly MDD patients; one of the 6 positive studies supporting approval, and the only trial specifically supporting use in an elderly population

- FDA's Executive Summary: "In the dose range of 5-20 mg, statistically significant treatment effect of Lu AA21004 with respect to placebo was demonstrated in at least one short-term study for each investigated dose (5mg, 10mg, 15mg, and 20mg). The doses lower than 20 mg were not statistically significantly better than placebo in US studies."

### 11. Flutemetamol F 18 (Vizamyl) — NDA 203137

**Sponsor:** GE Healthcare

**Indication approved:** Radioactive diagnostic agent for Positron Emission Tomography (PET) imaging of the brain to estimate β-amyloid neuritic plaque density in adult patients with cognitive impairment who are being evaluated for Alzheimer's disease (AD) or other causes of cognitive decline

**Approval date:** October 25, 2013

**Pivotal trial:** Three diagnostic-accuracy studies — GE067-007 (autopsy-confirmation study, "Study One"), NCT01165554; GE067-015 (young healthy volunteer specificity study, ultimately dropped from the label), NCT01265394; GE067-021 (electronic reader-training/pooled-read reproducibility study, "Study Two"), NCT01672827

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison to histopathology truth standard); autopsy-confirmation cohort (terminally ill/end-of-life population, not the intended cognitively-impaired-outpatient population); electronic/web-based reader-training validation study, distinct from in-person-trained reader cohorts in the same program

- *Endpoints:* sensitivity and specificity of blinded visual PET interpretation vs. histopathology (Bielschowsky silver stain, modified CERAD neuritic-plaque density) standard of truth; inter-reader and intra-reader agreement (Fleiss' kappa, percent agreement)

- *Primary analysis:* exact two-sided 95% binomial confidence interval on sensitivity/specificity by reader, evaluated against a pre-specified lower-bound success threshold for a majority of readers; Fleiss' kappa with a pre-specified lower-CI-bound success threshold for inter-reader agreement

- *Missing data/bias:* performance-measure analysis without a reference standard fully independent of the test itself (verification bias) — the FDA reviewer explicitly criticized the sponsor's original specificity-only study (GE067-015) for evaluating specificity without any paired sensitivity assessment, and recommended it be dropped from the label

- *Regulatory:* no FDA advisory committee meeting held for this NDA; the product class's trial-design conventions (histopathology as standard of truth) were set at two earlier class-wide amyloid-imaging advisory committee meetings (2008, 2011) rather than at a meeting specific to this NDA

**Trial design & endpoints**

- GE067-007 ("Study One," pivotal autopsy study): multicenter, open-label, single-arm Phase 3 study; 180 subjects ≥55 years with terminal illness/life expectancy <1 year (end-of-life population) dosed and scanned; 176 imaged/evaluable; 69 died during the study, of whom 68 had autopsy-determined amyloid status usable in the primary analysis (43 positive, 25 negative)
- Standard of truth: Bielschowsky silver-stained sections from 8 cortical regions, scored on a modified CERAD 0-3 neuritic-plaque-density scale; a region was classified abnormal if mean score >1.5, and a brain classified abnormal if ≥1 region was abnormal
- 5 independent readers, trained in person, blinded to the standard of truth and to all clinical information; each read PET-only images first, then re-read with CT anatomic images added
- Primary endpoint: sensitivity of blinded PET-only visual interpretation vs. the autopsy standard of truth; pre-specified success criterion: lower bound of the two-sided 95% exact binomial CI for sensitivity >70% for at least 3 of 5 readers
- Secondary endpoints: specificity (PET-only and with CT); sensitivity/specificity with CT added; SUVR-vs-immunohistochemistry correlation in the first 30 autopsied brains
- Results: sensitivity by reader ranged 81.4%-93.0% (median 88%), meeting the pre-specified criterion; specificity by reader ranged 44%-92% (median 88%), with only 2 of 5 readers meeting a comparable specificity threshold — a limitation the FDA statistical reviewer flagged explicitly, since specificity was not part of the pre-specified primary success criterion
- GE067-015 (young healthy volunteer specificity study): 181 healthy adults aged 18-40, presumed amyloid-negative by design (the assumption of negativity constitutes the standard of truth; no independent truth standard exists); primary endpoint specificity only, with a pre-specified success criterion of lower-CI-bound specificity >80% for ≥3 of 5 readers (met: 4 of 5 readers). FDA's reviewer concluded sensitivity could not be evaluated in this study at all by design, and recommended — because "for any given diagnostic test there is a trade-off between sensitivity and specificity" that must be evaluated together — that this study's data be removed from the approved label; this recommendation was followed
- GE067-021 ("Study Two," electronic-training/pooled-read study): single-arm, open-label, retrospective re-read of 305 images (276 unique + 29 duplicates for intra-reader reproducibility) drawn from prior studies (68 GE067-007 autopsy subjects, 36 NPH-biopsy subjects, 31 young healthy volunteers, 80 amnestic-MCI subjects, and others), read by 5 readers newly trained via an electronic/web-based self-training program (rather than in-person training) and required to pass a qualification test before participating
- GE067-021 primary endpoint (Analysis Population 1, n=135: autopsy + biopsy + young-healthy-volunteer subjects): sensitivity and specificity of blinded PET-only visual read vs. the combined standard of truth, with a pre-specified success criterion requiring lower-CI bounds for both sensitivity AND specificity to exceed 70% for the same ≥3 of 5 readers; secondary endpoint (Analysis Population 4, n=276): inter-reader agreement via Fleiss' kappa, pre-specified success criterion lower-CI-bound κ>0.6
- GE067-021 results: sensitivity by reader 84.3%-94.1% (median 92%), specificity 77.4%-96.4% (median 81%) — 3 of 5 readers met both thresholds simultaneously; Fleiss' kappa across all 5 readers on the n=276 population was 0.83 (95% CI 0.79-0.86), meeting the pre-specified secondary criterion; intra-reader reproducibility on 29 duplicate images ranged 93%-100% by reader
- The final approved label describes only "Study One" (GE067-007) and "Study Two" (GE067-021); GE067-015 was dropped per the FDA reviewer's recommendation above

Approval letter: "Your application for Vizamyl (flutemetamol F 18 injection) was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary; there were no controversial issues that would benefit from an advisory committee discussion." The product class was discussed at two earlier, non-NDA-specific Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee meetings (October 23, 2008 and January 20, 2011) that established histopathology as the standard of truth for Phase 3 amyloid-PET trial designs generally.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

No standalone SAP document is posted publicly for any of the three studies; the FDA Statistical Review itself is the most complete public articulation of the pre-specified analysis plan for this diagnostic-accuracy submission and is quoted directly below.

*[verbatim, FDA Approval Letter, "ADVISORY COMMITTEE" section]*

> "Your application for Vizamyl (flutemetamol F 18 injection) was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary; there were no controversial issues that would benefit from an advisory committee discussion."

**Reverse-engineered SAP** *[inferred]*

- *[inferred, from FDA Statistical Review §3.4.1 pre-specified success criteria for GE067-007]* The primary hypothesis structure — sensitivity-only success criterion (lower 95% exact-CI bound >70% for ≥3 of 5 readers), with specificity relegated to a secondary/non-gating role — is reconstructed from the reported per-reader sensitivity/specificity point estimates and CIs (StatR Tables 3-4) rather than from a quoted protocol/SAP passage, since no such document is public.

- *[inferred, from FDA Statistical Review §5.4 labeling recommendation and the final approved label's Study One/Study Two structure]* The removal of GE067-015 from the approved label is inferred to reflect the FDA reviewer's stated concern that a specificity-only design (with assumed rather than histopathology-confirmed negatives) cannot be evaluated on the same footing as a paired sensitivity/specificity design — evidenced by the label's final Section 14 including only GE067-007 and GE067-021.

- *[inferred, from FDA Statistical Review Table 5 and label Tables 6-8]* The GE067-021 electronic/web-based reader-training program is inferred to have been accepted as adequately equivalent to in-person training because its sensitivity/specificity and kappa results (median sensitivity 92%, specificity 81%, κ=0.83) were of comparable magnitude to the in-person-trained GE067-007 results (median sensitivity 88%, specificity 88%), despite the autopsy-only subgroup within GE067-021 meeting the combined sensitivity/specificity threshold for only 1 of 5 readers — a discrepancy the label does not resolve explicitly.

### 12. Eslicarbazepine acetate (Aptiom) — NDA 22416

**Sponsor:** Sunovion Pharmaceuticals Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adjunctive treatment of partial-onset seizures in patients with epilepsy 18 years of age and older

**Approval date:** November 8, 2013

**Pivotal trial:** Three Phase 3 trials — Study 301 (BIA-2093-301), NCT00957684; Study 302 (BIA-2093-302), NCT00957047; Study 304 (BIA-2093-304), NCT00988429

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, fixed-dose, adjunctive (add-on) design across three dose arms per trial; Complete-Response-Letter-driven resubmission with a newly conducted confirmatory trial (Study 304) added to two originally-submitted trials (301/302)

- *Endpoints:* standardized seizure frequency per 28 days (percent reduction from placebo) over a 12-week maintenance period; ≥50% responder rate, seizure-free rate (secondary)

- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA on log-transformed (natural log, +0.333 constant) standardized seizure frequency, back-transformed via the exponential function

- *Multiplicity:* two-stage gatekeeping procedure (Bonferroni-style Stage 1 across two doses in the ITT population, Dunnett's method Stage 2 in the diary-format-restricted population), per Dmitrienko et al. 2008

- *Missing data/bias:* discontinuations during the 2-week titration period (before the maintenance period began) were treated as missing in the primary analysis, with three pre-specified sensitivity imputations plus two FDA-added imputations; a mid-trial diary-format change (Event-Entry to Daily-Entry) required a diary-version covariate and a supplementary diary-restricted analysis population

- *Regulatory:* Complete Response Letter (April 30, 2010) citing GCP violations, data-presentation deficiencies, and inadequate documentation in the original Studies 301/302; documented reviewer-vs-reviewer disagreement on the resubmission (medical reviewer recommended a second CRL; statistical reviewer, clinical team leader, and Division Director recommended approval)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- All three trials: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter, adjunctive-therapy design with an 8-week baseline period, 2-week titration period, and 12-week double-blind maintenance period
- Study 301 (Bial-sponsored, Europe/South America, N=402) and Study 302 (Bial-sponsored, N=395) each randomized to ESL 400/800/1200 mg/day or placebo; Study 304 (Sunovion-led resubmission trial, N=653, randomized 1:1:1) tested only ESL 800/1200 mg/day vs. placebo, stratified by IVRS-permuted-block randomization with region (North America vs. Rest of World) as a stratification factor
- Primary endpoint: standardized seizure frequency (per 28 days) over the 12-week maintenance period, analyzed by ANCOVA on the natural-log-transformed (+0.333 constant to avoid ln(0)) seizure frequency, with treatment as a fixed effect and ln-transformed baseline frequency and diary version as covariates; LS means and 95% CIs back-transformed by exponentiation and subtraction of the constant, with standard errors via the Delta Method
- Study 304's SAP was submitted to IND 67,466 on August 11, 2011, finalized December 6, 2011, then amended and re-signed March 5, 2012 following a compliance issue at one site; the database was locked for unblinding March 12, 2012 and briefly reopened/relocked May 25, 2012 to correct one subject's drug-accountability data
- Multiplicity control in Study 304: a 2-stage gatekeeping procedure — Stage 1 tested each of ESL 800 mg and 1200 mg vs. placebo in the ITT population at α=0.025 each (effectively Bonferroni); if both were significant, Dunnett's method was applied at α=0.05 in the diary-restricted (Daily-Entry) population in Stage 2; if only one Stage-1 comparison was significant, its α carried forward alone to Stage 2
- Secondary endpoints (responder rate, seizure-free rate, exacerbation, distribution of seizure-reduction categories) were analyzed via Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel tests stratified by region and diary version
- Key results (Study 304, ITT population): ESL 1200 mg vs. placebo — log-scale LS-mean difference −0.26, Bonferroni-adjusted p=0.004 (significant), 22.9% seizure-frequency reduction over placebo; ESL 800 mg — adjusted p=0.058 (not significant), 16.3% reduction. In the Daily-Entry-diary-only subpopulation, neither dose reached significance at the Dunnett-adjusted α=0.025 level
- Studies 301/302 were reanalyzed for the resubmission's Integrated Summary of Efficacy (excluding two non-compliant Study 301 sites, adding previously omitted diary pages, redefining the evaluation-period end date), yielding adjusted p-values of 0.0468 (301, 800 mg) and 0.0057 (302, 800 mg)

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §3.2.1, p.7, on Study 304's SAP provenance]*

> "The Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) was submitted to IND 67,466 serial number 242 on 11 August 2011 for the Agency to review, and was finalized on 06 December 2011. The SAP was amended after final approval as a result of compliance issues identified at Site 952, and was revised and signed off on 05 March 2012. The clinical database was locked and released for unblinding on 12 March 2012. The database was opened and relocked on 25 May 2012 to update the drug accountability data for Subject 00901."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2, p.8, primary analysis model]*

> "For the purpose of the primary efficacy analysis, standardized seizure frequency was natural logarithmically transformed (ln). To avoid the ln(0) problem, a constant (0.333) was added. The ln standardized seizure frequency during the maintenance period was analyzed using an ANCOVA model. The model included treatment as a fixed effect, ln standardized seizure frequency at baseline, and diary version as covariates."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2, p.8, multiplicity]*

> "To control the family-wise Type I error for the analysis of the primary efficacy variable in the ITT and DE Diary ITT populations, a 2-stage gate-keeping procedure was used (Dmitrienko et al Biometrical Journal 2008). In Stage 1, each of the two pair-wise comparisons of ESL 800 mg and 1200 mg to placebo in the ITT population was conducted using an alpha level of 0.025. If both comparisons were statistically significant, the Dunnett's method would be conducted at an alpha level of 0.05 for the DE population in Stage 2. If only one of two pair-wise comparisons was statistically significant in Stage 1, an alpha level of 0.025 would be carried over to the Stage 2 testing. If neither of the two pair-wise comparisons was statistically significant in Stage 1, the procedure would stop."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2, p.8-9, missing-data handling]*

> "If subjects discontinued during the 2-week titration period, before the start of the 12-week maintenance period, they were treated as missing in the primary efficacy analysis."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, on the internal reviewer disagreement]*

> "The totality of the findings supports the acceptability of the two pivotal studies reviewed in the first cycle (Study 301 and Study 302), and of the new study (Study 304)."

### 13. Florbetaben F 18 (Neuraceq) — NDA 204677

**Sponsor:** Piramal Imaging SA

**Indication approved:** Radioactive diagnostic agent for Positron Emission Tomography (PET) imaging of the brain to estimate β-amyloid neuritic plaque density in adult patients with cognitive impairment who are being evaluated for Alzheimer's disease or other causes of cognitive decline

**Approval date:** March 19, 2014

**Pivotal trial:** Study 14595 (autopsy/histopathology study), NCT01020838; Study 16034 (pooled-read reproducibility study, no CT.gov registration found — non-interventional re-read, no subjects dosed); Study FBB-01_01_13 (electronic-training "new read" amendment study, no separate CT.gov registration — filed under IND 78868)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison to histopathology truth standard); autopsy-confirmation cohort combining end-of-life subjects and young healthy volunteers as assumed-negative controls; non-interventional pooled-image reread study; FDA-required post-hoc reanalysis under an amended standard-of-truth definition

- *Endpoints:* sensitivity and specificity of majority visual read vs. histopathology (Bielschowsky silver stain ± immunohistochemistry, CERAD criteria); inter-reader and intra-reader kappa agreement

- *Primary analysis:* exact (Clopper-Pearson) binomial confidence interval for sensitivity/specificity, required by FDA in place of the sponsor's original normal-approximation (Rao-Scott) method given the small number of independent clusters (brains)

- *Missing data/bias:* FDA rejected the sponsor's originally proposed region-level primary analysis and BSS+IHC standard of truth, substituting a subject-level, BSS-only standard of truth as the regulatory primary analysis; no autopsy-confirmed MCI subjects were available in any study, a limitation the concurring statistical reviewer called "an extremely restraining factor"

- *Regulatory:* no FDA advisory committee meeting held for this NDA; FDA General Advice Letter (October 18, 2013) redirected the sponsor to a different standard-of-truth definition and CI methodology than originally submitted, resolved via a major amendment (New Read Study, submitted November 22, 2013) rather than a Complete Response

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 14595 ("the autopsy study," NCT01020838): open-label, non-randomized, single-arm Phase 3 study; 216 subjects dosed — 137 AD, 31 other dementia, 5 dementia with Lewy bodies, 32 non-demented volunteers, 11 healthy volunteers (including 10 young healthy volunteers as assumed-negative controls); truth standard was histopathology at autopsy, read by a masked 3-neuropathologist Consensus Panel using Bielschowsky silver stain, BSS+immunohistochemistry, and CERAD criteria across 6 pre-defined brain regions
- Sponsor's original primary analysis was region-level (majority read among 3 masked readers, matching ≥2 of 3) against regional histopathology, tested against H0: sensitivity ≤0.6/specificity ≤0.8 using a normal-approximation (Rao-Scott) CI method; FDA's reviewer found this improper given the small number of independent clusters (brains) and required exact (Clopper-Pearson) CIs instead, and directed a shift to subject-level analysis
- Study 16034 ("pooled read study"): non-interventional; no new subjects dosed; pooled re-read of 461 images (+46 for re-read) drawn from 6 prior florbetaben studies including Study 14595, by 5 new blinded readers trained via a web-based tool (versus in-person training in Study 14595); primary endpoint was inter-reader kappa across all 5 readers (H0: κ≤0.6 vs. H1: κ>0.6, rejected if lower 95% CI bound exceeded 0.6); sponsor-reported result κ=0.787 (95% CI 0.750-0.824), exceeding the threshold
- Secondary analysis in Study 16034 re-derived sensitivity/specificity in a 54-subject autopsy subset (plus 10 young healthy volunteers) against the same combined hypothesis (sensitivity ≤0.6/specificity ≤0.7); the pre-specified success criterion (≥3 of 5 readers meeting both thresholds) was met by only 1 of 5 readers — the "low-specificity" finding that triggered a major protocol amendment
- Study FBB-01_01_13 ("New Read Study," conducted October 8-9, 2013, submitted as a major amendment November 22, 2013): re-read of images from the full 82-subject autopsy cohort (31 from Study 14595, 23 added in Study 16034, 28 newly added) plus the 10 young healthy volunteers (n=92), by 5 new web-trained readers; FDA required the standard of truth to be BSS-only (not the sponsor's proposed BSS+IHC), per General Advice Letter COR-NDAIR-10 (October 18, 2013)
- FDA's required primary hypotheses for the New Read Study: H0,sensitivity ≤0.6 vs. H1 >0.6; H0,specificity ≤0.5 vs. H1 >0.5, combined hypothesis rejected if exact 95% CI lower bounds exceeded both thresholds for the same ≥3 of 5 readers
- Results (BSS-only standard of truth, n=82, excluding young healthy volunteers): lower CI bounds for sensitivity exceeded 0.7 for all 5 readers; lower CI bounds for specificity exceeded 0.5 for 3 of 5 readers (below 0.6 for the other 2) — the pre-specified criterion was met by exactly 3 of 5 readers, though 2 readers had specificity lower-CI bounds as low as 28% and 37%, a limitation the FDA statistical reviewer explicitly flagged while still recommending approval
- Inter-reader agreement in the New Read Study (n=92, BSS standard of truth): kappa 0.76 (95% CI 0.70-0.81); intra-reader agreement (20-image re-read) ranged 85%-100% by reader
- The final approved label organizes the evidence as "Study A" (Study 14595, in-person training, 3 readers), "Study B" (Study FBB-01_01_13, electronic training, 5 readers, same 82 subjects), and "Study C" (Study 16034, reproducibility, 461 images, kappa 0.79-0.80 across subgroups)

### 14. Suvorexant (Belsomra) — NDA 204569

**Sponsor:** Merck Sharp & Dohme LLC

**Indication approved:** Insomnia, characterized by difficulties with sleep onset and/or sleep maintenance

**Approval date:** August 13, 2014

**Pivotal trial:** Study P028 ("Trial 1"/"Study A"), NCT01097616; Study P029 ("Trial 2"/"Study B"), NCT01097629

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter; age-stratified dosing (non-elderly vs. elderly); 3:2:3 randomization to high dose : low dose : placebo; blindly-monitored sample-size re-estimation mid-trial

- *Endpoints:* co-primary subjective/objective sleep-maintenance endpoints (subjective total sleep time by e-diary; wake-after-sleep-onset by polysomnography) and sleep-onset endpoints (subjective time-to-sleep-onset by e-diary; latency to persistent sleep by polysomnography), each assessed at Month 1 and Month 3

- *Primary analysis:* longitudinal data analysis (FDA's term; functionally a mixed model for repeated measures) with an unstructured covariance matrix, adjusting for baseline value, age group, region, gender, treatment, time, and treatment-by-time interaction

- *Multiplicity:* Bonferroni split (0.025 each) between sleep-maintenance and sleep-onset endpoint families; fixed-sequence testing of high dose before low dose within each family; Hochberg adjustment between objective and subjective endpoints within each timepoint; all type-I-error allocation weighted toward the high-dose comparisons by design

- *Missing data/bias:* pre-specified worst-case imputation conventions for non-sleep nights (e.g., latency to persistent sleep imputed at 8 hours if the subject never fell asleep); multiple-imputation and rank-based (ETRANK) sensitivity analyses

- *Regulatory:* Complete Response Letter (June 28, 2013) rejecting the originally proposed 15-40 mg dose range on safety grounds after a Psychopharmacologic and CNS Drugs Advisory Committee vote (12-4 sleep onset; 16-0 sleep maintenance) on May 22, 2013; approved doses (5/10/20 mg) were never directly tested as distinct Phase 3 efficacy arms, resting instead on a bioavailability bridge to the tested 20 mg dose

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Two identically designed Phase III trials (P028/Study A, P029/Study B): randomized, double-blind (in-house blinding), placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter; screening period with a 2-week single-blind placebo run-in, a 3-month double-blind core treatment period (P028 had an optional 3-month double-blind extension), and a 1-week double-blind run-out period
- Randomization 3:2:3 to high dose : low dose : placebo; doses assigned by age — non-elderly (18-<65y) high/low = 40/20 mg; elderly (≥65y) high/low = 30/15 mg; two enrollment cohorts (diary-only, and PSG+diary)
- Co-primary endpoints: change from baseline at Month 1 and Month 3 in — Maintenance: subjective total sleep time (e-diary) and wake-after-sleep-onset (PSG); Onset: subjective time to sleep onset (e-diary) and latency to persistent sleep (PSG); secondary analyses at Week 1 (diary) / Night 1 (PSG)
- Sample size: 360 randomized to high dose and placebo each, 240 to low dose (diary-based, total N≈960); powered at 91% for maintenance endpoints and 62% for onset endpoints, based on Phase 2b (Study P006) effect sizes reduced by 10%
- Multiplicity strategy (from the Statistical Review): "to account for the evaluation of two distinct indications a Bonferroni approach was to be used; within each indication, a fixed sequential testing procedure was to be used to move from the first set of primary hypotheses (Month 1) to the next set of primary hypotheses (Month 3). Within each time point, a Hochberg approach was to be used to evaluate the objective and subjective endpoints" — with all type-I-error allocation weighted to the high-dose vs. placebo comparisons, since the low dose enrolled 30-40% fewer subjects by design
- Key finding: after multiplicity adjustment, the low dose was statistically significant for both maintenance endpoints in both trials, but for the sleep-onset endpoints only in Study P028 (not replicated in Study P029) — the FDA reviewer's executive summary states this failure to replicate meant "any secondary efficacy measures of Sleep Onset must be viewed as exploratory at best" for the low dose
- Missing-data conventions: if a subject never fell asleep, latency to persistent sleep was imputed at 8 hours (worst outcome, since time-in-bed was 8h for PSG nights) while wake-after-sleep-onset was set to missing; for e-diary data, subjective time-to-sleep-onset was imputed at 480 minutes when subjective total sleep time was 0
- Advisory Committee (May 22, 2013): committee voted 12-4 (1 abstain) that the proposed dose range was effective for sleep onset, and 16-0 (1 abstain) for sleep maintenance; discussion was split on whether the 10 mg dose (tested only in the Phase 2b crossover Study P006) was adequately established as effective
- Complete Response Letter (June 28, 2013) concluded the sponsor had shown substantial evidence of effectiveness at doses of 10-80 mg but had not shown the proposed 15/20 mg doses were safe, citing suicidal-ideation, next-day impairment/motor-vehicle-accident risk, unconscious nighttime activity, and cataplexy-like/hallucination signals that increased with dose; required the 10 mg dose (and a new 5 mg strength for use with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors) to be available at approval, and concluded the 30/40 mg doses were "unlikely to be safe"
- Resubmission relied on two new relative-bioavailability studies (P055, P056) establishing dose-proportional PK bridges from four 5 mg tablets and two 10 mg tablets, respectively, to the tested 20 mg dose — meaning the marketed 5 mg and 10 mg strengths, and the label's 10 mg recommended starting dose, were never directly tested as distinct efficacy arms in the pivotal PSG trials
- Approved August 13, 2014 for 5/10/15/20 mg tablets (30/40 mg voluntarily withdrawn from labeling by the sponsor); DEA scheduling was not finalized at the time of approval
