### 15. Peginterferon beta-1a (Plegridy) — BLA 125499

**Sponsor:** Biogen Idec Inc.

**Indication approved:** Relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis

**Approval date:** August 15, 2014

**Pivotal trial:** ADVANCE (Study 301 / 105MS301), NCT00906399

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, 3-arm (two dosing frequencies vs. placebo), with placebo re-randomized to active treatment for Year 2; single pivotal trial supported by the already-approved status of the parent molecule (non-pegylated interferon beta-1a) in a different formulation

- *Endpoints:* annualized relapse rate at 1 year (primary), proportion of subjects relapsed, EDSS-confirmed disability progression, new/newly-enlarging T2 MRI lesions (secondary)

- *Primary analysis:* negative binomial regression (log-likelihood ratio test) with a pre-specified fallback to Poisson regression if under-dispersion was detected via the Pearson chi-square statistic; Cox proportional-hazards model for time-to-first-relapse; negative binomial regression for MRI lesion counts

- *Multiplicity:* sequential (closed) testing procedure — the more frequent (every-2-week) dosing regimen tested first at α=0.05 per endpoint, with the every-4-week regimen tested at the same level only if the every-2-week comparison was significant; secondary endpoints rank-prioritized and gated behind the primary endpoint's sequential structure for both dose groups

- *Missing data/bias:* relapses occurring after a subject started an alternative MS therapy were excluded from analysis with censoring at the switch date; blinded, pooled-ARR-based sample-size re-estimation increased planned enrollment from 420 to 500 per group mid-trial; an interim futility analysis of MRI lesion data was conducted after the first 200 patients completed 24 weeks

- *Regulatory:* no FDA advisory committee meeting held; only one pivotal trial was required because the active moiety (interferon beta-1a) was already approved in a non-pegylated formulation

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ADVANCE: 2-year, global, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled trial; 1512 randomized subjects with relapsing-remitting MS (1516 total randomized per the CSR, 4 never dosed); randomized 1:1:1 to peginterferon beta-1a 125 mcg every 2 weeks, every 4 weeks, or placebo for Year 1, after which placebo subjects were re-randomized to one of the two active dosing regimens for Year 2 (not the primary hypothesis and not complete at BLA submission)
- Primary endpoint: annualized relapse rate (ARR) over Year 1, based on protocol-defined relapses (new/recurrent neurologic symptoms lasting ≥24 hours, not associated with fever/infection, with new objective findings on exam) confirmed by a centralized, blinded Independent Neurology Evaluation Committee (INEC); relapses within 29 days of a prior relapse's onset were counted as the same relapse
- Sample size: originally 420 per group (90%/87%/85% power at assumed placebo ARR of 0.6/0.55/0.5, assuming a 32% relative reduction), blindly increased to 500 per group after monitoring the pooled (blinded) ARR relative to the assumed treatment effect
- Primary analysis method: negative binomial regression (log-likelihood ratio test), with number of relapses as the response variable, log(time on study) as an offset, and treatment, baseline relapse rate (relapses over the prior 3 years, divided by 3), age (<40 vs. ≥40), and baseline EDSS (<4 vs. ≥4) as covariates; a Poisson model was the pre-specified fallback if the Pearson chi-square/degrees-of-freedom ratio indicated under-dispersion (<1), with the Poisson method also run as a routine sensitivity analysis regardless
- Secondary endpoints: proportion of subjects relapsed at 1 year (Cox proportional-hazards model, adjusted for baseline EDSS, age, baseline relapse rate, and Gd-enhancing-lesion status, with Kaplan-Meier-based proportions); confirmed EDSS disability progression at 1 and 2 years; number of new/newly-enlarging T2 lesions (negative binomial regression)
- Multiplicity: a sequential (closed) testing procedure tested the every-2-week dose vs. placebo first for the primary endpoint; the every-4-week dose was only formally tested if the every-2-week comparison was significant. Secondary endpoints were rank-prioritized under the same sequential structure across both dose groups, with no adjustment for tertiary endpoints
- An interim futility analysis of MRI T2-lesion data was conducted after the first 200 subjects completed 24 weeks; the FDA statistical reviewer found no indication this compromised trial integrity
- Only 3% of randomized subjects were enrolled in the US; the reviewer noted a numerically unfavorable US-subgroup trend for the every-2-week regimen on ARR and time-to-first-relapse that was not consistent across all endpoints (MRI T2 data favored the treatment arm in the same subgroup) and attributed it to small-subgroup variability rather than a genuine regional effect

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2014/125499lbl.pdf

- FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID 3438824, reviewer Tristan Massie, Ph.D.) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/125499Orig1s000StatR.pdf

- FDA Summary Review (Reference ID 3609116) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/125499Orig1s000SumR.pdf

"Pegylated interferon β-1a for relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (ADVANCE): a randomised, phase 3, double-blind study." *Lancet Neurol.* 2014;13(7):657-665. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1474-4422(14)70068-7>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24794721/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Pegylated%20interferon%20beta-1a%20for%20relapsing-remitting%20multiple%20sclerosis%20ADVANCE)

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Executive Summary]*

> "Only one study was required to support the application since the active ingredient in this product is approved in another formulation." ... "The primary endpoint was the annualized relapse rate over the first year. Relapses were adjudicated by a centralized committee. The multiplicity adjustment was sequential testing of a hierarchy of endpoints testing the more frequent administration first for each endpoint, and only formally testing the next endpoint if both doses won on the current one."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Multiplicity Adjustment section]*

> "Statistical testing for efficacy endpoints was to be made between the BIIB017 every 2 week group and the placebo group, and between the BIIB017 every 4 week group and the placebo group separately. A sequential (closed) testing procedure was to be used to control the overall Type I error rate due to multiple comparisons for the primary endpoint. If the first comparison (the every 2 week group versus placebo) was statistically significant (p ≤ 0.05) then the second comparison (the every 4 week group versus placebo) would also be made at the 0.05 alpha level. However, if the first comparison was not statistically significant, then the second comparison could not be considered statistically significant."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, primary analysis method]*

> "The primary analysis method for annualized relapse rate was to be negative binomial regression (log-likelihood ratio test assuming the number of relapses follows a negative binomial distribution). If the data is under-dispersed or if the negative binomial regression model does not converge a Poisson model was to be used instead... The model was to include a term for treatment, the baseline relapse rate, age (<40 vs. ≥ 40), and EDSS (<4 or ≥ 4)."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, relapse-censoring rule]*

> "Relapses that occur after subjects receive any alternative drug treatments directed toward the treatment of MS ... were to be excluded from the analyses of relapse rate, and the subject's time on study was to be censored at the time the alternative MS medication was started."

### 16. Brexpiprazole (Rexulti) — NDA 205422

**Sponsor:** Otsuka Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (co-developed with H. Lundbeck A/S)

**Indication approved:** Adjunctive treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD) in adults, and treatment of schizophrenia in adults — approved simultaneously for both indications under one NDA, internally reviewed by FDA as two separate sub-applications (Orig1 = MDD, Orig2 = schizophrenia)

**Approval date:** July 10, 2015

**Pivotal trial:** MDD — Polaris (331-10-227), NCT01360632, and Pyxis (331-10-228), NCT01360645; Schizophrenia — BEACON (331-10-230), NCT01393613, and VECTOR (331-10-231), NCT01396421

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, fixed-dose, parallel-group trials; MDD trials used an 8-week single-blind prospective antidepressant-treatment run-in (Phase A) followed by a 6-week randomized adjunctive Phase B; schizophrenia trials were 6-week fixed-dose (3-arm) acute-exacerbation trials; single NDA carrying two independently-reviewed indications

- *Endpoints:* MDD — MADRS total score change from baseline (primary), Sheehan Disability Scale mean score change (key secondary); Schizophrenia — PANSS total score change from baseline (primary), CGI-S change (key secondary)

- *Primary analysis:* mixed model repeated measures (MMRM) with unstructured covariance and Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom, fixed effects for treatment, center/pooled-center, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction, and baseline (and baseline-by-visit) as covariates — used for both indications

- *Multiplicity:* Hochberg's procedure across the two brexpiprazole dose groups vs. placebo (schizophrenia trials, and the two-dose MDD trial Polaris); fixed-sequence gatekeeping from primary to key-secondary endpoint in the single-dose MDD trial Pyxis; a global average-effect test preceding individual-dose comparisons in the schizophrenia trials

- *Missing data/bias:* MMRM as the primary analysis (sponsor's original primary was ANCOVA with LOCF prior to a protocol amendment in the MDD program); pattern-mixture models via multiple imputation, shared-parameter models, and random-coefficient pattern-mixture models used as missing-data sensitivity analyses in both indications

- *Regulatory:* no FDA advisory committee meeting held for either indication; FDA statistical review explicitly declined to extend the schizophrenia 2 mg dose claim onto the label after it was significant in only one of two trials ("An additional evidence... may be required")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- MDD program: Polaris (331-10-227) tested brexpiprazole 1 mg/day and 3 mg/day adjunctive to antidepressant therapy (677 randomized in Phase B); Pyxis (331-10-228) tested a single dose, 2 mg/day (379 randomized in Phase B); both used an 8-week single-blind prospective Phase A (antidepressant + single-blind placebo) to identify inadequate responders, followed by a 6-week double-blind randomized Phase B
- MDD primary endpoint: change from end of Phase A (Week 8) to end of Phase B (Week 14) in MADRS total score, analyzed by MMRM (unstructured covariance, Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom); key secondary: Sheehan Disability Scale mean score change, tested only if the primary endpoint's null hypotheses were rejected
- MDD multiplicity: Polaris used Hochberg's procedure across the two doses for the primary endpoint, with a second Hochberg procedure (α=0.05, two-sided) for the key secondary endpoint gated behind both primary comparisons; Pyxis (single dose) used simple fixed-sequence gatekeeping from primary to key secondary
- MDD results: Pyxis (2 mg) — LS-mean difference from placebo −3.12, p=0.0001 (statistically significant, single positive trial); Polaris — 1 mg not significant (p=0.0925), 3 mg nominally p=0.0327 but not significant after the Hochberg-adjusted threshold of 0.025. FDA's statistical review concluded: "There is some evidence that brexpiprazole is efficacious in treating major depressive disorder... Study 228 showed efficacy for Brexpiprazole 2mg. Study 227 seemed to suggest a modest treatment effect for brexpiprazole 3mg; however, it was not statistically significant after adjusting for multiplicity"
- A pre-specified sensitivity analysis (ANCOVA with LOCF) had been the sponsor's original primary analysis before Protocol Amendment 3 (March 23, 2012) switched the primary method to MMRM; the FDA review presents this as a sponsor-initiated protocol amendment rather than an FDA-mandated change
- Schizophrenia program: BEACON (331-10-230) and VECTOR (331-10-231) were both 6-week, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 3-fixed-dose trials (BEACON: 1/2/4 mg/day, 674 randomized; VECTOR: 0.25/2/4 mg/day, 636 randomized)
- Schizophrenia primary endpoint: PANSS total score change from baseline to Week 6 by MMRM; key secondary: CGI-S change, tested only if both dose comparisons of the primary endpoint were significant
- Schizophrenia multiplicity: the average effect of the 2 mg and 4 mg doses vs. placebo was tested first (global test, α=0.05); only if significant were the individual 4 mg and 2 mg dose comparisons vs. placebo tested (each at α=0.05)
- Schizophrenia results: BEACON — 4 mg LS-mean difference −6.5 (95% CI −10.6, −2.3; p=0.0022), 2 mg not significant (p=0.15); VECTOR — 4 mg p=0.0006, 2 mg p<0.0001 (nominal). FDA's statistical review concluded 4 mg was supported by two positive trials, but declined to extend a 2 mg claim: "An additional evidence (such as another positive clinical trial) may be required to include a claim on Brexpiprazole 2mg into the label"

### 17. Cariprazine (Vraylar) — NDA 204370

**Sponsor:** Forest Laboratories, LLC

**Indication approved:** Schizophrenia, and treatment of manic or mixed episodes associated with bipolar I disorder — approved simultaneously for both indications

**Approval date:** September 17, 2015

**Pivotal trial:** Schizophrenia — RGH-MD-04, NCT01104766; RGH-MD-05, NCT01104779; RGH-MD-16 (phase 2, supportive), NCT00694707; supportive RGH-MD-03, NCT00404573; Bipolar mania — RGH-MD-31, NCT00488618; RGH-MD-32, NCT01058096; RGH-MD-33, NCT01058668

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, fixed and fixed-flexible dose designs across seven trials (four schizophrenia, three bipolar mania); active comparator arms (aripiprazole, risperidone) included in some trials to establish assay sensitivity, at FDA's encouragement

- *Endpoints:* PANSS total score change from baseline to Week 6 (schizophrenia primary) and CGI-S (key secondary); YMRS total score change from baseline to Week 3 (bipolar mania primary) and CGI-S (key secondary)

- *Primary analysis:* mixed model repeated measures (MMRM) as the pre-specified primary method in the phase 3 trials, with ANCOVA (LOCF) as a pre-specified sensitivity analysis; the phase 2 trials used ANCOVA (LOCF) as primary with MMRM as sensitivity

- *Multiplicity:* matched parallel gatekeeping (Chen, Luo & Capizzi 2005) linking each dose's primary-endpoint significance to that dose's key-secondary-endpoint testing eligibility; sequential testing (PANSS/YMRS then CGI-S) in other trials

- *Missing data/bias:* a pattern-mixture multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis (Kenward, Molenberghs & Thijs 2003) with a pre-specified shift parameter; one site with ~200 potentially unreported adverse events (identified post-unblinding) was retained in the efficacy analysis, with dedicated sensitivity analyses excluding it

- *Regulatory:* no FDA advisory committee meeting held; FDA statistical review explicitly stated efficacy of a fixed 9 mg/day dose was not established despite label language implying an effective range up to 9 mg

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Schizophrenia program: RGH-MD-04 (9-week duration; 1:1:1:1 to placebo, cariprazine 3 mg, 6 mg, or aripiprazole 10 mg), RGH-MD-05 (1:1:1 to placebo, cariprazine 3-6 mg, or 6-9 mg fixed-flexible), RGH-MD-16 (phase 2; 1:1:1:1:1 to placebo, cariprazine 1.5/3/4.5 mg, or risperidone 4 mg), and supportive RGH-MD-03 (1:1:1 to placebo, cariprazine 1.5-4.5 mg, or 6-12 mg); all used a 6-week double-blind treatment phase with a no-drug washout beforehand, patients hospitalized for a minimum of 3-4 weeks after randomization
- Bipolar mania program: RGH-MD-31 (1:1 to placebo or cariprazine, 5-week duration), RGH-MD-32 (1:1 to placebo or cariprazine 3-12 mg), RGH-MD-33 (1:1:1 to placebo, cariprazine 3-6 mg, or 6-12 mg); all used a 3-week double-blind treatment phase with a minimum 14-day post-randomization hospitalization
- Primary analysis: for the phase 3 trials (MD-04, MD-05 schizophrenia; MD-33 bipolar), the pre-specified primary method was MMRM (treatment group, pooled study center, visit, and treatment-by-visit interaction, with baseline as covariate), with ANCOVA (LOCF) as a pre-specified sensitivity analysis; the phase 2 trials (MD-16, MD-03, MD-31) used ANCOVA (LOCF) as primary with MMRM as sensitivity
- Multiplicity: MD-04 (and similarly MD-33) used a matched parallel-gatekeeping procedure — two null hypotheses for the primary endpoint (each dose vs. placebo) formed a gatekeeper family that had to be at least partially rejected before the corresponding key-secondary-endpoint (CGI-S) hypothesis for that dose could be tested; MD-16 and MD-03 used sequential testing (PANSS/YMRS, then CGI-S only if all PANSS/YMRS tests were significant, testing doses in descending order)
- Results: statistically significant efficacy was established for PANSS/CGI-S at daily doses of 1.5, 3, and 4.5 mg (phase 2 dose-finding study MD-16) and confirmed for fixed doses of 3 and 6 mg (phase 3 study MD-04); FDA's statistical reviewer explicitly stated efficacy of a fixed 9 mg/day dose "has not been established" and "no data is available to sufficiently assess whether or not the 9 mg is as effective as any other lower dose" — the only supportive data for 9 mg came from a flexible-dose arm (MD-05, 6-9 mg) where the mean daily exposure was calculated at 6.55 mg/day, not a true fixed 9 mg regimen
- A data-integrity issue was identified: of 220 unique sites, 8 were inspected by FDA's Office of Regulatory Affairs, and the Office of Scientific Investigations identified approximately 200 potentially unreported adverse events at one investigator's site (discovered only after unblinding); this site was retained in the efficacy analysis, with sponsor-conducted sensitivity analyses showing no change to the efficacy conclusions
- A pattern-mixture multiple-imputation missing-data sensitivity analysis (Kenward, Molenberghs & Thijs 2003 method) with a pre-specified shift parameter was used as an additional check on the primary MMRM results

> "The Office of Scientific Investigations (OSI) Investigator identified approximately 200 potentially unreported adverse events in the FDA Form 483 issued to one of the investigators who participated in the cariprazine clinical program. Unlike other GCP violations, this site was included in the efficacy analysis, as the GCP violation of this site was found after the data was unblinded. The sponsor conducted efficacy sensitivity analyses for the pivotal studies that this investigator participated in... This site did not alter the efficacy conclusions."

### 18. Aripiprazole lauroxil (Aristada) — NDA 207533

**Sponsor:** Alkermes, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Schizophrenia, as a long-acting intramuscular injectable (extended-release prodrug of aripiprazole)

**Approval date:** October 5, 2015

**Pivotal trial:** ALK9072-003, NCT01469039

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single pivotal randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (two active fixed doses vs. placebo), supported by a pharmacokinetic bridge to already-approved oral aripiprazole rather than a second independent efficacy trial

- *Endpoints:* PANSS total score change from baseline to Day 85 (primary); CGI-I score at Day 85 (secondary)

- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA model with last-observation-carried-forward (LOCF) imputation as the sponsor's pre-specified primary method, with treatment group and study region as fixed effects and baseline PANSS as covariate

- *Multiplicity:* Hommel procedure (two-sided α=0.05) linking the CGI-I secondary endpoint to the primary endpoint's significance

- *Missing data/bias:* FDA statistical reviewer disputed the sponsor's LOCF-based primary analysis given a 42.1% dropout rate, and required MMRM (observed-data, no imputation) as a co-primary sensitivity analysis at the protocol/SAP review stage; a disputed single-subject exclusion (Subject 502-002) from the sponsor's analysis population was reinstated by the FDA reviewer, who repeated all analyses with and without the subject

- *Regulatory:* no FDA advisory committee meeting held; FDA explicitly grounded its efficacy conclusion in "the results of this single study... together with additional pharmacokinetic data that provides an adequate bridge" to oral aripiprazole (Abilify) efficacy findings

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ALK9072-003: multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial in subjects with acute exacerbation of schizophrenia, conducted at 107 centers in the US, Asia, and Europe; subjects randomized 1:1:1 on Day 1 to aripiprazole lauroxil 882 mg, 441 mg, or placebo (Intralipid), with IM doses on Days 1, 29, and 57, plus 3 weeks of double-blind oral aripiprazole or oral placebo as an initiation regimen; 623 subjects randomized (208 placebo, 207 at 441 mg, 208 at 882 mg)
- Primary efficacy endpoint: change in PANSS total score from baseline to Day 85, analyzed by the sponsor's pre-specified ANCOVA model with LOCF imputation (treatment group and region as fixed effects, baseline PANSS as covariate); secondary endpoint: CGI-I score at Day 85, tested via Hommel procedure at two-sided α=0.05 if the primary endpoint was significant
- FDA's statistical reviewer flagged the high dropout rate (42.1%) as undermining the LOCF-based primary analysis and noted that "during the protocol/SAP review stage, FDA raised the concern about the LOCF method and requested the sponsor to use the MMRM method and other methods as sensitivity analyses" — MMRM (observed data only, no imputation, unstructured covariance, treatment-by-visit interaction) was run alongside LOCF, along with per-protocol ANCOVA-LOCF and non-parametric rank-ANCOVA analyses
- A data-handling dispute arose over Subject "502-002," whom the sponsor excluded from the Full Analysis Set on the grounds of an unrated post-baseline PANSS assessment; the FDA reviewer disagreed with this exclusion under the sponsor's own FAS definition and repeated all primary and sensitivity analyses with and without the subject, finding the same conclusions either way
- Both aripiprazole lauroxil doses (441 mg and 882 mg) were statistically significantly better than placebo on the primary endpoint by both ANCOVA-LOCF and MMRM; CGI-I scores were also statistically significantly better for both active groups than placebo
- Because efficacy rested on a single pivotal trial, FDA's Summary Review states the conclusion explicitly relied on a pharmacokinetic bridge: "The results of this single study support the effectiveness of the product, together with additional pharmacokinetic data that provides an adequate bridge to the Agency's efficacy findings for Abilify Tablets (oral aripiprazole tablets); and provide safety information for the new drug"

- FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID 3774690, reviewer Jinglin Zhong, Ph.D.) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/207533Orig1s000StatR.pdf

- FDA Summary Review (Reference ID 3828479) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/207533Orig1s000SumR.pdf

"A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of aripiprazole lauroxil in acute exacerbation of schizophrenia." *J Clin Psychiatry.* 2015;76(8):1085-1090. **SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Executive Summary]*

> "This review describes statistical findings about the sponsor's study report ALK9072-003 supporting the request for approval of aripiprazole lauroxil in subjects with schizophrenia... This NDA submission includes one pivotal safety and efficacy study (ALK9072-003) to support the efficacy of two aripiprazole lauroxil dose levels (441 mg and 882 mg) in subjects with schizophrenia."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, primary analysis and the FDA-required MMRM sensitivity analysis]*

> "The primary efficacy endpoint was analyzed by the ANCOVA model using the LOCF approach... Reviewer's note: The primary efficacy analysis uses LOCF to impute the missing data. Given the high dropout rate (42.1%) for this trial, the LOCF method is not very sensible. During the protocol/SAP review stage, FDA raised the concern about the LOCF method and requested the sponsor to use the MMRM method and other methods as sensitivity analyses."

The change from baseline from Day 22 or Day 29 to Day 85 was statistically significantly better for each active treatment group (aripiprazole lauroxil 441 mg and 882 mg) than for placebo. CGI-I scores at Day 85 were statistically significantly better for each active treatment group than for placebo. No significant subgroup differences were identified." ... "The results of this single study support the effectiveness of the product, together with additional pharmacokinetic data that provides an adequate bridge to the Agency's efficacy findings for Abilify Tablets (oral aripiprazole tablets); and provide safety information for the new drug."

### 19. Brivaracetam (Briviact) — NDA 205836

**Sponsor:** UCB, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adjunctive treatment of partial-onset (focal) seizures in patients 16 years of age and older with epilepsy

**Approval date:** February 18, 2016

**Pivotal trial:** N01252, NCT00490035; N01253, NCT00464269; N01358, NCT01261325

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* three randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, fixed-dose, parallel-group, multicenter adjunctive trials; concomitant levetiracetam use capped at 20% of enrollment in the first two trials, then excluded entirely in the third trial after being identified as a confounding factor

- *Endpoints:* seizure frequency per week (N01252, N01253) or per 28 days (N01358), analyzed as percent reduction over placebo (primary); ≥50% responder rate, seizure-free rate (secondary)

- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA on log-transformed (ln(x+1)) seizure frequency, with treatment and stratification effects as factors and log-transformed baseline seizure frequency as covariate; stratification varied by study (region and concomitant levetiracetam use in N01252/N01253; country and levetiracetam-by-prior-AED-count in N01358)

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence testing across doses in N01252 and N01253 (a higher dose tested only if a specified lower/anchor dose reached significance first); Hochberg step-up procedure across the two doses in N01358

- *Missing data/bias:* seizure frequency computed only over non-missing days within a period, with no explicit imputation for partial missingness; a Longitudinal Linear Mixed-Effects model and a non-parametric rank-ANCOVA were pre-specified sensitivity analyses; an FDA addendum corrected a sponsor calculation error in the reported percent-reduction formula

- *Regulatory:* no FDA advisory committee meeting held; none of the three trials individually replicated a positive result for every tested dose, with FDA's executive summary noting doses ≥100 mg/day were the most consistently supported

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Three Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, fixed-dose, multicenter trials in adults (≥16 years) with refractory partial-onset seizures, each with an 8-week prospective baseline period followed by a 12-week double-blind treatment period without up-titration

- N01252 (Europe and India, N=399 randomized): brivaracetam 20/50/100 mg/day vs. placebo; concomitant levetiracetam capped at 20% of enrollment (given the shared SV2A binding site)

- N01253 (global, N=400 randomized): brivaracetam 5/20/50 mg/day vs. placebo; same 20% levetiracetam cap

- N01358 (global, initiated after N01252/N01253 completion, N=768 randomized): brivaracetam 100/200 mg/day vs. placebo; patients on levetiracetam within 90 days of entry were excluded entirely, following the confounding signal observed in the first two trials

- Primary analysis: seizure frequency (per 7 days for N01252/N01253, per 28 days for N01358) log-transformed as ln(x+1) and analyzed by ANCOVA, with treatment and stratification factors and log-transformed baseline frequency as covariate; estimated seizure frequencies were back-transformed via exponentiation and subtraction of 1

- Multiplicity: N01252 tested doses sequentially in the order 50 mg → 100 mg → 20 mg (a later dose tested only if the current dose was significant at α=0.05); N01253 tested 50 mg → 20 mg → 5 mg. N01358 used the Hochberg procedure across the 100 mg and 200 mg doses: the larger of the two p-values was tested first at 0.05; if not significant, the smaller p-value was tested at 0.025

- Results: N01252 — 100 mg/day nominally significant vs. placebo (11.7% reduction over placebo, p=0.037) but the primary conclusion was not reached because the required anchor dose (50 mg) did not reach significance under the sequential procedure; N01253 — 50 mg/day achieved significance (p=0.025); N01358 — both 100 mg and 200 mg achieved significance (p<0.001 for both)

- FDA's executive summary: "Although none of the tested BRV doses had duplicated positive efficacy in 2 or more of the trials, the data strongly suggested that BRV 100 mg/day and 200 mg/day were effective. The effectiveness of BRV 50 mg/day could not be conclusively determined as statistical significance was reached in Study N01253, but not in N01252. BRV at doses below 50 mg daily did not show effectiveness."

- An FDA statistical-review addendum corrected the sponsor's calculation of "% reduction in seizure frequency": the sponsor's formula omitted the SAP-specified subtraction of 1 from the back-transformed LS-mean estimates of x+1, understating the true percent reduction (more so for the 7-day than the 28-day endpoint); FDA recalculated the corrected percent-reduction figures used in the final label

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, primary analysis method]*

> "The obtained seizure frequency per week or per 28 days was then transformed by logarithm ln(x+1) (where x was the seizure frequency per week or per 28 days). The log-transformed POS frequency over the Treatment Period was analyzed applying an ANCOVA model, including treatment and stratification effects as factors and the log-transformed Baseline seizure frequency per week as covariate."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, multiplicity — N01252/N01253]*

> "In Studies N01252 and N01253, the 3 doses of BRV were tested at the 5% level against placebo sequentially in the following order: Study N01252: 50mg/day, then the 100mg/day, and finally the 20mg/day dose. Study N01253: 50mg/day, then the 20mg/day, and finally the 5mg/day dose. Thus, a next dose was compared with placebo if and only if statistical significance was reached with the current dose."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, multiplicity — N01358, Hochberg procedure]*

> "For Study 01358, statistical testing was based on the comparison of each BRV treatment group (BRV 100 and 200mg/day) to placebo with control of overall type I error rate based on the Hochberg procedure. The Hochberg procedure was applied by first testing the BRV treatment group with the larger p-value. If the larger p-value was < 0.05, then statistical significance was achieved and both BRV treatment groups were to be declared statistically different from placebo. If the largest p-value was greater than 0.05, then the procedure was to compare the smaller p-value to 0.025."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review addendum, on the sponsor's calculation error]*

> "According to the Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP), seizure frequency in Studies N01252 and N01253 was calculated and analyzed on a per 7-day basis while seizure frequency for Study N01358 was calculated and analyzed on a per 28-day basis. Also specified in the SAP, that a log transformation of log(x+1) ... was to be performed... In the results reported in the Clinical Study Report, correct seizure frequencies were reported, i.e., 1 was subtracted from the estimate of seizure frequency. However, in calculating the % reduction of seizure frequency, the definition given by the SAP did not include the subtraction of 1... The obtained estimates of the % reduction were thus smaller than what actually should be."

### 20. Pimavanserin (Nuplazid) — NDA 207318

**Sponsor:** Acadia Pharmaceuticals Inc.

**Indication approved:** Hallucinations and delusions associated with Parkinson's disease psychosis — the first FDA-approved drug for this indication

**Approval date:** April 29, 2016

**Pivotal trial:** ACP-103-020, NCT01174004 (single pivotal efficacy trial; supportive earlier trials ACP-103-006 [60 randomized] and ACP-103-012 [298 randomized, India] were not independently sufficient)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single pivotal randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, fixed-dose (40 mg) trial in Parkinson's disease psychosis, with FDA basing regular approval on this one adequate and well-controlled trial

- *Endpoints:* SAPS-PD (Scale for the Assessment of Positive Symptoms adapted for Parkinson's Disease, a modified 9-item instrument) total score change from baseline to Week 6 (primary); UPDRS Parts II+III combined score change (key secondary, non-inferiority framing to confirm no worsening of motor symptoms)

- *Primary analysis:* REML-based mixed model repeated measures (MMRM) with fixed categorical effects of treatment, visit, and treatment-by-visit interaction, plus baseline score as a continuous covariate, unstructured covariance, Kenward-Roger denominator degrees of freedom; primary analysis used observed data only (no imputation)

- *Multiplicity:* the key secondary endpoint (UPDRS II+III, non-inferiority margin of 5 points) was tested only if the primary endpoint's null hypothesis was rejected at two-sided α=0.05

- *Missing data/bias:* pre-specified ANCOVA sensitivity analyses using worst-observation-carried-forward (WOCF) and last-observation-carried-forward (LOCF) imputation, both consistent with the primary MMRM conclusion; a post hoc sensitivity analysis removing patients who met certain exclusion criteria despite being randomized did not alter the primary conclusion

- *Regulatory:* Psychopharmacologic Drugs Advisory Committee (PDAC) meeting held March 29, 2016, voted 12-2 that benefits outweighed risks; FDA's Division Director concluded "the robustly positive single study 020 is sufficient" to support approval, over the primary medical reviewer's dissenting recommendation not to approve

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ACP-103-020: multicenter, randomized, fixed-dose, double-blind, placebo-controlled efficacy study; 199 subjects randomized across 66 centers (63 in the US) to pimavanserin 40 mg or placebo; modified intent-to-treat (mITT) population of 185 patients had a baseline and at least one post-baseline SAPS-PD assessment
- Inclusion required psychotic symptoms (hallucinations and/or delusions) developing after a Parkinson's disease diagnosis, present for at least one month and active weekly in the month before screening, with severity thresholds on the NPI Hallucinations/Delusions items and on SAPS-PD global items
- Primary endpoint: change from baseline to Week 6 in SAPS-PD total score, analyzed by REML-based MMRM (fixed effects: treatment, visit [Weeks 2/4/6], treatment-by-visit interaction; covariate: baseline score; unstructured covariance; Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom); significance tested at Week 6 using a two-sided α=0.05, observed data only, no imputation
- Key secondary endpoint: change from baseline to Week 6 in combined UPDRS Parts II (activities of daily living) and III (motor examination) score, with only one post-baseline assessment, analyzed by ANCOVA (observed-cases, mITT), assessed via a pre-specified non-inferiority margin of 5 points; tested only if the primary endpoint's null hypothesis was rejected at α=0.05
- Primary result: LS-mean change was −5.79 (pimavanserin) vs. −2.73 (placebo), difference −3.06 (95% CI −4.91, −1.20; p=0.0014); the treatment difference was not significant at Week 2 but emerged by Week 4 (p=0.037) and strengthened by Week 6
- Sensitivity analyses (ANCOVA with WOCF and LOCF imputation) yielded treatment differences of −2.78 and −2.91 respectively, both consistent with the primary MMRM conclusion (−3.06); FDA's reviewer also examined removing 24-45 randomized patients who met certain exclusion criteria (concomitant medications) and found no material change to the efficacy estimate
- Key secondary result: UPDRS II+III combined score changes were similar between groups (pimavanserin −1.36 vs. placebo −1.73), confirming non-inferiority (no worsening of motor symptoms) within the pre-specified 5-point margin
- Two earlier trials (ACP-103-006, 60 randomized, and ACP-103-012, 298 randomized in India using doses of 10 mg and 40 mg) did not independently establish efficacy; FDA's Division Director explicitly grounded the approval decision in Study 020 alone, describing it as "the robustly positive single study 020," while noting the primary medical reviewer "recommended that it not be approved," based on his view that "efficacy was only minimally clinically significant, and not outweighed" by safety signals

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2016/207318Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2016/207318lbl.pdf

- FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID 3890507; addendum Reference ID 3924615) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/207318Orig1s000StatR.pdf

"Pimavanserin for patients with Parkinson's disease psychosis: a randomised, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial." *Lancet.* 2014;383(9916):533-540. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(13)62106-6>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24183563/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Pimavanserin%20for%20patients%20with%20Parkinson%27s%20disease%20psychosis%20randomised%20placebo-controlled%20phase%203%20trial)

**Other resources**

- No Acadia-specific data-sharing program participation was confirmed in this pass; state as unconfirmed rather than assumed.

- FDA Psychopharmacologic Drugs Advisory Committee (PDAC) meeting held March 29, 2016; voted 12-2 that the benefits of the drug outweighed the risks of treatment.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, primary analysis method]*

> "Mean change from baseline in SAPS-PD was analyzed using a restricted maximum likelihood (REML)-based mixed model repeated measures (MMRM) method. The model included the fixed, categorical effects of treatment (placebo or pimavanserin; 2 levels), visit (Weeks 2, 4 and 6; 3 levels) and treatment-by-visit interaction, as well as the continuous, fixed covariate of baseline score. An unstructured covariance matrix was used to model the within-subject errors. The Kenward-Roger approximation was used to estimate denominator degrees of freedom... The primary analysis used observed measurements alone and no missing data were imputed."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, key secondary endpoint and multiplicity]*

> "The key secondary endpoint was the mean change from baseline to Week 6 in the combined score of the UPDRS Part II (activities of daily living) and Part III (motor examination). There was only one post-baseline assessment, and the primary analysis was the ANCOVA analysis (OC, i.e., completers only) with the mITT analysis set. To control the study-wise type I error rate, the test for key secondary endpoint was planned to be performed only when the null hypothesis for the primary efficacy endpoint was rejected at the significance level of 0.05 (two-sided)."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, primary efficacy result]*

> LS Mean Estimate (SE): Pimavanserin −5.79 (0.66), Placebo −2.73 (0.67); Difference from Placebo in LS Mean Estimate (SE): −3.06 (0.94); 95% CI (−4.91, −1.20); p=0.0014.

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, Division Director's conclusion on the single-trial basis]*

> "Dr. Andreason, the primary medical reviewer, agrees that efficacy has been demonstrated, but he maintains in his review that efficacy is modest and must be weighed against the safety signals for the drug... I conclude that the drug has demonstrated substantial evidence of effectiveness, and that the robustly positive single study 020 is sufficient to reach this conclusion."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, Advisory Committee]*

> "This application was presented to the Psychopharmacologic Drugs Advisory Committee (PDAC) on 29 March 2016. The PDAC voted 12 to 2 that the benefits of the drug outweighed the risks of treatment."

### 21. Daclizumab (Zinbryta) — BLA 761029

**Sponsor:** Biogen Idec (co-developed with AbbVie Biotherapeutics)

**Indication approved:** Relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (RMS)

**Approval date:** May 27, 2016

**Pivotal trial:** DECIDE (Study 301), NCT01064401 (confirmatory, active-controlled vs. interferon beta-1a); SELECT (Study 201), NCT00390221 (supportive, placebo-controlled dose-ranging)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled [DECIDE]; randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging [SELECT]
- *Endpoints:* annualized relapse rate (ARR)
- *Primary analysis:* negative binomial regression with an offset for exposure time (not yet in Keyword_Taxonomy.md § Primary analysis method)
- *Regulatory:* Good Clinical Practice (GCP) misconduct finding at a trial site (two DECIDE sites excluded in a sensitivity analysis, no change to conclusion); FDA "No Agreement" letter rejecting a proposed SAP modification, followed by a sponsor-revised SAP accepted before database lock (distinct from the existing SPA-rescission/SPA-amendment rows, since here it is a post-SPA SAP dispute resolved short of rescinding the underlying SPA); Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) with Elements to Assure Safe Use required at approval (Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy with Elements to Assure Safe Use required at approval); voluntary global market withdrawal in 2018 for post-marketing serious/fatal immune-mediated neuroinflammatory adverse events, not tied to a failed confirmatory trial (distinct from the existing "market withdrawal after confirmatory-trial failure" rows in Keyword_Taxonomy.md)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- DECIDE (Study 301): randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, parallel-group, active-controlled, monotherapy trial in patients with RMS; daclizumab HYP 150 mg subcutaneously every 4 weeks vs. interferon beta-1a (IFN β-1a) 30 mcg intramuscularly weekly, for at least 96 and up to 144 weeks; N=1841 randomized 1:1, stratified by site and prior IFN-β use; relapses adjudicated by a blinded Independent Neurology Evaluation Committee (INEC)
- SELECT (Study 201): randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 3-arm dose-ranging trial (placebo, daclizumab HYP 150 mg, 300 mg, each SC every 4 weeks), 52 weeks, N=621, 1:1:1 randomization
- Primary endpoint (both trials): annualized relapse rate (ARR), counting only INEC-confirmed relapses occurring up to end of treatment period, switch to alternative MS medication, or study withdrawal
- Primary analysis: negative binomial regression model adjusting for baseline relapse rate (relapses in the 3 years pre-study, divided by 3), prior IFN-β use, baseline EDSS (≤2.5 vs. >2.5), and age (≤35 vs. >35), with log(years in study) as the model's offset term
- Five pre-specified sensitivity analyses: (1) all data through Last Patient Last Treatment-Period Visit rather than End of Treatment; (2) including relapses occurring after starting an alternative MS medication; (3) including all protocol-defined relapses regardless of INEC confirmation; (4) an alternative censoring rule (earliest of alternative-medication start, End of Treatment Visit, or 96 weeks post-first-dose); (5) a Poisson-regression alternative to the negative binomial model
- Results: DECIDE — adjusted ARR ratio 0.55 (daclizumab vs. IFN β-1a), a 45% relative reduction (p<0.0001); SELECT — ARR reduced 54% at 150 mg and 50% at 300 mg vs. placebo (p<0.0001 and p=0.0002)
- Two DECIDE sites — Site 235 (Brazil, 11 subjects) and Site 453 (Italy, 40 subjects) — were found non-compliant with Good Clinical Practice; excluding them in a sensitivity analysis did not change the result
- SAP history: an SPA Agreement letter was issued June 7, 2010; the final protocol (dated April 29, 2013) changed the secondary-endpoint ranking and testing procedure from the SPA-agreed version; FDA issued a formal "No Agreement" letter to a further proposed SAP modification on April 28, 2014; the sponsor revised the SAP again in response, finalizing it May 23, 2014, which FDA accepted before database lock on September 16, 2014

N Engl J Med. 2015;373(15):1418-1428. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1501481), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26444729/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Daclizumab%20HYP%20versus%20Interferon%20Beta-1a%20in%20Relapsing%20Multiple%20Sclerosis)

- Pivotal publication (SELECT): Gold R, Giovannoni G, Selmaj K, Havrdova E, Montalban X, Radue EW, et al; SELECT study investigators. "Daclizumab high-yield process in relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (SELECT): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial." Lancet. 2013;381(9884):2167-2175. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(12)62190-4>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23562009/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Daclizumab%20high-yield%20process%20in%20relapsing-remitting%20multiple%20sclerosis%20SELECT)

**Other resources**

- Biogen and AbbVie participate generally in cross-industry IPD-sharing platforms (e.g., Vivli); trial-specific DECIDE/SELECT dataset availability was not individually confirmed here, and given the 2018 global withdrawal, ongoing sponsor-managed access is uncertain.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was referenced in the reviewed FDA documents for this BLA; not independently confirmed beyond that.

- REMS: Zinbryta was approved with a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) with Elements to Assure Safe Use, reflecting risks of hepatotoxicity (including a fatal case of autoimmune hepatitis observed in the trials) and other immune-mediated conditions; prescribers, pharmacies, and patients were required to enroll in a restricted-distribution program at launch.

- Market withdrawal: per the European Medicines Agency's referral record, EMA's safety review of Zinbryta began February 26, 2018; a suspension was recommended March 6, 2018 and adopted by the European Commission March 8, 2018; the marketing authorization was formally withdrawn March 27, 2018, after EMA concluded the medicine "poses a risk of serious and potentially fatal immune reactions affecting the brain, liver and other organs," present "from the start of treatment and for several months after stopping." Biogen and AbbVie voluntarily withdrew Zinbryta worldwide, including the US market, in March 2018. Source: [EMA — Zinbryta referral](https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/medicines/human/referrals/zinbryta). This followed an earlier (2017) EU restriction on use in patients with pre-existing liver disease after emerging hepatic-injury signals.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, BLA 761029, Reference ID 3904502, p.5]* — "A Special Protocol Assessment (SPA) Agreement letter was issued on June 7, 2010. The final protocol was dated April, 29 2013. The major changes in the final version of the protocol include the ranking of the secondary endpoint and the testing procedure for the efficacy analyses. A No Agreement letter to proposed modifications to the Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) was issued on April 28, 2014. In response to the non-agreement letter, the Sponsor modified the statistical analysis plan prior to database lock. The SAP was finalized on May 23, 2014 and was considered acceptable by the Agency."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, p.5]* — "The primary endpoint of ARR was analyzed using a negative binomial regression model adjusting for the baseline relapse rate (number of relapses in the 3 years prior to study entry divided by 3), history of prior IFN β use, baseline EDSS score (≤2.5 vs. >2.5), and age (≤35 vs. >35 years). The logarithmic transformation of the number of years in the study was included in the model as the 'offset' parameter. Only INEC-confirmed relapses until either the end of the treatment period, switch to alternative MS medication, or withdrawal from the study were included in the primary analysis."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, p.10]* — DECIDE result: "The ARR ratio (DAC HYP/ IFN β-1a) was 0.55, indicating that DAC HYP reduced the ARR by 45% compared with IFN β-1a (p<0.0001)." And: "Site 235 (11 subjects) in Brazil and Site 453 (40 subjects) in Italy were noted to be noncompliant with GCP. The results of the analysis that excluded Sites 453 and 235 were similar to those of the ITT population."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, p.20]* — SELECT result: "The adjusted annualized relapse rate in the placebo group was 0.458 compared to 0.211 in the DAC HYP 150 mg group and 0.230 in the DAC HYP 300 mg group. The annualized relapse rate ratio was 0.461 and 0.503 for DAC HYP 150 mg and DAC HYP 300 mg versus placebo, respectively, indicating that the annualized relapse rate was reduced by 54% in the DAC HYP 150 mg group (p<0.0001) and by 50% (p = 0.0002) in the DAC HYP 300 mg group, compared with placebo."

- **Reverse-engineered SAP** *[inferred]* — the REMS scope (hepatotoxicity + immune-mediated-condition monitoring, restricted distribution) is inferred from the approval letter and label rather than quoted verbatim here, since the exact REMS document text was not independently re-extracted for this entry.

### 22. Safinamide (Xadago) — NDA 207145

**Sponsor:** Newron Pharmaceuticals S.p.A. (US development/commercialization rights licensed to US WorldMeds, LLC)

**Indication approved:** Adjunctive treatment to levodopa/carbidopa in patients with Parkinson's disease experiencing "off" episodes

**Approval date:** March 21, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** SETTLE (Study 27919), NCT00627640 (confirmatory); Study 016, NCT01187966 (supportive dose-ranging; its extension, Study 018, is NCT01286935)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 3-arm fixed-dose (Study 016); randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 2-arm flexible-dose (SETTLE); add-on to a stable levodopa regimen
- *Endpoints:* change in total daily "on" time without troublesome dyskinesia (18-hour patient diary)
- *Primary analysis:* Mixed model for repeated measurements (MMRM) with Kenward-Roger approximation (Study 016) (proposed refinement — the existing Keyword_Taxonomy.md MMRM row specifies a sandwich variance estimator; this trial instead used an unstructured covariance matrix with Kenward-Roger degrees-of-freedom adjustment, a distinct MMRM variant); ANCOVA (SETTLE)
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence hierarchical testing of secondary endpoints controlling family-wise alpha=0.05 (SETTLE: off-time → UPDRS-III → UPDRS-II → CGI responder → PDQ-39)
- *Missing data/bias:* last observation carried forward (LOCF) for missing diary/rating-scale data at Week 24
- *Regulatory:* Reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan (sponsor's Study 016 clinical study report used analysis methods that deviated from the pre-specified protocol/SAP; FDA required corrected reanalysis via information requests)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 016: 24-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 3-arm, parallel-group trial of two fixed doses (50 mg/day, 100 mg/day) of safinamide as add-on therapy to a stable levodopa regimen in Parkinson's disease patients with motor fluctuations; 52 centers in India, Italy, and Romania; 660 patients planned 1:1:1, 669 randomized
- SETTLE (Study 27919): 24-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 2-arm, parallel-group, confirmatory trial of a flexible 50-100 mg/day safinamide dose vs. placebo, add-on to levodopa; 126 centers across Asia, Eastern Europe, Latin America, North America, and Western Europe; 484 patients planned 1:1, 549 randomized
- Primary endpoint (both trials): change from Baseline to Week 24 in total daily "on" time (18-hour diary), defined as "on" time without dyskinesia plus "on" time with non-troublesome dyskinesia
- Secondary endpoints: change in total daily "off" time; change in UPDRS Section III ("on" phase); change in UPDRS Section II ("on" phase); (SETTLE only, additionally) proportion of patients improved on Clinical Global Impression of Change (CGI), and change in PDQ-39
- Study 016 primary analysis: MMRM on the modified intent-to-treat (mITT) population — treatment, center, visit, and treatment-by-visit interaction as fixed effects, baseline as covariate, unstructured covariance matrix, Kenward-Roger approximation, "on-treatment" censoring (censored at rescue-medication intake or dropout)
- SETTLE primary analysis: ANCOVA on the mITT population — treatment and region effects, baseline "on" time as covariate, "on-treatment" approach with LOCF for missing data
- SETTLE secondary-endpoint multiplicity: fixed pre-specified hierarchical order (off-time → UPDRS-III → UPDRS-II → CGI responder [logistic regression] → PDQ-39) to control family-wise two-sided alpha=0.05
- Results: Study 016 — LS mean safinamide-placebo difference in "on" time +0.50h (50 mg, p=0.0356, 95% CI 0.03-0.96) and +0.53h (100 mg, p=0.0238, 95% CI 0.07-1.00); SETTLE — LS mean difference +0.99h (p<0.001, 95% CI 0.58-1.39)
- Missing data: 15-20% missing at Week 24 in Study 016 (18.4% placebo, 16.6% 50mg, 15.7% 100mg); 19.8% (placebo) vs. 14.4% (safinamide) in SETTLE; FDA reviewer characterized these rates as "not alarmingly unusual" for neurology trials and confirmed robustness via ANCOVA-LOCF and MMRM sensitivity analyses
- Notable regulatory finding: FDA's statistical reviewer found that Study 016's original clinical study report did not follow the statistical methods pre-specified in the protocol/SAP; FDA sent information requests for corrected analyses, which the sponsor provided (submitted July 24, 2015) and which became the analysis of record

### 23. Ocrelizumab (Ocrevus) — BLA 761053

**Sponsor:** Genentech, Inc. (F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd)

**Indication approved:** Relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (RMS) and primary progressive multiple sclerosis (PPMS) — the first FDA-approved treatment for PPMS

**Approval date:** March 28, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** OPERA I (WA21092), NCT01247324, and OPERA II (WA21093), NCT01412333 (identically-designed RMS trials, active-controlled); ORATORIO (WA25046), NCT01194570 (PPMS, placebo-controlled)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled (vs. interferon beta-1a) [OPERA I/II]; randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled [ORATORIO]
- *Endpoints:* annualized relapse rate (ARR) [OPERA I/II, primary]; 12-week confirmed disability progression (CDP) [ORATORIO, primary]; 24-week CDP [ORATORIO, secondary]
- *Primary analysis:* negative binomial regression with an offset for exposure time (per entry 1 above) [OPERA I/II]; stratified log-rank test (region × age) + stratified Cox model for the hazard ratio [ORATORIO]
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing of secondary endpoints [OPERA I/II, OPERA sequence stopped at MSFC/brain volume respectively; ORATORIO, testing hierarchy re-ranked mid-conduct by SAP amendment]
- *Missing data/bias:* FDA-conducted randomization-based imputation-uncertainty sensitivity analysis re-censoring imputed CDP events in repeated random subsets (a distinct FDA-originated bootstrap-style sensitivity method not yet in Keyword_Taxonomy.md § Missing data/censoring/bias handling)
- *Regulatory:* SAP amendment implementing sponsor-requested EMA Scientific Advice, replacing Van Elteren tests/LOCF with MMRM for continuous secondary endpoints, before database lock [ORATORIO]

**Trial design & endpoints**

- OPERA I (WA21092) and OPERA II (WA21093): identically-designed, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, parallel-group, active-controlled, 96-week trials in RMS; ocrelizumab 600 mg IV every 24 weeks (as two 300 mg infusions 14 days apart in the first cycle, then single 600 mg infusions) vs. interferon beta-1a 44 μg SC three times weekly
- ORATORIO (WA25046): randomized 2:1, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in PPMS, ages 18-55, EDSS 3.0-6.5; ocrelizumab 600 mg IV (two 300 mg infusions 14 days apart) every 24 weeks; N=732 (488 ocrelizumab / 244 placebo); primary database lock targeted at ≥253 confirmed disability progression (CDP) events, no later than 3 years after last patient randomized
- OPERA I/II primary endpoint: protocol-defined annualized relapse rate (ARR) at 96 weeks, analyzed via negative binomial regression adjusting for region (US vs. rest-of-world) and baseline EDSS (<4.0 vs. ≥4.0), with log-transformed exposure time as an offset
- ORATORIO primary endpoint: time to onset of 12-week confirmed disability progression (CDP) — an EDSS increase (≥1.0 point from baseline EDSS ≤5.5, or ≥0.5 point from baseline EDSS >5.5) sustained at a regularly scheduled visit 12 weeks later — compared between arms using a two-sided log-rank test stratified by region (US vs. ROW) and age (<45 vs. ≥45); Kaplan-Meier estimation for cumulative CDP proportions; a stratified Cox regression model (same strata) for the hazard ratio
- ORATORIO secondary endpoints included 24-week CDP and change in 25-foot timed walk; a pre-database-lock SAP amendment, implementing EMA Scientific Advice "to increase statistical rigor," replaced Van Elteren tests/LOCF with MMRM for continuous secondary endpoints, and re-ranked the testing hierarchy (moving T2-lesion-volume change down a rank, timed-walk change up)
- OPERA I/II sensitivity analyses on the primary endpoint: all protocol-defined relapses through 96 weeks regardless of treatment status; per-protocol population; safety population; additional-covariate adjustment (pre-study relapse count, baseline Gd-lesion status, prior MS treatment, age <40/≥40); a Poisson-model alternative; and two competing missing-data approaches (multiple imputation vs. an alternative rule) for patients who discontinued treatment early
- Results: OPERA I/II — ARR reduced 46.4% (WA21092) and 46.8% (WA21093) vs. interferon beta-1a (both p<0.0001; Cox-model hazard ratio 0.536 for both studies on time-to-first-confirmed-relapse); ORATORIO — 24% reduction in risk of 12-week CDP and 25% reduction in risk of 24-week CDP (hazard ratio 0.75, 95% CI 0.58-0.98, p=0.0365)
- FDA statistical addendum (Reference ID 4054630): of 256 observed CDP events in ORATORIO, 235 were directly confirmed and 21 were "imputed" as CDP because the patient had an initial progression event and withdrew before the 12-week confirmation visit; FDA estimated a 22.89% base rate of non-confirmation (76 of 332 patients with an initial-onset event were not ultimately confirmed) and ran a sensitivity analysis re-assigning 5 of the 21 imputed-event patients to censoring in randomly selected subsets, repeated 500 times, to test robustness of the primary log-rank p-value to the imputation rule

In order to account for different study treatment durations among patients, the exposure of each patient was to be taken into account by including log-transformed exposure time in the model as an 'offset' variable."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Reference ID 4004651]* — "ocrelizumab had a statistically significant reduction on the ARR by 46.4% for WA21092 and 46.8% in WA21093 compared with interferon beta-1a (p < 0.0001 for both studies)." And, on ORATORIO: "to a 25% reduction in the risk of 24-week CDP compared with placebo (hazard ratio 0.75 [95% CI: 0.58, 0.98], p = 0.0365)."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review Addendum, Reference ID 4054630]* — "In the PPMS study 25046, a total of 256 confirmed disability progression (CDP) events were observed. Among them, 235 events were actually confirmed and 21 events were imputed as CDP events due to patients who had an initial onset and then withdrew before possible confirmation could be made at a second visit 12 weeks after. ... Under the assumption that 22.89% of the 21 patients who had an initial onset event and then withdrew from the study would not likely to be confirmed, 5 patients ... were randomly selected from these 21 patients and their event status were modified from the CDP to censoring at the withdrawal. The same primary model of the log-rank test was then applied to the modified data to obtain the p-value from the treatment comparison. The procedure was repeated for 500 times."

### 24. Deutetrabenazine (Austedo) — NDA 208082

**Sponsor:** Teva Pharmaceuticals (originally developed by Auspex Pharmaceuticals, acquired by Teva in 2015)

**Indication approved:** Chorea associated with Huntington's disease (HD) — note: a *separate* NDA, 209885, reviewed by FDA's Division of Psychiatry Products, was approved August 30, 2017 for tardive dyskinesia (TD), based on the ARM-TD and AIM-TD trials; the two indications were only administratively merged into a single Austedo label later (per the FDA's June 6, 2018 approval letter for NDA 208082 supplement S-002). This entry covers NDA 208082/HD chorea only, matching the NDA number and approval date given for this census entry.

**Approval date:** April 3, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** FIRST-HD (Study SD-809-C-15), NCT01795859

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, dose-titration trial
- *Endpoints:* Total Maximal Chorea (TMC) score (sum of 7 items, Unified Huntington's Disease Rating Scale 1999 version), change from baseline to "maintenance" (mean of Week 9 + Week 12 scores)
- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA (treatment factor, baseline TMC as covariate)
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing of secondary endpoints (PGIC → CGIC → SF-36 Physical Functioning → Berg Balance Test), each at two-sided alpha=0.05
- *Missing data/bias:* last observation carried forward (LOCF) for two patients missing the Week 12 PGIC/CGIC assessment; MMRM used as a robustness check on the primary ANCOVA result

**Trial design & endpoints**

- FIRST-HD (SD-809-C-15): randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in patients with chorea associated with Huntington's disease; dose titrated from 6 mg/day upward (capped at 36 mg/day total if on a strong CYP2D6 inhibitor) to the level achieving adequate chorea control with acceptable tolerability; 123 screened, 90 randomized 1:1 (45 placebo / 45 deutetrabenazine)
- Primary endpoint: change from Baseline to "maintenance" (mean of the Week 9 and Week 12 TMC scores) in Total Maximal Chorea (TMC) score — the sum of seven items from the Unified Huntington's Disease Rating Scale (1999 version), each scored 0-4, for a total range of 0-28; Baseline TMC was the mean of Screening and Day-0 scores; a defined imputation rule filled ≤20%-missing component items from the most recent non-missing value, otherwise the visit score was treated as missing
- Secondary endpoints (tested in a fixed pre-specified sequence at two-sided alpha=0.05 each): treatment success on Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC, "Much Improved"/"Very Much Improved" at Week 12) via Pearson's chi-square; treatment success on Clinical Global Impression of Change (CGIC) via Pearson's chi-square; change in SF-36 Physical Functioning score via ANCOVA; change in Berg Balance Test (BBT) score via ANCOVA
- Primary analysis: ANCOVA on the modified intent-to-treat (mITT) population (all randomized, treated patients with ≥1 post-baseline TMC assessment), treatment as a factor, baseline TMC as covariate
- Results: LS mean deutetrabenazine-placebo difference in TMC score −2.49 points (95% CI −3.69 to −1.29, p<0.0001), confirmed robust by an MMRM sensitivity analysis and low dropout (2.2% deutetrabenazine, 4.4% placebo); secondary endpoints significant in sequence for PGIC (p=0.0020), CGIC (p=0.0022), and SF-36 Physical Functioning (p=0.0308)
- FDA's independent reviewer reran ANCOVA analyses on PGIC/CGIC/BBT without LOCF imputation and on SF-36 carrying forward last-available observations; conclusions were unchanged

### 25. Valbenazine (Ingrezza) — NDA 209241

**Sponsor:** Neurocrine Biosciences, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Tardive dyskinesia in adults

**Approval date:** April 11, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** KINECT 3 (Study NBI-98854-1304), NCT02274558 (Phase 3, primary basis for approval); Study NBI-98854-1202 (Phase 2, supportive/replication)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, two-fixed-dose trial (Study 1304); randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-titration trial (Study 1202, non-pivotal per FDA)
- *Endpoints:* Abnormal Involuntary Movement Scale (AIMS) dyskinesia total score (items 1-7), change from baseline to Week 6, centrally rated from blinded video
- *Primary analysis:* Mixed model for repeated measurements (MMRM)
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence hierarchical testing (80 mg AIMS → 80 mg CGI-TD → 40 mg AIMS → 40 mg CGI-TD) (the taxonomy's existing "Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing" row applies, but flagged here as a case where the FDA reviewer documents that the Division recommended a different order pre-specification and the sponsor declined to change it)
- *Regulatory:* Reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan (Division recommended testing both doses' primary endpoints before the key secondary; sponsor tested the 80 mg primary + key secondary first); non-pivotal-trial protocol amendment (central-rater switch, primary-endpoint redefinition) implemented without full statistical review because the trial was deemed non-pivotal at the time (Study 1202)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 1304 (KINECT 3): 6-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter trial of two fixed doses of valbenazine (40 mg, 80 mg) vs. placebo in adults with tardive dyskinesia; N=234 randomized (78 placebo / 76 40mg / 80 80mg)
- Study 1202: 6-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with dose titration (25→50→75 mg every 2 weeks by response/tolerability, mean Week-6 dose 64.4 mg/day); N=102 randomized (51 placebo / 51 valbenazine); an earlier Phase 2 trial (Study 1201) with site-based AIMS raters had failed to reach statistical significance, prompting an expert panel to recommend central video-based AIMS raters and revised AIMS score descriptors, implemented in Studies 1202 and 1304
- Primary endpoint (both trials): AIMS dyskinesia total score (items 1-7) change from baseline to Week 6, based on centrally rated (Study 1304) or, per a mid-study protocol amendment, centrally rated in lieu of site-rated (Study 1202) blinded video assessments
- Primary analysis: MMRM with baseline AIMS as covariate, treatment (placebo/40mg/80mg), disease category, and visit as fixed effects, subject as random effect, plus treatment-by-visit and baseline-by-visit interactions
- Multiplicity: fixed testing sequence — 80 mg AIMS, then 80 mg Clinical Global Impression of Change-TD (CGI-TD, key secondary), then 40 mg AIMS, then 40 mg CGI-TD; FDA's reviewer noted the Division had recommended, at the IND stage, testing the primary endpoint for both doses before the key secondary endpoint, and that "the sponsor had decided not to modify their approach"
- Results: 80 mg dose met the primary endpoint (LS mean difference −3.1 vs. placebo, 95% CI −4.2 to −2.0, p<0.0001) and was approved; 40 mg showed a similar numeric effect (−1.8 vs. placebo, nominal p=0.0021) but could not be formally declared statistically significant because the 80 mg CGI-TD key secondary (p=0.056) — which sat earlier in the fixed testing sequence — was not itself significant, precluding formal testing of any 40 mg endpoint; Study 1202 (dose-titration, ~64 mg/day mean) showed a −2.4 point AIMS difference vs. placebo (95% CI −3.7 to −1.1), treated by FDA as replication support for the 80 mg finding
- Study 1202's non-pivotal status meant a protocol amendment switching the primary analysis population/method (to central raters and an ANCOVA-based analysis effectively restricted to completers) did not receive a dedicated statistical review at the time; FDA's own tipping-point-style exploratory analysis of the 12 patients excluded from the "ITT" set concluded their omission did not materially change the efficacy conclusion
- Sensitivity analyses: Tipping Point and Jump-to-Reference multiple-imputation analyses for missing data around the MMRM primary model

- FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID 4064319) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209241Orig1s000StatR.pdf

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 209241, Reference ID 4064319, p.5]* — "Patients treated with the 80 mg dose of Valbenazine had an average of -3.1 points greater reduction on the primary efficacy endpoint (i.e., AIMS total score change from baseline to week 6) compared to placebo (95% CI: -4.2, -2.0; p < 0.0001). The 40 mg Valbenazine group also had favorable numeric results (average improvement on the AIMS of -1.8 points over placebo). However, the results for the 40 mg group were not statistically significant because the 80 mg dose was not statistically significant (p=0.056) on the key secondary endpoint Clinical Global Impression of Change-TD, which was placed before any 40 mg dose tests in the fixed testing sequence."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, p.5]* — "This reviewer did not find any major statistical issues for Study 1304, besides the unfortunate order of endpoints in the fixed testing sequence which the Division had recommended revising during the IND stage. The sponsor had decided not to modify their approach."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, p.6]* — on Study 1304's testing-sequence history: "The Division recommended testing the primary endpoint for both high and low dose first, before testing the key secondary endpoint. The sponsor did not implement that recommendation and proceeded with testing the primary and key secondary endpoint first for the high dose, before testing any endpoint for the lower dose."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Table, p.7]* — "Fixed sequence: 80 mg AIMS, 80 mg CGI-TD, 40 mg AIMS, 40 mg CGI-TD."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, p.7]* — "Not per se a statistical issue, but the pre-specified fixed testing procedure in Study 1304 precludes the formal statistical testing of the primary efficacy endpoint for the 40 mg dose (nominal p-value of 0.0021)."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, p.6, on Study 1202]* — "The protocol was amended to include scoring of AIMS items 1-7 by a central, blinded video rater, to make the AIMS dyskinesia total score (items 1-7) change from baseline derived from the blinded, central video rater's scores the primary endpoint of the study and to make the AIMS dyskinesia total score as scored by the site's certified, independent AIMS rater a secondary efficacy endpoint. As previously discussed with the sponsor, this study is not a pivotal trial; therefore, these changes are deemed acceptable."
