### 26. Edaravone (Radicava) — NDA 209176

**Sponsor:** Mitsubishi Tanabe Pharma Development America, Inc. (Mitsubishi Tanabe Pharma Corporation)

**Indication approved:** Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS)

**Approval date:** May 5, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** Study 19 (MCI186-19), NCT01492686 (confirmatory, positive) — designed to test a post-hoc subgroup identified in the earlier, overall-negative Study 16 (MCI186-16), NCT00330681. Both trials were conducted exclusively in Japan, in Japanese subjects, entirely outside a US IND.

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, entirely Japan-conducted, in a population restricted to a post-hoc subgroup identified in a prior overall-negative trial
- *Endpoints:* ALS Functional Rating Scale-Revised (ALSFRS-R) score, change from baseline (Cycle 1) to end of Cycle 6 (24 weeks)
- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA-type group comparison using the dynamic-allocation (minimization) factors as covariates, with last observation carried forward (LOCF) for missing Cycle 6 data
- *Missing data/bias:* last observation carried forward (LOCF) imputation for missing end-of-Cycle-6 ALSFRS-R values
- *Regulatory:* confirmatory trial restricted to a post-hoc-derived subgroup of a failed prior trial (a second trial enrolling exclusively the post-hoc subgroup identified from a first trial's overall-negative result, distinct from existing single-trial post-hoc-subgroup rows in Keyword_Taxonomy.md); FDA statistical reviewer recommends against viewing the submission as sufficient for approval on the two-adequate-and-well-controlled-trials standard, contingent on risk-benefit/orphan-drug considerations, and the drug was approved anyway (distinct from the existing "Reviewer-vs-reviewer statistical dispute" row, since this is a reviewer-vs-final-decision divergence, not a dispute between reviewers); reviewer-identified baseline covariate imbalance (Riluzole use) within the post-hoc subgroup, tested via Breslow-Day statistic

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 16 (MCI186-16): randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in ALS, Japan; N=199 (99 placebo / 100 edaravone), 24-week double-blind period; primary endpoint ALSFRS-R change from baseline to end of Cycle 6; FAILED its pre-specified primary endpoint in the full analysis set (LS mean difference 0.7, placebo −6.4 vs. edaravone −5.7, p=0.4108)
- Following the negative overall result, the sponsor identified — post-hoc, not pre-specified — an "Efficacy Expected Subpopulation" (EESP): every individual ALSFRS-R item ≥2 at baseline (functionality retained in most ADL domains) and %FVC ≥80% at baseline (normal respiratory function); a narrower "definite or probable/EESP/2y" subgroup added a Definite/Probable El Escorial ALS diagnosis and enrollment within 2 years of symptom onset. The EESP subgroup (n=104: 54 edaravone/50 placebo) showed a nominally positive difference (2.2±1.0, p=0.036); the narrower definite/probable/EESP/2y subgroup (n=72: 40/32) showed a larger nominal effect (3.0±1.3, p=0.027) — both explicitly labeled post-hoc by the FDA reviewer
- Study 19 (MCI186-19): designed to prospectively confirm the post-hoc subgroup signal by enrolling only patients meeting the "definite or probable/EESP/2y" criteria; randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 24-week double-blind period, Japan; N=137 (69 edaravone / 68 placebo); randomization via dynamic allocation (minimization) stratified by pre-observation-period ALSFRS-R decline category, El Escorial diagnostic category, and age (≥65 vs. <65)
- Sample size: 128 patients (64/arm) planned, based on an assumed 3.0-point placebo-edaravone difference with SD 6, 80% power, two-sided alpha=0.05, derived from the Study 16 subgroup data
- Study 19 primary analysis: difference between Cycle-1 baseline and end-of-Cycle-6 (or discontinuation) ALSFRS-R score, analyzed using the dynamic-allocation factors as covariates (an ANCOVA-type model), with LOCF for missing end-of-Cycle-6 data; per the final analysis plan (dated June 6, 2014), no multiplicity adjustment was applied to secondary endpoints because all were designated exploratory
- Result: Study 19 was positive — placebo −7.5 vs. edaravone −5.0, LS mean difference 2.49±0.76 (95% CI 0.99-3.98), p=0.0013; most non-ALSFRS-R secondary endpoints did not reach nominal significance
- FDA's statistical reviewer flagged a baseline covariate imbalance within Study 16's post-hoc subgroup: 21.9% of placebo-arm subjects were not on Riluzole vs. 7.5% of edaravone-arm subjects (Breslow-Day test for homogeneity of odds ratios across the subgroup/complement split, p=0.0347) — raised as a possible confound of the "signal" that drove Study 19's design
- The reviewer's stated conclusion: because Study 16 failed its pre-specified primary hypothesis and Study 19 was designed on Study 16's post-hoc subgroup, the submission does not constitute the traditional standard of "two studies ... positive on their originally prespecified primary hypotheses," and approval would require weighing risk-benefit/orphan-drug considerations rather than resting on the statistical evidence alone

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2017/209176Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/209176lbl.pdf

- FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID 4044694) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209176Orig1s000StatR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (Study 16) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00330681 (completed; no protocol/SAP documents posted)

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (Study 19) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01492686 (completed; no protocol/SAP documents posted)

- Pivotal publication: Writing Group; Edaravone (MCI-186) ALS 19 Study Group. "Safety and efficacy of edaravone in well defined patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial." Lancet Neurol. 2017;16(7):505-512. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1474-4422(17)30115-1>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28522181/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Safety%20and%20efficacy%20of%20edaravone%20in%20well%20defined%20patients%20with%20amyotrophic%20lateral%20sclerosis)

**Other resources**

- Mitsubishi Tanabe's general participation in cross-industry IPD-sharing platforms was not confirmed; trial-specific Study 16/19 dataset availability was not individually confirmed here.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was referenced in the reviewed FDA documents for this NDA; not independently confirmed beyond that.

- Both pivotal trials enrolled exclusively Japanese subjects, entirely outside a US IND; the FDA reviewer explicitly notes "there is no data in American subjects," a generalizability point worth flagging alongside the post-hoc-subgroup design issue.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 209176, Reference ID 4044694, p.4]* — "The submission's first study, 16, failed on it's primary endpoint and the second study was designed on the basis of a post-hoc subgroup result in the first study. One could always data dredge a failed study for a 'positive' subgroup and then showing that subgroup is positive in a new study does not erase the fact that the first study failed. It requires circular logic to consider the second study to validate the first so that the submission might approach the efficacy standard of two positive studies. ... Note, also that the studies in this submission were done exclusively in Japanese subjects, so there is no data in American subjects."

- *[verbatim, p.5]* — "In the post-hoc subgroup 21.9% of Placebo were not treated with Riluzole as compared to just 7.5% in Edaravone. ... an exploratory statistical test of this, a Breslow Day test for Homogeneity of Odds ratios, rejects homogeneity between these two complementary subgroups, p=0.0347. ... Study 19 does not seem very persuasive on it's own since many of the secondary analyses were not nominally significant ... Some alternative subjective interpretation (e.g., risk benefit considerations or orphan drug status) would seem necessary if one was to view this submission as sufficient for approval since it does not contain two studies that were each positive on the prespecified primary hypothesis."

- *[verbatim, p.10]* — "Efficacy Expected Subpopulation (EESP) Definition: Subjects who met the following criteria • Each individual item of the ALSFRS-R of 2 and better at Baseline ... • A %FVC of 80% and greater at Baseline ... Definite or probable/EESP/2y Definition: In addition to meeting EESP criteria, • Definite or Probable ALS diagnosis based on the El Escorial and revised Airlie House diagnostic criteria at preregistration ... • Within 2 years of initial ALS symptom onset at preregistration."

- *[verbatim, p.22]* — "A total of 128 patients (64 patients per group) were planned as the primary analysis set for the primary efficacy endpoints. ... the difference (adjusted value) in ALSFRS-R between the placebo group and the edaravone group may be 3.0, and the standard deviation 6. The sample size calculated based on the significance level of 5% (two-sided) and the power of 80% was 128 patients in total." And on the primary analysis: "The difference between 'at baseline in Cycle 1' and 'the end of Cycle 6 or at discontinuation' was to be analyzed by using the factors in the dynamic allocation as covariates to perform group comparisons. For patients whose data 'at the end of Cycle 6' are missing, data was to be complemented by the last observation carried forward (LOCF)."

- *[verbatim, p.35]* — Study 19 result: "the mean was 2.49±0.76 (0.99 to 3.98), and the difference between the groups was significant (P=0.0013)."

### 27. Erenumab-aooe (Aimovig) — BLA 761077

**Sponsor:** Amgen Inc. (co-developed with Novartis)

**Indication approved:** Preventive treatment of migraine in adults — the first FDA-approved CGRP-receptor-targeting antibody for migraine prevention

**Approval date:** May 17, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** STRIVE (Study 20120296), NCT02456740 (episodic migraine, 24-week); ARISE (Study 20120297), NCT02483585 (episodic migraine, 12-week); supportive Phase 2 chronic-migraine study (Study 20120295)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter trials (24-week for STRIVE, 12-week for ARISE), two dose arms (70 mg, 140 mg monthly) plus placebo
- *Endpoints:* change in monthly migraine days (MMD) from baseline to the last 3 months (STRIVE) or last month (ARISE) of the double-blind treatment phase
- *Primary analysis:* Mixed model for repeated measurements (MMRM) (generalized linear mixed-effects model; treatment, baseline value, stratification factors, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction; no imputation for missing data)
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing combined with hierarchical gate-keeping and the Hochberg procedure, splitting two-sided alpha=0.05 study-wise as 0.04 (70 mg) / 0.01 (140 mg)
- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation (NRI) for the ≥50%-responder secondary endpoint, analyzed via stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test

**Trial design & endpoints**

- STRIVE (Study 20120296): Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial in episodic migraine (4 to <15 migraine days/month, <15 headache days/month), 121 centers in North America, Europe, and Turkey; ~852 patients planned 1:1:1 to placebo, erenumab 70 mg, or 140 mg monthly SC injection for a 24-week double-blind phase; randomization stratified by region and prophylactic-medication status (prior only/current/neither)
- ARISE (Study 20120297): Phase 3, similarly designed episodic-migraine trial with a 12-week double-blind phase, randomized 1:1 to placebo or erenumab 70 mg, 69 centers across North America, Europe, and Russia
- Primary endpoint: change in monthly migraine days (MMD) from baseline to the last 3 months (STRIVE, months 4-6) or the 12-week endpoint (ARISE) of the double-blind phase
- Primary analysis: MMRM (generalized linear mixed-effects model) with treatment group, baseline value, stratification factors, scheduled visit, and treatment-by-visit interaction as terms, no missing-data imputation; the 50%-responder secondary endpoint used non-responder imputation plus a stratified CMH test
- Multiplicity: a pre-specified sequential procedure combining hierarchical gate-keeping with the Hochberg method controlled the two-sided study-wise Type I error at 0.05 across the two doses and the primary/secondary endpoint families; the primary endpoint was tested at 0.04 (70 mg) and 0.01 (140 mg), and only if significant for a given dose were that dose's secondary endpoints tested via Hochberg at the same per-dose alpha
- Results: STRIVE — LSM MMD difference vs. placebo −1.40 days (95% CI −1.88 to −0.92, 70 mg) and −1.85 days (95% CI −2.33 to −1.37, 140 mg), both p<0.001; ≥50%-responder rates 26.6% (placebo), 43.3% (70 mg, common OR 2.13), 50.0% (140 mg, common OR 2.81); ARISE — LSM MMD difference −0.94 days (95% CI −1.23 to −0.64, 70 mg) and −1.86 days (95% CI −2.60 to −1.13, chronic-migraine supportive study)

### 28. Cannabidiol (Epidiolex) — NDA 210365

**Sponsor:** GW Research Ltd / GW Pharmaceuticals plc

**Indication approved:** Seizures associated with Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (LGS) or Dravet syndrome (DS), in patients 2 years of age and older — the first FDA-approved drug derived from the marijuana plant

**Approval date:** June 25, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** GWPCARE1/Study 1332B (Dravet syndrome), NCT02091375; GWPCARE3/Study 1414 (LGS, 3-arm dose-ranging), NCT02224560; GWPCARE4/Study 1423 (LGS, 2-arm confirmatory), NCT02224690

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, add-on to existing anti-epileptic drug regimen, parallel-group, multicenter trials (14-week double-blind phase in all three)
- *Endpoints:* percent change from baseline in convulsive seizure frequency (Dravet, GWPCARE1) or drop-seizure frequency (LGS, GWPCARE3/GWPCARE4), 28-day rate
- *Primary analysis:* Wilcoxon rank-sum test with Hodges-Lehmann estimator (already in Keyword_Taxonomy.md § Primary analysis method, previously seen in Telotristat ethyl/TELESTAR)
- *Multiplicity:* hierarchical gate-keeping procedure, 8-step pre-specified testing sequence across two doses × (primary + 3 key secondaries) [GWPCARE3]
- *Regulatory:* Reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan (GWPCARE4/Study 1423: FDA's Cross Discipline Team Leader Review states the US SAP was internally inconsistent about whether secondary-endpoint hierarchical testing applied in the US vs. EU, with the sponsor's post-hoc clarification "difficult to verify"); FDA Advisory Committee meeting held; DEA scheduling review conducted alongside NDA review given Schedule I status of the cannabis-derived active ingredient at time of review

**Trial design & endpoints**

- GWPCARE1 (Study 1332B, Part B): 14-week, randomized 1:1, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of CBD 20 mg/kg/day vs. placebo, add-on therapy, in Dravet syndrome; N=120, stratified by age group; centers in US/UK/France/Poland
- GWPCARE3 (Study 1414): 14-week, randomized 1:1:1, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 3-arm trial (CBD 20 mg/kg/day, 10 mg/kg/day, placebo), add-on therapy, in Lennox-Gastaut syndrome; N=225, stratified by age group; centers in US/UK/France/Spain
- GWPCARE4 (Study 1423): 14-week, randomized 1:1, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 2-arm trial (CBD 20 mg/kg/day vs. placebo), add-on therapy, in Lennox-Gastaut syndrome; N=171; centers in US/Netherlands/Poland
- Primary endpoint (all three): percent change from baseline in seizure frequency (28-day rate) — total convulsive seizures (GWPCARE1/Dravet) or drop seizures (GWPCARE3/GWPCARE4/LGS) — analyzed on the intention-to-treat population (randomized, ≥1 dose, ≥1 post-baseline efficacy assessment) via Wilcoxon rank-sum test, with the median between-group difference and approximate 95% CI from the Hodges-Lehmann estimator
- GWPCARE3 multiplicity: an 8-step hierarchical gate-keeping sequence controlled the two-sided study-wise alpha=0.05 — (1) primary endpoint 20mg vs. placebo, (2) primary endpoint 10mg vs. placebo, (3)-(5) three key secondary endpoints for 20mg vs. placebo, (6)-(8) the same three key secondaries for 10mg vs. placebo
- Results: GWPCARE1 — median seizure-frequency reduction −38.9% (CBD) vs. −13.3% (placebo), estimated median difference −22.8 (95% CI −41.1 to −5.4), p=0.0123; GWPCARE3 — 20 mg/kg/day estimated median difference −21.6 (95% CI −34.8 to −6.7), p=0.0047; 10 mg/kg/day −19.2 (95% CI −31.2 to −7.7), p=0.0016; GWPCARE4 — estimated median difference −17.2 (95% CI −30.3 to −4.1), p=0.0135
- Notable regulatory finding: for GWPCARE4, FDA's Cross Discipline Team Leader Review states the sponsor's US SAP was internally inconsistent about whether secondary endpoints were pre-specified for hierarchical testing; the sponsor claimed a sentence limiting hierarchical testing to the EU SAP was a drafting error, which the reviewer states was "difficult to verify"
- Advisory Committee: the Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee met April 19, 2018 and voted 13-0 that the benefit-risk profile was favorable for both the LGS and Dravet syndrome indications

### 29. Stiripentol (Diacomit) — NDA 206709

**Sponsor:** Biocodex SA (originally developed by Laboratoires Biocodex, France)

**Indication approved:** Seizures associated with Dravet syndrome, in conjunction with clobazam, in patients 2 years of age and older

**Approval date:** August 20, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** STICLO France (1996-1998), a French investigator-initiated trial; STICLO Italy (1999-2000), an Italian investigator-initiated trial (supportive, not independently stand-alone-pivotal per FDA's own reanalysis — see below). Neither trial has an NCT registration; both predate ClinicalTrials.gov's 2000 launch and US registration requirements. NDA 206709 was reviewed jointly with a companion NDA 207223 (a different strength/formulation); all Drugs@FDA filenames for this submission use a comma-joined dual-application-number pattern.

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, add-on trial to a stable optimized regimen (valproate + clobazam); two independently-conducted, non-US, investigator-initiated trials serving as the entire pivotal evidence base (no US-conducted, sponsor-run pivotal trial) (distinct from the existing "retrospective/non-prospective diagnostic evidentiary basis" and "literature-based approval" rows, since these were genuine prospective RCTs, just decades-old, non-US, and not sponsor-initiated)
- *Endpoints:* binary "treatment success/failure" (responder status) by Week 12/Month 2, defined by absence of any of four pre-specified non-responder criteria
- *Primary analysis:* Chi-square test (STICLO France); Fisher's exact test (STICLO Italy, small sample size)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential interim analysis after 20 patients/arm in each trial's original protocol, with a reduced nominal significance threshold (alpha'=2.5%) for early stopping
- *Regulatory:* FDA post hoc recalculation of a group-sequential (O'Brien-Fleming) alpha-spending boundary to downgrade a trial's stand-alone pivotal status (FDA applied O'Brien-Fleming spending-function logic retrospectively to conclude STICLO Italy's observed p-value did not clear the boundary implied by its own interim-analysis design, and therefore could not stand alone as a second pivotal trial); sponsor unable to produce or date the original trial SAPs for either investigator-initiated trial, decades after conduct

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Both trials: multicenter (14 centers in France; 6 in Italy), 4-week baseline period on a stable, optimized antiepileptic regimen (valproate sodium + clobazam), followed by an 8-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group treatment period; stiripentol 50 mg/kg/day added on, with no dose titration
- STICLO France: N=42 (22 stiripentol / 20 placebo); STICLO Italy: N=23 (12 stiripentol / 11 placebo)
- Primary endpoint (both trials): binary "treatment success" (responder) vs. "failure" by Week 12 (Month 2 of double-blind treatment), per Protocol Amendment No. 2; a patient was classified a non-responder if meeting any of several pre-specified criteria (e.g., <50% reduction in generalized tonic-clonic/clonic seizure frequency vs. baseline, discontinuation for status epilepticus, or a defined early-seizure-increase pattern) — this was the amended, qualitative version of the endpoint; an earlier protocol version had specified a quantitative (continuous seizure-frequency-reduction) primary criterion
- Primary analysis: proportion of responders compared between arms using a Chi-square test (STICLO France) or Fisher's exact test (STICLO Italy, given the small sample size)
- Both original protocols specified a single planned interim analysis after enrollment of 20 patients per arm, without unblinding, using a reduced significance threshold alpha'=2.5% for early stopping; if not stopped early, enrollment would continue to a sponsor-recalculated target (capped at 100 patients/arm total, 18-month maximum accrual)
- Results: STICLO France — 71.4% (stiripentol) vs. 5.0% (placebo) responders, p<0.00002; STICLO Italy — 66.7% vs. 9.1%, p=0.009
- Notable FDA statistical finding: because both protocols specified a group-sequential interim look, FDA's reviewer independently recalculated the O'Brien-Fleming nominal significance boundary implied by each trial's actual information fraction at analysis — 0.00305 at 40% information for STICLO France (cleared by its p<0.0001) vs. a much stricter <0.00001 at 20% information for STICLO Italy (NOT cleared by its p=0.009) — concluding STICLO Italy could not be considered a stand-alone pivotal trial in its own right
- Notable regulatory/data-provenance finding: both trials being decades-old, non-US, investigator-initiated studies, FDA could not confirm when either trial's SAP was finalized or whether it preceded database lock; when asked (November 28, 2016), the sponsor responded (December 14, 2016) that STICLO France was an investigator-initiated trial and that the SAP had remained with the original academic investigator's department and "cannot be found currently," though the sponsor maintained the primary analyses followed the finalized protocol; the reviewer also found and reconciled several dataset-vs.-Final-Study-Report discrepancies in individual seizure-frequency values for both trials
- FDA's overall conclusion: efficacy "rests mainly on" STICLO France, with STICLO Italy providing supportive (not independently sufficient) evidence

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2018/206709Orig1s000,207223Orig1s000Ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/206709s000,207223s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID 4180289) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/206709Orig1s000,207223Orig1s000StatR.pdf

- FDA Medical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/206709Orig1s000,207223Orig1s000MedR.pdf

- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/206709Orig1s000,207223Orig1s000SumR.pdf

- Pivotal publication (STICLO France): Chiron C, Marchand MC, Tran A, Rey E, d'Athis P, Vincent J, Dulac O, Pons G; STICLO study group. "Stiripentol in severe myoclonic epilepsy in infancy: a randomised placebo-controlled syndrome-dedicated trial." Lancet. 2000;356(9242):1638-1642. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(00)03157-3>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11089822/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Stiripentol%20in%20severe%20myoclonic%20epilepsy%20in%20infancy%20STICLO)

- STICLO Italy: no standalone peer-reviewed publication of this trial's results was found via PubMed E-utilities (searched by author, journal, and title keywords); FDA's Statistical Review cites only the unpublished sponsor Final Study Report. The closest verifiable published reference — a pooled individual-patient-data meta-analysis of both STICLO trials, with Guerrini as a co-author, plausibly the source of the "Guerrini 2002" citation sometimes referenced for this trial — is: Kassaï B, Chiron C, Augier S, Cucherat M, Rey E, Gueyffier F, Guerrini R, Vincent J, Dulac O, Pons G. **Other resources**

- Biocodex's general participation in cross-industry IPD-sharing platforms was not confirmed; given the trials' age and investigator-initiated origin, individual-patient dataset availability beyond the Kassaï et al. 2008 pooled meta-analysis is unclear.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was referenced in the reviewed FDA documents for this NDA; not independently confirmed beyond that.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 206709/207223, Reference ID 4180289, p.7]* — "Study STICLO France and Study STICLO Italy are non-US studies. The sponsor never submitted the study protocols for review before the NDA submission."

- *[verbatim, p.7-8]* — "This reviewer calculated the nominal significance level using the Obrien-Fleming spending function at 40% information for Study France and at 20% information for Study Italy. For Study France, the nominal significance level is 0.00305, which is greater than the p-value of <.0001 for the Fisher's exact test. However, for Study Italy, the nominal significance level is <.00001, which is smaller than the p-value of 0.01 for the Fisher's exact test. Therefore, Study Italy may not be considered as a stand-alone pivotal trial."

- *[verbatim, p.8]* — "Only one version of statistical analysis plan (SAP) was provided without signatures and dates. It was not clear when the SAP was finalized and whether it was finalized prior to the study database lock. ... We requested the sponsor to clarify when the two SAPs were finalized on 11/28/2016. The sponsor stated in their response dated 12/14/2016 that the STICLO France was an Investigator-initiated Trial and the SAPs remained at Prof. Pon's department and cannot be found currently. However, they emphasized that the primary efficacy analyses were conducted according to the final protocols which were finalized prior to un-blinding the data."

- *[verbatim, p.5]* — results: "the responder (i.e., treatment success) rates were 5.0% in the placebo group and 71.4% in the STP group (p <0.00002 versus placebo)" [STICLO France]; "the responder (i.e., treatment success) rates were 9.1% in the placebo group and 66.7% in the STP group (p = 0.009 versus placebo)" [STICLO Italy].

- *[verbatim, p.28]* — conclusion: "This application for a labeling claim on Stiripentol for [adjunctive] treatment of [refractory generalized tonic-clonic] seizures associated with Dravet syndrome rests mainly on the multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial: STICLO France and STICLO Italy provides supportive evidence."

### 30. Fremanezumab-vfrm (Ajovy) — BLA 761089

**Sponsor:** Teva Pharmaceuticals

**Indication approved:** Preventive treatment of migraine in adults (episodic and chronic migraine)

**Approval date:** September 14, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** Study 050/HALO EM (episodic migraine), NCT02629861; Study 049/HALO CM (chronic migraine), NCT02621931

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, 12-week trials; two dosing regimens each (quarterly single-dose vs. monthly, with a loading dose in the chronic-migraine trial's monthly arm)
- *Endpoints:* change in monthly average number of migraine days (EM) or headache days of at least moderate severity (CM), from baseline over the 12-week double-blind period
- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA with normality-contingent fallback to a non-parametric test (Wilcoxon rank-sum) (already in Keyword_Taxonomy.md § Primary analysis method, previously seen in Riociguat/CHEST-1/PATENT-1 — add fremanezumab to its "Seen in" list)
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing of primary/key-secondary endpoints across the two dosing regimens, overall two-sided alpha=0.05
- *Missing data/bias:* MMRM used as a sensitivity analysis alongside the ANCOVA/Wilcoxon primary analysis

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 050 (HALO EM): 12-week (after a 4-week baseline), randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in episodic migraine; adults 18-70 with ≥4 to <15 migraine days/month; randomized 1:1:1 to placebo, fremanezumab 675 mg quarterly (single dose), or fremanezumab 225 mg monthly; N=290/288/287
- Study 049 (HALO CM): 12-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in chronic migraine; adults 18-70 with ≥15 headache days/month and ≥8 migraine days/month; randomized 1:1:1 to placebo, fremanezumab 675 mg quarterly, or fremanezumab 675 mg loading dose + 225 mg monthly; N=371/375/375; concomitant use of one stable prophylactic medication was permitted in both trials (20-22% of patients)
- Primary endpoint: mean change from baseline in monthly average number of migraine days (Study 050) or monthly average number of headache days of at least moderate severity (Study 049), over the 12-week double-blind period, analyzed on the Full Analysis Set (all randomized, dosed ≥1 time, ≥10 days of post-baseline efficacy assessment)
- Primary analysis (both trials): pre-specified as ANCOVA, with a normality-contingent fallback — "because of significant deviation from the normal distribution assumption, the non-parametric analysis of Wilcoxon rank-sum test was assumed to be the primary analysis based on the SAP"; MMRM served only as a sensitivity analysis
- Multiplicity: overall two-sided alpha=0.05 apportioned across the two dosing regimens for the primary and key secondary endpoints via a pre-specified fixed-sequence (hierarchical) testing procedure
- Results, Study 050 (ANCOVA): LS mean change −2.2 (placebo) / −3.4 (675 mg quarterly) / −3.7 (225 mg monthly) days; LS mean differences −1.3 (95% CI −1.79 to −0.72) and −1.5 (95% CI −2.01 to −0.93) days vs. placebo, both p<0.0001; Wilcoxon rank-sum (primary analysis of record) p<0.0001 both doses; MMRM sensitivity at Month 3: differences −1.0 (p=0.0013) and −1.2 (p=0.0002)
- Results, Study 049 (ANCOVA): LS mean change −2.5 (placebo) / −4.3 (675 mg quarterly) / −4.6 (675/225 mg monthly) days; LS mean differences −1.8 (95% CI −2.46 to −1.15) and −2.1 (95% CI −2.76 to −1.45) days vs. placebo, both p<0.0001; Wilcoxon rank-sum p<0.0001 both doses; MMRM sensitivity at Month 3: differences −1.4 (p=0.0007) and −1.9 (p<0.0001)
- No REMS was required; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held for this BLA

### 31. Galcanezumab-gnlm (Emgality) — BLA 761063

**Sponsor:** Eli Lilly and Company

**Indication approved:** Preventive treatment of migraine in adults

**Approval date:** September 27, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** EVOLVE-1 (I5Q-MC-CGAG, NCT02614183) and EVOLVE-2 (CGAH, NCT02614196) — episodic migraine; REGAIN (CGAI, NCT02614261) — chronic migraine; all three jointly reviewed as pivotal

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trials with two dose arms (120 mg/month, 240 mg/month) vs. placebo, separate episodic-migraine (EVOLVE-1/2) and chronic-migraine (REGAIN) populations pooled into one regulatory review

- *Endpoints:* overall mean change from baseline in the number of monthly migraine headache days during the 6-month double-blind treatment phase (primary)

- *Primary analysis:* REML-based mixed model repeated measures (MMRM), unstructured covariance, Kenward-Roger denominator degrees of freedom

- *Multiplicity:* overall superchain multiple testing procedure (Kordzakhia & Dmitrienko 2013) with alpha propagation/recycling across primary and key secondary endpoints across the three trials

- *Missing data/bias:* pre-specified covariance-structure fallback sequence for MMRM non-convergence (Heterogeneous Toeplitz → Heterogeneous AR(1) → Toeplitz → AR(1)), with a Diggle-Kenward sandwich-estimator fallback

- *Regulatory:* FDA Summary Review states a REMS was determined not necessary for this product

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Three randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group Phase 3 trials: EVOLVE-1 and EVOLVE-2 enrolled episodic-migraine patients (approximately 825 patients per trial, randomized 2:1:1 to placebo, galcanezumab 120 mg/month, or 240 mg/month); REGAIN enrolled chronic-migraine patients under the same randomization structure

- Primary endpoint: overall mean change from baseline in the number of monthly migraine headache days during the 6-month double-blind treatment phase, with sample sizes powered at 95% for the episodic trials

- Primary analysis: REML-based MMRM with an unstructured covariance matrix and Kenward-Roger degrees-of-freedom approximation; a pre-specified covariance-structure fallback order (Heterogeneous Toeplitz → Heterogeneous AR(1) → Toeplitz → AR(1)) applied if the primary model failed to converge, with a Diggle-Kenward sandwich estimator as a further fallback

- Multiplicity: per the FDA Statistical & Clinical Efficacy Review, the primary and key secondary objectives across all three trials were tested using "an overall superchain procedure multiple testing approach (sponsor reference: Kordzakhia and Dmitrienko 2013), providing control of the familywise type 1 error rate at a 2-sided 0.05 alpha level with alpha propagation (or alpha recycling) techniques" — the underlying testing-order flowchart (Figure 5.2 in the sponsor's SAP) is presented as an image and not text-extractable

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, EVOLVE-1/EVOLVE-2 shared SAP Version 4, p.9]* — "The primary efficacy objective is to test the hypothesis that at least 1 dose of LY2951742 (120 or 240 mg/month) is superior to placebo... at an overall one-sided 0.025 significance level, as measured by the overall mean change from baseline in the number of monthly migraine headache days during the 6-month double-blind treatment phase."

*[verbatim, SAP, p.5.2]* — sample size: "approximately 825 patients... randomized... with a randomization ratio of 2:1:1... 95% power," stratified within region.

*[verbatim, SAP, p.37-38]* — primary analysis: "REML-based mixed models repeated measures (MMRM) technique," unstructured covariance, Kenward-Roger denominator degrees of freedom, with the covariance-structure fallback order described above.

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical & Clinical Efficacy Review, BLA 761063 MedR]* — "For episodic migraine studies (CGAG and CGAH) and chronic migraine study CGAI, the primary and key secondary objectives were tested using an overall superchain procedure multiple testing approach (sponsor reference: Kordzakhia and Dmitrienko 2013), providing control of the familywise type 1 error rate at a 2-sided 0.05 alpha level with alpha propagation (or alpha recycling) techniques."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review]* — "A REMS is not necessary for this product."

### 32. Amifampridine (Firdapse) — NDA 208078

**Sponsor:** Catalyst Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome (LEMS) in adults

**Approval date:** November 28, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** LMS-002 (NCT01377922) and LMS-003 (NCT02970162), both randomized-withdrawal trials in LEMS patients already stabilized on amifampridine

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized-withdrawal (randomized-discontinuation) design in patients pre-stabilized on open-label active drug, not a de novo placebo-controlled trial in treatment-naive patients

- *Endpoints:* co-primary endpoints Quantitative Myasthenia Gravis (QMG) score and Subject Global Impression (SGI), each analyzed as change from baseline

- *Primary analysis:* mixed effect model repeated measures (MMRM) / fixed-effects linear model on change from baseline, with treatment-comparison p-values determined by a permutation/randomization test rather than an asymptotic p-value ("Permutation/randomization test for empirical p-value of a fixed-effects or MMRM treatment-comparison model")

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing — key secondary endpoint (CGI-I) tested only if both co-primary endpoints (QMG and SGI) were statistically significant

- *Missing data/bias:* no missing-value imputation used for LMS-003 (analysis based on observed data only)

- *Regulatory:* Special Protocol Assessment (SPA) agreement for LMS-003 (10/25/2016), later modified (6/6/2017) to add SAP detail; no REMS required

**Trial design & endpoints**

- LMS-002 (NCT01377922, n=38) and LMS-003 (NCT02970162, n=26, FDA-designated "confirmatory" trial): both randomized-withdrawal designs in LEMS patients previously stabilized on open-label amifampridine, randomized 1:1 to continue amifampridine or switch to placebo for a short double-blind period (4 days for LMS-003), stratified by baseline dose (LMS-003: >60 vs. <60 mg/day)

- Co-primary endpoints: change from baseline in Quantitative Myasthenia Gravis (QMG) score and in Subject Global Impression (SGI); key secondary: Clinical Global Impression-Improvement (CGI-I)

- Sample size (LMS-003 SAP): at least 24 subjects for ≥80% power on QMG, at least 26 subjects for ≥80% power on SGI; a total of 26 subjects was judged to provide ≥80% power for each co-primary endpoint. LMS-002 sample size (per Sanders et al.): 36 subjects randomized to provide 80% power to detect a difference of 2.44 units in mean QMG change

- Primary analysis: a fixed-effects linear model (LMS-003 SAP) / MMRM (LMS-002, per FDA review) fit to change from baseline, with treatment and baseline score as covariates; treatment-comparison p-values for LMS-002 were determined using a permutation test (empirical p-value = proportion of randomized-treatment-assignment replicates with a smaller p-value than the observed dataset); both QMG and SGI comparisons required significance at the two-sided alpha=0.05 level. LMS-003's SAP additionally pre-specified a randomization-test sensitivity analysis as "an alternative to a full permutation" evaluating the same fixed-effects model under permuted treatment assignments

- Multiplicity: step-down method — CGI-I (first secondary) tested only if both co-primary endpoints were statistically significant, so "no adjustment for multiplicity was needed" per the FDA review

- Missing data: LMS-003 SAP specifies "No missing value imputation will be used in this analysis. All analyses will be based on the observed data."

- GCP: FDA's Office of Scientific Investigations inspected sites for both trials; data were judged acceptable for both, though monitoring practices were noted as "problematic" for LMS-002 without an assessed impact on the safety/efficacy conclusions

Both the QMG and the SGI treatment comparisons need to be significant using a two-sided test at the alpha=0.05 level."

### 33. Brexanolone (Zulresso) — NDA 211371

**Sponsor:** Sage Therapeutics, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of postpartum depression (PPD) in adults, administered as a continuous 60-hour intravenous infusion

**Approval date:** March 19, 2019

**Pivotal trial:** 547-PPD-202B (NCT02942004, severe PPD) and 547-PPD-202C (NCT02942017, moderate PPD), the two Phase 3 trials FDA treated as pivotal; supportive Phase 2 trial 547-PPD-202A (NCT02614547, severe PPD)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trials of a single 60-hour continuous IV infusion, separate moderate- and severe-PPD populations analyzed as distinct trials rather than pooled

- *Endpoints:* change from baseline in 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAM-D) total score at Hour 60 (primary), assessed at the end of the infusion

- *Primary analysis:* mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) with Kenward-Roger degrees-of-freedom approximation ("Kenward-Roger degrees-of-freedom approximation for MMRM," distinct from the already-catalogued MMRM-with-sandwich-variance approach)

- *Multiplicity:* graphical multiple-comparison procedure (202B) controlling type I error jointly across two dose arms

- *Missing data/bias:* pre-specified Missing Not at Random (MNAR) sensitivity analysis (202B/202C); sequential covariance-structure fallback for MMRM convergence failure (unstructured → Toeplitz/AR(1) → compound symmetry), with no result reported if no structure converged

- *Regulatory:* REMS-restricted product — ZULRESSO REMS Program requires administration only in a certified healthcare setting with continuous monitoring; FDA Advisory Committee held (Nov 2, 2018, joint Psychopharmacologic Drugs / Drug Safety and Risk Management Advisory Committee)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Three multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled trials under the "547-PPD-202" program, each testing a single continuous 60-hour IV infusion of brexanolone: 202A (Phase 2, severe PPD, 90 µg/kg/h vs. placebo, 1:1 randomization); 202B (Phase 3, severe PPD, randomized 2:2:1:1 to 60 µg/kg/h, 90 µg/kg/h, or one of two pooled placebo arms, stratified by baseline antidepressant use); 202C (Phase 3, moderate PPD, 90 µg/kg/h vs. placebo, 1:1, stratified by baseline antidepressant use from January 2017 onward)

- Primary endpoint (all three trials): change from baseline in HAM-D (17-item) total score at Hour 60, the end of the 60-hour infusion

- Primary analysis: MMRM including center, treatment, baseline HAM-D total score, assessment time point, and time-point-by-treatment interaction as fixed effects, unstructured covariance, Kenward-Roger denominator degrees of freedom; a pre-specified fallback covariance-structure sequence (Toeplitz → AR(1) → compound symmetry) was used if the unstructured model failed to converge, and no result was reported for a comparison if no structure converged

- Multiplicity (202B): a graphical multiplicity procedure controlled the overall type I error rate across the two dose arms (60 µg/kg/h and 90 µg/kg/h) tested against placebo

- Missing data: no imputation was planned in the 202A SAP ("There was no planned method for handling missing data"); 202B/202C additionally pre-specified a Missing Not at Random (MNAR)-based sensitivity analysis

- Results: 202B Hour-60 placebo-subtracted LS-mean difference, 60 µg/kg/h: -5.5 (95% CI -8.8, -2.2), p=0.0013; 90 µg/kg/h: -3.7 (95% CI -6.9, -0.5), p=0.0252 (both significant after multiplicity adjustment). 202C Hour-60 placebo-subtracted difference: -2.5 (95% CI -4.5, -0.5), p=0.0160 (significant); the Day-30 secondary comparison was not significant (p=0.6710)

- FDA reviewer note on 202A: "The Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) was not submitted during the IND stage. Therefore, FDA did not review the SAP" — flagged as a documented review-process gap for the Phase 2 supportive trial

*[verbatim, p.93-94, Study 202A SAP]* — "The change from baseline in HAM-D total score at all post-baseline visits was analyzed using a mixed effects model for repeated measures (MMRM), the model included center, treatment, baseline HAM-D total score, assessment time point, and time point-by-treatment as explanatory variables... A sensitivity analyses based on Missing Not at Random (MNAR) to handle missing data was pre-specified... To control the type I error rate for conducting multiple comparisons, the approach in Figure 15 was utilized" (graphical multiplicity procedure across two doses × two endpoints).

*[verbatim, p.115-116, Study 202C design/SAP]* — 1:1 randomization, moderate PPD, stratified (from Jan 2017) by baseline antidepressant use; same MMRM structure, unstructured → Toeplitz → AR(1) → compound symmetry fallback sequence "until convergence was achieved. If convergence was not achieved, no results were reported."

*[verbatim, p.120, Table 53, Study 202C results]* — Hour 60 placebo-subtracted difference -2.5 (95% CI -4.5, -0.5), p=0.0160 (significant); Day 30 secondary not significant (p=0.6710).

*[verbatim, p.161]* — "Evidence of brexanolone's effectiveness as a 60-hour infusion in treating PPD was assessed in three controlled studies: 547-PPD-202A, 202B, and 202C... All three studies showed a statistically significant reduction in depressive symptoms..."

*[verbatim, REMS Document, p.1-2]* — "Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Document — ZULRESSO (brexanolone) REMS Program." Goal: "to mitigate the risk of serious harm resulting from excessive sedation and sudden loss of consciousness during the ZULRESSO infusion by: i. Ensuring that ZULRESSO is administered only to patients in a medically supervised setting that provides monitoring while ZULRESSO is administered. ii. Ensuring pharmacies and healthcare settings that dispense ZULRESSO are certified. iii. Ensuring that each patient is informed of the adverse events... iv. Enrollment of all patients in a registry..." Certified healthcare settings must "Be able to monitor patients continuously for the duration of the infusion" and "Have the following onsite: continuous pulse oximetry, fall precaution protocol, intravenous programmable infusion pumps with alarms..."

### 34. Solriamfetol (Sunosi) — NDA 211230

**Sponsor:** Jazz Pharmaceuticals (developed by Aerial BioPharma/Jazz; NDA held by Jazz Pharmaceuticals Ireland Ltd.)

**Indication approved:** To improve wakefulness in adults with excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) associated with narcolepsy or obstructive sleep apnea (OSA)

**Approval date:** March 20, 2019

**Pivotal trial:** 14-002 / "TONES 2" (NCT02348593, narcolepsy) and 14-003 / "TONES 3" (NCT02348606, OSA); NDA 211230 was filed and approved as two parallel original applications (Orig1 = narcolepsy, Orig2 = OSA) reviewed jointly

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, multi-dose-arm parallel-group trials (4 arms for narcolepsy, 5 arms for OSA); combined single NDA number covering two original-approval applications for two distinct indications reviewed jointly ("Combined-application (Orig1 + Orig2) NDA/BLA reviewed and approved jointly for two indications")

- *Endpoints:* co-primary endpoints — change from baseline in Maintenance of Wakefulness Test (MWT) and Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) at Week 12; key secondary: Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIc), percent improved

- *Primary analysis:* mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) with covariance-structure fallback (unstructured → AR(1) → compound symmetric)

- *Multiplicity:* gatekeeping testing procedure across two co-primary endpoints and multiple dose arms, controlling overall type I error at 0.05 ("Gatekeeping testing procedure across co-primary endpoints and multiple doses")

- *Missing data/bias:* last observation carried forward (LOCF) for the key secondary endpoint; sensitivity analyses using single imputation (LOCF, mean imputation) and multiple imputation via Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) and regression methods ("Multiple imputation via MCMC as a sensitivity analysis for a continuous co-primary endpoint")

- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented deviation — FDA assessed the primary endpoint strictly at Week 12, differing from the sponsor's last-post-baseline-assessment approach

**Trial design & endpoints**

- 14-002/TONES 2: 12-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, 4-arm (placebo, 75/150/300 mg) parallel-group trial in narcolepsy. 14-003/TONES 3: same structure, 5-arm (placebo, 37.5/75/150/300 mg), in OSA. Supporting trials: ADX-N05-202 (Phase 2 narcolepsy, "TONES 1"), 14-004 ("TONES 4," OSA randomized-withdrawal), 14-005 ("TONES 5," long-term randomized-withdrawal)

- Co-primary endpoints in both pivotal trials: change from baseline (CFB) in Maintenance of Wakefulness Test (MWT) at Week 12, and CFB in Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) at Week 12. Key secondary: Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIc), percent improved, at Week 12

- Primary analysis: MMRM with treatment, time, treatment-by-time interaction, and randomization stratification factor as fixed effects and baseline value as a covariate; unstructured covariance matrix, with a fallback to AR(1) and then compound symmetric structure if the model failed to converge. The key secondary endpoint (PGIc) was analyzed using chi-squared tests with LOCF for missing data

- Multiplicity: a gatekeeping testing procedure controlled the overall type I error rate at 0.05 jointly across the two co-primary endpoints and the multiple dose arms

- Sensitivity analyses: ANCOVA models with single-imputation approaches (LOCF and mean imputation) and multiple-imputation approaches based on the Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method and a regression method

- FDA-documented deviation: "The Sponsor's primary endpoints were assessed at the last post-baseline assessment. The varying endpoint visit is different from FDA agreed primary endpoints, which were assessed at Week 12... This reviewer performed analyses on the primary endpoints assessed at Week 12."

- Results (Week 12, MMRM, 14-002): CFB in MWT, 150 mg vs. placebo: 7.7 min (95% CI 4.0, 11.3), p<0.0001; 300 mg: 10.1 (6.4, 13.9), p<0.0001. CFB in ESS: 150 mg: -3.8 (-5.6, -2.0), p<0.0001; 300 mg: -4.7 (-6.6, -2.9), p<0.0001. Results (14-003): CFB in MWT, 150 mg: 10.7 (8.1, 13.4), p<0.0001; 300 mg: 12.8 (10.0, 15.6), p<0.0001. CFB in ESS: 150 mg: -4.5 (-5.7, -3.2), p<0.0001; 300 mg: -4.7 (-5.9, -3.4), p<0.0001

- No explicit sample-size/power justification text for 14-002/14-003 was located in the FDA Statistical Review — noted here as a documented gap rather than inferred

### 35. Siponimod (Mayzent) — NDA 209884

**Sponsor:** Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation

**Indication approved:** Treatment of relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS), including secondary progressive MS (SPMS) with active disease, in adults

**Approval date:** March 26, 2019

**Pivotal trial:** EXPAND (protocol A2304, NCT01665144), secondary progressive MS; supportive Phase 2 dose-ranging trial A2201 (relapsing-remitting MS)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, event-driven Phase 3 trial (2:1 randomization), stratified by country; supportive Phase 2 trial used an adaptive MCP-mod dose-response design

- *Endpoints:* time to 3-month confirmed disability progression (CDP) on the Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) (primary); key secondaries include confirmed worsening in Timed 25-Foot Walk (T25W) and T2 lesion volume

- *Primary analysis:* Cox proportional-hazards model with treatment, country, baseline EDSS, and SPMS subgroup (with/without superimposed relapses in the prior 2 years) as covariates

- *Interim/alpha-spending:* O'Brien-Fleming alpha-spending function following a futility-only interim analysis by an independent DMC, adjusted significance level 0.0434 at final analysis

- *Missing data/bias:* bootstrap-simulation sensitivity analysis quantifying whether an observed effect-size reduction after a blinding-integrity breach was attributable to chance (proposed refinement of the existing "Blinding-integrity sensitivity analysis" term, adding a formal bootstrap null-distribution test)

- *Regulatory:* reviewer-documented sample-size/duration extension post-interim without independent statistical re-review; reviewer-documented blinding-integrity breach (unauthorized database access); reviewer-documented concern about the supportive trial's (A2201) unpreserved type I error rate after an unblinded interim re-estimation; label requires CYP2C9 genotyping, contraindicated in *3/*3 genotype, dose-reduced for *1/*3 and *2/*3 genotypes; no REMS

**Trial design & endpoints**

- EXPAND: multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial in 1651 patients with secondary progressive MS (1105 siponimod 2 mg once daily, 546 placebo), randomized 2:1, stratified by country; event-driven, planned to terminate once 374 confirmed 3-month CDP events were observed

- Primary endpoint: time to 3-month confirmed disability progression based on EDSS, defined as an increase of 1 point in patients with baseline EDSS 3.0-5.0, or 0.5 point in patients with baseline EDSS 5.5-6.5, confirmed at a visit approximately 3 months (76 days) later

- Primary analysis: Cox proportional-hazards model with treatment, country, baseline EDSS, and SPMS subgroup (with/without superimposed relapses in the 2 years prior to screening) as covariates. Key secondary endpoints (confirmed T25W worsening; T2 lesion volume) were analyzed via a Cox model and an MMRM, respectively

- Interim monitoring: a single futility-only interim analysis was reviewed by an independent DMC (continued 14-Jul-2015, at >60% of planned events); the final significance level was adjusted per an O'Brien-Fleming alpha-spending function to 0.0434

- Results: siponimod N=1099, 288/1096 (26.3%) events; placebo N=546, 173/545 (31.7%) events; HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.65-0.95), p=0.0134 — a statistically significant reduction in risk of 3-month CDP

- FDA-flagged confound: the reviewer noted "there appeared to be a nominally highly significant effect of siponimod on the annualized relapse rate, suggesting that the effect on disability progression could be partially due to siponimod's effect on relapses" rather than a disability-specific effect independent of relapse activity

- FDA-documented reviewer concerns: (1) the trial's target event count/duration was extended post-interim without the change itself receiving independent statistical re-review at the time; (2) a blinding-integrity breach was identified — "34 users of the Main database and 3 EDSS raters had inappropriate access to the First Dose database, which potentially compromised the treatment blinding for over 100 subjects" — addressed via a bootstrap-simulation sensitivity analysis (removing potentially unblinded subjects gave a 17% risk reduction vs. 21% in the full analysis set); (3) FDA's inspection found that central-adjudication SPMS entry-criteria attestations "were not properly conducted," raising a population-definition concern; (4) the supportive Phase 2 trial (A2201) used an MCP-mod primary-analysis framework for its dose-response claim but "did not account for the unblinded interim analysis that was performed to re-estimate sample size and choose the two additional doses for Stage 2... the overall type I error rate was not preserved," and the same statistician executed both the unblinded interim analysis and the primary efficacy programming

- Regulatory: siponimod's label requires CYP2C9 genotyping prior to dosing; contraindicated in CYP2C9 *3/*3 genotype; maintenance dose reduced for *1/*3 and *2/*3 genotypes

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2019/209884Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2019/209884s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/209884Orig1s000StatR.pdf (note: this PDF's text layer is obfuscated by a constant character-code shift rather than being plain text; all excerpts below were recovered via a deterministic decode of that shift, not standard `pdftotext` extraction, and are labeled accordingly)

- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01665144 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)

- Pivotal publication: Kappos L, Bar-Or A, Cree BAC, et al.; EXPAND Clinical Investigators. "Siponimod versus placebo in secondary progressive multiple sclerosis (EXPAND): a double-blind, randomised, phase 3 study." *Lancet.* 2018;391(10127):1263-1273 (Erratum PMID 30496099). [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(18)30475-6>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29576505/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Siponimod%20versus%20placebo%20secondary%20progressive%20multiple%20sclerosis%20EXPAND)

**Other resources**

- Novartis participates in general cross-industry IPD-sharing platforms (e.g., Vivli); trial-specific EXPAND availability was not individually confirmed here.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was referenced in the Statistical Review.

- Sourcing note for future entries: this NDA's Statistical Review PDF was found to use a constant-shift character-code obfuscation of its text layer (every glyph, including digits, shifted by the same offset), distinct from the previously documented Novo Nordisk inter-word-spacing-stripping failure mode — a straightforward deterministic decode recovers full body text and was used for all quotations below.

The primary efficacy analysis demonstrated a statistically significant reduction of the risk of 3-month confirmed disability progression (CDP) in the siponimod group compared to the placebo group (HR 0.79, p=0.0134)." And: "there appeared to be a nominally highly significant effect of siponimod on the annualized relapse rate, suggesting that the effect on disability progression could be partially due to siponimod's effect on relapses."

*[verbatim (decoded)]* — design: "Study A2304 was a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled Phase 3 study in 1651 patients (1105 siponimod 2mg once daily, 546 placebo)... randomized in a 2:1 ratio... stratified by country," planned to "terminate when the required number of 374 3-month CDP would be observed."

*[verbatim (decoded)]* — primary endpoint: "time to 3-month CDP based on EDSS... Disability progression was defined as an increase of 1 point in patients with baseline EDSS 3.0-5.0, or 0.5 point in patients with baseline EDSS 5.5-6.5."

*[verbatim (decoded)]* — primary analysis: "Cox proportional hazards model with treatment, country, baseline EDSS and SPMS group (with/without superimposed relapses in the 2 years prior to screening) as covariates."

*[verbatim (decoded)]* — alpha-spending: "significance level... adjusted according to the O'Brien-Fleming alpha spending function, which was calculated to be 0.0434," following a futility-only interim analysis (DMC continued 14-Jul-2015, >60% of events).

### 36. Pitolisant (Wakix) — NDA 211150

**Sponsor:** Bioprojet Pharma (US rights held by Harmony Biosciences)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) in adult patients with narcolepsy (2019 original approval; a cataplexy indication was added later via a 2020 efficacy supplement, outside this entry's scope)

**Approval date:** August 14, 2019

**Pivotal trial:** HARMONY I (P07-03, NCT01067222) and HARMONY I-bis (P09-15, NCT01638403), co-pivotal for the EDS indication; HARMONY CTP (P11-05, NCT01800045) was supportive/secondary evidence only

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-comparator-controlled, parallel-group trials (pitolisant vs. modafinil vs. placebo)

- *Endpoints:* change from baseline to Week 8 in Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) total score (primary, HARMONY I/I-bis); weekly rate of cataplexy (WRC) during a 4-week stable-dose period (primary, HARMONY CTP, supportive only)

- *Primary analysis:* mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM); FDA also conducted an independent Hodges-Lehmann/permutation-based re-analysis of the primary endpoint

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) testing — superiority of pitolisant vs. placebo tested first, followed by non-inferiority of pitolisant vs. modafinil at a fixed non-inferiority margin (NI=2 points on ESS)

- *Missing data/bias:* last-two-values mean carried forward for missing post-baseline ESS values; for patients with no post-baseline values, the final value was assimilated to baseline; SAP-timing verification dispute over pre-specification of a post-hoc center-clustering method ("SAP-timing verification dispute (regulator vs. EMA) over pre-specification of a post-hoc analytic choice")

- *Regulatory:* FDA explicitly documented an absence of prospectively planned multiplicity control for secondary endpoints across the program; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- HARMONY I: Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo- and comparator-controlled, parallel-group study; pitolisant 10-40 mg/day (n=31), modafinil 100-400 mg/day (n=33), placebo (n=30). HARMONY I-bis: same 3-arm structure (pitolisant 5/10/20 mg vs. modafinil 100/200/400 mg vs. placebo), randomized 2:2:1

- Primary endpoint (both trials): change from baseline to Week 8 in ESS total score. Testing structure: a step-down approach tested superiority of pitolisant over placebo first, then non-inferiority of pitolisant vs. modafinil at a fixed non-inferiority margin of 2 points on ESS

- HARMONY I result: LS-mean ESS at Week 8, pitolisant 12.39 vs. placebo 15.48 (Applicant analysis, difference -3.10, p=0.022); FDA's independent MMRM re-analysis gave a larger, more significant difference (-3.68 ± 1.16, 95% CI -5.96 to -1.39, p=0.002), and a Hodges-Lehmann/permutation-test re-analysis by the FDA biometrics reviewer was consistent (median shift 4, 95% CI 0.5-7, p=0.02; permutation p=0.01)

- HARMONY I-bis result and documented SAP-timing dispute: mean ESS decrease with pitolisant vs. placebo was -2.19 (95% CI -4.17, -0.22; p=0.03) using a pre-specified re-allocation of small study centers into clusters; the EMA's public assessment report had stated this center-pooling was not pre-planned, but FDA's review verified that "the SAP which was issued a month (February 13, 2013) before the database lock (March 13, 2013) included an Appendix... to display the random re-allocation of small centers into clusters." Without the re-allocation, the same comparison did not reach significance (-1.94, 95% CI -4.05 to 0.07, p=0.065)

- HARMONY CTP (supportive only): randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, N=106 randomized; primary endpoint was weekly rate of cataplexy (WRC) during a 4-week stable-dose period, analyzed via a non-linear mixed-effects model; secondary endpoints included WRC during the last 2 weeks, WRC>15 responder rate, ESS, and MWT. The FDA review's numeric WRC results tables were not text-extractable from the source PDF (image-only pages) — this is a documented gap in this entry, not an inferred result

- Missing data (HARMONY I): "Estimation for missing values were made by carrying forward the arithmetic mean of the last 2 values. For patients who did not have any post-baseline values, the final value was assimilated with baseline."

- FDA-documented multiplicity gap: "There was no prospectively planned correction for multiplicity to control the overall type I error rate for these secondary endpoints" (regarding a cataplexy subgroup analysis within HARMONY I), and separately, "The statistical analysis plan did not include a plan to prospectively assess secondary endpoints with control of the Type-I error rate"

- Regulatory scope note: the FDA biostatistics reviewer's efficacy conclusion supported only the EDS indication ("efficacy results from HARMONY I and HARMONY IBIS showed improved daytime sleepiness which supports the indication of EDS"); no equivalent recommendation was given for cataplexy at this 2019 approval — a cataplexy indication was added via a separate 2020 supplemental application, outside this entry's approval-date scope

### 37. Istradefylline (Nourianz) — NDA 022075

**Sponsor:** Kyowa Kirin, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Adjunctive treatment to levodopa/carbidopa in adult patients with Parkinson's disease experiencing "OFF" episodes

**Approval date:** August 27, 2019

**Pivotal trial:** Study 6002-009 (NCT00955526, Phase 3, Japan) and Study 6002-0608 (NCT00455507, Phase 2b, Japan); a third trial, Study 6002-014 (NCT01968031, Phase 3, North America/Europe), was submitted in the same resubmission but failed its primary endpoint and was excluded from FDA's efficacy review

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trials; NDA resubmitted after an 11-year gap following an original 2007 submission and a 2008 Not Approvable letter, built on two Japan-conducted trials plus one new (failed) US/EU trial

- *Endpoints:* total hours per day spent in the "OFF" state (primary), assessed at the last available post-baseline value

- *Primary analysis:* analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) with treatment group, study center, and baseline value as covariates

- *Multiplicity:* Williams' test procedure for ordered dose-response comparison against placebo — highest dose (40 mg/day) tested against placebo first at one-sided alpha=0.025, stepping down to the lower dose (20 mg/day) only if significant

- *Missing data/bias:* last observation carried forward (LOCF) for the primary analysis; pre-specified worst-case sensitivity analysis substituting missing 30-minute diary periods with "OFF"; MMRM sensitivity analysis with compound-symmetry covariance

- *Regulatory:* prior Not Approvable action (2008) on the original NDA submission; reviewer-vs-reviewer dispute documented within the review, with a senior FDA reviewer overriding a dissenting clinical reviewer's Complete Response recommendation; a failed confirmatory-type trial (Study 014) excluded from the efficacy review rather than pooled

**Trial design & endpoints**

- NDA 22075 was originally submitted March 29, 2007, based on earlier US/EU studies; FDA issued a Not Approvable action letter February 25, 2008, citing weak/inconsistent effectiveness evidence. The applicant did not resubmit until February 27, 2019 (Class 2 resubmission), based on two new Japan-conducted trials (6002-009, 6002-0608) plus a new US/EU trial (6002-014) that failed its primary endpoint

- Study 6002-009 (Japan, N=373) and Study 6002-0608 (Japan, N=363): randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter trials of istradefylline 20 mg or 40 mg once daily for 12 weeks as adjunctive Parkinson's disease therapy

- Primary endpoint: total hours (of awake time) per day spent in the OFF state; primary assessment time was the time of the last available post-baseline value

- Primary analysis: ANCOVA with terms for treatment group and study center, and baseline value as a covariate. The two dose groups were compared to placebo using the Williams' test procedure, assuming a monotonic dose-response relationship: the 40 mg/day vs. placebo comparison was tested first at one-sided alpha=0.025; if significant, the 20 mg/day vs. placebo comparison was tested at the same one-sided level

- Missing data: the primary analysis used observed-case data (invalid diary entries treated as missing) with LOCF for a missing full-visit value; a pre-specified worst-case sensitivity analysis substituted missing 30-minute diary periods with OFF; an MMRM sensitivity analysis with compound-symmetry covariance was also pre-specified

- Results: Study 0608 LS-mean difference from placebo, 20 mg/day: -0.65 (p=0.028); 40 mg/day: -0.92 (p=0.002). Study 009: 20 mg/day: -0.76 (p=0.006); 40 mg/day: -0.74 (p=0.008). Study 014 (excluded from the efficacy conclusion): 20 mg/day: -0.32 (p=0.156); 40 mg/day: -0.27 (p=0.234) — "In this document, the results of the failed study 014 were not reviewed"

- Williams' test result: "compared with placebo, 20 mg and 40 mg of KW-6002 significantly (one-sided p=0.003 for both groups) reduced the total hours per day spent in the OFF state"

- FDA internal reviewer dispute (Summary Review): a dissenting clinical reviewer recommended a Complete Response action based on three studies (006, 018, 014) not showing statistical significance on the primary endpoint; the Division's senior reviewers explicitly disagreed and recommended approval based on the totality of the 009/0608 results

- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/022075Orig1s000StatR.pdf

**Other resources**

The applicant submitted a Resubmission to NDA 22075 on February 27, 2019 with new data from two trials 6002-0608 and 6002-009... conducted in Japan... The resubmission also included a new study 6002-014... conducted in the U.S.... which failed to reach statistical significance for the primary endpoint... In this document, the results of the failed study 014 were not reviewed."

*[verbatim, p.6, Study 009 design]* — "randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter... 20 mg or 40 mg once daily for 12 weeks... primary variable was the total hours (of awake time) per day spent in the OFF state... primary assessment time was the time of the last available post-baseline value."

If this test was significant, then the comparison of istradefylline 20 mg/day versus placebo was also performed at the one-sided 0.025 level."

The results of Williams' test showed that, compared with placebo, 20 mg and 40 mg of KW-6002 significantly (one-sided p=0.003 for both groups) reduced the total hours per day spent in the OFF state."

### 38. Fluorodopa F 18 (unbranded, "Fluorodopa F 18 Injection") — NDA 200655

**Sponsor:** The Feinstein Institutes for Medical Research (Northwell Health) — an academic medical research institute, not a pharmaceutical company

**Indication approved:** A PET imaging agent for visualization of dopaminergic nerve terminals in the striatum, as an adjunct to differentiate Parkinsonian syndromes from essential tremor and other conditions not associated with reduced striatal dopaminergic activity

**Approval date:** October 10, 2019

**Pivotal trial:** No registered NCT trial exists. The approval basis is a prospective, single-center, single-arm diagnostic-accuracy study conducted under an expanded-access IND ("Study #18"), the third and final study in a decade-long, three-cycle submission history

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient), prospective, single-center, academic-sponsor, validated against a delayed blinded-clinician reference standard rather than a paired imaging or pathology reference test ("Prospective single-center academic diagnostic-accuracy study validated against a delayed clinical-follow-up reference standard")

- *Endpoints:* positive percent agreement (PPA) and negative percent agreement (NPA) between blinded PET-scan readers and a final clinical diagnosis (Parkinsonian syndrome vs. non-Parkinsonian syndrome) made by a movement-disorder specialist blinded to the PET result, established after ≥6 months of follow-up

- *Primary analysis:* exact binomial confidence intervals (Clopper-Pearson-type) around each of three independent readers' PPA/NPA point estimates

- *Missing data/bias:* performance-measure analysis without an independent reference standard — a clinical (not histopathological) reference diagnosis, explicitly noted by FDA as less definitive than a true-standard comparison

- *Regulatory:* retrospective/non-prospective diagnostic evidentiary basis used and rejected in two earlier submission cycles (2009 refuse-to-file on literature alone; 2012 resubmission on a retrospective 185-patient chart review, met with a 2013 Complete Response Letter; a 2015 prospective but unblinded/incomplete-follow-up study also drew a 2016 Complete Response Letter) before the 2019 approval on a corrected prospective, blinded design; two independent Special Government Employee (SGE) consultations (members of the Medical Imaging Drug Advisory Committee, MIDAC) used in lieu of a public advisory committee meeting

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Submission history: original NDA submitted October 30, 2009, based on peer-reviewed literature alone — refused to file. Resubmitted October 23, 2012, based on a retrospective chart review of 185 patients at the Applicant's own institution — met with a Complete Response Letter October 22, 2013, judged inadequate, with FDA recommending a prospective study. Resubmitted December 15, 2015, based on a prospective Study #17 (45 patients, expanded-access IND, single center) — met with a Complete Response Letter September 15, 2016, citing incomplete 1-year follow-up in many patients and unblinding of reference-standard clinicians to the PET result before their diagnosis. Resubmitted April 10, 2019, based on prospective Study #18 (68 patients enrolled, 56 completed ≥6-month follow-up, same single center, blinded reference standard) — approved

- Study #18 design: prospective, single-center, single-arm diagnostic-accuracy study under an expanded-access IND. 56 patients with suspected Parkinsonian syndrome (PS) completed ≥6 months of clinical follow-up. Reference standard: final clinical diagnosis (PS vs. non-PS) made by a movement-disorder specialist blinded to the 18F-FDOPA PET result. Three independent readers, blinded to clinical information, each interpreted scans as positive or negative

- Primary endpoints: positive percent agreement (PPA) and negative percent agreement (NPA) between each blinded reader's PET interpretation and the blinded clinical reference diagnosis — the FDA review explicitly avoids the terms "sensitivity" and "specificity" because "a clinical reference standard is not as definitive as a histopathological truth standard"

- Results (exact/Clopper-Pearson-type 95% CIs): Reader 1: PPA 73% (55, 87), NPA 91% (72, 99); Reader 2: PPA 49% (31, 67), NPA 91% (72, 99); Reader 3: PPA 58% (39, 75), NPA 83% (61, 94). High NPA but low PPA (95% CI lower bound below 50% for 2 of 3 readers) — the approved label restricts use to an adjunct role rather than a standalone diagnostic claim, consistent with this asymmetric accuracy pattern

- No NCT/ClinicalTrials.gov record exists for either Study #17 or Study #18 — consistent with a small, single-center, expanded-access-IND-based program that was never independently registered

- No Advisory Committee meeting was held. Instead, during the 2016 review cycle, "the FDA review team consulted two independent Special Government Employees (SGE)... both... members of MIDAC (Medical Imaging Drug Advisory Committee). Neither consultant was aware of the other's participation. No clinical data were available to either consultant" — reusing (and generalizing beyond ODAC to MIDAC) the existing taxonomy term for SGE consultation in lieu of a public advisory committee meeting

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2019/200655Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2019/200655s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (statistical reviewer: Satish Misra, PhD) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/200655Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record — none exists for Study #17 or Study #18

- No genuine pivotal publication exists for Study #18 (it was not published in the peer-reviewed literature). The one verified literature citation in the FDA review is background/foreign-approval evidence, not the US pivotal basis: Eshuis SA, Jager PL, Maguire RP, Jonkman S, Dierckx RA, Leenders KL. "Direct comparison of FP-CIT SPECT and F-DOPA PET in patients with Parkinson's disease and healthy controls." *Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging.* 2009;36(3):454-462. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00259-008-0989-5), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19037637/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Direct%20comparison%20FP-CIT%20SPECT%20F-DOPA%20PET%20Parkinson%27s%20disease%20healthy%20controls) — cited in the FDA review only as the basis for an earlier French/EU approval

**Other resources**

- No IPD/dataset access program participation applies; this is an academic single-center diagnostic study, not an industry-sponsored trial.

- No public FDA Advisory Committee (e.g., ODAC/MIDAC) meeting was held; two individual Special Government Employee consultations were used instead (see above).

- A 2025 efficacy supplement to this NDA (200655Orig1s001) also exists, outside the scope of this 2019 original-approval entry.

**Reverse-engineered SAP [inferred]**

No genuine sponsor SAP or protocol document is public for Study #18 (no ClinicalTrials.gov record exists at all). The following is reconstructed from the FDA Multi-Discipline Review's reported design and results:

- *[inferred, traced to the FDA Multi-Discipline Review's Study #18 design description]* — the study appears to have pre-specified PPA and NPA (rather than sensitivity/specificity) as co-primary accuracy measures precisely because the reference standard is a clinical diagnosis, not a pathological truth standard, and the review's explicit terminological care about this distinction suggests it was a designed feature of the analysis plan, not an ad hoc choice after the fact.

- *[inferred, traced to the exact binomial 95% CIs reported per reader in the Multi-Discipline Review]* — the use of an exact (Clopper-Pearson-type) binomial CI, rather than a Wald-normal-approximation CI, for a modest sample size (n=56) is consistent with a pre-specified small-sample-appropriate analysis plan, matching the same exact-CI convention already documented in this census for other single-arm diagnostic-accuracy PET-tracer approvals (Fluciclovine F 18/Axumin, Gallium Ga 68 dotatate/Netspot).

- *[inferred, traced to the CRL history]* — the shift from Study #17 (2016 CRL, unblinded reference-standard clinicians, incomplete follow-up) to Study #18 (blinded reference clinicians, ≥6-month completed follow-up required for inclusion) indicates the analysis plan for Study #18 pre-specified both a minimum follow-up duration and reference-standard blinding as inclusion/quality-control criteria, directly responsive to FDA's 2016 CRL deficiencies.
