FDA's Summary Review states explicitly: *[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, NDA 209899]* — "This application was not referred to an Advisory Committee for review because this drug is not the first in its class, the safety profile is similar to that of the two other drugs in this class approved for this indication, the clinical trial designs were acceptable and performed under agreed SPAs, the efficacy findings were clear, and the safety profile was acceptable in light of the serious nature of the disease being treated."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 209899, p.9]* — "The primary analysis for the ARR was to be carried out using a Poisson regression model. The model was to compare treatment groups, adjusted for region, age, and the number of Gd-enhancing (GdE) lesions at baseline, with the natural log transformation of time on study as an offset term. Two sensitivity analyses were to be performed. The first sensitivity analysis was to repeat the primary analysis counting both confirmed and unconfirmed relapses. The second sensitivity analysis was to use a negative binomial regression model, instead of the Poisson regression model, to compare relapse rates."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 209899, p.9]* — "The key secondary endpoints of cumulative number of new or newly enlarging T2 lesions between baseline and Month 12 and the number of GdE lesions at Month 12 were to be analyzed using a negative binomial regression model with factors for treatment, region, age, and baseline number of GdE lesions, with the natural log transformation of the number of available MRI scans as an offset term."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 209899, p.10]* — "Statistical testing for the primary efficacy endpoint was to be made between each ozanimod dose group and the IFN β-1a group (2 treatment contrasts). To account for multiple comparisons, each of the 2 treatment comparisons with IFN β-1a was to be tested at the α = 0.025 level. The 3 key secondary endpoints were to be tested in a sequential, closed hierarchical testing procedure with ozanimod 1 mg dose to be tested before ozanimod 0.5 mg dose for each key secondary endpoint following the given rank order... If only 1 ozanimod dose was significant on the primary endpoint, then the hierarchical testing procedure was to be employed on the rank-ordered key secondary endpoints for the surviving dose only, at the 2.5% level of significance."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 209899, p.18]* — "For Study 201B, ... A higher percentage of patients with 3-month disability progression was observed in ozanimod 1 mg group compared to two other treatment groups. Similarly, more patients treated with ozanimod than patients treated with IFN β-1a had disability progression confirmed at 6 months. Therefore, pooling of the data was not considered appropriate. ... Based on the results of 3-month and 6-month disability progression for the two studies, it is concluded that no treatment benefit of ozanimod was observed in the confirmed disability progression."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 209899, p.29-30, Conclusions]* — "Studies 301 and 201B provided consistent evidence that the treatment of ozanimod was effective as compared to interferon beta-1a in reducing the relapse rate in patients with relapsing forms of MS. There is no evidence that ozanimod has benefit in delaying disability progression."

*[verbatim, FDA Clinical Review, NDA 209899, §2.1/5.2]* — "the incidence of bradycardia was 0.8% (versus 0.7% with IFN beta-1a) after the first day taking the drug. Since the heart rate nadir occurred on Day 8, the utility of performing first-dose cardiac monitoring after starting ozanimod is unclear." — and separately, on REMS: "A REMS does not appear to be necessary for the safe use of ozanimod in the indicated population." (This distinguishes ozanimod from the first-in-class S1P modulator fingolimod, which does require first-dose observation; ozanimod instead uses a mandatory 7-day outpatient dose-titration regimen plus a baseline ECG/cardiology-consult gate, per the approved label §2.1-2.2/5.2.)

**Reverse-engineered / reconstructed SAP detail — RADIANCE (RPC01-201B) Statistical Analysis Plan Part B, v2.0**

- *[reconstructed, not verbatim — decoded from a substitution-cipher-obfuscated PDF text layer, RADIANCE SAP §9.1.1]* — the posted SAP describes the ARR primary analysis in language matching the FDA Statistical Review almost exactly: relapse rate for each treatment group is the total relapses divided by total patient-days on study (the "unadjusted relapse rate"), with the formal primary analysis performed via a Poisson regression model comparing treatment groups adjusted for region, age at baseline, and baseline number of GdE lesions, with a log-time-on-study offset; the section explicitly labels a repeat of this same model, substituting negative binomial regression, as a named "Sensitivity Analysis" (§9.1.2) — confirming the FDA reviewer's characterization that negative binomial regression was the sponsor's pre-specified sensitivity method, not the formal primary method, for ARR
- *[reconstructed, §9.2.1]* — for the key secondary MRI endpoints, the SAP text (decoded) states the primary analysis of new/enlarging T2 lesions and of GdE lesions "will be performed using a negative binomial regression model adjusted for region, age at Baseline, and Baseline number of GdE lesions" with the log of available MRI scans as the offset — i.e., negative binomial regression, not Poisson, was the sponsor's designated primary method specifically for these two secondary endpoints, consistent with the StatR
- *[reconstructed, §9.2.1]* — three pre-specified sensitivity analyses are described for each MRI lesion endpoint: mean-value imputation from same-arm patients, LOCF, and an observed-cases-only analysis, each substituting exposure-time for scan-count as the offset — matching the StatR's description exactly
- *[reconstructed, §9.2.1, disability progression]* — the SAP defines sustained disability progression as a ≥1.0-point EDSS increase from baseline confirmed after a 3-month and a 6-month period, with progression not confirmable at a relapse-assessment visit, death due to MS counted as a confirmed progression, and censoring at the later of the last EDSS assessment or last dose date; the primary analysis method given in this section is a Cox proportional-hazards model, with sensitivity analyses varying the EDSS-progression threshold definition and the handling of unconfirmed progressions/premature discontinuations
- *[reconstructed, §5.1]* — the SAP's sample-size section cites Mikol (assumed control ARR) and Nicholas (sample-size method), targeting power to detect a specified ARR reduction with an assumed dropout rate, but the specific numeric assumptions (control ARR value, dispersion parameter, target N) were not recoverable from the extracted text — these figures were rendered in a way that dropped entirely from the PDF's text layer (distinct from the redaction of literally patient-identifying content described in the document's own disclosure notice); the actually-achieved sample size (1,320 randomized, 1,200 planned) is instead sourced from the FDA Statistical Review above
- *[reconstructed, §5.3.1-5.3.3]* — analysis populations: Intent-to-Treat (all randomized patients confirmed to have received ≥1 dose, analyzed as randomized); Per-Protocol (ITT subset excluding major protocol deviations, e.g., McDonald-criteria MS diagnosis violations, baseline EDSS out of range, insufficient qualifying relapse/GdE-lesion history, or poor drug compliance), to be fully defined before database lock; Safety population (all patients receiving ≥1 dose, analyzed by highest dose actually received)

### 47. Opicapone (Ongentys) — NDA 212489

**Sponsor:** Neurocrine Biosciences, Inc. (applicant; opicapone was licensed from BIAL – Portela & Ca, S.A. in February 2017 for North American development/commercialization — BIAL is the drug's innovator, ran both pivotal trials, and holds the EU marketing authorization, granted June 24, 2016, under the same brand name Ongentys)

**Indication approved:** ONGENTYS (opicapone) capsules as adjunctive treatment to levodopa/carbidopa in patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) experiencing "off" episodes

**Approval date:** April 24, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** BIPARK-I (BIA-91067-301), NCT01568073, and BIPARK-II (BIA-91067-302), NCT01227655 — both conducted years earlier in support of the 2016 EU approval; the US NDA relied on these already-completed trials rather than new US-based Phase III studies

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* five-arm randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled (entacapone 200 mg), parallel-group, multicenter dose-finding trial (BIPARK-I/Study 301: opicapone 5/25/50 mg vs. entacapone vs. placebo, 1:1:1:1:1); three-arm randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter trial (BIPARK-II/Study 302: opicapone 25/50 mg vs. placebo, 1:1:1); each 14-15-week double-blind period followed by a non-controlled, 1-year open-label extension in which all subjects received active opicapone; entire clinical development program conducted outside the US without a US IND, reviewed under 21 CFR 314.106 (foreign data)/21 CFR 312.120

- *Endpoints:* continuous patient-diary-based endpoint — change from baseline in absolute OFF-time (minutes, averaged over the 3 days preceding each visit) at the end of the double-blind period (primary, both trials); OFF-time responder and ON-time responder (≥1-hour change from baseline, key secondary); UPDRS III (ON state), absolute ON-time without troublesome dyskinesia, percentage OFF-time, PDSS, NMSS (other secondary/exploratory endpoints)

- *Primary analysis:* analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) with treatment group and region/pooled-country as fixed effects and baseline OFF-time as a covariate; Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by region for the responder secondary endpoints; mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) used as a missing-data sensitivity analysis in both trials

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing via a sequential gatekeeping procedure (BIPARK-I: three one-sided superiority-vs-placebo tests, one per dose, within a 0.025 one-sided family-wise error rate, with non-inferiority-vs-entacapone [30-minute margin] tested only for doses found superior); Dunnett's alpha-level adjustment for the two pairwise dose-vs-placebo comparisons (BIPARK-II)

- *Missing data/bias:* last-available-post-baseline-observation carried forward for a missing primary-endpoint value in both trials (FDA reviewer explicitly objected to calling this "LOCF" and recommended "last available value" instead); FDA-conducted additional sensitivity analyses beyond the sponsor's own — opposite-arm-mean imputation scenarios in BIPARK-I, and a missing-at-random robustness check plus an awake-time-covariate reanalysis in BIPARK-II, the latter prompted by a markedly higher, adverse-event-driven dropout rate (16.9%) in the 50 mg arm

- *Regulatory:* reliance on foreign clinical data not conducted under a US IND (21 CFR 314.106/312.120); drug already approved in the EU (June 2016) years before the US NDA (April 2020), under the same trade name; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- BIPARK-I (Study 301): randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled, parallel-group trial at 104 sites in 19 countries (Europe + Russia) in idiopathic PD patients aged 30-83 with ≥3 years' disease duration, Hoehn & Yahr stage I-III at ON, treated with levodopa/DDCI for ≥1 year with "wearing-off" (end-of-dose motor fluctuations) and ≥1.5 hours average daily OFF-time (excluding early-morning pre-first-dose OFF); randomized 1:1:1:1:1 to opicapone 5/25/50 mg QD, entacapone 200 mg with every levodopa/DDCI intake, or placebo, for a 14-15-week double-blind period, followed by a 1-year open-label extension in which all subjects (including former placebo/entacapone patients) received opicapone
- BIPARK-II (Study 302): randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial at 69 sites in 12 countries (including South America, Asia, South Africa), same core eligibility criteria; randomized 1:1:1 to opicapone 25/50 mg QD or placebo for 14-15 weeks, followed by the same 1-year open-label extension structure; no entacapone arm
- Primary endpoint (both trials): change from baseline in absolute OFF-time (minutes) at the end of the double-blind period, based on patient self-rating diaries; baseline = mean OFF-time over the last 3 diary days before randomization, endpoint = mean OFF-time over the last 3 diary days before the final double-blind visit
- Key secondary endpoints: OFF-time responders (≥1-hour reduction) and ON-time responders (≥1-hour increase) from baseline to endpoint (CMH test, stratified by region); UPDRS I/II(ON)/III total score change; absolute ON-time without troublesome dyskinesia; Parkinson's Disease Sleep Scale (PDSS) and Non-Motor Symptoms Scale (NMSS) as further secondaries; BIPARK-II additionally listed UPDRS III (ON) and percentage OFF-time as key secondaries
- Sample size/power: BIPARK-I sized at ~110/arm (assuming a 10% major-protocol-violation rate) for >95% marginal power to detect the most efficacious dose vs. placebo (assuming 105-minute vs. 30-minute OFF-time reduction) and ~84% disjunctive power for the subsequent non-inferiority-vs-entacapone step; BIPARK-II sized at 135/arm (405 total) for >95% marginal power at the more efficacious dose and ~85% at the less efficacious dose (assuming 90-/105-minute vs. 30-minute reductions)
- Statistical methods: ANCOVA (treatment + region/pooled-country as fixed effects, baseline OFF-time as covariate) for the primary superiority comparisons; missing primary-endpoint values imputed via last-available-post-baseline-observation; MMRM used as the principal missing-data sensitivity analysis in both trials, with FDA's reviewer performing additional independent sensitivity re-analyses (imputation-scenario swaps in BIPARK-I; MAR-robustness check and an awake-time covariate reanalysis in BIPARK-II) because of higher, AE-driven dropout in the 50 mg arms
- Results: BIPARK-I — LS-mean OFF-time reduction of -116.8 min (50 mg), -85.9 min (25 mg), -91.3 min (5 mg), -56.0 min (placebo); only 50 mg was statistically superior to placebo (adjusted difference -60.8 min, p=0.0015) and non-inferior to entacapone (-26.2 min, 95% CI -63.8 to 11.4, p=0.0051 for non-inferiority). BIPARK-II — LS-mean reduction of -118.8 min (50 mg), -101.7 min (25 mg), -64.5 min (placebo); only 50 mg reached significance after Dunnett adjustment (-54.3 min, p=0.0081); 25 mg did not (-37.2 min, p=0.11). Neither trial's 5 mg or 25 mg dose reached statistical significance vs. placebo — this is the basis for FDA approving only the 50 mg dose (no titration regimen), consistent with the EU label's use of 50 mg as the studied/marketed dose

In Study 301, subjects treated with OPC 50mg showed a statistically significant decrease in absolute OFF-time of 60.8 minutes (p-value=0.0015) compared to the placebo. Study 302 also showed a statistically significant decrease in absolute OFF-time of 54.3 (p-value=0.0081) in subjects treated with OPC 50mg. Subjects treated with either OPC 5mg or 25mg failed to reach statistical significance."

Sensitivity analyses were performed on the primary endpoint using a mixed model for repeated measurement (MMRM)..."

The reviewer recommends calling the last available value approach throughout the report instead of last observation carried forward (LOCF)." — this is the one place the review explicitly distinguishes the EU regulatory framework (which required the entacapone non-inferiority comparison) from FDA's own review, which relied only on the placebo-superiority result and set the non-inferiority analysis aside as not affecting the US approval decision.

### 48. Flortaucipir F18 (Tauvid) — NDA 212123

**Sponsor:** Avid Radiopharmaceuticals, Inc. (an Eli Lilly and Company subsidiary; adverse-event reporting in the label routes through Eli Lilly and Company)

**Indication approved:** Radioactive diagnostic agent for positron emission tomography (PET) imaging of the brain to estimate the density and distribution of aggregated tau neurofibrillary tangles (NFTs) in adult patients with cognitive impairment who are being evaluated for Alzheimer's disease (AD); labeling explicitly excludes use for evaluating chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE)

**Approval date:** May 28, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** Two phase 3 trials formed the efficacy basis: Study 18F-AV-1451-A16 ("A16," the autopsy/neuropathological-correlation study), NCT02516046, and Study 18F-AV-1451-FR01 ("FR01," the reader-reproducibility substudy), NCT03901092. Two additional phase 3 trials, 18F-AV-1451-A05 ("A05C") and 18F-AV-1451-PX01 ("PX01"), tested a separate prognostic-risk hypothesis (baseline tau status predicting 18-month cognitive/functional decline) but did not meet their pre-specified success criteria and were not part of the approved indication's evidentiary basis.

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* diagnostic-accuracy study against an autopsy-confirmed neuropathological reference standard (single-arm, no comparator imaging/mapping agent) — a variant of the taxonomy's "Diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison)" in which the paired "reference standard" is postmortem histopathology rather than a second active comparator diagnostic agent (proposed refinement of existing term); co-primary endpoints (Study A16 required both a B3-Braak-stage hypothesis and a separate NIA-AA ADNC hypothesis to each reach significance); prospectively planned inter-reader/intra-reader reproducibility substudy using rereads of the same image set by a second independent panel of five blinded readers (Study FR01)

- *Endpoints:* per-reader sensitivity and specificity of blinded visual PET interpretation (τAD+/++ vs. τAD-) against postmortem Braak-stage (B3) and NIA-AA ADNC neuropathological criteria (A16, primary); majority-read sensitivity/specificity (A16, secondary); inter-reader reliability via Fleiss' kappa across a pooled reread of A16 and A05C images (FR01, primary)

- *Primary analysis:* Wilson score method for constructing 95% CIs around sensitivity/specificity, with a pre-specified win criterion (lower 95% CI bound ≥50% for at least 3 of 5 readers); Fleiss' kappa with a pre-specified win criterion (lower 95% CI bound ≥0.6) for inter-/intra-reader agreement; Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (A05C's gatekeeper procedure: primary-objective hypothesis tested first at α=0.05, secondary-objective hypothesis tested only if primary was significant)

- *Missing data/bias:* population/spectrum bias from an autopsy cohort of terminally ill patients not representative of the intended-use population (patients with cognitive impairment being evaluated for AD), which FDA's reviewers judged was weighted toward more severe/advanced tau pathology than the labeled population; reference-standard-threshold sensitivity analysis comparing the sponsor's primary B3 Braak-stage cutoff against an alternative B2/B3 cutoff, used by FDA to probe how much the reported sensitivity/specificity depended on the chosen pathology threshold — notably distinct from the "Performance-measure analysis without an independent reference standard (verification bias)" term used for prior radiopharmaceutical entries (Axumin, Netspot) in this census, because here the autopsy-based reference standard was genuinely independent of the imaging interpretation (blinded pathologists, no biopsy-directed circularity), so classic verification bias does not apply — the analogous limitation here is spectrum/population-representativeness bias, not verification bias

- *Regulatory:* FDA Advisory Committee meeting scheduled, then cancelled after the scientific issues motivating it were resolved without a public meeting (distinct from "FDA Advisory Committee meeting held")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study A16 was a multicenter (28 sites, 2 countries), open-label, phase 3 clinico-pathological correlation trial: terminally ill subjects (life expectancy ≤6 months) with AD/mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or who were cognitively normal were imaged with flortaucipir F18 (FTP) PET and, following death, underwent postmortem neuropathological assessment; five independent imaging physicians, blinded to clinical and neuropathological information, read each scan as showing an AD-consistent tau pattern (τAD+/τAD++) or a non-AD pattern (τAD-)
- Primary hypotheses (both required significant at two-sided α=0.05 for the study to be positive): (1) a τAD-positive PET pattern corresponds to Braak stage B3 (neocortical NFT spread) at autopsy; (2) a τAD-positive PET pattern corresponds to "high" AD neuropathologic change (ADNC) by NIA-AA criteria (Hyman et al. 2012); win criterion for each reader-level hypothesis was a lower 95% CI bound ≥50% for both sensitivity and specificity, required for at least 3 of the 5 readers (secondary objective: same win criterion applied to the 5-reader majority read)
- The Efficacy Analysis Set excluded an unblinded "front-runner" cohort (up to 6 early autopsy cases used non-blinded by the Applicant to refine PET-read and pathology-scoring methods before the primary analysis was locked) and required valid/evaluable PET data plus interpretable, Braak-stageable autopsy tissue; the realized primary cohort was 64 subjects (of 156 enrolled, 70 died, 67 completed with valid autopsy, 3 further excluded), 96.9% white, 53.1% female, mean age 82.5 years, median PET-to-autopsy interval 59.5 days (range 1-264 days)
- Sensitivity and specificity and their 95% CIs (Wilson score method) were calculated per reader; reported results (B3 threshold): sensitivity 92%-100% across the 5 readers (lower 95% CI bounds 80-91%), specificity 52%-92% (lower 95% CI bounds 34-75%); 3 of 5 readers met the ≥50% lower-bound win criterion for both metrics; majority read sensitivity 92% (95% CI 80-97), specificity 80% (95% CI 61-91)
- Study FR01 was a prospectively designed reader-reproducibility substudy added after an FDA pre-NDA-meeting recommendation (February 2019): five new independent readers, blinded to demographic/clinical data, reread all 82 A16 scans plus a subset of 159 A05C scans (241 total), including a 20-scan random subset reread twice to assess intrareader agreement; primary endpoints were diagnostic performance against the A16 autopsy truth standard and inter-reader reliability (Fleiss' kappa) across all included cases, using the same win criteria as A16 (sensitivity/specificity lower bound ≥50%) plus a kappa lower-bound win criterion of ≥0.6
- Reported FR01 result: overall Fleiss' kappa across all 241 rereads = 0.87 (95% CI 0.83-0.91), exceeding the 0.6 win criterion (all 5 readers agreed on 209/241 scans); FR01 reader performance against autopsy truth standard on the reread A16 images was similar to the original A16 reader performance, offered as confirmatory evidence for the A16 primary finding
- FDA's reviewers also ran an exploratory sensitivity analysis using an alternative B2/B3 pathology threshold (rather than the sponsor's primary B3-only threshold), recommended by the review division under IND 119863 and consistent with Hyman et al. 2012: sensitivity fell to 68%-86% across readers (specificity 63%-100%), and FDA calculated that using the Applicant's B3-only threshold, patients with "intermediate" (B2-level) AD neuropathologic change — a level FDA noted is sufficient by itself for a neuropathologic AD diagnosis in symptomatic patients — could be read as PET-negative; this became a labeled warning (Section 5.1, "Risk of Misdiagnosis," addressing false-negative risk in patients with intermediate-severity tau pathology) rather than a basis for non-approval
- Two additional phase 3 trials (A05C, and its follow-up PX01 using placebo-arm scans from the AZES therapeutic trial) tested whether baseline FTP PET status (τAD++ vs. non-τAD++) predicted 18-month clinically meaningful cognitive/functional decline (Cox proportional-hazards primary analysis, adjusted for age, ANART score, and baseline CDR-SB; secondary diagnostic-performance analysis of baseline tau status against dichotomized CDR-SB change as a truth standard, again using Wilson score CIs and the same ≥50%-lower-bound win criterion, gated behind the primary hypothesis in a step-down testing order); per FDA's review, A05C's pre-specified success criteria were not met, so this prognostic-risk claim was not pursued in the approved label
- No formal dose-finding study was conducted (Tauvid is a microdose radiodiagnostic, ≤20 µg); the to-be-marketed dose (370 MBq/10 mCi, 20-minute acquisition) was justified from pooled clinical-pharmacology/dosimetry studies (T807000, A01, A05, A10) on comparable count-density/image-quality grounds rather than a dedicated dose-ranging trial

- FDA Integrated Review (combined Multi-Discipline Review package; Reference ID 4615642) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/212123Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf (this NDA used FDA's newer single-document "Integrated Review Template" format rather than separate StatR/MedR/SumR PDFs, so the statistical review, clinical review, and summary review are combined in this one file; §6.2.3 "Statistical Analysis Plans" and §6.4 "Review Issues Relevant to the Evaluation of Benefit" contain the statistical-methodology detail)

- Pivotal publication: Fleisher AS, Pontecorvo MJ, Devous MD Sr, et al., for the A16 Study Investigators. "Positron Emission Tomography Imaging With [18F]flortaucipir and Postmortem Assessment of Alzheimer Disease Neuropathologic Changes." *JAMA Neurol.* 2020;77(7):829-839 (erratum: *JAMA Neurol.* 2023;80(8):873). [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1001/jamaneurol.2020.0528), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32338734/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Positron%20Emission%20Tomography%20Imaging%20With%20flortaucipir%20and%20Postmortem%20Assessment%20of%20Alzheimer%20Disease%20Neuropathologic%20Changes)

**Other resources**

- No IPD/dataset sharing was identified for this NDA specifically. Eli Lilly (Avid's parent) participates in industry data-sharing platforms (e.g., the YODA Project) for a number of its therapeutic drugs, but no Tauvid/flortaucipir-specific listing was found, and trial-specific IPD availability was not confirmed; this is unsurprising for a small, purpose-built autopsy-correlation imaging program rather than a large multi-site therapeutic RCT.
- FDA Advisory Committee: a Medical Imaging Drugs Advisory Committee meeting was scheduled for April 23, 2020, then cancelled. *[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, Reference ID 4615642, §11 Advisory Committee Summary]* — "The Medical Imaging Drugs Advisory Committee meeting scheduled for April 23, 2020, has been cancelled. This meeting was cancelled because the issues for which the Food and Drug Administration was seeking the scientific input of the Committee have been resolved." (Federal Register notice posted April 13, 2020.)

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, NDA 212123, Reference ID 4615642, §I.1 Summary of Regulatory Action, p.3]* — "There were two phase 3 studies. Study 1 (NCT02516046) compared the performance of blinded image readers to detect individuals with tau pathology from among patients who were terminally ill with life expectancy ≤9 months at the time of FTP administration... The number of readers for whom the lower bound of 95% CIs exceeded prespecified coprimary thresholds for sensitivity and specificity was 3, equal to the prespecified minimum the review division agreed was adequate to support efficacy during study planning meetings under investigational new drug (IND) 119863."

*[verbatim, same source, §6.2.1 Trial Design, p.27-28]* — "The diagnostic performance (sensitivity and specificity) of individual readers (primary objective) or majority reads (secondary objective) for the identification of histopathological status (both tau and AD pathology) through interpretation FTP PET imaging were calculated. Win criteria for sensitivity and specificity were proposed as a lower bound of the 95% CI ≥50% for the same three out of five individual readers (primary objective) and lower bound of the 95% CI ≥50% for the majority reading result (secondary objective). While an autopsy population is not generalizable to the intended use population, the design used in this trial is the most feasible design to obtain a truth standard (TS)."

*[verbatim, same source, §6.2.3 Statistical Analysis Plans, p.31]* — "For the primary efficacy analysis, the diagnosis performance (sensitivity, specificity) of five independent readers' interpretation of antemortem FTP PET scan images (τAD++/τAD+ or τAD-) for detection of a pattern of neocortical uptake that corresponds to NFT score B3 at autopsy were to be evaluated. The sensitivity and specificity along with their 95% CIs based on the Wilson score method were to be calculated for each of the five readers. The first primary hypothesis was to be considered met if the lower bounds of sensitivity and specificity were ≥50% for at least three of the five readers... Primary efficacy analysis hypothesis 2 would be the same as the first primary hypothesis except that the NIA-AA autopsy criteria would be used to define the TS. Both primary hypothesis 1 and primary hypothesis 2 would need to be significant at the two-sided 0.05 significance level for the study to be considered positive."

*[verbatim, same source, §6.2.3, p.31, Efficacy Analysis Set definition]* — "The Efficacy Analysis Set 1 was to include all safety analysis set subjects (provided informed consent and received study drug) recruited under this protocol who fulfilled all of the following: • Came to autopsy after the front-runner cohort (i.e., excluding the first three subjects who came to autopsy) • Had valid and evaluable PET data • Had valid and interpretable autopsy specimens, where interpretability was to be assessed for the Braak stage."

*[verbatim, same source, §6.2.1, p.28, Study FR01]* — "For this study, five new independent imaging physicians blinded to demographic and clinical data received image reading training similar to the A16 autopsy and A05 studies... The primary endpoints for this study focused on diagnostic performance versus autopsy TS, and on inter-reader reliability across all included cases... For both A16 and FR01, agreement across readers was assessed and the lower bound of the 95% CI for Fleiss' kappa was deemed acceptable if it was ≥0.6."

*[verbatim, same source, §6.2.3, p.32-33, Study A05C]* — "The key secondary hypothesis for testing is that, of the five independent imaging physicians, at least the same three will have the lower bounds of two-sided 95% CIs >50%, for both sensitivity and specificity. To control the overall type I error rate at a 2-sided 0.05 level, a gate keeper methodology would be employed. Hypotheses would be tested in the following order: 1. Testing of hypothesis for primary objective analysis 2. Testing of hypothesis for secondary objective analysis. Hypothesis testing would begin testing (1) at the 0.05 level. If the p-value is ≤0.05, the second hypothesis would be tested."

*[verbatim, same source, §6.2.1, Study A05C outcome, p.29]* — "As the prespecified success criteria for the above Study A05C were not met, following up on the discussions at the pre-NDA meeting, the Applicant designed this study using scans from placebo subjects in the AZES therapeutic trial [i.e., Study PX01]."

*[verbatim, same source, §6.4.2 Limitations of Efficacy Evidence for Tau Pathology Detection, p.41-43]* — "In the Applicant's submission, diagnostic performance characteristics were calculated for coprimary endpoints such that a positive FTP scan (Tauvid pattern—moderate or advanced) identified B3 level of NFT pathology (Primary Analysis 1) and high levels of ADNC. This approach may impose limitations on the utility of Tauvid imaging as a subset of patients with B2 level tau pathology could potentially be classified as Negative Tauvid scans... while still possessing tissue pathology sufficient for AD diagnosis... The number of primary patients in Study A16 with B3 tau pathology... was 39 (61% of those studied). The number of patients with B3 or B2 tau pathology... was 56 (88% of those studied). These high numbers demonstrate that the spectrum of disease studied in this sample of patients who are terminally ill is weighted toward severe tau pathology... In comparison, the spectrum of tau pathology in indicated patients with cognitive impairment being evaluated for AD is almost certain to be weighted more toward earlier stages of the pathological spectrum, since AD is a progressive neurodegenerative disease."

*Note on the reference standard (flagged per task scope):* unlike the prior radiopharmaceutical entries in this census (Technetium Tc 99m tilmanocept/Lymphoseek, Fluciclovine F 18/Axumin, Gallium Ga 68 dotatate/Netspot), where the reference standard was itself an in-vivo comparator test or biopsy-directed histology entangled with the index test's own results (yielding the "verification bias" limitation FDA reviewers flagged in those reviews), Tauvid's A16 reference standard was postmortem neuropathological staging performed by pathologists independent of, and blinded to, the antemortem PET interpretation — a genuinely independent truth standard. FDA's principal statistical concern here was correspondingly different in kind: not verification bias, but (1) whether an unavoidably non-representative, terminally-ill autopsy cohort generalizes to the labeled population of living patients with cognitive impairment being evaluated for AD, and (2) sensitivity of the sensitivity/specificity estimates to the sponsor's chosen B3-only pathology-positivity threshold versus a broader B2/B3 threshold — addressed in the label via a "Risk of Misdiagnosis" warning rather than a data gap requiring a reverse-engineered reconstruction.

### 49. Inebilizumab-cdon (Uplizna) — BLA 761142

**Sponsor:** Viela Bio, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) in adult patients who are anti-aquaporin-4 (AQP4) antibody positive.

**Approval date:** 2020-06-11

**Pivotal trial:** N-MOmentum (Study CD-IA-MEDI-551-1155), NCT02200770

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group (3:1 randomization, stratified by AQP4-IgG serostatus and by region [Japan vs. non-Japan]); event-driven trial (enrollment set to stop at 67 Adjudication Committee-confirmed attacks or 252 randomized subjects, whichever came first); early-stopped for efficacy (Independent Data Monitoring Committee recommendation on ethical grounds, not a pre-specified group-sequential efficacy boundary); population-based fixed-sequence primary-analysis hierarchy (AQP4-IgG seropositive cohort tested first; only if significant was the same endpoint retested in the full ITT/all-comers population)

- *Endpoints:* Time to first Adjudication Committee (AC)-determined NMO/NMOSD attack (a composite clinical/radiologic construct assessed against 18 protocol-defined criteria across three bodily domains — optic nerve, spinal cord, brain/brainstem — and confirmed by a blinded, independent adjudication committee)

- *Primary analysis:* Cox proportional-hazards model (stratified or with covariates); Kaplan-Meier estimation

- *Multiplicity:* Bonferroni-based chain/graphical alpha-propagation procedure across the primary and four secondary endpoints (EDSS worsening, low-contrast visual acuity, cumulative active MRI lesions, NMOSD-related hospitalizations), with a pre-specified alpha-propagation rule redistributing rejected hypotheses' alpha to remaining hypotheses — akin to the graphical alpha-propagation method (Maurer-Bretz) family

- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Data Monitoring Committee (DMC/DSMB) — the protocol's only formally described interim look was a masked/unmasked futility-oriented review; there is no group-sequential alpha-spending efficacy boundary documented in FDA's statistical review, and the trial's early termination was instead an IDMC ethical recommendation based on an unblinded interim look

- *Missing data/bias:* Standard right-censoring at last evaluable assessment (Day 197/discontinuation visit); FDA-conducted worst-case sensitivity analyses (treating all reported possible relapses as AC-confirmed, and treating all study discontinuations as AC-confirmed relapses)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Design: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, 2-arm, multicenter Phase 2/3 trial (231 randomized, 99 sites screening in 25 countries, 82 sites/24 countries randomizing) testing IV inebilizumab 300 mg (Day 1 and Day 15) vs. matching placebo in adults ≥18 years old with NMO/NMOSD, EDSS ≤7.5 (≤8 in special circumstances), who had at least one attack requiring rescue therapy in the last year (or two in the last two years); the trial enrolled both AQP4-IgG seropositive patients (n=213 of the ITT population) and AQP4-IgG seronegative patients (n=17), stratified 9:1 by design to approximate seropositive prevalence in the broader NMOSD population, and further stratified by region.
- Randomized-controlled period (RCP) ran to Day 197; patients who completed the RCP without an attack, or who exited early via an AC-confirmed attack, could enter an open-label extension (up to 3 years) followed by a 12-month safety follow-up period.
- Primary endpoint: time (days) from Day 1 to onset of an AC-determined NMO/NMOSD attack on or before Day 197/discontinuation, analyzed in the AQP4-IgG seropositive cohort with a Cox proportional-hazards model (treatment as an exploratory factor); the same model was fit in the full ITT population with AQP4-IgG serostatus as an added covariate — per an FDA-documented protocol amendment, "the primary analysis will first be tested in AQP4-IgG seropositive subjects, and if statistically significant, it will be further tested in all subjects" *[verbatim, FDA Clinical Review (MedR), Protocol Amendments summary, p. 32]*.
- Secondary endpoints (tested via the Bonferroni-based chain procedure, all restricted to the AQP4-IgG seropositive cohort as primary, with ITT-population versions as supportive): worsening from baseline in Kurtzke Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) score at last RCP visit (logistic regression, baseline EDSS covariate); change from baseline in low-contrast visual acuity (Landolt C Broken Rings Chart binocular score, ANCOVA with baseline covariate); cumulative total active MRI lesions (negative binomial regression); number of NMOSD-related in-patient hospitalizations (negative binomial regression).
- Sample size/enrollment plan was event-driven: enrollment was to stop when 67 AC-confirmed attacks had accrued or 252 subjects had been randomized, whichever came first (the plan was amended multiple times — an originally planned masked sample-size reassessment was removed by protocol Amendment 4 after FDA and sponsor agreed a formal SSR could no longer be sequenced ahead of the trial's planned futility analysis).
- The trial stopped early: on September 7, 2018, the Independent Data Monitoring Committee (IDMC) recommended stopping after an unblinded interim review, "reasoning it was not ethical to continue to expose patients to a higher relapse rate in the placebo arm given the efficacy findings in the active treatment arm" *[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, p. 13]* — at that point only 43 of the planned 67 AC-confirmed attacks had occurred (231 randomized, 230 treated). FDA's clinical reviewer separately flagged, from January 2017 IDMC minutes reviewed by the Division, that the interim hazard ratio was already 0.18 (95% CI 0.08–0.38) with conditional power >99.9%, and noted that "[b]ecause randomization ratio was 3:1, the identity of the group treated with inebilizumab was obvious and therefore, since the initial IDMC meeting, it is likely that members were aware of the primary analysis result" *[verbatim, FDA Clinical Review (MedR), p. 31]* — a documented concern about interim unblinding risk, though FDA's review does not conclude it invalidated the final result.
- Statistical result: in the AQP4-IgG seropositive cohort (ITT n=213: 161 inebilizumab / 52 placebo), hazard ratio 0.227 (95% CI 0.1214–0.4232, p<0.0001); in the small seronegative cohort (n=17: 13 inebilizumab / 4 placebo), the treatment effect was null (p=0.9977) — FDA's Summary Review states plainly that "the primary outcome analysis provides evidence of a significant treatment effect on relapses for anti-AQP4 seropositive patients but fails to provide any evidence of a treatment effect on relapses in anti-AQP4 seronegative patients" *[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, p. 15]*, which is why the approved label restricts the indication to AQP4-antibody-positive patients only, despite the trial having enrolled both serostatus groups.

- Pivotal publication: Cree BAC, Bennett JL, Kim HJ, Weinshenker BG, Pittock SJ, Wingerchuk DM, Fujihara K, Paul F, Cutter GR, Marignier R, Green AJ, Aktas O, Hartung HP, Lublin FD, Drappa J, Barron G, Madani S, Ratchford JN, She D, Cimbora D, Katz E; N-MOmentum study investigators. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(19)31817-3>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31495497/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Inebilizumab+for+the+treatment+of+neuromyelitis+optica+spectrum+disorder+N-MOmentum)

**Other resources**

- IPD/dataset access: no trial-specific IPD/dataset-sharing arrangement (Vivli, YODA Project, or otherwise) was confirmed for N-MOmentum in this pass. Viela Bio was acquired by Horizon Therapeutics in 2021, and Horizon was in turn acquired by Amgen in 2023; none of these entities' general data-sharing policy status for this specific dataset was independently verified here — treat as unconfirmed rather than unavailable.
- Advisory committee: none held. FDA's Summary Review states the application "was not referred to an Advisory Committee for review because the safety profile is similar to that of the other drugs with similar mechanisms approved for other indications, the clinical trial design was acceptable, the efficacy findings were clear, and the safety profile was acceptable in light of the serious nature of the disease being treated" *[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, p. 29]*.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Executive Summary, p. 4]* — "The study was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, clinical study that had two treatment groups (inebilizumab and placebo) and used the time (in days) from Day 1 to onset of an adjudication committee (AC)-determined NMO/NMOSD attack on or before the end of randomized-controlled period (Day 197/discontinuation visit) as the primary endpoint. The study showed that the estimated hazard ratio of inebilizumab group relative to placebo group was 0.227 (95% confidence interval = (0.1214, 0.4232), p-value < 0.0001) for the aquaporin-4-antibody (AQP4-IgG) seropostive subjects."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.1, p. 9]* — "The primary endpoint was the time (in days) from Day 1 to onset of an adjudication committee (AC)-determined NMO/NMOSD attack on or before the end of RCP (Day 197/discontinuation visit)."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.2, p. 9]* — "For the aquaporin-4-antibody (AQP4-IgG) seropostive cohort, the primary endpoint was analyzed using a Cox proportional hazards model with treatment as an exploratory factor; for the ITT population, the Cox model also included the AQP4-IgG serostatus. Subjects who completed the Day 197 visit of the RCP or discontinued the study before Day 197 for reasons other than an AC-determined NMO/NMOSD attack were censored in the Cox model at the time of the Day 197/discontinuation visit. Only AC-determined attacks with an assessment visit scheduled within 120 hours (5 days) of reporting symptoms AND all necessary assessments done within 10 days of an assessment visit were included in the primary analysis."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.2, p. 10]* — "The Bonferroni-based chain procedure was proposed to control the overall Type I error (i.e. alpha) of the study." (FDA's review states the underlying multiplicity graph and alpha-propagation rule were reproduced directly from "Table 7-5," "Figure 7-7," and "Table 7-7 in the statistical analysis plan," and describes the mechanics as: initial alpha of 0.05 allocated to the primary hypothesis; if rejected, alpha flows to the first key secondary hypothesis at α=0.05; if that is rejected, the remaining four secondary hypotheses are each tested at α=0.0125, with further redistribution among non-rejected hypotheses per the pre-specified propagation rule.)

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.4, p. 14]* — "Table 6 presents the analysis results of the primary endpoint. For the AQP4-IgG seropositive cohort, inebilizumab was statistically significantly better than placebo with a hazard ratio of 0.227 (p-value < 0.0001, 95% confidence interval = (0.1214, 0.4232)), indicating that the inebilizumab group had a lower risk of having NMO/NMOSD attacks. Although analysis results for all ITT subjects were similar to those for the AQP4-IgG seropositive cohort, it appeared that these results were driven entirely by the data from the AQP4-IgG seropositive cohort."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, p. 13]* — "Enrollment of patients was planned to end when a total of 67 AC-confirmed relapses had occurred in the randomized phase of the trial, or when 252 patients had been randomized and dosed, or following any recommendation by the Independent Data Monitoring Committee (IDMC) to stop the trial. On September 7, 2018, the IDMC recommended stopping the trial after reviewing the trial's interim unblinded findings reasoning it was not ethical to continue to expose patients to a higher relapse rate in the placebo arm given the efficacy findings in the active treatment arm. At the time of the trial's end, 43 AC-confirmed relapses had occurred; the trial had enrolled 231 patients with 230 of them having been treated."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, p. 15]* — "The primary efficacy analysis of Study 1155 was highly statistically significant (p<0.0001) in favor of inebilizumab-cdon in the anti-AQP4 antibody seropositive patients. The analysis failed to demonstrate any effect of treatment in the patients who were seronegative for anti-AQP4 antibodies (p=0.9977), and the overall result in all patients was clearly driven by the robust effect in the anti-AQP4 seropositive patients. Drs. Rodichok and Zhang agree that the results for the anti-AQP4 negative patients when considered separately provided no evidence of effectiveness and were not solely attributable to the relatively small number (n=17) of randomized patients."

*[verbatim, FDA Clinical Review (MedR), Protocol Amendments summary, p. 31–32]* — "In January, 2017, the Division received from the sponsor the minutes of the most recent IDMC meeting on January 13, 2017. The sponsor indicated that 212 subjects had been randomized as of January 9, 2017. As of the data cutoff, the AC had confirmed 38 NMO/NMOSD attacks among 34 subjects. ... The estimated Hazard ratio based on the data as of the cut-off point was 0.18 (0.08, 0.38) and the conditional power to predict a statistically significant difference between groups A and B was >99.9%." followed by the reviewer's comment: "Because randomization ratio was 3:1, the identity of the group treated with inebilizumab was obvious and therefore, since the initial IDMC meeting, it is likely that members were aware of the primary analysis result and that the sponsor became aware, at the latest, at the time of the interaction described above."

*[verbatim, FDA Clinical Review (MedR), Protocol Amendments summary, p. 32]* — "The primary analysis will first be tested in AQP4-IgG seropositive subjects, and if statistically significant, it will be further tested in all subjects" (Amendment 1, describing the sponsor's fixed-sequence population hierarchy for the primary endpoint).

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, p. 29]* — "This application was not referred to an Advisory Committee for review because the safety profile is similar to that of the other drugs with similar mechanisms approved for other indications, the clinical trial design was acceptable, the efficacy findings were clear, and the safety profile was acceptable in light of the serious nature of the disease being treated."

### 50. Satralizumab-mwge (Enspryng) — BLA 761149

**Sponsor:** Genentech, Inc. (Roche); satralizumab was co-developed and the pivotal trials were run by Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., sponsorship of the BLA was later transferred to Roche/Genentech

**Indication approved:** Treatment of neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) in adult patients who are anti-aquaporin-4 (AQP4) antibody positive

**Approval date:** August 14, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** SAkuraSky (protocol BN40898/SA-307JG, add-on to baseline immunosuppressant therapy), NCT02028884, and SAkuraStar (protocol BN40900/SA-309JG, monotherapy), NCT02073279

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, add-on to baseline treatment (SAkuraSky) and randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled monotherapy (SAkuraStar, 2:1 randomization), event-driven trial, randomized-withdrawal-style relapse-prevention design in a rare disease

- *Endpoints:* time to first protocol-defined relapse (TFR/TTR), adjudicated by an independent Clinical Endpoint Committee (CEC) (primary); change from baseline in VAS pain score and FACIT-Fatigue scale score at week 24 (key secondary)

- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test with hazard ratio and 95% CI from a stratified Cox proportional-hazards model

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (serial gatekeeping) hierarchical testing across TFR, VAS pain, and FACIT-Fatigue

- *Missing data/bias:* baseline-observation-carried-forward (BOCF) imputation for key secondary continuous endpoints, MMRM sensitivity analyses, sponsor-side unblinding/data-integrity breach (unauthorized use of an on-treatment biomarker to infer treatment assignment) formally assessed by FDA in a bias report

- *Regulatory:* Special Protocol Assessment (SAkuraStar), breakthrough therapy designation, subgroup (AQP4 serostatus) analysis driving a narrower approved indication than the enrolled trial population, no advisory committee meeting

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Two multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trials in adult (and, in SAkuraSky, adolescent ≥12 years) patients with NMO or NMOSD, both enrolling patients regardless of AQP4-antibody serostatus (with a cap on the seronegative proportion) — SAkuraSky (BN40898) added satralizumab or placebo to a stable baseline immunosuppressant (azathioprine, mycophenolate mofetil, or oral corticosteroids), randomized 1:1 (satralizumab n=41, placebo n=42); SAkuraStar (BN40900) tested satralizumab as monotherapy against placebo with no concurrent immunosuppressant permitted, randomized 2:1 (satralizumab n=63, placebo n=32)
- Satralizumab (or matching placebo) 120 mg subcutaneously at Weeks 0, 2, and 4, then every 4 weeks
- SAkuraSky randomization stratified by baseline annualized relapse rate (ARR: 1 vs. >1) and geographic region (Asia vs. Europe/USA); the proportion of adult patients who were AQP4-antibody seronegative was capped at ~30%, and pediatric enrollment required ≥4 of 8 adolescents to be seropositive
- SAkuraStar randomization stratified by prior NMOSD-prevention therapy (B-cell-depleting therapy vs. immunosuppressants/other) and most recent attack type (first attack vs. relapse) in the year before screening; AQP4-seronegative patients were similarly capped
- Both trials were event-driven: the double-blind period ended once a pre-specified number of CEC-adjudicated protocol-defined relapses (PDR) had accrued (26 for SAkuraSky; 44 for SAkuraStar, or 1.5 years after the last-enrolled patient's randomization, whichever came first)
- Primary endpoint: time to first PDR (TFR) — new/worsening neurological signs/symptoms attributable to NMO/NMOSD, persisting >24 hours, not attributable to confounders, adjudicated by an independent CEC, with the EDSS/Functional Systems Score (FSS) confirmatory assessment required within 7 days of symptom report for the relapse to count in the primary analysis
- Key secondary endpoints: change from baseline to week 24 in VAS pain score and FACIT-Fatigue scale score; other secondary endpoints included annualized relapse rate, relapse-free rate, EDSS, modified Rankin Scale, Zarit Burden Interview, SF-36, EQ-5D, and visual acuity
- Primary analysis population: intention-to-treat (ITT, all randomized patients); per-protocol population as a supportive analysis
- Primary analysis: two-sided stratified log-rank test (using the randomization strata) at the 5% significance level; treatment effect (hazard ratio, 95% CI) estimated from a stratified Cox proportional-hazards model using the same strata, with an added treatment-by-stratification-factor interaction term tested as a secondary check
- Multiplicity: serial gatekeeping/fixed-sequence testing across three endpoints in hierarchical order — TFR (PDR), then VAS pain at week 24, then FACIT-Fatigue at week 24 — each subsequent test performed only if the prior one was statistically significant, controlling family-wise error at 0.05
- Sensitivity analyses of TFR used alternative relapse definitions (any clinical relapse regardless of CEC confirmation, PDR regardless of the 7-day EDSS/FSS window, treated clinical relapse, treated optic-neuritis relapse only), each also analyzed by stratified log-rank test and stratified Cox regression
- Missing/censored data: for the primary TFR endpoint, censoring occurred at end of double-blind period, switch/increase in baseline treatment, or receipt of rescue therapy for relapse; for continuous secondary endpoints, BOCF imputation was the primary approach with MMRM (unstructured covariance) as a sensitivity analysis
- Sample size (SAkuraSky, per posted SAP): ~70 patients (1:1), 80% power at two-sided alpha=0.05, assuming a 66.5% relative risk reduction (HR=0.335) and an exponential placebo-arm relapse hazard (annual rate 0.4184), requiring 26 TFR events for the primary analysis; SAkuraStar's SAP documents ~90 patients (2:1) and a two-sided log-rank test, but the specific hazard-ratio/event-count assumptions are redacted in the version posted to ClinicalTrials.gov
- SAkuraStar was conducted under a Special Protocol Assessment (SPA) agreement with FDA (reached October 17, 2014); the SAP was amended multiple times, including FDA-driven changes from a permutation-based log-rank test to an asymptotic stratified log-rank test as the primary analysis method
- A major data-integrity issue arose during the trials: in November 2015 and again in May 2017, Chugai biostatisticians used unblinded on-treatment serum fibrinogen levels (reduced by satralizumab's IL-6 pathway blockade) to guess individual patients' treatment assignments and computed unauthorized interim hazard-ratio estimates, sharing results with colleagues including some investigators; FDA required a formal bias assessment as part of the BLA, and its Statistical Review concludes the SAkuraStar SPA sample-size/event-target increase (submitted shortly after the first unblinding attempt) could not be shown to be free of this influence, though a sensitivity analysis found no detectable difference in EDSS/secondary-endpoint data collected before vs. after the unblinding events
- Both trials enrolled AQP4-seropositive and seronegative patients; treatment effect on relapse was statistically significant and large in seropositive patients in both trials (FDA subgroup HR 0.21 [SAkuraSky] and 0.26 [SAkuraStar] for seropositive patients, nominal p=0.0086 and 0.0014) but not in seronegative patients (HR 0.66 [SAkuraSky] and 1.19 [SAkuraStar], i.e., numerically favoring placebo in the monotherapy trial) — this AQP4-serostatus interaction is what FDA cites as the basis for restricting the approved indication to AQP4-antibody-positive patients only, despite both trials enrolling a mixed population

- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/761149Orig1s000StatR.pdf

- SAkuraStar was conducted under a Special Protocol Assessment (SPA) agreement with FDA reached October 17, 2014; satralizumab received Breakthrough Therapy designation for NMOSD on December 18, 2018.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, ClinicalTrials.gov posted SAP, SAkuraSky/BN40898 (SA-307JG), Version 9.0, 20-Apr-2018, p.16-17]* — "This study is designed to assess the efficacy of SA237 over placebo on the treatment of NMO/NMO-SD. The null hypothesis for primary endpoint will be that there is no difference on the TFR between SA237 and placebo during double-blinded period... A two-sided stratified log-rank test at 5% level will be used to test this hypothesis." And: "estimates of the treatment effect will be expressed as hazard ratio and 95% CIs using a stratified (baseline ARR and geographical region) Cox proportional-hazards model."

*[verbatim, same SAP, p.17]* — "The serial gatekeeping methodology will be employed to control the rate of false positive for the primary endpoint (TFR based on protocol-defined relapses) and key secondary endpoints (change in VAS for pain at week 24 and change in the FACIT fatigue scale at week 24). The 3 efficacy endpoints will be analyzed in hierarchical order, beginning with the TFR based on protocol-defined relapses, followed by the VAS for pain, and ending with FACIT fatigue. A fixed-sequence approach will be applied to control the overall significance level at 0.05."

*[verbatim, same SAP, §5.14 Determination of Sample Size, p.36]* — "Approximately 70 subjects need to be recruited and randomized in a 1:1 ratio to the two treatment groups (SA237 and placebo). The sample size considerations are based on the following assumptions: A two-sided log-rank test; 80% power at the 5% significance level; A 66.5% reduction in the risk of relapse, i.e. the TFR hazard ratio of SA237 over placebo is 0.335; TFR in the placebo arm following an exponential distribution, with hazard rate for one year h(t) = 0.4184; A 2-year dropout rate of 10%. Based on the assumptions, 26 TFR events are needed for the primary analysis."

*[verbatim, ClinicalTrials.gov posted SAP, SAkuraStar/BN40900 (SA-309JG), Version 7.0, 28-Nov-2018, §5.5 "Amendment from Ver 5.0 to 6.0", p.40]* — "FDA Response dated 28th March 2017 for type C meeting Question 7: We agree that an asymptotic log-rank test instead of a permutation based log-rank test can be used as the primary analysis method. You may keep the permutation based log-rank test as a secondary analysis method... For primary endpoint, analysis method has changed to stratified log-rank test from the log-rank based permutation test."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, BLA 761149, p.9-10]* — "A stratified log-rank test using randomization strata of baseline ARR (one vs. more than one) and geographical region (Asia and EU/Other) was to be used. Censoring was defined as the earliest day of 1) the end of double-blind period for efficacy analysis, 2) switching or increasing the baseline treatment, or 3) receiving rescue therapy for clinical relapse... In addition, estimates of the treatment effect was to be expressed as hazard ratio and 95% CIs using a stratified Cox proportional-hazards model with the same strata as used in the log-rank test."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, p.13-14]* — SAkuraSky results: "Treatment difference in the primary endpoint of time to first PDR in the double-blind period reached statistical significance with a p-value of 0.0184 from the log-rank test. Treatment with satralizumab led to a 62% reduction in the risk of experiencing a PDR compared to placebo from the Cox regression model" — hazard ratio 0.38 (95% CI 0.16, 0.88).

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, p.21-22]* — SAkuraStar results: "Treatment difference in the primary endpoint of time to first PDR in the DB period reached statistical significance with a p-value of 0.0184 from the log-rank test. Treatment with satralizumab led to a 55% reduction in the risk of experiencing a protocol-defined relapse compared to placebo from the Cox regression model" — hazard ratio 0.45 (95% CI 0.23, 0.89).

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §4.2 "Other Special/Subgroup Populations", p.26]* — "It appeared that satralizumab might only be effective in patients with AQP4 positive. In the monotherapy study BN40900, the estimated hazard ratio of satralizumab/placebo was greater than 1 in patients whose AQP4 Status was negative." Reported AQP4-positive subgroup HRs: 0.21 (95% CI 0.06, 0.75), nominal p=0.0086 (SAkuraSky) and 0.26 (95% CI 0.11, 0.63), nominal p=0.0014 (SAkuraStar); AQP4-negative subgroup HRs: 0.66 (95% CI 0.20, 2.24), p=0.5047 (SAkuraSky) and 1.19 (95% CI 0.30, 4.78), p=0.8036 (SAkuraStar).

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §5.1 "Statistical Issues" / §5.3 "Conclusions and Recommendations", p.27-28]* — "The availability of fibrinogen data and attempts to use these data for efficacy purpose allowed for a highly accurate prediction of treatment assignments to patients and estimations of HR... It is almost certain that such attempts had serious impact on the trial conduct. It is inconceivable that the sample size adjustment and change in the end of the study were not influenced by the knowledge of the effect of fibrinogen and estimation of HR... Under the original protocol with 70 patients and 19 relapses events to end the study, the trial would have failed to show drug effect with HR=0.58 and p-value of 0.2413."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Appendix, p.28-29]* — "In May 2017, fibrinogen concentration data was used by two Chugai clinical science members to try to assume treatment assignment for the SA-307JG and SA-309JG studies. Individual treatment assignment assumptions were made based on the observed fibrinogen changes: when a clear decrease in fibrinogen levels was observed, it was assumed that the patient was treated with satralizumab... Once informed of this activity in July 2017, Roche... raised concerns and Chugai started to investigate the potential scope of the issue. It was found in this initial investigation that a previous attempt to assume treatment assignment and calculation of HR occurred during November 2015."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, BLA 761149, p.10-11]* — "The applicant performed an analysis using just fibrinogen serum levels (as the unauthorized team members had done) and found that serum fibrinogen values available at the times of these efficacy interim assessments predicted treatment assignment 73.3%-100%... However, analyses of data collection sensitive to bias such as EDSS and the secondary outcome measure assessments revealed no differences in data collected before and after the two internal unblinding events. The biometrics reviewer agreed with the applicant's numerical analyses to assess bias and that the integrity of the primary and secondary outcome scores... appeared intact and free of obvious bias despite the internal unblinding attempts." The same section notes an SPA amendment (submitted March 9, 2016, after the first unblinding attempt) increased SAkuraStar's target sample size/event count, without which "the study's primary outcome analysis using data available at this time would have failed to show a treatment effect (hazard ratio=0.58 and p-value of 0.2413)" — FDA states it "could not conclude definitively whether the protocol change had been in direct response to the internal unblinding attempts but did note there were other plausible reasons."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, p.2-3]* — "Two adequate and well-controlled studies (Studies 307JG and 309JG) provided substantial evidence that satralizumab-mwge is an effective treatment of NMOSD in adult patients who are anti-AQP4 antibody positive. These studies' findings did not support a conclusion that satralizumab-mwge is an effective treatment for patients with NMOSD who were anti-AQP4 antibody negative."

### 51. Serdexmethylphenidate/dexmethylphenidate (Azstarys) — NDA 212994

**Sponsor:** Corium, Inc. (developed under the KP415 program; marketed by KemPharm/Corium and Highland Therapeutics)

**Indication approved:** Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in patients 6 years of age and older

**Approval date:** March 2, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** KP415.E01, NCT03292952

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, laboratory classroom study; sequential open-label dose-optimization phase followed by double-blind randomized withdrawal-style comparison on a single analog-classroom assessment day
- *Endpoints:* SKAMP-C (Swanson, Kotkin, Agler, M-Flynn, and Pelham rating scale, combined score) average change from baseline across postdose time points on the laboratory classroom day (primary); onset and duration of effect derived from time-point-level SKAMP-C changes (secondary, not prespecified as key secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* mixed-effect model repeated measures (MMRM) with time, treatment, time-by-treatment interaction, and site as fixed effects and baseline SKAMP-C as covariate
- *Regulatory:* FDA rejected a sponsor-proposed post-hoc change to the primary-endpoint baseline definition made after unblinding; FDA also identified an unauthorized change in covariance structure (unstructured to Toeplitz) introduced in a late SAP amendment without the Agency's awareness

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study KP415.E01: multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group Phase 3 laboratory classroom study in children 6-12 years old with DSM-5 ADHD; 155 patients entered a 3-week open-label dose-optimization phase, followed by randomization (74 KP415, 76 placebo) to a 1-week double-blind phase ending in a single laboratory classroom assessment day (Day 28)
- Primary endpoint (per Protocol Amendment #2): difference between KP415 and placebo in the average of the mean changes from baseline in SKAMP-C across all postdose time points on the classroom day; protocol-specified baseline was the predose SKAMP-C score at Day 21 (the randomization/practice classroom visit); intent-to-treat population = all randomized patients who received ≥1 dose of double-blind medication with ≥1 postdose SKAMP-C assessment on Day 28
- Sample size: 126 subjects calculated for 80% power to detect a 0.5-point minimum clinically important difference (SD=1) at two-sided alpha=0.05; inflated to a target of 176 subjects for anticipated dropout (20% in open-label, 10% in double-blind phase)
- Primary analysis: MMRM with time, treatment, time-by-treatment interaction, and site as fixed effects, baseline (Day 21 predose) SKAMP-C as covariate, subject as random effect, and a Toeplitz covariance structure (per the sponsor's final SAP amendment); if the primary endpoint was significant, the same MMRM was used to generate secondary time-point-level analyses (unadjusted p-values, no formal multiplicity control across time points)
- Central regulatory dispute: after unblinding, the sponsor requested the Agency accept a post-hoc reanalysis redefining baseline as the Day 28 predose (classroom-day) score rather than the protocol-specified Day 21 score, arguing the original SAP was "flawed." The change would have increased the treatment effect by ~2 points and extended the estimated onset/duration of effect. FDA's clinical reviewer explicitly rejected this, calling the post-hoc analysis "inconsistent with good scientific principles and unacceptable despite the Applicant's explanations," noting the Agency had asked about the baseline choice before the study started and the sponsor had not responded, and that the 2-day end-of-optimization washout showed the Day 21 baseline was the deliberate original design choice, not an oversight. FDA additionally flagged that the covariance structure had been changed from unstructured to Toeplitz in a late SAP amendment submitted inside an unrelated meeting package, without the division's awareness that the change had occurred; the statistical reviewer re-ran the analysis under the original unstructured specification and found materially unchanged conclusions
- No formal AdCom; per the Multi-Disciplinary Review, "No advisory committee meeting or other external consultations were deemed to be necessary"

- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (contains Statistical, Clinical, and Regulatory review sections) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/212994Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf

"A Randomized, Controlled Laboratory Classroom Study of Serdexmethylphenidate and d-Methylphenidate Capsules in Children with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder." *J Child Adolesc Psychopharmacol.* 2021;31(9):597-606. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1089/cap.2021.0077), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34714120/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Randomized%20Controlled%20Laboratory%20Classroom%20Study%20Serdexmethylphenidate%20d-Methylphenidate)

- No sponsor-specific IPD/dataset sharing program (KemPharm/Corium/Highland) was identified; trial-specific availability not confirmed.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held for this NDA (confirmed in the Multi-Discipline Review, Section 9).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 212994, p.70]* — "According to the Amendment #2 of the protocol for Study KP415.E01, the primary efficacy endpoint was the difference between KP415 and placebo in the average of the mean changes from baseline in the [SKAMP-C] combined score across all postdose time points on the classroom day (Day 28). The protocol defined baseline as the predose score on Day 21 and the intent-to-treat population as all randomized patients who received at least one dose of double-blind study medication and have at least one post-dose SKAMP-C assessment on Day 28."

*[verbatim, p.71]* — "The estimate of the difference between KP415 and placebo on the primary endpoint was based on a repeated measures analysis using a mixed-effect model repeated measure (MMRM) model where: Time, treatment, the interaction of time and treatment, and site were fixed effects; Baseline SKAMP-C score (predose Visit 5 (Day 21)) was included as covariate; Subject was the random effect. The Toeplitz covariance structure was specified."

*[verbatim, p.71]* — reviewer's note on the undisclosed covariance-structure change: "In eCTD 11 the Agency asked the Applicant to use the unstructured covariance matrix. In eCTD 37 the Applicant pre-specified un. However, the Applicant changed from un to Toeplitz in eCTD 49. The Agency was not aware that it was changed to Toeplitz in this last SAP amendment embedded in a meeting package."

*[verbatim, p.70]* — on the post-hoc baseline dispute: "They felt that, in retrospect, the SAP was flawed in that the Day 28 predose assessment should have served as the baseline for computing changes to estimate onset and duration of effect... I consider the use of the post-hoc analysis that was proposed after study completion and data unblinding to be inconsistent with good scientific principles and unacceptable despite the Applicant's explanations."

*[verbatim, p.78, Table 26]* — primary result under the protocol-specified (Day 21) baseline: LS mean of average change from baseline, SDX/d-MPH -4.87 vs. placebo 0.54, treatment difference -5.4 (95% CI -7.1, -3.7), p<0.001.

### 52. Ponesimod (Ponvory) — NDA 213498

**Sponsor:** Janssen Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Actelion Pharmaceuticals, a Janssen/Johnson & Johnson company)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS), to include clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting disease, and active secondary progressive disease, in adults

**Approval date:** March 18, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** OPTIMUM (Study B301/AC-058B301), NCT02425644

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled (teriflunomide), parallel-group superiority trial, stratified by baseline EDSS and recent disease-modifying therapy use
- *Endpoints:* annualized relapse rate (ARR) to end of study (primary); change from baseline in FSIQ-RMS fatigue score, cumulative number of combined unique active lesions (CUAL), time to 12-week and 24-week confirmed disability accumulation (CDA) (key secondary, hierarchically ordered)
- *Primary analysis:* negative binomial regression (treatment, EDSS stratum, prior-DMT stratum, prior-year relapse count, log-time offset)
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence gatekeeping with alpha-splitting/reallocation across three parallel first-rank secondary endpoints, then passed to a final sequential endpoint only if the prior step succeeded (fallback-type hierarchical procedure) ("fallback-type multiplicity procedure with alpha-splitting across parallel secondaries")
- *Missing data/bias:* prespecified tipping-point sensitivity analyses via reference-based and delta-adjusted multiple imputation of post-withdrawal relapse rates

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled, parallel-group Phase 3 superiority study in adults with relapsing MS; 1133 subjects randomized 1:1 to ponesimod 20 mg or teriflunomide 14 mg over a 108-week treatment period, stratified by MS disease-modifying treatment use in the prior 2 years (yes/no) and baseline EDSS (≤3.5 vs. >3.5)
- Primary endpoint: annualized relapse rate (ARR) to end of study, defined as confirmed relapses per subject-year, with relapse confirmation requiring the treating neurologist's assessment plus an EDSS/Functional System score increase from an independent efficacy assessor
- Key secondary endpoints (in fixed testing order): change from baseline to Week 108 in FSIQ-RMS fatigue symptom score; cumulative number of combined unique active lesions (CUAL, new Gd+ T1 plus new/enlarging T2 lesions) at Weeks 60/108; time to 12-week confirmed disability accumulation (CDA); time to 24-week CDA
- Analysis population: Full Analysis Set (all randomized subjects)
- Primary analysis: negative binomial regression on confirmed relapses to end of study, with treatment, the two binary stratification factors, and prior-year relapse count (≤1/missing vs. ≥2) as covariates and log-time-on-study as an offset
- Multiplicity control: primary endpoint tested at full alpha; if rejected, alpha split evenly (1/3 each) among the three parallel first-rank secondary endpoints (fatigue, CUAL, 12-week CDA); alpha preserved from any endpoint that failed was passed forward within that sequence, and the summed alpha carried to 24-week CDA only if 12-week CDA succeeded
- Sensitivity analyses for missing/censored relapse data: missing-at-random multiple imputation (post-withdrawal rate = pre-withdrawal rate in the same arm); reference-based imputation (post-withdrawal rate in both arms imputed using the teriflunomide-arm rate); and a delta-adjustment tipping-point analysis multiplying assumed post-withdrawal rates by factors from 0.1 to 3.1 in each arm separately
- Result: ponesimod produced a 30.5% relative reduction in ARR vs. teriflunomide (adjusted ARR 0.202 vs. 0.290, rate ratio 0.695, p=0.0003); CUAL reduced 56% (new/enlarging T2 lesions, rate ratio 0.443, p<0.0001) and 58% (new Gd+ T1 lesions, rate ratio 0.415, p<0.0001) using MRI-derived offsets; fatigue (FSIQ-RMS) significantly improved; both CDA endpoints were numerically favorable but not statistically significant (12-week CDA hazard ratio 0.83, 95% CI 0.58-1.18, p=0.2939; 24-week CDA not formally tested per the hierarchy but reported nominal HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.57-1.24, p=0.3720)

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2021/213498s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/213498Orig1s000StatR.pdf

"Ponesimod Compared With Teriflunomide in Patients With Relapsing Multiple Sclerosis in the Active-Comparator Phase 3 OPTIMUM Study: A Randomized Clinical Trial." *JAMA Neurol.* 2021;78(5):558-567. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1001/jamaneurol.2021.0405), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33779698/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Ponesimod%20Compared%20With%20Teriflunomide%20Relapsing%20Multiple%20Sclerosis%20OPTIMUM)

**Other resources**

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 213498, p.5-6]* — "The B301 study evaluated the efficacy and safety of ponesimod 20 mg versus teriflunomide 14 mg, with Annualized Relapse Rate (ARR) as primary endpoint over a 108-week treatment period... A total of 1133 subjects were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to two groups: ponesimod 20 mg or teriflunomide 14 mg, stratified by use of multiple sclerosis (MS) disease-modifying treatment (DMT) in the last two years prior to randomization (yes, no) and by baseline Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) score (≤ 3.5, > 3.5)."

*[verbatim, p.6]* — "The testing strategy started with testing the primary endpoint at full alpha, followed hierarchically by a fallback type procedure for the secondary endpoints. If the primary endpoint null hypothesis was rejected, the alpha would be split evenly (1/3 of alpha) among the following 3 secondary endpoints: Fatigue, CUALs and 12-week CDA. If a secondary endpoint listed as part of the fallback procedure above was successful, the preserved alpha in the sequence was passed along to the next secondary endpoint in the sequence and the summed alpha was used for testing that endpoint."

*[verbatim, p.6]* — "The primary statistical analysis was performed based on the FAS using a negative binomial (NB) regression model for confirmed relapses up to EOS, with treatment as a factor and the binary stratification variables... and the number of relapses in the year prior to study entry... included in the model. The model also included an offset variable defined as the log of time on study (in years) from randomization up to EOS."

*[verbatim, p.7]* — missing-data sensitivity analyses: "Reference-based MI approaches: The rate in the reference (teriflunomide 14 mg) arm was used for imputation in both the ponesimod and teriflunomide arms. Delta adjustment MI approach: the rate after withdrawal was multiplied by δP, ranging from 1 (MAR...) to 3.1 (~tripling of relapse rate)... for the ponesimod arm, and by δT, ranging from 0.1 (relapse rate reduced by 90%) over 1 to 3.1... for the teriflunomide arm."

*[verbatim, p.13]* — key result: "Patients treated with ponesimod had a 30.5% relative reduction in ARR, compared to patients on teriflunomide (p =0.0003). The adjusted ARR was 0.202 and 0.290 in the ponesimod and [teriflunomide] group[s]..."
