### 53. Viloxazine (Qelbree) — NDA 211964

**Sponsor:** Supernus Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in pediatric patients 6 to 17 years of age

**Approval date:** April 2, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** Four Phase 3 trials — Study 301/NCT03247530 (children, low dose), Study 302/NCT03247543 (children, high dose), Study 303/NCT03247556 (adolescents, high dose), and Study 304/NCT03247517-family (dose-ranging trial that did not meet its primary endpoint after multiplicity adjustment)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* four independent randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, fixed-dose, parallel-group trials, each with a prespecified high-to-low dose testing hierarchy
- *Endpoints:* change from baseline to end-of-study (Week 6-8) in ADHD-RS-5 total score (primary, all four trials); CGI-I, Conners 3-Parent Composite T-score, and WFIRS-P total average score (key secondary, hierarchically tested)
- *Primary analysis:* mixed-effect model repeated measures (MMRM) with baseline ADHD-RS-5, age-group category, treatment, visit, and treatment-by-visit interaction as fixed effects
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (highest-to-lowest dose) hierarchical testing applied separately within each trial to both the primary endpoint and its own secondary-endpoint hierarchy
- *Missing data/bias:* MMRM assumed missing-at-random; multiple imputation under a missing-not-at-random mechanism used as a prespecified sensitivity analysis
- *Regulatory:* one of the four identically-structured pivotal trials (Study 304) failed to demonstrate a statistically significant treatment effect once the prespecified high-to-low dose sequential testing procedure was applied, despite a nominally significant p-value at the lower dose — illustrating how a fixed-sequence gatekeeping procedure can nullify a nominally positive result when the higher dose in the hierarchy fails first

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Four multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, fixed-dose Phase 3 trials in patients with DSM-5 ADHD (confirmed via the Mini International Neuropsychiatric Interview for Children and Adolescents), each with a baseline ADHD-RS-5 score ≥28 and CGI-S ≥4: Study 301 (children 6-11, viloxazine ER 100/200 mg/day, N=104/arm, placebo N=155); Study 302 (children 6-11, 200/400 mg/day, N≈94-104/arm); Study 303 (adolescents 12-17, 200/400 mg/day, N≈97-107/arm); Study 304 (400/600 mg/day, N≈96-99/arm)
- Primary endpoint (all four trials): change from baseline to end of study (Week 6 for 301/302, Week 8 for 303, Week 7 for 304) in ADHD-RS-5 total score, intent-to-treat population
- Key secondary endpoints, tested only if the primary endpoint hierarchy succeeded: CGI-I at end of study; change from baseline in the Conners 3-Parent Report Composite T-score; change from baseline in the WFIRS-P total average score — each trial applied its own high-to-low dose sequential gatekeeping within both the primary and secondary hierarchies
- Sample size: each trial powered (approximately 90% power, two-sided alpha=0.05, two-sample t-test) using an effect size (~0.45) estimated from a completed Phase 2b dose-finding study; Study 301 targeted 432 randomized subjects (144/arm) to allow for ~28% attrition
- Primary analysis: MMRM modeling change from baseline in ADHD-RS-5 with baseline score, age-group category, treatment, visit, and treatment-by-visit interaction as fixed effects, restricted maximum likelihood estimation, unstructured covariance matrix, and Kenward-Roger denominator degrees-of-freedom approximation; MMRM assumes a missing-at-random mechanism, with a prespecified multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis under a missing-not-at-random assumption
- Results: Study 301 — 100 mg/day LS-mean difference -5.8 (p=0.0004), 200 mg/day -6.9 (p<0.0001), both significant. Study 302 — 200 mg/day -4.5 (p=0.0232), 400 mg/day -5.1 (p=0.0091), both significant after multiplicity adjustment. Study 303 — 200 mg/day -6.0 (p=0.0063 adjusted), 400 mg/day -5.8 (p=0.0063 adjusted), both significant. Study 304 — 400 mg/day -5.1 (nominal p=0.0082) and 600 mg/day -3.5 (nominal p=0.071); because the hierarchy tested the higher dose (600 mg) first and it failed to reach significance (adjusted p=0.071), the lower dose's nominally significant result was not declared statistically significant under the prespecified sequential procedure — the FDA Integrated Review states plainly that a "similar hierarchy was used for the secondary endpoints" and confirms the multiplicity-adjusted, non-significant conclusion for Study 304 overall
- Only Studies 301, 302, and 303 supported the approved pediatric (6-17) indication; the FDA Integrated Review's efficacy discussion is explicit that the sequential (fixed-sequence dose) testing procedure was applied "in all four trials," and Study 304 is the one of the four in which the prespecified hierarchy was not satisfied

### 54. Olanzapine/samidorphan (Lybalvi) — NDA 213378

**Sponsor:** Alkermes, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of schizophrenia; treatment of bipolar I disorder, as monotherapy or as adjunct to lithium or valproate, for acute treatment of manic or mixed episodes and maintenance treatment, in adults

**Approval date:** May 28, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** ENLIGHTEN-1 (Study ALK3831-A305), NCT02634346 (antipsychotic-efficacy trial); ENLIGHTEN-2 (Study ALK3831-A303), NCT02694328 (weight-mitigation trial)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two independent randomized, double-blind, multi-arm trials — ENLIGHTEN-1 (4-week, placebo- and active-referenced efficacy trial in acute schizophrenia exacerbation) and ENLIGHTEN-2 (24-week, active(olanzapine)-controlled weight-comparison trial, U.S. sites only)
- *Endpoints:* PANSS total score change from baseline to Week 4 (ENLIGHTEN-1 primary); percent body-weight change from baseline to Week 24 and proportion with ≥10% weight gain (ENLIGHTEN-2 co-primary endpoints)
- *Primary analysis:* MMRM for PANSS (ENLIGHTEN-1); Cui-Hung-Wang (CHW) adaptive test statistic combining data before and after a blinded sample-size re-estimation for both co-primary endpoints (ENLIGHTEN-2) ("Cui-Hung-Wang (CHW) combination test for adaptive sample-size re-estimation")
- *Multiplicity:* co-primary endpoint requirement (both weight endpoints in ENLIGHTEN-2 had to be statistically significant) combined with the CHW-adjusted testing to control type I error after the sample-size increase
- *Regulatory:* joint FDA Psychopharmacologic Drugs / Drug Safety and Risk Management Advisory Committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ENLIGHTEN-1 (Study A305): 4-week, randomized, double-blind trial in adults with acute exacerbation of schizophrenia, comparing ALKS 3831 (olanzapine/samidorphan) to olanzapine alone and placebo; N=401 randomized (88% completed); primary endpoint was change from baseline to Week 4 in PANSS total score. This trial was designed to demonstrate that samidorphan does not meaningfully impair olanzapine's antipsychotic efficacy, relying on a prior FDA finding of efficacy for olanzapine itself (NDA 020592) rather than a formal non-inferiority margin ("although a non-inferiority (NI) design would not be [used]," per the FDA review, the trial instead assessed whether ALKS 3831 and olanzapine each separately beat placebo)
- Result: ALKS 3831 LS-mean PANSS improvement vs. placebo of -6.4 (SE 1.8, 95% CI -10.0 to -2.8, p<0.001); olanzapine alone vs. placebo -5.3 (SE 1.8, 95% CI -8.9 to -1.7, p=0.004) — comparable magnitude, supporting no meaningful efficacy impairment from samidorphan
- ENLIGHTEN-2 (Study A303): 24-week, multicenter (U.S.-only), randomized, double-blind, olanzapine-controlled trial in adults with schizophrenia designed specifically to demonstrate weight-mitigation; 561 subjects randomized 1:1 to ALKS 3831 or olanzapine alone; co-primary endpoints: (1) percent change from baseline in body weight and (2) proportion of subjects with ≥10% weight gain from baseline, both at Week 24; key secondary endpoint: proportion gaining ≥7% weight
- Adaptive design: the sponsor pre-specified a blinded sample-size re-estimation and increased the target enrollment from 400 (200/arm) to 540 (270/arm); to preserve the overall type I error rate after this increase, the Cui, Hung, and Wang (CHW) test statistic was pre-specified to combine information from before and after the re-estimation and derive the p-values for both co-primary endpoints
- Results: mean percent weight change from baseline significantly lower with ALKS 3831 than olanzapine (CHW test p=0.003; treatment difference -2.38%, 95% CI -3.88% to -0.88%); proportion gaining ≥10% weight significantly lower with ALKS 3831 (17.8% vs. 29.8-29.9%, odds ratio 0.50, 95% CI 0.31-0.80, CHW test p=0.003); waist circumference (a prespecified secondary endpoint) also favored ALKS 3831
- First review cycle ended in a Complete Response Letter for chemistry-manufacturing-and-controls (CMC) deficiencies, not efficacy or safety; approval followed CMC resolution

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.4088/JCP.19m12769), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32141723/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Efficacy%20Safety%20Combination%20Olanzapine%20Samidorphan%20ENLIGHTEN-1)

Vote 2 (adequately characterized safety profile): 13 Yes, 3 No, 1 Abstain. Vote 3 (is labeling sufficient to mitigate opioid-antagonist risks): 11 Yes, 6 No, 0 Abstain.

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Advisory Committee Section]* — Vote question: "Has the Applicant presented adequate evidence that samidorphan meaningfully mitigates olanzapine-associated weight gain? Result: 16 Yes, 1 No, 0 Abstain."

### 55. Aducanumab-avwa (Aduhelm) — BLA 761178

**Sponsor:** Biogen, Inc. (co-developed with Eisai)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of Alzheimer's disease, approved under accelerated approval based on reduction of amyloid beta plaques observed in treated patients; continued approval contingent on verification of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial

**Approval date:** June 7, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** Two identically-designed Phase 3 trials, both terminated early for futility — ENGAGE (Study 221AD301), NCT02477800, and EMERGE (Study 221AD302), NCT02484547; supportive Phase 1b Study 221AD103 (PRIME)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two identical randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 3-arm (placebo/low-dose/high-dose), APOE ε4-genotype-stratified dose trials in early (MCI-due-to-AD/mild dementia) Alzheimer's disease; both stopped early per a pre-specified futility rule based on interim conditional power; blinded sample-size re-estimation
- *Endpoints:* CDR-SB (Clinical Dementia Rating Scale-Sum of Boxes) change from baseline to Week 78 (primary); MMSE, ADAS-Cog13, ADCS-ADL-MCI (secondary); amyloid PET SUVR reduction (biomarker, basis of the accelerated-approval surrogate endpoint)
- *Primary analysis:* MMRM (treatment, categorical time, treatment-by-time, baseline CDR-SB, baseline-by-time, baseline MMSE, symptomatic-medication use, region, APOE ε4 status)
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* pre-specified futility interim analysis based on conditional power (<20% threshold in both dose groups in both trials required to declare futility); no formal alpha-spending was applied at the (unplanned) final analysis because no interim superiority analysis was conducted
- *Regulatory:* discordant twin-trial results (EMERGE nominally positive at high dose, ENGAGE negative) resolved via a sponsor-proposed post-hoc reanalysis after unblinding; Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee voted 10-0-1 (No-Yes-Uncertain) against considering EMERGE alone as primary evidence of effectiveness; FDA approved via the accelerated-approval pathway over the dissent of its own primary statistical reviewer and the Director of the Office of Biostatistics

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ENGAGE and EMERGE: identically-designed, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group Phase 3 trials (~1605 subjects each planned) in early AD (MCI due to AD or mild AD dementia, amyloid-PET or CSF confirmed); 1:1:1 randomization to placebo, low-dose, or high-dose aducanumab, stratified by APOE ε4 carrier status and site; monthly IV infusions for ~18 months (20 doses). Target high dose was originally 6 mg/kg for APOE ε4 carriers, increased to 10 mg/kg for all carriers under Protocol Version 4 (implemented mid-study, March 24, 2017) after emerging ARIA safety data allowed higher exposure; non-carriers received up to 10 mg/kg from the start
- Primary endpoint: change from baseline to Week 78 in CDR-SB (ITT population), analyzed via MMRM with treatment, categorical time, treatment-by-time interaction, baseline CDR-SB, baseline-by-time interaction, baseline MMSE, AD symptomatic medication use, region, and APOE ε4 status as fixed effects, unstructured covariance (or Toeplitz/AR(1) fallback), Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom, missing-at-random assumption
- Sample size: initially 450/arm (1350 total) for ~90% power to detect a 0.5-point CDR-SB difference (SD 1.92, two-sided alpha 0.05, 30% dropout); increased to 535/arm (1605 total) after a blinded sample-size re-estimation in November 2017 (~10.6% of primary-endpoint data available) using a modified Gould-Shih one-sample-variance method
- Interim futility rule: planned at ~50% of subjects reaching the opportunity to complete Week 78, using conditional power (probability of eventual statistical significance given interim data, assuming the future effect equals the interim maximum-likelihood estimate); both trials were declared futile (conditional power <20% in both dose groups in both trials) and publicly announced discontinued on March 21, 2019, based on the pooled interim estimate
- After the futility announcement, closeout follow-up data continued to accrue; the sponsor requested a meeting with FDA after discovering the final (unplanned) analysis showed a statistically significant high-dose effect in EMERGE (p=0.01) but not in ENGAGE (p=0.83) — a result FDA's statistical review calls "inconsistency on many levels," noting almost 50% of subjects were missing the Week 78 assessment and that "a chance worse placebo response in [EMERGE] than was observed in [ENGAGE] could explain the significance"
- The sponsor's central explanatory theory (accepted by FDA's clinical/pharmacology reviewers, rejected by the primary statistical reviewer) was that greater cumulative high-dose exposure — achieved by more EMERGE subjects reaching the Protocol Version 4 (PV4) 10 mg/kg target before the futility stop — explained EMERGE's positive result and ENGAGE's negative one; FDA's statistical reviewer (Dr. Tristan Massie) countered that the low dose was numerically better than the high dose in ENGAGE, that APOE ε4 non-carriers (who received full 10 mg/kg dosing from study start) showed less treatment effect than carriers, and that increased placebo-arm progression after PV4 could equally explain EMERGE's result
- Supportive Study 221AD103 (PRIME) was a Phase 1b, primarily safety/tolerability, dose-titration study with only exploratory efficacy endpoints; FDA's clinical/pharmacology teams treated its dose- and time-dependent amyloid-PET reduction and exploratory clinical trends as corroborative, while the statistical reviewer did not accept it as an adequate, well-controlled efficacy study
- Accelerated approval basis: FDA's Office Director (Dr. Billy Dunn/Office of Neuroscience with clinical pharmacology lead Dr. Kevin Krudys) concluded that amyloid-beta plaque reduction on PET, as demonstrated with statistical significance and a clear dose/time-response relationship across Studies 103, 301, and 302, is "reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit," meeting the accelerated-approval standard independent of whether the clinical (CDR-SB) data alone were persuasive
- November 6, 2020 Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee: Question 2 ("Does Study 302, viewed independently and without regard for Study 301, provide strong evidence that supports the effectiveness of aducanumab...?") — Yes 1, No 8, Uncertain 2. Question 4 (Study 103 as supportive evidence) — Yes 0, No 7, Uncertain 4. Question 6 (strong evidence of a pharmacodynamic/amyloid effect) — Yes 5, No 0, Uncertain 6. Question 8 (in light of all exploratory analyses, is it reasonable to consider Study 302 as primary evidence of effectiveness) — Yes 0, No 10, Uncertain 1
- FDA's primary biostatistics reviewer, Dr. Tristan Massie, did not recommend approval, concluding the totality of the data did not support efficacy given the study inconsistency, the incomplete (futility-terminated) datasets, and his exploratory finding that increased placebo-group decline after PV4 could account for EMERGE's result; the Director of the Office of Biostatistics, Dr. Sylva Collins, separately dissented from the final approval decision at an April 26, 2021 CDER Center Director briefing chaired by Dr. Patrizia Cavazzoni, stating she believed the evidence was insufficient to support accelerated or any other approval; the clinical review team (Dr. Kevin Krudys) and CDER leadership (Cavazzoni, CBER Director Peter Marks, OCE Director Rick Pazdur) ultimately supported approval via the amyloid-surrogate accelerated-approval pathway
- Required postmarketing confirmatory trial: a randomized controlled trial to verify clinical benefit was made a Postmarketing Requirement; Biogen's confirmatory Phase 3b/4 trial ENVISION (Study 221AD305, NCT05310071) was subsequently initiated but was terminated by sponsor's decision after Biogen discontinued the Aduhelm program in January 2024

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2021/761178Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2021/761178s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Statistical Review (Dr. Tristan Massie) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/761178Orig1s000StatR.pdf

- FDA Summary Review (includes Cavazzoni Center Director Briefing summary, Advisory Committee vote results, and PMR/PMC list) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/761178Orig1s000SumR.pdf

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.14283/jpad.2022.30), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35542991/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Two%20Randomized%20Phase%203%20Studies%20Aducanumab%20Early%20Alzheimer%27s%20Disease)

**Other resources**

- No Biogen-specific trial-level IPD availability was individually confirmed for ENGAGE/EMERGE; Biogen participates in general cross-industry data-sharing frameworks.

- FDA Advisory Committee: Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee, November 6, 2020 (held via teleconference); vote results detailed above. This is among the most widely reported adcom outcomes in FDA history given the near-unanimous negative vote followed by approval.

- Confirmatory trial ENVISION (NCT05310071) was terminated after Biogen's January 2024 announcement that it was discontinuing Aduhelm's development and commercialization (a business/pipeline-prioritization decision, distinct from a safety or efficacy finding); Aduhelm was formally withdrawn from the market in November 2024.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, BLA 761178, p.16-17]* — "The two phase 3 studies (study 301, study 302) were stopped early for futility (March 21, 2019 press announcement) when both studies had reached 50% completion since it was estimated based on the interim study-pooled estimate of the treatment effects that both studies individually had <20% chance of success for either dose if completed. Following a futility press release announcement and collection of subsequent study closeout follow up data, the sponsor requested a meeting to discuss the two trials final data after discovering that despite the futility conclusion, the final analysis on face showed a statistically significant effect for the high dose in one of the two trials (p=0.01) but not the other (p=0.83)."

*[verbatim, p.17]* — "Because the two phase 3 studies were terminated for futility, the NDA package doesn't contain a single phase 3 study that was fully completed according to the plan. In fact, almost 50% are missing the Week 78 time point assessment of CDRSB which is the only timepoint that shows any significance... A chance worse placebo response in study 302 than was observed in study 301 could explain the significance of study 302 (p=0.01)."

*[verbatim, p.20-21]* — "The futility decision was to primarily be based on the conditional power for the primary efficacy endpoint. The study was not to be considered as futile unless both studies 221AD301 and 221AD302 had conditional power for the primary efficacy endpoint less than 20% in both the high-dose and low-dose treatment groups."

*[verbatim, p.19]* — primary analysis specification: "A mixed model repeated measures (MMRM) model was to be used as the primary analysis to analyze change from baseline CDR-SB using fixed effects of treatment group, time (categorical), treatment group-by-time interaction, baseline CDR-SB, baseline CDR-SB by time interaction, baseline MMSE, AD symptomatic medication use at baseline (yes/no), region, and laboratory ApoE ε4 status (carrier/non-carrier)."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, p.53-54, Dr. Massie's conclusions]* — "Dr. Massie does not agree that the totality of the data provides sufficient evidence to support the efficacy of aducanumab in AD and does not recommend approval," citing "Inconsistency in the data with one positive study (302) and a second negative study (301)," incomplete Week-78 data due to early termination, and exploratory analyses suggesting "increased placebo progression post-PV4 may account for the treatment effect observed in Study 302."

*[verbatim, p.55, Advisory Committee Question 8]* — "In light of the understanding provided by the exploratory analyses of Study 301 and Study 302, along with the results of Study 103 and evidence of a pharmacodynamic effect on Alzheimer's disease pathophysiology, it is reasonable to consider Study 302 as primary evidence of effectiveness of aducanumab for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease? Vote Results: Yes: 0 No: 10 Uncertain: 1."

*[verbatim, p.56]* — on the final decision: "Dr. Sylva Collins, Director of the Office of Biostatistics (OB), dissented on the approach, stating her belief that there is insufficient evidence to support accelerated approval or any other type of approval."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, accelerated-approval rationale]* — "a surrogate outcome for which there is substantial evidence of effectiveness, reduction in amyloid beta plaques on PET imaging, has been assessed in the aducanumab development program, and is reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit, as demonstrated in the reviews discussing the relationship of amyloid plaque reduction to clinical outcome."

### 56. Atogepant (Qulipta) — NDA 215206

**Sponsor:** AbbVie, Inc. (developed by Allergan, acquired by AbbVie in 2020)

**Indication approved:** Preventive treatment of episodic migraine in adults

**Approval date:** September 28, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** ADVANCE (Study 3101-301-002), NCT03777059; supportive dose-ranging trial CGP-MD-01 (AGN-241689), NCT02848326

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multi-dose Phase 2/3 (CGP-MD-01) and Phase 3 (ADVANCE) trials in adults with episodic migraine
- *Endpoints:* change from baseline in mean monthly migraine days across the 12-week treatment period (primary); change in monthly headache days, ≥50% migraine-day responder rate, acute medication use days, and patient-reported outcome measures (MSQ, AIM-D domains) (key secondary, hierarchically tested)
- *Primary analysis:* MMRM (treatment, visit, prior-preventive-use, treatment-by-visit, baseline covariate, baseline-by-visit interaction)
- *Multiplicity:* graphical multiple-testing approach with weighted-Bonferroni alpha propagation across dose arms and endpoint hierarchies, including inter-dose alpha recycling when a dose's full hierarchy succeeded ("graphical weighted-Bonferroni alpha-recycling across dose arms")
- *Missing data/bias:* prespecified sensitivity analyses including reference-based (copy-reference) pattern-mixture imputation under a missing-not-at-random assumption

**Trial design & endpoints**

- CGP-MD-01: Phase 2/3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group dose-ranging trial testing atogepant 10, 30, 60 mg once daily and 30, 60 mg twice daily against placebo (N=178-182/arm) in adults with episodic migraine; primary endpoint (change from baseline in mean monthly migraine days across 12 weeks) was met for all five dosing regimens, with a relatively flat dose-response
- ADVANCE (Study 3101-301-002): Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial testing atogepant 10, 30, and 60 mg once daily (chosen based on CGP-MD-01's flat dose-response) against placebo (N=214-223/arm) in adults with episodic migraine (4-14 migraine days/month)
- Primary endpoint (both trials): change from baseline in mean monthly migraine days (combined migraine + probable migraine headache days) across the 12-week double-blind treatment period, modified intent-to-treat population (randomized, dosed, evaluable baseline and ≥1 evaluable postbaseline 4-week diary period)
- Secondary endpoints, in prespecified hierarchical order (ADVANCE): monthly headache days; monthly acute medication use days; ≥50% responder rate (3-month average); MSQ v2.1 Role Function-Restrictive domain; AIM-D Performance of Daily Activities domain; AIM-D Physical Impairment domain
- Primary analysis: MMRM with treatment group, visit, prior preventive-medication exposure (yes/no), and treatment-by-visit interaction as fixed categorical effects, baseline score and baseline-by-visit interaction as covariates, unstructured (or compound-symmetry fallback) covariance, Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom; sensitivity analyses included an ANCOVA on the 3-month average, MMRM restricted to double-blind-plus-follow-up data, multiple imputation within group, and a reference-based (copy-reference) pattern-mixture model under a missing-not-at-random assumption
- Multiplicity: overall alpha=0.05 controlled via a graphical approach with a weighted-Bonferroni test procedure; in ADVANCE, alpha was initially split 1/3 to each dose; within each dose, the primary endpoint was tested first, then the secondary-endpoint hierarchy; if the primary and specified secondary endpoints were rejected for one dose, a fraction of that dose's alpha was propagated to the other doses to increase their power, with a similar recycling rule in CGP-MD-01 (initial 1/2 split between QD/BID regimens, then high-to-low dose within regimen, with alpha recycling across doses/regimens upon hierarchy success)
- ADVANCE results: all three atogepant doses showed statistically significant reductions in monthly migraine days vs. placebo after multiplicity adjustment (10 mg: LSMD -1.21, 95% CI -1.78 to -0.64; 30 mg: -1.38, 95% CI -1.94 to -0.82; 60 mg: -1.72, 95% CI -2.28 to -1.15; all adjusted p<0.0001); no clear dose-response was observed, consistent with CGP-MD-01
- No formal Advisory Committee meeting; FDA's Integrated Review states the application "was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the clinical trial design was acceptable, the efficacy findings were clear, and the safety profile was acceptable for use in the intended population"

### 57. Efgartigimod alfa-fcab (Vyvgart) — BLA 761195

**Sponsor:** argenx US, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) in adult patients who are anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody positive

**Approval date:** December 17, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** ADAPT (Study ARGX-113-1704), NCT03669588

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter Phase 3 trial with a cyclical (variable-length) retreatment design based on clinical response, stratified by Japanese/non-Japanese, AChR-Ab serostatus, and concomitant immunosuppressive use
- *Endpoints:* percentage of MG-ADL responders after the first treatment cycle in the AChR-Ab seropositive population (primary), defined as a sustained ≥2-point MG-ADL reduction for ≥4 consecutive weeks; QMG responders, overall-population MG-ADL responders, time to clinically meaningful improvement, time to retreatment qualification, early responders (key secondary, hierarchically tested)
- *Primary analysis:* exact test using stratified logistic regression (baseline MG-ADL as covariate)
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence hierarchical testing of primary and secondary endpoints in prespecified order
- *Missing data/bias:* pattern-based rule classifying single intermittent missing post-onset assessments as responses unless due to disease worsening/AE; nonresponse imputation for dropouts; sensitivity analyses via CMH test and full missing-as-nonresponse imputation

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 1704 (ADAPT): multicenter (56 sites), multinational (15 countries), randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial in adults with gMG; randomization stratified by Japanese/non-Japanese status, AChR-Ab serostatus, and concomitant nonsteroidal immunosuppressive drug (NSID) use; 167 subjects enrolled (65 efgartigimod / 64 placebo in the AChR-Ab seropositive primary-analysis subset)
- Design used repeating 8-week treatment cycles (efgartigimod 10 mg/kg IV weekly x4 doses, or placebo) followed by a variable-length intertreatment cycle; retreatment in a new cycle required completion of the prior cycle, an MG-ADL score ≥5 (>50% from nonocular symptoms), and (if a prior responder) loss of response, up to a maximum of 26 weeks total
- Primary endpoint: percentage of MG-ADL responders in the AChR-Ab seropositive population after the first treatment cycle, where a responder had a ≥2-point decrease in total MG-ADL score sustained over 4 consecutive weekly visits, with onset by 1 week after the last infusion
- Analysis population: modified intent-to-treat (randomized subjects with baseline and ≥1 postbaseline MG-ADL assessment)
- Primary analysis: exact test using stratified logistic regression (stratified for Japanese/non-Japanese and NSID use, baseline MG-ADL as covariate) at two-sided alpha=0.05; sensitivity analyses used a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test and an alternative imputation treating intermittent missing data as nonresponse
- Missing/intercurrent-event handling: assessments after a new MG therapy or standard-of-care change were treated as non-response (or missing, for continuous analyses); dropouts/lost-to-follow-up prior to achieving response were treated as nonresponders; for a single intermittent missing post-onset visit in an otherwise-qualifying response window, the subject was still counted as a responder unless the missing visit was due to disease worsening or an AE; ≥2 intermittent missing post-onset visits meant the subject was counted as not achieving a sustained response regardless of cause
- Secondary endpoints tested in fixed hierarchical order: QMG responders (seropositive), MG-ADL responders (overall population, both serostatus groups), percentage of time with clinically meaningful improvement (ANCOVA), time to retreatment qualification (log-rank test), early MG-ADL responders (onset within 1-2 infusions)
- Result: MG-ADL responder rate 67.7% (efgartigimod) vs. 29.7% (placebo) in the AChR-Ab seropositive population (odds ratio 4.95, 95% CI 2.21-11.53, p<0.0001); QMG responder rate 63.1% vs. 14.1% (odds ratio 10.84, 95% CI 4.18-31.20)

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, BLA 761195, p.24]* — "The primary endpoint (MG-ADL responder) was defined as the percentage of subjects who, after the first cycle, had a decrease of ≥2 points on the total MG-ADL score (compared to the baseline of the first cycle (C1B)) for at least 4 consecutive weeks (i.e., the next 4 consecutive visits after onset) with the first of these decreases occurring, at the latest, 1 week after the last infusion of the investigational medicinal product (IMP) in AChR-Ab seropositive subjects."

*[verbatim, p.25]* — "The primary endpoint and secondary endpoints were tested in a hierarchical order as listed above to control the type I error. The primary endpoint of MG-ADL responder was analyzed with an exact test (using logistic regression) at the 2-sided 5% significance level in the AChR-Ab seropositive subjects, stratified for the stratification factors... and by using the baseline MG-ADL total score as a covariate."

*[verbatim, p.25]* — missing-data rule: "For intermittent missing data at only 1 of 4 post-onset (O) consecutive analysis windows, if the missing data followed one of four score patterns (OmXXX, OXmXX, OXXmX or OXXXmX), then the subject was considered as having achieved an MG-ADL response, providing that the missing data 'm' was not due to MG disease worsening or an adverse event (AE)... For intermittent missing data following onset of response at ≥2 of 4 consecutive post-onset analysis windows, the subject was considered as not having achieved a sustained response regardless of the reason for missing data."

*[verbatim, p.29]* — key result: "A statistically significantly higher percentage of MG-ADL responders was observed in the efgartigimod group (67.7%) compared to the placebo group (29.7%) during cycle 1 in the AChR-Ab seropositive population (odds ratio [OR] =4.95, p<0.0001)... Results from the prespecified sensitivity analyses are consistent with the primary analysis."

### 58. Daridorexant (Quviviq) — NDA 214985

**Sponsor:** Idorsia Pharmaceuticals US Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of insomnia, characterized by difficulties with sleep onset and/or sleep maintenance, in adults

**Approval date:** January 7, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** Two identical Phase 3 trials — Study ID-078A301, NCT03545191, and Study ID-078A302, NCT03575104

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two identical randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, polysomnography-confirmed Phase 3 trials in adult and elderly patients with DSM-5 insomnia disorder, each testing two fixed doses vs. placebo
- *Endpoints:* wake after sleep onset (WASO) and latency to persistent sleep (LPS) at Month 1 and Month 3, each dose vs. placebo — 8 co-primary hypotheses per trial (primary); subjective total sleep time (sTST) and IDSIQ sleepiness domain score at Month 1/3, same dose comparisons — 8 key secondary hypotheses (secondary)
- *Primary analysis:* longitudinal mixed-effects (MMRM-type) model with treatment-policy handling of intercurrent events
- *Multiplicity:* combination of Bonferroni allocation and a graphical multiple-testing procedure across 16 primary/secondary null hypotheses per trial (dose x endpoint x timepoint x domain)
- *Missing data/bias:* jump-to-reference multiple imputation and tipping-point sensitivity analyses (shift parameters 0-60 minutes) to probe departures from the missing-at-random assumption

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Two identically-designed, multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, polysomnography (PSG) trials in adults (18 to <65) and elderly (≥65) patients with DSM-5 insomnia disorder, corroborated at screening by 2-night in-lab PSG thresholds (mean LPS ≥20 min, mean WASO ≥30 min, mean TST <420 min) plus a self-reported Insomnia Severity Index ≥15; Trial ID-078A301 tested daridorexant 50 mg (high dose) and 25 mg (low dose) vs. placebo; Trial ID-078A302 tested 25 mg (high dose) and 10 mg (low dose) vs. placebo
- Co-primary endpoints: change from baseline in WASO and LPS (via 2-night PSG) at Month 1 and Month 3, for each dose vs. placebo — 8 primary null hypotheses per trial; secondary endpoints: sTST and IDSIQ sleepiness domain score at the same doses/timepoints — 8 secondary null hypotheses per trial
- Multiplicity control: type I error across all 16 primary and secondary null hypotheses per trial was controlled using a combination of Bonferroni allocation and a graphical multiple-testing method (prespecified in the protocol, illustrated in a graphical hypothesis-testing diagram); FDA's statistical reviewer found "the Applicant's proposed multiple comparison procedure is acceptable to control type I error"
- Primary analysis: longitudinal (linear mixed-effects/MMRM-type) model for change from baseline in WASO, LPS, sTST, and IDSIQ separately, using all available data regardless of intercurrent events (treatment-policy estimand), adjusting for baseline value, age group (<65/≥65), treatment, timepoint, and treatment-by-time and baseline-by-time interactions, with an unstructured covariance matrix (missing-at-random assumption)
- Sensitivity analyses for departures from MAR: (1) jump-to-reference multiple imputation (discontinuers assumed to follow the placebo-arm completer trajectory going forward); (2) tipping-point analysis using multiple imputation with an assumed fixed mean shift (0 to 60 minutes) applied to the completer trajectory for dropouts
- Results: for WASO, both the 25 mg and 50 mg doses were statistically significant vs. placebo in both trials at Month 1 and Month 3, with a clear dose-response; for LPS, both doses were significant in Trial ID-078A301, but the 25 mg (high) dose in Trial ID-078A302 was a "near miss" under the primary linear model (supported post hoc by a model FDA judged more suitable to the observed, non-normally-distributed LPS data); using the American Academy of Sleep Medicine's expert-consensus clinically-meaningful-difference thresholds (WASO ≥20 min, LPS ≥10 min vs. placebo), only the 50 mg dose met the threshold consistently across both trials and timepoints
- No formal Advisory Committee meeting; the Integrated Review states "An advisory committee was not held during this marketing application review. This drug is not [a novel mechanism requiring one]" (orexin-receptor antagonist class, with two prior approved members)

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2022/214985s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Integrated Review (combined Multi-Discipline Review) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/214985Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf

"Safety and efficacy of daridorexant in patients with insomnia disorder: results from two multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trials." *Lancet Neurol.* 2022;21(2):125-139. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1474-4422(21)00436-1>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35065036/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Safety%20efficacy%20daridorexant%20insomnia%20disorder%20two%20multicentre%20phase%203%20trials)

The primary endpoints consisted of WASO and LPS at both the high dose... and the low dose... at Month 1 and Month 3... The Applicant controlled Type I error rate over these 16 endpoints using a combination of Bonferroni and a graphical method."

*[verbatim, p.32]* — "Statistical Reviewer Comment: The Applicant's proposed multiple comparison procedure is acceptable to control type I error. The main analysis was performed using the full analysis set. A longitudinal data analysis method (i.e., linear mixed effects model) was used for the analysis of change from baseline in WASO, LPS, sTST, and IDSIQ scores, separately. All available data, regardless of occurrence of intercurrent events... was included in the model."

*[verbatim, p.32]* — sensitivity analyses: "Jump-to-reference: a multiple imputation sensitivity analysis in which patients who discontinue study treatment are assumed to have the same mean trajectory as patients who complete the study in the placebo arm. Tipping point analysis: multiple imputation analyses are conducted in which patients who drop out are assumed to follow a trajectory similar to the completers but with a fixed shift in the mean trajectory... The Applicant explored shift parameters from 0 to 60 minutes."

*[verbatim, p.54]* — key result: "the 50-mg dose produced numerically superior efficacy to the 25-mg dose and superiority to placebo, whereas the 25-mg dose demonstrated numerically superior efficacy to the 10-mg dose and statistically significant superiority to placebo on WASO in both Trial ID-078A301 and ID-078A302 and superiority to placebo on LPS in Trial ID-078A301, with a near miss in Trial ID-078A302."

### 59. Sodium phenylbutyrate/taurursodiol (Relyvrio) — NDA 216660

**Sponsor:** Amylyx Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) in adults — **voluntarily withdrawn from the U.S. and Canadian markets by the sponsor in April 2024** after the confirmatory trial failed; this entry documents the approval-era SAP/regulatory record

**Approval date:** September 29, 2022 (withdrawn April 4, 2024)

**Pivotal trial:** CENTAUR (Study AMX3500), NCT03127514 (single Phase 2 trial, plus open-label extension AMX3500OLE); confirmatory Phase 3 trial PHOENIX (Study A35-004), NCT05021536, failed in March 2024

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single Phase 2, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (24-week double-blind phase) with optional long-term open-label extension; approval supported by one trial rather than the customary two
- *Endpoints:* rate of decline (slope) of ALSFRS-R total score over 24 weeks (primary, prespecified); post hoc joint-rank analysis of survival and ALSFRS-R change (proposed by FDA before the trial, executed as post hoc by the sponsor after unblinding)
- *Primary analysis:* shared-baseline linear mixed-effects (slope) model, with a prespecified linearity check (quadratic time term) and FDA statistical reviewer sensitivity analyses (Mean-by-Visit MMRM; joint rank analysis with multiple imputation under missing-at-random for missing ALSFRS-R; single-site-removal influence analysis)
- *Multiplicity:* fixed hierarchical (gatekeeping) order across primary, secondary, and exploratory endpoints, all analyzed with the same statistical model
- *Missing data/bias:* sponsor's post hoc joint rank analysis used last-observation-carried-forward for post-death/missing ALSFRS-R; FDA's statistical reviewer's preferred version instead used multiple imputation under missing-at-random, which reduced statistical significance (p=0.079 vs. sponsor's p=0.03)
- *Regulatory:* two FDA Advisory Committee meetings on the same application, with opposite outcomes (March 30, 2022: 6 No / 4 Yes on effectiveness; September 7, 2022, after new data: 7 Yes / 2 No); approval followed the second, more favorable vote; confirmatory Phase 3 trial (PHOENIX) subsequently failed, leading to voluntary market withdrawal ("advisory committee reversal following resubmission with expanded survival data")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- CENTAUR (Study AMX3500): Phase 2, randomized (2:1 drug:placebo), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 137 adults with ALS (89 drug, 48 placebo) within ≤18 months of symptom onset and slow vital capacity >60% predicted; 24-week double-blind treatment phase followed by an optional open-label extension (AMX3500OLE, up to 132 weeks, primarily for long-term safety) and post hoc long-term survival follow-up
- Primary endpoint: rate of decline (slope) in total ALSFRS-R score over the 24-week double-blind period, analyzed via a shared-baseline linear mixed-effects model; the SAP prespecified a linearity check (adding quadratic time terms; if non-significant at p>0.10, the linear model was retained)
- FDA had recommended, before the trial (at the pre-IND meeting and via a March 2019 SAP-review advice email), that the sponsor instead use a combined function-and-survival analysis (e.g., a joint rank analysis) as the primary analysis, on the grounds that deaths during the double-blind period are not missing-at-random and that a pure ALSFRS-R slope analysis ignoring deaths could be biased; the sponsor did not adopt this advice prospectively
- Primary result: statistically significant slowing of ALSFRS-R decline (p=0.034), estimated LS-mean ALSFRS-R total score 2.32 points higher than placebo at Week 24
- FDA statistical reviewer sensitivity findings that complicated interpretation: (1) a Mean-by-Visit MMRM model (not reliant on the linearity assumption, also not incorporating deaths) found a non-significant Week-24 treatment difference of 1.86 points (SE 1.04, p=0.0749); (2) an influence analysis found the primary result was not robust to exclusion of a single site (removing site 701, n=13, reduced the effect to a non-significant p=0.1027 despite that site's treatment effect being more than twice the overall estimate); (3) baseline imbalances existed in prior disease-progression rate (del-FS) and in concomitant riluzole/edaravone use, and more subjects in the drug arm started new ALS medications during the trial (a potential unadjusted confounder)
- The sponsor's post hoc joint rank analysis (ranking subjects first by time to death, then by ALSFRS-R change), following FDA's earlier recommendation to use such a method, was statistically significant and directionally consistent with the primary analysis, but used last-observation-carried-forward imputation for post-death/missing ALSFRS-R data; FDA's statistical reviewer reran the joint rank analysis using multiple imputation under a missing-at-random assumption instead, which reduced the result to p=0.079 (not significant)
- Long-term open-label/survival analyses (post hoc, presented at the second Advisory Committee) compared survival in the combined AMX0035 arm (N=89, median overall survival 23.5 months) against external/predicted natural-history benchmarks and against the placebo-to-drug crossover cohort in the OLE, forming the core of the "new information" that shifted the second Advisory Committee vote

- FDA Summary Review (contains the statistical dispute, both Advisory Committee vote records, and Dr. Tristan Massie's sensitivity analyses) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/216660Orig1s000SumR.pdf

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1916945), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32877582/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Trial%20Sodium%20Phenylbutyrate-Taurursodiol%20Amyotrophic%20Lateral%20Sclerosis)

- Long-term/survival follow-up publication: Paganoni S, Hendrix S, Dickson SP, et al. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1136/jnnp-2022-329024), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35577511/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Effect%20sodium%20phenylbutyrate%20taurursodiol%20tracheostomy%20ventilation-free%20survival%20CENTAUR)

**Other resources**

- No Amylyx-specific IPD/dataset sharing program was identified; trial-specific availability not confirmed.

- FDA Advisory Committee: Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs (PCNS) Advisory Committee met twice. March 30, 2022 — Question: "Do the data from the single randomized, controlled trial and the open-label extension study establish a conclusion that sodium phenylbutyrate/taurursodiol is effective in the treatment of patients with ALS?" Vote: No 6, Yes 4, Abstain 0. September 7, 2022 (after the sponsor submitted new survival/long-term analyses, one fewer voting member) — Question: "Is the available evidence of effectiveness sufficient to support approval...?" Vote: Yes 7, No 2, Abstain 0.

- Confirmatory trial: PHOENIX (Study A35-004, NCT05021536), a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial (~664 patients, 48-week treatment), announced March 8, 2024 as not meeting its primary or secondary endpoints (no statistically significant difference vs. placebo). Amylyx announced on April 4, 2024 that it would voluntarily withdraw Relyvrio (U.S.) and Albrioza (Canada) from the market, while continuing to support patients already on therapy through an expanded-access-style program; this was a sponsor business/evidentiary decision, not a case of FDA-ordered withdrawal.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, NDA 216660, p.12]* — "FDA typically recommends the use of a combined analysis of function and survival, such as the joint rank analysis of the ALSFRS-R, as the primary analysis in ALS. FDA has long indicated that deaths may cause bias if ignored in the primary analysis since some deaths are expected in the double-blind period... The advice to use a combined analysis of function and survival, such as a joint rank analysis, was provided to the Applicant at the pre-IND meeting and in an advice email after review of the SAP in March 2019. A joint rank analysis was later conducted by the Applicant as a post hoc analysis."

*[verbatim, p.15]* — "The Applicant met its prespecified primary endpoint, demonstrating a statistically significant (p = 0.034) slowing of disease progression as measured by the ALSFRS-R total score compared to placebo, at the end of the 24-week, randomized, controlled phase of the study. The estimated least squares (LS) mean ALSFRS-R total score was 2.32 points higher at Week 24 compared to placebo."

*[verbatim, p.15]* — "In a sensitivity analysis, Dr. Massie used a more common model frequently used in FDA review work, a Mean-By-Visit MMRM model of change from baseline which does not rely on a linearity assumption... This analysis did not show a nominally significant treatment difference in ALSFRS-R at Week 24 in the mITT population, with an estimated difference of 1.86 (SE 1.04), p = 0.0749."

*[verbatim, p.15]* — influence analysis: "the removal of a single site from the study renders the primary analysis treatment effect no longer statistically significant [e.g., without site 701 (n = 13): slope difference = -0.079; SE=0.049; p=0.1027... This particular site had a within site estimated treatment difference more than twice as large as the overall estimate (5.75 vs 2.32)."

*[verbatim, p.16]* — on the post hoc joint rank re-analysis: "Dr. Massie performed a joint rank analysis with a preferred method of handling missing data of ALSFRS-R and death, using multiple imputation based on a missing-at-random assumption... the joint rank analysis has a p = 0.079."

*[verbatim, p.30]* — first Advisory Committee vote: "Vote: Do the data from the single randomized, controlled trial and the open-label extension study establish a conclusion that sodium phenylbutyrate/taurursodiol is effective in the treatment of patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS)? ... The Committee vote: NO: 6 YES: 4 Abstain: 0."

The Committee Vote: YES: 7 NO: 2 Abstain: 0."

### 60. Ublituximab-xiiy (Briumvi) — BLA 761238

**Sponsor:** TG Therapeutics, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (RMS), to include clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting disease, and active secondary progressive disease, in adults

**Approval date:** December 28, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** Two identical Phase 3 trials — ULTIMATE I (Study TG1101-RMS301), NCT03277261, and ULTIMATE II (Study TG1101-RMS302), NCT03277248

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two identical, 120-week, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled (teriflunomide) Phase 3 trials, agreed with FDA via Special Protocol Assessment; blinded interim sample-size re-estimation
- *Endpoints:* annualized relapse rate (ARR), IRAP (Independent Relapse Adjudication Panel)-confirmed, over 96 weeks (primary); Gd-enhancing T1 lesions, new/enlarging T2 lesions, time to 12-week confirmed disability progression (CDP, pooled across both trials), NEDA, SDMT, brain-volume change (key secondary, hierarchically tested)
- *Primary analysis:* negative binomial regression (treatment, EDSS strata, region, log-duration offset)
- *Multiplicity:* gatekeeping procedure requiring the primary endpoint and first two secondary endpoints to be significant in both individual trials before the pooled-data CDP test was considered confirmatory; subsequent endpoints tested only if the pooled CDP analysis was significant ("cross-trial pooled gatekeeping node embedded within twin confirmatory trials")
- *Missing data/bias:* multiple imputation (10 replicates) for relapses among subjects who withdrew consent; sensitivity analyses including all reported (not just IRAP-confirmed) relapses and post-discontinuation relapses

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ULTIMATE I and ULTIMATE II: identically-designed, 120-week (4-week screening, 96-week treatment, 20-week follow-up), randomized, multicenter, double-blind, double-dummy, active-comparator (teriflunomide 14 mg) Phase 3 trials in RMS patients aged 18-55 with recent relapse activity or a Gd-enhancing lesion and EDSS 0-5.5; protocols agreed with FDA under a Special Protocol Assessment; ublituximab given as IV infusions at Week 1/Day 1, Week 3/Day 15, and Weeks 24, 48, 72 (with matching oral/IV placebos in each arm)
- Primary endpoint: ARR, defined as IRAP-confirmed relapses per year, analyzed on the modified intent-to-treat population (randomized, ≥1 dose, ≥1 baseline and postbaseline efficacy assessment)
- Primary analysis: negative binomial regression on confirmed relapses (onset between randomization and last treatment day) with treatment group, EDSS strata (≤3.5 vs. >3.5), and region (USA/Western Europe vs. Eastern Europe) as covariates and log-transformed standardized treatment duration as an offset; sensitivity analyses included all reported relapses (not just confirmed), a stratified Cox model for time-to-first-relapse, relapses occurring after treatment discontinuation, and multiple imputation (10 replicates) of expected relapse counts for subjects who withdrew consent
- Blinded interim sample-size re-estimation: a Blinded Assessment Relapse Team (BART) reviewed pooled ARR after 210 of the planned 220/arm were randomized; if the combined rate was ≤0.19, enrollment would be increased by 30/arm/study. BART met October 15, 2020 and recommended the increase (to 220+30 per arm)
- Multiplicity: gatekeeping procedure at alpha=0.05 per test; the pooled (across both trials) 12-week CDP analysis was only treated as confirmatory if the primary endpoint (ARR) and the first two secondary endpoints (Gd-enhancing T1 and new/enlarging T2 lesion counts) were each statistically significant in both individual trials; subsequent secondary endpoints continued to be tested within each individual trial only if the pooled CDP analysis was itself significant
- Result (Study 301): LS-mean ARR 0.076 (ublituximab) vs. 0.188 (teriflunomide), rate ratio 0.406 (95% CI 0.268-0.615), 59.4% relative reduction, p<0.0001; all prespecified sensitivity analyses consistent with the primary result
- No formal Advisory Committee meeting; the FDA Summary Review states the application "was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because this biologic" raised no issues requiring one

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2023/761238Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2022/761238s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/761238Orig1s000StatR.pdf

- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/761238Orig1s000SumR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (ULTIMATE I) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03277261 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (ULTIMATE II) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03277248 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)

- Pivotal publication: Steinman L, Fox E, Hartung HP, et al. "Ublituximab versus Teriflunomide in Relapsing Multiple Sclerosis." *N Engl J Med.* 2022;387(8):704-714. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2201904), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36001711/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Ublituximab%20versus%20Teriflunomide%20Relapsing%20Multiple%20Sclerosis)

**Other resources**

- No TG Therapeutics-specific IPD/dataset sharing program was identified; trial-specific availability not confirmed.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held for this BLA; the FDA Summary Review states "This application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, BLA 761238, p.5]* — "These were two identical Phase III, 120-week, randomized, multicenter, global, double-blinded, double-dummy, active-controlled studies. The primary endpoint was ARR. The protocols for these studies were agreed upon with the FDA through a Special Protocol Assessment."

*[verbatim, p.6-7]* — "The primary analysis was a negative binomial regression model that included the total number of confirmed relapses with onset between randomization date and the day of last treatment as response variable, treatment group, EDSS strata (baseline EDSS score ≤3.5 versus >3.5), and clinic region... as covariates. To account for different treatment durations among subjects, the log-transformed standardized treatment duration was included in the model as an 'offset' variable."

*[verbatim, p.8]* — interim re-estimation: "A blinded interim analysis for sample size re-estimation was planned to be performed when 210 of the 220 participants per arm had been randomized... The sample size was reassessed based on the pooled annualized relapse rate (ARR). If the combined total rate <= 0.19, the sample size would be increased by 30 per treatment group in each study. The BART committee met on October 15, 2020 and recommended adding 30 subjects to the sample size."

*[verbatim, p.8]* — multiplicity: "A gatekeeping procedure was used where each test was tested at α=0.05. For the 12-week CDP endpoint, the testing was based on pooled data from the 2 studies to achieve sufficient statistical power to detect relevant treatment differences. This test was considered confirmatory only if all tests for the primary endpoint and first 2 secondary endpoints were statistically significant (α=0.05) in both studies."

*[verbatim, p.10]* — key result: "The least squares (LS) mean for the ARR was 0.076 in the ublituximab group and 0.188 in the teriflunomide group. The treatment effect of ublituximab versus teriflunomide was statistically significant in favor of ublituximab at a rate ratio of 0.406 (p<0.0001), corresponding to a relative reduction of 59.4%."

### 61. Lecanemab-irmb (Leqembi) — BLA 761269

**Sponsor:** Eisai Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of Alzheimer's disease; initially approved January 6, 2023 under accelerated approval based on reduction of amyloid beta plaques (a surrogate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit); converted to traditional approval on July 6, 2023 (efficacy supplement s001) based on verification of clinical benefit in Study 301 (CLARITY-AD)

**Approval date:** January 6, 2023 (accelerated approval, BLA 761269 Orig-1); July 6, 2023 (traditional approval, Orig-1 s001)

**Pivotal trial:** CLARITY-AD (Study 301, BAN2401-G000-301), NCT03887455 — confirmatory trial supporting traditional approval; the original January 2023 accelerated approval rested on Study 201 (BAN2401-G000-201), a Bayesian adaptive-randomization Phase 2b dose-finding study, NCT01767311

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, 18-month core study with open-label extension; randomization stratified by clinical subgroup (MCI due to AD vs. mild AD dementia), use of AD symptomatic medication at baseline, APOE4 carrier status, and geographical region; amyloid-PET substudy embedded in a subset (~35% of enrollment) for a biomarker key secondary endpoint
- *Endpoints:* Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) change from baseline at 18 months (primary) (no existing CDR-SB entry in Keyword_Taxonomy.md § Endpoint/outcome type); amyloid PET Centiloid change, ADAS-Cog14, ADCOMS, and ADCS-MCI-ADL (key secondaries)
- *Primary analysis:* Mixed model for repeated measurements (MMRM) with a sandwich variance estimator (unstructured covariance, with a pre-specified fallback sequence of structured covariance matrices and a sandwich estimator if a structured matrix was used)
- *Multiplicity:* single formal primary endpoint (no adjustment required); fixed-sequence hierarchical testing of four key secondary endpoints in a pre-specified order (amyloid PET Centiloids → ADAS-Cog14 → ADCOMS → ADCS-MCI-ADL), each gated on the prior endpoint's significance at two-sided alpha=0.05
- *Missing data/bias:* rank-ANCOVA-after-multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis; tipping-point analysis (multiple imputation) with treatment-group-specific shift parameters
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval based on a non-oncology biomarker surrogate (amyloid PET/CSF reduction), converted to traditional approval via a same-BLA efficacy supplement upon confirmatory-trial verification (existing "Accelerated approval..." rows in Keyword_Taxonomy.md § Regulatory process tags are oncology-specific); FDA Advisory Committee meeting held (unanimous 6-0 vote confirming clinical benefit)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- CLARITY-AD (Study 301): randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter trial in early Alzheimer's disease (MCI due to AD/prodromal AD or mild AD dementia) with confirmed amyloid pathology by PET or CSF; 1,795 subjects randomized 1:1 (897 placebo, 898 lecanemab 10 mg/kg biweekly) across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, and China
- Primary endpoint: change from baseline in CDR-SB at 18 months (Week 79), analyzed via MMRM on the Full Analysis Set (FAS+), including baseline CDR-SB, treatment, visit, stratification variables, and treatment-by-visit interaction as fixed effects
- Sample size: original plan of 1,566 subjects (783/arm) for 90% power to detect an assumed 0.373-point treatment difference (SD 2.031, from Study 201) at two-sided alpha=0.05; increased to ~1,766 to retain power after ~200 subjects missed ≥3 consecutive doses during COVID-19 dosing holds; protocol required ≥70% of subjects to be APOE4 carriers to match the population used in the power calculation
- Key secondary endpoints (hierarchically tested): amyloid PET Centiloid change, ADAS-Cog14, ADCOMS, ADCS-MCI-ADL, all at 18 months
- Sensitivity analyses for missing data: rank ANCOVA after multiple imputation (1,000 imputations, seed=2401, MAR assumption), tipping-point analysis with shift parameters (δ) applied separately by treatment arm, and an analysis using IxRS-classified (rather than actual-data) stratification variables
- Prespecified supportive analyses on the FAS+ and Per-Protocol sets, and an analysis censoring at treatment discontinuation or AD-medication initiation/dose change

- Package Insert / Label (traditional approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2023/761269Orig1s001lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review (accelerated approval, Study 201) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/761269Orig1s000StatR.pdf

- Pivotal publication: van Dyck CH, Swanson CJ, Aisen P, et al. "Lecanemab in Early Alzheimer's Disease." *N Engl J Med.* 2023;388(1):9-21. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2212948), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36449413/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Lecanemab%20in%20Early%20Alzheimer%27s%20Disease)

**Other resources**

- Eisai participates in general cross-industry IPD-sharing platforms; trial-specific CLARITY-AD availability was not individually confirmed here.
- FDA Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee meeting held June 9, 2023, to assess whether Study 301 verified clinical benefit; the committee voted unanimously (6-0) that the data confirm the clinical benefit of lecanemab for AD, and separately opined that the overall benefit-risk assessment was favorable and supported traditional approval, with specific discussion of ApoE4 homozygotes, concomitant anticoagulant use, and cerebral amyloid angiopathy as challenging subgroups.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, BLA 761269 s001, Reference ID 5200126, Executive Summary]* — "Based on highly significant results on the primary endpoint, CDR-SB, at Week 79 as well as multiplicity controlled key secondary endpoints, Study 301 appears to confirm the clinical benefit of lecanemab in early AD."

*[verbatim, same document, §3.2.1.2 Statistical Methodologies]* — "The primary analysis of the change from baseline in CDR-SB at 18 months was to be performed to compare BAN2401 versus placebo using an MMRM on the FAS... This study has one primary endpoint, so no adjustment for multiplicity is required for the primary analysis. If the primary endpoint is statistically significant, then the key secondary endpoints were to be tested in the following order: (1) change from baseline in amyloid PET using Centiloids at 18 months, (2) change from baseline in ADAS-Cog14 at 18 months, (3) change from baseline in ADCOMS at 18 months, and (4) change from baseline in ADCS MCI-ADL at 18 months."

*[verbatim, same document, §3.2.1.4.1 Applicant's Results]* — "There was a highly statistically significant difference between PBO and LEC10-BW on change from baseline of CDR-SB at 18 months, with an adjusted mean treatment difference of -0.451, 27.1% less decline with LEC10-BW compared to PBO, P=0.00005." FDA's own reproduced analysis on its preferred FAS (with COVID-related site exclusions) at Week 78 gave an adjusted mean difference of -0.394 (95% CI: -0.613, -0.176), p=0.00040, a 24.6% relative difference.

*[verbatim, same document, §3.2.1.4.1, key secondary results table]* — amyloid PET Centiloids: placebo-lecanemab difference 59.2 (95% CI 55.6, 62.7), p<.0001; ADAS-Cog14: difference 1.4 (0.6, 2.3), p=0.0007; ADCOMS (×100): difference 4.5 (2.2, 6.9), p=0.0002; ADCS-ADL-MCI: difference -2.0 (-2.8, -1.2), p<.0001.

*[verbatim, same document, §5.1 Statistical Issues]* — "The applicant reported a tipping point of 1.5 for the FAS+ population, meaning missing outcomes would have to have a 1.5 point worse shift on CDR-SB for lecanemab than the shift for placebo missing outcomes in order for the primary analysis to lose significance... If smaller shifts are considered the tipping point is closer to 1 than 1.5, being about 1.1. The tipping point is lower if data after both ARIA-E and/or changes in concomitant AD medications are censored," dropping to a tipping point of 0.5 under that stricter censoring rule.

*[verbatim, same document, §4.2 Other Special/Subgroup Populations]* — on the ApoE4-homozygote subgroup: "The effect was numerically worse than placebo in this subgroup for CDR-SB at Week 79, lecanemab-placebo=0.25 (S.E.=0.28) [95% C.I.=-0.30, 0.80], p=0.367. There was a nominally significant quantitative interaction (p=0.017) between treatment group and APOE4 genotype... but it did not reach the level of a qualitative interaction."

### 62. Zavegepant (Zavzpret) — NDA 216386

**Sponsor:** Pfizer Inc. (originally developed by Biohaven Pharmaceuticals, acquired by Pfizer in 2022)

**Indication approved:** Acute treatment of migraine with or without aura in adults (intranasal formulation)

**Approval date:** March 9, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** Study 301, NCT04571060 — Phase 3 confirmatory trial; a Phase 2/3 dose-ranging trial, Study 201, NCT03872453, provided supportive evidence across three doses

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, outpatient trial treating a single moderate-to-severe migraine attack; two pivotal trials (dose-ranging Study 201 and confirmatory Study 301) with identical co-primary and key secondary endpoint definitions
- *Endpoints:* co-primary endpoints of pain freedom at 2 hours post-dose and freedom from most bothersome symptom (MBS) at 2 hours post-dose (both binary, non-responder-imputed for missing/rescue-medication use)
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by prophylactic migraine medication use at randomization
- *Multiplicity:* hierarchical gate-keeping procedure — key secondary endpoints tested only if both co-primary endpoints were significant, each subsequent test conducted at a two-sided alpha of 0.0167 (Study 201) or 0.05 (Study 301)
- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation for missing binary/diary efficacy data (intervening rescue medication or missing assessment counted as non-response for both co-primary endpoints); varying-response-rate and multiple-imputation sensitivity analyses (with a sponsor programming error later corrected via an FDA information request)
- *Regulatory:* two independently conducted pivotal trials (dose-ranging plus confirmatory) both required to show efficacy at the to-be-marketed 10 mg dose

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 301 (pivotal): randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, outpatient trial of zavegepant 10 mg intranasal vs. placebo for a single migraine attack of moderate or severe intensity; 1,405 subjects randomized (703 zavegepant, 702 placebo), modified intent-to-treat (mITT) analysis population of 623/646
- Study 201 (dose-ranging): identical design, four arms (zavegepant 5 mg, 10 mg, 20 mg, placebo), 1,673 randomized, used to select the 10 mg to-be-marketed dose
- Co-primary endpoints (both trials): pain freedom at 2 hours post-dose (pain intensity of none, no intervening rescue medication) and MBS freedom at 2 hours post-dose (nausea, phonophobia, or photophobia reported before dosing, absent at 2 hours, no intervening rescue medication)
- Key secondary endpoints (hierarchically tested): pain relief at 2 hours, return to normal function at 2 hours (Functional Disability Scale), sustained pain freedom from 2-48 hours, phonophobia freedom at 2 hours, photophobia freedom at 2 hours
- Analysis population: modified intent-to-treat (randomized once, moderate/severe pain at dosing, took study drug, had post-dose efficacy data)

For the co-primary efficacy endpoint of pain freedom at 2 hours post-dose, there was a 7% therapeutic gain (percentage difference) in the zavegepant 10 mg group over placebo group in Study 201 and an 8.8% therapeutic gain for zavegepant 10 mg over placebo group in Study 301."

The updates in the corrected sensitivity analyses results were minor and did not change the conclusions."

### 63. Trofinetide (Daybue) — NDA 217026

**Sponsor:** Acadia Pharmaceuticals Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of Rett syndrome in adults and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older

**Approval date:** March 10, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** LAVENDER (Study ACP-2566-003, "Study 003"), NCT04181723

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, 12-week trial in a rare pediatric/adult population; randomization stratified by baseline RSBQ severity (<35 vs. ≥35 total score); weight-banded dosing
- *Endpoints:* co-primary endpoints of change from baseline to Week 12 in the Rett Syndrome Behaviour Questionnaire (RSBQ) total score (caregiver-rated) and Clinical Global Impression-Improvement (CGI-I) score at Week 12 (clinician-rated) (no RSBQ or Rett-specific CGI-I entries in Keyword_Taxonomy.md § Endpoint/outcome type); key secondary endpoint of Communication and Symbolic Behavior Scales Developmental Profile (CSBS-DP-IT) Social Composite Score
- *Primary analysis:* Mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) with fixed effects for treatment, baseline RSBQ severity stratum, visit, baseline score, age group, and treatment-by-visit and baseline-by-visit interactions
- *Multiplicity:* both co-primary endpoints required p<0.05 to declare study success; key secondary endpoint tested only if both co-primary endpoints were significant
- *Missing data/bias:* reference-based (placebo-completer) imputation model explored as a sensitivity analysis for violations of the missing-at-random assumption, given a substantially higher dropout rate on trofinetide (24.7%) than placebo (9.6%); a tipping-point sensitivity analysis was originally planned but removed via SAP Amendment 2

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 003 (LAVENDER): Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, two-arm, parallel-group, placebo-controlled trial of weight-based-dosed oral trofinetide (6-12 mg BID depending on body weight) vs. placebo over 12 weeks of double-blind therapy, in girls and women with genetically confirmed Rett syndrome
- 187 subjects randomized 1:1 (94 placebo, 93 trofinetide), Intent-to-Treat population
- Co-primary endpoints: change from baseline to Week 12 (CFB12) in RSBQ total score (0-90-point caregiver-completed scale, higher = worse) and CGI-I at Week 12 (7-point clinician-rated scale)
- Sample size: planned enrollment of 184 to provide ≥90% power to detect an assumed treatment effect of -4.4 points (SD 8) on RSBQ and -0.5 points (SD 0.7) on CGI-I, assuming 5% dropout, two-sided alpha=0.05
- Key secondary endpoint: CSBS-DP-IT Social Composite Score change from baseline to Week 12, tested only if both co-primary endpoints were significant
- A prior Phase 2 dose-ranging study (Neu-2566-rett-002, "Study 002") was exploratory, uncontrolled for multiplicity, and showed improvement at the 200 mg/kg BID dose on 3 of 5 pre-specified core variables

### 64. Tofersen (Qalsody) — NDA 215887

**Sponsor:** Biogen Inc. (label uses "Biogen Inc.")

**Indication approved:** Treatment of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) in adults who have a mutation in the superoxide dismutase 1 (SOD1) gene, approved under accelerated approval based on reduction in plasma neurofilament light chain (NfL) observed in tofersen-treated patients; continued approval contingent on verification of clinical benefit in confirmatory trial(s)

**Approval date:** April 25, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** VALOR (Study 233AS101, Part C), NCT02623699 — companion open-label extension Study 233AS102; confirmatory postmarketing trial ATLAS (Study 233AS303) ongoing in presymptomatic SOD1 carriers at approval

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized (2:1 active:placebo), double-blind, placebo-controlled, 28-week Phase 3 trial enriched for both "fast-progressor" and non-fast-progressor SOD1-ALS patients; randomization stratified by fast-progressor status, edaravone use, and riluzole use
- *Endpoints:* ALSFRS-R (ALS Functional Rating Scale-Revised) total score change from baseline to Week 28 (primary, missed); plasma neurofilament light chain (NfL) and total CSF SOD1 as key secondary/exploratory endpoints, used by FDA as the accelerated-approval surrogate
- *Primary analysis:* joint rank test (a combined survival-and-function outcome measure specific to ALS trials) with multiple imputation for missing/withdrawal data (no joint-rank-test entry in Keyword_Taxonomy.md § Primary analysis method)
- *Missing data/bias:* multiple imputation under the joint rank test framework; ANCOVA on MI-imputed data as a sensitivity/nominal analysis
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval granted despite the pivotal trial missing its primary clinical endpoint, based on a biomarker (plasma NfL) determined reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit; FDA Advisory Committee meeting held (unanimous vote favoring the surrogate determination)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- VALOR (Study 101C): Phase 3, multicenter (32 sites, 9 countries), randomized 2:1 (tofersen:placebo), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of intrathecal tofersen 100 mg (3 loading doses every 2 weeks, then 5 maintenance doses every 4 weeks) vs. placebo/sham procedure over 28 weeks, in adults with SOD1-mutated ALS; 108 subjects randomized (72 tofersen, 36 placebo), modified intent-to-treat (mITT) analysis population
- Primary endpoint: change from baseline to Week 28 (Day 197) in ALSFRS-R total score; nominal difference of 1.2 points favoring tofersen (-7.0 vs. -8.1 decline), joint rank test with multiple imputation p=0.9689 — not statistically significant
- Key secondary endpoints: plasma NfL and total CSF SOD1 (both showed statistically significant, large reductions with tofersen — 67% and 34-38% geometric-mean-ratio differences vs. placebo, respectively, nominal p<0.0001 for both), slow vital capacity (SVC) change, handheld dynamometry (HHD) megascore, time to death-or-permanent-ventilation (adjudicated), time to death (stratified log-rank test)
- FDA's surrogate-endpoint determination rested on mechanistic plausibility (SOD1 knockdown), NfL's established prognostic value in ALS, and observed correlation between NfL reduction and slowed ALSFRS-R decline, despite the underpowered, heterogeneous mITT population and the missed primary clinical endpoint

This is a very rare and devastating disease and there would be substantial challenges to conducting a second study in the same population." And: "issues that may have reduced the ability to detect a drug effect... the study was greatly underpowered, and the heterogeneity of the disease progression rate was not well-controlled in the mITT population, despite intention to do so with an enriched, fast-progressor population."
