**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Executive Summary, p.4]* — "For the LAL-CL03 trial, conducted in the Wolman Disease patient population, sebelipase alfa was demonstrated to be superior to an acceptable historical control group, extracted from retrospective natural history study LAL-1-NH01, with respect to survival, i.e., time to death from birth up to Month 12. For the LAL-CL02 trial, conducted in the Cholesteryl Ester Storage Disease (CESD) patient population, sebelipase alfa was demonstrated to be superior to placebo in the Week 20 change from baseline in low density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-c), non-high density lipoprotein cholesterol (non-HDL-c), triglycerides, and HDL-c."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.1.2.2-3.2.1.2.3, p.12]* — "There was no multiplicity adjustment pre-specified by the applicant. Formal hypothesis testing is conducted only for the primary endpoint... The applicant's pre-specified analysis was to compare median time to death from birth up to Month 12 between the patient groups through a standard Kaplan-Meier approach with formal hypothesis testing utilizing the log-rank test. In addition, a hazard ratio along with a corresponding 95% CI was presented."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.1.2.5, p.13]* — "To further assess the sensitivity of the results to censored data, the statistical reviewer espoused a worst-case imputation strategy for the primary analysis by designating censored patients as 'failures', i.e., having experienced death."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.2.1, p.22]* — "Assuming that 71% of patients randomized to sebelipase alfa and 17% of patients randomized to placebo achieve the primary efficacy endpoint, a sample size of 50 randomized patients (approximately 25 patients per treatment group) would provide 97% power to detect a statistically significant difference between sebelipase alfa and placebo, using Fisher's exact test at two-sided α=0.05."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.2.2.2, p.23]* — "In order to control the overall study-wise type I error rate, a step-down/closed sequential testing procedure was pre-specified by the applicant to adjust for the multiple comparisons on the study endpoints... Starting with the primary endpoint, the applicant stated that the step-down could only be carried to the next endpoint, within the order presented above, if and only if the current endpoint/step was found to be statistically significant in the comparison of sebelipase alfa to placebo (i.e., p-value less than 0.05). If the comparison of sebelipase alfa to placebo was not statistically significant at the current endpoint/step (i.e., p-value greater than or equal to 0.05), then all hypothesis testing for the subsequent endpoints/steps would be deemed as exploratory."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §1, p.4]* — "Overall, the design of the LAL-CL03 study, in addition to the LAL-1-NH01 protocol for extracting comparable retrospective natural history data to be utilized as a historical control, was ultimately deemed reasonable from a statistical perspective... Due to the scarcity of the Wolman Disease patient population, i.e., the prevailing public health circumstances related to Wolman Disease, and the fact that it is a highly progressive disease with an unmet medical need, the determination of the clinical effectiveness of sebelipase alfa will rely more on clinical judgment than on the statistical rigor usually required for larger randomized controlled studies."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §1, p.4]* — "The only review issue pertained to the adequacy of the primary endpoint, i.e., normalization of alanine aminotransferase (ALT); this was a clinical review issue. Throughout sebelipase alfa's clinical development program, the Division of Gastroenterology and Inborn Errors Products (DGIEP) had communicated to the applicant that ALT alone would not be sufficient as a basis for approval in the CESD patient population... it was adjudicated that the lipid parameters (i.e., LDL-c, non-HDL-c, triglycerides, and HDL-c) were the only clinically meaningful efficacy data captured in this CESD study, with LDL-c being chief among them."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §5.1, p.53]* — "For the LAL-CL03/LAL-1-NH01 study, it should be noted that comparisons to a historical control group are not considered to provide results that are as robust or reliable as those from comparisons within a randomized controlled study... the retrospective nature of the LAL-1-NH01 study introduces the potential for selection bias, i.e., patients ultimately chosen for the historical control group may be those that result in an overly optimistic estimate of efficacy when comparisons are made to the treated patients. Both of these issues are further magnified when operating with very small sample sizes, which is the case for Wolman Disease."

**Reverse-engineered SAP** (no genuine sponsor protocol/SAP document is publicly posted — ClinicalTrials.gov's Documents tab is empty for both NCT01757184 and NCT01371825; the excerpts above are FDA's description/quotation of the sponsor's pre-specified analyses, not the sponsor's original SAP PDF)

- [inferred] The LAL-CL03 historical-control matching almost certainly required the LAL-1-NH01 comparator infants to share the same core eligibility construct as trial infants (growth failure/rapidly progressive disease onset within 6 months of life, diagnosis consistent with the Wolman phenotype), since only 21 of 35 extracted natural-history patients were "adjudicated as being appropriate for comparison" — inferred from the FDA Statistical Review's disposition table (Table 2) reporting this 21/35 filter without spelling out the exact matching algorithm.

- [inferred] The natural-history comparator's outcome (0/21, 0.0% survival to Month 12, 95% CI 0-16.1%) functioned as the de facto "untreated" performance benchmark against which the 9-patient treated cohort's 66.7% survival was judged; given a historical fatality rate at or near 100% by convention for untreated infantile Wolman disease, essentially any surviving treated infant at Month 12 would have produced a nominally significant log-rank result — inferred from the near-total historical-control mortality (0/21 alive) combined with the small treated-cohort size (n=9) reported in Table 4.

- [inferred] The choice of "time to death from birth" (rather than time to death from first infusion/enrollment) as the time origin was likely necessitated by the historical-control arm having no intervention date to anchor to, forcing a birth-anchored clock for both arms to keep the comparison valid — inferred from the endpoint definition ("Time to Death from Birth up to Month 12") applied identically and necessarily to both the treated and historical-control groups.

- [inferred] The lack of any pre-specified multiplicity adjustment for LAL-CL03 (FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.1.2.2: "There was no multiplicity adjustment pre-specified") is consistent with a single, previously-agreed primary endpoint under Breakthrough Therapy Designation interactions with DGIEP, rather than any post hoc simplification — inferred from the review's chronology showing FDA advised on survival-as-primary-endpoint feasibility as early as the November 6, 2012 Type C meeting, well before the SAP was finalized (September 14, 2012 per §3.1.1, i.e., contemporaneous with that advice).

### 11. Eteplirsen (Exondys 51) — NDA 206488

**Sponsor:** Sarepta Therapeutics, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in patients who have a confirmed mutation of the DMD gene amenable to exon 51 skipping — approved under accelerated approval (21 CFR § 314.510) based on an increase in dystrophin production in skeletal muscle observed in some patients treated with eteplirsen

**Approval date:** September 19, 2016

**Pivotal trial:** Study 201 (double-blind, placebo-controlled core), NCT01396239, with continuous open-label extension Study 202, NCT01540409; postmarketing confirmatory trial Study 4658-301 (open-label, multicenter, with a concurrent untreated control arm), NCT02255552, publicly referred to by the sponsor as PROMOVI

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* small randomized, single-center, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multiple-dose trial (N=12) with a 4-week placebo-crossover, rolled into a continuous open-label extension; patient-level comparison of the open-label extension against an external historical-control/DMD-registry cohort (small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population)

- *Endpoints:* percent dystrophin-positive muscle fibers by immunohistochemistry (IHC), change from baseline (primary, biomarker surrogate); 6-Minute Walk Test (6MWT) change from baseline (key secondary/clinical endpoint)

- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA on ranked data for the dystrophin biomarker endpoint (with baseline value and time since DMD diagnosis as covariates); mixed model repeated measures (MMRM) for 6MWT

- *Multiplicity:* none — FDA statistical review explicitly states "the statistical analysis plan of Study 201 did not include a method for statistical adjustment for testing multiple doses and/or multiple endpoints," so all reported p-values (including the headline dystrophin p=0.002) are labeled nominal/exploratory only

- *Missing data/bias:* comparison against an externally, post-hoc-identified historical-control DMD registry cohort, which FDA's statistical reviewer called "statistically uninterpretable" due to lack of a prespecified analysis plan and inadequate control for selection bias; post-hoc, outcome-dependent "modified Intent-to-Treat" (mITT) population created by the sponsor to exclude 2 rapidly-progressing patients from the 6MWT analysis, which FDA's reviewer rejected as data-driven and potentially misleading

- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval granted over the primary statistical and clinical review team's non-approval recommendation; CDER Center Director-level override of the review team's recommendation (Janet Woodcock, M.D., overruling Ellis Unger, M.D., Director of the Office of Drug Evaluation I) — a materially more senior override than the existing "Division Director" precedent in this census (DaTscan/Ioflupane I 123); formal Scientific Dispute Resolution (SDR) appeal by the review-team director to the FDA Office of the Commissioner, decided by the Acting Chief Scientist as SDR Board chair (no other entry in this census documents an SDR appeal to the Commissioner's office); FDA Advisory Committee meeting held, with two separate, both unfavorable-to-sponsor votes (7-6 against accelerated approval on the surrogate endpoint; 7-3 with 3 abstentions that the Study 201/202 clinical data did not provide substantial evidence of effectiveness); accelerated approval conditioned on a required postmarketing confirmatory trial (Study 4658-301/PROMOVI)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 201: Phase 2/3, randomized, single-center (US), double-blind, placebo-controlled, multiple-dose study of once-weekly IV eteplirsen in 12 boys (ages 7-10) with genotypically confirmed DMD amenable to exon 51 skipping; patients randomized to 4 groups (50 mg/kg eteplirsen, n=4; 30 mg/kg eteplirsen, n=4; placebo→50 mg/kg crossover at Week 24, n=2; placebo→30 mg/kg crossover at Week 24, n=2); efficacy assessed through the first 24 placebo-controlled weeks, safety through Week 28; protocol amended 7 times, 3 after study start — Amendment 6 (Nov. 4, 2011) promoted 6MWT from exploratory to secondary endpoint mid-trial, and the SAP was not finalized until February 20, 2012, close to study completion

- Primary endpoint: change from baseline in percent dystrophin-positive muscle fibers by IHC (MANDYS106 antibody), assessed at Week 12 (Groups 1/3a) or Week 24 (Groups 2/3b) via muscle biopsy

- Key secondary/clinical endpoint: change from baseline to Week 24 in 6MWT distance, plus CD3/CD4/CD8 lymphocyte counts, timed function tests (4-step test, 10-meter run), and MVICT strength testing — several of these were labeled "exploratory" in the protocol but promoted to "key secondary" status in the February 2012 SAP with no clear hierarchical ordering specified

- All 12 patients rolled into an open-label extension (Study 202) continuing weekly eteplirsen for up to 168+ additional weeks at the time of NDA submission; FDA compared the combined eteplirsen group's Week 168 6MWT change against an externally identified historical-control DMD cohort assembled from 2 patient registries — FDA's statistical review concluded this comparison "did not have a prespecified statistical analysis plan, and had an inadequate control for bias" and was "statistically uninterpretable"

- Primary results (FDA Statistical Review, Table 3): no significant difference between 50 mg/kg eteplirsen and placebo at Week 12 (p=0.958); 30 mg/kg eteplirsen showed a 22.95-point mean increase in dystrophin-positive fibers vs. -4.05 for placebo (nominal p=0.002, exploratory only, no multiplicity control, and the 50 mg/kg arm was negative)

- 6MWT results (FDA Statistical Review, Table 4): placebo declined a mean 17.3 m from baseline to Week 24; the 30 mg/kg eteplirsen group declined 134.8 m (MMRM treatment effect nominally favored placebo, p=0.026); the 50 mg/kg group changed -2.3 m (p=0.563, not significant). The sponsor attributed the 30 mg/kg group's large decline to 2 rapidly-progressing patients and excluded them in a post-hoc "modified ITT" analysis not specified in the SAP; FDA's reviewer noted this population "was defined based on the outcome data (instead of enrollment criteria or baseline character)" and that "analysis on the mITT population could be misleading"

- Western blot dystrophin quantification (a more quantitative assay than IHC) in Study 201/202 patients at Week 180 showed a mean increase of only 0.93% of normal dystrophin levels — versus IHC's reported increase from 1.1%±1.3% to 17.4%±10.0% positive fibers over the same period — a discordance Ellis Unger's decisional memo called "striking"; a separate Western blot analysis in 13 confirmatory-trial (Study 301) patients showed a statistically significant but "exceptionally small" 0.22%-0.32% of normal dystrophin increase

- Sample size: not powered for efficacy — FDA's review states plainly, "Study 201 was not designed as a clinical efficacy study and not powered for efficacy analysis"

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2016/206488Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label (original, 2016) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2016/206488lbl.pdf

- FDA Statistical Review (Xiang Ling, PhD; concurred by Kun Jin, PhD and Hsien Ming J. Hung, PhD) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/206488Orig1s000StatR.pdf

- FDA Summary Review — an unusually rich combined package including (1) the August 8, 2016 Scientific Dispute Resolution Appeal memorandum from Luciana Borio, M.D. (Acting Chief Scientist, SDR Board Chair) to Commissioner Robert Califf, and (2) Ellis Unger, M.D.'s own July 16, 2016 Office Director Decisional Memo — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/206488Orig1s000SumR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov records — Study 201: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01396239; Study 202 (rollover extension): https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01540409; confirmatory Study 4658-301/PROMOVI: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02255552 (no protocol/SAP documents posted for any of the three)

- Pivotal publication: Mendell JR, Rodino-Klapac LR, Sahenk Z, Roush K, Bird L, Lowes LP, Alfano L, Gomez AM, et al. "Eteplirsen for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy." *Ann Neurol.* 2013;74(5):637-647. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1002/ana.23982), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23907995/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Eteplirsen%20for%20the%20treatment%20of%20Duchenne%20muscular%20dystrophy)

**Other resources**

- Sarepta IPD/dataset access via Vivli.org or YODA Project not individually confirmed here; no REMS was required for eteplirsen.

- FDA Advisory Committee (Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee) met April 25, 2016. The committee voted 7-6 against accelerated approval based on the dystrophin surrogate, and separately voted 7-3 (3 abstentions) that the Study 201/202 clinical data did not provide substantial evidence that eteplirsen is effective for DMD — "their vote was in the face of extraordinary pressure from patients and patient advocates to vote for approval. Two of the 3 'yes' votes were from patient representatives" (FDA Summary Review, Ellis Unger memo).

- This is among the most statistically contested accelerated approvals in FDA history: the primary statistical reviewer, the clinical review team, and the Office of Drug Evaluation I Director (Ellis Unger) all recommended against approval; CDER Center Director Janet Woodcock overruled them and granted accelerated approval, prompting Dr. Unger to file a formal Scientific Dispute Resolution appeal — a rare, high-visibility instance of a Center Director-level override documented in a public FDA record.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 206488, §1 "Executive Summary," p.4]*

> "The data, overall, did not provide statistical evidence to support the efficacy of eteplirsen in patients who have a confirmed mutation of the DMD gene that is amenable to exon 51 skipping. The only randomized controlled study submitted by the applicant, Study 201, can only be considered as exploratory because of study design and statistical analysis issues... The statistical analysis plan of Study 201 did not include a method for statistical adjustment for testing multiple doses and/or multiple endpoints... There was no nominally significant difference between eteplirsen 50 mg/kg, eteplirsen 30mg/kg and placebo for the 6MWT, which was the key clinical endpoint in Study 201."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.2.4.1 "Analyses of the Primary Endpoint," pp.9-10]*

> "There was no statistically significant difference between the 50 mg/kg eteplirsen group and placebo at Week 12 (p=0.958)... Patients treated with 30 mg/kg eteplirsen demonstrated 23% increase in the mean percentage of dystrophin positive fibers from baseline to Week 24... the nominal p value (0.002) for the comparison between eteplirsen 30 mg/kg group and the placebo group can only be considered exploratory, as there was no plan to control the type 1 error due to multiple comparisons, and the other comparison between 50mg/kg and placebo in Study 201 was negative."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.2.4.2 "Analyses of 6MWT," p.11]*

> "The result of the MMRM analysis showed a nominally statistically significant difference between the placebo and 30 mg/kg eteplirsen groups, in favor of placebo (p=0.026)... The mITT population was not pre-specified in the SAP. Moreover, the mITT was defined based on the outcome data (instead of enrollment criteria or baseline character). Therefore, analysis on the mITT population could be misleading."

*[verbatim, same source, §5.3 "Conclusions and Recommendations," p.16]*

> "The data overall did not provide statistical evidence to support the efficacy in subjects who have a confirmed mutation of the DMD gene that is amenable to exon 51 skipping."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review — SDR Board memorandum, Luciana Borio, M.D. to Commissioner Robert Califf, August 8, 2016, p.1]*

> "In his scientific dispute resolution (SDR) appeal, dated July 18, 2016, Dr. Unger challenges the basis for a decisional memorandum issued by Janet Woodcock, M.D., Director of the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER). Dr. Woodcock's decisional memorandum concludes that a new drug application (NDA) submitted by Sarepta Therapeutics Inc. (Sarepta) for eteplirsen... meets the standard for accelerated approval under 21 CFR § 314.510... Dr. Unger states that he disagrees... because he does not believe 'the findings on the dystrophin surrogate endpoint are reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.'"

*[verbatim, same source, quoting Woodcock Decisional Memorandum at 2]*

> "Much of the controversy over the adequacy of these assessments relates to the fact that rigorously validated assays were not used to evaluate the initial 3 muscle biopsies, apparently resulting in overestimation of the various readouts and some irreproducibility of IHC and Western blot dystrophin assays. For these reasons, I do not discuss or rely upon the results of these earlier assays, or on re-reads of them."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review — Ellis F. Unger, M.D., Office Director Decisional Memo, July 16, 2016, p.42]*

> "FDA is charged with the responsibility of ensuring that drugs are shown to be effective prior to marketing, based on substantial evidence. If we were to approve eteplirsen without substantial evidence of effectiveness, or on the basis of a surrogate endpoint with a trivial treatment effect, we would quickly find ourselves in the position of having to approve a myriad of ineffective treatments for groups of desperate patients, in essence, allowing marketing based on desperation, patient lobbying, and the desire and need of hope."

*[verbatim, same source, p.2361 excerpt region — Unger memo]*

> "The Advisory Committee voted (7 to 3 with 3 abstentions) that the clinical results of Study 201/202 did not provide substantial evidence that eteplirsen is effective for the treatment of DMD, and their vote was in the face of extraordinary pressure from patients and patient advocates to vote for approval. Two of the 3 'yes' votes were from patient representatives."

### 12. Nusinersen (Spinraza) — NDA 209531

**Sponsor:** Biogen Inc. (antisense oligonucleotide originally developed by Ionis Pharmaceuticals)

**Indication approved:** Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) in pediatric and adult patients — approved as full/regular approval, not accelerated, on the strength of an early-terminated Phase 3 interim analysis

**Approval date:** December 23, 2016

**Pivotal trial:** ENDEAR (Study CS3B), NCT02193074, in infantile-onset SMA (2 copies of SMN2); supportive topline (not yet independently FDA-reviewed at approval) data from CHERISH (Study CS4) in later-onset SMA

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized (2:1), double-blind, sham-procedure-controlled, event-driven, group-sequential Phase 3 trial, stratified by disease duration at screening (≤12 weeks vs. >12 weeks), with a separate randomization list for Japan; early-stopped for efficacy at a prespecified interim analysis

- *Endpoints:* proportion of Hammersmith Infant Neurological Examination (HINE) Section 2 motor-milestone responders (primary); time to death or permanent ventilation, centrally adjudicated by a blinded Event Adjudication Committee (secondary, ranked)

- *Primary analysis:* two-proportion test (motor milestone responder rate, unconditional CI for the difference in response rates) for the primary endpoint; stratified log-rank test (disease duration) for time to death/permanent ventilation

- *Interim/alpha-spending:* group-sequential design with a gamma-family alpha-spending function (γ=-3); interim analysis stopping boundary at a significance level of 0.035; independent DSMB reviewed unblinded interim results and recommended early termination for benefit

- *Missing data/bias:* last-observed-value (LOV) imputation for missing motor-milestone assessments caused by the abrupt interim-driven study stop; FDA reviewer confirmed the primary result was "insensitive to all but very unlikely worst case scenarios for missing data"

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held; Orphan Drug designation; reviewed under a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ENDEAR (Study CS3B): Phase 3, multicenter, randomized 2:1, double-blind, sham-procedure-controlled trial of intrathecal nusinersen (scaled-equivalent 12 mg dose) vs. sham lumbar puncture in infantile-onset SMA (2 copies of SMN2); ~111 subjects planned; randomization stratified by disease duration at screening (≤12 vs. >12 weeks); sham-control patients underwent a sham procedure on the same visit schedule (Days 1, 15, 29, 64, 183, 302) to preserve blinding; blinded safety data monitoring throughout

- Primary efficacy endpoints ranked: (1) proportion of motor-milestone responders per HINE Section 2 (head control, sitting, voluntary grasp, kick, rolling, crawling, standing, walking — voluntary grasp excluded from the responder definition), assessed at the later of Day 183/302/394, requiring both a minimum category-specific point improvement and more improved than worsened categories among the other 7; (2) time to death or permanent ventilation (tracheostomy or ≥16 hrs/day ventilatory support for >21 days absent an acute reversible event), analyzed via stratified log-rank test

- The interim analysis and SAP were expedited/revised mid-trial; per FDA's reviewer, "the interim analysis plan and statistical analysis plan were expedited and revised for [CS3B]," and a late SAP amendment (dated 4/22/2016) added a "more improvement than worsening" requirement to the responder definition that was absent from the original November 2015 SAP

- Sample size: powered for ~78% to differentiate a 38.5% (nusinersen) vs. 11.5% (sham) response rate; the trial was stopped early for efficacy at the prespecified interim analysis (~74% of planned enrollment), based on an independent DSMB recommendation, at a boundary significance level of 0.035 under a gamma-family (γ=-3) alpha-spending function

- Primary results, Interim Efficacy Set (FDA Statistical Review, Table 4): 21/52 (41%) motor-milestone responders in the nusinersen arm vs. 0/30 (0%) in the sham arm, p<0.0001 (primary analysis p-value reported as smaller than 0.025²); treatment effect was consistent across age and disease-duration subgroups and across US/non-US sites

- The interim cutoff created substantial missing data at the final scheduled Day 394 assessment; FDA's reviewer concluded the missing data were likely uninformative (a byproduct of abrupt early stopping rather than differential dropout) and confirmed the primary result was robust to sensitivity analyses under worst-case assumptions

- CHERISH (Study CS4, later-onset SMA, mostly 3 copies of SMN2) was also stopped early for a highly significant effect on the Hammersmith Functional Motor Scale-Expanded (HFMSE) (p=0.000002 per sponsor topline data); FDA's Summary Review states these results "although not yet independently reviewed by FDA, are supportive of efficacy in later-onset SMA patients" and contributed to the broad approved label spanning infantile- and later-onset SMA

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2016/209531Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label (original, 2016) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2016/209531lbl.pdf

- FDA Statistical Review (Tristan S. Massie, PhD; concurred by Kun Jin, PhD and Hsien Ming J. Hung, PhD) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/209531Orig1s000StatR.pdf

- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/209531Orig1s000SumR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (ENDEAR) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02193074 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)

- Pivotal publication: Finkel RS, Mercuri E, Darras BT, Connolly AM, Kuntz NL, Kirschner J, Chiriboga CA, Saito K, et al. "Nusinersen versus Sham Control in Infantile-Onset Spinal Muscular Atrophy." *N Engl J Med.* 2017;377(18):1723-1732. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1702752), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29091570/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Nusinersen%20versus%20Sham%20Control%20in%20Infantile-Onset%20Spinal%20Muscular%20Atrophy)

**Other resources**

- Biogen/Ionis IPD/dataset access via Vivli.org not individually confirmed here.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held for nusinersen. The approval letter confirms Orphan Drug designation and that the application was reviewed using a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher.

- Nusinersen's approval is a notable contrast to the eteplirsen entry above within this same therapeutic-area batch: here, FDA's own statistical reviewer concluded the single pivotal trial's results "seem sufficiently compelling" despite the small sample size, and no internal dispute or override is documented in the public review package.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 209531, §5.1 "Statistical Issues," p.32]*

> "The study was stopped due to early benefit at a prespecified interim analysis at a significance level of 0.035. The interim cutoff together with the interim eligibility requirement to have reached only the Day 183 visit caused significant missing data for the final scheduled assessment time Day 394. However, the missing data could be expected to be uninformative since it is all due to abrupt stopping of the study... Overall, the primary analysis results appear insensitive to all but very unlikely worst case scenarios for missing data."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.2.1 "Study Design," p.5-7]*

> "This is a Phase 3, multicenter, double-blind, randomized, sham-procedure-controlled study... Approximately 111 subjects were to be randomized 2:1 to receive a scaled equivalent 12 mg dose ISIS 396443 or undergo a sham procedure as control, respectively. Randomization was to [be] stratified by... disease duration at Screening ≤ 12 weeks vs. > 12 weeks."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.2.1.4.1 "Sponsor's Results," p.20]*

> "...in the ISIS 396443 group (21; 41%) compared to the sham control group (0; 0%) (p<0.0001)... A consistent effect was observed on the proportion of responders at Day 183, 302, and 394."

*[verbatim, same source, §5.3 "Conclusions and Recommendations," p.33]*

> "The data from study CS3B seem to support the efficacy of the drug. Although the sample size is small the p-value is very small for the primary and several other secondary analyses, there is no suggestion of regional or significant site differences and the results appear reasonably consistent over subgroups. Therefore, although only one controlled efficacy study was submitted in this application for this drug in this rare and serious disease with an unmet need for effective treatments the study results seem sufficiently compelling."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, "Benefit-Risk Summary and Assessment," p.3]*

> "This application includes data from an interim analysis of a double-blind, sham-procedure controlled trial in infantile-onset SMA patients who have 2 copies of the SMN2 gene (Study CS3B). This trial demonstrated a clear and important benefit of nusinersen, with 21/52 (40%) of nusinersen-treated patients who met a motor milestone development responder definition, vs. 0/30 (0%) of sham-procedure controls (p<0.0001)... During the review cycle, the applicant provided the topline results of a double-blind, sham-procedure controlled trial in patients with later-onset SMA Study (Study CS4)... The study was stopped based on a highly statistically significant (p=0.000002) treatment effect on the Hammersmith Functional Motor Scale – Expanded (HFMSE)... The findings of this study, although not yet independently reviewed by FDA, are supportive of efficacy in later-onset SMA patients."

### 13. Deflazacort (Emflaza) — NDA 208684

**Sponsor:** Marathon Pharmaceuticals, LLC (data for the pivotal trials licensed from the original study sponsors; NDA later transferred to PTC Therapeutics)

**Indication approved:** Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in patients age 5 years and older

**Approval date:** February 9, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** Study MP-104-NM-001 ("Study NM-001," US/Canada, 1993-1995) and supportive Study MP-104-NM-002 ("Study NM-002," Italy, 1988 era) — both conducted more than 20 years before this NDA and neither registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (predating routine US trial registration)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled (prednisone), parallel-group trial (NM-001, 1993-1995) plus a supportive randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (NM-002); retroactively reconstructed statistical analysis of decades-old completed trials, with a sponsor-drafted 2015 SAP deviating from the original 1992 protocol's pre-specified primary analysis method (analysis of a historical trial dataset via a modern SAP written decades after study completion, with source documents partially destroyed)

- *Endpoints:* change in average muscle strength score (11-point modified Medical Research Council scale, mean of 34 measurements) from baseline to Week 12 (primary, NM-001); change in muscle strength (0-5 point scale converted to MRC index, sum of 4 measurements) from baseline to 2 years or loss of ambulation, whichever came first (primary, NM-002); timed function tests (time to stand, climb 4 stairs, walk/run 30 feet) as supportive secondary measures

- *Primary analysis:* original 1992 protocol pre-specified ANCOVA (baseline muscle strength, site, treatment as main effects); the sponsor's 2015 SAP substituted a mixed-effect model repeated measures (MMRM) analysis, a change FDA's statistical reviewer flagged as a deviation from the pre-specified protocol method, though the reviewer confirmed both methods gave consistent results

- *Missing data/bias:* CRF (case report form) source documents for the 1990s trial were destroyed at 6 of the original sites; only 56 of 196 (28.6%) original CRF books were recovered, and patient disposition/discontinuation data could not be fully reconstructed; last observation carried forward (LOCF) used by FDA's reviewer as a sensitivity analysis for the primary ANCOVA

- *Regulatory:* standard NDA 505(b)(1) full approval (not accelerated); no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held ("no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion"); orphan drug indication, not subject to PREA

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study NM-001: multicenter (4 US, 5 Canada sites), randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled, parallel-group trial in 196 boys (ages 5-15) with DMD/Becker muscular dystrophy and a documented dystrophin-gene mutation; randomized 1:1:1:1 to deflazacort 0.9 mg/kg/day, deflazacort 1.2 mg/kg/day, prednisone 0.75 mg/kg/day, or placebo, stratified by center and ambulatory status; Segment 1 (Weeks 1-12) compared each active arm to placebo; in Segment 2, placebo patients were re-randomized to one of the three active arms for a further 40 weeks. First patient enrolled April 26, 1993; study completed April 20, 1995; original protocol finalized December 18, 1992, but the SAP for the "available data" was not drafted by Marathon and finalized until January 19, 2015 — 20+ years later, ahead of NDA submission

- Study NM-002: multicenter Italian trial (1988 enrollment era), randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, in 31 ambulatory boys (ages 5-11) with confirmed DMD, testing an alternate deflazacort regimen (2 mg/kg once every 2 days) vs. placebo over up to 2 years or loss of ambulation

- Primary endpoint (NM-001): change from baseline to Week 12 in average muscle strength score (11-point modified MRC scale, mean of 34 measurements); primary endpoint (NM-002): change in muscle strength (0-5 scale converted to an MRC index, sum of 4 measurements) from baseline to Year 2 or loss of ambulation

- FDA's statistical reviewer determined the protocol's stated "key secondary endpoint" was ambiguous, noting: "The key secondary endpoint as specified in the protocol is not clear," and independently concluded — based on the study-objective language and design — that change in muscle strength score from baseline to Week 52 (not the sponsor's proposed Week 12-to-Week 52 change) was the more sensible key secondary endpoint

- Primary results (NM-001, sponsor's MMRM analysis, Table 3): active-vs-placebo differences in Week-12 muscle-strength change of 0.25 (deflazacort 0.9 mg/kg/day, p=0.0173), 0.36 (deflazacort 1.2 mg/kg/day, p=0.0003), and 0.37 (prednisone, p=0.0002); FDA's independently re-run MMRM and ANCOVA analyses (with LOCF for the limited ~4% missing Week-12 data) produced similar, slightly stronger results (e.g., deflazacort 1.2 mg/kg/day p<0.0001)

- Supportive NM-002 result: the Year-2 (primary time point) muscle-strength change was not statistically significant, with FDA's reviewer noting the analysis "was not conclusive because of the high percentage (about 50%) of missing data," though Month-6 and Year-1 treatment effects (with limited missing data) were nominally significant

- Dose comparison: deflazacort 1.2 mg/kg/day showed a small additional benefit over 0.9 mg/kg/day at Week 12 but a higher adverse-event incidence and no additional Week-52 benefit, supporting 0.9 mg/kg/day as the labeled optimal dose (per FDA Summary Review benefit-risk assessment)

- Sample size: not re-derived by FDA from first principles given the trial's age; original NM-001 protocol targeted 180 boys (actual N=196 randomized)

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2017/208684Orig1s000,208685Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label (original, 2017) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/208684s000,208685s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/208684,208685Orig1s000StatR.pdf

- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/208684,208685Orig1s000SumR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov: no record was identified for Study NM-001 or Study NM-002 — both conducted (1988-1995) before routine US trial registration; a large number of later, non-pivotal deflazacort/DMD trials are registered (e.g., NCT02295748, NCT02251600) but do not correspond to the pivotal efficacy studies

- Pivotal publication: Griggs RC, Miller JP, Greenberg CR, Fehlings DL, Pestronk A, Mendell JR, Moxley RT 3rd, King W, Kissel JT, Cwik V, Vanasse M, Florence JM, Pandya S, Dubow JS, Meyer JM. "Efficacy and safety of deflazacort vs prednisone and placebo for Duchenne muscular dystrophy." *Neurology.* 2016;87(20):2123-2131. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1212/WNL.0000000000003217), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27566742/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Efficacy%20and%20safety%20of%20deflazacort%20vs%20prednisone%20and%20placebo%20for%20Duchenne%20muscular%20dystrophy)

**Other resources**

- Marathon/PTC Therapeutics IPD/dataset access via Vivli.org or YODA Project not individually confirmed here.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held. Per the FDA Summary Review: "This application was not referred for review to an advisory committee, because outside expertise was not necessary. There were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion."

- Regulatory/pricing context (non-statistical): deflazacort had been used off-label in the US via personal importation for DMD for years before this NDA, at a fraction of the price Marathon initially set for the FDA-approved product in early 2017, which drew significant public and congressional criticism — noted here for context though it does not bear on the trial statistics documented above.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 208684, §3.1 "Data and Analysis Quality," p.5]*

> "For the pivotal Study NM-001, all source data were sent to [REDACTED] for entry into a SAS database. Original CRF books were then destroyed in 6 sites and a total of 56 of 196 (28.6%) original completed CRF books were located and retrieved... Both studies were conducted more than 20 years ago. The statistical analysis plans (SAP) for the available data were drafted by Marathon in 2015. The analyses methods stated in the SAP for Study NM-001 were deviated from those pre-specified in the protocol."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.2.1.2 "Statistical Methodologies," p.8]*

> "The primary analysis method specified in the protocol is an analysis of covariance model (ANCOVA)... The statistical analysis plan changed the primary analysis from ANCOVA to a mixed-effect model repeated measures (MMRM). The applicant's reason for the change was that the technology to perform MMRM was not yet available at the time the study was conducted, but is the most appropriate analysis technique for data that were collected repeatedly over time."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.2.1.4 "Results and Conclusions," pp.9-11]*

> "Both analyses showed a statistically significant difference between active treatment and placebo for each of the 3 active treatment groups. An increase in average muscle strength was observed at Week 12 in each of the active treatment groups, compared to a decrease in average muscle strength in the placebo group. Differences from placebo in change from baseline in the muscle strength score are 0.25, 0.35 and 0.37 for the deflazacort 0.9 mg/kg/day group, the deflazacort 1.2 mg/kg/day group and the prednisone group, respectively."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, "Benefit-Risk Summary and Assessment," p.3]*

> "Study NM-001 was a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 52-week study conducted in the US and Canada... Efficacy was evaluated by assessing the change between Baseline and Week 12 in the average strength of 18 muscle groups. That change was significantly better for deflazacort 0.9 mg/kg/day than for placebo... Results on several timed measures of patient function... numerically favor deflazacort over placebo, and support the clinical meaningfulness of the modest effect on muscle strength demonstrated by the primary endpoint."

**Reverse-engineered SAP** [inferred]

- [inferred] No genuine contemporaneous SAP for either pivotal trial's original conduct is public; the only "SAP" on file is the sponsor's 2015 retrospective document, itself quoted verbatim above and explicitly flagged by FDA as deviating from the 1992 protocol's ANCOVA specification — traced to FDA Statistical Review §3.1 and §3.2.1.2.

### 14. Cerliponase alfa (Brineura) — BLA 761052

**Sponsor:** BioMarin Pharmaceutical Inc.

**Indication approved:** To slow the loss of ambulation in symptomatic pediatric patients 3 years of age and older with late infantile neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis type 2 (CLN2) disease, also known as tripeptidyl peptidase 1 (TPP1) deficiency (a form of Batten disease)

**Approval date:** April 27, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** Study 190-201/202 (continuous single-arm, open-label, intracerebroventricular dosing study), NCT01907087, compared against non-treatment natural-history cohort Study 190-901 (the DEM-CHILD registry)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label, dose-escalation trial (no concurrent control) with efficacy assessed via patient-level matched comparison against an external natural-history registry cohort (matched comparison against an independently conducted, multi-rater natural-history registry, distinct from the taxonomy's existing "non-inferiority analysis against a fixed historical-control threshold," which uses no patient-level matching)

- *Endpoints:* Motor and Language domains of the CLN2 Clinical Rating Scale (clinician-reported outcome), responder analysis (absence of an unreversed 2-category decline or a score of 0) in the Motor domain over 96 weeks (final primary analysis, after the 48- and 72-week analyses were found insufficient)

- *Primary analysis:* matched-pairs responder analysis (McNemar's exact test and Fisher's exact test) comparing proportion of "non-decliners" between 22 treated patients and 42 natural-history patients matched on baseline Motor score, age (±3 months), and genotype; supportive time-to-decline, ordinal, and binary logistic regression analyses on the full unmatched populations

- *Missing data/bias:* COA (clinical outcome assessment) rating-scale comparability issues between the treatment-study raters and the natural-history-registry raters (documented via a video comparability sub-study), with a "next observation carried backward" (NOCB) sensitivity analysis for irregularly spaced natural-history visits

- *Regulatory:* three sequential Center Director briefings during a single review cycle, with the first two (48-week and 72-week data) concluding "no substantial evidence of efficacy" before a third briefing on 96-week data supported approval; Breakthrough Therapy Designation (initially denied, later granted); Priority Review; Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 190-201 (with continuation as Study 190-202): single-arm, open-label, dose-escalation trial of intracerebroventricular (ICV) cerliponase alfa administered via a surgically implanted reservoir/catheter, in 24 symptomatic pediatric CLN2 patients enrolled at sites in Germany, the UK, and elsewhere; 12 of 24 patients were already enrolled at initial IND opening (July 2014); no concurrent placebo or untreated arm — comparator was the independently conducted Study 190-901 natural-history cohort (part of the multi-site DEM-CHILD registry), from which 42 of 69 enrolled patients were ultimately judged evaluable (after excluding patients without a score assessment, patients who switched onto cerliponase alfa, and one identical twin)

- Efficacy endpoint construction was heavily disputed and evolved during review: the applicant's original (pre-BLA) proposed responder analysis used an absence of unreversed 2-category decline or score of 0 in the combined Motor-Language total score at 48 weeks; FDA's COA statistical reviewer found the video comparability study showed insufficient rating consistency in the Language domain specifically, and required the primary analysis be restricted to the Motor domain alone

- Because the 48-week and 72-week Motor-domain matched analyses (both reviewed at dedicated Center Director briefings, December 15, 2016 and January 27, 2017) did not show "substantial evidence of efficacy," FDA requested additional 96-week data; the sponsor submitted a supplemental SAP (March 9, 2017) and a November 1, 2016 data cut providing 96 weeks of follow-up for all subjects, reviewed at a third Center Director briefing (April 18, 2017) that recommended full approval

- Primary result (96-week data, 17 matched pairs from the 22-treated/42-natural-history matched population): 21/42 (50%) natural-history patients experienced an unreversed 2-category decline or score of 0 in the Motor domain over 96 weeks, versus 1/22 (5%) of cerliponase alfa-treated patients; the upper bound of the 95% CI for the McNemar's-exact odds ratio was below 1, and supportive time-to-decline, ordinal, and binary logistic regression analyses on the larger unmatched 42/22 population were consistent

- Given the complexity of the natural-history comparison, FDA's statistical review team sent the sponsor over 30 information requests across the review cycle addressing dataset transcription errors, imputed dates of birth, and analysis-population definitions

- Sample size: N=24 enrolled in Study 201/202 (22 in the primary Population #1 efficacy analysis, after excluding 2 patients without motor/language symptoms at baseline); N=42 evaluable in the natural-history comparator (from 69 in the underlying DEM-CHILD database)

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2017/761052Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label (original, 2017) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/761052lbl.pdf

- FDA Statistical Review (Min Min, PhD, Primary Statistical Reviewer; Yeh-Fong Chen, PhD, Statistical Team Leader; Lili Garrard, PhD, COA Statistical Reviewer) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/761052Orig1s000StatR.pdf

- FDA Clinical/Medical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/761052Orig1s000MedR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01907087 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)

- Pivotal publication: Schulz A, Ajayi T, Specchio N, de Los Reyes E, Gissen P, Ballon D, Dyke JP, Cahan H, et al. "Study of Intraventricular Cerliponase Alfa for CLN2 Disease." *N Engl J Med.* 2018;378(20):1898-1907. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1712649), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29688815/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Study%20of%20Intraventricular%20Cerliponase%20Alfa%20for%20CLN2%20Disease)

**Other resources**

- BioMarin IPD/dataset access via Vivli.org or YODA Project not individually confirmed here.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held: "There was no Advisory Committee Meeting. All scientific and methodological review issues" were resolved through the internal information-request and Center Director-briefing process described above (FDA Summary Review).

- Breakthrough Therapy Designation was initially denied and later granted (August 27, 2016) after submission of additional analyses; Brineura also received a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher and Orphan Drug designation.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, BLA 761052, §3.1.1, p.26-27]*

> "The COA statistical reviewer disagreed with the applicant's conclusion that adequate CLN2 rating scale similarity was demonstrated between the control and treatment studies... the Agency disagreed with the applicant's proposed responder analysis using an absence of an unreversed (sustained) 2-point rate (slope) of decline or a score of 0 in the Motor-Language total score over 48 weeks... because of the inconsistent scale ratings in the Language domain... the COA statistical reviewer concludes that the efficacy evaluation primarily should focus on the Motor domain."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.2.1, "History of FDA Information Requests and Meetings," p.28]*

> "12/15/2016 First center director (CD) briefing (48-week data): no substantial evidence of efficacy was found... 01/27/2017 Second center director (CD) briefing (72-week data): no substantial evidence of efficacy was found... 04/18/2017 Third center director (CD) briefing (96-week data): full approval recommended for the study drug."

*[verbatim, same source, §3.2.2, p.38]*

> "Based on this start time, 21 (50%) patients in the Study 901 experienced an unreversed (sustained) 2-category decline or unreversed score of 0 in the Motor domain of the CLN2 measure over a 96 week period and 5% (1 out of 22) subjects in Study 201/202 declined."

*[verbatim, same source, §5.2 "Conclusions and Recommendations," p.38]*

> "All the analysis results based on 96-week data support the indication of Brineura (cerliponase alfa) to slow the loss of ambulation in symptomatic pediatric patients 3 years of age and older with late infantile neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis type 2 (CLN2)."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, "Benefit-Risk Summary and Assessment"]*

> "The BLA was submitted on May 27, 2016... It was granted Priority Review. The BLA included efficacy data for up to 48 weeks of treatment. During the review of the BLA it became apparent that the efficacy data at the 48 week timepoint was not robust enough to demonstrate a treatment effect. The Agency requested sequentially efficacy data for the 72-week datapoint... and 96 weeks... the review team had 33 information requests sent to the applicant. Three Center Director briefings were held for this BLA (December 15, 2016; January 27, 2017; and April 18, 2017)."

### 15. Vestronidase alfa-vjbk (Mepsevii) — BLA 761047

**Sponsor:** Ultragenyx Pharmaceutical Inc.

**Indication approved:** Mucopolysaccharidosis VII (MPS VII, Sly syndrome), an ultra-rare lysosomal storage disease

**Approval date:** November 15, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** Study UX003-CL301, NCT02230566 — a randomized, placebo-controlled, "Blind Start," single-crossover (delayed-start) trial; supportive Study CL201 (Phase 1/2 dose-finding, NCT01856218) and Study CL203 (patients <5 years, NCT02418455)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, placebo-controlled, "Blind Start," single-crossover (delayed-start) trial in an ultra-rare disease population (N=12) — a named design (Signorovitch 2014) in which subjects and investigators remain blinded to the timing of each patient's individual crossover from placebo to active drug ("Blind Start"/staggered-crossover design is more specific than the taxonomy's existing general "small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population" entry and was explicitly contested by FDA as a study design during pre-BLA meetings)

- *Endpoints:* urinary glycosaminoglycan (uGAG) excretion, percent reduction from baseline (primary endpoint ex-US; no primary endpoint was formally declared for US regulatory purposes given the heterogeneous population); multi-domain clinical responder index (MDRI) incorporating six-minute walk test (6MWT), forced vital capacity (FVC), shoulder flexion, visual acuity, and BOT-2 fine/gross motor scores as key secondary/exploratory measures

- *Primary analysis:* Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) modeling for uGAG (sponsor, ex-US endpoint); FDA-conducted supplementary ANCOVA and permutation tests comparing the UX003-treatment period to each patient's own prior placebo period on 6MWT, since the sponsor's original analysis did not exploit the placebo-period data from the crossover design

- *Missing data/bias:* no natural-history comparator was used; FDA repeatedly flagged the absence of "rigorously collected natural history data to ensure a reliable comparator," missing data from heterogeneous assessment schedules, and non-independence of placebo/treatment-period observations within the same 9 of 12 patients who contributed both

- *Regulatory:* FDA statistical review's bottom-line conclusion ("no substantial evidence is demonstrated supporting the efficacy of UX003") was not adopted by the clinical review team, who recommended approval based on totality-of-evidence reasoning about disease rarity/heterogeneity and individual patient narratives — reusing this census's existing "statistical reviewer's non-approval recommendation overruled by division leadership" pattern (DaTscan precedent), here at the clinical-team level rather than a single Division Director; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held; regular (not accelerated) approval

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study UX003-CL301: Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, placebo-controlled, Blind Start, single-crossover trial; 12 MPS VII patients ages 8-25 (median 14) randomized 1:1:1:1 to 4 groups differing only in the length of an initial blinded placebo period (Group A: no placebo, active from Day 1; Group B: 8 weeks placebo then crossover; Group C: 16 weeks placebo then crossover; Group D: 24 weeks placebo then crossover), all subsequently receiving UX003 4 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks through Week 48; FDA's pre-BLA-meeting minutes record the Agency's initial skepticism: "We cannot agree with the study design at this time. The Blind Start trial design may be appropriate in certain circumstances, such as studies with objective endpoints like laboratory measurements. However, we need to have further discussion regarding study endpoints before we can agree on the study design"

- No primary endpoint was declared for US regulatory purposes; the sponsor instead argued efficacy via the "totality of the clinical evidence," proposing uGAG reduction (the primary endpoint accepted in the EU/rest-of-world) plus a 6-domain multi-domain clinical responder index (MDRI), of which FDA's clinical team ultimately judged only the 6MWT at 24 weeks suitable for efficacy evaluation

- The sponsor's efficacy claim compared each patient's own post-crossover (UX003) period to their pre-crossover (placebo) baseline, without a formal across-cohort (placebo-period-vs-treatment-period, using the full crossover structure) comparison; FDA's statistical reviewer performed additional ANCOVA and permutation-test analyses to test superiority of the UX003 period over the placebo period on 6MWT change from baseline at 24 weeks, given 9 of the 12 patients contributed data to both periods (raising a within-patient correlation/independence concern for any naive analysis)

- FDA's statistical review concluded uGAG results were confirmed as reported but that "no substantial evidence is demonstrated supporting the efficacy of UX003 in treating patients with MPS VII" based on the available quantitative analyses, while acknowledging "UX003's effect appears to increase gradually over time" and that "no quantitative analysis will overcome the small sample size and lack of assessments in some patients for some of the outcomes"

- FDA's clinical review team took a different view: an observed 18-meter mean increase in 6MWT distance at 24 weeks was interpreted as "a trend toward clinically meaningful improvement," bolstered by individual patient narratives showing 65-105 meter improvements with longer treatment duration; the clinical team's memo states it is "willing to accept this degree of uncertainty at the week 24 time point and recommend approval," acknowledging "the lower bound of the standard error includes the possibility for harm" but judging that possibility unlikely and monitorable post-marketing

- Sample size: N=12 total in the pivotal trial (3-4 patients per Blind Start staggered-entry cohort), reflecting MPS VII's extreme rarity; no subgroup analyses were performed due to sample size

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2017/761047Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label (original, 2017) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/761047s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/761047Orig1s000StatR.pdf

- FDA Clinical/Medical Review (contains both the negative statistical conclusion and the clinical team's differing benefit-risk recommendation) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/761047Orig1s000MedR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02230566 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)

- Pivotal publication: Harmatz P, Whitley CB, Wang RY, Bauer M, Song W, Haller C. "A novel Blind Start study design to investigate vestronidase alfa for mucopolysaccharidosis VII, an ultra-rare genetic disease." *Mol Genet Metab.* 2018;123(4):488-494. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ymgme.2018.02.006), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29478819/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=A%20novel%20Blind%20Start%20study%20design%20to%20investigate%20vestronidase%20alfa%20for%20mucopolysaccharidosis%20VII)

**Other resources**

- Ultragenyx IPD/dataset access via Vivli.org or YODA Project not individually confirmed here.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held: "An Advisory Committee was not convened during the review of BLA 761047" (FDA Medical Review).

- This entry is a useful methodological companion to cerliponase alfa/Brineura (#4 above, same year, also BioMarin-sponsored program): both use N<25 trials in ultra-rare lysosomal/neurodegenerative diseases, but Brineura's positive approval was grounded in a statistically supportive 96-week responder analysis, whereas Mepsevii's approval proceeded despite the primary statistical reviewer's explicit "no substantial evidence" conclusion, illustrating a real divergence in how FDA divisions handle formally negative statistics in ultra-rare-disease programs.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, BLA 761047, "Type B, pre-BLA meeting" minutes excerpt, p.5]*

> "We cannot agree with the study design at this time. The Blind Start trial design may be appropriate in certain circumstances, such as studies with objective endpoints like laboratory measurements. However, we need to have further discussion regarding study endpoints before we can agree on the study design."

*[verbatim, same source, §1 "Executive Summary," p.3]*

> "Study CL301 contained 12 patients with MPS VII between the ages of 8 and 25 years (median age 14 years) who received UX003 4 mg/kg every two weeks for 24 to 48 weeks. Due to the heterogeneity of the patient population, efficacy of UX003 in treating MPS VII patients was based on the totality of the clinical evidence. No primary endpoint was declared beforehand."

*[verbatim, same source, §5.2 "Conclusions and Recommendations," p.19]*

> "According to the reviewer's thorough evaluation and the applicant's confirmation of the reviewer's results through 48 weeks, no substantial evidence is demonstrated supporting the efficacy of UX003 in treating patients with MPS VII, i.e., Sly syndrome. We note, however, UX003's effect appears to increase gradually over time. While many other analyses could be performed, no quantitative analysis will overcome the small sample size and lack of assessments in some patients for some of the outcomes."

*[verbatim, FDA Clinical/Medical Review, Dr. Donohue CDTL Comment]*

> "The point estimate of an 18-meter increase in mean 6MWT distance after 24 weeks of treatment may reflect a trend toward clinically meaningful improvement... careful review of individual patient narratives identified 3 patients with 65 to 105-meter improvement in 6MWT with longer durations of treatment... It is our conclusion that it may not be feasible in this exceedingly rare and heterogeneous disease to generate statistically significant evidence of efficacy for a drug with a modest, but clinically meaningful, effect size... the clinical team is willing to accept this degree of uncertainty at the week 24 time point and recommend approval."

### 16. Tezacaftor/ivacaftor; ivacaftor (Symdeko) — NDA 210491

**Sponsor:** Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated

**Indication approved:** Cystic fibrosis (CF) in patients age 12 and older who are homozygous for the F508del mutation in the CFTR gene, or who have at least one mutation in the CFTR gene that is responsive to tezacaftor/ivacaftor based on in vitro and/or clinical evidence

**Approval date:** February 12, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** EVOLVE (Study 106), NCT02347657 (F508del homozygous); EXPAND (Study 108), NCT02392234 (F508del/residual-function heterozygous, crossover); supportive Study 107, NCT02516410 (F508del/minimal-function heterozygous — negative, contributed to the boundaries of the approved population)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two independent randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trials supporting distinct genotype populations — EVOLVE (parallel-group) and EXPAND (2-period, 3-treatment [tezacaftor/ivacaftor, ivacaftor monotherapy, placebo], 6-sequence crossover) — plus a third, differently-genotyped parallel-group trial (Study 107) that was negative and helped define the exclusion of minimal-function mutations from the label

- *Endpoints:* absolute change from baseline in percent-predicted FEV1 (ppFEV1) through Week 24 (EVOLVE primary) or to the average of Week 4/Week 8 (EXPAND primary, Study 107 primary at Week 12); relative change in ppFEV1, pulmonary exacerbation rate, BMI change, and CFQ-R Respiratory Domain score as key secondary endpoints across all three trials

- *Primary analysis:* mixed model repeated measures (MMRM) with treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction, and baseline ppFEV1/baseline-by-visit interaction as fixed effects (EVOLVE, Study 107); MMRM with treatment, period, and baseline ppFEV1 as fixed effects, subject as random effect (EXPAND crossover); negative binomial regression for pulmonary exacerbation rate

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing within each trial (absolute ppFEV1 change → relative ppFEV1 change → other secondary endpoints), each gated on the prior endpoint's significance

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held, given prior approvals of ivacaftor and lumacaftor/ivacaftor in overlapping genotypes; orphan/CF-specific regulatory pathway, not subject to PREA

**Trial design & endpoints**

- EVOLVE (Study 106): Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter trial in patients 12+ with CF homozygous for F508del; 504 subjects randomized (248 tezacaftor/ivacaftor, 256 placebo), stratified by age, sex, geographic region, baseline ppFEV1, common CF medication use, and P. aeruginosa infection status; 24-week treatment period followed by an option to enroll in rollover extension Study 110

- EXPAND (Study 108): Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 2-period, 3-treatment, 6-sequence crossover trial in patients 12+ with CF heterozygous for F508del and a second CFTR mutation predicted to have residual function; subjects randomized 1:1:1:1:1:1 across 6 treatment sequences combining tezacaftor/ivacaftor, ivacaftor-alone, and placebo across two 8-week treatment periods, allowing a within-patient assessment of tezacaftor's individual contribution to the combination

- Study 107: Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial (168 subjects, 1:1) in patients heterozygous for F508del and a second CFTR mutation not likely to respond to tezacaftor and/or ivacaftor (minimal-function genotype) — a negative trial that, per FDA's statistical review, factored into limiting the approved indication to genotypes with demonstrated response, rather than all F508del-heterozygous patients broadly

- Primary results (EVOLVE, FAS, Table 12/13): mean ppFEV1 absolute change from baseline through Week 24 was 3.4 (tezacaftor/ivacaftor, N=248) vs. -0.6 (placebo, N=256), a difference of 4.0 percentage points (95% CI 3.1-4.8, p<0.0001); relative change difference was 6.8 percentage points (95% CI 5.3-8.3, p<0.0001)

- Primary result (Study 107, negative trial): tezacaftor/ivacaftor showed a 5.1-point absolute ppFEV1 difference over placebo (95% CI 3.2-7.0) with a BMI treatment difference also reported; FDA's statistical reviewer noted this and other Study 107 results could "only [be] considered as the strong evidence of efficacy of TEZ/IVA although these results are nominally significant according to the hierarchical testing procedure" — i.e., statistically positive on ppFEV1 in this genotype but not judged sufficient by itself to support labeling minimal-function heterozygotes, given the totality of the CFTR-response evidence package

- Combination-rule statistical issue: FDA's review specifically evaluated "whether the overall study program meets the combination rule for fixed dose combination drug development" — i.e., whether data demonstrated tezacaftor's individual contribution to the tezacaftor/ivacaftor combination, addressed primarily through EXPAND's ivacaftor-monotherapy treatment arm

- Sample size/design rationale: Studies 106 and 108 were independently powered and analyzed; no formal cross-trial pooling was used for the primary approval decision — FDA's conclusions rest on "two independent studies" (106 and 108) each independently meeting the primary endpoint

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2018/210491Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label (original, 2018) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/210491lbl.pdf

- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/210491Orig1s000StatR.pdf

- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/210491Orig1s000SumR.pdf

### 17. Pegvaliase-pqpz (Palynziq) — BLA 761079

**Sponsor:** BioMarin Pharmaceutical Inc.

**Indication approved:** To reduce blood phenylalanine (Phe) concentrations in adult patients with phenylketonuria (PKU) who have uncontrolled blood Phe concentrations greater than 600 micromol/L on existing management

**Approval date:** May 24, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** PRISM clinical program — Study 165-301 (open-label, randomized dose-regimen induction/titration/maintenance study, NCT01819727) and Study 165-302 (4-part randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized-withdrawal study, NCT01889862)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized-withdrawal (randomized discontinuation) trial design — patients who responded during open-label induction/titration/maintenance are re-randomized to continue active drug or switch to placebo for a fixed period (Keyword_Taxonomy.md does not currently list a "randomized withdrawal/randomized discontinuation" trial-design term; distinct from the taxonomy's crossover and Blind-Start designs)

- *Endpoints:* change in blood Phe concentration from Part 2 baseline to Part 2 Week 8 (primary, Study 302 Part 2); ADHD RS-IV Inattention Subscale and PKU-specific Profile of Mood States (POMS) subscales (secondary, neurocognitive/neuropsychiatric)

- *Primary analysis:* mixed-model repeated measures (MMRM) with treatment group, visit, and treatment-by-visit interaction, adjusting for baseline blood Phe, comparing 20 mg/day-vs-20 mg/day-placebo and 40 mg/day-vs-40 mg/day-placebo separately

- *Missing data/bias:* modified Intent-to-Treat (mITT) population restricted to subjects who reached target dose and had ≥20% blood Phe reduction from their Study 301/other prior-study baseline before randomization into the Part 2 withdrawal phase — a responder-enriched analysis population inherent to the randomized-withdrawal design

- *Regulatory:* Priority Review (reclassified from standard review during the review cycle); Boxed Warning for anaphylaxis; REMS with Elements to Assure Safe Use (ETASU), including prescriber certification and mandatory in-office observation after each dose during induction/titration; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 165-301: Phase 3, open-label, randomized, multicenter study assessing an induction/titration/maintenance (I/T/M) dosing regimen of subcutaneous pegvaliase (starting 2.5 mg once weekly, increased in increments up to a 20 mg/day or 40 mg/day target dose based on trough ADA activity/blood Phe response) in 261 subjects randomized 1:1 to different starting dose-escalation regimens; establishes the dosing algorithm and initial blood-Phe response used to select patients for the randomized-withdrawal study

- Study 165-302: 4-part design — Part 1 (open-label blood-Phe screening/eligibility assessment for entry into Part 2); Part 2 (the pivotal Randomized Discontinuation Trial [RDT]: responders from Part 1, previously exposed to pegvaliase, re-randomized in a double-blind, placebo-controlled fashion to continue pegvaliase [20 or 40 mg/day] or switch to matching placebo for 8 weeks); Part 3 (PK/PD comparability of vial-and-syringe vs. prefilled-syringe presentations); Part 4 (long-term open-label extension); 215 subjects enrolled across 29 US sites, with the Part 2 sample size adjusted downward (via Protocol Amendment 3) from the original target to ~85 randomized subjects "due to limited enrollment opportunity of subjects from the adult PKU patient population in the United States"

- Primary efficacy endpoint (Part 2): change in blood Phe concentration from Part 2 baseline to Part 2 Week 8, analyzed on the mITT population (subjects who reached target dose with ≥20% blood-Phe reduction from their pre-Part-2 baseline) via the pre-specified MMRM, separately for the 20 mg/day-vs-placebo and 40 mg/day-vs-placebo comparisons

- Primary result: "Both active arms maintained blood Phe significantly better than their corresponding placebo with p-values less than 0.0001. The difference in LS means in the 20 mg/day arm versus placebo comparison was numerically higher than for the 40 mg/day arm versus placebo comparison" (FDA Multi-Discipline Review)

- Safety/design interaction: because anaphylaxis and injection-related reactions were a known risk, treatment compliance and blinding-integrity were closely monitored; compliance exceeded 96% in the mITT population across both arms

- Sample size: 261 total subjects across Study 301 (dose-regimen assignment); within Study 302 Part 2, the randomized-withdrawal population was reduced to approximately 86 (40 mg/day-eligible) and 78 (20 mg/day-eligible) subjects reaching the target dose per the disposition tables, reflecting substantial attrition from screening through randomization inherent to the multi-part design

### 18. Migalastat (Galafold) — NDA 208623

**Sponsor:** Amicus Therapeutics, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Fabry disease in adults with a genetic variant of the alpha-galactosidase A (GLA) gene determined to be "amenable" based on in vitro assay data — accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.510 (Subpart H)

**Approval date:** August 10, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** FACETS (Study AT1001-011), NCT00925301 (randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled); ATTRACT (Study AT1001-012), NCT01218659 (randomized, open-label, active-controlled switch trial vs. enzyme replacement therapy)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (FACETS) plus a randomized, open-label, active-controlled non-inferiority switch trial from ERT (ATTRACT); efficacy population narrowed after unblinding because a companion in vitro amenability assay was still undergoing validation in parallel with the trial ("efficacy population redefined post hoc by a concurrently-validated companion assay," distinct from the taxonomy's existing FDA-conducted independent expansion/contraction-of-population entries, which involve FDA-driven not assay-driven changes)

- *Endpoints:* percent change from baseline to Month 6 in average number of GL-3 (globotriaosylceramide) inclusions per kidney interstitial capillary (KIC) by light-microscopy biopsy — the same histological endpoint previously used for accelerated approval of agalsidase beta (Fabrazyme) — analyzed as a ≥50% responder rate (FACETS primary); annualized eGFR slope (ATTRACT, non-inferiority vs. continued ERT)

- *Primary analysis:* proportion of patients achieving ≥50% GL-3 reduction, compared between arms in both the full ITT population and the reduced "ITT-amenable" population (patients later confirmed to have an amenable GLA variant by the validated assay); no formal multiplicity-controlled hypothesis test reported as statistically significant on the pre-specified primary endpoint in the population ultimately deemed relevant

- *Missing data/bias:* companion diagnostic/assay validation occurring in parallel with, rather than before, the pivotal trial — of 67 patients enrolled in FACETS based on a non-final "CT HEK-293" assay classification, 17 were reclassified as "non-amenable" once the validated GLP HEK-293 assay was finalized, shrinking the efficacy-relevant population from 67 to 50 (45 with baseline-and-Month-6 histology data)

- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval (Subpart H) recommended by the review team despite FDA's Division of Gastroenterology and Inborn Errors Products (DGIEP) having concluded in 2015 that the same trial data did not reach statistical significance on its pre-specified endpoints and did not support a valid surrogate; sponsor's initial 2015-2016 attempt to submit for accelerated approval was rejected pre-filing by DGIEP, followed by a 2016-2017 detour toward a new gastrointestinal-symptom confirmatory trial (abandoned as infeasible, 5-7 years to conduct), before CDER leadership involvement in 2017 led DGIEP to permit NDA submission on the existing "collective body of evidence"; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- FACETS (AT1001-011): Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; patients 16+ with Fabry disease randomized 1:1 to migalastat 123 mg orally every other day or placebo for 6 months (Stage 1), with GL-3 inclusions per KIC counted via light microscopy at baseline and Month 6; 67 patients enrolled (43 female, 24 male) based on a preliminary ("CT HEK-293") in vitro amenability assay; as the validated GLP HEK-293 assay completed validation in parallel with the trial, 17 of the 67 were reclassified "non-amenable," reducing the primary efficacy ("ITT-amenable") population to 50, and further to 45 with complete baseline-and-Month-6 histology data

- ATTRACT (AT1001-012): Phase 3, randomized, open-label, active-controlled (continued enzyme replacement therapy) switch/non-inferiority trial in Fabry patients already on ERT, comparing 18-month change in annualized eGFR slope between those switched to oral migalastat and those remaining on ERT

- Primary result (FACETS ITT population, N=67, including 17 non-amenable patients): ≥50% GL-3 reduction achieved in 13/34 (38%) migalastat vs. 9/33 (27%) placebo (p=0.3, not significant); in the ITT-amenable population with available histology (N=45): 13/25 (52%) migalastat vs. 9/20 (45%) placebo — also not a statistically significant difference

- Subgroup pattern used to support approval: of the 45 ITT-amenable evaluable patients, 28 had low baseline GL-3 substrate burden (<0.3 inclusions per KIC, indicating milder disease) and showed minimal, comparable change in both arms; among the 17 patients with higher baseline substrate burden (≥0.3), 7/9 migalastat-treated patients achieved the primary responder criterion vs. 2/8 on placebo — a result concentrated in male patients (5/7 [71%] migalastat vs. 4/9 [44%] placebo) more than female patients (8/18 [44%] migalastat vs. 5/11 [45%] placebo, i.e., no apparent drug effect in females)

- FDA's Multi-Discipline Review states plainly that the histological endpoint "previously formed the basis for accelerated approval of agalsidase beta" and, despite the null result in the primary pre-specified ITT-amenable analysis, "the review team recommends approval for Galafold 123 mg orally once every other day under the accelerated approval regulations as described in 21 CFR 314.510 (subpart H)" based on the totality of the subgroup, biomarker, and mechanistic evidence

- Regulatory history (from the Division's own "Regulatory History" memo): at a September 2015 meeting, DGIEP "did not agree with [Amicus's] proposed plan, noting that Study 011 did not reach statistical significance for the pre-specified study endpoints and that Study 012 was not powered to test a specific statistical hypothesis," and further noted "the applicant had not provided sufficient evidence to support treatment effects on GL-3 deposition in renal interstitial capillaries as a surrogate endpoint." A subsequent 2016 proposal for a new GI-symptom confirmatory trial was abandoned when a feasibility report concluded it would take 5-7 years. Only after the applicant's 2017 escalation to "interactions with CDER leadership" did DGIEP agree, in a July 7, 2017 letter, that Amicus could submit an NDA on the existing data

- Sample size: FACETS N=67 (50 amenable, 45 with complete histology); ATTRACT N not separately re-derived here — non-inferiority margin/eGFR analysis reviewed by FDA's Division of Cardiovascular and Renal Products as a specialty consult

- FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation (includes the appended "Regulatory History" memo detailing the 2015-2017 pre-submission dispute) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/208623Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf

- Companion diagnostic note: a standalone companion diagnostic GLA-genotyping assay was not required for marketing, since GLA gene sequencing is already standard commercial diagnostic practice for Fabry disease (per CDRH/OIR consultation referenced in the Multi-Discipline Review).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**
