### 25. Risdiplam (Evrysdi) — NDA 213535

**Sponsor:** Genentech, Inc. (member of the Roche Group)

**Indication approved:** Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) in patients 2 months of age and older

**Approval date:** August 7, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** FIREFISH, NCT02913482 (Type 1 SMA, open-label, single-arm, two-part); SUNFISH, NCT02908685 (Type 2/3 SMA, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, two-part)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* FIREFISH — open-label, single-arm, two-part (Part 1 dose-finding/Part 2 confirmatory), external natural-history/performance-goal comparator, no concurrent control; SUNFISH — two-part seamless, multicenter, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, with age-stratified randomization (2-5, 6-11, 12-17, 18-25 years)
- *Endpoints:* FIREFISH primary — proportion of infants sitting without support for at least 5 seconds at Month 12 per item 22 of the modified BSID-III Gross Motor Scale (central-reader adjudicated); SUNFISH primary — change from baseline in MFM-32 total score at Month 12
- *Primary analysis:* FIREFISH — one-sample exact (Clopper-Pearson) binomial test of the observed sitting rate against a pre-defined 5% performance criterion derived from natural-history data; SUNFISH — mixed model repeated measures (MMRM, unstructured covariance, REML) under a hypothetical estimand assuming no prohibited SMA medications and continued randomized treatment
- *Multiplicity:* FIREFISH — pre-specified hierarchical (fixed-sequence) testing of secondary endpoints, each gated on rejection of the prior test at alpha=0.05; SUNFISH — graphical gatekeeping procedure across 7 hypotheses grouped into 6 ordered families, with a truncated Hochberg procedure (truncation fraction 0.95, equivalent to truncated Hommel for the 2-hypothesis family) used within the family containing HFMSE and FVC ("truncated Hochberg/Hommel gatekeeping procedure")
- *Interim/alpha-spending:* FIREFISH Part 2 — a single pre-specified futility assessment after the first 14 infants reached 12 months/withdrew, using predictive probability of trial success (a Bayesian-flavored futility rule), reviewed by an independent Data Monitoring Committee; SUNFISH Part 2 — no interim analysis was performed prior to the primary analysis
- *Missing data/bias:* FIREFISH — non-responder imputation (missing, withdrawn, or dead infants classified as non-sitters) for all binary responder endpoints; SUNFISH — MMRM under missing-at-random, with a treatment-policy-estimand sensitivity analysis and a tipping-point analysis exploring departures from MAR (a delta of -7.75 was needed to overturn the primary conclusion, against an observed treatment difference of 1.55 points)
- *Regulatory:* no FDA advisory committee meeting held; single-arm FIREFISH Part 1 (originally designated exploratory) was elevated to serve as the pivotal efficacy study for Type 1 SMA after positive interim results — FDA's biometrics reviewer explicitly deemed this "not well controlled," a documented cross-disciplinary (statistics vs. clinical) disagreement within the same review that the Summary Review team overruled ("documented intra-review statistical/clinical disagreement over whether a single-arm trial is 'well controlled,' resolved by the Summary Review overruling Biometrics")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- FIREFISH (Study BP39056, Roche/Genentech): Phase 2/3, multicenter, multinational, open-label, single-arm, two-part study in infants with genetically confirmed 5q Type 1 SMA (onset 28 days to under 3 months of age, 2 SMN2 copies, gestational age 37-42 weeks, adequate nutrition/no invasive ventilation at screening); Part 1 (n=21) was dose-finding/ascending-dose with an Internal Monitoring Committee selecting the Part 2 ("pivotal") dose based on safety, exposure below an AUC cap, and SMN protein increase, confirmed by an external independent Data Monitoring Committee; Part 2 (n=41) treated all infants at the selected dose for 24 months, with primary analysis at Month 12; per the FDA Summary Review, positive Part 1 interim results led the Division to agree the Part 2 SAP would be retrospectively applied to Part 1, making Part 1 (n=21) the pivotal efficacy dataset actually reviewed for approval — Part 2 topline data existed but "the primary data were not submitted or reviewed by the Agency during this review cycle"
- SUNFISH (Study BP39055, Roche/Genentech): two-part seamless, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study in Type 2/3 SMA (ages 2-25 years; Part 2 restricted to non-ambulant patients able to sit independently with RULM entry item A of at least 2); Part 1 (dose-finding) established the Part 2 dose (5 mg once daily for body weight at least 20 kg or 0.25 mg/kg for under 20 kg); Part 2 (confirmatory) randomized 180 patients 2:1 to risdiplam (n=120) vs. placebo (n=60), stratified by age group, with a 24-month placebo-controlled/blinded-crossover design (placebo patients switched to risdiplam after Month 12) and primary analysis at Month 12
- Sample size/power: FIREFISH Part 2 was powered so that at least 6/41 infants sitting would put the lower bound of the 90% Clopper-Pearson CI above the 5% performance threshold (one-sided alpha=0.05 exact binomial test); SUNFISH Part 2 target N=168 (112 risdiplam:56 placebo), assuming a treatment difference of 3 points and common SD of 6 on MFM-32 (effect size 0.5), gave at least 80% power at two-sided alpha=0.05 allowing 10% dropout; actual enrollment (180) exceeded this target
- Secondary endpoints: FIREFISH — CHOP-INTEND at least 40 and at least 4-point CHOP-INTEND improvement, HINE-2 motor-milestone responders, time to death or permanent ventilation (Kaplan-Meier, 90% CI), respiratory/feeding outcomes; SUNFISH — MFM-32 responder (at least 3-point improvement) rate, RULM, HFMSE, FVC (percent predicted), caregiver/patient-reported SMAIS, and Clinician/Caregiver Global Impression of Change, each analyzed via MMRM analogous to the primary model
- Statistical methods: FIREFISH primary via an exact one-sample binomial test versus an external performance goal (no within-study comparator); SUNFISH primary via MMRM with fixed effects for baseline score, treatment, time (categorical), treatment-by-time and baseline-by-time interactions, and the randomization stratification factor (age group), random patient effect, unstructured covariance, REML estimation

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/213535Orig1s000Approv.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/213535Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/213535Orig1s000StatR.pdf
- FDA Clinical (Medical) Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/213535Orig1s000MedR.pdf

[DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S1474-4422(21)00367-7>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34942136/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Safety%20and%20efficacy%20of%20once-daily%20risdiplam%20in%20type%202%20and%20non-ambulant%20type%203%20spinal%20muscular%20atrophy)

**Other resources**

- No trial-specific IPD/dataset-sharing program (Vivli, YODA, ClinicalStudyDataRequest) was individually confirmed for FIREFISH or SUNFISH; Roche/Genentech maintains a general clinical-trial data-sharing policy, but a specific risdiplam dataset-access record was not verified, so this should be stated as unconfirmed rather than available.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held; the Summary Review states: "This application was not referred for review to an advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary; there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FIREFISH SAP, Section 4.4.1, p. 22]*

> "The primary endpoint for the confirmatory Part 2 of the study is the proportion of infants who are sitting without support after 12 months of treatment. Sitting is defined as 'sits alone without support for at least 5 seconds' as assessed in item 22 of the modified BSID-III gross motor scale... The pre-defined performance criterion for the primary endpoint will be 5%... The hypothesis to be tested is that the proportion of infants who sit on treatment (p) is: H0: p <= 5% (null) versus Ha: p > 5% (alternative)."

*[verbatim, FIREFISH SAP, Section 4.8, p. 51]*

> "A futility assessment for efficacy will be conducted after the first 14 infants enrolled into the confirmatory Part 2 of the study have reached 12 months of treatment or have been withdrawn. If the predictive probability of 'success' (defined as observing 5 out of 40 sitting) is less than 10%... then the Sponsor may consider stopping the study."

*[verbatim, SUNFISH SAP, Section 4.4.1, p. 24]*

> "The primary endpoint in Part 2 is the change from (original) baseline in the total motor function measure 32 (MFM32) score at Month 12... The primary efficacy estimand is based on a hypothetical treatment strategy assuming no prohibited medications intended for treatment of SMA are available and patients continue on their randomized treatment until the primary analysis time point."

*[verbatim, SUNFISH SAP, Section 4.4.2.6, pp. 36-38]*

> "To control the Type I error rate due to multiple testing of risdiplam versus placebo for the primary and the six key secondary efficacy endpoints in the ITT population of Part 2 of the study, a gatekeeping approach will be applied to the seven null hypotheses which are grouped into six families... the truncated Hochberg procedure will be used in the family which contains more than one hypothesis... the truncation fraction is set to 0.95... As there are only two null hypotheses in Family 4, the truncated Hochberg procedure is equivalent to the truncated Hommel procedure."

*[verbatim, SUNFISH SAP, Section 4.10, p. 69]*

> "No interim analysis will be performed prior to the primary analysis of Part 2 of the study."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Section 3.2.1.4.1, p. 15]*

> "In the MMRM analysis of the MFM32 total score, the least square means (lsmeans) (SE) change from baseline at Month 12 was 1.36 (0.38) in patients receiving risdiplam and -0.19 (0.52) in patients receiving placebo... the least square difference [95% CI]... 1.55 [0.30, 2.81]; p=0.0156."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Section 5.1, p. 24, biometrics reviewer's dissent]*

> "Part 1 of the open label single arm study, Firefish, in the more severe Type 1 SMA was submitted for evidence of efficacy even though it was originally designated as exploratory. This creates a multiplicity issue because knowledge of the results influenced the change in designation... the key source of evidence for efficacy is the placebo controlled study, Sunfish part 2, because the evidence from Firefish, though impressive on face compared to the reported natural history, is not well controlled."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, p. 13]*

> "After initial positive interim results in Part 1, it was decided, with the concurrence of the Division, that the SAP for Part 2 of BP39056 would be applied to Part 1, and that Part 1 would serve as the pivotal efficacy study for infantile-onset SMA patients... Topline efficacy results for Part 2 became available during review of this NDA submission; however, the primary data were not submitted or reviewed by the Agency during this review cycle."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, p. 24, direct rebuttal of the Biometrics dissent]*

> "Although the biometrics review stated that 'the evidence from [BP39056], though impressive on face compared to the reported natural history, is not well controlled', we do not agree with that assertion... Although Study BP39056 was open-label, it is a well-controlled study. The known natural history of the disease... and the pre-defined threshold of 5/40 patients... serve as an external control for the study."

Risdiplam/Evrysdi is a documented case of an explicit, on-the-record intra-agency statistical dispute: FDA's own biometrics reviewer concluded the single-arm FIREFISH trial was "not well controlled" and that only SUNFISH (the randomized trial) constituted real evidence, while the Summary Review overruled that assessment and treated FIREFISH's natural-history/performance-goal comparison as an adequate external control — both positions preserved verbatim in the same review package.

### 26. Viltolarsen (Viltepso) — NDA 212154

**Sponsor:** NS Pharma, Inc. (a subsidiary of Nippon Shinyaku Co., Ltd.)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in patients who have a confirmed mutation of the DMD gene that is amenable to exon 53 skipping

**Approval date:** August 12, 2020 (accelerated approval)

**Pivotal trial:** Study NS-065/NCNP-01-201 ("Study 201"), NCT02740972

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* very small (n=16), 2-period, multicenter dose-finding trial: a 4-week randomized (3:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled safety period in two sequentially enrolled dose cohorts (40 mg/kg/week, then 80 mg/kg/week), followed by continued open-label dosing through Week 25 with all patients (including former placebo patients) on active drug; functional secondary endpoints compared descriptively against an external natural-history cohort (CINRG DNHS) rather than a concurrent control
- *Endpoints:* dystrophin protein level by biceps-muscle-biopsy Western blot (primary biomarker/surrogate endpoint, change from Baseline to Week 25); mass spectrometry, immunofluorescence, and RT-PCR dystrophin/exon-skipping measures and functional/strength measures (6MWT, NSAA, TTSTAND, TTRW, TTCLIMB, QMT) as secondary endpoints
- *Primary analysis:* paired t-test of within-patient change from baseline in dystrophin (percent of normal) within each dose level, plus a two-sample t-test comparing the two dose levels and a combined-dose paired-difference t-test; planned fallback to a nonparametric test or normalizing transformation if normality failed
- *Multiplicity:* no planned formal multiple-testing procedure for either the four primary-endpoint analyses (2 normalization methods x 2 doses) or the secondary endpoints; FDA's biometrics reviewer noted results remained nominally significant under any reasonable multiplicity adjustment
- *Missing data/bias:* efficacy analyses based on a modified intent-to-treat population (randomized, dosed, with a baseline and at least 1 post-baseline assessment); triplicate Western blot gel values averaged per patient/timepoint, with available non-missing replicates averaged when some were missing; no discontinuations occurred in the small pivotal cohort
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval on a surrogate biomarker (dystrophin production), explicitly benchmarked by FDA against its own precedent for eteplirsen and golodirsen; confirmatory Phase 3 trial (RACER53) required as a postmarketing requirement; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 201 was a multicenter, 2-period, dose-finding study in males aged 4 to <10 years with genetically confirmed DMD amenable to exon 53 skipping, on stable corticosteroids for at least 3 months, without symptomatic cardiomyopathy, and able to walk independently
- Period 1 (Weeks 1-4): randomized (3:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled IV dosing in two sequentially enrolled cohorts of 8 patients each (6 viltolarsen/2 placebo) at 40 mg/kg/week, then, after a clean safety review, 80 mg/kg/week; Period 2: all patients (including the 4 former placebo patients) continued/switched to open-label viltolarsen at their cohort's dose through Week 25 (24 weeks of active treatment for originally-randomized patients, 20 weeks for former placebo patients), then rolled into a separate open-label extension study (NS-065-202) at the same dose
- Primary endpoint: change from Baseline to Week 25 in dystrophin protein level (percent of normal) in biceps muscle biopsies, determined by Western blot, normalized separately to two housekeeping proteins (myosin heavy chain and alpha-actinin), analyzed in the modified intent-to-treat population (n=8 per dose cohort)
- Secondary endpoints: dystrophin induction by mass spectrometry, immunofluorescence, and RT-PCR (mRNA exon-skipping); muscle strength/function measures (6MWT, NSAA, TTSTAND, TTRW, TTCLIMB, QMT) compared descriptively to a matched natural-history control group (CINRG Duchenne Natural History Study)
- Sample size was fixed by feasibility (a small dose-finding cohort, not a power calculation for a between-arm comparison); no formal interim analysis or alpha-spending plan beyond the built-in dose-escalation safety gate between the 40 mg/kg and 80 mg/kg cohorts
- Statistical methods: within-dose paired t-tests of dystrophin change from baseline (both normalization methods), a two-sample t-test comparing the two doses (nonsignificant, p=0.94), and a combined-dose paired-difference t-test; no adjustment for the resulting four primary comparisons or for secondary endpoints, though FDA's biometrics reviewer noted the results were robust to reasonable multiplicity correction; FDA's Office of Biotechnology Products concluded myosin-heavy-chain normalization was more reliable than alpha-actinin normalization, and that RT-PCR/immunofluorescence data should be used only qualitatively, not for quantitative dose/efficacy conclusions
- Confirmatory trial required as an accelerated-approval postmarketing requirement: Study NS-065/NCNP-01-301 ("RACER53"), a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial of viltolarsen 80 mg/kg over 48 weeks with Time to Stand as the primary endpoint (NCT04060199) — run to verify the clinical benefit only inferred from the dystrophin biomarker at accelerated approval

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter (Accelerated Approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2020/212154Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (original, 2020) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2020/212154s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Summary Review (includes the Clinical/Statistical Efficacy section reproduced in this entry) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/212154Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- FDA Medical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/212154Orig1s000MedR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (Study 201) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02740972 (no protocol/SAP documents posted; record confirms 2-period randomized/open-label design, actual enrollment 16)
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (confirmatory trial, RACER53/NS-065/NCNP-01-301) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04060199
- Protocol / SAP: not posted on ClinicalTrials.gov
- Pivotal publication: Clemens PR, Rao VK, Connolly AM, et al; CINRG DNHS Investigators. "Safety, Tolerability, and Efficacy of Viltolarsen in Boys With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy Amenable to Exon 53 Skipping: A Phase 2 Randomized Clinical Trial." *JAMA Neurol.* 2020;77(8):982-991. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1001/jamaneurol.2020.1264), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32453377/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Safety%2C%20Tolerability%2C%20and%20Efficacy%20of%20Viltolarsen%20in%20Boys%20With%20Duchenne%20Muscular%20Dystrophy%20Amenable%20to%20Exon%2053%20Skipping)

**Other resources**

- No trial-specific IPD/dataset-sharing program (Vivli, YODA, Project Data Sphere) was individually confirmed for this ultra-rare-disease dataset.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held; the Summary Review states this application "was not referred for review to an advisory committee because the safety profile of viltolarsen is acceptable for the intended population, the clinical trial designs were acceptable, and the findings on the surrogate marker were clear."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, NDA 212154, "Clinical/Statistical - Efficacy," Statistical Analysis section]*

> "For each of the western blot tests, immunoblot dystrophin was normalized to each alpha-actin and to myosin. Three responses from 3 triplicate gels run were averaged to attain a single result for summarizing and analyzing. If any responses were missing, then the available non-missing responses were averaged. Efficacy analyses were based on the modified intent-to-treat (mITT) population, consisting of all randomized patients who received at least 1 dose of investigational product and had a baseline assessment and at least 1 post baseline efficacy assessment... Western blot within-patient change in percentage of normal dystrophin production was tested using a paired t-test within each dose level. A two-sample t-test was used to compare change across the two dose levels. The two doses were also combined and tested using a paired difference t-test. Normality of change in percentage of normal dystrophin at post-baseline was to be assessed and if needed, a nonparametric test or a transformation to achieve normality would be performed. There was no planned formal multiple-testing procedure for secondary endpoints."

*[verbatim, same source, on the primary endpoint result and multiplicity]*

> "A statistically significant increase in dystrophin from baseline was observed after 20 to 24 weeks of treatment with once-weekly IV viltolarsen at 40 mg/kg and 80 mg/kg, based on western blot... Dr. Ling notes that there were four primary analyses, as western blot analysis included normalization to both myosin heavy chain and alpha-actinin and there were 2 doses. Although a formal multiple-testing procedure was not planned, the analysis results remain nominally statistically significant for any reasonable adjustment for multiplicity control... There was no statistically significant difference between the 40 mg/kg and 80 mg/kg dosages (p=0.94)."

*[verbatim, same source, on assay reliability]*

> "OBP notes that the western blot method was validated using myosin heavy chain and alpha actinin as housekeeping proteins for normalization; however, there is some residual variability in dystrophin results in this method using either normalization control protein. The degree of variability was less when dystrophin intensities were normalized with myosin heavy chain compared to alpha-actinin... OPB states that due to concerns for the potential of overestimation of drug-induced effects, RT-PCR data should only be used to confirm the mechanism of action and to qualitatively support dystrophin production measured by western blot as a treatment effect."

*[verbatim, same source, on the accelerated-approval rationale and precedent]*

> "The increase in dystrophin levels demonstrated for viltolarsen is similar in size or may be slightly greater to that established for eteplirsen and golodirsen, drugs that received accelerated approval based on a previous conclusion by CDER that the increase in dystrophin level was reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit. Based on these precedents, and barring any evidence to suggest otherwise, the statistically significant increase in de novo (truncated) dystrophin protein demonstrated in Study NS-065/NCNP-01-201 supports accelerated approval of viltolarsen for the treatment of DMD in patients with a confirmed mutation of the DMD gene that is amenable to exon 53 skipping."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, Postmarketing Recommendations]*

> "In order to verify the clinical benefit of viltolarsen, complete Study NS-065/NCNP-01-301 ('a Phase 3 Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled, Multi-center Study to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of Viltolarsen in Ambulant Boys with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy'). The study will assess treatment with viltolarsen 80 mg/kg over 48 weeks. The primary endpoint will be Time to Stand."

Viltolarsen is the third of four Duchenne exon-skipping antisense oligonucleotides in this census (after eteplirsen and golodirsen, before casimersen) approved on the identical dystrophin-biomarker accelerated-approval logic, each time from a progressively smaller or shorter pivotal dataset (here, n=16 and a 24-week biopsy endpoint) with functional outcomes benchmarked only against an external natural-history cohort rather than a concurrent control arm.

### 27. Lonafarnib (Zokinvy) — NDA 213969

**Sponsor:** Eiger BioPharmaceuticals, Inc. (NDA holder at approval; Eiger partnered with the Progeria Research Foundation, which had sponsored the original investigator-initiated trials; Sentynl Therapeutics later acquired U.S. commercialization rights to Zokinvy)

**Indication approved:** To reduce the risk of mortality in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome (HGPS); and for the treatment of processing-deficient progeroid laminopathies (PL) with either a heterozygous LMNA mutation with progerin-like protein accumulation, or homozygous/compound heterozygous ZMPSTE24 mutations, in patients 12 months of age and older with a body surface area of 0.39 m2 and above

**Approval date:** November 20, 2020 (regular approval, not accelerated approval)

**Pivotal trial:** two investigator-initiated, open-label, single-arm Phase 2 trials — ProLon1 (Study 07-01-0007), NCT00425607, and ProLon2 (Study 09-06-0298, a zoledronic-acid/pravastatin/lonafarnib triple-therapy protocol), NCT00916747 — with efficacy demonstrated via a post hoc retrospective survival comparison against a 1:1-matched, untreated natural-history cohort from the Progeria Research Foundation's International Progeria Registry (no registered NCT number for the natural-history cohort itself)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two sequential, non-randomized, open-label, single-arm trials (no concurrent control) pooled and compared retrospectively to a 1:1-matched external natural-history control cohort — a within-disease matched historical-control survival-comparison design run and revised largely under FDA direction after NDA submission ("post hoc 1:1-matched natural-history-control survival analysis, matching algorithm revised by FDA after submission")
- *Endpoints:* time to all-cause mortality (primary efficacy outcome), censored both at 3 years (monotherapy-comparable follow-up) and at last known follow-up; incidence of all-cause mortality (supporting endpoint)
- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test (two-sided alpha=0.05) comparing survival distributions between treated and matched-untreated groups; Kaplan-Meier estimation of survival probabilities, restricted mean survival time (RMST), and percentile survival times; Cox proportional-hazards regression for the hazard ratio
- *Missing data/bias:* differential censoring between treated and untreated groups (treated-patient follow-up censored at dual-therapy initiation) was identified by FDA as biased in favor of the treated group and required a revised, FDA-recommended censoring approach; matching algorithm itself (random selection among same-sex/same-continent candidates) was rejected by FDA as inadequate because it produced a variant-status imbalance favoring the treated cohort, and FDA substituted its own fixed-50th-percentile algorithm matched additionally on variant status as the primary analysis
- *Regulatory:* approval based on two adequate and well-controlled investigator-initiated trials reanalyzed via a retrospective, post hoc SAP that FDA explicitly deviated from mid-review once its own re-examination found the original SAP-defined analysis biased; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held; FDA noted at a pre-IND meeting that the sponsor's failure to pre-submit its analysis plan for Agency agreement before analyzing the data "was a missed opportunity for the program and may be a review issue"

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ProLon1 (Study 07-01-0007) and ProLon2 (Study 09-06-0298) were investigator-initiated (Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, then Boston Children's Hospital, in partnership with the Progeria Research Foundation), open-label, single-arm trials of lonafarnib (as monotherapy, then later combined with zoledronic acid/pravastatin as "triple therapy") in children with genetically confirmed HGPS (and a small number of processing-deficient PL patients), enrolled from 1991 onward; there was no randomized concurrent comparator in either trial
- The efficacy claim rested on a retrospective, contemporaneous intent-to-treat survival comparison: all HGPS patients treated in ProLon1 and ProLon2 combined (N=62) vs. 62 untreated patients 1:1-matched from a pool of 173 treatment-naive patients (born 1991 or later, to match the treated cohort's earliest birth year) drawn from the Progeria Research Foundation's International Progeria Registry (196 patients total, 23 excluded)
- Primary efficacy outcome: time to all-cause mortality (database cutoff June 1, 2019), assessed separately with follow-up censored at 3 years (the maximum monotherapy duration in ProLon2, to isolate a monotherapy-comparable effect) and with follow-up censored at last known age alive (to capture longer-term treatment, including triple/dual therapy periods)
- Supporting endpoints: incidence of all-cause mortality by the cutoff date, both crude and patient-time-adjusted
- No conventional power calculation was performed (a fixed retrospective cohort of 62 matched pairs, not a prospectively powered trial); sample size was determined entirely by how many HGPS patients had been treated across the two investigator-initiated trials and how many eligible untreated matches existed in the registry
- Statistical methods: log-rank test stratified by continent of residency (2-sided alpha 0.05) comparing treated vs. matched-untreated survival distributions at both censoring times; Kaplan-Meier curves, RMST, and 25th/50th/75th percentile survival times with normal-approximation and bootstrap (1,000 samples) confidence intervals; Cox proportional-hazards model for the hazard ratio. Matching criteria were originally specified in the sponsor's SAP as sex and continent of residency only, with a randomly selected match among eligible candidates as the primary method (fixed 50th/75th-percentile matching as supportive methods); FDA rejected the random-matching method as the primary analysis (because it produced an arbitrary, re-derivable-only-by-chance untreated cohort) and rejected the sex/continent-only matching criteria (because the resulting matched cohort was imbalanced on classic vs. nonclassic HGPS variant status, which the natural-history data showed strongly predicts mortality, biasing results in the treated group's favor); FDA instead designated the fixed-50th-percentile algorithm matched on variant status, sex, and continent of residency as the primary analysis. FDA separately identified and corrected a censoring-rule deviation from the SAP (the applicant had censored treated patients' follow-up at dual-therapy initiation rather than at last known age alive, disproportionately truncating treated-patient follow-up in a way that favored the treated group) and required a reanalysis using FDA's recommended censoring approach

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2020/213969Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label (original, 2020) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2020/213969s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Integrated Review (combined clinical/statistical/regulatory review; NDA 213969 did not receive separately posted Statistical, Summary, or Medical Review documents — all review content is in this single Integrated Review) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/213969Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (ProLon1) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00425607 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)
- ClinicalTrials.gov record (ProLon2, triple-therapy protocol; exact NCT-to-"Study 09-06-0298" correspondence not independently confirmed beyond title/design match) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00916747
- Protocol / SAP: not posted on ClinicalTrials.gov; the retrospective survival-analysis SAP's content is extensively reproduced (not verbatim-quoted as a standalone document) within the FDA Integrated Review, Section 6.2.1.3
- Pivotal publication (original investigator survival analysis, precursor to the NDA's revised retrospective analysis): Gordon LB, Shappell H, Massaro J, et al. "Association of Lonafarnib Treatment vs No Treatment With Mortality Rate in Patients With Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome." *JAMA.* 2018;319(16):1687-1695. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2018.3264), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29710166/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Association%20of%20Lonafarnib%20Treatment%20vs%20No%20Treatment%20With%20Mortality%20Rate%20in%20Patients%20With%20Hutchinson-Gilford%20Progeria%20Syndrome)

**Other resources**

- No trial-specific IPD/dataset-sharing program (Vivli, YODA, Project Data Sphere) was individually confirmed for this ultra-rare-disease dataset; the Progeria Research Foundation's International Progeria Registry itself functions as a natural-history data source but is not a conventional IPD-sharing repository for the treated-cohort trial data.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held; the Integrated Review states plainly: "An advisory committee was not held for this application. It did not raise challenging efficacy or safety issues that needed external input."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, NDA 213969, Section 6.2.1.3 "Statistical Analysis Plan," on the missed pre-analysis-agreement opportunity]*

> "Prior to the creation of the statistical analysis (SAP) for the NDA, the mortality data of ProLon1 and ProLon2 captured during lonafarnib monotherapy years were analyzed and published by the trial investigators (Gordon et al. 2018). Consequently, during the pre-IND meeting the Agency stated, 'Ideally, analysis plans for marketing applications should be submitted to the FDA for agreement before analyzing the data; this was a missed opportunity for the program and may be a review issue.'"

*[verbatim, same source, on the revised SAP and its post hoc status]*

> "The Applicant agreed with the Agency's recommendation and revised the SAP with a cut-off date of June 1, 2019 for follow-up. The SAP was also revised based on Agency feedback pertaining to the matching approach and censoring. The revised SAP was deemed acceptable by the Agency prior to NDA submission, with the caveat that analyses were retrospectively planned and considered post-hoc."

*[verbatim, same source, on the matching methodology]*

> "According to the SAP, the matching criteria were defined by sex and continent of residency... If the matching pool had more than one candidate, the match was randomly selected. This matching method was considered as the primary matching method and was used in the Applicant's main efficacy analysis. As supportive analyses, the SAP considered various alternative methods, including the fixed 50th and 75th percentile matching algorithms."

*[verbatim, same source, on FDA's rejection of the SAP-defined matching as the primary analysis]*

> "The Agency, however, does not consider the SAP-defined matching criteria adequate based on the following two observations identified during our review of the NDA: The resultant matched untreated cohorts had more patients with the nonclassic variant than the treated cohort did. This imbalance in variant status favored the treated cohort because the natural history data showed an increased risk of mortality in patients with the nonclassic variant... Therefore, during the NDA review, the Agency requested the Applicant submit survival analyses based on the data of the treated and untreated patients who were matched by variant status (classic/unknown versus non-classic), sex, and continent of residency using the fixed 50th (primary) and 75th (supportive) percentile matching algorithms... While the Agency does not generally deviate from an agreed upon SAP, we determined that these changes to the main analyses were necessary because the problematic issues discussed above were not appreciated prior to submission of the NDA and we had concerns for biased results if we followed the SAP."

*[verbatim, same source, on the censoring-rule deviation FDA identified and corrected]*

> "However, contrary to the SAP-defined follow-up time, in the NDA and subsequently submitted datasets, the Applicant censored follow-up time for treated patients at the date of dual therapy initiation for those who were alive and the time to death for those who died... Because of the censoring approach the Applicant adopted... the treated cohort had a substantially higher censoring rate over time than the matched untreated cohorts... This censoring imbalance favored the treated patients... To address the resulting imbalance in the censoring rate, the Agency requested the Applicant submit survival analyses censoring the follow-up time of the untreated patients... at the follow-up time of the treated patients (this censoring approach is referred to as the Agency's recommended censoring approach)."

*[verbatim, same source, primary analysis method]*

> "For the analysis of time to all-cause mortality censored at 3 years and time to all-cause mortality censored at last follow-up, the main efficacy analysis compared the survival distributions between the treated and matched untreated groups using a log-rank test at a two-sided significance level of 5%. Kaplan-Meier survival curves were created for the treated and matched untreated groups. The restricted mean survival time... and the 25th, 50th (median), and 75th percentile survival times... were presented... A Cox proportional hazards regression model was also fitted to estimate the hazard ratio between the treated and matched untreated groups."

*[verbatim, same source, main results, Table 9 and surrounding text]*

> "The hazard ratio for the risk of death was 0.30 (95% CI: 0.10 to 0.89) for follow-up censored at 3 years and was 0.40 (95% CI: 0.21 to 0.77) for follow-up censored at the last follow-up" (stratified log-rank p=0.02 and p=0.005, respectively; 5 deaths among 62 treated vs. 12 among 62 matched-untreated patients by 3 years; 21 vs. 25 deaths by last follow-up).

Lonafarnib/Zokinvy is a distinctive case in this census of a **regular** (non-accelerated) approval built entirely on a retrospective, post hoc matched-historical-control survival analysis of two non-randomized, investigator-initiated single-arm trials — with FDA's own Integrated Review documenting, in unusual detail, how the Agency itself revised the sponsor's pre-agreed SAP mid-review (both the patient-matching algorithm and the censoring rule) after identifying that the original SAP-defined approach was biased in the treated group's favor.

### 28. Lumasiran (Oxlumo) — NDA 214103

**Sponsor:** Alnylam Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of primary hyperoxaluria type 1 (PH1) to lower urinary oxalate levels in pediatric and adult patients

**Approval date:** November 23, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** ILLUMINATE-A, NCT03681184

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter/multinational Phase 3 trial in an ultra-rare genetic disease (PH1), ages 6 and older, with stratified randomization on baseline urinary oxalate level
- *Endpoints:* MMRM analysis of percent change from baseline in 24-hour urinary oxalate excretion corrected for body surface area (BSA), averaged over Months 3-6
- *Primary analysis:* REML-based mixed model repeated measures (MMRM) with fixed effects of treatment, visit, and baseline covariate, patient as random effect, unstructured covariance (AIC-guided fallback to AR(1)/compound symmetry/Toeplitz), Satterthwaite degrees of freedom, Full Analysis Set
- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (hierarchical) gatekeeping across six secondary endpoints, each tested only if the prior test in the sequence was significant at 2-sided alpha 0.05
- *Missing data/bias:* MMRM under a missing-at-random assumption; sensitivity analyses relaxing the steady-state assumption (treatment-by-visit interaction terms, and inclusion of Months 1-2 data)
- *Regulatory:* orphan drug designation, breakthrough therapy designation, rare pediatric disease designation with priority review voucher; no Advisory Committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ILLUMINATE-A (Protocol ALN-GO1-003) was a multicenter, multinational Phase 3 study in patients aged 6 years and older with genetically confirmed PH1, urinary oxalate excretion above threshold, and eGFR at least 30 mL/min/1.73m2 at screening; the study comprised a 2:1 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled 6-month period, followed by a 3-month blinded treatment extension and an open-label extension of up to 51 months; randomization was stratified by mean 24-hour urinary oxalate level from screening; 39 patients were randomized (26 lumasiran, 13 placebo)
- Primary endpoint: percent change in 24-hour urinary oxalate excretion, corrected for BSA, from baseline through Month 6, with the primary comparison based on percent changes at Months 3, 4, 5, and 6
- Secondary endpoints (tested in fixed hierarchical order): absolute change in 24-hour urinary oxalate corrected for BSA to Month 6; percent change in 24-hour urinary oxalate:creatinine ratio to Month 6; percent change in plasma oxalate to Month 6; proportion of patients with 24-hour urinary oxalate at or below 1.5x ULN at Month 6; proportion at or below ULN at Month 6; absolute change in plasma oxalate to Month 6; exploratory endpoints included KDQOL/PedsQL, EQ-5D, renal stone events, nephrocalcinosis, urinary/plasma glycolate, PK, and anti-drug antibodies
- Sample size/power: planned enrollment approximately 30 patients; 24 patients were projected to yield 90% power to detect a 37% treatment difference at 2-sided alpha 0.05, assuming a 17% mean percent reduction (SD 25%) in placebo vs. a 54% mean percent reduction (SD 25%) in lumasiran; no sample size re-estimation was planned or performed; no formal group-sequential/alpha-spending interim efficacy analysis — an independent DMC monitored safety on a semi-blinded basis, and the 6-month database lock served as the single primary-analysis timepoint before the long open-label extension
- Statistical methods: REML-based MMRM with fixed effects of treatment arm and scheduled visit (Months 3-6), continuous fixed covariate of baseline 24-hour urinary oxalate corrected for BSA, patient as random effect; unstructured covariance matrix as primary, with AR(1)/compound symmetry/Toeplitz as AIC-selected fallbacks; Satterthwaite approximation for denominator degrees of freedom; two prespecified sensitivity analyses added a treatment-by-visit interaction term, one restricted to Months 3-6 and one including Months 1-6; secondary endpoints controlled for multiplicity via a fixed-sequence hierarchical gatekeeping procedure

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/214103Orig1s000Approv.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/214103Orig1s000Lbl.pdf
- FDA Integrated Review (combined multidisciplinary review, includes Office of Biostatistics assessment; no separate StatR/SumR/MedR documents were filed for this NDA) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/214103Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03681184
- Protocol (Amendment 2, posted) — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/84/NCT03681184/Prot_002.pdf
- Statistical Analysis Plan (Version 2.0, November 21, 2019, posted) — https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/84/NCT03681184/SAP_001.pdf
- Pivotal publication: Garrelfs SF, Frishberg Y, Hulton SA, et al; ILLUMINATE-A Collaborators. "Lumasiran, an RNAi Therapeutic for Primary Hyperoxaluria Type 1." *N Engl J Med.* 2021;384(13):1216-1226. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2021712), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33789010/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Lumasiran%2C%20an%20RNAi%20Therapeutic%20for%20Primary%20Hyperoxaluria%20Type%201)

**Other resources**

- IPD/dataset access via Vivli or YODA is not confirmed for this trial/sponsor; state plainly as unconfirmed rather than assumed absent.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held: the Integrated Review states, "The application does not raise significant issues regarding the safety or effectiveness of the drug; hence, no Advisory Committee Meeting was held."
- Regulatory designations: orphan drug designation (granted February 8, 2016), breakthrough therapy designation (granted February 23, 2018), and rare pediatric disease designation (granted December 20, 2019) with an associated priority review voucher issued at approval, per the FDA Approval Letter.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, posted SAP, Protocol ALN-GO1-003, Version 2.0, November 21, 2019, Section 5.1 "Sample Size Justification," p. 14]*

> "Twenty-four patients will yield 90% power to detect a treatment difference of 37% at a 2-sided 5% significance level assuming the mean percent reduction from baseline to Month 6 in 24-hour urinary oxalate corrected for BSA is 17% with a standard deviation (SD) of 25% in the placebo arm, and a mean percent reduction from baseline to Month 6 in 24-hour urinary oxalate corrected for BSA of 54% with SD of 25% in the lumasiran arm."

*[verbatim, same source, Section 7.1 "Primary Endpoint," p. 21]*

> "The primary analysis will be performed using a restricted maximum likelihood (REML) based Mixed-Effect Model Repeated Measures (MMRM) approach. The outcome variable is percent change from baseline in 24-hour urinary oxalate corrected for BSA (mmol/24hr/1.73m2) at months 3, 4, 5, and 6. Analysis will include fixed effects of treatment arm (lumasiran vs. placebo) and scheduled visits (months 3, 4, 5 and 6), as well as continuous, fixed covariate of baseline 24-hour urinary oxalate corrected for BSA (mmol/24hr/1.73m2) level and patient as a random factor... An unstructured covariance structure matrix will be used to model the within-patient error. If the fit of the unstructured covariance structure matrix fails to converge, then the following covariance structures will be assessed: autoregressive (1), compound symmetry, and Toeplitz and the structure selected will be based upon the best fit chosen by Akaike Information Criteria (AIC). The Satterthwaite approximation will be used to estimate denominator degrees of freedom."

*[verbatim, same source, Section 5.6 "Multiple Comparisons/Multiplicity," p. 16]*

> "The family-wise Type I error control for the primary and secondary endpoints will be achieved by the gatekeeping testing strategy. Once the primary hypothesis testing is statistically significant at a 2-sided 0.05 significance level, the secondary endpoints will be tested in the following hierarchical order... Only if the comparison is significant at a 2-sided 0.05 significance level will the next endpoint in the hierarchy be formally tested; if a given comparison is not significant at a 2-sided 0.05 significance level, the subsequent tests will be performed, and the results will be summarized, but statistical significance will not be inferred."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, Section 6.2.2.3 "Statistical Analysis Plan, ILLUMINATE-A," p. 25]*

> "The statistical analysis plan (SAP) for ILLUMINATE-A was originally submitted on March 19, 2019. An updated version was submitted on November 27, 2019 after the trial was fully enrolled to align secondary endpoints with protocol Amendment 2 and change sensitivity analyses... No sample size re-estimation was planned or performed."

*[verbatim, same source, "Analysis of Primary Endpoint" and Table 11, p. 29]*

> "As shown in Table 11, there was a statistically significant decrease in 24-hour urinary oxalate excretion corrected for BSA in the lumasiran group compared with placebo (LS mean difference -53.6%; p<0.0001). The findings were consistent in prespecified sensitivity analyses that did not assume the treatment effect was at steady state from Months 3 to 6 (Sensitivity Analysis 1) and included data from Months 1 to 6 (Sensitivity Analysis 2)."

*[verbatim, same source, "Adequacy of 24-hour Urine Collections," p. 29]*

> "Missing data were rare. Thirty-five patients (90%) had no missing data at baseline and Months 3 to 6. All 39 enrolled patients (100%) had valid data at baseline and at least one valid assessment between Months 3 and 6 included in the MMRM model for the primary efficacy analysis."

**Reverse-engineered SAP** (supplementing the verbatim excerpts above):

- *[inferred]* the trial used an independent DMC and a semi-blinded statistical data analysis center rather than a formal group-sequential/alpha-spending interim monitoring plan for efficacy, inferred from the FDA Integrated Review's description that the database was locked and unblinded only once, at the single 6-month primary-analysis timepoint, with no sample-size re-estimation or alpha adjustment reported

Lumasiran/Oxlumo is one of the few entries in this batch with a genuinely posted sponsor SAP (ClinicalTrials.gov), documenting a conventionally powered, randomized, placebo-controlled trial with a pre-specified MMRM primary analysis and hierarchical secondary-endpoint gatekeeping — a notably more standard design than most of the other ultra-rare-disease drugs in this batch.

### 29. Casimersen (Amondys 45) — NDA 213026

**Sponsor:** Sarepta Therapeutics, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in patients who have a confirmed mutation of the DMD gene that is amenable to exon 45 skipping

**Approval date:** February 25, 2021 (accelerated approval, 21 CFR 314.500/Subpart H)

**Pivotal trial:** Study 4045-301 ("ESSENCE"; a double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter study with an open-label extension to evaluate the efficacy and safety of SRP-4045 and SRP-4053 in patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy), NCT02500381 — casimersen (SRP-4045) arm, interim Part 1 dystrophin data at Week 48

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter combined trial enrolling two genetically distinct DMD subgroups (exon-45-skip-amenable and exon-53-skip-amenable) into parallel drug-specific arms (casimersen vs. placebo; golodirsen vs. placebo) within one protocol, each arm independently analyzed and used to support a separate NDA ("interim single-arm-of-a-combined-trial biomarker analysis supporting accelerated approval"); 96-week randomized double-blind period (Part 1) plus 48-week open-label extension (Part 2) to Week 144; accelerated approval relied on an interim analysis of the casimersen-arm subset only
- *Endpoints:* accelerated-approval analysis endpoint was change from Baseline to Week 48 in dystrophin protein expression (percent of normal) by western blot in biceps muscle biopsy — a protocol-specified secondary/biological endpoint repurposed as the primary endpoint for the interim analysis; the trial's own primary clinical endpoint was change from baseline in six-minute walk test (6MWT) at Week 96; exploratory endpoint at interim: change in percent exon-45 skipping by RT-ddPCR
- *Primary analysis:* two-sample permutation test (10,000 re-randomizations) comparing casimersen vs. placebo change-from-baseline dystrophin at Week 48 in n=43 evaluable patients (27 casimersen, 16 placebo) drawn from the first 45 exon-45-amenable enrollees ("permutation-test primary analysis of an interim biomarker sub-study"); an FDA-conducted sensitivity analysis with the Wilcoxon rank-sum test corroborated the result
- *Multiplicity:* Type 1 error of 0.01 (2-sided) pre-allocated to the interim dystrophin comparison; a gatekeeping procedure spanning the interim analysis and the trial's eventual final analysis was pre-specified to control overall 2-sided alpha at 0.05 across the ongoing study ("interim/final gatekeeping within a single ongoing trial for staged accelerated- then regular-approval analyses"); the exon-skipping (RT-ddPCR) endpoint was analyzed at interim without formal multiplicity adjustment
- *Missing data/bias:* below-LLOQ (0.25%) western blot values were retained as measured (not censored), with pre-specified imputation for values outside assay quantification limits; replicate gel runs (4 per subject per timepoint) averaged; a supplemental binary dichotomization sensitivity analysis (below LLOQ vs. above LLOQ, odds ratio 9.0 favoring casimersen) and an outlier-exclusion sensitivity analysis were also supportive; the unblinded interim analysis was performed by an independent CRO statistical team not otherwise involved in trial conduct, to preserve blinding of the still-ongoing Study 4045-301
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval on a dystrophin-biomarker surrogate "reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit," the same pathway used for Sarepta's eteplirsen, golodirsen, and (Nippon Shinyaku's) viltolarsen; no advisory committee meeting held; Study 4045-301 (ESSENCE) itself, still ongoing, was designated as the postmarketing confirmatory trial required to verify clinical benefit; no internal FDA dissent memo was identified in the released review package, in contrast to the well-documented internal disagreement on golodirsen's accelerated approval

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Randomized (2:1, active:placebo within each genetic subgroup), double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial (ESSENCE) enrolling male patients aged 7-13 years with genotypically confirmed DMD amenable to exon 45 or exon 53 skipping; overall trial N=228 (both subgroups combined); the exon-45 (casimersen) subgroup was designed for approximately 111 subjects (74 casimersen : 37 placebo, 2:1); Part 1 is 96 weeks randomized double-blind, followed by Part 2, a 48-week open-label extension (to Week 144); casimersen dosed 30 mg/kg IV once weekly
- Eligibility: stable oral corticosteroid dose for at least 24 weeks; intact biceps brachii (or alternate) muscle for biopsy; mean 6MWT 300-450 meters at screening and baseline; FVC at least 50% predicted, no nocturnal ventilation requirement; LVEF at least 50%; QTcF under 450 msec; exclusions included prior gene therapy and prior exposure to certain other exon-skipping investigational agents
- Accelerated-approval interim analysis population: the first 45 exon-45-amenable enrollees; 1 randomized-in-error patient excluded (no biopsy); of 44 with both Baseline and Week 48 biopsies, 1 further patient excluded because the genetic mutation predicted a truncated dystrophin isoform lacking the epitope recognized by validated western blot antibodies, yielding 43 evaluable patients (27 casimersen, 16 placebo)
- Primary endpoint for accelerated approval: change from Baseline to Week 48 in dystrophin protein level (percent of normal) by western blot in biceps muscle biopsy (protocol-labeled a secondary endpoint of the ongoing trial, elevated to primary biological endpoint for the interim analysis per FDA agreements at meetings in February 2018, August 2018, and June 2019). Result: mean dystrophin rose from 0.9% to 1.7% of normal (casimersen) vs. 0.5% to 0.8% of normal (placebo); mean between-group difference approximately 0.59%, p=0.004
- Secondary/exploratory endpoint at interim: change from Baseline to Week 48 in percent exon-45 skipping by RT-ddPCR, mean between-group difference 1.599, p<0.001 (no multiplicity adjustment at interim); additional dystrophin analyses (immunohistochemistry intensity, percent dystrophin-positive fibers) were, per a pre-NDA agreement, not quantitatively submitted, and instead representative immunofluorescent images were reviewed qualitatively to confirm sarcolemmal localization
- The trial's overarching clinical primary endpoint was change from baseline in the 6MWT at Week 96, with additional functional assessments (10-meter walk/run velocity, North Star Ambulatory Assessment, rise-from-floor/4-stair-ascend velocity) at Week 96 and Week 144; clinical/functional data were withheld from the casimersen NDA to preserve the blind of the still-ongoing confirmatory trial
- Statistical methods: primary comparison via a two-sample permutation test (10,000 re-randomizations of treatment labels; two-sided nominal p-value = 2 x proportion of permuted differences more extreme than observed); Type 1 error of 0.01 (two-sided) allocated to the interim dystrophin comparison, with a pre-specified gatekeeping procedure linking the interim and final analyses to control overall two-sided alpha at 0.05; sensitivity analyses included a Wilcoxon rank-sum test, outlier-exclusion reanalysis, alternative imputation methods for below-LLOQ values, and a binary LLOQ-threshold dichotomized analysis (odds ratio 9.0 favoring casimersen); the unblinded interim analysis was conducted by an independent CRO statistical team uninvolved in trial design/conduct

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2021/213026Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2021/213026lbl.pdf
- FDA combined Clinical/Statistical (Medical) Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/213026Orig1s000MedR.pdf
- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/213026Orig1s000SumR.pdf
- FDA Other Review (Immunogenicity Assessment) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/213026Orig1s000OtherR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02500381
- Protocol / SAP: not posted on ClinicalTrials.gov for NCT02500381
- Related dose-titration/PK publication (not the pivotal accelerated-approval dataset; covers the separate first-in-human Study 4045-101): Wagner KR, Kuntz NL, Koenig E, et al. "Safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of casimersen in patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy amenable to exon 45 skipping: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-titration trial." *Muscle Nerve.* 2021;64(3):285-292. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1002/mus.27347), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34105177/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Safety%2C%20tolerability%2C%20and%20pharmacokinetics%20of%20casimersen%20in%20patients%20with%20Duchenne%20muscular%20dystrophy%20amenable%20to%20exon%2045%20skipping)
- Pivotal publication for the ESSENCE Part 1 casimersen-arm interim dystrophin results (the actual accelerated-approval dataset): no dedicated peer-reviewed publication was identified via PubMed as of this research; the only public source for these interim Week-48 results is the FDA review documents above. State plainly: not found.

**Other resources**

- ClinicalTrials.gov lists the study's individual participant data sharing statement as "UNDECIDED"; no Vivli or YODA listing was identified. State plainly: not confirmed.
- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held; the Summary Review states: "This application was not referred for review to an advisory committee because the safety profile of casimersen is acceptable for the intended population, the clinical trial designs were acceptable, and the findings on the surrogate marker were clear."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, NDA 213026, Benefit-Risk Assessment, p. 2]*

> "This submission contains biomarker and safety data from the casimersen arm of Study 4045-301, a double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter clinical trial with an open-label extension study to assess the efficacy and safety of casimersen and golodirsen in patients with DMD... Although the assessment of dystrophin protein expression (in biceps muscle biopsy samples) determined by western blot at Week 48 is listed as a secondary endpoint in the protocol, this served as the primary biological endpoint in the interim analysis to support accelerated approval for casimersen in this submission."

*[verbatim, same source, Clinical/Statistical — Efficacy, p. 13]*

> "For each time point (Baseline vs. Week 48 of Part 2), replicate gel runs were performed to determine dystrophin level (% normal) by western blot... A two-sample permutation test was conducted to compare the treatment groups. A permutation of 10,000 re-randomizations was performed... For the interim analysis, a Type 1 error of 0.01 was assigned to the comparison between casimersen and placebo in change from Baseline to Week 48 in the quantity of dystrophin expression, as measured by western blot. Change from Baseline to Week 48 in exon 45 skipping... was analyzed as an exploratory endpoint for the interim analysis, without formal adjustment of multiplicity. A gatekeeping testing procedure that covers the interim analysis and the final analysis will be used to adjust for multiplicity in order to control the overall Type 1 error rate at a 2-sided significance level of 0.05."

*[verbatim, same source, p. 14]*

> "To ensure the integrity of the study conduct and maintain the blinding of the trial, the interim analysis was performed by a contract research organization (CRO) unblinded statistical team that was not otherwise involved in the trial design or conduct of Study 4045-301, other than for support of the DMC and for the unblinded integrity safety summary."

*[verbatim, same source, Results, p. 16]*

> "These results were verified by the FDA statistical and clinical reviewers. The statistical reviewer also conducted a sensitivity analysis using a Wilcoxon Rank Sum test, which is a nonparametric test with very few assumptions. The analysis result (p-value = 0.0008, not shown in table) supported the primary analysis."

*[verbatim, same source, p. 18]*

> "Although there remains uncertainty regarding the level of dystrophin that would be likely to confer clinical benefit, the increase in dystrophin levels demonstrated for casimersen is similar in size to other approved ASO's, such as eteplirsen and golodirsen, that have received accelerated approval based on a conclusion by CDER that the increase in dystrophin level was reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit."

*[verbatim, FDA combined Clinical/Statistical Review, Section 7.3.3, p. 127]*

> "For decades there have been widespread scientific and clinical discussions about the threshold of dystrophin expression that is needed in skeletal muscle fibers in order to increase or to normalize muscle function in patients with DMD. The discussions have reached no consensus, and hence this reviewer will not provide an exhaustive review or summary of the pertinent biomedical literature."

**Reverse-engineered SAP** (points not directly quotable verbatim, inferred and traced to reported results):

- *[inferred]* the 43-patient interim analysis set (27 casimersen : 16 placebo) implies the interim look was locked at a pre-specified enrollment count (first 45 exon-45-amenable enrollees) rather than a calendar cutoff, traced to the Summary Review's "Patient Disposition" subsection describing the first 45 patients enrolled as the analysis trigger
- *[inferred]* the choice of a permutation test (rather than a t-test) for a 43-subject, 2:1-randomized biomarker comparison suggests the SAP pre-specified an exact/re-randomization-based test to avoid normality assumptions given the expected non-normal, LLOQ-truncated distribution of dystrophin values, traced to the reported below-LLOQ proportion (24/43, 56%) and the parallel Wilcoxon and LLOQ-dichotomization sensitivity analyses run by FDA
- *[inferred]* the pre-specified gatekeeping structure linking the interim (dystrophin, alpha=0.01) and final (functional/6MWT) analyses implies the original SAP treated the accelerated-approval dystrophin analysis as a formal alpha-consuming interim look nested within the overall Type I error budget of the still-ongoing ESSENCE trial, rather than as a wholly separate/exploratory analysis, traced to the explicit "Type 1 error of 0.01... gatekeeping testing procedure" language with no further public detail on the final-analysis testing hierarchy

Casimersen is the fourth Sarepta/Nippon-Shinyaku exon-skipping DMD drug in this census approved via the dystrophin-biomarker accelerated-approval pathway, but distinctively drew its pivotal biomarker data from an interim look at one arm of a larger, still-ongoing randomized confirmatory trial (ESSENCE) rather than from a separate small dedicated biomarker study — and, unlike golodirsen, drew no recorded internal FDA dissent in the released review package.

### 30. Fosdenopterin (Nulibry) — NDA 214018

**Sponsor:** Origin Biosciences, Inc. (applicant of record on the NDA and approval letter; Origin licensed/acquired the program, including IND 117502, from Alexion Pharmaceuticals, Inc., the original developer, via an IND transfer in September 2018; the drug is currently marketed by Sentynl Therapeutics, Inc., a BridgeBio Pharma affiliate, which was not the NDA holder at the time of approval)

**Indication approved:** To reduce the risk of mortality in patients with molybdenum cofactor deficiency (MoCD) Type A, an ultra-rare (estimated US prevalence 45-54 patients, all under age 10), autosomal-recessive, usually fatal neonatal/infantile metabolic disease caused by MOCS1 mutations leading to cyclic pyranopterin monophosphate (cPMP) deficiency and toxic accumulation of S-sulfocysteine

**Approval date:** February 26, 2021 (regular, traditional approval, not accelerated approval, since survival is a direct clinical outcome rather than a surrogate)

**Pivotal trial:** no single randomized pivotal trial; the "adequate and well-controlled investigation" was a pooled, cross-study, genotype-matched external-control survival comparison built from four studies: MCD-501 (retrospective observational, NCT01640717), MCD-201 (open-label, NCT02047461), and MCD-202 (open-label Phase 2/3, originally intended as the confirmatory trial, NCT02629393) as the treated cohort, versus MCD-502 (retrospective-and-prospective natural-history study, NCT01735188) as the untreated historical-control cohort

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* uncontrolled, open-label, single-arm/multi-study pooled treatment cohort (n=13 across three trials) compared to an external, non-contemporaneous, genotype-matched natural-history control cohort (n=18 matched of a 37-patient full untreated cohort) — a genotype-matched external/historical-control survival comparison ("genotype-matched full-matching survival comparison against a pooled external natural-history cohort, with inverse-probability weighting for unequal match ratios"); the originally planned confirmatory trial (MCD-202) used a Bayesian design comparing a responder proportion to a fixed threshold derived from an interim natural-history analysis, but was abandoned after enrollment failure (1 patient enrolled) in favor of a post hoc pooled overall-survival analysis
- *Endpoints:* primary — overall survival (OS), defined as the interval in months from date of birth to date of death or date last known alive; secondary/confirmatory — urinary and plasma S-sulfocysteine reduction (biomarker), growth, seizure frequency, feeding, motor/neurocognitive function, neuroimaging, and PK
- *Primary analysis:* log-rank test comparing treated vs. untreated groups; Kaplan-Meier estimation of survival probabilities at 6 months/1/2/3 years; Cox proportional-hazards model with hazard ratio and 95% CI computed via the modified score-test method of Lin et al. (2016) rather than Wald CIs, to align with log-rank results; inverse-probability weighting (Austin and Stuart 2017) to estimate an average treatment effect across unbalanced full-matching strata; genotype-based 1:many patient matching (exact homozygous mutation match preferred, else similar-impact mutation class) used as the primary bias-mitigation strategy in place of randomization
- *Multiplicity:* no formal multiplicity control; FDA explicitly treated all mortality analyses as post hoc (formulated after outcomes were known) and reported that "all p-values presented in this review are nominal"
- *Missing data/bias:* extensive dedicated FDA sections on potential selection bias and potential detection bias / spurious mortality benefit, addressed via genotype matching, comparison of age-at-symptom-onset distributions, geographic/standard-of-care matching, and sensitivity analyses excluding mismatched pairs, excluding early treatment discontinuers under two alternative censoring rules, restricting to exact-genotype matches only, and restricting to overlapping birth-year cohorts (all yielded consistent conclusions)
- *Regulatory:* Orphan Drug Designation, Breakthrough Therapy Designation, Rare Pediatric Disease Designation with an accompanying priority-review-voucher request, and Priority Review; no Advisory Committee meeting; no REMS (phototoxicity risk mitigated via labeling and enhanced postmarketing pharmacovigilance)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- MCD-201 (NCT02047461): uncontrolled, open-label, nonrandomized, unblinded study of fosdenopterin in patients with MoCD Type A already on rcPMP; 8 patients treated across 5 centers (US, Australia, Netherlands, UK, Tunisia); primary endpoint safety, with growth/seizure frequency/feeding/motor/neurocognitive function/neuroimaging/biomarkers/PK/long-term safety as secondary endpoints
- MCD-202 (NCT02629393): uncontrolled, open-label, nonrandomized study in neonates (first 28 days of life) with confirmed or suspected MoCD Type A; originally planned as the confirmatory adequate-and-well-controlled study with target enrollment of 5-10 patients and a primary endpoint of the proportion of patients alive and able to sit upright independently for at least 30 seconds at Month 12, to be analyzed with a Bayesian method comparing the treated response rate to a 10% threshold derived from an interim analysis of the MCD-502 natural-history study; enrollment paused after 1 patient due to recruitment difficulty, so this design was never executed as planned
- MCD-501 (NCT01640717): retrospective, observational, noninterventional chart-review study of patients with MoCD Type A/B/unknown type previously treated with rcPMP under individual-patient IND/named-patient use; 15 patients enrolled (10 with confirmed MoCD Type A) across 13 centers in Germany, UK, Netherlands, Australia, Turkey, and the US
- MCD-502 (NCT01735188): retrospective-and-prospective natural-history study of untreated/historically treated MoCD patients; 37 patients with confirmed MoCD Type A included in the Full Analysis Set (20 already deceased at enrollment via retrospective chart review, 17 living, 14 of whom entered a 12-month prospective follow-up) across 27 centers in Canada, Germany, Spain, UK, Israel, Italy, Japan, Malaysia, and others; no prespecified primary endpoint, since the study's objective was to characterize natural history including survival
- Primary efficacy endpoint (final, FDA-agreed pooled analysis): overall survival, interval in months from birth to death or date last known alive; patients still enrolled were censored at the safety-update data cutoffs (initial NDA data cutoff July 4, 2019)
- Analysis populations: the Full Analysis Set (all MoCD Type A patients, treated and untreated, across the four studies: 13 treated vs. 37 untreated); and the Genotype-Matched Analysis Set (the 13 treated patients matched via full matching, not 1:1, to 18 untreated natural-history patients sharing the same homozygous MOCS1 mutation, 9 of 13 exact matches, or, failing that, a mutation of similar predicted functional impact for the remaining 4)
- Sample size/power: no prospective power calculation; the analysis set was fixed by the number of patients available across the four completed/ongoing studies; no formal interim-analysis/alpha-spending plan for the pooled survival analysis
- Statistical methods: log-rank test (unadjusted, and stratified by matched ID); Kaplan-Meier method for survival probabilities at 6 months, 1, 2, and 3 years, and median survival time; Cox proportional-hazards model for hazard-ratio estimation, with 95% CIs from both Wald and the modified score-test method of Lin et al. (2016); an inverse-probability-weighted Cox model to estimate an average treatment effect accounting for unequal match ratios (weights ranging approximately 0.6-2.1); FDA added restricted mean survival time as a supplementary summary; planned covariate-adjusted analyses for sex and age-at-symptom-onset (the latter not implemented, since no treated patients had onset after 28 days)

**Other resources**

> "Substantial evidence of effectiveness for Nulibry for the treatment of MoCD Type A was established with one adequate and well-controlled investigation plus confirmatory evidence. The adequate and well-controlled investigation demonstrated improved survival for a cohort of patients treated with synthetic or recombinant cPMP pooled from two clinical trials and a retrospective observational study compared to a matched observational cohort of untreated patients."

*[verbatim, same source, Section 6.2.1.3 "Statistical Analysis Plan," p. 26]*

> "Study MCD-202 was originally intended to be the confirmatory, adequate and well-controlled study and planned enrollment of 5 to 10 patients with MoCD Type A. The primary endpoint was specified to be the proportion of patients alive and able to sit upright independently for at least 30 seconds at month 12. This endpoint was planned to be analyzed using a Bayesian method comparing the response rate for the primary endpoint in the treated patients to 10%, which was based on an interim analysis of the natural history study (Study MCD-502)... Subsequently, discussions began with the Agency regarding the combined use of data from all three studies of treated patients to compare to the untreated patients in the natural history study."

*[verbatim, same source, Section 6.2.1.3, p. 27]*

> "Because all the mortality analyses performed in the SAP were post hoc (these analyses were formulated after mortality outcomes were known for each patient), the focus of the review of efficacy is to conduct various analyses of OS to ensure that the results are not driven by a single choice of statistical methodology, to assess for biases, and to address risk of type 1 error. Due to the post hoc nature of the analyses, all p-values presented in this review are nominal."

*[verbatim, same source, Section 6.2.1.3, p. 28]*

> "The SAP specified using the log-rank test to compare treated and natural history control patients and using Kaplan-Meier (KM) plots and methods to estimate survival parameters for each group, including OS rates at 6 months, 1 year, and 2 years. Additionally, the SAP specified analyzing OS using the Cox proportional hazards model... Hazard ratios were estimated... and 95% confidence intervals were estimated based on the modified score test statistic under the Cox model as described in (Lin et al. 2016)."

*[verbatim, same source, Table 14, p. 37]*

> Unadjusted HR, fosdenopterin (n=13) vs. untreated genotype-matched analysis set (n=18): 0.18; 95% CI (Lin et al. method) 0.04 to 0.72; p=0.012.

*[verbatim, same source, Section 6.3.1 "Potential for Selection Bias," p. 39]*

> "The lack of a randomized control group resulted in the potential for selection bias that could lead to uncertainty regarding the comparability of the treatment and control groups... Genotype matching between treated patients and untreated control patients was used in the survival analysis for Nulibry (Misko et al. 2020)."

*[verbatim, same source, Section 6.3.2 "Potential for Detection Bias," p. 41]*

> "We are reassured that detection bias was not a contributing factor and that the mortality benefit observed was not spurious."

*[verbatim, same source, Benefit-Risk Table 2, pp. 5-6]*

> "Despite the limitations resulting from the lack of randomization, the use of an external noncontemporaneous control group, and the use of retrospective observational data in the treatment cohort, we determined that the efficacy data were adequate to support a conclusion that Nulibry provides a survival benefit in patients with MoCD Type A."

Fosdenopterin/Nulibry closes this batch with the same fundamental design logic as lonafarnib/Zokinvy — a genotype/natural-history-matched external-control survival comparison built after the fact from pooled treated and untreated cohorts across multiple non-randomized studies — but here pooling three separate treated-cohort trials (one of which, MCD-202, was the abandoned attempt at a genuinely randomized/Bayesian-threshold confirmatory design) against a fourth, dedicated natural-history study, with FDA's review devoting extended, explicit sections to ruling out selection and detection bias in lieu of randomization.
