*[verbatim, sponsor SAP §2.2.2.1, "Primary Efficacy Endpoint"]* — "The primary efficacy endpoint of this study is the area under the curve from Day 90 to Day 180 (AUC24-hour Uox), based on percent change from baseline in 24-hour Uox (adjusted per 1.73 m2 body surface area [BSA] in participants aged <18 years)."

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP §8.1, "Primary Efficacy Analysis"]* — "This is a superiority study. For the primary endpoint, the null hypothesis to be tested is: H0: AUC24-hour Uox, a = AUC24-hour Uox, p against one-sided alternative hypothesis HA: AUC24-hour Uox, a > AUC24-hour Uox, p... All hypotheses will be tested at the one-sided significance level alpha of 2.5%. Mean AUC24-hour Uox from Day 90 to Day 180 will be compared between treatment groups using an ANCOVA model with treatment group as a main effect in the model; and age category..., eGFR category..., and baseline Uox as covariates... The primary efficacy analysis will be based on the MITT dataset."

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP §6.1.4, "Multiple Comparisons"]* — "A hierarchical testing procedure will be used to control type I error. If the superiority is established for the primary endpoint, statistical testing and p-value estimation for the secondary endpoints will be performed in a pre-specified sequence... Step 1. Test for superiority of the AUC for DCR-PHXC versus control, and record the one-sided p-value, p1. If p1 <0.025, then declare the test for primary endpoint to be statistically significant and proceed to Step 2; otherwise record the nominal p-values for all the secondary endpoints."

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP §4.2, "Interim Analysis and Data Monitoring"]* — "No interim analysis will be conducted. The final analysis will use an alpha of 0.025. A DSMC was convened to provide periodic review of the efficacy and safety data. The DSMC is comprised of three voting members independent of the study team and sponsor."

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP §3.2, "Sample Size and Power"]* — "For the sample size calculations, the primary endpoint of AUC24-hour Uox from Day 90 to Day 180 based on percent change from baseline was used. The group sequential design with pre-specified alpha spending for interim analysis and final analysis was utilized... The above sample size calculation was performed under the assumption that there may be an interim analysis to re-estimate sample size after two-thirds of participants complete the study. However due to late enrollment experienced in the study, an interim analysis will not be performed."

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP §6.1.5.1, "Missing Efficacy Endpoint Data"]* — "For the analysis of AUC related efficacy endpoints, based on the MITT or ITT populations, a multiple imputation (MI) approach under the missing-at-random (MAR) assumption will be used to handle missing endpoint data... This process will be repeated 50 times, resulting in 50 complete analysis data sets."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review §6.2.1.3, "Statistical Analysis Plan, DCR-PHXC-201"]* — "Despite the Agency's recommendation to conduct key efficacy analyses on the intent-to-treat (ITT) rather than the modified ITT (mITT) population, all of the Applicant's analyses were conducted on the mITT population, defined as all randomized participants who had at least one efficacy assessment after the Day 90 dosing visit. Consistent with the Agency's recommendation, analyses which conform to the ITT principle are provided in this review."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review §6.3.1, "The Interpretability of AUC as Descriptor of Efficacy"]* — "Unlike mean percentage change, the value of AUC may vary according to the temporal sequence in which the underlying values of percentage change are recorded and, as a consequence, in small trials, such as the present one, AUC is more likely to generate random highs and lows in mean outcome that are not clinically meaningful... The fact that the treatment effect of nedosiran on AUC was large and highly statistically significant despite this 'noise' supports the conclusion that there is a true treatment effect... the review team has also requested inclusion in labeling of the least-squares mean percentage change from Baseline in 24 h urinary oxalate excretion... averaged over Days 90, 120, 150, and 180 as this will be more easily understood by prescribers and this analysis does not have the same statistical issues as the AUC endpoint."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review §16.2, "Adaptive Randomization and Assessment of Statistical Significance"]* — "Given the adaptive randomization, rerandomization tests are preferable when testing for statistical significance. To conduct such tests, 50 new randomizations were first conducted with randomized arm assigned to each individual according to the Applicant's adaptive randomization scheme... Rerandomization tests performed in this manner confirmed the statistical significance of the primary endpoint results. To provide adequate precision in the estimated p-values, at least 10,000 rerandomizations were needed. The analysis documented here was based on 13,500 trial rerandomizations and yielded a p-value of 0.001 when participants with PH1 or PH2 were analyzed, and a p-value of <0.001 when participants with PH1 were analyzed."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review §16.5, "Potential Impact of Missing Data on Analysis Results"]* — "Sensitivity analysis to account for potential inaccuracies in the imputation of missing data should address a broad range of 'extreme' scenarios in which the investigational treatment has no or even negative effects on outcome among participants missing data. The Applicant did not provide extensive sensitivity analyses and so these analyses were conducted by the review team."

Note on source-document quality: both the ClinicalTrials.gov-posted SAP (`SAP_001.pdf`) and Protocol (`Prot_000.pdf`) extracted cleanly via `pdftotext -layout` — normal inter-word spacing, no evidence of the character-by-character-spacing-stripped artifact seen in some other Novo Nordisk-posted CTG documents — so no text reconstruction was necessary for this entry; every SAP/Protocol passage above is a direct, undamaged extraction. A small number of isolated spans within the SAP (specific numeric age/eGFR covariate-category cutoffs in §6.1.3, §6.1.9, and §8.1) are corrupted by an apparent custom-font glyph-substitution artifact affecting only those spans (not a spacing-stripping issue, and not confidently reversible to exact digits); those specific cutoff values are therefore omitted from this entry rather than guessed, and the Trial design & endpoints section above describes the covariates only in the general terms ("age category," "eGFR category") that extract cleanly and are corroborated by the FDA Integrated Review's own (undamaged) description of the same model.

### 46. Vamorolone (Agamree) — NDA 215239

**Sponsor:** Santhera Pharmaceuticals (Switzerland) Ltd. (applicant of record on the original NDA and the FDA approval letter, dated October 26, 2023); the underlying IND (118,942) had been held by ReveraGen BioPharma, Inc. through most of development and was transferred to Santhera on October 1, 2022, shortly before NDA submission; Catalyst Pharmaceuticals, Inc. became the applicant of record on the first efficacy supplement (NDA 215239/S-001, approved 2024) after acquiring North American commercialization rights, and is now listed as the current "Company" on Drugs@FDA's overview page for this application

**Indication approved:** Treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in patients 2 years of age and older (the pivotal trial itself enrolled only ages 4 to <7; the 2-to-<4 and older age ranges were extrapolated — see Documents/SAP below)

**Approval date:** October 26, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** Study VBP15-004 ("VISION-DMD"), NCT03439670

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo- and active-controlled trial in which the placebo and prednisone arms crossed over to vamorolone at a fixed protocol timepoint (Week 24-28) rather than at investigator/patient-triggered progression — this fixed-timepoint mandatory crossover of control arms is distinct from the taxonomy's existing "crossover permitted at progression" entry ("fixed-timepoint mandatory crossover of control arms to the experimental drug"); six treatment groups (vamorolone 2.0 mg/kg, vamorolone 6.0 mg/kg, prednisone 0.75 mg/kg, placebo, each further split by Period 2 vamorolone dose) randomized 2:2:1:1:1:1, stratified by baseline age (<6 years vs. ≥6 years); small randomized trial (n=121) in a rare pediatric neuromuscular disease

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint is a continuous motor-function change-from-baseline measure — time-to-stand (TTSTAND) velocity, rises/second — which is not covered by the taxonomy's existing "continuous psychiatric/neurological rating-scale change-from-baseline endpoint" entry ("continuous motor-function change-from-baseline endpoint"); key secondary motor endpoints were 6-minute walk test (6MWT) distance and time-to-run/walk (TTRW) 10-meter velocity, each tested at both vamorolone doses vs. placebo and vs. prednisone

- *Primary analysis:* REML-based mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) with an unstructured covariance matrix and Kenward-Roger denominator degrees of freedom, analyzed on observed cases without imputation as the primary approach — a specific MMRM variant not already captured by the taxonomy's sandwich-variance-estimator MMRM entry; non-parametric Wilcoxon rank-sum test used as a normality-assumption sensitivity check

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing across 7 pre-ordered dose/endpoint comparisons (TTSTAND 2.0mg→6MWT 6.0mg→6MWT 2.0mg→TTRW 6.0mg→TTRW 2.0mg→6MWT 6.0mg-vs-prednisone→6MWT 2.0mg-vs-prednisone), each at two-sided α=0.05, testing stopped at the first p>0.05 or wrong-direction result

- *Interim/alpha-spending:* no interim efficacy analyses were planned; an independent DSMB reviewed safety data only

- *Missing data/bias:* multiple imputation (MCMC, missing-at-random) followed by a Copy-Reference (control-based pattern-mixture, missing-not-at-random) imputation step for remaining non-COVID-related missingness — a reference-based MNAR method distinct from the taxonomy's existing jump-to-reference (J2R) entry ("Copy-Reference multiple imputation"); dedicated sensitivity analyses re-classifying assessments that were missing, delayed, or collected by video because of the COVID-19 pandemic ("pandemic-driven assessment-disruption sensitivity analysis"); a floor-effect/influential-observation sensitivity analysis truncated all TTSTAND raw times <2.5 seconds to 2.5 seconds before computing velocity

- *Regulatory:* approval rested on a single adequate and well-controlled trial in a rare pediatric disease, explicitly invoking FDA's 2019 guidance "Demonstrating Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness for Human Drug and Biological Products" ("single-trial approval in a rare disease under the 2019 substantial-evidence-of-effectiveness guidance"); FDA extrapolated the approved age range down to 2 years using regulatory precedent from a different, already-approved drug in the same indication (deflazacort's prior age-extrapolation reasoning), not from data generated in this pivotal trial ("cross-drug, same-indication age-extrapolation precedent," distinct from the taxonomy's existing single-drug/single-trial-setting extrapolation entry); no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held; sponsor's request for a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher was denied and the application received a standard (not priority) review; sponsor-of-record change (Santhera → Catalyst Pharmaceuticals) via a post-approval efficacy supplement

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study VBP15-004 (VISION-DMD) was a randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, multicenter (33 sites), multinational (11 countries) Phase IIb trial in ambulant boys ages 4 to <7 years with genetically confirmed DMD, able to walk independently and complete the TTSTAND test unassisted in <10 seconds at screening; key exclusions included prior glucocorticoid/immunosuppressive treatment, symptomatic cardiomyopathy, and current treatment with eteplirsen or ataluren

- Period 1 (Weeks 1-24) randomized subjects 2:2:1:1:1:1, stratified by baseline age (<6 vs. ≥6 years), to vamorolone 2.0 mg/kg/day, vamorolone 6.0 mg/kg/day, prednisone 0.75 mg/kg/day, or placebo (planned n=120; 121 actually randomized); Period 2 (Weeks 28-48) was an open-label-controlled double-blind extension in which placebo- and prednisone-assigned subjects crossed over to one of the two vamorolone doses, followed by a 4-week dose-tapering period (Weeks 49-52); only Period 1 (through Week 24) is covered by the publicly posted SAP (Final v3.0, 17 May 2021) — the Week 48 analysis was pre-specified as "the subject of a second SAP," which was not found posted on ClinicalTrials.gov

- Primary efficacy endpoint: change from baseline to Week 24 in TTSTAND velocity (1/TTSTAND seconds, rises/sec) for vamorolone 6.0 mg/kg vs. placebo; TTSTAND measures time to rise from supine to standing and is a NorthStar Ambulatory Assessment (NSAA) item previously used as a secondary endpoint in the deflazacort DMD trials

- Secondary efficacy endpoints (fixed sequential order, all vs. placebo unless noted): TTSTAND velocity (2.0 mg/kg), 6MWT distance (6.0 mg/kg), 6MWT distance (2.0 mg/kg), TTRW velocity (6.0 mg/kg), TTRW velocity (2.0 mg/kg), 6MWT distance (6.0 mg/kg vs. prednisone), 6MWT distance (2.0 mg/kg vs. prednisone); additional non-multiplicity-controlled secondaries included TTCLIMB velocity, NSAA total score, and knee/elbow myometry

- Sample size: powered from external Phase IIa (VBP15-002/003) TTSTAND data using two-sided unequal-variance t-tests at α=0.05; 30 subjects/arm (2.0 mg/kg, 6.0 mg/kg, prednisone, placebo; 120 total) was estimated to give ~91% power to detect a significant 6.0 mg/kg-vs-placebo difference in TTSTAND velocity at Week 24

- Statistical methods: primary/secondary analyses used a REML-based MMRM (fixed effects: treatment, baseline age group, week, baseline value of the endpoint as covariate, treatment-by-week interaction; unstructured covariance; Kenward-Roger denominator degrees of freedom) on the modified intention-to-treat (mITT-1) population — all randomized subjects with ≥1 dose and ≥1 post-baseline efficacy assessment during Period 1; extensive sensitivity analyses covered multiple-imputation missing-data handling, COVID-19-driven missingness/video-assessment substitution, and an influential-observation (TTSTAND-floor) transformation; a Per-Protocol population served as a secondary/supportive analysis set

- Results (FDA statistical reviewer's independent re-analysis, mITT-1): TTSTAND velocity LS-mean difference 0.0603 rises/sec (95% CI 0.0230-0.0976), p=0.0018 for vamorolone 6.0 mg/kg vs. placebo (primary endpoint met); TTSTAND 2.0 mg/kg vs. placebo, 0.0449 (0.0082-0.0816), p=0.0171; 6MWT 6.0 mg/kg vs. placebo, 42.485 m (15.577-69.394), p=0.0023 (also reported elsewhere in the same FDA review as 41.586 m, p=0.0033 — the two FDA-review passages give slightly different point estimates/p-values for this comparison, a discrepancy present in the source document rather than introduced here); 6MWT 2.0 mg/kg vs. placebo, 37.124 m (9.553-64.696), p=0.0089; TTRW 6.0 mg/kg vs. placebo, 0.2439 m/sec (0.0932-0.3945), p=0.0018; TTRW 2.0 mg/kg vs. placebo, 0.1273 m/sec (-0.0263-0.2809), p=0.1031 — not significant, so the fixed-sequence procedure stopped there and the two 6MWT-vs-prednisone comparisons were reported only as nominal (non-multiplicity-controlled) p-values

### 47. Eplontersen (Wainua) — NDA 217388

**Sponsor:** Ionis Pharmaceuticals, Inc. was the applicant of record at the time of FDA approval — the NDA approval letter (December 21, 2023) is addressed to Ionis Pharmaceuticals, and FDA's Integrated Review lists "Applicant: Ionis Pharmaceuticals" in its Application Information table — eplontersen was developed by Ionis in collaboration with Akcea Therapeutics under IND 139521. Drugs@FDA's current overview page for NDA 217388 lists "AstraZeneca AB" as the sponsor, reflecting AstraZeneca's role as Ionis's global collaboration/commercialization partner for eplontersen; the exact administrative date on which applicant-of-record status transferred to AstraZeneca was not independently confirmed in this research pass

**Indication approved:** Treatment of the polyneuropathy of hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis (hATTR-PN) in adults — a transthyretin-directed, GalNAc-conjugated (ligand-conjugated antisense, LICA) antisense oligonucleotide administered by monthly subcutaneous injection

**Approval date:** December 21, 2023 (standard review; orphan drug designation granted January 6, 2022)

**Pivotal trial:** NEURO-TTRansform (Study ION-682884-CS3), NCT04136184; its efficacy comparator was not a concurrent placebo arm but the external/historical placebo cohort from the earlier pivotal inotersen trial NEURO-TTR (ISIS-420915-CS2, NCT01737398, EudraCT 2012-001831-30)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized (6:1), open-label, multicenter, multinational Phase 3 trial with a concurrent active-reference arm (inotersen, summarized descriptively only, no statistical comparison) plus a propensity-score-weighted external (cross-trial) historical placebo control drawn from a prior, separately conducted pivotal trial of a different drug in the same indication, used in place of a concurrent placebo arm ("randomized, open-label trial with a propensity-score-weighted external/historical placebo control substituting for a concurrent placebo arm"); single adequate/well-controlled trial supported by pharmacodynamic/mechanistic confirmatory evidence and same-class precedent (*Regular approval supported by same-pharmacologic-class precedent as confirmatory evidence*)

- *Endpoints:* continuous neurological rating-scale change-from-baseline endpoints (reuse: *Continuous psychiatric/neurological rating-scale change-from-baseline endpoint*) — modified Neuropathy Impairment Score +7 (mNIS+7) at Week 35, treated by FDA's clinical review as the primary clinical endpoint, and the Norfolk Quality of Life Questionnaire-Diabetic Neuropathy (Norfolk QOL-DN) at Week 35, a key secondary/co-primary endpoint; percent change from Baseline in serum TTR concentration was the sponsor's third co-primary/first-ranked endpoint in the SAP's testing sequence but was explicitly downgraded by FDA to an "additional" pharmacodynamic/mechanistic endpoint rather than a primary clinical endpoint

- *Primary analysis:* MMRM (for serum TTR) and ANCOVA (for mNIS+7 and Norfolk QOL-DN, since only one post-baseline assessment existed at the Week 35 analysis), both adjusted by propensity-score weighting/covariate (logistic-regression propensity score built from disease stage, V30M mutation status, and prior tafamidis/diflunisal treatment) to improve comparability between the trial's eplontersen arm and the external historical placebo cohort ("propensity-score-adjusted MMRM/ANCOVA for cross-trial external-control comparability"); full analysis set defined as all randomized/treated subjects with a baseline and ≥1 post-baseline mNIS+7 or Norfolk QOL-DN assessment

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) ranking-strategy hierarchical testing — serum TTR → mNIS+7 → Norfolk QOL-DN → five further secondary endpoints, each two-sided at α=0.025 (α=0.05 for endpoints not reached in the ranked sequence); for any endpoint tested at both the Week 35 interim and a hypothetical Week 66 final analysis, the final-analysis alpha level was to be set by a Westfall & Young (1993) resampling procedure (10,000 re-randomizations to estimate the interim/final test-statistic correlation, then solving for a joint-error-rate-preserving critical value) — since all three ranked endpoints reached significance at the Week 35 interim look, this resampling step was never actually invoked ("Westfall-Young resampling-based alpha reallocation between an interim and final test of the same hierarchically ranked endpoint")

- *Interim/alpha-spending:* single prespecified interim analysis at Week 35, prespecified in the protocol/SAP to serve as the final efficacy analysis for any endpoint that reached significance at that look — because all three ranked endpoints (TTR, mNIS+7, Norfolk QOL-DN) were significant at Week 35, the interim analysis became the sole confirmatory analysis and the planned Week 66 "final analysis" of these endpoints was never conducted

- *Missing data/bias:* multiple imputation (missing-at-random imputation model stratified by treatment group, 500 imputed datasets combined via Rubin's rules) for missing Week 35 mNIS+7/Norfolk QOL-DN values; FDA's own worst-case-scenario sensitivity analysis imputed a fixed +20-point (drug arm) / −20-point (placebo arm) penalty for missing mNIS+7 data (20 points being the planning-stage assumed effect size) and confirmed the primary conclusion held (p<0.05) under this penalty; open-label design with an external placebo control was explicitly flagged by FDA as "potentially subject to bias," mitigated (per FDA) by the historical cohort's similar eligibility criteria/sites/era and by using a largely objective composite endpoint (mNIS+7)

- *Regulatory:* FDA rejected the sponsor's proposed use of serum TTR reduction as a primary endpoint at a pre-IND meeting (February 21, 2019), directing mNIS+7 and Norfolk QOL-DN as co-primary clinical endpoints instead; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held ("did not raise significant efficacy or safety issues"); approval rested on a single adequate/well-controlled trial plus confirmatory pharmacodynamic (serum TTR reduction) and same-drug-class precedent (inotersen, approved 2018 on the same endpoint pair)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- NEURO-TTRansform (ION-682884-CS3) was a Phase 3, multinational (16 countries), multicenter (52 sites), randomized, open-label trial in adults with Stage 1 or Stage 2 hATTR-PN; subjects were randomized 6:1 via IXRS to eplontersen 45 mg SC once every 4 weeks or inotersen 300 mg SC once weekly (the latter switching to eplontersen at Week 37 after completing Week 35 assessments); all subjects received daily supplemental vitamin A; a ≤10-week screening period preceded an 84-week treatment period and a 20-week post-treatment evaluation period (or rollover into an open-label extension, ION-682884-CS13)

- The efficacy comparator was not a concurrent placebo arm but the placebo cohort (n=60 randomized, 59 in the FAS) of the earlier pivotal inotersen trial NEURO-TTR (ISIS-420915-CS2, NCT01737398), selected for comparable eligibility criteria (disease stage, age range, gender, comorbidity exclusions, concomitant-medication restrictions), enrolled by the same sponsor within the prior 8 years; FDA agreed to this external-control design at a February 29, 2019 pre-IND meeting given the availability of highly effective standard-of-care therapies (making a concurrent placebo arm difficult to justify) and the expectation that the anticipated effect size would be large enough to overcome biases inherent to an external control; FDA separately required inclusion of the concurrent inotersen active-reference arm to characterize eplontersen's relative efficacy/safety against an approved comparator

- Primary/co-primary efficacy endpoints, per the sponsor's protocol/SAP (Amendment 5, 12 Aug 2021; SAP v2.1/2.1 Addendum, 03 Jun 2022): (1) percent change from Baseline to Week 35 in serum TTR concentration, (2) change from Baseline to Week 35 in mNIS+7, and (3, secondary in the SAP's own labeling but co-primary in FDA's Week 66 framing) change from Baseline to Week 35 in Norfolk QOL-DN, all comparing the eplontersen arm to the NEURO-TTR external placebo cohort; the reference (inotersen) arm was summarized descriptively only, with no statistical comparison against either the eplontersen arm or the external placebo

- Sample size: approximately 140 patients randomized 6:1 (~120 to eplontersen); assuming 10% dropout, ~108 evaluable eplontersen-treated patients compared against 52 evaluable NEURO-TTR placebo patients gave ≥90% power to detect a 19.6-point mNIS+7 difference (2-sided α=0.025), ≥80% power for a 10.7-point Norfolk QOL-DN difference, and ≥95% power for a 70.3-percentage-point serum-TTR difference; actual enrollment was 168 randomized (144 eplontersen, 24 inotersen)

- Statistical methods: MMRM (serum TTR, and later Week 66 endpoints) and ANCOVA (mNIS+7, Norfolk QOL-DN at Week 35, since only one post-baseline assessment existed), both models adjusted by a propensity score (logistic regression on disease stage, V30M mutation status, and prior tafamidis/diflunisal treatment) computed for each external-placebo or eplontersen subject, plus model terms for treatment, time, disease stage, V30M status, prior treatment, and baseline value; a pre-specified normality check (Shapiro-Wilk on ANCOVA residuals, α=0.01) triggered a stratified Wilcoxon rank-sum test as fallback; serum TTR values from the external (historical) placebo cohort were converted with the polynomial formula y=0.0057x²+0.5843x−0.3819 to match the current assay before use in the primary analysis; multiplicity controlled via a fixed-sequence ranking strategy (TTR → mNIS+7 → Norfolk QOL-DN → five further secondaries), each requiring significance at 2-sided α=0.025 (0.05 thereafter) to proceed, with a Westfall & Young (1993) resampling procedure specified (but never invoked) to reallocate alpha for any endpoint tested at both the Week 35 interim and a Week 66 final analysis

- Results (FDA Integrated Review, confirmed the Applicant's figures): mNIS+7 change from Baseline to Week 35, LS-mean difference −9.01 (95% CI −13.48, −4.54), p<0.0001 (FDA's independent re-analysis gave −9.03, attributed to Monte Carlo variation in the 500-run multiple imputation); Norfolk QOL-DN, LS-mean difference −11.79 (95% CI −16.82, −6.76), p<0.0001; serum TTR percent change, LS-mean difference −66.43 (95% CI −71.39, −61.47), p<0.0001; because all three ranked endpoints were significant at the Week 35 interim look, the interim analysis was treated as final and the Week 66 analyses of these three endpoints were never conducted

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

Approximately 140 patients will be randomized 6:1 to receive subcutaneous (SC) injections of either ION-682884 once every 4 weeks or inotersen once a week... At Week 35, an interim analysis will be performed in hierarchical order for the following 3 efficacy endpoints: 1) serum TTR reduction; 2) mNIS+7; 3) Norfolk QOL-DN."

*[verbatim, Protocol §10.5 Interim Analysis and Multiplicity, p.78]* — "An interim analysis will be performed to assess the efficacy and safety profile of ION-682884 comparing to the placebo arm of Neuro-TTR when all patients on ION-682884 complete Week 35 assessments... The statistical analysis will be conducted with 2-sided alpha level of 0.025. If any of the endpoint is not statistically significant, the remaining test(s) will not be conducted in the interim analysis."

*[verbatim, Protocol §10.5, p.78]* — "In the Week 66 Final Analysis, for those statistically significant endpoints at Week 35 Interim Analysis, their corresponding tests at the Week 66 Final Analysis will not be conducted in the ranking strategy for multiplicity... The alpha level for this endpoint will be determined by the resampling procedure (Westfall and Young 1993)... Repeat the above procedure N times (N = 10000) and obtain N pairs of test statistics T1 and T2. The correlation between T1 and T2 will then be estimated as the sample correlation of the N pairs."

*[verbatim, Statistical Analysis Plan v2.1, §4.10.2.1, "682884-CS03 Statistical Analysis Plan," p.46 of 47]* — "As noted in the Section 4.10.1, the TTR level from the Placebo arm in the NEURO-TTR trial will be converted using the following formula to match data generated by the current assay y=0.0057x^2+0.5843x-0.3819."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review §6.2.1.1 Design, p.33]* — "The open-label design with an external placebo control is potentially subject to bias. This was mitigated by using an external placebo group in the same disease population collected by the same Applicant within the last 8 years, using similar eligibility criteria, sites/regions, and staff, blinding the primary endpoints to the Applicant's team, and utilizing endpoints that are largely objective such as mNIS+7."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review §6.2.1.1, p.33, quoting the Division's February 29, 2019 pre-IND position]* — "the Division agreed to the use of an external control given the availability of highly effective therapies as standard of care, with the expectation that there would be a large magnitude of effect that could overcome the biases inherent to the use of an external control."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review §6.2.1.2, p.35, quoting FDA's February 21, 2019 pre-IND written response to the sponsor]* — "We do not agree with your proposal to use TTR reduction as a primary endpoint for your Phase 3 study. Although we note the importance of TTR reduction based on the mechanism of the drug, clinical outcomes should be assessed as the primary endpoints for the study. We strongly recommended the use of the Norfolk-QOL-DN and mNIS+7 as coprimary endpoints. TTR reduction would be most appropriate as a secondary endpoint, with adjustment for multiplicity."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review §6.2.1.4.2, Table 13, p.42-43]* — "The difference in least squares mean (LSM) (95% CI) was −9.01 (−13.48, −4.54) for eplontersen versus placebo (p<0.0001)" (mNIS+7, Week 35)

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review §6.2.1.4.3, p.44]* — "In the Agency's sensitivity analyses, a worst-case scenario imputing for missing data was performed where the missing from the placebo arm was assigned a change of -20 points while the missing from drug arm had a change of +20 points... Under the 'worst case scenario', the p-value was still less than 0.05, although larger than the p-value in the primary analysis."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review §2.2 Conclusions Regarding Benefit-Risk, p.21]* — "The effect sizes on the clinical endpoints were large and supported by the objective finding of reduction in TTR protein, and were adequate to overcome potential biases from the use of an external control. Therefore, the study is capable of serving as a single, adequate and well-controlled clinical study plus confirmatory evidence to establish substantial evidence of effectiveness of eplontersen treatment in adult patients with hATTR-PN."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review §11 Advisory Committee Summary, p.124]* — "This application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant efficacy or safety issues in the intended population."

### 48. Givinostat (Duvyzat) — NDA 217865

**Sponsor:** Italfarmaco S.p.A. (Italian parent company, applicant of record on the NDA; U.S. commercial distribution and labeling is through ITF Therapeutics, LLC, Italfarmaco's U.S. subsidiary; the NDA's U.S. regulatory agent of record was Freyr Inc.)

**Indication approved:** Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in patients 6 years of age and older — givinostat is a histone deacetylase (HDAC) class I and II inhibitor, the first HDAC inhibitor approved for DMD

**Approval date:** March 21, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** EPIDYS (Italfarmaco/Veristat internal designation "Study 48," DSC/14/2357/48; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02851797; EudraCT 2016-000401-36)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicentre, quadruple-masked (participant/caregiver/investigator/outcomes-assessor) Phase 3 trial; 2:1 randomization (givinostat:placebo); stratified by concomitant corticosteroid regimen (4 strata: deflazacort daily, deflazacort intermittent, other-steroid daily, other-steroid intermittent); biomarker-selected/enriched population — a prospectively defined "Target Population" (baseline vastus lateralis muscle fat fraction [VL MFF] by MRS >5% and ≤30%) served as the sole primary-efficacy analysis population, with a concurrently enrolled "Off-Target Population" (VL MFF ≤5% or >30%) providing supportive-only data, not formally tested; single planned interim analysis conducted by an independent data monitoring committee (IDMC)

- *Endpoints:* timed function test (TFT) change-from-baseline endpoint — primary endpoint was mean change from baseline to Month 18 in time (seconds) to climb 4 standard stairs (4-stair climb, 4SC) (existing taxonomy's "continuous ... rating-scale change-from-baseline endpoint" row covers clinician-rated scales like MADRS/RSBQ, not physical timed-performance tests); key secondary endpoints (functional): time to rise from floor, six-minute walk test (6MWT) distance, total North Star Ambulatory Assessment (NSAA) score, cumulative loss of function on the NSAA, muscle strength (knee extension/elbow flexion by hand-held myometry); key secondary endpoint (imaging): VL MFF by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) in a pre-specified MR Cohort, used post hoc as pharmacodynamic confirmatory evidence

- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA on the (log-transformed, back-transformed for presentation) continuous primary/key-secondary endpoints, with baseline value and re-derived age at first dose as covariates and randomized treatment/concomitant-steroid stratum as classification factors, reported as a generalized least-squares (GLS) mean ratio; negative binomial regression for cumulative NSAA loss-of-function counts; logistic regression for binary functional-decline endpoints; Cox proportional hazards for time-to-event functional endpoints

- *Multiplicity:* Hochberg step-up procedure applied to the family of 7 key secondary efficacy endpoints at the final analysis, gated behind (but not contingent on) the primary endpoint's own significance; 1-sided alpha of 0.025 (2-sided 0.05) for the primary endpoint; all other analyses (different timepoints, off-target population, subgroups) explicitly "supportive only," reported as nominal p-values

- *Interim/alpha-spending:* blinded internal-pilot sample-size re-estimation, triggered by a single interim futility gate on a non-primary pharmacodynamic surrogate (VL MFF, not the primary 4SC endpoint), performed without unblinding the primary endpoint and with no alpha spent/no early stopping for efficacy (distinct from the taxonomy's existing unblinded-conditional-power sample-size re-estimation entry, since here the primary endpoint itself was never unblinded and the futility check operated on a different, non-primary endpoint)

- *Missing data/bias:* two-class missing-data taxonomy (Class 1: missing for reasons unrelated to inability to perform the test, mean-imputed within treatment/stratum; Class 2: missing because non-ambulatory/physically unable to perform the test, imputed as zero or twice the maximum observed value depending on endpoint directionality) applied prior to the primary ANCOVA; tipping-point analysis (multiple imputation) pre-specified as a sensitivity analysis if the primary result was significant; FDA's statistical reviewers independently re-analyzed the primary endpoint via MMRM and a rank-based ANCOVA and found the sponsor's single-value imputation approach understated variability in a way that could inflate Type I error, and that the tipping-point sensitivity analysis (performed correctly per its own pre-specified method) no longer reached significance at zero shift

- *Regulatory:* approval based on a single adequate and well-controlled trial plus confirmatory evidence (2019 FDA draft guidance on substantial evidence of effectiveness), with the trial's MRS/VL-MFF pharmacodynamic signal and a post hoc open-label-extension-vs-natural-history comparison serving as the confirmatory evidence (this "one trial + confirmatory pharmacodynamic biomarker + natural history comparator" pathway is not yet represented in the taxonomy's regulatory-process table); FDA's own Integrated Review explicitly states the single trial, on its own, "is not statistically robust and is not capable of providing substantial evidence of effectiveness"; reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan (statistical reviewers flagged the sponsor's missing-data imputation method as biased/variance-underestimating, a concern not resolved before approval but offset by the totality-of-evidence framework)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Phase 3, randomized (2:1 givinostat:placebo), double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicentre trial in ambulant male subjects ≥6 years old with genetically confirmed DMD, on stable background corticosteroids for ≥6 months; conducted at sites in the U.S., Canada, and Europe (Italy, Germany, Spain, and others); enrollment window June 2017-February 2022 per ClinicalTrials.gov, 18-month double-blind treatment period plus a 4-week follow-up

- Eligibility required a screening 4SC ≤8 seconds (two assessments within ±1 second of each other), time to rise from floor 3-<10 seconds, and manual muscle testing of quadriceps ≥Grade 3; exclusions included recent investigational-drug or dystrophin-restoration-therapy (e.g., exon-skipping) exposure and ankle contracture ≥30 degrees

- Design used a two-population structure: a prospectively defined "Target Population" (baseline VL MFF by MRS >5% and ≤30%) was the sole basis for all formal (alpha-controlled) efficacy analyses; a concurrently enrolled "Off-Target Population" (VL MFF ≤5% or >30%, up to ~35% of total enrollment) contributed supportive-only, non-alpha-controlled data; of 359 subjects screened, 179 were randomized (118 givinostat, 61 placebo), of whom 120 (81 givinostat, 39 placebo) were in the Target Population analyzed for primary efficacy

- Primary endpoint: mean change from baseline to Month 18 in time (seconds) to climb 4 standard stairs (4SC), assessed by evaluators blinded to safety data, in the Target-Population ITT analysis set

- Key secondary endpoints (7, subject to Hochberg-adjusted formal testing at Month 18 in the Target Population): time to rise from floor, 6MWT distance, total NSAA score, cumulative loss of function on the NSAA, knee-extension and elbow-flexion muscle strength (hand-held myometry), and VL MFF by MRS in the MR Cohort

- Sample size: originally powered for N=192 (90% power, 1-sided alpha 2.5%, assumed SD=6 seconds, minimum detectable difference 3 seconds) based on published ataluren/drisapersen DMD trial data plus internal Italfarmaco data; a single planned interim analysis (IDMC review at the point the first 50 Target-Population subjects reached Month 12) assessed futility on VL MFF only (not the primary endpoint, and without unblinding it); futility was not met (January 2020), triggering a pre-specified blinded sample-size re-estimation that revised the assumed 4SC SD down to ~3 seconds, reducing the required Target-Population sample size to N=102 (subsequently N=110 with an 8% dropout allowance)

- Primary statistical method: ANCOVA on (log-transformed) 4SC change from baseline to Month 18, covariates for baseline value and re-derived age at first dose, factors for treatment and concomitant-steroid stratum, reported as a GLS mean ratio (givinostat/placebo) with 2-sided CI and p-value; back-transformed/untransformed results also reported

- Multiplicity: primary endpoint tested at 1-sided alpha=0.025 (2-sided 0.05); the 7 key secondary endpoints subject to the Hochberg step-up procedure at the final analysis, ordering 1-sided p-values from largest to smallest and comparing sequentially against 0.025, 0.025/2, 0.025/3, etc.; all other analyses (off-target population, subgroups, non-Month-18 timepoints) explicitly designated supportive/nominal only

- Missing data: continuous efficacy variables classified as "Class 1" (missing for reasons other than inability to perform the test — mean-imputed within treatment group/steroid stratum) or "Class 2" (missing due to non-ambulatory status/physical inability — imputed as zero, or twice the maximum non-missing value, depending on endpoint directionality); a pre-specified tipping-point multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis (10 imputed datasets, Rubin's-rules combination, incremental shift applied only to the givinostat arm) was triggered because the primary result was significant

- Results: Applicant's primary analysis showed 4SC change from baseline to Month 18 of 1.25 seconds (givinostat) vs. 3.03 seconds (placebo), treatment difference -1.78 seconds, p=0.037 (untransformed) / GLS mean ratio 0.86, p=0.035 (log-transformed, as reported in FDA's Integrated Review executive summary); key secondary NSAA total score showed a nominally significant difference (LS mean difference 1.91, p=0.021) but none of the 7 key secondary endpoints reached formal significance after the pre-specified Hochberg adjustment; VL MFF (used post hoc as confirmatory pharmacodynamic evidence rather than as a formally tested key secondary) showed a smaller increase (less fat infiltration) with givinostat (LS mean difference -2.92%, nominal p=0.0354)

- FDA statistical reviewers' independent re-analysis raised substantive concerns about the primary result's robustness: the sponsor's single-value imputation (12 Class-1 + 1 Class-2 imputations at Month 18) produced imputed values with lower variance than observed data (a pattern the reviewers said could inflate Type I error), and imputed means slightly more favorable to givinostat than corresponding observed-data means; reviewer sensitivity analyses using MMRM (p=0.083) and rank-based ANCOVA (p=0.147) did not reach significance, and the sponsor's own pre-specified tipping-point analysis, performed by the reviewers per its stated method, was not significant even at zero shift (p=0.064-0.117 depending on approach) — a result the reviewers stated "illustrates the inadequacy of the Applicant's primary missing data handling method"

### 49. Mavorixafor (Xolremdi) — NDA 218709

**Sponsor:** X4 Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Patients 12 years of age and older with WHIM syndrome (warts, hypogammaglobulinemia, infections, and myelokathexis), to increase the number of circulating mature neutrophils and lymphocytes — a pharmacodynamic-endpoint-based indication, not a labeled infection/wart clinical-benefit claim (see Trial design & endpoints)

**Approval date:** April 26, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** Study X4P-001-103 ("4WHIM"), NCT03995108

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group (not crossover), multicenter, international phase 3 trial in an ultra-rare disease population; 1:1 randomization stratified by prior immunoglobulin (Ig) replacement use; 52-week Randomized Placebo-Controlled Period followed by an open-label extension, with a prespecified "Early Release" pathway (blinded independent Adjudication Committee-determined) allowing subjects with recurrent/significant infections to cross over early into open-label treatment — also fits *Small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population*

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint time above threshold-absolute neutrophil count (TATANC, hours ≥500 cells/µL over a 24-hour dense-sampling period), assessed quarterly over 12 months — a pharmacodynamic/exposure-response surrogate endpoint, not a validated clinical-benefit surrogate per FDA; four key secondary endpoints in a prespecified hierarchy: time above threshold-absolute lymphocyte count (TATALC, ≥1000 cells/µL), a composite clinical efficacy endpoint (total infection score + total wart change score, ranked equally via O'Brien's rank-sum method), total wart change score (central-reader CGI-C), and total infection score (adjudicated, severity-weighted, annualized)

- *Primary analysis:* MMRM (mixed-effects model for repeated measures; SAS PROC MIXED, REML, unstructured covariance, Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom) on TATANC/TATALC, with treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit, Ig-use stratum, and baseline TAT as covariates; composite clinical efficacy endpoint analyzed via ANCOVA on the O'Brien rank sum of its two components; total infection score via ANCOVA; total wart change score via MMRM

- *Multiplicity:* single primary endpoint plus fixed hierarchical (fixed-sequence gatekeeping) testing of the four key secondary endpoints in prespecified order (TATALC → composite clinical efficacy → total wart change score → total infection score); primary and first key secondary reached significance, but the second key secondary (composite clinical efficacy, the highest-ranked *direct*-clinical-benefit endpoint) failed under the sponsor's ANCOVA rank-sum method, formally halting the hierarchy — the two lowest-ranked endpoints were reported only descriptively/nominally

- *Missing data/bias:* no imputation for TATANC/TATALC (missing-at-random assumption under MMRM; within-visit dense-sampling gaps handled by linear interpolation between adjacent ANC/ALC time points); multiple imputation (SAS PROC MI) for missing Week-52 total wart change scores; FDA-requested post hoc sensitivity analyses to address (a) a documented dosing-crossover protocol deviation at Week 52 (3 placebo subjects mistakenly dosed with open-label mavorixafor before blood draw; 1 mavorixafor subject who missed dosing) and (b) a single extreme-outlier subject inflating the mean-based ANCOVA for total infection score (addressed via Wilcoxon rank-sum, Van Elteren, and rank-based ANCOVA as outlier-robust alternatives)

- *Regulatory:* orphan drug designation (Oct 10, 2018), Breakthrough Therapy Designation (Nov 8, 2019), Fast Track (Oct 1, 2020), and Rare Pediatric Disease Designation (Dec 4, 2020, RPD# 2020-472) preceded a first-cycle approval with priority review and a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher request; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held ("the application did not raise efficacy, safety or public health questions requiring advice from external experts"); post hoc win-ratio reanalysis (Pocock et al. 2012 methodology, prioritizing infection over warts) of the failed composite clinical efficacy endpoint, proposed by FDA during trial design (Type B meeting, April 9, 2020) but not adopted by the sponsor as the primary method — used only as supportive/sensitivity evidence, not a formal endpoint — "Post hoc win-ratio reanalysis of a prespecified composite endpoint that failed under its sponsor-chosen equal-weighting method, used as FDA sensitivity evidence rather than a re-designated primary analysis" (distinct from the taxonomy's existing prospectively-specified Finkelstein-Schoenfeld hierarchical composite test)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study X4P-001-103 (4WHIM) was a phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter, international trial in patients ≥12 years old with a genotype-confirmed CXCR4 mutation consistent with WHIM phenotype and a confirmed screening ANC ≤400 cells/µL; 31 participants were randomized 1:1 (17 placebo, 14 mavorixafor; dosed 400 mg/day if >50 kg or 200 mg/day if ≤50 kg), stratified by prior Ig-replacement use within 5 months of screening

- Sample size was based on interim Phase 2 data (Study X4P-001-MKKA): assuming mean TATANC of 11.4h (mavorixafor) vs. 1.4h (placebo) and a pooled SD of 4.7, 18 participants (9/arm) gave >90% power via a 2-sample t-test (2-sided alpha=0.05); 31 were actually enrolled to allow for dropout/flexibility

- Primary endpoint: TATANC (hours ≥500 cells/µL over a 24-hour period), measured via dense pre/post-dose ANC sampling (0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24h) at Baseline, Weeks 13, 26, 39, and 52, with time-above-threshold computed by linear interpolation between adjacent time points where the ANC curve crosses 500 cells/µL

- Result (ITT population, MMRM, FDA-confirmed): overall LS-mean TATANC 15.04h (95% CI 11.16-18.93) for mavorixafor vs. 2.75h (95% CI 0.00-5.89) for placebo; LS-mean difference 12.30h (95% CI 7.16-17.43), two-sided p<0.0001 — the study met its primary endpoint

- First key secondary (TATALC ≥1000 cells/µL): also significant — LS-mean 15.80h (mavorixafor) vs. 4.55h (placebo), difference 11.25h (95% CI 7.53-14.96), p<0.0001

- Second key secondary (composite clinical efficacy endpoint, O'Brien rank-sum ANCOVA of total infection score + total wart change score): did NOT reach statistical significance under the sponsor's prespecified primary method — result redacted [(b)(4)] in the public Integrated Review — formally halting the prespecified testing hierarchy; the two remaining key secondaries (total wart change score, nominal p=0.94; total infection score, nominal p=0.21) were reported only descriptively per protocol

- FDA's Key Efficacy Review Issue (§6.3.1, "Adequacy of Study X4P-001-103 to Establish Clinical Benefit"): TATANC/TATALC are pharmacodynamic endpoints, not validated/direct surrogates of clinical benefit in WHIM syndrome, and the highest-ranked endpoint measuring direct clinical benefit (the composite infection/wart endpoint) failed under the sponsor's analysis — FDA's statistical review team noted the sponsor's equal-weighting rank-sum method for the composite was "less powerful than other methods such as the win ratio test" because it did not allow the drug's differential effect on infection vs. warts to be prioritized

- FDA-requested win-ratio reanalysis (unstratified, pairwise, infection-score-prioritized-then-wart-score): win ratio 2.76 (95% CI 1.60-4.76), nominal p=0.00025 (unstratified); win ratio 2.31 (95% CI 1.34-3.96), nominal p=0.0025 (stratified by baseline Ig use) — but FDA explicitly flagged this as not sponsor-adopted, based on asymptotic (small-sample-fragile) win-ratio CI theory, and driven entirely by the infection component, not warts

- Outlier-adjusted total infection score sensitivity analyses (addressing one mavorixafor subject with an infection score of ~35 due to two post-discontinuation infections against an IQR of 2-7 for the rest of the arm): Wilcoxon rank-sum nominal p=0.027, Van Elteren (stratified) nominal p=0.063, rank-based ANCOVA nominal p=0.049 — all directionally supportive of benefit despite the primary ANCOVA's nonsignificant p=0.21

- Exploratory annualized infection rate: 60% reduction (4.2 placebo vs. 1.7 mavorixafor per year, nominal p=0.007); no convincing effect on warts was found (LS-mean difference in total wart change score 0.07, 95% CI -1.69 to 1.82)

- Given the failed composite clinical-benefit endpoint, FDA's approved indication rests on the PD endpoints (TATANC/TATALC — "to increase the number of circulating mature neutrophils and lymphocytes") rather than a claim of reduced infections/warts, consistent with the label's Indications and Usage statement

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held; per the Integrated Review, "the application was not referred to an Advisory Committee meeting because the application did not raise efficacy, safety or public health questions requiring advice from external experts."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.1.3, p.32]* — "The primary endpoint was time above threshold-absolute neutrophil count (TATANC; in hours) of ≥500 cells/μL over a 24-hour period, assessed 4 times throughout the study (every 3 months for 12 months)."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.1.3, p.35]* — "The primary endpoint analysis compared the difference between mavorixafor and placebo with respect to the mean time above ANC threshold using mixed-effects model for repeated measures (MMRM) analysis. The model used TATANC as a dependent variable; treatment, visit (Weeks 13, 26, 39 and 52), treatment*visit, Ig use (randomization strata), and baseline TAT as covariates; and participant as the repeated random effect."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.1.3, p.38]* — "Multiplicity was controlled by specification of a single primary endpoint and use of a hierarchical approach to the analysis of the key secondary endpoints. If the primary endpoint TATANC achieved a statistically significant result, each key secondary endpoint was hierarchically tested in the order below: TATALC; Composite Clinical Efficacy Endpoint...; Total wart change score; Total infection score. If the analysis for a specific endpoint was not statistically significant, formal statistical testing did not continue on subsequent endpoints."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.1.4, p.42]* — "The study met its primary efficacy endpoint of statistically significant superiority of mavorixafor over placebo in the TATANC... The overall LS mean based on the MMRM model for TATANC was 15.04 (95% CI: 11.16, 18.93) for the mavorixafor group and 2.75 (95% CI: 0.00, 5.89) for the placebo group, with a LS mean difference of 12.30 (95% CI: 7.16, 17.43), 2-sided p-value<0.0001."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §6.3.1, p.51]* — "Study 103 failed to demonstrate superiority of mavorixafor over placebo on the highest ranked secondary clinical benefit endpoint using the Applicant's primary analysis method. While Study 103 demonstrated statistically significant superiority of mavorixafor over placebo for the primary (TATANC) and first key secondary (TATALC) endpoints, both of these endpoints are PD endpoints and not considered direct or validated surrogate measures of clinical benefit in WHIM syndrome."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §6.3.1, p.53]* — "During the design of the trial, the Agency instead recommended the win-ratio method for the primary analysis for the composite clinical efficacy endpoint (Pocock et al. 2012)... because this method can prioritize each of the components of the composite endpoint based on its individual contribution... The unstratified win-ratio analysis... win-ratio 2.76 (95% CI: 1.60, 4.76)... nominal p-value 0.00025."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §6.3.1, p.54]* — "Although the win-ratio analysis for the composite efficacy endpoint shows benefit on the mavorixafor arm compared to the placebo arm, further evidence is needed to support the benefit due to the following limitations: The win-ratio analysis was not adopted by the Applicant as the primary analysis method. The method for calculating the CI and p-value for the win-ratio (Pocock et al. 2012) was derived based on asymptotic theory. The asymptotic estimate for small sample cases like Study X4P-001-103 may not be robust."

### 50. Arimoclomol (Miplyffa) — NDA 214927

**Sponsor:** Zevra Denmark A/S (the application was originally submitted by Orphazyme A/S in 2020; ownership of NDA 214927 and IND 124547 was transferred to KemPharm Denmark A/S on June 10, 2022, and KemPharm's corporate name was changed to Zevra Denmark A/S on April 13, 2023; the September 2024 NDA approval letter is addressed to "Zevra Denmark A/S c/o Zevra Therapeutics, Inc.")

**Indication approved:** Use in combination with miglustat for the treatment of neurological manifestations of Niemann-Pick disease type C (NPC) in adults and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older — an ultra-rare, autosomal-recessive lysosomal storage/cholesterol-trafficking disorder with no other FDA-approved therapy at the time of approval

**Approval date:** September 20, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** CT-ORZY-NPC-002 ("Study NPC-002"), a 12-month randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, NCT02612129

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population, 2:1 randomization stratified by background-miglustat-use status, post-Complete-Response-Letter primary-endpoint redefinition on the same pivotal trial's dataset

- *Endpoints:* composite multi-domain clinician/caregiver-rated clinical severity scale, change-from-baseline (the 5-domain and rescored 4-domain NPC Clinical Severity Scale, "5DNPCCSS"/"R4DNPCCSS"), Clinical Global Impression of Improvement (CGI-I) responder analysis (originally proposed by FDA as a co-primary/anchor endpoint, later excluded from the primary analysis for missing baseline data)

- *Primary analysis:* mixed model for repeated measurements (MMRM, unstructured covariance, baseline covariate, treatment-by-visit interaction), ANCOVA (label's miglustat-subgroup analysis), ICH E9(R1) estimand framework — hypothetical vs. while-on-treatment vs. treatment-policy estimands compared head-to-head by FDA

- *Missing data/bias:* no imputation for the primary/continuous key-secondary endpoints (non-responder imputation only for binary responder endpoints), multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis, tipping-point analysis, nonparametric sensitivity analysis, missing-at-random (MAR) assumption disputed between sponsor and FDA reviewer

- *Regulatory:* Complete Response Letter (CRL) followed by resubmission and approval, FDA Advisory Committee meeting held (11-5 vote), cross-disciplinary statistical/clinical dissent documented within a single review (Patient-Focused Statistical Support team, Division of Clinical Outcome Assessment reviewer, and primary clinical reviewer recommended non-approval while the Cross-Discipline Team Lead, Division Director, and statistical review team recommended approval, yet the signatory authority issued a CRL)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Phase 2/3, multinational, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, 12-month trial (Study NPC-002) in patients 2-19 years of age with a molecularly confirmed NPC1 or NPC2 diagnosis and at least one neurological symptom at baseline; patients under 12 years of age first received a single open-label PK dose before randomization into the double-blind phase

- Randomization was stratified by miglustat-use status at baseline (patients could be on a stable miglustat dose for ≥6 months, off miglustat for ≥3 months, or miglustat-naive); 50 patients were randomized (34 arimoclomol, 16 placebo) per ClinicalTrials.gov's posted results, and 76-81% of randomized patients were taking background miglustat

- Original (2020 NDA) prespecified primary endpoint: change from baseline to Month 12 in the 5-domain NPC Clinical Severity Scale (5DNPCCSS: ambulation, fine motor skills, swallow, cognition, speech; each domain scored 0-5, total range 0-25, higher = more severe), analyzed via MMRM (fixed effects for treatment, miglustat level, visit, and treatment-by-visit interaction, plus a baseline-score covariate; unstructured covariance) under a "hypothetical" ICH E9(R1) estimand assuming full adherence to blinded treatment through Month 12

- FDA's January 2018 Type B meeting recommended CGI-I (Clinical Global Impression of Improvement) responder status at Month 12 as a co-primary/anchor endpoint for the 5DNPCCSS; this was later dropped from the primary/co-primary analysis because baseline CGI-S/CGI-I data were missing for 42 of 50 patients, and the eventual CGI-I responder analysis (58.8% arimoclomol vs. 56.3% placebo, p=1.00 by chi-squared test) showed no treatment difference

- No formal statistical power calculation was performed for the primary endpoint; the posted SAP instead derives its sample-size assumptions from the mean rate of 5DNPCCSS progression and its standard deviation observed in a separate natural-history study, with supplementary post hoc power tables for the CGI-I anchor endpoint at several assumed relative-risk and significance-level scenarios

- Secondary/exploratory endpoints included: responder analyses of the 5DNPCCSS (stable-or-improved), time-to-worsening (minimal clinically important difference [MCID] of 2 points), percentage of patients worsening, the 17-domain NPCCSS excluding hearing/auditory-brainstem-response domains, individual NPCCSS domain scores, the NPC Clinical Database ("modified Stampfer") score, EQ-5D-Y quality of life, the Scale for Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (SARA), and the 9-Hole Peg Test

- Using the sponsor's prespecified MMRM/hypothetical-estimand analysis, the full-population 5DNPCCSS treatment difference was -1.4 (95% CI: -2.76, -0.03; p=0.0456) — nominally significant at the conventional two-sided 0.05 level

- FDA's June 17, 2021 Complete Response Letter (original NDA) cited three deficiencies: (1) interpretability of the 5DNPCCSS primary endpoint, particularly its swallow and cognition domains; (2) lack of conventional statistical significance (p<0.05) in FDA's own post hoc reanalysis of the 5DNPCCSS mean change using an alternative (while-on-treatment) estimand, which produced a treatment difference of -1.2 (95% CI: -2.7, 0.3; p=0.12); and (3) weak/contradictory nonclinical and pharmacodynamic-biomarker confirmatory evidence

- In the December 2023 Class 2 resubmission, the Applicant proposed a revised, post hoc primary endpoint — the rescored 4-domain NPC Clinical Severity Scale (R4DNPCCSS) — removing the cognition domain (deemed "not fit-for-purpose" by both the Applicant and Agency) and rescoring the swallow domain; FDA's statistical review team required the analysis be run under two Agency-preferred estimands (a "while-on-treatment" strategy for intercurrent events, and a "treatment-policy" strategy using multiple imputation informed by observed placebo-arm data) rather than the sponsor's original hypothetical estimand

- Full-population R4DNPCCSS results (FDA's Table 1, Statistical Review): while-on-treatment estimand, treatment difference -1.4 (95% CI: -2.8, -0.0; p=0.0451); treatment-policy estimand, -1.4 (95% CI: -2.9, 0.1; p=0.0709, not conventionally significant)

- The R4DNPCCSS treatment effect was substantially larger and more consistent in the subgroup of patients also receiving background miglustat: while-on-treatment estimand, -2.2 (95% CI: -3.7, -0.8; p=0.0028); treatment-policy estimand, -2.2 (95% CI: -3.8, -0.6; p=0.0077) — versus a result numerically favoring placebo in the small (n=11), imbalanced non-miglustat subgroup — and this miglustat-combination subgroup analysis (using a simpler ANCOVA model adjusted for baseline score) is the analysis reported in the approved label's Table 3, consistent with the approved indication being restricted to arimoclomol used in combination with miglustat

- FDA ultimately concluded that the confirmatory evidence originally offered (nonclinical/PD-biomarker data alone) was inadequate, but that the totality of evidence — Study NPC-002, supportive data from a related trial (NPC-001) and NPC-002's open-label extension, and clinical-pharmacology data — was adequate confirmatory evidence specifically for arimoclomol used in combination with miglustat

**Other resources**

- No Vivli, YODA Project, or Project Data Sphere participation was found for Orphazyme A/S or Zevra Therapeutics/Zevra Denmark A/S; trial-specific IPD availability was not confirmed and is stated here only as unconfirmed, not absent

- FDA Advisory Committee: the Genetic Metabolic Diseases Advisory Committee met on August 2, 2024, and voted 11 (Yes) to 5 (No) that the results of Study NPC-002, together with other clinical and nonclinical data, support a conclusion that arimoclomol is effective for NPC; dissenting members cited unresolved evidentiary problems with both the clinical and nonclinical data and recommended an additional study with a prospective (not post hoc) statistical analysis plan

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

A genuine sponsor Statistical Analysis Plan (Orion Clinical, for Orphazyme A/S, Final Version, dated 10-Sep-2018) is posted on ClinicalTrials.gov, but its PDF text layer uses a non-standard, consistently-offset character encoding — a fixed +29 (mod-94, over the printable ASCII range) substitution cipher, confirmed by decoding and cross-checking against unambiguous words (e.g., "Orphazyme," "Statistical Analysis Plan") — and, separately, all digit characters and dot-leader/whitespace glyphs in the same PDF are rendered as low (non-printable) control-code bytes that this substitution does not recover; the passages quoted below from the SAP are therefore reconstructed letter-for-letter from the cipher (word spacing is preserved correctly by the PDF's own layout, unlike some other sponsors' redaction pipelines seen elsewhere in this census) but contain no numeric content, which is why every quantitative figure in this entry is instead drawn from the FDA Integrated Review or ClinicalTrials.gov's posted results.

*[reconstructed from source, SAP §"Primary Efficacy Analysis" (Statistical Methods/Statistical Output section), posted SAP_001.pdf]* — "A general linear mixed model for repeated measurements will be used to analyse the primary endpoint defined as the change from baseline to months in the domain NPCCSS...The model will be fitted with treatment, miglustat level and visit as fixed effects along with a treatment by visit interaction term. The estimated treatment effect will be taken from the treatment by visit interaction term at months...sij and eijk are assumed to be independent from each other and follow a multivariate normal distribution. The covariance matrix for e is chosen to be the unstructured variance covariance matrix; it assumes pairwise correlations are not constrained by the data. Missing data will not be imputed for the primary endpoint analysis. If a baseline value is missing, no change from baseline will be calculated."

*[reconstructed from source, SAP §"Missing Data"]* — "There will be no imputation of missing data for the primary endpoint and the continuous key secondary endpoint analyses in this study. If a baseline value is missing, no change from baseline will be calculated. For the responder key secondary endpoints, a patient who discontinues before months will be considered a non-responder. Sensitivity analyses will be performed using a multiple imputation approach, a tipping analysis approach, and a nonparametric analysis."

*[reconstructed from source, SAP §"Sample Size Considerations"]* — "No formal statistical calculation has been used to determine sample size. A similar study (ASIS) with patients reported a mean rate of progression as points per year and the standard deviation (SD) was...For a submission to the FDA it has been requested that Clinical Global Impression Improvement (CGI-I) be included as a coprimary endpoint but a requirement that the significance level for this endpoint being P may not be necessary, given that the study was not designed or powered for this endpoint. Below are example power calculations for and significance levels for CGI-I based on randomised patients."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, Executive Summary of the original 2021 NDA review, p.~118]* — "There were intra- and inter-disciplinary differences of opinion regarding the adequacy of the efficacy data to support approval. The Patient Focused Statistical Support (PFSS) team, primary reviewer for the Division of Clinical Outcome Assessment (DCOA), and primary clinical reviewer do not recommend approval, primarily due to validity concerns with the 5DNPCCSS...The Cross Discipline Team Lead and Clinical Division Director conclude that the strengths of the overall efficacy evidence overcome the limitations of the data...This conclusion is supported by the statistical team...The Cross Discipline Team Lead, Clinical Division Director and statistical team recommend approval. Based on the efficacy assessment and after considering the various viewpoints on approvability, the signatory authority is proceeding with a Complete Response action."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, "History of Drug Development," quoting the Meeting Minutes for the Type B Meeting of January 17, 2018, p.~557]* — "The Agency agreed that a Mixed Model Repeated Measures (MMRM) analysis is acceptable for the NPCSS, provided that the sponsor demonstrates that the Missing At Random (MAR) assumption is met."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, Statistical Review of the resubmission, Table 1 discussion, p.~551]* — "During the review of the original submission, the Agency did not agree with the hypothetical estimand primarily due to inadequate assumption of hypothetical scores after death and exclusion of the observed data after early escape which indicated disease worsening in the arimoclomol arm...Despite both while-on-treatment and treatment-policy estimands being post-hoc, we consider these two estimands more relevant than the Applicant's hypothetical estimand."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, Advisory Committee Summary, p.~95]* — "VOTE: Do the results of trial NPC-002 in concert with the other data (clinical and nonclinical in particular) support a conclusion that arimoclomol is effective in the treatment of patients with NPC?...Vote Result: Yes: 11 No: 5 Abstain: 0...The Committee members who voted 'No' noted, both the clinical and nonclinical data had problems and did not meet evidentiary standards for approval."

### 51. Levacetylleucine (Aqneursa) — NDA 219132

**Sponsor:** IntraBio Ltd. (applicant of record at approval; the product was acquired by Zevra Pharmaceuticals shortly after approval and is now marketed under the Zevra corporate umbrella, per assignment brief — the FDA review and label of record both name IntraBio Ltd./IntraBio Inc. as applicant/distributor)

**Indication approved:** To improve neurological manifestations of Niemann-Pick disease type C (NPC) in adults and pediatric patients weighing ≥15 kg

**Approval date:** September 24, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** IB1001-301, NCT05163288 (supportive: IB1001-201, NCT03759639)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, two-period crossover trial (no washout period between periods); small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (N=60)

- *Endpoints:* continuous neurological rating-scale change-from-baseline endpoint (fSARA — a modified/rescored Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia, restricted by FDA to 4 of the 8 original SARA domains and rescored to equalize response categories across domains)

- *Primary analysis:* mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) (a "plain" MMRM adjusting for period/sequence/treatment/baseline/baseline-by-period interaction, distinct from the taxonomy's existing MMRM-with-sandwich-variance row); Mainland-Gart test (Fisher's exact variant, a McNemar-type test for dichotomous crossover data) used for a post hoc responder analysis

- *Missing data/bias:* last observation carried forward (LOCF) imputed on a per-period basis; carryover/sequence effect formally tested and found nonsignificant (p=0.60)

- *Regulatory:* regular approval based on a single adequate and well-controlled trial plus confirmatory evidence, per FDA's September 2023 draft guidance on Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness With One Adequate and Well-Controlled Clinical Investigation and Confirmatory Evidence; Breakthrough Therapy, Orphan Drug, and Rare Pediatric Disease designations; no Advisory Committee meeting held; no REMS

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Multinational, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, two-period crossover Phase 3 trial (IB1001-301) at 11 sites across 7 non-US countries; 60 subjects aged ≥4 years with confirmed NPC (all 60 ultimately had genetically confirmed diagnoses) were randomized 1:1 to Sequence 1 (levacetylleucine 12 weeks, then placebo 12 weeks) or Sequence 2 (placebo then levacetylleucine), with no washout period between periods; eligibility required a baseline SARA score of 7-34 and specific gait/9HPT-D performance thresholds, weight ≥15 kg

- Applicant's primary endpoint was the modified SARA (mSARA, 6 of 8 domains) total score at end of treatment; FDA had previously (advice letters Dec 2021 and Mar 2022) recommended a narrower, differently-scored 4-domain "functional SARA" (fSARA: gait, stance, sitting, speech, each rescored to 5 equal-interval levels, range 0-16) as more clearly interpretable for daily functioning, and used the fSARA as primary evidence of efficacy in its review rather than the Applicant's mSARA

- Secondary/key secondary: original SARA total score (key secondary for the U.S. application); responder analysis (≥1-point improvement in any of the 4 fSARA domains)

- SAP finalized September 29, 2022, before database lock/unblinding (June 14, 2023); primary analysis population was the ITT population (all randomized subjects dosed at least once, N=60); primary analysis used MMRM (unstructured covariance) adjusting for treatment, period, sequence, baseline mSARA/fSARA value at Visit 2, and baseline-by-period interaction; intercurrent events (AE-driven discontinuation, rescue/prohibited medication use) were handled with a treatment-policy strategy — all collected data retained regardless of intercurrent events; missing data (2 of 60 subjects missing Visit 4 or 6, one of whom died 88 days after a non-drug-related aspiration event following unplanned surgery) were imputed via per-period LOCF

- Reported primary result (fSARA, FDA's rescored primary evidence): LS mean difference levacetylleucine vs. placebo of -0.45 (95% CI: -0.70, -0.19), p=0.0009; a between-subject (Period-1-only) analysis, though underpowered, showed a consistent direction of effect (-0.35, 95% CI: -0.90, 0.19, p=0.202); sequence/carryover effect was tested and non-significant (p=0.6027); sensitivity analyses excluding the ineligible/deceased subject, varying the LOCF assumption, and a completers-only analysis (n=58, difference -0.48, 95% CI: -0.73, -0.22, p<0.001) all supported the primary conclusion; a post hoc responder analysis (≥1-point improvement in any fSARA domain) found 33/58 completers (56.8%) were treatment responders, with a Mainland-Gart (Fisher's exact) test of discordant-period responses yielding p=0.011 favoring levacetylleucine

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/219132s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Integrated Review (combined clinical/statistical/summary review, per FDA's Integrated Review Template v4.0) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/219132Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2310151), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38294974/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Trial%20of%20N-Acetyl-l-Leucine%20in%20Niemann-Pick%20Disease%20Type%20C)

**Other resources**

- IntraBio/Zevra IPD/dataset access via Vivli.org or YODA Project not individually confirmed here; no trial-specific access program identified.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held; the review states the application "did not raise challenging efficacy" issues warranting one.

- A 2-year open-label extension of IB1001-301 was ongoing at the time of NDA submission (not included in the efficacy database); FDA separately reviewed 12-month interim extension data (5DNPCCSS endpoint, different from the parent-study endpoint) as supportive but not determinative of long-term durability, given the absence of a concurrent control in the extension.
