### 52. Vanzacaftor/tezacaftor/deutivacaftor (Alyftrek) — NDA 218730

**Sponsor:** Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated

**Indication approved:** Treatment of cystic fibrosis (CF) in patients aged ≥6 years who have at least one F508del mutation or another responsive mutation in the CFTR gene

**Approval date:** December 20, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** SKYLINE Trials VX20-121-102 (Trial 102), NCT05033080, and VX20-121-103 (Trial 103), NCT05076149 (supportive pediatric PK/safety: RIDGELINE Trial VX21-121-105)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two co-pivotal randomized, double-blind, active-controlled (elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor [ELX/TEZ/IVA]), parallel-group noninferiority trials, each with a 4-week active run-in period to establish an on-treatment baseline; randomization stratified by age, run-in ppFEV1, run-in sweat chloride, and prior CFTR-modulator use

- *Endpoints:* absolute change from baseline in percent-predicted FEV1 (ppFEV1) through Week 24 (primary, noninferiority); sweat chloride (SwCl) absolute change and categorical thresholds (<60 and <30 mmol/L, pooled across the two trials) as key secondary pharmacodynamic-marker endpoints; pulmonary exacerbations and CFQ-R respiratory domain score as other (non-multiplicity-controlled) secondary endpoints

- *Primary analysis:* mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) adjusted for treatment, visit, age category, treatment-by-visit interaction, with baseline ppFEV1 and baseline SwCl as covariates; noninferiority margin of -3.0% derived via the FDA 2016 non-inferiority guidance's "preserve ≥50% of the active-control effect" principle (Trial 102) and, novelly, via a Bucher network indirect-comparison approach (Bucher et al. 1997) to estimate the same M1/M2 margin in a population (F/F and other genotypes) with no historical placebo-controlled data (Trial 103) (Bucher's indirect-comparison method used specifically to derive a noninferiority margin, distinct from its more common use for comparative-effectiveness estimation)

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence testing limited to the primary (ppFEV1) plus SwCl-based key secondary endpoints only; FDA explicitly noted it had advised the sponsor to add a non-SwCl clinically meaningful key secondary (e.g., pulmonary exacerbations, CFQ-R) to the controlled hierarchy, which the sponsor did not do — those endpoints remained uncontrolled "other" secondaries

- *Missing data/bias:* intercurrent events (early discontinuation, off-protocol CFTR-modulator use >3 days) handled via treatment-policy strategy; missing-at-random assumption assessed via tipping-point analysis; a post hoc, FDA/Division-recommended Week-24 landmark MMRM analysis was run alongside the sponsor's pre-specified "through-Week-24" (Weeks 16+24 average) analysis to better capture durability

- *Regulatory:* approved via priority review voucher redemption; no Advisory Committee meeting held ("no scientific, technical, or policy issues" warranting one); no REMS

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Trial 102 (N=405 randomized, 398 in the Full Analysis Set) enrolled subjects ≥12 years old heterozygous for F508del and a minimal-function variant; Trial 103 (N=574 randomized, 573 FAS) enrolled subjects homozygous for F508del or heterozygous for F508del plus a gating/residual-function variant or another responsive non-F508del variant; both trials used a 4-week ELX/TEZ/IVA run-in, then 1:1 randomization to vanzacaftor 20 mg/tezacaftor 100 mg/deutivacaftor 250 mg QD vs. continued ELX/TEZ/IVA for 52 weeks, with the same design, endpoints, and statistical analysis plan (Trial 103 differed only in powering at 95% vs. 90% for Trial 102)

- Placebo control was judged unethical/infeasible given ELX/TEZ/IVA's established efficacy and >80% U.S. CF-population uptake, so both trials used ELX/TEZ/IVA as an active comparator in a noninferiority design

- Primary result, Trial 102: LS mean difference in ppFEV1 change from baseline through Week 24 was 0.2% (95% CI: -0.7%, 1.1%) for vanzacaftor/tezacaftor/deutivacaftor vs. ELX/TEZ/IVA (1-sided NI p<0.00001; lower bound of 95% CI well above the -3.0% margin); an FDA/Division-requested post hoc Week-24 landmark MMRM gave a consistent LS mean difference of 0.3% (95% CI: -1.3%, 0.8%; note the reviewed text's CI ordering)

- Key secondary result, Trial 102: SwCl LS mean difference of -8.4 mmol/L (95% CI: -10.5, -6.3; p<0.0001) favoring the new combination, though FDA's review explicitly cautions that SwCl is a pharmacodynamic marker, not a validated predictor of clinical response, so the clinical meaning of an ~8 mmol/L further reduction (beyond an already-effective comparator) is unclear

- Other secondary endpoints (uncontrolled for multiplicity) were numerically similar between arms: pulmonary exacerbation rate difference through Week 52 of -0.10 (95% CI: -0.24, 0.04); CFQ-R respiratory domain change difference of 2.3 points (95% CI: -0.6, 5.2)

- Subgroup analyses were generally consistent with the overall population, except an adolescent (<18 years) subgroup in Trial 102 whose 95% CI (-3.9%, 1.3%) crossed the noninferiority margin — FDA attributed this to small sample size/wide CI rather than a true qualitative interaction

[DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S2213-2600(24)00411-9>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39756424/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Vanzacaftor-tezacaftor-deutivacaftor%20versus%20elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor%20in%20individuals%20with%20cystic%20fibrosis%20aged%2012%20years%20and%20older)

**Other resources**

- Vertex's general participation in Vivli.org/YODA-style IPD-sharing programs was not individually confirmed for this trial pair.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held.

- Trial VX21-121-105 (RIDGELINE), a single-arm Phase 3 PK/safety/exploratory-efficacy trial in children 6-11 years old, supported the pediatric dosing extension within the same NDA; its results were published separately (Lancet Respir Med 2025;13(3), PMID 39756425).

### 53. Atrasentan (Vanrafia) — NDA 219208

**Sponsor:** Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation (compound originated at Abbott Laboratories/AbbVie as ABT-627/CHK-01, then licensed to Chinook Therapeutics, which Novartis acquired in 2023)

**Indication approved:** To reduce proteinuria in adults with primary IgA nephropathy (IgAN) at risk of rapid disease progression, generally a UPCR ≥1.5 g/g — granted under accelerated approval

**Approval date:** April 2, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** ALIGN Trial (Study CHK01-01), NCT04573478

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* ongoing, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial with background RASi therapy in all subjects; two enrollment strata (main non-SGLT2i stratum and an exploratory SGLT2i stratum) with separate randomization schedules; group-sequential design with a single pre-specified unblinded interim analysis at the first 270 randomized subjects' Week-36 visit, used as the basis for accelerated approval while the trial continues to its Week-136 eGFR-slope readout

- *Endpoints:* proteinuria surrogate endpoint — natural-log-transformed ratio-to-baseline in 24-hour urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR) at Week 36 (interim primary, basis for accelerated approval); eGFR slope/change at Week 136 (key secondary, intended for a future traditional-approval/confirmatory readout); composite renal endpoints (≥30%/≥40% sustained eGFR decline, ESRD, transplant, death)

- *Primary analysis:* mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) on log-transformed UPCR ratio-to-baseline, adjusted for baseline log UPCR, baseline eGFR, treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction, and region stratum; Kenward-Roger approximation for denominator degrees of freedom; unstructured covariance matrix with pre-specified fallback to heterogeneous-then-homogeneous autoregressive(1) structures if convergence failed

- *Multiplicity:* Fallback Procedure (Wiens 2005) allocating 2-sided alpha of 0.01 to the primary (UPCR) and 0.04-0.05 to the key secondary (eGFR), with further sequential testing of two eGFR-decline composites and a proteinuria-remission endpoint using alpha retained from the eGFR test

- *Missing data/bias:* data after kidney transplant or ≥30-day chronic dialysis excluded from primary analyses (missing-at-random assumption); sensitivity analyses included an all-data-regardless-of-censoring MMRM and a Copy Reference multiple-imputation method (Markov Chain Monte Carlo imputation of intermittent missing values, plus reference-based monotone-missing imputation under an MNAR assumption borrowing the control arm's post-rescue profile) — a variant of the taxonomy's Jump-to-reference/tipping-point family; notably, the Division disagreed with the sponsor's censoring rules for intercurrent events (steroid/immunosuppressant/SGLT2i rescue) and required an all-data-regardless-of-rescue analysis for its own efficacy review

- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval based on a proteinuria surrogate endpoint in IgA nephropathy (the emerging renal-surrogate accelerated-approval pathway also used for sparsentan/Filspari), following the class precedent of other endothelin-receptor antagonists (bosentan, sparsentan) that required boxed warnings/REMS for hepatotoxicity and embryo-fetal toxicity; no Advisory Committee meeting held ("did not raise significant or controversial issues... concerns that public release of information could impact the integrity of the ongoing trial")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ALIGN enrolled adults with biopsy-proven IgAN, blood pressure ≤150/95, on a maximally tolerated stable RASi dose, total urine protein ≥1 g/day, eGFR ≥30 mL/min/1.73m²; randomized 1:1 to atrasentan 0.75 mg QD or placebo for 132 weeks, stratified by region (Asia vs. other), screening UPCR (≥2 vs. <2 g/g), and SGLT2i status; 404 subjects total were randomized (340 main stratum, 64 SGLT2i stratum) as of the April 2024 data cut, with the interim analysis based on the first 270 main-stratum subjects reaching Week 36

- Key exclusions: BNP >200 pg/mL, platelet count <80,000/µL, hemoglobin <9 g/dL, suspected rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis/IgA vasculitis, prior organ transplant, history of heart failure/fluid overload — reflecting the endothelin-receptor-antagonist class's known fluid-retention/hepatotoxicity risk profile

- Primary result (interim analysis, main-stratum ITT, N=270): geometric mean ratio (GMR) of Week-36 UPCR to baseline was 0.6 with atrasentan vs. 1.0 with placebo; ratio-of-GMRs 0.64 (95% CI: 0.55, 0.74), corresponding to a 36% relative reduction (95% CI: 26%-45% lower) vs. placebo, p<0.0001; results were similar (ratio of GMR 0.63) when all UPCR data were included regardless of rescue-medication use, addressing the Division's disagreement over the sponsor's censoring rules

- eGFR-slope key secondary endpoint (Week 136) was not yet analyzed at the time of this accelerated-approval review — the trial continues to that readout as the confirmatory/traditional-approval endpoint

- A February 2026 Lancet publication (PMID 42242268) reports the trial's final 2.5-year results, published after this NDA's accelerated approval and therefore not part of the FDA statistical review reflected above; it is listed here as a forward-looking confirmatory-evidence reference, not verified against a subsequent FDA supplement review

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2025/219208Orig1s001ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label (original, 2025) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/219208s000lbl.pdf (a corrected label was subsequently posted at https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/219208Orig1s001Correctedlbl.pdf)

- FDA Integrated Review (combined clinical/statistical/summary review) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219208Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04573478 (no protocol/SAP posted)

- Pivotal (interim-analysis) publication: Heerspink HJL, Jardine M, Kohan DE, et al. "Atrasentan in Patients with IgA Nephropathy." *N Engl J Med.* 2025;392(6):544-554. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2409415), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39460694/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Atrasentan%20in%20Patients%20with%20IgA%20Nephropathy)

- Final-results publication (post-approval, not FDA-reviewed as of this entry): "Atrasentan in patients with IgA nephropathy (ALIGN): final 2·5-year results from a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial." *Lancet.* 2026;[in press]. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(26)00960-8>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42242268/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Atrasentan+in+patients+with+IgA+nephropathy+ALIGN%22)

**Other resources**

- Novartis/Chinook IPD/dataset access via Vivli.org not individually confirmed for this trial.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held.

- Atrasentan is the second endothelin-receptor antagonist approved for IgAN proteinuria reduction (after sparsentan/Filspari); the class's REMS requirement for embryo-fetal toxicity has since been removed, and Vanrafia's label carries a Boxed Warning (not a REMS) for that risk, with a Warning and Precaution (not boxed) for hepatotoxicity.

### 54. Sepiapterin (Sephience) — NDA 219666

**Sponsor:** PTC Therapeutics, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of hyperphenylalaninemia (HPA) in pediatric and adult patients with phenylketonuria (PKU)

**Approval date:** July 28, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** APHENITY (PKU-003), NCT05099640 (supportive: PKU-002; long-term extension: PKU-004)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two-part, phase 3, global trial — Part 1 an open-label, single-arm 14-day responsiveness-determination run-in (≥15% blood Phe reduction required to proceed), followed by a 14-day washout, then Part 2 a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-escalating (20→40→60 mg/kg QD) parallel-group trial restricted to Part-1 responders aged ≥2 years; run-in responder-enrichment design (open-label lead-in used to select pharmacodynamic responders before randomization, distinct from a randomized-withdrawal design since no one was exposed to drug during a subsequent placebo phase)

- *Endpoints:* continuous metabolic biomarker endpoint — mean change in blood phenylalanine (Phe) concentration from baseline to Weeks 5-6 (primary); proportions crossing clinically relevant Phe thresholds of <600 µmol/L and <360 µmol/L (key secondaries); blood tyrosine and Phe:Tyr ratio (exploratory)

- *Primary analysis:* mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) adjusted for treatment, baseline Phe, baseline Phe stratum (<600/≥600 µmol/L), visit, and visit-by-treatment interaction, unstructured covariance; primary analysis population (PAP) restricted to the subset of randomized subjects who were ≥30% Part-1 responders (not all randomized responders), a narrower population than the trial's own Full Analysis Set (FAS)

- *Multiplicity:* two-stage gatekeeping — the ≥30%-responder stratum tested first at 2-sided alpha 0.05; only if positive was the broader ≥15%-responder population tested, also at 0.05; secondary Phe-threshold endpoints then tested sequentially within each stratum only if both gates passed

- *Missing data/bias:* MMRM's implicit missing-at-random assumption supplemented by two non-MAR sensitivity methods — control-based imputation (post-discontinuation values in the sepiapterin arm imputed as following the placebo/control-group distribution, a variant of the taxonomy's Jump-to-reference approach) and a formal tipping-point analysis; amount of missing primary-endpoint data was minimal (1 placebo subject missing one time window)

- *Regulatory:* orphan drug designation (March 2021); standard (not accelerated) approval; no Advisory Committee meeting held ("no scientific, technical, or policy issues... that would benefit from an advisory committee discussion")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- PKU-003 enrolled 157 participants of any age with uncontrolled blood Phe ≥360 µmol/L and a documented history of ≥2 Phe measurements ≥600 µmol/L; Part 1 (open-label, 14 days) assessed sepiapterin responsiveness; 114/156 (73.1%) responded ≥15% and 103/156 (66.0%) responded ≥30%; 110 responders (≥15% stratum) were randomized 1:1 to sepiapterin (dose-escalated 20→40→60 mg/kg QD over 6 weeks) or matched placebo for Part 2, with 98 of those also meeting the ≥30% stratum threshold (the PAP)

- Participants continued their usual diet unchanged throughout, with weekly 3-day diet records collected and reviewed by a dietician to confirm dietary Phe intake was not itself changing (fewer than 5% had a qualifying diet change)

- The SAP was finalized April 13, 2023 — notably, after topline trial results were already known to the Applicant (the trial completed April 2023); the FDA review states the only SAP change made after topline unblinding was the addition of one secondary endpoint (proportion achieving <360 µmol/L), which it did not flag as a substantive concern

- Primary result (PAP, N=49 vs. 49): LS mean blood Phe at Weeks 5-6 was 237.73 µmol/L (SE 24.06) with sepiapterin vs. 635.39 µmol/L (SE 24.06) with placebo, LS mean difference -397.66 µmol/L (95% CI: -465.20, -330.11), p<0.0001; an FDA-run alternative MMRM adjusting additionally for BH4-responsiveness status at screening gave a consistent LS mean difference of -400.3 µmol/L (95% CI: -469.52, -331.08), p<0.0001

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2025/219666Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/219666s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Integrated Review (combined clinical/statistical/summary review) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219666Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05099640 (no protocol/SAP posted)

- Pivotal publication: Muntau AC, Longo N, Ezgu F, et al. "Effects of oral sepiapterin on blood Phe concentration in a broad range of patients with phenylketonuria (APHENITY): results of an international, phase 3, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial." *Lancet.* 2024;404(10460):1333-1345. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(24)01556-3>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39368841/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Effects%20of%20oral%20sepiapterin%20on%20blood%20Phe%20concentration%20in%20a%20broad%20range%20of%20patients%20with%20phenylketonuria)

- Long-term extension data (PKU-004, including participants <2 years old who entered directly from Part 1) informed the pediatric dosing regimen but were reviewed as supportive safety/PK data rather than as an independent efficacy trial.

### 55. Elamipretide (Forzinity) — NDA 215244

**Sponsor:** Stealth BioTherapeutics Inc.

**Indication approved:** To improve muscle strength in adult and pediatric patients with Barth syndrome weighing at least 30 kg — granted under accelerated approval

**Approval date:** September 19, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** SPIBA-201 / TAZPOWER, NCT03098797 (Part 1: randomized crossover; Part 2/TAZPOWER Extension: single-arm open-label); supportive externally-controlled study SPIBA-001

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* small (N=12), randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, two-period crossover trial (Part 1, no washout gap issue but a 4-week washout between periods) followed by a long-term (192-week), single-arm, open-label extension in a subset (Part 2/TAZPOWER Extension, N=10); small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (Barth syndrome, ~150 U.S. patients)

- *Endpoints:* co-primary endpoint family — 6-minute walk test (6MWT) distance and total fatigue score on the Barth Syndrome Symptom Assessment (BTHS-SA), both assessed at Week 12 (Part 1); knee-extensor muscle strength by hand-held dynamometry (HHD, MAKE test) was a pre-specified secondary endpoint in both Part 1 and Part 2, later repurposed by FDA as the accelerated-approval "intermediate clinical endpoint"

- *Primary analysis:* mixed effects model (treatment, period, sequence fixed effects, subject random effect; compound-symmetry or unstructured covariance selected by corrected AIC) for the co-primary family; Hochberg step-up procedure to control family-wise alpha at 0.05 across the two co-primary endpoints; carryover/sequence effect tested at alpha=0.1, with a period-1-only ANCOVA fallback if significant

- *Multiplicity:* pre-specified sequential secondary-endpoint testing (PGI→CGI→PROMIS fatigue→Sway balance→HHD→5XSST), gated on both co-primary endpoints reaching significance — a gate that was never opened, since neither co-primary endpoint was met, so all secondary p-values (including HHD) are nominal, unadjusted, and explicitly labeled as such in the FDA review

- *Missing data/bias:* Part 2 (the source of the eventual approval basis) was open-label and single-arm with no control for confounders such as growth, effort-dependence, expectation bias, or supplemental nutrition/physical therapy; FDA's review explicitly flags "random high bias" from post hoc selection of the most favorable of five explored secondary endpoints

- *Regulatory:* Refusal-to-File (RTF) action under 21 CFR 314.101(d)(3) in 2021 (a pre-filing rejection, distinct from the taxonomy's existing post-filing Complete Response Letter row) on the original NDA submission, because it "does not contain a single adequate and well-controlled trial"; sponsor resubmitted in January 2024 without a new trial; a public Advisory Committee (Cardiovascular and Renal Drug Advisory Committee, October 10, 2024) voted 10-6 that available evidence supports effectiveness; FDA issued a Complete Response Letter on May 15, 2025 (manufacturing-facility deficiencies plus a clinical/statistical conclusion of no substantial evidence of effectiveness); sponsor resubmitted August 15, 2025 with no new efficacy data; the review team's clinical and statistical disciplines and Cross-Discipline Team Leader again recommended a Complete Response action on efficacy grounds, but the Signatory Authority overruled that recommendation and granted accelerated approval — closely analogous to the taxonomy's "Statistical reviewer's non-approval recommendation overruled by division leadership" pattern (seen previously with Ioflupane I 123/DaTscan), though here the override came at an even later, post-CRL-resubmission stage

**Trial design & endpoints**

- SPIBA-201 Part 1 (TAZPOWER) enrolled 12 males ≥12 years old with genetically confirmed Barth syndrome (BTHS) at a single U.S. site, randomized 1:1 to elamipretide 40 mg SC QD then placebo, or the reverse sequence, 12 weeks per period with a 4-week washout; both co-primary endpoints (6MWT distance, BTHS-SA total fatigue) were negative — a similar increase from baseline occurred in both arms, consistent with effort/expectation bias in an effort-dependent walk test; the pre-specified secondary HHD analysis likewise showed no treatment effect (LS mean difference 6.7 N, 95% CI: -24.8, 38.2, p=0.65; FDA's baseline-adjusted reviewer analysis: -3.0 N, 95% CI: -32.5, 26.6, p=0.83)

- All 12 subjects completed Part 1; 10 continued into the open-label, single-arm, 192-week Part 2 extension (whose stated primary objective was long-term safety, with HHD only a secondary, non-alpha-controlled endpoint); over more than 3 years of open-label follow-up, HHD showed a sustained, roughly 5-10-fold-larger increase from baseline than the placebo-period change seen in Part 1 (e.g., +48 N at Week 36 vs. screening, nominal p<0.01 at most timepoints), which the sponsor and, ultimately, the Signatory Authority treated as the operative efficacy signal, despite the same trial's own randomized, blinded data having shown no such effect over the comparable 12-week window

- A separate externally-controlled study, SPIBA-001, compared 6MWD in the same Part-2 elamipretide-treated subjects against a constructed natural-history control; FDA's review found this uninterpretable for the same effort/expectation-bias reasons as Part 2, compounded by concerns about the propensity-score matching and imputation methods used to build the control

- FDA's own multi-year regulatory history (documented in the Integrated Review) shows the elamipretide/BTHS program moved across four different FDA review divisions (Neurology, then Gastroenterology and Inborn Errors, then Rare Diseases and Medical Genetics, then Cardiology and Nephrology) between 2014 and 2021, with each division independently declining to accept 6MWD, echocardiographic parameters, or left-ventricular stroke volume as adequate efficacy evidence or a reasonably likely surrogate, before the original NDA was refused-to-file in 2021

- The Signatory Authority's approval rationale (Section 7.1.1 of the Integrated Review) explicitly frames this as a deliberate departure from the standard evidentiary bar: it "agrees that there is more uncertainty than we would accept for more common diseases" but "conclude[s] that we should accept the extent of uncertainty in the data in the context of this very rare... serious disease with no approved treatments," designating knee-extensor HHD strength as the accelerated-approval intermediate clinical endpoint and requiring a new randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled postmarketing confirmatory trial (design details redacted in the public review) as a condition of continued approval

**Documents**

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/215244s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Integrated Review, current (resubmission) review cycle, including full Section 12 regulatory history (RTF, prior CRL, Advisory Committee) and Section 7.1.1 Signatory Authority rationale — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/215244Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41436-020-01006-8), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33077895/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=A%20phase%202%2F3%20randomized%20clinical%20trial%20followed%20by%20an%20open-label%20extension%20to%20evaluate%20the%20effectiveness%20of%20elamipretide%20in%20Barth%20syndrome)

**Other resources**

- Stealth BioTherapeutics' general participation in Vivli.org/YODA-style IPD-sharing programs was not individually confirmed for this trial.

- FDA Advisory Committee: Cardiovascular and Renal Drug Advisory Committee (CRDAC), October 10, 2024; voted 10-6 "Yes" that available evidence supports effectiveness, following an open public hearing in which patients/caregivers described perceived improvements in fatigue, school participation, and (for infants) survival.

- Elamipretide was also studied for primary mitochondrial myopathy (MMPOWER-3 randomized trial) under the same sponsor, which did not show a treatment effect (PMID 37268435) — a second, independently-negative program for the same molecule, underscoring the contentiousness of the eventual Barth syndrome approval.

- The required postmarketing confirmatory trial (randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, in BTHS patients ≥5 years old) has agreed milestones with FDA per the Integrated Review, but full design details are redacted in the public document.

### 56. Doxecitine/doxribtimine (Kygevvi) — NDA 219792

**Sponsor:** UCB Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of thymidine kinase 2 deficiency (TK2d) in adults and pediatric patients with an age of symptom onset on or before 12 years

**Approval date:** November 3, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** Integrated Summary of Efficacy (ISE) pooling Trial TK0102 (NCT03845712, ongoing single-arm open-label), Study MT-1621-101 (NCT03701568, retrospective chart review), Study MT-1621-107 (NCT05017818, retrospective chart review), EAP/TK0114 (NCT06590493), and a literature-derived Updated Untreated Patient Database

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* cross-trial pooled/integrated analysis combining a prospective single-arm open-label trial, two retrospective chart-review natural-history studies, an expanded-access program, and a literature-derived untreated-patient database, compared via a matched external-control survival analysis (4-parity matched-pair external-control design — random, 50th-, 75th-, and 100th-percentile selection rules for assigning one untreated match per treated subject from an eligible "upper-half" pool)

- *Endpoints:* overall survival (OS) from treatment initiation (primary) and OS from symptom onset (supportive); restricted mean survival time (RMST) at multiple time horizons

- *Primary analysis:* three parallel Cox models per matching scheme — Cox Model 1 (stratified by matched pair, treatment-only), Cox Model 2 (stratified by pair, plus age-at-onset covariate), and Cox Model 3 (marginal Cox model, Lee et al. 1992, accounting for within-pair correlation via a closed-form covariance estimate) (marginal/Lee-1992 Cox model for matched-pair external-control survival data) — plus log-rank tests and RMST, run identically across all four matching schemes as a form of built-in sensitivity analysis

- *Missing data/bias:* substantial missingness in untreated-cohort birth year (~27-30%), race/ethnicity (~63-65%), and region (~20-22%) data, explicitly quantified and discussed as a limitation of the external-control comparison; a data-derivation discrepancy (one untreated subject incorrectly excluded from being flagged as symptomatic within 4 weeks of birth) was caught during FDA review and corrected, which — because that subject had died early — made the treated-group survival advantage numerically *less* favorable after correction, a detail the review documents transparently

- *Regulatory:* regular approval based on a single-source integrated analysis plus confirmatory evidence, per FDA's September 2023 SEE guidance (as in entry 1); FDA rejected the sponsor's initially proposed single retrospective chart review (Study MT-1621-101) as the sole adequate/well-controlled source because of survivorship/selection bias built into its eligibility criteria (requiring subjects alive as of a fixed date), instead requiring the broader integrated analysis with "all known treated subjects"; no Advisory Committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- The Applicant's efficacy case rested on an Integrated Summary of Efficacy (ISE) rather than a single named pivotal trial: 104 treated subjects (38 from the original 1990-2013 retrospective chart review MT-1621-101, plus additional subjects captured via the ongoing prospective trial TK0102, the MT-1621-107 chart review, and the TK0114 expanded-access program) were compared against 114 untreated subjects (drawn from MT-1621-107 case ascertainment plus a literature-search-derived "Updated Untreated Patient Database" of 128 patients)

- FDA's key efficacy review issue (Section 6.3.1) was comparability of the external control; the SAP (Draft 5, June 2021; Amendment 1, June 2023) was iterated with FDA across a July 2021 preliminary-comments letter and a November 2022 pre-NDA meeting, both flagging missing birth-year/region data and requiring a "robust discussion of potential biases"

- The evaluable population (EP) restricted both treated and untreated subjects to those born after 1999 with a severe ATP7A mutation type (deletion/duplication, nonsense, or canonical splice junction) and complete birth/death/last-known-alive data, yielding 104 treated and 114 untreated eligible subjects; four matched-pair datasets (95 pairs each) were built from this EP using the age-of-symptom-onset-group-stratified matching scheme described above, defining an early-treatment (ET, N=31) and late-treatment (LT, N=35) cohort with corresponding historical-control cohorts (HC-ET N=17, HC-LT N=16)

- Primary result (ET vs. HC-ET, log-rank/Cox Model 1): median OS from treatment initiation 177.1 months (treated) vs. 17.6 months (untreated); HR 0.22 (95% CI: 0.10, 0.49), p<0.0001. Secondary result (LT vs. HC-LT): median OS 62.4 vs. 20.7 months; HR 0.27 (95% CI: 0.12, 0.57), p=0.0003. Results were directionally and statistically consistent across all four matching schemes (Cox Model 1 HRs 0.10-0.15 for OS-from-symptom-onset; 0.27-0.28 for OS-from-treatment-initiation) and across all three Cox model specifications, and RMST differences (e.g., +11.6 to +11.8 years at a 30-year horizon for OS from symptom onset) told the same story

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2025/219792Orig1000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/219792s000lbl.pdf

- Pivotal publication: Hirano M, Garone C, Haas R, et al. "Efficacy and safety of pyrimidine nucleos(t)ide therapy in thymidine kinase 2 deficiency." *Brain Commun.* 2026;8(3):fcag201. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1093/braincomms/fcag201), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42318512/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Efficacy%20and%20safety%20of%20pyrimidine%20nucleos%28t%29ide%20therapy%20in%20thymidine%20kinase%202%20deficiency)

- Companion natural-history publication: "Disease burden of untreated thymidine kinase 2 deficiency: insights from a large patient dataset." *Brain Commun.* 2026;8(3). [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42318511/)

**Other resources**

- UCB's general participation in Vivli.org/YODA-style IPD-sharing programs was not individually confirmed for this program.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held.

- This is one of the clearest examples in this census of a fully external-control (no concurrent randomization at all) survival-based approval for an ultra-rare, uniformly fatal pediatric metabolic disease (TK2d, ~100-200 cases in the literature), with the entire "trial" being a multi-decade retrospective/prospective data-pooling exercise rather than a single protocol-driven study — worth cross-referencing against Zycubo/copper histidinate (entry 8 below), which uses a structurally similar matched-external-control survival design for a different ultra-rare disease.

### 57. Sibeprenlimab-szsi (Voyxact) — BLA 761434

**Sponsor:** Otsuka Pharmaceutical Company, Ltd.

**Indication approved:** To reduce proteinuria in adults with primary IgA nephropathy (IgAN) at risk for disease progression — granted under accelerated approval

**Approval date:** November 25, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** VISIONARY (Trial 417-201-00007), NCT05248646 (long-term extension: NCT05248659)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* ongoing, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial with background ACEI/ARB (± SGLT2i) therapy; main cohort (eGFR ≥30) plus a small exploratory cohort (eGFR 20-29, not the focus of this review); randomization stratified by screening UPCR, screening eGFR band, and SGLT2i use; group-sequential design with a single pre-specified unblinded interim analysis at 62.5% information fraction, used as the basis for accelerated approval

- *Endpoints:* proteinuria surrogate endpoint — ratio of 24-hour UPCR at 9 months to baseline (interim primary, basis for accelerated approval); annualized eGFR slope at ~24 months (key secondary, intended confirmatory/traditional-approval endpoint); composite kidney failure (CKF: sustained ≥40% eGFR decline, eGFR <15, dialysis, transplant, death) as a further secondary

- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA on log-transformed UPCR ratio-to-baseline (per-protocol MMRM-then-ANCOVA workflow); FDA required the sponsor to re-run the primary analysis using a treatment-policy estimand strategy (rather than the sponsor's originally planned hypothetical strategy for rescue-medication intercurrent events), with missing post-ICE data imputed via a placebo-based multiple-imputation approach — a clear instance of the taxonomy's "reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan" pattern, here initiated by FDA directing an estimand change mid-review (June 17, 2025 request, June 24, 2025 sponsor response)

- *Multiplicity:* graphical alpha-propagation method (Maurer-Bretz-style, per the taxonomy's Camizestrant/SERENA-6 precedent) — initial 2-sided alpha of 0.035 to the primary (UPCR) and 0.015 to the key secondary (eGFR), with full alpha (0.05) passed to eGFR if UPCR is significant at the interim, followed by sequential testing of two CKF-related secondaries at the final analysis

- *Missing data/bias:* three intercurrent-event categories handled by different strategies (treatment policy for early discontinuation, hypothetical-then-treatment-policy for rescue medication, and a composite strategy with worst-observed-value-plus-random-error imputation for kidney-failure-related terminal events); fully-conditional-specification multiple imputation for remaining missing-at-random data; two-way tipping-point analysis; a Bayesian hierarchical shrinkage estimator (noninformative priors, Cauchy scale prior on between-subgroup variance) applied to subgroup forest plots to stabilize small-subgroup point estimates

- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval based on a proteinuria surrogate endpoint in IgA nephropathy (as in entry 3 — Vanrafia/atrasentan), making sibeprenlimab the third approved drug on this specific renal-surrogate accelerated-approval pathway after sparsentan and atrasentan; no Advisory Committee meeting held (one was tentatively scheduled for May 2025, then cancelled as unnecessary)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Trial 417-201-00007 (VISIONARY) enrolled adults with biopsy-proven IgAN on stable maximally-tolerated ACEI/ARB (± stable SGLT2i), screening UPCR ≥0.75 g/g or urine protein ≥1.0 g/day, eGFR ≥30 (main cohort); randomized 1:1 to sibeprenlimab 400 mg SC every 4 weeks (26 doses over 100 weeks) vs. placebo; 510 subjects enrolled in the main cohort (plus 20 in the exploratory low-eGFR cohort) as of the March 2024 data cut, with the interim analysis based on the first 62.5% of randomized main-cohort subjects (uPCR-24h at 9 months)

- Primary result (Interim Analysis Full Analysis Set #1, treatment-policy/placebo-based-imputation analysis, N=152 vs. 168): ratio of geometric means of UPCR-24h at Month 9 to baseline was 0.50 (sibeprenlimab) vs. 1.02 (placebo); ratio-of-ratios 0.49 (96.5% CI: 0.42, 0.58), corresponding to a 50.8% relative reduction (96.5% CI: 42.4%-57.9%), p<0.0001

- Subgroup analyses were broadly consistent, with the North America regional subgroup and the baseline-hematuria-negative subgroup showing numerically smaller, less precise point estimates; FDA's shrinkage-estimator reanalysis of the same subgroups produced narrower, more stable estimates, illustrating (per the review's own methodological framing) how small-subgroup point estimates in a rare-disease trial can otherwise look like spurious "random highs and lows"

- The eGFR-slope key secondary/confirmatory endpoint had not yet reached its ~24-month readout at the time of this accelerated-approval review; the trial continues toward that endpoint as the traditional-approval confirmatory measure

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2025/761434Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/761434s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Integrated Review (combined clinical/statistical/summary review) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/761434Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record, pivotal — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05248646 (no protocol/SAP posted)

- ClinicalTrials.gov record, open-label extension — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05248659

- Pivotal publication: Perkovic V, Trimarchi H, Tesar V, et al. "Sibeprenlimab in IgA Nephropathy — Interim Analysis of a Phase 3 Trial." *N Engl J Med.* 2026;394(7):635-646. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2512133), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41211929/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Sibeprenlimab%20in%20IgA%20Nephropathy%20Interim%20Analysis%20of%20a%20Phase%203%20Trial)

**Other resources**

- Otsuka's general participation in Vivli.org/YODA-style IPD-sharing programs was not individually confirmed for this trial.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held.

- Sibeprenlimab (an anti-APRIL monoclonal antibody) and atrasentan (entry 3, an endothelin-receptor antagonist) now sit alongside sparsentan as three distinct mechanistic classes approved on the same proteinuria-reduction accelerated-approval pathway for IgAN within about 18 months of each other — a useful cross-entry comparison for how FDA's renal division has operationalized a single surrogate endpoint across different drug classes.

### 58. Copper histidinate (Zycubo) — NDA 211241

**Sponsor:** Sentynl Therapeutics, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of Menkes disease (MD) in pediatric patients

**Approval date:** January 12, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** Integrated efficacy analysis pooling Study 90-CH-0149 (NCT00001262, NIH, 1990-2013) and Study 09-CH-0059 (NCT00811785, NIH Phase 3, 2009-2019), both open-label single-arm studies conducted at the NIH Clinical Center; supportive ongoing expanded-access program CYP-001

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* cross-trial pooled/integrated analysis of two decades-spanning, NIH-run, open-label single-arm academic studies, compared against an untreated historical-control cohort via four parallel age-of-symptom-onset-stratified matching schemes (random, 50th-, 75th-, and 100th-percentile selection of one untreated match per treated subject) — structurally the same matched-external-control survival design as Kygevvi/doxecitine-doxribtimine (entry 6), independently arrived at by a different sponsor/review division for a different ultra-rare metabolic disease

- *Endpoints:* overall survival (OS) time from date of birth, split into an early-treatment (ET, treatment started ≤4 weeks after birth) vs. historical-control (HC-ET) primary comparison and a late-treatment (LT) vs. historical-control (HC-LT) secondary comparison, gated on the primary comparison reaching significance

- *Primary analysis:* log-rank test (primary comparison) plus a Cox proportional-hazards model (treatment-only) for the hazard ratio, with Kaplan-Meier estimation of median survival; the secondary (LT vs. HC-LT) comparison used matched-cohort exclusion rules (excluding LT subjects whose treatment-initiation age exceeded the HC-LT cohort's maximum survival time, and vice versa) to keep the risk sets comparable

- *Missing data/bias:* the historical-control (untreated) cohort was assembled via patient-advocacy-group referrals, professional-society requests, investigator personal knowledge of untreated patients, and identification of older affected first-degree relatives of enrolled subjects — a convenience-sample external control with correspondingly large missingness in birth year, race/ethnicity, and region; during FDA review, one untreated subject was found to have been miscategorized as asymptomatic at 4 weeks (actually symptomatic with seizures at day 7) and was excluded from the historical-control cohorts after correction — a change that made the treated group's relative survival advantage numerically *smaller* (since the corrected subject had died early), which FDA's review adopted as the operative analysis rather than the Applicant's original (more favorable) numbers

- *Regulatory:* Complete Response Letter issued September 30, 2025 for manufacturing-facility (Zydus Lifesciences, Gujarat, India) cGMP deficiencies identified on a Warning-Letter-triggering inspection — a purely CMC-driven CRL following years of efficacy negotiation on a 3-part rolling NDA (Part 1 filed December 2021); Class 1 resubmission November 14, 2025 after facility remediation (For Cause reinspection outcome: Voluntary Action Indicated); no Advisory Committee meeting held; orphan drug designation (2012), Fast Track (2018), and Rare Pediatric Disease designations

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 0149 began in June 1990 at NIH's Porter Neuroscience Research Center (plus 5 other sites) to study clinical/biochemical effects of copper histidinate in Menkes disease; a 2007 amendment narrowed enrollment to newborns diagnosed pre-symptomatically, after early data suggested older/symptomatic infants did not benefit — 59 subjects enrolled (56 MD, 3 non-MD). Study 0059, a Phase 3 open-label study begun February 2009 at the NIH Clinical Center (plus 10 sites), originally assessed neurodevelopmental/neurological response to copper injection; a 2016 amendment (Amendment M) added collection of an untreated comparator cohort, and a 2017 amendment (Amendment O) formalized survival as a secondary objective — 113 subjects enrolled, 78 treated

- Neither study's original eligibility criteria were sufficient on their own to define a clean efficacy population (Study 0149's required biochemical/clinical MD diagnosis and Study 0059's simple low-serum-copper threshold were both non-specific), so FDA's review restricted the integrated efficacy analysis to subjects born after 1999 carrying a severe ATP7A mutation type (deletion/duplication, nonsense, or canonical splice junction) — 66 treated and 18 untreated subjects met this bar, further split by treatment-timing into ET (N=31)/HC-ET (N=17) and LT (N=35)/HC-LT (N=16) matched cohorts

- Primary result (ET vs. HC-ET): 15/31 (48.4%) deaths in the treated group vs. 15/17 (88.2%) in the historical control; median survival 177.1 months (treated) vs. 17.6 months (untreated); hazard ratio 0.22 (95% CI: 0.10, 0.49), p<0.0001. Secondary result (LT vs. HC-LT): 23/35 (65.7%) vs. 14/16 (87.5%) deaths; median survival 62.4 vs. 20.7 months; HR 0.27 (95% CI: 0.12, 0.57), p=0.0003

- The regulatory record here is notably different from Kygevvi's (entry 6): the efficacy conclusion itself (Section 6.2.1, dated to an earlier September 26, 2025 Integrated Review) was not the site of controversy — the delay to final approval was entirely a manufacturing-quality/CMC issue at a third-party facility, resolved between the September 2025 CRL and the January 2026 approval

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2026/211241Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/211241s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Integrated Review (resubmission review cycle, embedding the September 26, 2025 efficacy Integrated Review as well as the safety-focused December 2025 resubmission review) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/211241Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record, Study 0149 — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00001262 (no protocol/SAP posted; NIH intramural protocol)

- ClinicalTrials.gov record, Study 0059 — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00811785 (no protocol/SAP posted; NIH intramural protocol)

- Foundational academic publication (predates the NDA by over a decade; describes the early-treatment survival/developmental benefit that the later integrated analysis formalizes): Kaler SG, Holmes CS, Goldstein DS, et al. "Neonatal diagnosis and treatment of Menkes disease." *N Engl J Med.* 2008;358(6):605-614. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa070613), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18256395/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Neonatal%20diagnosis%20and%20treatment%20of%20Menkes%20disease)

- No dedicated pivotal-trial-results publication corresponding to the specific matched-cohort integrated survival analysis submitted in NDA 211241 was identified via PubMed as of this entry; the regulatory analysis appears to postdate and extend the 2008 NEJM findings using additional NIH cohort data not yet published in that form.

**Other resources**

- Sentynl's general participation in Vivli.org/YODA-style IPD-sharing programs was not individually confirmed; the underlying data are NIH intramural research data, not sponsor-generated trial data in the conventional sense.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held.

- This entry and entry 6 (Kygevvi/doxecitine-doxribtimine) form a natural pair for studying how FDA's Division of Rare Diseases and Medical Genetics has, independently, converged on the same statistical toolkit (multiple matching-rule sensitivity analyses, Cox models with matched-pair strata, RMST) for ultra-rare pediatric metabolic diseases where a randomized placebo-controlled trial is not ethically feasible.

### 59. Pegzilarginase-nbln (Loargys) — BLA 761211

**Sponsor:** Immedica Pharma AB (originally developed by Aeglea BioTherapeutics, Inc.; BLA ownership transferred to Immedica in September 2023)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of hyperargininemia in adult and pediatric patients ≥2 years old with Arginase 1 Deficiency (ARG1-D), in conjunction with dietary protein restriction — granted under accelerated approval

**Approval date:** February 23, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** PEACE (Trial CAEB1102-300A), NCT03921541

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, single-pivotal-trial (single adequate and well-controlled trial) superiority trial, stratified by severity of prior hyperammonemia history; small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (N=32)

- *Endpoints:* biomarker/surrogate endpoint — change from baseline in plasma arginine at Week 24 (primary, basis for accelerated approval); two key secondary mobility/motor-function endpoints — 2-minute walk test (2MWT) and Gross Motor Function Measure-88 Part E (GMFM-E) — intended as the traditional-approval clinical-benefit evidence, plus GMFM Part D as a gated further secondary

- *Primary analysis:* mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) on log-transformed plasma arginine, Kenward-Roger denominator degrees of freedom (as in entry 3); key secondary motor endpoints analyzed by MMRM plus, at FDA's initiative, an exact Wilcoxon rank-sum test on ANCOVA residuals; FDA additionally conducted two post hoc, permutation-based global tests across the secondary-endpoint sets — a t-test-statistics-sum method and an O'Brien rank-sum method (each with a 2,000-permutation null distribution) (FDA-conducted post hoc global test for a family of secondary clinical endpoints in a small rare-disease trial, distinct from a pre-specified multiplicity procedure)

- *Multiplicity:* Hochberg step-up procedure (one-sided alpha 0.025) for the two key secondary endpoints (2MWT, GMFM-E), with GMFM-D gated behind both

- *Missing data/bias:* one pegzilarginase subject who withdrew at Week 6 had the Week 24 primary-endpoint value imputed from the subject's own Week 6 value (sensitivity analyses using baseline-value imputation instead were consistent); no formal imputation was pre-specified for the key secondary endpoints (missing-at-random via MMRM), with 3/32 subjects (9.4%) missing 2MWT data and 1/32 (3.1%) missing GMFM data, prompting additional FDA sensitivity analyses

- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval based on a biomarker (plasma arginine) surrogate endpoint despite the same pivotal trial missing both of its key secondary clinical (motor-function) endpoints under the pre-specified Hochberg procedure (2MWT one-sided p=0.30; GMFM-E one-sided p=0.07) — closely analogous to the taxonomy's Tofersen/Qalsody precedent, but here compounded by a Complete Response Letter (August 6, 2025) issued not for an efficacy deficiency but because of the lack of an FDA-authorized in vitro diagnostic device to measure plasma arginine for treatment monitoring, resolved only after CDRH separately authorized a companion diagnostic; original 2022 BLA (under prior sponsor Aeglea) was refused-to-file for CMC deficiencies and insufficient evidence of effectiveness; a public Advisory Committee meeting was tentatively scheduled (May 27, 2025) then cancelled as unnecessary

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Trial CAEB1102-300A (PEACE) enrolled subjects ≥2 years old with ARG1-D, screening plasma arginine ≥250 µM, and a mobility deficit on at least one secondary-outcome component, across 19 sites in 7 countries; randomized 2:1 to weekly IV pegzilarginase (starting 0.1 mg/kg, titratable 0.05-0.2 mg/kg based on arginine levels, n=21) or placebo (n=11) for a 24-week double-blind period, followed by an open-label extension of up to 150 weeks

- Primary result (FAS): plasma arginine reduced substantially with pegzilarginase (exact figures redacted/not reported as a treatment-difference statistic in the reviewed excerpt, but described as meeting the primary objective); of the two key secondary motor endpoints, 2MWT showed a treatment difference of 5.5 m (95% CI: -15.6, 26.7; one-sided p=0.30) and GMFM-E showed 4.1 points (95% CI: -1.5, 9.7; one-sided p=0.07) — neither reaching the Hochberg-adjusted significance threshold, though both numerically favored pegzilarginase; the non-gated GMFM-D endpoint showed a treatment difference of 3.0 points (95% CI: 0.3, 5.7; one-sided p=0.02), formally uninterpretable per the pre-specified gating rule but presented for context

- FDA's post hoc global tests (combining the key secondary endpoints, or all three motor endpoints together) produced nominal one-sided p-values that varied by which endpoint set and global-test method were used (t-test-sum vs. O'Brien rank-sum) — the review explicitly frames global testing as attractive but limited for small rare-disease trials, since "rejecting the global null hypothesis does not imply a statistically significant treatment effect on any one endpoint"

- FDA's own exposure-efficacy (linear regression) analyses of plasma arginine, GMFM-D/E, and 2MWT against average weekly drug exposure found a statistically significant arginine-lowering trend (p=0.0000037) but no significant exposure-response relationship for any of the three motor-function measures, consistent with the trial's key secondary endpoints having missed formal significance

- Regulatory history: FDA repeatedly told the original sponsor (Aeglea BioTherapeutics) from 2018-2022 that a ~24-week trial was too short and that plasma-arginine reduction alone was insufficient evidence of clinical benefit; the March 2022 BLA was refused-to-file; after BLA ownership transferred to Immedica (September 2023), FDA's signatory authority ultimately concluded — in the first substantive review cycle — that plasma arginine qualified as a reasonably-likely-surrogate endpoint supporting accelerated approval, with confirmatory evidence to be generated post-marketing; the August 2025 CRL that followed was unrelated to this efficacy conclusion, addressing only the absence of an FDA-authorized companion diagnostic for plasma arginine monitoring

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2026/761211Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/761211Orig1s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Integrated Review (BLA Resubmission Review, embedding the original efficacy review and regulatory history) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761211Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03921541 (no protocol/SAP posted)

- Pivotal publication: Russo RS, Gasperini S, Bubb G, et al. "Efficacy and safety of pegzilarginase in arginase 1 deficiency (PEACE): a phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multi-centre trial." *EClinicalMedicine.* 2024;68:102405. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eclinm.2023.102405), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38292042/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Efficacy%20and%20safety%20of%20pegzilarginase%20in%20arginase%201%20deficiency%20PEACE)

**Other resources**

- Immedica's/Aeglea's general participation in Vivli.org/YODA-style IPD-sharing programs was not individually confirmed for this trial.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held (one was scheduled for May 2025, then cancelled).

- The August 2025 CRL tying approval to companion-diagnostic device availability (rather than a clinical or CMC deficiency in the drug product itself) is a comparatively unusual regulatory posture worth flagging: continued marketing of a biomarker-driven accelerated approval was made contingent on a *diagnostic device* clearance at CDRH, a cross-center dependency not seen elsewhere in this census to date.

### 60. Tividenofusp alfa-eknm (Avlayah) — BLA 761485

**Sponsor:** Denali Therapeutics Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of neurologic manifestations of Hunter syndrome (mucopolysaccharidosis type II, MPS II) — granted under accelerated approval

**Approval date:** March 24, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** DNLI-E-0002, NCT04251026 (supportive natural-history study: DNLI-E-0001; long-term extension: NCT06075537)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Phase 1/2, single-arm, open-label, multi-cohort dose-escalation trial with no concurrent control, accepted by FDA as a "baseline-controlled" adequate and well-controlled trial for a biomarker endpoint rather than a randomized design; brain-penetrant enzyme-replacement therapy using a transferrin-receptor-targeting fusion protein (an "ETV"/BBB-crossing platform) engineered to cross the blood-brain barrier, distinguishing it from conventional (non-CNS-penetrant) MPS II enzyme-replacement therapies

- *Endpoints:* biomarker/surrogate endpoint — percent change from baseline in cerebrospinal fluid heparan sulfate (CSF HS) at Week 24 (key secondary objective, but the operative accelerated-approval endpoint); urine HS as supportive (non-surrogate) evidence; neurodevelopmental/cognitive composite endpoint — a composite cognitive age-equivalent score (CCAES) derived from BSID-III/KABC-II, plus Vineland-3 adaptive-behavior raw scores (ABRS-8), collected as confirmatory-evidence-level data rather than as a formally tested primary/secondary endpoint (continuous psychiatric/neurological rating-scale-type change-from-baseline measure, per the taxonomy's existing category, here applied to a neurodevelopmental rather than psychiatric construct)

- *Primary analysis:* mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) on log-transformed biomarker data (visit, age-at-initiation category, genotype, log-baseline as fixed effects; Satterthwaite denominator degrees of freedom), entirely descriptive with no formal hypothesis testing per the SAP; FDA's reviewers substituted a plain (non-log-scale) descriptive change/percent-change analysis in place of the Applicant's geometric-mean-of-fold-change approach, explicitly because the Applicant's transformed estimand "cannot be interpreted as the mean or median percent change from baseline"

- *Missing data/bias:* no formal imputation — MMRM's implicit missing-at-random handling only; population PK/PD modeling (exposure-response for CSF HS and urine HS) supplemented the sparse per-dose-cohort observed data; no significant exposure-response relationship was found between drug exposure and the neurodevelopmental (CCAES) endpoint, consistent with the trial not yet demonstrating a clinical (as opposed to biomarker) benefit

- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval based on a CNS biomarker (CSF HS) reasonably-likely-surrogate endpoint from a single-arm trial with no concurrent control, where the "adequate and well-controlled" designation itself rested on confirmatory evidence rather than a true external/historical control — FDA explicitly rejected the Applicant's own natural-history study (DNLI-E-0001) as inadequate for this purpose (it only measured CSF biomarkers at baseline, not their untreated trajectory), instead relying on a published *external* RCT in a different drug (Muenzer et al. 2016, intrathecal idursulfase) to argue CSF glycosaminoglycan levels do not spontaneously decline without treatment (single-arm biomarker trial accepted as adequate/well-controlled using literature-derived confirmatory evidence of non-spontaneous-improvement, in lieu of a concurrent or genuine historical control); no Advisory Committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- DNLI-E-0002 enrolled male pediatric subjects with confirmed MPS II (reduced IDS activity plus an IDS gene mutation) across seven sites in the US, Canada, UK, and Netherlands, into five predefined cohorts (A-E) differentiated by age, neuronopathic-vs-non-neuronopathic status, prior ERT exposure, and (for one subgroup) pre-existing organomegaly; neuronopathic-MPS-II eligibility required a cognitive standard score ≤85, a documented ≥7.5-point cognitive decline, a genetically-confirmed affected relative, or a large IDS deletion/rearrangement per independent panel review; dosing ranged from 3 to 30 mg/kg QW, with the approved regimen (3 mg/kg starting dose escalating to 15 mg/kg maintenance) chosen from population PK/PD modeling showing near-maximal CSF/urine HS reduction at that maintenance level

- As of the October 2024 data cutoff, 47 subjects were enrolled; 46 completed the 24-week Part 1 (one pegzilarginase-unrelated AE-driven discontinuation), 27 completed the 18-month Part 2 safety extension, and no subjects had yet completed the Part 3 long-term open-label extension

- Primary (RLSE) result: observed median percent reduction in CSF HS from baseline to Week 24 ranged from 88% to 94% across all dose levels studied (3-30 mg/kg), with urine HS reductions more dose-dependent (69% at 3 mg/kg vs. 91-92% at 15-30 mg/kg); population PK/PD modeling predicted CSF HS reduction plateaus at doses ≥3 mg/kg while urine HS reduction plateaus at doses ≥15 mg/kg, supporting the approved maintenance dose

- Neurodevelopmental data (CCAES, Vineland-3 ABRS-8) were reviewed as confirmatory-evidence context for the CSF HS surrogate's link to clinical benefit, not as an independently powered or formally tested efficacy claim; FDA found no significant dose/exposure relationship with the cognitive composite, and the review frames the CSF HS surrogate as reasonably likely — not yet demonstrated — to predict neurodevelopmental benefit, consistent with a required postmarketing confirmatory trial

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2026/761485Orig1s000correctedltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/761485s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Integrated Review (combined clinical/statistical/summary review) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761485Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record, pivotal — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04251026 (no protocol/SAP posted)

- ClinicalTrials.gov record, long-term extension — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06075537

- Pivotal publication: Muenzer J, Burton BK, Harmatz P, et al. "An Intravenous Brain-Penetrant Enzyme Therapy for Mucopolysaccharidosis II." *N Engl J Med.* 2026;394(1):39-50. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2508681), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41467650/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=An%20Intravenous%20Brain-Penetrant%20Enzyme%20Therapy%20for%20Mucopolysaccharidosis%20II)

**Other resources**

- Denali's general participation in Vivli.org/YODA-style IPD-sharing programs was not individually confirmed for this trial.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held; the review states the team concluded the evidence was "robust" and "outside expertise was deemed not necessary."

- Tividenofusp alfa is, per the FDA review, the first BBB-crossing enzyme-replacement therapy approved for an MPS disorder; its accelerated-approval basis rests entirely on a CNS biomarker (CSF HS) rather than any direct neurocognitive measurement, making the required postmarketing confirmatory trial (expected to assess neurodevelopmental outcomes directly) the key open question for verifying the drug's central clinical promise.

### 61. Atacicept-vymj (Trutakna) — BLA 761486

**Sponsor:** Vera Therapeutics, Inc.

**Indication approved:** To reduce proteinuria in adults with primary immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) who are at risk of disease progression; approved under the accelerated approval pathway based on reduction in urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR), a reasonably likely surrogate endpoint for loss of kidney function; continued approval is contingent on verification of clinical benefit (slowing of eGFR decline) at the confirmatory final analysis of the same pivotal trial.

**Approval date:** July 7, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** ORIGIN 3 (Study VT-001-0050), NCT04716231 — Week 36 interim analysis (Interim Analysis Set, N=203 of 428 dosed); final analysis (eGFR slope through Week 104) pending as the accelerated-approval confirmatory endpoint

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter Phase 2b/3 trial; accelerated approval granted from a prespecified unblinded interim analysis of an ongoing randomized trial, with that same trial's later final analysis serving as the confirmatory/verification evidence rather than an independently conducted confirmatory trial (distinct from the taxonomy's existing "Confirmatory evidence via continuation/expansion of the same pivotal single-arm trial," which covers single-arm, not randomized, designs; this proteinuria-to-eGFR paradigm is shared with other recent IgAN drugs such as sparsentan and atrasentan)
- *Endpoints:* percent reduction in 24-hour UPCR from baseline to Week 36 (primary, interim analysis); annualized eGFR total slope through Week 104 (confirmatory/key secondary endpoint, final analysis); serum galactose-deficient IgA1 (Gd-IgA1) as an exploratory pharmacodynamic biomarker
- *Primary analysis:* MMRM on natural log-transformed UPCR (24-hour collection), adjusted for baseline SGLT2 inhibitor use, region, baseline eGFR category, and baseline log-transformed UPCR; treatment effect expressed as percent reduction via back-transformed geometric mean ratio
- *Multiplicity:* Fallback Procedure (already in Keyword_Taxonomy.md § Multiplicity, per CLL14) — primary endpoint tested at α=0.01 two-sided; key secondary (eGFR) endpoint at α=0.05 if the primary is significant or α=0.04 if it is not; further secondary endpoints at α=0.05/0.04/0 depending on primary and key-secondary results; only the primary endpoint was formally tested at the interim analysis
- *Missing data/bias:* mixed reference-based/multiple-imputation approach within one MMRM model — jump-to-reference (J2R) imputation for atacicept-arm dropouts (n=3), multiple imputation under the missing-at-random (MAR) assumption for placebo-arm dropouts (n=2)
- *Regulatory:* accelerated approval; Breakthrough Therapy Designation (granted May 23, 2024); no FDA advisory committee meeting held; postmarketing requirements include completion of ORIGIN 3's final analysis, a PREA pediatric PK/PD/safety study (ages 2-17), a lactation study, and a worldwide pregnancy-exposure registry study

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ORIGIN 3 (VT-001-0050): Phase 2b/3, multicenter, randomized 1:1, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of atacicept 150 mg subcutaneously once weekly vs. placebo in adults with biopsy-proven primary IgAN, eGFR ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m², and UPCR ≥1 g/g (or total urine protein ≥1.0 g/24h) on a stable, maximally-tolerated renin-angiotensin-system inhibitor regimen with or without a stable SGLT2 inhibitor and/or mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist; patients with other glomerulopathies or recent systemic immunosuppression were excluded. 750 subjects were screened; 431 randomized; 428 dosed (214 per arm), comprising the Full Analysis Set (FAS) and safety population.
- Primary endpoint at the interim analysis: change from baseline to Week 36 in natural log-transformed UPCR (24-hour urine collection), analyzed in the prespecified Interim Analysis Set (IAS) — the first 203 randomized/dosed subjects (106 atacicept, 97 placebo) who reached Week 36 or discontinued as of the May 15, 2025 data cutoff.
- Key secondary/confirmatory endpoint: annualized rate of change (slope) in eGFR through Week 104 in the Full Analysis Set, to be assessed at the trial's final analysis and used both to verify clinical benefit and to support potential conversion to traditional approval.
- Exploratory endpoints at the interim analysis: annualized eGFR slope through Week 52 and change from baseline in eGFR by visit through Week 52, both analyzed with a mixed-effects model with random intercept and random slope (MMRIRS), without formal statistical testing.
- Sample size: 100 subjects per group gives 92% power at a two-sided α=0.01 to detect a 33% greater UPCR reduction with atacicept (geometric mean ratio 0.67, SD=0.7 for log-transformed change); no sample-size inflation for withdrawal was applied because missing data were to be imputed and retained in the primary analysis.
- Efficacy result: atacicept achieved a 45.7% reduction in UPCR from baseline at Week 36 (95% CI 37.6, 52.7) vs. 6.8% with placebo (95% CI −7.6, 19.2); between-group difference 41.8% (95% CI 28.9, 52.3; prespecified 99% CI 24.3, 55.2, corresponding to the two-sided 0.01 significance threshold used at the interim analysis), p<0.0001.
- Multiplicity: fallback procedure controlling family-wise type I error at α=0.05 across the primary endpoint (α=0.01) → key secondary eGFR endpoint (α=0.05 or 0.04) → other secondary endpoints (α=0.05/0.04/0); formal hypothesis testing at the interim analysis was restricted to the primary endpoint only, per the SAP, with the rest of the hierarchy deferred to the final analysis.
- Missing data/intercurrent events: treatment discontinuation and initiation of prohibited or rescue therapy were prespecified intercurrent events; jump-to-reference imputation was applied to the 3 atacicept-arm subjects with missing Week-36 UPCR data, and multiple imputation under the MAR assumption was applied to the 2 placebo-arm subjects with missing data.

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2026/761486Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/761486Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Integrated Review (combined statistical/clinical review format) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761486Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04716231 (no protocol/SAP documents posted as of September 2026)
- Pivotal publication: Lafayette R, Barbour SJ, Brenner RM, et al.; ORIGIN Phase 3 Trial Investigators. "A Phase 3 Trial of Atacicept in Patients with IgA Nephropathy." *N Engl J Med.* 2026;394(7):647-657. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2510198), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41196369/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=A%20Phase%203%20Trial%20of%20Atacicept%20in%20Patients%20with%20IgA%20Nephropathy)

**Other resources**

- Vera Therapeutics is a small, single-product biotech; no confirmed participation in a cross-industry IPD-sharing platform (e.g., Vivli) was identified — trial-specific data availability was not individually confirmed here.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was held for this application (per FDA Integrated Review §11: "an Advisory Committee Meeting was not held for this application").
- Postmarketing requirements: completion of the ORIGIN 3 final analysis (eGFR slope) to verify clinical benefit; a PREA pediatric pharmacodynamic/pharmacokinetic/safety/tolerability study in patients 2-17 years old; a lactation study measuring atacicept and metabolites in breast milk; and a worldwide descriptive pregnancy-exposure registry study.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, BLA 761486, §6.2.1.5, p.33]* — "The Applicant's original statistical analysis plan (SAP) for the interim analysis (IA) (database lock cutoff date: May 15, 2025) was finalized on February 11, 2025, and is referred to as version 1.0. The SAP for the IA was amended once. Version 2 was finalized on May 23, 2025, based on FDA feedback provided on April 29, 2025, and May 9, 2025. The changes that were made to the SAP in this amendment do not raise concerns about the interpretability of the trial results."

*[verbatim, same document, §6.2.1.5, p.34]* — "The trial uses a fallback procedure to control type I error at α=0.05, testing the primary endpoint first at α=0.01, then the key secondary endpoint at α=0.05 (if primary is significant) or α=0.04 (if primary is not significant), followed by sequential testing of other selected secondary endpoints at α=0.05, 0.04, or 0 depending on the primary and key secondary results (Figure 2). At the interim analysis, formal testing was restricted to the primary endpoint. The key secondary endpoint and other secondary endpoints will be formally tested according to the testing procedure at the final analysis."

*[verbatim, same document, §6.2.1.5, p.35]* — "Due to its skewed distribution, UPCR was natural log transformed. The primary endpoint is the change from baseline to Week 36 in natural log-transformed UPCR. Sample size calculations assume atacicept would achieve 33% greater UPCR reduction than placebo (geometric mean ratio 0.67) with SD =0.7 for log-transformed changes. With 100 subjects per group, the trial has 92% power to detect this effect at α=0.01 (two-sided). Missing data after subject withdrawals will be imputed and included in the primary efficacy endpoint analysis, therefore no increase in sample size for withdrawals is necessary."

*[verbatim, same document, §6.2.1.6.3, p.42]* — "The primary analysis of UPCR at Week 36 was conducted using an MMRM analysis on the IAS, with intercurrent events handled according to strategies prespecified in the SAP... Missing data were imputed using jump to reference for the atacicept arm (n=3) and multiple imputation under the MAR assumption for the placebo arm (n=2)... At Week 36, subjects randomized to atacicept achieved a 45.7% reduction in UPCR (95% CI: 37.6%, 52.7%) compared with a 6.8% reduction (95% CI: −7.6%, 19.2%) in subjects randomized to placebo. This corresponded to a statistically significant between-group difference of 41.8% (95% CI: 28.9%, 52.3%; p<0.0001) favoring atacicept at the prespecified significance level of 0.01 (2-sided)."

*[verbatim, same document, §1.1, p.3]* — "This trial met its primary endpoint at the interim analysis: At Week 36, compared to placebo, subjects on atacicept had a 42% (95% CI: 29, 52; p<0.0001) greater reduction in UPCR compared to baseline. The result was generally consistent across subgroups and prespecified stratification factors, including age, sex, race, baseline proteinuria, and baseline eGFR."

*[verbatim, same document, §1.1, p.4]* — "FDA's accelerated approval regulations and the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act indicate that confirmatory trials must be completed with due diligence (21 U.S.C. 356c). As noted above, the ORIGIN 3 trial is ongoing, and the primary endpoint at the final analysis in this trial will be used to verify and describe the clinical benefit. The ORIGIN 3 trial is fully enrolled and is expected to be completed in a timely manner following accelerated approval."
