### 62. Garetosmab-grts (Pasatru) — BLA 761508

**Sponsor:** Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of heterotopic ossification (HO) and flare-ups in adults with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP)

**Approval date:** August 19, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** Study 1, NCT05394116 (Phase 3, 56-week double-blind period plus double-blind extension)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* small (N=63), randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, multicenter, placebo-controlled, three-arm (two active doses + placebo) Phase 3 trial in an ultra-rare disease population — an extension of the taxonomy's existing "Small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population" entry (previously seen in Lomitapide, Mipomersen, Metreleptin, Evinacumab-dgnb) to a three-arm dose-comparison version
- *Endpoints:* number of new heterotopic ossification (HO) lesions at Week 56 by whole-body low-dose CT, co-primary with treatment-emergent adverse events of special interest (AESIs); key secondary endpoints: clinician-assessed flare-ups through Week 56, proportion of patients with any new HO lesion, and total volume of new HO lesions
- *Primary analysis:* [inferred] rate-ratio comparison of new-HO-lesion counts per dose arm vs. placebo, consistent with a log-linear overdispersed count-regression model such as the taxonomy's existing "Negative binomial regression with an exposure-time offset" — the exact model family is not confirmed, only the resulting rate ratios and CIs are disclosed in the label
- *Multiplicity:* [inferred] some prespecified multiple-testing correction across the two active-dose-vs-placebo comparisons and/or the primary/key-secondary endpoint family, evidenced only by the label's "multiplicity-adjusted p-value <0.05" footnote on the primary result; the specific procedure is not public
- *Missing data/bias:* label reports a "pre-specified Wilcoxon rank-sum test" for the total new-HO-lesion-volume secondary endpoint, implying a non-parametric method was specified for this heavily skewed/zero-inflated outcome even though a parametric mean difference and CI are also reported descriptively
- *Regulatory:* orphan drug designation confirmed at approval; no FDA Statistical/Multi-Discipline Review posted on Drugs@FDA as of September 2026 (approval was roughly three weeks before this census entry was written); no FDA advisory committee meeting identified

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 1: Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, multicenter, placebo-controlled trial in 63 adults with FOP confirmed by an ACVR1 FOP-causing mutation (95% R206H). Patients were randomized to garetosmab 10 mg/kg (N=23), garetosmab 3 mg/kg (N=19), or placebo (N=21), given intravenously every 4 weeks for 56 weeks via infusion pump; 61 of the 63 patients continued into a double-blind extension phase on their original assigned treatment.
- Baseline: median age 25 years (range 18-42); 60% female; 67% White, 30% Asian, 19% Hispanic or Latino, 2% Black or African American; mean baseline CAJIS (Cumulative Analog Joint Involvement Scale) score 13 (range 0-19, scale 0-30).
- Primary efficacy endpoint: number of new HO lesions at Week 56 by whole-body low-dose CT, with the treatment effect summarized as an estimated rate ratio vs. placebo.
- Key secondary endpoints: number of clinician-assessed flare-ups through Week 56; proportion of patients with any new HO lesion at Week 56; total volume of new HO lesions at Week 56; occurrence of patient-reported flare-ups.
- Results — new HO lesions: 19 total lesions across 5/21 (24%) placebo patients vs. 2 total lesions in 2/23 (9%) patients on 10 mg/kg (rate ratio 0.10, 95% CI 0.01-0.76; 90% reduction) and 1 total lesion in 1/19 (5%) patients on 3 mg/kg (rate ratio 0.06, 95% CI 0-0.73; 94% reduction), both flagged in the label as "statistically significant (multiplicity-adjusted p-value <0.05)."
- Results — flare-ups through Week 56: 9 events (10 mg/kg), 53 events (3 mg/kg), 66 events (placebo); rate ratio vs. placebo 0.12 (95% CI 0.03-0.42) for 10 mg/kg and 0.85 (95% CI 0.26-2.73) for 3 mg/kg — only the 10 mg/kg result reflects a clear treatment effect.
- Results — total new HO lesion volume at Week 56: 10.5 cm³ (placebo) vs. 0.02 cm³ (10 mg/kg) and 0.01 cm³ (3 mg/kg); mean differences vs. placebo of −10.4 cm³ for both doses (95% CI −27.5, −0.3) were explicitly reported as "not statistically significant based on the pre-specified Wilcoxon rank-sum test," despite the descriptive confidence interval not crossing zero — an apparent inconsistency the label does not reconcile, most plausibly reflecting a rank-based test on a small, zero-inflated sample behaving differently from the reported parametric mean-difference CI.
- Occurrence of patient-reported flare-ups was not significantly different between garetosmab and placebo groups.

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2026/761508Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/761508Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical/Multi-Discipline Review — not posted on Drugs@FDA as of September 2026; direct-pattern checks at accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761508Orig1s000{StatR,MedR,SumR,CrossR,MultidisciplineR,IntegratedR,ClinPharmR}.pdf all return HTTP 404
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05394116 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)
- Pivotal publication: no Phase 3 (Study 1) results publication was identified via PubMed as of September 2026, consistent with the August 19, 2026 approval date. For background only (not the pivotal trial for this approval): the predecessor Phase 2 LUMINA-1 trial (NCT03188666) was published as Di Rocco M, Forleo-Neto E, Pignolo RJ, et al. "Garetosmab in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 trial." *Nat Med.* 2023;29(10):2615-2624. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-023-02561-8), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37770652/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Garetosmab%20in%20fibrodysplasia%20ossificans%20progressiva%20a%20randomized%20double-blind%20placebo-controlled%20phase%202%20trial)

**Other resources**

- Regeneron participates in general cross-industry/company data-sharing arrangements; trial-specific IPD availability for Study 1 was not individually confirmed here.
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was identified for this application; none is referenced in the approval letter or label.
- Orphan drug designation is confirmed in the FDA approval letter ("Because this drug product for this indication has an orphan drug designation...").

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

No genuine sponsor SAP, protocol, or FDA Statistical/Multi-Discipline Review is publicly posted for this application as of September 2026 — Drugs@FDA lists only the Label and Approval Letter for BLA 761508, and ClinicalTrials.gov lists no documents for NCT05394116. The following is reverse-engineered from the approved label (Package Insert §14, Clinical Studies).

**Reverse-engineered SAP**

- *[inferred, Package Insert §14]* The primary analysis of the count endpoint (new HO lesions at Week 56) is reported only as a "rate ratio" with a confidence interval for each dose vs. placebo — a summary statistic characteristic of a log-linear count-regression model (e.g., negative binomial or Poisson regression with an exposure-time offset) rather than a simple proportion or t-test comparison; the exact model family is not stated in the label.
- *[inferred, Package Insert §14]* The label's parenthetical "(multiplicity-adjusted p-value <0.05)" attached only to the primary HO-lesion-count result implies a prespecified multiple-testing correction across the two active-dose-vs-placebo comparisons and/or across the primary and key secondary endpoint family, but neither the specific procedure (e.g., Hochberg step-up, fixed-sequence, graphical) nor exactly which comparisons it spans is disclosed.
- *[inferred, Package Insert §14]* The flare-up endpoint uses the same rate-ratio framework as the HO-lesion endpoint, but no adjusted p-value is reported for the 3 mg/kg result (rate ratio 0.85, 95% CI 0.26-2.73), which did not reach significance — consistent with only the 10 mg/kg arm clearing whatever multiplicity-adjusted threshold the SAP specified.
- *[inferred, Package Insert §14]* The non-significant total-HO-lesion-volume result is explicitly attributed to "the pre-specified Wilcoxon rank-sum test," indicating the SAP specified a non-parametric method for this particular secondary endpoint — plausibly because lesion volume in a 63-patient trial is a heavily zero-inflated, right-skewed measure poorly suited to a parametric mean-difference test, even though the label also reports a descriptive mean difference and CI.
- *[inferred, Package Insert §14]* No stratification factor for randomization is disclosed in the label's Clinical Studies section (unlike the atacicept and zilganersen entries in this batch, where stratification factors are explicitly named), suggesting either no formal stratification was used in this trial or that level of SAP detail simply was not carried into the label.

### 63. Zilganersen (Zanvastro) — NDA 220210

**Sponsor:** Ionis Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of Alexander disease in pediatric and adult patients

**Approval date:** September 3, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** Study 1, NCT04849741 — double-blind, randomized, controlled Main Study (N=49, ages 2-65) plus a 4-patient open-label substudy in children under 2 years

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* small (Main Study N=49; total N=53 with the open-label substudy), randomized (2:1 within ascending-dose cohorts), double-blind, controlled, multi-part Phase 1-3 trial in an ultra-rare pediatric/adult leukodystrophy population, with randomization stratified by age, motor-symptom onset, and a gross-motor-abnormality criterion — an instance of the taxonomy's existing "Small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population" entry
- *Endpoints:* percent change from baseline in gait speed (10-meter walk test) at Week 61 in the ambulatory Stratum 1 subgroup (primary); Gross Motor Function Measure-88 (GMFM-88) Dimension D+E combined score change at Week 61 in the 2-4-year-old subgroup (prespecified alternate endpoint); plasma GFAP reduction as a pharmacodynamic/target-engagement biomarker
- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA on percent change in gait speed from baseline to Week 61, with treatment group and baseline value as covariates
- *Missing data/bias:* label states the "ANCOVA model used prespecified imputation methods that utilized all patients in the primary analysis" (n=17 zilganersen 50 mg, n=13 control) — the specific imputation method (e.g., multiple imputation, LOCF, a reference-based approach) is not named in the label
- *Regulatory:* Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher granted at approval; orphan drug designation; New Molecular Entity, Priority Review; no FDA Statistical/Multi-Discipline Review posted as of September 2026; no advisory committee meeting identified

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 1 (NCT04849741): a multicenter trial combining a double-blind, randomized, controlled Main Study (N=49, ages 2-65) with an open-label substudy in 4 patients under 2 years old; total planned duration up to 274 weeks (6-week screening; 60-week double-blind period ending at Week 61; 60-week open-label period; 120-week long-term extension; 28-week post-treatment follow-up). All patients had Alexander disease confirmed by clinical phenotype, brain MRI, and a pathogenic GFAP gene variant.
- During the double-blind period, patients 2 years and older were enrolled into two ascending-dose cohorts (25 mg, n=8; 50 mg, n=24) and randomized 2:1 within each cohort to intrathecal zilganersen every 12 weeks or control (n=17 total controls across both cohorts).
- Randomization stratification: Stratum 1 = patients ≥5 years old, or (if ≥18) with onset of motor symptoms within 5 years and a demonstrated gross-motor-skills abnormality; Stratum 2 = all other enrolled patients. The formal primary endpoint was evaluated only in Stratum 1; secondary endpoints were assessed across the full randomized Main Study population (both strata). Patients aged 2-4 (a subset of Stratum 2) were evaluated on a prespecified alternate motor endpoint rather than gait speed.
- Baseline (randomized population, n=49): median age 11 years; mean gait speed (10-meter walk test) 1.2 m/sec; 65% female, 86% White, 8% other/multiple races, 6% Asian, 10% Hispanic or Latino; 12 patients enrolled in the 25 mg cohort and 37 in the 50 mg cohort.
- Primary endpoint (Stratum 1, 50 mg vs. control): difference in mean percent change in gait speed (10-meter walk test) from baseline to Week 61. Result: −2.1% (zilganersen 50 mg) vs. −35.4% (control); adjusted least-squares mean difference 33.3% (95% CI 1.44, 65.25), p=0.041, favoring zilganersen — i.e., near-arrested gait-speed decline on treatment vs. continued decline on control.
- Alternate endpoint (2-4-year-old subgroup, n=4 zilganersen vs. n=3 control): change from baseline to Week 61 in the GMFM-88 Dimension D (standing) plus Dimension E (walking, running, jumping) combined score; the zilganersen group showed an observed improvement while the control group showed an observed decline (least-squares mean difference 22.9, SE 5.2) — descriptive only, given the N=7 total in this subgroup.
- Pharmacodynamic biomarker: plasma GFAP (an indirect measure of target engagement) — geometric mean ratio to baseline 33.6% lower with zilganersen vs. control at Week 61 (after 5 doses).
- Statistical method: ANCOVA with treatment group and baseline value as covariates for the primary endpoint; per the label, "the ANCOVA model used prespecified imputation methods that utilized all patients in the primary analysis (n=17 ZANVASTRO 50 mg, n=13 Control)" — i.e., the full randomized/dosed 50-mg-vs-control comparison population was retained via imputation rather than analyzed as observed/complete cases only.
- Safety: no boxed warning; the principal safety signal called out in patient counseling is aseptic meningitis, consistent with an intrathecally administered antisense oligonucleotide.

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2026/220210Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/220210Orig1s000lbl.pdf
- FDA Statistical/Multi-Discipline Review — not posted on Drugs@FDA as of September 2026; direct-pattern checks at accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/220210Orig1s000{StatR,MedR,SumR,CrossR,MultidisciplineR,IntegratedR,ClinPharmR}.pdf all return HTTP 404
- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04849741 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)
- Pivotal publication: no results publication for Study 1 was identified via PubMed as of September 2026 (searches on "zilganersen," "ION373," and "Alexander disease" combined with antisense/GFAP terms returned only unrelated reviews and pharmacodynamic-biomarker papers), consistent with the September 3, 2026 approval date and this being a very recently completed ultra-rare-disease trial.

**Other resources**

- Ionis Pharmaceuticals has an established antisense-oligonucleotide development franchise, but no trial-specific IPD-sharing confirmation was identified for Study 1; general participation in cross-industry data-sharing platforms was not confirmed here.
- A Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher was granted at approval, per the FDA approval letter ("we also inform you that you have been granted a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher, as provided under section 529 of the FD&C Act").
- No FDA advisory committee meeting was identified for this application.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

No genuine sponsor SAP or protocol, and no FDA Statistical/Multi-Discipline Review, is publicly posted for this application as of September 2026 — Drugs@FDA lists only the Label and Approval Letter for NDA 220210, and ClinicalTrials.gov lists no documents for NCT04849741. The following is reverse-engineered from the approved label (Package Insert §14, Clinical Studies).

**Reverse-engineered SAP**

- *[inferred, Package Insert §14, Figure 3 footnote]* "The p-value was estimated from an ANCOVA model with treatment group and Baseline value as covariates" — establishes the primary analysis as a standard baseline-adjusted ANCOVA on percent change in gait speed at a single fixed timepoint (Week 61), not a rank-based test or a mixed-model-repeated-measures approach, despite gait speed having been measured longitudinally across the double-blind period.
- *[inferred, Package Insert §14, Figure 3 footnote]* "The ANCOVA model used prespecified imputation methods that utilized all patients in the primary analysis (n=17 ZANVASTRO 50 mg, n=13 Control)" — indicates the 50-mg-vs-control primary comparison required imputation to retain all n=17/n=13 patients, meaning some of the 24 (50 mg) and 17 (control) randomized/enrolled patients had incomplete Week-61 gait-speed data; the specific imputation method (e.g., multiple imputation, last-observation-carried-forward, a reference-based method) is not named in the label.
- *[inferred, Package Insert §14]* The trial's two-stratum design — with the formal primary endpoint restricted to Stratum 1 and a distinct, prespecified "alternate endpoint" (GMFM-88) reserved for the youngest (2-4-year-old) subgroup — implies the SAP anticipated that a walking-speed measure would not be assessable or interpretable in the youngest, potentially non-ambulatory or pre-ambulatory patients, and built in a developmentally appropriate substitute endpoint for that subgroup rather than excluding them from all efficacy analysis.
- *[inferred, Package Insert §14]* No multiplicity adjustment is described for the coexistence of the formal Stratum 1 primary endpoint, the descriptive 2-4-year-old alternate endpoint, and the plasma GFAP biomarker; the absence of any stated correction suggests these were treated as a primary/exploratory hierarchy, with the alternate endpoint and biomarker as supportive/descriptive rather than co-primary or multiplicity-controlled comparisons.
- *[inferred, Package Insert §14]* Given the small dose-cohort sizes (25 mg, n=8; 50 mg, n=24) and the 2:1 randomization within each cohort, the SAP most plausibly prespecified the 50-mg-vs-control comparison as the sole confirmatory analysis (consistent with 50 mg being the labeled recommended dosage), with the 25 mg cohort serving a dose-ranging/exploratory role rather than a second formally tested comparison — the label reports no formal statistical result for the 25 mg arm alone.

## Immunology / Rheumatology / Dermatology

### 1. Belimumab (Benlysta) — BLA 125370

**Sponsor:** Human Genome Sciences, Inc. (co-developed with GlaxoSmithKline)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adult patients with active, autoantibody-positive systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) who are receiving standard therapy — the first new drug approved for SLE in approximately 50 years (since hydroxychloroquine in 1955)

**Approval date:** March 9, 2011

**Pivotal trial:** BLISS-52 (HGS1006-C1057), NCT00424476, and BLISS-76 (HGS1006-C1056), NCT00410384

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 1:1:1 parallel-group, multicenter, international phase 3 trials (52-week BLISS-52 and 76-week BLISS-76), two co-identical dose arms (belimumab 1 mg/kg and 10 mg/kg) plus placebo, all on top of standard-of-care SLE therapy; randomization stratified by baseline SELENA-SLEDAI score (6-9 vs. ≥10), proteinuria level, and race (African/indigenous-American descent vs. other)

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint SLE Responder Index (SRI, later termed SRI-4) response at Week 52 — a multi-instrument composite requiring simultaneous ≥4-point reduction from baseline in SELENA-SLEDAI, no new BILAG A / no more than one new BILAG B organ-domain score, and no worsening (<0.30-point increase) in Physician's Global Assessment (PGA); SRI response at Week 76 elevated to a major secondary endpoint for BLISS-76 at FDA's recommendation

- *Primary analysis:* stratified logistic regression (treatment group, baseline SELENA-SLEDAI category, baseline proteinuria category, race) on the modified intent-to-treat (mITT) population (all randomized subjects who received ≥1 dose); non-responder imputation for dropouts/protocol-defined "medication failures" before Week 52

- *Multiplicity:* step-down sequential testing across the two belimumab doses — 10 mg/kg vs. placebo tested first (two-sided alpha=0.05); only if significant was 1 mg/kg vs. placebo tested; no multiplicity adjustment across the numerous secondary endpoints, which were tested only supportively

- *Missing data/bias:* subjects who discontinued before Week 52, or whose concurrent SLE-medication changes triggered a protocol-defined "medication failure" rule, were counted as SRI non-responders regardless of clinical status

- *Regulatory:* FDA Arthritis Advisory Committee meeting held November 16, 2010 (Summary Minutes document this meeting; exact vote count not independently confirmed in the documents reviewed for this entry); novel primary endpoint (SRI) developed specifically because earlier SLE trials using single-instrument endpoints (SLEDAI alone or BILAG alone) had repeatedly failed to detect treatment effects — *Multi-instrument composite responder index requiring simultaneous success across ≥3 independently validated disease-activity instruments, developed prospectively in response to a history of failed single-instrument SLE trial endpoints*

**Trial design & endpoints**

- BLISS-52 and BLISS-76 were near-identically designed phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials in adults with active SLE (SELENA-SLEDAI ≥6) on stable standard therapy (antimalarials, NSAIDs, corticosteroids up to 40 mg/day, or immunosuppressives); ten inclusion and nineteen exclusion criteria were protocol-specified. Subjects were randomized 1:1:1 to IV belimumab 1 mg/kg, 10 mg/kg, or placebo, dosed on Days 0, 14, 28, then every 28 days through Week 52 (BLISS-52, n=867) or Week 76 (BLISS-76, n=826, per the FDA statistical review's "eight hundred twenty-six subjects were randomized")

- Primary endpoint: SRI response at Week 52, a composite requiring (1) ≥4-point reduction from baseline SELENA-SLEDAI, (2) no new BILAG A or no more than one new BILAG B organ-domain score, and (3) no worsening (increase <0.30 points) in PGA — all three components had to be met simultaneously for a subject to be scored a responder

- Primary analysis: stratified logistic regression with treatment group, baseline SELENA-SLEDAI category, baseline proteinuria category, and race as covariates, in the mITT population; step-down testing of 10 mg/kg vs. placebo first, then 1 mg/kg vs. placebo only if the higher dose was significant, both at two-sided alpha=0.05

- Results (per FDA's statistical review): belimumab (both doses pooled and individually) achieved statistically significantly higher SRI response rates than placebo in both studies (p=0.02 for BLISS-76/Study 1056 and p=0.0006 for BLISS-52/Study 1057, comparing the pooled/highest-performing arms as characterized in the review); subcomponents of the SRI were numerically higher for belimumab across both studies. No multiplicity correction was planned for the numerous secondary endpoints (prednisone-sparing, lupus flares) since these were tested only if the primary endpoint reached significance; the Week-76 SRI response was elevated to a "major secondary endpoint" for BLISS-76 specifically at FDA's request

- An independent Data Monitoring Committee reviewed safety only (not efficacy) after the first 100 combined subjects reached Day 56, then approximately every four months; no interim efficacy look and no associated alpha adjustment was made

- The primary composite endpoint (SRI) was purpose-built for this program: earlier SLE trials (including an earlier belimumab phase 2 trial and prior lupus programs industry-wide) had failed using conventional single-instrument endpoints (SLEDAI alone, BILAG alone), which were considered insufficiently sensitive to detect a treatment effect against a background of fluctuating, multi-organ disease activity. Furie et al. (2009) developed and reported the SRI methodology — validated post hoc against the phase 2 belimumab trial data — combining SLEDAI (global disease-activity reduction), BILAG (organ-specific worsening ceiling), and PGA (no worsening), explicitly designed to require broad, simultaneous improvement rather than any single measure's isolated change

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review and Evaluation, BLA 125370, Executive Summary]* — "Studies 1056 and 1057 adequately demonstrate that the proportion of subjects achieving SRI [response is higher for belimumab than placebo]" (quoted fragment; surrounding words affected by the PDF's letter-dropping extraction artifact and omitted here rather than guessed).

**Reverse-engineered SAP** [inferred]

- [inferred] The primary estimand was almost certainly defined as the treatment policy effect on SRI response at Week 52 in all randomized/dosed subjects (mITT), given FDA's statistical review explicitly describes non-responder imputation for dropouts and "medication failures," and describes the primary analysis population as mITT — traced to the review's Sections 2/3 design description and Table-based SRI response reporting.

- [inferred] The step-down dose-testing procedure (10 mg/kg vs. placebo tested first, unlocking 1 mg/kg vs. placebo only if significant) was almost certainly the pre-specified type-I-error-control method for the two-dose, one-placebo design, consistent with FDA's review language describing sequential dose comparisons at two-sided alpha=0.05 — traced to the review's description of the primary efficacy analysis and the absence of any Bonferroni/Hochberg-style parallel adjustment across doses.

- [inferred] The SRI's three-component structure (SLEDAI + BILAG + PGA) was deliberately designed so no single instrument alone could drive a false-positive responder classification, directly responsive to the pattern of earlier failed lupus trials that used SLEDAI or BILAG in isolation — traced to the rationale given in Furie et al. 2009's development/validation paper and reflected in FDA's adoption of the same composite as the regulatory primary endpoint for both BLISS trials.

### 2. Belatacept (Nulojix) — BLA 125288

**Sponsor:** Bristol-Myers Squibb

**Indication approved:** Prophylaxis of organ rejection in adult patients receiving a kidney transplant, in combination with basiliximab induction, mycophenolate mofetil, and corticosteroids — restricted to Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-seropositive recipients

**Approval date:** June 15, 2011

**Pivotal trial:** BENEFIT, NCT00256750, and BENEFIT-EXT, NCT00114777

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two randomized, active-controlled (cyclosporine), open-label(-ish; blinded central adjudication where feasible), parallel-group, multicenter, international phase 3 trials, each with 3 arms — belatacept more-intensive (MI) regimen, belatacept less-intensive (LI) regimen, and cyclosporine — in standard-criteria/living-donor kidney recipients (BENEFIT) or extended-criteria-donor (ECD) kidney recipients (BENEFIT-EXT)

- *Endpoints:* three co-primary endpoints at Month 12 assessed independently (not combined into one composite): (1) composite patient/graft survival, (2) a composite renal-impairment endpoint (measured GFR <60 mL/min/1.73m² at Month 12, or a ≥10 mL/min/1.73m² decrease in mGFR from Month 3 to Month 12), and (3) incidence of acute rejection

- *Primary analysis:* each of the three co-primary endpoints tested independently for each belatacept regimen (MI, LI) vs. cyclosporine, without a single combined hierarchy across the three endpoints — *Transplant tri-component co-primary endpoint set (patient/graft survival, composite renal impairment, acute rejection incidence), each independently powered/tested rather than combined into a single hierarchy or composite*

- *Multiplicity:* no single formal multiplicity-controlled hierarchy spanning all three co-primary endpoints and two belatacept regimens was identified in the public literature/label; each endpoint-by-regimen comparison reported its own p-value/CI

- *Regulatory:* approval restricted to EBV-seropositive recipients because belatacept carries a boxed warning for post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder (PTLD), particularly CNS PTLD, observed at higher rates in EBV-seronegative recipients during the pivotal program

**Trial design & endpoints**

- BENEFIT enrolled adult recipients of a kidney from a living or standard-criteria deceased donor; BENEFIT-EXT enrolled recipients of extended-criteria-donor (ECD) kidneys (a higher-risk population for graft dysfunction). Both were 3-arm, randomized, phase 3 trials comparing a more-intensive (MI) and a less-intensive (LI) belatacept-based regimen against a cyclosporine-based regimen, with all arms also receiving basiliximab induction, mycophenolate mofetil, and corticosteroids

- Co-primary endpoints at Month 12 (assessed independently, not as a single composite hierarchy): (1) composite patient/graft survival; (2) a composite renal-impairment endpoint defined as the percentage of subjects with measured GFR (mGFR) <60 mL/min/1.73m² at Month 12, or a decrease in mGFR ≥10 mL/min/1.73m² from Month 3 to Month 12; (3) incidence of acute rejection

- BENEFIT results (Vincenti et al. 2010): Month-12 patient/graft survival was similar across arms (MI 95%, LI 97%, cyclosporine 93%); both belatacept regimens showed superior renal function on the composite renal-impairment endpoint (MI 55%, LI 54%, cyclosporine 78%; p≤0.001 for MI or LI vs. cyclosporine) and higher mean mGFR (65, 63, and 50 mL/min for MI, LI, cyclosporine respectively; p≤0.001); belatacept arms had a higher incidence and grade of acute rejection (MI 22%, LI 17%, cyclosporine 7%)

- BENEFIT-EXT results (Durrbach et al. 2010): Month-12 patient/graft survival was similar (MI 86%, LI 89%, cyclosporine 85%); fewer belatacept-treated ECD recipients met the composite renal-impairment endpoint (MI 71%, LI 77%, cyclosporine 85%; p=0.002 MI vs. cyclosporine, p=0.06 LI vs. cyclosporine); mean mGFR was 4-7 mL/min higher on belatacept (p=0.008 MI vs. cyclosporine); acute rejection incidence was similar across arms (MI 18%, LI 18%, cyclosporine 14%)

- Both trials found posttransplant lymphoproliferative disorder (PTLD), including CNS PTLD, occurred more frequently in belatacept-treated arms — the safety finding underlying the boxed warning and the EBV-seropositive-only approved population

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

No genuine sponsor SAP/protocol text is public (not posted to ClinicalTrials.gov; the FDA Statistical/Medical/Summary Reviews are almost entirely redacted under the (b)(4) trade-secret exemption, unusually so even for a 2011-era BLA). All statistical-method content below is reverse-engineered from the peer-reviewed publications.

**Reverse-engineered SAP** [inferred]

- [inferred] Each of the three co-primary endpoints (patient/graft survival; composite renal impairment; acute rejection incidence) was almost certainly tested independently per regimen-vs-cyclosporine comparison, each with its own point estimate/CI/p-value, rather than combined under a single alpha-controlled hierarchy — traced to the publications' presentation of each endpoint with a separate p-value per comparison and no stated joint significance threshold or gatekeeping order.

- [inferred] The composite renal-impairment endpoint's two-part definition (mGFR<60 at Month 12 OR a ≥10 mL/min/1.73m² mGFR decline from Month 3 to Month 12) functions as an "OR"-composite (a subject need meet only one of the two mechanically different renal-decline criteria to be scored a treatment "failure" on this endpoint) — traced directly to the endpoint definition reported identically in both BENEFIT and BENEFIT-EXT abstracts/publications.

- [inferred] Analysis population was very likely all randomized-and-transplanted subjects (an ITT-like population), given 12-month patient/graft survival, renal-impairment, and acute-rejection rates are reported for essentially the full randomized cohort in both publications with no substantial per-arm exclusions described.

### 3. Ingenol mebutate (Picato) — NDA 202833

**Sponsor:** LEO Pharma (Leo Pharmaceuticals)

**Indication approved:** Topical field treatment of actinic keratosis (AK) — originally approved for two anatomically distinct regimens: 0.015% gel for face/scalp (3 consecutive days) and 0.05% gel for trunk/extremities (2 consecutive days)

**Approval date:** January 23, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** Four phase 3 trials — Study 016 (PEP005-016, NCT00916006) and Study 025 (PEP005-025, NCT00915551) for face/scalp; Study 014 (PEP005-014, NCT00742391) and Study 028 (PEP005-028, NCT00942604) for trunk/extremities

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* four near-identical, randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter (US + Australia) phase 3 trials, run as two co-identical pairs (one pair per anatomic location/dose/regimen), each 1:1 randomized and stratified by site (and, for the head trials, by anatomic sub-location target of ~80% face/~20% scalp); Special Protocol Assessment (SPA) agreement reached with FDA for the non-head-location design in June 2008, before the head-location trials were designed by extension of the same agreed template

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint complete clearance rate of AK lesions in the treatment area at Day 57 (binary, no clinically visible AK lesions); secondary endpoint partial clearance rate (≥75% reduction in lesion count) at Day 57, gated behind primary-endpoint significance

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by site, on the intent-to-treat (ITT) population with last-observation-carried-forward (LOCF)/treatment-failure imputation for missing Day-57 assessments; supportive per-protocol (PP) analysis

- *Multiplicity:* no multiplicity adjustment across the two co-identical trials per location (each analyzed and reported independently); secondary (partial clearance) endpoint tested only if the primary (complete clearance) endpoint reached significance — fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing between primary and secondary within each trial

- *Missing data/bias:* missing/out-of-window Day-57 assessments imputed as treatment failures (LOCF), agreed with FDA at the End-of-Phase-2 meeting as the primary imputation method, with a caveat that (because efficacy was assessed only at Baseline and Day 57) this imputation is nearly indistinguishable from simply counting dropouts as failures

- *Regulatory:* approved under a June 2008 Special Protocol Assessment for the non-head-location pivotal design; post-approval safety signal (non-melanoma skin cancer, including reports of rapidly growing cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma) led the EMA to withdraw the EU marketing authorization for ingenol mebutate in 2020, and FDA subsequently required a new Section 5.3 "Non-Melanoma Skin Cancer" Warnings and Precautions labeling change under FDCA Section 505(o)(4) (added March 2021); as of this writing both Picato strengths (0.015% and 0.05%) are listed as **Discontinued** in Drugs@FDA's marketing-status field, i.e. the product is no longer marketed in the US

**Trial design & endpoints**

- The sponsor initially sought approval only for non-head (trunk/extremities) AK and reached a Special Protocol Assessment with FDA (June 2, 2008) for a "multi-site, randomized, parallel-group, double-blind, vehicle-controlled study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of 0.05% PEP005 Topical Gel" applied once daily for 2 consecutive days; this design was then extended by the sponsor to a second, face/scalp-specific pair of trials at 0.015% gel applied once daily for 3 consecutive days, agreed at an End-of-Phase-2 meeting (June 3, 2009)

- Both face/scalp trials (Study 016, n=269; Study 025, n=278) enrolled adults with 4-8 clinically typical, discrete AK lesions in a contiguous 25 cm² area on the head, randomized 1:1 to PEP005 0.015% gel or vehicle, stratified by site and by anatomic sub-location (target ~80% face/~20% scalp); both trunk/extremities trials (Study 014, n=255; Study 028, n≈205 based on reported arm sizes of 100+103+126+129) enrolled adults with 4-8 AK lesions in a 25 cm² area on nonhead locations (predominantly arm/back-of-hand, ~87% of subjects), randomized 1:1 to PEP005 0.05% gel or vehicle, stratified by site and anatomic location; Study 014 used a dynamic (minimization-style) randomization already underway when FDA later suggested a simpler method, while Study 028 used simple block randomization per FDA's subsequent recommendation

- Primary endpoint (all four trials): complete clearance rate of AK lesions in the treatment area at Day 57, defined as no clinically visible AK lesions; secondary endpoint: partial clearance rate (≥75% reduction from baseline lesion count) at Day 57, tested only if the primary endpoint was significant (no formal alpha-splitting needed since it is a strict gate)

- Analysis: CMH test stratified by site on the ITT population (all randomized subjects), with LOCF imputation for missing Day-57 assessments; a pre-specified Breslow-Day test for site-by-treatment heterogeneity, with a sensitivity analysis dropping the most extreme site(s) if significant

- Results per FDA's statistical review (reviewer's own reanalysis): Study 016 complete clearance 37% (PEP005) vs. 2.2% (vehicle), p<0.0001; Study 025 complete clearance 47.2% vs. 5.2%, p<0.0001; Study 014 (nonhead) complete clearance 27.8% (35/126) vs. 4.7% (6/129), p<0.001; Study 028 complete clearance 42.0% (42/100) vs. 4.9% (5/103), p<0.001. Partial-clearance secondary results were also significant in both head trials (Study 016: 60% vs. 6.7%, p<0.0001; Study 025: 67.6% vs. 8.1%, p<0.0001)

- Post-marketing long-term safety follow-up studies (conducted per FDA's End-of-Phase-2 request that all subjects be followed ≥1 year for recurrence/safety) subsequently identified a non-melanoma skin cancer signal in ingenol-mebutate-treated skin areas; this evidence, reviewed cumulatively by EMA, led to the drug's EU withdrawal in 2020, and FDA required a corresponding US labeling update in 2021 rather than a market withdrawal at that time — the product was nonetheless discontinued from the US market at some point thereafter per Drugs@FDA's current marketing-status listing

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 202833, §2.1 Overview, Reference ID 3046458]* — "The proposed dose regimen (once daily for two consecutive days) and the primary efficacy endpoint 'Complete clearance rate of AK lesions defined as the proportion of subjects at the Day 57 visit with no clinically visible AK lesions in the selected treatment area' is acceptable."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.1.1 Study design]* — "The primary endpoint was defined in the protocol as the complete clearance rate of AK lesions at the Day 57 visit. Subjects were considered complete clearance if there were no clinically visible AK lesions in the selected treatment area. The secondary endpoint was defined as partial clearance rate of AK lesions at the Day 57 visit. Subjects were considered partial clearance if they achieved a reduction of at least 75% in the number of clinically visible AK lesions... No multiplicity adjustment was planned as the secondary endpoint would be tested only if the primary endpoint was significant."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, nonhead-location review, Executive Summary, Reference ID 3045557]* — "PEP005 topical gel, 0.05% was statistically superior to vehicle gel in two studies (PEP005-014 and PEP005-028) in the treatment of AK on nonhead locations. The primary efficacy endpoint was the complete clearance rate of AK lesions; defined as the proportion of subjects at Day 57 with no clinically visible AK lesions in the selected treatment area."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, End of Phase 2 Meeting minutes excerpt, §2.1]* — "The Agency noted that all subjects, regardless of AE status, should be followed for at least one year after the primary efficacy time point, to obtain recurrence and safety data." — this Agency-mandated long-term follow-up requirement is the direct regulatory ancestor of the later post-marketing evidence base that fed into the 2020 EU withdrawal and 2021 US labeling change.

*[verbatim, FDA Supplement Approval Letter, NDA 202833/S-013, March 2021]* — "This 'Changes Being Effected' supplemental new drug application provides response to our letter dated January 7, 2021, notifying you, under Section 505(o)(4) of the FDCA, of new safety information that we believe should be included in the labeling for PICATO. This information pertains to the risk of non-melanoma skin cancers."

### 4. Tofacitinib (Xeljanz) — NDA 203214

**Sponsor:** Pfizer Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adult patients with moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis (RA) who have had an inadequate response or intolerance to methotrexate — the first Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor approved for any indication, and the first oral targeted synthetic DMARD approved for RA

**Approval date:** November 6, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** ORAL Solo (A3921045), NCT00814307; ORAL Standard (A3921064), NCT00853385; ORAL Sync (A3921046), NCT00856544; ORAL Scan (A3921044), NCT00847613; and A3921032 (TNF-inadequate-responder trial), NCT00960440

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* five phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trials differing in background therapy/population (monotherapy in ORAL Solo; background methotrexate with an adalimumab active-comparator arm in ORAL Standard; background non-biologic DMARD in ORAL Sync; background methotrexate with 2-year radiographic follow-up in ORAL Scan; background methotrexate in TNF-inadequate responders in A3921032); placebo patients advanced (rescued) to tofacitinib at Month 3 (all placebo non-responders) and/or Month 6 per trial, blinding maintained via a pre-determined blinded treatment sequence

- *Endpoints:* per-study fixed-sequence primary-endpoint set tested in order — (1) ACR20 response (at Month 3 for ORAL Solo/A3921032; Month 6 for ORAL Standard/ORAL Sync/ORAL Scan), (2) change from baseline in HAQ-DI, (3) proportion achieving DAS28-4(ESR) <2.6; ORAL Scan added a co-primary radiographic endpoint (change from baseline in van der Heijde-modified Total Sharp Score at Month 6), tested first in that trial's four-endpoint sequence

- *Primary analysis:* ACR20/DAS28 analyzed via normal-approximation test for the difference in binomial proportions with non-responder imputation (baseline-observation-carried-forward, "BOCF"/NRI) for missing/discontinued/advanced patients; HAQ-DI analyzed via MMRM (compound-symmetry working covariance, no imputation, missing-at-random assumption); modified Total Sharp Score analyzed via ANCOVA with linear-extrapolation imputation for missing radiographs

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) gatekeeping across the ordered primary-endpoint list within each trial, combined with a within-endpoint step-down across the two doses (10 mg BID tested before 5 mg BID, or vice versa per trial); FDA's Statistical Review explicitly flagged as a major statistical issue that "the proposed sequential test appears not to control family-wise type 1 error rate" — i.e., FDA did not simply accept the sponsor's multiplicity-control claim at face value

- *Regulatory:* FDA Arthritis Advisory Committee convened May 9, 2012 (10 voting members) and returned multiple separate votes: 8-2 that the radiographic (structural-damage) data were *not* adequate; 10-0 that efficacy on signs/symptoms and quality of life was demonstrated; 7-2 that safety data (particularly for the 5 mg dose) were adequate, conditioned on long-term postmarketing data; and 8-2 overall for approval of the 5 mg dose specifically, with changes to the proposed indication — the 10 mg BID dose was not part of the recommended approval; a boxed warning was added roughly a decade later (2021) based on the dedicated postmarketing safety trial ORAL Surveillance (see note below)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Five phase 3 trials (A3921032, A3921044, A3921045, A3921046, A3921064) shared a common analytic backbone — randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled comparison of tofacitinib 5 mg BID and 10 mg BID — but differed in population (TNF-inadequate responders in A3921032; DMARD-inadequate responders as monotherapy in ORAL Solo/A3921045; MTX-inadequate responders with an adalimumab 40 mg SC Q2W active-comparator arm in ORAL Standard/A3921064; non-biologic-DMARD-inadequate responders on background DMARD in ORAL Sync/A3921046; and MTX-inadequate responders followed 2 years with radiographic assessment in ORAL Scan/A3921044)

- Four of the five trials (1032, 1045, 1046, 1064) had three ordered primary endpoints — ACR20 at Month 3 or 6, HAQ-DI change from baseline, and DAS28-4(ESR) <2.6 — while ORAL Scan (1044) had four, adding structural preservation (modified Total Sharp Score) as the second endpoint in its sequence; a step-down gatekeeping procedure required each endpoint to reach significance before the next in the sequence could be formally claimed, applied within each of the two doses

- Missing-data handling differed by endpoint type: binary ACR20/DAS28 endpoints used non-responder imputation for any patient with a missing assessment, an adverse-event or lack-of-efficacy dropout, or advancement to a new treatment in the placebo-rescue sequence; HAQ-DI used an MMRM model under a missing-at-random assumption with no imputation; radiographic (mTSS) endpoints used linear extrapolation from available radiographs for patients who advanced or withdrew before their scheduled assessment

- FDA's independent reanalysis reproduced the sponsor's primary and secondary efficacy results with no material deviations, but identified and had the sponsor correct a DAS28 calculation error (the sponsor had used physician's rather than subject's global assessment in the formula) that did not propagate to other efficacy endpoints; FDA's review separately flagged, as a major statistical issue, that the sponsor's proposed sequential (gatekeeping) testing procedure across doses and endpoints "appears not to control family-wise type 1 error rate," requiring further discussion beyond the sponsor's original proposal

- **Post-marketing safety note (not part of the original efficacy SAP, but essential trial-design context):** a decade after approval, FDA required Pfizer to conduct ORAL Surveillance (A3921133, NCT02092467), a randomized, active-comparator (TNF-inhibitor), non-inferiority postmarketing-requirement safety trial in RA patients ≥50 years old with ≥1 cardiovascular risk factor, comparing tofacitinib 5 mg and 10 mg BID against a TNF inhibitor for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and malignancy. The trial found tofacitinib failed to meet its pre-specified non-inferiority margin for both MACE and malignancy versus the TNF inhibitor, leading FDA to require a Boxed Warning (2021) for increased risk of serious cardiovascular events, malignancy, thrombosis, and death across the entire JAK-inhibitor drug class, and to restrict tofacitinib's (and other JAK inhibitors') RA/psoriatic-arthritis/ulcerative-colitis indications to patients who have had an inadequate response or intolerance to one or more TNF blockers

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §2.1.3/2.1.4, Reference ID 3150054]* — "The Arthritis Advisory Committee convened on May 9, 2012 to discuss the efficacy and safety of tofacitinib 5 mg and 10 mg doses. The 10-member committee discussed the efficacy of treatment on signs and symptoms, quality of life, and radiographic structural damage progression, as well as potential safety signals including malignancy, serious infections and laboratory abnormalities. The committee voted 8 to 2 that the available radiographic data were not adequate but voted 10 to 0 that efficacy has been demonstrated for signs and symptoms and quality of life in patients with rheumatoid arthritis. The committee voted 7 to 2 that the available data for safety (particularly in the 5 mg dose group) were adequate, but asked for long term postmarketing data. Overall, they voted 8 to 2 for approval (5 mg dose) with changes to the indication."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §2.1.4]* — "Following is a list of statistical issues found in the submission: 1. Robustness of efficacy data... 2. Multiplicity adjustment – proposed sequential test appears not to control family-wise type 1 error rate."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Table 1/§3.2.1, summary of study design]* — "Studies 1032, 1045, 1046, and 1064 have three primary efficacy endpoints (in sequence): 1. Signs and symptoms as measured by ACR20 at Month 3 (studies 1032 and 1045) or at Month 6 (studies 1046 and 1064); 2. Physical function as measured by the HAQ-DI change from baseline at Month 3; 3. Incidence of DAS <2.6 at Month 3 (Studies 1045 and 1032) or at Month 6 (Studies 1046 and 1064). Study 1044 has four primary efficacy endpoints (in sequence): 1. Signs and symptoms as measured by ACR20 at Month 6; 2. Structural preservation as measured by modified Total Sharp score (mTSS) at Month 6; 3. Physical function as measured by the HAQ-DI change from baseline at Month 3; 4. Incidence of DAS <2.6 at Month 6."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2]* — "For the binary endpoints such as ACR20 and DAS28 at Month 3 or Month 6, the normal approximation for the difference in binomial proportions was used to compare treatment difference. Missing values due to a patient dropping from the study for any reason... will be set to nonresponsive (that is, baseline observation carried forward, BOCF) on or after Month 3 visit. This also goes by the name Non Responder Imputation (NRI)... Because there were multiple doses and multiple endpoints being tested, a gatekeeping or step-down approach was pre-specified to control the probability of type 1 error."

### 5. Apremilast (Otezla) — NDA 205437

**Sponsor:** Celgene Corporation

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adult patients with active psoriatic arthritis (PsA)

**Approval date:** March 21, 2014

**Pivotal trial:** PALACE 1 (CC-10004-PSA-002), NCT01172938; PALACE 2 (CC-10004-PSA-003), NCT01212757; PALACE 3 (CC-10004-PSA-004), NCT01212770

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* three near-identical, multicenter, international, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group phase 3 trials, each 1:1:1 to apremilast 20 mg BID (A20), apremilast 30 mg BID (A30), or placebo, with a titration period during the first 7 days; concurrent stable background DMARD therapy (methotrexate, sulfasalazine, or leflunomide) permitted; blinded early-escape mechanism at Week 16 for inadequate responders (<20% joint-count improvement), with placebo-arm early-escapers re-randomized 1:1 (blinded) to A20 or A30; at Week 24 all remaining placebo patients crossed over to A20/A30 under a blinded re-randomization

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint modified ACR20 response at Week 16 (originally planned for Week 24, revised to Week 16 by agreement with FDA in mid-2012); key secondary endpoint change from baseline in HAQ-DI at Week 16; PALACE 3 added a psoriasis-skin-lesion population/endpoint given its enrollment of patients with qualifying skin involvement

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test (stratified by baseline DMARD use, and for PALACE 3 also by baseline body-surface-area psoriasis involvement ≥3%) for ACR20; ANCOVA (baseline value as covariate, same strata) for HAQ-DI; non-responder imputation for ACR20 at Week 16 for missing data, extended at Week 24 to also impute early-escape patients as non-responders

- *Multiplicity:* Hochberg procedure controlling Type I error across the two doses within each endpoint (both A30-vs-placebo and A20-vs-placebo significant at 0.05, or one significant at 0.025), combined with a fixed-sequence hierarchy across endpoints (primary ACR20, then key secondary HAQ-DI, then other secondary endpoints in a pre-specified order) — FDA's review explicitly notes that endpoints below a hierarchy step that failed (e.g., enthesitis at Week 16 in some trials) were "only exploratory" with "nominal" p-values that underestimate Type I error

- *Regulatory:* FDA's Statistical Review found apremilast 30 mg statistically significant for both primary and key secondary endpoints across all three trials, while apremilast 20 mg reached significance for the primary endpoint in all three trials but for the key secondary (HAQ-DI) in only two of three — the reviewer explicitly framed approval of the lower (20 mg) dose as potentially justifiable "if apremilast 30 mg poses large additional risks to safety," though 30 mg was the dose ultimately approved; substantial differential dropout (~70% of placebo patients discontinued before Week 24) undermined the interpretability of Week-24 "sustained effect" claims beyond ACR20

**Trial design & endpoints**

- PALACE 1, 2, and 3 were multicenter, international, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials in adults with active PsA despite prior DMARD therapy (with prior TNF-blocker failure capped at ≤10% of enrollment per trial); subjects were randomized 1:1:1 to A20, A30, or placebo, with dosage titrated over the first 7 days (10→20 mg for A20; 10→20→30 mg for A30) using visually identical blister cards to preserve blinding

- Endpoints were originally planned for Week 24 assessment but were revised, per FDA agreement communicated June 29, 2012, to be tested at Week 16 instead — primary endpoint modified ACR20 (including distal interphalangeal joints, 78 tender/76 swollen joints assessed) and key secondary change from baseline HAQ-DI, both at Week 16

- Statistical methodology: CMH test for ACR20 and other binary endpoints, ANCOVA for HAQ-DI and other continuous endpoints, both stratified by baseline DMARD use (and additionally by baseline BSA-psoriasis involvement ≥3% in PALACE 3/Study 4); Type I error controlled within each endpoint via the Hochberg procedure across the two apremilast doses, and across endpoints via a pre-specified testing hierarchy (primary, then key secondary, then other secondary endpoints in the order listed in the protocol appendix)

- Results (FDA reviewer's summary): apremilast 30 mg produced an average ~18-percentage-point ACR20 treatment effect over placebo at Week 16 across the three trials (statistically significant in all three) and an average HAQ-DI treatment difference of about -0.14 (also significant in all three); apremilast 20 mg was statistically significant for ACR20 in all three trials but for HAQ-DI in only two of the three trials — the reviewer characterized evidence for an incremental benefit of 30 mg over 20 mg as "suggestive but not conclusive or even consistent"

- Because early-escape and Week-24 crossover of placebo patients eroded the placebo comparator (approximately 70% of placebo-arm patients discontinued their initially randomized treatment before Week 24), FDA's review treated Week-24 claims of sustained effect as confirmed for ACR20 specifically, but undermined for other secondary endpoints by this loss of adequate control

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Executive Summary, Reference ID 3410358]* — "This submission demonstrates benefits of apremilast 30 mg tablets compared to placebo for the treatment of adult patients with active PsA. Three randomized double blinded placebo controlled parallel arm Phase 3 trials show that apremilast 30 mg provides statistically significant benefits compared to placebo for the primary endpoint ACR 20 at week 16 (average 18%) as well as for the key secondary endpoint ΔHAQ-DI at week 16 (average -0.14)."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Executive Summary]* — "Evidence for additional efficacy benefits of apremilast 30 mg over apremilast 20 mg are suggestive but not conclusive or even consistent... Approval of apremilast 20 mg rather than apremilast 30 mg may therefore be justifiable if apremilast 30 mg poses large additional risks to safety compared to apremilast 20 mg."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §2.1.2]* — "The sponsor proposed three multicenter, international, randomized, double-blind, parallel group Phase 3 studies, CC-10004-PSA-002, -003, and -004 (studies 2, 3, and 4), to compare to placebo (P), after 24 weeks of treatment, two doses of apremilast, 20 mg bid (A20) and 30 mg bid (A30), with primary endpoint ACR20 analyzed using the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test and key secondary endpoint change from baseline HAQ-DI analyzed using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA)... To control Type I error for testing multiple doses, the sponsor proposed using the Hochberg procedure, with an analysis hierarchy to control Type 1 error when testing statistical significance of multiple endpoints."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2]* — "Control of Type I error within each endpoint was maintained using the Hochberg procedure. In particular, pairwise comparisons were made between A30 and P and between A20 and P, with differences considered statistically significant if both comparisons were significant at the 0.05 level or if one comparison was significant at the 0.025 level. Endpoints were tested in a hierarchy, with the primary endpoint tested first, then the key secondary endpoint, followed by other secondary endpoints in the order listed in the Appendix."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §3.2.4.1]* — "A large number of proposed claims were based on endpoints in the analysis hierarchy below failed significance tests on enthesitis at week 16. Because analyses of these endpoints were only exploratory, tests of their statistical significance were considered only nominal, with p-values underestimating the probability of Type I error."

### 6. Secukinumab (Cosentyx) — BLA 125504

**Sponsor:** Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation

**Indication approved:** Treatment of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in adult patients who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy — the first interleukin-17A (IL-17A) inhibitor approved for any indication

**Approval date:** January 21, 2015

**Pivotal trial:** ERASURE (Trial 2302 / A2302), NCT01365455, and FIXTURE (Trial 2303 / A2303), NCT01358578

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, international phase 3 trials — ERASURE was 3-arm (secukinumab 300 mg, 150 mg, placebo); FIXTURE was 4-arm, adding an EU-sourced etanercept active-comparator arm; both used lyophilized-formulation (LYO) secukinumab, subcutaneous, with an induction schedule followed by monthly maintenance dosing; randomization stratified by geographic region and baseline body weight (<90 kg vs. ≥90 kg)

- *Endpoints:* co-primary endpoints PASI 75 response and Investigator's Global Assessment (IGA) modified 2011 score of 0 or 1 (with ≥2-grade improvement), both at Week 12 vs. placebo; key secondary endpoints included PASI 90 at Week 12, and (in FIXTURE only) non-inferiority then superiority testing of secukinumab vs. etanercept on PASI 75 and superiority on IGA 0/1 at Week 12, plus maintenance-of-response comparisons vs. etanercept at Week 52

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by geographic region and baseline body-weight stratum for the co-primary binary endpoints; ANCOVA (with the same stratification factors plus baseline value as covariate) for continuous patient-reported-outcome secondary endpoints (itch, pain, scaling, each on an 11-point numeric rating scale); non-responder imputation for missing binary efficacy data

- *Multiplicity:* **graphical alpha-propagation method (Maurer-Bretz)**, per Bretz et al. 2009 — family-wise error rate set at 0.05, with alpha initially split 0.025/0.025 between the two co-primary hypotheses (PASI75, IGA0/1) for each dose, propagating along a pre-specified graph to secondary hypotheses (PASI 90, then PRO endpoints of pain/itch/scaling) only as earlier nodes in the graph were rejected, with unused alpha reallocated across the two dose-specific hypothesis families if an entire family was rejected; FIXTURE's graph additionally incorporated etanercept non-inferiority (margin -10% on PASI 75) and superiority hypotheses

- *Regulatory:* although both the 150 mg and 300 mg doses were statistically superior to placebo on both co-primary endpoints in both trials, the sponsor sought and FDA approved only the 300 mg dose, because it produced consistently larger (roughly 10-percentage-point) responses than 150 mg on both co-primary and secondary endpoints; FDA's review separately flagged, as a study-quality caveat (not an efficacy concern), that FIXTURE's large multi-center design with a required minimum enrollment per site was not consistently achieved (many sites enrolled only 1-2 subjects per arm), limiting the ability to assess center-to-center variability

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ERASURE (Trial 2302, n=738, 86 sites) and FIXTURE (Trial 2303, n=1306, 154 sites) enrolled adults ≥18 years with moderate-to-severe chronic plaque-type psoriasis (PASI ≥12, IGA ≥3, BSA involvement ≥10%); both trials randomized to secukinumab 300 mg, 150 mg, and placebo (ERASURE) or to those three arms plus EU-sourced etanercept (FIXTURE), with randomization stratified by geographic region and baseline weight (<90 kg vs. ≥90 kg) via IVRS/IWRS

- The protocol-specified co-primary endpoints were PASI 75 response and IGA 0/1 (with ≥2-grade improvement) at Week 12, tested via CMH test stratified by region and weight; four core hypotheses were defined per trial (H1-H4: each of the two doses vs. placebo on each of the two co-primary endpoints)

- Type I error was controlled across this expanding hypothesis set using the graphical approach of Bretz et al. (2009): the family-wise alpha (0.05) was split 0.025/0.025 within each dose's pair of co-primary hypotheses, with further testing of that dose's secondary hypotheses (PASI 90, then Psoriasis Diary pain/itch/scaling) permitted only if both co-primary hypotheses for that dose were rejected, and with provision to pass any unused alpha across the two dose-specific hypothesis families if an entire family was rejected. FIXTURE's graph additionally embedded etanercept comparisons: a non-inferiority test of secukinumab vs. etanercept on PASI 75 (margin -10%), followed by superiority tests vs. etanercept on PASI 75 and IGA 0/1 at Week 12, and maintenance-of-response superiority tests at Week 52

- Results (co-primary endpoints, Week 12): both secukinumab doses were superior to placebo (p<0.0001) in both trials; in FIXTURE, secukinumab (both doses) also established non-inferiority to etanercept on PASI 75 and, per the sponsor's pre-specified sequential testing, superiority findings against etanercept as well, "although the applicant only sought approval for the 300 mg dose because the secukinumab 300 mg dose yielded about 10% higher responses for the co-primary as well as for the secondary endpoints compared to those for the 150 mg dose"

- FDA's review recommended use of the Intent-to-Treat analysis set (all randomized, medication-dispensed subjects) over the sponsor's proposed Full Analysis Set (all subjects to whom treatment was assigned) as the primary analysis population, per Agency advice letters dated July 12 and November 16, 2011, and July 6, 2012

"Secukinumab in plaque psoriasis--results of two phase 3 trials." *N Engl J Med.* 2014;371(4):326-338. **SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Executive Summary, Reference ID 3623211]* — "Secukinumab (AIN457) 300 mg and 150 mg in lyophilisate in vial (LYO) were superior to placebo... (2302 and 2303) with one trial that included an etanercept arm... The co-primary endpoints were the proportion of subjects achieving PASI 75 response (i.e., ≥ 75% reduction in PASI score) at Week 12 and scoring IGA 0 or 1 at Week 12."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Executive Summary]* — "As for safety, adverse events were comparable across both the 300 mg and 150 mg doses of secukinumab, and both doses were superior to placebo in achieving PASI 75, and IGA 0 or 1 at Week 12. However, the applicant is only seeking approval for the 300 mg dose, because the secukinumab 300 mg dose yielded about 10% higher responses for the co-primary as well as for the secondary endpoints compared to those for the 150 mg dose."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2]* — "The protocol-specified co-primary endpoints were: The proportion of subjects with PASI 75 at Week 12; The proportion of subjects with IGA of 0 or 1 at Week 12 with at least a 2-grade improvement on the IGA. The protocol specified the primary analysis method of the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by geographical region and body weight stratum."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2]* — "To control the Type I error rate, the protocol specified the graphical approach of Bretz et al. (2009) where the family-wise error was set at 0.05. Using this method, within each pair of (H1, H3) and (H2, H4), the α was equally split at 0.025, and only if both hypotheses of a pair were rejected, the testing sequence could continue... If all hypotheses within a set referring to a secukinumab dose regimen were to be rejected... then the approach allows that the corresponding Type I error rate to be passed onto the other group of hypotheses, and if needed, retested at a new significance level."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2, analysis-set discussion]* — "The sponsor used the FAS as the primary analysis set; however, the Agency recommended (Advice letters dated: 7/12/2011, 11/16/2011 and 7/6/2012) the Intent to Treat (ITT) analysis set defined as all randomized subjects, dispensed of medication."

### 7. Mepolizumab (Nucala) — BLA 125526

**Sponsor:** GlaxoSmithKline

**Indication approved:** Add-on maintenance treatment of severe eosinophilic asthma in patients aged ≥12 years — the first anti-interleukin-5 (IL-5) biologic approved for any indication

**Approval date:** November 4, 2015

**Pivotal trial:** MENSA (Study 88/MEA115588, NCT01691521) and SIRIUS (Study 75/MEA115575, NCT01691508)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, international phase 3 trials with different regimens and objectives — MENSA (exacerbation-reduction trial, 32 weeks, 3-arm: mepolizumab 75 mg IV, 100 mg SC, or placebo, added to standard of care) and SIRIUS (oral-corticosteroid-sparing trial, 24 weeks including a 3-4 week OCS-optimization run-in, 2-arm: mepolizumab 100 mg SC or placebo, with a mandatory OCS down-titration schedule); a supportive Phase 2b dose-ranging trial (Study 97/DREAM, IV doses 75/250/750 mg vs. placebo) preceded both and informed dose selection

- *Endpoints:* MENSA primary endpoint — rate of clinically significant asthma exacerbations over 32 weeks; SIRIUS primary endpoint — percent reduction in daily oral corticosteroid (OCS) dose from baseline to Weeks 20-24 while maintaining asthma control, analyzed via an ordinal categorical variable (0%, >0-<50%, 50-<75%, 75-<90%, 90-100% reduction)

- *Primary analysis:* MENSA — generalized linear model with negative binomial distribution, covariates treatment, baseline OCS use, region, prior-year exacerbation count, and baseline disease severity, with log(time-on-study) as an offset; a linear trend test across doses was required to be significant before individual dose-vs-placebo comparisons were tested; SIRIUS — proportional odds (ordinal logistic regression) model with covariates treatment, years on OCS (<5 vs. ≥5), region, and baseline OCS dose (*proportional-odds/ordinal-logistic-regression model for a categorical percent-dose-reduction responder endpoint*)

- *Multiplicity:* Hochberg-type truncated hierarchical procedure for MENSA (a significant overall dose-trend test gated all further individual-dose-vs-placebo comparisons; those comparisons then followed a pre-specified ordered hierarchy: exacerbation rate → FEV1/AQLQ at Week 52 → AQLQ alone → hospitalization/ED-visit exacerbation rate → ACQ-6, with p-values below a failed step in the hierarchy reported only as nominal); no formal multiplicity adjustment described for SIRIUS's single primary endpoint

- *Missing data/bias:* SIRIUS assigned patients who withdrew prematurely, or who did not maintain asthma control between Weeks 20-24, a rank/category corresponding to a worse OCS-reduction outcome than any observed value ("worst-rank" imputation), with a tipping-point-style sensitivity analysis (all mepolizumab withdrawals counted as treatment failures) to probe robustness — FDA noted the sponsor's approach deviated from the Division's recommendation to continue data collection on withdrawn patients

- *Regulatory:* FDA Pulmonary-Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee meeting held June 11, 2015, which the Statistical Review cites directly on the reliability of enrollment-criterion blood-eosinophil-count data (historical counts were often patient-reported rather than derived from medical records)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- MENSA enrolled patients ≥12 years old with severe eosinophilic asthma (blood eosinophils ≥150 cells/µL at screening or ≥300 cells/µL in the prior year) on high-dose inhaled corticosteroid plus additional controller therapy, with ≥2 exacerbations in the prior year; randomized to mepolizumab 75 mg IV, 100 mg SC, or placebo, added to standard of care, for 32 weeks

- SIRIUS enrolled a similarly eosinophil-selected, OCS-dependent population (prednisone 5-35 mg/day), with a 3-5 week run-in during which OCS dose was optimized to the lowest tolerated level before randomization to mepolizumab 100 mg SC or placebo for 24 weeks; post-randomization OCS dose then followed a predefined step-down schedule unless specific loss-of-control criteria were met (e.g., mean AM peak flow <80% of baseline stability limit, ACQ-5 increase ≥0.5, rescue-medication-use thresholds, symptoms of adrenal insufficiency)

- Result (MENSA, FDA reviewer's Table 9): annual exacerbation rate was 1.7 (placebo) vs. 0.9 (75 mg IV, rate ratio 0.5, p<0.0001) vs. 0.8 (100 mg SC, rate ratio 0.5, p<0.0001) — roughly a 47-53% relative reduction versus placebo, with no evidence of a meaningfully larger benefit at higher doses in the supportive DREAM dose-ranging data

- Result (SIRIUS): the proportional-odds analysis of percent OCS-dose-reduction categories favored mepolizumab over placebo; per-category results (e.g., proportion achieving 90-100% reduction) were reported by age and other subgroups, with the FDA reviewer noting effect-modification signals (e.g., a statistically significant treatment-by-age [<40 vs. ≥40 years] interaction) that warranted labeling discussion

- The FDA reviewer's overall assessment found the pre-specified type-I-error control plan for MENSA "questionable" on methodological grounds specific to the linear-trend-then-pairwise-comparison structure, though this did not change the conclusion that both mepolizumab doses reduced exacerbations

- Package Insert / Label (original, 2015) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2015/125526s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Statistical Review, BLA 125526 (Statistical Reviewer Robert Abugov, PhD; Reference ID 3790390) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/125526Orig1s000StatR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov records — MENSA: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01691521 · SIRIUS: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01691508 (no sponsor protocol/SAP posted in either Documents tab)

- Pivotal publication (MENSA): Ortega HG, Liu MC, Pavord ID, et al. "Mepolizumab treatment in patients with severe eosinophilic asthma." *N Engl J Med.* 2014;371(13):1198-1207. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1403290), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25199059/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Mepolizumab%20treatment%20in%20patients%20with%20severe%20eosinophilic%20asthma%20MENSA)

- Pivotal publication (SIRIUS): Bel EH, Wenzel SE, Thompson PJ, et al. "Oral glucocorticoid-sparing effect of mepolizumab in eosinophilic asthma." *N Engl J Med.* 2014;371(13):1189-1197. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1403291), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25199060/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Oral%20glucocorticoid-sparing%20effect%20of%20mepolizumab%20in%20eosinophilic%20asthma%20SIRIUS)

- FDA Pulmonary-Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee meeting held June 11, 2015; the Statistical Review cites this meeting specifically regarding the reliability of patient-reported historical eosinophil-count enrollment criteria, not a formal up-or-down vote on approvability.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2.2, p.11]* — "Analysis of the primary endpoint, exacerbation rate, first evaluated a linear trend test for decrease in exacerbation rate as a function of mepolizumab dose. Then, if the trend was significant at the 0.05 level, each dose was tested against placebo. Exacerbation rates were analyzed using a generalized linear model with negative binomial distribution having independent factors treatment, OCS usage at baseline, region, number of exacerbations in year prior to study, and baseline disease severity (% predicted FEV1). The planned offset variable was logarithm of time on treatment."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2.2, p.11]* — "Type 1 error across these comparisons was to be controlled at the 0.05 level by a truncated Hochberg procedure. First, tests of individual doses against placebo were conducted only if the overall linear trend test across doses (including placebo) was statistically significant."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2.4, p.14]* — "Comparison of M100 SC and placebo for percent reduction of daily prednisone dose while maintaining asthma control was analyzed using a proportional odds model with the following categories of percent reduction: 0%, >0% to <50%, 50% to <75%, 75% to 90%, and 90% to 100%. The model included independent variables treatment, number of years on OCS (< 5 years, ≥ 5 years), region, and baseline OCS dose."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2.4, p.14-15]* — "Contrary to Division recommendations, data collection was not continued on patients who withdrew from treatment. Instead, patients who withdrew prematurely or who did not maintain asthma control between weeks 20 and 24 were assigned a rank corresponding to the worst OCS percent reduction category. To examine the robustness of treatment results to patient withdrawal from treatment, tipping point analyses were conducted in which all mepolizumab patients who withdrew were considered treatment failures."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, p.39]* — "As alluded to on page 142 of the applicant's clinical study report, and confirmed during the June 11, 2015 Advisory Committee meeting for this drug, such historical blood counts were often patient reported rather than derived from medical records."

### 8. Ixekizumab (Taltz) — BLA 125521

**Sponsor:** Eli Lilly and Company

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy — second anti-IL-17A biologic approved (after secukinumab)

**Approval date:** March 22, 2016

**Pivotal trial:** UNCOVER-1 (Trial RHAZ/I1F-MC-RHAZ), UNCOVER-2 (Trial RHBA/I1F-MC-RHBA), UNCOVER-3 (Trial RHBC/I1F-MC-RHBC)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* three randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, international phase 3 trials in moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis (PASI≥12, sPGA≥3, BSA≥10%); UNCOVER-1 was 3-arm (ixekizumab Q2W, ixekizumab Q4W, placebo); UNCOVER-2 and UNCOVER-3 were 4-arm, adding a US-licensed (Enbrel) or EU-approved etanercept active-comparator arm depending on study site; all ixekizumab arms received a 160 mg loading dose at baseline followed by 80 mg Q2W or Q4W through Week 12; UNCOVER-1 and UNCOVER-2 continued into a 48-week maintenance/re-randomization period

- *Endpoints:* co-primary endpoints at Week 12 — proportion achieving sPGA 0/1 (clear/minimal, with ≥2-point improvement) and proportion achieving PASI 75; secondary endpoints included sPGA 0, PASI 90, PASI 100, and a ≥4-point improvement on an itch Numeric Rating Scale (NRS)

- *Primary analysis:* non-responder imputation (NRI) applied to the ITT population for the co-primary and secondary binary endpoints, compared via (per the FDA review's hypothesis numbering) a pre-specified sequence of statistical tests per trial

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence hierarchical testing spanning up to 16 ordered hypotheses per trial (both doses × co-primary endpoints × secondary endpoints × — for UNCOVER-2/3 — non-inferiority-then-superiority comparisons against etanercept and maintenance-of-response comparisons at Week 12/Week 60), each hypothesis tested only if all hypotheses above it in the sequence were rejected

- *Missing data/bias:* UNCOVER-2's etanercept arm was dosed with US-licensed Enbrel at US sites and EU-approved etanercept at non-US sites (except 30 subjects); the FDA review specifically assessed whether pooling these two etanercept sources was appropriate for the sponsor's claim of superiority versus etanercept, since the comparator arm was not a single uniform product across the trial

- *Regulatory:* substantial evidence of effectiveness from three adequate and well-controlled trials; UNCOVER-2/UNCOVER-3 additionally supported comparative-effectiveness superiority claims against an active biologic already marketed for the same indication

**Trial design & endpoints**

- UNCOVER-1 (RHAZ, n=1296: 433 Q2W / 432 Q4W / 431 placebo), UNCOVER-2 (RHBA, n=1224: 351 Q2W / 347 Q4W / 358 etanercept / 168 placebo), and UNCOVER-3 (RHBC, n=1346: 385 Q2W / 386 Q4W / 382 etanercept / 193 placebo) enrolled adults ≥18 years with moderate-to-severe chronic plaque psoriasis (≥6 months' duration) at PASI≥12, sPGA≥3, BSA≥10%

- Result (FDA reviewer's Table 1, ITT/NRI): sPGA 0/1 at Week 12 — RHAZ 82%(Q2W)/76%(Q4W)/3%(placebo); RHBA 83%/73%/2%(placebo); RHBC 81%/75%/7%(placebo). PASI 75 at Week 12 — RHAZ 89%/83%/4%; RHBA 90%/78%/2%; RHBC 87%/84%/7%. All ixekizumab-vs-placebo and (in RHBA/RHBC) ixekizumab-vs-etanercept comparisons were statistically significant (p<0.001) for all endpoints in Table 1

- Because RHBA and RHBC used both US-licensed Enbrel (at US sites) and EU-approved etanercept (at non-US sites, except 30 subjects who received the other source) for the active-comparator arm, the FDA review specifically evaluated whether results were consistent between the pooled comparator population and the US-only (Enbrel-only) subset before accepting the pooled superiority comparison

For all three trials, both dose regimens of TALTZ were statistically superior (p-values < 0.001) to placebo for all of the efficacy endpoints listed in Table 1."

In both trials, all subjects randomized to etanercept at US study sites received US-licensed Enbrel.
