**Note on Keyword_Taxonomy.md:** the mixed active-comparator-product-sourcing pattern here (a single "etanercept" trial arm actually dosed with two different regulatory-approved formulations of the same molecule, split by site geography, with FDA separately checking result consistency by comparator source) does not appear to already be captured in the taxonomy's Trial design or Missing data/bias sections. Flagged as "": *Active-comparator arm sourced from two different national formulations of the same approved biologic, split by site geography, with FDA-conducted consistency check across comparator sources*.

### 9. Reslizumab (Cinqair) — BLA 761033

**Sponsor:** Teva Respiratory, LLC (originally developed by Cephalon/Ception Therapeutics)

**Indication approved:** Add-on maintenance treatment of severe eosinophilic asthma in adults with elevated blood eosinophils — second anti-IL-5 biologic approved (after mepolizumab), and the only one of the two originally approved via intravenous administration

**Approval date:** March 23, 2016

**Pivotal trial:** Study 3082 (C38072/3082, NCT01287039) and Study 3083 (C38072/3083, NCT01285323), two identically-designed 52-week exacerbation trials; supportive Study 3081 (C38072/3081, 16-week FEV1 trial) and Study 3084 (C38072/3084, 16-week FEV1 trial in an eosinophil-unselected population)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* four principal phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trials — two identically-designed, concurrently-conducted 52-week trials (3082, 3083) powered for exacerbation-rate reduction in an eosinophil-selected population (≥400 cells/µL at screening), plus two 16-week trials (3081, testing two IV doses [0.3 mg/kg, 3.0 mg/kg] in the same eosinophil-selected population; 3084, testing 3.0 mg/kg in an eosinophil-unselected population) powered for FEV1 change from baseline; primary efficacy analyses pre-specified to include all randomized subjects regardless of prohibited-medication use or discontinuation

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint for Studies 3082/3083 — frequency of clinical asthma exacerbations (independently adjudicated) over 52 weeks; primary endpoint for Studies 3081/3084 — absolute change from baseline in FEV1 at Week 16 (secondary endpoint in 3082/3083)

- *Primary analysis:* negative binomial regression with a log(time-on-study) offset for the exacerbation-rate endpoint (3082/3083); mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) for FEV1 change from baseline (3081, 3082, 3083); Study 3084's primary analysis specifically modeled the dependence of the reslizumab-vs-placebo FEV1 treatment difference on baseline blood eosinophil count (a pre-specified treatment-by-biomarker interaction test)

- *Missing data/bias:* not separately detailed beyond the ITT-based, all-randomized-subjects analysis population; independent event adjudication was used for the exacerbation endpoint to standardize event classification across the two replicate trials

- *Regulatory:* FDA advised the sponsor (End-of-Phase 2 meeting, August 18, 2010) that more than one dose should be evaluated and that patients across a spectrum of eosinophil counts should be studied so labeling could reflect the dependence of safety/benefit on baseline eosinophil count; Study 3084's negative result in an eosinophil-unselected population directly supported the eosinophil-based patient-selection language in the approved indication

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Studies 3082 and 3083 enrolled adults and adolescents (12-75 years) with asthma inadequately controlled on inhaled corticosteroids, elevated blood eosinophils (≥400 cells/µL at screening), and a history of exacerbations, randomized to reslizumab 3.0 mg/kg IV or placebo every 4 weeks for 52 weeks; the primary endpoint (frequency of clinical asthma exacerbations) used a consistent, independently adjudicated exacerbation definition across both trials, developed per "regulatory and expert guidance" discussed with the Division

- Result: reslizumab reduced the annualized exacerbation rate by 50% (Study 3082) and 59% (Study 3083) relative to placebo; reductions in events requiring oral corticosteroids (56%/60%) and systemic corticosteroids (55%/61%) were also reported; the reduction in exacerbations resulting in hospitalization/emergency-room visits (34%/31%) was not statistically significant in either trial; reslizumab also improved FEV1, ACQ, and AQLQ relative to placebo in both trials

- Study 3081 (supportive, 16 weeks) found average FEV1 improvements over placebo of 115 mL (0.3 mg/kg) and 160 mL (3.0 mg/kg); Study 3084 (supportive, eosinophil-unselected population) found no significant FEV1 benefit and no significant association between baseline eosinophil count and treatment effect in that unselected population — a negative finding that, per the FDA review, directly supports restricting the approved indication to patients with elevated blood eosinophils

- Package Insert / Label (original, 2016) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2016/761033s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Statistical Review, BLA 761033 (Statistical Reviewer Lan Zeng, MS; Reference ID 3874259) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/761033Orig1s000StatR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov records — Study 3082: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01287039 · Study 3083: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01285323 (no sponsor protocol/SAP posted in either Documents tab)

- Pivotal publication (pooled Studies 3082/3083): Castro M, Zangrilli J, Wechsler ME, et al. "Reslizumab for inadequately controlled asthma with elevated blood eosinophil counts: results from two multicentre, parallel, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trials." *Lancet Respir Med.* 2015;3(5):355-366. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S2213-2600(15)00042-9>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25736990/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Reslizumab%20for%20inadequately%20controlled%20asthma%20with%20elevated%20blood%20eosinophil%20counts)

**Other resources**

- No trial-specific Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere participation was independently confirmed for this program; not confirmed either way.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was identified for this application in the documents reviewed.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §1, Executive Summary, p.5]* — "Two identically-designed concurrently-conducted studies, 37082/3082 (referred to as 3082) and 37082/3083 (referred to as 3083), showed that reslizumab provided statistically significant benefit over placebo with regard to the primary endpoint, frequency of asthma exacerbations during 52 weeks of treatment period. Reslizumab reduced the annual rate of exacerbations by 50% and 59% relative to placebo in studies 3082 and 3083, respectively."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §2.1.2, p.6]* — "The primary analysis of exacerbations would employ a negative-binomial regression model with an offset to account for differences in study durations for each patient. ... Overall change from baseline in FEV1 over 16 weeks and change from baseline to each clinic visit would be analyzed using a mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) in studies 3081, 3082, and 3083. The primary analysis in study 3084 should evaluate dependence of the treatment difference between reslizumab and placebo groups on eosinophil count in change from baseline FEV1 at week 16."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §2.1.2, p.6-7]* — "The primary efficacy analyses should include all patients who were randomly assigned to a treatment, regardless of whether or not they took prohibited medications or discontinued treatment. ... the Division recommended to study patients across a spectrum of eosinophil counts and noted that labeling would take into account safety and treatment benefit dependence on baseline eosinophil count."

### 10. Crisaborole (Eucrisa) — NDA 207695

**Sponsor:** Anacor Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Topical treatment of mild-to-moderate atopic dermatitis in patients 2 years of age and older

**Approval date:** December 14, 2016

**Pivotal trial:** Trial 301 (AD-301) and Trial 302 (AD-302), two identically-designed phase 3 trials

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two identically-designed, randomized, multicenter, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group phase 3 trials (2:1 randomization to crisaborole 2% ointment or vehicle ointment, twice daily for 28 days) in patients ≥2 years old with atopic dermatitis, BSA involvement ≥5% (excluding scalp), and Investigator's Static Global Assessment (ISGA) of 2 (mild) or 3 (moderate); centers with low enrollment were pooled into combined "analysis centers" per a pre-specified minimum-enrollment rule before being used as a stratification factor

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint success in ISGA at Day 29, defined as ISGA 0 (clear) or 1 (almost clear) with ≥2-grade improvement from baseline; secondary endpoints ISGA 0/1 (regardless of grade-improvement magnitude) at Day 29, and time to ISGA success (Kaplan-Meier/log-rank), tested only if the first secondary endpoint was significant

- *Primary analysis:* logistic regression with treatment group and analysis center as factors, using Firth's penalized-likelihood correction (*Firth's penalized-likelihood logistic regression for a binary responder endpoint*), pre-specified to test a treatment-by-analysis-center interaction at the 0.10 level with a leave-one-center-out sensitivity analysis if that interaction was significant

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing between the two secondary endpoints (ISGA 0/1 tested first; time-to-success tested only if that endpoint was significant at 0.05), with no separate multiplicity correction needed between the primary and secondary family since the secondaries were gated behind the primary

- *Missing data/bias:* primary imputation method was Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) multiple imputation, performed separately within each treatment arm (140 imputed datasets for Trial 301, 135 for Trial 302), with two pre-specified sensitivity analyses — a repeated-measures logistic regression model (GEE) using all observed post-baseline visits with no imputation, and a separate model-based multiple-imputation approach (logistic regression imputation model with treatment and analysis center) (*arm-specific MCMC multiple imputation for a missing binary responder endpoint, cross-checked against a GEE repeated-measures model as a no-imputation sensitivity analysis*)

- *Regulatory:* substantial evidence of effectiveness from two adequate and well-controlled, identically-designed replicate trials; no Advisory Committee meeting identified

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Trial 301 (763 randomized: 507 crisaborole/256 vehicle, 47 US centers) and Trial 302 (764 randomized: 514 crisaborole/250 vehicle, 42 US centers) enrolled patients ≥2 years old with a clinical diagnosis of atopic dermatitis (BSA≥5% excluding scalp, ISGA 2 or 3), randomized 2:1 to crisaborole 2% ointment or vehicle ointment applied twice daily for 28 days

- Primary endpoint: ISGA success at Day 29 (ISGA 0 or 1 with ≥2-grade improvement from baseline), analyzed via logistic regression with treatment and analysis center as factors; result (ITT, MI-averaged): Trial 301 — 32.8% (crisaborole) vs. 25.4% (vehicle), p=0.038; Trial 302 — 31.4% vs. 18.0%, p<0.001

- Secondary endpoint (ISGA 0/1 regardless of grade improvement): Trial 301 — 51.7% vs. 40.6%, p=0.005; Trial 302 — 48.5% vs. 29.7%, p<0.001; median time to ISGA success could not be calculated in either trial because fewer than 50% of subjects in any arm achieved success, though the log-rank comparison of the time-to-event curves was significant (p<0.001) in both trials

- Missing binary ISGA outcome data were imputed via arm-specific MCMC multiple imputation as the pre-specified primary method, with GEE (no imputation, all observed visits) and an alternative logistic-regression-based multiple-imputation model as sensitivity analyses; the FDA reviewer's independent analysis reproduced the applicant's results

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jaad.2016.05.046), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27417017/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Efficacy%20and%20safety%20of%20crisaborole%20ointment%20atopic%20dermatitis)

**Other resources**

- No trial-specific Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere participation was independently confirmed for this program; not confirmed either way.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was identified for this application in the documents reviewed.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §1, Executive Summary]* — "The applicant submitted data from two identically-designed, randomized, multicenter, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group, pivotal Phase 3 trials (Trials 301 and 302). ... The protocol-specified primary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of subjects achieving success in ISGA at Day 29, where success in ISGA was defined as an ISGA score of 0 (clear) or 1 (almost clear) with at least a 2-grade improvement from baseline."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Table 1 footnote 3]* — "P-value from a logistic regression (using Firth's Penalized Likelihood) with treatment and analysis center as factors."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2]* — "The protocol specified the primary imputation method to be the multiple imputation (MI) approach. For each treatment arm separately, missing data was imputed using the Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method. The protocol specified the following two sensitivity analyses for the handling of missing data: Repeated-measures logistic regression model (GEE), with dichotomized ISGA success as the dependent variable and treatment, analysis center, and visit ... as independent factors. In this analysis, data from all post-baseline visits will be included with no imputation for missing data. Model-based multiple imputation method to impute missing data for the dichotomized ISGA data. The imputation model (i.e., logistic regression) will include treatment and analysis center."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2]* — "To control the Type I error rate for testing two secondary efficacy endpoints, the protocol specified analyzing these endpoints sequentially, where the 2nd secondary endpoint would only be tested if the 1st secondary endpoint was significant at the 0.05 level."

### 11. Brodalumab (Siliq) — BLA 761032

**Sponsor:** Valeant Pharmaceuticals Luxembourg S.à r.l. (via Valeant Pharmaceuticals North America LLC) — originally developed by Amgen Inc. (co-developed with AstraZeneca); see regulatory history below.

**Indication approved:** Moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in adults who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy.

**Approval date:** February 15, 2017.

**Pivotal trial:** AMAGINE-2, NCT01708603, and AMAGINE-3, NCT01708629 (identically designed, placebo- and ustekinumab-active-comparator-controlled); supportive placebo-only AMAGINE-1, NCT01708590.

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-comparator (ustekinumab)-controlled, parallel-group trials (AMAGINE-2/3); randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (AMAGINE-1)
- *Endpoints:* co-primary static Physician's Global Assessment (sPGA) 0/1 and PASI75 response vs. placebo at Week 12; PASI100 vs. ustekinumab (AMAGINE-2/3, Week 12); key secondary PASI100, sPGA 0, and Psoriasis Symptom Inventory (PSI) responder vs. placebo
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by baseline body weight (≤100 kg/>100 kg), prior biologic use, geographic region, and baseline value group
- *Multiplicity:* Bonferroni-based recycling framework (Burman-Sonesson-Guilbaud, *Stat Med* 2009) splitting two-sided alpha between a placebo family (α=0.01) and an ustekinumab family (α=0.04) for AMAGINE-2/3, with alpha from a family recycled to the other family if all hypotheses within it were rejected; AMAGINE-1 tested co-primaries at α=0.05 (placebo-only)
- *Regulatory:* boxed warning for suicidal ideation and behavior plus a REMS program required at approval; original co-developer Amgen discontinued the program in 2015 after a completed-suicide safety signal, licensing rights to Valeant/AstraZeneca; the pivotal trials were "not designed, and consequently not powered," to compare suicidal-ideation-and-behavior (SIB) or major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) between treatment arms

**Trial design & endpoints**

- All three trials enrolled adults 18-75 with stable moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis diagnosed ≥6 months prior, PASI≥12, sPGA≥3, BSA involvement ≥10%; brodalumab given as a loading dose of weekly injections for 2 weeks then 140 mg or 210 mg every 2 weeks (Q2W)
- AMAGINE-2 (N=1831) and AMAGINE-3 (N=1881) additionally randomized to an ustekinumab arm (dosed per US/EU label) and a weight-based brodalumab dosing arm (140 mg ≤100 kg / 210 mg >100 kg); AMAGINE-1 (N=661) was placebo-controlled only, with a randomized-withdrawal/retreatment design
- Co-primary endpoints (all three trials, Week 12, vs. placebo): proportion achieving sPGA 0/1, and proportion achieving PASI75 (≥75% reduction in PASI score); secondary endpoints: PASI100 (100% reduction), sPGA 0, and PSI responder
- In AMAGINE-2/3, for the comparison against ustekinumab at Week 12, the primary endpoint was PASI100, with sequential testing planned comparing brodalumab 210 mg vs. ustekinumab first
- Missing data handled via non-responder imputation (NRI); analysis population was all randomized subjects (ITT/FAS)
- Results: both brodalumab doses were superior to placebo on all co-primary and secondary endpoints at Week 12 (p<0.001); against ustekinumab, the 210 mg dose and the weight-based dosing were superior on PASI100 (p<0.001), but the 140 mg dose was not (p=0.078) in AMAGINE-3 — the FDA reviewer noted "there is no replication of study findings for the brodalumab 140 mg against ustekinumab for the PASI 100 endpoint"
- Sample size/power was not presented as a formal power calculation in the Statistical Review; the review states the safety database was not designed or powered to compare SIB/MACE rates between arms
- Safety signal driving the regulatory history: across all brodalumab clinical programs (psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, rheumatoid arthritis), 6 completed suicides occurred, all in brodalumab-exposed subjects (4 in the psoriasis program); FDA's dedicated safety consult found 35 SIB events among 4464 brodalumab users (0.78%; 95% CI 0.63-1.25), incidence rate 0.38/100 subject-years, with a 12-18-fold increase among subjects with a history of suicidality; MACE incidence was 1.1% (95% CI 0.83-1.49), with 9-fold and 4.7-fold increases in subjects with histories of ischemic heart disease and cardiac/vascular disorder, respectively

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, BLA 761032, Reference ID 3954002, p.27]* — "In all three trials, for the comparison of brodalumab against placebo at Week 12, the co-primary endpoints were the proportion of subjects achieving PASI 75 response (i.e., ≥75% reduction in PASI score) and a sPGA score of 0 or 1. Secondary endpoints were PASI 100 (i.e., 100% reduction in PASI score), sPGA score of 0, and Psoriasis Symptom Inventory (PSI) responder at Week 12. In Trials 03 and 04, for the comparison of brodalumab against ustekinumab at Week 12, the primary endpoint was PASI 100."

- *[verbatim, Reference ID 3954002, p.37]* — "To maintain the family-wise Type I error rate at 5%, the SAP for Trial 02 specified testing the co-primary endpoints at α=0.05, and the SAPs for Trials 03 and 04 specified that 'a combination of parallel, sequential, and Bonferroni-based recycling testing' was followed for the Week 12 primary and secondary endpoints. For Trials 03 and 04, the SAPs specified that the Week 12 primary and key secondary endpoints were tested in the placebo family at α=0.01 (2-sided) and in the ustekinumab family at α=0.04 (2-sided). If and only if the null hypotheses for all the primary and key secondary endpoints within either the placebo (α=0.01) or ustekinumab (α=0.04) family were rejected, the fraction of the overall alpha (either 0.01 or 0.04) allocated to that family were recycled to the testing of the hypotheses in the other family (Burman, C.-F., Sonesson, C., Guilbaud, O., A recycling framework for the construction of Bonferroni-based multiple tests. Statistics in Medicine, 2009; 28:739-61)."

- *[verbatim, Reference ID 3954002, p.54]* — "For the comparison of each brodalumab dose against placebo, both brodalumab doses were superior to placebo for all co-primary as well as secondary endpoints at Week 12 (p<0.001); however, for the comparison against ustekinumab, only the brodalumab 210 mg dose and the weight-based brodalumab dosing were superior to ustekinumab for the protocol-specified primary endpoints of PASI 100 (p<0.001), and the brodalumab 140 mg was not superior to ustekinumab for the PASI 100 response at Week 12 (p=0.078) in Trial 3. Consequently, there is no replication of study findings for the brodalumab 140 mg against ustekinumab for the PASI 100 endpoint." The review's overall conclusion (p.54, §5.2): "Although the findings from three pivotal trials (Trials 02, 03, and 04) support the efficacy of brodalumab 210 mg for the treatment of adults with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis, given the safety concerns related to SIB and MACE events, the benefit-risk of brodalumab use should be taken into account."

- *[verbatim, Reference ID 3955202, pp.6-7]* — "In total, 35 SIB events occurred in 4464 brodalumab users (0.78%; 95% CI: 0.63–1.25) and the follow-up time adjusted incidence rate was 0.38 per 100 subject-years (95% CI: 0.27–0.53). The incidence of MACE among 4273 subjects exposed to brodalumab was 1.1% (95% CI: 0.83–1.49)... The subgroup analysis of SIB incidence rate by history of suicidality resulted in a 12–18 fold increase among subjects with history compared to those without. Similarly, the subgroup analysis of MACE incidence rate by (1) history of ischemic heart diseases and (2) history of cardiac or vascular disorder yielded a 9-fold and 4.7-fold increase, respectively, among subjects with history compared to those without."

- *[verbatim, Reference ID 3955202, p.10]* — "Because the PsO program was not designed, and consequently not powered, to compare the treatment arms with respect to the safety outcomes, we did not conduct statistical testing."

### 12. Dupilumab (Dupixent) — BLA 761055

**Sponsor:** Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (co-developed with Sanofi).

**Indication approved:** Treatment of moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis in adult patients whose disease is not adequately controlled with topical prescription therapies or when those therapies are not advisable — the first biologic approved for atopic dermatitis.

**Approval date:** March 28, 2017.

**Pivotal trial:** SOLO 1 (Study R668-AD-1334), NCT02277743, and SOLO 2 (Study R668-AD-1416), NCT02277769 — identically designed co-primary monotherapy registration trials; supportive combination-with-topical-corticosteroids trial CHRONOS (Study R668-AD-1224), NCT02260986.

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter Phase 3 trials (SOLO 1 and SOLO 2 monotherapy; CHRONOS as dupilumab + topical corticosteroids vs. placebo + topical corticosteroids)
- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint (Week 16, all three trials) proportion achieving IGA 0 or 1 with ≥2-point reduction from baseline; key secondary EASI75 and pruritus Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) improvement ≥4
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by baseline disease severity (IGA 3 vs. 4) and region
- *Multiplicity:* hierarchical testing procedure at two-sided α=0.025 per dose regimen, using a sponsor-termed "serial gatekeeping procedure" testing secondary endpoints in a pre-specified order
- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation from time of rescue-medication use or study withdrawal; LOCF and all-observed-data sensitivity analyses; reviewer-documented deviation from a late sponsor SAP amendment (see below)
- *Regulatory:* twin identically designed trials (SOLO 1/SOLO 2) both serving as co-primary pivotal evidence — first-in-class biologic approval for atopic dermatitis

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Population (all three trials): adults ≥18 with chronic atopic dermatitis ≥3 years, EASI≥16, IGA≥3, BSA≥10% AD involvement, baseline pruritus NRS≥3, and documented inadequate response/intolerance to topical AD medications or for whom topicals were medically inadvisable
- SOLO 1 (Trial 1334): 671 randomized 1:1:1 to dupilumab 300 mg QW / 300 mg Q2W / placebo (223/224/224), 131 centers; SOLO 2 (Trial 1416): 708 randomized 1:1:1 (239/233/236), 136 centers; both monotherapy, no background topical therapy
- CHRONOS (Trial 1224): 740 randomized 3:1:3 to dupilumab+TCS QW / dupilumab+TCS Q2W / placebo+TCS (319/106/315), 160 centers, 52-week treatment plus 12-week follow-up
- Randomization stratified by disease severity (IGA 3 vs. 4, i.e., moderate vs. severe) and region (Asia Pacific, Eastern Europe, Western Europe, North/South America) in all three trials
- Primary endpoint (Week 16, all three trials): proportion of subjects achieving IGA 0 or 1 AND ≥2-point reduction from baseline; secondary endpoints included EASI75 (≥75% improvement), pruritus NRS reduction ≥4 (FDA-preferred threshold per a 2015 advice letter) and ≥3 (supportive), and percent change in pruritus NRS
- Primary analysis: CMH test stratified by baseline disease severity and region; missing binary data (withdrawal or rescue-medication use) counted as non-responder from the time of the event, with LOCF and all-observed-data sensitivity analyses
- Results at Week 16 (FDA Statistical Review): SOLO 1 — IGA0/1 37% (QW)/38% (Q2W) vs. 10% placebo, EASI75 53%/51% vs. 15%; SOLO 2 — IGA0/1 36%/36% vs. 9%, EASI75 47%/44% vs. 12%; CHRONOS — IGA0/1 39%/39% vs. 12%, EASI75 64%/69% vs. 23%; both doses superior to placebo in all three trials (p<0.0001 for the primary endpoint)
- Notable SAP-amendment/reviewer-deviation finding: the sponsor submitted a SAP amendment (dated Feb 6, 2016 — after both SOLO trials had already completed, Feb 12, 2016 and Jan 21, 2016) adding a "rescue medication algorithm" exempting subjects who used topical corticosteroids during the first 14 days from being counted as rescue-medication users; the FDA statistical reviewer explicitly disagreed and re-analyzed those subjects as non-responders anyway, since the protocols still listed TCS as a prohibited medication
- FDA had also previously advised (Oct 27, 2014 letter) that Week-52 endpoints "do not appear to add significant additional information to what has been shown by the primary endpoint and the first secondary endpoint and will therefore be unlikely to be incorporated into labeling"
- Per-protocol sensitivity analyses closely matched the FAS/ITT primary results (e.g., SOLO 1 IGA0/1 FAS 37%/38%/10% vs. PP 38%/38%/10%)

### 13. Sarilumab (Kevzara) — BLA 761037

**Sponsor:** Sanofi-Aventis (co-developed with Regeneron).

**Indication approved:** Moderately-to-severely active rheumatoid arthritis in adults with an inadequate response or intolerance to one or more disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs).

**Approval date:** May 22, 2017.

**Pivotal trial:** MOBILITY (SARIL-RA-MOBILITY, Study EFC11072), NCT01061736 — methotrexate-inadequate-responder population; TARGET (SARIL-RA-TARGET, Study EFC10832), NCT01709578 — TNF-inadequate-responder/intolerant population.

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, international add-on trials (MOBILITY: add-on to background methotrexate; TARGET: add-on to background non-biologic DMARD in TNF-inadequate-responders); MOBILITY was an operationally seamless two-part dose-ranging-and-confirmatory design
- *Endpoints:* primary ACR20 response at Week 24; key secondary hierarchy including HAQ-DI change, modified total Sharp score (mTSS) radiographic progression at Week 52, and major clinical response
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by prior biologic use and region (MOBILITY) or number of previous anti-TNFs and region (TARGET)
- *Multiplicity:* hierarchical (fixed-sequence) testing procedure with a Bonferroni correction splitting two-sided α=0.05 as 0.025 per dose regimen, each with its own ranked endpoint hierarchy
- *Missing data/bias:* post-discontinuation/rescue data set to missing (no LOCF) for the binary ACR20 responder endpoint; MMRM for continuous HAQ-DI; tipping-point sensitivity analyses requested by FDA; estimand framework analysis (ICH E9(R1)-style treatment-policy vs. hypothetical estimand) for the rescue/escape-crossover mTSS radiographic endpoint; linear extrapolation single-imputation for missing longitudinal radiographic data, criticized by the FDA reviewer as unverifiable
- *Regulatory:* mid-conduct SAP amendments changed the primary missing-data handling (LOCF → non-responder-from-rescue) and the HAQ-DI analysis method (ANCOVA → MMRM)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- MOBILITY (Part B Cohort 2): 1197 randomized to sarilumab 150 mg / 200 mg SC Q2W / placebo (400/399/398), stratified by region and prior biologic use, add-on to background methotrexate, 52 weeks
- TARGET: 546 randomized (181/184/181) to sarilumab 150 mg / 200 mg SC Q2W / placebo, add-on to a non-biologic DMARD in TNF-inadequate-responders/intolerant patients, 24 weeks
- Primary endpoint (both trials): ACR20 response at Week 24, analyzed via two-sided CMH test stratified by prior biologic use and region (MOBILITY) or number of previous anti-TNFs and region (TARGET)
- Endpoint hierarchy (MOBILITY): (1) ACR20 Week 24, (2) HAQ-DI change Week 16, (3) mTSS change Week 52 (radiographic), (4) major clinical response Week 52; each dose tested independently at α=0.025 with a hierarchical Bonferroni-corrected procedure
- Sample size: MOBILITY powered on mTSS (Wilcoxon/Mann-Whitney via nQuery), α=0.025, 90% power, assumed Week 52 means 1.10 (placebo)/0.35 (active), SD 2.6, 15% missing data → 372/group, based on tocilizumab LITHE-study estimates; TARGET powered on HAQ-DI Week 24 change, α=0.025, ≥90% power, SD 0.52 → 174/group (N=522)
- Missing data: primary approach set post-discontinuation/rescue data to missing (no LOCF) for the binary ACR20 endpoint; continuous HAQ-DI analyzed by MMRM with no imputation, with LOCF-based sensitivity analyses added by a mid-conduct SAP amendment; FDA requested tipping-point sensitivity analyses for TARGET's primary endpoint
- Radiographic (mTSS) endpoint: FDA's statistical review addendum contains an extended estimand discussion distinguishing a "de facto or treatment policy" estimand from a "no-escape" hypothetical estimand, given that 29%/39% of placebo patients escaped to sarilumab by Week 24/52; the sponsor's pre-specified primary method was single-imputation "linear extrapolation" (fitting a line through baseline and the last pre-escape score), which the FDA reviewer criticized as unverifiable and uncertainty-underestimating, requesting a supplementary linear mixed-effects slope-comparison analysis treating post-escape placebo data as missing
- No sample-size/power narrative issues were otherwise flagged; results (Week 24 ACR20) were not individually re-derived here beyond the FDA review's confirmation that both doses were superior to placebo in both trials

### 14. Guselkumab (Tremfya) — BLA 761061

**Sponsor:** Janssen Biotech, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in adults who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy — the first IL-23 (p19)-specific inhibitor approved.

**Approval date:** July 13, 2017.

**Pivotal trial:** VOYAGE 1 (Trial 3001), NCT02207231, and VOYAGE 2 (Trial 3002, with a randomized-withdrawal-and-retreatment period), NCT02207244 — both placebo- and adalimumab-active-comparator-controlled.

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-comparator (adalimumab)-controlled, parallel-group Phase 3 trials; VOYAGE 2 added a randomized-withdrawal-and-retreatment period (Week 28-76) for Week-28 PASI90 responders
- *Endpoints:* co-primary IGA 0/1 and PASI90 response vs. placebo at Week 16; a ranked secondary hierarchy including superiority- and non-inferiority-vs-adalimumab comparisons
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by investigational site (pooled) for binary co-primary/secondary endpoints; ANOVA (treatment + pooled site) for continuous secondaries; log-rank test stratified by pooled site for time-to-loss-of-PASI90 response (VOYAGE 2 only)
- *Multiplicity:* sequential gatekeeping approach spanning superiority-vs-placebo, superiority-vs-adalimumab, and non-inferiority-vs-adalimumab hypotheses in one ranked chain — each secondary tested only if both co-primaries and all prior secondaries in the chain were significant (0.05, or 0.025 for non-inferiority comparisons)
- *Missing data/bias:* "treatment failure" rule (discontinuation for lack of efficacy/psoriasis-worsening AE, or prohibited rescue medication → non-responder), with two pre-specified expanded sensitivity definitions; primary imputation non-responder imputation (NRI) for binary endpoints and LOCF for continuous endpoints
- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Both trials: multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo- and adalimumab-active-controlled, parallel-group Phase 3 trials in moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis (IGA≥3, PASI≥12, BSA≥10%); randomization stratified by investigational site (pooled) in both trials
- VOYAGE 1 (Trial 3001): ~750 subjects randomized 2:1:2 to guselkumab 100 mg (Week 0, 4, 12, then Q8W; ITT N=329) / placebo→crossover to guselkumab at Week 16 (ITT N=174) / adalimumab 80 mg loading then 40 mg Q2W (ITT N=334); blinded through Week 48
- VOYAGE 2 (Trial 3002): active-comparator-controlled period Week 0-24 (ITT guselkumab N=496, adalimumab N=248, placebo N=248), then Week-28 PASI90 responders on guselkumab re-randomized to continued guselkumab vs. withdrawal-to-placebo through Week 76
- Co-primary endpoints (both trials, Week 16, vs. placebo): proportion achieving IGA 0/1, and proportion achieving PASI90; results — VOYAGE 1 IGA0/1 85% (280/329) vs. 7% (12/174), PASI90 73% (241/329) vs. 3% (5/174); VOYAGE 2 IGA0/1 84% (417/496) vs. 8% (21/248), PASI90 70% (347/496) vs. 2% (6/248); all p<0.001
- Sequential gatekeeping tested a ranked list of major secondary endpoints (IGA0 Week 24, IGA0/1 Week 24, PASI90 Week 24, time-to-loss-of-PASI90 [VOYAGE 2], Week-48 endpoints [VOYAGE 1], DLQI change, then non-inferiority and superiority-vs-adalimumab tests for IGA0/1, PASI75, PASI90 at Week 16, then ss-IGA and PSSD symptom-score endpoints); non-inferiority comparisons used a one-sided α=0.025 CMH Z-test against a 10% margin on the risk-difference lower 95% CI bound
- Continuous PSS-related endpoint sensitivity: after applying the treatment-failure rule, missing data was primarily handled via NRI (binary) / LOCF (continuous), with LOCF, complete-case, and multiple-imputation (5 imputations via logistic regression) as pre-specified sensitivity analyses for the co-primary endpoints and the first three ranked secondaries
- No dedicated sample-size/power-calculation narrative was located in the extractable text of the combined Multi-Discipline Review; realized ITT sample sizes are as above

### 15. Benralizumab (Fasenra) — BLA 761070

**Sponsor:** AstraZeneca Pharmaceuticals LP.

**Indication approved:** Add-on maintenance treatment of severe eosinophilic asthma in patients 12 years and older.

**Approval date:** November 14, 2017.

**Pivotal trial:** SIROCCO (Study D3250C0017), NCT01928771, and CALIMA (Study D3250C0018), NCT01914757 (both exacerbation-reduction trials); ZONDA (Study D3250C0020), NCT02075255 (oral-corticosteroid-sparing trial).

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled trials with two benralizumab dosing regimens (30 mg Q4W throughout, vs. 30 mg Q4W ×3 then Q8W); co-enrollment biomarker-stratified enrichment design with primary analysis restricted to the enriched high-eosinophil stratum, while the low-eosinophil stratum was also enrolled but not multiplicity-protected (distinct from the taxonomy's existing full-restriction "biomarker-selected/enriched population" term)
- *Endpoints:* primary annual asthma exacerbation rate over the double-blind treatment period (SIROCCO/CALIMA); primary percent reduction in final oral-corticosteroid (OCS) dose while maintaining asthma control (ZONDA)
- *Primary analysis:* negative binomial regression (treatment, region, prior-year exacerbation count, maintenance-OCS use; log follow-up time as offset), with a marginal standardization method for covariate-adjusted rate estimation proposed by the sponsor SAP and endorsed by FDA over naive mean-covariate-level prediction; Wilcoxon rank-sum test with Hodges-Lehmann estimator (ZONDA OCS-reduction endpoint)
- *Multiplicity:* Hochberg procedure nested in a hierarchical gatekeeping structure across the two dose regimens and endpoint families, controlling family-wise error at 0.05
- *Missing data/bias:* mid-conduct SAP amendment adding a sensitivity analysis for OCS-dose-interruption handling after a protocol deviation was found during blinded review, which FDA still considered insufficient to "recover the robustness in assessment of OCS sparing"
- *Regulatory:* sponsor-conducted (not independent-DMC) blinded interim sample-size re-estimation, flagged by FDA as a study-conduct concern absent submitted interim-meeting minutes

**Trial design & endpoints**

- SIROCCO (48-week) and CALIMA (56-week), ages 12-75, high-dose (SIROCCO) or medium-or-high-dose (CALIMA) ICS/LABA background therapy ± OCS; randomization stratified by region, age group, and baseline blood eosinophil count (≥300/µL "EHS" vs. <300/µL "ELS"), enrolling both strata but enriching EHS at a 2:1 ratio, with multiplicity-protected primary/key-secondary testing restricted to EHS; SIROCCO N=1205 (Q4W 400, Q8W 398, placebo 407), CALIMA N=1306 (Q4W 425, Q8W 441, placebo 440)
- Primary endpoint (SIROCCO/CALIMA): annual asthma exacerbation rate, analyzed via negative binomial regression with treatment, region, prior-year exacerbation count, and maintenance-OCS use as covariates and log follow-up time as an offset; the sponsor's SAP proposed, and FDA endorsed, a marginal standardization method over SAS's naive `LSMEANS OBSMARGINS` mean-covariate-level prediction as more appropriate for covariate-adjusted rate summaries in this negative-binomial setting
- Multiplicity: Hochberg procedure nested in a hierarchical gatekeeping structure across the two dose regimens, controlling family-wise error at 0.05 (per "SIROCCO Study SAP Edition 4, Section 4.1"); secondary endpoints (FEV1, ACQ-6, AQLQ(S)+12, asthma symptom score) via MMRM, binary responders via stratified CMH, time-to-first-exacerbation via Cox proportional-hazards model
- Results (EHS, primary endpoint): Q8W reduced exacerbations by 51% (rate ratio 0.49, 95% CI 0.37-0.64, p<0.001) and Q4W by 45% (rate ratio 0.55, 95% CI 0.42-0.71, p<0.001) vs. placebo in SIROCCO; CALIMA showed 28% (rate ratio 0.72, p=0.019, Q8W) and 36% (rate ratio 0.64, p=0.002, Q4W) reductions
- ZONDA (28-week, ages 18-75, chronic-OCS-dependent severe eosinophilic asthma ≥150 cells/µL, N=220, randomized 1:1:1, stratified by eosinophil stratum and region): primary endpoint = percent reduction from baseline in final OCS dose (Week 24-28) while maintaining asthma control, analyzed via Wilcoxon rank-sum test with Hodges-Lehmann estimator, multiplicity controlled via Hochberg across the two dose regimens only
- Notable finding: an OCS-dose-titration protocol deviation was found during blinded review, prompting a mid-conduct SAP amendment adding a sensitivity analysis for how to handle exacerbation-triggered OCS interruptions; FDA's review states these methods still "could not recover the robustness in assessment of OCS sparing expected for supporting regulatory approval"
- Regulatory-process finding: FDA's filing memo documents that SIROCCO/CALIMA used a blinded, pooled interim sample-size re-estimation analysis (based on the blinded placebo exacerbation rate and shape parameter) that was "performed by AstraZeneca internal personnel or its designees" rather than an independent monitoring committee, with no interim meeting minutes submitted — FDA explicitly called this "potentially concerning from a study conduct perspective," though it noted the blinded-pooled-data analysis does not itself affect the Type I error rate

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, BLA 761070, Reference ID 4127210, p.15]* — "In the primary analysis, annual exacerbation rate in each of the 2 Benralizumab dose regimen groups was compared to annual exacerbation rate in the placebo group using a negative binomial model... In the study SAP, the applicant raised the concern that in regression models such as the negative binomial that transform the linear predictor, estimation of response evaluated at the mean covariate levels may not closely approximate the overall mean population response. The study SAP proposed the marginal standardization method in calculating mean annual exacerbation rates... We agree with the applicant's proposal in that, in the negative binomial regression setting, the marginal method more closely aligns with the crude annual exacerbation rate, and as such, provides a more appropriate covariate-adjusted summary within treatment groups."

- *[verbatim, p.43 (ZONDA)]* — "While the study SAP outlined both data handling methods for situations of treatment/asthma control interruption and a sensitivity assessment approach, we still consider these methods could not recover the robustness in assessment of OCS sparing expected for supporting regulatory approval."

- *[verbatim, Reference ID 4041532, p.80]* — "In each of the exacerbation studies (SIROCCO and CALIMA), both the SAP and Clinical Study Report described that there was an interim sample size re-estimation analysis based on a blinded estimate of the placebo exacerbation rate and shape parameter conducted before the last patient with eosinophil counts ≥ 300/μL was randomized. The applicant noted that the blinded sample size re-estimation analysis was 'performed by AstraZeneca internal personnel or it designees.' This type of analysis based on pooled blinded data does not directly affect the type I error rate, so no adjustment is needed, but it is potentially concerning from a study conduct perspective that the analysis was done by 'AstraZeneca internal personnel' rather than by an independent monitoring committee. Also, there are no interim meeting minutes submitted under the current BLA."

### 16. Tildrakizumab-asmn (Ilumya) — BLA 761067

**Sponsor:** Merck Sharp & Dohme Corporation (sponsor of record at original approval; rights later transferred to Sun Pharmaceutical Industries post-approval).

**Indication approved:** Moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in adults who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy.

**Approval date:** March 20, 2018.

**Pivotal trial:** reSURFACE 1 (Protocol MK-3222-010), NCT01722331, and reSURFACE 2 (Protocol MK-3222-011, with an etanercept active-comparator arm), NCT01729754.

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (reSURFACE 1) and placebo- and active-comparator (etanercept)-controlled (reSURFACE 2), parallel-group, three-part Phase 3 trials
- *Endpoints:* co-primary PASI75 response and Physician's Global Assessment (PGA) 0/1 response at Week 12
- *Primary analysis:* not confirmed from a public FDA review (see below) — inferred as CMH-type stratified analysis by weight and prior biologic exposure, consistent with contemporaneous IL-23-class trials, but not independently verified for this drug
- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation (NRI), per the approved label's efficacy-results table footnote
- *Regulatory:* no genuine FDA Statistical Review or Multi-Discipline Review is publicly posted for this BLA — see sourcing note below

**Trial design & endpoints**

- reSURFACE 1 (118 sites, Australia/Canada/Japan/UK/USA) and reSURFACE 2 (132 sites, Europe/Israel/USA): three-part, parallel-group, double-blind, randomized controlled trials in adults ≥18 with moderate-to-severe chronic plaque psoriasis (BSA≥10%, PGA≥3, PASI≥12)
- reSURFACE 1: randomized 2:2:1 to tildrakizumab 200 mg / 100 mg / placebo (N=772: 308/309/155); reSURFACE 2: randomized 2:2:1:2 to tildrakizumab 200 mg / 100 mg / placebo / etanercept 50 mg (N=1090: 314/307/156/313)
- Randomization via interactive voice/web response system (IVRS/IWRS), stratified by region, body weight (≤90 kg or >90 kg), and previous biologic exposure (per the pivotal publication's Methods section)
- Co-primary endpoints (both trials, Week 12): proportion achieving PASI75, and proportion achieving PGA response (score of 0 or 1 with ≥2-grade reduction from baseline)
- Results (per label, NRI-based, 100 mg approved dose only): reSURFACE 1 (Trial 2) — PGA 0/1, 58% (179/309) vs. 7% (11/154); PASI75, 64% (197/309) vs. 6% (9/154); reSURFACE 2 (Trial 3) — PGA 0/1, 55% (168/307) vs. 4% (7/156); PASI75, 61% (188/307) vs. 6% (9/156); other outcomes included PASI90/PASI100 at Week 12 and maintenance of efficacy to Week 64
- Only the 100 mg dose was approved (the 200 mg dose studied in both trials was not); the label states no differences in response were identified across age, gender, race, or prior-biologic subgroups
- **Sourcing note:** no genuine FDA Statistical Review or Multi-Discipline Review PDF is publicly accessible for this BLA. The Drugs@FDA table-of-contents page flags a `MultidisciplineR` document as expected, but the file returns HTTP 404 under every year-folder tried; openFDA's `drugsfda` API likewise lists only the approval letter and label for this application. Neither pivotal trial (reSURFACE 1 or reSURFACE 2) has a protocol/SAP posted on ClinicalTrials.gov. Given this, the statistical-methodology detail above beyond the label's results table is drawn from the pivotal Lancet publication's Methods/Findings sections (title, design, and results independently confirmed via PubMed), not from a genuine FDA or sponsor SAP document — see the Reverse-engineered SAP section below.

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter (replacement letter correcting a PMR-date error; effective approval date unchanged at March 20, 2018) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2018/761067Orig1s000REPLACEMENT_ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/761067s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Statistical Review / Multi-Discipline Review — not publicly available (see sourcing note above); no `StatR` or `MultidisciplineR` PDF resolves for this BLA under the standard Drugs@FDA URL patterns

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (reSURFACE 1) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01722331 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (reSURFACE 2) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01729754 (no protocol/SAP documents posted)

- Pivotal publication (reSURFACE 1 & reSURFACE 2, combined): Reich K, Papp KA, Blauvelt A, Tyring SK, Sinclair R, Thaçi D, et al. "Tildrakizumab versus placebo or etanercept for chronic plaque psoriasis (reSURFACE 1 and reSURFACE 2): results from two randomised controlled, phase 3 trials." Lancet. 2017;390(10091):276-288. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(17)31279-5>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28596043/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Tildrakizumab%20versus%20placebo%20or%20etanercept%20for%20chronic%20plaque%20psoriasis%20reSURFACE)

**Other resources**

- Merck (original sponsor) is a general participant in the YODA Project (Yale); trial-specific reSURFACE 1/2 dataset availability was not individually confirmed here.

- Whether an FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held could not be confirmed either way, since no FDA review package is publicly available for this BLA — treat as unconfirmed, not as a negative finding.

**Reverse-engineered SAP [inferred]**

- *[inferred, from ClinicalTrials.gov registry + label Table 2 + Reich et al. 2017 Lancet abstract]* Randomization was stratified by region, baseline body weight (≤90 kg/>90 kg), and prior biologic exposure — a design choice typical of IL-23-class psoriasis trials of this era (cf. guselkumab's site-stratified design and risankizumab's weight/prior-TNF-stratified design in this same batch), inferred from the publication's Methods statement that "Randomisation was done by region and stratified for bodyweight... and previous exposure to biologics therapy."

- *[inferred, from label Table 2 footnote "NRI = Non-Responder Imputation"]* The primary analysis population was the intent-to-treat/full-analysis set, with missing binary response data at Week 12 imputed as non-response (NRI) — consistent with essentially every other IL-23/IL-17-class psoriasis trial in this batch (brodalumab, guselkumab, risankizumab), but not independently confirmed via a genuine FDA or sponsor statistical document for tildrakizumab specifically.

- *[inferred, from the co-primary endpoint structure reported identically in the label and the Lancet publication]* The two co-primary endpoints (PASI75 and PGA 0/1 at Week 12) were most likely tested via a stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test analogous to the contemporaneous guselkumab and risankizumab programs, and a multiplicity-control procedure would have been needed to protect the family-wise error rate across two co-primary endpoints and two active doses (200 mg and 100 mg) tested against placebo — this specific procedure is not documented in any source located for this entry and is flagged here as a gap rather than asserted as fact.

### 17. Baricitinib (Olumiant) — NDA 207924

**Sponsor:** Eli Lilly and Company (co-developed with Incyte).

**Indication approved:** Moderately-to-severely active rheumatoid arthritis in adult patients with an inadequate response to one or more TNF antagonist therapies, at the 2 mg once-daily dose only — narrower than the 4 mg dose studied and narrower than the methotrexate-inadequate-responder population the Arthritis Advisory Committee discussed (see regulatory history below).

**Approval date:** May 31, 2018 (original NDA submitted January 14/15, 2016; Complete Response Letter issued April 12, 2017; resubmitted December 4, 2017).

**Pivotal trial:** RA-BEAM, NCT01710358 (MTX-inadequate-responders, active comparator adalimumab) — FDA's primary efficacy/statistical source; supportive RA-BUILD, NCT01721057 (cDMARD-inadequate-responders), and RA-BEACON, NCT01721044 (TNF-inadequate-responders, the population matching the approved indication).

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-comparator (adalimumab)-controlled, parallel-group Phase 3 trial (RA-BEAM), add-on to background methotrexate
- *Endpoints:* primary ACR20 response at Week 12 ("on treatment," non-responder imputation for rescued/discontinued patients); ranked major secondary hierarchy including HAQ-DI change, radiographic progression (mTSS), DAS28, SDAI≤3.3, and ACR20 vs. adalimumab
- *Primary analysis:* categorical efficacy via logistic regression (treatment + randomization strata); continuous endpoints via ANCOVA (treatment + baseline + strata); efficacy analyzed on the modified intent-to-treat (mITT) population
- *Multiplicity:* graphical alpha-propagation method (Bretz, Maurer, Brannath & Posch, 2009) controlling Type I error across multiple doses and endpoints at the 0.05 level
- *Missing data/bias:* sponsor required to pre-specify and justify a causal "de facto" (treatment-policy) estimand per a 2010 NRC-report-style framework, with tipping-point multiple imputation sensitivity analyses required by FDA after an initial sponsor imputation approach (linear extrapolation for radiographic data) was rejected
- *Regulatory:* Complete Response Letter (April 2017) over venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk; April 23, 2018 Arthritis Advisory Committee meeting with dose-split votes; FDA approval restricted to the lower/narrower 2 mg dose and to a more refractory (TNF-IR) population than either dose's studied MTX-IR population, following the split AC vote by dose

**Trial design & endpoints**

- RA-BEAM (Study JADV): N=1305 randomized in a ~3:2:3 ratio to baricitinib 4 mg (B4, N=487) / adalimumab (N=330) / placebo (N=488), stratified by region and presence/absence of joint erosion; adults with moderate-severe active RA, MTX-inadequate-responders, biologic-DMARD-naive, ≥1 erosion (or RF/ACPA-positive if <3 erosions), on background MTX
- Primary endpoint: ACR20 response at Week 12, analyzed on treatment (non-responder imputation for rescued/discontinued patients) via logistic regression with treatment and randomization strata; results — B4 70% (339/487) vs. placebo 40% (196/488), OR 3.6 (95% CI 2.7-4.7, p<0.001); at Week 24 (nominal, exploratory), B4 74% vs. placebo 37%, OR 5.0 (95% CI 3.8-6.7, p<0.001)
- Major secondary hierarchy (graphically alpha-propagated per Bretz et al. 2009): ΔHAQ-DI Week 12, mTSS (radiographic) Week 24, DAS28 Week 12, SDAI≤3.3 Week 12, ACR20 B4-vs-adalimumab Week 12, morning stiffness duration/severity, worst tiredness, worst pain
- Missing-data/estimand handling: FDA required the sponsor to define and justify the causal estimand for the primary/key-secondary analyses (citing the 2010 National Research Council report on missing data in clinical trials), settling on a treatment-policy-style "de facto" estimand (including all post-discontinuation data regardless of treatment switch) as primary; FDA rejected the sponsor's initial linear-extrapolation imputation approach for radiographic (mTSS) missing data and required tipping-point multiple-imputation sensitivity analyses instead; Hodges-Lehmann point estimate/CI used for the morning-stiffness-duration secondary endpoint
- Regulatory history: the original NDA (submitted Jan 2016) received a Complete Response Letter on April 12, 2017, identifying VTE as a unique risk occurring with both the 2 mg and 4 mg doses at rates higher than placebo, some fatal; after resubmission, the FDA Arthritis Advisory Committee met April 23, 2018 and voted: Efficacy 2 mg 14-1, Efficacy 4 mg 15-0, Safety 2 mg 9-6, Safety 4 mg 5-10, Benefit/Risk 2 mg 10-5, Benefit/Risk 4 mg 5-10 (all Yes-No, 0 abstain in each vote); FDA approved only the 2 mg dose, and further restricted the indication to TNF-inadequate-responders (narrower than the MTX-IR population the AC had discussed), explicitly citing the regulatory precedent of Actemra's 2010 approval being limited to TNF-IR patients on safety grounds
- No boxed warning was present at the original 2018 approval; the later class-wide JAK-inhibitor boxed warning (thrombosis/malignancy/MACE/serious infection, following tofacitinib's ORAL Surveillance trial) was added in a subsequent supplement, not part of this original-approval entry

- *[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, Reference ID 4271040, p.3]* — AAC Vote (Efficacy 2 mg): "14 Yes, 1 No, 0 Abstain... The single no vote was because of the lack of robust radiographic progression data with the 2 mg dose." Vote (Efficacy 4 mg): "15 Yes, 0 No, 0 Abstain." Vote (Safety 2 mg): "9 Yes, 6 No, 0 Abstain." Vote (Safety 4 mg, p.4): "5 Yes, 10 No, 0 Abstain."

- *[verbatim, p.6]* — "Recommendations for Regulatory Action... Approval of baricitinib 2 mg once daily for the treatment of adult patients with moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis who have had an inadequate response to one or more TNF antagonist therapies... The AC panel recommended approval of baricitinib 2 mg in patients who are MTX-IR; however, some members voiced preference to reserve baricitinib for patients with an incomplete response to biologic therapy. There is precedent for limiting an RA product to a TNF-IR patient population, based upon benefit/risk assessment. When Actemra was approved in January 2010, it was limited to patients with an incomplete response to TNF inhibitors because of concerns with the safety profile."

### 18. Lanadelumab-flyo (Takhzyro) — BLA 761090

**Sponsor:** Dyax Corporation (a Shire/Takeda subsidiary at the time of approval; Dyax is the applicant of record on the BLA).

**Indication approved:** Prophylaxis to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in patients 12 years and older.

**Approval date:** August 23, 2018.

**Pivotal trial:** HELP Study (DX-2930-03), NCT02586805.

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized (2:1 active:placebo), double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial with three active dosing regimens, preceded by a 4-8-week run-in to establish baseline attack rate; randomization stratified by baseline attack rate (1-<2, 2-<3, ≥3/month)
- *Endpoints:* primary number of investigator-confirmed HAE attacks during Day 0-182 (efficacy window changed from Day 14-182 to Day 0-182 by protocol amendment, per FDA recommendation)
- *Primary analysis:* generalized linear model for count data assuming a Poisson distribution with a log-link function and Pearson chi-square scaling for overdispersion, with log(observation days) as an offset; hypothesis tested via a Wald-based chi-square test on the model-based least-squares-mean treatment difference
- *Multiplicity:* Bonferroni-based general gatekeeping procedure (distinct from the taxonomy's existing simple sequential Bonferroni-Holm row) — a branching structure with each of three active-dose-vs-placebo comparisons tested sequentially at 0.0167 (0.05/3), FWER strongly controlled at two-sided 0.05
- *Missing data/bias:* tipping-point multiple imputation and negative-binomial GLM as pre-specified sensitivity analyses to the primary Poisson GLM
- *Regulatory:* genuine sponsor SAP (original + one amendment) posted on ClinicalTrials.gov — rare for this batch; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Randomized 2:1 (active:placebo, active arms equally split across 3 dose regimens), double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, 26-week treatment period (13 doses), preceded by a 4-8-week run-in requiring ≥1 investigator-confirmed attack/4 weeks for eligibility; stratified by baseline attack rate tercile; arms: lanadelumab 150 mg SC Q4W (N=28), 300 mg SC Q4W (N=29), 300 mg SC Q2W (N=27), placebo (N=41); ages 12-70 included (adolescent subgroup N=10)
- Primary endpoint: number of investigator-confirmed HAE attacks during Day 0-182 — the efficacy window was changed from Day 14-182 to Day 0-182 via Protocol Amendment 2 (April 21, 2016) at FDA's recommendation
- Rank-ordered secondary endpoints: (1) attacks requiring acute treatment (Day 0-182), (2) moderate/severe attacks (Day 0-182), (3) attacks Day 14-182 (added via Amendment 3, Jan 9, 2017, specifically to be folded into the multiple-testing procedure)
- Sample size/power: powered for a 60% reduction in attack rate (conservative relative to the ~100% reduction seen in Phase 2), planned N=80 active/40 placebo for ≥95% power at one-sided α=0.025; actual enrollment (84 active/41 placebo) exceeded the plan
- Primary analysis: Poisson GLM with log-link and Pearson chi-square overdispersion scaling; fixed effects for treatment group and normalized baseline attack rate; log(observation days) offset; H0: λ(lanadelumab)/λ(placebo)=1 vs. H1≠1, tested via a Wald-based chi-square test on the model-based LS-mean treatment difference
- Multiplicity: Bonferroni-based general gatekeeping procedure with branches for each active-treatment-vs-placebo comparison, each tested sequentially at 0.0167, FWER strongly controlled at two-sided 0.05
- Sensitivity analyses: tipping-point multiple imputation (progressively conservative post-dropout attack-rate assumptions) and a negative-binomial GLM alternative to the primary Poisson GLM, both pre-specified in the SAP
- Results (Day 0-182, model-based rate, attacks/4 weeks): placebo 1.967 (95% CI 1.640-2.358); 150 mg Q4W 0.480 (-75.6% vs. placebo); 300 mg Q4W 0.526 (-73.3%); 300 mg Q2W 0.257 (-86.9%); all three doses p<0.001 vs. placebo, adjusted for multiplicity

The hypothesis was tested using the model-based least squares means estimate of the treatment difference using a Wald-based chi-square test."

Formal statistical hypothesis testing was performed on the primary and rank ordered secondary efficacy endpoints with the global family-wise type I error rate (FWER) strongly controlled for multiplicity at two-sided 0.05 using a Bonferroni-based general gatekeeping procedure."

However, given the results of the studies submitted, the Division decided that the evidence supporting approval for the indicated population was sufficiently robust that discussion at an AC was not necessary."

### 19. Sarecycline (Seysara) — NDA 209521

**Sponsor:** Allergan, Inc. (originator/co-developer Almirall, S.A., which holds the ClinicalTrials.gov sponsor registration and ran the pivotal trials).

**Indication approved:** Treatment of inflammatory lesions of non-nodular moderate-to-severe acne vulgaris in patients 9 years of age and older.

**Approval date:** October 1, 2018.

**Pivotal trial:** SC1401, NCT02320149, and SC1402, NCT02322866 — identically designed 12-week Phase 3 trials.

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter, identically designed twin Phase 3 trials in facial acne vulgaris (ages 9-45)
- *Endpoints:* co-primary absolute change from baseline in inflammatory lesion counts, and proportion achieving IGA success (score of 0 [clear] or 1 [almost clear] with ≥2-point decrease from baseline) at Week 12
- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA (baseline covariate + treatment + pooled site, SAS PROC MIXED, methodology of Littell et al. 2006) for the lesion-count endpoint; Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by pooled site for IGA success
- *Missing data/bias:* multiple imputation (20 imputations) as the primary missing-data method, with LOCF, BOCF, MMRM, rank-transform ANCOVA, and a "worst-case" imputation as pre-specified sensitivity analyses
- *Regulatory:* SAP amendment for one twin trial (SC1401) made after unblinding and analyzing its identically-designed companion trial (SC1402); no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Two multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, identically designed Phase 3 trials in patients 9-45 years of age with moderate-to-severe acne vulgaris (IGA≥3, 20-50 inflammatory lesions, ≤100 non-inflammatory lesions); sarecycline dosed by weight tier (approximately 1.5 mg/kg/day, using 60 mg/100 mg/150 mg tablets) vs. placebo, once daily for 12 weeks
- SC1401: 968 randomized (483 sarecycline/485 placebo), 56 US sites; SC1402: 1034 randomized (519/515), 54 US sites
- Co-primary efficacy endpoints (both trials, Week 12): absolute change from baseline in inflammatory lesion counts, and proportion of subjects with an IGA score of 0 or 1 with ≥2-point decrease from baseline
- Missing-data handling: multiple imputation (20 imputations) as the primary method for both co-primary endpoints, with LOCF, BOCF, MMRM (unstructured, falling back to Toeplitz), rank-transform ANCOVA, and a "worst-case" imputation (sarecycline missing=failure, placebo missing=success) as pre-specified sensitivity analyses; secondary endpoints tested hierarchically, only if both co-primaries were significant at α=0.05
- Results (ITT, MI-based): IGA success — SC1401 21.9% (sarecycline) vs. 10.5% (placebo), p<0.001; SC1402 22.6% vs. 15.3%, p=0.004; inflammatory lesion count mean absolute reduction — SC1401 15.3 vs. 10.2, p<0.001; SC1402 15.5 vs. 11.1, p<0.001
- Notable SAP-timing finding: the sponsor submitted finalized SAPs for SC1402 (Feb 13, 2017) and SC1401 (Feb 28, 2017), then submitted an amended SAP for SC1401 on March 6, 2017 — adding non-inflammatory lesion count as a secondary endpoint — after already unblinding and analyzing SC1402's data; the FDA review flags this timing explicitly

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held — confirmed explicitly in the Multi-Discipline Review.

The Applicant submitted an amended SAP for Study SC1401 on March 6, 2017, which added absolute and percent change from baseline in non-inflammatory lesion as secondary efficacy endpoints. It should be noted that the Applicant amended the SAP after unblinding and analyzing the data from Study SC1402."

Results table: IGA of 0 or 1 — 21.9% (sarecycline) vs. 10.5% (placebo), p<0.001, SC1401; 22.6% vs. 15.3%, p=0.004, SC1402. Absolute reduction in inflammatory lesion counts (mean) — 15.3 vs. 10.2, p<0.001, SC1401; 15.5 vs. 11.1, p<0.001, SC1402.

### 20. Risankizumab-rzaa (Skyrizi) — BLA 761105

**Sponsor:** AbbVie Inc. (originally co-developed with Boehringer Ingelheim, compound code BI 655066/ABBV-066).

**Indication approved:** Moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in adults who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy.

**Approval date:** April 23, 2019.

**Pivotal trial:** ultIMMa-1 (Trial 1311.3/M16-008), NCT02684370, and ultIMMa-2 (Trial 1311.28/M15-995), NCT02684357 — both placebo- and ustekinumab-active-comparator-controlled.

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo- and ustekinumab-active-comparator-controlled, 52-week Phase 3 trials; randomization stratified by body weight (≤100 kg vs. >100 kg) and prior TNF-antagonist exposure
- *Endpoints:* co-primary PASI90 response and static PGA (sPGA) 0/1 response vs. placebo at Week 16
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by weight and prior TNF-antagonist exposure for binary co-primary/secondary endpoints; van Elteren test (stratified Wilcoxon-family test) for the continuous Psoriasis Symptom Scale (PSS) endpoint
- *Multiplicity:* fixed 16+-endpoint hierarchical testing sequence at two-sided α=0.05, gated on both co-primaries being significant first
- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation (NRI) primary for binary endpoints (LOCF/logistic regression/multiple imputation as sensitivity analyses); LOCF primary for the continuous PSS endpoint (MMRM as sensitivity analysis)
- *Regulatory:* FDA-directed re-ordering of the statistical testing hierarchy to prioritize placebo comparisons, agreed during protocol review before unblinding; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ultIMMa-1 (N=560) and ultIMMa-2 (N=577): randomized, double-blind, placebo- and ustekinumab-controlled, 52-week trials in moderate-to-severe chronic plaque psoriasis; randomization stratified by body weight (≤100 kg/>100 kg) and prior TNF-antagonist exposure (yes/no)
- Co-primary endpoints (both trials, Week 16): PASI90 response and sPGA 0/1 response vs. placebo, analyzed via CMH test stratified by the two randomization factors; missing binary data handled by non-responder imputation (NRI), with LOCF, logistic regression, and multiple imputation as sensitivity analyses
- Continuous PRO endpoint (Psoriasis Symptom Scale, PSS): van Elteren test as the primary analysis, with LOCF as the primary imputation method and MMRM as a sensitivity analysis
- Multiplicity: fixed hierarchical testing sequence (16+ endpoints, two-sided α=0.05) gated on both co-primaries being significant first; FDA's review documents that for both trials the statistical testing hierarchy was re-ordered, during protocol review (before unblinding), to prioritize comparisons with placebo
- Results (Week 16): ultIMMa-1 — sPGA 0/1, risankizumab 88% vs. placebo 8% vs. ustekinumab 63%; PASI90, 75% vs. 5% vs. 42%; ultIMMa-2 — sPGA 0/1, 84% vs. 5% vs. 62%; PASI90, 75% vs. 2% vs. 47%; all p<0.001 vs. placebo
- No sample-size/power narrative was located in the extractable Multi-Discipline Review text beyond the realized ITT sample sizes above

### 21. Upadacitinib (Rinvoq) — NDA 211675

**Sponsor:** AbbVie

**Indication approved:** Moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis in adults with an inadequate response or intolerance to methotrexate (original 2019 approval; later expanded to other indications not covered here)

**Approval date:** August 16, 2019

**Pivotal trial:** SELECT-COMPARE (M14-465), NCT02629159

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled (adalimumab), multicenter, phase 3 trial; 2:2:1 randomization (placebo : upadacitinib 15 mg QD : adalimumab 40 mg every-other-week), stratified by prior biologic-DMARD exposure; treat-through design with blinded rescue/crossover for inadequate responders at Weeks 14/18/22 — patients on any arm meeting a pre-specified non-response rule (≤20% improvement in tender/swollen joint counts) were blindly switched to a different randomized arm rather than simply continuing or being classified as failures in place ("Blinded rescue-crossover (treat-through) design," distinct from the taxonomy's existing "Crossover permitted at progression," which is unblinded and post-progression only)

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint ACR20 response at Week 12 (US/FDA regulatory purposes); EU/EMA primary endpoint was clinical remission (DAS28(CRP) <2.6) at Week 12; ranked key secondary endpoints included change from baseline in DAS28(CRP), change in modified Total Sharp Score (mTSS, radiographic progression) at Week 26, change in HAQ-DI, and ACR50 (non-inferiority then superiority vs. adalimumab)

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by prior bDMARD exposure for the difference in binomial proportions (ACR20 and other responder endpoints); ANCOVA (treatment, baseline value, stratification factor) for DAS28(CRP) and HAQ-DI; MMRM for other continuous secondary endpoints; FDA reviewer's own random-coefficient model (random slope/intercept, unequal variance by arm) as an alternative to the applicant's linear-extrapolation approach for the radiographic progression estimand

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing of the primary endpoint followed by 13 ranked key secondary endpoints at two-sided alpha=0.05, notably different from the graphical alpha-splitting procedure the same sponsor used in its other four upadacitinib RA phase 3 trials

- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation (NRI) for binary responder endpoints under the treat-through/rescue design; multiple imputation (5 imputed datasets, Rubin's rule) for continuous endpoints (DAS28(CRP), HAQ-DI); FDA-conducted independent tipping-point sensitivity analysis for the radiographic endpoint after finding the applicant's single-imputation "linear extrapolation" approach for early dropouts methodologically inadequate

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting (not first-in-class, no unexpected safety/efficacy issues); FDA statistical reviewer explicitly disputed the scientific rationale for the applicant's embedded non-inferiority comparison (ACR50, upadacitinib vs. adalimumab, 10% margin) within a placebo-controlled trial's testing hierarchy, given the blinded-crossover design's effect on randomization integrity ("Reviewer disputes rationale for an embedded head-to-head non-inferiority comparison within a placebo-controlled hierarchy")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- M14-465/SELECT-COMPARE was a 26/48-week (26-week primary analysis period, with placebo-arm crossover to upadacitinib thereafter), multicenter (286 sites, 41 countries), randomized, double-blind trial in 1,629 adults with moderate-to-severe active RA and an inadequate response to methotrexate, randomized 2:2:1 to placebo (n=651), upadacitinib 15 mg QD (n=651), or adalimumab 40 mg EOW (n=327), all on background MTX; randomization was stratified by prior bDMARD exposure (region was a randomization stratum but not included in the statistical model)

- Treat-through/rescue design: at Weeks 14, 18, or 22, patients with inadequate response (≤20% improvement in both tender and swollen joint counts) were blindly switched — adalimumab non-responders to upadacitinib, upadacitinib non-responders to adalimumab, placebo non-responders to upadacitinib; after Week 26, all remaining placebo patients crossed over to upadacitinib regardless of response, which FDA noted limited interpretation of any post-Week-26 safety or efficacy data

- Primary endpoint: ACR20 response at Week 12 (US), defined as ≥20% improvement in tender (68) and swollen (66) joint counts plus ≥20% improvement in at least 3 of 5 additional core-set measures (physician global, patient global, pain, HAQ-DI, hsCRP); EU/EMA primary endpoint was DAS28(CRP) <2.6 clinical remission at Week 12

- Ranked key secondary endpoints (SAP §9.2.3, in order): DAS28(CRP) change at Week 12; mTSS change at Week 26; HAQ-DI change at Week 12; ACR50 (non-inferiority vs. adalimumab); SF-36 PCS change; DAS28(CRP) LDA (≤3.2); DAS28(CRP) clinical remission; CDAI LDA (≤10); morning-stiffness-duration change; FACIT-F change; ACR50 (superiority vs. adalimumab); patient pain-assessment change (superiority vs. adalimumab); HAQ-DI change (superiority vs. adalimumab)

- Sample size: 1,500 planned (2:2:1) for ≥90% power to detect a 22-percentage-point ACR20 difference (37% assumed placebo rate) and a 19.3-point CR-rate difference at two-sided alpha=0.05 with 10% dropout, and ≥90% power for a 0.39-unit mTSS difference at Week 26 (SD=2); actual randomized N=1,629

- Reported ACR20 at Week 12 (FDA reviewer's independent NRI analysis): placebo 237/651 (36%); upadacitinib 15 mg 459/651 (71%), difference vs. placebo 34.1% (95% CI 29.0, 39.2, p<0.001); adalimumab 206/327 (63%), difference vs. placebo 26.6% (95% CI 20.2, 33.0, p<0.001)

- Reported mTSS change at Week 26 (treatment-policy estimand, ANCOVA): placebo +0.7 (SD 3.0); upadacitinib +0.2 (SD 1.4), difference vs. placebo −0.56 (95% CI −0.83, −0.29, p<0.001); adalimumab 0.0 (SD 2.4), difference vs. placebo −0.72 (95% CI −1.1, −0.39, p<0.001); FDA's own random-coefficient-model estimand gave an adjusted linear progression rate of 0.78 (placebo) vs. 0.15 (upadacitinib), difference −0.52 (95% CI −0.75, −0.28, p<0.001)

- Safety analyses of special interest (MACE, adjudicated VTE) used exposure-adjusted incidence rates with Mantel-Haenszel weighting rather than a formal hypothesis test, given small event counts and the crossover-limited comparator period (14-week placebo-controlled window): MACE 3/171.3 (placebo) vs. 0/172.5 (upadacitinib) vs. 1/86.0 (adalimumab) per 100 patient-years; adjudicated VTE 1/171.4 vs. 1/172.5 vs. 3/85.9 per 100 patient-years

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP, M14-465 v2.0, 07 Dec 2017, §9.2.5 "Handling of Multiplicity"]* — "In order to preserve Type I error, a step-down approach will be used to test the primary and ranked key secondary endpoints where statistical significance can be claimed for a lower ranked endpoint only if the previous endpoint in the sequence meets the requirements of significance. Specifically, the testing will utilize the endpoint sequence of primary endpoint followed by ranked key secondary endpoints in the order as specified in Section 9.2.3, using α of 0.05."

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP §4.3, sample size]* — "The planned total sample size of 1500 for this study (with a 2:2:1 randomization ratio) provides at least 90% power for a 22% difference in ACR20 response rate at Week 12 (assuming a placebo ACR20 response rate of 37%) at two-sided significance level of 0.05 and accounting for a 10% dropout rate... approximately 90% power to detect a treatment difference of 0.39 in change from baseline in mTSS at Week 26 with a standard deviation of 2."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, p.12-13, treat-through/crossover design]* — "At either Week 14, 18, or 22, patients with inadequate efficacy response... were offered escape to other treatment arms... Because of the multiple crossovers, the lack of placebo patients, the interpretation of safety results or efficacy data after week 26 is limited."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, p.22, on the embedded non-inferiority comparison]* — "I did not agree with the proposed margin for the following reasons. First, it is reasonable to conduct comparative effectiveness studies between products in an active controlled study. However, with a placebo arm in place, the objective is less clear. Second, it is more reasonable to conduct the NI comparison at a later timepoint due to the chronic nature of the disease. Thirdly... escape was potentially possible at multiple timepoints... breaking the integrity of the randomization."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review §3.2.3.3, p.23, radiographic-endpoint imputation critique]* — "The Agency did not agree with the use of linear extrapolation as a single imputation approach to impute radiographic scores in patients who escape or withdraw from the study early... This assumption is strong and unverifiable, and may in some situations tend to overstate true progression on placebo."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, p.53, tipping-point conclusion]* — "In the tipping point sensitivity analysis targeting the treatment policy estimand, there was further supportive evidence of the robustness of evidence for upadacitinib 15 mg QD dosing relative to placebo arm... These sensitivity analyses indicated that results did not tip in favor of the placebo arm even under implausible assumptions."
