### 22. Trifarotene (Aklief) — NDA 211527

**Sponsor:** Galderma Research and Development

**Indication approved:** Topical treatment of acne vulgaris in patients 9 years of age and older

**Approval date:** October 4, 2019

**Pivotal trial:** Study 1, NCT02566369, and Study 2, NCT02556788 (per the FDA-approved label; these two identically-designed trials are not given a named acronym in the label, SAP, ClinicalTrials.gov, or the pivotal publication — a "PERFECT 1/2" name sometimes attached to this program in secondary sources could not be verified against any primary source and should not be used)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two identically-designed, randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled, multicenter, parallel-group phase 3 trials; 1:1 randomization stratified by clinical trial center; approximately 1,200 subjects planned per trial (612/596 and 602/610 randomized to trifarotene/vehicle respectively)

- *Endpoints:* three co-primary endpoints, all required to be significant (facial IGA success — score of 0/1 with ≥2-grade improvement from baseline at Week 12; absolute change in facial non-inflammatory lesion count; absolute change in facial inflammatory lesion count), plus a parallel co-secondary triplet for truncal acne (PGA success, non-inflammatory and inflammatory truncal lesion counts) tested only if the co-primary endpoint succeeded

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by pooled analysis center for the binary IGA/PGA success endpoints; ANCOVA (treatment, center, baseline lesion count) for the lesion-count endpoints; primary analysis population ITT (face) / ITTT (trunk, a truncal-acne-eligible subset)

- *Multiplicity:* no formal Type I error adjustment across the three co-primary (or three co-secondary) endpoints, because all three must independently reach significance for the composite primary (or secondary) claim to succeed — a conjunctive "all-must-win" structure that does not inflate family-wise error by construction, gated hierarchically (co-secondary tested only if the co-primary succeeded)

- *Missing data/bias:* multiple imputation (SAS MI procedure, MAR assumption, 5 imputed datasets, protocol-number-derived seed) as the pre-specified primary missing-data method for both binary and continuous endpoints, with a Pattern-Mixture Model under MNAR (imputing from vehicle-arm profiles) and LOCF as sensitivity analyses

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting; FDA's combined Multi-Discipline/Statistical Review document — listed as included in the approval package's own contents table — returned a genuine 404 from FDA's document server across every filename/year variant tried, so this entry's statistical-methodology detail is sourced from the genuine sponsor-posted SAP and the approved label rather than an FDA reviewer's independent statistical narrative (a documented sourcing gap, not a study-design finding)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Two phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled trials of identical design (Study 1/NCT02566369, N=1,208; Study 2/NCT02556788, N=1,212), each randomizing subjects 1:1, stratified by clinical trial center, to trifarotene 50 µg/g cream or vehicle cream, both applied once daily in the evening for 12 weeks, in subjects 9 years and older with moderate facial and truncal acne vulgaris

- Co-primary endpoints (all three required for success, SAP §4.1.1): IGA success (score of 0 [clear] or 1 [almost clear] with ≥2-grade improvement from baseline) at Week 12; absolute change from baseline in facial non-inflammatory lesion count; absolute change from baseline in facial inflammatory lesion count

- Co-secondary (truncal) endpoints, same structure (SAP §4.1.2): PGA success (score 0/1 with ≥2-grade improvement), absolute change in truncal non-inflammatory lesion count, absolute change in truncal inflammatory lesion count, all at Week 12, tested only conditional on co-primary success

- Sample size/power (SAP §6): powered from a Phase 2 study (SPR18223) assuming IGA success rates of 23% (trifarotene) vs. 15% (vehicle); 504 evaluable subjects/arm for 90% power at two-sided alpha=0.05, inflated to 600 randomized/arm (1,200 total) for an estimated 16% dropout/non-evaluable rate; assumed lesion-count treatment differences of 3 (inflammatory) and 6 (non-inflammatory) lesions gave >95% power at 504 evaluable/arm

- Reported results at Week 12 (label Tables 2-3, ITT/ITTT, multiple imputation): facial IGA success 29.4% (trifarotene) vs. 19.5% (vehicle) in Study 1, 42.3% vs. 25.7% in Study 2; facial inflammatory-lesion LS-mean percent reduction 54.4% vs. 44.8% (Study 1), 66.2% vs. 51.2% (Study 2); facial non-inflammatory-lesion LS-mean percent reduction 49.7% vs. 35.7% (Study 1), 57.7% vs. 43.9% (Study 2); truncal PGA success 35.7% vs. 25.0% (Study 1), 42.6% vs. 29.9% (Study 2) — the approved label reports point estimates only, without p-values or CIs, in its Clinical Studies section

### 23. Teprotumumab-trbw (Tepezza) — BLA 761143

**Sponsor:** Horizon Therapeutics (Horizon Pharma Ireland Ltd.)

**Indication approved:** Active thyroid eye disease (TED) — the first FDA-approved treatment for this indication

**Approval date:** January 21, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** OPTIC (Study 301/HZNP-TEP-301), NCT03298867; supported by Phase 2 Study TED01RV (RV 001), NCT01868997

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, parallel-group phase 2 and phase 3 trials of identical design; 1:1 randomization stratified by tobacco/smoking status; 8 IV infusions (10 mg/kg Day 1, then 20 mg/kg q3W) over a 24-week double-masked treatment period, in a rare-disease-scale population (N=87 Phase 2, N=83 Phase 3)

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint proptosis responder rate at Week 24 (≥2 mm reduction in proptosis in the study eye without ≥2 mm worsening in the fellow eye) — designated FDA's preferred primary measure for the phase 3 trial, with the phase 2 trial's original primary (a broader "overall responder" composite of CAS and proptosis criteria) demoted to first secondary endpoint in Study 301; hierarchically ordered secondary endpoints included overall responder rate, CAS-based responder rate, change in proptosis, diplopia responder rate, and GO-QoL change from baseline

- *Primary analysis:* stratified (by tobacco-use status) difference in proportions, with strata combined via Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel weights — FDA's statistical reviewer explicitly substituted this method for the applicant's preferred covariate-adjusted logistic regression as the analysis presented in labeling ("FDA reviewer substitutes CMH-stratified difference-in-proportions for the applicant's preferred logistic-regression primary analysis"); supportive MMRM analysis of continuous proptosis change from baseline

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence hierarchical testing of ordered secondary endpoints, each tested at alpha=0.05 only if the endpoint immediately preceding it in the hierarchy was statistically significant

- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation (missing Week-24 responder status counted as treatment failure) as the primary approach for both binary responder endpoints, with LOCF, "all dropouts as failures," and observed-cases sensitivity analyses; no special rare-disease-specific inferential accommodation (e.g., no Bayesian borrowing across the two trials, no adaptive design) was used despite the small sample sizes

- *Regulatory:* FDA Dermatologic and Ophthalmologic Drugs Advisory Committee (DODAC) met December 13, 2019 and voted unanimously that benefits outweighed risks; statistical and clinical/medical reviews were filed as separate documents rather than a combined Multi-Discipline Review

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Both trials (Phase 2 TED01RV/NCT01868997, N=87 ITT; Phase 3 OPTIC/NCT03298867, N=83 ITT) were randomized, multicenter, double-masked, placebo-controlled, parallel-group studies in adults with active TED (Clinical Activity Score ≥4 of 7 at baseline), randomized 1:1 stratified by tobacco-use status, receiving 8 infusions of teprotumumab (10 mg/kg Day 1, 20 mg/kg q3W thereafter) or placebo over 24 weeks

- Primary endpoint definitions differed between the two trials: TED01RV's primary was an "overall responder" composite (≥2-point CAS decrease AND ≥2 mm proptosis reduction in the study eye, with no CAS or proptosis deterioration in the non-study eye) at Week 24; OPTIC's primary was the narrower proptosis responder rate (≥2 mm proptosis reduction in the study eye without ≥2 mm proptosis worsening in the fellow eye) at Week 24, with the TED01RV-style overall responder rate carried forward only as OPTIC's first secondary endpoint

- Sample size/power: TED01RV planned for 80% power at two-sided alpha=0.05 (chi-square test) assuming 30% (placebo) vs. 60% (teprotumumab) overall responder rates, yielding ~42/arm; OPTIC planned for 90% power assuming a 39-percentage-point proptosis-responder-rate difference with a 16% dropout allowance, yielding ~45/arm

- Primary statistical method: FDA's statistical review stated the stratified (tobacco status) difference in proportions, combined across strata via Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel weights, was used for the label-presented primary analysis for both trials, in place of the applicant's preferred covariate-adjusted logistic regression, because a logistic model's conditional odds ratio assumes the odds ratio is constant across tobacco-use strata — an assumption FDA did not require

- Reported results (ITT, Week 24): TED01RV proptosis responders 30/42 (71.3%) teprotumumab vs. 9/45 (20.0%) placebo, difference 51.1% (95% CI 32.5, 69.7); overall responders 29/42 (69.1%) vs. 9/45 (20.0%), difference 48.9% (95% CI 30.2, 67.6). OPTIC proptosis responders 34/41 (82.9%) vs. 4/42 (9.5%), difference 73.4% (95% CI 58.9, 87.9); overall responders 32/41 (78.1%) vs. 3/42 (7.1%), difference 70.9% (95% CI 56.0, 85.8)

- FDA also conducted supportive analyses of the non-study (fellow) eye and of relapse among Phase 2 responders during a 48-week off-treatment follow-up (~40% of teprotumumab responders relapsed by Week 72), prompting FDA to suggest the sponsor plan future re-treatment studies for relapsed patients

- FDA's Statistical Review concluded: "There are no major statistical issues identified for the two pivotal studies submitted"

**Other resources**

- No evidence of Vivli or YODA Project participation was identified for Horizon Therapeutics or Amgen (which later acquired Horizon) specific to this program; not independently confirmed as absent beyond a homepage/summary-listing check.

- FDA Advisory Committee: the Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee (DODAC) met December 13, 2019, and "unanimously voted 'Yes', that the potential benefits of using teprotumumab as recommended outweigh the potential risks," while suggesting a larger post-marketing safety study and a possible registry.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

No sponsor SAP or protocol is publicly posted for either trial; the passages below are verbatim FDA Statistical Review text (not a reverse-engineered/inferred reconstruction), quoted directly from the Agency's own description of the pre-specified and as-conducted analyses.

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, p.11, primary endpoint definitions]* — "For Study TED01RV, the primary efficacy endpoint was whether the subject was an overall responder or not (yes or no) at Week 24... For Study 301, the primary efficacy endpoint was the proptosis responder rate, defined as the percentage of subjects with a ≥2 mm reduction from Baseline in proptosis in the study eye, without deterioration [≥2 mm increase] of proptosis in the fellow eye at Week 24. The overall responder rate defined the same as in Study TED01RV was the first secondary efficacy endpoint in this study."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Executive Summary, p.4]* — "It should be noted that the proptosis responder rate is the Agency's clinical review team preferred primary efficacy measure."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, p.12-14, primary analysis method]* — "For Study 301, the primary analysis of the proptosis responder endpoint assessed the stratified difference in the proportions of proptosis responders between the treatment groups... Estimates from the two strata were combined using Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel weights."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, p.13, override of the applicant's method]* — "As discussed in the meeting held on December 12, 2018 with the sponsor, a logistic regression model (with tobacco use as a categorical covariate) estimates the conditional odds ratio based on the assumption that the odds ratio is the same for tobacco users and non-users... Therefore, the statistical review focused on the results of responder analysis using CMH weights where all missing values were considered as treatment failures for both Study TED01RV and Study 301."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, p.14, multiplicity]* — "Secondary endpoints... were analyzed using the ITT Population in a hierarchical manner... teprotumumab was tested against placebo at the 0.05 significance level only if the test statistic was statistically significantly in favor of teprotumumab for the outcome measure preceding it in the hierarchical order."

*[verbatim, FDA Clinical (Medical) Review, Section 7]* — "At least five patients reported hypoacusis/loss of hearing... The mechanism of action for hypoacusis remains unknown. The adverse reaction section of the labeling will include potential hearing impairment." Note: this hearing-impairment signal appears only in the Clinical/Medical Review, not the Statistical Review — no formal inferential statistical test was applied to it in either document.

### 24. Clascoterone (Winlevi) — NDA 213433

**Sponsor:** Cassiopea SpA (c/o Ground Zero Pharmaceuticals, Inc.) — sponsor of record at approval; Sun Pharmaceutical acquired Cassiopea after this original 2020 approval and was not the sponsor of record at the time

**Indication approved:** Topical treatment of acne vulgaris in patients 12 years of age and older

**Approval date:** August 26, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** CB-03-01/25, NCT02608450, and CB-03-01/26, NCT02608476

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two identically-designed, randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled, multicenter, parallel-group phase 3 trials; 1:1 randomization (no stratification factor beyond site); 708 and 732 subjects randomized respectively

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint IGA treatment success at Week 12 (IGA 0/1 with ≥2-grade improvement from baseline); secondary endpoints absolute and percent change from baseline in inflammatory and noninflammatory lesion counts

- *Primary analysis:* logistic regression (treatment, analysis center) for IGA success; ANCOVA (treatment, baseline value, analysis center) for lesion-count endpoints; sites pooled into "analysis centers" by geography/climate when a site had fewer than 8 ITT subjects per arm

- *Multiplicity:* sequential gatekeeping — secondary endpoints tested only if all three co-primary-adjacent efficacy endpoints (IGA success plus both lesion-count endpoints) reached significance at alpha=0.05

- *Missing data/bias:* multiple imputation (Markov Chain Monte Carlo, 10 imputations) as the pre-specified primary missing-data method, with "missing as worst value," "worst case," LOCF, and baseline-observation-carried-forward as sensitivity analyses; FDA found the primary conclusion robust except under the worst-case/worst-value sensitivity analyses, whose assumptions FDA judged unreasonable

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting; FDA's Multi-Discipline Review noted a beneficial treatment effect was not observed in the 9-11-year-old subgroup (very small n), though the approved indication was ultimately not age-restricted above 12

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Two phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled trials of identical design (CB-03-01/25/NCT02608450, N=708: 353 clascoterone/355 vehicle; CB-03-01/26/NCT02608476, N=732: 369/363), enrolling subjects ≥9 years with moderate-to-severe facial acne (IGA 3 or 4, 30-75 inflammatory and 30-100 noninflammatory lesions, ≤2 nodules), randomized 1:1 to clascoterone cream 1% or vehicle cream, both applied twice daily for 12 weeks

- Co-primary-adjacent efficacy endpoints (protocol-specified, all three required before secondary testing proceeded): proportion achieving IGA success (0/1 with ≥2-grade improvement) at Week 12; absolute change from baseline in noninflammatory lesion count at Week 12; absolute change from baseline in inflammatory lesion count at Week 12 — analyzed on the ITT population

- Statistical methods (FDA Multi-Discipline Review, §8): "For the analysis of binary efficacy endpoints, protocols specified using logistic regression with treatment group and analysis center as factors in the model. The protocols specified analyzing continuous efficacy endpoints using analysis of covariance with treatment group, baseline value, and analysis center as factors in the model"

- Missing-data handling: primary method was multiple imputation (Markov Chain Monte Carlo, 10 imputations); sensitivity analyses included Missing as Worst Value, Worst Case, LOCF, and Baseline Observation Carried Forward — FDA found results generally consistent across methods except under the worst-case/worst-value approaches, whose underlying assumption (that all discontinued placebo/vehicle subjects would have succeeded) FDA judged unreasonable

- Sample size/power: not stated with an explicit numeric power calculation in the FDA Multi-Discipline Review's statistical section; the pivotal publication (Hebert et al., *JAMA Dermatol.* 2020) states "at least 350 patients in each treatment arm in each study were required to provide sufficient power (90%)," carried over from an earlier Phase 2 dose-escalation study, without a fully specified effect-size assumption in the portion of the paper reviewed — this power justification is sourced to the publication, not the FDA review, and is flagged accordingly

- Reported results at Week 12 (ITT, adjusted proportions/LS-means): IGA success 18.8% (clascoterone) vs. 8.9% (vehicle) in Study 25, difference 9.9% (95% CI 4.0, 15.7, p<0.001); 20.8% vs. 6.5% in Study 26, difference 14.3% (95% CI 8.9, 19.7, p<0.001); inflammatory lesion change −19.4 vs. −15.5 (Study 25, difference −3.9, 95% CI −6.5, −1.3, p=0.003), −20.0 vs. −12.6 (Study 26, difference −7.4, 95% CI −9.8, −5.0, p<0.001); noninflammatory lesion change −19.4 vs. −13.1 (Study 25, difference −6.3, 95% CI −10.2, −2.4, p=0.002), −19.4 vs. −10.9 (Study 26, difference −8.4, 95% CI −12.4, −4.5, p<0.001)

- FDA's Statistical Issues conclusion: "There were no major statistical issues affecting overall conclusions. The treatment effects were generally consistent across trials and endpoints... It does not appear that any single center drove the overall efficacy results"

The protocols specified that the secondary efficacy endpoints would be tested only if all three coprimary efficacy endpoints were statistically significant at the 0.05 [level]."

### 25. Berotralstat (Orladeyo) — NDA 214094

**Sponsor:** BioCryst Pharmaceuticals

**Indication approved:** Prophylaxis to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adults and pediatric patients 12 years and older

**Approval date:** December 3, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** APeX-2 (BCX7353-302), NCT03485911

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, three-part phase 3 trial in a rare disease (type I/II HAE); 1:1:1 randomization to berotralstat 110 mg, 150 mg, or placebo QD, stratified by baseline attack rate (≥2 vs. <2 attacks/month); Part 1 = 24-week blinded RCT (primary efficacy), Part 2 = 24-week blinded safety extension, Part 3 = 48-week open-label safety

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint rate of investigator-confirmed HAE attacks over the 24-week Part 1 dosing period; secondary endpoints AE-QoL total score change from baseline at Week 24, proportion of days with angioedema symptoms, and attack rate during an "effective treatment period" (Day 8-168)

- *Primary analysis:* negative binomial regression (attack count as dependent variable, treatment as fixed effect, baseline attack-rate stratum as covariate, log duration-on-treatment as offset), selected over the pre-specified default Poisson model per a SAP decision rule triggered by a significantly nonzero dispersion parameter

- *Multiplicity:* combination of hierarchical (step-down) testing and Hochberg step-up procedure across a four-endpoint hierarchy with two doses tested at each level; testing halted after the second endpoint (AE-QoL) failed to reach significance for either dose, converting the remaining two endpoints to nominal/exploratory results

- *Missing data/bias:* on-treatment estimand (ICH E9(R1)) as primary, with treatment-policy (all data including post-discontinuation), and tipping-point sensitivity analyses all giving consistent results

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting/PADAC consultation; single pivotal trial accepted as adequate given "the rarity of the disease" and the robustness of the primary result; FDA statistical review recommended the 150 mg dose based on numerically greater efficacy, while retaining 110 mg for patients with hepatic impairment or GI intolerance

**Trial design & endpoints**

- APeX-2 (BCX7353-302/NCT03485911) was a three-part phase 3 trial in 121 adolescents/adults (≥12 years) with type I or II HAE; Part 1 (24 weeks, the primary efficacy period) randomized subjects 1:1:1 to berotralstat 110 mg QD (N=41), 150 mg QD (N=40), or placebo QD (N=40), stratified by baseline attack rate

- Primary endpoint: "the rate of investigator-confirmed HAE attacks during dosing in the entire 24-week treatment period, defined as day 1 to the time of the first dose of study drug in Part 2 (day 1 to day 168)"

- Statistical method: pre-specified Poisson regression with a built-in decision rule to switch to negative binomial regression if the Poisson model's dispersion parameter indicated significant overdispersion; overdispersion was detected, so the negative binomial model (attack count as dependent variable, treatment as fixed effect, baseline attack-rate stratum as covariate, log treatment-duration as offset) was reported as the primary analysis

- Multiplicity: a combined hierarchical/Hochberg step-up procedure tested, in order, (1) the primary attack-rate endpoint, (2) AE-QoL change from baseline at Week 24, (3) proportion of days with angioedema symptoms, and (4) attack rate during the "effective treatment period" (Day 8-168); AE-QoL was not significant for either dose (110 mg p=0.453, 150 mg p=0.188), so endpoints 3-4 are reported as nominal/exploratory only, not confirmatory

- Sample size/power: the FDA Multi-Discipline Review states only that "the study had adequate statistical power to detect a clinically meaningful difference," without an explicit numeric power/sample-size calculation locatable in the public review — flagged as a sourcing gap, since no protocol/SAP is posted on ClinicalTrials.gov

- Reported primary results (Table 28, FDA review): estimated attack rate/28 days 2.35 (placebo), 1.65 (110 mg), 1.31 (150 mg); attack rate ratio vs. placebo 0.70 (95% CI 0.51, 0.95, p=0.024) for 110 mg and 0.56 (95% CI 0.41, 0.77, p<0.001) for 150 mg; rate reduction 30.0% (95% CI 4.6, 48.7) for 110 mg and 44.2% (95% CI 23.0, 59.5) for 150 mg — attack rate ratio between the two doses was 0.80 (95% CI 0.58, 1.10)

- Dose selection: FDA's review concluded "the totality of safety and efficacy data also support use of the 110 mg once-daily dose for patients who may not tolerate the higher dose due to GI-related adverse reactions or who have moderate to severe hepatic impairment," while recommending 150 mg as the primary approved dose based on its numerically greater effect

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2020/214094s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (Reference ID 4711626; Statistical Reviewer Mingyu Xi, PhD; Statistical Team Leader Yongman Kim, PhD) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/214094Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

No sponsor SAP or protocol is publicly posted for this trial; the passages below are verbatim FDA Multi-Discipline Review text describing the protocol-specified analysis.

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, design]* — "Study BCX7353-302 (Figure 5) is a phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, three-part study in adolescent and adult subjects 12 years of age and older with type I or II HAE."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, primary endpoint]* — "The primary endpoint for Part 1 is the rate of investigator-confirmed HAE attacks during dosing in the entire 24-week treatment period, defined as day 1 to the time of the first dose of study drug in Part 2 (day 1 to day 168)."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, primary analysis method/decision rule]* — "Comparisons of the rate of investigator-confirmed HAE attacks between each berotralstat dose and placebo during the entire dosing period for Part 1 was conducted using a Poisson regression model... the Applicant proposed to analyze the data using a negative binomial model to evaluate the dispersion parameter. If the dispersion parameter of the negative binomial model was significantly greater than zero, the negative binomial model was to be considered primary."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, multiplicity]* — "A combination of hierarchical testing and the Hochberg step-up procedure was used to control the Type I error rate for testing the primary and secondary endpoints in Part 1... At each level of the hierarchy, the Hochberg step-up procedure was used to control the Type I error rate if two doses were tested."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Statistical Issues conclusion]* — "The study achieved clinical and statistical significance on the primary endpoint... There were no statistically significant secondary endpoints after adjusting for multiple testing using the Hochberg procedure. Considering the rarity of the disease, the current unmet need and the robustness of the primary endpoint analysis, the statistical reviewer concludes that substantial evidence of effectiveness was met."

### 26. Tirbanibulin (Klisyri) — NDA 213189

**Sponsor:** Athenex (originator, sponsor of record in the FDA review); Almirall (subsequent commercial licensee, now listed as the ClinicalTrials.gov organization of record)

**Indication approved:** Topical treatment of actinic keratosis on the face or scalp

**Approval date:** December 14, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** KX01-AK-003, NCT03285477, and KX01-AK-004, NCT03285490

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two identically-designed, randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter phase 3 trials; 1:1 randomization stratified by treatment location (face vs. scalp) and site; 5 consecutive once-daily doses (first in-clinic, remaining 4 self-administered); 351 subjects randomized per trial

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint complete (100%) clearance rate of AK lesions in the treatment area at Day 57; key secondary endpoint partial (≥75%) clearance rate at Day 57; additional endpoint recurrence rate at 3/6/9/12 months post-Day-57 among Day-57 complete responders (Kaplan-Meier)

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test controlling for treatment location, with a Breslow-Day test (10% significance level) to explore odds-ratio heterogeneity across treatment-location subgroups

- *Multiplicity:* gatekeeping — the key secondary (partial clearance) endpoint tested only if the primary (complete clearance) endpoint's null hypothesis was rejected

- *Missing data/bias:* very few missing observations (2 vehicle-arm subjects in one trial); pre-specified non-responder imputation for those with missing Day-57 status; FDA reviewer flagged and recommended removing the applicant's unplanned face/scalp subgroup p-values and an unplanned "efficacy over time" plot, both outside the pre-specified SAP (which called for Clopper-Pearson exact CIs by subgroup with no between-subgroup test)

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting; FDA's Multi-Discipline Review explicitly identified and required removal of post hoc, multiplicity-uncontrolled analyses the applicant had added to the proposed label ("FDA reviewer requires removal of applicant-added post hoc/unplanned subgroup or time-course analyses from proposed labeling")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- KX01-AK-003 (NCT03285477) and KX01-AK-004 (NCT03285490) were identically-designed phase 3, randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter trials, each randomizing 351 adults with actinic keratosis of the face or scalp 1:1 to tirbanibulin (KX2-391) ointment 1% or vehicle, applied once daily for 5 consecutive days to a 25 cm² marked treatment area; randomization was stratified by treatment location (face or scalp, enrolled at approximately 2:1) and by study site

- Primary endpoint: "complete (100%) clearance rate of AK lesions, defined as the proportion of subjects at Day 57 with no clinically visible AK lesions in the treatment area"; key secondary endpoint: "partial (≥75%) clearance rate... the proportion of subjects at Day 57 with a ≥75% reduction in the number of AK lesions identified at Baseline"

- Statistical method (FDA Multi-Discipline Review): "analysis of the complete clearance is to be conducted using the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) model controlling for treatment location and treatment group. The Breslow-Day test, with a significance level of 10%, is to be used to explore heterogeneity of the odds ratios across treatment location subgroups... analysis of the Key Secondary Efficacy Endpoint... [uses] the same approach... A gatekeeping testing strategy is applied to control the Type I error rate"

- Sample size/power: as with berotralstat, no explicit numeric power/sample-size justification was locatable in the public FDA Multi-Discipline Review; flagged as a sourcing gap given no protocol/SAP is posted on ClinicalTrials.gov

- Reported primary results (Day 57, complete clearance): Study 003, tirbanibulin 77/175 (44.0%) vs. vehicle 8/176 (4.5%), difference 39.5% (95% CI 31.6, 47.5, p<0.0001); Study 004, tirbanibulin 97/178 (54.5%) vs. vehicle 22/173 (12.7%), difference 41.9% (95% CI 33.1, 50.7, p<0.0001)

- Reported key secondary results (Day 57, partial ≥75% clearance): Study 003, 119/175 (68.0%) vs. 29/176 (16.5%), difference 51.6% (95% CI 42.9, 60.4, p<0.0001); Study 004, 136/178 (76.4%) vs. 34/173 (19.7%), difference 56.9% (95% CI 48.3, 65.4, p<0.0001)

- FDA reviewer flagged and recommended removal of two applicant-added analyses outside the pre-specified SAP: unplanned face/scalp subgroup p-values (the SAP called for Clopper-Pearson exact CIs only, with no between-subgroup hypothesis test), and an unplanned "efficacy over time" plot with uncontrolled multiplicity and unaddressed missing data

No sponsor SAP or protocol is publicly posted for either trial; the passages below are verbatim FDA Multi-Discipline Review text describing the protocol-specified analysis.

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, design]* — "The sponsor conducted identical phase 3 pivotal trials, KX01-AK-003 (003) and KX01-AK-004 (004)... KX02-AK-003 and KX02-AK-004 trials were randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group design conducted at multiple centers. Subjects were enrolled for treatment on the face or scalp at approximately 2:1 ratio, respectively."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, primary/key secondary endpoints]* — "The primary endpoint was complete (100%) clearance rate of AK lesions, defined as the proportion of subjects at Day 57 with no clinically visible AK lesions in the treatment area... The applicant defined the key secondary endpoint as partial (≥75%) clearance rate of AK lesions."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, statistical method]* — "The Protocol/SAP specifies that analysis of the complete clearance is to be conducted using the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) model controlling for treatment location and treatment group... A gatekeeping testing strategy is applied to control the Type I error rate; that is, this endpoint is tested only if the null hypothesis for the primary endpoint is rejected."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, unplanned-analysis critique]* — "The Statistical analysis plan pre-specified that for subgroup analysis, 'Clopper-Pearson Exact 95% CI will be provided for each estimation. But no statistical test will be performed between subgroups.' Yet, the applicant reported p-values for the face and scalp treatment areas for the primary and secondary endpoints in the label. The reviewer suggested to remove the p-values for the treatment area."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, missing data]* — "Missing data were very few, only two subjects in the vehicle arms in Study 003 were discontinued prior to the Day 57 visit, and consequently, treating these two subjects as non-responders, as prespecified in the protocol, had a negligible impact on the reported efficacy results."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Statistical Issues conclusion]* — "There were no major statistical issues affecting the overall conclusions. The treatment effect was generally consistent across the two studies and analysis populations. There were no substantial differences in efficacy among subgroups."

### 27. Voclosporin (Lupkynis) — NDA 213716

**Sponsor:** Aurinia Pharmaceuticals

**Indication approved:** Active lupus nephritis, in combination with a background immunosuppressive therapy regimen, in adults

**Approval date:** January 22, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** AURORA 1, NCT03021499; supported by Phase 2 AURA-LV, NCT02141672

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter (142 sites/27 countries), phase 3 trial; 1:1 randomization to voclosporin 23.7 mg BID or placebo, both arms on background mycophenolate mofetil plus a rapid oral corticosteroid taper, in biopsy-proven Class III, IV, or V lupus nephritis; single pivotal phase 3 trial accepted with a Phase 2 trial (AURA-LV) as confirmatory evidence

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint complete renal response (CRR) at Week 52, a four-component composite (UPCR ≤0.5 mg/mg; eGFR ≥60 mL/min/1.73m² or no confirmed >20% decrease from baseline or no eGFR-associated adverse event; no rescue medication; no more than 10 mg prednisone for ≥3 consecutive days or ≥7 total days during Weeks 44-52); key secondary endpoints partial renal response (50% UPCR reduction) at Weeks 24/52, time to 50% UPCR reduction, and adjudicated renal response at Week 24

- *Primary analysis:* logistic regression (treatment, baseline UPCR, biopsy class, MMF use at baseline, region as covariates) for the binary CRR endpoint, despite the SAP's sample-size calculation having been based on a two-group continuity-corrected chi-squared test

- *Multiplicity:* Hochberg step-up procedure controlling the primary and key secondary endpoints at overall alpha=0.05, applied only if the primary endpoint was significant

- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation embedded directly in the composite endpoint definition (rescue medication, discontinuation, or steroid-taper failure each independently convert a patient to a non-responder); FDA statistical reviewer explicitly recommended reframing rescue medication and steroid use as ICH E9(R1) intercurrent events rather than folding them into the endpoint definition itself; FDA-conducted tipping-point analysis found the result robust (65% of placebo missing-data patients would need to be true responders to lose significance)

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting; FDA accepted a single phase 3 trial as adequate, explicitly invoking "large effect sizes and p-values <0.001" plus Phase 2 (AURA-LV) confirmatory evidence, rather than requiring two independent phase 3 trials

**Trial design & endpoints**

- AURORA 1 randomized 357 adults with active, biopsy-proven Class III, IV, or V lupus nephritis 1:1 to voclosporin 23.7 mg BID (n=179) or placebo (n=178), both arms receiving background mycophenolate mofetil 2 g/day plus an IV methylprednisolone bolus (500 mg/day × 2 days) and rapid oral corticosteroid taper, over 52 weeks, with protocol-specified eGFR- and blood-pressure-based dose adjustment

- Primary endpoint (label-quoted definition): complete renal response at Week 52 requiring UPCR ≤0.5 mg/mg, an eGFR criterion (≥60 mL/min/1.73m², or no confirmed >20% decline from baseline, or no eGFR-associated adverse event), no more than 10 mg prednisone for ≥3 consecutive days or ≥7 total days during Weeks 44-52, and no rescue medication or study withdrawal (both automatically classified as non-response)

- Sample size/power (SAP): planned N=324 (162/arm) for 80% power to detect a placebo response rate of 20.0% vs. a voclosporin rate of 34.4% (OR=2.1) at two-sided alpha=0.05 using a chi-squared test — a different test than the logistic-regression model actually used for the primary analysis

- FDA statistical reviewer's estimand critique (MDR §8.3.3): recommended describing rescue medication and steroid-taper failure as ICH E9(R1) intercurrent events rather than as literal components of the endpoint definition, for better interpretability, while confirming the reported result via an independent tipping-point analysis

- Reported results (ITT, N=357): complete renal response 73/179 (40.8%) voclosporin vs. 40/178 (22.5%) placebo, OR 2.65-2.7 depending on source (95% CI 1.6, 4.3, p<0.001); UPCR component alone 45.3% vs. 23.0% (OR 3.1, 95% CI 1.9, 5.0); eGFR component alone 82.1% vs. 75.8% (OR 1.5, 95% CI 0.8, 2.5, p=0.1, not independently significant — FDA and the sponsor both attribute the overall treatment effect primarily to the UPCR component); complete renal response at Week 24 32.4% vs. 19.7% (OR 2.2, 95% CI 1.3, 3.7); time to 50% UPCR reduction, median 169 vs. 372 days (HR 2.0, 95% CI 1.51, 2.70)

- Supportive Phase 2 (AURA-LV): complete renal response 32.6% (voclosporin) vs. 19.3% (placebo), OR 2.0 (95% CI 1.1, 4.1) — cited by FDA as confirmatory evidence supporting reliance on a single phase 3 trial

- FDA's adequacy-of-evidence rationale (MDR §8.3.2): "FDA generally requires evidence of effectiveness from at least two phase 3 clinical studies... However, evidence from this [single] study was persuasive (large effect sizes and p-values <0.001). In addition, the results from the previous phase 2 study (AURA-LV) provided further evidence of efficacy."

### 28. Anifrolumab-fnia (Saphnelo) — BLA 761123

**Sponsor:** AstraZeneca

**Indication approved:** Moderate to severe systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), in adults receiving standard therapy

**Approval date:** July 30, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** TULIP-2 (study 04), NCT02446899; TULIP-1 (study 05), NCT02446912, a first phase 3 trial that failed its pre-specified primary endpoint; Phase 2 study 1013 (CD-IA-MEDI-546-1013) as additional supportive evidence

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two independent randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter phase 3 trials plus a supportive phase 2 dose-ranging trial; TULIP-1 randomized 1:2:2 (placebo:150mg:300mg, N=457) and TULIP-2 randomized 1:1 (placebo:300mg, N=362), both stratified by screening SLEDAI-2K (<10 vs. ≥10), baseline OCS dose (<10 vs. ≥10 mg/day), and type I IFN gene-signature test result (high vs. low); mid-program primary-endpoint switch, made via a protocol/SAP amendment to the second (not-yet-unblinded) trial before its database lock

- *Endpoints:* TULIP-1's pre-specified primary was SRI-4 (composite of ≥4-point SLEDAI-2K reduction, no PGA worsening, no new BILAG-2004 A/2 new B items, no drug discontinuation, no restricted-medication use) at Week 52; TULIP-2's primary, following the amendment, was BICLA (composite requiring improvement in all baseline BILAG A/B organ systems with no new A or ≥2 new B items, no SLEDAI-2K worsening, no PGA worsening, plus the same discontinuation/medication conditions) at Week 52, with SRI-4 demoted to a key secondary endpoint in TULIP-2

- *Primary analysis:* difference in proportions using Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) weights stratified by the three randomization strata, identical statistical framework applied to both trials' primary endpoints despite the endpoint switch

- *Multiplicity:* weighted Holm procedure (Zhang 1997/Burman 2009) allocating unequal alpha shares (e.g., TULIP-1: 0.04/0.004/0.004/0.001/0.001 across 5 key secondaries) to the primary-plus-ranked-secondary hierarchy, contingent on the primary endpoint reaching significance first; because TULIP-1's primary (SRI-4) failed, none of its secondary results carry formal multiplicity-controlled significance — all are nominal/exploratory only

- *Missing data/bias:* composite (non-responder-imputation) strategy as primary, in which discontinuation or use of restricted/excess medication is folded directly into non-response classification, with a treatment-policy (observed-data) strategy as a supportive ICH E9(R1)-style estimand in both trials; TULIP-1's failure was traced by the sponsor to overly restrictive NSAID- and mild-flare-OCS-use rules misclassifying true responders as non-responders, corrected via a protocol amendment to the still-blinded TULIP-2 before its analysis

- *Regulatory:* no public FDA Advisory Committee meeting, but an internal FDA Medical Policy and Program Review Council (MPPRC) meeting (January 22, 2021) evaluated whether TULIP-2 alone, or TULIP-2 plus TULIP-1/study-1013 as confirmatory evidence, satisfied the substantial-evidence-of-effectiveness standard under 21 U.S.C. §355(d) for a single adequate/well-controlled trial plus confirmatory evidence ("Internal FDA policy-review-council (MPPRC) evaluation of single-trial-plus-confirmatory-evidence adequacy," distinct from a public Advisory Committee)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- TULIP-1 (study 05, NCT02446912, N=457) and TULIP-2 (study 04, NCT02446899, N=362) were both multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials of anifrolumab (150 mg and/or 300 mg IV Q4W) added to standard SLE therapy, stratified by screening SLEDAI-2K, baseline OCS dose, and IFN-signature status; TULIP-1 additionally included a 150 mg dose arm not carried into TULIP-2

- TULIP-1's pre-specified primary endpoint, SRI-4 at Week 52, failed: anifrolumab 300 mg 36% vs. placebo 40%, risk difference −4.2 (95% CI −14.2, 5.8) — the sponsor traced this to protocol-specified restricted-medication rules (particularly NSAID-use rules) that classified some clinically-improved patients as non-responders; a post-hoc reanalysis under revised medication rules found TULIP-1's key secondary BICLA endpoint nominally positive (47% vs. 30%, risk difference 17.0, 95% CI 7.2, 26.8), though this could not be treated as a formal confirmatory result because the primary endpoint had already failed

- In May 2019, before TULIP-2's database lock/unblinding, the sponsor amended TULIP-2's protocol and SAP (with FDA Division agreement) to change its primary endpoint from SRI-4 to BICLA and to revise the restricted-medication rules; FDA's contemporaneous caution, quoted below, explicitly flagged the interpretability risk this created for the overall program

- TULIP-2 primary result: BICLA response 48% (anifrolumab) vs. 31% (placebo), risk difference 16.3 (95% CI 6.3, 26.3), formally significant; SRI-4 (key secondary in TULIP-2) 56% vs. 37%, risk difference 18.2 (95% CI 8.1, 28.3)

- Sample size/power: TULIP-1 planned 180/arm assuming SRI-4 rates of 39% (placebo) vs. 63% (anifrolumab 300 mg), yielding >99% power — the placebo rate landed almost exactly as assumed (40% observed) while the anifrolumab rate came in far below assumption (36% vs. 63% assumed), independently contributing to the failed result beyond the medication-rule issue; TULIP-2's revised power calculation assumed BICLA rates of 30% (placebo) vs. 46% (anifrolumab), based on TULIP-1's own observed results, yielding ~88% power at 180/arm

- FDA's substantial-evidence-of-effectiveness rationale treated TULIP-2 as the single adequate/well-controlled trial, with TULIP-1 and Phase 2 study 1013 — neither individually adequate (TULIP-1 failed its primary; study 1013 used inadequate multiplicity control, tested only at one-sided alpha=0.10) — combined as confirmatory evidence, citing consistency of secondary endpoints (OCS reduction, flare reduction) and interferon-gene-signature neutralization across all three studies, plus mechanistic plausibility

- FDA's internal MPPRC meeting (January 22, 2021) considered two evidentiary framings — treating study 1013 and TULIP-2 as the two adequate/well-controlled trials (if statistically justifiable), or treating TULIP-2 alone as the pivotal trial with the rest as confirmatory evidence — ultimately finding "the evidence for effectiveness persuasive"

An internal FDA Medical Policy and Program Review Council (MPPRC) meeting was held January 22, 2021 to evaluate the substantial-evidence question — this is an internal FDA body, not a public advisory committee, and should not be conflated with one.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, sponsor SAP, TULIP-1 (study 05), Edition 3.0, 20 Aug 2018, multiplicity]* — "To account for multiplicity to test the primary and five key secondary endpoints, a testing strategy will be followed to control the overall type I error rate in the strong sense... the weighted Holm procedure (Zhang, 1997 and Burman, 2009) will be used... the five key secondary endpoints (SRI(4) in the IFN test-high subgroup, steroid reduction, CLASI reduction, SRI(4) at Week 24, and flare rate) will be tested at alpha levels of 0.04, 0.004, 0.004, 0.001, and 0.001, respectively."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Executive Summary, on why TULIP-1 failed]* — "Upon further review of the data, the Applicant indicated that some of the protocol-specified restrictions on medication were not implemented as intended per protocol and were not appropriate based on clinical practice... These rules included restricted use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and limited oral corticosteroids (OCSs) used for mild SLE flares."

*[verbatim, FDA MDR, "Protocol Amendment 2—Change in Restricted Medication Rules"]* — Original rule: "Patients were classified as NR for all subsequent efficacy assessments if a new NSAID was initiated and/or there was an increase in NSAID dosage after day 1." Revised: "Initiation of a new NSAID within 14 days of week 52 and documented use on the day before the week-52 assessment led to classification as NR at the week-52 visit. NSAID use prior to week 50 did not lead to classification as NR."

*[verbatim, FDA MDR, on the mid-program endpoint switch]* — "Noting the treatment effects in BICLA response rate in studies 05 and 1013, the Applicant proposed changing the primary endpoint to BICLA response rate at week 52 for the second phase 3 study (study 04) prior to database lock and unblinding. In May 2019, with agreement from the Division, the Applicant amended the protocol and statistical analysis plan for the ongoing second phase 3 trial, study 04."

*[verbatim, FDA MDR, contemporaneous caution]* — "The Division cautioned that the revision in the statistical plan to incorporate changes to the medication rules and primary endpoint may affect the overall interpretability of efficacy in the overall anifrolumab IV clinical program for SLE."

*[verbatim, FDA MDR, substantial-evidence rationale]* — "There are situations when FDA finds one adequate and well-controlled clinical investigation with confirmatory evidence, including supportive data outside of a controlled trial, is sufficient to establish effectiveness... 04 represents an adequate and well-controlled trial showing favorable and statistically significant changes on the pre-specified, clinically meaningful primary and secondary endpoints... the review team feels that when these trials are considered in combination, the consistent results observed in studies 1013 and 05 do provide confirmatory evidence that support the effectiveness of anifrolumab 300 mg IV."

*[verbatim, FDA MPPRC summary, January 22, 2021]* — "Given the markedly positive study 04, consistency with study 1013, and supportive evidence from the post hoc analysis of study 05, the Council deemed the evidence for effectiveness persuasive."

### 29. Avacopan (Tavneos) — NDA 214487

**Sponsor:** ChemoCentryx (acquired by Amgen in 2022; NDA now held as "ChemoCentryx, Inc., a subsidiary of Amgen")

**Indication approved:** Adjunctive treatment of adult patients with severe active ANCA-associated vasculitis (granulomatosis with polyangiitis and microscopic polyangiitis), in combination with standard therapy including glucocorticoids — label explicitly states "TAVNEOS does not eliminate glucocorticoid use"

**Approval date:** October 7, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** ADVOCATE (CL010_168), NCT02994927

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single randomized, double-blind, active-controlled (prednisone taper), multicenter, phase 3 trial, complement C5a-receptor inhibitor added on to standard induction therapy (rituximab or cyclophosphamide/azathioprine); a genuinely contentious FDA Advisory Committee review with a dead-even efficacy vote

- *Endpoints:* dual primary endpoints — remission at Week 26 (BVAS=0, no glucocorticoid use for AAV in the prior 4 weeks, no BVAS>0 in the prior 4 weeks), tested for non-inferiority (20-percentage-point margin) then superiority; and sustained remission at Week 52 (Week-26 remission maintained with no relapse and no glucocorticoid use for AAV in the prior 4 weeks), also tested for non-inferiority then superiority, in a four-step sequential gatekeeping hierarchy

- *Primary analysis:* summary (stratified) score test using inverse-variance stratum weights with Miettinen-Nurminen score confidence limits — not a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test, despite superficial resemblance to other stratified-proportion analyses in this census

- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation for missing Week-26/Week-52 status, with FDA-conducted tipping-point sensitivity analyses (multiple imputation, 50 datasets, Rubin's method)

- *Regulatory:* FDA Arthritis Advisory Committee met May 6, 2021 and split 9-9 on whether efficacy data supported approval (10-8 favorable on the safety and benefit-risk questions); FDA's own review team recommended a Complete Response Letter, overridden by the Division Director and Office Director; a 2026 Federal Register Notice of Opportunity for Hearing revealed that unblinded sponsor personnel manipulated the Week-52 sustained-remission readjudication after an initial database lock showed the endpoint failing (p=0.1025), reclassifying 5 of 6 flagged avacopan-arm subjects as responders to produce the reported p=0.0132 — the pivotal NEJM publication was formally retracted June 29, 2026, and FDA proposed withdrawal of the NDA in April 2026 ("Post-approval discovery of unblinded-personnel endpoint-readjudication data manipulation, contradicted by a database-lock analysis that failed the pre-specified threshold" and "Pivotal publication retraction triggering an active FDA marketing-withdrawal proceeding, independent of confirmatory-trial failure")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ADVOCATE (CL010_168/NCT02994927) randomized 330 adults with severe active AAV (GPA or MPA) to oral avacopan 30 mg BID (n=166) or oral prednisone taper (n=164), both arms receiving standard induction therapy (rituximab or cyclophosphamide followed by azathioprine); avacopan-arm subjects received a placebo-taper alongside their induction therapy in place of the comparator's prednisone taper

- Primary endpoints (both tested for non-inferiority, margin −20 percentage points, then superiority, in a pre-specified sequential order — NI-Week26, NI-Week52, superiority-Week52, superiority-Week26): remission at Week 26, defined as BVAS=0 (per blinded Adjudication Committee), no glucocorticoid use for AAV in the 4 weeks prior, and no BVAS>0 in the 4 weeks prior; sustained remission at Week 52, defined as Week-26 remission maintained through Week 52 with no relapse (per Adjudication Committee) and no glucocorticoid use for AAV in the prior 4 weeks

- Non-inferiority margin (20 percentage points) was based on the sponsor's meta-analysis of 20 published historical-remission-rate studies — a margin and justification the FDA statistical review explicitly disputed as inadequately supported

- Statistical method: stratified summary score test (inverse-variance stratum weighting, Miettinen-Nurminen score confidence limits), not a CMH test

- Reported results (as originally submitted/reviewed): Week 26 remission 120/166 (72.3%) avacopan vs. 115/164 (70.1%) comparator, difference 3.4% (95% CI −6.0, 12.8); NI met (p<0.0001), superiority not met (FDA table p=0.48; the since-retracted NEJM paper reported p=0.24 — this discrepancy was never independently resolved and may relate to the data-manipulation finding below). Week 52 sustained remission 109/166 (65.7%) vs. 90/164 (54.9%), difference 12.5% (95% CI 2.6, 22.3); NI met (p<0.0001), superiority met as originally reported (FDA table p=0.0132; NEJM p=0.007) — this Week-52 superiority result is the one later shown to have been produced by unauthorized readjudication (see below)

- FDA's internal review split (Multi-Discipline Review): the primary clinical/statistical review team recommended a Complete Response Letter, citing the unjustified non-inferiority margin, failed Week-26 superiority, a Week-52 effect apparently concentrated in the rituximab-induction subgroup rather than the cyclophosphamide/azathioprine subgroup, an Investigator-vs-Adjudicator BVAS discrepancy, and unadjusted secondary-endpoint multiplicity; the Office of Biostatistics Division Director stated she "does not consider the findings statistically very persuasive"; the Division Director for the clinical division (Division of Rheumatology and Transplant Medicine) and the Office Director overrode this recommendation and approved, reasoning that requiring Week-26 superiority given both arms received induction therapy "would be a very high bar"

- FDA Arthritis Advisory Committee, May 6, 2021: voted 9-9 on "Do the efficacy data support approval of avacopan...?" (a dead-even split), 10-8 on whether the safety profile was adequate, and 10-8 on overall benefit-risk adequacy at the proposed dose; committee discussion centered on the appropriateness of the Week-26 non-inferiority comparison, non-study-supplied glucocorticoid use confounding that comparison, the lack of Week-26 superiority, and the Investigator-vs-Adjudicator BVAS discrepancy driving the Week-52 result

- 2026 development: a Federal Register Notice of Opportunity for Hearing (91 Fed. Reg. 23278, April 30, 2026, Docket FDA-2026-N-1321), triggered by an expert report filed in unrelated shareholder securities litigation, found that after a November 5, 2019 database lock showed the Week-52 sustained-remission superiority result failing (p=0.1025 against the pre-specified 0.05 threshold), unblinded ChemoCentryx personnel (Director of Biostatistics and Chief Medical Officer, with an outside statistical consultant) identified 9 subjects for readjudication in violation of the Adjudication Committee Charter's prohibition on post-unblinding readjudication; the Adjudication Committee Chair reclassified 5 of 6 flagged avacopan-arm subjects as responders, flipping the result to the reported p=0.0132, and this earlier failing analysis was not disclosed to FDA in the NDA; the pivotal NEJM publication was retracted June 29, 2026, and FDA's proposal to withdraw approval cites both lack-of-substantial-evidence and untrue-statements-of-material-fact grounds under 21 CFR 314.150(a)(2)(iii)/(iv), separately noting that even without the manipulation finding, "the primary review team did not recommend approval of TAVNEOS" — directly corroborating the internal review dispute documented in 2021

- AstraZeneca-style Vivli/YODA participation does not apply here: ChemoCentryx and Amgen are not listed as Vivli members or YODA Project partners.

- FDA Arthritis Advisory Committee met May 6, 2021, with a 9-9 efficacy vote (see above); as of this writing (September 2026), the drug remains marketed pending the outcome of FDA's 2026 withdrawal proceeding under Docket FDA-2026-N-1321.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA MDR, primary endpoint definitions]* — "The proportion of subjects achieving disease remission at Week 26. Disease remission at Week 26 was defined by: Achieving a BVAS of 0 as determined by the AC; No administration of glucocorticoids for treatment of AAV within 4 weeks prior to Week 26; No BVAS >0 during the 4 weeks prior to Week 26."

*[verbatim, FDA MDR, primary analysis method]* — "The primary analysis compared the remission rates, adjusted for randomization strata, based on the summary score test... using inverse-variance stratum weights and Miettinen-Nurminen (score) confidence limits."

*[verbatim, FDA MDR §8.3, statistical dispute over the NI margin]* — "There are several statistical issues with Study CL010_168, beginning with the Applicant's proposed method to derive the non-inferiority margin... it would be very difficult to determine if a finding of similar remission rates on the proposed comparator arms was due to the efficacy of avacopan or to the fact that the remission rates on both arms were primarily driven by the induction treatment with cyclophosphamide or rituximab."

*[verbatim, FDA MDR §8.4, review team's Complete Response recommendation]* — "The review team recommends a Complete Response for NDA 214487 for avacopan for adult patients with ANCA-associated vasculitis (GPA and MPA), based on the currently available data."

*[verbatim, FDA MDR, OB Division Director]* — "The statistical concerns are clearly articulated in the review... The OB Division Director does not consider the findings statistically very persuasive."

*[verbatim, FDA MDR, Arthritis Advisory Committee, May 6, 2021]* — "Do the efficacy data support approval of avacopan for the treatment of adult patients with AAV (GPA and MPA)?" — Vote: Yes 9, No 9, Abstain 0. "The committee members who voted 'No' agreed that there is not enough substantial clinical and statistical evidence from a single trial to support approval... The committee members who voted 'Yes' agreed that, although the results did not demonstrate complete replacement of steroids, the sparing effect was sufficient enough to warrant approval."

*[verbatim, FDA Federal Register Notice of Opportunity for Hearing, April 30, 2026]* — "New information shows that the applicant's unblinded study personnel manipulated endpoint results for the phase 3 study, CL010_168, referred to as the ADVOCATE study, which was the sole study used to establish substantial evidence of effectiveness for approval of TAVNEOS. That manipulation was designed to change results that were not statistically significant and make the product look effective when the original analysis did not support that conclusion."

*[verbatim, FDA Federal Register Notice, internal email quoted by FDA]* — Dr. Pirow Bekker (ChemoCentryx CMO) to Dr. Huibin Yue (Director of Biostatistics), November 9, 2019: "Regarding sustained remission at Week 52 it is, of course, of paramount importance that the data are correct (especially the p-value for superiority)... We cannot afford to miss a superiority outcome."

*[verbatim, FDA Federal Register Notice, on the original review team's position]* — "the primary review team did not recommend approval of TAVNEOS. In other words, even without knowledge of the data manipulation by unblinded personnel, the primary review team had significant concerns regarding whether there was a demonstration of substantial evidence of effectiveness."

### 30. Tezepelumab-ekko (Tezspire) — BLA 761224

**Sponsor:** AstraZeneca (co-developed with Amgen)

**Indication approved:** Add-on maintenance treatment of adult and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older with severe asthma, without a required eosinophilic/allergic-phenotype biomarker restriction

**Approval date:** December 17, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** NAVIGATOR, NCT03347279; supported by Phase 2 PATHWAY; a third trial, SOURCE (steroid-sparing), failed its primary endpoint and was not part of the effectiveness basis

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, global phase 3 trial (297 sites/18 countries); enrollment deliberately not restricted by baseline eosinophil count, with enrollment quotas targeting similar proportions of <300 and ≥300 eosinophils/µL subjects, so the phenotype-agnostic efficacy claim was a planned analysis from the outset rather than a post hoc finding

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint annualized asthma exacerbation rate (AAER) over 52 weeks; pre-specified biomarker-stratified subgroup analyses across four eosinophil strata (<150, 150-<300, 300-<450, ≥450 cells/µL) and three FeNO strata

- *Primary analysis:* negative binomial regression (treatment, region, age group, baseline exacerbation history as covariates; log time-at-risk as offset), overdispersion parameter 1.41

- *Multiplicity:* primary endpoint tested at a strengthened one-sided-equivalent threshold (0.01, not the conventional 0.05) within an overall strongly-controlled family-wise alpha of 0.05 across primary and key secondary endpoints; FDA directed the applicant to add the pre-specified <300 eosinophils/µL subgroup into the formal multiple-testing procedure rather than leaving it as an unprotected exploratory analysis

- *Missing data/bias:* multiple imputation under both MAR and MNAR ("copy reference"/dropout-reason-based) assumptions, with tipping-point sensitivity analyses for key continuous secondary endpoints; FDA concluded the missing-data sensitivity analyses "did not impact any conclusions from the primary analyses"

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting ("the review team did not identify any controversial or precedent setting issue"); substantial evidence of effectiveness rested on two adequate/well-controlled trials (NAVIGATOR phase 3 plus PATHWAY phase 2, the latter acknowledged to have "some statistical issues" including no alpha=0.05 power target and no secondary-endpoint multiplicity adjustment), with a third trial (SOURCE, steroid-sparing) excluded from the effectiveness basis after failing its primary endpoint

**Trial design & endpoints**

- NAVIGATOR (NCT03347279) randomized 1,061 patients (528 tezepelumab 210 mg SC Q4W / 531 placebo) aged 12-80 with severe, uncontrolled asthma on medium/high-dose inhaled corticosteroids plus at least one additional controller, at 297 sites in 18 countries, with enrollment not restricted by baseline eosinophil count and quotas set to balance <300 and ≥300 eosinophils/µL enrollment

- Primary endpoint: annualized asthma exacerbation rate at Week 52, analyzed via negative binomial regression with treatment, region, age group, and exacerbation history as covariates and log time-at-risk as an offset (overdispersion parameter 1.41 per the CSR)

- Reported primary result: AAER reduced 56% vs. placebo overall (rate ratio 0.44, 95% CI 0.37, 0.53, p<0.001; crude rates 0.84 vs. 1.91 exacerbations/year)

- Pre-specified biomarker-stratified subgroup results, added to the formal multiple-testing procedure at FDA's direction for the <300 eosinophils/µL stratum: rate ratio 0.59 (95% CI 0.46, 0.75, p<0.001), a 41% reduction; across four eosinophil strata (<150, 150-<300, 300-<450, ≥450 cells/µL), reductions of 39%, 43%, 59%, and 77% respectively, with all four confidence intervals excluding 1; across three FeNO strata (<25, 25-<50, ≥50 ppb), reductions of 32%, 60%, and 73% — magnitude of benefit increased with biomarker level, but efficacy was demonstrated across every stratum including the lowest

- FDA's framing of the phenotype-agnostic result: "This benefit was demonstrated regardless of baseline eosinophil or FeNO levels. This distinguishes tezepelumab from other biologic products that are indicated for a specific asthma population, such as eosinophilic phenotype or allergic asthma"

- Multiplicity: primary endpoint tested at alpha=0.01 (strengthened from the conventional 0.05) as part of an overall family-wise-controlled 0.05 hierarchy spanning the primary and key secondary endpoints; subgroup interaction testing found both eosinophil count and FeNO had statistically significant treatment-by-subgroup interaction terms, while IgE did not

- Effectiveness basis: two adequate/well-controlled trials — NAVIGATOR (phase 3) and PATHWAY (phase 2, N=552, three dose arms) — with PATHWAY's contribution qualified by FDA as having "some statistical issues that could have limited its utility" (not powered at conventional alpha, no secondary-endpoint multiplicity control); a third trial, SOURCE (steroid-sparing indication, N=150), failed its primary endpoint (oral-corticosteroid-dose-reduction odds ratio 1.28, 95% CI 0.69, 2.35) and was excluded from the effectiveness basis, though it did not prevent approval of the add-on maintenance indication actually sought

### 31. Tralokinumab-ldrm (Adbry) — BLA 761180

**Sponsor:** LEO Pharma A/S

**Indication approved:** Treatment of moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis in adult patients whose disease is not adequately controlled with topical prescription therapies or when those therapies are not advisable; can be used with or without topical corticosteroids

**Approval date:** December 27, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** ECZTRA 1, NCT03131648; ECZTRA 2, NCT03160885; ECZTRA 3, NCT03363854 (ECZTRA 1/2 are identically designed 52-week monotherapy trials; ECZTRA 3 is a 32-week trial of tralokinumab as add-on to topical corticosteroids; all three were co-pivotal for the BLA)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* multicenter randomized double-blind placebo-controlled parallel-group phase 3, two identically-designed monotherapy trials plus one TCS-combination trial, ICH E9(R1) estimand framework, initial-treatment/re-randomized-maintenance design (ECZTRA 1/2), initial/continuation-treatment design (ECZTRA 3)

- *Endpoints:* co-primary/key-secondary binary responder endpoints (IGA 0/1 at Week 16 as primary, EASI-75 at Week 16 as key secondary per FDA advice letter), secondary Worst Daily Pruritus NRS ≥4-point reduction, secondary maintenance endpoints (IGA 0/1 and EASI-75 at Week 52/Week 32 among Week-16 responders)

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by region and baseline disease severity (IGA 3 vs 4); primary ("composite") estimand defined as treatment difference in response achieved without rescue medication regardless of treatment discontinuation

- *Multiplicity:* dedicated modified fixed-sequence testing hierarchy for the US submission (IGA 0/1 → EASI-75 → Pruritus NRS, each at 5%, sequential), followed by parallel alpha-split (1% Week-16 secondary endpoints via Holm procedure / 4% Week-52 maintenance endpoints) with reallocation if one family fully rejects; separate non-US (EU/Japan) hierarchy retained from protocol

- *Missing data/bias:* multiple imputation (SAS PROC MI, prespecified seeds) under missing-at-random within composite/hypothetical/treatment-policy estimands; non-responder imputation for rescue-medication users; post-hoc tipping-point sensitivity analyses (added after FDA advice) for both binary and continuous secondary endpoints

- *Regulatory:* BLA (biologic, IL-13 antagonist), no advisory committee meeting held, three co-primary trials pooled in an FDA "Integrated Review" template rather than a separate stand-alone Statistical Review

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ECZTRA 1 (NCT03131648) and ECZTRA 2 (NCT03160885): identically designed, randomized, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 monotherapy trials in adults with moderate-to-severe AD inadequately controlled by topical therapy or for whom topicals were inadvisable; key eligibility included AD ≥1 year, BSA ≥10%, IGA ≥3, EASI ≥16, Worst Daily Pruritus NRS ≥4 in the week before baseline; ~780 subjects per trial randomized 3:1 to tralokinumab 300 mg Q2W (600 mg loading dose) or placebo, stratified by region and baseline IGA (3 vs 4); 16-week initial treatment period, 36-week re-randomized maintenance period (Week 16 responders re-randomized 2:2:1 to tralokinumab Q2W/Q4W/placebo), 16-week off-treatment follow-up

- ECZTRA 3 (NCT03363854): randomized, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial of tralokinumab as adjunct to topical corticosteroids (TCS) in adults with moderate-to-severe AD; ~369 subjects randomized 2:1 to tralokinumab 300 mg+TCS or placebo+TCS, stratified by region and baseline IGA; 16-week initial treatment period, 16-week continuation-treatment period (Week-16 responders re-randomized 1:1 to continue tralokinumab Q2W or de-escalate to Q4W), 14-week follow-up

- Primary endpoints (all three trials, Week 16): proportion of subjects with IGA 0 (clear) or 1 (almost clear) ("IGA 0/1"); proportion with ≥75% reduction in EASI from baseline ("EASI-75"); per the FDA's 6/23/2017 advice letter, because IGA 0/1 and EASI-75 are tested sequentially with IGA 0/1 first, IGA 0/1 is the primary endpoint and EASI-75 is a key secondary endpoint

- Secondary endpoints: ≥4-point reduction in Worst Daily Pruritus NRS weekly average from baseline to Week 16 (among subjects with baseline score ≥4); change in SCORAD and DLQI from baseline to Week 16 (exploratory per FDA — not required for labeling, per Pre-BLA meeting minutes); maintenance endpoints — IGA 0/1 and EASI-75 at Week 52 (ECZTRA 1/2) or Week 32 (ECZTRA 3) among subjects who were Week-16 responders on tralokinumab

- Sample size/power (from protocol, Section 12.1): a total of 780 subjects were to be randomized 3:1 to initial treatment (585 tralokinumab; 195 placebo) in ECZTRA 1/2; for IGA 0/1 at Week 16, this provides >99% power to detect a difference of 30% for tralokinumab vs. 10% for placebo at a 5% two-sided significance level; for EASI-75 at Week 16, the same sample provides >99% power assuming response rates of 40% and 15% respectively; no formal efficacy interim analysis/alpha-spending was used (single fixed Week-16/Week-52 analyses); safety was monitored on an ongoing basis without an efficacy DMC

- Statistical methods: CMH test stratified by region and baseline IGA severity for binary endpoints; three estimands per ICH E9(R1) — primary ("composite": response without rescue medication regardless of discontinuation), secondary ("hypothetical": response assuming full adherence, no rescue, no discontinuation), tertiary ("treatment policy": response regardless of rescue/discontinuation); multiple imputation via SAS PROC MI for the hypothetical and treatment-policy estimands; tipping-point sensitivity analyses added late in development at FDA's request

For the endpoint IGA 0/1 at Week 16, a sample size of 780 subjects randomised at 3:1 will provide >99% power to detect a difference between the 2 arms of 30% for tralokinumab and 10% for placebo at a 5% 2-sided level of significance. If all three tests are significant, the significance level (alpha) will be split between the analyses of the 2 secondary endpoints at Week 16 and the analyses of the 2 maintenance endpoints at Week 52. These groups of tests are tested in parallel with alpha=1% for the endpoints at Week 16 and with alpha=4% for the maintenance endpoints at Week 52... The evaluations of the 2 secondary endpoints at Week 16 between tralokinumab and placebo will use the Holm method (3) for 2 ordered p-values at a 1% significance level to adjust for multiplicity."

- *[verbatim, ECZTRA 3 SAP (LP0162-1339, v1.0, 15-Jul-2019), Section 6.6.1, pp.13-14]* — "If all three tests are significant, the evaluations of the other two secondary endpoints SCORAD and DLQI at Week 16 between tralokinumab and placebo will use the Holm method (3) for 2 ordered p-values at a 5% significance level to adjust for multiplicity" — note this differs slightly from the ECZTRA 1/2 alpha-split structure because ECZTRA 3 has no separate maintenance-period co-testing family

Secondary estimand, hypothetical: Treatment difference in response rates of IGA 0/1 and EASI-75 after 16 weeks if all subjects adhered to the treatment regimen... Tertiary estimand, treatment policy: Treatment difference in response rate after 16 weeks regardless of rescue medication and treatment discontinuation."

ECZTRA-2: IGA 0/1 123/577 (21%) vs 18/193 (9%), difference 12% (7%,17%), p<0.001; EASI-75 188/577 (33%) vs 19/193 (10%), difference 22% (17%,28%), p<0.001

### 32. Abrocitinib (Cibinqo) — NDA 213871

**Sponsor:** Pfizer Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adults with refractory, moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis whose disease is not adequately controlled with other systemic drug products, including biologics, or when use of those therapies is inadvisable (limitation of use: not recommended in combination with other JAK inhibitors, biologic immunomodulators, or other immunosuppressants); boxed warning for serious infections, mortality, malignancy, MACE, and thrombosis

**Approval date:** January 14, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** JADE MONO-1 (B7451012), NCT03349060; JADE MONO-2 (B7451013), NCT03575871; JADE COMPARE (B7451029), NCT03720470 (JADE MONO-1/2 are identically designed 12-week monotherapy trials in ages ≥12; JADE COMPARE is an adults-only trial adding placebo/dupilumab arms on background topical therapy)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* multicenter randomized double-blind (double-dummy in JADE COMPARE) placebo-controlled parallel-group phase 3, two identically-designed monotherapy trials plus one active/placebo-controlled combination-therapy trial, adolescents included in monotherapy trials (age ≥12), external Data Monitoring Committee (E-DMC) for safety

- *Endpoints:* co-primary binary responder endpoints (IGA 0/1 with ≥2-point improvement, and EASI-75, both at Week 12), key secondary endpoints including PP-NRS4 (≥4-point pruritus reduction) at Weeks 2/4/12 and PSAAD, JADE COMPARE additionally added dupilumab as active comparator (non-inferiority/superiority not formally tested against dupilumab — only against placebo) with Week-16 secondary endpoints

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test adjusting for baseline disease severity (all trials) and age category (monotherapy trials only); non-responder imputation as primary handling of intercurrent events (permanent discontinuation → non-responder at all subsequent visits)

- *Multiplicity:* sequential Bonferroni-based iterative multiple testing procedure ("gatekeeping"/consonant closed-test class per Hommel et al. 2007) across two doses (200 mg, 100 mg) and a fixed sequence of co-primary and key secondary endpoints, with unused alpha reallocated between parallel testing paths depending on which hypotheses are rejected first

- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation (NRI) as primary approach; tipping-point multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis using a Bayesian GLMM with MCMC and weighted MAR/jump-to-reference mixtures (weights 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1; 500 replications, seed=332786); acknowledged pruritus-NRS eDiary data-collection technical failure in the monotherapy trials required a hybrid imputation approach

- *Regulatory:* NDA, review-clock extension and missed PDUFA goal date due to class-wide JAK-inhibitor safety signal from the tofacitinib ORAL Surveillance postmarketing trial, resulting in a narrowed/refractory-population indication and boxed warning; no advisory committee meeting held; 4-year postmarketing observational safety study required

**Trial design & endpoints**

- JADE MONO-1 (B7451012, NCT03349060) and JADE MONO-2 (B7451013, NCT03575871): identically designed, randomized, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group phase 3 monotherapy trials of abrocitinib in subjects ≥12 years (body weight ≥40 kg) with moderate-to-severe AD; eligibility required BSA ≥10%, IGA ≥3, EASI ≥16, pruritus NRS ≥4 at baseline, and a documented recent history of inadequate response to topicals (or topicals medically inadvisable); ~375 subjects per trial randomized 2:2:1 to abrocitinib 200 mg QD, 100 mg QD, or placebo, stratified by baseline disease severity (IGA 3 vs 4) and age (<18 vs ≥18); 28-day screening, 12-week double-blind treatment period, 4-week follow-up (or transition to long-term extension B7451015)

- JADE COMPARE (B7451029, NCT03720470): multicenter, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial in adults only, adding an active dupilumab arm, all on standardized background topical therapy (emollients + TCS, with topical calcineurin inhibitors/crisaborole permitted on thin-skin areas); ~700 subjects randomized in a 4:4:4:1:1 ratio across abrocitinib 100 mg/200 mg (each with dupilumab-matching placebo), dupilumab 300 mg Q2W (600 mg loading, with abrocitinib-matching placebo), and two placebo sequences later pooled into an effective 2:2:2:1 ratio through Week 16; randomization not stratified by severity or age per protocol; 28-day screening, 16-week randomized double-blind/double-dummy period plus 4 additional weeks of oral-only blinded treatment (Weeks 16-20) to wash out dupilumab before long-term extension eligibility, 4-week follow-up

- Co-primary efficacy endpoints (all three trials, Week 12): IGA 0/1 (clear or almost clear, with ≥2-point improvement from baseline); EASI-75 (≥75% reduction in EASI from baseline). Per the FDA's 2/15/2018 advice letter, IGA was considered the "main primary endpoint" even though both were co-primary

- Key secondary endpoints: monotherapy trials — PP-NRS4 (≥4-point pruritus NRS reduction) at Weeks 2, 4, and 12, and change in PSAAD total score at Week 12; JADE COMPARE — PP-NRS4 at Week 2, IGA 0/1 at Week 16, and EASI-75 at Week 16

- Sample size/power: from the JADE MONO-1 SAP — a sample of 150 subjects randomized to abrocitinib 200 mg QD, 150 to 100 mg QD, and 75 to placebo would provide at least 95% power to detect a difference in IGA response rate of at least 20% between either dose and placebo, assuming a placebo response rate of 6% at Week 12; the same design provides at least 99% power to detect a difference in EASI-75 response rate of at least 30%, assuming a placebo response rate of 15%; the power to reject both co-primary hypotheses simultaneously was estimated at least 94% depending on the correlation between endpoints. No formal interim efficacy analysis was conducted in any of the three trials; each used a single external Data Monitoring Committee (E-DMC) for safety oversight, not alpha-spending

- Statistical methods: CMH test adjusting for randomization strata (baseline severity and, in monotherapy trials, age) for binary endpoints; MMRM (unstructured covariance, falling back to compound symmetry on non-convergence) for continuous PSAAD; sequential Bonferroni-based gatekeeping multiple testing procedure across doses and the endpoint hierarchy; non-responder imputation as the primary missing-data method, with a Bayesian tipping-point multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis
