A sample of 150 subjects randomized to PF-04965842 200 mg QD, 150 subjects randomized to PF-04965842 100 mg QD and 75 subjects randomized to placebo would provide at least 95% power to detect a difference in IGA response rate of at least 20% between PF-04965842 200 mg QD (or PF-04965842 100 mg QD) and placebo, assuming the placebo response rate is 6% at Week 12... The Type-I error for testing each individual co-primary endpoint was set at 5%. Since both endpoints are co-primary, the study will meet its primary endpoint only if both hypotheses... are rejected."

- *[verbatim, JADE MONO-1 SAP, Section 3.1 "Primary Endpoints", p.9]* — "The co-primary efficacy endpoints are: Response based on the IGA score of clear (0) or almost clear (1); and a reduction from baseline of 2 points at Week 12."

- *[verbatim, JADE MONO-1 SAP, pp.14-16 "Multiple Testing Procedure"]* — "A sequential Bonferroni-based iterative multiple testing procedure to strongly control the familywise Type 1 error at 5% will be used for testing each of the two PF-04965842 doses (200 mg QD and 100 mg QD) versus placebo on the primary and key secondary endpoints. The procedure belongs to a class of consonant multiple test procedures (Hommel et al. 2007) which are a subclass of the closed test procedures (Marcus et al. 1976). The procedure will first test the Week 12 co-primary endpoints (IGA and EASI-75) for 200 mg QD vs placebo at a 5% significant level. If this hypothesis is not rejected, then no further testing will be conducted... Hypotheses for all other endpoints not described here are to be tested at the nominal 5% significant level, without making adjustments for multiple comparisons."

- *[verbatim, JADE MONO-1 SAP, tipping-point method description, p.86 of FDA MDR quoting SAP]* — "The observed IGA/EASI-75 responses at Weeks 2, 4, 8, and 12 are used for the imputation model which is a logit Generalized Linear Mixed Model (GLMM)... Estimation of the parameters from this model is performed under the Bayesian framework using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC)... Five sets of complete imputed data are created using weight=0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1. Values of 0 and 1 for this weight corresponded to analyses under Missing at Random (MAR) and Jump-to-Reference (JTR), respectively. The process is repeated 500 times using seed=332786."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, "Analysis methods for the primary and key secondary endpoints", p.83]* — "The protocols/SAPs specified analyzing the co-primary endpoints (i.e., IGA 0/1 and EASI-75) and the binary key secondary endpoints using the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test adjusting for baseline disease severity (all trials) and age (only for monotherapy trials)."

A re-evaluation of the benefits vs. risks of abrocitinib was deemed necessary in a more refractory patient population... A 4-year prospective observational study will be required to assess potential serious risks associated with use of the product including major adverse cardiovascular events, malignancy, thrombosis, serious infections and retinal detachment."

### 33. Tapinarof (Vtama) — NDA 215272

**Sponsor:** Dermavant Sciences, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Topical treatment of plaque psoriasis in adults

**Approval date:** May 23, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** PSOARING 1 (Protocol DMVT-505-3001), NCT03956355; PSOARING 2 (Protocol DMVT-505-3002), NCT03983980 — two identically designed replicate Phase 3 trials, per the FDA statistical review: "The Applicant conducted two identically designed Phase 3 trials"

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* replicate randomized double-blind vehicle-controlled trials, parallel-group, topical dermatology cream, stratified randomization

- *Endpoints:* binary responder endpoint (PGA treatment success), PASI-75/PASI-90 co-secondary, static Physician Global Assessment (PGA)

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by baseline PGA, ANCOVA for continuous secondaries, multiple imputation as primary missing-data method

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (hierarchical) gatekeeping across 4 ordered secondary endpoints, testing stops at first non-significant result

- *Missing data/bias:* multiple imputation (MI, 100 imputations, fully conditional specification) as primary method; LOCF, non-responder imputation (NRI), and observed-case as sensitivity analyses; tipping-point sensitivity analysis; COVID-19 alternative-visit (phone/virtual) handling

- *Regulatory:* standard review, no Advisory Committee meeting held ("no efficacy or safety issues were identified that required input from Advisory Committee")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Design: two identical double-blind, randomized, vehicle-controlled, multicenter, parallel-group Phase 3 trials (~50-60 US/Canada sites each); 34-day screening then 12 weeks double-blind treatment, optional rollover into a 40-week open-label long-term extension (PSOARING 3 / DMVT-505-3003), with a Week 16 follow-up for non-continuers

- Population/eligibility: adults 18-75 years with chronic plaque psoriasis, stable disease ≥6 months, body surface area (BSA) involvement ≥3% and ≤20% (excluding scalp/palms/nails/soles from %BSA), baseline PGA score of 2 (mild), 3 (moderate), or 4 (severe)

- Randomization/stratification: 2:1 tapinarof cream 1% vs. vehicle cream, once daily; stratified by baseline PGA score so that PGA=2 and PGA=4 subjects were each capped at ~10% of the randomized population and ~80% had PGA=3 (moderate disease)

- Arms: tapinarof cream 1% once daily (~333 subjects/trial) vs. vehicle cream once daily (~167 subjects/trial)

- Primary endpoint: proportion of subjects achieving a PGA treatment response, defined as a PGA score of clear (0) or almost clear (1) with a minimum 2-grade improvement from baseline, at Week 12

- Secondary endpoints (tested in fixed hierarchical order): (1) proportion with ≥75% improvement in PASI (PASI-75) from baseline at Week 12; (2) proportion with PGA score of 0 or 1 at Week 12; (3) mean change in %BSA affected from baseline to Week 12; (4) proportion with ≥90% improvement in PASI (PASI-90) from baseline to Week 12

- Exploratory endpoints: time to PGA response (Kaplan-Meier, censored at last PGA assessment for non-responders), PGA/PASI/%BSA at Weeks 2, 4, 8; patient-reported outcomes (Peak Pruritus-NRS, DLQI)

- Sample size/power: assumed 40% tapinarof vs. 15% vehicle response; with 500 subjects randomized 2:1 (~333:167), power >99% at 2-sided α=0.05 (Fisher exact sample-size calculation, described in the SAP as "conservative"); power remained >94% under a more conservative 35% vs. 20% assumption; up to 25% loss to follow-up assumed and handled via multiple imputation within the ITT population; no formal interim analysis

- Statistical methods: primary analysis population was intent-to-treat (ITT, all randomized subjects), with per-protocol (PP) as a supportive analysis; binary endpoints analyzed via CMH test stratified by baseline PGA; continuous endpoints via ANCOVA with treatment, baseline PGA (categorical), and baseline value as covariates; missing efficacy data primarily handled via multiple imputation (100 imputations, SAS PROC MI, fully conditional specification with treatment, baseline PGA, and prior post-baseline values as predictors), with LOCF, non-responder imputation, and observed-case as sensitivity analyses, plus an Applicant tipping-point analysis; multiplicity controlled via fixed-sequence (hierarchical) gatekeeping — secondary endpoints tested only if the primary endpoint reached significance at 2-sided α=0.05, and testing stopped at the first non-significant secondary comparison; both trials additionally required ad hoc handling of COVID-19-driven "alternative visits" (modified in-clinic, phone, virtual), analyzed both as-observed and as-missing

"For both analyses, tapinarof was statistically superior to vehicle in both trials (p-values < 0.001)."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review, Section 8.1.5, p.81, describing tipping-point sensitivity]* — "The results tip for Trial DMVT-505-3001 when a very high proportion of the missing data for vehicle is imputed as successes and a very high proportion of the missing data for tapinarof is imputed as failures. ### 34. Spesolimab-sbzo (Spevigo) — BLA 761244

**Sponsor:** Boehringer Ingelheim Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of generalized pustular psoriasis (GPP) flares in adults

**Approval date:** September 1, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** Effisayil 1 (BI Trial No. 1368-0013), NCT03782792 — "Effisayil™ 1: Multi-center, Double-blind, Randomised, Placebo-controlled, Phase II Study to Evaluate Efficacy, Safety and Tolerability of a Single Intravenous Dose of Spesolimab (BI 655130) in Patients With Generalized Pustular Psoriasis (GPP) Presenting With an Acute Flare of Moderate to Severe Intensity"

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* small-N single-dose randomized placebo-controlled Phase 2 trial, rare-disease pivotal trial, single adequate and well-controlled trial supporting approval, orphan drug, breakthrough therapy

- *Endpoints:* binary responder endpoint at Day 8 (GPPGA pustulation subscore of 0), key secondary GPPGA 0/1, hierarchical secondary endpoints (GPPASI-75, pain VAS, PSS, FACIT-Fatigue)

- *Primary analysis:* Suissa-Shuster Z-pooled test (an exact unconditional test, more powerful than Fisher's exact test), one-sided α=0.025, Wilson-score/Chan-Zhang confidence interval for risk difference

- *Multiplicity:* pre-specified sequential/hierarchical gatekeeping across 6 ordered endpoints at one-sided α=0.025, each step conditional on rejection of the prior null

- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation (NRI) as primary method for the binary primary endpoint, with escape/rescue medication and death treated as non-response; worst-case rank imputation for continuous secondary endpoints; small sample size explicitly limited subgroup and safety-database interpretability (FDA statistical reviewer)

- *Interim/alpha-spending:* none — single planned analysis at trial completion (sample size not adequately large to support interim analysis in a rare-disease trial)

- *Regulatory:* Orphan Drug designation (Oct 3, 2018), Breakthrough Therapy designation (Apr 30, 2021), Priority Review; no Advisory Committee meeting; approval grounded in a single pivotal trial under 21 CFR 314.126 given disease rarity/severity

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Design: multicenter, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, single-dose Phase 2 trial in patients presenting with an acute GPP flare; single 900 mg IV dose of spesolimab or placebo on Day 1, followed for 12 weeks (extendable to 28 weeks depending on response); randomization stratified by Japan vs. non-Japan (operational only, not an analysis covariate); patients with continued/worsening disease at Day 8 were eligible for open-label rescue spesolimab

- Population/eligibility: adults with a documented history of GPP (per ERASPEN criteria) presenting with an acute flare of moderate-to-severe intensity, defined by GPPGA total score ≥3 (moderate), fresh pustules (new appearance or worsening), GPPGA pustulation subscore ≥2, and ≥5% body surface area covered by erythema with pustules; no active-comparator arm was used because no approved GPP therapy existed to serve as a comparator and biologics/retinoids/cyclosporine lacked established effect sizes in acute GPP

- Arms: spesolimab 900 mg single IV dose (35 randomized) vs. placebo (18 randomized); planned enrollment was "at least 51 patients" (2:1); 85 patients were screened across 37 centers in 12 countries to reach the 53 randomized

- Primary endpoint: a GPPGA pustulation subscore of 0 (indicating no visible pustules) at Week 1 (Day 8); death or any use of escape medication before the Week 1 assessment was counted as non-response

- Key secondary endpoint: GPPGA total score of 0 or 1 at Week 1, tested hierarchically only if the primary endpoint was significant

- Additional hierarchical secondary endpoints (tested in pre-specified order, each conditional on the prior step): GPPASI-75 at Week 4; change from baseline in Pain VAS at Week 4; change from baseline in Psoriasis Symptom Scale (PSS) at Week 4; change from baseline in FACIT-Fatigue total score at Week 4

- Sample size/power: protocol Section 7.7 specified a simulation-based power calculation (R v3.3.2) assuming ~60% response with spesolimab vs. ~10% with placebo on both the primary and key secondary endpoints (endpoint correlation fixed at 0.65, derived from proof-of-concept study 1368.11); for N=51 (34:17) at one-sided α=0.025, power to jointly achieve both the primary and key secondary endpoints was estimated at 93.9% under the 60%-vs-10% scenario; no interim analysis was planned

- Statistical methods: primary analysis population was the Randomized Set (RS, all randomized subjects), with the Per-Protocol Set (PPS) as a supportive analysis; the primary binary endpoint was analyzed with the Suissa-Shuster Z-pooled test — an exact test chosen explicitly because "the traditional Fisher's exact test may be unnecessarily conservative" while the Suissa-Shuster test "always preserves the type I error level and is usually more powerful than the Fisher's exact test"; 95% CI for the risk difference used the Chan and Zhang / Wilson-score method; continuous secondary endpoints used the Wilcoxon rank-sum test with pre-specified worst-case rank imputation for patients who died, used escape/rescue medication, or received open-label spesolimab at Day 8 before the Week 4 assessment; missing binary data were primarily handled via non-responder imputation

- Advisory committee meeting: none held. The FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review states: "The application was not presented to an Advisory Committee or other external consult."

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, Effisayil 1 protocol (BI 1368-0013), Section 3.3 Selection of Trial Population, p.39]* — "Eleven to 20 countries have been invited to participate in order to minimize the risk of under recruiting and to meet the goal of 51 patients entered. Recruitment will be very challenging due to the rareness of the disease and because GPP patients must have an acute flare of moderate to severe intensity in order to be randomized on the trial."

- *[verbatim, Effisayil 1 protocol, Section 7.1 Statistical Design – Model, p.81]* — "Given the small sample size proposed to be used in this trial, an exact statistical test, the Suissa-Shuster Z-pooled test, will be used to perform the primary analysis. Confirmation of efficacy is then given if the proportion of patients achieving a response on the primary endpoint is statistically significantly higher for BI 655130 than for placebo. Formal statistical hypothesis testing will be performed at an overall 1-sided alpha level of 0.025."

- *[verbatim, Effisayil 1 protocol, Section 7.6 (Statistical Analysis of Primary Endpoint)]* — "Due to the small sample size of the trial, an exact statistical test will be used to assess the statistical significance of the treatment effect versus Placebo. Since the traditional Fisher's exact test may be unnecessarily conservative, an alternative test, the Suissa-Shuster Z-pooled test, will be implemented in this trial. The Suissa-Shuster Z-pooled test always preserves the type I error level and is usually more powerful than the Fisher's exact test."

- *[verbatim, Effisayil 1 protocol, Section 7.7 Determination of Sample Size, p.94]* — "The power estimates below for detecting the clinically relevant differences... were derived using R version 3.3.2, for a sample size of 51 patients (2:1 ratio), and a 1-sided type I error of 0.025... with an expected response rate of 0.6 on BI 655130 and 0.1 on placebo for each of the primary endpoint and key secondary endpoint... this trial will be able to detect an effect of BI 655130 relative to placebo, for both primary endpoint and key secondary endpoint simultaneously, with an overall power of 93.9%."

- *[verbatim, Effisayil 1 TSAP, Section 5.1 Primary Endpoint, p.10]* — "The primary endpoint of the study is: A GPPGA pustulation subscore of 0 indicating no visible pustules at Week 1... death or any use of escape medication prior to week 1 will be considered to represent a non-response at the Week 1 timepoint."

- *[verbatim, Effisayil 1 TSAP, Section 7.4 Primary Endpoint, p.48-49]* — "The Suissa-Shuster Z-pooled test, will be implemented to test the treatment effect on the primary endpoint on the RS (estimand EN), at a 1-sided, alpha level of 0.025. Confirmation of efficacy is then given only if the null hypothesis on the primary endpoint is rejected. In the output, the result will be reported at 2-sided alpha level of 0.05 which is more common way in CTR but it is exactly same as 1-sided alpha level of 0.025. Confidence intervals (95%) around the risk difference will be produced using the Chan and Zhang method."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review, Section 1.2 Conclusions on the Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness, p.16]* — "The Applicant submitted data from one adequate and well-controlled trial [Trial 1368-0013 (Effisayil-1)] with supportive evidence from trials 1368-0011 (phase 1, completed), 1368-0025 (phase 2, ongoing), and 1368-0027 (phase 2, ongoing)... Spesolimab was statistically superior to placebo for the primary efficacy endpoint (one-sided p-value = 0.0004). The Applicant demonstrated that spesolimab is effective for its intended use in the target population and has met the evidentiary standard required by 21 CFR 314.126 to support approval."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review, Section 1.3 Benefit-Risk Summary, p.17]* — "Substantial efficacy was demonstrated in one pivotal Trial 1368-0013, which enrolled 53 adult subjects with GPP flare of moderate-to-severe intensity... subjects were randomized (2:1) to either a single intravenous dose of 900 mg of spesolimab (N=35) or placebo (N=18)... spesolimab was superior to placebo on GPPPGA pustulation sub score of 0 at Week 1 (54% vs 6%; one-sided p-value = 0.0004)."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review, Table 10 / Section 8.1.4, p.73]* — "GPPPGA Pustulation Score of 0 at Day 8: Spesolimab (N=35) n (%) = 19 (54.3); Placebo (N=18) n (%) = 1 (5.6). Risk Difference (95% CI), % = 48.7 (21.5, 67.2). P-value = 0.0004" (footnoted: "Confidence interval based on the Wilson method"; "P-value based on the Suissa-Shuster Z-pooled test (1-sided p-value)")

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review, Section 8.1.6 Findings in Special/Subgroup Populations, p.75]* — "Due to the overall small sample size, one cannot reliably determine whether there are differences in response across these subgroups."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review, Section 8.1.2 Statistical Methodologies, p.68-69]* — "The protocol specified using a sequential gatekeeping approach to control the Type I error rate for testing the primary and secondary efficacy endpoints. These endpoints were specified to be tested in the following order at the one-sided α = 0.025 level: Proportion of subjects achieving GPPPGA pustulation score of 0 at Week 1 (Day 8); Proportion of subjects achieving GPPPGA total score of 0 or 1 at Week 1 (Day 8); Proportion of subjects achieving a GPPPASI-75 at Week 4; Change from baseline in pain VAS at Week 4; Change from baseline in total PSS score at Week 4; Change from baseline in the total FACIT-Fatigue score at Week 4."

**Reverse-engineered SAP** (points not directly quoted above but inferable from reported results)

- *[inferred]* The trial's escape/rescue-medication framework functioned as a built-in ethical safeguard for a severe, potentially life-threatening flare population: patients failing to improve by Day 8 could receive open-label spesolimab rescue, which is why 15/18 (83%) placebo patients ultimately crossed over to open-label spesolimab by Day 8 — inferred from the FDA MDR Table 6/7 disposition data showing 27/53 (51%) of all randomized subjects received open-label spesolimab on Day 8.

- *[inferred]* The choice of a single-dose, single-timepoint (Day 8) primary readout rather than a longer, repeated-measures design reflects a deliberate trade-off to keep the trial short enough to be ethically and operationally feasible in a rare, acute, severe-flare population — inferred from the protocol's explicit statement that "recruitment will be very challenging due to the rareness of the disease" and the 4-year gap between Orphan Drug designation (2018) and only 53 patients being randomized.

### 35. Deucravacitinib (Sotyktu) — NDA 214958

**Sponsor:** Bristol Myers Squibb Company

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy

**Approval date:** September 9, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** POETYK PSO-1 (Trial IM011046), NCT03624127; POETYK PSO-2 (Trial IM011047), NCT03611751

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two identically-designed 52-week phase 3 RCTs, multicenter, double-blind, double-dummy, placebo- and active-comparator-controlled (apremilast), 2:1:1 randomization, stratified randomization, first-in-class allosteric TYK2 inhibitor, randomized withdrawal and re-treatment period (PSO-2 only), blinded switch of placebo arm at Week 16

- *Endpoints:* co-primary composite (sPGA 0/1 with ≥2-grade improvement, PASI 75) at Week 16, hierarchical key-secondary endpoints (PASI 90, PASI 100, sPGA 0, scalp-specific PGA, PGA-Fingernails, PSSD symptom domain)

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by randomization factors (region, prior biologic use, body weight), Full Analysis Set (all randomized subjects), supportive Per-Protocol Set

- *Multiplicity:* dual-branch fixed-sequence (hierarchical/gatekeeping) testing procedure, separate alpha=0.025 (2-sided) branches for placebo-comparison and apremilast-comparison, both co-primary endpoints required significant at alpha=0.05 before secondary testing proceeds

- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation (primary), sensitivity analyses via LOCF, LOCF+NRI, multiple imputation (FCS, PROC MI/MIANALYZE, Rubin's rules), tipping-point analysis, prespecified COVID-19 data-handling rules (default-to-deucravacitinib imputation for missed/remote visits after Week 24)

- *Regulatory:* standard review, no advisory committee meeting held, active-comparator (apremilast) superiority claims required Agency concurrence on clinically relevant endpoints/timepoints per multiplicity control

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Design: POETYK PSO-1 (IM011046, n=666) and POETYK PSO-2 (IM011047, n=1020) were both multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active comparator-controlled (apremilast 30 mg BID) phase 3 trials in adults ≥18 years with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis (BSA ≥10%, PASI ≥12, sPGA ≥3) eligible for systemic therapy or phototherapy; randomization was 2:1:1 (deucravacitinib 6 mg QD : placebo : apremilast) stratified by geographic region, prior biologic use, and body weight (≥90 kg vs <90 kg, weight stratum not applied in Japan/China); placebo subjects switched blinded to deucravacitinib at Week 16; PSO-1 continued to Week 52 with apremilast non-responders (< PASI 50 at Week 24) switched to deucravacitinib; PSO-2 added a Week 24 randomized-withdrawal/retreatment period in which deucravacitinib PASI-75 responders were re-randomized 1:1 to continued deucravacitinib or placebo (with relapse-triggered rescue back to deucravacitinib) to assess maintenance/durability

- Primary endpoint(s): co-primary endpoints at Week 16 — (1) sPGA response of 0 (clear) or 1 (minimal) with ≥2-grade improvement from baseline; (2) PASI 75 (≥75% reduction from baseline in PASI score). Both endpoints had to reach significance for trial success

- Secondary endpoints: PASI 90, PASI 100, sPGA 0, scalp-specific PGA (ss-PGA) 0/1 among subjects with baseline ss-PGA ≥3, PGA-Fingernails 0/1 among subjects with baseline PGA-F ≥3, PSSD symptom-domain score of 0, all assessed against both placebo and apremilast per a prespecified testing hierarchy, plus efficacy at Weeks 24/52 and maintenance-period outcomes (PSO-2)

- Sample size/power: approximately 600 subjects planned for PSO-1 and 1000 for PSO-2 (actual 666 and 1020 randomized); no formal interim analysis for efficacy was conducted

- Statistical methods: co-primary and binary secondary endpoints analyzed with the CMH test stratified by randomization factors; continuous secondary endpoints via ANCOVA (treatment + stratification factors as fixed effects, baseline as covariate); primary missing-data method was non-responder imputation (NRI), with LOCF, LOCF+NRI, multiple imputation (FCS/PROC MI, pooled via PROC MIANALYZE and Rubin's rules), and tipping-point sensitivity analyses; multiplicity controlled via two parallel alpha=0.025 (2-sided) fixed-sequence hierarchies (one for deucravacitinib-vs-placebo comparisons, one for deucravacitinib-vs-apremilast comparisons), each endpoint tested only if the prior endpoint in its branch was significant, with all further comparisons in a branch treated as descriptive once one step failed

(4) Tipping point analysis..."

In the extreme case (i.e., worst case scenario), deucravacitinib remained statistically significant to placebo (p-values < 0.001) for both co-primary efficacy endpoints. ### 36. Leniolisib (Joenja) — NDA 217759

**Sponsor:** Pharming Technologies B.V. (Pharming Group N.V.)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of activated phosphoinositide 3-kinase delta (PI3Kδ) syndrome (APDS) in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older weighing at least 45 kg

**Approval date:** March 24, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** Study CCDZ173X2201, Part 2 ("Study 2201, Part 2"), NCT02435173

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* ultra-rare-disease trial, single pivotal phase 2/3 study with an internal two-part structure (Part 1: open-label, non-randomized within-subject dose-finding, n=6; Part 2: the pivotal 12-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial, n=31), 2:1 randomization, first-in-class PI3Kδ inhibitor, approval based on a single adequate and well-controlled trial plus mechanistic confirmatory evidence (small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population, Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1)

- *Endpoints:* co-primary composite of a biomarker (change from baseline in percentage of naïve B cells out of total B cells) and an imaging-based lymphoproliferation endpoint (change from baseline in log10-transformed sum of product of diameters, SPD, of index lymph-node lesions by MRI/CT using Cheson criteria) at Day 85

- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA (treatment as fixed effect, baseline as covariate, glucocorticoid use and IVIG use as categorical covariates), PD analysis set (n=27), naïve-B-cell analysis restricted to subjects with baseline naïve B cells <48% (n=13)

- *Multiplicity:* none formally applied — both co-primary endpoints were required to be significant at a nominal two-sided alpha=0.05; all secondary/sensitivity analyses reported as nominal, unadjusted for multiplicity

- *Missing data/bias:* small-N reliance on a single external uncontrolled historical study (everolimus in mantle cell lymphoma, n=43) to estimate SPD variability for power calculation; longitudinal repeated-measures mixed-model sensitivity analysis for naïve B cells; no Data Monitoring Committee-mandated interim efficacy analysis

- *Regulatory:* Orphan Drug Designation (2018), Rare Pediatric Disease Designation (2020) with accompanying priority review voucher, Priority Review, no Advisory Committee meeting held, first approved therapy for APDS, approval anchored on one adequate/well-controlled trial (21 CFR 314.126) supported by confirmatory mechanistic/biomarker evidence given disease ultra-rarity (estimated prevalence <1,000 patients worldwide)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Design: Study CCDZ173X2201 was conducted in two parts. Part 1 (n=6) was an open-label, non-randomized, within-subject dose-finding phase. Part 2 — the pivotal trial — was a 12-week, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter study in subjects ≥12 years of age with APDS, conducted at 10 sites in the US, UK, Italy (2 sites), Czech Republic, Netherlands, Ireland, Belarus, Russia, and Germany from December 2017 to August 2021; subjects were randomized to leniolisib 70 mg or placebo orally twice daily for 12 weeks, with eligible subjects able to roll over into an open-label extension (CCDZ173X2201E1)

- Population/eligibility: males and females 12-75 years with a documented APDS-associated PIK3CD or PIK3R1 mutation, nodal/extranodal lymphoproliferation consistent with APDS, at least one measurable nodal lesion on CT/MRI, minimum body weight 45 kg; key exclusions included recent use of mTOR/PI3Kδ inhibitors, B-cell depleters, belimumab/cyclophosphamide, or high-dose glucocorticoids

- Primary endpoint(s) and exact definition: two co-primary efficacy endpoints assessed at Day 85 — (1) change from baseline in the log10-transformed sum of product of diameters (SPD) of index lymph-node/extranodal lesions selected per Cheson (1999) lymphoma-response criteria from contrast-enhanced MRI or CT (neck, chest, abdomen, pelvis; up to 14 lesions: 6 lymph nodes, 4 liver/spleen, 4 other extranodal), read by a single blinded central radiologist; and (2) change from baseline in the percentage of naïve B cells (CD19+CD27-CD10-) out of total B cells by flow cytometry, analyzed only in subjects with baseline naïve B cells <48% (the low end of the normal 48-85% range)

- Secondary endpoints: change from baseline in 3D volume of index/non-index lesions and spleen size (bi-dimensional and 3D volume); leniolisib PK parameters; change in SF-36 and WPAI-CIQ; PGA/PtGA visual analogue scales; change in CRP, LDH, beta-2 microglobulin, ferritin, fibrinogen, ESR

- Sample size/power: the target N (20 active : 10 placebo = 30) was driven by the SPD endpoint. Variability was estimated from an unrelated, uncontrolled historical study of everolimus in mantle cell lymphoma (n=43) after 2 months of treatment (assumed SD=0.2 on the log10 scale), giving 80% power at N=30 to detect a treatment difference of -0.225 (~40% decrease on the original scale) at two-sided alpha=0.05 by t-test; using the lower observed SD (0.14) from the 6 Part 1 subjects, power rose to 97%. For the naïve-B-cell endpoint, assuming 10% attrition to ~27 evaluable subjects, an anticipated 25-percentage-point treatment difference, and SD=14 (from Part 1), power was 98% at the 5% level; the sponsor calculated the joint probability of both co-primary endpoints reaching significance as at least 78%. No formal efficacy interim analysis was planned; a Data Monitoring Committee provided ongoing safety oversight only

- Statistical methods used: ANCOVA for both co-primary endpoints (treatment as fixed effect; log10-baseline SPD or baseline naïve-B-cell percentage as covariate; baseline glucocorticoid use and baseline IVIG/IRT use as categorical Yes/No covariates), two-sided alpha=0.05, no multiplicity adjustment (both endpoints required significant per the estimand strategy rather than via alpha-splitting); sensitivity analysis for naïve B cells used a longitudinal repeated-measures mixed model (treatment, time, treatment-by-time, baseline, baseline-by-time as fixed effects, unstructured covariance matrix); baseline naïve-B-cell value defined as the arithmetic mean of screening and Day-1 values when both available

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1182/blood.2022018546), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36399712/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=A+randomized+placebo-controlled+phase+3+trial+of+the+PI3K%CE%B4+inhibitor+leniolisib+for+activated+PI3K%CE%B4+syndrome)

**Other resources**

- IPD/dataset access: no Pharming/leniolisib-specific data-sharing policy (e.g., Vivli, YODA Project, Project Data Sphere) could be confirmed; given the ultra-rare disease population (estimated prevalence <1,000 patients worldwide per the FDA review) and n=31 trial size, re-identification risk would likely constrain any individual patient-data release even if a general policy exists

- Advisory committee meeting: none held. Per the Multi-Discipline Review, Section 9, the Division noted "there are few controversial issues requiring external input and discussion given the favorable benefit-risk assessment," despite the endpoints being novel and not previously used to support approvals in this review division

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Section 8.1.3, p.101]* — "The sample size (20 subjects in active and 10 subjects in placebo for a total of 30 subjects) was mostly driven by the analysis of one of the two co-primary efficacy variables, the change from baseline in the log10-transformed SPD of index lesions. Data from 43 subjects in the uncontrolled everolimus study CRAD001N2201 in mantel cell lymphoma after 2 months of treatment were used to estimate the variability of the change from baseline in log10-transformed SPD of index lesions... with 30 subjects this part of the study had 80% power to detect a treatment difference of -0.225 between leniolisib and placebo groups... using a 5% type I error in a two-sided t-test. On the original scale, this corresponds to a decrease of around 40%."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Section 8.1.3, p.101]* — "Assuming that 10% of subjects are excluded from the analysis of the other co-primary variable, the change from baseline in the percentage of naïve B cells out of total B cells, due to no reduced percentage of naïve B cells at baseline, it was anticipated that 27 subjects would have provided data for the analysis... With the above assumptions, the power to achieve a statistical significance in both endpoints was at least 78%."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Section 8.1.4, p.112]* — "Leniolisib met statistical significance for both co-primary endpoints at α=0.05 significance level, demonstrating an improvement over placebo in change from baseline in the log10 transformed SPD in the index lesions and percentage of naïve B cells out of total B cells at Day 85. The LS mean treatment difference estimate was -0.25 [95% CI: -0.38, -0.12; p-value = 0.0006]... and 37.30 [95% CI: 24.06, 50.54; p-value = 0.0002] in change from baseline at Day 85 in naïve B cells."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Section 1.2, p.21]* — "Substantial evidence of effectiveness for leniolisib in subjects with APDS was established with one adequate and well-controlled trial, with confirmatory evidence. The 12-week, pivotal phase 3 trial (Study CCDZ173X2201 Part 2) conducted in 31 adults and adolescents 12 years of age and older demonstrated a clinically meaningful and statistically significant improvement in the percentage of naïve B cells and lymphadenopathy..."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Section 9, p.142]* — "Additional considerations centered around the use of novel co-primary endpoints. While the co-primary endpoints of lymph node size and percentage of naïve B cells out of total B cells are not direct reflections of clinically meaningful outcomes and have not been used by the Division to support prior approvals, they are based on a clear understanding of the pathophysiology of the disease and mechanism of action of leniolisib... the study met statistical significance for both of these co-primary endpoints."

**Reverse-engineered SAP** (points not found verbatim in the public SAP text extraction, traced to specific reported results)

- *[inferred]* The trial's true analyzable N for the naïve-B-cell co-primary endpoint was far smaller than the 31 randomized subjects — only 13 of 31 subjects (8 leniolisib, 5 placebo) had baseline naïve B cells <48% and were included in that analysis, inferred from Table 26 of the FDA review reporting "Leniolisib (N=19) 8 ... Placebo (N=8) 5" for the naïve-B-cell ANCOVA.

- *[inferred]* Roughly one-third of randomized subjects were excluded or ineligible for at least one co-primary analysis (PD analysis set n=27 of 31 randomized; further restriction to n=13 for the B-cell endpoint), suggesting the sponsor's statistical plan anticipated this attrition explicitly in the power calculation ("assuming that 10% of subjects are excluded... due to no reduced percentage of naïve B cells at baseline") — the actual exclusion rate (18 of 31, ~58%, lacked baseline naïve B cells <48%) was substantially higher than the 10% assumption, which the FDA review does not flag as invalidating the result, implying the statistical reviewer treated the pre-specified subgroup-restricted estimand as robust to this deviation.

- *[inferred]* Given the extremely small subgroup sizes (n=8 vs n=5 for the pivotal biomarker analysis), the trial's substantial-evidence claim likely rested as much on the mechanistic/biomarker plausibility argument (pAKT pathway inhibition, well-characterized monogenic etiology) as on the frequentist p-values themselves, consistent with the FDA review's explicit invocation of "confirmatory evidence" from mechanism of action alongside the statistical result, a pattern typical of the 21st Century Cures Act's flexibility provisions for ultra-rare diseases rather than a standard two-adequate-and-well-controlled-trials paradigm.

### 37. Ritlecitinib (Litfulo) — NDA 215830

**Sponsor:** Pfizer, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of severe alopecia areata (AA) in adults and adolescents 12 years and older

**Approval date:** June 23, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** ALLEGRO-2b/3 (Study B7981015), NCT03732807

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, dose-ranging, placebo-controlled, multicenter phase 2b/3 trial; seven parallel arms (five ritlecitinib dosing regimens plus two placebo-to-active switch arms) allocated 2:2:2:2:1:1:1; randomization stratified by age group (<18 vs. ≥18 years) and alopecia totalis/universalis (AT/AU) status; 24-week placebo-controlled period followed by a 24-week active-treatment extension

- *Endpoints:* SALT (Severity of Alopecia Tool) ≤20 at Week 24 (primary for FDA/PMDA submissions; SALT≤10 at Week 24 was the EMA primary endpoint and the FDA key secondary endpoint); secondary endpoints included SALT≤10 at Week 24, SALT≤20/≤10 at multiple visits through Week 48, SALT75 response, Eyebrow Assessment (EBA) and Eyelash Assessment (ELA) responder endpoints, and Patient's Global Impression of Change

- *Primary analysis:* full analysis set (all randomized subjects); Miettinen-Nurminen method for 95% CI of the risk difference vs. placebo for each active dose (unstratified); primary missing-data rule excluded COVID-19-related missing Week-24 assessments and imputed other missing data as non-responders ("Analysis #1")

- *Multiplicity:* graphical multiple-testing procedure controlling familywise Type I error at α=0.00125 across the four higher dose regimens (200/50 mg, 200/30 mg, 50 mg, 30 mg) vs. placebo — sequential/Holm's-method gated testing (10 mg arm excluded from multiplicity control); secondary endpoints, including the key secondary SALT≤10 endpoint and all eyebrow/eyelash assessments, were not brought under multiplicity control and were excluded from labeling claims

- *Interim/alpha-spending:* protocol allowed an internal-decision-making interim analysis once ≥90% of subjects reached 24 weeks post-randomization, with no planned adjustment to conduct, analysis, or reporting and unblinded personnel firewalled from the study team; the Applicant ultimately elected not to conduct it

- *Missing data/bias:* COVID-19-related missing data handled separately from other missing data; four pre-specified combinations of multiple imputation (MAR, GLMM with Bayesian priors for placebo response) and non-responder imputation ("Analysis #1"-"#4"); FDA additionally required a tipping-point sensitivity analysis under multiple missing-not-at-random scenarios, and recommended Analysis #4 (MI for COVID-19 missingness) over the applicant's primary Analysis #1 for labeling as the more defensible MAR-based approach

- *Regulatory:* standard review, Division of Dermatology and Dentistry; no Advisory Committee meeting held; postmarketing requirements included pediatric (6 to <12 and 12 to <18 years) and pregnancy-exposure studies; no REMS required beyond routine pharmacovigilance and the Active Risk Identification and Analysis (ARIA) system

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study B7981015 enrolled subjects ≥12 years of age with ≥50% scalp hair loss (SALT≥50) due to alopecia areata without terminal scalp regrowth in the prior 6 months and current episode duration ≤10 years; 718 subjects were randomized across arms: ritlecitinib 200/50 mg (loading dose then 50 mg), 200/30 mg, 50 mg, 30 mg, 10 mg (all once daily), and two placebo arms that switched to 200/50 mg or 50 mg at Week 24; enrollment targets were ~40% AT/AU and ~15% adolescents

- Primary endpoint: proportion of subjects achieving SALT≤20 (no more than 20% scalp hair loss) at Week 24 for FDA/PMDA submissions (the EMA submission instead specified SALT≤10 at Week 24 as primary, at overall significance level 0.01 rather than 0.00125, with a different primary COVID-19 missing-data method)

- Secondary endpoints: SALT≤10 at Week 24 (key secondary); SALT≤20 and SALT≤10 at Weeks 4, 8, 12, 18, 28, 34, 40, 48; SALT75 response; ≥2-grade improvement (or score of 3) in EBA/ELA scales at each visit through Week 48

- Sample size: 718 randomized (132/130/130/132/63 per active arm, 131 placebo); no explicit power calculation was reproduced in the FDA review; the trial was "designed to provide substantial evidence of effectiveness as an adequate and well-controlled large multicenter trial using a significance level of 0.00125"; a single optional interim analysis for internal decision-making was permitted at ≥90% of subjects reaching Week 24, but was not conducted, so the full alpha was available at final analysis

- Statistical methods: Miettinen-Nurminen method for primary binary-endpoint comparisons; graphical gatekeeping procedure controlling the four-dose family at α=0.00125 with Holm's method at the second stage; multiple imputation for COVID-19-related missingness modeled via a generalized linear mixed model (logistic-normal, treatment/visit/treatment-by-visit interaction, subject-level random intercept, Bayesian diffuse priors for placebo response), ≥100 (500 used) imputations combined via Rubin's rules; protocol amended five times, most consequentially Amendment 3 (7/14/2020), which switched the FDA primary endpoint from SALT≤10 to SALT≤20 and added the pre-specified interim analysis

The study was designed to provide substantial evidence of effectiveness as a an adequate and well-controlled large multicenter trial using a significance level of 0.00125."

This analysis does not include stratification factors."

Subjects with missing SALT scores due to other reasons were counted as non-responders. This method of handling missing data is referred to as Analysis #1."

Multiplicity was controlled using the following graphical procedure. At the first stage the hypothesis H1 (200/50 mg vs. placebo) is tested at level α. At the second stage, multiplicity was controlled across the hypotheses H2 (50 mg vs. placebo) and H3 (200/30 mg vs. placebo) using Holm's method. If both the tests for the 50 mg arm and the 200/30 mg doses are rejected at the α/2 level, then the final hypothesis H4 (30 mg vs. placebo) can be tested at level α."

Unblinded personnel were to be kept separate from the rest of the team. No adjustments in the conduct, analysis, or reporting were planned. The applicant decided not to conduct the interim analysis, and the trial was not unblinded until all subjects completed the trial."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 215830, §8.1.4 "Integrated Assessment of Effectiveness", Table 17, p.105]* — "SALT ≤20 response Ritlecitinib 50 mg 23.0[%]... Placebo 1.6[%]... Difference from Placebo (95% CI) 21.4 (13.4, 29.5)"

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 215830, §8.3 "Statistical Issues", p.175]* — "Because the multiplicity control scheme in Study B7981015 only extended across multiple doses for the primary efficacy endpoint, and did not extend to the secondary endpoints, it is difficult to interpret the results of the secondary endpoints... the endpoints [EBA/ELA] are not capable of supporting efficacy claims and are not recommended for inclusion in labeling."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 215830, §8.4 "Conclusions and Recommendations", p.175]* — "The applicant provided substantial evidence of effectiveness for ritlecitinib 50 mg in the treatment of severe alopecia areata. This was supported by an adequate and well-controlled large multicenter Phase 2b/3 trial (B7981015, N=718)... For the to-be-marketed dose of ritlecitinib 50 mg daily, SALT≤20 response was 23.0%, compared to 1.6% for placebo at week 24 (a treatment effect of 21.4% [95% CI: 13.4%, 29.5%], p-value <0.00001)."

**Reverse-engineered SAP** (minor inferences beyond the directly quoted text above)

- *[inferred]* The choice to recommend the flat 50 mg dose (rather than the 200/50 mg loading-dose regimen that showed a numerically larger Week-24 effect, 30.65% vs. 23.39%) reflects a benefit-risk tradeoff rather than a statistical-superiority finding — inferred from the juxtaposition of Table 10 (200/50 mg numerically higher response) with the review's separate "Rationale for selection of 50 mg QD dose" discussion of converging Week-48/2-year efficacy and a less favorable safety profile (lymphopenia, TEAEs) for the loading-dose arm.

- *[inferred]* The EMA-vs-FDA divergence in primary endpoint choice (SALT≤10 vs. SALT≤20) and in significance level (0.01 vs. 0.00125) implies the sponsor ran two formally distinct pre-specified confirmatory analyses from a single trial for different regulators, each with its own alpha budget — inferred from the review's statement that "the protocol specified different sets of primary and secondary endpoints and analysis plans by regulatory region," without a single global alpha reconciling both.

### 38. Bimekizumab (Bimzelx) — BLA 761151

**Sponsor:** UCB, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adult patients who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy

**Approval date:** October 17, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** Three phase 3 trials supported the original efficacy demonstration — BE VIVID (PS0009), NCT03370133; BE READY (PS0013), NCT03410992; and BE SURE (PS0008), NCT03412747. Only BE VIVID and BE READY (both placebo-controlled) contributed the labeled placebo-controlled efficacy comparison; BE SURE (active-comparator-only, no placebo arm) is described in labeling's trial-design narrative but its head-to-head adalimumab data were not included in the approved label. BE RADIANT (PS0015), NCT03536884, an active-comparator (secukinumab) trial, was not part of the original efficacy package — it was submitted only as new safety data during the Complete-Response resubmission

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* three multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group phase 3 trials — BE VIVID (placebo- and ustekinumab-controlled), BE READY (placebo-controlled with randomized-withdrawal maintenance period), and BE SURE (adalimumab-controlled, no placebo arm) — randomization stratified by geographic region and prior biologic exposure; resubmission after a Complete Response Letter driven by manufacturing-facility (GMP) deficiencies unrelated to the efficacy/safety data package

- *Endpoints:* co-primary endpoints in all three trials — PASI90 (≥90% improvement in Psoriasis Area and Severity Index from baseline) and IGA 0/1 (Investigator Global Assessment of clear/almost clear with ≥2-grade improvement), both at Week 16; key secondary endpoints included PASI100, IGA 0, Scalp IGA 0/1, PASI75 at Week 4, and Patient Symptom Diary (itch/pain/scaling) responses

- *Primary analysis:* Randomized Set (all randomized subjects; repeated on Full Analysis Set and Per-Protocol Set), non-responder imputation for missing data; Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by region and prior biologic exposure for the pooled bimekizumab-arm vs. comparator comparison, with a pre-specified logistic-regression sensitivity analysis (Fisher's exact test as fallback if the model failed to converge)

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (hierarchical) testing procedure controlling the familywise two-sided Type I error rate at 0.05 across co-primary and selected secondary endpoints per trial (separate testing hierarchies for PS0008, PS0009, PS0013); for BE VIVID and BE READY, non-inferiority to the active comparator was tested first (1-sided α=0.025, 10% margin, Wald CI) followed by superiority pairwise CMH comparisons

- *Missing data/bias:* primary non-responder imputation supplemented by protocol-specified sensitivity analyses (MI-MCMC monotone regression, MI-MCMC reference-based, observed cases, LOCF) plus an FDA reviewer-added "worst-case" imputation (bimekizumab missing = non-responder, comparator missing = responder); results were robust to all methods (p<0.001 in the worst case)

- *Regulatory:* standard review, Division of Dermatology and Dentistry/Office of Immunology and Inflammation; original BLA (submitted July 15, 2020) received a Complete Response Letter (May 12, 2022) solely for GMP/facility-inspection deficiencies at UCB's Braine, Belgium drug-product facility — efficacy and safety were already found adequate in the initial review cycle; resubmission (November 21, 2022) also carried new open-label extension (PS0014) and active-comparator (BE RADIANT/PS0015) safety data that surfaced a suicidal-ideation/behavior (SI/B) signal, requiring a Medication Guide and Warnings and Precautions labeling (no formal REMS); no Advisory Committee meeting held at either review cycle; comparative efficacy data vs. adalimumab (BE SURE) and ustekinumab (BE VIVID) were excluded from labeling because the US-licensed and EU-approved active comparators were treated as distinct, unbridged products and findings were not replicated across comparators

**Trial design & endpoints**

- All three pivotal trials enrolled adults ≥18 years with chronic plaque psoriasis ≥6 months, IGA≥3, PASI≥12, and BSA involvement ≥10%, candidates for systemic therapy/phototherapy. BE SURE (PS0008, N≈450 planned, 1:1:1): bimekizumab 320 mg Q4W throughout vs. bimekizumab 320 mg Q4W to Week 16 then Q8W vs. adalimumab (80 mg load, then 40 mg Q2W) through Week 24, then all arms converged on bimekizumab; 16-week active-comparator-controlled initial period, 40-week maintenance period, no placebo arm. BE VIVID (PS0009, N≈560 planned, 4:2:1): bimekizumab 320 mg Q4W vs. ustekinumab (weight-based) vs. placebo (placebo crossed to bimekizumab at Week 16); 16-week initial period, 36-week maintenance. BE READY (PS0013, N≈400 planned, 4:1): bimekizumab 320 mg Q4W vs. placebo for 16 weeks; Week-16 PASI90 responders entered a 40-week randomized-withdrawal period (re-randomized 1:1:1 to continued Q4W, Q8W, or placebo-withdrawal); non-responders and later relapsers entered an open-label escape arm

- Co-primary endpoints (all three trials): PASI90 and IGA 0/1 at Week 16, analyzed by pooling both bimekizumab dosing schedules where applicable

- Secondary endpoints: PASI100, IGA 0, Scalp IGA 0/1 (in subjects with baseline scalp disease), PASI75 at Week 4, PSD-based itch/pain/scaling responder rates at Week 16, and (BE READY only) PASI90 maintenance at Week 56 among Week-16 responders

- Interim CSRs reflected clinical cutoffs of October 28, 2019 (PS0008), September 4, 2019 (PS0009), and October 18, 2019 (PS0013), covering the first 56 (52 for PS0009) weeks; no formal group-sequential interim analysis or alpha-spending function was used — the design relied on a single confirmatory analysis at the Week-16 primary timepoint under fixed-sequence multiplicity control, per trial

- Statistical methods: stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test (region, prior biologic exposure) with Greenland-Robins method for the stratified risk difference; logistic-regression sensitivity model with pre-specified convergence fallback (drop prior-biologic-exposure term, then region term, then Fisher's exact test); center-pooling algorithm (threshold 15 subjects per center in PS0008/PS0013, 21 in PS0009) for a center-by-treatment interaction sensitivity analysis; non-inferiority margin of 10% (1-sided 97.5% Wald CI) vs. adalimumab/ustekinumab in PS0008/PS0009 before superiority testing

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761151, §8.3.2 "Conclusions and Recommendations", p.214-215]* — "To establish the effectiveness of bimekizumab, the Applicant submitted data from 2 pivotal phase 3 trials, PS0009 and PS0013... Bimekizumab was statistically superior to placebo (p-values < 0.001) for the co-primary efficacy endpoints in both trials... However, data regarding comparative efficacy vs adalimumab and ustekinumab will not be included in labeling because the lack of replication of findings for each of the active comparators, as well as the lack of a scientific bridge between US-licensed and EU-approved products."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761151 (resubmission review), §1.1, p.11]* — "This resubmission is a complete response to the deficiencies outlined in the Complete Response Letter (CRL dated May 12, 2022...). The original BLA for bimekizumab (BLA 761151) was submitted on July 15, 2020. The Agency issued a CR during the initial review cycle because of Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) deficiencies identified during inspection of the UCB Braine Drug Product Manufacturing Facility."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761151 (resubmission review), §1.1, p.11-12]* — "The Agency identified a new safety signal of suicidal ideation and behavior (SI/B) associated with the use of bimekizumab... A re-review of controlled SI/B data collected in previously submitted Trials PS0008, PS0009, and PS0013, using the electronic Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale (eC-SSRS) found nearly threefold more positive responses in a pooled bimekizumab group compared to a pooled placebo/active group (most reporting passive wish to be dead, 1.7% versus 0.6%, respectively)."

**Reverse-engineered SAP** (minor inferences beyond the directly quoted text above)

- *[inferred]* BE SURE (PS0008) was excluded from the labeled placebo-controlled efficacy comparison not for a statistical-methods reason but purely a design one — it never had a placebo arm — inferred from the design description (bimekizumab Q4W, bimekizumab Q4W/Q8W, and adalimumab only) combined with the label's "Clinical Response at Week 16 (Trial-Ps-1 and Trial-Ps-2)" heading, which silently omits Trial-Ps-3 (BE SURE) from the co-primary results table.

- *[inferred]* BE RADIANT (PS0015, active-comparator vs. secukinumab) was very likely already complete or far advanced as an independent Phase 3 program by the time of the 2022-2023 resubmission (it had been published in the Lancet in 2021) but was deliberately not incorporated into the efficacy package for this BLA — inferred from the resubmission review's characterization of PS0015 solely as a source of "new safety data" alongside the OLE trial PS0014, with no mention of PS0015 efficacy data anywhere in the Section 14 labeling discussion.

### 39. Birch triterpenes (Filsuvez) — NDA 215064

**Sponsor:** Amryt Pharmaceuticals DAC (c/o Amryt Pharmaceuticals Inc., Boston, MA) — this is the applicant named in both the December 18, 2023 approval letter and its February 26, 2024 "corrected" reissue (which fixed an "incorrect applicant name" error) and in the approved label's adverse-event contact information; Chiesi Farmaceutici S.p.A. acquired Amryt Pharma plc in September 2023, before approval, and FDA's live Drugs@FDA record for NDA 215064 currently lists the company of record as Chiesi, reflecting a subsequent administrative transfer of the application rather than the applicant named in the approval action itself

**Indication approved:** Treatment of wounds associated with dystrophic and junctional epidermolysis bullosa (EB) in adult and pediatric patients 6 months of age and older

**Approval date:** December 18, 2023 (original action letter; FDA reissued a corrected approval letter on February 26, 2024 solely to fix the applicant name, with the December 18, 2023 effective date unchanged)

**Pivotal trial:** EASE (Study BEB-13), NCT03068780 — "Double-blind, Randomised, Vehicle-controlled, Phase III, Efficacy and Safety Study With 24-month Open-label Follow-up of Oleogel-S10 in Patients With Inherited Epidermolysis Bullosa"

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single pivotal Phase 3 randomized, triple-masked (participant/care provider/investigator), vehicle-controlled, parallel-group trial plus mechanistic confirmatory evidence from separate open-label intra-patient (split-wound) trials in non-EB partial-thickness wounds; rare-disease "one adequate and well-controlled trial plus confirmatory evidence" evidentiary pathway; adaptive group-sequential design with unblinded sample-size re-estimation

- *Endpoints:* binary responder primary endpoint (first complete closure of a designated target wound within 45 days, investigator-assessed); hierarchical key secondary endpoints (time to closure by Day 90, closure proportion at Day 90, wound-infection incidence/severity, EBDASI total-body wound-burden score, itch)

- *Primary analysis:* stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test for the common odds ratio (stratified by EB subtype and target wound size class), with the final p-value adjusted via the Cui-Hung-Wang (CHW) weighted combination statistic to account for the unblinded sample-size re-estimation

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (hierarchical) gatekeeping of key secondary endpoints, tested only if the primary endpoint reached significance at the two-sided 5% level; separate "other" secondary endpoints were excluded from the multiplicity scheme and analyzed purely descriptively

- *Interim/alpha-spending:* unblinded interim analysis at ~50% enrollment (December 21, 2018) with a conditional-power futility/continuation rule; IDMC recommended increasing the planned sample from 192 to 250 enrolled/treated (230 evaluable); the CHW method (adaptive sample-size re-estimation with weighted combination test, Cui-Hung-Wang 1999) did not require lowering the nominal significance level to accommodate the increase

- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation (missing wound-closure data treated as failure) as the primary method; worst-case imputation and multiple imputation (MCMC + sequential regression) with tipping-point-style exploration showed the primary result was fragile — the unadjusted p=0.041 could move to roughly 0.06-0.07 by reclassifying only 1-2 subjects per arm

- *Regulatory:* initial Complete Response Letter (February 26, 2022) concluding inadequate substantial evidence of effectiveness, reversed via a granted Formal Dispute Resolution Request decided by the OND Deputy Director in 2023 after an external wound-healing expert consult; rare pediatric disease priority review voucher awarded; no advisory committee held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Randomized (1:1), triple-masked, vehicle(control-gel)-controlled, parallel-group trial (BEB-13/EASE) in patients with dystrophic EB, junctional EB, or Kindler EB (EB simplex was eligible under the earliest protocol version but excluded after an April 2018 amendment), each with an eligible partial-thickness "target wound" 10-50 cm² and no more than 9 months old; enrolled 223 subjects (109 Oleogel-S10, 114 control) at 49 sites in 26 countries, including 14 US subjects at 8 sites; randomization was stratified by EB subtype and target-wound-size class; note the trial's own enrollment allowed subjects as young as 21 days old under earlier protocol versions, whereas the approved label restricts use to patients 6 months of age and older

- Primary endpoint: proportion of subjects with first complete closure of the EB target wound within 45±7 days, based on clinical assessment by the investigator (wound rated "closed" at first appearance of complete re-epithelialization without drainage); this endpoint was modified during development — at FDA's request during a Type B meeting — from an original design requiring photographic confirmation of closure at two consecutive visits two weeks apart, to the simpler direct clinical assessment ultimately used

- Key secondary endpoints, tested in pre-specified hierarchical order: time to first complete closure through Day 90 (non-stratified log-rank test, non-closure censored at Day 90); proportion with complete closure at Day 90 (stratified CMH test); incidence of target-wound infection between baseline and Day 90 (stratified CMH test) and its maximum severity (stratified Wilcoxon rank-sum test); change from baseline to Day 90 in total body wound burden via EBDASI Section I (ANCOVA with terms for treatment, EB subtype, wound-size class, and baseline EBDASI); change in itch using an age-specific scale (Itch Man Scale ages 4-13, Leuven Itch Scale ages ≥14), analyzed by a stratified Wilcoxon rank-sum test. Additional "other" endpoints (procedural/background pain via FLACC or Wong-Baker FACES, sleep impact, missed school/work days, and TSQM treatment satisfaction) were descriptive only, outside the multiplicity scheme

- Sample size/power: assumed 27% control response rate; 182 patients (91/arm) were planned to give 80% power to detect a 20-percentage-point improvement using a two-sided chi-square test at α=0.05 (FDA had recommended a smaller alpha given reliance on a single pivotal trial, but the sponsor retained 0.05); 192 patients were planned for enrollment/treatment to allow for 5% dropout; following the unblinded interim analysis at ~50% enrollment, the IDMC recommended increasing the sample by 48 patients to 230 evaluable (250 planned enrolled/treated)

- Statistical methods: primary analysis used the stratified CMH test for the common odds ratio, with the final significance test adjusted via the CHW-weighted combination statistic spanning pre- and post-interim cohorts; missing wound-closure data were imputed as treatment failures in the primary analysis, with worst-case imputation and MCMC/sequential-regression multiple imputation (with a tipping-point-style sensitivity exploration) used to test robustness; key secondary endpoints were tested in a fixed hierarchical sequence gated on primary-endpoint significance, with no further multiplicity adjustment applied for the interim sample-size change

### 40. Berdazimer (Zelsuvmi) — NDA 217424

**Sponsor:** LNHC, Inc. (c/o Therapeutics Inc., San Diego, CA) — this is the applicant named in FDA's January 5, 2024 approval letter; LNHC, Inc. is Novan, Inc.'s post-restructuring corporate successor. The approved label lists the manufacturing/distribution entity as EPIH SPV, LLC, Wilmington, Delaware

**Indication approved:** Topical treatment of molluscum contagiosum (MC) in adults and pediatric patients 1 year of age and older

**Approval date:** January 5, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** Two trials provided the substantial evidence of effectiveness — NI-MC304 ("B-SIMPLE4"), NCT04535531, and NI-MC302 ("B-SIMPLE2"), NCT03927703. A third, identically designed trial, NI-MC301 ("B-SIMPLE1"), NCT03927716, did not reach statistical significance on its primary endpoint and was used only as supportive/safety data

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* three co-designed, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group Phase 3 trials, with household-clustered randomization (1 or 2 randomized subjects per household, assigned the same treatment); NI-MC301/NI-MC302 randomized 2:1 (active:vehicle), NI-MC304 randomized 1:1 with an added baseline-inflammation stratification factor

- *Endpoints:* binary responder primary endpoint (complete clearance — lesion count of 0 — of all treatable molluscum contagiosum lesions at Week 12); key secondary endpoint of complete clearance at Week 8 (NI-MC304 added three further hierarchical secondary endpoints)

- *Primary analysis:* generalized estimating equations (GEE) logistic regression with an exchangeable working correlation structure to account for within-household correlation, covariate-adjusted for investigator type, household size, baseline lesion count, and (NI-MC304 only) baseline inflammation score

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence hierarchical testing; secondary endpoint(s) tested only if the primary endpoint was significant at the two-sided 5% level

- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation (missing Week-12 assessment = failure) as the primary method, with multiple imputation (monotone MCMC/regression, fixed random seed) as a pre-specified sensitivity analysis; FDA's statistical review found that imbalanced missingness (more dropout on the active arm) combined with non-responder imputation attenuated the treatment effect in NI-MC301/NI-MC302

- *Regulatory:* totality-of-evidence effectiveness conclusion spanning three trials — one clearly positive (NI-MC304, p<0.0001), one that "just missed" the 0.05 threshold but was judged persuasive on point estimates and secondary/sensitivity evidence (NI-MC302, p=0.0510) (near-miss trial counted toward substantial evidence via a totality-of-evidence argument across a multi-trial program), and one non-significant trial retained only for safety (NI-MC301, p=0.3637); FDA statistical reviewer identified and corrected a sponsor programming error in the confidence-interval calculation across all three studies; PREA pediatric assessment fulfilled for ages 1-18, with the 0-to-1-year age group waived as impracticable to study; no advisory committee

**Trial design & endpoints**

- NI-MC301 and NI-MC302 were conducted concurrently with an identical design: subjects with 3-70 baseline molluscum contagiosum lesions randomized 2:1 to berdazimer gel, 10.3% (then SB206), or vehicle, stratified by investigator type (dermatologist vs. other) and household size (1 vs. 2 randomized subjects); enrolled N=352 (NI-MC301) and N=355 (NI-MC302)

- NI-MC304 (B-SIMPLE4) followed the same protocol but randomized 1:1 and added a third stratification factor (baseline inflammation score, 0 vs. ≥1); conducted at 55 US clinics from September 1, 2020 to July 21, 2021 (partly during the COVID-19 pandemic, permitting some remote contacts); enrolled N=891 (444 berdazimer, 447 vehicle), ages 6 months and older with 3-70 lesions

- Study drug or vehicle was applied once daily to all treatable lesions for up to 12 weeks, with clinic visits at baseline, Weeks 2, 4, 8, 12, and 24

- Primary endpoint (all three trials): proportion of subjects with complete clearance (lesion count of 0) of all treatable molluscum contagiosum lesions at Week 12

- Secondary endpoints: NI-MC301/NI-MC302 specified one key secondary endpoint (complete clearance at Week 8); NI-MC304 specified four secondary endpoints tested hierarchically — lesion count of 0 or 1 at Week 12, ≥90% lesion-count reduction from baseline at Week 12, complete clearance at Week 8, and percent change in lesion count from baseline at Week 4

- Sample size (NI-MC304): assumed vehicle response rate of 20% versus a berdazimer rate of 29.5% (a 9.5-percentage-point covariate-adjusted difference, informed by simulated integration of the NI-MC301/NI-MC302 data); 850 subjects (425/arm) were planned for 90% power at two-sided α=0.05

- Statistical methods: the primary analysis in all three trials was a GEE logistic regression with an exchangeable working correlation structure, adjusting for stratification factors and baseline lesion count; FDA's statistical reviewer identified that the applicant's SAS programming used the standard error of the predicted proportion rather than of the predicted log-odds when constructing 95% CIs for the treatment difference, and corrected this across all three studies, producing minor differences from the applicant's reported results; missing Week-12 responses were treated as non-responses in the primary analysis, with multiple imputation as a pre-specified sensitivity analysis

Thus, Studies NI-MC304 and NI-MC302 are adequate and well-controlled trials that demonstrate substantial evidence of effectiveness."

### 41. LetibotulinumtoxinA-wlbg (Letybo) — BLA 761225

**Sponsor:** Hugel, Inc. (Chuncheon, Gangwon, Republic of Korea), U.S. License No. 2237; correspondence handled via Strategic Drug Development Services, LLC (Hillsborough, NC). Croma-Pharma GmbH (Austria) is listed as the ClinicalTrials.gov "lead sponsor" for all three pivotal trials — likely Hugel's ex-US development partner for these studies — but is not the BLA applicant of record.

**Indication approved:** Temporary improvement in the appearance of moderate to severe glabellar lines associated with corrugator and/or procerus muscle activity in adult patients.

**Approval date:** February 29, 2024 (original BLA received March 31, 2021; a first-cycle action letter issued April 12, 2023 was resolved by an August 31, 2023 resubmission that FDA's approval letter describes as "a complete response").

**Pivotal trial:** Three identically-designed Phase 3 trials — BLESS I (NCT02677298), BLESS II (NCT02677805), and BLESS III (NCT03985982).

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter trials, 3:1 active:placebo randomization, with an open-label extension permitting up to three retreatments (last retreatment ≤Week 48)

- *Endpoints:* Composite, dual-scale concurrent responder endpoint — the Applicant's "composite responder rate," which FDA's review calls a "multi-component responder rate": a score of 0 or 1 (none/mild) *and* a ≥2-point improvement from baseline, required concurrently on both the Glabellar Line Scale-Investigator (GLS-I) and Glabellar Line Scale-Subject (GLS-S), at maximum frown, Week 4 (a two-instrument, concurrently-scored aesthetic responder endpoint distinct from any single-scale responder definition already catalogued)

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by study center; the Applicant pre-specified one-sided testing at α=0.025 while FDA's statistical reviewers used the two-sided p-value at α=0.05; FDA also recalculated confidence intervals using the Mantel-Haenszel stratified estimator (Mantel & Haenszel 1959; Sato 1989) rather than the Applicant's unstratified Newcombe method, because of zero-frequency placebo-response cells in two of the three trials

- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing of the primary endpoint against four key secondary endpoints (Weeks 12, 16, 20, and a ≥1-point-at-rest endpoint) in BLESS I and BLESS II; BLESS III's secondary endpoints were exploratory only, with no multiplicity control

- *Missing data/bias:* Non-responder imputation as the primary approach, with pre-specified observed-case, LOCF, and tipping-point sensitivity analyses; the BLESS I tipping-point analysis specified in the SAP was not executed by the Applicant ("the data were not compatible with this type of analysis"), so FDA's reviewers ran an independent worst-case imputation in its place

- *Regulatory:* Complete Response Letter (CRL) followed by resubmission and approval (April 12, 2023 action letter; August 31, 2023 resubmission); no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held ("this product does not raise significant safety or efficacy issues that would benefit from advice from an advisory committee")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- All three trials were randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 studies of a single 20-Unit treatment (0.1 mL/injection at 5 sites: 1 procerus, 2 corrugator each side), 3:1 randomization to letibotulinumtoxinA or placebo, followed by an open-label extension with up to three further retreatments through Week 48.

- BLESS I (NCT02677298, protocol CPH-301-201030): 18 sites (US, Germany, Poland); 528 letibotulinumtoxinA / 175 placebo per the label's trial-level counts. BLESS II (NCT02677805, CPH-302-201030): 6 US-only sites; 160/53. BLESS III (NCT03985982, CPH-303-201400): 7 US sites plus Austria; 266/89. Label Section 14 states combined enrollment of 1,276 subjects (957 letibotulinumtoxinA/319 placebo, 1,271 in the Full Analysis Set); the FDA Multi-Discipline Review's narrative text separately cites a combined total of "1272" and "1,129" for an immunogenicity subset — the two sources are not perfectly reconciled and both figures are reported here as found.

- Population: adults 19–75 years old (observed range) with a Glabellar Line Scale score of moderate or severe at maximum frown; excluded for ptosis, deep dermal scarring, or inability to substantially lessen glabellar lines by manual spreading.

- Primary endpoint: the composite/multi-component responder rate described above, assessed at Week 4 after the first treatment.

- Statistical methods: CMH test stratified by center (primary), Mantel-Haenszel stratified risk-difference estimator for confidence intervals (FDA's substitution for the Applicant's unstratified Newcombe method), fixed-sequence hierarchical testing of key secondaries in BLESS I/II, non-responder imputation as the primary missing-data approach with LOCF/observed-case/tipping-point sensitivity analyses.

- Interim analysis: BLESS III used a pre-specified interim analysis (data cutoff February 10, 2020) to support the efficacy claim.

- SAP amendment history (from the Multi-Discipline Review): the BLESS I SAP was finalized June 23, 2017 and amended June 7, 2018 — after unblinding — to add a post hoc ≥1-point endpoint and subgroup analyses; the BLESS III SAP was finalized November 19, 2019 and amended February 21, 2020 following a site-level (Site 110) unblinding-integrity audit finding.

- Primary efficacy results (label Table 3, Mantel-Haenszel method): BLESS I 47% (95% CI 43–51%) vs. 0%; BLESS II 45% (36–54%) vs. 2%; BLESS III 65% (59–71%) vs. 0%.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held for this application.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, §8, p.42]* — "the primary efficacy endpoint was measured at Week 4 after the first treatment and was defined as the proportion of subjects who achieved treatment success, that is, a score of 0 or 1 (none or mild) and an improvement of at least 2 points from baseline to Week 4 at maximum frown, based concurrently on both the GLS-I and GLS-S. The Applicant refers to this endpoint as 'composite responder rate'... FDA calls it a 'multi-component responder rate.'"

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, §8, p.42-43]* — "the primary and secondary endpoints to be analyzed using the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by study center using a significance level of 0.025 [one-sided, per Applicant]... FDA statistical reviewers used the two-sided p-value for the CMH test with a significance level of 0.05."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, §8, p.44]* — describing the primary missing-data approach as non-responder imputation, with sensitivity analyses of "observed-only, LOCF, and tipping-point analysis"; noting that for BLESS I, "the data were not compatible with this type of analysis" per the Applicant, so FDA's reviewers substituted their own worst-case imputation.

- **Reverse-engineered SAP note** — *[inferred]* The exact zero-cell-adjustment rationale for FDA's shift from the Applicant's Newcombe-method CI to a Mantel-Haenszel stratified estimator is inferred from the observed 0% placebo response rates reported in BLESS I and BLESS III (label Table 3) combined with the Multi-Discipline Review's discussion of this substitution — the review documents the change in method but the underlying zero-cell numeric trigger is reconstructed from the reported placebo-arm response rates rather than quoted directly.
