### 42. Sofpironium (Sofdra) — NDA 217347

**Sponsor:** Botanix SB Inc. (King of Prussia, PA); the drug was originally developed by Kaken Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (Japan) — the FDA Multi-Discipline Review confirms a Kaken/Botanix development relationship but does not itself document the specific licensing chain (reported elsewhere as Kaken → Brickell Biotech → Botanix), so that chain is noted here as general industry background, not independently verified in FDA or ClinicalTrials.gov primary sources.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of primary axillary hyperhidrosis in adults and pediatric patients 9 years of age and older.

**Approval date:** June 18, 2024 (original NDA submitted September 23, 2022; a Complete Response Letter for Human Factors deficiencies was issued September 22, 2023, followed by a December 20, 2023 resubmission and a further Discipline Review Letter on additional Human Factors concerns February 28, 2024).

**Pivotal trial:** Cardigan I (protocol BBI-4000-CL-301, NCT03836287) and Cardigan II (protocol BBI-4000-CL-302, NCT03948646); a related long-term safety study, protocol BBI-4000-CL-303 (NCT03627468), was not part of the primary efficacy basis.

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter trials, 1:1 randomization stratified by site, once-daily topical application to each axilla for 42 days; ages 9 and older eligible, though the ≥12-year instrument (HDSM-Ax-7 Adult) drove the primary analysis because only 5 subjects aged 9–<12 were enrolled/evaluable across both trials

- *Endpoints:* Co-primary endpoints — (1) proportion of subjects with a ≥2-point improvement from baseline to end of treatment (Day 43) on the Hyperhidrosis Disease Severity Measure-Axillary-7-item scale (HDSM-Ax-7, not the older Hyperhidrosis Disease Severity Scale), and (2) change from baseline to end of treatment in gravimetric sweat production (GSP)

- *Primary analysis:* HDSM-Ax-7 responder endpoint analyzed by logistic regression with terms for treatment, baseline score, and analysis center (not a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test, despite that being the more common approach for binary responder endpoints elsewhere in this census); GSP analyzed by ANCOVA with terms for treatment, baseline GSP, and analysis center, with a pre-specified Shapiro-Wilk normality check on residuals and fallback to a rank-based analysis if violated — matching the existing taxonomy term "ANCOVA with normality-contingent fallback to a non-parametric test"

- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing — three secondary efficacy endpoints (combinations of HDSM-Ax-7 improvement thresholds with 70%/50% GSP-reduction thresholds) tested sequentially only if both co-primary endpoints reached significance

- *Missing data/bias:* Differential, arm-specific multiple-imputation assumption — missing data on the vehicle arm imputed under a Missing at Random (MAR) assumption, while missing data on the sofpironium arm was imputed under a Missing Not at Random (MNAR) assumption using a control-based imputation (CBI) model, 20 imputations, with 3-SD outlier trimming before imputation (this specific per-arm-asymmetric MAR/MNAR-CBI split is not the same as the single named jump-to-reference method already catalogued); supportive modified-ITT population added via SAP amendment after 4 subjects were found to have been randomized twice (10 duplicate randomizations across both trials); sensitivity analyses included observed-case, non-responder imputation, a tipping-point analysis, and a per-item influence analysis

- *Regulatory:* Complete Response Letter (CRL) followed by resubmission and approval, though the CRL was for Human Factors/labeling deficiencies, not efficacy or safety; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held ("this application did not present any novel or [contentious] issues" — Multi-Discipline Review, §9)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Cardigan I (NCT03836287): 350 randomized, 35 U.S. centers. Cardigan II (NCT03948646): 351 randomized, 33 U.S. centers. Both randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled, parallel, quadruple-masked, once-daily application to both axillae for 42 days.

- Eligibility: age ≥9 years; HDSM-Ax-7 score of 3–4 at Visits 1 and 4; gravimetric sweat production ≥50 mg per axilla and ≥150 mg combined over 5 minutes at room temperature; symptoms of primary axillary hyperhidrosis for ≥6 months.

- Co-primary endpoints assessed at end of treatment (Day 43): ≥2-point HDSM-Ax-7 improvement (responder proportion) and GSP change from baseline.

- Statistical methods: logistic regression (treatment, baseline HDSM-Ax-7, center) for the responder co-primary; ANCOVA (treatment, baseline GSP, center) with a Shapiro-Wilk normality check and rank-based fallback for the GSP co-primary; differential MAR/MNAR-CBI multiple imputation described above.

- Primary co-primary results (ITT, multiple imputation; Multi-Discipline Review Table 1, p.17): Cardigan I — HDSM-Ax-7 responder 50.4% (sofpironium) vs. 32.1% (vehicle), treatment difference 18.3 (95% CI 8.0–28.7), p=0.0005; GSP rank-based difference p=0.0019. Cardigan II — 63.3% vs. 47.1%, difference 16.2 (95% CI 5.4–26.9), p=0.0040; GSP rank-based p=0.0296.

- FDA reviewer commentary: the review notes an interpretive distinction between analyzing "the difference of the ranks" versus "the ranks of the differences" for the GSP endpoint, and reports its own "ranks of the differences" analysis alongside the Applicant's for comparison — a methodological nuance specific to the rank-transformation fallback used here.

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2024/217347Orig1s000ltr.pdf (approval letter is the Reference ID 5398431 Multi-Discipline Review context document; letter itself confirms 6/18/2024 approval)

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/217347s000lbl.pdf (labeled strength "12.45% (w/w) sofpironium," stated as equivalent to "15% sofpironium bromide," the salt-form strength used in trial/MDR nomenclature)

- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (Reference ID 5398431/5249224; no separate Statistical Review, Summary Review, or Medical Review posted) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/217347Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (Cardigan I) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03836287; genuine Protocol (2020-08-06) and SAP (2021-07-30) posted

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (Cardigan II) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03948646; genuine Protocol and SAP (2021-08-10) posted

- Pivotal publication (pooled): Pariser D, Glaser DA, Del Rosso J, Bhatia N, Hooper D, Nestor MS. "Sofpironium topical gel, 12.45%, for the treatment of axillary hyperhidrosis: Pooled efficacy and safety results from 2 phase 3 randomized, controlled, double-blind studies." *J Am Acad Dermatol.* 2025 Jul. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jaad.2025.02.086), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40054501/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Sofpironium%20topical%20gel%2012.45%25%20for%20the%20treatment%20of%20axillary%20hyperhidrosis) — this pooled analysis is the only located pivotal-trial publication; no standalone per-trial (Cardigan I only, or Cardigan II only) publication was found.

**Other resources**

- No Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere participation was identified for Botanix or Kaken; not independently confirmed.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held for this application.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, p.87]* — the HDSM-Ax-7 responder analysis "was to be analyzed using logistic regression with terms for treatment, baseline score, and analysis center."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, p.87]* — the GSP endpoint "was to be analyzed with ANCOVA with terms for treatment, baseline GSP, and analysis center. A Shapiro-Wilk's test was to be conducted on the residuals to assess normality. If the assumption of normality is violated in either treatment arm, the analysis was to be conducted on the ranks."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, p.88]* — "Missing data on the vehicle arm was to use the Missing at Random (MAR) assumption. Missing data on the sofpironium arm was to be handled using a missing not a random (MNAR) assumption using a control-based imputations (CBI) model."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, p.86]* — "To control multiplicity, if the co-primary endpoints were statistically significant, the three secondary efficacy endpoints were analyzed sequentially in the order listed above."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, p.87-88]* — "the analysis for the 'difference of the ranks' and the 'ranks of the differences' ... may be reasonable, but the interpretation may be slightly different. This reviewer has included an analysis of the 'ranks of the differences' in the study results section for comparison."

### 43. Deuruxolitinib (Leqselvi) — NDA 217900

**Sponsor:** Sun Pharmaceutical Industries, Inc. Concert Pharmaceuticals, Inc. was the original sponsor for both pivotal trials and merged with Sun Pharmaceutical Industries, Inc. on March 31, 2023, becoming the Applicant of record for this NDA.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adults with severe alopecia areata.

**Approval date:** July 25, 2024, on a single review cycle (NDA received July 28, 2023; no Complete Response Letter was issued for this application — Drugs@FDA's action history shows only one approval action, and no blood-pressure-monitoring labeling language appears anywhere in the approved label or the Multi-Discipline Review text, contrary to an initial hypothesis that a mid-2023 CRL on that basis had occurred).

**Pivotal trial:** THRIVE-AA1 (protocol CP543.3001, NCT04518995) and THRIVE-AA2 (protocol CP543.3002, NCT04797650).

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, quadruple-masked, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trials; THRIVE-AA1 randomized 3:5:2 (12 mg:8 mg:placebo), THRIVE-AA2 randomized 1:2:1, stratified by baseline scalp hair loss category (partial, SALT 50–<95, vs. complete/near-complete, SALT ≥95); the 12 mg dose was placed on partial clinical hold May 17, 2023 for a potential dose-dependent thrombosis safety signal, and the approved NDA ultimately covers only the 8 mg twice-daily dose (partial clinical hold restricting an otherwise dual-dose NDA submission to its lower dose only); FDA rescinded the drug's Breakthrough Therapy Designation in a two-step process (Intent to Rescind, September 21, 2023; final rescission, March 14, 2024) after two competing JAK inhibitors (baricitinib, ritlecitinib) were approved for the same indication and removed the "substantial improvement over available therapy" basis for the designation (Breakthrough Therapy Designation rescinded due to intervening competitor approvals)

- *Endpoints:* Primary endpoint — percentage of participants achieving an absolute Severity of Alopecia Tool (SALT) score ≤20 at Week 24; key secondary endpoints included Scalp Hair Assessment PRO (SPRO) responder rate, earlier-week SALT≤20 rates, eyebrow (BETA) and eyelash (BELA) assessments, and CGI-I/PGI-I and HADS anxiety/depression scores

- *Primary analysis:* Mantel-Haenszel common-risk-difference test stratified by baseline scalp-hair-loss category (a variant of the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test already catalogued), comparing each active dose to placebo

- *Multiplicity:* Graphical alpha-propagation (Maurer-Bretz-type) procedure, implemented as parallel hierarchical/gatekeeping trees for the 12 mg and 8 mg doses (each starting at one-sided α=0.025), cascading through SALT≤20 at Week 24 → SPRO → SALT≤20 at Weeks 20/16/12/8

- *Missing data/bias:* Multiple imputation via a Fully Conditional Specification (FCS) regression method for missing SALT scores classified as Missing at Random, combined via SAS PROC MIANALYZE, as the primary approach (FCS-based MI is not the same named method as the jump-to-reference or tipping-point approaches already catalogued); pre-specified sensitivity analyses under a Missing Not at Random assumption and a separate tipping-point analysis

- *Regulatory:* No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held ("there were no issues that warranted an advisory committee discussion"); FDA's pre-submission review documented disagreement with the sponsor's originally proposed LOCF-based missing-data plan and originally proposed non-multiplicity-adjusted dose-hierarchy testing, both of which were revised in the final SAP

**Trial design & endpoints**

- THRIVE-AA1 (NCT04518995): 706 enrolled, 2020–2022, randomized 3:5:2 (12 mg:8 mg:placebo). THRIVE-AA2 (NCT04797650): 517 enrolled, June–December 2021, randomized 1:2:1. Neither trial has a posted protocol/SAP document on ClinicalTrials.gov.

- Eligibility: adults 18–65 with a current alopecia areata episode of 6 months to 10 years' duration and a baseline SALT score ≥50 (at least 50% scalp hair loss).

- Primary analysis population and method: Mantel-Haenszel common risk difference (stratified by baseline hair-loss category) at Week 24, with multiple imputation (FCS regression) as the primary missing-data handling and graphical multiplicity control across the dose/endpoint hierarchy described above.

- Primary efficacy results (Multi-Discipline Review Table 24, multiple-imputation/MAR analysis, efficacy population): THRIVE-AA1 — 8 mg BID vs. placebo, common risk difference 0.28 (95% CI 0.23–0.33, p<0.0001); 12 mg BID vs. placebo, 0.39 (95% CI 0.32–0.46, p<0.0001). THRIVE-AA2 — 8 mg BID, 0.31 (95% CI 0.25–0.37, p<0.0001); 12 mg BID, 0.36 (95% CI 0.27–0.45, p<0.0001).

- No separate FDA Statistical Review PDF exists for this NDA; FDA used its combined Multi-Discipline Review format, with the statistical evaluation embedded as Section 8.

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter (corrected) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2024/217900Orig1s000correctedltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label (corrected) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/217900Orig1s000correctedlbl.pdf

- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (Reference ID 5418639, §8 statistical evaluation) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/217900Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (THRIVE-AA1) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04518995 (no protocol/SAP posted)

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (THRIVE-AA2) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04797650 (no protocol/SAP posted)

- Pivotal publication (THRIVE-AA1): King B, Senna MM, Mesinkovska NA, et al. (Cassella J, senior author). "Efficacy and safety of deuruxolitinib, an oral selective Janus kinase inhibitor, in adults with alopecia areata: Results from the Phase 3 randomized, controlled trial (THRIVE-AA1)." *J Am Acad Dermatol.* 2024;91(5):880-888. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jaad.2024.06.097), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39053611/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Efficacy%20and%20safety%20of%20deuruxolitinib%20THRIVE-AA1)

- Pivotal publication (THRIVE-AA2): Tsianakas A, Passeron T, Magnolo N, et al. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jaad.2025.11.070), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41317911/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Efficacy%20and%20safety%20of%20deuruxolitinib%20THRIVE-AA2) — note the unusually long ~4-year gap between trial completion and this publication, which is an internally consistent PubMed record, not a citation error.

**Other resources**

- No Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere participation was identified for Sun Pharma or Concert Pharmaceuticals; not independently confirmed.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held for this application.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, p.95]* — "Randomization was stratified by scalp hair loss into one of the following two categories: 1) Partial scalp hair loss (SALT ≥50 and <95); 2) Complete or near-complete scalp hair loss (SALT ≥95)."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, p.98]* — "Pairwise treatment group differences from placebo will be assessed with the Mantel-Haenszel test (common risk difference) using baseline scalp hair loss (partial vs. complete/near-complete) as the stratification factor, for each active treatment group versus placebo."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, pp.98-99]* — "prior to database lock, the missing data pattern for missing SALT scores will be classified as either missing at random (MAR) or potentially missing not at random (MNAR)... multiple imputation will be used to handle missing data using the Fully Conditional Specification regression method... combined using SAS PROC MIANALYZE."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, p.100]* — "Multiplicity was controlled using graphical procedures for Trial CP543.3001 and Trial CP543.3002," per "Figure 8. Hierarchical Testing," citing "pg 72 of CP543-3001 clinical study report."

After the completion of the Covered Studies, CP543.3001 and CP543.3002, Concert merged with Sun Pharmaceutical Industries (Sun), Inc. (March 31, 2023), the Applicant for this NDA."

### 44. Nemolizumab-ilto (Nemluvio) — BLA 761390

**Correction to source list:** nemolizumab-ilto's actual brand name is **Nemluvio**, not Ebglyss, and its sponsor is **Galderma Laboratories, L.P.**, not Eli Lilly. BLA 761306/brand "Ebglyss," approved the same week (September 13, 2024) by Eli Lilly, is actually **lebrikizumab-lbkz**, an IL-13 antagonist for atopic dermatitis with its own distinct pivotal program (ADvocate 1, ADvocate 2, ADhere) — a different drug entirely from the IL-31 receptor alpha antagonist described in the task brief and researched here. This entry documents nemolizumab-ilto/Nemluvio/BLA 761390 (Galderma), matching the IL-31RA mechanism, ARCADIA 1/ARCADIA 2 trials, and atopic dermatitis indication actually described in the task.

**Sponsor:** Galderma Laboratories, L.P.

**Indication approved:** Nemluvio was originally approved (BLA 761390, August 12, 2024) for adults with prurigo nodularis. The atopic dermatitis indication researched here was added by supplement (761390s002/761391s001, approved June 26, 2025): "treatment of adults and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis in combination with topical corticosteroids and/or calcineurin inhibitors when the disease is not adequately controlled with topical prescription therapies."

**Approval date:** August 12, 2024 (original BLA, prurigo nodularis); June 26, 2025 (atopic dermatitis indication added via supplement, based on the ARCADIA trials).

**Pivotal trial:** ARCADIA 1 (NCT03985943) and ARCADIA 2 (NCT03989349).

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trials with background topical corticosteroid and/or calcineurin-inhibitor therapy in both arms, approximately 2:1 randomization (1,728 subjects total across both trials, ages ≥12); a responder re-randomization at Week 16 (nemolizumab every 4 weeks, nemolizumab every 8 weeks, or placebo every 4 weeks) extended the controlled comparison through Week 48

- *Endpoints:* Co-primary endpoints — IGA success (IGA 0 or 1 with ≥2-point reduction from baseline) and EASI-75 (≥75% improvement in EASI from baseline), both at Week 16; key secondary endpoint — ≥4-point improvement in the Peak Pruritus Numerical Rating Scale (PP-NRS) at Week 16

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by analysis center and baseline body weight (<90 kg vs. ≥90 kg) for all primary/key secondary binary endpoints — this stratification detail comes from FDA's Integrated Review of the companion prurigo nodularis (OLYMPIA) program rather than an ARCADIA-specific FDA review, since no FDA statistical/multi-discipline review of the atopic-dermatitis supplement has been posted as of this research; treat as illustrative of Galderma's standard analytic approach for this drug rather than as ARCADIA-review-confirmed text

- *Multiplicity:* Fixed sequential (step-down) testing to control the two-sided Type I error rate at 0.05, in a pre-specified hierarchical order across primary and key secondary endpoints, stopping at the first non-significant step (order documented for the OLYMPIA/prurigo nodularis program; ARCADIA-specific order not independently located in a posted FDA document)

- *Missing data/bias:* ICH E9(R1) estimand framework explicitly specified in the protocol/SAP — composite-variable strategy for rescue-therapy use (rescue before the assessment timepoint counted as non-response) and treatment-policy strategy for treatment discontinuation (observed post-discontinuation data used as collected); non-responder imputation applied for missing PP-NRS diary data (fewer than 4 entries in a 7-day window); pre-specified sensitivity analyses included tipping-point analysis, MAR multiple imputation (MCMC/regression), and MNAR multiple imputation via controlled pattern (placebo-based) imputation (explicit ICH E9(R1) estimand-strategy specification, combining a composite and a treatment-policy intercurrent-event handling rule for a single binary responder endpoint, is not yet a distinct entry in this taxonomy)

- *Regulatory:* No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held for the original BLA ("Your application for nemolizumab was not referred to an FDA advisory committee"); Breakthrough Therapy Designation was granted November 25, 2019 (scope — prurigo nodularis and/or atopic dermatitis — not disambiguated in the documents reviewed); no FDA review package specific to the atopic-dermatitis supplement (SUPPL-2) has been posted on Drugs@FDA as of this research

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ARCADIA 1 (NCT03985943): 620 nemolizumab / 321 placebo. ARCADIA 2 (NCT03989349): 522 nemolizumab / 265 placebo. Both randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials in patients ≥12 years old with chronic atopic dermatitis (≥2 years by AAD consensus criteria), EASI ≥16, IGA ≥3, BSA involvement ≥10%, Peak Pruritus NRS ≥4.0, and documented inadequate response to topical medications; weight exclusion <30 kg.

- Dosing: initial 60 mg (two 30 mg injections), then 30 mg every 4 weeks through Week 16 with background TCS/TCI; responders re-randomized at Week 16 to nemolizumab every 4 weeks, nemolizumab every 8 weeks, or placebo every 4 weeks through Week 48.

- Co-primary results at Week 16 (label Table 4): ARCADIA 1 — IGA 0/1 36% vs. 25% (difference 12%, 95% CI 6–17%); EASI-75 44% vs. 29% (difference 15%, CI 9–21%); PP-NRS ≥4 33% vs. 15% (difference 18%, CI 13–23%). ARCADIA 2 — broadly similar magnitude differences (IGA ~12%, EASI-75 ~12%, PP-NRS ~21%).

- Both trials had a Data Monitoring Committee. Protocol dated 2021-11-17; SAP dated 2022-11-10, both posted on ClinicalTrials.gov.

- FDA's Integrated Review of the original (prurigo nodularis) program describes the estimand framework and CMH/multiplicity methodology detailed above; this same Galderma-standard framework is presumed (not confirmed via an ARCADIA-specific FDA document) to extend to the atopic-dermatitis supplement.

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter (original, prurigo nodularis) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2024/761390Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label (current, includes atopic dermatitis/ARCADIA data) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/761390s002,761391s001lbl.pdf

- FDA Integrated Review (original BLA, prurigo nodularis/OLYMPIA program only — contains no ARCADIA content) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/761390Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf

- No FDA review package (Statistical Review, Multi-Discipline Review, or Integrated Review) has been posted for the atopic-dermatitis supplement (761390s002) as of this research

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (ARCADIA 1) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03985943; genuine Protocol (2021-11-17) and SAP (2022-11-10) posted

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (ARCADIA 2) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03989349

- Pivotal publication: Silverberg JI, Wollenberg A, Reich A, et al.; ARCADIA 1 and ARCADIA 2 Study Investigators. "Nemolizumab with concomitant topical therapy in adolescents and adults with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (ARCADIA 1 and ARCADIA 2): results from two replicate, double-blind, randomised controlled phase 3 trials." *Lancet.* 2024;404(10451):445-460. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(24)01203-0>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39067461/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Nemolizumab%20with%20concomitant%20topical%20therapy%20ARCADIA%201%20ARCADIA%202)

**Other resources**

- Galderma's Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere participation could not be confirmed for this specific program; not independently verified.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held for the original BLA; not separately confirmed for the atopic-dermatitis supplement, though no evidence of one was found.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review of the original (prurigo nodularis) BLA, p.29 — cited here as the best available public documentation of Galderma's standard nemolizumab statistical framework, not as ARCADIA-specific confirmed text]* — "Estimands — The protocol and statistical analysis plan (SAP) specified the following as the main estimand for the primary and key secondary efficacy endpoints (all binary endpoints): Treatments: nemolizumab and placebo; Population: ITT Population; Endpoint: a binary response at a specified timepoint; Intercurrent Events (ICEs) and Strategy for Handling: – Rescue Therapy: subjects who use rescue therapy on or prior to the specified timepoint for the endpoint are considered as non-responder (composite variable strategy) – Treatment Discontinuation: observed data after treatment discontinuation will be used (treatment policy strategy); Population-level Summary Measure: difference in proportions between nemolizumab and placebo."

- *[verbatim, same source]* — "...analyzing the primary and key secondary efficacy endpoints (all binary endpoints) using the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by analysis center and baseline body weight (<90 kg and ≥90 kg)... Missing data was specified to be imputed using the non-responder imputation approach."

- *[verbatim, same source]* — "...using a fixed sequential testing approach to control the Type I error rate at the two-sided 0.05 level," with endpoints tested in a pre-specified hierarchical order, stopping when non-significant; sensitivity analyses specified: Tipping Point Analysis, Multiple Imputation (MAR, via MCMC + regression), Multiple Imputation (MNAR, controlled pattern imputation using placebo-only data), and LOCF.

- *[verbatim, label §14.2]* — for the ARCADIA program specifically: "Subjects who received rescue treatment or had missing data (fewer than 4 PP-NRS daily diary entries in a 7-day period) were considered non-responders."

- **Reverse-engineered SAP note** — *[inferred]* Because no ARCADIA-specific FDA statistical review is yet public, the CMH-stratification and fixed-sequence multiplicity details above are inferred to carry over from the OLYMPIA/prurigo nodularis program to ARCADIA based on the shared sponsor, shared drug, and the label's confirmation of the same composite (rescue-as-non-responder) missing-data convention in both programs — not from a directly quoted ARCADIA statistical review.

### 45. Lebrikizumab-lbkz (Ebglyss) — BLA 761306

**Sponsor:** Eli Lilly and Company (the three pivotal trials were originally sponsored by Dermira, Inc., which Lilly acquired in January 2020; ClinicalTrials.gov records still carry Dermira protocol numbers DRM06-AD04/-AD05/-AD06 alongside Lilly's J2T-DM-KGAB/-KGAC/-KGAD numbering).

**Indication approved:** "EBGLYSS is an interleukin-13 antagonist indicated for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older who weigh at least 40 kg with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis whose disease is not adequately controlled with topical prescription therapies or when those therapies are not advisable. EBGLYSS can be used with or without topical corticosteroids." (label §1).

**Approval date:** September 13, 2024 (a corrected approval letter, effective the same date, was issued later to fix an erroneous PREA post-marketing-requirement completion date). This was Lilly's second review cycle: the original BLA (submitted September 28, 2022) received a Complete Response Letter on September 28, 2023 for unresolved CMC/manufacturing-facility-inspection deficiencies — not for any efficacy or statistical issue — and was resubmitted March 14, 2024.

**Pivotal trial:** ADvocate1 (Study J2T-DM-KGAB / DRM06-AD04, NCT04146363) and ADvocate2 (Study J2T-DM-KGAC / DRM06-AD05, NCT04178967) — identically designed 16-week monotherapy trials with a Week-16-to-52 randomized-withdrawal maintenance period; ADhere (Study J2T-DM-KGAD / DRM06-AD06, NCT04250337) — a 16-week trial of lebrikizumab added to background topical corticosteroids (TCS).

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group Phase 3 trials; ADvocate1 (N=424) and ADvocate2 (N=445) randomized 2:1 (lebrikizumab:placebo) as monotherapy through Week 16, with Week-16 responders (IGA 0/1 or EASI-75) re-randomized to lebrikizumab Q2W, lebrikizumab Q4W, or placebo through Week 52; ADhere (N=228) randomized 2:1 with background TCS in both arms through Week 16 only; randomization stratified by geographic region (US vs. EU vs. rest of world), age (adolescent 12–<18 years vs. adult ≥18 years), and baseline disease severity (IGA 3 vs. 4) in all three trials; a Good Clinical Practice misconduct finding at a site shared by ADvocate2 and ADhere (same investigator, "implausible homogeneity" of IGA scores) led to a mid-conduct SAP amendment defining a modified intent-to-treat (mITT) population, excluding 18 subjects from ADvocate2 and 17 from ADhere, as the primary efficacy population for those two trials

- *Endpoints:* Co-primary endpoints at Week 16 (all three trials) — percentage of patients with an Investigator's Global Assessment (IGA) score of 0 or 1 with a ≥2-point reduction from baseline, and percentage achieving EASI-75 (≥75% reduction in Eczema Area and Severity Index score from baseline); major secondary hierarchy included EASI-90, Pruritus Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) ≥4-point improvement at Weeks 2/4/16, IGA 0/1 at Week 4, and sleep-loss score improvement at Week 16

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by geographic region, age category, and baseline disease severity for binary endpoints; ANCOVA (single timepoint) or MMRM (multiple timepoints) for continuous endpoints, both adjusted for the same stratification factors

- *Multiplicity:* Graphical alpha-propagation ("Algorithm 2" of Bretz et al. 2009/2011 — an already-catalogued Maurer-Bretz-type procedure) controlling the overall two-sided Type I error rate at 0.05 across all primary and major secondary endpoints per trial; the FDA statistical reviewer found the sponsor's submitted graphical-scheme figure for ADvocate1/ADvocate2 ambiguous and inconsistently drawn for the bottom four endpoints, and substituted its own reinterpretation of the intended alpha-recycling order rather than accepting the figure as submitted

- *Missing data/bias:* ICH E9(R1) hybrid estimand — combining a composite strategy (rescue medication or discontinuation for lack of efficacy imputed as failure by carrying baseline values forward) with a hypothetical strategy (discontinuation for other reasons treated as missing, to estimate the effect had treatment continued) for the primary/major-secondary analysis — followed by Markov Chain Monte Carlo Multiple Imputation, "MCMC-MI", for remaining missing data; a separate composite-strategy supportive estimand used non-responder imputation (NRI) instead, and a hypothetical-strategy supportive estimand for continuous endpoints used MMRM/LOCF; FDA required an added post hoc sensitivity analysis (during label review) comparing the Pruritus NRS endpoint under the sponsor's final, less-stringent ≥1-of-7-days observed-data criterion against FDA's originally preferred ≥4-of-7-days criterion, finding minimal impact on results

- *Regulatory:* No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held ("there were no efficacy, safety, or novel/complex regulatory issues that required input from an Advisory Committee"); Fast Track Designation was granted December 6, 2019; FDA issued pre-submission advice letters (December 11, 2019 and March 27, 2020) specifically on secondary-endpoint selection and missing-data handling; the original BLA received a Complete Response Letter (September 28, 2023) for CMC/facility-inspection deficiencies unrelated to the statistical package; a Good Clinical Practice (GCP) misconduct finding at a shared trial site (already-catalogued keyword) triggered the sponsor's SAP amendment to an mITT primary population, discussed at length by the FDA statistical reviewer

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Population (all three trials): adults and adolescents (12 to <18 years, weighing ≥40 kg) with chronic moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis, IGA ≥3, EASI ≥16, BSA involvement ≥10%, and documented inadequate response/intolerance to topical AD medications or for whom topicals were medically inadvisable.

- ADvocate1 (KGAB): 424 randomized (283 lebrikizumab / 141 placebo), monotherapy. ADvocate2 (KGAC): 445 randomized (295/150), monotherapy; mITT population (427) excluded 18 subjects from one investigator's site (14 lebrikizumab/4 placebo) following a GCP audit finding. ADhere (KGAD): 228 randomized (153 lebrikizumab+TCS/75 placebo+TCS); mITT population (211) excluded 17 subjects from the same investigator's second site (8/9).

- Induction dosing (all three trials): 500 mg (two 250 mg injections) at Weeks 0 and 2, then 250 mg every 2 weeks (Q2W) through Week 16. In ADvocate1/ADvocate2, Week-16 responders (IGA 0/1 or EASI-75) were re-randomized to lebrikizumab 250 mg Q2W, 250 mg Q4W, or placebo through Week 52 (maintenance/withdrawal design); ADhere ran combination therapy with TCS only through Week 16, with no maintenance period.

- Co-primary results at Week 16, MCMC-MI/ITT or mITT analysis (FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Executive Summary): ADvocate1 — IGA 0/1 43.1% (lebrikizumab) vs. 12.7% (placebo); EASI-75 58.8% vs. 16.2%. ADvocate2 — IGA 0/1 33.2% vs. 10.8%; EASI-75 52.1% vs. 18.1%. ADhere — IGA 0/1 41.2% (lebrikizumab+TCS) vs. 22.1% (placebo+TCS); EASI-75 69.5% vs. 42.2%. All comparisons p<0.0001 (Table 29/30 of the review, primary endpoint tables, are embedded as images in the PDF and not text-extractable, but the same figures are restated in the Executive Summary and corroborated in Tables 31–33 for the secondary endpoints).

- Major secondary results at Week 16 (Multi-Discipline Review Tables 31–33, CMH-adjusted difference, 95% CI): ADvocate1 — EASI-90 difference 28.8 (21.3, 36.3); Pruritus NRS-4 difference 32.9 (24.6, 41.3), both p<0.0001. ADvocate2 — EASI-90 difference 20.7 (13.3, 28.1); Pruritus NRS-4 difference 28.3 (20.0, 36.5), both p<0.0001; the Pruritus NRS-4 endpoint at Week 2 for ADvocate2 was the one major secondary endpoint that did not reach significance (difference 2.7, 95% CI −0.1–5.4, p=0.11), consistent with a graphical-testing branch that could still pass alpha to sibling nodes. ADhere — EASI-90 difference 18.9 (6.1, 31.7), p=0.01; Pruritus NRS-4 difference 19.2 (4.3, 34.1), p=0.02.

- FDA's site-exclusion/mITT finding (Multi-Discipline Review, "Compliance with Good Clinical Practices"): following database lock, the applicant identified "implausible homogeneity of efficacy results" from one investigator (Dr. Jose Carpio) who ran Site 5042 in ADvocate2 and Site 6006 in ADhere; nearly all his ADvocate2 subjects had identical IGA scores across multiple visits, and all 17 of his ADhere subjects (both arms) were recorded as Week-16 IGA responders. An OSI site inspection documented unreported protocol deviations and the investigator's evident lack of command of study procedures. FDA noted that including this site's data would have made the ADhere IGA endpoint non-significant, and separately flagged that 60.1% of ADhere's investigators also participated in ADvocate1 or ADvocate2 — concluding ADhere was "not fully independent" of the other two trials and treating it as supportive rather than co-equal pivotal evidence, notwithstanding its formal FDA-accepted role in the approval.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, p.95]* — "The protocol / statistical analysis plan (SAP) prespecified using the graphical multiple testing approach to control the overall Type I error rate at two-sided alpha of 0.05, for all primary and major secondary endpoints for the induction period (through Week 16) in each of the pivotal studies."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, p.95, Statistical Reviewers' Comment]* — "It should be noted that left Figure 7 does not display appropriately the recycling of the alpha level among the last 4 endpoints in the figure and some of arrows are incorrectly directed toward the 'IGA 01 adult W16' endpoint. It appears likely that the intention is to pass unused alpha among the four endpoints at the bottom of the hierarchy. However, because the exact procedure is unclear, we consider splitting the alpha level for testing the 'IGA 01 adult W16' endpoint among the 3 endpoints shown in the figure with their assigned weights and ignore recycling the alpha level among these 3 endpoints; then we consider a sequential approach for passing the alpha level for testing 'Pruritus NRS-4 W4' to 'Pruritus NRS-4 W2'."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, p.95–96]* — "Three types of estimands were used for the efficacy analysis in the induction period. The primary estimand was used for primary and all major secondary endpoints... The primary estimand used composite and hypothetical strategies for handling intercurrent events for the primary and key secondary endpoint analyses. Subjects who received topical or systemic rescue medication, or discontinued the treatment due to lack of efficacy, had values set to their baseline values subsequent to this time through Week 16 (composite); data after treatment discontinuation due to any other reasons were treated as missing (hypothetical). After the handling of intercurrent events, the missing data were imputed with the Markov Chain Monte Carlo Multiple Imputation (MCMC-MI) method... The supportive estimand used a composite strategy for handling intercurrent events for the primary and secondary categorical endpoints analyses... After the handling of intercurrent events, any remaining missing data were imputed with nonresponder imputation (NRI)... For the secondary continuous endpoints analyses conducted relative to the supportive estimand (hypothetical), data after the use of rescue medication or treatment discontinuation were treated as missing and missing data was handle with mixed-effects model of repeated measures (MMRM) or last observation carried forward (LOCF)."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, p.96–97, Compliance with Good Clinical Practices]* — "For Studies KGAC and KGAD, following the primary outcome database lock, the applicant identified implausible homogeneity of efficacy results on one investigator (Dr. Carpio) who participated in two studies (Site 5042 in Study KGAC and 6006 in Study KGAD)... As a result of the findings of the site audit, the applicant defined a modified intent to treat (mITT) population that excluded the 18 subjects in Study KGAC... and 17 subjects in Study KGAD... from efficacy and safety analyses. The mITT population became the primary efficacy analysis population... in Study KGAD, inclusion of the data from the site causes IGA endpoint to no longer be statistically significant because the site had 100% response rates in both groups... a substantial proportion (60.1%) of the investigators who participated in Study KGAD also participated in one of the other two trials. Thus, Study KGAD is not fully independent from Study KGAB and KGAC... To minimize the impact of the common investigators, we consider Study KGAD to be supportive."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Table 31 footnote, p.112]* — "Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test adjusted by geographic region (US versus EU versus rest of world), age (adolescent patients 12 to <18 versus adults ≥18 years) and disease severity (IGA 3 versus 4)."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, p.198]* — "The Agency did not hold an Advisory Committee Meeting for this application, because there were no efficacy, safety, or novel/complex regulatory issues that required input from an Advisory Committee."

- *[reconstructed from a character-spaced PDF text layer, ADvocate1 SAP (J2T-DM-KGAB) Version 4, §5.2, ClinicalTrials.gov — the posted PDF's text layer has every glyph individually positioned with near-uniform inter-character and inter-word spacing, so this passage was manually re-segmented into words rather than recovered by an automated single/double-space heuristic; treat as a faithful paraphrase-by-transcription, not a verbatim copy-paste]* — "A sample size of 96 for lebrikizumab 250 mg Q2W versus 48 for placebo will have more than 95% power to detect a statistically significant difference based on a two group continuity corrected chi-square test with a two-sided significance level of 0.05 for each of the co-primary endpoints, which imply an overall power of at least 90%. However, to ensure sufficient safety information is collected and to ensure sufficient responders for the Maintenance Period, the sample size will be increased to 400 in total with a randomization ratio of 2:1 lebrikizumab:placebo."

- *[reconstructed from a character-spaced PDF text layer, same source, §6.2.1.1]* — "The primary estimand is a hybrid estimand representing the primary clinical question of interest: what is the difference between treatment conditions, i.e., Lebrikizumab vs Placebo, in the target patient population, in successful responses or means after 16 weeks achieved without use of rescue medication and if all patients continued with treatment except those who discontinued due to lack of efficacy?"

- **Reverse-engineered SAP note** — *[inferred]* No FDA statistical review addresses ADvocate1's primary-endpoint table directly by page (Tables 29–30 of the Multi-Discipline Review are embedded as images and not text-extractable); the Week-16 co-primary results quoted above are inferred to be consistent with the SAP's pre-specified CMH/MCMC-MI hybrid-estimand analysis because they match, to within rounding, the same figures independently restated in the review's Executive Summary and corroborated by the major-secondary-endpoint tables (31–33) that do carry the identical CMH/stratification footnote.

### 46. Garadacimab-gxii (Andembry) — BLA 761367

**Sponsor:** CSL Behring LLC.

**Indication approved:** Prophylaxis to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adult and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older.

**Approval date:** June 16, 2025 (BLA received June 29, 2023; a Complete Response Letter was issued October 7, 2024; the sponsor's complete-response resubmission was dated December 17, 2024).

**Pivotal trial:** VANGUARD (protocol CSL312_3001, NCT04656418).

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-arm trial, 3:2 active:placebo randomization, with a prospective 1-2-month Run-in Period (no prophylaxis permitted) used to confirm disease activity and establish each subject's baseline HAE attack rate before randomization into a 6-month double-blind Treatment Period; randomization required experiencing ≥2 attacks during the Run-in Period (a prospective observation/run-in period establishing a within-subject baseline attack rate as an eligibility gate for randomization, distinct from any run-in design already catalogued, and directly comparable to the run-in design used in donidalorsen/Dawnzera's OASIS-HAE trial below)

- *Endpoints:* Primary endpoint — time-normalized number of HAE attacks per month during the 6-month Treatment Period

- *Primary analysis:* Two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test (not negative binomial or Poisson regression, contrary to an initial hypothesis) as the pre-specified primary analysis, comparing time-normalized attack rates between arms; a Poisson regression model (log link, Pearson chi-square scaling for overdispersion, baseline run-in attack rate as covariate, log-treatment-duration offset) was pre-specified only as a sensitivity analysis (Wilcoxon rank-sum test as the primary confirmatory analysis for a recurrent-event HAE-prophylaxis endpoint, with a count-regression model relegated to sensitivity-analysis status, is the reverse of the more typical count-regression-as-primary pattern seen elsewhere in this taxonomy)

- *Missing data/bias:* Primary endpoint treated as missing only if a subject discontinued study treatment within 30 days of the first dose; FDA's Integrated Review separately flagged an estimand/test mismatch — "the population-level summary specified in the Applicant's primary estimand was the median, but the Wilcoxon rank sum test is not a median test" — and noted a similar mismatch for a key secondary endpoint where only descriptive statistics could be presented

- *Regulatory:* Complete Response Letter (CRL) followed by resubmission and approval; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held ("the application did not raise challenging efficacy or safety issues that required external input")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- VANGUARD (NCT04656418): 64 randomized, 3:2 (garadacimab:placebo), ages ≥12, C1-INH HAE Type 1/2, with prior documented attack history. Design: Screening Period (up to 1 month) → Run-in Period (up to 2 months, no prophylaxis) → 6-month double-blind Treatment Period → follow-up or rollover to an open-label extension.

- Randomization eligibility (verbatim protocol criterion): subjects had to have "participated in the Run-in Period for at least 1 month" and "experienced at least an average of 1 HAE attack per month during the Run-in Period (eg, experienced a total of at least 2 HAE attacks)." Stratification factors at randomization: age (≤17 vs. >17) and baseline Run-in attack rate (1 to <3/month vs. ≥3/month).

- Sample size/power (SAP §4.5): 60 subjects planned, with 40 completers targeted to give approximately 90% power for a two-sided Wilcoxon test at α=0.05, assuming Poisson-distributed monthly attack rates of 0.3125 (garadacimab) and 1.3 (placebo).

- Primary result (label Table, LS means from the sensitivity-analysis Poisson model, p-value from the primary Wilcoxon test): garadacimab 0.22 attacks/month (95% CI 0.11–0.47) vs. placebo 2.07 (95% CI 1.49–2.87); 89.2% reduction (95% CI 75.6–95.2%); p<0.001.

### 47. Sebetralstat (Ekterly) — NDA 219301

**Sponsor:** KalVista Pharmaceuticals Limited.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of acute attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adult and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older — the first oral, on-demand rescue therapy for acute HAE attacks (all previously approved on-demand treatments — icatibant, C1-inhibitor, ecallantide — are injectable or infused).

**Approval date:** July 3, 2025 (NDA received June 17, 2024).

**Pivotal trial:** KONFIDENT (protocol KVD900-301, NCT05259917); a long-term open-label extension, KONFIDENT-S (protocol KVD900-302, NCT05505916), provided supportive safety data.

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, three-treatment, three-period complete crossover trial — each of 136 enrolled patients was randomized to a sequence covering all three treatments (placebo, 300 mg, 600 mg sebetralstat), treating one qualifying HAE attack per period (a complete crossover design for an acute/episodic on-demand indication, in which each patient treats multiple independent qualifying attacks under a randomized treatment sequence, rather than the parallel-group or simple two-period crossover designs already catalogued)

- *Endpoints:* Primary endpoint — time to beginning of symptom relief (Patient Global Impression of Change ≥"a little better," at 2 consecutive timepoints) within 12 hours; key secondary endpoints — time to first decrease in symptom severity (Patient Global Impression of Severity) within 12 hours, and time to complete attack resolution within 24 hours

- *Primary analysis:* Gehan score transformation of the time-to-event data, followed by a linear mixed model on the resulting scores with fixed effects for sequence, period, and treatment and a random effect for patient nested within sequence — the mechanism used to account for within-patient correlation across multiple attacks in a censored time-to-event crossover design (Gehan-score-transform-plus-linear-mixed-model analysis of censored time-to-event crossover data, citing Siegel, Ounpraseuth & Kodell 2014, is not a generalized-estimating-equations/sandwich-variance approach and is not yet catalogued)

- *Multiplicity:* Two pairwise dose-vs-placebo comparisons controlled via a Bonferroni split (0.025 each) with a "loop-back" feature reallocating unused alpha from a fully-rejected comparison to the other comparison — related to, but a specific named extension of, the existing "alpha recycling" concept — combined with fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing per dose across the primary and two key secondary endpoints

- *Missing data/bias:* Composite-variable strategy for the intercurrent event of conventional (rescue) attack treatment; missing data treated as right-censored under a Missing at Random assumption; FDA statistical reviewers overrode the sponsor's pre-specified SAP convention of censoring underivable results at Time 0, instead requiring censoring at the assessment-window boundary (Hour 12), and the primary analysis as reported reflects FDA's censoring rule, not the sponsor's original SAP specification (FDA-directed change to a pre-specified censoring-time convention for underivable time-to-event results, applied to the primary analysis actually reported)

- *Regulatory:* Substantial evidence of effectiveness rests on a single adequate and well-controlled trial (KONFIDENT) plus confirmatory pharmacologic/mechanistic evidence, rather than two independent pivotal trials (single-trial approval supported by confirmatory mechanistic/pharmacologic-plausibility evidence, outside the oncology same-class-precedent context already catalogued); no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- KONFIDENT (NCT05259917): 136 enrolled (ClinicalTrials.gov total), 66 sites in 20 countries; FDA's Drug Trials Snapshot reports 110 completers (60% female, 40% male; 97 adults, 13 adolescents 12–17; 92% HAE Type I, 8% Type II) — the two enrollment figures are not fully reconciled and both are reported here as found. Complete 3×3 crossover: each patient received placebo, 300 mg, and 600 mg sebetralstat across three separate qualifying attacks, in a randomized sequence.

- FDA Drug Trials Snapshot result: 76% of attacks reported symptom relief within 12 hours on the 600 mg dose vs. 49% on placebo.

- Sample size/power: powered from Phase 2 (Trial 201) assumptions of a 1.6-hour (active) vs. 9-hour (placebo) median time to symptom relief; target ~66 completers per arm gave approximately 90% power at two-sided α=0.025 per comparison, using a simulation-based power calculation (parallel-group Gehan-Wilcoxon approximation, since no commercial software existed for the intended crossover-specific power method).

**Documents**

### 48. Delgocitinib (Anzupgo) — NDA 219155

**Sponsor:** LEO Pharma A/S (c/o LEO Pharma Inc., Madison, NJ).

**Indication approved:** Topical treatment of moderate to severe chronic hand eczema (CHE) in adults who have had an inadequate response to, or for whom, topical corticosteroids are not advisable.

**Approval date:** July 23, 2025 (NDA received July 23, 2024).

**Pivotal trial:** DELTA 1 (protocol LP0133-1401, NCT04871711) and DELTA 2 (protocol LP0133-1402, NCT04872101) — not "DELTA FORCE," despite that name appearing in some secondary sources; a long-term extension, DELTA 3 (NCT04949841), followed completers of DELTA 1/2.

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group trials, 2:1 randomization (delgocitinib cream 20 mg/g : cream vehicle), stratified by region (Europe/North America) and baseline Investigator's Global Assessment for Chronic Hand Eczema (IGA-CHE) score (3 or 4), ~55 sites across Europe and Canada, 16-week treatment period; eligibility required IGA-CHE 3 or 4 and a Hand Eczema Symptom Diary (HESD) itch score ≥4, not the Hand Eczema Severity Index (HECSI) as sometimes assumed — HECSI is a secondary endpoint only, not an eligibility criterion

- *Endpoints:* Primary endpoint — IGA-CHE treatment success (IGA-CHE 0 or 1 with ≥2-step improvement from baseline) at Week 16; key secondary endpoints — HESD itch and composite score improvement thresholds, HECSI-90/HECSI-75, DLQI change, Hand Eczema Impact Scale (HEIS)

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by region and baseline IGA-CHE score for binary endpoints; ANCOVA (treatment, region, baseline IGA-CHE, baseline value) for continuous endpoints

- *Multiplicity:* Closed testing procedure with hierarchical (fixed-sequence) tests, alpha splitting, and alpha recycling, controlling overall Type I error at one-sided 2.5% within each trial separately — IGA-CHE treatment success at Week 16 had to be established before testing any key secondary endpoint

- *Missing data/bias:* Composite estimand strategy — intercurrent events (rescue treatment initiation, permanent discontinuation) counted as non-response for binary endpoints; supplementary "pandemic-modified composite" and treatment-policy estimands were specified as COVID-19-era SAP provisions (a pandemic-modified composite estimand as a named supplementary intercurrent-event handling strategy, distinct from the primary composite/treatment-policy estimand pair); multiple imputation and worst-observation-carried-forward specified for certain supplementary-estimand sensitivity analyses, plus a tipping-point analysis

- *Regulatory:* No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held; no FDA Statistical Review, Multi-Discipline Review, or Summary Review has been posted for this NDA as of this research — only the approval letter and label are public

**Trial design & endpoints**

- DELTA 1 (NCT04871711): 487 enrolled (325 delgocitinib / 162 vehicle in the label's efficacy table). DELTA 2 (NCT04872101): 473 enrolled (313 delgocitinib / 159 vehicle). Both randomized 2:1, double-blind, vehicle-controlled, parallel, twice-daily application for 16 weeks.

- Sample-size justification (SAP §14.1, verbatim): "With a one-sided significance level of 2.5%, a sample size of 470 subjects randomised will provide at least 99% power for detecting a treatment difference for the primary endpoint, assuming an IGA-CHE TS response rate at Week 16 of 40% vs. 10% for delgocitinib cream 20 mg/g and cream vehicle, respectively." Assumptions were based on the Phase 2b dose-ranging trial (LP0133-1273).

- Analysis sets: Full Analysis Set (all randomized, IMP-exposed subjects, analyzed as randomized per ICH E9 §5.2.1); Safety Set (all IMP-exposed).

- Primary results (label Table, IGA-CHE treatment success): DELTA 1 — 20% (64/325) delgocitinib vs. 10% (16/162) vehicle, difference 10% (95% CI 4–16%). DELTA 2 — 29% (91/313) vs. 7% (11/159), difference 22% (95% CI 16–29%).

- Baseline population (pooled): mean age 44.1 years; 64% female; chronic hand eczema subtypes — atopic 35.9%, hyperkeratotic 21.5%, irritant contact 19.6%, allergic contact 13.9%, vesicular 9.1%; 28% had ≥2 overlapping subtypes.

### 49. Donidalorsen (Dawnzera) — NDA 219407

**Sponsor:** Ionis Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Prophylaxis to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older.

**Approval date:** August 21, 2025 (NDA received August 21, 2024).

**Pivotal trial:** OASIS-HAE (NCT05139810); a related open-label extension, OASISplus (NCT05392114), provided long-term safety/immunogenicity follow-up.

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, quadruple-masked, placebo-controlled, parallel trial with a prospective 8-week Run-in/screening period requiring ≥2 investigator-confirmed HAE attacks for eligibility (the same run-in-to-establish-baseline-attack-rate design used in garadacimab/Andembry's VANGUARD trial above); 2:1 randomization overall between two dosing-regimen cohorts (80 mg subcutaneously every 4 weeks, n=45; every 8 weeks, n=23) and a pooled placebo group (n=22)

- *Endpoints:* Primary endpoint — time-normalized investigator-confirmed HAE attack rate per month from Week 1 (registry: through Week 25; label: Week 0 through Week 24 — a labeling/registry numbering-convention difference, not reconciled further here, reported as found in each source)

- *Primary analysis:* Poisson regression (log link, Pearson chi-square scaling for overdispersion, time-normalized run-in attack rate as a covariate, log-time-in-months offset) as the primary analysis; negative binomial regression specified as a pre-specified sensitivity analysis, with Fisher's exact test as a pre-specified fallback if the Poisson model failed to converge (e.g., zero post-baseline events in one arm) — both of these are existing catalogued methods, but the primary/sensitivity role assignment (Poisson primary, negative binomial secondary) matches this taxonomy's existing "Poisson regression with an exposure-time offset" entry directly

- *Missing data/bias:* Treatment-policy strategy (all available data used) as the primary approach to missing data; pre-specified sensitivity analyses included a pattern-mixture multiple-imputation model and a tipping-point analysis

- *Regulatory:* No FDA Statistical Review or Multi-Discipline Review has been posted for this NDA as of this research (confirmed via the review-package table-of-contents flags, all discipline-review flags except chemistry/integrated/name/risk set to zero); no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was identified, though this was not exhaustively confirmed against FDA's advisory-committee calendar archive

**Trial design & endpoints**

- OASIS-HAE (NCT05139810): 90-91 patients (label vs. registry counts differ slightly), ages ≥12, HAE Type I/II, ≥2 investigator-confirmed attacks during an 8-week run-in. Dosing: 80 mg every 4 weeks (Weeks 1, 5, 9, 13, 17, 21) or every 8 weeks (Weeks 1, 9, 17), vs. matching placebo.

- Sample-size justification (Protocol/SAP §10.2, verbatim): "Assuming an HAE attack rate of 13.26 attacks per 6-month period in the placebo group and an HAE attack rate of 1.38 attacks per 6-month period in the ISIS 721744 80 mg every 4 weeks group, the sample size of 54 patients (2:1 ratio) will provide at least 90% power for the primary endpoint, with a 0.05 significance level."

- Platelet-count safety monitoring (ASO-class-specific): every-4-week monitoring during treatment and post-treatment, with a tiered dose-modification/stopping algorithm based on platelet-count thresholds (label: mean platelet count fell 9.6% from baseline at Week 25 on the every-4-week regimen; no patient across OASIS-HAE and two other studies had a platelet count <50,000/mm³, and no major bleeding events were associated with low platelet counts).

- Primary results (label Table 4): 80 mg every 4 weeks — attack rate 0.44/4 weeks (95% CI 0.27–0.73) vs. placebo 2.26 (95% CI 1.66–3.09), −81% reduction (95% CI −89, −65), p<0.001. Every 8 weeks — 1.02 (95% CI 0.65–1.59), −55% reduction (95% CI −74, −22), p=0.004.

### 50. Remibrutinib (Rhapsido) — NDA 218436

**Sponsor:** Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) in adult patients who remain symptomatic despite H1-antihistamine treatment; limitation of use — not indicated for other forms of urticaria. Note: this is narrower than an "adults and adolescents" population — both the label and the approval letter specify adult patients only; a separate adolescent trial (NCT05677451) is ongoing but was not part of this approval.

**Approval date:** September 30, 2025 (NDA received January 31, 2025).

**Pivotal trial:** REMIX-1 (protocol CLOU064A2301, NCT05030311) and REMIX-2 (protocol CLOU064A2302, NCT05032157).

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Two identical, randomized, quadruple-masked, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, 52-week trials (24-week double-blind placebo-controlled period followed by 28-week open-label extension), 2:1 randomization (remibrutinib 25 mg twice daily : placebo); 925 total randomized (REMIX-1 n=462, REMIX-2 n=450), with 912 in the efficacy analysis from the 24-week controlled period; eligibility required CSU ≥6 months, UAS7 ≥16, ISS7 ≥6, and HSS7 ≥6 in the 7 days before randomization

- *Endpoints:* Co-primary endpoints — absolute change from baseline in Itch Severity Score over 7 days (ISS7) and Hive Severity Score over 7 days (HSS7) at Week 12; key secondary endpoint — absolute change from baseline in Urticaria Activity Score over 7 days (UAS7) at Week 12; additional secondaries included proportions achieving UAS7 ≤6 and UAS7=0 (complete absence of itch/hives) at Weeks 2 and 12

- *Primary analysis:* Mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) with unstructured covariance for continuous endpoints (ISS7, HSS7, UAS7) — fixed effects for treatment, baseline score, randomization strata, week, and treatment-by-week and baseline-by-week interactions; logistic regression (treatment, region, prior anti-IgE biologic exposure, baseline UAS7) for binary responder endpoints

- *Multiplicity:* Strictly hierarchical (fixed-sequence) graphical testing procedure — matching this taxonomy's existing "Graphical alpha-propagation method (Maurer-Bretz)" entry, citing the same Bretz et al. (2009) methodological reference — with a union-intersection rule requiring both co-primary elementary hypotheses (ISS7 and HSS7) to be individually rejected before the union null is rejected, and secondary hypotheses tested only if the co-primary union hypothesis is rejected; two parallel primary-endpoint "scenarios" (ISS7/HSS7 co-primary for the US; UAS7-only primary for Japan/China) were pre-specified in the SAP to satisfy different regulators' precedent — one trial design supporting two distinct regional primary-endpoint definitions is a notable feature, though it did not require a new taxonomy term given the existing graphical-testing framework

- *Missing data/bias:* ICH E9(R1) estimand framework explicitly specified — treatment-policy strategy for treatment discontinuation regardless of compliance, and composite strategy for intake of strongly confounding prohibited medication (e.g., biologics before Week 12, cyclosporine after Week 8, systemic corticosteroids after Week 8); missing data handled by reference-based multiple imputation using jump-to-reference (J2R) — matching this taxonomy's existing "Jump-to-reference (J2R) multiple imputation" entry — implemented as a two-stage Bayesian (MCMC) repeated-measures approach

- *Regulatory:* No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held ("evaluation of the safety data ... did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues ... and there were no controversial issues"); no FDA Statistical Review or Multi-Discipline Review has been posted for this NDA as of this research

**Trial design & endpoints**

- REMIX-1 (NCT05030311, 470 planned/462 enrolled) and REMIX-2 (NCT05032157, 450 enrolled): identically designed, randomized 2:1, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 24-week controlled period plus 28-week open-label extension.

- Sample size (SAP, verbatim): target 300 active : 150 placebo (450 total) per trial "to fulfill registration and ICH E1 requirements on the number of participants treated for 6 months and 12 months"; power >99% individually for UAS7/ISS7/HSS7 (one-sided α=0.025) and >90% family-wise power for the co-primary union test (conservatively assuming zero correlation between ISS7 and HSS7).

- Primary results at Week 12 (label Table 3, LS-mean differences vs. placebo): ISS7 — REMIX-1 −2.63 (95% CI −3.70, −1.56), REMIX-2 −3.23 (−4.29, −2.16). HSS7 — REMIX-1 −3.61 (−4.85, −2.36), REMIX-2 −4.47 (−5.71, −3.23). UAS7 (key secondary) — REMIX-1 −6.22 (−8.45, −4.00), REMIX-2 −7.68 (−9.91, −5.46).

- No formal interim-analysis alpha adjustment was required: per the SAP, "Formal testing of the primary endpoint and key secondary endpoints will only be performed at the primary analysis time point; thus, no adjustment for multiplicity is required" for that single analysis.

- No FDA Statistical Review, Multi-Discipline Review, Medical Review, Summary Review, or Clinical Pharmacology Review has been posted for NDA 218436 as of this research

If significant, the second hypothesis is tested with full-level alpha; otherwise, the testing procedure stops. The testing is strictly hierarchical... ### 51. Difamilast (Adquey) — NDA 219474

**Sponsor:** Acrotech Biopharma Inc.

**Indication approved:** Topical treatment of adults and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older with mild to moderate atopic dermatitis.

**Approval date:** February 12, 2026 (NDA received February 13, 2025) — confirmed directly via FDA's Drugs@FDA overview page and approval letter, as this approval postdates general knowledge cutoffs and was independently verified rather than assumed.

**Pivotal trial:** Trial 271-102-00007 (NCT03908970, adult/adolescent, Japan) and Trial 271-102-00008 (NCT03911401, pediatric ages 2–14, Japan) — both conducted in Japan, not the United States; a US-based trial, MEDI-MM36-301, was terminated early "for business reasons" after enrolling 153 of 336 planned subjects and was explicitly excluded from the efficacy analysis.

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Approval based on foreign (Japanese) pivotal Phase 3 trials with a concurrently-run, terminated, and excluded US trial (a hybrid approval strategy relying on non-US pivotal data plus an explicit generalizability/bridging argument, where a domestic trial exists but was terminated and excluded from the efficacy claim rather than analyzed, is distinct from a straightforward foreign-data bridging study or a standard multi-region trial); both Japanese pivotal trials were randomized, triple-masked, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group

- *Endpoints:* Primary endpoint — Investigator's Global Assessment (IGA) responder rate at Week 4; secondary endpoints included Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) change and a pruritus visual rating scale (VRS)

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test, stratified by baseline IGA (both trials) and additionally by age group (2–6 vs. 7–14 years) in the pediatric trial

- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) testing of the 1% then 0.3% dose vs. vehicle in the pediatric trial (271-102-00008) to control Type I error for the primary endpoint only; the adult trial (271-102-00007) specified no multiplicity control beyond the single primary endpoint

- *Missing data/bias:* Non-responder imputation (NRI) for the primary IGA responder endpoint in both pivotal trials; no ICH E9(R1) estimand framework was specified in either pivotal trial's protocol (both pre-date that guidance's adoption), though the terminated US trial (MEDI-MM36-301) had specified an estimand framework in its own protocol before its SAP dropped all efficacy analysis following termination

- *Regulatory:* FDA's Multi-Discipline Review explicitly documents the terminated US trial's negative result (11.7% vs. 11.9% responder rate, p=0.702) and the Applicant's declination to provide an efficacy analysis of it, alongside FDA's acceptance of a generalizability argument for the Japanese data based on comparable AD prevalence/epidemiology between Japan and the US; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Trial 271-102-00007 (NCT03908970): 364 randomized, ages 15–70, Japan. Trial 271-102-00008 (NCT03911401): 251 randomized (168 in the primary two-arm comparison: 85 difamilast 1% / 83 vehicle; a third 0.3%-dose arm was also enrolled but is not part of the primary efficacy comparison, an enrollment/reporting discrepancy not further reconciled here), ages 2–14, Japan. A supportive Phase 2 trial (NCT02068352, ages 10–70, US/Australia/Poland, n=121) was also submitted but is smaller and not one of the two cited pivotal trials.

- MEDI-MM36-301 (US trial, NCT number not identified in any source checked despite multiple searches): terminated early for business reasons after enrolling 153 of a planned 336 subjects; per the FDA Multi-Discipline Review, the SAP was revised after termination to state that "all efficacy analyses defined in the protocol, including statistical testing, sub-group analyses, and per protocol population analysis will not be performed," with only descriptive listings provided.

- Primary results (FDA Multi-Discipline Review, verbatim): Trial 271-102-00007 — IGA success 70/182 (38.5%) difamilast vs. 23/182 (12.6%) vehicle, difference 25.9 (95% CI 17.5–34.4), p<0.001. Trial 271-102-00008 — 40/85 (47.1%) vs. 15/83 (18.1%), difference 28.7 (95% CI 15.0–42.5), p<0.001.

- Generalizability/bridging rationale (FDA Multi-Discipline Review, verbatim): "The efficacy results from the trials conducted in Japan are generalizable to the US population because the prevalence (~10%) and epidemiological characteristics of AD are comparable between the two populations, and the distribution of AD severities are similar despite some differences in clinical presentation and genetic variability."

### 52. Icotrokinra (Icotyde) — NDA 220149

**Sponsor:** Janssen Biotech, Inc. (Johnson & Johnson)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in adults and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older who weigh at least 40 kg and who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy

**Approval date:** March 17, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** Four Phase 3 trials formed the efficacy basis: ICONIC-LEAD (Protocol 77242113PSO3001, NCT06095115), ICONIC-ADVANCE 1 (Protocol 77242113PSO3002, NCT06143878), ICONIC-ADVANCE 2 (Protocol 77242113PSO3004, NCT06220604), and ICONIC-TOTAL (Protocol 77242113PSO3003, NCT06095102)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (ICONIC-LEAD, ICONIC-TOTAL); randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-comparator-controlled versus deucravacitinib (ICONIC-ADVANCE 1, ICONIC-ADVANCE 2); approval basis built from four independently protocoled, differently-enrolled Phase 3 trials analyzed and reported as a single coordinated evidentiary package rather than pooled into one dataset (closest existing taxonomy analogue is "Cross-trial pooled/integrated analysis," but here each trial retains its own separate primary analysis rather than being statistically pooled: a "multi-trial coordinated-SAP approval basis, each trial independently analyzed"); embedded randomized-withdrawal-and-retreatment sub-design within ICONIC-LEAD from Week 24 through Week 52, with retreatment triggered by a pre-specified ≥50% loss of Week-24 PASI improvement (not the same construct as "Early-stopped for efficacy"); novel mechanistic class — icotrokinra is an oral 13-amino-acid peptide IL-23 receptor antagonist, the first oral therapy in the IL-23 inhibitor class (prior approved IL-23 inhibitors — guselkumab, risankizumab, tildrakizumab, and the related IL-12/23 inhibitor ustekinumab — are all injectable monoclonal antibodies)

- *Endpoints:* co-primary endpoints of IGA 0/1 response (IGA score of clear/0 or almost-clear/1 with ≥2-grade improvement from baseline) and PASI-90 response, both at Week 16, in three of the four trials (ICONIC-LEAD, ICONIC-ADVANCE 1, ICONIC-ADVANCE 2); single primary endpoint of IGA 0/1 response at Week 16 in the fourth trial (ICONIC-TOTAL), which enrolled a population defined by special-area (scalp/genital/palmoplantar) involvement for which PASI-90 was not a fit-for-purpose measure; extensive multiplicity-controlled secondary endpoint families built on PASI-75/100, scalp-specific IGA (ss-IGA), the Psoriasis Symptom and Sign Diary (PSSD symptom score and itch-item score), and (ICONIC-TOTAL only) genital- and hand/foot-specific instruments (sPGA-G, hf-PGA, GPSS, GenPs-SFQ)

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) chi-square test, two-sided α=0.05, stratified by randomization factors (age group, adult baseline weight category, and geographic region for ICONIC-LEAD; baseline weight category and geographic region for ICONIC-ADVANCE 1/2; special-area-involvement category, geographic region, and BSA category for ICONIC-TOTAL); risk difference and 95% CI via the Mantel-Haenszel-weighted Miettinen-Nurminen method

- *Multiplicity:* estimand framework (ICH E9(R1)-style) specifying a composite-variable intercurrent-event (ICE) strategy for treatment discontinuation due to lack of efficacy/worsening psoriasis and for rescue-therapy initiation (treated as non-response), and a treatment-policy strategy for discontinuation for other reasons (no existing taxonomy entry captures a formally specified multi-ICE estimand with mixed composite-variable/treatment-policy strategies per ICE); tiered/serial gatekeeping combining a truncated Bonferroni-Holm procedure within each tier with graphical alpha-propagation across tiers (ICONIC-LEAD: 4 tiers; ICONIC-TOTAL: 2 tiers with one-third alpha propagation; ICONIC-ADVANCE 1/2: 11 tiers incorporating pre-specified noninferiority-then-superiority sub-tests against deucravacitinib with a 12% margin) (the taxonomy's existing "Bonferroni-Holm sequentially rejective procedure" and gatekeeping entries do not capture this specific truncated-Holm-within-tier-plus-graphical-propagation-across-tiers structure)

- *Missing data/bias:* fully conditional specification (FCS) multiple-imputation logistic regression for missing binary responder endpoints, combined via Wilson-Hilferty-transformed test statistics in SAS PROC MIANALYZE and Rubin's rule; tipping-point analysis (multiple imputation) with 200 Bernoulli-draw imputed datasets per assumed response-rate scenario (0-100% by 10% increments), seed=20240719 (existing taxonomy term, "Tipping-point analysis (multiple imputation)," applies directly); post hoc sensitivity analysis excluding one ICONIC-ADVANCE 2 site (n=8) after a mid-conduct Good Clinical Practice (GCP) noncompliance finding, with no material change to conclusions

- *Regulatory:* Priority Review; New Molecular Entity; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held ("our review did not raise issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion"); Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA) deferral for ages 4 to <12 and waiver for ages 0-4; postmarketing requirements for a pregnancy registry and a lactation study

**Trial design & endpoints**

- All four pivotal trials were randomized, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group Phase 3 studies of oral icotrokinra 200 mg once daily; ICONIC-ADVANCE 1 and ICONIC-ADVANCE 2 additionally included deucravacitinib 6 mg once daily as an active comparator (with placebo dosing maintained in the deucravacitinib arm through Week 24 to preserve blinding). ICONIC-LEAD (n=684, randomized 2:1 icotrokinra:placebo) enrolled adults and adolescents (≥12 years) with total BSA ≥10%, PASI ≥12, and IGA ≥3, and added a randomized-withdrawal/retreatment period from Week 24-52 (icotrokinra responders re-randomized to continued treatment or withdrawal, with retreatment triggered by ≥50% loss of Week-24 PASI improvement) followed by an open-label extension to Week 156. ICONIC-ADVANCE 1 (n=774, randomized 2:1:2 icotrokinra:placebo:deucravacitinib) and ICONIC-ADVANCE 2 (n=731, randomized 4:1:4) enrolled adults only (≥18 years) with the same disease-severity thresholds, ran a 16-week placebo-controlled period concurrently with a 24-week active-comparator-controlled period, and switched placebo subjects to icotrokinra at Week 16 and deucravacitinib subjects at Week 24. ICONIC-TOTAL (n=311, randomized 2:1) enrolled subjects ≥12 years with plaque psoriasis involving special areas (scalp, genitalia, and/or hands/feet), with lower BSA (≥1%) and IGA (≥2) thresholds but a requirement for at least one qualifying special-area severity score (ss-IGA, sPGA-G, or hf-PGA ≥3), capping the <10% BSA subpopulation at 40% of enrollment.

- Co-primary endpoints (ICONIC-LEAD, ICONIC-ADVANCE 1, ICONIC-ADVANCE 2): IGA 0/1 response and PASI-90 response, both at Week 16. Single primary endpoint (ICONIC-TOTAL): IGA (overall) 0/1 response at Week 16. Each estimand's intercurrent-event strategy classified treatment discontinuation for lack of efficacy/AE-driven worsening and initiation of alternative psoriasis therapy as composite-variable non-response, and discontinuation for other reasons under a treatment-policy strategy (data used as observed).

- Multiplicity-controlled secondary endpoints spanned PASI-75/90/100 at multiple timepoints (Weeks 4, 8, 16, and — for ICONIC-ADVANCE 1/2 versus deucravacitinib — Week 24), IGA 0 response, ss-IGA response, and PSSD symptom/itch responses; ICONIC-TOTAL's secondary family additionally covered sPGA-G, hf-PGA, GenPs-SFQ, GPSS Genital Itch NRS, and Scalp Itch NRS. ICONIC-LEAD's Week 52 key secondary endpoints (PASI-75/90 maintenance and time-to-loss-of-response among Week-24 responders) used a distinct estimand incorporating a fourth ICE (loss of ≥50% Week-24 PASI improvement).

- Sample-size targets: approximately 600 (ICONIC-LEAD), 750 (ICONIC-ADVANCE 1), 675 (ICONIC-ADVANCE 2), and 300 (ICONIC-TOTAL) randomized subjects; actual enrollment was 684, 774, 731, and 311 respectively.

- Primary analysis method: two-sided (α=0.05) CMH chi-square test stratified by each trial's randomization factors; risk differences and 95% CIs via the Mantel-Haenszel-weighted Miettinen-Nurminen method. Multiplicity across coprimary/primary and multiplicity-controlled secondary endpoints was gated first on both/the coprimary endpoint(s) reaching significance, then propagated across secondary-endpoint tiers via a combination of truncated Bonferroni-Holm (within tier) and graphical Type I error propagation (across tiers); ICONIC-ADVANCE 1/2 additionally embedded 12%-margin noninferiority tests against deucravacitinib ahead of superiority tests within specific tiers. Missing binary-endpoint data at Week 16 were handled via a pre-specified FCS multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis and a Bernoulli-draw tipping-point analysis; both were reported by FDA's Statistical Reviewer as robust to worst-case assumptions (p<0.001 for both coprimary endpoints in all four trials even under the extreme tipping-point scenario).

- Results: in all four trials, icotrokinra was statistically superior to placebo on every coprimary/primary endpoint at Week 16 (p<0.0001). IGA 0/1 response was 64.7% vs. 8.3% (ICONIC-LEAD), 68.5% vs. 10.9% (ICONIC-ADVANCE 1), 56.7% vs. 5.8% (ICONIC-TOTAL), and 70.5% vs. 8.5% (ICONIC-ADVANCE 2), icotrokinra vs. placebo; PASI-90 response was 49.6% vs. 4.4%, 55.0% vs. 3.8%, not applicable, and 57.1% vs. 1.2%, respectively. Icotrokinra was also statistically superior to deucravacitinib on both coprimary endpoints in ICONIC-ADVANCE 1 and ICONIC-ADVANCE 2. A mid-review GCP-noncompliance finding at one ICONIC-ADVANCE 2 site (n=8) did not materially change conclusions when those subjects were excluded.
