### 53. Brepocitinib (Lisraya) — NDA 220106

**IMPORTANT NOTE ON APPLICATION NUMBER:** the census's master tracking index lists brepocitinib's NDA as "pending, not in bulk data yet." This has now been confirmed as **NDA 220106**, via FDA's openFDA `drugsfda` API (query: `openfda.brand_name:"Lisraya"` and, independently, `openfda.substance_name:"BREPOCITINIB"`), cross-checked against the live FDA Approval Letter and Package Insert links below, both of which resolve under the `220106` application number. The master index should be corrected accordingly.

**Sponsor:** Priovant Therapeutics, Inc. (a Roivant Sciences company)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of dermatomyositis in adults

**Approval date:** August 27, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** VALOR (Protocol PVT-2201-301), NCT05437263 — Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of oral brepocitinib in adults with dermatomyositis

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, three-arm dose-comparison trial (two active dose levels of the same drug versus a shared placebo arm — distinct from the taxonomy's existing "Randomized non-comparative dose-regimen cohort design," which describes randomization across regimens of the same drug without a placebo arm); 52-week double-blind primary treatment period with background standard-of-care therapy (corticosteroids, hydroxychloroquine, and/or a non-steroid immunosuppressant) continued at stable dose and glucocorticoids tapered per protocol, followed by an optional 52-week open-label extension; ultra-rare autoimmune disease population (dermatomyositis prevalence on the order of 1 in 20,000-25,000); first-in-class oral TYK2/JAK1 inhibitor mechanism in this indication

- *Endpoints:* Total Improvement Score (TIS) at Week 52 as primary endpoint — a validated composite myositis-activity index (International Myositis Assessment and Clinical Studies Group/ACR-EULAR-endorsed) combining six core-set measures (Physician Global Assessment, Patient Global Assessment, Manual Muscle Testing of 8 muscles, Extramuscular Global Assessment, HAQ-Disability Index, and a composite muscle-enzyme measure) into a single continuous 0-100 improvement score (no existing taxonomy entry for this composite myositis-specific continuous index); nine multiplicity-controlled key secondary endpoints spanning cutaneous disease activity (CDASI Activity Score), a dermatomyositis-specific patient/physician combined outcome (DMOMS), corticosteroid-tapering responder endpoints, and physical function (HAQ-DI)

- *Primary analysis:* analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) model for the continuous TIS primary endpoint, adjusted for stratification factors, per the approved label's table footnote; Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) method for binary TIS-threshold responder-rate differences (TIS≥20/40/60), also adjusted for stratification factors

- *Multiplicity:* label and pivotal-publication abstract state that "key secondary end points ... were tested in a multiplicity-controlled sequence," with brepocitinib 30 mg reported superior to placebo on all nine; the specific hierarchical/gatekeeping structure and exact stratification factors are not disclosed in either the label or the publicly available abstract (no FDA Statistical Review is yet posted — see Documents below), so the precise multiplicity procedure cannot currently be verified beyond this description

- *Missing data/bias:* not independently confirmed — no FDA Statistical Review is yet public (see below); the label does not describe an estimand/intercurrent-event framework or a missing-data sensitivity analysis, though one was very likely pre-specified given contemporaneous (2020s) FDA practice for continuous composite endpoints in immunology trials with a 52-week primary timepoint and background-therapy tapering

- *Regulatory:* Priority Review; Orphan Drug designation; New Molecular Entity; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held ("your application for Lisraya was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because our review did not raise issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- VALOR (PVT-2201-301) was a Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind (triple-masked per ClinicalTrials.gov: participant, investigator, and outcomes assessor), placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial in adults (18-75 years) with dermatomyositis per 2017 EULAR/ACR classification criteria, with active muscle and skin disease at screening/baseline and prior or current therapy with corticosteroids, hydroxychloroquine, and/or a non-steroid immunosuppressant. Key exclusions included end-stage or irreversible organ/muscle involvement, cancer-associated dermatomyositis, active malignancy or cancer within 5 years, overlap connective-tissue disease (other than Sjögren's), and elevated thrombosis/cardiovascular or herpes zoster reactivation risk.

- 241 patients were randomized 1:1:1 to brepocitinib 30 mg once daily (n=81), brepocitinib 15 mg once daily (n=81, an unapproved dose — see Results), or placebo (n=79) for a 52-week double-blind treatment period, with background dermatomyositis therapies continued at stable dose and an option to continue into a 52-week open-label extension (all participants receiving brepocitinib) thereafter.

- Primary endpoint: mean Total Improvement Score (TIS) at Week 52, a composite index (range 0-100, higher = more improvement) built from six core-set measures (Physician Global Assessment, Patient Global Assessment, Manual Muscle Testing of 8 muscles, Extramuscular Global Assessment, HAQ-Disability Index, and the most abnormal of five muscle enzymes: aldolase, creatine kinase, ALT, AST, and LDH).

- Nine key secondary endpoints (per ClinicalTrials.gov and the NEJM publication) were tested in a multiplicity-controlled sequence: change from baseline in CDASI Activity Score at Week 52 and at Week 4; Dermatomyositis Outcomes for Muscle and Skin (DMOMS) at Week 52; proportion achieving TIS≥40 (moderate improvement) at Week 52 (overall, and specifically with minimal-to-no corticosteroid use); time to sustained (≥2 consecutive visits) TIS≥40 by Week 52; proportion achieving ≥40% improvement with a ≥4-point improvement in CDASI Activity Score; proportion achieving TIS≥60 (major improvement); and change from baseline in HAQ-DI.

- Results: at Week 52, mean TIS was 47.5 (brepocitinib 30 mg), 37.5 (brepocitinib 15 mg), and 31.2 (placebo); the difference for 30 mg vs. placebo was 15.3 (95% CI 6.7-24.0 per the NEJM publication; 14.2, 95% CI 5.5-22.9 per the approved label's LS-mean ANCOVA estimate — the two point estimates and CIs differ slightly, consistent with differing analysis populations/models between the publication and the final label text, and both are reported here rather than reconciled), p<0.001; the 15 mg vs. placebo difference (6.3, 95% CI -2.4 to 14.9) was not statistically significant. Brepocitinib 30 mg was superior to placebo on all nine key secondary endpoints, including corticosteroid-tapering measures (55% vs. 30% achieving TIS≥40 with ≤2.5 mg/day prednisone-equivalent at Week 52) and TIS≥60 major improvement (48% vs. 26%). Only the 30 mg dose was approved; the label explicitly identifies 15 mg as "unapproved dosage."

- Safety: serious infections were more frequent with brepocitinib 30 mg than placebo (10% vs. 1%); no deaths occurred during the double-blind period. The approved label carries a boxed-warning-adjacent JAK-inhibitor class safety framework (serious infection, malignancy, major adverse cardiovascular events, and thrombosis risks), referencing the postmarketing safety experience of other JAK inhibitors in rheumatoid arthritis as contextual class information rather than trial-specific data.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA-approved Package Insert (Lisraya label), Section 14 "Clinical Studies," p.10-11 of the labeling PDF]* — "The efficacy of LISRAYA in the treatment of dermatomyositis in adults was assessed in a Phase 3 randomized, double-blind, multicenter, placebo-controlled trial in 241 adult patients with dermatomyositis (Trial DM; NCT05437263). Patients were randomized 1:1:1 to receive oral LISRAYA 30 mg once daily, brepocitinib 15 mg once daily (unapproved dosage), or placebo once daily for a 52-week double-blind treatment period... In Trial DM, the primary endpoint was the mean Total Improvement Score (TIS) at Week 52."

*[verbatim, same label, Table 3 footnote, "TIS and TIS Responder Rates (% of Patients) at Week 52"]* — "LS mean TIS, difference and 95% CI based on an analysis of covariance model adjusted for stratification factors. Response rate (risk) differences calculated using the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel method adjusted for stratification factors."

*[verbatim, same label, Table 4 footnote, "Mean Change from Baseline in Core Set Measures"]* — "LS means, difference and 95% CI based on an analysis of covariance model adjusting for stratification factors."

*[verbatim, PubMed abstract of the pivotal publication, Methods and Results]* — "In this phase 3, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial, adults with dermatomyositis were assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive once-daily oral brepocitinib at a dose of 30 mg, brepocitinib at a dose of 15 mg, or placebo for 52 weeks... Key secondary end points, including skin disease activity, glucocorticoid tapering, and physical function, were tested in a multiplicity-controlled sequence... Brepocitinib 30 mg was superior to placebo across all nine key secondary end points, including skin disease activity, systemic glucocorticoid tapering, and functional disability, with improvements observed as early as week 4."

**Reverse-engineered SAP** (no FDA Statistical Review, sponsor protocol, or SAP is yet public for VALOR; the following extend beyond what the label and journal abstract state verbatim, and are traced to the specific reported results below — all marked [inferred])

- *[inferred]* The unnamed "stratification factors" referenced identically in both the label's TIS-responder-rate footnote (Table 3, CMH method) and its core-set-measure footnote (Table 4, ANCOVA) were almost certainly applied consistently across both the primary continuous ANCOVA model and the secondary CMH-based responder analyses, given that both footnotes use near-identical wording ("adjusted for stratification factors" / "adjusting for stratification factors") — but the specific factors (candidates given the trial's design would plausibly include baseline oral corticosteroid dose category, given the prominence of corticosteroid-tapering as a headline secondary endpoint, and/or geographic region, consistent with the stratification approach used contemporaneously in icotrokinra's ICONIC program) are not stated in either the label or the publicly available journal abstract, and are not otherwise confirmed.

- *[inferred]* Given that the NEJM abstract reports brepocitinib 30 mg succeeded on the primary endpoint (p<0.001) and "across all nine key secondary end points," while the 15 mg dose was not significant on the primary endpoint (95% CI for the difference crossing zero, -2.4 to 14.9), the multiplicity-controlled testing sequence for secondary endpoints was most likely gated on (or at minimum reported separately for) the 30 mg-vs-placebo comparison passing its own primary test, rather than requiring both doses to pass before any secondary testing proceeded — consistent with the label listing 15 mg as an "unapproved dosage" whose secondary-endpoint results are not reported in the approved labeling at all.

- *[inferred]* The 52-week primary timepoint combined with permitted continuation of background corticosteroid/immunosuppressive therapy at a stable dose (per the label and ClinicalTrials.gov eligibility criteria) implies the SAP very likely pre-specified handling of intercurrent events such as rescue-therapy initiation or premature discontinuation via an estimand framework analogous to the composite-variable/treatment-policy structure documented contemporaneously for other 2020s-era immunology registration trials with similarly long primary timepoints (e.g., icotrokinra's ICONIC program, this same census entry above) — but no such framework is named or described in any currently public document for VALOR, so this remains an inference rather than a confirmed fact.

## Other / Misc

### 1. Spinosad (Natroba) — NDA 22408

**Sponsor:** ParaPRO, LLC

**Indication approved:** Topical treatment of head lice infestation (pediculosis capitis) in patients four (4) years of age and older

**Approval date:** January 18, 2011

**Pivotal trial:** SPN-301-07 (NCT00545753) and SPN-302-07 (NCT00545168), two identically protocoled Phase 3 trials; supportive Phase 2 dose-ranging trial SPN-202-06 (NCT00311779)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, evaluator/investigator-blinded (intended double-blind, but compromised by product-identifiable packaging — see Missing data/bias), active-controlled, three-arm household/cluster-unit randomization stratified by study site, allocation ratio 4:4:1 (NatrOVA without nit combing : NIX with nit combing : NatrOVA with nit combing) (household/cluster-unit randomization with a designated "primary subject" per household); supportive Phase 2 dose-ranging, vehicle(placebo)-controlled trial (SPN-202-06) used only to assess the topical vehicle's own contribution to efficacy, not as a pivotal study in its own right

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint the proportion of "primary" (youngest per-household) subjects who were lice-free 14 days after their last treatment application; secondary endpoint the corresponding Day-7 lice-free rate; SPN-202-06's endpoint was the proportion of subjects free of live lice and viable nits at Day 7 and Day 14 after a single treatment application

- *Primary analysis:* protocol-specified logistic regression (terms for treatment, study site, and treatment-by-site interaction) on transformed log-odds estimates back-transformed to success-rate point estimates and CIs; FDA's statistical reviewer additionally re-analyzed the Phase 3 data using a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by site, given a concern that the logistic model's multiplicative-effect assumption might not hold; SPN-202-06 used a protocol-specified chi-square test on the per-protocol population

- *Missing data/bias:* last-observation-carried-forward (LOCF) imputation for missing final evaluations, with three sponsor-conducted sensitivity analyses; FDA's reviewer flagged an unresolved risk to blinding integrity because nit combs were supplied only with two of the three arms and the product's trade name was printed on the take-home packaging, addressed only by the applicant's own post hoc unblinding-impact analyses (inter-study comparisons, misuse-of-combs review) rather than an independent corrective method; FDA's reviewer separately flagged, as an unresolved issue at the time of the cited statistical review, that some physical households had been enrolled more than once (upon re-infestation) or split into more than one "household" unit for randomization purposes, violating the independence assumption underlying the primary analysis, without the submission providing the number of affected households or a household-deduplicated sensitivity analysis

- *Regulatory:* while spinosad's NDA was under review, FDA approved a different head-lice product (Ulesfia, benzyl alcohol 5%) whose active ingredient is also a vehicle component of the spinosad formulation, raising a contribution-of-components question; because neither Phase 3 trial included a benzyl-alcohol-alone arm, FDA's Biostatistics Team Leader instead constructed a post hoc, non-randomized, cross-trial "upper bound" estimate of benzyl alcohol's plausible response rate by pooling the two Phase 2 trials' vehicle arms and comparing it against the Phase 3 spinosad response rate, explicitly disclaimed by the reviewer as a sensitivity exercise rather than a formal inferential comparison of components (distinct from the existing "Contribution-of-components trial-part addition" entry, which describes a randomized trial-part addition rather than a post hoc cross-trial numerical exercise)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- SPN-301-07 and SPN-302-07 shared a common protocol titled "A comparative safety and efficacy study between NatrOVA Crème Rinse ... in subjects ≥ 6 months of age with Pediculosis capitis," both active-controlled and evaluator/investigator-blinded, conducted at six non-overlapping US sites each; eligible households contained at least one healthy subject ≥6 months old with ≥3 live lice at screening, with the youngest qualifying member of each household designated the "primary subject" for the primary efficacy analysis

- Households were randomized 4:4:1 (stratified by study site) to NatrOVA without nit combing, NIX (permethrin) with nit combing, or NatrOVA with nit combing (the third arm included only to help preserve blinding and provide a general comparison); treatment was applied at randomization and, for subjects with live lice at Day 7, again at Day 7, with lice-free subjects evaluated again at Day 14 (and, if retreated, Day 21)

- Primary endpoint: proportion of primary subjects lice-free 14 days after their last treatment application; SPN-301-07 randomized 203 households (558 subjects: 91 NatrOVA-without-combing, 89 NIX, 23 NatrOVA-with-combing primary subjects) and SPN-302-07 randomized 188 households (480 subjects: 83, 84, and 21 respectively per arm), with completion rates of 91.6% and 91.3%

- Sample size was based on 76 primary subjects per arm (NatrOVA-without-combing and NIX) providing 80% power to detect a 21-percentage-point difference at two-sided alpha=0.05, assuming an 86% success rate in the NatrOVA-without-combing arm; an additional 19 subjects were planned for the smaller NatrOVA-with-combing arm to complete the 4:4:1 ratio; sample size was calculated via a continuity-corrected chi-square test, but the protocol specified logistic regression as the primary analysis method

- Results: approximately 85% of NatrOVA-without-combing subjects were lice-free at Day 14 versus approximately 45% of NIX subjects in both trials (treatment difference 40 percentage points, 95% CI 27-52%, in SPN-301-07; 44 percentage points, 95% CI 32-56%, in SPN-302-07; p<0.001 by both the sponsor's logistic-regression analysis and FDA's independent site-stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel re-analysis in each trial); results were reported as consistent across study sites

- SPN-202-06 (Phase 2, n=122: spinosad 0.5% n=40, spinosad 1.0% n=39, vehicle/benzyl-alcohol n=43) found spinosad 1.0% statistically significantly superior to vehicle at Day 14 (p<0.001); FDA's statistical reviewer used this trial, together with the smaller SPN-201-05 dose-ranging study, to construct the post hoc benzyl-alcohol "upper bound" sensitivity analysis described above, concluding that spinosad appeared to retain a meaningful treatment effect even against a generously estimated upper-bound vehicle response rate, while explicitly cautioning that the exercise rested on unverifiable cross-study assumptions and was not a substitute for an adequate, well-controlled component trial

**Documents**

- Package Insert / Label (original, 2011) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2011/022408lbl.pdf

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2008-3762), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19706558/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Efficacy%20and%20safety%20of%20spinosad%20and%20permethrin%20creme%20rinses%20for%20pediculosis%20capitis)

**Other resources**

- No Vivli/YODA Project/Project Data Sphere participation specific to ParaPRO or these trials was identified; not confirmed either way.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review and Evaluation, NDA 22-408, Section 1.3 "Statistical Issues and Findings"]* — "The primary statistical issues are the lack of blinding on the part of study participants who were enrolled in the Phase 3 studies and the potential for them to reveal treatment-related information to study site personnel, the contribution of spinosad to the efficacy of [the product] and households being enrolled multiple times."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review and Evaluation, NDA 22-408, Section 1.3]* — "Responses from households that are enrolled more than once or from households that are enrolled as more than one household are correlated and, therefore, cannot be assumed to be independent. Independence of observations is a key assumption of the analyses of the primary endpoint. The applicant needs to provide further information on the households that were enrolled more than once or as more than one household."

*[verbatim, Biostatistics Team Leader Memorandum, NDA 22-408, Section III "Conclusion"]* — "Please note that this exercise should be viewed as sensitivity analysis to find out whether we might still have a certain treatment effect for Spinosad beyond what could potentially be considered an upper limit for the efficacy of benzyl alcohol ... Any conclusions from this hypothetical exploration depend on unverifiable assumptions and extrapolation of observed point estimates ... The goal here is not to get a reliable estimate for Benzyl alcohol to use for inferential decision-making or to establish the added efficacy of the Spinosad product – for this, we would need the usual adequate and well-controlled trials that are designed to provide direct comparisons of the Spinosad to its vehicle."

### 2. Gadobutrol (Gadavist) — NDA 201277

**Sponsor:** Bayer HealthCare Pharmaceuticals Inc.

**Indication approved:** Intravenous gadolinium-based contrast agent for diagnostic MRI in adults and children (2 years of age and older) to detect and visualize areas with disrupted blood-brain barrier and/or abnormal vascularity of the central nervous system (CNS)

**Approval date:** March 14, 2011

**Pivotal trial:** Study 310123 (NCT00709852) and Study 310124 (no registered NCT identified), two Phase 3 within-patient paired-comparison diagnostic-accuracy trials

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison) (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1) — every subject imaged both Unenhanced and with Gadovist-Enhanced MRI ("Paired" read), read independently by three blinded expert-radiologist readers, with a fourth read type by two additional blinded readers (plus adjudicator) confined to Paired reads only; Study 310123 was multicenter, randomized (order of Gadovist vs. active-comparator ProHance/gadoteridol dosing sequence), double-blind, with a secondary active-comparator arm (paired ProHance reads) at FDA's request; Study 310124 was multicenter and open-label with no active comparator; final diagnosis in both studies established by independent, region-specific two-physician Truth/Standard-of-Reference committees using all non-imaging clinical information, blinded to the study's own image reads

- *Endpoints:* four co-primary endpoints — three subjective visualization endpoints (Degree of Contrast Enhancement, Border Delineation, Internal Morphology), each scored per-lesion/per-structure by each reader on a graded scale, averaged within reader and then across readers into a single reader-averaged score per endpoint; and a fourth endpoint, total number of detected lesions (also reader-averaged); secondary diagnostic endpoints (sensitivity/specificity/accuracy for presence/absence of abnormal tissue, malignant-lesion detection, and exact subject-level diagnosis) assessed against the independent Truth-committee reference standard, required only for the secondary (not primary) analyses

- *Primary analysis:* paired t-test on reader-averaged visualization scores, Paired-read minus Unenhanced-read, with the null (Paired ≤ Unenhanced) rejected if the lower bound of the two-sided 95% CI for the difference exceeded zero, for all three visualization endpoints simultaneously (superiority); paired t-test for non-inferiority in reader-averaged lesion-detection counts (Paired minus Unenhanced), null rejected if the lower bound of the two-sided 95% CI exceeded a pre-specified fixed margin of -0.35 (related to but distinct from the existing "Diagnostic-accuracy study" design entry, which does not specify an analysis method)

- *Missing data/bias:* FDA's reviewer noted the visualization endpoints were "somewhat soft" — subjective reader scores, smoothed first within reader across structures/lesions and then averaged again across readers before testing — but noted this approach had been accepted in prior CNS gadolinium-agent submissions; a secondary comparison of Gadovist-paired to ProHance-paired reads was added at FDA's request specifically to benchmark Gadovist's performance against an already-approved agent rather than relying solely on the Unenhanced comparison

- *Regulatory:* joint Advisory Committee meeting convened January 21, 2011 (committee name not independently confirmed in the documents reviewed for this entry, but FDA's practice for gadolinium-based contrast agent submissions in this era was to convene a joint session of the Medical Imaging Drugs Advisory Committee and the Drug Safety and Risk Management Advisory Committee — not confirmed specifically for this meeting), held largely to evaluate nephrogenic systemic fibrosis (NSF) risk; the committee concluded a boxed NSF warning specific to Gadovist was not warranted at that time, notwithstanding the drug-class boxed warning already required for gadolinium agents generally

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 310123 ("A multicenter, randomized, double-blind, Phase III Study to determine the Safety and Efficacy of Gadobutrol 1.0 molar (Gadovist) in patients referred for Contrast-Enhanced MRI of the Central Nervous System") enrolled 419 subjects (June 2008-April 2009) at 51 centers (US, Germany, Japan, other); 380 completed dosing/imaging, with a Full Analysis Set of 336 and Per-Protocol Set of 316; subjects underwent Unenhanced MRI followed by Contrast-Enhanced MRI in two sessions, with the order of Gadovist vs. ProHance randomized

- Study 310124 (open-label, no active comparator) enrolled 347 subjects (December 2009) at 22 centers (US, South America, China, South Korea); 336 completed, FAS 321, PPS 314; design and primary endpoints otherwise identical to Study 310123 apart from the absence of an active-comparator arm

- Both studies required subjects to be referred for a contrast-enhanced MRI of the CNS (brain and/or spine) based on symptoms or prior imaging; three independent blinded expert-radiologist readers read all Unenhanced and Paired (Gadovist and, in Study 310123, ProHance) images for both primary and secondary endpoints, with a separate pair of blinded readers (plus adjudicator, as needed) reading only Paired Gadovist and Paired ProHance images for additional secondary comparisons, and unblinded investigator reads recorded separately; final diagnoses ("Truth") were adjudicated by region-specific two-physician committees using all non-imaging clinical/pathological information collected within three months of the study, explicitly excluding the study's own image-read results

- Results (Study 310123, reader-averaged, N≈316 for visualization endpoints): Paired reads exceeded Unenhanced reads for Contrast Enhancement (difference 1.29, 95% CI 1.23-1.35, on a 1-4 scale), Border Delineation (difference 0.60, 95% CI 0.54-0.65, on a 1-4 scale), and Internal Morphology (difference 0.61, 95% CI 0.56-0.66, on a 1-3 scale) — all lower CI bounds above zero, meeting the superiority criterion for all three visualization endpoints; for lesion detection (N=336), the reader-averaged Paired-minus-Unenhanced difference was 0.17 lesions (95% CI -0.44 to 0.78), whose lower bound did not clear the pre-specified -0.35 non-inferiority margin, though FDA's reviewer considered the result (individual-reader differences ranged from -0.44 to 0.56) "close enough to be considered borderline" and not decisive once integrated with Study 310124 and the ProHance-comparator results; secondary Gadovist-vs-ProHance comparisons in Study 310123 were reported as "virtually identical" performances

- FDA's reviewer explicitly flagged that "the rationale for the Non-Inferiority limit [-0.35 lesions] is not completely convincing, but it was accepted by the Agency" — i.e., the fixed non-inferiority margin for the lesion-detection endpoint was not independently re-derived or challenged by the statistical reviewer despite reservations about its basis

- Standard safety analyses revealed no new safety signals; because gadobutrol is a gadolinium-based agent, the review discussed the class-wide risk of nephrogenic systemic fibrosis (NSF) in patients with significant renal impairment, concluding the available evidence did not place Gadovist in the higher-NSF-risk category among approved gadolinium agents at that time

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review and Evaluation, NDA 201277, Section 1 "Executive Summary"]* — "The Sponsor achieved the objective of Superiority in visualization of paired reads of images (Unenhanced plus Gadovist Enhanced MRI) over Unenhanced MRI for all three [visualization endpoints]. The Non-Inferiority objective for the fourth endpoint for numbers of detected lesions for paired reads versus unenhanced reads was achieved in Study310123, and was borderline successful in Study310124. The reviewer considers this borderline success as adequate for non-inferiority in lesion detection."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review and Evaluation, NDA 201277, Section 3.2.1]* — "Null: Mean Paired Score ≤ Mean Unenhanced Score / Alternative: Mean Paired Score > Mean Unenhanced Score / Statistical Test: T-Test for Paired Observations / Decision Criterion: The mean score was calculated as an average smoothed across readers. The Null was rejected if the 2-sided 95% CI for the difference – Paired Score minus Unenhanced Score - had its lower limit above zero."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review and Evaluation, NDA 201277, Section 3.2.1]* — "Null: Mean # Paired Read minus Unenhanced Read Lesion Detections ≤ -.35 / Alternative: Mean # Paired Read minus Unenhanced Read Lesion Detections > -.35 / Statistical Test: T-Test for Paired Observations ... Note: The rationale for the Non-Inferiority limit is not completely convincing, but it was accepted by the Agency."

### 3. Glucarpidase (Voraxaze) — BLA 125327

**Sponsor:** BTG International Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of toxic plasma methotrexate concentrations (>1 micromole per liter) in patients with delayed methotrexate clearance due to impaired renal function; labeled with an explicit limitation of use against off-label routine/planned use to reduce methotrexate exposure

**Approval date:** January 17, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** Study PR001-CLN-rpt006 ("NCI PD study"), a single-arm, open-label, historically-referenced trial with no registered NCT identifier; safety additionally supported by Study PR001-CLN-rpt016 and expanded-access experience

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label trial (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1), historically-referenced (no concurrent randomized or placebo comparator; efficacy interpreted against well-characterized historical methotrexate excretion/clearance curves), conducted under a National Cancer Institute-sponsored IND predating routine ClinicalTrials.gov registration (enrollment 2004-2007); efficacy analysis restricted to a 22-patient per-protocol subset of a larger enrolled population (184 patients in Study 006 with post-treatment safety data submitted for 149), a substantial exclusion from the full enrolled/safety population to reach the efficacy-evaluable set

- *Endpoints:* primary efficacy endpoint a rapid (≤15 minutes), sustained (≥8 days), clinically important reduction (RSCIR) in plasma methotrexate concentration to ≤1 micromole/L in all post-glucarpidase samples, measured by a centralized, validated, sensitive assay specifically designed to exclude ex vivo (post-sampling) methotrexate metabolism as a confound (a prospectively-agreed, single-threshold pharmacodynamic/biomarker responder endpoint used as the primary efficacy measure for an emergency-use enzyme therapy, absent any clinical-outcome primary endpoint)

- *Primary analysis:* descriptive single-arm response-rate analysis (point estimate + 95% CI, no formal hypothesis test against a null) (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §3); supportive pharmacodynamic descriptive analyses of percentage reduction in plasma methotrexate concentration at 15 minutes and through 8 days in the full 22-patient set, reported without formal inferential testing

- *Missing data/bias:* efficacy population limited, by pre-specified eligibility and "documentation of appropriate sample handling," to 22 of the patients enrolled in Study 006 who met all eligibility criteria — a per-protocol restriction rather than an intent-to-treat analysis, explicitly flagged by FDA's Summary Review as a review issue ("Reliance on results obtained in a per-protocol rather than an intent-to-treatment population"); the single-arm design was explicitly noted by FDA as precluding any assessment of glucarpidase's effect on the duration/severity of methotrexate toxicity or on mortality risk from methotrexate toxicity, as distinct from its demonstrated pharmacodynamic effect on plasma methotrexate concentration

- *Regulatory:* application not referred to the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee, per FDA's Summary Review, "because the application did not raise significant public health issues"; no REMS required; post-marketing requirement imposed under the Animal Rule (21 CFR 601.90) to evaluate intrathecal glucarpidase administration for intrathecal methotrexate overdose, an anticipated off-label use for which a human efficacy trial was deemed infeasible given case rarity; prior FDA warning letter (DDMAC, November 14, 2008) to the sponsor's predecessor (Protherics) for promotional claims suggesting routine/planned adjunctive use beyond the eventual approved emergency indication

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Key efficacy/regulatory agreements were reached at a September 8, 2006 pre-BLA meeting: the primary analysis population would be all enrolled patients with impaired methotrexate clearance and methotrexate levels >1 μmol/L prior to glucarpidase treatment; the primary endpoint would be the proportion achieving a durable clinically important reduction (CIR) in plasma methotrexate concentration (pMTX) to ≤1 μmol/L in all post-glucarpidase samples, with a point estimate and 95% CI to be reported (FDA did not reach prospective agreement with the sponsor on the required lower confidence limit); and planned subgroup analyses by baseline methotrexate level, underlying disease (osteosarcoma vs. other), and other justified subgroups

- Study Design: single-arm, open-label, in patients with delayed methotrexate clearance secondary to renal impairment, with diagnosis-specific eligibility criteria (e.g., for osteosarcoma: plasma methotrexate >50 μmol/L at 24h, >5 μmol/L at 48h, or >2 SD above the mean excretion curve at >12h post-methotrexate, plus renal-function criteria; broader thresholds for other diagnoses); treatment was a single 50 Units/kg intravenous dose over 5 minutes, with a second dose at 48 hours for patients with baseline concentrations >100 μmol/L

- Efficacy results: of 22 evaluable patients (receiving 1 dose, n=16, or 2 doses, n=6), 10 (45.5%, 95% CI 26.9-65.3%) achieved the pre-specified RSCIR; however, all 22 patients showed a ≥97% reduction in plasma methotrexate within 15 minutes, and 20 of 22 maintained a >95% reduction from pre-treatment levels for up to 8 days — FDA's Division Director Summary Review concluded these pharmacodynamic results, in the context of well-characterized historical methotrexate clearance curves used as an implicit comparator, were "sufficient to provide a clear assessment of the treatment effect" despite the modest sample size and the binary RSCIR responder rate falling short of the majority of patients

- Safety was evaluated in a pooled 290-patient population across two single-arm trials (Study 006, n=149 with submitted post-treatment safety data of 184 enrolled; Study 016, ongoing at BLA submission, n=141 of 244 enrolled) plus small pharmacokinetic studies in healthy volunteers/renal-impairment patients; 21/290 patients (7%) had glucarpidase-related adverse reactions (most commonly paresthesia, flushing, nausea/vomiting, hypotension, headache, mostly Grade 1-2); 8 deaths within 30 days of exposure were adjudicated as not clearly attributable to glucarpidase; anti-glucarpidase antibodies developed in 16/96 tested patients (17%), not considered clinically important given the single-dose regimen and rapid pharmacodynamic effect

- FDA's review explicitly listed, as issues considered in the approval decision: use of a single-arm trial to establish efficacy and safety; use of a pharmacodynamic (rather than clinical-outcome) endpoint; reliance on a per-protocol rather than intent-to-treat population; the small size of the efficacy (22-patient) and safety databases; and inadequate dose-finding — all resolved in favor of approval given the rarity and life-threatening nature of the target emergency population, which the review concluded made a larger or randomized trial infeasible

- No separate FDA biostatistics Statistical Review document was located on Drugs@FDA for this BLA; per the Division Director Summary Review, the primary endpoint's integral relationship to pharmacokinetic/bioanalytical assay methodology meant "the evaluation of the assay methodology and conduct as well as the statistical analyses of the data were conducted by the clinical pharmacology reviewer" rather than a dedicated biostatistics reviewer — consistent with the very small, single-arm evidentiary basis for this emergency-use indication

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2012/125327s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label (original, 2012) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2012/125327lbl.pdf

- FDA Division Director Summary Review, BLA 125327 (Patricia Keegan, M.D., Director, Division of Oncology Products 2, January 12, 2012) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/125327Orig1s000SumR.pdf

- FDA Medical Review(s) and Clinical Pharmacology/Biopharmaceutics Review(s) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/125327Orig1s000MedR.pdf and https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/125327Orig1s000ClinPharmR.pdf (both PDFs are scanned/image-only in the copies retrieved for this entry; text beyond the title page could not be machine-extracted, so content described above is drawn from the machine-readable Summary Review rather than quoted from these two documents)

- No ClinicalTrials.gov record was identified for Study PR001-CLN-rpt006 (consistent with its 2004-2007 conduct, predating routine trial registration); a related, later NCI protocol (PR001-CLN-rpt002) is registered as NCT00219791, and a leucovorin-interaction PK sub-study is registered as NCT00634504, but neither is the pivotal efficacy trial

- Pivotal publication: Widemann BC, Balis FM, Kim A, Boron M, Jayaprakash N, Shalabi A, O'Brien M, Eby M, Cole DE, Murphy RF, Fox E, Ivy P, Denicola S, Sato J, Adamson PC. "Glucarpidase, leucovorin, and thymidine for high-dose methotrexate-induced renal dysfunction: clinical and pharmacologic factors affecting outcome." *J Clin Oncol.* 2010;28(25):3979-3986. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.2009.25.4540), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20679598/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Glucarpidase%20leucovorin%20and%20thymidine%20for%20high-dose%20methotrexate-induced%20renal%20dysfunction)

**Other resources**

- No Vivli/YODA Project/Project Data Sphere participation specific to BTG International or this program was identified; not confirmed either way. Given the trial's small, decade-old, NCI-sponsored single-arm design, individual-patient-data sharing infrastructure of this kind is unlikely to apply.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held for this BLA (see Regulatory keyword above).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Division Director Summary Review, BLA 125327, Section 1 "Introduction"]* — "The primary efficacy outcome measure was a rapid (≤ 15 minutes), sustained (≥ 8 days), clinically important reduction (RSCIR) in methotrexate concentration as determined by a centralized laboratory using a validated, sensitive assay. Evidence for efficacy was evaluated in 22 patients ... Ten of the 22 patients achieved RSCIR [45.5% (95% CI: 26.9, 65.3%)]. However, all 22 patients showed evidence of pharmacodynamic effects with reduction in the plasma methotrexate concentration of ≥97% within 15 minutes, and there was evidence of >95% reduction from pre-treatment methotrexate levels up to 8 days in 20 of the 22 patients."

*[verbatim, FDA Division Director Summary Review, BLA 125327, "Issues to be considered further in this review"]* — "The use of a single-arm trial(s) to establish efficacy and safety[;] The use of a pharmacodynamic endpoint for demonstration of clinical benefit[;] Reliance on results obtained in a per-protocol rather than an intent-to-treatment population[;] The size of the efficacy and safety databases[;] Inadequacy of dose-finding."

*[verbatim, FDA Division Director Summary Review, BLA 125327, "Regulatory history of efficacy trial"]* — "Key agreements reached regarding the efficacy trial during the Sept. 8, 2006 pre-BLA meeting were: The primary analysis population for PR001-CLN-rpt006 would consist of all enrolled patients with impaired methotrexate clearance with methotrexate levels > 1 μmol/L prior to treatment with glucarpidase. The primary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of patients who achieved a durable, clinically important reduction (CIR) in plasma methotrexate concentration (pMTX) ... FDA agreed that the point estimate for the CIR rate and 95% confidence intervals should be provided but did not reach prospective agreement on the lower confidence limit."

*[verbatim, FDA Division Director Summary Review, BLA 125327, efficacy-trial discussion]* — "A limitation of the study design (single-arm trial) is that the effects of a rapid reduction of toxic methotrexate concentrations on duration or severity of methotrexate toxicity and on the risk of death arising from methotrexate toxicity, cannot be determined."

### 4. Avanafil (Stendra) — NDA 202276

**Sponsor:** Vivus, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of erectile dysfunction (ED) in men

**Approval date:** April 27, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** TA-301 (general ED population), NCT00790751, and TA-302/REVIVE-D (diabetic-male ED population), NCT00809471

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group phase 3 trials, each with a 4-week non-treatment run-in period followed by a 12-week double-blind treatment period; TA-301 randomized 1:1:1:1 to placebo/avanafil 50 mg/100 mg/200 mg in a general ED population (n=646), TA-302 randomized 1:1:1 to placebo/avanafil 100 mg/200 mg in a diabetic-male ED population (n=390); randomization stratified by baseline ED severity (IIEF erectile-function-domain score: mild 17-25, moderate 11-16, severe ≤10); a Special Protocol Assessment (SPA) was requested for TA-301's protocol in 2006 but no agreement was reached with FDA

- *Endpoints:* three co-primary efficacy variables derived from a subject diary (Sexual Encounter Profile questions 4 and 5, i.e. SEP2/SEP3) plus the IIEF questionnaire — change in percentage of sexual attempts achieving successful intercourse (SEP3), change in percentage of attempts achieving vaginal penetration (SEP2), and change in IIEF erectile-function (EF) domain score from baseline to end of the 12-week treatment period; a dose could be claimed effective only if it reached significance on all three simultaneously (conjunctive co-primary requirement)

- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA model (treatment and baseline ED-severity category as factors, baseline value as covariate) for each co-primary endpoint in the Intent-to-Treat population, with LS-mean differences, standard errors, 95% CIs, and two-sided p-values

- *Multiplicity:* pre-specified fixed-sequence (step-down) dose-vs-placebo testing, highest dose first, at two-sided alpha=0.05 per study, requiring all three co-primary endpoints to win before testing proceeded to the next-lower dose; the sponsor's SAP did not pre-specify a method for the planned follow-on comparisons among active doses once multiple doses beat placebo, so FDA's reviewer applied its own post hoc Hochberg step-up procedure to make that comparison for TA-301

- *Missing data/bias:* no imputation (observed-data-only) for the two diary-based co-primary endpoints; last-observation-carried-forward (LOCF) imputation used only for the IIEF-based co-primary endpoint — flagged at the original 74-day filing review, which requested (and received) an observed-data-only sensitivity analysis of the IIEF endpoint as a condition of filing

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was convened (per the Summary Review, Section 9: "no Advisory Committee was convened" for avanafil, a fourth-in-class PDE5 inhibitor)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- TA-301 (general ED, ≥18 years, ED of ≥6 months' duration, excluding ED from spinal cord injury or radical prostatectomy) and TA-302 (same criteria, restricted to type 1/2 diabetic men) were near-identically designed double-blind, placebo-controlled trials at multiple US sites; eligible subjects entered a 4-week non-treatment run-in period, then were randomized only if they had ≥4 documented intercourse attempts during run-in, failed to maintain a sufficient erection in ≥50% of those attempts, and had a baseline IIEF-EF domain score of 5-25.

- During the 12-week double-blind treatment period, subjects took one dose ~30 minutes before sexual activity (up to two doses per 24 hours, ≥12 hours apart) and were asked to attempt intercourse ≥4 times per month; efficacy was derived from a 7-item subject diary completed after each attempt and from the IIEF questionnaire completed at each visit.

- Analysis populations: Safety (≥1 dose, safety data available), ITT (randomized, ≥1 dose per diary, ≥1 post-dose efficacy assessment — 622/646 in TA-301, 379/390 in TA-302), and Evaluable (ITT subjects with ≥6 doses taken and ≥4 run-in attempts).

- Results: in TA-301, relative to placebo, all three avanafil doses were statistically significant on all three co-primary endpoints (e.g., SEP3 treatment effect of 13.8%/29.3%/30.2% for 50/100/200 mg, all p≤0.0002); in TA-302, avanafil 100 mg and 200 mg were significant on all three co-primary endpoints versus placebo (SEP3 treatment effect 15.2%/20.4%, both p<0.0001). Using its own post hoc Hochberg procedure on the pairwise between-dose comparisons in TA-301 (since the sponsor's SAP did not pre-specify how these would be conducted), FDA's reviewer concluded avanafil 100 mg and 200 mg were each statistically superior to 50 mg and not different from each other; numerically, 200 mg outperformed 100 mg, especially in diabetic subjects.

- Subgroup analyses (age, race, baseline ED severity, ED duration) used the same ANCOVA model with added subgroup and treatment-by-subgroup interaction terms; in TA-302 the treatment-by-race interaction was statistically significant for each co-primary endpoint, with the treatment effect essentially confined to white subjects (FDA's reviewer noted the non-white subgroup was too small to draw conclusions).

- Discontinuation rates were 14.9% (TA-301) and 14.6% (TA-302), driven mainly by protocol non-compliance/withdrawal of consent, loss to follow-up, and adverse events; the reviewer replicated the sponsor's primary-endpoint results directly from the submitted datasets.

- Substantial portions of the posted FDA Statistical Review — including the remainder of Section 3.2.4.2 (efficacy-by-dose-timing results), Section 3.3 (safety evaluation), and Section 5 (Summary and Conclusions) — are blank/non-extractable in the public PDF (a `(b)(4)` trade-secret redaction marker appears at the start of the affected passage), so this entry's design/endpoint description is drawn only from the unredacted sections.

**Other resources**

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 202276, Executive Summary, p.5]* — "For the comparisons between Avanafil dose groups with placebo, the Applicant used a step-down, multiple-comparison procedure starting from the highest Avanafil dose to the lowest one. Under this step-down procedure, all three Avanafil doses in study TA-301 are significantly better than placebo on all co-primary endpoints. The Applicant's statistical analysis plan (SAP) for TA-301 stated that 'If multiple active dose groups are significantly better than placebo, then those Avanafil dose groups will be compared'. But the Applicant did not pre-specify how these pair-wise comparisons between Avanafil doses would be conducted in the SAP."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Section 3.2.4.1, p.12-13]* — "The Applicant's multiplicity control approach stated that 'if multiple active dose groups are significantly better than placebo, then those Avanafil dose groups will be compared' in study TA-301 without pre-specifying how these comparisons would be conducted in the SAP. With regards of this issue, the reviewer used Hochberg procedure on each co-primary endpoint to compare three Avanafil doses in TA-301... Using Hochberg procedure, this review concluded that in study TA-301, Avanafil 100 mg and 200 mg are statistically significantly better than 50 mg and they are not different from each other."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Section 3.2.3.3, p.12]* — "In the analysis of co-primary endpoints derived from the subject diaries, only the observed data were employed. For the co-primary endpoint based on IIEF data, the last observation carried forward (LOCF) algorithm was used."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistics Filing Checklist for a New NDA, requests to Applicant on 74-day letter]* — "To assess the sensitivity of missing data, the Applicant should analyze the observed data for the EFS of the IIEF questionnaire without LOCF imputation using ANCOVA model specified in the study protocol."

### 5. Mirabegron (Myrbetriq) — NDA 202611

**Sponsor:** Astellas Pharma Global Development, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of overactive bladder (OAB) with symptoms of urge urinary incontinence, urgency, and urinary frequency

**Approval date:** June 28, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** Studies 178-CL-046 (NCT00689104), 178-CL-047 (NCT00662909), and 178-CL-074 (NCT00912964)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* three multinational, multicenter, double-blind, randomized, parallel-group, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials with a single-blind 2-week placebo run-in before a 12-week double-blind treatment period; 178-CL-046 (Europe) was also active-controlled, randomizing 1:1:1:1 to placebo/mirabegron 50 mg/100 mg/tolterodine SR 4 mg (n=1987); 178-CL-047 (US/Canada) randomized 1:1:1 to placebo/mirabegron 50 mg/100 mg (n=1329); 178-CL-074 (Europe/US/Canada) randomized 1:1:1 to placebo/mirabegron 25 mg/50 mg (n=1306); Special Protocol Assessment sought for 178-CL-046/047 in 2007 and again in 2009 but no agreement was reached with FDA on either occasion

- *Endpoints:* two co-primary endpoints from a 3-day micturition diary — change from baseline to end of treatment (final visit) in mean number of micturitions per 24 hours, and change from baseline to final visit in mean number of incontinence episodes per 24 hours; key secondary endpoints included change in mean volume voided per micturition and the same two co-primary measures assessed at Week 4, with 178-CL-074 adding urgency-level and urgency-incontinence-episode secondary endpoints

- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA (treatment, gender, geographic region, baseline value) for micturitions and volume-voided endpoints; because change in incontinence episodes was non-normally distributed, a stratified rank ANCOVA (region-standardized ranks, gender and baseline rank as covariates) was used instead for that endpoint; LOCF used for subjects missing a Week-12 value

- *Multiplicity:* stepwise parallel gatekeeping procedure across ordered stages (incontinence episodes → micturitions → volume voided → incontinence at Week 4 → micturitions at Week 4, plus three additional 178-CL-074-specific stages for urgency measures), with a dose group advancing to the next stage only if it won the prior stage, and a Hochberg procedure applied within each stage across the mirabegron dose groups at overall alpha=0.05 (a multi-stage parallel gatekeeping ladder spanning both endpoints and dose groups, with within-stage Hochberg adjustment at each stage — not itself an existing taxonomy entry)

- *Missing data/bias:* LOCF for the primary/key-secondary diary endpoints; no major imputation controversy noted by the reviewer

- *Regulatory:* FDA Reproductive Health Drugs Advisory Committee meeting held April 5, 2012 (voted 8-4 that data provided substantial evidence of benefit, 9-3 that safety was adequately demonstrated, and 7-4-1 that the overall benefit-risk assessment supported approval); two postmarketing-required studies stemmed from Committee-raised cardiovascular and neoplasm safety signals

**Trial design & endpoints**

- All three studies enrolled adults with OAB symptoms for ≥3 months, ≥8 micturitions per 24 hours, and ≥3 episodes of grade-3/4 urgency (with or without incontinence) in a 3-day diary period; a single-blind placebo run-in preceded the 12-week double-blind treatment period, with a 30-day (178-CL-046/047) or 2-week (178-CL-074) follow-up.

- Analysis populations were the Full Analysis Set (FAS: randomized, ≥1 dose, baseline + ≥1 post-baseline micturition diary measurement) for micturitions/volume-voided endpoints, and the FAS-incontinence subset (additionally requiring ≥1 baseline incontinence episode) for the incontinence endpoint.

- Results: in 178-CL-046, both mirabegron doses beat placebo on all co-primary/key-secondary endpoints under the gatekeeping procedure (incontinence episodes: -0.41 [50 mg] and -0.29 [100 mg] more reduction than placebo, p=0.003/0.010; micturitions: -0.60/-0.44, p<0.001/0.005), while tolterodine SR 4 mg did not reach significance on the co-primary endpoints, halting further key-secondary testing for that arm. In 178-CL-047, both mirabegron doses were significant on both co-primary endpoints. In 178-CL-074, mirabegron 25 mg and 50 mg produced "very similar efficacy on the co-primary endpoints," per FDA's reviewer, prompting the review's stated conclusion that mirabegron 25 mg — not only the sponsor-proposed 50 mg dose — should be considered for general OAB patients.

- Subject discontinuation rates ranged 9.9%-13.6% across the three studies, mainly for adverse events and withdrawal of consent; demographics were broadly similar across arms within each trial (roughly 68-75% female, mean age 59-60 years, predominantly white).

- The April 5, 2012 Reproductive Health Drugs Advisory Committee discussion centered on blood-pressure findings from phase 1/3 studies, increased neoplasm reports at the 100 mg dose, hepatic adverse events, and hypersensitivity reactions, alongside the efficacy votes described above; FDA's Summary Review states the Committee's recommendations on efficacy/dosing were largely incorporated into labeling, while cardiovascular-outcome and neoplasm safety signals were deferred to postmarketing-required studies.

### 6. Sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and citric acid (Prepopik) — NDA 202535

**Sponsor:** Ferring Pharmaceuticals

**Indication approved:** Cleansing of the colon as a preparation for colonoscopy in adults

**Approval date:** July 16, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** SEE CLEAR I / Study FE2009-01 (split-dose), NCT01073930, and SEE CLEAR II / Study FE2009-02 (day-before dose), NCT01073943

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two phase 3, randomized, multicenter, assessor-blinded (bowel-cleansing endpoint rated by a colonoscopist blinded to treatment, while only the subject and an unblinded site coordinator knew assignment), active-controlled, non-inferiority trials, each randomizing ~600 subjects 1:1 to PicoPrep/Prepopik versus HalfLytely/Bisacodyl Bowel Prep Kit (10 mg bisacodyl + 2 L PEG-electrolyte solution, day-before dosing); FE2009-01 tested a split-dose PicoPrep regimen (evening-before + morning-of), FE2009-02 tested a same-day-before regimen (both pouches the evening before); randomization was sequential via Interactive Voice Response System, with 8 subjects manually randomized due to kit unavailability — no stratification factors described (assessor-blinded active-controlled non-inferiority design for a bowel-cleansing-quality endpoint — not itself an existing taxonomy entry)

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint was the proportion of responders (rated "Excellent" or "Good" on the 4-point Aronchick Scale) for overall colon cleansing at the colonoscopy visit, assessed by a blinded colonoscopist; key secondary endpoint was the proportion of responders (rated "Excellent," "Good," or "Fair" on the 5-point Ottawa Scale) specifically for ascending-colon cleansing (blinded-colonoscopist-rated ordinal bowel-cleansing-quality scale as primary/secondary efficacy endpoint — not itself an existing taxonomy entry)

- *Primary analysis:* non-inferiority assessed via a 97.5% one-sided (equivalently, 95% two-sided) confidence interval for the risk difference (PicoPrep minus HalfLytely) in responder proportions in the ITT population, using SAS PROC FREQ RISKDIFF (Wald asymptotic CI); non-inferiority declared if the lower confidence bound exceeded -9%, with a pre-specified follow-on superiority test (lower bound > 0) if non-inferiority held; Breslow-Day test substituted post hoc for an originally planned site-adjusted logistic-regression site-homogeneity check (a change from the original SAP)

- *Multiplicity:* sequential non-inferiority-then-superiority gate within each trial (test superiority only if non-inferiority is met first); no adjustment for testing this structure across the two independently-run trials

- *Missing data/bias:* no imputation of missing efficacy data; untreated/no-efficacy-assessment subjects were handled via the sponsor's ITT analysis (treated as failures) versus the reviewer's mITT dataset (excluded), which the review found did not change conclusions; the FDA statistical reviewer explicitly disagreed with the sponsor's chosen 9% non-inferiority margin as too permissive (having recommended 4% at the IND stage) and with the sponsor's choice of a 10 mg (rather than 20 mg) bisacodyl comparator dose, though FDA proceeded to evaluate the trials as conducted

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was convened

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Both trials enrolled adults undergoing elective colonoscopy at US sites (FE2009-01: 10 sites, May-October 2010; FE2009-02: 12 sites, May-October 2010), following a screening visit (Visit 1, eligibility confirmed within 21 days) and randomization at Visit 2; the primary efficacy/safety assessment occurred at Visit 3 (day of colonoscopy), with follow-up visits at 24-48 hours, 7 days, and 4 weeks post-procedure. A placebo-controlled design was considered neither practical nor ethical, since placebo subjects would risk a failed colonoscopy.

- Sample size (~300/arm, ~600 total per trial) was powered for 85% at a one-sided alpha of 0.025 assuming an 85% PicoPrep/HalfLytely responder rate and a 9.0% non-inferiority margin; the sponsor derived that margin using a "M1/M2" approach referencing historical HalfLytely/OsmoPrep response-rate literature (constancy assumption), a margin the FDA statistical reviewer considered too wide and recommended tightening to 4% at the IND stage — a recommendation the sponsor did not adopt.

- Analysis populations were ITT/Full Analysis Set (all randomized subjects who received any treatment), modified ITT (mITT, additionally requiring an Aronchick/Ottawa efficacy assessment — the reviewer's principal analysis population), Per-Protocol (excluding major protocol violations, e.g. dosing outside the prescribed window), and Safety (by actual treatment received).

- Results, Study FE2009-01 (split-dose): responder rates were 84.2% (PicoPrep) vs. 74.9% (HalfLytely), 95% CI for the difference (2.9%, 15.7%) — the entire interval excluding zero, meeting both the non-inferiority and the pre-specified follow-on superiority criteria (per the FDA reviewer's and sponsor's conclusions, PicoPrep split-dose was superior to HalfLytely).

- Results, Study FE2009-02 (day-before dose): responder rates were 82.9% (PicoPrep) vs. 79.7% (HalfLytely), 95% CI for the difference (-3.0%, 10.0%) — meeting non-inferiority (lower bound above the -9% margin) but not superiority (interval crosses zero).

- Key secondary (ascending-colon, Ottawa Scale) results were directionally consistent with the primary endpoint in both trials (e.g., in Study FE2009-02, PicoPrep vs. HalfLytely "Excellent" ascending-colon ratings were 15% vs. 10%); subgroup analyses by age and gender showed generally consistent or larger PicoPrep-favoring differences, notably in men in both trials (Study FE2009-01: 14% [3%, 25%] difference in men vs. 6% [-2%, 14%] in women).

- Table-count discrepancies between the sponsor's Table 7-1 (study report) and Table 14.1.1 (demographic dataset) subject-disposition figures were identified by the reviewer and resolved with the sponsor (attributed to differing treatment of untreated randomized subjects across the ISE/ISS integration).

### 7. Ospemifene (Osphena) — NDA 203505

**Sponsor:** Shionogi Inc. (product originated under Homos Medical, acquired by Shionogi USA Inc. in April 2010)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of moderate to severe dyspareunia, a symptom of vulvar and vaginal atrophy (VVA), due to menopause

**Approval date:** February 26, 2013

**Pivotal trial:** Study 15-50310, NCT00276094, and Study 15-50821, NCT00729469 (two randomized, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trials)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, multicenter, parallel-group Phase 3 trials in postmenopausal women aged 40-80; Study 15-50310 was 3-arm (ospemifene 30 mg, 60 mg, placebo; randomization stratified by uterine status), Study 15-50821 was 2-arm (ospemifene 60 mg, placebo; randomization stratified by most-bothersome-symptom category); all subjects also received an as-needed non-hormonal vaginal lubricant

- *Endpoints:* four co-primary endpoints in both trials — change from baseline to Week 12 in percentage of parabasal cells, percentage of superficial cells (vaginal maturation index), vaginal pH, and severity of the patient-self-identified most bothersome VVA symptom (vaginal dryness or dyspareunia, on a 0-3 severity scale); secondary endpoints were the same four measures at Week 4

- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA (treatment, uterine status where applicable, study center, baseline value as covariate) for the three continuous/cytologic co-primary endpoints, with a rank-based ANCOVA fallback if model assumptions were violated; Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test (stratified by study center and, in Study 15-50310, uterine status) for the categorical most-bothersome-symptom severity endpoint; FDA's reviewer additionally ran a mixed-model-repeated-measures (MMRM) sensitivity analysis against the sponsor's last-observation-carried-forward (LOCF) primary approach, with concordant results

- *Multiplicity:* step-down testing across doses (60 mg tested first; 30 mg tested only if all four 60 mg co-primary comparisons were significant) in Study 15-50310; no multiplicity adjustment was applied between the two most-bothersome-symptom strata (vaginal dryness vs. dyspareunia) as agreed with FDA, since either symptom alone was an acceptable regulatory claim — FDA's reviewer nonetheless applied his own post hoc Bonferroni adjustment between the two symptoms for internal verification

- *Missing data/bias:* LOCF used for missing Week 12 values, with a mixed-model repeated-measures sensitivity analysis; the mITT primary efficacy population imposed after enrollment (per FDA's May 2011 meeting minutes) restricted analysis to subjects meeting all three baseline inclusion criteria (vaginal pH >5, superficial cells ≤5%, qualifying most-bothersome symptom), shrinking the analyzable population well below the number randomized in Study 15-50310 (655 of 826) while including slightly more than planned in Study 15-50821 (905 of a 750 target, reflecting the trial's larger realized enrollment); 8 subjects in Study 15-50821 received study drug without ever being assigned identification numbers in the randomization scheme, and were analyzed both with and without inclusion

- *Regulatory:* efficacy claim ultimately restricted to dyspareunia only — ospemifene 60 mg did not achieve statistically significant improvement in vaginal dryness in either pivotal trial, and the 30 mg dose (tested in Study 15-50310 only) did not achieve significance on the co-primary battery at all — a asymmetric-endpoint-support outcome (drug approved for one of two originally sought symptom claims, based on the same co-primary battery run separately by symptom subgroup) not itself captured by an existing taxonomy term

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Both trials enrolled postmenopausal women 40-80 years old with vaginal superficial cells ≤5% on smear, vaginal pH >5.0, and at least one self-identified moderate-to-severe VVA symptom (vaginal dryness and/or dyspareunia); Study 15-50310 enrolled 826 subjects (planned 795) across 76 US sites and additionally tested a 30 mg ospemifene dose, while Study 15-50821 enrolled 919 subjects (planned 750) across 112 US sites and tested only 60 mg

- The four co-primary endpoints (percentage parabasal cells, percentage superficial cells, vaginal pH, and most-bothersome-symptom severity, each change from baseline to Week 12) were identical across trials; the FDA-preferred primary efficacy (mITT) population, per May 2011 meeting minutes, required all three baseline eligibility criteria to be met simultaneously — narrower than the sponsor's own original ITT-based mITT definition, and it substantially reduced the effective analysis population in Study 15-50310 (655/826) while including nearly the full randomized population in Study 15-50821 (905/919), reflecting that trial's stricter upfront eligibility screening

- Sample-size assumptions (per protocol): a 20-percentage-point placebo-adjusted difference in parabasal cells (SD 40.3), a 5-point difference in superficial cells (SD 12.4), a 0.5 difference in vaginal pH (SD 1.1), and 81% power for a 0.4-point difference in symptom severity (SD 0.94), assuming 40% of subjects had vaginal dryness as their most-bothersome symptom, at two-sided alpha=0.05 with a 15% anticipated dropout

- Results (mITT, dyspareunia subjects only, both trials): ospemifene 60 mg statistically significantly improved all four co-primary endpoints at Week 12 in both studies (all nominal p≤0.0012, most p<0.0001); placebo-adjusted mean change in dyspareunia severity was -0.51 (95% CI -0.81, -0.20; Study 15-50310) and -0.36 (95% CI -0.53, -0.18; Study 15-50821); placebo-adjusted changes in vaginal pH were -0.97 and -0.87/-0.90, in percent superficial cells +8.2 and +10.7, and in percent parabasal cells -40.3 and -40.0, respectively — ospemifene 60 mg did not statistically significantly improve vaginal dryness in either trial, and the 30 mg dose in Study 15-50310 failed the co-primary battery, so FDA's reviewer's detailed results presentation was limited to the 60 mg-versus-placebo, dyspareunia-only comparison

- Exploratory subgroup analyses by uterine status and lubricant use showed no clear evidence of effect-modification on vaginal pH, superficial cells, or parabasal cells, though subjects using lubricant showed numerically larger symptom-severity improvement in one trial

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review and Evaluation, NDA 203505, "3.2.4 Results and Conclusion"]* — "This section presents the efficacy results only for ospemifene 60 mg compared with placebo at 12 weeks in dyspareunia subjects; because ospemifene 30 mg did not statistically significantly improve a VVA symptom at 12 weeks, and neither ospemifene doses statistically significantly improved a VVA symptom at 4 weeks or vaginal dryness at 12 weeks in both studies."

*[verbatim, same review, same section]* — "Our analysis showed that ospemifene 60 mg did not improve vaginal dryness in either study. Therefore, only results for dyspareunia are shown here in more detail... As shown in Table 5, ospemifene 60 mg statistically significantly improved all four primary efficacy endpoints at week 12 in both studies in dyspareunia subjects."

*[verbatim, same review, "3.2.2 Statistical Methodologies"]* — "Type–I error rate for between dose comparisons was controlled by step-down approach. Ospemifene 60 mg dose was tested first: if all four co-primary endpoints were statistically significant, then ospemifene 30 mg dose was tested. There was no multiplicity adjustment for evaluating the two VVA symptoms as agreed upon with the Agency in order to claim either or both symptoms. A Bonferroni multiplicity adjustment was performed by this reviewer between vaginal dryness and dyspareunia."

### 8. Gadoterate meglumine (Dotarem) — NDA 204781

**Sponsor:** Guerbet LLC

**Indication approved:** Intravenous use with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in brain (intracranial), spine, and associated tissues in adults and pediatric patients (2 years of age and older) to detect and visualize areas with disruption of the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and/or abnormal vascularity

**Approval date:** March 20, 2013

**Pivotal trial:** Study DGD-44-050 ("SENTIO" study), NCT01211873 (randomized, double-blind, active-comparator), and Study DGD-44-051 (a blinded, centralized re-read of a previously conducted, non-US Phase 3 study, DGD-3-44; no NCT identifier found)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* diagnostic-accuracy study (within-patient paired comparison) (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1, "Diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison)"); Study 050 was multicenter, international (US, Europe, Korea, Latin America), randomized 2:1, double-blind, fixed-sequence (unenhanced MRI always preceding contrast-enhanced MRI), active-comparator (gadopentetate dimeglumine/Magnevist) trial in adults (n=364) and a Dotarem-only pediatric cohort (n=38, ages 2-18); Study 051 was a blinded, centralized re-read by three new independent readers of images from a previously completed, differently-purposed Phase 3 study (DGD-3-44, n=150) rather than a freshly conducted trial — *a "re-read" pivotal study design in which a prior, independently-conducted trial's existing images are freshly and blindedly re-interpreted under a new endpoint-scoring charter to serve as a second pivotal efficacy dataset, rather than running a new prospective trial*; all images in both studies read by three off-site readers blinded to clinical information

- *Endpoints:* three co-primary visualization endpoints — border delineation, internal morphology, and degree of contrast enhancement — each scored 0 (unevaluable), 1 (seen imperfectly), or 2 (seen completely) for up to the 5 largest lesions per patient, summed within patient per MRI modality ("Pre" unenhanced vs. "Paired" unenhanced-plus-contrast), with the primary analysis based on the within-patient Paired-minus-Pre score difference; secondary endpoints included Pre-vs-Post-only (contrast-alone) comparisons, lesion-count endpoints, and (in Study 050 only) a Dotarem-vs-Magnevist comparison

- *Primary analysis:* multiple regression modeling each patient's co-primary score as a function of MRI modality with adjustment for center and repeated measures within patient (compound-symmetry covariance); to be declared successful, at least 2 of 3 blinded readers had to show a statistically significant (one-sided p<0.025) positive Paired-vs-Pre difference for each of the three co-primary visualization variables; all three co-primary variables met this bar for all three readers in both Study 050 and Study 051 (p<0.001 for every reader/endpoint combination)

- *Missing data/bias:* a pre-specified imputation rule assigned a score of 0 (no lesion) on whichever MRI modality had no lesion identified when the other modality did, preserving the paired-difference calculation rather than excluding the patient; visualization scores were explicitly flagged by FDA's own reviewer as "soft" and potentially difficult-to-interpret subjective endpoints, though consistent with FDA's established 2004 guidance-based paradigm for gadolinium contrast agent approval and with the six other CNS-indicated gadolinium agents already on the market

- *Regulatory:* FDA Medical Imaging Drugs Advisory Committee convened February 14, 2013, specifically to evaluate the pediatric (under-2-years) indication the sponsor was separately seeking; the committee voted unanimously (17-0) that the risk-benefit balance favored approval for adults and children 2 years and older, but voted 10-6 (1 abstention) against approving Dotarem for children younger than 2 years, citing insufficient pharmacokinetic and juvenile-animal data — FDA followed the committee's split recommendation, approving only the 2-years-and-older population

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study DGD-44-050 (SENTIO) enrolled 364 adults (245 Dotarem : 119 Magnevist, 2:1 randomization) plus 38 children aged 2-18 (Dotarem only) across 11 countries; each subject received unenhanced MRI immediately followed by contrast-enhanced MRI with the randomly assigned agent; the primary efficacy comparison (Dotarem Paired vs. Pre) was assessed only within the Dotarem arm, while the Magnevist arm served as an internal active-comparator validation, with a secondary Dotarem-vs-Magnevist comparison performed at FDA's request

- Study DGD-44-051 was a re-read, by three new off-site blinded readers, of the previously conducted (and, per FDA's review, less definitive-by-design) Phase 3 study DGD-3-44 in 150 adults with known or suspected cerebral/spinal tumors, most enrolled to undergo biopsy or surgery; because the underlying trial had originally been conducted and interpreted for a different purpose, FDA's statistical reviewer explicitly treated Study 051's results as supportive rather than a definitive/independent confirmatory dataset

- Primary objective (both studies): demonstrate superiority of Dotarem-enhanced Paired MRI over unenhanced Pre MRI for lesion visualization (border delineation, internal morphology, degree of contrast enhancement) in CNS lesions with blood-brain-barrier disruption and/or abnormal vascularity (tumoral, vascular, inflammatory, or infectious)

- Results (Study 050, adult full analysis set, patient-level scores): mean Paired-minus-Pre score differences ranged from approximately 1.2 to 3.7 points across the three endpoints and three readers, all with p<0.001 by the pre-specified regression model; the percentage of patients showing improved (vs. not-better) lesion visualization with Paired images ranged from 56% to 94% across readers and endpoints; pediatric subjects (2 years and older) and Dotarem-vs-Magnevist secondary comparisons showed a generally consistent pattern of improvement; Study 051's blinded re-read produced the same qualitative pattern (all three co-primary endpoints statistically significant for all three readers, p<0.001)

- Pediatric limitation: efficacy/safety data for children younger than 2 years were limited to only 7 subjects with no pharmacokinetic data submitted, which FDA's statistical reviewer and the Advisory Committee both concluded were inadequate to support approval in that subgroup, notwithstanding the sponsor's citation of historical non-US clinical experience

- Package Insert / Label (original) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2013/204781s000lbl.pdf
