### 9. Conjugated estrogens/bazedoxifene (Duavee) — NDA 22247

**Sponsor:** Wyeth Pharmaceuticals Inc. (a wholly owned subsidiary of Pfizer Inc.)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms (VMS) associated with menopause, and prevention of postmenopausal osteoporosis, in women with a uterus

**Approval date:** October 3, 2013

**Pivotal trial:** Study 3115A1-305 ("SMART-2"), NCT00234819, for the VMS indication; Study 3115A1-303 ("SMART-1"), NCT00675688, and Study 3115A1-3307 ("SMART-5"), NCT00808132, for the osteoporosis-prevention/endometrial-safety indication (a related trial, Study 3115A1-306, NCT00238732, also assessed VMS)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* bazedoxifene (BZA) substitutes for a progestin in a "tissue-selective estrogen complex" (TSEC) paired with conjugated estrogens (CE), specifically to protect the endometrium from unopposed-estrogen-driven hyperplasia without a progestin's side effects — *a combination product in which a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) substitutes for the progestin component of a conventional estrogen/progestin regimen, marketed as a "tissue-selective estrogen complex"*; randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled (raloxifene, and/or CE/medroxyprogesterone acetate) parallel-group Phase 3 trials; Study 303 (SMART-1) was an 8-arm, 24-month trial (n=3,397 dosed) with two nested BMD substudies stratified by years-since-menopause; Study 3307 (SMART-5) was a 1-year, 5-arm trial; Study 305 (SMART-2) was a dedicated, 12-week, 3-arm (BZA 20 mg/CE 0.45 mg, BZA 20 mg/CE 0.625 mg, placebo) VMS efficacy trial (n=332) in women with ≥7 moderate/severe hot flushes per day or ≥50 per week

- *Endpoints:* VMS co-primary endpoints (Study 305): change from baseline in average daily number and average daily severity of moderate-to-severe hot flushes at Weeks 4 and 12; osteoporosis-prevention endpoints (Studies 303, 3307): primary endpoint mean percent change from baseline in lumbar spine BMD at Month 24 (Study 303) or Month 12 (Study 3307), key secondary endpoint mean percent change in total hip BMD; each of Study 303 and Study 3307's overall (not-substudy-specific) primary endpoint was the safety co-primary of endometrial hyperplasia incidence at Year 1 — a genuine safety-as-gating-primary-endpoint structure, distinguishing this program from an ordinary co-primary efficacy pair

- *Primary analysis:* VMS — ANCOVA (treatment and study site as factors, baseline value as covariate, treatment-by-site interaction term), last-observation-carried-forward for missing data, on the modified intent-to-treat population; osteoporosis-prevention — ANCOVA (treatment, region [US vs. non-US], baseline BMD, years-since-menopause as covariate) with LOCF on the modified intent-to-treat population

- *Multiplicity:* three-tier hierarchical/gatekeeping testing sequence across endpoint domains within Study 303 — hyperplasia incidence tested first (0.05 level); only if the hyperplasia rate met acceptability criteria were BMD endpoints tested (at an alpha of 0.048, adjusted from 0.05 to reserve alpha for a planned interim analysis per an O'Brien-Fleming spending function); only if BMD endpoints were statistically significant were hot-flush frequency/severity endpoints tested (0.05 level) — *a cross-domain (safety-then-efficacy-then-a-second-efficacy-domain) hierarchical gatekeeping procedure spanning three conceptually distinct endpoint types (a safety incidence rate, a surrogate bone-density efficacy measure, and a patient-reported symptom efficacy measure) within one trial*; within each efficacy domain, sequential dose-then-regimen testing (e.g., VMS: 0.625 mg CE dose tested before the 0.45 mg CE dose could be tested)

- *Interim/alpha-spending:* O'Brien-Fleming-type alpha-spending for Study 303's planned Year-1 interim analysis of BMD (significance level 0.005 at the interim, 0.048 at the Month-24 final analysis), conducted for dose-selection planning purposes rather than early-stopping/success-declaration

- *Missing data/bias:* FDA's Office of Scientific Investigations identified data-integrity concerns at multiple Study 303 sites, most notably ~80 patients (9% of that site's enrollment) with entirely missing source documentation at one site and a further data-integrity-flagged site ("Christopher Hutchison") whose ~22 patients (~7% of the VMS modified-intent-to-treat population) were excluded in a dedicated sensitivity analysis for the VMS endpoint; results were materially unchanged whether or not affected patients/sites were excluded, per both the sponsor's and FDA's own reanalyses

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was convened; the vulvar-and-vaginal-atrophy (VVA) indication was also studied (a separate, heavily-redacted FDA statistical review by a different reviewer, Kate Dwyer, Ph.D., exists in the public record with the bulk of its substantive content — 20 pages — withheld as confidential commercial information) but was not part of the final approved label, which covers only VMS and osteoporosis prevention

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 305 (SMART-2) enrolled 332 healthy postmenopausal women (40-65 years) with moderate-to-severe hot flushes (≥7/day or ≥50/week), randomized to BZA 20 mg/CE 0.45 mg, BZA 20 mg/CE 0.625 mg, or placebo for 12 weeks; both active doses significantly reduced hot-flush frequency and severity at Weeks 4 and 12 versus placebo (all p<0.001); at Week 12, hot flushes fell from a baseline of 10.3-10.5/day by 74% (BZA/CE 0.45 mg) and 80% (BZA/CE 0.625 mg) versus 51% for placebo, with placebo-subtracted treatment effects of -3.1 (95% CI -4.4, -1.7) and -2.7 (95% CI -3.8, -1.6) hot flushes/day at Weeks 4 and 12 respectively (frequency), and parallel statistically significant reductions in severity

- Study 303 (SMART-1) was an 8-arm, 24-month trial randomizing 3,544 postmenopausal women (3,397 dosed) with an intact uterus to six BZA/CE dose combinations (BZA 10/20/40 mg, each with CE 0.45 or 0.625 mg), raloxifene 60 mg, or placebo, across two nested osteoporosis-prevention substudies (Substudy I: >5 years postmenopausal, n=1,454; Substudy II: 1-5 years postmenopausal, n=861); the overall trial's primary endpoint (basis for the total sample size) was endometrial hyperplasia incidence at Year 1, gating subsequent testing of the BMD endpoints and, in turn, the hot-flush endpoints in a three-step hierarchical procedure

- Study 3307 (SMART-5) randomized 590 postmenopausal women (≤5 years postmenopausal) across 5 arms (BZA/CE 0.45 mg or 0.625 mg [20 mg BZA], bazedoxifene 20 mg alone, CE 0.45 mg/medroxyprogesterone acetate 1.5 mg, placebo) for 1 year, with the same overall hyperplasia-gated hierarchical structure and BMD substudy design as Study 303 but a single 12-month analysis rather than an interim/final two-stage design

- Osteoporosis-prevention results: for the to-be-marketed BZA 20 mg/CE 0.45 mg and 0.625 mg doses, lumbar spine BMD increased significantly versus placebo at Month 24 in both Study 303 substudies (e.g., BZA 20 mg/CE 0.45 mg: +3.08 to +3.61 percentage points versus placebo depending on substudy, both p<0.001), with parallel, smaller but still statistically significant improvements in total hip BMD (key secondary endpoint); Study 3307 showed a consistent pattern at 12 months

- Endometrial hyperplasia (safety primary/gating endpoint): incidence remained at or near 0% through Year 1 for the to-be-marketed BZA 20 mg doses in both Study 303 (0/335 for CE 0.45 mg/BZA 20 mg) and Study 3307 (1/335 for CE 0.45 mg/BZA 20 mg), meeting the pre-specified upper-confidence-bound acceptability threshold and permitting the hierarchical procedure to advance to BMD/VMS testing; a body-mass-index-related pharmacokinetic finding (16% lower bazedoxifene exposure in patients with BMI >27 kg/m² versus ≤27 kg/m²) raised a documented concern about reduced endometrial protection at higher BMI with the lower (10 mg) bazedoxifene doses, though this did not affect the to-be-marketed 20 mg dose's acceptability

- Cardiovascular/cerebrovascular safety across the five pooled Phase 3 trials (adjudicated by independent event committees) showed low, inconclusive-due-to-small-numbers event counts for stroke, transient ischemic attack, and myocardial infarction, attributed in part to the younger mean trial population (mid-50s) relative to the Women's Health Initiative (mid-60s); the approved label nonetheless carries the standard boxed class warning for estrogens (endometrial cancer, cardiovascular disorders, probable dementia)

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, Division Director Review, VMS efficacy discussion]* — "The primary analysis was conducted using an ANCOVA model with treatment and study site as factors and baseline value as a covariate with a term for treatment-by-study-site interaction. The Applicant controlled the type 1 error rate using a stepwise testing procedure so that the conjugated estrogens/bazedoxifene 0.45 mg/20 mg dose was tested only if there was a win on all four co-primary endpoints with the higher 0.625 mg/20 mg dose."

*[verbatim, same review, same discussion]* — "As shown in Table 2, conjugated estrogens/bazedoxifene results in a statistically significant reduction in both the frequency and severity of moderate to severe hot flushes from baseline to Week 4 and from baseline to Week 12 (all p-values <0.001)... the mean treatment difference between drug and placebo in hot flush frequency at Weeks 4 and 12 is greater than 2/day, which is the threshold that has historically been considered acceptable without the need to further evaluate clinical meaningfulness using an anchoring question."

*[verbatim, same review, osteoporosis-prevention discussion]* — "The Applicant used an alpha of 0.048 for the primary efficacy analyses of bone mineral density because some alpha was spent on an interim analysis. The Applicant used hierarchical testing to control the overall type 1 error rate across the different conjugated estrogens and bazedoxifene doses."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review and Evaluation, NDA 22247/0000, Sonia Castillo review, "3.1 Data and Analysis Quality"]* — "There was one statistical analysis issue identified in this submission for the prevention of postmenopausal osteoporosis indication. During the pre-NDA process for this application, the Division learned of multiple problems with the availability/existence of source documents... I performed a sensitivity analysis of the efficacy data for lumbar spine BMD and total hip BMD that excluded those subjects with missing source documents... The impact of missing source documents did not appreciably affect the results."

*[verbatim, same review, "3.2.2 Study 3115A1-303: Statistical Methodologies," Testing Procedure]* — "The final analysis was done in a stepwise manner to control the overall type I error rate. The hyperplasia rate was tested at a 0.05 significance level... If the hyperplasia rate met the acceptability criteria, then BMD endpoints were compared at the two-sided 0.048 level significance level. Finally, if the BMD endpoints were statistically significant, then the daily mean number and severity of hot flushes were compared at the 0.05 significance level."

**Reverse-engineered SAP** [inferred]

- [inferred] Because the public FDA statistical review for the VVA indication (reviewed separately by Kate Dwyer, Ph.D.) has 20 of its substantive pages withheld in full as confidential commercial information, and because the approved Duavee label covers only VMS and osteoporosis prevention with no VVA claim, VVA efficacy was almost certainly judged insufficient or was not pursued to approval in this cycle — traced to the redaction pattern in the public StatR PDF and the absence of any VVA indication language in the approved label's Indications and Usage section.

### 10. Tasimelteon (Hetlioz) — NDA 205677

**Sponsor:** Vanda Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of Non-24-Hour Sleep-Wake Disorder (Non-24) in totally blind individuals

**Approval date:** January 31, 2014

**Pivotal trial:** SET Study (protocol VP-VEC-162-3201), NCT01163032, and RESET Study (protocol VP-VEC-162-3203), NCT01430754

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two multicenter, randomized, double-masked, placebo-controlled, parallel-group phase 3 trials — SET (a ~5-6 week Pre-Randomization Phase followed by a ~26-week Randomization Phase or Open-Label Extension) and RESET (a randomized-withdrawal design enrolling only patients pre-screened through SET, entrained on open-label tasimelteon during a run-in, then randomized to continue tasimelteon or switch to placebo); SET's primary endpoint was changed by protocol amendment after roughly 95% of subjects were already randomized and 56% had completed the trial

- *Endpoints:* the sponsor's primary endpoints in both trials were a circadian-biomarker measure of "entrainment" (urinary aMT6s-derived circadian period τ); FDA rejected biomarker entrainment as the regulatory primary endpoint for SET and instead based its efficacy conclusion on a panel of clinical endpoints (LQ-nTST, UQ-dTSD, MoST, and CGI-C, combined by the sponsor into a step-down "Clinical Response" composite requiring entrainment plus an N24CRS score ≥3)

- *Primary analysis:* sponsor's ANCOVA (baseline covariate + treatment + a pooled-site factor) vs. the FDA reviewer's preferred permutation ANCOVA without the site factor, given the small sample size, non-normal distributions, heterogeneous variances, and randomization that was not actually stratified by site — *Permutation ANCOVA as an FDA-preferred alternative primary-analysis method for a small-N trial*

- *Multiplicity:* SET's sponsor-specified step-down sequence tested biomarker entrainment first, then the composite Clinical Response second; FDA's own substituted clinical-endpoint analyses (LQ-nTST, UQ-dTSD, MoST, CGI-C, dTSD) were explicitly conducted as post-hoc exploratory analyses without multiplicity adjustment

- *Missing data/bias:* the sponsor excluded 12 of 84 SET-randomized patients from its clinical-endpoint analysis via post-randomization data-completeness filters (Sponsor ITT n=78; Sponsor Analysis Population n=72); the FDA reviewer reran the clinical-endpoint analyses on all 84 randomized patients as a true intent-to-treat population

- *Regulatory:* a genuine, unresolved Agency-sponsor disagreement over the primary efficacy endpoint, analysis population, and analysis method for both trials, with FDA substituting its own clinical-endpoint-based analysis as the basis for approval — *FDA-substituted primary endpoint replacing a sponsor's proposed biomarker endpoint, following unresolved Agency-sponsor disagreement*; Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee met November 14, 2013

**Trial design & endpoints**

- SET Study (VP-VEC-162-3201): multicenter (US and Germany), randomized, double-masked, placebo-controlled, parallel-group; N=84 (42 tasimelteon/42 placebo), 62 (73.8%) completed. The primary endpoint and sample size changed twice by protocol amendment before the final design: originally powered on nighttime total sleep time (nTST) at N=160 (assumed mean difference 39 min, SD 66 min); Amendment 6 reduced this to N=100 (mean difference 30 min, SD 45 min); Amendment 9 (May 21, 2012) changed the primary endpoint entirely to circadian entrainment, finalizing at N=84. The SAP was signed off December 11, 2012, and the trial unblinded December 12, 2012

- Sponsor's primary endpoint (SET): entrainment of the circadian melatonin rhythm, measured via urinary aMT6s, defined as a post-baseline circadian period τ<24.1 hours with a 95% CI including 24.0; step-down secondary "Clinical Response" required entrainment plus an N24CRS (Non-24 Clinical Response Scale) score ≥3, a composite of four clinical measures of nighttime sleep, daytime nap duration, function, and clinical global impression of change (abbreviated by FDA's review as LQ-nTST, UQ-dTSD, MoST, and CGI-C)

- Sponsor's reported SET results: entrainment difference 17.4% (p=0.0171); Clinical Response difference 23.7% (p=0.0028)

- RESET Study (VP-VEC-162-3203): multicenter (US only), randomized-withdrawal, double-masked, placebo-controlled, parallel-group; N=20 (10/10), all completed. Phases: Pre-Randomization (open-label tasimelteon run-in, ~6 weeks, plus a τ-estimation period, ~6 weeks) then an 8-week Randomized Withdrawal Phase. Primary endpoint: proportion of patients becoming non-entrained (by aMT6s) after randomization to placebo vs. continued tasimelteon. Result: non-entrainment difference of −70.0% favoring continued tasimelteon (p=0.0026)

- Randomization was not stratified by site in either trial; the sponsor's ANCOVA nonetheless included a pooled-site factor, which the FDA reviewer considered inappropriate and dropped from its own permutation-ANCOVA reanalysis. Subgroup analyses (sex, race, age <50/≥50, country) were conducted for SET only, given RESET's small size (n=20); treatment-effect point estimates were directionally consistent across most subgroups, though not for non-white patients on some clinical endpoints (only 14 non-white patients were enrolled, not considered a meaningful signal by the reviewer)

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2014/205677Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label (original) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2014/205677s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Statistical Review and Evaluation, NDA 205677 (Reference ID 3409480; Division of Biometrics I; Statistical Reviewers Jingyu (Julia) Luan, Ph.D. and Kun Jin, Ph.D.; Concurring Reviewer H.M. James Hung, Ph.D.; Medical Division: Division of Neurology Products, medical reviewer Devanand Jillapalli, M.D., clinical team lead Ronald Farkas, M.D.) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/205677Orig1s000StatR.pdf

- FDA Summary Review (Reference ID 3440713) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/205677Orig1s000SumR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record, RESET Study — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01430754 — no protocol/SAP posted, same confirmation method

"Tasimelteon for non-24-hour sleep-wake disorder in totally blind people (SET and RESET): two multicentre, randomised, double-masked, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials." *Lancet.* 2015;386(10005):1754-1764. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(15)60031-9>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26466871/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Tasimelteon%20for%20non-24-hour%20sleep-wake%20disorder%20in%20totally%20blind%20people)

**Other resources**

- No trial-specific Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere participation was identified for Vanda Pharmaceuticals; not confirmed either way.

- FDA's Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee met November 14, 2013 to discuss Non-24 as a diagnostic entity and this application; the full vote tally was not independently confirmed from a primary source in this review.

- Tasimelteon (also known as VEC-162/BMS-214778) was originally developed by Bristol-Myers Squibb (IND filed 1997) and licensed to Vanda in 2004; it received Orphan Drug designation on January 9, 2010. Mechanism: dual melatonin receptor (MT1/MT2) agonist.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review and Evaluation, NDA 205677, Executive Summary, p.6]* — "For both Study 3201 and Study 3203, no agreement was reached between the Agency and the sponsor regarding the primary efficacy endpoint(s), analysis populations and analysis methods. The Agency has decided that the primary efficacy evaluation for tasimelteon should be based on the clinical endpoints."

**Reverse-engineered SAP** [inferred]

- [inferred] Given that FDA's own reanalysis explicitly labeled its substituted clinical-endpoint testing as "post-hoc exploratory analyses without multiplicity adjustment," and the review notes it is "unknown whether the overall type I error is properly controlled," approval most likely rested on a preponderance-of-evidence judgment across five nominally significant clinical endpoints rather than on a single, formally alpha-controlled confirmatory analysis — traced to the Statistical Review's Executive Summary discussion of its own substituted analysis (p.6-7).

- [inferred] RESET's very small sample size (N=20) and the absence of any covariate-adjustment discussion for its primary analysis in the material reviewed suggest its primary comparison of binary non-entrainment proportions was most likely a simple, unadjusted test (e.g., Fisher's exact test) rather than a regression-based method — consistent with the reviewer's stated rationale that subgroup analyses were run for SET only "because [Study] 3203 [is] too small."

### 11. Olodaterol (Striverdi Respimat) — NDA 203108

**Sponsor:** Boehringer Ingelheim Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Long-term, once-daily maintenance treatment of airflow obstruction in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), including chronic bronchitis and/or emphysema — not indicated for the relief of acute deteriorations of COPD

**Approval date:** July 31, 2014 (original NDA submitted May 14, 2012; not approved in the first review cycle because of an outstanding facility-inspection issue rather than an efficacy finding; resubmission approved 2014)

**Pivotal trial:** four replicate 48-week phase 3 trials — Study 1222.11 (NCT00782210) and Study 1222.12 (NCT00782509), placebo-controlled; Study 1222.13 (NCT00793624) and Study 1222.14 (NCT00796653), placebo- and active (formoterol)-controlled

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* four near-identical, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, multicenter, 48-week phase 3 trials run as two co-identical pairs — Studies 11/12 (placebo-controlled only) and Studies 13/14 (double-dummy, placebo- and active-controlled against open-label-comparator formoterol 12 mcg twice daily); stratified by background tiotropium use (and, for Studies 11/12, by country); two olodaterol doses studied (5 mcg and 10 mcg once daily via Respimat), only the 5 mcg dose ultimately approved

- *Endpoints:* co-primary endpoints FEV1 AUC0-3h response and trough FEV1 response at Week 12 (Studies 11/12) or Week 24 (Studies 13/14) from baseline; Studies 13/14 added a third co-primary endpoint, Mahler Transition Dyspnea Index (TDI) focal score at Week 24; key secondary endpoints St. George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ) total score and time to first COPD exacerbation

- *Primary analysis:* REML-based repeated-measures mixed model (Studies 11/12) or mixed model for repeated measures/MMRM (Studies 13/14), each specifying a spatial power covariance structure and Kenward-Rogers degrees of freedom, fit on the Full Analysis Set (FAS)

- *Multiplicity:* within each trial, a fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchy tested the olodaterol 10 mcg-vs-placebo comparisons ahead of the 5 mcg-vs-placebo comparisons, separately per co-primary endpoint; a separate cross-study secondary hierarchy (pooled Week-24 SGRQ for 10 mcg, then pooled exacerbation rate for 10 mcg, then for 5 mcg) was gated on all co-primary endpoints in Studies 13/14 first reaching significance

- *Missing data/bias:* patients discontinuing due to symptom worsening had post-discontinuation FEV1 values imputed via "least favorable observation carried forward" (LFOCF), which the FDA reviewer flagged as problematic for the MMRM analyses and supplemented with sensitivity analyses omitting this imputation

- *Regulatory:* original NDA not approved in the first review cycle owing to an outstanding facility-inspection issue, not an efficacy finding; Pulmonary-Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee met January 29, 2013 and voted 15-1-1 (yes/no/abstain) in favor of substantial evidence of efficacy, safety, and overall approvability

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Population: COPD, age ≥40, >10 pack-years smoking history, post-bronchodilator FEV1 ≤80% predicted, FEV1/FVC ≤70%; background inhaled corticosteroid, short-acting beta-agonist, or anticholinergic therapy permitted as needed

- Studies 11/12 (n≈208-217 per arm): olodaterol 5 mcg or 10 mcg vs. placebo, primary endpoints assessed at Week 12

- Studies 13/14 (n≈225-235 per arm): olodaterol 5 mcg or 10 mcg vs. placebo vs. formoterol 12 mcg twice daily (double-dummy design), primary endpoints assessed at Week 24; formoterol here is the European twice-daily formulation, not a US-marketed comparator

- Results (per FDA's statistical review): trough FEV1 benefit of approximately 65 mL at Week 12, statistically significant across all four trials; FEV1 AUC0-3h benefit of approximately 155 mL at Week 12 (approximately 122 mL for AUC0-12h in the two trials measuring it); no significant difference between the olodaterol 5 mcg and 10 mcg doses on any co-primary endpoint, consistent with only the 5 mcg dose being approved; SGRQ reached significance in only one of the two Studies 13/14, and even that trial's mean between-group reduction (3.15 points) fell short of the established 4.0-point minimal clinically important difference, a limitation the review states explicitly; no significant effect on exacerbation rate or on TDI focal score

- Safety signal discussed by the Advisory Committee: 4 cases of small-cell lung carcinoma, all occurring in the olodaterol 10 mcg arm (not the dose ultimately approved)

- Supportive crossover exercise-endurance substudies (not part of the core registration claims) showed statistically significant increases in exercise endurance time (~47 seconds) and inspiratory capacity (~130 mL) at isotime, but exercise/dyspnea benefit was not a sought indication

- Note: this NDA's four trials (Studies 11-14) are distinct from the later "TONADO 1/2" trials (NCT01431274/NCT01431287), which registered the fixed-dose combination tiotropium/olodaterol (Stiolto Respimat) under a separate submission — not part of this entry

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 203108, §3.1.2]* — the applicant's imputation method for FEV1 values following discontinuation due to symptom worsening, "least favorable observation carried forward" (LFOCF), was described by the FDA reviewer as "problematic when conducting MMRM analyses," prompting an FDA-added sensitivity analysis that omitted this imputation.

The remaining primary-analysis and multiplicity-structure detail below is paraphrased/reconstructed from the FDA Statistical Review rather than quoted verbatim, since no sponsor SAP/protocol is posted on ClinicalTrials.gov for any of the four trials:

- Primary analysis: REML-based repeated-measures mixed model (Studies 11/12) or MMRM (Studies 13/14), each specifying a spatial power covariance structure and Kenward-Rogers degrees of freedom, fit on the Full Analysis Set.

- Multiplicity: within each trial, a fixed-sequence hierarchy tested the olodaterol 10 mcg-vs-placebo comparisons before the 5 mcg-vs-placebo comparisons, separately for each co-primary endpoint (AUC0-3h, then trough FEV1, then — for Studies 13/14 — TDI); a separate cross-study secondary hierarchy (pooled Week-24 SGRQ for 10 mcg, then pooled exacerbation rate for 10 mcg, then for 5 mcg) was gated on all co-primary endpoints in Studies 13/14 first reaching significance.

### 12. Sulfur hexafluoride lipid microspheres (Lumason) — NDA 203684

**Sponsor:** Bracco Diagnostics Inc.

**Indication approved:** For use in patients with suboptimal echocardiograms, to opacify the left ventricular (LV) chamber and to improve delineation of the LV endocardial border (an ultrasound contrast agent, not a therapeutic drug). A 2016 supplement (NDA 203684/S-001) added contrast-enhanced ultrasound of the liver in adult and pediatric patients to characterize focal liver lesions; a separate 2016 supplement (S-002) added pediatric urinary-tract ultrasonography for suspected/known vesicoureteral reflux — both noted here for context but outside the scope of this entry's focus on the original echocardiography approval

**Approval date:** October 10, 2014 (original NDA submitted December 21, 2011; a first Complete Response Letter issued October 19, 2012 cited facility-inspection/compliance deficiencies, not efficacy; a second CRL followed in November 2013 requesting further compliance-related information; approved on the third review cycle, with statistical review content unchanged since the original 2012 review)

**Pivotal trial:** three confirmatory studies — BR1-019A, BR1-019B, and BR1-013 (no NCT numbers; conducted under the original NDA 21-315 submission in the 1990s-2000s, predating ClinicalTrials.gov registration), plus two supportive studies, BR1-011 and BR1-012

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* a paired, within-patient diagnostic-accuracy comparison (unenhanced/baseline image vs. contrast-enhanced image, read blind by independent off-site readers) layered on top of a randomized, active (Albunex)- and placebo (agitated saline)-controlled, multicenter, dose-ranging trial structure; FDA's review explicitly deprioritized the nominal active-comparator contrast in favor of the within-patient baseline-vs-enhanced comparison as the operative efficacy evidence — *Randomized active-controlled trial reanalyzed by FDA as a within-patient baseline-vs-enhanced paired diagnostic comparison, distinct from a single-arm paired diagnostic-accuracy design (extending the existing Keyword_Taxonomy.md "Diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison)" row)*

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint left ventricular endocardial border delineation (LVEBD), a 12-segment blinded-reader score (each segment scored 0/+1/+2, total range 0-24), compared pre- vs. post-contrast; secondary endpoint left ventricular opacification (LVO), a 4-point scale; exploratory endpoint accuracy of LVEF measurement against a reference standard (cardioangiography, nuclear angiography, or cardiac MRI) in a patient subset

- *Primary analysis:* paired t-test for the baseline-to-enhanced LVEBD change within each dose group; Wilcoxon rank-sum test for between-group (SonoVue vs. Albunex/control) LVO comparisons; Wilcoxon signed-rank test for within-patient paired SonoVue-vs-Albunex LVO comparisons

- *Missing data/bias:* no missing-data handling was specifically flagged in the FDA statistical review; the reviewer's principal caveat was a validity concern rather than a missing-data issue — LVEBD improvement did not correlate with improvement in LVEF-measurement accuracy against the reference standard

- *Regulatory:* two prior Complete Response Letters (2012, 2013) issued for facility-inspection/compliance reasons rather than efficacy findings, with the underlying statistical evidence unchanged across review cycles; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was identified for this NDA

**Trial design & endpoints**

- BR1-019A (n=76 SonoVue/67 Albunex, 11 centers) and BR1-019B (n=62/59, 10 centers): identically designed, single-blind (patient-blinded), parallel-group-plus-crossover dose-ranging studies, active-controlled (Albunex) and placebo-controlled (agitated saline), testing SonoVue at 0.5/1/2/4 mL doses

- BR1-013 (n=53, 6 centers): single-blind, randomized crossover design, SonoVue (1 mL, 2 mL) vs. Albunex (0.22 mL/kg)

- Supportive studies BR1-011 (n=215) and BR1-012 (n=437 per one reporting table in the FDA review, described differently elsewhere in the same document)

- Two to four independent, blinded, off-site readers scored all images per a prospectively defined blinded-read methodology

- Power: trials were powered at 80% to detect a mean LVEBD gain of at least 2 units (enhanced vs. baseline, BR1-011) or at least a 4-unit SonoVue-vs-Albunex LVO difference (BR1-013, BR1-019A/B)

- Results (per FDA's statistical review): baseline-to-enhanced LVEBD improvement reached p<0.001 for all four SonoVue doses across all readers; SonoVue-vs-Albunex/control LVO differences also reached p<0.001; the reviewer separately noted minimal improvement in LVEF-measurement accuracy over baseline and no correlation between LVEF accuracy and LVEBD score — a caveat on the surrogate nature of the primary endpoint relative to a clinically anchored accuracy measure

- FDA's reviewer explicitly set aside the SonoVue-vs-Albunex active-comparator analyses because Albunex was no longer in routine clinical use by the time of review, focusing the statistical evaluation on the within-patient baseline-vs-enhanced comparison instead

### 13. Pirfenidone (Esbriet) — NDA 22535

**Sponsor:** InterMune, Inc. (later acquired by Roche/Genentech, 2014)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), to reduce decline in lung function

**Approval date:** October 15, 2014 (original NDA submitted November 4, 2009; Complete Response Letter issued May 4, 2010 for lack of replicated efficacy evidence; resubmission, adding a third phase 3 trial, approved October 15, 2014 — the same day as nintedanib/Ofev, a different sponsor's competing IPF therapy)

**Pivotal trial:** ASCEND (Study PIPF-016), NCT01366209, and CAPACITY 1/CAPACITY 2 (Studies PIPF-006 and PIPF-004), NCT00287729 and NCT00287716

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* three randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multinational phase 3 trials — the two original CAPACITY trials (Study 004 and Study 006, 72-week treatment period, nearly identical design, submitted together in 2009) and ASCEND (Study 016, a 52-week trial added in the 2014 resubmission after a Complete Response Letter cited the CAPACITY program's lack of replicated efficacy) — *Approval program with a substantial proportion of negative/failed pivotal trials* (existing taxonomy term, since CAPACITY Study 006 was a genuine negative trial retained and reported alongside the two positive trials)

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint absolute change in percent-predicted FVC (post-bronchodilator) from baseline to Week 52 (ASCEND) or Week 72 (CAPACITY); key secondary endpoints (ASCEND only, formally multiplicity-controlled) progression-free survival (a composite of confirmed ≥10% absolute %predicted-FVC decline, confirmed ≥50-meter 6-minute-walk-test [6MWT] decline, or all-cause mortality) and change in 6MWT distance at Week 52; all-cause mortality was an unadjusted secondary/exploratory endpoint in all three trials, explicitly underpowered

- *Primary analysis:* rank ANCOVA (standardized-rank change in FVC as the outcome, standardized-rank baseline FVC as covariate, per Stokes et al. 2000), tested via the Mantel-Haenszel mean-score chi-square test, on the intent-to-treat population, at a two-sided alpha of 0.0498 (adjusted for two anticipated interim mortality analyses)

- *Multiplicity:* ASCEND used a Hochberg-based gatekeeping procedure — the primary endpoint had to reach significance at the 0.0498 level before the two key secondary endpoints (progression-free survival, 6MWT change) were tested, with a specific largest-p-value/second-p-value Hochberg step-up rule between the two; CAPACITY Studies 004/006 applied no formal multiplicity adjustment to secondary endpoints, consistent with their exploratory status in the original 2009 submission

- *Missing data/bias:* deaths were ranked as the worst outcome (ranked by shortest time-to-death as worst), and non-death missing data were imputed via a sum-of-squared-differences (SSD) nearest-neighbor method matching each missing patient to the 3 most similar complete patients at the same visit — *SSD nearest-neighbor imputation for missing continuous efficacy data in a rank-based analysis*; the FDA reviewer additionally ran ANCOVA-with-placebo-mean-imputation and random-coefficient-regression-without-imputation sensitivity analyses, all concordant with the primary result

- *Regulatory:* a Complete Response Letter (May 4, 2010) citing lack of replicated FVC efficacy between CAPACITY Study 004 (positive) and Study 006 (negative), and no demonstrated all-cause-mortality benefit; a March 9, 2010 Pulmonary-Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee (PADAC) meeting on the original NDA split 7-5 on substantial evidence of efficacy but voted 9-3 in favor of approval overall, a recommendation the Agency did not follow at that time; a post-hoc pooled all-cause-mortality analysis across all three trials (Studies 016+004+006) reached statistical significance (HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.31-0.87, p=0.011) even though no single trial was powered to show it

**Trial design & endpoints**

- CAPACITY Study 004 (n=174 pirfenidone 2403mg/d, 87 pirfenidone 1197mg/d, 174 placebo) and Study 006 (n=171 pirfenidone 2403mg/d, 173 placebo): nearly identical 72-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group phase 3 trials, conducted 2006-2008; ASCEND (Study 016, n=278/277) was a 52-week trial of the same design conducted 2011-2014, differing from CAPACITY mainly in treatment duration and in substituting "confirmed ≥50-meter 6MWT decline" for "confirmed ≥15% Hgb-corrected DLco decline" as a progression-free-survival component

- Eligibility (all three trials): confident clinical/radiographic IPF diagnosis (surgical lung biopsy only if diagnostically uncertain), %predicted FVC 50-90%, %predicted DLco 30-90%, 6MWT distance ≥150m; treatment escalated over 15 days to a maintenance dose of pirfenidone 2403 mg/day (three 267mg capsules three times daily)

- ASCEND primary-endpoint results (per FDA's statistical review, multiple analytic approaches, all p<0.001): applicant's rank-ANCOVA-with-SSD-imputation mean %predicted-FVC change was -3.7 (pirfenidone) vs. -6.6 (placebo), a difference of 2.9 points; FDA's sensitivity analyses (placebo-mean imputation; random-coefficient regression without imputation) produced treatment-effect estimates ranging from 2.8 to 4.8, all directionally and statistically consistent

- ASCEND progression-free-survival results: pirfenidone reduced the combined risk of disease progression or death by 43% relative to placebo (HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.43-0.77, p<0.001), driven mainly by the FVC-decline component (7% of pirfenidone patients vs. 18% of placebo patients had a confirmed ≥10% %predicted-FVC decline)

- ASCEND 6MWT results: applicant's rank-ANCOVA analysis found a 26.7-meter treatment difference favoring pirfenidone (p=0.036), but FDA's own sensitivity analysis with placebo-mean imputation lost statistical significance (difference 7.2 meters, p=0.302) — a genuine reviewer-documented fragility in this secondary endpoint

- All-cause mortality: ASCEND alone showed a nonsignificant trend favoring pirfenidone (11/278 vs. 20/277 deaths, HR 0.55, 95% CI 0.26-1.15, p=0.105); a post-hoc analysis pooling all-cause mortality across Studies 016, 004, and 006 (623 vs. 624 patients pooled ITT) reached statistical significance (22/623 vs. 42/624 deaths, HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.31-0.87, p=0.011) — explicitly framed by the reviewer as a post-hoc analysis conducted "to increase the power to detect difference if any," since none of the individual trials was adequately powered for mortality (even pooled, power to detect a 0.77 hazard ratio was under 20%)

- Reviewer's overall conclusion: Study 004 and Study 016 were each independently significant on the primary FVC endpoint; Study 006 was not (the specific non-replication that drove the 2010 CRL); progression-free survival was significant in Study 004 and Study 016 but not independently confirmed in Study 006; 6MWT change was significant in Study 006 and Study 016. The reviewer concluded that, taken across all three trials, "the overall package seems to provide substantial evidence on both primary and key secondary endpoints" — an explicit totality-of-evidence judgment built from partial, non-fully-replicated wins across three trials rather than clean replication in two independent trials

- The SAP was amended twice (March 12, 2012 and December 23, 2013), both before unblinding; the substantive change added ranked baseline DLco as a covariate in the 6MWT analysis model, based on a documented association between DLco and disease progression observed in the earlier CAPACITY trials

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review and Evaluation, NDA 22,535/0045, Executive Summary]* — "The applicant previously submitted two studies, 004 and 006, in 2009 but received Complete Response Letter (CRL) citing lack of replicated evidence for efficacy as only Study 004 demonstrated statistically significant treatment effect with respect to the primary endpoint, absolute change lung function after 72 weeks of treatment."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, quoting the Complete Response Letter of May 4, 2010]* — "The submitted data do not provide substantial evidence of efficacy of pirfenidone for the treatment of patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) to reduce the decline in lung function. The positive finding of forced vital capacity (FVC) in trial PIPF-004 was not replicated in trial PIPF-006... Mortality is the ideal primary endpoint in clinical trials in patients with IPF. The submitted data did not demonstrate a statistically significant benefit in all-cause mortality."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §2.1 Overview, describing the October 1, 2008 pre-NDA meeting]* — "The Division stated that mortality is the ideal primary endpoint in a study of IPF treatment... the efficacy of pirfenidone will not be based solely upon 'winning' on the primary endpoint of change in FVC, but also based on the totality of the data and what drives the primary endpoint."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §5, Summary and Conclusions]* — "with this evidence from the three studies, overall package seems to provide substantial evidence on both primary and key secondary endpoints."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, describing the primary analysis method]* — "The analysis of the primary endpoint was a rank ANCOVA, with a standardized rank change in FVC as the outcome and standardized rank baseline FVC as a covariate... The treatment effect was to be tested using the Mantel-Haenszel mean score chi-square test. The test of significance for the primary analysis of the primary efficacy outcome variable was to use a two-sided alpha of 0.0498; adjusting for two anticipated interim mortality analyses."

**Reverse-engineered SAP** [inferred]

- [inferred] The specific choice to add a 6MWT-based progression-free-survival component in ASCEND (replacing CAPACITY's DLco-decline component) most likely reflects the sponsor's effort to strengthen the composite endpoint's chances of reaching significance in a single confirmatory trial, following FDA's 2010 rejection of the CAPACITY program for non-replication — traced to the statistical review's explicit note that the composite definition changed between CAPACITY and ASCEND and that the sponsor's own rationale for adding baseline DLco to the 6MWT model (via SAP amendment) invoked a documented DLco-disease-progression association observed in the earlier trials.

### 14. Nintedanib (Ofev) — NDA 205832

**Sponsor:** Boehringer Ingelheim Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF)

**Approval date:** October 15, 2014 (approved on the first review cycle, no Complete Response Letter — the same day as pirfenidone/Esbriet, a different sponsor's competing IPF therapy, following years of parallel/competing IPF drug-development programs)

**Pivotal trial:** INPULSIS-1 (Study 1199.32), NCT01335464, and INPULSIS-2 (Study 1199.34), NCT01335477

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two identically designed, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, international phase 3 trials (INPULSIS-1, n=309 nintedanib/206 placebo; INPULSIS-2, n=331/220), nintedanib 150mg twice daily vs. placebo over 52 weeks, randomized 3:2, plus a supportive phase 2 dose-ranging trial (Study 1199.30); IPF diagnosis confirmed by central HRCT review with or without biopsy

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint annual rate of decline in forced vital capacity (FVC, mL/year) from baseline to Week 52; pre-specified fixed-sequence key secondary endpoints, time to first acute IPF exacerbation, then St. George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ) total score change

- *Primary analysis:* random-coefficient (random-intercept, random-slope) linear regression model with an unstructured/variance-components covariance structure, fit on observed cases without missing-data imputation, on the Treated Set (all randomized patients receiving ≥1 dose)

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing — FVC decline tested first, then time-to-first-acute-exacerbation, then SGRQ change, each gated on the prior endpoint reaching significance, applied independently within each trial

- *Missing data/bias:* no formal imputation for missing FVC assessments — each patient's own declining slope is implicitly extrapolated by the random-coefficient model; FDA's earlier (2010 End-of-Phase-2) review had flagged the missing-at-random assumption underlying this approach and requested pattern-mixture-model sensitivity analyses

- *Regulatory:* approved on the first review cycle (no CRL), the same day (October 15, 2014) as pirfenidone/Esbriet for the same indication; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was identified in the documents reviewed

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Population: IPF confirmed by central HRCT review with or without surgical lung biopsy; age ≥40, diagnosis within ≤5 years, %predicted FVC ≥50%, %predicted DLCO 30-79%

- INPULSIS-1 (1199.32, n=309/206) and INPULSIS-2 (1199.34, n=331/220): randomized 3:2 nintedanib 150mg twice daily vs. placebo, over 52 weeks

- Primary-endpoint results: INPULSIS-1 annual FVC-decline rate -114.7 mL/year (nintedanib) vs. -239.9 mL/year (placebo), a difference of approximately 125 mL/year (p<0.001); INPULSIS-2 also reached significance (p<0.001); FDA's own reanalysis concurred with the applicant's results in both trials

- Key secondary endpoint (acute exacerbation) — discordant between the two trials: INPULSIS-2 hazard ratio 0.38 (95% CI 0.19-0.77), 12/331 (3.6%) nintedanib vs. 21/220 (9.6%) placebo, p=0.005 — significant, unlocking SGRQ testing for that trial (SGRQ change, analyzed via a mixed model for repeated measures, also significant, p<0.001); INPULSIS-1 hazard ratio 1.15 (95% CI 0.54-2.42), 19/309 (6.1%) vs. 11/206 (5.4%), not significant — per the pre-specified hierarchy, SGRQ was therefore not formally tested for INPULSIS-1, since that trial's gate was not met

- Pooled all-cause mortality across all three studies (1199.32 + 1199.34 + 1199.30) showed a numerical trend favoring nintedanib but did not reach statistical significance; FDA's Executive Summary frames all-cause mortality as "the primary endpoint of interest in patients with IPF" from a clinical standpoint, even though it was not the formal regulatory primary endpoint

- Regulatory history: IND opened 2007 with the Division of Pulmonary, Allergy and Rheumatology Products; a December 2007 Pre-IND meeting flagged the slope-analysis plan and the need for multiplicity/missing-data justification; a December 2010 End-of-Phase-2 meeting found the primary/key-secondary endpoints reasonable and requested a pre-specified covariance structure; Orphan Drug Designation was granted June 2011, Fast Track designation May 2013; an August 2013 Type C meeting recommended an event-driven mortality analysis and discussed pattern-mixture-model sensitivity analyses for missing data. NDA submitted May 2, 2014; approved October 15, 2014 on the first review cycle

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review and Evaluation, NDA 205832, Executive Summary]* — all-cause mortality, though not the formal regulatory primary endpoint, is described as "the primary endpoint of interest in patients with IPF" from a clinical perspective.

The remaining primary-analysis and multiplicity-structure detail below is paraphrased/reconstructed from the FDA Statistical Review rather than quoted verbatim, since no sponsor SAP/protocol is posted on ClinicalTrials.gov for either trial:

- Primary analysis: random-coefficient (random-intercept, random-slope) linear regression model for the annual rate of FVC decline, fit on observed cases without imputation, on the Treated Set.

- Multiplicity: a fixed-sequence hierarchy tested FVC decline first, then time-to-first-acute-exacerbation, then SGRQ change, each gated on the prior endpoint's significance, applied independently within each trial — accounting for the discordant secondary-endpoint results between INPULSIS-1 and INPULSIS-2 (SGRQ was formally tested only for INPULSIS-2, whose acute-exacerbation gate was met).

### 15. Deoxycholic acid (Kybella) — NDA 206333

**Sponsor:** Kythera Biopharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Improvement in the appearance of moderate to severe convexity or fullness associated with submental fat (the "double chin") in adults

**Approval date:** April 29, 2015

**Pivotal trial:** REFINE-1 (Study 22), NCT01542034, and REFINE-2 (Study 23), NCT01546142

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter phase 3 trials (Study 22, n=506: 256 deoxycholic acid/250 placebo; Study 23, n=516: 258/258) in adults 18-65 with clinician- and patient-reported submental-fat severity scores of 2-3 (moderate-severe); up to 6 treatment sessions (up to 50 injections of 0.2 mL each on a 1-cm grid) at 4-week intervals; two earlier European "supportive" phase 3 trials (Studies 16 and 17) used different dose concentrations and a different primary-endpoint definition and are distinct from the two US pivotal trials

- *Endpoints:* two co-primary endpoints, both required to reach significance — (1) at least a 1-grade improvement on both a clinician-reported (CR-SMFRS) and a patient-reported (PR-SMFRS) submental-fat rating scale at 12 weeks post-last-treatment, and (2) at least a 2-grade improvement on both scales at the same timepoint; secondary endpoints an MRI-assessed responder rate (≥10% submental-fat-volume reduction, in a patient subset) and change in the Patient-Reported Submental Fat Impact Scale (PR-SMFIS) total score

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by analysis center, for each co-primary endpoint

- *Multiplicity:* both co-primary endpoints (1-grade and 2-grade composite responder rates) were required to reach significance; multiplicity across secondary endpoints was controlled via Holm's method

- *Missing data/bias:* the primary approach was multiple imputation (a logistic-regression model using baseline/last-known CR-SMFRS/PR-SMFRS as core variables); the FDA reviewer independently reconstructed last-observation-carried-forward (LOCF) analyses because the applicant's dataset did not adequately account for missing data, and compared observed-case, multiple-imputation, and two LOCF variants as sensitivity analyses

- *Regulatory:* Study 22 (REFINE-1) was conducted under a Special Protocol Assessment (SPA agreement issued December 16, 2011); FDA agreed on the trial design and the 2-grade co-primary endpoint but explicitly did not agree that the 1-grade endpoint was adequate as a co-primary — the sponsor retained it as a co-primary regardless, and both ultimately reached statistical significance in both trials; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was identified for this NDA

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Population: adults 18-65 with moderate-to-severe submental fat (CR-SMFRS/PR-SMFRS scores of 2-3) and a stable body-weight history

- Results (both studies, all p<0.001 vs. placebo): Study 22 — 2-grade responders 13.4% (deoxycholic acid) vs. <0.1% (placebo); 1-grade responders 70.0% vs. 18.6%; MRI responders 46.0% vs. 5.3%; PR-SMFIS least-squares-mean change -3.61 vs. -1.10. Study 23 — 2-grade 18.6% vs. 3.0%; 1-grade 66.5% vs. 22.2%; MRI 40.5% vs. 5.2%; PR-SMFIS -3.44 vs. -1.46

- Regulatory history: Guidance meeting August 19, 2009; End-of-Phase-2 meeting April 20, 2011; SPA request November 4, 2011, SPA agreement December 16, 2011; Pre-NDA meeting November 13, 2013; NDA submitted May 13, 2014, PDUFA date May 13, 2015, standard review, approved April 29, 2015

- Two earlier European "supportive" phase 3 trials (Study 16, n=363; Study 17, n=360) used different concentrations (0.5%/1%) and a different primary-endpoint combination (1-grade CR-SMFRS plus a separate Subject Self-Rating Scale ≥4) and are distinct from the two US pivotal registrational trials; they were not the basis for FDA's efficacy conclusion

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

No verbatim-quoted passage from either a genuine sponsor SAP/protocol or the FDA Statistical Review was captured for this entry; the design, endpoint, and analysis-method detail described above (co-primary CMH tests, Holm's-method secondary-endpoint control, and the SPA history) is paraphrased/reconstructed from the FDA Statistical Review and Evaluation, NDA 206333, rather than quoted verbatim, since no sponsor SAP/protocol is posted on ClinicalTrials.gov for either pivotal trial.

**Reverse-engineered SAP** [inferred]

- [inferred] Because both co-primary endpoints (1-grade and 2-grade composite responder rates) reached statistical significance in both REFINE-1 and REFINE-2, FDA's SPA-stage disagreement over whether the 1-grade endpoint alone was an adequate primary endpoint was never tested against an actual discordant result — it remains unclear from public documents how FDA would have resolved approval if only the 2-grade endpoint, and not the 1-grade endpoint, had reached significance.

- [inferred] The consistent responder-rate pattern across both co-primary endpoints and the MRI-volume secondary endpoint (all favoring deoxycholic acid by a wide margin in both trials) suggests the primary analysis population was very likely the full intent-to-treat/randomized population with multiple imputation for the small fraction of missing 12-week assessments, consistent with a typical aesthetic-dermatology registration-trial design of this era, rather than a completer-only or per-protocol population.

### 16. Flibanserin (Addyi) — NDA 22526

**Sponsor:** Sprout Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (originally developed by Boehringer Ingelheim)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of acquired, generalized hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD) in premenopausal women

**Approval date:** August 18, 2015 (following two prior Complete Response Letters — August 27, 2010, to original sponsor Boehringer Ingelheim, and September 27, 2013, to Sprout Pharmaceuticals, which had acquired the drug in 2012)

**Pivotal trial:** VIOLET (Study 511.71), NCT00360529; DAISY (Study 511.75), NCT00360555; BEGONIA (Study 511.147), NCT00996164; and a 48-week randomized-withdrawal trial (Study 511.74), NCT00277914; plus the dedicated alcohol-interaction pharmacodynamic study SPR-12-03

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* multiple randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter phase 3 trials in premenopausal women with DSM-IV-TR generalized acquired HSDD (VIOLET, 3 arms: placebo/50mg/100mg; DAISY, 4 arms: placebo/25mg BID/50mg BID/100mg uptitration; BEGONIA, added after the first CRL), plus a 48-week randomized-withdrawal trial (511.74) and a separate 5-way crossover alcohol-interaction pharmacodynamic study (SPR-12-03) in healthy volunteers

- *Endpoints:* two pre-specified co-primary endpoints across all main efficacy trials — change from baseline to Week 24 in FSFI© desire-domain score, and change in the number of satisfying sexual events (SSE) per 28 days via eDiary

- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA adjusting for center and baseline value (Wilcoxon rank-sum used where normality assumptions failed); a Hochberg-type step-up procedure controlled multiplicity across the two co-primary endpoints in the North American trials, while the European trial (511.77) used a hierarchical testing plan instead

- *Multiplicity:* Hochberg step-up procedure for the two co-primary endpoints (North American trials); hierarchical testing (511.77, Europe, not significant even on the SSE endpoint); post-hoc responder-analysis and receiver-operating-characteristic (ROC)-based threshold analyses were later applied across all three main phase 3 trials to support the 2015 resubmission

- *Missing data/bias:* not separately detailed in the material reviewed for this entry

- *Regulatory:* two Complete Response Letters (August 27, 2010, to Boehringer Ingelheim; September 27, 2013, to Sprout Pharmaceuticals), a denied Formal Dispute Resolution Request appeal (February 7, 2014), two FDA Advisory Committee meetings (June 18, 2010, voting 11-0 against approval; June 4, 2015 joint Bone, Reproductive and Urologic Drugs Advisory Committee/Drug Safety and Risk Management Advisory Committee meeting, voting 18-6 in favor of approval with a REMS), and a Division Director approval that explicitly overrode the clinical review team's non-approval recommendation — *Statistical reviewer's non-approval recommendation overruled by division leadership* (existing taxonomy term)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- VIOLET (511.71) and DAISY (511.75): North American, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials in premenopausal women with generalized acquired HSDD (FSDS-R≥15 at screening), each reaching statistical significance on the SSE co-primary endpoint but not on the FSFI-desire co-primary endpoint — the specific deficiency underlying FDA's first (2010) non-approval decision, since both trials failed the pre-specified requirement that both co-primary endpoints reach significance

- The European trial (511.77), supportive only, did not reach significance even on the SSE endpoint; a 48-week randomized-withdrawal trial (511.74) was the only trial from the original submission fully positive across both endpoints

- BEGONIA (511.147): a new phase 3 trial added by Sprout after the first CRL, using the same instrument suite (SSE, FSFI-desire, FSDS-R item 13 distress score)

- The 2015 resubmission included no new efficacy trial data, but added post-hoc, ROC-based responder/Patient-Global-Impression-anchored analyses across all three main phase 3 trials (VIOLET, DAISY, BEGONIA), finding a "modest statistically significant treatment benefit" in all three studies, with responder-rate differences of approximately 9-15 percentage points between flibanserin and placebo across the SSE, FSFI-desire, and FSDS-R item 13 endpoints

- Alcohol-interaction study SPR-12-03: a randomized, double-blind, single-dose, 5-way crossover design in 25 healthy moderate drinkers (23 men, 2 premenopausal women — an enrollment imbalance later criticized by FDA's own clinical review team despite an FDA recommendation to enroll only or predominantly women), testing flibanserin alone and with ethanol 0.4 g/kg or 0.8 g/kg; flibanserin alone caused somnolence in 67% (16/24) of subjects, rising to 74%/92% with 0.4/0.8 g/kg ethanol; 6 of 25 subjects (24%) experienced syncope or symptomatic hypotension requiring medical intervention (ammonia salts, supine/Trendelenburg positioning), including one witnessed syncope event with blood pressure 83/49 mmHg

- FDA's Cross-Discipline Team Leader and clinical reviewers recommended non-approval based on this study, citing its predominantly male enrollment as inadequate to characterize risk in the actual (female) target population; Sprout's Formal Dispute Resolution Request appealing the resulting second CRL was denied by the Office of New Drugs on February 7, 2014

- The 2015 resubmission added a simulated-driving study and two CYP2C9/CYP2C19 clinical-pharmacology studies, but no new efficacy trial

- June 4, 2015 joint meeting of the Bone, Reproductive and Urologic Drugs Advisory Committee and the Drug Safety and Risk Management Advisory Committee: single question on overall benefit-risk profile — 0 votes for approval on labeling alone, 18 votes for approval with a REMS, 6 votes against approval, the latter citing continued concern over the alcohol interaction

- Division Director Hylton V. Joffe, M.D., signed the Summary Review approving the application on August 18, 2015, explicitly acknowledging the clinical review team's continued non-approval recommendation and the drug's public controversy (including the sponsor's ties to the "Even the Score" advocacy campaign) before giving his own approval rationale, centered on the Advisory Committee's benefit-risk vote and the REMS program

- No trial-specific Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere participation was confirmed for Sprout Pharmaceuticals or Valeant Pharmaceuticals (which acquired Sprout approximately one day after FDA approval, in a deal publicly reported at roughly $1 billion).

- REMS structure at approval: FDA determined a REMS was necessary under FDCA Section 505-1 for the alcohol-interaction hypotension/syncope risk, concluding a Medication Guide and communication plan alone were insufficient; the REMS required prescriber and pharmacy certification, with training to counsel patients on the alcohol-interaction risk, plus an implementation system to monitor certification compliance. Four postmarketing requirements were imposed: three dedicated alcohol-interaction trials in women aged 18-44 (varying alcohol quantity, timing relative to dosing, and "typical real-world use"), and a maternal-fetal outcome/pregnancy registry study.

- A non-clinical signal (mouse mammary tumor findings of unknown clinical significance) was addressed through labeling (Warnings and Precautions plus the Animal Toxicology section) rather than a required epidemiology study, after FDA's Division of Epidemiology identified "major feasibility and methodological issues" with such a study.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 022526, 2010 Executive Summary]* — "the evidence submitted with this application does not support the efficacy of flibanserin... I base my conclusion primarily on the finding that the two major Phase 3 studies... failed to achieve statistical significance on both pre-specified co-primary endpoints."

*[verbatim, FDA Cross-Discipline Team Leader / Medical Review, discussing Study SPR-12-03]* — "Despite FDA's recommendation that the study enroll only women or at least have a pre-specified minimum number of women... Study SPR-12-03 enrolled predominantly male subjects (23 of 25)... this NDA should not be approved" until a dedicated study in women was conducted.

**Reverse-engineered SAP** [inferred]

- [inferred] Because both VIOLET and DAISY reached significance on the SSE co-primary endpoint but not the FSFI-desire co-primary endpoint, and because FDA's 2010 non-approval rested specifically on the requirement that both co-primary endpoints succeed, the original SAP most likely specified a strict "both-must-win" co-primary structure (not a Hochberg-type step-up or hierarchical rule that would let one endpoint substitute for the other) for the North American phase 3 program at that time — traced to the Statistical Review's 2010 Executive Summary language quoted above.

- [inferred] The shift, by the 2015 resubmission, to post-hoc ROC-based responder analyses and Patient-Global-Impression-anchored thresholds across all three main trials suggests the sponsor's analytic approach was substantively reframed after the second CRL to present the same underlying continuous-endpoint data as responder/threshold-based evidence, likely because the original continuous-endpoint co-primary analyses had already been reviewed unfavorably twice — traced to the Statistical Review's description of these analyses as newly conducted for the 2015 cycle.

### 17. Sugammadex (Bridion) — NDA 22225

**Sponsor:** Merck Sharp & Dohme Corp. (originally developed by N.V. Organon, later Schering-Plough, acquired by Merck in 2009)

**Indication approved:** Reversal of neuromuscular blockade induced by rocuronium bromide or vecuronium bromide in adults undergoing surgery

**Approval date:** December 15, 2015 (original NDA submitted by Organon in October 2007; a Not Approvable letter issued July 31, 2008 and a Complete Response Letter issued September 20, 2013 preceded final approval)

**Pivotal trial:** Study 301 (shallow block, Europe), Study 302 (profound block, US), Study 310 (shallow block, Europe), and Study 303 ("immediate" reversal, US/Canada) — no NCT numbers identified (conducted 2005-2006, predating this sponsor's routine ClinicalTrials.gov registration practice)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* four randomized, active-controlled (neostigmine), multicenter phase 3 trials in adults undergoing elective surgery with rocuronium- or vecuronium-induced neuromuscular blockade, spanning shallow block (Studies 301, 310), profound block (Study 302), and immediate reversal 3 minutes after rocuronium administration (Study 303); a supportive later trial (Study 194334) in elective open abdominal surgery; a dedicated bleeding/coagulation safety trial (Study P07038) in major orthopedic surgery patients on thromboprophylaxis; and a dedicated hypersensitivity trial (Study P101/MK-8616-101), a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, repeated-dose (3 periods) trial in healthy volunteers

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint time to recovery of the train-of-four (TOF) ratio to 0.9 (Studies 301/302/310) or time to recovery of T1 to 0.1 (Study 303, immediate-reversal scenario); Study P07038's primary safety endpoint was adjudicated major/non-major unanticipated bleeding onset within 24 hours; Study P101's primary safety endpoint was the incidence of hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis reactions

- *Primary analysis:* not further specified in the material reviewed beyond the reported time-to-recovery point estimates (see below) and, for Study P07038, a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel-stratified relative risk (stratified by renal function and antithrombotic type)

- *Missing data/bias:* Study 194334's secondary time-to-recovery endpoint used a worst-case (sugammadex)/best-case (neostigmine) imputation approach; its primary binary TOF-ratio endpoint used a 5th/95th-percentile imputation method

- *Regulatory:* a 2008 Not Approvable letter (inadequate characterization of hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis risk, especially on repeat exposure, and inadequate evaluation of effects on coagulation) and a 2013 Complete Response Letter (a routine site inspection found protocol deviations undermining the reliability of the sponsor's first hypersensitivity trial, Study P06042, while the coagulation deficiency had been resolved); a new hypersensitivity trial (P101) was required and completed before the final resubmission; the Anesthetic and Analgesic Drug Products Advisory Committee met November 6, 2015 and voted 14-0 that the risk-benefit profile supported approval

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 301 (Europe, shallow block, 2 mg/kg, N=196): time to TOF ratio 0.9 of 1:29 min (rocuronium)/2:48 min (vecuronium) for sugammadex vs. 18:30/16:48 min for neostigmine (p<0.0001 for each)

- Study 302 (US, profound block, 4 mg/kg, N=182): 2:52 min (rocuronium)/4:28 min (vecuronium) vs. 50:22/66:12 min (p<0.0001)

- Study 310 (Europe, shallow block, 2 mg/kg, N=84): 2:02 min vs. 8:46 min (p<0.0001)

- Study 303 (US/Canada, immediate reversal 3 minutes post-rocuronium, 16 mg/kg, N=115): time to T1 ratio 0.1 of 4:22 min vs. 7:04 min (p<0.0001)

- Study 194334 (10 US centers, elective open abdominal surgery, randomized/active-controlled/safety-assessor-blinded): primary endpoint TOF ratio <0.9 at extubation (binary, chi-square test, 5th/95th-percentile imputation for missing data); secondary time-to-recovery endpoint analyzed via ANOVA with worst-case/best-case imputation

- Study P07038 (bleeding safety, randomized, sugammadex vs. usual-care/neostigmine, major orthopedic surgery patients on heparin/low-molecular-weight-heparin thromboprophylaxis): major/non-major unanticipated bleeding within 24 hours occurred in 2.9% (sugammadex) vs. 4.1% (usual care), relative risk 0.70 (95% CI 0.38-1.29) — no increased bleeding risk identified, resolving the coagulation deficiency from the 2008 Not Approvable letter

- Study P101 (final hypersensitivity trial, N=375 healthy volunteers, 3 arms: sugammadex 4 mg/kg, 16 mg/kg, placebo): 137 suspected hypersensitivity events occurred in 94 of 299 sugammadex-exposed subjects (all-subjects-treated population: placebo 76, 4 mg/kg 151, 16 mg/kg 148); one confirmed anaphylaxis case (0.33%, 1/299), occurring on first exposure in the 16 mg/kg arm; a dose-response relationship was observed for erythema, pruritus, urticaria, nausea, sneezing, and vomiting, with no clear increase on repeated exposure

- FDA's Division of Pulmonary, Allergy and Rheumatology Products, consulted on the hypersensitivity data, concluded that sugammadex causes anaphylaxis and hypersensitivity events, that this risk increases with higher doses, and that it does not appear to increase with repeated exposure

- During the final review cycle, FDA's Office of Scientific Investigations found a potential unblinding episode among sponsor statisticians (March-April 2014) and inspected all six Study P101 sites (4 rated No Action Indicated, 2 Voluntary Action Indicated for minor findings); the data were still judged reliable and valid

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2015/022225Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2015/022225lbl.pdf

- FDA Statistical Review, NDA 022225 (combined multi-review-cycle document, including the original efficacy review, a bleeding/coagulation-safety supplement review by Qing Xu, Ph.D., Division of Biometrics V, consulting the Division of Hematology Products, and a later efficacy-supplement review by Yan Zhou, Ph.D., Division of Biometrics II, Division of Anesthesia, Analgesia, and Addiction Products) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/022225Orig1s000StatR.pdf

- FDA Summary Review (combined document spanning all three review cycles: 2008 Not Approvable, 2013 Complete Response, and 2015 approval) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/022225Orig1s000SumR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov records — Study P06042 (superseded hypersensitivity trial): https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00988065 ; Study P101 (final hypersensitivity trial): https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02028065 — neither has a posted protocol/SAP; the four original efficacy pivotal trials (301/302/303/310), conducted 2005-2006, predate ClinicalTrials.gov registration and no NCT numbers were identified

- Pivotal publication (Study 302): Jones RK, Caldwell JE, Brull SJ, Soto RG. "Reversal of profound rocuronium-induced blockade with sugammadex: a randomized comparison with neostigmine." *Anesthesiology.* 2008;109(5):816-824. - Related program publication (same investigator group/era, not one of the four core pivotal studies by number): Sacan O, White PF, Tufanogullari B, Klein K. "Sugammadex reversal of rocuronium-induced neuromuscular blockade: a comparison with neostigmine-glycopyrrolate and edrophonium-atropine." *Anesth Analg.* 2007;104(3):569-574. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1213/ane.0b013e31818a9932), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19224792/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=The%20effect%20of%20residual%20neuromuscular%20blockade%20on%20the%20speed%20of%20reversal%20with%20sugammadex)

- No independently PubMed-verified publication was identified specifically for Studies 301, 310, or 303 by their FDA-review study numbers in the time available for this research pass; the 2008 FDA Summary Review's results table is the best public source for those three studies' exact results

**Other resources**

- Merck is a founding member of the YODA Project (Yale University), a general trial-data-sharing initiative; whether Bridion/sugammadex trial-level data are specifically listed on YODA's platform was not independently confirmed in this review.

- The Anesthetic and Analgesic Drug Products Advisory Committee met November 6, 2015: voted 13-1 that there was sufficient information on hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis risk, 14-0 that there was sufficient information on cardiac dysrhythmia risk, and 14-0 that the overall risk-benefit profile supported approval.

- No boxed warning was added to the label at approval; anaphylaxis/hypersensitivity is addressed as a Warnings and Precautions item, consistent with the Advisory Committee's "sufficient information" votes.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

No verbatim-quoted passage from a genuine sponsor SAP/protocol was captured for this entry (none of the four core pivotal trials has a ClinicalTrials.gov record); the design, endpoint, and results detail described above is paraphrased/reconstructed from the FDA Statistical Review and Summary Review rather than quoted verbatim.

**Reverse-engineered SAP** [inferred]

- [inferred] Given that all four pivotal efficacy trials reported time-to-recovery as a direct point-estimate comparison (sugammadex vs. neostigmine) with p<0.0001 in each case, and given the era (2005-2006) and typical practice for small anesthesiology reversal-agent trials of this kind, the primary analysis most likely used a simple parametric or log-transformed t-test/ANOVA on time-to-recovery rather than a Cox/survival-analytic method, since every subject in these trials reaches the recovery event (TOF ratio 0.9 or T1 ratio 0.1) with no meaningful censoring expected in a routine post-surgical reversal setting.

- [inferred] The 2008 Not Approvable letter's twin deficiencies (hypersensitivity characterization and coagulation effects) imply the original SAP/protocol package did not pre-specify a dedicated hypersensitivity-surveillance or bleeding-safety endpoint of the rigor FDA ultimately required — traced to the fact that both deficiencies were resolved only by two entirely new, purpose-built trials (P101 and P07038) added after the original submission, rather than by a reanalysis of the original efficacy trials' existing safety data.

### 18. Lesinurad (Zurampic) — NDA 207988

**Sponsor:** Ardea Biosciences, Inc. (a wholly owned subsidiary of AstraZeneca)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of hyperuricemia associated with gout, in combination with a xanthine oxidase inhibitor, in patients who have not achieved target serum uric acid levels with a xanthine oxidase inhibitor alone — not indicated as monotherapy

**Approval date:** December 22, 2015

**Pivotal trial:** CLEAR 1 (Study 302), NCT01493531; CLEAR 2 (Study 301), NCT01510158; and CRYSTAL (Study 304), NCT01510769

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* three randomized, double-blind, multicenter, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials — CLEAR 1 (US) and CLEAR 2 (multinational), each randomizing gout patients with an inadequate response to allopurinol 1:1:1 to lesinurad 200mg+allopurinol, lesinurad 400mg+allopurinol, or placebo+allopurinol for 12 months, stratified by renal function and baseline tophus status; and CRYSTAL, an equivalent 3-arm design in tophaceous-gout patients on background febuxostat instead of allopurinol, stratified by renal function and baseline serum uric acid level

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint proportion of patients achieving serum uric acid <6.0 mg/dL (CLEAR 1/2) or <5.0 mg/dL (CRYSTAL, reflecting its tophaceous-gout population) at Month 6; key secondary endpoints gout flare rate and tophus resolution, tested in all three trials

- *Primary analysis:* intent-to-treat population with non-responder imputation for missing Month-6 serum-uric-acid values; each dose tested against placebo with 97.5% confidence intervals, consistent with a two-dose alpha-split (each dose vs. placebo at half-alpha)

- *Multiplicity:* two doses (200mg, 400mg) each independently tested against placebo per trial; only the 200mg dose was ultimately approved

- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation (NRI) was the pre-specified approach for the primary serum-uric-acid endpoint

- *Regulatory:* the sponsor-proposed 400mg dose was not approved because of a renal-safety signal (elevated serum creatinine, acute renal failure, and a numerically higher rate of major adverse cardiovascular events at 400mg vs. 200mg vs. placebo); the FDA Arthritis Advisory Committee met October 23, 2015, voting 14-0 that efficacy was demonstrated, 7-6-1 on whether safety was adequately characterized, and 10-4 that the overall risk-benefit profile supported approval — *Surrogate-endpoint approval despite uniform failure of all key clinical secondary endpoints across the full pivotal program*

**Trial design & endpoints**

- CLEAR 1 (Study 302) and CLEAR 2 (Study 301): gout patients with serum uric acid ≥6.5 mg/dL, at least 2 flares in the prior year, and an inadequate response to allopurinol; randomized 1:1:1 to lesinurad 200mg+allopurinol, lesinurad 400mg+allopurinol, or placebo+allopurinol for 12 months

- CRYSTAL (Study 304): equivalent design in tophaceous-gout patients on background febuxostat 80mg instead of allopurinol, stratified by renal function and baseline serum uric acid level (all patients had tophi, an enrichment feature)

- Primary-endpoint results: CLEAR 1 and CLEAR 2 (allopurinol combination) succeeded at both the 200mg and 400mg doses vs. placebo. CRYSTAL's primary endpoint (febuxostat combination) failed at the to-be-marketed 200mg dose — per FDA's statistical review, "patients assigned to receive LESU 200 did not show statistically greater improvement in pre-defined sUA responder rate than patients assigned to receive placebo" — with only the unapproved 400mg dose showing benefit in that trial

- Key secondary endpoints (gout flare rate, tophus resolution): per FDA's statistical review, "no statistically significant benefits of LESU over placebo were identified for any of the key secondary efficacy endpoints, gout flare and tophi resolution, in any study or at any dose" — approval rested entirely on the serum-uric-acid surrogate endpoint, not on any clinical secondary endpoint

- Renal and cardiovascular safety (integrated phase 3 add-on studies, per FDA's benefit-risk memo): renal-related on-treatment adverse events occurred in 4.5% (placebo), 5.7% (lesinurad 200mg), and 11.8% (lesinurad 400mg) of patients; serum creatinine ≥1.5× baseline occurred in 2.3%/5.7%/14.3%; serum creatinine ≥2.0× baseline occurred in 0%/1.8%/6.7%; major adverse cardiovascular event incidence per 100 person-years was 0.7/1.0/1.9 (incidence rate ratio vs. placebo 1.4 [95% CI 0.2-9.3] for 200mg, 2.7 [0.7-16.0] for 400mg); deaths per 100 person-years were 0/0.5/0.9. FDA's benefit-risk reviewer concluded "there is general agreement between FDA and the applicant that the benefit-risk profile for lesinurad 400 mg is not favorable," while cautioning that even the 200mg dose showed numerical imbalances in the same direction

- The label carries a boxed warning: "RISK OF ACUTE RENAL FAILURE, MORE COMMON WHEN USED WITHOUT A XANTHINE OXIDASE INHIBITOR," reinforcing that the approved indication is combination therapy only, not monotherapy

- No REMS was ultimately required; the sponsor's risk-management plan used a Medication Guide, a communication plan, and routine pharmacovigilance surveillance instead

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2015/207988lbl.pdf
