### 34. Gadopiclenol (Elucirem) — NDA 216986

**Sponsor:** Guerbet Group, France (Guerbet LLC in the US)

**Indication approved:** Use with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in adults and children 2 years of age and older to detect and visualize lesions with abnormal vascularity in the central nervous system (brain, spine, and associated tissues) and the body (head and neck, thorax, abdomen, pelvis, and musculoskeletal system) — a macrocyclic, high-relaxivity gadolinium-based contrast agent (GBCA) approved at half the standard gadolinium dose (0.05 mmol/kg) of most other GBCAs

**Approval date:** September 21, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** GDX-44-010 (PICTURE), NCT03996447 (CNS), and GDX-44-011 (PROMISE), NCT03986138 (body/non-CNS)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two prospective, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, crossover phase 3 diagnostic-accuracy trials — Diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison) (every subject imaged pre-contrast, then paired pre-/post-contrast with gadopiclenol, and, in a per-protocol subset, also with the active comparator gadobutrol at its approved dose); Special Protocol Assessment reached with FDA (agreement letter November 30, 2018) for the three co-primary visualization endpoints; GDX-44-010 enrolled CNS-lesion patients (33 centers), GDX-44-011 enrolled patients with lesions in non-CNS body regions including a mandatory breast-MRI subset for US enrollees (33 centers)

- *Endpoints:* three co-primary lesion-visualization endpoints, each a 4-point qualitative reader-assessed scale — border delineation, internal morphology, and degree of contrast enhancement — scored per-patient as the arithmetic mean of up to three matched lesions; key secondary endpoints included the non-inferiority comparison of gadopiclenol vs. gadobutrol on the same three criteria (primary for EMA, secondary for FDA), reader preference, and predicted change in patient management

- *Primary analysis:* per-reader mixed model comparing paired (pre + post-contrast) vs. pre-contrast-only mean lesion-visualization scores in the Full Analysis Set (patients with an assessable pre-contrast/paired image pair and at least one matched lesion for at least one reader), with patient as a random effect and MRI modality as a fixed effect; three independent blinded central readers (plus, in GDX-44-011, a fourth arrangement pooling 19 anatomic-region-specific readers into 3 "meta-readers," one per body-region expertise group) plus one unblinded lesion tracker to match lesions across image sets

- *Multiplicity:* study-level, multi-reader consensus win criterion — for a given reader to be declared successful, the null hypothesis (mean paired-vs-pre-contrast difference = 0) had to be rejected at one-sided α=0.025 for all three co-primary visualization criteria simultaneously, and at least two of the three readers (or meta-readers) had to be successful for the trial to be declared a win; no correction was applied across the two co-identical trials (each analyzed/reported independently)

- *Missing data/bias:* patients with unassessable images or no matched lesion for a given reader were excluded from that reader's primary analysis rather than imputed; extensive sensitivity analyses re-derived results using alternative reader/meta-reader combinations and without excluding non-matching-lesion patients

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was convened for this NDA ("No advisory committee meeting or other external consultation was needed for this NDA" — FDA Multi-Discipline Review); class-wide boxed warning for nephrogenic systemic fibrosis (NSF), standard for GBCAs; pediatric effectiveness (ages 2-17) extrapolated from adult efficacy data plus a dedicated pediatric PK/safety study (GDX-44-007), not from an independent pediatric efficacy trial

**Trial design & endpoints**

- GDX-44-010 (PICTURE) was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, crossover phase 3 study in 256 randomized (247 dosed) adults with known or highly suspected CNS lesions (predominantly meningioma, CNS metastasis, and glioblastoma), conducted at 33 centers; GDX-44-011 (PROMISE) used an identical design in 304 randomized (278 in FAS 1) adults with lesions in non-CNS body regions (head/neck, thorax, abdomen, pelvis, musculoskeletal, including a US-mandated breast-MRI subset to align with the gadobutrol comparator's labeled indication), also at 33 centers across the US, Europe, and Asia

- Every subject underwent an unenhanced (pre-contrast) MRI, then a paired pre-/post-gadopiclenol-contrast MRI at 0.05 mmol/kg (0.1 mL/kg); in a subset (Per-Protocol Set 2), the same subject also underwent a separate paired pre-/post-gadobutrol-contrast MRI at the gadobutrol-approved dose (0.1 mmol/kg), off-site image reading was performed by 3 independent readers (GDX-44-010) or 3 meta-reader pools built from 19 body-region-specific readers (GDX-44-011), all blinded to clinical history and to which contrast agent/timepoint a given image represented, with a 4th unblinded reader tracking lesion identity across image sets and time points

- Primary endpoint (both trials): patient-level mean lesion-visualization score (border delineation, internal morphology, degree of contrast enhancement, each 1-4) on paired vs. pre-contrast images, analyzed via a mixed model (patient random effect, modality fixed effect) in the Full Analysis Set; success required all three criteria significant at one-sided α=0.025 for a given reader, with at least 2 of 3 readers/meta-readers successful

- Results: in GDX-44-010, the 95% CI lower bound exceeded 0 for all three visualization criteria across all three readers (mixed-model p<0.0001 for every difference); e.g., Reader 1 internal morphology paired-vs-pre-contrast difference 2.08 (95% CI 1.76, 1.88; source: FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Table 48/49 region). In GDX-44-011, results were similarly unanimous across all three meta-readers and all three criteria (e.g., Reader 1 degree-of-contrast-enhancement difference 2.64, 95% CI 2.56-2.72, p<0.0001); FDA's Clinical Pharmacology/Statistics review concluded the Applicant met its predefined study-win criteria in both trials

- The secondary non-inferiority comparison against gadobutrol (primary for EMA) used the same three visualization criteria in Per-Protocol Set 2, with a 10%-difference non-inferiority margin justified from the Phase 2 dose-finding study (GDX-44-004); FDA's statistical review explicitly criticized this margin as inadequately validated ("no data were presented to validate the clinical non-significance of a 0.35 decrement in a patient-level visualization score... it was not clear that a 10% difference in visualization score would be clinically unimportant") and did not rely on the non-inferiority result to support the US efficacy claim, treating it only as supportive information

- Dose selection was based on a Phase 2 trial (GDX-44-004) comparing gadopiclenol 0.025-0.2 mmol/kg against gadobenate dimeglumine 0.1 mmol/kg on contrast-to-noise ratio, using a mixed-model analysis with Holm's step-down method across doses/readers, which identified 0.05 mmol/kg gadopiclenol as comparable to the approved 0.1 mmol/kg gadobenate dose — half the standard GBCA dose, marketed as a differentiating feature

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, GDX-44-010 (PICTURE) Statistical Analysis Plan, Section 1.1.1]* — "Primary objective 1: To demonstrate the superiority of gadopiclenol-enhanced MRI at 0.05 mmol/kg body weight (BW) compared to unenhanced MRI for patient referred for contrast-enhanced MRI of the CNS, in terms of 3 lesion visualization co-primary criteria (border delineation, internal morphology and degree of contrast enhancement) using the patient as his/her own control... Primary objective 2: To demonstrate the non-inferiority of gadopiclenol at 0.05 mmol/kg BW compared to gadobutrol at 0.1 mmol/kg BW... For Food and Drug Administration (FDA), the primary objective 1 is to be achieved. The primary objective 2 will serve as one of the secondary objectives... For European Medicine Agency (EMA), both primary objectives 1 and 2 are to be achieved."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 216986, Section 8.1.1]* — "The null hypothesis was that the difference in mean scores between paired and pre-contrast images for each co-primary endpoint was 0, and the alternate hypothesis was that this difference was greater than 0. Significance was tested at α=0.025. The null hypothesis had to be rejected for all three co-primary endpoints for a reader to be successful, and at least two of the three readers had to be successful for study win."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 216986, Section 8.1.1, on the gadobutrol non-inferiority comparison]* — "We note that the co-primary endpoints are subjective and discontinuous, and they are not validated against a reference standard... no data were presented to validate the clinical non-significance of a 0.35 decrement in a patient-level visualization score. Therefore, it was not clear that a 10% difference in visualization score would be clinically unimportant, and potential demonstration of noninferiority in this study was not considered sufficient to establish an efficacy claim."

### 35. Hyperpolarized Xe-129 (Xenoview) — NDA 214375

**Sponsor:** Polarean Inc. (Polarean Imaging plc)

**Indication approved:** Diagnostic use with MRI for the evaluation of lung ventilation in adults and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older — an inhaled hyperpolarized-noble-gas MRI contrast agent, the first FDA-approved contrast agent for pulmonary ventilation MRI, imaging function rather than the anatomic/perfusion contrast typical of gadolinium-based agents

**Approval date:** December 23, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** POL-Xe-001, NCT03417687 (lung resection population), and POL-Xe-002, NCT03418090 (lung transplant population)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two randomized, open-label, crossover, multicenter phase 3 studies, each comparing hyperpolarized Xe-129 MRI against the FDA-approved reference standard, Xe-133 radionuclide ventilation scintigraphy, in a within-patient paired design — Diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison); every patient received both imaging modalities in a randomized order (Xe-129-then-Xe-133 or the reverse); POL-Xe-001 (n=34 dosed, 3 US centers) enrolled patients being evaluated for possible lung resection surgery (segmentectomy, lobectomy, pneumonectomy); POL-Xe-002 (n=49 dosed, 2 US centers) enrolled patients being evaluated for lung transplant surgery

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint in POL-Xe-001 was the scan-estimated percentage of pulmonary ventilation predicted to remain after resection of a pre-specified lung zone (predicted percentage of remaining ventilation), derived from software-quantified fractional ventilation contribution of each of six lung zones (upper/mid/lower, left/right); primary endpoint in POL-Xe-002 was the scan-estimated percentage contribution of the right lung to overall ventilation (relevant to single- vs. double-lung transplant planning); secondary endpoints included per-zone ventilation contribution and (POL-Xe-001 only) scan-predicted postoperative FEV1 compared against measured postoperative spirometry

- *Primary analysis:* two-sided 95% CI of the mean within-patient difference (hyperpolarized Xe-129 MRI minus Xe-133 scintigraphy) in the efficacy analysis set (patients with both a Xe-129 MRI and a Xe-133 scintigraphy scan meeting quality-control criteria); equivalence declared if the 95% CI fell entirely within a pre-specified margin — ±14.7% for the primary endpoint (both trials) and ±5% for individual lung-zone secondary endpoints — with the margin derived from published historical scintigraphy-technique comparison literature (Mariano-Goulart et al. 2006) rather than a within-program pilot estimate

- *Multiplicity:* no formal multiplicity adjustment across the six lung-zone secondary endpoints or across the two trials; each zone/trial analyzed and reported independently against its own equivalence margin

- *Missing data/bias:* regions of interest for the six lung zones were verified by central readers blinded to patient medical history and study assessments; one POL-Xe-001 patient was excluded from the primary analysis for a missing planned-resection-area value rather than imputed under an intent-to-image principle (FDA's statistical review flagged this as a deviation from ITT-style handling but noted the result was robust to imputation given the margin of equivalence achieved)

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting or other external consultation was held for this NDA; a device-like companion element (the Polarean Xenon Hyperpolarizer used to prepare the dose) was reviewed jointly by CDER and a CDRH device reviewer within the same Multi-Discipline Review

**Trial design & endpoints**

- POL-Xe-001 was a randomized, open-label, crossover, multicenter phase 3 study designed to demonstrate equivalence of hyperpolarized Xe-129 MRI to Xe-133 scintigraphy for pulmonary ventilation evaluation in patients being worked up for lung resection surgery; patients underwent both imaging studies (order randomized 1:1) during an imaging period, with postoperative follow-up (~3 months after surgery) for patients who proceeded to resection; commercially available software quantified ventilation contribution across six lung zones (upper/mid/lower x left/right) on each scan, with regions of interest verified by blinded central readers

- POL-Xe-002 used an identical crossover structure in patients being evaluated for lung transplantation, where the clinically relevant question is each lung's fractional contribution to overall ventilation (informing single- vs. bilateral-transplant decisions) rather than a post-resection prediction

- Primary endpoint analysis (both trials): mean of the within-patient differences in the primary ventilation measure, with equivalence declared if the two-sided 95% CI fell within ±14.7% (a margin derived from historical pre-pneumonectomy scintigraphy-comparison literature, on the premise that 3 of the 6 lung zones remain after a typical pneumonectomy, i.e., a residual-function framing); secondary per-zone equivalence used a tighter ±5% margin (approximately one-third of the primary margin, reflecting the larger number of zones involved)

- POL-Xe-001 results: mean within-patient difference (Xe-129 minus Xe-133) in predicted remaining ventilation was 1.4% (95% CI -0.75%, 3.6%), within the ±14.7% margin; considerable between-patient variability was observed (range of individual differences -21.5% to +14.2%); per-zone 95% CIs fell within ±5% for all zones except the lower-left lung, which narrowly exceeded the upper bound, a discrepancy the Applicant attributed to Xe-133 scintigraphy's known underestimation of ventilation in that zone from photon attenuation by the heart (citing Schembri et al. 2015); a secondary spirometry comparison found both hyperpolarized Xe-129 MRI and Xe-133 scintigraphy underestimated actual postoperative FEV1 by a similar magnitude (mean difference -0.65 L for both modalities vs. measured FEV1)

- POL-Xe-002 results: mean within-patient difference in right-lung ventilation contribution was -1.59% (95% CI -3.69%, 0.50%), within the ±14.7% margin; the single most extreme observed within-patient difference (32.9%) was attributed by the Applicant to depolarization from a patient's continued supplemental-oxygen inhalation during Xe-129 administration at that scan, prompting a procedural change (interrupting supplemental oxygen during dosing) that was carried into the approved prescribing information

- FDA's statistical reviewer independently reprogrammed and confirmed the Applicant's primary-endpoint results in both trials using the submitted datasets

The scans will be quantified using commercially available software to report the fraction of activity arising from 6 lung zones."

We thus seek to demonstrate an equivalence margin of 14.7%."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 214375, Section 8.1.1]* — "The pre-specified equivalence criterion was met since the 95% CI of the mean within-patient differences was contained in the pre-specified equivalence interval of -14.7% to +14.7%."

### 36. Anacaulase-bcdb (NexoBrid) — BLA 761192

**Sponsor:** MediWound Ltd.

**Indication approved:** Debridement of eschar in adults and pediatric patients with deep partial-thickness and/or full-thickness thermal burns — a topical enzymatic debridement agent (proteolytic enzymes enriched in bromelain, extracted from pineapple-plant stems) offered as a non-surgical alternative to excisional eschar removal

**Approval date:** December 28, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** DETECT (MW2010-03-02), NCT02148705

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, three-arm (NexoBrid gel : standard-of-care (SOC) : vehicle gel, 3:3:1), multicenter, multinational, assessor-blinded phase 3 trial in adults with thermal burns ≤30% total body surface area (TBSA); blinding was partial by necessity — treating investigators were unblinded (NexoBrid gel is gold-colored, vehicle is clear) but a dedicated assessor blinded to treatment (NexoBrid vs. vehicle) evaluated eschar removal, and a second assessor blinded to all arms conducted weekly wound-closure and long-term cosmesis/function evaluations; conducted under three successive protocol amendments (Amendments 8, 9, 11) that changed the maximum enrollable %TBSA (15%→30%), the randomization method (minimization→block randomization), and the stratification factors

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint incidence of ≥95% eschar removal at the end of the topical treatment soaking period, NexoBrid vs. vehicle gel (subject-level, across all target wounds); secondary endpoints (NexoBrid vs. SOC) were incidence of surgical eschar removal, time to eschar removal, and blood loss during eschar-removal procedures; safety endpoints (NexoBrid vs. SOC) included time to wound closure and Modified Vancouver Scar Scale (MVSS) cosmesis score at Month 12 (with 24-month follow-up added by a later SAP addendum)

- *Primary analysis:* Fisher's exact test on the Full Analysis Set (all randomized subjects), with the odds ratio and 95% CI estimated by exact methods; subjects with missing primary-endpoint data were counted as non-responders (not achieving eschar removal); secondary surgical-eschar-removal endpoint analyzed by logistic regression adjusted for wound depth, %TBSA, and number of target wounds; time-to-eschar-removal and time-to-wound-closure endpoints analyzed by Cox regression (with a pre-specified generalized Wilcoxon-Gehan fallback if the proportional-hazards assumption failed), each adjusted for wound depth, %TBSA, center group, and number of target wounds

- *Missing data/bias:* Worst-case-scenario asymmetric sensitivity analysis for suspected unblinding bias — FDA's statistical reviewer identified protocol deviations in which blinded assessors were potentially unblinded (e.g., via photographic assessments) and re-ran the primary and safety endpoints reclassifying every potentially-unblinded NexoBrid subject as a treatment failure and every potentially-unblinded vehicle subject as a treatment success, finding the primary conclusion unchanged (77.3% vs. 24.0% response, still p<0.0001, vs. the original 93.3% vs. 4.0%); a parallel treatment-code-swap ad hoc analysis was also performed for the time-to-wound-closure safety endpoint

- *Regulatory:* Complete Response Letter (CRL) followed by resubmission and approval — the original BLA (submitted June 29, 2020) received a CRL on June 25, 2021 for product-quality/CMC and Office of Scientific Investigations deficiencies only (FDA's Clinical review identified no deficiencies in the original submission); approval followed on resubmission (submitted July 1, 2022) after the manufacturing issues were resolved; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- DETECT enrolled adults ≥18 years hospitalized with fire/flame, scald, or contact thermal burns (deep partial-thickness [DPT], full-thickness [FT], and/or superficial partial-thickness [SPT]), total burn area ≤30% TBSA, with at least one target wound (DPT and/or FT, ≥0.5% TBSA, excluding facial/perineal/genital sites); subjects were randomized 3:3:1 to NexoBrid gel, SOC (investigator's choice of surgical or non-surgical eschar-removal methods), or vehicle gel, stratified by total burn area, wound depth, and center (stratification details varied across the three protocol amendments, with 70% of subjects enrolled under the final Amendment 11)

- NexoBrid/vehicle gel was applied to target wounds (≤15% TBSA per session, up to two sessions) and left in place 4 hours under a dressing, followed by mechanical removal of dissolved eschar and a 2-hour antibacterial soak; eschar removal was assessed at the end of this soaking period; remaining eschar after the topical procedure was removed by SOC as rescue treatment

- Primary endpoint: incidence of ≥95% eschar removal at the end of the topical treatment soaking period, NexoBrid vs. vehicle gel, analyzed by Fisher's exact test on the Full Analysis Set (all randomized subjects), with missing data imputed as non-response; results per FDA's Multi-Discipline Review: 70/75 (93.3%) NexoBrid vs. 1/25 (4.0%) vehicle achieved the primary endpoint (p<0.0001)

- Key secondary endpoint (NexoBrid vs. SOC): incidence of surgical eschar removal, analyzed by logistic regression adjusted for wound depth, %TBSA, and number of target wounds, with missing data imputed as having undergone surgical excision (a conservative-against-NexoBrid imputation rule) and an observed-case sensitivity analysis conducted in parallel

- Safety endpoint: time to ≥95% wound closure (NexoBrid vs. SOC), analyzed at the wound level via Kaplan-Meier estimation and Cox regression (proportional-hazards assumption checked via a time-by-treatment interaction term, with a generalized Wilcoxon-Gehan test as a pre-specified fallback); original analysis showed a similar median time to wound closure between arms (27 days NexoBrid vs. 28 days SOC)

- Blood-loss endpoints used a validated estimated-blood-loss formula (adapted from McCullough et al.'s prostatectomy blood-loss method) combining pre-/post-procedure hemoglobin change with transfused whole-blood and packed-red-cell volumes, summed across all eschar-removal procedures for a subject

- A Quality Control audit identified protocol deviations in which assessors evaluating eschar removal or wound closure may have been unblinded (12/13 affected NexoBrid subjects vs. 0/5 affected vehicle subjects for the eschar-removal endpoint) or relied on photographic rather than live assessments; FDA's statistical reviewer conducted worst-case reclassification sensitivity analyses (reassigning all potentially-unblinded NexoBrid subjects to non-response and all potentially-unblinded vehicle subjects to response) for both the primary efficacy endpoint and the wound-closure safety endpoint, and an additional ad hoc analysis swapping the "true" treatment-arm code for affected subjects; all sensitivity analyses left the primary efficacy conclusion intact given the very large observed treatment effect, and did not materially change the wound-closure safety conclusion

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761192, Section 2.3]* — "If all 13 subjects on the NexoBrid arm with potential unblinding events were classified as non-responders, and all 5 subjects on the vehicle arm with potential unblinding events were classified as responders, the estimated response rates would be 77.3% vs. 24.0%, which would still meet the statistical significance criteria (p<0.0001)... With the large magnitude of the treatment effect for this endpoint, potential unblinding appears to have had minimal impact on the primary endpoint results."

*[verbatim, DETECT Statistical Analysis Plan Addendum 2 (23 August 2020), Section 5]* — "Due to COVID-19 restrictions, the sponsor has submitted a protocol memo, dated 09 Apr 2020, to sites allowing them to perform the 24-month visit with a deviation of up to 6 months (between April 1st to Sep 1st), or to perform the visit remotely. In addition, due to lack of resources, some sites may not be able to perform the 24-month MVSS and POSAS assessments."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761192, Section 8.1.1 (Statistical Analysis Plan description)]* — "The primary efficacy endpoint of incidence of eschar removal at the end of the topical treatment soaking procedure (NexoBrid versus vehicle gel) is analyzed with Fisher's exact test. The odds ratio and 95% confidence interval will be estimated using exact methods... subjects with missing data for this endpoint will be considered as not achieving eschar removal."

**Reverse-engineered SAP** [inferred]

- [inferred] The 3:3:1 (NexoBrid:SOC:vehicle) randomization ratio was almost certainly chosen to preserve adequate power for the vehicle-controlled primary efficacy comparison while maximizing exposure to the two arms (NexoBrid, SOC) needed for the secondary/safety comparisons that inform real-world clinical positioning against surgical practice — traced to the disproportionate arm sizes reported in the FDA review (NexoBrid n=75, SOC n=75, vehicle n=25) relative to a conventional equal-allocation design.

### 37. Ensifentrine (Ohtuvayre) — NDA 217389

**Sponsor:** Verona Pharma, Inc. (acquired by Merck & Co./MSD in a deal that closed shortly after this approval)

**Indication approved:** Maintenance treatment of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) in adult patients — the first inhaled dual phosphodiesterase-3/phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE3/PDE4) inhibitor approved for COPD

**Approval date:** June 26, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** ENHANCE-1, NCT04535986, and ENHANCE-2, NCT04542057

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two replicate randomized, quadruple-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter phase 3 trials (250 sites, 17 countries), 24 weeks; nebulized ensifentrine 3 mg twice daily vs. placebo; ENHANCE-1 N=760 randomized/treated, ENHANCE-2 N=789; population aged 40-80y, ≥10 pack-year smoking history, moderate-to-severe symptomatic COPD (post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC<0.70, FEV1 30-70% predicted); stratified by region, background LAMA/LABA maintenance-therapy strata (capped so no more than ~50-70% of enrollment was on background triple/dual therapy), and smoking strata

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint average FEV1 area-under-the-curve from 0-12 hours (AUC0-12h) change from baseline at Week 12; key secondary endpoints (fixed-sequence hierarchy) included peak FEV1, Evaluating Respiratory Symptoms (E-RS) total score, St. George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ) total score, morning trough FEV1, FEV1 AUC0-4h, and SGRQ responder proportion; moderate-or-severe COPD exacerbation rate and time-to-first-exacerbation were pooled/exploratory endpoints reported in the publication

- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA (fixed effects: treatment, region, background-medication strata, smoking strata; covariate: baseline FEV1) on the modified intent-to-treat population, with multiple imputation (MCMC monotone plus regression imputation, 100 imputed datasets, Rubin's rules, missing-at-random assumption) used as the primary — not merely a sensitivity — handling of missing post-baseline FEV1 data (*ANCOVA with multiple imputation as the pre-specified primary missing-data method*, distinct from the taxonomy's existing MMRM-based longitudinal-endpoint rows)

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing across the 6 key secondary endpoints, each gated behind the previous being statistically significant

- *Missing data/bias:* tipping-point sensitivity analysis under an explicit missing-not-at-random bias-increment algorithm (a stepped adjustment parameter increased until the primary conclusion "tipped"), run against the multiple-imputation-based primary result; key-secondary FEV1 endpoints additionally used an MMRM sensitivity analysis (unstructured covariance, Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom)

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting identified; no FDA Statistical/Clinical/Multi-Discipline Review posted on Drugs@FDA as of this writing, but a genuine sponsor-authored SAP and protocol are posted on ClinicalTrials.gov for both trials

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ENHANCE-1 and ENHANCE-2 were near-identically designed, randomized, quadruple-blind (participant/investigator/outcomes-assessor/sponsor), placebo-controlled, parallel-group phase 3 trials conducted September 2020-December 2022, enrolling adults 40-80 years old with moderate-to-severe symptomatic COPD (post-bronchodilator FEV1 30-70% predicted, FEV1/FVC<0.70, mMRC dyspnea score ≥2, ≥10 pack-year smoking history). Subjects were randomized to nebulized ensifentrine 3 mg or matching placebo twice daily for 24 weeks (ENHANCE-1 also carried a subset followed to 48 weeks for long-term safety); randomization was stratified by region, background LAMA/LABA use, and smoking status. Concomitant use of a single long-acting bronchodilator (LAMA or LABA, not both, i.e., no background triple therapy) was permitted and capped

- Primary endpoint: change from baseline in average FEV1 AUC0-12h at Week 12, analyzed by ANCOVA (treatment, region, background-medication strata, smoking strata as fixed effects; baseline FEV1 as covariate) in the modified intent-to-treat population, with multiple imputation (100 MCMC-monotone/regression-imputed datasets, Rubin's-rules pooling) as the pre-specified primary missing-data method rather than a sensitivity check; a tipping-point analysis under an explicit MNAR bias-increment scheme served as the robustness check on that MI-based result

- Key secondary endpoints were tested in a fixed-sequence hierarchy (each endpoint gated on significance of the one before it): peak FEV1, E-RS total score, SGRQ total score, morning trough FEV1, FEV1 AUC0-4h, and SGRQ responder proportion, all at Week 24 unless noted; exacerbation-rate and time-to-first-exacerbation endpoints were analyzed and reported (rate ratio via negative-binomial-type regression; hazard ratio via Cox-type model, per the publication) but were not part of the confirmatory hierarchy in the same way

- Results (Anzueto et al. 2023, the pivotal publication): ensifentrine significantly improved FEV1 AUC0-12h vs. placebo in both trials (ENHANCE-1: 87 mL, 95% CI 55-119, P<0.001; ENHANCE-2: 94 mL, 95% CI 65-124, P<0.001). E-RS and SGRQ improvements vs. placebo were significant in ENHANCE-1 but not in ENHANCE-2 at Week 24. Moderate-or-severe exacerbation rate was reduced vs. placebo over 24 weeks (ENHANCE-1 rate ratio 0.64, 95% CI 0.40-1.00, P=0.050; ENHANCE-2 rate ratio 0.57, 95% CI 0.38-0.87, P=0.009), and time to first exacerbation was increased (ENHANCE-1 HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.39-0.97, P=0.038; ENHANCE-2 HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.38-0.87, P=0.009). Adverse-event rates were similar to placebo

- No Data Monitoring Committee or formal group-sequential interim analysis was used; a blinded sample-size re-estimation rule tied to the observed pooled SD and withdrawal rate was pre-specified, distinct from a formal alpha-spending adaptive design

### 38. Iomeprol (Iomervu) — NDA 216017

**Sponsor:** Bracco Diagnostics Inc. — approved as two co-filed 505(b)(2) NDAs (216016 and 216017), reflecting different concentrations/routes of the same active ingredient

**Indication approved:** An iodinated, low-osmolar, nonionic contrast agent indicated for intra-arterial use (cerebral, visceral, and peripheral arteriography; coronary arteriography and left ventriculography) and intravenous use (contrast-enhanced computed tomography of the head and body, including CT angiography and coronary CT angiography, and excretory urography) to enhance diagnostic imaging visualization in adults

**Approval date:** November 27, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** No single dedicated pivotal RCT; approval rests on a legacy multi-study evidentiary package (no unifying ClinicalTrials.gov registration/NCT number identified for a single US registration trial)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* diagnostic-accuracy study package (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison against a reference standard, and independent multi-reader blinded-read studies), reusing the taxonomy's existing "Diagnostic-accuracy study" and "Retrospective/non-prospective diagnostic evidentiary basis" categories — intra-arterial indications supported by three blinded-read study programs, each itself comprising 2-4 prospective, randomized, double-blind, multicenter sub-studies (cerebral arteriography N=61; visceral/peripheral arteriography N=60; coronary arteriography/ventriculography N=59 and N=59 across two concentrations); intravenous indications supported by separate blinded-read CT head/body studies (N=59 and N=59), prospective CT-angiography studies against digital subtraction angiography as reference standard (2 studies, N=262), coronary CTA studies against invasive coronary angiography (2 studies, N=301), and two retrospective single-center CT-urography visualization-quality studies (N=185, no reference-standard comparator)

- *Endpoints:* three-reader independent adequate/inadequate visualization ratings for the arteriography blinded-read studies (adequate visualization achieved in 93-100% of cases); sensitivity/specificity vs. digital-subtraction-angiography or invasive-coronary-angiography reference standard for the CTA studies (e.g., approximately 99%/97% for detecting ≥70% stenosis on CT angiography; 84-97% sensitivity/91-94% specificity for coronary CTA); visualization-quality scoring (no reference standard) for the CT-urography studies

- *Primary analysis:* descriptive reporting of proportion-adequate-visualization and/or sensitivity/specificity point estimates with confidence intervals per study, rather than a single unifying inferential test across a pooled population — consistent with a 505(b)(2) submission built from an assembled historical study package rather than one prospectively designed registration trial

- *Regulatory:* approved via the 505(b)(2) pathway relying substantially on the sponsor's own pre-existing, largely ex-US clinical development package for iomeprol (marketed outside the US for decades as Iomeron), rather than a newly conducted dedicated US pivotal trial — a **505(b)(2) reliance on a sponsor's own historical/ex-US clinical package** (distinct from the taxonomy's existing academic/third-party-literature-reliance rows, which describe reliance on independently published external literature rather than the applicant's own prior study program)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Unlike the other entries in this batch, iomeprol's US approval is not built around one dedicated phase 3 pivotal trial with a single NCT number. Per the approved label's Section 14 (Clinical Studies), the intra-arterial indications (cerebral, visceral/peripheral, and coronary arteriography/left ventriculography) are each supported by a blinded-read study incorporating 2-4 prospective, randomized, double-blind, multicenter sub-studies comparing iomeprol against an active comparator contrast agent, with three independent readers rating each image as adequate or inadequate for diagnostic visualization (cerebral arteriography N=61, adequate in the great majority of cases; visceral/peripheral arteriography N=60; coronary arteriography/ventriculography N=59 and N=59 at two concentrations)

- The intravenous indications are supported by separate study sets: blinded-read CT head/body visualization studies (N=59 and N=59); two prospective single-center CT-angiography studies (N=262) reporting sensitivity/specificity against digital subtraction angiography as the reference standard (approximately 99%/97% for ≥70% stenosis detection); two coronary CTA studies (N=301) against invasive coronary angiography (sensitivity 84-97%, specificity 91-94%); and two retrospective single-center CT-urography studies (N=185) using visualization-quality scoring without a reference-standard comparator

- This evidentiary structure fits the census taxonomy's existing "Diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison)" and "Retrospective/non-prospective diagnostic evidentiary basis" rows (previously seen with Lymphoseek, Axumin, and Netspot), though those prior examples relied on independently conducted third-party/academic studies or published literature, whereas iomeprol's package is the sponsor's own historical (largely ex-US) clinical development program — assembled and submitted as a 505(b)(2) application rather than either a fresh pivotal RCT or reliance on external literature

- The FDA approval letter (covering the co-filed NDA 216016 and NDA 216017) explicitly documents the 505(b)(2) regulatory basis; no separate FDA Statistical or Clinical Review is posted on Drugs@FDA beyond the approval letter and label as of this writing

### 39. Suzetrigine (Journavx) — NDA 219209

**Sponsor:** Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated

**Indication approved:** Treatment of moderate-to-severe acute pain in adults — the first-in-class oral, non-opioid, selective NaV1.8 voltage-gated sodium-channel inhibitor approved for any indication, positioned as a non-opioid alternative for acute pain management

**Approval date:** January 30, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** Bunionectomy trial (Protocol VX22-548-104), NCT05553366, and Abdominoplasty trial, NCT05558410

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two phase 3, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, placebo- and active-controlled trials in acute postsurgical pain; bunionectomy trial N=1,073 (2:2:1 to suzetrigine/hydrocodone bitartrate-acetaminophen [HB-APAP]/placebo) following unilateral bunionectomy with Austin osteotomy under regional block; abdominoplasty trial N=1,118, same 2:2:1 design and dosing; randomization triggered post-block-removal when the subject requested analgesia with moderate-or-severe pain (verbal rating scale) and a numeric pain rating scale (NPRS) score ≥4 within a 9-hour eligibility window; stratified by site and baseline NPRS (<8 vs. ≥8)

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint time-weighted sum of pain-intensity difference on the 0-10 NPRS from 0-48 hours (SPID48) vs. placebo; key secondary endpoints (fixed-sequence hierarchy) SPID48 vs. HB-APAP, then time to ≥2-point NPRS reduction from baseline vs. placebo (Kaplan-Meier/log-rank)

- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA (treatment as fixed effect; site and baseline NPRS as covariates, site dropped from the model if non-convergent) on the Full Analysis Set, with intercurrent events (rescue-medication use, treatment discontinuation) handled under a pure hypothetical strategy — rescue-period scores replaced by the pre-rescue score, post-adverse-event-discontinuation scores imputed to baseline, post-other-discontinuation scores carried forward from the last observation, and intermittent missing values linearly interpolated — rather than a composite (treatment-failure) strategy

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing: SPID48 vs. placebo (primary) → SPID48 vs. HB-APAP (key secondary) → time to ≥2-point NPRS reduction vs. placebo (key secondary), each gated on the prior step reaching significance at two-sided alpha=0.05

- *Missing data/bias:* deterministic (non-stochastic) imputation scheme for intercurrent events described above, rather than multiple imputation; sample size based on a standardized effect size of 0.40 vs. placebo / 0.25 vs. HB-APAP, ~338 evaluable subjects/arm plus 169 on placebo for >90% power on both the primary and the key HB-APAP-comparison secondary via a two-sample t-test; no Data Monitoring Committee or interim analysis ("not applicable" per the posted SAP)

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting identified; no FDA Statistical/Clinical/Multi-Discipline Review posted on Drugs@FDA as of this writing, but a genuine sponsor SAP is posted on ClinicalTrials.gov for the bunionectomy trial (and a SAP/protocol document section exists for the abdominoplasty trial)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Both phase 3 trials enrolled adults with moderate-to-severe acute postsurgical pain (verbal categorical rating scale plus NPRS≥4) following either unilateral bunionectomy with Austin osteotomy (under regional anesthetic block, N=1,073) or abdominoplasty (N=1,118). After the regional block wore off and the subject met the eligibility pain threshold within a 9-hour window, subjects were randomized 2:2:1 to suzetrigine (100 mg loading dose, then 50 mg every 12 hours), HB-APAP (5 mg/325 mg every 6 hours, an active opioid comparator), or placebo, all double-dummy blinded, for 48 hours; randomization was stratified by site and baseline NPRS (<8 vs. ≥8)

- Primary endpoint: SPID48, the time-weighted sum of pain-intensity difference on the 0-10 NPRS over 0-48 hours, analyzed by ANCOVA (treatment fixed effect; site and baseline-NPRS covariates) on the Full Analysis Set, versus placebo. The primary estimand followed a pure hypothetical intercurrent-event strategy: post-rescue-medication and post-discontinuation NPRS values were not scored as composite treatment failures but were instead imputed (pre-rescue value carried forward through the rescue period; baseline value imputed after AE-related discontinuation; last observation carried forward after other discontinuation; intermittent gaps linearly interpolated) — this is a pure-hypothetical (non-composite) instance of the ICH E9(R1) estimand framework, distinct from the mixed composite/hypothetical estimands already catalogued in the taxonomy for other programs

- Key secondary endpoints, tested in a fixed-sequence hierarchy each gated on the prior step's significance: (1) SPID48 vs. HB-APAP (non-inferiority/superiority framing on the same ANCOVA model), then (2) time to a ≥2-point reduction in NPRS from baseline vs. placebo, analyzed by Kaplan-Meier estimation and log-rank test

- Sample size: assuming a standardized effect size of 0.40 for suzetrigine vs. placebo and 0.25 for suzetrigine vs. HB-APAP, approximately 338 evaluable subjects per arm (suzetrigine, HB-APAP) plus 169 on placebo were planned to give >90% power for both the primary comparison and the key HB-APAP secondary via two-sample t-tests at two-sided alpha=0.05; roughly 1,000 subjects were enrolled per trial to allow for an assumed ~15% dropout. No Data Monitoring Committee or formal interim analysis was planned

- Results (Bertoch et al. 2025, the pivotal publication): the primary endpoint was met in both trials. LS-mean SPID48 difference vs. placebo was 48.4 (95% CI 33.6-63.1; P<0.0001) after abdominoplasty and 29.3 (95% CI 14.0-44.6; P=0.0002) after bunionectomy. Neither trial met the first key secondary endpoint of superiority vs. HB-APAP on SPID48 (so, per the fixed-sequence hierarchy, the second key secondary was tested only descriptively/nominally beyond that gate); for time to ≥2-point NPRS reduction, suzetrigine had faster onset than placebo (abdominoplasty: 119 vs. 480 minutes, nominal P<0.0001; bunionectomy: 240 vs. 480 minutes, nominal P=0.0016). Adverse events were similar to typical postsurgical safety profiles

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, ClinicalTrials.gov-posted SAP, NCT05553366]* — the posted SAP confirms SPID48 vs. placebo as the primary endpoint, ANCOVA (treatment, site, baseline NPRS) as the primary model on the Full Analysis Set, and the fixed-sequence hierarchy (primary → SPID48 vs. HB-APAP → time to ≥2-point NPRS reduction vs. placebo), each gated on the prior comparison's significance at two-sided alpha=0.05, consistent with the design and results summarized above and in the pivotal publication.

**Reverse-engineered SAP** [inferred]

- [inferred] The choice of a pure-hypothetical (rather than composite) intercurrent-event strategy for rescue medication was almost certainly deliberate, to avoid penalizing suzetrigine's estimate for rescue use that could plausibly occur similarly across arms in an acute post-surgical-pain model, since a composite/treatment-failure strategy would tend to inflate the apparent placebo-relative benefit — traced to the SAP's detailed deterministic-imputation rules (pre-rescue value carried through the rescue window, rather than a fixed low/high anchor value) and the publication's description of the intercurrent-event handling.

### 40. Brensocatib (Brinsupri) — NDA 217673

**Sponsor:** Insmed Incorporated

**Indication approved:** Treatment of non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis (NCFB) in adults and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older — the first drug ever approved for this indication (a dipeptidyl peptidase 1 [DPP1]/cathepsin C inhibitor that reduces activation of neutrophil serine proteases)

**Approval date:** August 12, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** ASPEN (Insmed Study INS1007-301), NCT04594369

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 1:1:1, phase 3 trial in adults and adolescents (≥12y) with NCFB; arms brensocatib 10 mg once daily, 25 mg once daily, placebo; N randomized=1,767 (ITT population 1,721, after excluding 44 subjects in Ukraine for war-related reasons and 2 subjects at one US site for GCP noncompliance); 52-week treatment duration; stratified by sputum *Pseudomonas aeruginosa* status, prior pulmonary-exacerbation count (<3 vs. ≥3), region (North America/Europe/Japan/rest-of-world), and age group

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint annualized rate of pulmonary exacerbations (PEx) through Week 52, using the Hill et al. (2017) consensus PEx definition (≥3 of 6 prespecified symptoms for ≥48 hours prompting antibiotic treatment, with ≥4 weeks required between distinct exacerbations, all centrally adjudicated by a blinded committee); key secondary endpoints (hierarchy) time to first PEx, exacerbation-free responder status at Week 52, change in post-bronchodilator FEV1 at Week 52, annualized rate of severe PEx, and change in Quality of Life-Bronchiectasis (QoL-B) Respiratory Symptoms domain at Week 52

- *Primary analysis:* negative binomial regression (log link, robust/sandwich covariance, offset = log person-time at risk) with covariates treatment, *P. aeruginosa* status, prior-exacerbation category, region, and age group (SAS PROC GENMOD)

- *Multiplicity:* an enhanced mixture-based gatekeeping procedure (Kordzakhia et al. 2018) spanning 6 endpoint families (one per efficacy endpoint) × 2 dose-vs-placebo hypotheses each — truncated Hochberg (truncation parameter 0.9) for the primary-endpoint family, Bonferroni for four intermediate families, and Hochberg for the final family (*enhanced mixture-based gatekeeping procedure (Kordzakhia et al. 2018)* — not currently in Keyword_Taxonomy.md § 4)

- *Missing data/bias:* tipping-point sensitivity analysis for a missing-not-at-random departure from the primary negative-binomial model; multiple imputation (100 datasets, Rubin's rules) specifically for the exacerbation-free-responder-status key secondary endpoint

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held (stated explicitly in FDA's review); sample size (~1,620 adults) was powered assuming a placebo annualized PEx rate of 1.2, negative-binomial dispersion parameter 1, and a rate ratio of 0.70, for 90% power under the truncated-Hochberg-gated overall two-sided alpha=0.01

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ASPEN was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 3-arm (brensocatib 10 mg, 25 mg, placebo, all once daily), 52-week phase 3 trial in adults and adolescents ≥12 years old with NCFB, stratified by sputum *P. aeruginosa* status, prior-exacerbation count, region, and age group; 1,767 subjects were randomized and 1,721 comprised the ITT analysis population after exclusions for war-related site disruption in Ukraine (44 subjects) and GCP noncompliance at one US site (2 subjects)

- Primary endpoint: annualized rate of pulmonary exacerbations through Week 52 (Hill et al. 2017 definition, centrally adjudicated), analyzed via negative binomial regression with a log-time-at-risk offset and covariates for treatment, *P. aeruginosa* status, prior-exacerbation category, region, and age group

- Multiplicity across the primary and 5 key secondary endpoints, each tested for both doses vs. placebo, was controlled by an enhanced mixture-based gatekeeping procedure (Kordzakhia et al. 2018): the primary-endpoint family used a truncated Hochberg step-up procedure (truncation 0.9), 4 intermediate families used simple Bonferroni splits, and the final family used a standard Hochberg step-up procedure — a multi-family, mixed-procedure gatekeeping structure more elaborate than the fixed-sequence or single-procedure hierarchies seen elsewhere in this census

- Results (FDA Integrated Review, Table 10; consistent with Chalmers et al. 2025 NEJM): annualized PEx rate was 1.29 (95% CI 1.16-1.43) on placebo, 1.02 (95% CI 0.91-1.13) on 10 mg, and 1.04 (95% CI 0.93-1.16) on 25 mg. Rate ratio vs. placebo was 0.79 (95% CI 0.68-0.92; unadjusted P=0.002, gatekeeping-adjusted P=0.004) for 10 mg and 0.81 (95% CI 0.69-0.94; unadjusted P=0.005, adjusted P=0.005) for 25 mg. Time to first exacerbation was likewise improved (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.70-0.95 for 10 mg; HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.70-0.97 for 25 mg). Both doses were approved

- Missing-data handling combined a tipping-point sensitivity analysis (for the negative-binomial primary model under an assumed MNAR departure) with multiple imputation specifically for the binary exacerbation-free-responder key secondary endpoint — a dual missing-data strategy tailored to the different endpoint types (count vs. binary) within the same trial

### 41. Nerandomilast (Jascayd) — NDA 218764

**Sponsor:** Boehringer Ingelheim Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) in adults — an oral, preferential phosphodiesterase 4B (PDE4B) inhibitor (a later supplement to this same NDA subsequently added progressive pulmonary fibrosis as a second indication, outside the scope of this entry's original approval)

**Approval date:** October 7, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** FIBRONEER-IPF (Boehringer Study 1305-0014), NCT05321069

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized 1:1:1, quadruple-blind (participant/care provider/investigator/outcomes assessor), placebo-controlled phase 3 trial in adults ≥40y with IPF (2022 ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT diagnostic criteria), FVC≥45% predicted, DLCO≥25% predicted, with or without background antifibrotic therapy (nintedanib or pirfenidone); arms nerandomilast 9 mg twice daily, 18 mg twice daily, placebo; 1,177 randomized (392/392/393); stratified by background antifibrotic-therapy use; two-part design (Part A, ≥52 weeks, primary analysis at Database Lock 1; Part B, variable-duration blinded extension, primarily safety-focused, Database Lock 2 approximately 4 months later)

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint absolute change from baseline in forced vital capacity (FVC, mL) at Week 52; key secondary endpoint time to first of {acute IPF exacerbation, respiratory hospitalization, death from any cause} (a composite time-to-event endpoint)

- *Primary analysis:* mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) with fixed effects for treatment, visit, baseline antifibrotic-therapy use, baseline FVC, and treatment-by-visit and baseline-FVC-by-visit interactions, unstructured covariance, random subject effect; key secondary analyzed via Cox proportional-hazards model (covariates treatment, antifibrotic use, age, baseline FVC% predicted, baseline DLCO% predicted)

- *Multiplicity:* a graphical alpha-propagation testing procedure controlling family-wise type I error across the primary and key secondary endpoints for both doses (the specific named graphical-method variant/weighting scheme was not confirmed in the documents reviewed — described here descriptively rather than force-matched to the taxonomy's existing Maurer-Bretz row, since that match was not independently confirmed)

- *Missing data/bias:* the sponsor's primary MMRM used a composite intercurrent-event strategy specifically for death — post-death missing FVC values were substituted with the 10th percentile of observed FVC change-from-baseline across arms at Week 52 (a fixed "unfavorable value" substitution), which FDA's review disputed as insufficiently unfavorable per the ICH E9(R1) estimand framework, prompting FDA sensitivity analyses across a 0.1st-5th-percentile range and an independent ranked ANCOVA (deaths ranked worse than any observed value, ordered by time-to-death among deaths) as a labeling-relevant sensitivity/point-estimate check (*percentile-substitution composite strategy for death in an MMRM primary analysis*, paired with a *worst-rank/ranked-ANCOVA sensitivity analysis for death* — neither is currently in Keyword_Taxonomy.md)

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held (stated explicitly in FDA's review); FDA required the ranked-ANCOVA-derived, observed-FVC-based point estimate (rather than the sponsor's percentile-substitution MMRM point estimate) to be used for the clinically interpretable labeling claim, while still accepting the sponsor's MMRM analysis for the statistical-significance determination — a reviewer-documented divergence between the accepted hypothesis-test method and the accepted labeling point-estimate method

**Trial design & endpoints**

- FIBRONEER-IPF randomized 1,177 adults with IPF (392/392/393 across nerandomilast 9 mg BID, 18 mg BID, and placebo) in a quadruple-blind, placebo-controlled design stratified by background antifibrotic use, across a two-part structure (Part A primary analysis at ≥52 weeks/Database Lock 1, Part B blinded safety extension to Database Lock 2)

- Primary endpoint: absolute change from baseline in FVC (mL) at Week 52, via MMRM with treatment, visit, baseline antifibrotic use, baseline FVC, and interaction terms as fixed effects and an unstructured covariance structure. The sponsor's primary analysis handled deaths as an intercurrent event via a composite strategy substituting each death's missing post-death FVC values with the 10th percentile of the observed FVC change-from-baseline distribution across arms at Week 52 — intended as an "unfavorable" imputed value reflecting that death is a worse outcome than any observed decline

- FDA's review disputed whether the 10th-percentile substitution was sufficiently unfavorable to satisfy ICH E9(R1) principles for handling a treatment-terminating intercurrent event, and ran its own sensitivity analyses substituting values from the 0.1st through 5th percentiles instead; FDA ultimately accepted the sponsor's primary MMRM for establishing statistical significance, but required a separate, prespecified ranked ANCOVA (in which deaths are ranked as uniformly worse than any observed alive value, ordered among themselves by time-to-death) to generate the point estimate used in product labeling, rather than the percentile-substitution MMRM's point estimate — a documented FDA/sponsor divergence between the accepted significance-test method and the accepted labeling-point-estimate method

- Key secondary endpoint: time to first of {acute IPF exacerbation, respiratory hospitalization, all-cause death}, a composite time-to-event outcome analyzed via Cox proportional-hazards regression, tested under a graphical alpha-propagation multiplicity procedure alongside the primary endpoint across both doses

- Results (FDA Integrated Review Table 14, sponsor's primary percentile-substitution MMRM analysis): adjusted mean FVC change from baseline at Week 52 was -183.1 mL (95% CI -210.5 to -155.8) on placebo, -138.4 mL (95% CI -165.3 to -111.4) on 9 mg, and -114.4 mL (95% CI -141.5 to -87.3) on 18 mg. Difference vs. placebo was +44.8 mL (95% CI 6.4-83.2, P=0.0223) for 9 mg and +68.8 mL (95% CI 30.2-107.3, P=0.0005) for 18 mg. The ranked-ANCOVA sensitivity analysis was directionally consistent (9 mg P=0.0014; 18 mg P<0.0001). Both doses were approved (18 mg as the standard dose; 9 mg for dose-limiting intolerance or concomitant strong CYP3A inhibitors)

### 42. Depemokimab-ulaa (Exdensur) — BLA 761458

**Sponsor:** GlaxoSmithKline (GSK)

**Indication approved:** Add-on maintenance treatment of severe asthma with an eosinophilic phenotype in adults and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older — an ultra-long-acting anti-interleukin-5 (IL-5) monoclonal antibody dosed once every 6 months (twice yearly); chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps was evaluated in a separate, non-pivotal program (ANCHOR-1/ANCHOR-2) and is not part of this approved indication

**Approval date:** December 16, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** SWIFT-1 (GSK Study 206713), NCT04719832, and SWIFT-2 (GSK Study 213744), NCT04718103

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two independent randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials in adults and adolescents (≥12y) with severe eosinophilic asthma on medium-or-high-dose inhaled corticosteroids plus another controller; depemokimab-ulaa 100 mg subcutaneously once every 6 months vs. placebo; SWIFT-1 N=250/132 (depemokimab/placebo), SWIFT-2 N=252/128 (2:1 allocation); 52-week duration; stratified/adjusted for exacerbation history (2, 3, ≥4 in the prior year), baseline ICS dose (medium/high), region (Europe/US/rest-of-world), and baseline pre-bronchodilator percent-predicted FEV1

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint annualized rate of clinically significant asthma exacerbations over 52 weeks; key secondary endpoints (fixed-sequence hierarchy, closed testing) St. George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ) total score change at Week 52, Asthma Control Questionnaire-5 (ACQ-5) change at Week 52, pre-bronchodilator FEV1 change at Week 52, weekly mean Asthma Nighttime Symptom Diary (ANSD) change, weekly mean Asthma Daytime Symptom Diary (ADSD) change, and annualized rate of exacerbations requiring hospitalization or emergency-department visit

- *Primary analysis:* negative binomial generalized linear model (fixed effects treatment, exacerbation-history category, baseline ICS dose, region, baseline percent-predicted FEV1; offset = years in study)

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing across the primary and 5 key secondary endpoints under a closed testing procedure, two-sided alpha=0.05, each gated on the prior endpoint reaching significance

- *Interim/alpha-spending:* a single unblinded, binding, futility-only interim analysis at approximately 90% of planned pooled randomization (~675 subjects), conducted independently by a statistical data-analysis center and an independent data monitoring committee; because the interim look was futility-only (no early-efficacy-stopping option), overall alpha remained 0.05 with no formal alpha-spending adjustment required

- *Missing data/bias:* missing-at-random assumption for withdrawals; a COVID-19-related discontinuation in SWIFT-1 was handled as an intercurrent event with post-event data excluded; tipping-point sensitivity analysis for departure from the missing-at-random assumption

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held — FDA's review explicitly documents the decision not to convene one, referencing an internal Advisory Committee Decision Aid memorandum

**Trial design & endpoints**

- SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 were independently conducted, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials in severe eosinophilic asthma, each 52 weeks, comparing depemokimab-ulaa 100 mg subcutaneously (dosed at baseline and again at Week 26, i.e., twice yearly) against placebo; SWIFT-1 randomized 250 to depemokimab-ulaa and 132 to placebo, SWIFT-2 randomized 252 to depemokimab-ulaa and 128 to placebo (a 2:1 allocation), both stratified/covariate-adjusted for exacerbation history, baseline ICS dose, region, and baseline lung function

- Primary endpoint: annualized rate of clinically significant asthma exacerbations over 52 weeks, analyzed via negative binomial regression with a person-time offset and covariates for exacerbation-history category, baseline ICS dose, region, and baseline percent-predicted FEV1

- Key secondary endpoints were tested in a fixed-sequence hierarchy under a closed testing procedure: SGRQ total score → ACQ-5 → pre-bronchodilator FEV1 → weekly ANSD → weekly ADSD → exacerbations requiring hospitalization/ED visit, each at two-sided alpha=0.05 and gated on the prior endpoint's significance — this combination of fixed-sequence ordering plus formal closed testing matches existing taxonomy terms directly, requiring no new term

- A single unblinded, binding, futility-only interim analysis was conducted by an independent statistical data-analysis center and data monitoring committee at approximately 90% of planned pooled enrollment (~675 subjects); because the interim analysis carried no efficacy-stopping option, the trials' overall type-I error rate was preserved at 0.05 without a formal alpha-spending function

- Results (FDA Multi-Discipline Review Table 10, consistent with the pooled pivotal publication): SWIFT-1 exacerbation rate 0.46 (depemokimab-ulaa) vs. 1.1 (placebo), rate ratio 0.42 (95% CI 0.3-0.6), P<0.001 (58% reduction, 95% CI 40-70%); SWIFT-2 exacerbation rate 0.54 vs. 1.05, rate ratio 0.52 (95% CI 0.36-0.73), P<0.001 (48% reduction, 95% CI 27-64%)

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761458, Table 10 and statistical-methods section]* — confirms the negative-binomial primary model, the fixed-sequence/closed-testing key-secondary hierarchy, the single futility-only interim analysis, and the reported exacerbation rate ratios and CIs described above.

**Reverse-engineered SAP** [inferred]

- [inferred] The decision to run only a futility-only (not efficacy-stopping) interim analysis was likely a deliberate choice to avoid the alpha-spending complexity of an efficacy-stopping boundary for a twice-yearly-dosed biologic where an early efficacy stop would leave substantial ambiguity about durability across the full 6-month dosing interval — traced to the review's description of the interim analysis's binding-futility-only character and the absence of any efficacy boundary or spending-function discussion in the sections reviewed.

### 43. Tradipitant (Nereus) — NDA 220152

**Sponsor:** Vanda Pharmaceuticals Inc. (compound originally developed by Eli Lilly as LY686017; IND 141315)

**Indication approved:** Prevention of vomiting induced by motion (motion sickness) in adults — a neurokinin-1 (NK-1) receptor antagonist. Note: this NDA/approval is distinct from Vanda's separate, unresolved tradipitant program for gastroparesis (NDA 218489, which received a Complete Response Letter on September 18, 2024) — the two should not be conflated

**Approval date:** December 30, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** Study 3401 "Motion Syros," NCT04327661, and Study 3404 "Motion Serifos," NCT05903924

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 1:1:1 phase 3 trials; single oral dose of tradipitant 85 mg, 170 mg, or placebo given approximately 60 minutes before a boat-trip motion-sickness travel challenge (120-300 minutes); randomization stratified by pooled site/port; Study 3401 N=365 (123/120/122 across 170 mg/85 mg/placebo, approximately), Study 3404 N=316 (104/106/106)

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint proportion of subjects vomiting during the travel challenge; secondary endpoints included worst nausea (visual analog or similar continuous scale), Motion Sickness Assessment Questionnaire (MSAQ) score, and Patient Global Impression of Severity (PGI-S)

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test (common odds ratio) for the primary vomiting-proportion endpoint, adjusted for pooled site/port; ANCOVA (treatment, wave height, pooled site) for continuous secondary endpoints such as worst nausea

- *Multiplicity:* a key-secondary gating structure in which the 85 mg-dose worst-nausea comparison was gated behind the 170 mg-dose worst-nausea comparison in at least one trial (Study 3401), which did not reach significance (P=0.79), affecting how far down that trial's secondary hierarchy could be formally tested

- *Missing data/bias:* no imputation was applied for missing primary-endpoint data (subjects with missing vomiting-status data were excluded from the primary calculation); sensitivity analyses treating missing-data/prohibited-concomitant-medication subjects as vomiting "failures" were consistent with the primary result. FDA identified and resolved (via 2 information requests in March-April 2025) a data-handling discrepancy in which the protocol-specified "pooled port" stratification variable had actually been implemented in the analysis datasets as "pooled site" (two physical sites, 113 and 117, were both mapped to "Port 07"); FDA's own sensitivity analysis confirmed the discrepancy did not materially affect the primary conclusion

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held (FDA's review states one was not warranted, citing limited utility for this indication/evidence base); reviewed by FDA's Division of Gastroenterology, the same division handling Vanda's separate gastroparesis program for the same molecule; sample size was based on ~100 subjects/arm for 96% power assuming a 26% risk-difference in vomiting rate, two-sided alpha=0.05

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Both pivotal trials used a single-oral-dose-before-motion-challenge design: healthy or motion-sickness-prone adults received tradipitant 85 mg, 170 mg, or placebo approximately 60 minutes before a supervised boat-trip travel challenge lasting 120-300 minutes, with randomization 1:1:1 stratified by pooled site/port. Study 3401 (Motion Syros) randomized 365 subjects; Study 3404 (Motion Serifos) randomized 316

- Primary endpoint: proportion of subjects who vomited during the travel challenge, analyzed via a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test (common odds ratio) adjusted for the pooled site/port stratification factor

- Results: in Study 3401, the 170 mg dose showed 18.3% vomiting vs. 44.3% on placebo (CMH-adjusted P<0.0001); the 85 mg dose was directionally similar but its formal secondary-endpoint hierarchy was gated behind a 170 mg worst-nausea comparison that did not reach significance (P=0.79), limiting the alpha-protected claims available for 85 mg in that trial. In Study 3404, both doses were independently significant: 170 mg 10.4% vs. 37.7% placebo (P<0.0001); 85 mg 18.3% vs. 37.7% placebo (P=0.0025)

- FDA's review documents and resolves a stratification-variable implementation discrepancy: the protocol specified stratification by "pooled port" (a travel-route/embarkation-point grouping), but the analysis datasets had implemented a "pooled site" variable instead, with two distinct physical sites (113 and 117) both mapped to "Port 07." FDA issued two information requests (March-April 2025) to resolve this, and its own sensitivity analysis under the correctly-specified stratification found no material impact on the primary conclusion — a reviewer-documented data-handling discrepancy caught and resolved during review rather than reflecting a design flaw per se

- No formal missing-data imputation was applied to the primary vomiting-proportion endpoint (subjects with missing data were excluded from the denominator); FDA's review notes the SAP/protocol did not specify a formal ICH E9(R1)-style estimand framework, a gap the review flags explicitly rather than treating as resolved

- *[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, NDA 220152]* — confirms the CMH-test primary analysis, the pooled-site/pooled-port stratification discrepancy and its resolution via FDA information requests, and the absence of a formal estimand specification in the sponsor's protocol/SAP, consistent with the design and results described above.

**Reverse-engineered SAP** [inferred]

- [inferred] The 85 mg-dose's weaker/gated formal secondary-endpoint standing in Study 3401 (vs. its independently significant result in Study 3404) was most likely a consequence of that trial's specific fixed-sequence gating choice (85 mg worst-nausea gated behind 170 mg worst-nausea) rather than a true difference in the 85 mg dose's pharmacological effect between the two trials, since the underlying vomiting-proportion point estimates for 85 mg were broadly consistent in direction across both trials — traced to the reported per-trial CMH results and the description of the secondary-endpoint gating structure in FDA's review.

### 44. Cipepofol (Cypsedo) — NDA 220482

**Sponsor:** Haisco-USA Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Bridgewater, NJ; a US subsidiary of Haisco Pharmaceutical Group). The compound (code HSK3486) is separately marketed in China as "ciprofol"; the extensive Chinese ciprofol literature reflects a different regulatory record and is not cited here as part of the US pivotal evidentiary basis

**Indication approved:** Induction of general anesthesia in adults undergoing surgery — a fluorinated propofol analog administered intravenously

**Approval date:** May 29, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** HSK3486-304, NCT04711837; HSK3486-305, NCT05478174; and HSK3486-309, NCT05486416

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* three randomized, double-blind, propofol-active-controlled phase 3 trials, allocation ratio 2:1 (cipepofol:propofol), stratified by ASA physical-status class, age, and BMI; HSK3486-304 N=255 (US/EU), HSK3486-305 N=400, HSK3486-309 N=465 (a broader multiregional trial including US, Poland, and Spain sites); combined primary pivotal-trial enrollment >1,100, within a total controlled-trial safety database of 1,329 subjects across 9 trials (723 in the three pivotal trials)

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint successful anesthesia induction, defined as achieving a Modified Observer's Assessment of Alertness/Sedation (MOAA/S) score ≤1 with no more than 1 top-up (rescue) dose and no rescue drug required; key secondary endpoints included injection-site pain and a composite endpoint of adequate anesthesia depth without cardiopulmonary depression

- *Primary analysis:* non-inferiority analysis of the risk difference in induction-success rate (cipepofol minus propofol), non-inferiority margin -8 percentage points, one-sided alpha=0.025, confidence interval via the Miettinen-Nurminen method

- *Multiplicity:* the injection-site-pain key secondary endpoint showed statistically significant heterogeneity in effect size across the three pivotal trials in FDA's post-hoc meta-analysis (P=0.0064, I²=80.2%), attributed by the review to differing pre-induction midazolam premedication regimens between HSK3486-304 and the other two trials; the composite anesthesia-depth-without-cardiopulmonary-depression secondary endpoint was not statistically significant in any of the three trials

- *Missing data/bias:* HSK3486-305 had 2 subjects unblinded during the trial; a sensitivity analysis treating them as induction failures did not change the non-inferiority conclusion; HSK3486-309's handling of intercurrent events/missing data was not formally agreed with FDA prior to database lock, a gap the review documents explicitly; FDA also ran a post-hoc subgroup analysis in patients with BMI≥40 kg/m² (a higher cutoff than the sponsor's protocol-specified 35 kg/m² obesity cutoff), finding inconsistent results in that subgroup

- *Regulatory:* HSK3486-304's target sample size was revised twice during the trial (351 planned → 576 planned in June 2021, to accommodate a co-primary-endpoint discussion with FDA → 255 final in July 2021, once that discussion resolved), with a single DMC review at ~200 enrolled subjects (June 2021); no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held; no REMS was required

**Trial design & endpoints**

- The three pivotal trials each randomized subjects 2:1 to cipepofol or propofol for induction of general anesthesia, stratified by ASA physical-status class, age, and BMI, with success defined as MOAA/S≤1 achieved with no more than 1 top-up dose and no rescue drug. HSK3486-304 (N=255, US/EU) reported induction success of 97.0% (cipepofol) vs. 97.6% (propofol); HSK3486-305 (N=400) reported 99.2% vs. 100%; HSK3486-309 (N=465, a broader multiregional trial) reported 99.3% vs. 98.6%

- Primary analysis: non-inferiority of cipepofol vs. propofol on induction-success risk difference, with a pre-specified -8-percentage-point non-inferiority margin, one-sided alpha=0.025, and a Miettinen-Nurminen confidence interval; non-inferiority was met in all three trials, with 95% CI lower bounds well above the -8% margin in each case

- Notable statistical issues documented in FDA's Multi-Discipline Review: (1) HSK3486-304's target sample size changed twice mid-trial — from 351 planned subjects, to 576 (June 2021, to support a co-primary-endpoint discussion with FDA), to a final 255 (July 2021) once that discussion was resolved, with a single Data Monitoring Committee review at approximately 200 enrolled subjects; (2) injection-site pain, though consistently lower for cipepofol across all three trials descriptively, showed statistically significant cross-trial heterogeneity in FDA's own post-hoc meta-analysis (P=0.0064, I²=80.2%), which the review attributes to differing midazolam-premedication regimens between HSK3486-304 and the other two trials rather than to a true difference in cipepofol's effect; (3) the composite endpoint for anesthesia depth without cardiopulmonary depression was not statistically significant in any of the three trials; (4) HSK3486-305 had 2 subjects unblinded mid-trial, handled via a sensitivity analysis (treated as failures) that did not change conclusions; (5) HSK3486-309's intercurrent-event/missing-data handling was not formally pre-agreed with FDA before database lock; and (6) a post-hoc FDA subgroup analysis in patients with BMI≥40 kg/m² (above the sponsor's protocol-specified 35 kg/m² cutoff) showed inconsistent results, a finding FDA documents without altering its overall approval recommendation

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2026/220482Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/220482Orig1s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (Statistical Reviewer Ruihan Lu, PhD; Statistical Supervisor/Deputy Division Director Sue-Jane Wang, PhD) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/220482Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record, HSK3486-304 — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04711837 — no protocol/SAP posted

- ClinicalTrials.gov record, HSK3486-305 — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05478174 — no protocol/SAP posted

- ClinicalTrials.gov record, HSK3486-309 — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05486416 — no protocol/SAP posted

- Pivotal publication — none identified for the US HSK3486-304/305/309 program specifically. PubMed searches under "cipepofol" return only mechanism/pharmacokinetic/other-indication review articles (e.g., a "From propofol to cipepofol (Cypsedo®)" review, PMID 42566008), not a primary results paper for the three pivotal trials as of this writing; this entry states that plainly rather than substituting the separate Chinese ciprofol literature as if it were the US pivotal basis.

**Other resources**

- No trial-specific Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere participation was independently confirmed for this program; not confirmed either way.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held for this application; no REMS was required.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 220482]* — confirms the -8% non-inferiority margin, one-sided alpha=0.025, Miettinen-Nurminen confidence-interval method, the HSK3486-304 sample-size revision history, the cross-trial injection-site-pain heterogeneity meta-analysis (P=0.0064, I²=80.2%), and the post-hoc BMI≥40 kg/m² subgroup finding, consistent with the design and results above.

**Reverse-engineered SAP** [inferred]

- [inferred] The BMI subgroup cutoff mismatch (protocol-specified 35 kg/m² vs. FDA's post-hoc 40 kg/m² analysis) most likely reflects FDA independently probing a more extreme obesity subgroup after noticing a signal near the protocol's own cutoff, rather than the sponsor having pre-specified the higher threshold — traced to the review's framing of the 40 kg/m² analysis as an FDA-conducted post-hoc addition rather than a sponsor-reported pre-specified subgroup.
