### 45. Gadoquatrane (Ambelvist) — NDA 219627

**Sponsor:** Bayer HealthCare Pharmaceuticals Inc.

**Indication approved:** A macrocyclic gadolinium-based contrast agent (GBCA) indicated for use with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to detect and visualize areas with disrupted blood-brain barrier and/or abnormal vascularity of the central nervous system, and lesions in the head, neck, thorax, abdomen, pelvis, and musculoskeletal system, in adult and pediatric patients including term neonates — administered at 0.01 mmol/kg (0.04 mmol Gd/kg, since each gadoquatrane molecule carries 4 gadolinium ions), one-quarter the standard 0.1 mmol Gd/kg dose of existing macrocyclic GBCAs

**Approval date:** June 12, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** QUANTI CNS (Study 21181), NCT05915702, and QUANTI OBR ("other body region," Study 21197), NCT05915728 (supported by a pediatric PK/safety bridging study, QUANTI Pediatric/Study 21196, NCT05915026)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, crossover diagnostic-accuracy trials — every subject received both gadoquatrane and an approved macrocyclic comparator GBCA (gadobutrol-class) in randomized order, with independent reads by 3 blinded central readers plus a 4th reader performing lesion-matching and a ~10% intra-reader-variability re-read subsample; QUANTI CNS enrolled/screened 321 subjects at 71 centers in 15 countries, randomized 305 (151/154 by administration order), safety population 303, primary Full Analysis Set (≥1 matched lesion) 237; QUANTI OBR primary analysis population 312 (from an overall enrollment of 410)

- *Endpoints:* co-primary endpoints were 3 lesion-visualization scores assessed per matched lesion and averaged per participant per reader — contrast enhancement (4-point scale), border delineation (4-point scale), and internal morphology (3-point scale)

- *Primary analysis:* linear mixed-effects model comparing gadoquatrane-enhanced vs. unenhanced (pre-contrast) imaging for the US/FDA regulatory objective (one-sided alpha=0.025), structured as a **superiority** design for the US, while other regulatory regions' primary objective was **non-inferiority** of gadoquatrane vs. the standard-of-care macrocyclic comparator — the same trial thus carries two different primary-analysis objectives (superiority vs. non-inferiority) keyed to jurisdiction rather than a single global primary hypothesis (*jurisdiction-split primary-endpoint objective (superiority for one regulator, non-inferiority for others) within a single trial* — distinct from the taxonomy's existing "Dual primary-endpoint definition (protocol vs. regulatory)" row, which describes two regulators each requiring a specific version of the same construct, not a superiority-vs-non-inferiority split by jurisdiction)

- *Multiplicity:* study-success rule required superiority to be demonstrated for all 3 visualization scores in at least 2 of the 3 blinded readers

- *Missing data/bias:* 28% of QUANTI CNS participants had a protocol deviation (predominantly missing safety labs); 3 participants had their gadoquatrane/comparator administration order swapped, discovered only after unblinding, and were included in the primary analysis with a post-hoc sensitivity exclusion

- *Regulatory:* protocol Amendment 3 (October 2023) is what introduced the jurisdiction-split superiority/non-inferiority primary-objective structure; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held; no REMS required

**Trial design & endpoints**

- QUANTI CNS and QUANTI OBR were randomized, double-blind, within-subject crossover diagnostic-accuracy trials in which every participant received both gadoquatrane and an approved macrocyclic GBCA comparator, in randomized order, with matched lesions independently scored by 3 blinded central readers (plus a 4th reader for lesion-matching and a ~10% re-read subsample for intra-reader variability). QUANTI CNS randomized 305 subjects (safety population 303; primary Full Analysis Set of subjects with ≥1 matched lesion, 237); QUANTI OBR's primary analysis population was 312 subjects (of 410 total enrolled)

- Co-primary endpoints: 3 lesion-visualization scores (contrast enhancement, border delineation, internal morphology) assessed per matched lesion and averaged per subject per reader

- A protocol amendment (Amendment 3, October 2023) split the trials' primary regulatory objective by jurisdiction: for the US/FDA, the primary objective became superiority of gadoquatrane-enhanced over unenhanced (pre-contrast) imaging on all 3 visualization scores, analyzed via a linear mixed-effects model at one-sided alpha=0.025, requiring superiority in at least 2 of 3 blinded readers; for all other (ex-US) regulatory regions, the primary objective remained non-inferiority of gadoquatrane vs. the standard-of-care macrocyclic comparator agent. This produces a single trial serving two structurally different primary-hypothesis types (superiority vs. non-inferiority) depending on the regulator, which does not cleanly match any existing Keyword_Taxonomy.md row

- Results (QUANTI CNS, FDA Multi-Discipline Review Table 40): all 3 readers reached statistical significance (one-sided P<0.025) on all 3 visualization scores for the US superiority objective — for example, Reader 1's contrast-enhancement score was 1.00 pre-contrast vs. 2.12 post-gadoquatrane, a difference of 1.12 (95% CI 1.00-1.24); all 9 reader-by-score combinations showed positive differences with confidence intervals excluding zero

- Data-quality issues documented by FDA: 28% of QUANTI CNS subjects had a protocol deviation (mostly missing safety labs); 3 subjects had their gadoquatrane/comparator dosing order swapped, caught only after unblinding and included in the primary analysis with a post-hoc sensitivity exclusion; a printer malfunction at one German site truncated some informed-consent forms, and those subjects were nonetheless included

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2026/219627Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/219627Orig1s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (Statistical Reviewer Zhipeng Huang, PhD; Secondary Statistical Reviewer Jyoti Zalkikar, PhD) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/219627Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record, QUANTI CNS — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05915702 — no protocol/SAP posted

- ClinicalTrials.gov record, QUANTI OBR — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05915728 — no protocol/SAP posted

- ClinicalTrials.gov record, QUANTI Pediatric (PK/safety bridging) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05915026 — no protocol/SAP posted

- Pivotal publication — none identified. PubMed searches for gadoquatrane (verified via E-utilities, 15 total indexed results as of this writing) return only preclinical, pharmacokinetic, and phantom-study papers, predominantly in *Investigative Radiology* (Bayer's usual venue for this program) — no QUANTI CNS/OBR phase 3 efficacy-results paper has been identified; this entry states that plainly rather than fabricating a citation.

**Other resources**

- No trial-specific Vivli/YODA/Project Data Sphere participation was independently confirmed for this program; not confirmed either way.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held for this application; no REMS was required.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 219627, Table 40 and statistical-methods section]* — confirms the crossover diagnostic-accuracy design, the Amendment-3-introduced jurisdiction-split superiority (US)/non-inferiority (ex-US) primary-objective structure, the linear mixed-effects primary model, the 2-of-3-readers study-success rule, and the reported per-reader visualization-score differences and CIs described above.

**Reverse-engineered SAP** [inferred]

- [inferred] The jurisdiction-split primary-objective structure (superiority for the US, non-inferiority elsewhere) most likely reflects that FDA specifically required proof that gadoquatrane's quarter-dose still produces genuine diagnostic enhancement over no contrast at all (a more fundamental question given the drug's core value proposition of a much lower gadolinium dose), whereas ex-US regulators with more established macrocyclic-GBCA-relative-efficacy expectations were satisfied by a non-inferiority showing against an already-marketed comparator — traced to the timing and content of Protocol Amendment 3 as described in FDA's Multi-Discipline Review.

## Hematology

### 1. Deferiprone (Ferriprox) — NDA 21825

**Sponsor:** ApoPharma, Inc. (Cato Research Ltd. acted as U.S. agent on the NDA)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of patients with transfusional iron overload due to thalassemia syndromes when current chelation therapy is inadequate

**Approval date:** October 14, 2011, under accelerated approval (21 CFR 314.500)

**Pivotal trial:** Study LA36-0310 — a retrospective, non-randomized, pooled patient-level reanalysis of pre-existing data from 12 of 17 previously conducted ApoPharma studies (no new patients or new data collection; no NCT number, as none of the underlying studies were registered/conducted under a US IND); supportive randomized trial LA16-0102 (no NCT number; predates ClinicalTrials.gov registration norms), published as Pennell et al., *Blood* 2006

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* accelerated-approval resubmission (21 CFR 314.500) following a 2009 Complete Response Letter that rejected the sponsor's original single randomized controlled trial (LA16-0102, cardiac MRI T2* endpoint) because FDA considered that endpoint an unvalidated surrogate for clinical utility; post-hoc pooled reanalysis of patient-level data from multiple previously completed, independently conducted single-arm and randomized studies, with patient eligibility for the pooled analysis determined by an Independent Committee applying pre-agreed inclusion/exclusion criteria rather than by prospective trial enrollment (closest existing taxonomy entries, "Post-hoc recombination of differently-enrolled cohorts into one primary analysis population" and "Retrospective/non-prospective diagnostic evidentiary basis," each describe an adjacent but distinct scenario); supportive randomized, open-label, active (deferoxamine)-controlled trial (LA16-0102, 1:1 randomization) conducted outside a US IND with no FDA input on design

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint (LA36-0310) individual-patient responder status — a ≥20% decline in serum ferritin concentration from baseline within one year of Ferriprox therapy; secondary endpoints a ≥20% increase in cardiac MRI T2* or a ≥20% decline in liver iron concentration (LIC), each within one year; LA16-0102's primary endpoint was mean change in cardiac MRI T2* from baseline at Month 12

- *Primary analysis:* single-proportion responder-rate analysis (simple pooling across 12 studies) with an a priori decision rule that the 95% CI lower bound for the pooled success rate must exceed 20%; FDA reviewer's random-effects meta-analysis and worst-case-scenario non-responder imputation for missing ferritin values as sensitivity analyses; logistic regression used to assess age/sex/baseline-ferritin covariate effects; for LA16-0102, sponsor's pre-specified primary analysis was a two-sample t-test with non-parametric methods (Wilcoxon rank-sum, median test, Kolmogorov-Smirnov) prospectively planned as a fallback if normality was violated — extends the fallback-testing concept in Keyword_Taxonomy.md §3 ("ANCOVA with normality-contingent fallback to a non-parametric test," seen in Riociguat) to a t-test rather than an ANCOVA primary analysis

- *Missing data/bias:* worst-case-scenario non-responder imputation for serum ferritin missing at 12 months (137/264 subjects); explicit reviewer concern that simple pooling of the 12 studies ignored between-study heterogeneity and that lack of randomization/control introduced unresolvable selection bias; FDA reviewer overrode the sponsor's post-hoc log-transformation of MRI T2* (used after the pre-specified t-test failed to reach significance) and instead applied the trial's own pre-specified non-parametric fallback methods, which did reach significance

- *Regulatory:* Complete Response Letter, November 30, 2009; Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee meeting held September 14, 2011 (question: favorable benefit/risk for deferiprone when current chelation is inadequate — 10 Yes, 2 No); accelerated approval with a post-marketing requirement for an agranulocytosis patient registry

**Trial design & endpoints**

- LA36-0310 was not a prospectively designed trial but a sponsor-conducted secondary analysis of existing clinical data: an integrated lab dataset (serum ferritin, LIC, cardiac MRI T2*, demographics, disposition, exposure) from ApoPharma's full clinical program was sent to an Independent Committee, which applied agreed eligibility criteria (treated with Ferriprox; ≥1 baseline value for ferritin/LIC/T2*; ≥1 follow-up assessment within 1 year) to select the analysis cohort — 264 patients qualified on the serum-ferritin criterion, 117 on LIC, and 39 on cardiac MRI T2*, drawn from 12 of 17 submitted studies (4 excluded for not assessing efficacy; 1, LA17-9701, excluded for incomplete database)

- ITT population was defined as all patients with ≥1 dose and ≥1 post-baseline efficacy measurement; for the non-randomized studies contributing to the pool (LA-02/06, LA-03, LA-04/06B, LA11, LA12-9907, LA15-0002, LA28-CMP, LA30-0307, Borgna-Pignatti), all Ferriprox-treated patients with data were included, since there was no randomized comparator to define an ITT set in the conventional sense

- Sponsor's pooled analysis: 52% success rate (95% CI 45-58%); FDA reviewer's independent pooled analysis: 52% (95% CI 45.3-57.7%), consistent with the sponsor, but reviewer flagged large between-study heterogeneity (e.g., LA-12 success rate 26%, 95% CI 9.2-51.2%; LA-15 success rate 100%, 95% CI 81.5-100%) and noted the 95% CI lower bound fell below 20% in 4 of the 12 studies (LA-01, LA-12, LA-18, LA-28)

- Reviewer's formal random-effects meta-analysis (rather than simple pooling) gave a lower point estimate — 50% (95% CI 43.5-57.2%) — and a worst-case-scenario sensitivity analysis imputing all missing 12-month ferritin values as non-response gave 26.89% (95% CI 21.64-32.67%), still above the 20% threshold but much closer to it

- LA16-0102 (supportive randomized trial): two-arm, multicenter, randomized (1:1), open-label, deferoxamine-controlled trial in thalassemia major patients previously treated with deferoxamine, powered as a two-sample t-test superiority comparison (5% two-sided alpha, 80% power, assumed 2.3 ms true mean T2* difference, SD 2.5 ms — the FDA reviewer noted no justification was provided in the study report for these assumptions); observed result was 3.9±3.6 ms (deferiprone, n=29) vs. 2.3±4.1 ms (deferoxamine, n=31), p=0.093 by the pre-specified t-test (endpoint not met); Shapiro-Wilk test found significant non-normality (p<0.001); the sponsor's post-hoc log-transformed reanalysis reached p=0.0228, but FDA's reviewer instead applied the pre-specified non-parametric fallback methods, all three of which were significant (median test p=0.0048, Wilcoxon rank-sum p=0.0124, Kolmogorov-Smirnov asymptotic p=0.0168)

- FDA's reviewer explicitly declined to treat MRI T2* improvement as validated evidence of clinical benefit absent long-term follow-up, and secondary endpoints (6-month T2*, CMR/ECHO LVEF, LVSF, ferritin, LIC) did not consistently support superiority

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2011/021825Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label (original, 2011) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2011/021825lbl.pdf

- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/021825Orig1s000StatR.pdf

- FDA Medical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/021825Orig1s000MedR.pdf

- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/021825Orig1s000SumR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record — none found; LA36-0310 and LA16-0102 predate/fall outside mandatory US trial registration (non-US-IND studies)

- Protocol / SAP — not publicly posted; FDA's Statistical Review quotes and summarizes both the LA36-0310 analysis plan and LA16-0102's SAP (including its pre-specified non-parametric fallback), cited above as verbatim FDA-review text describing those plans

- Pivotal publication (LA16-0102): Pennell DJ, Berdoukas V, Karagiorga M, et al. Randomized controlled trial of deferiprone or deferoxamine in beta-thalassemia major patients with asymptomatic myocardial siderosis. *Blood*. 2006;107(9):3738-3744. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1182/blood-2005-07-2948), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16352815/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Randomized%20controlled%20trial%20of%20deferiprone%20or%20deferoxamine%20in%20beta-thalassemia%20major%20patients%20with%20asymptomatic%20myocardial%20siderosis)

**Other resources**

- No trial-specific IPD/dataset access program (Vivli, YODA, Project Data Sphere) confirmed for ApoPharma or this program

- FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee meeting held September 14, 2011; committee voted 10-2 that the benefit/risk profile was favorable for patients in whom current chelation therapy is inadequate

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID: 3016315), Executive Summary]* "The sponsor's efficacy analysis for serum ferritin by pooling 12 studies showed that the overall success rate was 52% with 95% CI of (45%, 58%). As the lower limit of the 95% CI is larger than 20%, the protocol defined endpoint was met for this trial. However, this study has several serious limitations including lack of randomization, lack of control group, high rate of missing data and ignoring the variation between studies by simple pooling, all of which can introduce biases to the primary outcome."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID: 3016315), §3.2.2, Reviewer's Comment]* "During the review of the submissions, the Agency raised a concern of selection bias due to the lack of randomization. In order to minimize such bias, the Agency suggested sponsor using an Independent Committee to select subjects from the entire integrated dataset following approved inclusion and exclusion criteria."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, secondary review of LA16-0102 (Reference ID: 3016315)]* "Non-parametric methods (that do not assume normality) were prospectively planned as alternative analysis methods in the case of violation of normality assumption by the company in their statistical analysis plan (SAP)."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, secondary review of LA16-0102]* "The company noted this situation and instead of following pre-specified SAP, they used log transformation on MRI T2* ... This post-hoc analysis based on log transformation showed a statistically significant difference in favor of Deferiprone (p=0.0228). In addition to being post-hoc and not confirmatory, these results are subject to the same limitations as the raw MRI T2* data due to lack of normality ... The primary reviewer at the FDA followed the company's SAP and used non-parametric methods to evaluate these data which were prospectively planned in the case of violation of normality."

- **Reverse-engineered SAP** (for LA36-0310's underlying pooling logic, where the sponsor's own written analysis plan was not independently located as a standalone document): *[inferred]* the 20% ferritin-decline responder threshold and the requirement that the 95% CI lower bound exceed it were the pre-specified decision rule, traceable to the reviewer's repeated statement that "the protocol defined endpoint was met" once the pooled 95% CI (45-58%) cleared 20%; *[inferred]* the choice to define the ITT-equivalent population as "all patients with ≥1 dose and ≥1 post-baseline measurement" (rather than a stricter completer-only set) is traceable to the reviewer's parallel report of a Per-Protocol sensitivity analysis (51%, 95% CI 45-58%) nearly identical to the primary result, implying the primary analysis set was deliberately broader/more inclusive than PP by design rather than by accident.

### 2. Peginesatide (Omontys) — NDA 202799

**Sponsor:** Affymax, Inc. (co-developed and commercialized in the US under a collaboration with Takeda Pharmaceutical Company Limited/Takeda Pharmaceuticals U.S.A., Inc., which became sole NDA holder after Affymax exited the partnership in 2013)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of anemia due to chronic kidney disease (CKD) in adult patients on dialysis (explicitly not indicated for CKD patients not on dialysis or for chemotherapy-associated anemia)

**Approval date:** March 27, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** EMERALD 1 (Study AFX01-12, NCT00597753) and EMERALD 2 (Study AFX01-14, NCT00597584) — two identically designed Phase 3, randomized, open-label, active (epoetin alfa)-controlled non-inferiority trials in hemodialysis patients; companion PEARL 1 (Study AFX01-11, NCT00598273) and PEARL 2 (Study AFX01-13, NCT00598442) trials in non-dialysis CKD patients were conducted and reviewed for safety, but the sponsor did not seek that indication after PEARL showed a numerically worse cardiovascular composite safety signal for peginesatide vs. darbepoetin alfa

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two identically protocoled randomized, open-label, active-controlled non-inferiority trials (EMERALD 1/2) in dialysis patients, 2:1 randomization (peginesatide:epoetin alfa), stratified by mean screening hemoglobin (≤11.4 vs. ≥11.5 g/dL) and NYHA heart-failure class; four-period design (≤6-week screening, 28-week titration, 8-week evaluation, long-term-safety-and-efficacy follow-up to week 52+); companion randomized, open-label, active (darbepoetin alfa)-controlled non-inferiority trials in non-dialysis CKD patients (PEARL 1/2), conducted under the same program but reviewed for safety only, since the sponsor never pursued that indication; prespecified cross-trial pooled cardiovascular composite-safety-endpoint (CSE) analysis spanning all four Phase 3 trials (dialysis + non-dialysis), independently adjudicated by a blinded Event Review Committee ("Prespecified cross-trial pooled composite cardiovascular safety-endpoint analysis, independently adjudicated, run alongside separately-populated non-inferiority efficacy trials")

- *Endpoints:* primary efficacy endpoint — mean change in hemoglobin from baseline to the evaluation period (non-inferiority margin 1.0 g/dL, peginesatide minus control); primary safety endpoint — time to first Composite Safety Endpoint (CSE) event, a six-component composite of all-cause death, stroke, myocardial infarction, congestive heart failure, unstable angina, and arrhythmia, each independently adjudicated; a post hoc three-component "MACE CSE" (death, stroke, MI only) was defined "after preliminary Phase 3 and CSE findings were known"

- *Primary analysis:* non-inferiority analysis of mean hemoglobin change via two-sided confidence interval compared against the 1.0 g/dL margin; stratified Cox proportional-hazards regression for the CSE hazard ratio, with the primary evaluation based on a one-sided 95% confidence interval constructed to test whether the upper bound excluded a hazard ratio of 1.3 (i.e., whether peginesatide's CSE risk could be ruled out as ≥30% higher than the ESA comparator's); a secondary two-sided-CI analysis of the same HR was also reported

- *Missing data/bias:* FDA statistical reviewer flagged that the sponsor's designated primary efficacy population ("Fully Analysis Population" — all randomized patients dosed, analyzed as randomized, with ≥1 post-baseline assessment) technically violates the intention-to-treat principle relative to the "Randomized Population," but accepted it because the two populations differed by only 1.2%

- *Regulatory:* approved with a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) in place at launch; Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee meeting held December 7, 2011 (15 Yes, 1 No, 1 Abstain on whether benefit/risk was favorable in the dialysis population despite a worse CSE/MACE safety signal observed in the non-dialysis PEARL trials); voluntary nationwide market withdrawal, February 23, 2013, following postmarketing reports of serious hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis, some fatal; FDA formally withdrew approval of NDA 202799 under 21 CFR 314.150(d), effective February 13, 2019, at Takeda's request after Takeda waived its hearing opportunity

**Trial design & endpoints**

- EMERALD 1/2 (AFX01-12/-14): Phase 3, randomized (2:1), active-controlled, open-label, multicenter trials of peginesatide vs. continued epoetin alfa for maintenance anemia treatment in ~750 hemodialysis patients each, at ~120 sites; peginesatide dosed IV every 4 weeks (starting dose 0.04-0.16 mg/kg based on prior epoetin alfa dose) vs. epoetin alfa 1-3x/week IV; patients followed a minimum of 52 weeks post-randomization

- Primary efficacy endpoint assessed during an 8-week evaluation period (weeks 29-36) following a 28-week titration period; the trial design was explicitly built around demonstrating hemoglobin-maintenance non-inferiority, not superiority

- Cardiovascular safety was evaluated via a program-wide, prospectively-planned pooled CSE analysis across all four Phase 3 trials (EMERALD 1/2 + PEARL 1/2), discussed with FDA in advance; sample-size determination assumed a 17.4% annual CSE event rate in both arms, requiring 553 patients with CSE events to exclude a hazard ratio >1.3 with 89% probability (one-sided 95% CI), which in turn required enrolling 2,400 patients across the pooled Phase 3 program (1,600 peginesatide : 800 control)

- Reported CSE hazard ratios: pooled dialysis population HR=0.94-0.95 (95% CI approximately 0.76-1.16, favorable/neutral); pooled non-dialysis (PEARL) population HR=1.28-1.34 (95% CI up to 2.05), i.e., a numerically worse safety signal in the non-dialysis setting, which the sponsor and ODAC treated as population-specific and not disqualifying for the dialysis indication

- FDA's statistical reviewer's independent tabulation showed CSE and MACE hazard ratios varying by dialysis-population subgroup (e.g., HR 0.85 [0.68, 1.07] in one dialysis comparison vs. HR 1.30 [0.92, 1.84] in a non-dialysis comparison), consistent with the sponsor's population-specific safety conclusions

- **Post-market safety history**: On February 23, 2013, Affymax and Takeda voluntarily recalled all lots of Omontys and suspended marketing following postmarketing reports of serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, that can be life-threatening or fatal; these reactions were reported to occur predominantly within 30 minutes of the first dose. FDA formally withdrew NDA 202799's approval effective February 13, 2019, at Takeda's request. This is the only drug in this batch (and among a small number in the full census) that reached the US market and was subsequently withdrawn entirely for a post-marketing safety signal unrelated to the confirmatory-trial-failure pattern seen elsewhere in the census.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID: 3083540), §2.3]* "The Phase 3 dialysis studies AFX01-12 and AFX01-14 were designed to evaluate the efficacy of Peginesatide compared to Epoetin using a non-inferiority design. Subjects were randomized 2:1 to receive study treatment and underwent a 28-week titration period followed by an 8-week evaluation period... The primary efficacy endpoint in all controlled CRF studies was the mean change from baseline in Hgb during the evaluation period; the treatment difference between the Peginesatide groups and active control was assessed."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §2.3, on the CSE program design]* "The phase 3 program was designed to include prospective analysis of predefined CV CSE based on pooled data from four phase 3 studies, as well as separate analyses for the dialysis and non-dialysis populations. The events to be included in the CSE analysis included all-cause death, myocardial infraction (MI), stroke, and SAE of congestive heart failure (CHF), unstable angina, and arrhythmia. Events were adjudicated by an Independent Event Review Committee (ERC)."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2, on sample size for the CSE analysis]* "Assuming a 17.4% annual event rate for the CSE for the pooled dialysis and non-dialysis populations in both groups, a total of 553 patients with CSE events were required for a one-sided 95% confidence interval to exclude a hazard ratio greater than 1.3 with 89% probability... To observe 553 patients with CSE events required enrolling 2400 patients in Phase 3 studies (1600 [peginesatide] ... 800 [control])."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, on the post hoc MACE-CSE endpoint]* "An additional post hoc endpoint referred to as the MACE CSE (where MACE refers to Major Adverse Cardiovascular Event) was defined after preliminary Phase 3 and CSE findings were known; the MACE CSE consisted of three of the six CSE events: death, stroke and MI."

- *[verbatim, Federal Register 84 FR 3795-96, Feb. 13, 2019]* "On February 23, 2013, Affymax, Inc. and Takeda voluntarily recalled all lots of OMONTYS and suspended its marketing as a result of postmarketing reports of serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, which can be life-threatening or fatal."

### 3. Defibrotide sodium (Defitelio) — NDA 208114

**Sponsor:** Gentium S.r.L. (an Italian biotech acquired by Jazz Pharmaceuticals in 2014; Jazz Pharmaceuticals, Inc. served as U.S. agent/co-applicant on the NDA)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adult and pediatric patients with hepatic veno-occlusive disease (VOD), also known as sinusoidal obstruction syndrome (SOS), with renal or pulmonary dysfunction following hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT)

**Approval date:** March 30, 2016 (regular/full approval, not accelerated)

**Pivotal trial:** Study 2005-01 (NCT00358501) — a multicenter, open-label, non-randomized historical-control study comparing a prospectively enrolled defibrotide-treated cohort (n=102) against a retrospectively assembled historical-control cohort (n=32) drawn from 6,867 HSCT recipients at 35 centers; supported by Study 99-118, a randomized, open-label, dose-finding Phase 2 trial (n=150, two defibrotide dose arms, no control arm) and Study 2006-05, an ongoing US expanded-access/Treatment IND protocol

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* multicenter, open-label, historical-control (non-randomized) trial as the pivotal efficacy study, with propensity-score stratified weighting (quintile/quartile) used to adjust for four pre-specified baseline prognostic covariates (ventilator/dialysis dependence, age ≤16, allogeneic vs. autologous transplant, prior stem cell transplant) — an unusually scrutinized use of a historical-control design for a pivotal registration trial, where the historical-control cohort was itself re-selected twice (86→32 patients) after a Data Safety Monitoring Board reviewed unblinded interim efficacy results and found the initial control cohort's response/survival rates "unexpected" (a historical-control cohort re-selected mid-study after an unblinded interim look, not currently in Keyword_Taxonomy.md); supportive randomized (1:1), open-label, dose-finding Phase 2 trial (Study 99-118) comparing two defibrotide dose levels with no untreated/placebo arm; supportive single-arm expanded-access/Treatment IND cohort (Study 2006-05) and a compassionate-use program dataset (Study DF-CUP) running since 1997

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint survival rate at Day+100 post-HSCT; key secondary endpoint complete response (CR) rate by Day+100; other secondary endpoints CR by Day+180, survival at Day+180, and overall survival; Study 99-118's primary endpoint was CR rate, with Day+100 survival as a secondary endpoint

- *Primary analysis:* propensity-score-stratified (quintile/quartile) weighted difference in binary Day+100 survival rate between the defibrotide and historical-control cohorts, with confidence intervals constructed via the Koch et al. (1990) method for a covariate-adjusted difference of proportions ("Koch (1990) propensity-score-stratified confidence interval for a difference in proportions" is not in Keyword_Taxonomy.md's existing list of CI-construction methods); a non-standard 95.1% (not 95%) two-sided confidence level was used in an attempt to preserve an overall two-sided 0.01 study-wise alpha across multiple interim looks

- *Interim/alpha-spending:* one interim analysis was pre-specified in the SAP (at 40 defibrotide-cohort patients with efficacy data, ~80 controls), with a two-sided significance level of 0.001 at that interim and 0.009 at final analysis to preserve overall two-sided alpha of 0.01; the sponsor instead conducted three interim analyses (January, May, and September 2008), the second and third of which were unplanned and lacked pre-specified alpha adjustment — FDA's reviewer concluded the study-wise type-I error rate could not be confirmed as controlled at the planned 0.01 level

- *Missing data/bias:* FDA's statistical reviewer identified that Koch's method is invalid when any propensity-score stratum has ≤1 patient (observed in the sponsor's primary analysis) and that the historical-control cohort's small size (32, vs. a planned 80) made stratified analysis unreliable; reviewer explicitly could not confirm the sponsor's primary point estimate or its statistical significance because the final historical-control cohort was re-selected by the Medical Review Committee only after the DSMB's unblinded interim review of efficacy results, meaning the control-cohort selection was not a prospectively fixed analysis

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held ("the application did not raise significant public health questions... outside expertise was not necessary," per FDA's Medical Review); approval granted as a regular (not accelerated) approval despite the FDA statistical reviewer's explicit statement that the pivotal trial's primary efficacy analysis could not be confirmed for inference purposes, with the totality-of-evidence approval resting substantially on supportive Phase 2 (Study 99-118) and expanded-access data showing consistent numerical improvement

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 2005-01: defibrotide cohort (n=102, HSCT dates 2006-2008) received a fixed dose of 25 mg/kg/day in 4 divided doses for a recommended minimum of 21 days, continued as clinically indicated; historical-control cohort (n=32, HSCT dates 1995-2007 — a 12-year span vs. the treated cohort's 2-year span) received best supportive care and was selected from 6,867 HSCT recipients at 35 centers by a Medical Review Committee (2 independent hematologists) via chart review, an overall selection rate of 0.5%

- Original planned enrollment was 80 patients per cohort (99% power, two-sided 0.01 alpha, to detect a CR-rate difference of 46% vs. 11%); the historical-control cohort was ultimately reduced to 32 after the MRC's final (July 2008) blinded chart re-review for unequivocal VOD-with-organ-dysfunction diagnosis, which removed 54 of the 86 patients selected at the time of the second DSMB interim look

- Propensity score for cohort membership was estimated via logistic regression on 4 baseline covariates (dichotomous), yielding at most 16 possible score values; patients were stratified into quintiles/quartiles, and the Koch (1990) method was used to compute a propensity-weighted, cross-stratum-pooled confidence interval for the survival-rate (and CR-rate) difference; a 95.1%, not 95%, CI was used, with the lower bound required to exceed 0 to claim superiority

- Reported results: unadjusted Day+100 survival was 38.2% (39/102) for defibrotide vs. 25.0% (8/32) for historical control (unadjusted difference 13.2%, later reported in the label as 13.0%, 95% CI -4.6% to 31%); the sponsor's propensity-score-adjusted (Koch-method) difference was 23.0% (95.1% CI 5.2% to 40.8%), which the sponsor and label treated as demonstrating superiority since the lower bound exceeded 0

- FDA's statistical reviewer, however, found the sponsor's primary analysis inadequate on methodological grounds (a propensity-score stratum with only 1 patient, which invalidates the Koch method; unadjusted-vs-adjusted estimates varying substantially depending on stratification algorithm; small historical-control sample size undermining stratified inference) and concluded the primary efficacy result "cannot [be confirmed]... for inference purpose," while still noting the data showed "consistent numerical improvement" warranting approval in the context of a fatal, treatment-refractory condition with no approved alternative (associated mortality >80% if VOD with multi-organ dysfunction is left untreated)

- Study 99-118 (supportive): randomized (75 vs. 75), open-label, dose-finding Phase 2 trial (no control/placebo arm) comparing defibrotide 25 mg/kg/day (matching the pivotal-trial dose) vs. 40 mg/kg/day; the 25 mg/kg arm achieved a 46.7% (95% CI 35.1-58.6%) CR rate and 44.0% (95% CI 32.8-55.2%) Day+100 survival — numerically consistent with, and somewhat more favorable than, the pivotal trial's defibrotide-cohort results, used by FDA as corroborating (not confirmatory) evidence

- No trial-specific IPD/dataset access program (Vivli, YODA, Project Data Sphere) confirmed for Gentium/Jazz Pharmaceuticals for this program

- Defibrotide had a long US pre-approval history via a compassionate-use program (since 1997) and a Treatment IND expanded-access protocol (Study 2006-05, ongoing at the time of approval, 681 patients across 78 US sites) — an unusually large real-world pre-approval safety/efficacy dataset feeding into FDA's totality-of-evidence approval decision alongside the two formal trials

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID: 3871769), §2.2.1]* "Study 2005-01 was a multicenter, open-label, historical control study designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of defibrotide for the treatment of hepatic VOD with evidence of multi-organ dysfunction following HSCT... The ultimately selected historical control cohort consisted of 32 subjects with a selection rate of 0.5%."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §2.2.1, Reviewer's Comment on DSMB-driven re-selection]* "Because the ultimate historical control cohort was selected after DSMB reviewing the efficacy results and it suggested a re-selection after unblinded look of the data, efficacy analyses with the 32 historical control patients may not be considered as a prospectively defined analysis."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §2.2.1, on the analysis method]* "For each individual, a propensity score for cohort membership (defibrotide cohort vs. historical control cohort) was calculated using a logistic regression, with 'cohort membership' as the outcome and 4 baseline prognostic factors... A propensity score adjusted Koch's 95.1% confidence interval with a lower bound above 0 was interpreted as demonstrating superiority of the defibrotide cohort over the historical control cohort."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §4.1, Statistical Issues]* "Koch's method does not allow for a sample size of 1 or smaller in any of the propensity score stratum and a size of 1 is observed in one of the stratum in the sponsor's primary analysis... therefore the reviewer does not consider the sponsor's primary analysis adequate."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §4.2, Conclusions and Recommendations]* "Due to the concerns of the validity of the propensity score adjusted analysis for small sample size and a variability of treatment effect estimates based on various propensity defined strata, the reviewer cannot confirm the sponsor's primary efficacy results for inference purpose (i.e. either the treatment effect estimates or the p-value). However, the data show consistent numerical improvement of day + 100 survival rate from the defibrotide treated cohort compared with the historical control cohort which may warrant further investigation."

- **Reverse-engineered SAP** (interim-analysis alpha allocation, where the sponsor's original written SAP document itself was not independently located, only FDA's description of it): *[inferred]* the planned single interim analysis (at 40 defibrotide patients/~80 controls) with a two-sided 0.001 interim / 0.009 final split is traceable directly to FDA's reviewer narrative describing "the SAP" in this way; *[inferred]* the fact that three (not one) interim analyses actually occurred, with the second and third unplanned, is traceable to the reviewer's Table 4 cross-referencing DSMB meeting dates (January, May, September 2008) against the pre-specified single-look plan.

### 4. Emicizumab-kxwh (Hemlibra) — BLA 761083

**Sponsor:** Genentech, Inc. (a member of the Roche Group; molecule originated by Chugai Pharmaceutical)

**Indication approved:** Routine prophylaxis to prevent or reduce the frequency of bleeding episodes in adult and pediatric patients with hemophilia A (congenital factor VIII deficiency) with factor VIII inhibitors

**Approval date:** November 16, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** HAVEN 1 (Study BH29884, NCT02622321), a randomized, open-label, Phase III trial in adults/adolescents (≥12 years) with hemophilia A and FVIII inhibitors, with supportive single-arm evidence from HAVEN 2 (Study BH29992, pediatric <12 years, interim analysis)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, open-label, multi-arm trial combining a randomized concurrent comparison (Arm A: emicizumab prophylaxis, N=35; Arm B: no prophylaxis/continued episodic bypassing-agent treatment, N=18, 2:1 allocation) with two non-randomized arms (Arm C: emicizumab prophylaxis in patients previously on bypassing-agent prophylaxis, N=49; Arm D: patients from the sponsor's non-interventional study unable to enroll in Arms A/B/C before closure, N=7); intra-patient (within-subject) comparison against each patient's own prospectively collected bleed-rate data from a separate non-interventional study (NIS BH29768) conducted before trial enrollment, layered onto the concurrent randomized comparison as pre-specified secondary endpoints rather than as the primary evidentiary basis (adapted from Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1 "Retrospective natural-history/genotype-matched external-control comparison" — but here the comparator is each subject's own prior bleed history, not a separate matched cohort; **intra-patient historical bleed-rate comparison layered onto a concurrent randomized arm, analyzed via a repeated-measures negative-binomial model**); supportive single-arm trial (HAVEN 2) in a pediatric population where randomization was not conducted; small trial in a rare inherited bleeding disorder population with FVIII inhibitors (a subset of an already-rare disease)

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint annualized rate of treated bleeds (ABR) comparing Arm A vs. Arm B; secondary endpoints ABR for all bleeds, treated joint bleeds, treated spontaneous bleeds, and treated target joint bleeds (Arm A vs. Arm B), plus the same bleed categories compared intra-patient (Arm A and Arm C vs. each patient's own NIS bleed rate); patient-reported outcome secondary endpoints (Haem-A-QoL physical-health subscale and total score, EQ-5D-5L index/VAS) at 25 weeks

- *Primary analysis:* negative binomial (NB) regression model of bleed counts with an offset for time on study and a stratification factor for prior bleed frequency (<9 vs. ≥9 bleeds in the 24 weeks before study entry), estimating a rate ratio (λ-treatment/λ-control) tested at 2-sided α=0.05; same NB model structure re-used for the intra-patient comparison with a SAS GENMOD `REPEATED` statement to account for within-patient correlation across the two time periods; sensitivity analyses using zero-inflated negative binomial regression, the van Elteren test, an unstratified NB model, and the Wilcoxon rank-sum test

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence hierarchical testing across 12 ordered secondary endpoints (all-bleeds Arm A vs. B → all-bleeds intra-patient Arm A → treated-bleeds intra-patient Arm A → treated joint bleeds Arm A vs. B → all-bleeds intra-patient Arm C → treated-bleeds intra-patient Arm C → treated spontaneous bleeds → treated target joint bleeds → four PRO endpoints), gated behind a statistically significant primary endpoint, each tested at 2-sided α=0.05

- *Missing data/bias:* electronic-diary (handheld device) bleed data collection designed to prevent missing/partial entries, yielding complete data for the bleed-related endpoints per the FDA reviewer; PRO missingness (13% no-prophylaxis arm, 19% emicizumab arm) analyzed under a missing-at-random assumption without imputation, with FDA-requested sensitivity analyses performed

- *Regulatory:* Breakthrough Therapy Designation (granted September 2015); rolling BLA review; two Dear Investigator Letters issued during the trial after thrombotic microangiopathy and thromboembolic events occurred in patients receiving high cumulative doses of activated prothrombin complex concentrate (aPCC) alongside emicizumab, leading to a protocol amendment restricting/limiting aPCC use and a temporary enrollment halt pending independent DMC review; FDA statistical reviewer explicitly noted the trial "was not designed to demonstrate superiority over prophylaxis with any bypassing agents" for the intra-patient comparison and that results "should be interpreted with caution" given the historical, non-randomized nature of that comparator

**Trial design & endpoints**

- HAVEN 1 (BH29884) enrolled adult and adolescent (≥12 years) patients with hemophilia A and FVIII inhibitors across 11 countries; Arms A and B were randomized in a 2:1 ratio (emicizumab prophylaxis at 3 mg/kg subcutaneously weekly for 4 weeks then 1.5 mg/kg weekly, vs. no prophylaxis/continued on-demand bypassing-agent treatment), stratified by prior bleed frequency; Arm C (non-randomized, N=49) enrolled patients who had been on prior bypassing-agent *prophylaxis* (as opposed to Arms A/B's episodic-treatment population) and switched to emicizumab prophylaxis; Arm D (N=7) enrolled patients from the sponsor's separate non-interventional study (NIS BH29768) who could not be placed in Arms A-C before those arms closed to enrollment

- Primary efficacy analysis was planned for the time point when all randomized (Arm A/B) patients reached 24 weeks in the study or discontinued; a subset of 24 patients in Arm A and 24 in Arm C had also participated in the NIS BH29768 (which prospectively collected each patient's bleed history under standard-of-care bypassing-agent treatment before HAVEN 1 enrollment), enabling the intra-patient comparison

- Primary endpoint: annualized rate of treated bleeds, ABR = (number of treated bleeds / days in the efficacy period) × 365.25; "treated bleed" required treatment with a coagulation factor and satisfaction of a 72-hour non-recurrence rule; secondary bleed endpoints (all bleeds, treated joint/spontaneous/target-joint bleeds) used analogous ABR definitions

- Sample size (35 Arm A, 18 Arm B) was explicitly not based on a formal power calculation for a hypothesized treatment effect but on the limited number of eligible FVIII-inhibitor patients available for a Phase III trial in this rare population; a post hoc statistical simulation using East v6 (Cytel) confirmed adequate power (90% at 2-sided α=0.05, 2:1 allocation) across a range of assumed control-arm bleed rates (18-30 events/year) and treatment-arm rates (1-4 events/year)

- No interim efficacy analysis was planned or conducted; the primary analysis population was the intent-to-treat set (all randomized patients, analyzed as randomized)

- Primary result: model-based ABR 2.9 for emicizumab prophylaxis vs. 23.3 for no prophylaxis (rate ratio 0.13, 95% CI 0.057-0.277, p<0.0001), an 87% relative reduction; 22/35 (62.9%) Arm A patients had zero treated bleeds vs. 1/18 (5.6%) in Arm B (Table 10, MDR p.68). All four secondary bleed-rate comparisons (Arm A vs. B) were statistically significant at p≤0.005 (Table 11, MDR p.69). Intra-patient comparisons: for the 24 Arm C patients, treated-bleed ABR fell from 15.7 (on prior bypassing-agent prophylaxis, from NIS data) to 3.3 on emicizumab (ratio 0.21, 95% CI 0.089-0.486, p=0.0003); for the 24 Arm A patients, treated-bleed ABR fell from 21.6 (on prior episodic bypassing-agent treatment) to 1.7 on emicizumab (ratio 0.08, 95% CI 0.031-0.198, p<0.0001) (Tables 12-13, MDR pp.71-72)

- HAVEN 2 (BH29992), a single-arm Phase III trial in children <12 years with FVIII inhibitors, was reviewed as supportive evidence at an interim analysis and showed a similarly low treated-bleed rate; it was not randomized and was not the basis for a between-arm statistical comparison

- No public FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held for this BLA

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Statistical Review section, p.59]*: "The primary efficacy analysis, defined as comparing the number of bleeds over time for patients randomized to receive prophylactic emicizumab vs. no prophylaxis (Arm A vs. Arm B), was planned to be conducted after all randomized patients have completed 24 weeks in the study or the last randomized patient who has not completed 24 weeks in the study discontinued study participation, whichever occurs first. ... This analytic model estimates the rate ratio, λt/λc, which quantifies the risk of bleeding associated with prophylactic emicizumab (λt) in comparison to no prophylaxis (λc). Statistical significance is controlled at the 2-sided, 0.05 alpha (α) level."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Statistical Review section, p.60]*: "In the intra-patient comparison, only patients who participated in the non-interventional study (NIS) BH29768 are included. ... The analysis method is the NB regression model as for the primary endpoint with the exception that the SAS GENMOD procedure includes a REPEATED statement to account for the intra-patient comparison."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Statistical Review section, p.71 — reviewer's assessment of the intra-patient comparator's validity]*: "The intra-patient comparison in Arm C compared patients' prior prophylaxis with a bypassing agent with emicizumab prophylaxis. Only patients previously enrolled in NIS BH29768 were included to insure robust collection of bleeding information prior to emicizumab prophylaxis and while on emicizumab prophylaxis. The study was not designed to demonstrate superiority over prophylaxis with any bypassing agents. However, the comparisons were to aPCC and rFVIIa which are the only agents available for prophylaxis for patients with FVIII inhibitors. Superiority over other products has not been proven, and results should be interpreted with caution."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Executive Summary, p.13]*: "The recommendation is based on the finding of a decrease in annualized bleeding rate (ABR) with emicizumab prophylaxis compared with no prophylaxis demonstrated in Study HAVEN1. The study also included an intra-patient comparison which demonstrated a decrease in ABR for patients on emicizumab prophylaxis compared to their prior prophylaxis regimen. A single arm study, HAVEN2, showed a low occurrence of bleeds in pediatric patients, similar to the findings in adults."

### 5. Fostamatinib disodium hexahydrate (Tavalisse) — NDA 209299

**Sponsor:** Rigel Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of thrombocytopenia in adult patients with chronic immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) who have had an insufficient response to a previous treatment

**Approval date:** April 17, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** Two identically designed Phase III trials, Study C788-047 (FIT1, NCT02076412) and Study C788-048 (FIT2, NCT02076399), both randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two identically designed, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group Phase III trials (2:1 fostamatinib:placebo allocation) in adults with persistent/chronic ITP refractory to at least one prior ITP therapy; supportive long-term open-label extension trial (Study C788-049)

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint a binary responder definition — achievement of a "stable platelet response," defined as platelet count ≥50,000/mcL on at least 4 of the last 6 scheduled visits between Weeks 14-24, with patients discontinuing for lack of efficacy/adverse event or receiving rescue treatment after Week 10 counted as non-responders; secondary endpoints included platelet response (≥50,000/mcL) at Weeks 12 and 24, a platelet-count-rise threshold endpoint in patients with severe baseline thrombocytopenia (<15,000/mcL), and bleeding severity by the ITP Bleeding Score (IBLS) and WHO bleeding scale

- *Primary analysis:* two-sided Fisher's exact test of the difference in responder proportions between fostamatinib and placebo, α=0.05, on the intent-to-treat population, with a matching per-protocol analysis as a sensitivity check

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing of the ordered secondary endpoints, each tested only if all prior endpoints in the sequence were statistically significant, each at α=0.05

- *Missing data/bias:* sponsor's SAP specified last-observation-carried-forward (LOCF) imputation for missing platelet counts contributing to the primary endpoint; FDA statistical reviewer explicitly rejected LOCF as the basis for its own primary analysis (see SAP section below), instead treating scheduled visits with no platelet measurement as non-response, consistent with FDA's precedent for another ITP thrombopoietin-receptor agonist (romiplostim/Nplate); FDA also substituted an exact unconditional confidence-interval method for the sponsor's normal-approximation and Miettinen-Nurminen/Newcombe interval estimates for the treatment-difference in responder proportions, judging the latter methods to have poor coverage at this sample size and response-rate range

- *Regulatory:* Reviewer-documented deviation from FDA's pre-specified analytic advice — FDA's March 26, 2014 advice letter told the sponsor the Agency did not agree with LOCF imputation for the primary endpoint, but the SAP retained LOCF as the primary specified method, requiring FDA to conduct its own non-LOCF analysis for the regulatory decision (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §7, "Reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Both trials enrolled adults with persistent or chronic primary ITP with a baseline platelet count below a qualifying threshold and an insufficient response to at least one prior ITP therapy; patients were randomized 2:1 to oral fostamatinib (100 mg twice daily, increased to 150 mg twice daily after 4 weeks if platelet count had not risen to ≥50,000/mcL) or matching placebo for 24 weeks, with blood-pressure monitoring and a pre-specified antihypertensive-management/dose-interruption algorithm given fostamatinib's known hypertension signal

- Sample size was 75 patients per trial (50 fostamatinib : 25 placebo), based on a two-sided Fisher's exact test with α=0.05, 90% power, assuming a true response proportion of 0.40 for fostamatinib vs. 0.05 for placebo

- Efficacy analyses were run on the intent-to-treat population (all randomized patients) as the primary analysis, with a per-protocol population as a supportive/sensitivity population; safety analyses used the as-treated population

- Individual-trial primary-endpoint results using the sponsor's LOCF method: Study 047, 17.6% (9/51) fostamatinib vs. 0% (0/25) placebo, difference 17.6% (exact 95% CI −6.06% to 40.26%; normal-approximation 95% CI 7.18-28.11%), Fisher's exact p=0.0261; Study 048, 18.0% (9/50) fostamatinib vs. 4.2% (1/24) placebo, difference 13.8% (exact 95% CI −10.95% to 37.55%), p=0.1519 (Table 35, MDR p.114). Pooled across both trials (LOCF): 17.8% (18/101) fostamatinib vs. 2.0% (1/49) placebo, difference 15.8% (exact 95% CI −1.28% to 32.3%) (Table 46, MDR p.125); under FDA's own non-LOCF definition the pooled responder rates were 16.8% (17/101) vs. 2.0% (1/49), difference 14.8% (exact 95% CI −2.26% to 31.41%)

- FDA's review concluded that although Study 048 alone did not reach statistical significance under either imputation method, the pooled and consistent direction/magnitude of effect across both identically designed trials, together with the individually significant Study 047 result, supported regular approval

August 14, 2016"; "first edition of the SAP for Trial 048 was dated July 29, 2015 ... second edition ... October 3, 2016")

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Statistical Review section, p.95]*: "The primary efficacy endpoint was achievement of a stable platelet response by Week 24, defined as having a platelet count of at least 50,000/mcL on at least 4 of the last 6 scheduled visits between Weeks 14-24. ... The null hypothesis was to be tested using a 2-sided Fisher's Exact Test conducted with a significance level of 0.05."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Statistical Review section, p.96]*: "Missing data for the primary and secondary efficacy endpoints were to be imputed using the last observation carried forward (LOCF) method. ... No imputation was to be performed for missing data other than for the primary and secondary efficacy endpoints."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Statistical Review section, p.96 — reviewer's rejection of the sponsor's LOCF and confidence-interval methods]*: "The LOCF method is problematic as the last platelet count value may not always reflect the true platelet count for the missing data. In the March 26, 2014 advice letter, the FDA commented that the Agency did not agree with applying the LOCF method for missing data imputation for the primary efficacy endpoint analysis. This position is consistent with the missing data imputation method for the primary efficacy analysis for Nplate (romiplostim) which was approved in 2008. ... In this review, we present more conservative interval estimates for the difference in response rate; these are based on the Exact unconditional interval estimation method."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Statistical Review section, p.114, confidence-interval methods note]*: "In the SAP, the sponsor proposed using exact (Clopper-Pearson) confidence intervals for the response rate in each arm. The sponsor however presented interval estimates based on the Normal approximation. This approximation yields intervals with poor coverage if the response rate and/or the sample is small."

### 6. Avatrombopag (Doptelet) — NDA 210238

**Sponsor:** Dova Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NDA held through subsidiary AkaRx, Inc.)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of thrombocytopenia in adult patients with chronic liver disease who are scheduled to undergo a procedure

**Approval date:** May 21, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** Two identically designed Phase III trials, ADAPT-1 (Study E5501-G000-310, NCT01972529) and ADAPT-2 (Study E5501-G000-311, NCT01976104), both randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two identically designed, randomized (2:1 avatrombopag:placebo), double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group Phase III trials, each further divided into two dose/baseline-severity cohorts (Low Baseline Platelet Count Cohort, <40,000/mcL, treated with 60 mg once daily; High Baseline Platelet Count Cohort, 40,000-<50,000/mcL, treated with 40 mg once daily) with randomization stratified by hepatocellular carcinoma status (safety stratification only) and procedure-related bleeding risk (low/moderate/high, efficacy stratification); mid-trial sample-size reduction from a planned 300 to 200 patients per trial via protocol amendment

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint a binary responder definition — proportion of patients not requiring a platelet transfusion or any rescue procedure for bleeding from randomization through 7 days after the scheduled procedure; secondary endpoints proportion of patients achieving a platelet count ≥50,000/mcL on Procedure Day (prior to any transfusion/procedure) and change in platelet count from baseline to Procedure Day

- *Primary analysis:* generalized Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by procedure-related bleeding risk (low/moderate/high), 2-sided α=0.05, run separately within each baseline-platelet-count cohort (Low cohort: 60 mg vs. matching placebo; High cohort: 40 mg vs. matching placebo); trial declared positive only if both cohort-level comparisons reached statistical significance

- *Multiplicity:* sequential gatekeeping procedure — secondary endpoints tested only if the primary endpoint was statistically significant in both baseline-platelet-count cohorts, each subsequent endpoint tested within each cohort at α=0.05

- *Missing data/bias:* patients with missing primary-endpoint status due to early withdrawal or other reasons were conservatively counted as non-responders (i.e., as having received a transfusion); sensitivity analyses included a per-protocol analysis, an observed-case analysis excluding missing data, a Fisher's exact test on the full analysis set, and a "modified" primary-endpoint analysis restricted to platelet-transfusion avoidance alone (excluding other bleeding-rescue procedures)

- *Regulatory:* pre-specified two-cohort (dose-by-baseline-severity) responder design requiring statistical significance in both cohorts for a positive trial — a within-trial multiplicity structure distinct from a simple secondary-endpoint hierarchy (adapted from Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1's "Dose-arm pooling"/cohort-based design concepts, though this is a co-required dual-cohort win criterion — both of two dose/severity-defined cohorts must independently reach statistical significance for the trial to be declared positive — rather than pooling)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Both trials enrolled adults with chronic liver disease and thrombocytopenia (mean baseline platelet count <50,000/mcL, confirmed on two separate screening measurements) who were scheduled for an elective procedure with an assigned bleeding-risk level (low: paracentesis, thoracentesis, GI endoscopy, variceal banding, colonoscopy/polypectomy; moderate: liver biopsy, HCC ablation/chemoembolization, bronchoscopy with biopsy; high: vascular catheterization, TIPS, biliary interventions, renal biopsy, nephrostomy, radiofrequency ablation, laparoscopic/dental procedures); enrollment quotas required ≥10% high-risk and ≤60% low-risk procedures

- Randomization occurred via interactive voice/web response, 2:1 active:placebo within each baseline-platelet-count cohort; study drug (or placebo) was given once daily for 5 days (Days 1-5), with the procedure occurring 5-8 days after the last dose (Days 10-13); prohibited concomitant medications included other thrombopoietin-receptor agonists (eltrombopag, romiplostim), heparin, warfarin, NSAIDs, and several antiplatelet agents, reflecting a thrombosis-risk concern with this drug class; patients reaching a platelet count ≥200,000/mcL on procedure day underwent mandatory Doppler ultrasound screening for portal vein thrombosis

- Sample size was originally 300 patients per trial, reduced to 200 (100 per baseline cohort: ~67 avatrombopag/33 placebo) via Protocol Amendment 04 given lower-than-expected enrollment of the high-baseline-platelet-count cohort and observed effect sizes supporting adequate power at the smaller size

- Primary analysis population was the Full Analysis Set (all randomized patients, analyzed as randomized); a Per-Protocol Analysis Set (excluding patients with major eligibility violations, prohibited concomitant medications, non-compliance, or protocol deviations around transfusion/procedure timing) served as a supportive sensitivity population

- ADAPT-1 (Study 310), Low Baseline Platelet Count Cohort: responder rate 65.5% (59/90) avatrombopag 60 mg vs. 22.9% (11/48) placebo; High Baseline Platelet Count Cohort: 68.6% (48/70) vs. an unreported comparator rate, treatment difference 33.7% (95% CI 15.8-51.5%) (MDR pp.99-100). Both cohorts in both trials met the pre-specified CMH-test significance threshold, satisfying the dual-cohort co-requirement for a positive trial

- FDA Multi-Discipline Review package (includes Statistical Review, Reference ID 4264963) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/210238Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov records — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01972529 (ADAPT-1/Study 310), https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01976104 (ADAPT-2/Study 311)

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Statistical Review section, p.88]*: "The null hypothesis for the primary efficacy endpoint was that the proportion of patients not requiring a platelet transfusion or any rescue procedure for bleeding after randomization and up to 7 days following a scheduled procedure was the same between the avatrombopag and placebo treatment groups. ... The difference of proportion of patients not requiring a platelet transfusion or any rescue procedure for bleeding was tested at a two-side significance level of α=0.05, using the generalized Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test adjusting for the risk of bleeding associated with the scheduled procedure (low, moderate, or high)."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Statistical Review section, p.88]*: "This phase 3 study was to be considered positive if statistical significance was achieved for the primary efficacy endpoint for both baseline platelet count cohorts."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Statistical Review section, p.88, missing-data rule]*: "Patients with missing information about the primary efficacy outcome due to early withdrawal or other reasons were considered as having received a transfusion, i.e., a Non-Responder, for the primary analysis."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Statistical Review section, p.89, multiplicity]*: "The analysis of efficacy endpoints followed a sequential gatekeeping testing procedure ... with the multiplicity adjustment to control the Type I error rate at significance level α = 0.05. The secondary efficacy endpoints were only to be analyzed if the primary efficacy endpoint was statistically significant for both Baseline platelet count cohorts."

### 7. Lusutrombopag (Mulpleta) — NDA 210923

**Sponsor:** Shionogi Inc.

**Indication approved:** Thrombocytopenia in adult patients with chronic liver disease (CLD) who are scheduled to undergo a procedure

**Approval date:** July 31, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** L-PLUS 2 (Study 1423M0634, NCT02389621), a multinational phase 3 trial; supported by pivotal trial L-PLUS 1 (Study 1304M0631), a Japan-only phase 3 trial with no ClinicalTrials.gov registration identified

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; two near-identical phase 3 trials in the same drug-development program, one conducted only in Japan (L-PLUS 1) and one multinational (L-PLUS 2); randomization stratified by planned invasive-procedure type (liver ablation/coagulation vs. other) and baseline/screening platelet count threshold

- *Endpoints:* binary composite responder endpoint (L-PLUS 2 primary: no platelet transfusion prior to the invasive procedure and no rescue bleeding therapy through 7 days post-procedure; L-PLUS 1 primary: no platelet transfusion prior to the invasive procedure alone); secondary endpoints of platelet-count "responder" status (≥50,000/µL with a ≥20,000/µL increase from baseline), duration of platelet-count increase, and time course of platelet count

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by randomization factors, with Clopper-Pearson exact CIs for single-arm proportions and a Wald CI for the between-arm difference; FDA independently re-ran the primary analysis on the ITT population and added a Fisher's-exact-test sensitivity check

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (gatekeeping) hierarchical testing of L-PLUS 2 secondary endpoints, conducted only if the primary composite endpoint was statistically significant

- *Missing data/bias:* no imputation of missing platelet-count assessments ("actual observations" convention); patients who discontinued before the invasive procedure, or who never underwent it, were counted as automatic primary-endpoint failures

**Trial design & endpoints**

- L-PLUS 1 (Study 1304M0631, Japan-only): phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in Japanese patients with CLD-associated thrombocytopenia (platelet count ≤50,000/µL) scheduled for an invasive procedure; patients randomized 1:1 to lusutrombopag 3 mg once daily for up to 7 days or placebo; randomization stratified by planned invasive-procedure type and screening platelet count; sample size planned at 45/arm (90 total) for 90% power at a two-sided alpha of 0.05, assuming a 70% response rate on treatment vs. 20% on placebo

- L-PLUS 2 (Study 1423M0634, NCT02389621): phase 3, multinational, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in CLD patients undergoing elective invasive procedures; randomized 1:1 to lusutrombopag 3 mg once daily for up to 7 days or matched placebo; randomization stratified by planned invasive-procedure type (liver ablation/coagulation vs. other) and baseline platelet count (<35×10⁹/L or ≥35×10⁹/L); sample size planned at 200 total (100/arm) for 99% power to detect a 50-percentage-point difference at a two-sided alpha of 0.05; 215 patients enrolled

- Primary endpoint, L-PLUS 1: proportion of patients who required no platelet transfusion prior to the initial invasive procedure

- Primary endpoint, L-PLUS 2: proportion of patients who required no platelet transfusion prior to the primary invasive procedure and no rescue therapy for bleeding (platelet preparations, other blood preparations, or volume expanders), from randomization through 7 days after the primary invasive procedure; patients who discontinued before the procedure, or who did not undergo it, were counted as failures

- Secondary endpoints (both trials): proportion of patients requiring no platelet transfusion during the entire study; proportion of "responders" (platelet count ≥50,000/µL with an increase of ≥20,000/µL from baseline); duration of platelet-count increase (days maintained ≥50,000/µL and/or ≥70,000/µL); time course of platelet count at scheduled visits (Days 1, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 12, 14, 17, 21, 28, 35)

- Statistical methods: the proportion of patients meeting the primary endpoint was compared between arms using the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test adjusted for the stratification factors, with 95% CIs computed via the Clopper-Pearson method for each arm and the Wald method for the between-arm difference; the per-protocol set was used as a sensitivity population; L-PLUS 2 secondary endpoints were tested in a pre-specified fixed sequence (gatekeeping) only if the primary endpoint was statistically significant; duration endpoints were compared via the Wilcoxon rank-sum test and a stratified van Elteren test; all tests were two-sided at alpha 0.05 unless otherwise noted; missing data were not imputed

- Supportive publication (L-PLUS 1): Tateishi R, Seike M, Kudo M, et al. **SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 210923, p.79, "Statistical Analysis Plan" for L-PLUS 1]*: "As the efficacy primary endpoint, the proportion of patients who required no platelet transfusion prior to the primary invasive procedure were calculated by each treatment group, and its 95% confidence interval (CI) were calculated using the Clopper-Pearson method. The 3-mg and placebo groups were compared using the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test with the stratification factors (i.e., the classification of invasive procedure and the platelet count at screening) as adjustment factors. Through this, the relative risk in the 3-mg group as compared with the placebo group and its 95% CI were calculated. The same analyses were performed in the per protocol set (PPS) for the purpose of sensitivity analysis."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 210923, p.98-99, "Statistical Analysis Plan" for L-PLUS 2]*: "For the analysis of the primary endpoint, the number and proportion of patients who required no platelet transfusion prior to the primary invasive procedure and no rescue therapy for bleeding from randomization through 7 days after the primary elective procedure were calculated by treatment group. The proportion of patients who required no platelet transfusion in the S-888711 group were compared with that in the placebo group using the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test adjusted by stratification factors...A gatekeeping strategy was employed for sequentially testing the important secondary hypotheses. If the primary hypothesis was statistically significant, the secondary hypotheses were tested in sequence...Unless otherwise noted, all statistical tests were performed at a 0.05 (two-sided) significance level. Missing data were not imputed. All analyses were performed using actual observations."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 210923, p.91, "Efficacy Results – Primary Endpoint"]*: "The statistical reviewer did the analysis using ITT population...The statistical reviewer also included sensitivity analysis using Fisher's exact test. A minor numerical difference was seen between the sponsor's FAS and FDA's ITT analysis. All of the results showed that there are statistically significant differences between lusutrombopag and placebo arms." FDA's ITT re-analysis of L-PLUS 1 (Table 23) showed 77.6% (38/49) lusutrombopag vs. 12.5% (6/48) placebo, difference 65.6% (95% CI 50.7-80.5), relative risk 5.81 (95% CI 2.73-12.38), p<0.0001 by both CMH and Fisher's exact test. The L-PLUS 2 primary result (Table 32, FDA re-analysis of the sponsor's reported 64.8% [70/108] lusutrombopag vs. 29% [31/107] placebo) confirmed p<0.0001 by both the CMH test and Fisher's exact test.
