**Other resources**

- No Vivli/YODA Project/Project Data Sphere participation was identified for PharmaEssentia Corporation; not independently confirmed either way (PharmaEssentia is a considerably smaller sponsor than most others in this census and does not appear on either platform's public member listings).

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was convened for this application.

- This entry's central regulatory feature — the pivotal randomized trial (PROUD-PV) explicitly failing its primary endpoint, with approval instead resting on a much smaller single-arm dose-finding study (PEGINVERA) newly designated as the "adequate and well-controlled" trial — makes this one of the clearest documented examples in this census of FDA's "one AWC plus confirmatory evidence" pathway (FDAMA §115(a)) being used to approve a drug after its primary randomized comparative evidence failed, rather than in the more typical situation where a single-arm trial is the only trial ever attempted. Readers interested in the FDA's substantial-evidence flexibility framework should read the Summary Review's "Benefit-Risk Assessment" section in full alongside the Statistical Review's blunt "failed to demonstrate non-inferiority" conclusion.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, "Executive Summary," pp.6-8]* — "In PROUD-PV study, patients with PV were randomized 1:1 to either the study drug, AOP2014, or the control drug, Hydroxyurea (HU). The primary objective is to show that AOP2014 was non-inferior to HU, in the primary endpoint, disease response rate at month 12, with a proposed non-inferiority margin of 10.5%... There were several statistical issues with the design and analysis of PROUD-PV. PROUD-PV was originally designed to demonstrate a superiority of AOP2014 compared to HU. In the amended clinical study protocol version 4.0, dated June 15, 2016, sponsor changed the superiority comparison to a non-inferiority comparison. This change was made 2 months after the completion of PROUD-PV (08 April 2016). Given that the study was open-label and the sponsor had access to the unblinded data during the study, it was possible for the sponsor to make changes based on the failed results observed from the superiority comparison, which could violate the integrity of the study."

*[verbatim, same review, p.6, primary result]* — "The difference in response rate was -6.3% (95% CI: -16.7, 4.1). Since the lower bound of the 95% CI was -16.7% and is less than the NI margin of -10.5%, the non-inferiority of AOP2014 to HU at month 12 was not demonstrated."

*[verbatim, same review, "Statistical Analysis of Primary Efficacy Endpoint," pp.17-18, on the retrospective power]* — "Later, the sponsor proposed a change of the study primary objective from a superiority comparison to a non-inferiority comparison of AOP2014 to HU with a NI margin of 10.5%... the statistical power for non-inferiority hypothesis was retrospectively calculated... Given a NI margin of -10%, the statistical power to conclude non-inferiority is roughly 4%... A study with a statistical power of 4% is not considered a well-designed study."

*[verbatim, same review, p.17, primary analysis method]* — "The primary analysis was conducted using a weighted Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test (using SAS® terminology)... The stratification factors were those used in the randomization scheme, namely: age groups (≤60 years vs. >60 years), previous thrombotic event (presence vs absence), and previous HU exposure (yes vs. no)."

*[verbatim, same review, p.7-8, on CONTINUATION-PV and the pooled post-hoc analysis]* — "CONTINUATION-PV also had several statistical issues. The patient population was consisted of a subgroup of patients who completed the PROUD-PV study and met certain outcome dependent eligibility criteria. This was not a randomized study. Without proper randomization, selection bias may exist and confounders... could undermine the study results... Supportive data from the single-arm experience from the PROUD-PV/CONTINUATION study demonstrated a CHR of 52.8% at month 24 and 36 (95% CI of 44.1, 61.4) with median duration of response beyond 48 months."

*[verbatim, same review, p.8, reviewer's overall conclusion]* — "Based on the data submitted, this reviewer concludes that the pivotal study, PROUD-PV, failed to demonstrate non-inferiority of study drug, AOP2014, to the active control, HU, in the primary endpoint, disease response rate... However, there may exist some limitations to the statistical interpretability of the efficacy findings in PEGINVERA due to its single arm design, and the post-hoc analysis nature of the single arm of combined PROUD-PV/CONTINUATION study. Whether a substantial evidence of effectiveness of AOP2014 has been demonstrated in this application need clinical judgment and should be considering unmet medical need."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, "Benefit-Risk Assessment," on the final regulatory framework]* — "The applicant submitted three studies as part of this application: PROUD-PV, CONTINUATION-PV, PEGINVERA. The PROUD-PV study was intended to be an adequate and well-controlled (AWC) study to provide substantial evidence of effectiveness... Despite these critical concerns, the study failed on its primary endpoint... The review team evaluated the effectiveness of ropeginterferon alfa-2b from a single adequate and well-controlled study, the PEGINVERA study... The confirmatory evidence is based on pharmacodynamic biomarkers and natural history of the disease (historical control group)... Therefore, given the natural history of PV, the unmet medical need and rarity of the disease, flexibility is warranted for the amount and type of evidence needed to meet the substantial evidence standard. Approval based on a single AWC plus confirmatory evidence is appropriate for this proposed indication."

*[verbatim, same Summary Review, on PEGINVERA's designation as AWC]* — "In summary, PEGINVERA was a well-planned, executed and conducted study demonstrating clinically meaningful decreases in PLTS and WBC as demonstrated by the CHR rate... The comparison of these changes to a valid external control group is acceptable and PEGINVERA can be considered an adequate and well controlled study when its treatment group is compared to a historical control."

*[verbatim, same Summary Review, Advisory Committee]* — "Neither an Advisory Committee Meeting nor an external consultation was deemed necessary."

*[verbatim, FDA Approval Letter, opening paragraph]* — "We acknowledge receipt of your resubmission dated May 13, 2021, which constituted a complete response to our March 12, 2021, action letter."

**Reverse-engineered SAP** (the passages above are drawn from FDA's Statistical Review and Summary Review, both of which document extensive sponsor SAP/protocol content and FDA's own reasoning verbatim; the following extend beyond what was directly reproduced and are traced to specific reported results)

- *[inferred]* PEGINVERA's original protocol was almost certainly never designed with the intention of one day serving as the pivotal AWC trial for a BLA — its Stage 1/Stage 2 structure (MTD-finding, then a descriptive efficacy assessment) is characteristic of an early Phase I/II dose-finding study, not a registration trial; its elevation to AWC status appears to have been a consequence of PROUD-PV's post-hoc failure rather than a plan set at PEGINVERA's outset, though the Summary Review frames this as a considered application of FDAMA §115(a) flexibility rather than an ad hoc rescue of a failed development program.

- *[inferred]* The sponsor's retrospective, ~4%-power non-inferiority framing for PROUD-PV was very likely a last-resort attempt to salvage some claim of comparability to hydroxyurea after the originally-planned superiority comparison failed, given the FDA reviewer's explicit timeline showing the protocol amendment came only ~2 months after study completion and used only blinded/pooled DMC data — meaning the sponsor could reasonably have inferred the superiority comparison had failed (since a 4%-power non-inferiority reframing would not otherwise have been an obviously appealing choice) without technically having seen the unblinded arm-level result at the time of the amendment.

- *[inferred]* FDA's willingness to accept PEGINVERA as a valid AWC trial "compared to a historical control" despite the general rarity of single-arm/historical-control approvals for a chronic, slowly-progressive disease like PV (as opposed to, e.g., a rapidly fatal cancer) likely reflects the specific combination of (a) PV's genuine lack of any FDA-approved first-line cytoreductive therapy at the time, (b) the mechanistic directness of the laboratory-parameter endpoints (which are difficult to attribute to placebo/regression-to-mean given PV's well-documented natural history of progressive count elevation), and (c) the existence of the independent CYTO-PV trial providing a causal bridge from those laboratory parameters to clinical (thrombotic) outcomes — a combination of factors the Summary Review discusses but does not weight explicitly against each other.

### 20. Sutimlimab-jome (Enjaymo) — BLA 761164

**Sponsor:** Sanofi (via Bioverativ Therapeutics Inc., a Sanofi subsidiary since 2018); post-approval commercial rights for the CAD indication were later transferred to Recordati Rare Diseases

**Indication approved:** Treatment to decrease the need for red blood cell (RBC) transfusion due to hemolysis in adults with cold agglutinin disease (CAD)

**Approval date:** February 4, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** CARDINAL (Study BIVV009-03, Part A), NCT03347396 — single-arm, open-label trial

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label trial (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1; 24 adult CAD patients with a recent transfusion history, no concurrent control arm); FDA-justified no-control design for an ultra-rare disease with no approved therapy (adapted from Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1's small-single-arm-trial entries) — FDA's review states a control group was "acceptable prior to the BLA submission given the stringent composite efficacy endpoints and lack of available effective therapies"; regular approval on one adequate/well-controlled (here, baseline-controlled) single-arm trial plus mechanistic confirmatory evidence from an earlier Phase 1 cohort (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §7, closely related to the "Regular approval grounded in durable-ORR-as-direct-clinical-benefit" and "single adequate trial plus confirmatory evidence" patterns seen elsewhere in this batch, e.g., ropeginterferon)

- *Endpoints:* composite responder endpoint requiring (a) no blood transfusion from Week 5 through Week 26 (the treatment assessment endpoint) and no CAD treatment beyond protocol-permitted therapy, AND (b) either Hgb ≥12 g/dL at the treatment assessment endpoint (mean of Weeks 23, 25, 26) or a ≥2 g/dL increase from baseline (a composite transfusion-avoidance-plus-hemoglobin-threshold-or-increase responder definition distinct from the census's other transfusion-independence endpoints, which typically use only a duration-based transfusion-free criterion without an additional Hgb-level branch); secondary endpoints (bilirubin normalization, FACIT-Fatigue score, LDH, Hgb change from baseline)

- *Primary analysis:* single-proportion analysis with an exact (Clopper-Pearson) confidence interval against a pre-specified 30% performance-goal threshold (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §3, "Exact binomial test against a pre-specified performance goal"); Composite Estimand treating any missing response component as non-response, with Completer and Per-Protocol Estimands as sensitivity analyses; Mixed Model for Repeated Measures (MMRM) under Hypothetical and De-facto Estimands for continuous secondary endpoints, with multiple-imputation sensitivity analyses

- *Missing data/bias:* Composite Estimand's built-in non-responder default for any missing primary-endpoint component (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §6, adapted from "Non-responder imputation for missing binary/diary efficacy data"); ICH E9(R1)-style multiple named estimands (Composite, Completer, Per-Protocol, Hypothetical, De-facto) applied to a single small (N=24) single-arm trial (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §4's ICH E9(R1) estimand-framework entry, extended here to a baseline-controlled single-arm context rather than the randomized-trial intercurrent-event settings the taxonomy entry was written from); reviewer-flagged, unresolved gender-subgroup asymmetry (73.3% female responders vs. 22.2% male) explicitly described as "difficult to interpret given the small sample size" rather than resolved by any subgroup-specific sensitivity analysis

- *Regulatory:* Orphan Drug designation (July 27, 2016) and Breakthrough Therapy designation (May 17, 2017), the latter granted after an end-of-Phase-1/breakthrough-therapy meeting that reached agreement on population, endpoints, and study duration for CARDINAL; Priority Review (granted at filing); Complete Response Letter issued November 13, 2020 for facility/data-integrity deficiencies at a third-party drug-substance manufacturing site (CMC/OPQ, not an efficacy finding) — Type A meeting held April 6, 2020 specifically to discuss this integrity investigation; resubmission August 5, 2021 resolved the OPQ deficiencies and updated safety data, leading to approval; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting

**Trial design & endpoints**

- CARDINAL (BIVV009-03, Part A) was an open-label, single-arm, international trial (Australia, Germany, France, Italy, Japan, Norway, UK, US) enrolling 24 adult patients with CAD who had at least 1 blood transfusion in the prior 6 months, Hgb <10 g/dL, and clinical symptoms. FDA's review justifies the absence of a control arm as "acceptable prior to the BLA submission given the stringent composite efficacy endpoints and lack of available effective therapies" for CAD. Sample size was planned at approximately 20 patients (24 enrolled): assuming a true responder rate of 66% against a minimum acceptable rate of 30%, 20 patients gave 90% probability that the lower bound of the 95% CI would exceed 30%.

- The primary endpoint was a composite: a patient was a responder if they (a) received no blood transfusion from Week 5 through Week 26 and received no CAD treatment beyond what the protocol permitted, and (b) either had Hgb ≥12 g/dL at the treatment assessment endpoint (the mean of Weeks 23, 25, and 26) or had a Hgb increase of ≥2 g/dL from baseline. The primary analysis used the exact Clopper-Pearson method for the responder-rate CI under a "Composite Estimand" (any missing component classified as non-response), with Completer and Per-Protocol Estimands as sensitivity analyses. Secondary endpoints (bilirubin, FACIT-Fatigue, LDH, and Hgb change from baseline) were analyzed via MMRM under Hypothetical and De-facto Estimands, with multiple-imputation sensitivity analyses; no formal multiplicity adjustment across secondaries was described, consistent with there being a single pivotal trial and no formally alpha-controlled secondary hierarchy.

- Results: 13 of 24 patients (54.2%, 95% CI 32.8%-74.4%) met the composite primary endpoint, with the lower CI bound exceeding the pre-specified 30% success threshold. Individual components: 15 patients (62.5%) met the Hgb criterion; 17 (70.8%) were transfusion-free from Week 5 through Week 26; 22 (91.7%) received no prohibited CAD medications. A subgroup analysis showed a marked gender asymmetry — 11 of 15 female patients (73.3%) were responders versus 2 of 9 male patients (22.2%) — which FDA's reviewer flagged as "difficult to interpret given the small sample size" rather than resolved by any additional analysis.

- FDA's benefit-risk rationale explicitly frames this as a single-trial-plus-mechanistic-confirmatory-evidence approval: "A single, baseline-controlled trial provides substantial evidence of effectiveness for this application, given the robust improvement in objective laboratory parameters that would be extremely unlikely to occur spontaneously in an untreated population with this disease. Thus, substantial evidence of effectiveness was established via one adequate and well controlled trial plus confirmatory evidence (mechanistic evidence of increase in hgb and decreases in LDH and bilirubin levels... from study BIVV009-01 Part C)." That confirmatory mechanistic evidence came from a small (N=6) Phase 1 cohort in which median Hgb rose from 7.7 to 10.7 g/dL after the last dose (reverting after washout) and bilirubin normalized in all 5 evaluable patients by Day 14 (also reverting after washout) — a pharmacodynamic reversibility pattern used to corroborate causality rather than as an independent efficacy trial.

- Regulatory history: sutimlimab's original BLA cycle was not approved on its first review — FDA's inspection of a drug-substance manufacturing facility found "lack of quality oversight, significant data integrity concerns, and failure to conduct a comprehensive assessment to ensure [accurate] and reliable results submitted to the BLA," leading to a Complete Response Letter on November 13, 2020 that was explicitly a CMC/facility action, with all clinical/statistical review disciplines having recommended approval on the merits of CARDINAL's efficacy data in that first cycle. The August 5, 2021 resubmission addressed the manufacturing deficiencies and included an updated safety database (76 total CAD patients across studies, with 5 developing treatment-emergent anti-drug antibodies and no associated hypersensitivity reactions), leading to approval on February 4, 2022.

- Package Insert / Label (original, February 2022) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2022/761164s000lbl.pdf

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2027760), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33826820/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Sutimlimab%20in%20Cold%20Agglutinin%20Disease)

**Other resources**

- Vivli: Sanofi is a confirmed named Vivli member, and CARDINAL's own ClinicalTrials.gov record explicitly names Vivli as the data-access route ("Further details on Sanofi's data sharing criteria... can be found at: https://vivli.org"). Bioverativ and Recordati Rare Diseases were not found as separately named Vivli members (plausibly covered under Sanofi's umbrella post-acquisition, but not individually confirmed). YODA Project's current data-partner list does not include Sanofi, Bioverativ, or Recordati. Project Data Sphere participation could not be confirmed either way.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held for this BLA.

- Post-marketing requirements include a 5-year registry study characterizing long-term CAD safety, completion of CARDINAL Part B (long-term extension) and BIVV009-01 Part E, and completion of Part B of BIVV009-04 (CADENZA) — a separate, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial in CAD patients without a recent transfusion history, providing a second, controlled trial in the broader post-marketing development program even though CARDINAL alone supported the original approval.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, ClinicalTrials.gov-posted Statistical Analysis Plan / FDA Medical Review, primary endpoint definition]* — "A patient was considered a responder if he or she did not receive a blood transfusion from Week 5 through Week 26 (end of treatment) and did not receive treatment for CAD beyond what was permitted per protocol. Additionally, the patient's Hgb level must have met either of the following criteria: Hgb level ≥12 g/dL at the treatment assessment endpoint (mean of Weeks 23, 25, 26) OR Hgb level increased by ≥2 g/dL from baseline."

*[verbatim, same review, on trial design]* — "A control group was not included in the study. This was determined to be acceptable prior to the BLA submission given the stringent composite efficacy endpoints and lack of available effective therapies."

*[verbatim, same review, primary result]* — "13/24 (54.2%, 95% CI: 32.8%–74.4%) met the composite responder definition; lower bound of 95% CI exceeded the pre-specified 30% success threshold... 15 (62.5%) met the Hgb criterion; 17 (70.8%) transfusion-free Weeks 5–26; 22 (91.7%) received no prohibited CAD medications."

*[verbatim, same review, subgroup finding]* — Females 11/15 (73.3%) responders vs. males 2/9 (22.2%) — described by the reviewer as "difficult to interpret given the small sample size."

*[verbatim, FDA Medical Review, Benefit-Risk section]* — "A single, baseline-controlled trial provides substantial evidence of effectiveness for this application, given the robust improvement in objective laboratory parameters that would be extremely unlikely to occur spontaneously in an untreated population with this disease. Thus, substantial evidence of effectiveness was established via one adequate and well controlled trial plus confirmatory evidence (mechanistic evidence of increase in hgb and decreases in LDH and bilirubin levels... from study BIVV009-01 Part C)."

*[verbatim, same review, on the manufacturing-related Complete Response Letter]* — the November 2020 action followed findings of "lack of quality oversight, significant data integrity concerns, and failure to conduct a comprehensive assessment to ensure [accurate] and reliable results submitted to the BLA" at a drug-substance manufacturing facility — a CMC/facility deficiency, with clinical and statistical disciplines having recommended approval on the efficacy/safety data in that review cycle.

*[verbatim, same review, "Advisory Committee"]* — "The application for sutimlimab was not referred to an FDA advisory committee."

**Reverse-engineered SAP** (genuine SAP text is posted on ClinicalTrials.gov and substantially reproduced within FDA's Medical Review as quoted above; the following extend beyond what was directly reproduced, traced to specific reported results)

- *[inferred]* The pre-specified 30% performance-goal threshold (versus an assumed true response rate of 66%) was very likely calibrated against expectations of spontaneous/placebo-like transfusion avoidance in untreated CAD patients with recent transfusion histories — a population selected specifically for high baseline transfusion dependence — making a 30% "spontaneous" composite-responder rate a conservative benchmark that a working complement inhibitor would be expected to clear substantially, consistent with the trial's ultimately observed 54.2% rate comfortably exceeding it.

- *[inferred]* The unresolved gender-subgroup asymmetry (73.3% vs. 22.2% response) was most plausibly left uninvestigated in the primary review because of the small subgroup sizes (15 and 9 patients) rather than a documented mechanistic hypothesis; because CAD itself has a well-documented female-predominant epidemiology and the trial was not stratified by sex at randomization (there being no randomization at all), this asymmetry cannot be distinguished from a chance finding in a 24-patient trial without a dedicated post-marketing analysis, which the review does not appear to have required as a specific PMR.

### 21. Mitapivat (Pyrukynd) — NDA 216196

**Sponsor:** Agios Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Hemolytic anemia due to pyruvate kinase (PK) deficiency in adults

**Approval date:** February 17, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** ACTIVATE (Study AG-348-C-006, NCT03548220) and ACTIVATE-T (Study AG-348-C-007, NCT03559699)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (ACTIVATE; Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1) paired with a single-arm, open-label trial (ACTIVATE-T; §1) as a two-trial pivotal program split by transfusion status; small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (§1; PK deficiency prevalence ~3.2-8.5 per million; ACTIVATE N=80, ACTIVATE-T N=27)

- *Endpoints:* Hemoglobin response as a sustained-increase responder endpoint (ACTIVATE primary); a transfusion-burden-reduction responder endpoint benchmarked against a within-patient standardized historical control period (ACTIVATE-T primary) — (Transfusion-burden-reduction responder endpoint benchmarked to a within-patient standardized historical-control period")

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test (§3, ACTIVATE — used as the SAP's pre-specified fallback after the planned logistic regression failed to converge due to quasi-complete separation, since zero placebo patients responded); Exact/Clopper-Pearson-type binomial confidence interval (§3, ACTIVATE-T); Non-inferiority analysis against a fixed historical-control threshold (no concurrent comparator arm) (§1, ACTIVATE-T, closely analogous)

- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing combined with Hochberg step-up procedure within tiers (§4, ACTIVATE: primary → key secondary [Hb change] → Hochberg step-up across four remaining tied endpoints); ACTIVATE-T had no formal multiplicity control across its descriptive secondary endpoints

- *Missing data/bias:* Non-responder imputation for missing binary/diary efficacy data (§6, exact match — both trials counted missing Hb assessments, or receipt of less than the minimum treatment duration, as non-response)

- *Regulatory:* No FDA Advisory Committee meeting held; Orphan Drug, Fast Track, and Priority Review designations; FDA reviewer disputed the clinical meaningfulness of two patient-reported-outcome secondary endpoints despite their statistical significance, consulting the Division of Clinical Outcome Assessment ("FDA reviewer disputes clinical-meaningfulness of a sponsor PRO secondary endpoint despite statistical significance"); FDA required additional sponsor justification for an expert-opinion-derived (rather than literature-derived) responder-rate performance-goal threshold in ACTIVATE-T ("FDA-negotiated performance-goal threshold justified by expert opinion rather than external literature")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ACTIVATE (Study AG-348-C-006, NCT03548220): Phase 3, randomized 1:1, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial in adults ≥18 years with PK deficiency (≥2 variant PKLR alleles, at least one missense) who were not regularly transfused (≤4 transfusion episodes in the prior 12 months, none in the prior 3 months) and had baseline hemoglobin ≤10.0 g/dL; excluded R479H/R479H homozygotes, nonmissense/nonmissense genotype, and splenectomy within the prior 12 months. Randomization was stratified by average screening hemoglobin (<8.5 vs. ≥8.5 g/dL) and PKLR variant category (missense/missense vs. missense/nonmissense). The design comprised a 12-week Dose Optimization Period (Part 1) followed by a 12-week Fixed-Dose Period (Part 2, through Week 24), with an independent Data Monitoring Committee reviewing safety; 80 patients were randomized (40 mitapivat/40 placebo).

- ACTIVATE-T (Study AG-348-C-007, NCT03559699): Phase 3, single-arm, open-label trial using the same genotype/exclusion criteria as ACTIVATE but enrolling regularly transfused patients (≥6 transfusion episodes in the prior 52 weeks, excluding >18 transfusions/52 weeks), who were also required to receive folic acid supplementation (≥0.8 mg/day) for at least 21 days before dosing. 27 patients were enrolled and treated over a 42-week duration including a 3-week dose taper.

- Primary endpoint (ACTIVATE): hemoglobin response, defined as a ≥1.5 g/dL increase in Hb concentration from baseline sustained at two or more scheduled assessments at Weeks 16, 20, and 24; patients with fewer than two Hb assessments during the Fixed-Dose Period were counted as non-responders regardless of any observed increase.

- Primary endpoint (ACTIVATE-T): proportion of patients achieving a ≥33% reduction in RBC units transfused during the 24-week Fixed-Dose Period relative to a "Standardized Control Period" — each patient's own historical transfusion burden mathematically standardized to a 24-week equivalent; patients completing fewer than 12 weeks of treatment were counted as non-responders regardless of transfused-unit reduction. The pre-specified efficacy criterion required the lower bound of the two-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson exact confidence interval for the responder rate to exceed 10% (H0: true rate ≤10% vs. H1: rate >10%).

- Key secondary endpoints (ACTIVATE, tested via a fixed-sequence hierarchy: primary → key secondary [Hb change] → Hochberg step-up across the remaining four): average hemoglobin change from baseline over Weeks 16/20/24 analyzed by a mixed model for repeated measures; the PK Diary Total Symptom Score and PK Diary Item domain scores (PKDD/PKDIA, sponsor-developed patient-reported-outcome instruments); and change from baseline in LDH and haptoglobin.

- Sample-size/threshold rationale: ACTIVATE's design was informed by Phase 2 dose-finding data. For ACTIVATE-T, FDA required the Applicant to justify both the 33-percentage-point clinical-benefit threshold and the 10% statistical decision threshold at the design stage; the Applicant's rationale rested on expert opinion and approximate iron-burden arithmetic (~200 mg iron per unit transfused) rather than external published literature, which FDA's review team accepted as adequate — noting the observed result "was considerably exceeded" relative to that threshold.

- Results: in ACTIVATE, 16/40 (40.0%) mitapivat-treated patients achieved hemoglobin response vs. 0/40 (0%) on placebo, with an exact CMH two-sided p<0.0001 and a Mantel-Haenszel stratum-weighted adjusted difference of 39.3% (95% CI 24.1-54.6); the mixed-model average-Hb-change key secondary showed an LS-mean difference of 1.8 g/dL (95% CI 1.2-2.4, p<0.0001); all six endpoints in the testing hierarchy reached statistical significance, though FDA's review team specifically flagged concerns about the clinical relevance of the two PRO endpoints despite their significance. In ACTIVATE-T, 10/27 (37.0%) patients met the transfusion-reduction responder criterion (95% CI 19.4-57.6), with the lower bound clearing the pre-specified 10% threshold; notably, one patient with a 100% reduction in transfused units was nonetheless classified as a non-responder solely because they received fewer than 12 weeks of treatment, illustrating the protocol-defined non-responder rule overriding an otherwise favorable raw result.

**Other resources**

- No Agios/Vivli/YODA Project/Project Data Sphere participation specific to these trials was identified; not independently confirmed either way.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was convened for this NDA (FDA Integrated Review, §11: "The application did not raise safety or effectiveness issues requiring external expert advice. Therefore, an Advisory Committee meeting was not held.").

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §11, p.111]* — "The application did not raise safety or effectiveness issues requiring external expert advice. Therefore, an Advisory Committee meeting was not held."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, ACTIVATE-T efficacy-threshold discussion, p.48-49]* — "however this threshold was considerably exceeded" (referring to the pre-specified 10% lower-CI-bound decision threshold against the observed 19.4% lower bound).

**Reverse-engineered SAP** (genuine sponsor SAP/protocol text is not public for either trial; the following extend beyond the verbatim excerpts above and are traced to specific reported results in the FDA Integrated Review)

- *[inferred]* ACTIVATE's primary analysis almost certainly specified logistic regression (adjusted for the two randomization stratification factors) as the first-choice model, with exact CMH as a named fallback, because the observed result — zero responders in the 40-patient placebo arm — produces quasi-complete separation that would prevent a logistic model from converging; the reported use of an "exact" CMH p-value together with a Mantel-Haenszel stratum-weighted difference (rather than a model-based odds ratio) is consistent with a fallback having been triggered rather than the primary model succeeding.

- *[inferred]* The Hochberg step-up ordering across ACTIVATE's four non-key-secondary endpoints (PKDD, PKDIA, LDH, haptoglobin) was most likely pre-specified as a tied family (rather than individually sequenced) given that FDA's review discusses all four as a single step following the Hb-change key secondary, and that FDA's stated concern was about the PRO pair's clinical interpretability as a category, not about their position within the family.

- *[inferred]* ACTIVATE-T's "Standardized Control Period" formula most likely pro-rated each patient's pre-study transfusion history over a fixed lookback window to a 24-week equivalent (rather than using a raw historical count), since the trial's inclusion criterion itself was defined in 52-week transfusion-frequency terms while the responder analysis compared against a 24-week on-treatment period — a scaling step is necessary to make the two periods comparable, though the exact lookback window and pro-ration arithmetic are not reproduced in available sources.

### 22. Daprodustat (Jesduvroq) — NDA 216951

**Sponsor:** GlaxoSmithKline

**Indication approved:** Anemia due to chronic kidney disease (CKD) in adults who have been receiving dialysis for at least four months

**Approval date:** February 1, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** ASCEND-D (Study 200807, NCT02879305), with supportive programs ASCEND-ND (Study 200808, NCT02876835, non-dialysis — did not support approval), ASCEND-NHQ (Study 205270), and ASCEND-ID (Study 201410, NCT03029208)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, open-label (sponsor-blinded), active-controlled (epoetin alfa for hemodialysis, darbepoetin alfa for peritoneal dialysis), event-driven, parallel-group trial (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1, §4); co-primary endpoints (§1) combining an efficacy non-inferiority margin (mean Hb change) and a safety non-inferiority margin (MACE hazard ratio) within a single trial pair — no existing taxonomy entry captures a design where the *second* co-primary is itself a safety-only non-inferiority margin rather than an efficacy or symptom endpoint ("Co-primary non-inferiority margins on both an efficacy biomarker and a safety composite (dual risk-margin design)")

- *Endpoints:* MACE composite (§2, all-cause mortality + nonfatal MI + nonfatal stroke) as a co-primary safety non-inferiority endpoint; mean hemoglobin change from baseline over Weeks 28-52 as the co-primary efficacy non-inferiority endpoint; principal secondary endpoints (HHF, CV death, MACE2, all-cause mortality) gated behind both co-primaries ruling out their respective margins

- *Primary analysis:* Cox proportional-hazards model (§3, MACE, stratified by study/region/dialysis type); ANCOVA (§3, Hb change, adjusted for baseline Hb, dialysis type/current ESA use, region)

- *Multiplicity:* Bonferroni-Holm sequentially rejective procedure (§4) for the principal secondary endpoints, gated behind both co-primary margins being met

- *Missing data/bias:* Tipping-point analysis (multiple imputation) (§6) — Jackson et al. (2014) method, 200 imputed datasets combined via Rubin's rules, applied separately to ASCEND-D and ASCEND-ND's MACE non-inferiority conclusions with markedly different robustness (ASCEND-D tipped only under extreme asymmetric hazard-multiplier assumptions; ASCEND-ND tipped under comparatively modest ones)

- *Regulatory:* FDA Advisory Committee meeting held (§7; Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee, October 26, 2022); divergent regulatory outcome across the drug's two co-developed populations, with dialysis approved and non-dialysis not, driven by differential cardiovascular-safety subgroup findings across an otherwise identically designed trial pair — no existing taxonomy term captures this split-indication-by-safety-subgroup pattern ("Divergent regulatory outcome across pre-specified sub-populations of the same pivotal-trial pair based on differential CV-safety subgroup findings")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ASCEND-D (Study 200807, NCT02879305): Phase 3, randomized 1:1, open-label (with the sponsor blinded to treatment assignment), active-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter, event-driven trial in dialysis-dependent CKD patients switched from a prior ESA to daprodustat or continued recombinant erythropoietin (epoetin alfa for hemodialysis, darbepoetin alfa for peritoneal dialysis); randomized stratified by region and dialysis type. N=2,964 (1,487 daprodustat/1,477 ESA), 431 centers across 35 countries, mean follow-up 2.48 years.

- ASCEND-ND (Study 200808, NCT02876835): identical design against darbepoetin alfa in non-dialysis-dependent CKD; N=3,872 (1,937/1,935), 506 centers across 39 countries, mean follow-up 1.86 years — this trial's results did not support a non-dialysis indication (see Results, below).

- Supportive trials: ASCEND-NHQ (Study 205270, placebo-controlled, double-blind, non-dialysis, N=614, efficacy-only) and ASCEND-ID (Study 201410, NCT03029208, incident dialysis, active-controlled, N=312).

- Co-primary endpoints (both ASCEND-D and ASCEND-ND): (1) mean hemoglobin change from baseline over the Week 28-52 evaluation period, non-inferiority margin −0.75 g/dL on the lower CI bound, analyzed by ANCOVA (treatment, baseline Hb, dialysis type/current-ESA-use, region); (2) time to first adjudicated MACE (all-cause mortality, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke), non-inferiority margin of 1.25 on the MACE hazard ratio's upper CI bound, analyzed by a Cox proportional-hazards model (treatment, region, dialysis type for ASCEND-D or current-ESA-use for ASCEND-ND). The MACE margin was revised across Type C meetings between 2015 and 2016 (1.25→1.2→back to 1.25), and the target MACE event count was revised to 664 events via a 2020 protocol amendment that also accelerated timelines given the COVID-19 pandemic.

- Principal secondary endpoints, tested via Bonferroni-Holm sequentially rejective procedure only if both co-primary margins were met: MACE2 (MACE plus HF hospitalization plus thromboembolic events), CV-cause-specific MACE, all-cause mortality, and CV death.

- Results (ASCEND-D): MACE HR 0.93 (95% CI 0.81-1.07), ruling out the 1.25 margin (non-inferiority demonstrated); none of the principal secondary superiority tests reached significance; hospitalization for heart failure HR 1.10 (95% CI 0.84-1.45), a signal later attributed largely to patients with a pre-existing heart-failure history.

- Results (ASCEND-ND): on-study MACE HR 1.03 (95% CI 0.89-1.19), nominally ruling out the margin, but an on-treatment (rather than on-study/ITT-style) analysis gave HR 1.40 (95% CI 1.17-1.68); every individually adjudicated cardiovascular component analyzed (CV-cause-restricted MACE, CV mortality, stroke, HF hospitalization) produced HRs ranging from 1.06 to 1.49, uniformly disfavoring daprodustat — this consistent directional pattern across secondary CV analyses, not the primary on-study MACE result alone, drove FDA's non-approval for the non-dialysis population. Additional non-dialysis-specific safety signals included serious acute kidney injury (relative risk 1.47, 95% CI 1.07-2.00) and a higher rate of gastric/esophageal erosions than in the dialysis population.

- Sensitivity analysis: a tipping-point multiple-imputation analysis (Jackson et al. 2014 method, 200 imputations, Rubin's rules) showed ASCEND-D's non-inferiority conclusion tipped only under extreme, asymmetric hazard-multiplier assumptions (4.5x/0.4x), while ASCEND-ND's tipped under far more modest assumptions (1.7x) — reinforcing FDA's framing of the non-dialysis MACE result as comparatively fragile.

FDA's dialysis-only approval was explicitly stated as consistent with this recommendation.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

Genuine sponsor SAP/protocol text is not publicly posted for either trial; the FDA Integrated Review reproduces the study design, endpoint definitions, and analysis methods described above at length, but the specific passages available were paraphrased rather than directly quoted during sourcing, so no verbatim excerpts are presented here to avoid misattributing paraphrase as quotation.

**Reverse-engineered SAP** (traced to the specific reported results and design elements above)

- *[inferred]* The co-primary structure's ordering — with the Hb-change margin and the MACE margin treated as independently must-both-be-met endpoints rather than a hierarchy — is inferred from the fact that FDA's review discusses non-inferiority conclusions for each endpoint separately (neither is described as gated behind the other), and that the Bonferroni-Holm-tested principal secondaries are explicitly gated behind *both* co-primaries.

- *[inferred]* The MACE non-inferiority margin's revision history (1.25→1.2→1.25) and the 2020 event-count amendment to 664 are most plausibly documented in Special Protocol Assessment correspondence and protocol amendment records referenced but not reproduced verbatim in the Integrated Review; the amendment's stated COVID-19 rationale is consistent with the global timing of the change.

- *[inferred]* The stark divergence between ASCEND-ND's on-study (HR 1.03) and on-treatment (HR 1.40) MACE analyses implies the SAP pre-specified both an intention-to-treat-style "on-study" analysis (following patients regardless of treatment discontinuation) and a supportive "on-treatment" (as-treated, censored-at-discontinuation) analysis as a formal sensitivity analysis — a design choice inferable from the magnitude of the discrepancy and FDA's evident reliance on the on-treatment analysis as more informative of the drug's true cardiovascular effect.

### 23. Motixafortide (Aphexda) — NDA 217159

**Sponsor:** BioLineRx, Ltd. (US commercialization now under Ayrmid Pharma)

**Indication approved:** In combination with granulocyte-colony stimulating factor (G-CSF), to mobilize hematopoietic stem cells to the peripheral blood for collection and subsequent autologous transplantation in patients with multiple myeloma

**Approval date:** September 8, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** GENESIS (Study BL-8040.SCM.301, NCT03246529)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1) trial with an open-label, DMC-monitored dose-confirmation lead-in (Part 1, single-arm) preceding a separately randomized Part 2 — no existing taxonomy term captures a single-arm dose-confirmation stage that gates entry into, rather than internally adapting within, a subsequent randomized trial part ("Open-label dose-confirmation lead-in followed by a separately randomized, placebo-controlled trial part"); triple-masked (participant/care provider/investigator), permuted-block randomization stratified by remission status and baseline platelet count

- *Endpoints:* Hematopoietic stem-cell mobilization responder endpoint — proportion of subjects collecting ≥6×10⁶ CD34+ cells/kg within ≤2 apheresis sessions after a single dose — with no existing taxonomy match ("Hematopoietic stem-cell mobilization responder endpoint (CD34+ cell-yield threshold within a limited apheresis-session count)"); key secondary endpoints using the same CD34+-threshold construct at a lower yield and a single-session cap

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test (§3, stratified by remission status and baseline platelet count), with logistic-regression and multiple-imputation (MAR/MNAR) sensitivity analyses

- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (§4) across a primary plus two key-secondary CD34+-threshold endpoints

- *Interim/alpha-spending:* Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function (§5) at a single pre-specified interim analysis (final two-sided α=0.0466256, interim α=0.0108678 at ~65% enrollment), conducted by an independent unblinded statistician reporting only to the DMC

- *Missing data/bias:* Tipping-point analysis (multiple imputation) (§6), required by FDA to confirm robustness of results after enrollment was halted early on DMC recommendation

- *Regulatory:* FDA-directed correction of a sponsor's favorable-rounding convention for a threshold responder endpoint (FDA required re-derivation of CD34+ yield classifications after finding the sponsor's rounding convention could favor the treatment arm); reviewer-documented use of an unplanned-for-efficacy interim analysis result as the trial's final efficacy basis, validated via tipping-point/robustness sensitivity analyses (related to but distinct from the existing "Unplanned unblinded interim looks prompting an ad hoc multiplicity correction" row, §7, Vorapaxar)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- GENESIS (Study BL-8040.SCM.301, NCT03246529): Phase 3, two-part design agreed with FDA at an April 26, 2017 Type C meeting. Part 1 (open-label, up to 30 subjects in staggered ~10-subject cohorts reviewed by an independent DMC) confirmed the 1.25 mg/kg dose. Part 2 (randomized 2:1, triple-masked, placebo-controlled) enrolled adults ages 18-78 with histologically confirmed multiple myeloma, ≥1 week post last induction chemotherapy, eligible for autologous transplant, in first/second complete or partial remission, ECOG 0-1; key exclusions included prior transplant, prior failed HSC collection, and prior venetoclax. Regimen: G-CSF on Days 1-5 (±6-8), motixafortide or placebo subcutaneously on Day 4 (±6), apheresis starting Day 5. 162 subjects were screened, 124 treated with G-CSF, and 122 randomized (80 motixafortide/42 placebo); enrollment was stopped early on DMC recommendation at approximately 68.9% of the planned 177-subject sample after the trial's sole pre-specified interim analysis.

- Primary endpoint: proportion of subjects mobilizing ≥6×10⁶ CD34+ cells/kg within ≤2 apheresis sessions after a single motixafortide/placebo dose. Key secondary endpoints (hierarchical gatekeeping order): (1) proportion collecting ≥2×10⁶ CD34+ cells/kg in 1 apheresis session; (2) proportion collecting ≥6×10⁶ CD34+ cells/kg in 1 apheresis session. Additional secondaries: time to neutrophil/platelet/overall engraftment, graft durability at 60 days/100 days/6 months/12 months, and a pharmacoeconomic endpoint; exploratory endpoints included overall survival, relapse-free survival, and myeloma-cell mobilization.

- Sample-size/power: Part 2 assumed a placebo+G-CSF success rate of 35% (from plerixafor's pivotal trial) vs. 70% for motixafortide (worst-case ITT-adjusted to 63% assuming 20% non-adherence); the target 177 subjects (20%-attrition-inflated) gave 89.8% power at a final two-sided alpha of 0.0466256 (Lan-DeMets-adjusted), with an interim-analysis alpha of 0.0108678 at approximately 65% enrollment.

- Primary analysis: CMH test stratified by remission status and baseline platelet count on central-lab CD34+ data, intent-to-treat population (N=122). Result: 67.5% (motixafortide) vs. 9.5% (placebo) responders; CMH common proportion difference 56.8% (95% CI 42.6-71.0%, p<0.0001); OR 15.1 (95% CI 4.86-46.9). Key secondary #1 (≥2×10⁶/kg, 1 apheresis): 87.5% vs. 38.1%, difference 48.3% (95% CI 31.6-65.0%), p<0.0001. Key secondary #2 (≥6×10⁶/kg, 1 apheresis): 63.8% vs. 2.4%, difference 60.0% (95% CI 49.0-72.0%), p<0.0001.

- FDA-identified rounding dispute: the sponsor's original analysis rounded CD34+ yields of ≥5.5 million to 6 million and ≥1.5 million to 2 million for responder classification; FDA's clinical/statistical teams found this convention unacceptable as it could favor the investigational arm, and required a re-analysis rounding only ≥5.95 million to 6 million and ≥1.95 million to 2 million — the re-analysis was consistent with the original.

- FDA efficacy-review issues (documented at the December 17, 2021 pre-NDA meeting and February 24, 2023 mid-cycle meeting): (1) the observed placebo response rate (9.5% central-lab) was markedly lower than the SAP's assumed 35% and than plerixafor's own pivotal-trial placebo rate (34%), attributed to central- vs. local-lab measurement differences (local-lab placebo response was 21.4%) and evolving multiple-myeloma induction regimens (70% prior lenalidomide exposure in GENESIS vs. 6% in the plerixafor trial); a post-hoc site-level subgroup analysis ruled out a single site (with 0% placebo responders) as the driver. (2) Because the trial's sole pre-specified interim analysis was designed only to support an enrollment-continuation decision (not an efficacy claim), and the DMC's October 29, 2020 recommendation to halt enrollment given "unambiguous efficacy" led to stopping at 122 of the planned 177 subjects, FDA required documentation of the DMC's recommendation and additional tipping-point sensitivity analyses projecting results at full (177) and 75%-of-target (132) enrollment; FDA concluded the observed results were robust despite the early stop.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

Genuine sponsor Protocol and SAP text is publicly posted for GENESIS (combined document, cited above), and the FDA Integrated Review discusses its content extensively; however, the specific passages retrieved during sourcing were summarized rather than transcribed verbatim, so precise quotations are not presented here to avoid misattributing paraphrase as quotation — a follow-up pass against the posted `Prot_SAP_000.pdf` and the Integrated Review PDF directly would allow verbatim excerpting of the interim-analysis, multiplicity, and rounding-convention sections in particular.

**Reverse-engineered SAP** (traced to the specific reported results and design elements above)

- *[inferred]* The SAP's sample-size assumptions (35% placebo/70% motixafortide) were most likely benchmarked directly to plerixafor's own pivotal trial (DiPersio 2009) given that GENESIS's control arm is G-CSF alone, the standard comparator design for this drug class, and FDA's review explicitly attributes the lower-than-assumed observed placebo rate to differences from that historical benchmark trial's population.

- *[inferred]* The SAP's rounding convention for CD34+ yield classification (≥5.5M→6M, ≥1.5M→2M) most plausibly reflected a standard significant-figures rounding rule applied mechanically to lab-reported values, rather than a deliberate attempt to favor the treatment arm — inferred from FDA's characterization of the issue as a data-handling concern requiring correction rather than a misconduct finding, and from the fact that the corrected (stricter) rounding rule did not change the trial's conclusions.

### 24. Momelotinib (Ojjaara) — NDA 216873

**Sponsor:** GlaxoSmithKline (development conducted by Sierra Oncology, Inc. prior to GSK's 2022 acquisition)

**Indication approved:** Intermediate or high-risk myelofibrosis (including primary myelofibrosis and post-polycythemia vera/post-essential thrombocythemia myelofibrosis) in adults with anemia

**Approval date:** September 15, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** MOMENTUM (Study SRA-MMB-301, NCT04173494)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1, vs. danazol) trial, quadruple-masked, using a non-deterministic biased-coin covariate-adaptive minimization randomization scheme (Pocock 1975; Han 2009) with non-1.0 allocation probabilities (0.9/0.8) — distinct from the ad hoc "stochastic-minimization" language used for icatibant's FAST-3 trial and possibly warranting its own taxonomy row if this method recurs ("Non-deterministic biased-coin covariate-adaptive minimization randomization (Pocock-Han)"); FDA-directed trial redesign following an earlier failed pivotal program (SIMPLIFY-1/SIMPLIFY-2)

- *Endpoints:* MFSAF v4.0 Total Symptom Score (TSS) response rate at Week 24 (primary); Transfusion Independence status, Splenic Response Rate, TSS change from baseline, and rate of no transfusion as key secondaries in a pre-specified hierarchy

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test (§3, stratified by the three randomization strata) for binary endpoints, with Mantel-Haenszel common risk difference and a stratified Newcombe method (§3) confidence interval; Mixed Model for Repeated Measures (factors: treatment, baseline TSS/spleen-length/transfusion strata) for the continuous TSS-change key secondary; Koch et al. (1989) method for the non-inferiority proportion-difference confidence interval on the Transfusion Independence endpoint — a named method for a scaled/retained-fraction margin, distinct from the taxonomy's existing fixed additive/ratio-margin entries ("Koch et al. (1989) method for a scaled/retained-fraction non-inferiority margin CI")

- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (§4) across five key secondaries, with the Transfusion Independence endpoint tested first as a non-inferiority-then-nominal-superiority step (margin: momelotinib proportion ≥0.8× danazol proportion)

- *Missing data/bias:* Non-responder imputation for missing binary/diary efficacy data (§6) for the primary/key-secondary binary endpoints; a January 2023 data-management correction affecting 6 subjects' non-responder coding for prohibited concomitant therapy, with conclusions unchanged after correction

- *Regulatory:* FDA-conducted independent regional-consistency/applicability analysis of a global trial's US subgroup (FDA's Integrated Review §6.3.1 separately examined whether the small 24-subject US cohort's results were consistent with the full global trial, concluding a lower US baseline TSS, not a lack of effect, explained an observed discrepancy); no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held; SIMPLIFY-1/SIMPLIFY-2 (an earlier, non-pivotal Phase 3 program) failed to demonstrate substantial evidence of effectiveness, prompting FDA to require a new pivotal trial and to directly shape MOMENTUM's design (rejecting the sponsor's initially proposed Transfusion-Independence-as-primary-endpoint design and requiring TSS remain primary)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- MOMENTUM (Study SRA-MMB-301, NCT04173494): Phase 3, randomized 2:1 (momelotinib:danazol+momelotinib-placebo), quadruple-masked, multicenter trial in symptomatic, anemic adults with primary myelofibrosis, post-polycythemia-vera myelofibrosis, or post-essential-thrombocythemia myelofibrosis previously treated with a JAK inhibitor. A 24-week randomized double-blind treatment period was followed by an open-label extension to Week 48, during which danazol-arm responders could cross over to open-label momelotinib. Randomization used a non-deterministic biased-coin minimization method (allocation probabilities 0.9/0.8), stratified by baseline MFSAF TSS (<22 vs. ≥22), baseline palpable spleen length (<12 vs. ≥12 cm below the left costal margin), and baseline RBC/whole-blood transfusion units in the 8 weeks pre-randomization (0, 1-4, ≥5). 195 patients were randomized (130 momelotinib/65 danazol+placebo).

- Sample size: 180 planned (195 actual), powered via the Fleiss et al. (1980) method to 98.8% for a 21-point TSS response-rate difference (23% momelotinib vs. 2% danazol) and 90% for a 15-point difference (17% vs. 2%); also approximately 90% powered for the Transfusion Independence (45% vs. 21%) and Splenic Response Rate (15% vs. 1%) key secondaries.

- Primary endpoint: MFSAF v4.0 TSS response rate at Week 24 (≥50% reduction in mean TSS over the 28 days immediately preceding the end of Week 24, versus baseline). Key secondaries, tested via a pre-specified hierarchy gated on the primary being significant: (1) Transfusion Independence status at Week 24 — non-inferiority first (margin: momelotinib proportion ≥0.8× danazol proportion, lower 95% CI bound >0; a nominal, non-multiplicity-controlled superiority p-value was also computed); (2) Splenic Response Rate ≥25% volume reduction at Week 24 — superiority; (3) MFSAF TSS change from baseline at Week 24 — superiority; (4) Splenic Response Rate ≥35% volume reduction — superiority; (5) rate of no transfusion at Week 24 — superiority.

- Primary analysis: CMH test stratified by the three randomization strata for binary endpoints (exact binomial 95% CI per arm; Mantel-Haenszel common risk difference with a stratified Newcombe CI for the between-arm difference); MMRM for the continuous TSS-change key secondary; the Koch et al. (1989) method for the non-inferiority proportion-difference CI on the Transfusion Independence endpoint. Missing primary/key-secondary binary-endpoint data was imputed as non-responder. Intent-to-treat population primary, per-protocol population for sensitivity.

- Results: primary endpoint met — TSS response 24.6% momelotinib vs. 9.2% danazol, difference 15.7% (95% CI 5.5-25.8), p=0.0095. All five key secondaries met in the pre-specified order: Transfusion Independence 30.0% vs. 20.0% (non-inferiority difference 13.6%, 95% CI 1.9-25.3, p=0.023; nominal superiority difference 9.8%, p=0.13, not multiplicity-controlled); Splenic Response Rate ≥25%: 39.2% vs. 6.2% (difference 33.1%, p<0.0001); TSS change LS-mean difference −6.2 (95% CI −10.0, −2.4, p=0.0014); Splenic Response Rate ≥35%: 22.3% vs. 3.1% (difference 18.2%, p=0.001); no-transfusion rate 35.4% vs. 16.9% (difference 17.2%, p=0.001).

- Notable review issues: a January 17, 2023 clinical-information amendment corrected a data-management vendor error in which 6 subjects who received prohibited anti-MF therapy had not been coded as non-responders per the SAP rule; the correction flipped one subject's status on three key secondaries, with conclusions unchanged. FDA's Integrated Review §6.3.1 ("Applicability of MOMENTUM Results to U.S. Population") documents a dedicated FDA sub-analysis: only 24 US subjects were enrolled, and 0 of 15 with evaluable Week-24 TSS achieved the primary responder threshold; FDA ran additional continuous-scale/MMRM sensitivity analyses on the small US subgroup (numerically favoring momelotinib with overlapping CIs) and concluded via a CDF-curve comparison that a lower US baseline TSS, not a lack of drug effect, explained the discrepancy.

- Regulatory history: momelotinib's first-generation Phase 3 program — SIMPLIFY-1 (NCT01969838, vs. ruxolitinib, JAK-inhibitor-naive, non-inferiority design on Splenic Response Rate) and SIMPLIFY-2 (vs. best available therapy) — did not provide substantial evidence of effectiveness (SIMPLIFY-2 primary Splenic Response Rate: 6.7% momelotinib vs. 5.8% best-available-therapy, p=0.90). A January 2017 Type C meeting concluded a new pivotal trial was required; FDA rejected the sponsor's initially proposed design making Transfusion Independence the primary endpoint (January 2019 meeting), instead requiring TSS remain primary with Transfusion Independence as the first alpha-controlled key secondary.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

Genuine sponsor Protocol and SAP documents are both publicly posted for MOMENTUM (cited above); the FDA Integrated Review and the posted SAP together document the design, hierarchy, and analysis methods described above in detail, but exact quoted sentences were not transcribed during sourcing — a follow-up pass directly against the posted `SAP_001.pdf` (particularly §9.1 "Hierarchical Testing" and §9.1.1's historical-control derivation of the 80% non-inferiority retention fraction, citing Cervantes 2015) would allow verbatim excerpting.

**Reverse-engineered SAP** (traced to the specific reported results and design elements above)

- *[inferred]* The 80%-retention non-inferiority margin for the Transfusion Independence endpoint was most likely derived from a historical benchmark of danazol's own expected response rate in myelofibrosis-associated anemia (plausibly Cervantes et al. 2015, given the citation appearing in the SAP's table of contents structure reported by reviewers), since a proportional retention margin requires an assumed comparator response rate to anchor the 0.8× multiplier.

- *[inferred]* The gap between the multiplicity-controlled non-inferiority test (p=0.023) and the nominal, uncontrolled superiority p-value (p=0.13) for Transfusion Independence implies the SAP's pre-specified inferential claim for that endpoint was non-inferiority only, with superiority reported strictly for descriptive completeness — consistent with FDA reporting both figures without treating the superiority p-value as contributing to the overall Type-I-error-controlled conclusion.

### 25. Efbemalenograstim alfa-vuxw (Ryzneuta) — BLA 761134

**Sponsor:** Evive Biotechnology (formerly Generon)

**Indication approved:** To decrease the incidence of infection, as manifested by febrile neutropenia, in adult patients with non-myeloid malignancies receiving myelosuppressive anti-cancer drugs associated with a clinically significant incidence of febrile neutropenia

**Approval date:** November 16, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** GC-627-05 (NCT03252431), supported by GC-627-04 (NCT02872103)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, open-label, active-controlled (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1, GC-627-05, vs. pegfilgrastim/Neulasta) non-inferiority trial, supported by a randomized, quadruple-masked, placebo-controlled trial (GC-627-04) in which all subjects received open-label study drug from cycle 2 onward; this is a novel (351(a)) BLA, not a biosimilar, but FDA applied biosimilar-development "biocreep" reasoning to tighten its non-inferiority margin — no existing taxonomy term captures this cross-pollination of biosimilar NI-margin discipline onto a novel BLA in a crowded me-too drug class ("FDA imports biosimilar-development 'biocreep' non-inferiority-margin discipline onto a novel (non-biosimilar) BLA in a crowded me-too drug class")

- *Endpoints:* Duration in days of Grade 4 (severe) neutropenia (ANC <0.5×10⁹/L) in chemotherapy cycle 1, a continuous non-inferiority endpoint against an active comparator

- *Primary analysis:* Two-sample t-test (GC-627-05) on the mean-duration difference against a pre-specified non-inferiority margin

- *Multiplicity:* Fallback Procedure (§4) across six secondary endpoints with pre-allocated per-endpoint alpha (0.0486, 0.001, and four at 0.0001), continuous secondaries tested via t-test/Wilcoxon fallback and categorical secondaries via chi-square/Fisher's exact

- *Missing data/bias:* Tipping-point analysis (multiple imputation) (§6, exact match, both trials); Worst-case-scenario asymmetric sensitivity analysis (§6, GC-627-04, direction-asymmetric imputation rule by arm); multiple imputation via SAS PROC MIANALYZE, fully conditional specification, and bootstrap-MI variants for missing ANC values underlying the primary endpoint

- *Regulatory:* No FDA Advisory Committee meeting held; FDA statistical reviewers rejected the sponsor's originally proposed 1-day non-inferiority margin (benchmarked to filgrastim/Neupogen's own NI margin against Neulasta) as inadequately justified and required a tighter 0.6-day margin explicitly to guard against biocreep; the pivotal GC-627-05 non-inferiority trial itself has no PubMed-indexed peer-reviewed publication, so FDA's Integrated Review/CSR is the sole public source for its exact results

**Trial design & endpoints**

- GC-627-05 (NCT03252431, "Neulasta-controlled Trial of F-627 in Women With Breast Cancer Receiving Myelotoxic Chemotherapy"): Phase 3, randomized 1:1, multicenter, open-label, fixed-dose, active-controlled non-inferiority trial vs. pegfilgrastim (Neulasta) 6 mg, in women with stage I-III breast cancer receiving docetaxel 75 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² (TC) for 4 cycles. N=393 (197/196) across 41 sites in 5 countries (Ukraine, Russia, Hungary, Bulgaria, and 1 US site), conducted April 2018-March 2020; randomization stratified by country/region. The trial was open-label by necessity given differing device/vial appearance between the two products, with the ANC-based primary endpoint treated as objectively assessed and dosing staff kept separate from blinded outcome assessors where feasible.

- GC-627-04 (NCT02872103, "Placebo-controlled Trial of F-627..."): Phase 3, randomized 2:1 (F-627:placebo), quadruple-masked, supportive trial. N=122 (83/39), stage II-IV breast cancer, docetaxel+doxorubicin (TA) chemotherapy; all subjects received open-label F-627 in cycles 2-4. Sites in Ukraine, Russia, Hungary, and the US, conducted August 2016-November 2017.

- Both trials had genuine sponsor SAPs and protocols posted on ClinicalTrials.gov: GC-627-05's SAP is dated April 3, 2017; GC-627-04's SAP is dated separately (SAP_002).

- A third trial, NCT04174599 (China, filgrastim-active-controlled, N=239), is a supportive China-registration trial not discussed in the FDA Integrated Review's efficacy sections and not part of the US approval basis.

- Primary endpoint (both pivotal trials): duration in days of Grade 4 (severe) neutropenia (ANC <0.5×10⁹/L) in chemotherapy cycle 1.

- GC-627-05 statistical design: H0: mean duration difference (F-627 minus Neulasta) ≥0.6 days vs. Ha: <0.6 days; non-inferiority margin 0.6 days, primary analysis by two-sample t-test, intent-to-treat population (with a per-protocol population as sensitivity, though the SAP and the Integrated Review's final analysis-method description differ on which population was designated primary for the non-inferiority claim). At the IND stage, the sponsor originally proposed a 1-day non-inferiority margin, benchmarked to Neulasta's own licensure basis (a non-inferiority trial of pegfilgrastim vs. filgrastim/Neupogen using a 1-day margin); FDA's statistical review team found this justification inadequate and required the tighter 0.6-day margin specifically to guard against biocreep — the risk that repeatedly using an inadequately conservative non-inferiority margin across successive me-too products could allow a cumulatively ineffective drug onto the market.

- Sample size: 174/arm for 90% power, 386 total planned with 10% dropout, based on Phase 2 (GC-627-02) data.

- Multiplicity: a Fallback Procedure across six secondary endpoints with pre-allocated per-endpoint alpha (0.0486, 0.001, and four at 0.0001); continuous secondaries tested via t-test/Wilcoxon fallback, categorical secondaries via chi-square/Fisher's exact.

- Missing data: the primary endpoint's missing ANC values were handled via multiple imputation (SAS PROC MIANALYZE, plus fully-conditional-specification and bootstrap-MI variants as sensitivity analyses), a named tipping-point analysis, and — in GC-627-04 — a worst-case-scenario asymmetric imputation sensitivity analysis.

- Results: GC-627-05 — mean duration of Grade 4 neutropenia in cycle 1 was 0.2 days in both arms; multiple-imputation-adjusted mean difference 0.0 days (95% CI −0.1, 0.1); the one-sided 97.5% CI upper bound was below 0.6, demonstrating non-inferiority (superiority was not demonstrated, as the two-sided 95% CI upper bound was not below 0). None of the six secondary endpoints reached significance under the fallback procedure (e.g., IV-antibiotic days, p=0.0538 vs. an allocated α of 0.0486 — narrowly missed). GC-627-04 (vs. placebo) — LS-mean duration 1.4 vs. 4.3 days, difference 2.9 days (95% CI 2.3-3.4, p<0.0001), with all sensitivity analyses (bootstrap MI, fully-conditional-specification MI, worst-case imputation, tipping-point) consistent.

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2023/761134s000lbl.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record, GC-627-04 — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02872103 (genuine sponsor SAP posted at https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/03/NCT02872103/SAP_002.pdf)

- Pivotal publication (GC-627-04, placebo-controlled, supportive): Glaspy J, Bondarenko I, Burdaeva O, et al. "Efbemalenograstim alfa, an Fc fusion protein, long-acting granulocyte-colony stimulating factor for reducing the risk of febrile neutropenia following chemotherapy: results of a phase III trial." *Support Care Cancer.* 2023;32(1):34. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00520-023-08176-6), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38103088/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Efbemalenograstim%20alfa%2C%20an%20Fc%20fusion%20protein%2C%20long-acting%20granulocyte-colony%20stimulating%20factor)

- Pivotal trial GC-627-05 (Neulasta-controlled, the trial supporting the primary non-inferiority claim): no PubMed-indexed peer-reviewed publication was found (searched directly by NCT03252431 and by title/keyword combinations); the FDA Integrated Review/CSR is the only public source for its exact results.

**Other resources**

- No Vivli/YODA Project/Project Data Sphere participation was identified for Evive Biotechnology (Shanghai/Singapore); not independently confirmed either way.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was convened for this BLA (FDA Integrated Review, §11: no safety or efficacy issues arose needing an Advisory Committee meeting).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.3.3, p.48-49]* — "At the IND stage, there were several correspondences between the Applicant and the FDA statistical review team in regard to the acceptability of the NI margin... The Applicant originally proposed a NI margin of 1 day, however, the FDA statistical review team concluded that the justification for this margin of 1 day was not adequate and acceptable. The statistical review team further recommended a NI margin of 0.6 day to avoid potential biocreep (i.e., ineffective biosimilar drug may be allowed on the market if an inadequate NI margin is repeatedly used for some time) based on a trial using Neulasta as the comparator, since it was US-licensed based on a noninferiority trial to Neupogen (filgrastim) with a NI margin of 1 day."

*[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §11, p.123]* — "No Advisory Committee was convened for this application because there were no safety or efficacy issues that arose needing an Advisory Committee meeting."

**Reverse-engineered SAP** (traced to the specific reported results and design elements above)

- *[inferred]* GC-627-05's discrepancy between the SAP's stated primary analysis population (per-protocol, per the fork research summary of the SAP text) and the Integrated Review's final analysis using intent-to-treat as primary most likely reflects a standard NI-trial convention where both populations are examined and the more conservative/concordant one is emphasized in the label, rather than a deviation FDA treated as a review issue — inferred from the absence of any FDA commentary flagging this as a problem, unlike the explicit rounding/margin disputes documented elsewhere in this drug class's other entries in this batch.

### 26. Iptacopan (Fabhalta) — NDA 218276

**Sponsor:** Novartis

**Indication approved:** Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH) in adults with hemolytic anemia

**Approval date:** December 5, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** APPLY-PNH (Study CLNP023C12302, NCT04558918) and APPOINT-PNH (Study CLNP023C12301, NCT04820530)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, open-label, active-controlled (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1, APPLY-PNH, 8:5 randomization, switch design vs. continued anti-C5 antibody therapy) paired with a single-arm, open-label trial (§1, APPOINT-PNH, complement-inhibitor-naive) as a two-trial pivotal program; small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (§1, N=97 and N=40)

- *Endpoints:* Co-primary endpoints (§1) — a family of two hemoglobin-based responder endpoints (sustained ≥2 g/dL increase from baseline; sustained Hb ≥12 g/dL), each requiring transfusion avoidance over the same window

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test (§3) — notably imposed on the sponsor by FDA over the Applicant's own preferred method (see Regulatory, below); Marginal standardization (g-computation) for a covariate-adjusted risk difference (§3, transfusion-avoidance secondary); Non-inferiority analysis against a fixed historical-control threshold / FDA post-hoc-derived non-inferiority margin for a single-arm trial (§1/§3, APPOINT-PNH's 15% fixed performance-goal threshold, here sponsor-derived via simulation from historical eculizumab trials and FDA-endorsed rather than FDA-derived)

- *Multiplicity:* Graphical alpha-propagation method (Maurer-Bretz) (§3/§4, already tagged to Camizestrant — reuse and extend "Seen in" to APPLY-PNH) across the two co-primary endpoints, a 4-endpoint secondary family, and a final tier

- *Missing data/bias:* Jump-to-reference (J2R) multiple imputation (§6, closely related "copy-reference" variant for iptacopan-arm dropouts) combined with multiple imputation under MAR (100 imputations, Rubin's rules) for intermittent missingness; Tipping-point analysis (§6)

- *Regulatory:* Reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan (§7, exact match — FDA recommended CMH as the primary analysis method in a September 2020 "safe to proceed" letter and re-emphasized this at a December 2022 pre-NDA meeting, but the Applicant's final SAP retained a permutation-test/logistic-regression method instead, and FDA required its own CMH re-analysis to be used in labeling); no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held; a post-database-lock data correction (over a year after the primary cutoff) reversed one subject's transfusion-related responder classification, reviewed and accepted by FDA — no existing taxonomy row captures this benign-clerical-error-driven late correction, distinct from the misconduct-focused §7 rows ("Post-database-lock data correction reversing an individual subject's primary/key-secondary responder status, reviewed and accepted by FDA")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- APPLY-PNH (Study CLNP023C12302, NCT04558918): Phase 3, randomized 8:5, open-label, active-comparator (continued eculizumab or ravulizumab), parallel-group switch trial in adults ≥18 with PNH (flow-cytometry clone ≥10%) on stable anti-C5 therapy for ≥6 months with mean Hb <10 g/dL, randomized stratified by prior anti-C5 agent and transfusion history in the last 6 months. N=97 (62 iptacopan/35 anti-C5); a 24-week randomized core period was followed by crossover of the anti-C5 arm to iptacopan through Day 336 (48 weeks total).

- APPOINT-PNH (Study CLNP023C12301, NCT04820530): Phase 3, single-arm, open-label trial in complement-inhibitor-naive adults with LDH >1.5×ULN. N=40 enrolled/treated, same 24-week core + 48-week total structure.

- Co-primary endpoints (APPLY-PNH): "Family of Two Primary Endpoints: 1. Proportions of participants achieving a sustained increase in hemoglobin levels from baseline ≥2 g/dL between Day 126 (Week 18) and Day 168 (Week 24) in the absence of transfusions between Day 14 and Day 168; 2. Proportions of participants achieving sustained hemoglobin levels ≥12 g/dL between Day 126 and Day 168 in the absence of transfusions between Day 14 and Day 168." Responder status required 3 of 4 measurements in the window meeting the threshold; the transfusion-need definition was Hb ≤9 g/dL with qualifying signs/symptoms, or Hb ≤7 g/dL regardless of symptoms. APPOINT-PNH's primary endpoint used the same ≥2 g/dL responder definition as a single primary (the ≥12 g/dL threshold was a secondary there), tested against a fixed 15% performance-goal threshold rather than an active comparator.

- Sample-size rationale (APPLY-PNH): "Under an assumption that participants on iptacopan treatment would achieve a proportion of 50% of responders having an increase of ≥2 g/dL from baseline compared to a proportion of 16% of responders on anti-C5 antibody treatment, the planned sample size of 56 participants on iptacopan and 35 participants on anti-C5 antibody treatment would provide 83.2% power for this endpoint at a one-sided significance level of 0.0125... Power for the simultaneous test could not be exactly derived, but a minimum power corresponding to assuming a Bonferroni adjustment was approximately 95%." The 50% assumption was benchmarked to eculizumab's PNH Study 1 (NCT00122330). APPOINT-PNH's N=40 was instead set by a target confidence-interval half-width (≤0.155) around the responder-rate estimate.

- Primary analysis method dispute: "In the 'safe to proceed' letter dated September 28, 2020, the Agency recommended that the primary analysis for all binary endpoints be based on the stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test. The Agency re-emphasized this recommendation... during the pre-NDA meeting dated December 14, 2022... However, the Applicant did not change the primary analysis method to CMH in their final version of the statistical analysis plan (SAP)." FDA required the Applicant to re-run CMH analyses during review and mandated the CMH results (not the sponsor's permutation-test/logistic-regression numbers) be used in the label.

- Results (APPLY-PNH, FDA's CMH analysis): ≥2 g/dL Hb responders 51/62 (82.3%) iptacopan vs. 0/35 (0.0%) anti-C5, Mantel-Haenszel stratum-weighted difference 81.5% (95% CI 71.6-91.4); Hb ≥12 g/dL 42/62 (67.7%) vs. 0/35 (0.0%), difference 66.6% (95% CI 54.6-78.6), both p<0.0001. APPOINT-PNH: marginal responder proportion 92.2% (95% CI 82.5-100.0) against the 15% fixed threshold (itself derived by FDA-accepted simulation from historical eculizumab trials, ALXN1210-PNH-301 and TRIUMPH), comfortably clearing the bar.

- Multiplicity: a graphical alpha-propagation approach (sourced to the Applicant's SAP): the two co-primary endpoints tested first at equal weight; alpha passed to a 4-endpoint secondary family (transfusion avoidance, Hb change, FACIT-Fatigue, reticulocytes); alpha passed on again, only after all four secondaries were rejected, to a final tier (LDH, breakthrough hemolysis, major adverse vascular events).

- Missing data: multiple imputation (100 imputations, Rubin's rules) under MAR for intermittent missingness; a "copy-reference" imputation for iptacopan-arm dropouts (imputing as if treatment had continued); tipping-point sensitivity analyses (deducting a 2 g/dL delta from imputed Hb in the iptacopan arm) confirmed robustness (APPLY-PNH primary results held at 76.8%/64.1% differences vs. the 80.2%/67.0% base case).

- Notable data-integrity event (APPLY-PNH): after the primary data cutoff (September 26, 2022), the Applicant discovered on October 24, 2023 that a transfusion given to an iptacopan-arm subject during the 24-week core period had been omitted from the locked database due to a site error; the database was unlocked, corrected, and re-analyzed (the subject flipped from responder to non-responder on the transfusion-avoidance/primary-endpoint-adjacent analyses). FDA reviewed the sponsor's quality-management/audit response and accepted the correction.
