### 36. Narsoplimab-wuug (Yartemlea) — BLA 761152

**Sponsor:** Omeros Corporation

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adult and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older with hematopoietic stem cell transplant-associated thrombotic microangiopathy (TA-TMA)

**Approval date:** December 23, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** Study OMS721-TMA-001 ("Study TMA-001"), NCT02222545, with confirmatory evidence from an Expanded Access Program (EAP) patient-level subgroup

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Single-arm, open-label, uncontrolled, three-stage dose-escalation-then-fixed-dose Phase 2 trial in adults with TA-TMA, with effectiveness assessed against a historical control response rate derived from pooled published literature rather than a concurrent comparator arm (closest existing taxonomy match: "Non-inferiority analysis against a fixed historical-control threshold (no concurrent comparator arm)," though this design used a literature-pooled response-rate benchmark with non-overlapping confidence intervals rather than a pre-specified non-inferiority margin) ("single-arm trial with a literature-pooled historical-control response rate as primary comparator, corroborated by a second independent data source (an expanded-access program's patient-level data) serving as confirmatory evidence in lieu of a second pivotal trial" — distinct from the taxonomy's matched-historical-control entries, which use patient-level genotype/natural-history matching rather than a literature-pooled aggregate rate); a prior (2021) Complete Response Letter and full resubmission with new external-control data

- *Endpoints:* TA-TMA response rate (primary) — improvement in TMA-associated laboratory markers (platelet count and LDH) plus improvement in clinical status (organ function or transfusion freedom) at any post-baseline timepoint; overall survival (supportive, propensity-score-adjusted external-control comparison)

- *Primary analysis:* Response-rate point estimate with 95% CI (Clopper-Pearson/exact-type), compared descriptively (non-overlapping CIs) against a literature-derived historical control rate; propensity-score matching/weighting (logistic regression on baseline covariates) for a supportive OS comparison against an external registry cohort (Kyoto Stem Cell Transplantation Group [KSCTG] registry)

- *Missing data/bias:* FDA noted low-to-moderate propensity-score overlap/common support and extreme (near-0/near-1) propensity scores in the external-control comparison as a reliability limitation of the supportive OS analysis

- *Regulatory:* Complete Response Letter issued October 15, 2021, citing failure to demonstrate substantial evidence of effectiveness; resubmission (March 26, 2025) added external-control literature data and expanded-access patient-level data, including a new major amendment (May 2025 KSCTG registry data) that extended the PDUFA date by 3 months; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was convened for either review cycle

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study TMA-001 was a Phase 2, uncontrolled, three-stage dose-escalation trial of narsoplimab (a MASP-2-inhibiting monoclonal antibody targeting the lectin pathway of complement) in adult patients with high-risk TA-TMA persisting at least 2 weeks after modification/discontinuation of calcineurin inhibitors (or ≥30 days post-transplant), with platelet count <150,000/µL, evidence of microangiopathic hemolysis, and renal dysfunction, meeting high-risk criteria per Schoettler et al. (2023) consensus guidelines. The primary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of patients achieving a TMA response (improvement in platelet count and LDH, plus improvement in organ function at any post-baseline timepoint or freedom from transfusion).

- Results: 17 of 28 patients (61%; 95% CI 40.6–78.5) achieved a TMA response in Study TMA-001. This was compared against a historic response rate of 23.3% (95% CI 15.1–34.2), derived from FDA's/the Applicant's analysis of 149 literature-identified TA-TMA patients who had not received narsoplimab or other pharmacologic TA-TMA treatment; FDA's review concluded that because this literature-derived rate pooled less-stringent response criteria than Study TMA-001 used, it would likely overestimate the true historic response rate and could therefore serve as an acceptable (conservative-against-the-applicant) benchmark. The non-overlapping confidence intervals (61% vs. 23.3%) supported the effectiveness conclusion.

- Confirmatory evidence: 19 patients (13 adult, 6 pediatric) treated under an Expanded Access Program with patient-level data available ("EAP Subgroup 1") had a TA-TMA response rate of 13/19 (68%), consistent with the Study TMA-001 primary result; the 6 pediatric patients in this subgroup had baseline characteristics and response rates consistent with the adult population, supporting partial extrapolation of effectiveness to pediatric patients 2 years of age and older.

- Supportive OS analysis: propensity-score-based methods (logistic regression on baseline covariates) were used to compare narsoplimab-treated patients against an external comparator cohort drawn from the Kyoto Stem Cell Transplantation Group (KSCTG) registry (both 1:1 and 1:2 propensity-score-matching strategies were examined, alongside a pooled-dataset comparison). FDA's review noted only low-to-moderate covariate overlap between cohorts and some propensity scores at the extremes (near 0 or 1), limiting confidence in this supportive analysis even though point estimates and very small p-values (<0.001) nominally favored narsoplimab across methods.

- Regulatory history: the original BLA (submitted October 15, 2021, immediately preceding the original review cycle's CRL) was found not to demonstrate substantial evidence of effectiveness. The March 26, 2025 resubmission added a formal external-control literature analysis and expanded-access patient-level data; a further submission of individual-patient KSCTG registry data (May 20 and 27, 2025) was deemed a major amendment, extending the PDUFA goal date by three months to allow full review.

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/761152Orig1s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Integrated (Clinical, Statistical, and Clinical Pharmacology) Review; Reference ID 5718152; Division of Nonmalignant Hematology — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761152Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf

**Other resources**

The adequate and well-controlled investigation is Study OMS-721-TMA-001... Confirmatory evidence was provided by efficacy data from patients treated under an expanded access program for whom patient level data was available (EAP Subgroup 1)."

This was compared to a historic response rate of 23.3% (95% CI: 15.1, 34.2), which was based on analysis of 149 patients with TA-TMA identified in the literature who had not received narsoplimab or other pharmacologic treatment for TA-TMA... The TMA-001 response rate of 61% is higher than the selected literature based historic control response rate 23.3% (95% CI: 15.1, 34.2) with non-overlapping confidence intervals."

This extrapolation is reasonable given the similarity in the pathophysiology, clinical signs and symptoms, and course of TA-TMA in adults and pediatric patients."

### 37. Rusfertide (Mimrylo) — NDA 220605

**Sponsor:** Takeda Pharmaceuticals (Takeda Pharmaceuticals America, Inc.; rusfertide originated at Protagonist Therapeutics)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of erythrocytosis in adults with polycythemia vera (PV)

**Approval date:** August 28, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** VERIFY, NCT05210790

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial (add-on to each patient's ongoing PV standard of care — phlebotomy alone or phlebotomy plus one or more cytoreductive agents), 1:1 randomization for a 32-week blinded period, followed by open-label rusfertide for all patients through Week 156

- *Endpoints:* Proportion of patients achieving response (absence of phlebotomy eligibility) from Week 20 through Week 32 (primary); mean number of phlebotomies (Baseline to Week 32); proportion maintaining hematocrit <45% (Week 0–32); change from baseline in PROMIS Fatigue Short Form 8a score at Week 32

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratifying by ongoing standard-of-care therapy (common risk difference and 95% CI, same Mantel-Haenszel common-risk-difference-plus-CMH approach flagged as a proposed new taxonomy term under this batch's rilzabrutinib entry) for the binary response and hematocrit-maintenance endpoints; ANCOVA (adjusted for pre-treatment phlebotomy count, treatment, and stratification variable) for mean-phlebotomies; MMRM (adjusted for baseline, treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit and baseline-by-visit interaction, and stratification variable) for the fatigue score

- *Regulatory:* This is a very recent approval (2 weeks before this entry's research date); no FDA Statistical/Clinical/Multi-Discipline Review or Drugs@FDA "Review" TOC page was posted as of this writing — only the Approval Letter and Package Insert are available on Drugs@FDA. This entry's trial-design and analysis details are therefore drawn from the approved package insert's Clinical Studies (Section 14) description, not from a verified FDA statistical review

**Trial design & endpoints**

- VERIFY randomized 293 adult PV patients (mean age 57 years; 73% male; 89.4% White) who required at least 3 phlebotomies in the 28 weeks (or 5 in 1 year) prior to randomization due to inadequate hematocrit control on standard-of-care therapy (phlebotomy alone [44.7%], phlebotomy+hydroxyurea [38.9%], phlebotomy+ruxolitinib [2.4%], phlebotomy+interferon [13.3%], or phlebotomy+combination cytoreductive therapy [0.6%]); 53.2% were low-risk (age <60, no prior thrombotic event) and 46.8% high-risk. Patients were randomized 1:1 to rusfertide (starting dose 19 mg SC once weekly, titrated to maintain hematocrit <45%) or placebo, added on to standard of care, for a 32-week double-blind period, with open-label rusfertide offered thereafter through Week 52 and long-term extension through Week 156.

- Primary endpoint: proportion of patients achieving a response (absence of phlebotomy eligibility) between Week 20 and Week 32, where phlebotomy eligibility was defined as a confirmed hematocrit ≥45% that was at least 3 percentage points (absolute) above baseline (confirmed by 2 consecutive qualifying assessments), or a single hematocrit ≥48%.

- Statistical methods (as reported in the package insert): the primary binary-response endpoint and the hematocrit-maintenance endpoint were each analyzed via a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by ongoing standard-of-care therapy, reporting the common risk difference and 95% CI. Mean number of phlebotomies was analyzed via ANCOVA (adjusted for pre-treatment phlebotomy count, treatment, and the stratification variable), reporting least-squares-mean differences. The PROMIS fatigue score was analyzed via an MMRM adjusted for baseline score, treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction, baseline-by-visit interaction, and the stratification variable.

- Results: response (absence of phlebotomy eligibility, Week 20–32) was achieved by 113/147 (76.9%) on rusfertide vs. 48/146 (32.9%) on placebo; common risk difference 43.8% (95% CI 33.5–54.2%), p<0.0001. Mean phlebotomies (baseline to Week 32) were 0.53±0.224 (rusfertide) vs. 1.82±0.227 (placebo); LSM difference −1.29±0.152 (95% CI −1.59, −1.00), p<0.0001. Hematocrit <45% was maintained (Week 0–32) in 92/147 (62.6%) on rusfertide vs. 21/146 (14.4%) on placebo; common risk difference 48.2% (95% CI 38.4–57.9%), p<0.0001. Mean change in PROMIS fatigue score at Week 32 favored rusfertide (LSM difference −1.98±0.88, 95% CI −3.71, −0.25, p=0.0252).

- Because no FDA statistical review is yet posted, the multiplicity-control strategy across these four endpoints (whether hierarchically gated behind the primary endpoint, as is standard practice for this class of trial in this census, or independently tested) could not be confirmed from the label text alone; this is marked as an open item rather than assumed.

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2026/220605Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/220605Orig1s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Statistical/Clinical/Multi-Discipline Review — not yet posted on Drugs@FDA as of this writing (the per-application "Review" TOC page, e.g. `220605Orig1s000TOC.html`, returns HTTP 404); checked directly via `accessdata.fda.gov` with a browser User-Agent header per this project's sourcing playbook.

- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05210790 ; no sponsor protocol or SAP is posted (checked via the ClinicalTrials.gov API `documentSection` field — empty)

- Pivotal publication: as of this writing, no peer-reviewed primary-results publication of the VERIFY Phase 3 trial was identified via PubMed/NCBI E-utilities (searches: "rusfertide AND polycythemia vera AND phase 3"; author searches for Kremyanskaya M and Mascarenhas J, both associated with rusfertide's earlier trials). The published NEJM article on rusfertide — Kremyanskaya M, et al. "Rusfertide, a Hepcidin Mimetic, for Control of Erythrocytosis in Polycythemia Vera." *N Engl J Med.* 2024;390(8):723-735. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2308809), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38381675/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Rusfertide%2C+a+Hepcidin+Mimetic%2C+for+Control+of+Erythrocytosis+in+Polycythemia+Vera%22) (verified via NCBI E-utilities, PMID 38381675) — reports the earlier, smaller Phase 2 PACIFIC trial, not the Phase 3 VERIFY trial that supported this approval; this is noted plainly rather than citing the Phase 2 paper as the pivotal publication.

**Other resources**

- Takeda participates in clinical-trial-data-sharing arrangements (including through Vivli) as a general company policy; trial-specific data availability for VERIFY was not individually confirmed.

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was identified for this application; given the absence of a posted FDA review, this could not be independently confirmed beyond the absence of any public record of one.

**Reverse-engineered SAP [inferred — no FDA statistical review or sponsor SAP/protocol was public as of this writing; all statistical-method detail below is traced to the approved package insert's Clinical Studies section]**

- *[inferred, from Package Insert Section 14, "VERIFY"]* — the primary endpoint's use of a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by standard-of-care therapy, reported alongside a common risk difference and 95% CI (rather than, e.g., a logistic-regression odds ratio), mirrors the analysis approach used for binary responder endpoints elsewhere in this census (e.g., CINV complete-response endpoints), and is consistent with the endpoint being pre-specified as the sole formal primary hypothesis test at a single analysis timepoint (Week 20–32), given the trial's single primary p-value (p<0.0001) and no mention of an alpha-splitting or interim-analysis structure in the label text.

- *[inferred, from Package Insert Section 14]* — the ANCOVA (phlebotomy count) and MMRM (fatigue score) secondary analyses, each reported with their own nominal p-value (p<0.0001 and p=0.0252 respectively) rather than as part of an explicit gated hierarchy, suggest these were likely tested either as key secondary endpoints in a fixed-sequence hierarchy behind the primary endpoint or with some other formal multiplicity control — but the label text does not state this explicitly, so this is inferred rather than confirmed, and is flagged above as an open item pending the FDA review's eventual posting.

## Gastroenterology

### 1. Linaclotide (Linzess) — NDA 202811

**Sponsor:** Forest Laboratories, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) in adults, 290 mcg once daily (a separate, lower-dose 145 mcg once-daily strength was approved concurrently for chronic idiopathic constipation, CIC, based on a separate pair of trials, MCP-103-303 and LIN-MD-01, reviewed in a separate FDA statistical review not obtained for this entry)

**Approval date:** August 30, 2012

**Pivotal trial (IBS-C):** Study MCP-103-302 (NCT00938717, 26-week, US, 111 sites) and Study LIN-MD-31 (NCT00948818, 12-week treatment plus 4-week randomized-withdrawal period, US/Canada, 118 sites)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group (both trials); LIN-MD-31 added a 4-week double-blind randomized-withdrawal period after the 12-week treatment period, a "Randomized-withdrawal enrichment"-adjacent design though here applied to the whole randomized population rather than a run-in-selected responder subset, so distinct from the taxonomy's existing randomized-withdrawal-enrichment entry (Palynziq/PRISM-2); 5-step serial gatekeeping multiplicity procedure across 4 co-primary and 9 secondary efficacy parameters, combining a fixed-sequence first step with Hochberg procedures within later steps

- *Endpoints:* four pre-specified, alternative primary efficacy parameters, each a weekly composite responder criterion required for ≥9 (or ≥6, for the loosest definition) of the first 12 treatment weeks: (1) 9/12-Week Abdominal Pain and CSBM (APC) 3+1 Responder (≥3 complete spontaneous bowel movements [CSBMs] and a ≥1-CSBM increase from baseline, plus ≥30% decrease in mean abdominal pain score, in a given week); (2) 9/12-Week CSBM 3+1 Responder; (3) 9/12-Week Abdominal Pain Responder; (4) 6/12-Week APC +1 Responder

- *Primary analysis:* the first step of the gatekeeping procedure applied fixed-sequence testing across the four primary parameters in the order listed above (each tested at two-sided alpha=0.05, testing stopping if any hypothesis was not rejected); subsequent secondary-endpoint families (steps 2-5) were tested only if all four primary hypotheses were rejected, each step using a Hochberg procedure for its own family of parameters

- *Multiplicity:* FDA's reviewer explicitly disputed the sponsor's use of the Hochberg procedure within each gatekept step, on the grounds that Hochberg's family-wise error control is not assumption-free and its properties for negatively correlated endpoints are not fully established, recommending a Bonferroni-based gatekeeping procedure instead — though the reviewer noted this had no practical impact here because nearly all secondary p-values were <0.001 and would have passed any reasonable multiplicity-adjusted threshold (a "reviewer disagreement with a sponsor's chosen within-step multiplicity method inside an otherwise-accepted serial gatekeeping procedure, judged immaterial to the conclusion" pattern)

- *Regulatory:* no dedicated Advisory Committee meeting was held; MCP-103-302's 26-week, ~800-patient design and 9.7% treatment-difference result on the primary APC 3+1 responder endpoint were replicated in LIN-MD-31 with a more modest 7.0% treatment difference over its shorter (12-week) treatment window

**Trial design & endpoints**

- MCP-103-302: 26-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial; ~800 patients (400/arm) randomized 1:1 to linaclotide 266 mcg/day or placebo, with daily IVRS-based patient diary assessments of abdominal pain and bowel movements used to determine weekly responder status; a patient needed ≥4 complete IVRS diary calls in a week to be evaluable as a responder that week

- LIN-MD-31: same design over a 12-week treatment period, followed by a 4-week double-blind randomized-withdrawal period; conducted at 118 centers (111 US, 7 Canada)

- Linaclotide was statistically superior to placebo on all four primary efficacy parameters in MCP-103-302 (treatment differences 9.7%-20%) and on the primary APC 3+1 responder endpoint in LIN-MD-31 (7.0% difference); secondary endpoints supported by superiority included change from baseline in 12-week CSBM frequency, SBM frequency, stool consistency, and percent of abdominal-pain-free days

- FDA's reviewer identified that the sponsor had not pre-specified subgroup analyses (gender, age, race) of the primary APC 3+1 responder rate and requested these post hoc; results were consistent across subgroups (gender, age <65, race, BMI ≥30 kg/m², and baseline abdominal pain severity strata)

### 2. Teduglutide (Gattex) — NDA 203441

**Sponsor:** NPS Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (acquired by Shire in 2015, after this approval)

**Indication approved:** Short Bowel Syndrome (SBS) in adults dependent on parenteral support

**Approval date:** December 21, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** Study CL0600-020, NCT00798967 (24-week, placebo-controlled, the sole adequate and well-controlled trial per 21 CFR 314.126); principally supportive trial CL0600-004, NCT00081458 (24-week, three-arm dose-ranging)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; 24-week parallel-group design in an orphan indication (Short Bowel Syndrome); dose-ranging supportive trial with a fixed-sequence step-down multiplicity procedure across two active doses

- *Endpoints:* binary "Responder" endpoint (≥20% reduction from baseline in weekly parenteral nutrition/IV fluid volume, sustained Week 20 to Week 24); ordered categorical ("graded") response endpoint capturing both intensity and duration of PN reduction (used as primary in the supportive trial only)

- *Primary analysis:* two-sided Fisher's Exact test (pivotal trial CL0600-020); Rank ANCOVA on the graded-response endpoint (supportive trial CL0600-004)

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) gatekeeping across the two active doses in CL0600-004 — the 0.10 mg/kg/day-vs-placebo comparison failed, which formally rendered all subsequent comparisons (including the nominally significant 0.05 mg/kg/day result) exploratory under the pre-specified procedure

- *Missing data/bias:* worst-case non-responder imputation for the primary binary/graded endpoint; no-change-from-baseline imputation for change-from-baseline secondary endpoints; FDA-run "ultra-worst-case" sensitivity analysis recoding placebo dropouts as successes still favored teduglutide (exploratory)

- *Regulatory:* Gastrointestinal Drugs Advisory Committee meeting, October 16, 2012, concurred the Binary Response endpoint was clinically meaningful; orphan drug designation (granted 2000); SAP amended (April 20, 2007) to introduce the graded-response endpoint before the corresponding protocol amendment (Amendment 4b, June 29, 2007) — a blinded independent expert-panel consultation drove the endpoint redefinition (**"Blinded independent expert-panel-driven primary endpoint redefinition, with the SAP amended before the protocol"**; closest existing entry, "Mid-trial SAP amendment changing endpoint status," describes promotion of an existing secondary endpoint rather than a panel-driven replacement of the primary endpoint's definition itself)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- CL0600-020 (pivotal): randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, 24 weeks, teduglutide 0.05 mg/kg/day (n=43) vs. placebo (n=43), 1:1 randomization stratified by baseline PN/IV fluid weekly volume (≤6 L/week vs. >6 L/week). Primary endpoint: "Binary Response," ≥20% reduction from baseline in weekly PN volume sustained from Week 20 through Week 24. Sample size of 86 gave 90% power to detect a 35% (teduglutide) vs. 6% (placebo) responder-rate difference, two-sided Fisher's Exact test at α=0.05. Result: the 0.05 mg/kg/day dose was significantly better than placebo (FDA Statistical Review, Table 13).

- CL0600-004 (supportive, dose-ranging): three arms — placebo (n=16), teduglutide 0.05 mg/kg/day (n=35), teduglutide 0.10 mg/kg/day (n=32), 1:2:2 randomization, stratified by participation in a 72-hour nutrient absorption test (yes/no) and PN consumption level (3 levels). The original primary endpoint (the same Binary Response definition later used in CL0600-020) was replaced, via an SAP amendment dated April 20, 2007 (preceding the corresponding protocol Amendment 4b, June 29, 2007), with an ordered categorical "graded response" endpoint intended to capture both the intensity and duration of PN reduction. The change followed a July 28, 2006 sponsor-convened, blinded meeting of independent "Regulatory Expert Consultants" (clinicians and statisticians) who recommended the new endpoint without access to unblinded trial data. The original Binary Response endpoint was demoted to a key secondary endpoint.

- CL0600-004 multiplicity: a pre-specified fixed-sequence (step-down) procedure tested, in order: (1) 0.10 mg/kg/day vs. placebo, (2) 0.05 mg/kg/day vs. placebo, (3) 0.05 vs. 0.10 mg/kg/day on the primary graded-response endpoint, then repeated the same sequence for each secondary endpoint. Step 1 (0.10 mg/kg/day vs. placebo) did not reach significance on the graded-response endpoint (Rank ANCOVA p=0.161), versus p=0.007 for 0.05 mg/kg/day vs. placebo — under the gatekeeping rule, this formally rendered the nominally significant 0.05 mg/kg/day result exploratory rather than confirmatory in this trial. The 0.05 mg/kg/day dose that was ultimately approved was therefore statistically supported as primary evidence only by CL0600-020, which used the simpler Binary Response endpoint and a single active dose vs. placebo (no gatekeeping problem).

- Missing data: both trials used non-responder/worst-case imputation for the primary binary or graded endpoint and no-change-from-baseline imputation for continuous secondary endpoints. In CL0600-020, an FDA-run "ultra-worst-case" sensitivity analysis that recoded placebo dropouts as responders instead of non-responders still favored teduglutide (Fisher's exact p=0.0271, exploratory).

- Analysis populations: ITT defined as all randomized subjects who received at least one dose; Per-Protocol (completers, compliant, no major deviations) used as a sensitivity population and was consistent with ITT in all cases.

- Regulatory: rolling NDA submission with the PDUFA clock starting November 30, 2011; the standard 10-month review cycle was extended to 13 months to accommodate a Gastrointestinal Drugs Advisory Committee meeting on October 16, 2012, at which the committee concurred that the Binary Response primary endpoint was clinically meaningful.

### 3. Vedolizumab (Entyvio) — BLA 125476

**Sponsor:** Takeda Pharmaceuticals U.S.A., Inc.

**Indication approved:** Moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis and moderately to severely active Crohn's disease in adults with inadequate response, loss of response, or intolerance to a TNF blocker or immunomodulator, or inadequate response with, intolerance of, or demonstrated dependence on corticosteroids

**Approval date:** May 20, 2014

**Pivotal trial:** GEMINI I, Study C13006, NCT00783718 (ulcerative colitis, co-pivotal); GEMINI II, Study C13007, NCT00783692 (Crohn's disease, co-pivotal); supportive GEMINI III, Study C13011, NCT01224171 (Crohn's disease, induction-only)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multinational trials combining an induction phase and a maintenance phase within one protocol; induction-responder re-randomization design in which patients who achieve clinical response to induction (whether from blinded randomized or open-label induction) are freshly re-randomized into two or more maintenance dosing arms plus placebo, with the maintenance phase's sample size, endpoints, and multiplicity structure powered and analyzed independently of the induction phase (**"Induction-responder re-randomization design (into multiple maintenance-dose arms)"**; distinct from the existing "Randomized-withdrawal enrichment design" entry, which is a simpler two-arm continue-vs.-switch-to-placebo structure)

- *Endpoints:* clinical response at Week 6 (primary, induction); clinical remission at Week 52 (primary, maintenance); in GEMINI II, "enhanced clinical remission" was elevated mid-trial from a secondary endpoint to a co-primary endpoint alongside clinical response

- *Primary analysis:* prespecified pairwise comparisons of each maintenance dose (Q4W, Q8W) vs. placebo on the primary and secondary endpoints

- *Multiplicity:* gate-keeping procedure using the Hochberg method for the multiple maintenance-dose comparisons, which FDA's statistical reviewer judged methodologically inadequate because the Hochberg method's non-separable property may not properly preserve the study-wise Type I error rate — though the finding was rendered moot in GEMINI I because all comparisons of the primary and secondary endpoints were independently significant, and largely moot in GEMINI II because the pattern of significant/non-significant results made the multiplicity concern immaterial

- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation for patients who withdrew prematurely during both induction and maintenance; FDA noted the missing-data rate in the placebo arm was nearly double that of the vedolizumab arm during maintenance in GEMINI I, a possible source of bias judged "defendable" given trial length; in GEMINI II, a post hoc data-integrity review found 107 patients' Week-6 response status had been miscategorized relative to the sponsor's own IVRS/CDAI-based recalculation, prompting sensitivity re-analyses that did not change the conclusions

- *Regulatory:* joint Gastrointestinal Drugs Advisory Committee/Drug Safety and Risk Management Advisory Committee meeting, December 9, 2013, to assess PML/REMS risk by analogy to natalizumab; Entyvio was approved without a REMS

**Trial design & endpoints**

- GEMINI I (ulcerative colitis, C13006, NCT00783718): a Phase 3, multinational, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial combining a 6-week blinded Induction Phase and a 46-week Maintenance Phase within one protocol. Induction enrolled two sequential cohorts: Cohort 1 was randomized (blinded) to vedolizumab 300 mg IV at Weeks 0 and 2, or placebo, and served as the primary efficacy population for induction; Cohort 2 received open-label vedolizumab induction to supply additional Week-6 responders for the Maintenance Phase. Primary induction endpoint: clinical response at Week 6; secondary (sequentially tested): clinical remission and mucosal healing, both at Week 6. Patients achieving clinical response to induction — pooled across Cohort 1 and open-label Cohort 2 — were re-randomized for the Maintenance Phase (Week 6 to Week 52) to vedolizumab 300 mg every 4 weeks (Q4W), every 8 weeks (Q8W), or placebo. Primary maintenance endpoint: clinical remission at Week 52; secondary (sequential): durable clinical response, mucosal healing, durable clinical remission, and corticosteroid-free remission, all at Week 52. Planned induction sample size across both cohorts was 1059, with 370 in Cohort 1; the Maintenance Phase required 501 induction responders across both cohorts to adequately power its endpoints.

- GEMINI II (Crohn's disease, C13007, NCT00783692): the same overall two-cohort induction plus re-randomized maintenance structure as GEMINI I. During the trial, the sponsor amended the protocol to redesignate "enhanced clinical remission" — originally a secondary endpoint — as a co-primary endpoint alongside clinical response at Week 6, proposing the Hochberg method to adjust for the two primary comparisons; in the same amendment the CDAI eligibility upper limit was lowered from 480 to 450. The sponsor stated both changes were made using blinded demographic data from only the first 50 accrued patients. The trial met its original primary endpoint (clinical response at Week 6, statistically significant vs. placebo) but did not reach significance on the newly designated co-primary endpoint (enhanced clinical remission) or the CRP secondary endpoint at Week 6. Maintenance primary endpoint: clinical remission at Week 52 (met); secondary endpoints tested in fixed sequence with Hochberg gate-keeping across dose arms — enhanced clinical response and corticosteroid-free remission were also met, but durable clinical remission (last in the sequence) was not.

- GEMINI III (Crohn's disease, C13011, NCT01224171): a supportive, induction-only trial enriched for prior TNF-antagonist failure (approximately 75% of enrolled patients). Its primary comparison did not reach statistical significance, meaning all other pre-specified comparisons in the trial could only be viewed as exploratory; GEMINI III did not independently support the Crohn's disease approval and functioned as supportive context alongside GEMINI II.

- Multiplicity: in both GEMINI I and GEMINI II, FDA's statistical reviewer explicitly found the sponsor's Hochberg-based gate-keeping procedure across multiple dose comparisons methodologically inadequate in principle (non-separable, may not preserve the study-wise Type I error rate), but concluded in each case that the inadequacy was "no longer a concern" because the actual pattern of significant and non-significant results across endpoints made the multiplicity flaw immaterial to the conclusions reached.

- A post hoc data-integrity finding in GEMINI II: 107 patients' Week-6 clinical-response status, as recorded by investigators, differed from the sponsor's own recalculation using IVRS/CDAI subscore data; 51 of these patients had been re-randomized into the Maintenance ITT population. Sensitivity analyses including and excluding these patients gave consistent results (treatment differences of approximately 17.7% and 16.6% for the Q8W and Q4W arms respectively, both p<0.01).

- A joint meeting of the Gastrointestinal Drugs Advisory Committee and the Drug Safety and Risk Management Advisory Committee was held December 9, 2013, focused on whether vedolizumab — an anti-integrin biologic in the same class as natalizumab (Tysabri), which carries a REMS for progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) risk — needed a comparable REMS. The committee voted that vedolizumab's risk/benefit assessment was favorable, and FDA ultimately concluded a REMS was not warranted, reasoning that vedolizumab's gut-selective α4β7 mechanism differs meaningfully from natalizumab's CNS-penetrant α4β1/α4β7 mechanism; Entyvio was approved without a REMS.

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, BLA 125476, Reference ID 3509148, p.2 (UC) and p.5 (CD, same wording repeated)]* "The sponsor's gate-keeping testing procedure with the Hochberg method for the multiple dose comparisons was inadequate because of the non-separable property of the Hochberg method, i.e., it may not properly preserve the study-wise type I error rate. However, all the comparisons of the primary and secondary efficacy endpoints have shown statistical significance and it is no longer a concern."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, BLA 125476, Reference ID 3509148, p.4]*, on GEMINI II's result: "The study results demonstrated statistically significant treatment benefit of vedolizumab compared with placebo in the original primary endpoint of clinical response at Week 6 and failed to show statistical significance on both the other primary endpoint of enhanced clinical remission and the secondary efficacy endpoint of CRP at Week 6. The study should be considered successful per the final protocol specifications."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, BLA 125476, Reference ID 3509148, p.4]*, repeating the same multiplicity critique for GEMINI II's co-primary structure: "The sponsor's gate-keeping testing procedure with the Hochberg method for the multiple primary comparisons was inadequate as it may not properly preserve the study-wise type I error rate. Although only one of the comparisons of the primary efficacy endpoints showed statistical significance, the secondary efficacy endpoint failed to show statistical significance even with a nominal p-value; and so the inadequacy of the pre-specified multiplicity adjustment method is no longer a concern."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, BLA 125476, Reference ID 3509148, p.3]*, on GEMINI III: "Study C13011 failed to demonstrate statistically significant treatment difference for the primary comparison and so all the other comparisons pre-specified in the protocol can only be viewed as exploratory."

- **Reverse-engineered SAP** (for details beyond what the excerpted Statistical Review text resolves): *[inferred]* the exact planned sample size for GEMINI II's maintenance phase beyond the reviewer's cited Table 38 total (N=396) is traceable to that table but was not independently re-derived here; *[inferred]* the choice to pool induction responders from both the blinded Cohort 1 and open-label Cohort 2 before maintenance re-randomization is traceable to the reviewer's description of the Maintenance Phase's 501-patient target spanning both cohorts, implying the design intentionally used open-label induction as a recruitment mechanism for the blinded maintenance comparison rather than as an incidental afterthought.

### 4. Naloxegol (Movantik) — NDA 204760

**Sponsor:** AstraZeneca Pharmaceuticals LP (compound originated at Nektar Therapeutics as NKTR-118, licensed to AstraZeneca)

**Indication approved:** Opioid-induced constipation (OIC) in adult patients with chronic non-cancer pain

**Approval date:** September 16, 2014

**Pivotal trial:** Study D3820C00004, NCT01309841 (publicly known as KODIAC-04); Study D3820C00005, NCT01323790 (KODIAC-05); supportive long-term safety Study D3820C00008, NCT01336205 (KODIAC-08)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trials, up to 18 weeks total duration (2-week OIC-confirmation period, 12-week double-blind treatment, 2-week follow-up), stratified by baseline laxative-response category

- *Endpoints:* weekly responder status during Weeks 1-12 (≥3 spontaneous bowel movements/week and ≥1 SBM/week increase over baseline, sustained ≥9 of 12 weeks and ≥3 of the last 4 weeks)

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by baseline laxative-response category (laxative-inadequate, laxative-adequate, laxative-unknown responder), applied separately for each active dose vs. placebo

- *Multiplicity:* Bonferroni-based recycling multiplicity framework (Burman-Sonesson-Guilbaud) — Bonferroni-Holm allocation of alpha across the two dose-vs-placebo group comparisons, with fixed-sequence testing of the primary and three key secondary endpoints within each group, and alpha "recycled" from a fully-successful group comparison to the other group (already an existing Keyword_Taxonomy.md term, previously seen only in brodalumab/Siliq; naloxegol is a second example)

- *Missing data/bias:* per the SAP, weeks with fewer than 4 days of recorded eDiary data were set to missing rather than numerically imputed; FDA's information request confirmed these missing weeks were analyzed as non-response (treatment failure) for the primary endpoint; an FDA-identified data-integrity issue (patients inadvertently randomized more than once across centers) required re-analysis on FDA-defined broader populations (Full Analysis Set and All-Randomized) as a robustness check

- *Regulatory:* Anesthesia and Analgesia Drug Products Advisory Committee met June 11-12, 2014; the 12.5 mg dose was not shown superior to placebo in one of the two pivotal trials, so substantial evidence of efficacy for that dose was not demonstrated on its own

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Two identically designed Phase 3, multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trials. Study D3820C00004 (NCT01309841, "KODIAC-04" in AstraZeneca's public naming, though the FDA Statistical Review refers to it only by protocol number) enrolled 652 randomized patients (641 ITT) across 98 centers in the US, Australia, Germany, and Slovakia. Study D3820C00005 (NCT01323790, "KODIAC-05") enrolled 700 randomized patients (696 ITT) across 117 centers in the US, Belgium, Croatia, Czech Republic, Hungary, Spain, Sweden, and the UK. Both trials randomized patients 1:1:1 to placebo, naloxegol 12.5 mg, or naloxegol 25 mg once daily, centrally allocated via IVRS and stratified by baseline laxative response (laxative-inadequate responder [LIR], laxative-adequate responder [LAR], laxative-unknown responder [LUR]), with a minimum 50% of patients required to fall in the LIR stratum.

- Primary endpoint (identical in both trials): weekly responder status during Weeks 1-12, defined as ≥3 spontaneous bowel movements (SBMs, meaning without rescue-laxative use in the prior 24 hours) per week and an increase of ≥1 SBM/week over baseline, sustained for at least 9 of the 12 treatment weeks and at least 3 of the last 4 weeks. Three key secondary endpoints, included in the same multiplicity adjustment and tested in fixed order within each dose-vs-placebo comparison: (1) response rate in the LIR subgroup during Weeks 1-12 (chi-square test); (2) time to first post-dose laxation without rescue-laxative use (log-rank test stratified by baseline laxative-response category); (3) mean number of days/week with ≥1 SBM over the 12-week period (mixed model for repeated measures, MMRM).

- Primary analysis: two-sided Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by baseline laxative-response category, run separately for 12.5 mg-vs-placebo and 25 mg-vs-placebo, on the ITT population as primary and mITT/Per-Protocol as sensitivity analyses.

- Multiplicity: a Bonferroni-Holm allocation of alpha across the two dose-group comparisons combined with fixed-sequence testing within each group, following the recycling framework of Bretz, Maurer, Brannath, and Posch (2009) and Burman, Sonesson, and Guilbaud (2009) — the same "Bonferroni-based recycling multiplicity framework (Burman-Sonesson-Guilbaud)" already in Keyword_Taxonomy.md. Sample size: 105 patients/group were needed for 90% power at two-sided α=0.025 to detect a 25-percentage-point response-rate difference (60% naloxegol vs. 35% placebo), inflated to 210/group (630 total) to also power the LIR-subgroup secondary endpoint.

- Missing data: per the SAP, missing eDiary entries were not numerically imputed; if fewer than 4 days of data were recorded in a given week, that week's rate was set to missing. Following an FDA information request (December 20, 2013), the sponsor confirmed that a missing week was analyzed as non-response (treatment failure) for the primary endpoint.

- Data-integrity finding: FDA identified that some subjects had been inadvertently randomized more than once across different centers and excluded from the sponsor's ITT/mITT populations; FDA required re-analysis on two FDA-defined broader populations — a "Full Analysis Set" (all randomized patients dosed at least once, including duplicate randomizations) and an "All-Randomized" population — as well as validation of the MMRM secondary-endpoint result with a non-parametric fallback (blocked two-sample Wilcoxon rank-sum test stratified by pooled centers).

- Results: both trials met the primary endpoint at the 25 mg dose (D3820C00004: 44.4% vs. 29.4% placebo; D3820C00005: 39.7% vs. 29.3% placebo, both significant by CMH test). The 12.5 mg dose was not shown superior to placebo in one of the two studies, so FDA concluded substantial evidence of efficacy for that dose alone was not demonstrated — reflected in the label's designation of 25 mg as the recommended starting dose, with 12.5 mg reserved for patients with reduced tolerability (e.g., moderate renal impairment).

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 204760, Reference ID 3528359, §3.1.1.2]* "The applicant indicated that in order to control the overall type I error rate to be less than 0.05 for the multiple comparisons in the primary and the key secondary endpoints, a MTP with Bonferroni-Holm over groups, and fixed-sequence within groups was applied. Specifically, there were two group comparisons defined by the NKTR-118 doses of 12.5 mg versus placebo and 25 mg versus placebo. Within each group comparison, there was a pre-defined fixed-sequence MTP of comparisons of the primary and key secondary endpoints vs. placebo... at level of α/2. If the null hypotheses for one group comparison was rejected entirely (i.e., significant difference between active vs. placebo for all 4 endpoints at α = 0.025), the level was increased to α (i.e., 0.05) for the other group comparison. This amounted to using Bonferroni-Holm over groups, and fixed-sequence within groups. This multiplicity adjustment method followed the general results described by Bretz et al. and Burman et al."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 204760, Reference ID 3528359, §3.1.1.2]* "In the statistical analysis plan (SAP), the applicant indicated missing data entries in the eDiary would not be imputed... If fewer than 4 days of data are recorded within a particular week, the data for that week will be considered insufficient and the rate will be set to missing for that week. In the Agency IR letter, the applicant was asked to clarify if the missing rate for that week was to be analyzed as a non-response (treatment failure). The applicant indicated that it would be analyzed as a non-response."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 204760, Reference ID 3528359]* "Since Movantik 12.5 mg was not shown to be superior to placebo in one study, substantial evidence of efficacy for that dose was not demonstrated."

- **Reverse-engineered SAP** (for details beyond the excerpted text): *[inferred]* the specific center flagged by FDA's independent robustness check (center 5267, per research notes) as a candidate outsized driver of the Study D3820C00004 treatment effect is traceable to the Statistical Review's center-level sensitivity analysis, which concluded no single center dominated the result.

### 5. Eluxadoline (Viberzi) — NDA 206940

**Sponsor:** Furiex Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (acquired by Forest Laboratories in 2014; Forest subsequently merged into Actavis, renamed Allergan in 2015, which launched Viberzi commercially — corporate lineage noted for context, not independently re-verified against a primary source)

**Indication approved:** Abdominal pain and diarrhea in adult patients with diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-d)

**Approval date:** May 27, 2015

**Pivotal trial:** IBS-3001, NCT01553591; IBS-3002, NCT01553747 (two identically designed, co-pivotal trials)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trials; dose-ranging Phase 2 trial (IBS-2001) using a Bristol Stool Scale-only responder definition later replaced by a composite endpoint for Phase 3

- *Endpoints:* composite responder over Weeks 1-12, requiring a daily pain response (≥30% improvement in worst abdominal pain vs. baseline) and a daily stool-consistency response (Bristol Stool Scale <5, or no bowel movement accompanied by ≥30% pain improvement) on ≥50% of diary-entry days in the interval; dual primary-endpoint definition by regulator (US primary window Weeks 1-12; EU primary window Weeks 1-26)

- *Primary analysis:* two-sided Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test, pairwise for each active dose vs. placebo

- *Multiplicity:* Bonferroni adjustment across the two active-dose-vs-placebo comparisons to preserve the family-wise Type I error rate; the individual pain- and stool-consistency-responder component endpoints had no pre-specified multiplicity-controlling procedure and were reported descriptively rather than as confirmatory tests

- *Missing data/bias:* worst-case-scenario sensitivity analysis (missing counted as non-responder); more than 50 patients per study who failed inclusion/exclusion criteria were nonetheless randomized, prompting an FDA-requested re-analysis of the primary endpoint excluding those patients

- *Regulatory:* no advisory committee meeting identified for the original approval; the drug was subject to a DEA Controlled Substances Act scheduling analysis prior to marketing; a 2017 post-marketing safety signal (pancreatitis/sphincter of Oddi spasm in patients without a gallbladder) led to a later label contraindication

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Two identically designed, Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trials: IBS-3001 (NCT01553591, N=1282 randomized to eluxadoline 75 mg BID, 100 mg BID, or placebo) and IBS-3002 (NCT01553747, N=1146 randomized, same three arms). Both trials enrolled adults with IBS-d meeting Rome III criteria.

- Primary endpoint (US approval basis): proportion of "composite responders" over Weeks 1-12, where a daily composite response required both a daily pain response (worst abdominal pain in the past 24 hours improved ≥30% versus baseline) and a daily stool-consistency response (Bristol Stool Scale score <5, or no bowel movement accompanied by ≥30% pain improvement), with response required on at least 50% of diary-entry days within the interval. The EU regulatory submission used an analogous definition over Weeks 1-26 instead of Weeks 1-12 — a dual primary-endpoint definition set by regulator, the same concept already documented in this census for CLL14.

- Primary analysis: a two-sided Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test for each active dose vs. placebo, on the ITT analysis set (all randomized patients); a modified ITT set (dosed, with baseline and at least one post-randomization diary entry) was used for durability/4-week-interval analyses. Because two active doses were each compared to placebo, a Bonferroni adjustment was applied across the two comparisons to preserve the family-wise Type I error rate.

- Secondary endpoints — the individual pain-responder and stool-consistency-responder components of the composite — had no pre-specified multiplicity-controlling procedure; FDA's reviewer noted explicitly that "formal testing for statistical significance is not appropriate" for these and that results should be presented "in descriptive fashion only." Both doses were statistically significant vs. placebo on the composite primary endpoint in both trials; of the two individual components, the stool-consistency response was significant at both doses in both studies, but the abdominal-pain response alone was not statistically significant at either dose in either study — the composite endpoint succeeded despite its pain component failing on its own.

- FDA's reviewer independently ran a mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) analysis directly on daily pain scores as an exploratory sensitivity check and concluded both doses appeared to show a treatment benefit on pain, despite the formal pain-responder endpoint's non-significant result.

- Missing data: a worst-case-scenario sensitivity analysis (missing data counted as non-response) was run by the sponsor; FDA's reviewer noted that for the 75 mg dose at Weeks 1-26, the worst-case analysis actually produced a larger treatment effect and smaller p-value than the primary analysis — i.e., the missing-data handling was not conservative in the direction typically expected.

- A protocol-deviation issue arose in both studies: more than 50 patients per study who failed inclusion/exclusion criteria were nonetheless randomized, and no per-protocol analysis had originally been submitted; FDA required the sponsor to re-run the primary-endpoint analysis excluding these patients as a sensitivity check.

- FDA's overall statistical conclusion: "Data from both Studies 3001 and 3002 support the efficacy of 75 mg and 100 mg of eluxadoline as a treatment for adult patients with diarrhea predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-d)." A March 2017 post-marketing safety signal for pancreatitis (associated with sphincter of Oddi spasm) in patients without a gallbladder subsequently led to a label update contraindicating use in that population.

### 6. Obeticholic acid (Ocaliva) — NDA 207999

**Sponsor:** Intercept Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Primary biliary cholangitis (PBC), in combination with ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) in adults with an inadequate response to UDCA, or as monotherapy in adults unable to tolerate UDCA — approved under accelerated approval (21 CFR 314.510 / FD&C Act §506(c)(1))

**Approval date:** May 27, 2016 (NDA voluntarily withdrawn effective November 24, 2025, under 21 CFR 314.150(d), after the confirmatory trial failed to verify clinical benefit — see Regulatory below)

**Pivotal trial:** POISE, Study 747-301, NCT01473524 (accelerated-approval basis); confirmatory outcomes trial COBALT, Study 747-302, NCT02308111 (post-marketing requirement, statistically null, terminated early)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group accelerated-approval trial on a surrogate biomarker endpoint, with a pre-negotiated post-marketing confirmatory outcomes trial required under 21 CFR 314.510; accelerated-approval confirmatory trial statistically null, followed by negotiated/voluntary NDA withdrawal (**"Accelerated-approval confirmatory trial statistically null, followed by negotiated/voluntary NDA withdrawal"**; distinct from an ordinary Complete Response Letter, which occurs pre-approval, and from ordinary accelerated-to-traditional-approval conversion); FDA-requested withdrawal under 21 CFR 314.150(d) accepted by the sponsor without a contested hearing (**"FDA-requested withdrawal under 21 CFR 314.150(d) accepted by sponsor without contested hearing"**; for the specific mechanism used here, distinguishing it from an involuntary/contested withdrawal proceeding under §506(c)(3)(B))

- *Endpoints:* composite surrogate biochemical responder endpoint at Month 12 (alkaline phosphatase <1.67×ULN, total bilirubin ≤1.0×ULN, and ALP reduction from baseline ≥15%) for accelerated approval (POISE); composite clinical outcomes endpoint (time to death, liver transplant, MELD score ≥15, uncontrolled ascites, or hospitalization for variceal bleeding/hepatic encephalopathy/spontaneous bacterial peritonitis) for the confirmatory trial (COBALT), which returned a null result

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test adjusted for randomization strata, with a Breslow-Day test for homogeneity of treatment effect across strata (POISE)

- *Multiplicity:* a step-down/closed sequential testing procedure narrowly scoped to the two OCA-dose-vs-placebo comparisons on the primary surrogate endpoint alone (10 mg tested first; the OCA-Titration arm tested only if the 10 mg comparison was significant)

- *Missing data/bias:* non-responder imputation (NRI) for missing values at the Month 12 assessment window; FDA's independent statistician was deliberately blinded to POISE trial data while separately analyzing the Global PBC Study registry to assess whether 12-month ALP reduction predicts clinical outcome in a population matched to POISE's enrollees

- *Regulatory:* Gastrointestinal Drugs Advisory Committee (GIDAC) met September 13, 2024, to assess whether COBALT and a supporting observational study (Study 405) verified clinical benefit; voted 1-13-0 that the evidence did not verify clinical benefit and 1-10-3 that the benefit-risk profile was unfavorable; NDA and three referencing ANDAs voluntarily withdrawn effective November 24, 2025

**Trial design & endpoints**

- POISE (Study 747-301, NCT01473524): a Phase 3, 12-month, multinational, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial with a target enrollment of 180 (60/arm); 217 patients were actually randomized (216 dosed), 1:1:1 to obeticholic acid 10 mg, an OCA-Titration arm (5 mg titrated to 10 mg), or placebo, stratified by pre-treatment liver-biochemistry severity (ALP >3.0×ULN and/or AST >2.0×ULN and/or total bilirubin >ULN, yes/no) and UDCA intolerance (yes/no). Primary endpoint: a composite responder definition at Month 12 requiring ALP <1.67×ULN, total bilirubin ≤1.0×ULN, and an ALP reduction from baseline of at least 15%, with non-responder imputation for missing values. Primary analysis used a CMH test adjusted for the randomization strata, plus a Breslow-Day test for homogeneity of the treatment effect across strata. Results: 10 mg OCA 46.6% responders vs. 9.6% placebo (CMH p<0.0001); OCA-Titration 45.7% vs. 9.6% placebo (CMH p<0.0001); Breslow-Day tests were non-significant (p=0.9072 and 0.5045 respectively), indicating homogeneity across strata.

- FDA's original (2016) Statistical Review explicitly flagged the central tension in the submission: the population enrolled in POISE was not well matched to the broader-spectrum PBC population studied by the Global PBC Group, whose registry data had been used to develop the primary composite endpoint as a claimed surrogate for clinical outcome — rendering "questionable" the endpoint's overall adequacy as a basis for accelerated approval on its own. To address this, an FDA statistician was deliberately kept blinded to POISE's own trial data and instead independently analyzed the Global PBC Study's subject-level registry data, matched to a clinically meaningful subset resembling POISE's actual enrollees, and confirmed that a 12-month ALP reduction was a reasonably predictive marker in that matched population — supporting (but not proving) the surrogate's validity for this population.

- Multiplicity: a step-down/closed testing procedure was pre-specified, but narrowly scoped only to the comparison of the two OCA dose groups against placebo on the primary endpoint — starting with 10 mg vs. placebo, proceeding to OCA-Titration vs. placebo only if the first comparison was significant.

- As a condition of accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.510, Intercept was required to have an ongoing confirmatory outcomes trial: COBALT (Study 747-302, NCT02308111), whose protocol and SAP were first submitted to FDA (under IND 63,307) on October 9, 2014 — before accelerated approval was granted in 2016. COBALT enrolled 334 patients (of a target of approximately 127 primary-endpoint events over up to 7 years of follow-up) and was randomized, quadruple-masked, and placebo-controlled. The trial was terminated early: per its ClinicalTrials.gov record, the Data Monitoring Committee recommended against further enrollment "given the lack of feasibility for this post-marketing study as designed." Despite early termination, results were posted. Primary composite clinical-outcomes endpoint (time to death, liver transplant, MELD score ≥15, uncontrolled ascites, or hospitalization for variceal bleeding/hepatic encephalopathy/spontaneous bacterial peritonitis): log-rank hazard ratio 1.01 (95% CI 0.68-1.51), p=0.954 — a fully null result, numerically slightly unfavorable to OCA. A secondary "Expanded Endpoint" likewise did not favor OCA (71 events on OCA vs. 80 on placebo).

- Post-approval regulatory arc: a 2021 safety labeling change narrowed the indication to PBC patients without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis without portal hypertension. FDA convened the Gastrointestinal Drugs Advisory Committee (GIDAC) on September 13, 2024, to review sNDA 207999 S-011, Intercept's attempt to convert the accelerated approval to full/traditional approval using COBALT plus the observational Study 405. On Voting Question 3 ("Does the available evidence verify the benefit of OCA on clinical outcomes... in the USPI-labeled population?"), the committee voted 1 Yes, 13 No, 0 Abstain; on Voting Question 4 ("Is the benefit-risk profile of OCA favorable... ?"), the committee voted 1 Yes, 10 No, 3 Abstain. Members who voted "No" on benefit cited COBALT's failure to meet its primary endpoint and the trial's crossover complications after OCA's commercial availability; members who voted "No" on benefit-risk also cited an imbalance of liver transplants and deaths favoring placebo over OCA. In August 2025, FDA notified Intercept that the postmarketing trial "did not verify clinical benefit" and that early-stage-disease patients on OCA in that trial had an excess of liver transplants and deaths, recommending withdrawal under 21 CFR 314.150(d) and requesting that Intercept waive the expedited-withdrawal hearing procedures of §506(c)(3)(B). Intercept submitted a withdrawal request on September 10, 2025, "while noting disagreement with the Agency's assessment," and three ANDA holders referencing the NDA (Apotex, Lupin, MSN) followed with their own voluntary-withdrawal requests. NDA 207999 and the three ANDAs were formally withdrawn effective November 24, 2025 (Federal Register, docket FDA-2025-N-5935).

### 7. Plecanatide (Trulance) — NDA 208745

**Sponsor:** Synergy Pharmaceuticals Inc. (later acquired by Bausch Health, 2019)

**Indication approved:** Chronic idiopathic constipation (CIC) in adults

**Approval date:** January 19, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** Study SPD304203-00 ("Trial 1"), NCT01982240, and Study SPD304203-03 ("Trial 2"), NCT02122471

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, three-arm dose-comparison (3 mg / 6 mg plecanatide / placebo)
- *Endpoints:* Durable diary-based bowel-movement responder rate, change in CSBM/SBM frequency, stool consistency (Bristol Stool Form Scale), straining score, treatment satisfaction
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by gender
- *Multiplicity:* Holm-based tree-gatekeeping procedure spanning two dose arms and multiple endpoint families
- *Missing data/bias:* Mean replacement approach (MRA) for partial-week diary imputation; non-responder/missing-week handling for weeks with <4 diary days; sensitivity analyses via Multiple Imputation, Observed Cases, and LOCF

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Two identical Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, 12-week trials in men and women 18-80 years old with CIC (modified Rome III criteria), excluding structural/post-surgical GI disease, IBS, or other chronic disease that could cause constipation.

- After a 2-week Pre-Treatment electronic-diary screening period (patients had to have <3 CSBMs, ≤2 days of rescue-medication use, and ≥6 of 7 diary entries per week in both pre-treatment weeks), eligible patients were stratified by gender and randomized 1:1:1 to plecanatide 3 mg, plecanatide 6 mg, or placebo, once daily for 12 weeks, with clinic visits at Weeks 4, 8, and 12.

- Primary endpoint: durable overall CSBM (complete spontaneous bowel movement) responder rate — a "weekly CSBM responder" was a patient with ≥1 CSBM in a given week; an "overall CSBM responder" was a weekly responder in ≥9 of the 12 treatment weeks; a "durable overall CSBM responder" additionally had to be a weekly responder in ≥3 of the last 4 weeks.

- Secondary endpoints: change from baseline in CSBM and SBM frequency rate, stool consistency (BSFS), straining score, treatment satisfaction, and Daily Symptom Diary abdominal-symptom scores.

- Sample size: powered from a prior dose-ranging study's response-rate assumptions (16.9% for each plecanatide dose arm vs. 9.4% for placebo), using a chi-square continuity-corrected test targeting ~90% power at a two-sided 5% significance level; enrollment of ≥450 patients per treatment arm was planned.

- Analysis populations: efficacy analyses were based on the Intent-to-Treat (ITT) population, with the Per-Protocol (PP) population used as a sensitivity analysis.

- Missing data: for the responder analysis, weeks with <4 complete diary days were treated as non-responder weeks; weeks with 4-6 (of 7) diary days present used a mean replacement approach (MRA), recalculating the weekly CSBM/SBM rate as 7×(observed CSBMs/SBMs)/(days reported). Patients with zero diary days in a week were left missing (not imputed) in the linear mixed model/ANCOVA used for continuous secondary endpoints, under a missing-at-random (MAR) assumption. Sensitivity analyses re-ran the primary and weekly responder analyses under Multiple Imputation, Observed-Cases, and Last-Observation-Carried-Forward (LOCF) methods.

- Multiplicity: family-wise Type I error was controlled separately within each of two hypothesis families (3 mg vs. placebo; 6 mg vs. placebo) using a Holm-based tree-gatekeeping procedure across seven hierarchical steps — beginning with the 6 mg primary endpoint, then the 3 mg primary endpoint bundled with two 6 mg secondary endpoints (Holm-adjusted within-step), cascading through further secondary-endpoint bundles for each dose, with progression to a later step contingent on all hypotheses in the prior step being rejected.

**Documents**

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 208745, §3.1.3 "Primary and Secondary Endpoints," p.7]*

> "The primary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of patients who were durable overall CSBM responders over the 12-week Treatment Period. A CSBM weekly responder was defined as a patient who had ≥ 1 CSBM for that same week. An overall CSBM responder was defined as a patient who was a weekly responder for at least 9 of the 12 treatment weeks, and a durable overall CSBM responder was also a weekly responder in at least 3 of the last 4 weeks."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 208745, §3.2.1 "Determination of Sample Size," p.8-9]*

> "The power calculation assumes that the 6 mg plecanatide overall responder rate was the same as seen in the 3 mg plecanatide dose group; 16.9% response rate for each plecanatide arm and 9.4% for placebo. Using these assumptions, and based on a chi-square continuity-corrected test with the intention of providing approximately 90% power at 5% significance level, enrollment of at least 450 patients per treatment arm was required... The primary efficacy endpoint was based on an analysis of the durable overall CSBM responder rates using a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by gender."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 208745, §3.2.2 "Controlling for Multiplicity of Endpoints," p.9-10]*

> "Control of family-wise type I error was applied to two sets of hypotheses—one for testing plecanatide 3.0 mg versus placebo and the other for testing plecanatide 6.0 mg versus placebo. The Holm-based tree-gatekeeping procedure was applied to p-values adjustment to control the family-wise Type I error rate at 5% (2-sided) by taking into account multiple doses and multiple primary and secondary endpoints... Following this multiple comparison procedure, progression to the next step(s) only occurred if all individual hypotheses within a step were rejected and the previous step(s) were all rejected at the step-specific overall significant level."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 208745, §3.1.5 "Imputing Missing Values and Early Terminations," p.7-8]*

> "The primary method for imputation of missing diary data was the mean replacement approach (MRA). For the responder analyses, patients who had fewer than four complete diary days were considered 'non-responders' for that week... Sensitivity analyses based on alternative missing diary data imputation methods (such as the Multiple Imputation [MI], Observed Cases [OC], and Last Observation Carried Forward [LOCF] methodologies) were performed on the primary endpoint and the CSBM weekly responder rates by week over the 12-week Treatment period."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 208745, §1 "Executive Summary," p.3]*

> "The sponsor has submitted the results of two identical, Phase 3, multicenter, randomized double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group studies (Study SPD304203-00 and Study SPD304203-03) to support the efficacy of Truelance® (Plecanatide) for the indication of Chronic Idiopathic Constipation (CIC)... After thorough evaluation and clarifications with the sponsor, the statistical review team concluded that results of the submitted two studies are statistically significance and can be used to support Plecanatide's efficacy for the indication of Chronic Idiopathic Constipation (CIC) in adults."

### 8. Naldemedine (Symproic) — NDA 208854

**Sponsor:** Shionogi Inc.

**Indication approved:** Opioid-induced constipation (OIC) in adults with chronic non-cancer pain

**Approval date:** March 23, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** COMPOSE-1 (Study 1314V9231), NCT01965158, and COMPOSE-2 (Study 1315V9232), NCT01993940; long-term safety supported by COMPOSE-3 (Study 1326V9235), NCT01965652

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group (identical designs, COMPOSE-1 and COMPOSE-2); randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 52-week long-term safety companion trial (COMPOSE-3)
- *Endpoints:* Durable diary-based bowel-movement responder rate, change in SBM/CSBM frequency, MACE (major adverse cardiovascular events) as a dedicated safety endpoint
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test adjusted by opioid-dose strata; Clopper-Pearson confidence intervals; Koch et al. (1990) estimator for the stratified risk difference; ANCOVA for key secondary continuous endpoints
- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing (primary endpoint, then 4 key secondary endpoints, in predefined order)
- *Missing data/bias:* Non-responder imputation for missing binary/diary efficacy data (Worst Case and Modified Worst Case sensitivity variants)
- *Regulatory:* Class-wide post-marketing MACE surveillance carried across sequentially approved drugs in the same pharmacologic class (PAMORA)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- COMPOSE-1 (68 sites, 7 countries) and COMPOSE-2 (69 sites, 6 countries) were identical Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trials in adults 18-80 with chronic non-cancer pain and OIC on a stable opioid regimen (≥30 mg oral morphine-equivalent/day for ≥1 month), without concomitant laxative treatment, structured as a 2-4 week Screening Period, 12-week double-blind Treatment Period, and 4-week Follow-up Period.

- Eligibility required, via a 14-day electronic Bowel Movement and Constipation Assessment diary: ≤4 total SBMs (and ≤3 in any week) over the 14-day qualifying period, ≥1 of 4 bowel symptoms in >25% of bowel movements, and ≥78% diary compliance.

- Randomization: 1:1 to naldemedine 0.2 mg or placebo once daily, stratified by average total daily opioid dose (30-100 mg vs. >100 mg oral morphine-equivalent).

- Primary endpoint: proportion of SBM responders — a "positive-response week" required ≥3 SBMs and an increase of ≥1 SBM from baseline; a responder had a positive-response week in ≥9 of 12 treatment weeks, including ≥3 of the last 4 weeks. Weeks with <4 diary days were counted as non-response weeks.

- Four pre-specified key secondary endpoints, tested in a fixed hierarchical sequence at 5% two-sided alpha: change in SBM frequency (baseline to last 2 weeks), change in SBM frequency (baseline to Week 1), change in complete SBM (CSBM) frequency (baseline to last 2 weeks), and change in SBMs-without-straining frequency (baseline to last 2 weeks) — each analyzed by ANCOVA with treatment arm and opioid-dose stratum as factors.

- Analysis population: Intention-to-Treat (ITT), defined as all randomized subjects, analyzed as randomized.

- Sensitivity analyses for missing diary data: a "Worst Case" analysis (any missing defecation-related diary entry in a week → non-response week) and a "Modified Worst Case" analysis (missing days imputed as 0 SBMs; weeks with <4 diary days → non-response week).

- COMPOSE-1: 130/273 (47.6%) responders on naldemedine vs. 94/272 (34.6%) on placebo (difference 13.0%, 95% CI 4.8-21.3; p=0.002). COMPOSE-2: 145/276 (52.5%) vs. 92/274 (33.6%) (difference 18.9%, 95% CI 10.8-27.0; p<0.0001).

- Safety/regulatory context: because a class-wide MACE (cardiovascular death, MI, stroke) safety signal had previously arisen with another PAMORA (alvimopan/Entereg), FDA required prospective, independently adjudicated MACE assessment across naldemedine's Phase 3 program (COMPOSE-1, -2, and the 52-week COMPOSE-3 safety trial); no increased MACE risk was identified (11 events among 2,328 subjects), and — consistent with the postmarketing requirement imposed on the other approved PAMORAs (Movantik, Relistor SC, Relistor oral) — a dedicated postmarketing cardiovascular-safety study was required as a condition of approval.

Based on the pre-specified primary statistical analysis, Cochran Mantel Haenszel test adjusted by the opioid dose strata, naldemedine 2mg QD demonstrated efficacy compared to placebo in both trials as measured by the primary endpoint, proportion of spontaneous bowel movement (SBM) responders."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 208854, §3.2.1.1 "Study Design and Endpoints," p.6]*

> "The Primary Efficacy Endpoint was the proportion of SBM responders. A responder was defined as a subject with a positive-response week in at least 9 out of the 12 weeks and in at least 3 of the last 4 weeks of the 12-week treatment period. A positive-response week was defined as a week with ≥3 SBMs per week and an increase from baseline ≥1 SBM per week. Any subject who had less than 4 days of diary entries (related to BMs) for a week, was treated as 'non-responder' for that week."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 208854, §3.2.1.2 "Statistical Methodologies," p.7]*

> "The primary efficacy endpoint, the proportion of SBM responders, was analyzed by the Cochran Mantel Haenszel test adjusted by the opioid dose strata for the comparison between naldemedine and placebo. The confidence intervals for proportion of responders by treatment group were calculated with the Clopper-Pearson method. Difference in the responder proportion between naldemedine and placebo was adjusted by the opioid dose strata and derived using the estimator given by Koch et al ['Categorical Data Analysis' (1990)]... The primary and the 4 key secondary endpoints were tested at 5% in a predefined hierarchical order to control the overall Type 1 error."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, NDA 208854, §"Advisory Committee Meeting" context on MACE, p.4-5 region]*

> "A class-wide safety concern of increased risk of MACE arose from safety data with another member of this class – Entereg (alvimopan)... In the naldemedine clinical trials, no increased risk of MACE was identified; however, [the required postmarketing study is] similar to the PMR that was a condition of approval for the other PAMORAs."
