### 18. Resmetirom (Rezdiffra) — NDA 217785

**Sponsor:** Madrigal Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment, in conjunction with diet and exercise, of adults with noncirrhotic nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH, now generally termed MASH) with moderate to advanced liver fibrosis (F2 or F3) — granted under accelerated approval, the first FDA approval of any drug for this indication

**Approval date:** March 14, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** MAESTRO-NASH (Study MGL-3196-11, NCT03900429), a Phase 3, multinational, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial; supportive Phase 3 safety trial MAESTRO-NAFLD-1 (Study MGL-3196-14, NCT04197479) and supportive Phase 2 trial MGL-3196-05

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized (1:1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of resmetirom 80mg vs. 100mg vs. placebo, stratified by type 2 diabetes status and baseline fibrosis stage (F1B/F2 vs. F3); approval rests on a pre-specified **Week 52 interim histology analysis** of an ongoing, longer trial whose final analysis (a clinical-outcomes composite at Month 54) will serve as the required accelerated-approval confirmatory endpoint — i.e., the same trial supplies both the surrogate basis for accelerated approval and its own eventual confirmatory verification (matching Keyword_Taxonomy.md's "Accelerated approval based on an interim analysis, confirmed by the same trial's own final analysis," previously seen only in atacicept-vymj); dual co-primary histologic endpoints, each requiring a **paired liver biopsy** (baseline and Week 52, read by two independent masked pathologists) — an unusually invasive procedural requirement for a primary efficacy endpoint, layered on a post-unblinding-finalized consensus-read adjudication process for pathologist disagreements that FDA's reviewer could not confirm was adequately prespecified (see SAP excerpts below) ("invasive paired-biopsy dual-histology surrogate endpoint with a post-hoc/near-unblinding-finalized consensus-adjudication process for reader disagreement")

- *Endpoints:* dual co-primary histologic endpoints at Week 52, each independently required to be met for its own significance claim (not a combined/either-or composite): (1) NASH resolution (ballooning score 0, inflammation score 0-1, ≥2-point NAS reduction) with no worsening of liver fibrosis; (2) ≥1-stage improvement in liver fibrosis with no worsening of NASH; each patient's biopsy outcome was scored as 1.0 (both pathologists agree responder), 0.5 (pathologists disagree), or 0 (both agree nonresponder) — a continuous/fractional responder-scoring convention not seen elsewhere in this census; key secondary endpoint was LDL-cholesterol percent change from baseline at Week 24; the ultimate confirmatory/regular-approval endpoint (assessed later, at Month 54) is a composite clinical-outcome endpoint (all-cause mortality, MELD ≥15, new/progressive varices with bleed, new ascites, hepatic encephalopathy, MELD-driven transplant listing, liver transplant)

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test and Mantel-Haenszel mean-score-statistic Wald 95% CI (per Stokes et al. 2012) for the fractional-outcome (1/0.5/0) analyses, stratified by baseline diabetes status and fibrosis stage (F2 vs. F3); a parallel binary-outcome analysis (consensus-read or individual-pathologist reads, 1/0 only) used stratified Newcombe 95% CIs instead — the SAP did not explain why different CI methods were used for the two outcome codings; a supportive GEE model (pathologist scores as repeated/correlated binary measurements) was also pre-specified

- *Multiplicity:* two-stage parallel gatekeeping structure controlling overall two-sided alpha at 0.05 — Stage 1 tested all four Week-52 histology hypotheses (2 doses × 2 co-primary endpoints) via a truncated Hochberg procedure (truncation parameter 0.9) at an allocated alpha of 0.04, with any unused Stage-1 alpha propagating to Stage 2, which tested the LDL-C key secondary endpoint (Bonferroni, both doses) at an allocated 0.01 (plus propagated alpha); the remaining alpha (0.05 plus anything propagated from the Week 52 interim) is reserved for the Month-54 composite clinical-outcome endpoint (Hochberg, both doses)

- *Missing data/bias:* participants missing a Week 52 biopsy (for any reason, including COVID-19-related study discontinuation) were counted as nonresponders in the primary analysis — the sponsor's October 2022 SAP submission had proposed *excluding* COVID-19-affected missing-biopsy participants from the analysis population entirely, which "the Agency did not agree with"; missing-data rates were higher in the resmetirom arms than placebo; sponsor-prespecified sensitivity analyses included multiple imputation (details changed across SAP addenda) and a two-dimensional-in-concept but only one-dimensional-as-executed tipping-point analysis, prompting FDA to conduct its own two-dimensional tipping-point analysis (varying responder proportions in both arms from 0-100% by 10% increments, pooling via Rubin's rule after a Wilson-Hilferty transformation of the CMH statistic)

- *Regulatory:* **reviewer-documented, unusually compressed SAP finalization directly bracketing unblinding** — SAP Version 1.0 was submitted October 20, 2022 (interim database lock November 18, 2022); pathologist "consensus read" adjudication sessions were held December 1-2 and December 5, 2022; the statistical CRO was unblinded December 2, 2022 (between the first two consensus-read sessions); SAP Version 3.0 plus a first SAP Addendum were submitted December 15, 2022 — after the Applicant itself was unblinded; a second SAP Addendum followed in September 2023, nearly a year after unblinding; FDA's reviewer stated it was "not clear whether the consensus read process was adequately prespecified" given this timeline, and separately disagreed with the Applicant's SAP-Version-3.0 algorithm for defining the F2/F3 analysis population, substituting its own "eligibility read"-based population definition for its primary analysis while also reporting the Applicant's approach for comparison; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held; accelerated approval requires MAESTRO-NASH's own Month-54 final analysis as the confirmatory endpoint (Keyword_Taxonomy.md's "Accelerated approval based on an interim analysis, confirmed by the same trial's own final analysis")

**Trial design & endpoints**

- MAESTRO-NASH enrolled 1,050 subjects (352 resmetirom 80mg, 349 100mg, 349 placebo) with biopsy-proven NASH and fibrosis stage F1B, F2, or F3; most had F2 (32%) or F3 (53%) fibrosis at baseline; randomization was stratified by type 2 diabetes status and fibrosis stage (F1/F2 vs. F3); doses were subject to a pre-specified, free-T4-triggered down-titration algorithm (a safety measure given resmetirom's thyroid-hormone-receptor mechanism), with 12 of 1,050 subjects dose-adjusted at Week 12; liver biopsies were performed at screening and Week 52 for all subjects

- FDA's own primary analysis (using "eligibility read," rather than the Applicant's SAP-Version-3.0-specified "primary read," to define the F2/F3 population) reported: NASH-resolution-without-fibrosis-worsening model-based response rates of 11% (placebo), 26% (80mg), 30% (100mg) — differences vs. placebo of 15% (95% CI 10, 21; p<0.0001) for 80mg and 19% (95% CI 13, 25; p<0.0001) for 100mg; fibrosis-improvement-without-NASH-worsening response rates of 14% (placebo), 23% (80mg), 26% (100mg) — differences of 9% (95% CI 4, 15; p=0.0009) for 80mg and 12% (95% CI 7, 18; p<0.0001) for 100mg; all four Stage-1 hypotheses were significant at p<0.037, so the full 0.04 Stage-1 alpha propagated to the LDL-C key secondary endpoint, which was also significant for both doses (p<0.02)

- FDA's reviewer explicitly declined to treat the Applicant's SAP-Version-3.0 primary-read-based analysis population definition as reliable given its concerning proximity to unblinding, instead constructing and presenting its own "eligibility read"-based population as the Agency's primary analysis, while also reporting Applicant-population results for comparison — a documented instance of FDA substituting its own analysis-population definition for the sponsor's late-finalized one, rather than merely flagging a concern

- Accelerated approval rests on the Week 52 histologic surrogate; the ongoing trial's Month-54 composite clinical-outcome endpoint (hepatic decompensation events, transplant, liver-related mortality) is the required post-marketing confirmatory endpoint, to be assessed within the same trial rather than a separate confirmatory study

- Package Insert / Label (original, 2024) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/217785s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Integrated Review (combined Summary/Clinical/Non-Clinical/Statistical/Clinical Pharmacology Review, Reference ID: 5346512) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/217785Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf

A Phase 3 Trial of Resmetirom in NASH with Liver Fibrosis. *N Engl J Med*. 2024;390(17):1632. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMc2402905), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38692302/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22A+Phase+3+Trial+of+Resmetirom+in+NASH+with+Liver+Fibrosis%22+Harrison+Taub+reply)

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review (Reference ID: 5346512), §6.2.1.3, Statistical Analysis Plan Amendments]* "There were major changes to the analysis plan for the Week 52 primary endpoints shortly before unblinding the results of the interim analyses. There were multiple correspondences between the Applicant and Agency shortly before unblinding regarding these changed analyses. These late changes were concerning as there was little to no time for FDA to review, and some changes were made after unblinding by the contract research organization."

- *[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §6.3.2, Table 23 milestone log, reviewer's summary]* "As unblinding occurred on December 2, 2022, the Agency was not able to provide feedback on the last version (3.0) of the SAP submitted on December 15, 2022. Table 23 does not include earlier versions of the SAP incorporated in meeting packages submitted to the IND, and these versions of the SAP specified a different primary analysis from the later submissions depicted in the table."

- *[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §6.3.2, on the consensus-read timeline]* "Although the Agency recommended a consensus read process during the IND development program, the Agency identified deficiencies in the consensus read performed by the Applicant during the NDA review. Table 23 presents the milestone dates relevant to the SAP and the consensus read; given the short time between the consensus reads, unblinding, and subsequent SAP addenda, it is not clear whether the consensus read process was adequately prespecified."

- *[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §6.3.2, on FDA's choice of analysis population]* "Considering these advantages and disadvantages, the Agency considers eligibility read to be the most appropriate option to define the analysis population with F2 or F3 fibrosis in Trial MGL-3196-11, and this analysis population was used in the Agency's primary analysis results."

- *[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.1.3, on Type I Error Control]* "The overall type I error rate for the study is controlled at the two-sided alpha=0.05 significance level. An alpha level of 0.04 was allocated to evaluate histological endpoints for the Week 52 interim analysis and an alpha level of 0.01 was allocated to the clinical outcome endpoint at the end of the trial, with the potential for propagation of alpha from the interim analysis to the final analysis. A two-stage parallel gatekeeping procedure was used to test the primary and the key secondary endpoints for the two dose groups at Week 52 interim analysis. In the first stage, the two dose groups of resmetirom and the two histologic surrogate endpoints (i.e., four hypotheses) were tested using the truncated Hochberg procedure with a truncation parameter of 0.9."

- *[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.1.3, on the sponsor's rejected missing-data proposal]* "The criterion excluding participants with a missing a Week 52 biopsy due to the COVID-19 pandemic was first proposed in an SAP submitted on October 20, 2022 (shortly before unblinding). The Agency did not agree with excluding such participants from the analysis and communicated this to the Applicant."

### 19. Elafibranor (Iqirvo) — NDA 218860

**Sponsor:** Ipsen Biopharmaceuticals, Inc. (elafibranor was originally developed by Genfit; Ipsen licensed global rights in 2021)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) in combination with ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) in adults with an inadequate response to UDCA, or as monotherapy in adults unable to tolerate UDCA

**Approval date:** June 10, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** ELATIVE (Study GFT505B-319-1, NCT04526665), a Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of elafibranor 80mg vs. placebo in PBC patients with inadequate UDCA response or UDCA intolerance, stratified by (1) ALP >3×ULN or total bilirubin (TB) >ULN, and (2) baseline PBC Worst Itch Numeric Rating Scale (WI-NRS) score ≥4; a 52-week common double-blind period followed by a variable-duration double-blind period (up to 104 weeks total) and an open-label long-term extension

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint biochemical response at Week 52, a three-component composite requiring ALP <1.67×ULN, TB ≤ULN, and ALP decrease ≥15% from baseline; key secondary endpoints in fixed hierarchical order: (1) ALP normalization (≤1.0×ULN) at Week 52; (2) change in PBC WI-NRS pruritus score from baseline through Week 52 (in patients with baseline WI-NRS ≥4); (3) the same pruritus endpoint through Week 24; FDA additionally explored four alternative ALP-threshold/percent-decrease combinations as robustness checks on the primary composite, all directionally consistent

- *Primary analysis:* exact Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test stratified by both randomization factors for the primary composite and ALP-normalization key secondary endpoint, on the intent-to-treat (ITT) population; the posted SAP's stated intent (an exact CMH odds ratio with exact p-value) was ambiguous relative to what the sample SAS code and study report actually produced (a standard, not exact, CMH odds ratio paired with an exact Newcombe 95% CI and exact p-value) — FDA's reviewer flagged this internal SAP-vs.-code inconsistency explicitly; response rates and risk differences (Newcombe 95% CI, CMH-weighted) were also reported alongside the OR

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (fully hierarchical) testing of the primary endpoint then the three key secondary endpoints in the pre-specified order above, each tested only if the preceding endpoint was statistically significant, to control overall two-sided alpha

- *Missing data/bias:* intercurrent events (ICE-1, study-treatment discontinuation; ICE-2, PBC rescue therapy) were handled via a composite strategy (treated as nonresponders) for the primary/key-secondary binary endpoints; subjects with Week-52 missing data but no ICE had the closest non-missing post-baseline value substituted per protocol (affecting only 2 subjects); extensive pre-specified sensitivity analyses included a monotone-regression multiple-imputation approach under missing-at-random (treating subjects as continuing their assigned treatment), a placebo-based pattern-mixture multiple imputation under missing-not-at-random, a two-parameter (δ1, δ2) tipping-point analysis on the log-odds scale, and a Bayesian sequential-regression multiple imputation the Applicant pre-specified but could not execute for lack of sufficient post-ICE observations to fit the required monotone-regression model — the Applicant's SAP mislabeled one of its own pre-specified-but-unexecuted analyses a "treatment policy strategy," which FDA's reviewer noted does not align with the ICH E9(R1) (May 2021) definition of that term, since the analysis in question still imputed rather than used observed post-ICE data (a documented SAP terminology/estimand-framework misapplication, distinct from Keyword_Taxonomy.md's existing ICH E9(R1) entry, which describes correct mixed-strategy usage rather than a mislabeling)

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held, per the Integrated Review's explicit statement that no issues warranted one; sample-size assumptions were explicitly benchmarked against the placebo/response rates observed in obeticholic acid's (Ocaliva) pivotal PBC trial rather than elafibranor's own earlier-phase data

**Trial design & endpoints**

- 161 subjects (108 elafibranor, 53 placebo) were randomized and dosed across 82 centers (37 North America, 30 Europe, 9 Latin America, 6 other regions), of an original 150-subject enrollment target; sample size assumed a placebo response rate of ~10-12% (informed by OCA's pivotal trial) and an elafibranor response rate of ~47%, yielding ≥90% power at two-sided alpha 0.05 via an exact Fisher's test for the primary endpoint, and ≥80% power for the ALP-normalization and pruritus key secondaries

- Population was 96% female, 91% White, median age 57 (range 36-76); baseline mean ALP was 322 U/L (39% of subjects >3×ULN) and baseline mean PBC WI-NRS was 3.3, with 41% of subjects meeting the ≥4 pruritus-cohort threshold for the pruritus key secondary endpoints

- Primary endpoint result: biochemical response at Week 52 was 50.9% (55/108) elafibranor vs. 3.8% (2/53) placebo, risk difference 47.2% (95% CI 32.0, 56.9), CMH odds ratio 37.6 (95% CI 7.6, 302.2), p<0.0001; FDA's independent recalculation of the exact CMH OR (33.01, via R) differed numerically from the Applicant's reported value, consistent with the SAP-vs.-code ambiguity noted above; individual components — ALP <1.67×ULN (51.9% vs. 9.4%), ALP decrease ≥15% (75.0% vs. 17.0%), TB <ULN (85.2% vs. 83.0%, the only component not clearly differentiating arms — expected, since baseline TB was within normal range for the great majority of enrolled subjects) — were each individually reported

- Discontinuation was low and balanced (8.3% elafibranor vs. 7.5% placebo prior to Week 52); one death occurred in the elafibranor arm prior to Week 52 (a second occurred during the variable-duration period)

**Documents**

**Other resources**

- No trial-specific IPD/dataset access program (Vivli, YODA, Project Data Sphere) confirmed for Ipsen or this program

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting held, per the Integrated Review's Section 11 ("The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because there were no issues that warranted an advisory committee discussion")

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review (Reference ID: 5395225), §6.2.1.3, on the primary analysis method]* "The prespecified primary analysis for the primary endpoint was the exact Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test adjusted for both randomization stratification variables. It was not clear in the Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) whether the standard CMH odds ratio (OR) or exact CMH OR would be reported. The SAP stated 'The response proportions at Week 52 will be compared between the treatment groups using the exact CMH test stratified by the randomization strata. The estimate of the odds ratio and the corresponding 95% exact CI and exact p-value will be provided', potentially implying an exact CMH OR would be provided to match the test, CI, and p-value. However, the sample SAS code in SAP and the study report reflects estimating the standard CMH OR with exact Newcombe 95% CI and exact p-value."

- *[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.1.3, Multiplicity Adjustment]* "A fixed-sequence testing approach was pre-specified to control the overall study-wise type I error rate. The key secondary endpoints were tested in the order described in Section 6.2.1.1. The first key secondary endpoint was tested only if the primary endpoint was statistically significant. Each subsequent key secondary endpoint was tested only if the previous key secondary endpoint was statistically significant."

- *[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.1.3, on the mislabeled "treatment policy strategy"]* "The SAP named this as a 'treatment policy strategy,' though this does not align with the same terminology described in the International Council for Harmonisation E9 R1 (May 2021) describing a strategy to handle ICEs using observed data following the ICE. The Applicant stated that this analysis was not displayed in the Study Report because there were not enough observations to fit a monotone regression model based on the population with ICEs."

- *[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §17.2, Sample Size Justification]* "The assumptions used for the determination of the sample size were: An expected response rate in the placebo group slightly higher than that in the Phase 3 pivotal study supporting the regulatory approval of obeticholic acid (OCA, Ocaliva®) (10%), [a]n expected response rate in the elafibranor group at least similar to OCA (47%)... A total of 150 participants (100 on elafibranor versus 50 on placebo) allowed to achieve at least 90% power to demonstrate a statistically significant between-group difference of 35%... using an exact Fisher test."

### 20. Linerixibat (Lynavoy) — NDA 220295

**Sponsor:** GlaxoSmithKline LLC (GSK) — **correction to task brief:** the FDA NDA approval letter (dated March 2026) is addressed to GSK's Senior Director of Global Regulatory Affairs, and the approved label's adverse-event-reporting and manufacturing lines both list GlaxoSmithKline, not Intercept Pharmaceuticals/Alfasigma; linerixibat (GSK2330672) was originally a GSK-discovered asset and appears to remain GSK's NDA at approval, though Intercept/Alfasigma has been publicly associated with earlier-phase development of ileal bile acid transporter inhibitors in cholestatic pruritus more broadly

**Indication approved:** "LYNAVOY is an ileal bile acid transporter (IBAT) inhibitor indicated for the treatment of cholestatic pruritus associated with primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) in adult patients" (verbatim, FDA-approved label)

**Approval date:** March 17, 2026 (per openFDA submission record; NDA approval letter dated March 2026)

**Pivotal trial:** GLISTEN (Trial 212620, NCT04950127, N=238) — a Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 24-week trial of linerixibat 40 mg twice daily vs. placebo in adults with PBC-associated pruritus; companion Phase 2b dose-finding trial GLIMMER (Trial 201000) supported dose selection and safety

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial (GLISTEN/Trial 212620); companion five-arm, adaptive, phase 2b dose-finding trial (GLIMMER/Trial 201000) whose interim-data-informed dose adaptations were, per FDA's review, "not accounted for in the statistical analysis" of that supportive study

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint change from baseline in Monthly Itch Score (MIS, the worst Weekly Itch Score within a 4-week period, derived from a twice-daily 11-point Worst Itch Numeric Rating Scale) over 24 weeks; five key secondary endpoints in rank order — Weekly Itch Score change at Week 2, Monthly Sleep Score change over 24 weeks, and three responder-threshold endpoints (≥2-, ≥3-, and ≥4-point MIS reduction at Week 24)

- *Primary analysis:* mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) with baseline MIS, treatment, visit, baseline concomitant itch therapy, and their interactions as factors (compound-symmetry covariance structure used in the final analysis after the pre-specified unstructured-then-CS-then-AR fallback sequence); stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel analysis (adjusting for baseline itch severity and concomitant itch-medication regimen) for the three binary responder key-secondary endpoints, with the Sato variance estimator for the common risk difference

- *Multiplicity:* step-down/hierarchical fixed-sequence testing across the primary endpoint and 5 key secondary endpoints, all at a 5% two-sided significance level, per the sponsor's SAP submitted March 24, 2025

- *Missing data/bias:* continuous primary/key-secondary endpoints (MIS, WIS, MSS) handled via the MMRM's missing-at-random model without separate imputation; binary responder key secondaries (#3-5) used multiple imputation (100 datasets) of missing MIS values, converted to binary responses per imputed dataset, then combined via Rubin's rules; a tipping-point sensitivity analysis was pre-specified for the primary endpoint; FDA's review documents a **partial unblinding before database lock** (core Applicant team unblinded October 28, 2024, database lock November 14, 2024) that FDA investigated in detail and concluded did not affect the primary conclusion, since the SAP was finalized November 8, 2024 (before any unblinded analysis) and the only SAP changes in that window addressed subgroup-analysis specification and tipping-point shift parameters, partly in response to FDA feedback — matches "Reviewer-documented deviation from agreed analysis plan" in spirit but describes a distinct unblinding-timeline concern rather than an analysis-plan deviation — flagged **("Reviewer-investigated partial unblinding before database lock, resolved without primary-analysis impact")**

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held ("No advisory committee was deemed needed for this application" — FDA Integrated Review)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- GLISTEN (Trial 212620) randomized 238 adult PBC patients with baseline pruritus 1:1 (119 linerixibat, 119 placebo) for 24 weeks; 97% were on background ursodeoxycholic acid and 47% were on concomitant antipruritic medication at baseline; 11% (linerixibat) and 10% (placebo) had compensated (Child-Pugh A) cirrhosis

- Primary result: LS-mean MIS change -2.86 (linerixibat) vs. -2.15 (placebo), difference -0.72 (95% CI -1.15, -0.28), p=0.001; Weekly Itch Score at Week 2 also favored linerixibat (difference -0.71, 95% CI -1.07, -0.34, p<0.001)

- Key secondary Monthly Sleep Score result: LS-mean change -2.77 (linerixibat) vs. -2.24 (placebo), difference -0.53 (95% CI -0.98, -0.07), p=0.024; per FDA's review, alpha ran out after key secondary endpoint #3 in the hierarchical sequence, so hierarchical testing (and formal inference) stopped there for the remaining key secondaries

- Sample-size/design context: GLIMMER (Trial 201000) was a Phase 2b, five-arm, adaptive dose-finding trial in moderate-to-severe PBC pruritus that informed the Phase 3 dose but whose own adaptive elements were not incorporated into its statistical analysis

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2026/220295Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/220295Orig1s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Integrated Review (combined statistical/clinical review) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/220295Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04950127 (GLISTEN); no protocol/SAP posted, but FDA's Integrated Review quotes extensively from the sponsor's actual SAP for Trial 212620 (cited by SDN/submission date)

- Pivotal publication: not yet identified via PubMed as of this research (September 2026); the FDA Integrated Review is the primary public source for GLISTEN's methods and results

**Other resources**

- No trial-specific IPD/dataset access program (Vivli, YODA, Project Data Sphere) confirmed for GSK for this program; GSK more broadly participates in clinicalstudydatarequest.com-style data-sharing, not individually confirmed here

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting held

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.1.3, Statistical Analysis Plan, Trial 212620]* "The statistical analysis plan (SAP) specified that efficacy analyses for the primary and key secondary endpoints would be performed on the intent-to-treat (ITT) analysis population, defined as all randomized subjects."

- *[verbatim, same section, Analysis of Primary Endpoint]* "The SAP specified that the primary endpoint was to be analyzed using mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM)... An unstructured covariance structure was assumed; if analysis did not converge then compound symmetry (CS) structure would be used, followed by an autoregressive covariance structure if CS did not converge. Compound symmetry structure was used in the final analysis."

- *[verbatim, same section, §6.3.3, Partial Unblinding Before Database Lock]* "Trial 212620 was partially unblinded before database lock... the study was 'partially unblinded (core Applicant team unblinded, site remained blinded)' since October 28, 2024... The final SAP for the Trial 212620 was approved on November 08, 2024, and no further changes/modifications were made... Based on the versions of the SAP included in the NDA submission, the changes to SAP made between October 28, 2024, and November 8, 2024, did not impact the primary analysis and were to partly to address the Agency's feedback... Therefore, the conclusions based on the primary analysis were not impacted by the partial unblinding prior to database lock."

- *[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §11]* "No advisory committee was deemed needed for this application."

## Endocrine

### 1. Pasireotide (Signifor) — NDA 200677

**Sponsor:** Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adult patients with Cushing's disease for whom pituitary surgery is not an option or has not been curative

**Approval date:** December 14, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** Study B2305 (NCT00434148) — a single, randomized, double-blind, two-dose (600 mcg and 900 mcg subcutaneous, twice daily), non-comparative Phase 3 trial; this was a "one study application" (per FDA's own review keywords), with orphan-drug designation granted in 2009 given the rarity of Cushing's disease

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, dose-comparison trial in which the two dose arms were each independently evaluated against a fixed responder threshold rather than compared to each other or to a placebo/control arm — matching the taxonomy's existing "Wald confidence interval decision rule for a single activity-threshold responder rate" entry, applied here in parallel to two independently randomized dose arms of the same drug within one trial rather than a single-arm design; a blinded dose-titration/response-adaptive element was embedded mid-trial — non-responding patients (by an interim mUFC criterion) were unblinded at Month 3 and dose-escalated, while responders remained blinded through Month 6

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint proportion of responders at Month 6, defined per dose group as a patient with mean urinary free cortisol (mUFC) ≤ upper limit of normal (145 nmol/day) whose dose was not increased after Month 3; patients discontinuing before Month 3 were classified as non-responders, and those discontinuing between Months 3 and 6 had their last available mUFC (≥3 samples) carried forward to Month 6

- *Primary analysis:* independent, per-dose-group estimation of the responder rate and its 95% CI (normal-approximation/Wald CI); a dose was considered to demonstrate clinically meaningful efficacy if the lower bound of its 95% CI exceeded a pre-specified 15% threshold, agreed between FDA's Division and the Applicant during protocol development as a clinically meaningful floor rather than tested via a formal between-dose hypothesis test; a Hochberg step-down procedure was originally specified to control Type I error across the two dose comparisons but was removed by the sponsor in a later protocol amendment (Amendment 6) in favor of nominal, unadjusted tests and CIs per dose

- *Missing data/bias:* the 600 mcg twice-daily dose did not meet the pre-specified success criterion — 12/82 responders (14.6%, 95% CI 7.0%-22.3%), lower bound below the 15% threshold — while the 900 mcg twice-daily dose did meet it (21/80, 26.3%, 95% CI 16.6%-35.9%); both doses nonetheless appear on the approved label, with 600 mcg twice-daily as the recommended starting dose and dose titration to 900 mcg permitted based on response and tolerability; responder rate fell sharply with higher baseline mUFC severity (only 1 responder among 21 patients with baseline mUFC >10x ULN)

- *Regulatory:* Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee (EMDAC) meeting held November 7, 2012 — unanimous "yes" vote that the Applicant provided sufficient evidence of efficacy and safety, with members explicitly weighing the drug's hyperglycemia/diabetes risk against the paucity of alternative treatment options for Cushing's disease and the trial's single-study evidentiary basis

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study B2305 enrolled adult patients with persistent or recurrent Cushing's disease following pituitary surgery (or, for surgery-ineligible/refusing de novo patients, evidence of hypercortisolism), confirmed by elevated mUFC (≥1.5x ULN) and morning plasma ACTH criteria, plus imaging/histopathology or inferior-petrosal-sinus-sampling confirmation depending on prior surgical/tumor status

- 165 patients were randomized (162 treated: 82 to 600 mcg bid, 80 to 900 mcg bid); patients whose mUFC was reduced from baseline and fell below 2x ULN by an interim assessment remained blinded on their randomized dose through Month 6, while non-responders were unblinded, dose-escalated by 300 mcg bid increments (to a maximum of 1200 mcg bid), or discontinued if escalation was not feasible/tolerated

- There was no pre-specified formal statistical comparison between the 600 mcg and 900 mcg dose groups; per-protocol, cross-dose differences were to be assessed only descriptively via frequencies and summary statistics, and no sample-size/power calculation was performed for a between-dose comparison

- Hyperglycemia-related adverse events were common and dose-related; the trial and subsequent label carried extensive glucose-monitoring guidance, reflecting the Advisory Committee's explicit acknowledgment of this risk in its unanimous approval recommendation

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2012/200677Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label (original, 2012) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2012/200677lbl.pdf

- FDA Statistical Review (a joint clinical/statistical review document) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/200677Orig1s000StatR.pdf

- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/200677Orig1s000SumR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (Study B2305) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00434148

- Protocol / SAP — not identified as individually posted; FDA's Statistical Review quotes and summarizes the pre-specified statistical analysis plan in detail, cited above as verbatim FDA-review text

- Pivotal publication: Colao A, Petersenn S, Newell-Price J, Findling JW, Gu F, Maldonado M, et al; Pasireotide B2305 Study Group. A 12-month phase 3 study of pasireotide in Cushing's disease. *N Engl J Med*. 2012;366(10):914-924. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1105743), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22397653/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=A%2012-month%20phase%203%20study%20of%20pasireotide%20in%20Cushing%27s%20disease)

**Other resources**

- No trial-specific IPD/dataset access program (Vivli, YODA, Project Data Sphere) confirmed for Novartis or this program

- EMDAC meeting held November 7, 2012; unanimous "yes" vote on efficacy/safety sufficiency (see Regulatory keywords above)

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID: 3212809), §1.3.3]* "In Study B2305, the pre-specified primary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of responders at Month 6 by individual dose group (pasireotide 600 μg s.c. bid or 900 μg s.c. bid) in the Full Analysis Set (FAS)... A dose was considered to be effective in lowering mUFC if the lower bound of the 95% CI exceeded the pre-specified 15% non-inferiority margin."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §1.3.3]* "There was no plan to formally test for statistical differences in mUFC between dose groups. The Applicant did not perform sample size or power calculations for the purpose of comparing the dose groups... The Hochberg sequential step-down procedure was to be used initially to control type 1 error for testing across the two doses. In protocol Amendment 6, the sponsor removed the Hochberg procedure in favor of nominal statistical tests and 95% CIs for each dose."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, brief-summary table]* "SOM230B2305... 600 µg bid, 12/82 (14.6%, 95% CI 7.0, 22.3)... 900 µg bid, 21/80 (26.3%, 95% CI 16.6, 35.9)... prespecified lower bound of the 95% CI threshold: 15%."

- *[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, §9]* "A unanimous vote of 'yes' was rendered by the committee... The glycemic risk was acknowledged to be of concern but many members still felt that physicians could either treat with the many available anti-diabetic therapies or discontinue if unable to control."

### 2. Parathyroid hormone (Natpara) — BLA 125511

**Sponsor:** NPS Pharmaceuticals (acquired by Shire in 2015)

**Indication approved:** Adjunct to calcium and vitamin D to control hypocalcemia in patients with hypoparathyroidism

**Approval date:** January 23, 2015

**Pivotal trial:** REPLACE, Study CL1-11-040, NCT00732615

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 24-week trial with a pre-randomization "optimization period" to bring all subjects to a common calcium/vitamin D baseline before treatment allocation, and an individually flexible, titratable active dose

- *Endpoints:* responder status at Week 24, a three-component composite endpoint (≥50% reduction from baseline in oral calcium dose; ≥50% reduction from baseline in active vitamin D dose using a prespecified alphacalcidol-to-calcitriol dose-equivalence conversion; and albumin-corrected serum calcium maintained or normalized without exceeding the upper limit of normal)

- *Primary analysis:* two-sided Fisher's Exact test for the responder-rate difference on the ITT population, with Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel and MMRM sensitivity analyses

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence (step-down) testing procedure — each secondary endpoint tested only if the prior endpoint in the sequence was significant

- *Missing data/bias:* Last Observation Carried Forward (LOCF) for missing Week-24 data, with a worst-case-scenario (all-missing-as-non-responder) sensitivity analysis; an FDA Office of Scientific Investigations inspection found major protocol violations at one clinical site, leading FDA to exclude 10 of 134 subjects (7.46%) from its primary reporting basis rather than accept the sponsor's full dataset (**"FDA-driven post hoc exclusion of an entire investigative site for confirmed data-integrity violations (OSI-inspection-triggered)"**; no existing taxonomy row was found covering an FDA-driven, inspection-triggered full-site exclusion as the Agency's default analysis population, as distinct from a sponsor-run sensitivity analysis)

- *Regulatory:* boxed warning for osteosarcoma risk (informed by rat carcinogenicity data and the prior teriparatide/Forteo experience), approved with a REMS; advisory committee meeting held September 12, 2014, to discuss osteosarcoma risk specifically

**Trial design & endpoints**

- REPLACE (CL1-11-040, NCT00732615): a 6-month (24-week), multicenter, multinational (8 countries, 29 sites — 20 in the US, 3 in Canada, 3 in Denmark, 3 in Hungary, 1 each in Belgium, France, Italy, and the UK), double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of a flexible, individually titrated dose of rhPTH(1-84) (starting 50 μg subcutaneously daily, titratable in 25 μg increments every 2 weeks up to a 100 μg maximum, down-titratable to a 50 μg floor) vs. placebo, randomized 2:1 (90 to active drug, 44 to placebo). A pre-randomization "optimization period" brought all subjects to a common calcium/vitamin D baseline before the 24-week treatment period began, specifically to ensure cross-arm comparability at treatment start.

- Primary endpoint: percentage of responders at Week 24, defined by a three-component composite requiring all of: (1) ≥50% reduction from baseline in oral calcium dose; (2) ≥50% reduction from baseline in active vitamin D dose, using a prespecified dose-equivalence conversion (2 doses of alphacalcidol equated to 1 dose of calcitriol) to combine the two vitamin D analogs used across sites; and (3) an albumin-corrected total serum calcium concentration maintained or normalized versus baseline (≥7.5 mg/dL) and not exceeding the upper limit of normal. Baseline was defined as the last available pre-dose value; subjects with insufficient drug exposure (discontinuing before Visit 14/Week 16) were classified as non-responders.

- A mid-trial protocol amendment (Amendment 7.0) changed the wording of the third composite component from a qualitative criterion ("clinically stable in the opinion of the Investigator") to the quantitative albumin-corrected-calcium definition above. FDA's reviewer independently re-analyzed both the pre- and post-amendment definitions and found the primary result essentially unchanged (only one subject's responder status differed).

- Secondary endpoints, tested in fixed sequence only if the prior test in the sequence reached significance (p<0.05): (1) percent change from baseline in calcium supplementation dose at Week 24; (2) proportion of subjects achieving both independence from supplemental active vitamin D and an oral calcium dose ≤500 mg/day by Week 24; (3) frequency of clinical symptoms of hypocalcemia (paresthesiae, muscle cramping, tetany, seizures) during Weeks 16-24.

- Primary analysis: two-sided Fisher's Exact test for the responder-rate difference, on an ITT population (all randomized subjects who received at least one dose and had at least one post-baseline efficacy measurement), with Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel and MMRM sensitivity analyses. Missing Week-24 data were handled by Last Observation Carried Forward, with a worst-case-scenario sensitivity analysis (all missing counted as non-responder) also run.

- A data-integrity issue arose during FDA's Office of Scientific Investigations (OSI) inspection: major protocol violations were found at one clinical site (a co-investigator's site), and 10 of 134 randomized subjects (7.46%) were excluded from the primary analysis population as a result. FDA's Statistical Review explicitly re-ran the primary and secondary analyses on this "modified dataset" as its default reporting basis, rather than the sponsor's full 134-subject dataset. Primary result on the modified dataset: 46/84 (55%) responders on active drug vs. 1/40 (3%) on placebo, p<0.0001.

- Supportive, non-pivotal studies (dose-finding or safety only, not part of the statistically reviewed efficacy claim): PAR-C10-007/RELAY, PAR-C10-008/RACE, PAR-C10-009/REPEAT, and an investigator-initiated trial, all using similar composite-endpoint definitions but not independently supporting the efficacy determination — REPLACE alone is the primary registration study.

- FDA's carcinogenicity concern for the boxed warning stemmed directly from teriparatide (Forteo)'s prior osteosarcoma signal in rats, a related PTH-analog product carrying its own boxed warning and post-marketing osteosarcoma-surveillance requirements. An advisory committee meeting held September 12, 2014, discussed osteosarcoma risk specifically; Natpara was approved with a boxed warning for osteosarcoma risk and a REMS.

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2015/125511Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label (original, 2015) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2015/125511s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID 3532530) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/125511Orig1s000StatR.pdf

- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/125511Orig1s000SumR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00732615

- Protocol / SAP — not posted on ClinicalTrials.gov; FDA's Statistical Review describes the SAP's testing procedures and composite-endpoint definition directly

- Pivotal publication: Mannstadt M, Clarke BL, Vokes T, et al. Efficacy and safety of recombinant human parathyroid hormone (1-84) in hypoparathyroidism (REPLACE): a double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised, phase 3 study. *Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol*. 2013;1(4):275-283. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S2213-8587(13)70106-2>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24622413/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Efficacy%20and%20safety%20of%20recombinant%20human%20parathyroid%20hormone%201-84%20in%20hypoparathyroidism%20REPLACE) (an erratum, "Dosage error in article text," was subsequently published, *Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol*. 2014;2(1):e3)

**Other resources**

- No trial-specific IPD/dataset access program (Vivli, YODA, Project Data Sphere) confirmed for NPS Pharmaceuticals/Shire for this program

- Advisory committee meeting held September 12, 2014, focused on osteosarcoma risk (see boxed-warning discussion above)

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, BLA 125511, Reference ID 3532530, §3.2.2]* "A fixed sequence testing procedure was used to control the Type I Error. If the primary endpoint was found to be significant then the first secondary endpoint was tested."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, BLA 125511, Reference ID 3532530, §1.3]* "The biggest concern involved the reliability of some of the data in the study. Due to major protocol violations in the data from one of the clinical co-investigators, observations at site 1002 were deemed unreliable. Therefore, parts of the analysis were rerun excluding patients from this site."

- **Reverse-engineered SAP** (for the advisory committee's exact voting language, which was only partially captured in research for this entry): *[inferred]* the committee's overall conclusion that osteosarcoma risk was manageable under a boxed warning and REMS is traced to the fact that Natpara was ultimately approved with exactly that risk-management structure, rather than to a fully re-verified verbatim transcript of the September 12, 2014 vote.

### 3. Etelcalcetide (Parsabiv) — NDA 208325

**Sponsor:** KAI Pharmaceuticals, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Amgen Inc.

**Indication approved:** Secondary hyperparathyroidism (HPT) in adult patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) on hemodialysis

**Approval date:** February 7, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** Study 20120229, NCT01785849; Study 20120230, NCT01788046 (both placebo-controlled); Study 20120360, NCT01896232 (active-controlled vs. cinacalcet)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (Studies 229, 230); randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled, dose-titration (Study 360, vs. cinacalcet)
- *Endpoints:* Biochemical threshold responder endpoint (>30% reduction in intact PTH during an efficacy-assessment phase)
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test (stratified by region and screening iPTH category), stratified logistic regression (concordant sensitivity analysis)
- *Multiplicity:* Non-inferiority-then-superiority hierarchy (Study 360; both pre-specified and both met)
- *Missing data/bias:* Non-responder imputation (sponsor's primary analysis); retrieved-dropout imputation using each arm's own retrieved-dropout iPTH trajectory to impute non-retrieved dropouts; un-stratified tipping-point analysis
- *Regulatory:* Sponsor-derived non-inferiority margin justified by historical trial data (Amgen EVOLVE trial) rather than a concurrent reference arm

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Three randomized controlled trials were selected for full statistical review: two placebo-controlled, dose-titration, double-blind, multicenter, multinational trials (Studies 20120229 and 20120230; N=254 etelcalcetide/254 placebo and N=255 etelcalcetide/260 placebo, respectively) and one active-controlled, double-blind, double-dummy trial (Study 20120360; N=340 etelcalcetide/343 cinacalcet). All three had a 26-week treatment period with dose titration allowed up to 16 weeks, then maintained for the final 10 weeks, plus a 4-week follow-up period.

- Randomization stratification: region (North America/Other) and screening iPTH category (<600, 600-1000, >1000 pg/mL for the placebo studies; <900 vs. >900 pg/mL for the active-control study).

- Primary endpoint: proportion of patients achieving >30% reduction from baseline in intact PTH (iPTH), assessed as the average of all available iPTH measurements during a pre-specified Efficacy Assessment Phase (EAP, Weeks 20-27).

- Non-inferiority margin (Study 360, vs. cinacalcet): both non-inferiority and superiority were pre-specified; the 12% non-inferiority margin was derived from historical data in Amgen's EVOLVE trial (a placebo-controlled cinacalcet trial in a similar population), not from a concurrent reference arm in Study 360 itself.

- Sensitivity/robustness analyses (reviewer-conducted): an un-stratified tipping-point analysis, and a retrieved-dropout imputation method that used the observed post-dropout iPTH trajectory of "retrieved" dropouts (those who discontinued but returned for an EAP measurement) to impute the missing change for "non-retrieved" dropouts, separately by treatment arm and by early (≤8 weeks) vs. late (>8 and <20 weeks) dropout timing.

- Results: excluding missing data, >30% iPTH reduction was achieved by 74% (Study 229) and 75% (Study 230) of etelcalcetide patients vs. 8% and 10% of placebo patients (both p<0.0001); in Study 360, 68% of etelcalcetide patients vs. 58% of cinacalcet patients (non-responder-imputed; p=0.004), or 78% vs. 64% excluding missing data.

- A Statistical Review Addendum (Jan 2017, following a Type 1 resubmission) corrected a table-heading error and clarified the missing-data imputation method used for Study 360.

### 4. Abaloparatide (Tymlos) — NDA 208743

**Sponsor:** Radius Health, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of postmenopausal women with osteoporosis at high risk for fracture

**Approval date:** April 28, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** ACTIVE (Study BA-058-05-003), NCT01343004, with supportive data from ACTIVExtend (Study BA-058-05-005), NCT01657162

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, three-arm (abaloparatide 80 μg / teriparatide 20 μg / placebo) with the active-comparator arm restricted to a safety endpoint, not used for efficacy comparison; open-label, blinded-to-prior-treatment extension study with all patients receiving alendronate (ACTIVExtend)
- *Endpoints:* Incidence of new morphometric (x-ray-verified) vertebral fracture; BMD percent change (lumbar spine, total hip, femoral neck); time to first nonvertebral fracture
- *Primary analysis:* Wilson's score method (proportion estimate/CI), Newcombe method (CI for the risk difference), Fisher's exact test (primary endpoint); ANCOVA with LOCF (BMD, with MMRM as sensitivity); log-rank test and Cox proportional-hazards model (nonvertebral fracture)
- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence (step-down) hierarchical testing across 5 ordered endpoints (vertebral fracture → total hip BMD → femoral neck BMD → lumbar spine BMD → nonvertebral fracture)
- *Regulatory:* FDA reviewer flags limited US-population generalizability for a predominantly ex-US-enrolled pivotal trial

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ACTIVE (Study 003) was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, international Phase 3 trial in ambulatory postmenopausal women (50-85 years, ≥5 years postmenopausal) with severe osteoporosis at high fracture risk (BMD T-score ≤-2.5 and >-5.0 at lumbar spine/hip with radiographic evidence of prevalent vertebral fracture, or a qualifying low-trauma fracture history, or age/T-score-adjusted variants of these criteria).

- Three arms, equally randomized: abaloparatide 80 μg SC daily (N=824), teriparatide 20 μg SC daily (N=818, included solely to characterize a safety endpoint of interest, hypercalcemia — its efficacy/safety data were not otherwise analyzed in the FDA statistical review), and matching placebo (N=821), for an 18-month treatment period plus a 1-month follow-up.

- Primary efficacy endpoint: percentage of patients with ≥1 incident x-ray-verified new vertebral fracture from baseline to month 18, analyzed in the modified ITT (mITT) population (ITT patients with a baseline and ≥1 post-baseline evaluable spine x-ray).

- Key secondary endpoints, tested in a pre-specified fixed sequence (each at 2-sided 5%, contingent on the prior step's significance): percent change from baseline to month 18 in total hip BMD, then femoral neck BMD, then lumbar spine BMD, then time to first incident nonvertebral fracture by month 19.

- Results: new vertebral fracture incidence 0.55% (abaloparatide) vs. 4.2% (placebo) at month 18 (p<0.0001, 86% relative risk reduction); nonvertebral fracture 2.7% vs. 4.7% (p=0.045) at month 19; BMD increases of 3.5% (total hip), 3.3% (femoral neck), and 8.7% (lumbar spine) over placebo at month 18.

- ACTIVExtend (Study 005) was a 24-month open-label extension in which all Study 003 completers (both former abaloparatide and former placebo patients) received alendronate 70 mg weekly; patients/investigators remained blinded to the original Study 003 treatment assignment through the first 6 months. The FDA review treated the integrated Study 003 + first-6-months-of-Study-005 analysis (through month 25) as confirmatory: new vertebral fracture 0.55% (former abaloparatide→alendronate) vs. 4.40% (former placebo→alendronate) (p<0.0001, 87% relative risk reduction); nonvertebral fracture reduced 52% (p=0.0168).

- Statistical methods: primary endpoint used Wilson's score method for each arm's proportion/CI, the Newcombe method for the between-arm risk-difference CI, and Fisher's exact test for the treatment comparison, all in the mITT population. BMD endpoints used an ANCOVA model (fixed effects: DXA instrument manufacturer, treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction; covariate: baseline BMD) with LOCF imputation for missing values, with MMRM as a sensitivity analysis, in the ITT population. Nonvertebral fracture used a log-rank test and Cox proportional-hazards model with Kaplan-Meier estimation.

- FDA reviewer caveat: the Executive Summary explicitly flagged that "the submitted studies enrolled very few U.S. patients and the efficacy of abaloparatide was not evaluable in the U.S. patients from a statistical perspective," leaving generalizability of the largely ex-US efficacy findings to the US population as an FDA-identified open question resolved as a clinical (not statistical) judgment.

Total hip BMD 3. Femoral neck BMD 4. Lumbar spine BMD 5. Nonvertebral fracture."

The absolute risk reduction and its corresponding 95% confidence interval for the treatment difference were derived using the Newcombe approach. The Fisher's exact test was used to compare the two treatment groups with respect to the primary efficacy endpoint."

### 5. Macimorelin (Macrilen) — NDA 205598

**Sponsor:** Aeterna Zentaris GmbH

**Indication approved:** Diagnostic agent for the diagnosis of adult growth hormone deficiency (AGHD) — a growth hormone-stimulation test (GHST), not a treatment

**Approval date:** December 20, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** Study 52 (AEZS-130-052), open-label, randomized, single-dose, 2-way crossover diagnostic-accuracy trial vs. the insulin tolerance test (ITT); original Study 47 (AEZS-130-047) was the initial pivotal study submitted under an SPA and failed its pre-specified primary analysis, contributing to a Complete Response recommendation before Study 52 was conducted

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison) (existing taxonomy term — 2-way crossover of macimorelin GHST vs. insulin tolerance test, same subjects receiving both); primary-analysis-framework change across submission cycles following a failed SPA-agreed endpoint (ROC/AUC threshold replaced by a percent-agreement/benchmark framework)
- *Endpoints:* Percent Positive Agreement and Percent Negative Agreement vs. a non-reference-standard comparator test; Kendall's tau-b (rank correlation without use of cut points)
- *Primary analysis:* Clopper-Pearson exact confidence interval (lower bound vs. pre-specified benchmark); logistic-regression/ROC AUC analysis (original Study 47 framework, superseded)
- *Missing data/bias:* Spectrum bias from sponsor's exclusion of intermediate/low-likelihood subjects (Groups B/C) from secondary sensitivity/specificity analyses, flagged by the FDA reviewer as inflating apparent test performance
- *Regulatory:* Diagnostic-test approval despite a missed pre-specified co-primary agreement threshold, supported by retrospective/exploratory re-analyses and framed around the test's "rule-in" (not "rule-out") performance

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Regulatory history: the original NDA cycle rested on Study AEZS-130-047, a diagnostic-accuracy study in 100 subjects (52 previously enrolled AGHD patients/matched controls plus 48 later enrolled under an SPA, receiving macimorelin only) using a pre-specified primary analysis of ROC AUC ≥0.85 (99% one-sided lower confidence bound) for macimorelin peak GH vs. confirmed AGHD status. This primary analysis **failed** in the modified ITT population (lower bound 0.83) though it passed in a sponsor-defined per-protocol population (0.851); the original FDA statistical review recommended a Complete Response, citing possible confounding by race and study site and non-reproducible, data-driven cut-point selection.

- Following the Complete Response, the sponsor conducted Study 52 (AEZS-130-052) as a new pivotal trial: an open-label, randomized, single-dose, 2-way crossover diagnostic-accuracy study at 30 sites in 9 countries (25 in Europe, 5 in the US), enrolling 166 of 238 screened subjects assigned to four groups of descending AGHD likelihood (Group A: high likelihood/structural lesions; Group B: intermediate likelihood; Group C: low likelihood; Group D: healthy controls matched to Group A).

- Every subject received both the macimorelin GHST and the insulin tolerance test (ITT, the existing clinical reference test), in a randomized order (7 days to 1 month washout), with serum GH measured at 15, 30, 45, 60, and 90 minutes post-dose. Pre-specified cut points: macimorelin GH <2.8 ng/mL and ITT GH <5.1 ng/mL identify AGHD; the macimorelin cut point was carried over from Study 47.

- Analysis population: modified Intent-to-Treat (subjects with both GHSTs evaluable).

- Co-primary endpoints: Percent Negative Agreement (benchmark ≥75%) and Percent Positive Agreement (benchmark ≥70%) between the macimorelin test and the ITT (a "non-reference standard," since neither test can confirm AGHD with 100% certainty), each required to clear its benchmark using the lower bound of a Clopper-Pearson confidence interval. Secondary endpoints: Percent Overall Agreement, and descriptive sensitivity/specificity of both tests against the same non-reference benchmark.

- Sample size: planned at 110 subjects (55 ITT-positive, 55 ITT-negative), assuming ≥82% agreement with a 1-sided exact CI lower bound ≥69.3%; the FDA reviewer noted the sponsor's sample-size calculation incorrectly assumed independence between the two tests despite the crossover (paired) design.

- FDA reviewer critique of secondary analyses: the sponsor's sensitivity/specificity analyses excluded the intermediate/low-likelihood subjects (Groups B and C) — precisely the population the reviewer identified as the actual intended-use population for a diagnostic test, since high-likelihood (Group A) and healthy (Group D) subjects would not typically need testing in clinical practice. Restricting the performance analysis to Groups A/D introduces spectrum bias and overestimates sensitivity/specificity.

- Results: the sponsor met the negative-agreement benchmark, but the estimated lower bound of the 95% CI around Percent Positive Agreement was 63%, below the pre-specified 70% margin — the sponsor did not meet this co-primary endpoint. FDA's Division Director Summary Review concluded the data reliably support macimorelin to "rule in" (confirm) AGHD when positive, but perform "slightly less well" at ruling out disease, and approved the diagnostic on that (positive-agreement-focused) basis despite the missed threshold, following the sponsor's retrospective/exploratory re-analyses of the moderate positive-agreement finding.

- FDA Statistical Review (Addendum, Study 52 — Statistical Reviewer: Anna Kettermann, Dipl. Math, MA; Concurring Reviewer: Gregory Levin, PhD, Acting Team Leader; the same PDF also contains the original, earlier Study 47 statistical review that recommended a Complete Response) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/205598Orig1s000StatR.pdf

"Macimorelin as a Diagnostic Test for Adult GH Deficiency." *J Clin Endocrinol Metab.* 2018;103(8):3083-3093. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1210/jc.2018-00665), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29860473/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Macimorelin%20as%20a%20Diagnostic%20Test%20for%20Adult%20GH%20Deficiency)

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 205598, Study 52 section, §3.2.1 "Study Design and Endpoints," p.12]*

> "Co-primary efficacy variables were 'Percent Negative Agreement' and 'Percent Positive Agreement' when using predefined cut-off points of both GHSTs. The benchmark for negative agreement was set to 75% and the benchmark for positive agreement was set to 70%. The goal for each of the co-primary endpoints was to show with high statistical confidence (based on the lower bound of the Clopper-Pearson confidence interval) that the agreement was equal or higher than each of the prespecified benchmarks."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 205598, §3.2.2 "Statistical Methodologies," p.13-14]*

> "For all secondary analyses, the sponsor excluded subjects from groups B and C. Thus, subjects who will likely be candidates for the ITT test... were excluded from the sponsor's evaluation. Furthermore, the sponsor-defined 'sensitivity' and 'specificity' are not valid estimates of those characteristics for the test in the intended use population. An analysis that does not include the intended use population but rather includes only subjects on the extremes introduces spectrum bias... and leads to biased estimates of sensitivity and specificity (tending to overestimate the performance characteristics of the test)."

*[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, NDA 205598, original Study 47 review, §1.1 "Conclusions and Recommendations," p.4 (Reference ID 3539050)]*

> "The statistical results in terms of accuracy do not provide enough evidence to support the claims proposed in this NDA. The sponsor failed in the pre-specified primary ROC AUC analysis. The ROC AUC results may be biased because of possible confounding of the test with race and study site... We recommend CR with additional confirmatory study with pre-specified cut-point and intended patient population."

*[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, NDA 205598, discussion of the co-primary positive-agreement endpoint, p.13 region]*

> "The sponsor did not meet one of the two co-primary endpoints (demonstrating that the estimated lower bound of the 95% CI around positive agreement was > 70%)... The moderate level of positive agreement observed between the two tests suggests that the likelihood of a false negative result with the Macrilen test is also moderate... the data in the application clearly establishes that a maximally stimulated serum GH level of 2.8 ng/mL on the Macrilen test can be used to reliably confirm or rule-in the presence of disease. The test has utility in that regard and should be approved for that purpose given the multiple issues with currently available alternatives."

### 6. Burosumab-twza (Crysvita) — BLA 761068

**Sponsor:** Ultragenyx Pharmaceutical Inc. (co-developed with Kyowa Kirin)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH) in adult and pediatric patients 1 year of age and older

**Approval date:** April 17, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** Adults: Study UX023-CL303, NCT02526160 (randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled); Pediatrics: Study UX023-CL201, NCT02163577 (randomized, open-label, dose-finding, ages 5-12, compared via propensity-score analysis to the external Study UX023-CL002 conventional-therapy cohort) and Study UX023-CL205, NCT02750618 (ages 1-4)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (adult Study CL303); randomized non-comparative dose-regimen cohort design (existing taxonomy term — pediatric Study CL201, Q2W vs. Q4W dosing-interval randomization, no placebo/active-control arm); propensity-score-weighted external/historical comparator substituting for a concurrent control arm, using an active conventional-therapy cohort (Study CL002) rather than placebo (extension of existing taxonomy term, which is defined for a placebo comparator)
- *Endpoints:* Biochemical threshold responder endpoint (serum phosphorus above the lower limit of normal at dosing-interval midpoint, averaged across cycles) (same construct as the etelcalcetide entry above); Brief Pain Inventory (BPI) Question 3 (Worst Pain); WOMAC Stiffness and Physical Function domains; Radiographic Global Impression of Change (RGI-C) and Rickets Severity Score (RSS, pediatric)
- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test (adult primary endpoint, stratified by randomization factors); Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) model with compound-symmetry covariance (change-from-baseline secondary PRO endpoints)
- *Multiplicity:* Fixed-sequence hierarchical testing (primary endpoint gates a group of 3 secondary PRO endpoints) with Hochberg adjustment within the secondary group (adult Study CL303)
- *Missing data/bias:* Non-responder imputation for missing primary-endpoint biochemical data; reviewer-documented randomization-stratification deviation (interactive response system used BPI-Q5 "average pain" instead of the protocol-specified BPI-Q3 "worst pain" as the stratification factor, affecting all enrolled subjects, with a sponsor sensitivity analysis substituting the intended factor)
- *Regulatory:* No FDA advisory committee meeting was held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Adult pivotal trial (Study CL303): a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial at 25 centers in the US, Europe, Japan, and South Korea, enrolling ~120 adults (18-65 years) with XLH and substantial bone/joint pain (BPI-Q3 Worst Pain ≥4/10). Conventional therapy (phosphate/calcitriol) was discontinued at screening; patients were randomized 1:1 to burosumab 1.0 mg/kg SC Q4W (fixed dose, halved only for hyperphosphatemia) or placebo for 24 weeks, followed by open-label burosumab for all subjects (blinded to original assignment through week 48).

- Randomization was intended to be stratified by BPI-Q3 (worst pain, >6.0 vs. ≤6.0) and region, but an interactive web response system (IWRS) programming error substituted BPI-Q5 (average pain) for the entire study; this was logged as a protocol violation, all subjects were nonetheless included in the primary analysis (using the as-implemented BPI-Q5 stratification), and the sponsor ran a sensitivity analysis using the intended BPI-Q3 stratification to assess impact.

- Primary efficacy endpoint (adult, CL303): proportion of subjects achieving mean serum phosphorus above the lower limit of normal (2.5 mg/dL) at the midpoint of the 4-week dosing interval, averaged across cycles from baseline to week 24 (i.e., mean of weeks 2, 6, 10, 14, 18, 22); missing data at a cycle midpoint were counted as non-response. Analyzed via a CMH test stratified by the as-implemented randomization factors (BPI-Q5 category and region), 2-sided alpha 0.05.

- Key secondary endpoints (adult, CL303), tested via fixed-sequence multiplicity control (primary endpoint must reach p<0.05 to unlock a group of 3 secondaries tested together with Hochberg adjustment at 0.05): change from baseline to week 24 in BPI Worst Pain, WOMAC Stiffness, and WOMAC Physical Function, each modeled via a GEE model (treatment, stratification factor, region, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction, baseline covariate; compound-symmetry working covariance).

- Sample size (CL303): 60/arm (120 total), assuming 60% (burosumab) vs. 10% (placebo) response, for >95% power at 2-sided alpha 0.05.

- Results (CL303): 94.1% (64/68) of burosumab-treated adults vs. 7.6% (5/66) of placebo-treated adults achieved the primary endpoint (p<0.0001).

- Pediatric evidence (Study CL201, ages 5-12): a randomized, open-label, dose-finding trial with no placebo or active-control arm — FDA and the sponsor agreed a placebo arm was unethical given XLH's risk of irreversible disability, and the sponsor argued conventional-therapy standardization/blinding problems against using it as an active comparator. Patients were sequentially assigned to one of three starting-dose cohorts and, within each, randomized 1:1 (stratified by sex) to Q2W vs. Q4W dosing, with doses individually titrated to a serum-phosphorus target; comparative efficacy context (radiographic rickets healing, via RGI-C and RSS scores) was obtained through a propensity-score-matched comparison against a separate, retrospectively assembled cohort from conventional-therapy study UX023-CL002, rather than a concurrent randomized control.

- Study CL205 (ages 1-4) supported extension of the pediatric indication down to age 1 using a similar dose-titration design.

- No formal Advisory Committee meeting was convened for this BLA.

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761068, §8.1.4, "Statistical Analysis Plan / Randomization," p.209]*

> "The study was planned to randomize patients stratified by BPI-Q3 (worst pain). However, the IWRS erroneously used BPI-Q5 (average pain) as the stratification factor instead... All enrolled subjects were affected by this IWRS error. The applicant included the IWRS error to the list of protocol violations. Although all subjects were affected by this protocol violation, they were included in the primary efficacy analysis."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761068, §8.1.4, "Multiplicity Control," p.211]*

> "Step 1: Test the primary endpoint of the proportion of subjects achieving mean serum phosphorus levels above the lower limit of normal at the mid-point of the dose interval. Step 2: Test the three secondary PRO endpoints (change from baseline to week 24 in BPI Worst Pain, WOMAC stiffness, and WOMAC physical function) between treatment groups as a group at 0.05 level. Hochberg adjustment was applied for multiple testing of these three endpoints."

*[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761068, §8.1.4, "Serum phosphorus" results, p.212 region]*

> "A total of 94.1% of subjects in the KRN23 group achieved a mean serum phosphorus level above the LLN at Week 24, compared with only 7.6% of subjects in the placebo group (p < 0.0001)."

### 7. Romosozumab-aqqg (Evenity) — BLA 761062

**Sponsor:** Amgen Inc. (co-developed with UCB)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women at high risk for fracture, defined as a history of osteoporotic fracture, or multiple risk factors for fracture, or patients who have failed or are intolerant to other available osteoporosis therapy

**Approval date:** April 9, 2019 (following a July 13, 2017 Complete Response Letter and a July 9, 2018 resubmission)

**Pivotal trial:** FRAME (Study 20070337, NCT01575834), randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, and ARCH (Study 20110142, NCT01631214), randomized, double-blind, active (alendronate)-controlled

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two co-primary Phase 3 trials with different comparators run in parallel — FRAME (placebo-controlled, N=7,180, 12 months double-blind then all subjects switched to open-label denosumab) and ARCH (active alendronate-controlled, N=4,093, romosozumab-then-alendronate vs. alendronate-alone, event-driven follow-up to a target of 440 confirmed nonvertebral-fracture events); a cardiovascular safety signal appeared in ARCH (active-controlled) but not in FRAME (placebo-controlled), producing a **cross-trial safety-signal discordance by comparator type** that drove a Complete Response Letter — closest existing taxonomy concept is "Approval program with a substantial proportion of negative/failed pivotal trials" (Vortioxetine), but that describes efficacy-trial discordance rather than a safety signal appearing only against one comparator type; propose **"Post-hoc cross-trial safety-signal reconciliation following comparator-dependent discordance (CRL-triggering)"**

- *Endpoints:* co-primary endpoints in both trials — new vertebral fracture incidence through Month 12 and through Month 24; key secondary endpoints (hierarchically tested, contingent on co-primary success) included clinical fracture, nonvertebral fracture, and BMD percent change at spine/total hip/femoral neck; a Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE) composite (cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke) was added post-hoc, at FDA's explicit request after the CRL, as an adjudicated safety analysis — the original ARCH SAP (April 2017, three months before the CRL) pre-specified cardiovascular event adjudication as descriptive only ("No statistical tests will be performed")

- *Primary analysis:* co-primary vertebral-fracture endpoints tested using Hochberg's step-up procedure to control family-wise error across the two co-primary endpoints (ARCH); secondary BMD endpoints tested in a fixed hierarchical sequence at 2-sided 0.05; nonvertebral fracture (ARCH key secondary) tested via a group-sequential approach at both an interim ("primary") and final analysis, using a Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function approximating a Pocock boundary

- *Multiplicity:* Hochberg's method for the two co-primary endpoints, followed by fixed-sequence (hierarchical) gatekeeping for secondary endpoints — FRAME's testing sequence stopped at the nonvertebral-fracture endpoint when it failed to reach the required significance threshold at the pre-specified alpha, per the review: "Because of the failed significance on nonvertebral fractures, statistical testing of the remaining hierarchical secondary endpoints should not proceed"

- *Missing data/bias:* MACE hazard ratios were computed post-hoc across both trials after imbalance was identified, which FDA's own review flags as a limitation ("most of the analyses... were conducted post-hoc after the imbalance... was identified... the low number of MACE during the 12-month double-blind period (approximately 60 events in each trial)")

- *Regulatory:* Complete Response Letter July 13, 2017, citing "a higher incidence of cardiovascular serious adverse events with romosozumab compared to alendronate" in ARCH; FDA Bone, Reproductive and Urologic Drugs Advisory Committee met January 16, 2019 and voted 15-3-1 (Yes-as-proposed / Yes-different-indication / No) that the overall benefit/risk profile supported approval; approved with a Boxed Warning restricting use in patients with recent (within 1 year) MI or stroke

**Trial design & endpoints**

- FRAME: multicenter, international, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial; romosozumab 210 mg SC monthly (n=3,589) vs. placebo (n=3,591) for 12 months, after which all subjects transitioned to open-label denosumab; co-primary endpoints new vertebral fracture through Month 12 and Month 24

- ARCH: multicenter, international, randomized, double-blind, alendronate-controlled trial (N=4,093); romosozumab 210 mg SC monthly for 12 months followed by alendronate, vs. alendronate alone throughout; co-primary endpoints new vertebral fracture through Month 12 and Month 24; sample size for the event-driven nonvertebral-fracture endpoint (440 confirmed events) derived via 10,000-iteration simulation (EAST 5.4 software), per the posted SAP

- FRAME results: new vertebral fracture 0.5% (romosozumab) vs. 1.8% (placebo) at 12 months (p<0.001); clinical fracture (first hierarchical secondary) 1.6% vs. 2.5% (p<0.01); nonvertebral fracture did not reach the required significance threshold (p=0.10 at 12 months, p=0.029 at 24 months against a required α=0.025), halting further hierarchical secondary testing per the pre-specified gatekeeping procedure

- Cardiovascular adjudication results (independently adjudicated, per label §6.1 and FDA review Table 40): FRAME (placebo-controlled) 12-month MACE 0.8% (30/3,589) vs. 0.8% (29/3,591), HR 1.03 (95% CI 0.62-1.72), no signal; ARCH (active-controlled) 12-month MACE 2.0% (41/2,005) vs. 1.1% (22/2,014), HR 1.87 (95% CI 1.11-3.14), driven by MI (0.8% vs. 0.2%) and stroke (0.6% vs. 0.3%); a FRAME+ARCH-only meta-analysis gave HR 1.38 (95% CI 0.96-1.99)

- FDA's own discordance discussion (verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review): "It is unclear whether romosozumab truly increases cardiovascular risk, as there are several factors that make the interpretation of the signal difficult. The fracture studies were not specifically designed to assess cardiovascular safety outcomes... most of the analyses... were conducted post-hoc after the imbalance... was identified."
