**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, ARCH posted SAP, §10.6.3, dated April 7, 2017 — before the July 2017 CRL]* "All deaths and potential cardiovascular-related serious adverse events will be submitted to an external independent committee comprised of experienced cardiologists for blinded adjudication... Only events confirmed positive by the adjudication committee to meet cardiovascular event definition criteria will be included for analyses... No statistical tests will be performed."

- *[verbatim, ARCH posted SAP, on the nonvertebral-fracture group-sequential testing procedure]* "tested using a group sequential approach at the primary analysis and the final analysis based on a 1-sided test (α=0.025). The Lan-DeMets alpha spending function (Lan and DeMets, 1983) that approximates a Pocock boundary (Pocock, 1977)... will be used to determine the significance level."

- *[verbatim, ARCH posted SAP, on co-primary multiplicity control]* "Hochberg's method (Hochberg, 1988) to adjust for the multiplicity of the primary endpoints."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, on the July 2017 CRL deficiency]* "Preliminary findings from Study 20110142 show a higher incidence of cardiovascular serious adverse events with romosozumab compared to alendronate in women with postmenopausal osteoporosis. A similar signal was seen in Study 20110174... Although Study 20070337 did not appear to have a cardiovascular safety signal, these disparate findings across studies require detailed review."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, §9, on the January 2019 Advisory Committee]* "An Advisory Committee meeting was held on January 16, 2019 to discuss the cardiovascular safety findings," with a voting question on whether "the overall benefit/risk profile of romosozumab [is] acceptable to support approval" — result 15 Yes-as-proposed, 3 Yes-different-indication, 1 No.

- **Reverse-engineered SAP** (for FRAME, since no protocol/SAP is publicly posted for that trial): *[inferred]* FRAME's hierarchical secondary-endpoint testing sequence and its required alpha threshold for nonvertebral fracture are traceable to the FDA review's statement that testing halted after nonvertebral fracture failed to reach significance ("Because of the failed significance on nonvertebral fractures, statistical testing of the remaining hierarchical secondary endpoints should not proceed"), implying a pre-specified fixed-sequence gatekeeping procedure structurally identical to ARCH's, even though FRAME's own SAP document is not public.

### 8. Osilodrostat (Isturisa) — NDA 212801

**Sponsor:** Recordati Rare Diseases, Inc. (originally developed by Novartis as LCI699; licensed to Recordati)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of adult patients with Cushing's disease for whom pituitary surgery is not an option or has not been curative

**Approval date:** March 6, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** Study C2301/CLCI699C2301 (LINC-3, NCT02180217), a randomized-withdrawal design — the sole trial submitted that included randomization; supportive single-arm studies C1201 and C2201 (LINC-1/LINC-2) and an unfinished, separately conducted placebo-controlled Study C2302/CLCI699C2302 (LINC-4, NCT02697734), submitted for safety only at the time of this NDA

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* a single randomized-withdrawal (RW) trial (LINC-3) as the only submitted study with randomization, comprising a 12-week dose-titration period, a 12-week single-arm (open-label) treatment period, and an 8-week randomized-withdrawal period (osilodrostat continuation vs. placebo substitution) — the FDA statistical reviewer explicitly flagged this design as "not designed to directly evaluate the treatment effect in comparison to placebo in treatment-naïve patients," since randomization occurred only among patients who had already responded to 24 weeks of open-label osilodrostat; this maps to the existing taxonomy term "Randomized-withdrawal enrichment design" (seen in Pegvaliase-pqpz/Palynziq), extending it to an endocrine/orphan-disease context with a companion separately-sponsored-at-the-time placebo-controlled confirmatory trial (LINC-4) submitted for safety only

- *Endpoints:* primary — proportion of randomized patients who were "complete responders" at the end of the 8-week randomized-withdrawal period (Week 34), defined as mean urinary free cortisol (mUFC) ≤ upper limit of normal (ULN), no discontinuation during the RW period, an mUFC assessment at Week 34, and no dose increase above the Week 26 level; key secondary — complete-responder rate at the end of the single-arm period (Week 24), tested only if the primary endpoint reached significance, against a fixed null-hypothesis threshold of ≤30% (not a concurrent comparator) — the FDA reviewer separately noted, "the key secondary endpoint lacks a comparator arm by design"

- *Primary analysis:* two-sided Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel exact test stratified by the two randomization stratification factors (osilodrostat dose at Week 24, and history of pituitary radiation), applied to the randomized analysis set (RAS) following the intent-to-treat principle; the key secondary endpoint used a two-sided 95% exact confidence interval (Clopper-Pearson method) against the 30% threshold

- *Multiplicity:* a hierarchical (fixed-sequence) testing strategy controlling overall two-sided Type I error at 0.05 — the key secondary endpoint was tested only if the primary endpoint's null hypothesis was rejected, "to ensure preservation of the overall 2-sided type 1 error at 5%"

- *Missing data/bias:* patients who discontinued during the randomized-withdrawal period were counted as non-responders for the primary endpoint; patients with a missing Week-24 mUFC assessment were counted as non-responders for the key secondary endpoint; only 70 of 137 enrolled/treated patients (51%) were evaluable for the primary endpoint, since it was assessed only among the subset who both responded during the open-label period and were subsequently randomized

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held; no REMS required; FDA's statistical reviewer recommended that if approved, "labeling using results from this study should be descriptive in nature," given the RW design's inherent limitations and an aggressive dose-titration schedule "not likely what would be used in clinical practice"

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study C2301 (LINC-3) enrolled adult male and female patients (18-75 years) with persistent/recurrent Cushing's disease after pituitary surgery/irradiation, or de novo patients who were not surgical candidates or refused surgery; Period 1 was a 12-week dose-titration; Period 2 was a 12-week single-arm (open-label) continuation (secondary endpoint assessed at its end, Week 24); patients meeting response criteria at Week 24 (mUFC < ULN, no further dose increase since Week 12) were randomized 1:1 to continued osilodrostat (n=36) or placebo (n=34) for an 8-week randomized-withdrawal period (primary endpoint assessed at its end, Week 34)

- Primary result: complete responder rate at Week 34 was significantly higher with osilodrostat than placebo (a large, statistically significant difference of 57 percentage points, per FDA's review), though the reviewer cautioned that "only 70 (51%) of patients qualified to be evaluated for the primary endpoint" and that the design could not isolate the drug's effect from a treatment-naïve placebo comparison

- Study C2302 (LINC-4) was a separately protocoled Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, 48-week study with an initial 12-week placebo-controlled period, agreed with FDA at an End-of-Phase-2 meeting (October 2013) as the second pivotal study, but was still ongoing at the time of this NDA submission and contributed safety data only; its efficacy results (published later, see below) were not part of the FDA statistical review underlying this approval

- FDA statistical comments to the sponsor prior to submission (verbatim, from the review's meeting-record excerpt) requested clarification of missing-mUFC handling and disposition of patients discontinued under the SAP's rule that "the patient must be discontinued from the randomized withdrawal period, declared a non-responder, if the mUFC increases to > 1.5 x ULN, and at least 2 individual urine samples show UFC > 1.5 ULN at a single visit"

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, ClinicalTrials.gov-posted LINC-3 SAP for Final CSR, §2.5]* "The primary objective was to compare the complete response rates at the end of the 8 weeks period of randomized withdrawal (Week 34) between patients randomized to continued LCI699 therapy vs. placebo... a Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel exact test stratified by the two stratification factors considered for randomization will be performed using the RAS following the intent-to-treat principle."

- *[verbatim, same document, §2.6]* "For the key secondary objective, the statistical null hypothesis states that the complete response rate at week 24 [with] LCI699 is ≤ 30%. The analysis of the key secondary objective will be based on the 2-sided 95% exact confidence interval (Clopper-Pearson method)... The above testing on the key secondary objective will only be carried out if the null hypothesis for the primary objective is rejected. This sequential procedure will ensure preservation of the overall 2-sided type 1 error at 5%."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Reference ID 4537365, §1.2 Major Statistical Issues]* "The study was not designed to directly evaluate the treatment effect in comparison to placebo in treatment-naïve patients... The primary endpoint is assessed at the end of the RW period and includes only 70 (51%) of the 137 patients that were enrolled and treated in the study. The key secondary endpoint lacks a comparator arm by design."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §1.3 Conclusion and Recommendations]* "Due to limitations of the design of this study and due to the aggressive dose titration, quantification of the magnitude of the efficacy is difficult. Therefore if the drug is approved, labeling using results from this study should be descriptive in nature."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §2.1.2, quoting a September 4, 2018 statistical comment to the sponsor]* "In the SAP, it stated 'during the randomized withdrawal study period, the patient must be discontinued from the randomized withdrawal period, declared a non-responder, if the mUFC increases to > 1.5 x ULN, and at least 2 individual urine samples show UFC > 1.5 ULN at a single visit.'"

- *[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, §9]* "There was no Advisory Committee Meeting held for this application."

- **Reverse-engineered SAP**: not required for LINC-3's primary analysis, since a genuine SAP is publicly posted (see above); *[inferred, for LINC-4's efficacy conclusions]* since LINC-4 contributed safety data only to this 2020 NDA and its efficacy results were published later (Gadelha et al., 2022), any efficacy-related statistical detail for LINC-4 in future census updates should be sourced from that 2022 publication and/or a subsequent supplemental-approval review, not attributed to this original 2020 approval's statistical review.

### 9. Somapacitan-beco (Sogroya) — BLA 761156

**Sponsor:** Novo Nordisk A/S

**Indication approved:** Replacement of endogenous growth hormone in adults with growth hormone deficiency (AGHD)

**Approval date:** August 28, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** REAL 1, NCT02229851

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with an added open-label, active-referenced arm (daily Norditropin) not powered or intended for a formal non-inferiority claim — 2:1 randomization between once-weekly somapacitan and daily placebo, plus a separate open-label daily-Norditropin reference arm; 34-week double-blind main period followed by a 52-week open-label extension

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint change from baseline to Week 34 in truncal fat percentage (DXA-measured, truncal fat mass / [truncal fat mass + truncal lean body mass] × 100)

- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA (factors: GHD-onset type, sex, region, diabetes status, sex×region×diabetes interaction; covariate: baseline truncal fat%) applied after multiple imputation (100 imputed datasets, fixed seed) of post-withdrawal data, pooled via Rubin's rules; comparison vs. open-label Norditropin reported descriptively (estimate + CI only, explicitly not held to a non-inferiority margin or given a p-value) — *("Open-label active-reference arm reported descriptively without a non-inferiority margin, alongside a formally powered placebo-controlled comparison")*

- *Missing data/bias:* multiple imputation of a withdrawn subject's post-withdrawal trajectory from an ANCOVA model fit to the placebo arm only, explicitly designed to mimic "an intention-to-treat scenario where withdrawn subjects are assumed to be switched to no treatment (placebo) after withdrawal" (sponsor's SAP language); a formal tipping-point-style delta-shift sensitivity analysis for departures from missing-at-random was pre-specified — *("Multiple imputation of post-withdrawal trajectories using a placebo-arm-only reference model, i.e., a de facto ITT switch-to-placebo assumption")*

- *Regulatory:* FDA End-of-Phase-2 meeting minutes document a negotiated dispute over which missing-data method would serve as the *primary* (not merely sensitivity) analysis — FDA's preference for the placebo-referenced multiple-imputation approach as primary prevailed, with the sponsor's SAP as filed reflecting FDA's position; FDA's statistical reviewer additionally applied an unplanned Bayesian hierarchical shrinkage model to stabilize small-sample regional-subgroup estimates after the North America subgroup showed a treatment effect in the opposite direction from the overall result — *("FDA-conducted Bayesian hierarchical shrinkage model applied to regional/subgroup treatment-effect estimates to address small-sample instability")*

**Trial design & endpoints**

- REAL 1 randomized 301 adults with AGHD (2:1) to once-weekly somapacitan or daily placebo (both double-blind), with a separate open-label arm receiving daily Norditropin (FlexPro) as an active reference; 34-week double-blind main period, then a 52-week open-label extension in which all subjects received somapacitan

- Primary endpoint: change from baseline to Week 34 in truncal fat percentage (DXA); the primary objective was superiority of somapacitan over placebo, not non-inferiority to Norditropin

- Sample size determination assumed a true mean difference of 2.5 percentage points (SD 4.5%), two-sided two-sample t-test, α=0.05, 2:1 randomization, yielding a planned 104:52 allocation for 90% power (260 total planned, with a 7% dropout buffer bringing enrollment to 301)

- Primary analysis: multiple imputation (100 imputed datasets) of post-withdrawal data using an ANCOVA model fit to the placebo arm only (factors: GHD-onset type, sex, region, diabetes status, and the sex×region×diabetes interaction; covariate: baseline truncal fat%), pooled per Rubin's rules; superiority declared if the upper bound of the two-sided 95% CI for (somapacitan − placebo) fell below 0

- Reported result: treatment difference −1.41 percentage points, 95% CI (−2.61, −0.22), meeting statistical significance; the somapacitan-vs-Norditropin comparison showed a difference of 1.28 in the same direction (i.e., somapacitan numerically inferior to daily Norditropin on this endpoint), reported descriptively without a formal non-inferiority margin or hypothesis test

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2020/761156Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2020/761156s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID 4598661) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/761156Orig1s000StatR.pdf

The SAP's cover-page redaction stamp itself is corrupted by a different mechanism — a simple alphabetic (Caesar/ROT-3) letter shift — rendering as "Redacted VWDWLVWLFDODQDO\VLVSODQ," which decodes to "STATISTICALANALYSISPLAN"; this is confined to that one cover-page stamp and does not affect the body text.

**Other resources**

- No trial-specific IPD/dataset access program (Vivli, YODA, Project Data Sphere) independently confirmed for Novo Nordisk in this program

- No FDA advisory committee meeting identified for this BLA

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, ClinicalTrials.gov-posted Protocol/SAP, NCT02229851]* the primary analysis was pre-specified to impute a withdrawn subject's post-withdrawal data "assuming an intention to treat (ITT) scenario where withdrawn subjects are assumed to be switched to no treatment (placebo) after withdrawal," using an ANCOVA model fit to the placebo arm only, with 100 imputed datasets pooled per Rubin's rules

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Reference ID 4598661, Executive Summary]* "This BLA relies on a single efficacy study to support efficacy." / "The treatment difference appears small (less than 60% of the assumed effect of 2.5%...)" / "Somapacitan is statistically inferior to Norditropin, and the magnitude of the difference is almost as much as the difference between Somapacitan and Placebo."

- *[verbatim, FDA End-of-Phase-2 meeting minutes, quoted in the Statistical Review]* FDA: "We did not agree with your approach [of using the placebo-referenced multiple-imputation method only as a sensitivity analysis]... You agreed that you would follow the approach described in our preliminary comments" — documenting FDA's success in requiring the placebo-referenced MI method be used as the *primary*, not sensitivity, analysis, over the sponsor's initial written objection that it "does not find that the multiple imputation (MI) analysis would be the preferred primary analysis."

- **Reverse-engineered SAP** (for the Bayesian regional-subgroup shrinkage analysis, not itself part of the sponsor's pre-specified SAP): *[inferred]* the FDA reviewer's decision to apply a hierarchical shrinkage model to regional subgroup estimates is traceable to the Statistical Review's discussion of the North America subgroup showing a treatment effect in the direction opposite the overall result, a small-sample instability concern the reviewer addressed independently of the sponsor's pre-specified analysis plan.

### 10. Setmelanotide (Imcivree) — NDA 213793

**Sponsor:** Rhythm Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Chronic weight management in adult and pediatric patients 6 years of age and older with obesity due to pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC), proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 1 (PCSK1), or leptin receptor (LEPR) deficiency confirmed by genetic testing

**Approval date:** November 25, 2020

**Pivotal trial:** Study RM-493-012 (POMC/PCSK1 deficiency), NCT02896192, and Study RM-493-015 (LEPR deficiency), NCT03287960 — two identically designed single-arm, open-label, 1-year Phase 3 trials, each with an embedded 8-week double-blind, placebo-controlled withdrawal period

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single-arm, open-label, 1-year trial design in an ultra-rare genetically-defined population (matches "Small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population," Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1, seen in Lomitapide/Mipomersen/Metreleptin/Evinacumab-dgnb), with an embedded fixed-sequence double-blind placebo-controlled withdrawal period (4 weeks continued drug, then 4 weeks placebo, in that fixed order for every subject, not randomized) serving as a within-subject control absent any parallel comparator arm — *("Fixed-sequence double-blind placebo re-challenge window embedded within an open-label single-arm trial, providing a within-subject control without randomized withdrawal")*, distinct from the taxonomy's existing "Randomized-withdrawal enrichment design" (Pegvaliase/PRISM-2), where continuation vs. withdrawal is itself randomized among responders

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint proportion of patients achieving ≥10% weight loss from baseline at approximately 1 year (Full Analysis Set, "pivotal cohort" — patients with ≥1 year of therapeutic-dose treatment at data cutoff); key secondary endpoints: percent change in body weight and in weekly-average "most hunger" score at 1 year (Designated Use Set — subjects who entered the double-blind withdrawal period), and proportion of patients age ≥12 achieving ≥25% improvement in hunger score

- *Primary analysis:* one-sided exact binomial test (α=0.05) of the responder rate against a pre-specified historical reference rate of 5%, with a 90% Clopper-Pearson exact confidence interval for the observed proportion — statistical significance required the CI lower bound to exceed 5%, equivalent to at least 3 of 10 pivotal-cohort responders (matches "Exact binomial test against a pre-specified performance goal," Keyword_Taxonomy.md §3, seen in Technetium Tc 99m tilmanocept, Ibrutinib, Rucaparib, Copanlisib, Acalabrutinib); continuous key secondaries analyzed via a linear mixed model (fixed effect for time and baseline value, random effect for subject, compound-symmetry covariance) in the sponsor's primary analysis, with an FDA reviewer ANCOVA (final-visit outcome, baseline covariate) as a supporting analysis

- *Multiplicity:* pre-specified hierarchical testing procedure — after the primary endpoint reached significance, the three key secondary endpoints were tested in a fixed pre-specified order to control Type I error (fixed-sequence step-down testing, Keyword_Taxonomy.md §4)

- *Missing data/bias:* Study 015 (LEPR) imputed study-drug-related missingness as zero change from baseline (baseline-observation-carried-forward) and non-drug-related missingness via linear extrapolation; FDA's statistical reviewer ran two sensitivity analyses — an all-BOCF "worst case" treating every missing value as a non-responder, and a multiple-imputation (monotone regression) approach combined via Rubin's rule — both consistent with the primary conclusion; because neither trial had a concurrent parallel-arm control, the FDA reviewer explicitly noted "the treatment effect that is attributable to the drug cannot be accurately quantified," relying instead on the embedded double-blind withdrawal period (worsening on placebo, improvement on drug reinitiation) as within-subject corroborating evidence

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Both trials enrolled patients ≥6 years old with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m² if adult, ≥95th percentile if pediatric) and biallelic loss-of-function POMC/PCSK1 (Study 012) or LEPR (Study 015) mutations; approximately 10 patients per trial were planned for the "pivotal cohort" (≥1 year of therapeutic-dose treatment at data cutoff), with enrollment remaining open afterward for a supplemental cohort analyzed as a secondary population

- Design: 12 weeks open-label treatment, then patients achieving ≥5 kg (or ≥5% if baseline weight <100 kg) weight loss proceeded into an 8-week double-blind withdrawal period (4 weeks continued setmelanotide, 4 weeks placebo, fixed order, blinded to patients/investigators/sites), then resumed open-label treatment for an additional 32 weeks to complete 1 year

- Results: 8 of 10 (80%, 95% CI 44.4-97.5%) POMC/PCSK1 patients and 5 of 11 (45.5%, 95% CI 16.8-76.6%) LEPR patients achieved ≥10% weight loss at 1 year, both meeting the pre-specified statistical threshold against the 5% historical reference rate; treatment differences on all three key secondary endpoints were statistically significant at α=0.05 in both studies

- FDA's statistical reviewer treated the double-blind withdrawal period as the key internal-validity feature given the absence of a parallel control: body weight and hunger score increased during the 4-week placebo sub-period and decreased again after study drug was reinitiated, supporting a causal attribution to setmelanotide despite the single-arm design; the reviewer separately flagged that the hunger-score endpoint had no historical control data (unlike weight loss, for which historical natural-history comparator data existed) and that the outcome-assessment ("COA") team could not confirm the hunger-score instrument's construct validity given the small sample size

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID 4667988), Executive Summary]* "Both studies are single-arm, 1-year, and open-label except for a 8-week double-blind withdrawal period containing 4 weeks of placebo. The primary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of responders, defined as patients who demonstrated at least 10% weight reduction at approximately 1 year compared to baseline. It was compared to a historical reference response rate of 5% via an exact binomial test."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.2 Statistical Methodologies]* "Formal statistical hypothesis testing was performed on the primary and key secondary endpoints at 1-sided, 0.05 level of significance... A 90% confidence interval (CI) for the proportion of responders was obtained using the Clopper-Pearson (exact) method. Statistical significance is met if the lower bound of the CI larger than 5%. At least 3 responders out of 10 subjects is needed to achieve statistical significance."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.2]* "A pre-specified hierarchical testing procedure was used to control Type I error. After statistical significance was achieved for the primary endpoint, the three key secondary endpoints were tested in the order stated in Section 3.2.1."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Executive Summary]* "Despite the lack of a parallel control arm in these studies, the double-blind withdrawal period allowed each subject to serve as their own control... However, there was lack of historical control data for hunger score, making it difficult to assess the effect of setmelanotide on hunger score. Moreover, the COA team has difficulty confirming the construct validity of the instrument due to the small sample size of the studies."

### 11. Lonapegsomatropin-tcgd (Skytrofa) — BLA 761177

**Sponsor:** Ascendis Pharma Endocrinology Division A/S

**Indication approved:** Treatment of pediatric patients 1 year of age and older who weigh at least 11.5 kg with growth failure due to inadequate secretion of endogenous growth hormone (growth hormone deficiency, GHD)

**Approval date:** August 25, 2021

**Pivotal trial:** heiGHt Trial (Study CT-301), NCT02781727

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized (2:1), open-label, active-controlled (daily Genotropin) non-inferiority trial with a pre-specified superiority test to follow if non-inferiority was met (matches "Non-inferiority-then-superiority hierarchy," Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1, seen in EMPA-REG/DECLARE-TIMI58); prepubertal treatment-naive children with GHD, 52-week treatment period

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint annualized height velocity (AHV) at Week 52

- *Primary analysis:* non-inferiority margin of 2.0 cm/yr, tested one-sided at α=0.025 (non-inferiority declared if the lower bound of the two-sided 95% CI for [lonapegsomatropin − Genotropin] exceeded −2.0 cm), followed by a superiority test (lower bound >0) only if non-inferiority succeeded; ANCOVA (covariates: baseline age, log-transformed peak GH, baseline height SDS minus average parental height SDS; factors: treatment, gender) applied to 100 multiply-imputed datasets (missing-at-random assumption), pooled per standard MI combination rules

- *Missing data/bias:* multiple imputation (100 datasets, MAR) for missing AHV values, detailed in the SAP's imputation model, pooled via standard MI rules; familywise Type I error controlled at two-sided α=0.05

- *Regulatory:* FDA End-of-Phase-2 (April 26, 2016) and Type B (August 25, 2016) meetings required the sponsor to justify the proposed 2 cm/yr non-inferiority margin against historical Genotropin AHV data per FDA's non-inferiority draft guidance, which FDA later confirmed was adequate ("Your justification for the non-inferiority margin [2 cm/yr] is adequate," per FDA meeting correspondence quoted in the Statistical Review); FDA's review also identified and required resolution of an internal inconsistency between the SAP's stated one-sided 0.025 significance level and an earlier SAP draft's testing-hierarchy language, and required removal of an endpoint that had been placed in the key-secondary testing hierarchy without adequate justification

**Trial design & endpoints**

- heiGHt Trial: randomized 2:1, open-label (unblinded — daily injections vs. weekly injections precluded blinding), active-controlled trial of once-weekly lonapegsomatropin vs. daily Genotropin (somatropin) in 162 prepubertal, treatment-naive children with GHD (protocol targeted a minimum of 150), over 52 weeks

- Sample size determination assumed a standard deviation of 3.5 cm/yr for AHV and a non-inferiority margin of 2.0 cm, requiring N=147 (ITT) for 90% power at a one-sided α=0.025, with 2:1 randomization; 150 patients were targeted to allow for imbalance, and 162 were ultimately randomized

- Result: treatment difference +0.80 cm/yr in AHV at Week 52, 95% CI (0.13, 1.47), meeting both the pre-specified non-inferiority margin and the subsequent superiority test

- FDA's statistical reviewer concurred that lonapegsomatropin "achieves statistical significance for superiority over Genotropin" but cautioned in the Executive Summary that "the treatment difference is small and it is not clear that statistical superiority would be replicated in another study. This study on its own may not provide sufficient evidence for a determination of superiority to another approved drug" — the approval rested primarily on the non-inferiority finding, with superiority treated as supportive rather than as an independently reproduced claim

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID 4749627), Executive Summary]* "achieves statistical significance for superiority over Genotropin," but "the treatment difference is small and it is not clear that statistical superiority would be replicated in another study. This study on its own may not provide sufficient evidence for a determination of superiority to another approved drug."

### 12. Teplizumab-mzwv (Tzield) — BLA 761183

**Sponsor:** Provention Bio, Inc.

**Indication approved:** To delay the onset of clinical (Stage 3) type 1 diabetes in adults and pediatric patients 8 years of age and older with Stage 2 type 1 diabetes — the first FDA-approved disease-*delay* immunotherapy for type 1 diabetes, a genuinely novel approval category distinct from a treatment-of-established-disease claim

**Approval date:** November 17, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** TN-10, NCT01030861 — a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial conducted by the NIH-funded Type 1 Diabetes TrialNet Study Group (lead sponsor on ClinicalTrials.gov is NIDDK, not Provention Bio); PROTECT, NCT03875729, an ongoing Provention-sponsored trial, contributed only safety/bridging data (see below), not efficacy, to this approval

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* efficacy claim built entirely on a single externally-sponsored, investigator-initiated (NIH/TrialNet) trial that the BLA applicant did not design or run under its own IND oversight — *("BLA efficacy claim built on a single externally-sponsored/investigator-initiated trial not conducted under the applicant's own IND")* — FDA's statistical reviewer noted explicitly that "TN-10 was first brought to the FDA after study completion or near completion. Reviewer's knowledge on protocol changes are all based on the applicant's narrative"; randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, single 14-day drug course, event-driven follow-up (median 50.6 months) in autoantibody-positive, dysglycemic (Stage 2) relatives of type 1 diabetes patients age ≥8

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint time to clinical (Stage 3) type 1 diabetes diagnosis (per ADA diagnostic criteria via oral glucose tolerance testing or unequivocal hyperglycemia with acute metabolic decompensation) — *("Time to clinical diagnosis of a chronic disease [disease-delay, not disease-treatment] as the primary regulatory efficacy endpoint")*, a genuinely distinct endpoint construct from standard time-to-progression/time-to-death endpoints already in this taxonomy, since the "event" is a diagnostic threshold crossing in previously asymptomatic/pre-clinical subjects rather than a clinical deterioration or death in already-diagnosed patients

- *Primary analysis:* Cox proportional-hazards regression / log-rank framework on the primary time-to-diagnosis endpoint, with Kaplan-Meier estimation as the primary descriptive display; confirmatory evidence for the BLA was built from an FDA-reviewed, sponsor-conducted random-effects meta-analysis of 5 independently completed Stage-3 (new-onset) T1D trials using change in C-peptide AUC as a biomarker explicitly acknowledged as "not a validated surrogate endpoint for clinical benefit," approved on the basis that "literature reviews and inputs from some key opinion leaders suggest it may likely predict clinical benefit" and citing FDA's 1998 "Providing Clinical Evidence of Effectiveness" guidance standard

- *Missing data/bias:* FDA flagged "imbalances in prognostic factors at randomization" between TN-10 arms as a key statistical issue; sensitivity analyses addressing missing follow-up data and the baseline imbalance were reported as "similar to those in the primary analysis in effect size and significance level"

- *Regulatory:* original BLA submitted October 31, 2020; FDA's Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee met May 27, 2021 and voted 10-7 in favor of approval; a Complete Response Letter followed on July 2, 2021 — notably, this CRL concerned manufacturing/product-comparability issues (bridging the Eli Lilly-manufactured clinical-trial material used in TN-10 to the to-be-marketed AGC Biologics-manufactured product via a joint population-PK model and a blinded safety comparison drawing on the then-ongoing PROTECT trial), not a re-litigation of the TN-10 efficacy result or the AdCom's vote; Class 2 resubmission approved November 17, 2022

**Trial design & endpoints**

- TN-10 randomized 76 subjects (44 teplizumab : 32 placebo) with Stage 2 type 1 diabetes (≥2 diabetes-related autoantibodies plus abnormal OGTT glucose tolerance) age ≥8 to a single 14-day course of teplizumab or placebo, with event-driven follow-up to clinical (Stage 3) T1D diagnosis (median follow-up 50.6 months, range 9-88 months)

- Reported result: adjusted hazard ratio 0.41 (95% CI 0.22-0.79, p=0.0066) for progression to clinical diabetes; median time to diagnosis 49.5 months (teplizumab) vs. 24.9 months (placebo)

- Because PROTECT (the Provention-sponsored confirmatory trial) remained blinded and ongoing at both the original BLA submission and the 2022 resubmission, it could not and did not supply efficacy data for approval; instead, supportive/confirmatory evidence came from an FDA-reviewed meta-analysis of 5 independently conducted new-onset (Stage 3) T1D trials assessing C-peptide preservation, which the reviewer described as showing "notable heterogeneity" across trials (addressed via a random-effects model) and a statistically significant effect on 1-year C-peptide preservation that was not significant at 2 years

- FDA's Statistical/Medical Review documents a minor internal date inconsistency regarding the CRL (July 2, 2021 is stated in most places in the review; a reference to "Complete Response on November 2, 2020" also appears in one location) — the July 2, 2021 date is corroborated in multiple places and is treated here as the operative CRL date

- FDA Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee meeting held May 27, 2021 — voted 10-7 in favor of approval; the vote and efficacy debate preceded the subsequent Complete Response Letter, which concerned manufacturing/product-comparability issues rather than a re-examination of TN-10's efficacy result

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID 4818231)]* "TN-10 was first brought to the FDA after study completion or near completion. Reviewer's knowledge on protocol changes are all based on the applicant's narrative."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, on the confirmatory C-peptide meta-analysis]* "Change in C-peptide AUC is not a validated surrogate endpoint for clinical benefit... but literature reviews and inputs from some key opinion leaders suggest it may likely predict clinical benefit."

- **Reverse-engineered SAP** (for TN-10's exact statistical test specification, since the public FDA review presents headline results rather than the full pre-specified analytic detail): *[inferred]* the reported adjusted hazard ratio (0.41, 95% CI 0.22-0.79) and accompanying p-value (0.0066) are traceable to a stratified Cox proportional-hazards model consistent with a log-rank-type test of the primary time-to-diagnosis endpoint, standard for a TrialNet-sponsored prevention trial of this design, though the exact stratification factors and covariate adjustment set were not independently verified from a standalone SAP excerpt in this research pass.

### 13. Fezolinetant (Veozah) — NDA 216578

**Sponsor:** Astellas Pharma, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms (hot flashes) due to menopause

**Approval date:** May 12, 2023

**Pivotal trial:** SKYLIGHT 1, NCT04003155, and SKYLIGHT 2, NCT04003142 — two identically designed Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two identically designed randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, each with a 12-week placebo-controlled period followed by a non-controlled active-treatment extension; two doses (30 mg, 45 mg) tested in parallel against placebo in both trials, though the sponsor ultimately sought approval only for the 45 mg dose

- *Endpoints:* four co-primary efficacy endpoints per trial — change from baseline in mean frequency of moderate-to-severe vasomotor symptoms (VMS) at Week 4 and at Week 12, and change from baseline in mean severity of moderate-to-severe VMS at Week 4 and at Week 12 — each assessed via a daily electronic diary

- *Primary analysis:* mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM analysis of covariance) as pre-specified in the protocol for all four co-primary endpoints in both trials; regulatory review additionally applied a clinical-meaningfulness threshold alongside the formal statistical test — both doses needed to show a reduction in VMS frequency of at least 2 per day or 14 per week vs. placebo, in addition to statistical significance, to support a superiority claim — *("Responder/clinical-meaningfulness magnitude threshold applied jointly with a formal statistical test for a continuous co-primary endpoint")*, structurally similar in spirit to the dual statistical-and-clinical criterion used for omidenepag's non-inferiority claim (Entry 7, this batch) but applied here to a superiority claim on a co-primary continuous endpoint rather than a non-inferiority margin

- *Multiplicity:* no formal alpha-splitting or gatekeeping procedure across the four co-primary endpoints or the two doses was identified in the FDA Statistical Review; all eight dose-by-endpoint comparisons (2 doses × 4 co-primary endpoints) reached p<0.001 in both trials except two comparisons at p=0.009 and p=0.09 in one trial's severity endpoints

- *Regulatory:* approved with a boxed warning and label requirement for hepatic function/injury monitoring prior to treatment initiation and every 3 months during the first 9 months of therapy (at 3, 6, and 9 months), reflecting a hepatotoxicity signal identified in the clinical program; the sponsor additionally agreed to enhanced postmarketing pharmacovigilance for hepatic adverse events

**Trial design & endpoints**

- SKYLIGHT 1 (N=527) and SKYLIGHT 2 (N=501) randomized women with moderate-to-severe menopausal VMS to placebo, fezolinetant 30 mg, or fezolinetant 45 mg once daily for a 12-week double-blind period, stratified by smoking status, followed by a non-controlled extension

- Baseline VMS burden was similar across trials (~11 moderate-to-severe hot flashes/day, severity score ~2.4); at Week 12, LS mean differences from placebo in VMS frequency were −2.39 (30 mg) and −2.55 (45 mg) in SKYLIGHT 1, and −1.86 (30 mg) and −2.53 (45 mg) in SKYLIGHT 2 (all p<0.001 except the SKYLIGHT 2 30 mg comparison at p=0.019); severity endpoints showed a similar pattern, with all comparisons statistically significant except two at p=0.09 and p=0.501 (identified in the Statistical Review's efficacy tables)

- The Summary Review states the regulatory bar explicitly: "Astellas is requesting approval for only the 45 mg dose... both 30 mg and 45 mg were tested in phase 3 and both doses showed [a reduction] by at least 2 per day or 14 per week when compared to placebo at Weeks 4 and 12" — indicating both doses cleared the clinical-meaningfulness threshold even though only the 45 mg dose was submitted for approval

In addition, Astellas has agreed to enhanced pharmacovigilance to assess post-marketing adverse hepatic events."

### 14. Somatrogon-ghla (Ngenla) — BLA 761184

**Sponsor:** Pfizer Inc. (in collaboration with OPKO Health, Inc., which co-developed somatrogon/MOD-4023)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of pediatric patients ≥3 years of age with growth failure due to inadequate secretion of endogenous growth hormone (pediatric growth hormone deficiency, GHD)

**Approval date:** June 27, 2023 (resubmission; the original BLA received a Complete Response Letter on January 21, 2021)

**Pivotal trial:** Study CP-4-006 / C0311009 (NCT02968004), a Phase 3, randomized, open-label, active (Genotropin)-controlled, 52-week non-inferiority trial; supportive Phase 2 dose-finding study CP-4-004 and supportive Japanese Phase 3 trial CP-4-009 (published as a distinct dataset, no independently located NCT number)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* single adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 randomized, open-label, active-controlled, parallel-group non-inferiority trial (CP-4-006) plus confirmatory evidence resting on strong mechanistic understanding of the GH/IGF-1 pathway, rather than a second independent pivotal trial — FDA explicitly invoked the precedent that "historically, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has accepted a single adequate and well controlled trial for the approval of hGH products with native GH sequences for the pediatric GHD indication" because of the rarity of pediatric GHD (closest Keyword_Taxonomy.md term, "Small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population," describes an adjacent but distinct scenario — a single randomized non-inferiority trial substituting for two independent pivotal trials specifically on same-pharmacologic-class/mechanistic grounds is not currently catalogued); prior Complete Response Letter (January 21, 2021) for unresolved immunogenicity (anti-drug antibody, including neutralizing antibody) concerns plus quality deficiencies, resolved via a resubmission with additional long-term/immunogenicity data — not a new efficacy trial

- *Endpoints:* primary efficacy endpoint annualized height velocity (AHV) at 52 weeks; key secondary endpoints included AHV at 6 months, change in height standard deviation score (SDS) at 6 and 12 months, change in bone maturation at 12 months, and IGF-1/IGFBP-3 levels and SDS across visits; safety/immunogenicity endpoints (anti-drug antibody and neutralizing antibody incidence) were central to the review given the prior CRL

- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA model with treatment and gender as factors and screening peak GH level and height SDS as covariates; non-inferiority declared if the lower limit of the two-sided 95% CI for the mean difference (somatrogon minus Genotropin) exceeded a pre-specified margin of ≥ -1.8 cm/year

- *Missing data/bias:* not detailed as a distinct sensitivity-analysis section in the excerpted Multi-Discipline Review; immunogenicity was the dominant bias/safety concern rather than missing-data handling — 77% of subjects became ADA-positive during the main 12-month period of CP-4-006, with FDA's Division concluding no discernible impact of ADA/NAb positivity on growth (efficacy) outcomes during long-term follow-up

- *Regulatory:* Complete Response Letter issued January 21, 2021 (high rate/persistence of anti-drug antibodies and neutralizing antibodies, insufficient evidence of no efficacy impact, plus four quality-related deficiencies); resubmission included a Japanese Phase 3 bridging trial (CP-4-009) submitted at FDA's request during pre-BLA-resubmission discussions specifically to provide additional immunogenicity-vs-efficacy data; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held, per the Division's statement that this was "not the first drug in class" and raised no controversial issues warranting outside consultation

**Trial design & endpoints**

- CP-4-006: 224 treatment-naïve, pre-pubertal pediatric subjects with short stature due to GHD randomized 1:1 to weekly somatrogon (0.66 mg/kg/week) or daily Genotropin, followed by an open-label long-term extension (LT-OLE) for subjects completing the 52-week randomized comparison; supportive CP-4-009 randomized 44 Japanese pre-pubertal children 1:1 to the same regimens with a 12-month controlled period plus a single-arm open-label extension

- Reported primary result (CP-4-006): estimated treatment difference in mean AHV at week 52, somatrogon (10.07 cm/year) minus Genotropin (9.73 cm/year), was 0.34 cm/year (95% CI -0.23, 0.91); the CI lower bound (-0.23 cm/year) exceeded the pre-specified non-inferiority margin of ≥ -1.8 cm/year, so non-inferiority was declared; secondary/supportive results were consistent — height SDS at week 52 was 0.91 (somatrogon) vs. 0.86 (Genotropin), and IGF-1 SDS normalized in both arms (0.65 vs. -0.69)

- CP-4-009 (Japanese bridging trial) results: mean AHV at week 52, somatrogon 10.07 cm/year vs. Genotropin 9.73 cm/year, treatment difference 0.34 cm/year (95% CI -0.23, 0.91) — consistent with CP-4-006 and used to support that immunogenicity did not compromise growth outcomes in an independent (non-US) population

- FDA's immunogenicity review documented ADA positivity in the large majority of somatrogon-treated subjects (77% during the main 12-month CP-4-006 period; 64% of subjects who discontinued the OLE period prematurely were ADA-positive) and found no discernible correlation between neutralizing-antibody development and reduced growth response, concluding an "overall low risk of the impact of antibody on efficacy or safety"

- Study CP-4-004 (Phase 2, open-label, dose-finding, three somatrogon doses vs. Genotropin) provided supportive dose-selection evidence: growth-parameter changes were dose-dependent, and the highest dose tested (0.66 mg/kg/week, the dose carried into CP-4-006) produced growth changes similar to those later observed in the pivotal trial

- FDA Approval Letter (Corrected) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2023/761184Orig1s000Corrected_ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label (original, corrected, 2023) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2023/761184Orig1s000Corrected_lbl.pdf

- FDA Multi-Discipline Review (Reference ID: 5197623, incorporating prior-cycle reviews Reference IDs 4924352 and 4888851 from the original 2021 review cycle) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/761184Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (CP-4-006) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02968004

- Protocol / SAP — a genuine sponsor SAP is posted on ClinicalTrials.gov for Study CP-4-006, but the posted document (`SAP_002.pdf`, dated January 3, 2024) is specifically the Statistical Analysis Plan for the long-term open-label extension (LT-OLE) period, not the original 52-week randomized primary-endpoint comparison's SAP; it defines the LT-OLE estimand (treatment-policy strategy, all patients dosed in OLE regardless of intercurrent events) but does not restate the original non-inferiority analysis plan, which is instead documented (and quoted below) via the FDA Multi-Discipline Review's description of the Applicant's pre-specified analysis

- Pivotal publications: Deal CL, Steelman J, Vlachopapadopoulou E, et al. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1210/clinem/dgac220), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35405011/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Efficacy%20and%20Safety%20of%20Weekly%20Somatrogon%20vs%20Daily%20Somatropin%20in%20Children%20With%20Growth%20Hormone%20Deficiency%20A%20Phase%203%20Study) — and — Tanaka T, Yokoya S, Seino Y, et al. **Other resources**

- No trial-specific IPD/dataset access program (Vivli, YODA, Project Data Sphere) confirmed for this program; Pfizer more broadly participates in clinical-data-sharing initiatives but trial-specific availability was not individually confirmed

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting held, per the Multi-Discipline Review's explicit statement (Section 9)

- Orphan drug designation in effect (submission_property_type "Orphan" recorded in FDA's Drugs@FDA data for this BLA), consistent with the rare-disease (pediatric GHD) justification FDA cited for accepting a single pivotal trial

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review (Reference ID: 5197623), §1 Executive Summary]* "The Applicant provided substantial evidence of effectiveness of somatrogon for the treatment of pediatric subjects ≥3 years of age with growth failure due to growth hormone deficiency (GHD). This is based on data from one adequate and well-controlled phase 3 study CP-4-006, plus confirmatory evidence consisting of strong mechanistic support."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, §1]* "A single adequate and well-controlled trial plus confirmatory evidence is acceptable for this BLA because pediatric GHD is a rare disease. It is therefore challenging to conduct two adequate and well controlled trials, and, historically, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has accepted a single adequate and well controlled trial for the approval of hGH products with native GH sequences for the pediatric GHD indication."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, §1, describing CP-4-006's primary analysis]* "The primary efficacy endpoint was AHV after 12 months of treatment. The Applicant's prespecified analysis of the primary efficacy endpoint was performed using an analysis of covariance model. The model included treatment and gender as factors, and peak GH levels at screening and height SDS as covariates. Non-inferiority was to be establish if the lower limit of the two-sided 95% CI for mean difference 'somatrogon-Genotropin' in the primary analysis was ≥-1.8 cm/year."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, §1, on the CRL history]* "The original BLA submission received a complete response (CR) letter on January 21, 2021, because of a high rate and persistence of anti-drug antibody (ADA) formation and development of neutralizing antibodies with insufficient evidence that there was no impact on efficacy. In addition, four quality-related deficiencies were communicated in the CR letter."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, §9]* "No advisory committee meeting was held, as this was not the first drug in class, the application did not raise significant public health questions on the role of the biologic, and there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion."

- **Reverse-engineered SAP** (for elements of the original 52-week primary analysis not restated in the publicly posted LT-OLE SAP): *[inferred]* the four-attribute ICH E9(R1)-style estimand structure (population/variable/intercurrent-event handling/population-level summary) used in the posted LT-OLE SAP mirrors language likely carried over from the original CP-4-006 SAP's primary-endpoint estimand, since Pfizer's contemporaneous submissions (e.g., the Miebo GOBI/MOJAVE SAPs, above) show the same template-driven estimand format company-wide in this era; *[inferred]* the reviewer's statement that "results of secondary analyses were supportive" (height SDS, IGF-1 SDS) but were not part of a formal alpha-controlled hierarchical test is traceable to the absence of any stated multiplicity-adjustment procedure for CP-4-006's secondary endpoints in the Multi-Discipline Review, unlike the explicit hierarchical structures documented for the ophthalmology entries in this batch — consistent with a single-primary-endpoint non-inferiority design where secondary endpoints were treated as supportive/descriptive only.

### 15. Palopegteriparatide (Yorvipath) — NDA 216490

**Sponsor:** Ascendis Pharma Bone Diseases A/S (Ascendis Pharma)

**Indication approved:** Treatment of hypoparathyroidism in adults

**Approval date:** August 9, 2024 (resubmission; the original NDA received a Complete Response Letter on April 28, 2023, for critical product-quality deficiencies and device concerns — not efficacy)

**Pivotal trial:** PaTHway (Study TCP-304, NCT04701203), a Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial with an open-label extension; supportive Phase 2 trial TCP-201

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized (3:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial with a 26-week blinded treatment period followed by a 156-week open-label extension; randomization stratified by etiology of hypoparathyroidism (postsurgical vs. other) "as per FDA recommendation"; dose titrated (6-60 mcg/day, in 3 mcg increments no more than every 7 days) based on serum calcium, aiming for independence from conventional calcium/active-vitamin-D therapy; the trial permitted study-drug up-titration throughout the blinded period even though FDA had recommended a fixed-dose period specifically to assess persistence of effect — FDA accepted the deviation from its own recommendation because the responder definition already treated any late study-drug increase as a treatment failure (a documented instance of FDA accepting a sponsor's departure from an Agency design recommendation because a countervailing feature of the responder-endpoint definition addressed the Agency's underlying concern)

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint a multi-component composite responder definition at Week 26 requiring ALL of: albumin-adjusted serum calcium within normal range (8.3-10.6 mg/dL); independence from active vitamin D (all standing doses zero, PRN use ≤7 of the prior 28 days); independence from therapeutic calcium (average standing dose ≤600 mg/day, PRN use ≤7 of 28 days); and no increase in prescribed study-drug dose in the 4 weeks prior to Week 26; five ranked key secondary endpoints, all patient-reported outcomes: change from baseline in the Hypoparathyroidism Patient Experience Scale (HPES)-Symptom Physical and Cognitive domains, HPES-Impact Physical Functioning and Daily Life domains, and SF-36 v2.0 Physical Functioning subscale — the HPES is a de novo sponsor-developed PRO instrument whose content validity was the subject of extensive FDA psychometric review (concerns over patient incomprehension, double-barreled items, and measurement redundancy) predating the pivotal trial

- *Primary analysis:* Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test, stratified by the randomization factor (etiology), for the primary composite and other categorical endpoints; continuous key secondary endpoints analyzed via ANCOVA with unequal-variance/Satterthwaite degrees-of-freedom adjustment, covariates treatment, etiology, and baseline value

- *Multiplicity:* fixed sequential (fully hierarchical) testing of the primary endpoint, then the five key secondary endpoints in the pre-specified PRO-domain order above, each tested only if the prior endpoint reached significance; remaining secondary endpoints unadjusted

- *Missing data/bias:* for the primary endpoint, subjects with no Week-26 serum calcium value, or with >25% (>7 of 28 days) missing vitamin-D/calcium diary data in the 4 weeks before Week 26, were classified as nonresponders; key secondary (PRO) endpoint missing data were handled via a multiple-imputation model stratified by treatment group under a missing-at-random assumption; the primary endpoint's responder definition was itself a point of extended FDA-sponsor disagreement — FDA disagreed with the Applicant's allowance of limited PRN vitamin-D/calcium use within the responder definition and requested a post-hoc sensitivity analysis under a stricter FDA-recommended definition (no PRN use permitted, any missing diary data counted as nonresponse), which the sponsor ran and which showed a materially similar (though numerically lower) treatment effect

- *Regulatory:* Complete Response Letter, April 28, 2023, for CMC/device deficiencies (dose-delivery variability across the pen-injector's three presentations, inadequate pen-functionality/stability data, high batch-failure rate) — the clinical efficacy/safety findings underlying this entry were not the basis of the CRL and were essentially unchanged at resubmission; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was identified in the excerpted Multi-Discipline Review text; FDA's End-of-Phase-2 advice letter (December 16, 2020) had explicitly flagged that "the proposed single phase 3 trial of 76 subjects may not provide statistically persuasive efficacy results," reflecting the rare-disease constraint on trial size, similar to this batch's somatrogon entry but for hypoparathyroidism rather than pediatric GHD

**Trial design & endpoints**

- 106 subjects were screened (22 screen failures, mostly for the TSH inclusion criterion); 84 were randomized (63 palopegteriparatide, 21 placebo) at 21 sites across 7 countries; 82 were included in the efficacy/safety analyses (2 randomized-but-untreated palopegteriparatide subjects excluded); sample size (76 planned) assumed a 70% palopegteriparatide vs. 15% placebo response rate and provided ~99% power at two-sided alpha 0.05 (95% power at alpha 0.01)

- Population: median age 48.5 years (range 19-78), 78.0% female, 92.7% White, 85.4% postsurgical hypoparathyroidism etiology; baseline demographics were generally balanced except for a higher proportion of premenopausal women in placebo (83.3%) vs. palopegteriparatide (58.7%)

- Primary result (Applicant-defined responder definition): 78.7% (48/61) palopegteriparatide vs. 4.8% (1/21) placebo achieved Week-26 response, difference 74.0% (95% CI 60.4, 87.6; p<0.0001); under FDA's stricter post-hoc responder definition (no PRN use permitted, any missing diary data = nonresponse), the response rate was 73.8% (45/61) vs. 4.8% (1/21), difference 69.1% (95% CI 54.9, 83.2; p<0.0001) — a materially similar, nominally significant conclusion under both definitions

- Individual responder components under the FDA-recommended definition: serum calcium within normal range 80.3% vs. 47.6% (difference 32.7%, p=0.0044); vitamin-D independence 95.1% vs. 23.8% (difference 71.3%, p<0.0001); calcium independence 86.9% vs. 4.8% (difference 82.2%, p<0.0001); no study-drug dose increase 93.4% vs. 57.1% (difference 36.4%, p<0.0001); FDA's reviewer concluded the primary result was "robust" across both responder-definition variants and attributed the placebo arm's relatively low serum-calcium-in-range rate (47.6%) partly to protocol-mandated down-titration of background calcium/vitamin-D therapy whenever a placebo subject's serum calcium normalized, a mechanistic feature of the trial design rather than a bias artifact

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review (Reference ID: 5427853/5165921), §6.2.2.3, Sample Size Justification]* "A sample size of 76 was planned to have approximately 99% power at two-sided alpha of 0.05, and 95% power at two-sided alpha of 0.01, to demonstrate a statistically significant difference between palopegteriparatide and placebo for the primary endpoint at 26 weeks. The sample size justification assumed a randomization ratio of 3:1 to palopegteriparatide versus placebo, a response rate of 70% for palopegteriparatide and 15% for placebo, and a 10% dropout rate."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, §6.2.2.3, Multiplicity Adjustment]* "The primary and key secondary endpoints were tested sequentially in the following prespecified order: 1. Primary endpoint[;] 2. Key secondary endpoint 1: HPES-Symptom Physical domain score[;] 3. Key secondary endpoint 2: HPES-Symptom Cognitive domain score[;] 4. Key secondary endpoint 3: HPES-Impact Physical Functioning domain score[;] 5. Key secondary endpoint 4: HPES-Impact Daily Life domain score[;] 6. Key secondary endpoint 5: SF-36 v2.0-Physical Functioning subscale score. The remaining secondary endpoints were not adjusted for multiplicity."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, §6.2.2.1, on the FDA-vs-Applicant responder-definition dispute]* "FDA disagreed with allowance of PRN doses of vitamin D and calcium supplements during the last 4 weeks as part of the responder definition to support the proposed indication of treatment of hypoparathyroidism. FDA recommended that subjects who require any PRN doses of calcium or vitamin D, or with missing data during the 4 weeks prior to Week 26 should also be classified as nonresponders. FDA agreed with the Applicant's plan to submit results of a post-hoc sensitivity analysis of the primary efficacy endpoint, which included a responder definition consistent with FDA recommendations."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, §1 Executive Summary, on the original CRL]* "The Applicant (Ascendis Pharma) submitted this complete response for the New Drug Application (NDA) for Palopegteriparatide, under 21 CFR 314.110(b)(1). The original NDA submission received a Complete Response letter on April 28, 2023, due to critical product quality deficiencies and device concerns."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Discipline Review, §9 Product Quality, original review cycle]* "The Office of Pharmaceutical Quality (OPQ) recommends a Complete Response action. From the chemistry, manufacturing, and controls (CMC)/quality perspective, there are currently unresolved deficiencies concerning a) significant variability of the delivered dose, a product critical quality attribute, b) lack of adequate data to support feasibility of revised assay, pen functionality, and delivered dose specifications, c) high-level of batch failure, indicative of inadequate formulation and device design, and d) inadequate stability data to support shelf-life determination of the product per revised specification for the delivered dose."

### 16. Crinecerfont (Crenessity) — NDA 218808/218820

**Sponsor:** Neurocrine Biosciences, Inc.

**Indication approved:** "CRENESSITY is indicated as adjunctive treatment to glucocorticoid replacement to control androgens in adults and pediatric patients 4 years of age and older with classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH)" (verbatim, FDA-approved label)

**Approval date:** December 13, 2024

**Pivotal trial:** CAHtalyst Adult (Study NBI-74788-CAH3003, NCT04490915, N=182) and CAHtalyst Pediatric (Study CAH2006, NCT04806451, N=103) — both Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of crinecerfont (a corticotropin-releasing factor type 1 receptor antagonist) added to existing glucocorticoid therapy

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with an unblinded interim analysis using the "promising zone" adaptive sample-size re-estimation method (Mehta and Pocock, 2011), managed by an Independent Statistical Committee (ISC) and a Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) with access to the Adaptation Plan restricted to a firewalled subset of sponsor staff — closest existing taxonomy term is "Adaptive seamless enrollment with a conditional-power enrollment gate" (Harvoni/ION-1), but that entry describes a simple stop/continue enrollment gate rather than a promising-zone conditional-power-driven sample-size increase (Stage 1 sample fixed at ~76 subjects/46% of planned N, Stage 2 sample size increased up to 210 subjects depending on interim conditional power) — flagged **("Promising-zone adaptive sample-size re-estimation (Mehta-Pocock)")**; adjunctive add-on design (both arms continued background glucocorticoid therapy)

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint (adult trial) percent change from baseline in glucocorticoid daily dose at Week 24 among subjects with androstenedione controlled (≤120% of baseline or ≤ULN); primary endpoint (pediatric trial) change from baseline to Week 4 in androstenedione; key secondary endpoints include change in androstenedione at Week 4 (adult), achievement of a physiologic glucocorticoid dose (≤11 mg/m2/day hydrocortisone-equivalent, adjusted for BSA), and change in 17-hydroxyprogesterone

- *Primary analysis:* the promising-zone method's stagewise test statistics (Z1, Z2) combined per the pre-specified final-analysis adjustment, requiring no significance-level penalty for the interim look; ANCOVA-type modeling of percent-change and change-from-baseline endpoints

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence hierarchical testing (primary endpoint, α=0.05) → first 2 key secondary endpoints tested at unequal, pre-allocated one-sided-equivalent significance levels (0.02 and 0.03) → remaining key secondary endpoints tested via the Holm (1979) procedure, with the family-wise significance level for that remaining family made *dependent* on whether the first 2 key secondaries were significant (Wiens 2003) — an extension of "Bonferroni-Holm sequentially rejective procedure" in Keyword_Taxonomy.md with an unequal-allocation, result-dependent-alpha twist not previously captured — flagged **("Result-dependent Holm procedure with unequal alpha allocation (Wiens 2003)")**

- *Missing data/bias:* subjects classified as Completers / Retrieved Dropouts / Non-retrieved Dropouts / On-Drug-Missing-Endpoint per a pre-specified taxonomy, each handled by a different multiple-imputation rule (100 imputed datasets, SAS PROC MI, seed 1234); two-way tipping-point sensitivity analyses for the primary endpoint

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held ("An advisory committee meeting was not convened for this application because we determined that the application did not raise efficacy, safety, or other issues requiring input from external experts" — FDA Integrated Review)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- CAHtalyst Adult (CAH3003): adults with classic CAH on stable glucocorticoid therapy randomized to crinecerfont or placebo, added on to existing glucocorticoid regimen, for a 24-week double-blind period; randomization stratified factors not fully extracted from the posted SAP excerpt reviewed, but sample size (165, expandable to 210) was powered around a mean percent-change treatment difference in glucocorticoid dose

- CAHtalyst Pediatric (CAH2006): pediatric patients (4 years and older) with classic CAH, randomized double-blind placebo-controlled design with a 4-week primary hormonal endpoint (androstenedione) and a longer glucocorticoid-dose-reduction endpoint at Week 28

- Reported adult trial results (per pivotal publication/FDA review): glucocorticoid daily dose reduced by a least-squares mean of -27% (SE 2.4) with crinecerfont vs. -10% (SE 3.2) with placebo, LS-mean difference -17% (95% CI -24, -10); androstenedione change at Week 4 favored crinecerfont by -366 ng/dL (95% CI -457, -232); physiologic-glucocorticoid-dose responder rate 63% (crinecerfont) vs. 18% (placebo)

- Reported pediatric trial results: androstenedione change at Week 4 favored crinecerfont by -268 ng/dL (95% CI -403, -132); glucocorticoid-dose percent change at Week 28 favored crinecerfont by -24% (95% CI -30, -17)

- Interim analysis mechanics (verbatim from the posted SAP, Section 5.1): "An unblinded interim analysis on the primary endpoint using the 'promising zone' method (Mehta and Pocock, 2011) will be conducted when approximately the first 76 subjects (approximately 46% of the planned number of enrolled subjects) have had the opportunity to complete the Week 24 assessments... The DMC will assess futility and consider sample size re-estimation based on the observed treatment effect and the conditional power at the time of the interim analysis," with a four-zone decision rule (Futility / Unfavorable / Promising [sample size increased up to 210] / Favorable) based on conditional power thresholds CPmin/CPmax kept confidential from the unblinded review team outside the ISC/DMC/named biostatisticians

### 17. Paltusotine (Palsonify) — NDA 219070

**Sponsor:** Crinetics Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of acromegaly, in patients who have had an inadequate response to surgery and/or radiation, or for whom surgery and/or radiation are not an option (per FDA-approved label)

**Approval date:** September 25, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** PATHFNDR-1 ("Trial 09" in the FDA review, NCT04837040, N=58) and PATHFNDR-2 ("Trial 08," NCT05192382, N=111) — two Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of paltusotine (an oral nonpeptide somatostatin receptor ligand), each in a distinct acromegaly population

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials — PATHFNDR-2 (Trial 08) enrolled medically naive, previously-treated, and washout subgroups (24-week randomized-control phase) while PATHFNDR-1 (Trial 09) enrolled only subjects previously biochemically controlled on injectable somatostatin analogs, testing paltusotine as maintenance therapy after a washout (36-week randomized-control phase); both followed by an open-label extension; note both trials' ClinicalTrials.gov records show overall status "Terminated," but this reflects early administrative closure of the post-approval open-label-extension follow-up for business reasons in 2026, not a failure of the randomized-controlled primary-endpoint phase (which completed normally in 2023-2024 and is the basis for approval)

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint (both trials) responder rate — biochemical response/maintenance in IGF-1 (≤1.0×ULN) at end of the randomized-control phase (Week 24 for PATHFNDR-2, Week 36 for PATHFNDR-1); key secondary (PATHFNDR-2) change from baseline in IGF-1; other secondaries include proportion achieving IGF-1 <1.3×ULN, growth-hormone <1 ng/mL, and Acromegaly Symptoms Diary (ASD) total score change

- *Primary analysis:* exact logistic regression model (treatment group as factor, prior-treatment-strata covariate) for the binary primary/key-secondary endpoints, with 95% CI via the Miettinen-Nurminen method; ANCOVA (treatment, strata, baseline covariate) for continuous secondary endpoints

- *Multiplicity:* fixed-sequence hierarchical testing — primary → key secondary → remaining secondary endpoints tested in a pre-specified order, "to control the family-wise Type I error rate" (FDA Integrated Review)

- *Missing data/bias:* subjects with missing IGF-1 at both assessment timepoints, or who discontinued treatment, required rescue therapy, or up-titrated dose after a pre-specified cutoff, were counted as nonresponders for the binary primary endpoint (a non-responder-imputation rule); sensitivity analyses used multiple imputation based on on-treatment placebo-arm values for both trials, consistent with the primary conclusions

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held; Orphan Drug designation granted July 7, 2020

**Trial design & endpoints**

- PATHFNDR-2 (Trial 08): 209 subjects screened, 111 randomized (54 paltusotine, 57 placebo) across three eligibility groups — medically naive (IGF-1 ≥1.3×ULN, untreated), previously treated (IGF-1 ≥1.3×ULN after ≥4 months off treatment), and washout (biochemically controlled on octreotide/lanreotide monotherapy, then developed a ≥30% IGF-1 rise to ≥1.1×ULN after washout); randomization stratified by prior-treatment status (naive/previously-treated vs. washout); starting dose 20 mg/day titratable to 60 mg/day

- PATHFNDR-1 (Trial 09): 115 subjects screened, 58 randomized (30 paltusotine, 28 placebo), all previously biochemically controlled (IGF-1 ≤1×ULN) on stable-dose octreotide LAR or lanreotide, randomized 1:1 after washout to paltusotine or placebo for a 36-week maintenance-phase; randomization stratified by screening IGF-1 (<0.86×ULN vs. ≥0.86×ULN) and prior treatment (lanreotide vs. octreotide); starting dose 40 mg/day, up-titratable to 60 mg/day through Week 24

- PATHFNDR-2 primary result: 55.6% (30/54) paltusotine vs. 5.3% (3/57) placebo achieved IGF-1 ≤1.0×ULN at Week 24 (treatment difference 50.3%, 95% CI 35.1-63.8, p<0.0001); stratum-level sensitivity analysis showed the washout subgroup had the largest effect (92.9% vs. 13.3%, p<0.0001) and the medically-naive subgroup the smallest (22.7% vs. 4.2%, p=0.1509)

- PATHFNDR-1 primary result: 83.3% (25/30) paltusotine vs. 3.6% (1/28) placebo maintained IGF-1 ≤1.0×ULN at Week 36 (treatment difference 79.8%, 95% CI 59.8-90.5, p<0.0001); 60.7% of placebo-arm subjects required rescue therapy/discontinued vs. 6.7% of paltusotine-arm subjects

- Key secondary ASD total-score result (PATHFNDR-2): LS-mean change -2.67 (paltusotine) vs. +2.75 (placebo), difference -5.4 (95% CI -9.07, -1.78, p=0.0039)

### 18. Elinzanetant (Lynkuet) — NDA 219469

**Sponsor:** Bayer HealthCare Pharmaceuticals Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms due to menopause (per FDA-approved label)

**Approval date:** October 24, 2025

**Pivotal trial:** OASIS 1 (NCT05042362, N=396), OASIS 2 (NCT05099159, N=400), and OASIS 3 (NCT05030584, N=628) — three Phase 3, randomized, quadruple/double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of elinzanetant (a neurokinin-1,3 receptor antagonist); OASIS 1 and 2 were 26-week identically designed efficacy trials, OASIS 3 a 52-week supportive/safety trial with a single primary endpoint

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two identically protocoled randomized, quadruple-blind (participant/care-provider/investigator/outcomes-assessor), placebo-controlled, parallel efficacy trials (OASIS 1, OASIS 2) plus a third supportive/longer-duration double-blind placebo-controlled trial (OASIS 3) without subgroup-analysis or key-secondary-endpoint testing, all stratified by region (US vs. rest of world)

- *Endpoints:* four coprimary efficacy endpoints in OASIS 1/2 — mean change from baseline in frequency and in severity of moderate-to-severe hot flashes, each assessed at Week 4 and Week 12 via a daily Hot Flash Diary; OASIS 3's single primary endpoint was change in hot-flash frequency at Week 12; three key secondary endpoints in OASIS 1/2 (PROMIS Sleep Disturbance SF 8b, MENQOL total score, and — implicitly gated — further scales)

- *Primary analysis:* mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) with treatment, week, and region as factors, baseline VMS frequency/severity as covariate, and treatment-by-week and baseline-by-week interactions, using the Kenward-Roger approximation for denominator degrees of freedom, under a treatment-policy strategy (all randomized subjects analyzed regardless of treatment interruption or prohibited-medication use)

- *Multiplicity:* within each study, superiority on **all four** coprimary endpoints was required to claim study success, each tested at a one-sided 2.5% significance level, so the study-wise Type I error was controlled at one-sided 2.5% without further correction across the four endpoints (a co-primary "all evaluated must succeed" gate, extending the existing Keyword_Taxonomy.md "Co-primary endpoints" term to a four-endpoint, single-study, all-must-pass structure — closest prior example DECLARE-TIMI58's two-endpoint dual-primary is a smaller-scale version) — flagged **(proposed refinement of existing term: "Co-primary endpoints" to cover a 4-endpoint all-must-succeed structure)**

- *Missing data/bias:* nonmonotone and monotone missing data multiply imputed via Monte Carlo Markov Chain methods (500 imputed datasets per study, combined via Rubin's Rule) under a missing-at-random assumption; sensitivity analyses included an unimputed MMRM (SA1, performed post hoc at FDA's request), a tipping-point analysis (SA2, delta-adjustments applied only to the elinzanetant arm's imputed values), and two supplementary censoring-based estimands addressing COVID-19-related and other intercurrent events differently

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held ("An advisory committee meeting was not held to discuss this application because there were no considerations that warranted a discussion at an advisory committee meeting" — FDA Integrated Review)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- OASIS 1 (N=396: 199 elinzanetant 120 mg, 197 placebo) and OASIS 2 (N=400: 200/200) randomized postmenopausal women 40-65 years with moderate-to-severe vasomotor symptoms to elinzanetant 120 mg once daily or placebo for 26 weeks; OASIS 3 (N=628: 313/315) used the same design over 52 weeks as a longer-term supportive/safety study

- Baseline mean frequency of moderate-to-severe hot flashes was 13-16 episodes/day across the trials; FDA's Division applies a "14/2 criteria" — reduction of at least 2 episodes/day (14/week) beyond placebo, at both Week 4 and Week 12 — as its threshold for clinically meaningful benefit, separate from statistical significance

- OASIS 1/2 primary results: frequency reduction favored elinzanetant over placebo at Week 4 (difference -3.29, 95% CI -4.47 to -2.10, OASIS 1; -3.04, 95% CI -4.40 to -1.68, OASIS 2; both p<0.0001) and at Week 12 (difference -3.22, 95% CI -4.81 to -1.63, OASIS 1; -3.24, 95% CI -4.60 to -1.88, OASIS 2; both p<0.0001), meeting both the statistical and the Division's clinical-meaningfulness threshold
