### 19. Navepegritide (Yuviwel) — NDA 219164

**Sponsor:** Ascendis Pharma Growth Disorders A/S (Ascendis Pharma Endocrinology, Inc., U.S. applicant)

**Indication approved:** "YUVIWEL is indicated to increase linear growth in pediatric patients 2 years of age and older with achondroplasia with open epiphyses. This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on an improvement in annualized growth velocity" (verbatim, FDA-approved label) — **correction to task brief:** navepegritide/Yuviwel is a C-type natriuretic peptide (CNP) analog for **achondroplasia**, not growth hormone deficiency; it is a distinct Ascendis asset (TransCon CNP) from the company's growth-hormone-deficiency product lonapegsomatropin (TransCon hGH/Skytrofa)

**Approval date:** February 27, 2026 (accelerated approval; priority review; orphan drug designation)

**Pivotal trial:** ApproaCH (Trial ASND0036 in the FDA review; "Trial 1" in the label; NCT05598320, N=84) — a Phase 2b/3, multicenter, quadruple-masked, randomized (2:1), placebo-controlled, 52-week trial of once-weekly subcutaneous navepegritide in treatment-naive children with genetically confirmed achondroplasia, followed by a single-arm open-label extension

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized (2:1), quadruple-masked, placebo-controlled parallel trial with a 52-week double-blind period followed by an OLE; accelerated approval on a surrogate growth endpoint in a pediatric rare-disease population

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint annualized growth velocity (AGV) at Week 52; multiplicity-controlled secondary endpoints included change from baseline in achondroplasia-specific height Z-score, SF-10 Physical Health Summary (age ≥5 only), and three Achondroplasia Child Experience Measure (ACEM) domains (Physical Functioning, Daily Living Functioning, Observable Signs Measure); CDC-based (general-population) height Z-score was evaluated outside the multiple-testing strategy

- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA model (AGV as response; treatment, baseline age, baseline height Z-score, and randomization strata as covariates), using unequal-variance ("Satterthwaite-type") assumptions to account for the 2:1 randomization ratio

- *Multiplicity:* graphical multiple-testing procedure (Maurer-Bretz-family approach, per the SAP's Figure 2/Figure 8) allocating and propagating alpha across the primary AGV endpoint and five secondary endpoints — reuses the existing Keyword_Taxonomy.md term "Graphical alpha-propagation method (Maurer-Bretz)" (previously seen in Camizestrant/SERENA-6); add navepegritide/ApproaCH to "Seen in"

- *Missing data/bias:* ICH E9(R1)-style mixed intercurrent-event strategy — treatment-policy strategy for subjects who withdrew from trial drug but continued follow-up; hypothetical strategy for subjects who withdrew entirely or underwent growth-affecting surgical intervention; missing Week-52 height imputed via multiple imputation using retrieved-dropout data from the same arm when ≥5 such subjects existed, otherwise via copy-reference imputation from the placebo group

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held ("An advisory committee meeting was not held for this application as it did not raise efficacy, safety, benefit/risk, or other issues needing public input" — FDA Integrated Review); accelerated approval, so continued approval is contingent on confirmatory verification of clinical benefit

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ApproaCH (ASND0036/NCT05598320) enrolled 84 treatment-naive pediatric patients (mean age 5.7 years, range 2-12) with genetically confirmed achondroplasia; 57 received navepegritide 0.1 mg/kg subcutaneously once weekly, 27 received placebo, for 52 weeks

- Sample size (52 navepegritide : 26 placebo planned) was powered at ~90% to detect a 1.2 cm/year AGV treatment difference at a 2-sided alpha of 0.05, assuming a common SD of 1.5 cm/year

- Primary result: AGV of 5.9 cm/year (navepegritide) vs. 4.4 cm/year (placebo), LS-mean treatment difference 1.5 cm/year (95% CI 1.0, 1.9), p<0.0001; achondroplasia-specific height Z-score improved by 0.3 (95% CI 0.2, 0.4) vs. 0.0, p<0.0001; the CDC-based (general-population) height Z-score result (0.3, 95% CI 0.1-0.5) was explicitly reported as analyzed outside the pre-specified multiple-testing strategy and therefore descriptive only

- Subgroup consistency: treatment difference in AGV was 1.0 cm/year in children <5 years and 1.8 cm/year in children ≥5 years, with improvements observed across all predefined subgroups (age, sex, region)

- Long-term/supportive evidence: all 57 patients from a separate 52-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2 dose-finding trial (Trial 2, NCT04085523) entered a single-arm OLE and maintained AGV improvement through 2 years of navepegritide treatment

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2026/219164Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/219164Orig1s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Integrated Review (combined statistical/clinical review) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/219164Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05598320 (ApproaCH); no protocol/SAP posted

- Pivotal publication: Savarirayan R, McDonnell C, Bacino CA, et al. Once-Weekly Navepegritide in Children With Achondroplasia: The APPROACH Randomized Clinical Trial. *JAMA Pediatr*. 2026;180(1):18-25. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1001/jamapediatrics.2025.4771), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41247754/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Once-Weekly%20Navepegritide%20in%20Children%20With%20Achondroplasia%20The%20APPROACH%20Randomized%20Clinical%20Trial)

**Other resources**

- No trial-specific IPD/dataset access program (Vivli, YODA, Project Data Sphere) confirmed for Ascendis

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting held; a companion trial, COACH (published *Eur J Endocrinol* 2026), evaluated navepegritide combined with lonapegsomatropin in achondroplasia but is not part of this NDA's approval basis

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.2.3, Statistical Analysis Plan, Trial ASND0036]* "A sample size of 52 in the navepegritide group and 26 in the placebo group provided approximately 90% power to detect a treatment difference in AGV of 1.2 cm/year, assuming a 2-sided significance level of 0.05, and a common standard deviation of 1.5 cm/year."

- *[verbatim, same section, Handling of Intercurrent Events and Missing Data]* "Participants with missing height data at Week 52 had missing height measurements (cm) imputed by a multiple imputation method. The multiple imputation of the missing measurements of non-retrieved dropouts was based on known measurements from retrieved dropouts in the same treatment group... If there was an insufficient number of retrieved dropouts, a copy reference imputation method was used where the off-treatment missing data was imputed based on the model built from the placebo group."

- *[verbatim, same section, Analysis Method]* "The primary analysis of the primary endpoint was an ANCOVA model, with AGV at Week 52 as the response variable, and treatment (navepegritide versus placebo), baseline age, baseline height Z-score and strata as covariates. Given a randomization ratio of 2:1 (navepegritide versus placebo), the ANCOVA model assuming unequal variances was used to account for possible unequal residual variance."

- *[verbatim, FDA Integrated Review, §11]* "An advisory committee meeting was not held for this application as it did not raise efficacy, safety, benefit/risk, or other issues needing public input."

### 20. Relacorilant (Lifyorli) — NDA 220641

**Sponsor:** Corcept Therapeutics Incorporated

**Indication approved:** "LIFYORLI is a glucocorticoid receptor antagonist indicated in combination with nab-paclitaxel for the treatment of adults with platinum-resistant epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer who have received one to three prior systemic treatment regimens, at least one of which included bevacizumab" (verbatim, FDA-approved label) — **major correction to task brief:** NDA 220641/LIFYORLI is verified via the FDA label and approval letter to be approved for **platinum-resistant ovarian cancer in combination with nab-paclitaxel**, not Cushing's syndrome as stated in the assignment brief. Corcept has a separate, long-running relacorilant development program for Cushing's syndrome (the GRACE trial), but that program's regulatory status/application number was not verified in this research and is not the subject of this entry. This entry documents the verified, actually-approved NDA 220641/ovarian-cancer indication; the census compiler should confirm whether a separate Cushing's-syndrome entry is warranted under a different application number

**Approval date:** March 25, 2026

**Pivotal trial:** ROSELLA (Trial CORT125134-556, NCT05257408, N=381) — a Phase 3, multicenter, open-label, randomized, active-controlled, two-arm trial of relacorilant plus nab-paclitaxel vs. nab-paclitaxel alone in platinum-resistant epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized (1:1), open-label, active-controlled, two-arm add-on trial (relacorilant + nab-paclitaxel vs. nab-paclitaxel alone), stratified by number of prior lines of therapy (1 vs. >1) and region (North America vs. Europe vs. Korea/Australia/Latin America); dual primary endpoints with a group-sequential alpha-recycling structure

- *Endpoints:* dual primary endpoints — progression-free survival (PFS) by blinded independent central review (BICR, RECIST v1.1) and overall survival (OS); study declared positive if either primary endpoint reached significance

- *Primary analysis:* stratified log-rank test for both PFS and OS; stratified Cox proportional-hazards model (treatment arm as the only main effect, stratification factors as strata) for hazard ratios; Kaplan-Meier estimation with Brookmeyer-Crowley CIs for medians; Greenwood's-formula CIs for event-free rates at fixed timepoints

- *Multiplicity:* group sequential weighted Holm procedure across the dual primary endpoints — PFS tested at 2-sided α=0.04, OS allocated 2-sided α=0.01 at trial design, with OS re-tested at α=0.05 (Holm-recycled) if PFS was rejected; OS itself used a group-sequential Haybittle-Peto-boundary interim analysis (conducted at the time of the PFS primary analysis, spending α=0.0001) with the remaining α=0.0499 reserved for the OS final analysis — reuses "Alpha recycling" and "Haybittle-Peto boundary" from Keyword_Taxonomy.md but combines them with a group sequential weighted Holm dual-primary structure not previously catalogued together — flagged **("Group sequential weighted Holm procedure for dual primary endpoints with Haybittle-Peto-spent OS interim analysis")**

- *Missing data/bias:* detailed pre-specified PFS censoring-rule hierarchy (censored at randomization if no baseline/post-baseline assessment; at last adequate assessment if no BICR-documented progression; special rules for ≥2 consecutive missed scheduled assessments, keyed to assessment-window length); no OS-specific censoring beyond standard last-contact-date censoring for patients alive at cutoff

- *Regulatory:* FDA explicitly told the Applicant (February and May 2025) that a ~1-month PFS improvement without a statistically significant OS improvement would likely not be "clinically meaningful" or adequate for approval in this add-on setting, and recommended awaiting final OS data before submitting; the Applicant submitted the NDA anyway using the positive final-PFS/interim-OS data, with final OS data submitted later during review — not referred to an Oncology Drugs Advisory Committee meeting

**Trial design & endpoints**

- ROSELLA randomized 381 patients (188 relacorilant + nab-paclitaxel, 193 nab-paclitaxel alone); relacorilant 150 mg given orally the day before, day of, and day after each nab-paclitaxel infusion (80 mg/m2 relacorilant-arm dose vs. 100 mg/m2 in the nab-paclitaxel-alone arm, on Days 1/8/15 of 28-day cycles); all patients had received prior bevacizumab, 61% a prior PARP inhibitor, up to three prior systemic lines permitted

- PFS-by-BICR result (pre-specified final analysis): median 6.5 months (relacorilant arm) vs. 5.5 months (control), HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.54, 0.91), 2-sided log-rank p=0.0076 (compared against the pre-allocated α=0.04 significance threshold)

- OS result (pre-specified final analysis): median 16.0 months vs. 11.9 months, HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.51, 0.83), 2-sided log-rank p=0.0004 (compared against the recycled α=0.0499 threshold) — both dual-primary endpoints ultimately reached significance

- FDA's review documents the Agency's pre-submission concern in detail: "the FDA did not consider the marginal 4-week improvement in median PFS, which was less than the imaging interval, to be clinically meaningful in an add-on trial," and recommended waiting for OS; the Applicant elected to submit before final OS data were available, submitting the final OS analysis later during the review cycle

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2026/220641Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/220641s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review and Evaluation (combined statistical/clinical review) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/220641Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05257408 (ROSELLA)

- Pivotal publications: Olawaiye AB, Gladieff L, O'Malley DM, et al. Relacorilant and nab-paclitaxel in patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (ROSELLA): an open-label, randomised, controlled, phase 3 trial. *Lancet*. 2025;405(10496):2205-2216. [DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(25)01040-2>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40473448/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Relacorilant%20and%20nab-paclitaxel%20in%20patients%20with%20platinum-resistant%20ovarian%20cancer%20ROSELLA); Lorusso D, Gladieff L, O'Malley DM, et al. **Other resources**

- No trial-specific IPD/dataset access program (Vivli, YODA, Project Data Sphere) confirmed for Corcept

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting held

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review, §8.1.1.4, Statistical Analysis Plan and Amendments, PFS]* "The analysis of the primary endpoint of PFS assessed by BICR was planned to occur when at least 230 PFS events assessed by BICR had been observed. Based on the 1:1 randomization ratio, the 230 PFS events were to provide 86.4% power for a stratified 2-sided log-rank test with an α = 0.04 level of significance to detect a 50% increase in PFS."

- *[verbatim, same section, Multiplicity Adjustment for Efficacy Analyses]* "To maintain experiment-wise 2-sided type I error at 0.05, a group sequential weighted Holm procedure was used for the dual primary endpoints of PFS and OS. The study was positive if either of the 2 primary endpoints reached statistical significance... At the time of the primary analysis of PFS, an interim OS analysis using a 2-sided stratified log-rank test was conducted at an α = 0.0001 significance level (this constitutes the alpha spending function)... the final OS analysis was conducted at an α=0.0499 significance level."

- *[verbatim, same review, FDA's Assessment]* "The FDA communicated to the Applicant that in this add-on trial, a 1-month improvement in median PFS without a statistically significant improvement in OS is unlikely to be clinically meaningful and would not be adequate to support a marketing application (February 2025 and May 2025)... The FDA recommended that the Applicant await the final OS results before submitting an NDA. The Applicant elected to submit the NDA application prior to the final OS data availability."

- *[verbatim, FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review, §9]* "The Application was not referred for discussion at an Oncology Drug Advisory Committee meeting."

## Ophthalmology

### 1. Aflibercept (Eylea) — BLA 125387

**Sponsor:** Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of neovascular (wet) age-related macular degeneration (AMD)

**Approval date:** November 18, 2011

**Pivotal trial:** VIEW 1 (Study VGFT-OD-0605, NCT00509795) and VIEW 2 (Study 311523, NCT00637377) — two identically designed, multicenter, double-masked, randomized, active (ranibizumab)-controlled non-inferiority trials

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled non-inferiority trial design, 1:1:1:1 randomization across four arms (2 mg every 4 weeks [2Q4], 0.5 mg every 4 weeks [0.5Q4], 2 mg every 8 weeks after 3 monthly loading doses [2Q8], and 0.5 mg ranibizumab every 4 weeks [RQ4]); two identically protocoled trials (VIEW 1, VIEW 2) run in parallel by the same sponsor, a design pattern close to but not identical to the taxonomy's "two identically protocoled randomized... trials" entry (EMPA-REG/DECLARE-TIMI58 pattern), reused here; Independent Data Monitoring Committee (IDMC) periodic safety review with an alpha-spending-style significance-level correction (0.1%) applied to preserve overall Type I error across repeated safety looks

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint proportion of subjects maintaining vision at Week 52 (loss of <15 ETDRS letters from baseline) — the identical primary endpoint used in ranibizumab's own pivotal MARINA/ANCHOR trials; secondary endpoints change from baseline in BCVA (ETDRS letter score), proportion gaining ≥15 letters, change in NEI VFQ-25 quality-of-life score, and change in CNV lesion area

- *Primary analysis:* non-inferiority margin of 10 percentage points, evaluated via a step-wise conditional sequence of 95.1% confidence intervals (2Q4 vs. RQ4, then 0.5Q4 vs. RQ4, then 2Q8 vs. RQ4) — non-inferiority declared if the CI of the difference (ranibizumab minus VEGF Trap-Eye) lay entirely below 10%, with superiority assessable only if the CI lay entirely below zero and only after the full conditional sequence cleared non-inferiority; secondary endpoints tested for superiority using a pre-specified, endpoint-by-dose testing order (Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel-adjacent Pearson chi-square for proportions, ANCOVA for continuous outcomes), gated on non-inferiority of all three VEGF Trap-Eye arms being established first

- *Missing data/bias:* primary/secondary analyses used last-observation-carried-forward (baseline values not carried forward); FDA's reviewer additionally performed multiple imputation (Markov Chain Monte Carlo, 10 imputed datasets, multivariate-normal model for repeated BCVA measures) as a sensitivity analysis, which gave results consistent with but with wider confidence intervals than the LOCF primary analysis; FDA's data-quality review found 36 subjects in VIEW 2 mis-flagged as screening failures in the sponsor's analysis dataset despite being randomized — the reviewer reconstructed the correct disposition table from raw data and confirmed the error did not affect any efficacy analysis population or conclusion

- *Regulatory:* Dermatologic and Ophthalmologic Advisory Committee meeting held June 17, 2011 — unanimous 10-0 vote that efficacy and safety were demonstrated, with the committee specifically recommending the 2 mg every-8-weeks (2Q8) regimen (after 3 monthly loading doses) as the practical dosing regimen, despite 2Q8 not showing statistical superiority to ranibizumab on any endpoint

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Both trials enrolled men and women ≥50 years old with active primary subfoveal choroidal neovascularization (CNV) secondary to AMD, screening BCVA of 20/40 to 20/320 (ETDRS letter score 25-73), and CNV ≥50% of total lesion size in the study eye; all three angiographic AMD subtypes (occult, minimally classic, predominantly classic) were eligible, mirroring the ranibizumab development program's enrollment criteria

- Planned enrollment was 1200 subjects/study (300/arm); assuming a 90% vision-maintenance rate in both arms, 191 subjects/arm gave 90% power for a 10% non-inferiority margin at a (safety-look-adjusted) significance level of 0.049

- At Week 52 (Full Analysis Set, LOCF), the proportion maintaining vision was 93.8%-95.1% across all four arms in VIEW 1 and 94.5%-95.4% in VIEW 2; all three VEGF Trap-Eye regimens were non-inferior to ranibizumab in both trials (upper bound of each 95.1% CI below the 10% margin), but none showed superiority

- Secondary BCVA-change analysis showed a statistically significant advantage for 2Q4 over ranibizumab in VIEW 1 only (LS-mean difference 3.15 letters, 95.1% CI 0.92-5.37, p=0.0054), which was not reproduced in VIEW 2 (numerically favoring ranibizumab, not significant); per the pre-specified gated testing sequence, failure to replicate superiority in VIEW 2 ended confirmatory secondary-endpoint testing after the first step, leaving all further secondary comparisons descriptive only

- Safety data pooled across 1,824 aflibercept-treated subjects showed arterial thromboembolic events in 1.8% (32/1824) vs. 1.7% (10/595) for ranibizumab; endophthalmitis in 8 patients; transient post-injection intraocular pressure elevation in 1%-4% of patients

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2011/125387s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label (original, 2011) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2011/125387lbl.pdf

- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/125387Orig1s000StatR.pdf (scanned-image PDF; OCR'd for this entry)

- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/125387Orig1s000SumR.pdf (scanned-image PDF; OCR'd for this entry)

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (VIEW 1) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00509795

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (VIEW 2) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00637377

- Pivotal publication: Heier JS, Brown DM, Chong V, Korobelnik JF, Kaiser PK, Nguyen QD, et al; VIEW 1 and VIEW 2 Study Groups. Intravitreal aflibercept (VEGF trap-eye) in wet age-related macular degeneration. *Ophthalmology*. 2012;119(12):2537-2548. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ophtha.2012.09.006), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23084240/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Intravitreal%20aflibercept%20VEGF%20trap-eye%20in%20wet%20age-related%20macular%20degeneration)

**Other resources**

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID, OCR'd from scanned PDF), Executive Summary]* "These two studies demonstrated that VEGF Trap-Eye is non-inferior to 0.5 mg ranibizumab with respect to the proportion of subjects who maintained vision at week 52, based on a pre-determined non-inferiority margin of 10%... the design and conduct of both non-inferiority studies for the VEGF Trap-Eye program are considered adequate."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.3.1, OCR'd]* "The non-inferiority margin was set at 10%. The analysis included a step-wise conditional calculation of the 95.1% CIs of the difference in the proportion of subjects who maintained vision at week 52 between the group treated with 0.5 mg ranibizumab and each of the groups treated with VEGF Trap-Eye. The conditional sequence was: 2Q4, 0.5Q4, and then 2Q8 compared to RQ4."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.3.2, OCR'd]* "By Week 52 in study VIEW 2... the difference was not statistically significant. Thus, the sequential hypothesis testing for superiority of VEGF Trap-Eye to ranibizumab in a confirmatory manner had to stop after the first step (comparison of 2Q4 vs. RQ4) failed to show statistically significant difference. Therefore, any subsequent statistical tests no longer served any confirmatory statistical hypothesis testing."

- *[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, §9, OCR'd]* "the committee voted unanimously (10 vs. 0) that the product demonstrated efficacy and safety in neovascular AMD, and recommended the 2 mg every 8 weeks regimen (after 3 loading doses given every 4 weeks)."

### 2. Tafluprost (Zioptan) — NDA 202514

**Sponsor:** Merck & Co., Inc. (originally developed by Santen Pharmaceutical/Asahi Kasei Pharma)

**Indication approved:** Reduction of elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) in patients with open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension

**Approval date:** February 10, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** Study 001 ("MK-2452-001," NCT01026831, preservative-free tafluprost vs. preservative-free timolol, 12 weeks) and Study 15-003 (preservative-containing tafluprost vs. preservative-containing timolol, 12 months, no NCT identified — appears to predate/fall outside mandatory ClinicalTrials.gov registration as a non-US-only-era trial); bridging Study 77550 (preservative-containing vs. preservative-free tafluprost, crossover, no NCT identified) established formulation equivalence; supportive Study 74458 (tafluprost vs. latanoprost, 24 months) failed to demonstrate non-inferiority and was not used as a basis for approval

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Non-inferiority analysis against a fixed historical/regulatory-agreed margin, applied here as randomized, double-masked, active(timolol)-controlled parallel-group trials (Studies 15-003, 001) rather than a historical-control single-arm design — reuse of the taxonomy's non-inferiority-margin concept in a conventional concurrently-randomized active-controlled setting; separate crossover bridging study (77550) used specifically to establish preservative-free/preservative-containing formulation equivalence (PK/exposure-equivalence-bridging-adjacent concept, though here on a PD/efficacy endpoint rather than PK exposure); one of three "pivotal" non-inferiority trials submitted (Study 74458, vs. latanoprost) failed its own pre-specified non-inferiority criterion and was reviewed for safety only, not efficacy

- *Endpoints:* IOP change from baseline (mmHg) at multiple within-day timepoints (8:00, 10:00, 16:00, and in some studies 12:00/20:00) across visits through Month 6, 12, or 24 depending on study

- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA of IOP change from baseline with treatment and baseline IOP as covariates, evaluated at each visit/timepoint; non-inferiority margin of 1.5 mmHg (recommended to the Applicant by FDA's clinical review team during protocol design) — non-inferiority declared if the upper bound of the 95% CI for the between-treatment difference at every specified timepoint was below 1.5 mmHg

- *Missing data/bias:* primary analysis used last-observation-carried-forward; FDA's reviewer additionally performed a multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis (Markov Chain Monte Carlo, non-monotone missing-data pattern, 10 imputed datasets per treatment group, pooled ANCOVA), consistent with the LOCF primary analysis; the Applicant additionally used baseline-observation-carried-forward and worst-observation-carried-forward as sensitivity analyses, all conforming to the primary conclusion

- *Regulatory:* no dedicated Advisory Committee meeting was held for tafluprost specifically; FDA's Summary Review states the application was not referred to committee because tafluprost is a member of the ophthalmic prostaglandin-analog class whose benefit/risk profile had previously been discussed at a 1995 Dermatologic and Ophthalmologic Advisory Committee meeting, and tafluprost's own safety profile "did not raise any new significant safety issues"

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Study 15-003: randomized, double-masked, parallel-group, 12-month trial of preservative-containing (PC) tafluprost 0.0015% vs. PC timolol 0.5% (N=458, 267 tafluprost/191 timolol); IOP measured at 8AM/10AM/16PM at baseline, Week 2, Week 6, Month 3, 6, 9 (8AM/10AM only), and 12

- Study 001: randomized, multicenter, active-comparator, 12-week, double-masked trial of preservative-free (PF) tafluprost 0.0015% vs. PF timolol 0.5% (N=643, 320 tafluprost/323 timolol)

- Study 74458: randomized, double-masked, active-controlled, parallel-group, 24-month, multinational trial of PC tafluprost vs. PC latanoprost 0.005% (N=533); tafluprost did not meet the pre-defined 1.5 mmHg non-inferiority criterion against latanoprost at all specified timepoints (upper 95% CI bound exceeded 1.5 mmHg at several timepoints), so the study did not support the efficacy claim and was reviewed for safety only

- Study 77550: randomized, investigator-masked, multicenter, two-period crossover trial (N=43) comparing PC and PF tafluprost formulations (4-week treatment periods separated by ≥4-week washout); demonstrated that IOP-lowering effects of the two formulations were within the pre-specified ±1.5 mmHg equivalence range

- Across Studies 15-003 and 001, IOP reduction differences between tafluprost and timolol at nearly all visit/timepoint combinations had 95% CIs entirely within ±1.5 mmHg, supporting non-inferiority; representative results from Study 001 at Week 6, 16:00: tafluprost LS-mean change -6.33 mmHg vs. timolol -5.52 mmHg (difference -0.81, 95% CI -1.26 to -0.36)

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2012/202514s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label (original, 2012) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2012/202514s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Statistical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/202514Orig1s000StatR.pdf

- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/202514Orig1s000SumR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (Study 001) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01026831

- ClinicalTrials.gov records for Studies 15-003, 74458, and 77550 — none identified; these appear to be European-conducted trials predating or falling outside mandatory ClinicalTrials.gov registration

- Pivotal publication (Study 001): Chabi A, Varma R, Tsai JC, Lupinacci R, Pigeon J, Baranak C, Noble L, Lines C, Ho TW. ### 3. Ocriplasmin (Jetrea) — BLA 125422

**Sponsor:** ThromboGenics, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of symptomatic vitreomacular adhesion (VMA), including when associated with macular hole ≤400 microns in diameter

**Approval date:** October 17, 2012

**Pivotal trial:** TG-MV-006 (MIVI-TRUST, NCT00781859) and TG-MV-007 (MIVI-TRUST, NCT00798317) — two identically designed, multicenter, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-masked, 6-month Phase 3 trials

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-masked, placebo(vehicle-injection)-controlled, parallel-group; the two MIVI-TRUST trials were identical in design and conduct except treatment allocation ratio (2:1 in TG-MV-006, US-only; 3:1 in TG-MV-007, EU+US) — a vehicle (not sham) injection was used specifically to preserve masking

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint proportion of subjects with non-surgical resolution of focal vitreomacular adhesion in the study eye at Day 28, by masked Central Reading Center (CRC) OCT evaluation; key secondary endpoint proportion with total posterior vitreous detachment (PVD) at Day 28 by masked investigator B-scan ultrasound; additional secondary endpoints included non-surgical full-thickness macular hole closure (FTMHC) and categorical best-corrected visual-acuity (BCVA) change, each without a formal pre-specified multiplicity adjustment across the ≥5 secondary endpoints

- *Primary analysis:* Fisher's exact test for the between-arm comparison in each trial individually; Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by study for the integrated two-trial analysis; two-sided 95% CIs and exact odds ratios also reported; Full Analysis Set (all randomized, treated subjects), missing data imputed by last-observation-carried-forward as the primary approach, with observed-case and worst-case sensitivity analyses

- *Multiplicity:* FDA's reviewer explicitly flagged the FTMHC secondary endpoint as lacking multiplicity adjustment despite being tested across ≥5 secondary endpoints; applying a Bonferroni-corrected two-sided significance threshold of 0.01 to account for this, the reviewer found FTMHC was not statistically significant in TG-MV-007 (p=0.354) though it remained significant in TG-MV-006 (p=0.005) — leading FDA to recommend an additional pivotal trial specifically in patients with full-thickness macular hole at baseline before that indication could be independently supported

- *Missing data/bias:* primary/key-secondary analyses used LOCF; a multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis was also performed by the Applicant and found consistent with the LOCF primary results; notably, the improvement in the primary VMA-resolution and PVD endpoints was not accompanied by a corresponding improvement in visual acuity — more ocriplasmin-treated than placebo-treated patients showed worsening BCVA, a benefit/risk tension specifically discussed at the Advisory Committee meeting

- *Regulatory:* Dermatologic and Ophthalmologic Advisory Committee meeting held July 26, 2012 — unanimous vote that substantial evidence supported efficacy for VMA treatment, but only a majority (not unanimous) agreement that substantial evidence supported efficacy for macular holes generally regardless of adhesion status; the committee unanimously agreed the benefit-risk balance favored approval for the VMA indication despite anticipating that only a minority of the treated population would derive benefit

**Trial design & endpoints**

- TG-MV-006 enrolled 326 patients (219 ocriplasmin/107 placebo) at 42 US sites; TG-MV-007 enrolled 326 patients (245 ocriplasmin/81 placebo) at 48 EU/US sites; both used a single 125 mcg intravitreal ocriplasmin (or vehicle) injection

- Primary endpoint (VMA resolution at Day 28): TG-MV-006 27.9% (ocriplasmin) vs. 13.1% (placebo), difference 14.8% (95% CI 6.0-23.5%, p=0.003); TG-MV-007 25.3% vs. 6.2%, difference 19.1% (95% CI 11.6-26.7%, p<0.001)

- Key secondary endpoint (total PVD at Day 28): TG-MV-006 16.4% vs. 6.5% (difference 9.9%, p=0.014); TG-MV-007 10.6% vs. 0% (difference 10.6%, p<0.001)

- FDA's independent Bonferroni-adjusted (alpha=0.01) re-analysis of the FTMHC secondary endpoint found it not statistically significant in TG-MV-007, undermining a broader macular-hole claim without an adhesion requirement — leading directly to the label's restriction to VMA (with or without associated macular hole ≤400 microns) rather than an unrestricted macular-hole indication

- Package Insert / Label (original, 2012) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2012/125422s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/125422Orig1s000SumR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov record (TG-MV-007/MIVI-TRUST) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00798317

Enzymatic vitreolysis with ocriplasmin for vitreomacular traction and macular holes. *N Engl J Med*. 2012;367(7):606-615. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1110823), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22894573/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Enzymatic%20vitreolysis%20with%20ocriplasmin%20for%20vitreomacular%20traction%20and%20macular%20holes)

### 4. Lifitegrast (Xiidra) — NDA 208073

**Sponsor:** Shire Development LLC (lifitegrast originated at SARcode Bioscience, acquired by Shire in 2013)

**Indication approved:** Signs and symptoms of dry eye disease

**Approval date:** July 11, 2016

**Pivotal trial:** OPUS-2, NCT01743729, and OPUS-3, NCT02284516 (the two trials FDA ultimately relied on as the efficacy basis); OPUS-1, NCT01421498, was part of the original submission but is supportive rather than independently confirmatory (see Regulatory history below)

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials with co-primary sign/symptom endpoints in the original submission (OPUS-1, OPUS-2), followed by a Complete Response Letter and a single confirmatory resubmission trial (OPUS-3) in which the "sign" endpoint was redefined as a safety variable at FDA's request

- *Endpoints:* inferior corneal staining score (ICSS, "sign") and either the OSDI visual-related-function subscale (OPUS-1) or Eye Dryness Score (EDS, "symptom," OPUS-2/OPUS-3) at Day 84, co-primary in OPUS-1/OPUS-2; EDS alone as the single primary endpoint in OPUS-3, with ICSS retained as a safety variable analyzed as an efficacy variable for cross-study comparison only

- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA adjusting for baseline value (Phase 2) or baseline plus randomization stratification factors (Phase 3 trials), applied by FDA's reviewer as a common model across all four studies for cross-study comparability

- *Multiplicity:* co-primary endpoints in OPUS-1/OPUS-2 each required independent significance, with no combined-testing procedure bridging the two trials; substantial evidence of efficacy for the final "signs and symptoms" label claim was ultimately assembled by combining different, non-overlapping trials for each half of the claim (sign evidence from Phase 2 and OPUS-1; symptom evidence from OPUS-2 and OPUS-3) rather than from any single trial meeting both co-primary endpoints — a CRL-driven endpoint-status change carried across sequential trials in one resubmission program (**"CRL-driven endpoint status change in a resubmission trial"**; the existing "Mid-trial SAP amendment changing endpoint status" entry describes an amendment within one ongoing trial, not a status change made between sequential trials following a Complete Response Letter)

- *Missing data/bias:* last-observation-carried-forward-like imputation (last available data, including baseline if all post-baseline data were missing) applied consistently across the four studies for FDA's harmonized cross-study ANCOVA

- *Regulatory:* Complete Response Letter issued October 16, 2015, after OPUS-1 and OPUS-2 failed to replicate both co-primary endpoints in the same trial; resubmission (January 22, 2016) added OPUS-3 as a single new confirmatory trial

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Original NDA (submitted September 25, 2015) rested on a Phase 2 dose-ranging trial (mild-to-moderate dry eye disease), OPUS-1 (NCT01421498, N=588, mild-to-moderate dry eye disease), and OPUS-2 (NCT01743729, N=720, moderate-to-severe dry eye disease), plus a Phase 3 safety-only trial, SONATA. OPUS-1 and OPUS-2 both used co-primary endpoints: a "sign" endpoint (mean change from baseline in inferior corneal staining score, ICSS, 0-4 scale, at Day 84) and a "symptom" endpoint (OPUS-1 used the visual-related-function subscale of the Ocular Surface Disease Index, OSDI; OPUS-2 used the Eye Dryness Score, EDS, a 0-100 visual-analog scale).

- The two co-primary trials dissociated: OPUS-1 met its sign endpoint (p=0.0007) but missed its symptom endpoint (p=0.8261); OPUS-2 met its symptom endpoint (p<0.0001) but missed its sign endpoint (p=0.6122). Neither trial independently replicated both co-primary endpoints. FDA's review team concluded there was a lack of substantial evidence to support approval and recommended an additional adequate and well-controlled study, leading to a Complete Response Letter on October 16, 2015.

- The sponsor conducted a single new confirmatory trial, OPUS-3 (NCT02284516, N=711, 41 US sites), designed at FDA's request (raised at a Type A End-of-Review meeting and in written comments, December 2015) to redefine "sign" (ICSS) as a safety variable rather than a co-primary efficacy endpoint, retaining only the Eye Dryness Score symptom endpoint as OPUS-3's single primary endpoint — deliberately designed to reproduce OPUS-2's successful symptom result rather than re-attempt the sign endpoint that OPUS-2 had missed. FDA nonetheless required that ICSS results be reported and analyzed as an efficacy variable in OPUS-3 for cross-study comparison purposes, despite its formal reclassification as a safety variable within that trial.

- The resubmission (January 22, 2016) was ultimately approved for the general "signs and symptoms" indication, with FDA's Concluding Summary explicitly assembling substantial evidence by drawing sign evidence from Phase 2 and OPUS-1, and symptom evidence from OPUS-2 and OPUS-3 — i.e., no single trial supported both halves of the final labeled claim, but the combination of non-overlapping trials across the program did.

- FDA's statistical reviewer applied a common ANCOVA model across all four studies (Phase 2, OPUS-1, OPUS-2, OPUS-3) to enable cross-study comparability, adjusting for baseline value (Phase 2) or baseline plus randomization stratification factors (the three Phase 3 trials); missing data were handled via a last-observation-carried-forward-like approach (last available data, including baseline itself if no post-baseline data existed). Treatment differences in EDS at Day 84 (ANCOVA, LS means) were approximately 12 units in OPUS-2, 8 units in OPUS-3, 5 units in OPUS-1, and 7 units in Phase 2 — all favoring lifitegrast, though only OPUS-2 and OPUS-3 reached formal significance since only those trials pre-specified EDS as the (co-)primary symptom endpoint.

### 5. Latanoprostene bunod (Vyzulta) — NDA 207795

**Sponsor:** Bausch & Lomb Incorporated (originally developed by Nicox S.A.; licensed to Bausch & Lomb)

**Indication approved:** Reduction of elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) in patients with open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension

**Approval date:** November 2, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** APOLLO (Study 770), NCT01749904, and LUNAR (Study 769), NCT01749930

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-masked, active-controlled (vs. timolol 0.5%), parallel-group, multi-timepoint co-primary non-inferiority design requiring the NI margin to hold at every one of 9 measurement timepoints plus a tighter margin at a majority of timepoints
- *Endpoints:* Mean diurnal IOP at 3 visits (Week 2, Week 6, Month 3) × 3 daily timepoints (8 AM, 12 PM, 4 PM) = 9 co-primary timepoints
- *Primary analysis:* ANCOVA (treatment + time-matched baseline IOP as covariate, per timepoint), least-squares mean difference with 95% CI
- *Missing data/bias:* Time-matched LOCF for missing IOP values; reviewer-conducted repeated-measures ANCOVA as a robustness check
- *Regulatory:* Reviewer-documented FDA-sponsor negotiation over the primary analysis population (FDA rejected a sponsor proposal to redefine/narrow the ITT population post-hoc for the integrated efficacy summary)

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Two Phase 3, randomized, multicenter, double-masked, parallel-group trials (Study 769/LUNAR and Study 770/APOLLO) of near-identical design, each randomizing 420 subjects with open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension 2:1 to latanoprostene bunod 0.024% once daily or timolol maleate 0.5% twice daily, with a 3-month double-masked efficacy period followed by an open-label Vyzulta safety-extension period (9 months in Study 769, 3 months in Study 770).

- Primary efficacy endpoint: mean IOP in the study eye at 9 pre-specified timepoints (8 AM, 12 PM, and 4 PM at Week 2, Week 6, and Month 3).

- Non-inferiority criteria (both a "Statistical Criterion" and a "Clinical Criterion" had to be met): the upper limit of the 95% CI for the mean IOP difference (Vyzulta − timolol) had to be <1.5 mmHg at all 9 timepoints, and <1.0 mmHg at a majority (≥5 of 9) of timepoints.

- Primary analysis population ("Bausch-ITT"): randomized and treated subjects with a baseline and ≥1 post-baseline IOP assessment. An ANCOVA model (terms for treatment and time-matched baseline IOP) was fit separately at each of the 9 timepoints, with missing IOP values imputed by time-matched LOCF.

- Regulatory back-and-forth documented in the review: at a pre-NDA meeting (Feb 2015), the sponsor asked to redefine the ITT population for the integrated summary of efficacy to exclude randomized-but-minimally-assessed subjects; FDA declined, stating this "could potentially introduce bias," and required the primary analysis to include all randomized subjects with LOCF, plus worst-observed-outcome imputation for subjects with no IOP data at any visit. FDA also required a per-study (not solely pooled/integrated) submission to support the non-inferiority and superiority claims, on the standard requirement of ≥2 independently supportive trials for each claim.

- Results: IOP reductions of 7.5-9.0 mmHg (Vyzulta) vs. 6.5-7.9 mmHg (timolol) across the 9 timepoints; both statistical and clinical non-inferiority criteria were met in both trials. The secondary objective of statistical superiority over timolol was met at most, but not all, timepoints — one post-baseline timepoint in Study 770/APOLLO did not reach superiority.

- FDA reviewer robustness checks: an ANCOVA re-analysis using all randomized-and-treated subjects ("FDA-ITT," i.e., without the Bausch-ITT's post-baseline-assessment requirement), and a repeated-measures ANCOVA accounting for within-subject correlation across the 9 timepoints; both were consistent with the sponsor's findings.

### 6. Netarsudil (Rhopressa) — NDA 208254

**Sponsor:** Aerie Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

**Indication approved:** Reduction of elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) in patients with open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension

**Approval date:** December 18, 2017

**Pivotal trial:** ROCKET-1 (Study AR-13324-CS301), NCT02207491; ROCKET-2 (Study AR-13324-CS302), NCT02207621; ROCKET-4 (Study AR-13324-CS304), NCT02558374

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* Randomized, double-masked, active-controlled (vs. timolol 0.5% BID) non-inferiority trials, multi-timepoint co-primary non-inferiority design requiring the NI margin to hold at every one of 9 measurement timepoints plus a tighter margin at a majority of timepoints (shared with Vyzulta/latanoprostene bunod); post-hoc subgroup from a failed pivotal trial promoted to the pre-specified primary analysis population of subsequent same-program trials
- *Endpoints:* Mean IOP at 3 visits (Day 15, Day 43, Day 90) × 3 daily timepoints (8:00, 10:00, 16:00) = 9 co-primary timepoints; mean IOP change from baseline (protocol-defined secondary, but the basis for the label claims)
- *Primary analysis:* Per-protocol population primary analysis (unusual as the primary, rather than sensitivity, population); analysis restricted to a baseline-IOP-defined subgroup (<25 mmHg) in two of the three trials
- *Regulatory:* FDA Advisory Committee meeting held (Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee, October 13, 2017); reviewer-documented post-hoc subgroup promoted to pre-specified status in later same-program trials

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Three randomized, double-masked, active-controlled, non-inferiority Phase 3 trials of similar design but differing in baseline-IOP eligibility, dosing frequency, and duration: ROCKET-1 (Study 301; baseline IOP <27 mmHg; netarsudil QD vs. timolol BID; 3 months), ROCKET-2 (Study 302; baseline IOP <27 mmHg; netarsudil QD, netarsudil BID, and timolol BID; 12 months), and ROCKET-4 (Study 304; baseline IOP <30 mmHg; netarsudil QD vs. timolol BID; 6 months).

- Primary efficacy endpoint (all three trials): mean IOP in the study eye at 8:00, 10:00, and 16:00 hours on Day 15, Day 43, and Day 90 (9 timepoints total). Non-inferiority required the upper limit of the 95% CI for the mean IOP difference (netarsudil QD − timolol) to be within 1.5 mmHg at all 9 timepoints through Month 3, and within 1.0 mmHg at ≥5 of the 9 timepoints.

- Critical regulatory/statistical history: ROCKET-1's pre-defined primary analysis, conducted in the full per-protocol (PP) population, **failed** to demonstrate non-inferiority of netarsudil QD to timolol. A post hoc subgroup analysis restricted to patients with maximum baseline IOP <25 mmHg did demonstrate non-inferiority. Based on this post hoc finding, the sponsor pre-specified the <25 mmHg baseline-IOP PP subgroup as the primary analysis population in both subsequent trials (ROCKET-2 and ROCKET-4), and both met non-inferiority in that pre-specified subgroup.

- FDA reviewer's overall conclusion, stated in the Executive Summary: across all three studies, netarsudil QD was less efficacious than timolol 0.5% BID in patients with higher baseline IOP (≥25 mmHg), with the largest treatment gaps at the 8 AM and 10 AM morning timepoints on Days 43 and 90 (differences up to ~3 mmHg); the reviewer recommended the label present IOP-change results stratified by the <25/≥25 mmHg baseline subgroups.

- FDA Advisory Committee: the Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee met October 13, 2017, and voted 10-0 that the trials supported efficacy for IOP reduction, and 9-1 that efficacy outweighed the identified safety risks; the committee's labeling discussion recommended adding corneal verticillata to the Highlights section, among other changes.

- Pediatric context: two pediatric subjects (ages 11 and 14) were enrolled in ROCKET-2 (Study 302) under an agreed Pediatric Study Plan, but this was not a dedicated pediatric efficacy trial.

### 7. Cenegermin-bkbj (Oxervate) — BLA 761094

**Sponsor:** Dompé farmaceutici S.p.A.

**Indication approved:** Treatment of neurotrophic keratitis (topical ophthalmic solution)

**Approval date:** August 22, 2018

**Pivotal trial:** two co-pivotal trials — REPARO (Study NGF0212, NCT01756456), a Phase 1/2 trial conducted at 32 sites across 6 EU countries, and Study NGF0214 (NCT02227147), a Phase 2 trial conducted at 11 US sites; no Phase 3 trial was conducted for this program

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two co-pivotal, randomized, multicenter, double-masked, vehicle-controlled trials of low sample size (REPARO Phase 2 part N=156, 1:1:1 across two rhNGF concentrations and vehicle; NGF0214 N=48, 1:1 rhNGF 20 µg/mL vs. vehicle) — no Phase 3 trial was run for this orphan-designated program

- *Endpoints:* complete corneal healing/resolution of corneal staining, a binary responder endpoint whose definition was changed after both trials were already complete — closest existing taxonomy concept is a sponsor-driven "mid-trial SAP amendment changing endpoint status," but here the change was imposed by FDA after trial completion rather than by the sponsor before it: **"FDA-recommended primary endpoint (regulator-imposed post-hoc endpoint redefinition)"** — an endpoint version accepted by EMA and used in both original Clinical Study Reports was superseded, via CSR/SAP addenda following a March 2016 Type C meeting, by a stricter FDA-specified definition (0 mm lesion size with no residual/persistent staining, vs. the original <0.5 mm lesion-size threshold), with both endpoint versions reported in parallel in the US statistical review

- *Primary analysis:* chi-square test of responder proportions in the intent-to-treat population at Week 8 (and, for REPARO, also Week 4)

- *Multiplicity:* sponsor applied a Pocock-method alpha adjustment (two-sided α=0.0294) in REPARO to control for testing two rhNGF dose levels against vehicle; the FDA statistical reviewer identified this as a misapplication — **"Misapplied Pocock-method multiplicity adjustment for simultaneous multi-dose-vs.-control comparisons, corrected via a reviewer-substituted Bonferroni check"** — since the Pocock method is designed for repeated (group-sequential/interim) looks at accumulating data, not for a single-look comparison of multiple concurrent dose arms against a common control; FDA re-ran the analysis with a Bonferroni-adjusted α=0.0125 as a check, and both dose comparisons remained statistically significant under either method

- *Missing data/bias:* last-observation-carried-forward (LOCF) as the primary imputation method in both trials, with subjects lacking any post-baseline measurement excluded from the analysis population; sensitivity analyses in both trials included worst-case (missing=failure) imputation, multiple imputation, and observed-case analysis, and NGF0214 additionally used a tipping-point analysis ("replaced missing values with failures incrementally one-by-one until all missing values were replaced")

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held for this application; original NGF0214 protocol (per an April 2014 IND) proposed a corneal-lesion-diameter primary endpoint that the FDA clinical reviewer rejected in writing before the trial began, on the grounds that a statistically significant difference in lesion diameter "may be demonstrated that is not clinically significant"

**Trial design & endpoints**

- REPARO (NGF0212): randomized, multicenter, double-masked, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group trial in 6 EU countries (France, Germany, Italy, Poland, Spain, UK); Phase 2 part randomized 156 subjects 1:1:1 to rhNGF 10 µg/mL, rhNGF 20 µg/mL, or vehicle, all with unilateral (monolateral) neurotrophic keratitis; an 8-week masked treatment period was followed by an optional 8-week uncontrolled period (vehicle non-responders re-randomized to active drug) and a 48-week follow-up

- NGF0214: randomized, multicenter (11 US sites), double-masked, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group trial randomizing 48 subjects 1:1 to rhNGF 20 µg/mL + L-methionine vs. vehicle + L-methionine; unlike REPARO, bilateral neurotrophic keratitis was permitted (worse eye designated the study eye); follow-up was 24 weeks (vs. REPARO's 48)

- Primary endpoint (as ultimately analyzed by FDA in both trials): percentage of subjects with complete resolution of corneal staining — 0 mm lesion size and no residual/persistent staining, per reading-center (REPARO) or investigator (NGF0214) adjudication — assessed at Week 8; REPARO also reported the endpoint at Week 4

- Secondary endpoints (REPARO): healing at Week 6 (reading center) and Weeks 4/6/8 (investigator); corneal sensitivity improvement (Cochet-Bonnet esthesiometer); corneal clearing (modified Oxford scale = 0); incidence of deterioration; best-corrected distance visual acuity (BCDVA) change from baseline (ANCOVA); ≥15-letter BCDVA gain; time to deterioration onset; investigator global evaluation (5-point ordinal scale, analyzed via a multinomial proportional-odds mixed model); a post-hoc percent-change-in-lesion-size analysis (MMRM model, LOCF)

- Results at the FDA-recommended Week 8 endpoint: REPARO — rhNGF 10 µg/mL 62.7% vs. vehicle 33.3% (difference 29.4%, 95% CI 10.9–47.9, p=0.003); rhNGF 20 µg/mL 72.0% vs. vehicle 33.3% (difference 38.7%, 95% CI 20.7–56.6, p<0.001). NGF0214 — rhNGF 20 µg/mL 65.2% (15/23) vs. vehicle 16.7% (4/24) (difference 48.6%, 95% CI 24.0–73.1%, nominal p<0.001)

- No pre-specified multiplicity control was applied to NGF0214's secondary endpoints (nominal α=0.05)

- FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID 4272369) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/761094Orig1s000StatR.pdf

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Reference ID 4272369, quoting the reviewer's pre-trial comment on the original NGF0214 protocol]* "The primary efficacy variable as proposed is not recommended; a statistically significant difference in corneal lesion diameter may be demonstrated that is not clinically significant. We recommend that you utilize the primary efficacy variable discussed at the October 22, 2012, Pre-IND meeting (i.e. percentage of patients experiencing complete corneal healing at Week 4 or Week 8)."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Reference ID 4272369, on REPARO's multiplicity method]* "the Pocock method is discussed as a statistical test for a group sequential design, not as a method for multiplicity due to testing more than one active treatment versus vehicle"

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Reference ID 4272369, §5.3, p.37]* "In conclusion, based on the collective evidence summarized above, rhNGF 20 µg/mL demonstrated sufficient efficacy for the treatment of moderate or severe NK."

- **Reverse-engineered SAP** (for the endpoint-definition history, where no standalone sponsor SAP document was located as public): *[inferred]* the original protocol-defined endpoint ("complete healing," lesion size <0.5 mm) was accepted by EMA and used in both trials' original Clinical Study Reports, traceable to the Statistical Review's parallel reporting of results under both the original and FDA-recommended endpoint definitions; *[inferred]* the FDA-recommended endpoint's stricter "0 mm plus no residual/persistent staining" threshold was operationalized by reading-center (REPARO) or investigator (NGF0214) re-adjudication of the same underlying corneal images/exams rather than new data collection, traceable to the Statistical Review noting that usable ADaM datasets under the new endpoint definition were not received until March 28, 2018, well after both trials had completed follow-up.

### 8. Brolucizumab-dbll (Beovu) — BLA 761125

**Sponsor:** Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation

**Indication approved:** Treatment of neovascular (wet) age-related macular degeneration (AMD)

**Approval date:** October 7, 2019

**Pivotal trial:** HAWK (Study RTH258-C001, NCT02307682) and HARRIER (Study RTH258-C002, NCT02434328), both randomized, double-masked, active (aflibercept)-controlled, non-inferiority trials

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* two-year, multicenter, randomized, double-masked, active(aflibercept 2 mg)-controlled, non-inferiority trials — HAWK (3-arm, 1:1:1, brolucizumab 3 mg/6 mg/aflibercept, N=1,082 randomized) and HARRIER (2-arm, 1:1, brolucizumab 6 mg/aflibercept, N=743 randomized); both used a fixed default q12w dosing interval after loading doses, with protocol-defined disease-activity criteria triggering an individualized switch to q8w dosing — **"Response-adaptive fixed-interval dosing with criteria-triggered rescue-to-shorter-interval switching"** (distinct from a treat-and-extend design, since the default interval is fixed and only shortens on a defined trigger rather than continuously extending/contracting)

- *Endpoints:* primary — mean best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA, ETDRS letters) change from baseline to Week 48; key secondary endpoints included average BCVA change over Weeks 36-48 and q12w-dosing-maintenance status at Week 48 (time-to-first-q8w-need, analyzed via Kaplan-Meier: probability of remaining on q12w at Week 48 was 0.56 [95% CI 0.50-0.61] in HAWK and 0.51 [0.46-0.56] in HARRIER); anatomic secondary endpoints included central subfield thickness (CSFT) change and presence of intraretinal/subretinal fluid

- *Primary analysis:* ANOVA model (treatment, baseline BCVA category, age category) for the non-inferiority comparison against a pre-specified margin of 4 letters (one-sided); results — HAWK brolucizumab 6 mg vs. aflibercept: difference −0.16 letters (95% CI −2.13, 1.80); HARRIER: −0.70 letters (95% CI −2.39, 1.00); both met non-inferiority

- *Multiplicity:* a graphical alpha-recycling approach (Bretz et al., *Stat Med* 2009) splitting Type I error across three pre-specified test families, with the alpha allotted to any rejected-hypothesis family passed 50:50 to the two remaining families; applied to CSFT endpoints in HAWK but not in HARRIER

- *Missing data/bias:* full analysis set with last-observation-carried-forward/last-available-observation-prior-to-rescue as the primary approach; a mixed-model-for-repeated-measures (MMRM) analysis without imputation served as a sensitivity analysis; the FDA statistical reviewer disputed the sponsor's treatment of post-rescue data as "censored" rather than missing

- *Regulatory:* no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held; the original 2019 label carried no Boxed Warning; a 2020 label update (s004) added retinal vasculitis/retinal vascular occlusion language as Warnings and Precautions (§5.2), not as a Boxed Warning

- *Non-inferiority margin derivation:* the 4-letter margin was justified by FDA through an indirect, chained historical comparison — **"Non-inferiority margin chained through an intermediate (non-placebo-controlled) historical trial"** — anchoring first to ranibizumab's placebo-controlled effect size in MARINA (M1 margin ≥14 letters), then bridging via VIEW1/VIEW2's <4-letter aflibercept-vs.-ranibizumab difference, rather than a direct historical aflibercept-vs.-placebo trial

**Trial design & endpoints**

- Both trials enrolled treatment-naïve patients ≥50 years with active choroidal neovascularization secondary to AMD and BCVA 78-23 ETDRS letters; three monthly loading doses (Weeks 0, 4, 8), then aflibercept q8w to Week 88 vs. brolucizumab q12w to Week 92 (individualized switch to q8w per protocol-defined disease-activity criteria)

- Sample size (per the posted HAWK SAP, verbatim): "A sample size of 297 subjects per treatment arm is sufficient to demonstrate noninferiority (margin = 4 letters)... at a two-sided alpha level of 0.05 with a power of approximately 90% assuming equal efficacy and a common standard deviation of 15 letters... To account for a drop-out rate of 10%, a total of 330 subjects will be randomized per treatment arm (990 total)."

- FDA's NI-margin justification (verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Appendix J): "the reviewer also relies on one of the pivotal studies of Lucentis (ranibizumab 0.5mg)... MARINA... the estimated treatment effect of ranibizumab 0.5mg against sham was 17.4 letters... the lower bound of a 95% CI for the treatment effect was 14.4 letters... Given an M1 margin of ≥14 letters... and the similar performance (with a difference less than 4 letters) between aflibercept 2mg and ranibizumab 0.5mg in VIEW 1 and VIEW2, the reviewer finds the NI margin of 4 letters in the primary analysis acceptable." The reviewer separately flagged that baseline BCVA in HAWK/HARRIER (60-61 letters) was higher than in the historical MARINA/VIEW1/VIEW2 trials (52-55 letters), a population difference noted but not treated as disqualifying

- Package Insert / Label (original, 2019, no Boxed Warning) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2019/761125s000lbl.pdf

- Package Insert / Label (2020 update, s004, adds retinal vasculitis/occlusion Warnings and Precautions) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2020/761125s004lbl.pdf

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, HAWK posted SAP, sample-size section]* "A sample size of 297 subjects per treatment arm is sufficient to demonstrate noninferiority (margin = 4 letters)... at a two-sided alpha level of 0.05 with a power of approximately 90% assuming equal efficacy and a common standard deviation of 15 letters."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, Appendix J, on the non-inferiority margin]* "Given an M1 margin of ≥14 letters... and the similar performance (with a difference less than 4 letters) between aflibercept 2mg and ranibizumab 0.5mg in VIEW 1 and VIEW2, the reviewer finds the NI margin of 4 letters in the primary analysis acceptable."

- *[verbatim, FDA Statistical Review, on multiplicity]* graphical approach per "Bretz et al., Stat Med 2009;28:586-604," under which "once all null-hypotheses related to one set could be rejected, the corresponding alpha assigned to this set is passed with a 50:50 split to the two other sets."

- *[verbatim, 2020 label update, §5.2]* "Retinal vasculitis and/or retinal vascular occlusion, typically in the presence of intraocular inflammation, have been reported following BEOVU injections."

- **Reverse-engineered SAP**: not required for the primary efficacy analysis, since genuine SAP and Protocol documents are publicly posted for both trials (see Documents above); *[inferred]* the specific q12w-to-q8w disease-activity switching criteria used operationally in practice (as opposed to the general Kaplan-Meier "time to first q8w need" outcome reported in the label) are traceable to the posted protocols' visit-schedule and retreatment-criteria sections rather than restated verbatim here, given the length of those documents.

### 9. Brilliant Blue G (TissueBlue) — NDA 209569

**Sponsor:** D.O.R.C. (Dutch Ophthalmic Research Center) International b.v.

**Indication approved:** As an aid in ophthalmic surgery, to selectively stain the internal limiting membrane (ILM) of the retina (a disclosing/visualization dye, not a systemic drug)

**Approval date:** December 20, 2019

**Pivotal trial:** none — approved under 505(b)(2) based entirely on FDA's own review of published literature; the applicant "has not conducted or sponsored any clinical studies of this product"

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* a 505(b)(2) NDA for a surgical visualization dye with no sponsor-conducted or sponsor-sponsored clinical trial of any kind; FDA's Medical Officer instead performed a MEDLINE literature search (searches run in March 2015 and September 2019) identifying 18 independently conducted clinical studies (12 controlled) using Brilliant Blue G from varied manufacturers, and reviewed a representative sample study-by-study — this maps closely to the existing taxonomy term "Literature-based approval (no dedicated pivotal trial)" (seen in Landiolol), but differs in that the underlying studies here were heterogeneous non-RCT designs (systematic review/meta-analysis, electron-microscopy specimen studies, nonrandomized comparative case series, one randomized 2-arm trial) rather than a set of published RCTs, and no pooled/composite endpoint was constructed across them — propose as a refinement: **"FDA-conducted qualitative narrative literature synthesis across heterogeneous non-sponsor study designs, with no formal Biostatistics review performed"**

- *Endpoints:* no single pre-specified primary endpoint; individual literature studies used varied endpoints (ILM closure rate, BCVA, surgeon ordinal staining/visibility ratings such as a 1-4 "Surgeon's Intraoperative Assessment of Facility of Dye Usage" scale, tissue-preservation assessment by electron microscopy)

- *Primary analysis:* none in the sense of a formal hypothesis test performed by the applicant or FDA; the FDA review states plainly, "This is a 505(b)(2) application relying on published literature. The applicant has not conducted or sponsored any clinical studies... Biostatistics did not perform a review of this application" [reviewer's own text contains the typo "Biostatitics"]; individual source studies sometimes reported their own p-values internally, but these were not synthesized into a pooled statistical estimate

- *Missing data/bias:* not applicable in the conventional sense (no sponsor trial, no analysis population, no missing-data handling plan); FDA's review is a qualitative narrative synthesis, study-by-study, each with an independent author's conclusion and a separate FDA "Reviewer's Conclusion"

- *Regulatory:* orphan drug designation; the labeling's Full Prescribing Information omits Section 14 ("Clinical Studies") entirely, consistent with no single trial underlying the approval; no FDA Advisory Committee meeting held

**Trial design & endpoints**

- No sponsor-run pivotal trial exists. FDA's Medical Officer identified 18 published clinical studies (12 controlled) via a MEDLINE search using the terms "brilliant blue and eye," and reviewed a representative subset in the Medical Review and Summary Review, each labeled "Study #1" through at least "Study #8+," with a brief description of each study's design, an author's stated conclusion, and FDA's own reviewer conclusion on that study

- Representative example (Study #3, quoted from the Summary Review): a nonrandomized comparative interventional case series of "Fifty eyes of 50 patients," using a "Surgeon's Intraoperative Assessment of Facility of Dye Usage (1=satisfactory, 4=excellent)" rating ease of preparation, staining intensity, ease of use, ease of ILM peeling, and ease of dye removal, with an outcomes table reporting p-values (e.g., 0.010, 0.197, 0.049, 0.480) internal to that individual study, not pooled across the literature set

- Study #1 was a published systematic review/meta-analysis of Brilliant Blue G-assisted ILM peeling for macular hole surgery; other reviewed studies included electron-microscopy specimen studies assessing retinal tissue preservation and at least one randomized 2-arm trial

- No FDA-conducted or sponsor-conducted pooled statistical model, composite endpoint, or formal safety population/table was constructed across the reviewed literature; safety was assessed via an aggregate narrative review of adverse events reported across the individual published studies

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2019/209569Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label (original, 2019; Full Prescribing Information omits a Section 14 Clinical Studies section) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2019/209569s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Medical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/209569Orig1s000MedR.pdf

- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/209569Orig1s000SumR.pdf

- Drugs@FDA overview — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cder/daf/index.cfm?event=overview.process&ApplNo=209569

- ClinicalTrials.gov record — none; no registered trial underlies this approval, confirmed by CT.gov queries for both "TissueBlue" and "Brilliant Blue G ILM" (the latter returns only unrelated investigator-initiated trials)

- Protocol / SAP — none exists; no sponsor trial was conducted, and FDA's review states "Biostatistics did not perform a review of this application"

- Pivotal publication — none; the evidentiary basis is an FDA-curated review of 18 independently published studies rather than a single trial report. The Study #1 systematic review/meta-analysis cited in the Summary Review, on Brilliant Blue G-assisted ILM peeling for macular hole surgery, corresponds to PMID 27115851 (*Retina*. 2016;36(5):851-858) — [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27115851/) — but this is a supporting literature-review citation, not a company-sponsored pivotal trial publication, and should not be labeled as one

**Other resources**

- No IPD/dataset access program (Vivli, YODA Project, Project Data Sphere) applies — no patient-level dataset was ever submitted, since no sponsor trial was conducted

- No FDA Advisory Committee meeting was held ("Your application for TissueBlue was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary.")

**SAP — exact text / key excerpts**

- *[verbatim, FDA Summary Review]* "This is a 505(b)(2) application relying on published literature. The applicant has not conducted or sponsored any clinical studies of this product; however, clinical studies using this particular product have been conducted by individual clinicians and published."

- *[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, Biostatistics section]* "BIOSTATISTICS — This is a 505(b)(2) application relying on published literature. The applicant has not conducted any clinical studies... Biostatitics did not perform a review of this application." [typo present in original FDA document]

- *[verbatim, FDA Medical Review]* "The applicant has not conducted or sponsored any clinical trials of the product; however, individual investigators have conducted studies with the product and published their results in the literature supporting the safety and efficacy..."

- *[verbatim, FDA Summary Review, Advisory Committee section]* "No Advisory Committee Meeting was held for this application. There were no issues that were thought to benefit from a discussion at an advisory committee meeting."

- **Reverse-engineered SAP**: not applicable in the usual sense, since no sponsor trial or SAP was ever written for this product; the closest equivalent evidentiary structure is: *[inferred]* a MEDLINE search strategy (terms "brilliant blue and eye," searched March 2015 and September 2019) identifying candidate studies; *[inferred]* no prespecified primary/secondary endpoints across the literature set, since each source study's own endpoints (ILM closure rate, BCVA, surgeon ordinal staining/ease ratings, electron-microscopy tissue preservation) were retained rather than harmonized; *[inferred]* the "analysis" consisted of qualitative narrative synthesis, study-by-study, by the FDA Medical Officer rather than a pooled meta-analytic statistical model — traceable to the explicit statement that Biostatistics did not review the application.

### 10. Faricimab-svoa (Vabysmo) — BLA 761235

**Sponsor:** Genentech, Inc. (a member of the Roche Group)

**Indication approved:** Neovascular (wet) age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) and diabetic macular edema (DME), approved simultaneously as the first FDA-approved bispecific antibody for an eye disease (targets both VEGF-A and angiopoietin-2)

**Approval date:** January 28, 2022

**Pivotal trial:** for nAMD, TENAYA (NCT03823287) and LUCERNE (NCT03823300); for DME, YOSEMITE (NCT03622580) and RHINE (NCT03622593) — four identically structured Phase 3, randomized, double-masked, active-comparator (aflibercept)-controlled, non-inferiority trials

**Keywords:**

- *Design:* randomized (1:1:1), double-masked, active-comparator-controlled non-inferiority design comparing faricimab administered on a protocol-defined personalized treatment interval (PTI, extendable up to every 16 weeks based on objective disease-activity criteria) against fixed every-8-week aflibercept, replicated across two identically designed trials per indication — *("Personalized/extendable treatment-interval non-inferiority design tested against a fixed-interval active comparator")*; ICH E9(R1) estimand framework with mixed composite/hypothetical intercurrent-event strategies (treatment-policy strategy for non-COVID-19 intercurrent events, hypothetical/censored strategy for COVID-19-related intercurrent events) — matches Keyword_Taxonomy.md §4 term seen in Icotrokinra/Lebrikizumab-lbkz

- *Endpoints:* primary endpoint change from baseline in best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA, ETDRS letter score) averaged over Weeks 40/44/48 (nAMD) or Weeks 48/52/56 (DME); secondary endpoints included binary responder thresholds (≥15/≥10/≥5/≥0-letter gain, avoidance of ≥15/≥10/≥5-letter loss)

- *Primary analysis:* mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM; factors: treatment arm, visit, visit-by-treatment interaction, baseline BCVA continuous and categorical, prior anti-VEGF therapy or low-luminance deficit, region; unstructured covariance), non-inferiority margin of −4.0 letters, sample size of 320/arm per trial (640 total) providing ≥90% power assuming a true difference of 0 and common SD of 14 letters (two-sample t-test framework, one-sided α=0.025, 10% dropout); binary secondary endpoints analyzed via stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test with Miettinen-Nurminen-type weighted CI

- *Multiplicity:* study-wise Type I error controlled at a two-sided 5% significance level, with a nominal Type I error penalty (0.0003-0.0004) allocated for three or four unmasked independent Data Monitoring Committee interim reviews prior to the primary analysis, yielding a family-wise significance level of ~0.0497-0.0496 for the primary non-inferiority test; no formal multiplicity adjustment was applied across secondary endpoints, which were reported descriptively only

- *Missing data/bias:* FDA's statistical reviewer disagreed with the Applicant's primary-estimand strategy of excluding COVID-19-related intercurrent events from the treatment-policy population, instead treating the treatment-policy (all-observed-data) strategy as primary since COVID-19-related events "appeared not to be treatment-related" and were balanced across arms; for secondary binary endpoints, the reviewer further disagreed with the Applicant's use of observed-data-only analysis (which "does not maintain the study randomization") and instead imputed missing BCVA data via multiple imputation (MAR) as primary and LOCF as supporting — a reviewer-documented deviation from the Applicant's proposed analysis approach

**Trial design & endpoints**

- TENAYA (671 randomized) and LUCERNE (658 randomized) enrolled treatment-naive nAMD patients; YOSEMITE (940 randomized) and RHINE (951 randomized) enrolled DME patients; all four trials randomized 1:1:1 to faricimab on a fixed every-8-week schedule, faricimab on a personalized treatment interval (extendable up to q16w based on protocol-defined disease-activity criteria), or aflibercept every 8 weeks, with sham injections used to preserve masking

- Randomization was stratified by baseline BCVA category, prior anti-VEGF therapy or low-luminance deficit (nAMD trials), and region (US/Canada, Asia, rest of world)

- Both TENAYA/LUCERNE (nAMD) and YOSEMITE/RHINE (DME) met their pre-specified non-inferiority margin (−4.0 letters) versus aflibercept on the primary BCVA endpoint; e.g., in TENAYA the LS mean change was +6.4 letters (faricimab) vs. +6.6 letters (aflibercept)

- Discontinuation rates were low and comparable between arms (approximately 4% from study, 5-8% from treatment) in TENAYA/LUCERNE; a small number of COVID-19-related treatment discontinuations occurred in TENAYA (4 of 671 subjects), balanced across arms

**Documents**

- FDA Approval Letter — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2022/761235Orig1s000ltr.pdf

- Package Insert / Label — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2022/761235s000lbl.pdf

- FDA Statistical Review (Reference ID 4886826) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/761235Orig1s000StatR.pdf

- FDA Medical Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/761235Orig1s000MedR.pdf

- FDA Summary Review — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/761235Orig1s000SumR.pdf

- ClinicalTrials.gov records — TENAYA: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03823287; LUCERNE: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03823300; YOSEMITE: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03622580; RHINE: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03622593 — no protocol/SAP documents posted in the Documents tab for any of the four trials

[DOI](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(22)00010-1>), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35085502/), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Efficacy%20durability%20and%20safety%20of%20intravitreal%20faricimab%20up%20to%20every%2016%20weeks%20for%20neovascular%20age-related%20macular%20degeneration) — and — Wykoff CC, Abreu F, Adamis AP, et al.
